title: STRIDE threat model for the repository, CI and board administration surface
body:
## Context

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires a STRIDE threat-model kickoff for any epic labelled `security`, and `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes "threat model STRIDE per epic" a non-negotiable SDLC requirement. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 already models ten product areas (API keys, order path, rule engine, fan-out, WS, auth/RBAC, admin screens, recorder, Electron, network) — but **not the development and governance surface itself**, and §6.13/§6.14 cover supply chain and CI secrets as requirements without a threat model behind them.

That gap matters more here than in most projects. CandleViewer handles exchange API keys and live order flow; the repository and its CI are the upstream of every one of those controls. An attacker (or a careless insider) who can merge unreviewed code, alter a workflow, or weaken branch protection defeats every downstream control in `04-security-program.md` without touching a single runtime asset. E01 is also the epic that *creates* privileged automation (E01-T07's guard credential, E01-T08's repository-administration credential), so it must be modelled before those are built — hence this ticket blocks both.

## Scope / Deliverables

A STRIDE model committed as a new section of `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (**§5.12 — Area 11: Development, CI and governance surface**, keeping that document the single owner of the STRIDE content per C-16.5), covering:

- **Assets**: repository contents; `main` branch integrity; branch-protection configuration; CODEOWNERS; workflow definitions; the E01-T07 guard credential; the E01-T08 administration credential; Actions secrets in general; the GitHub Project board and its data; the backlog JSON tree; release tags and artefacts (forward-looking to E03).
- **Actors and trust levels**: Owner (`@basiltt`), engineers, contractors, **AI coding agents acting under `AGENTS.md`**, GitHub as a platform, third-party Actions authors, dependency maintainers.
- **Trust boundaries**: developer workstation → GitHub; PR from a branch vs from a fork; workflow runner → repository write scope; GitHub Projects API → board data; committed governance config → live platform settings (the drift boundary). Extends the TB-1…TB-8 register in `04-security-program.md` §4.1 with a new boundary id for the CI/SCM boundary, numbered to follow the existing register.
- **STRIDE enumeration** per boundary, with at minimum these threats explicitly analysed:
  - **S**: impersonating a code-owner approval; forging a QA/security sign-off by typing a marker into an issue body; a spoofed commit author identity (unsigned commits).
  - **T**: modifying `.github/workflows/` to disable a guard; weakening branch protection in the UI; tampering with `CONSTITUTION.md` to retro-justify a bypass; poisoning a third-party Action by floating tag.
  - **R**: an admin disabling and re-enabling protection with no record; a break-glass merge with no audit trail.
  - **I**: a secret leaked into logs by a workflow; a credential pasted into an issue body; repository contents exposed through an over-permissive workflow.
  - **D**: a required check that never reports blocking all merges; a guard credential expiring and failing closed indefinitely; CI exhaustion by a runaway workflow.
  - **E**: `pull_request_target` pwn-request giving a fork PR write access; an over-scoped PAT; a workflow with `permissions: write-all`; a compromised dependency of a checker script.
- **Risk rating** per threat using the same scale as `04-security-program.md` §5.11, with the existing risk-summary table extended.
- **Control mapping**: each threat mapped to a specific control shipped by this epic (E01-T04 ownership totality, E01-T07 fail-closed actor-attributed guards, E01-T08 `enforce_admins` + drift detection, E01-Q02 canary self-tests + weekly drift job, SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege permissions) or to an accepted risk with a dated owner sign-off.
- **New security requirements** (`SR-xxx` ids continuing the existing numbering in `04-security-program.md` §6.13/§6.14) for anything the epic's current design does not yet cover — e.g. commit signing, Actions SHA-pinning as a policy, a required-approval environment for admin-credential workflows.
- **Abuse cases** written as executable-style scenarios for QA/security to attempt (feeding E01-X02 and E01-Q01's charter).

## Out of scope

- Product-runtime threat models (keys, OMS, fan-out, RBAC) — already modelled in `04-security-program.md` §5.1–§5.10 and owned by E08/E09/E27/E29/E34.
- Implementing the controls — E01-T04/T07/T08/Q02 and E03.
- Pen-testing — R4 / E43.
- Threat-modelling the Electron shell, network or storage — existing areas, other epics.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category is enumerated for the new surface
  Given the development, CI and governance surface
  When the threat model is reviewed
  Then each of Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service and Elevation of privilege has at least one analysed threat
  And each threat has a risk rating on the same scale as the existing section 5.11 summary

Scenario: Every threat maps to a control or an accepted risk
  Given the enumerated threats
  When the control mapping is reviewed
  Then each threat names either a shipped control with its ticket key, or an accepted risk with a dated owner sign-off
  And no threat is left with an empty disposition

Scenario: The privileged automations are modelled before they are built
  Given E01-T07 and E01-T08 both create privileged credentials
  When those tickets enter development
  Then this threat model is already Done
  And its required controls appear in their acceptance criteria

Scenario: An unmitigated critical threat blocks the epic (failure path)
  Given a threat rated critical with no control and no signed acceptance
  When the epic is assessed for Done
  Then the epic cannot reach Done
  And the gap is tracked as a priority/p0-critical security ticket

Scenario: The pwn-request class is explicitly addressed
  Given the workflows shipped by this epic
  When the model reviews fork-triggered execution
  Then it records that pull_request_target with untrusted checkout is prohibited
  And it names the check or review step that enforces the prohibition
```

## Technical notes / design

Method: a 2-hour STRIDE-per-boundary workshop (Security engineer facilitating; Architect, DevSecOps, and the E01-T07/T08 owners attending), following the structure already used in `04-security-program.md` §5 so the new section reads as part of the same document rather than a bolt-on. Reuse its table format exactly: threat id, STRIDE category, description, affected asset, likelihood/impact/rating, control or acceptance.

Explicitly include **AI coding agents** as an actor class. `AGENTS.md` is a 529-line document that autonomous agents read and act upon, making it an instruction surface with real privilege implications: an agent that obeys a tampered `AGENTS.md`, or that is steered by injected content in an issue body it reads, is a genuine tampering/elevation path for this project. This is not a hypothetical for a repository whose planning artefacts are themselves agent-authored, and the model must state the control (CODEOWNERS on `AGENTS.md`, human approval on every PR regardless of author, no agent-triggered privileged workflow).

Commit signing: assess and make a recommendation with a cost/benefit note rather than mandating it reflexively — if adopted, it becomes an `SR-xxx` requirement and a branch-protection setting owned by E01-T08; if declined, that is recorded as an accepted risk with the reason.

## Test plan

- **Review**: the model is walked through at the Security Review ceremony (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §3) with the Architect and DevSecOps; sign-off recorded.
- **Abuse-case validation**: each written abuse case is attempted on a scratch repository by E01-X02/E01-Q01 and the observed outcome recorded against the predicted control — a control that does not actually stop its abuse case is a defect in the control, filed as a bug.
- **Traceability check**: every control named in the model resolves to a real ticket key in this epic or to an existing `SR-xxx` requirement.
- No unit tests (analysis artefact). Coverage: N/A.

## Security notes

This ticket *is* the security analysis. Its own risks: (a) a threat model that is written and then never revisited becomes false assurance — mitigated by a stated review trigger (re-review on any change to `.github/workflows/`, branch protection, or the credential set, and at the R4 live-enablement gate); (b) the model itself names attack paths, so it is kept in the private repository and must not include real credential identifiers, account names or token values — only classes and locations. Data classification: **internal-confidential** (attack-path detail), stored in the private repo only. Sign-off: Security engineer (author) + Architect + Owner `@basiltt`, as `04-security-program.md` is co-owned.

## Accessibility notes

N/A for the analysis itself. The document contribution follows the governance markdown conventions (single H1 context, nested headings, header-row tables, prose adjacent to any diagram) verified in E01-D02.

## Performance notes

N/A — no runtime component. One denial-of-service threat carries a performance dimension and must be analysed: a required check that never reports, or a governance job that grows past its 60 s budget, degrades into a delivery-availability problem; the model records that as a D-category threat with E01-Q02's duration budget as its control.

## Observability

The model must specify, per threat, **how we would know it happened** — this is its most operationally useful output: branch-protection drift → weekly drift job (E01-T08/Q02); workflow disabled → drift job's workflow-enabled check; guard credential expiry → fail-closed blocking plus the drift job; secret in logs → `secrets-scan` plus log redaction policy; unreviewed merge → git history audit. Threats with no detection path are called out explicitly as blind spots and either given one or accepted in writing.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] §5.12 (Area 11) added to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; boundary register §4.1 and risk summary §5.11 extended consistently.
- [ ] All STRIDE categories enumerated; every threat rated and dispositioned (control or dated accepted risk).
- [ ] New `SR-xxx` requirements added with ids continuing the existing numbering; no renumbering of existing requirements.
- [ ] Abuse cases written and handed to E01-X02 and E01-Q01.
- [ ] Detection path (or explicit blind-spot acceptance) recorded per threat.
- [ ] AI-agent actor class analysed with its controls.
- [ ] Commit-signing recommendation recorded (adopt with an `SR-xxx`, or decline with a reason).
- [ ] Reviewed at Security Review; **sign-off comments from the Security engineer, Architect and `@basiltt`**.
- [ ] Re-review trigger documented.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated with any new epic-level risk.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner (`/docs/plan/04-security-program.md` → security + architecture).

## Dependencies

No blockers — must run first in Sprint 01, because it **blocks E01-T07 and E01-T08**: neither privileged automation should be designed before its threats are known (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the kickoff at epic entry, not at epic close). Feeds E01-X02 (which verifies the controls on the shipped workflows) and E01-Q01's exploratory charter.

## Branch

`docs/gov-stride-ci-surface`. PR size: ~300 lines of analysis; within guidance.

## References

- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §4.1 boundary register, §5 STRIDE areas 1–10, §5.11 risk summary, §6.13 supply chain, §6.14 CI secrets
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 STRIDE kickoff, §8 security gating
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §3 Security Review ceremony
- `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (STRIDE per epic, non-negotiable)
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`
- `CONSTITUTION.md` §12 security constitution, §9 quality gates, C-16.5
- `AGENTS.md` (agent actor class)


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §4.1 boundary register, §5 STRIDE areas 1–10, §5.11 risk summary, §6.13 supply chain, §6.14 CI secrets
2. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 STRIDE kickoff, §8 security gating
3. `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §3 Security Review ceremony
4. `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (STRIDE per epic, non-negotiable)
5. `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`
6. `CONSTITUTION.md` §12 security constitution, §9 quality gates, C-16.5

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan/`
- `docs/adr/`
- `docs/research/`
- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what's listed in References.

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint (markdown lint job)`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `docs/gov-stride-ci-surface`
- PR title: "E01-X01: STRIDE threat model for the repository, CI and board administration surface"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/architecture
- Labels: type/task, area/docs, priority/p0-critical, security

**Done means**
- §5.12 (Area 11) added to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; boundary register §4.1 and risk summary §5.11 extended consistently.
- All STRIDE categories enumerated; every threat rated and dispositioned (control or dated accepted risk).
- New `SR-xxx` requirements added with ids continuing the existing numbering; no renumbering of existing requirements.
- Abuse cases written and handed to E01-X02 and E01-Q01.
- Detection path (or explicit blind-spot acceptance) recorded per threat.
- AI-agent actor class analysed with its controls.

**Do NOT**
- Product-runtime threat models (keys, OMS, fan-out, RBAC) — already modelled in `04-security-program.md` §5.1–§5.10 and owned by E08/E09/E27/E29/E34.
- Implementing the controls — E01-T04/T07/T08/Q02 and E03.
- Pen-testing — R4 / E43.
- Threat-modelling the Electron shell, network or storage — existing areas, other epics.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

title: Monorepo scaffold & toolchain
body:
## Context
CandleViewer today contains planning documents only — there is no `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `turbo.json` or `pyproject.toml` in the tree (`AGENTS.md` §4 status note). Every other R0 epic (E03 CI/CD, E05 design system, E06 engine spike, E07 storage spike, E08 ingestion) is blocked on a working workspace: `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 encodes `E01 --> E02 --> E03`, `E02 --> E05`, `E02 --> E06`, `E02 --> E07`, `E02 --> E08`, and §12 puts E02 first on the critical path `E02 → E06 → E11 → E12 → E18 → E26 → E38 → E44 → E46 → GA`.

This epic creates the repository skeleton described in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §5 (monorepo layout) and makes the module boundaries of `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 (M1–M24 backend modules, the five frontend package rules C-3.5) **machine-enforced** from the first commit via `import-linter` and `dependency-cruiser`, so boundary rot can never start. It also delivers the local runtime (`docker compose` on WSL Ubuntu: api, postgres, questdb, grafana, prometheus, minio) so engineers and the CI integration job have an identical stack.

Scope per `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2: "pnpm workspace + uv/poetry Python workspace; packages `chart-engine`, `protocol`, `ui`, `app-web`, `app-electron`; services `api`; `import-linter` contracts encoding `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 module edges; ESLint/Prettier/Biome, ruff, mypy strict, pytest, vitest; commitlint + husky; `.editorconfig`; Docker Compose for WSL Ubuntu" — 42 pts, sprints S01–S02.

References: `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md#5-monorepo-layout`, `/CONSTITUTION.md` §3 and §9, `/AGENTS.md` §4.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Root pnpm workspace + Turborepo task graph implementing **every** task name in `AGENTS.md` §4 (`pnpm lint`, `lint:fix`, `format`, `typecheck`, `test`, `test:cov`, `build`, `size`, `generate`, `verify`).
- `packages/config` shared ESLint flat config, Prettier, tsconfig bases, Vitest preset.
- Package skeletons: `packages/chart-engine`, `packages/ui`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/fixtures`, `packages/config`.
- App skeletons: `apps/web` (Vite + React 18 + TS), `apps/desktop` (Electron shell, no business logic).
- `services/api` Python package skeleton with module directories M1–M24 per `CONSTITUTION.md` §3, composition root `app.py`, `settings.py` (module **M1 `config`**), `uv` + Hatch project, ruff/black/mypy-strict/pytest.
- `import-linter` contracts encoding the M1–M24 allowed-dependency table and C-3.2/C-3.3; `dependency-cruiser` + `no-restricted-imports` for TS (C-3.5, deep-import ban).
- commitlint + husky + lint-staged + `.editorconfig` + `scripts/check-agents-commands.mjs`.
- `infra/compose/` docker-compose for WSL Ubuntu: api, postgres, questdb, grafana, prometheus, minio; `.env.example`; `make up|dev|test|gen`.
- Protocol generation pipeline (`pnpm generate`) from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` + `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` with a staleness check.
- Coverage gates wired locally at the thresholds of `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 (#3 ≥85% backend, #4 ≥85% engine, #5 ≥80% web/ui).
- ADR-0016 "Monorepo tooling and task graph"; QA, security and design-handoff tickets listed in §Story list of this body.

## Out of scope
- GitHub Actions workflows, merge queue, branch protection, deploy jobs — **E03**.
- Prometheus dashboards/alert rules and structlog redaction implementation — **E04** (this epic only starts the containers).
- Actual design tokens, components, Storybook content — **E05** (this epic provides the package and token-build wiring only).
- Any chart-engine rendering code — **E06**/**E11**; any Bybit code — **E08**.
- Alembic migrations content and QuestDB DDL — **E07**.
- Android/mobile targets, a separate admin app, non-Bybit exchanges (C-1.2).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a clean clone of the repository on WSL Ubuntu with pnpm, Node LTS, uv and Docker installed
When an engineer runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm verify`
Then every task named in AGENTS.md §4 exists and the whole gate exits 0 in under 10 minutes

Given the scaffold is merged
When a developer adds an import from services/api/oms into services/api/secrets
Then the `architecture` check (import-linter contract for C-3.2) fails with a named contract violation

Given the scaffold is merged
When a developer adds `import { x } from "apps/web/src/.."` inside packages/ui
Then dependency-cruiser fails the build citing C-3.5

Given `make up` is run on WSL Ubuntu with no Bybit credentials
When the compose stack starts
Then api, postgres, questdb, prometheus, grafana and minio all reach healthy within 120s and `curl localhost:8000/healthz` returns 200

Given docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml is edited
When `pnpm generate` has not been re-run
Then the generated-code staleness check fails with a non-empty diff
```

## Technical notes / design
Layout is fixed by `20-architecture.md` §5 and must be reproduced exactly (paths are cited by CODEOWNERS, import-linter contracts and later tickets). JS: pnpm workspaces + Turborepo; Python: `uv` + Hatch, single `services/api/pyproject.toml`. A `Makefile` is the human front-end (`make dev|test|gen|up`) delegating to pnpm/uv so there is one entry point per `20-architecture.md` §5 Tooling. Package names are `@candleviewer/<name>` per `AGENTS.md` §4 filters. All TS projects use `strict: true`; Python uses `mypy --strict`. No package may declare a dependency on an app (C-3.5).

## Test plan
Each child ticket carries its own plan; epic-level: a **clean-clone bootstrap matrix** (fresh WSL Ubuntu container, fresh Windows+WSL dev box) executed by QA (Q02), plus the toolchain regression pack (Q03) that asserts every Constitution §9 gate is runnable locally with the same command CI will use.

## Security notes
Supply-chain is the epic's dominant threat (STRIDE model in X01): dependency confusion, malicious postinstall scripts, lockfile tampering, leaked secrets in `.env`, and container images pulled by mutable tag. Controls: frozen lockfiles, `pnpm` `ignore-scripts` review, pinned image digests in compose, license allowlist (§9 #14), gitleaks baseline, `.env.example` only — never a real `.env` committed. Data classification: no production data touched; compose volumes are local-only and must bind to `127.0.0.1` (C-2 trust boundary B2).

## Accessibility notes
No user-facing screens are introduced. The epic wires the `a11y` tooling seams (axe-core devDependency, Storybook a11y addon hook point in `packages/ui`) consumed by E05/E03. D01 covers the token-pipeline handoff contract.

## Performance notes
No runtime budget from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` applies yet. Toolchain budgets: `pnpm verify` ≤10 min cold / ≤3 min warm (Turbo cache) on reference hardware (§3.1); `make up` ≤120 s to all-healthy. The chart-engine `bench` task must exist (empty baseline) so E06 can land numbers without re-plumbing.

## Observability
`/healthz` and `/readyz` stubs in `services/api` returning static payloads plus a `build-info` field (git sha, version) — E04 fills in real checks. Compose ships prometheus scraping `api:/metrics` (stub registry) so E04 has a target on day one.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] `pnpm verify` and `uv run pytest` green on a clean clone; coverage gates configured at §9 thresholds (may report 100% on empty packages — the *gate must exist*).
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` §4 corrected in the same PR wherever a real script name deviates; `check-agents-commands.mjs` green.
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged.
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §5 updated if the shipped layout diverged.
- [ ] STRIDE model (X01) complete, findings triaged; Security engineer sign-off.
- [ ] QA epic-level sign-off (Q01–Q03) recorded.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review: clean clone → `pnpm verify` → `make up` → healthy stack.
- [ ] Retro note filed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E01` — CODEOWNERS, PR/issue templates, branch protection and the Constitution ratification must exist before the tree they own is created. Downstream: E03, E04, E05, E06, E07, E08 all consume this scaffold.

## Branch
`feat/monorepo-scaffold-*` per child ticket; epic itself has no branch. PR size: each child ≤400 LOC diff excluding lockfiles and generated output (C-4.8); lockfile-only churn declared in the PR body.

## References
- docs/plan/20-architecture.md#5-monorepo-layout
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §4.2, §11.1, §12
- /CONSTITUTION.md §3, §9
- /AGENTS.md §4
- docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md, docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md

## Dependency graph of children
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    K01[K01 Spike tooling ADR] --> T01[T01 pnpm+Turbo root]
    K01 --> T02[T02 Python uv workspace]
    T01 --> T03[T03 TS package skeletons]
    T01 --> T07[T07 commitlint/husky/editorconfig]
    T03 --> T04[T04 apps/web + apps/desktop]
    T02 --> T05[T05 services/api skeleton M1-M24]
    T05 --> T06[T06 import-linter + dep-cruiser]
    T03 --> T06
    T05 --> T08[T08 docker compose + Makefile]
    T03 --> T09[T09 protocol codegen + staleness]
    T05 --> T09
    T03 --> T10[T10 coverage + verify gates]
    T05 --> T10
    T06 --> T11[T11 ADR-0016 + AGENTS reconcile]
    T09 --> T11
    D01[D01 token pipeline handoff] --> T03
    T10 --> Q01[Q01 scaffold test plan]
    T08 --> Q02[Q02 clean-clone charter]
    T10 --> Q03[Q03 toolchain regression pack]
    T01 --> X01[X01 STRIDE supply chain]
    X01 --> X02[X02 SAST/secrets/license baseline]
```

## Estimate reconciliation (2026-09-14)
The locked roadmap allocates **42 pts** to E02 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, line 102; §4.2 R0 scope table, line 185). An earlier backlog draft summed to 64 pts (+52%), far outside the ±15% tolerance. **Resolution: the roadmap is authoritative and unchanged; the backlog was re-estimated down to 42 pts.** Every child ticket carries an "Estimate reconciliation" note recording its old and new figure and the rationale (scaffolding work is overwhelmingly generator-driven: `pnpm create`, `uv init`, Turborepo/Vitest presets, Electron Forge and upstream compose templates; the original numbers priced it as bespoke implementation).

Current roll-up (must stay equal to the roadmap figure — any change requires a roadmap PR, not a silent backlog edit):

| Kind | Tickets | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| Spike | K01 | 2 |
| Task (engineering) | T01–T10 | 27 |
| Task (docs) | T11–T12 | 3 |
| Design | D01 | 2 |
| QA | Q01–Q03 | 4 |
| Security | X01–X02 | 4 |
| **Total** | **19** | **42** |

Guard: if in-sprint discovery pushes the true size above 48 pts (42 + 15%), the disposition is to **descope T12 (onboarding docs) and Q02 (second-machine exploratory charter) into R0 sprint S03/E03**, not to overrun S02 — both are P2 and neither gates E03/E05/E06/E07/E08.

## Schedule risk & buffer
E02 is the single highest-fan-out node in the roadmap: `E01 → E02 → {E03, E05, E06, E07, E08}` (§11.1) and it opens the critical path `E02 → E06 → E11 → E12 → E18 → E26 → E38 → E44 → E46 → GA` (§12). It starts in **Sprint 01 (2026-09-25)**, the same sprint as its blocker E01, so an E01 slip propagates with no natural slack. This is accepted, with the following explicit mitigations rather than implicit optimism:

1. **Parallel start, not serial.** `E02-K01` (tooling spike) and `E02-D01` (token-handoff contract) are deliberately **not** blocked on E01 — they produce decision documents, not merges into a protected `main`, so they proceed from day 1 of S01 while E01 ratifies the constitution and branch protection.
2. **E01 hard-gate is narrow.** Only `E02-T01` takes the E01 dependency, and only for `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 (module edge table) + CODEOWNERS paths. If E01 slips past S01 day 3, T01 proceeds against the **draft** §3 table on a feature branch; the import-linter contracts in T06 are re-verified against the ratified text before the epic's DoD is claimed.
3. **Named slack in S02.** The S02 tail (`T11`, `T12`, `Q02`, `Q03`, `X02` — 7 pts, all P1/P2, none on the critical path) is the epic's buffer. If S01 delivery slips, these absorb the slip inside E02 rather than pushing the S02 exit date or E06's S02 start.
4. **Downstream unblock order.** Ticket completion is sequenced so the highest-fan-out artefacts land first: `T01/T03` (packages exist) unblocks E05/E06 mid-S01; `T02/T05` unblocks E07/E08; `T06/T10` (gates) unblocks E03. E03/E05/E06 do **not** wait for the whole epic to close.
5. **Tracking.** Logged as a schedule-risk item against **R5 Scope** in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`; reviewed at the S01 mid-sprint checkpoint. Trigger: if `E02-T01` is not merged by S01 day 5, escalate at once and cut T12/Q02 per the guard above.


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Design: define the design-token → code handoff contract for the packages/ui build
body:
## Context
E02 introduces no screens of its own, but it does create `packages/ui` and must wire its **token build** (E02-T03). `16-design-system-brief.md` §2 defines a three-tier token architecture (Tier 1 global/primitive, Tier 2 alias/semantic — the layer `15-component-catalogue.md` entries reference, e.g. `color.buy`, `font.mono`, `space.field.gap` — and Tier 3 component tokens used sparingly), §11 defines the handoff spec (tokens JSON → code) and §13 defines the design-ahead process and sign-off definition. E05 (design system v0, S01–S04, design-led) will author the actual token values; if the *file format, naming and build contract* are not agreed before `packages/ui` is scaffolded, E05 lands two sprints later into a pipeline shaped by an engineer's guess and pays for it in rework across every component. The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`: design runs ≥2 sprints ahead) makes S01 the correct slot for this contract, ahead of its consuming work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A written **handoff contract** (added as a subsection of `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §11, not a new doc) specifying: the tokens JSON format (W3C Design Tokens Community Group format), directory layout in `packages/ui/src/tokens/`, the Tier 1/2/3 file split, naming rules and the casing convention, theme file structure for dark (default), light and high-contrast, and the density-mode dimension (`16-design-system-brief.md` §3).
- The Style Dictionary transform/format list and the exact generated outputs engineering may consume: CSS custom properties, a TS token module (typed, autocompletable), and a **plain JSON export for the chart engine**, since `packages/chart-engine` renders to canvas and cannot read CSS variables (`16-design-system-brief.md` §8 downstream note: the engine consumes colour/typography tokens for canvas rendering, and C-2.16 forbids it depending on React/DOM styling).
- Figma variable-collection → tokens JSON export procedure and its cadence/ownership.
- Sign-off criteria and the named sign-off roles (CDO or delegate for the design side, chart-engine owner for the engine export shape, frontend lead for the TS surface).
- Two worked examples carried end-to-end through the contract (`color.buy` and `space.field.gap`) so E02-T03 can write the build against something concrete.

## Out of scope
- Actual token values, palettes, type scale, motion curves, themes — **E05**.
- Any component design or screen design (E02 introduces no screens; `12-sitemap.md`/`14-screens-catalogue.md` entries are untouched).
- Storybook content and visual-regression baselines — E05.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the handoff contract
When the chart-engine owner reviews it
Then a plain-JSON token export consumable without DOM or CSS is specified, and sign-off is recorded on the ticket

Given the contract's two worked examples
When an engineer implements the Style Dictionary build in E02-T03
Then color.buy and space.field.gap resolve through Tier 1 → Tier 2 to all three outputs with no ambiguity and no question raised back to design

Given a token that exists in Tier 1 but is referenced directly by a component
When the contract's lint rule is applied
Then it is flagged, enforcing the §2 rule that Tier 1 is never referenced directly by components

Given the high-contrast theme
When the contract is reviewed against 05-accessibility-standard.md
Then every semantic colour pair carries a stated minimum contrast ratio and the WCAG 2.2 AA target is explicit, with sign-off from the accessibility specialist
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the W3C DTCG JSON format (`$value`, `$type`, `{alias.reference}` syntax) so Figma variables, Style Dictionary and any future tool interoperate without a bespoke converter. The engine export must be flat and resolved (no aliases left unresolved) with colours as both hex and normalised float RGBA, because WebGL needs the latter and a per-frame string parse would be unacceptable against frame budget #1 (≤16.6 ms p95). Theme switching for the engine is a data swap, not a CSS cascade — the contract must say so explicitly so E11 does not assume otherwise.

## Test plan
N/A as automated tests — this is a design/contract artefact. Verification is by review: the contract is walked through by the frontend lead and the chart-engine owner against the two worked examples, and the resulting build in E02-T03 is the acceptance evidence. A schema-validation test of the tokens JSON against the DTCG schema is specified here and implemented in E02-T03.

## Security notes
N/A — no data, no credentials, no runtime surface. (Figma access control is covered by the design org's own tooling policy, not by this ticket.)

## Accessibility notes
The contract must require, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` and `16-design-system-brief.md` §9: a high-contrast theme as a first-class theme rather than an afterthought; documented minimum contrast ratios on every semantic foreground/background pair (WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text and non-text UI); a `prefers-reduced-motion` token dimension for the motion tokens of §7; and focus-ring tokens that remain visible in all three themes. Accessibility specialist sign-off is a gating criterion.

## Performance notes
The engine token export must be resolved and numeric to avoid per-frame parsing (budget #1). Token build time ≤10 s so `pnpm generate` stays inside its 60 s budget.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Contract merged into `16-design-system-brief.md` §11 with the two worked examples.
- [ ] Sign-offs recorded on the ticket: CDO (or delegate), chart-engine owner, frontend lead, accessibility specialist.
- [ ] Status Done ≥2 sprints before the consuming FE work in E05 (design-ahead rule) — verified at E05 DoR.
- [ ] E02-T03 implements the build against the contract with no clarification requests (evidence: no blocking questions on that ticket).
- [ ] markdownlint green; PR merged via merge queue with CDO approval.

## Dependencies
Blocked by E01 (design ticket conventions, labels and CODEOWNERS for `docs/plan/16-*`). Blocks E02-T03 and de-risks E05.

title: Create root pnpm workspace, Turborepo task graph and shared config package
body:
## Context
The repository has no JS workspace at all. Every frontend and engine ticket from R0 onward (`E05` design system, `E06` engine spike, `E10` shell, `E11` engine core) needs a workspace root with a task graph whose task **names** match `AGENTS.md` §4 exactly — that file is the single place command names are enumerated, and `generated-code-check` (Constitution §9 #19) fails the build when the documented set and the real task graph diverge.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `/package.json` (private, packageManager pinned), `/pnpm-workspace.yaml` covering `apps/*`, `packages/*`.
- `/turbo.json` defining pipelines with correct `dependsOn` edges and cache inputs/outputs for: `lint`, `lint:fix`, `format`, `typecheck`, `test`, `test:cov`, `build`, `size`, `generate`, `verify`.
- `packages/config`: shared **ESLint flat config** (`eslint.config.mjs`), Prettier config, `tsconfig.base.json` (+ `tsconfig.node.json`, `tsconfig.dom.json`), Vitest preset, and a `no-restricted-imports` rule set stub consumed by E02-T06.
- `/.nvmrc` + engines field pinning Node LTS; `/.npmrc` with `ignore-scripts` policy and `frozen-lockfile` defaults.
- `scripts/check-agents-commands.mjs`: parses the `|`-rows of `AGENTS.md` §4, resolves each against `turbo run --dry=json` / `pnpm -r run --help`, exits non-zero on a missing documented task or an undocumented user-facing task.
- Root `Makefile` targets `dev`, `test`, `gen`, `up` delegating to pnpm/uv (`20-architecture.md` §5 Tooling).

## Out of scope
- Individual package contents (E02-T03/T04), Python side (E02-T02), compose (E02-T08), CI workflows (E03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a clean clone
When `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` runs
Then it completes without network writes to the lockfile and exits 0

Given the workspace root
When `pnpm verify` runs
Then it executes lint, typecheck, test:cov and build in dependency order and exits 0

Given AGENTS.md §4 documents a task `pnpm size`
When that task is removed from turbo.json
Then `node scripts/check-agents-commands.mjs` exits non-zero naming the missing task

Given a single file changes in one package
When `pnpm verify` is re-run
Then Turbo reports cache hits for all unaffected packages and the warm run completes within the budget recorded in ADR-0018 (docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0018-monorepo-tooling.md, drafted by spike E02-K01)
```

## Technical notes / design
ESLint must use the **flat config** form (`eslint.config.mjs`) with `--max-warnings=0` to satisfy Constitution §9 #1. Prettier runs in check mode inside `lint` and write mode inside `format`. `verify` = `lint && typecheck && test:cov && build && size` — the local mirror of the PR gate, so an engineer can reproduce CI without pushing. Turbo `outputs` must include `dist/**` and `coverage/**`; `inputs` must exclude `**/*.md` so doc edits do not bust the cache. Do not add a remote cache yet (E03 decides the CI cache backend).

## Test plan
- Unit: Vitest tests for `check-agents-commands.mjs` covering (a) all documented tasks present, (b) a documented-but-missing task, (c) an undocumented extra task, (d) a malformed table row.
- Integration: a shell test that runs `pnpm verify` on the scaffolded tree and asserts exit 0 and the expected task ordering from `turbo run --dry=json`.
- Coverage: `packages/config` and `scripts/` count toward the ≥80% frontend threshold.

## Security notes

title: Create services/api Python workspace with uv, ruff, black, mypy strict and pytest
body:
## Context
The backend is a single deployable Python 3.12+ modular monolith (`20-architecture.md` §2.1 C4, `CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.1) living at `services/api`. Nothing exists yet: no `pyproject.toml`, no lock, no lint/type/test configuration. Constitution §9 requires `lint` (Ruff + Black `--check`), `typecheck` (`mypy --strict` for `services/`) and `unit-backend` (pytest, line ≥85%, branch ≥75%) as blocking checks — this Task creates the project those checks run against.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/pyproject.toml` (Hatch build backend, `requires-python = ">=3.12"`), `uv.lock` committed.
- Dependency baseline matching `20-architecture.md` §2.1: fastapi, starlette, uvicorn[standard] (uvloop), pydantic v2 + pydantic-settings, sqlalchemy 2.0, alembic, httpx, websockets, numpy, duckdb, prometheus-client, structlog.
- Dev group: pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, hypothesis, ruff, black, mypy, import-linter, bandit, pip-audit.
- `ruff.toml`/`[tool.ruff]` rule selection (E,F,I,UP,B,S,ASYNC,RUF) with zero-warning policy; `[tool.black]`; `[tool.mypy]` with `strict = true`, no per-module ignores except a documented, dated allowlist.
- `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`: `asyncio_mode=auto`, markers registered incl. `flaky` (Constitution C-9.3), `--cov=candleviewer --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=85`.
- `services/api/tests/{unit,contract,integration,load}/` directories with a `conftest.py` exposing an `AppContext`-fake fixture placeholder.
- `uv sync --frozen`, `ruff check .`, `black --check .`, `mypy --strict`, `pytest` all runnable per `AGENTS.md` §4 `services/api` section, and reachable from root via `make test`.

## Out of scope
- The module tree M1–M24 and composition root (E02-T05).
- import-linter **contracts** (E02-T06) — only the dependency is added here.
- Alembic migration content (E07); any Bybit dependency (E08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a clean clone and uv installed
When `uv sync --frozen` runs in services/api
Then the environment resolves from the committed lock without contacting an index for resolution and exits 0

Given the project
When `mypy --strict candleviewer` runs
Then it exits 0 with zero errors and no blanket `ignore_errors` module override

Given a test file that deliberately drops coverage below 85%
When `pytest` runs
Then the run fails on `--cov-fail-under`, proving the gate is real and not merely configured

Given a Python file with an unsorted import block
When `ruff check .` runs
Then it exits non-zero (rule I), demonstrating zero-warning enforcement
```

## Technical notes / design
Python packaging/lock tool choice (uv + Hatch) is decided by ADR-0018 (docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0018-monorepo-tooling.md, drafted by spike E02-K01) - do not re-litigate the choice here. Python version is pinned via `.python-version` so `uv` provisions identically on every dev box and in the CI container. Coverage thresholds are floors and may never be lowered in a PR that fails them (C-9.4) — encode `--cov-fail-under=85` in `pyproject.toml`, not in a CI flag, so local and CI agree. Bandit is configured here (`[tool.bandit]`, excluding `tests/`) but wired to CI in E03/E02-X02. Prefer `uv` groups (`dev`, `test`) over extras so the runtime image never ships test deps.

## Test plan
- Unit: a canary test module (`tests/unit/test_toolchain.py`) asserting the interpreter is ≥3.12, that `candleviewer` imports, and that the settings module loads with defaults.
- Integration: none yet (E02-T08 adds the compose-backed one).
- Contract: none yet.
- A meta-test asserting `mypy --strict` exits 0 on the tree, run as part of `lint` locally.

## Security notes
Supply chain: `uv.lock` is committed and installs are `--frozen`; hashes are enforced. `pip-audit` is added as a dev dependency here so E02-X02 can baseline it. No secrets in `pyproject.toml`; `pydantic-settings` reads from env only, with `.env.example` (E02-T08) as the documented template. Bandit rule `S` family in ruff catches `subprocess`/`eval`/hardcoded-password patterns at lint time.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
`uv sync --frozen` ≤90 s cold on reference hardware; `pytest` on the empty tree ≤10 s (guards against an accidental import-heavy conftest).

## Observability
None yet; `structlog` and `prometheus-client` are added as dependencies so E04 has no packaging work to do.

- [ ] Coverage gate demonstrably fails when breached (negative test executed and recorded).

title: Scaffold packages chart-engine, ui, protocol and fixtures with build and test wiring
body:
## Context
`20-architecture.md` §5 fixes the package tree and `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 fixes each package's rule: `chart-engine` has no React/app-state/`fetch`/Bybit knowledge (C-2.16), `protocol` is generated types + codecs only, `ui` may depend on `protocol` and `chart-engine`, and `packages/*` may never import from `apps/*` (C-3.5). Creating these shells now — with their directory structure, build, test and bench entry points already correct — means E05 (design system v0), E06 (engine spike) and E11 (engine core) start writing code instead of arguing about layout. `20-architecture.md` §7 also records `packages/chart-engine` as a tsup build, semver, workspace-only artifact.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine`: `src/{core,gl,layers,text,worker,plugins}`, `bench/`, `test/`; tsup build to ESM; `test` (Vitest, ≥85% gate) and `bench` + `bench:baseline` scripts per `AGENTS.md` §4, with an empty-but-runnable benchmark that emits `bench/results.json` in the shape E06/E03's `engine-bench` gate will consume.
- `packages/ui`: `src/{tokens,primitives,components}`, Storybook 8 configured with the a11y addon and a `storybook` script; Style Dictionary token-build entry point (`pnpm --filter @candleviewer/ui build:tokens`) wired to the contract agreed in E02-D01.
- `packages/protocol`: `src/generated/` (with a `.gitattributes` `linguist-generated` marker and a header-guard lint forbidding hand edits) and `src/runtime/` for binary frame decoders and seq/resync helpers.
- `packages/fixtures`: `raw/`, `golden/`, `scripts/` with README stating the redaction requirement; a placeholder `verify` script.
- Each package: `package.json` name `@candleviewer/<name>`, `exports` map (no deep imports), `tsconfig.json` extending `packages/config`, Vitest config extending the shared preset, coverage thresholds set per Constitution §9 (#4 ≥85% for chart-engine, #5 ≥80% for ui).

## Out of scope
- Any actual tokens, components, stories (E05), engine rendering code (E06/E11), generated protocol content (E02-T09), recorded fixtures (E08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the four packages exist
When `pnpm build` runs at the root
Then each package builds in topological order and emits its declared exports with type declarations

Given packages/chart-engine
When a source file imports React or calls fetch
Then the lint rule enforcing C-2.16 fails the build with a message citing C-2.16

Given packages/protocol/src/generated
When a file there is edited by hand
Then the generated-file header guard lint fails, directing the author to `pnpm generate`

Given packages/chart-engine
When `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench` runs
Then it exits 0 and writes bench/results.json containing frameTimeMs p50/p95/p99, drawCalls and memoryMb keys (values may be zero on the empty scene)

Given packages/ui
When `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/ui storybook` starts and the a11y addon runs on the placeholder story
Then axe reports zero serious/critical violations
```

## Technical notes / design
Every package exposes a single `exports` entry (plus `./bench` for chart-engine) so `dependency-cruiser`'s deep-import ban (E02-T06) has something to enforce. The chart-engine bench must emit its JSON shape now even with a trivial scene, because `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #16 gates on ">5% regression in frame time, draw calls or memory vs the `main` baseline (median of 5 runs, headless Chromium, fixed dataset)" — the harness contract must not be invented later under time pressure during E06. Storybook config lives in `packages/ui/.storybook` and is the a11y gate surface referenced by Constitution §9 #9 until real screens exist.

## Test plan
- Unit: one smoke test per package asserting the public export surface matches a snapshot of the `exports` map (prevents accidental API widening).
- Unit: lint-rule tests for the C-2.16 restriction and the generated-file header guard.
- Integration: root `pnpm build` topological-order assertion.
- a11y: axe on the placeholder Storybook story.
- Coverage: chart-engine ≥85%, ui ≥80% (trivially met; the gate must be wired and demonstrated to fail when breached).

## Security notes
`packages/fixtures` will hold recorded exchange sessions — the README and a CI-checkable `scripts/verify` must assert redaction (no API keys, signatures, account ids, order ids tied to a real account) before any fixture is committed; this is the control for the "recorded fixture leaks credentials" threat in E02-X01. `packages/protocol` decoders will parse untrusted WS frames: the runtime directory is flagged now as a fuzz target for E03's Schemathesis/contract job.

## Accessibility notes
Storybook a11y addon is installed and wired into `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/ui test` so every component E05 adds is checked from its first commit. Focus-visible and reduced-motion primitives are E05's content; this ticket only guarantees the harness exists and runs axe.

## Performance notes
No runtime budget applies yet. The bench harness must be deterministic and complete in ≤60 s so `engine-bench` can stay inside the ≤15 min pipeline (R0 exit criterion 2).

## Observability
N/A (build-time). `bench/results.json` is the artefact E03 uploads per run.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five acceptance scenarios pass.
- [ ] Coverage gates configured and demonstrated to fail when breached.
- [ ] Storybook builds and axe is green.
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §5 updated if directory names shipped differently.
- [ ] Design sign-off on the token-build contract from E02-D01 recorded.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. chart-engine code-owner.

## Dependencies
Blocked by E02-T01 (workspace root) and E02-D01 (token pipeline contract, needed for the `ui` Style Dictionary entry point). Blocks E02-T04, E02-T06, E02-T09, and epics E05, E06.

title: Scaffold apps/web (Vite+React+TS) and apps/desktop (Electron shell) skeletons
body:
## Context
`20-architecture.md` §5 defines `apps/web` (React SPA, Vite, feature-sliced `src/features/`, `src/lib/{ws,state,auth}`, `e2e/`) and `apps/desktop` (Electron shell, `src/main`, `src/preload`, `e2e/`, `electron-builder.yml`) with **no business logic** in the shell (C-3.5). E10 builds the real routing tree, RBAC guards and hardened Electron main; this Task delivers only the bootable skeletons plus the security switches asserted by a test, because R0 exit criterion 9 requires the Electron shell to "start with the hardened security switches enabled (verified by an automated assertion, not by inspection)" and it is far cheaper to make that assertion true from the first commit than to retro-fit it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web`: Vite + React 18 + TS app booting to a single placeholder route; directory skeleton `src/{routes,features,lib/ws,lib/state,lib/auth}` with README stubs stating ownership; Vitest component test setup; `e2e/` with Playwright configured and one smoke spec; dependencies on `@candleviewer/{ui,protocol,chart-engine}` declared.
- `apps/desktop`: Electron main + context-isolated preload loading the web build; `electron-builder.yml`; `e2e/` with Playwright-Electron and a main-window smoke spec.
- Hardened defaults asserted in code and test: `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, `webSecurity: true`, strict CSP header/meta, `window.open` denied via `setWindowOpenHandler`, `will-navigate` restricted to the app origin, and an explicit IPC channel allow-list in preload (empty at this stage).
- `apps/web` size-limit budget entry wired to the `size` task (Constitution §9 #15; budget #9 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: ≤8 MB gzipped initial Electron renderer).

## Out of scope
- Route tree per `12-sitemap.md`, auth/RBAC guards, env badge, global shortcut registry, auto-update, crash reporting — all **E10**.
- Any chart rendering, WS client implementation, or state stores beyond empty directories.
- GPU flag tuning — depends on E06's findings and lands in E10.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a built web bundle
When `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/desktop dev` launches Electron
Then the main window loads the app and the Playwright-Electron smoke spec passes

Given the Electron main process
When the hardening assertion test runs
Then it reads the actual BrowserWindow webPreferences at runtime and fails if any of contextIsolation, sandbox or webSecurity is false or nodeIntegration is true

Given the renderer
When it attempts window.open to an external URL
Then the request is denied by setWindowOpenHandler and an audit-able log line is emitted

Given apps/web
When the initial bundle exceeds 8MB gzipped or regresses more than 5% versus main
Then the `size` task fails, per Constitution §9 #15

Given apps/web
When axe-core runs against the placeholder route via @axe-core/playwright
Then zero serious or critical violations are reported
```

## Technical notes / design
The preload exposes exactly one namespaced object (`window.cv`) built from an explicit allow-list array; adding a channel later requires editing that array, which is code-owned by the security engineer (trust boundary B4, `20-architecture.md` §2.2). CSP is `default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws: wss:; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` — `'unsafe-inline'` for styles only, with a follow-up ticket to move to nonces once the design system's styling approach is fixed in E05. The shell must keep all shell-specific code behind a `ShellPort` abstraction because ADR-0011 (Electron vs Tauri) is `proposed`, not decided (`20-architecture.md` note; E06 closes it).

## Test plan
- Unit (Vitest): preload allow-list builder rejects a channel not in the list; CSP string builder snapshot.
- Integration: Electron hardening assertion test reading live `webPreferences`.
- E2E: Playwright web smoke (app boots, placeholder route renders) and Playwright-Electron main-window smoke — these become the seeds of the `e2e-smoke` gate (Constitution §9 #8).
- a11y: `@axe-core/playwright` on the placeholder route.
- Perf: `size` budget check.
- Coverage: ≥80% for `apps/web` per §9 #5.

## Security notes
Threats (STRIDE, E02-X01 + `04-security-program.md`): renderer compromise escalating to Node (mitigated by contextIsolation+sandbox+nodeIntegration off), malicious navigation/phishing window (mitigated by `will-navigate` allow-list and denied `window.open`), unsafe IPC surface (empty allow-list by default, security code-owner on the file). This Task is `security`-labelled and requires a Security engineer review comment before Done (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8). No secrets, no keys, no account data touched — data classification: none at this stage.

## Accessibility notes
The placeholder route must have a landmark structure (`<main>`), a document title, `lang` attribute, and a visible focus style inherited from `packages/ui`; axe must be green. This establishes the baseline the a11y gate (§9 #9) runs against before E05/E10 add real screens. Keyboard: the placeholder must be reachable and the app must not trap focus.

## Performance notes
Budget #9 (≤8 MB gz initial renderer, soft, alert at +10%) and budget #10 (≤3 s cold start to interactive) from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. Cold start is measured but **not gated** here (no real workspace to restore); the instrumentation hook (`app.whenReady()` → `workspace-ready` event) is added so E10 can gate it.

## Observability
Electron main writes structured startup lines (version, chromium version, GPU feature status, hardening flags) to a local log file — the precursor to E10's crash reporting and E04's build-info endpoint.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five acceptance scenarios pass in CI-equivalent local runs.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% for `apps/web`.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present; hardening assertions reviewed.
- [ ] a11y: axe green; manual keyboard pass on the placeholder route recorded.
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §5/§2.2 updated if the shipped shell structure diverged.
- [ ] Demo at Sprint Review: Electron boots, hardening test shown failing when a flag is flipped.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. security code-owner on preload/main.

## Dependencies
Blocked by E02-T03 (packages must exist to be depended on). Blocks E10 and E06's in-Electron measurements.

## Branch
`feat/monorepo-scaffold-apps` · two PRs: (1) `apps/web`, (2) `apps/desktop` + hardening tests.

## References
- docs/plan/20-architecture.md §5, §2.1 C3, §2.2 B4
- /CONSTITUTION.md §3 frontend table, C-3.5, §9 #5, #8, #9, #15
- docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md budgets #9, #10
- docs/plan/04-security-program.md
- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md

## Estimate reconciliation (2026-09-14)

title: Create services/api module tree M1-M24, composition root and typed settings
body:
## Context
`CONSTITUTION.md` §3 enumerates 24 backend modules (M1 `config` … M24 `observability`) with a fixed path, responsibility and allowed-dependency list, and §2 makes their boundaries an *invariant that must hold after every merged commit*. `20-architecture.md` §6.1 requires a composition root (`app.py`) that builds an `AppContext` — "No module constructs its own dependencies; everything is injected, which makes every module unit-testable with fakes." This Task is the backend module for E02: **M1 `config`** (typed settings, environment enum `live`/`demo`/`testnet`) is actually implemented; the other 23 are created as conforming empty modules so that E04/E07/E08/E09 drop code into a correct shape and so E02-T06's import-linter contracts have real packages to bind to.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/candleviewer/` package with one subpackage per module M1–M24 at the exact paths of `CONSTITUTION.md` §3, each following the convention of `20-architecture.md` §3: `__init__.py` exporting only the public interface, `service.py` (lifecycle), `models.py` (pydantic v2 domain types), `errors.py`.
- **M1 `config` implemented**: `settings.py` using `pydantic-settings` with env layering, `Environment` enum (`live`|`demo`|`testnet`), datastore DSNs (Postgres, QuestDB, DuckDB/Parquet root, MinIO), feature-flag defaults, and a `CV_FEED` switch (`live`|`synthetic`) per `20-architecture.md` §5 note on the synthetic feed.
- `app.py` composition root building `AppContext` (settings, bus, storage clients, key vault, metric registry, clock guard, module instances) — all fields present and typed, with fakes/None-objects where the owning epic has not landed; module supervisor with the documented start/stop ordering hook (`20-architecture.md` §6.2).
- FastAPI application factory exposing `/healthz`, `/readyz` and a build-info payload (git sha, version, environment) — static responses; E04 replaces them with real probes.
- `services/api/candleviewer/migrations/` alembic skeleton directory (empty revision tree, single-head check runnable) — content is E07's.

## Out of scope
- Any module's real logic (exchange, ingestion, book, bars, orderflow, oms, rules, paper, recorder, replay, accounts, risk, auth, audit, journal, admin, api routers, ws gateway, storage implementations, observability wiring) — owned by later epics.
- import-linter contract files (E02-T06). Docker packaging (E02-T08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the module tree
When a reviewer compares it to CONSTITUTION.md §3
Then all 24 module paths exist with the exact names M1..M24 map to, and a test asserts this programmatically against a checked-in manifest

Given CV_ENV=demo and a .env file
When the settings object loads
Then the Environment enum resolves to demo and an invalid value raises a pydantic ValidationError naming the allowed values

Given the composition root
When `create_app()` is called in a unit test with fake storage clients
Then it constructs without touching Postgres, QuestDB or the network, and GET /healthz returns 200 with a build-info body containing gitSha, version and environment

Given a module's __init__.py
When it re-exports an internal implementation symbol not listed in its public interface manifest
Then the public-surface test fails, citing the §3 convention
```

## Technical notes / design
`AppContext` is a frozen dataclass; modules receive it (or narrower protocols) by constructor injection — never a global. The supervisor start order follows the dependency numbering of §3 (config → secrets → storage → bus → exchange → ingestion → …) and shutdown is the reverse, with a bounded drain timeout. Settings must never log their own values: `__repr__` redacts any field whose name matches `(key|secret|token|password|dsn)` — an early instance of E04's redaction filter requirement. `Environment` is used later by C-1 guardrails (trading mode refuses to start if a stored key has withdrawal enabled, `20-architecture.md` §2.2 B3) so the enum lives in M1, not in a trading module.

## Test plan
- Unit: module-manifest test (24 paths, public-surface check); settings validation (valid/invalid env, missing required DSN, env-file layering precedence); redacting `__repr__`; `create_app()` with fakes; `/healthz` and `/readyz` response schema.
- Contract: `/healthz` response shape asserted against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` if the path is defined there; otherwise the path is added to the spec in the same PR (C-6 contract-first).
- Integration: none (E02-T08 runs the app inside compose).
- Coverage: ≥85% line / ≥75% branch for the files this Task actually implements; empty modules are excluded from coverage via an explicit, dated `omit` list that E-later tickets must shrink.

## Security notes
The redacting `__repr__` and the ban on logging settings are the primary controls here (Information Disclosure). M2 `secrets` is created as an empty module but its import restriction (C-3.2: importable only by M4 and M21) must already be encoded in the manifest so T06 can enforce it. No real credentials are introduced; `.env.example` only. `/healthz` and `/readyz` must not leak versions of datastores or internal hostnames to an unauthenticated caller — build-info is limited to git sha, semver and environment name.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend module tree, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
`create_app()` cold construction ≤200 ms with fakes (keeps unit tests and the `integration` gate fast). No runtime budget from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` applies yet; budget #8 (≤300 MB per recorded symbol) is a later concern.

## Observability
`/healthz` (liveness, static 200), `/readyz` (readiness, static 200 with a `checks: []` array E04 fills), build-info endpoint. A `prometheus_client` registry is instantiated in `AppContext` and exposed at `/metrics` with process metrics only, so E04 and E02-T08's prometheus scrape target work immediately.

title: Encode module boundaries as import-linter and dependency-cruiser contracts
body:
## Context
`CONSTITUTION.md` C-3.1 ("dependencies flow one way … cycles are forbidden"), C-3.2 (M2 `secrets` importable only by M4 and M21, "Enforced by CI"), C-3.3 (M19 `audit` write-only except M21/M23 read paths), C-3.5 (`apps/web` never imports another app; `packages/*` never import `apps/*`) and C-2.16 (chart-engine framework-free) are stated as CI-enforced invariants, and §9 #18 names the blocking check: "`architecture` — `import-linter` module-boundary contracts (§3) + `dependency-cruiser` for TS + deep-import ban". None of this exists yet. This Task writes the contracts; E03 wires the job into GitHub Actions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/.importlinter` with, at minimum: a **layers** contract encoding the M1→M24 numbering of §3; a **forbidden** contract for C-3.2 (only `exchange.bybit` and `admin` may import `secrets`); a **forbidden** contract for C-3.3 (only `admin` and `api` may import `audit` read APIs); an **independence** contract between sibling engine modules that §3 does not connect; a global no-cycles assertion.
- Per-module `allowed` lists transcribed verbatim from the §3 table into a single machine-readable manifest (`docs/plan/module-contracts.toml` or `services/api/module_contracts.toml`) that both import-linter and the §3 doc-drift test read, so the table and the contracts cannot diverge.
- `.dependency-cruiser.js` at the root: `packages/* -/-> apps/*`, `apps/web -/-> apps/desktop` (and reverse), deep-import ban (only package `exports` entry points), `packages/chart-engine -/-> react|react-dom` and no `fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest`/`bybit` identifiers (C-2.16, C-2.2), `packages/protocol` may not import `packages/ui` or `apps/*`.
- ESLint `no-restricted-imports` mirror for fast editor feedback (C-3.5 note: "enforced by `no-restricted-imports` and by `import-linter` on the Python side").
- A **drift test** asserting the manifest matches the §3 table in `CONSTITUTION.md` (parses the markdown table) — so amending §3 without amending the contracts fails CI, and vice versa.
- `make arch` / `pnpm arch` task running both linters; added to `verify` and documented in `AGENTS.md` §4.

## Out of scope
- The GitHub Actions `architecture` job definition (E03).
- Adding new modules or edges (requires an ADR per C-3.4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the contracts are in place
When `make arch` runs on the clean scaffold
Then both import-linter and dependency-cruiser exit 0 with every contract reported as kept

Given a deliberate violation adding `from candleviewer.secrets import KeyVault` to candleviewer/oms/service.py
When `make arch` runs
Then it exits non-zero naming the C-3.2 contract and the offending import chain

Given a deliberate violation adding `import React from "react"` to packages/chart-engine/src/core/index.ts
When `make arch` runs
Then dependency-cruiser fails citing C-2.16

Given a deliberate deep import `@candleviewer/ui/src/primitives/Button` from apps/web
When `make arch` runs
Then the deep-import ban fails the build

Given the M14 row of CONSTITUTION.md §3 is edited to add a dependency
When the drift test runs without a matching manifest change
Then the test fails, stating that §3 and module_contracts.toml disagree
```

## Technical notes / design
The manifest is the single source of truth *for machines*; `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 remains the source for *humans*, and the drift test binds them (this mirrors C-16.5: never duplicate an owned list without a mechanical check). Import-linter layers alone cannot express C-3.2/C-3.3 — use additional `forbidden` contracts with `ignore_imports` empty (no exceptions). Cycle detection: `import-linter`'s independence contracts plus a `grimp`-based no-cycles test. For TS, dependency-cruiser's `forbidden` rules carry a `comment` field citing the exact Constitution rule id so failures are self-explanatory. Every violation message must name the rule id — reviewers cite rule ids in PRs (Constitution preamble).

## Test plan
- Unit: the drift test (markdown table parser) with fixtures for matching, added-edge and removed-edge cases.
- Integration: a **negative-test suite** that, for each of the five acceptance violations, applies a patch in a temp copy of the tree, runs `make arch`, asserts non-zero exit and the expected rule id in stderr, then restores. This is the only way to prove the gate is real rather than merely configured.
- Coverage: the drift-test helper counts toward the backend threshold.

## Security notes
This Task *is* a security control: C-3.2 keeps the envelope-encryption/key-vault module (M2 `secrets`) unreachable from business logic, which is the structural mitigation for key-leakage threats in `04-security-program.md`; C-3.3 keeps the audit log append-only from every module's perspective, protecting non-repudiation. A weakened or `ignore_imports`-ridden contract is itself a security finding — the contract files must be added to `.github/CODEOWNERS` under the security engineer (coordinated with E01). Requires Security engineer review before Done.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — build-time static analysis, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
`make arch` must complete in ≤60 s on the full tree so it can live inside `verify` and the ≤15 min pipeline (R0 exit criterion 2). Cache dependency-cruiser results per Turbo inputs.

## Observability
Both linters emit machine-readable reports (`arch-report.json`) uploaded as a CI artefact by E03, giving a trend of contract count over time.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five acceptance scenarios pass, including the negative-test suite.
- [ ] Every row of `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 is represented in the manifest; drift test green.
- [ ] Contract files assigned to security + architect code-owners.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` §4 documents `pnpm arch` / `make arch`.
- [ ] Demo: violation patches shown failing at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with architect approval.

title: Add commitlint, husky, lint-staged and .editorconfig with conventional-commit enforcement
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` §SDLC requires conventional commits, and `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #20 (`pr-metadata`) gates on "Conventional-commit title, `Closes #N` present, branch-name pattern, diff-size policy (C-4.8)". Release automation in `07-release-and-prr.md` derives the changelog and semver bump from commit types, so a single non-conforming commit on `main` corrupts a release note. Catching this locally (husky) is far cheaper than catching it in the merge queue.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `commitlint.config.cjs` extending `@commitlint/config-conventional`, with the scope allow-list derived from the component values used by the board (`chart-engine`, `data-feeds`, `indicators`, `drawing-tools`, `alerts`, `backtesting`, `scripting`, `web`, `api`, `auth`, `collaboration`, `infra`, `docs`) plus package names.
- husky hooks: `commit-msg` (commitlint), `pre-commit` (lint-staged: eslint --fix + prettier on staged JS/TS, ruff --fix + black on staged Python), `pre-push` (typecheck on changed projects only, with an escape hatch documented for emergencies).
- `lint-staged` config in the root `package.json`.
- `/.editorconfig`: UTF-8, LF, final newline, trim trailing whitespace, 2-space for JS/TS/JSON/YAML/MD, 4-space for Python, `max_line_length` matching Ruff/Black (88) and Prettier (100 for TS).
- `scripts/check-branch-name.mjs` validating `feat/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`, `design/…`, `spike/…` per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`, wired into `pre-push` and reusable by E03's `pr-metadata` job.

## Out of scope
- The GitHub Actions `pr-metadata` job and PR template (E01/E03).
- release-please / changelog automation (E03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a commit message "fixed stuff"
When the commit-msg hook runs
Then the commit is rejected with a message showing the conventional-commit format and the allowed scopes

Given a commit message "feat(chart-engine): add SDF glyph atlas"
When the commit-msg hook runs
Then the commit is accepted

Given staged TypeScript with formatting errors and staged Python with import-order errors
When the pre-commit hook runs
Then both are auto-fixed and re-staged, and the commit proceeds

Given a branch named "my-work"
When the pre-push hook runs
Then the push is rejected citing the branch-name pattern from 01-sdlc-and-branching.md

Given an engineer needs to bypass a hook in an emergency
When they use the documented --no-verify escape hatch
Then the push proceeds and CI still enforces the same rules server-side, so the bypass cannot reach main
```

## Technical notes / design
Hooks must be fast (pre-commit ≤5 s on a typical diff) or engineers will disable them; therefore lint-staged only touches staged files and pre-push typechecks only affected Turbo projects. Husky install runs via a `prepare` script — note this is an npm lifecycle script and must be reconciled with the `ignore-scripts` policy from E02-T01 (allow it explicitly for the root package only, documented in `.npmrc` comments and reviewed in E02-X01). Every client-side rule must be mirrored server-side by E03 — hooks are a convenience, never the enforcement boundary.

## Test plan
- Unit: commitlint config test asserting accept/reject for a table of ~12 messages (valid types, invalid type, missing scope where required, unknown scope, >100 char subject, breaking-change footer).
- Unit: `check-branch-name.mjs` tests for each allowed prefix plus three invalid names.
- Integration: a temp git repo fixture exercising the three hooks end to end.
- Coverage: counted under the frontend ≥80% threshold.

## Security notes
Husky's `prepare` lifecycle script is the one deliberate exception to the `ignore-scripts` posture (Tampering vector: a malicious dependency hiding in a hook path). Mitigations: hooks live in the repo under `.husky/`, are code-owned, and their content is reviewed like any source; no hook may execute a script downloaded at run time. `--no-verify` is documented but cannot weaken `main` because branch protection re-runs everything.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — developer tooling, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
pre-commit ≤5 s p95 on a 20-file diff; pre-push ≤60 s on an affected-projects-only typecheck, on reference hardware.

## Observability
N/A. Hook failures print the rule and a link to `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Five acceptance scenarios pass via the temp-repo integration fixture.
- [ ] Hook latency measured and within budget.
- [ ] `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` cross-checked; `AGENTS.md` §4 updated if a task name is added.
- [ ] `.npmrc` exception for `prepare` documented and reviewed.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
Blocked by E02-T01. Feeds E03's `pr-metadata` job, which reuses `check-branch-name.mjs`.

## Branch
`chore/monorepo-scaffold-hooks` · small PR (<200 LOC).

## References
- /CONSTITUTION.md §9 #20, C-4.8
- docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md
