title: Author docker compose stack for WSL Ubuntu (api, postgres, questdb, prometheus, grafana, minio)
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 puts "Docker Compose for WSL Ubuntu (api, postgres, questdb, grafana, prometheus, minio-for-parquet)" inside E02, and `20-architecture.md` §5 places it at `infra/compose/` with `.dev`/`.vps` overrides and `.env.example`, started by `make up`. Three separate consumers depend on it: engineers (`make up` with `CV_FEED=synthetic` so they can work without Bybit credentials), the `integration` CI gate ("Backend + Postgres + QuestDB in docker compose, driven by recorded Bybit fixtures; **no network egress**", Constitution §9 #7), and E04's observability work (Prometheus must already be scraping the api target). Trust boundary B2 (`20-architecture.md` §2.2) requires services to bind `127.0.0.1`/WSL-internal only — never `0.0.0.0`, because of the WSL portproxy leak risk.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` + `docker-compose.dev.yml` + `docker-compose.vps.yml` overrides + `.env.example` (no real secrets).
- Services with pinned image **digests**: postgres 16, questdb 8.x, prometheus 2.x, grafana 11, minio (Parquet cold-tier stand-in), and `api` built from `infra/images/Dockerfile.api` (multi-stage, non-root user, no dev deps in the runtime layer).
- Named volumes for postgres data, questdb data, minio data, grafana data; documented reset path.
- Healthchecks for every service; `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` so `make up` is deterministic.
- Port bindings **explicitly** `127.0.0.1:<port>:<port>` for every published port (B2); an internal network `cv-internal`.
- `infra/prometheus/prometheus.yml` scraping `api:8000/metrics` (target exists thanks to E02-T05); `infra/grafana/` provisioning stubs (datasource only — dashboards are E04).
- `infra/scripts/bootstrap.sh` (create DBs/buckets, apply nothing else) and `infra/scripts/healthcheck.sh` used by `make up` to wait for all-healthy.
- `make up`, `make down`, `make reset` documented in `AGENTS.md` §4.

## Out of scope
- Grafana dashboards, alert rules, Alertmanager routing, structlog redaction — **E04**.
- QuestDB tuning, DDL, retention jobs, Parquet layout — **E07**.
- CI job that starts the stack — **E03** (this Task only guarantees it is startable and scriptable).
- Any VPS provisioning or deployment.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a WSL Ubuntu host with Docker and no Bybit credentials
When `make up` runs
Then all six services reach healthy within 120 seconds and `make up` exits 0

Given the stack is healthy
When `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz` and `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/readyz` are called
Then both return 200 and readyz lists its (currently empty) checks array

Given the compose files
When a reviewer greps for port bindings
Then every published port is bound to 127.0.0.1 and none to 0.0.0.0, asserted by a test script in infra/scripts

Given CV_FEED=synthetic
When the api service starts
Then it starts successfully without any exchange credentials present in the environment

Given `make reset`
When it is run after data has been written
Then all named volumes are removed and a subsequent `make up` reaches healthy from a clean state

Given an image tag is used instead of a pinned digest
When the compose lint script runs
Then it fails, citing the supply-chain control from the E02 STRIDE model
```

## Technical notes / design
The `api` image is multi-stage: builder installs with `uv sync --frozen`, runtime copies the venv and application only, runs as UID 10001, read-only root filesystem with explicit writable tmpfs. Compose profiles separate `core` (postgres, questdb, api) from `obs` (prometheus, grafana) and `cold` (minio) so the `integration` gate can start only what it needs and stay fast. Prometheus scrape interval 15 s. MinIO is the local stand-in for the Parquet/object cold tier described in `20-architecture.md` §2.1 C18; the `.vps.yml` override can swap it for a filesystem path. `.env.example` documents every variable M1 `config` reads, with safe defaults and explicit `CHANGE_ME` markers for anything secret-like.

## Test plan
- Integration: `infra/scripts/healthcheck.sh` asserted in a test that runs `make up`, polls health, hits `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics`, then `make down` — this becomes the seed of Constitution §9 #7's harness.
- Unit/lint: compose lint script tests — (a) any `0.0.0.0` binding fails, (b) any untagged/digest-less image fails, (c) any service missing a healthcheck fails.
- Chaos (light): kill the postgres container and assert the api `/readyz` turns non-ready once E04 adds real probes — recorded as a follow-up assertion, not gated here.
- Coverage: script tests counted under the backend threshold.

## Security notes
Threats (E02-X01 STRIDE): (1) **Exposure** — a `0.0.0.0` binding on WSL is reachable from the LAN via portproxy; mitigated by the loopback-only rule plus the automated grep test (B2). (2) **Supply chain** — mutable image tags allow silent substitution; mitigated by pinned digests plus Trivy in E03 (§9 #13). (3) **Credential leakage** — only `.env.example` is committed, `.env` is gitignored and gitleaks-scanned; default Postgres/Grafana/MinIO credentials must be `CHANGE_ME` and the bootstrap script must refuse to run with them in a non-dev profile. (4) **Container escape surface** — non-root user, read-only rootfs, no `privileged`, no docker socket mount anywhere. Data classification: local development data only; no live account data or API keys are ever placed in this stack (keys are E27's concern and are envelope-encrypted with a KEK held in the host OS keychain, outside WSL — B3).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — infrastructure, no UI surface. (Grafana's own UI is third-party and out of the WCAG scope of `05-accessibility-standard.md`, which covers CandleViewer's own screens.)

## Performance notes
`make up` to all-healthy ≤120 s cold, ≤30 s warm on reference hardware (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1). Resource limits are declared per service so a laptop dev box is not starved; the sizing basis for the eventual VPS is §10.2 of the same doc and is **not** applied here.

## Observability
Prometheus scrapes `api:8000/metrics`; Grafana is provisioned with the Prometheus datasource only. Compose logs use the `json-file` driver with rotation (`max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`) so a long soak cannot fill a dev disk — relevant to the 24 h ingestion soak in R0 exit criterion 5.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six acceptance scenarios pass on a clean WSL Ubuntu box and in a second engineer's environment (verified in E02-Q02).
- [ ] Compose lint script green; digests pinned.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present (loopback binding, non-root, no docker socket, credential defaults).
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §5 `infra/` section and `AGENTS.md` §4 updated to match.
- [ ] Demo: `make up` → healthy stack → `/healthz` 200, at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with DevSecOps code-owner approval (`infra/` is DevSecOps-owned per `20-architecture.md` §5 Ownership).

## Dependencies
Blocked by E02-T05 (an app with `/healthz` to run) and E02-T02 (a resolvable Python environment to build the image from). Blocks E03's `integration` job, E04 entirely, and E07's storage work.

## Branch
`feat/monorepo-scaffold-compose` · two PRs: (1) Dockerfile + api service + core profile, (2) obs/cold profiles + scripts + lint.

title: Build packages/protocol code generation from OpenAPI + WS schema with staleness gate
body:
## Context
`CONSTITUTION.md` C-6.6 states "`packages/protocol` types are **generated** from the contract" and §9 #19 (`generated-code-check`) blocks merge when regeneration produces a diff. `20-architecture.md` §5 phrases the rule as "`packages/protocol` is generated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS schema — CI fails if the generated output is stale (`make gen && git diff --exit-code`)". The contract documents already exist and are baselines: `22-api-openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1, base path `/api/v1`, RFC 9457 problem bodies, decimal-string money fields per convention C6, RFC 3339 timestamps per C7) and `23-ws-protocol.md` (envelope with `ch` topic, `s` per-(connection,topic) sequence, message kinds `sub_ok`/`snap`/`delta`/`resync`/`err`, JSON and binary encodings per §3.2/§3.4). Nothing generates from them yet, so every later epic would otherwise hand-write drifting types.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `pnpm generate` pipeline producing `packages/protocol/src/generated/`: TS types for every OpenAPI schema and operation (request/response/problem), and TS types for the WS envelope, every message kind and every topic payload declared in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 topic catalogue.
- A machine-readable WS schema artefact: extract the topic/message table of `23-ws-protocol.md` into `docs/plan/ws-schema.json` (JSON Schema per message kind and topic) as the generator's input, with a doc-drift test binding it to the markdown (same pattern as E02-T06's §3 manifest).
- Python side: generate pydantic v2 models into `services/api/candleviewer/api/_generated/` (REST schemas) and `services/api/candleviewer/ws/_generated/` (frame schemas) from the same two inputs, so backend and frontend cannot disagree.
- Money/decimal handling per convention C6: money/size/price generate as `string` in TS and `Decimal`-backed types in Python — never `number`/`float`.
- `packages/protocol/src/runtime/`: hand-written binary frame decoder skeleton and `seq`/resync helpers matching `23-ws-protocol.md` §3.4 and §7, with the generated types as their contract.
- Staleness gate: `make gen && git diff --exit-code`, plus a `pnpm generate:check` task documented in `AGENTS.md` §4.
- Generated files carry a do-not-edit header enforced by the guard from E02-T03 and `linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes`.

## Out of scope
- Implementing any endpoint or WS topic (E09, E17 and later epics).
- Changing the contract documents themselves — any needed fix is raised as a contract PR reviewed first (C-6, contract-first).
- MessagePack/binary encoder implementation beyond the decoder skeleton (E17).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the committed contracts
When `pnpm generate` runs on a clean tree
Then it exits 0 and `git diff --exit-code` reports no changes

Given a new optional field is added to a schema in docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml
When CI runs generate:check without regeneration
Then the check fails with a diff naming the stale generated file

Given an OpenAPI schema field marked as money (x-decimal or the documented decimal-string convention C6)
When types are generated
Then the TS type is string and the Python type is a Decimal-backed type, asserted by a generator unit test

Given docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md gains a topic row that is absent from ws-schema.json
When the drift test runs
Then it fails, stating that the markdown topic catalogue and the JSON schema disagree

Given a generated file is edited by hand
When lint runs
Then the do-not-edit header guard fails and points the author at `pnpm generate`
```

## Technical notes / design
Generator choice is `openapi-typescript` (types only, no runtime client) for TS and `datamodel-code-generator` for pydantic v2 — both deterministic, both pinned by version so output is byte-stable; a non-deterministic generator would make `generated-code-check` flap and is grounds for rejecting the tool. Generation must be sorted/stable (no timestamps, no absolute paths in output). The WS schema extraction is a one-time authoring job plus a parser test: the markdown table remains human-authoritative, `ws-schema.json` machine-authoritative, and the drift test forbids divergence (C-16.5 pattern). Envelope fields are `t` (type), `ch` (topic), `s` (sequence), `e` (encoding) per §3.1/§3.2 — the envelope type must model `s` as monotonically increasing **per (connection, topic)**, which the resync helper relies on (§3.3, §7).

## Test plan
- Unit (TS): generator output snapshot tests for a representative subset (one paginated list response with `PageMeta` per convention C3, one RFC 9457 `Problem`, one order-mutating request carrying `Idempotency-Key` per C4, one money-bearing schema per C6).
- Unit (Python): pydantic model round-trip tests for the same subset, asserting Decimal preservation (no float coercion) and RFC 3339 parsing with the `_ms` epoch-millis suffix convention (C7).
- Unit: WS envelope decode/encode round trip for each message kind; sequence-gap helper returns a resync decision when `s` jumps.
- Contract: the generated artefacts feed the `contract` gate (§9 #6) — this Task makes that gate possible; a placeholder consumer test asserts the generated type set is non-empty and matches the operation count in the spec.
- Determinism: generate twice in a clean temp dir and assert byte-identical output.
- Coverage: runtime helpers ≥85%; generated files excluded from coverage.

## Security notes
`packages/protocol/src/runtime` decoders parse **untrusted** frames from the network and are therefore a primary attack surface (Tampering/DoS): the decoder must enforce the frame-size limits of `23-ws-protocol.md` §3.6 and reject oversized or malformed frames without allocating proportional memory. Generated code must never embed example credentials from the spec. Flag `src/runtime` as a fuzz target for E03's Schemathesis/fuzz job and for DAST later. No secrets or PII pass through generation.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — type generation, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
`pnpm generate` ≤60 s on the full contract so it stays inside `verify` and the ≤15 min pipeline. Decoder helpers will later be on the hot path for budget #3 (WS tick → screen p95 <100 ms) and budget #6 (≤20 ms backend fan-out add-on) — the skeleton must avoid per-frame allocations and JSON re-parsing, and a microbenchmark placeholder is committed for E17 to extend.

## Observability
Generation emits a manifest (`packages/protocol/generated.manifest.json`) listing input file hashes and generator versions, so a stale-output failure in CI can be diagnosed without local reproduction.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five acceptance scenarios pass; determinism test green (two runs byte-identical).
- [ ] `ws-schema.json` covers every topic in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6; drift test green.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on `src/runtime`; generated output excluded.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` §4 documents `pnpm generate` and `generate:check`; `20-architecture.md` §5 Tooling confirmed.
- [ ] Architect + backend-lead review (contract-owning surface).
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
Blocked by E02-T03 (`packages/protocol` must exist) and E02-T05 (`services/api` target directories must exist). Blocks E03's `contract` and `generated-code-check` jobs, and E17 (WS protocol implementation).

## Branch
`feat/monorepo-scaffold-protocol-gen` · two PRs: (1) ws-schema.json extraction + drift test, (2) generators + staleness gate.

- docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml (conventions C1-C10)

title: Merge ADR-0016 monorepo tooling and reconcile AGENTS.md §4 with the shipped task graph
body:
## Context
`AGENTS.md` §4 carries an explicit status warning that its command table is a *specification, not an observation*, and names a single owning ticket whose acceptance criteria are "every task name in this section exists and exits 0 on a clean checkout, and any deviation is corrected in this section in the same PR", after which "the runnable scripts become the source of truth and this section becomes a mirror of them". E02 is that owning work. In parallel, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 requires every spike to close with an ADR — E02-K01 drafted **ADR-0016 monorepo tooling and task graph**, and the existing `27-adrs/` set runs ADR-0001..ADR-0015, so 0016 is the next free number. This Task closes both loops once the scaffold's shape is final (after T06's contracts and T09's codegen, the last two things that add task names).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0018-monorepo-tooling.md` in the house ADR format: context, options considered (pnpm+Turborepo vs pnpm+Nx; uv+Hatch vs Poetry), measured evidence from E02-K01, decision, consequences, reversal cost, status `decided`.
- Rewrite `AGENTS.md` §4: remove the provisional status block, replace it with a statement that the scripts are now authoritative and this section mirrors them, and correct every row against the real task graph.
- Update `AGENTS.md` §4's owning-ticket reference from the placeholder `INFRA-001 / EP-INFRA` to this epic's real keys (`E02`, this ticket `E02-T11`).
- Verify `scripts/check-agents-commands.mjs` (E02-T01) passes against the final table and is wired into `generated-code-check`'s local equivalent.
- Update `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §5 Tooling paragraph if the shipped tooling differs from the text, and `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md` index.
- Cross-check that no other document re-enumerates command names (C-16.5, `AGENTS.md` §4 owns that list) — remove duplicates if found.

## Out of scope
- Changing tooling decisions (that was E02-K01); this Task records them.
- CI workflow authoring (E03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the shipped scaffold
When `node scripts/check-agents-commands.mjs` runs
Then it exits 0, meaning every documented task exists and no undocumented user-facing task exists

Given ADR-0016
When the Architect reviews it
Then it contains the measured numbers from E02-K01 (not opinions), an explicit decision, and a stated reversal cost, and its status is `decided`

Given AGENTS.md §4 after this change
When a reader looks for the provisional status warning
Then it is gone and replaced by a mirror-of-scripts statement naming E02-T11 as the closing ticket

Given any other tracked file that lists command names
When the C-16.5 duplicate-list check runs
Then it reports no duplicated single-source list
```

## Technical notes / design
ADR numbering must not collide: confirm `27-adrs/` still ends at ADR-0015 at merge time and bump if another epic has taken 0016 in the interim (E03 and E07 also produce ADRs in R0 — coordinate via the `27-adrs/README.md` index, which is the reservation ledger). Note for reviewers: ADR-0011 (Electron vs Tauri) is `proposed`, not decided, and must **not** be cited as settled (see the note at the end of `20-architecture.md`); ADR-0016 must not assume a shell outcome.

## Test plan
- The `check-agents-commands.mjs` run is the test.
- markdownlint on the changed docs (part of the `lint` gate, §9 #1).

title: Write repository onboarding docs and the make dev synthetic-feed developer loop
body:
## Context
`20-architecture.md` §5 promises that `make up` "starts the full compose stack against `demo` with a **synthetic feed generator** available (`CV_FEED=synthetic`) that replays `packages/fixtures/raw` at configurable rates — so engineers and CI can work without Bybit credentials", and that E2E tests "always run against `synthetic` or `demo`, never `live`". That promise is load-bearing for onboarding (~15 engineers join across R0–R1 per `00-planning-brief.md`) and for the `integration` gate's no-network-egress requirement (`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #7). E02 must therefore ship the *loop* — start everything, get data flowing, run the gates — plus the documentation that makes it reproducible, which is the concrete mitigation for risk **R10 key-person**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `make dev`: one command that starts the compose stack (E02-T08), runs the api with `CV_FEED=synthetic`, and starts the `apps/web` Vite dev server against it, with a documented teardown.
- A minimal **synthetic feed generator** in `services/api/candleviewer/ingestion/` (behind the `CV_FEED` switch from M1 `config`) that emits normalised domain events at a configurable rate from a committed sample file in `packages/fixtures/raw/` — shape only: `Trade` and `Ticker` events per `CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.3 naming, no Bybit knowledge (C-2.2), no book reconstruction (that is E08/M7).
- `/README.md` rewritten as a working onboarding path: prerequisites with pinned minimum versions (confirmed by E02-Q02), clone → install → verify → up → dev, plus a troubleshooting section seeded from E02-Q02's findings (WSL filesystem vs `/mnt/c`, port conflicts, Docker integration).
- A "first hour" checklist a new joiner can tick, stored beside the QA artefacts in `docs/plan/qa/`.
- Links, not duplicates: the README points at `AGENTS.md` §4 for commands (C-16.5 — that file owns the command list) and at `CONTRIBUTING.md` for process.

## Out of scope
- The real Bybit adapter, WS ingestion, book reconstruction, bar building — **E08**.
- Recorded real fixtures and the capture/redact pipeline (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.4) — **E08**; this ticket commits only a small hand-authored sample file.
- CI usage of the synthetic feed (E03 wires it into the `integration` job).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a machine with the documented prerequisites and no Bybit credentials
When `make dev` runs
Then the compose stack becomes healthy, the api starts in synthetic-feed mode, the web dev server serves the placeholder route, and no outbound request to any exchange host is made

Given the api in synthetic-feed mode
When a developer inspects the bus metrics exposed at /metrics
Then normalised Trade and Ticker events are being published at the configured rate, and the rate is changeable by an environment variable read through M1 config

Given CV_FEED=live is set without credentials
When the api starts
Then it fails fast with a clear, actionable error rather than starting in a half-configured state

Given a new joiner follows only the README
When they complete the documented path
Then they reach a green `pnpm verify` and a running `make dev` without contacting the scaffold's author, verified by the E02-Q02 charter
```

## Technical notes / design
The generator is intentionally thin: it reads a JSONL sample, maps records to the normalised event dataclasses, and publishes to the bus on a timer with jitter, honouring backpressure from the bounded queues (M5). It must not become a second ingestion implementation — a comment and a Semgrep-visible marker state that it is a test double and that E08 owns the real path. The `CV_FEED` enum lives in M1 `config` alongside `Environment` (E02-T05) so the switch is structural and explicit, never inferred (the same principle the OpenAPI convention C9 applies to `environment`).

## Test plan
- Unit: generator emits well-formed normalised events; rate configuration honoured; backpressure causes drop-or-block per the configured policy rather than unbounded growth; `CV_FEED=live` without credentials raises the documented startup error.
- Integration: `make dev` smoke — stack healthy, events observed on the bus within 10 s, clean shutdown.
- E2E: the existing Playwright placeholder smoke runs against `make dev` rather than a hand-started server, proving the loop is the one the tests use.
- Docs test: E02-Q02's charter is the acceptance evidence for the README.
- Coverage: generator ≥85% (backend threshold).

## Security notes
The synthetic path is also a safety control: it guarantees that development and CI never require, and therefore never hold, real exchange credentials — directly supporting the E02-X01 objective that no real key can appear in the local stack, and the B3 boundary rule (`20-architecture.md` §2.2) that the KEK never resides in WSL. The sample fixture must contain no account identifiers, order ids or keys, enforced by the `packages/fixtures` redaction verify script (E02-T03). `CV_FEED=live` must be impossible to select accidentally: it requires an explicit environment value and explicit credentials, and the startup error must not echo any credential material.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the backend loop. The README is a documentation surface: it must use proper heading structure and avoid conveying meaning by colour alone, per the spirit of `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
`make dev` to a usable state ≤150 s cold (compose ≤120 s per E02-T08 plus Vite start). The generator must sustain its configured rate without unbounded memory growth — an early, cheap rehearsal of budget #8 (≤300 MB resident per recorded symbol) although no real symbol load applies yet.

## Observability
The generator increments the same bus-publish counters the real ingestion path will use, so Grafana panels built in E04 work against synthetic data before E08 lands — a deliberate sequencing win.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Four acceptance scenarios pass.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the generator; mypy --strict clean.
- [ ] README rewritten and validated by a non-author (E02-Q02).
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §5 synthetic-feed note confirmed accurate; `AGENTS.md` §4 documents `make dev`.
- [ ] Security engineer confirms no credential path and clean fixture.
- [ ] Demo at Sprint Review: clean machine → `make dev` → events flowing.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
Blocked by E02-T08 (stack) and E02-T04 (web dev server to start). Feeds E03's `integration` job and E04's dashboards; superseded in part by E08 when real ingestion lands.

## Branch
`feat/monorepo-scaffold-dev-loop` · two PRs: (1) synthetic generator + config switch, (2) `make dev` + README.

title: Security: STRIDE threat model for the monorepo supply chain and local dev stack
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 lists "STRIDE models complete for E03 (supply chain), E08 (exchange boundary), E09 (auth/RBAC)" as an R0 quality gate. E02 is where the supply chain is actually *created* — lockfiles, registries, lifecycle scripts, base images, git hooks, a local stack with datastores — so its model must land in S01, before E03 formalises the pipeline on top of it, and must hand E03 a ready list of controls to implement as CI jobs. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the STRIDE kickoff to be scheduled for any epic touching this ground.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model at `docs/plan/security/E02-threat-model.md` decomposing: developer workstation → git → package registries (npm, PyPI) → lockfiles → build (Turbo/uv/Docker) → local compose stack (postgres, questdb, prometheus, grafana, minio) → the WSL/Windows host boundary.
- Data-flow diagram (mermaid) with trust boundaries, reusing and extending `20-architecture.md` §2.2 boundaries B2 (host↔WSL) and B4 (renderer↔Electron main).
- Threat enumeration with at least: **S** — registry account/typosquat impersonation, forged commit identity; **T** — lockfile tampering, malicious postinstall/`prepare` script, mutable base-image tag substitution, hook tampering; **R** — unsigned commits/artefacts; **I** — secrets committed to git, `.env` leakage, recorded fixtures containing credentials, services bound to `0.0.0.0` reachable from the LAN via WSL portproxy; **D** — dependency-confusion outage, oversized image/volume filling the dev disk during a soak; **E** — container running as root, docker-socket mount, renderer→Node escalation via disabled Electron hardening.
- For each threat: likelihood/impact rating, the control, **where the control is implemented** (ticket key in E02 or E03), and the residual risk with an accept/mitigate decision.
- Abuse cases written as concrete scenarios (e.g. "a compromised transitive npm dependency adds a postinstall script that exfiltrates `~/.ssh`"; "a contributor commits a real `.env` with a Bybit demo key"; "an attacker on the same LAN reaches QuestDB because a port was bound to 0.0.0.0").
- Findings routed into `32-risk-register.md` where they represent programme-level risk.

## Out of scope
- Modelling the application's runtime threats (exchange boundary is E08; auth/RBAC is E09; key vault is E27) — this model stops at the scaffold and local stack.
- Implementing the scanners (E02-X02/E03) — this ticket specifies them.
- Pen-testing (R4, E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the threat model document
When the Security engineer reviews it
Then every STRIDE category has at least one enumerated threat with a rated likelihood/impact, a named control and an owning ticket key

Given a threat whose control is not implemented anywhere in E02 or E03
When the model is finalised
Then either a new ticket is filed or the residual risk is explicitly accepted with the Owner's recorded sign-off — never left blank

Given the abuse case "service bound to 0.0.0.0 on WSL"
When the model is traced to its control
Then it points at the automated loopback-binding assertion in E02-T08 and the regression assertion in E02-Q03

Given the model
When E03 plans its supply-chain jobs
Then every scanner it configures (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit, pip-audit, npm audit, gitleaks, Trivy, license-check) traces back to at least one threat in this model
```

## Technical notes / design
Model at the data-flow level, not the file level, so it stays valid as the scaffold evolves. Explicitly record the two deliberate exceptions made in E02 and their compensating controls: the husky `prepare` lifecycle script (E02-T07) and the `packages/fixtures` redaction requirement (E02-T03). Note that the KEK for API-key envelope encryption lives in the **host OS keychain, never in WSL** (`20-architecture.md` §2.2 B3) — the local dev stack must therefore never be a place where real keys can appear, which is why default credentials are `CHANGE_ME` and the bootstrap refuses them outside the dev profile.

## Test plan
N/A as code. Verification: (a) Security engineer review; (b) a traceability check that every control names an existing ticket key; (c) each abuse case is either automated (by E02-T08/T06/Q03 assertions) or listed as a manual check in E02-X02.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security artefact. Data classification for E02's scope: **no production data, no PII, no live keys** — the model's job is to keep it that way by making "a real credential in this stack" structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — security documentation, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Controls must not push the pipeline past R0 exit criterion 2 (≤15 min commit→dev). Where a scanner is slow (CodeQL, full-history gitleaks), the model states whether it belongs on the PR path or the nightly path (C-9.2) and why.

## Observability
Specifies the security signals E03/E04 must surface: scanner findings by severity over time, a failed-gate counter, and an alert if `secrets-scan` ever fires on `main`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Model merged at `docs/plan/security/E02-threat-model.md` with DFD, full STRIDE enumeration and ratings.
- [ ] Every threat has a control with an owning ticket key, or a recorded accepted-risk with Owner sign-off.
- [ ] Abuse cases listed and each mapped to an automated assertion or a manual check in E02-X02.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated with any programme-level risk.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment on E02.
- [ ] Findings presented at the Security Review; PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
Blocked by E02-T01 (the supply chain must exist in concrete form — registries, lockfile, `.npmrc` policy — to be modelled accurately). Feeds E02-X02, E02-T08 and all of E03's security jobs.

## Branch
`docs/security-e02-threat-model` · docs-only PR.

## References
- docs/plan/04-security-program.md
- docs/plan/20-architecture.md §2.2 (B2, B3, B4)
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §4.4
- docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md §2.1, §8
- /CONSTITUTION.md §12, §9 #10-#14
- docs/plan/32-risk-register.md

## Estimate reconciliation (2026-09-14)
Rebaselined from 3 to 2 pts as part of the epic-level reconciliation to the roadmap-locked **42 pts** for E02 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 line 102 and §4.2 line 185). The roadmap allocation is authoritative and was not changed; the backlog was re-estimated. Scope in this ticket is unchanged — the earlier number double-counted generator/boilerplate effort that `pnpm create`, `uv init`, Turborepo presets and the compose templates supply for free. If delivery shows the new figure is wrong, raise it at sprint review and re-plan the epic; do **not** silently re-inflate the ticket.

title: CI/CD pipeline & environments
body:
## Context
R0's second goal is blunt: *"Make the pipeline real: a commit to `main` builds, tests, scans, and deploys to dev with no manual step"* (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.1). Every other epic assumes the gates in `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§7 (required checks, merge queue, 2 approvals incl. a code-owner) exist and actually block. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0013-ci-pipeline.md` already decided the *shape* - GitHub Actions, path-filtered parallel jobs, a self-hosted runner for GPU benchmarks, Turborepo/uv caching, image-based immutable deploys. This epic **builds** it.

E03 sits on the critical path: the roadmap graph (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§11.1) has `E02 --> E03`, `E03 --> E04` and `E03 --> E09` - observability and auth cannot ship before the pipeline they ship through exists. E03 also owns one of the three mandatory R0 STRIDE models (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4: *"STRIDE models complete for E03 (supply chain), E08 (exchange boundary), E09 (auth/RBAC)"*), because CI is the highest-leverage supply-chain surface in the repository (threat boundary TB-8, `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§5).

E03 has **no user-story domain** (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§2 epic table lists domains "-" for E03): it delivers engineering infrastructure, so its children are Tasks, a Spike, design tickets for the developer-facing surfaces it creates, QA tickets that verify the gates really gate, and security tickets for the supply chain.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Pipeline skeleton**: `dorny/paths-filter` change detection, the job matrix, a *required-checks resolver* job (ADR-0013 rule 2), concurrency groups, least-privilege `permissions:` blocks, SHA-pinned actions (SR-132). -> `E03-T01`
- **Language lanes**: JS (eslint, `tsc`, vitest, build, Turborepo remote cache) and Python (ruff, `mypy --strict`, pytest, uv cache) over the E02 layout `packages/chart-engine`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/ui`, `apps/app-web`, `apps/app-electron`, `services/api`. -> `E03-T02`, `E03-T03`
- **Coverage gate**: >=85% backend & engine packages, >=80% frontend, build fails below (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4). -> `E03-T04`
- **Generated-code freshness gate**: `packages/protocol` regenerated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS schema of `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; any diff fails (ADR-0013 rule 3). -> `E03-T05`
- **Upper pyramid layers**: contract, integration (recorded fixtures only - never `api.bybit.com`, ADR-0012), `e2e-web`, `e2e-electron`, `a11y-axe`. -> `E03-T06`
- **Security lane**: CodeQL, Semgrep (incl. the `cv-*` rules of `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.2), Bandit, pip-audit, npm audit, gitleaks, license-scan (SR-136 allowlist), Trivy. -> `E03-T07`, `E03-X02`
- **Supply-chain release path**: container build + GHCR push tagged `semver+sha`, CycloneDX SBOM (syft, SR-133), cosign signature + provenance attestation (SR-137). -> `E03-T08`
- **Environments**: dev auto-deploy on every merge to `main`; staging (demo) deploy behind a GitHub Environment with required reviewers; documented rollback (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§9). -> `E03-T09`
- **Migrations**: Alembic job with `alembic heads` == 1 and `alembic check` drift detection (`21-database-schema.md` Ã‚Â§9), expand/contract assertion (ADR-0013 rule 9). -> `E03-T10`
- **Release automation**: release-please-style changelog job appending to `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased (`07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§3). -> `E03-T11`
- **Branch protection & merge queue as code**: the required-check set from `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3, linear history, no force-push, signed release tags. -> `E03-T13`
- **Security lane rules**: the `cv-*` Semgrep corpus and CodeQL suite are consumed by `E03-T07`; authoring them is deferred (see Deferred scope).
- **Governance artefacts**: CI runbook and the ADR-0013 validation exercises. -> `E03-T15`
- **Gate verification & QA sign-off**: a negative fixture proving every required check actually blocks, plus the epic-level regression pass. -> `E03-Q01`

## Deferred scope (rebaselined to the roadmap budget)
`30-release-roadmap.md` §2 allocates E03 **42 points across the S01-S03 train window**. The first pass of this backlog
sized 82 points and scheduled five children into Sprint 04, outside the window. Rather than silently overrun the agreed
train allocation, E03 is rebaselined to **46 points, all inside S01-S03** (+9.5%, within the +-15% planning tolerance);
the residual 4 points are the re-sizing of `E03-T06` and `E03-Q01` after they shed the work listed below.

The following work is **deferred out of E03** and carried as separate `Backlog` items to be pulled into an R1 train
(a follow-on CI/CD hardening epic) once R0's exit criteria are met. None of it is required by an R0 exit criterion:

| Deferred | Why it can wait past R0 | Re-entry trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `E03-K01` Spike: GPU runner isolation | Engine benchmarks belong to E06/E11, which start in R1. | Before E06 needs a benchmark gate. |
| `E03-T14` GPU benchmark job + baseline | Same; ADR-0013 rule 4 has no R0 consumer. | With `E03-K01`. |
| `E03-T12` Nightly scheduled matrix | Every slot's owner (load, soak, chaos, DAST, a11y sweep) is itself deferred or in a later epic; an all-stub scheduler is cost without signal. | When >=2 slots have real content. |
| `E03-Q02` k6/Locust perf harness | Budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` need a real API/WS surface (E08/E09) to measure. | R1, with E08. |
| `E03-Q03` Pipeline chaos + flaky quarantine | Needs deploy history to quarantine against; manual flake triage is acceptable for one train. | After 1 train of flake data. |
| `E03-Q05` a11y CI harness validation | `E03-T06` ships the harness; there is no product UI to scan until E05. | With E05. |
| `E03-X02` Custom `cv-*` Semgrep rules | `E03-T07` runs the default CodeQL/Semgrep suites in R0; the bespoke corpus targets code (OMS, auth) that does not exist yet. | With E09. |
| `E03-X03` CI secrets/permissions audit | The controls are *implemented* under `E03-X01`'s STRIDE model in R0; the independent audit is the verification pass. | R1 hardening. |
| `E03-X04` ZAP DAST integration | No authenticated surface exists before E09. | With E09. |
| `E03-X05` Security sign-off on signing/SBOM | `E03-T08` DoD keeps the security-engineer review inline; the standalone sign-off ticket duplicated it. | Pre-R4 live-enablement gate. |
| `E03-D01`/`E03-D02` Pipeline-experience design | E03 ships no product screen; failure-message quality is captured as a DoD line on `E03-T01`/`E03-T15` instead of a design-ahead pair. | If CI messaging becomes a measured pain point. |

Work **retained** because an R0 exit criterion or a mandatory gate depends on it: the STRIDE model (`E03-X01`,
`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4), every blocking PR gate (`T01`-`T08`, `T10`, `T13`), dev/staging deploy (`T09`),
release automation (`T11`), the runbook (`T15`) and gate verification + QA sign-off (`Q01`).

## Out of scope
- Kubernetes/cloud orchestration - targets are docker compose on WSL Ubuntu, later a single VPS (`00-planning-brief.md`).
- Terraform/IaC modules - ADR-0013 states "terraform-free (n/a)".
- The observability stack itself (Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager exporters, dashboards, alert routing) - that is **E04**, which depends on E03.
- Authoring engine benchmarks B1-B10 (`26-chart-engine-design.md` Ã‚Â§13) - E03 provides the runner and the comparison harness only; the benchmarks belong to E06/E11.
- Pen-test execution and the Live-enablement gate (R4 / E43, `07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§6).
- Android/mobile build lanes - Android is out of scope per the owner decision of 2026-09-14.
- Any product UI: E03 ships no application screen from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Everything in the Deferred scope table above - it is out of E03 and must not be pulled in without a roadmap change to the 42-point allocation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fast, complete signal on a pull request
  Given a pull request touching "services/api" and "packages/protocol"
  When the pipeline runs
  Then the Python lane, contract, integration, generated-code freshness and security jobs execute
  And the chart-engine GPU benchmark job is reported not-applicable by the required-checks resolver
  And end-to-end PR feedback completes within 15 minutes at p90

Scenario: A commit to main reaches dev with no manual step
  Given a pull request is merged to "main" through the merge queue
  When the post-merge workflow completes
  Then an image tagged "<semver>+<sha>" is pushed to GHCR with a CycloneDX SBOM and a cosign signature
  And the dev docker compose stack is redeployed to that exact image digest automatically
  And the deploy smoke test against /health/live, /health/ready and build-info passes

Scenario: A drifted generated protocol cannot merge
  Given a pull request edits "docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml" without regenerating "packages/protocol"
  When the freshness job runs "make gen && git diff --exit-code"
  Then the job fails and the pull request is not mergeable

Scenario: Staging promotion requires a human
  Given a green build on "main"
  When the staging deploy workflow is triggered
  Then it pauses on the "staging" GitHub Environment awaiting a required reviewer
  And no deployment happens until an authorised reviewer approves

Scenario: The supply-chain gate blocks a prohibited licence
  Given a pull request adds a dependency licensed AGPL-3.0
  When the license-scan job evaluates it against the SR-136 allowlist
  Then the job fails and names the offending package in the log
```

## Technical notes / design
- Workflows in `.github/workflows/`: `pr.yml` (matrix entry point), `main.yml` (build/sign/deploy-dev), `staging.yml` (gated deploy), `nightly.yml`, `release.yml`, plus reusable `_job-*.yml` workflows so lanes are composed, not copy-pasted.
- The required-checks resolver is a terminal job reading the paths-filter outputs and each lane's `result`, emitting a single `ci-required` conclusion; it is the only aggregate check in branch protection, so a skipped-but-inapplicable job never wedges the queue while a skipped-but-applicable job fails it.
- Every `uses:` is pinned to a full commit SHA, with a Dependabot `github-actions` ecosystem entry to bump them (SR-132, SR-134).
- Caching: Turborepo remote cache, `uv` cache keyed on `uv.lock`, Playwright browser cache keyed on version, Docker layer cache.
- Deployment is image-based and immutable (rule 8); rollback = redeploy the previous tag, never a down-migration (rule 9).

## Test plan
- Every child carries its own tests. At epic level, verification is the **pipeline verification test plan** (`E03-Q01`) driven by deliberate-failure fixtures: drifted protocol, planted synthetic secret, prohibited licence, coverage drop, unpinned action, Critical Trivy finding, unsigned image, second Alembic head.
- The R0 exit criterion "green pipeline from commit to dev deployment <= 15 min" is measured and recorded by `E03-Q01`.

## Security notes
- The STRIDE model for supply-chain boundary TB-8 is a blocking R0 quality gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4) and is delivered by `E03-X01`.
- Binding controls: SR-130 locked deps, SR-131 digest-pinned non-root base images, SR-132 SHA-pinned actions and least-privilege permissions with `pull_request_target` prohibited, SR-133 SBOM, SR-136 licence policy, SR-137 CI-only signed builds, SR-138 `--ignore-scripts`, SR-140 **no production Bybit credentials in CI ever**, SR-141 OIDC over long-lived tokens plus environment protection, SR-142 gitleaks, SR-146 no secret leakage into CI logs.
- Data classification: CI holds no customer data and no exchange credentials; it holds signing material and registry tokens (Secret/High).

## Accessibility notes
E03 ships no product UI, so WCAG 2.2 AA conformance does not apply to its own output. It owns the **enforcement mechanism**: the `a11y-axe` required check and the nightly `pa11y-ci` sweep on which every UI epic depends (`05-accessibility-standard.md`). Developer-facing artefacts (runbook, failure-triage guide, status surfaces) follow the plain-language, heading-structure and colour-independence rules of `05-accessibility-standard.md` - CI status must never be conveyed by colour alone.

## Performance notes
- Pipeline budget: **p90 PR feedback <= 15 minutes** (ADR-0013 rule 5, R0 exit criterion 2), measured weekly; a breach triggers a matrix rebalance.
- E03 provides the harnesses enforcing the product budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (#3 WS tick->screen, #4 order submit->ack, #5 24 h ingestion soak, #13 REST p95) and the >10% regression rule on engine benchmarks B1-B10.

## Observability
- Workflow-level: job duration and outcome exported into a CI metrics summary; flaky retries recorded (three in a week auto-opens a quarantine issue, ADR-0013 rule 10).
- Deploy-level: each deploy emits an annotated event (image digest, git sha, actor, environment) that E04's Grafana consumes once it exists.
- Audit: environment-approval events for staging promotion are retained in the GitHub audit log and referenced in the release checklist.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion 2 demonstrated end-to-end and timed (<= 15 min p90 over a sprint of real PRs).
- [ ] Required status checks of `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 configured and demonstrably blocking (a deliberately failing PR shown unmergeable).
- [ ] STRIDE model finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] CI runbook merged and linked from `CONTRIBUTING.md`: failure triage, benchmark-runner override, rollback, secret rotation.
- [ ] ADR-0013 Ã‚Â§Validation satisfied: the deliberate "break the protocol" PR failed the freshness gate, evidence recorded.
- [ ] QA sign-off from `E03-Q01`; PRR-lite item "dev environment rebuild runbook" green.
- [ ] Developer-facing failure messaging reviewed against `E03-T01`'s summary spec and the `E03-T15` runbook (no separate design ticket: E03 ships no product UI; the design-ahead pair is deferred).
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at a Sprint Review: a live failing gate and a live dev deploy.

## Dependencies
- **E02** monorepo scaffold & toolchain - the pipeline runs the commands E02 defines (`make gen`, workspace lint/type/test entry points); without the workspace layout there is nothing to path-filter.
- **E01** governance - CODEOWNERS, PR/issue templates and branch-protection policy which E03 encodes as required checks.
- Downstream: **E04** observability and **E09** auth/RBAC are blocked on E03 (`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§11.1).

## Branch
`feat/e03-cicd-<short>` per child (e.g. `feat/e03-cicd-skeleton`). PR size guidance: one workflow concern per PR, <= 400 LOC diff; workflow YAML changes must describe the resulting job graph in the PR body.

## Children dependency graph
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    E02[E02 Monorepo] --> T01[E03-T01 Pipeline skeleton + resolver]
    E01[E01 Governance] --> T13[E03-T13 Branch protection + merge queue]
    E01 --> X01[E03-X01 STRIDE supply chain]

    T03 --> T04

    T02 --> T06[E03-T06 Contract/integration/e2e/a11y jobs]
    T03 --> T06
    X01 --> T07[E03-T07 Security scanning lane]
    T01 --> T07
    T07 --> T08[E03-T08 Image build + SBOM + cosign]
    T08 --> T09[E03-T09 Dev auto-deploy + gated staging]
    T03 --> T10[E03-T10 Alembic migration job]
    T10 --> T09
    T08 --> T11[E03-T11 Changelog + release job]
    T04 --> T13
    T06 --> T13
    T07 --> T13
    T13 --> T15[E03-T15 CI runbook + ADR-0013 validation]
    T05 --> Q01[E03-Q01 Gate verification + QA sign-off]

    T09 --> Q01
    T13 --> Q01
```
Deferred children (`K01`, `T12`, `T14`, `D01`, `D02`, `Q02`-`Q05`, `X02`-`X05`) are not shown: they are out of the
S01-S03 train per the Deferred scope table.

## Risks
| Risk | Handling |
|---|---|
| R2 Render performance (benchmark runner) | A single pinned GPU runner is a merge-blocking single point of failure; `E03-K01`/`E03-T14` define the architect-approved manual-override path (ADR-0013 Ã‚Â§Consequences). |
| R5 Scope | Pipelines absorb unlimited polish; the first sizing pass hit 82 pts against a 42-pt allocation, which is why the Deferred scope table exists and is binding. Scope is fixed to the ADR-0013 job list, with nightly-only work isolated in `E03-T12`. |
| Supply-chain compromise (TB-8) | `E03-X01` STRIDE, SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege permissions, OIDC, `--ignore-scripts`, signed images, gitleaks full-history. |
| CI cost/minutes | Path filters, concurrency cancellation, caching; measured weekly against the 15-minute budget. |

- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` - axe-core merge gate, pa11y-ci sweep
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` - budgets #3, #4, #5, #13 and the k6/Locust harness spec
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§3 changelog automation, Ã‚Â§4 release checklist, Ã‚Â§5 PRR

- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4 R0 goals/scope/exit criteria/quality gates, Ã‚Â§11.1 epic dependency graph


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Build the Actions PR skeleton with path filters and a checks resolver
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0013-ci-pipeline.md` chooses "GitHub Actions with path-filtered, parallel jobs". Binding rule 2 is the hard part: *"Path filtering decides which jobs run, but the required set is computed from the same filter so a skipped-but-required job reports success only when genuinely not applicable (a 'required checks resolver' job emits the conclusion)."* Without this, GitHub branch protection either blocks forever on skipped jobs or is satisfied by jobs that should have run. This Task lays the entry-point workflow every other E03 Task plugs lanes into.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/pr.yml`: triggers `pull_request` (opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review) against `main`; top-level `permissions: contents: read`; `concurrency: group: pr-${{ github.head_ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true` (ADR-0013 rule 7).
- `changed-paths` job using `dorny/paths-filter` pinned by SHA, emitting boolean outputs: `js`, `py`, `engine`, `protocol`, `infra`, `docs`, `e2e`, `migrations`.
- Reusable-workflow skeletons `.github/workflows/_job-js.yml`, `_job-py.yml`, `_job-contract.yml`, `_job-security.yml`, `_job-e2e.yml`, `_job-engine-bench.yml` - each a `workflow_call` stub in this Task, filled in by T02/T03/T06/T07/T14.
- `ci-required` resolver job: `if: always()`, consumes `needs.*.result` plus the filter outputs, fails when an *applicable* lane is not `success`, succeeds when a lane is `skipped` **and** its filter output is `false`, and fails loudly ("gate misconfiguration") when a lane is `skipped` while its filter is `true`.
- Always-on jobs wired here: commitlint (conventional commits, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§6), licence-header check, docs link check (ADR-0013 pipeline shape line "[always]").
- `.github/actions-pins.md` documenting each pinned action SHA + its upstream tag, and a Dependabot entry for the `github-actions` ecosystem (SR-132, SR-134).
- `CODEOWNERS` entry making DevSecOps a code-owner of `.github/workflows/**`.

## Out of scope
- Any lane's actual commands (T02, T03, T06, T07, T14).
- Branch-protection configuration - T13 consumes `ci-required`.
- Post-merge, staging, nightly and release workflows (T08, T09, T11, T12).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Docs-only pull request skips code lanes yet reports green
  Given a pull request that changes only files under "docs/"
  When the pipeline runs
  Then the js, py, contract, e2e and engine lanes are skipped
  And commitlint, licence-header and docs-link jobs run
  And the "ci-required" job concludes success

Scenario: An applicable lane that is skipped fails the gate
  Given a pull request that changes "packages/chart-engine/src/renderer.ts"
  And the engine lane is disabled by a misconfigured condition so it reports skipped
  When the "ci-required" job evaluates results
  Then it fails with the message "gate misconfiguration: engine applicable but skipped"

Scenario: Superseded runs are cancelled
  Given a pull request with a run in progress
  When a new commit is pushed to the same head ref
  Then the in-progress run is cancelled by the concurrency group
  And only the newest run reports a conclusion

Scenario: An unpinned action is rejected
  Given a workflow file references "actions/checkout@v4" by tag
  When the workflow-lint step runs the SR-132 pin check
  Then the job fails naming the unpinned reference
```

## Technical notes / design
- Resolver logic (pseudo-code, runs in `actions/github-script`):
```
LANES = {js: needs.js, py: needs.py, contract: needs.contract, e2e: needs.e2e,
         security: needs.security, engine: needs.engine, a11y: needs.a11y}
for name, lane in LANES:
    applicable = filters[name]
    if applicable and lane.result != 'success': fail(name + ' required and not successful')
    if not applicable and lane.result == 'skipped': continue
    if applicable and lane.result == 'skipped': fail('gate misconfiguration: ' + name)
```
- The pin check is a small script (`tools/ci/check_action_pins.py`) grepping `uses:` lines for a 40-hex SHA; it also asserts no workflow uses `pull_request_target` (SR-132).
- Config keys: repository variables `CV_CI_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` (default 20), `CV_CI_DEBUG` (never enables `set -x` around secrets, SR-146).
- Error codes surfaced in the resolver summary: `CI-GATE-001` applicable lane failed, `CI-GATE-002` gate misconfiguration, `CI-GATE-003` unpinned action.

## Test plan
- Unit: pytest for `tools/ci/check_action_pins.py` - pinned SHA passes, tag fails, `pull_request_target` fails, comment lines ignored.
- Unit: node test for the resolver matrix over all (applicable x result) combinations, including `cancelled` and `failure`.
- Integration: `act`-free approach - three fixture PRs in a scratch branch (docs-only, python-only, engine-only) with the resulting conclusions recorded in the ticket.
- Coverage target: >=85% for `tools/ci` (Python package threshold).

## Security notes
- SR-132: SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege `permissions`, `pull_request_target` prohibited - all three enforced by the pin-check step added here.
- SR-146: workflows must not `set -x` around secret usage or dump environment; a lint rule greps for `env | ` and `set -x` in workflow run blocks.
- Threat: a malicious PR modifying a workflow to exfiltrate secrets - mitigated because PR workflows receive no secrets (ADR-0013 rule 6) and `.github/workflows/**` is CODEOWNER-gated.
- Data classification: no secrets touched by this Task.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for WCAG (no product UI). The resolver's job summary must not convey status by colour alone - it writes explicit PASS/FAIL/SKIPPED words plus the reason, per the colour-independence principle of `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
The skeleton itself must add <= 60 s of overhead to any run; `changed-paths` and the resolver are the only always-on serial points. Contributes to the p90 <= 15 min budget (ADR-0013 rule 5).

## Observability
- Each run writes a job summary table (lane, applicable, result, duration).
- Durations are appended to a `ci-metrics` artifact consumed by the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q04 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope) for the 15-minute measurement.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified with the three fixture PRs, evidence links on the ticket.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met for `tools/ci`.
- [ ] `docs/` CI section and `.github/actions-pins.md` merged in the same PR.
- [ ] Security engineer reviewed the permissions blocks and the pin check (SR-132).
- [ ] Demoed: a docs PR going green in under two minutes.
- [ ] PR merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E02` provides the workspace layout the path filters reference; without `packages/*`, `apps/*`, `services/api` the filters are meaningless.

## Branch
`feat/e03-cicd-skeleton`. PR size: ~250 LOC of YAML + a small Python tool; single PR is acceptable.

- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` - budgets #3, #4, #5, #13 and the k6/Locust harness spec

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**

## Context
ADR-0013's pipeline shape defines the JS lane as `lint (eslint) - typecheck (tsc) - unit (vitest) - build`, cached via Turborepo to hold the p90 <= 15 min budget (rule 5). `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 names `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit-frontend` and `unit-engine` as required checks on `main`. E02 defines the pnpm workspace (`packages/chart-engine`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/ui`, `apps/app-web`, `apps/app-electron`) and the ESLint/Prettier/Biome + vitest configuration; this Task runs them in CI, correctly and fast.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-js.yml` (`workflow_call`), invoked from `pr.yml` when the `js` or `engine` filter is true.
- Steps: checkout (SHA-pinned) -> setup-node with the version from `.nvmrc` -> `corepack enable` -> `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` (SR-130, SR-138, with the documented exception list) -> `pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test build --filter=...[origin/main]`.
- Turborepo remote cache: self-hosted cache endpoint configured through repository variables `TURBO_API`, `TURBO_TEAM`; the token supplied as an environment secret only on `main` runs, never on PR runs from a branch lacking write access (ADR-0013 rule 6).
- Split job outputs so branch protection sees distinct checks: `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit-frontend`, `unit-engine` (matrix over `{ui,app-web,app-electron}` vs `{chart-engine,protocol}`).
- Vitest JUnit + coverage (v8) reporters emitting `coverage/lcov.info` per package, uploaded as artifacts for `E03-T04`.
- Playwright browser cache keyed on the Playwright version (used by `E03-T06`, provisioned here).
- `pnpm dedupe --check` and a `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` hand-off marker consumed by `E03-T07` (the audit itself lives in the security lane).

## Out of scope
- Coverage thresholds and the failing gate - `E03-T04`.
- E2E/Playwright execution - `E03-T06`.
- npm audit / licence scanning - `E03-T07`.
- GPU engine benchmarks - the deferred R1 backlog item E03-T14 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full JS lane on a cold cache
  Given an empty Turborepo remote cache
  When the js lane runs on a pull request touching "packages/ui"
  Then lint, typecheck, unit-frontend and build all execute and pass
  And the total lane duration is recorded in the job summary

Scenario: Warm cache short-circuits unaffected packages
  Given the remote cache holds results for the current inputs of "packages/chart-engine"
  When a pull request touches only "apps/app-web"
  Then the chart-engine tasks are reported as cache hits and are not re-executed
  And the lane completes in under 5 minutes

Scenario: A type error fails the lane
  Given a pull request introducing "const x: number = 'a'" in "packages/ui"
  When the typecheck job runs
  Then the job fails and the error is annotated on the offending line in the pull request

Scenario: A tampered lockfile fails the install
  Given "pnpm-lock.yaml" does not match "package.json"
  When "pnpm install --frozen-lockfile" runs
  Then the job fails before any test executes
```

## Technical notes / design
- `--filter=...[origin/main]` restricts to affected packages; the resolver in T01 still marks the lane applicable so the check is meaningful.
- `--ignore-scripts` is mandatory (SR-138); packages genuinely needing postinstall (e.g. Playwright browser download) are listed in `tools/ci/allowed-postinstall.json` and invoked explicitly.
- Node version is pinned in `.nvmrc` and asserted against `package.json#engines`; a mismatch fails fast with `CI-JS-001`.
- Timeouts: 20 min per job, matching `CV_CI_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`.

## Test plan
- Unit: reuse the packages' own vitest suites - this Task adds no product code.
- Integration: fixture PRs proving cold-cache, warm-cache, type-error and lockfile-drift behaviour (the four scenarios), with durations recorded.
- Perf: record cold vs warm lane duration in the ticket; warm must be <= 5 min.
- Coverage target: N/A for the workflow itself; the lane must not lower any package's measured coverage.

## Security notes
- SR-130 frozen lockfile with hash verification; SR-138 `--ignore-scripts` with an explicit exception list reviewed by the Security engineer.
- The Turborepo cache token is an environment secret, write-scoped only on `main`; PR runs use read-only or no cache credentials (SR-141, ADR-0013 rule 6).
- Threat: cache poisoning producing a "passing" build from an attacker-supplied artifact - mitigated by signed cache entries where supported and by the fact that release images are always built from a clean, cache-free job in `E03-T08`.

N/A - no product UI. The lane provisions the axe-core/Playwright toolchain that `E03-T06` and the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q05 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope) use to enforce a11y.

## Performance notes
Budget: warm-cache JS lane <= 5 min, cold <= 12 min; contributes to the p90 <= 15 min pipeline budget (ADR-0013 rule 5).

Job summary records per-task cache hit/miss and duration; these feed the `ci-metrics` artifact from `E03-T01`.

title: Implement the Python CI lane with ruff, mypy strict, pytest and uv caching
body:
## Context
The mirror of `E03-T02` for `services/api` and any Python tooling packages. ADR-0013 defines the lane as `lint (ruff) - typecheck (mypy --strict on modules) - unit (pytest) - build`; `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 names `lint`, `typecheck` and `unit-backend` as required checks. `ADR-0004-modular-monolith.md` additionally requires an **import-linter architecture test** (`services/api/tests/test_architecture.py`) asserting the module dependency graph is acyclic and respects declared layers - that test must run in this lane on every PR, because module boundaries "erode under deadline pressure".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-py.yml` (`workflow_call`), invoked when the `py` filter is true.
- Steps: checkout -> `astral-sh/setup-uv` (SHA-pinned) with cache keyed on `uv.lock` -> `uv sync --frozen` -> `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` -> `mypy --strict` over the module list -> `pytest -m "not exchange_smoke" --cov` -> package build (`uv build`).
- **Pytest network guard**: enforce ADR-0012's rule that "no test may contact `api.bybit.com` or the live WS" - a `conftest.py` autouse fixture patching socket creation to reject non-loopback connections, plus a CI-level assertion that the `exchange_smoke` marker is deselected.
- Import-linter contract execution (`ADR-0004`), reported as its own check `architecture`.
- Coverage XML/lcov artifacts for `E03-T04`.
- Postgres/QuestDB service containers for the subset of tests marked `integration_db`, pinned by digest (SR-131).

## Out of scope
- The coverage threshold gate (`E03-T04`), Bandit/pip-audit (`E03-T07`), Alembic migration checks (`E03-T10`), contract and integration pipeline suites (`E03-T06`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backend lane passes on a clean tree
  Given a pull request touching "services/api"
  When the py lane runs
  Then ruff, mypy --strict, pytest and the architecture contract all pass
  And a coverage report artifact is uploaded

Scenario: A module-boundary violation fails the build
  Given a pull request where the ingestion module imports an internal symbol from the OMS module
  When the import-linter architecture check runs
  Then the job fails naming the forbidden edge

Scenario: A test attempting to reach the live exchange is blocked
  Given a test that opens a connection to "api.bybit.com"
  When pytest runs under the network guard
  Then the test errors with "outbound network denied in CI" and the job fails

Scenario: An unfrozen dependency change fails
  Given "pyproject.toml" adds a dependency without updating "uv.lock"
  When "uv sync --frozen" runs
  Then the job fails before tests execute
```

## Technical notes / design
- `mypy --strict` scope is the module list declared in E02's `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.mypy] files = ...`); new modules must be added there or the lane fails with `CI-PY-002 module not covered by mypy`.
- Network guard implementation: `socket.socket.connect` wrapper allowing `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and the service-container hostnames listed in `CV_CI_ALLOWED_HOSTS`; anything else raises `RuntimeError`.
- Service containers: `postgres:16-<digest>`, `questdb:<digest>`; credentials are ephemeral and generated per run, never GitHub secrets (SR-140).
- Timeouts: 20 min; `-p no:randomly` is **not** used - test order randomisation stays on, with the seed printed for reproduction.

## Test plan
- Unit: tests for the network-guard fixture itself (loopback allowed, external denied, allow-list honoured).
- Integration: fixture PRs for each of the four scenarios above.
- Contract: none here (`E03-T06`).
- Coverage target: >=85% for `services/api` measured, gate applied in `E03-T04`.

## Security notes
- SR-140 is the headline control: **CI must not hold production Bybit credentials**; this lane is where that rule is structurally enforced by the network guard plus the `exchange_smoke` deselection.
- SR-130 frozen, hash-verified Python lockfile; SR-131 digest-pinned service containers.
- SR-145: a test asserts that no fixture matches real key patterns - wired to run in this lane.
- Data classification: fixtures only, synthetic keys with a dummy prefix.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Budget: py lane <= 8 min warm. `uv` cache hit rate reported in the job summary.

## Observability
Job summary: ruff/mypy error counts, pytest pass/fail/skip counts, slowest 10 tests, uv cache hit ratio.

title: Enforce coverage thresholds as a blocking CI gate
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4 makes coverage a gate with a stated behaviour: ">=85% backend & engine packages, >=80% frontend (**enforced, build fails below**)". `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Ã‚Â§3.2 additionally requires "no regression to package baseline" - a per-package ratchet, not just a floor. `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 names `coverage-thresholds` as a required check on `main`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-coverage.yml` consuming the coverage artifacts produced by `E03-T02` (lcov per JS package) and `E03-T03` (coverage.xml for `services/api`).
- `tools/ci/coverage_gate.py`: reads `tools/ci/coverage-baselines.json` (package -> {floor, baseline}) and fails when `measured < floor` or `measured < baseline - tolerance` (tolerance 0.5 pp to absorb line-count noise).
- Floors seeded per the standard: `services/api` 85, `packages/chart-engine` 85, `packages/protocol` 85, `packages/ui` 80, `apps/app-web` 80, `apps/app-electron` 80.
- Baseline-raise automation: when a package's measured coverage exceeds its baseline by >=1 pp on `main`, a bot PR raises the baseline (ratchet up, never down).
- Baseline **lowering** requires an explicit commit editing `coverage-baselines.json` with a `Reason:` line, CODEOWNER approval from the QA lead - enforced by a CODEOWNERS rule on that file.
- A PR-comment summary table (package, floor, baseline, measured, delta, verdict) with words not colours.

## Out of scope
- Writing tests to reach the thresholds (owned by each feature epic).
- Mutation testing and flakiness quarantine (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q03 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A package below its floor fails the build
  Given "services/api" measures 83.2% line coverage
  When the coverage gate runs
  Then the job fails with "services/api 83.2% < floor 85.0%"

Scenario: A regression against baseline fails even when above the floor
  Given "packages/ui" has baseline 91.0% and measures 88.0%
  When the coverage gate runs
  Then the job fails with "regression 3.0pp beyond 0.5pp tolerance"

Scenario: An improvement ratchets the baseline on main
  Given "packages/protocol" has baseline 88.0% and measures 89.4% on a merge to main
  When the gate runs in ratchet mode
  Then a bot pull request is opened raising the baseline to 89.4%

Scenario: A package with no coverage artifact is treated as a failure
  Given the js lane failed to upload lcov for "packages/chart-engine" while the engine filter was true
  When the coverage gate runs
  Then the job fails with "missing coverage artifact" rather than silently passing
```

## Technical notes / design
- Missing-artifact-is-failure is deliberate: a silently-absent report is the most common way a coverage gate becomes decorative.
- Tolerance and floors live in one JSON file so the policy is reviewable in a diff; the file is CODEOWNER-gated by the QA lead.
- Error codes: `CI-COV-001` below floor, `CI-COV-002` baseline regression, `CI-COV-003` missing artifact.

## Test plan
- Unit (pytest, >=85%): `coverage_gate.py` over a fixture matrix - below floor, at floor, above baseline, within tolerance, missing artifact, malformed lcov, malformed coverage.xml.
- Integration: a fixture PR deleting tests from `packages/ui` must fail the gate; a fixture PR adding tests must ratchet on merge.
- Coverage target: >=85% for `tools/ci`.

## Security notes
- Low direct surface. The bot PR uses a least-privilege token (`contents: write`, `pull-requests: write` only) scoped to the baselines file path; SR-141 favours OIDC/GitHub App over a PAT.
- Threat: an author lowering a baseline to sneak past the gate - mitigated by the CODEOWNERS rule and the mandatory `Reason:` line.

## Accessibility notes
The PR comment table states PASS/FAIL in words and uses no colour-only signalling (`05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Gate adds <= 60 s. No product performance impact.

## Observability
Per-package coverage values are appended to the `ci-metrics` artifact for trend reporting in the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q04 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four scenarios demonstrated.
- [ ] `coverage-thresholds` registered as a required check name for `E03-T13`.
- [ ] QA lead is CODEOWNER of `tools/ci/coverage-baselines.json`.
- [ ] Documented in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` cross-reference and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (labelled `qa`).
- [ ] PR merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

- `E03-T02`/`E03-T03` produce the artifacts this gate consumes; without them the gate can only fail.

title: Add the generated-code freshness gate for packages/protocol
body:
## Context
ADR-0013 binding rule 3: *"Generated-code freshness is a hard gate. `packages/protocol` is regenerated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS schema; any diff fails the build. Generated files are committed so consumers need no codegen step."* `ADR-0005-ws-protocol-and-binary-encoding.md` reinforces it: *"Binary framing is unforgiving of drift. Mitigated by the `version` byte, a CI check that regenerates `packages/protocol` and fails on a diff, and fuzz tests feeding malformed frames to the decoder."* ADR-0013 Ã‚Â§Validation requires a deliberate "break the protocol" PR during Sprint 01 to prove the gate bites - executed under `E03-T15`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-gen.yml`, always-on (the contract sources may change from any lane).
- Step: `make gen && git diff --exit-code -- packages/protocol` per ADR-0013's literal wording, plus `git status --porcelain` to catch *untracked* generated files that `git diff` would miss.
- Sources wired: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (REST models/clients) and the WS schema definitions of `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (topic envelopes, snapshot/delta frames, binary framing constants).
- Failure output: the actual unified diff rendered in the job summary plus the exact reproduction command (`make gen`), so a contributor never has to guess.
- A deterministic-generation assertion: `make gen` twice in a row must produce a byte-identical tree (catches map-ordering nondeterminism, which would make the gate flaky and therefore ignored).
- Codegen toolchain versions pinned in `Makefile`/`tools/gen/requirements.txt`; a version bump that changes output must be a deliberate, reviewed commit.

## Out of scope
- Contract *conformance* tests (server actually matching the schema) - `E03-T06`.
- Authoring the protocol schema itself - `E17` (WS protocol epic) and the API epics.
- Fuzz tests of the decoder - owned by the engine/protocol epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An in-sync tree passes
  Given "packages/protocol" matches the output of "make gen"
  When the freshness job runs
  Then "git diff --exit-code" succeeds and the job passes

Scenario: A schema edit without regeneration fails
  Given a pull request adds a field to a schema in "docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml"
  And "packages/protocol" is unchanged
  When the freshness job runs
  Then the job fails and the job summary shows the missing generated diff and the command "make gen"

Scenario: Untracked generated output fails
  Given "make gen" produces a new file that is not committed and is git-ignored by mistake
  When the freshness job runs
  Then "git status --porcelain" is non-empty and the job fails

Scenario: Non-deterministic generation is caught
  Given the generator emits map keys in a non-deterministic order
  When "make gen" runs twice and the outputs are compared
  Then the job fails with "codegen is not deterministic" before any diff check is reported
```

## Technical notes / design
- Order matters: determinism check first, then freshness - otherwise a flaky generator presents as a random freshness failure and erodes trust in the gate.
- The job runs on a clean checkout with no cache to prevent a stale cached artifact masking drift.
- Error codes: `CI-GEN-001` drift, `CI-GEN-002` untracked output, `CI-GEN-003` non-deterministic generation, `CI-GEN-004` generator toolchain version mismatch.

## Test plan
- Integration: four fixture PRs, one per scenario, with run links recorded.
- The ADR-0013-mandated "break the protocol" validation PR is executed and recorded under `E03-T15` and cross-linked here.
- Coverage: N/A (workflow + Makefile target); the generator's own tests belong to E02/E17.

## Security notes
- Generated-code drift is a correctness *and* security issue: the chart engine decodes binary frames and SR-128 requires bounds-checked decoding driven by the generated constants. Drift between generator and consumer is exactly the state SR-128 assumes cannot happen.
- The job needs `contents: read` only; no secrets.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Target <= 90 s. It is always-on, so it sits directly in the p90 <= 15 min budget.

## Observability
Job summary records the generator version, the two-run determinism hash, and the diff size when failing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-contract.yml`: OpenAPI conformance (server routes vs `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`), WS schema conformance against `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, and the `packages/protocol` codec round-trip property tests.
- `.github/workflows/_job-integration.yml`: the fixture-driven pipeline suite (recorded WS session -> book -> bars -> order-flow -> gateway frames compared to golden outputs) and the OMS fake-exchange suite, per `03-testing-strategy.md` Ã‚Â§integration and ADR-0012's table. Fixtures are fetched from Git LFS with a pinned pointer; a missing/corrupt fixture fails with a distinct code rather than silently skipping.
- `.github/workflows/_job-e2e.yml`: Playwright `e2e-web` on PRs (against a compose stack with the synthetic/recorded feed); `e2e-electron` on `release/*` branches and nightly; sharded across 4 runners; traces/videos uploaded on failure only.
- `a11y-axe` job: `@axe-core/playwright` over the key routes of the E2E suite plus `vitest-axe` component assertions, failing on any new serious/critical violation.
- **`@demo-rest-only` job wiring** (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§9): a dedicated `e2e:staging` job definition that runs only the `@demo-rest-only`-tagged specs against demo REST endpoints and asserts no WS order-entry frames were sent. In R0 there are no order specs yet, so the job runs with an empty-but-valid tag selection and fails if the *tag itself* disappears from the suite configuration - the harness must exist before R3 needs it.
- Flake handling: one automatic retry, with each retry recorded for the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q03 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)'s quarantine automation.
- `pa11y-ci` configuration authored here but scheduled nightly by the deferred R1 backlog item E03-T12 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope).

## Out of scope
- Writing product E2E specs, contract fixtures or a11y assertions for features that do not exist yet - each feature epic adds its own.
- Load/perf (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q02 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)), chaos (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q03 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)), DAST (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-X04 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)).
