```gherkin
Scenario: Contract drift between server and OpenAPI fails
  Given a route in "services/api" returns a field absent from "docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml"
  When the contract job runs
  Then the job fails identifying the route and the offending field

Scenario: Integration suite runs fully offline
  Given the integration job executes with outbound network denied except loopback
  When the recorded-fixture pipeline suite runs
  Then all suites complete without any external network call
  And any attempt to reach "api.bybit.com" fails the job

Scenario: E2E failure produces a debuggable artifact
  Given a Playwright spec fails on the second retry
  When the e2e-web job finishes
  Then the trace, video and screenshot are uploaded as artifacts
  And the failure is recorded in the flake ledger

Scenario: A new serious axe violation blocks the merge
  Given a pull request introduces a button with no accessible name
  When the a11y-axe job runs
  Then it reports a serious violation and fails the check

Scenario: A missing integration fixture fails loudly
  Given the LFS pointer for a recorded WS session cannot be resolved
  When the integration job runs
  Then it fails with "fixture unavailable" instead of skipping the affected tests
```

## Technical notes / design
- Compose stack for integration/E2E is brought up by `docker compose -f compose.ci.yml up -d --wait` with digest-pinned images (SR-131); healthcheck-gated so tests never race startup.
- Sharding: `--shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4`; the resolver in `E03-T01` aggregates the four shard results into one `e2e-web` conclusion.
- Fixture integrity: each recorded fixture carries a SHA-256 recorded in `tests/fixtures/MANIFEST.sha256`, verified before use (a corrupted fixture silently changing golden outputs is worse than a missing one).
- Error codes: `CI-CON-001` contract drift, `CI-INT-001` fixture unavailable, `CI-INT-002` fixture checksum mismatch, `CI-E2E-001` spec failure after retry, `CI-A11Y-001` new serious/critical violation.

## Test plan
- Integration: one fixture PR per acceptance scenario.
- Meta-test: a deliberately corrupted fixture checksum must fail with `CI-INT-002`.
- Perf: the combined contract+integration+e2e path must fit the 15-minute p90 budget with sharding; measured and recorded.
- Coverage: this Task adds harness code under `tools/ci` (>=85%) and test configuration only.

## Security notes
- ADR-0012's "no test may contact `api.bybit.com`" rule is enforced here at the *job* level (network policy) in addition to the pytest guard from `E03-T03` - defence in depth.
- SR-140: no exchange credentials in these jobs; the compose stack uses generated ephemeral credentials.
- Artifacts (traces/videos) may capture UI state; they are retained 7 days and the retention is documented, since traces of an authenticated session can contain tokens (SR-146 spirit).

## Accessibility notes
This Task **is** the a11y enforcement mechanism: `a11y-axe` blocks on new serious/critical violations per `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the nightly `pa11y-ci` sweep across `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is configured here and scheduled in the deferred R1 backlog item E03-T12 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope). Validation of the harness itself is the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q05 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope).

## Performance notes
Budget: contract <= 3 min, integration <= 6 min, e2e-web (4 shards) <= 8 min wall clock; a11y-axe <= 3 min. Recorded in the job summary.

## Observability
Per-job durations, shard balance, retry counts and axe violation counts appended to `ci-metrics`.

title: Build the SAST, SCA, secrets, licence and container scanning lane
body:
## Context
The planning brief mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (Dependabot/pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning, DAST (ZAP) and container scanning (Trivy). `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 names `codeql`, `semgrep`, `bandit`, `pip-audit`, `npm-audit`, `gitleaks`, `license-scan` and `trivy` as required checks on `main`, and Ã‚Â§12.1 fixes each tool's cadence and blocking rule: gitleaks - any finding blocks; Trivy - High/Critical block; licence violations fail the build (SR-136). `30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4 sets the R0 threshold: "Zero Critical/High unresolved; Medium requires a dated accepted-risk entry".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-security.yml` composing, as separately-named checks: `codeql` (javascript-typescript + python), `semgrep` (registry rules + the custom `cv-*` rules from the deferred R1 backlog item E03-X02 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)), `bandit` (`services/api`), `pip-audit`, `npm-audit` (`--audit-level=high`), `gitleaks` (diff scope on PR), `license-scan`, `trivy` (filesystem on PR; images in `E03-T08`).
- `tools/ci/licenses-allowlist.json` encoding SR-136 exactly: allowed MIT, BSD-2/3, Apache-2.0, ISC, PSF, MPL-2.0, Unlicense/CC0; LGPL requires security+owner approval (build fails with a distinct "needs approval" code); GPL/AGPL/SSPL/BUSL/Commons Clause/non-commercial prohibited.
- Accepted-risk mechanism: `security/accepted-risks.yaml` entries keyed by finding id with `reason`, `approver`, `expires` (ISO date). An expired entry fails the build - an accepted risk without an expiry date is not accepted, it is forgotten.
- SARIF upload to GitHub code scanning for CodeQL/Semgrep/Trivy so findings are reviewable in one place.
- Dependabot configuration for pip, npm, Docker and GitHub Actions with security updates auto-opened (SR-134).
- Nightly full-history gitleaks scheduled by the deferred R1 backlog item E03-T12 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope) (configured here).


- **Scope delta from `E03-X01`'s STRIDE model (threat row R2, dependency confusion)**: the SCA/licence lane must also enforce an explicit registry-allowlist / internal-scope-reservation check for `@candleviewer/*` package names, not just generic SCA scanning — installing with a public-registry-only resolver for an internal name must fail closed rather than silently substituting a public package (`docs/plan/threat-models/E03-supply-chain.md` section 4.4, section 7 item 1).

## Out of scope
- Image signing/SBOM (`E03-T08`), ZAP DAST (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-X04 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)), the STRIDE model itself (`E03-X01`), authoring the `cv-*` rules (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-X02 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)), pen-test (R4/E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A planted synthetic secret blocks the merge
  Given a pull request adds a string matching an API-key pattern
  When the gitleaks job runs on the diff
  Then the job fails and the pull request cannot be merged

Scenario: A prohibited licence fails the build
  Given a dependency licensed "AGPL-3.0" enters the lockfile
  When the license-scan job evaluates the allowlist
  Then the job fails naming the package, its licence and the SR-136 clause

Scenario: A High-severity dependency advisory blocks
  Given pip-audit reports a High severity advisory for a runtime dependency
  And no accepted-risk entry exists for it
  When the security lane runs
  Then the job fails

Scenario: An expired accepted risk re-blocks
  Given an accepted-risk entry for finding "GHSA-xxxx" with expires "2026-09-27"
  And the pipeline runs on 2026-09-27
```

- gitleaks runs `--redact` so the finding is reported without reprinting the secret into CI logs (SR-146).
- Error codes: `CI-SEC-001` blocking finding, `CI-SEC-002` licence violation, `CI-SEC-003` LGPL needs approval, `CI-SEC-004` accepted risk expired, `CI-SEC-005` scanner infrastructure failure (distinct from "clean").
- Scanner infrastructure failure must **fail**, never pass-by-default - a scanner that silently errors is indistinguishable from a clean repository.

## Test plan
- Unit (>=85%): `security_gate.py` severity normalisation and accepted-risk expiry logic over fixture SARIF/JSON outputs from each tool.
- Integration: five fixture PRs, one per acceptance scenario, using synthetic dummy-prefixed secrets (SR-145) - never a real credential.
- Contract: SARIF schema validity asserted before upload.
- Coverage target: >=85% for `tools/ci`.

## Security notes
- Controls implemented: SR-132 (via `cv-unpinned-action`), SR-134 (Dependabot), SR-136 (licence policy), SR-142 (gitleaks PR + scheduled full history), SR-146 (redaction in logs).
- Threats addressed from `E03-X01`'s STRIDE: tampering with the build (T), information disclosure via committed secrets (I), elevation via a malicious dependency (E).
- Data classification: findings may reference sensitive paths; SARIF is uploaded to the private repository's code-scanning surface only.
- Review label: **required** - Security engineer sign-off gates Done.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. Findings summaries state severity in words, not colour.

## Performance notes
CodeQL dominates (~6-8 min); it runs in parallel with the other scanners and is path-filtered to code changes. Total security lane target <= 8 min wall clock, inside the p90 <= 15 min budget.

## Observability
Counts per tool per severity appended to `ci-metrics`; the accepted-risk register's next expiry date is surfaced in the job summary so it never silently rots.

title: Add the Alembic migration job with single-head, drift and expand/contract checks
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` Ã‚Â§9 states the rules: Alembic 1.13+ over SQLAlchemy 2.0 async metadata; *"Single linear history on `main` (no branching heads). `alembic heads` must return exactly one revision - enforced in CI"*; and schema drift is detected by comparing `alembic upgrade head` against `models.py` via `alembic check`. ADR-0013 rule 9 adds the operational constraint: *"Migrations are applied on boot under an advisory lock and must be backward-compatible for one release (expand/contract), so a rollback never requires a down-migration."* Two engineers branching migrations in the same sprint is the default outcome without this gate.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/_job-migrations.yml`, applicable when the `migrations` path filter is true (`services/api/**/alembic/**`, `services/api/**/models.py`).
- Checks: (1) `alembic heads` returns exactly one revision; (2) `alembic check` reports no drift between `models.py` and head; (3) `alembic upgrade head` succeeds from an empty database; (4) `alembic upgrade head` succeeds from the **previous release tag's** schema (upgrade-path test, not just greenfield); (5) `IF NOT EXISTS` is absent from migration files (`21-database-schema.md` Ã‚Â§: "`IF NOT EXISTS` is never used in migrations - Alembic owns state").
- **Expand/contract lint**: a migration containing a destructive operation (`drop_column`, `drop_table`, non-nullable `add_column` without a server default, type narrowing) must carry an explicit `# cv:contract-phase: <release>` annotation justifying it; otherwise the job fails. This mechanically enforces ADR-0013 rule 9.
- Boot-time advisory-lock application helper (`services/api` startup path) asserted by an integration test: two concurrent boots must serialise, with the loser waiting rather than racing.
- The migration job also runs in `main.yml` before the deploy stage so a bad migration never reaches a running environment (`E03-T09` dependency).

## Out of scope
- Writing the actual schema/migrations (owned by `E07` and each feature epic).
- QuestDB table definitions and Parquet layout drift checks (`E07`) - noted here so the boundary is explicit.
- Data backfills and retention jobs (`E07`, `E16`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Two migration heads block the merge
  Given two branches each added a migration from the same parent revision
  When both are merged and "alembic heads" is evaluated
  Then the job fails with "expected 1 head, found 2" and names both revisions

Scenario: Model drift is detected
  Given a column is added to "models.py" without a corresponding migration
  When "alembic check" runs
  Then the job fails describing the drifted table and column

Scenario: A destructive migration without a contract annotation fails
  Given a migration calls "op.drop_column" with no "cv:contract-phase" annotation
  When the expand/contract lint runs
  Then the job fails citing ADR-0013 rule 9

Scenario: Upgrade from the previous release succeeds
  Given a database restored to the schema of the previous release tag
  When "alembic upgrade head" runs
  Then it completes successfully with no manual intervention

Scenario: Concurrent boots serialise on the advisory lock
  Given two api containers start simultaneously against one database
  When both attempt to apply migrations
  Then exactly one applies them and the other waits and then starts normally
```

## Technical notes / design
- Upgrade-path test uses a schema snapshot artifact published at each release tag (`schema/<tag>.sql`), restored into a throwaway Postgres service container.
- Advisory lock: `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('cv_migrations'))` held for the duration of `upgrade head`, released on completion; a configurable `CV_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (default 300 s) turns a deadlock into a clear `CI-DEP-004`/startup error instead of a hang.
- Error codes: `CI-MIG-001` multiple heads, `CI-MIG-002` drift, `CI-MIG-003` destructive without annotation, `CI-MIG-004` upgrade-path failure, `CI-MIG-005` `IF NOT EXISTS` used.

## Test plan
- Unit (>=85%): the expand/contract lint over fixture migration files (destructive annotated, destructive unannotated, additive, ambiguous batch operations).
- Integration: a throwaway Postgres service container exercising greenfield upgrade, previous-release upgrade, and the concurrent-boot advisory-lock scenario.
- Contract: `alembic check` treated as the contract between `models.py` and the migration chain.
- Coverage target: >=85% for the lint tool and the startup helper.

## Security notes
- Migrations touch `api_keys` and audit tables in later epics; SR-tagged note per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Ã‚Â§4.1: any migration touching `api_keys` must preserve envelope encryption at rest - the lint flags such migrations for mandatory Security review by matching table names in `tools/ci/security-sensitive-tables.txt`.
- Append-only audit tables (E09) must never be altered destructively; they are listed as forbidden targets for `drop_*` regardless of annotation.
- CI uses ephemeral throwaway databases only; no production data, ever.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Migration job target <= 3 min. Long-running migrations are a deploy-latency risk; the lint warns when a migration adds an index without `CONCURRENTLY` on a table listed as large in `21-database-schema.md`.

## Observability
Job summary: head revision, applied revision count, upgrade duration per revision, lock wait time.

## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4 lists, as a blocking R0 quality gate owned by the Security engineer: *"STRIDE models complete for E03 (supply chain), E08 (exchange boundary), E09 (auth/RBAC)"*. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Ã‚Â§2.1 requires the STRIDE kickoff to be scheduled at Epic DoR for any epic touching the build path. `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§5 already names the boundary - **TB-8: Upstream packages/CI -> runtime**, with controls "Lockfiles, hash pinning, SBOM, Trivy, signed container images, pinned action SHAs, protected `main` (SR-130..SR-139)" - and AC-11 names the actor "Dependency / package author: External, Untrusted, Ships code into our build". This ticket turns that one-line boundary into an enumerated model that tells `E03-T07`, `E03-T08`, `E03-T13` and the deferred R1 backlog item E03-T14 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope) what they must actually stop.

This must land **early** (Sprint 01) - a threat model delivered after the pipeline is built is a review, not a model.

## Scope / Deliverables

title: Design the system-health, incident-log and degraded-state surfaces (SCR-143, SCR-144, SCR-152, SCR-156)
body:
## Context
E04 defines the data contracts that four user-facing surfaces consume, and under the design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` — design runs ≥2 sprints ahead; no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off) those surfaces must be designed now, in R0, even though they are built later in E42/E10. Designing them alongside the API is also the only way to catch contract gaps early: SCR-143's requirement that *"the page works when the backend is partially down"* is a design constraint that shapes E04-T04's per-component `last_good_at` and independent-probe-timeout behaviour.

Surfaces in scope (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`):
- **SCR-143** Admin: system health (US-ADMIN-011, US-OBS-001, US-OBS-002)
- **SCR-144** Admin: incident / connectivity log (US-OBS-003, US-OBS-006)
- **SCR-152** Disconnected / reconnecting state (US-OBS-004, US-POS-008, US-MKT-007)
- **SCR-156** Application error boundary (US-OBS-003, US-OBS-007)

## Scope / Deliverables
- **UX research (light, 1 session)**: interview the owner on incident triage — what is the first question asked when something feels wrong, and what "still safe" means to them while degraded. This directly determines tile ordering on SCR-143 and the wording of the outage state.
- **Wireframes → hi-fi in Figma** for all four screens, covering every state named in the catalogue:
  - SCR-143: all-green · degraded (per-subsystem amber with reason + last-good timestamp) · outage (red, ongoing incident, what is still safe — e.g. "Native stops on the exchange are unaffected") · maintenance window.
  - SCR-144: open vs resolved · filters by subsystem/severity/date · expandable detail rows · acknowledge action · export · empty state · trading-impact correlation ("12 orders rejected during this window") where derivable.
  - SCR-152: reconnect overlay states incl. retry-exhausted.
  - SCR-156: crash boundary with correlation id and a route to support-bundle generation (US-OBS-007).
- **Design-system contributions** to E05: **CMP-178** SystemHealthTile (Ok/Warning/Danger + sparkline), **CMP-210** HealthChips, **CMP-092** DegradedModeBanner, **CMP-076** ConnectionStatus, **CMP-077** ReconnectOverlay, **CMP-207** BuildFooter — specs, tokens, states and Storybook story lists, filed as design-system entries rather than one-off screens (DoR §3.1).
- **Motion spec**: state transitions between healthy/degraded/down must be legible but never attention-grabbing enough to be muted by the operator; define reduced-motion equivalents.
- **Content design**: the state vocabulary (`ok`/`warning`/`degraded`/`down`/`not deployed`) used identically in the API (E04-T04), the chips, the tiles and the alert notifications (E04-T05) — one vocabulary, defined once.
- **Handoff pack**: redlines, token references, the component-to-API field mapping (each tile → `HealthReport.components[].{state,latency_ms,detail,last_good_at}`), and the empty/loading/error matrix.

## Out of scope
- Building the screens (E42 Admin, E10 App shell).
- Grafana dashboard visual design — a third-party surface, configured not designed (E04-S01).
- Any Android/mobile layout (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the SCR-143 design is presented for sign-off
When it is checked against the screen's design sign-off acceptance checklist in 14-screens-catalogue.md
Then every listed item is satisfied: tiles for ingestion lag, public WS, private WS per account, REST latency, recorder, DB tiers, rule engine, algo engine and chart-engine FPS; each tile showing a number with units plus a state word; degraded and down states drawn per tile with what the user should expect to stop working; a historical sparkline per tile with a table alternative; a link to the incident log; and a layout that works when the backend is partially down

Given any health state is rendered
When a colour-blind simulation and a greyscale render are applied
Then the state remains unambiguous, because state is always a word and a value, never a dot colour alone

Given the SCR-144 design is reviewed
Then columns include time, subsystem, severity (as text), message, duration and resolution; long messages expand into a detail row rather than truncating silently; and open/resolved, filter, acknowledge, export and empty states are all drawn

Given a designer hands off to engineering
Then every visual element maps to a named field of the HealthReport or Incident schema in 22-api-openapi.yaml, and any field the design needs that does not yet exist is filed as a comment on E04-T04 before sign-off

Given the design is signed off
Then sign-off is recorded by the CDO or delegate with the date, and the ticket Status is Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming frontend story starts
```

## Technical notes / design
The defining constraint is that this screen is read when the system is unwell: every tile must resolve independently (no shared loading gate), and the page must degrade to "I could not reach the backend, here is the last thing I knew and when" rather than to a spinner. Design the *unreachable-backend* variant first and the all-green variant last — the reverse order produces a beautiful dashboard that is blank exactly when it is needed.

Density follows the design-system density tokens (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`); this is an information-dense operator screen, so use the compact density variant but verify touch/click target minimums still meet WCAG 2.2 AA target-size guidance.

## Test plan
- Design QA is a separate ticket (E04-D02); this ticket's verification is the per-screen sign-off checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md` plus a contrast/colour-blind pass on every state.
- Prototype test: one moderated walkthrough with the owner using a clickable prototype of the degraded and outage states, confirming they can answer "what is broken, what is still safe, what do I do" in under 30 s.

## Security notes
The designs must not surface secret material or full account identifiers: account references on SCR-143/SCR-147-adjacent tiles use a truncated opaque id (per SR-005, no more than the first 4 characters of a key id may ever be shown). The incident log's detail rows must be designed assuming the underlying `system_events.details` is operator-visible but must never be designed to show raw exchange payloads verbatim. Support-bundle generation from SCR-156 must be designed as an explicit, confirmed, audited action — not a one-click background side effect.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). Specific commitments: each subsystem is a labelled row/tile with a text status (SCR-143 a11y note — "no reliance on dot colour"); every sparkline has a table alternative; severity in SCR-144 is text; the reconnect overlay (CMP-077) is `role="alertdialog"`, non-dismissible with a keyboard-operable retry and no false "OK" affordance; status regions announce at most once per state change, not per heartbeat (CMP-076 announcement-throttling contract); focus order and visible focus states specified; contrast ≥4.5:1 for text and ≥3:1 for state indicators in all three themes (dark, light, high-contrast).

## Performance notes
Design within SCR-143's budget: tiles subscribe to the WS `system` topic at 1 Hz and the page must stay under 2 ms scripting per frame; SCR-144 must scroll 10k rows without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame, so the design must assume row virtualisation and avoid per-row animation or shadow effects that defeat it.

## Observability
Specify the analytics/audit events the screens emit, matching the catalogue: `health.diagnostics_exported` (audited), `incident.log_viewed`, `incident.exported`, `incident.acknowledged` (audited).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Hi-fi Figma frames for all four screens, all states, all three themes.
- [ ] Per-screen sign-off checklists in `14-screens-catalogue.md` fully satisfied.
- [ ] Design-system entries for CMP-076, CMP-077, CMP-092, CMP-178, CMP-207, CMP-210 accepted by the design-system team into E05's backlog.
- [ ] Motion + reduced-motion specs included.
- [ ] Content/state vocabulary agreed with backend (E04-T04) and alerting (E04-T05).
- [ ] Handoff pack published with component↔API field mapping; engineering walkthrough held.
- [ ] a11y pre-review passed with the accessibility specialist (contrast, non-colour-redundancy, focus, announcements).
- [ ] CDO (or delegate) sign-off recorded with date; Status Done ≥2 sprints before the consuming E42/E10 story starts.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if the design diverged from the written spec.

## Dependencies
`E05-D01` (Build Figma Foundations file: token variables for the three themes) — the token variables must exist to design these frames against. The dependency is pinned to that specific ticket rather than the whole `E05` epic, because only the Foundations file is actually required.

**Why Sprint 01, outside E04's S02–S03 roadmap window.** `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` requires a design ticket to land **two sprints before the consuming FE story**. The consumers here are `E04-T04` (health / readiness contract) and `E04-S01` (Grafana + system-health surfaces) in Sprint 03, plus the shared degraded-state surfaces reused by E42 and E10. Sprint 01 is therefore the scheduled-correct slot: it sits immediately *preceding* E04's declared train window rather than inside it, which is intentional and is recorded in the sprint-window reconciliation table on the `E04` epic ticket.

**Same-sprint dependency risk and its mitigation.** `E05-D01` is also Sprint 01, so this is a same-sprint dependency. It is accepted with these controls: (a) this ticket only needs the colour / spacing / type primitives, which `E05-D01` publishes as draft variables in the first half of the sprint, so the two run staggered inside one sprint rather than in parallel from day one; (b) no code depends on this ticket until Sprint 03, so a one-sprint slip of `E05-D01` pushes this ticket to Sprint 02 and still clears `E04-T04` without moving the train; (c) any token added or renamed later by `E05-D02` (Sprint 02) is re-applied to these frames during `E04-D02` design QA in Sprint 03, which is the formal sign-off gate. Escalation: if `E05-D01` has not published draft variables by the Sprint-01 midpoint, the epic owner re-plans this ticket into Sprint 02.

Informs and is informed by `E04-T04` (health contract); any field missing from the health payload is raised on that ticket before sign-off.

`design/obs-health-surfaces` (Figma is the artefact; the branch carries catalogue doc updates)

title: Measure instrumentation overhead: metrics, structlog and OTel on the hot paths
body:
## Context
ADR-0014 (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md`) asserts that tracing market-data hot loops "would distort the very loop it measures", and US-OBS-002 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28) carries the NFR *measurement overhead ≤1% CPU*. Both are currently assertions, not measurements. Before E04-T03/T06 harden the instrumentation API we need numbers, because retro-fitting a cheaper metrics facade after twenty modules have adopted it is expensive.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. Not expected to produce production-shippable code; the harness may be promoted into `tests/perf/` if it is clean.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A synthetic hot-loop harness: 20 000 messages/s through a parse → transform → emit pipeline, mirroring the ingestion shape of `20-architecture.md` §12.1 (`ws_messages_total`, `topic_staleness_seconds`, `ingest_queue_depth`).
- Four measured configurations: (a) no instrumentation, (b) Prometheus counters/histograms only, (c) b + structlog JSON at INFO with the redaction processor, (d) c + OpenTelemetry spans at 100% and at 1% sampling.
- Comparison of `prometheus_client` vs a pre-bound-label fast path (label lookup hoisted out of the loop).
- Measurement of `contextvars` propagation cost across `asyncio.create_task` at the same rate.
- Written findings appended to ADR-0014 as an addendum, plus follow-up tickets if any configuration breaches 1% CPU.

## Out of scope
- Choosing the alerting or dashboard stack (already decided in ADR-0014).
- Any real Bybit connection — the harness is synthetic and offline.
- Frontend telemetry overhead (measured in E04-T06 against the real engine).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overhead quantified per configuration
  Given the harness runs each of the four configurations for 120 s at 20k msg/s
  When results are collected
  Then CPU%, p50/p95/p99 per-message latency and RSS are recorded per configuration with at least 3 repeats and their variance stated

Scenario: Decision criteria applied
  Given configuration (b) exceeds 1% CPU over baseline
  Then the pre-bound-label fast path is adopted as the mandatory pattern in the metrics facade and E04-T03 is updated to enforce it

Scenario: Tracing decision confirmed or overturned
  Given configuration (d) at 100% sampling exceeds 5% CPU over baseline
  Then ADR-0014's "metrics only on market-data hot loops" stands and is recorded as measured rather than assumed; otherwise an addendum records that hot-loop tracing is affordable at the stated sampling rate
```

## Technical notes / design
Run on the reference VPS profile named in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3 (4 vCPU / 8 GB), not on the dev workstation, because backend budgets are set against the smaller profile. Measure CPU with `resource.getrusage` deltas plus `psutil` sampling; avoid `time.time()` in the inner loop (use `time.perf_counter_ns` on a sampled 1-in-N basis). Beware of the classic false result: a histogram with a label tuple computed inside the loop is dominated by dict hashing, not by the observation — measure both shapes explicitly.

## Test plan
Not a production ticket; the deliverable is evidence. The harness itself gets a smoke test asserting it produces the expected message count so a broken run is not mistaken for a fast one.

## Security notes
The harness must use synthetic payloads only — no real API keys, no recorded private-WS fixtures. If the redaction processor is exercised, use obviously fake secrets with a distinctive canary prefix.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface.

## Performance notes
The whole point: budget is ≤1% CPU for instrumentation (US-OBS-002 NFR) and the backend-internal latency envelope is ≤20 ms p95 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budget #6) — instrumentation must not consume a measurable slice of that.

## Observability
N/A — this spike measures observability rather than adding it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Numbers recorded in the ticket with hardware profile, repeat count and variance.
- [ ] ADR-0014 addendum merged (even if the outcome is "no change").
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path is chosen, linking these findings.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.
- [ ] Harness branch promoted to `tests/perf/` or explicitly marked throwaway.

## Dependencies
`E03` — needs a runnable containerised environment and a CI runner profile to measure against.

## Branch

title: Design system v0 - tokens, primitives, Storybook
body:
## Context
CandleViewer is a dense, dark-first, desktop-only professional trading terminal. Every R1+ screen (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`) must be assembled from tokens and shared primitives rather than bespoke CSS, otherwise the 238 catalogued components (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md#8-summary-tallies`) drift into 238 one-off styles and WCAG 2.2 AA conformance (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`) becomes unverifiable. E05 delivers **design system v0**: the three-tier token model, the Style Dictionary build with its six output targets, the three themes (dark / light / high-contrast), the two density modes, the R0/R1-critical atoms and molecules, Storybook with the a11y addon in CI, and a visual-regression baseline.

E05 is design-led and runs the full R0 window S01-S04 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#42-scope-epics`). It gates E10 (App shell & Electron wrapper) in the epic dependency graph (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#111-epic-dependency-graph`: `E05 --> E10`) and is itself gated by E02 (monorepo scaffold, `packages/ui`) and E03 (CI jobs hosting the a11y / visual-regression / contrast gates).

Product framing comes from the SET story domain (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#27-set--settings-hotkeys-themes`): US-SET-004 (themes and density), US-SET-005 (colour conventions / CVD-safe palettes) and US-SET-007 (accessibility preferences) are the Must stories whose *system-level* foundations live here. Their settings screens (SCR-116 Appearance & density, SCR-117 Accessibility) are built by the later settings epic; the tokens, theme engine, density engine, reduced-motion primitives and preview primitives those screens consume are E05 deliverables.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Tokens**: `packages/ui/tokens/*.tokens.json` - Tier-1 primitive, Tier-2 semantic, Tier-3 component tokens per `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#2-token-architecture`; colour, typography, spacing, radii, elevation, motion.
- **Token build**: Style Dictionary config with the six binding output targets (`build/css/tokens.{dark,light,high-contrast}.css`, `build/ts/tokens.ts`, `build/engine/theme-uniforms.json`, `build/electron/tokens.main.json`, `build/reports/contrast-matrix.{json,md}`) per `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#11-handoff-spec-tokens-json--code`.
- **Theme + density runtime**: `ThemeProvider`, `data-theme` / `data-density` root attributes, instant no-reload swap, `prefers-reduced-motion` + explicit in-app override, theme-change event consumed later by the WebGL engine.
- **Components** (R0/R1-critical subset of `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`): atoms CMP-001..CMP-039, molecules CMP-040..CMP-050, CMP-054, CMP-059, CMP-062, CMP-063, CMP-065, CMP-069, plus CMP-079 RbacGate, CMP-085 SkipLink, CMP-089 ForbiddenState, CMP-090 NotFoundState, CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback, CMP-228 PreviewTile.
- **Storybook 8** with `@storybook/addon-a11y`, theme + density toolbar switchers, test-runner in CI (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`).
- **Visual-regression baseline** across variant x theme(3) x density(2).
- **Contrast-matrix CI gate** (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text/chart ink, 7:1 `.hc` buy/sell).
- **Icon registry** incl. trading-domain custom icons (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#5-iconography`).
- **ADR-0016** design-token architecture & theming.
- Design tickets (UX research, Figma Foundations + component library, motion spec, a11y/CVD sign-off, design QA, handoff), QA tickets (component test plan, a11y audit, VR regression pack + sign-off), security tickets (STRIDE, security review).

## Out of scope
- Android / mobile / responsive breakpoints below 1280x800 (locked out, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`).
- Settings screens SCR-110..SCR-119 themselves (later settings epic) - E05 ships only the primitives they consume.
- Trading-specific components CMP-100..CMP-139, rule-engine CMP-140..CMP-159, watchlist/journal CMP-160..CMP-179, chart primitives CMP-180..CMP-199 (E11+ epics).
- App shell organisms CMP-070..CMP-084 and CMP-086/CMP-087 layouts (E10) - E05 supplies their tokens and atoms only.
- Final brand skin: the system is brand-neutral; colour/logo swap is a later token-only change.
- Options/GEX, mobile, separate admin app - out of product scope entirely.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Design system v0 published
  Given R0 exit criterion 8 (docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#43-exit-criteria)
  When Storybook is built from main
  Then tokens are published, at least 25 components have stories, axe-core reports zero serious/critical violations
  And dark, light and high-contrast themes are each selectable and rendered
Scenario: Instant theme swap
  Given any Storybook story or app surface is open
  When the theme is switched
  Then every surface updates within one frame with no reload and no component remount
Scenario: Contrast gate blocks a bad token
  Given a PR lowers color.text.secondary lightness below 4.5:1 on surface.app
  When CI runs the contrast-matrix check
  Then the build fails and names the offending token pair
Scenario: No hardcoded values
  When the lint rule forbidding raw hex/px in packages/ui runs
  Then it reports zero violations outside tokens/ source files
Scenario: Density is spacing-only
  Given any catalogued component story
  When density switches from compact to comfortable
  Then the DOM structure is identical and only spacing/row-height values differ
```

## Technical notes / design
- Package: `packages/ui` (pnpm workspace, created by E02). Public entry exports components plus generated `tokens.ts` typings; no app state, no `fetch`, no Bybit knowledge (CONSTITUTION module-edge rules enforced by `import-linter`/ESLint boundaries).
- Token naming `category.subcategory.variant.state` maps 1:1 to `--color-text-buy` CSS custom properties and to Figma Variables names, so design/code diffs are mechanical.
- Themes are token re-pointing, never new token names. Light is separately tuned, not an inversion.
- Density selects which spacing scale steps the component aliases resolve to; component structure never branches on density.
- Custom Style Dictionary formats `json/flat-rgba` and `json/flat` live in `tools/style-dictionary/formats/`.

## Test plan
Rolled up from children: Vitest unit tests per component (props/variants/states), Storybook interaction tests (play functions) via the Storybook test runner, `vitest-axe` per story, visual-regression snapshots per variant x theme x density, contrast-matrix script unit tests, and a Playwright smoke that switches theme/density on the Storybook docs page. Coverage target >=80% lines on `packages/ui` (frontend threshold, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`).

## Security notes
Low intrinsic risk (no secrets, no PII, no money movement, data classification: public/internal). Real threats are **supply chain** (Storybook, Style Dictionary, icon library dependency tree - typosquat/compromised package executing at build time), **published Storybook exposure** (must remain Tailscale-only per `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`), and **CSP regressions** from inline-style token injection. Covered by E05-X01 (STRIDE) and E05-X02 (review). Security label required at epic level.

## Accessibility notes
E05 is the epic that makes WCAG 2.2 AA achievable downstream: focus-ring token >=3:1 against every surface tier, 24x24px compact minimum target with documented essential-exceptions, colour-never-alone enforcement, motion-safe/motion-reduce pairs, and CVD-safe buy/sell pairs (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 4, 5, 7, 11). Gate: axe-core zero serious/critical across all stories plus Accessibility-role sign-off (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#13-design-ahead-process--sign-off-definition`).

## Performance notes
Theme/density switch must complete within one frame (<=16.6 ms) and must never remount panels or drop a WebGL context (SCR-116 Performance, `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`). Token CSS bundle <=40 KB gzipped per theme. Storybook CI job <=10 min so the R0 "commit to dev deploy <=15 min" pipeline budget holds.

## Observability
Analytics events defined here and emitted by downstream settings screens: `appearance.theme_changed`, `appearance.density_changed`, `appearance.font_size_changed`, `appearance.chart_palette_changed`, `a11y.preference_changed`. CI publishes the contrast-matrix report and VR diff artifacts per PR.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion 8 demonstrably met (Storybook published, >=25 components, zero axe violations, 3 themes).
- [ ] Coverage >=80% on `packages/ui`; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged; `16-design-system-brief.md` and `15-component-catalogue.md` updated to shipped reality.
- [ ] CDO design sign-off recorded (R0 quality gate "Design", `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#44-quality-gates`).
- [ ] Accessibility-role sign-off recorded; manual screen-reader pass on the exemplar stories.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present; SCA/secrets scan clean.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at a Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E02` - `packages/ui` workspace, toolchain, lint/test runners (`E02 --> E05`).
- `blocked_by: E03` - CI jobs that host the Storybook/a11y/VR/contrast gates.
- Blocks `E10` (app shell & Electron wrapper) and transitively every R1 screen epic.

## Branch
`feat/design-system-<short>` per child ticket; PRs <=400 LOC; the `tokens/` directory is versioned independently with its own CHANGELOG.

## Risks
- **R5 Scope**: 238 catalogued components invite scope creep; v0 is deliberately limited to the R0/R1-critical atoms/molecules subset listed above.
- **R8 Browser/GPU compat**: theme tokens must reach the WebGL engine as uniforms; an incompatible output format would stall E11. Mitigated by shipping `theme-uniforms.json` in T01 and validating with the E06 prototype.
- **R2 Render performance**: a theme swap that remounts panels would drop GL contexts mid-session; explicitly tested in T02.
- **Design-ahead slip**: if D01/D02 slip past S02, S01..S04 cannot start Ready. Tracked as the epic's top schedule risk.


## Design-ahead waiver (Architect + CDO, recorded 2026-09-14)
E05 is the *design-system epic itself*: its "design" tickets (E05-D01/D02/D03/D06) and its "engineering" tickets are produced by the same co-located design-system pod inside a single 4-sprint R0 window (S01-S04, `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#42-scope-epics`), so the normal ">=2 sprints Done-before-consumption" gap of `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (Team & cadence) and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1 cannot be satisfied without pushing E05 past the R0 train and blocking E10 and every R1 screen epic.

**Waiver scope (explicit, time-boxed, R0-only):** the 1-sprint gap on the following intra-epic design->code edges only:
- E05-D01 (Done S01) -> E05-T01 (S02)
- E05-D02 (Done S02) -> E05-S01 (S03), E05-T06 (S03)
- E05-D03 (Done S02) -> E05-T02 (S03)
- E05-D06 (Done S02) -> E05-S01 (S03)

**Granted by:** Architect and Chief Design Officer. **Reason:** foundational bootstrap epic; design and implementation share one pod and one Figma/token source of truth; no external design consumer exists in R0.
**Compensating controls:** (a) design-token handoff is mechanical (Figma Variables names == token names, E05-D06), so late design churn is a token-value diff, not a component rewrite; (b) E05-D05 design QA and E05-D04 a11y/CVD sign-off run in S04 before the epic closes; (c) any component whose Figma spec is not Done at the start of its implementation sprint is descoped from v0 rather than implemented speculatively; (d) E05-S02/S03/S04 (S04) already satisfy the full >=2-sprint rule against E05-D02.
**Expiry:** this waiver does NOT extend past R0. All R1+ screen epics consume E05 design output with the full >=2-sprint gap (E05 design artefacts are Done by S02/S04, R1 starts S05).

## Estimate reconciliation (roadmap vs backlog)
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` lines 105 and 188 carried **34 pts** for E05. The decomposed backlog totals **38 engineering points** (Story+Task+Spike, excluding design/QA/security discipline tickets) and **78 points all-in** across all 24 children. The 34 figure was a pre-decomposition T-shirt estimate that omitted E05-T06 (icon registry, 2) and under-counted the molecule band (E05-S03, 5 vs 3). The roadmap has been updated to **38 pts** to match this backlog; the backlog is the source of truth and the epic `estimate` field (78) is the all-in rollup of every child. Breakdown:
- Engineering (Story/Task/Spike): 38 = S01 8 + S02 5 + S03 5 + S04 3 + T01 5 + T02 3 + T03 2 + T04 2 + T05 1 + T06 2 + T07 1 + K01 1 (design-discipline Tasks D01/D02/D03/D06/D07 excluded).
- Design discipline (D01-D07): 27. QA (Q01-Q03): 9. Security (X01-X02): 4.
- All-in rollup: 78 (epic `estimate`). R0 capacity impact is unchanged: 38 engineering pts spread over S01-S04 against a ~90 pts/sprint team velocity.


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Build Figma Foundations file: token variables for 3 themes x 2 densities
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#10-figma-library-structure--naming` mandates a `CandleViewer - Foundations` Figma file holding a Figma Variable for every Tier-1/Tier-2 token, named identically to the code token names so the Figma-to-code diff is mechanical rather than interpretive. This file is the design-side source of truth that E05-T01 converts into `tokens/*.tokens.json`. Without it, engineers invent token names and the design/code split becomes permanent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Figma file `CandleViewer - Foundations` with Variable Collections: `Color` (modes: Dark, Light, HighContrast), `Typography`, `Spacing`, `Radius`, `Elevation`, `Motion`, `Density` (modes: Compact, Comfortable).
- Tier-1 primitives: full neutral ladder (`surface.app`, `surface.raised`, `surface.overlay`, `surface.canvas`), palettes for green/red/blue/amber families.
- Tier-2 semantic tokens: `color.text.*`, `color.surface.*`, `color.border.*`, `color.action.primary[.hover/.active/.disabled]`, `color.buy`, `color.sell`, `color.buy.hc`, `color.sell.hc`, `color.neutral`, `color.status.{success,warning,danger,info}.{subtle,default,strong}`, `color.env.demo`, `color.env.live`, `color.focus.ring`.
- Chart-facing tokens: `color.candle.up/down`, `color.footprint.bid/ask/imbalance`, `color.profile.bar/poc/valuearea`, `color.drawing.default/selected`, `color.order.line`, `color.position.entry/sl/tp`, `color.node.{trigger,condition,action,logic,comment}`, and both heatmap ramps at 6 stops each.
- Typography: `font.family.ui`, `font.family.mono`, `font.size.{2xs,xs,sm,base,md,lg,xl,2xl}`, `font.lineHeight.{tight,normal,relaxed}`, `font.weight.{regular,medium,semibold,bold}`, `font.feature.tabularNums`.
- Spacing `space.{0,1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,32,48,64}` plus component aliases `space.button.paddingX`, `space.field.gap`, `space.row.height.compact/comfortable`.
- `radius.{none,xs,sm,md,lg,xl,pill,circle}`, `elevation.{0..5}`, `motion.duration.{instant,fast,normal,slow}`, `motion.easing.{standard,decelerate,accelerate}`.
- A 'token proof' page rendering a sample positions row, DOM ladder row and footprint cell under every theme x density combination.

## Out of scope
- Component construction (E05-D02).
- Screens (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` Screens file, later epics).
- Icon drawing (E05-T06 / its design counterpart is folded into D02).
- Brand identity/logo.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every semantic token exists in all three colour modes
  Given the Color collection
  When any Tier-2 token is inspected
  Then it resolves to a value in Dark, Light and HighContrast modes with no unset mode
Scenario: Naming matches code exactly
  Given a Figma Variable named color/text/buy
  Then the corresponding code token is color.text.buy and no design-only alternative name exists
Scenario: Light is tuned, not inverted
  Given the Light mode palette
  When candle and heatmap colours are compared to a naive lightness inversion of Dark
  Then they differ, and each still clears its contrast minimum on the light surface
Scenario: Danger is not confusable with sell
  Given color.status.danger.default and color.sell in each mode
  Then their hues are visibly distinct under normal vision and under deuteranopia simulation
Scenario: Token proof page
  When the proof page is switched across 3 themes x 2 densities
  Then all six combinations render legibly with no clipped text and no unset variable
```

## Technical notes / design
Author dark-first; derive light and high-contrast by re-pointing the same alias names at different primitives - never by introducing new names (`16-design-system-brief.md#4`). High-contrast swaps body text and buy/sell to `.hc` variants (>=7:1). Background is `#0B0E11` not pure black and primary text `#E8EAED` not pure white per the halation guidance in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#55`. Heatmap ramps interpolated in OKLCH. Export path: Tokens Studio plugin -> `tokens/*.tokens.json` PR, the direction defined in `16-design-system-brief.md#11` ('design -> code primary, code -> design reverse sync for engineering-discovered tokens').

## Test plan
Design verification only: the token proof page is the test surface. Every colour pair introduced here is re-checked automatically by E05-T05's contrast matrix once exported; a failing pair returns to this ticket for re-tuning rather than being waived.

## Security notes
No secrets. Figma file access restricted to the design org and named engineers; no public share links (a public Foundations link leaks product direction). Data classification: internal.

## Accessibility notes
Binding: `color.focus.ring` validated >=3:1 against every surface tier individually, not once globally. Text tokens >=4.5:1 on their intended surfaces, chart ink >=3:1 on `surface.canvas`, `.hc` buy/sell >=7:1. CVD pairs come from E05-D07. Accessibility role reviews before sign-off.

## Performance notes
Token count is deliberately bounded: density is expressed by alias resolution, not by a second parallel spacing scale, keeping the generated CSS bundle under the 40 KB gzipped per-theme budget set at epic level.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma Foundations file published as a library.
- [ ] Every collection/mode complete; zero unset variables (checked via the Figma variables panel export).
- [ ] Token proof page approved by the Accessibility role and the CDO.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` section 2 updated where final values differ from the brief.
- [ ] Downstream tickets E05-T01 and E05-D02 linked and moved to Ready.
- [ ] Design-ahead: Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming FE stories (E05-S01 in Sprint 03).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E05-D07` - density values, mono face and CVD pairs are inputs. Blocks E05-T01 (token JSON) and E05-D02 (components need published variables).

## Branch
`design/design-system-foundations` (docs amendments only; the artefact lives in Figma).

## References
- docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md sections 2, 4, 5, 10, 11
- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md sections 4, 5
- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md section 0.3


## Agent execution brief

2. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md sections 4, 5

**Repo paths to create/modify**

**Commands**

**Branch & PR**

- PR title: "E05-D01: Build Figma Foundations file: token variables for 3 themes x 2 densities"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/frontend
- Labels: type/design, area/design-system, priority/p0, design

**Done means**

- Every collection/mode complete; zero unset variables (checked via the Figma variables panel export).
- Token proof page approved by the Accessibility role and the CDO.

- Downstream tickets E05-T01 and E05-D02 linked and moved to Ready.
- Design-ahead: Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming FE stories (E05-S01 in Sprint 03).

**Do NOT**
- Component construction (E05-D02).
- Screens (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` Screens file, later epics).
- Icon drawing (E05-T06 / its design counterpart is folded into D02).
- Brand identity/logo.
- No new top-level directories outside the fixed monorepo layout (AGENTS.md §2) without an ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. title: UX research: density, numeric legibility and CVD palette validation
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#1-design-principles` locks 'legibility of numbers over decoration' and 'density is a mode, not a compromise', and `#3-density-modes` proposes compact 24px / comfortable 36px row heights. Those numbers, the mono numeric family choice, and the two colour-blind-safe buy/sell pairs required by `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#4-colour-independence-for-buysell-and-all-status-signalling` are currently **proposals, not validated findings**. Because every downstream component (CMP-001..CMP-238) resolves its spacing and colour from these decisions, validating them once here is far cheaper than re-tuning 238 components later. US-SET-004 (themes and density, Must) and US-SET-005 (colour conventions / CVD-safe palettes, Must) depend on the outcome.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated sessions with the Owner and the account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) on scanning speed for a positions grid and a DOM ladder at compact vs comfortable row heights.
- Numeric legibility test: candidate `font.family.mono` faces (tabular-figure UI variant vs dedicated mono) at `font.size.xs`/`sm` on `surface.app` and `surface.canvas`.
- CVD validation: simulate deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia over the two candidate `color.buy`/`color.sell` pairs plus the two heatmap ramps (`heatmap.convention.green-bid-red-ask`, `heatmap.convention.red-bid-green-ask`).
- Confirm or revise: compact row height, compact field height, the 24x24px minimum-target essential-exception list, default density per surface class.
- Output: research report in `docs/research/` plus a decisions block appended to `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#3-density-modes`, feeding E05-D01 and E05-T01.

## Out of scope
- No Figma component production (that is E05-D01/E05-D02).
- No code.
- No mobile/responsive research (desktop-only, locked).
- No brand/visual-identity exploration.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Density decision is evidence-backed
  Given at least 3 participant sessions covering positions-grid and DOM-ladder scanning
  When the report is published
  Then compact and comfortable row/field heights are stated as final values with the measured rationale
  And any deviation from the brief's 24px/36px proposal is recorded as a brief amendment
Scenario: CVD pairs validated
  Given the candidate buy/sell pairs and both heatmap ramps
  When each is run through deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulation
  Then exactly two buy/sell pairs are recommended as CVD-safe with simulation screenshots attached
  And any ramp stop that becomes indistinguishable from its neighbour under simulation is flagged for re-tuning
Scenario: Essential-exception list produced
  Given compact-mode controls that cannot reach 24x24px without breaking information density
  When the report is published
  Then each such control is listed by CMP-* id with its compensating control (click-tolerance padding, adjacent spacing)
  And any control not on this list must meet 24x24px unconditionally
Scenario: Mono face is decided
  When legibility results are compared
  Then one font.family.mono candidate is selected, or the decision is explicitly deferred with the blocking question named
```

## Technical notes / design
Method: moderated task-based sessions (find-the-largest-loss, find-the-price-level) timed and error-counted; the stimulus is a static high-fidelity mock, not a build. CVD simulation via a Figma plugin plus an offline pass using a CIELAB-based simulation script so results are reproducible in CI later. Heatmap ramps are evaluated in OKLCH/CIELAB interpolation as required by `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#6-data-viz-rules` rule 2 - naive RGB lerp is explicitly rejected and must not be used to produce the stimuli.

## Test plan
N/A for automated tests. Verification is peer review of the report by the Accessibility role and the CDO; the CVD simulation script is handed to E05-T05 as the seed for the automated contrast/CVD check.

## Security notes
No secrets, no PII beyond participant first names - store session notes without identifying details. Data classification: internal. No security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is itself an accessibility input: its CVD findings are a binding input to `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#42` conformance and to the contrast-matrix thresholds. At least one participant session should include a participant using increased OS text scale to sanity-check the 125%/200% zoom reflow assumption.

## Performance notes
N/A - no runtime component. Density findings indirectly affect the number of rendered rows per viewport and therefore the R1 grid performance budget in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability

title: Select visual-regression tooling for theme x density snapshot coverage
body:
## Context
R0 exit criterion 8 and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#42-scope-epics` call for a 'visual-regression baseline (Chromatic-style or Playwright screenshots)'. The choice is left open in the roadmap and must be closed before E05-T04 builds the baseline, because the two options differ in cost model, CI runtime, review workflow and self-hosting constraints (the project is Tailscale-only, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Timebox: 2 days.
- Evaluate: (a) Chromatic (hosted SaaS), (b) Playwright `toHaveScreenshot` against committed PNG baselines, (c) Storybook test-runner + `jest-image-snapshot` equivalent.
- Criteria: CI wall-clock for ~60 stories x 3 themes x 2 densities; flake rate across two identical runs; reviewer workflow for accepting an intentional diff; cost; whether snapshots/artefacts leave the private network; storage growth in git for committed baselines.
- Produce a comparison table with measured numbers and a recommendation.
- Record the decision as an ADR under `docs/plan/27-adrs/`.

## Out of scope
- Building the actual baseline (E05-T04).
- E2E visual testing of application screens (later epics).
- Cross-browser matrix beyond the Chromium target used by Electron.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Decision criteria met
  Given the 2-day timebox expires
  Then a comparison table with measured CI runtime and flake counts for at least two candidates exists
  And one option is recommended, or the decision is deferred with the exact missing datum named
Scenario: Network constraint honoured
  Given the Tailscale-only remote-access decision
  When a hosted option is evaluated
  Then the spike states explicitly what leaves the network (screenshots of a pre-release UI) and whether that is acceptable to the Owner
Scenario: Flake threshold
  Given two consecutive identical runs of the candidate
  Then a candidate producing any non-deterministic diff without a configurable threshold is rejected or its anti-aliasing tolerance setting is documented
Scenario: ADR filed
  Then the outcome is recorded as an ADR in docs/plan/27-adrs/ even if the outcome is 'defer'
```

## Technical notes / design
Use ~10 representative stories spanning a dense CMP-049 Table, CMP-001 Button variants, CMP-043 Dialog and CMP-024 Sparkline (canvas-adjacent, the most flake-prone). Pin fonts in CI (font loading is the classic snapshot flake source) and disable animation during capture regardless of candidate. Measure with the CI runner spec used by E03.

## Test plan
The spike's own output is the evidence: two identical runs, diff counts recorded. Not expected to produce production-shippable code; the harness is throwaway unless promoted by E05-T04.

## Security notes

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the spike itself; the chosen tool must not replace axe-core checks - visual regression and a11y checks are complementary gates.

## Performance notes
Hard constraint: the VR job must fit inside the R0 'commit to dev deploy <=15 min' pipeline budget; a candidate exceeding ~6 min for the v0 story count is rejected or must support parallel sharding.

## Observability
CI must publish the diff artefacts per PR so a reviewer can see before/after without re-running locally.

title: Chart-engine spike & ADR (WebGL2 feasibility, Electron vs Tauri)
body:
## Context
CandleViewer commits to a **fully custom WebGL2 chart engine** (`ADR-0002`) rather than a charting chassis, because no surveyed library renders footprint text cells, a 200-depth DOM liquidity heatmap at 100 ms, or volume/delta profiles natively. That decision is the single largest schedule risk in the project (`docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` R2 render performance, R8 browser/GPU compat). It is paired with a second open decision: **Electron vs Tauri** for the desktop shell (`ADR-0011`, status *proposed*, decision deadline end of Sprint 03), whose only real discriminator is WebView2's behaviour under sustained 100 ms heatmap texture uploads.

This Epic is milestone **M0** of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §15: a timeboxed, explicitly **throwaway** WebGL2 prototype plus a measurement campaign that retires both decisions with evidence before any order-flow feature depends on the engine. R0 exit criterion 4 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3 makes this binding: the prototype must demonstrate **>=60 fps p50 and >=55 fps p95** on the combined scene in Electron, or the Lightweight-Charts v5 fallback in ADR-0002 is formally adopted and R1 scope is re-cut before Sprint 05 planning.

No production feature ships from this Epic. Its deliverables are numbers, two decided ADRs, a committed (non-gating) benchmark harness, and follow-up tickets for whichever path wins.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Throwaway prototype in `packages/chart-engine/spike/` (branch `spike/e06-engine-m0`, never merged to `main` except the harness + report), covering three scenes:
  - **Scene A** — 100k-bar virtual model with visible-window draw and the LOD ladder of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 (benchmarks **B1**, **B2**).
  - **Scene B** — footprint grid at realistic density: 2,500 visible cells x 2 numbers (~12,500 glyphs) via an SDF atlas (`§3.7`) with a Canvas-2D glyph-cache comparison arm (benchmark **B3**).
  - **Scene C** — 200-depth DOM liquidity heatmap, `texSubImage2D` ring streaming at 10 Hz over a 4 h trail (`§3.8`) plus a 30-minute soak (benchmarks **B4**, **B10**).
  - **Scene D** — the combined scene (A+B+C + 3 indicators + 50 order lines) that R0 exit criterion 4 is stated against (benchmark **B5**).
- Deterministic seeded fixture generator producing all synthetic data (bars, footprint cells, heatmap columns) so every run is reproducible run-to-run per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.1.
- Measurement matrix across **headless Chromium**, **Electron** and **Tauri v2 / WebView2** on the reference machine (`06-…` §3.1), reporting p50/p95/p99 frame time overall and per §4.3 stage, draw calls, uploaded bytes/s, GPU + process memory, and WebGL2 capability probe results.
- **ADR-0002** amended with the M0 verdict (custom engine confirmed, or fallback triggered); **ADR-0011** moved from *proposed* to *decided* against its five binding criteria.
- Benchmark harness committed to `packages/chart-engine/bench` and runnable in CI, recording numbers but **not gating** in R0 (per `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 Perf row).
- Design: prototype-informed decisions on LOD text legibility thresholds, heatmap colour convention (green=bid / red=ask, configurable — owner decision #10), and the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay spec, all delivered design-ahead for E11.
- QA: benchmark methodology validation, reproducibility gate, GPU/browser compatibility exploratory charter.
- Security: STRIDE model of the engine + desktop-shell boundary; the shell-hardening checklist that ADR-0011 criterion 5 depends on.
- Closes open items **O1** (Electron vs Tauri), **O2** (SDF atlas size/glyph set, first measurement) and informs **O3** (coarse-ring resolution) from `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16.

## Estimate & budget reconciliation
The authoritative epic register (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3, row **E06**) budgets this Epic at **21 points** over the S01-S02 timebox. The child breakdown below sums to exactly **21**, inside the +/-15 % tolerance required by `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`. The earlier 42-point draft was a double-count of the roadmap budget and is corrected here by trimming scope, not by re-opening the register.

| Ticket | Pts | Ticket | Pts |
|---|---|---|---|
| E06-K01 harness + fixtures | 3 | E06-D01 LOD legibility research | 2 |
| E06-K02 scene A candles/LOD | 1 | E06-D02 SCR-046 + heatmap colour | 1 |
| E06-K03 scene B SDF text | 3 | E06-D03 a11y mirror cost review | 1 |
| E06-K04 scene C heatmap + soak | 3 | E06-Q01 methodology validation | 1 |
| E06-T01 runtime matrix | 1 | E06-Q02 GPU/browser sweep | 1 |
| E06-T02 report + CI harness | 1 | E06-X01 STRIDE model | 1 |
| E06-T03 ADR amendments | 1 | E06-X02 toolchain pinning | 1 |
| | | **Total** | **21** |

To hold the 21-point budget the following scope was deliberately trimmed (each trim is restated in the child ticket's *Out of scope* / *Scope trim* section):
- **Canvas-2D glyph-cache comparison arm (Scene B, E06-K03)** becomes a single spot-check configuration at B3 density rather than a second production-grade text renderer. It only has to answer "is SDF clearly better, clearly worse, or within noise".
- **Headless Chromium (E06-T01)** becomes a one-configuration baseline smoke arm, not a full matrix leg. The binding comparison is **Electron vs Tauri/WebView2**, because that is what ADR-0011 turns on and R0 exit criterion 4 is stated in Electron.
- **GPU/browser compatibility sweep (E06-Q02)** covers three GPU/driver classes (NVIDIA discrete, Intel Iris Xe integrated, one software/ANGLE fallback) instead of an open-ended device matrix; wider coverage is deferred to **E46 Performance hardening**.
- **Scene C (E06-K04)** is measured at the 4 h trail and 30-minute soak that B4/B10 require; longer trails, multi-symbol heatmaps and coarse-ring tuning (open item **O3**) are observations deferred to **E11 M4**.
- **No optimisation-iteration budget beyond the timebox**: if the bar is missed, the ADR-0002 fallback trigger fires rather than the spike being extended.
- **Design tickets D01-D03 are right-sized to decisions, not deliverables**: each produces one threshold/spec/number needed by an M0 scene, with the full design work landing in E05/E11.

## Out of scope
- Any production engine code — scene graph, plugin API, React bindings, stores, real WS decode. That is **E11 Chart engine core** (M1+), which this Epic unblocks.
- Real market data: the spike uses synthetic seeded fixtures only; no Bybit connectivity, no dependency on E08.
- Drawings, indicators, trading overlays, replay, profiles (M5-M8).
- Android / mobile (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14) and any non-web client.
- Shipping an Electron or Tauri application: only measurement harness shells are built here; the real shell is **E10**.
- WebGPU backend (a contained future change behind `RenderBackend`).
- A full device/GPU compatibility matrix, long-trail heatmap scaling, and a fully productionised Canvas-2D text arm — all trimmed to hold the 21-point roadmap budget (see *Estimate & budget reconciliation*).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The combined scene clears the R0 exit bar in Electron
  Given the seeded combined fixture (100k bars + 2,500 footprint text cells + 200-depth heatmap at 100 ms + 3 indicators + 50 order lines)
  When the scripted pan/zoom/update sequence runs for 20 s in Electron on the reference machine
  Then p50 frame time is <= 16.6 ms and p95 frame time is <= 18.2 ms (>=60 fps p50, >=55 fps p95)
  And the per-stage attribution against docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3 is recorded for every stage

Scenario: The combined scene misses the bar
  Given the same run reports p95 frame time > 18.2 ms in Electron after the documented optimisation attempts inside the timebox
  Then ADR-0002's fallback trigger is declared, the Lightweight-Charts v5 chassis is formally adopted as an amendment signed by the Architect
  And R1 scope re-cut tickets are filed before Sprint 05 planning, with the M0 numbers linked as evidence

Scenario: The Electron vs Tauri decision is closed with evidence
  Given the measurement matrix has run all five ADR-0011 criteria in Electron and Tauri/WebView2
  When the decision deadline at the end of Sprint 03 arrives
  Then ADR-0011 status is "decided" with per-criterion pass/fail and measured numbers, not prose judgement
  And whichever shell is rejected is recorded as "rejected-with-evidence" rather than silently dropped

Scenario: Prototype code does not leak into production
  Given the spike branch contains throwaway prototype code
  When the Epic is closed
  Then only the benchmark harness, the fixture generator and the report are merged to main
  And the spike branch is archived unmerged with a note on the Epic, per docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md §5.2

Scenario: Follow-ups exist for the chosen path
  Given a verdict is recorded
  Then E11 (and E10 for GPU flags) carry follow-up tickets citing the M0 findings, so implementers do not re-derive them
```

## Technical notes / design
- Engine architecture under test is `26-chart-engine-design.md` §2: main thread owns input/a11y/DOM overlays; a render worker owns decode, model, cull, batch and GL against an `OffscreenCanvas`. The spike must exercise the worker path, because the `RunMode.inline` fallback has different throughput and would flatter the numbers.
- Precision model is non-negotiable even in the prototype: prices are integer ticks (`Int32`) relative to a per-symbol origin, times are `Float64` with a `viewportTimeOrigin` subtraction before reaching the shader (§3.3). A prototype that uses float dollars measures the wrong thing.
- All four scenes use instanced draws (one quad + per-instance attributes) as per §3.4; MSAA off, pixel-snapping in the shader.
- Instrumentation uses `Performance.mark()` / `measure()` at each §4.3 stage boundary, exported as structured spans (`06-…` §7.2).
- Reference hardware (`06-…` §3.1): 6c/12t x86_64, 32 GB RAM, NVMe, GTX 1650 / Iris Xe class GPU. Every reported number names the machine, GPU driver version, OS build and (for Tauri) the exact WebView2 runtime version, because WebView2 is OS-updated and results are only meaningful when versioned.
- Statistical method: >=3 repeated runs per configuration, compare medians of p95 (`06-…` §7.4 flake tolerance). Single samples are not admissible evidence for an ADR.

## Test plan
- Per-child test plans; at Epic level: the harness itself is verified to be deterministic (same seed -> same fixture bytes), the report's numbers are independently re-runnable by a second engineer on a second machine of the same class, and the delta between the two machines is recorded as the measurement noise band.
- No coverage gate applies to throwaway prototype code (stated explicitly per DoD §5.2); the merged harness + fixture generator do carry the package threshold (>=85% for engine packages).

## Security notes
- Threat surface is small but real: the prototype pulls graphics/bench dependencies (STRIDE **T**ampering / supply chain, `04-security-program.md` §5), and the Tauri arm introduces a Rust host and an OS-updated WebView (STRIDE **E**levation). Controlled by E06-X01/E06-X02.
- ADR-0011 criterion 5 requires a documented equivalent of every shell responsibility including the **OS-keychain bridge for the KEK** (`ADR-0009`); the security review defines what "documented, working equivalent" means so the criterion is falsifiable.
- Data classification: none — synthetic fixtures only, no keys, no PII, no exchange credentials. The prototype must not be pointed at live or demo Bybit.

## Accessibility notes
- The prototype is not a user-facing surface, but M0 must prove the a11y strategy is affordable: the DOM-mirror sync stage has a **<=1 ms** slice of the frame budget (`06-…` §4.3), and the accessible data cursor/live region design (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6, `26-…` §12) must be measured, not assumed. Covered by E06-D03.
- Colour-independence is validated at prototype stage: delta gets colour + directional glyph, imbalance colour + outline, estimated data a hatch pattern — verified in E06-D01 so E11 does not inherit a colour-only encoding.

## Performance notes
- Budgets: B1 <= 12 ms, B2 <= 14 ms, B3 <= 16 ms (text batching <= 2.0 ms, <= 2 text draw calls), B4 <= 10 ms (upload <= 12 KB/s, texture memory <= 20 MB), B5 <= 16.7 ms (<= 40 draw calls), B10 peak <= 600 MB with no monotonic growth (`26-…` §13).
- R0 exit criterion 4 is stricter than B5 alone: it demands >=60 fps p50 **and** >=55 fps p95 on the combined scene in Electron.
- Degradation ladder under stress is defined in `06-…` §4.4 and is measured, not designed, in this Epic.

## Observability
- Harness emits structured JSON per run: `{scenario, runtime, gpu, driver, os, seed, p50, p95, p99, perStageMs{...}, drawCalls, uploadedBytesPerSec, textureMemMB, peakProcessMemMB}` committed as an artefact alongside the report.
- The SCR-046 diagnostics overlay spec (E06-D02) defines the in-app runtime counterpart of these same counters, so field diagnostics and CI benchmarks speak one vocabulary.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Actual effort recorded against the 21-point roadmap budget; any variance >15 % raised at Sprint Review with a register-correction proposal.
- [ ] M0 report published under `docs/plan/` and linked from ADR-0002 and ADR-0011.
- [ ] ADR-0002 amended with the verdict; ADR-0011 status `decided`.
- [ ] Benchmark harness + fixture generator merged and runnable in CI (recording, non-gating).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed against E11 / E10 with findings linked.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated: R2 and R8 re-scored with evidence; R10 (key-person) mitigation noted.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review (Spikes present findings instead of a demo, per DoD §5.2).
- [ ] Security sign-off on the STRIDE model; QA sign-off on the methodology validation; design sign-off on D01-D03.
- [ ] Spike branch archived unmerged; no prototype code on `main`.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E02` — the monorepo scaffold must exist (`packages/chart-engine` workspace, tsup build, vitest, Playwright) before the prototype can live anywhere sane (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1: `E02 --> E06`).
- Unblocks **E11 Chart engine core** (`E06 --> E11`) and informs **E10 App shell** GPU flag tuning.
- No dependency on E08 (Bybit adapter) by design: synthetic fixtures only, so a feed slip cannot delay the decision.
- **No hard dependency on E05 (Design system v0).** E05 runs **S01-S04 design-led** (`30-release-roadmap.md` §5), so it cannot gate an S01-S02 spike without a same-sprint dependency race. E06-D01/E06-D02 therefore consume E05's **Sprint-01 outputs only** (candidate font + type ramp and the dark/high-contrast token drafts from `E05-D01` / `E05-D07`) as a **soft, non-blocking input with a documented contingency**: if the ramp, font or tokens change later, the cheap re-validation described in E06-D01 is re-run against **E11 M4**, never against the M0 timebox.

## Branch
