title: UX research: footprint LOD legibility thresholds and non-colour encodings
body:
## Context
The footprint LOD ladder in `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 degrades cell rendering as pixels-per-bar falls: **L0** cell + two numbers -> **L1** cell + one number (delta) -> **L2** coloured cell only -> **L3** hidden (candles only). The stated trigger is "cell text needs >= 11 px of height and enough width for the widest formatted number". That 11 px figure is currently an engineering guess, and the spike is about to hard-code it into benchmark **B3** (2,500 visible cells with text, `26-…` §13). The performance target therefore depends on an unvalidated legibility threshold: if 11 px is unreadable, B3 measures a scene no trader would use; if it is larger than needed, the engine is made to look slower than it is.

This is also the last cheap moment to settle **non-colour encodings**. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §4 forbids colour-only signalling, and `26-…` §12 commits to delta = colour + directional glyph, imbalance = colour + outline, estimated data = hatch. Those glyphs cost atlas slots and a second fragment threshold, so they must be specified **before** E06-K03 generates the SDF atlas (§3.7, open item **O2**), not retrofitted during E11/M3.

Runs design-ahead of its consumers (E06-K03 this sprint; E11 M3 footprint work from Sprint 04), per the design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated legibility study with the Owner plus 2 order-flow-literate participants, on static renders of **CMP-109 FootprintCell** and **CMP-184 FootprintSeries** (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` §7) at cell heights 8/9/10/11/12/14/16 px, in the dark theme and the high-contrast theme from E05, at devicePixelRatio 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0.
- **Output 1 — LOD threshold table**: binding minimum px height and width per level (L0/L1/L2/L3) plus the +/-15 % hysteresis dead band of §3.6; this is the density E06-K03 uses for B3.
- **Output 2 — non-colour encoding spec**: directional glyph set for delta, outline treatment for imbalance, hatch pattern for `inputSource === "orderEstimated"`, with the exact glyph list so the SDF glyph set can be frozen (open item **O2**).
- **Output 3 — number-format decision per level** (full vs compact `1.2K`), since §3.7 caches a per-cell glyph run and a format change invalidates that cache.
- Design-system contribution: glyph and hatch tokens added to the `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` vocabulary rather than living as engine one-offs.
- Catalogue corrections: **CMP-109**, **CMP-184**, and the **SCR-030** "low-GPU degraded" state copy ("Reduced detail: footprint text hidden below 6 px cells") — validate or correct that 6 px figure against the study.
- Stories informed: **US-CHART-001**, **US-CHART-003**, **US-CHART-008**.

## Out of scope
- Re-running the study against E05's *final* tokens/font — deferred to E11 M4 by design (see Dependencies), so that M0 is never gated on an S01-S04 epic.
- Hi-fi Figma screens for the footprint panel — that is E11/M3 design work; this produces thresholds and encodings, not a screen.
- Heatmap colour convention (green=bid / red=ask) — owned by **E06-D02**.
- Profile/TPO rendering, drawing tools, indicator styling.
- Implementing the LOD switch — prototype in E06-K03, production in E11.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Thresholds are derived from observation, not assertion
  Given the legibility study has run with 3 participants across 7 cell heights and 2 themes
  When results are tabulated
  Then each LOD level's minimum px height and width is stated with the observed read-accuracy that justifies it
  And any deviation from the provisional 11 px figure in 26-chart-engine-design.md §3.6 is filed as a correction to that document

Scenario: Every colour-coded signal has a redundant channel
  Given the encoding spec is reviewed against docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §4
  When delta, imbalance and estimated-data are each checked
  Then each has a documented non-colour channel (glyph, outline, hatch)
  And a greyscale proof render of a dense footprint bar is attached showing all three remain distinguishable

Scenario: The glyph set is frozen before the atlas is built
  Given E06-K03 needs a final glyph list to generate the SDF atlas
  When this ticket reaches Done
  Then the exact glyph set (digits, separators, unit suffixes, directional glyphs) is published and frozen for M0
  And any later addition is handled as a change request against open item O2, not a silent edit

Scenario: Contrast holds at the smallest legible size
  Given the chosen L0 cell height
  When cell text is measured against the most saturated cell background in both dark and high-contrast themes
  Then contrast is >= 4.5:1 per docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §5, or an outline treatment is specified that achieves it

Scenario: Hysteresis does not straddle the legibility cliff
  Given the +/-15 % dead band around the L0/L1 threshold
  When the lower edge of the band is rendered
  Then text at that edge is still readable, or the band is specified asymmetrically so it never drops below the readable size

Scenario: The design-system font or type ramp changes after Sprint 01
  Given the legibility thresholds were measured against E05's Sprint-01 candidate font and type ramp
  When E05 finalises a different font or ramp later in S02-S04
  Then a re-validation run using the same protocol is filed against E11 M4, not against the M0 timebox
  And the M0 report's threshold table is annotated with the font, ramp and theme actually used, so no downstream ticket inherits an unattributed number

Scenario: The E05 Sprint-01 candidate font is not available when this ticket starts
  Given E05-D01 has not yet published a candidate font or type ramp
  When this study begins
  Then it proceeds against the fallback font stack in docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md
  And the deviation and its risk to the threshold are recorded in the findings, rather than the ticket being blocked
```

## Technical notes / design
- Study renders are produced with Canvas 2D at the three target DPRs; no engine dependency, so this runs in parallel with E06-K01.
- Text on saturated cell backgrounds is expected to need the SDF outline pass (`alpha_outline` at a second threshold, §3.7). If the study confirms it, say so explicitly: it roughly doubles per-glyph fragment work and B3's 2.0 ms text-batching budget must absorb it.
- Define the widest possible formatted string per level; L0 width thresholds are a function of it.
- Deliver thresholds as a named constant set (e.g. `LOD_PROFILE_M0`) so a benchmark run records which threshold set produced its numbers.

## Test plan
- Not a code ticket. Validation is: (a) study protocol reviewed by the UX research lead before running; (b) results re-scored blind by a second reviewer on the same renders, agreement recorded; (c) greyscale proof checked by the accessibility specialist.
- Artefacts are consumed as inputs by E06-K03's B3 scene and by E06-Q01's methodology validation.

## Security notes
N/A — no code, no data, no credentials; synthetic values only in study renders.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* an accessibility deliverable: it closes colour-independence (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §4) and contrast (§5) where they are cheapest to satisfy. It also feeds CMP-109's canvas-surrogate contract, whose `aria-label` composes "Price 65,430; bid 12.4; ask 8.1; delta +4.3" plus "(estimated)" — the "(estimated)" suffix must correspond to the hatch pattern chosen here so the visual and announced encodings agree.

## Performance notes
Directly sets the density of benchmark **B3** (p95 <= 16 ms, text batching <= 2.0 ms, <= 2 text draw calls). The chosen threshold must be defended in the M0 report so the benchmark cannot be accused of being tuned to pass.

## Observability
N/A — research artefact. The resulting thresholds appear as a named constant in the harness config and are echoed in every run's JSON report.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Study protocol, raw scores and analysis written up and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] LOD threshold table published; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 corrected if it disagrees.
- [ ] Non-colour encoding spec + frozen glyph set published; open item **O2** updated.
- [ ] Greyscale proof render and contrast measurements attached.
- [ ] Design sign-off by the CDO or delegate; accessibility sign-off by the accessibility specialist.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` (CMP-109, CMP-184) and `14-screens-catalogue.md` (SCR-030 degraded copy) updated to match.
- [ ] Written handoff note to E06-K03 (label `handoff`).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E02` — the monorepo/doc workspace must exist for the research artefacts to land.
- **Soft (non-blocking) input: E05 Design system v0.** The earlier draft hard-blocked this Sprint-01 ticket on the whole of E05, which the roadmap schedules across **S01-S04 design-led** (`30-release-roadmap.md` §5) — E05 is therefore *not* guaranteed complete in the sprint this ticket starts, and the hard block was a same-sprint dependency race that could stall the S01-S02 spike timebox. **Resolution:** this ticket consumes only E05's **Sprint-01 artefacts** — the candidate font selection and type ramp plus dark/high-contrast token drafts from `E05-D01` and `E05-D07`, available in week 1 of Sprint 01 and stable enough to fix a legibility threshold.
- **Contingency if that input is late:** the study runs against the fallback font stack named in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`, and the report records the exact font, ramp and theme used so the threshold is always interpretable. If E05 later finalises a different font or ramp, the thresholds are re-validated by the cheap re-run defined in the acceptance criteria, scheduled against **E11 M4** — M0 is never blocked on it.
- Blocks **E06-K03** (atlas glyph set, B3 density) — K03 must not generate its atlas before the glyph set and minimum cell-text height are fixed here.

## Branch
`design/e06-lod-legibility` — research artefacts and doc corrections. PR size guidance: docs-only, one PR.

## References

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

title: Design SCR-046 diagnostics overlay and heatmap colour/legend convention
body:
## Context
Two design artefacts must exist before the spike can report meaningful numbers or before E11 can build the engine's runtime surfaces.

First, **SCR-046 Chart engine diagnostics overlay** (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`): the `Ctrl+Shift+D` developer/owner overlay showing FPS, frame time p50/p95, draw calls, GPU memory, buffer uploads/s, WS message rate, dropped frames and a "copy diagnostics" button. It is the in-app counterpart of the benchmark harness's JSON report — the two must share one counter vocabulary, otherwise a field bug report and a CI benchmark describe the same problem in two incompatible languages. Its own budget is strict: **<= 0.5 ms per frame, sampled at 2 Hz, not per frame**.

Second, the **heatmap colour convention and legend**: owner decision #10 fixes green = bid, red = ask, configurable. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8 implements colour via a **256x1 LUT texture**, so a theme change is a one-texture update rather than a data re-upload — which means the palette must be expressible as a 256-entry ramp with a documented linear/log intensity mapping and an age-decay curve. **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend** (built from CMP-035 LegendItem) is the user-facing reading of that ramp.

Design-ahead: delivered in Sprint 01 for E06-K04 (Sprint 02) and for E11's M4 heatmap milestone, comfortably ahead of the >= 2-sprint rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-046** hi-fi spec in Figma: layout, counter list, threshold colouring paired with text (e.g. "below budget"), pinned/unpinned states, copy-diagnostics affordance, enable path from **SCR-118** renderer settings, hidden-by-default behaviour. Must satisfy the screen's existing design sign-off checklist verbatim.
- Counter vocabulary table shared with the harness: every counter name, unit, sampling rate and source, cross-referenced to the §4.3 stage names in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and to the harness JSON keys defined in E06-K01.
- **Heatmap LUT spec**: 256-entry ramp for the default (green=bid / red=ask) convention plus a colour-blind-safe alternative candidate (informing open item **O5**), the intensity mapping (linear and log variants) and the age-decay curve, delivered as data a shader can consume, not as a screenshot.
- **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend** spec: value ticks, unit labelling, side labelling, and the non-colour reading path (tooltip / cursor announcement carries intensity as text per `26-…` §12).
- Components touched: **CMP-024 Sparkline**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-069 InfoPanel**, **CMP-178 SystemHealthTile** (SCR-046) and **CMP-035 LegendItem**, **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend** (heatmap).
- Stories informed: **US-SET-008**, **US-OBS-002** (diagnostics overlay); **US-CHART-001**, **US-CHART-006** (engine surfaces).

## Out of scope
- Implementing SCR-046 against the built E05 component library (that is E11); this ticket ships a token-referential spec only.
- The DOM ladder and heatmap *panel* design (SCR-050 and the DOM domain) — this ticket covers only the colour ramp and legend that the engine renders.
- Implementing the overlay — E11 builds it; the spike only uses the counter vocabulary.
- Backend observability dashboards (E04) — SCR-046 is client-side engine telemetry only.
- Final colour-blind-safe palette selection, which `26-…` §16 assigns to the M8 a11y pass (open item **O5**); this ticket only supplies a candidate.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overlay and harness speak one vocabulary
  Given the SCR-046 counter list and the E06-K01 harness JSON schema
  When the two are diffed
  Then every overlay counter maps to exactly one harness key with the same name, unit and definition
  And any counter present in only one of them is either added to both or explicitly justified in the spec

Scenario: Thresholds are never colour-only
  Given a counter exceeds its budget from docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3
  When the overlay renders that counter
  Then the breach is shown with text ("above budget") as well as colour
  And the overlay remains readable in the high-contrast theme

Scenario: The LUT is machine-consumable
  Given the heatmap colour spec
  When an engineer implements the 256x1 LUT texture
  Then they can generate it directly from the delivered ramp definition without sampling a picture
  And switching the bid/ask convention is expressed as swapping ramp halves, matching the one-texture-update design in 26-chart-engine-design.md §3.8

Scenario: The overlay cannot flood a screen reader
  Given the overlay is pinned open and values update at 2 Hz
  When a screen reader is active
  Then values are exposed as a static readable table with polite (not assertive) updates, per the SCR-046 a11y note
```

## Technical notes / design
- SCR-046 sampling is 2 Hz and the whole overlay costs <= 0.5 ms/frame; the design must therefore avoid per-frame sparkline redraws — CMP-024 Sparkline updates on the 2 Hz tick with a fixed-length ring of samples.
- Counter definitions must be unambiguous: "frame time" is the worker's render-loop wall time including GL submission, not rAF-to-rAF delta; "draw calls" counts `drawArraysInstanced`/`drawElementsInstanced` invocations per frame; "GPU memory" is an estimate derived from tracked buffer/texture allocations, labelled as an estimate in the UI.
- "Copy diagnostics" must produce the same JSON shape the harness writes, so a user-submitted bug report can be diffed against a CI baseline.
- LUT: the ramp is defined in a perceptually uniform space and converted to sRGB at generation time; log intensity mapping is `t = log1p(v * k) / log1p(k)` with `k` a documented constant so shader and legend agree exactly.

## Test plan
- Design QA against the SCR-046 sign-off checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- The LUT ramp is validated by generating the 256x1 PNG from the spec and confirming a round-trip: legend tick values map to the same colours the shader produces for those intensities.
- Contrast checks on overlay text in dark and high-contrast themes.
- Feeds E06-K04 (heatmap scene) and E06-Q01 (methodology validation).

## Security notes
"Copy diagnostics" is the one real threat surface: the payload must contain **no** symbol-identifying account context, no user identifiers, no correlation IDs tied to orders — it is engine telemetry only (STRIDE **I**nformation disclosure, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5). The spec must state the exact allowed field list; E06-X01's threat model reviews it.

## Accessibility notes
- Overlay is a text panel, not a canvas; updates polite, never assertive; pinnable and readable as a static table (SCR-046 a11y note).
- All threshold states carry text in addition to colour (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §4).
- Heatmap intensity must be available as text via tooltip and the cursor announcement (`26-…` §12), so the legend is not the only path to the value.

## Performance notes
- Overlay budget: <= 0.5 ms/frame, 2 Hz sampling (SCR-046).
- Heatmap targets the ticket informs: **B4** p95 <= 10 ms, upload <= 12 KB/s, texture memory <= 20 MB.

## Observability
Defines the client-side counter vocabulary used by both SCR-046 and the harness report, and the `diagnostics.overlay_toggled` / `diagnostics.snapshot_copied` analytics events already declared on SCR-046.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma hi-fi for SCR-046 published; every box on the screen's design sign-off checklist ticked.
- [ ] Counter vocabulary table merged and referenced from both the harness (E06-K01) and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-046.
- [ ] Heatmap LUT ramp delivered as generatable data + documented intensity/decay mapping; CMP-113 spec updated.
- [ ] Colour-blind-safe candidate recorded against open item **O5**.
- [ ] Design sign-off (CDO or delegate) and accessibility review comment recorded.
- [ ] Handoff note to E06-K04 and to E11 (label `handoff`).

## Dependencies
- **Soft (non-blocking) input: E05 Design system v0** (hard block removed). E05 runs **S01-S04 design-led**, so hard-blocking this Sprint-01 spike ticket on it was a same-sprint dependency race. This ticket specs SCR-046 and the heatmap LUT **against E05's Sprint-01 token drafts** (`E05-D01` colour/spacing/type variables) and references CMP-024/036/069/178 by ID and state rather than by implemented code. The spec is written **token-referential** (`--cv-*` variable names, never literal hex), so a later token change re-themes it for free; only the contrast checks need re-running, and that re-check rides along with `E05-D04` instead of blocking M0.
- `blocked_by: E06-K01` — the harness JSON schema is one half of the shared counter vocabulary; specifying the overlay before it exists would guarantee a mismatch.
- Blocks **E06-K04** (heatmap colour/legend) and informs E11's M4.

## Branch

## References

title: Build M0 benchmark harness and deterministic seeded fixture generator
body:
## Context
Every number this Epic produces, and therefore both ADR decisions, rests on the harness built here. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.1 is explicit that ad hoc DevTools profiling is not acceptable: the benchmark must be a mode built into the chart-engine package, driving a scripted sequence over a **version-controlled, deterministically seeded** synthetic dataset, reporting p50/p95/p99 overall and per §4.3 stage. §7.4 adds the statistical rules (>= 3 repeated runs, compare medians of p95) that keep CI-runner noise from producing false verdicts.

The fixture generator matters as much as the harness. If the synthetic data is not reproducible byte-for-byte from a seed, two engineers measuring on two machines are not measuring the same thing, and the M0 report is unfalsifiable — which is exactly what an ADR must not be.

This is the first child of E06 to start and it gates the three scene spikes (K02/K03/K04), the QA methodology validation (Q01) and the diagnostics counter vocabulary (D02).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/bench/` — harness runnable headless via Playwright + Chromium with a fixed GPU flag set (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §13), and as an Electron and a Tauri target for E06-T01.
- **Fixture generator** in `packages/fixtures` (or `packages/chart-engine/bench/fixtures` if the shared package does not yet exist in E02's scaffold — state which in the PR):
  - 100k synthetic OHLCV bars with realistic volatility clustering and gaps, prices emitted as **integer ticks** with a per-symbol origin (never float dollars — `26-…` §3.3 precision rule).
  - Footprint cell stream at realistic density: enough cells that 2,500 are visible at the L0 threshold set by **E06-D01**, with bid/ask/trade-count per cell.
  - 200-depth heatmap column stream at 100 ms cadence covering a 4 h trail, plus a 30-minute continuation for the B10 soak.
  - Deterministic: same seed -> byte-identical output, asserted by a hash test.
- **Scripted driver sequences** (one per benchmark): continuous pan at 1000 px/s (B1), wheel zoom sweep 0.1 -> 50 px/bar (B2), static footprint hold with periodic updates (B3), heatmap streaming with panning (B4), combined scene (B5), live update storm 20 msg/s x 6 stores (B7), cold init to first frame (B9), 30-minute soak (B10).
- **Instrumentation**: `Performance.mark()`/`measure()` at every §4.3 stage boundary — input handling, data-window recompute, candle geometry, footprint text/geometry, heatmap upload, pane redraw, overlay redraw, DOM-mirror sync, composite+present — exported as structured spans (`06-…` §7.2).
- **Report writer**: one JSON per run — `{scenario, runtime, runtimeVersion, gpu, driver, os, seed, lodProfile, repetitions, p50, p95, p99, perStageMs{}, drawCalls, uploadedBytesPerSec, textureMemMB, peakProcessMemMB}` — plus a human-readable markdown summary. Schema shared with **SCR-046** via E06-D02.
- Runner ergonomics: `pnpm bench --scenario=B5 --runtime=electron --reps=3 --seed=…`, with a machine-descriptor block captured automatically (CPU, GPU, driver, OS build, WebView2 version where applicable).

## Out of scope
- Any production engine code; the harness renders whatever scene the K02/K03/K04 prototypes provide behind a tiny scene interface.
- CI *gating*: per `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 the harness is committed and runnable with numbers recorded, but **not yet a required check** in R0. Wiring it as a gate belongs to E11.
- Backend load testing (k6/Locust) — that is E07/E08 territory.
- Real Bybit data or any network access during a run.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fixtures are byte-reproducible
  Given seed 20260928 and the fixture generator
  When the generator runs twice on two different machines
  Then both outputs hash identically
  And the hash is asserted by a unit test that fails loudly if the generator's behaviour ever drifts

Scenario: A run reports per-stage attribution, not just a total
  Given the B5 combined scenario runs for 20 s
  When the JSON report is written
  Then it contains p50/p95/p99 overall and a perStageMs entry for each of the nine stages named in docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3
  And the stage costs sum to within 10 % of the measured frame time, with the residual reported as "unattributed"

Scenario: Statistical rules are enforced by the tool, not by discipline
  Given a run is requested with fewer than 3 repetitions
  When the report is generated
  Then it is marked "not admissible for ADR evidence" in the JSON and the markdown summary
  And the default repetition count is 3

Scenario: The machine is always identified
  Given any run on any runtime
  When the report is written
  Then CPU, GPU, driver version, OS build and (for Tauri) the exact WebView2 runtime version are captured automatically
  And a run missing any of these fields fails rather than reporting anonymous numbers

Scenario: The harness does not perturb what it measures
  Given instrumentation is enabled
  When the same scenario is run with instrumentation disabled
  Then the difference in p95 frame time is <= 3 %, or the overhead is documented and subtracted consistently
```

## Technical notes / design
- Scene interface kept deliberately minimal so prototype scenes are swappable: `interface BenchScene { init(gl, fixture): Promise<void>; step(t: number, input: DriverEvent | null): void; stats(): FrameStats; dispose(): void }`.
- Driver events are synthesised deterministically from a script (time-parameterised, not frame-parameterised) so a slow machine executes the same logical motion as a fast one — otherwise a slow runtime silently gets an easier test.
- Warm-up: discard the first 2 s of every run (shader compilation, atlas generation, JIT) and report cold-init separately as B9; conflating them would slander every runtime equally but uselessly.
- GPU memory is an estimate from tracked allocations (WebGL exposes no true figure); label it as an estimate everywhere, including in the SCR-046 vocabulary.
- Peak process memory via `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` where available, falling back to the Electron/Tauri host process metrics; state which source produced the figure in the report.
- Zero allocation in the frame path is a design rule of the engine (`26-…` §3.2 rule 4); the harness samples an allocation counter so K02/K03/K04 can be checked against it.
- Flag set for headless Chromium must be pinned and printed in the report — GPU flags change results materially and an unpinned flag set makes runs incomparable across weeks.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: fixture determinism (hash equality across runs and platforms); tick-integer price invariants (no float dollars anywhere in the fixture); driver-script time-parameterisation (same logical motion at 30 fps and 144 fps); report-schema validation; "< 3 reps -> not admissible" flag; missing-machine-descriptor -> failure.
- **Integration**: full B5 run against a stub scene producing known synthetic frame times, asserting the reported p50/p95/p99 match the injected distribution within tolerance (this validates the statistics, not the GPU).
- **Contract**: report JSON validated against the schema shared with E06-D02's counter vocabulary.
- Coverage: >= 85 % on the merged harness + generator (engine-package threshold). Prototype scenes are exempt as throwaway code.
- Fixtures: seeds are checked into the repo; generated artefacts are not (they are reproducible by definition).

## Security notes
- Supply chain is the live threat (STRIDE **T**ampering, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 and §12): the harness pulls Playwright, an Electron build and, for the Tauri arm, a Rust toolchain. All must be pinned by exact version with lockfile entries, and go through the same Dependabot/npm-audit/pip-audit gates as production code. Reviewed by **E06-X02**.
- The harness performs no network I/O at run time; assert this (no fetch/XHR/WS during a benchmark run) so a fixture can never be silently sourced from the internet.
- No credentials, no exchange connectivity, no PII. Data classification: none.

## Accessibility notes
The harness itself is a developer tool with no user surface (N/A for WCAG conformance), but it must expose the **DOM-mirror sync** stage as a first-class measured stage so the a11y layer's cost is never invisible — required by E06-D03 and by the 1 ms allocation in `06-…` §4.3.

## Performance notes
Harness overhead <= 3 % of measured p95 (see acceptance criteria). Establishes the baselines later governed by the <= 5 % regression gate (`06-…` §7.4), including the baseline-update policy that baselines move only via a reviewed PR.

## Observability
Defines the run-report JSON that is the Epic's primary evidence artefact, and the counter vocabulary mirrored by SCR-046. Reports are committed as artefacts alongside the M0 report so future engine work can diff against M0 numbers.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Harness and fixture generator merged to `main` (this part is **not** throwaway) with >= 85 % coverage.
- [ ] `pnpm bench` documented in the package README with the pinned flag set.
- [ ] Determinism test green in CI; schema contract test green.
- [ ] Report JSON schema agreed with E06-D02's counter vocabulary.
- [ ] Runs successfully in headless Chromium; Electron and Tauri targets stubbed ready for E06-T01.
- [ ] Security review of pinned dependencies (E06-X02 input) recorded.
- [ ] Code review with 2 approvals incl. code-owner (`packages/chart-engine` -> chart-engine owner + architect).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E02` — needs the pnpm workspace, `packages/chart-engine` package, vitest and Playwright from the monorepo scaffold.
- Blocks **E06-K02**, **E06-K03**, **E06-K04**, **E06-Q01**, **E06-D02**, **E06-X02**.

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-bench-harness` (merged to `main`). PR size guidance: split into 2-3 PRs <= 400 LOC — (1) fixture generator + determinism tests, (2) harness runner + instrumentation, (3) report writer + schema.

## References

title: Prototype scene A: 100k-bar model, visible-window draw and LOD ladder
body:
## Context
The first thing the custom engine must prove is the thing every charting library already does well, because if we cannot match chassis parity we should be using a chassis. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md` is candid that the fully custom route adds "~4-8 weeks to reach chassis parity (pan/zoom momentum, axis decimation, multi-pane sync, crosshair, DPI correctness)" and makes milestone **M1 (chassis parity)** deliberately first so the riskiest unknown resolves early. M0's job is the cheaper precursor: demonstrate that a 100k-bar virtual model with visible-window draw and a working LOD ladder holds **B1** (<= 12 ms p95, <= 8 draw calls, continuous pan at 1000 px/s) and **B2** (<= 14 ms p95, <= 6 LOD changes over a 0.1 -> 50 px/bar zoom sweep, no flicker).

The subtlety that makes this worth measuring rather than assuming is in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.1: the 16.6 ms budget is a **per-frame visible-window** cost, not an "iterate 100k bars per frame" cost. Getting that wrong is the classic way a custom engine dies — and the L2 decimation rule (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6) adds a correctness requirement on top: per-pixel-column min/max preserving reduction, so price spikes never vanish when zoomed out. A fast engine that eats spikes is a broken engine.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype scene A on branch `spike/e06-engine-m0`, implementing the `BenchScene` interface from E06-K01:
  - `BarStore`-shaped columnar model (`time: Float64Array`, OHLC/volume/delta as `Float32Array`, ring indices, capacity doubling) per `26-…` §3.3, holding 100k bars.
  - Visible-window slicing with a prefetch margin; off-window bars never touched by the render loop.
  - Instanced candle rendering (one quad, per-instance attributes) with pixel-snapping for hairlines, MSAA off, depth test off (`26-…` §3.4).
  - LOD ladder L0 full OHLC bodies+wicks / L1 bodies only / L2 min-max column strip, with the px-per-bar thresholds and +/-15 % hysteresis of §3.6.
  - Viewport math per §3.5: bar-index-space panning with `barSpacing` clamped to [0.05, 200] px, cursor-anchored zoom (world coordinate under the anchor invariant), momentum with exponential decay (tau = 120 ms, terminate below 0.02 px/ms).
  - Time and price axes with decimation, enough to be representative of real per-frame cost — this is not chrome, axis label layout is a measurable cost.
  - `priceOrigin` double-precision offset on the CPU, integer-tick prices, `time - viewportTimeOrigin` passed to the shader as float32 (§3.3 precision rule).
- Benchmarks wired: **B1**, **B2**, and **B9** (cold init to first frame with 100k bars, <= 900 ms).
- Correctness proof for L2 decimation: a test asserting the min/max-preserving reduction retains every spike present in the source data for a fixture containing deliberate single-bar extremes.
- Measured output feeding **E06-T01** (runtime matrix) and **E06-T02** (report).

## Out of scope
- Footprint cells and SDF text (**E06-K03**), heatmap (**E06-K04**).
- Multi-pane layout and sync, crosshair interaction polish, drawings, indicators, trading overlays — all M1+ production work in E11.
- Any production-quality API, React bindings, or option diffing. This is throwaway code and must be labelled as such in its README.
- Touch/pinch gestures (measured only if trivial; the reference surface is mouse/trackpad).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: B1 continuous pan holds the budget
  Given the 100k-bar seeded fixture loaded into the prototype
  When the scripted continuous pan at 1000 px/s runs for 20 s in headless Chromium
  Then p95 frame time is <= 12 ms and draw calls per frame are <= 8
  And per-stage attribution shows data-window recompute <= 2 ms and candle geometry update <= 2 ms per docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3

Scenario: B2 zoom sweep does not flicker between detail levels
  Given a wheel zoom sweep from 0.1 to 50 px/bar
  When the sweep runs
  Then p95 frame time is <= 14 ms
  And the number of LOD level changes over the whole sweep is <= 6, demonstrating the +/-15 % hysteresis band works

Scenario: Decimation never eats a spike
  Given a fixture containing isolated single-bar high/low extremes
  When the view is zoomed out far enough to engage L2 min-max column reduction
  Then every extreme is still present in the rendered column strip, verified by reading back the framebuffer or the emitted geometry
  And a regression test encodes this so the property cannot be optimised away later

Scenario: Only the visible window is processed
  Given 100k bars are loaded and ~300 are visible
  When a static frame is rendered
  Then the number of bars touched by the render loop is within the visible window plus the prefetch margin, asserted by an instrumentation counter
  And frame time does not scale measurably with total bar count (10k vs 100k differ by <= 10 % on a static frame)

Scenario: Cold init stays under budget
  Given a cold page load with the 100k-bar fixture
  When time-to-first-frame is measured
  Then it is <= 900 ms (B9), reported separately from steady-state numbers
```

## Technical notes / design
- Bar-space vs time-space: pan/zoom operate in bar-index space with a monotone index->time map; the scene exposes both `indexToScreen` and `timeToScreen` because the heatmap scene (K04) needs true time (§3.5). Getting this dual mapping right in M0 is what makes K04's alignment work rather than a fudge.
- Auto-scale recomputes only when the visible bar range changes, throttled to once per frame (§3.5) — measure it in the data-window stage, not hidden in draw.
- No allocation in the hot path (§3.2 rule 4): pool all per-frame structures; the harness's allocation counter must show zero GC-triggering allocations during a steady pan.
- Render-on-demand: with no data and no interaction the loop parks. Verify this is true, since a prototype that spins rAF forever will flatter nothing but will mislead the battery/idle discussion for E10.
- Axis decimation: label density chosen by available px per label with a nice-number ladder; label text uses the same text path that K03 builds if available, otherwise Canvas-2D overlay — state which was used, because it changes the text-stage cost attribution.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (on the harness-side helpers that survive): index<->screen transform round-trip; `barSpacing` clamping; LOD threshold selection including hysteresis boundaries (just inside/outside the dead band); min/max decimation correctness on spike fixtures; momentum decay integration is dt-based (same outcome at 30 and 144 fps).
- **Integration**: full B1/B2/B9 runs via the E06-K01 harness against the seeded fixture, 3 repetitions, medians of p95 compared to budget.
- **Visual**: golden-image capture at each LOD level so E11 inherits reference images (not gating in M0, but captured).
- **Perf**: B1, B2, B9 as above; static-frame scaling check (10k vs 100k bars).
- Coverage: throwaway prototype code is exempt (stated per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2); helpers promoted into the harness carry >= 85 %.

## Security notes
No new surface beyond E06-K01's supply chain (STRIDE **T**ampering). No network I/O during a run; synthetic fixtures only; no credentials. Data classification: none. Shader code is authored in-repo, not fetched, so there is no remote-code path into the GPU pipeline.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for this scene in isolation — the a11y layer is measured in **E06-D03** against the combined scene. One constraint carried here: the LOD ladder must expose its current level as state that the accessible layer can read (US-CHART-001 requires "the aggregation level is indicated"), so the prototype exposes `currentLod` in `stats()` rather than keeping it internal.

## Performance notes
Budgets: **B1** p95 <= 12 ms, <= 8 draw calls; **B2** p95 <= 14 ms, <= 6 LOD changes; **B9** cold init <= 900 ms. Stage slices: data-window recompute <= 2 ms, candle geometry <= 2 ms, input handling <= 1 ms (`06-…` §4.3). US-CHART-001 NFR: >= 55 fps at 100k bars; US-CHART-006 NFR: input-to-pixel latency <= 1 frame.

## Observability
Scene reports `{visibleBars, barsTouched, currentLod, lodChanges, drawCalls, bufferBytesUploaded, allocationsInFramePath}` through `stats()` into the harness JSON; these become the SCR-046 counters (E06-D02) in production.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] B1, B2, B9 measured in headless Chromium with >= 3 reps; numbers recorded in the harness report format.
- [ ] Decimation spike-preservation test green.
- [ ] Visible-window-only processing proven by counter, not by inspection.
- [ ] Golden images captured per LOD level and handed to E11.
- [ ] Findings (what was hard, what surprised, what M1 must budget for) written up for the E06-T02 report.
- [ ] Prototype README states clearly that the code is throwaway and why.
- [ ] Reviewed by the chart-engine owner (spike branch review, not merge-queue).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E06-K01` — needs the harness, fixtures, driver scripts and instrumentation.
- Blocks **E06-T01** (runtime matrix runs this scene in all three runtimes).

## Branch
`spike/e06-engine-m0` (archived unmerged). PR size guidance: no PR to `main`; branch reviewed in place, findings land in the docs PR of E06-T02.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 (architecture), §3.4 (GL backend), §3.6 (LOD), §3.7 (SDF text), §3.8 (heatmap streaming), §13 (benchmarks B1-B10), §14 (test strategy), §15 (milestone M0), §16 (open items O1-O3)

title: STRIDE model of the engine and desktop-shell boundary; hardening checklist
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires a STRIDE kickoff for any Epic touching a trust boundary, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 names STRIDE models for E03, E08 and E09 as R0 quality gates. E06 is not on that list because the spike itself handles no secrets — but it **chooses the desktop shell**, and the shell is one of the product's most consequential trust boundaries (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §4). Choosing it on performance numbers alone, then discovering afterwards what hardening costs, would be exactly backwards.

`ADR-0011` makes this concrete in two places. Its "Interim consequences" list Electron's security posture as requiring deliberate hardening — `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, strict CSP, an allow-list preload, navigation and `window.open` blocked, signed auto-updates — and notes these are "mandatory checklist items in `04-security-program.md`, not defaults". And its **criterion 5** requires, for Tauri to be adoptable, "a documented, working equivalent of every shell responsibility: OS-keychain bridge for the KEK, auto-update with signature verification, deep links, multi-window workspace persistence, and Playwright-drivable E2E". Criterion 5 is a security deliverable wearing an architecture hat, and without a checklist it is unfalsifiable prose.

This ticket therefore does two things: models the threats, and turns criterion 5 into a checkable list that **E06-T01** applies and **E06-T03** decides against.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **STRIDE threat model** for this Epic's scope, following `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5's method and recorded in the security programme's model set:
  - *Assets*: the desktop shell's privilege boundary, the KEK held in the OS keychain (`ADR-0009`), the auto-update channel, the rendering pipeline's inputs (WS frames, shaders, fonts), the diagnostics payload.
  - *Trust boundaries*: renderer <-> preload <-> main process (Electron) or WebView <-> Rust host (Tauri); web page <-> shared worker; app <-> OS keychain; app <-> update server.
  - *Threats per STRIDE category*, at minimum: **S** — a malicious page impersonating the app's deep-link handler; **T** — supply-chain tampering of engine/bench dependencies, font or shader assets, unsigned updates; **R** — none material at this layer, stated explicitly; **I** — diagnostics payload leaking account/user context (SCR-046 "copy diagnostics"), the DOM-mirror reproducing sensitive values into the DOM, GPU memory residue; **D** — context-loss loops, unbounded ring growth, a rogue WS producing upload storms; **E** — `nodeIntegration` or a permissive preload granting a compromised renderer OS access, WebView2's OS-updated component changing behaviour under the app.
  - Each threat: likelihood, impact, existing control, required control, owner, and whether it is an E06 action or an E10/E11 constraint.
- **Shell hardening checklist** (the measurable form of ADR-0011 criterion 5), covering both candidates, each item stated as a verifiable check:
  - `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, strict CSP with no `unsafe-eval`, allow-list preload exposing a named API surface only, navigation and `window.open` blocked by default, remote module disabled;
  - OS-keychain bridge able to store and retrieve the KEK per `ADR-0009`, with the failure mode when the keychain is unavailable;
  - auto-update with signature verification and a documented rollback;
  - deep-link handling that validates and refuses unexpected schemes/targets;
  - multi-window workspace persistence without writing secrets to disk in plaintext;
  - Playwright-drivable E2E (a shell that cannot be automated cannot be regression-tested, which is itself a security property).
- **Applied to the harness shells**: E06-T01's Electron and Tauri harnesses must be built with these settings on, so the measured numbers are numbers we can actually ship against.
- **Abuse cases** for the diagnostics payload (E06-D02) and for the engine's input surface, written as concrete misuse scenarios with expected defences.
- Handoff of the checklist and the unresolved constraints to **E10** (shell implementation) and **E11** (engine).

## Out of scope
- Implementing the hardening in the production shell — **E10**.
- Auth, RBAC, session handling, API-key storage — **E09** and the ACCT domain.
- Backend threat models (exchange boundary E08, supply chain E03, auth E09) — separately gated in `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4.
- Penetration testing, which `04-security-program.md` §13 schedules before Live enablement (R4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The model covers every STRIDE category explicitly
  Given the threat model for E06's scope
  When it is reviewed against docs/plan/04-security-program.md §5
  Then each of the six STRIDE categories has either at least one identified threat with a control, or an explicit "not material here, because…" statement
  And no category is silently omitted

Scenario: Criterion 5 becomes checkable
  Given ADR-0011 criterion 5's five shell responsibilities
  When the hardening checklist is published
  Then each responsibility maps to one or more items that a reviewer can mark pass or fail by observation
  And E06-T01 can execute the checklist against both candidate shells without further interpretation

Scenario: Harness shells are hardened before they are measured
  Given the Electron and Tauri harness shells used by E06-T01
  When their configuration is inspected
  Then contextIsolation is true, nodeIntegration is false, sandbox is true and a strict CSP is in force
  And any hardening item that could not be enabled in the harness is recorded with its expected performance implication, so the measurement's validity is known

Scenario: The diagnostics payload cannot leak context
  Given the SCR-046 "copy diagnostics" payload specified in E06-D02
  When it is reviewed against the abuse cases
  Then the allowed field list contains no user identifier, no account context, no symbol-linked order correlation id
  And a violation of that list is defined as a security defect, not a product decision

Scenario: Unresolved risks land on an owning epic
  Given threats that E06 cannot close inside its scope
  When the model is finalised
  Then each is recorded as a named constraint on E10 or E11 with an owner
  And none is left owned by the closed spike
```

## Technical notes / design
- Electron's hardening settings have measurable cost (sandboxing and context isolation add IPC overhead), which is exactly why they must be on during measurement rather than bolted on after the shell is chosen — a hardened-vs-unhardened delta should also be recorded, since it is useful evidence in its own right.
- WebView2's OS-updated nature is a security property as well as a performance one: the app cannot pin the engine it runs on, so the model must state what changes when Microsoft ships a new WebView2 (both the benefit — security patches arrive without us shipping — and the risk — behaviour changes under the application).
- Electron's counterpart is the Chromium update treadmill: we own shipping security patches. Name the owner and the cadence as a required control if Electron wins.
- Shader and font assets must be vendored and pinned, not fetched — the SDF atlas is generated at runtime from the design-system font (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.7), which makes the font an executable-adjacent input.
- The DOM mirror reproduces rendered values into the DOM; in production that inherits the chart's data classification. Record it now so E11 does not treat the mirror as an unclassified invisible surface.

## Test plan
- Threat model reviewed in a working session with the Architect and the chart-engine lead (per `04-security-program.md` §5's process), findings minuted.
- Checklist dry-run against the harness shells before E06-T01's matrix begins; each item marked pass/fail with evidence.
- Abuse cases exercised against the diagnostics payload spec: attempt to include a user id, an account id and an order correlation id, and confirm the spec's field allow-list rejects each.
- Negative check on the harness: confirm no network egress during a run (shared with E06-Q01), since the shell's network posture is part of the boundary.
- Security-tooling gates per `04-security-program.md` §12 apply to any merged code (harness): Semgrep/CodeQL, npm audit, gitleaks.

## Security notes
This ticket **is** the Epic's security deliverable. Data classification for the spike itself: none (synthetic data, no credentials, no PII). The classification that matters is the one the chosen shell will later hold — the KEK — which is why criterion 5's keychain item is non-negotiable and is reviewed by the Security engineer before **E06-T03** finalises the ADR.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no user surface. One intersection worth recording: `role="application"` on the chart wrapper (`26-…` §12) hands keystrokes to the app, so the shell's global shortcut registry (E10) and the engine's keyboard handling must not create a state where a user cannot escape the canvas. Recorded here as a constraint for E10 rather than a threat.

## Performance notes
Hardening settings are enabled during measurement, and the hardened-vs-unhardened delta is recorded, so the M0 report's numbers reflect a shippable configuration rather than a permissive one.

## Observability
Required controls include: audit-relevant shell events (update applied, update signature failure, deep link refused) defined now so E10 implements them, and the diagnostics-payload field allow-list, which becomes a reviewable constant rather than ad hoc serialisation.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] STRIDE model complete, all six categories addressed, reviewed and minuted with Architect + chart-engine lead.
- [ ] Shell hardening checklist published and handed to **E06-T01** before the matrix runs.
- [ ] Harness shells verified hardened; any exception recorded with its performance implication.
- [ ] Abuse cases for the diagnostics payload executed against E06-D02's spec; field allow-list agreed.
- [ ] Unresolved threats recorded as named constraints on E10/E11 with owners.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated where the model surfaced or retired a risk.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E01` — needs the governance baseline (`SECURITY.md`, CODEOWNERS, the security review process) that defines how a model is recorded and signed off.
- Blocks **E06-T01** (hardened harness shells) and feeds **E06-T03** (criterion 5 evaluation).

## Branch

title: Create M10 storage package: repository Protocols, AppContext wiring, in-memory fakes, import-linter contract
body:
## Context
ADR-0003 states the binding structural rule that makes the whole storage decision reversible: "**all storage access goes through repository interfaces** in `services/api/candleviewer/storage/`. No module issues SQL or ILP directly. This is what makes the hot tier swappable." `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 defines module **M10 `storage`** (`services/api/storage/`, depends only on M1 `config`) as the owner of "Postgres repositories, QuestDB writer/reader, Parquet/DuckDB tier, retention". `20-architecture.md` §3 fixes the module package layout (`__init__.py` exporting only the public interface, `service.py` lifecycle, `models.py` pydantic v2 types, `errors.py`) and §6.2 puts `storage` **first** in the supervisor start order.

This task builds that contract surface before any engine-specific code exists, so E07-T02/T03/T04 are implementations behind it and every other module can be written and unit-tested against fakes from day one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/candleviewer/storage/__init__.py` exporting only: the repository Protocols, `StorageService`, domain models, error types.
- `storage/service.py` implementing the lifecycle contract `async start(ctx: AppContext)`, `async stop(grace_s: float)`, `health() -> HealthReport`, opening/closing the three tier clients and reporting per-tier health.
- `storage/models.py` (pydantic v2): `TimeRange` (integer microseconds UTC), `SymbolStream`, `StreamKind` (`trades | orderbook_delta | orderbook_snapshot | tickers | klines | liquidations | open_interest | funding_rates | bars | footprint_cells | profiles | orderflow_metrics | heatmap_cells`, aligned with `22-api-openapi.yaml` `StreamKind` and `21-database-schema.md` §4), `TierHint` (`hot | cold | auto`), `ExportRun`, `RetentionDecision`.
- `storage/errors.py`: `StorageTierUnavailable`, `StorageExportVerifyFailed`, `StorageSchemaDrift`, `StorageRetentionBlockedByPin`, `StorageDiskCritical` - each with a stable string code used in logs and `system_events`.
- `storage/repositories/` Protocols:
  - `MarketDataRepository` - `write_trades`, `write_book_deltas`, `write_book_snapshot`, `write_tickers`, `write_bars`, `read_bars`, `read_trades`, `read_book_snapshot_at`, `read_book_deltas`, `read_orderflow_metrics`, `read_footprint_cells`, `latest_ticker`.
  - `RelationalRepository` factory exposing per-aggregate repositories (`UserRepository`, `AuditRepository`, ... created by their owning epics; E07 ships the base `UnitOfWork` and session management only).
  - `ColdTierRepository` - `export_partition`, `list_manifest`, `query` (DuckDB), `verify_checksums`.
  - `RetentionRepository` - `policies()`, `plan(dry_run: bool)`, `apply(plan)`.
- In-memory fakes for every Protocol in `storage/testing/fakes.py`, shipped as part of the package's public test surface so other modules import them (`from candleviewer.storage.testing import FakeMarketDataRepository`).
- `AppContext` wiring in `services/api/candleviewer/app.py`: storage clients constructed once and injected (`20-architecture.md` §6.1 - "No module constructs its own dependencies").
- `import-linter` contract in the repo config (extending `E02-T06`): forbidden imports of `asyncpg`, `psycopg`, `sqlalchemy`, `duckdb`, `pyarrow`, `questdb` from any package other than `candleviewer.storage.*` and `backend.db.*`.

## Out of scope
- Any real engine client (E07-T02 Postgres, E07-T03 QuestDB, E07-T04 cold tier).
- Aggregate-specific relational repositories (owned by E09/E27/E29 etc.).
- Retention *logic* - E07-T05 (this task defines only the Protocol).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the storage package with only fakes registered
When the app supervisor boots with CV_STORAGE_BACKEND=fake
Then storage starts first, health() reports all three tiers as "fake/healthy", and the app reaches SelfCheck without any database container running

Given a module outside M10
When it adds `import asyncpg` and CI runs
Then the import-linter contract fails the build with a message naming ADR-0003

Given FakeMarketDataRepository
When a contract test suite written once is parametrized over [fake] today and [questdb, timescale] later
Then the same suite passes unchanged, proving the Protocol is engine-agnostic

Given storage.stop(grace_s=5) is called while a write is in flight
When the grace window elapses
Then in-flight writes are awaited or cancelled deterministically, connections are closed, and no "Event loop is closed" warning is emitted

Given a tier client fails to connect at boot
When health() is called
Then it returns degraded for that tier with the StorageTierUnavailable code, and the supervisor refuses readiness rather than serving with a silently missing tier
```

## Technical notes / design
Protocols, not ABCs, so implementations need no inheritance and fakes stay trivial:
```python
class MarketDataRepository(Protocol):
    async def write_trades(self, rows: Sequence[TradeRow]) -> None: ...
    async def read_bars(self, sym: str, family: BarFamily, param: str,
                        rng: TimeRange, tier: TierHint = "auto") -> list[BarRow]: ...
    async def read_book_snapshot_at(self, sym: str, ts_us: int,
                                    depth: int) -> BookSnapshotRow | None: ...
```
Every read method takes `TierHint`; the `auto` resolution lives in E07-T05's router, not in call sites. Write methods are batch-only (`Sequence[...]`) on purpose - a per-row API would make the ILP batching budget of §4.14 unreachable.

`HealthReport` per tier: `{tier, state: ok|degraded|down, latency_ms, detail}`. Readiness (`/readyz`, E04) requires `postgres=ok`; `questdb` degraded is allowed to serve reads-from-cold but must surface on the health screen; `cold` degraded blocks export only.

Config is read exclusively from M1 (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3195 `ParquetConfig` and siblings). The package must not call `os.environ` directly - checked by a unit test.

## Test plan
- Unit: Protocol conformance test (`typing.runtime_checkable` + a structural assertion per implementation), fake behaviour (round-trip write/read, range filtering, ordering by `ts`, dedup on natural key), error-code stability test (a frozen mapping of exception class -> string code, so log consumers do not break silently), lifecycle test (start/stop idempotency, stop during in-flight write).
- Contract: the shared repository suite that E07-T02/T03/T04 must each pass - authored here, executed there.
- Integration: app boots with fakes and no containers.
- Coverage target: >=90% on this package (it is small and interface-dense).

## Security notes
No credentials handled here beyond passing DSNs from M1; DSNs are `SecretStr` and `__repr__` must never render them (SR-006/SR-007 secret type wrapper, SR-120..SR-124 logging redaction). A unit test asserts `repr(settings.pg_dsn)` contains no password substring. The import-linter contract is itself a security control: it is what keeps SQL construction in one reviewed place, limiting injection surface.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Interface shape is a performance decision: batch-only writes, `TierHint` on reads, and returning `list[Row]` of pydantic-lite dataclasses (not ORM entities) for market data, because §13.2 targets (<100 ms for 100k bars) cannot absorb ORM hydration. Market-data rows use `msgspec.Struct`/slots dataclasses, not pydantic models, on the read path - benchmark recorded in the PR.

## Observability
Registers the metric names the implementations will populate: `questdb_write_seconds`, `questdb_ilp_rows_total`, `pg_pool_in_use`, `pg_query_seconds`, `storage_tier_health{tier}` (`20-architecture.md` §12). Structured log context keys `tier`, `stream`, `symbol`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] AC verified by tests; coverage >=90% on the package.
- [ ] `import-linter` contract merged and demonstrated failing on a deliberate violation (screenshot/CI link in the PR).
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §5 monorepo layout updated if the final file names diverge.
- [ ] Docstrings on every Protocol method stating the tier semantics and ordering guarantees.
- [ ] 2 approvals incl. code-owner; merged via merge queue.
- [ ] No demo required (internal refactor-class change) - note recorded per DoD §4.2.

## Dependencies
- `E02-T05` module tree M1-M24 and composition root.
- `E02-T06` import-linter/dependency-cruiser harness to extend.

## Branch
`feat/storage-tier-repositories`; ~250 LOC of interface + fakes, one PR.

## References
- `CONSTITUTION.md` §3 (M10)
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md` (repository rule)
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3, §5, §6.1, §6.2, §12
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §config models

2. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md` (repository rule)

title: UX research: how traders read staleness, gaps and resync in live data
body:
## Context
E08 (Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton, modules M3 Exchange adapter interface, M4 Bybit v5 adapter, M5 internal bus, M6/M7 book reconstruction) is the first epic in the programme that produces *conditionally trustworthy* data. `US-MKT-005` requires a "reconnecting" state rather than stale values, `US-MKT-006` requires gapped windows to be marked as gapped after a sequence gap or REST backfill, `US-MKT-007` requires dependent views to show "resyncing" while the L2 book is re-seeded, and `US-MKT-003` requires watchlist cells to grey out with a stale marker "rather than showing frozen values as if live".

Those three requirements describe a single cross-cutting UX primitive that does not exist yet: a **data-confidence vocabulary** (live / stale / reconnecting / resyncing / gapped / backfilling / delisted). Getting the vocabulary wrong is a trading-safety problem, not a cosmetic one — a frozen price that looks live can cause a real order at a wrong price. This research ticket exists so that the hi-fi work in E08-D02..E08-D10 is grounded in evidence rather than designer intuition, and so the design-system contribution in E08-D04 is defined once rather than re-invented per panel.

The audience is small and known (`10-personas.md`: the Owner/principal trader, and account managers), so this is a qualitative study: structured interviews plus a stimulus-based comparison task, not a statistically powered test.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Research plan and discussion guide covering the stories `US-MKT-003`, `US-MKT-005`, `US-MKT-006`, `US-MKT-007`, `US-MKT-008`, `US-MKT-009`.
- 4–6 sessions (Owner + available managers + 2 external perp traders if recruitable) covering: (a) what they currently do when a feed looks frozen on TradingView/Bybit/DeepCharts; (b) recognition test of 3 candidate visual treatments per state; (c) tolerance thresholds — how long a gap must be before it must be visible at all.
- Stimulus set: static comparison boards for the *stale* and *reconnecting* treatments applied to `SCR-100` Watchlist panel, `SCR-053` Tape panel and `SCR-050` DOM ladder + heatmap panel; and for the *gapped window* treatment on the chart price axis region.
- Findings report at `docs/research/findings/E08-data-confidence.md` with: a recommended state vocabulary (names + definitions + precedence order when two states co-occur), recommended time thresholds (when a cell becomes stale, when a banner escalates), and explicit "do not do this" anti-patterns.
- Decision log entries for anything that contradicts the current wording in `14-screens-catalogue.md` (`SCR-100`, `SCR-152`) so those docs are corrected rather than silently diverged from.
- Input handoff to E08-D02 (wireframes) and E08-D04 (design-system contribution) recorded as comments on those tickets.

## Out of scope
- Any pixel-level or hi-fi visual design — that is E08-D03, E08-D05..E08-D10.
- Order-entry or execution safety research (owned by the E2x trading epics); this study covers *market data confidence only*.
- Quantitative usability benchmarking / SUS scoring — the participant pool is too small to be meaningful.
- Mobile or Android contexts (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Study executed and reported
  Given the research plan is approved by the CDO
  When at least 4 sessions have been run and transcribed
  Then a findings report exists at docs/research/findings/E08-data-confidence.md
  And it defines every state in the data-confidence vocabulary with a one-line definition and a precedence rule

Scenario: Recommendations are actionable by design and engineering
  Given the findings report is published
  When a designer opens E08-D02 or an engineer opens an E08 ingestion story
  Then each recommended state maps to a named condition the backend can actually emit (e.g. last-message age, sequence gap detected, resync in progress, REST backfill in progress)
  And any recommendation the ingestion layer cannot currently detect is filed as an explicit gap with a linked follow-up

Scenario: Evidence contradicts an existing catalogue statement
  Given participants consistently misread the greyed-out stale treatment described for SCR-100
  When the findings are reviewed
  Then a correction to 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-100 is raised in the same sprint
  And the superseded wording is recorded in the decision log rather than deleted silently

Scenario: Colour-only signalling is rejected (edge/failure)
  Given a candidate treatment distinguishes live from stale by hue alone
  When it is evaluated against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  Then it is recorded as rejected in the report with the reason
  And a non-colour redundant channel (text, icon, opacity plus label) is recommended in its place

Scenario: Sessions cannot be recruited
  Given fewer than 4 external participants are available
  When the study is executed with Owner plus managers only
  Then the report states the reduced sample explicitly as a validity limitation
  And the CDO records whether the reduced evidence is sufficient for sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Anchor stimuli in real conditions: use recorded Bybit fixtures (the same fixtures E08 integration tests use) so the shown densities and update rates are realistic, not invented.
- Run the comparison task in a neutral tool (static boards or a Figma prototype); do not build throwaway front-end code.
- Cover the co-occurrence matrix explicitly: stale + delisted, reconnecting + gapped, resyncing + backfilling. Precedence must be total (no ambiguous pairs) or the hi-fi work cannot be consistent.
- Capture *thresholds as numbers*, because they become configuration in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` terms and defaults in the client.

## Test plan
- Peer review of the discussion guide by a second researcher for leading questions before session 1.
- Pilot session (not counted in the 4) to validate stimulus legibility and timing.
- Analysis triangulated by two people coding the transcripts independently; disagreements resolved and noted.
- Report reviewed by: CDO (sign-off), Architect (feasibility of the detectable conditions), and one QA/SDET (testability of the stated thresholds).

## Security notes
- Sessions may expose real account balances or positions if the Owner screen-shares their live terminal — use fixture data and instruct participants not to share account screens; redact any incidental account identifiers from recordings and transcripts.
- Recordings and transcripts are stored in the private research area only; no third-party transcription service that retains data.
- Participant consent recorded for each session.

## Accessibility notes
- Every candidate treatment must be evaluated against `05-accessibility-standard.md`: redundant encoding beyond colour, contrast of the degraded/stale state against the surface (a greyed cell still needs AA contrast for its text), and an announced equivalent for screen-reader users.
- The report must recommend the live-region behaviour: what is announced on entering/leaving each state, and how announcements are rate-limited so a flapping connection does not spam assistive tech.

## Performance notes
- Any recommended treatment must be cheap at watchlist/tape/DOM update rates: the report must flag treatments that imply per-cell animation or per-update layout changes, because `SCR-100` coalesces ticker updates to 4 Hz and the tape/DOM run far hotter.
- Thresholds must be expressed so they can be evaluated with a single timestamp comparison per row, not per-pixel work.

## Observability
- Recommend the analytics events that let us verify the design later: `data_confidence.state_entered {surface, state, duration_ms}` and `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}` (already catalogued on `SCR-151`).
- Note which backend metrics the states depend on (last-message age per topic, gap counter, resync counter) so E08 engineering exposes them.

## Definition of Done
- Findings report merged; CDO sign-off comment recorded and this ticket's Status set to **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done).
- Vocabulary + precedence table linked from E08-D02 and E08-D04.
- Corrections to `14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` raised where evidence contradicts them.
- Validity limitations stated; participant consent on file; recordings stored in the private area.
- Handoff walkthrough held with the designers on E08-D03/D05/D07 and the E08 engineering lead.

## Dependencies
- None blocking; must complete early in Sprint 01 to keep the design-ahead rule (≥2 sprints ahead of the Sprint 02–04 engineering stories).

## Branch
`design/e08-research-data-confidence`

## References

title: Wireframes: market-data connection, staleness and resync states
body:
## Context
Before any hi-fi screen work, E08 needs a single low-fidelity structural pass that decides *where* connection and data-confidence information lives across the app: a global banner (`SCR-152` Disconnected / reconnecting state), per-panel treatments, per-row treatments (`SCR-100` Watchlist panel) and per-field treatments (`SCR-103` Symbol info drawer live block). Deciding this once, structurally, prevents each subsequent hi-fi ticket from inventing its own placement and prevents the classic failure where three different indicators contradict each other on one screen.

The ingestion behaviours that must be representable come straight from the adapter design: WS reconnect with exponential backoff and resubscribe (`US-MKT-005`), sequence-gap detection with REST backfill and a gapped window (`US-MKT-006`), book invalidation and re-snapshot (`US-MKT-007`), paged historical backfill with rate-limit backoff (`US-MKT-008`), and clock-offset drift (`US-MKT-009`).

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Wireframe set (low-fi, greyscale, annotated) in Figma covering:
  - `SCR-152` Disconnected / reconnecting — global banner anatomy, attempt/backoff countdown, "Trading is disabled while offline" and "Your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected" lines, `Retry now` / `Details` actions.
  - `SCR-100` Watchlist panel — stale row/cell treatment, delisted row, subscription-cap state.
  - `SCR-053` Tape panel and `SCR-050` DOM ladder + heatmap panel — per-panel "resyncing" overlay placement (structure only; visual design belongs to the consuming epics).
  - `SCR-103` Symbol info drawer — live block vs static contract-spec block separation, so a stale live field never makes the contract specs look stale.
  - `SCR-147` Admin: exchange connectivity & rate limits — placement of clock-skew indicator and throttled/banned states.
  - `SCR-151` Empty state pattern — the "data not recorded yet" / "backfill in progress" variants.
- A **state placement matrix**: rows = data-confidence states from E08-D01, columns = surfaces, cells = which indicator level (global / panel / row / field) is authoritative, plus the precedence rule when several apply.
- Annotated flow sketches for: disconnect → backoff attempts → reconnect → resubscribe → resync → live; and gap detected → REST backfill → gapped window marked.
- Open-questions list routed to the Architect and the E08 engineering lead.

## Out of scope
- Colour, typography, iconography, motion — E08-D03, E08-D04, E08-D11.
- The DOM/tape/chart panels' own content design (owned by their epics); this ticket only fixes where the confidence layer sits on them.
- Copywriting final strings (drafted here, finalised in E08-D03 with the content reviewer).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every ingestion condition has exactly one authoritative surface
  Given the state placement matrix is complete
  When any data-confidence state is selected
  Then exactly one indicator level is marked authoritative for it on each surface
  And the precedence rule resolves every co-occurring pair without ambiguity

Scenario: Reconnect flow is representable end to end
  Given the reconnect wireflow
  When walked with the E08 engineering lead against the adapter's actual lifecycle (drop, backoff attempt n, resubscribe, snapshot re-seed)
  Then every transition the backend can emit has a wireframe frame
  And any backend transition with no frame is either given one or explicitly marked as not user-visible with a reason

Scenario: A frozen value can never masquerade as live (failure case)
  Given a wireframe for SCR-100 with a symbol whose ticker stream has dropped
  When reviewed
  Then the last value is either visually demoted with an explicit stale label or replaced by a dash with a timestamp of last update
  And no frame shows an unchanged value with unchanged styling

Scenario: Two states at once
  Given a symbol is both delisted and its feed is stale
  When the wireframe is reviewed
  Then delisted wins per the precedence rule and the stale marker is suppressed
  And the frame is annotated with that rule

Scenario: Review sign-off
  Given the wireframes are complete
  When reviewed by CDO, Architect and the accessibility specialist
  Then all blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use the ASCII anatomies already in `14-screens-catalogue.md` (`SCR-100`, `SCR-152`) as the starting structure rather than inventing new layouts — divergence must be deliberate and noted.
- Keep the global banner non-blocking: it must not reflow panel content on appearance (reserve space or overlay), because reflow during a reconnect storm is both ugly and a performance problem.
- Annotate every state with the backend condition that drives it, named exactly as E08 will expose it (last-message age, gap detected, resync in progress, backfill in progress, clock offset > 500 ms per `US-MKT-009`).
- Model the "grace period" from `US-MKT-005` (30 s unsubscribe grace) so panels do not flicker on rapid open/close.

## Test plan
- Structured walkthrough with the E08 engineering lead against the adapter lifecycle (documented above as an AC).
- Design critique with 2 product designers + design-system representative.
- Accessibility pre-review: check that each state has a text equivalent planned and a sensible focus/announcement story before hi-fi starts.
- Cross-check against `18-traceability-matrix.md` rows for `US-MKT-003`, `US-MKT-005`, `US-MKT-006`, `US-MKT-007` to confirm no referenced screen was missed.

## Security notes
- The `Details` affordance on `SCR-152` must not expose internal endpoints, API keys, account identifiers or raw exchange error payloads to non-owner roles; wireframe annotations must state the RBAC-filtered content (Owner sees diagnostic detail; Manager/Viewer see a plain status).
- No wireframe may show an API key, secret or signed URL, even as placeholder text.

## Accessibility notes
- Each state must be annotated with: the accessible name/description, whether it is announced (`role="status"` vs `role="alert"`), and the rate-limit for announcements on a flapping connection.
- The banner must be reachable and dismissible (where dismissal is allowed) by keyboard, and must not steal focus from an in-progress interaction.
- Stale rows must remain readable: contrast requirements are annotated, not left to the visual pass.

## Performance notes
- Annotate which indicators update at what cadence: watchlist 4 Hz coalesced (per `SCR-100`), banner countdown at 1 Hz max, panel overlays event-driven only.
- Forbid per-row animation in the wireframe annotations for surfaces that can hold 200 symbols (`SCR-100` cap) — the treatment must be a static style change.

## Observability
- Annotate the analytics events each state should emit (`data_confidence.state_entered`, `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}`) so instrumentation is specified before implementation.

## Definition of Done
- Wireframe file and state placement matrix published in Figma and linked from this ticket and from `14-screens-catalogue.md` entries touched.
- Walkthrough with engineering completed and open questions closed or explicitly deferred with owners.
- CDO sign-off comment recorded; Status set to **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done).
- Handoff to E08-D03/D04/D05/D07/D09/D10 noted on those tickets.
