title: Hi-fi: SCR-152 disconnected / reconnecting banner and per-panel treatment
body:
## Context
`SCR-152` is the single most safety-relevant surface E08 introduces: it is what the trader sees when the Bybit public WS drops, when the adapter is backing off, when a topic is resubscribing and when the L2 book is being re-seeded. The catalogue already fixes its content (`attempt n, next in n s`, last-data age, "Trading is disabled while offline", "Your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected", `Retry now` / `Details`), so this ticket turns that into a production-ready hi-fi spec with all states, tokens, and RBAC variants — and defines the per-panel degraded treatment that other epics will reuse verbatim.

This design is consumed by the E08 ingestion stories in Sprint 02–04 and, later, by every live surface, so it must be signed off in Sprint 01.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-152` in light and dark themes, at the supported densities from `16-design-system-brief.md`, covering states: connected (banner absent) · degraded (some topics stale) · reconnecting with attempt/countdown · disconnected beyond threshold · resyncing book · backfilling history · clock-skew warning (`US-MKT-009`, offset > 500 ms) · recovered (transient confirmation).
- RBAC variants: Owner (diagnostic `Details` with adapter state, topic list, last error class incl. rate-limit `10018`) vs Manager/Viewer (plain status, no internals).
- Per-panel degraded treatment spec applied to `SCR-050` (DOM ladder + heatmap), `SCR-053` (Tape), `SCR-100` (Watchlist panel) — overlay vs inline, what stays interactive, what is disabled.
- Final copy for every string, content-reviewed; no placeholder lorem.
- Component usage: `CMP-028` Callout / Banner (new variants if needed, routed through E08-D04), `CMP-023` Progress Bar for backfill, `CMP-019` Icon, `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-021` Link, `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge where a value is derived rather than exchange-reported.
- Redline/spec page: spacing, tokens, motion references (pointing at E08-D11), z-index and stacking relative to modals and the command palette.

## Out of scope
- Order-entry disablement behaviour and its copy in the ticket itself (owned by the trading epics) — this ticket only states that trading is disabled and links.
- Replay-mode banners (`SCR-152` is live-only here; replay states belong to the replay epic).
- Motion timing curves themselves (specified in E08-D11; referenced here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All states designed and tokenised
  Given the hi-fi file is complete
  When each of the eight states is inspected
  Then every colour, spacing and type value resolves to a design-system token, not a raw hex or magic number
  And both light and dark themes are present for each state

Scenario: Safety statements are always present when trading is affected
  Given the disconnected or reconnecting state
  When the banner is rendered
  Then it states that trading is disabled and that exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected
  And neither line can be truncated at the narrowest supported viewport

Scenario: Diagnostic detail is role-gated (failure/abuse case)
  Given a Viewer role session in the disconnected state
  When Details is opened
  Then no endpoint, account identifier, API key fragment or raw exchange payload is shown
  And the Owner variant shows the diagnostic content instead

Scenario: Flapping connection does not produce a strobing UI (edge case)
  Given the connection drops and recovers repeatedly within a few seconds
  When the spec is reviewed
  Then the banner defines a minimum visible duration and a debounce before it reappears
  And the announcement policy prevents repeated screen-reader alerts

Scenario: Long outage
  Given the connection has been down beyond the escalation threshold from E08-D01
  Then the banner escalates its severity styling and shows the age of the last data
  And the Retry now action remains available and keyboard reachable

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given review by CDO, accessibility specialist and the E08 engineering lead
  Then all blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- The banner must be implementable as an overlay that does not reflow the workspace (decided in E08-D02); the spec states the reserved region and the behaviour when a modal is open.
- Countdown text is derived from the adapter's backoff schedule — the spec must define rounding (whole seconds) and the wording when the next attempt is imminent (`retrying…`).
- "Last data" age must be defined precisely: age of the newest message across subscribed topics, not per-topic, with the per-topic breakdown in `Details`.
- Rate-limit (`10018`) and exchange 5xx are distinct error classes with distinct copy; both map to the same visual severity but different explanation and recovery hint.
- Provide the degraded-panel spec as a reusable pattern so E12/E16/E17 consume rather than copy.

## Test plan
- Design review + critique; accessibility design review scheduled as part of E08-D12.
- Contrast verification of every state in both themes with a token checker (AA for text, AA non-text for the status iconography).
- Copy review by the content reviewer; truncation test at the narrowest and widest supported viewport widths.
- Walkthrough with QA/SDET to confirm each state is externally observable and therefore testable in Playwright (a stable test id per state is specified).

## Security notes
- Explicit RBAC content split for `Details` (above) — documented in the spec, not implied.
- No raw exchange error bodies surfaced to any role; only mapped error classes from the adapter error taxonomy.
- The banner must never claim trading is safe when the app cannot verify state; copy is reviewed against `R9 Advice boundary` wording rules.

## Accessibility notes
- Banner is `role="status"` when degraded and `role="alert"` when trading is disabled; announcement rate-limited per E08-D01.
- `Retry now` and `Details` are in the focus order immediately after the banner text; focus is not stolen on appearance.
- Per-panel overlays must not trap focus and must expose the panel's state via `aria-describedby` on the panel region.
- All state distinctions carry an icon + text, never colour alone; the stale treatment keeps AA text contrast.

## Performance notes
- Countdown updates at ≤1 Hz; the spec forbids per-frame animation of banner content.
- Per-panel overlays must be a single composited layer with no per-row work, so a 200-row watchlist or a hot tape panel is unaffected.
- The banner must not trigger layout of the chart canvas; annotated in the redlines.

## Observability
- Specify `data_confidence.state_entered {surface, state, duration_ms}` emission points and the `connectivity.reconnect_forced` audited event on `Retry now` (already catalogued on `SCR-147`).
- Specify stable test/analytics identifiers per state for Playwright and for dashboards.

## Definition of Done
- Hi-fi frames, all states, both themes, fully tokenised; redline page complete.
- Copy final and content-reviewed; RBAC variants documented.
- New/changed component variants raised against E08-D04 and accepted by the design-system team.
- `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-152` entry updated where the design diverged from the original description.
- CDO sign-off comment recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done) — at least 2 sprints before the consuming FE story.

- `blocked_by`: E08-D02.

title: Design-system contribution: data-confidence tokens, states and badges
body:
## Context
The data-confidence vocabulary defined in E08-D01 and placed in E08-D02 will be consumed by essentially every live surface in the product (watchlist, tape, DOM, heatmap, chart series, CVD, positions). If it is expressed as ad hoc styling inside `SCR-152` and `SCR-100`, every downstream epic will re-implement it slightly differently and the product will be inconsistent exactly where consistency is a safety property. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 also forbids ad hoc one-off components: "any new component has a design-system entry".

This ticket therefore contributes the vocabulary to the design system as tokens + a small set of catalogued components/variants, so E08 engineering and all later epics consume a single source.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- **Tokens** added to `16-design-system-brief.md`: a `data-confidence.*` semantic token set (live, stale, reconnecting, resyncing, gapped, backfilling, delisted) mapping to surface, text, border and icon roles in both themes, with contrast-verified values.
- **Component contributions** to `15-component-catalogue.md`:
  - `CMP-028` Callout / Banner — new `connection` severity variants used by `SCR-152`.
  - `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge — confirm/extend contract so "estimated" and "stale/gapped" never collide visually (they are different claims: derived vs untrustworthy).
  - A new atom/molecule entry for the per-value freshness marker used by `CMP-161` WatchlistRow, `CMP-036` KeyValueRow live fields and tape/DOM cells — proposed as a design-system entry with full contract (tiers, props, a11y, tokens), allocated an ID by the design-system team.
  - `CMP-026` EmptyState — new `variant="backfill-in-progress"` and confirmation of `variant="recording-not-started"` usage for `SCR-151`.
- **States matrix** documented per component: default, hover/focus where interactive, each confidence state, and the disabled/degraded composition.
- Figma library publication of the above, with the components named exactly as catalogued so handoff (E08-D13) is unambiguous.

## Out of scope
- Motion definitions (E08-D11) beyond referencing the token names.
- Screen-level layout (the hi-fi tickets).
- Building the React components — that is engineering work in the consuming stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Vocabulary exists exactly once
  Given the contribution is published
  When any E08 hi-fi frame uses a confidence state
  Then it references the published token/component and defines no local style
  And a lint of the Figma file reports zero detached instances for these states

Scenario: Contrast holds in both themes
  Given every data-confidence token pair
  When checked against WCAG 2.2 AA
  Then text-on-surface pairs meet 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large text) and non-text indicators meet 3:1
  And any pair that fails is corrected before sign-off, not waived

Scenario: Estimated and stale are distinguishable (edge case)
  Given a value that is both heuristically derived and stale
  When rendered
```

title: Hi-fi: SCR-102 symbol search and SCR-041 quick-switcher from the catalogue
body:
## Context
E08 delivers the instruments-info cache (`US-MKT-001`) that every symbol-selection surface reads from. `US-MKT-002` demands type-ahead results in <=50 ms from the local catalogue with full ARIA combobox semantics, and explicit handling of the v1 scope boundary ("v1 supports Bybit USDT linear perpetuals only") and of delisted symbols. Two surfaces consume this: the global modal `SCR-102` Symbol search and the compact in-chart `SCR-041` Symbol/interval quick-switcher.

These are the first surfaces where E08's catalogue freshness (12-hour refresh, on-demand refresh for unknown symbols, delisted status) becomes visible, so the design must show catalogue state, not just results.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-102` (modal, `Ctrl+P`): idle with recents/favourites, typing with matched-substring highlighting, results with metadata (24 h change, volume), per-result actions (open chart, add to watchlist, open ladder), recording indicator, no-results with the scope reminder, catalogue-stale/refreshing state, delisted result treatment.
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-041` (in-chart quick-switcher): symbol field, interval field, keyboard-only path, delisted banner entry point, narrow-width behaviour.
- Components used and specified: `CMP-048` Combobox / AutoComplete, `CMP-160` SymbolSearchInput, `CMP-213` FuzzyList, `CMP-219` SymbolPicker, `CMP-220` IntervalPicker, `CMP-011` Tag / Chip, `CMP-026` EmptyState, `CMP-021` Link.
- Interaction spec: keyboard map (open, navigate, select, per-result action, escape-and-restore-focus), ranking/highlight rules, and the exact behaviour when the catalogue has not loaded yet.
- Copy for the scope reminder, the delisted explanation and the refresh state, content-reviewed.

## Out of scope
- The command palette `SCR-012` itself (hosts search but is owned elsewhere) - only the shared `CMP-213` behaviour is aligned here.
- Watchlist management flows (`SCR-101`, covered in E08-D07).
- Server-side search/scanner design (`SCR-104`, covered in E08-D08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Keyboard-only operation is fully specified
  Given the interaction spec
  When a keyboard-only path from opening search to switching the focused chart's symbol is traced
  Then every step has a defined key, a visible focus treatment and an announced change
  And Esc closes the modal and restores focus to the previously focused element

Scenario: Scope boundary is explicit on no results
  Given a query matching no USDT linear perpetual
  When the no-results state renders
  Then it states that no USDT perpetual matches the query and that v1 covers linear perps only
  And it offers a next action rather than a bare 'No data'

Scenario: Delisted symbol (edge case)
  Given a symbol whose exchange status is no longer Trading
  When it appears in history, favourites or an existing chart
  Then it is visually marked as delisted with an explanation, is not offered as a new selection, and order entry entry points are absent
  And the frame is annotated with the precedence rule against the stale marker

Scenario: Catalogue not yet loaded (failure case)
  Given the instruments cache is empty or refreshing on first start
  When search is opened
  Then a loading state is shown that does not present an empty result list as 'no matches'
  And a retry path is available if the refresh fails

Scenario: Highlighting does not rely on colour
  Given a fuzzy match with highlighted substrings
  When reviewed against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  Then the highlight uses weight or background plus sufficient contrast, not hue alone

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO, accessibility specialist and the E08 engineering lead have reviewed
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Results come from the local cached catalogue (`GET /api/v1/instruments`, refreshed hourly client-side / <=12 h server-side per `US-MKT-001`); design must make a common-case network round-trip unnecessary - no spinner in the typing path.
- Ranking rule must be specified deterministically (exact prefix > base-asset prefix > substring > fuzzy) so engineering does not invent it and tests can assert it.
- Specify the maximum rendered result count and the virtualisation threshold so the 50 ms budget is achievable.
- Distinguish three different empty-ish states: catalogue loading, no matches, and matches filtered out by a scope rule - they have different copy.

## Test plan
- Keyboard walkthrough by a designer and by QA/SDET against the spec, including screen-reader dry-run of the combobox semantics.
- Copy review; truncation checks for long symbol names and large volume figures.
- Review against `18-traceability-matrix.md` rows for `US-MKT-001` and `US-MKT-002` to confirm every listed component is either used or explicitly not needed.
- Specification of Playwright-stable test ids for each state, agreed with QA.

## Security notes
- Search must not leak the existence of non-permitted data: results are public instrument metadata only; no account, position or key information appears in any result row for any role.
- Query strings are user input rendered as highlighted text - the spec notes that highlighting must be structural, never HTML injected from the query.
- No exchange credentials or internal endpoint names appear in any state, including error states.

## Accessibility notes
- Full ARIA combobox pattern with `aria-activedescendant` per `SCR-102`; result count announced on change; each option announces symbol, base/quote and recording indicator.
- Per-result actions must be reachable without a pointer and must not require a hover-only affordance.
- Focus is trapped inside the modal while open and restored on close; the quick-switcher must not trap focus.
- Highlight and status chips carry text equivalents.

## Performance notes
- Budget from `US-MKT-002`/`SCR-102`: results within 50 ms of a keystroke with no network call in the common case; the spec forbids per-keystroke layout thrash and mandates virtualised lists beyond the stated threshold.
- Metadata columns (24 h change/volume) are read from the cached ticker snapshot, not subscribed per result; live subscription is limited to visible rows if used at all, and that limit is annotated.

## Observability
- `symbol.searched` and `symbol.search_result_opened` analytics events specified with their properties (query length, result count, rank of selection).
- `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}` specified for each of the three empty-ish states so we can detect a catalogue that is failing to load.

## Definition of Done
- Hi-fi frames for both surfaces, all states, both themes, fully tokenised against E08-D04.
- Interaction/keyboard spec and ranking rule documented and agreed with engineering.
- `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-102`/`SCR-041` design sign-off acceptance checklists all ticked in the ticket.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done), >=2 sprints before the consuming FE story.

title: Spike: book depth-tier and cadence policy (200 vs 500) under recorded load
body:
## Context
Bybit linear offers depth tiers 1 / 50 / 200 / 500 at cadences 10 / 20 / 100 / 200 ms (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14.1 `book_cadence_ms`). The plan assumes **200** for DOM/heatmap plus **1** for best bid/ask, but that assumption commits three expensive budgets at once: storage growth, per-symbol memory and CPU. Depth 500 at 200 ms gives a deeper heatmap while *halving* update cadence - a materially different product, not a tuning knob.

R0's exit criterion (24 h soak, memory flat within +/-5%) cannot be planned honestly until this is measured. **Timebox: 3 days**, Architect + ingestion lead. This spike is explicitly not expected to produce production-shippable code.

## Scope / Deliverables
Questions to answer with numbers, per tier (200@100 ms and 500@200 ms), for BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT and one mid-cap symbol over a >=2-hour recorded window:
1. Level-rows/s and bytes/day written to QuestDB `orderbook_deltas`.
2. Resident memory per symbol for `BookState` plus the liquidity ring.
3. CPU per symbol and event-loop lag contribution.
4. Book-apply p50/p95/p99 latency.
5. Practical heatmap depth coverage in price terms (how many ticks from mid are actually populated at each tier for each symbol).
6. Whether a mixed policy (500 for pinned/recorded symbols, 200 otherwise, 1 for watchlist-only symbols) is operationally sane.

Deliverables: a comparison table, a recommendation, **ADR-0016 `book-depth-tier-policy`** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (even if the decision is 'defer'), follow-up tickets against `E08-S05`/`E16`, and a `32-risk-register.md` update for R3.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the chosen policy (`E08-S05` consumes this).
- Heatmap rendering or aggregation design - **E21**.
- Retention/disk budget policy - **E16** (this spike hands it the bytes/day figure).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Decision is backed by measurements, not estimates
  Given the spike is complete
  Then the comparison table contains measured values for all six questions on all three symbols
  And no row is marked "estimated"

Scenario: Decision criteria were set before measuring
  Given the pre-agreed rule "if depth 500 exceeds 0.5 vCPU/symbol or 300 MB/symbol, depth 200 is chosen outright"
  When the numbers are in
  Then the decision follows the rule mechanically and any deviation is justified in the ADR

Scenario: Inconclusive result still produces a decision
  Given the two tiers are within noise on every budget
  Then the ADR records "defer, default 200, revisit at E21 with heatmap evidence" with the trigger for revisiting stated
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure by replaying recorded fixtures through the real `BookState` prototype and the merged bus (`E08-T03`), not against a live socket, so the experiment is repeatable and does not consume the connection budget. Instrument with the E04 metrics registry so the harness and production report the same names.

## Test plan
Not a test-bearing ticket. The harness itself is kept as `bench/book_depth_compare.py` and is re-runnable in CI on demand; measurement methodology is documented so the numbers can be reproduced.

## Security notes
Fixtures used must be public market data only, secret-free, and verified by the secret-scanner before being committed to `packages/fixtures`.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI surface. The chosen tier determines the effective heatmap depth a trader can perceive, so the recommendation is shared with the design track before sign-off.

## Performance notes
The spike *is* the performance evidence for budgets: <=300 MB/symbol memory, <=0.5 vCPU/symbol, book apply p95 <=2 ms (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`).

## Observability
Reuses `book_apply_seconds`, `book_levels_total{symbol}`, `ingest_events_total{stream}`; any gap found in instrumentation is filed as a follow-up against `E08-T06`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All questions answered with recorded evidence; comparison table attached to the ticket.
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed with findings linked so implementers do not re-derive them.
- [ ] Spike branch left unmerged/archived except the promoted benchmark harness.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; `32-risk-register.md` updated for R3.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E08-T03** (bus, to measure end-to-end rather than in isolation). Blocks `E08-S05`.

`spike/e08-book-depth-tier`

body:
## Context
Principle P3 (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §0) requires that Bybit vocabulary exists in exactly one package. That is only enforceable if the **port** is defined and merged before any implementation PR - the interface-first gate of `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10. Every other E08 ticket, and E29 (OMS) later, is authored against this contract.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/candleviewer/exchange/base.py` implementing `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14.1 verbatim:
  - `MarketDataPort` protocol (`instruments`, `instrument`, `subscribe_trades`, `subscribe_book`, `subscribe_ticker`, `subscribe_klines`, `subscribe_liquidations`, `fetch_klines`, `fetch_recent_trades`, `fetch_orderbook`, `server_time_us`, ...), `@runtime_checkable`.
  - `TradingPort` protocol **declared only** (signatures, no implementation) so E29 can be authored against a merged contract.
  - `ExchangeCapabilities` pydantic model with every field of §14.1, incl. `max_ws_topics_per_request=10`, `book_depths=(1,50,200,500)`, `book_cadence_ms={1:10,50:20,200:100,500:200}`, `supports_ws_order_entry`, `trailing_stop_unit="price_distance"`, `has_public_ws`.
- `services/api/candleviewer/exchange/errors.py` - internal taxonomy: `AuthError`, `ClockDriftError`, `RateLimitError`, `InsufficientMarginError`, `InstrumentFilterError`, `DuplicateClientIdError`, `NotFoundError`, `TransportError`, `UnknownStateError`, each carrying `retryable: bool` and `retry_after_s: float | None`.
- `TsUs` alias and the microsecond time convention module (`24-internal-schemas.md` C4).
- Lint rule (ruff custom/Semgrep) enforcing P3: no `retCode`, no Bybit camelCase identifiers outside `exchange/bybit/`; wired into CI as a required check.
- A `FakeExchange` in-memory implementation of `MarketDataPort` for tests of downstream modules.

## Out of scope
- Any Bybit HTTP/WS code (`E08-T02`, `E08-T04`).
- Implementing `TradingPort` (E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Port matches the specification
  Given docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md section 14.1
  When a test compares the declared method signatures against the documented ones
  Then every method, argument name and return type matches and the test fails on any drift

Scenario: Fake adapter satisfies the protocol
  Given FakeExchange
  When isinstance(FakeExchange(), MarketDataPort) is evaluated
  Then it is True and downstream modules can be unit-tested without network access

Scenario: Leak of exchange vocabulary fails CI
  Given a PR that references retCode or orderLinkId in candleviewer/ingestion/
  When the P3 lint check runs
  Then CI fails with a message naming the offending file, line and the principle

Scenario: Unmapped exchange error
  Given an adapter raises an error class that is not in the taxonomy
  When the boundary wrapper handles it
  Then it is re-raised as UnknownStateError with the original preserved as __cause__ and a metric incremented
```

## Technical notes / design
Protocols, not ABCs - structural typing keeps the fake and the real implementation independent. Capabilities are data, never branching: consumers read fields, they never test `exchange == "bybit"` (§14.2 rule 3). All streaming methods are `AsyncIterator`; all methods must propagate `asyncio.CancelledError` cleanly (rule 8).

## Test plan
Unit: protocol conformance, taxonomy exhaustiveness, capability model validation. Contract: the signature-drift test above. CI: the P3 lint check with positive and negative fixtures. No integration layer (no I/O in this ticket).

## Security notes
The taxonomy defines `AuthError` and `ClockDriftError`, both of which will later gate trading; their semantics ('never retry auth failures silently', 'clock drift blocks trading mode') are documented in docstrings now so E29 cannot reinterpret them. No secrets are handled here; `ExchangeCapabilities` must never carry credentials.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI surface. Error classes carry a `user_message` field with plain-language text so downstream UI never renders a raw exception string or an exchange code alone.

## Performance notes
Zero runtime cost by design: protocols are typing-only, and the capability record is constructed once per adapter instance at startup.

## Observability
`exchange_errors_total{class,exchange,env}` counter defined here (incremented by implementations). Every error class carries a stable `code` string used as the metric label and log field.

title: Implement the in-process topic bus with bounded queues and backpressure policy
body:
## Context
Every module of the modular monolith communicates over one in-process bus (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3 bus contract, ADR-0004). The bus is where the backpressure matrix of §4 becomes executable code: *trades and executions are never dropped*; *a book delta is never skipped - the book is invalidated instead*; *state-like topics conflate to latest*. Getting this wrong is the difference between a chart that is late and a chart that is silently wrong - risk **R7 Data accuracy**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/candleviewer/bus/` with `Bus.publish(topic, event)` and `Bus.subscribe(topic, queue_policy)` exactly per the §3 bus contract; topic strings `{env}.{domain}.{symbol?}.{detail?}` with a typed `Topic` helper and wildcard subscription.
- Bounded `asyncio.Queue` per subscriber (default 4096 per topic class) with three policies: `NEVER_DROP` (await, apply real backpressure - trades, executions), `INVALIDATE_ON_FULL` (drop the stream and raise a `StreamInvalidated` signal - book deltas), `CONFLATE_LATEST` (keep newest only - tickers, health).
- Slow-consumer detection: per-subscriber high-water mark, `bus_subscriber_lag` gauge, and a log at a configurable threshold naming the subscriber.
- Deterministic ordering guarantee per topic (single producer per topic, FIFO per subscriber) documented and property-tested.
- Graceful shutdown: `drain(grace_s)` that stops accepting publishes, drains never-drop queues, and reports what was outstanding.
- Benchmark harness `bench/bus_throughput.py` reporting publish->deliver p50/p95/p99 at 5 000 and 50 000 events/s.

## Out of scope
- Cross-process/broker transport (not planned; ADR-0004 keeps it in-process).
- The client-facing WS fan-out and its own coalescing - **E17**.
- Persistence of bus events - **E16**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Trades are never dropped
  Given a NEVER_DROP subscriber whose queue is full
  When a trade is published
  Then publish awaits, ingest_queue_full_total{class="trade"} increments, and no event is lost once the consumer drains

Scenario: Book deltas invalidate rather than skip
  Given an INVALIDATE_ON_FULL subscriber whose queue is full
  When a book delta is published
  Then the subscriber receives a StreamInvalidated marker instead of a partial sequence
  And no delta is silently discarded without that marker

Scenario: State topics conflate
  Given a CONFLATE_LATEST subscriber that is paused for 500 ms while 50 tickers are published
  When it resumes
  Then it receives exactly one ticker and it is the newest, and bus_conflated_total increments by 49

Scenario: Slow consumer is named, not guessed
  Given a subscriber that lags beyond the configured threshold
  Then bus_subscriber_lag records it and a structured warning identifies the subscriber name and topic

Scenario: Shutdown loses nothing that matters
  Given never-drop queues hold pending events when drain(5.0) is called
  Then all pending never-drop events are delivered or the outstanding count is logged and returned
```

## Technical notes / design
One event loop (uvloop), so the bus is lock-free and synchronous on the publish path; the only await point is a full never-drop queue. Publishing is O(number of subscribers of that topic) with a pre-resolved subscriber list cached per topic to keep the hot path free of string matching. Events are immutable frozen models (`24-internal-schemas.md` §2), so fan-out shares references without copying.

## Test plan
Unit: each policy, wildcard resolution, ordering, drain. Property-based: for any interleaving of publishes and consumer stalls, a never-drop stream is a permutation-free prefix-preserving sequence. Perf: the benchmark harness, asserted in CI against a regression threshold rather than an absolute number.

## Security notes
The bus carries no credentials. `Topic` construction must reject user-controlled strings containing wildcards to prevent a future client-facing subscription (E17) from widening its scope by injection - topics are constructed from validated symbol/domain enums only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - the topic bus is a backend in-process component with no UI surface, no rendered output and no user-facing control. Accessibility obligations for the surfaces that consume this bus (staleness banners, watchlist live cells) are carried by E08-D12 and audited by E08-Q05; drop-and-backpressure events emitted here must be expressible as the non-visual-only status text those tickets specify, so the bus exposes a machine-readable reason code rather than a colour/icon hint.

## Performance notes
Budget: publish->deliver p99 <=1 ms at 50 000 events/s with 8 subscribers; zero allocations on the steady-state path beyond the queue slot. Event-loop lag contribution measured and reported by the benchmark.

## Observability
`bus_published_total{topic_class}`, `bus_delivered_total{subscriber}`, `bus_conflated_total{topic_class}`, `ingest_queue_full_total{class}`, `bus_subscriber_lag{subscriber}`, `bus_stream_invalidated_total{topic_class}`. Exported through the E04 registry.

- [ ] Coverage >=85% on `candleviewer/bus/`.

title: UX research: sign-in, 2FA and recovery mental models
body:
## Context
Every human entry into CandleViewer passes through the same five surfaces: SCR-001 Login, SCR-002 TOTP challenge, SCR-003 TOTP enrolment, SCR-005 session-expired re-auth and SCR-006 step-up. They are the first thing a new manager ever sees (SCR-017) and the most frequently repeated interaction the Owner has with the product after the chart itself.

Authentication in a *trading terminal* is not the same problem as authentication in a SaaS app, and that difference is the reason this research exists rather than reusing a generic pattern. `11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-004 requires an idle lock that freezes the UI **while live data keeps streaming underneath**; US-ONB-005 requires a step-up prompt that can appear in the middle of a privileged action; SCR-005 promises that "your layout and unsent ticket inputs are preserved". A trader interrupted by an auth prompt at the wrong moment either loses a trade or, worse, learns to pre-emptively defeat the mechanism. The research must establish where the tolerance line actually is for this Owner and these managers, not where a security checklist assumes it is.

The second unknown is recovery. US-ONB-003 shows ten single-use recovery codes exactly once, hashed at rest, and US-ONB-010 lets the Owner reset another user's TOTP. Recovery-code UX is famously where users fail silently: they click through, store nothing, and discover it months later when locked out. This research establishes what storage behaviour these specific users will actually perform, so D04 can design a gate that matches reality instead of a checkbox that is always ticked without reading.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3 moderated sessions, 45 minutes: the Owner plus up to 2 prospective account managers (P1/P2 in `10-personas.md`), run against a clickable greyscale prototype and a scripted interruption harness.
- Probe set A - **entry**: first sign-in with an invite (US-ONB-006), repeat daily sign-in, sign-in on a second device, sign-in while the account is rate-limited (US-ONB-001 5-failures/15-min lockout copy).
- Probe set B - **interruption**: idle lock firing at 15 minutes with a chart and an unsent order ticket on screen (US-ONB-004, SCR-005); absolute 12-hour expiry firing mid-session; step-up (SCR-006) demanded while rotating an API key. For each: "what do you believe happened to your data?", "what do you do next?", "what would you have wanted to happen?".
- Probe set C - **recovery**: enrolment (SCR-003) with QR and text secret, the once-only recovery-code screen, lost-authenticator recovery, exhausted codes ("contact the owner").
- Findings written to `docs/design/research/e09-auth-mental-models.md`: a ranked list of friction points, verbatim quotes, the observed recovery-code storage behaviour of each participant, and 6-10 **adopted decisions** each phrased as a testable statement a wireframe can satisfy or violate.
- A specific, evidenced recommendation on three open questions: (1) default idle timeout inside the configurable 5-60 min range of US-ONB-004; (2) whether "Remember this device (30 d)" on SCR-001 and "Trust this device for 30 days" on SCR-002 are one decision or two, and how they are worded; (3) whether the step-up grace window (5 min, US-ONB-005) must be visible as a countdown or merely stated.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design: greyscale wireframes begin in E09-D02, hi-fi in E09-D03/D04/D05/D06.
- RBAC denied-state vocabulary - that is E09-D09, which has its own sessions.
- Bybit-side authentication and API-key handling (E27).
- Password policy *content* (breach-list rules are fixed by `04-security-program.md`); only its presentation is in scope.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Interruption tolerance is evidenced, not assumed
  Given all three participants have experienced the idle lock with an unsent order ticket on screen
  When docs/design/research/e09-auth-mental-models.md is reviewed
  Then it states a recommended default idle timeout with the observations that justify it
  And it records what each participant believed happened to their unsent ticket

Scenario: Recovery-code storage behaviour is observed, not self-reported
  Given a participant reaches the once-only recovery-code screen
  When they proceed past it
  Then the report records what they actually did with the codes (copied, downloaded, photographed, nothing)
  And at least one adopted decision addresses the gap between the observed behaviour and the intended one

Scenario: A participant defeats the security mechanism
  Given a participant states or demonstrates a workaround (e.g. keeping a second tab active to avoid the idle lock)
  Then the workaround is recorded verbatim as a finding
  And it is raised with the Security engineer as an input to the E09 STRIDE model rather than designed around silently

Scenario: A finding contradicts a locked document
  Given a finding contradicts 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-001..006 or an NFR in 11-user-stories.md US-ONB-001..005
  Then it is filed as an explicit amendment proposal against that document
  And no wireframe is drawn against the contradicted behaviour until the amendment is accepted or rejected

Scenario: Screen-reader participant path is covered
  Given at least one session is run with a screen reader active
  Then the report records whether the OTP entry, the QR text-secret alternative and the error announcements were usable unaided
```

## Technical notes / design
The prototype is a Figma clickable flow plus a dev-only harness page that can fire the idle lock, the absolute-expiry modal and the step-up modal on command; it must not reach production code. Auth responses are stubbed - no backend is required and none of E09's engineering work blocks this ticket, which is exactly why it sits in Sprint 01.

Validity controls: the interruption scripts are fired in a different order per participant so the severity ranking is not an artefact of ordering; participants are never told in advance that an interruption is coming.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Quality control: two researchers code the transcripts independently for the friction-point ranking and reconcile; any decision supported by a single participant is marked as such in the report rather than presented as consensus.

## Security notes
No real credentials, TOTP secrets, recovery codes or API keys appear in the prototype - fixtures only, and the QR codes encode a throwaway `otpauth://` URI. Session recordings follow `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md`. Any workaround a participant reveals is shared with the Security engineer under the E09 threat-model kickoff (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1).

## Accessibility notes
One of the three sessions is run with NVDA or VoiceOver active per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 8, focusing on the OTP field (announced as one field, not six), the QR text alternative and the `role="alert"` error announcement on failed sign-in. Findings feed E09-D10 directly.

## Performance notes
The prototype's perceived latency is deliberately set to the documented budgets (TOTP verify <=400 ms p95 per SCR-002, step-up token issue <=400 ms p95 per SCR-006) so participants judge the real experience rather than an instant mock.

## Observability
N/A (no production code). The analytics/audit event names the screens will emit (`auth.login.attempt`, `auth.mfa.failure`, `auth.stepup.denied`) are reviewed with participants only to confirm that nothing user-identifying beyond what `21-database-schema.md` `audit_log` already stores is implied.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report merged at `docs/design/research/e09-auth-mental-models.md` with >=6 adopted, testable decisions.
- [ ] Recommended idle-timeout default, trusted-device wording and step-up-grace treatment stated with evidence.
- [ ] Findings presented at Design Review; decisions carried into the E09-D02 wireframe scope with a line-by-line trace.
- [ ] Security engineer has received any workaround findings.
- [ ] Any contradiction with `14-screens-catalogue.md` or `11-user-stories.md` filed as an amendment proposal.

title: Wireframes: end-to-end auth, session and onboarding flow
body:
## Context
E09 introduces eight user-facing surfaces that are only meaningful as a *sequence*: SCR-001 Login → SCR-002 TOTP → (first time) SCR-003 enrolment → (if forced) SCR-004 password change → SCR-010 App shell, with SCR-005 and SCR-006 able to interrupt any authenticated screen at any moment, and SCR-017/SCR-019 wrapping the whole thing for an invited manager. `14-screens-catalogue.md` section 0 draws exactly this chain (`L → T → SH`) as the first flow in the document.

Drawing them individually in hi-fi first would guarantee seams: a back-button that leads nowhere, a state ("expired challenge") that returns to a screen with no matching entry message, an invited user who lands in SCR-003 with no idea they are mid-wizard. This ticket fixes the **structure and state machine** in greyscale, cheaply, so that E09-D03..D06 only have to solve visual and interaction detail inside an agreed skeleton.

The research from E09-D01 is a required input: its adopted decisions on interruption handling, trusted-device wording and recovery-code gating are what the wireframes are measured against.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Greyscale wireframes in Figma (`CV / E09 Auth / Wireframes`) for every screen and every enumerated state:
  - **SCR-001 Login**: idle, submitting, generic error, rate-limited with countdown, account-disabled, server-unreachable (SCR-152 inline variant), plus the server env badge (CMP-075) and build footer (CMP-207).
  - **SCR-002 TOTP challenge**: idle, verifying, invalid code, expired challenge, locked-after-5, recovery-code entry path.
  - **SCR-003 TOTP enrolment wizard**: 3 steps (scan / confirm / recovery codes) plus the re-enrol variant triggered by US-ONB-010 owner reset and by recovery-code consumption.
  - **SCR-004 Forced password change**: policy-shown-up-front, typing, server rejection (reused password / breached password), success.
  - **SCR-005 Session expired / re-auth modal**: default, expiry-during-order-entry, "sign out instead" branch.
  - **SCR-006 Step-up modal**: code only, code + typed confirmation, remaining-grace variant, failure and 3-strike downgrade (US-ONB-005).
  - **SCR-017 Manager/viewer onboarding wizard** (4 steps) and **SCR-019 Setup checklist**, including the role-scoped task sets.
- A single **state-machine diagram** (mermaid, contributed to `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`) covering the full chain including every failure edge: wrong password, disabled account, rate limit, expired MFA challenge, recovery-code consumption forcing re-enrolment, exhausted recovery codes, idle lock, absolute expiry, step-up denial.
- A **states matrix** (screen x state x role) as a Figma page, the artefact E09-D03..D06 and E09-D11 both check against.
- An explicit annotation on every screen naming the CMP-* it is composed from (`18-traceability-matrix.md` rows for US-ONB-001..008 are the source list) and flagging any component that does not yet exist, as an input to E09-D07.
- Proposed amendments to `14-screens-catalogue.md` where the wireframes reveal a missing state, raised as a doc PR rather than an undocumented divergence.

## Out of scope
- Colour, type, iconography, elevation, motion - hi-fi work is E09-D03..D06; motion is E09-D08.
- Admin-side user management screens (SCR-120, SCR-121, SCR-123) - owned by the admin epic; this ticket only draws the *invitee's* side of the invite flow.
- The RBAC denied-state pattern (E09-D09) and the admin re-auth gate SCR-149 (drawn in E09-D06 only as the step-up variant it reuses).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every documented state is drawn
  Given the states matrix is compared against the States bullets of SCR-001..006, SCR-017 and SCR-019 in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the comparison is run at design review
  Then every enumerated state has a corresponding frame
  And any state present in the wireframes but absent from the catalogue is filed as a catalogue amendment

Scenario: No dead ends in the flow
  Given the mermaid state machine
  When each terminal node is inspected
  Then every node either reaches the app shell, reaches an explicitly designed terminal state with a recovery action, or names the human who can unblock the user

Scenario: Recovery-code exhaustion is designed, not deferred
  Given a user has consumed all ten recovery codes and has lost their authenticator
  When the wireframes are walked
  Then a frame exists showing the exact message, the owner-contact path and what the user can still see (nothing) while locked out

Scenario: Interruption preserves context visibly
  Given the SCR-005 wireframe fires over a workspace with an unsent order ticket
  Then the underlying screen is shown frozen and preserved rather than blanked
  And the frame annotates that WS subscriptions pause rather than tear down, per SCR-005

Scenario: Research decisions are traced
  Given the adopted decisions in docs/design/research/e09-auth-mental-models.md
  When the wireframe review runs
  Then each decision is marked satisfied by a named frame, or consciously rejected with a recorded reason
```

## Technical notes / design
The wireframes are assembled from E05's greyscale primitives only - no bespoke boxes - so that the CMP-* annotation is honest and the gap list handed to E09-D07 is complete.

Two structural decisions must be settled here and recorded on the matrix, because they change engineering shape and cannot be discovered in hi-fi: (1) whether SCR-003 enrolment is a standalone route (`/login/2fa/enroll`) or an embedded step inside SCR-017's wizard - the catalogue implies both, and the answer determines whether enrolment is routable and resumable; (2) whether SCR-005 (idle/expiry) and SCR-006 (step-up) share one modal chassis with variants or are two distinct organisms - this determines whether CMP-098 composes CMP-043 or stands alone.

The mermaid diagram is authored to be mergeable into `13-user-flows.md`, not as a Figma picture, so it stays reviewable in PRs.

## Test plan
Design-side verification only: (a) a walkthrough with the Architect confirming every frame's data needs map to an operation that exists in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/auth/login`, `/auth/mfa/verify`, `/auth/mfa/enroll`, `/auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `/auth/mfa/recovery`, `/auth/password`, `/auth/step-up`, `/auth/session`, `/auth/sessions`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`); (b) a keyboard-path dry run on paper - tab order annotated on every frame; (c) a QA review to confirm each state is externally observable and therefore testable.

## Security notes
The wireframes must not introduce a user-enumeration channel: the error copy for wrong-password, unknown-user and disabled-account is reviewed against US-ONB-001's NFR ("no hint about which was wrong") - the disabled-account message is the one deliberate exception the story allows and is annotated as such for the Security engineer to confirm. The rate-limit countdown must not reveal whether the account exists. No frame displays a TOTP secret or recovery code anywhere other than SCR-003 step 1/3.

## Accessibility notes
Every frame carries an annotation layer with: heading level, tab order, focus-on-entry target, focus-return target on dismissal, the `role`/`aria-live` of each error region (per SCR-001 `role="alert"`, SCR-005/SCR-006 `role="alertdialog"`), and the non-colour signalling of each state. Per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 3 no path may be mouse-only, and per WCAG 2.2.1 the idle lock must be preceded by the CMP-098 warning rather than firing silently.

## Performance notes
The wireframes annotate the budgets the hi-fi work must not break: SCR-001 first paint <=1 s cold with no chart bundle on the route (code-split), SCR-002 verify round-trip <=400 ms p95 with auto-submit on the 6th digit and no extra render pass, SCR-003 QR render <=100 ms client-side from the provisioning URI, SCR-005 modal mount <=100 ms.

## Observability
Each frame annotates the audit/analytics event it emits (`auth.login.attempt|success|failure|rate_limited`, `auth.mfa.success|failure|recovery_used`, `auth.mfa.enrolled`, `auth.mfa.recovery_generated`, `auth.password.changed`, `auth.session.expired|reauth`, `auth.stepup.granted|denied`, `onboarding.*`) so the engineering tickets inherit the list rather than inventing it.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Mermaid state machine merged into `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`.
- [ ] CMP gap list handed to E09-D07; catalogue amendments raised as doc PRs.

`design/e09-auth-wireframes`

title: Hi-fi design: Login and TOTP challenge (SCR-001, SCR-002)
body:
## Context
SCR-001 and SCR-002 are the two screens every user sees every day and the only two screens a hostile visitor could ever reach. They therefore carry a double burden: they must be fast and forgettable for the Owner, and they must leak nothing to anyone else. `11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-001 fixes the security behaviour (argon2id, per-account and per-IP rate limiting at 5 failures/15 minutes, constant-time comparison, no user enumeration) and US-ONB-002 fixes the TOTP behaviour (RFC 6238, 30 s step, +/-1 step skew, replay-protected). This ticket turns the agreed wireframe skeleton into the final, buildable visual and interaction specification.

Two details make these screens more than a generic login. First, SCR-001 renders the **server's** environment badge (CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal: "server: DEMO default" / "Live-enabled") before authentication - the user must know which machine they are about to trade on before they commit a credential. Second, the 6-digit field (CMP-204 OtpInput) auto-submits on the sixth character, which means a paste, a typo and a screen-reader interaction all have to behave correctly without a visible submit press.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma frames, dark theme and light theme, at 1280x800 and 2560x1440, plus a 125% browser-zoom pass, for:
  - **SCR-001**: idle, focused, submitting (button busy, fields locked), generic error (`role="alert"`, focus moved to it), rate-limited with a live countdown ("Too many attempts. Try again in 14:32."), account-disabled, server-unreachable inline variant, caps-lock warning on the password field.
  - **SCR-002**: idle, per-digit fill, paste-of-6, verifying, invalid code, code-expiry countdown, expired challenge returning to SCR-001 with its entry message, locked-after-5-attempts, and the "Use a recovery code" alternate entry with its own idle/error states.
- Final composition from published library components only: CMP-200 AuthCard, CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-007 TextInput, CMP-005 Checkbox, CMP-001 Button, CMP-021 Link, CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-207 BuildFooter.
- Final **copy deck** for both screens: every label, helper, error and countdown string, reviewed against the no-enumeration rule and written at plain-English reading level.
- Interaction spec: Enter submits; tab order username → password → remember → submit; OTP auto-advance, paste-fill, Backspace-steps-back, auto-submit on the 6th digit; what happens to focus on every error.
- Redlines and token references for every spacing, colour, radius and type decision (no raw values).
- Updated `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001/SCR-002 entries so the catalogue matches the final artefact exactly (`16-design-system-brief.md` section 13.3.2).

## Out of scope
- Enrolment (E09-D04), forced password change (E09-D05), session/step-up modals (E09-D06).
- Motion curves and reduced-motion variants - specified once for the whole auth band in E09-D08.
- Any new component's full design-system entry - gaps go to E09-D07.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The screen never reveals whether an account exists
  Given the copy deck for SCR-001
  When wrong-password, unknown-username and rate-limited states are compared
  Then the visible message, the layout and the state timing are indistinguishable between unknown-username and wrong-password
  And the Security engineer has recorded that confirmation on the ticket

Scenario: The environment is unmistakable before sign-in
  Given the SCR-001 frame in both themes
  When it is viewed in greyscale and through a deuteranopia simulation
  Then a Live-enabled server is distinguishable from a Demo-default server by text and shape, not colour alone

Scenario: Six-digit entry survives a paste
  Given the SCR-002 interaction spec
  When a user pastes six digits into any cell
  Then all six cells fill, the code auto-submits once, and the spec states that no second submission can be triggered by the subsequent blur

Scenario: Lockout is honest about time
  Given the rate-limited state of SCR-001 and the locked-after-5 state of SCR-002
  Then both show a remaining time derived from a server-provided expiry, annotated as such
  And neither offers a control that appears to retry while locked

Scenario: Zoom does not break the card
  Given the 125% zoom pass at 1280x800
  Then no content is clipped or requires two-dimensional scrolling and the error region remains visible with the field it describes

Scenario: An error moves focus exactly once
  Given a failed sign-in
  Then focus moves to the alert region, the alert is announced once, and returning focus to the form does not re-announce it
```

## Technical notes / design
The route is code-split and must not pull the chart bundle (SCR-001 performance note), so the design may not depend on any engine-rendered surface, background animation or webfont that is not already in the core bundle.

The OTP field is specified as **one** control to assistive technology with six visual cells - the visual treatment must therefore survive being a single focus stop: the "current cell" indication is a rendered caret position, not six independently focusable inputs. `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-204 already binds this contract; this ticket must not contradict it.

The "Remember this device (30 d)" checkbox on SCR-001 and "Trust this device for 30 days" on SCR-002 are resolved per the E09-D01 recommendation - if they remain two controls, the frames must make clear that they mean different things, since one suppresses a password and the other suppresses a factor.

## Test plan
Design verification: axe-style manual audit of the Figma prototype annotations; contrast measurement of every text/background and every focus ring against `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 5 (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text and focus indicators) in both themes; a keyboard-only click-through of the prototype; CVD simulation (protan/deutan/tritan) of both themes. Results attached to the ticket and reused as the baseline for E09-D11 design QA.

## Security notes
No frame may display a password in plain text except behind the explicit CMP-201 reveal toggle; no frame shows a partially masked username as a hint. The build footer (CMP-207) shows version and Tailscale node name - reviewed with Security to confirm that exposing the version pre-auth is acceptable given Tailscale-only reachability (US-ONB-008), and annotated with that decision. Error copy is reviewed against the enumeration rule as an explicit sign-off line, not a general assurance.

## Accessibility notes
Target WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Specific gates: labelled inputs with `aria-describedby` for errors; error region `role="alert"` receiving focus on failure; `autocomplete="username"` / `"current-password"` / `"one-time-code"`; the OTP group carries one accessible name ("Six-digit authentication code"); the caps-lock warning is a polite live region; the countdown updates politely and never more than once per second; no focus trap on either page; the recovery-code path is reachable by keyboard from SCR-002.

## Performance notes
SCR-001 first paint <=1 s cold. The design must not require a blocking webfont load for the first paint, nor an image asset over 20 KB, nor any pre-auth network call beyond `GET /api/v1/system/build`. SCR-002 auto-submits on the sixth character with no extra render pass - the spec must not introduce an animation that delays submission.

## Observability
Frames annotate the events emitted: `auth.login.attempt`, `auth.login.success`, `auth.login.failure` (audited with source IP per US-ONB-001), `auth.login.rate_limited`, `auth.mfa.success`, `auth.mfa.failure`, `auth.mfa.recovery_used` (high severity). The annotation states explicitly that no event carries the submitted password or code.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states drawn in both themes at both resolutions plus the 125% zoom pass.
- [ ] Composed only from published library components; any gap raised to E09-D07.
- [ ] Copy deck complete and enumeration-reviewed with the Security engineer.
- [ ] Contrast + CVD + keyboard audit attached.
- [ ] Accessibility acceptance-criteria template (`05-accessibility-standard.md` section 10) completed and attached.
- [ ] Design QA checklist (`16-design-system-brief.md` section 12) completed and attached.
- [ ] Data/API contract confirmed against `/auth/login`, `/auth/mfa/verify`, `/auth/mfa/recovery`, `/api/v1/system/build`.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001/SCR-002 updated to match the final artefact.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done) and the downstream FE story moved Backlog → Ready with the Figma link attached.

## Dependencies
- **E09-D02** wireframes and states matrix.
- **E05** design-system v0 (tokens, CMP-001/005/007/021/027/075/200/201/204/207 published).

## Branch

title: Hi-fi design: TOTP enrolment, recovery codes and owner reset
body:
## Context
SCR-003 is the only screen in CandleViewer that shows a secret exactly once and never again. US-ONB-003 requires TOTP enrolment on first login and ten single-use recovery codes, hashed at rest, displayed once, with copy and download. US-ONB-010 lets the Owner reset another user's TOTP, which re-enters the same wizard in a re-enrol variant. US-ONB-003's third scenario - all ten codes consumed - ends outside the product entirely ("contact the owner"), and that dead end must be designed rather than discovered.

This screen is where E09-D01's most uncomfortable finding lands: users click past recovery codes without storing them. The design's job is to make the storage step genuinely load-bearing without turning it into a lie the user learns to click through. The catalogue already requires an "I saved them" gate before step 3 can be left; the hi-fi work has to make that gate *earn* its checkbox.

The QR itself has two hard constraints: the quiet zone must stay pure white in the dark theme or scanners fail (CMP-205 explicitly forbids a themed tint), and the secret must always also be available as selectable text so QR scanning is never the only path (US-ONB-003 NFR, `05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma frames, dark + light, 1280x800 and 2560x1440, 125% zoom pass, for:
  - **SCR-003 step 1 Scan**: QR (CMP-205) plus the manual secret in a `<code>` block with CMP-033 CopyButton, issuer/account label as it will appear in the authenticator, and the "can't scan?" path.
  - **SCR-003 step 2 Confirm**: CMP-204 OtpInput, verifying, wrong-code, expired-enrolment-challenge.
  - **SCR-003 step 3 Recovery codes**: CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList with copy / download `.txt` / print, the once-only warning, the "I saved them" gate, and the post-gate confirmation.
  - **Re-enrol variant** (existing factor present): the extra step-up confirmation, the "your old authenticator stops working" warning, and the "old recovery codes are invalidated" warning.
  - **Owner-initiated reset landing** (US-ONB-010): what the *reset user* sees on next sign-in, including who reset it and when.
  - **Recovery-code consumption path**: signing in with a recovery code, the forced re-enrolment that follows (US-ONB-003 scenario 2), and the remaining-codes count.
  - **Exhausted-codes terminal state**: the message, the owner-contact path, and what remains visible (nothing).
  - **SCR-112 Security settings** sections owned by E09: regenerate recovery codes (with the "old codes stop working" warning), re-enrol TOTP, disable TOTP behind step-up.
- Wizard chrome spec: CMP-066 Stepper behaviour, back/forward semantics, and resume-from-server-stored-step (SCR-016 performance note applies equally here - an interrupted wizard resumes from the server, not client memory).
- Copy deck for every string, including the four warnings (once-only, old-authenticator, old-codes-invalidated, exhausted).
- Updated `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-003 and the SCR-112 auth sections.

## Out of scope
- The Admin-side "force 2FA re-enrol" row action on SCR-121 - that is the admin epic's surface; this ticket designs only what the affected user experiences.
- Password change (E09-D05) even though SCR-112 hosts both.
- Motion (E09-D08) and the RBAC denied-state pattern (E09-D09).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The secret is never QR-only
  Given the SCR-003 step 1 frame in both themes
  Then the base32 secret is present as selectable text with a copy control
  And the QR carries an accessible name stating what it is rather than the secret itself

Scenario: The QR stays scannable in the dark theme
  Given the dark-theme step 1 frame
  When the QR quiet zone is measured
  Then it renders on an untinted surface at the contrast the scanner needs
  And the frame annotates that the QR never inherits the theme surface token

Scenario: The storage gate is not a reflex click
  Given a user reaches step 3
  When they attempt to continue without copying, downloading or printing
  Then the design states the exact friction applied and the evidence from E09-D01 that justifies it
  And the codes cannot be recovered after leaving the step, which is stated before the gate rather than after it

Scenario: Re-enrolment invalidates loudly
  Given a user with an existing factor enters the re-enrol variant
  Then the frame states that the previous authenticator and the previous recovery codes both stop working
  And the destructive confirmation names the consequence in words, not an icon

Scenario: Exhaustion is a designed terminal state
  Given all ten recovery codes are consumed and the authenticator is lost
  Then a frame exists showing the message, the owner-contact instruction and the absence of any self-service path

Scenario: A screen-reader user can complete enrolment unaided
  Given the annotation layer for all three steps
  Then each step announces its position, the secret is reachable as text, the OTP group is a single named control, and the recovery codes are a list that can be read item by item
```

## Technical notes / design
The QR is rendered client-side from the `otpauth://` provisioning URI returned by `POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enroll`; the secret does not round-trip for rendering and the design must not require a server-rendered image (SCR-003 performance note, <=100 ms render).

The recovery-code download is a plain `.txt` per the catalogue - the copy deck must specify the file's contents and header line, including which account and server the codes belong to, because a user with two environments will otherwise have two indistinguishable files.

The re-enrol variant is gated by step-up (SCR-006) rather than reimplementing a confirmation - the frames reference E09-D06's modal rather than drawing a second one.

The enrolment route's standalone-vs-embedded decision was fixed in E09-D02; these frames implement that decision and must not reopen it.

## Test plan
Contrast and CVD audit of both themes including the QR quiet zone; keyboard-only completion of all three steps plus the re-enrol variant in the prototype; screen-reader walkthrough of step 1 (text secret), step 2 (OTP) and step 3 (code list); a scanner test - the final QR spec is rendered at the specified size and contrast and scanned with at least two authenticator apps before sign-off.

## Security notes
Highest-sensitivity screen in E09. Hard rules the frames must honour and annotate: the secret and the recovery codes appear in exactly one place each and are never re-displayed; nothing here may be captured in analytics, session replay or a screenshot-based support flow; the `.txt` download and the clipboard are the only exfiltration paths and both are deliberate; the codes are hashed at rest so no screen can ever show them again, which the copy must state as fact rather than warning. The re-enrol and disable paths require a fresh step-up token (US-ONB-005), and "disable TOTP" must never be reachable without it. Reviewed jointly with the Security engineer under the E09 STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Specific gates: QR `role="img"` with a descriptive name plus the text-secret equivalent (this is the named alternative, not a nicety); the stepper exposes `aria-current="step"`; recovery codes are a semantic list, each item individually readable, with a monospace face chosen for character disambiguation (0/O, 1/l); the "I saved them" gate is a real checkbox with a label that states the consequence; all warnings are text, never colour or icon alone; no step depends on a time limit.

## Performance notes
QR render <=100 ms client-side. The design may not require a QR library larger than the budget agreed with FE, nor an animated transition between wizard steps that delays the code field's focus. Step transitions <=200 ms per SCR-017's wizard budget.

## Observability
Frames annotate `auth.mfa.enrolled`, `auth.mfa.recovery_generated`, `auth.mfa.recovery_used` (high severity), `auth.recovery_regenerated`, and the US-ONB-010 owner-reset audit entry, with an explicit note that no event payload contains the secret, the codes or their hashes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All frames and variants drawn in both themes at both resolutions plus 125% zoom.
- [ ] Scanner test passed with >=2 authenticator apps against the dark-theme spec.
- [ ] Copy deck complete including the `.txt` file contents and all four warnings.
- [ ] Security engineer review recorded on the ticket (secret/code handling, step-up gating).
- [ ] Accessibility acceptance-criteria template completed and attached; screen-reader walkthrough logged.
- [ ] Design QA checklist completed and attached.
- [ ] Data/API contract confirmed against `/auth/mfa/enroll`, `/auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `/auth/mfa/recovery`, `/auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-003 and SCR-112 auth sections updated.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done); downstream FE story moved to Ready with the Figma link.

## Dependencies
- **E09-D02** wireframes, states matrix and the enrolment-routing decision.
- **E09-D06** supplies the step-up modal the re-enrol and disable paths reuse (may run in parallel; the link must exist before sign-off).
- **E05** design-system v0 (CMP-033, CMP-066, CMP-204, CMP-205, CMP-206 published).

title: Spike: session, token rotation and revocation model (ADR)
body:
## Context
Two normative documents describe the session model at slightly different levels: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4 (server-side `sessions` rows, refresh-token hash, 12 h absolute, 30 min idle, rotation family revocation) and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1 (`Session` with `idle_expires_at`, `refresh_expires_at` 7 d, `elevated_until`). `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3 additionally requires a **bearer access token presented in the WS first frame**, refreshed in place at `expires_at - 60 s` without tearing down subscriptions, while `20-architecture.md` §5 states "no JWT in localStorage". US-ONB-004 also requires an idle lock that must *not* tear down WS subscriptions.

These constraints interact: a cookie-only design cannot feed the WS first frame; a long-lived access token defeats revocation; a short one causes refresh storms. Getting it wrong is expensive — E27, E29, E34 and E42 all build on the resulting session semantics. The Architect has asked for a timeboxed decision before E09-T01 freezes the schema.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Timebox: 3 days.** Answer, with evidence: (1) access-token format — opaque server-side handle vs signed JWT with `sid`/`jti` — given that revocation must be effective within 5 s (US-ONB-009); (2) storage split — refresh in HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict/Secure cookie `cv_refresh`, access token held in memory only and fetched via `POST /auth/refresh`; (3) access-token TTL and refresh cadence that keep WS re-auth (`23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3) at most once per 10 minutes per connection; (4) idle-lock semantics that keep the socket and subscriptions alive while blocking order entry; (5) rotation-family revocation walk over `sessions_rotation` and its cost at expected row counts; (6) step-up representation — `sessions.mfa_satisfied_at` vs `Session.elevated_until` — reconciled to one field.
- Prototype branch `spike/e09-session-model` with a throwaway FastAPI + Postgres harness measuring revocation latency and refresh throughput.
- **ADR** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` recording the decision and the rejected alternatives.
- A written reconciliation note listing every edit needed to `21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1 so the two agree.

## Out of scope
- Production code — this spike is explicitly not shippable; the promoted parts are re-implemented under E09-T01/S03 with full DoD.
- WebAuthn, device trust, and any second access channel beyond the web app.
- Bybit-side key or session handling (E27).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Revocation latency is measured, not assumed
  Given the prototype with N active sessions
  When a session is revoked
  Then the time until the next request and the next WS frame on that session are rejected is recorded, and the 5 s requirement of US-ONB-009 is shown met or the design is changed

Scenario: Refresh cadence does not storm the WS layer
  Given the chosen access-token TTL
  When 20 concurrent clients run for one hour in the harness
  Then the measured re-auth frame rate per connection is at most one per 10 minutes and no reconnect is triggered by refresh

Scenario: Rotated token reuse kills the family
  Given a refresh token that has already been rotated
  When it is presented again
  Then every session in its rotation family is revoked and the event is emitted as auth.refresh_reuse_detected at severity critical

Scenario: The decision is recorded even if it is to defer
  When the timebox expires
  Then an ADR exists stating the decision or an explicit deferral with what further data is needed

Scenario: The two schema documents are made to agree
  Then the note enumerates the exact field-level divergences between 21-database-schema.md 3.1.4 and 24-internal-schemas.md 15.1 and the chosen resolution for each
```

## Technical notes / design
Decision criteria agreed up front: if opaque handles meet p99 < 2 ms lookup with the per-request revocation check, they win outright over JWT (simpler revocation, no key rotation burden); JWT is chosen only if the measured lookup cost materially threatens the API latency budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. Cookie attributes are non-negotiable (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Secure`, `Path=/api/v1/auth`) per `04-security-program.md`.

## Test plan
Harness-level only: a load script for refresh throughput, a revocation-latency probe, and a reuse-detection assertion. No coverage gate applies to throwaway spike code; the harness is archived, not merged.

## Security notes
Threats weighed explicitly: token theft via XSS (argues against localStorage), CSRF (argues for SameSite=Strict plus an origin check), replay of rotated tokens, revocation lag, and step-up downgrade. Findings feed the E09 STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no user interface is produced. Stated explicitly rather than skipped, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §1.

## Performance notes
Record: session-lookup p50/p99, refresh endpoint throughput, rotation-family walk cost at 10k rows, and the projected WS re-auth frame rate. These numbers become the budget line for E09-S03.

## Observability
The harness emits the metric names proposed for production (`auth_sessions_active`, `auth_refresh_reuse_total`, `auth_revocation_latency_ms`) so the spike also validates that the chosen model is measurable.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2: questions answered with recorded evidence, ADR merged in `27-adrs/`, follow-up edits filed against E09-T01 and E09-S03, spike branch archived unmerged, findings presented at Sprint Review, `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E03** (CI/CD and a runnable Postgres in dev).

## Branch
`spike/e09-session-model`

## References
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3, §9.5; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`, `/auth/sessions`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-004, US-ONB-009; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

title: Postgres migration: identity, sessions, MFA and RBAC tables
body:
## Context
Every other ticket in E09 — and E27, E29, E39 and E42 after it — reads or writes the identity tables. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 specifies them exactly: `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_methods`, `mfa_challenges`, `recovery_codes`, together with the enums (`user_status`, `role_name`, `mfa_method_kind`), the check constraints, the partial unique indexes, and the **owner-floor** deferred constraint trigger `trg_owner_floor` that refuses any change leaving zero active owners. Without this migration nothing else in the Epic can start, so it is the first implementation ticket after the session-model ADR.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating, verbatim against `21-database-schema.md` §3.1: enums `user_status`, `role_name`, `mfa_method_kind`; domains `citext`, `sha256_hex`; tables `users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_methods`, `mfa_challenges`, `recovery_codes`; all listed indexes (`ux_users_email`, `ux_users_username`, `ix_users_status`, `ix_role_permissions_perm`, `ix_user_roles_role`, `ix_uaa_account`, `ix_uaa_frozen`, `ix_sessions_user_live`, `ix_sessions_expiry`, `ux_mfa_webauthn_cred`, `ix_mfa_user_active`, `ix_mfa_ch_user_open`, `ix_recovery_unused`).
- All CHECK constraints from the document, including `users_pwd_argon` (`password_hash LIKE '$argon2id$%'`), `uaa_trade_implies_view`, `sessions_expiry`, `mfa_totp_shape`, `mfa_wa_shape`, `mfa_ch_purpose`.
- `trg_owner_floor` deferred constraint trigger on `user_roles` and `users` raising SQLSTATE 23514.
- Column `COMMENT`s marking SECRET and PII columns exactly as the document does (`users.password_hash`, `users.email`, `sessions.ip`, `sessions.user_agent`, `sessions.tailscale_node`, `mfa_methods.secret_enc`, `recovery_codes.code_hash`, `mfa_challenges.nonce`).
- **Seed**: the three system roles (`owner`, `manager`, `viewer`) with `is_system = true`, and the permission rows generated from the `x-rbac.permissions` blocks of `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` with `is_dangerous` set for the step-up-requiring codes.
- Nightly cleanup job deleting `mfa_challenges` older than 24 h (retention policy, `21-database-schema.md` §3.1.5).
- Down-migration, and SQLAlchemy models/typed repository stubs under `services/api/auth/`.

## Out of scope
- `audit_log` and its chain trigger — **E09-T02**.
- `exchange_accounts`, `api_keys`, `account_profiles` — **E27**.
- Any endpoint or business logic; this ticket is schema only.
- Populating `user_account_access` rows (E27/E39 own the grant flows); the table is created here because `sessions`/RBAC scoping references it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and reverses cleanly
  Given an empty Postgres 16 database
  When the migration is applied and then reversed and re-applied
  Then both directions succeed with no manual intervention and the final schema diff against 21-database-schema.md 3.1 is empty

Scenario: The owner floor is enforced by the database
  Given exactly one active user holds the owner role
  When a transaction removes that role or disables that user
  Then the commit fails with SQLSTATE 23514 and the row is unchanged

Scenario: Non-Argon2id password hashes are rejected at the storage layer
  When a row is inserted with a bcrypt-shaped password_hash
  Then the users_pwd_argon check constraint rejects it

Scenario: Soft-deleted users free their email and username
  Given a user is soft-deleted by setting deleted_at
  When a new user is created with the same email
  Then the insert succeeds because the unique indexes are partial on deleted_at IS NULL

Scenario: Permission seed matches the API contract
  When the seed is compared with the x-rbac.permissions blocks of 22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then the code sets are identical and any divergence fails CI
```

## Technical notes / design
Alembic revision under `services/api/migrations/versions/`, naming convention per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`. `citext` and `pgcrypto` extensions are created idempotently. The owner-floor trigger is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` so multi-statement role reshuffles inside one transaction are legal as long as the end state is valid. The permission seed is generated, not hand-written, by `tools/rbac/generate.py` (built in E09-T03) — for this ticket the generator's output is committed as a checked-in fixture and the drift check wired in T03.

## Test plan
