title: Tailscale-only reachability self-check and CIDR guard (US-ONB-008)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-008 (Must) requires the backend to refuse connections that did not arrive over the private network, so the terminal is never publicly exposed. `20-architecture.md` §WSL hazards names the specific failure this guards against: a `0.0.0.0` binding leak via Windows `portproxy`, which would silently publish a trading terminal to the LAN. The story is unusual in that it is enforced **before authentication** and can put the whole app into read-only mode, so it is implemented as a platform Task rather than a UI Story, and it lands in Sprint 02 alongside the schema so no later auth work is ever exercised against an unsafe binding.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Boot self-check**: assert no listener is bound to `0.0.0.0` or `::`; log the bound interfaces explicitly at startup. Re-run hourly (sleep/resume on WSL can change the picture).
- **CIDR guard middleware**: requests whose source address is outside the configured Tailscale CIDR (and loopback) are rejected with **403 before authentication** and audited via `audit.emit("net.off_mesh_request", severity="warning")` with the source address. Applies to REST and to the WS upgrade.
- **Read-only degradation**: if the self-check detects a public binding, the app starts (so the operator can see why) in read-only mode — order placement disabled at the OMS boundary, a blocking banner surfaced through the `system` WS topic (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6 `system`), and the condition is non-dismissible until resolved.
- Prometheus gauge `net_binding_safe` (1/0) and the self-check result exposed on the health payload consumed by SCR-137 Admin security centre and SCR-016 first-run wizard.
- `make audit-net` check runnable in CI-on-host, per `20-architecture.md`.
- Configuration: allowed CIDR list and trusted-proxy handling documented in the deployment runbook; the source address is taken from the socket peer, never from a client-controllable header unless an explicitly configured trusted proxy is in front.

## Out of scope
- Provisioning Tailscale itself, ACLs and device approval — infrastructure (E01/E03) and the ops runbook.
- The Admin security-centre screen (SCR-137) — **E42**; this ticket provides its data.
- Per-user IP allow-listing on Bybit API keys — **E27**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Safe binding passes the self-check
  Given the backend binds only loopback and the Tailscale interface
  When it starts
  Then the self-check passes, the bound interfaces are logged, and net_binding_safe is 1

Scenario: Off-mesh request is refused before authentication
  Given a request arrives from an address outside the allowed CIDR
  When it reaches the application
  Then it is rejected with 403 without any credential being evaluated and an audit entry records the source address

Scenario: Public binding degrades the app instead of trading unsafely
  Given the process is started with a 0.0.0.0 binding
  Then the app starts read-only, order placement is refused at the OMS boundary, a blocking banner is published on the system topic and net_binding_safe is 0

Scenario: A header cannot forge an on-mesh source
  Given no trusted proxy is configured
  When an off-mesh request sets X-Forwarded-For to a Tailscale address
  Then the header is ignored, the socket peer address is used, and the request is still rejected

Scenario: Drift after resume is caught
  Given the host sleeps and resumes with a changed binding
  When the hourly re-check runs
  Then the new state is detected within the hour and the gauge and banner update accordingly
```

## Technical notes / design
The self-check enumerates listening sockets of the process (and, on WSL, cross-checks the Windows-side portproxy table when the helper is available) rather than trusting the configured bind string, because the leak mode is precisely a mismatch between configuration and reality. Read-only mode is a single process-wide flag consulted by the OMS validator (`20-architecture.md` §3.x `Validator`) so it cannot be bypassed by any route.

## Test plan
Unit tests for the CIDR matcher (IPv4/IPv6, boundaries, loopback, mapped addresses); integration tests binding a test server to `0.0.0.0` and asserting degraded start; middleware tests asserting rejection precedes authentication (a valid session from an off-mesh address is still refused); a spoofing test for the header case; a chaos test toggling the binding at runtime and asserting the hourly re-check reacts.

## Security notes
Labelled `security` and central to the deployment threat model: this is the control that keeps a money-moving application off the public internet. Fail-closed is mandatory — if the self-check cannot determine the binding state, it is treated as unsafe. The 403 response body is deliberately generic (no hint about the allowed CIDR). Audited entries carry the source address, which is PII-adjacent and is retained under the audit retention policy.

## Accessibility notes
The blocking banner it triggers is rendered by CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner / the shell (E10) and must be announced assertively, carry an icon and text (not colour alone), and be reachable in the focus order, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. This ticket supplies the machine-readable reason code and human sentence.

## Performance notes
The CIDR check is an in-memory prefix match on every request: budget < 50 µs p99, no allocation per request. The hourly self-check must not block the event loop — it runs in a thread executor with a 2 s timeout.

## Observability
`net_binding_safe` gauge, `net_off_mesh_requests_total{reason}` counter, structured log at boot listing bound interfaces, and an alert that fires immediately when the gauge goes to 0.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2: AC verified by tests, coverage met, runbook and `20-architecture.md` updated, Security engineer review recorded, demonstrated at Sprint Review by deliberately misconfiguring a staging instance.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-K01** only for ordering within the Epic; functionally it needs the E03 deployment scaffolding.

## Branch
`feat/e09-tailscale-guard`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-008; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.1 (SCR-001, SCR-016, SCR-137); `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` (WSL hazards, `make audit-net`, Validator); `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6 `system` topic; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

title: Wireframe app shell, nav rail, command surfaces and system states
body:
## Context
Low-fidelity structure for every surface E10 builds, resolved before pixels are spent. The screens catalogue already fixes the anatomy (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010 wireframe block, SCR-011..015, SCR-027, SCR-153..159) and the component inventory; these wireframes turn that prose into layout decisions that engineering can be estimated against, and they encode the E10-D01 findings.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
Wireframes (Figma file `CandleViewer — E10 Shell (Wires)`), one frame per state, at 1280x800, 1920x1080 and 2560x1440:
- **SCR-010 App shell**: top bar, nav rail, workspace canvas, right rail, status bar. States: normal, disconnected, degraded, frozen, lockout, read-only (viewer). Role variants owner / manager / viewer with the Admin entry absent for non-owners.
- **SCR-011 Nav rail & workspace switcher**: collapsed (icons) and expanded (labels); >20 workspaces with scroll + search; empty state.
- **SCR-012 Command palette**: empty query (recent + suggested), results grouped (navigate / panel / symbol / action / setting), no-results, RBAC-disabled entries with a reason.
- **SCR-013 Hotkey cheatsheet**: two-column grouped layout, conflict chip, printable variant.
- **SCR-015 Global toast host**: single, stacked, overflow, error (sticky) variants.
- **SCR-027 Floating panel window (Electron)**: title bar with panel/symbol/env, re-dock control, browser fallback notice.
- **System states**: SCR-153 degraded banner, SCR-155 404, SCR-157 version mismatch (non-blocking banner + blocking modal), SCR-159 offline / tailnet-unreachable / backend-unreachable / GPU-unavailable, the 403 surface (CMP-089) and the global error-boundary fallback (CMP-091) in both panel-level and route-level variants.
- A component-usage map listing, per frame, the CMP-* ids consumed, so E05 gaps are discovered now rather than in Sprint 03.

**Absorbed from the withdrawn E10-D01 (R0-gating research only):**
- **Study 1 - environment legibility**: greyscale and colour mock chrome for DEMO and LIVE at 3 m viewing distance on 1920x1080 and 2560x1440, 5 participants (owner + 2 managers + 2 proxies). Gate: 5/5 correct identification in **both** colour and greyscale.
- **Study 2 - panic-control reachability**: accidental-activation count over a 15-minute simulated session across candidate CMP-211 placements, plus time-to-activate when deliberately sought. Gate: zero accidental activations, deliberate activation <=2 s.
- Findings recorded in `docs/design/e10/research-findings.md` and carried into the wireframe decisions in this same ticket.

The navigation card-sort / first-click study over the R-100..R-360 groups and the health-chip vocabulary study are **deferred to E15**, which now owns the workspace switcher and command surfaces they inform.

## Out of scope
- Colour, typography, iconography and elevation decisions — E10-D03.
- Motion specification — E10-D04.
- Any screen owned by another epic (terminal content, admin pages, settings pages).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E10 surface has a wireframe
  When the wireframe file is reviewed against the E10 scope list
  Then SCR-010, 011, 012, 013, 015, 027, 153, 155, 157, 159, the 403 surface and the error-boundary fallback each have at least one frame, and every state enumerated in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md for those screens is drawn

Scenario: Role variants are structural
  Given the owner, manager and viewer variants of SCR-010
  Then the manager and viewer frames omit the Admin entry entirely rather than disabling it, and the viewer frame shows mutating controls in their disabled-with-reason treatment

Scenario: A required component is missing from the design system
  Given a frame needs a component with no CMP-* entry in docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md
  Then it is listed in the component-usage map as a gap with a proposed CMP id, and a follow-up ticket is filed against E05 rather than an ad hoc one-off being drawn

Scenario: Research findings are honoured
  Then each adopted decision from docs/design/research/e10-shell-ia.md is traceable to at least one wireframe element, and any deviation is annotated with a reason
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Environment signal survives the greyscale check before any pixels are spent
  Given the DEMO and LIVE mock chrome frames
  When 5 participants view each at 3 m in both colour and desaturated conditions
  Then all 5 identify the environment correctly in both conditions
  And any frame that fails is re-worked and re-tested before the wireframes are signed off

Scenario: Panic controls are reachable but not trippable
  Given the candidate CMP-211 placements
  When each participant completes a 15-minute simulated session
  Then there are zero accidental activations
  And deliberate activation takes <=2 s, and the winning placement is recorded in the findings

Scenario: A deferred study is not silently dropped
  Given the navigation card-sort and health-chip vocabulary studies were deferred
  When this ticket is moved to Done
  Then an E15 research ticket exists carrying them, referenced from this ticket's Dependencies section
```

## Technical notes / design
Wireframes are greyscale and use the E05 spacing/size variables only — no bespoke colour — so that the E10-D03 hi-fi pass is purely a theming exercise. Frames use auto-layout so the three breakpoints are generated from one source rather than hand-drawn thrice. Each frame carries an annotation layer naming the CMP ids, the route ID (R-###) and the WS topic or endpoint that feeds any live value.

The frames must show that the DEMO/LIVE badge cannot be hidden by any layout or theme option (safety invariant, `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §1.1) and that panic controls carry their confirm treatment (hold / typed) rather than firing on a single click.

Annotate focus order, landmark regions, the skip-link position (CMP-085, first focusable), and the accessible name of every health chip and badge. Draw the 125%-text-scale reflow of the top bar and nav rail (US-SET-007).

## Performance notes
Annotate which regions are 1 Hz-updating (health chips, status bar) and which must never re-render the workspace subtree, so engineering encodes the isolation boundary from the start (budget note on SCR-010).

## Observability

title: UX research: how traders choose, parameterise and trust non-time bars
body:
## Context
E12 introduces a capability that no other epic in the programme introduces: bars whose x-axis is **not the clock**. `US-CHART-003` (volume bars, tick bars) is a Must, `US-CHART-004` (range, delta, Renko, P&F) is Should/Could, and `US-CHART-005` adds sub-minute and custom time intervals on top. `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-042 already states the surface must expose "Volume, Tick, Range, Renko and Point & Figure modes with inline parameter fields", and `CMP-220 IntervalPicker` already carries the a11y note that bar modes "are a separate labelled group with an explanatory note, since they change the meaning of the x-axis".

That note is a design problem, not a copy problem. A trader who does not realise the x-axis stopped being time will misread every drawing, every session boundary and every alert anchored to that chart. Two further trust problems are specific to this epic: (a) non-time bars are built from the **recorded trade tape**, so history is only as deep as the recorder (`US-CHART-003` scenario "Insufficient tick history", `US-CHART-005` "Sub-minute interval"), and (b) changing a parameter triggers a **rebuild from stored prints with a progress indicator** (`US-CHART-004` scenario "Parameter change"), which is a long, cancellable operation the user must understand rather than fear.

This study exists so that E12-D02..E12-D08 are grounded in how the Owner and managers actually reason about these modes, and so the vocabulary used for "partial history", "rebuilding", "aggregated/LOD" and "forming vs closed bar" is decided **once**, before six separate hi-fi tickets invent six variants of it. The participant pool is small and known (`10-personas.md`), so this is qualitative: structured interviews plus a stimulus comparison task.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Research plan and discussion guide covering `US-CHART-002`, `US-CHART-003`, `US-CHART-004`, `US-CHART-005`, `US-CHART-010`.
- 4–6 sessions (Owner, available account managers, and up to 2 external perp/order-flow traders if recruitable) covering: (a) which bar modes they use today and on which platform, and what parameter they reach for first; (b) how they currently discover that a chart is *not* time-based; (c) what they expect to happen to drawings, indicators and alerts when the bar mode or parameter changes; (d) their tolerance for a rebuild that takes seconds.
- Stimulus set: comparison boards of 3 candidate treatments each for — the **non-time x-axis banner/affordance** on `SCR-030`, the **partial-history marker** ("tick data begins here") on the price area, the **rebuild progress + cancel** affordance, and the **LOD/aggregation indicator** required by `US-CHART-001` scenario "Deep zoom out".
- A recommended **bar-mode vocabulary**: canonical user-facing names and one-line descriptions for time / tick / volume / range / delta / Renko / P&F, matching the `bar_type` enum in `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 topic `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, plus the unit label for each `param` (trades, base-asset volume, ticks, signed volume, ticks-or-`atr:14`, `box:reversal`).
- Findings report at `docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md` including recommended defaults per mode, the precedence rule when two states co-occur (e.g. *partial history* **and** *rebuilding*), and explicit "do not do this" anti-patterns.
- Corrections raised against `14-screens-catalogue.md` (SCR-042, SCR-047) and `15-component-catalogue.md` (CMP-220, CMP-222) wherever evidence contradicts the current wording, rather than silently diverging.
- Input handoff recorded as comments on E12-D02 (wireframes) and E12-D09 (design-system contribution).

## Out of scope
- Any pixel-level or hi-fi visual design — that is E12-D03..E12-D08.
- Footprint cell design, profiles and TPO (E18/E19) — this study covers the **price series and its bar construction only**.
- Drawing-tool re-anchoring interaction design (E14 owns the tools; this study only captures the *expectation*, and files the finding to E14).
- Indicator parameter UX (E13) and replay controls (E26).
- Quantitative usability benchmarking / SUS scoring — the pool is too small to be meaningful.
- Mobile/Android contexts (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Study executed and reported
  Given the research plan and discussion guide are approved by the CDO
  When at least 4 sessions have been run and transcribed
  Then a findings report exists at docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md
  And it names every bar mode with a user-facing label, a one-line description and the unit of its parameter

Scenario: Recommendations map to something the backend can emit
  Given the findings recommend a state such as "partial history" or "rebuilding"
  When an engineer opens an E12 story
  Then each recommended state maps to a real condition available from GET /api/v1/market/bars or the bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param} topic
  And any recommendation that no current API or topic can express is filed as an explicit gap with a linked follow-up ticket

Scenario: Evidence contradicts the screens catalogue
  Given participants consistently fail to notice that the x-axis is no longer time in the SCR-042 stimulus
  When the findings are reviewed with the CDO
  Then a correction to 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-042 is raised in the same sprint
  And the superseded wording is recorded in the decision log rather than deleted silently

Scenario: Colour-only or motion-only signalling is rejected (edge)
  Given a candidate treatment distinguishes a forming bar from a closed bar by hue or by a pulse alone
  When it is evaluated against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  Then it is recorded as rejected with the reason
  And a redundant non-colour, non-motion channel (text, glyph, outline weight) is recommended in its place

Scenario: Participants cannot be recruited (failure)
  Given fewer than 4 participants are available in the sprint
  When the study runs with Owner plus managers only
  Then the report states the reduced sample explicitly as a validity limitation
  And the CDO records in the ticket whether the reduced evidence is sufficient for sign-off of E12-D02
```

## Technical notes / design
- Anchor every stimulus in **real recorded Bybit data** — reuse the same recorded fixtures the E08/E12 integration tests use, so densities, tick sizes and print rates are realistic rather than invented. A synthetic tape makes range and Renko bars look far tidier than they are.
- Run the comparison task in a neutral prototyping tool with no CandleViewer branding, so participants react to the encoding rather than to the product.
- Include at least one stimulus at **extreme density** (100 k bars zoomed to fit, where LOD aggregation is active) and one at **extreme sparsity** (a 1 500-contract volume bar chart on a quiet symbol where bars are minutes apart) — these are the two ends E12's renderer must survive and where mode confusion is worst.
- Capture, per mode, the **first parameter a participant types**; those become the designed defaults in E12-D03 and the engineering defaults in the E12 stories.
- Record how participants read the `confirm: false` semantics described in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 ("A client MUST NOT treat it as closed") — the forming-bar treatment is the visual expression of that protocol rule.

## Test plan
- Not a code deliverable; validated by review rather than automated tests.
- Pilot the discussion guide with one internal participant before the first real session; revise and record the revision.
- Each stimulus board is checked against `05-accessibility-standard.md` for contrast and non-colour redundancy **before** it is shown, so the study never legitimises an inaccessible treatment.
- Findings are cross-checked against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.
- Peer review of the report by a second designer and by the Architect for feasibility.

## Security notes
- Sessions use recorded fixtures only; no live account, no API keys and no order-entry surface is shown to any participant.
- External participants sign an NDA; recordings are stored in the private research drive and referenced by ID, never committed to the repo.
- The report must not contain account identifiers, balances, position sizes or key material; screenshots are scrubbed of anything account-scoped.
- No participant PII beyond a pseudonymous participant ID appears in `docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md`.

## Accessibility notes
- At least one participant session must be run against the **keyboard-and-screen-reader path** for changing bar mode, since `CMP-220 IntervalPicker` requires bar modes to be an announced, separately labelled group.
- Every candidate treatment must be evaluated for a redundant non-colour channel; colour-only treatments are recorded as rejected with the reason.
- The report must state, per recommended state, how it is announced to a screen reader (text in the accessible name, a live-region message, or a row in the SCR-045 data table).
- Reduced-motion: any candidate that relies on animation to communicate "rebuilding" must have a static equivalent specified.

## Performance notes
- Stimuli must not promise interactions the engine cannot meet: `US-CHART-005` budgets a timeframe switch at ≤200 ms from cache and SCR-042 budgets ≤600 ms first paint uncached. Any treatment implying instant rebuild of a 1 M-print series is recorded as infeasible (the `US-CHART-003` NFR is ≤10 s for 1 M prints).
- Findings must state the **maximum acceptable silent wait** before a rebuild must show progress; that number becomes the threshold specified in E12-D08 and implemented by the E12 engineering stories.

## Observability
- The report lists the analytics events the designed flows imply, aligned with those already named in the catalogue: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed` (SCR-042), `chart.symbol_changed` (SCR-041), `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason}` (SCR-047).
- Recommends one new event if justified by the findings (e.g. `chart.bar_rebuild_cancelled`) with its property set, so E12's engineering stories can instrument it rather than retrofitting.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus the design-specific gates: research plan approved, ≥4 sessions run (or the reduced-sample limitation explicitly accepted by the CDO), findings report merged at `docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md`.
- Bar-mode vocabulary table merged and cross-referenced to the `bar_type` enum in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Contradictions with `14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` raised as tickets, not left implicit.
- Handoff comments posted on E12-D02 and E12-D09.
- **CDO sign-off recorded on this ticket; Status = Done.** E12-D02 may not leave Ready until this ticket is Done.

## Dependencies
- No blocking dependencies; runs at the very start of the design-ahead window.
- Consumes recorded Bybit fixtures produced by E08 (ingestion skeleton) if available; if not yet available, a captured tape from the E06 chart-engine spike is an acceptable substitute and the substitution is recorded.
- Feeds E12-D02, E12-D03, E12-D08, E12-D09.

## Branch
`design/e12-bar-mode-research` — research artefacts and the findings report only; no application code.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §5 CHART — US-CHART-002, US-CHART-003, US-CHART-004, US-CHART-005, US-CHART-010
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-030, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-047
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-181, CMP-220, CMP-222, CMP-226
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` — `/market/bars` (`bar_type`/`param` table)
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6 — `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, unconfirmed-bar rule
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`, `docs/plan/10-personas.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 (E12 register row), §11 (dependency graph)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-181, CMP-220, CMP-222, CMP-226, SCR-030, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-047, US-CHART-001, US-CHART-002, US-CHART-003
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench (if perf-labelled) · pnpm lint · pnpm typecheck
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e12-bar-mode-research`
- PR title: `E12-D01: UX research: how traders choose, parameterise and trust non-time bars`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E12-D01)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/design, area/chart-engine, priority/p0, design, ux-research, a11y

**Done means**
- [ ] All Acceptance criteria scenarios pass under automated test
- [ ] Coverage floor held for touched packages
- [ ] CI gates (lint, typecheck, security scan) green

**Do NOT**
- No GL calls issued from scene-graph nodes — nodes append to batches only (26-chart-engine-design.md §3.1).
- No allocation in the hot render path; anything per-frame must come from an object pool.
- Do not ship a hover-only or drag-only interaction; every affordance needs a keyboard path (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E12-D01 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.
- Move the issue's Status to `Blocked` in the project board; do not leave it silently `In Progress`.
- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Market-data WS protocol & binary framing
body:
## Context
Every live surface in CandleViewer - chart series, footprint, DOM ladder, liquidity heatmap, tape, CVD, order/position state - arrives over **one multiplexed client WebSocket**. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.1 goal 4 makes freezing that transport an R1 objective precisely so R2 (order flow) and R3 (trading) can *add topics* without renegotiating framing, sequencing or backpressure. R1 exit criterion 7 states it bluntly: "WS protocol is frozen: `23-ws-protocol.md` matches the implementation, contract tests pass, and a deliberate breaking change fails CI."

The contract already exists and is normative: `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (2 689 lines: envelope 3.1, binary format 3.4, lifecycle 4, sub/unsub/ctl 5, topic catalogue 6, snapshot+delta 7, throttling/coalescing/backpressure 8, heartbeats/revocation 9, error catalogue 10, replay 11, JSON Schemas 13-15, conformance matrix 16). This Epic **implements** that document in the API/WS Gateway (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.12, module **M23**) and in the web client, and wires the machinery that makes the document and the code provably identical.

The architectural decision is already made in `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0005-ws-protocol-and-binary-encoding.md`: JSON/MessagePack control plane plus a hand-rolled fixed-layout binary data plane, snapshot+delta with per-topic sequence numbers, no checksums. That ADR carries an explicit validation gate ("Spike S5: at least 40% bandwidth reduction and 30% decode-time reduction, else the data plane stays JSON and this ADR is amended") which E17-K01 discharges in this Epic.

Two properties of this Epic are load-bearing for the whole product:
1. **Bounded memory under a slow consumer** (`20-architecture.md` principle P6, protocol goal G4). A backgrounded Electron window must never be able to grow server memory.
2. **Server-authoritative, revocable authorisation** (principle P8, goal G5). A manager must not be able to subscribe to another manager's accounts even by hand-crafting a raw frame.

Story domain: **MKT**. Backend module: **M23** (API/WS Gateway). Train **R1**, sprints **S05-S06**, so that E11/E12 (engine, bar builders) and E16 (recorder) consume a stable transport from the first week of R1.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories covered (MKT domain, transport slice):** US-MKT-005 (live ticker stream: single upstream subscription fanned out, unsubscribe grace, reconnect), US-MKT-006 (tape stream delivery including gap marking to consumers), US-MKT-007 (order-book snapshot+delta, sequence break to resync), US-MKT-003 (batched `ticker` topic for the watchlist: one subscription, at most 10 topics per subscribe frame as the story's NFR demands). US-MKT-001/002/004/008/009 belong to E08/E12 and are **not** re-implemented here; this Epic only carries their data on the wire.

**Engineering (38 pts, Sprints 05-06)**
- **E17-K01** - discharge the ADR-0005 validation gate: measured binary vs JSON bandwidth and decode time on the reference workspace; resolves open items W1 and W2 of `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.6.
- **E17-T01** - `packages/protocol`: `tools/contracts/extract_ws_schemas.py` producing `ws-schemas.json`, generated Python models and TS types, and the blocking `ws_message_schemas` CI gate.
- **E17-T02** - binary codec: the `CVWB` 24-byte header and body kinds 1-6 (section 3.4), Python encoder plus TypeScript decoder, round-trip property tests and a fuzz corpus.
- **E17-S01** - connection lifecycle: subprotocol negotiation, `hello`/`welcome`/`auth`/`auth_ok`, in-place re-auth, heartbeats, close codes, `bye`-before-close.
- **E17-S02** - `SubscriptionManager`: `sub`/`sub_ok`/`unsub`/`ctl`, the section 6 topic registry and parser, the section 6.3 permission matrix, limits, and mid-connection `revoked`.
- **E17-S03** - `SnapshotService` plus sequencing: per-(connection, topic) sequence domain, `snap`/`d`, the six server-initiated resync triggers, client-initiated `resync` with its rate limit, snapshot chunking above 4 MiB.
- **E17-T03** - `CoalescingQueue` and backpressure: per-family coalescing rules (8.2), adaptive throttle classes (8.3), bounded 8 MiB / 2 000-frame outbound budget and the four-step overflow ladder (8.4).
- **E17-T04** - web client (`apps/web/src/ws`): reconnect with full-jitter backoff, priority resubscription, per-topic gap detection, hidden-tab and off-screen `ctl` throttling, binary decode in a shared worker.
- **E17-T05** - single-source error registry: `tools/errorcodes/generate.py` and the blocking `error_registry_single_source` gate.
- **E17-T06** - observability: `cv_ws_*` metrics, connection-quality spans and the budget #6 assertion.
- **E17-T07** - freeze: reconcile `23-ws-protocol.md` with the implementation, amend ADR-0005 with the measured numbers, add the deliberate-breaking-change CI test.

**Design (8 pts, Sprints 03-06)** - E17-D01 research on how degraded fidelity and disconnection must read to a trader; E17-D02 hi-fi for SCR-152 and CMP-076/077/078/092 with handoff; E17-D03 DES-HEATMAP-01 legibility band; E17-D04 design QA and a11y review of the shipped states.

**QA (12 pts)** - E17-Q01 conformance suite plus black-box plan; E17-Q02 chaos; E17-Q03 k6 load; E17-Q04 E2E, exploratory charter, regression pack and sign-off.

**Security (6 pts)** - E17-X01 STRIDE; E17-X02 review, abuse cases, fuzzing and SAST/DAST rules.

**Screens/components touched:** SCR-152 (disconnected/reconnecting), plus the transport-driven states of SCR-030, SCR-050, SCR-053, SCR-100. Components CMP-076 ConnectionStatus, CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay, CMP-078 StaleDataShade, CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner.

## Out of scope
- **Order entry over WS** - orders/amend/cancel/kill-switch are REST (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`); this Epic carries order *state* only (section 1.2).
- **Bulk history** - windows of bars/footprint/profiles/metrics come from REST `/market/*`.
- **The producers of the data** - Bybit ingestion, book reconstruction and bar building are E08/E12; order-flow engines are E18-E25. This Epic transports whatever those modules publish on the bus.
- **Private topic payload semantics** (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`, `trade_groups`) - the *transport rules* for them (never coalesced, causal ordering S5) are in scope; their content is E29/E34.
- **Replay routing** (`replay_session_id`, section 11) - the `sub` field is accepted and validated here, but the replay clock and session lifecycle are **E26**.
- **Session resumption** - explicitly not in v1 (section 9.3, open item W4).
- Android or any non-web client.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The protocol is frozen and drift is impossible
  Given the implementation is complete
  When CI runs the contracts job
  Then ws_message_schemas, error_registry_single_source and runtime_spec_parity all pass
  And a deliberate breaking change to a frame layout fails the build

Scenario: A trader's workspace attaches and stays correct
  Given an authenticated client subscribes to book.BTCUSDT.50, trades.BTCUSDT, bars.BTCUSDT.time.1 and ticker
  Then each topic delivers a snap before any delta and sequence numbers increase by exactly 1 per frame
  And end-to-end tick-to-pixel latency is under 40 ms p95 locally and backend fan-out add-on is under 20 ms p95

Scenario: A slow consumer cannot hurt the server or other users
  Given a client stops reading its socket for 60 seconds while subscribed to the reference workspace
  Then server memory attributable to that connection never exceeds 8 MiB
  And the documented degradation ladder is followed before the connection is closed with 4429
  And no other connected client observes a sequence gap or latency regression

Scenario: Authorisation is revocable mid-connection
  Given a manager is subscribed to positions for account A
  When the owner withdraws that account grant
  Then a revoked frame naming the account arrives within 1 second and other subscriptions continue untouched

Scenario: Upstream desync never reaches the client as a gap
  Given the upstream Bybit book stream produces a gap in u
  Then the client receives a snap with reason upstream_desync and never a delta applied across the gap
```

## Technical notes / design
Implementation lives in `services/api/app/ws/` per `20-architecture.md` section 3.12: `Handshake` to `SubscriptionManager` to `SnapshotService`/`FeedMultiplexer` to `CoalescingQueue` to `FrameEncoder`. One asyncio TaskGroup per connection with exactly one reader and one writer task (architecture TG5). Bus fan-out is "encode once, send many": a topic's frame is encoded a single time per emission tick and the same buffer is handed to every subscriber, which is what keeps CPU flat in client count.

Config keys (`20-architecture.md` environment table): `CV_MAX_WS_TOPICS_PER_CONN`, plus the limits of section 16.2 surfaced verbatim in `welcome.limits`.

Error codes come exclusively from `23-ws-protocol.md` section 10.2 (28 codes); close codes from section 4.4.

## Test plan
`23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.4 is the master matrix and is implemented across E17-Q01..Q04 and E17-X02: contract (schema parity, binary/structured equivalence, error-catalogue closure), unit (sequence generator, coalescer, book delta application, heatmap bucket selection), integration (upstream gap, revocation, token expiry, replay series), chaos (upstream kill, slow consumer, 5 000 msg/s burst, restart), load (8 connections x 40 symbols x 1 h), E2E (hidden tab, kill-switch), security (query-string token, cross-account subscribe, fuzzed binary bodies). Coverage floor at least 85% on `services/api/app/ws` and `packages/protocol`.

## Security notes
Primary STRIDE areas from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 5: spoofing (first-frame token auth, never in the URL), elevation (topic-to-permission matrix, account-scope narrowing, live revocation), DoS (bounded outbound queue, inbound rate limit, subscription/symbol/connection caps, resync rate limit), tampering (SR-128 bounds-checked binary decode, SR-155 fuzzed decoders). Data classification: market data is internal; private topics are confidential and account-scoped. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
The transport itself has no UI, but it *drives* four accessible states: CMP-076 ConnectionStatus (icon plus text plus colour triad, assertive announcement once per state change and not per heartbeat), CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay (`role="alertdialog"`, focus-trapped, non-dismissible), CMP-078 StaleDataShade (visible "Last update Xs ago" text, never opacity alone), CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner. A degraded-fidelity `connection_quality` notice must be announced as `role="status"`, not `alert`, so a lagging connection does not hijack a screen reader mid-trade.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: #3 WS tick to screen p95 under 100 ms and p99 under 250 ms; #6 backend fan-out add-on at most 20 ms p95. From `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.3: binary book delta decode under 0.15 ms p99; footprint bar (400 cells) under 1.0 ms p99; reference-workspace bandwidth under 350 KiB/s; full re-snapshot under 700 KiB and under 400 ms; upstream_desync resyncs under 1 per hour per topic.

## Observability
`cv_ws_resync_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_overflow_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_clients`, `cv_ws_topics_per_client`, `cv_ws_conflated_total`, per-topic emit latency histogram, connection-quality class gauge. Audit entries for `auth_failed` (warning), slow-consumer close (warning), and every `revoked`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R1 exit criterion 7 demonstrated: doc equals implementation, contract tests green, breaking change fails CI.
- [ ] Budgets #3 and #6 measured and met; section 16.3 client-side budgets recorded.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85% backend/protocol, at least 80% web client.
- [ ] STRIDE finalised and findings triaged; Security engineer sign-off.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-152 and the connection chrome; manual NVDA pass on state announcements.
- [ ] QA epic-level regression and exploratory pass recorded; zero open P0/P1.
- [ ] ADR-0005 amended with measured numbers; `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.6 open items W1/W2 closed.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
- **E02** - `packages/protocol` codegen scaffold and the monorepo task graph (E02-T09 builds the generator this Epic extends).
- **E04** - metrics facade, correlation-id propagation across WS, latency-budget instrumentation.
- **E08** - Bybit adapter and the internal bus: there is nothing to transport until ingestion publishes normalised events.
- **E09** - auth, sessions and RBAC: the `auth` frame validates the same access tokens and reads the same permission model.
- Consumers: **E11**, **E12**, **E16** in R1; **E21**, **E26** in R2 (roadmap graph edges E17 to E11, E17 to E21).

## Branch
`feat/e17-ws-protocol-epic`; one PR per child ticket, at most 400 LOC diff preferred.

## References
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md (the normative contract)
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0005-ws-protocol-and-binary-encoding.md
- docs/plan/20-architecture.md sections 3.12, 4 (P6, P8), 5-7
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md section 5 (R1 scope, exit criteria, quality gates)
- docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md budgets #3, #6
- docs/plan/04-security-program.md section 5, SR-128, SR-155
- docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 4 MKT
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-152; docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-076..078, CMP-092

## Child dependency graph
```mermaid
graph TD
  D01[E17-D01 research] --> D02[E17-D02 hi-fi SCR-152]
  D02 --> D04[E17-D04 design QA + a11y]
  D03[E17-D03 DES-HEATMAP-01]
  K01[E17-K01 binary-vs-JSON spike] --> T02[E17-T02 binary codec]
  T01[E17-T01 protocol package + schema gate] --> T02
  T01 --> S01[E17-S01 lifecycle + auth]
  T01 --> T05[E17-T05 error registry gate]
  S01 --> S02[E17-S02 subscriptions + authz]
  S02 --> S03[E17-S03 snapshot + delta + resync]
  T02 --> S03
  S03 --> T03[E17-T03 coalescing + backpressure]
```

title: Design-QA and accessibility review of the built contributor surfaces
body:
## Context

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI and requires the built artefact to be compared against the design spec by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer, with discrepancies fixed or filed. §8 is explicit that a11y is default-on "for any ticket that ships or changes a UI surface, including owner/admin screens — there is no 'internal tool, a11y doesn't matter' exception".

E01's UI surface is the contributor surface specified in **E01-D01** and built in **E01-T05** (issue forms, issue chooser, PR template) and **E01-T07** (automation comments, which are the automation's entire user interface). This ticket is the verification pass: does what shipped match what was designed, and is it accessible to a screen-reader or keyboard-only contributor? A contributor who cannot file a ticket cannot participate in this project at all — this is an inclusion gate, not a polish pass.

It runs in Sprint 02, one sprint after the build, which is the normal design-QA cadence. Note that D02 also consumes the E01-D01 specification only one sprint after it was produced; that shortfall against the 2-sprint design-ahead rule is covered by the same explicit Architect/CDO waiver, restated in full below so this ticket is self-sufficient.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Design-QA pass** comparing the shipped `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`, `config.yml` and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` against the E01-D01 specification: field presence, order, label wording, help text, required flags, dropdown option text, section headings, and the PR-template checklist ceiling. Every discrepancy either fixed in place (trivial wording) or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*`.
- **Keyboard-only pass** over the real GitHub surfaces: issue chooser → each of the six forms → submit; PR template → fill → submit. Verify reachability, visible focus, logical order, and that no control is operable only by pointer.
- **Screen-reader pass** (NVDA on Windows as primary, per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §12; VoiceOver as secondary if available) over one representative form (Story — the richest) and the issue chooser: are labels announced, is required state announced programmatically, are dropdown options comprehensible out of context, is help text associated with its field, is the error state on a failed submit announced.
- **Rendered-output review** of the E01-T07 automation comments: plain-text readable, status stated in words (not colour/emoji alone), heading/list structure correct, actionable next step present.
- **Governance-document markdown pass**: `CONSTITUTION.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` — single H1, correctly nested headings, header-row tables, descriptive link text, and a prose summary adjacent to every mermaid diagram (rendered diagrams are images without accessible text).
- **Findings report** with severity per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3, where any WCAG 2.2 AA violation is **P2 minimum**.
- Reconciliation: if the build diverged from the spec for a good reason, the E01-D01 spec is updated so the record reflects what shipped (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 docs rule).

## Out of scope

- Fixing GitHub's own product accessibility — out of our control; such findings are recorded as "platform limitation, accepted" with the reason, and only our *content* choices are treated as defects.
- Product screens/components — none exist in E01; the R0 product a11y gate (Storybook + auth/shell routes) belongs to E05/E09/E10.
- axe-core CI wiring — E03 ships the `a11y` job for the web app; GitHub-hosted surfaces cannot be axe-scanned by us, so this pass is manual by necessity, and that constraint is stated in the findings report rather than left as an implied gap.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Built forms match the approved specification
  Given the shipped issue forms and the E01-D01 field-set specification
  When a design-system-trained reviewer compares them field by field
  Then every discrepancy is either fixed or filed as a Bug with a priority label
  And the comparison table is attached to this ticket

Scenario: Every form is completable keyboard-only
  Given a contributor using only the keyboard
  When they navigate from the issue chooser through each of the six forms and submit
  Then every control is reachable and operable with a visible focus indicator
  And no step requires a pointer

Scenario: Required state is announced, not merely shown (failure path)
  Given a screen-reader user submits the Story form with acceptance criteria empty
  When the validation error appears
  Then the error is announced and associated with the offending field
  And if it is not, a finding is raised at P2 minimum with the responsible content fix or an accepted platform-limitation note

Scenario: Automation comments carry no colour-only meaning
  Given a blocked-close comment produced by the E01-T07 guards
  When it is read as plain text with images and emoji suppressed
  Then the decision and the required next step are fully understandable

Scenario: Every governance diagram has a text equivalent
  Given all mermaid diagrams in the governance documents
  When each is reviewed
  Then each has adjacent prose conveying the same information
  And any that does not is fixed in this ticket
```

## Design-ahead waiver (Architect/CDO) — explicit record

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires a linked design artefact to have been **Done for ≥2 sprints** before the consuming ticket starts, *or* an explicit Architect/CDO waiver recorded with a reason. This chain — `E01-D01` (design, Sprint 01) → `E01-T05` (build, Sprint 01) → `E01-D02` (design-QA, Sprint 02) — runs at a 0–1 sprint gap, so the waiver path applies and is recorded here explicitly rather than left implicit in the Kind=Task classification.

- **Waiver granted by:** Architect (repo/architecture owner) and CDO, at Sprint 01 planning; both countersign as a ticket comment before this ticket leaves Ready.
- **Scope of waiver:** the E01 contributor surface only — `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, and the rendered governance markdown. It does **not** extend to any `SCR-*` product screen; every customer-facing screen from E05 onward observes the full 2-sprint rule with no exception.
- **Reasons (all four hold):**
  1. **No Sprint −1 exists.** E01 is the first ticket set of the first sprint of the programme; a 2-sprint lead time is arithmetically unavailable and no sequencing creates it.
  2. **Contributor-facing, not customer-facing.** The audience is the delivery team plus reviewers. Iteration cost is one PR against a YAML file, the feedback loop is hours rather than a release train, and there is no migration, no stored user state and no public commitment to the layout.
  3. **No design-system dependency.** These surfaces are rendered by GitHub's own chrome — the design freedom is information architecture, field set, wording and required flags, none of which consume the design-system v0 tokens delivered in E05. There is no risk of designing against an unbuilt foundation, which is the risk the 2-sprint rule exists to prevent.
  4. **Blocking cost is programme-wide.** Deferring the forms to Sprint 03 means every ticket filed in Sprints 01–02 across E01–E10 is captured without the DoR fields the board automation parses, producing a backlog that must be retro-fitted by hand.
- **Compensating controls (the waiver is not a free pass):**
  - Design lands **first within Sprint 01** — `E01-D01` must be Status=Done before `E01-T05` opens a PR; `blocked_by` enforces the ordering even though the sprint is shared.
  - A **mid-sprint 30-minute design/engineering walkthrough** of the field set replaces the missing soak time; deltas are amended into the D01 spec, not absorbed silently in the build.
  - The **full design-QA and a11y pass still happens** (`E01-D02`, Sprint 02) and the epic cannot reach Done without it — verification is deferred by one sprint, never skipped.
  - Any discrepancy found in D02 is fixed or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*`, so the shortened lead time surfaces as tracked defects rather than silent quality loss.
- **Expiry:** this waiver covers E01 only and sets no precedent. If a second Sprint-01-style exception is requested in R0, the Architect raises it at the R0 retro as a proposed standing amendment to `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §1 instead of granting waivers case-by-case.

## Technical notes / design

Method: scripted walkthrough with a recorded session (screen capture + NVDA audio) so findings are reviewable asynchronously by the CDO and the a11y specialist rather than re-performed. Use the `03-testing-strategy.md` §12 protocol and the acceptance-criteria template in `05-accessibility-standard.md` §10 for phrasing findings.

Where GitHub's rendering limits us (e.g. no control over focus styling in their UI), classify precisely: **content defect** (ours, fix it) versus **platform limitation** (theirs, record and accept). Blurring the two is how a11y debt becomes invisible, so each finding must be explicitly one or the other.

For the markdown pass, a mechanical pre-check (heading-level sequence, table header rows, bare-URL link text, mermaid blocks without adjacent prose) can be scripted quickly and folded into the `governance` job by E01-Q02 if it proves useful — propose it as a follow-up rather than expanding this ticket.

## Test plan

- **Manual a11y**: keyboard-only pass (all six forms + chooser + PR template); NVDA pass (Story form + chooser); plain-text/no-emoji reading of automation comments.
- **Design-QA**: field-by-field comparison table against the D01 spec.
- **Mechanical**: heading/link/table/diagram checks over the five governance documents.
- **Regression**: findings that are fixable in content are re-verified after the fix; a follow-up check is added to E01-Q02 where automatable.
- No unit tests (verification ticket, not code). Coverage: N/A.

## Security notes

Verify, as part of the same pass, two security-relevant content behaviours designed in E01-D01: (a) every form displays the "never paste API keys, tokens, session cookies or real account identifiers" warning, and it is announced by a screen reader rather than being a visual-only aside; (b) the issue chooser diverts vulnerability reports to the private route in `SECURITY.md` and no form invites vulnerability details. A missing or invisible warning is a **security finding**, not a cosmetic one, and is raised at P2 minimum. Data classification: public-internal metadata.

## Accessibility notes

This ticket *is* the accessibility review. Conformance target **WCAG 2.2 AA** per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §1. Specific criteria exercised: 1.3.1 info & relationships (label/field association, heading structure, table headers), 1.4.1 use of colour (status in words), 2.1.1 keyboard, 2.4.3 focus order, 2.4.4 link purpose, 2.4.7 focus visible, 3.3.1/3.3.2 error identification and labels/instructions, 4.1.3 status messages (guard comments and validation errors). Findings use the `05-accessibility-standard.md` §10 acceptance-criteria template and the §11.3 severity taxonomy with P2 as the floor for any AA violation.

## Performance notes

N/A — no runtime surface. The human-time budgets from E01-D01 (Task ≤2 min, Story ≤5 min, PR ≤3 min) are re-measured on the *built* forms during the keyboard pass, since keyboard-only completion time is the honest worst case and would reveal a form that is only fast with a mouse.

## Observability

Findings are recorded as issues with the `a11y` label, which means E01-T07's a11y guard applies to their own closure — they cannot be closed without evidence, which is a pleasing and deliberate self-application of the epic's own control. The findings report is archived under the epic for the R0 quality-gate evidence pack (`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 A11y row).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Design-QA comparison table attached; all discrepancies fixed or filed with priorities.
- [ ] Keyboard-only and NVDA passes executed; session recordings attached.
- [ ] Automation-comment and governance-document passes complete; content fixes merged.
- [ ] Findings report published with severities and a clear content-defect vs platform-limitation classification.
- [ ] Any WCAG 2.2 AA violation is fixed or has a recorded, justified acceptance (P2 minimum severity, never silently closed).
- [ ] E01-D01 spec updated where the build legitimately diverged.
- [ ] Waiver compensating controls audited: confirm D01 was Done before T05’s PR, the mid-sprint walkthrough happened, and every delta reached the spec — any gap recorded as a retro input for the R0 review of the design-ahead rule.
- [ ] **Design sign-off: CDO accepts at Design Review; a11y specialist signs off on the accessibility findings.**
- [ ] Security: the no-secrets warning and report-diversion checks verified; findings routed to the Security engineer if failing.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (this ticket's own verification is the evidence; QA reviews the report).
- [ ] PR(s) with content fixes merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

`blocked_by: E01-T05` (the built forms and PR template), `E01-T07` (the automation comments that form the guards' user interface), `E01-D01` (the specification being verified against). Nothing depends on this ticket, but the **epic cannot reach Done without it** — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires a11y verification for any epic with a UI surface, and §8 removes the internal-tool exemption.

## Branch

`design/gov-design-qa-a11y` for content fixes; the findings report is committed alongside. PR size: small.

## References

- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 conformance target, §4 colour-independence, §8 screen-reader protocol, §10 acceptance-criteria template
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 severity taxonomy, §12 accessibility testing protocol
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2, §3.2 design-qa, §8 a11y default-on
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §3 Design Review gate
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 quality gates (A11y row)
- E01-D01 specification; shipped `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 conformance target, §4 colour-independence, §8 screen-reader protocol, §10 acceptance-criteria template
2. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 severity taxonomy, §12 accessibility testing protocol
3. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2, §3.2 design-qa, §8 a11y default-on
4. `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §3 Design Review gate
5. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 quality gates (A11y row)
6. E01-D01 specification; shipped `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan/`
- `docs/adr/`
- `docs/research/`
- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what's listed in References.

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint (markdown lint job)`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/gov-design-qa-a11y`
- PR title: "E01-D02: Design-QA and accessibility review of the built contributor surfaces"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/architecture
- Labels: type/task, area/docs, priority/p2-medium, design-qa, a11y, design

**Done means**
- Design-QA comparison table attached; all discrepancies fixed or filed with priorities.
- Keyboard-only and NVDA passes executed; session recordings attached.
- Automation-comment and governance-document passes complete; content fixes merged.
- Findings report published with severities and a clear content-defect vs platform-limitation classification.
- Any WCAG 2.2 AA violation is fixed or has a recorded, justified acceptance (P2 minimum severity, never silently closed).
- E01-D01 spec updated where the build legitimately diverged.

**Do NOT**
- Fixing GitHub's own product accessibility — out of our control; such findings are recorded as "platform limitation, accepted" with the reason, and only our *content* choices are treated as defects.
- Product screens/components — none exist in E01; the R0 product a11y gate (Storybook + auth/shell routes) belongs to E05/E09/E10.
- axe-core CI wiring — E03 ships the `a11y` job for the web app; GitHub-hosted surfaces cannot be axe-scanned by us, so this pass is manual by necessity, and that constraint is stated in the findings report rather than left as an implied gap.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

title: Ship the governance regression pack as a required CI job
body:
## Context

E01 ships five independent checkers (`check-rule-refs`, `check-sot-duplication`, `check-codeowners-coverage`, `validate-backlog`, plus the issue-form schema/parser tests) and four board guards. E01-Q01 proves they work **once**, by hand. Without automation they decay: a new directory lands un-owned, an enum drifts from `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §5.2, a form field is renamed and a guard silently stops finding its section.

`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #20 assigns the rule-reference and single-source-list checks to the `pr-metadata` required check; §9 also requires that required-check names be exact and stable. This ticket assembles E01's checks into one coherent, fast, required job and connects it to E01-T08's protection configuration, closing the loop between "we wrote a rule", "we wrote a checker", and "the checker actually blocks a merge".

## Scope / Deliverables

- **`.github/workflows/governance.yml`** defining a job named exactly **`governance`** (the name is added to `.github/branch-protection.json` by E01-T08, and the reconciliation check in T08 verifies the two agree) that runs on every PR and on `main`, executing:
  1. `scripts/check-rule-refs.sh` (`GOV-002`)
  2. `scripts/check-sot-duplication.py` (`GOV-003`)
  3. `scripts/check-codeowners-coverage.py` (`GOV-001`)
  4. `scripts/validate-backlog.py` (`GOV-004`)
  5. issue-form schema validation + rendered-body parser contract tests (E01-T05/T07 shared fixtures)
  6. `scripts/check-branch-protection-drift.py --offline` (config-vs-§9 reconciliation only; the live-API drift comparison stays on the weekly schedule, since PR jobs must not require an admin credential — `GOV-005`)
  7. markdownlint over governance documents + relative-link resolution
- **Unit-test suite for all `scripts/`** wired into the same job with the ≥85% coverage gate (`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 #3 threshold applied to Python).
- **Regression cases from E01-Q01** — every manually-validated case that can be automated is encoded as a test with a comment naming its originating case id, so each automated check traces to a real observed failure.
- **Canary self-tests** — the job proves it can still fail: a `--self-test` mode runs each checker against a deliberately-broken fixture tree and asserts a non-zero exit. This is the guard against the worst outcome, a green check that no longer checks anything.
- **`.github/workflows/governance-drift.yml`** — weekly schedule running the live branch-protection drift check and a workflow-enabled check; opens a `priority/p1-high` `security`-labelled issue on drift.
- **Artefacts** — ownership report (E01-T04 `--report`) and backlog summary (E01-T06 `--summary`) uploaded per run for diffable history.
- **Runbook section** in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (one paragraph + link): what each `GOV-00n` code means and how to fix it locally.

## Out of scope

- The other 19 required checks in `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 — E03.
- Enabling `governance` as *required* in branch protection — that edit belongs to E01-T08's configuration file; this ticket delivers the job and confirms the name matches.
- Load/perf testing of the product (k6/Locust) — `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` scope, not governance.
- Board-guard integration tests against the live repository — those live with E01-T07; only its pure parser/evaluator units run here.

**Security-control linkage (added per PR #1411 review, AC3):** this ticket is the owning delivery for SR-163 (issue/PR bodies MUST be in the secret-scanning surface, via `validate-backlog`'s secret-pattern scan - `04-security-program.md` §6.17 / G11), for G14's credential-expiry mitigation (the weekly drift job proactively checks the E01-T07 guard credential's validity and alerts before it lapses), and for G17's drift-detection half (alerting if the E01-T08 credential's actual scopes exceed its documented scope). Add explicit test-plan coverage for a credential-expiry-alert case (G14) and a scope-drift-alert case (G17) alongside the existing drift scenarios in the Acceptance criteria above.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: The governance job blocks a non-compliant pull request
  Given a pull request that adds a directory with no CODEOWNERS rule
  When the governance job runs
  Then it fails with GOV-001 naming the offending path
  And the pull request cannot be merged once the job is required

Scenario: The job proves it can still fail
  Given the --self-test mode with deliberately broken fixtures
  When the governance job runs it
  Then every checker returns a non-zero exit against its broken fixture
  And the job fails if any checker reports success against a known-bad fixture

Scenario: The job is fast enough not to be the bottleneck
  Given a normal pull request
  When the governance job runs on CI
  Then it completes in 60 seconds or less
  And the measured duration is recorded as a job annotation

Scenario: The required-check name matches the protection configuration
  Given .github/branch-protection.json and .github/workflows/governance.yml
  When the offline reconciliation check runs
  Then the job name governance appears identically in both
  And a rename in either file alone fails the check with GOV-005

Scenario: Backlog drift across epics is caught (failure path)
  Given another epic's backlog file introduces a blocked_by pointing at a key that does not exist
  When the governance job runs on that pull request
  Then validate-backlog fails with GOV-004 naming the unresolvable dependency
  And the pull request is blocked until it is fixed

Scenario: Weekly drift detection opens an issue
  Given someone disables require-code-owner-review in the GitHub UI
  When the weekly governance-drift workflow runs
  Then it opens a priority/p1-high security-labelled issue naming the changed setting
```

## Technical notes / design

Single job, not seven — one required check whose log is read top to bottom, with each checker emitting a clear section header and its `GOV-00n` codes. Seven separate required checks would multiply merge-queue overhead for no diagnostic gain.

Run order is cheapest-first with **no fail-fast**: all checkers run even if an earlier one fails, so a contributor sees every problem in one iteration instead of a drip-feed of CI failures. The job fails if any checker failed.

Exit-code discipline from E01-T01 is load-bearing here: exit 2 (internal error) must fail the job, never be treated as clean. The self-test mode exists specifically because a crashing checker that exits 0 is indistinguishable from a passing one in a green tick.

Python setup avoids a full E02 toolchain dependency (E02 lands in parallel): the job uses `actions/setup-python` with a pinned version and installs only `jsonschema` from a pinned, hash-checked requirements file, so governance CI works before the monorepo tooling exists and does not break when it arrives. All actions pinned to full commit SHAs (`04-security-program.md` §6.13).

`permissions:` is `contents: read` only for the PR job; the drift job additionally needs `issues: write`. Neither needs an admin credential, which is why the live-API drift comparison is split onto the scheduled workflow with its own environment-protected secret.

## Test plan

- **Unit**: all `scripts/` tests, ≥85% line coverage, run inside this job.
- **Contract**: issue-form schema validation and the rendered-body parser fixtures shared with E01-T05/T07 — the check that catches a form change silently breaking a guard.
- **Regression**: automated encodings of E01-Q01's validated cases, each annotated with its originating case id.
- **Meta/canary**: `--self-test` against broken fixtures, asserting each checker fails; a mutation check that removing a checker invocation from the workflow is caught (the workflow lists its checkers in a manifest the self-test compares against).
- **Perf**: job duration asserted ≤60 s, recorded per run.
- **Chaos**: simulate a checker crashing (exit 2) and assert the job fails rather than passing.

## Security notes

A CI job is executable code running on every PR and is therefore a supply-chain surface (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13, §6.14). Controls: least-privilege `permissions:` per job; all actions SHA-pinned; pinned hash-checked Python dependencies; no secrets in the PR-triggered job (so a fork or untrusted branch cannot exfiltrate one); no `pull_request_target`; checkers treat all repository content as data and never execute it. The drift workflow's admin credential lives behind a protected environment and is reviewed in E01-X02. Additional security value delivered: `validate-backlog`'s secret-pattern scan over ticket bodies and the `governance-drift` alert are both detective controls for the R4 live-enablement evidence. Security-engineer review required on the workflow files.

## Accessibility notes

CI output is a read surface for every contributor: failures are written as words with `GOV-00n` codes and an explicit fix instruction, never colour- or emoji-only; GitHub annotations carry file and line so the failure is navigable rather than requiring visual log scanning. Consistent with `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §4.

## Performance notes

**Budget: the `governance` job completes in ≤60 s** (the epic-level budget), protecting R0 exit criterion #2's ≤15 min commit-to-dev pipeline. Per-checker budgets inherited from their tickets: rule-refs and duplication ≤5 s, CODEOWNERS coverage ≤5 s, backlog validation ≤10 s. Duration is recorded per run as an annotation so regression is visible; exceeding the budget is treated as a defect against this ticket, not as an accepted cost — because a slow required check is the thing that makes a merge queue unusable.

## Observability

- Per-run artefacts: ownership report, backlog summary, coverage report, job duration.
- Stable `GOV-00n` codes across all checkers make CI history greppable for trend analysis.
- Weekly drift job as the detective control for protection/workflow tampering, escalating to a P1 issue.
- Metrics worth watching from R0 (noted for the retro): governance-job failure rate by code, median job duration, and the count of `# future:`-marked CODEOWNERS rules still outstanding.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `governance` job live, running on every PR, name matching `.github/branch-protection.json` (reconciliation green).
- [ ] All checkers, unit tests and the coverage gate (≥85% on `scripts/`) run inside it.
- [ ] Self-test/canary mode implemented and demonstrated failing against broken fixtures.
- [ ] Every automatable case from E01-Q01 encoded, each annotated with its originating case id; non-automatable cases listed with reasons.
- [ ] Weekly `governance-drift` workflow live and demonstrated opening an issue on a deliberate mutation.
- [ ] perf: job duration measured and ≤60 s, recorded.
- [ ] Docs: `GOV-00n` runbook paragraph in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; `AGENTS.md` §4 command entries current; no duplicated owned lists.
- [ ] Security: workflows reviewed by the Security engineer (E01-X02), actions SHA-pinned, permissions least-privilege.
- [ ] QA sign-off: QA confirms the automated pack reproduces the manual results from E01-Q01.
- [ ] Demo: a non-compliant PR shown being blocked by the `governance` check at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
