title: Security review of governance automation: tokens, pinning, abuse cases
body:
## Context

E01-X01 models the threats; this ticket verifies that the automation E01 actually shipped mitigates them. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2 require a Security-engineer review comment before any `security`-labelled ticket reaches Done, and §8 states that anything touching the fan-out safety invariant, key handling or RBAC is *always* treated as security-labelled whether or not the label was applied.

E01 ships three privileged things: the board-guard credential (E01-T07), the repository-administration credential used to apply branch protection (E01-T08), and a set of workflows that run on every PR (E01-Q02). `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13 (supply chain) and §6.14 (secrets in CI and developer environments) state the requirements; nobody has yet checked the shipped artefacts against them. Getting this wrong is unusually costly here: a workflow token with excess scope in *this* repository is a path to modifying the code that will later place live orders with real exchange API keys.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Token/permission audit** of every workflow shipped by E01 (`board-automation.yml`, `governance.yml`, `governance-drift.yml`): confirm an explicit `permissions:` block at job level (never repository-default, never `write-all`), that each granted scope is actually used, and that the least-privilege principle holds per job. Any unused scope is removed.
- **Credential review**: for the guard credential and the administration credential — type (GitHub App installation token strongly preferred over PAT, per ADR-0016), scope set, storage (Actions secret / protected environment), who can read it, rotation interval and named rotation owner, revocation procedure, and blast radius if leaked. Recorded in a short table appended to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.14's secret inventory (that document owning the content per C-16.5).
- **Fork-safety review**: confirm no workflow uses `pull_request_target` with a checkout of an untrusted ref; confirm no secret is available to a fork-triggered run; confirm no step interpolates issue/PR body content directly into a `run:` shell (the script-injection class) — content must be passed via environment variables or files.
- **Action pinning audit**: every third-party action pinned to a full commit SHA with a version comment; no floating tags; a pinned dependency list for the Python setup with hashes.
- **Abuse-case execution** — attempt, on a scratch repository, each abuse case written by E01-X01, at minimum: forge a QA sign-off by typing the marker in the issue body; close a `security` ticket using a comment from a non-security member; supply an `a11y` link pointing at an external site; trigger the guard with the credential revoked (fail-closed); attempt to have a workflow print the token to the log; attempt a script-injection via an issue title/body containing shell metacharacters; disable a workflow and confirm the drift job notices.
- **Findings report** with severity per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3, each finding either fixed within this ticket (small) or filed with a `priority/*` and blocking the epic if P0/P1.
- **Security sign-off comments** on E01-T07, E01-T08, E01-Q02 and the epic.

## Out of scope

- Reviewing E03's pipeline workflows — E03's own security review (this ticket covers only workflows E01 ships, and says so explicitly to avoid a coverage gap being assumed away).
- Product security controls (key encryption, RBAC, audit chaining) — E09/E27 and the security epics.
- Pen-testing — R4/E43.
- Authoring the threat model — E01-X01.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every workflow job declares least-privilege permissions
  Given the workflows shipped by E01
  When each job is reviewed
  Then each declares an explicit permissions block
  And every granted scope is demonstrably used by a step in that job
  And no job uses write-all or relies on the repository default

Scenario: No secret is reachable from an untrusted trigger
  Given all E01 workflows
  When their triggers are reviewed
  Then no workflow combines pull_request_target with a checkout of the pull request head
  And no secret is referenced in a job reachable from a fork-originated event

Scenario: Issue content cannot inject shell commands (failure path)
  Given an issue whose title contains shell metacharacters and a command substitution
  When the board automation processes it on the scratch repository
  Then the content is treated as data and no injected command executes
  And the review records which mechanism prevented it

Scenario: A forged sign-off is rejected
  Given a Story whose author typed the QA sign-off marker into the issue body
  When the author closes the issue
  Then the guard rejects the close
  And the abuse case is recorded as passed with evidence

Scenario: The guards fail closed without their credential
  Given the guard credential is revoked on the scratch repository
  When a Story is closed without sign-off
  Then the guard does not allow the close
  And it posts a comment stating the gate could not be verified

Scenario: Every action is pinned to an immutable reference
  Given all E01 workflow files
  When third-party action references are listed
  Then each is a full commit SHA with a version comment
  And no floating tag or branch reference is present
```

## Technical notes / design

Review method: static read of the workflow YAML against a checklist derived from `04-security-program.md` §6.13/§6.14 and the E01-X01 threat list, followed by **dynamic abuse-case execution** on a scratch repository. Static-only review would miss exactly the class of bug that matters most — a guard that looks correct and fails open under a condition nobody tried.

Script-injection check specifically: grep every `run:` block for `${{ github.event.*.body }}`, `${{ github.event.*.title }}` and similar direct interpolation of user-controlled fields; the required pattern is passing via `env:` and referencing the shell variable, quoted. This one grep catches the single most common GitHub Actions vulnerability and belongs in the checklist permanently — propose adding it as a Semgrep rule to E03's `sast` job as a follow-up ticket rather than expanding this one.

Credential preference order to assert: GitHub App installation token (short-lived, repository-scoped, revocable, attributable) > fine-grained PAT (repository-scoped, expiring) > classic PAT (rejected). If a classic PAT is in use, it is a finding at P1.

The administration credential (E01-T08) must be reachable only from a `workflow_dispatch` behind a protected environment with required reviewers, never from an automatic PR trigger — verified explicitly, since that credential can rewrite branch protection itself.

## Test plan

- **Static**: permission-block audit table (job → granted → used → verdict); pinning audit table; injection-pattern grep across all workflows; trigger-vs-secret reachability matrix.
- **Dynamic (scratch repo)**: each abuse case from E01-X01 executed with the observed result recorded against the predicted control.
- **Regression**: every abuse case that can be automated is handed to E01-Q02 to encode (e.g. the injection-pattern grep and the pinning audit become checker steps in the `governance` job) so these properties cannot silently regress.
- **Evidence**: transcripts/screenshots for each executed abuse case attached to the ticket.
- Coverage: N/A (review ticket); any code fixes made here inherit the ≥85% `scripts/` gate.

## Security notes

This ticket *is* the security verification for the epic. Handling rules for its own conduct: abuse cases run on a **scratch repository only** — never attempt to disable protection or revoke credentials on the real repository outside a scheduled, announced window; any credential revoked for testing must be confirmed restored with a recorded post-check, since a half-restored guard credential is a silent governance outage. Findings containing exploitable detail are written in the private repo only and, if a live exposure is found (e.g. a token printed in a public-readable log), the incident path in `SECURITY.md` is followed immediately rather than filing an ordinary ticket. Data classification: internal-confidential. Sign-off: Security engineer, with the Owner informed of any P0/P1.

## Accessibility notes

One adjacent check: security-relevant automation output (a blocked close, a drift alert) must be comprehensible without colour or emoji, since a contributor relying on a screen reader must be able to act on it. Detailed a11y verification of the automation's comments belongs to E01-D02; this ticket only confirms that security-critical messages are not colour-only.

## Performance notes

N/A at runtime. One availability check is in scope: confirm that fail-closed behaviour cannot deadlock delivery indefinitely — there must be a documented, audited manual override (the break-glass runbook from E01-T08), and the review verifies it exists, names who may use it, and that its use is recorded.

## Observability

Verify that each control has the detection path E01-X01 predicted: drift job covers protection and workflow-disabled; `secrets-scan` covers committed secrets; guard audit comments cover gate decisions; log redaction prevents token echo. Any threat whose detection path does not actually work is a finding, not a note — this is the difference between a monitored control and an assumed one.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Permission, pinning, trigger/secret-reachability and injection audits complete with tables attached.
- [ ] Credential inventory (type, scope, storage, rotation owner, revocation, blast radius) appended to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.14.
- [ ] All E01-X01 abuse cases executed on a scratch repo with evidence; any control that failed its abuse case has a filed bug.
- [ ] No open P0/P1 security findings against E01 scope.
- [ ] Automatable checks handed to E01-Q02 and encoded; Semgrep-rule follow-up filed for E03.
- [ ] Any test-revoked credential confirmed restored (recorded post-check).
- [ ] Break-glass override verified to exist, be scoped, and be audited.
- [ ] **Security sign-off comments posted on E01-T07, E01-T08, E01-Q02 and the epic** (required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§8 before those can be Done).
- [ ] Findings report committed; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk was surfaced.
- [ ] PR(s) with any fixes merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

## Dependencies

`blocked_by: E01-T07` (the automation must exist to be reviewed) and `E01-X01` (the threat model supplies the abuse cases and the control expectations — reviewing without it would be an unstructured skim). Blocks the Done status of `E01-T07`, `E01-T08`, `E01-Q02` and the epic itself, since all four require a Security-engineer sign-off comment.

## Branch

`chore/gov-security-review` for the findings report and any workflow fixes. PR size: small.

## References

- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.12 (Area 11, from E01-X01), §6.13 supply chain, §6.14 secrets in CI
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, §4.2, §8 security gating

## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1 requires a black-box test plan per story group, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 forbids silently skipping QA sign-off. E02 is infrastructure rather than user-facing, but it is the *most* leveraged work in the plan: if the scaffold's gates are configured-but-not-real, every later epic inherits false confidence and R0 exit criterion 2 (green pipeline ≤15 min covering lint, typecheck, unit, contract, container build, Trivy, CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit, gitleaks, pip-audit/npm audit) cannot be honestly claimed. This ticket writes and executes the plan that treats the toolchain as the system under test.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A written test plan at `docs/plan/qa/E02-scaffold-test-plan.md` covering, as black-box cases against the documented commands only (no reading of configs to "know" the answer):
  1. Clean-clone bootstrap: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --frozen`, `pnpm verify` — each asserted for exit code, wall time and absence of network lockfile writes.
  2. Every task in `AGENTS.md` §4 executed and asserted to exist and exit 0.
  3. Gate reality matrix: for each of the gates E02 implements (lint, typecheck, arch, unit coverage per package, size, generate:check, a11y on the placeholder surfaces), one *positive* run and one *negative* run using the harness from E02-T10.
  4. Compose stack: `make up` → all-healthy → `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics` → `make down` → `make reset` → `make up` again.
  5. Boundary enforcement: the five violation patches of E02-T06 executed manually and confirmed to fail with a rule id in the message.
  6. Hooks: commitlint/branch-name/lint-staged behaviours from E02-T07.
- Execution record with pass/fail per case, environment details (OS, WSL version, Docker version, Node, pnpm, Python, uv versions), and defects filed as Bugs with `priority/*` set.
- A results summary posted as the QA sign-off comment on **E02**.

## Out of scope
- Authoring automated tests (each implementing ticket owns its own).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

When the QA lead reviews it
Then every gate E02 claims to implement has both a positive and a negative case, and gates that cannot run locally are explicitly listed as CI-only rather than omitted

Given the plan is executed on a clean WSL Ubuntu environment
```

title: QA: exploratory charter — clean-clone onboarding on a second engineer's machine
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 mandates exploratory charters alongside scripted plans. The specific risk here is **R10 key-person**: a scaffold that only works on the machine of the engineer who built it is a silent single point of failure, and with ~15 engineers joining across R0–R1 (`00-planning-brief.md` §Team) a broken first-hour experience costs multiples of what it costs to find now. `20-architecture.md` §5 targets WSL Ubuntu with docker compose, an environment with well-known sharp edges (portproxy exposure, clock skew, file-permission and CRLF issues on `/mnt/c`, Docker Desktop vs native engine differences).

## Scope / Deliverables
- A 2-session, time-boxed exploratory charter (90 minutes each) executed by a QA/SDET **who did not build the scaffold**, on a machine that has never built this repo:
  - Session 1 — *"From zero to green gate"*: install prerequisites following only the README/`AGENTS.md`, clone, install, run `pnpm verify` and the Python gate. Explore: missing prerequisite versions, unclear errors, silent failures, path/permission issues when the repo lives on `/mnt/c` versus the WSL filesystem, CRLF/LF damage from `.editorconfig` gaps.
  - Session 2 — *"From zero to running stack"*: `make up`, health checks, `make down`, `make reset`, re-up. Explore: port conflicts with other local services, Docker Desktop integration off, insufficient memory, stale volumes, what happens with no network, what happens with no Bybit credentials (must still work via `CV_FEED=synthetic`).
- Session notes in the charter format of `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 (charter, areas explored, risks found, bugs filed, coverage assessment, time split setup/test/bug-reporting).
- Bugs and documentation defects filed with reproduction steps and environment.

## Out of scope
- Scripted regression cases (E02-Q01) and the automated regression pack (E02-Q03).
- CI runner environments (E03).
- macOS/native-Windows support — the target is WSL Ubuntu per `20-architecture.md` §5; a finding that something *only* works on one host OS is still reportable.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given a tester who did not build the scaffold and a machine that has never built this repo
When they follow only the committed documentation
Then they reach a green `pnpm verify` and a healthy `make up` without asking the scaffold's author a question, or every question asked is filed as a documentation defect

Given the repository is cloned onto /mnt/c rather than the WSL filesystem
When the gates are run
Then either they pass, or the documentation explicitly warns against that location with a stated reason and the warning is verified to be present

Given no network connectivity and a warmed package cache
When `make up` runs
Then the behaviour is either success or a clear, actionable error — never a hang

Given both sessions complete
When the charter notes are reviewed
Then each records areas explored, risks found, bugs filed and a time split, per 03-testing-strategy.md §11.2
```

## Technical notes / design
Exploratory means unscripted within the charter's boundary: the tester deliberately tries the wrong thing (skip a prerequisite, run from the wrong directory, interrupt an install, start with a port already bound) because those are the real first-day failure modes. Record the exact versions of every prerequisite that worked, so `AGENTS.md`/README can pin minimums.

## Test plan

title: QA: automated toolchain regression pack guarding the scaffold's gates
body:
## Context
Gates decay. A contract gets an `ignore_imports` exception "just for now", a coverage `omit` entry is added and never removed, a task is renamed and its documentation row rots. `CONSTITUTION.md` C-9.4 forbids lowering thresholds and C-9.3 bounds flaky-test quarantine to 10 working days, but neither is self-enforcing. E02-Q01 verifies the gates once, by hand; this ticket makes that verification **repeatable and automated**, so the guarantee survives every future PR rather than being true only on the day E02 closed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A regression pack at `tests/toolchain/` (runnable via `pnpm test:toolchain`, included in nightly per C-9.2 and not in the PR-blocking path unless fast enough) asserting:
  1. Every gate name in `CONSTITUTION.md` §9's table is either implemented locally or explicitly registered as CI-only, with an owning epic — no gate silently missing.
  2. Every documented task in `AGENTS.md` §4 resolves in the task graph (reuses `check-agents-commands.mjs`).
  3. Coverage thresholds equal or exceed the §9 values for every package (threshold-guard from E02-T10 run as an assertion, not only as a diff).
  4. The coverage `omit`/exclusion lists carry a dated ticket reference and none is past its stated expiry.
  5. Every `import-linter`/`dependency-cruiser` contract from E02-T06 is present and has zero exceptions; an added exception fails the pack unless accompanied by an ADR reference.
  6. Every `@flaky`-marked test has a ticket reference and a quarantine start date within 10 working days (C-9.3).
  7. Compose invariants: all published ports bound to loopback, all images digest-pinned, all services healthchecked.
- A short README explaining how to extend the pack when a new gate is added (so E03/E04 add to it rather than around it).

## Out of scope
- Re-implementing the gates themselves (owned by T06/T10/T08).
- CI scheduling and nightly workflow definition (E03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the regression pack
When `pnpm test:toolchain` runs on the merged scaffold
Then every assertion passes and the run completes in under 3 minutes

Given a coverage threshold is lowered from 85 to 70 in any package config
When the pack runs
Then it fails citing C-9.4 and naming the package

Given an `ignore_imports` exception is added to an import-linter contract without an ADR reference
When the pack runs
Then it fails naming the contract and the missing ADR

Given a test is marked @flaky with a quarantine date older than 10 working days
When the pack runs
Then it fails citing C-9.3 and the owning ticket

Given a new compose service is added without a healthcheck or with a mutable image tag
When the pack runs
Then it fails naming the service and the violated invariant
```

## Technical notes / design
The pack parses `CONSTITUTION.md` §9's table as its source of truth for gate names (the same parse-the-doc pattern used by E02-T06's drift test and E02-T10's meta-test), which keeps the Constitution genuinely authoritative rather than aspirational. Registration of a CI-only gate lives in `quality-gates.json` with an `owner` epic key — so "missing" and "deliberately elsewhere" are distinguishable. Assertions must produce actionable messages naming the rule id, file and owning ticket; a failing toolchain test that does not say what to do is worse than no test.

## Test plan
- Unit: each assertion has a fixture-driven positive and negative case (a temp tree with the violation injected), so the pack itself is proven to fail correctly.
- Integration: full pack run against the real repo.
- Coverage: pack helpers counted under the frontend threshold.
- Scheduling: registered for the nightly suite of C-9.2 with results feeding the coverage-trend report.

## Security notes
Two assertions are security controls: the import-linter exception check protects C-3.2 (M2 `secrets` reachable only from M4/M21) and C-3.3 (M19 `audit` write-only) from erosion, and the compose invariants protect trust boundary B2 (loopback-only) and the digest-pinning supply-chain control. Weakening either without an ADR is intended to be *loud*. Security engineer reviews these two assertions specifically.

## Accessibility notes
The pack asserts the `a11y` gate (§9 #9) is registered and runnable; the actual axe execution belongs to the a11y job, not here.

## Performance notes
Pack runtime ≤3 min so it can be promoted into the PR path later if desired. It must not start Docker containers for the compose invariants — those are static file assertions.

## Observability
Emits `reports/toolchain-regression.json` summarising gate status, threshold values and exception counts — a small dashboard of quality-gate health over time.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Five acceptance scenarios pass, each with an injected-violation negative test.
- [ ] Pack registered for the nightly suite and documented in `03-testing-strategy.md` §14/§15 cross-reference.
- [ ] README for extending the pack merged.
- [ ] QA lead and Security engineer review comments present.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

Blocked by E02-T10 (gate composition, `quality-gates.json`) and E02-T06 (contracts to assert over). Extended by E03 as CI-only gates come online.

title: Wire coverage gates, size-limit budgets and the local `verify` gate to Constitution §9 thresholds
body:
## Context
`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 lists 20 required checks with exact thresholds — line coverage ≥85% for `services/api/**` with branch ≥75% (#3), ≥85% for `packages/chart-engine/**` (#4), ≥80% for `apps/web/**` and `packages/ui/**` (#5), size-limit budgets per entry (#15) — and C-9.4 makes those thresholds floors that may never be lowered in the PR that fails them. `03-testing-strategy.md` §15 owns the coverage gate and reporting rules. Individual scaffold tickets configure their own package; this Task makes the set *coherent and demonstrably real*: one aggregated report, one local command that reproduces the CI verdict, and a negative test per gate proving each one actually fails.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Aggregated coverage: merge Vitest (`packages/*`, `apps/web`) LCOV and pytest-cov XML into a single report with per-package thresholds enforced independently (a high-coverage package must not mask a low one).
- `pnpm test:cov` and `make test` producing that report; `pnpm verify` composing lint → typecheck → arch → test:cov → build → size → generate:check, matching the PR gate one-for-one so `AGENTS.md` §4's "Full local gate (what CI runs on a PR)" is literally true.
- size-limit configuration for `apps/web` entry points against budget #9 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (≤8 MB gzipped initial renderer) with the +5% regression rule of §9 #15.
- Coverage-baseline file so "no decrease vs `main`" (#3) is checkable locally, plus a documented procedure for the dated, ticket-referenced `omit` list created in E02-T05.
- Negative-test harness (`scripts/gate-negative-tests.mjs`): for each gate, apply a temporary breaking change, assert the gate fails with the expected message, revert.
- Flaky-test plumbing: the `@flaky` pytest marker and Vitest equivalent registered with a quarantine report, per C-9.3 and `03-testing-strategy.md` §14.

## Out of scope
- CI workflow files, coverage upload/publishing, PR annotations (E03).
- Writing real tests for real features (owning epics).
- The `engine-bench` 5% gate logic (E06 supplies the baseline; E02-T03 supplied the harness shape).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the scaffold
When `pnpm verify` runs
Then it executes exactly the same gate list as the PR required-checks table in CONSTITUTION.md §9, in order, and exits 0

Given a package whose coverage is dropped below its threshold by a temporary change
When the negative-test harness runs
Then that package's gate fails and no other package's gate is affected, proving per-package enforcement

Given apps/web's bundle is inflated past 8MB gzipped by a temporary dependency
When `pnpm size` runs
Then it fails citing budget #9

Given a test marked @flaky
When the suite runs
Then it is quarantined (non-blocking) and listed in the quarantine report with its ticket reference, and an unreferenced @flaky marker fails the run per C-9.3

Given someone lowers a coverage threshold in the same change that would otherwise fail it
When `verify` runs
Then the threshold-guard test fails, citing C-9.4
```

## Technical notes / design
Thresholds are declared once, in each package's own config, and mirrored into a root `quality-gates.json` that the threshold-guard test reads; the guard compares the working tree's thresholds against `main`'s and fails on any decrease not accompanied by an amendment reference. This is deliberately mechanical because C-9.4 is otherwise unenforceable by review alone. Coverage merging uses LCOV as the common format; pytest-cov emits both XML and LCOV. `verify` must be fast enough to be used: target ≤3 min warm via Turbo caching, with the slow gates (`arch`, `size`, `generate:check`) cached on their real inputs.

## Test plan
- Unit: threshold-guard test (decrease, increase, unchanged, missing-package cases); quarantine-report generator tests.
- Integration: the negative-test harness itself, run in CI-equivalent mode — it is the evidence that every gate is real.
- Meta: assert the gate list in `verify` matches the check-name table in `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 by parsing that table (drift protection, C-16.5 pattern).
- Coverage: harness scripts counted under the frontend threshold.

## Security notes
The `sast`, `sca`, `secrets-scan`, `container-scan` and `license-check` gates (§9 #10–#14) are *named* in the `verify` composition but implemented in E02-X02/E03 — this Task must not silently omit them from the list, because an incomplete local gate breeds the false confidence that produces red merge-queue runs. Where a gate cannot run locally (e.g. CodeQL), `verify` prints an explicit "runs in CI only" line rather than skipping quietly.

## Accessibility notes
The `a11y` gate (§9 #9, axe-core via `@axe-core/playwright`, zero serious/critical) is included in the `verify` composition so a11y failures surface before push, using the Storybook and placeholder-route surfaces created in E02-T03/E02-T04.

## Performance notes
`pnpm verify` ≤10 min cold, ≤3 min warm on reference hardware. The `size` gate implements budget #9; the `engine-bench` gate's 5% rule (§9 #16) is wired as a no-op placeholder until E06 lands a baseline, and the placeholder must fail loudly if it is still a no-op after R0 (assert a `TODO-E06` marker with an expiry date).

## Observability
The merged coverage report and the quarantine report are written to `reports/` for E03 to upload; the coverage-trend requirement of C-9.2 (nightly trend report) consumes the same format.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Five acceptance scenarios pass; negative-test harness green for every implemented gate.
- [ ] `verify` gate list provably matches `CONSTITUTION.md` §9 (drift test green).
- [ ] Coverage thresholds enforced per package at §9 values.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` §4 updated; `03-testing-strategy.md` §15 cross-checked.
- [ ] QA lead sign-off (this Task defines the quality gate surface QA depends on).

title: Security: baseline SAST, secrets, SCA and license scanning configuration for the scaffold
body:
## Context
`CONSTITUTION.md` §9 makes `sast` (#10 CodeQL + Semgrep with custom rules incl. **withdrawal-endpoint ban**, secret-leak and raw-SQL rules, + Bandit), `sca` (#11 pip-audit + npm audit, zero high/critical without an approved expiring exception), `secrets-scan` (#12 gitleaks full-history + trufflehog on the diff, any finding fails) and `license-check` (#14 allowlist MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-2-3/ISC/MPL-2.0/Python-2.0/Unlicense/CC0, denylist GPL/AGPL/SSPL/BUSL, unknown = fail) blocking checks. E03 owns the workflow files; but the **configurations, custom rules, baselines and suppression policy** must live with the code and be runnable locally, or E03 will be wiring jobs to tools nobody has tuned. Doing it now also means the very first dependency set is scanned before it becomes load-bearing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `semgrep/` rule pack with CandleViewer-specific rules derived from the Constitution: (a) **withdrawal-endpoint ban** — any code path referencing Bybit withdrawal/transfer/funding endpoints fails (C-1.2 item 5, C-2.7); (b) Bybit-identifier ban outside `services/api/candleviewer/exchange/bybit/`, `packages/protocol` enums, docs and config keys (C-2.2); (c) raw-SQL/string-interpolated query detection; (d) secret-shaped literal detection; (e) a rule flagging any log call that passes a settings object or a field matching `(key|secret|token|password|signature)`.
- CodeQL configuration (JS/TS + Python) with the query suites selected and a documented, dated suppression policy.
- Bandit config (already added in E02-T02) tuned: excluded paths, severity floor, and no blanket `# nosec` without a dated justification comment — enforced by a Semgrep rule.
- gitleaks config + a clean full-history baseline; trufflehog diff-mode config; `.gitignore` verified for `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, coverage and build output.
- `pip-audit` and `npm audit --audit-level=high` wrappers plus the **exception file format**: every exception has a CVE, a reason, an owner and an expiry date, and an expired exception fails the check.
- `license-check` configuration implementing the exact allow/deny lists of §9 #14, with unknown-license = fail, and a generated SBOM (CycloneDX) per ecosystem.
- A single `make security` / `pnpm security` entry point running everything runnable locally, documented in `AGENTS.md` §4.

## Out of scope
- GitHub Actions job definitions, Dependabot configuration, code scanning alert routing, Trivy container scanning in CI (#13) — **E03** (though the Trivy *policy file* is authored here if it is a repo-level config).
- DAST/OWASP ZAP (nightly, E03/E43) and pen-testing (E43).
- Remediating findings in application code that does not exist yet.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the scaffold
When `make security` runs
Then SAST, secrets, SCA and license checks all execute and report zero high/critical findings on the baseline

Given a test file containing a call to a Bybit withdrawal endpoint
When Semgrep runs
Then the withdrawal-endpoint-ban rule fires with a message citing C-1.2 and C-2.7

Given the string "bybit" is introduced in services/api/candleviewer/oms/service.py
When Semgrep runs
Then the adapter-isolation rule fires citing C-2.2

Given a committed file containing an AWS-style key or a Bybit API secret pattern
When gitleaks runs over the full history
Then the scan fails and identifies the file and commit

Given an SCA exception whose expiry date has passed
When the SCA wrapper runs
Then the check fails naming the expired exception, its CVE and its owner

Given a dependency licensed under AGPL-3.0
When license-check runs
Then it fails, and an unknown/unparseable license also fails rather than being ignored
```

## Technical notes / design
Custom Semgrep rules must be unit-tested using Semgrep's own `--test` fixtures (a rule that never fires is worse than no rule — it manufactures confidence). The withdrawal-endpoint ban is the single highest-value rule in the repository: `CONSTITUTION.md` C-1.2 item 5 puts withdrawal/transfer/funding operations out of scope "of any kind, through any code path", and the architecture's startup self-check refuses trading mode if a stored key has withdrawal enabled (`20-architecture.md` §2.2 B3); the Semgrep rule is the *static* half of that defence and must match endpoint paths, method names and the Bybit-specific asset-transfer nomenclature. Suppressions (`# nosec`, `// nosemgrep`, gitleaks allowlist entries) require a dated justification and an owner, checked by a meta-rule.

## Test plan
- Unit: Semgrep rule tests with positive and negative fixtures for each of the five custom rules.
- Unit: SCA exception-file parser tests (valid, missing field, expired, future expiry).
- Integration: `make security` full run on the scaffold; a deliberately seeded secret in a scratch branch confirmed to fail gitleaks (then removed and the history of that scratch branch discarded).
- Integration: a temporarily added AGPL dependency confirmed to fail license-check.
- Coverage: wrapper scripts counted under the relevant package thresholds.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* a security control set, implementing the mitigations enumerated in E02-X01 for Tampering (malicious dependency), Information Disclosure (committed secrets, logged credentials) and Elevation (raw SQL → injection). Note the deliberate ordering: the gitleaks **full-history** baseline is established now, while history is short and cheap to scan; establishing it later is materially more expensive and risks grandfathering a real leak. Data classification: the scanners themselves must not upload source to third-party services — CodeQL runs in GitHub's own environment (already the code host), and Semgrep runs with the local rule pack, not the cloud platform, per the "no third-party SaaS that receives market, order or account data" guardrail (C-1.2 item 6) applied conservatively to source as well.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — security tooling, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
The locally runnable set (`make security`) must complete in ≤5 min; CodeQL and full-history gitleaks may exceed this and are allocated to the CI/nightly split decided in E02-X01, protecting R0 exit criterion 2 (≤15 min pipeline).

## Observability
All scanners emit SARIF where supported, written to `reports/security/` so E03 can upload to code scanning and E04 can trend finding counts by severity.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Six acceptance scenarios pass, including every negative/seeded case.
- [ ] Custom Semgrep rules have passing rule-tests; no rule is untested.
- [ ] Baselines established (gitleaks full history clean; SCA and license baselines recorded).
- [ ] Suppression/exception policy documented with required fields and expiry enforcement.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` §4 documents `make security`; `04-security-program.md` cross-referenced/updated.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off; findings traced back to E02-X01's model.

title: Build, scan, SBOM and cosign-sign container images on merge to main
body:
## Context
ADR-0013 rule 8: *"Deployment is image-based and immutable: every merge to `main` produces a tagged image with an SBOM and a signature."* `04-security-program.md` SR-137 requires release artefacts to be built in CI (never on a developer machine) and images to be signed with cosign plus a provenance attestation; SR-133 requires a CycloneDX SBOM for the backend, the web bundle and the Electron app; SR-131 requires digest-pinned, multi-stage, non-root images scanned by Trivy.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/main.yml` build stage: multi-stage Dockerfile builds for `services/api` and the web bundle server; buildx with layer caching; base images pinned **by digest**; non-root runtime user; read-only root filesystem where feasible; dropped Linux capabilities (SR-131).
- Tagging scheme: `ghcr.io/<org>/candleviewer-api:<semver>-<shortsha>` plus a moving `:dev` tag; the immutable digest is the deployment reference, never the tag (ADR-0013 rule 8).
- SBOM: syft -> CycloneDX JSON per artifact, attached to the image as an attestation and uploaded as a workflow artifact (SR-133); SBOM diff vs the previous image posted in the job summary for review.
- Signing: cosign keyless (OIDC) signature + SLSA provenance attestation; the signature is verified in the same workflow immediately after push (a signature nobody verifies is decoration).
- Trivy image scan gating on High/Critical (Ã‚Â§12.1), post-push, blocking the deploy stage rather than the build.
- Electron installer build/sign hooks stubbed for `release.yml` (`E03-T11`) - R0 only needs the web/api images; the Electron packaging pipeline is wired but exercised on release branches.

## Out of scope
- Deployment itself (`E03-T09`), release tagging and changelog (`E03-T11`), the Electron hardening assertions (`E10`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Merge to main produces a signed, attested image
  Given a pull request is merged to "main"
  When the build stage completes
  Then an image is pushed to GHCR tagged "<semver>-<shortsha>"
  And a CycloneDX SBOM attestation and a cosign signature are attached
  And an immediate "cosign verify" of the pushed digest succeeds

Scenario: A Critical image vulnerability blocks the deploy
  Given the built image contains a package with a Critical CVE and no accepted-risk entry
  When the Trivy image scan runs
  Then the deploy stage does not execute
  And the image remains in the registry marked unfit for deployment

Scenario: The image runs as a non-root user
  Given the built api image
  When the hardening assertion runs "docker inspect" and a container "id" probe
  Then the runtime user is not uid 0
  And the assertion fails the build if it is

Scenario: A floating base image is rejected
  Given a Dockerfile uses "FROM python:3.12-slim" without a digest
  When the Dockerfile lint step runs (hadolint + the SR-131 digest check)
  Then the build fails naming the unpinned base image
```

## Technical notes / design
- Build provenance uses GitHub OIDC; **no long-lived registry password** exists as a secret (SR-141).
- The SBOM diff is generated by comparing the previous `:dev` image's attestation; a new transitive dependency appearing without a lockfile change is a strong tamper signal and is highlighted (SR-135).
- Reproducibility: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set from the commit timestamp and layer ordering is deterministic, so two builds of one commit differ only in signature.
- Error codes: `CI-IMG-001` unpinned base, `CI-IMG-002` root user, `CI-IMG-003` Trivy High/Critical, `CI-IMG-004` cosign verification failed, `CI-IMG-005` SBOM generation failed.

## Test plan
- Integration: four fixture branches, one per acceptance scenario (including a deliberately vulnerable base image pinned to an old digest to prove the Trivy gate).
- Contract: CycloneDX document validated against the schema before attestation.
- Chaos: registry-unavailable path must fail the job with a retry, never silently skip the push.
- Coverage: assertion scripts under `tools/ci` >=85%.

## Security notes
- Implements SR-131, SR-133, SR-137, SR-141 and supports SR-130.
- Threat (STRIDE-T, tampering with the artefact between build and deploy): closed by deploying **by digest** with signature verification at deploy time (`E03-T09`), not by trusting the tag.
- Data classification: signing identity is OIDC-federated; no private key material is stored.
- Security review label required; the deferred R1 backlog item E03-X05 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope) is the dedicated sign-off ticket.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Image build target <= 6 min with layer cache; it runs post-merge so it does not consume the PR budget, but a slow build delays dev deploy and is tracked.

## Observability
Job summary: image digest, size, layer count, SBOM component count and diff, Trivy severity counts, signature verification result. Emitted as a deploy annotation event for E04.

title: Automate dev deploy and add a gated staging deploy with rollback
body:
## Context
R0 exit criterion 2 requires "a green pipeline from commit to dev deployment" with no manual step, and `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§9 defines three environments - dev (docker compose on WSL Ubuntu, tip of `main`), staging (= Bybit demo), prod (= live) - with promotion gates. ADR-0013 rule 8 makes deployment image-based and immutable and makes production "a deliberate, checklisted action". This Task delivers dev auto-deploy and the *gated* staging deploy job; prod promotion remains a checklisted human action per `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/main.yml` deploy stage: after a successful signed build, deploy to dev by **digest**, verifying the cosign signature immediately before applying (`E03-T08` threat closure).
- Deployment mechanism: a self-hosted runner on the dev host executing `docker compose -f compose.dev.yml up -d --wait` against a rendered compose file with the pinned digest; no SSH keys held in GitHub (the runner is inside the trust boundary).
- Post-deploy smoke test: `GET /health/live`, `GET /health/ready` (paths per `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`) and the build-info endpoint asserting the deployed git sha equals the just-built sha - the single most common silent-failure mode is "deploy succeeded, old image still running".
- `.github/workflows/staging.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` + release-branch trigger, bound to a GitHub Environment `staging` with **required reviewers** and a deployment branch policy restricting it to `main`/`release/*` (SR-141 environment protection).
- Staging smoke: health checks, WS connect, and the `@demo-rest-only` E2E subset job registration from `E03-T06` (empty in R0, mandatory from R3).
- Rollback: `workflow_dispatch` input `rollback_to_digest`; documented procedure re-deploying the previous digest with **no down-migration** (ADR-0013 rule 9, expand/contract).
- Deployment records: every deploy appends to `deployments/ledger.jsonl` (sha, digest, environment, actor, timestamp, outcome) committed by the workflow for auditability until E04's observability lands.

## Out of scope
- Prod/live deployment and the Live-enablement gate (R4, `07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§6).
- Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager (`E04`).
- Feature-flag service implementation (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§10.4 assigns the flag *service* to infra, delivered in a later epic); this Task only ensures deploys do not reset flag state.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Merge to main auto-deploys to dev
  Given a signed image for commit "abc1234" exists
  When the deploy stage runs
  Then the dev stack is updated to that image digest
  And the build-info endpoint reports git sha "abc1234"
  And the deployment ledger gains a success entry

Scenario: An unsigned or tampered image is refused
  Given an image whose cosign signature does not verify
  When the deploy stage attempts to apply it
  Then deployment aborts before any container is replaced
  And the ledger records a "signature-verification-failed" entry

Scenario: Staging requires a named reviewer
  Given the staging deploy workflow is dispatched
  When it reaches the "staging" environment gate
  Then it waits for approval from a required reviewer
  And it is cancelled automatically after the configured wait timer without deploying

Scenario: Rollback restores the previous digest without a down-migration
  Given the current dev deployment is digest D2 and the previous was D1
  When the rollback workflow is dispatched with "rollback_to_digest=D1"
  Then D1 is redeployed and the smoke test passes
  And no Alembic down-migration is executed

Scenario: A failed smoke test marks the deployment failed
  Given the deployed container fails "/health/ready" for 60 seconds
  When the smoke step times out
  Then the job fails, the ledger records the failure, and the previous digest is automatically restored
```

## Technical notes / design
- Auto-rollback on smoke failure is deliberate for **dev only**; staging failures alert and stop, because a half-rolled-back staging environment during a soak (`07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§4.2) is harder to reason about than a stopped one.
- Migrations run on boot under an advisory lock (ADR-0013 rule 9) - delivered by `E03-T10`; the deploy step waits for the migration to report completion before smoke-testing.
- Environment variables and non-secret settings come from a committed `.env.example`-derived render; **no exchange secret ever enters CI** (SR-140, SR-144).
- Error codes: `CI-DEP-001` signature verification failed, `CI-DEP-002` smoke failed, `CI-DEP-003` sha mismatch after deploy, `CI-DEP-004` migration lock timeout.

## Test plan
- Integration: five fixture runs, one per scenario, including a deliberately tampered image and a container forced to fail readiness.
- Chaos: kill the dev host runner mid-deploy and assert the ledger and stack converge to a known state on the next run (feeds the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q03 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)).
- E2E: staging smoke path executed once end-to-end with a real approval.
- Coverage: deploy helper scripts under `tools/ci` >=85%.

## Security notes
- SR-141: staging is a protected GitHub Environment with required reviewers; the self-hosted dev runner is inside the trust boundary and holds no GitHub secrets beyond its registration token.
- SR-140: **no production Bybit credentials in CI** - the dev and staging stacks obtain demo credentials from the host's envelope-encrypted store, not from GitHub secrets.
- Signature verification at deploy time closes the tamper-in-transit path opened between build and run.
- Threat: a compromised self-hosted runner deploying arbitrary images - mitigated by digest+signature verification, restricted runner labels, and an ephemeral workspace.
- Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no product UI. The deployment ledger and job summaries are text-based and screen-reader friendly.

## Performance notes
Deploy + smoke target <= 3 min so the full commit-to-dev path stays inside R0's 15-minute exit criterion together with the build.

## Observability
- Ledger entries (sha, digest, environment, actor, outcome, duration).
- Deploy annotation events for E04's Grafana.
- Smoke-test latency recorded; a regression in startup time is an early warning of a migration problem.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Five scenarios demonstrated with run links.
- [ ] Rollback procedure documented in the CI runbook (`E03-T15`) and rehearsed once.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off recorded (`security` label).
- [ ] QA sign-off on the smoke-test suite.

- [ ] PR merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code-owner.

title: Add the release workflow: changelog, semver tagging and artefacts
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§3 requires a changelog-generation job (release-please-style or conventional-changelog) running on every merge to `main`, appending to an **Unreleased** section of `CHANGELOG.md` grouped by `Features`, `Fixes`, `Performance`, `Security`, `Breaking Changes`, with the release-train cut finalising it under a version heading and drafting a GitHub Release. Ã‚Â§2 fixes the semver rules: `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` -> MAJOR, `feat:` -> MINOR, otherwise PATCH, staying `0.x.y` until the first Live-enablement release, when `1.0.0` is declared **explicitly, not automatically**. ADR-0013's pipeline shape lists `release tag -> changelog - Electron installers (signed) - release checklist + PRR gate`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `.github/workflows/changelog.yml`: on merge to `main`, parses conventional commits since the last tag and updates the `## Unreleased` section of `/CHANGELOG.md` via a bot commit.
- Changelog-fragment enforcement on PRs: a PR whose title is not conventional-commit-parseable and which lacks a `Changelog: <one-line>` footer fails, **except** for `chore:`/`ci:`/`docs:`-only PRs (`07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§3 final bullet).
- Security-fix wording guard: entries under `Security` must not include exploit detail; a lint warns on lines containing CVE proof-of-concept markers or the words "exploit"/"payload", pointing the author to the internal finding tracker.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: on `release/*` branch or a `vX.Y.Z` tag - compute the semver bump, finalise the Unreleased section under the version heading with the release date, draft the GitHub Release with that section as the body, attach SBOMs (`E03-T08`), and build + sign Electron installers.
- **`1.0.0` guard**: the workflow refuses to produce a `1.0.0` tag unless a `RELEASE_ALLOW_1_0_0=true` input is explicitly supplied, encoding the "declared explicitly, not automatically" rule.
- Release-checklist automation: the workflow opens a release-checklist issue from a template containing `07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§4 items, and refuses to publish a non-draft release while the PRR gate item is unchecked.
- Signed tags: release tags require signed commits (`04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 branch protection note).

## Out of scope
- Executing the PRR itself and the Live-enablement gate (R4 / `E43`, `E44`).
- Actual Electron packaging configuration (`E10`); this Task calls the packaging target and signs its output.
- Deploying releases to prod (`07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§4.4, a human checklisted action).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A feature merge lands in the Unreleased changelog
  Given a pull request titled "feat(chart): add volume pane" is merged to main
  When the changelog workflow runs
  Then "CHANGELOG.md" gains a bullet under "Unreleased > Features"
  And the bot commit is "docs(changelog): update unreleased"

Scenario: A PR without a usable changelog line is blocked
  Given a pull request titled "wip fixes" with no "Changelog:" footer and code changes
  When the changelog-fragment check runs
  Then the check fails asking for a conventional title or a Changelog footer

  Then it proposes a MAJOR bump and states the triggering commit

  Given the computed bump from 0.9.x would be MAJOR
  When the release workflow runs without "RELEASE_ALLOW_1_0_0=true"
  Then it fails with "1.0.0 requires explicit Live-enablement declaration"

Scenario: A docs-only PR is exempt
  Given a pull request titled "docs: fix typo in sitemap"
```

- Release artefacts must be built in CI, never on a developer machine (SR-137) - the workflow refuses to run from a non-`main`/`release/*` ref.
- Security-relevant changelog entries are general-description only, exploit detail retained internally (`07-release-and-prr.md` Ã‚Â§3) - enforced by the wording guard.

title: Configure branch protection, required checks and the merge queue
body:
## Context
`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§7 defines the merge contract: 2 approvals including 1 CODEOWNER, a named set of required checks, and GitHub Merge Queue serialising merges with max concurrency 3, rebasing each PR onto the latest `main` and re-running required checks. `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 enumerates the exact required-check names and the branch-protection posture: no force-push, no direct commits, linear history, signed commits for release tags. R0 exit criterion 1 requires that "a PR without 2 approvals incl. a code-owner is demonstrably unmergeable" - demonstrated, not assumed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Branch-protection ruleset for `main` expressed as committed configuration (`.github/rulesets/main.json`) applied by a workflow, so the policy is diff-reviewable rather than click-configured.
- Required checks wired to the names produced by the earlier tasks: `ci-required` (resolver, `E03-T01`), `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit-backend`, `unit-frontend`, `unit-engine`, `architecture`, `coverage-thresholds`, `contract`, `integration`, `e2e-web`, `a11y-axe`, `migrations`, `codeql`, `semgrep`, `bandit`, `pip-audit`, `npm-audit`, `gitleaks`, `license-scan`, `trivy` - plus `e2e-electron` and `electron-hardening` and `rbac-matrix` registered as required on `release/*` and enabled on `main` as their owning epics (E10, E09) land.
- Merge queue enabled: max 3 building in parallel, strict queue order, required checks re-run on the rebased head (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` Ã‚Â§7).
- Expedited lane configuration for the hotfix flow (Ã‚Â§8) that jumps ordering but never skips checks.
- Bypass register: `.github/rulesets/bypass-register.md` naming every actor permitted to bypass (release bot for changelog commits only) with justification and a review date - an unlisted bypass is a finding.
- A drift-detection job asserting the live ruleset matches the committed JSON; drift fails and opens an issue.
- Evidence capture for R0 exit criterion 1: a recorded demonstration that a 1-approval PR and a direct push to `main` are both refused.


- **Scope delta from `E03-X01`'s STRIDE model (threat row P2, workflow-edits-its-own-gate)**: the required-checks configuration must be enforced by branch-protection settings (server-side, GitHub-owned) rather than by the workflow YAML itself — a fixture PR that edits `.github/workflows/*` to remove a required check must still fail that check, closing a self-referential bypass the original ticket text did not name (`docs/plan/threat-models/E03-supply-chain.md` section 4.1, section 7 item 2).

## Out of scope
- Creating CODEOWNERS itself (`E01`); this Task consumes it and asserts full path coverage.
- The checks themselves (`E03-T02`..`T10`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A PR with one approval cannot merge
  Given a pull request with all checks green and exactly one approval
  When merge is attempted
  Then GitHub refuses the merge citing the required review count

Scenario: A PR without a code-owner approval cannot merge
  Given a pull request with two approvals from non-code-owners of the touched paths
  When merge is attempted
  Then GitHub refuses the merge citing code-owner review

Scenario: A direct push to main is rejected
  Given a maintainer attempts "git push origin main"
  When the push is evaluated
  Then it is rejected by the ruleset and no commit lands

Scenario: Ruleset drift is detected
  Given someone edits the branch protection in the GitHub UI
  When the drift-detection job runs
  Then it fails and opens an issue showing the difference from ".github/rulesets/main.json"

Scenario: The merge queue re-runs checks on the rebased head
  Given two pull requests are enqueued and the first changes a shared module
  When the second is rebased in the queue
  Then its required checks re-run against the rebased head
  And it is evicted if they fail
```

## Technical notes / design
- Required checks are declared once in `.github/rulesets/main.json` and cross-checked against the job names emitted by the workflows by a lint step - a renamed job that silently stops being required is the classic failure mode this prevents.
- CODEOWNERS path-coverage assertion: every top-level path in the repo must match at least one CODEOWNERS rule (R0 exit criterion 1: "no path in the repo is un-owned").
- Error codes: `CI-PROT-001` ruleset drift, `CI-PROT-002` required check name not produced by any workflow, `CI-PROT-003` uncovered CODEOWNERS path, `CI-PROT-004` unregistered bypass actor.

## Test plan
- Integration: the five acceptance scenarios executed against the real repository settings on a scratch branch pattern where possible, and against `main` for the refusal cases (attempts that are expected to fail harmlessly).
- Unit (>=85%): the required-check-name cross-check and the CODEOWNERS coverage assertion.
- Evidence for R0 exit criterion 1 archived on the ticket.

## Security notes
- This Task *is* a security control: branch protection is the boundary preventing unreviewed code from reaching the signed-build path (threat boundary TB-8).
- Linear history plus no force-push preserves the auditability the security programme assumes; signed commits are required for release tags (Ã‚Â§12.3).
- The bypass register closes the most common real-world erosion: an emergency bypass granted once and never revoked.
- Security engineer sign-off required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Merge-queue concurrency 3 balances throughput against re-run cost; if queue wait exceeds 30 min at p90 the concurrency is revisited alongside the 15-minute PR budget.

## Observability
Drift-detection job result and merge-queue wait times recorded in `ci-metrics`; bypass usages are audited monthly against the register.

body:
## Context
ADR-0013 Ã‚Â§Validation commits the team to three things: measure PR feedback time weekly and rebalance if p90 exceeds 15 minutes; review action pins and workflow permissions quarterly; and *"A deliberate 'break the protocol' PR must fail the freshness gate (tested once during Sprint 01)"*. `30-release-roadmap.md` Ã‚Â§4.4 also requires a PRR-lite item: a runbook for "dev environment rebuild". A pipeline without a runbook is a pipeline only its author can operate, which contradicts the bus-factor concerns recorded in ADR-0002 and `32-risk-register.md` (R10 key-person).

## Scope / Deliverables

- Weekly PR-feedback-time measurement: a small report job publishing p50/p90 from `ci-metrics`, with the rebalance trigger documented.
- Quarterly review checklist for action pins and workflow permissions (SR-132), filed as a recurring issue template.

title: Observability baseline: structured logs, metrics, health, dashboards, alerting
body:
## Context
CandleViewer runs unattended while holding real positions; its failure modes are silent by default (a stale topic still renders a chart, a slow event loop still serves requests, an order stuck in `Unknown` looks like nothing at all). This epic builds the observability floor that every later epic's Definition of Done depends on — `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` makes metrics part of a module's DoD, and `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md` states plainly: *a module without metrics is not finished*.

Plan material:
- Roadmap train: `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2 (E04, 26 pts, S02–S03), §4.3 exit criterion 10 ("Grafana shows ingestion rate, WS state, queue depth and API latency; a synthetic alert fires and is received").
- Architecture: `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12 (Observability) is the authoritative metric catalogue, logging, tracing, dashboard and alert policy; §3 defines the per-module package / lifecycle / `health()` conventions this epic instruments, and §3.12 (API / WS Gateway) hosts the `/metrics`, `/healthz`, `/readyz` and build-info endpoints. (Note: `20-architecture.md` identifies modules by named section, not by M-numbered ids; the `M24` shorthand used in the roadmap §4.2 table has no counterpart in the architecture document and is therefore not used anywhere in this backlog.) See §12.
- ADR: `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md` (Prometheus + Grafana + Alertmanager, structlog JSON, OTel on exactly two paths, two alert severities, Loki deliberately deferred).
- User stories domain **OBS**: `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28 — US-OBS-001..007.
- Security requirements SR-120…SR-126 (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.9) and threat K1 (key material leaking into logs).
- Budgets: `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 and §5.1 stage allocation.

### Estimate reconciliation (roadmap 26 — engineering 29 — epic 46)
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 104/187 sizes E04 at **26 pts**. That roadmap figure prices *engineering* scope only (the structlog / metrics / health / alerting / dashboard build). The three numbers reconcile as follows, with no scope missing or double-counted:

| Figure | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Roadmap allocation | 26 | Engineering build, as sized during roadmap planning. |
| Engineering children (`E04-K01`, `E04-T01..T07`, `E04-S01`, `E04-S02`) | 29 | The same scope, re-estimated at grooming: 29 vs 26 = **+11.5%**, inside the ±15 % tolerance of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, so the roadmap train needs no re-baselining. |
| This epic's `estimate` field | 46 | Per the backlog schema an epic's estimate is the **sum of all children**, which additionally includes the discipline tickets the roadmap line never priced: design `E04-D01`+`E04-D02` (7), QA `E04-Q01`+`E04-Q02` (5) and security `E04-X01`+`E04-X02` (5) = 17. 29 + 17 = 46. |

The +3-point engineering delta is absorbed inside the S02–S03 window; no roadmap change is requested.

### Sprint-window reconciliation (roadmap S02–S03 vs scheduled tickets)
The roadmap window **S02–S03** is the *engineering build* window. Every engineering ticket (`E04-K01`, `E04-T01..T07`, `E04-S01`, `E04-S02`) plus `E04-X01` (threat model, must precede `E04-T01`) and `E04-Q01` (scripted test plan) sits inside it. Three tickets sit deliberately outside it, each carrying its own justification section:

| Ticket | Sprint | Why outside S02–S03 |
|---|---|---|
| `E04-D01` | Sprint 01 | Design must land **two sprints before** the consuming FE work (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`); consumers `E04-T04` / `E04-S01` are Sprint 03. Sprint 01 immediately precedes the train window. |
| `E04-Q02` | Sprint 04 | Exploratory QA + regression pack over **shipped** code that only exists at the end of Sprint 03; epic QA sign-off (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2) is by definition a post-build gate. |
| `E04-X02` | Sprint 04 | Security review / abuse cases / SAST rules over merged artefacts from `E04-T01..T06` and `E04-S02`; the R0 SAST/SCA/secrets gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4) is a milestone gate, not a sprint-internal one. |

Neither Sprint-04 ticket consumes S02–S03 capacity, and no dependent epic consumes their output before Sprint 05, so the R0 milestone (assessed at the end of Sprint 04) is unaffected.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-OBS-001** Metrics pipeline — `/metrics` Prometheus endpoint, the metric catalogue of `20-architecture.md` §12.1 with bounded cardinality and an `env` label, Prometheus scrape config (10 s, 15 d retention).
- **US-OBS-002** Latency-budget instrumentation — per-stage timers (ingest → internal fan-out → client render), the frontend telemetry push endpoint, recording rules expressing the §2 budgets as burn rates.
- **US-OBS-003** Structured logging — `structlog` JSON to stdout, mandatory correlation field set, handler-level redaction filter, runtime per-subsystem log-level override with auto-revert.
- **US-OBS-004** Alerting — Alertmanager with exactly two severities (Page / Ticket) per ADR-0014 §6, grouping/dedup, owner routing, runbook link mandatory per rule.
- **US-OBS-005** Rate-limit budget metrics (`bybit_rate_remaining{endpoint_group}`, `oms_rate_reject_total`) exported here; the SCR-147 UI belongs to E42.
- **US-OBS-007** Support bundle — `POST`-triggered diagnostic bundle with pre-write secret scanning and size cap.
- Health surface: `/health/live`, `/health/ready`, build-info, and `GET /api/v1/admin/health` returning `HealthReport` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`).
- Six provisioned Grafana dashboards as reviewed JSON under `infra/grafana` (`20-architecture.md` §12.4).
- Postgres `system_events` writer feeding `GET /api/v1/admin/incidents` and SCR-144.
- Design, QA and Security tickets for the surfaces above (SCR-143, SCR-144, SCR-152, SCR-156, CMP-178, CMP-210, CMP-207, CMP-092, CMP-076).

## Out of scope
- The Admin screens themselves as finished product UI (SCR-143 system health, SCR-144 incident log) — built in **E42 Admin**; E04 delivers the data contracts, the design specs and the health/incident API.
- Chaos & failure drills as a release gate (**US-OBS-006**) — owned by **E45 Reconciliation, chaos & failover resilience**; E04 only seeds a WS-disconnect harness fixture.
- Loki / centralised log search (deferred by ADR-0014), Tempo/Mimir, any SaaS observability.
- Trading, rule-engine and recorder metrics *implementations* — each owning epic registers its own metrics against the registry E04 provides.
- Android / mobile telemetry (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Metrics visible end to end
  Given the api service is running in dev
  When Prometheus scrapes /metrics
  Then every metric named in 20-architecture.md §12.1 that belongs to a module shipped in R0 is present, carries an env label, and the scrape completes in under 50 ms

Scenario: A secret never reaches a log
  Given a Bybit API secret, a session cookie and a TOTP code are passed through log calls, an exception traceback and an httpx request log
  When the JSON log output is captured
  Then none of the three values appears at any log level, and the CI redaction test fails the build if one does

Scenario: Synthetic alert is received (R0 exit criterion 10)
  Given a synthetic condition is injected in staging
  When the rule's for-duration elapses
  Then Alertmanager delivers the alert to the owner's channel within 60 s, the notification names the severity and links to a runbook section in 07-release-and-prr.md

Scenario: Degraded dependency does not fail liveness
  Given QuestDB is stopped
  When /health/live and /health/ready are probed
  Then /health/live returns 200 and /health/ready returns 503 naming questdb, and GET /api/v1/admin/health reports overall=degraded with that component's state and last-good timestamp
```

## Technical notes / design
The observability module (`services/api/candleviewer/observability/`, following the §3 module conventions of `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`) owns a single process-wide Prometheus `CollectorRegistry` plus a `metrics.py` facade so other modules never import `prometheus_client` directly (enforced by an `import-linter` contract from E02). Logging is configured once at process start; the redaction processor is installed at the *handler* level (SR-121) so a new call site cannot bypass it. Correlation ids are carried in a `contextvars.ContextVar` set by the ASGI middleware (`request_id`) and by the WS connection handler (`conn_id`), and copied into every task spawned by OMS/ingestion so async hops do not lose them. Tracing is OpenTelemetry on exactly two paths only (order path, replay session start) — market-data hot loops are metrics-only because sampling them would distort the loop being measured.

## Test plan
Unit: redaction matrix, correlation propagation across `asyncio.create_task`, metric registration idempotence, cardinality guard, health aggregator with each component failing in turn. Contract: `HealthReport` / `Incident` schemas against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; Prometheus exposition format parses with `prometheus_client.parser`. Integration: docker-compose stack with prometheus + grafana + alertmanager; dashboard JSON loads without "panel datasource not found". E2E: synthetic alert drill. Perf: scrape latency under full label set. Coverage ≥85% on the backend observability package.

## Security notes
Threats K1 (key material in logs), U5 (token theft via logs), D3 (over-exposing operational payloads), A-17 (telemetry asset). Controls: SR-006/SR-007 secret wrapper, SR-120…SR-126 logging/redaction/alerting requirements, SR-005 (no secret prefix beyond 4 chars anywhere). `/metrics` binds to the private network only and is never publicly routable. Support bundles are secret-scanned before write, audited, and never uploaded automatically. Data classification: telemetry = Internal; bundles may transit Confidential operational data and stay on the local machine.

## Accessibility notes
E04 ships design specs (not final UI) for SCR-143/SCR-144 and the health chrome components CMP-178, CMP-210, CMP-092, CMP-076, CMP-207. Every health state must be conveyed as a *word* plus a number with units — never colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AA, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). Status regions use `role="status"`/`role="alert"` by severity with announcements throttled to ≤1 Hz.

## Performance notes
Instrumentation overhead ≤1% CPU (US-OBS-002 NFR). `/metrics` scrape < 50 ms with the full label set (ADR-0014 validation). Metric cardinality is bounded and documented — symbol/account/env labels only, never order ids or user emails.

## Observability
This epic *is* the observability surface: metrics catalogue §12.1, log field set §12.2, two traced paths §12.3, six dashboards §12.4, two-severity alert policy §12.5, plus `system_events` rows for every operational incident.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All children Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion 10 demonstrated live at Sprint Review (dashboards populated, synthetic alert received).
- [ ] ADR-0014 reconciled with what actually shipped; `20-architecture.md` §12 updated if the catalogue diverged.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on touched backend packages; CI gate green.
- [ ] STRIDE model for E04 complete and signed off by the Security engineer (E04-X01).
- [ ] QA epic-level regression + exploratory pass recorded (E04-Q01, E04-Q02).
- [ ] Design sign-off (CDO or delegate) on E04-D01/E04-D02 outputs.
- [ ] Runbook entries exist for every alert rule — an alert without a runbook is a merge blocker.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E03` — CI/CD pipeline and the dev/staging environments must exist before dashboards, scrape targets and alert routing can be deployed. E02 (monorepo, docker compose with prometheus/grafana) is a transitive prerequisite via E03. E08 (ingestion) and E09 (auth) consume this epic's registry and correlation context but do not block it.

## Branch
`feat/obs-baseline-*`; PRs ≤400 LOC diff, one concern per PR (logging, metrics, health, dashboards, alerting kept separate).

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2, §4.3, §11.1
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md`
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28 (US-OBS-001..007)
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.9 (SR-120…SR-126)
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2, §5.1
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/admin/health`, `/health/live`, `/admin/incidents`)
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.2 `system_events`, §4.13 `engine_metrics`

## Child dependency graph
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    D01[E04-D01 Design: health & incident specs] --> D02[E04-D02 Design QA + a11y review]
    K01[E04-K01 Spike: tracing & instrumentation overhead] --> T06
    T01[E04-T01 structlog + redaction] --> T02[E04-T02 Correlation ids + runtime log level]
    T01 --> T03[E04-T03 Prometheus registry + metric catalogue]
    T03 --> T04[E04-T04 Health, readiness, build-info, admin health]
    T03 --> T06[E04-T06 Latency budget + FE telemetry]
    T03 --> S01[E04-S01 Grafana dashboards]
    T03 --> T05[E04-T05 Alertmanager rules + routing]
    T02 --> S02[E04-S02 Support bundle]
    T04 --> S02
    T04 --> S01
    T05 --> T07[E04-T07 ADR-0014 reconciliation + runbooks]
    S01 --> T07
    X01[E04-X01 STRIDE threat model] --> T01
    X01 --> X02[E04-X02 Security review + abuse cases]
    S02 --> X02
    T05 --> Q01[E04-Q01 Black-box test plan + drill]
    S01 --> Q01
    Q01 --> Q02[E04-Q02 Exploratory charter + regression pack]
    D02 --> Q02
```


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.
