title: Implement QuestDB hot tier: DDL runner, batched ILP writer, PGWire reader and MarketDataRepository
body:
## Context
The hot tier serves every chart, footprint, profile and recent-replay read in the product; `21-database-schema.md` §13.2 lists twelve query shapes with targets from <10 ms (last price) to <200 ms (replay seek). §4 gives the complete DDL for thirteen tables, all WAL-enabled, all with `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS`, partitioned by hour/day/month according to the query window and retention unit. §4.14 gives the operational settings. R0 exit criterion #6 requires "ticks, L2 deltas and 1-minute bars ... readable from QuestDB".

This ticket implements the tier behind the `MarketDataRepository` Protocol from E07-T01. It starts only after E07-K01 has confirmed (or replaced) QuestDB, so that no implementation effort is spent on a rejected engine; if the spike takes the ADR-0003 reversal path, this ticket is retargeted to TimescaleDB with the same Protocol, same tests and the same estimate - the Protocol is what makes that a retarget rather than a rewrite.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `backend/db/questdb/0001_core_tables.sql` and `0002_footprint_cells.sql` transcribing §4.1-§4.13 exactly: `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `tickers`, `klines`, `liquidations`, `open_interest`, `funding_rates`, `bars_time` (+ the other `bars_*` families), `footprint_cells`, `profiles`, `orderflow_metrics`, `heatmap_cells`, `engine_metrics`.
- Idempotent DDL runner keyed on a `_cv_migrations` table **inside QuestDB** (§9.1), run at boot by the storage service, never by request handlers.
- `storage/questdb/ilp_writer.py`: batched ILP-over-TCP writer, flush at **5 000 rows or 100 ms** per §4.14, per-table buffers, bounded queue with explicit backpressure (never silently drop - trades and executions must never be dropped, per `20-architecture.md` §3.1), reconnect with exponential backoff, and a `flush()` that is awaited on `stop()`.
- `storage/questdb/reader.py`: PGWire (8812) async pool using a **read-only** QuestDB user; parameterised queries only (no string interpolation of user input); per-shape query builders for §13.2 shapes 1-11.
- `storage/questdb/repository.py`: `MarketDataRepository` implementation passing the contract suite from E07-T01 unchanged.
- Engine settings applied and asserted at boot: `o3MaxLag=300s`, `maxUncommittedRows=500000`, explicit `SYMBOL CAPACITY` per §4 DDL, WAL on every table.
- Column-drift guard: at boot, the runner compares live table columns against the DDL files and raises `StorageSchemaDrift` rather than writing into a mismatched shape.
- Metrics + health wiring (see Observability).

## Out of scope
- Producing the derived values (`footprint_cells`, `profiles`, `orderflow_metrics`, `heatmap_cells` contents) - E18/E19/E21/E23. This ticket creates the tables and the write/read path only; a fixture-populated row proves the path.
- Export to Parquet and retention drops - E07-T04/T05.
- Ingestion from Bybit - E08 (this ticket is exercised from `packages/fixtures`).
- The `bars_*` builders themselves - E12.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given an empty QuestDB 8.x instance
When the storage service boots
Then all tables from 21-database-schema.md §4 exist with WAL enabled and the declared DEDUP UPSERT KEYS, and _cv_migrations records the applied DDL files

Given the DDL runner runs a second time against the same instance
When boot completes
Then no DDL is re-applied and boot adds under 200 ms, proving idempotency

Given one hour of recorded BTCUSDT trades from packages/fixtures
When they are written through MarketDataRepository.write_trades and then the same file is replayed a second time (simulating E08 resubscribe-on-gap)
Then the row count in `trades` is identical after both runs, proving DEDUP UPSERT KEYS idempotency end-to-end

Given trades for one symbol-day are present
When read_bars is called for bars_time/1m over that day
Then 100k bars return within 100 ms p95 on the reference profile, matching §13.2 shape #1

Given the replay seek shape
When read_book_snapshot_at(ts) then read_book_deltas(ts, ts+1min) are called
Then the snapshot seek completes within 200 ms and the applied deltas reproduce a book whose CRC32 matches orderbook_snapshots.checksum at the next snapshot anchor

Given QuestDB is stopped mid-write
When the ILP writer's queue fills
Then it applies backpressure and increments questdb_write_errors_total, no trade row is dropped, health() reports the tier degraded, and on reconnect the buffered batch is flushed exactly once

Given a table's live column set differs from the DDL file
When the service boots
Then it raises StorageSchemaDrift and refuses readiness instead of writing into a mismatched table

Given a symbol string containing a quote character
When it reaches a read query
Then the parameterised PGWire path escapes it and a SQL-injection test asserts no query-shape change
```

## Technical notes / design
Write path: one `asyncio.Queue` per table class; a single flusher task per table drains it, serialising rows into the ILP line format and writing to the socket. Timestamps are integer microseconds; the designated timestamp is always exchange event time and `recv_ts` is a plain column (§4 conventions). `SYMBOL` columns must be emitted as ILP *tags*, doubles as ILP fields - getting this wrong silently changes the storage shape, so a unit test asserts the serialised line for one golden row of each table.

Read path: asyncpg against PGWire. QuestDB has no secondary indexes; performance comes from the designated timestamp, partition granularity and `SYMBOL` equality filters (§13.2 closing note), so every query builder must (a) filter on `symbol` by equality, (b) bound `ts` on both sides, and (c) never `ORDER BY` a non-timestamp column. A lint test parses each builder's SQL and asserts these three properties.

`LATEST ON ts PARTITION BY symbol` is used for last price (shape #5); `SAMPLE BY` for roll-ups (#3, #8); `ASOF JOIN` for trade<->ticker alignment (#11).

Reversal path note: if E07-K01 selects TimescaleDB, `backend/db/questdb/*.sql` becomes an Alembic revision of hypertable DDL and `ilp_writer.py` becomes a `COPY`-based batch writer; the repository module name and the contract suite do not change.

## Test plan
- Unit: ILP line serialisation golden files per table; batch/flush trigger logic (5 000 rows vs 100 ms, whichever first) with a fake clock; backpressure behaviour at queue-full; query-builder lint (equality symbol filter, bounded ts, timestamp ordering); drift detector.
- Integration (testcontainers QuestDB): DDL idempotency; dedup replay; each of §13.2 shapes 1-11 returning correct results against a fixture dataset with a golden result file; book-reconstruction CRC check; connection-loss and reconnect.
- Contract: E07-T01 repository suite, run against the real engine.
- Perf: shapes A-F from E07-K01 re-run as a regression harness with the spike's `results.json` as the baseline; ILP sustained rows/s vs the >=600k target (§11.4).
- Chaos: covered by E07-Q04.
- Coverage target: >=85% on `storage/questdb/`.

## Security notes
- Read path uses a dedicated **read-only** QuestDB user; the service never issues DDL at runtime except the boot runner and the retention job (§4.14).
- QuestDB's HTTP console and its ports are not published to the host or tailnet (SR-048, threat S6 in `04-security-program.md` §5.8); the compose bind assertion from `E02-T08` covers this and this ticket adds a boot-time self-check enumerating listening sockets (SR-047).
- All queries parameterised; symbol/interval values are additionally validated against an allowlist derived from `instruments` before reaching SQL, because `SYMBOL` filters are the only user-controlled predicate.
- No credentials or PII in this tier (classification A-10, Internal); fixture data only in tests (SR: no real keys in fixtures, `03-testing-strategy.md` §11).

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Targets: §13.2 shapes #1-#11 as tabulated; ILP ingest >=600k rows/s sustained (§11.4, 20x headroom over the 25k rows/s peak for 5 symbols at 200 depth); write path must not contribute to the <=20 ms backend-internal fan-out budget (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.1 budget #6) - storage writes are off the fan-out path by construction (bus subscriber, not inline), and a test asserts the publisher does not await the writer.

## Observability
`questdb_write_seconds` (histogram, per table), `questdb_ilp_rows_total{table,result}`, `questdb_ilp_queue_depth{table}` (gauge), `questdb_write_errors_total{kind}`, `questdb_query_seconds{shape}`, `storage_tier_health{tier="questdb"}`. Structured logs on reconnect and on drift with `tier`, `table`, `symbol` context. `system_events` CRITICAL on schema drift.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All AC green; contract suite passes against the real engine.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on `storage/questdb/`.
- [ ] Perf regression harness committed with baseline numbers recorded (not yet gating, per R0 quality gates).
- [ ] `21-database-schema.md` §4 updated if any DDL detail changed during implementation.
- [ ] Security engineer confirms the bind/console/read-only-user controls.
- [ ] QA sign-off (E07-Q01 cases executed).
- [ ] Demo at Sprint Review: fixture replay -> QuestDB -> a chart-shaped read.

- `E07-T01` Protocols and contract suite.
- Consumed by `E07-T04` (export reads from here) and `E12`/`E16`.

title: Implement Parquet cold tier: hot->cold exporter with checksum manifest, compactor and DuckDB view layer
body:
## Context
Parquet is the archive, the replay source beyond the hot window, and - per ADR-0003 - "an open, portable archive format, an exit hatch even if every database choice changes". `21-database-schema.md` §5 specifies the Hive-partitioned directory layout (§5.1), the exact file-format rules (§5.2: Parquet v2, **ZSTD level 6**, 128 MiB row groups, 1 MiB pages, rows sorted by `ts` then `price`, dictionary on `symbol`/`side`/`action`/`tick_dir`, `TIMESTAMP(MICROS, UTC)`, SHA-256 per file in the manifest), the export job with its **non-negotiable ordering invariant** (§5.3), the compactor (§5.4) and the DuckDB view layer (§5.5). R0 exit criterion #6 requires "a DuckDB query returns one symbol-day".

The invariant, stated in §5.3, is the single most important line in this ticket: *no hot partition is ever dropped before its Parquet counterpart is written, checksummed and row-count-verified*; a crash between steps must leave duplicate data (harmless, dedup on read), never missing data.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `storage/cold/exporter.py` implementing the §5.3 flow: resolve retention policy -> select closed partitions older than `archive_after_days` -> read from QuestDB via PGWire into Arrow -> write Parquet per §5.2 -> SHA-256 + row-count verify against the source `COUNT` -> write manifest entry -> (hand the drop decision to E07-T05's reaper). On verify mismatch: write a `system_events` CRITICAL row, abort the run, keep the hot data.
- Directory layout exactly as §5.1 under `CV_COLD_ROOT` (`/var/lib/candleviewer/cold`, WSL `/mnt/data/candleviewer/cold`), including the `_manifests/` tree and `schema-registry.json`.
- Per-file provenance columns on every export: `_export_run_id STRING`, `_exported_at TIMESTAMP`, `_source STRING`.
- **Schema-drift fail-closed**: the exporter compares the column set against `cold/_manifests/schema-registry.json` and refuses to write on drift (§5.2 last paragraph).
- `storage/cold/manifest.py`: manifest read/write, per-file SHA-256, `verify_checksums()` used by the weekly scrub (SR-094) and on read.
- `storage/cold/compactor.py` per §5.4: trigger at >4 files per partition or any file <16 MiB with siblings; merge to one file per partition <=512 MiB; write `.tmp` -> fsync -> atomic rename -> delete originals, with row count and SHA-256 recorded **before** deletion; skip any partition referenced by an active `replay_sessions` row (idle guard).
- `storage/cold/duckdb_views.py`: builds `cold/analytics.duckdb` views from source on every start (they hold no state, §9.1), including `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `bars`, `footprint_cells`, `executions_cold`, `journal_all` and the analytics helpers `v_daily_pnl`, `v_session_tape_stats` from §5.5; `ATTACH ... AS pg (TYPE postgres, READ_ONLY)` using the `cv_ro` role from E07-T02.
- `ColdTierRepository` implementation satisfying the E07-T01 Protocol.
- **Dataset-id registry**: `query()` accepts a registered dataset id + partition predicates, never a filesystem path (SR-097).

## Out of scope
- Deciding *when* to export/drop and the retention policy engine - E07-T05 (this ticket exposes `export_partition` and `verify`, the reaper orchestrates).
- Cold-cold downsampling of `orderbook_deltas`/`heatmap_cells` past 180 days (§5.4 rollup rule) - deferred to **E16** with a TODO referencing this ticket; the `action='downsample'` branch raises `NotImplementedError` with that reference, and a test asserts the error rather than silent no-op.
- Backup/restic of the lake - E43/PRR (this ticket documents the path).
- Journal/OMS export producers (`oms/` subtree contents) - E41/E29; the layout and the writer support them, a fixture proves the shape.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given one closed symbol-day of trades in QuestDB
When the exporter runs for that partition
Then a Parquet file exists at cold/trades/symbol=BTCUSDT/dt=2026-10-17/part-0000.parquet, is Parquet v2 with ZSTD-6 compression and 128 MiB target row groups, is sorted by ts then price, and carries _export_run_id/_exported_at/_source

Given the exported file
When the manifest is read
Then it contains the file's SHA-256, row count and source table, and the row count equals the QuestDB COUNT(*) for that partition exactly

Given a deliberately corrupted byte in an exported Parquet file
When verify_checksums() runs (weekly scrub or on read)
Then the file is quarantined, a CRITICAL system_event and an alert are raised, and no reader is served data from it

Given the exporter is SIGKILLed after writing Parquet but before the manifest entry
When it is re-run
Then the partition is re-exported, the duplicate file is reconciled to a single manifest entry, and no rows are lost - and because the drop step is downstream, the hot partition is still present

Given the exporter detects a column present in QuestDB but absent from schema-registry.json
When it runs
Then it fails closed with StorageSchemaDrift, exports nothing and leaves the hot partition untouched

Given a partition directory with six 10 MiB files
When the compactor runs
Then it produces a single part-0000.parquet, records its row count and SHA-256 before deleting the originals, and the post-merge row count equals the sum of the inputs

Given a partition referenced by an active replay_sessions row
When the compactor runs
Then that partition is skipped and the skip is logged with the session id

Given cold/analytics.duckdb
When `SELECT count(*) FROM trades WHERE symbol='BTCUSDT' AND dt='2026-10-17'` is issued
Then it returns the exported row count within the §13.3 budget, satisfying R0 exit criterion 6

Given a query() call with dataset_id="../../etc/passwd" or a symlinked partition directory
When it is resolved
Then the registry rejects it, a path-traversal test asserts no filesystem read occurs outside CV_COLD_ROOT (SR-097)
```

## Technical notes / design
Read QuestDB partitions in `ts`-ordered chunks into `pyarrow.RecordBatch`es (target ~1 M rows for trades, ~4 M for deltas so a row group lands near 128 MiB), then `pyarrow.parquet.ParquetWriter(..., version="2.6", compression="zstd", compression_level=6, data_page_size=1<<20, write_statistics=["ts","price","notional","symbol"], use_dictionary=["symbol","side","action","tick_dir"])`. Sorting matters twice - for min/max pruning and for the cheap merge on read - so the writer asserts monotonic `ts` per row group and fails otherwise rather than writing an unsorted file that silently defeats §13.3.

Timestamps must be written as `TIMESTAMP(isAdjustedToUTC=true, unit=MICROS)` to match QuestDB microsecond resolution exactly; a round-trip test asserts no precision loss. Market data stays `DOUBLE`; OMS exports use `DECIMAL(38,18)` (§5.2) - two different writer profiles, selected by dataset id, not by guessing.

Atomicity: every write goes to `part-NNNN.parquet.tmp`, is fsynced, then `os.rename`d within the same directory (rename is atomic on the same filesystem); the manifest entry is appended after the rename. Crash ordering is therefore: file present without manifest (recoverable, re-export) is possible; manifest without file is not.

DuckDB views are recreated from source at every start; the `postgres` extension attachment is `READ_ONLY` with `cv_ro`, which is what prevents an analytics query from ever mutating the ledger.

## Test plan
- Unit: writer profile selection; row-group sizing maths; sort assertion; provenance columns; manifest SHA-256 and append semantics; drift detector; compaction trigger rules and idle guard; dataset-id registry rejection cases (traversal, symlink, absolute path, unregistered id).
- Integration (testcontainers QuestDB + a tmpfs cold root): full export of a fixture symbol-day with row-count parity; corrupted-file scrub; kill-and-resume at each of the three crash points (after write, after checksum, after manifest); compaction of a many-small-files partition; DuckDB symbol-day query returning the exact count; `journal_all` union view across Parquet + Postgres.
- Contract: `ColdTierRepository` suite from E07-T01.
- Perf: export throughput vs the >=200 MB/s write target (§11.4); DuckDB cold-replay scan vs <500 ms/hour of deltas and <2 s/month for trades (§13.3); compression ratio recorded against the 0.5-0.75 GB/day/symbol planning figure (budget #12) and reported so E16 can replace the estimate.
- Coverage target: >=85% on `storage/cold/`.

## Security notes
Threats from `04-security-program.md` §5.8: **S1** silent Parquet corruption -> SR-094 per-file checksum manifest verified on read and by the weekly scrub, with quarantine + alert; **S3** path traversal via export/replay endpoints -> SR-097 registry-addressed datasets, zero user-supplied paths, mandatory traversal and symlink-escape tests (both present in the AC); **S6** DuckDB console exposure -> the DuckDB file is opened in-process only, no server mode, no published port (SR-048). Backups of the lake are encrypted with a key distinct from the runtime KEK (SR-091/SR-092) - documented here, automated in E43. Data classification A-10/A-13. This ticket carries the `security` label and requires Security engineer review before merge.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Budgets: Parquet export >=200 MB/s (§11.4); DuckDB replay scan >=1 GB/s from page cache (§11.4) and the §13.3 per-caller targets; storage growth budget #12 with 0.75 GB/day/symbol as the provisioning figure. The compactor exists specifically because unsorted small files defeat both row-group pruning and the sort-order merge (§13.3 closing note) - its effect is measured before/after and recorded.

## Observability
`storage_export_rows_total{stream,result}`, `storage_export_bytes_total{stream}`, `storage_export_duration_seconds{stream}`, `storage_export_verify_failures_total`, `storage_compaction_files_merged_total`, `storage_cold_bytes{stream}`, `storage_scrub_mismatches_total`. `system_events` CRITICAL on verify failure and on quarantine; audit entry for compaction-triggered deletions. These feed the SCR-142 panel designed in E07-D01.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All AC green, including all three crash-point resume tests.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on `storage/cold/`.
- [ ] Measured compression ratio and export throughput recorded in the PR and in `21-database-schema.md` §14 open-to-verify items.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off on SR-094/SR-097 controls.
- [ ] QA sign-off (E07-Q01 cases).
- [ ] Demo: export a fixture symbol-day and query it through DuckDB (R0 exit #6).
- [ ] 2 approvals incl. code-owner; merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- `E07-T03` - the exporter reads QuestDB partitions.
- `E07-T02` - the `cv_ro` role for the DuckDB Postgres attachment and the `replay_sessions`/`backups` tables' existence for the idle guard and run records (tables land with their owning revisions; until then the guard reads an empty set and a test covers that path).
- Consumed by `E07-T05` (reaper) and by E16/E26.

## Branch
`feat/storage-tier-cold-parquet`; 3 PRs (writer+manifest, compactor, DuckDB views).

- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md`

title: Write and merge ADR-0008 hot-tier selection; reconcile ADR-0003, architecture and schema docs
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3 exit criterion 3 requires **ADR-0008 (hot tier)** merged "with measured numbers attached, not opinions", and §4.5 dates it **2026-10-15**. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 makes an ADR the mandatory output of every spike - "even if the decision is 'defer, need more data'". ADR-0003 already specifies the reversal path, so ADR-0008 either **confirms** ADR-0003's hot tier (and ADR-0003 stands unamended) or **triggers** the amendment ("This ADR is then amended, not superseded").

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0008-hot-tier-selection.md` following the repository ADR template (context, decision drivers, considered options, decision outcome, consequences, validation, references), containing:
  - The full E07-K01 results table: p50/p95/p99 per query shape (A-F) per engine, warm and cold cache, plus ILP/COPY ingest rate and on-disk size after one identical week.
  - The decision rule as it was stated *before* measuring, and the arithmetic of applying it - so a reader can check the conclusion rather than trust it.
  - Explicit treatment of the disputed-benchmark claim that motivated the spike (ADR-0003 decision drivers).
  - Operational comparison (backup/restore, retention primitive, out-of-order handling, dedup/idempotency, daemon count).
  - The reversal path *from this decision*: what would have to be observed in R1/R2 to revisit, and the cost estimate of doing so given the repository abstraction.
- Reconciliation edits:
  - `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md` - Validation section updated with "S2 executed, see ADR-0008"; amended if the fallback was taken.
  - `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §14 risk row and §15 spike S2 row marked resolved; §16 ADR index gains ADR-0008.
  - `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §14 open-to-verify items updated with measured latencies, ingest rate and on-disk size.
  - `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` - the hot-tier risk retired or re-scored with the measured evidence.
- If the fallback is taken: follow-up tickets filed for the TimescaleDB repository implementation, with E07-T03's scope restated and E12/E16 notified via their blocked_by edges.

## Out of scope
- Re-running or extending the benchmark (E07-K01 owns measurement; if the evidence is insufficient, this ticket records "defer" and files the extension, it does not silently measure more).
- ClickHouse reconsideration (needs its own ADR per ADR-0003).
- Implementation changes - E07-T03.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the E07-K01 findings document
When ADR-0008 is drafted
Then every latency figure in the ADR is traceable to a row in the committed results.json, and a reviewer can re-run the quoted harness command line

Given the ADR states a decision
When a reviewer applies the pre-stated decision rule to the tabulated numbers
Then the same conclusion follows deterministically, with no unexplained judgement step

Given the decision confirms QuestDB
When ADR-0003 is reviewed
Then its Validation section cites ADR-0008 and its status remains "decided" with no contradictory text left in place

Given the decision takes the reversal path
When the docs are reviewed
Then ADR-0003 is amended (not superseded), 21-database-schema.md §4 carries the TimescaleDB equivalent DDL, and follow-up implementation tickets exist and are linked

Given the evidence is insufficient within the spike timebox
When ADR-0008 is written
Then it records "defer, need more data" as an explicit decision with the named follow-up and the interim operating assumption, rather than being left unwritten

Given ADR-0008 is merged
When 20-architecture.md §15 and 32-risk-register.md are inspected
Then spike S2 is marked resolved and the corresponding risk row is retired or re-scored
```

Numbers go in the ADR body (a reader must not need a second file to see the decision), raw data stays in `docs/plan/spikes/S2-hot-tier.md` and `results.json`. title: Security: STRIDE threat model for recorder data & storage (Area 8) with abuse cases
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` makes a STRIDE threat model per epic non-negotiable, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the kickoff scheduled at Epic DoR. `04-security-program.md` §5.8 already contains **Area 8 - Recorder data & storage (A-10, A-12, A-13)** with six threats (S1 Parquet corruption, S2 disk exhaustion **Critical**, S3 path traversal, S4 export scoping, S5 pinned-data deletion, S6 console exposure). That table is the *planning-level* model; this ticket produces the **implementation-level** model for what E07 actually builds, confirms or refutes the residual-risk ratings against the real design, and hands E07-T05 the constraints it must implement (which is why it blocks T05).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implementation-level STRIDE model document `docs/security/threat-models/E07-storage.md` covering:
  - Assets: A-10 recorded market data (QuestDB hot, Parquet cold), A-13 backups, plus the relational tier's role/privilege surface created by E07-T02.
  - Trust boundaries touched: **TB-3** host -> WSL/docker network (loopback binds), **TB-6** live data -> backups, and the new internal boundary between the analytics path (DuckDB, `cv_ro`) and the ledger (Postgres, `cv_app`/`cv_owner`).
  - Actors: AC-07 recorder/ingestion worker (machine, medium trust, no credentials), AC-12 LAN network adversary, AC-01/AC-02 Owner/Manager identities reaching storage through admin endpoints.
  - Per-element STRIDE enumeration for: the ILP write path, the PGWire read path, the exporter + manifest, the compactor, the DuckDB view layer + Postgres attachment, the retention reaper, the Alembic migration path, and the three data-store network binds.
- **Abuse cases** written as adversary narratives with a concrete test each:
  - "As a Manager with `recording:read`, I enumerate another user's symbols and infer their strategy" (S4 adjacency, scope checks).
  - "As anything that can reach the host, I open the QuestDB HTTP console and read the tape" (S6).
  - "As a caller of any read endpoint, I supply a dataset id that resolves outside `CV_COLD_ROOT`" (S3, incl. symlinked partition dirs).
  - "As a user who can change retention, I set hot_days=0 globally and destroy the recording" (privilege + audit + confirmation).
  - "As a process on the box, I fill the recording volume and take trading down with it" (S2).
  - "As a corrupted disk, I return a Parquet file whose checksum still matches its stale manifest entry" (S1, manifest-file binding).
  - "As a migration author, I ship a revision that drops an audited table" (tampering with the ledger of record).
- Constraint hand-off to E07-T05: the ordered control flow (alert-before-delete, dry-run-first, pins honoured, export-verified-before-drop) written as testable requirements referencing SR-094/SR-096/SR-097/SR-099.
- Residual-risk table with sign-off, and any new threat merged back into `04-security-program.md` §5.8.
- Data-classification confirmation per `21-database-schema.md` §12 for every column E07's revisions create.

## Out of scope
- Auth/RBAC threat modelling (Area on auth) - E09.
- Exchange-boundary threats - E08.
- Key management / envelope encryption - E27/E09 (this model only asserts that no key material reaches the storage tier E07 builds).
- Implementing the controls - E07-T02..T05; verifying them - E07-X02.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the implementation-level model
When it is compared against 04-security-program.md §5.8
Then every one of S1-S6 is either confirmed with its planning-level residual rating, or re-rated with a written justification, and any newly discovered threat is added to §5.8 in the same PR

Given each abuse case
When it is reviewed
Then it names a concrete test (unit, integration, chaos or manual procedure) and an owning ticket, so no abuse case ends as prose only

Given the model's constraint hand-off
When E07-T05 is implemented
Then its control flow matches the ordered requirements (alert before delete, dry-run first, pins honoured, export verified before drop) and a reviewer can trace each to an SR id

Given a threat rated High or Critical
When triage completes
Then it is either mitigated by a named control in an E07 ticket or accepted with the Owner's recorded sign-off - never left untriaged

Given the migration path is modelled
When a revision that would drop or rewrite an audited table is proposed
Then the model prescribes the control (code-owner approval on backend/db/**, forward-only rule, pre-migration backup) and E07-T02 implements it
```

## Technical notes / design
Model the system as it will exist at R0 end, not as the finished product - but call out where an R3 addition (journal exports, replay endpoints) will reopen a threat, so those epics inherit a warning rather than rediscovering it. Use the existing §5.8 table format for continuity (T id, STRIDE category, threat, L, I, Risk, Mitigations with SR ids, Residual).

Particular attention to the **manifest-file binding** (abuse case 6): a checksum stored beside the file it describes is only integrity, not authenticity. Record whether that is acceptable at this threat level (it likely is - the adversary model here is corruption, not a privileged attacker) and state the reasoning, so a later reviewer does not assume it was overlooked.

## Test plan
The model itself is reviewed, not tested; but each abuse case must land as a test in E07-Q01 (scripted), E07-Q04 (chaos) or E07-X02 (control verification). A traceability table (abuse case -> test id -> ticket) is part of the deliverable and is checked at epic DoD.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security work. Classification: the model document itself is Internal and must not contain live hostnames, ports as deployed, or any credential.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Where a control has a performance cost (per-read checksum verification, dry-run before every reaper run), the model states the cost and the chosen trade-off so E07-Q03 measures it deliberately rather than discovering it.

## Observability
Specifies the security-relevant signals E07 must emit: audit entries for every deletion and every retention-policy change, `system_events` on quarantine and verify failure, and an alert path for the disk thresholds - each mapped to the SR that requires it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Model document committed and reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect.
- [ ] `04-security-program.md` §5.8 updated with any new or re-rated threat.
- [ ] Abuse-case -> test traceability table complete, every case owned.
- [ ] Constraints handed to E07-T05 before its implementation starts (this ticket blocks it).
- [ ] High/Critical threats mitigated or accepted with Owner sign-off.
- [ ] Data classification confirmed for every column created by E07's revisions.
- [ ] Findings presented at a Security Review.

## Dependencies
- `E02` for the module layout and compose topology being modelled.
- Blocks `E07-T05`; informs `E07-T02`, `E07-T03`, `E07-T04` and `E07-X02`.

## Branch
`chore/e07-threat-model`.

## References

- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §12 (PII/secret classification), §9.3

title: Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton
body:
## Context
Every downstream feature of CandleViewer - charting, bar builders, footprint, profiles, DOM heatmap, CVD, detectors, recorder, replay and OMS reconciliation - consumes exactly **one** market-data path. This Epic builds that path: the exchange-agnostic adapter port (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §9, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14), its Bybit v5 implementation for **USDT linear perpetuals only** (`category=linear`), the public WebSocket ingestion skeleton (`publicTrade`, `orderbook.200`, `tickers`), local L2 book reconstruction, and the in-process bus with bounded queues and backpressure (modules **M3 exchange adapter, M4 Bybit implementation, M5 bus, M6 ingestion**).

`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11 places E08 on the critical path: `E02 -> E08` and then `E08 -> {E12, E16, E17, E22, E24, E29}`. Nine downstream epics depend on it, so its contracts are frozen early and its quality gates are non-negotiable.

Two architectural principles are binding here and shape the whole ticket tree:
- **P3 - no Bybit field name exists outside `candleviewer/exchange/bybit/`** (`20-architecture.md` §0, `24-internal-schemas.md` C9), lint-enforced.
- **Correctness under loss is deterministic, not best-effort.** Bybit's L2 stream carries no checksum, so a sequence gap invalidates the book and forces a re-snapshot - never a silent patch (`20-architecture.md` §3.1/§3.2).

## Scope / Deliverables
User stories delivered (all Must, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §4 MKT):
- **US-MKT-001** Instrument catalogue -> `E08-S01`
- **US-MKT-004** Precision & filter validation -> `E08-S02`
- **US-MKT-005** Live ticker stream -> `E08-S03`
- **US-MKT-006** Trade (tape) stream ingestion -> `E08-S04`
- **US-MKT-007** Order-book reconstruction -> `E08-S05`
- **US-MKT-008** Historical OHLCV backfill -> `E08-S06`
- **US-MKT-009** Clock sync and server-time offset -> `E08-S07`

Technical deliverables:
- `services/api/candleviewer/exchange/base.py` - `MarketDataPort`, `TradingPort` (declared only), `ExchangeCapabilities`, internal error taxonomy (`E08-T01`).
- `services/api/candleviewer/exchange/bybit/` - signed REST client, per-UID token bucket, `X-Bapi-Limit-Status` feedback, retCode classification incl. `10018`/`10002` (`E08-T02`); `Normalizer` for the eight public event families (`E08-S03`, `E08-S04`, `E08-S05`).
- `services/api/candleviewer/bus/` - topic bus, bounded queues, per-class backpressure matrix (`E08-T03`).
- `services/api/candleviewer/ingestion/` - `ConnectionManager`, `SubscriptionPlanner` (<=10 args/frame), `Heartbeat/Watchdog`, `ReconnectPolicy`, `SequenceTracker`, `ClockGuard` (`E08-T04`, `E08-S07`).
- `services/api/candleviewer/book/` - `BookState`, `Resyncer`, depth-tier switch (`E08-S05`).
- REST surface: `GET /instruments`, `GET /instruments/{symbol}`, `POST /instruments/refresh`, `GET /instruments/{symbol}/ticker`, `GET /market/klines` (`22-api-openapi.yaml`).
- Postgres `instruments`, `instrument_versions`; QuestDB `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `tickers`, `klines` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`).
- Recorded fixture corpus + `pytest -m exchange_smoke` demo smoke suite (`E08-T05`); ingestion metrics and ADR reconciliation (`E08-T06`).

## Out of scope
- Client-facing WS protocol, topics and binary framing - **E17** (this Epic publishes on the internal bus only).
- Bar building, footprint, profiles, heatmap engines - **E12**, **E18**-**E21**.
- Persistence/retention policy and the recorder - **E16** (E08 writes only what its own stories need).
- Private WS, authenticated trading, order entry - **E29** (`TradingPort` is declared, not implemented).
- Open interest, funding history, liquidations ingestion - **E24**.
- Any exchange other than Bybit, any category other than `linear`, inverse/spot/options.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One path, one vocabulary
  Given the backend is running against Bybit demo with three symbols subscribed
  When the lint rule for principle P3 runs over services/api/candleviewer/
  Then no Bybit field name or retCode integer appears outside candleviewer/exchange/bybit/
  And every consumer receives only normalised domain events from the bus

Scenario: A 24-hour soak stays within budget
  Given three symbols are ingested continuously for 24 hours
  Then resident memory is flat within +/-5%, no bounded queue has overflowed a never-drop class
  And ingest->bus p95 is <=20 ms and book-apply p95 is <=2 ms

Scenario: The feed rots and the system notices
  Given a socket stops delivering messages while the TCP connection stays open
  Then the per-topic staleness watchdog fires within its threshold, the connection is recycled with backoff
  And downstream consumers observe an explicit stale/resyncing state rather than frozen values

Scenario: Sequence gap never becomes silent corruption
  Given an orderbook update arrives with a non-contiguous sequence number
  Then the book is marked DESYNCED, a fresh snapshot is requested, buffered deltas are replayed in order
  And no consumer is ever served a book assembled across the gap
```

## Technical notes / design
Modules M3-M6 per `20-architecture.md` §3.1/§3.2. Adapter rules §14.2 of `24-internal-schemas.md` are binding: normalized events only, adapters never touch Postgres, all methods cancellable, contract-tested against recorded fixtures. Time is integer microseconds (`TsUs`); Bybit millisecond fields are x1000 at the adapter boundary and nowhere else.

Depth tier and cadence are a measured decision, not an assumption - `E08-K01` settles 200 @ 100 ms vs 500 @ 200 ms with numbers before `E08-S05` commits.

## Test plan
- Unit: normalizer mapping tables, sequence tracker, token bucket, rounding rules (property-based).
- Contract: recorded Bybit fixtures replayed through the adapter; OpenAPI contract tests for the `/instruments` and `/market/klines` surfaces.
- Integration: full ingestion pipeline over fixtures with invariant assertions (no crossed book, monotonic levels, exactly-once trades by `tradeId`).
- Chaos: WS drop, exchange 5xx, `10018` rate limit, sequence gap, clock skew.
- Perf: 24 h soak + 5x burst injector against budgets in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.
- Smoke: `pytest -m exchange_smoke` against Bybit **demo** only, never live.

## Security notes
Epic is `security`-labelled: a STRIDE model for the exchange boundary must be finalised before R0 exit (`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 threat-model row). Key handling: E08's public path needs no credentials, but the signed REST path built here is the one the OMS will later use, so signing, `recv_window` handling and secret redaction in logs/fixtures are reviewed now. Recorded fixtures must be provably secret-free.

## Accessibility notes
E08 is a backend Epic with one user-visible surface family: stale/resyncing/disconnected state semantics consumed by SCR-152, SCR-147 and SCR-151. This Epic must *emit* the states those screens need (staleness, resync, gap, drift) with text-expressible semantics, never colour-only signals invented downstream. Design tickets for those screens live in chunk B.

## Performance notes
Budgets (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md`): ingest->bus p95 <=20 ms; book apply p95 <=2 ms; sustained 5 000 prints/s across subscribed symbols without loss; per-symbol memory <=300 MB; CPU <=0.5 vCPU/symbol; event-loop lag p99 within the §12 budget.

## Observability
Metrics: `ingest_events_total{stream,symbol}`, `ingest_queue_full_total{class}`, `ingest_lag_seconds`, `ws_reconnects_total{reason}`, `ws_topic_staleness_seconds{topic}`, `book_resyncs_total{symbol,reason}`, `bybit_rate_limit_remaining`, `bybit_rate_limited_total{code}`, `bybit_clock_drift_ms`, `instruments_refresh_total{result}`. Structured logs carry `symbol`, `stream`, `seq`, `conn_id`. Grafana row "Ingestion" plus alerts on staleness, drift and resync rate.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child Stories/Tasks/Spikes Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level AC verified end-to-end on demo, not just per child.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on `services/api/candleviewer/{exchange,ingestion,book,bus}`.
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §3.1/§3.2/§9 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §2/§14 reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] STRIDE model finalised, findings triaged, Security-engineer sign-off (chunk B).
- [ ] 24 h soak numbers recorded against the budgets above; ADR for depth-tier policy merged.
- [ ] QA epic-level regression + exploratory pass recorded; demoed to Owner at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated for R6/R7 with the measured evidence.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E02** (monorepo scaffold, packages, lint/typecheck), **E04** (observability baseline: metrics registry, tracing, Grafana), **E07** (storage tier wiring: QuestDB/Postgres access). Downstream: E12, E16, E17, E21, E22, E24, E29.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  T01[E08-T01 adapter ports] --> T02[E08-T02 REST client]
  T01 --> T03[E08-T03 bus]
  T02 --> S01[E08-S01 instrument catalogue]
  T02 --> S07[E08-S07 clock sync]
  S01 --> S02[E08-S02 precision rules]
  T03 --> K01[E08-K01 depth-tier spike]
  T01 --> T04[E08-T04 WS skeleton]
  T03 --> T04
  T04 --> S03[E08-S03 ticker stream]
  S03 --> S04[E08-S04 trade tape]
  T04 --> S05[E08-S05 book reconstruction]
  K01 --> S05
  S01 --> S06[E08-S06 kline backfill]
  S04 --> T05[E08-T05 fixtures & smoke]
  S05 --> T05
  S05 --> T06[E08-T06 metrics & ADR reconcile]
  S06 --> T06
```

## Branch
`feat/e08-bybit-ingestion` as the umbrella naming convention; each child ships its own `feat/e08-<short>` branch, PRs <=400 LOC.

## References
`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §0, §3.1, §3.2, §4, §9; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §2, §14; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §4; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/instruments*`, `/market/klines`); `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5, §11; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0004-modular-monolith.md`.


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. title: ADR-0006 exchange-adapter boundary and the market-data trust contract doc
body:
## Context
Nine downstream epics will consume E08's output, and every one of them needs to know two things that currently live only in ticket bodies and reviewers' heads: **what the adapter boundary guarantees** (and what it deliberately does not), and **how much a consumer may trust a given piece of market data**. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires the `2x-*` architecture docs to reflect *shipped* behaviour rather than the original proposal, and `E08-T06` reconciles the implementation docs — but the *decisions* need an ADR, and the trust semantics need a document a downstream developer can read in ten minutes.

Without this, each downstream epic re-derives the rules, and they will derive them differently — which is exactly how a chart ends up rendering an unconfirmed bar as closed, or an estimated metric as measured.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR** `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0006-exchange-adapter-boundary.md` in the established ADR format (context, decision, consequences, alternatives, validation gate), recording:
  - The port/adapter split (`MarketDataPort`, `TradingPort` declared-only, `ExchangeCapabilities`) and why capability-record-driven behaviour beats per-call conditionals.
  - Principle P3 (no Bybit vocabulary outside the adapter package) and its lint enforcement (`E08-X03`).
  - The deterministic invalidate-and-resync rule for gapped L2, and the explicit rejection of checksum-less silent patching.
  - The depth-tier and cadence decision from `E08-K01` (200 vs 500), with the measured evidence that settled it.
  - Environment separation: one client instance per environment, capability-record-enforced (SR-040a).
  - Decimal-only arithmetic for price/quantity, and µs-normalised timestamps anchored to exchange time.
  - Consequences for a future second exchange adapter, and the contract-suite reuse that adapter rule 5 buys.
- **Trust contract doc** `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` addendum (or a linked `docs/plan/25-market-data-trust-contract.md` if it exceeds an addendum), stating per data class:
  - **Measured vs derived vs estimated** — bars and trades are measured; CVD and imbalance are derived; iceberg/stop-run detection is *estimated* and must be labelled as such in any UI that shows it (an `R9 Advice boundary` and honesty requirement, and already a product rule for `SCR-104`).
  - **Confirmed vs unconfirmed** — the `confirm` flag semantics and the prohibition on treating the last bar as closed (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 note).
  - **Fresh vs stale vs desynced** — the three states, their thresholds, who publishes them and how a consumer must render them.
  - **Complete vs gapped** — how coverage is expressed (`GET /market/data-coverage`) and what a consumer must do with a hole rather than interpolating it.
  - A short "rules for consumers" checklist that E12/E17/E22/E24/E29 can be reviewed against.
- Cross-links added from `20-architecture.md` §3, `24-internal-schemas.md` §14 and the E08 epic ticket.

## Out of scope
- Reconciling the implementation detail of `20-architecture.md`/`24-internal-schemas.md` with shipped behaviour (`E08-T06` owns that).
- The WS protocol document and its framing decisions (E17, ADR-0005).
- Writing downstream epics' own ADRs.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR records decisions with their evidence
  Given ADR-0006 is merged
  When it is reviewed against the E08-K01 spike results
  Then the depth-tier decision cites the measured numbers that settled it
  And every decision states at least one rejected alternative and why

Scenario: A downstream developer can classify any data they receive
  Given a developer starting E22 who has read only the trust contract doc
  When they are shown a footprint cell, an unconfirmed bar and a detector output
  Then they can state for each whether it is measured, derived or estimated and how it must be labelled
  And they can state the required rendering for stale and desynced states

Scenario: Failure case - the doc contradicts the implementation
  Given the implementation changes the staleness threshold
  When the doc reconciliation check in E08-T06 runs
  Then the mismatch is reported and blocks the R0 exit review
  And the doc is corrected rather than the mismatch being annotated

Scenario: Edge case - estimated data must never be presented as measured
  Given any detector or scanner output described in the trust contract
  When a consumer epic is reviewed against the consumer checklist
  Then an unlabelled estimated value is recorded as a defect against that epic
  And the checklist item names the required label text convention

Scenario: The ADR is discoverable
  Given a reader starting from 20-architecture.md section 3
  When they follow the links
  Then they reach ADR-0006 and the trust contract without prior knowledge of the file names
```

## Technical notes / design
- The ADR is written *after* `E08-K01` and `E08-X01` deliberately, so it records decisions that were actually made and tested rather than intentions.
- The trust contract is written as rules for *consumers*, not as a description of producers — this is what makes it usable as a review checklist.
- Anything the docs assert must be enforced somewhere (a test, a lint rule, or a schema); assertions with no enforcement are marked as conventions, honestly labelled as such.

## Test plan
- Doc review by the Architect, the E08 tech lead, the Security engineer and one engineer from a downstream epic (E12 or E22) acting as the target reader.
- Comprehension check: the downstream reviewer answers the classification questions in acceptance scenario 2 without asking the author; failures rewrite the doc.
- A link-check job ensures the cross-references resolve.

## Security notes
- The trust contract is a security-relevant document: "what may be trusted" is precisely the question `E08-X01` models, and the doc must not overstate guarantees. Security engineer review is required, not optional.
- No host names, credentials or egress details beyond what is already public in the architecture docs.

## Accessibility notes
- The trust contract states the *accessibility obligations* that flow from data honesty: stale/desynced/estimated states must be conveyed by more than colour and must be announced as status messages (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.1, 4.1.3), so downstream UI epics inherit the requirement rather than rediscovering it.
- Mermaid diagrams include text alternatives/descriptions per the docs conventions.

## Performance notes
- The ADR records the cadence/depth trade-off in performance terms (bandwidth, parse cost, book-rebuild cost) with the `E08-K01` numbers, so a future proposal to move to depth 500 starts from measured evidence rather than preference.

## Observability
- The trust contract names, per state, the metric and log signal that proves the state was published — connecting the consumer-facing contract to the `E08-T06` dashboard so "is this stale?" is answerable operationally.

## Definition of Done
- ADR-0006 merged in the standard ADR format with a validation gate stated.
- Trust contract merged and cross-linked from `20-architecture.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md` and the E08 epic.
- Downstream-reader comprehension check passed and recorded.
- Architect and Security engineer review comments present.
- ADR index updated.

## Dependencies
- `E08-K01` (depth/cadence evidence), `E08-X01` (trust and threat framing); complements `E08-T06` (implementation-doc reconciliation).

title: Hi-fi: SCR-103 symbol info drawer - contract specs and precision rules
body:
## Context
`US-MKT-001` makes the instruments-info cache the single source of precision truth, and `US-MKT-004` requires the same validation rules on client and server with property-based tests. `SCR-103` Symbol info / instrument detail is where those rules become visible to the trader: tick size, lot size, min/max qty, min notional, max leverage, risk-limit tiers, funding interval and next settlement, settlement asset, status - plus CandleViewer-side facts (recording status, coverage start, disk used, retention, pin state).

The design problem is separating three classes of fact that look similar but have very different trust properties: exchange-enforced contract rules (static, authoritative), live market values (subject to staleness), and our own recorder facts (local). Conflating them is how a trader ends up trusting a stale funding countdown.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-103` covering: populated (recorded), populated (not recorded), live block stale/reconnecting, delisted/suspended, catalogue refresh in progress, load error.
- Explicit three-band layout separating contract rules / live values / CandleViewer facts, with the "these rules are enforced by the exchange" note required by the catalogue checklist.
- Components specified: `CMP-036` KeyValueRow (with units), `CMP-046` Drawer, `CMP-125` SymbolInfoPopover, `CMP-126` FundingCountdown, `CMP-177` RecorderStatusRow, `CMP-021` Link, plus the freshness marker from E08-D04.
- Number formatting spec: how tick/lot sizes and min notional are rendered (significant digits, no lossy rounding), and how a precision rule is shown next to an example so the rule is understandable.
- Cross-links: recording status links to the recorder admin screen for Owner only; delisted state links to the chart banner behaviour from E08-D03.

## Out of scope
- The order ticket's own validation UI (`US-MKT-004` enforcement at entry) - owned by the trading epics; this drawer only *explains* the rules.
- Recorder configuration screens (referenced, not designed here).
- Funding/OI analytics views (DERIV epic).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fact classes are visually separated
  Given the populated drawer
  When reviewed
  Then contract rules, live values and CandleViewer recorder facts occupy distinct labelled bands
  And the exchange-enforcement note appears with the contract rules band

Scenario: Live block degrades without contaminating static facts
  Given the ticker stream for the symbol is stale
  When the drawer is rendered
  Then only the live band carries the stale treatment
  And the contract-rule band remains presented as authoritative

Scenario: Delisted or suspended symbol (edge case)
  Given the instrument status is not Trading
  When the drawer opens
  Then a prominent status explanation is shown, the funding countdown is suppressed rather than counting to a settlement that will not happen, and order-entry entry points are absent

Scenario: Catalogue load failure (failure case)
  Given GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol} fails
  When the drawer opens
  Then an error state explains that contract rules could not be loaded and that order entry is blocked until they are
  And a retry action is offered

Scenario: Precision values are never rounded misleadingly
  Given a tick size such as 0.00001
  When rendered
  Then the full precise value is shown, not a truncated approximation
  And the formatting rule is stated in the spec

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO and accessibility review are complete
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data sources per the catalogue: `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` and `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage?symbol`; live fields subscribe to `ticker.{symbol}` only while the drawer is open (and must unsubscribe on close, respecting the 30 s grace from `US-MKT-005`).
- The funding countdown depends on the clock offset from `US-MKT-009`; the spec must define what the countdown shows when the offset alarm is active (show the warning, do not silently display a possibly-wrong countdown).
- Risk-limit tiers can be a long table - specify collapse/expand and the maximum default height inside a drawer.
- Recorder facts are Owner-relevant; specify the Manager/Viewer variant.

## Test plan
- Review against the `SCR-103` design sign-off acceptance checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md`, item by item, recorded on the ticket.
- Screen-reader dry run of the description-list structure and units.
- Formatting spec validated against real Bybit instrument fixtures (smallest and largest tick/lot values present in the linear universe).
- QA walkthrough to agree test ids and to confirm each state is reachable in a test environment.

## Security notes
- Recorder facts (disk used, retention, coverage) reveal system internals; the spec defines RBAC visibility (Owner full, Manager limited, Viewer none) so an over-sharing default is not shipped.
- Links to admin screens must be hidden, not merely disabled, for roles without access.
- No API keys, account ids or internal hostnames rendered in any state including errors.

## Accessibility notes
- Facts are a description list with explicit units per `SCR-103`; the contract-rules section uses plain sentences.
- External references are labelled as leaving the app.
- The countdown is a live region updated at <=1 Hz with a text alternative ("funding in 3 h 12 m"), and is not announced continuously.
- Drawer follows the standard dialog focus rules from the design system (focus moves in, is trapped, restores on close).

## Performance notes
- Static metadata is cached; the drawer must open without a network round-trip when the catalogue is warm.
- Only the live band subscribes; subscription is torn down on close.
- Countdown updates <=1 Hz; risk-limit table virtualised or collapsed if long.

## Observability
- `symbol.info_viewed` analytics event specified.
- Error state emits an event distinguishing catalogue-load failure from coverage-load failure so we can tell which dependency broke.

## Definition of Done
- Frames for all states in both themes, tokenised against E08-D04.
- Formatting and RBAC visibility rules documented; catalogue checklist fully ticked.
- `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-103` updated where the design diverged.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done), >=2 sprints ahead of the consuming FE story.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E08-D04 (data-confidence tokens and state set must be published before this drawer is specified).
- Consumes contract-spec field semantics from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` and the instrument cache shape delivered by E08-S01.
- Rounding/precision copy must match the single rule source defined by E08-S02; any divergence is a design bug, not an implementation choice.
- Downstream: E08-D13 (handoff pack) and E08-D14 (design QA) both cover this surface; frontend build of SCR-103 is gated on this ticket being Done.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-100 watchlist panel & SCR-101 manager with live-column states
body:
## Context
The watchlist is the highest-density consumer of E08's ticker fan-out: `US-MKT-003` requires live last price, 24 h %, 24 h volume, funding, next-funding countdown and OI change for up to 200 symbols, driven by **one batched tickers subscription** with <=10 topics per subscribe frame, and requires stale cells to grey out with an explicit marker rather than freeze. `SCR-100` additionally caps updates at 4 Hz coalesced and virtualises beyond 60 rows.

This is where the E08-D04 freshness marker gets its hardest test: it must be legible at row density, cheap at 4 Hz across 200 rows, and unambiguous when only *some* columns are stale (e.g. tickers fine, OI feed lagging).

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-100`: populated, loading, empty ("Add symbols to watch"), partially stale (per-column and per-row), fully disconnected, delisted row (struck through with explanation), subscription cap reached ("Watching 200 symbols - remove some to add more"), REC chip states.
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-101` Watchlist manager modal: create/rename/duplicate/delete, reorder (drag plus explicit move up/down buttons), bulk add by paste, import/export, per-list column configuration, delete confirmation, empty state, validation errors (duplicate name, >200 symbols).
- Column spec: which columns are live-subscribed vs derived, sort behaviour, column picker defaults, and the numeric formatting/sign conventions (plus/minus signs per the catalogue a11y note).
- Components: `CMP-011` Tag / Chip, `CMP-026` EmptyState, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-056` ColumnPicker, `CMP-161` WatchlistRow, `CMP-162` WatchlistGroupTabs, `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-044` ConfirmDialog, `CMP-067` FileDrop.
- Interaction spec: click to set active symbol for the focused sync group, drag onto a panel to rebind, `Del` to remove, right-click menu (record/unrecord Owner-only, open in new chart, add alert, copy symbol).

## Out of scope
- The scanner/screener (`SCR-104`) - E08-D08.
- Recorder administration screens (linked only).
- Alert creation flow (entry point only).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Per-column staleness is expressible
  Given tickers are live but the OI-derived column has not updated within its threshold
  When the row renders
  Then only the affected cells carry the stale marker and the row is not marked wholly stale
  And the spec states the per-column thresholds

Scenario: Frozen values never look live (failure case)
  Given the tickers stream drops for the whole list
  When the panel renders
  Then every live cell is demoted with an explicit stale treatment and the panel-level indicator from E08-D03 is shown
  And no cell retains its live styling

Scenario: Subscription cap
  Given the list already contains 200 symbols
  When the user attempts to add another
  Then the cap state is shown with the exact message and a path to remove symbols
  And the add control communicates the cap before the attempt where possible

Scenario: Reorder without a pointer
  Given a keyboard-only user in SCR-101
  When they reorder a list
  Then explicit move up / move down controls are available and announce the new position

Scenario: Delisted row (edge case)
  Given a symbol is delisted while on a watchlist
  Then the row is struck through with 'Delisted by the exchange', the stale marker is suppressed per the precedence rule, and its chart/order entry points are disabled

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO, accessibility specialist and engineering have reviewed
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Design must respect the subscription model: one batched `ticker.{symbol}` subscription set with <=10 args per subscribe frame, fan-out internally (`US-MKT-005`); the spec forbids any design that implies a per-row independent connection.
- Virtualisation beyond 60 rows means off-screen rows have no subscriptions - the spec must define what an off-screen row shows when scrolled into view (a brief initialising state, not a fabricated value).
- Next-funding countdown per row at 1 Hz would be 200 timers; the spec mandates a single shared clock tick and identical rounding across rows.
- Import/export format for `SCR-101` must be specified (plain symbol list, validation on import, what happens to unknown/delisted symbols on import).

## Test plan
- Density review at the supported density settings with 200 rows of realistic Bybit symbols.
- Screen-reader pass on the ARIA grid, sortable headers and the REC chip text.
- Walkthrough with engineering against the batched subscription constraints and the 4 Hz coalescing budget.
- Both catalogue design sign-off checklists (`SCR-101`) ticked item by item on the ticket.

## Security notes
- Record/unrecord is an Owner-only, audited action (`recorder.auto_record_started`) - the spec must hide, not merely disable, the control for other roles.
- Import accepts a user-supplied file: the spec mandates that imported symbol strings are validated against the instrument catalogue and rendered as text, never interpreted; oversized files are rejected with a clear message.
- Exported files contain only symbol lists - the spec states that no account or key data is ever included.

## Accessibility notes
- Table is a proper ARIA grid with sortable headers and a caption; percentage changes carry explicit plus/minus signs (not colour alone).
- REC chip has a text label; stale markers have text equivalents; announcements are summarised at panel level rather than per-cell to avoid flooding.
- Every action button in `SCR-101` names its target; reorder has non-drag equivalents; delete is a ConfirmDialog.
- Right-click actions are available from a keyboard-accessible menu too.

## Performance notes
- Budget: ticker updates coalesced to 4 Hz; virtualised beyond 60 rows (`SCR-100`).
- Stale marking must be a class toggle on existing cells - no extra DOM per cell, no per-row animation (constraint inherited from E08-D04).
- Countdown driven by one shared timer; sorting must not re-mount rows.

## Observability
- Analytics per catalogue: `watchlist.symbol_added`, `watchlist.symbol_removed`, `watchlist.reordered`, `watchlist.column_changed`, `watchlist.symbol_activated`, `watchlist.created|renamed|deleted|duplicated|imported`; audited `recorder.auto_record_started`.
- `data_confidence.state_entered {surface: SCR-100, state}` so we can measure how often traders see stale data.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-104 scanner panel - live criteria, caps and estimated metrics
body:
## Context
`SCR-104` Scanner / screener filters the whole USDT-perp universe by live criteria (24 h change, volume, funding rate, OI delta, tape-speed z-score, spread, volatility) against `GET /api/v1/scanner?filters=` on a 5 s cadence, capped at 200 results. It depends on E08's instruments catalogue (`US-MKT-001`) and ticker fan-out (`US-MKT-005`), and it is the first surface that mixes exchange-reported facts with **heuristic, estimated** metrics (tape-speed z-score, regime) that must be flagged with `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge per the `R9 Advice boundary` discipline.

The design risk is that a screener implies precision it does not have; the design must make "estimated" and "only live metrics for non-recorded symbols" unmissable.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-104`: filter bar with the full criteria set, results table with sparklines, no matches, too many matches (capped at 200 with a note), filter validation error ("Minimum must be less than maximum"), scan failed, scan stale/degraded when the underlying feeds are degraded.
- Saved-preset UI: save, rename, delete, apply, default preset, and the copy explaining that presets store criteria, not results.
- Result actions: open chart, add to watchlist, create alert.
- Estimated-metric treatment: `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge in the *filter list itself* (not only on results) and the explanatory note that scanning is limited to live metrics for symbols we are not recording.
- Components: `CMP-011` Tag / Chip, `CMP-024` Sparkline, `CMP-026` EmptyState, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-055` FilterBar, `CMP-056` ColumnPicker, `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge.

## Out of scope
- The detector algorithms themselves (DET epic) - this design only presents their outputs and flags them as estimated.
- Alert configuration (entry point only).
- Server-side scan implementation and its query language.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Estimated criteria are flagged before use
  Given the filter bar lists tape-speed z-score and regime
  When a user opens the criteria list
  Then those options carry the estimated badge in the option list itself
  And selecting one surfaces a one-line explanation of how it is derived

Scenario: Result cap is explained, not silent
  Given more than 200 instruments match
  When results render
  Then exactly 200 are shown with an explicit note that the result set is capped and how to narrow it
  And sorting is stated to apply to the capped set, not the universe

Scenario: Invalid filter range (failure case)
  Given a minimum greater than the maximum
  When the filter is applied
  Then an inline validation error names the offending filter and the rule
  And the previous result set is retained rather than cleared to an ambiguous empty state

Scenario: Underlying feed degraded (edge case)
  Given the ticker or OI feed is stale
  When a scan returns
  Then results are marked as computed from possibly stale inputs using the E08-D04 vocabulary
  And the scan is not presented as authoritative

Scenario: No matches vs scan failed are distinct
  Given a scan that returns zero rows and a scan that errors
  Then each has its own state and copy, and neither reuses the other's wording

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO and accessibility review are complete
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Per the catalogue, scanning is server-side over the hot tier; the panel polls at <=0.2 Hz or subscribes to a scan topic and **never** evaluates criteria client-side across the universe - annotate this constraint in the spec so no future designer proposes client-side filtering.
- Sparklines must be cheap: specify sample count and that they are static per refresh, not animated.
- Preset storage is per user; specify conflict behaviour if a preset references a criterion later removed.
- Copy must preserve the advice boundary: the scanner surfaces conditions, never recommendations.

## Test plan
- Review against the `SCR-104` design sign-off acceptance checklist, item by item, recorded on the ticket.
- Content review of all estimated-metric explanations by the content reviewer and the Architect (accuracy of the derivation description).
- Screen-reader pass on the filter controls, the result count announcement and the table caption stating the active filter set in plain language.
- Density/perf review with 200 rows and sparklines at the supported densities.

## Security notes
- Scanner results are public market metadata; the spec states that no account-scoped data (positions, PnL) may ever be added as a column without a separate RBAC review.
- Filter values are user input echoed into the table caption - spec requires text rendering, no interpretation.
- Presets are user-scoped; the spec forbids cross-user preset visibility.

## Accessibility notes
- Results are a sortable table with a caption stating the active filter set in plain language; every filter is a labelled control; result count is announced on change.
- Sparklines require a text alternative or an adjacent numeric column - colour-only trend indication is rejected.
- Estimated badges carry text, not just an icon.
- Cap and error notes are associated with the table via `aria-describedby`.

## Performance notes
- Refresh <=0.2 Hz from the panel; full-universe scan returns in <=3 s per the catalogue budget.
- Table virtualised at the 200-row cap; sparkline rendering budgeted and static between refreshes.
- No client-side universe evaluation - stated as a hard constraint.

## Observability
- `scanner.filter_changed`, `scanner.preset_saved`, `scanner.result_opened`, `scanner.alert_created_from_result` analytics specified with properties.
- An event distinguishing cap-reached from zero-results so we can tune default filters.

## Definition of Done

- Estimated-metric copy reviewed and approved; catalogue checklist ticked.
- `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-104` updated on divergence.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done), >=2 sprints ahead of the consuming FE story.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-147 exchange connectivity, rate limits and clock skew
body:
## Context
E08 introduces the parts of the system most likely to fail quietly: the Bybit REST client with its error taxonomy (including rate-limit `10018`), the subscription manager with its <=10-args-per-request budget, sequence-gap detection and resubscribe, and the clock-offset measurement required by `US-MKT-009` (re-measured every 5 minutes, alarm above 500 ms drift). `SCR-147` Admin: exchange connectivity & rate limits is the Owner-facing surface where all of that becomes inspectable, and it is the screen the Owner will open first when something feels wrong.

It is RBAC-gated inside the web app (there is no separate admin app), rendered in `CMP-087` AdminLayout, and per the catalogue it includes a fan-out budget simulator ("a 5-account fan-out with brackets costs about 15 requests - 9 % of your minute budget"). E08 only needs the market-data half to be real in R0, but the screen must be designed whole so later epics slot in without redesign.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-147`: healthy, approaching limit, throttled, banned with the exchange's stated recovery time, WS disconnected, resubscribe storm, clock-skew warning and alarm, historical usage view, and a data-unavailable state (our own metrics pipeline down).
- Per-endpoint-class table (REST order, REST query, public WS, private WS) with limit, current usage, window and headroom as numbers with units, per-account rows labelled by account.
- Subscription inspector for E08: active topics per connection, args-per-request budget consumption, gap counter, last resubscribe, last snapshot re-seed per symbol.
- Clock-skew indicator: current offset, last measurement time, next measurement, alarm state at >500 ms, and the copy explaining consequences (bar boundaries, signatures).
- Force-reconnect action with confirmation, marked as audited (`connectivity.reconnect_forced`), and the request-budget change control (`connectivity.budget_changed`, audited).
- Historical usage sparkline **with a table alternative** (catalogue requirement).
- Components: `CMP-023` Progress Bar, `CMP-024` Sparkline, `CMP-036` KeyValueRow, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-087` AdminLayout, `CMP-178` SystemHealthTile, `CMP-044` ConfirmDialog, `CMP-093` AuditActionTrigger.

## Out of scope
- Private/order endpoints' real data (arrives with the OMS epics) - designed as placeholders with the layout reserved.
- The general system-health screen and maintenance mode (other epics).
- Alerting/notification routing for these conditions (observability epic) - only the on-screen state is designed.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budget consumption is legible as numbers, not just bars
  Given any endpoint class row
  When rendered
  Then limit, current usage, window and headroom appear as explicit numbers with units alongside any progress bar
  And the bar is never the only representation

Scenario: Throttled and banned are distinct and actionable (failure case)
  Given the adapter has received a 10018 rate-limit error
  When the screen renders
  Then a throttled state names the endpoint class, the observed limit and the recovery time the exchange stated
  And a banned state is visually and textually distinct from throttled, with what the operator may and may not do

Scenario: Clock drift alarm
  Given the measured offset to Bybit server time exceeds 500 ms
  When the screen renders
  Then the skew indicator is in its alarm state with the offset value, the measurement age and the stated consequences
  And a re-measure action is offered

Scenario: Force reconnect is deliberate and audited
  Given the Owner triggers Force reconnect
  Then a confirmation states exactly what will be interrupted (subscriptions dropped and re-established, brief resync on dependent panels)
  And the action is marked as written to the audit log

Scenario: Our own metrics are unavailable (edge case)
  Given the backend cannot report its rate-limit counters
  When the screen renders
  Then it shows an explicit unknown state rather than zeros
  And zeros are never shown as if they meant 'no usage'

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO, the Security engineer and accessibility review are complete
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Usage figures come from the backend's own accounting plus exchange response headers, sampled at 1 Hz; the browser never queries the exchange directly (catalogue constraint) - annotate it so no one proposes a direct call.
- The subscription inspector must be designed for realistic scale: dozens of topics across a few connections; specify grouping (by connection, then by topic type) and virtualisation threshold.
- Show the <=10 args/request subscribe budget explicitly, because it is a real constraint of the Bybit adapter and an operator needs to see when it is the bottleneck.
- Distinguish three failure origins in the UI: exchange-side (rate limit, 5xx, maintenance), network-side (disconnect), and our side (bus backpressure, bounded-queue drops from M5). Each has different operator action.

## Test plan
- Review against the `SCR-147` design sign-off acceptance checklist, item by item, recorded on the ticket.
- Walkthrough with the E08 engineering lead confirming every displayed figure maps to a metric the adapter actually exports.
- Security review of the RBAC and content exposure (below) recorded by the Security engineer.
- Screen-reader pass on the per-endpoint table and the alarm states; table-alternative for the sparkline verified.

## Security notes
- The screen is Owner-gated via `CMP-087` AdminLayout; Manager/Viewer must not see it at all, and its route must not be discoverable in navigation for those roles.
- No API key material, key ids beyond a masked label, or signed request contents may appear; account rows are labelled with the account alias, not credentials.
- Force-reconnect and budget-change are audited actions and must use `CMP-093` AuditActionTrigger with typed/explicit confirmation per the admin pattern.
- Raw exchange error bodies are mapped to error classes before display, preventing incidental leakage of request metadata.

## Accessibility notes
- Per the catalogue: a per-endpoint-class table with limit, usage, window and headroom as numbers with units; per-account rows labelled with the account.
- Alarm states use `role="alert"` once on entry, not repeatedly; degraded states use `role="status"`.
- The historical sparkline has an equivalent data table toggle (mandated by the catalogue checklist).
- Progress bars expose `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext` with the real numbers and units.

## Performance notes
- Sampling at 1 Hz; the spec forbids animated bars and mandates that the table updates in place without re-mounting rows.
- Subscription inspector virtualised beyond the stated row threshold.
- Historical view fetches on demand, not on every sample tick.

## Observability
- `connectivity.panel_viewed` (analytics); `connectivity.budget_changed` and `connectivity.reconnect_forced` (audited) - specified with their payloads.
