title: Append-only hash-chained audit writer (M19) and audit query API
body:
## Context
Module **M19** is the append-only, tamper-evident audit log that every later Epic writes into: key rotation (E27), order submission and fan-out (E29/E34), rule arming (E35/E37), kill-switch (E39), admin actions (E42). `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1 specifies it precisely — `audit_log` with `prev_hash`/`entry_hash` forming a SHA-256 chain computed **by a database trigger, never by the application**, `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_log FROM cv_app, cv_ro`, a daily head-hash checkpoint written to `audit_checkpoints` and to an off-box file so tail truncation is detectable. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` exposes `GET /admin/audit`, `POST /admin/audit/verify` and `POST /admin/audit/export`.

Building this early, in the same sprint as the first auth flows, is deliberate: the auth stories themselves must emit audit entries (failed sign-in with source IP per US-ONB-001, invite reuse per US-ONB-006, high-severity TOTP reset per US-ONB-010), so the writer must exist before them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration for `audit_log` exactly per `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1: all columns, the `au_action_fmt` CHECK, indexes `ix_audit_time`, `ix_audit_actor`, `ix_audit_action`, `ix_audit_object`, `ix_audit_sev`, the `audit_chain()` trigger function and its BEFORE INSERT trigger, and the `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` grants; plus `audit_checkpoints`.
- `audit.emit(action, *, actor, object, outcome, severity, before_state, after_state, reason, request_id, env)` API in `services/api/audit/`, with a typed action registry so `action` strings are not free-form at call sites.
- **Redaction layer**: `before_state`/`after_state` diffs pass through a redactor that removes any field classified SECRET (password hashes, TOTP seeds, recovery codes, refresh tokens, invite tokens, API keys) and hashes PII where the value itself is not needed.
- Durable buffering: writes are asynchronous but survive a Postgres outage via the bounded on-disk WAL described in `20-architecture.md` §F8, replayed on recovery in original order so the chain stays monotonic.
- Endpoints `GET /admin/audit` (filter by actor, action, object, severity, time range; cursor pagination), `POST /admin/audit/verify` (walk and verify the chain, return first divergence if any), `POST /admin/audit/export` (NDJSON export with the head hash attached).
- Daily checkpoint job writing the head hash to `audit_checkpoints` and to a file outside the database volume.

## Out of scope
- The admin audit-browser UI — **E42** (this ticket ships the API it calls).
- Emitting audit events from trading, rules or key management — those Epics call `audit.emit` themselves.
- Long-term archival to Parquet/cold storage — **E16**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The chain is computed by the database
  Given an application that inserts an audit row without supplying prev_hash or entry_hash
  When the insert commits
  Then the trigger has populated both, prev_hash equals the previous row's entry_hash, and the genesis row's prev_hash is 64 zeros

Scenario: The application role cannot rewrite history
  Given the cv_app database role
  When it attempts UPDATE or DELETE on audit_log
  Then Postgres refuses with insufficient privilege and the attempt itself is logged

Scenario: Tampering is detected and located
  Given a row is altered by a superuser out of band
  When POST /admin/audit/verify runs
  Then it reports the chain as broken and returns the id of the first divergent entry

Scenario: Secrets never reach the log
  Given an audit emission whose before_state contains a password hash and a TOTP seed
  When the entry is written
  Then those fields are absent from the stored JSON and a redaction marker is present in their place

Scenario: Postgres outage does not lose events
  Given Postgres is unavailable for 60 seconds while 500 auditable actions occur
  When it returns
  Then all 500 entries appear in original order with an intact chain and no duplicates

Scenario: Non-owner cannot read the audit log
  Given a manager session
  When it calls GET /admin/audit
  Then the request is denied with 403 and the denial is itself audited
```

## Technical notes / design
The canonical serialisation hashed by `audit_chain()` is fixed in the migration (sorted keys, explicit null handling, UTC timestamps at microsecond precision) and must never change without a documented chain-break checkpoint. Inserts are serialised through a single writer task to keep the chain well-ordered under concurrency — the trigger's `SELECT ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1` would otherwise race; the writer holds an advisory lock for the duration of the insert. `verify` streams in batches so it does not load the table into memory.

## Test plan
Unit tests for the redactor (property-based over the SECRET field registry) and the action registry; integration tests for chain continuity under 1000 concurrent emissions, out-of-band tamper detection, grant enforcement, WAL replay after a simulated Postgres outage, and the checkpoint job; contract tests for the three endpoints against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; a chaos test that kills the process mid-buffer and asserts no loss and no duplication.

## Security notes
This is a core control for non-repudiation. Threats: tamper (mitigated by chain plus revoked grants plus off-box checkpoint), truncation (checkpoint), secret leakage into `before_state`/`after_state` (redactor with a fail-closed default — unknown fields in a SECRET-classified object are dropped, not passed), log injection via crafted `object_label` (stored as data, rendered escaped), and denial-of-service by flooding (bounded WAL with a drop-oldest-plus-alarm policy, never dropping silently). Security engineer review is mandatory before merge.

## Accessibility notes
No UI here; the consuming screen is E42's. The API returns machine-readable `severity` and `reason` fields so E42 can render status without relying on colour alone, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
Budget: `audit.emit` returns in < 1 ms at the call site (enqueue only); sustained write throughput ≥ 2000 entries/s; `GET /admin/audit` p99 < 300 ms for a 30-day window on the indexed filters; `verify` processes ≥ 50k rows/s. Measured against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and recorded on the ticket.

## Observability
Metrics `audit_entries_written_total{action,severity}`, `audit_buffer_depth`, `audit_write_errors_total`, `audit_chain_verified` (gauge, set by the daily job), `audit_checkpoint_age_seconds`. Alerts: chain verification failure (critical), buffer depth above threshold, checkpoint older than 26 h.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2, plus: `21-database-schema.md` and `22-api-openapi.yaml` match the implementation, Security engineer sign-off comment present, perf numbers recorded, QA verification of the tamper-detection scenario recorded.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-T01**.

## Branch
`feat/e09-audit-writer`

## References
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1, §2 (grants); `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/admin/audit`, `/admin/audit/verify`, `/admin/audit/export`; `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10, failure mode F8; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/20-architecture.md
2. docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `services/api/auth/`
- `services/api/accounts/`
- `services/api/secrets/`
- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what's listed in References.

**Commands**
- `ruff check services/api`
- `mypy --strict services/api`
- `pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e09-audit-writer`
- PR title: "E09-T02: Append-only hash-chained audit writer (M19) and audit query API"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/security @CandleViewer/backend
- Labels: type/feature, area/auth-rbac, priority/p0, security, qa

**Done means**
- All Gherkin scenarios in this ticket pass as automated tests (or are recorded as a manual QA step with a linked follow-up automation ticket).
- Local gate green: lint, typecheck, unit tests for every touched package (AGENTS.md §4).
- Coverage threshold for the touched package is met (frontend >=80% per DoD unless the ticket states otherwise; backend --cov-fail-under=85 per AGENTS.md §4).
- PR uses the filled template, links `Closes #<issue>`, and is merged only via the merge queue.

**Do NOT**
- The admin audit-browser UI — **E42** (this ticket ships the API it calls).
- Emitting audit events from trading, rules or key management — those Epics call `audit.emit` themselves.
- Long-term archival to Parquet/cold storage — **E16**.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

title: STRIDE threat model for authentication, sessions, 2FA, RBAC and audit
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 requires a STRIDE model per epic, re-reviewed when the epic enters design, and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes the kickoff a DoR item that is default-on for any epic touching auth. §5.6 "Area 6 — Authentication & RBAC (A-03, A-04)" already lists threats **U1–U10**, but that table was written at programme level against an intended design; E09 now has a concrete design (ADR-0010: Argon2id + mandatory TOTP, opaque server-side sessions in Postgres, one central `authorize()`/`ScopeResolver`, hash-chained append-only audit) with concrete data flows, and the model must be re-derived against what is actually being built.

This epic is also where three assets with the highest classification in the programme live: **A-03 credentials (SECRET)**, **A-04 session/refresh tokens (SECRET)**, and the audit log that every other epic's non-repudiation depends on. A modelling miss here is not contained to E09 — E27 (key vault), E39 (kill switch), E42 (admin) and E44 (live enablement) all inherit its controls.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Data-flow diagram** (mermaid, committed with the model) with trust boundaries drawn explicitly: browser ↔ Tailscale ↔ API gateway; gateway ↔ **M18 Auth/RBAC**; M18 ↔ Postgres (`users`, `sessions`, `sessions_rotation`, `mfa_methods`, `mfa_challenges`, `recovery_codes`); M18 ↔ **M19 Audit** (`audit_log`, `audit_checkpoints`); WS gateway ↔ M18 for the `auth` → `auth_ok` handshake and mid-connection revocation; the offline break-glass CLI ↔ host filesystem + KEK; the invite flow's out-of-band link delivery.
- **STRIDE analysis per element and per flow**, in the `04-security-program.md` §5 table format (`T` id, category, threat, likelihood, impact, risk, mitigating SR ids, residual risk), re-deriving and extending U1–U10 with at minimum:
  - **Spoofing** — credential stuffing (U1); phishing a manager's password (U2); session-token theft via XSS or logs (U5); session fixation if rotation is missed on any transition (U6); TOTP code replay within the skew window; an invite token guessed or replayed; the WS `auth` frame replayed onto a second socket.
  - **Tampering** — direct `UPDATE`/`DELETE` on `audit_log`; a forged `account_id` in a request body; role/permission seed drift between the OpenAPI `x-rbac` vocabulary, the DB seed and the Python enum; an Alembic migration that silently widens a grant; client-side manipulation of the step-up marker.
  - **Repudiation** — an authenticated action with no audit row; a shared login making attribution impossible (U7); audit chain gaps across a restart or a migration; clock manipulation making audit ordering untrustworthy.
  - **Information disclosure** — user enumeration via differing error bodies, status codes or timing (U8); a token in a URL, log line, metric label, error message or Sentry-style report; recovery codes persisted in the DOM or in browser history; `users.email`, `sessions.ip`, `audit_log.actor_ip` as PII in exports; a 403 that reveals the existence of a resource; Viewer-visible `build`/`git_sha` metadata.
  - **Denial of service** — lockout weaponised against a legitimate user (an attacker locking the owner out deliberately); Argon2id's ≥100 ms cost used as an amplification vector; session-table growth; owner total lockout on a lost TOTP device (U10).
  - **Elevation of privilege** — a new endpoint shipped without a capability declaration (U3, Critical); self-service role escalation (U4); an admin API callable despite a hidden UI (D1); shared handlers exposing owner-only mutation through a self-service route (D5); a stale permission snapshot in a live session surviving a role change; account-scope bypass (O1) and cross-manager data leakage (O7) as they apply to the auth layer's `ScopeResolver`.
- **Control mapping**: every threat maps to at least one of SR-010..SR-029, SR-050, SR-051, SR-055, SR-112, SR-122 — or to a **new** requirement proposed back into `04-security-program.md`, or to an accepted risk with a dated Owner signature.
- **Verification mapping**: every mitigation names the test that proves it (`E09-Q03` matrix cell, `E09-Q02` E2E spec, a unit test, or `E09-X03`'s SAST/DAST rule). A mitigation with no named verification is itself a finding.
- **Residual-risk register update**: `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` entries added/retired.
- Model committed at `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`, reviewed with the Architect and the epic owner in a scheduled session.

## Out of scope
- Implementing controls (the E09 `T*`/`S*` tickets) or writing the detection rules (`E09-X03`).
- Abuse-case execution (`E09-X02`) and the review/drill (`E09-X04`).
- API-key vault threats (E27's own model) and OMS/fan-out threats (§5.7/§5.9, later epics) except where they consume E09's `authorize()`.
- External pen-testing (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element and flow is analysed
  Given the committed data-flow diagram
  When the STRIDE tables are checked against it
  Then every element and every cross-boundary flow has at least one row per applicable STRIDE category or a recorded "not applicable" reason
  And no element appears in the diagram without a corresponding analysis section

Scenario: Every threat has a mitigation and a named verification
  Given the completed threat table
  When each row is inspected
  Then it names a mitigating SR id (existing or newly proposed) and the specific test that verifies it
  And any row without a verification is filed as a finding with an owner and a due date

Scenario: Failure case - a Critical threat with no control
  Given threat U3, a route shipped without a capability declaration
  When the model checks the mitigation
  Then it must demonstrate that application start-up fails on an undeclared route, not merely that a review would catch it
  And if the implementation does not fail closed, the model records a Critical finding blocking R0

Scenario: Edge case - owner total lockout
  Given the owner loses the TOTP device and all recovery codes
  When the model analyses U10
  Then the break-glass path is modelled as its own trust boundary, including who can reach the host filesystem and the KEK
  And the residual risk of that path being abused is stated explicitly, not assumed away

Scenario: Model is reviewed, not just written
  Given the model document is complete
  When the review session is held
  Then the Architect and the epic owner have recorded comments
  And the risk register reflects any new or retired risk
```

## Technical notes / design
Model the design in ADR-0010 as built, not as idealised. Two areas deserve disproportionate attention because they are where this design differs from a generic web app:

1. **The single `authorize()` chokepoint** is a strength (one place to get right) and a concentration risk (one place to get wrong). Model what happens if it is bypassed, if it is called with a default-permissive argument, and if a route's declared capability is correct but its *scope* argument is not — the second-layer domain check (SR-050) exists precisely for that case and must be modelled as a distinct control, not a duplicate.
2. **The audit hash chain** is computed by a Postgres trigger with `UPDATE`/`DELETE` revoked. Model the trust placed in the database role: who can alter the trigger, who can `ALTER TABLE`, what a compromised migration could do, and how the nightly chain verifier detects each case. A chain that only detects row edits but not trigger replacement is a finding.

Use the same table shape as §5 so the model can be folded into the programme document without reformatting, and keep threat ids stable (`U*` for area 6) so cross-references from other epics keep resolving.

## Test plan
The model is a document, but it is falsifiable: for each of the top five risks, write a one-line "how we would know this control failed" statement and confirm that detection exists (a test, a metric, or an alert). Where detection does not exist, file it. The model's own review checklist is the `04-security-program.md` §5 completeness criteria.

## Security notes

No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.

Figma file `CandleViewer — E10 Shell (Hi-fi)`, all three themes (dark, light, high-contrast) and both densities (comfortable, compact):

- SCR-011 nav rail collapsed/expanded incl. badge counts and the >20-workspace scroll+search case.
- SCR-012 command palette with grouped results and the destructive-action marking.
- SCR-013 hotkey cheatsheet incl. the remapped-binding and conflict presentations and the printable variant.
- SCR-015 toast host: info/success/warning/error, stacking, overflow, reduced-motion variant.
- SCR-027 floating window frame: DEMO and LIVE, always-on-top, browser fallback.
- SCR-153 degraded, SCR-155 404, SCR-157 version mismatch (banner + blocking modal), SCR-159 offline/tailnet/backend-unreachable/GPU-unavailable, 403 (CMP-089), error-boundary fallback (CMP-091) panel-level and route-level.
- **Redlines**: spacing, sizing, token names (never raw hex), focus-ring treatment, and the exact accessible name string for every badge, chip and icon-only control.
- **Environment-signal spec**: the DEMO/LIVE treatment rendered in all three themes and in greyscale, proving the E10-D01 legibility result survives theming.

```gherkin

Scenario: Theme and density coverage
  Then every listed screen renders in dark, light and high-contrast, and in comfortable and compact density, without clipping or overlap at 1280x800

Scenario: Environment signal survives every theme
  When the DEMO and LIVE chrome is exported at saturation 0 in all three themes

Scenario: Contrast conformance
  When the contrast report is generated for the file

```

Built on E05 published libraries; variable modes drive theme and density so the six combinations are mode swaps, not duplicated frames. Design QA is performed later against the build (E10-D05); at this stage the checks are: the catalogue sign-off checklist per screen, the automated contrast report, and the detached-instance audit.

The LIVE treatment may never be reachable through a theme, density or user preference that weakens it (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §1.1 safety invariant). The blocking variant of SCR-157 must visibly list what stops working, so a user cannot mistake an incompatible client for a cosmetic warning.

title: Specify shell motion, run the a11y design review and publish handoff

## Context
Shell motion sits on top of a GPU-saturated trading surface: a careless width or layout animation on the nav rail reflows the workspace and can drop a WebGL context mid-frame (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-011 performance note). Motion must therefore be specified as a contract, not a vibe. The same pass closes the accessibility review of the hi-fi designs and produces the handoff package engineering consumes in Sprint 03.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion spec** (`docs/design/e10/motion.md`): nav-rail expand/collapse (transform-only, <=120 ms), right-rail drawer open/close, toast enter/exit/stack-shift, command-palette open/close (within one frame budget on a loaded workspace), banner appearance for SCR-153/157/159, error-boundary swap. Each entry gives property, duration, easing token and the reduced-motion substitute.
- **Reduced-motion spec**: the exact behaviour when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set or the in-app override from US-SET-007 is on — instant state change, no fade on heatmap or panels, no inertia.
- **A11y design review**: focus order per surface, keyboard-only route through the shell (skip link -> nav -> main -> right rail -> status bar), live-region strategy (polite for info, a separate `role="alert"` region for errors per CMP-212), announcement throttling for 1 Hz chips (CMP-076, CMP-208, CMP-210), reserved-key policy surfaced in the cheatsheet.
- **Handoff package**: Dev Mode links, token map, per-screen state matrix, the accessible-name string table, the analytics/audit event list per surface, and an open-questions log with named owners.
- Handoff walkthrough session with the frontend engineers who will build E10-S01..S04.

## Out of scope
- Chart-surface motion (E11) and trading-confirmation motion such as hold-to-confirm progress (E30/E39).
- Implementing any of it — this ticket produces the specification only.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every shell animation has a contract
  When the motion spec is reviewed against the hi-fi file
  Then every animated element has a property, duration, easing token and reduced-motion substitute, and no entry animates width, height, top or left on a region adjacent to a WebGL canvas

Scenario: Reduced motion is a first-class state
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then the spec defines an instant, non-animated result for every entry, and no entry degrades to "shorter duration" only

Scenario: Keyboard route is complete
  When the a11y review traces a keyboard-only path through the shell
  Then skip link, nav rail, main content, right rail and status bar are all reachable in a documented order, every icon-only control has an accessible name in the string table, and Esc returns focus to the invoking trigger for every overlay

Scenario: Handoff is accepted
  Given the walkthrough session with the implementing engineers
  Then every open question has a named owner and a due date, and the Frontend lead records acceptance on the ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Durations and easings are E05 motion tokens (`motion.drawer`, `motion.toast`), never hard-coded ms in component code. The reduced-motion substitution is specified at the token level so a single provider switch satisfies it globally rather than per component. The accessible-name string table is delivered as a JSON file engineering imports, so names cannot drift between design and build.

## Test plan
Verified later by the built implementation: the a11y audit (E10-Q03) tests the documented keyboard route verbatim, and the perf benchmark (E10-Q04) asserts the nav-rail transition causes no layout of the workspace subtree.

## Security notes
Motion must never be usable to hide or delay a safety signal: the DEMO/LIVE badge and the disconnected banner appear immediately with no entrance delay, specified explicitly.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the a11y design review: WCAG 2.2 AA focus appearance (2.4.11/2.4.13), no motion-triggered content (2.3.3), consistent help (3.2.6), and the `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 single-hotkey-layer and reserved-key rules reflected in the cheatsheet design.

## Performance notes
Every motion entry must be compositor-only (transform/opacity). Explicit budget: no shell animation may add more than 1 ms of main-thread scripting per frame while a chart is rendering.

## Observability
N/A — specification artefact.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/design/e10/motion.md` merged with a complete entry per animated element.
- [ ] Accessible-name string table merged as JSON under `docs/design/e10/`.
- [ ] A11y design review completed by the accessibility specialist with a sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handoff walkthrough held; attendance and open questions recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] CDO sign-off; Status Done by end of Sprint 02.

## Dependencies
- `E10-D03` — hi-fi frames are the subject of both the motion spec and the a11y review.

**Design-ahead waiver (recorded per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1).** The design-ahead rule wants a consuming Story to start >=2 sprints after its design ticket is Done. E10's hi-fi pack (E10-D03) and handoff (E10-D04) complete in Sprint 02 and E10-S01 starts in Sprint 03 - a one-sprint gap. The gap cannot be widened: Sprint 01 is the first sprint of the programme, so no E10 design ticket can land earlier, and E10 must complete in R0 (S03-S04) because `E10 --> E11` gates the entire R1 chart-engine train. The waiver is granted on the condition that the shell is assembled from already-signed-off E05 design-system components rather than novel visual work, which is what makes a one-sprint gap tolerable here. This waiver applies only to E10 and is not a precedent for R1+ epics, where the full two-sprint gap is enforced.

title: Define and validate the ShellPort abstraction (Electron vs browser vs Tauri)
body:
## Context
ADR-0011 (Electron vs Tauri) is the **only** ADR in the plan that is still `proposed`, with a decision deadline at the end of Sprint 03 gated on spike S1 / engine milestone M0 (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md`). The instruction to the team is explicit: "build against Electron, keep all shell-specific code behind `apps/desktop`'s `ShellPort` abstraction". That abstraction does not yet exist, and E10-T02/T03 cannot start without it or they will hard-wire Electron APIs into the renderer and make the ADR irreversible in practice.

This spike is timeboxed to **3 days** and answers: what is the minimal port surface that covers every shell responsibility listed in ADR-0011's decision criterion 5, and can a browser implementation degrade each capability honestly (US-SET-009: shell-only settings are *hidden with an explanation*, never shown disabled)?

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- Enumerate every shell responsibility from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §2.2 C3 and ADR-0011 criterion 5: window management and multi-window workspace persistence, OS-keychain bridge for the KEK (opaque handle only, SR-119), auto-update, deep links, tray, OS notifications, GPU info/flags, crash log, and Playwright-drivability.
- Draft `packages/protocol` or `apps/web/src/shell/ShellPort.ts`: a typed interface plus a `capabilities` record so the UI can ask "is `windows.float` available?" rather than sniffing for Electron.
- Prototype two implementations: `ElectronShellAdapter` (preload-backed) and `BrowserShellAdapter` (capability-false, no-op).
- Verify the preload bridge can satisfy the interface **without** a generic `invoke(channel, …)` (SR-111 forbids it) — i.e. every method is a named, typed, allowlisted channel.
- Record which capabilities a hypothetical Tauri adapter could satisfy and which would need redesign, as evidence for the ADR-0011 decision.
- Output: a short report, the interface file (production-quality, promoted), and a decision recommendation appended to ADR-0011's consequences.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the Electron main process itself (E10-T02) or window persistence (E10-T03).
- Building a Tauri adapter — Tauri is measured in E06 only; this spike records feasibility on paper.
- Any keychain implementation; the port only defines the opaque-handle signature.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The port covers every shell responsibility
  When the ShellPort interface is reviewed against ADR-0011 criterion 5 and docs/plan/20-architecture.md §2.2 C3
  Then every listed responsibility maps to exactly one named method or capability flag, with none missing and none unused

Scenario: No generic IPC escape hatch
  When the ElectronShellAdapter and its preload counterpart are reviewed
  Then no method accepts a caller-supplied channel name, and every channel is a compile-time constant validated on both sides, satisfying SR-111

Scenario: Browser degradation is honest
  Given the BrowserShellAdapter
  When the UI queries capabilities
  Then unavailable capabilities report false with a human-readable reason string, enabling the "hidden with an explanation" behaviour of US-SET-009 rather than a disabled control

Scenario: Timebox is respected
  Given the 3-day timebox expires
  Then whatever is known is written up and a decision recommendation is recorded, rather than the spike being extended silently
```

## Technical notes / design
Sketch:

```ts
export interface ShellCapabilities {
  floatingWindows: boolean; tray: boolean; autoUpdate: boolean;
  keychain: boolean; osNotifications: boolean; gpuInfo: boolean;
  reason?: Partial<Record<keyof Omit<ShellCapabilities,'reason'>, string>>;
}
export interface ShellPort {
  readonly capabilities: ShellCapabilities;
  windows: { float(paneId: string, route: string): Promise<void>;
             redock(windowId: string): Promise<void>;
             saveState(state: WindowState[]): Promise<void>;
             restoreState(): Promise<WindowState[]>; };
  tray:    { setStatus(s: 'ok'|'warn'|'error'): void };
  updates: { check(): Promise<UpdateStatus>; apply(): Promise<void> };
  keychain:{ getKekHandle(): Promise<string> };   // opaque handle only, never key material (SR-119)
  crashLog:{ append(entry: CrashEntry): Promise<void> };
  gpu:     { info(): Promise<GpuInfo> };
}
```
The renderer imports only this interface; `apps/desktop` supplies the Electron implementation through the preload `contextBridge`. An `import-linter` contract (E02) forbids `electron` imports anywhere under `apps/web`.

## Test plan
Not production-shippable except the interface file and the two adapters, which are promoted and then carry normal Task DoD: unit tests for capability reporting, a type-level test that the preload surface and the interface stay in sync, and an import-linter contract test asserting `apps/web` never imports `electron`.

## Security notes
Directly implements SR-111 (fixed, typed, allowlisted preload API) and SR-119 (no key material and no exchange contact from renderer or main). The `keychain.getKekHandle` signature returns an opaque handle deliberately so that a renderer compromise (STRIDE E1/E2, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9) yields no usable secret.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The capability-reason strings feed a11y-relevant explanatory copy consumed by US-SET-009.

## Performance notes
N/A for the port itself; the `gpu.info()` result feeds the E06 GPU flags used by E10-T02 and the degraded-2d fallback decision.

## Observability
The report records which capabilities need telemetry (`shell.gpu_unavailable`, `shell.window_restored`) so E10-T03 emits them.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Questions answered with recorded evidence (interface file, two adapters, capability matrix).
- [ ] Recommendation appended to `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md` consequences section.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets confirmed or filed (E10-T02, E10-T03 scope adjusted if needed).

## Branch

title: Wireframes: bar-mode selection, parameter entry and rebuild flow
body:
## Context
Before any hi-fi pixels are drawn, E12 needs an agreed **flow skeleton**: how a trader gets from a time chart to a 1 500-contract volume chart, what happens to the view while the series rebuilds, what happens to drawings and indicators, and how they get back. `US-CHART-005` demands that a timeframe switch "reuses cached bars and preserves the visible time window centre" with "no flash of empty chart"; `US-CHART-004` demands that a parameter change "rebuilds from stored prints with a progress indicator and drawings re-anchor by timestamp"; the E12 epic scope in `30-release-roadmap.md` §5 explicitly includes "symbol + timeframe switching without a full engine teardown". Those are flow requirements, and flows are cheapest to get wrong in wireframe.

This ticket produces low-fidelity wireframes and flow diagrams for the whole bar-mode surface — `SCR-042` (interval / bar-mode menu), `SCR-041` (quick-switcher), the relevant part of `SCR-031` (chart settings General tab, which already sketches Volume/Tick/Range/Renko fields), and the in-canvas states on `SCR-030` (forming bar, partial history, rebuilding, LOD aggregation) plus the terminal states `SCR-047` (empty/no data) and `SCR-048` (error).

The wireframes are the artefact the Architect reviews for feasibility against `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 (data model), §3.6 (LOD and decimation) and §9 (wire→GPU data flow), so that a flow the engine cannot serve is killed here rather than after it has been rendered at hi-fi.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Wireframe set covering: `SCR-042` menu (grouped time ladder + non-time bar modes with inline `param` fields and the "edit favourites" row defining the `1..9` hotkey ladder), `SCR-041` quick-switcher (symbol + interval in one overlay), `SCR-031` General tab bar-mode block, `SCR-030` in-canvas states, `SCR-047`, `SCR-048`.
- Flow diagrams (to be merged into `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` as mermaid) for: **F-BAR-1** switch time interval (cache hit → cache miss → progressive backfill); **F-BAR-2** switch to a non-time bar mode and enter its parameter; **F-BAR-3** change a parameter on an existing non-time series (rebuild, progress, cancel, revert); **F-BAR-4** switch chart type (candle → Heikin-Ashi → baseline) with the `US-CHART-002` "unsupported combination" branch where Heikin-Ashi is requested together with footprint; **F-BAR-5** insufficient recorded history (partial-history marker → SCR-047 when the whole window is unrecorded).
- A **state matrix** for the chart price area listing every E12 state (cache-loading, progressive-backfill, streaming, forming-bar, closed-bar, rebuilding, partial-history, LOD-aggregated, empty, error) against how it is signalled visually, in text, and to a screen reader, with the precedence order recommended by E12-D01.
- Annotated wireframes marking which existing components are reused (`CMP-041 Menu`, `CMP-048 Combobox`, `CMP-069 InfoPanel`, `CMP-213 FuzzyList`, `CMP-219 SymbolPicker`, `CMP-220 IntervalPicker`, `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle`, `CMP-226 BarCountdown`, `CMP-026 EmptyState`, `CMP-027 ErrorState`, `CMP-029 Skeleton-Chart`) and which behaviours are new and therefore need a design-system entry in E12-D09.
- Architect feasibility review comment recorded on this ticket, referencing `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3, §3.6 and §9.

## Out of scope
- Visual design, typography, colour and token application — E12-D03..E12-D08.
- Footprint, profile, CVD and indicator panes (E13, E18, E19, E23).
- Drawing re-anchoring mechanics beyond stating the requirement in F-BAR-3 (E14 owns the tools).
- Replay-specific bar behaviour (E26) and multi-chart propagation (SCR-049, owned by the layouts epic).
- Any Android or non-web surface.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E12 surface has a wireframe and a flow
  Given the wireframe set is submitted for review
  When it is checked against 14-screens-catalogue.md
  Then SCR-030 (E12 states), SCR-031 (General tab bar block), SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-047 and SCR-048 each have at least one wireframe
  And flows F-BAR-1 through F-BAR-5 each have a mermaid diagram ready to merge into 13-user-flows.md

Scenario: The state matrix is complete and ordered
  Given the state matrix is reviewed
  When two states can co-occur, for example partial history and rebuilding
  Then the matrix states which one wins and what the other degrades to
  And no state is signalled by colour alone in any row

Scenario: A flow the engine cannot serve is rejected (edge)
  Given a wireframe implies that changing the Renko brick size repaints instantly with no intermediate state
  When the Architect reviews it against 26-chart-engine-design.md and the US-CHART-003 NFR of 10 s per 1 M prints
  Then the flow is revised to include an explicit progress and cancel path
  And the rejected variant is recorded in the ticket rather than silently dropped

Scenario: Cancelling a rebuild is a first-class path (failure)
  Given F-BAR-3 is walked with a user who cancels a rebuild at 40 percent
  When the flow is inspected
  Then it specifies exactly what the chart shows afterwards, namely the previous series restored with its previous parameter, not an empty chart
  And the parameter field is restored to its previous value with an explanation

Scenario: Unsupported combination is designed, not error-handled by accident
  Given a user selects Heikin-Ashi while footprint cells are enabled
  When F-BAR-4 is inspected
  Then the flow shows an explanatory message naming why a real-price bar type is required and offering to switch back, per US-CHART-002
  And it does not silently disable footprint
```

## Technical notes / design
- Wireframes are **greyscale and token-free** on purpose; any decision that needs colour to be understood is a finding for E12-D01's vocabulary, not a wireframe decision.
- Model SCR-042 as a real menu with grouped items (time / tick / volume / range / delta / Renko / P&F) per its a11y note, with the `param` field **inside** the group, so mode and parameter are chosen in one gesture rather than two dialogs.
- The parameter field's unit label must come straight from the `/market/bars` `bar_type`/`param` table in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (trades, base-asset volume, ticks, signed volume, ticks or `atr:14`, `box:reversal`) so design and API never disagree about units.
- "No full engine teardown" implies the wireframe for a mode switch keeps the axes, drawings layer and toolbar mounted and swaps only the series; show that explicitly so engineering reads it as a requirement, not an aesthetic.
- The LOD/aggregation indicator required by `US-CHART-001` ("the aggregation level is indicated") is wireframed as persistent chrome, not a transient toast — it is a statement about what the user is looking at.
- Sub-minute intervals (1 s, 5 s, 15 s, 30 s) and custom intervals (e.g. `7m`) share one entry affordance; wireframe the validation message position for "Values below one tick / interval not allowed" style errors.

## Test plan
- Design walkthrough of each flow with the Owner and one QA/SDET, recorded in the ticket, checking that each branch has a designed destination (no dead ends).
- Cross-check every wireframed control against `15-component-catalogue.md`; any control with no CMP entry is listed as a new-component candidate for E12-D09.
- Cross-check every data element against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 so nothing is drawn that no endpoint or topic can supply.
- Keyboard walkthrough on paper: every flow must be completable without a pointer, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Architect sign-off comment for engine feasibility.

## Security notes
- No secrets, keys or account identifiers appear in any wireframe; symbol and market data only.
- RBAC is reflected in the wireframes: the `Record this symbol` action on SCR-041/SCR-047 is owner-only, and the manager/viewer variant shows explanatory copy instead of a CTA, per the catalogue.
- No wireframe may imply that an order can be placed from the bar-mode surface; chart trading is armed separately and belongs to another epic.

## Accessibility notes
- Every flow is drawn with an explicit keyboard path, including opening SCR-042 (via the toolbar button and via the `1..9` interval hotkeys), moving between the bar-mode groups, and reaching the `param` field.
- The state matrix must record, per state, the screen-reader expression (accessible name text, polite live-region message, or a row in the SCR-045 data table alternative).
- Focus behaviour is specified for the rebuild flow: where focus goes when a rebuild starts, and that it is not stolen when the rebuild completes.
- Grouped menu semantics (`role="menu"` with groups) per CMP-220's contract are annotated on the wireframe.

## Performance notes
- Wireframes annotate the budgets they must respect: interval switch ≤200 ms from cache (`US-CHART-005`), first paint of an uncached interval ≤600 ms with progressive backfill (SCR-042), chart-type switch ≤100 ms client-side with no refetch (`US-CHART-002`), rebuild of 1 M prints ≤10 s and cancellable (`US-CHART-003`, `US-CHART-004`).
- The "no flash of empty chart" requirement is annotated as a designed behaviour: the previous frame remains visible until the first new data arrives.

## Observability
- Each flow annotates the analytics event it should emit: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed`, `chart.symbol_changed` with `{source}`, `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason}`, `chart.error_shown` with `{code, correlationId}`.
- F-BAR-3 annotates a rebuild start/complete/cancel event pair so rebuild duration is measurable against the 10 s budget in production.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Wireframe set and flow diagrams reviewed by the CDO, the Architect (feasibility) and a11y design lead; review comments resolved.
- Flow diagrams merged into `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`; the state matrix merged into the `SCR-030` entry of `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- New-component candidates listed and linked to E12-D09.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done.** E12-D03..E12-D08 may not leave Ready until this ticket is Done.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D01 (bar-mode vocabulary and state precedence).
- Informed by E06 (chart-engine spike & ADR) for what the renderer can actually do; informed by E11 (chart engine core) for the pane/axis chassis the wireframes assume stays mounted.
- Feeds E12-D03, E12-D04, E12-D05, E12-D06, E12-D07, E12-D08, E12-D09.

## Branch
`design/e12-bar-mode-wireframes` — wireframes, flow diagrams and the doc updates to `13-user-flows.md` / `14-screens-catalogue.md`.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §5 — US-CHART-002..005, US-CHART-010
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-047, SCR-048
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-041, CMP-048, CMP-069, CMP-181, CMP-213, CMP-219, CMP-220, CMP-222, CMP-226, CMP-026, CMP-027, CMP-029

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-042 interval & bar-mode menu with parameter entry
body:
## Context
`SCR-042` is the single control surface through which every bar type in the product is chosen. It carries the full time ladder (1 s, 5 s, 15 s, 30 s, 1 m, 3 m, 5 m, 15 m, 30 m, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 6 h, 12 h, 1 d, 1 w) **plus** Volume, Tick, Range, Renko and Point & Figure modes with inline parameter fields, **plus** the "edit favourites" row that defines the `1..9` hotkey ladder used from the chart. It is referenced by `US-CHART-002`, `US-CHART-004`, `US-CHART-005` and `US-FP-004`.

The catalogue already fixes the hard parts: bar modes must be a separately labelled group with a one-line description each (because they change the meaning of the x-axis), intervals unavailable for the symbol's recorded depth are greyed with "Needs recorded ticks", and the design sign-off checklist requires all bar modes drawn with their parameter inputs, favourites/pinned intervals, custom-interval validation messaging, and an explicit statement of which non-time modes require recorded tick history.

This ticket turns the E12-D02 wireframe into the signed-off hi-fi spec that the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories build against, at least two sprints ahead of them per the design-ahead rule in `00-planning-brief.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi Figma frames for `SCR-042` in both density modes (comfortable/compact per `16-design-system-brief.md`) and both themes: default (time ladder), bar-modes group expanded, each of the five non-time modes with its `param` field populated, favourites-editing mode, and the greyed "Needs recorded ticks" state.
- Per-mode specification table: user-facing label, one-line description, `param` field type, unit suffix, default value, min/max, and the validation message — units and semantics taken verbatim from the `/market/bars` `bar_type`/`param` table in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`time` interval string, `tick` trades/bar, `volume` base-asset volume/bar, `range` high-low in ticks, `delta` absolute signed volume, `renko` ticks or `atr:14`, `pnf` `box:reversal`).
- Custom-interval entry design (`US-CHART-005` scenario "Custom interval": entering `7m` aggregates from 1 m data and is added to the recent list) including the recent-intervals region and its overflow rule.
- Favourites editor design defining the `1..9` hotkey ladder, including how a slot is reassigned and how the assigned digit is displayed (`CMP-022 Kbd`).
- Validation and error specimens: value below one tick, Renko brick ≤ 0, range < 1 tick, volume below min lot, P&F reversal malformed — copy written for each, per `SCR-031`'s existing validation wording ("Values below one tick are not allowed.").
- Composition spec naming the reused components — `CMP-041 Menu`, `CMP-069 InfoPanel`, `CMP-220 IntervalPicker`, `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle`, `CMP-008 NumericStepperInput` — and any new variant handed to E12-D09.
- Redlines: spacing, type ramp, token names (no raw hex), focus rings, hit targets, and the popover anchoring/placement rules against the chart toolbar.

## Out of scope
- The quick-switcher overlay `SCR-041` (E12-D04) and the chart settings dialog `SCR-031` (E12-D05).
- The in-canvas rendering of the resulting series (E12-D06, E12-D07) and its failure states (E12-D08).
- Footprint bar-mode interactions beyond the shared `US-FP-004` reference (E18).
- Motion and transition specification (E12-D10).
- Implementation, Storybook stories and tokens code (engineering stories in Sprint 05–08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every bar mode is drawn with its parameter input
  Given the hi-fi frames are submitted for CDO review
  When they are checked against the SCR-042 design sign-off acceptance checklist
  Then time, tick, volume, range, Renko and Point & Figure are each drawn as a labelled group member with a one-line description
  And each non-time mode shows its param field with the correct unit suffix and default value

Scenario: Recorded-history dependency is visible before selection, not after
  Given a symbol whose recorder has only three days of prints
  When the bar-modes group is drawn for that symbol
  Then modes requiring tick history are greyed with the text "Needs recorded ticks"
  And the reason is available as text, not only as a reduced opacity

Scenario: Custom interval validation
  Given the custom-interval field is drawn
  When an invalid value such as 0m or 3x is entered
  Then the specimen shows an inline message naming the accepted format and the allowed range
  And the message is associated with the field for assistive technology, not rendered as a detached toast

Scenario: Renko ATR parameter is representable (edge)
  Given the Renko mode param accepts either a tick count or the string atr:14 per 22-api-openapi.yaml
  When the Renko row is drawn
  Then both entry forms are designed with a single control and a stated precedence, not two conflicting fields
  And the ATR form states its source interval

Scenario: Menu overflows at narrow chart widths (failure)
  Given a chart panel docked at its minimum width
  When SCR-042 is opened
  Then the frames show the menu scrolling or repositioning within the viewport with the selected item visible
  And no group is silently truncated, per the CMP-221 overflow rule
```

## Technical notes / design
- The menu must stay a **menu**, not a form disguised as one: mode selection commits on activation, while the `param` field commits on blur or Enter with the current value echoed in the menu-button accessible name ("Interval: volume 1 500").
- Group order follows the research recommendation from E12-D01 (expected: time first, then tick, volume, range, delta, Renko, P&F) and must match the group order used by `CMP-220 IntervalPicker` so the picker and the menu never disagree.
- The one-line descriptions are the product's only chance to explain a non-time x-axis; write them as consequences ("a new bar opens every 500 trades — the x-axis is no longer evenly spaced in time") rather than definitions.
- Favourites map to `1..9`; the spec must state what happens when fewer than nine favourites exist and when a favourite is a non-time mode with a parameter (the parameter travels with the slot).
- Anchor placement: the menu opens from the interval control in `CMP-221 ChartToolbar`; specify the flip/shift behaviour when the chart panel is near a screen edge or inside a floating Electron window (`SCR-027`).
- Use `CMP-069 InfoPanel` for the "which modes need recorded ticks" explanation rather than a tooltip, so the explanation is reachable by keyboard and persists while reading.

## Test plan
- Design review against every line of the `SCR-042` design sign-off acceptance checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md`; each box ticked with evidence.
- Token audit: every colour, space and type value resolves to a `16-design-system-brief.md` token; zero raw hex values in the delivered frames.
- Contrast audit of the greyed "Needs recorded ticks" state — disabled-looking items must still meet the contrast floor for text that conveys information.
- Copy review of all six descriptions and all five validation messages by the CDO and the Owner.
- A prototype click-through of F-BAR-2 and F-BAR-3 (from E12-D02) walked keyboard-only.
- Cross-check the per-mode spec table against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and the `barType` definition in `23-ws-protocol.md` §14; any mismatch is a blocking review comment.

## Security notes
- No account, key or balance data appears on this surface; it is market-data scoped only (`x-rbac: marketdata:read`).
- The "Record this symbol" affordance is **not** part of SCR-042; if the greyed state offers a route to recording, it must link to the owner-only surface and the spec must show the non-owner variant without the action.
- Parameter values are user input that reaches a backend query string; the design must bound them (min/max, max length 24 per the API's `param` schema) so the UI cannot originate an out-of-range request.

## Accessibility notes
- `role="menu"` with real group semantics; each non-time mode group is labelled and each item carries its description in the accessible name or via `aria-describedby`.
- The menu button's accessible name always states the current interval or mode plus parameter, per `CMP-220`'s contract, and is readable without opening the popover.
- Full keyboard operation: open, arrow between groups and items, type-ahead, reach and edit the `param` field, Esc restores the previous selection without changing the chart.
- Disabled items are still focusable and announce their reason ("Needs recorded ticks"), rather than being skipped silently.
- Hit targets and focus rings meet `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the `1..9` shortcuts are documented in `SCR-013` hotkey cheatsheet and shown with `CMP-022 Kbd`.

## Performance notes
- The spec states the budgets the built menu must honour: opening ≤80 ms from a cached instrument list (SCR-041's budget applies to the shared popover machinery), interval change reusing the cached series when present, otherwise ≤600 ms first paint with progressive backfill (SCR-042 Performance).
- The design must not require re-measuring or re-laying out the whole menu on each keystroke in the `param` field.

## Observability
- Emissions specified on the frames: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed` with `{from, to, param}` (analytics), plus the rebuild start event agreed in E12-D02 when a parameter change triggers a rebuild.
- No audit-log records are produced by this surface; the spec states that explicitly so engineering does not add one.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- All frames, the per-mode spec table and the redlines published in Figma and linked from the `SCR-042` entry of `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Every checklist item in the `SCR-042` design sign-off acceptance checklist ticked with evidence.
- a11y design lead review comment resolved; token audit clean.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, at least two sprints before the consuming frontend story starts (Sprint 05).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D02 (wireframes and flows).
- Depends on the design-system foundations from the E0x design-system epic for tokens, `CMP-041 Menu` and `CMP-008 NumericStepperInput`.
- Feeds E12-D04 (shared popover behaviour), E12-D09 (design-system contribution for CMP-220/CMP-222), E12-D12 (handoff) and the Sprint 05–08 frontend stories.

## Branch
`design/e12-scr042-bar-mode-menu` — Figma links, redline exports and the `14-screens-catalogue.md` update.

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-042 (and its design sign-off acceptance checklist), SCR-031, SCR-013, SCR-027
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` — US-CHART-002, US-CHART-004, US-CHART-005, US-FP-004
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-008, CMP-022, CMP-041, CMP-069, CMP-220, CMP-221, CMP-222
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6, §14
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/research/findings/E12-bar-modes.md`


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-008, CMP-022, CMP-041, CMP-069, CMP-220, CMP-221, CMP-222, SCR-013, SCR-027, SCR-031, SCR-041, SCR-042
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench (if perf-labelled) · pnpm lint · pnpm typecheck
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e12-scr042-bar-mode-menu`
- PR title: `E12-D03: Hi-fi design: SCR-042 interval & bar-mode menu with parameter entry`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E12-D03)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/design, area/chart-engine, priority/p0, design, a11y

**Done means**
- [ ] All Acceptance criteria scenarios pass under automated test
- [ ] Coverage floor held for touched packages
- [ ] CI gates (lint, typecheck, security scan) green

**Do NOT**
- No GL calls issued from scene-graph nodes — nodes append to batches only (26-chart-engine-design.md §3.1).
- No allocation in the hot render path; anything per-frame must come from an object pool.
- Do not ship a hover-only or drag-only interaction; every affordance needs a keyboard path (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E12-D03 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.
- Move the issue's Status to `Blocked` in the project board; do not leave it silently `In Progress`.
- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Hi-fi design: price series visual language (candle, bar, line, area, HA)
body:
## Context
This is the ticket that decides what CandleViewer's charts actually *look like*. `US-CHART-001` requires candlesticks that are "legible and smooth at any zoom"; `US-CHART-002` adds OHLC bars, line, area, Heikin-Ashi and a volume column sub-pane; `CMP-181 CandleSeries` additionally lists equi-volume and delta-volume; `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle` adds hollow candles and baseline. Every one of those is drawn by the WebGL renderer built in E12's engineering stories, which means the visual language must be expressed as **geometry rules and tokens**, not as a picture — the renderer cannot consult a Figma frame at runtime.

The constraints are unusually tight. `SCR-030` budgets ≥58 fps at 2560×1440 with 100 k bars; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 defines LOD and decimation, which means at high bar counts a "candle" stops being a body-plus-wicks and becomes an aggregated mark — and `US-CHART-001` requires that the aggregation level be *indicated*. Body width, minimum wick width, the doji/zero-range case and the sub-pixel case are therefore product decisions with performance consequences, and they belong to design, made once, here.

This ticket also sets the **up/down encoding** rule. `05-accessibility-standard.md` forbids colour-only signalling, and green/red is exactly that; the spec must define the redundant channel (hollow vs filled body, or an outline-weight rule) that survives at every zoom level including LOD.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A **series visual specification** document (markdown + Figma) covering, for each type in `CMP-181`/`CMP-222` — candle, hollow candle, OHLC bar, line, area, baseline, Heikin-Ashi, equi-volume, delta-volume: geometry rules (body width as a function of bar spacing, minimum width, wick/tick width, cap style), colour token mapping (`color.candle.up/down` per `CMP-180`/`CMP-181`), and the up/down redundant non-colour encoding.
- **Density ladder**: the rendering rules at bar spacings of ≥8 px, 4–8 px, 2–4 px, 1–2 px and <1 px (LOD-aggregated), including when bodies collapse to a single column, when wicks are dropped, and the exact appearance of an aggregated mark.
- The **LOD/aggregation indicator** design required by `US-CHART-001` ("the aggregation level is indicated") — persistent chart chrome stating what the user is looking at, with its text form.
- **Forming vs closed bar** treatment, expressing the `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 rule that the last bar may carry `confirm: false` and MUST NOT be treated as closed: a designed distinction that is not colour-only and not motion-only, plus its relationship to `CMP-226 BarCountdown`.
- **Gap rule**: a gap is drawn as a gap and never interpolated (`US-CHART-011` scenario "Misaligned history"); the visual treatment of a missing window inside an otherwise live series, and how it differs from the partial-history boundary designed in E12-D08.
- **Volume column sub-pane** design (`US-CHART-002`): linked sub-pane sharing the time axis and crosshair, its own scale treatment, and its up/down encoding consistent with the price series.
- **Non-time bar visual consequences**: how range, Renko, tick, volume and delta bars differ visually from time bars (uniform widths, no wall-clock spacing, brick geometry for Renko, column geometry for P&F) and what the time axis shows when spacing is not time-linear.
- Token contributions handed to E12-D09 for the design-system: any new `color.chart.*` / `color.candle.*` entries required.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cells (`CMP-109`, `CMP-182`) and profiles (E18/E19) — this covers the price series layer only.
- Indicator overlays (`CMP-194`, E13), drawings (`CMP-191`, E14), order/position overlays (`CMP-192`).
- Axis design (`CMP-188`, `CMP-189`) and crosshair/tooltip (`CMP-190`, `CMP-197`) — owned by the E11 chart-engine-core design; this ticket only states what the series contributes to them.
- The data-table alternative `SCR-045` (E12-D07).
- Motion (E12-D10) and the empty/error states (E12-D08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every supported chart type has an implementable geometry rule
  Given the series visual specification is submitted for review
  When an engineer reads it without access to Figma
  Then each of candle, hollow candle, OHLC bar, line, area, baseline, Heikin-Ashi, equi-volume and delta-volume has a stated geometry rule as a function of bar spacing and tokenised colours
  And no rule requires a value that is not a token or a computed quantity the renderer already has

Scenario: Up and down are distinguishable without colour
  Given the up/down encoding is reviewed against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  When the specification is rendered in greyscale
  Then direction remains readable at every step of the density ladder
  And the redundant channel is stated explicitly rather than left to the implementer

Scenario: Sub-pixel bars degrade to a designed mark (edge)
  Given 100 000 bars are zoomed to fit so bar spacing falls below one pixel
  When the density ladder is inspected
  Then it specifies an aggregated mark rather than overlapping candles
  And the aggregation indicator states the aggregation level in text

Scenario: A zero-range bar is still visible (edge)
  Given a bar whose open, high, low and close are identical
  When the geometry rules are applied
  Then the specification yields a visible mark of a stated minimum height
  And it is distinguishable from a rendering artefact

Scenario: A data gap is never interpolated (failure)
  Given a series is missing a window of bars
  When the gap rule is inspected
  Then the gap is drawn as a gap with a stated treatment
  And no line, area or baseline type bridges the missing range
```

## Technical notes / design
- Express every rule as **pixels derived from bar spacing**, e.g. "body width = clamp(round(spacing × 0.7), 1, 24) px; wick width = max(1, round(bodyWidth / 6)) px", so the renderer implements arithmetic rather than taste. Exact values are set in this ticket; the formula shape is fixed here.
- Align with `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 (LOD and decimation): the design must not require per-bar detail the decimation stage has already discarded. Confirm with the Architect which quantities survive decimation (typically open/high/low/close of the aggregate plus a count) and design the aggregated mark from exactly those.
- Heikin-Ashi is a client-side transform (`US-CHART-002`); its geometry is the candle geometry, but the spec must state that HA values are derived and therefore that crosshair readouts and drawings anchor to **real** time/price, matching the story's requirement that "drawings stay anchored to real time/price".
- Equi-volume and delta-volume vary **width** by volume/delta; state the width mapping, its clamp, and what happens when a single bar's volume dwarfs the window (cap plus an indicator rather than a bar that consumes the viewport).
- Renko bricks and P&F columns have no wall-clock spacing at all; specify the time-axis label strategy for those modes (labels at brick boundaries with their timestamps, spacing non-linear) so `CMP-189 TimeAxis` has a rule rather than an accident.
- The forming-bar treatment must survive on a 1 s interval where the "forming" state is nearly always true — it cannot be visually loud.
- Keep the token surface small: prefer reusing `color.candle.up/down`, `color.chart.grid`, `color.chart.background` over introducing new tokens; every proposed new token needs a justification in E12-D09.

## Test plan
- Render the specification against **real recorded fixtures** at each step of the density ladder and attach the images to the ticket; a rule that has not been seen against real data is not signed off.
- Greyscale and colour-vision-deficiency simulation (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) of every chart type at three densities.
- Contrast measurement of body/wick/background pairs in both themes against `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Architect review for renderability against `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.1, §3.6, §4 and the memory budgets in §7.
- Review with the Owner on the reference monitor at 2560×1440 — the target resolution named in `SCR-030` — not on a designer's laptop.
- Cross-check every type against `CMP-181` and `CMP-222` prop enums; a type in the design that no component prop can express is a blocking finding.

## Security notes
- No security-sensitive data is rendered by the series layer; the spec must not introduce any affordance that places or amends an order (chart trading is a separate, armed surface).
- The specification must not encode account-derived information (e.g. position side) into the series colouring, which would leak account state into a market-data view shared in screenshots.

## Accessibility notes
- Direction (up/down) must be conveyed by at least one non-colour channel at every density; the spec states it per type.
- `CMP-181`'s DOM-mirror contract applies: the focused bar surfaces OHLCV through the mirror node with arrow-key bar-to-bar movement and `Home`/`End` jumps. This ticket defines **what text** that mirror exposes per chart type (including what Heikin-Ashi exposes — the spec must state whether HA or real OHLC is announced, and why).
- The aggregation indicator is text, not an icon alone, and is included in the chart's rolling `aria-label` summary per `CMP-180`.
- Forming-bar state is expressed in the accessible name of the focused bar, not only visually.
- Reduced-motion users must lose no information: nothing in this spec may depend on animation.

## Performance notes
- The spec is bounded by `SCR-030`'s budget: ≥58 fps at 2560×1440 with 100 k bars, ≤450 MB per chart panel, and `US-CHART-001`'s ≥55 fps at 100 k bars with ≤512 MB GPU per pane.
- Any rule that would require per-bar text, per-bar alpha blending or an extra draw call per bar is flagged and justified, or replaced; the density ladder exists precisely to keep the draw-call count flat as bar count grows.
- The chosen geometry is handed to the E12 engineering stories together with a target: no rule may increase the vertex count per bar beyond the budget agreed with the Architect in review.

## Observability
- The aggregation level shown by the indicator is also a diagnostics value surfaced in `SCR-046` (chart engine diagnostics overlay: visible bars, cell count, fps); the spec names the field so the two never disagree.
- No analytics events originate from the series layer itself; stated explicitly so engineering does not instrument per-frame.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Series visual specification merged into the repo alongside the Figma links, and referenced from `CMP-181`/`CMP-222` in `15-component-catalogue.md` and from `SCR-030`.
- Density-ladder renders against real fixtures attached to the ticket.
- Architect renderability review and a11y design lead review both resolved.
- Token additions (if any) accepted by the design-system team via E12-D09.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, ≥2 sprints before the Sprint 05 rendering stories.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D01 (vocabulary, forming/closed and aggregation language).
- Depends on E06 (chart-engine spike) evidence and E11 (chart engine core) for the pane/scale chassis; the LOD stage in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 must be understood before the aggregated mark is designed.
- Feeds E12-D07, E12-D08, E12-D09, E12-D10, E12-D11, E12-D12 and all E12 rendering stories.

## Branch
`design/e12-series-visual-language`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` — US-CHART-001, US-CHART-002, US-CHART-003, US-CHART-004, US-CHART-011
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-030, SCR-042, SCR-046
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-180, CMP-181, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-222, CMP-226
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.1, §3.3, §3.6, §4, §5, §7, §12, §13
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6 (unconfirmed bars), §3.4 (binary bars, kind 4)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.

title: UX research: how traders add, tune and manage indicators

## Context
E13 introduces three net-new surfaces (SCR-034 library, SCR-035 settings, SCR-036 object tree) and a new interaction class: live parameter tuning of a computed series over a 100k-bar chart. Before wireframes are drawn we need evidence on how the Owner and the account managers actually work with indicators today in TradingView/DeepCharts - what they add first, how often they re-tune, whether they use templates, and how they find an indicator among ~28. `docs/plan/10-personas.md` gives the personas; this ticket produces the behavioural facts the wireframes are argued from.

## Scope / Deliverables
