title: UX research: drawing, magnet and object-management mental models
body:
## Context
Drawing tools are the single most muscle-memory-bound surface in any charting product. The Owner and the account managers arrive with years of TradingView habits: `Alt+T` for a trendline, magnet snapping to OHLC, click-click for two-point tools, drag-drag for zones, `Esc` to cancel, `Ctrl+Z` to undo. E14 delivers thirteen-plus tools (US-DRAW-001..009) onto SCR-037 and SCR-036 in Sprints 06-09; every millimetre of divergence from that muscle memory is felt as a defect, and every divergence we *deliberately* keep must be justified by evidence rather than by a designer's preference.

Three things are genuinely unknown and cannot be settled from the catalogue. First, **magnet behaviour**: CMP-223 exposes `magnetMode: "off"|"weak"|"strong"`, US-DRAW-002 requires anchors to snap to nearest OHLC within a radius with the snap target highlighted - but the default mode, the radius in px, and whether the highlight is enough feedback are unresolved. Second, **precision versus speed**: US-DRAW-001 requires drag handles >=24 px, which on a dense footprint chart is a large target that may cover the very cells the user is reading. Third, **object management at scale**: US-DRAW-008 expects the object tree to be virtualised for >=500 objects, yet we do not know whether users actually curate drawings or simply accumulate them until the chart is unreadable and then delete-all.

This research runs in Sprint 02, four sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story, so that wireframes (E14-D02) and the hi-fi decks are drawn against observed behaviour rather than assumption.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3 moderated sessions, 60 minutes: the Owner plus up to 2 prospective account managers (P1/P2 personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`), each run half as a **contextual inquiry** on their current tool and half against a greyscale clickable prototype of SCR-037.
- Probe set A - **tool selection**: how the participant picks a tool today (rail click, hotkey, right-click menu); which tools they actually use weekly versus never; expected hotkeys for trendline / horizontal / fib / rectangle / measure (compare against SCR-037's `Alt+T`/`Alt+H`/`Alt+F`/`Alt+R`/`Alt+M`); whether a tool should stay active after one use or revert to cursor.
- Probe set B - **magnet & precision**: place a horizontal level at a specific swing high with magnet off, weak and strong; observe mis-snaps and corrections; establish the preferred default and whether snapping must be visible before commit (US-DRAW-002 snap-target highlight).
- Probe set C - **editing & undo**: move, clone, lock, delete; deliberate mis-drag then recovery (does the participant reach for `Ctrl+Z`, the object tree, or redraw?); expectations of what undo restores (US-DRAW-008 requires all properties restored).
- Probe set D - **accumulation**: show a chart pre-loaded with 120 drawings; observe the curation strategy; test whether "hide all" or "lock all" (US-DRAW-008) is the instinct; test the object-tree concept (SCR-036) as a management surface.
- Probe set E - **position tool**: US-DRAW-007's long/short tool drag order (entry -> stop -> target vs entry -> target -> stop), what numbers must be visible without hovering (R:R, risk USDT, reward USDT, size), and reaction to the risk-cap error state.
- Findings written to `docs/design/research/e14-drawing-mental-models.md`: ranked friction list, verbatim quotes, an observed-hotkey table versus the SCR-037 proposal, and 8-12 **adopted decisions** each phrased as a testable statement that a wireframe can satisfy or violate.
- Explicit recommendation on five open questions: (1) default magnet mode and snap radius; (2) sticky-tool versus revert-to-cursor after a completed drawing; (3) handle size versus occlusion on dense footprint charts; (4) whether cross-chart level sync (US-DRAW-009) defaults on or off; (5) the position tool's drag order and its primary read-out.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design, colour or token decisions - greyscale only; hi-fi begins at E14-D03.
- Indicator management (E13) even though it shares SCR-036; only the drawings branch of the tree is probed here.
- Chart trading order lines (CMP-192, E30-series) - visually adjacent but a different epic and a different safety model.
- Backend persistence design for `/api/v1/drawings` - engineering concern, E14 engineering chunk.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Hotkey expectations are evidenced against the catalogue
  Given all three participants have been asked to invoke each of the five primary tools without looking at the rail
  When docs/design/research/e14-drawing-mental-models.md is reviewed
  Then it contains a table of expected hotkey per participant per tool
  And every divergence from SCR-037's documented hotkeys is either adopted as an amendment proposal or recorded as a deliberate keep with a reason

Scenario: Magnet default is chosen from observation
  Given each participant has placed the same level with magnet off, weak and strong
  Then the report records mis-snap counts and correction time per mode
  And it recommends a default mode and a snap radius in pixels backed by those observations

Scenario: A participant cannot recover from a mis-drag
  Given a participant accidentally moves an existing drawing while aiming at another
  When they attempt recovery
  Then the attempted recovery path is recorded verbatim
  And if recovery failed, the failure is raised as a ranked friction item that E14-D02 must resolve in the wireframes

Scenario: Screen-reader participant path is covered
  Given at least one session is run with a screen reader and no mouse
  When the participant attempts to create a horizontal line via the keyboard-draw flow described in CMP-191
  Then the report records whether the flow was completable unaided, where it broke, and what was announced at each step

Scenario: A finding contradicts a locked document
  Given a finding contradicts SCR-037 in 14-screens-catalogue.md or an NFR in US-DRAW-001..009
  Then it is filed as an explicit amendment proposal against that document
  And no wireframe is drawn against the contradicted behaviour until the amendment is accepted or rejected
```

## Technical notes / design
The prototype is a Figma clickable greyscale flow plus a small throwaway canvas harness for the magnet probes - snapping cannot be evaluated in a static prototype because the whole question is about continuous feedback during a drag. The harness renders a static candle series at a realistic density and implements the three magnet modes only; it is explicitly throwaway code and is not promoted.

Probe D uses a seeded 120-drawing fixture generated from the same generator the engine benchmark harness (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 14, B8) uses, so the density shown to participants matches the density engineering will benchmark against.

Sessions are recorded with consent; recordings are stored on the Tailscale-only internal share and deleted after the findings doc is signed off.

## Test plan
Not an engineering deliverable; validation is methodological. Pilot the script with one internal participant before the first real session and correct leading questions. Each adopted decision must be traceable to at least two observations or one strong Owner directive, and this traceability is checked in the CDO review. The findings doc is reviewed by the Architect for anything that implies an engine capability not in `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.10.

## Security notes
No production data, no live accounts and no API keys are used in any session; the harness is fed a recorded BTCUSDT fixture. Session recordings may contain participants' own screens during contextual inquiry - participants are instructed to close broker windows first, and any incidental account identifier captured is redacted before the recording is stored. Drawing text notes (US-DRAW-006) are user-authored content that will later be sanitised before storage and render; the research must record whether participants expect to paste rich text or links, because that expectation drives the sanitisation requirement rather than the other way round.

## Accessibility notes
One full session is run keyboard-only with a screen reader, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9. The keyboard-draw flow in CMP-191 (activate tool -> `Enter` places first point at the crosshair -> arrows move -> `Enter` commits) is a hard CI gate later, so its usability must be established now, not discovered during design QA. The research also establishes what the announcement of a mode change should say, since an active drawing tool is invisible to a screen-reader user.

## Performance notes
The magnet harness must itself run at >=58 fps so that latency in the harness is not mistaken for a UX finding; frame time is logged during each probe and any session with dropped frames is annotated. Observed tolerance for snap feedback latency is captured as an input to the engine's <=1 ms picking budget (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.9).

## Observability
The analytics events already annotated on SCR-037 (`drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`) are reviewed against the observed behaviour: the research states which of them, plus any new event (e.g. `drawing.magnet_mode_changed`), would answer the questions we will have after release about tool usage and abandonment.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] 3 sessions completed (or a documented deviation approved by the CDO if a participant is unavailable), at least one keyboard-only with a screen reader.
- [ ] `docs/design/research/e14-drawing-mental-models.md` merged with ranked findings, verbatim quotes, hotkey table and 8-12 adopted decisions.
- [ ] Recommendations given on all five open questions with supporting observations.
- [ ] Amendment proposals filed against `14-screens-catalogue.md` / `11-user-stories.md` for every contradiction found.
- [ ] Findings presented at the design review; Architect has reviewed engine implications.
- [ ] Recordings redacted and retention noted.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done).

## Dependencies
- None blocking; runs in Sprint 02, four sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story.
- Uses the recorded BTCUSDT fixture produced by the data/fixtures work in E04/E16; a synthetic series is an acceptable substitute if that fixture is not yet available.

title: UX research: multi-pane workflows, sync groups and panel-docking mental models
body:
## Context
E15 delivers the surface the Owner and the account managers will spend their entire working day inside: SCR-020 is *the* application, and every other screen in the product is a panel hosted by it. Eight stories (US-LAY-001..008) introduce grid layouts, saved workspaces, cross-pane sync groups, scale linking, panel docking/floating, layout hotkeys, workspace export/import and a reduced-capability profile. Between them they touch twelve screens (SCR-011, SCR-020..029, SCR-049, SCR-150, SCR-153) and roughly thirty components. That is far too much interaction surface to design on intuition.

Three questions are genuinely open and cannot be answered from `14-screens-catalogue.md`.

**(1) How many panes do people actually work with, and how do they arrange them?** US-LAY-001 offers 1/2/3/4/6-pane presets plus custom splits; SCR-022 lists ten named presets (Scalping, Order-flow, Swing 3TF, Analyst, Fan-out review, plus five geometric grids). We do not know whether users live in one preset all day, switch presets per market session, or build one bespoke layout and never touch the gallery. The answer decides whether the preset gallery is a prominent modal or a quiet menu, and whether `Ctrl+1..9` hotkeys are the primary path.

**(2) What does "synced" mean to a trader?** US-LAY-003 exposes six independent sync axes (symbol, interval, crosshair, time range, drawings, account/group scope) across lettered groups A/B/C. Six independent booleans times three groups is a configuration space users routinely get wrong in competitor products - the classic failure is "I changed the symbol in one chart and it wrecked my other five". We need to know the expected default (all-on within a group? symbol+crosshair only?) and whether the group badge alone is sufficient to predict propagation before acting.

**(3) Is docking worth its complexity?** US-LAY-005 specifies drag-to-dock with six drop targets, floating OS windows, hide/restore and per-workspace persistence. Docking is expensive to build, expensive to make keyboard-accessible (CMP-214 mandates a full keyboard equivalent) and historically under-used. We need evidence on whether users re-dock panels regularly or arrange once and freeze.

This research runs in Sprint 02, four sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story in Sprint 06, so the wireframes (E15-D02) and every hi-fi ticket downstream are grounded in evidence rather than in a designer's preference.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Participants**: the Owner plus 4-6 comparable multi-chart traders (a mix of scalper and swing profiles, at least one on a 1280x800 laptop and at least one keyboard-dominant user), recruited per the research protocol in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`.
- **Method**: (a) 45-minute contextual interview over the participant's current terminal, screen-recorded, counting panes, recording how often layout changes and what triggers it; (b) a card-sort of the ten SCR-022 presets to establish naming and grouping; (c) a paper/Figma-prototype comprehension test of the SCR-023 sync model - shown a lettered group configuration, the participant predicts what happens when the symbol changes in one pane; (d) a docking-need probe: how the participant currently rearranges, and whether they would use a keyboard move mode.
- **Instruments**: discussion guide, consent form, sync-comprehension stimulus set (6 configurations), preset card deck, note template - all committed under `docs/design/research/e15-layouts/`.
- **Outputs** written to `docs/design/research/e15-layouts/findings.md`:
  - Recommended **default pane count and default preset** for first run of SCR-020, with evidence.
  - Recommended **default sync-axis set** per new group, and whether groups default to on or off.
  - A ranked list of the SCR-022 presets by expressed value, so the gallery can order and, if needed, cut them.
  - A go/no-go/reduce recommendation on **free-form docking** vs a simpler fixed-slot model for v1, with the cost of the mandatory keyboard equivalent stated.
  - Findings on the **workspace-switching** mental model (tabs in SCR-020 vs the CMP-073 switcher in SCR-011) - are workspaces documents or modes?
  - The **unsaved-changes expectation** (SCR-029): do users expect layout autosave, or explicit `Ctrl+S`? This directly sets a default that, if wrong, loses work.
  - A first cut of analytics events worth instrumenting (`layout.preset_applied`, `sync.group_changed`, `layout.panel_moved`, `workspace.saved`) so post-release we can check the research conclusions.
- **Open-question register** listing anything that must be resolved by prototype testing instead (feeds E15-D02's validation round).

## Out of scope
- Any visual design, token, colour or type decision - this ticket produces evidence and recommendations only; hi-fi work lives in E15-D03..D12.
- The chart panel's own internals (E11/E12/E13/E14 own those); this study treats a chart as an opaque rectangle.
- Trading-panel research (order ticket, DOM) - those belong to E30/E21.
- Quantitative A/B testing; the population is too small for statistical claims and the findings must say so.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All four research questions are answered with evidence
  Given the findings document is reviewed by the CDO and the E15 FE lead
  When each of the four questions (pane count, sync defaults, docking need, workspace model) is checked
  Then each has a stated recommendation, the evidence behind it, and a confidence level
  And any question the study could not settle is listed in the open-question register with how it will be settled

Scenario: The sync model is comprehensible before it is used
  Given six sync configurations are shown to participants as static stimuli
  When each participant predicts the effect of changing the symbol in one pane
  Then the prediction accuracy is recorded per configuration
  And any configuration predicted correctly by fewer than 4 of 6 participants is flagged as a redesign requirement for E15-D06

Scenario: A recommendation contradicts the catalogue
  Given research shows that free-form docking is not valued enough to justify its cost
  When the findings are presented
  Then a scope-change proposal is written naming the affected stories (US-LAY-005) and screens (SCR-021, SCR-027)
  And the Owner decides before E15-D02 wireframes begin, with the decision recorded in the ticket

Scenario: Keyboard-only and low-resolution users are represented
  Given the participant mix
  Then at least one participant works keyboard-dominantly and at least one on a 1280x800 display
  And their specific findings are called out separately rather than averaged away

Scenario: Recruitment falls short
  Given fewer than four external participants can be recruited within the sprint
  Then the study still runs with the Owner plus whoever is available
  And the findings document states the reduced sample prominently at the top, with the conclusions that are therefore low-confidence explicitly marked
```

## Technical notes / design
The sync-comprehension test is the highest-value instrument here, because sync errors are *silent and destructive*: a mis-predicted propagation changes what the trader is looking at without any error message, and in a trading context that is a correctness problem, not a usability nicety. Design the stimuli so that the lettered badge (per SCR-023, letter carries meaning, never colour alone) is the only cue available - if participants cannot predict from the badge, the badge needs more information, and that requirement lands in E15-D06.

For the docking probe, ask participants to *do*, not to *say* - observed rearrangement frequency over a session beats stated preference. If the observed answer is "arranges once per week", the recommendation should be to keep drag-docking but demote it below presets in the visual hierarchy, which is a cheap change now and an expensive one later.

Record pane counts against the performance budget from US-LAY-001 (>=55 fps with four active order-flow panes): if the observed working set is six-plus panes, that is a finding for E11/E15 engineering, not just for design, and it must be escalated in the sprint review.

## Test plan
(1) Pilot the discussion guide and stimulus set with one internal participant and revise before the real sessions. (2) Run sessions; two researchers present, one facilitating, one noting. (3) Two independent analysts code the transcripts and reconcile; disagreements above a stated threshold are re-examined rather than averaged. (4) Findings walkthrough with the CDO, Architect and E15 FE lead; every recommendation is challenged for feasibility before it is accepted. (5) Traceability check: every one of US-LAY-001..008 is named at least once in the findings, or explicitly recorded as not covered by this study.

## Security notes
Sessions are screen-recorded over participants' live trading terminals, which can expose account balances, positions, API-key management screens and, in the worst case, credentials typed on camera. The protocol therefore requires: explicit written consent naming what is recorded; a pre-session checklist asking the participant to close key-management and funding screens; a facilitator instruction to pause recording immediately if a secret becomes visible; storage of recordings in the private research drive with access limited to the research team; and deletion on the retention schedule in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. No recording, transcript or quote in `findings.md` may contain an account id, an API key fragment, a real position size or a participant's real name - participants are P1..P6 throughout.

## Accessibility notes
Accessibility is a research input here, not an afterthought. The keyboard-dominant participant's session specifically probes: how they would move a panel without a mouse, whether `F6`-style region cycling matches their expectation, and whether they can tell which pane is focused. The findings must state the keyboard model that E15-D04 and E15-D15 will specify, including what the mandatory keyboard equivalent for docking (CMP-214) should feel like. Sessions themselves are run accessibly - materials at >=16px, no colour-only stimuli in the sync test, and time limits relaxed on request.

## Performance notes
The study collects the empirical inputs to the E15 performance budgets: observed working pane count, observed number of simultaneously visible order-flow panels, and the display resolutions in use. These numbers are handed to E11/E15 engineering to validate the >=55 fps four-pane target from US-LAY-001 and the <=3 s four-pane restore target from US-LAY-002. If the observed working set exceeds what the budget assumes, the mismatch is raised as a risk (R2 Render performance) in the sprint review rather than absorbed silently.

## Observability
The findings propose the analytics event set for the layout domain (`layout.preset_applied`, `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.reset`, `sync.group_changed`, `workspace.saved`, `workspace.restored`) with the properties needed to verify each research conclusion post-release - for example, `layout.preset_applied{presetId}` tells us whether the preset ranking from the card sort matched reality. These are analytics-only events on user preference state, not audit events, per SCR-021's analytics note.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Discussion guide, consent form and stimulus set committed under `docs/design/research/e15-layouts/`.
- [ ] >=5 sessions run (Owner + >=4 others) or the shortfall documented at the top of the findings.
- [ ] `findings.md` merged with a recommendation and confidence level for each of the four research questions.
- [ ] Sync-comprehension results tabulated per configuration, with failures flagged as requirements for E15-D06.
- [ ] Docking go/no-go/reduce recommendation recorded, and an Owner decision captured if it proposes a scope change.
- [ ] Analytics event proposal listed and accepted by the FE lead.
- [ ] Open-question register created and linked from E15-D02.
- [ ] Recordings stored per policy; no secrets, account ids or real names in any artefact.
- [ ] Findings walkthrough held with CDO, Architect and E15 FE lead; attendance recorded.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded on the ticket (Status = Done)** - this is the gate that unblocks E15-D02, at least four sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 consuming stories.

## Dependencies
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md` for participant profiles and the research protocol.
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 16 (US-LAY-001..008) as the question source.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-011, SCR-020..029, SCR-049, SCR-153 for the surfaces under study.
- No ticket dependencies - this is the first E15 design activity.

title: Verify every CI gate with negative fixtures and give epic QA sign-off
body:
## Context
A CI gate is a control, and an untested control is an assumption. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Ã‚Â§8 forbids silently skipping QA sign-off, and R0 exit criterion 2 asserts a specific pipeline composition exists and works. This ticket is the black-box test plan for E03 as a whole: for every required check, a deliberately-broken fixture PR that **must** fail, plus a clean fixture PR that **must** pass - because a gate that fails everything is as useless as one that fails nothing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/ci-gates/PLAN.md`: the black-box plan, one row per required check from `04-security-program.md` Ã‚Â§12.3 with a positive and a negative case.
- Negative fixtures (each a scripted branch under `tests/ci-gates/fixtures/`): drifted protocol (`CI-GEN-001`); untracked generated output (`CI-GEN-002`); lint error; type error; failing unit test; coverage below floor (`CI-COV-001`); coverage baseline regression (`CI-COV-002`); missing coverage artifact (`CI-COV-003`); contract drift (`CI-CON-001`); corrupted fixture checksum (`CI-INT-002`); E2E failure; new serious axe violation (`CI-A11Y-001`); planted **synthetic dummy-prefixed** secret (SR-145); prohibited AGPL licence (`CI-SEC-002`); expired accepted risk (`CI-SEC-004`); unpinned action (`cv-unpinned-action`); Critical Trivy finding; two Alembic heads (`CI-MIG-001`); model drift (`CI-MIG-002`); unannotated destructive migration (`CI-MIG-003`); module-boundary violation (import-linter); one-approval merge attempt; direct push to `main`.
- Positive control: a clean no-op PR that must pass every applicable check, proving the gates are not failing indiscriminately.
- Execution record: each case run, with the run URL, the observed error code and PASS/FAIL of the *expectation*.
- Exploratory charter (timeboxed 4 h): "Can I get code onto `main`, or into a deployed image, without passing the gates?" - attempts include renaming a job so a required check vanishes, merging while a check is queued, editing workflows in the same PR being gated, force-push attempts, and bypassing via the release bot's allowance.
- A `ci-gates` regression job registering the highest-value negative fixtures (protocol drift, planted secret, prohibited licence, two heads) to run monthly so the gates cannot rot silently.

## Out of scope
- Load/perf (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q02 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)), chaos (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q03 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)), a11y harness validation (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q05 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)), DAST (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-X04 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)). Fixing gate defects found here (filed as Bugs against the owning task).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every required check has a proven negative case
  Given the list of required checks from 04-security-program.md Ã‚Â§12.3
  When the plan is executed
  Then each check has a fixture that made it fail with the expected error code
  And a check with no proven negative case blocks QA sign-off

Scenario: The positive control passes cleanly
  Given a no-op pull request touching one comment line
  When the pipeline runs
  Then every applicable check passes and no check fails
  And the run completes within the 15-minute budget

Scenario: The exploratory charter finds no bypass
  Given the four-hour exploratory session
  When the tester attempts each bypass technique
  Then no technique lands code on main without the required checks
  And any successful bypass is filed as a priority/p0-critical Bug

Scenario: A renamed check is detected, not silently dropped
  Given a pull request renames the "coverage-thresholds" job
  When the pipeline and branch-protection cross-check run
  Then the mismatch fails with CI-PROT-002
```

## Technical notes / design
- Fixtures are scripted (`make ci-gate-fixture <name>`) rather than long-lived branches, so they stay valid as the codebase evolves.
- Planted secrets are synthetic with an obvious dummy prefix and are asserted by SR-145's own test to not match real key patterns - never use a real or realistic credential to test a secret scanner.
- Expectation inversion is explicit: the record states "expected FAIL, observed FAIL" so a reader cannot misread a red run as a problem.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan; its own verification is the execution record plus peer review of the plan by the second QA/SDET.
- Layers exercised: all of them, black-box, from the pull-request boundary.
- Fixtures: `tests/ci-gates/fixtures/*`.
- Coverage target: N/A (no product code); the coverage *gate* is one of the subjects.

## Security notes
- The exploratory charter is effectively an abuse-case session against the SDLC controls; findings feed `E03-X01`'s STRIDE model and the deferred R1 backlog item E03-X03 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope).
- Synthetic secrets only (SR-145). No real credential may ever be committed, even to prove a scanner works - that is how scanner-testing becomes an incident.

## Accessibility notes
The execution record and plan follow the document conventions of `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the a11y gate's own negative fixture is included here and validated in depth by the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q05 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope).

## Performance notes
The positive-control run doubles as a measurement of the clean-path pipeline duration, feeding the deferred R1 backlog item E03-Q04 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)'s 15-minute budget evidence.

## Observability
Execution record committed under `tests/ci-gates/records/<date>.md`; the monthly `ci-gates` regression job posts its result to the nightly digest (the deferred R1 backlog item E03-T12 (see `E03` Â§Deferred scope)).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan merged, peer-reviewed by the second QA/SDET.
- [ ] Every required check has a recorded negative and positive result.
- [ ] Exploratory charter executed and written up; any bypass filed as P0.
- [ ] Monthly `ci-gates` regression job wired into the nightly/scheduled matrix.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario (`qa` label).
- [ ] Gate defects found are filed against the owning task and triaged before `E03` closes.

title: Run design QA and the accessibility review on the shipped observability surfaces
body:
## Context
DoD §3.2 makes design QA default-on for net-new UI and mandates an a11y pass (axe-core CI green plus a manual screen-reader spot-check). E04's own UI surface in R0 is limited — the health chrome components and the Grafana operator surface — but the design specs from E04-D01 and the API-level state vocabulary must be verified *now*, while the contracts are still cheap to change, rather than at E42 when the screens are built and the vocabulary is embedded in three places.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Design QA of the design-system contributions delivered into E05 by E04-D01: **CMP-076** ConnectionStatus, **CMP-077** ReconnectOverlay, **CMP-092** DegradedModeBanner, **CMP-178** SystemHealthTile, **CMP-207** BuildFooter, **CMP-210** HealthChips — built Storybook stories compared against the design spec for spacing, tokens, type, colour and every declared state.

- Contrast verification across dark, light and high-contrast themes for every state token used by health surfaces.
- Colour-blind and greyscale verification that no state is distinguishable by colour alone.
- Review of the alert notification text from E04-T05 as a content surface: severity is a word, no colour/emoji-only meaning.
- Grafana dashboard a11y spot-check (E04-S01): panel titles, units, non-colour-alone thresholds, colour-blind-safe palette.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given each of the six components is rendered in Storybook in every declared state and theme
When axe-core runs
Then zero violations are reported, and the run link is attached to the ticket per the a11y run-link guard

Given the ConnectionStatus component receives 60 heartbeat updates while in the degraded state
When screen-reader output is captured
Then exactly one announcement is made for the state change, not sixty

Given every health state token is rendered in dark, light and high-contrast themes
When contrast is measured
Then text meets ≥4.5:1 and non-text state indicators meet ≥3:1 in all three themes, with any failure filed as a Bug

Given a greyscale render of every state
When a reviewer who has not seen the colour version reads it
Then they can correctly name each state, because state is always a word plus a value

Given a keyboard-only user encounters the ReconnectOverlay
Then the retry control is reachable and operable, focus is not lost, and there is no dismiss affordance implying the stale data is acceptable
```

## Technical notes / design
The announcement-throttling check is the one most likely to be skipped and the one most likely to be broken: a `role="alert"` region bound to a value that updates at 1 Hz turns a screen reader into an unusable metronome, and it passes axe-core cleanly. Test it behaviourally, not statically.

Use the design-system's visual-regression baseline (E05) so token drift is caught by diff rather than by eye.

## Test plan
- Automated: axe-core across all Storybook stories in CI; visual-regression snapshots per state and theme; a unit test asserting announcement count under repeated updates.
- Manual: NVDA pass over each component; keyboard-only traversal; greyscale and colour-blind simulation review; contrast measurement with a tool, recorded per token pair.
- Evidence: run links and screenshots attached to the ticket.

## Security notes
Verify no component renders more than the first 4 characters of any key id and that no `detail` string is rendered as HTML (CMP components must not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` — SR-127). Confirm the BuildFooter exposes version/commit but no internal hostnames or paths.

## Accessibility notes
The entire ticket is the a11y pass: WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, covering perceivable (contrast, non-colour-redundancy), operable (keyboard, focus, target size), understandable (state vocabulary consistent across chips, tiles, banners and alerts) and robust (roles, names, live-region politeness levels).

## Performance notes
Confirm CMP-208/CMP-210's 1 Hz update path causes no re-render storm (the component catalogue lists a performance test for exactly this) — measure render count over 60 s of updates.

## Observability
N/A — this ticket verifies rather than instruments.

title: Write and execute the black-box test plan and alert drill for the observability baseline
body:
## Context
R0 exit criterion 10 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3) requires that *"Grafana shows ingestion rate, WS state, queue depth and API latency; a synthetic alert fires and is received"* — an assertion that must be executed and recorded by QA, not asserted by the implementer. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature, and DoD §8 forbids silently skipping QA sign-off.

The specific quality risk this ticket exists to address: observability defects are *invisible by construction*. A dashboard panel querying a typo'd metric renders an empty graph that looks like calm; an alert rule with a label matcher that matches nothing never fires and reads as "no problems". Black-box testing here must therefore be adversarial — prove each signal fires, not merely that the system looks healthy.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A written black-box test plan covering US-OBS-001, US-OBS-002, US-OBS-003, US-OBS-004, US-OBS-005, US-OBS-007, mapped scenario-by-scenario to the Gherkin in `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28 and to the epic's children.
- **Alert drill matrix**: every Page and Ticket rule from E04-T05 is *deliberately fired at least once* in staging and its runbook walked — ADR-0014's Validation section makes this a PRR item; this ticket executes the R0 subset and hands the remainder to E45/R4.
- **Negative drills**: for each rule, a near-miss series that must *not* fire (threshold minus epsilon, duration minus epsilon), proving the rule discriminates rather than merely triggering.
- Dashboard verification: each of the six dashboards opened under synthetic load; each panel confirmed to show data or be explicitly annotated "awaits module X"; no silently-empty panel accepted.
- Health-endpoint matrix: each dependency stopped in turn, asserting `/health/live`, `/health/ready` and `/admin/health` behave per E04-T04's criteria, including the slow-probe isolation case.
- Logging verification: canary secrets pushed through every logging path (app, stdlib, third-party, traceback) and confirmed absent from output; correlation id followed end to end through a request; runtime log-level override raised, scoped and confirmed self-reverting.
- Support-bundle verification: happy path, secret-detection failure path, truncation path, RBAC denial, concurrent-request rejection.
- E2E suite additions (Playwright where UI exists; API-level otherwise) for the health endpoints and the telemetry endpoint's rejection behaviours, added to the CI regression pack.
- k6 script exercising `/metrics` scrape latency at full cardinality and the frontend-telemetry endpoint at expected session load.
- QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.

## Out of scope
- Full chaos/failure drills as a release gate (US-OBS-006) — E45.
- Exploratory testing — E04-Q02.
- White-box unit/contract testing — owned by the implementing tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the black-box test plan is written
When it is reviewed against 11-user-stories.md §28
Then every Gherkin scenario of US-OBS-001..005 and US-OBS-007 maps to at least one numbered test case, and every case states its expected observable result in advance

Given every alert rule shipped in E04-T05
When the drill matrix is executed in staging
Then each rule has fired at least once, the notification was received, its runbook was walked and found executable, and the result is recorded per rule

Given a near-miss series just below each rule's threshold and duration
When it is injected
Then the rule does not fire, proving it discriminates; any rule that fires on the near-miss is filed as a Bug

Given each of the six dashboards under synthetic load
When every panel is inspected
Then no panel is silently empty: it either shows data or carries an explicit "awaits module X" annotation, and any unannotated empty panel is filed as a Bug

Given canary secrets are pushed through all four logging paths at DEBUG
When captured output is searched
Then zero canaries are found; a single hit is a priority/p0-critical Bug

Given Prometheus is stopped for 10 minutes
When the period is reviewed afterwards
Then fallback snapshot log entries exist for the window, so the gap is not invisible
```

## Technical notes / design
Drive alert drills by injecting synthetic series rather than by breaking real components where possible (faster, repeatable, and it isolates "the rule works" from "the failure is detectable") — but execute at least the Postgres-down and WS-down drills against genuinely stopped components, because synthetic injection cannot prove the *metric* reacts to the real failure. Both halves are needed: synthetic proves the rule, real proves the signal.

Record each drill with timestamps (condition injected → alert received) so the ≤60 s delivery expectation is evidenced rather than assumed.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the test plan. Layers exercised: E2E (health, telemetry endpoints), integration (compose stack with dependencies stopped), load (k6 scrape and telemetry), manual/exploratory-adjacent (drill execution and runbook walking). Fixtures: synthetic Prometheus series generator; canary-secret fixture set shared with E04-T01's unit tests; a recorded 10-minute market-data fixture for the dashboard load.

## Security notes
Canary secrets used in testing must be obviously fake and distinctively prefixed so a leak of the *test* fixture is harmless and greppable. Drills that fire security alerts (failed-login spike, audit-chain failure) must be coordinated with the Security engineer so a drill is never mistaken for a real incident — and, equally, so a real incident during a drill window is not dismissed as the drill. Record drill windows in `system_events`.

## Accessibility notes
The QA pass includes verifying that alert notification text and dashboard panels convey state without relying on colour (the deeper a11y review is E04-D02); any finding is filed as a Bug with the `a11y` label.

## Performance notes
Validate `/metrics` scrape < 50 ms at full declared cardinality and alert delivery ≤ 60 s for Page severity; record both numbers against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
Test artefacts (drill reports) are retained as release evidence per US-OBS-006's reporting principle, even though the full drill programme is E45's.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test plan written, reviewed by the QA lead and the epic owner.
- [ ] Every case executed with pass/fail recorded; failures filed as Bugs with priority.
- [ ] Alert drill matrix complete: every R0 rule fired, received and runbook-walked, with timestamps.
- [ ] Near-miss negative drills executed for every rule.
- [ ] E2E and k6 additions merged into the CI regression pack and green.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion 10 evidence package attached to the epic.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with per-scenario results.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E04-T05` (rules to drill), `E04-S01` (dashboards to verify). Exercises E04-T01..T04, T06 and S02 as the system under test.

## Branch

- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3 exit criterion 10, §4.4 quality gates

title: Instrument the latency budget end to end and add the frontend telemetry endpoint
body:
## Context
Implements **US-OBS-002** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §28): *"exchange timestamp to on-screen paint is measured per stage (ingest, internal fan-out, client render) and reported as percentiles"*, *"Given p95 exceeds 250 ms for 60 seconds, then an alert fires naming the stage that consumed the budget"*, and a compact latency indicator available in the UI. ADR-0014 §2 adds the frontend telemetry push: *"Field performance regressions in the chart engine are otherwise invisible until a user complains."* The stage allocation is fixed in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.1 (parse ≤3 ms, … fan-out ≤7 ms summing to the ≤20 ms backend-internal envelope; total tick → pixel ≤250 ms).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stage timestamping: an exchange event carries `t_exchange` (Bybit's own ts), `t_received`, `t_parsed`, `t_derived`, `t_emitted` through the internal bus, so each stage's cost is a subtraction rather than a guess. Exposed as `ingest_stage_seconds{stage}` and `ws_fanout_latency_seconds` histograms with buckets straddling the §5.1 allocations.
- Clock-offset correction: `t_exchange` is on the exchange's clock, so raw subtraction measures clock skew, not latency. Correct using the offset from `bybit_clock_drift_ms` (E08/US-MKT-009) and, until that exists, report the exchange-origin stage as `unavailable` rather than as a plausible-looking wrong number.
- `POST /api/v1/telemetry/frontend` — authenticated, strict-schema, low-rate (one aggregated payload per 10 s per session) accepting `fe_frame_time_ms` (histogram buckets, not raw samples), `fe_dropped_frames_total`, `fe_ws_decode_ms`, `fe_gpu_memory_mb`, plus `screen` and `engine_version`. Server-side rate limit and payload size cap; rejected payloads counted, never logged verbatim.
- Client-side aggregator in the web app that batches locally and drops silently when offline (telemetry must never retry-storm a degraded backend).
- Recording rules encoding the `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 budgets as SLO burn rates, so Grafana shows "is this getting worse" rather than raw numbers (ADR-0014 §8), consumed by E04-S01's dashboards and E04-T05's alerts.
- Budget-breach alert naming the offending stage: the alert annotation is computed from the per-stage histograms, so the notification says *which* stage consumed the budget, as US-OBS-002 requires.
- OpenTelemetry spans on exactly the two paths sanctioned by ADR-0014 §5: the order path (`http.request → oms.validate → oms.fanout → exchange.place_order → private_ws.fill`) and replay session start. Span scaffolding and context propagation ship here; the OMS/replay spans are attached by E29/E26 against this scaffolding.
- Data contract for the compact in-UI latency indicator (CMP-208 StatusBar's `latencyMs`, CMP-210 HealthChips) — the widget itself is E10's.

## Out of scope
- The StatusBar/HealthChips UI implementation (E10 App shell) — contract and design spec only here.
- Engine FPS benchmarking harness in CI — E06 Chart-engine spike owns the benchmark; this ticket receives its field telemetry.
- Tracing market-data hot loops — explicitly rejected by ADR-0014 §5 and confirmed by E04-K01.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Per-stage percentiles are reported
  Given market data is flowing for three symbols
  When the latency dashboards are queried
  Then p50/p95/p99 are available per stage (ingest parse, derive, fan-out, client decode, client paint) and the stages sum to the end-to-end figure within measurement tolerance

Scenario: Budget breach names the stage
  Given end-to-end p95 exceeds 250 ms for 60 s because fan-out is slow
  Then a Ticket-severity alert fires whose annotation names fan-out as the consuming stage, not merely "latency high"

Scenario: Clock skew is not mistaken for latency
  Given the exchange clock is 800 ms ahead of local time
  When the exchange-origin stage is computed
  Then the reported latency is offset-corrected, and if no offset measurement is available the stage reports unavailable rather than a negative or inflated value

Scenario: Frontend telemetry is bounded and safe
  Given a client posts a 5 MB payload, or posts 100 times per second, or posts an unknown field
  Then the request is rejected with 400 or 429, the rejection is counted, the payload is not logged verbatim, and no unbounded series is created in Prometheus

Scenario: Telemetry never harms the app
  Given the backend is unreachable
  When the client aggregator tries to push
  Then it drops the batch after one attempt, does not queue unboundedly, and no user-visible error appears
```

## Technical notes / design
Histogram-of-histograms is the correct shape for frontend data: clients send pre-bucketed counts, the server adds them into a server-side histogram. Sending raw frame samples would be both a cardinality disaster and a privacy smell. Label `screen` from a **closed enum** of route ids — never a free-form path, or one dynamic route id blows up cardinality.

Percentile arithmetic warning to reviewers: **percentiles do not sum**. The "stages sum to end-to-end" check is valid for p50-ish central tendency and for the *budget allocation* narrative, but the end-to-end p95 must be measured directly with a single correlated timestamp pair, not assembled from per-stage p95s. Implement the end-to-end measurement as a genuine paired measurement (a sampled 1-in-N event carrying its origin timestamp all the way to paint) and use the per-stage histograms for attribution only.

Measurement overhead ≤1% CPU (US-OBS-002 NFR) — the 1-in-N sampling for end-to-end pairing exists precisely to stay inside that.

Config keys: `CV_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`, `CV_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_N` (default 100), `CV_OTEL_ENABLED`, `CV_OTEL_ENDPOINT`.

## Test plan
- Unit: stage-subtraction arithmetic incl. clock-offset correction and the unavailable path; negative-duration guard; payload schema validation (unknown field, oversize, wrong types, hostile `screen` value); client aggregator batching, drop-on-offline, no unbounded queue.
- Contract: `POST /telemetry/frontend` added to `22-api-openapi.yaml` and diff-checked; recording-rule output names asserted stable (dashboards depend on them).
- Integration: synthetic feed through the full pipeline; assert measured stage latencies match injected delays within tolerance.
- Perf: instrumentation overhead measured against the E04-K01 baseline, asserted ≤1% CPU; `/metrics` scrape stays <50 ms with the added series.
- Load: k6 posting telemetry at the expected session count; assert rate limiting holds and no cardinality growth.
- Coverage ≥85% backend, ≥80% frontend aggregator.

## Security notes
ADR-0014 flags frontend telemetry as *"a (small) new endpoint with a new data flow"* mitigated by authentication, aggressive aggregation, strict schema validation and no PII. Enforce all four: session-authenticated, schema-closed (`additionalProperties: false`), rate-limited per session, and no free-form strings accepted into labels or logs. Telemetry must never carry symbol+account combinations that reveal positions to anyone who gains read access to metrics. Threat: A-17 (telemetry asset — order-intent disclosure). Reject-and-count rather than log-and-store unknown payloads.

## Accessibility notes
The latency indicator contract must supply a numeric value with an explicit unit and a state word so CMP-210 HealthChips can name it "WS latency: ok, 38 ms" — state is never colour alone (`05-accessibility-standard.md`). Updates throttled to ≤1 Hz so the `role="status"` region does not produce announcement spam (CMP-208 contract).

## Performance notes
Budgets enforced: tick → screen p95 < 100 ms / p99 < 250 ms (#3); backend-internal fan-out add-on ≤20 ms p95 (#6); WS frame decode p95 ≤4 ms; instrumentation overhead ≤1% CPU. Recording rules express these as burn rates.

## Observability
Adds `ingest_stage_seconds{stage}`, `ws_fanout_latency_seconds`, `e2e_tick_to_paint_seconds`, `fe_frame_time_ms`, `fe_dropped_frames_total`, `fe_ws_decode_ms`, `fe_gpu_memory_mb`, `telemetry_rejected_total{reason}`, plus the SLO burn-rate recording rules.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios automated.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` updated; contract test green.
- [ ] Benchmark recorded showing ≤1% CPU overhead (perf label DoD).
- [ ] Coverage gates green backend and frontend.
- [ ] Security review of the telemetry endpoint (schema closure, rate limit, no PII).
- [ ] `20-architecture.md` §12.1 frontend-metrics row reconciled with what shipped.
- [ ] Demo: dashboard showing per-stage latency under synthetic load.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E04-T03` (registry, histograms), `E04-K01` (overhead budget and hot-path API shape). Clock offset comes from E08/US-MKT-009; the unavailable path exists so this ticket is not blocked on it.

## Branch
`feat/obs-baseline-latency`; split backend instrumentation and the telemetry endpoint+client into separate PRs.

## References

title: Implement token source of truth and Style Dictionary multi-target build
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#11-handoff-spec-tokens-json--code` specifies the binding build contract: one `style-dictionary build` run produces six artefacts consumed by four distinct consumers (React app, Storybook, the WebGL chart engine, and the Electron main process). Without this build, every consumer would re-declare colours - and the WebGL engine in particular cannot read CSS custom properties inside a GL context, which is precisely why `build/engine/theme-uniforms.json` exists. This task is the single most load-bearing technical deliverable of E05.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/ui/tokens/*.tokens.json` - the authored source, exported from the Figma Foundations file (E05-D01): colour (3 themes), typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, density aliases.
- `style-dictionary.config.json` with the four platforms `css`, `ts`, `engine`, `electron` exactly as sketched in the brief.
- Custom formats `json/flat-rgba` and `json/flat` registered in `tools/style-dictionary/formats/`, with their own unit tests and a README next to the config.
- Outputs: `build/css/tokens.dark.css` (`[data-theme="dark"]`), `build/css/tokens.light.css`, `build/css/tokens.high-contrast.css`, `build/ts/tokens.ts` (typed ES6 declarations), `build/engine/theme-uniforms.json`, `build/electron/tokens.main.json`.
- npm script `pnpm --filter ui tokens:build`, wired into the package build so a stale build cannot be published.
- `tokens/CHANGELOG.md` and independent semver for the token directory.
- ESLint rule forbidding raw hex colours and raw px values in `packages/ui/src/**` (tokens source exempt).

## Out of scope
- The contrast report generation and CI gate (E05-T05, consumes this build).
- Runtime theme switching (E05-T02).
- Consuming the engine uniforms inside the WebGL renderer (E11).
- Figma authoring (E05-D01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One build, six artefacts
  Given a clean checkout
  When pnpm --filter ui tokens:build runs
  Then all six documented artefact paths exist and are non-empty
  And a second run produces byte-identical output (deterministic build)
Scenario: Theme parity
  Given the three generated CSS files
  When their custom-property name sets are compared
  Then the sets are identical; a token present in one theme and missing in another fails the build with the token name in the error
Scenario: Engine uniforms are numeric RGBA
  Given build/engine/theme-uniforms.json
  Then every chart-category token is emitted as a 4-float RGBA array in 0..1 range, with no CSS syntax and no hex strings
Scenario: Electron main JSON is flat
  Given build/electron/tokens.main.json
  Then it is a single-level key to value map parseable without any CSS or TypeScript tooling
Scenario: Hardcoded value is rejected
  Given a component committing color: #2B6CE8
  When lint runs
  Then it fails naming the file, line and the token that should have been used
Scenario: Stale build cannot ship
  Given tokens/*.tokens.json changed without re-running the build
  When CI runs
  Then the build output diff check fails
```

## Technical notes / design
Token name `category.subcategory.variant.state` -> CSS `--color-text-buy` via the standard `css` transform group; -> TS as a nested typed object so `tokens.color.text.buy` type-checks. The `engine` platform filters `category == "chart"` and converts hex/oklch to linear-ish RGBA floats; document whether values are sRGB 0..1 (chosen: sRGB 0..1, conversion to linear happens in the shader) so E11 does not guess. Theme filtering uses a `theme` attribute on each token. Determinism: sort keys, pin Style Dictionary version, no timestamps in output headers. Error codes: build fails with `TOKENS-E001` missing-theme-parity, `TOKENS-E002` unresolved alias reference, `TOKENS-E003` unknown category for the engine filter.

## Test plan
Unit (Vitest): custom format `json/flat-rgba` converts `#2B6CE8` to the expected RGBA floats; `json/flat` flattens nested input; theme-parity checker detects an intentionally removed token; alias resolver detects a dangling reference. Integration: run the real build in CI and assert all six artefacts exist, are non-empty and are byte-stable across two runs. Contract: a snapshot test of the generated `tokens.ts` public shape so an accidental rename is caught by consumers' CI. Coverage target >=85% on `tools/style-dictionary/` (build tooling treated as engine-grade).

## Security notes
Supply chain: pin Style Dictionary and its transitive deps with a lockfile; the build executes third-party code, so it runs in CI without repository write credentials. No secret may appear in a token file - add a gitleaks path rule over `packages/ui/tokens/`. Data classification: internal, non-sensitive.

## Accessibility notes
This build is the vehicle for a11y enforcement: the contrast report (E05-T05) is generated from these artefacts. Ensure `.hc` variants of buy/sell and the focus-ring token are emitted in all themes so the high-contrast theme is complete rather than partially inheriting dark.

## Performance notes
Each generated theme CSS must be <=40 KB gzipped (epic budget). The build must complete in <=10 s locally so it can run on every `pnpm dev` start without friction.

## Observability
Build emits a one-line summary (token count per category, per theme, output byte sizes) to CI logs so an unexpected token explosion is visible in PR review.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six artefacts generated and committed-or-ignored per the agreed strategy, documented in `packages/ui/README.md`.
- [ ] Unit + integration tests green; coverage threshold met.
- [ ] ESLint no-raw-value rule enabled and clean.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md#11` updated if the implemented config diverges from the sketch.
- [ ] `tokens/CHANGELOG.md` initialised at 0.1.0.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. code-owner.
- [ ] Before/after evidence shown at Sprint Review (observable-effect Task).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E05-D01` (authored Figma variables are the source), `blocked_by: E02` (pnpm workspace and `packages/ui` must exist). Blocks E05-T02, E05-T03, E05-T05, E05-T07 and all component stories.

title: Build contrast-matrix generator and CI gate over token changes
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#11` requires `build/reports/contrast-matrix.json` plus a human-readable `.md`, generated in the same build step, with CI failing a token PR if any required pair drops below its threshold (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text/chart ink, 7:1 buy/sell high-contrast). `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#54` additionally requires every heatmap ramp stop to be independently validated against the chart background. US-SET-004's NFR states 'contrast verified automatically in CI for both themes and all palettes'. Manual spot-checking cannot hold this; a generator can.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tools/contrast/` script consuming the generated token artefacts from E05-T01.
- Pair registry: an explicit declarative list of which token pairs must be validated at which threshold (text-on-surface pairs, chart-ink-on-canvas pairs, focus-ring-on-every-surface-tier, each heatmap ramp stop on `surface.canvas`, `.hc` buy/sell on their surfaces) - so a newly added token without a declared pair fails loudly rather than passing silently.
- Outputs `build/reports/contrast-matrix.json` and `.md`.
- CVD simulation check (deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia) asserting adjacent heatmap ramp stops and the buy/sell pair remain distinguishable, using the simulation method fixed in E05-D07.
- CI job gating any PR touching `packages/ui/tokens/**`, publishing the `.md` report as a PR artefact.

## Out of scope
- Runtime, user-selected custom palette validation on SCR-116 ('This combination fails contrast' warning) - that is the settings epic; this ticket ships the reusable ratio function it will call.
- Component-level axe checks (E05-T03).
- Manual CVD review (E05-D04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Failing pair blocks the PR
  Given a token change dropping color.text.secondary to 4.2:1 on surface.app
  When the CI gate runs
  Then the job fails and the report names the pair, the measured ratio and the required threshold
Scenario: Undeclared token fails loudly
  Given a new colour token with no entry in the pair registry
  Then the gate fails asking for an explicit pair declaration or an explicit exemption with a reason
Scenario: Heatmap stops validated individually
  Given a 6-stop heatmap ramp
  Then all six stops are checked against surface.canvas at the 3:1 non-text threshold, not just the extremes
Scenario: High-contrast threshold
  Given color.buy.hc and color.sell.hc in the high-contrast theme
  Then both are asserted at >= 7:1
Scenario: CVD distinguishability
  Given adjacent heatmap ramp stops under deuteranopia simulation
  Then a pair that collapses below the configured perceptual distance fails with both stop names
```

## Technical notes / design
Ratio computation per WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula; colours parsed from the generated artefacts (single source of truth - never re-parse the Figma file). Perceptual distance for the CVD check uses a CIELAB deltaE threshold documented in the script's README with the value chosen in E05-D07. Exemptions live in an `exemptions.json` requiring a `reason` and an `owner` field; the gate prints the full exemption list on every run so exemptions cannot quietly accumulate. Error codes: `A11Y-C001` below-threshold pair, `A11Y-C002` undeclared token, `A11Y-C003` CVD collapse.

## Test plan
Unit (Vitest): known-good pair (#E8EAED on #0B0E11) computes the expected ratio to 2 decimals; a known-bad pair fails; undeclared-token detection; exemption handling requires reason+owner; CVD simulation of a known deuteranopia-confusable red/green pair is detected. Integration: run the gate against the real token set in CI. Coverage >=85% on `tools/contrast/`.

## Security notes
No security surface. Note only that the report is published as a CI artefact and contains nothing sensitive.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the automated enforcement of `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 4 and 5 and is a named R0 quality gate. It must not be weakened to a warning: below-threshold pairs fail the build.

## Performance notes
Gate must run in <=30 s so it can be part of the token build rather than a separate slow job.

## Observability
`contrast-matrix.md` published per PR; the job logs pass/fail counts per threshold class and the active exemption count.

- [ ] Generator and gate implemented and wired to `packages/ui/tokens/**` path filter.
- [ ] Report artefacts produced by the same `style-dictionary build` step per the brief.
- [ ] Unit tests green; coverage met.

title: Write ADR-0016: design-token architecture and theming strategy
body:
## Context
The three-tier token model, the Style Dictionary multi-target build, the decision to express density as alias resolution rather than a parallel scale, and the decision to deliver theme colours to the WebGL engine as a separate uniforms JSON are architectural decisions with long-lived consequences for E11 (engine core) and E10 (Electron shell). `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md` requires such decisions to be recorded; without an ADR, the next engineer re-litigates them (risk R10).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0020-design-token-architecture-and-theming.md` following the existing ADR template (Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives considered / Status).
- Decisions recorded: (1) three-tier global->alias->component token model; (2) Style Dictionary with four platforms and two custom formats; (3) themes as alias re-pointing with dark canonical, light separately tuned, high-contrast as `.hc` variants; (4) density as alias-step selection, never a second scale, never structural branching; (5) WebGL theming via `theme-uniforms.json` rather than CSS custom properties; (6) Electron main gets a flat JSON so it never parses CSS or TS; (7) tokens versioned independently of the component library.
- Alternatives explicitly rejected with reasons: CSS-in-JS runtime theming (frame-budget risk, no engine path), Tailwind-config-as-token-source (no multi-consumer output), two parallel density scales (token sprawl), inverting dark to produce light (washed-out heatmap/candle colours).
- Consequences for E10 and E11 called out by name, including the CSP inline-script hash requirement from E05-T02.

## Out of scope
- ADRs for the engine (ADR-0006) or shell (ADR-0007) decisions - owned by E06.
- Re-opening the Style Dictionary choice; this ADR records it, it does not evaluate it.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
  Given the ADR template in docs/plan/27-adrs/
  When ADR-0016 is reviewed
  Then Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives and Status are all populated and Status is Accepted
Scenario: Consequences are actionable
  Then each consequence names the epic or ticket it constrains (E10 CSP hash, E11 uniform consumption)
Scenario: Alternatives are honest
  Then each rejected alternative states the specific measured or structural reason for rejection, not a preference
Scenario: Matches shipped reality
  Given the merged E05-T01 implementation
  Then the ADR describes what was actually built, and any divergence from 16-design-system-brief.md is reconciled in that brief too
```

## Technical notes / design
Cross-link from `16-design-system-brief.md` section 2 and section 11, and from `packages/ui/README.md`, so the ADR is discoverable from both the design and code entry points.

## Test plan
Review-based: Architect approval required. A docs link-check job verifies the cross-references resolve.

## Security notes
N/A (no security decision recorded here beyond referencing the CSP consequence).

## Accessibility notes
Records the high-contrast theme as a first-class token-swap rather than a filter/overlay hack, which is the architectural precondition for `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#56` conformance.

## Performance notes

title: STRIDE threat model: design-system supply chain and Storybook exposure
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` require a STRIDE threat model per epic. E05 handles no money and no secrets at runtime, which is exactly why it is easy to skip - and exactly why it is an attractive target: the design system is a build-time dependency of every frontend surface, so a compromised token build or icon pipeline executes in every developer's machine and in CI, and a leaked Storybook exposes the entire unreleased product surface.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Abuse cases: malicious dependency executing at token-build time with repo credentials; typosquatted icon package; Storybook published to an internet-reachable host; VR screenshots of unreleased trading UI leaving the network via a SaaS; a component prop rendered as HTML enabling stored XSS in a later screen; an attacker relying on a disabled button as the only control.
- Mitigations mapped to concrete tickets/controls (lockfile pinning, least-privileged CI token, gitleaks path rule over `tokens/`, Tailscale-only hosting, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` lint rule, CSP hash rather than `unsafe-inline`, explicit docs that RbacGate is an affordance).
- Residual-risk statement with the Owner's acceptance where applicable (e.g. SaaS VR tool).
- Findings recorded in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` where they represent new project risks.

## Out of scope
- Auth/RBAC threat modelling (E09 owns it).
- Exchange-boundary and OMS threat models (E08/E29).
- Pen-test (R4, E43).

title: A11y design review: cost and shape of the engine DOM-mirror layer
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 allocates the **DOM-mirror (a11y layer) sync** exactly **1 ms** of the 16.6 ms frame budget, and adds a hard rule in §4.4: desyncing the DOM-mirror from what is visually rendered is *never acceptable*. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §12 specifies what that mirror is — a visually hidden `<table>` exposing the visible window capped at 200 rows, a keyboard data cursor with `aria-live="polite"` announcements throttled to 1 per 250 ms, and a `role="application"` wrapper. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 is the governing canvas/WebGL strategy.

Every other epic treats this as settled. It is not: nobody has measured what mirroring 200 rows of a live-updating window costs on the main thread while the worker is rendering at 60 fps, nor whether 250 ms throttling is usable when a trader is arrowing across bars quickly, nor what happens to the mirror during the LOD degradation ladder (if footprint text is hidden at L2, does the mirror still expose per-cell values, and if so is the mirror now *more* informative than the canvas?).

M0 is the only point where this can be measured cheaply, before E11 builds the production layer and before **US-CHART-014** (Accessible chart data alternative, Must) and **SCR-045** (Chart data-table alternative) are designed in detail. This ticket rides the prototype to get real numbers and settle the shape.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Instrumented DOM-mirror stub added to the E06-K04 prototype scene: 200-row hidden table bound to the visible window, updated per frame, with `Performance.measure` spans so its cost lands in the §4.3 stage attribution alongside the render stages.
- Measurement: main-thread cost of mirror sync at 60 fps, for a static view, a continuous pan, and a live-update storm (20 data messages/s), in all three runtimes.
- Design decision record on **announcement throttling**: validate or revise the 250 ms / 1-per-250 ms figure (`26-…` §12) and the "<= 2 announcements per second" NFR on **US-CHART-008**, using a screen-reader walkthrough with NVDA and VoiceOver against the prototype.
- Design decision record on **mirror behaviour under LOD degradation**: what the mirror exposes at L0/L1/L2/L3, and whether parity with the canvas or informational superiority is the rule (this is a product decision with an a11y consequence, so it needs a written answer, not an implementation accident).
- Early shape for **SCR-045** (Chart data-table alternative) and **CMP-180 ChartRoot**'s focus contract: `role="application"` wrapper, `aria-label` composition, tab-entry behaviour, and the relationship between crosshair position and the table's focused row (US-CHART-014 requires bidirectional sync).
- Stories informed: **US-CHART-008**, **US-CHART-014**; screens **SCR-030**, **SCR-045**; components **CMP-180**, **CMP-225**, **CMP-227**, **CMP-032 VisuallyHidden-class utility** and the focus-ring utility used by canvas surrogates.

## Out of scope
- Building the production accessibility layer — that is E11's M8 milestone.
- Full hi-fi design of SCR-045 — only its structural shape and sync contract are settled here.
- Footprint per-cell surrogate nodes (CMP-109's cell-level `aria-label` behaviour) beyond measuring whether per-cell mirroring is affordable at all.
- Screen-reader support matrix decisions beyond NVDA + VoiceOver (the protocol in `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8 governs the full matrix later).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The 1 ms budget is validated with numbers
  Given the instrumented DOM-mirror stub running against the combined prototype scene
  When a 20 s continuous-pan run is measured in Electron on the reference machine
  Then the mirror-sync stage's p95 cost is reported and compared to the 1 ms allocation in docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3
  And if it exceeds 1 ms, a concrete mitigation (windowing depth, update coalescing, or a lower mirror cadence) is specified with its own measured cost

Scenario: Announcement cadence is usable, not just compliant
  Given a screen-reader user arrows across bars at a realistic speed
  When announcements are throttled at the candidate interval
  Then the final state is always announced (no lost last update) per 26-chart-engine-design.md §12
  And the reviewer confirms the cadence is neither flooding nor lagging, with the chosen interval recorded

Scenario: Mirror behaviour under LOD is defined, not emergent
  Given the engine has degraded footprint rendering to L2 (coloured cells, no text)
  When the mirror is inspected
  Then the specification states exactly what the mirror exposes at that level and why
  And the rule is consistent with docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.4 (the mirror never desyncs from what is rendered)

Scenario: The mirror survives the degraded-2d profile
  Given the capability probe selects the degraded-2d render profile
  When the chart renders
  Then the accessible layer is unchanged in content and behaviour, confirming a11y is not coupled to the GL path
```

## Technical notes / design
- The mirror is main-thread work by construction (the worker has no DOM), so its cost competes with React, not with GL. Measure it on the main thread's timeline, not the worker's, and report both so the combined picture is honest.
- Windowing: cap at 200 rows (`26-…` §12). Test whether a smaller window (e.g. 60 rows centred on the cursor) is materially cheaper — if it is, that is the mitigation lever.
- Update coalescing: the mirror does not need per-frame fidelity for rows the user is not on; a candidate design is "cursor row updated at interaction cadence, remaining rows at 4 Hz", which must be checked against the never-desync rule.
- Announcements: use one `aria-live="polite"` region with last-write-wins semantics, so throttling can never drop the final state.
- `role="application"` on the wrapper is deliberate (it hands keystrokes to the app rather than the screen reader's browse mode) and must be paired with a documented, discoverable escape path; verify this in the walkthrough.

## Test plan
- Measurement runs: static / pan / update-storm x 3 runtimes, >= 3 repetitions, medians of p95 reported (`06-…` §7.4).
- Manual screen-reader walkthrough per the protocol in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8, with NVDA (Windows) and VoiceOver (macOS), findings logged per scenario.
- axe-core run against the prototype page to confirm the hidden table and live region produce no violations (this is a prototype, so the bar is "no violations attributable to the mirror design", not full page conformance).
- Results feed E06-T02's report as a dedicated section.

## Security notes
N/A for data — synthetic fixtures only. One note: the hidden mirror table reproduces on-screen values into the DOM, so in the production engine it inherits whatever data classification the chart itself carries; recorded here so E11 does not treat the mirror as an invisible, unclassified surface.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the a11y review for the Epic. It closes: keyboard reachability of the canvas, the data-cursor announcement contract, the DOM-mirror windowing rule, focus-visible treatment for canvas surrogates, and the behaviour of all of the above under `prefers-reduced-motion` (momentum disabled, instant snapping — `26-…` §12), ensuring E11 inherits measured decisions rather than aspirations.

## Performance notes
Budget under test: **<= 1 ms/frame** DOM-mirror sync (`06-…` §4.3). Secondary: announcements <= 2/s (US-CHART-008 NFR), table virtualisation must keep the view >= 55 fps (US-CHART-014 NFR).

## Observability
Mirror-sync duration is added as a named stage in the harness JSON and in the SCR-046 counter vocabulary (E06-D02), so a11y cost is visible in every future benchmark rather than being invisible overhead.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Measured mirror-sync costs (3 scenarios x 3 runtimes) recorded and compared to the 1 ms budget.
- [ ] Announcement cadence decision recorded; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §12 and US-CHART-008's NFR updated if they change.
- [ ] LOD/mirror parity rule written into `26-chart-engine-design.md` §12.
- [ ] SCR-045 structural shape + CMP-180 focus contract drafted and linked.
- [ ] Screen-reader walkthrough findings logged; axe-core run attached.
- [ ] Accessibility specialist sign-off; design sign-off.
- [ ] Feeds into E06-T02 as a report section.

## Dependencies

- Blocks **E06-T02** (the report cannot conclude without the a11y cost section).

## Branch
`design/e06-a11y-dom-mirror` (spec + findings); measurement stub lives on `spike/e06-engine-m0`. PR size guidance: docs-only PR; stub code stays on the spike branch.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 (architecture), §3.4 (GL backend), §3.6 (LOD), §3.7 (SDF text), §3.8 (heatmap streaming), §13 (benchmarks B1-B10), §14 (test strategy), §15 (milestone M0), §16 (open items O1-O3)
