title: Prototype scene B: SDF text atlas and 2,500-cell footprint density (B3)
body:
## Context
Dense per-cell text is the single largest CPU-side cost in the product and the flagged engineering risk: `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 gives footprint cell text/geometry the largest slice of the frame budget (**<= 4 ms**), and `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` records CMP-184 FootprintSeries as "the highest-effort chassis piece per research — the single largest line item". No surveyed charting library renders it at all (`ADR-0002`), so this is precisely the capability the custom engine exists to provide. If it cannot be done at density, the custom-engine decision fails on its own terms.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.7 commits to a specific strategy — a runtime-generated **signed distance field** atlas (1024x1024, two-pass Felzenszwalb EDT, shelf-packed, cached in IndexedDB keyed by `(fontFamily, weight, hash(glyphSet))`), instanced glyph draws, per-cell glyph runs precomputed on data update rather than per frame, and <= 6 text draw calls per pane. It also records the alternative the spike must actually measure against: a **Canvas-2D glyph cache**. `26-…` §16 keeps the exact atlas size and glyph set open as item **O2**. This ticket closes the strategy question with numbers, not preference.

Benchmark **B3** is the gate: 2,500 visible cells with text, p95 <= 16 ms, text batching <= 2.0 ms, <= 2 text draw calls. Per §3.7's own arithmetic that is ~12,500 glyphs at 5 characters average.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype scene B on `spike/e06-engine-m0`:
  - **SDF atlas pipeline**: glyph rasterisation from the design-system font (frozen glyph set from **E06-D01**), two-pass EDT to an 8-bit single-channel SDF, shelf packing into a 1024x1024 atlas, IndexedDB caching with the documented key, and a measured generation cost (§3.7 claims ~40 ms once per font/size-class).
  - **Instanced glyph rendering**: per-instance `vec2 posPx, vec2 sizePx, vec4 uvRect, vec4 colour`; fragment shader `alpha = smoothstep(0.5 - w, 0.5 + w, sdf)` with `w = fwidth(sdf)`; optional second-threshold outline pass for legibility over saturated cells (required if E06-D01 says so).
  - **FootprintStore**-shaped data (parallel `barIndex: Uint32Array`, `priceLevel: Int32Array`, `bidVol/askVol: Float32Array`, `tradeCount: Uint16Array`, `offsets` prefix sums) per §3.3, with `upsertFootprintCells` returning affected ranges for partial `bufferSubData`.
  - **Per-cell glyph-run caching**: values formatted to strings on data update, glyph runs cached alongside the cell; format change invalidates only the run cache.
  - LOD ladder L0/L1/L2/L3 using the thresholds from **E06-D01**, including the non-colour encodings (delta glyph, imbalance outline, estimated-data hatch).
  - **Comparison arm**: the same scene rendered with a Canvas-2D glyph cache, measured identically, so the SDF choice is evidence-backed.
- Benchmark **B3** wired and run; atlas generation cost and cached-load cost (<= 5 ms from cache, per B9's secondary gate) measured.
- Answer to open item **O2**: final atlas dimensions, glyph set and size-class strategy, recorded as an update to `26-…` §16.
- Components exercised: **CMP-109 FootprintCell**, **CMP-184 FootprintSeries**.
- Stories informed: **US-CHART-001**, **US-CHART-003**, **US-CHART-008**.

## Out of scope
- Imbalance detection logic, Deep-Stats rows, stacked-imbalance semantics — order-flow *computation* is backend work (FP/DS domains, later epics); this scene renders precomputed synthetic cells.
- Cell tooltips, pick-based cell detail drawers, the CMP-109 per-cell DOM surrogate (measured structurally in **E06-D03**).
- Candles and axes (**E06-K02**) and heatmap (**E06-K04**), except as composited in the combined scene owned by **E06-T01**.
- Production-quality text layout: bidi, complex scripts, ligatures. The glyph set is numeric plus Latin labels (E06-D01), which is the real product requirement.

### Scope trim (21-point roadmap budget)
The Canvas-2D glyph-cache arm is a **single spot-check configuration** at B3 density, not a second production-grade text renderer. It exists only to answer "is the SDF atlas clearly better, clearly worse, or within noise". If the spot check lands within noise, that is recorded as a finding and the full comparison is deferred to **E11 M3** rather than extending the M0 timebox.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: B3 holds at product density
  Given 2,500 visible footprint cells each rendering two numbers at the L0 threshold set by E06-D01
  When the B3 scenario runs for 20 s in headless Chromium with 3 repetitions
  Then the median p95 frame time is <= 16 ms
  And text batching costs <= 2.0 ms per frame with <= 2 text draw calls

Scenario: SDF beats or loses to Canvas-2D on evidence
  Given both the SDF atlas arm and the Canvas-2D glyph-cache arm render the identical scene
  When both are measured under the same conditions and repetitions
  Then a comparison table reports p95 frame time, text-stage ms, draw calls and memory for each
  And 26-chart-engine-design.md §3.7's text strategy is confirmed or amended to match the winner

Scenario: Atlas generation is paid once, not per launch
  Given a cold first launch with an empty IndexedDB
  When the atlas is generated
  Then generation cost is measured and reported (target ~40 ms per font/size-class)
  And on a second launch the atlas loads from cache in <= 5 ms, keyed by (fontFamily, weight, hash(glyphSet))

Scenario: Text stays legible over saturated cells
  Given the most saturated cell background in the dark theme
  When cell numbers are rendered at the L0 size
  Then measured contrast is >= 4.5:1 per docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §5, using the outline pass if E06-D01 requires it
  And the cost of the outline pass is reported separately so its budget impact is explicit

Scenario: Degradation sheds text, not correctness
  Given pixels-per-bar falls below the L1 threshold
  When the LOD ladder degrades to L2 (coloured cells, no text)
  Then no cell disappears and no value is misrepresented — only text is withheld
  And the transition is hysteretic, with no flicker over a slow zoom

Scenario: Formatting changes do not cost a frame
  Given the number format switches from full to compact (1.2K)
  When the change is applied
  Then only the glyph-run cache is invalidated, not the cell data
  And the reformatting cost is reported and does not exceed one frame's data-mutation budget of 4 ms, spilling to subsequent frames if needed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Batching rule from §3.7: all cell text in a pane is one draw call; axis labels a second; drawing labels a third; target <= 6 text draw calls per pane per frame. B3's gate of <= 2 text draw calls applies to the footprint scene specifically.
- Precompute formatting on data update, never per frame — this is the difference between hitting and missing the 4 ms stage budget.
- The `fwidth`-based smoothstep gives crisp text at any scale; verify at DPR 1.0/1.5/2.0 since the design-system font's stem widths behave differently at fractional DPRs.
- Shelf packing must be deterministic so the atlas is reproducible; record the packing order hash in the report.
- Memory: atlas is 1024x1024x1 byte = 1 MB; report actual GPU texture memory including any driver padding.
- If the glyph count at L0 exceeds what one instanced draw can carry comfortably, chunk by fixed instance budget and report the chunk count — silently exceeding the draw-call gate is a failure, not an implementation detail.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: EDT correctness against a reference implementation on known shapes; shelf packer determinism and no-overlap invariant; glyph-run cache invalidation on format change only; `offsets` prefix-sum correctness for `FootprintStore`; LOD threshold selection at hysteresis boundaries.
- **Integration**: B3 via the harness, 3 reps, both arms (SDF and Canvas-2D); atlas cold-generate vs cached-load timing.
- **Visual**: golden images per LOD level at DPR 1.0 and 2.0, handed to E11's M3.
- **A11y-adjacent**: contrast measurement on rendered output (automated sampling of text pixels against cell background).
- Coverage: prototype exempt; any helper promoted to the harness carries >= 85 %.

## Security notes
- Font handling is the notable surface: the atlas is generated at runtime from the design-system font, so the font must be a pinned, vendored asset, not fetched from a third-party CDN (STRIDE **T**ampering, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5/§6). Record this as a constraint for E11.
- IndexedDB caching stores only glyph bitmaps keyed by a font hash — no user data, no PII; the key must not incorporate anything user-identifying.
- No network I/O during a benchmark run. Data classification: none (synthetic cells).

## Accessibility notes
- The non-colour encodings from **E06-D01** (delta glyph, imbalance outline, estimated hatch) are implemented in this scene precisely so their rendering cost is inside the measured budget rather than discovered later (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §4).
- Contrast >= 4.5:1 for cell text over its own background is an acceptance criterion here, not a later fix (§5).
- Per-cell DOM surrogates (CMP-109's `aria-label` composition and cell-to-cell arrow navigation) are structurally measured in **E06-D03**; this ticket must expose cell values through `stats()`/a data accessor so that measurement is possible.

## Performance notes
Budgets: **B3** p95 <= 16 ms, text batching <= 2.0 ms, <= 2 text draw calls; stage slice for footprint text/geometry <= 4 ms (`06-…` §4.3); atlas from cache <= 5 ms (B9 secondary). Text density degradation is the *second* lever in the degradation ladder (`06-…` §4.4), after heatmap cadence — so this scene must also demonstrate that shedding text actually recovers the budget.

## Observability
Scene reports `{visibleCells, glyphCount, textDrawCalls, textBatchMs, outlinePassMs, atlasGenMs, atlasCacheHit, atlasTextureBytes}` into the harness JSON; `glyphCount` and `textBatchMs` become SCR-046 counters via E06-D02.

title: Prototype scene C: 200-depth heatmap texture ring, 4h trail and 30-min soak
body:
## Context
The DOM liquidity heatmap is the surface that decides the **Electron vs Tauri** question. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md` says so plainly: "Tauri's WebView2 behaviour under sustained 100 ms heatmap texture updates is unverified, and it varies by OS-provided WebView version". Three of ADR-0011's five binding criteria are about this scene specifically — p95 within 10 % of Electron for B5, no frame-time outliers above 33 ms during a 30-minute soak that are absent under Electron, and no progressive degradation of `texSubImage2D` streaming at 10 Hz over 30 minutes.

The technique under test is the rolling-texture ring of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8: quantise each column to R16F, upload **one 1 x rows texture column** (512 x 2 bytes = 1 KB) per update regardless of trail length, advance a ring cursor mod 2048, draw one or two textured quads, and colour through a 256x1 LUT so a theme change is a single texture update. Constant upload cost independent of history is "the entire reason for the texture approach" — and it is exactly the property a WebView might fail to sustain.

Longer trails roll into a **coarse ring** (1 column per second instead of per 100 ms), giving 4 h+ of history at a tenth of the memory. Whether that coarse resolution should be 1 s or 2 s is open item **O3**, assigned for resolution from the soak.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype scene C on `spike/e06-engine-m0`:
  - **Fine ring**: R16F texture, width 2048 columns, height 512 price rows, `writeCol` cursor, `colTime: Float64Array(2048)` for time mapping, `priceOrigin`/`priceStep` in integer ticks (`26-…` §3.3/§3.8). Memory target ~2 MB.
  - **Coarse ring**: 14,400 columns x 512 rows (~14 MB) for 4 h+ of history, with the shader selecting source by column age; both 1 s and 2 s candidate resolutions measured to close **O3**.
  - **Streaming**: `texSubImage2D(x = writeCol, w = 1, h = rows)` at 10 Hz from the seeded heatmap fixture; ring wrap drawn as two sub-quads.
  - **Colour**: 256x1 LUT texture using the ramp delivered by **E06-D02** (green = bid, red = ask per owner decision #10, configurable); theme switch implemented as a LUT swap and its cost measured to prove the one-texture-update claim. Log and linear intensity mappings and the age-decay curve as specified.
  - **Price-origin shifting**: when the market moves outside the row window, shift `priceOrigin` and re-upload only newly exposed rows (a vertical scroll of the ring) — never the whole texture. This path must be exercised by the fixture, since it is the easy thing to get wrong and the expensive thing to get wrong in production.
  - **Alignment** with the price scale and with scene A's time mapping (`timeToScreen`), so panning costs nothing extra.
  - DPR capped at 2 for the heatmap layer to bound texture cost (`26-…` §3.4).
- Benchmarks wired: **B4** (100 ms columns, 4 h trail, panning: p95 <= 10 ms, upload <= 12 KB/s, texture memory <= 20 MB) and **B10** (30-minute memory/streaming soak: peak <= 600 MB, no monotonic growth, no outliers > 33 ms).
- Capability probe results recorded: `EXT_color_buffer_float`, `R16F` render/sample support, `OES_texture_float_linear`, instancing, `OffscreenCanvas` in a worker — these are ADR-0011 criterion 4 verbatim.
- Components exercised: **CMP-193 HeatmapOverlay** (engine mount point, render/upload performance contract), **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend**.
- Stories informed: **US-CHART-001**, **US-CHART-006**; the DOM-domain heatmap stories consume this engine capability later.

## Out of scope
- Real order-book reconstruction, L2 delta application, iceberg/stop-run estimation — backend order-flow work in later epics; this scene consumes synthetic pre-aggregated columns.
- The DOM ladder UI (SCR-050 and the DOM domain screens).
- Final colour-blind-safe palette selection (open item **O5**, assigned to the M8 a11y pass); only E06-D02's candidate is exercised.
- Multi-symbol heatmaps and the per-symbol memory multiplication question beyond reporting per-symbol figures.

### Scope trim (21-point roadmap budget)
Measured at the 4 h trail and 30-minute soak required by benchmarks **B4** and **B10** only. Longer trails, multi-symbol heatmaps and coarse-ring resolution tuning (open item **O3**) are recorded as observations and deferred to **E11 M4**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: B4 holds with a 4-hour trail while panning
  Given the fine ring plus coarse ring holding a 4 h trail and columns arriving at 10 Hz
  When the B4 scenario runs for 20 s with panning, 3 repetitions
  Then median p95 frame time is <= 10 ms
  And uploaded bytes are <= 12 KB/s and total heatmap texture memory is <= 20 MB

Scenario: Upload cost is constant in trail length
  Given trails of 5 minutes, 1 hour and 4 hours
  When each is measured under identical column cadence
  Then uploaded bytes per second are equal within measurement noise across all three
  And frame time does not increase with trail length, proving the ring design rather than assuming it

Scenario: 30-minute soak shows no progressive degradation
  Given the B10 soak running the heatmap at 10 Hz for 30 minutes
  When frame times and process memory are sampled throughout
  Then peak memory is <= 600 MB with no monotonic growth beyond the documented steady-state variance band
  And there are no frame-time outliers above 33 ms, recorded per runtime so ADR-0011 criteria 2 and 3 can be evaluated

Scenario: Price-origin shift re-uploads only new rows
  Given the market moves outside the current row window
  When priceOrigin shifts
  Then only the newly exposed rows are uploaded, asserted by an instrumentation counter of uploaded bytes for that frame
  And the frame containing the shift does not exceed the frame budget

Scenario: Theme change is a LUT swap
  Given the bid/ask colour convention is switched
  When the change is applied
  Then exactly one 256x1 texture upload occurs and no heatmap data is re-uploaded
  And the switch completes within a single frame

Scenario: Capability gaps degrade rather than break
  Given a runtime where EXT_color_buffer_float or R16F sampling is unavailable
  When the capability probe runs
  Then the scene selects a reduced or degraded-2d profile and still renders correct (if coarser) output
  And the probe result is recorded in the run report for ADR-0011 criterion 4
```

## Technical notes / design
- Quantisation: normalise each column by column max or a global scale (both measured — the choice changes how spikes read and is a product question worth an explicit answer in the report).
- Column aggregation when more than one column maps to a pixel uses **max** of columns, preserving liquidity spikes (`26-…` §3.6) — same correctness principle as candle min/max decimation.
- The 100 ms cadence is a **visual refresh** cadence decoupled from message cadence (`06-…` §4.2): deltas are coalesced and sampled at 10 Hz, so a message-rate spike must not translate 1:1 into upload spikes. Demonstrate this by driving the fixture at 5x message rate and confirming upload bytes stay flat.
- Degradation lever #1 in `06-…` §4.4 is reducing heatmap cadence from 100 ms toward 250 ms; implement and measure it so the ladder is evidence-backed.
- Coarse-ring selection by column age happens in the shader; the boundary must be exact or a visible seam appears at the transition — check it in a golden image.
- Report memory per symbol (fine + coarse) so the capacity discussion for 10 recorded symbols (`06-…` §10) is grounded.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ring cursor wrap arithmetic (including the two-sub-quad draw case); `colTime` mapping monotonicity; price-origin shift computing exactly the newly exposed row range; LUT generation from the E06-D02 ramp matching legend tick values; coarse/fine selection boundary by age.
- **Integration**: B4 and B10 via the harness; constant-upload-vs-trail-length experiment; 5x message-rate coalescing experiment; theme-swap cost.
- **Chaos** (per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §9): simulate a WebGL **context loss** mid-soak and verify the documented recovery (stop loop, invalidate GPU resources, rebuild from the data model, one-frame flash, no data loss — `26-…` §3.4). This is the cheapest place to prove context-loss recovery works at all.
- **Visual**: golden images at the fine/coarse boundary and at the ring wrap.
- Coverage: prototype exempt; promoted helpers >= 85 %.

## Security notes
No new surface beyond E06-K01's pinned toolchain (STRIDE **T**ampering). Synthetic data only; no book data, no credentials, no network I/O during runs. One forward-looking note for E11: heatmap columns in production derive from exchange book state, which is not user data but is rate-limited/licensed material — the recorder's retention rules (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`) govern it, not the engine.

## Accessibility notes
- Heatmap intensity must be available as text via tooltip and cursor announcement (`26-…` §12), so the scene exposes an intensity accessor at cursor position through `stats()`; **E06-D03** uses it when measuring the mirror.
- The bid/ask colour convention is configurable specifically so colour-vision differences can be accommodated; the E06-D02 colour-blind-safe candidate is rendered and reviewed here, feeding open item **O5**.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: the age-decay animation must be expressible as an instant state rather than a continuous fade; verify the scene honours that.

## Performance notes
Budgets: **B4** p95 <= 10 ms, upload <= 12 KB/s, texture memory <= 20 MB; **B10** peak <= 600 MB, no monotonic growth, no > 33 ms outliers; stage slice for heatmap upload <= 2 ms (`06-…` §4.3). ADR-0011 criteria 2 and 3 are evaluated directly from this scene's soak numbers.

## Observability
Scene reports `{columnsPerSec, uploadedBytesPerSec, fineRingBytes, coarseRingBytes, ringWraps, priceOriginShifts, rowsReuploaded, lutSwapMs, capabilityProbe{}}` into the harness JSON; the upload and texture-memory counters become SCR-046 counters via E06-D02.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] B4 and B10 measured with >= 3 reps (soak once per runtime, given duration); numbers recorded.
- [ ] Constant-upload-vs-trail-length and 5x-message-rate coalescing experiments reported.
- [ ] Open item **O3** closed: coarse-ring resolution (1 s vs 2 s) chosen from the soak and recorded in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16.
- [ ] Capability probe results captured per runtime for ADR-0011 criterion 4.
- [ ] Context-loss recovery demonstrated during the soak.
- [ ] Golden images at ring wrap and fine/coarse boundary captured for E11.
- [ ] Findings written up for E06-T02, including per-symbol memory figures.
- [ ] Reviewed by the chart-engine owner; design reviewer confirms LUT output matches E06-D02.

## Dependencies

- `blocked_by: E06-D02` — the LUT ramp and legend spec; a prototype with an invented palette cannot validate the one-texture-update claim against the real design.
- Blocks **E06-T01** and **E06-D03** (which measures the a11y mirror against this, the harshest live-update scene).

- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).

title: GPU/browser compatibility sweep and degraded-2d exploratory charter
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` carries **R8 Browser/GPU compat** as a standing risk, and the engine design answers it with a capability probe that selects one of three render profiles — `full`, `reduced`, `degraded-2d` (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.4) — plus an explicit claim in §2 that when `OffscreenCanvas` is unavailable "the same worker code runs on the main thread behind an identical facade (`RunMode.inline`); only throughput changes, not behaviour. This is a supported, tested mode, not an accident."

Two claims there are untested: that `degraded-2d` is a *supported profile* rather than a euphemism for a broken chart, and that `RunMode.inline` changes throughput but not behaviour. Both matter beyond the spike — managers may use the browser rather than the desktop shell (`ADR-0011`: "The browser remains a fully supported deployment target for managers"), so the browser path is a real product surface, not a fallback nobody uses.

The compatibility findings also feed E06-T01: the matrix needs to know what "reference hardware" deliberately excludes, so the report does not over-claim from a single favourable GPU.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Capability/compatibility sweep** of the prototype (scenes A and B, plus C where capabilities allow) across:
  - Chrome/Chromium, Edge and Firefox on the reference machine (the browser deployment target);
  - a low-end integrated-GPU machine (Intel UHD class — below the reference bar, deliberately) to force `reduced` and `degraded-2d` profiles;
  - a machine with a deliberately outdated GPU driver, to see what an un-updated user actually experiences;
  - software rendering (SwiftShader / `--disable-gpu`) as the floor case.
- **Capability probe result table** per environment: max texture size, max texture units, `EXT_color_buffer_float`, `OES_texture_float_linear`, `R16F` render/sample, instancing, integer attributes, max vertex attributes, `OffscreenCanvas` in a worker — the same list ADR-0011 criterion 4 requires, extended to browsers.
- **`degraded-2d` evaluation**: with the GL path forced off, is the chart usable? Does the Canvas-2D path render correct (if coarser) output, is footprint limited to L2/L3 as designed (§3.7), and what is the honest frame rate? Recorded as a usability verdict, not only a number.
- **`RunMode.inline` behavioural-equivalence check**: the same scenario run in worker mode and inline mode, with outputs compared for behavioural identity (same LOD decisions, same rendered geometry, same interaction semantics) and throughput reported separately.
- **Exploratory charters** (per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11), timeboxed 2 h each, findings triaged as expected/defect/needs-decision:
  1. *Context loss and recovery*: force `WEBGL_lose_context` at varied moments (mid-pan, mid-upload, during atlas generation) and observe recovery against the documented behaviour (`26-…` §3.4).
  2. *Hostile display conditions*: fractional DPR (1.25, 1.5, 1.75), browser zoom to 200 % (required by `26-…` §12 reflow rule), monitor switch mid-session, HDR display, multi-monitor with mixed DPI.
  3. *Resource starvation*: heavy CPU load, another GPU-hungry tab, backgrounded tab (rAF throttling), laptop on battery saver.
- **Chaos scenario** contribution back to `03-testing-strategy.md` §9's catalogue: the context-loss scenario as a reusable, documented test for E11.

## Out of scope
- Mobile browsers and Android (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).
- Safari/macOS unless a machine is available — record as a gap with an owner rather than silently omitting it, since WKWebView is the Tauri path on macOS.
- Fixing what is found: defects are filed against the scene tickets or recorded as E11 constraints.
- Performance verdicts on the reference machine (**E06-T01**) — this ticket is about the edges, not the centre.

### Scope trim (21-point roadmap budget)
The sweep covers **three GPU/driver classes** — NVIDIA discrete (GTX 1650 class), Intel Iris Xe integrated, and one software/ANGLE fallback path — the minimum needed to characterise risk **R8**. A wider device matrix is deferred to **E46 Performance hardening**; this ticket records the classes *not* covered as a known gap in the M0 report.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every environment yields a profile decision, not a crash
  Given each environment in the sweep
  When the capability probe runs and the prototype loads
  Then a render profile (full / reduced / degraded-2d) is selected and the scene renders correct output at that profile
  And any environment where the prototype fails to render at all is recorded as a defect with the probe output attached

Scenario: degraded-2d is usable, and we say how usable
  Given the GL path is forced off
  When scenes A and B render through the Canvas-2D path
  Then footprint is limited to L2/L3 per 26-chart-engine-design.md §3.7 and candles/axes still render correctly
  And an honest frame-rate figure and usability verdict are recorded, rather than the mode being described only as "supported"

Scenario: Inline mode changes throughput, not behaviour
  Given the same scenario in worker mode and in RunMode.inline
  When outputs are compared
  Then LOD decisions, rendered geometry and interaction semantics are identical
  And any behavioural difference is filed as a defect against the claim in 26-chart-engine-design.md §2

Scenario: Context loss recovers as documented
  Given WEBGL_lose_context is triggered mid-pan, mid-upload and during atlas generation
  When the context is restored
  Then the engine stops the loop, invalidates GPU resources, rebuilds from the data model and resumes with at most a one-frame flash and no data loss
  And any case that loses data or fails to recover is a defect, not an accepted limitation

Scenario: Browser zoom to 200 % reflows rather than clips
  Given browser zoom is increased to 200 %
  When the chart renders
  Then density classes scale and content is not clipped, per 26-chart-engine-design.md §12
  And the resulting cell sizes are checked against E06-D01's legibility thresholds
```

## Technical notes / design
- The probe table is the durable artefact: E11 will use it to decide which capabilities may be assumed and which need a fallback path. Capture raw probe output, not a summary.
- Fractional DPR is a known source of hairline and text-crispness bugs given the engine's pixel-snapping strategy (§3.4); examine rendered output visually, not only frame times.
- Backgrounded-tab rAF throttling interacts with the render-on-demand design (§3.2 rule 5) and with the heatmap's 10 Hz cadence: when the tab returns to the foreground, does the heatmap catch up correctly or replay a burst? A burst on return is a real production concern for a trader switching windows.
- Outdated-driver environments are where `EXT_color_buffer_float` tends to go missing, which forces the heatmap to a lower-precision format — record what visual difference that actually makes.
- Software rendering will be far below budget; the question is whether the app degrades gracefully and says so (the SCR-030 "low-GPU degraded" state and the SCR-048 WebGL-unavailable messaging), not whether it is fast.

## Test plan
- Sweep executed per environment with the capability probe and scenes A/B (C where supported), results tabulated.
- Three exploratory charters executed, timeboxed, with session notes recorded per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.
- Worker-vs-inline behavioural comparison via golden images plus a LOD-decision trace diff.
- Context-loss chaos scenario documented for reuse and contributed to the §9 catalogue.
- Findings triaged with the chart-engine lead; each becomes a defect, an E11 constraint, or an accepted limitation with rationale.

## Security notes
- Testing across machines must not introduce unpinned tooling: each environment uses the same pinned harness build (STRIDE **T**ampering, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §12).
- No credentials or real data on any test machine; synthetic fixtures only. Data classification: none.
- The outdated-driver machine is deliberately unpatched for testing and must not be used for anything else; record it as an isolated test asset so it never becomes a shadow workstation.

## Accessibility notes
- Browser zoom to 200 % is a WCAG 2.2 reflow requirement (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `26-…` §12) and is tested here as a first-class scenario.
- `degraded-2d` must not lose the accessible layer: the DOM mirror and data cursor are DOM-based and independent of the GL path, so the sweep verifies a11y behaviour is unchanged across all three render profiles (also an acceptance criterion of **E06-D03**).
- The "reduced live detail" indicator required by `06-…` §4.4 must be non-colour-only; check its presence wherever degradation engages.

## Performance notes
Not a budget-verification ticket. It produces the *context* for the budget numbers: which environments meet the reference bar, which degrade, and what degradation actually delivers. Feeds the M0 report's compatibility section.

## Observability
Capability probe output is captured into the harness report per environment, so any future benchmark result carries the capability context that produced it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Sweep completed across all listed environments (or gaps recorded with owners, e.g. macOS/WKWebView).
- [ ] Capability probe table published and handed to E11.
- [ ] `degraded-2d` usability verdict and frame-rate figures recorded.
- [ ] Worker-vs-inline behavioural-equivalence result recorded; defects filed if they differ.
- [ ] Three exploratory charters executed with session notes; findings triaged.
- [ ] Context-loss chaos scenario documented and contributed to `03-testing-strategy.md` §9.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted; findings handed to **E06-T01** and **E06-T02**.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E06-K02, E06-K03` — needs renderable scenes; scene C is included where the environment supports it.
- Blocks **E06-T01** (the matrix needs to know what reference hardware excludes).

## Branch
`test/e06-compat-sweep` (probe tables, charters, chaos scenario docs). PR size guidance: docs + test-scenario definitions, one PR.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 (architecture), §3.4 (GL backend), §3.6 (LOD), §3.7 (SDF text), §3.8 (heatmap streaming), §13 (benchmarks B1-B10), §14 (test strategy), §15 (milestone M0), §16 (open items O1-O3)

title: Run the measurement matrix across Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2
body:
## Context
The three prototype scenes exist; this ticket turns them into the evidence table that both ADRs consume. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.1 names the three runtimes: headless Chromium (primary CI target), Electron (release-representative), and Tauri/WebView2 **during the engine spike only**. `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md` lists five binding criteria, all of which are decided by numbers produced here, and sets the deadline at the end of Sprint 03 — so the matrix must complete inside Sprint 02 to leave room for the decision and any re-runs.

The reason this is a separate ticket rather than a step inside each scene spike is that cross-runtime comparison has its own discipline: identical fixtures, identical seeds, identical driver scripts, the same machine, versions of everything captured, and enough repetitions that a 10 % criterion (ADR-0011 criterion 1) means something. Folding it into the scene work invites each scene being measured slightly differently, which would make the comparison worthless precisely where it matters most.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Runtime targets built and pinned:
  - **Headless Chromium** via Playwright with the pinned GPU flag set from E06-K01.
  - **Electron** harness shell with `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true` and the GPU flags under evaluation (the hardening baseline from **E06-X01**; also the input to E10's shell configuration).
  - **Tauri v2 / WebView2** harness shell, with the exact WebView2 runtime version recorded — the whole point of the arm is that this version is OS-updated and results are only meaningful when versioned.
- Full matrix executed: scenarios **B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B7, B9, B10** x 3 runtimes, >= 3 repetitions each (soaks once per runtime), medians of p95 per `06-…` §7.4.
- **B5 combined scene** assembled here from scenes A+B+C plus 3 synthetic indicator series and 50 order lines — this is the scene R0 exit criterion 4 is stated against (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3), so its composition is documented precisely and its gates are p95 <= 16.7 ms and <= 40 draw calls.
- **B7 live update storm** (20 data messages/s x 6 stores, decode p95 <= 4 ms, zero dropped messages) exercising the worker + `OffscreenCanvas` path and the `RunMode.inline` fallback for runtimes lacking `OffscreenCanvas`.
- ADR-0011 criteria evaluated one by one with the measured figure and a pass/fail, including criterion 5 (shell responsibility parity) whose checklist comes from **E06-X01**.
- Machine descriptor and full version manifest per run (CPU, GPU, driver, OS build, Electron version, Chromium version, Tauri version, WebView2 version, Node version, flag set).
- Raw JSON artefacts committed alongside the report.

## Out of scope
- Writing the report or the ADRs (**E06-T02**, **E06-T03**).
- Optimising the scenes: if a budget is missed, this ticket records it; whether to spend timebox on optimisation is an Architect call made against the M0 timebox, and any optimisation lands in the scene tickets.
- Measuring on secondary hardware beyond the reference machine and the one compatibility-sweep machine from **E06-Q02**.
- Standing CI runs of the Tauri arm — explicitly not a standing CI target once the decision is finalised (`06-…` §7.1).

### Scope trim (21-point roadmap budget)
The binding matrix legs are **Electron** and **Tauri v2 / WebView2** — ADR-0011 turns on their difference and R0 exit criterion 4 is stated in Electron. **Headless Chromium** is retained as a one-configuration baseline smoke arm (useful for attributing a regression to the shell vs the engine), not as a full leg.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The matrix is complete and comparable
  Given eight scenarios and three runtimes
  When the matrix has run
  Then every cell has a median-of-p95 result from >= 3 repetitions, or a documented reason it could not run (e.g. missing WebGL2 capability)
  And every run used the same seed, fixture and driver script, asserted by the seed and fixture hash recorded in each report

Scenario: R0 exit criterion 4 is answered unambiguously
  Given the B5 combined scene in Electron on the reference machine
  When results are tabulated
  Then p50 and p95 frame times are stated against the >= 60 fps p50 / >= 55 fps p95 bar from docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §4.3
  And the verdict is stated as pass or fail without hedging, with per-stage attribution showing where the time went

Scenario: ADR-0011 criterion 1 is decided on a like-for-like comparison
  Given B5 p95 in WebView2 and in Electron on the same machine in the same session
  When the difference is computed
  Then it is reported as a percentage against the 10 % threshold
  And the WebView2 runtime version is recorded next to the figure

Scenario: Soak outliers are attributed to a runtime, not to noise
  Given the 30-minute B10 soak in each runtime
  When frame-time outliers above 33 ms are counted
  Then outliers present in WebView2 but absent in Electron are identified as such per ADR-0011 criterion 2
  And any outlier present in all runtimes is investigated as an engine issue rather than a shell issue

Scenario: A capability gap is a result, not a blocker
  Given a runtime that lacks EXT_color_buffer_float, R16F sampling, instancing or OffscreenCanvas in a worker
  When the capability probe runs
  Then the gap is recorded against ADR-0011 criterion 4
  And the affected scenarios run in the reduced or degraded-2d profile with results labelled accordingly, rather than being omitted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Same machine, same session, alternating runtimes (A/B/A ordering) to cancel thermal drift — a sequential "all Electron then all Tauri" schedule would let a warm machine slander the second runtime.
- Close everything else on the reference machine; record background load. Note that the backend stack (WSL, Docker, QuestDB, Postgres) is the realistic co-tenant per ADR-0011's memory argument, so run one **co-tenancy variant** of B5 with the dev stack running, and report resident memory for each shell — this is the evidence for ADR-0011's "roughly 100-150 MB higher than Tauri" claim.
- `OffscreenCanvas` availability differs across WebViews; where absent, run `RunMode.inline` and label the result, because the inline mode's numbers are not comparable to worker-mode numbers and must never be averaged together.
- Electron GPU flags are themselves a variable; measure the default flag set and the tuned set, and hand the winner to **E10** as the recommended configuration.
- Tauri arm needs a minimal Rust host; keep it to the smallest possible shell that can load the harness page and expose the same driver hooks, to avoid measuring our Rust code instead of WebView2.

## Test plan
- The matrix *is* the test. Its own validity is checked by **E06-Q01** (methodology validation) and its cross-machine reproducibility by **E06-Q02** (compat sweep).
- Sanity gate before accepting results: run the same scenario twice in the same runtime and confirm the two medians of p95 agree within the documented noise band; if they do not, the matrix is not admissible and the noise source must be found first.
- Contract: every emitted report validates against the E06-K01 JSON schema.

## Security notes
- The Electron harness shell must already carry the mandatory hardening from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` — `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, strict CSP, allow-list preload, navigation and `window.open` blocked — because these settings have measurable performance implications and measuring an unhardened shell would produce numbers we can never ship against (STRIDE **E**levation of privilege). Checklist supplied by **E06-X01**.
- The Tauri arm introduces a Rust toolchain and crate dependencies: pinned, lockfile-committed, and scanned (**E06-X02**).
- No network access during runs; no credentials; synthetic data only. Data classification: none.

## Accessibility notes
The DOM-mirror stage from **E06-D03** is included in the matrix runs so its cost is measured in all three runtimes, not just Chromium — a WebView with slower DOM performance would hit the a11y layer hardest, and that must be part of the shell decision rather than a later surprise.

## Performance notes
All budgets from `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 (B1-B10) and the stage allocations of `06-…` §4.3 apply. The decisive figures are B5 in Electron (R0 exit criterion 4) and B5/B10 in WebView2 vs Electron (ADR-0011 criteria 1-3).

## Observability
Produces the complete set of run-report JSON artefacts that become the project's first performance baselines, subject afterwards to the baseline-update policy in `06-…` §7.4 (baselines move only via a reviewed PR with rationale).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All matrix cells executed or explicitly justified as not-runnable.
- [ ] Raw JSON artefacts committed; version manifest complete for every run.
- [ ] Co-tenancy variant and resident-memory comparison recorded.
- [ ] ADR-0011 criteria 1-5 each carry a measured figure and a pass/fail.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion 4 answered pass/fail with per-stage attribution.
- [ ] Recommended Electron GPU flag set handed to **E10**.
- [ ] Noise-band sanity gate passed before results were accepted.
- [ ] Architect review of the matrix before it is used as ADR evidence.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E06-K02, E06-K03, E06-K04` — the three scenes.
- `blocked_by: E06-X01` — the Electron/Tauri hardening checklist; measuring an unhardened shell wastes the run.
- `blocked_by: E06-Q02` — the compatibility charter defines which GPU/driver combinations the sweep covers, so the matrix knows what "reference" excludes.
- Blocks **E06-T02**.

## Branch
`spike/e06-engine-m0` for shell harnesses; result artefacts land via the E06-T02 docs PR. PR size guidance: artefacts + manifest only.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 (architecture), §3.4 (GL backend), §3.6 (LOD), §3.7 (SDF text), §3.8 (heatmap streaming), §13 (benchmarks B1-B10), §14 (test strategy), §15 (milestone M0), §16 (open items O1-O3)
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md` (fallback trigger)

title: Write the M0 findings report and commit the CI benchmark harness job
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 requires a Spike to answer its questions "with recorded evidence (benchmark numbers, prototype repo/branch link, comparison table)" and to record the decision as an ADR. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 adds a specific R0 quality-gate row: "E06 benchmark harness committed and runnable in CI (numbers recorded, not yet gating)". This ticket produces both — the written M0 report that ADR-0002 and ADR-0011 cite as their validation, and the CI job that keeps the numbers alive after the spike ends.

The report matters beyond the two decisions. Everything E11 builds over ten sprints is sized against these numbers, and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15's milestone estimates are only credible if M0's findings say what M1-M8 must budget. A report that just says "it was fast enough" would satisfy the letter of the gate and waste the spike.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **M0 findings report** at `docs/plan/28-m0-engine-spike-report.md` (new file, linked from ADR-0002, ADR-0011 and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15), containing:
  - Executive verdict: custom engine go/no-go against R0 exit criterion 4; Electron vs Tauri recommendation against ADR-0011's five criteria.
  - Full results matrix: B1-B10 x 3 runtimes, medians of p95 from >= 3 repetitions, with p50/p95/p99 and per-stage attribution against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3.
  - Machine and version manifest, including the WebView2 runtime version, so the results are reproducible and their shelf life is understood.
  - Text-strategy comparison (SDF atlas vs Canvas-2D glyph cache) from **E06-K03**, with the decision and its rationale.
  - Heatmap findings from **E06-K04**: constant-upload proof, coarse-ring resolution choice (open item **O3**), per-symbol memory, context-loss recovery evidence.
  - A11y cost section from **E06-D03**: measured DOM-mirror sync cost against its 1 ms allocation, announcement cadence decision, LOD/mirror parity rule.
  - Compatibility findings from **E06-Q02**: which GPU/driver combinations were swept, what degraded, what the `degraded-2d` profile actually delivers.
  - **What M1-M8 must budget**: a section translating findings into concrete guidance per milestone in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15, so E11's tickets inherit evidence rather than re-deriving it.
  - Residual unknowns explicitly listed as open items with owners, rather than being quietly omitted.
- **CI job**: benchmark harness wired into the pipeline (GitHub Actions, per `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0013-ci-pipeline.md` and E03's workflow set) on a dedicated runner — headless Chromium per PR touching `packages/chart-engine`, Electron nightly (startup cost makes per-PR impractical, per `06-…` §7.1). **Recording only, not gating**, with baselines committed and the baseline-update policy of `06-…` §7.4 documented in the package README.
- Follow-up tickets filed against **E11** (per-milestone guidance) and **E10** (recommended GPU flag set, shell hardening settings), each linking the report so implementers do not re-derive findings — required by DoD §5.2.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated: **R2** and **R8** re-scored with evidence; **R10** key-person mitigation noted (the report is the transferable artefact).

## Out of scope
- The ADR edits themselves (**E06-T03**) — this ticket supplies the evidence they cite.
- Making the benchmarks a required check: that is E11's job once the engine is real and baselines are meaningful (`30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 says "not yet gating" for R0).
- Backend/API load-testing CI (E03/E07 territory).
- Re-running the matrix: if the report reveals a gap, a re-run is a change to E06-T01, not a silent extension here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The report is self-sufficient evidence
  Given a reader who was not involved in the spike
  When they read docs/plan/28-m0-engine-spike-report.md
  Then they can state the verdict on the custom engine and on the shell choice, see the numbers behind each, and identify the machine and software versions that produced them
  And every claim in the executive verdict traces to a row in the results matrix

Scenario: The CI job runs and records without blocking
  Given a PR touching packages/chart-engine
  When CI runs
  Then the headless Chromium benchmark job executes and publishes its report artefact
  And a regression does not fail the build in R0, but is visible as a published comparison against the committed baseline

Scenario: Nightly Electron coverage exists
  Given the nightly schedule
  When the Electron benchmark variant runs
  Then its results are published and compared to the Electron baseline
  And a failure to run is itself surfaced, rather than silently producing no data

Scenario: Follow-ups exist before the Epic closes
  Given the report's "what M1-M8 must budget" section
  When the Epic is reviewed for closure
  Then follow-up tickets exist against E11 and E10 citing specific report sections
  And the risk register reflects the re-scored R2 and R8

Scenario: Unknowns are stated, not hidden
  Given questions the spike could not answer inside its timebox
  When the report is finalised
  Then each is listed as a named open item with an owner and a resolution path, consistent with 26-chart-engine-design.md §16
```

## Technical notes / design
- Report structure follows the ADR validation sections it feeds, so ADR-0002's "Validation" and ADR-0011's "Validation" can cite specific headings rather than the document as a whole.
- Numbers in the report are generated from the committed JSON artefacts by a small script, not transcribed by hand — transcription errors in an ADR's evidence base are unacceptable and easily avoided.
- CI runner must be a dedicated machine with a stable GPU and a pinned flag set (`26-…` §13); a shared runner produces noise that would make even non-gating numbers misleading. Document the runner's specification in the report's manifest section.
- Baselines are committed as JSON alongside the harness; the update policy (baselines move forward only via a reviewed PR with rationale) is documented where an engineer will actually read it — the package README, not only the standards doc.
- Repetition and median-of-p95 rules from `06-…` §7.4 are enforced by the harness (E06-K01), so the CI job inherits them rather than restating them.

## Test plan
- **Contract**: the report-generation script validates every input artefact against the E06-K01 JSON schema and fails on a missing machine descriptor or a sub-3-repetition run marked inadmissible.
- **Integration**: CI job verified by a deliberate dry run on a branch, confirming artefact publication and baseline comparison output.
- **Review**: report reviewed by the Architect, the chart-engine lead and a second engineer who did not run the measurements (reproducibility reviewer from **E06-Q01**).
- Coverage: report-generation script carries the package threshold (>= 85 %).

## Security notes
- The published report and CI artefacts must contain no machine-identifying information beyond hardware class, no internal hostnames, no absolute paths containing usernames (STRIDE **I**nformation disclosure, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5). The generation script strips these.
- CI job runs only committed, pinned tooling; no fetching of fixtures or flags at run time (STRIDE **T**ampering). Verified by **E06-X02**.
- Data classification: none.

## Accessibility notes
The report includes the a11y cost section from **E06-D03** as a first-class result rather than an appendix, because the 1 ms DOM-mirror allocation is part of the frame budget and hiding it would misstate the engine's real cost. The report document itself follows the repo's docs conventions (headings, tables with headers, no information conveyed by colour alone).

## Performance notes
Establishes the project's first committed performance baselines for B1-B10 and the <= 5 % regression-gate machinery that becomes binding in E11 (`06-…` §7.4).

## Observability
CI publishes a per-run artefact and a comparison summary; the harness's JSON schema is the long-lived contract that later engine work and the SCR-046 overlay both speak.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/plan/28-m0-engine-spike-report.md` merged, linked from ADR-0002, ADR-0011 and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15.
- [ ] All numbers generated from committed artefacts by script, not transcribed.
- [ ] CI job merged: Chromium per-PR (path-filtered), Electron nightly; recording, non-gating; baselines committed.
- [ ] Baseline-update policy documented in the package README.

- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated (R2, R8 re-scored; R10 noted).
- [ ] Reviewed by Architect + chart-engine lead + the independent reproducibility reviewer.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E06-T01` — the matrix results are the report's substance.
- `blocked_by: E06-Q01` — methodology validation must pass before results are published as ADR evidence.
- `blocked_by: E06-D03` — the a11y cost section.
- Blocks **E06-T03** (the ADRs cite this report).

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-bench-harness` (CI job) and `docs/e06-m0-report` (report). PR size guidance: two PRs — CI job <= 200 LOC, report docs-only.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 (architecture), §3.4 (GL backend), §3.6 (LOD), §3.7 (SDF text), §3.8 (heatmap streaming), §13 (benchmarks B1-B10), §14 (test strategy), §15 (milestone M0), §16 (open items O1-O3)

title: Amend ADR-0002 and move ADR-0011 to decided with measured evidence
body:
## Context
Two ADRs are waiting on this spike. **ADR-0002** (custom WebGL chart engine) is already `decided` but carries a **binding fallback trigger**: the Lightweight Charts v5 chassis is adopted if spike S1/M0 fails its exit criteria, with the decision belonging to the Architect and recorded as an amendment. **ADR-0011** (Electron vs Tauri) is still `proposed` with a hard deadline — "end of Sprint 03, gated on spike S1 / engine milestone M0" — and five binding criteria that are adopted only if **all** hold.

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 makes this non-optional for a Spike: the decision must be recorded as an ADR "even if the decision is 'defer, need more data' — that itself is an ADR entry". And `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3 exit criterion 4 ties the whole R0 release to the outcome: a failure obliges formal adoption of the fallback and a re-cut of R1 scope **before Sprint 05 planning**.

This ticket is deliberately separate from the report (E06-T02) because the decision is an act of governance with named deciders, not a documentation chore, and because a failing result triggers real downstream work that must be filed the same week it is known.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR-0002 amendment** (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md`): a dated "M0 outcome" section stating whether the fallback trigger fired, citing the report's results matrix, signed by the Architect. If the trigger fired, the amendment states the adoption of the Lightweight Charts v5 chassis and what of the engine design survives (the data model and plugin API are explicitly designed to be re-hostable — `ADR-0002` "Key structural commitments").
- **ADR-0011 finalisation** (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md`): status `proposed` -> `decided`; each of the five criteria annotated with its measured figure and pass/fail; the rejected option recorded as "rejected-with-evidence"; the `Validation` section linked to `docs/plan/28-m0-engine-spike-report.md`.
- **Downstream consequences filed the same week**:
  - If the engine is confirmed: E11 milestone guidance tickets (already filed by E06-T02) are confirmed, and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15 estimates are adjusted if the findings contradict them.
  - If the fallback fired: R1 re-cut tickets filed against the roadmap before Sprint 05 planning, with `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3, §5 and the epic table updated, plus a note to the Owner.
  - Either way: E10's shell tickets updated with the decided shell, the recommended GPU flag set and the hardening settings from **E06-X01**.
- Open items **O1** (Electron vs Tauri) closed in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16; **O2** and **O3** confirmed closed by K03/K04.
- Decision communicated at Sprint Review and recorded on the Epic with the Owner's explicit acceptance.

## Out of scope
- Producing new measurements — if a criterion cannot be evaluated from the report, the gap goes back to **E06-T01** rather than being judged on impression.
- Implementing whichever path is chosen (E10, E11).
- Revisiting ADR-0009 (secrets/key management) beyond confirming the OS-keychain bridge requirement in ADR-0011 criterion 5 is satisfiable in the chosen shell.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: ADR-0011 closes with per-criterion evidence
  Given the M0 report's results matrix
  When ADR-0011 is finalised
  Then each of its five binding criteria carries a measured figure and an explicit pass/fail
  And the status field reads "decided" with the decision date and the named deciders (Architect, Chart-engine lead, Frontend lead, Owner)

Scenario: A single failed criterion confirms Electron
  Given ADR-0011 requires all five criteria to hold for Tauri to be adopted
  When at least one criterion fails
  Then Electron is confirmed and Tauri is recorded as rejected-with-evidence, naming which criterion failed and by how much
  And no further Tauri spike is scheduled without a new, stated question

Scenario: The fallback trigger is honoured, not argued
  Given the B5 combined scene missed >= 60 fps p50 or >= 55 fps p95 in Electron on the reference machine
  When ADR-0002 is amended
  Then the Lightweight Charts v5 fallback is formally adopted by the Architect
  And R1 re-cut tickets are filed before Sprint 05 planning, per docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md §4.3 exit criterion 4

Scenario: An inconclusive result is still a decision
  Given the timebox ended with a criterion unmeasurable
  When the ADRs are updated
  Then the outcome is recorded as "defer with data", stating exactly what is unknown, who owns resolving it and by when
  And the deadline consequence for the shell choice is stated explicitly rather than left open

Scenario: Downstream epics learn the outcome
  Given a decision is recorded
  When the Epic is closed
  Then E10 and E11 carry tickets reflecting the decided shell, GPU flags and engine path
  And open item O1 is closed in 26-chart-engine-design.md §16
```

## Technical notes / design
- ADR house style: keep the original text intact and append a dated outcome/amendment section; do not rewrite history, because the reasoning at proposal time is part of the record's value.
- ADR-0011 criterion 5 (shell responsibility parity: OS-keychain bridge for the KEK, signed auto-update, deep links, multi-window workspace persistence, Playwright-drivable E2E) is not a performance measurement — it is a checklist evaluated from **E06-X01**'s work. Record each item as satisfiable/not with a link to the evidence, so the criterion is falsifiable rather than rhetorical.
- If Electron is confirmed, the mandatory hardening list (`contextIsolation`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`, strict CSP, allow-list preload, blocked navigation and `window.open`, signed auto-updates) moves from ADR-0011's "Negative/risks" into E10's acceptance criteria — file that explicitly; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` treats them as mandatory checklist items, not defaults.
- The Chromium update treadmill (security patches tracked and shipped) needs an owner if Electron is confirmed: name it in the amendment and file the recurring chore.

## Test plan
- Not a code ticket. Verification: (a) every criterion's cited figure exists in the committed report artefacts; (b) a reviewer independently re-reads the matrix and reaches the same pass/fail per criterion; (c) links resolve (report, risk register, roadmap sections).
- Docs CI (markdown lint, link check) green.

## Security notes
- ADR-0011 criterion 5's keychain requirement is a security dependency on `ADR-0009` (secrets and key management): whichever shell wins must be able to hold the KEK in the OS keychain. Confirm with the Security engineer before finalising, and record their sign-off comment (STRIDE **I**nformation disclosure / **E**levation, `04-security-program.md` §5, §6).
- If Electron is confirmed, its hardening items become binding acceptance criteria on E10 — file them rather than assuming E10 remembers.

## Accessibility notes
N/A directly. One consequence to record: the chosen shell determines the screen-reader stack the E2E a11y tests run against (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §8), so the amendment names which screen readers are in scope for the desktop surface.

## Performance notes
No new measurement. The ADRs must state which figures are shelf-life-limited: WebView2 is OS-updated, so ADR-0011's Tauri numbers are valid only for the recorded runtime version — say so, so nobody cites them in a year as if they were durable.

## Observability
N/A — governance artefact. The report and its artefacts remain the durable evidence.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ADR-0002 amended with the dated M0 outcome; Architect sign-off recorded.
- [ ] ADR-0011 status `decided`, all five criteria annotated with figures and pass/fail, rejected option recorded with evidence.
- [ ] Open item **O1** closed in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16; O2/O3 confirmed closed.
- [ ] Downstream tickets filed against E10 and E11 (shell, GPU flags, hardening, milestone guidance; plus R1 re-cut tickets if the fallback fired).

- [ ] Owner acceptance recorded on the Epic; decision presented at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies

## Branch

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

title: Verify the shipped StorageUsage payload against the operator content model
body:
## Context
**Correction of scope (DoR gate finding #2).** This ticket previously performed design QA + an a11y review of the SCR-142
hi-fi. Inside E07 that had nothing to validate: E07 ships **no FE/UI Story**, so there was no engineering deliverable in
this epic for the design QA to be QA *of*, and the real screen QA already exists as **E16-D07** (design QA, Sprint 09) and
**E16-Q05** (a11y audit, Sprint 08) against **E16-S04**'s implementation.

Re-scoped, this ticket now validates an artefact that **does** ship inside E07 and inside the same R0 train: the
`StorageUsage` payload that **E07-T05** actually emits, checked against the operator content model agreed in **E07-D01**.
It is the executable half of D01 - D01 agrees what an operator must be able to decide; D02 proves the shipped contract
lets them, using the real payload from the T05 integration test rather than the OpenAPI example. Moving it from Sprint 04
to **Sprint 03** puts it in the same sprint as E07-T05/T06, so a contract defect is fixed before ADR-0008 closes R0 rather
than after the train has left.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Contract reconciliation run**: capture the real `GET /api/v1/recording/storage` response from the E07-T05 integration
  test (and from a live `make up` stack with one recorded symbol-day), and trace it row by row against E07-D01's operator
  decision list. Output is a committed checklist: decision -> field -> observed value -> pass/fail.
- **Reachable-state coverage audit**: drive the storage tier into each state the implementation can actually reach and
  confirm the payload/error surface reports it with the agreed vocabulary - healthy, migration pending (version delta from
  `pg_migration_pending`), lag warning, accelerated retention (<15 % free), critical/read-only (<5 % free, recording
  paused), `STORAGE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE`, `STORAGE_EXPORT_VERIFY_FAILED` (hot data deliberately retained) and
  `STORAGE_SCHEMA_DRIFT` (readiness refused). Any state the system can enter but the contract cannot express is a defect.
- **Metric/event name reconciliation**: the names E07-T03/T04/T05 emit (`storage_export_rows_total`,
  `storage_export_duration_seconds`, `storage_retention_dropped_bytes_total`, `storage_disk_free_ratio`,
  `questdb_write_seconds`, `pg_migration_pending`) versus the names E07-D01 specified; discrepancies filed against T05.
- **Text-not-colour check at contract level**: every health/severity value in the payload is a machine-readable enum with
  a human text label and a unit, so no downstream consumer is forced to encode meaning in colour.
- **Leakage check**: no filesystem paths, DSNs or credentials in any field or error message, in any of the above states.
- **Defect list** filed against E07-T05 (contract gaps) or E07-D01 (model gaps), each with severity and owner; re-verified
  after fixes.
- **Frozen baseline handed to E16**: the verified payload sample plus the checklist, committed as the fixture/reference
  that **E16-D04** designs against and **E16-S04** builds against.

## Out of scope
- Any screen, hi-fi, redline, prototype or React code - SCR-142 is designed in **E16-D04** and built in **E16-S04**.
- WCAG 2.2 AA audit of a rendered UI, axe-core runs, screen-reader or keyboard walkthroughs - **E16-Q05** / **E16-D07**;
  there is no rendered UI in E07 to audit.
- Contrast measurement - no visual design exists in this epic.
- Functional/perf testing of the storage tiers themselves - **E07-Q01** (contract/integration suite), **E07-Q03** (perf),
  **E07-Q04** (chaos). This ticket only judges whether the *reported* picture matches reality.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the StorageUsage payload captured from the E07-T05 integration test
When every row of the E07-D01 operator decision list is traced against it
Then each decision is answerable from real fields with correct units, and zero rows are unowned - any exception is a
  recorded, accepted decision

Given a tier is stopped so the API cannot reach QuestDB
When GET /api/v1/recording/storage is called
Then the response reports STORAGE_TIER_UNAVAILABLE for that tier, still returns valid data for the reachable tiers, and
  distinguishes "unreachable" from "reachable but empty"

Given an export whose checksum verification failed
When the payload is inspected
Then STORAGE_EXPORT_VERIFY_FAILED is reported together with a field or text indicating hot data was retained and no data
  was lost, so the state is not indistinguishable from a generic failure

Given free disk is forced below 5 percent
When the payload is inspected
Then the critical state is expressed as a machine-readable enum plus a human text consequence stating that recording
  pauses before trading is affected, and pinned symbols are reported as exempt

Given daily_growth_bytes has insufficient history to project
When projected_full_at is read
Then it is null (or the agreed sentinel) rather than a misleading far-future timestamp, and the response marks the
  projection as an estimate

Given any of the above states
When every string field and error message is scanned
Then no filesystem path, DSN or credential appears anywhere in the payload

Given defects are filed and fixed
When the Architect and CDO re-review
Then sign-off is recorded here, the verified payload sample is frozen as the E16 reference fixture, and E07-D01 is
  confirmed Done
```

## Technical notes / design
Reconciliation runs against captured real responses, never the OpenAPI `example`. Drive the degraded states with the same
harness E07-Q04 builds for chaos (stop the QuestDB container; fill a loopback volume to trip the <15 % / <5 % thresholds;
corrupt a Parquet checksum in the manifest; bump `alembic_version` to fake a pending migration) so this ticket reuses
fixtures instead of inventing them. Commit the verified payload as a JSON fixture under the storage test fixtures so both
the contract test in E07-Q01 and E16's future MSW/mock layer load the same bytes.

## Test plan

- Eight state-forcing scenarios (the list above), each executed manually once and, where cheap, promoted into E07-Q01's

- String-scan test over the payload for `/`-rooted paths and `postgresql://`, `password`, `token` patterns.
- Peer review of the checklist by a second reviewer (Architect or QA lead).

This ticket *is* the leakage control for the storage telemetry surface: it verifies SR-097-spirit path non-disclosure and

## Dependencies

title: QA: black-box test plan and storage contract/integration suite for the three tiers
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires every Story to ship with a QA-authored or QA-reviewed test plan before development starts, and `03-testing-strategy.md` §"test plans" requires it to live inline in the backlog ticket so it travels with the work. E07 has no user-facing story surface, so its QA artifact is a **black-box plan against the storage tier's observable behaviour**: what goes in through the repository API comes out unchanged, at the right tier, with the right dedup, and nothing is ever lost.

`03-testing-strategy.md` §5 defines the integration environment this suite runs in (`docker-compose.test.yml` with QuestDB + Postgres + a fixture-replay mock, `testcontainers-python` for finer-grained suites, **no network egress**) and §5 names the exact scenario this epic must cover end to end: "Recorder: auto-record trigger -> QuestDB write -> retention/pin logic -> Parquet roll-off to cold tier -> DuckDB query of rolled-off data."

## Scope / Deliverables
- The black-box test plan document (`docs/qa/plans/E07-storage.md`), organised by observable behaviour, not by implementation file: write-read fidelity, idempotency, tier routing, lifecycle, safety invariants, failure surfaces.
- The shared **repository contract suite** parametrised over implementations - authored jointly with E07-T01, executed here against real engines: every `MarketDataRepository`, `ColdTierRepository` and UoW method, with the same assertions for the fake and the real implementation.
- Integration suite additions to `docker-compose.test.yml` runs:
  - Fixture replay -> QuestDB -> read back: row counts, value fidelity (no float drift), `ts` ordering, microsecond precision preserved end to end.
  - Dedup/idempotency: replay the same fixture twice and three times; assert stable row counts for every table with a `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` clause.
  - Out-of-order delivery within `o3MaxLag`: shuffled fixture still yields a `ts`-ordered read.
  - Full lifecycle: write -> export -> verify -> drop -> DuckDB read returns the same rows (the §5 scenario).
  - Tier routing: hot-only, cold-only and straddling ranges, using the overlap fixture; assert zero duplicates and zero gaps at the seam.
  - Postgres: migration up/down/up, role privilege matrix, UoW transaction boundaries and savepoints.
- Negative/edge cases: empty range; range entirely in the future; symbol with no data; a single-row partition; a partition spanning a DST-irrelevant but month-boundary edge; `ts` exactly at the hot/cold boundary (boundary-1us / boundary / boundary+1us).
- Golden-file fixtures for each §13.2 query shape's result set, regenerable only via `--update-golden` with a written rationale (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.2).
- CI wiring: the suite runs in the `integration` gate; flaky-test quarantine policy applied.

## Out of scope
- Perf/load measurement - E07-Q03.
- Chaos/failure injection - E07-Q04.
- Security control verification - E07-X02.
- UI testing - no UI in this epic (SCR-142 is designed here, built in E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the black-box plan
When a reviewer cross-references it against E07's tickets
Then every acceptance-criteria scenario in E07-T02, E07-T03, E07-T04 and E07-T05 maps to at least one plan case, and the plan additionally contains cases no ticket listed (negative and edge coverage)

Given the contract suite
When it is run against the fakes and against QuestDB+Postgres+cold
Then it passes unchanged in all cases, proving the abstraction that ADR-0003 depends on

Given one symbol-day fixture replayed through the full lifecycle
When export, verify, drop and a DuckDB read are executed in sequence
Then the DuckDB row count and a checksum over the sorted rows equal the pre-export QuestDB values exactly

Given the overlap fixture spanning the hot/cold boundary
When the router serves a straddling range
Then the merged result has no duplicate natural keys and no missing rows compared to the union of both tiers

Given the same fixture replayed three times
When row counts are compared
Then they are identical after each replay for every dedup-keyed table

Given a test in this suite fails intermittently twice in a week
When the flake policy is applied
Then it is quarantined the same day with a tracking ticket, per 03-testing-strategy.md

Given the suite runs in CI
When the integration gate executes
Then it completes without network egress and within the gate's time budget
```

## Technical notes / design
The suite is parametrised at the fixture level: one `pytest` fixture yields an implementation tuple (`fake`, `real`), and the same test bodies run for both - this is the mechanism that proves the ADR-0003 abstraction rather than asserting it. Heavy cases are marked `@pytest.mark.slow` and excluded from the per-PR gate.

Value-fidelity assertions compare floats with an explicit tolerance of 0 for prices/sizes (they must round-trip exactly through `DOUBLE`) and 1e-9 for derived aggregates; microsecond timestamps are compared as integers, never as datetimes, because a datetime comparison hides a µs truncation bug.

Golden result files are stored per query shape under `packages/fixtures/golden/storage/`; regeneration requires `--update-golden` plus a written rationale in the PR description (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.2).

## Test plan
(This ticket *is* a test plan; this section records how the plan itself is validated.)
- Peer review by the second QA/SDET and by the backend lead.
- Traceability matrix row per E07 ticket AC -> plan case id, committed alongside the plan.
- A deliberate mutation exercise: introduce three seeded defects (drop the dedup clause on one table; off-by-one on the router boundary; skip the row-count verify in export) and confirm the suite catches all three. Any miss is a coverage gap fixed before sign-off.
- Coverage contribution recorded toward the >=85% backend threshold.

## Security notes
Fixtures only; no real Bybit keys or account identifiers, enforced by the CI lint that scans fixture files for real-key-shaped patterns (`03-testing-strategy.md` §11). The integration environment has no network egress. Test databases start empty every run - no shared mutable state across CI runs.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI surface in this epic's engineering scope.

## Performance notes
The suite must stay inside the `integration` gate budget; heavy volume cases (100k bars, full symbol-day) are marked `slow` and run in the nightly job rather than per-PR, per `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Observability
Suite asserts that the metrics E07 promises are actually emitted with the promised label sets (`questdb_write_seconds`, `storage_export_rows_total{stream,result}`, `storage_retention_skipped_total{reason}`) - a metric named in a DoD but never emitted is a defect this suite catches.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Traceability matrix complete; every E07 AC mapped.
