title: Build retention/archive job skeleton and the source_tier=auto query router
body:
## Context
Two mechanisms turn three separate stores into one coherent data tier, and both are E07's responsibility:

1. **The retention/archive job** - `21-database-schema.md` §6 (lifecycle Live -> Hot -> Archive -> Downsample -> Purge, pinning, disk-pressure behaviour) and §7 (the per-stream retention matrix, e.g. `orderbook_deltas` 7 d hot / 180 d raw cold, `trades` 30 d hot / 24 mo cold, pinned = infinite everywhere). `24-internal-schemas.md` specifies the daily job at 03:00 UTC that "never touches pinned data; never deletes a period referenced by an unexported journal trade, a saved replay session or an open investigation", with an emergency pass under disk pressure that "raises a critical alert **before** deleting anything".
2. **The tier router** - `21-database-schema.md` §5.5: "if `range_start >= now() - hot_retention(stream)` -> QuestDB; if fully older -> DuckDB; if straddling -> both, merged by `ts` with dedup on the natural key. The merge is implemented once in `backend/storage/router.py` and contract-tested with an overlap fixture."

This is a **skeleton** in R0 scope: the engine, the safety invariants and the router are real and tested; the operator surface (recorded-symbol management, per-symbol caps, the admin screen) belongs to E16/E42. The threat model E07-X01 must be Done first, because SR-096/SR-099 shape this job's control flow.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `storage/retention/policy.py` - loads `retention_policies` (Postgres, §3.6.3) with the §7 defaults seeded from `backend/db/seeds/retention_defaults.yaml`; most-specific-first evaluation (per-symbol beats global), matching the `/recording/retention-policies` semantics in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- `storage/retention/reaper.py` - the daily job: **dry-run first, always**, producing a report (symbol, stream, range, row count, bytes) before any destructive action; `apply()` executes only what the report listed; every deletion writes an audit entry (SR-099).
- Blocking predicates, each individually tested: pinned symbol (`recorded_symbols.pinned AND removed_at IS NULL`); partition referenced by an active `replay_sessions` row; partition not yet exported+verified to cold (the §5.3 ordering invariant); unexported journal trade in range.
- Disk-pressure behaviour per §6 and SR-096: below 15 % free -> accelerated mode (non-pinned symbols in ascending `recorded_symbols.priority`, effective retention halved, `warning` system event per affected symbol) until free > 25 %; below 5 % free -> ingestion paused for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols with a `critical` event. Alert is raised **before** any deletion.
- Orchestration of E07-T04's exporter: export -> verify -> only then `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION` (QuestDB) / partition-directory delete (cold).
- `storage/router.py` - `source_tier` resolution (`hot | cold | auto`) with the straddle merge: merge by `ts`, dedup on the stream's natural key (the same key as the QuestDB `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` clause), and every response states which tier(s) served it (the `22-api-openapi.yaml` read endpoints declare this - "Each response states which" tier served the window).
- Scheduler registration (03:00 UTC retention, 02:15 UTC export per §5.3, 03:00 Sunday compaction per §5.4) behind a feature flag so it is off by default in dev.

## Out of scope
- Recorded-symbol CRUD, auto-record triggers, per-symbol caps and priorities as a *user-managed* surface - **E16** (M11). This ticket reads `recorded_symbols` and honours it; it does not manage it.
- `GET /api/v1/recording/storage` and `/recording/retention-policies` HTTP endpoints - E16/E42; this ticket produces the `StorageUsage` data shape internally and a unit test asserts it matches the OpenAPI schema.
- Cold-cold downsampling (`action='downsample'`) - E16, per E07-T04's out-of-scope note.
- The SCR-140/SCR-142 screens - E42.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given default retention policies and a symbol with 40 days of trades in QuestDB
When the reaper runs in dry-run mode
Then it reports exactly the partitions older than 30 days, with row counts and byte estimates, and deletes nothing

Given the same state and a pinned symbol
When apply() runs
Then no partition of the pinned symbol is dropped at either tier, and the skip reason "pinned" appears in the report

Given a partition that has not yet been exported and verified to Parquet
When apply() runs
Then the drop is refused with STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_* and the run continues with the remaining partitions rather than aborting wholesale

Given an active replay_sessions row referencing a cold partition
When apply() runs
Then that partition directory is not deleted and the skip is logged with the session id

Given every deletion performed by a run
When the audit log is inspected
Then there is one append-only entry per deletion carrying symbol, stream, time range and freed bytes (SR-099)

Given free disk falls below 15 percent
When the reaper runs
Then it enters accelerated mode, processes non-pinned symbols in ascending priority with halved effective retention, and raises a warning system event per affected symbol BEFORE deleting anything

Given free disk falls below 5 percent
When the guard evaluates
Then recording for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols is paused, a critical event is raised, and the trading path remains functional because it does not share the recording volume (SR-096)

Given a read whose range lies entirely inside the hot window
When the router resolves it
Then it queries QuestDB only, and the response reports tier="hot"

Given a read whose range straddles the hot/cold boundary
When the router resolves it
Then both tiers are queried, results are merged by ts and deduplicated on the natural key with zero duplicate rows at the seam and zero gaps, verified by the overlap fixture, and the response reports tier="both"

Given a read whose range is entirely older than the hot window
When the router resolves it
Then DuckDB serves it and the response reports tier="cold"
```

## Technical notes / design
Reaper control flow, in order (the order is a safety property, not a style choice):
```
plan = policy.resolve(all_streams)            # most-specific-first
plan = plan.exclude(pinned)                   # SR-099
plan = plan.exclude(referenced_by_replay)
plan = plan.exclude(not_exported_or_unverified)   # §5.3 invariant
report = plan.dry_run()                       # persisted, audited
if disk.free_pct < 15: report = report.accelerate()   # alert FIRST
audit.write(report)
for item in report: storage.drop(item); audit.write(deletion(item))
```
Every step is idempotent and resumable - a run killed halfway leaves a consistent state and the next run re-derives the plan from current facts rather than from a cached plan.

Router straddle merge:
```python
async def read(stream, sym, rng, tier="auto"):
    boundary = now_us() - hot_retention_us(stream)
    if tier == "hot" or rng.start >= boundary:   return await hot.read(...)
    if tier == "cold" or rng.end < boundary:     return await cold.read(...)
    hot_rows, cold_rows = await gather(hot.read(...), cold.read(...))
    return dedup_merge(cold_rows, hot_rows, key=NATURAL_KEY[stream])  # hot wins ties
```
Hot wins ties because the hot row is the freshest representation after a dedup upsert. `NATURAL_KEY` is derived from the same constant that generates the QuestDB `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` clause in E07-T03 - one definition, two consumers, asserted equal by a test, so the two can never drift.

Config keys: `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (7), `CV_RECORDER_RETENTION_DAYS` (30), `CV_STORAGE_MIN_FREE_PCT` (15), `CV_STORAGE_CRITICAL_FREE_PCT` (5), `CV_RETENTION_CRON` (`0 3 * * *`), `CV_EXPORT_CRON` (`15 2 * * *`), `CV_COMPACT_CRON` (`0 3 * * 0`), `CV_RETENTION_ENABLED` (false in dev).

Error codes: `STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_BY_PIN`, `STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_UNVERIFIED`, `STORAGE_RETENTION_BLOCKED_REPLAY`, `STORAGE_DISK_CRITICAL`.

## Test plan
- Unit: policy resolution precedence (global vs per-symbol vs pinned); each blocking predicate in isolation and in combination; accelerated-mode ordering by priority; alert-before-delete ordering (a test asserts the event is emitted before any drop call, using a call-order spy); router boundary maths at exactly `now - hot_retention` (inclusive/exclusive off-by-one is the classic bug here - explicit cases at boundary-1us, boundary, boundary+1us).
- Contract: the §5.5 overlap fixture - a dataset deliberately present in *both* tiers for a 10-minute window, asserting the merged output has the same row count as the union-by-natural-key and is `ts`-ordered.
- Integration: full export -> verify -> drop cycle against QuestDB + cold root; dry-run report matches what apply() actually deletes, row for row; pinned symbol survives a full cycle; audit entries present and hash-chain-valid.
- Chaos: E07-Q04 covers kill-mid-drop and disk-full.
- Coverage target: >=85% on `storage/retention/` and `storage/router.py`.

## Security notes
Directly implements threats S2 (disk exhaustion takes trading down - **Critical**) and S5 (retention deletes pinned data) from `04-security-program.md` §5.8, via SR-096 (separate volume, 75 %/90 % thresholds, recorder pauses before trading is affected) and SR-099 (pins honoured, dry-run first, every deletion audited). Retention *policy changes* are a dangerous action requiring the `retention.change` permission with a before/after audit entry (`21-database-schema.md` §7 closing note) - this ticket enforces the permission check at the service boundary even though the screen that calls it is E42's. The reaper runs as a scheduled internal job with no user-supplied paths (SR-097). Requires E07-X01 threat model Done before merge.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. The data shape it produces is what SCR-142 renders (E07-D01); units and per-tier separation in the payload are what let that screen state figures as text.

## Performance notes
Retention reaper: QuestDB `DROP PARTITION` is partition-metadata-only, target <1 s (§13.2 shape #12). The whole nightly export window must complete inside the off-peak window - §11.4 gives >=200 MB/s export, so 13 GB/symbol completes in minutes. The reaper must not contend with ingestion: it runs at 03:00 UTC and yields between partitions, with a test asserting event-loop lag stays within the 50-100 ms threshold (`03-testing-strategy.md` §6) during a run.

## Observability
`storage_retention_runs_total{result}`, `storage_retention_dropped_bytes_total{symbol,stream}`, `storage_retention_skipped_total{reason}`, `storage_disk_free_ratio{volume}`, `storage_router_queries_total{tier}`, `storage_router_merge_rows_total`. `system_events`: warning at <15 % free, critical at <5 %, critical on verify-blocked drops. Audit: one entry per deletion and per policy change. Grafana panel additions handed to E04.

- [ ] Demo: dry-run report, then a real cycle on fixture data, with the audit entries shown.

- `E07-T02` `retention_policies`, `recorded_symbols`, `replay_sessions` table access and the audit writer surface (tables arrive with their owning revisions; where a table is not yet present the code reads an empty set and a test covers that path).
- `E07-X01` threat model.
- Consumed by **E16** (recorder, retention & disk budget) which puts the operator surface on top of this engine.

title: SAST/SCA rules, secret scanning and the P3 vocabulary-leak lint gate
body:
## Context
The planning brief makes SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (Dependabot/pip-audit/npm audit) and secrets scanning non-negotiable, and E03/E04 provide the pipeline. This ticket adds the **E08-specific rules** — the checks that generic scanners cannot know to make, derived directly from the `E08-X01` threat model.

Three of them are architectural invariants that this epic exists to establish and that will silently erode without automation:
1. **P3 — no Bybit field name exists outside `candleviewer/exchange/bybit/`** (`20-architecture.md` §0, `24-internal-schemas.md` C9), described in the architecture as lint-enforced. That lint does not exist yet.
2. **Environment separation** — live and demo transports must be impossible to mix (SR-040a).
3. **Nothing secret reaches logs, metrics or traces** — trivially violated by a well-meaning `logger.debug(response)` on the adapter's hot path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Custom Semgrep rule pack** `tools/semgrep/e08/`:
  - `bybit-vocabulary-leak`: flags Bybit-native identifiers (`retCode`, `retMsg`, `X-BAPI-*`, `publicTrade`, `orderbook.200`, `tickers`, `category`, `recvWindow`, `confirm`, `qtyStep`, `tickSize`, `lotSizeFilter`, …) appearing in any path outside `services/api/candleviewer/exchange/bybit/` and the fixture/test directories; a maintained allow-list with justification is the only escape.
  - `exchange-base-url-mutation`: flags assignment to or mutation of a client base URL / host attribute outside construction, enforcing SR-040a's one-client-per-environment rule.
  - `raw-response-logging`: flags logging, metric-labelling or span-attributing a raw exchange response, request headers, or any variable named like a key/secret/signature.
  - `unbounded-read`: flags reading a response body or WS frame without a size bound in the adapter and ingestion packages.
  - `broad-except-on-ingest`: flags bare `except Exception: pass`-shaped handlers on the ingestion hot path, which is how a validation failure becomes a silent wrong-data bug.
  - `decimal-discipline`: flags `float` used for price or quantity in the adapter, ingestion and policy modules (a correctness rule with security consequences for order validation).
- **Bandit/CodeQL configuration** scoped to the new packages with the relevant rule families enabled and a documented, ticket-linked suppression policy (no bare `# nosec`).
- **Secret scanning extension**: patterns for Bybit API keys, HMAC signatures and `X-BAPI-*` headers added to the repo scanner and to the **fixture pre-commit check**, so a captured fixture containing credentials cannot be committed.
- **SCA scope**: the ingestion dependency set (WS client, JSON parser, HTTP client, `Decimal`/numeric libs) pinned, hash-verified where the toolchain supports it, and subscribed to advisories; a fast-parser CVE must reach the E08 owner, not a generic queue.
- **DAST note**: E08 exposes only read-only `/market/*` and `/instruments*` endpoints; these are added to the ZAP scan scope configured in E03/E04, with the authenticated context and the expected 4xx contract documented so the scan produces signal rather than noise.
- **CI wiring**: all of the above run on PRs touching `exchange/`, `ingestion/`, `bus/` and `packages/fixtures/`, blocking on new findings while grandfathering a documented baseline.

## Out of scope
- Building the CI/scanner platform itself (E03 supply chain, E04 pipeline) — this ticket contributes rules and scope to it.
- Auth/RBAC-specific rules (`E09-X03`), key-vault rules (E27), order-path rules (E29).
- The external pen-test (pre-R4) and the runtime abuse suite (`E08-X02`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A vocabulary leak fails the build
  Given a branch that references retCode in a module outside exchange/bybit/
  When CI runs the Semgrep pack
  Then the build fails naming the file, line and rule
  And adding an allow-list entry requires a justification comment and a linked ticket

Scenario: Raw response logging is caught before review
  Given a branch adding logger.info with the raw exchange response object
  When the raw-response-logging rule runs
  Then the finding is reported as an error, not a warning
  And the rule also catches the same object used as a metric label or span attribute

Scenario: Failure case - a credential-bearing fixture cannot be committed
  Given a captured fixture containing an X-BAPI-API-KEY header
  When the fixture pre-commit check and the CI secret scan run
  Then the commit is rejected locally and the CI job fails if bypassed
  And the failure message names the file and the matched pattern class, not the secret value

Scenario: Edge case - suppressions are governed, not free
  Given a developer adds a suppression to silence a finding
  When CI evaluates suppressions
  Then a suppression without a justification and a linked ticket fails the build
  And the suppression inventory is reported in the job summary

Scenario: Rules do not drown the team in noise
  Given the pack runs across the existing codebase at baseline
  When the findings are reviewed
  Then the false-positive rate is recorded and each noisy rule is either tightened or downgraded with a reason
  And a baseline file grandfathers pre-existing findings so only new ones block
```

## Technical notes / design
- Rules are written as Semgrep YAML with **unit tests** (positive and negative samples) under `tools/semgrep/e08/tests/`, so a rule that silently stops matching is itself caught — an untested lint rule is worse than none.
- `bybit-vocabulary-leak` uses an explicit identifier list rather than a heuristic, and the list is co-located with the adapter so adding a new Bybit field forces a conscious decision about the lint.
- The baseline file is dated and reviewed; it is a migration aid, not a permanent amnesty, and a Chore tracks draining it.
- Scanner scope is expressed by path so future exchange adapters inherit the same rules automatically.

## Test plan
- Rule unit tests: each rule has ≥2 true-positive and ≥2 true-negative samples, run in CI.
- End-to-end verification: open a scratch PR containing one deliberate violation per rule and confirm each is caught with a readable message; record the PR link on the ticket.
- Secret-scan verification: plant a synthetic key matching each pattern class, confirm detection, then confirm it never appears in the failure output.

## Security notes
- This ticket converts three `E08-X01` mitigations from claims into enforced gates; the threat model is updated to reference the rule ids as the enforcing controls.
- Suppression policy is explicit: justification comment + linked ticket + expiry review; blanket `# nosec` / `nosemgrep` without those fails CI.
- Scanner output may itself contain sensitive snippets; job artifacts are access-controlled and the failure messages print pattern classes rather than matched values.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A — CI tooling with no UI surface. Stated explicitly per the DoR rule on justified N/A.

## Performance notes
- The rule pack's CI runtime is measured and budgeted to ≤60 s on the touched-path subset so it can block PRs without slowing the loop; the full-repo run is nightly.

## Observability
- Findings are summarised in the PR job summary with counts by rule and severity, and trended over time so an increase in suppressions is visible rather than buried.
- The suppression inventory is published as a build artifact for the R0 security review.

## Definition of Done
- Semgrep pack merged with rule unit tests green; Bandit/CodeQL scoped; secret patterns and fixture pre-commit check live.
- Scratch-PR verification recorded (one deliberate violation per rule, each caught).
- Baseline file committed and dated; drain Chore filed.
- ZAP scope updated for `/market/*` and `/instruments*` with documented expectations.
- `E08-X01` updated to reference the rule ids as enforcing controls; Security engineer sign-off comment posted.

## Dependencies
- `E08-X01` (threats to enforce), `E08-T01` (package layout and vocabulary to lint against), E03/E04 (scanner platform, secret-pattern set, CI).

## Branch
`chore/e08-sast-rules`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (SAST/SCA/secrets/DAST programme, suppression policy)
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §0 principle P3
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` C9, §14.2
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §7 (required checks)
- `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (SDLC non-negotiables)


## Agent execution brief

1. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (SAST/SCA/secrets/DAST programme, suppression policy)
2. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §0 principle P3
3. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` C9, §14.2

5. `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (SDLC non-negotiables)

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm verify`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e08-sast-rules`
- PR title: "E08-X03: SAST/SCA rules, secret scanning and the P3 vocabulary-leak lint gate"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/devsecops
- Labels: type/security, area/ingestion, priority/p1, security

title: Black-box test plan for the E09 auth, session and RBAC story groups
body:
## Context
E09 ships the controls that every later epic assumes: password sign-in, mandatory TOTP, opaque server-side sessions, step-up re-authentication, deny-by-default RBAC and a tamper-evident audit log. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 and §8 make a recorded black-box QA sign-off non-skippable for every Story here, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 requires a written test plan per feature plus a white-box review checklist. Nothing in that plan exists yet: the story tickets each state *what* to build, but there is no single artefact a QA engineer can execute end-to-end against a staging build to say "authentication behaves as specified".

This ticket produces that artefact — a black-box test plan organised by story group, traced to `US-ONB-001..010` and to the security requirements `SR-010..SR-029`, `SR-050`, `SR-051` in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.3–6.4. It is deliberately black-box: written against the screens (`SCR-001..006`, `SCR-017`, `SCR-019`, `SCR-111`, `SCR-112`, `SCR-123`, `SCR-154`) and the public REST/WS contract, with no knowledge of internal helpers, so it stays valid if the implementation is refactored.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e09-auth-rbac-test-plan.md` with five executable sections, one per story group:
  1. **Sign-in & second factor** (US-ONB-001, US-ONB-002) — `SCR-001`, `SCR-002`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/mfa/verify`, `POST /auth/mfa/recovery`.
  2. **Enrolment, recovery codes & forced password change** (US-ONB-003) — `SCR-003`, `SCR-004`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `PUT /auth/password`.
  3. **Session lifetime, idle lock & step-up** (US-ONB-004, US-ONB-005) — `SCR-005`, `SCR-006`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `POST /auth/step-up`, `GET /auth/session`.
  4. **Sessions list, sign-out everywhere & TOTP reset** (US-ONB-009, US-ONB-010) — `SCR-111`, `SCR-112`, `GET /auth/sessions`, `POST /auth/logout`, `DELETE /auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`.
  5. **Invite, onboarding & permission denial** (US-ONB-006, US-ONB-007, US-ONB-008) — `SCR-017`, `SCR-019`, `SCR-123`, `SCR-154`, `GET /invites/{inviteToken}`, `GET|POST /users`, `GET /onboarding/checklist`, `POST /onboarding/complete`.
- Per case: id (`E09-TC-<group><nn>`), preconditions (seeded fixture user + role), steps, expected result, the `US-ONB-*` / `SR-*` id it verifies, the child ticket it covers, and whether it is automated (`E09-Q02`/`E09-Q03`) or manual-only.
- A **test data & fixture appendix**: seeded owner, manager-with-grants, manager-without-grants, viewer, disabled user, invited-but-not-onboarded user; a deterministic TOTP secret so codes can be generated in test; a frozen-clock helper for skew/expiry cases.
- A **traceability table** US-ONB-001..010 × test cases × automation status, mirroring `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` conventions, proving no story is untested.
- **Negative/abuse-adjacent cases owned by QA** (the deeper ones live in `E09-X02`): unknown-user vs wrong-password indistinguishability, TOTP replay, recovery-code reuse, expired MFA challenge, session cookie stripped/edited, role change mid-session.
- Defect-reporting conventions for this epic: severity mapping per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3, with anything that grants access without a completed factor filed as `priority/p0-critical` by definition.

## Out of scope
- Writing the Playwright automation itself (`E09-Q02`) and the RBAC matrix pack (`E09-Q03`).
- Accessibility auditing (`E09-Q04`), performance/chaos (`E09-Q05`), exploratory charters (`E09-Q06`).
- Security-owned artefacts: STRIDE model (`E09-X01`), abuse cases (`E09-X02`), SAST/DAST rules (`E09-X03`).
- Admin user-management beyond `SCR-123` invite (E42) and key-vault flows (E27).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every ONB story is covered by at least one executable case
  Given the test plan is merged at qa/plans/e09-auth-rbac-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against US-ONB-001..010
  Then every story id maps to at least one test case with steps and an expected result
  And every case names the SR-* requirement or child ticket it verifies

Scenario: A plan case is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer with only a staging URL and the seeded fixture set
  When they execute group 3 (session lifetime, idle lock, step-up) without asking the author a question
  Then every step resolves to an unambiguous observable outcome
  And any step that needs a clock or TOTP helper names the exact helper and its invocation

Scenario: Failure case - indistinguishable login errors
  Given a request for an unknown user and a request with a wrong password for a known user
  When both are executed per case E09-TC-A07
  Then the plan requires body, status code and response-time band to be compared
  And a measurable difference is recorded as a P1 defect against SR-014

Scenario: Edge case - role change while a session is live
  Given a manager is signed in and viewing an account-scoped screen
  When the owner revokes the manager's grant per case E09-TC-D05
  Then the plan requires the next request to return 403, the WS connection to receive a revoked frame, and the session id to have rotated
  And no cached client state is accepted as evidence of continued access

Scenario: Plan stays honest when a case cannot be automated
  Given a case that depends on a 7-day absolute session lifetime
  When the plan marks it manual-only
  Then it records the time-travel technique to be used and a follow-up ticket reference to automate it later
```

## Technical notes / design
Write the plan against the contract, not the code: every expectation must be phrased in terms of an HTTP status/body from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, a WS frame from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4/§9.5, a visible screen state from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, or an `audit_log` row. Where `14-screens-catalogue.md` enumerates states (e.g. `SCR-002`: idle · verifying · invalid code · expired challenge · locked after 5 tries), each state gets its own case — state coverage is the structural backbone of the plan.

Fixtures are seeded through the same migrations/seed path used by CI (`E09-T01`), never by hand-editing Postgres, so the plan is runnable on an ephemeral docker-compose environment and on staging identically. The deterministic TOTP secret lives in the test fixture set only and is documented as such; it must never appear in a non-test seed.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan, so its own verification is a dry run: execute the full plan once against the Sprint 03 staging build, record pass/fail per case, and file defects found. A plan that passes 100% on first execution is treated as suspicious — at least the negative cases must have been genuinely attempted, evidenced by screenshots/HAR snippets attached to the run record.

## Security notes
The plan itself contains security-relevant expectations (SR-014 uniform errors, SR-021 TOTP replay, SR-022 recovery-code single use, SR-013 rotation). It must not contain real secrets: only fixture credentials, clearly labelled. Any defect that implies an authentication bypass, privilege escalation or credential disclosure is routed to the Security engineer the same day and is a release blocker for R0.

Each manual case notes whether it must also be executable keyboard-only; the deep a11y audit is `E09-Q04`, but a case whose steps are impossible without a mouse is itself a defect against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 and is filed as such.

## Performance notes
Cases record wall-clock observations where the screen catalogue states a budget (`SCR-002` TOTP verify ≤400 ms p95, `SCR-006` step-up issue ≤400 ms p95, `GET /auth/session` ≤100 ms p95) as smoke-level sanity only; the measured budget run is `E09-Q05`.

title: Password sign-in with lockout and uniform failures (US-ONB-001)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-001 (Must): *"As a user, I want to sign in with an email/username and password over Tailscale, so that only invited people reach the terminal."* This is the first leg of the two-legged login defined in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` — `POST /auth/login` returns an `mfa_required` challenge (`mfa_token`, `methods`) rather than a session when MFA is enrolled, and `POST /auth/mfa/verify` (E09-S02) completes it. The story covers the backend credential check and SCR-001 Login end to end, including the states the screen catalogue enumerates: idle, submitting, invalid credentials, disabled account, locked, and server-unreachable.

The NFRs are security-critical and explicit in the story: Argon2id hashing, per-account **and** per-IP rate limiting (5 failures → 15 min lockout), constant-time comparison, and **no user enumeration** — the same message and the same timing whether the username is unknown, the password wrong, or the account disabled is revealed only after correct credentials.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `POST /auth/login` per `22-api-openapi.yaml`: accepts username/email + password; returns `status=mfa_required` with an opaque `mfa_token` when an MFA method is enrolled, or a full `TokenBundle` plus the `cv_refresh` cookie when it is not (viewer without optional MFA, per `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1).
- Argon2id verification with the parameters stored per user in `users.password_algo_params` (`m=65536,t=3,p=4` default), a per-user pepper derived from the KEK-held secret, constant-time comparison, and transparent rehash-on-login when parameters change.
- Lockout: increment `users.failed_login_count`, set `users.locked_until` after 5 failures for 15 minutes; independent per-IP throttle so one attacker cannot lock every account; both counters reset on success.
- `PUT /auth/password` and **SCR-004 Forced password change** when `users.status = 'invited'` or a reset was issued — CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-202 PasswordStrengthMeter, CMP-203 RequirementChecklist.
- **SCR-001 Login** in `apps/web`: CMP-200 AuthCard, CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-005, CMP-007, CMP-027, CMP-075, CMP-207 BuildFooter; states idle / submitting / invalid / disabled / locked (with remaining time) / server-unreachable (E17's SCR-152 inline variant).
- Audit emissions via E09-T02: `auth.login_succeeded`, `auth.login_failed` (with source IP and reason, severity warning), `auth.account_locked` (severity warning), `auth.login_blocked_disabled`.

## Out of scope
- The TOTP challenge screen and code verification — **E09-S02**.
- Session lifetime, idle lock and revocation semantics — **E09-S03**.
- Invite redemption — **E09-S05**.
- Password reset by the owner and self-service recovery beyond recovery codes (owner resets are E42/E09-S04 territory).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Successful sign-in advances to the second factor
  Given I am a registered, enabled user reaching the app over Tailscale
  When I submit my correct username and password
  Then the response is status mfa_required with an mfa_token and the enrolled methods, no session cookie is set, and auth.login_succeeded is audited

Scenario: Wrong password gives no hint and is audited
  Given I am a registered user
  When I submit an incorrect password
  Then I see "Username or password is incorrect" with no indication of which was wrong
  And the attempt is audited with the source IP

Scenario: Disabled account
  Given my account has been disabled by the owner
  When I submit correct credentials
  Then I see "Account disabled - contact the owner" and no session and no mfa_token are created

Scenario: Lockout after five failures
  Given I have failed five times within the window
  When I submit even the correct password
  Then I am refused for 15 minutes, the remaining time is shown, and auth.account_locked is audited

Scenario: Unknown user is indistinguishable from a wrong password
  Given a username that does not exist
  When I submit any password
  Then the message, the HTTP status and the response time distribution match the wrong-password case within the agreed tolerance

Scenario: Keyboard and screen reader
  Given I navigate the login form with the keyboard only
  Then every control is reachable, errors are programmatically associated with their field and announced via aria-live, and focus moves to the error summary on failure
```

## Technical notes / design
Enumeration resistance is implemented by always performing an Argon2id verification — against a fixed dummy hash when the user does not exist — so the timing profile is flat; the disabled-account message is returned only when the password actually verified, which is a deliberate, documented trade-off (the user already proved knowledge of the secret). Rate limiting uses a token bucket keyed on both `user_id` and source address, held in-process (single-process deployment per `20-architecture.md` C4) with the counters additionally persisted on `users` so a restart does not clear a lockout. The `mfa_token` is single-use, bound to the source address, and expires in 5 minutes (`mfa_challenges` row with `purpose='login'`).

## Test plan
Unit: Argon2id verify/rehash, pepper handling, token-bucket edge cases, lockout arithmetic across restarts. Contract: `/auth/login` request/response against `22-api-openapi.yaml`, including the 401 shape. Integration: real Postgres, lockout persistence, audit rows written with the right severity. E2E (Playwright): all six SCR-001 states, forced password change on an invited user. Security: timing-difference test over 1000 samples for unknown vs wrong-password; enumeration attempt via response-shape diffing. a11y: axe-core on SCR-001 and SCR-004 plus a manual screen-reader pass. Load: k6 login profile asserting throttle behaviour and that Argon2id cost does not exhaust the worker pool.

## Security notes
Threats: credential stuffing (per-IP and per-account throttling, lockout), user enumeration (uniform messaging and timing), offline cracking if the database leaks (Argon2id with tuned parameters plus pepper outside the database), pepper compromise (KEK handling per `04-security-program.md`), and denial of service by locking out a known username (per-IP limiter is separate, and the owner can always be unlocked from the admin path in E42). Passwords are never logged, never echoed, and never placed in an error message or audit `before_state`. Data classification: credentials SECRET, source IP PII.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-001 per `05-accessibility-standard.md`: single `h1`, labelled inputs with `autocomplete="username"`/`"current-password"`, error summary focused on submit with `role="alert"`, lockout countdown announced politely and not by colour alone, password-reveal control labelled and keyboard operable, contrast ≥ 4.5:1, visible focus ring on every control, and CMP-202's strength meter exposing its level as text.

## Performance notes
Argon2id parameters tuned so a single verification is ~150 ms on the target host and concurrency is bounded so a burst of logins cannot starve market-data handling — verification runs in a dedicated thread pool. Endpoint p99 target < 400 ms including hashing under the k6 login profile of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
`auth_login_attempts_total{outcome}`, `auth_login_duration_seconds` histogram, `auth_lockouts_total`, `auth_argon2_pool_saturation`. Alert on a spike in failures from a single source and on any lockout of the owner account.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2: all Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests, coverage ≥85% backend / ≥80% frontend, OpenAPI matches implementation, axe-core green plus manual screen-reader pass, design-qa comparison against the SCR-001 spec, Security engineer review with the abuse cases exercised, QA sign-off, demoed at Sprint Review, feature-flag state recorded (none — auth is always on).

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-T01** (tables), **E09-T02** (audit writer), **E09-T04** (off-mesh requests must already be refused before a login form is exposed). Design for SCR-001/SCR-004 must be Done per the design-ahead rule.

`feat/e09-password-signin`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-001; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.1; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-001, SCR-004; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-200, CMP-201, CMP-202, CMP-203, CMP-207; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/auth/login`, `/auth/password`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.1, §3.1.5; `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10 `PasswordAuth`; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

title: TOTP second factor, enrolment and recovery codes (US-ONB-002/003)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-002 (Must) and US-ONB-003 (Must) together make the second factor real: an app-level TOTP independent of Bybit's, plus first-login enrolment with ten single-use recovery codes so a lost authenticator is recoverable without the owner minting passwords. `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1 makes MFA **mandatory for owner and manager** and optional for viewer. The schema exists (`mfa_methods` with envelope-encrypted `secret_enc` + `secret_key_ref`, `mfa_challenges` with `purpose`, `recovery_codes` hashed) and the endpoints are specified: `POST /auth/mfa/verify`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll`, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll/confirm`, `POST /auth/mfa/recovery`, `DELETE /auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`.

The two stories are one deliverable because enrolment and verification share the secret handling, the replay window and the screens (SCR-002 challenge, SCR-003 enrolment, SCR-112 security settings); splitting them would ship a factor nobody can enrol or an enrolment nothing verifies.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Verification** `POST /auth/mfa/verify`: exchanges `mfa_token` + TOTP code (or a recovery code) for a session. RFC 6238, SHA-1, 6 digits, 30 s step, ±1 step skew, **replay-protected** — a code accepted within a time step cannot be reused, tracked per `(method_id, time_step)`.
- **Enrolment** `POST /auth/mfa/enroll` returning the `otpauth://` URI and a displayable text secret, `POST /auth/mfa/enroll/confirm` requiring one valid code before `mfa_methods.confirmed_at` is set; the method stays `pending` until confirmed.
- **Recovery codes**: 10 single-use codes generated at enrolment, shown exactly once with copy and download, stored only as `sha256_hex` in `recovery_codes`; consuming one signs the user in, marks `used_at`, and **forces re-enrolment of TOTP**; exhaustion returns a message directing the user to the owner (US-ONB-010 path). `POST /auth/mfa/recovery` regenerates codes, hard-deleting unused ones and auditing `auth.recovery_codes_regenerated`.
- **Secret handling**: the TOTP seed is envelope-encrypted at rest (`secret_enc`, `secret_key_ref`) using the KEK path from `04-security-program.md`; it is returned to the client exactly once during enrolment and never again — `GET` on a method never exposes it.
- **Screens**: SCR-002 Two-factor challenge (CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-200 AuthCard) with states idle / verifying / invalid / expired-challenge (returns to SCR-001) / locked after 5 tries; SCR-003 TOTP enrolment (CMP-205 QrCode, CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList, CMP-203 RequirementChecklist); SCR-112 Security settings showing enrolled methods, remaining recovery-code count and regeneration.
- Audit: `auth.mfa_verified`, `auth.mfa_failed` (reason: invalid / reused / expired), `auth.mfa_enrolled`, `auth.recovery_code_used` (severity warning), `auth.recovery_codes_exhausted` (severity error).

## Out of scope
- WebAuthn/passkeys — columns exist in `mfa_methods`, flows are reserved for SCR-007..009 in a later Epic.
- Step-up re-authentication using an already-enrolled factor — **E09-S04**.
- Owner-initiated TOTP reset — **E09-S04**.
- SMS or email factors — never in scope for this product.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Valid code creates a session
  Given I have completed the password step and enrolled TOTP
  When I enter the current 6-digit code
  Then a session is created and I land on my default workspace

Scenario: Reused code is rejected
  Given I have just used code 123456 successfully
  When I attempt to sign in again with 123456 inside the same time step
  Then the code is rejected as already used and auth.mfa_failed records reason reused

Scenario: Clock drift within one step is tolerated
  Given my authenticator is 25 seconds ahead
  When I enter the code it shows
  Then it is accepted within the plus or minus one time-step window

Scenario: First-login enrolment
  Given I sign in for the first time with a valid invite
  When I scan the QR code and confirm one valid code
  Then TOTP is enabled and 10 single-use recovery codes are displayed once

Scenario: Recovery code use forces re-enrolment
  Given I have lost my authenticator
  When I sign in using an unused recovery code
  Then I am signed in, that code is consumed, and I am forced to re-enrol TOTP before reaching the workspace

Scenario: Recovery codes exhausted
  Given all 10 recovery codes are consumed
  When I attempt recovery
  Then I am told to contact the owner and no session is created

Scenario: Codes never appear in logs
  Given any of the above flows runs with debug logging enabled
  When the logs and audit entries are searched
  Then no TOTP code, seed, otpauth URI or recovery code appears anywhere

Scenario: Screen-reader enrolment without a camera
  Given I use a screen reader and cannot scan a QR code
  Then the equivalent text secret is exposed as selectable text with a labelled copy control and the same enrolment completes by keyboard only
```

## Technical notes / design
Replay protection stores the last accepted `time_step` per method and rejects any step less than or equal to it, which also closes the ±1-window replay hole that a naive implementation leaves open. Challenge state lives in `mfa_challenges` (`purpose='login'|'enroll'|'step_up'`, `attempts` capped at 5, `expires_at` 5 min); five failed attempts abandon the challenge and return the user to SCR-001. Recovery-code verification is constant-time against the hashed set and is rate-limited identically to passwords. Codes are generated from `secrets.token_bytes` with an unambiguous alphabet (no 0/O/1/l) and are grouped for readability.

## Test plan
Unit: RFC 6238 vector tests, skew boundary tests at ±1 and ±2 steps, replay rejection, recovery-code hashing and single use, envelope encrypt/decrypt round trip. Contract: all five endpoints against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: enrolment → confirm → verify → recovery → forced re-enrolment on real Postgres with audit assertions. E2E: SCR-002 and SCR-003 including the expired-challenge and locked states, and download/copy of recovery codes. Security: log-scrape test asserting no secret material; brute-force test on the 6-digit space asserting the attempt cap holds. a11y: axe-core on SCR-002, SCR-003, SCR-112 plus a manual screen-reader pass on enrolment.

## Security notes
Threats: seed exfiltration (envelope encryption, never re-displayed, never logged), code replay (per-step tracking), brute force (5-attempt challenge cap plus per-IP throttle — the 6-digit space is small, so the cap is the control), recovery-code theft (hashed at rest, single use, shown once), and enrolment hijack (confirm requires a valid code from the same authenticated challenge). Mandatory-MFA invariant: the last remaining method cannot be deleted while `users.mfa_required` is set, enforced server-side on `DELETE /auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`, which additionally requires the `X-Reauth-Password` header per the OpenAPI contract.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-204 OtpInput must behave as a single labelled field for assistive technology (not six unlabelled boxes), accept paste of a full code, announce validation errors via `aria-live`, and never rely on a time limit the user cannot see; the 30 s expiry is surfaced as text. CMP-205 QrCode carries an `alt` description and is always accompanied by the text secret. CMP-206 RecoveryCodeList is a semantic list with a copy-all and download control, both labelled, and warns that the codes will not be shown again.

## Performance notes
TOTP verification is pure computation — p99 < 5 ms excluding the session write; envelope decryption of the seed is cached per request only, never across requests. Endpoint p99 < 150 ms.

## Observability
`auth_mfa_verifications_total{method,outcome}`, `auth_mfa_failures_total{reason}`, `auth_recovery_codes_remaining` gauge per user (exported as a low-cardinality histogram), `auth_mfa_enrollments_total`. Alerts: recovery-code exhaustion, and a burst of `reason=invalid` indicating brute force.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, with explicit Security engineer sign-off (this Story is default-on for the `security` label), design-qa against SCR-002/SCR-003, manual screen-reader pass recorded, and QA sign-off on the recovery-code lifecycle including exhaustion.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S01** (the password leg produces the `mfa_token` this Story consumes).

## Branch
`feat/e09-totp-mfa`

## References

title: Session lifetime, idle lock and sign-out everywhere (US-ONB-004/009)
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** Session lifetime is B16 `session` built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` via the factory (`statechart/factory.py`); idle-lock and absolute-expiry are coarse `after:` timers in `machines/B16.session.machine.json` (BENCH-6 p99 55-92 ms is acceptable here, C-04 hoists revocation onto the root so it fires from every substate). No hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime: `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/bindings/b16_session.py` is the only place idle/absolute/revocation logic lives.

US-ONB-004 (Must) and US-ONB-009 (Should) define what a session *is* in this product: 12 h absolute lifetime, a configurable 5–60 min idle lock that re-auths without tearing down the WebSocket, and server-side revocation of any session within 5 seconds. The requirement that the lock "must not tear down WS subscriptions (reconnect storms)" and that "live data keeps streaming underneath" makes this a joint auth/transport Story: it implements the in-place re-auth contract of `23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3 and the mid-connection revocation frames of §9.5 on the auth side. The token and rotation model was decided in E09-K01.

A second safety requirement sits here: on absolute expiry "any armed one-click trading is disarmed", and on sign-out-everywhere "any armed rules owned by me continue running server-side" — the rule runtime is deliberately independent of UI sessions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1`: `machines/B16.session.machine.json` (states `active` / `idle_locked` / `expired`; `after:` timers for the idle deadline and the 12h absolute lifetime; `REVOKE` arm on the root per C-04) plus `bindings/b16_session.py` (guards: `is_within_absolute_lifetime`; actions: `disarm_one_click`, `clear_ws_resubscribe_flag`; no services needed for the timer path).
- `POST /auth/refresh` with rotation: every refresh issues a new `sessions` row, marks the old `revoked_reason='rotated'`, links them in `sessions_rotation`; presenting an already-rotated refresh token revokes the **entire family** transitively and writes `auth.refresh_reuse_detected` at severity critical.
- `GET /auth/session` (introspection: identity, roles, permissions, account scope, expiry timestamps), `GET /auth/sessions` (list: device label, shell Electron/browser, first seen, last seen, source address), `POST /auth/logout` (current session), and sign-out-everywhere revoking all sessions of the user including the current one.
- **Idle lock**: `sessions.last_seen_at` drives an idle deadline (per-user configurable 5–60 min, default 15); on expiry the client shows **SCR-005** re-auth overlay, order entry is disabled server-side for that session, one-click arming is cleared, and the WS connection and all subscriptions are **preserved**. Unlock requires the password only (not TOTP) while inside the absolute lifetime.
- **Absolute expiry** at 12 h: full sign-out, WS `bye` with `token_expired` and close `4401`, armed one-click trading disarmed.
- **Revocation propagation**: a revoked session's next REST request is refused and the WS connection receives a revocation frame and closes within 5 s, per `23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5.
- Frontend: SCR-005 session-expired/re-auth modal, SCR-112 Security settings session list with per-session revoke and "Sign out everywhere", state restoration to exactly the same workspace and scroll position after unlock.
- Audit: `auth.session_created`, `auth.session_refreshed`, `auth.session_revoked{reason}`, `auth.refresh_reuse_detected` (critical), `auth.idle_locked`.

## Out of scope
- Step-up elevation for dangerous actions — **E09-S04**.
- The WS transport implementation itself (framing, backpressure, revocation frame plumbing) — **E17**; this Story defines and calls the auth-side contract and tests against E17's client where available, with a stub otherwise.
- Workspace persistence mechanics — **E10**/layouts Epic; this Story only asserts restoration behaviour.
- Rule-runtime independence is asserted, not implemented (rules land in E35+).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Idle lock preserves the data feed
  Given my idle timeout is 15 minutes
  When I do not interact for 15 minutes
  Then the UI locks to a re-auth overlay, the WebSocket stays open with its subscriptions intact, and no re-snapshot is requested

Scenario: Unlock restores context
  Given the screen is locked
  When I enter my password
  Then I return to exactly the same workspace and scroll position and TOTP is not requested

Scenario: Absolute expiry disarms trading
  Given my session is older than 12 hours
  When it expires
  Then I am fully signed out, one-click trading is disarmed, and the socket closes with code 4401 and reason token_expired

Scenario: Order entry is refused while locked
  Given my session is idle-locked
  When an order submission is attempted with that session's token
  Then the server refuses it regardless of what the client believes

Scenario: Revoke one session
  Given two active sessions
  When I revoke the other one from Settings, Sessions
  Then that client is disconnected within 5 seconds and must re-authenticate, and my own session is unaffected

Scenario: Refresh-token reuse kills the family
  Given a refresh token that has already been rotated
  When it is presented again
  Then every session in its rotation family is revoked and auth.refresh_reuse_detected is audited at severity critical

Scenario: Sign out everywhere leaves server-side rules running
  Given I own an armed rule
  When I sign out everywhere
  Then all my sessions end and the rule continues to run server-side
```

## Technical notes / design
Session lifecycle state (`active`, `idle_locked`, `expired`) is published by `statechart/factory.build("B16", ...)`/`restore(...)`; the interpreter is the single source of truth read by the auth decision point (E09-T03) and by the WS gateway (`E17-T08`). `machine_hash` for B16 is locked in `machines/machine_hashes.lock`. Snapshot recipe: quiescent HMAC-enveloped blob on every `sessions` row write, restored on process start via `statechart.restore("B16", blob, clock=..., lane="platform")`. `CV-LINT-IMPORT` keeps every import of `xstate_statemachine` out of this module; only `factory.py`/`persistence.py` import it.

Revocation is checked **per request and per WS frame batch**, not only at issue, so the 5 s requirement is met without polling: a revoked session id is published on the internal bus, the gateway drops the matching connection immediately, and the per-request check is the backstop. Idle state is a property of the session row, not the browser, so closing and reopening a tab cannot reset it. The lock does not refresh tokens in the background — if the absolute lifetime elapses while locked, unlocking fails and becomes a full sign-in. One-click arming is server-side state on the session, cleared on lock and on expiry, so a stale client cannot submit with it.

## Test plan
Contract: `tests/xstate_contract/test_b16.py` asserts all B16 states/events, snapshot round-trip at every quiescence point, and the mandatory-config block (`strict_config`, `strictTargets`, `actionErrorPolicy`, `guardErrorPolicy`, `onUnhandled`) per `79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7. Unit: idle/absolute deadline arithmetic across clock changes, rotation-family walk, revocation set. Contract: `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/session`, `/auth/sessions`, `/auth/logout` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; WS `auth`/`auth_ok`/revocation frames against `23-ws-protocol.md` §13–15 schemas. Integration: reuse-detection family revocation; locked-session order refusal; restart mid-session. E2E: lock/unlock with a live subscription asserting no re-snapshot (network assertion on frame counts), revoke-other-session within 5 s, absolute expiry disarming one-click. Chaos: WS disconnect during lock, clock jump after WSL resume. a11y: axe-core on SCR-005 and SCR-112 plus a manual pass on the modal focus trap.

## Security notes
Threats: session fixation (new session id issued on every authentication and every refresh), token replay (rotation with family revocation), CSRF on refresh (SameSite=Strict cookie plus origin check), revocation lag (bus-driven immediate drop), and the idle lock being bypassed by a modified client (server-side enforcement — the client lock is cosmetic). The session list exposes IP and user-agent, which are PII shown only to the owning user and the owner role. Refresh tokens are stored only as `sha256_hex`.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-005 is a modal dialog with a proper focus trap, `aria-modal`, an accessible name, focus returned to the prior element on unlock, and an assertive announcement when the lock engages so a screen-reader user is not left typing into a dead UI. The session list is a table with row headers, an explicit "revoke" action name per row (not a bare icon), and a confirmation for "Sign out everywhere" that states the consequence in text.

## Performance notes
Per-request revocation check must add < 1 ms p99 (in-process set, invalidated by bus events). Refresh cadence per the E09-K01 decision keeps WS re-auth to at most one frame per connection per 10 minutes; the lock must generate **zero** re-subscribe traffic — asserted by counting frames in the E2E test, per the reconnect-storm concern in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
`auth_sessions_active`, `auth_session_revocations_total{reason}`, `auth_refresh_total`, `auth_refresh_reuse_total`, `auth_idle_locks_total`, `auth_revocation_latency_seconds` histogram. Alerts on any refresh-reuse detection and on revocation latency above 5 s.

## Definition of Done
B16 contract test green in the blocking gate (`E50-T31`); `CV-LINT-IMPORT` and `CV-LINT-HOTPATH` clean. Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, plus perf evidence for the no-resubscribe assertion, Security engineer sign-off on the rotation and revocation behaviour, and QA verification of the 5-second revocation requirement with a stopwatch-style recorded run.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S02**. Interacts with **E17** (WS transport) — the auth-side contract here is the input to E17-T04's client.

## Branch
`feat/e09-sessions-idle-lock`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-004, US-ONB-009; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-005, SCR-111, SCR-112; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-044, CMP-049, CMP-098, CMP-201; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/session`, `/auth/sessions`, `/auth/logout`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3, §4.4, §9.5; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

title: Step-up re-authentication and owner-initiated TOTP reset (US-ONB-005/010)
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** Step-up re-auth is the step-up sub-state of B16 `session`, built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` via the factory. The per-action-class grace window and the no-grace list (`live_enablement`, `killswitch`) are guards in `machines/B16.session.machine.json`; the three-failure downgrade is a transition to a read-only child state. No hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime.

US-ONB-005 (Must): sensitive actions demand a fresh TOTP so a hijacked session cannot rotate keys or enable Live. US-ONB-010 (Should): the owner can reset a manager's second factor so a lost phone does not strand them. The two belong together because the reset is itself the archetypal step-up-protected action and shares the `mfa_challenges` (`purpose='step_up'`) plumbing and the SCR-006 modal.

The policy is precise: a 5-minute grace **per action class**, a grace that **never applies** to Live enablement or kill-switch disable, and three invalid codes abandoning the action, downgrading the session to read-only for 5 minutes and auditing at high severity. The permission registry already distinguishes dangerous actions via `permissions.is_dangerous` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.1.2), and `sessions.mfa_satisfied_at` / `Session.elevated_until` carry the freshness window — reconciled to one field by E09-K01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1`: the step-up sub-state lives inside `machines/B16.session.machine.json` (states `elevated.{action_class}` / `readonly_downgrade`); `bindings/b16_session.py` supplies the guard `grace_window_valid(action_class)` (false unconditionally for `live_enablement` and `killswitch`, per the no-grace list) and the action `record_step_up_failure` driving the 3-strike transition to `readonly_downgrade`.
- `POST /auth/step-up` per `22-api-openapi.yaml`: accepts a TOTP code for a named action class, sets the elevation window on the session, returns the window expiry so the UI can display it.
- **Server-side gate**: any route whose declared permission is `is_dangerous` requires a live elevation for its action class; the check lives in the E09-T03 decision point so no route can forget it. Action classes: `keys` (reveal-scope/rotate/revoke), `users` (invite, role change, TOTP reset), `live_enablement`, `killswitch`, `risk_caps`.
- **No-grace list**: `live_enablement` and `killswitch` disable always require a fresh code regardless of an existing window.
- **Failure policy**: three invalid codes abandon the action, mark the session read-only for 5 minutes (server-side, enforced on every write route), and audit `auth.step_up_failed` at severity `error`.
- **Owner TOTP reset**: an owner endpoint that revokes the target's `mfa_methods`, forces re-enrolment on next sign-in, revokes all their sessions, and **does not** cancel orders or flatten positions; the confirmation surface shows the target's open-position state before confirming, and the secret is never revealed to the owner.
- **Screens**: SCR-006 step-up modal and SCR-149 admin re-authentication gate (CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-043, CMP-201), showing the remaining grace window in text; SCR-003 re-enrolment forced for the reset user.
- Audit: `auth.step_up_granted`, `auth.step_up_failed` (error), `auth.session_readonly_downgrade`, `auth.mfa_reset_by_owner` (severity critical, actor and target recorded).

## Out of scope
- The key-rotation, Live-enablement and kill-switch actions themselves — **E27**, **E44**, **E39**; this Story provides the gate they declare.
- Self-service TOTP reset — deliberately impossible; recovery codes (E09-S02) are the self-service path.
- The admin user-management screen chrome — **E42**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Step-up required for a dangerous action
  Given I am signed in and open Admin, API keys
  When I attempt to reveal-scope, rotate or revoke a key
  Then I must enter a fresh TOTP code before the action proceeds

Scenario: Grace window within an action class
  Given I completed step-up 3 minutes ago for the keys action class
  When I perform a second keys action within 5 minutes
  Then no new code is required and the remaining grace window is shown in the dialog

Scenario: Grace never applies to Live enablement
  Given I completed step-up 1 minute ago for another action class
  When I attempt to enable Live trading or disable the kill-switch
  Then a fresh code is required regardless

Scenario: Three failures downgrade the session
  Given I enter an invalid code three times
  Then the action is abandoned, the session is read-only for 5 minutes, and a high-severity audit entry is written

Scenario: Owner reset does not disturb positions
  Given a manager with open positions has lost their authenticator
  When I reset their TOTP with step-up auth
  Then their sessions are revoked and re-enrolment is forced, no order is cancelled, no position is flattened, and I was shown that state before confirming

Scenario: Reset reveals nothing
  When the reset completes
  Then no TOTP secret or recovery code is returned to me, and the target enrols a fresh secret themselves

Scenario: Elevation cannot be forged by the client
  Given a client that sets an elevation flag locally
  When it calls a dangerous route without a server-side elevation
  Then the route is refused with 403 and the attempt is audited
```

## Technical notes / design
Elevation state is the B16 interpreter's own state, not a token claim or a bolted-on counter: it is revocable and cannot be replayed on another session because each session owns exactly one B16 machine instance keyed by `session_id`. `machine_hash` for B16 covers this sub-state too (one chart, one hash). Per-tick verification of the TOTP code itself stays plain code (not a statechart concern, BENCH-2).

Elevation is stored on the session row keyed by action class with its own expiry, never in a token claim, so it is revocable and cannot be replayed on another session. The read-only downgrade is the same process-wide mechanism E09-T04 uses for unsafe binding, scoped to one session. The reset flow is a single transaction: revoke methods, revoke sessions, set `users.mfa_required`, emit audit — with the position-state snapshot fetched and displayed *before* the confirmation, not after.

## Test plan
Contract: `tests/xstate_contract/test_b16.py` (shared with E09-S03) covers the elevation sub-states, the no-grace guard for `live_enablement`/`killswitch`, and the 3-failure downgrade transition. Unit: grace-window arithmetic per action class, no-grace list, failure counter and downgrade expiry. Contract: `/auth/step-up` and the reset endpoint against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: a dangerous route called with, without and just after an expired elevation; reset with open positions asserting no OMS side effects (mocked OMS with a strict no-call assertion). E2E: SCR-006 happy path, grace display, three-failure downgrade; SCR-149 gate. Security: client-forged elevation, cross-session elevation replay, brute force on the step-up code. a11y: axe-core on SCR-006 and SCR-149 plus a manual focus-trap and announcement pass.

## Security notes
This Story exists to blunt session hijacking, so its own bypasses are the threat model: elevation forged client-side (server-side only), elevation leaked across sessions (bound to `session_id`), grace abused to chain unrelated dangerous actions (per-action-class windows), reset used as an account-takeover primitive by a compromised owner session (reset itself requires fresh step-up and is audited at critical severity with actor, target and timestamp). No secret is ever transported to the owner. All step-up codes are subject to the same replay protection as login codes.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-006 and SCR-149 are modal dialogs with focus traps, accessible names describing the action being authorised (not a generic "Confirm"), the remaining grace window stated as text, error announcements via `aria-live`, and a keyboard-operable cancel that provably abandons the action. The reset confirmation states the position-impact in text, not only in an icon or colour.

## Performance notes
The elevation check rides the existing per-request principal snapshot — no extra query, < 100 µs. The step-up endpoint itself matches the TOTP verification budget (p99 < 150 ms).

## Observability
`auth_step_up_total{action_class,outcome}`, `auth_step_up_failures_total`, `auth_readonly_downgrades_total`, `auth_mfa_resets_total`. Alerts: any `auth.mfa_reset_by_owner`, and repeated step-up failures on one session.

## Definition of Done
B16 contract test green in the blocking gate (`E50-T31`). Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, with mandatory Security engineer sign-off including the manual abuse-case checks (attempt privilege escalation, attempt the withdrawal/Live toggle without elevation), design-qa on SCR-006/SCR-149, and QA sign-off on the reset-with-open-positions scenario.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S03** (elevation lives on the session) and **E09-T03** (the gate is enforced inside the decision point).

## Branch
`feat/e09-step-up-auth`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-005, US-ONB-010; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-003, SCR-006, SCR-149, SCR-154; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-043, CMP-201, CMP-204; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/auth/step-up`, `/auth/mfa/methods/{methodId}`, `/users/{userId}`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.2, §3.1.4, §3.1.5; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.1; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

title: Invite-based user creation and redemption (US-ONB-006)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-006 (Must): *"As the owner, I want to invite a manager or viewer by generating a one-time link, so that I never set someone else's password."* This is the only way a user account comes into existence in CandleViewer — there is no self-registration and no owner-set password, which removes a whole class of credential-handling risk. `users.status` starts at `invited`, `users.invited_by` records provenance, and the role is fixed at invite time and cannot be self-elevated. The endpoints are `POST /users` (create the invite) and `GET|POST /invites/{inviteToken}` (inspect and redeem).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `POST /users` (permission `users:write`, `is_dangerous` → step-up from E09-S04): creates a `users` row with `status='invited'`, assigns the chosen role in `user_roles`, zero `user_account_access` rows, and mints a **256-bit single-use invite token stored only as a hash**, valid 72 hours.
- `GET /invites/{inviteToken}`: validates without consuming, returning the invited role and expiry for the redemption screen; rejects expired, already-redeemed and unknown tokens with one uniform message.
- **Redemption wizard SCR-017** (4 steps per `14-screens-catalogue.md`): accept invite → set password (SCR-004 embedded, CMP-201/202/203) → enrol TOTP (SCR-003 embedded, from E09-S02) → orientation card; completing all steps flips `users.status` to `active`.
- **SCR-123 Admin: invite user**: form for email, username, role, with the generated link shown once and copyable, a re-issue action for expired invites, and a pending-invite list with revoke.
- Role immutability: the role is bound to the token at creation; the redemption payload cannot alter it, and an attempt to do so is a 403 plus an audit entry.
- Audit: `users.invited` (actor, target, role), `users.invite_redeemed`, `users.invite_rejected{reason}` (severity warning for reuse), `users.invite_reissued`, `users.invite_revoked`.

## Out of scope
- Granting account access and profiles to the new user — **E27**/**E39**; a new user deliberately starts with zero bindings.
- The full admin user-list and role-editing screens — **E42**.
- Email delivery of the invite: the link is displayed to the owner to transmit out of band (there is no SMTP dependency in a Tailscale-only deployment).
- The first-run checklist the invitee then sees — **E09-S06**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Invite accepted
  Given I create an invite for role manager valid for 72 hours
  When the invitee opens the link, sets a password and enrols TOTP
  Then their account becomes active with role manager and zero account bindings

Scenario: Expired invite
  Given an invite is older than 72 hours
  When it is opened
  Then it is rejected and I can re-issue a new one from Admin

Scenario: Invite reuse
  Given an invite has already been redeemed
  When the same link is opened again
  Then it is rejected and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Role cannot be self-elevated
  Given an invite issued for role viewer
  When the redemption request is tampered with to request owner
  Then the request is refused with 403, the account is still created as viewer or not at all, and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Partially completed redemption is not usable
  Given the invitee sets a password but abandons TOTP enrolment
  Then the account remains status invited, cannot sign in to the workspace, and the invite is still consumed exactly once

Scenario: Creating an invite requires step-up
  Given my step-up grace for the users action class has expired
  When I submit the invite form
  Then I am challenged for a fresh TOTP code before the invite is minted

Scenario: The link is shown once
  When the invite is created
  Then the raw token is displayed once with a copy control and is not retrievable afterwards, only re-issuable
```

## Technical notes / design
The token is `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, stored as `sha256_hex` with its expiry and consumed-at timestamp; lookup is by hash, so a database leak does not yield usable links. Redemption is a single transaction that consumes the token, writes the password hash and (via E09-S02) the confirmed TOTP method, and flips status — so an abandoned enrolment leaves the account unusable rather than half-open. Uniform rejection messaging for unknown/expired/redeemed tokens prevents probing which links ever existed.

## Test plan
Unit: token generation entropy and hashing, expiry arithmetic, single-use consumption under concurrency (two simultaneous redemptions — exactly one wins). Contract: `POST /users`, `GET|POST /invites/{inviteToken}` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: full redemption on real Postgres asserting role, zero bindings and audit rows; re-issue after expiry. E2E: SCR-123 create → SCR-017 wizard → workspace, plus expired and reused link paths. Security: role-tampering, token brute-force rate limiting, timing uniformity across rejection reasons. a11y: axe-core on SCR-017 and SCR-123 plus a manual pass on the multi-step wizard.

## Security notes
Threats: invite interception (short 72 h life, single use, hash-at-rest, out-of-band transmission), privilege escalation via the redemption payload (role read from the stored invite only), token enumeration (256-bit space plus rate limiting plus uniform errors), and invite-farming by a compromised owner session (creation requires step-up and is audited with actor and role). The raw token is never logged, never stored, and never included in an audit `after_state`.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-017 is a multi-step wizard: each step has a heading, progress is exposed as text ("Step 2 of 4"), errors are announced and focus-managed on step transitions, and the flow is completable by keyboard alone including the embedded TOTP enrolment. SCR-123's one-time link is selectable text with a labelled copy control and an explicit warning that it will not be shown again — not conveyed by styling alone.

## Performance notes
No hot path; the only cost is the Argon2id hash when the invitee sets a password, subject to the same thread-pool bound as E09-S01. Invite lookup is a single indexed query.

## Observability
`users_invites_created_total{role}`, `users_invites_redeemed_total`, `users_invites_rejected_total{reason}`, `users_invites_pending` gauge. Alert on repeated rejections from one source (token probing).

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, with Security engineer review of the token lifecycle, design-qa against SCR-017/SCR-123, manual screen-reader pass on the wizard, and QA sign-off covering expiry, reuse and abandonment.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S04** (invite creation is a step-up-gated action). Requires **E09-S02** for the embedded enrolment step and **US-ADMIN-001** groundwork delivered here as the `POST /users` endpoint; the admin screen chrome is E42.
