title: Guided first-run checklist for a new manager (US-ONB-007)
body:
## Context
US-ONB-007 (Should): a newly invited manager lands in a terminal where most things are deliberately blocked — no account bindings, possibly no API key yet, and Bybit itself refuses API-key creation for 48 hours after a sub-account is created. Without an explanation this reads as a broken product. The checklist (SCR-019 setup checklist card, embedded in SCR-017/SCR-018) tells them what is green, what is pending, and why, with a **server-verified** condition behind every step — the story's NFR is explicit: "no step may be faked client-side".

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `GET` checklist endpoint returning, per step, a server-evaluated state (`ok` / `pending` / `blocked`) plus a reason and, where applicable, an unblock timestamp: **Tailscale OK** (from E09-T04's self-check), **TOTP enrolled** (`mfa_methods.confirmed_at`), **sub-account bound** (`user_account_access`), **API key status** (E27, including the Bybit 48-hour restriction with the UTC unblock time), **profile limits** (E39/E27 account profile present), **Demo session** (a demo-environment account is reachable).
- **SCR-019 Setup checklist card** (CMP-021, CMP-023, CMP-050, CMP-097): per-step state, reason text, a countdown for the 48-hour Bybit restriction, and a call to action per step that deep-links to the owning screen.
- **SCR-018 guided tour / coach marks** wiring: first-run only, dismissible, never re-shown once the checklist completes.
- Collapse behaviour: when all steps are green the card collapses to a dismissible summary and does not reappear; dismissal is persisted server-side per user so it survives device changes.
- Graceful degradation: steps whose owning Epic has not shipped yet (API key, profile limits) render as `pending` with a "coming soon in this environment" reason driven by a feature flag, not by a client-side stub.

## Out of scope
- Creating API keys, binding sub-accounts or editing profiles — the checklist links to **E27**/**E39** screens, it does not perform those actions.
- The full onboarding wizard for the owner (SCR-016) — that is the owner's first-run, covered by E27's key setup.
- Any content that constitutes trading advice or a tutorial on strategy (advice-boundary constraint, risk R9).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Checklist shown on first sign-in
  Given I sign in for the first time as an invited manager
  Then I see steps Tailscale OK, TOTP enrolled, sub-account bound, API key status, profile limits, Demo session, each with a server-evaluated state

Scenario: 48-hour Bybit restriction is surfaced with a countdown
  Given my Bybit sub-account was created less than 48 hours ago
  Then the API key step shows that Bybit blocks API key creation until a stated UTC timestamp, with a live countdown
  And Demo exploration is offered in the meantime

Scenario: Checklist completes and stays gone
  Given all steps are green
  Then the card collapses into a dismissible summary, and after dismissal it does not reappear on any device

Scenario: A step cannot be faked from the client
  Given I tamper with local state to mark the TOTP step complete
  When the page reloads
  Then the step returns to its true server-evaluated state

Scenario: A dependency is unavailable
  Given the account service is unreachable
  Then the affected steps render an error state with a retry, the rest still render, and the card never blocks the workspace

Scenario: Keyboard and screen-reader completion
  Given I use the keyboard only
  Then every step, its call to action and the dismiss control are reachable and announced with their state as text
```

## Technical notes / design
The endpoint composes read-only probes from other modules behind a small interface so that unimplemented Epics return a typed `not_available` rather than failing the whole response; each probe has its own timeout (250 ms) and the response is assembled best-effort. The dismissal flag is a per-user preference row, not local storage, satisfying "does not reappear" across devices. The 48-hour restriction timestamp comes from the exchange-account creation time recorded in E27, not from a client clock.

## Test plan
Unit: state-derivation per step including the `not_available` and error branches; countdown formatting across the DST-free UTC boundary. Contract: the checklist response schema. Integration: probes against a seeded database in each of the six step-states. E2E: first sign-in shows the card, completing TOTP flips the step without a manual reload, tamper test, dismissal persistence across a new browser profile. a11y: axe-core on SCR-019 and SCR-018 plus a manual screen-reader pass on the coach marks.

## Security notes
Low-sensitivity surface, but it must not leak: the checklist is scoped to the requesting user and never reveals other users' accounts, key states or UIDs; the API-key step reports only a status, never key material or a masked key; probes run with the caller's own permissions through the E09-T03 decision point rather than with elevated service rights.

## Accessibility notes
Each step is a list item whose state is conveyed by text and icon, never colour alone; the countdown updates politely (`aria-live="polite"`, throttled to once per minute so it does not spam a screen reader); coach marks are dismissible by Escape, trap focus only while open, restore focus on close, and are suppressed entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion` for their animated variant per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
The composed endpoint must return in p99 < 400 ms with all probes timing out independently at 250 ms; it is called once per session start and on explicit refresh, never polled, so it adds no sustained load.

## Observability
`onboarding_checklist_views_total`, `onboarding_step_state_total{step,state}` (shows where new users actually get stuck), `onboarding_checklist_dismissed_total`, `onboarding_probe_timeouts_total{step}`.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2: automated coverage of all scenarios, ≥80% frontend coverage, design-qa against SCR-019/SCR-018, axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass, QA sign-off, demoed at Sprint Review with a freshly invited test manager, feature-flag state recorded for the not-yet-shipped steps.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S05** (there must be an invited manager to onboard). Reads data owned by **E27** (accounts, keys) and **E39** (profile limits) behind feature-flagged probes, so it can ship in R0 ahead of them.

## Branch
`feat/e09-first-run-checklist`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ONB-007; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-017, SCR-018, SCR-019; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-017, CMP-021, CMP-023, CMP-040, CMP-050, CMP-066, CMP-097; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.1; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.3, §3.2.1; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` R14.

title: RBAC decision point, generated permissions, deny-by-default enforcement
body:
## Context
Architecture principle **P8** states that the frontend is never trusted for account scope, risk caps or environment; `20-architecture.md` §3.10 assigns role/scope resolution to the Auth/RBAC/Audit component; `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.2 declares the `Permission` enum **generated** from the `x-rbac.permissions` blocks in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, which is the single canonical registry, cross-checked against the database seed by the contract test `rbac_vocabulary_single_source`. `30-release-roadmap.md` §12 lists "RBAC enforcement — E09" as a must-not-descope item.

This Task builds the one place that answers "may this principal do this thing to this object?" — consumed by every REST route, by the WS `auth_ok` permission payload and per-subscribe checks (`23-ws-protocol.md` §4.3, §9.5, G5), and later by the OMS validator for account scoping.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Generator** `tools/rbac/generate.py`: reads `x-rbac.permissions` from `22-api-openapi.yaml`, emits the `Permission` StrEnum consumed by `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.2 and the database seed rows for `permissions` (including `is_dangerous`, which drives step-up in E09-S04). Generated files are committed and CI fails on drift.
- **Policy decision point** in `services/api/auth/scopes.py`: `decide(principal, permission, object) -> Allow | Deny(reason)`, resolving roles via `user_roles` → `role_permissions` → `permissions`, and account scope via `user_account_access` (`can_view`, `can_trade`, `frozen`); empty `allowed_account_ids` means all, owner only.
- **Deny-by-default enforcement**: a FastAPI dependency applied globally; a route without an explicit `x-rbac.permissions` declaration (or an explicit `security: []` public marker for login/refresh/health) **fails the build**, not just the request.
- **WS integration**: `auth_ok` carries `roles`, resolved permissions and account scope; every `sub` is permission-checked per topic (`23-ws-protocol.md` §5, §6); revocation or role change publishes a live permission-change frame so a downgrade takes effect mid-connection.
- **403 semantics**: a uniform `forbidden` error body with a machine-readable `reason`, feeding **SCR-154 Permission denied**; every denial is audited (`rbac.denied`, severity warning) with the permission code.
- Role seeds: `owner` (all permissions), `manager` (trading and read within granted accounts, no `users:write`, no `keys:manage`, no `killswitch:write` beyond own scope), `viewer` (read-only across granted scope, includes audit and journal read).

## Out of scope
- Risk caps, freeze and kill-switch behaviour on `user_account_access` — **E39** (the columns are read here, the policy that sets them is not).
- Custom or user-defined roles — the three system roles are fixed in v1.
- Admin UI for granting roles and account access — **E42**.
- Rule-engine permission gates (`rules.arm_live`) — declared in the vocabulary here, enforced by E35/E37.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every route declares a permission or is explicitly public
  Given the full route inventory of the FastAPI application
  When the conformance test runs
  Then each route either declares x-rbac.permissions or is marked explicitly public, and an undeclared route fails CI

Scenario: Deny by default
  Given a newly added route whose declaration is missing
  When any principal calls it at runtime in the test harness
  Then the decision is Deny and the response is 403, never an accidental allow

Scenario: Vocabulary has one source of truth
  Given the generated enum, the OpenAPI blocks and the database seed
  When rbac_vocabulary_single_source runs
  Then the three sets are identical and any hand edit to the generated file fails the check

Scenario: A manager cannot reach another manager's account
  Given a manager granted access to account A only
  When they request data or submit an order for account B
  Then the request is denied with 403, the denial names the permission and scope, and rbac.denied is audited

Scenario: Downgrade takes effect mid-connection
  Given a connected manager whose role is reduced to viewer
  When the change commits
  Then a permission-change frame is delivered, trading topics are unsubscribed server-side, and the next order attempt on that socket is refused

Scenario: Owner floor cannot be removed through the API
  Given a single active owner
  When an attempt is made to strip that role via PUT /users/{userId}/roles
  Then the request fails and the database trigger is never relied on as the only guard
```

## Technical notes / design
The decision point is pure and synchronous over a per-request snapshot of the principal's roles, permissions and account scope, loaded once per request and invalidated by bus events on role or access change — so a decision costs a set lookup, not a query. Object-scoped decisions (account id, environment) take the object as an explicit argument; there is no ambient context, which makes the function trivially testable and keeps the OMS validator's later use honest. Endpoints touched: `POST /users`, `GET|PATCH /users/{userId}`, `PUT /users/{userId}/roles`, `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access`.

## Test plan
Unit: decision matrix over (role × permission × scope × object) generated exhaustively from the seed, with golden expectations; frozen and `can_trade=false` cases. Contract: route-inventory conformance test; `rbac_vocabulary_single_source`; WS `auth_ok` payload schema. Integration: role change propagation, account-scope isolation between two managers. Security: automated privilege-escalation suite attempting every owner-only route as manager and viewer, asserting 403 and an audit row for each. Performance: decision latency benchmark.

## Security notes
This is the authorisation control for a money-moving system. Fail-closed everywhere: an unresolvable principal, an unknown permission code, or a missing declaration all yield Deny. Denials never leak whether the object exists (a manager asking about another manager's account gets the same 403 as for a non-existent account). The generator is treated as security-relevant code — changes to it require Security-engineer review, and the generated seed diff is reviewed in every PR that touches it. Feeds the E09 STRIDE model (elevation of privilege branch).

## Accessibility notes
SCR-154 Permission denied must state in text what was denied and what to do next, be announced assertively, and offer a keyboard-reachable route back; it must not rely on an icon or colour alone. This ticket supplies the `reason` code and human sentence it renders.

## Performance notes
Budget: decision p99 < 200 µs, snapshot load adds < 2 ms to the first decision of a request, zero additional queries for subsequent decisions in the same request. Measured under the API load profile in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
`rbac_denials_total{permission,role}`, `rbac_decision_duration_seconds`, `rbac_snapshot_loads_total`, and a build-time metric of declared-vs-total routes exported to the PRR checklist. Alert on a burst of denials for one principal (possible compromised session or a broken client).

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2, plus the interface-first rule: the `x-rbac.permissions` diff to `22-api-openapi.yaml` is reviewed and merged **before** implementation; Security engineer review recorded; the privilege-escalation suite is green and its report attached.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09-S02** (a principal must be fully authenticated before authorisation is meaningful) and **E09-T02** (denials must be auditable).

## Branch
`feat/e09-rbac-pdp`

## References
`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` P8, §3.10; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.2; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `x-rbac.permissions`, `/users*`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` G5, §4.3, §5, §9.5; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.2, §3.1.3, §10.1; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-154; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.2.0; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12.

title: App shell, routing & Electron wrapper
body:
## Context
CandleViewer is a single-page React + TypeScript app wrapped by an Electron desktop shell (primary surface for the owner; a plain browser over Tailscale is a fully supported surface for managers/viewers). Before any R1 charting screen can be built, the app needs the frame everything else mounts into: the React Router route tree of `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2, auth- and RBAC-guarded routes (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §4), the persistent global chrome SCR-010, the single global hotkey layer mandated by `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1, the Electron main/preload process hardened to SR-110..SR-119 of `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.11, and the system-state surfaces (offline, degraded, version mismatch, 404/403, crash) that every later epic reuses instead of inventing its own.

E10 sits at the end of the R0 dependency chain: `E05 --> E10` and `E09 --> E10` in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1, and it in turn gates `E10 --> E11` (chart engine core). Its roadmap scope line (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2) is: "React Router route tree per `12-sitemap.md`; auth-guarded and RBAC-guarded routes; Electron main/preload with `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, strict CSP, GPU flags tuned per E06; auto-update channel stub; env badge (Demo/Live) in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to local log". R0 exit criterion 9 is owned by this epic: "Electron shell boots the web app, passes a Playwright-Electron smoke test, and starts with the hardened security switches enabled (verified by an automated assertion, not by inspection)".

Story domain: **SET** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §27). The SET stories realised at *shell* level here are US-SET-002 (global hotkey layer, Must) and US-SET-009 (Electron shell preferences, Should); US-SET-001/003/004/005/006/007/008 belong to the later settings epic and E05, and are explicitly out of scope except for the shell hooks they need.

ADR-0011 (Electron vs Tauri) is the only non-`decided` ADR in the plan (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16). E10 therefore builds against Electron **behind a `ShellPort` abstraction** so the decision stays reversible, exactly as `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16 instructs.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Goal** — a bootable, navigable, hardened application frame that every R1+ screen plugs into, with zero bespoke chrome per feature.

- **Routing**: `apps/web/src/routes/*` implementing every route ID R-001..R-903 of `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2 as declarations (real screens land in their own epics; E10 ships the tree, guards, loaders, error elements and placeholder route elements).
- **Guards**: auth guard, RBAC guard (Owner/Manager/Viewer), admin step-up guard (`/admin/**`, 30-min step-up TTL), deep-link param validation contract (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §7).
- **Shell chrome**: SCR-010 App shell, SCR-011 Navigation rail & workspace switcher shell, SCR-015 Global toast host mount; components CMP-070 AppShell, CMP-071 NavRail, CMP-072 TopBar, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-076 ConnectionStatus, CMP-084 GlobalSearchTrigger, CMP-085 SkipLink, CMP-208 StatusBar, CMP-209 RightRail, CMP-210 HealthChips, CMP-212 ToastHost.
- **Hotkeys**: the global hotkey/action registry, conflict engine and reserved-key policy (US-SET-002), plus `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/me/keymap`. The SCR-012 command palette and SCR-013 cheatsheet that consume the registry are **deferred to E15**.
- **Electron shell**: `apps/desktop` main + preload hardened per SR-110..SR-119, GPU flags from E06/ADR-0011, a single hardened `createWindow()` factory with minimal bounds persistence, and the auto-update channel **stub** (disabled until signing exists, SR-115). Multi-monitor state, system tray, SCR-027 pop-out windows and the US-SET-009 shell-preferences surface are **deferred to E15**.
- **System states**: SCR-153 degraded mode (CMP-092), SCR-155 not found (CMP-090), SCR-157 version mismatch (CMP-096, CMP-207, CMP-028), SCR-159 offline / shell-specific, 403 (CMP-089), global error boundary (CMP-091) with crash reporting to a local log.
- **Bootstrap**: `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/me/preferences`, `GET /api/v1/me/keymap`, WS topic `system` auto-subscription for health chips and env badge.
- Design (D), QA (Q) and Security (X) tickets carrying their own points.

**Children** (15 tickets, 36 pts): E10-D02, E10-D03, E10-D04, E10-K01, E10-T01, E10-T02, E10-T04, E10-S01, E10-S02, E10-S04, E10-Q02, E10-Q03, E10-Q04, E10-X01, E10-X02.

**Exit criteria (epic-level)**
1. Every route in `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2 resolves; unauthenticated access redirects to `/login`; RBAC-denied direct navigation renders `/403` (or 404 for `/admin/**`) and the corresponding API returns 403 with an audit row.
2. `/admin/**` is unreachable without a step-up token ≤30 min old; non-owners get 404 from the router.
3. The packaged Electron build asserts every SR-110 flag and every SR-112 CSP directive at build time; flipping any one fails CI (`electron-hardening` required check, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §9.4).
4. A Playwright-Electron smoke test boots the shell, logs in, reaches `/terminal` and asserts the DEMO/LIVE badge in every window including pop-outs.
5. Cold launch to interactive shell ≤3 s on reference hardware (budget #10, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3).
6. axe-core reports zero violations on SCR-010, 011, 012, 013, 015, 027, 153, 155, 157, 159 and the 403 surface.
7. One global hotkey layer exists, is remappable, detects conflicts, and refuses reserved keys (`Esc`, `Ctrl+K`).
8. No Bybit host appears in any CSP directive or in renderer-bundled code (SR-119 CI assertion).

**Risks**
- **R8 Browser/GPU compat** — GPU flags tuned for the reference machine may regress elsewhere; mitigated by the `degraded-2d` fallback (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` F15) and E06's `RenderProfile` probe.
- **R5 Scope** — the shell is a magnet for "just one more chrome element"; the component list above is closed for R0, additions go to R1 epics.
- **R10 Key-person** — Electron main-process knowledge concentrates in one engineer; mitigated by E10-T05 (architecture docs + ADR consequences) and a second `apps/desktop` reviewer via CODEOWNERS.
- ADR-0011 staying `proposed` past end of Sprint 03 would strand shell work; mitigated by the `ShellPort` abstraction (E10-K01) so a Tauri swap is a port implementation, not a rewrite.

### Scope reconciliation and descope register (2026-09-14)

E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 3 epic register; section 4.2; window S03-S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to **83 points** - 2.4x the allocation and far outside the +/-15% tolerance band (28.9-39.1). The R0 train has no room to absorb the difference: section 3.1 allocates 322 of 360 available points to E01-E10, leaving an 11% buffer that a 49-point overrun would consume twice over. Re-sizing the children without changing scope would have been a fiction, and raising the roadmap figure would have broken the train budget.

The epic has therefore been **re-cut to the roadmap scope line** - route tree and guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel stub; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary and crash reporting to a local log - which now decomposes to **36 points across 15 children**, inside the tolerance band. Everything removed is re-homed in a named existing epic; nothing is deleted, and **no R0 exit criterion is weakened** (criterion 9, the Electron hardening assertion and Playwright-Electron smoke test, is fully retained in E10-T02, E10-X02 and E10-Q02).

| Withdrawn | Was | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| E10-T03 window/monitor state, tray, SCR-027 pop-outs | 5 | **E15 Layouts & workspaces** (R1, S08-S09) | `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` section 6.2 keys pop-out and window state to the *layout*; E15 owns layouts. The roadmap-line auto-update stub and SCR-157 surface stay in R0, folded into E10-T02 and E10-S04. |
| E10-S03 command palette + cheatsheet | 3 | **E15** (R1) | Not in the E10 roadmap scope line. Both consume a populated command registry and symbol/route sources that only exist after E08/E11. E10-S02 still ships the registry they bind to, and reserves `Ctrl+K`. |
| E10-D01 shell UX research | 3 | **Split**: environment-legibility and panic-reachability studies folded into E10-D02; navigation card-sort and health-chip vocabulary to **E15** | The two studies that gate an R0 safety decision are kept in R0; the two that inform E15 surfaces move with them. |
| E10-D05 design-QA sweep | 3 | **E49 Defect burn-down & design-QA sweep** (R5); safety-signal subset folded into E10-Q03 | E49 exists for this pass. Badge and panic-control fidelity remain R0-blocking so no safety regression waits until R5. |
| E10-X03 abuse-case execution | 3 | **E43 Security hardening & pen-test remediation** (R4); scripted per-PR subset folded into E10-Q02 | E43 owns adversarial execution. The controls that must not regress per-PR are automated in R0 instead of being executed once. |
| E10-Q01 test plan and charters | 3 | Folded into **E10-Q02** | A separate planning ticket for a surface this size was ceremony; the plan is a deliverable of the suite that implements it. |
| E10-T05 architecture docs + ADR consequences | 2 | **E48 Documentation, runbooks & GA readiness** (R5) | E48 already owns "architecture and ADR index reconciled with the built system". The interim ADR-0011 position is recorded by E10-K01 so R0 loses no decision record. |

Remaining children were additionally right-sized against the reduced surface (notably E10-S02 registry-only at 2, E10-S04 at 2, and the QA/security tickets at 1-2 each), since each was originally scoped against the larger surface.

**Roadmap consequence**: no edit to `30-release-roadmap.md` is required - E10 now matches its published 34-point allocation within tolerance at 36. E15's allocation (34 pts, S08-S09) must absorb roughly 9 points of transferred scope and is flagged for review at R1 planning; E43, E48 and E49 absorb 3, 2 and 3 points respectively, all of which fit inside their existing reserves.

## Out of scope
- Screen content behind any route other than the shell surfaces listed above (charts, DOM, tickets, admin pages) — E11+ and E42.
- Settings screens SCR-110/111/113/116/117/118/119 themselves (US-SET-001/003/004/005/006/007/008) — later settings epic; E10 ships only the shell hooks (theme/density attribute application, keymap fetch, hotkey registry API).
- Workspace/layout persistence and the dock system (E15); E10 ships the nav-rail and workspace-switcher *shell*, not layout CRUD.
- Notification-centre content (SCR-014) — E40; E10 mounts CMP-209 RightRail only.
- Real auto-update delivery, code signing and release feeds — stub only (SR-115 keeps auto-update disabled until signing exists); real updates land in E48/R5.
- Android, any separate admin application, Tauri implementation work (measured in E06 only).
- Crash reporting to any remote service — local log file only.
- Window/monitor-state persistence, system tray, SCR-027 pop-out windows and the US-SET-009 shell-preferences surface - deferred to E15 (see descope register).
- SCR-012 command palette and SCR-013 hotkey cheatsheet - deferred to E15; E10 ships the registry they consume.
- Full design-QA sweep (E49) and adversarial abuse-case execution (E43); R0 retains only the safety-signal and per-PR-regression subsets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued route resolves
  Given the app is built
  When an automated test navigates to each route ID R-001..R-903 from docs/plan/12-sitemap.md
  Then each route renders its route element or its documented redirect, and none renders the 404 fallback unintentionally

Scenario: RBAC-denied navigation is structural, not cosmetic
  Given I am signed in as a Viewer
  When I navigate directly to /admin/users
  Then the router renders 404, any data call returns 403, and an audit row is written

Scenario: Hardened Electron build
  Given a packaged production Electron build
  When the SR-114 build-time assertion suite runs
  Then contextIsolation, sandbox and webSecurity are true, nodeIntegration is false, the CSP matches SR-112 exactly, and no Bybit host appears in connect-src or in renderer bundles

Scenario: Cold start budget
  Given the reference hardware of docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md
  When the Electron app is launched cold 10 times
  Then app.whenReady() to "shell interactive" is <= 3 s at p95

Scenario: Shell survives a renderer crash
  Given a panel throws an uncaught render error
  When the global error boundary catches it
  Then the surrounding shell stays operable, a correlation id and copy-diagnostics action are offered, and the crash is appended to the local crash log
```

## Technical notes / design
- Router: React Router v6+ data router. In the browser build `createBrowserRouter`; in Electron the app is served from a registered custom `app://` protocol handler (not `file://`) so history routing, CSP `'self'` and `Origin` checks (SR-042) all behave.
- Guards are route `loader`s reading the `/me` bootstrap cache; the client check is **UX only** — the security boundary is server-side (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.3, `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §4).
- `ShellPort` (E10-K01) abstracts every Electron-specific capability: `windows`, `tray`, `updates`, `keychainHandle`, `crashLog`, `gpuInfo`, `notifications`. The browser build supplies a capability-reporting no-op implementation so shell-only settings are *hidden with an explanation*, never shown disabled (US-SET-009 "Browser build" scenario).
- Env badge derives from the backend-reported environment on `/me` and the WS `system` topic; never inferred client-side and never defaulted to DEMO (SCR-150 rule).
- Errors: RFC 9457 problem+json from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`version_conflict`, `step_up_required`, …) rendered by shared shell error surfaces.

## Test plan
Roll-up of children: unit (guards, hotkey conflict algorithm, ShellPort, deep-link validators), contract (`/me`, `/me/preferences`, `/me/keymap` against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; WS `system` against `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9 `SystemUpdate`), integration (route matrix × role matrix), E2E (Playwright web + Playwright-Electron), perf (cold start, route change), a11y (axe + manual SR), security (hardening assertions, abuse cases). Coverage ≥80% on `apps/web` shell modules and `apps/desktop`.

## Security notes
Threat areas A-16 (Electron binary + auto-update) and AC-09 (Electron main process) from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §3; STRIDE rows E1..E5 (§5.9) plus O11/U5 (renderer XSS abusing a live session). Controls: SR-110..SR-119, SR-042 (Origin/`Sec-Fetch-Site` allow-list including the Electron app origin), SR-049 (TLS; plain HTTP only on 127.0.0.1 for the host-local shell), SR-012 cookie flags, SR-025 step-up re-auth. Data classification: session cookies (SECRET) and user identity (PII); the shell must never hold Bybit key material (SR-119). `sec:review` label required on every PR touching `apps/desktop` or CSP.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA across all shell surfaces (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). Landmarks (`header`/`nav`/`main`/`complementary`/`status`), CMP-085 SkipLink as first focusable element, `aria-current` on the nav rail, one global hotkey layer with reserved `Esc` and `Ctrl+K`, health chips expose state as words not colour, env badge announced on every route change, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured by every chrome transition, focus returns to the trigger when overlays close.

## Performance notes
Budget #10: cold launch to interactive workspace ≤3 s (Electron), ≤4 s (browser). Shell renders before workspace hydration; health chips update at 1 Hz and must never re-render the workspace subtree. Nav-rail expand/collapse ≤120 ms, transform-only, must not remount docked panels or drop GL contexts. Command-palette filter ≤16 ms over 2 000 entries. Toasts animate transform/opacity only.

## Observability
Structured logs via the E04 logger with redaction (never log cookies/tokens). Metrics: `shell_cold_start_ms`, `shell_route_change_ms`, `shell_ws_state`, `shell_crash_total`. Analytics/audit events from the screens catalogue: `command.executed` (name only, no payload), `help.hotkeys_opened`, `app.version_mismatch`, `app.update_applied`, `shell.offline_detected`, `shell.tailscale_unreachable`, `shell.gpu_unavailable`, `shell.window_restored`, `panel.floated`, `panel.redocked`. Correlation id propagated HTTP→WS per E04.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition (the descope register above is that record for the seven withdrawn tickets; each receiving epic must carry a linked ticket before E10 closes).
- [ ] Rolled-up child estimate is still within +/-15% of the 34-pt roadmap allocation at epic close; any drift is reconciled into `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` rather than absorbed silently.
- [ ] The eight epic exit criteria above verified end-to-end and evidenced on the ticket.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on `apps/web` shell modules and `apps/desktop`; no open P0/P1 bugs in E10 scope.
- [ ] `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `20-architecture.md` §2.1 C3 and ADR-0011 consequences updated to shipped reality.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on all shell routes + a manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] perf: cold-start and route-change numbers recorded against budget #10.
- [ ] security: STRIDE model (E10-X01) finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review with explicit acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Retro learnings filed as Chore tickets.

## Dependencies
- `E05` — design system v0 supplies tokens, themes and the atoms/molecules the chrome is assembled from (`E05 --> E10`).
- `E09` — auth/session/RBAC supplies the `/me` identity payload, session cookies and the step-up endpoint the guards depend on (`E09 --> E10`).
- `E02` — the `apps/web` / `apps/desktop` workspace packages and import-linter contracts.
- `E03` — CI jobs hosting the `electron-hardening`, `e2e-electron` and `a11y-axe` required checks.
- `E06` — GPU flags and the ADR-0011 interim decision the Electron build is configured from.
Interfaces relied on: `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/me/preferences`, `GET /api/v1/me/keymap`, `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up`, WS topic `system`.

## Branch
`feat/e10-app-shell-*` per child ticket; PRs ≤400 LOC diff, one concern each (routing, chrome, hotkeys, Electron main, states).

## References
- `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` — route tree, RBAC mechanics, Electron window model, deep-link contracts
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-010..015, SCR-027, SCR-119, SCR-152..159
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-059, 070, 071, 072, 075, 076, 080, 084, 085, 089..092, 094, 096, 207..213, 215
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §27 SET — US-SET-002, US-SET-009
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` — rows US-SET-002, US-SET-009, SCR-010..015
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9, §6.11 (SR-110..SR-119), §9.4
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3, §4
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` — budget #10
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §2.1 C3, F15, §16
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.2, §4.3, §11.1


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Implement the route tree, auth/RBAC/step-up guards and deep-link validation
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2 is the single source of truth for the route tree: 60+ route IDs from R-001 `/login` to R-903 `/maintenance`, each with an RBAC column (`O`/`M`/`V`/`A`, `◑` scoped, `⓪` read-only). §4 fixes the gating mechanics: every route is enforced twice — a router loader checks client-cached claims for UX, and every API call is independently authorised server-side; the client check is *never* the security boundary. §7 fixes the deep-link parameter contract (`symbol`, `tf`, `paneFocus`, `panel`, `account`, `groupBy`, `showClosed`, `from`, `to`, `speed`, `fromReplay`, `mode`, `standalone`) with validation rules per param.

Without this, every later epic invents its own routing and guard logic, and the `/admin/**` step-up rule (30-min TTL) gets implemented three different ways.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web/src/routes/tree.tsx` declaring every route ID R-001..R-903 from `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2, with the documented redirects (`/` → `/login` or `/terminal`; `/terminal` → `/terminal/:layoutId`; `/settings` → `/settings/profile`; `/` → `/login/first-run` when zero users exist).
- Placeholder route elements for routes owned by later epics, each rendering a labelled "owned by <Epic>" stub so the tree is complete and testable now.
- `requireAuth` loader: redirects unauthenticated users to `/login` preserving the intended destination.
- `requireRole(roles)` loader: renders `/403` (CMP-089 ForbiddenState) for denied non-admin routes; `/admin/**` denials render **404** for non-owners per `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §2 note.
- `requireStepUp` loader for `/admin/**`: 30-min TTL; on expiry surfaces the M-020 step-up modal contract and calls `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up`; handles the `step_up_required` problem+json type from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Deep-link validators per `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §7, one per param, with the documented fallbacks (invalid `symbol` → toast + last symbol; invalid `tf` → 15; `speed` clamped 0.5–100).
- Route-level `errorElement` wired to the global error boundary (E10-S04).
- A generated route manifest (`apps/web/src/routes/manifest.ts`) used by the command palette (E10-S03) and by the E10-Q01 route-matrix test.

## Out of scope
- Screen content for any route owned by another epic (stubs only).
- Server-side authorisation — implemented in E09; this ticket only consumes `/me` claims and renders the correct client-side outcome.
- Layout/workspace resolution behind `/terminal/:layoutId` (E15).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Complete route coverage
  Given the route manifest
  When the parameterised test iterates every route ID in docs/plan/12-sitemap.md §2
  Then each ID resolves to a route element or its documented redirect, and the test fails if the sitemap gains a route that the manifest lacks

Scenario: Unauthenticated access
  Given no session cookie
  When I navigate to /terminal/abc
  Then I am redirected to /login and, after a successful login, land on /terminal/abc rather than the default route

Scenario: Viewer hits an admin route
  Given I am signed in as a Viewer
  When I navigate directly to /admin/users
  Then the router renders the 404 surface, not 403, and no admin data request is issued

Scenario: Step-up expiry
  Given I am an Owner whose step-up token is 31 minutes old
  When I navigate to /admin/keys
  Then the step-up modal is shown, and on successful TOTP re-entry the original destination loads without a full page reload

Scenario: Malformed deep-link parameter
  When I navigate to /terminal/abc?tf=99
  Then the timeframe falls back to 15, a toast explains the fallback, and the URL is rewritten to the valid value
```

## Technical notes / design
React Router data router. Loaders read a module-scoped `/me` cache populated by E10-T04 so guards do not each issue their own request. Guard composition order is fixed: `requireAuth` → `requireRole` → `requireStepUp`. The admin-404 behaviour is implemented by having `requireRole` accept a `denyAs: '403' | '404'` option, defaulting to `'403'` and set to `'404'` for the `/admin` branch.

Validators live in `apps/web/src/routes/params.ts`, one pure function per param returning `{ value, corrected: boolean, reason?: string }` so the UI can both correct and explain. Server-side re-validation is assumed for every scope-bearing param (`account`, `symbol`) — the client correction is convenience only.

In Electron the app is served from a registered `app://` protocol handler rather than `file://` so history routing, the `'self'` CSP origin and the SR-042 `Origin` check all work identically to the browser build.

## Test plan
- Unit: each param validator (valid, invalid, boundary, missing); guard composition order; `denyAs` behaviour.
- Integration: route matrix × role matrix (owner/manager/viewer × every route ID) asserting rendered outcome — this is the test that would catch a future RBAC regression.
- Contract: `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up` and the `step_up_required` problem+json shape against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- E2E: login redirect-back, viewer admin 404, step-up expiry flow.
Coverage target >=85% on `apps/web/src/routes/**` given its security relevance.

## Security notes
Implements the client half of `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §4 and must be reviewed with the explicit understanding that it is **not** a security control (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.3). Threats: guard bypass by direct navigation (mitigated server-side; the client must still not leak admin-only data into the bundle or prefetch admin endpoints), and parameter tampering on `account`/`symbol` (server re-validates; the client must never treat a param as an authorisation grant). SR-025 step-up re-auth. `sec:review` label required. Data classification: the `/me` claims cache holds PII (display name, email) — it must not be persisted to `localStorage`.

## Accessibility notes
Route changes must move focus to the main landmark heading and announce the new route name plus the environment badge (SCR-010 a11y note: "the environment badge is announced on every route change"). The 403 and 404 surfaces use CMP-089 / CMP-090 with a heading and a named recovery action.

## Performance notes
Route-level code splitting: the admin branch and the replay branch are lazily loaded so they do not inflate the cold-start bundle (budget #10, ≤3 s). Guard loaders must not issue network requests on every navigation — they read the bootstrap cache; a stale cache is refreshed in the background, never blocking navigation.

## Observability
Metric `shell_route_change_ms` (histogram, labelled by route group). Log route-guard denials at info with the route ID and the reason, correlation-id propagated; never log the session cookie. Client denials are *not* audit events (the server-side 403 is the audited one) — this is stated in the code comment to prevent double-counting.

title: Build the hardened Electron main and preload processes (SR-110..SR-119)
body:
## Context
The Electron shell runs on the owner's trading host, alongside WSL, Docker, QuestDB and Postgres. A renderer compromise that reaches Node APIs is rated **Critical** (STRIDE E1, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9) because it is arbitrary code execution on the machine that holds the KEK. §6.11 therefore specifies a closed set of non-negotiable requirements SR-110..SR-119, and §9.4 makes `electron-hardening` a required CI check. R0 exit criterion 9 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.3) requires the shell to start with those switches enabled and to be *verified by an automated assertion, not by inspection*.

ADR-0011 remains `proposed`; per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16 this work builds against Electron behind the `ShellPort` from E10-K01, so the decision stays reversible.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/desktop/src/main.ts`: app bootstrap, single-instance lock, `BrowserWindow` factory that sets, for **every** window including pop-outs: `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `nodeIntegrationInWorker: false`, `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames: false`, `sandbox: true`, `webSecurity: true`, `allowRunningInsecureContent: false`, `experimentalFeatures: false`, `enableRemoteModule` absent (SR-110).
- `app://` custom protocol handler serving the built renderer bundle, with the SR-112 CSP applied as a response header plus a `<meta>` fallback: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' https://<tailnet-host> wss://<tailnet-host>; img-src 'self' data: blob:; worker-src 'self' blob:; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`. **No `unsafe-eval`.**
- Navigation lockdown: `will-navigate` and `setWindowOpenHandler` deny everything outside the app origin; external links open in the OS browser via `shell.openExternal` after an allow-list check.
- `apps/desktop/src/preload.ts`: `contextBridge` exposing the `ShellPort` surface as fixed, typed, allowlisted channels — **no** generic `invoke(channel, …)`, no `ipcRenderer` passthrough; arguments validated against a schema on both sides; unknown channels dropped and logged (SR-111).
- GPU flags from the E06 / ADR-0011 findings applied via `app.commandLine.appendSwitch`, recorded in a single documented list with the reason for each flag.
- `permissionRequestHandler` denying every Electron permission the app does not need (camera, microphone, geolocation, midi, notifications handled explicitly).
- KEK handle bridge: `keychain.getKekHandle()` returns an **opaque handle only** — never key material to the renderer (SR-119); the Electron main process holds no Bybit credentials and makes no exchange calls.
- Structured main-process logging into the E04 logger format, written to a local log file with redaction.

**Absorbed from the withdrawn E10-T03 (roadmap-line items only):**
- **Auto-update channel stub**: an `UpdateChannel` abstraction behind `ShellPort` plus a version check on boot and every 15 min against the E04 build-info endpoint. Download, signature verification and install are **not implemented**, and `capabilities.autoUpdate === false` until code signing exists (SR-115); the stub exposes only `getCurrentVersion()` and `checkForUpdate()` and can never install code.
- **Single-window baseline**: the hardened `createWindow()` factory ships here with one main window plus minimal saved bounds/maximised state under the Electron `userData` directory. Multi-monitor restore, tray and pop-out windows are E15.

## Out of scope
- Window-state persistence, tray, floating windows and the auto-update stub — E10-T03.
- The CI assertion suite itself and the security review — E10-X02 (this ticket makes the build assertable; X02 makes CI enforce it).
- Code signing and a real update feed (SR-115 keeps auto-update disabled until signing exists) — R5/E48.
- Any Tauri implementation.

- Multi-monitor window-state restore, the system tray and SCR-027 floating pop-out windows - **deferred to E15** (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` section 6.2 keys pop-out state to the layout, which E15 owns).
- Any auto-update *download or install* path - blocked by SR-115 until code signing lands in R5/E48; this ticket ships the disabled channel abstraction and nothing more.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every window is hardened
  Given a packaged production build
  When any BrowserWindow is created, including a pop-out
  Then contextIsolation, sandbox and webSecurity are true, nodeIntegration and its worker/subframe variants are false, and enableRemoteModule is absent

Scenario: CSP is exactly as specified
  When the renderer loads over app://
  Then the Content-Security-Policy response header matches SR-112 verbatim, no unsafe-eval is present, and no Bybit host (api.bybit.com, api-demo.bybit.com, api.bytick.com, stream*.bybit.com) appears in any directive

Scenario: Navigation escape is blocked
  When renderer code attempts window.open or a navigation to https://example.com
  Then the navigation is denied, nothing is opened inside the app, and the attempt is logged

Scenario: Preload exposes no generic IPC
  When the preload bridge is inspected at runtime
  Then window.shell exposes only the named ShellPort methods, ipcRenderer is not reachable, and invoking an unknown channel from the renderer is impossible because no channel name is caller-supplied

Scenario: KEK never reaches the renderer
  When the renderer calls keychain.getKekHandle()
  Then it receives an opaque handle string, and no code path exists that returns key material to the renderer
```

```gherkin
Scenario: The update channel cannot install code
  Given the packaged production build
  When a test exercises the update channel and requests an install
  Then capabilities.autoUpdate is false, no download is attempted, and the call is refused with UPDATE_CHANNEL_DISABLED
  And the electron-hardening job fails the build if an installer API is ever reachable (SR-115)
```

## Technical notes / design
Window options live in **one** `createWindow()` factory; a lint rule plus the E10-X02 assertion forbid `new BrowserWindow` anywhere else, so a future pop-out cannot be created with weaker options by accident.

Preload channel table is generated from the `ShellPort` interface (E10-K01) so drift is a type error. Both sides validate with a schema validator (zod or equivalent) — the main process must treat every renderer message as hostile input (STRIDE E2).

GPU flags: the exact list comes from the E06 benchmark findings; each flag is recorded in `apps/desktop/GPU_FLAGS.md` with the measurement that justifies it, because undocumented GPU flags are the classic source of "works on the reference machine only" (risk R8). `gpu.info()` exposes the probe result so the renderer can enter the `degraded-2d` path (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` F15) when WebGL2 is unavailable.

Dev-vs-prod: dev conveniences (devtools auto-open, relaxed CSP for the Vite dev server) are compiled out of production builds, and E10-X02's assertion fails the release if any leak through (SR-114, STRIDE E4).

## Test plan
- Unit: window-options factory returns the exact SR-110 option set; preload schema validation rejects malformed arguments; unknown-channel handling.
- Integration: CSP header presence and exact value on an `app://` response; navigation and `window.open` denial; permission handler denials.
- E2E (Playwright-Electron, E10-Q02): boot, assert hardening flags at runtime via the main-process test hook, assert no Bybit host in the CSP.
- CI gate: the `electron-hardening` required check (built in E10-X02).
Coverage >=85% on `apps/desktop/src` given the security weight.

## Security notes
This ticket **is** the SR-110..SR-119 implementation. Threats addressed: E1 (renderer→Node escalation), E2 (over-broad preload), E4 (dev flags leaking into release), and the SR-119 chokepoint rule that all Bybit traffic originates from the backend only. Data classification: the main process handles an opaque KEK handle (SECRET-adjacent) and session cookies within the Chromium session partition. `sec:review` label mandatory; Security engineer is a required code-owner on `apps/desktop/**` per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §9.3. Any deviation from §6.11 must be an explicit, dated accepted-risk entry signed by the Owner — never an undocumented default.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI. Two indirect obligations: the window title must include the environment word so the OS window list and the screen-reader window switcher disclose Demo vs Live (CMP-215 contract), and `prefers-reduced-motion` must be forwarded from the OS to the renderer rather than being swallowed by the shell.

## Performance notes
GPU flags are the main lever on budget #1 (frame time) and budget #10 (≤3 s cold start). The main process must not block `ready-to-show`: the window is created hidden and shown on first paint to avoid a white flash and to keep the measured cold-start honest. `app.whenReady()` → "shell interactive" instrumentation is emitted here and consumed by E10-Q04.

## Observability
Main-process structured logs (E04 format) to a rotating local file with redaction — never log cookies, tokens or the KEK handle. Metrics surfaced to the renderer for the health chips: `shell_gpu_available`, `shell_main_start_ms`. Events: `shell.gpu_unavailable` when the WebGL2 probe fails.

- `E06` — GPU flag findings and the ADR-0011 interim decision.

title: Implement shell bootstrap: /me, preferences, keymap and WS system topic
body:
## Context
SCR-010 lists its data sources as `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts`, `GET /api/v1/trade-groups` and the WS topics `system` and `recorder`. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` describes `/me` as "Single bootstrap call for the app shell… the UI uses this to decide which affordances to render; it is never the authorisation control itself", and pairs it with `/me/preferences` ("the app shell fetches it alongside `/me` on boot") and `/me/keymap` (used by SCR-012 and SCR-013). `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2 states that **`system` is auto-subscribed**: every authenticated connection is implicitly subscribed at `auth_ok`, it carries kill-switch transitions, feature-flag changes, degraded-data notices, connectivity changes and planned-shutdown warnings, and a client may not unsubscribe from it.

Every guard, every chip and the environment badge depend on this one bootstrap; doing it once, centrally, is what keeps cold start inside budget #10.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web/src/shell/bootstrap.ts`: a single parallel fetch of `GET /api/v1/me`, `GET /api/v1/me/preferences`, `GET /api/v1/me/keymap` on app start, exposed as a cache the route guards (E10-T01) and chrome (E10-S01) read synchronously.
- Application of preferences at the document root: `data-theme`, `data-density`, reduced-motion override, text scale — consuming the E05 theme runtime (this ticket wires, E05 owns the tokens).
- Environment resolution: the DEMO/LIVE value comes from `/me` and the WS `system` topic only; there is **no** client-side default and the badge renders an explicit "unknown" state until the value is known (SCR-150 rule: the environment is not shown until it is actually known).
- WS `system` consumption: connect on boot, honour the auto-subscription contract, and expose a typed `SystemUpdate` store (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9) feeding CMP-076 ConnectionStatus, CMP-210 HealthChips, CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner and the frozen/kill-switch chrome states.
- Reconnection with exponential backoff **1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s capped at 30 s with jitter** and a visible next-attempt time (SCR-152 performance note); on reconnect, restore subscriptions in priority order (private account state, focused panel, the rest).
- Offline detection driven by **actual request failure**, not only `navigator.onLine`, so a connected-but-unreachable tailnet is detected within 5 s (SCR-159 performance note).
- A `useShellState()` hook as the single read API for chrome components, so no component fetches `/me` itself.

## Out of scope
- The `/me`, `/me/preferences`, `/me/keymap` endpoints themselves (E09) and the WS gateway (E17).
- `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts` and `/trade-groups` consumption for the account picker — E27/E28 supply the data; E10 leaves the picker slot empty in R0.
- Recorder chip content (WS `recorder`) — E16; the chip slot exists but reports "not available" in R0.
- Preference *editing* UI (settings screens) — later settings epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One bootstrap, not many
  When the app starts
  Then exactly one request each to /api/v1/me, /api/v1/me/preferences and /api/v1/me/keymap is issued, they are issued in parallel, and no chrome component issues its own duplicate

Scenario: Environment is never guessed
  Given /me has not yet responded
  Then the environment badge renders an explicit unknown state and no DEMO or LIVE value is assumed; trading-capable affordances stay disabled until the value is known

Scenario: Preferences apply without reload
  Given the user's stored theme is high-contrast and density is compact
  When the bootstrap completes
  Then data-theme and data-density are set on the document root and the chrome renders in that theme without a page reload

Scenario: Reconnection backoff
  Given the WS connection drops
  Then reconnect attempts occur at approximately 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 s with jitter, the next attempt time is displayed, and subscriptions are restored in the documented priority order on success

Scenario: Tailnet unreachable
  Given the machine reports navigator.onLine true but every request to the backend fails
  Then the offline state is detected within 5 s and SCR-159 names the condition as a tailnet/backend reachability problem rather than a generic offline message

Scenario: Bootstrap failure is explicit
  Given /me returns 500
  Then the app shows the staged boot-failure state with a named recovery action (retry, sign in again, open diagnostics) rather than an empty shell
```

## Technical notes / design
The bootstrap runs before the router renders, but with a hard ceiling: if `/me` has not resolved within 5 s the "slow boot" state is shown explaining what is waiting (SCR-150 checklist). Preferences and keymap failures are non-fatal — the app proceeds with defaults and a warning, because a broken keymap must not prevent login.

The `SystemUpdate` payload is validated against the schema generated from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9 so a protocol drift surfaces as a contract-test failure rather than a silently missing chip.

Health chips update at 1 Hz from a store that is deliberately **outside** the workspace React tree, so a chip tick cannot re-render the chart subtree (SCR-010 performance note).

## Test plan
- Unit: backoff sequence and jitter bounds; offline detection from request failure; environment-unknown state machine; preference application to root attributes.
- Contract: `/me`, `/me/preferences`, `/me/keymap` responses against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; `SystemUpdate` frames against `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9 — both run in the `contract` CI job.
- Integration: bootstrap failure paths (401 → login, 500 → boot-failure state, timeout → slow-boot state).
- E2E: disconnect/reconnect drill with the WS gateway stubbed, asserting subscription restore order.

## Security notes
The `/me` cache holds PII (email, display name) and role claims: it is kept in memory only, never in `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, and is cleared on logout and on session revocation (a revoked session terminates the WS immediately per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5, which the client must treat as a hard logout rather than a reconnect). Role claims from `/me` are presentation hints only — never an authorisation decision (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §7.3). Never log the payload.

## Accessibility notes
Connection-state changes announce once via `role="alert"` on transition to degraded/offline and are not re-announced on every heartbeat (CMP-076 contract). The reconnect countdown is not announced on every tick (SCR-152). Health chips expose "label: state, value" as their accessible name. The slow-boot and boot-failure states have headings and named actions.

## Performance notes
This is the critical path for budget #10 (≤3 s cold start): the three bootstrap calls are parallel, the WS connects concurrently rather than after them, and nothing blocks first paint except `/me`. Health-chip updates are throttled to 1 Hz and isolated from the workspace subtree. Target time-to-usable after a 30 s outage is ≤5 s (SCR-152).

## Observability
Metrics: `shell_cold_start_ms`, `shell_bootstrap_ms` (per call), `shell_ws_state`. Events: `ws.disconnected {reason, subscriptions}`, `ws.reconnect_attempt {attempt}`, `ws.reconnected {outageMs, gapFilled}`, `shell.offline_detected {cause}`, `shell.tailscale_unreachable`. Correlation id from the HTTP bootstrap is carried onto the WS connection per E04.

title: Produce the STRIDE threat model for the app shell, routing and Electron wrapper
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes a STRIDE threat model per epic non-negotiable, and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes the kickoff a DoR item for any epic touching auth, keys or the OMS — the shell touches the session and the KEK bridge, so it qualifies. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9 already contains a partial model for the Electron shell (E1..E5) and §3 classifies asset A-16 (shell binary + auto-update) and actor AC-09 (Electron main process). This ticket completes that model for the *whole* E10 surface — which adds the routing/guard layer, the bootstrap, the deep-link parameter contract and the diagnostics bundle, none of which are covered by §5.9.

Doing this in Sprint 03, before E10-T02 lands, is deliberate: the model must shape the implementation, not audit it afterwards.

**Scope reconciliation (2026-09-14).** E10's roadmap allocation is **34 points** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register, §4.2, S03–S04). The first decomposition of this epic summed to 83 points — 2.4x its allocation and outside the ±15% tolerance band (28.9–39.1) — because it had absorbed work that the roadmap scope line does not place in R0. E10 has therefore been re-cut to exactly the roadmap line (route tree + guards; hardened Electron main/preload; auto-update channel **stub**; env badge in the global chrome; global keyboard-shortcut registry; error boundary + crash reporting to a local log) at **36 points**, and the remainder has been deferred to named later epics, not deleted — see the *Descope register* in the Epic ticket E10. No deferral removes an R0 exit criterion.


## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE decomposition of the E10 trust boundaries: B4 (renderer ↔ Electron main), the renderer ↔ backend boundary, and the OS ↔ main-process boundary (keychain, filesystem, tray, protocol handler).
- Data-flow diagram covering: bootstrap (`/me`, `/me/preferences`, `/me/keymap`), WS `system`, preload IPC channels, window-state file, crash log, diagnostics bundle, `app://` protocol handler, deep-link parameters.
- Per-element STRIDE rows with likelihood, impact, rating, existing control (SR-###) and residual risk, extending `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9 rather than duplicating it. Minimum coverage of these candidate threats:
  - Spoofing: a non-app origin loaded into a window; a forged `app://` request; a malicious deep link causing an unintended action on load.
  - Tampering: window-state or crash-log file tampering influencing main-process behaviour; unsigned update (E5).
  - Repudiation: a client-side denial not being audited server-side (by design) being mistaken for an audit gap.
  - Information disclosure: diagnostics bundle leaking tokens; `/me` cache persisted to storage; crash log containing PII; DEMO/LIVE misrepresentation leading a user to act on the wrong environment.
  - Denial of service: crash loop; reconnect storm against the backend; unbounded window creation.
  - Elevation of privilege: preload bridge abuse (E2); client-side guard treated as authorisation; step-up bypass by direct navigation or restored window.
- Abuse-case list handed to E10-X03 and to the E10-Q01 charters.
- Model merged into `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.9 as an extension, with any new SR requirement proposed explicitly.

## Out of scope
- Backend auth/RBAC threat modelling (E09's model) and the exchange boundary (E08's model).
- Penetration testing — R4/E43.
- Implementing controls; this ticket produces the model and the required-control list.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element has STRIDE coverage
  When the model is reviewed
  Then every data-flow element in the E10 DFD has each applicable STRIDE category either analysed or explicitly marked not-applicable with a reason

Scenario: Threats map to controls
  Then every threat rated Medium or above names an existing SR-### control or proposes a new one, with an owner and a target ticket

Scenario: The model shapes implementation
  Given the model is completed before E10-T02 merges
  Then any control it requires that E10-T02 does not yet implement is added to E10-T02's scope or filed as a blocking follow-up before E10 can close

Scenario: A threat has no adequate control
  Given a Critical or High threat with no sufficient control
  Then it is escalated to the Architect and Owner, and either a control is added or a dated accepted-risk entry is recorded with Owner sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Method: STRIDE-per-element over a DFD drawn in mermaid and committed alongside the model. Ratings use the likelihood/impact scale already used in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 so rows are comparable across epics. Each row records residual risk after controls, because "mitigated" without a residual statement is how risk quietly accumulates.

Particular attention to two shell-specific subtleties: (1) the client-side route guard is *not* a control and must be labelled as such in the model so a future reader does not credit it; (2) the DEMO/LIVE badge is a security control in the integrity sense — a user acting on a misrepresented environment is a real loss scenario, and it is modelled as an information-disclosure/tampering threat rather than as a UI concern.

## Test plan
The model's assertions are turned into testable claims: each control referenced must name the test that proves it (unit, ci-gate, e2e, manual-review), matching the "Verified by" column convention of `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6. Claims without a test are flagged.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security artefact. Classification of E10 data: session cookie (SECRET), `/me` identity (PII), KEK handle (SECRET-adjacent, opaque), window state and crash log (INTERNAL), diagnostics bundle (INTERNAL, must be redacted before it leaves the machine).

## Accessibility notes
One a11y-security intersection is explicitly modelled: environment and trading-disabled state must be perceivable non-visually, or a screen-reader user can be misled about which environment they are trading in.

## Performance notes
Models the DoS-shaped threats that are also perf concerns: reconnect storms (bounded by the capped backoff in E10-T04) and crash loops (bounded by the repeated-crash guard in E10-S04).

## Observability
The model lists which threats require detection rather than prevention (e.g. repeated step-up failures, unusual window-creation rates) and names the log or metric that provides it, feeding E04.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded with severity, affected control (SR-###) and owner.
- [ ] Every finding fixed, or accepted-risk with a dated Owner sign-off — never silently closed.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted on the ticket.
- [ ] `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if the analysis changed the model.
- [ ] Any new automated check added to CI as a blocking gate.

- [ ] Abuse-case list handed to `E10-X03` and `E10-Q01`.
- [ ] Every Medium+ threat has a named control and a test reference.
- [ ] Completed before `E10-T02` merges.

title: Run UX research on chart navigation, scale control and keyboard-first charting
body:
## Context
Everything else in E11 is parity work against a category norm the owner already has strong opinions about, formed over years in TradingView and DeepCharts. Designing the chart chassis from first principles would be both slower and worse than designing it from **observed** expectations — and getting pan/zoom feel, scale-lock behaviour or crosshair magnet wrong is the kind of defect that is felt on every single interaction but rarely reported as a bug ("it just feels off").

This research ticket exists because E11 introduces **two genuinely new interaction models** that have no obvious prior art to copy, and guessing at them would be expensive: (1) the **keyboard-first charting path** — a data cursor, keyboard rescale and keyboard crosshair that must be a *primary* path rather than a compliance afterthought (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6, CMP-190); and (2) the **equal-status data table** (SCR-045, `US-CHART-014`), which the standard insists is "not a stripped-down compliance minimum".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Participants**: the owner plus 2–3 account managers (the actual user population — `10-personas.md` Pavel/Marta/Viewer), plus **at least one screen-reader user** and one low-vision user recruited for the keyboard-first and table sessions. A11y sessions are not optional and not merged into the trader sessions.
- **Method**: 60-minute moderated sessions, split competitive walkthrough (TradingView, DeepCharts, Bookmap on the owner's own setup) + task-based think-aloud on a clickable prototype.
- **Research questions**, each with a decision attached so the study cannot end inconclusively:
  1. Which pan/zoom gesture bindings are expected, and which are *muscle memory* (wheel = zoom time vs scroll time is the highest-cost thing to get wrong)? -> fixes E11-S04's default bindings.
  2. What should happen to autoscale when the price axis is dragged — disengage silently, disengage with a badge, or ask? -> fixes `US-CHART-006`'s lock-badge behaviour and E11-S05.
  3. Is the crosshair magnet expected on by default, and snapping to OHLC or to the nearest price level? -> fixes E11-S07's default magnet mode.
  4. What does a keyboard-first user actually need to *do* on a chart, in priority order, and what is the minimum cursor-stepping vocabulary (bar, price level, page, extreme)? -> fixes E11-S13's key map.
  5. Is the data table a reading surface, a verification surface, or a working surface — and what column set makes it equal-status rather than a fallback? -> fixes E11-S14's default columns and its row actions.
  6. What does "aggregated" need to communicate so a trader trusts a zoomed-out chart? -> fixes E11-S12's disclosure wording.
- **Deliverables**: a findings report with a per-question decision, a prioritised issues list, session recordings/notes, and a one-page "chart interaction principles" summary pinned in the Figma file.
- **Competitive teardown** of scale menus and go-to-date flows in the three reference products, captured as annotated screenshots.

## Out of scope
- Visual design and hi-fi screens — **E11-D02**/**D03**/**D04**.
- Order-flow surfaces (footprint, heatmap, DOM) — researched in E18/E21's own design tracks.
- Quantitative A/B testing — the user population is single digits; this is qualitative research and an A/B test would be statistically meaningless.
- Usability testing of the *built* product — **E11-Q06**'s exploratory pass and the design-QA in E11-D08.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every research question ends in a decision, not a summary
  Given the six research questions above
  When the findings report is delivered
  Then each question has an explicit recommended decision, the evidence behind it and the E11 ticket it feeds
  And any question that could not be resolved is escalated with a named owner and a date, never left open

Scenario: Accessibility is researched with real users, not simulated
  Given the keyboard-first and data-table research questions
  When the sessions are conducted
  Then at least one screen-reader user and one low-vision user participated
  And their findings are reported as first-class results, not an appendix

Scenario: Findings reach the tickets that need them
  Given the findings report is signed off
  When E11-S04, E11-S05, E11-S07, E11-S12, E11-S13 and E11-S14 are inspected
  Then each carries the relevant decision and a link to the report
  And no engineering ticket is left guessing at a default that was researched

Scenario: Research lands before design needs it
  Given design work E11-D02 starts in Sprint 04
  Then this research is Done by the end of Sprint 03
  And a delay here is escalated immediately, because it pushes every downstream design and the design-ahead rule with it
```

## Technical notes / design
**Prototype fidelity is deliberately low** for gesture questions and deliberately high for the keyboard/table questions. Gesture feel cannot be tested in a clickable prototype at all — questions 1 and 3 are tested on the **E06 spike build** (a real engine prototype with real inertia), because asking someone how zoom should feel while looking at a static mock produces confident answers that do not survive contact with a scroll wheel. Questions 4 and 5 are tested on a semi-functional HTML prototype with real screen-reader output, since the only thing that matters there is what NVDA actually says.

**Session structure**: 10 min context, 20 min competitive walkthrough (their own tools, their own symbols — the owner's real workspace, not a demo account), 25 min task-based think-aloud, 5 min wrap. Tasks phrased as goals ("find where price rejected this level yesterday"), never as instructions ("click the go-to-date button"), so the navigation strategy is observed rather than dictated.

**Analysis**: thematic coding of session notes, with any finding that contradicts an existing planned behaviour flagged explicitly in the report — the contradictions are the valuable part and are easy to lose in a tidy summary.

## Test plan
Research validity rather than software testing:
- Task success/failure and time-on-task recorded per participant per task.
- Findings triangulated across at least two participants before becoming a recommendation; single-source findings are reported as such and marked lower confidence.
- The competitive teardown is verified against the live products at session time, not from memory or documentation.
- The report is reviewed by the CDO and the accessibility specialist before sign-off.

## Security notes
Research data handling: session recordings and notes contain participant identity and, for the owner's sessions, **live account context on screen** (balances, positions, symbols). Controls: recordings stored in the private research drive with access limited to the design and product leads; **the owner's sessions are conducted on the demo environment wherever possible**, and any accidental live-account capture is redacted before the recording is stored. No recording leaves the organisation. Consent captured in writing before each session, including consent for a11y participants to be recorded using their own assistive technology configuration.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is partly *about* accessibility, and the method has to match:
- At least one screen-reader user and one low-vision participant, recruited as participants rather than as reviewers.
- Sessions run with the participant's **own** AT setup and configuration, because the defaults people actually run with differ substantially from a clean install.
- Findings feed E11-S13 (keyboard cursor, live-region cadence) and E11-S14 (table as an equal-status surface) directly.
- Research materials themselves are accessible: the prototype is keyboard-operable, and consent forms and task sheets are provided in an accessible format.

## Performance notes
N/A — no runtime performance implications. One research-side note: the gesture-feel sessions must run on the **reference machine** (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §1), because inertia and zoom feel are inseparable from frame rate, and a finding gathered on a laggy laptop would be a finding about the laptop.

## Observability
N/A. The findings report itself is the artefact, linked from E11 and from each consuming ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.

## Dependencies

- Blocks **E11-D02** (and through it D03/D04/D06), and directly informs E11-S04, S05, S07, S12, S13, S14.

## Branch
