title: Wireframes: workspace shell, dock model, presets and sync - greyscale end to end
body:
## Context
With E15-D01's evidence in hand, this ticket settles the *structure* of the workspace surface in greyscale, before any pixel is polished. Wireframing first is not ceremony here: SCR-020 hosts every other panel in the product, so a structural mistake - a panel header that steals 40 px of chart height, a workspace switcher that hides which environment you are trading in, a sync badge that is unreadable at a glance - propagates into every screen E18..E41 will later drop into this shell. Fixing it in greyscale costs a day; fixing it after ten hi-fi files exist costs a sprint.

The wireframes cover the complete E15 surface as one coherent model: the workspace page and its tab strip (SCR-020), the docking interaction with all six drop targets and the mandatory keyboard move mode (SCR-021, CMP-214), the preset gallery (SCR-022), the sync configuration (SCR-023), the panel picker (SCR-024), workspace settings (SCR-025), import (SCR-026), the floating window (SCR-027), the panel context menu (SCR-028), the unsaved/conflict dialog (SCR-029), the multi-chart grid panel (SCR-049), the workspace switcher in the nav rail (SCR-011), the boot/restore state (SCR-150) and the reduced-capability layout (SCR-153).

Sprint 03 places this three sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story in Sprint 06, leaving Sprints 04-05 for hi-fi and Sprint 06 as slack.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Greyscale wireframes** for every screen listed above, at 1920x1080 and at the 1280x800 minimum from SCR-020's sign-off checklist, showing real content density (a chart with a footprint, a DOM ladder, a positions grid) rather than lorem rectangles.
- **The layout tree model** drawn explicitly: how a `LayoutTree` (CMP-081 prop) maps to what the user sees - rows, columns, tab groups, leaf panels - and what each split/tabify operation does to that tree. This diagram is the shared vocabulary for design, FE and the `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}` payload.
- **Docking storyboard** (SCR-021): drag start, hover over each of the six targets (N/S/E/W/centre-tabify/float), the translucent result preview, invalid-drop feedback, drop commit, and the undo path. Drawn as frames, not described in prose.
- **Keyboard move mode storyboard**: the CMP-216 PanelMenu "Move panel" path - directional chooser, live preview, commit, cancel - proving that no layout operation is pointer-only, per CMP-214's mandatory keyboard equivalent.
- **Sync model wireframes** (SCR-023): the six axes as independent switches, lettered group badges on panel headers, the "conflicting sync" warning, and the per-pane scale-link state from US-LAY-004 including the refusal case when two panes have incompatible price magnitudes.
- **State inventory per screen**: loading skeleton, empty workspace, populated, unsaved (`*` on tab), save conflict, restored-after-crash, too-many-panels warning, panel-too-small compact view, reduced-capability - each drawn, none described only in a note.
- **Flow diagrams** (mermaid, into `docs/design/specs/e15-layout-flows.md`): create workspace, switch workspace with unsaved changes, apply a preset over a dirty layout, add a panel, float and re-dock, export then import on another machine.
- **Hotkey map** for the layout layer: `Ctrl+1..9` presets, `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+Shift+S`, `Alt+drag` move, `F11` full-screen panel, `Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right` cycle panels, `F6` region cycle, `Ctrl+Shift+1..3` sync group, `Ctrl+Shift+0` unsync, `Shift+F10` panel menu - cross-checked against the global hotkey table so that US-LAY-006's conflict scenario has a concrete list to detect conflicts against.
- **Validation round**: a clickable greyscale prototype tested with the Owner plus two participants from E15-D01, focused on the three interactions research flagged as risky (preset over dirty layout, sync prediction, keyboard move).

## Out of scope
- Colour, type, elevation, iconography and final spacing - all deferred to E15-D03..D12.
- Motion timing and easing (E15-D14).
- The internals of any hosted panel (chart, DOM, ticket) - represented as labelled rectangles.
- Design-system token or component authoring (E15-D13).
- The Electron window-management implementation detail; SCR-027 is wireframed as a window with chrome, not as an OS integration spec.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E15 screen exists in greyscale at both reference widths
  Given the wireframe file is reviewed
  When SCR-011, SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-023, SCR-024, SCR-025, SCR-026, SCR-027, SCR-028, SCR-029, SCR-049, SCR-150 and SCR-153 are walked
  Then each has frames at 1920x1080 and 1280x800
  And at 1280x800 no frame contains an overlap or a clipped control

Scenario: No layout operation is pointer-only
  Given the docking storyboard and the keyboard move storyboard
  When every operation in the pointer storyboard is enumerated (move, split, tabify, resize, float, close, maximise)
  Then each has a named keyboard equivalent drawn in the keyboard storyboard
  And the equivalents are reachable from CMP-216 PanelMenu and from a documented shortcut

Scenario: Applying a preset over unsaved work is never silently destructive
  Given a workspace with unsaved layout changes
  When a preset is applied from SCR-022
  Then the wireframe routes through SCR-029 with Save / Discard / Cancel as explicit verbs
  And no destructive option is the default focus

Scenario: Sync prediction improves over the research baseline
  Given the greyscale prototype is tested with three participants using the E15-D01 stimulus configurations
  When they predict the effect of changing the symbol in one pane
  Then prediction accuracy is at least 5 of 6 configurations per participant
  And any configuration still mispredicted is redesigned before sign-off

Scenario: A panel is dragged somewhere it cannot go
  Given a panel is dragged over a region that cannot accept it (for example a leaf below minimum size)
  Then the wireframe shows the invalid-drop treatment and a plain-language reason
  And the drag can be cancelled with Esc, returning the panel to its origin with no layout mutation

Scenario: The workspace fails to restore
  Given a saved workspace references a delisted symbol (US-LAY-002 edge case)
  Then the affected pane is drawn in an explicit error state naming the symbol
  And the remaining panes are drawn as loaded, proving partial restore is designed rather than an all-or-nothing failure
```

## Technical notes / design
The single most consequential structural decision is **chrome budget**. Every pixel spent on tab strip, panel header, sync badge and status bar is a pixel not showing market data, and SCR-020 stacks up to four levels of chrome above a chart. The wireframes must state a maximum total vertical chrome allowance at 1280x800 and demonstrate the layout inside it, with the compact density mode showing how it shrinks.

The layout tree diagram matters beyond design: CMP-081 takes `layout: LayoutTree` and the workspace document is persisted through `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, so design, FE and API must share one mental model of what a split is. Draw the tree next to the rendered result for at least three non-trivial layouts (2x2, 1+3, a tabified stack inside a column).

Crash restore (SCR-020's "Restored your layout from 14:02") is designed here rather than bolted on, because it changes the tab strip's information design - the user must be able to tell a restored layout from a saved one before they hit `Ctrl+S` and overwrite a good workspace with a recovered one.

The "too many panels" case (>16 per SCR-020, and US-LAY-001's confirmation-with-measured-frame-cost requirement) is drawn as a real frame showing where the measured cost appears and what the confirm step says. A warning that cannot be located is not a warning.

## Test plan
(1) Screen-by-screen walkthrough against the sign-off checklists already written in `14-screens-catalogue.md` for SCR-020..029, SCR-049 and SCR-153 - every checkbox in those lists is treated as an acceptance item here. (2) Flow walkthrough of the six mermaid flows with the FE lead, checking each is buildable against the `/workspaces` API surface. (3) Moderated greyscale prototype test (Owner + 2 participants) on the three risky interactions. (4) Keyboard-path audit: attempt every operation with a pointer disallowed. (5) 1280x800 overlap sweep. (6) Traceability check that every one of US-LAY-001..008 maps to at least one wireframe frame.

## Security notes
The workspace surface is where environment confusion becomes dangerous: a panel shows a DEMO position while the ticket next to it is bound to LIVE. The wireframes must establish, structurally, that the environment is visible from every panel that can place an order and from every floating window (SCR-027, CMP-215) - not merely once in the top bar. SCR-020's checklist already requires DEMO and LIVE chrome variants; this ticket draws them. Additionally, the import wireframe (SCR-026) must show, in copy, that an imported workspace carries no credentials and no account bindings (US-LAY-007), and the export preview must visibly enumerate what is included so that a user sharing a workspace with a manager can verify it before sending.

## Accessibility notes
The wireframes specify the structural a11y contract that hi-fi will style: each panel is a `role="region"` with an accessible name that includes panel type, symbol and interval ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1m"); `F6` cycles regions and `Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right` cycles panels; the active panel has a focus affordance that is not colour-only; layout changes are announced through a polite live region ("Layout changed to 2 by 2", "Chart moved to bottom right") per CMP-081 and CMP-214; splitters are `role="separator"` with arrow-key resize and announced `aria-valuenow`; sync-group membership is conveyed by letter and name, never by colour alone. The keyboard move storyboard is a first-class deliverable, not an appendix.

## Performance notes
Structure drives cost. The wireframes must encode three performance-protecting decisions so hi-fi cannot undo them: (1) panels mount lazily on first visibility and hidden tabs unsubscribe after 30 s, so the empty/loading frames show a skeleton rather than data; (2) a layout change must never remount the WebGL context, so the tab and preset flows are drawn as re-parenting, not as re-creation; (3) the drag preview is a single translucent rectangle drawn with transforms, never a live panel, so the storyboard shows a ghost. The budgets these protect are US-LAY-001's >=55 fps with four order-flow panes and US-LAY-002's <=3 s four-pane restore.

## Observability
The wireframes annotate where each analytics event fires, using the names already fixed in the screens catalogue: `layout.panel_added`, `layout.panel_removed`, `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.maximised`, `layout.saved`, `layout.reset`, `layout.preset_previewed`, `layout.preset_applied`, `sync.group_changed`, `layout.conflict_detected`, `layout.conflict_resolved{choice}`, `layout.imported`, `layout.import_rejected{reason}`. Annotating on the wireframe means FE inherits the instrumentation plan with the structure instead of retrofitting it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Wireframes complete for all 14 screens at 1920x1080 and 1280x800, with real-density content.
- [ ] Layout tree model diagram merged and agreed with the FE lead and the API owner.
- [ ] Docking and keyboard-move storyboards complete; pointer/keyboard parity audit passed.
- [ ] State inventory drawn for every screen (no state exists only as a note).
- [ ] Six flow diagrams merged into `docs/design/specs/e15-layout-flows.md`.
- [ ] Layout hotkey map cross-checked against the global hotkey table with conflicts listed.
- [ ] Greyscale prototype test run; sync prediction accuracy >=5/6 per participant or the failing configurations redesigned.
- [ ] Every sign-off checklist item from `14-screens-catalogue.md` for SCR-020..029, SCR-049 and SCR-153 is either satisfied or explicitly deferred to a named hi-fi ticket.
- [ ] Chrome budget at 1280x800 stated numerically and demonstrated.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 03, three sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 consuming stories.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D01** - research findings, especially the sync defaults, preset ranking and docking go/no-go.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` sign-off checklists for the E15 screens.
- E05 design system v0 for the greyscale primitives and density scale.
- E10 app shell structure (SCR-010) - the workspace mounts inside it; the chrome budget must be agreed with E10's shell design.

## Branch

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-011, SCR-020..029, SCR-049, SCR-150, SCR-153

title: UX research: how a trader must experience a degraded or dropped feed
body:
## Context
The WS protocol has three distinct failure and degradation modes that a trader must be able to tell apart instantly, because each implies a different action:

1. **Stale** - the connection is alive but a topic has not updated for longer than expected (`14-screens-catalogue.md` section 0.5.4: shading after 2 s, last-good timestamp always shown).
2. **Degraded fidelity** - the connection is healthy but the server has classified it `lagging`/`saturated` and is multiplying throttles and forcing coalescing (`23-ws-protocol.md` section 8.3). Data is *correct* but *less frequent*. There is no equivalent in any charting product the Owner currently uses, and it is easy to mis-communicate as "broken".
4. **Disconnected/resyncing** - transport down (SCR-152) or a topic is rebuilding after a sequence gap (SCR-050 has an explicit "Book resynchronising..." state).

Getting this wrong has a trading consequence, not a cosmetic one: a trader who believes a frozen book is live will hit a price that no longer exists, and a trader who abandons a perfectly good chart because a yellow banner looked alarming has lost the trade for no reason. `23-ws-protocol.md` section 10.3 already fixes the *classes* of UI treatment; this research fixes the *vocabulary and prominence* inside those classes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3 moderated sessions (Owner plus up to 2 account managers), 40 minutes, driven by a scripted harness that injects each transport state into a live-looking workspace: stale topic, `connection_quality: saturated`, book resync, full disconnect, planned `shutdown_notice`, `slow_consumer` close.
- Probes: "what just happened?", "is the price on screen safe to trade on?", "what would you do now?", "which of these two states is worse?".
- Competitive scan of how TradingView, Sierra Chart/DeepCharts and the Bybit web terminal signal a stale or degraded feed - specifically whether they distinguish degraded-cadence from disconnected at all.
- Findings in `docs/design/research/e17-feed-states.md`: a ranked severity ordering of the six states, the plain-English label the Owner recognises for each, the minimum prominence each needs, and 5-8 adopted decisions each phrased as a testable statement a wireframe can satisfy or violate.
- A recommendation on the **degraded-fidelity** case in particular: banner, chip, or in-panel only - and whether `coalesced_count` should drive a visible "feed compressed" indicator on the tape-speed widget as `23-ws-protocol.md` section 8.2 suggests.

## Out of scope
- Visual design of any kind - greyscale wireframes begin in E17-D02.
- The recorder's "history starts at ts" empty state (E16) and the ingestion-lag half of CMP-092 (E04).
- Recruiting participants outside the Owner's circle.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every transport state has an evidenced treatment
  When docs/design/research/e17-feed-states.md is reviewed
  Then all six states are listed with a recommended label, prominence and severity rank, each traceable to a specific observation

Scenario: Degraded fidelity is distinguishable from disconnection
  Given participants were shown the saturated-class state and the disconnected state back to back
  Then the report records whether they distinguished them unaided and recommends the treatment that made the distinction reliable

Scenario: A safety misread is caught
  Given a participant treats a stale price as tradeable
  Then the incident is recorded verbatim and drives a decision that raises the prominence of the stale treatment

Scenario: A finding contradicts the catalogue
  Given a finding contradicts 14-screens-catalogue.md section 0.5.4 or 23-ws-protocol.md section 10.3
  Then it is raised as an amendment proposal to that document rather than silently designed around
```

## Technical notes / design
The injection harness is a thin dev-only page driving CMP-076/077/078/092 from a scripted frame log; it does not need the real backend and must not be promoted to production code. Frame scripts are taken verbatim from the worked sessions in `23-ws-protocol.md` section 12 (12.7 slow-consumer degradation then recovery is the key one for the degraded case; 12.3 sequence gap and recovery for the resync case).

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validity control: the same six states are shown in a different order to each participant so ordering does not manufacture the severity ranking.

## Security notes
Session recordings follow `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md`; no real account identifiers, balances or API keys appear in the harness - fixtures only.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session is run with a screen reader active so the announcement policy (assertive once per change for offline/degraded, polite for stale) is validated with a user rather than asserted in a spec.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

title: Confirm the heatmap column legibility band (DES-HEATMAP-01)
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` section 6.1.1 resolves former open item W3 by making `heatmap.time_bucket_ms` a **derived** value rather than a constant: a heatmap column should occupy between **2 and 8 device pixels**, with a **3 device-pixel target** encoded as the `/3` divisor in

```
ideal_ms  = (window_seconds * 1000) / (pane_css_width_px * devicePixelRatio / 3)
bucket_ms = smallest allowed value >= ideal_ms from {100, 250, 500, 1000, 5000}
```

plus a normative ladder clamp (never select 5000 when `ideal_ms <= 2500`) and a server fallback of `500` when the option is absent.

The section is explicit about ownership: "the design team owns only the *visual* band (the 2-8 device-pixel legibility range and the 3 px target) and the 'auto' affordance's appearance. Any change to those two numbers changes the formula's `/3` divisor and the clamp threshold, and therefore requires a change to this section plus a re-run of `heatmap_bucket_selection` - it cannot be adjusted silently in CSS or component code." This ticket is the named **DES-HEATMAP-01**, scheduled in Sprint 03 exactly as that section states, and it exists so the band is *confirmed on real displays* before E17 ships the protocol option and E21 builds the heatmap.

Getting the band wrong is expensive in both directions: too fine wastes bandwidth on columns the renderer aggregates away, too coarse throws away DOM detail a 4 K pane could show (the bandwidth table in section 6.1.1 spans 0.3 KiB/s to 16 KiB/s across the ladder).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Render a reference heatmap at 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 device pixels per column on the two reference displays named in section 6.1.1 (**3840x2160 at 100% scale** and **1920x1080 at 100%**), plus a half-width pane case, and judge legibility of a liquidity band and of a single-column wall.
- Confirm or amend the **2-8 device-pixel band** and the **3 px target**. If either changes, file the amendment to `23-ws-protocol.md` section 6.1.1 in the same review - the number may not diverge between design and spec.
- Design the **"auto" affordance** on the heatmap pane: how a user sees that bucket size is auto-derived, how they pin it manually (ladder rule 1), and how they hand control back. Include the state where a re-derivation is pending behind the 400 ms debounce.
- Provide the reference-values table of section 6.1.1 as a design-side sanity check: confirm the selected rung for each listed display reads acceptably.

## Out of scope
- The heatmap renderer, its colour mapping (green=bid/red=ask per locked decision) and its interactions - **E21**.
- The transport-side implementation of the option and the `ctl` re-derivation path - E17-S02/E17-T04.
- `price_grouping` legibility (E21).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The band is confirmed on real hardware
  Given the reference heatmap is rendered at 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 device pixels per column on a 4K and a 1080p display
  Then the review records for each width whether a liquidity band and a single-column wall are legible
  And the 2-8 band and the 3 px target are either confirmed verbatim or amended with a stated reason

Scenario: An amendment propagates
  Given the review concludes the target should not be 3 device pixels
  Then a PR amending 23-ws-protocol.md section 6.1.1 formula and clamp accompanies the design decision
  And the heatmap_bucket_selection unit test expectations are updated in the same change

Scenario: The auto affordance is designed
  Then the pane shows its current bucket, whether it is auto or pinned, and offers a keyboard-reachable control to pin and to return to auto

Scenario: Debounced re-derivation is visible, not silent
  Given a pane is resized across a rung boundary
  Then the drawn behaviour during the 400 ms debounce and the subsequent re-snapshot is specified, and does not present a blank pane as an error
```

## Technical notes / design
Use a static recorded column set (BTCUSDT, depth 200, price_grouping 1) rendered at fixed widths - this is a legibility judgement, not a live test, so a screenshot-grade harness is sufficient. Device-pixel width per column = `pane_device_px / columns_in_window`; state the DPR of each capture explicitly, because a 150%-scaled 4 K and a 100% 2 560 display produce identical device-pixel counts and must be recognised as the same case.

## Test plan
The `heatmap_bucket_selection` unit test in `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.4 is the enforcement mechanism; this ticket only changes its expectations if the band changes. No new tests here.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
The heatmap is a canvas surface and needs an equal-status non-canvas alternative under `05-accessibility-standard.md`; that alternative is E21's scope, but the auto/pinned bucket control designed here must itself be keyboard-reachable and announce its current value.

## Performance notes
Directly sets the steady-state bandwidth of the most expensive public topic: 16 KiB/s at 100 ms down to 0.3 KiB/s at 5 000 ms per the section 6.1.1 table, and determines whether the 2 000-column snapshot cap binds (it does at 100 ms and 250 ms).

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Captures at all five column widths on both reference displays attached to the ticket.
- [ ] Band and target confirmed, or amended with an accompanying PR to `23-ws-protocol.md` section 6.1.1.
- [ ] "Auto" affordance drawn with pinned, auto and re-deriving states.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off jointly by the chart-engine lead and the protocol owner (joint ownership is stated in section 6.1.1).
- [ ] Decision recorded so E21 inherits it rather than re-litigating it.

## Dependencies
- **E05** tokens for the pane chrome around the affordance.

## Branch
`design/e17-des-heatmap-01`

- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md section 6.1.1 (normative), section 16.4 heatmap_bucket_selection
- docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md section 3.8
- docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md budget #14

title: Machine-JSON registry: schema/target validation, recursive key walk (CV-C57), machine_hash, Stately export
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** absorbs E50-T44 (CV-C57); validation feeds the library factory instead of a shim.

The chart JSON is the normative contract (ADR-0016 Part 1). The registry is the single loader: it validates before `create_machine` ever sees a chart.

Runtime: xstate-statemachine==0.9.1 (tag v0.9.1 = 45bb7f3; wheel == tag 42/42; sha256 d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162; PEP 740 attested). There is no in-house shim and no dual runtime; this ticket builds directly on the library.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/registry.py`: loads `machines/B<nn>.<id>.machine.json`, JSON-Schema (2020-12) validation, absolute-target resolution, recursive `KNOWN_MACHINE_KEYS` walk incl. inline `invoke.src` (CV-C57)
- `machine_hash = sha256(canonical_json(chart))`; `registry.hash(key)`; `registry.export_stately(key)`
- `tools/statechart/render_catalogue.py`: regenerates `28-statechart-catalogue.md` tables; `make gen && git diff --exit-code` in CI
- Negative fixtures per rule

## Out of scope
- Hash lock file and upcasters (E50-T02)
- Authoring charts (E50-S01/S02)

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Unknown key anywhere is rejected
  Given a chart with an unknown key inside a nested invoke.src
  When registry.validate runs
  Then it raises naming the machine and the JSON path
Scenario: Relative or unknown target rejected
  Given a transition target ".child" or "#b01.nope"
  Then validation fails before create_machine is called
Scenario: machine_hash is stable
  When the same chart is loaded twice with keys reordered
  Then registry.hash returns the same sha256
```

## Technical notes / design
- Canonical JSON: sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8
- Library-side `strictTargets` is belt-and-braces; our validator runs first

FINAL mandatory config block (79-r14 §7, applied unconditionally by `statechart/factory.py`): `strict_config=True` + chart `"strictConfig": true`; recursive key walk (CV-C57); `actionErrorPolicy:"rollback"`; `guardErrorPolicy:"raise"` on order/control charts with an ordered unguarded auditing fall-through; `onUnhandled:"defer"` (control lane escalates via `CvErrorHooks`); `strictTargets:true`; `strict=True, event_schemas=CV_EVENT_SCHEMAS`; `max_queue_size=CV_INBOX_BOUND[lane], overflow_policy="refuse"`; `maxIterations` sized to the descent plateau (CV-C62); `service_pool_size` order 32 / control 8 / platform 16; injected `clock=`; plugins `[CvErrorHooks(), CvMetricsPlugin(), CvAuditPlugin()]` (restores pass `from_snapshot(plugins=...)`); `await asyncio.wait_for(interp.start(), CV_START_TIMEOUT)`; async `Interpreter` only (MUSTNOT-06).

## Test plan
- Unit tests per validation rule
- Round-trip `export_stately` on all registered charts
- Contract-suite membership: runs inside `tests/xstate_contract/` (or its lint/registry jobs) with `pytest -W error::RuntimeWarning`; both service spellings (`def`→coroutine and `async def`).

## Security notes
Library imported only via `candleviewer.statechart` (CV-LINT-IMPORT); pin is hash-locked and attestation-verified in CI (E50-T57). No secrets in machine context or snapshots.

## Accessibility notes
Not applicable: backend/tooling ticket with no UI surface.

## Performance notes

title: Run an exploratory charter on observability blind spots and build the regression pack
body:
## Context
Scripted tests (E04-Q01) prove that the signals we thought of work. The residual risk in an observability baseline is the signal nobody thought of — the subsystem that can fail in a way no metric expresses, the state that renders as healthy because the probe measures the wrong thing. That is exploratory territory, and it is best spent *before* R1 builds twenty modules on top of this foundation.

This ticket also assembles the durable regression pack so the epic's guarantees survive later refactors, and closes the epic's QA obligations for the R0 epic-level sign-off (Epic DoD: *"an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA"*).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charter 1 — "Lie detector"**: *Explore the system's health reporting with the goal of making it report healthy while something is genuinely broken.* Time-boxed 4 h. Techniques: stop a component after its probe has cached a good result; saturate a queue without crossing a threshold; desync a topic while its connection stays up; fill disk to 79%; stall a writer without erroring.
- **Exploratory charter 2 — "Silence detector"**: *Explore the alerting path with the goal of producing a real failure that generates no notification.* 4 h. Techniques: break Alertmanager's outbound path; fire during a quiet-hours window; produce a condition whose metric is emitted by a module that is down (so the series goes absent rather than crossing a threshold — the classic `absent()` gap); fire two alerts whose inhibition rules suppress each other.
- **Exploratory charter 3 — "Leak hunt"**: *Explore every output surface (logs, metrics labels, health details, alert payloads, support bundle, dashboard panels) for secret or PII exposure.* 3 h, run jointly with the Security engineer feeding E04-X02.
- A **regression pack** added to CI: the canary-secret suite, the health-matrix suite, the near-miss alert suite (promtool), the dashboard metric-existence check, the cardinality-guard test and the announcement-throttling test — the set of assertions whose silent breakage would leave the system blind.
- A written blind-spot report: conditions the system genuinely cannot currently detect, each either accepted with a rationale or filed as a ticket against the owning epic (E08 ingestion, E29 OMS, E16 recorder).
- Epic-level QA sign-off for E04.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fixes found (filed as Bugs/Tasks against the owning ticket).
- Full chaos drills (E45).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given charter 1 is executed for its full time box
When findings are reviewed
Then every technique attempted is documented with its outcome, and any case where the system reported healthy while broken is filed as a Bug at priority/p1-high or above

Given charter 2 discovers a real failure that produces no notification
Then the gap is either closed in-sprint (for example by adding an absent() guard or an inhibition-rule correction) or accepted in writing by the Owner with the residual risk recorded in 32-risk-register.md

Given charter 3 is executed across all six output surfaces
Then each surface is explicitly cleared or has a finding filed, and the results are handed to E04-X02 as input to the security review

Given the regression pack is added to CI
When any of its assertions is deliberately broken in a scratch branch
Then CI fails, proving the pack is actually wired in and not merely present

Given the epic-level pass is complete
Then a QA sign-off comment is posted on E04 listing scenarios covered, defects found, defects outstanding and residual risk
```

## Technical notes / design
Exploratory work is documented session-style (charter, duration, coverage areas, notes, bugs, obstacles, follow-ups) so it is auditable and repeatable, not anecdotal. The most productive technique in charter 1 is attacking the *caching* introduced for performance: a 2 s probe cache and a 1 Hz UI poll create a window where the displayed state is stale by design — establish that the window is bounded and that `last_good_at` makes the staleness visible rather than hiding it.

For charter 2, the highest-yield case is the absent-series gap: when a module dies, its metric stops existing, and a rule of the form `metric > threshold` can never fire. Confirm every such rule has an `absent()` companion — a systematic, checkable property rather than a one-off finding.

## Test plan
Charters as above. Regression-pack verification is itself tested by deliberate breakage in a scratch branch (the "is the smoke alarm wired in" check). Fixtures reused from E04-Q01.

## Security notes
Charter 3 is a security-adjacent exercise run with the Security engineer; findings feed E04-X02's review and, if a secret is found in any output surface, a `priority/p0-critical` Bug with the `security` label is filed immediately and the exposure window assessed (which environments, which retention, who could have read it).

## Accessibility notes
Exploratory pass includes a keyboard-only and screen-reader traversal of any observability UI available at this point (the chrome components from E04-D02); findings filed with the `a11y` label. Full audit is E47 for the app as a whole.

## Performance notes
Charters must not be run against an environment where a performance measurement is being taken for the record — schedule around E04-K01/T06 benchmark runs, or the benchmark measures the exploration.

## Observability
The blind-spot report is the deliverable that most directly improves observability: it enumerates what the system cannot currently see.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All three charters executed within their time boxes and documented session-style.
- [ ] Findings triaged: fixed, filed with priority, or accepted in writing with a risk-register entry.
- [ ] Regression pack merged into CI and verified by deliberate breakage.
- [ ] Blind-spot report published and follow-ups filed against owning epics.
- [ ] Epic-level QA sign-off posted on E04.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated for R11 residual risk.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

**Sprint-window justification (Sprint 04 vs E04's declared window S02–S03).** `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 104/187 allocates E04 the window **S02–S03**, which prices and schedules the *engineering build*. This ticket runs an exploratory charter and builds a regression pack **over shipped observability code**, all of which only exists once `E04-T05`, `E04-S01` and `E04-Q01` complete at the end of Sprint 03. Scheduling it inside S02–S03 would force exploration against half-provisioned dashboards and an unrouted Alertmanager, so every finding would be an artefact of incompleteness rather than a real blind spot; the epic QA sign-off required by `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 is by definition a post-build gate. This is trailing verification, not build scope: it consumes no S02–S03 capacity, no other epic depends on its output before Sprint 05, and the R0 exit criteria it feeds are assessed at the R0 milestone at the end of Sprint 04. The deviation is recorded in the sprint-window reconciliation table on the `E04` epic ticket.

`E04-Q01` (scripted coverage must exist first so exploration targets the gaps rather than duplicating), `E04-D02` (a11y baseline for the UI traversal).

title: Security review, abuse cases and SAST rules for logging, metrics and diagnostics
body:
## Context
Closes the security half of the epic's DoD: the STRIDE model from E04-X01 identified the threats; this ticket verifies that the shipped code actually resists them, and converts the durable properties into automated rules so they cannot silently regress once twenty more modules start logging. DoD §8 makes security sign-off non-optional for anything touching key handling — and the redaction filter is precisely the control standing between an API secret and a log file.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case execution** against staging, from E04-X01's list:
  1. As a Manager and as a Viewer, attempt to read `/admin/health` detail, `/admin/incidents`, generate a support bundle and set a log-level override — all must 403 and be audited.
  2. Attempt to reach `/metrics`, Grafana, Prometheus and Alertmanager from outside the private network — all must be refused.
  3. Attempt log injection via `X-Correlation-Id`, via a symbol parameter, and via a telemetry payload field — none may alter the log field structure or forge another request's id.
  4. Attempt to smuggle a secret into a support bundle via a config value, a log line and an exception message — the pre-write scan must fail generation in all three cases.
  5. Attempt a cardinality explosion via the telemetry endpoint's `screen` field and via a symbol label — the guard must hold and the process must not OOM.
  6. Attempt a log flood via the runtime log-level override — TTL cap, namespace scoping and disk-guard must hold.
  7. Inspect a real alert notification payload for account ids, order ids or key material.
- **SAST/lint rules** (Semgrep + ESLint + ruff/bandit), merged into the CI ruleset from E03:
  - Ban `print()` and direct `logging.getLogger()` in application modules (must use the `cv.obs` logger factory).
  - Ban bare `asyncio.create_task` outside `cv.obs` (correlation loss).
  - Ban direct `prometheus_client` imports outside `cv.obs` (bypasses the registry, `env` label and cardinality guard).
  - Flag any f-string interpolation of a variable named like a secret into a log call (SR-120's "no free-form string interpolation").
  - Flag any new Prometheus label name not on the approved label allow-list.
  - Frontend: SR-127 rules already required (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without sanitiser) verified to cover the health-chrome components.
- **DAST**: an OWASP ZAP baseline pass against the api in staging, scoped to the observability endpoints (`/health/*`, `/admin/health`, `/admin/incidents`, `/admin/log-level`, `/telemetry/frontend`, `/admin/support-bundle`), with findings triaged.
- **Secrets-scanning verification**: confirm gitleaks covers `infra/grafana`, `infra/prometheus`, `infra/alertmanager` (dashboard and rule files are exactly where an embedded webhook token or datasource password gets committed by accident).
- **Permission/key checks**: verify log files and bundle output are `0600`/`0700`, that log directories are excluded from CI artefact upload (SR-124), and that the alert webhook secret is injected at runtime and absent from the repo and from images.
- Security sign-off comment on E04 and on each child ticket carrying the `security` label.

## Out of scope
- Penetration testing (E43, pre-R4 gate).
- Auth/RBAC implementation review (E09's own security tickets) — this ticket only verifies enforcement *on the observability endpoints*.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given every abuse case from E04-X01 is executed against staging
When results are recorded
Then each case either fails safely with the expected status code, audit row and no data disclosure, or is filed as a security Bug at priority/p0-critical or priority/p1-high

Given a developer adds a module that calls logging.getLogger() directly and logs an f-string containing api_secret
When CI runs
Then the Semgrep rules fail the build naming both violations, before review

Given a webhook token is committed into an Alertmanager config file in a scratch branch
When gitleaks runs in CI
Then the build fails and the secret is identified

Given the ZAP baseline scan completes against the observability endpoints
Then zero Critical/High findings remain unresolved, and any Medium has a dated accepted-risk entry per the R0 quality gate

Given a real Page-severity alert notification is captured
When its payload is inspected
Then it contains component, severity, threshold and runbook link, and contains no account id, order id, symbol-plus-size combination or key material
```

## Technical notes / design
The rules that matter most are the *structural* ones (ban the bypass) rather than the *pattern* ones (detect the bad string). A Semgrep rule that greps for "password" in log calls catches the careless case; a rule that forbids obtaining a logger outside the sanctioned factory makes the redaction filter unbypassable by construction. Prefer the latter, and allow-list the handful of legitimate exceptions explicitly with a comment convention rather than weakening the rule.

For the cardinality abuse case, run it against a process with a memory limit set so a failure is a clean OOM-kill in staging rather than an unbounded host-memory consumption — and assert the guard fires *before* memory grows, not that the process survives.

## Test plan
- Abuse cases executed manually against staging and, where automatable, converted into E2E tests added to the regression pack (E04-Q02) so they re-run forever.
- SAST rules unit-tested with positive and negative fixtures (a rule that never fires is as useless here as an alert that never fires).
- ZAP baseline wired as a scheduled CI job, not a one-off.
- Permission checks scripted and added to the deployment smoke test.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security verification for threats K1 (High), U5, D3 and asset A-17 from `04-security-program.md`. Findings are triaged per the R0 quality gate: zero Critical/High unresolved, Medium requires a dated accepted-risk entry. Any confirmed secret exposure triggers the exposure-assessment procedure (which environments, what retention, who had read access) and, if a live key is implicated, immediate rotation per SR key-rotation requirements.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — security verification. Any a11y defect noticed incidentally is filed with the `a11y` label against E04-D02.

## Performance notes
The cardinality and log-flood abuse cases double as performance-guard verification; record the measured behaviour (memory ceiling held, disk guard triggered) against the E04-T03/T02 controls.

## Observability
Confirms that SR-125's security-relevant metrics are exported and alerted on, and that `log_redactions_total` and `metric_cardinality_breach_total` are wired into the alert rule set as early-warning signals of a control being exercised.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every abuse case executed with recorded outcome; failures filed with priority and linked.
- [ ] SAST/lint rules merged into the CI ruleset with positive/negative fixtures and green.
- [ ] ZAP baseline job scheduled; findings triaged to the R0 gate.
- [ ] gitleaks coverage of `infra/**` verified by deliberate-commit test.
- [ ] File permissions and secret-injection checks scripted into the deployment smoke test.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted on E04 and on each `security`-labelled child.
- [ ] `04-security-program.md` updated with any new SR agreed in E04-X01.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

**Sprint-window justification (Sprint 04 vs E04's declared window S02–S03).** `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 104/187 allocates E04 the window **S02–S03**, which prices and schedules the *engineering build*. This ticket reviews code delivered by `E04-T01..T06` and `E04-S02`, the last of which merges at the end of Sprint 03. A security review, abuse-case execution and SAST rule authoring can only assess merged artefacts — the support bundle, the alert payloads and the redaction filter must all exist before threats against them can be executed; the R0 SAST / SCA / secrets gate of `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 is a milestone gate, not a sprint-internal one. This is trailing verification, not build scope: it consumes no S02–S03 capacity, no other epic depends on its output before Sprint 05, and the R0 exit criteria it feeds are assessed at the R0 milestone at the end of Sprint 04. The deviation is recorded in the sprint-window reconciliation table on the `E04` epic ticket.

- Fix-or-file: trivial drift is fixed in the same sprint; anything else becomes a prioritised Bug linked to this ticket and to the owning story.

title: Write and execute component black-box test plan and exploratory charter
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 requires a QA-executed black-box test plan with a per-scenario sign-off before any Story reaches Done, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires an exploratory charter alongside scripted tests. A design system is deceptively easy to under-test: unit tests pass per component while cross-component composition (a Combobox inside a Dialog inside a reduced-motion high-contrast comfortable-density context) breaks.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box test plan covering E05-S01, E05-S02, E05-S03 and E05-S04 grouped by band, with one executable scenario per Gherkin AC in those stories plus composition scenarios not owned by any single component.
- Composition scenarios (the point of this ticket): Combobox inside Dialog (focus trap vs listbox portal), Toast while a Dialog is open, Menu inside a scrollable Drawer, Table reflow at 200% zoom with compact density and high-contrast theme, hold-to-confirm under reduced motion (progress must still be perceivable without animation), Tooltip on a disabled-with-reason control.
- An exploratory charter (session-based, 2 x 90 min): 'explore theme x density x motion x zoom combinations looking for clipping, unreadable text, lost focus and stuck overlays'.
- Defect log with priorities; regression candidates handed to E05-Q03.
- Per-scenario pass/fail sign-off comments on the owning stories.

## Out of scope
- Automated test implementation (owned by the stories themselves).
- a11y-specific audit (E05-Q02) and visual regression (E05-Q03).
- Application screens (none exist in R0 outside E09/E10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Plan covers every story AC
  Given the ACs of E05-S01..E05-S04
  When the plan is reviewed
  Then every scenario maps to at least one executable test-plan step, with no AC unmapped
Scenario: Composition defects are hunted deliberately
  Then the plan contains at least the six named composition scenarios and records a result for each
Scenario: Exploratory charter produces evidence
  Given two timeboxed exploratory sessions
  Then session notes list what was explored, what was found and what was not covered
Scenario: Sign-off blocks Done
  Given any failing scenario without an accepted-risk note
  Then the owning story cannot be moved to Done
```

## Technical notes / design
Execute against the built Storybook (the black-box surface for a library package), in Chromium at the Electron version, at 1280x800 (minimum supported viewport) and 1920x1080 (primary target), across 3 themes x 2 densities x motion-safe/reduce, at 100% and 200% zoom. Below 1280x800 the advisory state is expected rather than a reflow - verify that too.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the test activity. Deliverables: the plan document under `docs/plan/` or the QA space, execution results, and the defect log.

## Security notes
Include one abuse-oriented step per safety control: attempt to satisfy the hold-to-confirm gate with a single synthetic click event, and attempt to trigger an RbacGate-wrapped action by dispatching a click directly on the disabled control. Both must fail; findings go to E05-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Keyboard-only execution of at least one full pass (no mouse) is mandatory; anything unreachable is a defect regardless of axe result.

## Performance notes
Record subjective jank observations during theme/density switching on the 500-row table story; any observed stall is escalated against E05-T02's measured budget.

## Observability
Defect log linked from the epic; recurring classes proposed as automated tests.

- [ ] All scenarios executed; results recorded per scenario.
- [ ] Exploratory session notes attached.
- [ ] Defects filed with priorities and linked to owning stories.

title: Run a11y audit of design system v0 (axe sweep plus manual screen reader)
body:
## Context
R0's quality gate for a11y is 'axe-core zero violations on Storybook and on the auth + shell routes; manual keyboard pass' (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#44-quality-gates`), and R0 exit criterion 8 requires 'zero axe-core violations'. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#8-screen-reader-test-protocol` additionally defines a manual SR protocol with a coverage matrix that automation cannot substitute for - roughly 70% of real a11y defects (wrong accessible name, illogical order, missing announcement) are invisible to axe.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Full axe-core sweep across every Storybook story in all three themes and both densities; plus a `pa11y-ci` complementary-ruleset sweep as specified in `03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Manual screen-reader passes per the section 8.1 coverage matrix on the v0 components, using the screen-reader/browser combinations named in that standard.
- Keyboard-only pass: every interactive component operated without a pointer, including the hold-to-confirm gate, the combobox, the table's row navigation and the skip link.
- 200% zoom and 125% text-scale pass verifying reflow without clipping (CMP-049 Table specifically).
- Reduced-motion pass verifying no information is lost when animation is suppressed.
- Findings logged with WCAG SC references and severities; blocking findings fixed before the epic closes.

## Out of scope
- Design-contract sign-off (E05-D04) - this is execution, that is the gate.
- Application screens and routes (audited by E09/E10 and later by E47).
- Chart-engine canvas a11y (E11 onward; the DOM-mirror strategy is specified in `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6 but not implemented in R0).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Zero automated violations
  Given every v0 Storybook story in 3 themes x 2 densities
  When axe-core and pa11y-ci run
  Then zero serious or critical violations are reported
Scenario: Accessible names are correct, not merely present
  Given each interactive component under a screen reader
  Then the announced name matches the component's documented accessible-name table, and a name that is present but wrong is logged as a defect
Scenario: Keyboard-only completion
  Given no pointer device
  When every documented interaction is attempted
  Then all complete successfully, including the hold-to-confirm gate and the table row navigation
Scenario: 200% zoom
  Given a dense table at compact density and 200% zoom
  Then content reflows with no clipping and no loss of data
Scenario: No information lost under reduced motion
  Given data-motion="reduce"
  Then every state change previously conveyed by motion is still conveyed by a non-motion cue
Scenario: Blocking findings gate the epic
  Given an unresolved serious finding
  Then the epic DoD cannot be met
```

## Technical notes / design
Follow the manual protocol in `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 8.2, which the standard requires to be run per new/changed screen at design/dev handoff and per release candidate. Record the exact SR/browser versions used so results are reproducible. Any defect that axe *could* have caught results in a follow-up to tighten the automated rule set rather than relying on the manual pass to catch it again.

## Test plan
This ticket is the audit. Automated portions run in CI (already wired by E05-T03); the manual portions produce a signed report.

## Security notes
No security surface, but note that an accessible-name leaking a secret (e.g. announcing a masked API key) would be a security defect - explicitly check CMP-034 MaskedValue's announcements.

## Accessibility notes
Full-scope: WCAG 2.2 AA is the conformance target (`05-accessibility-standard.md` section 1). Keyboard (section 3), colour independence (4), contrast (5), reduced motion (7), SR protocol (8) all in scope.

## Performance notes
Record whether enabling reduce-motion measurably reduces frame work, per SCR-117's performance claim; a claim that does not hold is a defect.

## Observability
Audit report published as a CI artefact link on the epic; violation counts by severity recorded as the R0 baseline.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Automated sweep green (zero serious/critical) across all themes/densities.
- [ ] Manual SR passes executed per the coverage matrix with versions recorded.
- [ ] Keyboard-only, 200% zoom and reduced-motion passes executed.
- [ ] All findings logged with WCAG SC references; blocking ones fixed.
- [ ] Report attached; Accessibility role and QA both sign off.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed to automate any manually-caught defect class.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E05-S04` (complete v0 set), `blocked_by: E05-T03` (axe/pa11y harness). Feeds the epic DoD and R0 exit criterion 8.

## Branch
`chore/design-system-a11y-audit` (report + any test-rule tightening).

## References
- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9
- docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#43-exit-criteria

body:
## Context

- Define the triage workflow for a VR diff: who reviews, what counts as intentional, how a baseline update is approved.
- Execute a full epic-level regression run against `main` and record results.
- Record the epic QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per story group; list any accepted deviations explicitly.
- Hand over a one-page 'how to not break the design system' note for consuming epics (E10 first).

title: Implement interactive control atoms CMP-001..CMP-010 with full state matrix
body:
## Context
Every form, dialog, settings section and trading control in CandleViewer is built from these ten atoms. `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` section 1 specifies each of CMP-001..CMP-010 with Props, Variants, States, A11y contract, tokens used, Storybook stories and test requirements; section 0.3 adds the cross-cutting rules (dark-first, density-aware, colour-never-alone, keyboard contract, motion pair, numeric typography, test baseline, story organisation). Shipping these first unblocks S02/S03 and the R1 screen epics. This is the first engineering story of E05 and therefore the one that establishes the pattern every later component follows.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/ui/src/components/`: CMP-001 Button, CMP-002 IconButton, CMP-003 SegmentedControl, CMP-004 Toggle (Switch), CMP-005 Checkbox, CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-007 TextInput, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-009 Select, CMP-010 Slider.
- Each with: typed props per the catalogue entry, all documented variants and states (default/hover/focus/active/disabled/loading/error where applicable), `density` support, tokens-only styling, Storybook stories covering the full Variants x States matrix, an interaction (play-function) story, and unit tests.
- CMP-008 NumericStepperInput renders values in `font.family.mono` with tabular numerals and right alignment (cross-cutting rule 6) - it is the base of every price/qty input later used by the order ticket.
- Disabled-with-reason: any disabled state accepts a `reason` and surfaces it via tooltip + accessible description (CMP-079 pattern), never a bare disabled control.
- US ids served (system foundations): US-SET-001 (settings controls), US-SET-004, US-SET-005, US-SET-007.

## Out of scope
- CMP-011..CMP-039 (E05-S02) and molecules (E05-S03).
- Trading-specific numeric inputs with side tinting (CMP-1xx, R3 epics) - only the mono/tabular base behaviour lands here.
- Form validation orchestration (CMP-040 FormField, E05-S03).
- Server-backed state of any kind.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full matrix is rendered and snapshot-stable
  Given any of CMP-001..CMP-010
  When its Storybook stories are built
  Then every Variant x State combination documented in 15-component-catalogue.md has a story
  And each renders in dark, light and high-contrast at both densities
Scenario: Keyboard contract
  Given CMP-003 SegmentedControl has focus
  When ArrowRight is pressed
  Then selection moves to the next option per the WAI-ARIA radiogroup pattern and is announced
  And Tab moves focus out of the group, not between options
Scenario: Disabled states explain themselves
  Given a Button disabled with reason "Requires Owner role"
  When it receives hover or keyboard focus
  Then the reason is shown and is present in the accessible description
Scenario: Numeric input is tabular
  Given CMP-008 with the value 1234.50
  Then it renders in font.family.mono with tabular numerals, right-aligned
Scenario: Invalid numeric entry
  Given CMP-008 with min 0 and step 0.1
  When the user types -5 and blurs
  Then the error state is shown with a message, the value is not silently coerced, and aria-invalid is set
Scenario: Loading button cannot double-submit
  Given a Button in loading state
  When it is clicked or activated with Enter twice
  Then onClick fires zero additional times and the control is announced as busy
Scenario: No hardcoded values
  When lint runs over these components
  Then zero raw hex or px values are reported
```

## Technical notes / design
Each component follows the WAI-ARIA APG pattern named in its catalogue entry: Button (button), SegmentedControl (radiogroup), Toggle (switch), Checkbox (checkbox with indeterminate), RadioGroup (radiogroup with roving tabindex), TextInput/NumericStepperInput (textbox with `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`), Select (the native-pattern dropdown documented in the catalogue - native `select` semantics, styled shell), Slider (slider with `aria-valuemin/max/now/text`). Controlled and uncontrolled modes both supported. Focus ring via the CMP-039 FocusRing utility, 2px offset, `color.focus.ring`. Props are typed with no `any`; `mypy`-equivalent strictness is TypeScript `strict` from E02. NumericStepperInput parses with an explicit decimal-precision prop rather than locale-guessing, because the locale formatting utility (US-SET-006) lands later and must not be forked here.

## Test plan
Unit (Vitest + Testing Library) per component: props/variants/states rendering, controlled/uncontrolled behaviour, disabled does not fire handlers, error state sets `aria-invalid` and links `aria-describedby`. Interaction (play functions): keyboard paths for every component (Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter/Space/arrows), loading double-submit guard, Slider keyboard increments incl. PageUp/PageDown/Home/End. a11y: `vitest-axe` per story, zero serious/critical. Visual regression: baseline captured by E05-T04 across theme x density. Fixtures: none external. Coverage >=80% lines on the touched files, no regression to the package baseline.

## Security notes
No secrets, no network, no PII. Threats considered: (a) a `reason` string rendered as HTML would be an XSS vector - all text props render as text nodes, never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; (b) NumericStepperInput will later carry order quantities, so silent coercion of an out-of-range value is a safety bug, not a UX nit - explicitly tested above. Data classification: internal, non-sensitive.

## Accessibility notes
Binding per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 3: every control reachable by Tab/Shift+Tab, operable per its APG pattern, visible focus ring >=3:1 at 2px offset, keyboard table documented in the Storybook docs page (a DoD gate per section 11.6). Compact-mode hit targets >=24x24px, or an essential-exception from E05-D07's list logged in the component's Storybook a11y notes. Colour never alone: error state pairs `color.status.danger` with an icon and message text. Manual screen-reader spot-check required for each new interactive control (folded into E05-Q02).

## Performance notes
Atoms must render without layout-measuring effects (no ResizeObserver, no `getBoundingClientRect` in render) so a 500-row table of inputs stays inside the frame budget in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. No component may subscribe to the theme store unless it renders theme-dependent state, preserving E05-T02's no-re-render guarantee.

## Observability
No runtime telemetry from atoms. Storybook CI logs axe counts per story.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests referencing the scenario name.
- [ ] Coverage >=80% on `packages/ui`, gate green.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated if the implementation diverged from the catalogue draft.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on all new stories; keyboard-only path verified manually once per component.
- [ ] design-qa: built components compared to the Figma spec by a designer (formal pass in E05-D05).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (E05-Q01 plan executed for this group).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review (Storybook walkthrough).
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. code-owner; feature-flag state: N/A (library package, not runtime-gated).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E05-D02` (designs must be Done - design-ahead rule), `blocked_by: E05-D06` (handoff checklist), `blocked_by: E05-T03` (Storybook harness), `blocked_by: E05-T06` (icons for CMP-002). Blocks E05-S02.

This ticket starts 1 sprint after its design dependency is Done, not the >=2 sprints required by `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (Team & cadence) and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1. title: Implement display, feedback and utility atoms CMP-011..CMP-039
body:
## Context
The second atom band carries the system's information-display and feedback vocabulary: typography primitives (the mechanism that enforces tabular numerics app-wide), status badges, loading and empty/error states, tooltips/popovers, and the small utilities that later trading components depend on (CMP-032 confidence dots and CMP-034 MaskedValue in particular are safety-relevant). `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` section 1 specifies each entry.

## Scope / Deliverables
- CMP-011 Tag/Chip, CMP-012 Badge, CMP-013 Avatar/ProfileBadge, CMP-014 Spinner, CMP-015 Skeleton, CMP-016 Tooltip, CMP-017 Popover, CMP-018 Divider, CMP-019 Icon, CMP-020 Typography primitives (Text, Heading, NumericText, MonoText), CMP-021 Link, CMP-022 Kbd, CMP-023 ProgressBar, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-025 AvatarGroup, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError, CMP-028 Callout/Banner, CMP-029 Skeleton-Chart placeholder, CMP-030 Divider-Label, CMP-031 ColorSwatch/ThemeChip, CMP-032 Confidence Dots, CMP-033 CopyButton, CMP-034 MaskedValue, CMP-035 Countdown/Timer, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-037 SwatchLegendItem, CMP-038 InlineSpinnerText, CMP-039 FocusRing utility.
- CMP-020 NumericText enforces `font.feature.tabularNums` at the component level (catalogue rule: 'enforced at the CMP-020 level, not left to per-usage CSS').
- CMP-031 ColorSwatch and CMP-037 SwatchLegendItem are the primitives SCR-116 uses for palette selection (US-SET-005).
- CMP-032 Confidence Dots is the non-colour cue for estimated/heuristic values.
- Full Storybook matrix, interaction stories where interactive (Tooltip, Popover, CopyButton, MaskedValue), unit tests.

## Out of scope
- CMP-227 EstimatedBadge (trading band, later epic) - CMP-032 is its dependency only.
- Molecules (E05-S03).
- CMP-024 Sparkline data-fetching or streaming behaviour; it takes a static array in v0.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tabular numerics are enforced centrally
  Given a column of values rendered with CMP-020 NumericText
  Then every glyph advances identically and the digits align, with tabular-nums applied by the component and not by the consumer
Scenario: Tooltip keyboard and dismissal
  Given a focusable trigger with a Tooltip
  When it receives keyboard focus
  Then the tooltip appears and is linked via aria-describedby
  And Escape dismisses it while focus remains on the trigger
Scenario: Popover focus management
  Given an open Popover
  Then focus is moved into it, Tab is contained where the catalogue specifies a trap, and Escape returns focus to the trigger
Scenario: Masked value never leaks by default
  Given CMP-034 MaskedValue holding a secret
  Then the default state is masked, reveal is explicit, and the revealed value auto-remasks after the configured timeout
Scenario: Estimated confidence is not colour-only
  Given CMP-032 rendering low confidence
  Then the level is conveyed by filled-dot count and an accessible text label, not by hue alone
Scenario: Skeleton respects reduced motion
  Given data-motion="reduce"
  When a Skeleton renders
  Then the shimmer loop does not run and a static two-tone fill is shown
Scenario: Empty and error states are first-class
  Given CMP-026 and CMP-027
  Then each renders a title, a description and an optional action, and is announced appropriately (error via role="alert" where transient)
```

## Technical notes / design
Tooltip/Popover built on a single positioning primitive shared between them so behaviour cannot diverge; collision handling flips rather than clips. CMP-024 Sparkline renders to inline SVG (not canvas) at this size so it stays accessible and snapshot-testable; it exposes an accessible summary (`role="img"` plus a computed label such as '12 points, trending up 3.4%'). CMP-034 MaskedValue: reveal is a deliberate action, never a hover; copy-to-clipboard copies without logging and announces 'copied' politely. CMP-039 FocusRing is a non-visual utility export (a CSS class/mixin plus a hook) consumed by every interactive component rather than each redefining `:focus-visible`.

## Test plan
Unit per component (props/variants/states). Interaction: Tooltip focus/Escape, Popover focus containment and restore, CopyButton clipboard mock, MaskedValue reveal/auto-remask timer with fake timers. a11y: `vitest-axe` per story; explicit assertions for `aria-describedby` wiring, `role="alert"`, and Sparkline's accessible name. Reduced-motion tests for Spinner/Skeleton. Visual regression via E05-T04. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
CMP-034 MaskedValue is directly security-relevant: it will display API-key fragments and TOTP recovery codes in E09/E27. Requirements: masked by default, explicit reveal, time-limited reveal, no value in DOM attributes when masked, never written to logs or analytics, clipboard write does not echo the value. This component must be re-reviewed by the Security engineer in E05-X02. Data classification of the component's *inputs*: secret.

## Accessibility notes
Tooltip and Popover are the two most commonly mis-implemented a11y patterns - both must follow the APG pattern exactly, including Escape handling and focus restore. All status-carrying atoms (Badge, Tag, Callout, Confidence Dots) pair colour with icon/text per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 4. Live-region usage is deliberately conservative to avoid the verbosity problem US-SET-007 calls out.

## Performance notes
Sparkline must handle up to 200 points without measurable jank; Skeleton shimmer is CSS-only. No atom may attach a global scroll or resize listener - positioning primitives attach listeners only while an overlay is open.

## Observability
CopyButton and MaskedValue expose optional callbacks so consuming screens (e.g. key management) can emit audit events; the atoms themselves emit nothing.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios covered by automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage gate green.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` updated where implementation diverged.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader spot-check on Tooltip, Popover, MaskedValue.
- [ ] Security engineer has reviewed CMP-034 specifically.
- [ ] design-qa pass (E05-D05) covers this band.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded; demoed at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E05-S01` (shares the focus-ring utility, token conventions and story conventions established there). Blocks E05-S03.

## Branch

title: Implement molecules: forms, overlays, table and navigation primitives
body:
## Context
Molecules compose the atoms into the patterns every screen reuses: form fields with labels and errors, menus, tabs, dialogs (including the confirm-dialog pattern that US-SET-003's destructive-action policy will build on), toasts, drawers, the base data table that every grid in the app derives from, and the command palette that US-SET-002's global hotkey layer opens (SCR-012). `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` section 2 specifies each.

## Scope / Deliverables
- CMP-040 FormField, CMP-041 Menu, CMP-042 Tabs, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-045 Toast, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-047 DatePicker/DateRangePicker, CMP-048 Combobox/AutoComplete, CMP-049 Table (base data table), CMP-050 Card, CMP-054 SearchBox, CMP-059 CommandPalette, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-069 InfoPanel.
- CMP-044 ConfirmDialog ships all three confirm gates as variants - standard dialog, typed-confirm, and hold-to-confirm with a visible progress indicator and configurable 300-2000 ms duration - because US-SET-003 (Must) requires the policy and the hold duration to be configurable, and the later settings screen must not invent its own control.
- CMP-049 Table ships the zoom/text-scale reflow behaviour required by `16-design-system-brief.md#3` rule 4 (at high zoom, dense tables reflow to a stacked/card layout rather than clipping) as a required, tested state.
- CMP-059 CommandPalette provides the primitive SCR-012 composes; the global hotkey registration itself is E10.
- Full Storybook matrix, interaction stories, unit tests.

## Out of scope
- CMP-051..CMP-053, CMP-055..CMP-058, CMP-060, CMP-061, CMP-064, CMP-066..CMP-068 (deferred to the epic that first needs them).
- Screens composing these (SCR-012, SCR-029 etc.) - later epics.
- Virtualised rendering for very large tables (added by the epic that first needs 10k+ rows); v0 Table renders a bounded row count.
- Server-side sorting/pagination.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Form field wires label, help and error
  Given CMP-040 with a label, help text and an error
  Then the control has an accessible name from the label, aria-describedby referencing both help and error, and aria-invalid true
  And the label is persistent, never placeholder-only
Scenario: Dialog focus contract
  Given an open CMP-043 Dialog
  Then focus moves to the dialog, Tab is trapped inside, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the invoking element
  And the background is inert to both pointer and screen reader
Scenario: Hold-to-confirm gate
  Given CMP-044 in hold variant with an 800 ms duration
  When the user presses and releases after 400 ms
  Then the action does not fire and the progress indicator resets
  And a keyboard-only path exists that achieves the same gate without a pointer
Scenario: Typed confirm
  Given CMP-044 in typed variant requiring the text FLATTEN
  When any other text is entered
  Then the confirm control remains disabled with a stated reason
Scenario: Table reflow at 200% zoom
  Given a dense CMP-049 Table in compact density
  When the page is zoomed to 200%
  Then rows reflow to a stacked layout with no horizontal clipping and no loss of any column's data
Scenario: Toast does not steal focus
  Given a Toast appears while the user is typing
  Then focus is not moved, and the message is announced politely (assertively only for errors)
Scenario: Combobox keyboard
  Given CMP-048 with filtered options
  When ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Enter/Escape are used
  Then the APG combobox pattern is followed and the active option is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
Overlays (Dialog, Drawer, Popover-based Menu, CommandPalette) share one focus-management primitive and one scroll-lock primitive so behaviour cannot diverge per component; inertness uses `inert` where supported with an `aria-hidden` fallback. Toast host is a single portal (the CMP-212 ToastHost organism later wraps it). CMP-049 Table exposes column definitions declaratively, supports sticky header, keyboard row navigation and per-cell `NumericText` usage for numeric columns (mono/tabular/right-aligned per cross-cutting rule 6). Reflow threshold is expressed in `em` so it tracks text scale rather than device pixels.

## Test plan
Unit per component. Interaction: dialog focus trap and restore, Escape handling, hold-to-confirm timing with fake timers (fires at >=duration, not before), typed-confirm disabled-until-match, combobox keyboard matrix, tabs roving tabindex, table keyboard navigation and reflow at simulated 200% zoom. a11y: `vitest-axe` per story plus explicit assertions for dialog `aria-modal`, toast live-region politeness, and form-field description wiring. Visual regression via E05-T04 incl. the reflowed table state. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
CMP-044 ConfirmDialog is a safety control: it will gate flatten, cancel-all, reverse and freeze (US-SET-003). Threats: a confirm gate that can be satisfied programmatically or by a stray Enter keypress defeats the safety invariant. Tests must prove the hold gate cannot be satisfied by a single synthetic click and that the typed gate requires exact text. Flagged for the Security engineer's review in E05-X02. No secrets handled directly.

## Accessibility notes
Dialog/Drawer/Menu/Combobox each follow their APG pattern exactly. The hold-to-confirm gate must have a documented, tested keyboard-only equivalent - a pointer-only safety gate would exclude keyboard users from destructive actions entirely, which `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 3.1 forbids. Table reflow at 200% zoom implements section 5.7 of that standard. Toast politeness levels follow section 6.2.

## Performance notes
Table must render its bounded v0 row count within one frame; overlay open/close uses the motion recipes (CSS transitions) so no JS animation loop runs. Scroll-lock must not cause layout shift (compensate for scrollbar width).

## Observability
ConfirmDialog exposes an `onConfirm` metadata callback carrying the gate variant used, so downstream trading screens can write the audit event that `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-003 requires ('the choice is audited').

- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` updated where implementation diverged.

title: Implement theming, density, preview and app-state components
body:
## Context
US-SET-004 (themes and density, Must), US-SET-005 (colour conventions and CVD-safe palettes, Must) and US-SET-007 (accessibility preferences, Must) are delivered on SCR-116 and SCR-117 by the later settings epic - but those screens are explicitly composed (per `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` rows US-SET-004/005/007) from CMP-062 ThemeSwitcher, CMP-063 DensityToggle, CMP-031 ColorSwatch, CMP-037 SwatchLegendItem, CMP-228 PreviewTile, CMP-065 FormSection and CMP-069 InfoPanel. This story ships the design-system half so the settings epic assembles rather than invents. It also ships the app-state components (CMP-079, CMP-085, CMP-089, CMP-090, CMP-091) the E10 shell needs on day one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- CMP-062 ThemeSwitcher: dark / light / high-contrast selection driving the E05-T02 runtime, plus the optional 'match system' mode (default off).
- CMP-063 DensityToggle: compact / comfortable, global and per-panel scoped.
- CMP-228 PreviewTile: renders a live sample of a chart cell, a ladder row and a positions row under the currently-selected theme/density/palette - the control SCR-116 uses to preview a choice before committing it.
- CMP-079 RbacGate: the disabled-with-reason wrapper; in v0 it takes an explicit `allowed`/`reason` pair (the RBAC policy source arrives with E09).
- CMP-085 SkipLink, CMP-089 ForbiddenState (403), CMP-090 NotFoundState (404), CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback.
- Storybook stories demonstrating all three themes x two densities x motion-safe/reduce.
- US ids served: US-SET-004, US-SET-005, US-SET-007 (system-level primitives), plus the shell's 403/404/error surfaces.

## Out of scope
- SCR-116 and SCR-117 screens themselves, and persistence of preferences to the server (settings epic).
- The actual RBAC policy decision point and role model (E09).
- Chart palette *application* to WebGL surfaces (E11) - PreviewTile renders a static representative sample, not a live engine canvas.
- Crash reporting wiring behind CMP-091 (E10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Theme switch is immediate and complete
  Given CMP-062 in any story
  When high-contrast is selected
  Then the root data-theme becomes high-contrast within one frame, buy/sell resolve to their .hc variants, and no component remounts
Scenario: Match-system is opt-in
  Given a fresh profile
  Then 'match system' is off and the explicit user choice governs
Scenario: Preview before commit
  Given CMP-228 PreviewTile and a candidate CVD-safe palette
  When the palette is selected in the preview
  Then the tile updates to show a chart cell, a ladder row and a positions row in that palette without applying it globally
Scenario: Contrast warning on a failing combination
  Given a candidate custom palette whose text pair falls below 4.5:1
  When it is previewed
  Then a warning is shown stating the combination fails contrast
Scenario: Disabled-with-reason
  Given CMP-079 wrapping an action with allowed=false and reason "Viewer role cannot place orders"
  Then the control is non-operable, the reason is visible on hover and focus and present in the accessible description
Scenario: Skip link
  Given a page with CMP-085 as the first focusable element
  When Tab is pressed from the document start
  Then the skip link becomes visible and activating it moves focus to the main landmark
Scenario: Error boundary fallback
  Given a child component throws
  Then CMP-091 renders with a description, a retry action and a reference id, and the error does not blank the whole shell
```

## Technical notes / design
CMP-062/CMP-063 subscribe to the E05-T02 external store for their own checked state only - they must not cause a tree-wide re-render (this is the component-level half of the no-remount guarantee). CMP-228 PreviewTile renders DOM/SVG samples using the same semantic tokens the engine will later consume, and takes an optional token-override map so a candidate palette can be previewed without mutating the document root. The contrast warning reuses the ratio function shipped by E05-T05 rather than a second implementation. CMP-079 exposes `allowed`, `reason` and an optional `requiredRole` for message templating; it renders the reason via tooltip plus `aria-describedby`, never as a bare disabled attribute.

## Test plan
Unit: theme/density setters, match-system default off, RbacGate blocks handler invocation, error boundary catches and renders fallback, 403/404 states render their documented content. Interaction: keyboard operation of ThemeSwitcher and DensityToggle; skip-link tab-then-activate path; preview palette override does not leak to the document root. a11y: axe per story; explicit assertion that the reason text is in the accessible description. Perf: reuse E05-T02's no-remount assertion in a story containing a 500-row table plus these controls. Visual regression across the full theme x density matrix. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
CMP-079 RbacGate is a **UI affordance, not an authorisation control** - this must be stated in its docs and its Storybook notes: server-side deny-by-default enforcement (E09) is the real control, and a disabled button is never the security boundary. This note is a required outcome of E05-X01's STRIDE model (spoofing/elevation branch) and is re-checked in E05-X02. CMP-089 ForbiddenState must not leak why access was denied beyond the role requirement (no resource existence disclosure).

## Accessibility notes
This story is the a11y showcase band: SCR-117 is described in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` as 'itself the exemplar'. The high-contrast theme, the reduce-motion pathway and the skip link all land here. Every control has a visible persistent label and its state announced on change. PreviewTile must expose its sample content as text as well as visuals so a screen-reader user can evaluate a palette choice's labelling, not just its colours.

## Performance notes
Theme/density switch inherits E05-T02's one-frame budget; PreviewTile must re-render on palette change in <=16.6 ms. No GL context is created by PreviewTile in v0 (explicitly a DOM/SVG sample) precisely to avoid context-loss risk during rapid palette browsing.

## Observability
CMP-062/CMP-063 invoke the injectable analytics callback with `appearance.theme_changed` and `appearance.density_changed`; the a11y preference controls emit `a11y.preference_changed` `{key, value}`. The package ships a no-op default so `packages/ui` stays app-agnostic.

- [ ] Coverage gate green; axe-core green.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-116/SCR-117 component lists confirmed consistent with what shipped.
