title: Implement theme, density and reduced-motion runtime in packages/ui
body:
## Context
US-SET-004 (Must) requires that switching theme updates every surface **including WebGL canvases** immediately without reload; US-SET-007 (Must) requires reduced motion to apply immediately across all views. SCR-116's performance note is binding: theme and density changes are CSS custom-property swaps applied within one frame that never remount panels or drop GL contexts - a naive React re-render at the provider root would violate this and cost a WebGL context restore mid-session (R2). This task builds the runtime that makes that guarantee real.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `ThemeProvider` in `packages/ui/src/theme/`: sets `data-theme` (`dark` | `light` | `high-contrast`) and `data-density` (`compact` | `comfortable`) on `document.documentElement`, never on a React-owned subtree wrapper.
- `useTheme()` / `useDensity()` hooks returning current value and setter; values persisted per user (localStorage in v0, server-backed preference later by the settings epic).
- Optional 'match system' mode for theme, **off by default** (a trading terminal must not flip mid-session).
- `prefers-reduced-motion` detection plus an explicit in-app override, precedence: in-app override wins; exposed as `data-motion="reduce"` root attribute and a `useReducedMotion()` hook.
- A theme-change event (`candleviewer:themechange` CustomEvent with the resolved theme name and the `theme-uniforms` payload key) that the WebGL chart engine subscribes to in E11 - the binding requirement recorded in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#4`.
- `Ctrl+Shift+H` high-contrast toggle registered as a design-system-level shortcut contract (the global hotkey registry itself is E10/US-SET-002).
- Motion recipes from E05-D03 implemented as CSS custom properties plus a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block and a `[data-motion="reduce"]` block.
- Font-size scale support (100/112/125/150%) as a root `data-text-scale` attribute so SCR-116 can drive it later.

## Out of scope
- SCR-116 / SCR-117 settings screens themselves (later settings epic).
- The WebGL engine's uniform re-upload (E11) - E05 only emits the event and the payload.
- Server-side persistence of preferences.
- The global hotkey registry (E10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Instant swap without remount
  Given a mounted component tree with an instrumented mount counter
  When the theme is switched from dark to high-contrast
  Then the root data-theme attribute changes, styles update, and the mount counter is unchanged
Scenario: One-frame budget
  Given a story rendering 500 dense table rows
  When theme or density is switched
  Then the style recalculation completes within 16.6 ms measured via the Performance API
Scenario: Engine notification
  Given a listener registered for candleviewer:themechange
  When the theme changes
  Then the listener receives the resolved theme name exactly once per change
Scenario: Reduced motion override beats the OS
  Given the OS reports prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
  When the in-app Reduce Motion override is enabled
  Then data-motion="reduce" is set and no transition runs on any animated property
Scenario: Density is spacing-only
  Given any component rendered in compact mode
  When density switches to comfortable
  Then the serialized DOM structure is identical and only computed spacing values differ
Scenario: Persisted preference survives reload
  Given a user selected light + comfortable
  When the app reloads
  Then those values are restored before first paint with no flash of the wrong theme
```

## Technical notes / design
No flash-of-wrong-theme: a tiny synchronous inline script in the document head reads the persisted value and sets the root attributes before the first paint - documented as a required snippet that E10's shell must include. Theme switch must not re-render React: the provider stores the theme in a ref-backed external store and only components explicitly subscribing to the value (e.g. CMP-062 ThemeSwitcher's own checked state) re-render. Density likewise. Motion reduce is implemented purely with CSS so the frame budget benefit is real. Event payload: `{ theme: "dark"|"light"|"high-contrast", density: "compact"|"comfortable", motion: "safe"|"reduce" }`.

## Test plan
Unit (Vitest + Testing Library): attribute setting per theme; persistence round-trip; match-system mode off by default; reduced-motion precedence matrix (OS x override = 4 cases); density attribute change does not alter `container.innerHTML` structure. Interaction: Storybook play function toggling theme and asserting no remount via a mount-count decorator. Perf: a benchmark story measuring style-recalc time on a 500-row table across a theme switch, asserted under 16.6 ms. Contract: an assertion that every animated CSS property declared in `packages/ui` has a reduce counterpart (static scan over the compiled CSS). Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
The inline pre-paint script is the only inline script in the app - it must be allowlisted in the Electron CSP by hash, not by `unsafe-inline`, and this requirement is handed to E10 explicitly. Flagged to E05-X01's STRIDE model as a CSP-weakening temptation.

## Accessibility notes
Directly implements US-SET-007 reduced motion and the high-contrast theme required by `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#56`. `Ctrl+Shift+H` must be announced to screen readers via a polite live region when it toggles. Text-scale support must reflow rather than clip at 125% and 200% zoom.

## Performance notes
Hard budget: <=16.6 ms style recalculation on the 500-row benchmark; zero component remounts; zero WebGL context loss. Reduce mode must measurably lower per-frame transition work (recorded as a before/after number).

title: Set up Storybook 8 with a11y addon, theme/density toolbars and CI test-runner
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` makes Storybook interaction tests a named pyramid layer ('every design-system component and every trading-specific component has at least one interaction story; all interaction stories run in CI') and requires `vitest-axe` plus the Storybook a11y addon. R0 exit criterion 8 is literally 'Design-system v0 is published in Storybook ... zero axe-core violations'. This task builds that harness before components land, so every component story is born inside the gate rather than retro-fitted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Storybook 8 in `packages/ui` with the Vite builder, story globs `src/**/*.stories.tsx`.
- Organisation mirroring the ID bands (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` section 0.3 rule 8): `Atoms/*`, `Molecules/*`, `Organisms/*`, `Trading/*`, `RuleEngine/*`, `ChartEngine/*`.
- `@storybook/addon-a11y` enabled with serious/critical violations failing, plus the docs, controls and interactions addons.
- Global toolbar switchers for theme (dark/light/high-contrast) and density (compact/comfortable) driving the E05-T02 runtime, plus a reduced-motion toggle.
- Decorators: mount-count instrumentation (used by E05-T02's no-remount assertion) and a token-proof background matching `surface.app`.
- A docs page per band plus a Foundations docs page rendering the live token tables from `build/ts/tokens.ts`.
- Storybook test-runner wired into the CI workflow added by E03: runs play functions headless and executes axe per story.
- Static Storybook build published to the internal (Tailscale-only) host as a CI artefact.

## Out of scope
- Component stories themselves (each component story ships with its component in E05-S01..S04).
- Visual-regression snapshots (E05-T04).
- Application-level E2E (E10 and later).
- Any public/internet-facing Storybook hosting.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Storybook builds in CI
  Given a PR touching packages/ui
  When CI runs
  Then storybook build succeeds and the test-runner executes every play function
Scenario: a11y gate is real
  Given a story deliberately rendering a button with a 2:1 label contrast
  When the test-runner runs
  Then the job fails and names the rule and the element
Scenario: Toolbars drive the real runtime
  Given the theme toolbar is switched to high-contrast
  Then document.documentElement carries data-theme="high-contrast" and the story re-renders with .hc tokens
Scenario: Story organisation is enforced
  Given a story placed outside the documented band folders
  When lint runs
  Then it fails with the expected band path
Scenario: CI time budget
  Given the v0 story count
  Then the Storybook job completes in under 10 minutes
```

## Technical notes / design
Pin the Storybook major and the test-runner to avoid the classic version-drift breakage; the test-runner sits on Playwright, which E03 already provisions - reuse that browser cache rather than downloading a second copy. axe configuration: fail on `serious` and `critical`; `moderate`/`minor` are reported but non-blocking, matching `03-testing-strategy.md`. Storybook must consume the **generated** CSS bundles from E05-T01 so theme parity in Storybook equals theme parity in the app.

## Test plan
Self-testing harness: a deliberately-failing fixture story (kept in a `__fixtures__` glob excluded from the published build) proves the a11y gate fails closed; a smoke test asserts the three theme bundles load. CI runtime measured and recorded.

## Security notes
The static Storybook build must not be published to any internet-reachable host (Tailscale-only). Stories must never embed real API keys or recorded account data; fixture values are obviously synthetic. Dependency surface is large - Storybook and addons are included in the SCA scan and in E05-X02's review.

## Accessibility notes
This is the primary automated a11y gate for the design system (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#9-automated-gates-ci-enforced`). The a11y addon panel must be visible to designers reviewing stories, and every component's keyboard table is documented in its Storybook docs page as a DoD gate (`05-accessibility-standard.md` section 11.6).

## Performance notes
Storybook CI job <=10 min (epic budget) so the 15-minute commit-to-dev pipeline target holds; enable story-level lazy compilation in dev.

## Observability
CI publishes the Storybook static build and the a11y report as PR artefacts; the job logs story count and axe violation counts by severity.

- [ ] Storybook builds locally and in CI; test-runner green.
- [ ] a11y gate proven to fail closed via the fixture story.

- [ ] Internal hosting documented in `packages/ui/README.md`.

title: Establish visual-regression baseline across theme x density
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` section 0.3 rule 7 requires visual regression baselines 'per variant x theme (dark/light) x density', and rule 7 of `16-design-system-brief.md#4` makes theme parity enforceable specifically by the visual-regression suite. A design system without a VR baseline silently drifts: a token change that quietly breaks one variant in one theme is invisible to unit tests and to axe. E05-K01 selects the tool; this task installs the baseline.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement the tool chosen by E05-K01 in the E03-provided CI workflow.
- Baseline snapshots for every v0 component story across 3 themes x 2 densities (light theme included, extending the catalogue's dark/light rule to the high-contrast theme as well since `.hc` tokens are only exercised there).
- Deterministic capture setup: pinned fonts in the CI image, animations disabled during capture, fixed viewport (1920x1080 per the brief's primary target), device pixel ratio pinned.
- Reviewer workflow documented: how to inspect a diff, how to accept an intentional change, who approves (design-system code owner plus a designer for any visual change).
- A `pnpm --filter ui vr:update` script for intentional baseline updates, gated so it cannot run implicitly in CI.

## Out of scope
- Screen-level (SCR-*) visual regression - later epics.
- Cross-browser/cross-OS matrices; Chromium at the Electron version only.
- Chart-engine canvas snapshots (E11 uses its own FPS/benchmark harness).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Baseline covers the matrix
  Given the v0 component set
  When the VR job runs
  Then a snapshot exists for every story x theme(3) x density(2) combination with none skipped silently
Scenario: A token regression is caught
  Given a PR changing color.action.primary
  When the VR job runs
  Then it reports diffs on every affected story and blocks merge until reviewed
Scenario: Determinism
  Given two consecutive runs on an unchanged main
  Then zero diffs are reported
Scenario: Intentional update path
  Given a designer-approved visual change
  When vr:update is run and committed
  Then the new baseline is reviewable in the PR and requires a designer approval
Scenario: Time budget
  Then the VR job completes within 6 minutes or shards to stay within it
```

## Technical notes / design
Disable animation globally at capture time via the reduced-motion root attribute from E05-T02 rather than a tool-specific hack - this also exercises the reduce path. Anti-aliasing tolerance set explicitly and documented (a non-zero threshold is acceptable; an undocumented one is not). Snapshots keyed `{story}--{theme}--{density}` so a missing combination is detectable by name.

## Test plan
The job is itself the test. Verification: introduce a deliberate 1px padding change on CMP-001 Button in a throwaway branch and confirm it is reported in all six matrix cells; then confirm a no-op run is clean twice.

## Security notes
If a hosted service was selected, confirm the Owner's acceptance recorded in E05-K01 and ensure no story fixture contains realistic account, key or PnL data. Otherwise baselines are committed to the private repo - confirm repository size growth is acceptable and documented.

## Accessibility notes
High-contrast theme snapshots are the only automated proof that `.hc` variants render; they complement but do not replace axe. Snapshot review must not become a substitute for the manual screen-reader pass in E05-Q02.

## Performance notes
VR job <=6 min (from E05-K01's criterion); baseline storage growth per run recorded so the repo does not balloon.

## Observability
Diff artefacts published per PR; job logs matrix cell count and diff count.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Baseline committed/published for the full matrix.
- [ ] Deliberate-regression verification performed and evidence attached.
- [ ] Reviewer workflow documented in `packages/ui/README.md`.
- [ ] Job runtime recorded, under budget.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

title: Create icon registry and custom trading-domain icons
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#5-iconography` requires a single outline icon set at 16/20/24px optical sizes with 1.5px stroke, referenced by semantic `IconName` strings and never by raw inline SVG in component code, plus a set of custom trading-domain icons that no generic library provides. CMP-019 Icon's completeness test depends on the registry existing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/ui/src/icons/` registry: a typed `IconName` union, one component per icon, tree-shakeable, all drawn on the 1.5px-stroke grid at the three optical sizes (`size.icon.sm/md/lg`).
- Base set sourced from an open library (Lucide/Phosphor-equivalent), imported as a curated subset rather than the whole library.
- Custom trading-domain icons authored to the same grid: flatten-all, chase-limit, iceberg-order, TWAP, one-click-arm, native-SL-shield, estimated/heuristic badge glyph, node-graph node-type glyphs (trigger, condition, action, logic-gate, comment), heatmap-convention swap.
- Each icon registered with a canonical name and a short semantic description (feeds CMP-019's completeness test and the Figma icon page).
- Lint rule: raw `<svg>` in component source outside `src/icons/` fails; icon-only controls must supply `aria-label`; icon adjacent to visible text must be `aria-hidden`.

## Out of scope
- Brand/logo artwork.
- Icons for features not yet designed (add them with their owning epic).
- Animated icons.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Registry completeness
  Given the IconName union
  When the completeness test runs
  Then every name maps to an exported component and every component is reachable by exactly one name
Scenario: Custom icons match the grid
  Given any custom trading icon
  Then its stroke width is 1.5px and its bounding box matches the base set at each optical size
Scenario: Decorative vs meaningful is enforced
  Given an icon-only IconButton without an aria-label
  When lint and the axe story check run
  Then both fail
Scenario: No inline SVG leakage
  Given a component embedding a raw svg element
  When lint runs
  Then it fails naming the file and pointing at the registry
Scenario: Tree-shaking
  Given an app importing three icons
  When the bundle is analysed
  Then unused icons are absent from the output
```

## Technical notes / design
Icons compile from SVG source to React components at build time (SVGR or equivalent) with `currentColor` fills so they inherit the semantic colour token from their context - never hardcoded fills. `size.icon.sm/md/lg` map to 16/20/24px. Descriptions live alongside the name in a single `registry.ts` so the Figma icon page and the code stay comparable by diff.

## Test plan
Unit: completeness test (every name renders; every export is named); snapshot of the rendered SVG per icon at each size; a `currentColor` assertion so no icon hardcodes a fill. Lint-rule tests for the raw-SVG and aria-label rules. Bundle test asserting tree-shaking. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Third-party SVG source is executable-adjacent content: icons are compiled from vetted SVG files committed to the repo, never fetched at runtime; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Included in E05-X02's dependency review.

## Accessibility notes
The decorative-vs-meaningful rule is binding, not stylistic (`16-design-system-brief.md#5`): icon+text is `aria-hidden`; icon-only carries `aria-label`. The estimated/heuristic glyph is an accessibility-critical icon because it is the non-colour cue that a value is inferred rather than exchange-provided.

## Performance notes
Icons must not ship as a single monolithic sprite import; per-icon modules keep the app bundle small. Registry adds <=15 KB gzipped for a typical screen's icon usage.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Registry implemented; all listed custom icons drawn and committed.
- [ ] Completeness, aria and tree-shaking tests green.
- [ ] Lint rules enabled and clean across `packages/ui`.
- [ ] Figma icon page updated to match the registry exactly.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md#5` updated with the final icon list.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

`feat/design-system-icons`.

title: QA: exploratory charter - tier boundaries, backfill idempotency and lifecycle surprises
body:
## Context
Scripted suites find the defects someone anticipated. The storage tier's dangerous defects are the ones nobody wrote a case for: a partition that is exported twice and counted once, a pin applied *during* a reaper run, a symbol renamed on the exchange, a clock that steps backwards across the export window. `03-testing-strategy.md` mandates exploratory charters alongside scripted coverage; this is E07's.

## Scope / Deliverables
Four timeboxed session-based charters (90 minutes each, session notes committed to `docs/qa/exploratory/E07-*.md`):

1. **Charter: tier boundary.** "Explore reads whose ranges interact with the hot/cold boundary, with the boundary moving underneath them, to discover gaps, duplicates or ordering breaks." Includes: a read issued while the reaper drops the partition it is reading; a range whose boundary crosses during a long scan; `hot_retention` changed mid-flight; clock stepping backwards.
2. **Charter: backfill and replay idempotency.** "Explore repeated and partial ingestion of the same data to discover row-count drift." Includes: replay a fixture with one field altered (does dedup treat it as the same row or a new one - and is that the intended semantic per the `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` of that table?); interleave two symbols' replays; replay an overlapping window with different `epoch_id`; ingest a row whose `ts` is older than the current partition retention horizon.
3. **Charter: retention safety.** "Explore ways to make the reaper delete something it must not." Includes: pin applied mid-run; pin removed mid-run; `replay_sessions` row created between dry-run and apply; a journal trade referencing a range about to be purged; two reaper instances racing; accelerated mode entered while a manual compaction is in progress.
4. **Charter: operator's mental model.** "Read the storage state the way an operator would from the E07-D01 design and the real payload, and find where the system's truth and the screen's story diverge." Includes: `projected_full_at` after a growth spike; per-symbol figures during an export; what the panel shows while a tier is unreachable.

Deliverables per session: charter, duration, areas covered, bugs found with severity, questions raised, and follow-up test cases to promote into the scripted suite (E07-Q01).

## Out of scope
- Deliberate infrastructure failure injection (kill containers, fill disks) - E07-Q04 owns that as scripted chaos.
- Performance measurement - E07-Q03.
- Fixing the defects found (filed as Bugs against the owning ticket).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given four charters
When each session is run
Then session notes are committed with duration, coverage, findings and follow-ups, per the session-based test management format

Given any defect found
When it is filed
Then it has reproduction steps, environment, expected vs actual and a severity, satisfying the Bug DoR in 02-definition-of-ready-done.md §6.1

Given a finding that reveals a missing scripted case
When the session closes
Then the case is promoted into E07-Q01's suite in the same sprint, not left in the notes

Given charter 3 discovers any path that deletes pinned data
When it is triaged
Then it is priority/p0 regardless of likelihood, because pinned data loss is unrecoverable (no REST tick history)

Given all four sessions complete with zero P0/P1 findings outstanding
When QA reviews
Then the epic-level exploratory pass required by the Epic DoD is recorded as done
```

## Technical notes / design
Session-based test management: each charter is a timeboxed mission, not a script. Notes follow the standard sections (charter, duration, areas, findings, questions, follow-ups) and are committed so the reasoning survives the session.

Each session runs on its own scratch compose stack seeded from fixtures, so one charter's residue cannot explain another's finding. The tester works from the operator's surfaces only - logs, metrics, `system_events`, audit entries, and the E07-D01 payload - because a finding that required reading the source would not have been findable in production.

## Test plan
Session-based test management: each charter is timeboxed, notes follow the standard sections, and the debrief with the backend lead happens within one working day so findings are actionable while context is fresh. Fixtures from `packages/fixtures`; a scratch compose stack per session so state is never shared between charters.

## Security notes
Charter 3 overlaps the SR-099 control surface (pins honoured, dry-run first, deletions audited) - any finding there is copied to E07-X02 and to the Security engineer, since it is a control failure, not merely a bug. No real credentials are used in any session.

## Accessibility notes
Charter 4 reviews the operator narrative but not an implemented UI; a11y findings, if any, are routed to E07-D02.

## Performance notes
Observations only (e.g. "the reaper made reads slow for 40 s") are recorded and handed to E07-Q03 for measurement rather than judged here.

## Observability
Sessions deliberately use only what an operator would have - logs, metrics, `system_events`, audit entries. Where a session could not answer a question from those sources, that gap is itself a finding filed against E07's observability deliverables.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Four session notes committed.
- [ ] All findings filed as Bugs with owners; P0/P1 resolved or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off.
- [ ] Promoted cases merged into E07-Q01's suite.
- [ ] Debriefs held; learnings noted on the epic.
- [ ] QA sign-off contribution recorded on E07-T05.

## Dependencies

- `E07-D01` for charter 4's operator narrative.

title: QA: storage performance harness - ILP ingest rate, query-shape regression, export throughput
body:
## Context
E07-K01 measured two engines once, to make a decision. This ticket turns that one-off measurement into a **repeatable harness with recorded baselines**, so the numbers ADR-0008 is built on cannot silently rot as the code changes. `30-release-roadmap.md` §4.4 sets the R0 perf gate as "benchmark harness committed and runnable in CI (numbers recorded, not yet gating)" - recorded now, gating from R5/E46.

Budgets come from `21-database-schema.md` §11.4 (throughput) and §13.2/§13.3 (per-shape latency), plus `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 budget #12 (storage growth) and §6 (ingestion, memory, storage).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/perf/storage/` harness, runnable locally and in the nightly CI job, reusing the E07-K01 shape definitions so the numbers are directly comparable to ADR-0008's table.
- **Ingest**: sustained ILP rows/s via the real `ilp_writer`, for 10 minutes at the 5-symbol/200-depth profile (~25k rows/s realistic) and at a stress profile pushed until the queue backs up; reports achieved rows/s, p95 `questdb_write_seconds`, queue depth, and the backpressure onset point against the >=600k rows/s headroom claim.
- **Query shapes**: shapes #1-#11 from §13.2 run warm and cold-cache, 30 samples each, p50/p95/p99, compared against a committed `baseline.json`; a >20 % p95 regression fails the nightly job and opens a ticket (it does not block PRs in R0).
- **Cold tier**: Parquet export throughput MB/s vs the >=200 MB/s target; DuckDB scans vs §13.3 targets (cold replay <500 ms/hour of deltas, journal analytics <1 s over 12 months, trades <2 s/month, big-print research <1 s/month, audit export <500 ms/month); compaction before/after effect on scan time (this is the measurement that justifies the compactor's existence).
- **Storage growth**: measured compressed bytes/day/symbol at 200 depth from a real (or fixture-replayed) 24 h run, reported against the 0.5-0.75 GB/day planning range of budget #12 - this is the number `21-database-schema.md` §11 and `24-internal-schemas.md` explicitly flag as an estimate awaiting measurement.
- **Reaper impact**: event-loop lag during a retention run, against the 50-100 ms threshold of `03-testing-strategy.md` §6.
- Results published as a markdown table plus `results.json` per run; the R0 numbers appended to ADR-0008 and to `21-database-schema.md` §14.

## Out of scope
- API/WS load testing (k6/Locust) - E04/E46.
- Chart-engine FPS - E06.
- Making these gates blocking - E46 (R5).
- Multi-node scaling.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the harness and a seeded dataset
When it runs on the reference VPS profile (4 vCPU / 8 GB container limits)
Then it produces p50/p95/p99 for shapes #1-#11, ingest rows/s, export MB/s, DuckDB scan times and measured bytes/day/symbol, all in one results.json

Given a committed baseline.json
When a run's p95 for any shape exceeds the baseline by more than 20 percent
Then the nightly job fails with a report naming the shape and the delta, and does not fail per-PR builds in R0

Given the ILP stress profile
When the writer is pushed past its drain rate
Then the harness records the backpressure onset rows/s and confirms zero trade rows were dropped, matching the never-drop-trades invariant

Given a partition with many small files, measured before and after compaction
When DuckDB scan time is compared
Then the improvement is quantified and recorded, justifying the compactor per 21-database-schema.md §13.3

Given a 24 h recording (or equivalent fixture replay)
When storage growth is measured
Then a real bytes/day/symbol figure is recorded and 21-database-schema.md §11 and §14 are updated, replacing the estimate

Given the retention reaper runs during the measurement window
When event-loop lag is sampled
Then it stays within the 50-100 ms threshold, or the excess is filed as a perf defect against E07-T05
```

## Technical notes / design
Shape definitions are imported from the E07-K01 harness module rather than re-typed, so ADR-0008's numbers and this harness's numbers remain directly comparable; a test asserts the shape-id set is identical to the ADR's table.

Warm and cold runs are recorded as separate series and never averaged together. Cold runs drop the page cache between iterations (container restart in CI); warm runs execute 5 discarded iterations before sampling. Every result row carries its conditions (`engine`, `cache`, `cpu_limit`, `mem_limit`, `dataset_id`, `commit_sha`) so a number can never be quoted without them.

Percentiles are computed with the nearest-rank method over >=30 samples; runs with fewer samples are reported as raw values, not percentiles, to avoid manufacturing precision.

## Test plan
The harness has its own unit tests (timer correctness on a synthetic workload of known duration; percentile maths against a known distribution; baseline-comparison logic including the boundary at exactly 20 %). Cold-cache runs drop the page cache between iterations and are labelled separately from warm runs - conflating the two is the most common way a storage benchmark lies. Every number reports its measurement conditions inline.

## Security notes
Runs against fixtures in an egress-free environment. Stress profiles must not be pointed at any shared or production-like instance - the harness refuses to run unless `CV_ENV=test` (an assertion, not a convention). Results contain no credentials or real account identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance verification for E07. Targets: §11.4 (ILP >=600k rows/s, Parquet export >=200 MB/s, DuckDB >=1 GB/s page-cache scan, PG <=50 tx/s), §13.2/§13.3 per-shape, budget #12 storage growth, §6 memory ceiling (<=300 MB/symbol backend) sampled during the ingest run.

## Observability
Harness scrapes the storage metrics rather than instrumenting separately, which doubles as a test that those metrics are accurate: a metric that disagrees with the harness's own timer is a defect.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Harness committed, runnable via one command locally and in the nightly CI job.
- [ ] `baseline.json` committed with R0 numbers; regression check wired and demonstrated firing on a deliberate slowdown.
- [ ] Results appended to ADR-0008 and `21-database-schema.md` §14.
- [ ] Measured storage growth replaces the estimate in §11 (or the estimate is confirmed, explicitly).
- [ ] Reviewed by the backend lead and the Architect.
- [ ] Numbers presented at Sprint Review.

title: QA: chaos scenarios - DB down, disk full, crash between export and partition drop
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` §"chaos" names the storage failure explicitly: **"DB down (QuestDB or Postgres unavailable)"** - docker-compose stops the DB container mid-test - with the expectation "Ingestion buffers or fails loudly (no silent data loss beyond a defined bounded buffer window); OMS refuses to place orders it cannot durably record rather than trading blind; health dashboard reflects DB-down state immediately." `04-security-program.md` §5.8 rates disk exhaustion (S2) **Critical** because it takes trading down. And `21-database-schema.md` §5.3 states an ordering invariant whose only real proof is a crash test.

Scripted chaos in R0 establishes the baseline behaviour that E45 (Reconciliation, chaos & failover resilience, R4) later extends.

## Scope / Deliverables
Scenarios, each automated in `tests/chaos/storage/` and runnable in the nightly job:

1. **QuestDB down mid-ingest.** Stop the container while fixtures replay. Expect: writer applies backpressure within the bounded buffer, `questdb_write_errors_total` climbs, `storage_tier_health{tier="questdb"}` goes down, `/readyz` reflects it, and on restart the buffered batch flushes exactly once with no duplicate and no missing rows (dedup makes a re-flush safe).
2. **Postgres down.** Expect: the app fails readiness loudly rather than serving; no partial writes; on recovery, UoW transactions resume; a `system_events` row records both transitions.
3. **Disk full on the recording volume.** Fill to <5 % free. Expect: critical event **before** any deletion, recording paused for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols, pinned data untouched, **and the trading path still functional** because it does not share the volume (SR-096) - asserted by exercising a Postgres write while the recording volume is full.
4. **Crash between Parquet write and manifest entry.** SIGKILL the exporter at that exact point. Expect: re-run reconciles to a single manifest entry, zero rows lost, hot partition still present.
5. **Crash between manifest entry and hot-partition drop.** Expect: duplicate data across tiers (harmless, dedup on read), zero rows lost; the router's straddle merge returns no duplicates to the caller.
6. **Export verify mismatch.** Inject a row-count discrepancy. Expect: CRITICAL `system_events`, run aborted, hot data retained, alert delivered, no partition dropped.
7. **Corrupted Parquet file.** Flip a byte. Expect: scrub/read-time checksum detects it, quarantines the file, alerts, and serves no data from it (SR-094).
8. **Two reaper instances racing.** Expect: locking or idempotency prevents double-deletion and double-audit entries.
9. **Clock step backwards during the export window.** Expect: partition selection uses monotonic/exchange time semantics and does not re-export or skip a window.

## Out of scope
- Exchange-side chaos (WS disconnect, 5xx, rate-limit 10018) - E08/E45.
- Host/VM failover and backup restore drills - E43/PRR (this ticket proves the data invariants, not the recovery runbook).
- Network partition between tiers beyond container stop/start.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given each of the nine scenarios
When it runs in the nightly chaos job
Then the expected behaviour above is asserted programmatically, not observed manually, and a failure names the violated invariant

Given scenario 5 (crash after manifest, before drop)
When the system is inspected afterwards
Then rows exist in both tiers and a straddling read returns each row exactly once, proving the "duplicate is harmless, missing is not" design of 21-database-schema.md §5.3

Given scenario 3 (disk full)
When the guard trips
Then the critical alert timestamp precedes every deletion timestamp in the audit log, and a Postgres write succeeds during the event

Given scenario 6 (verify mismatch)
When the run aborts
Then zero QuestDB partitions were dropped and the hot data is fully readable

Given scenario 7 (corrupted file)
When a read touches the quarantined partition
Then it fails loudly with a named error rather than returning truncated or silently wrong results

Given any scenario leaves the system in an inconsistent state
When triaged
Then it is priority/p0 if data is lost and priority/p1 if data is duplicated or unavailable, per the data-loss severity rule
```

## Technical notes / design
Fault injection uses docker-compose container control for stop/start and `SIGKILL` at instrumented breakpoints for the crash scenarios: the exporter exposes test-only hook points (`AFTER_PARQUET_WRITE`, `AFTER_CHECKSUM`, `AFTER_MANIFEST`) that are no-ops unless `CV_ENV=test`, which is how scenarios 4 and 5 hit the exact instruction boundary the §5.3 invariant is written about.

Disk-full scenarios operate on a dedicated small loopback filesystem image mounted at the cold root, never on the CI runner's real volume; the harness refuses to run if the target mount is not that image.

Each scenario is structured as `arrange -> inject -> assert(data) -> assert(signals) -> assert(health) -> recover -> assert(recovery)` and cleans up in a `finally` block, so a failed assertion still leaves the environment reusable.

## Test plan
Implemented with docker-compose container control plus `pumba`-style fault injection for process kills, and a loopback filesystem image of fixed small size for the disk-full scenarios (filling a real volume in CI is not acceptable). Each scenario asserts on three surfaces: the data (row counts, checksums), the observability signals (metrics, `system_events`, audit entries) and the health/readiness endpoints. Every scenario must be **repeatable and self-cleaning** - a chaos test that leaves residue is a flaky test generator.

## Security notes
Scenarios 3, 6, 7 and 8 are direct verifications of security controls SR-096 (disk-budget guard, trading unaffected), SR-094 (checksum manifest, quarantine) and SR-099 (pins honoured, deletions audited, no double-deletion). Findings here are control failures and are copied to E07-X02 and the Security engineer, not merely filed as bugs. The disk-full scenario must never target a shared volume; the harness asserts it is operating on its own loopback image.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - though scenario outputs feed the SCR-142 degraded states reviewed in E07-D02.

## Performance notes
Recovery time is measured, not just correctness: time from container restart to `storage_tier_health` returning ok, and time to drain the buffered batch. Recorded as a baseline for E45's failover budgets.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts the expected signal appears: `system_events` severity and code, the metric that should move, the audit entry that should exist. A scenario that behaves correctly but silently is a **failure** of this suite - silent correct behaviour is indistinguishable from silent failure to an operator.

- [ ] Findings filed; P0/P1 resolved or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off.

title: Security: verify storage controls SR-047/048/090-099, add SAST rules and a DAST/path-traversal probe
body:
## Context
A control that is specified but never verified is a control that does not exist. `04-security-program.md` SR-150 requires every SR to map to at least one automated test or a scheduled manual procedure, with a traceability table checked at PRR. This ticket closes E07's half of that obligation for the storage-relevant SRs and adds the static/dynamic rules that stop the controls from regressing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Control verification** - one automated test or a documented procedure per SR:
  | SR | Control | Verification |
  |---|---|---|
  | SR-047 | Loopback/WSL-internal binds only; startup listener self-check | Automated: boot the stack, enumerate listening sockets, assert no non-loopback bind for postgres/questdb/minio; assert the app's own startup self-check refuses to start on a violation |
  | SR-048 | Data-store ports not published to host/tailnet; QuestDB console off/loopback-only | Automated: parse compose files, assert every published port binds 127.0.0.1; probe the QuestDB HTTP console from a non-loopback interface and assert refusal |
  | SR-090/091/092 | Backups cover PG + Parquet + config, encrypted with a key distinct from the runtime KEK, useless without it | Procedure: documented backup of the E07 tiers, decryption attempt without the backup key must fail; recorded in the PRR-lite evidence |
  | SR-093 | Restore drill per release | Procedure: one restore of Postgres + a Parquet partition into a scratch environment; assert the app starts and recorded data reads back |
  | SR-094 | Cold-tier checksum manifest verified on read and by a weekly scrub | Automated: corrupt a file, assert quarantine + alert; assert the weekly scrub job is scheduled and its last-run timestamp is observable |
  | SR-096 | Storage guard: separate volume, 75 % / 90 % thresholds, trading unaffected | Automated (shares E07-Q04 scenario 3): assert alert precedes deletion, recorder pauses, a Postgres write succeeds while the recording volume is full |
  | SR-097 | No filesystem paths in replay/export/read APIs; registry ids only | Automated: path-traversal and symlink-escape matrix against `ColdTierRepository.query` and any endpoint surface reaching it |
  | SR-099 | Retention honours pins, dry-run first, deletions audited | Automated: pinned symbol survives a full cycle; every deletion has exactly one audit entry with symbol/stream/range/bytes |
- **SAST rules** (Semgrep, added to the E03 pipeline): forbid f-string/`%`/`+` construction of SQL in `storage/**`; forbid `os.path.join` with any value derived from a request model in `storage/cold/**`; forbid `open()` on a path not rooted at `CV_COLD_ROOT`; forbid `pickle`/`eval`/`exec` anywhere in `storage/**`; forbid logging of any variable named `dsn`, `password`, `secret`, `token`.
- **DAST probe** (OWASP ZAP job addition, scoped to what exists at R0): path-traversal payloads against any storage-backed read route, plus a check that data-store ports are unreachable through the app's origin.
- **SCA/secrets**: confirm gitleaks covers the new `infra/` and `backend/db/` paths; pin and scan the new dependencies (`pyarrow`, `duckdb`, `asyncpg`, the QuestDB client) with pip-audit, and record an accepted-risk entry for any unavoidable Medium.
- **Traceability table** `docs/security/traceability/E07.md` mapping SR -> test id -> ticket, feeding the PRR checklist.

## Out of scope
- Auth/RBAC control verification - E09/E43.
- Full pen-test - E43 (before Live enablement).
- Key management controls (SR-001..SR-010) - E27; this ticket only asserts no key material reaches E07's tiers.
- Backup *automation* - E43; here the procedure is executed once, manually, and documented.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Given the traceability table
When it is reviewed at the R0 PRR-lite
Then every storage-relevant SR listed above has a test id or a dated executed procedure, and none is marked "to be done"

Given the bind assertions
When any compose file is changed to publish a data-store port on 0.0.0.0
Then CI fails, naming SR-047/SR-048

Given the Semgrep rules
When a developer builds SQL by string concatenation anywhere in storage/**
Then the SAST gate fails the PR with a message pointing at the rule and the threat it mitigates

Given the path-traversal matrix
When ../, absolute paths, URL-encoded traversal, symlinked partition directories and unregistered dataset ids are attempted
Then every attempt is refused and no filesystem access occurs outside CV_COLD_ROOT, asserted by an fs-access spy not merely by the returned error

Given an encrypted backup and no backup key
When decryption is attempted
Then it fails, satisfying SR-092, and the attempt is recorded in the drill notes

Given the restore drill
When Postgres and one Parquet partition are restored into a scratch environment
Then the app starts, the restored partition reads back with matching checksums, and the result is recorded for the PRR

Given any Critical or High SAST/SCA finding on the new dependencies
When the gate runs
Then the build fails; Medium findings require a dated accepted-risk entry per the R0 quality gates
```

## Technical notes / design
Bind assertions parse the compose files statically *and* probe the running stack, because a file can be correct while a runtime override is not. The path-traversal matrix asserts at the filesystem layer using an `open()` spy rather than trusting the returned error, since a control that returns 403 after having already stat-ed the target path has still leaked existence.

Semgrep rules are written against the repository's own idioms (they must not fire on SQLAlchemy Core expressions or on parameterised asyncpg calls) and each ships with a matching `*.fixed.py`/`*.bad.py` pair in the rule tests, so a rule that stops matching is itself caught.

The restore drill is scripted end to end (`infra/scripts/restore_drill.sh`) even though it is executed manually in R0, so E43 can promote it to a scheduled job without rewriting it.

## Test plan
Each row of the control table is a test case with an id; automated cases live in `tests/security/storage/` and run in the `security` CI job; procedures are executed once in R0 with dated notes. Negative controls are mandatory: each rule and assertion is demonstrated *failing* on a deliberately introduced violation, then passing after reverting - a green check that has never been seen red is not evidence.

## Security notes
This ticket is the verification layer for the threats modelled in E07-X01 (S1-S6). Findings are triaged with the Security engineer; Critical/High block the epic's DoD. The drill artifacts (backup files, restore notes) contain no production data - fixtures only - and the backup key used in the drill is a throwaway generated for it.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Per-read checksum verification and the weekly scrub have measurable cost; E07-Q03 measures it and this ticket records the accepted trade-off from E07-X01's model. The DAST job runs nightly, not per-PR, to stay inside the pipeline's 15-minute budget (R0 exit criterion 2).

## Observability
Verifies that each control emits evidence: audit entries for deletions and policy changes, `system_events` for quarantine/verify failure, the alert path for the 75 %/90 % thresholds, and an observable last-run timestamp for the weekly scrub. A control with no signal is filed as a defect against the owning ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every listed SR verified by an automated test or a dated executed procedure.
- [ ] Traceability table committed and accepted at PRR-lite.
- [ ] Semgrep rules merged into the E03 pipeline; each demonstrated failing then passing.
- [ ] DAST job addition merged and run once with results triaged.
- [ ] New dependencies scanned; Critical/High zero, Medium accepted-risk entries dated.
- [ ] Restore drill executed and recorded.
- [ ] **Security engineer sign-off comment** on the epic.

## Dependencies
- `E07-X01` (the model that says which controls matter and why).
- `E07-T05` (the controls must exist to be verified).
- `E03` pipeline for the SAST/DAST/SCA jobs; `E07-Q04` shares the disk-full scenario.

`chore/e07-security-controls`.

- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §8, §12

title: Design QA of the implemented E08 market-data surfaces
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI Stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec (spacing, tokens, type, colour, states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer, and discrepancies are either fixed or filed as prioritised follow-up bugs. E08 ships the first live-data surfaces in the product, and its most important states (stale, reconnecting, resyncing, gapped, throttled) are precisely the ones engineers cannot easily see during normal development - they only appear when something breaks. Without a deliberate design-QA pass that *forces* those states, they will ship wrong.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Design QA pass over the implemented surfaces: `SCR-041`, `SCR-100`, `SCR-101`, `SCR-102`, `SCR-103`, `SCR-104`, `SCR-147`, `SCR-151`, `SCR-152`.
- **Forced-state matrix**: for each confidence and failure state, the exact way to induce it in a test environment (kill the upstream WS, inject a sequence gap into a recorded fixture, force a `10018` rate-limit response, skew the clock beyond 500 ms, empty the instrument cache, exceed the 200-symbol cap, delist a fixture symbol) - produced jointly with QA/SDET so it is reusable for regression.
- Comparison report per surface: token fidelity (colour/spacing/type/motion), state completeness, copy fidelity, focus/keyboard behaviour, reduced-motion behaviour, both themes, supported densities.
- Defect list with severity and `priority/*`, each either fixed within the epic or filed as a follow-up Bug linked to the originating story.
- Design-system adoption check: any surface using a local style instead of an E08-D04 token is recorded as a defect, not accepted.
- Visual-regression baselines captured for the confidence states so future epics cannot silently drift.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of ingestion (covered by the epic's engineering and QA tickets) - design QA reports what is rendered, not whether the data is right.
- Re-designing anything; deviations either become defects or, if the design was wrong, a change request against the originating design ticket.
- Performance benchmarking (engineering perf tickets) beyond observing obvious jank in the reviewed states.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every designed state is verified against a forced instance
  Given the forced-state matrix
  When the pass completes
  Then each state in the E08-D13 enumeration has been induced and compared against its frame
  And any state that could not be induced is recorded with the reason and a follow-up to make it inducible

Scenario: Token drift is caught
  Given a rendered surface
  When inspected against the published tokens
  Then any colour, spacing, type or motion value not resolving to a token is filed as a defect
  And the defect names the correct token

Scenario: A frozen value ships looking live (failure case)
  Given the upstream feed is killed in the test environment
  When the watchlist is observed
  Then any cell retaining its live styling is filed as a priority/p0 defect
  And the epic cannot be signed off while it is open

Scenario: Reduced motion and both themes are covered (edge case)
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is enabled and the dark theme is active
  When the states are re-checked
  Then the pass covers this combination explicitly
  And defects found only in this combination are filed like any other

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given all p0/p1 design defects are closed and the remainder are filed with owners and priorities
  Then the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Run against a build with recorded Bybit fixtures so densities and update rates are realistic, and so the pass is repeatable.
- Use the stable test ids from E08-D13 to script the forced states where possible; the goal is a repeatable procedure, not a one-off manual sweep.
- Check the composition rules explicitly: estimated + stale, delisted + stale, reconnecting + backfilling - these are exactly where implementations diverge from precedence rules.
- Verify the RBAC content split on `SCR-152` `Details` and `SCR-147` by running the pass as each role, not only as Owner.

## Test plan
- Two reviewers: a product designer and a design-system-trained reviewer; QA/SDET assists with inducing states.
- Each surface checked in light and dark, at every supported density, keyboard-only once, and with reduced motion once.
- Screen-reader spot-check of the announcements against the E08-D12 live-region budget (flood check: watch that a flapping feed does not produce continuous speech).
- Visual-regression baselines committed and wired into CI so the states are protected going forward.

## Security notes
- Verify by observation that no role sees content it must not: run the pass as Manager and Viewer and confirm the absence (not mere disabling) of Owner-only diagnostics, record/unrecord controls and admin links.
- Confirm that no error state renders a raw exchange payload, endpoint, key fragment or account identifier - any occurrence is a `priority/p0` security-adjacent defect routed to the Security engineer as well.

## Accessibility notes
- Confirm the axe-core rule set from E08-D13 is green on each surface and that manual keyboard and screen-reader checks match the specified names, focus order and announcement policy.
- Verify WCAG 2.2 items the designs relied on: focus appearance, dragging-movement alternatives on the watchlist, target sizes in dense tables.
- Contrast re-measured in the *rendered* product for the degraded states, not only in the design file.

## Performance notes
- Observe the specified budgets during the pass: watchlist behaviour with 200 rows at 4 Hz, symbol search responsiveness, scanner refresh, and the mass-stale transition from E08-D11; obvious violations are filed and routed to the engineering perf ticket.
- Confirm that empty states initialise no GL context or subscriptions, per the `SCR-151` constraint.

## Observability
- Confirm the analytics/audit events from the E08-D13 table actually fire with the specified payloads during the pass (spot-check via the dev tooling), since missing instrumentation is invisible later.
- Record how many defects were state-related versus token-related, as an input to the epic retro.

## Definition of Done
- All in-scope surfaces reviewed in both themes, all densities, keyboard-only and reduced-motion; forced-state matrix executed.
- Defects filed with severity and priority; p0/p1 closed within the epic.
- Visual-regression baselines committed; adoption check complete with no unauthorised local styles.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done). This ticket is a prerequisite for the E08 epic's own DoD.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E08-D13; in practice also requires the E08 front-end implementation stories to be merged behind their flags.

## Branch
`design/e08-design-qa`

## References
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 (design-qa), §2.2 (Epic DoD)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (in-scope SCR entries), `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`, `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).

title: Black-box test plan for the E08 market-data and ingestion story groups
body:
## Context
E08 is the single market-data path that nine downstream epics consume (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11: `E08 -> {E12, E16, E17, E22, E24, E29}` plus the recorder/replay chain). A defect here does not show up as a broken screen — it shows up as a chart that is *quietly wrong*, which is risk **R7 Data accuracy** and the single worst failure mode in the product. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 requires a written black-box test plan per feature, and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes a recorded QA sign-off non-skippable for every Story in this epic.

No such artefact exists today: the engineering tickets (`E08-T01..T06`, `E08-S01..S07`) each state what to build, but there is nothing a QA engineer can execute end-to-end against a staging build wired to the recorded fixture corpus (`E08-T05`) to declare "market data behaves as specified". This ticket produces it.

It is deliberately **black-box**: written against the observable surface — REST endpoints in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, WS topics in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, screens `SCR-100..104`, `SCR-041`, `SCR-152`, and the Prometheus metrics/health endpoints — with no knowledge of internal helpers, so it survives the refactors that `E08-T06` and E17 will inevitably cause.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e08-market-data-test-plan.md`, organised into six executable groups mirroring the story structure:
  1. **Instrument catalogue & search** (US-MKT-001, US-MKT-002; `E08-S01`) — `GET /instruments`, `GET /instruments/{symbol}`, `POST /instruments/refresh`, `SCR-102`, `SCR-041`, `SCR-103`.
  2. **Precision & filter validation** (US-MKT-004; `E08-S02`) — shared rounding rule source, violation codes `PRICE_NOT_TICK_MULTIPLE`, `QTY_NOT_LOT_MULTIPLE`, `QTY_BELOW_MIN`, `QTY_ABOVE_MAX`, `NOTIONAL_BELOW_MIN`, `SYMBOL_NOT_TRADING`.
  3. **Live ticker stream** (US-MKT-005; `E08-S03`) — WS `ticker.{symbol}` and batched `ticker`, `GET /instruments/{symbol}/ticker`, `SCR-100`, `SCR-101`, `SCR-104`.
  4. **Tape ingestion** (US-MKT-006; `E08-S04`) — WS `trades.{symbol}`, `GET /market/trades`, ordering, dedup, gap detection.
  5. **Order-book reconstruction** (US-MKT-007; `E08-S05`) — WS `book.{symbol}.{depth}`, `GET /market/orderbook`, snapshot+delta, sequence-gap → invalidate → resync, crossed-book rejection.
  6. **Historical backfill & clock sync** (US-MKT-008, US-MKT-009; `E08-S06`, `E08-S07`) — `GET /market/klines`, `GET /market/data-coverage`, paging, cache coverage, drift alarm.
- Per case: id (`E08-TC-<group><nn>`), preconditions (named fixture from the `E08-T05` corpus + symbol + env), steps, expected observable result, the `US-MKT-*` id and child ticket it verifies, and automation status (`E08-Q02`/`E08-Q05` or manual-only).
- **Fixture/test-data appendix**: which corpus fixture drives which case — clean BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT window, mid-cap window, sequence-gap window, reconnect window, ticker delta-only burst, kline page-boundary set, `10018`/`10002`/5xx error payloads, `instruments-info` payload with a delisted symbol and a changed tick size.
- **Oracle definitions**: for every "is the data correct?" case, the plan names the independent oracle — REST `GET /v5/market/orderbook` snapshot diff for the book, `GET /v5/market/recent-trade` for the tape, exchange-side kline rows for backfill — rather than comparing the system to itself.
- **Traceability table** US-MKT-001..009 × test case × automation status, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, proving no story is untested.
- **Defect conventions for this epic**: any case where data is wrong *without a visible staleness/desync signal* is `priority/p0-critical` by definition; a visible-and-honest degradation is at most P2.

## Out of scope
- Writing the automation (`E08-Q02` integration/contract pack, `E08-Q05` E2E + a11y).
- Chaos scenarios (`E08-Q03`) and performance/load scripts (`E08-Q04`).
- Exploratory charters, epic regression pack and sign-off (`E08-Q06`).
- Security-owned artefacts: STRIDE (`E08-X01`), abuse cases (`E08-X02`), SAST/DAST rules (`E08-X03`).
- Anything consuming this data downstream: bar builders (E12), footprint/profiles (E22/E24), WS gateway framing (E17), OMS (E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every MKT story is covered by an executable case
  Given the plan is merged at qa/plans/e08-market-data-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against US-MKT-001 through US-MKT-009
  Then every story id maps to at least one case with preconditions, steps and an expected result
  And every case names the fixture it needs and the child ticket it covers

Scenario: A case is executable by an engineer who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer with a staging URL, the E08-T05 fixture corpus and no other context
  When they execute group 5 (order-book reconstruction) end to end
  Then every step resolves to an unambiguous observable outcome via REST, WS or a metric
  And no step requires reading backend source to decide pass or fail

Scenario: Failure case - silent book divergence must be catchable
  Given case E08-TC-E06 replays the sequence-gap fixture
  When the book is compared against an independent REST snapshot oracle after resync
  Then the plan requires a top-50-level price/size equality assertion
  And a divergence with no DESYNCED state having been published is recorded as a P0 defect

Scenario: Edge case - instrument metadata changes under a live chart
  Given the instruments-info fixture that changes BTCUSDT tick size between refreshes
  When case E08-TC-A08 forces a catalogue refresh
  Then the plan requires a new instrument_versions row, a bumped metadata_version and re-validated rounding on the client
  And stale client-side rounding is recorded as a P1 defect against US-MKT-004

Scenario: Non-automatable cases are declared, not hidden
  Given a case that requires a real 12-hour catalogue refresh window
  When the plan marks it manual-only
  Then it states the manual execution cadence and links the follow-up automation Task
  And it is not silently counted as automated coverage in the traceability table
```

## Technical notes / design
- The plan is written against fixtures, not live Bybit, so it is deterministic and consumes no rate-limit budget (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.3). Live/demo execution is a separate, explicitly-marked smoke subset owned by `E08-T05`.
- Group ordering matches dependency order so a partially-implemented staging build can still run groups 1-3.
- Cases must assert on **internal vocabulary only** (principle P3, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §0): a case that asserts a Bybit field name outside the adapter is itself a defect in the plan.
- Where the observable is a metric, the case names the exact metric and label set from `E08-T06`'s registry rather than "check the dashboard".

## Test plan
- Peer review by the second QA/SDET plus the E08 tech lead; review checklist: every case has an oracle, every case names a fixture, no case depends on wall-clock luck.
- Dry-run execution of one case per group against the current staging build; unexecutable steps are rewritten, not waived.
- The traceability table is generated/checked by a small script so it cannot silently drift from the case list.

## Security notes
- No credential appears in the plan or in any fixture reference; fixtures are pre-redacted by `E08-T05`'s capture tool and the plan restates that requirement.
- Cases that probe error-message content must assert that upstream exchange error bodies are not echoed verbatim to clients (deferred detail to `E08-X02`).

## Accessibility notes
- Group 3 and group 1 cases that touch `SCR-100..104`, `SCR-041` and `SCR-152` must state the keyboard-only path alongside the pointer path; the full audit lives in `E08-Q05`.
- Any case whose expected result is "the value turns red" must also state the non-colour signal (text, icon, `aria-live` announcement) per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
- The plan references but does not duplicate the budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 (#3 tick→screen, #5 ingestion throughput, #6 backend-internal, #8 memory/symbol); numeric assertions live in `E08-Q04`.
- Functional cases must be runnable inside a normal CI window; anything needing >10 minutes is tagged and routed to the nightly pack.

## Observability
- Each group lists the metrics and log events that should move while it executes (`ingest_events_total`, `bus_subscriber_lag`, `book_resync_total`, `clock_drift_seconds`, connection-state gauges), so a silent no-op implementation fails the case.
- Plan execution results are recorded in the QA run log referenced by `E08-Q06`.

## Definition of Done
- Plan merged, reviewed by a second QA engineer and the E08 tech lead.
- Traceability table complete for US-MKT-001..009 with zero uncovered stories.
- One case per group dry-run executed and the results recorded on the ticket.
- Automation split agreed and reflected in `E08-Q02`, `E08-Q03`, `E08-Q04`, `E08-Q05` scope.
- Linked from `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`.

## Dependencies
- `E08-T01` (ports/error taxonomy define the observable error vocabulary), `E08-S01` (catalogue endpoints), `E08-T04` (WS ingestion skeleton) must exist in at least contract form.
- Fixture corpus `E08-T05` is required for execution but not for authoring; authoring may proceed against the fixture manifest.

title: Contract & integration test pack for the adapter against recorded Bybit fixtures
body:
## Context
Adapter rule 5 (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14.2) is binding: every adapter ships a contract-test suite run against recorded fixtures plus an opt-in live smoke test. `E08-T05` builds the corpus and the replay harness; this ticket builds the **executable pack** that turns the black-box plan (`E08-Q01`) groups 1-6 into automated tests, and turns **R6 Feed rot** from an incident into a CI failure.

The distinction from the engineering tickets' own unit tests matters: those test each module's internals. This pack tests the *boundary* — raw recorded Bybit frames in, internal domain events and public REST/WS payloads out — so it stays valid across the refactors E17 will impose when the WS gateway is built on top.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/tests/contract/bybit/` — **adapter contract tests**, one module per stream, each feeding raw fixture frames through the real adapter and asserting the normalised event:
  - `publicTrade` → `TradeEvent` (side, price/qty as `Decimal`, ms→µs timestamp, trade id, block-trade flag).
  - `orderbook.200` snapshot/delta → `BookSnapshot`/`BookDelta` with `u`/`seq` monotonicity, zero-size deletes, and depth truncation.
  - `tickers` full vs delta frames → `TickerEvent` with correct merge of partial payloads.
  - `kline` list-of-lists (descending) → ascending `KlineEvent` with `end = start + interval_ms - 1` and `confirm → confirmed`.
  - `instruments-info` → `Instrument` incl. every filter field of `24-internal-schemas.md` §2.
  - Error payloads `10018`, `10002`, `10001`, 5xx and HTML error pages → the internal taxonomy of `E08-T01`.
- **Schema-drift / feed-rot guard**: a test that asserts the *set* of fields present in each fixture payload equals a checked-in expected-field manifest, failing loudly with a diff when Bybit adds, renames or removes a field — plus a documented triage procedure (update manifest + adapter, or file a defect).
- **Round-trip invariants** (property-based, Hypothesis): replaying any book fixture and then applying an independent REST snapshot produces identical top-N levels; replaying a trade fixture twice is idempotent; kline paging over arbitrary split points reconstructs the same series as a single call.
- `services/api/tests/integration/ingestion/` — **pipeline integration tests** over the `E08-T05` replay harness: fixture → ConnectionManager → bus → book/bar state → REST/WS read surface, asserting `GET /market/orderbook`, `GET /market/trades`, `GET /market/klines`, `GET /market/data-coverage` and the WS topics `book.{symbol}.{depth}`, `trades.{symbol}`, `ticker.{symbol}` match the plan's expected results.
- **OpenAPI/WS contract assertions**: every response asserted against the schemas in `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the JSON Schemas of `23-ws-protocol.md` §13-15 via the shared validator from E02's codegen pipeline — no hand-written duplicate expectations.
- **P3 leakage test**: a test that imports every module outside `candleviewer/exchange/bybit/` and asserts no Bybit-native field name appears in emitted payloads (complements the lint rule in `E08-X03`).
- CI wiring: the pack runs on every PR touching `exchange/`, `ingestion/` or `bus/`, and nightly in full; fixture-heavy cases are marked so the PR subset stays under the CI budget.

## Out of scope
- Building or refreshing the fixture corpus and capture tool (`E08-T05`).
- Live/demo connectivity smoke tests (`E08-T05`, run with `pytest -m exchange_smoke`).
- Chaos/failure-injection scenarios (`E08-Q03`) and load/soak (`E08-Q04`).
- Browser E2E and a11y (`E08-Q05`).
- Downstream consumers' own contract tests (E12, E17, E22).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every fixture in the corpus is exercised by at least one test
  Given the E08-T05 fixture manifest
  When the contract pack runs
  Then every manifest entry is referenced by at least one test id
  And an unreferenced fixture fails a coverage meta-test with its name

Scenario: A Bybit payload change fails CI instead of production
  Given a fixture is edited to add an unknown field and rename an existing one to a Bybit-side name
  When the feed-rot guard runs
  Then the test fails naming both the added and the renamed field
  And the failure message links the triage procedure in the pack README

Scenario: Failure case - a sequence gap must invalidate, never patch
  Given the sequence-gap fixture is replayed through the pipeline
  When the gap frame is processed
  Then the book state becomes DESYNCED, a resubscribe is issued and book_resync_total increments
  And no delta is applied across the gap, asserted by comparing against the REST snapshot oracle

Scenario: Edge case - kline page boundary
  Given the page-boundary kline fixture covering exactly 1000 and 1001 rows
  When fetch_klines pages across the boundary
  Then the reconstructed series has no duplicated or missing bar open time
  And the property test over arbitrary split points also passes

Scenario: Internal vocabulary never leaks
  Given the P3 leakage test
  When any module outside exchange/bybit/ emits an event or API payload
  Then no Bybit-native key name appears in the serialised output
  And a deliberate violation added in a scratch branch fails the test
```

## Technical notes / design
- Tests are authored against the **ports** of `E08-T01`, not concrete classes, so a second exchange adapter can reuse the same contract suite verbatim — that reuse is the point of adapter rule 5.
- Time is injected (frozen clock helper) so kline boundaries, staleness and clock-sync cases are deterministic.
- Fixture replay runs at accelerated speed for CI; the 1x path is exercised only in the nightly soak (`E08-Q04`).
- Expected-field manifests live next to the fixtures and are reviewed by CODEOWNERS for `exchange/` so a silent manifest update cannot slip through.

## Test plan
- Self-verifying: the pack is its own deliverable. Verification is done by **mutation**: deliberately break the delta-merge, the descending-kline reversal, the zero-size delete handling and the `confirm` flag, and confirm a distinct test fails for each.
- Coverage: the pack contributes to the ≥85% backend threshold of `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`; the `exchange/bybit/` package must reach ≥90% because it is the only place Bybit semantics live.
- Runtime budget measured and recorded; PR subset ≤ 4 minutes.

## Security notes
- A CI check asserts no fixture contains anything matching the secret patterns (API keys, signatures, `X-BAPI-*` headers, account ids); this test fails the build rather than warning.
- Error-mapping tests assert the internal error carries a sanitised message and that upstream bodies are logged at debug with redaction, never surfaced to a client payload.
- Fixtures are treated as untrusted input: parser tests include malformed JSON, truncated frames, oversized payloads and unexpected types to prove the adapter rejects rather than crashes.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A — no UI surface in this pack. UI verification is `E08-Q05`. Stated explicitly per the DoR "N/A must be justified" rule.

## Performance notes
- Replay throughput of the harness is asserted to exceed 10x real-time so the nightly full-corpus run completes inside its window.
- The pack records per-stream parse time and fails if median parse exceeds the ≤3 ms budget of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4 for the representative frame set (a smoke-level guard; the real numbers come from `E08-Q04`).

## Observability
- Integration tests assert the metric registry of `E08-T06` actually moves: `ingest_events_total`, `ingest_lag_seconds`, `book_resync_total`, `bus_queue_depth`, connection-state gauges.
- A test asserts every mapped error emits a structured log with the internal error code and no secret material.

## Definition of Done
- Pack merged, green in CI on PR subset and nightly full run.
- Mutation checks executed and recorded on the ticket (one deliberate break per invariant, each caught).
- Every `E08-Q01` case marked "automated" is genuinely automated and cross-linked by id.
- Feed-rot triage procedure documented in the pack README and linked from `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Coverage gate green; `exchange/bybit/` ≥ 90%.

## Dependencies
- `E08-Q01` defines the cases; `E08-T05` provides corpus + harness; `E08-S05`/`E08-S06` provide book and backfill behaviour to assert.
- E02 codegen pipeline supplies the shared OpenAPI/WS schema validator.

## Branch
`chore/e08-contract-integration-pack`

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §2 (mappings), §14.1-14.2 (ports, adapter rules)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (contract + integration layers)
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, §13-15
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §0 principle P3, §3.1-3.3
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` R6 Feed rot, R7 Data accuracy

2. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (contract + integration layers)
3. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, §13-15
4. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §0 principle P3, §3.1-3.3
5. `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` R6 Feed rot, R7 Data accuracy

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `services/api/ingestion/`
- `services/api/recorder/`
- `services/api/replay/`
- `services/api/bars/`
- `services/api/orderflow/`

- `tests/` — mirrored unit/integration test paths for the module(s) above
