title: Design the chart chassis: pane chrome, axes, crosshair, legend, diagnostics
body:
## Context
This is the visual foundation every other chart surface is built on. **SCR-030** is described in `14-screens-catalogue.md` as "the spine of the product", and its chrome — axes, crosshair, legend, pane backgrounds, the bar countdown — is what E12's series, E13's indicators, E14's drawings, E18's footprint and E21's heatmap all render *inside*. A chassis decision made loosely here is re-litigated in six Epics.

SCR-030 carries a hard gate that this ticket must respect: the **mandatory WebGL engine spike gate** (owner decision #2.2.1) — the screen "may not be signed off until the custom-engine spike demonstrates, on the reference machine and recorded as evidence attached to the sign-off," 100k bars with footprint text at >=60 fps, sustained 100 ms-cadence updates with no dropped frames over 10 minutes, and the same numbers in Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2. **E06** produces that evidence; this ticket attaches it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-030 chassis** (chrome only, not order-flow content): panel header, pane stack, gutters, the time-axis strip, the price-axis gutter, the Deep Stats strip slot, the sub-pane divider treatment.
- **CMP-188 PriceAxis** — tick density, label typography (`font.mono`), the drag-to-rescale affordance **and its keyboard equivalent**, the scale-lock badge, and the log/percent/inverted mode indicators.
- **CMP-189 TimeAxis** — label decimation rules at each zoom level (what is dropped first, and what is never dropped), session/day-boundary markers, maintenance-window markers, the auto/fit control cluster.
- **CMP-190 Crosshair** + **CMP-197 ChartTooltip** — line treatment, axis label pills, magnet-mode affordance, tooltip content layout and its collision/flip rules near pane edges.
- **CMP-226 BarCountdown** — normal, warning (amber in the final 10 s per `US-CHART-008`) and closed states; the warn state **adds a word, not just a colour**.
- **CMP-199 ChartLegend** — per-pane legend with swatch, value, visibility toggle; the "many indicators" overflow behaviour.
- **CMP-198 ChartWatermark / PaneBackground** — grid line hierarchy (major/minor), watermark treatment, pane background per theme.
- **Multi-pane chrome** — splitters (with their keyboard-resize affordance), collapsed-pane stubs, pane focus indication, per-pane labelling (feeds E11-S09).
- **SCR-046 diagnostics overlay** — layout, the threshold treatment **paired with text**, the sparkline row, the copy-diagnostics control.
- All of the above in **dark, light and high-contrast** themes and in **comfortable, compact and dense** density modes — the density triple is one coherent switch (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rule 5), so the three density variants must be drawn, not described.
- **States** per SCR-030: loading (skeleton grid), streaming, **stale** (canvas dims 15 %, "Stale 4 s" chip), disconnected, replay-mode border, demo/live badge, low-GPU degraded ("Reduced detail…").
- The **aggregation indicator** treatment for E11-S12's LOD disclosure.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cells, profiles, heatmap, bubbles, Deep Stats *content* — E18/E19/E20/E21/E22 design tracks; this ticket defines the chrome they sit in and the slots they occupy.
- Order/position line overlays — E31's design track.
- Drawing tools and their toolbar — E14.
- Scale/time context menus and go-to-date — **E11-D03**. Data table, empty and error states — **E11-D04**.
- Chart settings dialog beyond the Scales section — E15.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The engine spike gate is satisfied before sign-off
  Given SCR-030's mandatory WebGL engine spike gate
  When this design is submitted for sign-off
  Then the E06 spike evidence is attached: 100k bars with footprint text at >= 60 fps, a 10-minute sustained 100 ms-cadence run with no dropped frames, and the same numbers in Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2
  And sign-off is withheld if that evidence is absent or fails its targets

Scenario: Every chrome element is specified at all three densities
  Given comfortable, compact and dense density modes
  When the axis, crosshair, legend and pane chrome specs are inspected
  Then each is drawn at all three densities with explicit spacing, type scale and tick-density values
  And the three change together as one switch, with no density-specific one-off

Scenario: Axis labels decimate predictably
  Given the time axis at 0.5, 3, 12 and 50 pixels per bar
  When label decimation is specified
  Then the rule states what is dropped first and what is never dropped at each level
  And an implementer can derive the visible label set at any zoom without asking

Scenario: No state is conveyed by colour alone
  Given every state of SCR-030: loading, streaming, stale, disconnected, replay, demo/live, degraded
  When each is reviewed against the colour-only rule
  Then each carries a text or shape equivalent
  And the bar-countdown warn state adds a word, not only an amber colour

Scenario: Keyboard equivalents are designed, not assumed
  Given drag-to-rescale on the price axis and drag-to-resize on pane splitters
  When the specs are reviewed
  Then each drag affordance has a designed keyboard equivalent with its focus treatment and its announcement
  And no functionality exists that is reachable only by dragging or only by hovering

Scenario: Contrast holds in all three themes
  Given dark, light and high-contrast themes
  When every foreground/background pair in the chassis is measured
  Then text pairs meet 4.5:1 and non-text UI pairs meet 3:1
  And the measurements are recorded in the sign-off, not asserted
```

## Technical notes / design
**Gridline hierarchy** is the single highest-leverage decision in this ticket. Chart grids either recede and let price dominate, or they compete with it and the chart reads as noise. The spec must fix: major/minor line opacity per theme, the rule for *which* price levels get a major line (round numbers scaled to the instrument's tick size, not every nth pixel), and the interaction with the crosshair line so the two are distinguishable when they coincide.

**Axis label decimation** is specified as a rule, not as a picture, because it must hold at continuous zoom: labels are placed at "nice" intervals (1/2/5 × 10^n) with a minimum pixel gap, and the *last* things dropped are the boundary labels (session start, day start) — dropping a day boundary at low zoom loses the user's place entirely.

**Density coupling.** Each density mode fixes a triple: `{ cellPadPx, fontSizeClass, lodBias }` (E11-T04). The design must supply the actual numbers for all three modes, since a density mode that exists only as an adjective becomes three engineers' three interpretations.

**Tooltip collision.** The crosshair tooltip must flip rather than clip near pane edges, and must never cover the last-price line — SCR-030's constraint that labels "never obscure the last price" is a layout rule with a defined priority order, specified here.

## Test plan
Design verification rather than software testing:
- **Contrast audit** across every pair, in all three themes, recorded numerically.
- **Density walkthrough**: the full chassis rendered at all three densities, checked for collision, truncation and illegible type.
- **Edge-density check**: axis labels at the most extreme zoom in and out; legend with 12 indicators; tooltip at every pane edge.
- **Colour-blind simulation** (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) over every state, confirming each remains distinguishable — feeds open item **O5**.
- **Prototype review** against the E06 spike build so the specs are checked against what the engine can actually draw, not only against what looks good in Figma.
- Design QA of the built result is **E11-D08**.

## Security notes
No direct security surface. One relevant constraint carried from SCR-046: the diagnostics overlay is designed to be **screenshotted into bug reports**, so its layout must not include account identifiers, balances, order data or user identity — the design fixes what fields exist, and therefore fixes what a screenshot can leak. The demo/live badge is the inverse case and is a **safety-critical** design element: it must be unmistakable at a glance, because the cost of a trader misreading which environment they are in is a real order on a live account.

## Accessibility notes
- **Focus treatment** for every focusable chrome element, using CMP-004 FocusRing; focus order follows visual order across panes.
- **Keyboard equivalents designed for every pointer gesture**: axis rescale, splitter resize, crosshair movement, legend toggles (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6).
- **Target sizes** meet the §4 minimum, including splitters and axis drag zones, which are the easiest to draw too thin.
- **Contrast** measured, not eyeballed; the high-contrast theme is drawn as a first-class theme rather than derived.
- **No colour-only encoding** anywhere, including the stale, degraded, replay and demo/live states.
- **Reduced motion**: every animated affordance (crosshair, countdown, stale dimming) has a specified reduced-motion variant — see E11-D06 for the motion spec proper.
- **DOM-mirror alignment**: the canvas-control-surrogate pattern (§6.1) means invisible focusable elements are **sized to match their visual targets**, so the visual target sizes designed here *are* the a11y target sizes.
- Reviewed and signed off by the accessibility specialist; deeper review in **E11-D07**.

## Performance notes
Design decisions with direct frame-budget consequences, which is why this ticket is reviewed against the E06 build:
- Gridline count per pane and label count per axis feed the draw-call budget (<=18 per pane, <=40 for a 3-pane chart).
- Text quantity on screen drives the SDF batching budget (<=2.0 ms, <=6 text draw calls per pane).
- Effects that would require an extra render pass (blurs, shadows, translucent overlays) must be flagged at design time, because each one is a measurable slice of a 16.6 ms budget. Where such an effect is wanted, the design states the cheaper alternative it will fall back to under the degradation ladder.

## Observability
N/A for the design artefact. The diagnostics overlay design fixes which metrics are surfaced, which in turn fixes E11-T07's data contract — so the observability *surface* is decided here even though the instrumentation is not.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.
- [ ] **E06 spike evidence attached** and meeting its targets (SCR-030's mandatory gate, owner decision #2.2.1) — sign-off is blocked without it.
- [ ] SCR-030 and SCR-046 design sign-off acceptance checklists ticked item by item.
- [ ] All three density modes drawn with explicit numeric values for `cellPadPx`, font size class and tick density.

## Dependencies
- **E11-D01** — research decisions on gesture bindings, scale-lock behaviour and magnet defaults.
- **E05** — design-system v0 tokens, type scale, focus ring, density scale.
- **E06** — the spike evidence SCR-030's gate requires, and the build these specs are sanity-checked against.
- Blocks **E11-D03**, **E11-D04**, **E11-D05**, **E11-D06**, and the engineering stories **E11-S06**, **S07**, **S09** (design-ahead).

## Branch
`design/chart-engine-chassis` (Figma; repo branch only for `14-screens-catalogue.md`/`15-component-catalogue.md` updates arising from the work).

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-043, SCR-044, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047, SCR-048, SCR-049 (each entry's states, a11y, performance and design sign-off checklist)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` §7 — CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226, CMP-228, CMP-004
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` — tokens, theming, motion, density, a11y
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 (no hover/drag-only), §4 (focus, target size, zoom), §6 (canvas a11y), §7 (reduced motion)
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`, `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 (visual encoding rules, density modes)
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 (design-ready gate)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030 (spine, states, mandatory spike gate), SCR-046, SCR-049
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-006, US-CHART-008
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.5 (axes), §5 (encoding rules)
- `docs/research/24-owner-decisions.md` owner decision #2.2.1 (mandatory spike gate)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**

2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)

- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**

**Done means**

- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.

title: Design the price/time scale menus, scale settings and the go-to-date dialog
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-007` makes log and linear scales **Must** and percentage **Should**, and `US-CHART-006` makes the manual scale-lock behaviour explicit: dragging the price axis disengages autoscale, a lock badge appears, and double-clicking restores auto-fit. Those behaviours are exposed through two small but heavily-used surfaces — the scale context menus (**SCR-043**) and the Scales section of the chart settings dialog (**SCR-031**) — plus the go-to-date dialog (**SCR-044**) that `US-CHART-010` and the recorded-history boundary make non-trivial.

These are small surfaces with sharp edges. `US-CHART-007` requires that on a series containing non-positive values, **log scale is disabled with an explanation rather than rendering incorrectly**; SCR-044 requires a clear failure when the target **precedes recorded history**. Both are error states that must be designed, not discovered.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-043 price-scale menu**: auto / logarithmic / percentage / indexed-to-100, invert, lock, merge indicator scales, reset. Checkable menu items with state announced; reachable via `Shift+F10` when the scale has focus.
- **SCR-043 time-scale menu**: auto-fit, go to date (opens SCR-044), spacing presets, show/hide session dividers and maintenance-window markers, timezone.
- **Disabled-with-explanation** treatment: the log option on a series with non-positive values must show *why* it is unavailable, inline, not as a silent grey item (`US-CHART-007` scenario 3).
- **SCR-031 Scales tab**: the section of the chart settings dialog covering scale mode, precision, autoscale-includes-drawings, countdown toggle, and the **CMP-228 PreviewTile** live preview against a real chart.
- **SCR-044 go-to-date dialog**: date+time entry with **UTC and local shown side by side**, quick jumps (session open, yesterday, last swing, last journal entry, last alert), and the **"before recorded history" error state drawn with the recording-start timestamp**.
- The **scale-lock badge** treatment on the price axis (its resting, hover and focus states) and the double-click-to-reset affordance.
- "Applies to this panel / all panels / as new default" scope control for settings (SCR-031's checklist item).
- All states in dark, light and high-contrast.

## Out of scope
- The rest of the chart settings dialog (General, Appearance, Trading, Performance tabs) — E15.
- Footprint settings (SCR-032) — E18.
- The underlying scale projection maths — E11-S05.
- Session/day-boundary *semantics* (`US-CHART-009`) — owned by E12; this ticket designs the toggle that surfaces the markers.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An unavailable scale mode explains itself
  Given a series containing non-positive values
  When the price-scale menu is opened
  Then the logarithmic option is shown as unavailable with an inline explanation of why
  And it is never silently greyed out, and never allowed to render incorrectly

Scenario: Go-to-date fails fast and usefully before recorded history
  Given recorded history for the symbol starts on 2026-09-01 08:00 UTC
  When the user requests 2026-08-15
  Then an error state names the recording-start timestamp in text
  And it fails immediately rather than showing a spinner, and Esc cancels without moving the chart

Scenario: Both timezones are visible at entry time
  Given the go-to-date dialog is open
  Then UTC and local time are shown side by side with the active timezone stated next to the field
  And the format hint is explicit, so there is no ambiguity about what was entered

Scenario: Scale menus are real menus with announced state
  Given the price scale has keyboard focus
  When the user presses Shift+F10
  Then the context menu opens with menu semantics
  And auto, logarithmic, percent, invert and lock are checkable items whose state is announced

Scenario: The scale-lock badge is unmistakable and reversible
  Given the user drags the price axis
  Then autoscale disengages and a lock badge appears with a text label, not an icon alone
  And the design specifies double-click-to-reset and its keyboard equivalent
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why the disabled-log case gets its own design attention.** The naive implementation greys the item out, the user tries three times, and then files a bug. The design specifies an inline reason ("Log scale needs all-positive values; this series contains a value <= 0") attached to the item itself, because a tooltip on a disabled control is famously unreliable across platforms and assistive technology.

**Menu item state.** Checkable items use `aria-checked` with `role="menuitemradio"` for the mutually-exclusive scale modes and `role="menuitemcheckbox"` for the independent toggles (invert, lock, dividers). Drawing these as two visually distinct groups makes the mutual exclusivity readable without trial and error.

**Preview tile.** CMP-228 renders a live miniature of the actual chart, not a generic sample — SCR-031's requirement for a "live preview against a real chart". The design must specify what the tile shows when the chart is empty or errored, which is the case everyone forgets.

## Test plan
- Contrast audit across all three themes for menus, dialog and badge.
- Keyboard walkthrough: `Shift+F10` open, arrow navigation, `Esc` close and focus restoration, tab order within the dialog.
- Error-state review: every failure path in SCR-044 drawn (before history, invalid format, no data at target).
- Screen-reader review of menu semantics with the accessibility specialist.
- Design QA of the built result in **E11-D08**.

## Security notes
No security surface. - The scale-lock badge carries a **text label**; the lock state is never icon-or-colour-only.
- The date field has an explicit **format hint** and a keyboard-operable calendar; the active timezone is stated next to the field, not implied.
- Errors are described in **text**, including the recording-start timestamp.
- `Esc` cancels the dialog without moving the chart, and focus returns to the invoking control.
- Every numeric field in SCR-031 carries its **units in the label**; Reset requires confirmation.
- Design source reviewed with the accessibility specialist; deeper review in **E11-D07**.

## Performance notes
SCR-043's constraint is a design constraint too: a scale-mode change is a **projection change only — no data refetch, redraw within one frame**. The design must therefore not imply a loading state for a scale change; showing a spinner for something that takes one frame teaches users the app is slower than it is. SCR-044's budget: a jump inside recorded history renders the target window in <=800 ms; out-of-history requests fail fast.

## Observability
Design fixes the analytics surface: `chart.price_scale_changed`, `chart.time_scale_changed` (SCR-043), `chart.go_to_date` with `{target, found}` (SCR-044), `chart.settings_changed` with `{section, key}` (SCR-031).

title: Contribute chart primitives, tokens and density modes to the design system
body:
## Context
E11 introduces a band of components that exist nowhere else in the product: **CMP-180 ChartRoot, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-189 TimeAxis, CMP-190 Crosshair, CMP-196 MultiChartLinker, CMP-197 ChartTooltip, CMP-198 ChartWatermark/PaneBackground, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-226 BarCountdown**. `15-component-catalogue.md` classifies these as **chart primitives** — "engine-level render objects with no DOM" — which makes them a genuinely unusual design-system contribution: most of them have no CSS, no DOM node and no Storybook story in the conventional sense.

The reason to route them through the design system anyway is that **E12, E13, E14, E18, E19 and E21 all draw inside them**. If the chart token set is invented ad hoc in E11 and then extended ad hoc in each of those Epics, the chart ends up with six palettes. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 makes this a gate: "Component(s) used are in `15-component-catalogue.md`; any new component has a design-system entry, **not an ad hoc one-off**."

This ticket also ships the **density-mode triple** that `26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rule 5 requires to move as one switch.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Chart token slots** added to the design-system token set: `color.chart.axis`, `color.chart.grid.major`, `color.chart.grid.minor`, `color.chart.crosshair`, `color.chart.watermark`, `color.chart.pane.bg`, `color.chart.pane.bg.focused`, plus the up/down/neutral series slots and the delta-ramp endpoints — each defined for **dark, light and high-contrast**.
- **Colour ramps** (the source values E11-T04 turns into LUTs): the diverging delta ramp and the sequential intensity ramp, specified in **OkLab** stops so the engine's interpolation and the design's intent agree.
- **Density scale** for chart surfaces: `comfortable` | `compact` | `dense`, each fixing the triple `{ cellPadPx, fontSizeClass, lodBias }` with concrete numbers — the single switch of §5 rule 5.
- **Pattern/hatch registry** entries for the non-colour-only encodings: the `(estimated)` hatch (CMP-227's engine counterpart), the imbalance outline pattern, and the reduced-detail indicator — so later Epics attach a registered pattern id rather than inventing a new visual language.
- **Catalogue entries** for the nine chart primitives above: tier, purpose, props, a11y contract, tokens, Storybook plan and test requirements, matching the existing `15-component-catalogue.md` §7 format.
- **Storybook strategy for canvas components**: each primitive gets a story that mounts a real engine instance with a fixed fixture, so "Storybook coverage" for a no-DOM component means a rendered, inspectable canvas rather than a placeholder — the stories named in the catalogue (PriceAxis: Linear/Log/Dragging(keyboard demo); TimeAxis: Default/ZoomedIn/ZoomedOut; Crosshair: Default/SyncedAcrossPanes/KeyboardDriven).
- **CMP-004 FocusRing** usage contract for canvas-surrogate elements, since focus rings on invisible mirror nodes are a case the base component was not designed for.
- Updates committed to `15-component-catalogue.md` and `16-design-system-brief.md`.

## Out of scope
- Building the components — engineering, across E11's stories.
- Footprint, profile, heatmap and bubble primitives (CMP-181..187, CMP-192..195) — contributed by E18/E19/E21 against the foundation laid here.
- The design-system's own infrastructure (token pipeline, Storybook setup, visual-regression baseline) — **E05**.
- Final colour-blind-safe palette selection — open item **O5**, validated in the M8 a11y pass.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Chart colours come from tokens, not from code
  Given the engine's rendering code after this contribution lands
  When it is searched for colour literals
  Then no hard-coded colour exists outside the theme ingestion layer
  And every chart colour resolves to a named design-system token in all three themes

Scenario: Density is one switch with real numbers
  Given the comfortable, compact and dense modes
  When the density scale is inspected
  Then each fixes cellPadPx, font size class and lodBias with concrete values
  And no surface can adopt one of the three without the other two

Scenario: Every primitive has a catalogue entry before it is built
  Given CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199 and CMP-226
  When 15-component-catalogue.md is read
  Then each has tier, purpose, props, a11y contract, tokens, Storybook stories and test requirements
  And the engineering story that builds it references that entry rather than inventing a contract

Scenario: Non-colour encodings are registered, not improvised
  Given a later Epic needs to encode "estimated" or "imbalanced"
  When it consults the pattern registry
  Then a registered hatch or outline pattern exists with its usage rule
  And introducing a new encoding requires a design-system contribution, not a local decision

Scenario: Canvas components have real Storybook coverage
  Given a chart-primitive story is opened in Storybook
  Then a live engine instance renders with a fixed fixture
  And the story is inspectable and covered by the visual-regression baseline, not a static placeholder
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why OkLab stops.** A diverging ramp interpolated in sRGB passes through a desaturated grey-brown mid-band and has visibly uneven perceptual steps — on a delta ramp that means two meaningfully different delta values look identical. Specifying stops in OkLab and letting E11-T04 interpolate there keeps steps perceptually even. The design supplies stops; the engine supplies interpolation; neither reinvents the other's half.

**The density triple is the interesting constraint.** Density is usually a spacing token. Here it also changes *how much data is drawn*, because font size class determines the minimum legible cell-text height, which determines the LOD threshold at which text is dropped (§3.6). Splitting them would let a user select "dense" spacing with "comfortable" LOD thresholds and get unreadable overlapping text — which is exactly why §5 rule 5 requires them to move together, and why this ticket ships them as one object rather than three tokens.

**Storybook for no-DOM components.** The catalogue already demands stories and visual tests for these primitives. The approach: a `<ChartStoryHarness>` that mounts a real engine with a deterministic fixture and a fixed viewport, so a story is a real render. This also makes the stories usable as golden-image sources (E11-T08), which is why the harness is worth building once here rather than per component.

## Test plan
- **Token-coverage check**: every token slot defined for all three themes; a missing theme value fails the token build.
- **Contrast audit** over every chart token pair in every theme, recorded numerically (the design-side counterpart of E11-T04's automated CI test).
- **Ramp evaluation**: the delta ramp sampled at 16 stops and reviewed for perceptual evenness and for distinguishability under deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulation.
- **Catalogue completeness check**: each of the nine primitives has every required field.
- **Storybook review**: each named story renders and is captured in the visual-regression baseline.
- Design QA of the built components in **E11-D08**.

## Security notes
No security surface — tokens, ramps and catalogue entries.

One durable consequence worth recording: the **pattern registry is a safety mechanism, not a styling one**. The `(estimated)` hatch is how the product keeps its promise (principle P10 in `20-architecture.md`) that heuristic-derived data is never presented as measured fact. A later Epic that encodes estimated data without a registered pattern is making a truthfulness error, not a visual one, and routing the encoding through the design system is what makes that error reviewable.

## Accessibility notes
- Every token pair carries a **recorded contrast measurement**; the high-contrast theme is authored as a first-class theme, not derived by a filter.
- The **pattern/hatch registry exists so that colour is never the sole carrier of meaning** — it is the design-system enforcement of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rules 1–4 and of WCAG 1.4.1.
- Each primitive's catalogue entry states its **a11y contract** explicitly, as the existing entries do: PriceAxis's keyboard rescale, TimeAxis's keyboard pan/zoom, Crosshair's keyboard-primary path, ChartTooltip's `aria-hidden` (to prevent duplicate announcement alongside the DOM mirror), MultiChartLinker's once-only sync announcement.
- **CMP-004 FocusRing** on canvas-surrogate nodes: the ring must be visible against the canvas content behind it in all three themes, which is a harder case than a ring on a solid surface and is specified here.
- Colour-blind simulation over the ramps feeds open item **O5**.

## Performance notes
Token and density decisions have frame-budget consequences, so they are made with the budget in view: the number of distinct colours in a ramp determines LUT size (256 entries is the fixed budget), and the density mode's `lodBias` directly shifts how much is drawn at a given zoom. A density mode that retains too much detail would push B5 over budget — so the `dense` mode's `lodBias` is validated against the benchmark rather than chosen by eye.

## Observability
N/A for the artefacts. The density mode and theme name are reported in `frame` stats (E11-T04), so a performance report always states which density produced it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.

- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.

- [ ] Token set builds cleanly for all three themes with no missing values.

- [ ] Design-system team sign-off (this is a contribution to their surface, not a local addition).

title: Specify chart motion: momentum, transitions and reduced-motion variants
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-006` requires pan and zoom "with inertia that **respects reduced-motion settings**", and `05-accessibility-standard.md` §7 makes `prefers-reduced-motion` a binding requirement rather than a nicety. Momentum is also the single most "feel"-dependent thing in the engine: the difference between a chart that feels responsive and one that feels slippery is a time constant, and it is not a number an engineer should have to guess.

`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.5 already proposes the model — velocity-based with exponential decay `v *= exp(-dt/tau)`, tau = 120 ms, terminated below 0.02 px/ms, cancelled on any new pointer-down. This ticket validates that against the E06 build with real users (E11-D01's findings), fixes the remaining motion in the chassis, and specifies every reduced-motion variant so the fallback is designed rather than improvised as "turn the animation off".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Pan/zoom momentum**: decay constant tau, termination threshold, cancel-on-pointer-down behaviour, and the maximum fling distance — validated by feel against the E06 build, not chosen from the document alone.
- **Zoom transitions**: cursor-anchored zoom is instantaneous by design (it tracks the wheel), but double-click-to-reset and go-to-date jumps are **animated transitions**; their duration, easing and the rule for when a jump is too far to animate (beyond which it cuts, because a 3-second pan across 30,000 bars is disorienting, not elegant).
- **Crosshair**: no easing on position (it must track the pointer exactly — a lagging crosshair is a correctness problem in a trading tool), but the fade in/out and the magnet snap have specified timings.
- **CMP-226 BarCountdown**: the 1 Hz tick treatment and the transition into the warn state in the final 10 seconds — specified so the warn state is a **change of word and weight**, not a flash.
- **Stale-state dimming** (SCR-030: canvas dims 15 %): the fade duration and the recovery transition.
- **LOD step-down / step-up**: whether the transition is instantaneous or crossfaded, and the aggregation-indicator's appearance animation.
- **Pane splitter drag** and collapsed-pane expand/collapse timings.
- **Context-loss recovery** (SCR-048): the "restoring…" treatment's motion, if any.
- **A reduced-motion variant for every one of the above**, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §7 — stated individually rather than as a blanket "disable animation", because some of these (the countdown warn state, the stale dimming) carry information and must survive in a non-animated form.
- Output as a motion spec table: element, trigger, property, duration, easing curve, reduced-motion variant.

## Out of scope
- Drawing-tool and order-ticket motion — E14 and E31.
- Application-shell transitions (panel open/close, dialogs) — E05/E10.
- The motion implementation — E11-S04 and the consuming stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every animated element has a designed reduced-motion variant
  Given the motion spec table
  When prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is assumed
  Then every row states its reduced-motion variant explicitly
  And no row's variant is simply "no animation" where the animation carried information

Scenario: Momentum feel is validated on the real engine, not on paper
  Given the proposed decay constant of 120 ms
  When it is tested against the E06 build on the reference machine with the owner
  Then the final constant is recorded with the evidence behind it
  And any deviation from the 26-chart-engine-design.md proposal is noted with its reason

Scenario: The crosshair never lags the pointer
  Given the crosshair motion spec
  Then crosshair position has no easing and no interpolation
  And only its fade in/out and magnet snap carry timings

Scenario: Long jumps cut rather than animate
  Given a go-to-date jump spanning 30,000 bars
  When the transition rule is applied
  Then the distance exceeds the animate threshold and the view cuts to the target
  And the threshold is stated as a number, not as a judgement call

Scenario: Information-carrying states survive reduced motion
  Given the countdown warn state and the stale dimming
  When reduced motion is active
  Then each remains distinguishable through a non-animated means: a word change and a static dimmed treatment
  And no information is lost by disabling animation
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why tau is worth a ticket.** Exponential decay `v *= exp(-dt/tau)` is framerate-independent, which matters because a momentum implementation that multiplies per frame behaves differently at 30 fps and 60 fps — the chart would come to rest in a different place depending on how busy the machine was. The design fixes tau; the implementation (E11-S04) must integrate against elapsed time, not frame count, and the spec says so explicitly because this is a mistake that is easy to make and hard to notice.

**The "too far to animate" threshold.** Animated navigation is a spatial cue — it tells the user which direction they moved and how far. Beyond a certain distance that cue becomes useless and the animation is just a delay. The spec fixes a threshold in viewport-widths (proposed: 3), beyond which the transition cuts and the user is oriented by the axis labels instead.

**Reduced motion is not motion removal.** `05-accessibility-standard.md` §7's requirement is that motion not be *vestibularly triggering*, not that state changes become invisible. Where an animation conveys information — the countdown entering its warn state, the chart going stale — the reduced-motion variant substitutes an instant, non-animated change of the same information, which is why each row's variant is specified individually.

## Test plan
- **Feel validation** against the E06 build on the reference machine, with the owner, for momentum and zoom transitions specifically.
- **Reduced-motion walkthrough**: every specified element reviewed with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, confirming no information loss.
- **Vestibular review** with the accessibility specialist: no parallax, no large-area movement, no motion exceeding the standard's thresholds.
- **Frame-budget sanity**: any proposed transition that would require an extra render pass is flagged and re-specified.
- Implementation conformance is verified in **E11-D08** (design QA) and **E11-Q05** (a11y audit).

## Security notes
No security surface.

One safety note with a motion dimension: the **demo/live badge** and the replay-mode border are environment indicators where misreading has real financial consequence. Their motion spec must not include anything that could make the indicator momentarily ambiguous — no cross-fade between demo and live treatments, no transitional state where neither reads clearly. The change is instant, in both the normal and reduced-motion variants.

## Accessibility notes
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is honoured for **every** animated element, with a designed variant per element rather than a global switch (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §7).
- The engine reads the preference through `theme.reducedMotion` (E11-T04), giving one source of truth rather than per-component media queries.
- Information-carrying animations have non-animated equivalents, so reduced motion never costs a user information.
- No animation is the sole indicator of any state change.
- Motion durations stay within the standard's thresholds; nothing flashes more than three times per second (WCAG 2.3.1).
- The **keyboard** pan/zoom path (E11-S04) uses discrete steps rather than momentum, which is both the accessible path and the reduced-motion path — the spec notes that these coincide deliberately.

## Performance notes
Momentum is integrated by the scheduler's time-based animation loop, so dropped frames change nothing about where the chart comes to rest — a correctness property as much as a performance one, and specified here so it is not treated as an implementation detail. Transitions must not require an additional render pass; any that would are re-specified. Under the degradation ladder, animated transitions are among the first things shed, and the spec states which ones, so the shedding order is a design decision rather than an engineering convenience.

## Observability
N/A for the artefact. `theme.reducedMotion` is reported in `frame` stats so a perf or behaviour report states whether momentum was active.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.
- [ ] Motion spec table complete: element, trigger, property, duration, easing, reduced-motion variant for every animated element.
- [ ] Momentum constants validated against the E06 build with evidence recorded.
- [ ] Vestibular review signed off by the accessibility specialist.

## Dependencies
- **E11-D02** — the chassis whose elements are being animated.

- Blocks **E11-S04** (momentum implementation, design-ahead) and informs E11-S07, S09, S12.

## Branch

## References

title: Accessibility design review & screen-reader script for the bar/series band
body:
## Context
A WebGL canvas is, to assistive technology, an empty box. Everything E12 renders is therefore accessible only through deliberate constructions: the DOM mirror described in `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1–§6.2 and implemented by `CMP-180 ChartRoot`/`CMP-181 CandleSeries`, the rolling `aria-label` summary, the keyboard-driven crosshair, and the `SCR-045` data-table alternative that `US-CHART-014` declares to be an *equal-status* view.

Seven E12 design tickets have each made local a11y decisions. This ticket is the pass that checks them **as a set**, before any of them is built: it verifies that the vocabulary is consistent, that no state is announced twice or not at all, that the keyboard path across the whole band is unbroken, and it produces the **screen-reader script** — the normative, scenario-by-scenario expectation of what a user hears — that QA will later test against in E12's QA tickets and that engineering will implement against.

Without this ticket, a11y is verified per screen after the fact; with it, the band has one specification and one test oracle.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A **design-level a11y review** of E12-D03..E12-D08 producing a findings list with severities, each finding either fixed in the originating ticket before its sign-off or explicitly accepted with a reason recorded.
- The **screen-reader script**: for each scenario below, the expected announcement sequence, verbatim, with the mechanism (accessible name, `aria-describedby`, polite live region, or table cell) —
  - focusing the chart and hearing the rolling summary (`CMP-180`);
  - arrowing bar to bar and hearing OHLCV, including on Heikin-Ashi (where the script must state whether HA or real OHLC is read) and on each non-time mode;
  - `Home`/`End` jumps to range start/end;
  - opening `SCR-042` and moving across bar-mode groups, hearing each mode's one-line description and each disabled item's "Needs recorded ticks" reason;
  - entering a parameter and hearing its unit and validation error;
  - switching mode and hearing the single, polite confirmation;
  - a bar closing (forming → confirmed) without flooding;
  - a rebuild starting, progressing (not announced continuously), completing or being cancelled;
  - crossing an LOD threshold and hearing the new aggregation level;
  - reaching the partial-history boundary and the gap;
  - `Alt+T` into `SCR-045`, navigating rows, and returning focus to the chart;
  - `SCR-047` empty and `SCR-048` error, including the correlation id being selectable.
- A **keyboard map** for the band: every operation reachable without a pointer, with its key, its scope (global / chart / menu), and confirmation that nothing is hover-only (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 forbids hover-only functionality).
- An **announcement budget**: which events are announced, at what rate, and the throttling rule (`US-CHART-008` caps live-region announcements at ≤2/s; `CMP-226 BarCountdown` defaults to `aria-live="off"`).
- Contrast and non-colour-encoding audit results for every state introduced by E12, in both themes and under CVD simulation.
- The script handed to QA as the basis for the manual screen-reader pass required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, and to engineering as the implementation target via E12-D12.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell announcements (E18), profile/TPO panes (E19), indicator values (E13) — the script reserves their slots and states the contract, no more.
- Automated axe-core rule configuration and CI wiring (engineering/QA tickets).
- Remediation of components owned by other epics (findings are filed to them).
- Testing the built product — that is E12-D13's design QA pass and the E12 QA tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The whole band is operable by keyboard
  Given the keyboard map is complete
  When every E12 operation is listed
  Then each has a keyboard route with a stated key and scope
  And no operation exists that is reachable only by hovering or only by pointer

Scenario: The script is specific enough to test against
  Given a QA engineer reads the screen-reader script without access to the designs
  When they run a scenario
  Then they can determine pass or fail from the script alone, because the expected announcement is written verbatim
  And the mechanism producing each announcement is named

Scenario: Announcements are bounded (edge)
  Given a one-second interval where a bar closes every second and the crosshair is moving
  When the announcement budget is applied
  Then the combined announcement rate stays at or below two per second
  And the script states which announcement is dropped when they collide

Scenario: Heikin-Ashi ambiguity is resolved (edge)
  Given Heikin-Ashi is a derived transform of the real series
  When the bar-navigation script is inspected
  Then it states unambiguously whether the announced OHLC values are the Heikin-Ashi values or the real values, and how the other is reachable
  And the same rule is reflected in the SCR-045 table columns

Scenario: A finding cannot be fixed before sign-off (failure)
  Given a review finding requires a change that the design cannot absorb in this sprint
  When it is triaged
  Then it is recorded as an accepted risk with a named owner and a follow-up ticket
  And it is not silently closed, nor does it block sign-off without the CDO recording the decision
```

## Technical notes / design
- The DOM mirror is **windowed to the visible range** (`CMP-181`, standard §6.2); the script must therefore state what happens at the window edges — arrowing past the last mirrored bar must extend the window or announce the boundary, not fall silent.
- Two surfaces can announce the same fact (the canvas mirror and the `SCR-045` table). The script must assign ownership per fact so the user never hears it twice when both are open.
- Disabled menu items remain focusable and announce their reason; this is a deliberate deviation from the common "skip disabled items" pattern and must be written down so an implementer does not "fix" it.
- The rolling `aria-label` on `CMP-180` is throttled; specify its update trigger (range change, symbol change, mode change) rather than per render tick, which would flood.
- Where a state has no natural announcement moment (partial history is a property of the range, not an event), specify that it is part of the summary rather than a live-region message.
- Verify that every hotkey in the band is listed in `SCR-013` (hotkey cheatsheet) and editable in `SCR-113` (hotkey editor), so the keyboard map is discoverable by users, not only by this document.

## Test plan
- Walk each scenario against the E12-D03..E12-D08 frames with the a11y design lead and at least one screen-reader-proficient reviewer, using the reader(s) named in `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Contrast measurement of every new state pair in both themes; CVD simulation for all three common deficiency types.
- Keyboard-only traversal of the full band with no pointer attached, confirming focus is never lost or trapped.
- Cross-check the announcement budget arithmetic against the worst case (1 s bars + moving crosshair + a rebuild in progress).
- Confirm every hotkey appears in `SCR-013`; file any missing entry.
- Review findings triage with the CDO; each finding closed as fixed, deferred-with-owner or accepted-with-reason.

## Security notes
- The script must not cause account-scoped information to be announced on a market-data surface; verify that no announcement includes position, order or balance data (those belong to `US-CHART-013`'s overlay work, announced by its own surface).
- Correlation ids announced on `SCR-048` must be read as opaque identifiers; confirm they carry no session token or account identifier.
- The "Needs recorded ticks" announcement reveals recording state; confirm it is consistent with the RBAC rules for `GET /api/v1/recording/symbols` and is not announced to roles that cannot see it.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket **is** the accessibility deliverable for the band; it is governed by `05-accessibility-standard.md` end to end, targeting WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Non-negotiables verified here: no colour-only encoding of direction or state; no hover-only functionality; visible focus on every interactive element; announcements polite and throttled; the `SCR-045` table treated as equal status, not fallback.
- The script explicitly covers reduced-motion users, confirming they lose no information (cross-checked against E12-D10).
- Findings of severity "blocks a user from reading the chart at all" are P0 and block the originating ticket's sign-off.

## Performance notes
- The a11y constructions have a frame cost: the DOM mirror is windowed rather than full-series precisely so it does not scale with 100 k bars, and the rolling `aria-label` is throttled. The review must confirm no design decision here would force per-bar DOM for the whole series, which would breach the `SCR-030` budget.
- The `SCR-045` table reads the same in-memory series and issues no extra fetch; confirm the script does not imply otherwise.

## Observability
- No analytics are emitted by the a11y layer. The review notes which existing events (`chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.bar_mode_changed`) are sufficient to observe accessible-path usage, so adoption of the accessible view can be measured without adding assistive-technology detection, which the standard forbids.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Screen-reader script, keyboard map and announcement budget published in the repo and linked from `SCR-030`, `SCR-045` and `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- All findings triaged; P0 findings fixed in their originating design tickets before those tickets reach Done.
- Contrast/CVD audit results attached.
- Script handed to QA (referenced from the E12 QA tickets) and to engineering via E12-D12.
- **CDO and a11y design lead sign-off recorded; Status = Done**, before the Sprint 05 frontend stories begin.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D03, E12-D04, E12-D05, E12-D06, E12-D07, E12-D08 (all must have drafts to review; each may only reach Done after its findings are addressed).
- Cross-checks E12-D10 (reduced motion).
- Feeds E12-D12 (handoff), E12-D13 (design QA), the E12 QA tickets and every E12 frontend story.

## Branch
`design/e12-a11y-review-bar-series`

title: Engineering handoff pack for the bar-builder & series-rendering band
body:
## Context
E12's frontend stories run in Sprint 05–08 and are worth 63 points across two areas (`area/chart-engine`, `area/ingestion`, modules M7 and M8). The design-ahead rule in `00-planning-brief.md` requires their designs to be Done ≥2 sprints earlier; `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 additionally requires each Story to link a Done design artefact and to have its states enumerated before it can enter Ready.

This ticket produces the single artefact that makes those stories *Ready*: a handoff pack that collects every decision from E12-D01..E12-D11 into an implementable form — redlines, token names, the per-mode specification table, the geometry rules, the state matrix with precedence, the screen-reader script, the keyboard map, the motion spec, the error-mapping table, and the analytics event list — plus a walkthrough session with the frontend engineers who will build it.

The explicit goal is the planning brief's standard: "a developer must not need to ask for more details".

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A **handoff pack** (a document in the repo plus the linked Figma frames) indexed by consuming surface — `SCR-030` (series states), `SCR-031` General tab, `SCR-041`, `SCR-042`, `SCR-045`, `SCR-047`, `SCR-048` — and by component — `CMP-181`, `CMP-220`, `CMP-222`, `CMP-226` plus any entries accepted in E12-D09.
- **Per-mode implementation table** consolidating: `bar_type` value, user-facing label, description copy, `param` type/unit/default/min/max, validation message, whether recorded ticks are required, and the API/WS field each is bound to (`GET /api/v1/market/bars`, `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`).
- **Geometry and density rules** from E12-D06 in numeric, implementable form (formulas, clamps, token names), with the LOD ladder and the aggregated-mark definition.
- **State matrix with precedence** from E12-D02/E12-D08, plus the **error-mapping table** (`no_data_recorded` 422 → `SCR-047` variant; empty success → "no bars"; transport failure → `SCR-048`; context loss → `SCR-048` WebGL variant).
- **A11y pack** from E12-D11: screen-reader script, keyboard map, announcement budget, DOM-mirror text contract per bar mode.
- **Motion pack** from E12-D10 with durations, easings, reduced-motion equivalents and the drop-under-load rule.
- **Token and Storybook manifest**: every token used, every Storybook state the frontend must produce, so visual regression coverage matches the design intent.
- **Analytics manifest**: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed`, `chart.symbol_changed`, `chart.settings_changed`, `chart.empty_state_shown`, `chart.error_shown`, `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`, plus the rebuild start/complete/cancel events — each with its property set and its trigger point.
- A recorded **walkthrough session** with the E12 frontend engineers, QA/SDET and the Architect; questions raised are answered in the pack itself rather than in chat, and the pack is updated before sign-off.
- An **open-questions register** listing anything deliberately left to engineering judgement, so ambiguity is explicit rather than discovered mid-sprint.

## Out of scope
- Writing the engineering stories themselves (the E12 engineering chunk owns those).
- Backend bar-builder algorithm specification (module M8) — that is architecture/engineering, referenced here only where it constrains what the UI can show.
- Footprint, profile, indicator and drawing handoffs (E18, E19, E13, E14).
- Implementation, Storybook code and visual-regression baselines.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The pack makes the frontend stories Ready
  Given an E12 frontend story is being refined for Sprint 05
  When its Definition of Ready is checked
  Then the linked design artefact is this pack and it is Status Done
  And the story's states, tokens, a11y expectations and analytics events are all resolvable from the pack without asking a designer

Scenario: Every consuming surface is indexed
  Given the pack is reviewed
  When it is checked against the screens this epic touches
  Then SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-047 and SCR-048 each have an entry with frames, states, tokens and acceptance notes
  And each touched component entry links to its updated 15-component-catalogue.md record

Scenario: Walkthrough questions are absorbed, not answered in chat (edge)
  Given an engineer asks during the walkthrough what happens when a rebuild is cancelled while the symbol is also being switched
  When the question is triaged
  Then either the pack is updated with the answer or the case is added to the open-questions register with an owner
  And the answer is not left only in the meeting notes

Scenario: A design decision has no API or WS field to bind to (failure)
  Given the pack specifies a column or state with no source in 22-api-openapi.yaml or 23-ws-protocol.md
  When the binding audit is run
  Then the gap is filed as a blocking change ticket against the API or WS contract
  And the affected design element is marked as pending that change rather than handed over as buildable

Scenario: Late design change after handoff
  Given a design element changes after this pack is signed off
  When the change is made
  Then the pack is versioned and the affected engineering stories are notified on their tickets
  And the change is reflected in 14-screens-catalogue.md and 15-component-catalogue.md in the same sprint
```

## Technical notes / design
- Organise the pack **by what an engineer opens a ticket to do**, not by design artefact type: surface first, then component, then the cross-cutting packs (a11y, motion, analytics). A pack organised by Figma page is a pack nobody reads.
- Every visual value is a token name; the pack contains no raw hex, px-without-rule, or "match the mock" instructions.
- The binding audit is the highest-value part: every field the design shows is traced to `GET /api/v1/market/bars`, `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`, `GET /api/v1/recording/symbols`, `GET /api/v1/me/preferences` or the `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` topic. Anything untraceable is a contract change, filed before Sprint 05 starts, not discovered during it.
- Carry the `confirm: false` rule forward verbatim from `23-ws-protocol.md` §6 — the forming-bar visual, the table row label and the accessible name all descend from that one protocol fact, and the pack should present them together so their coupling is obvious.
- Include the **negative space**: what the design deliberately does not do (no approximation of missing tick data, no countdown on non-time bars, no sorting that silently breaks series order, no colour-only direction encoding). Engineers implement the absence of features badly when nobody wrote the absence down.
- Version the pack (`v1`, `v1.1`, …) and state the change log at the top; the design-ahead rule means the pack will outlive several sprints of memory.

## Test plan
- Dry-run the pack with one frontend engineer who was **not** in the design reviews: they attempt to spec a build for `SCR-042` using only the pack, and every question they must ask is a defect in the pack.
- Binding audit against `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md`, item by item, with the Architect.
- Cross-check the Storybook manifest against the states listed in `15-component-catalogue.md` for each touched component; mismatches resolved.
- Verify every DoR item in `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 that depends on design can be satisfied from the pack for at least three sample E12 stories.
- QA/SDET review: confirm the screen-reader script and state matrix are usable as test oracles.

## Security notes
- The pack states the RBAC expectations for every surface it covers: `marketdata:read` for the bar surfaces, owner-only for the "Record this symbol" action, and the rule that client-side hiding is presentational while the backend enforces.
- It states that user-entered `param` values are bounded client-side for usability but re-validated server-side (API `param` maxLength 24), so no engineer treats the UI bound as the security control.
- It states that error copy and correlation ids carry no internal detail, secrets or account identifiers.
- No credentials, keys, account ids or live account screenshots appear anywhere in the pack or its Figma frames.

## Accessibility notes
- The a11y pack from E12-D11 is included in full and is presented as a **build requirement**, not an appendix: screen-reader script, keyboard map, announcement budget and the DOM-mirror text contract per bar mode.
- Each surface entry lists its axe-core expectations and the manual screen-reader scenarios QA will run, so a11y work is scoped into the story estimate rather than discovered at review.
- The pack restates the non-negotiables: equal-status data table, no hover-only functionality, no colour-only encoding, visible focus, throttled announcements.

## Performance notes
- Budgets are restated per surface so they land in the story estimates: ≥58 fps at 2560×1440 with 100 k bars and ≤450 MB per chart panel (`SCR-030`); ≥55 fps / ≤512 MB GPU per pane (`US-CHART-001`); interval switch ≤200 ms cached, ≤600 ms uncached; chart-type switch ≤100 ms client-side; rebuild ≤10 s per 1 M prints, cancellable; data table ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame at 100 k rows.
- The pack names which benchmark in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 each budget is verified by, so the engineering stories reference an existing gate rather than inventing one.

## Observability
- The analytics manifest is part of the handoff, with each event's name, properties and trigger point, so instrumentation ships with the feature rather than after it.
- The pack notes which engine diagnostics values (`SCR-046`: fps, frame time p50/p95, visible bars, dropped frames) must agree with design-visible values such as the aggregation level, so the two cannot diverge.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) plus design gates.
- Pack published in the repo, versioned, and linked from every touched `14-screens-catalogue.md` entry and from the E12 epic ticket.
- Walkthrough session held with frontend, QA/SDET and the Architect; all questions absorbed into the pack or into the open-questions register with owners.
- Binding audit complete; any contract gaps filed as tickets against `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` before Sprint 05.
- Dry-run with an uninvolved engineer completed and resulting defects fixed.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done** before Sprint 05 planning, satisfying the design-ahead rule for all E12 frontend stories.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D09 (design-system contribution), E12-D10 (motion), E12-D11 (a11y pack) — which in turn depend on E12-D01..E12-D08.
- Consumed by every E12 frontend story in Sprint 05–08 and by E12-D13 (design QA), which tests the built result against this pack.

## Branch
`design/e12-handoff-pack`

title: Hi-fi design for SCR-034/035/036 and the indicator visual language
body:
## Context
Hi-fidelity, token-true design of the three indicator surfaces plus the on-chart visual language for indicator series. The roadmap requires "per-indicator styling from design tokens" - this ticket defines that vocabulary once so that every v1 indicator, and every R2 order-flow series that later registers through the same plugin API, inherits it rather than inventing colours.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for SCR-034, SCR-035, SCR-036 in light and dark themes at both densities defined in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- **Indicator palette spec**: the ordered `color.indicator.palette[]` token ramp (CMP-194 consumes it), with assignment rules (nth-indicator gets nth token; a second instance of the same indicator gets the next slot, not the same colour), contrast verified against both chart backgrounds, and a greyscale-safe dash-pattern ladder so two series are distinguishable with colour removed.
- **Series style spec** per output type: line, stepped line, area, band/channel fill (Bollinger/Keltner/Donchian with a shaded channel that keeps candle contrast, per US-IND-004), histogram (volume, MACD), markers (Supertrend flip, ZigZag pivots), dashed "provisional" treatment for an unconfirmed ZigZag leg with its "provisional" label.
- **Legend and chip spec**: CMP-199 legend row and CMP-224 chip anatomy - swatch, name, parameters, current value, visibility toggle, settings, remove; the ribbon case (one entry, expandable list); the errored case (error stated in text); the warming-up case.
- Sub-pane spec: guide levels at 30/70 for RSI, zero line for MACD, the divergence glyph + text label, pane header, and the collapse behaviour when the last indicator in a sub-pane is removed.
- Empty/loading/error/edge-density variants for all three screens.

## Out of scope
- Motion - E13-D04. Order-flow series styling (footprint cells, heatmap) - R2 epics.
- Any new atom not already in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` unless raised as an E05 contribution.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Colour is never the only carrier
  When the hi-fi chart frames are rendered in greyscale
  Then every simultaneously-visible series remains distinguishable by dash pattern or glyph, and every state (provisional, errored, warming up) is stated in text

Scenario: Contrast passes in both themes
  When every text and non-text UI element on SCR-034/035/036 is measured
  Then contrast meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text) in light and dark, evidenced by a measured table in the file

Scenario: Ten indicators still read
  Given a frame with ten active indicators across the price pane and two sub-panes
  Then the legend and chip row have a specified overflow behaviour and no series colour repeats within a pane

Scenario: Every token is real
  Then every colour, spacing and type value references an E05 token name, and any new token is filed as an E05 design-system contribution ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
The palette must be defined as an ordered list with a deterministic assignment function, because the engine assigns colours at add-time without a designer in the loop; the spec states the function, not just the swatches. Band fills specify an alpha that keeps candle body/wick contrast at the worst case (dense candles behind a Bollinger channel).

## Test plan
Contrast measured with a token-level automated check; greyscale export reviewed by the a11y specialist (E13-D05); a designer renders the 10-indicator stress frame and confirms legibility.

## Security notes
N/A - visual design introduces no new trust boundary. Note only that colour tokens must not be user-supplied free strings when preset styles are persisted in `indicator_presets.style`; the spec enumerates allowed token names.

## Accessibility notes
Focus states drawn for every interactive element; the dash-pattern ladder is the primary non-colour carrier; divergence and Supertrend flips get a glyph plus a text label per US-IND-003/005; reduced-motion variants noted for D04.

## Performance notes
Band fills and dashes must be expressible by the engine's instanced thick-line and fill passes (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.x draw-call table) - no design that would force a per-series extra draw call beyond the budgeted <=40 for the combined B5 scene.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every frame/state listed in Scope exists and is reviewed against the per-screen "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] CDO (or delegate) sign-off recorded on the ticket; artefact linked from the SCR entry.
- [ ] Component usage mapped to real CMP-* ids; any gap filed against E05 rather than drawn ad hoc.
- [ ] a11y reviewer has signed the contrast / focus / non-colour-encoding checks.
- [ ] Handoff notes (tokens, spacing, states, motion, empty/error copy) attached; engineering has acknowledged.
- [ ] Status Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule).

## Dependencies
E13-D02 wireframes; E05 tokens and theming.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.

`design/e13-indicators-hifi`.

- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.4 `indicator_presets`, §10.5 built-in indicator presets, migration `0011_workspace`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 Metric definitions (`MetricDescriptor`, `MetricRegistry`), §7.2 metric catalogue
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12 plugin API, `IndicatorPlugin` interface, §14 parity tests, open question O4
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.6 `MetricRegistry`; CONSTITUTION.md §3 module **M9** `orderflow`
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1 (16.6 ms frame), #2 (30 fps floor), §4.3 (indicator pane redraw <=2 ms)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`

title: Design-system contribution: indicator palette tokens and motion spec
body:
## Context
E13's visual decisions must land in the design system, not in the epic's own CSS, because R2's order-flow series (E18/E19/E23/E24) register through the same plugin API and must inherit the same palette and motion rules. This ticket promotes the E13-D03 output into E05 artefacts and specifies the motion of the three surfaces.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `color.indicator.palette[]` published as an E05 token set (light + dark), with the assignment function documented alongside it and a Storybook swatch page.
- Dash-pattern and marker ladders published as tokens/variants consumed by CMP-194 IndicatorOverlay and CMP-195 AnnotationMarker.
- CMP-199 ChartLegend and CMP-224 IndicatorChips variant additions (ribbon/expandable, errored, warming-up, provisional) added to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` and their Storybook stories specified.
- **Motion spec**: SCR-034/035/036 open/close transitions; the sub-pane create/collapse height animation when the first/last indicator in a pane is added/removed; the series re-compute transition on a parameter change (whether the series morphs or hard-cuts - specified, not left to the implementer); the chip add/remove transition. Each with duration, easing token and a `prefers-reduced-motion` variant that is a non-animated state change, never a removed affordance.
- Copy deck: every string on the three screens including the validation messages ("Period must be between 1 and 5000."), the insufficient-history message, the provisional label, and the blocked-removal message.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the tokens in code (that is the consuming engineering stories and E05's pipeline).
- Motion for drawings (E14) or layouts (E15).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tokens are in the system, not the epic
  Then color.indicator.palette[] and the dash/marker ladders exist as E05 tokens with light and dark values and a Storybook page, and no E13 frame references a raw hex value

Scenario: Every motion has a reduced-motion counterpart
  When prefers-reduced-motion is simulated for each specified transition
  Then the spec defines an instant state change that preserves the same information, with no loss of an affordance

Scenario: Sub-pane collapse is specified
  Given the last indicator in a sub-pane is removed (US-IND-003)
  Then the spec states the collapse duration, easing, and how the reclaimed vertical space is redistributed across remaining panes

Scenario: Copy is complete
  Then every string in the three screens is in the copy deck; any string discovered missing during implementation is a defect against this ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Durations must respect the frame budget: no transition may drive a per-frame recompute of indicator series; the series re-compute transition is specified as a buffer swap with a cross-fade of the existing draw, not a re-interpolation of computed values (which would misrepresent data).

## Test plan
Storybook visual review of the swatch/variant pages; a11y specialist reviews reduced-motion variants; the copy deck is proof-read by the product owner.

## Security notes
Enumerated token names only in `indicator_presets.style` - this spec provides the closed list the API validates against, which is what makes the persisted style safe.

## Accessibility notes
Reduced-motion variants mandatory; animation must never be the only signal that a value changed; the palette ramp is validated for both deuteranopia and protanopia simulation in addition to greyscale.

## Performance notes
Transitions are GPU-composited (opacity/transform) only; no layout-thrashing animations near the chart canvas.

N/A.

## Context
SCR-036 is explicitly designated in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` as "the a11y-complete alternative to manipulating canvas objects by mouse" and its sign-off checklist requires that this tree "is confirmed as the accessible equivalent for canvas objects (keyboard-reachable, named)". R1 exit criterion 9 requires every chart to be operable without a mouse. This review signs that claim off at design time, before engineering builds against it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Keyboard contract table for SCR-034 (listbox semantics, each entry announcing its pane target), SCR-035 (tab panel, form field labelling, colour pickers exposing token names) and SCR-036 (`role="tree"`, arrow navigation, expand/collapse, multi-select, bulk actions).
- Screen-reader script per surface: what NVDA and VoiceOver should announce on focus, on value change, and on the live-region events (indicator added, removed, errored, warming up).
- Confirmation that every mouse-only interaction on the chart canvas that E13 introduces (drag a sub-pane divider, click a legend to toggle visibility, click a chip's settings) has an equal-status keyboard path, with the path named.
- Contrast and non-colour-encoding audit of the E13-D03 frames, including the greyscale and colour-vision-deficiency simulations.
- Findings log with severity, each either fixed in the design or filed with an owner.

## Out of scope
- Automated axe-core runs against built code - that is E13-Q04.
- The engine's DOM-mirror a11y layer itself (E11); this review only verifies E13's surfaces plug into it correctly.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No canvas-only capability
  When every E13 interaction is enumerated
  Then each has a documented keyboard path of equal status, and SCR-036 covers every indicator object operation (add, configure, reorder, hide, lock, rename, remove)

Scenario: State is never colour-only
  When the frames are reviewed in greyscale and under deuteranopia/protanopia simulation
  Then provisional, errored, warming-up, hidden and locked states each remain identifiable by glyph or text

Scenario: Announcements are specified, not improvised
  Then each of add / remove / error / warm-up-complete has a written announcement string and a stated politeness level (polite vs assertive)

Scenario: A blocking finding stops sign-off

```

Reference `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` for the WCAG 2.2 AA criteria applied, the focus-visible requirement and the colour-independence rule. Announcements route through the global live region defined by E10's shell, not per-screen ad hoc regions.

## Test plan
Design-time walkthrough with the a11y specialist using the keyboard contract table as the script; simulated screen-reader read-through of the announcement strings.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility artefact; its output is the acceptance script reused verbatim by E13-Q04.
