title: Hi-fi design: drawing tool rail & tool palette (SCR-037, CMP-223)
body:
## Context
The tool rail is the permanent, always-visible chrome of the charting workspace: a vertical strip that sits beside the most information-dense surface in the product and must be legible without competing with it. It is also the primary discovery surface for a kit of twenty-plus tools, which means iconography, grouping and state feedback carry the whole learnability burden. This ticket takes the greyscale model from E14-D02 to a signed-off hi-fi specification for SCR-037's rail and CMP-223 DrawingToolbar, in Sprint 04 - two sprints before the Sprint 06 stories that consume it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for **CMP-223 DrawingToolbar** in both themes (dark default, light) and both densities (`16-design-system-brief.md` density scale): default, tool-active (`aria-pressed`), hover, focus-visible, disabled, magnet off/weak/strong, all-locked, all-hidden.
- Complete **icon set** for every tool in SCR-037's inventory, drawn on the design-system grid, with an explicit legibility check at the smallest supported rail size and at 200% zoom; each icon paired with its text label for the tooltip and its accessible name.
- **Grouping and overflow**: the rail's section order (cursor/crosshair · lines · shapes · fib family · analysis: VWAP, measure, position · annotation: text, arrow, brush, emoji · object controls: magnet, lock-all, hide-all, delete-all), separators, and the overflow menu (CMP-041 Menu) used when viewport height cannot show all sections.
- **Hotkey surfacing** via CMP-022 Kbd in every tooltip, using the hotkeys confirmed in E14-D02 (`Alt+T`, `Alt+H`, `Alt+F`, `Alt+R`, `Alt+M`, `Ctrl+M` magnet).
- **Token usage spec**: which tokens each element consumes (`color.surface.raised`, `space.1`, `color.drawing.default`, `color.drawing.selected`, focus ring, radius), with no raw values anywhere.
- Storybook story list agreed with engineering: Default, ToolActive, MagnetStrong, AllLocked, Overflowing, Light, Zoom200 - matching CMP-223's documented story set plus the two new cases.
- Redlines and a spec page in `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-toolbar.md`.

## Out of scope
- The properties popover (E14-D04) and per-tool visual language for fib/VWAP/measure (E14-D05) and the position tool (E14-D06).
- Object tree styling (E14-D07).
- Motion (E14-D09) beyond stating which transitions exist.
- Any new design-system token or component - if the rail needs one, it is raised into E14-D08 rather than invented here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state in the matrix is drawn in both themes
  Given the hi-fi file is reviewed
  When the state matrix (default, active, hover, focus, disabled, magnet x3, locked, hidden, overflow) is walked in dark and light
  Then every cell exists as a frame
  And no cell is represented by a note saying "same as dark"

Scenario: Active tool is distinguishable without colour
  Given the tool-active frame is rendered in greyscale and through a protanopia simulation
  Then the active tool remains identifiable by shape, fill or indicator, not by hue alone
  And the same is true of the three magnet modes

Scenario: Contrast passes over the chart background
  Given the rail is placed over the darkest and the lightest chart backgrounds in use
  When contrast is measured for icons, separators and the focus ring
  Then every measurement meets WCAG 2.2 AA (>=3:1 for UI components and graphics, >=4.5:1 for text)
  And the measured values are recorded in the spec page

Scenario: Rail does not fit the viewport
  Given a viewport height that cannot show all rail sections
  Then the overflow frame shows which sections collapse, in what order, and how the active tool stays visible even when its section is collapsed

Scenario: A tool has no distinguishable icon
  Given two icons in the same section are confusable at the smallest supported size
  Then the confusion is recorded as a defect and resolved before sign-off
  And the resolution is verified by a 5-participant icon-recognition check
```

## Technical notes / design
The rail is chrome, not content: it uses `color.surface.raised` and must recede visually so the canvas dominates. Icon strokes align to the same grid as the rest of the design system so the rail does not read as a foreign object next to CMP-221 ChartToolbar.

The active-tool indicator must survive the theme flip and the colour-blind simulation because a user who cannot tell which tool is armed will place a wrong object on a live chart; that is why a non-hue channel is mandatory rather than preferred.

The overflow behaviour deliberately keeps the *active* tool pinned visible - an armed tool that scrolls out of sight is the same failure as an invisible mode.

## Test plan
(1) State-matrix walk in dark, light, 125% and 200% zoom. (2) Automated contrast measurement of every icon/separator/focus-ring pair against both chart backgrounds, results pasted into the spec. (3) Colour-vision simulation pass (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, greyscale). (4) 5-participant unmoderated icon-recognition test: name the tool from the icon alone; anything below 4/5 recognition is redrawn. (5) Token audit - every value in the file resolves to a token. (6) Handoff dry run with an FE engineer who rebuilds one state from the spec alone.

## Security notes
The rail includes destructive controls (delete-all drawings) next to frequently used ones. The design must place delete-all outside the primary tap/click flow, give it a distinct treatment, and route it through a confirm step specified here (CMP-042 ConfirmDialog usage) - an accidental delete-all destroys server-persisted user content across every pane on that symbol. No credential, account or key data appears on this surface; the rail is RBAC-neutral (a Viewer may draw locally but, per E09's RBAC model, persistence is governed by the API, not by hiding the rail - the design must therefore not rely on rail visibility as an access control).

## Accessibility notes
Specified as a vertical `role="toolbar"` with roving tabindex; exactly one rail item is tabbable and arrows move within it. Each tool button has a stable accessible name that includes the tool name and its shortcut. The active tool carries `aria-pressed="true"` and its change is announced politely, since the canvas cannot convey mode to a screen reader. Focus-visible styling is specified explicitly and must be visible against both chart backgrounds. Targets are >=24x24 CSS px with >=44 px recommended for touch, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
Icons are specified as a sprite or inline SVG set that costs no layout work per frame; the rail must not re-render on chart frames. The spec states that hover/active feedback is CSS-only and must not trigger a canvas repaint, protecting the SCR-037 budget of >=58 fps while dragging a drawing with 200 objects present.

## Observability
The spec annotates `drawing.tool_selected` (tool id, entry method: rail click vs hotkey vs overflow menu) and `drawing.magnet_mode_changed`, both recommended by E14-D01, so that post-release we can tell which of twenty tools are actually used and which should be demoted in the rail.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Full state matrix drawn in dark and light, at 100/125/200% zoom.
- [ ] Icon set complete, recognition-tested, and legible at the smallest supported size.
- [ ] Contrast measurements recorded and passing AA over both chart backgrounds.
- [ ] Colour-blind simulation pass clean; active tool and magnet mode distinguishable without hue.
- [ ] Token audit clean - no raw values.
- [ ] Storybook story list agreed with engineering and written into the spec.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-toolbar.md` merged; `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-223 updated if anything diverged.
- [ ] Handoff dry run completed with an FE engineer.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the Sprint 06 consuming story.

## Dependencies

title: Hi-fi design: drawing properties popover, styling & template library
body:
## Context
Every drawing in the kit is configurable, and US-DRAW-009 requires those configurations to be saveable as named templates and applied to future drawings. The properties popover is therefore not a minor detail panel: it is the surface through which a user's chart becomes *their* chart, and it is shared by twenty-plus tools whose property sets differ. Designing it once as a shared frame with per-tool extension slots is what keeps the kit coherent and keeps the engineering cost linear instead of quadratic.

This ticket delivers the hi-fi spec for the popover (SCR-037), the per-tool property schemas, and the drawing-template library, in Sprint 04 - two sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 stories.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for the **shared properties popover** (CMP-017 Popover): header with tool name and object id affordance, colour (CMP-031 ColorSwatch), line width (CMP-008 NumericStepperInput), line style, extend-left/extend-right, opacity (CMP-010 Slider) for filled shapes, snap-to-OHLC toggle, "alert when price crosses" toggle, lock and visibility toggles, `Save as default`, `Save as template...`, `Delete`.
- **Per-tool property schema table**: for each tool, which of the shared fields apply plus its extension slot - fib level list (add/remove/reorder levels, per-level colour and label format, the 0.886 case from US-DRAW-004), channel width read-out, VWAP band toggles (1/2/3 sigma) deferred visually to E14-D05, text-note content field, measure units.
- **Filled-shape legibility controls**: fill opacity and the "flatten opacity" toggle required by US-DRAW-003, with frames showing three overlapping zones before and after flattening, and the stated rule that fills must preserve candle contrast.
- **Template library** frames: save-as-template dialog (name, scope: this tool / this tool family), the template picker on the popover, apply-to-existing versus apply-to-new semantics, rename/delete, and the empty state. Per US-DRAW-009 templates are per user; the frames state that a template never crosses symbols implicitly.
- **Multi-select properties**: what the popover shows when several objects of mixed types are selected (common fields only, mixed-value indicator, bulk apply).
- States: default, edited-unsaved, invalid value, saving, save failed (offline/server error), read-only because the object is locked.
- Redlines plus `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-properties.md`.

## Out of scope
- The tool rail itself (E14-D03) and the object tree (E14-D07).
- Fib/VWAP/measure on-canvas visual language (E14-D05) and the position tool's read-out (E14-D06).
- Alert configuration depth - the popover only offers the "alert when price crosses" toggle; the alert editor belongs to E40.
- Server-side template storage design; engineering decides the persistence shape against `21-database-schema.md` section 3.8.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Shared frame covers every tool
  Given the per-tool property schema table
  When every tool in SCR-037's inventory is checked
  Then each has a defined field set, and every field is either a shared field or a declared extension slot
  And no tool requires a bespoke popover layout

Scenario: A property change is applied live and persisted on release
  Given an object is selected and its colour is changed
  Then the frames define that the canvas updates immediately, and that persistence happens on commit, with an explicit saving and save-failed state
  And the save-failed frame states that the local value is retained and retried, not silently reverted

Scenario: Overlapping zones stay legible
  Given three overlapping rectangles at default opacity over candles
  When the flatten-opacity toggle is enabled
  Then the frames show the resulting composite
  And the spec states the maximum default fill opacity that keeps candle contrast above the documented threshold

Scenario: Invalid property value
  Given a line width outside the allowed range or an empty template name
  Then the field shows an inline error with text, the save action is disabled, and the error is associated with the field for assistive technology

Scenario: Locked object is edited
  Given the selected object is locked
  Then the popover renders read-only with an explicit explanation and an unlock affordance
  And no field silently discards input
```

## Technical notes / design
The popover is a standard form (SCR-037 a11y note) and must behave like one - it is not a canvas surface. That is deliberate: it makes the entire configuration path keyboard- and screen-reader-native for free, and it is why the extension slots are specified as form rows rather than bespoke canvas widgets.

Property changes are optimistic: the canvas reflects them instantly (the engine's drawing layer re-renders independently of price/footprint), and the server write is reconciled afterwards per `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.10. The design must therefore always have a visible answer to "did this save?" without blocking the interaction.

Templates carry style only, never geometry. The frames state this explicitly because "save as template" invites the opposite assumption.

## Test plan
(1) Schema completeness diff: every tool x every field. (2) State-matrix walk in dark/light, including saving, save-failed and locked-read-only. (3) Keyboard-only walkthrough: open popover from a selected object, traverse every field, commit, close, and confirm focus returns to the object's DOM mirror. (4) Screen-reader script for the popover including the mixed-value multi-select case. (5) Contrast check of the colour swatch set against both themes, including the selected-swatch indicator. (6) Content review of every error and empty-state string. (7) Handoff dry run with an FE engineer rebuilding the popover from the spec.

## Security notes
The text-note field (US-DRAW-006) is the only free-text input in the drawing kit and its content is persisted server-side in `drawings.geometry` and re-rendered on canvas and in the object tree. The spec states: plain text only, no HTML/markdown rendering, no auto-linkification, length-capped with the cap shown in the UI, and sanitised on both write and render - the design must not offer any affordance (rich-text toolbar, paste-as-HTML) that implies otherwise. Template names are equally user content and appear in menus, so the same plain-text rule and length cap apply. The "alert when price crosses" toggle creates a server-side object with notification side-effects; the spec notes it must respect the alert quota defined by E40 and shows the quota-exceeded state rather than failing silently.

## Accessibility notes
The popover uses the design system's dialog/popover semantics: focus moves into it on open, is trapped while open, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the originating object or tree row. Every control has a visible label, not a placeholder. Colour swatches are named by token name, not by hue, and the selected swatch carries a non-colour indicator. The mixed-value state in multi-select is conveyed in text, not only visually. Errors use `aria-describedby` association. All specified against `05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 5, 7 and 8.

## Performance notes
Property edits must repaint only the drawings layer; the spec forbids any property whose change would force a price/footprint re-render. Live-dragging the opacity slider is specified to coalesce to the engine's frame cadence rather than firing per input event, protecting the SCR-037 budget (>=58 fps with 200 drawings). The template picker is specified to render lazily since a user may accumulate many templates.

## Observability
Annotates `drawing.edited` (with the changed property key, never the note's text content), `drawing.template_saved`, `drawing.template_applied` and the save-failure event, so that template adoption and property-save reliability are measurable after release.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Shared popover frames complete for all states in dark and light.
- [ ] Per-tool property schema table complete and diffed against SCR-037's tool inventory.
- [ ] Flatten-opacity study done and a maximum default fill opacity stated with the contrast evidence.
- [ ] Template library frames complete including empty, rename, delete and apply semantics.
- [ ] Multi-select mixed-value behaviour specified.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs passed; focus-return behaviour defined.
- [ ] Content review of all strings completed.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-properties.md` merged; catalogue entries updated where they diverged.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the Sprint 06/07 consuming stories.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D02** - the interaction model and the tool inventory.
- Design-system components CMP-008, CMP-010, CMP-017, CMP-031, CMP-041 as catalogued.
- E40 alert quota semantics are referenced, not blocking; the toggle degrades to disabled-with-reason if E40 has not landed.

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-020 workspace page, tab strip and panel chrome
body:
## Context
SCR-020 is the product. Route `/w/:workspaceId`, it is where the Owner spends the trading day, and it is the host for every panel E11..E41 will ever build. This ticket takes the greyscale structure from E15-D02 to a signed-off hi-fi specification of the workspace page itself and the panel chrome that frames every hosted panel: CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher, CMP-080 DockPanel, CMP-081 DockGrid, CMP-082 PanelHeader, plus the tab strip and the top-bar layout/sync/save controls.

The design tension is stated in one number: at 1280x800, every pixel of chrome is a pixel of missing market data, yet a panel with no visible identity is a panel whose symbol and environment the user can get wrong. The specification must resolve that tension explicitly with a measured chrome budget per density mode, rather than leaving it to be discovered during implementation.

Sprint 04 is two sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 stories that consume it (US-LAY-001 grid layouts, US-LAY-002 saved workspaces, US-LAY-005 panel docking).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Hi-fi frames for SCR-020** in dark (default) and light themes, at 1920x1080 and 1280x800, in all three densities (compact / cosy / comfortable from `16-design-system-brief.md`), using real-density content: a footprint chart, a DOM ladder, a positions grid, a tape.
- **CMP-082 PanelHeader** specified completely: title, symbol/interval mini-controls, sync-group letter badge, environment indicator where applicable, action toolbar (`role="toolbar"` with arrow-key nav), overflow (CMP-216) and close. States: default, focused-panel, hovered, dragging, too-narrow (progressive disclosure order stated explicitly - what drops first), read-only (viewer role), error.
- **CMP-080 DockPanel** frame treatment: border, elevation, radius per tokens; the **active-panel affordance**, which must be perceivable without colour (SCR-020 checklist) and must not consume layout space when it changes state, so that focusing a panel never reflows the chart.
- **CMP-081 DockGrid** gutter, splitter hit areas (>=24 px per `05-accessibility-standard.md` while remaining visually thin), and the gutter's focus-visible treatment.
- **Tab strip**: workspace tabs with the unsaved `*` marker, active/inactive/hover/focus, the `+` new-workspace affordance, overflow when tabs exceed width, and a rename-in-place state.
- **CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher** as used in the tab strip context (its nav-rail placement is E15-D05): default, empty/first-run, many-workspaces.
- **Top-bar controls**: `[layout v] [sync v] [save] [reset]` with their disabled and dirty states, and the `Ctrl+S` / `Ctrl+Shift+S` hints via CMP-022 Kbd.
- **Role variants**: the default owner layout, manager layout and viewer layout drawn as three distinct frames (SCR-020 checklist), with viewer's read-only degradation visible in the chrome.
- **DEMO and LIVE chrome variants** drawn (SCR-020 checklist), including how the environment reads from a panel that is not adjacent to the top bar.
- **States**: loading skeleton (panel frames, no data), empty workspace with the panel picker entry point, unsaved changes, save conflict entry to SCR-029, restored-after-crash banner ("Restored your layout from 14:02"), and >16 panels performance warning with the measured frame cost shown.
- **Chrome budget table**: measured vertical and horizontal chrome per density at both reference widths, with the remaining canvas area stated.
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-workspace-page.md`; Storybook story list agreed with FE for CMP-073/080/081/082.

## Out of scope
- The docking interaction itself - drop zones, drag preview, keyboard move mode (E15-D04).
- Preset gallery (E15-D05), sync configuration UI (E15-D06), panel picker and context menu (E15-D07), settings/conflict dialogs (E15-D08), import (E15-D09), floating window (E15-D10), multi-chart grid (E15-D11), reduced-capability (E15-D12).
- Motion (E15-D14) beyond naming which transitions exist.
- Any new token or component - raised into E15-D13 instead of invented here.
- The internals of hosted panels.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The full state and density matrix is drawn
  Given the hi-fi file is reviewed
  When the matrix of (loading, empty, populated, unsaved, conflict, crash-restored, over-16-panels) x (compact, cosy, comfortable) x (dark, light) is walked
  Then every required cell exists as a frame
  And no cell is represented by a note reading "same as above"

Scenario: The focused panel is identifiable without colour
  Given the populated frame is rendered in greyscale and under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation
  Then the focused panel remains identifiable by a non-hue channel
  And the sync-group badge remains readable as a letter

Scenario: Chrome fits the minimum supported window
  Given the 1280x800 frame in compact density with four panels
  Then no control overlaps, no label is clipped, and the measured chrome total matches the budget table
  And every panel still shows its symbol, interval and environment

Scenario: Environment is unambiguous from any order-capable panel
  Given the LIVE variant frame
  When any panel capable of placing an order is examined in isolation, cropped away from the top bar
  Then the environment is still readable within that crop

Scenario: A panel is narrower than its header can show
  Given a panel resized below the width its header needs
  Then the progressive-disclosure frame shows which elements drop and in what order
  And the panel's accessible name is unchanged, so the screen-reader experience does not degrade with width

Scenario: Focus state causes no reflow
  Given the focused and unfocused frames of the same panel
  When their content rectangles are compared
  Then the content rectangle is identical, proving the focus affordance is drawn inside the existing frame
```

## Technical notes / design
The active-panel affordance is deliberately constrained to draw *inside* the existing panel frame. A focus ring that adds outward thickness changes the panel's content box, which forces a chart resize, which on a WebGL canvas means a re-allocation and a dropped frame - every time the user clicks between panels. Specify an inset treatment and say so in the spec, so the constraint survives implementation.

Panel header progressive disclosure needs an explicit order because it will be exercised constantly in 2x2 and 3x3 layouts: the recommended order is close > overflow > action toolbar > interval > symbol > title, with symbol and environment the last things standing, since those are the two facts a user must never lose.

Crash restore must be visually distinct from a normal load in the tab strip, not only in a transient banner: a user who misses the banner and presses `Ctrl+S` would overwrite a good saved workspace with a recovered one. Draw a persistent marker that clears on explicit save or discard.

The >16-panel warning carries the *measured* frame cost per US-LAY-001, not a generic caution. The spec must define where that number appears and what units it uses (ms/frame and the derived fps), because the story requires confirmation based on a measurement.

## Test plan
(1) Full matrix walk in dark, light, three densities, at 100/125/200% zoom. (2) Automated contrast measurement on every chrome element against the darkest and lightest hosted-panel backgrounds; values pasted into the spec. (3) Colour-vision simulation for focus affordance and sync badge. (4) Token audit - every value resolves to a token, no raw hex or px. (5) Crop test: each order-capable panel cropped alone must disclose symbol + environment. (6) Reflow test comparing focused/unfocused content rectangles. (7) Handoff dry run - an FE engineer rebuilds the panel header from the spec alone and the differences are recorded. (8) Checklist sweep against `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020's design sign-off list.

## Security notes
This surface is where environment confusion turns into real money lost. The specification must guarantee that DEMO/LIVE is disclosed on the workspace chrome *and* independently on every panel that can place an order, so that a maximised or cropped panel cannot hide it; it must also specify that the LIVE treatment is not a colour-only cue. Viewer-role chrome must show read-only affordances honestly - but the spec must state in writing that hiding a control is presentation, never authorisation: RBAC is enforced by the API (E09), and the design must not imply otherwise. Workspace names are user-supplied and rendered in tabs, so the spec states that names are truncated for display and treated as text, never as markup, and that the 1-40 character validation from SCR-020 is enforced at input.

## Accessibility notes
Each panel is a `role="region"` whose accessible name includes type, symbol and interval ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1 minute"); `F6` cycles regions and `Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right` cycles panels, with the focus affordance visible in both themes and at 200% zoom. CMP-082's action area is a `role="toolbar"` with roving tabindex. Splitter hit areas are >=24 px. The tab strip is a proper tablist with arrow-key navigation, and the unsaved marker is conveyed in the accessible name ("Scalping, unsaved changes"), not by the `*` glyph alone. Layout changes announce politely via CMP-081's live region. All text meets 4.5:1 and all UI/graphical elements 3:1, measured against both extremes of hosted-panel background.

## Performance notes
Three constraints are written into the spec as normative statements, not suggestions: the focus affordance must not change the content box (no chart resize on focus); chrome hover/active feedback is CSS-only and must never trigger a canvas repaint; and skeletons for the loading state must not fetch data, since panels mount lazily on first visibility and hidden tabs unsubscribe after 30 s. Target budgets inherited: >=55 fps with four active order-flow panes (US-LAY-001), panel mount <=150 ms (CMP-080), layout transition <=200 ms (CMP-081), four-pane restore to interactive <=3 s (US-LAY-002).

## Observability
The spec annotates `workspace.saved`, `workspace.restored`, `panel.added`, `panel.removed`, `layout.preset_applied`, `layout.reset` and the crash-restore event with the properties needed to answer real questions later: how often crash restore fires, how many panels people actually run, and how often the >16-panel warning is overridden. It also names the one metric FE must emit for the warning itself - measured frame cost at the moment of the warning - since the story's confirmation text depends on it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Full state x density x theme matrix drawn at both reference widths; no "same as above" cells.
- [ ] Owner, manager and viewer default layouts drawn; DEMO and LIVE variants drawn.
- [ ] Chrome budget table measured and recorded for all three densities at 1280x800 and 1920x1080.
- [ ] Contrast measurements recorded and passing WCAG 2.2 AA over both background extremes.
- [ ] Colour-blind simulation clean for focus affordance and sync badge.
- [ ] Focus-affordance reflow test passed (identical content rectangles).
- [ ] Crop test passed for every order-capable panel.
- [ ] Token audit clean; any needed new token raised into E15-D13.
- [ ] Storybook story lists agreed with FE for CMP-073, CMP-080, CMP-081, CMP-082.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-workspace-page.md` merged; `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020 and `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated where the design diverged.
- [ ] Every SCR-020 design sign-off checklist item satisfied.
- [ ] Handoff dry run completed with an FE engineer.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 04, two sprints before the Sprint 06 consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D02** - structure, chrome budget and state inventory.
- E05 design system v0 (tokens, density scale, elevation, focus ring).
- E10 app shell (SCR-010) - the workspace mounts inside the shell; chrome totals must be agreed jointly.

## Branch
`design/e15-workspace-page-hifi`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020 (incl. its design sign-off checklist)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-073, CMP-080, CMP-081, CMP-082, CMP-216, CMP-022
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-002, US-LAY-005
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` (tokens, density, elevation, focus)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces/{workspaceId}`


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant sections)
4. docs/plan/20-architecture.md (apps/web module map)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- apps/web/src/routes/** (per Scope screen), apps/web/src/lib/state/**, packages/ui/** (components), apps/web/e2e/**
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- apps/web route contracts, Zustand/Jotai store shapes consumed by other routes; named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-022, CMP-073, CMP-080, CMP-081, CMP-082, CMP-216, SCR-010, SCR-020, SCR-029
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build · pnpm e2e · pnpm test:a11y
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e15-workspace-page-hifi`
- PR title: `E15-D03: Hi-fi design: SCR-020 workspace page, tab strip and panel chrome`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E15-D03)
- Required reviewers: `apps/web` (@CandleViewer/frontend), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/design, area/charting-ui, priority/p0, design, handoff, a11y

**Done means**
- [ ] Full state x density x theme matrix drawn at both reference widths; no "same as above" cells.
- [ ] Owner, manager and viewer default layouts drawn; DEMO and LIVE variants drawn.
- [ ] Chrome budget table measured and recorded for all three densities at 1280x800 and 1920x1080.
- [ ] Contrast measurements recorded and passing WCAG 2.2 AA over both background extremes.
- [ ] Colour-blind simulation clean for focus affordance and sync badge.
- [ ] Focus-affordance reflow test passed (identical content rectangles).

**Do NOT**
- Do not ship a hover-only or drag-only interaction; every affordance needs a keyboard path (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E15-D03 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.
- Move the issue's Status to `Blocked` in the project board; do not leave it silently `In Progress`.
- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-021 dock system - drop zones, drag preview, keyboard move mode
body:
## Context
Docking is the interaction that makes SCR-020 feel like a terminal rather than a web page, and it is also the single most accessibility-hostile pattern in the product: drag-and-drop with spatial drop targets is, by default, unusable without a pointer. `15-component-catalogue.md` therefore makes the keyboard equivalent **mandatory** for CMP-214 DockDropZone, and this ticket specifies both paths to the same fidelity - the pointer storyboard and the keyboard move mode are equal deliverables, not a primary and a fallback.

SCR-021 covers six drop targets (north, south, east, west, centre-tabify, float), splitter resizing by mouse or `Alt+Shift+arrows`, invalid-drop feedback, the floating/maximised/minimised-to-tab states, and the "panel too small - showing compact view" case. It consumes CMP-083 SplitPane, CMP-214 DockDropZone, CMP-215 FloatingWindowFrame (frame reference only; full spec in E15-D10) and CMP-216 PanelMenu (menu spec in E15-D07).

Sprint 04, two sprints before the Sprint 06 US-LAY-005 story.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Pointer storyboard**, frame by frame: drag start (grab affordance, cursor, source panel treatment), hover over each of the six targets with its distinct zone highlight and a translucent preview of the *resulting rectangle* (not merely a highlighted edge), commit, and Esc-cancel returning to origin.
- **Zone geometry spec**: the pixel/percentage regions that map to each of the six targets within a panel, including how zones behave in a very small panel where naive edge bands would leave no centre region - the degenerate case must be drawn, not assumed away.
- **Invalid-drop treatment**: cursor, zone styling and the plain-language reason ("Can't dock here - the panel would be below its minimum size"), including where that text appears so it is visible while the pointer is held.
- **Keyboard move mode storyboard**, at equal fidelity: entered from CMP-216 PanelMenu "Move panel" or `Shift+F10`; a directional chooser showing the six destinations with their keys; live preview highlighting the resulting rectangle; Enter to commit, Esc to cancel; and the polite announcement text for each step ("Move mode. Choose a destination. Left, right, top, bottom, tab into, or float." / "Chart moved to bottom right.").
- **Keyboard resize**: splitter focus treatment, `Alt+Shift+arrow` and arrow-key behaviour on a focused `role="separator"`, the step size, the coarse/fine modifier, and the announced `aria-valuenow` text.
- **Splitter states**: rest, hover, active-drag, focused, at-minimum (cannot move further, with feedback), and the >=24 px hit area drawn over a visually thin divider.
- **Panel-too-small state**: the compact view threshold, what a panel shows below it, and how the user learns why.
- **Maximise / minimise-to-tab / float states** at the dock level: what the layout looks like while one panel is maximised (`F11`), how the rest is preserved, and how restore returns the exact previous tree.
- **Undo**: how a mis-drop is reverted, with the affordance drawn (toast with Undo, and/or `Ctrl+Z` scope stated explicitly - layout undo must not be confused with drawing undo from E14).
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-dock-system.md`; Storybook lists for CMP-083 and CMP-214.

## Out of scope
- The floating OS window's own chrome and multi-monitor behaviour (E15-D10).
- The panel context menu's full item set (E15-D07) - referenced here only as the entry point to move mode.
- Motion curves and durations (E15-D14); this ticket states which transitions exist and their perceptual requirement, not their easing.
- Workspace persistence of the resulting layout (E15-D08 settings, E15-D03 chrome).
- Multi-chart grid cell arrangement (E15-D11) - a different, panel-internal grid.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every pointer operation has an equal keyboard path
  Given the pointer storyboard enumerates move, split-left, split-right, split-top, split-bottom, tabify, float, resize, maximise and close
  When each is looked up in the keyboard storyboard
  Then each has a drawn keyboard path with a named key, a live preview and an announcement
  And no operation is documented as "pointer only"

Scenario: The drop preview shows the outcome, not the target
  Given a drag hovering the east zone of a panel
  Then the frame shows a translucent rectangle in the shape and position the panel will occupy after the drop
  And the existing panels are shown at the sizes they will have after the drop

Scenario: Drop zones remain usable in a small panel
  Given a panel at its minimum size where edge bands would consume the whole area
  Then the degenerate-case frame shows the reduced zone set that is offered and which targets are withdrawn
  And the withdrawn targets are still reachable through keyboard move mode

Scenario: A drop that would violate minimum size is refused
  Given a drag over a target that would make a neighbour smaller than its minimum
  Then the invalid-drop frame shows the refusal styling and a reason naming the constraint
  And releasing the pointer performs no layout mutation

Scenario: Esc during a drag restores the original layout exactly
  Given a drag in progress with a preview shown
  When Esc is pressed
  Then the frame shows the original layout unchanged and the preview removed
  And the same is specified for Esc during keyboard move mode

Scenario: A drag preview never obscures its own drop target
  Given the drag preview frames
  Then the ghost is specified to be offset or translucent such that the active zone highlight remains visible
  And this is demonstrated in the frame where the panel is larger than the target region
```

## Technical notes / design
Drop-zone geometry is specified in the design rather than left to FE because it is perceptual: bands that are too thin make docking feel like a dexterity test, bands that are too thick make tabify unreachable. Specify bands as a percentage of the panel's smaller dimension with an absolute minimum and maximum in px, and draw the result at three panel sizes.

Keyboard move mode is designed as a *mode with visible instructions*, not as a set of hidden shortcuts. A mode the user cannot see is a mode they cannot exit; the storyboard must show the persistent instruction affordance and the Esc route, matching SCR-021's checklist item "keyboard move mode drawn with its own visible instructions".

Layout undo scope must be stated explicitly. E14 gives `Ctrl+Z` to drawing operations on the chart canvas; if layout also claims `Ctrl+Z`, the binding is ambiguous depending on focus. The recommendation to specify and defend is: layout mutations are undone from a toast affordance and from the panel menu, and `Ctrl+Z` remains owned by the focused panel's own undo stack. Whatever is chosen must be recorded here and reflected in the E15-D02 hotkey map and in `US-SET-002`'s conflict detection.

The drop commits exactly one layout mutation (SCR-021 performance note) - the spec should make that visible by showing a single transition to the final state, never an intermediate reflow.

## Test plan
(1) Pointer/keyboard parity audit: enumerate operations, confirm each has both paths drawn. (2) Zone geometry validated at three panel sizes including minimum. (3) Contrast measurement of zone highlights and the focused-splitter treatment over the darkest and lightest panel content. (4) Colour-vision simulation - the active zone must be distinguishable without hue. (5) Moderated keyboard walkthrough with a keyboard-dominant participant using a clickable prototype of move mode; success criterion is completing a move to a named destination without instruction. (6) Announcement script review with the a11y specialist (feeds E15-D15). (7) Checklist sweep against SCR-021's sign-off list. (8) Handoff dry run rebuilding the splitter states from the spec alone.

## Security notes
No credentials, keys or account data appear on this surface, and layout operations are analytics-only, not audit events (per SCR-021). Two risks remain and are addressed in the spec. First, **destructive ambiguity**: a drag that lands wrongly can visually destroy a carefully built layout, and if the workspace autosaves, the damage is persisted; the spec therefore requires the undo affordance to remain available until the next explicit save, and requires that a drop never silently overwrites the saved workspace without either an explicit save or a clearly marked dirty state. Second, **maximise hiding environment**: `F11` full-screen on a trading panel must retain the DEMO/LIVE disclosure specified in E15-D03, so that a maximised panel cannot conceal which environment an order would reach.

## Accessibility notes
This is the ticket where WCAG 2.2's pointer-gesture and drag requirements are actually met. Every drag operation has a single-pointer alternative *and* a keyboard alternative (2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.1.1 Keyboard). Splitters are `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` and `aria-valuenow` announced as a percentage, arrow-key operable, with a >=24 px target (2.5.8). Move mode publishes its instructions visibly and announces each step through a polite live region; the commit announcement names the panel and its destination ("Chart moved to bottom right"). Focus never gets lost: after a move, focus stays on the moved panel's header. Zone highlights meet 3:1 against every possible underlying panel content, which is why the contrast measurement is taken against content extremes rather than against a neutral background.

## Performance notes
The spec states three normative constraints. The drag preview is CSS-transform-only - no live panel, no canvas in the ghost - so dragging cannot cost chart frames. The drop commits exactly one layout mutation, so the tree is rebuilt once. Splitter dragging must throttle layout writes to one per animation frame and must not remount the WebGL context, since a resize that recreates a GL context would stall visibly. The governing budgets are US-LAY-001's >=55 fps with four order-flow panes and CMP-081's <=200 ms layout transition.

## Observability
Annotated events: `layout.panel_moved{from,to,method:"pointer"|"keyboard"}`, `layout.split_created{orientation}`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.maximised`, `layout.drop_rejected{reason}` and `layout.move_cancelled{method}`. The `method` property is deliberate - it is the only way to find out post-release whether the mandatory keyboard path is actually used, which is the question that decides whether to invest further in it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Pointer storyboard complete for all six targets plus resize, maximise and float.
- [ ] Keyboard move-mode storyboard complete at equal fidelity, with visible instructions and announcements scripted.
- [ ] Pointer/keyboard parity audit passed; no operation is pointer-only.
- [ ] Zone geometry specified and drawn at three panel sizes including the degenerate minimum.
- [ ] Invalid-drop, at-minimum-splitter and panel-too-small states drawn with plain-language reasons.
- [ ] Undo model decided, drawn and reconciled with E14's `Ctrl+Z` ownership; hotkey map updated.
- [ ] Contrast and colour-vision checks passed against content extremes; measurements recorded.
- [ ] Keyboard walkthrough with a keyboard-dominant participant passed without instruction.
- [ ] SCR-021 design sign-off checklist fully satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-dock-system.md` merged; CMP-083 and CMP-214 Storybook lists agreed with FE.
- [ ] Handoff dry run completed.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 04, two sprints before Sprint 06.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D02** - the layout tree model and the keyboard move storyboard's greyscale origin.
- **E15-D03** - panel chrome, focus affordance and splitter visual language.
- E05 design system v0 (accent tokens, motion token names, focus ring).

## Branch
`design/e15-dock-system-hifi`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-021 (incl. design sign-off checklist)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-083, CMP-214, CMP-215, CMP-216
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-005, US-LAY-008
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (2.1.1, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, live regions)
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant sections)
4. docs/plan/20-architecture.md (apps/web module map)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- apps/web/src/routes/** (per Scope screen), apps/web/src/lib/state/**, packages/ui/** (components), apps/web/e2e/**

title: Hi-fi design: SCR-022 layout preset gallery & SCR-011 workspace switcher
body:
## Context
Most users will never build a layout by dragging panels; they will pick one from a gallery and live in it. That makes SCR-022 the real entry point to E15's value, and CMP-217 LayoutPresetMenu the control that actually gets used, with `Ctrl+1..9` behind it for the power path (US-LAY-006). SCR-011, the expanded navigation rail with CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher, is its sibling: the gallery picks an *arrangement*, the switcher picks a *saved workspace*, and users confuse the two unless the design distinguishes them clearly.

The gallery ships ten presets: five geometric (1x1, 2x1, 2x2, 1+3, 3+1) and five semantic (Scalping, Order-flow, Swing 3TF, Analyst, Fan-out review). E15-D01's card sort ranked them; this ticket applies that ranking to ordering and, if the research recommended cuts, records them. SCR-022's own checklist additionally names built-in presets (Scalper DOM, Footprint focus, Multi-chart 2x2, Analysis/journal, Replay) - reconciling that list with the catalogue's is part of this ticket's work, and the reconciled list must be written back into `14-screens-catalogue.md`.

Sprint 04, two sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 US-LAY-001/US-LAY-006 stories.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-022 hi-fi** in dark and light, both reference widths: the geometric preset row, the named-preset grid, the "Keep current symbols" option, and Apply/Cancel.
- **Preset thumbnails** as static SVG (performance note in SCR-022 mandates this), drawn so that the arrangement is readable at thumbnail size, plus the `alt`/accessible-name text for each one enumerating its panels ("Scalping: chart, DOM ladder, order ticket, tape").
- **Reconciled preset inventory**: one authoritative list merged from the catalogue's two lists, each with id, label, pane count, panel composition and a one-line description; delivered as a table in the spec and written back to SCR-022.
- **User presets**: saved-custom entries with rename and delete, the save-current affordance (`Ctrl+Shift+S` path), and the empty user-preset state with a clear first-run instruction.
- **Destructive confirmation**: the "Applying a preset replaces the current layout. Settings of surviving panels are kept." warning, drawn in place, plus the route into SCR-029 when the current layout is dirty.
- **CMP-217 LayoutPresetMenu** as the compact top-bar menu variant: default, active preset indicated, with custom saved presets, overflow.
- **SCR-011 hi-fi**: the expanded navigation rail with CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher - workspace list with active indicator, create, rename-in-place, delete (confirm-gated per CMP-073), search/filter when the list is long, and the empty/first-run state.
- **Hotkey surfacing**: `Ctrl+1..9` shown against the first nine presets via CMP-022 Kbd, with the mapping rule stated (which nine, and what happens when the user has more than nine).
- Redlines and spec page `docs/design/specs/e15-presets-and-switcher.md`; Storybook lists for CMP-217 and CMP-073.

## Out of scope
- The dock interaction that a preset ultimately produces (E15-D04).
- Workspace settings and the unsaved/conflict dialog internals (E15-D08).
- Panel picker (E15-D07).
- The layout-preset API shape - referenced (`GET /api/v1/layout-presets`, `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`) but owned by the engineering chunk.
- Motion (E15-D14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every preset is identifiable without seeing the thumbnail
  Given the accessible-name text for each preset
  When a screen-reader script is read aloud with thumbnails hidden
  Then each preset's arrangement and panel composition are understandable from text alone
  And no name relies on the word "this" or on visual position

Scenario: Applying a preset over unsaved work is confirmed
  Given the current workspace has unsaved layout changes
  When Apply is chosen in the gallery
  Then the frame routes through SCR-029 with Save, Discard and Cancel as explicit verbs
  And no destructive action holds initial focus

Scenario: Thumbnails remain readable at their smallest rendered size
  Given the thumbnails rendered at the gallery's smallest breakpoint and at 200% browser zoom
  Then each arrangement is still distinguishable from every other in the set
  And any two thumbnails judged confusable are redrawn before sign-off

Scenario: The user has no custom presets yet
  Given a first-run user opens the gallery
  Then the empty user-preset region explains how a custom preset is created rather than showing a bare empty box

Scenario: More presets exist than there are number hotkeys
  Given a user has saved twelve custom presets
  Then the spec states which nine carry Ctrl+1..9, how that assignment is changed, and how the remaining presets are reached

Scenario: Workspace switching with unsaved changes
  Given the active workspace is dirty
  When another workspace is selected in SCR-011
  Then the switcher routes through the same SCR-029 dialog
  And the dirty marker is visible in the switcher list, not only on the tab strip
```

## Technical notes / design
The gallery must make the *difference between a preset and a workspace* obvious, because the failure mode is a user believing they have switched setups when they have only rearranged panes and lost their symbol bindings. The design lever is language plus placement: presets live behind the layout control in the top bar and speak in arrangements; workspaces live in the tab strip and the nav rail and speak in names. The spec states this rule so later screens do not blur it.

"Keep current symbols" is the option that decides whether applying a preset is cheap or catastrophic. Draw its default state explicitly (recommended: on) and show, in the confirmation copy, what happens to panels that have no counterpart in the new arrangement.

Thumbnails are static SVG by mandate. That means the visual language must carry panel *type* without live content - use labelled regions with the panel-type glyph, not miniature screenshots, and verify the labels remain legible at the smallest size.

## Test plan
(1) Screen-reader script read-through with thumbnails suppressed. (2) Thumbnail distinguishability check at the smallest size and at 200% zoom, pairwise. (3) Contrast measurement on cards, active indicators, hotkey chips. (4) Keyboard walkthrough: open gallery, traverse as a listbox, apply, and cancel - all without a pointer. (5) Dirty-state routing test through SCR-029 from both the gallery and the switcher. (6) Token audit. (7) Checklist sweep against SCR-022's and SCR-011's sign-off lists. (8) Handoff dry run rebuilding a preset card.

## Security notes
Presets and workspaces are user content with user-supplied names rendered in lists, tabs and menus; the spec requires display truncation and text-only rendering with the 1-40 character validation from SCR-020 enforced at input, so a crafted name cannot break layout or inject markup. Deletion of a workspace is confirm-gated per CMP-073 and, per SCR-025, requires typing the name - this ticket draws the entry point but must not offer a one-click delete anywhere in the switcher. Presets carry no account bindings or credentials; where a named preset implies a trading panel (Scalping, Fan-out review), the spec states that applying it never changes the selected account or environment - only the arrangement - and the confirmation copy says so.

## Accessibility notes
The gallery is a listbox of cards: each option has an accessible name describing the arrangement in words (per CMP-217), arrow keys move between options, Enter applies, Esc cancels, and applying announces the result ("Layout changed to 2 by 2, four panes"). Thumbnails carry `alt` text enumerating panels and are never the sole carrier of meaning. The active preset is indicated by more than colour. In SCR-011 the workspace list is a proper list with the active item programmatically marked, rename-in-place moves focus into an input with a label, and the dirty state is in the accessible name ("Scalping, unsaved changes"). Hotkey hints use CMP-022 Kbd with text, not images.

## Performance notes
Thumbnails are static SVG; the gallery pre-warms nothing and makes no live panels. Applying a preset rebuilds the dock tree in <=300 ms (SCR-022) and reuses existing panel instances where the type matches, avoiding GL context churn - the spec states this as a design constraint so the visual transition does not imply a teardown. The switcher's list is virtualised above a stated threshold so a user with many workspaces does not pay a render cost on every open.

## Observability
Annotated events: `layout.preset_previewed{presetId}`, `layout.preset_applied{presetId, keepSymbols, entry:"gallery"|"hotkey"|"menu"}`, `layout.preset_saved_as`, `layout.preset_deleted`, `workspace.switched{from,to,dirty}`. The `entry` property validates E15-D01's finding on whether the gallery or the hotkeys are the real path, and `keepSymbols` tells us whether the default was right.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] SCR-022 and SCR-011 drawn in both themes at both reference widths, all states.
- [ ] Reconciled preset inventory table merged and written back into `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-022.
- [ ] Thumbnails drawn as static SVG with accessible names; distinguishability check passed.
- [ ] Empty user-preset state, rename and delete paths drawn; delete is confirm-gated.
- [ ] Dirty-layout routing through SCR-029 drawn from both gallery and switcher.
- [ ] `Ctrl+1..9` mapping rule stated, including the >9 presets case.
- [ ] Contrast and keyboard walkthroughs passed; token audit clean.
- [ ] SCR-022 and SCR-011 design sign-off checklist items satisfied.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-presets-and-switcher.md` merged; CMP-217 and CMP-073 Storybook lists agreed with FE.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** in Sprint 04, two sprints before Sprint 06.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D01** - preset ranking from the card sort.
- **E15-D02** - structure and flows.
- **E15-D03** - tab strip and chrome language the switcher must match.

## Branch
`design/e15-presets-switcher-hifi`

title: UX research: recorder mental model, auto-record surprise and disk anxiety
body:
## Context
Owner decision #4 makes recording opt-in and empty by default, with silent auto-record on chart/position open. ADR-0015 explicitly names two UX risks as "negative consequences": (a) users will want history for a symbol they only just started recording and it will not exist, and (b) auto-record on chart open surprises a user who browses many symbols. Both are UX problems, not engineering problems, and they must be resolved before SCR-140/141/142 wireframes are drawn (design-ahead rule, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated walkthrough with the Owner and both account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) on: what they expect "recording" to mean, what they expect to happen when they open a chart for a new symbol, and what disk figure they would act on.
- Concept test of three auto-record disclosure options: (1) silent + badge, (2) 60 s dwell then a toast with an undo, (3) explicit prompt on first open per symbol.
- Concept test of two disk-budget framings: "GB used / cap" vs "days of runway at current rate" (both are available from `GET /api/v1/recording/storage`: `daily_growth_bytes`, `projected_full_at`).
- Comprehension test of the recorder-dependent empty state copy ("History starts <ts> — recording began then") used by SCR-047/SCR-151 and every R2 view.
- Written findings doc + a ranked recommendation per question, attached to this ticket and linked from SCR-140 in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.

## Out of scope
- Producing wireframes or hi-fi screens (E16-D02..D05).
- Testing replay UX (E26).
- Quantitative analytics instrumentation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Auto-record disclosure decided
  Given three auto-record disclosure options were tested with at least three participants
  When findings are written up
  Then one option is recommended with the reasoning and the dissenting evidence recorded
  And the recommendation names the dwell/grace values it assumes (default 60 s dwell, 15 min linger)

Scenario: Disk framing decided
  When participants are shown both disk framings and asked which figure they would act on
  Then the findings state which framing is primary on SCR-140 and which is secondary

Scenario: Empty-state copy comprehension fails safely
  Given a participant misreads the "history starts" copy as an error
  Then the finding is logged as a blocking copy issue and a revised string is proposed and re-tested
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the real API shapes so the stimuli are truthful: `RecordedSymbol` (`reason`, `pinned`, `started_at`, `disk_bytes`, `retention_days`) and `StorageUsage` (`disk_used_bytes`, `daily_growth_bytes`, `projected_full_at`). Stimuli may be static; no build required. Sessions recorded with consent; recordings stored on the tailnet only.

## Test plan
N/A (research ticket). Validation is peer review of the findings doc by the Chief Design Officer and the Architect.

## Security notes
Session recordings may show symbol names and account labels — store on the tailnet, never in a public tracker. No API keys, balances or PII in stimuli. Data classification: internal.

## Accessibility notes
At least one participant session run with a screen reader or keyboard-only, so the empty-state and disk-meter copy is validated non-visually.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

body:
## Context
SCR-140 `/admin/recorder` is the control surface for the whole epic and is also step 4 of onboarding (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-140 and the onboarding wizard). It must make three things impossible to misread: nothing is recorded by default, what auto-record added and why, and what recording costs in disk. It is consumed by E16-S01/S02/S05/S07 in Sprint 06, so it must be signed off two sprints earlier.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Design-system contribution **CMP-177 RecorderStatusRow** (props `symbol`, `recording`, `diskUsageBytes`, `retentionDays`, `pinned`, `onToggleRecording`, `onTogglePin`, `onChangeRetention`) with Storybook states Recording, Stopped, Pinned, NearDiskBudget; composed from CMP-023 ProgressBar, CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-001 Button.
- Layout inside CMP-087 AdminLayout with CMP-049 Table and CMP-055 FilterBar; disk meter with the **projection formula shown as text**.
- The "auto-recorded" badge and its explanation of which trigger applied (`chart_open` / `position_open`), including a review-what-it-added affordance.
- Stop-recording confirmation copy ("history stops accruing, existing data is kept per policy") and the refusal state for a symbol with an open position.
- Motion spec: 1 Hz status updates must not animate rows (no flashing); only the disk meter tweens, ≤200 ms, disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Redlines/tokens handoff sheet.

## Out of scope
- SCR-141 retention editor (E16-D03) and SCR-142 storage panel (E16-D04).

- Implementation.

```gherkin
Scenario: Disk figures are never colour-only
  When a reviewer inspects the disk warning and disk critical states
  Then each carries a numeric value with units and a state word, and passes a 4.5:1 contrast check

Scenario: Auto-record is reviewable
  Given a symbol was added by the chart_open trigger
  When the design is walked through
  Then the row shows the trigger name and offers a one-click stop, matching the E16-D01 recommendation
```

## Technical notes / design
Bind every element to real data from `GET /api/v1/recording/status` and `GET /api/v1/recording/storage`: `symbols[].state` ∈ idle|starting|recording|degraded|stopping|stopped|error, `lag_ms`, `rows_last_hour`, `dropped_messages` (non-zero = incident wording, not a warning), `disk_bytes`, and `projected_full_at`. Depth tier control offers only 1/50/200/500 (`recorded_symbols.orderbook_depth` CHECK). Retention field range 1–3650 days; pinning nulls it.

## Test plan

Purge and retention changes are audited, high-severity actions — the design must route them through CMP-044 ConfirmDialog with typed confirmation and CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, and must not offer purge to non-owner roles (RBAC `recording:write` + step-up).

Disk meter has adjacent numeric text; the gap list is a table with start/end/duration columns; table rows are keyboard-reachable with visible focus; status is a word; the toggle has an accessible name including the symbol; live status updates use a polite live region that announces changes at most once per 10 s, not once per Hz.

## Performance notes
Design must survive 1 Hz updates without layout thrash: fixed-width numeric columns (tabular figures) so values changing do not reflow the table.

## Observability
Analytics events to specify on the design: `recorder.symbol_added`, `recorder.symbol_stopped`, `recorder.pin_toggled`; audit mirrors `recorder.start|stop|pinned|retention_changed|purged`.

title: Design SCR-141 retention policy editor with destructive-change confirmation
body:
## Context
SCR-141 is the only screen in the product that can irreversibly destroy recorded history by configuration rather than by an explicit purge: shortening retention makes data eligible for deletion at the next sweep. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-141 requires the screen to restate the consequence in text with the exact volume affected, and `04-security-program.md` §5.8 S5 requires a dry-run before destructive runs. Consumed by E16-S03 in Sprint 06.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi modal design for **SCR-141**: global default retention, per-stream rules (trades / orderbook_delta / orderbook_snapshot / tickers / klines / liquidations / open_interest / funding), cold-tier migration age (QuestDB → Parquet), per-symbol overrides table, pin overrides, live steady-state disk estimate under the chosen policy.
- The **dry-run / prune-preview** presentation: "this will make N GB covering dates X–Y eligible for deletion", grouped by symbol, range and size, with a typed confirmation for reductions.
- Validation messaging: retention ≥1 day; raw-tick retention ≤ bar retention ("Bars can't be deleted before the ticks they came from"); per-symbol beats global (most-specific-first) stated in the UI.
- Compaction/sweep job states: queued · running · complete · failed, with the next scheduled sweep time.
- Components: CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- Copy for the effect on replay and journal back-fill.

## Out of scope

- The purge flow's step-up authentication screens (owned by E09/E42 patterns; this design only links to it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given the owner lowers trades retention from 30 to 7 days
  When they attempt to apply
  Then the design shows a dry-run summary by symbol, range and size before any apply control is enabled
  And a typed confirmation is required

Scenario: Pinned data is visibly exempt
  Given a pinned symbol exists
  When the policy set is edited
  Then pinned symbols are listed separately with their size and are marked exempt unless applies_to_pinned is explicitly set

Scenario: Invalid tier ordering is explained, not just blocked
  Given raw-tick retention is set longer than bar retention is short
  When validation fires
  Then the message explains the rule in product terms rather than showing a constraint name
```

## Technical notes / design
Maps to `PUT /api/v1/recording/retention-policies` (with `apply_now`) and the `RetentionPolicy` shape: `scope` default|symbol, `symbol`, `stream`, `retain_days` 1–3650, `action` ∈ drop|archive_parquet|downsample|pin, `downsample_to`, `max_disk_gb`, `applies_to_pinned`. The default seed set must be shown as the baseline (trades 30 d, orderbook_delta 7 d, snapshots 30 d, tickers 30 d, klines 90 d, liquidations 90 d, open_interest 90 d, funding 365 d — `21-database-schema.md` §7).

## Test plan
Prototype walkthrough of: raising retention, lowering retention (dry-run path), adding a per-symbol override, unpinning a symbol (must surface the volume that becomes eligible). Design QA in E16-D07.

## Security notes
Every change here is audited (`retention.change`, `retention.purge`). The design must not allow a destructive apply without a dry-run having been viewed in the same session, and must show the actor that the action is audited (CMP-093).

## Accessibility notes
Every duration field states its unit in the label, not only in a suffix; the consequence text is a real paragraph associated with the field via `aria-describedby`; the typed confirmation input has an explicit instruction; the job-state region is a polite live region.

## Performance notes
The live disk estimate is computed from the already-fetched `StorageUsage` payload client-side — the design must not imply a per-keystroke server call.

## Observability
`retention.default_changed {before, after}`, `retention.symbol_override_set {symbol, before, after}`, `retention.pin_changed`, `retention.compaction_started|completed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All SCR-141 sign-off checklist items drawn and reviewed.
- [ ] Dry-run pattern reusable and documented as a design-system destructive-action pattern.
- [ ] CDO sign-off; Security engineer acknowledges the dry-run + typed-confirm flow satisfies SR-099.
- [ ] Done in Sprint 04, ≥2 sprints ahead of E16-S03.

E16-D02 establishes the admin surface language reused here.

title: Design SCR-152 and the connection-state component set to hi-fi with handoff
body:
## Context
E17 is a backend transport Epic with exactly one user-facing surface: the chrome that tells a trader what the transport is doing. That chrome is already enumerated in the catalogues - **SCR-152** (disconnected/reconnecting state, cited by US-MKT-007, US-OBS-004, US-POS-008) and components **CMP-076 ConnectionStatus**, **CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay**, **CMP-078 StaleDataShade**, **CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner** - but none of them has been drawn, and E17-T04 (the web WS client) cannot start until they are signed off (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`).

This ticket takes E17-D01's evidence to wireframes and then hi-fi, and contributes the results back to the design system rather than shipping one-offs in `apps/web`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Wireframes then hi-fi in Figma** for:
  - **SCR-152** full-workspace disconnected/reconnecting state and its **in-panel variant** (SCR-030 chart frozen with last-good timestamp, SCR-050 ladder frozen with click-trading hard-disabled) and its **inline variant** (SCR-001 login "server unreachable").
  - **CMP-076 ConnectionStatus** - all four states (`connected`, `reconnecting`, `degraded`, `offline`) with `lastGoodTs` and optional `latencyMs`, at both TopBar densities.
  - **CMP-077 ReconnectOverlay** - default and retry-exhausted, with the manual "Retry now" affordance and the attempt counter.
  - **CMP-078 StaleDataShade** - fresh and stale, with the mandatory visible "Last update Xs ago" text.
  - **CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner** - single-issue and multiple-issue, carrying the transport-sourced `connection_quality` issue alongside E04's ingestion-lag issue, with per-issue dismissal that reappears while the condition persists.
- **The degraded-fidelity treatment** decided in E17-D01, including the "feed compressed" indicator driven by `coalesced_count` if that was the recommendation.
- **Copy deck** for every state, with the exact strings: the `bye` reasons (`server_shedding_load`, `slow_consumer`), the `shutdown_notice` countdown ("Backend restarting for release X - N s"), the resync state ("Book resynchronising..."), and the six close codes of `23-ws-protocol.md` section 4.4 mapped to user-facing sentences that never expose a raw code alone.
- **Design-system contribution**: token additions or confirmations for `color.status.*`, `color.overlay.stale`, `color.surface.scrim`, `elevation.5`; entries written into `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` for any prop that changes.
- **Motion spec**: reconnect spinner and backoff countdown, banner entry/exit, and the `prefers-reduced-motion` variant of each; the stale shade must never pulse.
- **Handoff pack**: redlines, token names, state matrix, Storybook story list per component, and the announcement policy table (which state announces, with which politeness, how often).

## Out of scope
- SCR-143 Health and SCR-147 exchange-connectivity admin screens (E04/E42).
- The recorder "history starts at ts" empty state (E16) and SCR-151 (E12).
- Implementation - E17-T04 consumes this.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state a client can observe has a design
  Given the state list of 23-ws-protocol.md sections 8.3, 9.4, 10.3 and the SCR-152 variants
  When the Figma file is reviewed against it
  Then every state has exactly one drawn treatment and no state is left to implementation discretion

Scenario: Degraded is not confusable with disconnected
  When the degraded and offline treatments are shown side by side in greyscale
  Then they remain distinguishable without colour and their severity ordering matches E17-D01's ranking

Scenario: No information by colour alone
  When each artboard is checked against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  Then every status carries an icon and text in addition to colour, text contrast is at least 4.5:1 and non-text at least 3:1

Scenario: Reduced motion
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then the reconnect countdown and banner transitions have a drawn static variant and the stale shade has no animation in either variant

Scenario: A state the protocol can emit was not designed
  Given implementation discovers an emitted state with no artboard
  Then it is raised against this ticket as a design gap rather than improvised in code
```

## Technical notes / design
The state matrix is derived mechanically, not invented: rows are (`connected`, `reconnecting`, `degraded:lagging`, `degraded:saturated`, `offline`, `shutdown_pending`, `topic_resyncing`, `topic_stale`, `topic_revoked`) and columns are (global chrome, panel chrome, copy, announcement, motion). Every cell must be filled or explicitly marked "no treatment - reason".

`lastGoodTs` renders as relative age with an absolute UTC timestamp on hover/focus, because a trader reading a screenshot after the fact needs the absolute value.

## Test plan
Design QA in E17-D04. Storybook stories named in the handoff pack are implemented in E17-T04 and are the artefact design QA reviews against.

## Security notes
Copy must never surface a `request_id`, `connection_id`, `git_sha` or raw internal reason string to a Viewer-role user in a way that leaks server topology; diagnostic identifiers go behind a "copy details" affordance.

## Accessibility notes
Binding, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: CMP-077 is `role="alertdialog"`, focus-trapped, non-dismissible with a keyboard-operable retry; CMP-076 announces `degraded`/`offline` assertively **once** per transition, never per heartbeat; CMP-078 supplements shading with text; CMP-092 uses `role="status"` or `role="alert"` by severity. The announcement policy table is a sign-off artefact, not a note.

## Performance notes
Health chrome updates at 1 Hz and must not re-render the workspace subtree (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010 performance note); the design must not require per-frame values in the chrome.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Wireframes reviewed, then hi-fi artboards complete for SCR-152 (3 variants) and CMP-076/077/078/092 (all states).
- [ ] Copy deck complete and reviewed by the Owner for tone and accuracy.
- [ ] Token and component-catalogue entries merged into `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`.

`design/e17-connection-states`
