title: Chart engine core (scene, axes, interaction, LOD)
body:
## Context
CandleViewer renders every high-value surface in the product - candles, footprint cells with per-cell text, volume/delta profiles, a 200-depth DOM liquidity heatmap at 100 ms cadence, big-trade bubbles, draggable order/position lines and the whole drawing kit - through a **fully custom WebGL2 chart engine** (owner decision #1, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md`). No surveyed charting library provides those natively.

This Epic is the engine **chassis**: milestones **M1 (chassis parity)** and **M2 (data plane)** of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` 15, plus the DOM-mirror accessibility layer that `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` 6 makes a binding engine-design constraint rather than a later bolt-on. Everything else in R1 and R2 renders through what is built here: E12 bar builders and series, E13 indicators, E14 drawing tools, E15 layouts, E18 footprint, E21 DOM + heatmap. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` 13 names E11 as a single point of failure on the critical path `E02 -> E06 -> E11 -> E12 -> E18 -> E26 -> E38 -> E44 -> E46 -> GA`.

The research warning this Epic exists to honour: **parity work on the "boring things"** (pan/zoom momentum, axis decimation, multi-pane sync, crosshair, DPI correctness, transform math) costs 4-8 weeks and must finish *before* any order-flow feature can pay off. It is scheduled first, deliberately.

The package is **framework-free** (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16): `packages/chart-engine` contains no React, no application state, no `fetch` and no Bybit knowledge. React bindings are a thin layer in `apps/web`.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Engineering (91 pts across Sprint 05 - Sprint 07)**

- **Package and API** - `packages/chart-engine` with the public surface of `26-chart-engine-design.md` 8 (`Chart`, `Pane`, `SeriesHandle`, `ChartEvents`, `FrameStats`, `RenderContext`, `SeriesPlugin`), thin React bindings in `apps/web` (E11-T01).
- **Worker plane** - OffscreenCanvas render worker, main-to-worker message protocol ( 6), `RunMode.inline` fallback, transferable typed-array data path (E11-T02); columnar stores with an append/patch/prepend mutation API returning affected index ranges (E11-T03).
- **Scene and loop** - fixed-depth scene graph `Chart -> Pane -> Layer -> Series` with `DATA|LAYOUT|STYLE|TRANSFORM` dirty flags; `FrameScheduler` with a 16.7 ms budget, bounded 4 ms/frame data-mutation drain, time-based animation, render-on-demand parking (E11-S01).
- **GL backend** - WebGL2 context management, capability probe selecting `RenderProfile` (`full`/`reduced`/`degraded-2d`), program/VAO/buffer lifecycle, context-loss recovery within 2 s with no data loss wired to **SCR-048** (E11-S02, E11-T05).
- **Transform and scales** - bar-index vs time space, `indexToScreen`/`timeToScreen`/`screenToIndex`/`screenToPrice`, tick-integer price precision with a `priceOrigin` uniform (E11-S03); price scale linear / log / percent / inverted with autoscale, manual lock and the **SCR-043** context menus (E11-S05, `US-CHART-007`).
- **Interaction** - pan/zoom with cursor-anchored zoom, kinetic momentum honouring reduced-motion, wheel/pointer coalescing to <= 1 batch per frame, full keyboard equivalents (E11-S04, `US-CHART-006`).
- **Axes** - `CMP-188 PriceAxis`, `CMP-189 TimeAxis` with label decimation, device-pixel snapping, drag-to-rescale plus a keyboard rescale path (E11-S06).
- **Crosshair and readout** - `CMP-190 Crosshair`, `CMP-197 ChartTooltip`, `CMP-226 BarCountdown`, magnet modes, sync-group broadcast (E11-S07, `US-CHART-008`).
- **Hit-testing** - analytic structural index plus a 64 px uniform-grid object index, edge-triggered pick messages, <= 1 ms budget (E11-S08).
- **Multi-pane** - pane stacking with a shared time axis, height ratios, `CMP-196 MultiChartLinker` sync groups for time range / crosshair / price level (E11-S09).
- **DPI** - backing store at `devicePixelRatio` (heatmap layer capped at 2), hairline snapping, resize and DPR-change handling (E11-S10).
- **Text** - SDF glyph atlas pipeline, two-pass EDT generation, shelf packing, IndexedDB caching, instanced glyph batching, outline variant for legibility over saturated fills (E11-S11, spike E11-K01 closing open item **O2**).
- **LOD** - candle L0/L1/L2 ladder with **min/max-preserving** decimation, 15 % hysteresis dead band, automatic step-down after 3 consecutive over-budget frames, the degradation ladder of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` 4.4 (E11-S12).
- **Accessibility layer** - windowed DOM mirror, keyboard data cursor, throttled live regions, canvas `role="img"` rolling label (E11-S13); the **SCR-045** data-table alternative (E11-S14, `US-CHART-014`).
- **Memory and paging** - `MemoryGovernor` (600 MB budget, 5 s sampling, step-down over 70 %), `visibleRangeNeedsData` paging, days-to-load memory estimate feeding **SCR-044** and **SCR-047** (E11-S15, `US-CHART-010`).
- **Quality infrastructure** - theme/LUT/density ingestion (E11-T04), golden-image harness on SwiftShader (E11-T08), benchmark harness promoted to a **required CI check** with B1/B2/B5/B6/B9/B10 baselines (E11-T06), the **SCR-046** diagnostics feed (E11-T07), engine API freeze plus ADR amendment (E11-T09).

**User stories covered:** `US-CHART-006` (pan/zoom/autoscale, Must), `US-CHART-007` (log and percentage scales, Must/Should), `US-CHART-008` (crosshair, OHLCV readout, countdown, Must), `US-CHART-010` (days-to-load control, Must), `US-CHART-014` (accessible chart data alternative, Must). `US-CHART-001` (candlestick rendering, Must) is **jointly owned**: E11 provides the render loop, the LOD ladder, the empty/error states and the frame budget it is measured against; the candle series itself ships in E12.

**Screens:** SCR-030 (chart panel chassis), SCR-031 (chart settings - scale section), SCR-043 (price/time-scale context menus), SCR-044 (Go to date), SCR-045 (data-table alternative), SCR-046 (diagnostics overlay), SCR-047 (empty / no-data), SCR-048 (error state).

**Components:** CMP-180 ChartRoot, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-189 TimeAxis, CMP-190 Crosshair, CMP-196 MultiChartLinker, CMP-197 ChartTooltip, CMP-198 ChartWatermark / PaneBackground, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-226 BarCountdown, CMP-228 PreviewTile (settings previews), CMP-004 FocusRing (mirror-node focus ring).

**Engineering 102 pts** across E11-K01, E11-S01..S15 and E11-T01..T09 (of which E11-T06 and E11-T08 carry the `qa` label because they are test infrastructure, and are counted on the QA capacity line). **Design 32 pts** (E11-D01..D09), **QA 33 pts** (E11-Q01..Q07 plus T06/T08), **Security 8 pts** (E11-X01..X03) are tracked against their own capacity lines, per the planning brief's separate design/QA/security capacity rule.

## Out of scope
- **Series rendering** of candles / bars / line / area / baseline / Heikin-Ashi and all bar builders - E12 (`US-CHART-001`..`005`, `US-CHART-011`). E11 ships the plugin seam they register against, not the plugins.
- Indicators and indicator plugin implementations - E13. Footprint series, profiles, heatmap, bubbles, Deep-Stats - E18/E19/E20/E21/E22. Drawing tools - E14. Layouts, workspaces and chart templates (`US-CHART-012`) - E15. Order and position line overlays (`US-CHART-013`) - E31.
- Session / day-boundary configuration (`US-CHART-009`) - owned by E12 alongside the bar builders that consume it.
- Backend data supply: `GET /api/v1/market/bars`, `GET /api/v1/market/footprint`, `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` and the `bars.*` / `trades.*` / `ticker.*` WS topics - E17 and E12. The engine consumes typed arrays handed to it; it never performs I/O.
- WebGPU backend (explicit future seam only), SVG output, server-side rendering, third-party distribution of the package.
- Android and any mobile client (owner decision 2026-09-14). No separate admin app.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Frame budget met and enforced
  Given the CI benchmark harness runs scenario B5 on the reference machine in Electron
  When 100k bars plus all R1 overlays render through the engine chassis
  Then p95 frame time is <= 16.6 ms and p50 frame rate is >= 60 fps
  And a change regressing any hard-budget p95 by more than 5 % fails the required check

Scenario: 30 fps floor holds under worst case
  Given a 6-chart layout with every R1 overlay enabled (benchmark B6)
  When the frame budget is exceeded for 3 consecutive frames
  Then the engine steps down one LOD level per the degradation ladder and logs the step
  And frame rate never falls below 30 fps and no trading-critical overlay is shed

Scenario: Context loss recovers without data loss
  Given a chart with 100k bars, 3 panes and an active crosshair
  When WEBGL_lose_context is forced
  Then SCR-048 announces "Graphics context lost - restoring..." through a role="alert" region
  And a fully correct scene is restored from the DataModel within 2 s with zero data loss

Scenario: The chart is fully operable without a mouse
  Given a chart pane has keyboard focus
  When the user navigates with arrow keys, Home/End, +/- and Alt+T
  Then the data cursor steps bar by bar and the OHLCV readout is announced in a throttled live region
  And the SCR-045 data table exposes the same data at the same fidelity as the canvas

Scenario: The engine package stays framework-free
  Given packages/chart-engine is built
  When its dependency graph is inspected in CI
  Then it imports no React, no application store, no fetch/XHR/WS client and no Bybit-specific type
  And a PR introducing any of those fails the boundary check

Scenario: Engine degrades rather than fails without WebGL2
  Given a machine whose capability probe reports no WebGL2
  When a chart is mounted
  Then RenderProfile degraded-2d is selected and candles, axes and lines render through Canvas 2D
  And the user is told which capabilities are reduced and why, never shown a blank canvas
```

## Technical notes / design
Milestone mapping (`26-chart-engine-design.md` 15): **M1 chassis parity** = E11-S01..S12 plus T01/T04/T05/T08; **M2 data plane** = E11-T02/T03 plus S15. M1 exits on benchmarks **B1** and **B2** green plus golden images for candles/axes/crosshair; M2 exits on **B7** and **B9** green plus integration tests against fixtures.

Child dependency graph:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    T01[T01 Package + public API] --> T02[T02 Worker + OffscreenCanvas]
    T01 --> S01[S01 Scene graph + scheduler]
    T02 --> T03[T03 Columnar data model]
    S01 --> S02[S02 GL backend + context loss]
    S02 --> S03[S03 Viewport + transform math]
    S03 --> S04[S04 Pan / zoom / momentum]
    S03 --> S05[S05 Price scale modes]
    S03 --> S11[S11 SDF text atlas]
    K01[K01 Glyph-set spike O2] --> S11
    S11 --> S06[S06 Price + time axes]
    S04 --> S07[S07 Crosshair + readout]
    S06 --> S07
    S03 --> S08[S08 Hit-testing]
    S01 --> S09[S09 Multi-pane + sync groups]
    S02 --> S10[S10 DPI + resize]
    S03 --> S12[S12 LOD + decimation]
    S08 --> S13[S13 DOM-mirror a11y layer]
    S07 --> S13
    S13 --> S14[S14 SCR-045 data table]
    T03 --> S15[S15 Memory governor + paging]
    S02 --> T05[T05 degraded-2d fallback]
    S01 --> T04[T04 Theme, LUT, density]
    S06 --> T08[T08 Golden-image harness]
    S12 --> T06[T06 Benchmarks as CI gate]
    T06 --> T07[T07 SCR-046 diagnostics feed]
    S14 --> T09[T09 API freeze + ADR amendment]
    D01[D01 UX research] --> D02[D02 Chart chassis hi-fi]
    D02 --> D03[D03 Scale menus hi-fi]
    D02 --> D04[D04 Table / empty / error hi-fi]
    D02 --> D05[D05 Design-system contribution]
    D02 --> D06[D06 Motion spec]
    D04 --> D07[D07 A11y design review]
    D05 --> D09[D09 Handoff pack]
    D02 --> S06
    D03 --> S05
    D04 --> S14
    D06 --> S04
    D07 --> S13
    S07 --> Q01[Q01 Black-box test plan]
    S09 --> Q02[Q02 E2E suite additions]
    T06 --> Q03[Q03 Perf baseline sign-off]
    S02 --> Q04[Q04 Chaos / robustness charter]
    S14 --> Q05[Q05 A11y audit]
    Q05 --> Q06[Q06 Regression pack + sign-off]
    T05 --> Q07[Q07 GPU matrix exploratory]
    S01 --> X01[X01 STRIDE threat model]
    X01 --> X02[X02 SAST / SCA rules]
    X02 --> X03[X03 Abuse cases + review]
    S14 --> D08[D08 Design QA]
```

**Risks carried by this Epic.**

| Risk | Exposure | Mitigation inside this Epic |
|---|---|---|
| R2 Render performance | The whole product renders through this chassis | Benchmark harness becomes a required CI check in E11-T06 during Sprint 07; B1/B2 gate M1 exit; per-stage attribution makes regressions same-day diagnosable |
| R8 Browser/GPU compat | WebGL2 availability, driver quirks, WebView2 behaviour | Capability probe plus `degraded-2d` (E11-T05), GPU matrix exploratory (E11-Q07), golden images on SwiftShader (E11-T08) |
| R10 Key-person | One graphics-capable engineer carries the subsystem | Pairing rule on S01/S02/S11; every subsystem documented in `26-chart-engine-design.md`; no undocumented shader tricks |
| R5 Scope | Chassis parity expanding into series work | The Out-of-scope boundary above; series plugins live in E12 and register through the seam |

**Exit criteria (Epic level, verified end-to-end, not per child).**
1. Benchmarks B1, B2, B5, B6, B9 and B10 green on the reference machine in Electron, recorded as artefacts and enforced as a required check.
2. The 30 fps floor holds under the B6 worst case using the documented degradation ladder.
3. Forced `WEBGL_lose_context` restores a correct scene within 2 s with no data loss (R1 exit criterion 8).
4. Every chart is operable without a mouse; NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the accessibility specialist (R1 exit criterion 9).
5. `packages/chart-engine` at >= 85 % line coverage; property tests hold over 10k cases for transform round-trips, LOD selection and decimation extreme-preservation.
6. Golden images exist per layer and per theme including `degraded-2d`, at <= 0.1 % pixel diff.
7. Public engine API frozen and documented; `26-chart-engine-design.md` matches the shipped implementation; open item **O2** closed by an ADR amendment.
8. Zero open P0/P1 bugs against E11 scope; STRIDE findings triaged; QA and design sign-off recorded; demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review.

## Test plan
Epic-level rollup; per-child plans live on the children.
- **Unit / property** (Vitest + fast-check, >= 85 % lines): transform round-trips, log/percent projection, LOD thresholds with hysteresis, min/max decimation preservation, ring-buffer wrap, prefix-sum indexing, momentum integration, viewport clamping, colour-LUT generation.
- **Golden image** (Playwright + SwiftShader, <= 0.1 % diff): axes, crosshair, grid, pane chrome, text at each LOD, `degraded-2d`, per theme.
- **Contract**: engine consumes only `packages/protocol` types; `tsd` / `tsc --noEmit` compile-time assertion; framework-free boundary check.
- **Integration**: engine plus a fake WS server against a recorded fixture session - snapshot, deltas, sequence-gap resync, paging.
- **Interaction** (Playwright, web and Electron): pan, zoom, crosshair, axis drag, keyboard cursor, multi-pane sync.
- **Accessibility**: axe-core zero violations on all chart routes; live-region announcement assertions; reduced-motion behaviour; manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes.
- **Performance**: B1, B2, B5, B6, B7, B9, B10 at 3 repetitions, medians of p95 compared to baseline.
- **Fuzz / robustness**: malformed frames, out-of-order sequences, NaN/Infinity prices, zero-size canvas, mid-flight DPR change, injected context loss.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data only** (public, non-PII, no financial credentials). The engine holds no secrets, no API keys and no account identifiers beyond opaque ids passed for overlay labels in later Epics.

STRIDE surface (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** - malicious or corrupt binary frames reaching the decoder, shader/asset supply chain, IndexedDB-cached SDF atlas poisoning. **Denial of service** - unbounded data volume exhausting GPU/JS memory, pathological zoom or LOD causing allocation storms, worker starvation. **Information disclosure** - the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay and error correlation ids leaking internals into screenshots. **Repudiation** - not applicable (no state mutation). **Spoofing / elevation of privilege** - not applicable at engine level; topic authorization belongs to E17.

Controls: strict typed-array bounds validation at every ingest point; NaN/Infinity rejection; hard `maxBars` and `memoryBudgetMb` ceilings enforced by the `MemoryGovernor`; no `eval` and no dynamic shader source derived from data; pinned dependencies under npm-audit/Dependabot gates; CSP-compatible worker construction. The `security` label is required on E11-S02, E11-T02, E11-T03 and E11-S15.

## Accessibility notes
Binding, not advisory: `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` 6 makes the three-layer canvas strategy an engine-design constraint. This Epic ships all three layers - the windowed DOM mirror ( 6.1, E11-S13), throttled live regions ( 6.2, E11-S13) and the data-table alternative ( 6.3, E11-S14, SCR-045) - plus `role="img"` with a rolling `aria-label` on the canvas (CMP-180), keyboard rescale on both axes (CMP-188/189), a keyboard-driven crosshair as the *primary* path with hover as the pointer convenience layer (CMP-190), reduced-motion-respecting momentum, and non-colour-only encodings throughout. WCAG 2.2 AA; axe-core zero violations on all R1 chart routes; manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the accessibility specialist (E11-Q05, E11-D07).

## Performance notes
Hard gates: budget **#1** (16.6 ms p95 frame with 100k bars plus a 200-depth heatmap at 100 ms) and budget **#2** (30 fps floor under worst case). Budget **#14** (100 ms heatmap cadence) is prepared by this Epic's texture-streaming seam and gated in E21. The per-stage allocation of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` 4.3 is instrumented stage by stage, not just totalled. Memory <= 600 MB per chart instance (requirement R7), with the modelled chassis footprint about 116 MB for the 100k-bar case. Steady state <= 18 draw calls per pane and <= 40 for a 3-pane chart. Zero GC-triggering allocations in the frame path, asserted by an allocation-counter test. Regression gate: a p95 regression above 5 % on any hard budget fails the build.

## Observability

- Structured `Performance.mark()`/`measure()` spans at all nine 4.3 stage boundaries, correlated with the backend span id carried on the WS envelope.
- Engine error events with stable codes: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE`, `ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN`, `ENGINE_FRAME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, each with a `recoverable` flag and surfaced on SCR-048 with a copyable correlation id.
- Analytics events emitted from engine hooks but owned by the app layer: `chart.error_shown`, `diagnostics.overlay_toggled`, `diagnostics.snapshot_copied`.

title: Design the data-table alternative and the chart empty and error states
body:
## Context
Three surfaces, one shared property: they are what the user sees when the canvas is not enough.

**SCR-045** is the data-table alternative, and `US-CHART-014`'s NFR is unusually forceful — "this view is treated as an **equal-status alternative, not a degraded fallback**" — with `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 adding that it "is not a stripped-down compliance minimum". SCR-045's own sign-off checklist makes the point structural: it must be "reachable from the chart panel header, **not hidden in settings** — equal status verified". Designing this as a utility panel tucked behind a settings toggle would fail the ticket regardless of how it looks.

**SCR-047** (empty / no-data) and **SCR-048** (error) are the states most likely to be encountered by a new user on day one, and both carry explicit "no infinite spinner" and "never a blank canvas" requirements.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-045 data table**: the full table layout with columns time, open, high, low, close, volume, delta, CVD; the **expandable per-bar footprint cell row** (price, bid, ask, delta, imbalance flag); the filter toolbar; tri-state sort affordance with `aria-sort`; the row-action menu (create alert here, replay from here, add note); the TSV-copy affordance; and the **stale banner** ("Data is for bar X, no longer in view — press Alt+T to refresh to current").
- The **equal-status entry point**: a control in the chart panel header, designed at equal visual weight to other primary chart controls — plus `Alt+T`.
- Empty, loading and filtered-to-zero states of the table.
- **SCR-047 empty / no-data**: the three distinct reasons drawn separately — never recorded (with the "history starts when you record" explanation and the owner CTA to SCR-140), no data in this range, instrument not trading/delisted — plus the non-owner explanatory copy variant and the "live data is still streaming" note where true.
- **SCR-048 error**: distinct copy for engine/WebGL failure, data-feed failure and backend failure; the **WebGL-unavailable message naming the fallback path** (E11-T05's `degraded-2d`); the "Graphics context lost — restoring…" auto-retry treatment with attempt count and next-attempt time; a **copyable correlation id**; retry and "open diagnostics" actions; and the requirement that the rest of the workspace remains usable.
- All states in dark, light and high-contrast.

## Out of scope
- Footprint sub-row **content** semantics — E18 (this ticket designs the expandable mechanism and the column contract).
- The profile and DOM-ladder table variants of §6.3 — E19 and E21, which reuse this table shell.
- The recorder settings screen (SCR-140) the empty-state CTA links to — E16.
- Alert/replay/note flows behind the row actions — E40/E26/E41.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The table is designed as an equal-status view
  Given the SCR-045 design
  When the entry point is reviewed
  Then a control exists in the chart panel header at equal visual weight to other primary chart controls
  And the table is not reachable only from settings, and is not styled as a secondary or fallback surface

Scenario: The table carries the same information as the canvas
  Given the canvas shows bars with OHLCV, delta and per-bar footprint cells
  When the table columns are reviewed
  Then every one of those values has a column or an expandable sub-row
  And no information available on the canvas is missing from the table

Scenario: Every empty reason is drawn separately
  Given the three empty reasons: never recorded, no data in this range, instrument not trading
  When SCR-047 is reviewed
  Then each is drawn with its own copy and its own action
  And the owner CTA and the non-owner explanatory variant are both present, with no infinite-spinner path anywhere

Scenario: The error state names the fallback and is actionable
  Given WebGL2 is unavailable
  When SCR-048 is reviewed
  Then the copy names the degraded-2d fallback and what is reduced
  And a copyable correlation id, a retry action and an open-diagnostics action are present, and the rest of the workspace remains usable

Scenario: Context-loss recovery is communicated, not hidden
  Given the engine is auto-retrying after a lost graphics context
  Then the design shows "restoring", the attempt count and the next-attempt time
  And after three failed attempts a manual retry and a link to renderer settings are offered

Scenario: The stale banner prevents silent staleness
  Given the table's focused bar scrolls out of the chart's visible range
  Then a banner states which bar the data is for and how to refresh
  And the stale values are never presented as though they were current
```

## Technical notes / design
**Equal status is a layout decision, not a copy decision.** The table's entry point sits in the panel header alongside the chart-type and indicator controls, at the same size and weight. A "view as table" item buried in an overflow menu would satisfy the letter of the requirement and fail its intent, which is why SCR-045's checklist calls it out explicitly.

**Table density.** The table is the surface a low-vision user will zoom to 200 %, so the design must hold at that zoom without horizontal scrolling of the primary columns (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.10 reflow). The column-picker (CMP-056) is how a user drops columns they do not need, and the default column set must already fit comfortably.

**Error copy discipline.** Three distinct causes, three distinct messages, each naming what the user can do. "Something went wrong" is not acceptable copy for any of the three; the correlation id exists so the user can hand over something actionable, and it must be selectable text, not an image or a truncated ellipsis.

**Empty-state honesty.** The never-recorded case is the most common first-run experience, and the copy must be honest about the product's model: history exists because *you recorded it*. SCR-047's example copy — "No recorded history for BTCUSDT before 2026-09-01 08:00 UTC. Live data is streaming now." — is the tone to match.

## Test plan
- **Parity review**: canvas information inventory vs table column inventory, item by item, recorded in the sign-off.
- **Zoom review**: table at 200 % browser zoom, confirming reflow without horizontal scrolling of primary columns.
- **Screen-reader review** with the accessibility specialist over table semantics, sort announcement and filter announcement.
- **Copy review** for all empty and error variants, including the non-owner RBAC variants.
- **Colour-blind simulation** over delta signs and imbalance flags, confirming the text encodings carry the meaning.
- Design QA of the built result in **E11-D08**; the built table is audited in **E11-Q05**.

## Security notes
The error state is the security-relevant surface here. SCR-048 requires a **correlation id as selectable text**, which is deliberately opaque — it identifies a trace, not a user, an account or a session. The design must not surface internal exception messages, stack traces, hostnames or query strings, because this screen is screenshotted into issues by design. Plain-language copy plus an opaque id is the whole contract.

For SCR-047, the owner CTA ("Record this symbol") is a privileged action: the **non-owner variant is explanatory copy, not a disabled button**, so a `viewer` is not shown an action they can never take.

## Accessibility notes
This is the ticket where the accessibility standard's §6.3 becomes a drawn artefact:
- Real `<table>` semantics with column and row headers; tri-state sort with `aria-sort`; filter state announced with counts ("Showing 6 of 40 rows, filtered by: Bid-stacked").
- Keyboard navigation designed explicitly: arrows to move, `Enter` to expand, `Ctrl+C` to copy, `Alt+T` to open/close, with focus placement and restoration specified.
- **Equal status** is itself an accessibility requirement — this is the normative accessible equivalent of SCR-030.
- Delta signs as text `+`/`-`; imbalance flags as text labels; `(estimated)` carries the literal word (CMP-227) — never colour or icon alone.
- SCR-048 is a `role="alert"` region with plain-language copy and a focusable, non-colour-only retry.
- SCR-047 is a heading + paragraph + action, never an icon alone; the recording-start timestamp is text.
- Reviewed by the accessibility specialist; this ticket is a primary input to **E11-D07**.

## Performance notes
SCR-045's budget shapes the design: the table is **virtualised**, renders 100k rows without jank (<=8 ms scripting per scroll frame), and **reads the same in-memory series as the canvas so no extra fetch is issued** — meaning the design must not include anything that would require a separate query (a full-series aggregate footer, for instance, would). SCR-047 requires the empty state to render **without initialising the GL context**, so an empty chart costs no GPU budget — the design must therefore not depend on any canvas-rendered element. SCR-048's retry uses exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, capped 30s) with the next attempt time shown.

## Observability
Design fixes the analytics surface: `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported` (SCR-045); `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason}` (SCR-047); `chart.error_shown` with `{code, correlationId}` (SCR-048).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.
- [ ] SCR-045, SCR-047 and SCR-048 design sign-off acceptance checklists ticked item by item.
- [ ] Equal-status verification recorded explicitly in the sign-off comment (entry point placement and visual weight).

## Dependencies
- **E11-D02** — the chassis and panel header the table's entry point lives in.
- **E05** — CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-027 ErrorState, CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback.
- Blocks **E11-S14** (design-ahead) and informs **E11-S13** and **E11-T05**.

## Branch
`design/chart-engine-table-and-states` (Figma).

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` — SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-043, SCR-044, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047, SCR-048, SCR-049 (each entry's states, a11y, performance and design sign-off checklist)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` §7 — CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226, CMP-228, CMP-004
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` — tokens, theming, motion, density, a11y
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 (no hover/drag-only), §4 (focus, target size, zoom), §6 (canvas a11y), §7 (reduced motion)
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`, `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 (visual encoding rules, density modes)
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 (design-ready gate)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-045, SCR-047, SCR-048
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-014 (equal-status NFR)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 (table alternative, column sets, sort/filter/live-sync)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-004, CMP-026, CMP-027, CMP-049, CMP-053, CMP-056, CMP-091, CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-196

title: Run an accessibility design review of the chart engine's canvas strategy
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 opens by naming this "the **highest-risk area**" of the product: WebGL canvases are opaque to assistive technology, and the mitigation is a three-layer strategy that must be designed into the engine rather than retrofitted. §6.1 is explicit that the engine's visible-window/focused-unit query surface is "an **explicit chart-engine-design requirement, not an afterthought bolted on later**".

Retrofitting accessibility into a render engine is close to impossible — by the time the canvas is drawing, the information needed to describe it has already been discarded. This review exists to catch that class of problem while it is still a design change, and it is scheduled **before** E11-S13 and E11-S14 are built precisely so its findings are cheap.

It is also the ticket that verifies the **equal-status** claim for SCR-045, which is the product's main accessibility promise and the one most easily eroded in implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Layer-by-layer review** against `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6:
  - §6.1 DOM mirror — windowing strategy, the canvas-control-surrogate pattern, `clip-path` hiding (**not** `display:none`), surrogate sizing matching visual targets, focus ring visibility over canvas content, node-count cap.
  - §6.2 Live regions — politeness routing per event class, throttle cadence (default 1 update / 2 s, `US-CHART-008`'s <=2/s cap), region hygiene (pre-rendered containers, text-content-only swaps), the "reduce announcements" master toggle, and which events are `role="alert"` and therefore never throttled.
  - §6.3 Table alternative — equal-status verification, column-set completeness against the canvas, sort/filter announcements, live-patching without focus loss, the stale banner.
  - §6.4 Canvas semantics — `role="img"` with a rolling label that updates on data change.
- **Keyboard vocabulary review**: the complete key map across chart, axes, panes, crosshair, table and menus — checked for conflicts with the global hotkey table, with screen-reader reserved keys, and with browser defaults. A key map with a conflict is discovered in testing at ten times the cost of discovering it here.
- **No hover-only / no drag-only audit** (§3.1.6): every pointer gesture in E11 enumerated with its keyboard equivalent — pan, zoom, axis rescale, splitter resize, crosshair, magnet, legend toggles, table sort.
- **Focus-order review** across panes, axes, legend, table and overlay.
- **Target-size review** (§4) for splitters, axis drag zones and legend toggles.
- **Contrast and colour-independence re-check** across D02/D03/D04/D05 as a set, rather than per ticket — encodings that are individually fine can collide when composed.
- **Reduced-motion review** of D06's spec.
- Findings logged with severity and an owner, each routed to the specific engineering or design ticket that must change.

## Out of scope
- Auditing the **built** product — **E11-Q05** (the a11y audit with NVDA/VoiceOver passes on real code).
- Accessibility of order-flow surfaces — E18/E19/E21's own reviews against this same standard.
- The design system's base component accessibility — E05.
- Writing the DOM mirror — E11-S13.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All four layers are reviewed against the standard, clause by clause
  Given 05-accessibility-standard.md sections 6.1 through 6.4
  When the review is complete
  Then each clause has a verdict of compliant, at risk or non-compliant with evidence
  And every non-compliant and at-risk item has an owner and a target ticket

Scenario: Equal status is verified, not asserted
  Given SCR-045's equal-status requirement
  When the table design is compared against the canvas information inventory
  Then every value available on the canvas has a table equivalent
  And the entry point is confirmed to be in the panel header at equal visual weight, not in settings

Scenario: No functionality is pointer-only
  Given every pointer gesture E11 introduces
  When the audit table is inspected
  Then each has a keyboard equivalent of equal capability
  And any gesture without one is raised as a blocking finding

Scenario: The key map has no conflicts
  Given the complete E11 key map
  When it is checked against the global hotkey table, screen-reader reserved keys and browser defaults
  Then no conflict exists
  And any conflict found is resolved before the review is signed off, not deferred to implementation

Scenario: Findings land before the code is written
  Given E11-S13 starts in Sprint 07 and E11-S14 in Sprint 08
  Then this review is Done by the end of Sprint 05
  And its findings are reflected in those tickets before they start
```

## Technical notes / design
**Method.** Structured walkthrough against the standard's clauses, with the accessibility specialist, the chart-engine lead and the designer of record present. Each clause gets a verdict rather than a discussion, so the output is actionable rather than a set of notes.

**The highest-value check is the desync question.** The DOM mirror and the canvas can disagree — at an LOD step-down, mid-pan, or during a live update — and `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4 states plainly that desync is **never acceptable**. The review's job is to interrogate the design for every path where the two could diverge and confirm each is structurally prevented rather than merely unlikely. E11-S13's property test exists because of this review.

**Key-map conflicts worth checking specifically**, since they are the ones that actually bite: NVDA's browse-mode keys, JAWS's virtual cursor, VoiceOver's `VO`-prefixed combinations, and browser defaults (`Ctrl+F`, `Ctrl+D`, `Alt+arrow` for history). `Alt+T` for the table is chosen because it is clear in all four, and the review confirms that the rest of the map is too.

**Screen-reader coverage** for the review's purposes: NVDA + Chrome and VoiceOver + Safari as primary (matching E11-Q05's audit targets), JAWS noted where behaviour is known to differ.

## Test plan
Review verification rather than software testing:
- Every §6 clause has a recorded verdict with evidence.
- The pointer-gesture audit table is complete — enumerated from the design, not from memory.
- The key map is checked against three published reserved-key lists plus the product's own global hotkey table.
- Findings are triaged with severity, owner and target ticket; blocking findings prevent sign-off of the design tickets they affect.
- A prototype walkthrough with a screen reader is performed where the design's behaviour is ambiguous on paper — which, for live regions, it usually is.

## Security notes
No security surface.

One intersection worth recording: the DOM mirror is real DOM containing formatted market data, and the review confirms the design specifies `textContent` writes rather than `innerHTML`, so a malformed symbol name or number string cannot become markup. This is an accessibility ticket noticing a security property because the mirror is the one place where engine-rendered values become DOM — it is fed to E11-X01's threat model rather than handled here.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket **is** the accessibility work. Its authority: `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 is binding on the engine's design, WCAG 2.2 AA is the conformance target, and the accessibility specialist's sign-off is a gate on E11-S13 and E11-S14 entering Ready.

The findings feed:
- **E11-S13** — mirror windowing, surrogate sizing, throttle cadence, politeness routing, canvas label.
- **E11-S14** — equal status, column completeness, sort/filter announcements, live patching without focus loss.
- **E11-D02/D03/D04** — any design change the review requires.
- **E11-Q05** — the audit's test charter is derived from this review's findings, so the built product is audited against the same clauses.

## Performance notes
Accessibility and performance intersect in two specific places the review must confirm rather than assume: the mirror's node cap (500) and per-frame cost (<=1 ms) must be achievable given the designed surrogate density, and the announcement throttle must be slow enough for a screen reader to keep up at a 20 Hz tick rate. A design that requires a surrogate per footprint cell, for example, would be accessible on paper and unbuildable in practice — catching that here is the point.

## Observability
Findings and verdicts recorded on the ticket and summarised in the sign-off. `engine.a11y.desync_detected` (E11-S13) exists as a runtime counter because of this review's desync analysis.

- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.

- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.
- [ ] Every §6.1–§6.4 clause has a recorded verdict with evidence.
- [ ] Pointer-gesture audit table complete with a keyboard equivalent for every gesture.
- [ ] Key map verified conflict-free against reserved keys and the global hotkey table.
- [ ] All blocking findings resolved; non-blocking findings filed with owner and target ticket.
- [ ] Signed off by the accessibility specialist **and** the chart-engine lead.

## Dependencies
- **E11-D02**, **E11-D03**, **E11-D04**, **E11-D05**, **E11-D06** — the designs under review (D04 is the direct blocker since the table is the central artefact).

## References

- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 (no hover/drag-only), §4 (focus, target size, zoom), §6 (canvas a11y), §7 (reduced motion)
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`, `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`

title: Produce the chart-engine design handoff pack and run the engineering walkthrough
body:
## Context
The design-ahead rule exists so engineering never waits on design, but a signed-off Figma file is not the same as a usable specification. The chart chassis is unusually hard to hand off because most of it has **no DOM**: an engineer cannot inspect a canvas-rendered axis in a browser to find out what the tick spacing should be, and cannot derive label decimation behaviour from a static frame. Everything that would normally be discoverable has to be written down.

This ticket produces the pack that makes E11's design specs actionable without a conversation, and runs the walkthrough where the remaining ambiguities surface while both sides are in the room.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Redline specs** for every E11 surface: spacing, type scale, token names (not hex values), border radii, opacity, and the numeric values for all three density modes.
- **Behaviour specs** for what a static frame cannot express — the things most likely to be guessed at otherwise:
  - Axis label decimation as a **rule** (nice-interval selection, minimum pixel gap, drop order, what is never dropped).
  - Gridline major/minor selection rule relative to instrument tick size.
  - Tooltip collision/flip rules and the never-obscure-last-price priority order.
  - Crosshair magnet snap targets and their precedence.
  - Legend overflow behaviour with many indicators.
  - Pane splitter minimum heights and collapse thresholds.
- **The complete key map** as a table: key, context, action, announcement — as reviewed in E11-D07.
- **The motion spec table** from E11-D06 (element, trigger, property, duration, easing, reduced-motion variant).
- **Token mapping table**: every visual element -> its design-system token slot, so implementation is a lookup rather than an interpretation.
- **State matrix**: every surface × every state × every theme, with the expected treatment per cell.
- **Asset export**: any icons, the pattern/hatch definitions, and the font subset E11-K01 needs for the SDF atlas.
- **Walkthrough session** with the chart-engine lead and the frontend engineers who will build E11-S04..S14, recorded, with questions answered on the spot and any that cannot be answered assigned an owner and a date.
- **Open-question log** driven to zero before the pack is marked Done — carrying an open question into implementation is the failure mode this ticket exists to prevent.

## Out of scope
- The designs themselves — D02/D03/D04/D05/D06.
- Ongoing design support during implementation — normal sprint activity, not a deliverable here.
- Handoff for other Epics' chart surfaces — their own handoff tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An engineer can build from the pack without asking a question
  Given a frontend engineer assigned to E11-S06 with no prior involvement in the design
  When they build the axes from the handoff pack alone
  Then every value they need (spacing, tokens, type, decimation rule, keyboard behaviour) is in the pack
  And this is verified during the walkthrough by having them attempt exactly that

Scenario: Behaviour that a static frame cannot express is written as a rule
  Given axis label decimation, gridline selection, tooltip collision and magnet snapping
  When the pack is reviewed
  Then each is specified as a rule that produces a deterministic result at any zoom level
  And none is left as a set of example frames to interpolate between

Scenario: The key map is complete and unambiguous
  Given the key map table
  Then every key has its context, action and announcement
  And it matches the map reviewed and cleared of conflicts in E11-D07

Scenario: Open questions are closed, not carried
  Given the open-question log at the end of the walkthrough
  Then every question is either answered in the pack or has a named owner and a due date before the consuming sprint starts
  And the pack is not marked Done while an unowned question remains

Scenario: Tokens are handed over as names, not values
  Given the token mapping table
  Then every element maps to a design-system token slot
  And no hex value appears as an implementation instruction anywhere in the pack
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why rules rather than frames.** A chart is continuous: there is no "the" zoom level, so a design expressed as three example frames leaves the engineer to invent the behaviour between them — and they will invent something reasonable and different from what was intended. Every zoom-dependent behaviour in the pack is therefore expressed as an algorithm the engineer can implement directly:

```
timeAxisLabels(range, widthPx):
  candidates = niceIntervals(range)            // 1/2/5 x 10^n in time units
  interval   = smallest candidate whose label spacing >= minGapPx
  labels     = ticks at that interval
  always keep: session boundaries, day boundaries      // never dropped
  drop order when crowded: minor, then hour, then day  // day is last
```

**Tokens, not values.** Handing over hex values guarantees drift the first time a token changes. The mapping table gives slot names, which is also what makes E11-T04's "no hard-coded colours" check pass.

**The walkthrough's real purpose** is to surface the questions nobody knew they had. Having an engineer attempt a real implementation task from the pack during the session is the fastest way to find what is missing, and it is a scenario in the acceptance criteria rather than a suggestion because it is the step most likely to be skipped.

## Test plan
- **Completeness check** against the surface × state × theme matrix; every cell has a specified treatment.
- **Buildability check**: the walkthrough exercise above, with any gap found fixed before sign-off.
- **Token check**: no hex values present as implementation instructions.
- **Key-map check**: matches E11-D07's reviewed map exactly.
- Open-question log at zero.

## Security notes
No security surface. The pack contains design artefacts and no credentials, and any screenshots used for illustration are taken from the **demo** environment with synthetic data — a handoff pack full of real account screenshots is an easy and permanent leak.

## Accessibility notes
The pack carries the accessibility contract into implementation, because a specification that omits it produces an implementation that omits it:
- The complete key map with **announcement text per action**.
- Focus treatment and focus order per surface.
- Target sizes, including the canvas-surrogate sizing rule (surrogates match visual targets, §6.1).
- Contrast values per token pair per theme.
- The non-colour-only encodings and their registered patterns.
- The reduced-motion variant per animated element.
- E11-D07's findings and their resolutions, so an engineer sees what was already considered and decided rather than re-deciding it.

## Performance notes
The pack flags the design decisions with frame-budget consequences — gridline count, label count, text quantity, any effect requiring an extra pass — so the engineer knows which parts of the spec are performance-sensitive and which are free. Where a treatment is expensive, the pack names the cheaper degradation-ladder fallback, so the engineer does not have to invent one under time pressure.

## Observability
Walkthrough recording and open-question log attached to the ticket; the pack is linked from every consuming engineering story so it is findable from the work rather than only from this ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).

title: Spike: fix the SDF glyph set and atlas size for the design font (O2)
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §16 tracks **open item O2 — "Exact SDF atlas size/glyph set for the chosen design-system font"** — owned by the chart-engine lead plus the design-system team, due at engine milestone M3. §3.7 assumes a 1024×1024 single-channel atlas costing ~40 ms to generate once per font/size-class, cached in IndexedDB. Both the size and the generation cost are *assumptions carried from research*, not measurements against the font E05 actually ships.

Getting this wrong is expensive in two directions: an atlas too small silently drops glyphs (footprint numbers render as blanks at the densest zoom, the exact place the product is most valuable), and an atlas too large costs GPU memory against the 600 MB per-instance budget and slows cold start against B9 (<=900 ms to first frame).

The spike answers it with numbers before E11-S11 implements the pipeline.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Take the final design-system font family/weights from `16-design-system-brief.md` as shipped by E05.
- Enumerate the required glyph set from real product surfaces, not guesses: digits, `.`, `,`, `-`, `+`, `%`, `×`, `K`, `M`, `B` (compact number formatting), `A`–`Z`, `a`–`z` for axis/legend labels, plus the currency/unit glyphs actually used by `CMP-188`/`CMP-189` tick formatters and the `(estimated)` label.
- Generate the SDF atlas at 512², 1024² and 2048² for each size class (`comfortable`/`compact`/`dense` per §5 rule 5) using the two-pass EDT (Felzenszwalb) described in §3.7.
- Measure per variant: generation wall time (cold), IndexedDB read time (warm), atlas bytes, glyph coverage (any dropped glyph is a hard fail), and rendered legibility at 11 px and at the LOD text-hiding threshold.
- Compare shelf packing against a skyline packer if 1024² overflows — only if it overflows.
- Produce a decision table and an amendment to **ADR-0002** recording the chosen atlas size, glyph set, size classes and packer.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the production pipeline, batching, or the outline shader variant — E11-S11.
- Multi-language/CJK glyph coverage: the product is English-only (`locale` default `'en-GB'`, §8) and CJK would change the strategy entirely; if that ever changes, a new spike is required.
- MSDF (multi-channel) — evaluate only if single-channel SDF fails legibility at 11 px; record the finding either way.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The question is answered with measurements
  Given the shipped design-system font and the enumerated glyph set
  When the atlas is generated at 512, 1024 and 2048 for all three density size classes
  Then a table records generation time, warm-load time, bytes and glyph coverage for each
  And a single (size, glyph set, packer) combination is recommended with its rationale

Scenario: Coverage is a hard gate
  Given a candidate atlas size
  When any required glyph fails to pack
  Then that size is rejected outright regardless of its timing numbers
  And the rejection is recorded in the table rather than silently dropped

Scenario: The decision is recorded where implementers will find it
  Given the spike concludes
  Then ADR-0002 carries an amendment naming the chosen atlas configuration
  And open item O2 in 26-chart-engine-design.md §16 is marked closed with a link to it
  And E11-S11 is updated with the chosen values before it enters a sprint
```

## Technical notes / design
**Timebox: 3 working days**, agreed with the Architect; not extendable without an Architect note on the ticket.

**Decision rule, stated up front:** choose the smallest atlas size that achieves 100 % glyph coverage for all three size classes with cold generation <=60 ms and warm IndexedDB load <=5 ms (the B9 secondary gate). If 1024² meets it, 1024² is chosen and no further work is done. If 1024² fails coverage, split into per-size-class atlases before going to 2048² — two 1024² atlases beat one 2048² on both memory and generation time. If single-channel SDF fails legibility at 11 px in a blind A/B with two designers, escalate to MSDF and record the memory cost (3× bytes).

Explicitly **not** production code: the prototype lives on `spike/chart-engine-sdf-atlas` and is left unmerged; only the measurements and the ADR amendment are the deliverables.

## Test plan
Not a test-bearing ticket. Evidence required for DoD: the measurement table, screenshots of rendered numbers at 11 px and at the LOD threshold for each candidate, and the raw benchmark script committed on the spike branch so the numbers are reproducible.

## Security notes
No security surface: fonts are bundled first-party assets, generation is local and deterministic. One note carried forward to E11-S11: the IndexedDB atlas cache is keyed by `(fontFamily, weight, hash(glyphSet))` — the hash must cover the glyph set so a changed set cannot silently load a stale atlas (a correctness issue that would look like a rendering bug, not a security one, but is fixed by the same control).

## Accessibility notes
Legibility is an accessibility outcome, not only an aesthetic one. The blind A/B legibility check includes a low-vision reviewer from the accessibility team, and the recommendation must state the minimum cell height at which per-cell text remains legible — that number becomes the LOD text-hiding threshold in E11-S12 and is quoted in `05-accessibility-standard.md`'s chart section.

## Performance notes
Feeds B9 (cold init to first frame <=900 ms, with "SDF atlas from cache <=5 ms" as the secondary gate) and the §7 memory line "SDF atlas 1024×1024×1 B = 1.0 MB". Any recommendation above 1024² must state the new memory figure against the 600 MB per-instance budget.

## Observability
None (spike). The production pipeline in E11-S11 adds `engine.text.atlas_generate_ms` and `engine.text.atlas_cache_hit`.

- [ ] Question answered with recorded evidence: the measurement table and legibility screenshots are attached to the ticket.
- [ ] Decision recorded as an amendment to `27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md`; open item O2 marked closed in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16.

title: Render via a dirty-flagged scene graph and budgeted frame scheduler
body:
## Context
The scene graph and the frame scheduler are the engine's heartbeat: every later feature is a node that gets traversed and a cost that has to fit in 16.6 ms. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.1 specifies a **deliberately shallow, fixed-depth** tree (`Chart -> Pane -> Layer -> Series`) "because depth costs traversal time per frame", and §3.2 specifies the loop with five binding rules: one rAF per chart instance, time-based animation, bounded work per frame, no allocation in the hot path, and render-on-demand parking.

The most important optimisation in the whole engine lives in §3.1's dirty-flag propagation: **a viewport change marks series `TRANSFORM`-dirty but not `DATA`-dirty**, so GPU buffers are reused and only uniforms change. Pan and zoom — the interactions a trader performs constantly — therefore cost almost nothing in buffer traffic. Getting this wrong is not a micro-optimisation miss; it is the difference between meeting budget #1 and not.

User value: this is the part of `US-CHART-001` and `US-CHART-006` that makes rendering smooth at all — the candle series itself ships in E12 against the seam built here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/scene/` — node contract per §3.1: every node has `id`, `visible`, `zIndex`, `dirty` flags (`DATA | LAYOUT | STYLE | TRANSFORM`) and implements `update(frameCtx)` and `collect(batchBuilder)`. **Nodes never issue GL calls**; they append to batches so the backend can sort by program then texture.
- Fixed tree exactly as §3.1: `Chart -> TimeAxis (shared)` + `Pane[0..n]` where each pane holds `PriceAxis` and the ordered layers `background`, `heatmap`, `series[]`, `overlays`, `drawings`, `foreground`. Layer order is fixed and not configurable — z-order within a layer is `zIndex`.
- Dirty-flag propagation rules: data update -> affected series `DATA`; viewport change -> all series `TRANSFORM` (never `DATA`); theme change -> `STYLE`; pane resize -> `LAYOUT`. Flags clear after a successful collect.
- `src/scene/FrameScheduler.ts`: 16.7 ms budget, priority classification, **bounded 4 ms/frame data-mutation drain** with the remainder deferred, time-based (`dt`) animation integration, and render-on-demand parking (no rAF scheduled when nothing is dirty and no animation is running).
- `src/scene/BatchBuilder.ts`: per-layer draw batches, reused across frames, patched by sub-range rather than rebuilt; output is an ordered draw list sorted by program then texture.
- `src/scene/LayoutEngine.ts`: pane rects, axis gutters, height ratios (`Pane.setHeightRatio`), recomputed only on `LAYOUT` dirty.
- Object pooling for all per-frame structures (`frameCtx`, batch entries, pick results) so the hot path allocates nothing.
- LOD step-down hook: when the frame is over budget for **3 consecutive frames**, the scheduler drops one LOD level and logs it (the policy itself is E11-S12; the trigger lives here).

## Out of scope
- GL/context work and actual draw submission — E11-S02 consumes the ordered draw list.
- Viewport maths, momentum and autoscale — E11-S03/S04. The scheduler integrates animations; it does not know what a price is.
- Concrete series, overlay or drawing nodes — E12/E13/E14/E18/E19/E21. This story ships the node contract plus a test-only `NullSeries`.
- LOD *thresholds* and decimation algorithms — E11-S12.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Panning reuses GPU buffers
  Given a chart with 100 000 bars and a static data feed
  When the viewport is panned continuously for 5 seconds
  Then every series is marked TRANSFORM-dirty and none is marked DATA-dirty
  And the count of bufferSubData calls recorded over the pan is zero

Scenario: The loop parks when there is nothing to do
  Given a mounted chart with no data arriving and no pointer interaction
  When 2 seconds elapse
  Then no requestAnimationFrame callback is scheduled after the last dirty frame
  And a single data message or pointer event resumes rendering on the next frame

Scenario: Data mutations are bounded, not dropped
  Given a burst of mutations that would cost 12 ms to apply in one frame
  When the scheduler drains the mutation queue
  Then at most 4 ms of mutations are applied in that frame and the rest are applied in following frames
  And no mutation is lost and ordering is preserved

Scenario: Animation is time-based, so dropped frames do not change the outcome
  Given a momentum animation is running
  When three frames are artificially dropped mid-animation
  Then the final resting viewport is identical (within 0.5 px) to an undropped run
  And no animation step uses a frame counter

Scenario: Sustained over-budget frames trigger a step-down
  Given the frame time exceeds 16.7 ms for 3 consecutive frames
  When the fourth frame is scheduled
  Then the scheduler requests one LOD level down and emits ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN with the stage timings
  And the step-down is visible in FrameStats.lodCandles

Scenario: The hot path allocates nothing
  Given the allocation-counter harness runs 600 frames of pan plus data updates
  When GC-triggering allocations in the frame path are counted
  Then the count is zero
```

## Technical notes / design
Traversal is a flat pre-order walk over a pre-linearised node array rebuilt only on `LAYOUT` dirty — pointer-chasing a tree every frame is exactly the cost §3.1 warns about.

`frameCtx` (pooled, one instance reused): `{ t, dt, viewport, theme, lod, budgetMsRemaining, stats }`. Nodes read it; they never mutate it except through `stats`.

Priority classification inside the budget, matching the stage allocation in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3: input (<=1 ms) -> data drain (<=4 ms, hard-clamped) -> layout if dirty (<=2 ms) -> collect/cull (<=2 ms) -> GL submit -> present. When `budgetMsRemaining` goes negative, optional work (non-focused pane redraw, bubble clustering) is deferred to the next frame in the §4.4 order; **trading-critical overlays are never deferred** — that constraint is encoded as a `critical: true` flag on the node and asserted by a test.

Parking: `scheduleIfDirty()` is the only entry point that calls `requestAnimationFrame`. A `wake()` is called by the data port, the input router and the sync-group broadcaster. Double-scheduling is prevented by a single `frameHandle`.

Step-down hysteresis lives in E11-S12 (±15 % dead band); the scheduler only counts consecutive over-budget frames and raises the request.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (Vitest, `TestClock` replacing rAF per §14): dirty-flag propagation matrix (data/viewport/theme/resize -> expected flags on each node kind); flags clear after collect; parking and wake-up; budget clamping of the mutation drain; deferral order under budget pressure; `critical` nodes never deferred.
- **Property** (fast-check, 10 000 cases): for any random sequence of dirty marks and frames, no node is collected while clean, and every marked node is collected within one frame of being marked (or deferred with its flag retained — never silently cleared).
- **Determinism**: `TestClock` + `SeededRandom` (§14) — a 600-frame scripted session produces an identical draw-call trace across runs; asserted via the GL backend's trace recorder (structural assertions are cheaper and more stable than pixels).
- **Allocation**: allocation-counter test over 600 frames, zero GC-triggering allocations in the frame path.
- **Perf**: contributes the scheduler slice to B1/B5; scheduler overhead itself <=0.3 ms/frame with 3 panes and 12 nodes.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
The DOM-mirror sync (E11-S13) is a first-class stage in the frame, budgeted at <=1 ms per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3, and it is **not** deferrable under budget pressure: §4.4 names "desyncing the DOM-mirror accessibility layer from what's visually rendered" as never acceptable. This story encodes that by marking the mirror-sync node `critical: true`, with a test asserting it is still executed on a frame where optional work is shed.

Reduced-motion: the scheduler exposes `prefersReducedMotion` in `frameCtx` so animated nodes can resolve instantly instead of easing; the honouring is per-node (E11-S04 for momentum).

## Performance notes
Directly owns budget #1 (<=16.6 ms p95) and budget #2 (30 fps floor). Stage instrumentation is added here so a regression is triaged by identifying the over-budget stage (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §9 profiling playbook) rather than re-profiling from scratch. Benchmarks touched: B1 (pan), B5 (combined), B6 (4 charts — validates the one-rAF-per-page rule holds when 4 instances share the worker).

## Observability
`Performance.mark()`/`measure()` spans at all nine §4.3 stage boundaries, emitted into `FrameStats` and surfaced by SCR-046. Stable codes: `ENGINE_FRAME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` (with per-stage timings), `ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN` (with from/to level). Counters: `engine.frame.deferred_mutations`, `engine.frame.parked_ms`.

title: Build the WebGL2 backend with capability probing and context-loss recovery
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.4 owns the GL backend: program/VAO/buffer/texture lifecycle, the atlas, and the state sorting that keeps draw calls at the §4 target of **<=18 per pane and <=40 for a 3-pane chart**. §1 requirement R9 mandates that the engine still runs when WebGL2 is unavailable, and requirement R8 (`32-risk-register.md` R8 Browser/GPU compat) is the risk this story carries: driver quirks, WebView2 differences, and GPU resets in the middle of a trading session.

Context loss is not hypothetical — a driver reset, a laptop switching GPUs, or a browser reclaiming memory all trigger it, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 makes recovery an **R1 exit criterion (#8)**: "forcing `WEBGL_lose_context` restores a fully correct scene within 2 s with no data loss". Because the `DataModel` lives in the worker and is independent of GL, recovery is a rebuild of GPU state from CPU state — which is only true if nothing in the engine treats a GL object as the source of truth. This story enforces that.

The user-visible half is **SCR-048**: "Graphics context lost — restoring…", auto-retry ×3 then a manual Retry plus a link to SCR-118 renderer settings.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/gl/GLBackend.ts`: context acquisition with the E10-tuned attributes (`{ alpha: false, antialias: false, depth: false, stencil: false, powerPreference: 'high-performance', preserveDrawingBuffer: false, desynchronized: true }`), program compilation/caching, VAO and buffer lifecycle, texture and LUT management, draw-list submission sorted by program then texture.
- Shader programs required by §4 for this Epic's layers: `line` (grid, sessions, crosshair, indicator lines — thick-line expansion in the vertex shader from per-instance `p0`,`p1`,`width`, dash pattern index), `quad`, `sdf-text` (E11-S11 supplies the atlas), and a `bar`/`cell` program stub registered for E18/E19 to implement against.
- **Capability probe** run at `init`, producing the `ready` capability report and selecting `RenderProfile`: `full` (WebGL2 + required extensions + adequate `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`), `reduced` (WebGL2 but constrained limits — smaller atlas, fewer instanced attributes), `degraded-2d` (no WebGL2 — handled by E11-T05).
- Context-loss handling: listen for `webglcontextlost` (call `preventDefault()`), tear down GPU-side state only, emit `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST` with `recoverable: true`, and on `webglcontextrestored` rebuild programs, buffers, VAOs, textures and the atlas from CPU state within 2 s. Auto-retry ×3 with 1/2/4 s backoff, then `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED` and the manual-retry path of SCR-048.
- A **GL-object ownership rule** enforced by review and by a test: no subsystem may hold a GL handle across frames except via the backend's registry, so recovery can invalidate and recreate everything centrally.
- Draw-call trace recorder (`§14` determinism aid): an opt-in mode recording the ordered draw list for structural test assertions.
- Error code table owned here: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_SHADER_COMPILE_FAILED`.

## Out of scope
- The Canvas-2D rendering path itself — E11-T05 (this story selects the profile and hands off).
- The SDF atlas generation pipeline — E11-S11 (this story consumes an atlas texture).
- Heatmap texture streaming (`texSubImage2D` rolling ring) — E21; the texture-management seam is provided here.
- WebGPU backend — explicit future seam only, per §3.4 non-goals.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Context loss recovers within the R1 exit budget
  Given a chart with 100 000 bars, 3 panes and an active crosshair
  When WEBGL_lose_context is forced
  Then SCR-048 shows "Graphics context lost — restoring…" in a role="alert" region
  And a fully correct scene is restored within 2 s, verified by a golden image matching the pre-loss frame at <=0.1 % pixel diff
  And no bar, cell or drawing is lost from the DataModel

Scenario: Repeated loss gives up gracefully rather than looping
  Given context restoration fails three consecutive times
  When the third retry completes
  Then ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED is emitted and SCR-048 shows a manual Retry plus a link to SCR-118
  And the render loop is parked rather than spinning

Scenario: Capability probing selects a profile instead of crashing
  Given a runtime reporting WebGL2 with MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE below the atlas requirement
  When the chart initialises
  Then RenderProfile "reduced" is selected, reported in the ready message, and shown in SCR-046
  And the user is told which capabilities are reduced and why — never shown a blank canvas

Scenario: Draw calls stay within the architectural budget
  Given a 3-pane chart rendering grid, candles, indicator lines and a crosshair
  When the draw-call trace for one frame is inspected
  Then there are <=18 draw calls for any single pane and <=40 for the chart
  And the list is ordered so that program switches are minimised

Scenario: A shader that fails to compile is a handled error
  Given a shader source that fails to compile on a specific driver
  When the backend initialises
  Then ENGINE_SHADER_COMPILE_FAILED is emitted with the driver info string and the program name
  And the engine falls back to degraded-2d rather than rendering a blank canvas
```

## Technical notes / design
Context attributes are tuned deliberately: `antialias: false` because candle geometry is device-pixel-snapped (E11-S10) and MSAA costs fill rate for no benefit here; `depth: false`/`stencil: false` because ordering is done by layer and draw order; `desynchronized: true` to shave a frame of latency for budget #6 (input-to-photon <=2 frames).

Thick-line expansion in the vertex shader (§3.10): per-instance `p0`, `p1`, `width`, `dashPatternIdx`; the quad is expanded along the segment normal in clip space with a per-vertex sign attribute. No geometry shader (WebGL2 has none) and no CPU-side triangulation.

Precision: prices arrive as integer ticks; `priceOrigin` is a **uniform** subtracted in the vertex shader before the float conversion (E11-S03 owns the maths). Passing absolute BTC-magnitude prices as `float` attributes is the classic precision bug this avoids.

Recovery algorithm: on `webglcontextrestored`, walk the backend's resource registry and recreate in dependency order — programs -> LUT textures -> SDF atlas (from IndexedDB cache, <=5 ms) -> static buffers -> per-series dynamic buffers repopulated from the `DataModel` by marking every node `DATA`-dirty. The scene graph is untouched; only GPU mirrors are rebuilt.

State sorting: batches carry `(programId, textureId, layerIndex)`; submission sorts by `layerIndex` first (correctness — layers must composite in order) then by `programId`, then `textureId` within the layer.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: resource registry lifecycle (create/invalidate/recreate); draw-list sort stability; capability-probe decision matrix over synthetic `getParameter` responses (WebGL2 absent / limits low / all good / extension missing).
- **Robustness** (§14 fuzz layer, required check): injected context loss at 50 random points in a scripted session — including mid-`bufferSubData`, mid-atlas-upload and during a resize — must always recover or report, never hang; zero-size canvas; DPR change mid-flight.
- **Golden image** (Playwright + SwiftShader, <=0.1 % diff): pre-loss vs post-restore frame equality; grid + crosshair + line rendering per theme.
- **Contract**: draw-call trace assertions for the <=18/pane and <=40/chart budgets.
- **Cross-shell** (§14): the loss/recovery test runs in browser Chromium, Electron, and (while ADR-0011 is open) Tauri/WebView2; results reported per release.
- **E2E**: SCR-048 alert copy, correlation id selectability, retry button focusability.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data. Threats handled here:
- **Tampering / supply chain**: shader sources are static, bundled, first-party strings. There is **no dynamic shader construction from data** and no `eval` — a data-driven shader string would be a code-injection vector through the market feed. A lint rule forbids template-literal shader sources containing interpolation of non-constant values.
- **Denial of service**: a driver-level GPU hang cannot be prevented from JS, but the retry policy is bounded (3 attempts, exponential backoff) so a failing GPU degrades to `degraded-2d` instead of spinning the render loop and heating the machine — `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-048 states explicitly that "failures never spin the render loop".
- **Information disclosure**: the capability report includes `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` (GPU vendor/model) for diagnostics. This is fingerprinting-adjacent data; it is shown only in SCR-046 (owner/developer overlay, hidden by default per its catalogue entry) and included in copied diagnostics with an explicit note, never sent to any third party.
Requires the `security` label; covered by E11-X01's STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-048's contract is implemented against here: `role="alert"` region with plain-language text ("Graphics context lost — restoring…"), a **selectable** correlation id as text, and a focusable Retry button that is not colour-only. The reduced/degraded profile must be communicated in words ("Reduced detail: footprint text hidden below 6 px cells" per SCR-030's low-GPU state), never by appearance alone. During recovery, focus must not be stolen from wherever the user had it; the alert announces without moving focus.

## Performance notes
Owns the "composite + present" (<=1.6 ms) and draw-submission slices of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3, and the §4 draw-call targets. Benchmarks: B1 (draw calls <=8 for pure candles), B5 (total <=40), B9 (cold init to first frame <=900 ms — program compilation is the dominant term, so programs are compiled lazily per layer actually used, and compilation time is recorded). Recovery must complete <=2 s (R1 exit criterion 8), measured as an explicit benchmark, not by eye.

## Observability
Codes: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_SHADER_COMPILE_FAILED`, each with `recoverable`. `FrameStats` gains `drawCalls`, `triangles`, `gpuMemoryMbEstimate`, `renderProfile`. Counters: `engine.gl.context_losses`, `engine.gl.restore_ms`, `engine.gl.program_compile_ms{program}`. `chart.error_shown {code, correlationId}` is emitted by the app layer from these events (SCR-048 analytics).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S01** — the ordered draw list and the layer model.
- **E10** — Electron GPU flags and CSP; the renderer must already be launched with the flag set chosen in E06.
- Blocks **E11-S03** (uniforms), **E11-S10** (DPI/backing store), **E11-S11** (atlas texture), **E11-T05** (degraded-2d), **E21** (heatmap texture streaming).

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-gl-backend` · 3 PRs (context + resource registry; programs + draw submission; capability probe + loss recovery). Shader files are excluded from the <=400 LOC count but reviewed by the code owner. Pairing rule applies (R10).
