title: Project time and price to screen through one shared, tick-precise transform
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-007`'s NFR states the rule this story exists to enforce: **"projection is a single shared function used by every renderer, covered by unit tests"**. Every candle, cell, drawing, order line, profile row and axis tick must agree on where a price is, or overlays drift against the data they annotate — a class of bug that is invisible in code review and obvious to a trader.

`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.5 specifies the maths: viewport state `{timeStart, timeEnd}` in µs float64 plus per-pane `{priceLow, priceHigh}` and a scale mode; screen mapping computed on the CPU into uniforms once per pane per frame. It also fixes the **bar-space vs time-space** distinction that every trading chart needs: panning and bar spacing operate in bar-index space (`barSpacing` px/bar, `rightOffset` in bars) while overlays needing true time (heatmap columns, session shading) map through `time`, with `BarStore` keeping a monotone index->time map.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/viewport/Viewport.ts` — state `{ timeStart, timeEnd }` (µs, float64), per-pane `{ priceLow, priceHigh, scaleMode }`, `barSpacing`, `rightOffset`.
- The single projection module `src/viewport/transform.ts` exporting `indexToScreen`, `timeToScreen`, `priceToScreen`, `screenToIndex`, `screenToPrice`, `screenToTime` — used by **every** renderer and by hit-testing, with no second implementation anywhere in the codebase (enforced by a lint rule forbidding arithmetic on `priceLow`/`priceHigh` outside this module).
- Linear mapping per §3.5: `sx = (t - timeOrigin) * kx + bx` with `kx = plotWidth / (timeEnd - timeStart)`; `sy = (p - priceOrigin) * ky + by` with `ky = -plotHeight / (priceHigh - priceLow)`.
- Tick-integer precision: prices are integer ticks; `priceOrigin` is subtracted before the float conversion and passed to shaders as a uniform, so GPU-side floats never carry BTC-magnitude values.
- Uniform block assembly: one CPU-side computation per pane per frame feeding the GL uniforms, so a pan is a uniform update and not a buffer update (the §3.1 dirty-flag contract).
- `barSpacing` clamped to `[0.05, 200]` px; `rightOffset` clamped so the last bar cannot be panned entirely off-screen.
- Cursor-anchored zoom primitive: `zoomAt(anchorPx, factor)` keeping the world coordinate under the anchor invariant (used by E11-S04 for wheel and pinch).

## Out of scope
- Log/percent/inverted scale modes and autoscale — E11-S05 (they plug into this module as alternative `priceToScreen` implementations).
- Input handling, momentum and gesture recognition — E11-S04.
- Axis tick generation and label formatting — E11-S06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Round-trips are exact
  Given any viewport and any bar index within the loaded range
  When screenToIndex(indexToScreen(i)) is evaluated
  Then the result equals i for all 10 000 property-test cases
  And the same holds for screenToPrice(priceToScreen(p)) within half a tick

Scenario: One projection serves every renderer
  Given the codebase is scanned by the projection lint rule
  When any module other than viewport/transform.ts performs arithmetic on priceLow/priceHigh
  Then the build fails naming the offending module and the US-CHART-007 NFR

Scenario: Zoom keeps the point under the cursor fixed
  Given the cursor is over the bar at 2026-11-24T12:00:00Z at x = 640 px
  When zoomAt(640, 1.25) is applied
  Then that bar's time still maps to x = 640 px (±0.5 px)
  And barSpacing is clamped into [0.05, 200]

Scenario: Prices keep sub-tick precision at BTC magnitudes
  Given a symbol with tickSize 0.5 and prices around 64 000
  When a bar's high and a drawing anchored to it are both projected
  Then their screen y values differ by less than 0.5 px
  And no float32 value in the pipeline ever holds the absolute price

Scenario: Panning does not touch GPU buffers
  Given a viewport change of 200 px
  When the next frame is built
  Then only uniforms are updated and bufferSubData is not called
```

## Technical notes / design
Keep `time` in float64 microseconds everywhere on the CPU (float32 µs epoch loses ~minutes of precision). Only the *relative* values reach the GPU.

Bar-space is authoritative for panning: `timeStart/timeEnd` are derived from `(firstVisibleIndex, barSpacing, plotWidth)` via the store's index->time map, not the other way round — this is why bar spacing stays exact while time gaps (maintenance windows, thin liquidity) do not stretch bars. Overlays that are genuinely time-anchored (heatmap columns, session bands) use `timeToScreen`, which interpolates through the same monotone map.

`screenToIndex` is O(1) analytic (`floor((x - bx) / barSpacing) + firstVisibleIndex`); `screenToTime` is O(log n) through the index->time binary search. Hit-testing (E11-S08) relies on the O(1) path for its budget.

Clamping is applied in the setter, not the getter, so the viewport never holds an out-of-range value that a renderer could observe.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: mapping against hand-computed values for a fixed viewport; clamping at both `barSpacing` bounds; `rightOffset` limit; `zoomAt` anchor invariance at the left edge, centre and right edge; degenerate cases (`priceHigh === priceLow`, zero-width plot, single bar).
- **Property** (fast-check, must hold over 10 000 cases per §14): `screenToIndex(indexToScreen(i)) === i`; `priceToScreen` monotone decreasing in price; projecting then unprojecting a price is within half a tick; zoom anchor invariance for random anchors and factors in `[0.1, 10]`.
- **Integration**: a candle, a drawing anchored to its high, and an axis tick at the same price all render within 0.5 px in a golden image.
- **Perf**: transform computation <=0.05 ms per pane per frame; part of the <=2 ms "data-window recompute" stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3.
- Coverage >=90 % (pure maths; cheap to cover, catastrophic to get wrong).

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
The transform is what lets the DOM mirror place surrogate nodes exactly over the canvas region they represent — `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 requires the surrogate to be "sized to match the visual target for pointer users using it too", which simultaneously satisfies target-size and focus-visible rules. E11-S13 calls `indexToScreen`/`priceToScreen` for that placement, so a transform bug is an a11y bug; the golden-image test above includes a mirror-node bounding-box assertion.

## Performance notes
Serves budget #1. Because a pan is a uniform update rather than a buffer update, this story is the single largest contributor to B1 (100k candles, continuous pan at 1000 px/s, p95 <=12 ms, draw calls <=8). A regression here shows up as `bufferSubData` traffic during pan, which the B1 secondary gate catches directly.

## Observability
`viewport` worker->main message (<=1/frame) carrying `{ timeStart, timeEnd, priceLow, priceHigh, barSpacing }` — consumed by sync groups (E11-S09), the a11y layer and SCR-046. No new error codes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S02** — uniforms are delivered through the GL backend's program interface.
- **E11-T03** — the monotone index->time map lives on `BarStore`.
- Blocks **E11-S04**, **E11-S05**, **E11-S06**, **E11-S08**, **E11-S12**, and every renderer in E12+.

## Branch

## References

title: Render all chart text from an SDF glyph atlas with instanced, batched draws
body:
## Context
Footprint cells are the densest text surface in the product — 2,500 visible cells with two numbers each, roughly **12,500 glyphs per frame** — and `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.7 therefore makes text a first-class engine subsystem rather than a convenience. Canvas 2D `fillText` cannot reach that density at 60 fps, and per-glyph textured quads blow the draw-call budget.

The answer is a signed-distance-field atlas: glyphs are rasterised once from the design-system font, converted to an 8-bit SDF, packed into a 1024×1024 atlas and drawn as a **single instanced draw call per batch**, crisp at any scale with an optional outline pass that keeps numbers legible over saturated cell fills.

E11-K01 closes open item **O2** (exact glyph set and atlas size for the chosen design-system font) and hands this Story a measured, fixed answer rather than a guess.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/text/SdfGenerator.ts` — rasterise the glyph set to an offscreen 2D canvas, then a **two-pass Felzenszwalb EDT** to produce the signed distance field; 8-bit single channel.
- `src/text/ShelfPacker.ts` — shelf packing into a 1024×1024 atlas (size confirmed by E11-K01), emitting a `uvRect` per glyph plus per-glyph metrics (advance, bearing, size).
- Glyph set per §3.7: digits, `.` `,` `-` `+` `%` `×` `K` `M` `B`, and `A`–`Z` / `a`–`z` for labels — the exact final set is E11-K01's output.
- **IndexedDB cache** keyed by `(fontFamily, weight, sizeClass, hash(glyphSet))`; generation costs ~40 ms once, cached launches are instant (benchmark **B9** gates "SDF atlas from cache <=5 ms").
- `src/text/TextBatcher.ts` — instanced rendering with per-instance attributes `vec2 posPx`, `vec2 sizePx`, `vec4 uvRect`, `vec4 colour`; one draw call per batch.
- Fragment shader: `alpha = smoothstep(0.5 - w, 0.5 + w, sdf)` with `w = fwidth(sdf)`; optional **outline variant** at a second threshold for legibility over saturated fills.
- **Pre-computed glyph runs**: numbers are formatted on data update and cached as offsets into the atlas — never formatted per frame. A format change (e.g. compact `1.2K`) invalidates only the run cache.
- Batch budget: all cell text in a pane is one draw call, axis labels a second, drawing labels a third; **target <=6 text draw calls per pane per frame**.
- `degraded-2d` fallback path: Canvas 2D `fillText`, with footprint limited to L2/L3 (implemented in E11-T05, seam provided here).

## Out of scope
- The footprint cell renderer itself and its number semantics — **E18**. This Story ships the text machinery those cells draw with.
- Rich text, bidirectional text, CJK or emoji — the glyph set is Latin + symbols by design; a future non-Latin need is a new spike, not a silent widening.
- DOM tooltips and legends (CMP-197, CMP-199) — those are real DOM and use real fonts.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dense cell text renders within its measured budget
  Given a pane containing 2,500 footprint-style cells with two numbers each (~12,500 glyphs)
  When a frame is rendered
  Then all cell text is emitted in a single instanced draw call
  And CPU batching costs <= 2.0 ms total, meeting the B3 secondary gate

Scenario: Text stays crisp at every scale
  Given the same label is rendered at font size class 0, 1 and 2 and at devicePixelRatio 1, 1.25 and 2
  When the golden images are compared with the reference
  Then each differs by <= 0.1 % of pixels with no visible blur or aliasing fringe

Scenario: Atlas generation is cached across launches
  Given the atlas for the design-system font has been generated once
  When the application is relaunched
  Then the atlas is restored from IndexedDB in <= 5 ms
  And benchmark B9 cold-init-to-first-frame stays <= 900 ms

Scenario: Numbers stay legible over saturated fills
  Given a cell filled with the most saturated colour in the delta ramp
  When its numbers are drawn with the outline variant
  Then the text meets a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against that fill
  And the check is automated over every LUT endpoint, not spot-checked

Scenario: A corrupt cached atlas is detected and regenerated
  Given the IndexedDB-cached atlas fails its stored checksum
  When the engine initialises
  Then the cache entry is discarded and the atlas is regenerated from the font
  And ENGINE_ATLAS_CACHE_INVALID is logged once, with no visible text corruption

Scenario: Formatting is not per-frame work
  Given a static viewport of formatted cells
  When 60 consecutive frames are rendered
  Then zero number-to-string formatting calls occur in the frame path
  And the allocation counter reports zero allocations in that path
```

## Technical notes / design
**EDT.** Felzenszwalb's exact Euclidean distance transform is O(n) per row/column: run it over the inside set and the outside set, subtract, normalise to `[0,255]` with a spread of 4 px (the spread is what allows the outline pass; it is a stored atlas property, not a magic number in the shader).

**Shader** (fragment, single channel atlas):

```glsl
float d = texture(uAtlas, vUv).r;
float w = fwidth(d);
float a = smoothstep(0.5 - w, 0.5 + w, d);
// outline variant: a second, wider threshold composited underneath
float ao = smoothstep(0.5 - uOutline - w, 0.5 - uOutline + w, d);
outColor = mix(vec4(uOutlineColor.rgb, ao * uOutlineColor.a), vColor, a);
```

**Glyph runs.** A run is `{ atlasIds: Uint16Array, advances: Float32Array }` computed when the underlying value changes. The frame path walks runs and writes instance attributes into a pre-allocated `Float32Array` — no string work, no allocation.

**Cache integrity.** The IndexedDB record stores `{ atlasBytes, metrics, checksum }` where `checksum` is a FNV-1a hash of `atlasBytes`; a mismatch (corruption, a partially-written record, a tampered origin store) discards the entry and regenerates. This is also the Tampering control named in the STRIDE model (E11-X01).

**Size classes.** Three classes (small/medium/large) matched to the density modes of E11-T04; a DPR change (E11-S10) re-selects the class, which may trigger a regeneration — hence the cache key includes `sizeClass`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: EDT correctness against a brute-force reference on small bitmaps; shelf packer produces non-overlapping rects and reports occupancy; glyph-run construction and invalidation on format change; cache key derivation; checksum rejection.
- **Property** (fast-check): for random strings from the glyph set, run advances sum to the measured string width within 0.5 px.
- **Golden image**: every glyph at each size class, at dpr 1/1.25/2, plus the outline variant over the LUT endpoints.
- **Contrast test**: automated over all LUT endpoint fills with the outline variant, asserting >=4.5:1.
- **Perf**: B3's text sub-gate (batching <=2.0 ms, <=2 text draw calls) and B9's cached-atlas <=5 ms.
- **Allocation**: zero allocations and zero `toFixed`/template-literal calls in the frame path over 60 frames.
- **Robustness**: corrupt cache entry; IndexedDB unavailable (private mode) must fall back to in-memory generation, never fail the chart.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only**; the atlas contains rendered glyph shapes, no user content.

Residual STRIDE surface (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — the SDF atlas is cached in IndexedDB, which is same-origin-writable, so a poisoned entry could in principle render misleading numbers (a "9" drawn as a "0" is a *trading-relevant* integrity failure, not a cosmetic one). Control: the stored checksum is verified before use and any mismatch forces regeneration from the font. **Denial of service** — atlas generation is bounded by a fixed glyph set and a fixed 1024×1024 atlas, so no input can make it allocate unboundedly.

No `eval`, no dynamic shader source: the shader is a compile-time string constant and glyph data only ever becomes texture bytes and numeric attributes. `security` label applies (cache integrity), reviewed under E11-X03.

## Accessibility notes
- Text crispness is a direct **low-vision** requirement; SDF rendering is what makes the smallest legible size class actually legible.
- The **outline variant exists for contrast**, not decoration: it is the mechanism by which numbers over saturated delta fills meet 4.5:1, and the automated contrast test above is the proof.
- Text rendered into the canvas is invisible to assistive technology by construction — every number drawn here must also exist in the DOM mirror (E11-S13) and the SCR-045 table (E11-S14). This Story does not create an accessible surface; it must not be mistaken for one.
- Minimum legible cell-text height (>=11 px per §3.6) is the threshold at which E11-S12 degrades footprint text to colour-only, and it is defined here.

## Performance notes
Gate **B3** text sub-budget: <=2.0 ms CPU batching and <=2 text draw calls for the 12,500-glyph case; measured ~0.9 ms CPU / ~0.4 ms GPU on the reference machine, so the gate has headroom by design. Gate **B9**: cached atlas <=5 ms within a <=900 ms cold-init budget. Atlas memory 1024×1024×1 B = **1.0 MB** of the ~116 MB per-instance model (§7). Target <=6 text draw calls per pane per frame.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.text.glyphs_per_frame`, `engine.text.draw_calls`, `engine.text.batch_ms`, `engine.atlas.occupancy_pct`, `engine.atlas.cache_hit`. Errors: `ENGINE_ATLAS_CACHE_INVALID`, `ENGINE_ATLAS_GENERATION_FAILED` (the latter falls back to `degraded-2d` text rather than failing the chart). Atlas generation time logged once per launch.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-K01** — closes open item O2: the exact glyph set and atlas size for the design-system font. Without it this Story would guess at the atlas budget.
- **E11-S03** — the transform that positions text in world space.
- **E11-S10** — DPR/size-class re-selection.
- **E05** — the design-system font choice and type scale that fix the glyph set and the three size classes. (Runtime theme/density switching arrives with **E11-T04** in Sprint 06; this Story reads the font metrics directly, so it does not wait on it.)
- Blocks **E11-S06** (axis labels), **E18** (footprint cell text), **E19**/**E21** (profile and heatmap labels).

title: Create packages/chart-engine with the public API surface and thin React bindings
body:
## Context
Every later chart ticket compiles against this surface, so it is written **first and frozen early** (interface-first rule, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10). `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 already contains the complete TypeScript API sketch — `ChartOptions`, `Chart`, `Pane`, `SeriesType`, `SeriesOptionsMap`, `SeriesHandle`, `ChartEvents`, `FrameStats`, `RenderContext`, `SeriesPlugin`, `IndicatorPlugin` — this task transcribes it into a real package with compiling types and stub implementations, not new design.

`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16 makes the package **framework-free**: no React, no application store, no `fetch`/XHR/WS client, no Bybit-specific type. The React ergonomics shown in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 (`<Chart><Pane><CandleSeries/></Pane></Chart>`) live in `apps/web`, are deliberately thin, and are the only place where React and the engine meet. E12/E13/E14/E18/E21 all register through the seam created here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New workspace package `packages/chart-engine` (pnpm workspace member from E02), `"type": "module"`, ESM + types build via `tsup`, `sideEffects: false`, TS `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`.
- `src/index.ts` exporting exactly the §8 surface and nothing else: `ChartOptions`, `Chart`, `Pane`, `PriceScale`, `TimeScale`, `SeriesType`, `SeriesOptionsMap`, `SeriesDataMap`, `SeriesDeltaMap`, `SeriesHandle`, `OrderLine`, `ChartEvents`, `FrameStats`, `RenderContext`, `SeriesPlugin`, `OverlayPlugin`, `IndicatorPlugin`, `Unsubscribe`, `createChart(opts: ChartOptions): Chart`.
- Data shape types exactly as §8: `CandleData`, `FootprintData`, `HeatmapColumnData`, `FootprintOptions`, `HeatmapOptions` — prices as `Int32Array` ticks with `priceOrigin`/`tickSize`, times as `Float64Array` µs epoch.
- Stub `createChart` that mounts a canvas, fills it with `color.chart.background` and emits `frameStats`; real subsystems land in E11-S01/S02.
- `packages/chart-engine/README.md`: the package contract (framework-free, no I/O, transferable typed arrays in, pixels + events out) and a usage example.
- React bindings in `apps/web/src/chart/`: `<Chart>`, `<Pane>`, `useChartApi()`, `useCrosshair()`. Bindings own React lifecycle + option diffing only; they contain no rendering logic.
- CI boundary check: `eslint-plugin-import` `no-restricted-imports` + a `depcruise` rule failing the build if `packages/chart-engine` imports `react`, `react-dom`, any `apps/*` path, `fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest`/`WebSocket` usage, or any symbol whose name matches `/bybit/i`.
- `tsd` type tests asserting the exported surface is stable and that `packages/protocol` types are structurally assignable to the engine data shapes.

## Out of scope
- Any real rendering, scene graph, worker or GL code — E11-S01, E11-S02, E11-T02.
- Series/indicator/overlay plugin *implementations* — E12/E13/E14/E18/E19/E21. This task ships the interfaces only.
- Publishing the package to any registry; it is workspace-internal for the whole plan horizon.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The package builds and exports the designed surface
  Given packages/chart-engine is built with tsup and tsc --noEmit
  When the emitted .d.ts is compared against the API sketch in 26-chart-engine-design.md §8
  Then every named export in §8 exists with a matching signature
  And no symbol outside §8 is exported from the package root

Scenario: The framework-free boundary is enforced, not just documented
  Given a developer adds `import { useState } from "react"` inside packages/chart-engine
  When CI runs the boundary check
  Then the build fails naming the forbidden import and the rule (CONSTITUTION.md C-2.16)
  And the same happens for an import of fetch, WebSocket, or an apps/* path

Scenario: A chart mounts and reports frame stats through the stub
  Given createChart({ container, theme }) is called in apps/web
  When the component mounts
  Then a canvas sized to the container appears filled with color.chart.background
  And a frameStats event carrying renderProfile is delivered to the subscriber within 1 s

Scenario: Protocol types are assignable without adapters
  Given packages/protocol emits the generated WS payload types
  When the tsd contract test compiles
  Then a protocol BarsBatch payload is assignable to CandleData without a hand-written mapper
```

## Technical notes / design
Transcribe `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 verbatim; where the sketch is ambiguous, prefer the narrower type and record the choice in the README rather than widening the surface.

Precision rule (§3.3, non-negotiable and easy to get wrong): **prices are integer ticks** (`Int32Array`) relative to a per-symbol `priceOrigin`, never float prices. Float32 loses precision at BTC price magnitudes; the GL side subtracts `priceOrigin` in a uniform. Times are `Float64Array` microseconds since epoch.

`createChart` returns the facade object directly (no async) and resolves capability detection lazily so React bindings need no Suspense.

Directory layout, fixed here so later tickets do not relitigate it:
```
packages/chart-engine/
  src/index.ts        public surface only (re-exports)
  src/api/            facade: chart.ts, pane.ts, scales.ts
  src/scene/          (E11-S01)      src/gl/        (E11-S02)
  src/model/          (E11-T03)      src/worker/    (E11-T02)
  src/viewport/       (E11-S03)      src/text/      (E11-S11)
  src/interaction/    (E11-S04)      src/a11y/      (E11-S13)
  bench/              (E11-T06)      test/golden/   (E11-T08)
```

## Test plan
- **Unit** (Vitest): `createChart` mounts/disposes cleanly; `dispose()` is idempotent; `subscribe` returns a working `Unsubscribe`; option diffing in the React binding does not recreate the chart on an unrelated prop change.
- **Type/contract**: `tsd` assertions for each §8 export; `tsc --noEmit` across the workspace; a snapshot test of the emitted `.d.ts` public surface so an accidental export widening shows up in review.
- **Boundary**: a fixture file importing `react` is expected to fail lint; asserted in CI as a negative test.
- Coverage target >=85 % on the package (mostly type-level here; the stub paths are fully covered).

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
`getDomMirrorRoot(): HTMLElement` (CMP-180's a11y contract anchor) is part of the API from day one, and the visible-window/focused-unit query surface required by `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 is included in the frozen surface — it is an engine-design requirement, "not an afterthought bolted on later". The React binding renders the mirror root as a real DOM child of the container so focus can land in it.

## Performance notes
No runtime budget yet. Two structural budget guards: the package must tree-shake (`sideEffects: false`) and the initial engine chunk counts against budget #9 (<=8 MB gzipped initial bundle, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2) — record the stub's gzipped size as the baseline the later tickets are measured against.

## Observability
`frameStats` event shape wired end-to-end (even from the stub) so E11-T07's SCR-046 feed has a stable contract. Engine errors use the `ChartEvents["error"]` channel with stable string codes; the code table is owned by E11-S02.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E02** — pnpm workspace, TS config, lint/test tooling and the `import-linter`/dep-cruiser harness this task adds a contract to.
- **E06** — the spike's ADR must have confirmed the custom-engine path before the package exists.
- **E10** — `apps/web` and the Electron shell provide the mount point and theme provider the React bindings attach to.
- Blocks every other E11 ticket and all of E12/E13/E14/E18/E21.

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-package` · one PR, ~350 LOC (mostly type declarations) + config. Review by the `packages/chart-engine` code owner and the Architect (interface-first change).

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` — engine architecture (scene graph 3.1, render loop 3.2, data model 3.3, GL backend 3.4, viewport math 3.5, LOD 3.6, SDF text 3.7, heatmap streaming 3.8, hit-testing 3.9, interaction 3.11, plugin API 3.12, worker protocol 6, memory 7, API sketch 8, benchmarks 13, tests 14, milestones 15, open items 16)

title: Implement the OffscreenCanvas render worker, protocol and inline fallback
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 splits the engine across two threads and the split is the reason the frame budget is reachable: the main thread keeps React, DOM overlays, accessibility and input capture; **everything with a per-frame cost** — decode, model updates, culling, batching, GL calls — runs in a render worker against an `OffscreenCanvas`. Input is captured on the main thread, coalesced, and forwarded as compact messages so pan/zoom never waits on React.

§2 also mandates a **supported, tested** fallback: where `OffscreenCanvas` is unavailable (older WebView2), the identical worker code runs on the main thread behind the same facade as `RunMode.inline` — "only throughput changes, not behaviour". Shipping the fallback as an afterthought is how it rots, so it is built here with the worker.

§6 fixes the message tables in both directions; this task implements them exactly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/worker/render-worker.ts` — the worker entry, bundled same-origin (no `blob:` URL, so the Electron CSP from E10 needs no widening).
- `src/worker/host.ts` — the main-thread host: canvas `transferControlToOffscreen()`, worker lifecycle, message dispatch, backpressure, `terminate()` on `dispose()`.
- Main->worker messages per §6: `init` `{canvas, dpr, theme, chartConfig}`, `resize` `{width,height,dpr}` (debounced one frame), `input` `{kind: pointer|wheel|key|touch, coalesced[]}` (<=1/frame), `data` `{store, op: append|patch|prepend|replace, buffer}` (transferred, up to 20/s per store), `command` `{setViewport|setSeriesOptions|addDrawing|setTheme|setLod|pickAt|export}`, `sync` `{groupId, timeRange, crosshair}` (<=1/frame).
- Worker->main per §6: `ready` (capability report + selected `RenderProfile`), `frame` (`FrameStats`, sampled 1 Hz, full in bench mode), `pick` (edge-triggered), `viewport` (<=1/frame), `a11y` `{cursorSummary}`, `error` `{code,message,recoverable}`.
- `RunMode` selection: `'worker'` when `OffscreenCanvas` + `transferControlToOffscreen` exist, else `'inline'`; overridable via `ChartOptions.runMode` for tests. The inline path runs the *same* modules behind a synchronous message bus — no second implementation.
- **One rAF per worker**: N chart instances on a page share one worker and one rAF, rendering into their own canvases in sequence (§3.2 rule 1). The host registers/deregisters instances with the shared worker.
- Transferable discipline: every `data` message transfers its `ArrayBuffer`; a test asserts `buffer.byteLength === 0` on the sender afterwards (proof of zero-copy).
- Validation at the worker boundary: unknown message kind -> `error` with code `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, never a throw that kills the worker; buffer length must match the declared element count.
- Worker crash recovery: `onerror`/`onmessageerror` -> emit `error`, tear down, re-init from the retained `DataModel` snapshot request, max 3 attempts with 1/2/4 s backoff, then surface SCR-048.

## Out of scope
- The shared **WS client** worker that decodes wire frames (§9) — that is E17 plus the `apps/web` data layer. This task defines the port the decoded typed arrays arrive on; it never opens a socket.
- The `DataModel` stores the `data` messages mutate — E11-T03.
- GL work inside the worker — E11-S02.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rendering runs off the main thread
  Given a chart mounted in a browser supporting OffscreenCanvas
  When a 2 s artificial main-thread block is injected during a continuous pan
  Then the canvas keeps panning and rendering throughout the block
  And RunMode reported in the ready message is "worker"

Scenario: Inline fallback is behaviourally identical
  Given ChartOptions.runMode = "inline"
  When the interaction test suite for pan, zoom, crosshair and resize is run
  Then every assertion that passes in worker mode also passes in inline mode
  And the only permitted difference is throughput, recorded in the benchmark report

Scenario: Data buffers are transferred, never copied
  Given a 3.2 MB CandleData batch is handed to SeriesHandle.setData
  When the data message reaches the worker
  Then the sender's ArrayBuffer byteLength is 0
  And no structuredClone of the payload appears in a heap snapshot taken after the send

Scenario: A malformed message cannot kill the worker
  Given a message with kind "data", store "bars" and a buffer 3 bytes shorter than its declared element count
  When the worker processes it
  Then the message is rejected with an error event carrying code ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR and recoverable=true
  And the worker continues to render the previous frame contents

Scenario: Worker death is recovered
  Given the render worker is killed externally mid-session
  When the host observes the termination
  Then it re-initialises the worker and restores the scene within 2 s, retrying at most 3 times
  And if all retries fail, SCR-048 shows the error state with a copyable correlation id
```

## Technical notes / design
Message envelope (structured-cloneable, no JSON on the hot path):
```ts
type ToWorker =
  | { t: 'init'; id: ChartId; canvas: OffscreenCanvas; dpr: number; theme: ThemeLut; config: ChartConfig }
  | { t: 'resize'; id: ChartId; width: number; height: number; dpr: number }
  | { t: 'input'; id: ChartId; kind: 'pointer'|'wheel'|'key'|'touch'; events: Float32Array }
  | { t: 'data'; id: ChartId; store: StoreId; op: 'append'|'patch'|'prepend'|'replace'; layout: BufferLayout; buffer: ArrayBuffer }
  | { t: 'command'; id: ChartId; cmd: Command }
  | { t: 'sync'; groupId: string; timeRange: [number, number]; crosshair: number | null };
```
`input` events are packed into a `Float32Array` (`[type, x, y, buttons, modifiers, dt] × n`) rather than an object array — object-array cloning at 240 Hz trackpad rates was the measured cost the design is avoiding.

**Shared worker vs dedicated**: one *dedicated* worker per page shared by all chart instances (not a `SharedWorker`) — Electron renderer isolation makes `SharedWorker` lifetime awkward and the design only requires one rAF per page. The WS client separately uses a shared worker (E17), outside this scope.

Error codes owned here: `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, `ENGINE_WORKER_LOST`. Codes for GL failures are owned by E11-S02.

Backpressure: the host keeps at most 2 unacknowledged `data` messages per store; beyond that, `append` payloads are conflated (last-wins for `patch`/`replace`, concatenated for `append`) before sending. The feed is already conflated upstream, so this is a second guard, not the primary one.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (Vitest): message encode/decode round-trip for every kind in §6; conflation logic under a 3× overrun; length-mismatch rejection; `RunMode` selection matrix (OffscreenCanvas present/absent × explicit option).
- **Integration**: the whole interaction suite is parameterised over `runMode: ['worker','inline']` and must pass in both — this is what keeps the fallback honest.
- **Robustness/fuzz**: 10k randomly corrupted messages (truncated buffers, wrong store ids, NaN coordinates, unknown `t`) must produce zero unhandled rejections and zero worker terminations.
- **Perf**: B7 (live update storm, 20 msg/s × 6 stores) — decode + dispatch p95 <=4 ms, zero dropped messages.
- **E2E**: main-thread block test above, in Playwright and in the Electron driver.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data. Threats from `04-security-program.md` mapped to this boundary:
- **Tampering / memory safety**: the worker boundary is the engine's only untrusted-input surface. Every `data` message is validated before any typed-array view is created: declared element count × stride must equal `buffer.byteLength`, `store` must be a known id, and offsets must be within range. Failure yields a recoverable `error`, never an exception across the boundary.
- **Denial of service**: bounded queue depth (2 unacked per store) plus conflation; a hostile producer cannot grow the queue. `maxBars`/`memoryBudgetMb` ceilings are enforced downstream by E11-S15.
- **Supply chain / CSP**: the worker is bundled from a same-origin asset URL — no `blob:` worker, no `eval`, no data-derived code. This keeps the E10 Electron CSP strict (`worker-src 'self'`).
Requires the `security` label; reviewed as part of the E11-X01 STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
The `a11y` worker->main message (`{cursorSummary}`) is implemented here — it is the transport the live-region layer (E11-S13) consumes. Throttling to <=2 announcements/s (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2) is applied on the **main-thread** side, not the worker, so the worker never becomes the throttle authority. In `inline` mode announcements must arrive on exactly the same schedule; asserted by the shared interaction suite.

## Performance notes
Serves budget #1 directly: the main thread must stay free for React and the DOM mirror (<=1 ms of the 16.6 ms frame per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3). Targets: postMessage overhead <=0.2 ms per frame for the input batch; zero structured-clone of any data payload; B7 decode p95 <=4 ms. `inline` mode is expected to lose throughput and is exempted from B5/B6 gates but must still hold 30 fps on B1 — recorded, not gated.

## Observability
`frame` stats at 1 Hz (full rate in bench mode) carrying `renderProfile` and `runMode`. Counters: `engine.worker.messages_dropped`, `engine.worker.conflated`, `engine.worker.restarts`. `Performance.mark()` pairs around post->receive so the SCR-046 overlay can show the transport slice of the frame.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.

title: Implement columnar typed-array data stores with append/patch/prepend mutations
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 specifies the engine's data model as **columnar, typed-array based, append-optimised, with stable indices**. It is the M2 "data plane" milestone (§15) and the reason the memory budget in §7 closes at ~116 MB for the 100k-bar case against a 600 MB ceiling (requirement R7).

Stable indices matter beyond memory: drawings anchor to `barIndex` *and* `time` (§3.10), hit-testing computes bar index analytically (§3.9), and paging splices history at the front (`prependHistory`) without invalidating anything already on screen. A store that renumbers on mutation would break all three.

This task ships the stores and their mutation API. The series that read them ship in E12; the footprint/heatmap stores are declared here but only the bar store is exercised, because E18/E21 own their semantics.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/model/BarStore.ts` per §3.3: `time: Float64Array` (µs), `open/high/low/close: Int32Array` (ticks from `priceOrigin`), `volume/delta: Float32Array`, head/tail ring indices, capacity grown by doubling.
- `src/model/FootprintStore.ts`: parallel arrays sorted by `(barIndex, priceLevel)` — `barIndex: Uint32Array`, `priceLevel: Int32Array`, `bidVol/askVol: Float32Array`, `tradeCount: Uint16Array`, `offsets: Uint32Array` prefix sums mapping `barIndex -> first cell index`.
- `src/model/HeatmapRing.ts`: descriptor only (ring width 2048 columns × 512 price rows, `writeCol` cursor) — the texture itself is uploaded by E21.
- Mutation API returning **affected index ranges** so the batch builder can do `bufferSubData` on a sub-range instead of re-uploading: `append(data) -> {from,to}`, `patch(index, data) -> {from,to}`, `prepend(data) -> {from,to, indexShift}`, `replace(data) -> {from:0, to:n}`.
- `BarView` read facade (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 `IndicatorPlugin.compute`) giving bounds-checked, allocation-free access to a bar range.
- Index maps: monotone `index -> time` and a binary-search `time -> index` (`timeToIndex`, used by drawings and Go-to-date), both O(log n), both covered by property tests.
- Capacity policy: doubling growth up to `ChartOptions.maxBars` (default 200 000); at the ceiling, oldest bars are evicted from the front and `indexShift` is reported so anchors can be rebased.
- Snapshot/replace semantics (§9): a `replace` keeps the previous contents renderable until the new store is fully built, so there is **no blank flash**.

## Out of scope
- GPU buffer management and `bufferSubData` calls — E11-S02 consumes the returned ranges.
- Footprint and heatmap *semantics* (imbalance, price grouping, column cadence) — E18 and E21.
- Any fetching or paging policy — E11-S15 decides *when* to ask; this task only splices what arrives.
- Persistence: stores are in-memory only and are rebuilt from the backend on reload.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Appending a bar touches only the new range
  Given a BarStore holding 100 000 bars
  When append() adds one bar
  Then the returned range is {from: 100000, to: 100001}
  And no existing element is written and no reallocation occurs while capacity remains

Scenario: Prepending history preserves on-screen anchors
  Given a BarStore of 5 000 bars with a drawing anchored at barIndex 120 / time T
  When prependHistory splices 2 000 older bars
  Then indexShift is 2000 and timeToIndex(T) returns 2120
  And the drawing resolves to the same time and price as before the splice

Scenario: Prefix sums address footprint cells in O(1)
  Given a FootprintStore of 20 000 bars × up to 40 cells each
  When cells for bar 12 345 are requested
  Then they are returned as a subarray view between offsets[12345] and offsets[12346]
  And no copy is allocated

Scenario: Hostile values are rejected at the store boundary
  Given an append payload containing NaN in close and Infinity in volume
  When the mutation is applied
  Then the payload is rejected with ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR and the store is left byte-identical to before
  And a counter engine.model.rejected_mutations is incremented

Scenario: The bar ceiling evicts instead of growing without bound
  Given maxBars = 200000 and a full store
  When 1 000 more bars are appended
  Then the store still holds 200 000 bars, the oldest 1 000 are evicted
  And indexShift = 1000 is reported so every anchor can be rebased
```

## Technical notes / design
Precision (§3.3 note, the single most error-prone decision in the engine): OHLC are **integer ticks** in `Int32Array` relative to `priceOrigin`; float prices are never stored. Float32 at BTC magnitudes loses sub-tick precision, which shows up as candle wicks jittering during zoom.

Ring buffer: `head`/`tail` indices over a power-of-two capacity with masked indexing; logical index `i` maps to `(head + i) & (cap - 1)`. Growth doubles capacity and re-linearises (one copy, amortised O(1)). Eviction moves `head` — it never memmoves.

`prepend` cannot use the ring's front cheaply when capacity is tight, so it reallocates with the new bars leading, and returns `indexShift` so consumers rebase. Consumers that store indices (`drawings`, `hitIndex`, `picks`) subscribe to `indexShift` events; the design deliberately makes shifts explicit rather than hiding them.

Allocation discipline (§3.2 rule 4): mutations must not allocate in the hot path. Subarray views are cached per store; formatting caches are invalidated by range, not rebuilt. A dedicated allocation-counter test asserts zero GC-triggering allocations across a 1 000-mutation run.

Validation contract: `Number.isFinite` on every float column, `priceLevel` within `INT32` bounds, `time` monotonically non-decreasing for `append` (out-of-order -> reject and count, do not sort silently — silent sorting hides feed bugs).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ring wrap at capacity boundary; doubling growth; eviction with `indexShift`; prefix-sum construction and lookup; `timeToIndex` on exact/between/before/after; rejection matrix (NaN, Infinity, non-monotone time, length mismatch).
- **Property** (fast-check, must hold over 10 000 cases): for any random bar series and any sequence of append/patch/prepend, `timeToIndex(indexToTime(i)) === i`; the multiset of `(time, ohlcv)` after a prepend equals the union of the two inputs; `offsets` is non-decreasing and `offsets[n] === cellCount`.
- **Perf micro-bench**: 1 M appends <=120 ms; allocation-counter test asserting zero hot-path allocations.
- **Integration**: store + worker transport against a recorded fixture session — snapshot then deltas then a sequence-gap replace, asserting no blank frame.
- Coverage >=90 % (this is pure logic; the higher bar is cheap and the blast radius is the whole engine).

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data. This is the engine's **memory-safety chokepoint** — every hostile value entering from the decoder is stopped here.
- **Tampering**: bounds- and finiteness-validated before any indexed write; `priceLevel`/`barIndex` range-checked against the store's declared extent; a corrupt `offsets` array (non-monotone) is rejected wholesale rather than partially applied.
- **Denial of service**: `maxBars` and per-store byte ceilings cap allocation; growth is doubling-with-ceiling, never proportional to an attacker-declared length field. A declared element count larger than the ceiling is rejected before allocation, not after.
- **Information disclosure**: none — nothing here is persisted or logged beyond counters.
Requires the `security` label; covered by E11-X01 and by the fuzz corpus in E11-X02.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI surface — this ticket ships engine internals. Two binding constraints still apply from `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1, and the reviewer must check them:
- The public query surface for "current visible window + current focused unit" that the DOM mirror (E11-S13) consumes must exist and be frame-synchronous; it may not be bolted on later.
- Nothing here may make the DOM mirror unable to stay in sync with what is drawn (desync is called out explicitly as never acceptable in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4).

## Performance notes
Serves budget #7 (frontend memory) and the §7 memory table: BarStore 3.2 MB, FootprintStore 14.4 MB, glyph runs 9.6 MB for the 100k-bar/4 h case. Hard requirement: mutation application stays inside the **4 ms/frame** data-mutation drain of §3.2 rule 3 — anything not drained waits for the next frame. Micro-benchmarks recorded in the B7 report.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.model.rejected_mutations{reason}`, `engine.model.evictions`, `engine.model.reallocations`, `engine.model.bytes{store}`. `bytes` feeds the `gpuMemoryMbEstimate` field of `FrameStats` and hence SCR-046.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.

- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-T02** — stores live inside the render worker and are mutated by `data` messages.
- **E17** (via `packages/protocol`) — the decoded payload shapes the stores ingest.
- Blocks **E11-S15** (memory governor/paging), **E11-S08** (hit index), **E12** (series read these stores).

title: Build the STRIDE threat model for the chart engine and its data plane
body:
## Context
`04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per Epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes the kickoff a DoR item. E11 is an unusual case worth modelling carefully rather than dismissing: the engine holds **no secrets, performs no I/O and mutates no server state**, so three of STRIDE's six categories are genuinely out of band — and the temptation is to conclude there is nothing to model.

That would be wrong in a specific and important way. The engine is the component that **turns bytes off the wire into what a trader believes is true**, and it does so by indexing into typed arrays with values that came from those bytes. Its real threat surface is **tampering** (a corrupt or hostile frame producing an out-of-bounds read, or worse, a plausible-but-wrong chart) and **denial of service** (unbounded allocation from a declared length). Both have trading consequences rather than merely technical ones.

This model exists to make those two categories explicit, name their controls, and point at the tickets that implement them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Data-flow diagram** of the engine: WS shared worker -> `FeedDecoder` -> `DataModel` -> scene/cull/batch -> `GLBackend`; plus `InputRouter` -> worker, the IndexedDB atlas cache, the DOM mirror's write path, and the diagnostics snapshot's read path. Trust boundaries drawn explicitly: worker/main, origin/IndexedDB, engine/app.
- **STRIDE analysis per element and per flow**, with the out-of-band categories argued rather than assumed:
  - **Spoofing** — out of band: topic authorization and connection authentication belong to E17/E09; the engine receives already-authenticated frames. Recorded as transferred, with the owning Epic named.
  - **Tampering** — **in scope and primary**: malformed or hostile binary frames; out-of-bounds indices; `NaN`/`Infinity` poisoning the viewport; IndexedDB-cached SDF atlas poisoning (a "9" rendered as a "0" is a trading-relevant integrity failure); shader/asset supply chain.
  - **Repudiation** — not applicable: the engine mutates no state and takes no action; audit belongs to the OMS Epics.
  - **Information disclosure** — **in scope, narrow**: the SCR-046 diagnostics snapshot and error correlation ids are designed to be pasted publicly; the DOM mirror places market data into DOM.
  - **Denial of service** — **in scope and primary**: unbounded allocation from a declared length; pathological zoom or LOD causing allocation storms; worker starvation; GPU memory exhaustion.
  - **Elevation of privilege** — out of band at engine level, with one forward-looking note: the plugin seam is first-party-only in v1 and would need a sandbox before it could accept untrusted code.
- **Control mapping**: each in-scope threat mapped to a named control and the ticket implementing it — typed-array bounds and value validation (E11-T03), `maxBars`/`memoryBudgetMb` ceilings (E11-S15), atlas checksum verification (E11-S11), `textContent`-only DOM writes (E11-S13), diagnostics field allowlist (E11-T07), no `eval` / no data-derived shader source (E11-S02), CSP-compatible same-origin worker construction (E11-T02).
- **Residual-risk statement** with Owner sign-off for anything accepted.
- Model committed to `docs/plan/` and linked from the Epic.

## Out of scope
- WS authentication, authorization and topic access control — **E17** and **E09**.
- Backend threat models — those Epics' own models.
- Penetration testing — **E43**, before live enablement.
- Implementing the controls — the engineering tickets named above.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category has a reasoned disposition
  Given the six STRIDE categories
  When the model is reviewed
  Then each is either analysed with identified threats or argued as out of band with the owning component named
  And no category is omitted or dismissed without an argument

Scenario: Every in-scope threat has a named control and an implementing ticket
  Given the tampering, information-disclosure and denial-of-service threats
  When the control mapping is reviewed
  Then each threat names its control and the E11 ticket that implements it
  And any threat without a control is recorded as accepted risk with Owner sign-off

Scenario: The integrity argument is made explicitly
  Given that the engine renders what the user believes to be true
  When the tampering analysis is reviewed
  Then it distinguishes technical failures from integrity failures that produce a plausible but wrong chart
  And controls for the latter are named, not assumed to follow from the former

Scenario: Controls are verifiable, not aspirational
  Given each named control
  Then it is backed by a test, a scan rule or a documented manual check
  And a control that cannot be verified is recorded as such rather than counted as mitigation

Scenario: The model is reviewed before the controls are built
  Given the engineering tickets implementing the controls
  Then the model is complete before those tickets are executed
  And findings requiring new work are filed rather than folded silently into existing tickets
```

## Technical notes / design
**Method**: STRIDE-per-element over the data-flow diagram, following `04-security-program.md`, in a working session with the security engineer, the chart-engine lead and the Architect.

**The argument worth writing down carefully.** It is tempting to classify a rendering component as low-risk because it holds no secrets. The more useful framing is that the engine is an **integrity** component: its output is the basis for trading decisions, so a fault that produces a *plausible* wrong chart is more dangerous than one that crashes. A crash is loud and costs nothing but time; a wick silently dropped by a decimation bug, or a "9" rendered as a "0" by a poisoned glyph atlas, can cost money. This is why min/max-preserving decimation (E11-S12) and atlas checksum verification (E11-S11) are treated as security controls and not merely as correctness features.

**Trust boundary specifics.** The IndexedDB atlas cache is the least obvious boundary and the one most likely to be missed: it is same-origin-writable persistent storage whose contents become rendered glyphs. Any XSS elsewhere in the app, or any other same-origin code, can write it. The checksum is what stands between that and misrendered numbers.

**DoS reasoning.** The decoder must treat every length field as hostile until validated, because the cost of getting this wrong is not a slow chart but an unresponsive application during a trading session.

## Test plan
- Model completeness: every element and flow in the diagram analysed.
- Control verifiability: each control traced to a test, a scan rule or a documented manual check.
- Adversarial review: the security engineer attempts to identify a threat the model missed; the attempt and its outcome are recorded, so the model's coverage is evidenced rather than asserted.
- The model's DoS and tampering cases are handed to **E11-X03**'s abuse-case work and **E11-Q04**'s chaos charter as concrete inputs.

## Security notes
This ticket **is** the security analysis. Data classification for the whole Epic: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers, no financial records. That classification is what keeps the scope narrow and is stated at the top of the model so downstream reviewers do not have to re-derive it.

Controls inventory (each with an implementing ticket): typed-array bounds and value validation; `NaN`/`Infinity` rejection; hard `maxBars` and `memoryBudgetMb` ceilings enforced before allocation; SDF atlas checksum verification; `textContent`-only DOM writes; diagnostics-snapshot field allowlist; no `eval` and no dynamic shader source derived from data; same-origin bundled worker construction so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; pinned dependencies under npm audit and Dependabot.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the artefact. One intersection is recorded in the model: the DOM mirror (E11-S13) is where engine-rendered values become real DOM, making it the engine's only XSS-adjacent surface, and `textContent`-only writing is its control. The accessibility design review (E11-D07) independently noticed the same property, which is a useful cross-check rather than a duplication.

## Performance notes
The DoS analysis and the performance budgets are the same analysis viewed from two directions: the memory ceilings, the LOD degradation ladder and the frame-budget step-down are all simultaneously performance mechanisms and DoS mitigations. The model records this explicitly so that a future change relaxing a ceiling "for performance reasons" is understood to be weakening a security control.

## Observability
Threat model committed to `docs/plan/`. The error codes that indicate a control firing — `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE`, `ENGINE_ATLAS_CACHE_INVALID` — are identified in the model as **security-relevant telemetry**, so a spike in decode errors is recognised as a potential integrity signal rather than dismissed as feed noise.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Security artefacts (threat model, abuse cases, rule configuration, review notes) committed to `docs/plan/` or the security folder, and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Every identified threat has a disposition: mitigated (with the control named and its implementing ticket linked), accepted (with Owner sign-off recorded), or transferred.
- [ ] Controls verified by a test, a scan rule or a documented manual check - never by assertion alone.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scans green on the affected packages, or findings triaged with recorded justification.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted with date.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if the work surfaced a new risk or retired an existing one.
- [ ] Findings that require engineering work are filed as tickets with `priority/*` and an owner, not left inside the report.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S01** and **E11-T03** — the scene graph and data model whose flows are modelled; modelling before they exist would model a guess.
- **E11-T02** — the worker protocol boundary.
- Blocks **E11-X02** (scan rules derive from the identified threats) and **E11-X03** (abuse cases and the review).
- Feeds **E11-Q04**'s chaos charter.

## Branch

## References

- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 (data model), §6 (worker protocol), §7 (memory budgets)

title: Bar builders & series rendering (time/tick/volume/range/renko)
body:
## Context
CandleViewer does not trust the exchange to define what a bar is. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §2 states it plainly: "Exchange klines are a **cross-check and a cold-start backfill**, not the primary bar source: CandleViewer builds its own bars from trades (§3) so that time/tick/volume/range/delta/renko all share one code path." Every order-flow surface that follows in R2 — footprint (E18), profiles (E19), Deep-Stats (E20), CVD (E23) — is computed per bar, so the bar is the substrate of the whole product. If bars are wrong, everything downstream is wrong in a way no amount of rendering polish can hide.

This Epic delivers two halves that must agree exactly:

1. **Backend bar builders (module M8)** — the six `BarBuilder` implementations of `24-internal-schemas.md` §3 (time, tick, volume, range, delta, renko), each consuming `TradeEvent` only so that **live and replay produce byte-identical bars** (the tardis-machine property, §11 of the same document), plus `BarBuilderSet` multi-spec fan-out, `snapshot()`/`restore()` mid-bar resumption, the `bars_*` QuestDB tables of `21-database-schema.md` §4.8, the `/market/klines` and `/market/bars` REST endpoints of `22-api-openapi.yaml`, and the `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` WS topic of `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.
2. **Frontend series rendering (module M7, `packages/chart-engine`)** — candlestick, OHLC bar, line, area, baseline and Heikin-Ashi series drawn through the E11 chassis, the min/max-preserving LOD ladder of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6, forming-vs-closed bar semantics driven by the `confirm` flag, the volume column sub-pane, and symbol/timeframe/bar-mode switching that reuses the engine instead of tearing it down.

`30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 4 is the acceptance bar for the whole Epic: **"All five bar types produce identical results to a reference implementation on a recorded fixture day, byte-for-byte on OHLCV."** §13 places E12 on the critical path `E02 → E06 → E11 → E12 → E18 → E26 → E38 → E44 → E46 → GA`; §12 lists Renko and range bars as the second rung of the descoping ladder, so those two builders are deliberately scheduled last within the Epic and are the only cuttable scope.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Stories (US ids from `11-user-stories.md` domains CHART and MKT):**
- **US-MKT-008** Historical OHLCV backfill (Must) — paged `/v5/market/kline` backfill, cache-first paint, rate-limit backoff.
- **US-CHART-001** Candlestick rendering (Must) — the candle series itself and the deep-zoom LOD behaviour.
- **US-CHART-002** Alternative chart types (Should) — OHLC bars, line, area, baseline, Heikin-Ashi, volume column pane.
- **US-CHART-003** Order-flow bar modes (Must) — volume bars and tick bars from the shared ingestion path.
- **US-CHART-004** Range, Renko, delta bars (Should/Could) — P&F explicitly deferred out of this Epic.
- **US-CHART-005** Timeframe switching (Must) — standard ladder, sub-minute, custom intervals, no engine teardown.

(Chart chassis stories US-CHART-006/007/008/010/014 belong to **E11**, not here; US-CHART-012 templates belong to E15; US-CHART-013 overlays to E31.)

**Screens/components:** SCR-030 chart panel, SCR-041 symbol/interval quick-switcher, SCR-042 interval / bar-mode menu, SCR-047 chart empty / no-data state, SCR-151 empty-state pattern · CMP-219 SymbolPicker, CMP-220 IntervalPicker, CMP-221 ChartToolbar, CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle, CMP-226 BarCountdown, CMP-041 Menu, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-021 Skeleton, CMP-026 EmptyState.

**API/WS:** `GET /market/klines`, `GET /market/bars`, `GET /instruments` (consumed), WS topic `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` with `BarsBatch` payload kind 4.

**Tables:** QuestDB `bars_time`, `bars_tick`, `bars_volume`, `bars_range`, `bars_renko`, `bars_delta`; Postgres `chart_settings.bar_mode` (`21-database-schema.md` §1869–1909).

**Internal schemas:** `BarSpec`, `Bar`, `BarUpdate`, `BarBuilder`, `BuilderState`, `BarBuilderSet`, `BarSeries.densify()`.

## Out of scope
- Point & Figure bars (`pnf`) — the API and WS enums reserve the value; no builder ships in R1 (descoping-ladder rung 2 neighbourhood, Could-level in US-CHART-004).
- Footprint cells, profiles and Deep-Stats rows built *per bar* — E18/E19/E20.
- The indicator runtime that consumes bars — E13.
- The recorder that produces the trade tape the builders consume — E16.
- Chart chassis (scale math, pan/zoom, crosshair, axes, DOM-mirror a11y) — E11.
- Replay-driven bar construction — E26 reuses these builders unmodified; no replay-specific code here.
- Android/mobile clients — out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All bar types match the reference on a recorded fixture day
  Given the version-controlled BTCUSDT fixture day and a reference implementation
  When every builder (time, tick, volume, range, delta, renko) replays that day
  Then OHLCV is byte-identical to the reference for every bar of every spec
  And the total volume across bars equals the total traded volume (invariant BI-1)

Scenario: Live and replay agree
  Given the same trade sequence delivered live and then via replay
  Then the resulting Bar objects are identical including spec_hash (invariant BI-4)

Scenario: Switching bar mode does not tear down the engine
  Given a BTCUSDT chart on 5m time bars with drawings and indicators applied
  When I switch to "volume bars, 1500"
  Then the same engine instance re-binds to the new series within 200 ms of data arrival
  And drawings remain anchored by timestamp, and no WebGL context is recreated

Scenario: History is shallower than the requested window
  Given the recorder holds only 3 days of prints for the symbol
  When a tick-bar series is requested over 30 days
  Then bars are built for the available window only
  And an explicit partial-history marker names the timestamp where tick data begins
  And no REST klines are silently substituted for the missing tick-accurate region
```

## Technical notes / design
- Builders live in the backend (`M8`), never in the browser: `US-CHART-003` NFR requires one shared construction path for live and replay. The frontend receives `Bar` rows over REST/WS and renders them; the only client-side transform permitted is Heikin-Ashi (US-CHART-002 explicitly requires it client-side with no refetch).
- `spec_hash` (sha256 of canonical `BarSpec` JSON) is the cache key everywhere — QuestDB `bar_param`, WS topic `param`, builder-state blobs, and the frontend series cache all derive from the same spec.
- Renko/range bars have no fixed time width; the renderer spaces them by index (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 note and `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 renko edge case c). Time-based indicators over such series are disabled in the UI with an explanatory tooltip — that gating is E13's consumer-side work but the series must expose an `isTimeAligned: false` flag for it.
- LOD L2 candle decimation must be **min/max preserving** — a correctness requirement, not cosmetics.
- `confirm: false` on the last bar of any frame means "forming"; a client that treats it as closed reproduces the exact flicker bug Bybit's flag exists to prevent (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 note).

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85% on the `bar_builders` backend package and the series modules of `packages/chart-engine`.
- **Property** BI-1…BI-6 of `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.4 over ≥1M synthetic trades, plus random-cut-point snapshot/restore equivalence.
- **Golden file** recorded fixture day per builder, byte-compared.
- **Contract** generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines`, `/market/bars` and the `BarsBatch` schema.
- **Golden image** candle/bar/line/area/HA series at each LOD tier on SwiftShader (reusing E11-T08's harness).
- **E2E** Playwright + Electron: open chart, switch interval, switch bar mode, confirm forming-bar behaviour.
- **Perf** series-render benchmark wired into CI; backfill and rebuild throughput measured.

## Security notes
Market data is not secret, but this Epic adds a large user-controlled parameter surface. Threats (STRIDE, carried on E12-X-scope within E11's engine model plus this Epic's own review): **DoS** via an unbounded `from/to/limit` or an absurd `param` (`tick:1` over 30 days) — every endpoint enforces `BarLimit`, a per-request bar cap and a per-user concurrent-rebuild cap; **resource exhaustion** via subscribing to dozens of distinct `spec_hash`es — the `BarBuilderSet` cap (3–8 specs per symbol, §3.5) is enforced server-side with a clear error; **information disclosure** — `bars` topics require `marketdata:read` like every other market topic, RBAC-checked at subscribe. No PII, no secrets, no key material touched.

## Accessibility notes
Series rendering is canvas; accessibility is delivered through E11's DOM-mirror and the SCR-045 data table, which this Epic must **feed** with per-bar OHLCV, delta and the forming/closed flag. Specific obligations here: the bar-mode menu (SCR-042 / CMP-220) presents bar modes as a separate labelled group with an explanatory note because they change the meaning of the x-axis; chart-type options name the type in text, never icon-only (CMP-222); partial-history and no-data states are text, not colour; the bar countdown (CMP-226) is text with `aria-live="off"` by default. WCAG 2.2 AA, axe-core zero violations on SCR-030/041/042/047.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3: p95 frame ≤16.6 ms with 100k bars and all R1 overlays; ≥55 fps at 100k bars zoom-to-fit via LOD; ≤300 ms to first paint from cache for 5 000 bars (US-MKT-008); interval switch ≤200 ms from cache (US-CHART-005); chart-type switch ≤100 ms (US-CHART-002); rebuild of 1M prints ≤10 s and cancellable (US-CHART-003/004); ingest→bar-emit adds no measurable p95 to the ≤20 ms ingest→bus budget.

## Observability
Metrics: `bars_built_total{symbol,kind}`, `bars_late_trade_dropped_total`, `bar_build_latency_seconds`, `bar_rebuild_duration_seconds{kind}`, `bar_builder_specs_active`, `bar_backfill_pages_total`, `bar_backfill_rate_limited_total`, `bars_ws_frames_total`, `series_frame_ms` (engine). Structured logs on rebuild start/finish/cancel with `spec_hash`. A Grafana row "Bar builders" with build latency, active specs and late-trade drops; alert when `bars_late_trade_dropped_total` rate exceeds zero for 5 minutes.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2: every child Done or explicitly descoped; roadmap exit criterion 4 (byte-for-byte parity) demonstrated and recorded; coverage ≥85% backend/engine and ≥80% frontend; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3, `21-database-schema.md` §4.8, `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 reflect shipped behaviour; axe-core green plus one manual screen-reader pass on the chart surfaces introduced here; perf numbers recorded against the budgets above; QA epic-level regression pass recorded; demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review on staging (demo).

## Dependencies
- **E07** storage spike — QuestDB write path and Parquet cold tier decisions the `bars_*` tables depend on.
- **E08** Bybit adapter & ingestion — `TradeEvent` on the internal bus and the REST kline client.
- **E11** chart-engine core — scene graph, transforms, LOD infrastructure, data stores.
- **E17** WS protocol (via E11) — the `bars` topic rides the frozen transport.
- Consumed by **E13** indicators, **E18** footprint, **E26** replay.

## Branch
`feat/e12-bars-series`, with child branches `feat/e12-<ticket-slug>` merged into `main` via the merge queue (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §7); PRs ≤400 LOC diff preferred.

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §2 (trade events), §3 (bar builders, invariants BI-1…BI-6), §11 (replay bus)
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.8 `bars_*`, §4.9 footprint grid alignment, retention table

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.
