title: Build deterministic time bars from the trade tape with clock-driven closes
body:
## Context
Time bars are the default series every chart opens on and the reference every other builder is checked against. They are also the only builder with a second input besides trades: a **clock**. `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 is explicit that "a bar closes on `on_clock` even if no trade arrives, so `on_bar_close` rules fire on schedule in a dead market" — a requirement that comes from the rule engine (E35), not from charting, and that a trades-only implementation silently fails.

This Story implements the `time` kind of the `BarBuilder` protocol, serving **US-MKT-008** (the bars that backfill produces), **US-CHART-001** (the candles that render) and the substrate for **US-CHART-005** (timeframe switching) and **US-CHART-009** (session anchoring, whose `session_anchor_utc_min` this builder consumes).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `TimeBarBuilder` implementing `on_trade`, `on_clock`, `snapshot`, `restore` per `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.2.
- Boundary arithmetic: `floor((ts_event - anchor) / interval_ms) * interval_ms + anchor`, with `align_to_epoch` and `session_anchor_utc_min` from `BarSpec` (US-CHART-009's UTC-00:00 / funding-time / custom anchor all resolve to a minutes-past-midnight offset here).
- Empty-interval handling: no bar emitted by default; `gap_before=True` on the next real bar; `BarSeries.densify()` (from E12-T01) supplies synthetic flat bars to consumers that need a continuous index, and those are never persisted.
- Clock-driven close via `on_clock`, emitting a `close` `BarUpdate` on schedule in a dead market.
- Late-arriving trade handling: a trade whose `ts_event` falls in an already-closed bar is applied to that bar and re-emits `close` with `amended=True`; beyond 60 s the trade is dropped and counted in `bars_late_trade_dropped_total`.
- Full field population: `buy_volume`/`sell_volume` from the taker side, `delta`, running-path `min_delta`/`max_delta`, `trade_count`, `turnover`, `vwap`, `closed`, `partial`, `gap_before`.
- The standard interval ladder of US-CHART-005 (1 s … 1 D) plus arbitrary custom intervals (e.g. 7m), all expressed as `interval_ms`.

## Out of scope
- Non-time builders (E12-S02/S03/S04).
- Multi-spec fan-out and state persistence cadence (E12-T03).
- The kline REST backfill that seeds pre-recording history (E12-S05).
- Rendering (E12-S06) and the timeframe-switch UX (E12-S11).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bars close on the boundary
  Given a 1m time spec anchored to UTC 00:00
  And trades at 10:00:59.900 and 10:01:00.100
  Then the first trade belongs to the 10:00 bar and the second opens the 10:01 bar
  And the 10:00 bar is emitted with closed=true exactly once

Scenario: A dead market still closes bars
  Given a 1m spec and no trades for 5 minutes
  When on_clock advances past each boundary
  Then 0 bars are persisted (empty intervals emit nothing)
  And the bar that was open at the start of the silence is closed on its own boundary, not on the next trade

Scenario: Late trade amends a closed bar
  Given the 10:00 bar closed 20 seconds ago
  When a trade with ts_event inside 10:00 arrives
  Then that bar's OHLCV and delta are recomputed and re-emitted with amended=true
  And the total-volume invariant BI-1 still holds

Scenario: Very late trade is dropped, not silently merged
  Given the 10:00 bar closed 90 seconds ago
  When a trade with ts_event inside 10:00 arrives
  Then it is not applied to any bar
  And bars_late_trade_dropped_total is incremented with the symbol label

Scenario: Session anchor shifts the grid
  Given a 1h spec with session_anchor_utc_min = 480
  Then bar boundaries fall at 08:00, 09:00 … UTC rather than on the epoch grid
  And switching the anchor produces a different spec_hash and therefore a separate series
```

## Technical notes / design
- `min_delta`/`max_delta` track the running intra-bar delta **path**, updated on every trade — not `min(delta_start, delta_end)`. They are the input to exhaustion/absorption reads in R2, so an endpoint-only implementation is a silent correctness bug that no OHLCV comparison would catch.
- No allocation in the common path: the builder mutates an internal mutable draft and materialises a frozen `Bar` only on emit (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3.5).
- The amendment path must be idempotent against the QuestDB dedup upsert of E12-T02 — re-emitting a bar overwrites it.
- Clock source is the offset-corrected exchange clock (US-MKT-009), not the local wall clock.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85%: boundary arithmetic across DST-free UTC (crypto has no sessions, but anchors do shift the grid), each field's accumulation, amendment and drop thresholds.
- **Property**: BI-1 (volume conservation), BI-2 (`delta == buy - sell`), BI-3 (`min_delta <= delta <= max_delta`, both attained on the path), BI-6 (`vwap == turnover / volume` to 8 dp, or `open` when volume is 0) over ≥1M synthetic trades.
- **Golden file**: the recorded BTCUSDT fixture day at 1m/5m/1h compared against the reference implementation, byte-for-byte on OHLCV (roadmap exit criterion 4).
- **Integration**: builder driven by the real bus from E08 against a recorded fixture; cross-checked against Bybit `/v5/market/kline` for the same window with a documented tolerance for the known edge (exchange klines include bars we deliberately omit for empty intervals).

## Security notes
`interval_ms` is user-controlled via `param`. Bound it: minimum 1 s (the documented floor of US-CHART-005), maximum 1 D, and reject non-integer or zero values before a builder is instantiated — an interval of 0 or 1 µs is a CPU-exhaustion vector that would emit bars per trade forever. No secrets, no PII.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI. Two obligations flow downstream: the `gap_before` flag must be exposed so the renderer can draw a real gap (never interpolate) and the data-table alternative (SCR-045) can state it in text; and `partial=True` must be exposed so "history starts at <ts>" is a text statement rather than a visual cue.

## Performance notes
Per-trade cost must be O(1) with no allocation; the builder sits on the ingest hot path whose budget is ingest→bus ≤20 ms p95 at 5 000 prints/s (US-MKT-006). Benchmark: 1M trades through a single 1m spec in well under the 10 s rebuild budget, measured as part of E12-T04's harness.

## Observability
`bars_built_total{symbol,kind="time"}`, `bars_amended_total`, `bars_late_trade_dropped_total`, `bar_build_latency_seconds{kind="time"}`. Log at INFO on first bar per new spec, at WARN on a dropped late trade with the lateness in ms.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2: every Gherkin scenario backed by an automated test; coverage ≥85%; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 matches shipped behaviour; perf benchmark recorded; QA sign-off on the black-box plan; demoed (a chart rendering these bars, or a recorded terminal run if E12-S06 has not landed); feature-flag state recorded (`bars.time` is default-on, it is the baseline series); PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T01** — the domain model and `spec_hash`.
- **E08** — `TradeEvent` on the bus, the taker-side field, and the exchange clock offset (US-MKT-009).

## Branch
`feat/e12-time-bars`

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1–§3.5 (model, protocol, time-bar edge cases, invariants, multi-spec)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001, US-CHART-005, US-CHART-009, US-MKT-006, US-MKT-008, US-MKT-009
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.8 `bars_time`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 4

title: Build tick and volume bars with exact splitting and volume conservation
body:
## Context
**US-CHART-003 "Order-flow bar modes" is a Must**, and it is the story that makes CandleViewer an order-flow terminal rather than another candle viewer: "I want volume bars and tick/trade bars in addition to time bars, so that bars are built by activity rather than the clock." These two builders are also where the hardest correctness rule in the whole Epic lives — **volume-bar splitting**.

`24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3: "A trade that would overshoot is **split**: the bar takes exactly the remaining quota, the remainder opens the next bar at the same price and timestamp, both parts carry `split_from_trade_id`. Splitting preserves the total-volume invariant, which matters because profiles are built off the same trades." Get this wrong and invariant BI-1 breaks, which means E19's volume profile double-counts or under-counts — a defect that would surface in R2 as an unexplainable POC discrepancy rather than as an obvious bug here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `TickBarBuilder`: closes after exactly `tick_count` **trade events**. One exchange push containing 50 records produces 50 tick increments — batch boundaries are irrelevant. Block trades count as one tick and are flagged, with an `exclude_block_trades` option (default `false`).
- `VolumeBarBuilder`: accumulates `qty` until `>= volume_threshold`, with exact splitting as specified above, `split_from_trade_id` on both parts, and correct handling of consecutive overshoot (one huge print spanning N thresholds produces N bars of identical OHLC, rendered as a stack of flat bars — this is correct, not a bug).
- Both builders populate the full `Bar` field set including the running-path `min_delta`/`max_delta`, and implement `snapshot`/`restore`.
- Partial-history semantics: when the recorder holds less tape than the requested window, bars are built for the available window and `partial=True` marks the first bar, feeding the "tick data begins at <ts>" marker required by US-CHART-003's third scenario.
- Wire parameter mapping: `tick` → trades per bar, `volume` → base-asset volume per bar (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars`).

## Out of scope
- Range, delta and renko builders (E12-S03, E12-S04).
- The UI that selects these modes and shows the partial-history marker (E12-S12, E12-S12).
- Footprint cells per bar (E18).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Volume bar splits an overshooting trade
  Given a volume spec with threshold 1500 and a bar holding 1400
  When a single trade of 300 arrives
  Then the open bar closes with exactly 1500
  And a new bar opens with 200 at the same price and timestamp
  And both parts carry the same split_from_trade_id

Scenario: Volume is conserved across the whole series
  Given 1 000 000 synthetic trades and a volume spec
  Then the sum of bar.volume equals the sum of trade.qty exactly (invariant BI-1)
  And no bar exceeds the threshold

Scenario: One huge print spans several thresholds
  Given a threshold of 1500 and a single trade of 5000 into an empty bar
  Then bars of 1500, 1500, 1500 close and a bar of 500 remains open
  And the closed bars have identical OHLC and the same timestamp

Scenario: Tick bars count events, not pushes
  Given a tick spec of 500
  And one exchange push containing 50 trade records
  Then the tick counter advances by 50
  And a bar closes on exactly the 500th record regardless of how the records were batched

Scenario: Insufficient tick history
  Given the recorder holds 3 days of prints and a 30-day window is requested
  Then bars are built only for the available window
  And the first bar carries partial=true with the timestamp where tick data begins
  And no REST klines are substituted for the missing region

Scenario: Block trade handling is explicit
  Given exclude_block_trades is true
  When a block trade arrives
  Then it does not advance the tick counter
  And its volume is still counted so BI-1 is not violated, or it is excluded from both — whichever the implementation chooses, consistently, and the choice is documented and tested
```

## Technical notes / design
- Splitting is a *volume-bar only* behaviour. Delta bars deliberately do **not** split (E12-S03) because splitting an aggressor's fill across two delta bars misrepresents the aggression — the two builders must not share a "generic threshold" abstraction that accidentally unifies them.
- `split_from_trade_id` is what lets E18/E19 reconcile cells and profiles against raw trades; it must reach the persisted row and the wire payload, not just live in memory.
- Tick and volume bars are not time-aligned; `open_time`/`close_time` come from the first/last trade, matching `/market/bars`' documented behaviour and the `open_source_ts` column pattern of §4.8.
- `restore(snapshot())` must preserve a mid-split state: a snapshot taken between the two halves of a split trade must resume identically (this is the nastiest BI-5 case and deserves a dedicated test).

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85%: split arithmetic at the boundary, exactly-at-threshold, N-fold overshoot, zero-qty trade, block-trade flagging.
- **Property**: BI-1…BI-6 over ≥1M synthetic trades for both kinds; BI-5 with random cut points including mid-split.
- **Golden file**: the recorded fixture day at `tick:500` and `vol:1000` byte-compared against the reference implementation.
- **Integration**: driven from the real bus against the recorded fixture, with the partial-history path exercised by truncating the tape.

## Security notes
`tick_count` and `volume_threshold` are user-controlled. Enforce sane bounds (minimum tick count ≥ 1 and a documented floor such as 10 for a *subscribable* series; volume threshold > 0 and expressed in base units) — `tick:1` over a 30-day window is a straightforward CPU and storage exhaustion vector, producing one bar per trade. The bound is enforced at `BarSpec` validation (E12-T01) and re-checked at subscribe/endpoint level (E12-T05/T06); this Story supplies the numeric limits.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI. The `partial=True` flag and its timestamp are the data contract behind the text marker that SCR-047 and the data-table alternative render — the flag must carry the actual timestamp, not merely a boolean, so the UI can say "tick data begins 2026-10-27 00:00 UTC" rather than "partial".

## Performance notes
Both builders sit on the same per-trade hot path as E12-S01: O(1), no allocation in the common path. The rebuild budget from US-CHART-003 applies directly — 1M prints in ≤10 s — and is measured by E12-T04's harness and the E12-K01 findings. Volume-bar splitting must not allocate per split beyond the emitted `Bar`.

## Observability
`bars_built_total{kind="tick"|"volume"}`, `bar_volume_splits_total`, `bar_build_latency_seconds{kind}`, `bars_partial_series_total`. A split rate that is ~100% of trades indicates a misconfigured threshold and is worth a WARN-level log once per spec.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario above backed by an automated test; BI-1 property test green at 1M trades; coverage ≥85%; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 matches shipped behaviour including the block-trade decision; perf benchmark recorded against the 10 s rebuild budget; QA sign-off; demoed; feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S01** — the shared accumulation/emit machinery and the `Bar` field population proven on time bars.
- **E12-T01** — domain model.
- **E16** (recorder) supplies the tape depth that determines `partial`; this Story must degrade correctly when it is shallow rather than block on E16.

## Branch

title: Build range and delta bars with no phantom bars and no delta splitting
body:
## Context
**US-CHART-004** asks for range bars (Should) and delta bars (Should) so a trader can "filter noise in different ways". Both are threshold builders like volume bars, and both deliberately behave *differently* from volume bars at the threshold — which is exactly why they get their own Story rather than a shared generic implementation.

`24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 states the two traps:
- **Range bars**: "a single trade that jumps more than one range beyond the current bar closes the current bar at that price and opens **one** new bar (we do not synthesize intermediate phantom range bars, which would invent volume that never traded)". Most naive implementations emit the phantom bars; the result is a chart that shows volume at prices where nothing traded.
- **Delta bars**: "A trade that pushes delta past the threshold is **not** split (unlike volume bars) because splitting an aggressor's fill across two delta bars misrepresents the aggression; the overshoot carries into the bar's final `delta`."

`30-release-roadmap.md` §12 places range and Renko bars on rung 2 of the descoping ladder, which is why they are scheduled here in Sprint 06 rather than alongside the Must-level builders.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `RangeBarBuilder`: closes when `high - low >= range_ticks * tick_size`; the closing trade's price becomes `close`; the next bar opens at that same price with **no gap**; a multi-range jump closes one bar and opens exactly one new bar with `gap_before=True`.
- `DeltaBarBuilder`: closes when `abs(delta) >= delta_threshold`; running delta resets each bar; closure is evaluated after each trade and is **final** (an oscillating delta cannot un-close a bar); overshoot carries into the closed bar's final `delta` with no splitting.
- `tick_size` resolution from the instrument catalogue (US-MKT-001) at spec-construction time, with an explicit failure when the symbol is unknown — a range spec is meaningless without it.
- `open_source_ts` population for `bars_range` per `21-database-schema.md` §4.8.
- Both builders implement `snapshot`/`restore` and populate the full `Bar` field set including running-path `min_delta`/`max_delta`.
- Wire mapping: `range` → ticks, `delta` → signed volume threshold (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars`).

## Out of scope
- Renko (E12-S04) — it shares `range_ticks` but has entirely different formation and reversal rules.
- P&F — not built in R1.
- The rebuild-on-parameter-change UX (E12-S12).
- Rendering these index-spaced series (E12-S06/S09 handle the geometry; the `isTimeAligned=false` flag originates here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Range bar closes on span, next bar opens at the close
  Given a range spec of 20 ticks and tick_size 0.10
  And a bar whose high-low span reaches 2.00
  Then the bar closes at the price of the trade that completed the span
  And the next bar opens at exactly that price with no gap

Scenario: A jump does not invent phantom bars
  Given an open range bar and a single trade 5 ranges above its low
  Then exactly one bar closes and exactly one new bar opens
  And no intermediate bars are emitted
  And the new bar carries gap_before=true
  And total volume across bars still equals total traded volume (BI-1)

Scenario: Delta bar closure is final
  Given a delta spec of 2000 and a bar whose delta has just reached 2000
  When the next trade pushes delta back to 1900
  Then the bar remains closed and the new trade belongs to the following bar

Scenario: Delta overshoot is not split
  Given a delta spec of 2000 and a bar at delta 1900
  When a single sell of 500 arrives
  Then the bar closes with delta 2400 (overshoot carried, not split)
  And no split_from_trade_id is emitted for delta bars

Scenario: Unknown tick size is a hard failure
  Given a range spec for a symbol absent from the instrument catalogue
  When the builder is constructed
  Then construction fails with an error naming the symbol
  And no series is created and no partially-built bars are persisted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Range and delta must **not** be refactored into the volume builder's threshold abstraction. The three differ precisely at the threshold (volume splits, delta carries, range re-opens at the close price), and a shared abstraction is how those distinctions get lost in a later refactor. Document the divergence in the module docstring.
- `range_ticks * tick_size` uses exact Decimal arithmetic; a float multiplication here produces off-by-one-tick closures that a golden-file test will catch only on some symbols.
- `gap_before=True` is the renderer's signal to draw a real gap. It must never be interpolated (US-CHART-011's "the gap is drawn as a gap, never interpolated" principle applies to series generally).
- Neither series is time-aligned: expose `isTimeAligned=false` on the series metadata so E13 can disable time-based indicators over them with an explanatory tooltip, and so E12-S09 spaces them by index.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85%: exact-threshold closure, multi-range jump, delta oscillation around the threshold, Decimal tick arithmetic on symbols with 0.01 / 0.10 / 0.5 tick sizes.
- **Property**: BI-1…BI-6 over ≥1M synthetic trades for both kinds; BI-5 snapshot/restore at random cut points; an explicit property that no range series ever contains a bar with zero volume (the phantom-bar regression).
- **Golden file**: the recorded fixture day at `range:20` and `delta:500`, byte-compared against the reference implementation (roadmap exit criterion 4 counts these among the five bar types).
- **Integration**: driven from the real bus against the recorded fixture, including a symbol whose tick size differs from BTCUSDT's.

## Security notes
`range_ticks` and `delta_threshold` are user-controlled and both admit a pathological small value (`range:1` on a volatile symbol emits a bar per trade). Bound them at `BarSpec` validation with documented minima, and re-check at the endpoint/subscribe layer. The unknown-symbol hard failure above is also a security property: it prevents an arbitrary client-supplied symbol string from creating a builder and therefore a new QuestDB SYMBOL value.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI. Downstream obligation: because these series are not time-aligned, the x-axis no longer means clock time. E12-S12's bar-mode menu must state that in text (CMP-220's a11y contract already requires bar modes to be a separate labelled group "with an explanatory note, since they change the meaning of the x-axis"), and the data-table alternative must show `open_time`/`close_time` per bar rather than implying a uniform grid.

## Performance notes
Same hot-path constraints as E12-S01/S02: O(1) per trade, no allocation in the common path, 1M prints rebuilt in ≤10 s (US-CHART-004 NFR, measured by E12-T04). Range bars on a volatile symbol can emit far more bars than a time series — the emit path, not the accumulate path, is the cost to watch.

## Observability
`bars_built_total{kind="range"|"delta"}`, `bar_range_jump_gaps_total`, `bar_build_latency_seconds{kind}`. Log at WARN once per spec when the emitted bar rate exceeds a threshold suggesting a misconfigured parameter.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario backed by an automated test including the phantom-bar regression property; coverage ≥85%; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 matches shipped behaviour; perf benchmark recorded; QA sign-off; demoed; feature-flag state recorded (`bars.range`, `bars.delta` behind a flag, default-on in staging — these are the descopable rung, so the flag is the descoping mechanism); PR merged via the merge queue.

- **E12-S02** — the threshold-builder machinery and the BI-1 property harness.
- **E08 / US-MKT-001** — the instrument catalogue supplying `tick_size`.

title: Implement the bar domain model: BarSpec, Bar, BarUpdate and spec_hash
body:
## Context
Every other ticket in E12 — and E13 indicators, E18 footprint, E19 profiles, E26 replay — keys off one identifier: `spec_hash`. It is the QuestDB `bar_param`, the WS topic `param`, the builder-state blob key, the REST cache key and the frontend series cache key. Getting the canonicalisation wrong means two logically identical series get two caches, two builders and two sets of bars; getting it *unstable* means every process restart invalidates the whole hot store.

This Task lands the shared domain model of `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1–§3.2 before any builder is written, so all six builders are written against a frozen model rather than six drifting variants. It is the interface-first step required by `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `BarSpec` (Pydantic v2) with `kind` ∈ {time, tick, volume, range, delta, renko}, the per-kind parameter fields (`interval_ms`, `tick_count`, `volume_threshold`, `range_ticks`, `delta_threshold`), the shared options (`price_source`, `session_anchor_utc_min`, `align_to_epoch`, `renko_wick`, `reversal_bricks`) and the `_exactly_one` model validator that raises when `kind` and the populated parameter disagree.
- `Bar` with the full field set of §3.1 including `index`, `open_time`/`close_time` (`TsUs`), OHLC, `volume`, `buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, `delta`, `min_delta`, `max_delta`, `trade_count`, `turnover`, `vwap`, `closed`, `partial`, `gap_before`.
- `BarUpdate` (`kind` ∈ open|update|close, `bar`) and the `BarBuilder` Protocol (`on_trade`, `on_clock`, `snapshot`, `restore`) plus the `BuilderState` msgpack envelope — declarations only; implementations land in E12-S01…S04.
- `spec_hash`: sha256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, Decimals serialised as fixed-precision strings, defaults **explicitly included** so an omitted default and a stated default hash identically).
- Bidirectional mapping `BarSpec ⇄ (bar_type, param)` for the REST/WS wire convention of `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, including the rule that dots are illegal in `param` and colons separate compound params.
- `BarSeries` container with `densify()` producing synthetic flat bars (`volume=0`, `open=high=low=close=prev.close`, `synthetic=True`) that are **never persisted**.
- A mirrored TypeScript type module in `packages/chart-engine` (or its shared types package) generated from the Pydantic models, so the client cannot drift from the server model.

## Out of scope
- Any builder logic (E12-S01…S04) and the `BarBuilderSet` fan-out (E12-T03).
- QuestDB DDL (E12-T02) and the endpoints (E12-T05/T06).
- `pnf` and `heikin_ashi` as `BarSpec.kind` values — HA is a client-side transform over a time spec (E12-S07), P&F is not built in R1. The wire enum still accepts them so the 422 path is exercisable.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: spec_hash is stable and canonical
  Given two BarSpec instances that are semantically identical but constructed differently
    (one stating a default explicitly, one omitting it; one with Decimal("50"), one with Decimal("50.00"))
  Then their spec_hash values are equal
  And the hash is unchanged across process restarts and Python versions in CI

Scenario: Mismatched kind and parameter is rejected
  Given a BarSpec with kind="volume" and tick_count=500 and volume_threshold=None
  When it is constructed
  Then a validation error names both the kind and the offending field

Scenario: Wire round-trip
  Given any valid BarSpec
  When it is converted to (bar_type, param) and back
  Then the result equals the original and its spec_hash is unchanged
  And a param containing a dot is rejected before it reaches the topic namespace

Scenario: densify never leaks
  Given a time series with empty intervals
  When densify() is called
  Then the synthetic bars carry synthetic=True and volume=0
  And attempting to persist a synthetic bar raises rather than writing a row
```

## Technical notes / design
- Money and quantity are `Decimal`, never float, throughout the model — the QuestDB columns are DOUBLE but the *model* is exact, and conversion happens only at the storage boundary (see E12-T02).
- `spec_hash` truncation: the full 64-hex digest is stored internally; the wire uses the human-readable `(bar_type, param)` pair, not the hash, so a user can read a topic name. The hash is an internal identity, the pair is the external one — they must be 1:1, which is what the round-trip test above enforces.
- `min_delta`/`max_delta` are documented as running intra-bar path extremes, not endpoint values (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1); the model docstring must say so because the field names invite the wrong implementation.
- TypeScript mirror is generated in CI, and a drift between generated and committed types fails the build.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85%: validator matrix over all six kinds × populated/unpopulated parameter combinations; hash stability; Decimal normalisation; wire round-trip for every kind.
- **Property**: random valid specs round-trip through canonical JSON and through the wire pair with a stable hash.
- **Contract**: the generated TypeScript types compile against the `BarsBatch` schema fixtures from `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.3.

## Security notes
`param` arriving from the wire is untrusted input that becomes part of a topic name, a cache key and a QuestDB `SYMBOL` column value. Parse it with a strict whitelist per `bar_type` (bounded integers, the documented colon grammar only), enforce `maxLength: 24` as the OpenAPI schema states, and reject dots — an unbounded `param` is both a topic-namespace injection vector and a QuestDB SYMBOL-capacity exhaustion vector.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The validation error messages defined here surface verbatim in SCR-042, so they must be human-readable sentences naming the offending field, not exception reprs.

## Performance notes
`spec_hash` is computed once per spec and memoised; it must never be recomputed per trade. `Bar` materialisation is the hot path — the model must support construction from an internal mutable draft without a full re-validation pass (`model_construct` on the emit path, validated only at spec level).

## Observability
Expose `bar_specs_registered_total` and a debug endpoint/log line mapping `spec_hash → BarSpec` so an operator reading a QuestDB `bar_param` or a WS topic can resolve it back to a human-readable spec.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2: acceptance criteria verified by tests; coverage threshold met; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1–§3.2 matches the shipped model (amended if it drifted); generated TS types committed and drift-checked in CI; no demo required (internal model) with a one-line note; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E08** — `TradeEvent`, `Symbol`, `Px`, `Qty`, `TsUs` and the shared Decimal/precision primitives live in the ingestion package this model imports.

## Branch
`feat/e12-bar-domain-model`

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1 bar model, §3.2 builder protocol, §3.4 invariants
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` `bar_type`/`param` table, `BarType` schema
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 (`bars` param convention, dots illegal), §14.3 `BarsBatch`

title: Create the bars_* QuestDB tables, write path and retention policy
body:
## Context
Bars must survive a restart, must be queryable by range for backfill-free chart opens, and must be *rebuildable* when the builder algorithm changes. `21-database-schema.md` §4.8 specifies six sibling tables — `bars_time`, `bars_tick`, `bars_volume`, `bars_range`, `bars_renko`, `bars_delta` — with an identical column set, a `build_version` column whose bump triggers a rebuild, and `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol, bar_param)` so a re-emitted or amended bar overwrites rather than duplicates. `bars_renko` and `bars_range` additionally carry `open_source_ts` because their bars are not time-aligned.

Without this table set, every chart open pays a full rebuild from the trade tape, which E12-K01 is measuring at seconds-per-million-trades. This is the difference between a 300 ms chart open (US-MKT-008 NFR) and an unusable one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Migration creating all six tables exactly per `21-database-schema.md` §4.8, including `TIMESTAMP(ts) PARTITION BY MONTH WAL` (and `PARTITION BY DAY` where the schema doc specifies it for the higher-cardinality families), the dedup keys, and `open_source_ts` on `bars_renko`/`bars_range`.
- The async write path: batched ILP/WAL writes from the builder emit path, with backpressure that drops nothing (queue + await, never a silent discard) and a bounded in-flight buffer.
- Decimal→DOUBLE conversion at the storage boundary only, with the rounding rule documented and tested (the model stays exact per E12-T01).
- `build_version` constant per builder family, bumped by a code change, with a documented rebuild trigger: a read that finds rows at an older `build_version` than the current code serves them but schedules a background rebuild and marks `meta.sources` accordingly.
- Range-read query helpers (`read_bars(symbol, spec_hash, from, to, limit)`) used by E12-T05, returning oldest→newest with a cursor.
- Retention wiring per `21-database-schema.md` retention table: `bars_tick/volume/range/renko/delta` hot 90 d → Parquet 24 mo, rebuildable from `trades` while trades exist; `bars_time` per its own row. Retention *execution* is E16's job — this ticket registers the policy and the archive path, it does not build the job.
- Postgres `chart_settings.bar_mode` column and its CHECK constraint (`21-database-schema.md` §1896–1909) with an Alembic migration.

## Out of scope
- The retention/compaction job itself and the disk-budget UI — **E16**.
- `footprint_cells` (§4.9) — **E18**.
- Parquet cold-tier read path for windows older than hot retention — E07 delivers the adapter; E12-T05 consumes it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Schema matches the specification
  Given the migration has run against a clean QuestDB
  When the shipped DDL is diffed against 21-database-schema.md §4.8
  Then the column names, types, partitioning, WAL setting and dedup keys are identical
  And bars_renko and bars_range carry open_source_ts while the other four do not

Scenario: Amended bars upsert rather than duplicate
  Given a bar at (ts, symbol, bar_param) is already written
  When the same bar is re-emitted with a corrected close after a late trade
  Then exactly one row exists and it carries the corrected values

Scenario: Write backpressure never loses bars
  Given the write queue is saturated by a burst
  Then producers await rather than discard
  And a saturation metric is incremented and a warning logged with the queue depth

Scenario: Stale build_version is detected
  Given rows exist at build_version 1 and the running code is at build_version 2
  When those bars are read
  Then the response is served from the stale rows
  And a rebuild is scheduled exactly once for that (symbol, spec_hash) window, not once per request
```

## Technical notes / design
- `bar_param` is the human-readable form (`5m`, `tick:500`, `vol:1000`, `range:20`, `renko:10`, `delta:500`) per the §4.8 table — *not* the raw `spec_hash` — so QuestDB SYMBOL cardinality stays low and an operator can read a query. The `spec_hash` ⇄ `bar_param` mapping from E12-T01 is the bridge; SYMBOL `CAPACITY 64` is a hard cardinality budget, and exceeding it is an alertable condition rather than a silent capacity expansion.
- Rebuild scheduling must be idempotent and deduplicated by `(symbol, spec_hash, window)`; a chart that polls must not enqueue one rebuild per poll.
- WAL + DEDUP gives idempotent writes, which is what makes the late-trade amendment path of `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.3 safe.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: Decimal→DOUBLE conversion and rounding; `bar_param` formatting per kind; query-helper cursor logic.
- **Integration** against a containerised QuestDB: migration applies to a clean instance and is idempotent on re-run; dedup upsert verified; range reads return correct ordering and bounds; backpressure behaviour under a synthetic burst.
- **Migration test**: Alembic up/down for the Postgres `chart_settings.bar_mode` change, including the CHECK constraint rejecting an unknown mode.

## Security notes
Labelled for review because this Task adds a persistence surface fed by user-controlled parameters. `bar_param` reaches a QuestDB SYMBOL column, so an unbounded parameter space is a **disk- and cardinality-exhaustion DoS** — the same class of risk `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 calls out for E16. Mitigations: `param` whitelist validation (E12-T01), the SYMBOL capacity budget with an alert, a per-user cap on distinct active specs, and no string interpolation anywhere in the query path (parameterised queries only, since `symbol` and `bar_param` both originate from the client).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The disk/retention facts surfaced here are rendered by E16's screens.

## Performance notes
Write path must sustain the bar emit rate for 3–8 specs × the recorded-symbol list without adding measurable latency to the ingest→bus p95 ≤20 ms budget (the write is off the critical path, behind a queue). Range read of 5 000 bars must return in well under the 300 ms first-paint budget of US-MKT-008, leaving room for transport and render.

## Observability
Metrics: `bars_rows_written_total{kind}`, `bars_write_queue_depth`, `bars_write_saturation_total`, `bars_write_latency_seconds`, `bars_stale_build_version_total`, `bars_symbol_cardinality{table}`. Alert on sustained queue saturation and on SYMBOL cardinality approaching capacity.

## Definition of Done
Per §4.2: DDL verified against the schema doc; migrations reversible and tested; coverage met; `21-database-schema.md` amended if the shipped DDL diverged; security review comment present; before/after evidence for the write-path benchmark attached; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T01** — `BarSpec`/`Bar` and the `spec_hash ⇄ bar_param` mapping.
- **E07** — the storage adapter, QuestDB client, migration runner and Parquet cold-tier interface.

## Branch
`feat/e12-bars-tables`

## References
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.8 `bars_*` (column set, dedup keys, `open_source_ts`), §4.9 alignment note, retention table, `chart_settings` §1896–1909
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1 `Bar`, §3.3 late-trade amendment

title: STRIDE threat model for bar builders, backfill and the bars topic
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes a STRIDE threat model mandatory per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the kickoff to be scheduled before an Epic leaves Ready. E12 is not an obvious security epic — it moves no money and holds no keys — which is exactly why it deserves a deliberate model rather than an assumption.

Its real security property is **integrity of evidence**. `04-security-program.md` objective **O8** states it directly: recorded market data is evidence, and silent corruption invalidates decisions. Bars built by E12 feed footprint, profiles, CVD, replay, the journal and eventually rule-engine conditions that place live orders. A tampered or quietly wrong bar is therefore an input to automated trading. Secondary surfaces: E12 accepts user-controlled `bar_type`/`param`/`from`/`to`/`limit` on two public REST endpoints and a WS topic (injection, resource exhaustion), and it consumes a semi-trusted external feed (`AC-08`) whose responses must be treated as untrusted input (`SR-040`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model at `docs/plan/security/threat-models/e12-bars.md` covering the E12 data flow: Bybit WS/REST → ingestion → `BarBuilderSet` → QuestDB `bars_*` / Parquet → REST `/market/klines`, `/market/bars` → WS `bars.*` → chart engine.
- A data-flow diagram (mermaid) with the trust boundaries from `04-security-program.md` §: **TB-4** (client → backend API) and **TB-7** (backend → Bybit) explicitly drawn, plus the internal store boundary.
- Per-element STRIDE enumeration with at minimum these threats analysed, each with likelihood, impact, existing control, residual risk and an owning ticket:
  - **S**: forged upstream data — a compromised or spoofed upstream host injecting prints that become bars (control: TLS + pinned CA set, `SR-040` response validation, explicit `category=linear` per `SR-054`).
  - **T**: bar values altered in the store or during rebuild; a rebuild that silently changes history without a `build_version` bump; out-of-order/duplicate prints producing divergent bars (controls: `build_version` + dedup from `E12-T02`, golden conformance `E12-Q02`).
  - **R**: no record of which build produced a served bar, so a disputed trade decision cannot be reconstructed (control: `build_version` and `meta.sources` on every response; audit of rebuild triggers).
  - **I**: the bars endpoints leaking data beyond `marketdata:read`, or `include_delta` exposing recorded tape for symbols the session should not see; diagnostics/probe surfaces shipping to production.
  - **D**: resource exhaustion via a huge `limit`, an enormous `from..to` window, a pathological `param` (`tick:1` over a month), rebuild storms triggered by rapid parameter changes, or a slow WS consumer backpressuring ingestion (`SR-073`).
  - **E**: none expected — explicitly stated and justified rather than omitted, since E12 introduces no privileged operation; any future "rebuild" admin action must re-open this row.
- Mitigation mapping: every threat maps to an existing `SR-*` control, an E12 child ticket, or a **new** ticket filed by this one (input-validation caps, rebuild rate-limiting, `build_version` provenance in responses).
- Residual-risk statement with Owner sign-off for anything accepted.
- A row added to the epic-level risk register entries in `32-risk-register.md` if the model surfaces a risk not already tracked.

## Out of scope
- Executing the abuse cases (`E12-X02`) or writing SAST/DAST rules (`E12-X03`).
- Auth/session/RBAC design itself (E09) and key handling (E27) — referenced as assumed controls.
- WS transport security (E17 models the envelope, handshake and backpressure); this model covers the `bars` topic's use of it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model covers every element of the E12 data flow
  Given the threat model document is merged
  When it is reviewed against the data-flow diagram
  Then every process, data store, data flow and external entity has an explicit STRIDE row
  And every row states likelihood, impact, control and residual risk

Scenario: Every threat has an owner
  Given the mitigation mapping table
  Then each non-accepted threat references an SR id, an E12 child ticket or a newly filed ticket key
  And no row is left with an empty mitigation cell

Scenario: Failure case - an unmitigated high-risk threat blocks the epic
  Given a High residual-risk threat with no mitigation and no Owner acceptance
  When E12 epic DoD is evaluated
  Then the epic cannot be marked Done
  And the threat is named in the blocking comment

Scenario: Edge case - elevation-of-privilege row is justified, not omitted
  Given E12 introduces no privileged operation
  Then the E row states that explicitly with the reasoning and the condition that would reopen it

Scenario: Edge case - a new bar type reopens the model
  Given a future ticket adds a bar type with a new parameter shape
  Then the model's maintenance note requires the D (resource exhaustion) rows to be re-evaluated before that ticket is Ready
```

## Technical notes / design
- Run as a 2-hour workshop with the Security engineer, the E12 tech lead, the Architect and one QA representative; the document is written up from it within the same sprint, not weeks later.
- Use the same table format as the existing per-epic models in `04-security-program.md` §, so threats aggregate into the programme-level register without transcription.
- Be concrete about numbers where a control is a limit: the model should propose the actual caps (max `limit`, max window per bar type, max concurrent rebuilds per user) rather than saying "apply limits", so `E12-X03` and the implementation tickets have something to enforce.
- The evidence-integrity threats (T/R) are the ones with real consequence here; resist the pull to spend the workshop on generic web threats already handled by E09/E17.

## Test plan
- Each mitigation names its verification layer, mirroring `04-security-program.md`'s per-SR verification column: unit, integration, contract, load, or manual-review.
- Threats requiring adversarial verification are handed to `E12-X02`; threats requiring static enforcement to `E12-X03`; availability threats to `E12-Q05`/`E12-Q06`.
- The model is re-reviewed at `E12-X04` sign-off against what was actually built.

## Security notes
- The document is the security artefact; it is stored in the repo (not a wiki) so it versions with the code it describes.
- Classification: E12 handles public market data only — stated explicitly in the model, because that classification is what justifies the comparatively light controls, and a future change (per-user recorded data, account-scoped tape) would invalidate it.
- Explicit check that no diagnostics or probe surface introduced for testing (`E12-Q03`'s probe, `SCR-046`) is reachable in a production build.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A (document). The document follows repo docs conventions: heading hierarchy, header-row tables, mermaid diagrams accompanied by a text description so the diagram is not the only carrier of the information.

## Performance notes
- The denial-of-service rows must be reconciled with the performance budgets: any proposed cap (window size, `limit`, concurrent rebuilds) is cross-checked against budgets #5, #11 and #13 so a security control does not make a legitimate 30-day backfill impossible.

## Observability
- The model specifies the detection signal for each D and T threat: `bars_rebuild_total` rate per user, `api_request_rejected_total{reason="limit_exceeded"}`, `ws_client_disconnect_overflow_total`, `bars_gap_detected_total`, `exchange_response_invalid_total`.
- Anything modelled as a threat with no detection signal generates a ticket for instrumentation — an undetectable threat is an unmanaged one.

## Definition of Done
- Workshop held; model merged and reviewed by Security engineer and Architect.
- All rows populated; mitigations mapped to SR ids or ticket keys; new tickets filed and linked.
- Residual risks accepted in writing by the Owner where applicable.
- `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk emerged.
- Model linked from the E12 epic ticket and from `04-security-program.md`'s model index.
- Findings presented at the security review slot; no demo required.

## Dependencies

title: Design handoff pack for E13 indicator surfaces
body:
## Context
The design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1) forbids frontend work on a screen until its design ticket is Done, >=2 sprints ahead. E13 engineering starts in Sprint 07, so the handoff pack must be complete and signed off by the end of **Sprint 05** - two full sprints ahead, not one. This ticket is the gate, and its sprint placement is what makes the design-ahead rule true rather than merely asserted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Redlined specs for SCR-034, SCR-035, SCR-036: spacing, type, token names, component ids, breakpoints, and state matrix.
- Interaction spec: tab order, focus management on modal open/close, the SCR-035 live-preview update rule, the SCR-036 drag-reorder plus its keyboard alternative.
- Asset export: icons and preview thumbnails referenced by SCR-034 entries.
- The copy deck (from D04) and the accessibility acceptance script (from D05) attached as the QA-usable checklist.
- An engineering walkthrough session with the FE lead and the chart-engine lead; open questions answered in writing on the ticket.
- The per-screen "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` ticked for all three screens.

## Out of scope
- Any new design exploration - by this point the design is frozen; changes go through a change request that re-runs D03/D05 review.
- Implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Engineering can build without asking
  Given the FE lead walks through the pack
  Then no open question remains unanswered on the ticket, and every value engineering needs (spacing, token, duration, string, aria name) is present

Scenario: Sign-off is recorded
  Then the CDO (or delegate), the a11y specialist and the FE lead have each recorded sign-off on the ticket, and the artefact links are added to the SCR-034/035/036 entries

Scenario: Design-ahead is honoured
  Then this ticket reaches Done in Sprint 05, i.e. 2 full sprints before E13-S01/E13-S02 start in Sprint 07, and the design-ahead ledger on E13 records it; if it slips to Sprint 06 an explicit Architect/CDO waiver with a reason is recorded on every consuming story (E13-S01..S08) before any of them enters Ready

Scenario: A late change arrives
  Given a change is requested after sign-off
  Then it is filed as a new design ticket with its own review, not patched silently into the pack
```

## Technical notes / design
The pack is the single link surface: one Figma page per screen plus one markdown index in `docs/design/handoff/e13-indicators.md` listing artefact links, token names and the state matrix, so the repo has a durable pointer even if Figma moves.

## Test plan
The walkthrough itself is the test: the FE lead attempts to write the component skeletons live from the pack; anything they have to ask about is a defect against the pack and is fixed before sign-off.

## Security notes
Handoff notes must state that `params_schema`-driven forms render only enumerated control types and never raw HTML, so the constraint reaches the implementer.

## Accessibility notes
The D05 acceptance script is part of the pack and is the same script E13-Q04 executes, so design and QA cannot drift.

## Performance notes
The pack restates the <=250 ms add and <=100 ms re-tune budgets next to the affected interactions so the implementer sees them in context.

## Observability
The pack names the analytics event each interaction emits (`indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.reordered`, `indicator.visibility_toggled`, `indicator.removed`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every frame/state listed in Scope exists and is reviewed against the per-screen "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] CDO (or delegate) sign-off recorded on the ticket; artefact linked from the SCR entry.
- [ ] Component usage mapped to real CMP-* ids; any gap filed against E05 rather than drawn ad hoc.
- [ ] a11y reviewer has signed the contrast / focus / non-colour-encoding checks.
- [ ] Handoff notes (tokens, spacing, states, motion, empty/error copy) attached; engineering has acknowledged.
- [ ] Status Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule).

## Dependencies
E13-D04 (tokens, motion, copy) and E13-D05 (a11y sign-off) must both be Done.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.

title: Resolve O4: where each v1 indicator is computed (worker vs backend)
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` open question **O4** is still open: "Whether indicator computation belongs in the engine worker or the backend for heavy indicators". The doc already fixes the constraint - the rule engine runs server-side and must never depend on a browser, so **any indicator referenced by a rule IR is computed authoritatively in the backend** and the worker's copy is a display-only mirror that must reproduce it bit-for-bit (§14 parity test). O4 therefore only decides where *chart-only* indicators run. E13 cannot start T01/T02 without that decision, because it sets the `IndicatorDescriptor.compute` value (`client_worker` | `server`) for all ~28 v1 indicators and the shape of the parity test. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` schedules this at milestone M5; E13 is where it lands.

## Question(s) to answer
1. For each v1 indicator, is the worker able to compute it over a 100k-bar model, incrementally per closed bar, within the §4.3 allocation (<=2 ms/frame for indicator pane redraw, and <=250 ms for the first visible window on add)?
2. Which v1 indicators are rule-eligible today (per the `MetricRegistry` catalogue in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2: `atr`, `ema`, `sma`, `rsi`, `adx`, `swing_high`/`swing_low`, `cvd`, `delta`, volatility family) and therefore forced to `compute: server`?
3. Can a Python (`numpy`/`Decimal`-boundary) kernel and a TypeScript worker mirror agree bit-for-bit, or only to a stated epsilon? If only to an epsilon, what epsilon, and what does the parity test assert?
4. What is the cost of the mirror approach at ten active indicators - CPU in the worker, memory against the <=8 MB "profile/indicators/drawings" allocation in the engine memory table?

## Timebox
3 working days, agreed with the Architect. Not production code: a throwaway branch `spike/e13-indicator-compute` with a benchmark harness.

## Decision criteria (set before starting)
- If a worker implementation of the whole v1 set holds <=2 ms/frame and <=250 ms first-window at 100k bars, chart-only indicators default to `client_worker`.
- If any indicator exceeds it, that indicator is `server` and is delivered over the existing market-data WS as a derived series.
- If bit-for-bit parity is unachievable for the float-valued indicators, the parity test asserts `abs(a-b) <= 1e-8 * max(1, abs(a))` and the ADR records that this replaces "bit-for-bit" wording in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §14.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype worker kernel for the three worst cases (Ichimoku, MACD over a densified gapped series, VWAP with 3 sigma envelopes) plus one trivial case (SMA) as a control.
- Prototype Python kernel for the same four, in `services/api/orderflow/` spike form.
- Benchmark table: full compute and incremental update cost at 1k / 10k / 100k bars, worker CPU, memory delta.
- Parity table: max absolute and relative deviation per indicator over the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT fixture symbol-day.
- A `compute` assignment table for all ~28 v1 indicators, which becomes the seed data for `GET /api/v1/indicators`.
- ADR draft (finalised in E13-T04) recording the resolution, per the doc's instruction that resolving O4 must be recorded as an amendment to ADR-0007 if it changes rule eligibility.

## Out of scope
- Shipping any of the prototype code as-is.
- Order-flow indicators (they are `server` by definition - they read `orderflow_metrics`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every v1 indicator has a compute assignment
  When the spike report is reviewed
  Then all ~28 v1 indicators appear in the assignment table with compute = client_worker or server and a one-line reason

Scenario: The parity contract is decided
  Then the report states either bit-for-bit parity or the exact epsilon, and gives the measured worst-case deviation per indicator on the fixture day

Scenario: The budget question is answered with numbers
  Then full and incremental compute costs are tabulated at 1k/10k/100k bars for the four prototyped indicators, measured on reference hardware in Electron

Scenario: The decision criteria are actually applied
  Given a prototyped indicator exceeded its budget
  Then the report assigns it compute=server without a second spike, per the pre-registered criteria
```

## Technical notes / design
Reference hardware and measurement method per `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.2/§7. Use the same seeded synthetic dataset as the E11 benchmark harness for the scaling curves, and the recorded Bybit fixture for parity. Densification matters: `BarSeries.densify()` synthesises flat bars for gapped series (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §5) - the parity test must run over a day containing a real gap, otherwise it proves nothing.

## Test plan
The benchmark harness is the test. Numbers are re-runnable via a committed script even though the prototype code is throwaway, so the ADR's claims can be re-verified later.

## Security notes
The `server` assignment means an authenticated user can cause backend computation by adding an indicator; note the resulting resource-exhaustion surface for E13-X01 (rate/instance caps) rather than solving it here.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (no UI).

## Performance notes
This spike exists to protect budgets #1/#2 and the §4.3 <=2 ms indicator-pane allocation; findings feed E13-Q03's permanent benchmark.

## Observability
Propose the metric names the production implementation should emit (`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,where}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}`) based on what the prototype needed.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Questions answered with recorded evidence (benchmark and parity tables committed to `docs/plan/spikes/e13-o4.md`).
- [ ] Decision recorded as an ADR (drafted here, merged by E13-T04), including an ADR-0007 amendment if rule eligibility changed.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets updated: T01/T02 scope adjusted to the assignment table.
- [ ] Spike branch explicitly marked throwaway or the harness promoted into E13-Q03.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

## Dependencies
E12 provides the `BarStore`/`BarSeries` and the recorded fixture day the spike measures against.

## Branch
`spike/e13-indicator-compute` (throwaway).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §7 IND (US-IND-001..US-IND-008)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-034, SCR-035, SCR-036

- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.4 `indicator_presets`, §10.5 built-in presets, migration `0011_workspace`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 `MetricDescriptor` / `MetricRegistry` / §7.2 catalogue
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12 plugin API, `IndicatorPlugin`, §14 parity, open question O4

title: Hi-fi design: Fibonacci, anchored VWAP and measure tool visual language
body:
## Context
Most drawings are one or two strokes. Three are not: a Fibonacci retracement paints up to a dozen labelled levels across the chart, an anchored VWAP paints a curve plus up to six band lines that update on every tick, and the measure tool paints a transient ribbon with four numbers in it. Each of these puts a lot of ink over price at exactly the moment the user is trying to read price. Getting their visual language right - label placement, collision behaviour, line weight hierarchy, how much of the chart they may cover - is what separates a usable analysis tool from noise.

This ticket specifies that visual language in hi-fi for US-DRAW-004 (fib retracement/extension), US-DRAW-005 (anchored VWAP with sigma bands) and the measure tool, in Sprint 05, ahead of the Sprint 07-08 stories that build them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Fibonacci retracement & extension**: level line weight hierarchy (0/0.5/1 emphasised, intermediate levels lighter), per-level colour defaults from tokens, label content (price and percentage per US-DRAW-004) and its placement rules (left/right/inside, follow-viewport behaviour when an anchor is off-screen), label collision handling when levels compress at low price range, the inverted high-to-low drag case, and the custom level set (0.886) rendered.
- **Fibonacci time zones** frames: vertical level rendering against the time axis and its label strategy.
- **Anchored VWAP (US-DRAW-005)**: anchor marker on the anchored bar, the VWAP curve weight relative to indicator lines from E13 so the two are distinguishable, 1/2/3 sigma band strokes and optional fills, the individually-toggleable band state, the live-updating tail, and the **approximate badge** (CMP-227 EstimatedBadge) required when the anchor precedes recorded tick history.
- **Measure tool**: transient ribbon showing price delta, percentage, bar count and elapsed time; its dismissal rule; and its behaviour when dragged across a gap.
- **Density study**: each of the three rendered over a dense footprint chart at the density used in the engine benchmark, demonstrating that candles and cells remain readable; the maximum ink budget stated as a rule (e.g. maximum simultaneous labelled levels before auto-thinning).
- Dark and light frames for every above; colour-blind simulation pass for the level palette.
- `docs/design/specs/e14-fib-vwap-measure.md` with redlines and the label-collision algorithm described in words precise enough to implement.

## Out of scope
- The properties popover chrome for these tools (E14-D04 owns the shared frame; this ticket only supplies the on-canvas rendering and the extension-slot content requirements).
- Session/rolling VWAP as an indicator - that is E13's `VWAP (+session/anchored)` indicator entry; this ticket covers only the *drawing* form, though the two must be visually consistent and the spec states how.
- Pitchfork - deferred per the roadmap descoping ladder (section 12, item 3: pitchfork and fib time-zone tools may move to R2); frames are produced for fib time zones but pitchfork is explicitly marked deferred.
- Backend VWAP computation semantics - the incremental kernel is shared with US-IND-00x and is an engineering concern.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Levels stay labelled when they compress
  Given a Fibonacci retracement drawn over a narrow price range at a zoomed-out scale
  When levels come within one label height of each other
  Then the spec's collision rule produces a deterministic result (thinning, stacking or abbreviating) that is drawn as a frame
  And the 0, 0.5 and 1 levels are never the ones dropped

Scenario: VWAP is distinguishable from an indicator line
  Given an anchored VWAP drawing and an E13 EMA overlay on the same pane in the same theme
  Then the two are distinguishable by weight or style as well as colour
  And the spec states the rule that keeps them distinct as more overlays are added

Scenario: Anchor precedes recorded tick history
  Given the anchor bar is older than the recorded tick range for the symbol
  Then the approximate badge is shown on the drawing and repeated in its object-tree row and its tooltip
  And the frames show the badge's wording and its placement so it cannot be mistaken for an error state

Scenario: Ink budget is respected on a dense chart
  Given a footprint chart at benchmark density with a fib, an anchored VWAP with three bands and a measure ribbon active
  When the composite frame is reviewed
  Then candle bodies and footprint cell text remain readable against the documented contrast threshold
  And any element that fails is redesigned or placed behind the flatten-opacity control

Scenario: Inverted drag
  Given the user drags from high to low
  Then levels invert correctly, labels remain right-way-up and readable, and the frames show both orientations
```

## Technical notes / design
Label collision is specified as an algorithm, not a vibe, because the engine will implement it in the drawings layer with a text budget: all drawing labels together are one of the <=6 text draw calls per pane per frame (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.7). A design that needs unbounded labels is a design the engine cannot honour, so the spec caps simultaneous labelled levels and defines the thinning order.

The VWAP tail updates live (<=2 ms per anchored VWAP per US-DRAW-005 NFR). The design must therefore not require any per-tick text layout beyond the single value label at the tail.

The measure ribbon is transient and must never persist to the server - that is stated here because it is the one tool whose output looks like a drawing but is not one.

## Test plan
(1) Composite density frames reviewed against contrast thresholds with measured values. (2) Collision rule dry run: apply the written rule by hand to five compressed-level cases and confirm the drawn frames match. (3) Colour-vision simulation of the level palette and the band palette. (4) Side-by-side with E13 indicator overlays to confirm distinguishability. (5) Screen-reader script covering how a fib's levels and a VWAP's bands are exposed in the object tree and the data-table alternative. (6) Handoff dry run with the chart-engine engineer confirming the label budget is implementable.

## Security notes
No credentials, account data or secrets appear on these surfaces. The one integrity concern is the approximate badge on anchored VWAP: it communicates that a displayed number is derived from bar-approximated volume rather than recorded prints. Presenting an approximation as exact would mislead a trading decision, so the badge is a correctness requirement rather than a nicety - the spec forbids any state in which a fallback VWAP renders without it, and design QA (E14-D11) verifies that explicitly. Custom fib level sets are user content persisted server-side and are numeric-only with a bounded count; the spec states the bound so the UI cannot be used to persist an unbounded list.

## Accessibility notes
None of these three tools may rely on colour alone: fib levels carry numeric labels, VWAP bands are named (1/2/3 sigma) in the object tree and the tooltip, and the measure ribbon states its units in text. Each object's accessible name is specified (for example "Fibonacci retracement, 64 000 to 65 200, 7 levels"), and the per-level values are exposed through the object tree (SCR-036) and the data-table alternative (SCR-045), which are the normative accessible equivalents for canvas content. Reduced-motion users must still see the live VWAP tail update - the spec states that value updates are not animated.

## Performance notes
The spec carries three explicit budgets forward from the engine design: drawing labels share a single text draw call per pane; the anchored VWAP update is <=2 ms; and dragging any of these must not re-render the price/footprint layers. The density study doubles as the evidence that the design is inside the B8 benchmark envelope (200 drawings, drag one, <=12 ms frame, <=1 ms pick).

## Observability
Annotates `drawing.created`/`drawing.edited` payload fields for these tools (level-set id, band toggles, anchor bar time) and a `drawing.vwap_approximate_shown` event so we can measure how often users are looking at approximated VWAP and decide whether to extend tick retention.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Hi-fi frames complete for fib retracement/extension, fib time zones, anchored VWAP with bands, and the measure tool, in dark and light.
- [ ] Label-collision rule written precisely enough to implement and validated on five compressed cases.
- [ ] Density study complete with measured contrast values on a benchmark-density footprint chart.
- [ ] Approximate-badge behaviour specified and unavoidable in the fallback path.
- [ ] Distinguishability from E13 indicator overlays demonstrated.
- [ ] Chart-engine engineer has confirmed the label/text budget is implementable.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-fib-vwap-measure.md` merged; pitchfork explicitly marked deferred.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the consuming Sprint 07-08 stories.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D02** interaction model, **E14-D03** rail and token baseline.
- E13 indicator visual language for the distinguishability check (reference only).

## Branch
`design/e14-fib-vwap-measure`

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-036, SCR-037, SCR-045

title: Hi-fi design: long/short position tool and its send-to-ticket handoff
body:
## Context
The long/short position tool (US-DRAW-007) is the only drawing that produces numbers a user will act on with real money. Drag an entry, a stop and a target and it tells you your risk in USDT, your reward in USDT, your R:R and the position size implied by the active account profile - and then offers to open the order ticket pre-filled with all of it. That makes it a drawing in mechanics and a trading surface in consequence, and it is the reason this design ticket carries the `security` label while the rest of the drawing kit does not.

Two invariants drive the design. First, the sizing maths must be *identical* to US-PROF-002's (shared implementation, per the story's NFR) - the tool may not become a second, subtly different risk calculator. Second, when the implied risk exceeds the profile's cap, the tool must show it and disable send-to-ticket with the reason stated, rather than letting an over-risk trade flow onward.

Designed in Sprint 05, ahead of the Sprint 08-09 story that builds it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for the **long** and **short** variants: entry band, stop zone, target zone, the three drag handles, and the fill treatments that make risk-versus-reward readable at a glance without relying on red/green alone.
- **Read-out panel**: R:R, risk in USDT, reward in USDT, implied size in contracts and in USDT notional, entry/stop/target prices, and the account profile the sizing came from - with the primary read-out determined by E14-D01's findings and the rest secondary.
- **Drag order** frames following E14-D01's recommendation, including the intermediate states where only entry-and-stop exist and the reward side is still undefined.
- **State matrix**: default, dragging, selected, locked, risk-within-cap, **risk-exceeds-cap (error)**, no-account-profile-selected, symbol-not-tradable, stop-on-the-wrong-side-of-entry (invalid geometry), and tick/lot rounding applied (SCR-037 validation note).
- **Send-to-ticket handoff** frames: the affordance, the disabled state with its reason text, and the resulting pre-filled order ticket showing exactly which fields were populated and which the user must still confirm.
- **Multi-account context**: what the read-out shows when the active context is a trade group rather than a single account (either a stated per-account breakdown or an explicit statement that sizing shown is for the primary account only).
- Copy deck for every number label, unit and error string, reviewed for the advice boundary (R9) - the tool describes arithmetic, never a recommendation.
- `docs/design/specs/e14-position-tool.md` with redlines and the read-out field table.

## Out of scope
- The order ticket itself (E29/E30 series) - this ticket specifies only what is handed to it and what the handoff frame looks like.
- Risk-cap definition, lockouts and the kill switch (E39) - consumed here, not designed here.
- Placing an order from the drawing directly; the tool never places orders, and the design must make that impossible to misread.
- Native SL invariant enforcement (E32) - a backend guarantee, referenced in the copy but not designed here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Risk, reward and size are visible without hovering
  Given a completed long position tool on the chart
  When the frame is reviewed at default zoom and density
  Then R:R, risk in USDT, reward in USDT and implied size are all legible without any hover or click
  And each number carries its unit

Scenario: Implied risk exceeds the profile cap
  Given the dragged stop implies a loss greater than the active profile's risk cap
  Then the tool renders in its error state, the offending number is called out in text (not colour alone)
  And send-to-ticket is disabled with a reason string that names the cap and the computed value

Scenario: Invalid geometry
  Given the user drags the stop above the entry on a long
  Then the frames define whether the tool auto-flips to short or refuses with an inline explanation
  And whichever is chosen, no read-out ever displays a negative or nonsensical R:R

Scenario: No account profile is active
  Given no per-account profile is selected for the current context
  Then size is shown as unavailable with an explanation and a path to select a profile
  And send-to-ticket is disabled rather than defaulting to an assumed size

Scenario: Send to ticket pre-fills, it does not place
  Given send-to-ticket is used
  Then the frames show the order ticket opening pre-filled and unarmed
  And the spec states explicitly that no order is placed by this action under any circumstance
```

## Technical notes / design
The read-out is DOM, not canvas text: the numbers must be selectable, copyable, screen-reader readable and precisely typeset, and rendering them into the canvas would forfeit all four. The geometry (bands, handles, fills) is canvas; the panel is an anchored DOM overlay. The spec states this split because it determines the engineering shape.

Sizing values are *displayed* results of the shared US-PROF-002 implementation. The design annotates every number with its source so an implementer is never tempted to recompute locally: entry/stop/target from the drawing's anchors, tick/lot rounding from the instrument, size and risk from the profile engine.

Rounding is shown, not hidden: if lot rounding changes the implied size, the panel shows the rounded value as the operative one, because that is the number that would actually be traded.

## Test plan
(1) State-matrix walk in dark and light including every error state. (2) Number-formatting review against the product's number/locale rules for price, contracts and USDT notional, including very small and very large values. (3) Copy review against the advice boundary (R9) - no string may read as a recommendation. (4) Keyboard-only walkthrough: create by keyboard, move each handle by arrow keys with tick stepping, reach the read-out, reach send-to-ticket. (5) Screen-reader script covering the announcement of live-changing numbers during a drag (polite, coalesced - not a flood). (6) A cross-check session with the E39 risk-caps and E29 order-ticket design owners to confirm the handoff contract and the cap semantics match. (7) Handoff dry run with an FE engineer.

## Security notes
This is the drawing kit's sole safety-critical surface and is treated as such. The design forbids any path from the drawing to order placement: send-to-ticket produces an unarmed, pre-filled ticket that still passes the ticket's own validation, confirmation and arming, and the spec says so in normative language. The risk-cap error state is a *hard* gate in the design, not a warning that can be dismissed - a design that allows send-to-ticket while over cap is a design defect of the highest severity. The panel displays account-derived values (profile name, risk cap, size); it must show only the active context's account and must not enumerate other accounts a Viewer-role user cannot see, so RBAC filtering of the profile selector is stated as a requirement. Values in the read-out are display-only and never become a source of truth for the order - the ticket re-derives from the profile engine. Finally, the tool's inputs are user-dragged geometry, so the spec requires the ticket handoff to carry prices, not pixel positions, eliminating any scale-dependent mis-transfer. These items feed the E14 STRIDE session.

## Accessibility notes
Every handle is a focusable DOM-mirrored control with a name stating what it is and its current price; arrow keys move it by one tick, Shift+arrow by ten (US-DRAW-001 NFR, applied here). The read-out is a definition-list-shaped region whose values update politely and are coalesced so a drag does not flood the screen reader. Risk and reward are never distinguished by colour alone - each carries a text label and a direction word. The error state is announced when it is entered and its reason is programmatically associated with the disabled send-to-ticket control, so a screen-reader user learns why the action is unavailable. Specified against `05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 5, 7, 8.

## Performance notes
Dragging a handle recomputes size and risk on every frame; the spec requires the recomputation to be coalesced to the engine frame cadence and the DOM panel to update at no more than the documented rate, so the drag stays inside SCR-037's >=58 fps budget with 200 drawings present. The canvas geometry is part of the drawings layer and must not trigger a price/footprint re-render.

## Observability
Annotates `drawing.position_tool_created`, `drawing.position_tool_sent_to_ticket` (audit-relevant: it precedes a trading action) and `drawing.position_tool_blocked_by_cap` with the cap value and computed risk, so blocked-by-cap frequency is measurable and can inform whether caps are set sensibly.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Long and short frames complete with the full state matrix in dark and light.
- [ ] Read-out field table complete, each field annotated with its source of truth.
- [ ] Risk-exceeds-cap gate specified as hard and non-dismissible; send-to-ticket disabled with reason.
- [ ] Send-to-ticket handoff contract agreed in writing with the E29 order-ticket and E39 risk-cap design owners.
- [ ] Copy deck reviewed against the advice boundary and the number-formatting rules.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs passed, including live-value announcement coalescing.
- [ ] Security engineer has reviewed the surface as an input to the E14 STRIDE model.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-position-tool.md` merged; SCR-037 and US-DRAW-007 amended if anything diverged.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D01** (drag order and primary read-out), **E14-D02** (interaction model).
- Sizing semantics from US-PROF-002 and risk caps from E39; order-ticket handoff shape from E29/E30 (contract agreement, not delivery).

## Branch
`design/e14-position-tool-hifi`

## References
