title: Implement subscriptions, the topic registry, per-topic authorisation and live revocation
body:
## Context
This is the control plane a trader's workspace actually talks to: a four-pane chart layout opens and closes topics constantly as panes mount, symbols change, panes scroll out of view and tabs are backgrounded. `23-ws-protocol.md` section 5.4 is explicit about why `ctl` exists rather than unsub/sub: "a pane that scrolls out of view drops to 1 000 ms, a maximised DOM goes to 20 ms, a backgrounded Electron window goes to 1 000 ms for everything. Doing that with unsub/sub would re-snapshot a 200-level book every time the user switches tabs."

It is also where **authorisation** lives. `20-architecture.md` principle P8 and protocol goal G5 require authorisation to be server-authoritative and revocable mid-connection: a manager must not reach another manager's accounts even by hand-crafting a raw frame, and withdrawing a grant must terminate the affected subscriptions *visibly* (`revoked`) rather than silently emptying them, "which would look like a flat book or a closed position".

Covers US-MKT-005 (single upstream subscription fanned out to all consumers; unsubscribe after a 30-second grace period when the last consumer closes) and US-MKT-003's NFR (one batched `ticker` subscription for the whole watchlist, at most 10 topics per subscribe frame).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Topic registry and parser** for the full section 6 catalogue. Public: `book.{symbol}.{depth}` (depth in {1,50,200,500} in the *name*), `trades.{symbol}`, `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, `heatmap.{symbol}`, `profile.{symbol}.{kind}`, `metrics.{symbol}`, `ticker.{symbol}`, `ticker` (batched, `symbols` at most 40), `liquidations.{symbol}`, `liquidations`. Private: `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`, `trade_groups`, `rules`, `alerts`, `recorder`, `system`. Parsing rules: dots are illegal inside `param`; `atr:14` and `10:3` use a colon; an unknown family yields `unknown_topic`, a malformed string yields `invalid_topic_format`, a non-USDT-linear-perp symbol yields `unsupported_symbol`.
- **`sub` handling** (section 5.1): per-topic `opts`, `snapshot` flag, `replay_session_id` accepted and validated (routing is E26). **Unknown option keys are rejected, never ignored** (requirement S12) so typos surface immediately. Universal options `throttle_ms` (floored at 50), `encoding` (`binary`|`structured`, `encoding_unsupported` when the topic has no binary form), `coalesce`.
- **`sub_ok`** (section 5.2): exactly one result per requested topic, **in request order** (requirement S1); partial success is normal - one bad topic never fails the batch; every ok result carries `sub_id`, `snapshot_pending` and an `effective` block echoing the options **after clamping**.
- **`unsub` / `unsub_ok`** (section 5.3): idempotent - unsubscribing from an unknown or already-removed topic returns `ok: true, noop: true`, because pane-close races are normal.
- **`ctl` / `ctl_ok`** (section 5.4): retune `throttle_ms` live without re-snapshot; changing `depth`, `price_grouping`, `bar_type`/`param`, `time_bucket_ms` or the `metrics` list answers `ctl_ok` with `resnapshot: true` and triggers a fresh `snap` (the emission itself is E17-S03). `ctl` on an unsubscribed topic yields `not_subscribed`.
- **Permission matrix** (section 6.3): `marketdata:read` for all public families; `orders:read` for `orders`/`trade_groups`; `positions:read`; `executions:read`; `accounts:read` for `wallet`; `rules:read`; `alerts:read` (own alerts only); `recording:read`; `system` implicit and role-filtered. Missing permission yields `forbidden`.
- **Account-scope narrowing** (section 6.2): intersect requested `exchange_account_ids` with the caller's grants and **silently narrow**, reporting the effective list in `sub_ok.effective`; requesting *only* out-of-scope accounts yields `account_scope_denied`.
- **Live revocation** (section 9.5, requirement S7): re-evaluate authorisation on every change to roles, permissions, account grants and on kill-switch transitions; terminate affected subscriptions with a `revoked` frame carrying `reason` from the closed set (`permission_revoked`, `account_scope_changed`, `user_disabled`, `session_revoked`, `key_revoked`, `account_disabled`, `replay_session_ended`, `resync_rate_limited`, `topic_removed`), `removed_accounts` where applicable and `resubscribe_allowed`. A fully disabled user gets `bye` and close `4403`.
- **Limits** (section 16.2): 200 subscriptions per connection (`subscription_limit`), 50 topics per `sub` frame (`too_many_topics`), 40 symbols per connection, duplicate subscribe yields `duplicate_subscription` with the advice to use `ctl`.
- **Upstream reference counting** (US-MKT-005): one upstream subscription per (symbol, topic) regardless of how many connections or panes want it; when the last consumer unsubscribes, the upstream subscription is dropped after a **30-second grace period**, so a pane close followed by a reopen does not churn the exchange connection.
- **Replay coexistence** (section 11): a live and a replay subscription to the same topic name coexist, disambiguated by `sub_id`, with replay frames carrying `rs`. Private topics with a `replay_session_id` are rejected with `invalid_options`.

## Out of scope
- Emitting snapshots and deltas, sequencing and resync (E17-S03).
- Coalescing, adaptive throttling and backpressure (E17-T03) - this story clamps and records the *requested* values; enforcement of cadence is there.
- The replay clock and session lifecycle (E26).
- The content of any payload - produced by E08/E12/E18-E25/E29.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Partial success is normal
  Given a sub frame requesting book.BTCUSDT.50, trades.BTCUSDT and orders for an out-of-scope account
  Then sub_ok returns three results in request order, the first two ok with sub_id and effective, the third failing with account_scope_denied
  And the two accepted subscriptions are active

Scenario: Clamping is reported, not silent
  Given a client requests throttle_ms 5 on book.BTCUSDT.50
  Then sub_ok effective reports throttle_ms 50 so the client stops expecting 200 frames per second

Scenario: An unknown option is an error, not a shrug
  Given a client subscribes to footprint.BTCUSDT.time.5 with an option key min_stak
  Then the topic is rejected with invalid_options naming the field, and no subscription is created

Scenario: Malformed topic names are distinguished
  Given the topics book.BTCUSDT.77, bars.BTCUSDT.time.1.5 and book.ETHUSD.50
  Then they are rejected with invalid_topic_format, invalid_topic_format and unsupported_symbol respectively

Scenario: Teardown is idempotent
  Given a pane closes twice in a race and unsubscribes book.BTCUSDT.50 twice
  Then both unsub_ok results are ok true, the second carrying noop true, and no error is raised

Scenario: ctl retunes without re-snapshot
  Given an active book.BTCUSDT.50 subscription at sequence 3000
  When the client sends ctl with throttle_ms 200
  Then ctl_ok reports effective throttle_ms 200, resnapshot is absent or false, and the sequence continues from 3001

Scenario: ctl that changes state identity forces a re-snapshot
  Given an active heatmap.BTCUSDT subscription
  When the client sends ctl with time_bucket_ms 1000
  Then ctl_ok carries resnapshot true and a fresh snap follows

Scenario: A manager cannot reach another manager's accounts by raw frame
  Given a manager whose scope contains only account A
  When it sends a hand-crafted sub for positions with exchange_account_ids [B]
  Then the topic is rejected with account_scope_denied and no positions data is ever emitted for B

Scenario: Grants withdrawn mid-stream are announced
  Given a manager is subscribed to positions for accounts A and B
  When the owner withdraws account B
  Then a revoked frame arrives within 1 second with reason account_scope_changed and removed_accounts [B]
  And the subscription for A and all other topics continue uninterrupted

Scenario: Limits are enforced
  Given a connection holding 200 subscriptions
  When it subscribes to one more
  Then the request is rejected with subscription_limit and the existing subscriptions are untouched

Scenario: The upstream is shared and not churned
  Given three panes across two connections all view book.BTCUSDT.50
  Then exactly one upstream Bybit subscription exists
  And when the last of them closes, the upstream subscription is dropped only after a 30-second grace period

Scenario: system cannot be unsubscribed
  Given an authenticated connection
  When it sends unsub for system
  Then the request is refused and the connection remains subscribed
```

## Technical notes / design
`SubscriptionManager` holds per-connection state: `{sub_id -> Subscription{topic, opts_effective, seq, class, replay_session_id}}`, plus reverse indexes by topic and by account so a grant change resolves affected subscriptions in O(affected) rather than scanning every connection.

The topic registry is **data, not code branches**: one declarative table per family giving the name pattern, the option schema (with types, ranges and defaults), the required permission, the scope-narrowing rule, the default throttle, whether a binary form exists, and the payload schema `$id`. `sub_ok.effective`, the error messages and the E17-Q01 conformance tests are all generated from that table, so adding a topic in R2 (footprint, heatmap, profile, metrics already listed; detectors added later) is a table entry, not a new code path. This is the concrete mechanism behind the R1 goal "freeze the WS protocol so R2/R3 add topics without renegotiating transport".

Authorisation is evaluated by calling E09's RBAC service - never by a local copy of the rules. Revocation is driven by subscribing to E09's grant-change and kill-switch events on the internal bus; the handler must complete within 1 s for the acceptance criterion to hold, so it resolves affected subscriptions from the reverse index and enqueues `revoked` frames ahead of data frames.

Upstream reference counting is keyed by (symbol, family, params) across *all* connections, with a 30 s `asyncio` timer cancelled on re-subscription.

Errors: `unknown_topic`, `invalid_topic_format`, `unsupported_symbol`, `invalid_options`, `encoding_unsupported`, `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`, `subscription_limit`, `too_many_topics`, `duplicate_subscription`, `not_subscribed` - all from section 10.2, none invented (requirement S10).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: topic parser over a table of valid and invalid names covering every family, depth enum, bar-type/param colon forms, and dotted-param rejection; option validation per family including boundary values (`min_stack` 2 and 10, `throttle_ms` 5/50/1000, `symbols` 40 and 41); permission matrix as a role x topic fixture matrix; scope-narrowing intersection including the empty-intersection case.
- **Integration**: partial-success `sub`; idempotent `unsub`; `ctl` both with and without re-snapshot; **grant revocation mid-stream yields `revoked` within 1 s with other topics intact** (named in section 16.4); limits; upstream reference counting with the 30 s grace window (time-mocked); live plus replay coexistence on one topic name.
- **Contract**: `sub`, `sub_ok`, `unsub`, `unsub_ok`, `ctl`, `ctl_ok`, `revoked`, `err` validate against section 13.5-13.6 schemas; no emitted error code lies outside section 10.2.
- **Security**: cross-account raw-frame subscribe denied; viewer subscribing to `orders` succeeds read-only.
- Coverage target: at least 85%.

## Security notes
This is the Epic's primary **elevation-of-privilege** surface (`04-security-program.md` section 5). Controls: server-side permission check at subscribe time *and* on every grant change (never trusting a client-side gate); silent narrowing rather than error on partial scope so a client cannot probe which accounts exist by differential error messages; explicit `revoked` rather than silent emptying; closed `reason` enum so no internal detail leaks. Rejecting unknown option keys also closes a parameter-smuggling avenue. Data classification: private topic subscriptions are confidential and their subscribe attempts are audited. **Security review label required.**

## Accessibility notes
Indirect: the `revoked` reason strings surface to the user through the E17-D02 copy deck. They must be mapped to plain-English sentences ("Access to account ... was withdrawn") rather than raw enum values, and announced as `role="status"` unless the whole session ended.

## Performance notes
Subscribe of a 4-pane workspace (roughly 12 topics) must complete in under 100 ms p95 excluding snapshot construction. Grant-change fan-out must resolve and enqueue `revoked` within 1 s at 8 connections x 200 subscriptions. The registry lookup is a dict hit, not a regex scan per frame - topic strings are parsed once at subscribe time and never re-parsed on the data path.

## Observability
`cv_ws_topics_per_client` gauge; `cv_ws_subscribe_total{family,result}`; `cv_ws_revoked_total{reason}`; `cv_ws_upstream_refcount{symbol,family}` gauge; audit events `ws.subscribe.denied{code}` and `ws.subscription.revoked{reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated and green.
- [ ] Topic registry is declarative and the conformance tests are generated from it.
- [ ] Contract tests green for every control frame in scope; error-catalogue closure asserted.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85%.
- [ ] Security review recorded; the cross-account raw-frame test is present and green.
- [ ] Metrics and audit events on E04's dashboards.
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md` sections 5 and 6 reconciled with the implementation.
- [ ] Two approvals including one code-owner.

## Dependencies
- **E17-S01** - an authenticated connection with identity, permissions and account scope resolved.
- **E09** - RBAC service, grant-change events, audit writer.
- **E08** - upstream subscription management that reference counting drives.

## Branch
`feat/e17-ws-subscriptions`

## References
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md sections 5, 6, 9.5, 10.2, 11, 13.5, 13.6, 16.1 (S1, S7, S10, S12), 16.2
- docs/plan/20-architecture.md section 3.12, principle P8
- docs/plan/11-user-stories.md US-MKT-003, US-MKT-005
- docs/plan/04-security-program.md section 5

title: Build packages/protocol WS schema extraction, codegen and the ws_message_schemas gate
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` sections 13-15 contain **34 fenced JSON Schemas** - the control frames, the nine public payloads and the nine private payloads - and section 16.5 makes the Markdown the single source of truth: "`tools/contracts/extract_ws_schemas.py` parses every fenced json block in sections 13-15, keyed by its `$id`, and bundles them into `ws-schemas.json` - the single artefact consumed by the server (runtime response validation in dev/test), the TypeScript client codegen, and the `ws_message_schemas` gate. The Markdown is the source of truth; the bundle is always regenerated, never hand-edited."

Nothing in the rest of this Epic can be trusted without this: it is what turns "the doc says X" into "the build fails if the code does not do X", and it is the mechanism behind R1 exit criterion 7.

E02-T09 already built `packages/protocol` codegen from the OpenAPI document; this ticket adds the WS half.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tools/contracts/extract_ws_schemas.py`: parse every fenced ```json block in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` sections 13-15, key by `$id`, bundle to `packages/protocol/ws-schemas.json`. Deterministic output (sorted keys, stable formatting) so a regeneration diff is meaningful.
- `tools/contracts/validate_ws_schemas.py --draft 2020-12`: meta-validate every extracted schema, assert every `$ref` resolves **inside the bundle**, and validate **every example frame in section 12** against its declared schema. This is the blocking CI gate **`ws_message_schemas`** registered under `22-api-openapi.yaml` `x-contract-validation.gates`, running in job `contracts` / workflow `.github/workflows/contracts.yml`.
- Code generation into `packages/protocol`:
  - **Python**: `msgspec.Struct` (or pydantic v2, matching whatever E02-T09 chose for REST) models per frame type and payload, plus the topic-name and enum constants of section 6.
  - **TypeScript**: `.d.ts` types plus runtime validators for the same set, exported for `apps/web` and for `packages/chart-engine`'s feed decoder types.
- `make gen` integration and the staleness check: `make gen && git diff --exit-code` fails CI if generated output is stale (`20-architecture.md` section on tooling).
- Unit tests for the extractor itself: a schema block with a duplicate `$id` fails loudly; a block that is not valid JSON fails loudly; an added block appears in the bundle without any other edit.
- README in `packages/protocol` stating the one rule: edit the Markdown, never the bundle.

## Out of scope
- The binary codec (E17-T02) - schemas describe the *structured* form; binary/structured equivalence is asserted in E17-T02 and E17-Q01.
- The error registry generator (E17-T05).
- The REST half of `packages/protocol` (E02-T09, already done).
- Runtime validation being switched on in production - dev and test only, by config.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The bundle is generated and complete
  When make gen runs
  Then ws-schemas.json contains one entry per fenced schema in 23-ws-protocol.md sections 13-15, keyed by $id, with no duplicates

Scenario: The gate blocks drift
  Given a developer edits a generated TypeScript type by hand
  When CI runs
  Then the staleness check fails with a diff and the merge is blocked

Scenario: A malformed schema is caught
  Given a schema block in the Markdown uses an invalid JSON-Schema keyword
  When validate_ws_schemas.py runs
  Then the gate fails naming the offending $id and keyword

Scenario: Documented examples are truthful
  Given every example frame in 23-ws-protocol.md section 12
  When the gate runs
  Then each example validates against the schema it claims to be an instance of, and a deliberately broken example fails the gate

Scenario: A dangling ref is caught
  Given a schema references a $ref that exists in no other block
  Then the gate fails naming both the referring schema and the missing target
```

## Technical notes / design
Extraction keys on `$id`, not on heading order, so re-ordering the document is harmless and renaming a schema is a visible, reviewable change.

The extractor must tolerate `jsonc`-fenced blocks containing `//` comments (section 12's examples use them) by stripping line comments before parsing **only** for the example-validation path - schemas in sections 13-15 are strict `json` and must not contain comments; if one does, that is an error worth failing on.

`make contracts` must run this gate offline in under 10 s along with the other five local gates (section 16.5), so the extractor may not require a database or a running API.

Generated Python and TS live under a `generated/` directory with a header comment naming the generator and forbidding hand edits.

## Test plan
- Unit: duplicate `$id`; invalid JSON; unknown JSON-Schema keyword; dangling `$ref`; comment in a section 13-15 block; a new block appearing in the bundle; deterministic output across two runs.
- Contract: the gate itself is the contract test; a fixture repository state with a deliberately broken example is used to assert the gate fails (negative test, so the gate cannot silently pass forever).
- Coverage target: at least 85% on `tools/contracts/`.

## Security notes
The extractor parses a repository-controlled Markdown file, not user input, so injection risk is low - but it must not `eval` and must use a strict JSON parser. Generated code is committed, so the staleness gate also serves as a supply-chain integrity check: nobody can slip a change into a generated artefact without the source change being visible.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
`make contracts` budget: this gate's share of the under-10 s offline total is at most 3 s on the reference machine for 34 schemas plus the section 12 examples.

## Observability
CI job output lists the schema count and the example count validated, so a silent drop in coverage (extractor stops finding blocks) is visible rather than green.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Extractor, validator and generators merged; `ws-schemas.json` committed and deterministic.
- [ ] `ws_message_schemas` registered as a blocking gate in the `contracts` job and observed failing on a deliberate break.
- [ ] `make gen` staleness check wired and observed failing on a hand edit.
- [ ] Unit tests at at least 85% coverage; negative gate test in place.
- [ ] `packages/protocol` README documents the source-of-truth rule.
- [ ] Code review by a code-owner of `tools/contracts/`; PR merged via merge queue.

`feat/e17-ws-protocol-schemas`

title: Implement the CVWB binary frame codec (header + body kinds 1-6) in Python and TypeScript
body:
## Context
The whole point of ADR-0005's data plane is that the browser can take a received `ArrayBuffer` and produce typed-array views over it with **no parse and no copy**, hand them to the GPU, and stay inside the 16.6 ms frame budget. That only works if both ends agree, byte for byte, on the fixed layout specified in `23-ws-protocol.md` section 3.4.

This ticket implements that layout once, in two languages, generated from one declaration - the mitigation ADR-0005 names for its own stated risk: "Two encodings to maintain and test. Mitigated by generating both the Python encoder and the TS decoder from a single schema declaration in `packages/protocol`, with a round-trip property test."

It is also the single largest *security* surface of the Epic: `04-security-program.md` **SR-128** requires every array length and offset to be validated on decode and forbids allocating from an untrusted length field without bounds checks, and **SR-155** requires a fuzz corpus against this decoder.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Layout declaration** in `packages/protocol` (a single data structure describing header and each body kind), from which both implementations are generated or driven.
- **Common header, 24 bytes, little-endian** exactly as section 3.4: `magic u32 = 0x43565742` ("CVWB"), `format_version u8 = 1`, `body_kind u8`, `flags u8` (bit0 estimated, bit1 coalesced, bit2 replay, bit3 partial), `price_scale u8`, `qty_scale u8`, 3 reserved zero bytes, `record_count u32`, `ts_base_ms u64`.
- **Body kinds**:
  - 1/2 book snapshot/delta - 17-byte records `{u8 side, i64 price, u64 size}`; size 0 means delete; snapshot appends a 16-byte trailer `{u64 xu, u64 xseq}`; snapshot ordering bids descending then asks ascending.
  - 3 trades - 22-byte records `{u32 ts_offset_ms, i64 price, u64 size, u8 side, u8 flags}`.
  - 4 bars - 69-byte records `{u32 ts_offset_ms, i64 o,h,l,c, u64 v, u64 turnover, u32 trades, i64 delta, u8 flags}` with bit0 `confirm`.
  - 5 footprint - per-bar group `{u32 ts_offset_ms, u32 cell_count}` then cells of 33 bytes `{i64 price, u64 bid_volume, u64 ask_volume, u32 trades, u8 flags}`.
  - 6 heatmap column - `{u32 ts_offset_ms, i64 price_min, i64 price_step, u32 row_count}` then rows of 16 bytes `{u64 bid_size, u64 ask_size}`.
- **Python encoder** (`services/api`, via `packages/protocol`): builds frames from internal event objects using scaled integers derived from the symbol's `price_scale`/`qty_scale`; zero-copy where `memoryview` allows; one encode per topic emission reused across subscribers.
- **TypeScript decoder** (`packages/protocol`, consumed by `apps/web` and `packages/chart-engine`): returns typed-array views over the received buffer without copying; validates `magic` and `format_version`; ignores trailing unknown bytes (forward compatibility, client rule C10); raises a typed `FrameMalformedError` when body length disagrees with `record_count`.
- **Structured equivalence**: a `toStructured()` path for every kind producing the section 14 schema shape, used by contract tests and by `cv.v1.json` clients (base64, `e: "b64"`).
- **Base64 wrapping** for `cv.v1.json` per section 3.2.
- **Fuzz corpus** committed under `tests/fuzz/ws-frames/` with seeds: truncated bodies, `record_count` larger than the buffer, `record_count` of 2^32-1, wrong magic, future `format_version`, negative scales, NaN-shaped bit patterns in integer fields, zero-length bodies, oversized footprint `cell_count`.

## Out of scope
- Deciding *when* to send binary vs structured (E17-S02 option handling) and *what* to send (E17-S03).
- Compression (section 3.5: deflate off for msgpack, on for JSON) - a socket-level concern configured in E17-S01.
- Snapshot chunking above 4 MiB (E17-S03) - the codec only sets and reads the `partial` flag.
- Replay clock semantics (E26); the codec only sets the `replay` flag bit.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Round trip is exact
  Given any valid internal event batch for any of the six body kinds
  When it is encoded in Python and decoded in TypeScript
  Then the decoded values equal the source exactly, including scaled integers, deletes at size 0 and every flag bit

Scenario: Binary and structured agree
  Given a frame encoded in binary and the same source encoded structured
  When both are normalised
  Then they are deeply equal, and this is asserted for all six kinds in CI

Scenario: A malformed frame never crashes and never over-allocates
  Given a frame whose record_count is 4294967295 but whose body is 32 bytes
  When the decoder runs
  Then it raises FrameMalformedError without allocating memory proportional to record_count
  And the server-side decoder equivalently rejects without panicking

Scenario: Forward compatibility
  Given a frame with 8 unknown trailing bytes after a valid body
  Then the decoder returns the valid records and ignores the trailing bytes

Scenario: Wrong magic is rejected
  Given a frame whose first four bytes are not 0x43565742
  Then the decoder raises FrameMalformedError and the client resyncs rather than rendering

Scenario: Decode stays inside budget
  Given a 50-level binary book delta and a 400-cell footprint bar
  Then decode p99 is under 0.15 ms and under 1.0 ms respectively on the reference machine
```

## Technical notes / design
All integers little-endian. Prices and sizes are **scaled 64-bit integers** using the per-symbol `price_scale`/`qty_scale` announced in the topic snapshot - never floats, never decimal strings, because both cost the render path. `ts_base_ms u64` plus `u32` per-record offsets bounds a frame's time span to ~49 days, which is far beyond any real frame and is therefore safe.

Python: `struct`/`memoryview` with pre-sized `bytearray`; avoid per-record object allocation. TypeScript: a single `DataView` for the header then `BigInt64Array`/`BigUint64Array`/`Uint32Array` subarray views for the body; note that record strides of 17, 22, 33 and 69 bytes are **not** 8-byte aligned, so typed-array views cannot be taken directly over interleaved records - decode into pre-allocated column arrays (struct-of-arrays) sized from `record_count` **after** a bounds check against the actual buffer length. That bounds check is SR-128 and is the single most important line in the file.

Error code on failure is `frame_malformed` (section 10.2), connection-scoped, closes.

Records are hard-capped before allocation: `record_count * stride + header + trailer` must equal the remaining buffer length exactly, otherwise reject. This makes over-allocation structurally impossible rather than defended against.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: per kind, encode/decode of empty, single-record, and max-size bodies; every flag bit; size-0 delete; snapshot trailer presence and absence; scale round-trip at scales 0-8; bid/ask ordering in snapshots.
- **Property (hypothesis / fast-check)**: arbitrary valid event batches round-trip Python encode to TS decode to re-encode **byte-identical** (ADR-0005's stated contract test).
- **Contract**: binary decoded then validated against the section 14 structured schema, all six kinds (section 16.4 "binary/structured equivalence").
- **Fuzz**: Atheris against the Python decoder and a JS fuzzer against the TS decoder, corpus committed, nightly 30-minute run per `04-security-program.md` section on fuzzing; a new crash blocks the next release.
- **Bench**: decode p99 per kind asserted against the section 16.3 budgets, wired as a CI benchmark.
- Coverage target: at least 85%; the decoder's error branches specifically must be covered, not just the happy path.

## Security notes
Threats: `04-security-program.md` **T-W1** ("Malformed/hostile exchange frame crashes a parser or triggers unbounded allocation") applies symmetrically to our own client-facing frames if an attacker can inject them. Controls: SR-128 bounds checking (exact-length equality before allocation), SR-155 fuzz corpus, strict magic and version checks, no dynamic allocation from untrusted lengths, typed errors instead of exceptions escaping to a generic handler. Data classification: internal (public market data). **Security review label required.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Budgets from section 16.3: book delta (50 levels) decode under 0.15 ms p99 (hard fail above 0.5 ms); footprint bar (400 cells) under 1.0 ms p99 (hard fail above 3 ms). Server-side encode must fit inside the 7 ms fan-out slice of budget #6's 20 ms envelope (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.1 table). Encode-once-send-many is mandatory: per-subscriber re-encoding is a defect, not an optimisation opportunity.

## Observability
`cv_ws_frame_encode_seconds{kind}` and `cv_ws_frame_bytes{kind}` histograms server-side; a client-side decode-duration mark per kind feeding the frontend performance panel.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both implementations merged, driven from the single layout declaration.
- [ ] Round-trip property test green; binary/structured equivalence asserted for all six kinds.
- [ ] Fuzz corpus committed; nightly fuzz job wired; zero crashes.
- [ ] Decode benchmarks recorded against section 16.3 and wired into CI.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85% including error branches.
- [ ] Security engineer review recorded (SR-128, SR-155).
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md` section 3.4 amended if any layout detail proved wrong during implementation (spec follows reality once, deliberately, then freezes).

## Dependencies
- **E17-K01** confirms the binary data plane is the right choice before this is built.
- **E17-T01** supplies `packages/protocol` and the structured schemas the equivalence test validates against.

## Branch
`feat/e17-binary-codec`

## References

- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0005-ws-protocol-and-binary-encoding.md

title: STRIDE threat model for the client WS protocol and gateway
body:
## Context
`04-security-program.md` section 5 requires a STRIDE model per epic ("Every area is re-reviewed when its epic enters design"), `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1 makes the kickoff a DoR item, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 names the three concerns for E17 specifically: **WS auth, topic authorization, resource exhaustion**.

E17 deserves a careful model rather than a checkbox because it is the component where three security-relevant things meet: an **unauthenticated socket exists for up to 10 seconds by design** (browser WebSockets cannot carry headers, so auth is a first frame - section 4.3); **authorisation is evaluated continuously rather than once**, since grants can change mid-connection; and the server **deliberately holds per-connection state and queues**, which is exactly the shape an attacker exploits for resource exhaustion.

It is also the component through which a hostile or corrupt frame reaches a **binary decoder** on both ends - `04-security-program.md` threat **T-W1** ("Malformed/hostile exchange frame crashes a parser or triggers unbounded allocation") applies to our own client-facing framing, not only to the exchange's.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Data-flow diagram** of the gateway with trust boundaries drawn explicitly: untrusted client socket to `Handshake`; `Handshake` to E09 auth/RBAC; internal bus to `FeedMultiplexer`; `CoalescingQueue` to `FrameEncoder` to socket; the upstream ingestion boundary; and the browser-side worker/main boundary in `apps/web`.
- **STRIDE analysis per element and per flow**, in the table format of `04-security-program.md` section 5 (`T` id, STRIDE category, threat, likelihood, impact, risk, mitigating requirements, residual), covering at minimum:
  - **Spoofing** - token replay on a new socket; a stolen token used from another host; the 10 s unauthenticated window; `hello` impersonating another client build.
  - **Tampering** - hostile binary body (unbounded `record_count`, truncated body, wrong magic); option injection through unknown keys; topic-name injection attempting to escape the registry; envelope field injection.
  - **Repudiation** - a subscription to a private topic without an audit trail; a revocation that leaves no record.
  - **Information disclosure** - token in a URL, log, metric label or error message; cross-account data leaking through scope narrowing; differential error messages revealing which accounts exist; `connection_id`/`git_sha`/`request_id` exposure to a Viewer; `system` topic content not filtered by role.
  - **Denial of service** - slow consumer growing server memory; resync loop forcing snapshot rebuilds; subscription and symbol exhaustion; inbound frame flood; oversized inbound frame; connection exhaustion per user; expensive-topic amplification (200-depth book plus 2 000-column heatmap).
  - **Elevation of privilege** - subscribing to another account's private topics by raw frame; a stale permission set surviving a grant change; a `replay_session_id` reaching a private topic; kill-switch state not honoured.
- **Mapping each threat to its mitigating requirement** in `04-security-program.md` (notably **SR-040** strict schema plus size caps, **SR-128** bounds-checked binary decode, **SR-155** fuzzed decoders) and to the E17 ticket that implements it, so no threat is left with an unassigned control.
- **Residual risk statement** per threat, with Owner sign-off on anything accepted rather than mitigated.
- **Findings appended to `04-security-program.md` section 5** as a new area block (SR-157: per-epic output is appended, not kept in a side document).
- **Abuse-case seeds** handed to E17-X02 for adversarial testing.
- **Risk register update** (`32-risk-register.md`) for R3 (real-time cost) and any new entry the model surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the controls - they belong to E17-S01/S02/S03/T02/T03.
- Executing the adversarial tests (E17-X02).
- The auth and RBAC systems themselves (E09's own model); this model consumes them and asserts the boundary is used correctly.
- Upstream Bybit connection security (E08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category is addressed
  When the model is reviewed
  Then all six categories have at least one analysed threat or an explicit, reasoned out-of-band statement

Scenario: Every threat has an owner and a control
  Then each threat names a mitigating requirement and the E17 ticket implementing it, or is explicitly accepted with Owner sign-off

Scenario: The three named R1 concerns are covered in depth
  Then WS auth, topic authorization and resource exhaustion each have a dedicated analysis section rather than a single row

Scenario: A gap becomes work
  Given the model finds a threat with no implementing control
  Then a ticket is filed against the appropriate E17 story in the same sprint, not deferred to a backlog note

Scenario: The model is recorded where the programme expects it
  Then the findings are appended to 04-security-program.md section 5 as an E17 area block and referenced from this ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Two analyses deserve more than a table row and should be written out as short narratives:

**The 10-second unauthenticated window.** It cannot be removed (browser WebSockets cannot set headers, and a query-string token is worse - it lands in proxy logs and browser history). The model must therefore argue the window is *bounded and cheap*: 10 s timeout, 3 auth attempts, 8 connections per user, inbound rate limiting applied **before** auth as well as after, and no per-connection allocation beyond the socket until `auth_ok`. The residual risk is connection-slot exhaustion by an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the port - which Tailscale-only exposure reduces to "someone already on the tailnet", and that should be stated rather than assumed.

**Continuous authorisation.** A permission check at subscribe time is necessary but not sufficient, because a subscription can outlive the grant that justified it. The model must show that the revocation path (E17-S02's reverse index plus E09's grant-change events) has no gap in which data for a withdrawn account can still be emitted, and must consider the reconnect race that E17-Q02 tests.

## Test plan
The model produces the abuse cases E17-X02 executes; it is not itself a test. Its own review criterion: a second reviewer (Architect) attempts to name a threat the model missed, and either fails or the model is amended.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security deliverable. Data classification recorded per flow: public market-data topics are **internal**; private topics (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`, `trade_groups`) are **confidential** and account-scoped; the `auth_ok` payload is confidential (it enumerates the user's account scope); tokens are **secret**.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Several controls are also performance limits (subscription caps, queue bounds, resync rate limits). The model must state where a security limit and a performance budget are the same number, so neither is relaxed in isolation for the other's reasons - loosening the 8 MiB queue to help a slow link would silently remove a DoS control.

## Observability
The model specifies which threats must be **detectable**, not merely prevented: repeated `auth_failed` per identity, slow-consumer closes per identity, resync-rate-limit revocations, and denied cross-account subscribes - each with an audit event and a metric so abuse is visible rather than merely blocked.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] DFD with trust boundaries merged.
- [ ] STRIDE table complete, every threat mapped to a requirement and a ticket or explicitly accepted.
- [ ] The three R1-named concerns analysed in depth.
- [ ] Findings appended to `04-security-program.md` section 5 (SR-157).
- [ ] Abuse-case seeds handed to E17-X02.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated.
- [ ] Reviewed by the Architect and the Security engineer; Owner sign-off on any accepted residual risk.
- [ ] Any control gap filed as a ticket in the same sprint.

- **E17-S02** - the subscription and authorisation design being modelled must exist in reviewable form.
- **E09** - the auth and RBAC model this one builds on.

title: UX research: how traders read value, POC and profile period modes
body:
## Context
E19 introduces an analysis surface the Owner has used for years in other platforms but has never had drawn to our conventions: the volume / delta / TPO profile (SCR-038) and its settings dialog (SCR-039). The stories (US-VP-001 … US-VP-009) pack five period modes (session, fixed range, visible range, anchored, composite), three inputs (volume, delta, TPO), derived levels (POC, VAH, VAL, HVN/LVN, naked POC) and a developing-vs-final distinction into one panel. That is more simultaneous meaning than any other panel in the product carries, and the failure mode is not "ugly" — it is a trader reading a *developing* value area as if it were settled, or reading an *approximated-from-bars* profile (US-VP-001 scenario 3) as if it were tick-accurate, and trading it.

Before any pixels are committed we need evidence on three questions the catalogue does not answer: (a) which period mode is the default a trader reaches for first, and whether mode switching should be a segmented control or a menu; (b) how POC / VAH / VAL / HVN / LVN can be distinguished from each other *without relying on fill colour alone*, which `05-accessibility-standard.md` forbids and `16-design-system-brief.md` §6 data-viz rules re-state; (c) how strongly the "approximate" and "partial history" qualifiers must be signalled given `14-screens-catalogue.md` line 77 makes recorder-dependent emptiness a designed state.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3 moderated sessions (Owner + up to 2 account managers), 45 minutes each, using a scripted greyscale prototype of **SCR-038** fed from recorded BTCUSDT fixtures — no live backend.
- Tasks per session: find the session POC; switch to visible-range mode and pan; compare two sessions via a composite (US-VP-003); identify where sellers dominated using the delta profile (US-VP-007); read the TPO initial balance (US-VP-008); state whether the on-screen value area is final or still developing.
- Probes: "is this value area finished?", "what does this badge mean?", "which of these price levels would you put an order at and why?", "what is the smallest row size that still tells you something?".
- Competitive scan of profile presentation in TradingView (Fixed Range / Session Volume Profile), Sierra Chart / DeepCharts, and any market-profile tool the Owner already uses — specifically the labelling of POC/VAH/VAL, and whether developing value area is visually distinguished at all.
- Findings merged at `docs/design/research/e19-profiles.md`: default period mode recommendation, a ranked list of which derived levels must be *labelled in text* vs may be implied, the required prominence of the `EstimatedBadge` (CMP-227) and partial-history chip, and 6–10 adopted decisions each phrased as a testable statement a wireframe can satisfy or violate.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design, colour or token work — greyscale wireframes begin in E19-D02.
- Footprint cell reading (E18) and CVD pane reading (E23); the per-bar POC inside a footprint bar is E18's surface, not this one.
- Recorder administration (SCR-140) and retention policy comprehension — E16.
- Recruiting participants outside the Owner's circle.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every derived level has an evidenced treatment recommendation
  When docs/design/research/e19-profiles.md is reviewed
  Then POC, VAH, VAL, value-area shading, HVN, LVN, naked POC and single prints each carry a recommended label, prominence and a traceable observation

Scenario: Developing versus final value area is distinguishable
  Given a participant is shown a live developing session profile and a closed session profile side by side
  Then the report records whether they distinguished them unaided and recommends the treatment that made the distinction reliable

Scenario: An approximated profile is not mistaken for tick-accurate data
  Given a participant is shown a profile built from bar-approximated volume per US-VP-001
  When they are asked how the data was produced
  Then any misread is recorded verbatim and drives a decision that raises the prominence of the EstimatedBadge treatment

Scenario: A finding contradicts the catalogue
  Given a finding contradicts 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-038/SCR-039 or 24-internal-schemas.md section 5
  Then it is raised as a written amendment proposal against that document rather than silently designed around

Scenario: Colour-only encoding is challenged
  Given a participant views the prototype in the greyscale-only condition
  Then the report states which levels became unreadable and that finding is binding on E19-D03
```

## Technical notes / design
The prototype is a dev-only harness rendering `VolumeProfile` fixtures (`24-internal-schemas.md` §5.1) through greyscale primitives; it must not be promoted to production code. Fixtures must include at least one session with a POC tie (US-VP-004 scenario 3) and one composite where the recorder covers fewer sessions than requested (US-VP-003 scenario 3), because both are states we otherwise never rehearse with a user. Sessions are run in both the default density and the compact density mode from `16-design-system-brief.md` §3, since row height is the binding constraint on how many levels fit.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validity controls: task order is rotated per participant so the composite task does not always follow the session task; the greyscale-only condition is run last so it cannot prime colour expectations; two researchers code the transcripts independently and reconcile before a decision is marked adopted.

## Security notes
Session recordings follow `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md`. No real account identifiers, balances, positions or API keys appear in the harness — market fixtures only. Recordings are stored in the design drive with the standard retention, not in the repo.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session is run with a screen reader active against the table alternative described in SCR-038's a11y note, so the announcement of POC/VAH/VAL is validated with a user rather than asserted in a spec. A participant using the compact density mode is asked explicitly whether row labels remain legible at the smallest row size.

## Performance notes
N/A for the artefact. The research must however record the largest number of price rows participants found *useful* (not merely renderable); that number is an input to the 5 000-row budget stated in SCR-038 and to E19's rendering work.

## Observability
N/A. Analytics events `profile.period_changed`, `profile.mode_changed` and `profile.va_percent_changed` already exist in SCR-038; the report notes whether the observed switching behaviour justifies keeping all three.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report merged at `docs/design/research/e19-profiles.md` with at least 6 adopted, testable decisions.
- [ ] Default period mode and the labelled-vs-implied ranking agreed with the Architect (they constrain `24-internal-schemas.md` §5 defaults).
- [ ] Findings presented at Design Review; decisions carried explicitly into E19-D02 scope.
- [ ] Any contradiction with an existing plan document raised as a documented amendment proposal.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded on the ticket; Status = Done.**

## Dependencies
- **E05** design system v0 supplies the greyscale primitives and density modes the harness renders with.

## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires a black-box test plan executed by QA/SDET for every Story, with a sign-off comment carrying pass/fail per scenario. E11's interaction stories — pan/zoom (S04), scale modes (S05), axes (S06), crosshair (S07) — are where a black-box view earns its keep: the unit tests verify that `zoomAt` returns the right transform, and a user discovers that zooming near the right edge with autoscale on and a locked price axis does something surprising.

This plan covers the **interaction group**. Multi-pane, LOD, a11y and memory are covered by Q02, Q03, Q05 and Q06 respectively, so the four plans together cover the Epic without overlapping.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Test plan covering **E11-S04** (pan/zoom/momentum), **E11-S05** (linear/log/percent/inverted, autoscale, manual lock), **E11-S06** (axes, decimation, keyboard rescale) and **E11-S07** (crosshair, OHLCV readout, countdown).
- Scenarios derived from `US-CHART-006`, `US-CHART-007` and `US-CHART-008`, including every Gherkin scenario in those stories as a named, executable test case.
- **Combination coverage** — the part unit tests cannot reach: log scale + autoscale + manual lock; percent scale + a reference bar scrolled out of view; inverted + log together; zoom at the extreme right edge with the forming bar; momentum interrupted by a scale change; crosshair magnet across a gap in data.
- **Boundary cases**: single bar loaded; two bars; all bars identical price (zero range — a classic division-by-zero in autoscale); a series containing a non-positive value with log requested (`US-CHART-007` scenario 3); bar spacing at its minimum and maximum; the first and last bar of the series.
- **Failure cases**: scale change during an in-flight momentum decay; rapid repeated mode switching; keyboard and pointer input arriving in the same frame; interaction during a data update storm.
- **Reduced-motion path** exercised as a first-class case, not an afterthought.
- Exploratory charter for the interaction group (90 minutes, time-boxed, with a stated mission).
- Plan committed to `packages/chart-engine/test/plans/` so it lives beside the code it tests.

## Out of scope
- Multi-pane and sync — **E11-Q02**. Performance numbers — **E11-Q03**. Chaos and robustness — **E11-Q04**. Accessibility conformance — **E11-Q05**. Epic-level regression — **E11-Q06**. GPU matrix — **E11-Q07**.
- Series rendering behaviour (candles, Heikin-Ashi) — E12's QA.
- Writing the automated E2E implementations — **E11-Q02** owns the suite; this plan defines what it must cover.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every user-story scenario is an executable test case
  Given US-CHART-006, US-CHART-007 and US-CHART-008
  When the plan is reviewed
  Then every Gherkin scenario in those stories appears as a named test case with explicit steps and expected results
  And each case states which E11 ticket it verifies

Scenario: Combinations are covered, not just individual features
  Given the scale modes, autoscale, manual lock and zoom behaviours
  When the plan's combination matrix is inspected
  Then log + autoscale + lock, percent with an off-screen reference, and inverted + log are all covered
  And each combination states the expected behaviour precisely enough to fail a test on

Scenario: Degenerate data is covered
  Given a series where every bar has an identical price, giving a zero price range
  When the plan is reviewed
  Then a case exists asserting autoscale produces a sane range rather than a division by zero or a collapsed axis

Scenario: The plan is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer unfamiliar with the engine
  When they execute the plan
  Then every case has steps, expected results and the fixture to use
  And no case requires asking the author what "correct" means

Scenario: Execution produces a sign-off with per-scenario results
  When the plan is executed against a build
  Then a sign-off comment records pass or fail for every scenario with evidence
  And failures are filed as defects with priority and owner
```

## Technical notes / design
**Fixtures.** Cases reference named fixtures from `packages/fixtures` so results are reproducible: `btcusdt-1m-100k` (the volume case), `btcusdt-1m-spike` (decimation and autoscale extremes), `btcusdt-1m-gap` (missing data, for magnet and decimation), `synthetic-flat` (zero price range), `synthetic-nonpositive` (the log-disable case). Ad hoc "load some data and have a look" cases are not acceptable, because they cannot be re-run against a later build.

**Why combinations get their own matrix.** Each of scale mode, autoscale state, lock state and zoom anchor is individually simple; the defects live in their interaction. The matrix is explicit rather than left to exploratory testing because these combinations are all reachable in normal use, not obscure — a trader on a log-scaled chart who drags the price axis has entered a three-way combination without trying.

**Exploratory charter format** per `03-testing-strategy.md`: mission, areas, timebox, and a session sheet recording what was tried, what was found and what was not covered.

## Test plan
The deliverable is itself a test plan; its own verification is:
- Traceability check: every Gherkin scenario from the three user stories is present.
- Peer review by the chart-engine lead, to reconcile the black-box view with known implementation edges.
- A dry run against the current build to confirm every case is executable as written.
- Fixture existence check — a plan referencing a fixture that does not exist is not executable.

## Security notes
No security surface; the plan exercises market-data rendering with synthetic fixtures only. Any defect with a security or safety implication found during execution is routed to **E11-X03** and labelled `security` per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, rather than being filed as an ordinary rendering bug.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the **keyboard equivalents** for every pointer interaction it covers, because `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 makes them functional requirements rather than accessibility extras: keyboard pan/zoom/reset (`US-CHART-006`'s NFR), keyboard axis rescale (CMP-188/189), keyboard crosshair stepping (`US-CHART-008`). Conformance auditing — axe-core, screen readers, contrast — is **E11-Q05**; this plan simply verifies the keyboard paths work as functionality.

## Performance notes
Not a performance plan, but every interaction case is executed against the 100k-bar fixture so that a case which is functionally correct and unusably slow is caught here rather than being assumed to be someone else's problem. Measured budgets are **E11-Q03**.

## Observability
Execution results and the exploratory session sheets attached to the ticket. Defects link back to the plan case that found them, so the plan's yield is measurable and the weak areas of the next plan are informed by it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts (plan, charters, scripts, suites) committed to the repo, not held in a personal document.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the Gherkin acceptance criterion or the user story it verifies, so coverage is traceable rather than asserted.
- [ ] Execution results recorded with pass/fail per scenario and evidence (logs, screenshots, recordings, benchmark artefacts) attached.
- [ ] Defects filed with reproduction steps, environment, severity and `priority/*`, linked to the E11 ticket they came from.
- [ ] Automated suites wired into CI at the correct stage and green; flaky tests quarantined with a ticket, never silently retried.
- [ ] Coverage contribution recorded against the package thresholds (>= 85 % engine, >= 80 % web).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET with pass/fail per scenario and any deviation stated explicitly.
- [ ] Test plan reviewed by the chart-engine lead so the black-box view and the implementation view are reconciled.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S07** — the last story in the interaction group; planning before it lands would mean re-planning.
- **E11-S04**, **S05**, **S06** — the stories under test.
- Feeds **E11-Q02** (E2E automation) and **E11-Q06** (regression pack).

## Branch
`test/chart-engine-interaction-plan` · plan committed to `packages/chart-engine/test/plans/`.

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` — test pyramid, coverage floors, fixture conventions, flake policy

- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` — WCAG 2.2 AA target, canvas strategy, manual pass requirements

title: Pan and zoom with cursor-anchored zoom, momentum and keyboard equivalents
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-006` (Must) — *"As a trader, I want fluid pan/zoom with auto-fit and manual scale lock, so that navigation never fights me"* — with the NFR **"input-to-pixel latency <=1 frame; keyboard equivalents for pan/zoom/reset (arrow keys, +/-, Home)"**. This is the interaction a trader performs thousands of times a day; it is also the canonical "boring parity" item that `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1 warns costs 4–8 weeks and must be finished before order-flow features pay off.

§3.11 fixes the gesture table and §3.5 the momentum model. The a11y standard makes the keyboard path mandatory rather than a nicety: `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 forbids hover-only and drag-only functionality, so every pointer gesture here needs a keyboard equivalent of equal capability, and momentum must honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

This story covers **time-axis and plot-area navigation**. Price-scale modes, autoscale and the lock badge are E11-S05 (`US-CHART-007` and the autoscale/lock scenarios of `US-CHART-006`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/interaction/InputRouter.ts` (main thread): `setPointerCapture`, `getCoalescedEvents()` for pointers, wheel accumulation, and forwarding **at most one batch per frame** to the worker as the packed `input` message from E11-T02.
- Gestures per §3.11: drag on plot = pan time (and price when the price scale is unlocked); wheel = zoom time at cursor; `Shift+wheel` = horizontal pan; `Ctrl+wheel` = zoom price; drag on time axis = compress/expand `barSpacing`; double-click plot = reset to auto-scale + latest bar; pinch (touch/trackpad) = zoom at centroid, two-finger drag pans.
- Cursor-anchored zoom through `Viewport.zoomAt` (E11-S03) so the world coordinate under the cursor is invariant.
- Momentum per §3.5: velocity-based with exponential decay `v *= exp(-dt/tau)`, tau = 120 ms, terminated below 0.02 px/ms, **cancelled on any new pointer-down**; integrated by the scheduler's time-based animation so dropped frames do not change the resting position.
- **Reduced motion**: when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set (or the app-level setting from SCR-117 is on), momentum is disabled — the pan stops on pointer-up — and this is stated in the chart's keyboard-help text, not silently different.
- Keyboard equivalents (`US-CHART-006` NFR + §3.11): `<-/->` move the data cursor by a bar, `Shift+<-/->` by 10, `Home/End` jump to first/last bar, `+/-` zoom in/out about the cursor bar, `Space` as a pan-drag modifier, double-tap equivalent `Ctrl+Home` resets to auto-scale + latest bar.
- Kinetic scroll on touch with the same tau and the same reduced-motion rule.

## Out of scope
- Price-scale modes (log/percent/inverted), autoscale and the manual-lock badge — E11-S05.
- Crosshair rendering and the OHLCV readout — E11-S07.
- Cross-chart sync of the resulting viewport — E11-S09.
- `Alt+<-/->` replay tick stepping (§3.11) — E26.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Pan and zoom stay above the frame floor
  Given BTCUSDT 1m with 100 000 bars loaded
  When the chart is panned horizontally at 1000 px/s for 5 s and then wheel-zoomed from 0.1 to 50 px/bar
  Then the measured frame rate stays at or above 55 fps throughout (benchmarks B1 and B2)
  And input-to-pixel latency is at most 1 frame

Scenario: Zoom is anchored to the cursor
  Given the cursor rests over the 14:00 bar
  When the wheel is scrolled to zoom in three notches
  Then the 14:00 bar remains under the cursor within 0.5 px at every step

Scenario: Inertia respects reduced-motion settings
  Given the OS reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When the user flicks the chart and releases
  Then the chart stops immediately at the release position with no glide
  And the keyboard-help text states that inertia is disabled

Scenario: Every pointer gesture has a keyboard equivalent
  Given the chart pane has keyboard focus and no mouse is used
  When the user presses <-, ->, Shift+->, Home, End, + and -
  Then the view pans by one bar, ten bars, jumps to the first and last bar, and zooms in and out about the cursor bar
  And Ctrl+Home resets to auto-scale with the latest bar visible

Scenario: A high-rate trackpad cannot flood the worker
  Given a trackpad emitting 240 wheel events per second
  When the events are routed
  Then at most one input batch per frame is posted to the worker with the deltas accumulated
  And no zoom step is lost — the accumulated delta equals the sum of the raw deltas

Scenario: A new touch cancels momentum immediately
  Given a momentum glide is in progress
  When the user puts a finger or pointer down on the plot
  Then the glide stops on that frame and the new drag begins from the current position
```

## Technical notes / design
Wheel handling is the subtle part: trackpads emit far more than 60 events/s and mix pixel/line/page delta modes. Accumulate `deltaY` normalised to pixels (`deltaMode` 0/1/2 -> ×1/×16/×plotHeight) into a per-frame accumulator, apply once in the worker, then clear. Never apply per-event — that is the classic cause of zoom "racing" on macOS trackpads.

Pointer events use `getCoalescedEvents()` so a 240 Hz stylus/trackpad still yields one batch per frame carrying every sample (needed for accurate velocity), packed into the `Float32Array` layout defined in E11-T02.

Velocity estimate for momentum: exponentially weighted over the last 50 ms of coalesced samples, not a two-point difference (two-point is noisy at high sample rates and makes flicks feel inconsistent).

`Space` as a pan-drag modifier follows the design-tool convention and must not conflict with the global shortcut registry from E10 — register through it rather than attaching a raw listener, so a conflict is detected at registration time.

Reduced-motion resolution order: OS media query -> app accessibility setting (SCR-117) -> chart option. Any of them being "reduce" disables momentum; the engine never overrides a user preference in the other direction.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: wheel delta-mode normalisation; per-frame accumulation and clearing; velocity estimation over synthetic sample trains; momentum integration with `TestClock` (including dropped-frame equivalence); clamp behaviour at `barSpacing` bounds; reduced-motion resolution matrix.
- **Interaction/E2E** (Playwright web + Electron, §14 interaction layer): drag-pan, wheel-zoom, `Shift+wheel`, `Ctrl+wheel`, time-axis drag, double-click reset, pinch, and the full keyboard set — each asserted against the resulting viewport, not against pixels.
- **Perf**: B1 (pan, p95 <=12 ms, draw calls <=8) and B2 (zoom sweep 0.1->50 px/bar, p95 <=14 ms, **no LOD flicker — LOD changes <=6 over the sweep**).
- **A11y**: keyboard-only traversal of the whole gesture set with axe-core clean; reduced-motion assertion; announcement throttling verified with E11-S13's live region.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
This story is where the "no drag-only, no hover-only" rule of `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 is either honoured or lost. Requirements verified in QA, not just implemented:
- Every gesture in §3.11 has a keyboard equivalent of equal capability, documented in the global hotkey table (E10) and discoverable from the chart's keyboard-help affordance.
- The chart pane is a single tab stop with a visible focus ring (CMP-004 FocusRing); arrow keys move the data cursor rather than scrolling the page, and the pane does not trap focus — `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` leave it.
- Momentum honours `prefers-reduced-motion` (WCAG 2.2 AA 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions).
- Viewport changes are announced through the throttled polite live region at <=2/s (E11-S13), summarised ("showing 09:00 to 13:00, 240 bars") rather than per-frame.
- Motion spec and easing come from **E11-D06**, which must be signed off before this story starts (design-ahead rule).

## Performance notes
Budget #1 plus the <=1 ms input stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 and budget #6's input-to-photon <=2 frames (requirement R6). Hard gates: B1 and B2. The "no LOD flicker" secondary gate on B2 is what the ±15 % hysteresis dead band in E11-S12 exists for — if B2 reports more than 6 LOD changes across the sweep, this story is not done.

## Observability
Analytics emitted by the app layer from engine events: `chart.time_scale_changed` (SCR-043). Counters: `engine.input.batches_per_frame`, `engine.input.coalesced_ratio`, `engine.momentum.cancelled`. Frame stats already carry LOD level so a zoom sweep's LOD history is reconstructable from the SCR-046 feed.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S03** — `zoomAt` and the viewport clamps.
- **E11-D06** — the motion spec (easing curves, momentum feel, reduced-motion variants) must be Done >=2 sprints earlier.
- **E10** — global keyboard-shortcut registry (conflict detection).
- Blocks **E11-S07** (crosshair follows the cursor this routes), **E11-S09** (sync broadcasts the viewport this changes).

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-pan-zoom` · 2 PRs (pointer/wheel routing + zoom anchoring; momentum + keyboard equivalents), each <=400 LOC.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` — engine architecture (scene graph 3.1, render loop 3.2, data model 3.3, GL backend 3.4, viewport math 3.5, LOD 3.6, SDF text 3.7, heatmap streaming 3.8, hit-testing 3.9, interaction 3.11, plugin API 3.12, worker protocol 6, memory 7, API sketch 8, benchmarks 13, tests 14, milestones 15, open items 16)

title: Support linear, log, percent and inverted scales with autoscale and lock
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-007` (Must/Should) — log (Must), linear (Must) and percentage (Should) price scales — plus the autoscale and manual-lock scenarios of `US-CHART-006`. **SCR-043** (price-scale context menu) fixes the exact item set: auto / logarithmic / percentage / indexed-to-100, invert, lock, merge indicator scales, reset.

The NFR that makes or breaks this story is `US-CHART-007`'s: *"projection is a single shared function used by every renderer, covered by unit tests"*. A log scale that only the candle renderer knows about produces drawings, profiles and order lines floating away from the price they annotate. Every scale mode is therefore implemented **inside** the E11-S03 transform module as an alternative `priceToScreen`/`screenToPrice` pair, never as a per-renderer adjustment.

The failure case is explicit in the story: a series containing non-positive values must **disable** log with an explanation rather than rendering incorrectly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scale modes in `src/viewport/scales.ts`, all four plugged into the shared transform: `linear`, `log` (`sy = (log(p) - log(priceLow)) / (log(priceHigh) - log(priceLow)) × -plotHeight + plotBottom`, §3.5), `percent` (computed against an anchor bar's close — the left-edge bar by default), `indexed-to-100` (percent normalised so the anchor reads 100).
- `invert` flag (flips the y mapping) and `lock` flag (disables autoscale), both orthogonal to the mode.
- **Autoscale** per §3.5: computed from the visible range's min/max with a configurable margin, optionally including visible drawings and overlays ("include drawings" option from `US-CHART-006`), recomputed only when the visible bar range changes and throttled to once per frame.
- **Manual lock**: dragging the price axis disengages autoscale, a lock badge appears on the axis, and double-clicking the axis restores auto-fit (`US-CHART-006` third scenario).
- **SCR-043 price-scale context menu**: auto / logarithmic / percentage / indexed-to-100 / invert / lock / merge indicator scales / reset — real menu semantics (CMP-041 Menu), reachable by `Shift+F10` when the scale has focus, checkable items with state announced.
- Log-mode guard: when the visible series contains a value <=0, the log item is disabled with an explanatory tooltip ("Log scale needs positive prices; this series contains 0 or negative values") and the scale stays on its previous mode.
- Persistence of the per-pane scale mode into the chart options object handed back to the app (E15 persists it into workspaces).

## Out of scope
- Axis tick generation, label formatting and decimation — E11-S06.
- The chart settings dialog surface (SCR-031 scale section) — built by E15/E13's settings work; this story exposes the options it binds to.
- Merging *indicator* scales across panes — the menu item is present and wired, but indicator scale objects arrive with E13; until then the item is disabled with "No indicators on this pane".
- Price-axis drag-to-rescale gesture plumbing — E11-S06 owns the axis component's gesture surface; this story owns what a rescale *means* for the scale state.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Log scale re-projects everything, not just candles
  Given a chart with candles, a trend-line drawing, a horizontal level and a visible-range volume profile
  When the price scale is switched to logarithmic
  Then gridlines, candles, the drawing, the level and the profile all re-project through the shared transform
  And a golden image shows the drawing still anchored to the same two bar/price pairs

Scenario: Percent scale reads as change from the reference bar
  Given percentage mode with the left-edge bar as the reference
  When the crosshair moves across the visible range
  Then the axis and the readout display values as % change from that reference bar's close
  And switching the visible range re-anchors the reference to the new left-edge bar

Scenario: Log is refused, not faked, on non-positive data
  Given a series whose visible range contains a value of 0
  When the user opens the price-scale menu
  Then the "Logarithmic" item is disabled with an explanation of why
  And the scale remains on its previous mode with no rendering artefacts

Scenario: Manual drag disengages autoscale and is reversible
  Given autoscale is on
  When the user drags the price axis
  Then autoscale disengages and a lock badge appears on the axis with an accessible name "Price scale locked"
  And double-clicking the axis restores auto-fit and removes the badge

Scenario: Autoscale includes drawings only when asked
  Given a drawing extends 20 % above the visible price range and "include drawings" is off
  When the visible range changes
  Then the price range fits the bars only
  And enabling "include drawings" re-fits to include the drawing within one frame

Scenario: A scale change costs a projection change only
  Given a chart with 100 000 bars loaded
  When the scale mode is changed from linear to log
  Then no data refetch is issued and the redraw completes within one frame (SCR-043 performance note)
```

## Technical notes / design
All four modes are implemented as `{ toScreen(p, ctx), fromScreen(y, ctx), tickCandidates(range) }` triples registered in the transform module, so adding a mode never touches a renderer. `tickCandidates` is consumed by E11-S06 — log ticks are decade-anchored (1, 2, 5 × 10^n), percent ticks are round percentages, not linear price steps.

Percent/indexed anchor: the anchor is the **close of the left-most fully visible bar**, recomputed when the visible bar range changes (not every frame). Storing an absolute anchor price instead would make the percent scale drift as the user pans, which is not what traders expect.

Log guard: evaluated over the *visible* range only, re-evaluated when the range changes; a non-positive value scrolling into view while log is active switches the pane to linear with a polite announcement rather than producing `NaN` geometry — silently rendering `log(0)` is the failure `US-CHART-007` calls out.

Autoscale margin default 5 % top and bottom, configurable; computation is a single pass over the visible slice of `BarStore` (already bounded by the visible window, so it is O(visible bars) not O(100k)) and is throttled to once per frame per §3.5.

Inverted mode multiplies the mapping by -1 after the mode's own projection, so it composes with log and percent without special cases.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: each mode's `toScreen`/`fromScreen` against hand-computed values; round-trip within half a tick in all four modes; inverted composition with each mode; autoscale margin maths; anchor re-selection on range change; log guard triggering on 0 and on negative values.
- **Property** (fast-check, 10 000 cases): in every mode, `fromScreen(toScreen(p)) ~ p`; `toScreen` is strictly monotone in price (decreasing, or increasing when inverted); no mode ever returns `NaN` or `Infinity` for in-range input.
- **Golden image**: candles + drawing + level + profile rendered in linear and in log, per theme, asserting co-anchoring at <=0.1 % pixel diff.
- **E2E**: SCR-043 menu opened by right-click and by `Shift+F10`, every item toggled, checked state announced; axis drag then double-click restore; lock badge presence.
- **A11y**: axe-core on the menu; `aria-checked` state on each mode item; the lock badge has a text name, not colour alone.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-043's a11y contract is the acceptance bar: real menu semantics (`role="menu"`/`menuitemradio`/`menuitemcheckbox`), reachable via `Shift+F10` when the scale has focus, with each option's checked state announced. Additional requirements:
- The lock badge carries a text accessible name ("Price scale locked") — it may not be conveyed by an icon or colour alone.
- A mode change is announced once through the polite live region ("Price scale: logarithmic"), not on every subsequent frame.
- The disabled log item exposes its reason via `aria-describedby` so a screen-reader user learns *why* it is disabled, rather than finding an inert item.
- Design source: **E11-D03** (scale menus hi-fi) must be Done >=2 sprints before this story.

## Performance notes
SCR-043's performance note is a hard behaviour: "scale-mode changes are a projection change only — no data refetch, redraw within one frame". Autoscale recomputation is bounded to the visible window and throttled to once per frame (§3.5), contributing to the <=2 ms data-window recompute stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3. `Math.log` per vertex is avoided — the log mapping is applied CPU-side into the same uniform form, so the shader is unchanged across modes.

## Observability
Analytics: `chart.price_scale_changed` with `{mode, inverted, locked}` (SCR-043). Counters: `engine.scale.autoscale_recomputes`, `engine.scale.log_guard_trips`. A log-guard trip also emits a polite announcement and is visible in SCR-046.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S03** — modes are registered inside the shared transform module.
- **E11-D03** — scale-menu designs (SCR-043) signed off >=2 sprints earlier.
- **E05** — CMP-041 Menu primitive.
- Blocks **E11-S06** (tick candidates per mode), and is relied on by E12 (series render through the mode) and E14 (drawings re-project).

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-price-scales` · 2 PRs (modes + autoscale/lock; SCR-043 menu wiring), each <=400 LOC.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` — engine architecture (scene graph 3.1, render loop 3.2, data model 3.3, GL backend 3.4, viewport math 3.5, LOD 3.6, SDF text 3.7, heatmap streaming 3.8, hit-testing 3.9, interaction 3.11, plugin API 3.12, worker protocol 6, memory 7, API sketch 8, benchmarks 13, tests 14, milestones 15, open items 16)
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` 5 (R1 Charting alpha scope, exit criteria, quality gates)
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` 2 (budgets 1/2/14), 4 (frame breakdown, degradation ladder), 7 (measurement), 8 (regression gate)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` 6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility: DOM mirror, live regions, table alternative)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` 7 (CMP-180..199), `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-041..049)
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md`, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §5 US-CHART-007, US-CHART-006 (autoscale/lock scenarios)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-043 (menus, a11y, performance), SCR-031 (settings host)
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.5 (log/percent mapping, autoscale)
