title: Render price and time axes with label decimation and keyboard rescale
body:
## Context
`CMP-188 PriceAxis` and `CMP-189 TimeAxis` are the chart's frame of reference — the components every other surface is read against. They are also a classic parity trap: naive tick generation produces labels that collide at one zoom level, disappear at another, and jitter by a sub-pixel as the user pans. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1 names axis decimation and DPI correctness among the "boring things" that must be finished before order-flow features pay off.

The catalogue fixes the contracts. CMP-188: shared across panes bound to the same scale, supports linear/log, props `min/max`, `scaleType`, `tickFormatter`, `onDragScale`, and **"draggable-to-rescale has a keyboard equivalent (focus axis, arrow keys nudge scale)"**. CMP-189: horizontal time axis, "shared master clock across all panes in a chart (synced pan/zoom)", props `range`, `tickFormatter`, `onPan/onZoom`, with keyboard pan (`<-/->`) and zoom (`+/-`) documented in the global hotkey table.

Both expose their tick labels into the DOM mirror: `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 requires "a real, if visually-hidden-when-redundant, list of tick values".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/axes/PriceAxis.ts` (**CMP-188**): tick generation per scale mode using the `tickCandidates` from E11-S05 (linear: 1/2/5 × 10^n; log: decade-anchored; percent: round percentages), label formatting to the instrument's `tickSize` precision, last-price label pinned and never overlapped by a tick label, drag-to-rescale, double-click to auto-fit.
- `src/axes/TimeAxis.ts` (**CMP-189**): time tick generation at the appropriate granularity for the visible span (seconds -> minutes -> hours -> days -> months), **session and day-boundary markers** rendered from the boundary setting, drag to compress/expand `barSpacing`, and the master-clock role for all panes in the chart.
- **Label decimation**: a greedy pass that keeps the highest-priority ticks (round hours before round minutes, decades before intermediates) and drops any label whose bounding box would overlap an already-placed one, with a minimum gap of 1.5× the label height. Priority ordering is stable across frames so labels do not flicker in and out while panning.
- **Device-pixel snapping**: gridlines and axis rules are snapped to device pixels (`Math.round(x * dpr) / dpr + 0.5/dpr`) so hairlines are crisp at any DPR rather than being blurred across two pixels.
- Axis gutters computed by the layout engine from the widest formatted label, re-measured only when the formatter, font or price magnitude class changes — not per frame.
- Keyboard rescale (CMP-188 contract): focusing the price axis and pressing `Up/Down` compresses/expands the price scale by one step; `Home` restores auto-fit. Focusing the time axis and pressing `<-/->` pans, `+/-` zooms.
- Timezone: labels rendered in UTC by default (`ChartOptions.timeZone`, default `'UTC'`), with the active timezone stated in the SCR-043 time-scale menu.
- Text is drawn through the SDF pipeline (E11-S11) as a single batched draw call per axis (§4 draw-call table).

## Out of scope
- The scale *modes* themselves and the SCR-043 menu — E11-S05.
- Session/day-boundary **configuration** (`US-CHART-009`, which anchor, funding-time resets) — E12; this story renders the markers from whatever boundary setting it is given.
- "Go to date" (SCR-044) — E11-S15 owns the paging it triggers; the dialog is E15's surface.
- Indicator-scale merging visuals — E13.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Labels decimate instead of colliding
  Given a chart zoomed so that 400 bars span 1200 px
  When the time axis renders
  Then no two labels overlap and every retained label keeps at least 1.5 label-heights of clear space
  And the retained set is a stable subset as the user pans — a label does not blink on and off between adjacent frames

Scenario: Hairlines are crisp at fractional DPR
  Given devicePixelRatio is 1.25
  When gridlines and the axis rule are drawn
  Then each is snapped to a device pixel and a golden image shows a single-pixel line with no grey fringe

Scenario: The price axis rescales by keyboard
  Given the price axis has keyboard focus
  When the user presses Up five times and then Home
  Then the price range compresses one step per press with each new range announced politely at most twice per second
  And Home restores auto-fit and announces "Price scale: auto"

Scenario: The time axis is the master clock for every pane
  Given a three-pane chart
  When the time axis is dragged to expand bar spacing
  Then all three panes change bar spacing together in the same frame
  And no pane lags by a frame

Scenario: Tick labels are present in the accessibility tree
  Given a screen reader inspects a chart pane
  When it navigates the DOM mirror
  Then the current price-axis tick values and time-axis tick labels are exposed as a readable list
  And the values match the labels drawn on the canvas for that frame

Scenario: The last-price label never hides behind a tick
  Given the last price falls within one label height of a regular tick
  When the axis renders
  Then the regular tick label is suppressed and the last-price label is drawn in full
```

## Technical notes / design
Tick generation is "nice number" selection: for a target of `plotHeight / (2.5 × labelHeight)` ticks, choose the step from `{1, 2, 2.5, 5} × 10^n` closest at or above the ideal step, then emit ticks at multiples of that step, quantised to `tickSize`. Log mode anchors at decades and inserts 2× and 5× intermediates only while they clear the overlap test.

Time granularity ladder: 1 s, 5 s, 15 s, 30 s, 1 m, 5 m, 15 m, 30 m, 1 h, 4 h, 1 d, 1 w, 1 M — pick the smallest whose spacing is >= the minimum label gap. Boundary ticks (day starts, session anchors) get priority 0 and are never decimated away before ordinary ticks.

Stability rule (what stops flicker): decimation operates on a **priority-ordered** candidate list, never on "every other label". Zooming changes which candidates exist but not their relative priority, so retained labels are a monotone subset as you zoom out.

Gutter measurement uses a cached text-measure per (format, font, magnitude class). Re-measuring per frame was measured as a real cost in comparable engines and is explicitly avoided; `LAYOUT` dirty is the only trigger.

Snapping: in the vertex shader for GL-drawn rules, positions are rounded to the device-pixel grid after the transform; for the 0.5-px offset convention, half-pixel offsets are applied in device space, not CSS space, which is why the DPR (E11-S10) must be exact.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: nice-number step selection across three orders of magnitude and for `tickSize` 0.01/0.5/1; time granularity ladder selection for spans from 10 s to 5 years; decimation stability (a label retained at zoom z is retained at every zoom >= z for the same range); gutter cache invalidation.
- **Golden image** (SwiftShader, <=0.1 % diff): price axis linear/log, time axis at 5 granularities, DPR 1 / 1.25 / 2, both themes, plus the last-price-label collision case.
- **Interaction/E2E**: axis drag rescale, double-click auto-fit, keyboard rescale, master-clock sync across 3 panes.
- **A11y**: axe-core on the chart route; DOM-mirror tick list matches the drawn labels (assertion compares the mirror text against the frame's tick model); announcement throttling <=2/s.
- **Perf**: axis rendering <=0.5 ms per axis per frame; one draw call per axis text batch (§4).
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-188/CMP-189 a11y contracts are the acceptance bar:
- Axis tick labels are materialised into the DOM mirror as a real list (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1) — windowed to the visible ticks, not all of them.
- Drag-to-rescale has a full keyboard equivalent (focus axis, arrows nudge, `Home` resets) — required because `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6 forbids drag-only functionality.
- Keyboard pan/zoom on the time axis is registered in the global hotkey table (E10) so it appears in the shortcuts help.
- Rescale announcements go through the polite region, throttled to <=2/s per §6.2 — a per-step announcement at key-repeat speed would flood.
- Each axis is a focusable element with a visible focus ring (CMP-004 FocusRing) and an accessible name ("Price axis, logarithmic, locked").
- Design source: **E11-D02** (chart chassis hi-fi incl. axis treatment) signed off >=2 sprints earlier.

## Performance notes
Axis text is one batched SDF draw call per axis (§4 draw-call table) — falling back to per-label draw calls would blow the <=18/pane budget on its own. Gutter measurement is cached. Contributes to budget #1; measured inside B1/B5. Label decimation runs only on `LAYOUT`/`TRANSFORM` dirty frames and is O(candidate ticks), which is bounded by plot height / label height (tens), never by bar count.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.axis.ticks_drawn{axis}`, `engine.axis.labels_decimated{axis}`, `engine.axis.gutter_remeasures`. A sustained high `gutter_remeasures` is the signature of a formatter thrashing and is visible in SCR-046.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S05** — per-mode tick candidates.
- **E11-S11** — the SDF text pipeline that draws the labels; axes are its first consumer.
- **E11-S10** — exact DPR for device-pixel snapping (delivered in the same sprint; the snapping helper is imported from S10).
- **E11-D02** — chassis hi-fi design.
- Blocks **E11-S07** (crosshair axis labels), **E11-T08** (golden-image harness uses axes as its primary fixtures).

## Branch

title: Show a synced crosshair with an OHLCV readout and a bar-close countdown
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-008` (Must) — *"I want a crosshair with a precise data readout and a bar-close countdown, so that I always know exactly what I am looking at"* — with the NFR **"readout updates within one frame; live-region announcements throttled to <=2/s to avoid screen-reader flooding"**.

Three catalogue components carry the contract. **CMP-190 Crosshair**: synced across all panes and linked charts, props `position`, `syncGroupId`, and the binding a11y rule that "keyboard-driven crosshair movement is the accessible path — mouse-hover crosshair is the pointer-only convenience layer". **CMP-197 ChartTooltip**: the floating readout, explicitly `aria-hidden` because the same information is always available through the DOM mirror, preventing duplicate announcement. **CMP-226 BarCountdown**: text, never a bare progress ring, 1 Hz updates, `aria-live="off"` by default, and the warn state "adds a word, not just a colour".

The readout must include the values of visible indicators (`US-CHART-008` first scenario), so it is built as a composable field list that E13 extends rather than a fixed OHLCV struct.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/overlays/Crosshair.ts` (**CMP-190**): vertical + horizontal lines drawn in the `foreground` layer, snapping to bar centre horizontally, free or snapped vertically per magnet mode, plus price and time labels drawn on the respective axes.
- **Magnet modes**: `off` (free), `weak` (snap to the nearest OHLC value within 8 px), `strong` (always snap to the nearest OHLC value) — mode is a chart option and is announced when changed.
- `ChartEvents["crosshair"]` payload `{ time, price, barIndex, cell? }` emitted **edge-triggered** (only when the resolved bar/price cell changes), never per pointer-move.
- Readout field model: an ordered list of `{ label, value, unit, colorToken }` produced by asking each visible series/overlay for its value at the focused bar — OHLCV and delta from the bar store in this Epic, indicator values appended by E13 through the same interface.
- **CMP-197 ChartTooltip** in `apps/web`: DOM-rendered (crisp text, and it can carry real markup), positioned to avoid the pointer and to flip at viewport edges, `aria-hidden="true"`.
- **CMP-226 BarCountdown**: seconds to bar close for time-based intervals, updating at 1 Hz, turning amber **and adding the word "closing"** in the final 10 s (`US-CHART-008` second scenario + the component's "adds a word, not just a colour" rule). Hidden for non-time bar types with an explanatory title.
- **Keyboard crosshair**: `<-/->` step the data cursor by a bar, `Up/Down` step by price level, `Shift+<-/->` by 10 bars; the readout for the focused bar is announced through the throttled polite live region.
- Sync-group broadcast: the crosshair position is published once per frame to the pane's sync group (consumed by E11-S09).

## Out of scope
- The sync-group *mechanism* and cross-chart linking — E11-S09 (this story publishes and subscribes; S09 owns group membership and propagation).
- Footprint-cell tooltips and per-cell values — E18 (the `cell?` field of the crosshair payload is defined here and populated there).
- Indicator value fields — E13 supplies them through the field interface defined here.
- The full DOM-mirror structure and the data-table alternative — E11-S13 / E11-S14.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The readout is precise and complete
  Given the crosshair moves over a bar that has an indicator drawn on its pane
  When the readout renders
  Then it shows open, high, low, close, volume, delta, the bar time in the active timezone, and each visible indicator's value at that bar
  And the values match the DataModel exactly, not an interpolation between bars

Scenario: The countdown warns with a word, not only a colour
  Given a 1-minute interval with 8 seconds to bar close
  When the countdown renders
  Then it shows the remaining seconds with an amber token and the word "closing"
  And a colour-blind simulation of the frame still conveys the warning

Scenario: The keyboard crosshair announces without flooding
  Given the chart pane has focus
  When the user holds -> so that 30 bars are traversed in 3 seconds
  Then the crosshair steps bar by bar and the visual readout updates every frame
  And the live region announces at most 6 times, each carrying the latest bar's summary

Scenario: The tooltip does not double-announce
  Given a screen reader is active and the pointer hovers a bar
  When the tooltip appears
  Then it is aria-hidden and is not announced
  And the same values are reachable through the DOM mirror for the focused bar

Scenario: Crosshair events are edge-triggered
  Given the pointer moves 200 px within one bar's width
  When crosshair events are counted
  Then exactly one crosshair event is emitted for that bar
  And the vertical price component still updates the readout each frame without emitting an event

Scenario: Magnet mode snaps predictably
  Given magnet mode is "strong" and the pointer is 12 px from the bar's high
  When the crosshair resolves
  Then it snaps to the high and the readout labels the snapped value as "High"
```

## Technical notes / design
Edge-triggering is a message-traffic rule from §6 ("pick results posted only when the picked object changes") and applies to crosshair resolution too: the worker resolves `(barIndex, priceLevel)` every frame but posts only on change. The *visual* crosshair still follows the pointer at full frame rate inside the worker — the throttle is on the message, not the rendering.

Bar-centre snapping uses `screenToIndex` (O(1), E11-S03), then re-projects the bar centre with `indexToScreen` so the line lands exactly on the centre rather than under the raw pointer x.

Countdown maths: `msRemaining = barCloseTime - serverNow`, where `serverNow` is the WS-clock-corrected time (offset supplied by the app layer from E17's heartbeat) — using the local clock makes the countdown wrong by the client's clock skew, which traders notice immediately. Below 10 s the component re-renders at 1 Hz still, not faster; sub-second precision is not useful and costs a re-render per frame.

The readout field list is rebuilt only when the focused bar changes or a visible series changes — not per frame — and is a pooled array to keep the hot path allocation-free.

Tooltip positioning: offset 12 px from the pointer in the quadrant with the most space, flipped at pane edges, and clamped inside the chart container; it never covers the last-price label (SCR-030's "labels must never obscure the last price" rule).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: bar-centre snapping across bar spacings; magnet resolution for each mode at boundary distances; countdown formatting and warn threshold; clock-skew correction; edge-trigger logic; field-list assembly with 0/1/3 indicators.
- **Golden image**: crosshair + labels at DPR 1/2, both themes; tooltip at all four edge-flip positions; countdown normal/warning/closed.
- **Interaction/E2E**: pointer crosshair, keyboard crosshair including `Shift` multiples, magnet mode switching, tooltip flip at edges, countdown reaching zero and rolling to the next bar.
- **A11y**: live-region announcement assertions (content and <=2/s cadence); `aria-hidden` verified on the tooltip (axe rule); countdown default `aria-live="off"`; contrast of crosshair lines against both themes.
- **Perf**: readout update within one frame (`US-CHART-008` NFR); CMP-197's catalogue test "performance (update cost during rapid crosshair movement)" — <=0.3 ms/frame during a 1000 px/s pointer sweep.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
This story is one of the two places (with E11-S13) where the chart's accessibility is actually decided.
- **Keyboard is the primary path**, per CMP-190: mouse hover is the convenience layer. Everything reachable by hover is reachable by `<-/->/Up/Down` with the same fidelity.
- **Announcement throttling** at <=2/s with latest-value semantics (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2 and the `US-CHART-008` NFR) — the region is pre-rendered and only its text content is swapped, never the node.
- **Tooltip is `aria-hidden`** (CMP-197) so the mirror is the single announcement source; axe asserts it.
- **Countdown** (CMP-226) is text, `aria-live="off"` by default with opt-in announcement, and its warn state adds the word "closing".
- Crosshair lines meet the 3:1 non-text contrast requirement against both themes; the readout never relies on colour alone to distinguish up/down (sign is text).
- Design source: **E11-D02**; a11y review in **E11-D07**.

## Performance notes
`US-CHART-008` NFR: readout updates within one frame. Crosshair rendering is 2 lines + 2 DOM labels = 1 GL draw call (§4 table). The tooltip is DOM, so its cost is main-thread layout — it is positioned via `transform` only (no layout-triggering property writes) to stay off the critical path. Contributes to the <=1 ms overlay stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3.

## Observability
`a11y` worker->main message carrying `cursorSummary` (the text the live region announces). Counters: `engine.crosshair.events_emitted`, `engine.crosshair.announcements`, `engine.countdown.clock_skew_ms`. A persistent large skew is surfaced in SCR-046 because it usually indicates a WS heartbeat problem, not a chart problem.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S04** — pointer routing and the keyboard cursor it moves.
- **E11-S06** — axis label rendering for the crosshair's price/time labels.
- **E17** (via the app layer) — server-clock offset for the countdown.
- Blocks **E11-S13** (the mirror announces what this resolves), **E11-S09** (broadcasts this position), **E18** (populates the `cell` field).

title: Pick chart objects in under 1 ms via structural and uniform-grid indices
body:
## Context
Hard requirement **R5** in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1: "200 drawings + 50 order/position lines with hit-testing in <=1 ms". Everything interactive in the product depends on it — selecting a drawing (E14), dragging an order line (E31), hovering a footprint cell (E18), clicking a ladder row (E21) — and it runs inside the input stage of the frame, which has <=1 ms total (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3).

§3.9 specifies two complementary indices maintained incrementally in the worker: a **structural index** exploiting the fact that the chart is a regular grid (bar index and price level computed analytically in O(1)), and an **object index**, a uniform 64 px grid over drawings, order lines, position lines, alert lines and bubbles. The budget is met by never doing a linear scan over objects.

This story builds both indices and the picking pipeline. The objects that populate the object index arrive with later epics; the index and its contract ship now so those epics register rather than invent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/hit/StructuralIndex.ts`: `screenToIndex`/`screenToPrice` from E11-S03 wrapped into `pickStructural(pt) -> { barIndex, priceLevel, paneId }` in O(1). Covers crosshair, footprint-cell hover, ladder rows and profile rows.
- `src/hit/ObjectIndex.ts`: uniform grid of 64 px buckets storing object ids, maintained **incrementally** — an object insert/move/remove touches only the buckets it spans, never a rebuild.
- Query algorithm per §3.9: take the bucket under the cursor plus a 1-bucket ring, test candidates precisely (distance-to-segment for lines, rect containment for boxes, radius for bubbles), sort by `zIndex` then proximity, return the front-most.
- Tolerances: grab handles use an enlarged **10 px** tolerance; **touch input uses 16 px** (§3.9) — resolved from the pointer type, not hard-coded to mouse.
- `pickAt` command (worker inbound, §6) for explicit picks, plus continuous hover picking that posts `pick` messages **edge-triggered** when the picked object changes.
- Registration API for later epics: `registerPickable({ id, kind, bounds, zIndex, paneId, hitTest })` with `kind  in  'drawing'|'order-line'|'position-line'|'alert-line'|'bubble'|'cell'|'axis'`, and an `indexShift` subscriber so a `prepend` (E11-T03) rebases bar-anchored bounds.
- Invalidation: a viewport change marks the object index `TRANSFORM`-dirty and bounds are re-projected lazily on the next query, not eagerly on every pan frame.

## Out of scope
- The drawings, order lines, bubbles and cells themselves — E14, E31, E22, E18, E21. This story ships the index and the contract they register through.
- Drag/resize behaviour after a pick — E14/E31 own the interaction; this story returns what was picked.
- Multi-select and marquee selection — E14.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Picking meets the hard budget at the specified density
  Given a pane with 200 drawings and 50 order/position lines
  When 1 000 picks at random screen positions are timed
  Then the p95 pick time is at most 1 ms (requirement R5, benchmark B8)
  And no pick performs a linear scan over all registered objects

Scenario: The front-most object wins
  Given three overlapping drawings at the cursor with zIndex 1, 5 and 3
  When a pick is performed
  Then the drawing with zIndex 5 is returned
  And when two objects share a zIndex, the closer one by distance is returned

Scenario: Touch gets a larger tolerance than mouse
  Given an order line 13 px from the pointer position
  When the pointer type is touch
  Then the line is picked (16 px tolerance)
  And when the pointer type is mouse, nothing is picked (10 px handle tolerance)

Scenario: Pick messages are edge-triggered
  Given the pointer moves 300 px while staying over the same drawing
  When pick messages are counted
  Then exactly one pick message is posted for that drawing
  And one further message is posted when the pointer leaves it

Scenario: A history prepend does not misplace objects
  Given a drawing anchored at barIndex 120 and 2 000 bars are prepended
  When the drawing is picked after the splice
  Then it is found at its unchanged time/price anchor
  And the object index reports no stale bucket entries

Scenario: Panning does not rebuild the index
  Given 250 registered objects
  When the chart is panned continuously for 5 s
  Then no full index rebuild occurs and bucket membership is recomputed lazily per query
  And picking remains within budget throughout
```

## Technical notes / design
Bucket size 64 px is from §3.9 and is a deliberate trade: small enough that a bucket rarely holds more than a handful of objects, large enough that a long trend line spans few buckets. Long lines are stored in every bucket their bounding segment crosses (a DDA walk), not in a bounding-box fill, so a diagonal line across the pane costs O(cells along the line), not O(w×h cells).

Precise tests: distance-to-segment (with the segment's `width/2 + tolerance` as the threshold) for lines and rays; rect containment with an edge band for boxes so both the fill and the border are pickable; radius for bubbles; analytic grid maths for cells.

Anchors are stored in **world space** (time + price) and projected lazily on query using the current viewport, so a pan never invalidates stored geometry — only the cached screen-space bounds, which are recomputed per query batch (once per frame at most).

Handle picking takes priority over body picking: when a pointer is within 10 px of a control point *and* inside the object body, the handle is returned, because dragging a handle is the more specific intent.

Determinism: ties in both `zIndex` and distance are broken by registration order, so pick results are reproducible in tests (§14 determinism aids).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: bucket assignment for horizontal/vertical/diagonal segments; DDA walk correctness; distance-to-segment against hand-computed cases; tolerance resolution by pointer type; zIndex/proximity/registration-order tie-breaking; `indexShift` rebasing.
- **Property** (fast-check, 10 000 cases): for random object sets and random query points, the grid query returns exactly the same object as a brute-force linear scan — this is the test that makes the optimisation safe.
- **Perf**: B8 (200 drawings, drag one, p95 frame <=12 ms, **pick <=1 ms**); a dedicated micro-benchmark at 1 000 objects to show the margin.
- **Integration**: pick -> `pick` message -> main-thread selection state, edge-trigger counting.
- Coverage >=90 % (pure geometry).

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
Picking is the **pointer** path; the keyboard path is focus traversal of the DOM mirror (E11-S13), and the two must agree — an object that can be picked must be focusable in the mirror, and the mirror node's bounding box must match the pickable bounds so that pointer and keyboard users select the same thing. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 requires the surrogate to be "sized to match the visual target for pointer users using it too"; this story exposes the projected bounds that make that alignment possible, and a test asserts mirror-node rects match pickable bounds within 1 px.

Target size: the 10 px (mouse) / 16 px (touch) tolerances are what let small chart objects satisfy WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) via the spacing exception; the tolerance values are therefore an a11y control, not only an ergonomic one.

## Performance notes
Hard requirement R5 (<=1 ms for 200 drawings + 50 lines) and the <=1 ms input stage of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3. Benchmark B8 gates it. Edge-triggered messaging keeps worker->main traffic low, protecting the main thread for the DOM mirror and React.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.pick.duration_us` (histogram), `engine.pick.candidates_tested`, `engine.pick.index_rebuilds`, `engine.pick.objects_registered{kind}`. A rising `candidates_tested` is the early signal that bucket sizing needs revisiting; it is shown in SCR-046's detail view.

title: Ingest design-system theme tokens, colour LUTs and density modes into the engine
body:
## Context
The engine draws in GL, where a colour is four floats, while the product's source of truth for colour, type and spacing is the design-system token set shipped by **E05** (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`). Without a single ingestion path every renderer would hard-code colours, themes would drift and the high-contrast theme would be impossible to verify.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 additionally fixes three non-negotiable rules that this Task makes structurally enforceable rather than a review convention: colour is never the sole carrier of meaning, estimated data carries a hatch pattern plus an "(estimated)" label, and **density modes (`comfortable` | `compact` | `dense`) change cell padding, font size class and LOD thresholds together as one coherent switch** — not three independent settings a caller can desynchronise.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/theme/ThemeIngest.ts` — maps the E05 token JSON (`color.chart.*`, `color.surface.*`, `color.text.*`, `font.mono`, `elevation.*`, spacing scale) into a flat, frozen `EngineTheme` of premultiplied `Float32Array` RGBA plus scalar metrics. Resolution happens **once per theme change**, never per frame.
- `src/theme/ColorLut.ts` — generates 256-entry `Uint8Array` RGBA lookup textures for continuous encodings (delta ramp, heatmap intensity, imbalance intensity). Consumers sample the LUT; they never compute a colour in a shader from a token.
- `src/theme/Density.ts` — the `DensityMode` switch: one enum drives cell padding, font size class **and** the LOD thresholds of E11-S12 together (§5 rule 5). Exposed as `chart.setDensity(mode)`.
- `setTheme` command wired through the E11-T02 worker protocol; the whole scene is marked dirty and redrawn within one frame (SCR-031's "styling is a uniform/shader change, not a data reload" requirement).
- Three themes supported from day one: `dark` (default), `light`, `high-contrast`.
- Hatch/pattern registry for the `(estimated)` encoding (CMP-227's engine-side counterpart) so later Epics (E20, E22, E25) attach a pattern id rather than inventing one.
- Config keys: `theme.name`, `theme.density`, `theme.reducedMotion`, `theme.colorBlindSafePalette`.

## Out of scope
- Authoring the tokens themselves — **E05**; this Task consumes them.
- The settings UI that switches theme/density (SCR-031 Appearance tab) — E15/E10 chrome; this Task exposes the engine API it calls.
- Final colour-blind-safe palette selection — open item **O5** of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §16, due at M8, validated by the accessibility pass; this Task only proves a palette can be swapped without code changes.
- Heatmap-specific LUT tuning — E21.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Theme switch is a uniform change, not a reload
  Given a chart with 100k bars and an active crosshair in the dark theme
  When chart.setTheme("light") is called
  Then every layer redraws in light-theme colours within one frame
  And no data is refetched and no GPU vertex buffer is re-uploaded

Scenario: Density is one coherent switch
  Given density is "comfortable"
  When chart.setDensity("dense") is called
  Then cell padding, the font size class and the LOD thresholds all change together
  And no API exists that can change one of the three without the others

Scenario: High-contrast theme meets the contrast floor
  Given the high-contrast theme is active
  When every foreground/background token pair used by the engine is measured
  Then each pair meets at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for non-text UI components
  And a token pair failing the floor fails the CI contrast test

Scenario: Unknown token fails loudly at ingest, never at frame time
  Given a theme payload missing "color.chart.crosshair"
  When ThemeIngest resolves it
  Then it throws a descriptive ENGINE_THEME_INVALID error naming the missing key
  And no partially-resolved theme is ever installed into the scene
```

## Technical notes / design
`EngineTheme` is a frozen object of typed arrays so the frame path performs zero allocation and zero string lookups:

```ts
interface EngineTheme {
  readonly name: "dark" | "light" | "high-contrast";
  readonly density: DensityMode;
  readonly rgba: Readonly<Record<ThemeSlot, Float32Array>>; // premultiplied, length 4
  readonly luts: Readonly<Record<LutId, Uint8Array>>;       // 256 * 4 bytes
  readonly metrics: Readonly<{ cellPadPx: number; fontSizeClass: 0|1|2; hairlinePx: number }>;
  readonly lodBias: number; // folded into E11-S12's thresholds
}
```

LUT generation interpolates in **OkLab**, not sRGB, so a diverging delta ramp has perceptually even steps and no muddy mid-band; the result is converted back to sRGB bytes once at generation time. LUTs are uploaded as `LUMINANCE_ALPHA`-free `RGBA8` 256×1 textures and bound to a dedicated texture unit reserved by the GL backend (E11-S02).

Density -> LOD coupling: `Density.apply(mode)` returns `{ cellPadPx, fontSizeClass, lodBias }` and E11-S12 adds `lodBias` to its `barSpacing` thresholds, so `dense` steps down later (more detail retained) and `comfortable` earlier. The coupling lives in one function so there is exactly one place to reason about it.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: token -> `Float32Array` mapping incl. premultiplication; missing-key rejection; LUT monotonicity and endpoint exactness; OkLab round-trip; density triple-coupling (asserting the three values change together); frozen-object immutability.
- **Contrast test** (CI, automated): every foreground/background slot pair used by the engine measured against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text) for all three themes — a failing pair fails the build.
- **Golden image** (via E11-T08): axes + crosshair + grid rendered in `dark`, `light` and `high-contrast`, and in all three density modes.
- **Perf**: assert `setTheme` costs <=1 frame and allocates zero bytes in the frame path afterwards (allocation-counter test).
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
This Task is the mechanism by which the engine's a11y colour rules become testable rather than aspirational:
- The **high-contrast theme** is a first-class, CI-verified theme, not a stylesheet override.
- The contrast test above is the automated half of `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the manual half is E11-Q05.
- The hatch/pattern registry exists so that meaning is never colour-only (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rules 1–4) — a later Epic that encodes state must attach a pattern id, and the registry is the only way to get one.
- `theme.reducedMotion` is ingested here and consumed by E11-S04's momentum, so `prefers-reduced-motion` has a single engine-wide source of truth.
- Design source: **E11-D05** (design-system contribution).

## Performance notes
Theme resolution is off the frame path entirely (once per change). LUT generation <=2 ms per LUT. The frame path must remain allocation-free after a theme change — asserted, not assumed. No measurable contribution to budget #1.

## Observability
Counters `engine.theme.name`, `engine.theme.density` reported in the `frame` stats payload so SCR-046 diagnostics and any bug report state which theme/density produced the numbers. `ENGINE_THEME_INVALID` error code added to the engine error enum.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.

title: Build a deterministic golden-image regression harness running on SwiftShader
body:
## Context
Unit tests prove a transform returns the right number; they cannot prove a chart looks right. Rendering defects — a half-pixel axis offset, a gridline drawn under instead of over, text baseline drift after a font change, a theme token wired to the wrong slot — are invisible to every other test layer and obvious in a pixel diff.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §14 requires golden-image tests per layer and per theme at **<=0.1 % pixel difference**. The engineering problem is determinism: real GPUs produce different pixels on different drivers, so goldens captured on a developer's RTX 3060 will never match CI. The answer is **SwiftShader**, Chromium's software rasteriser, which is bit-identical across machines — the standard trade of absolute fidelity for absolute reproducibility.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/test/golden` — the harness: Playwright + Chromium launched with `--use-gl=swiftshader --disable-gpu-sandbox --deterministic-mode`, fixed viewport, fixed DPR per case, virtual clock.
- Golden coverage required by §14: **axes, crosshair, grid, pane chrome, text at each LOD, `degraded-2d`**, each in **`dark`, `light` and `high-contrast`** themes and in all three density modes.
- Comparison with a perceptual threshold (`pixelmatch` at <=0.1 % differing pixels) plus a **diff artefact** (before/after/diff triptych) attached to the PR on failure — a golden test that fails without showing you the image is a test people learn to ignore.
- Update workflow: `pnpm golden:update` regenerates, and the regenerated images must be reviewed **as images** in the PR. An update commit touching more than 5 goldens requires an explanatory note, so a "just update the goldens" reflex cannot quietly absorb a real regression.
- Deterministic inputs: fixed fixture, fixed seed, virtual clock, fonts loaded from a pinned local file rather than the system font stack (system fonts differ per machine and are the most common source of spurious diffs).
- Runs as a **required check** on PRs touching `packages/chart-engine`.
- Shares the Playwright infrastructure and fixture plumbing with the benchmark harness (E11-T06).

## Out of scope
- Benchmarking — **E11-T06**; goldens run on SwiftShader where performance is meaningless by design.
- Visual regression of the React chrome (toolbars, dialogs) — the design-system Storybook/Chromatic pipeline in **E05**.
- Cross-browser and real-GPU rendering verification — **E11-Q07**'s exploratory GPU matrix, which is a human activity precisely because it cannot be made deterministic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Golden images are reproducible across machines
  Given the golden suite is run on a developer machine and on the CI runner
  When the produced images are compared
  Then they are byte-identical, because SwiftShader rasterises deterministically
  And no golden is captured from a hardware GPU

Scenario: A rendering regression fails the check with visible evidence
  Given a change shifts the price axis by half a pixel
  When the golden suite runs
  Then the check fails on the axis goldens
  And a before/after/diff triptych is attached to the PR for each failing case

Scenario: Every layer, theme and density is covered
  Given the golden manifest is inspected
  Then axes, crosshair, grid, pane chrome, text at each LOD and degraded-2d are covered
  And each appears in dark, light and high-contrast themes

Scenario: Golden updates are reviewed as images, not rubber-stamped
  Given an intentional visual change updates 7 goldens
  When the PR is opened
  Then the regenerated images are rendered in the PR for review
  And the update carries an explanatory note because it exceeds the 5-golden threshold

Scenario: The suite is fast enough to gate every PR
  Given the full golden suite runs in CI
  Then it completes within 10 minutes
  And it runs in parallel with the unit suite rather than after it
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why SwiftShader and not a real GPU.** A hardware GPU gives fidelity but not reproducibility: driver versions, vendor extensions and even GPU temperature change the last bit of a blend. SwiftShader gives reproducibility but not fidelity — it will not catch a driver-specific bug. Both properties are needed, so they are split across two mechanisms: SwiftShader goldens as a **deterministic gate** (this Task), and a human **GPU matrix exploratory** (E11-Q07) for driver reality. Stating the split here prevents the recurring "why don't the goldens catch GPU bugs" question.

**Determinism checklist**, all of which must hold or diffs become noise: fixed viewport and DPR per case; fonts from a pinned local file (never the system stack); virtual clock (no animation captured mid-flight); fixed fixture and seed; animations disabled or advanced to a fixed frame; `prefers-reduced-motion` forced on during capture.

**Threshold.** `pixelmatch` with `threshold: 0.1` per-pixel and a failure at >0.1 % of pixels differing — tolerant of a single anti-aliased edge pixel, intolerant of a half-pixel layout shift.

The manifest is data (`golden.manifest.ts`), so adding a case is a data change, and coverage of the §14 matrix is verifiable by reading one file.

## Test plan
- **Self-test**: inject a deliberate 1 px offset and assert the harness fails; run unchanged and assert it passes — the same "has this gate ever fired" discipline as E11-T06.
- **Determinism test**: same commit, two runs, byte-identical output.
- **Manifest-coverage test**: assert the manifest covers every (layer × theme × density) combination required by §14; a missing combination fails the build rather than being noticed a year later.
- **Unit**: diff-threshold arithmetic; triptych generation; update-workflow guard rails (the 5-golden note requirement).
- Runtime assertion: full suite <=10 minutes.

## Security notes
Data classification: **synthetic fixture data only**; goldens are images of generated market data and contain no real account, order or user information — asserted by the same fixture-content check as E11-T06.

Supply chain: Playwright, Chromium and `pixelmatch` are pinned and covered by Dependabot/npm audit; the SwiftShader build ships with pinned Chromium rather than being fetched separately. Golden PNGs are committed binaries, so the review requirement ("reviewed as images") doubles as a control against a binary being swapped for something unrelated. Reviewed under **E11-X02**.

## Accessibility notes
Golden images are how the **high-contrast theme** stops being a claim and becomes a verified artefact: it is a first-class golden dimension, so a token change that quietly breaks high-contrast fails CI. The automated contrast-ratio test in E11-T04 checks the token pairs; the goldens check that the pairs actually reach the pixels. Neither substitutes for the manual screen-reader and low-vision passes in **E11-Q05**.

## Performance notes
Not a performance gate (SwiftShader timings are meaningless). The only performance requirement is on the harness itself: <=10 minutes for the full suite, parallelised across runner slots, so it can be a required check on every PR without becoming the reason people stop opening PRs.

## Observability
Diff artefacts (triptychs) published on every failure; a golden-count and manifest-coverage summary published on every run so drift in coverage is visible. Failures name the layer, theme and density of each failing case, not just the file name.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.

title: Configure SAST, SCA and CI guardrails for the chart-engine package
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` makes SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep), SCA (Dependabot/npm audit) and secrets scanning non-negotiable. Generic rules catch generic problems; this ticket adds the **engine-specific** rules that encode E11-X01's threat model and the architectural invariants that everything else in the Epic depends on.

The invariants are worth enforcing mechanically because they are exactly the kind that erode: "the engine performs no I/O" and "the engine imports no React" are true on day one and quietly false six months later after three reasonable-looking PRs. A CI rule is the only thing that keeps an architectural boundary real.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Boundary check** (the highest-value rule): `packages/chart-engine` must import no React, no application store, no `fetch`/`XHR`/WebSocket client and no Bybit-specific type. Implemented as a dependency-graph assertion (`dependency-cruiser` or equivalent) failing the build on violation — this is the Epic acceptance criterion "the engine package stays framework-free" made enforceable.
- **No-I/O rule**: no `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, `navigator.sendBeacon` or `localStorage` in the package (IndexedDB is permitted **only** in `src/text/` for the atlas cache, with the exception narrowly scoped and commented).
- **No dynamic code**: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no `setTimeout`/`setInterval` with a string argument, and no shader source constructed from non-constant data (the E11-X01 tampering control).
- **Typed-array safety Semgrep rules**: flag indexing into a typed array with a value derived from a message payload without a preceding bounds check; flag arithmetic on decoded values without `Number.isFinite` validation.
- **Debug-surface exclusion**: the E2E harness route (`/__engine-harness`) and any `window.__engine*` export must be absent from production builds — a build-time assertion, since a debug surface that ships is a genuine disclosure path.
- **Diagnostics allowlist rule**: the `copyDiagnostics()` payload's field set is asserted against an allowlist, so a future contributor cannot add account or user data to a payload designed to be pasted publicly.
- **SCA**: Dependabot and npm audit on the package with a policy for the graphics/test dependencies (Playwright, pixelmatch, `fast-check`); pinned versions; a documented response SLA by severity.
- **Secrets scanning** over the package including fixtures — a fixture recorded from a real session could contain account identifiers, and this is the check that catches it.
- **Fixture-content check**: assert no fixture contains account ids, order ids, API keys or anything matching the PII patterns, so "temporarily" recording a real session cannot become permanent.
- **CI runner hardening** for the self-hosted benchmark runner: fork PRs require maintainer approval before benchmarks execute.

## Out of scope
- Organisation-wide SAST/SCA configuration — the DevSecOps baseline; this adds package-specific rules on top.
- DAST/ZAP — backend surfaces, E43.
- Container scanning — infrastructure Epics.
- Penetration testing — E43.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The framework-free boundary is mechanically enforced
  Given a PR adding a React import to packages/chart-engine
  When CI runs
  Then the boundary check fails with a message naming the offending import
  And the same holds for an application-store import, a fetch client or a Bybit-specific type

Scenario: The no-I/O invariant is enforced with its one narrow exception
  Given a PR adding a fetch call anywhere in the package
  Then the rule fails
  And IndexedDB use remains permitted only within src/text/ for the atlas cache

Scenario: Unchecked typed-array indexing is flagged
  Given code indexing a typed array with a value taken from a decoded message without a bounds check
  When Semgrep runs
  Then the pattern is flagged with a reference to the E11-X01 control it protects
  And a deliberate exception requires an inline justification comment to pass

Scenario: Debug surfaces cannot ship
  Given a production build
  When it is inspected for the E2E harness route and window.__engine exports
  Then neither is present
  And their presence fails the build rather than being caught in review

Scenario: The diagnostics payload cannot silently grow
  Given a PR adding an account identifier to the copyDiagnostics payload
  Then the allowlist assertion fails
  And adding a field requires an explicit allowlist change that a security reviewer sees

Scenario: Fixtures cannot contain real data
  Given a fixture containing an account id or an API key pattern
  When the fixture-content check runs
  Then it fails, naming the file and the matched pattern
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why the boundary check is worth more than the SAST rules.** Generic SAST finds generic bugs, and the engine's generic bug surface is small. The architectural invariants — framework-free, no I/O, no dynamic code — are what make the engine portable, testable and safe, and they are invisible to generic tooling. `dependency-cruiser` with an explicit forbidden-dependency ruleset turns each invariant into a failing build, which is the only form of architectural documentation that survives contact with time pressure.

**Rule messages carry their reason.** Each custom rule's failure message names the control and the threat-model entry it protects, so a developer hitting it learns why rather than looking for the fastest way around it. A rule that only says "forbidden import" gets suppressed; one that says "the engine must stay framework-free so it can run in a worker and be ported per ADR-0002's fallback" gets respected.

**Narrow exceptions, explicitly scoped.** The IndexedDB exception is scoped to one directory rather than granted package-wide, because a blanket exception is indistinguishable from no rule.

## Test plan
- Each rule **self-tested** against a deliberate violation, asserting it fails — a rule never observed to fire is not known to work.
- False-positive review over the existing codebase before rules become blocking, so the first week is not spent suppressing noise.
- Response SLA documented per severity for SCA findings.
- Rule configuration reviewed by the security engineer and the chart-engine lead together.

## Security notes
This ticket implements the **preventive** half of E11-X01's controls; **E11-X03** provides the detective half through abuse cases and manual review. The rules encode: no dynamic code (tampering), typed-array bounds validation (tampering), diagnostics allowlist (information disclosure), debug-surface exclusion (information disclosure), fixture hygiene (information disclosure), and the dependency policy (supply chain).

The self-hosted benchmark runner executes repository code, so fork PRs require maintainer approval before benchmarks run — standard self-hosted runner hygiene, called out because it is easy to overlook when the runner exists for performance reasons rather than security ones.

## Accessibility notes
N/A. One adjacent rule is included because it is cheap and the failure mode is silent: flag `innerHTML` assignment in the DOM-mirror code path (E11-S13), which is simultaneously an XSS control and the mechanism that keeps the mirror's text writing safe.

## Performance notes
Rules run in CI at lint time and add under 30 seconds to the pipeline. The typed-array Semgrep rules are scoped to the decode and ingest paths rather than the whole package, keeping scan time low and, more importantly, keeping the signal-to-noise ratio high enough that failures are taken seriously.

## Observability
SAST/SCA findings surface in the CI security tab with the response SLA per severity. Rule-violation rates are tracked so a rule that fires constantly is recognised as either mis-specified or protecting a genuinely problematic area — both worth knowing, and both invisible without the metric.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Security artefacts (threat model, abuse cases, rule configuration, review notes) committed to `docs/plan/` or the security folder, and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Every identified threat has a disposition: mitigated (with the control named and its implementing ticket linked), accepted (with Owner sign-off recorded), or transferred.
- [ ] Controls verified by a test, a scan rule or a documented manual check - never by assertion alone.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scans green on the affected packages, or findings triaged with recorded justification.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted with date.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if the work surfaced a new risk or retired an existing one.
- [ ] Findings that require engineering work are filed as tickets with `priority/*` and an owner, not left inside the report.

## Dependencies
- **E11-X01** — the threat model the custom rules encode.
- **E11-T01** — the package must exist to configure rules against.
- **E11-Q02** — the E2E harness whose production exclusion is asserted.
- Feeds **E11-X03**'s review.

## Branch
`security/chart-engine-sast-rules` · 1 PR <=400 LOC (mostly configuration).

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` — STRIDE method, SAST/SCA/DAST tooling, review gates, data classification
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 (data model), §6 (worker protocol), §7 (memory budgets)
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` — binary framing the decoder consumes
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 (security sign-off is never silently skipped)
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §7 (required checks)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (security layer)
- `/CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16 (engine performs no I/O)

2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6)

**Commands**

- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**

title: Black-box test plan for the E12 bar-builder and series story groups
body:
## Context
E12 turns a raw trade tape into every bar family the terminal can draw (time, tick, volume, range, delta, renko) and into six series types on the WebGL canvas. Every later epic — indicators (E13), footprint (E18), profiles (E19), CVD (E23), replay (E26) — consumes those bars as if they were ground truth, so a silent off-by-one boundary or a mis-allocated renko volume propagates into order-flow analytics that a trader will act on with real money. That is risk **R7 Data accuracy** and it is exactly what `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 and §8 mean by a recorded, non-skippable QA sign-off.

Today the E12 child tickets each say *what* to build; nothing says how a QA engineer executes the epic end-to-end against a staging build and declares "bars are correct". `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a written black-box test plan plus a white-box review checklist per feature. This ticket produces that artefact. It is deliberately black-box: written against the screens, the REST contract in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS contract in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, with no knowledge of internal builder classes, so it stays valid when `E12-T01`..`E12-T05` are refactored.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e12-bars-and-series-test-plan.md` with six executable sections, one per story group:
  1. **Candlestick rendering & historical load** (US-CHART-001, US-MKT-008) — `SCR-047`, `SCR-048`, `CMP-180`, `CMP-181`, `GET /market/klines`, covers `E12-S01`, `E12-S05`.
  2. **Alternative series types** (US-CHART-002) — `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle`, `CMP-199 ChartLegend`, volume sub-pane; covers `E12-S02`.
  3. **Activity-based bars** (US-CHART-003) — `SCR-042`, `GET /market/bars?bar_type=tick|volume`, tables `bars_tick`, `bars_volume`; covers `E12-S03`, `E12-T03`.
  4. **Range, delta and renko bars** (US-CHART-004) — `GET /market/bars?bar_type=range|delta|renko`, tables `bars_range`, `bars_delta`, `bars_renko`, rebuild progress; covers `E12-S04`, `E12-T04`, `E12-T05`.
  5. **Symbol & timeframe switching** (US-CHART-005) — `SCR-041`, `CMP-220 IntervalPicker`, `CMP-029 Skeleton-Chart`; covers `E12-S05`.
  6. **Days-to-load & history honesty** (US-CHART-010) — `meta.recording_started_at`, partial-history marker, `SCR-047`; covers `E12-S06`, `E12-T06`.
- Per case: id `E12-TC-<group><nn>`, preconditions (named fixture symbol-day), steps, expected result, the `US-*` id verified, the child ticket covered, and automation status (automated in `E12-Q02`/`E12-Q03`/`E12-Q04`, or manual-only).
- A **fixture & test-data appendix** naming the recorded Bybit symbol-days used everywhere in E12 QA: `btcusdt-2026-09-01` (dense, 1.2 M prints), `btcusdt-2026-09-02-gap` (contains a deliberate WS sequence gap), `ethusdt-2026-09-03-thin` (thin tape, many empty 1 m intervals), `newlist-2026-09-04` (symbol listed mid-day, recording starts at 11:17Z), and a synthetic `edge-ticks` tape exercising exact-threshold volume, exact-range and exact-brick crossings.
- A **traceability table** US-CHART-001..006, US-CHART-010, US-MKT-008 × test cases × automation status, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, proving no story is untested.
- **Cross-bar-type invariant cases** that no single child ticket owns: the same tape rebuilt twice yields byte-identical bars; the sum of `v` across any bar family over a window equals the sum of trade sizes in `trades` for that window; `confirm:false` appears on exactly one bar per series; non-time bars always carry `close_t_ms`.
- Defect-reporting conventions for E12: severity per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3, with **any bar-value discrepancy against the tape filed `priority/p0-critical` by definition**, because downstream order-flow epics treat bars as evidence.

## Out of scope
- Writing the automation itself: golden-fixture suite (`E12-Q02`), Playwright E2E (`E12-Q03`), contract tests (`E12-Q04`).
- Performance and chaos execution (`E12-Q05`, `E12-Q06`) and the a11y audit (`E12-Q07`).
- Security-owned artefacts (`E12-X01`..`E12-X04`).
- Indicator correctness (E13), footprint cell aggregation (E18), replay determinism (E26) — referenced only where they consume E12 bars.
- Recorder retention behaviour (E16); the plan assumes a recorded window exists and tests the *honesty* of the history marker, not the retention job.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E12 story is covered by at least one executable case
  Given the test plan is merged at qa/plans/e12-bars-and-series-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against US-CHART-001..006, US-CHART-010 and US-MKT-008
  Then every story id maps to at least one E12-TC case
  And every case names the child ticket it covers and its automation status

Scenario: A QA engineer can execute the plan without asking questions
  Given a fresh staging build and the seeded fixture symbol-days
  When an engineer who did not write the plan executes group 3 end to end
  Then every precondition is satisfiable from the fixture appendix alone
  And each step has a single unambiguous expected result

Scenario: Failure case - a builder regression is caught by the plan
  Given a build where the volume builder does not split an overshooting print
  When case E12-TC-C04 (exact-threshold overshoot) is executed
  Then the case fails with an observed-vs-expected bar boundary recorded
  And the defect is filed priority/p0-critical per the plan's severity mapping

Scenario: Edge case - window predates recording
  Given a request for tick bars on newlist-2026-09-04 starting at 00:00Z
  When case E12-TC-F02 is executed
  Then the API returns 422 no_data_recorded rather than substituting REST klines
  And the chart shows the partial-history marker at 11:17Z, not an empty grid
```

## Technical notes / design
- Structure the plan so each group is independently executable in under 40 minutes; QA capacity is 2 SDETs across the whole R1 train.
- Expected values for bar boundaries are **derived from the fixture tape by an independent calculation** (a small spreadsheet/notebook committed next to the plan), never copied from the implementation's output — otherwise the plan can only confirm the code agrees with itself.

title: Backfill historical OHLCV from Bybit klines with paging, cache and backoff
body:
## Context
**US-MKT-008 (Must)**: "As a trader, I want historical bars loaded on chart open, so that a chart is useful immediately, not after hours of recording." The recorder starts empty; without kline backfill, a freshly opened chart shows nothing until enough tape accumulates, which would make R1 undemonstrable.

The subtlety is that klines are a *second-class* source. `24-internal-schemas.md` §2 calls them "a cross-check and a cold-start backfill, not the primary bar source", and `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines` encodes the source priority: (1) locally recorded tape aggregated by the bar builder, (2) Bybit REST kline backfill for windows predating recording, (3) Parquet cold tier. The response must state which tiers it touched in `meta.sources` and where native tick-accurate data begins in `meta.recording_started_at` — "before that point delta/footprint fields are null". Honesty about data provenance is a product requirement here, not a nicety.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Paged backfill client against Bybit v5 `/v5/market/kline`, respecting the 1 000-row response limit, paging until the configured days-to-load window is covered, oldest→newest normalisation into the `Bar` model.
- Persistence into `bars_time` via E12-T02's write path, marked as kline-sourced so delta/footprint fields are **null**, not zero — a zero delta is a lie, a null is a fact.
- Cache-first read: a window already in QuestDB is served locally and only the tail is fetched from the exchange.
- Rate-limit handling: exponential backoff with jitter on Bybit rate-limit responses (including code 10018), the partial result kept usable, and a non-blocking "loading older bars…" state emitted to the client.
- Progress reporting: backfill progress surfaced so SCR-030/SCR-047 can show it (the UI wiring is E12-S12; this Story emits the events).
- Cold-tier read-through to Parquet for windows older than QuestDB hot retention, via the E07 adapter.
- `meta.sources` and `meta.recording_started_at` populated correctly on every response (consumed by E12-T05's endpoints).
- Cross-check mode: compare a kline-sourced window against builder-produced bars for the same window where both exist, and log discrepancies — this is the "cross-check" role §2 assigns to klines.

## Out of scope
- The days-to-load control and memory-budget warning UI — **US-CHART-010 belongs to E11** (SCR-044/SCR-047); this Story consumes the configured value.
- Non-time bar backfill — tick/volume/range/renko bars cannot be reconstructed from klines at all; a window predating recording returns `no_data_recorded` (422) per `/market/bars` (E12-T05 implements the response, this Story supplies the boundary fact).
- The recorder itself (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backfill on chart open
  Given I open BTCUSDT 5m with a 30-day days-to-load setting
  Then bars are paged from /v5/market/kline until the window is covered
  And progress is emitted as pages complete
  And the chart becomes interactive before paging finishes

Scenario: Cache hit
  Given the requested bars are already in QuestDB
  Then they are served locally in under 300 ms for 5 000 bars
  And only the tail beyond the stored range is fetched from the exchange

Scenario: Rate limited
  Given Bybit returns a rate-limit error mid-backfill
  Then the client backs off exponentially with jitter and retries
  And the already-fetched partial result remains usable and rendered
  And the UI is told "loading older bars…" rather than being blocked

Scenario: Kline-sourced bars are honest about what they lack
  Given a window that predates recording_started_at
  Then its bars carry null delta, null min_delta, null max_delta and null cvd
  And meta.sources names bybit_rest
  And meta.recording_started_at states where tick-accurate data begins

Scenario: Non-time bars refuse rather than fake it
  Given a tick-bar request for a window predating recording
  Then the response is 422 no_data_recorded
  And no kline-derived substitute is returned

Scenario: Cross-check discrepancy is surfaced
  Given a window where both recorded tape and exchange klines exist
  When they are compared
  Then any OHLCV divergence beyond the documented tolerance is logged with the symbol, interval and bar timestamp
  And a metric is incremented so persistent feed rot is visible
```

## Technical notes / design
- Paging must be resumable: a backfill interrupted by a restart continues from the earliest stored bar rather than restarting from the present.
- Concurrency is bounded per symbol and globally, and shares the E08 rate-limit governor rather than implementing a second one — two independent limiters is how a 10018 storm happens.
- Idempotency comes free from the QuestDB dedup upsert (E12-T02); re-fetching an already-stored page is harmless, which is what makes the resumable path simple.
- Kline `confirm` semantics: never persist an unconfirmed candle as closed (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines` description; the same flag drives E12-S10's forming-bar rendering).

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85%: paging arithmetic at the 1 000-row boundary, backoff schedule with jitter bounds, cache-hit/tail-fetch decision, `meta` population.
- **Integration** against recorded Bybit fixtures (never the live exchange in CI): full backfill, interrupted-and-resumed backfill, rate-limited backfill, cold-tier read-through.
- **Contract**: `/market/klines` responses validated against the OpenAPI schema including `meta.sources` and `meta.recording_started_at`.
- **Chaos**: exchange 5xx and rate-limit storms injected mid-backfill; the partial result must stay usable (feeds E11-Q04's chaos charter).
- **Perf**: 5 000-bar cache hit measured against the 300 ms budget.

## Security notes
Outbound calls to the exchange are unauthenticated public market endpoints — no API keys are used or needed for kline backfill, and the code path must not acquire them (least privilege: a market-data path that never touches the key vault cannot leak it). Inputs `symbol`, `interval`, `from`, `to`, `limit` are all client-controlled: validate against the instrument catalogue and the documented enums, and bound the window so a single request cannot trigger unbounded paging — an unbounded `from` is both a self-DoS and a way to burn the shared rate-limit budget that E34's fan-out later depends on.

## Accessibility notes
Backfill progress and the rate-limited state must be exposed as text with a determinate value where known ("loading older bars… 12 of 30 days"), rendered by E12-S12 into SCR-047 and announced politely (not assertively) so it does not interrupt a screen-reader user mid-read. The "delta unavailable before <ts>" fact must be text, never conveyed by a greyed-out colour alone.

## Performance notes
Budgets from US-MKT-008: ≤300 ms to first paint from cache for 5 000 bars; paging respects the 1 000-row limit; retry with jitter. Backfill must never block the UI thread or the ingest path — it runs as a background task with bounded concurrency.

## Observability
`bar_backfill_pages_total{symbol,interval}`, `bar_backfill_bars_total`, `bar_backfill_duration_seconds`, `bar_backfill_rate_limited_total`, `bar_backfill_failures_total`, `bar_kline_crosscheck_divergence_total`. Log backfill start/finish with the window and the resulting row count; WARN on every rate-limit hit with the backoff applied.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario backed by an automated test; coverage ≥85%; `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines` semantics match the implementation; perf budget recorded; chaos scenarios executed; QA sign-off; demoed (open a fresh chart on an unrecorded symbol); feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T02** — the `bars_time` write path and cold-tier adapter.
- **E12-S01** — the `Bar` model population and the builder path klines are cross-checked against.
- **E08** — the Bybit REST client, rate-limit governor and instrument catalogue.

## Branch
`feat/e12-kline-backfill`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-MKT-008 (Must), US-MKT-001, US-CHART-010
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines` (source priority, `meta.sources`, `meta.recording_started_at`)
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §2 (klines as cross-check and cold-start only)
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.8, retention/cold-tier tables
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-MKT-008 → SCR-151, CMP-001/019/021/026
