title: Render candlestick and OHLC bar series through the WebGL engine
body:
## Context
**US-CHART-001 (Must)** is the headline of R1: "I want candlesticks rendered by the WebGL engine, so that price is legible and smooth at any zoom" — with an NFR of **≥55 fps at 100k bars on the reference GPU and ≤512 MB GPU memory per chart pane**. It is the first thing anyone sees and the benchmark the whole engine investment is judged by.

`26-chart-engine-design.md` §4 fixes the implementation shape: candles are "1 instanced quad for bodies + 1 for wicks", program `candle`, **2 draw calls**, per-instance attributes `x, openY, closeY, highY, lowY, colourIdx`. The steady-state target for a whole pane is ≤18 draw calls, so a candle series that spends more than 2 has already broken the budget for everything else.

E11 supplies the chassis (scene graph, transforms, LOD infrastructure, columnar stores, worker protocol). This Story supplies the first real series plugin that rides it, through the `SeriesPlugin` interface of §3.12 — and by being first, it proves the plugin interface is actually sufficient.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `CandleSeries` and `BarSeries` (OHLC bars) as `SeriesPlugin` implementations in `packages/chart-engine`, registered through the public API of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8.
- Instanced geometry: one quad instance per bar for bodies, one for wicks; colour via the theme LUT (`colourIdx`), never a hard-coded colour (§5.1).
- Binding to the engine's columnar typed-array stores (E11-T03) with append (new bar), patch (forming-bar update) and prepend (backfill of older bars) mutations, so a live update never re-uploads the whole series.
- Correct geometry at every bar spacing, including the degenerate cases: doji (open == close, body must remain a visible minimum-height line), zero-range bar (high == low), and single-bar series.
- Index-spaced rendering for non-time-aligned series (`isTimeAligned=false` from E12-S03/S04) — bricks and range bars are spaced by index, not by timestamp.
- Gap rendering: `gap_before=true` draws a real gap; values are never interpolated across it.
- Empty state: when the requested range has no bars, the pane shows the SCR-047 empty state naming the first available timestamp rather than an empty grid (US-CHART-001 scenario 3).
- Golden-image coverage through E11-T08's SwiftShader harness.

## Out of scope
- Line/area/baseline/Heikin-Ashi series — E12-S07.
- The volume column pane — E12-S08.
- LOD tier selection and decimation — E12-S09 (this Story renders L0 correctly; S09 adds the ladder).
- Forming-bar update semantics from the WS feed — E12-S10.
- Crosshair, axes, pan/zoom, price scales — **E11**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Candles render in one pass
  Given BTCUSDT 1m with 5 000 bars loaded
  Then bodies and wicks are drawn in exactly two draw calls
  And the pane's total draw calls remain within the 18-call steady-state budget

Scenario: Frame budget holds at scale
  Given 100 000 bars in the series
  When the view is zoomed to fit
  Then the p95 frame time stays within 16.6 ms on the reference GPU
  And GPU memory for the pane stays under 512 MB

Scenario: No data is an explicit state, not an empty grid
  Given the symbol has no bars in the requested range
  Then the empty state names the first available timestamp
  And no axes-only grid is rendered as though data existed

Scenario: Degenerate bars stay visible
  Given a doji where open equals close
  Then the body renders as a minimum-height line rather than disappearing
  Given a bar where high equals low
  Then it renders without a zero-area draw artefact

Scenario: Gaps are gaps
  Given a bar carrying gap_before=true
  Then a visual discontinuity is drawn
  And no value is interpolated across the gap

Scenario: Index-spaced series are spaced by index
  Given a renko series with isTimeAligned=false
  Then bricks are laid out at uniform index spacing
  And the time axis labels reflect each brick's actual open_time rather than implying a uniform time grid

Scenario: Theme switch does not re-upload data
  When the theme changes
  Then colours update through the LUT in under 1 ms
  And no vertex or instance buffer is re-uploaded
```

## Technical notes / design
- Two draw calls is a hard constraint, not an aspiration: any per-bar draw call or per-bar uniform update breaks the budget at 100k bars. Instance attributes carry everything per-bar.
- Minimum body height for a doji is a device-pixel-aware constant so it stays visible at any DPI without becoming chunky at high DPI (E11-S10 supplies DPI correctness).
- Colour comes from tokens via LUT textures (§5.1) — the engine holds no hard-coded colours, which is also what makes the <1 ms theme switch possible.
- The `SeriesPlugin` interface is being exercised for the first time here; any insufficiency found must be fixed in the interface (and reported to E11-T09's API freeze) rather than worked around with a private escape hatch.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80% (frontend threshold): geometry generation for normal, doji, zero-range, single-bar and gapped series; index-vs-time spacing selection; LUT colour mapping.
- **Golden image** on SwiftShader (E11-T08): candles and OHLC bars at several spacings and both themes, plus the degenerate cases.
- **Perf**: the engine benchmark harness (E11-T06) extended with a candle-series scenario at 5k / 100k bars; p95 frame time and GPU memory recorded and gated in CI.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): open a chart, confirm candles render, switch theme, confirm the empty state on a symbol with no data in range.
- **a11y**: axe-core on SCR-030 and SCR-047; the DOM-mirror (E11-S13) must expose the rendered bars.

## Security notes
The series consumes server-supplied bar data and renders it; the threat is malformed or hostile data causing a client-side crash or hang (a denial of service against the trader at exactly the wrong moment). Validate defensively at the store boundary: non-finite prices, inverted high/low, negative volume and absurd bar counts are rejected with a visible error state rather than propagated into buffer writes. No secrets and no credentials are handled in this package (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16 keeps the engine free of app state and `fetch`).

## Accessibility notes
The canvas is not the accessible artefact — E11's DOM mirror and the SCR-045 data table are, and this Story must feed them per-bar OHLCV plus the `gap_before`, `partial` and `confirm` flags so they can be stated in text. Colour alone must never distinguish up from down bars: the design system's candle tokens must satisfy the non-colour-only requirement of `05-accessibility-standard.md` (shape/outline differentiation for the colour-blind case), and this is checked at design QA against the E11-D02 chassis spec. Contrast of body and wick against the pane background meets WCAG 2.2 AA non-text contrast.

## Performance notes
Budgets: p95 frame ≤16.6 ms (budget #1 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, a hard CI gate); ≥55 fps at 100k bars zoom-to-fit; ≤512 MB GPU memory per pane; 2 draw calls for the series; theme switch <1 ms. A regression >10% fails the build per roadmap §5.3.

## Observability
Engine `FrameStats` already exports frame time and draw-call count (E11); this Story adds `series.candle` labels so the diagnostics overlay (SCR-046, E11-T07) attributes cost to the candle series specifically. Client-side error counter for rejected malformed bar data.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario backed by an automated test; frontend coverage ≥80%; golden images committed; perf benchmark recorded against budget #1 and gated in CI; axe-core green on SCR-030/047; manual screen-reader spot-check of the data cursor over candles; design-QA pass against the E11-D02/E12 design spec; QA sign-off; demoed at Sprint Review; feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E11** — scene graph, transforms, columnar stores, worker protocol, `SeriesPlugin` interface, theme LUT ingestion, golden-image harness.
- **E12-T05** — the REST endpoint supplying the initial bar window.

## Branch
`feat/e12-candle-series`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001 (Must)
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 data model, §3.12 plugin API, §4 render layers (candles: 2 draw calls), §5 theming, §8 API sketch

title: Show the forming bar distinctly from closed bars with a live countdown
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 gives this Story its reason to exist in one sentence: **"Unconfirmed bars. The last bar in any `bars`/`footprint` frame may have `confirm: false`. A client MUST NOT treat it as closed — this is the flicker bug Bybit's own `confirm` flag exists to prevent."** The same discipline appears in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`include_open` + `confirm`) and in `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1 (`Bar.closed`).

The trading consequence is concrete: a rule that fires `on_bar_close`, an indicator that computes on close, or a trader reading a completed pattern must all agree on *when* a bar is closed. A UI that renders a forming bar identically to a closed one invites a trader to act on a pattern that has not happened yet.

US-CHART-001 also requires that "the forming bar updates on every trade **without a full redraw**", and US-CHART-008 requires the bar-close countdown (CMP-226) that "turns amber in the final 10 seconds".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Consumption of the `bars` WS topic (E12-T06): snapshot application, delta application by sequence, and resync on a gap — with the forming bar patched in place rather than appended.
- Visual distinction of the forming bar per the design spec (E11-D02 chassis + this Epic's design tickets): a distinct treatment that is **not colour-only**.
- Patch-only updates: a forming-bar tick mutates one instance in the store and redraws, never re-uploading or re-decimating the series.
- Bar-close countdown via CMP-226 for time-aligned series: text, 1 Hz, `aria-live="off"` by default, amber warn state that adds a word rather than only a colour; hidden (not zeroed) for non-time-aligned series where no close time can be predicted.
- Transition on close: when `confirm` flips to true, the bar settles into the closed treatment and the next bar opens, with no flicker and no duplicated bar.
- Amended-bar handling: a re-emitted closed bar (late trade, `amended=true` from E12-S01) updates in place and is announced as a correction rather than silently changing under the user.
- Stale-feed handling: if the topic stops delivering, the forming bar is marked stale rather than continuing to display as live (mirroring US-MKT-003's "grey out with a stale marker rather than showing frozen values as if live").

## Out of scope
- The WS topic implementation — E12-T06.
- Crosshair readout layout — E11-S07 (this Story supplies the forming/closed fact it displays).
- `on_bar_close` rule semantics — E35.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Forming bar is visibly and programmatically distinct
  Given the last bar has confirm=false
  Then it renders with the forming treatment
  And that distinction is not conveyed by colour alone
  And the accessible readout for that bar states that it is still forming

Scenario: Updates patch, not rebuild
  Given 20 trades update the forming bar in one second
  Then only the last instance in the store is mutated
  And no full series re-upload or re-decimation occurs
  And the frame budget is unaffected

Scenario: Close transition is clean
  Given the forming bar's interval boundary passes
  When the close frame arrives with confirm=true
  Then that bar settles into the closed treatment exactly once
  And a new forming bar opens
  And no duplicate bar appears at the same open time

Scenario: Countdown behaves
  Given a 5m time series
  Then the countdown shows seconds remaining as text, updating at 1 Hz
  And in the final 10 seconds it adds a warning word in addition to any colour change
  Given a renko series
  Then no countdown is displayed, because no close time can be predicted

Scenario: Amendment is surfaced, not silent
  Given a closed bar is re-emitted with amended=true after a late trade
  Then the bar updates in place
  And the change is surfaced to the user rather than mutating silently

Scenario: Stale feed is not shown as live
  Given the bars topic stops delivering for longer than the staleness threshold
  Then the forming bar is marked stale in text
  And it is not presented as a live value
```

## Technical notes / design
- The forming bar must be excluded from LOD aggregation buckets that would freeze it (E12-S09's corresponding scenario) — the two Stories share this contract and it is tested from both sides.
- Countdown time comes from the offset-corrected exchange clock (US-MKT-009), not the browser clock; a browser clock skew would show a countdown that disagrees with the actual bar close.
- Resync after a sequence gap must not duplicate the forming bar: applying a fresh snapshot replaces the tail rather than appending to it.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: snapshot/delta application, forming-bar patching, close transition, amended handling, staleness detection, countdown formatting and warn threshold.
- **Integration**: against a scripted WS fixture replaying a real bar-close sequence including a gap and a resync.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): watch a live-ish 1m bar close on a fixture feed; assert exactly one closed bar and one new forming bar.
- **Perf**: forming-bar update path measured to confirm no re-upload and no frame-budget impact at 100k bars.
- **a11y**: axe-core; manual screen-reader pass confirming the forming/closed distinction and that the countdown does not flood announcements.

## Security notes
The client must not trust frame ordering blindly: apply deltas strictly by sequence, reject out-of-order or duplicate sequences, and resync rather than merging speculatively — a malformed or replayed frame must not be able to fabricate a bar state. Beyond that, no credentials or secrets are handled in this path.

## Accessibility notes
This is a case where a wrong visual is a trading hazard, so the forming/closed distinction must be available in three ways: the visual treatment (not colour-only), the accessible readout for the focused bar ("forming" / "closed"), and the SCR-045 data table's per-row state. CMP-226's contract is binding: text rather than a bare progress ring, 1 Hz updates, `aria-live="off"` by default so it never floods a screen reader, and the warn state adds a word, not just a colour. Amendment notifications must be polite, not assertive.

## Performance notes
A forming-bar update is a single instance patch plus a redraw; it must not trigger re-decimation, re-upload or a scene rebuild. US-CHART-001's "updates on every trade without a full redraw" is the acceptance condition, verified by an instrumented counter in the benchmark rather than by eye.

## Observability
`bars_forming_updates_applied_total`, `bars_ws_resyncs_total` (client side), `bars_stale_seconds` gauge, `bars_amendments_surfaced_total`. Frame attribution confirms the patch path does not re-upload.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario automated; coverage ≥80%; axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass on the forming/closed state and the countdown; design-QA pass on the forming treatment; perf assertion that no re-upload occurs; QA sign-off; demoed (watch a bar close); feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T06** — the `bars` WS topic supplying snapshots, deltas and the `confirm` flag.
- **E12-S06** — the candle series being patched.
- **E11-S07** — the crosshair/readout and countdown placement in the chassis.

## Branch
`feat/e12-forming-bar`

## References
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 (unconfirmed bars), §7 snapshot+delta
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines` `include_open`/`confirm`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.1 (`closed`), §3.3 (amended late trades)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001, US-CHART-008, US-MKT-003 (stale marker principle)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-226 BarCountdown

title: Implement BarBuilderSet fan-out with snapshot/restore state persistence
body:
## Context
A single symbol typically carries 3–8 active bar specs at once — 1m, 5m and 1h time bars plus a footprint tick or volume series. `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.5 fixes how that works: "`BarBuilderSet` fans one `TradeEvent` to all builders for that symbol in a single pass; **builders never subscribe to the bus individually**. Cost is O(specs) per trade with no allocation in the common path."

The second half of this Task is restart survival. §3.2: "`snapshot()`/`restore()` exist so a restart or a replay seek resumes mid-bar without replaying the whole day. `BuilderState` is a msgpack blob persisted every 60 s per `(symbol, spec_hash)`." Without it, every backend restart either loses the forming bar or pays a full-day rebuild for every active spec on every symbol — which at the recorder's symbol count is minutes of cold start.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `BarBuilderSet`: one bus subscription per symbol, fanning each `TradeEvent` to every registered builder in a single pass; register/unregister of specs at runtime without dropping trades.
- Lifecycle: a spec is registered when a chart, a footprint view, an indicator, a rule or the recorder needs it, and reference-counted so the last consumer's departure unregisters it after a grace period (mirroring the 30-second grace of US-MKT-005).
- A hard cap on concurrent specs per symbol and per user, with a clear error when exceeded (the resource-exhaustion mitigation named in the Epic's security notes).
- `BuilderState` msgpack serialisation for all six builders, persisted every 60 s per `(symbol, spec_hash)`, with atomic write and a corruption-safe read (a bad blob is discarded and the spec cold-starts rather than crashing).
- Restart path: on boot, restore each active spec from its blob, then replay only the trades newer than the blob's watermark before going live.
- Emit routing: `BarUpdate`s flow to the QuestDB write path (E12-T02) and to the WS publisher (E12-T06) from one place, so live and replay share the emit path exactly.

## Out of scope
- The WS topic and framing itself (E12-T06) and the REST endpoints (E12-T05).
- Replay-specific seek semantics — E26 reuses `restore()` as-is; no replay code here.
- The recorder's symbol-list management (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One pass, many specs
  Given 8 registered specs for BTCUSDT
  When a TradeEvent arrives
  Then the bus is read once and all 8 builders are advanced
  And no builder holds its own bus subscription

Scenario: Restart resumes mid-bar
  Given a 1h time bar is 40 minutes formed and a state blob was written 30 seconds ago
  When the process restarts
  Then the builder restores from the blob, replays only the trades after the blob watermark
  And the resulting bar is identical to the one an uninterrupted run would have produced (invariant BI-5)

Scenario: Corrupt state is survivable
  Given a truncated or unparseable state blob
  When restore is attempted
  Then the blob is discarded, a warning is logged with the spec_hash
  And the spec cold-starts by rebuilding from the tape rather than crashing the process

Scenario: Spec cap is enforced
  Given the per-symbol spec cap is reached
  When another distinct spec is registered
  Then registration is refused with an error naming the cap and the currently active specs
  And existing series are unaffected

Scenario: Last consumer releases the spec
  Given the only chart using vol:1000 on ETHUSDT closes
  Then the spec is unregistered after the grace period
  And its final state blob is written before teardown
```

## Technical notes / design
- "No allocation in the common path" is a measurable requirement, not a slogan: the fan-out loop must not build a list per trade. Verify with an allocation-count assertion in the benchmark.
- The state blob watermark is a `TsUs` of the last applied trade, so the post-restore replay window is exact. Persisting every 60 s bounds the replay to 60 s of tape per spec.
- Atomic write: write-temp-then-rename, so a crash mid-write never leaves a half blob (which the corruption path above then has to handle anyway — belt and braces).
- Reference counting must be robust to a client that disconnects without unsubscribing; the grace period plus a liveness sweep handles it.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥85%: registration/unregistration, reference counting, cap enforcement, msgpack round-trip per builder kind, corrupt-blob handling.
- **Property**: BI-5 — `restore(snapshot())` at random cut points across all six builders yields the same final series as an uninterrupted run, including mid-split (volume) and mid-reversal (renko) states.
- **Integration**: kill and restart the process mid-day against a recorded fixture; assert the resulting series equals the uninterrupted run byte-for-byte.
- **Perf**: fan-out benchmark at 8 specs × 5 000 prints/s with an allocation assertion.

## Security notes
This is where the resource-exhaustion mitigation actually lives. An attacker (or an over-enthusiastic client) subscribing to hundreds of distinct `spec_hash`es multiplies CPU, memory and QuestDB SYMBOL cardinality without bound. Enforce: per-symbol spec cap, per-user total spec cap, and a global cap; refuse with a clear error rather than degrading silently. State blobs are written to a server-controlled path derived from `(symbol, spec_hash)` where both components are already whitelist-validated (E12-T01) — no client string is ever concatenated into a filesystem path, which closes the path-traversal vector that `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 flags for E16's archive paths.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The cap-exceeded error message is rendered by SCR-042 and must be a human-readable sentence stating the cap and what to close, not a code.

## Performance notes
Budget: fan-out adds O(specs) with no allocation, keeping ingest→bus within the ≤20 ms p95 of US-MKT-006 at 5 000 prints/s. Cold start after restart must be bounded by the 60 s state cadence rather than by the day length — measured as "time from boot to first live bar emit" and recorded.

## Observability
`bar_builder_specs_active{symbol}`, `bar_builder_fanout_latency_seconds`, `bar_state_snapshots_written_total`, `bar_state_restore_failures_total`, `bar_builder_cold_starts_total`, `bar_builder_spec_cap_rejections_total`. Cold-start duration exported as a histogram.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2: acceptance criteria verified by tests including the restart integration test; coverage ≥85%; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.2/§3.5 matches shipped behaviour; perf benchmark with allocation assertion recorded; security review comment on the cap and path handling; demo of the restart-resume behaviour (observable effect); PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S01**, **E12-S02** — at least two builder kinds must exist before fan-out is meaningful; S03/S04 plug in without changing this code.
- **E12-T02** — the write path the emit routing targets.

## Branch
`feat/e12-builder-set`

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.2 (protocol, `BuilderState`), §3.5 (multi-spec efficiency), §3.4 BI-5
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-MKT-005 (30 s unsubscribe grace), US-MKT-006 (throughput NFR)

title: Implement GET /market/klines and GET /market/bars with source metadata
body:
## Context
Two REST endpoints are the bootstrap path for every chart: `GET /market/klines` for time candles and `GET /market/bars` as "the single entry point for every non-time bar construction". Both are fully specified in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, down to the `bar_type`/`param` table, the `x-rbac: { permissions: [marketdata:read] }` gate, the `meta.sources` / `meta.recording_started_at` honesty fields and the exact error semantics — `/market/bars` returns **422 `no_data_recorded`** for a window starting before recording began "rather than silently substituting REST klines, because tick-accurate construction is impossible there".

This Task implements the spec rather than inventing it. The interface is already merged, so per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10 the work here is implementation plus contract tests that prove the implementation and the document are the same thing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /market/klines`: `symbol`, `interval`, `from`, `to`, `limit`, `price_type` (trade|mark|index|premium_index), `include_open`, `include_delta`; source priority tape → kline backfill → Parquet; `confirm` flag on the in-progress candle only when `include_open=true`.
- `GET /market/bars`: `symbol`, `bar_type`, `param`, `from`, `to`, `limit`, `include_open`, `include_delta` (default true); the full `bar_type` enum with `param` parsed per the documented table; 422 `no_data_recorded` for pre-recording windows; `pnf` and (per ADR-0014) possibly `atr:*` returning a 422 that names the reason and the supported alternatives.
- Shared response assembly producing `KlineResponse` with `meta.next_cursor`, `has_more`, `count`, `sources`, `recording_started_at`, `generated_at`.
- Cursor-based pagination honouring `BarLimit`, oldest→newest ordering.
- RBAC: `marketdata:read`, scope none, enforced by the shared dependency from E09.
- Null-not-zero discipline for delta fields on kline-sourced windows.
- Generated contract tests asserting responses validate against the committed OpenAPI schemas, including every documented error.

## Out of scope
- `GET /market/footprint` — E18.
- The WS `bars` topic — E12-T06.
- Client-side consumption — E12-S06/S11.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bars endpoint serves every supported bar type
  Given recorded tape for BTCUSDT
  When /market/bars is called for each of time, tick, volume, range, delta and renko with a valid param
  Then each returns bars ordered oldest to newest with meta.sources naming the tiers touched
  And the response validates against the KlineResponse schema

Scenario: Pre-recording window is refused for non-time bars
  Given recording_started_at is 2026-10-27
  When /market/bars is called for tick:500 with from=2026-10-12
  Then the response is 422 with code no_data_recorded
  And no kline-derived bars are returned

Scenario: Klines degrade honestly
  Given the same pre-recording window on /market/klines with include_delta=true
  Then bars are returned from the kline tier
  And their delta, min_delta, max_delta and cvd are null rather than zero
  And meta.recording_started_at states where tick-accurate data begins

Scenario: Invalid param is rejected before it reaches a builder
  When /market/bars is called with bar_type=tick and param="../../etc"
  Then the response is 400 validation_failed naming the param
  And no builder is instantiated and no QuestDB SYMBOL value is created

Scenario: Unauthorised access is refused
  Given a caller without marketdata:read
  When either endpoint is called
  Then the response is 403 and no market data is disclosed

Scenario: Oversized window is bounded, not served
  When a request would exceed the documented bar limit
  Then the response paginates with meta.has_more and meta.next_cursor
  And never returns an unbounded result set
```

## Technical notes / design
- `param` parsing is a strict whitelist per `bar_type` (bounded integer, or the documented colon grammar), enforcing `maxLength: 24` and rejecting dots, reusing the E12-T01 mapping rather than re-implementing it.
- Reads go through E12-T02's query helpers and E12-T03's spec registry; an endpoint must never construct a builder directly, or the spec cap is bypassed.
- `meta.sources` is assembled from what the read path actually touched, not predicted — a chart that says `questdb` while silently falling back to REST is exactly the dishonesty the spec is written to prevent.
- `generated_at` uses the offset-corrected exchange clock (US-MKT-009), not local wall time.

## Test plan
- **Contract** (generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml`): every documented response and error code, for both endpoints.
- **Unit** ≥85%: param parsing matrix, cursor arithmetic, `meta` assembly, null-vs-zero delta logic.
- **Integration** against a seeded QuestDB + recorded fixtures: each bar type, cache hit, cold-tier read-through, pre-recording refusal.
- **Security**: RBAC matrix (Owner/Manager/Viewer), param fuzzing, oversized-window rejection.

## Security notes
Labelled `security`. Threats: **injection** — `symbol` and `param` reach a query and a SYMBOL column, so parameterised queries and whitelist validation only, never interpolation; **DoS** — unbounded `from/to/limit` or a pathological `param` (`tick:1` over months) triggers unbounded work, so bar caps, window caps, per-user concurrency limits and the E12-T03 spec cap all apply at this boundary; **broken access control** — `marketdata:read` enforced through the shared RBAC dependency, never a hand-rolled check; **information disclosure** — error bodies name the field at fault but never leak internal paths, SQL or `spec_hash` internals. Data classification: public market data, no PII, no secrets, no key material. STRIDE notes feed the Epic-level model.

## Accessibility notes
No UI, but the error `message` fields are rendered verbatim by SCR-042 and SCR-047: they must be human-readable sentences that state what happened and what to do ("Tick bars need recorded trade data; recording for BTCUSDT begins 1 Dec 2026"), never bare codes.

## Performance notes
5 000-bar cache-hit response within the 300 ms first-paint budget of US-MKT-008, measured server-side at p95 and leaving headroom for transport and render. Responses are streamed or chunked for large windows so the server does not materialise the whole set in memory.

## Observability

title: Publish the bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param} WS topic with snapshot and deltas
body:
## Context
Charts update live over the multiplexed client WebSocket frozen by **E17**. `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 defines the topic precisely: `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}`, options `include_delta` and `history` (≤1 000), snapshot = the last `history` bars, throttle 250 ms, **binary kind 4**, payload `BarsBatch` (§14.3). Two notes in that section are load-bearing: `param` follows the REST convention exactly (dots illegal, colons for compound values), and **"the last bar in any `bars` frame may have `confirm: false`. A client MUST NOT treat it as closed — this is the flicker bug Bybit's own `confirm` flag exists to prevent."**

This Task adds the topic to the already-frozen transport; it changes no framing, no sequencing and no backpressure policy. That is the entire point of E17 shipping first.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Topic registration for `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` with option validation (`include_delta`, `history` ≤1 000) and `param` parsing reusing E12-T01's mapping.
- Snapshot on subscribe: the last `history` bars from the E12-T05 read path, followed by deltas with per-topic sequence numbers per §7.
- Delta publication driven by `BarUpdate`s from E12-T03's emit routing — one source for live and replay.
- `BarsBatch` binary encoding (kind 4) per §14.3, with the JSON fallback path.
- 250 ms coalescing: within a window, repeated updates to the same forming bar collapse to the latest; a `close` update is never coalesced away (a closed bar must always be delivered).
- `confirm: false` on the forming bar, `true` on closed bars, matching the REST semantics exactly.
- Gap-driven resync: a sequence break triggers a fresh snapshot per §7, without inventing bar-specific resync semantics.
- Subscribe-time authorisation (`marketdata:read`) and the spec-cap check from E12-T03.
- Conformance tests generated from `23-ws-protocol.md` §16's matrix for this topic.

## Out of scope
- Transport, framing, heartbeats, backpressure, auth handshake — **E17**.
- `footprint.*` topic — E18.
- Client-side subscription management and rendering — E12-S10/S11.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Snapshot then deltas
  Given a client subscribes to bars.BTCUSDT.time.5 with history=500
  Then a snapshot of the last 500 bars is delivered first
  And subsequent frames are deltas carrying monotonically increasing sequence numbers

Scenario: Forming bar is flagged
  Given the current 5m bar is still forming
  Then it is delivered with confirm=false in every frame
  And when its boundary passes it is delivered exactly once with confirm=true

Scenario: Coalescing never drops a close
  Given 40 trades update the forming bar within one 250 ms window
  Then one coalesced update is sent carrying the latest state
  Given a bar closes and a new one opens within the same window
  Then the close update is still delivered, not collapsed into the open

Scenario: Sequence gap triggers resync
  Given a client detects a non-contiguous sequence number
  When it requests resync per the protocol
  Then a fresh snapshot is delivered and the sequence restarts per section 7
  And no bars are silently missing from the client's series

Scenario: Illegal param is refused at subscribe
  When a client subscribes to bars.BTCUSDT.tick.500.extra
  Then the subscription is refused with the documented protocol error
  And no builder is registered

Scenario: Unauthorised subscribe is refused
  Given a connection whose principal lacks marketdata:read
  When it subscribes to any bars topic
  Then the subscription is refused and no data frames are sent
```

## Technical notes / design
- Dots are illegal in `param` because the topic namespace is dot-delimited; `atr:14` and `10:3` use colons for exactly this reason (§6.1). Validation must reject the dot case explicitly, since a permissive parser here is a namespace-injection bug.
- `bars` and `footprint` for the same `(symbol, bar_type, param)` are **separate subscriptions with independent sequences**, guaranteed consistent (same builder) but not frame-synchronised; the client keys them by bar open time. Nothing here may assume otherwise.
- Publication is fan-out from one `BarBuilderSet` — N subscribers to the same spec share one builder, which is what keeps real-time cost (risk R3) bounded.

## Test plan
- **Contract/conformance**: generated from `23-ws-protocol.md` §16 for this topic; a deliberate breaking change to the payload must fail CI (roadmap exit criterion 7).
- **Unit** ≥85%: option validation, coalescing logic including the never-drop-a-close rule, sequence assignment, binary encode/decode round-trip.
- **Integration**: subscribe/unsubscribe lifecycle, snapshot correctness against the REST endpoint for the same window, resync after an injected gap.
- **Load** (k6, per §5.4): 5 concurrent WS clients × 10 symbols sustained 1 h with bars topics subscribed; fan-out add-on ≤20 ms p95.

## Security notes
Labelled `security`. Threats: **topic-namespace injection** via `param` (closed by the dot/whitelist rule above); **resource exhaustion** via many distinct specs per connection (closed by the E12-T03 spec cap, checked at subscribe, plus a per-connection topic cap from E17); **broken access control** (subscribe-time `marketdata:read`, re-checked on token refresh/revocation per §9, so a revoked session stops receiving frames rather than continuing on an established socket); **amplification** — `history=1000` × many topics on one subscribe frame is a bandwidth amplifier, bounded by E17's ≤10 topics per subscribe frame rule and the history cap.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — transport. One downstream contract: `confirm` must reach the client unmodified, because the data-table alternative (SCR-045) states "forming" versus "closed" in text for each bar, and that text is only as honest as this flag.

## Performance notes
Throttle 250 ms per §6.1; WS→screen p95 ≤250 ms (US-MKT-005) and the R1 exit criterion of tick→screen p95 <100 ms for last-trade applies to the `trades`/`ticker` topics rather than `bars`, but the bars path must not consume the shared budget: coalescing is mandatory, not optional. Binary kind 4 keeps per-bar overhead low at `history=1000` snapshots.

## Observability
`ws_topic_subscriptions{topic="bars"}`, `ws_bars_frames_total`, `ws_bars_coalesced_updates_total`, `ws_bars_resyncs_total`, `ws_bars_subscribe_rejected_total{reason}`, `ws_publish_latency_seconds{topic="bars"}`.

## Definition of Done
Per §4.2: conformance tests generated and green; a deliberate breaking change fails CI; coverage ≥85%; `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1/§14.3 matches the implementation; load test recorded; Security engineer review comment; QA sign-off; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T05** — the read path supplying snapshots.
- **E12-T03** — the emit routing supplying deltas and the spec cap.
- **E17** — the frozen transport, sequencing, backpressure and auth handshake this topic rides on.

## Branch
`feat/e12-bars-ws-topic`

## References
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 topic catalogue and notes, §7 snapshot+delta, §8 throttling/coalescing, §9 revocation, §14.3 `BarsBatch`, §16 conformance matrix
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/bars` param convention
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criteria 3 and 7, §5.4 load gate

title: Drawing tools
body:
## Context
A charting terminal is judged on two things: how fast it draws price, and how naturally the trader can mark it up. E11 delivers the first; this Epic delivers the second. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 scopes **E14 Drawing tools** as: "Trend line, ray, extended line, horizontal/vertical line, rectangle, ellipse, parallel channel, pitchfork, Fibonacci retracement/extension/time-zone, long/short position tool, text/note, measure tool; magnet-to-OHLC; multi-select, drag, resize, clone, lock, delete; per-drawing styling; persistence per symbol and per layout; keyboard-operable creation and nudge for a11y" (47 pts).

The engine contract is already written: `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10 (drawing model, two-phase interaction, magnet mode, command-stack undo/redo, instanced thick-line rendering), §3.9 (hit-testing via a 64 px uniform grid, ≤1 ms for 200 drawings + 50 lines), §14 milestone **M7 Drawings**. The persistence contract is `drawings` in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 (migration `0011_workspace`) exposed as `/api/v1/drawings`, `/api/v1/drawings/batch`, `/api/v1/drawings/{drawingId}` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`. The surface is **SCR-037 Drawing toolbar & drawing properties** with the object tree living in **SCR-036**.

The non-negotiable invariant across every ticket here: **drawings are stored in chart space (time + price), never pixels**. Zoom, log/linear scale flips, DPI changes and bar-type changes must not move an anchor. The second invariant is a11y: `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 requires a manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass "on chart and drawing flows", so every tool must be creatable, selectable, nudgeable and deletable without a mouse.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories covering every Must/Should DRAW story: **US-DRAW-001** … **US-DRAW-009**.
- Screens: **SCR-037** (toolbar + properties popover), object-tree contribution to **SCR-036**.
- Components: **CMP-223** DrawingToolbar, **CMP-224** (object tree row), CMP-002 IconButton, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-010 Slider, CMP-016 Tooltip, CMP-017 Popover, CMP-022 Kbd, CMP-031 ColorSwatch/ThemeChip, CMP-041 Menu, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-049 Table.
- API: `GET/POST /api/v1/drawings`, `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch`, `PUT/DELETE /api/v1/drawings/{drawingId}`.
- Tables: `drawings` (migration `0011_workspace`), soft-delete + 90 d purge per `21-database-schema.md` §retention.
- Engine: drawings layer (layer 3 of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3), object hit-test index, `addDrawing`/`pickAt` worker commands, `drawingChanged` event.

## Out of scope
- Line-cross **alerts** bound to a drawing (`drawings.alert_id`) — **E40 Alerts & notifications**; this Epic only keeps the column nullable and the UI affordance disabled.
- Sending the position tool to a real **order ticket** — **E30**; R1 ships the computation and a disabled/stubbed "send to ticket" behind a feature flag.
- Gann fans, brush/freehand polish and emoji markers beyond the catalogue enum — backlog Could items, not R1 exit criteria.
- Cross-**symbol** synchronisation of drawings (explicitly forbidden by US-DRAW-009 NFR).
- Multi-user/shared drawings — **E-collaboration**, R5.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The advertised tool set exists and persists
  Given a signed-in trader on a BTCUSDT chart
  When they create one drawing of each R1 tool and reload the app
  Then every drawing reappears at the identical time/price anchors on every pane showing BTCUSDT

Scenario: Anchors are chart-space, not pixels
  Given a trendline drawn on a 1m chart in linear scale
  When the trader switches to log scale, changes interval to 1h and changes bar type to range bars
  Then both anchors still resolve to the same timestamps and prices within one tick

Scenario: Interaction stays inside the frame budget
  Given 200 drawings on the chart
  When one drawing is dragged
  Then hit-testing costs ≤1 ms, the price/footprint layers are not re-rendered, and the drag sustains ≥58 fps (benchmark B8)

Scenario: Keyboard-only trader is not excluded
  Given a trader using only the keyboard with a screen reader
  When they enter keyboard drawing mode
  Then they can place both anchors, hear each anchor announced, nudge the result by 1 tick (arrow) and 10 ticks (Shift+arrow), and delete it — with no mouse event at any point

Scenario: Server rejects malformed geometry
  Given a client posts a drawing whose geometry has zero points or a tool outside the enum
  Then the API responds 422 with a field-level error and nothing is persisted
```

## Technical notes / design
Rendering lives in the engine worker as layer 3 (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3) so drags never invalidate the price layer. Lines are instanced quads expanded in the vertex shader (per-instance `p0`, `p1`, `width`, dash pattern index); labels use the shared SDF glyph atlas with a per-pane budget of ≤3 text draw calls. State lives in `DrawingStore` (§3.6) on the main thread, mirrored into the worker as an immutable snapshot per frame. Undo/redo is a 100-entry command stack shared with the toolbar. Persistence is optimistic-local with server reconciliation and a 500 ms debounce that collapses a whole drag into one `/drawings/batch` call.

## Test plan
Unit (engine geometry, magnet snap, fib level maths, R:R maths, command stack), property-based (anchor stability across bar-spec/scale changes, `screenToIndex∘indexToScreen` identity), contract (OpenAPI schemathesis over the four drawing operations), golden-image per tool per theme against SwiftShader (≤0.1 % diff), Playwright E2E for create/drag/undo/redo/lock/hide/keyboard creation, perf benchmark **B8**, axe-core + manual NVDA/VoiceOver pass.

## Security notes
Drawings are user-authored content: `label` and note `text` are sanitised on write and rendered as plain text into the glyph atlas — never as HTML. All endpoints are owner-scoped (`owner_user_id = current user`); a Viewer role may read but not mutate. IDOR on `/drawings/{drawingId}` is an explicit abuse case in the STRIDE model for R1.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The canvas surrogate pattern of `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 applies: every drawing has an off-screen focusable DOM node with a composed accessible name ("Trendline, 2026-10-13 14:00 at 64,120 to 2026-10-13 18:00 at 65,400, locked"). Tool selection, creation, nudging, locking and deletion are all keyboard-reachable; magnet snap targets are announced; colour is never the only carrier of state (locked/hidden also carry an icon and text).

## Performance notes
Budgets from `26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 R5 and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037: 200 drawings + 50 order/position lines hit-tested in ≤1 ms; drag at ≥58 fps with 200 drawings; drawings never decimated; drawing memory ≤8 MB; object tree virtualised for ≥500 objects; batch persistence debounced to one call per 500 ms of dragging.

## Observability
Analytics events per SCR-037: `drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`. Engine metrics: `engine_pick_duration_ms`, `engine_drawing_count`, `engine_drawing_layer_frame_ms`. API metrics: `http_request_duration_seconds{route="/drawings*"}`, `drawings_batch_size`, `drawings_conflict_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level AC verified end-to-end on staging with the Owner present.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend / ≥85% engine + backend packages touched; no open P0/P1 bugs against DRAW scope.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-036/SCR-037 plus one manual NVDA and one VoiceOver pass recorded.
- [ ] Benchmark B8 recorded against budget and wired as a CI regression gate.
- [ ] STRIDE findings for user-authored content triaged and signed off by Security.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10 updated to shipped behaviour.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review; QA epic-level regression pass recorded.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (engine core: scene graph, layers, interaction, worker protocol — `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 `E11 --> E14`), **E05** (design-system v0 tokens/primitives for the toolbar and popover), **E09** (auth/RBAC for owner-scoped persistence). Blocks: **E15** (layouts persist drawings), **E40** (line-cross alerts), **E30** (position tool → ticket).

## Branch
`feat/e14-drawing-tools`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §6 DRAW; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.6; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-223, CMP-224; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings*`; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3, §3.9, §3.10, §14 M7; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2, §11.1; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    K01[E14-K01 Spike: keyboard drawing + surrogate a11y] --> S01
    T01[E14-T01 drawings table + REST API] --> T02[E14-T02 Client DrawingStore, sync, undo/redo]
    T03[E14-T03 Engine drawings layer renderer] --> T04[E14-T04 Hit-test index, handles, multi-select]
    T02 --> S10[E14-S10 Toolbar SCR-037 + properties]
    T04 --> S10
    S10 --> S01[E14-S01 Horizontal/vertical line & ray]
    S01 --> S02[E14-S02 Trendline, ray, extended + magnet]
    S02 --> S03[E14-S03 Rectangle, ellipse, channel, triangle]
    S02 --> S04[E14-S04 Fibonacci retracement/extension/time-zone]
    S02 --> S05[E14-S05 Anchored VWAP + bands]
    S01 --> S06[E14-S06 Text, note, arrow annotations]
    S01 --> S08[E14-S08 Object tree, lock/hide, undo/redo UI]
    S03 --> S07[E14-S07 Long/short position tool]
    S08 --> S09[E14-S09 Templates & cross-pane sync]
```

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

- `E14-D07` (web) — Hi-fi design: drawings branch of the object tree & cross-chart sync (SCR-036); blocked by: `E14-D02`
- `E14-D08` (web) — Design-system contribution: drawing primitives, tokens & CMP-191/CMP-223 entries; blocked by: `E14-D03`, `E14-D04`

title: Client DrawingStore: optimistic sync, debounced batch writes and undo/redo stack
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 names `DrawingStore` as a first-class store, and §3.10 sets its behaviour: "optimistic local writes with server reconciliation" and "undo/redo is a command stack of 100 entries, shared with the drawing toolbar". US-DRAW-008 raises the floor further — "undo stack ≥50 operations per symbol, session-scoped" — and US-DRAW-001 requires that a deletion is "removed from all panes showing that symbol and the action is undoable". This Task is the single source of truth between the REST API (E14-T01) and the engine layer (E14-T03), so no tool story has to re-solve sync, history or fan-out to panes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web/src/features/drawings/store/` holding drawings keyed by `(symbol)` with derived per-pane views; a pane subscribes by symbol and receives every drawing for that symbol (the mechanism behind US-DRAW-001's "every BTCUSDT chart" and US-DRAW-009's cross-pane sync).
- Command model: every mutation is a reversible command (`create`, `update-geometry`, `update-style`, `delete`, `lock`, `hide`, `group-move`, `clone`) carrying before/after state; a 100-entry stack per symbol, session-scoped, with `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` bindings registered through the app hotkey service.
- Optimistic application: local state and the engine snapshot update on the same frame as the interaction; the network write follows.
- Debounced persistence: mutations coalesce for 500 ms (and flush immediately on pointer-up, tool change, pane close or `beforeunload`) into one `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch`.
- Reconciliation: server ids replace optimistic ids; a 409 conflict triggers a re-read of the symbol's drawings and a non-destructive merge (server wins for the conflicting object, local history stays intact); an offline/5xx write is retried with jittered backoff and surfaced as a "changes not saved" chip.
- Initial load on chart mount via `GET /api/v1/drawings?symbol=`, with in-memory caching so a second pane on the same symbol issues no second request.
- Engine bridge: publishes an immutable drawing snapshot to the worker per frame and consumes `drawingChanged` / selection events back.

## Out of scope
- Server-side schema and endpoints (**E14-T01**).
- Toolbar and properties UI (**E14-S10**); the object-tree UI (**E14-S08**).
- Per-layout scoping rules and sync toggles (**E14-S09** consumes this store's `layout_id` support).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A drag persists as exactly one request
  Given a trendline is dragged continuously for 3 seconds and released
  When network traffic is inspected
  Then at most one /drawings/batch request per 500 ms of dragging is sent, and a final flush occurs on release

Scenario: Undo restores every property
  Given a styled, labelled rectangle is deleted
  When Ctrl+Z is pressed
  Then it is restored with identical geometry, style, label, lock and visibility, and Ctrl+Shift+Z deletes it again

Scenario: Optimistic write survives a failed save
  Given the API returns 500 for a batch
  Then the drawing remains visible locally, a "changes not saved" chip appears, the write is retried with backoff, and the chip clears on success

Scenario: Conflict does not destroy local history
  Given the server returns 409 because the drawing changed elsewhere
  Then the store re-reads the symbol, adopts the server version of that object, keeps the undo stack usable, and informs the user once

Scenario: Two panes on one symbol stay identical
  Given two panes show BTCUSDT at 1m and 1h
  When a horizontal line is created in the 1m pane
  Then it appears in the 1h pane in the same frame and only one network request is made

Scenario: Stack is bounded and scoped
  Given 150 mutations are performed on BTCUSDT
  Then the undo stack holds the most recent 100 and switching to ETHUSDT presents that symbol's own independent stack
```

## Technical notes / design
State is immutable (structural sharing) so the per-frame worker snapshot is a reference comparison rather than a deep copy — this is what keeps the engine bridge inside the drag frame budget. Optimistic ids are client-generated UUIDv7 so ordering is stable and the server can accept them directly, making reconciliation an id-confirmation rather than an id-swap in the common case. The debounce holds a *coalescing map* keyed by drawing id (last write wins per object), not a queue of every intermediate frame, so a 3-second drag produces one update op, not 180. Prices are carried as strings/`Decimal` end to end; no float arithmetic touches an anchor.

## Test plan
Unit: command invert/apply, stack bounds and scoping, coalescing map, debounce/flush triggers, reconciliation paths (200/409/500/offline). Integration: store + mock server with fake timers proving request counts. E2E: Playwright two-pane sync, undo/redo after reload, offline save chip. Contract: store's request bodies validated against `DrawingInput`.

## Security notes
The store must not persist drawing content to `localStorage` in plaintext beyond the session cache policy agreed for chart state; note text is user content and is escaped at every render boundary. Retries must not replay a delete after a successful re-create (idempotency by op id) — a data-integrity rather than confidentiality concern.

## Accessibility notes
Undo/redo must announce their effect in a polite live region ("Trendline restored", "Delete redone") since the visual change occurs on a canvas that screen readers cannot observe. Hotkeys are registered through the shared hotkey service so they appear in the keyboard-shortcuts help (SCR settings) and can be remapped.

## Performance notes
Store update + worker snapshot publish ≤1 ms on the main thread per interaction frame; at most one network request per 500 ms of dragging; memory bounded by 500 drawings/symbol × 100 undo entries with before/after snapshots held by structural sharing rather than copies.

## Observability
Analytics `drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted` (SCR-037). Client metrics: `drawings_batch_requests_total`, `drawings_batch_retry_total`, `drawings_conflict_total`, `drawings_undo_total`, `drawings_store_apply_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the drawings feature package.
- [ ] Request-count assertions in CI (no chatty-drag regression).
- [ ] Hotkeys registered in the shared service and documented in the shortcuts screen.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, merge queue, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-T01** (endpoints and schema), **E14-T03** (engine layer and snapshot protocol). Blocks **E14-S10** and every tool story.

## Branch
`feat/e14-drawing-store`

## References
`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 stores, §3.10 persistence/undo; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings/batch`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-001, US-DRAW-008, US-DRAW-009; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037.


## Agent execution brief

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant sections)

**Repo paths to create/modify**

- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- apps/web route contracts, Zustand/Jotai store shapes consumed by other routes; named identifiers in this ticket: SCR-037
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**

- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**

title: Layouts & workspaces
body:
## Context
E11 gives us one fast chart; E12/E13/E14 give it bars, indicators and drawings. None of that becomes a *terminal* until a trader can arrange several of those surfaces at once, link them, and have the arrangement survive a restart. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 scopes **E15 Layouts & workspaces** as: "Grid layouts (1, 2, 3, 4, 6 charts) with drag-to-resize; symbol/timeframe/crosshair sync groups by colour; named workspace save/load/duplicate/delete; per-workspace theme and density; last-session restore; workspace export/import JSON; server-persisted per user" (34 pts, S08–S09, module **M10**).

Two R1 exit criteria land squarely on this Epic. §5.3 criterion 5: "Chart state (symbol, timeframe, indicators, drawings, layout) survives reload, app restart, and Electron relaunch with zero loss." §5.3 criterion 2: the 30 fps floor must hold "under the worst-case scenario (6-chart layout, all indicators, all drawings)" — which only exists because this Epic lets the trader build that layout in the first place. US-LAY-001's NFR is stricter still: ≥55 fps with four active order-flow panes on the reference machine.

The contracts are already written and normative. Persistence: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, migration `0011_workspace`). Transport: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`, `/chart-templates`, `/layout-presets`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/export` — all `x-rbac: {permissions: [workspaces:*], scope: self}`. Surface: **SCR-020** … **SCR-029** (the full workspace/dock band, 10 of 10 allocated), plus **SCR-049**, **SCR-011**, **SCR-150**, **SCR-153**. Engine hooks: `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2 pane synchronisation ("charts in a layout may share a `SyncGroup` for time range, crosshair position and/or price level, propagated once per frame after input integration, never re-entrantly"), the `sync` event (§6, ≤1/frame), `syncGroup` on `ChartOptions`, requirement **R8** ("4 synchronised chart instances on one page within budget") and benchmark **B6**.

The invariant that governs every ticket here: **a layout mutation must never remount a WebGL context**. SCR-020's performance line states it ("layout changes never remount the WebGL context"), and it is the difference between a 300 ms preset switch and a two-second white flash with a cold data window.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories covering every Must/Should LAY story: **US-LAY-001** (grids), **US-LAY-002** (saved workspaces), **US-LAY-003** (cross-pane sync), **US-LAY-004** (scale linking), **US-LAY-005** (docking/visibility/float), **US-LAY-006** (hotkeys & pane focus), **US-LAY-007** (export/import), **US-LAY-008** (responsive & reduced-capability).
- Screens: **SCR-020** Workspace page, **SCR-021** Dock/panel system, **SCR-022** Layout preset gallery, **SCR-023** Multi-chart sync configuration, **SCR-024** Panel picker, **SCR-025** Workspace settings modal, **SCR-026** Workspace import, **SCR-027** Floating panel window (Electron), **SCR-028** Panel context menu, **SCR-029** Unsaved-changes / layout-conflict dialog, **SCR-049** Multi-chart grid panel, plus the workspace switcher in **SCR-011**, restore on **SCR-150** and the reduced-capability variant of **SCR-153**.
- Components: **CMP-080** DockPanel, **CMP-081** DockGrid/Layout Manager, **CMP-082** PanelHeader, **CMP-083** SplitPane, **CMP-196** MultiChartLinker, **CMP-214** DockDropZone, **CMP-215** FloatingWindowFrame, **CMP-216** PanelMenu, **CMP-217** LayoutPresetMenu, **CMP-218** SyncMenu, **CMP-073** WorkspaceSwitcher, **CMP-213** FuzzyList, **CMP-067** FileDrop, **CMP-092** DegradedModeBanner, **CMP-227** EstimatedBadge.
- API: `GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, `GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`, `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/export`, `GET /api/v1/layout-presets`, `GET /api/v1/chart-templates`.
- Tables: `workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes` (migration `0011_workspace`); `ix_lp_symbol` is the index E16's recorder queries to decide which symbols count as "chart open".
- Packages: `packages/dock` (framework-light layout tree + drop resolution) and the app-level `SyncBus`; both unit-testable without a DOM canvas.

## Out of scope
- The panels' own content — chart (E11/E12), indicators (E13), drawings (E14), DOM/footprint/tape (E18–E23), order ticket and positions grid (E30, E31). This Epic mounts them through a registry; it does not implement them. Panel kinds whose implementing Epic has not shipped appear in SCR-024 disabled with a reason.
- **Shared / multi-user workspaces and collaboration** — R5.
- Per-workspace *account* binding and the DEMO/LIVE chrome variants beyond rendering whatever badge E10's shell provides — **E27/E44**.
- Chart-template CRUD UI (`chart_templates`) beyond referencing an existing template id from a pane — **E13**.
- Server-pushed cross-device layout conflict events over WS — R1 detects conflicts via `If-Match`/412 only; live conflict push is a later refinement.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A four-pane workspace survives a full restart
  Given a trader has built a 2x2 workspace with distinct symbols, intervals, indicators and drawings and saved it as "EU session"
  When they quit the Electron app and relaunch it
  Then the workspace restores with the same panes, sizes, symbols, intervals, indicators, drawings, sync groups and scroll position
  And it reaches interactive within 3 s from warm cache

Scenario: Layout changes never churn the GL context
  Given a workspace with four chart panes is open
  When a preset is applied, a divider is dragged and a panel is moved by keyboard
  Then no WebGL context is created or lost, the rebuild completes in <= 300 ms, and no pane refetches history it already holds

Scenario: Sync applies only inside its group
  Given panes 1 and 2 are in sync group A and pane 3 is in group B
  When the crosshair moves in pane 1 and the symbol is changed in pane 1 with symbol sync on and interval sync off
  Then pane 2 follows both at the same timestamp within one frame, pane 3 is untouched, and pane 2 keeps its own interval

Scenario: A delisted symbol does not take the workspace down
  Given a saved workspace references a symbol that has since been delisted
  When the workspace is restored
  Then that pane shows an explicit error state naming the symbol, every other pane loads normally, and the workspace remains savable

Scenario: Export carries no secrets
  Given any workspace, including one whose panes were bound to accounts
  When it is exported and the JSON is inspected
  Then it contains no API keys, no tokens, no account ids and no user ids, and importing it as a different user drops account-scoped elements with a visible report

Scenario: Every layout operation is reachable without a pointer
  Given a keyboard-only trader with a screen reader
  When they add, move, split, float, resize, focus and close panels using only the keyboard
  Then each operation has an equivalent in the panel menu, focus is never lost, and each result is announced once in a live region
```

## Technical notes / design
The layout is a **tree**, not a grid of absolute rectangles: `row`/`column`/`tabset`/`leaf` nodes with fractional sizes, serialised into `layouts.grid_spec` when `grid_preset = 'custom'` and reduced to a named preset (`1x1`, `2x1`, `1x2`, `2x2`, `1+3`, `3x3`) when it matches one — the CHECK constraint in §3.8.1 enumerates exactly those. Panes are rows in `layout_panes` keyed by `slot_index` (0..15, matching SCR-020's ">16 panels" warning), each carrying `pane_kind`, `symbol`, `interval_code`, `chart_template_id`, `indicator_preset_ids` and a free-form `pane_config`.

Reconciliation is keyed by stable pane id so a move is a *reparent*, not an unmount — this is what protects the GL context. Writes are debounced 2 s and sent as a full `PUT` with `If-Match` (the OpenAPI description says exactly this); a 412 raises SCR-029's conflict variant rather than clobbering.

Sync is a client-side bus, deliberately not a server round-trip (SCR-023: "runtime over a local sync bus"). It dispatches straight into engine instances, never through React state, to hold the ≤4 ms-across-6-panes budget.

Capability degradation (US-LAY-008) is measured, never sniffed: the frame-time probe from E11's benchmark harness decides, and the user is told the measured cost.

## Test plan
Unit: layout-tree algebra (split/move/tabify/close/normalise), preset↔tree round-trip, sync-bus fan-out, export/import schema validation. Contract: schemathesis over every `/workspaces*` operation including 412 and 422 paths. Integration: Postgres round-trip of workspace→layouts→panes with cascade delete. E2E (Playwright web + Electron): build 2x2, save, reload, restore; drag-resize; keyboard move; preset hotkeys; float/redock (Electron); export→import across users; delisted-symbol restore. Perf: B6 (4 synchronised charts) and the 6-pane worst case from §5.3 criterion 2; restore-to-interactive ≤3 s; preset apply ≤300 ms. A11y: axe-core on SCR-020..029 plus a manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass over the keyboard docking flow.

## Security notes
Everything here is `scope: self`: a user may only read and write their own workspaces, and cross-user access returns 404 rather than 403 so existence is not disclosed. The export file is the main new attack surface in both directions — outbound it must never embed keys, tokens, account ids or user ids (US-LAY-007 NFR); inbound it is untrusted JSON that must be schema-validated, size-capped and parsed in a worker before a single node is applied. Panel titles, workspace names and imported labels are user content: length-capped, control-characters stripped, never rendered as HTML. Viewer keeps `workspaces:write` (`21-database-schema.md` §RBAC note) precisely because arranging one's own panes cannot emit an order.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Each panel is a `role="region"` with an accessible name ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1m"); `F6`/`Ctrl+Tab` cycles regions with a visible focus indicator; every drag-and-drop dock operation has a mandatory keyboard equivalent via CMP-216's "Move panel" directional chooser (CMP-214's catalogue entry makes this non-negotiable). Splitters are `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow` and arrow-key resize. Sync group membership is conveyed by letter badge and name, never by colour alone. Layout changes announce once, politely.

## Performance notes
Budgets: ≥55 fps with four active order-flow panes (US-LAY-001 NFR); ≥30 fps floor in the 6-pane worst case (roadmap §5.3.2); restore to interactive ≤3 s for a 4-pane workspace from warm cache (US-LAY-002 NFR); sync propagation ≤1 frame and ≤4 ms across 6 panes (SCR-023); preset apply ≤300 ms and panel mount ≤150 ms (SCR-022/SCR-024); 2 MB import validates in ≤500 ms off the main thread (SCR-026). Hidden tabs unsubscribe after 30 s; panels mount lazily on first visibility.

## Observability
Analytics events per the screen catalogue: `workspace.saved`, `workspace.updated`, `workspace.deleted`, `workspace.exported`, `layout.preset_applied`, `layout.panel_added|removed|moved|floated|maximised`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.imported`, `layout.import_rejected{reason}`, `layout.conflict_detected`, `layout.conflict_resolved{choice}`, `sync.group_changed`, `degraded.entered{cause,sheddedFeatures}`. Metrics: `workspace_restore_seconds` histogram, `layout_apply_duration_ms`, `layout_conflict_total`, `panes_per_layout` histogram, `http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/workspaces*"}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R1 exit criterion 5 demonstrated end-to-end (reload, app restart, Electron relaunch, zero loss) and recorded.
- [ ] Worst-case 6-pane layout measured against the 30 fps floor and the 4-pane order-flow layout against 55 fps; numbers attached.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on `packages/dock` and the workspace feature, ≥85% on the workspace API router.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-020..029 plus a signed-off manual screen-reader pass of the keyboard docking flow.
- [ ] Security sign-off on export/import (no secrets outbound, validated untrusted input inbound) and the IDOR matrix.
- [ ] `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1, `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `14-screens-catalogue.md` reflect shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA epic-level regression pass recorded; zero open P0/P1; demoed to the Owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (chart engine instances, sync group plumbing, frame-time probe), **E13** (indicator presets referenced by `layout_panes.indicator_preset_ids`), **E10** (app shell, Electron window management, hotkey layer), **E09** (users, sessions, `workspaces:*` permissions). Blocks **E16** (auto-record via `ix_lp_symbol`), and every R2 panel that needs somewhere to be docked.

```mermaid
graph TD
  K01[E15-K01 Spike: pane budget & capability profile]
  T01[E15-T01 workspaces/layouts/panes API + migration]
  T02[E15-T02 packages/dock layout tree + DockGrid]
  T03[E15-T03 SyncBus + engine sync integration]
```
