title: Grid presets, preset gallery and layout hotkeys (SCR-022)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-001** ("Preset grid: when I choose 2×2, four panes are created, each independently bindable to a symbol and interval"; "Custom split: dragging a divider resizes with live preview and sizes persist"; "Pane limit: adding another pane beyond the performance budget warns with the measured frame cost and requires confirmation") and **US-LAY-006** ("Preset hotkey: Ctrl+1 loads layout preset 1 with its saved bindings"; "Pane focus: Ctrl+Tab advances focus with a visible indicator and screen-reader announcement"; "Conflict: a preset hotkey colliding with a trading hotkey is flagged in settings and must be resolved before saving").

The surfaces are **SCR-022** Layout preset gallery and the preset/focus behaviour on **SCR-020**. The hotkey slots are already modelled: `layouts.hotkey_slot` (1..9, unique per workspace) in `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1, and `layout.preset_1..9` → `Ctrl+1`–`Ctrl+9` in the default hotkey table.

This is the first Story to consume `packages/dock`, so it is also the first place the "reuse existing panel instances where the type matches, avoiding GL context churn" rule (SCR-022) is visible to a user.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Built-in grid presets wired to `presetToTree`: 1×1, 2×1, 1×2, 2×2, 1+3, 3×1, 3×3 — exactly the `lay_preset` CHECK enum plus the named compositions SCR-022 lists (Scalping = chart+DOM+ticket+tape, Order-flow = chart+footprint+CVD+profile, Swing = 3 timeframes, Analyst = read-only chart+journal+replay, Fan-out review). Compositions whose panel kinds are not yet implemented render their available subset and mark the rest disabled with a reason, per SCR-024's convention.
- **SCR-022** gallery modal (**CMP-217** LayoutPresetMenu, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-050 Card, CMP-001 Button): static SVG thumbnails (no live panels), a "Keep current symbols" checkbox, an Apply action, and the warning "Applying a preset replaces the current layout. Settings of surviving panels are kept."
- Preset application reuses matching pane instances by kind so no GL context is recreated; surviving panes keep symbol, interval, indicators and drawings when "Keep current symbols" is on.
- Saved custom presets: "Save current as preset" writes a layout with a `hotkey_slot`; rename and delete; the empty user-preset state.
- Hotkeys `Ctrl+1`–`Ctrl+9` bound through E10's global hotkey layer to `layouts.hotkey_slot`, remappable per US-LAY-006's NFR, with the collision check against trading hotkeys surfaced in settings and blocking save.
- Pane focus cycling: `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` and `F6` region cycling, with a visible focus ring and one polite announcement naming the pane ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1 minute, pane 2 of 4").
- Drag-to-resize dividers with live preview, committing exactly one layout mutation on release (SCR-021 performance line).
- Pane-limit guard: adding a pane beyond E15-K01's `recommendedMaxPanes` shows the measured frame cost and requires explicit confirmation; >16 panes is refused outright by `lp_slot`.

## Out of scope
- Persisting the applied layout to the server — **E15-S03** (this Story mutates client state and emits the change).
- Docking by drag, floating windows, the panel picker — **E15-S02**.
- Sync configuration — **E15-S04**.
- Chart-template selection inside a preset — **E13**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Applying 2x2 creates four independently bindable panes
  Given a 1x1 workspace showing BTCUSDT 1m
  When the trader applies the 2x2 preset
  Then four panes exist, each with its own symbol and interval control, and changing pane 3's interval leaves panes 1, 2 and 4 unchanged

Scenario: Surviving panes keep their state and their GL context
  Given a 2x2 layout of four chart panes with indicators and drawings
  When the 1+3 preset is applied with "Keep current symbols" checked
  Then all four panes keep their symbol, interval, indicators and drawings
  And zero WebGL contexts are created or lost, and the rebuild completes within 300 ms

Scenario: A preset hotkey loads its layout
  Given a custom preset is saved to slot 1
  When the trader presses Ctrl+1 from anywhere in the workspace
  Then that layout loads with its saved pane bindings and the change is announced once

Scenario: Hotkey collision blocks saving
  Given Ctrl+2 is already bound to a trading action
  When the trader assigns Ctrl+2 to a layout preset
  Then the conflict is shown in settings naming both actions, and the assignment cannot be saved until it is resolved

Scenario: Exceeding the measured pane budget requires confirmation
  Given the capability probe reported recommendedMaxPanes = 6 at 24 ms per frame
  When the trader adds a seventh pane
  Then a confirmation states the measured frame cost and what it means, and the pane is added only on explicit confirmation

Scenario: Keyboard-only pane focus
  Given a 2x2 layout and a keyboard-only trader
  When they press Ctrl+Tab three times
  Then focus visits each pane in visual reading order with a visible focus indicator, and each pane is announced by name and position

Scenario: Divider drag previews then commits once
  When a divider is dragged and released
  Then a live preview follows the pointer, exactly one layout mutation is committed on release, and the new sizes are reflected in the layout tree
```

## Technical notes / design
Presets are data, not code: a preset is `{ id, label, tree, paneKinds[], thumbnail }`, so adding one in R2 (an order-flow composition) is a data change. `matchPreset` from `packages/dock` keeps the gallery's active-preset highlight honest after manual resizing — a dragged divider silently turns `2x2` into `custom`, and the gallery must show that rather than lie.

Instance reuse is a matching problem: pair old leaves to new slots by `kind` first, then by original position, so a 2×2→1+3 transition keeps the visually corresponding panes. Unmatched old panes are closed; unmatched new slots mount fresh.

The pane-limit warning must quote a **measured** number (E15-K01), never a constant — US-LAY-001 says "states the measured frame cost", and a hard-coded 6 would be wrong on both the reference machine and a laptop.

Hotkeys route through E10's layer so remapping and conflict detection are one implementation across the app, not a layout-local special case.

## Test plan
Unit: preset data→tree mapping, instance-matching algorithm, `matchPreset` after manual resize, hotkey slot uniqueness. Component: gallery rendering, "keep symbols" behaviour, disabled panel kinds with reasons, empty custom-preset state. Integration: preset apply with live engines asserting zero GL churn and ≤300 ms. E2E (Playwright + Electron): Ctrl+1..9 preset switching, Ctrl+Tab focus cycle, divider drag, pane-limit confirmation. A11y: axe on SCR-022; screen-reader script verifying preset names describe the arrangement in words ("Two by two, four panes", CMP-217) and that thumbnails carry enumerating alt text; focus-ring visibility at AA contrast. Perf: preset apply ≤300 ms at 4 and 6 panes.

## Security notes
Low surface. Custom preset names are user content: 1..40 chars, control characters stripped, rendered as text. Hotkey bindings are per-user preference and cannot invoke a trading action indirectly — the collision check exists so a layout binding never shadows an order-entry binding, which is a safety property as much as a usability one. No new endpoints beyond `GET /api/v1/layout-presets` (read-only, built-in catalogue).

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The gallery is a listbox of cards; each preset's accessible name describes the arrangement in words, not by thumbnail alone, and thumbnails carry alt text enumerating their panels (CMP-217, SCR-022). Applying a preset announces the result once. `Ctrl+Tab`/`F6` pane cycling has a visible focus indicator and a name+position announcement (US-LAY-006). Dividers are keyboard-resizable via CMP-083's `role="separator"`. Applying a preset that would discard unsaved panes routes through SCR-029 rather than silently destroying work. Hotkey hints use CMP-022 Kbd so they are readable, not icon-only.

## Performance notes
Preset apply ≤300 ms rebuilding the dock tree and reusing panel instances (SCR-022); thumbnails are static SVG so the gallery costs nothing to open; layout transition ≤200 ms (CMP-081); divider drag uses CSS transforms with one mutation on release (SCR-021). Pane-limit thresholds come from E15-K01's measured curve.

## Observability
`layout.preset_previewed`, `layout.preset_applied {presetId, paneCount, reusedPanes}`, `layout.preset_saved_as`, `layout.preset_deleted`, `layout.panel_added {type, placement}`, `layout.pane_limit_warning_shown {measuredFrameMs, paneCount}`, `layout.pane_limit_confirmed`. Client metric `layout_apply_duration_ms` reported with pane count.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the preset and hotkey modules.
- [ ] SCR-022 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior (design-ahead rule) or a recorded waiver; its sign-off checklist items verified in the built UI.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-022; manual screen-reader pass of preset apply and pane focus cycling.
- [ ] Zero-GL-churn assertion passing for preset application; ≤300 ms recorded.
- [ ] Hotkey collision path demonstrated in settings.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T02** (tree, presets, instance reuse), **E15-K01** (measured pane budget), **E05** (design system: Dialog, Card, Button, Kbd tokens). Relies on **E10**'s hotkey layer.

## Branch
`feat/e15-preset-gallery`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-006; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-217, CMP-081, CMP-083, CMP-022, CMP-043, CMP-050; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-006 rows; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`lay_preset`, `hotkey_slot`, `ux_lay_slot`), §hotkey defaults `layout.preset_1..9`; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/layout-presets`.


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant sections)
4. docs/plan/20-architecture.md (apps/web module map)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- apps/web/src/routes/** (per Scope screen), apps/web/src/lib/state/**, packages/ui/** (components), apps/web/e2e/**
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- apps/web route contracts, Zustand/Jotai store shapes consumed by other routes; named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-001, CMP-022, CMP-043, CMP-050, CMP-081, CMP-083, CMP-217, SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-024, SCR-029
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build · pnpm e2e · pnpm test:a11y
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e15-preset-gallery`
- PR title: `E15-S01: Grid presets, preset gallery and layout hotkeys (SCR-022)`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E15-S01)
- Required reviewers: `apps/web` (@CandleViewer/frontend), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/feature, area/charting-ui, priority/p1, design, handoff, qa, a11y, perf

**Done means**
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the preset and hotkey modules.
- [ ] SCR-022 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior (design-ahead rule) or a recorded waiver; its sign-off checklist items verified in the built UI.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-022; manual screen-reader pass of preset apply and pane focus cycling.
- [ ] Zero-GL-churn assertion passing for preset application; ≤300 ms recorded.
- [ ] Hotkey collision path demonstrated in settings.

**Do NOT**
- Do not widen a performance budget or edit a benchmark baseline to make a regression pass (AGENTS.md §8).
- Do not ship a hover-only or drag-only interaction; every affordance needs a keyboard path (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E15-S01 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.
- Move the issue's Status to `Blocked` in the project board; do not leave it silently `In Progress`.
- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

title: workspaces/layouts/layout_panes migration and /workspaces REST API
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 5 requires chart state to survive "reload, app restart, and Electron relaunch with zero loss". That guarantee is only as good as the server-side store behind it, because local storage does not survive a machine change and the roadmap explicitly specifies workspaces as "server-persisted per user". This Task implements that store and its contract, interface-first, so the client work (E15-T02, E15-S03) codes against a merged API rather than a promise.

Both halves are already specified. The schema is `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 — `workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, shipped in migration `0011_workspace`. The contract is drafted in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` under the `workspaces` tag, every operation carrying `x-rbac: { permissions: [workspaces:read|write], scope: self }`.

One detail carries weight far outside this Epic: `ix_lp_symbol ON layout_panes (symbol) WHERE symbol IS NOT NULL` is, per §3.8.1, "what the recorder queries to decide which symbols are 'chart open' for auto-recording". E16 depends on this index existing and being accurate.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration `0011_workspace` (the workspaces portion) creating exactly per §3.8.1:
  - `workspaces` — `id`, `user_id` FK→`users` ON DELETE CASCADE, `name`, `is_default`, `icon_token`, `sort_order`, timestamps, `deleted_at`; unique indexes `ux_ws_name` (per user, lower(name), alive rows) and `ux_ws_default` (one default per user, alive rows).
  - `layouts` — `id`, `workspace_id` FK ON DELETE CASCADE, `name`, `grid_preset`, `grid_spec` jsonb, `crosshair_sync`, `level_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `hotkey_slot`, `is_default`, timestamps, `deleted_at`; constraints `lay_preset` and `lay_slot`; unique indexes `ux_lay_name`, `ux_lay_slot`.
  - `layout_panes` — `id`, `layout_id` FK ON DELETE CASCADE, `slot_index`, `pane_kind`, `symbol`, `interval_code`, `chart_template_id` FK→`chart_templates` ON DELETE SET NULL, `indicator_preset_ids` uuid[], `pane_config` jsonb, `scale_mode`, timestamps; constraints `lp_kind`, `lp_slot`, `lp_scale`; `UNIQUE (layout_id, slot_index)`; indexes `ix_lp_layout`, `ix_lp_symbol`.
- Endpoints per `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces`; `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`; `GET/POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`; `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`; `GET /api/v1/layout-presets` (static built-in catalogue, no auth-scoped rows).
- `PUT` on workspace and layout honours `If-Match` and returns **412** on a stale token — the OpenAPI description states the reason: "prevents a stale tab from clobbering a newer arrangement made in another window".
- `POST/PUT /layouts` replaces the pane set transactionally: panes are validated as a whole (slot uniqueness, `pane_kind` enum, `slot_index` 0..15, `scale_mode` enum, `grid_spec` shape when `grid_preset='custom'`) and written in one transaction; partial application is impossible.
- `GET /workspaces/{id}` returns `WorkspaceDetail` — workspace metadata plus its layouts in one round-trip, so restore is a single request per workspace.
- `is_default` is enforced by the partial unique index, and setting a new default clears the old one inside the same transaction.
- Soft delete via `deleted_at` on `workspaces`/`layouts`; deleting the **last** alive workspace of a user is refused with 409 (SCR-025: "You need at least one workspace.").
- Owner scoping on every read and write; cross-user ids return **404**.
- Contract tests generated from the OpenAPI document; drift fails CI.

## Out of scope
- `chart_templates`, `drawings`, `indicator_presets`, `hotkey_profiles` tables — same migration file, different Epics (E13/E14/E10); this Task only takes the FK reference to `chart_templates`.
- `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/export` and import — **E15-S07** (it needs the redaction rules, not just the rows).
- Any client code or debounce logic — **E15-T02**, **E15-S03**.
- WS push of layout changes to other sessions — out of R1 scope; conflicts are detected by `If-Match` only.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A workspace with layouts and panes round-trips exactly
  Given user A creates a workspace and a 2x2 layout with four panes of differing kinds, symbols and intervals
  When GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id} is called as user A
  Then the response contains the workspace and the layout with all four panes, each with identical slot_index, pane_kind, symbol, interval_code, indicator_preset_ids and pane_config

Scenario: A stale client cannot clobber a newer arrangement
  Given two sessions loaded the same layout and session B saved a change
  When session A sends PUT with its original If-Match token
  Then the API responds 412, the stored layout is unchanged, and session A can re-read the current version

Scenario: Cross-user access is denied without disclosing existence
  Given user B knows user A's workspaceId
  When user B calls GET, PUT or DELETE on it
  Then the API responds 404 and nothing is mutated

Scenario: An invalid pane set is rejected whole
  When a layout is PUT with two panes claiming slot_index 3, or a pane_kind outside the lp_kind enum, or slot_index 16
  Then the API responds 422 naming the offending pane, and the previously stored pane set is intact

Scenario: The last workspace cannot be deleted
  Given a user has exactly one alive workspace
  When they DELETE it
  Then the API responds 409 with an explanatory code and the workspace remains

Scenario: Deleting a workspace cascades to layouts and panes
  Given a workspace with two layouts of four panes each
  When it is deleted and the user has another workspace
  Then the workspace is soft-deleted, its layouts are no longer returned, and a subsequent hard purge removes the layout_panes rows

Scenario: The recorder can find chart-open symbols
  Given three layouts across two users contain panes bound to BTCUSDT
  When the recorder queries layout_panes by symbol
  Then the query uses ix_lp_symbol and returns those panes without a sequential scan
```

## Technical notes / design
The layout tree lives in `grid_spec` as jsonb only when `grid_preset = 'custom'`; named presets store their name and an empty spec, keeping the common case small and queryable. Validation of `grid_spec` is a JSON Schema check at the API boundary, not a database constraint — the CHECK constraints in §3.8.1 cover only the enums.

`If-Match` tokens are derived from `updated_at` (weak ETag over the layout aggregate including its panes, so a pane-only change bumps the token). A `PUT` that changes nothing still returns 200 with an unchanged token rather than a spurious write, so the client's 2 s debounce can be naive.

Pane writes are full replacement, not diff: the client always knows the whole tree, and replacement makes slot uniqueness trivially enforceable inside one transaction. Row churn is irrelevant here — §sizing caps all config tables at <100 MB, "bounded by human editing rate".

## Test plan
Unit: pane-set validators, ETag derivation, default-workspace transition, last-workspace guard. Contract: schemathesis across every operation including 412, 409, 422 and 404 paths. Integration: Postgres-backed round-trip; cascade delete; concurrent `PUT` race resolving to exactly one winner and one 412; `EXPLAIN` assertion that the recorder's symbol query uses `ix_lp_symbol`. Security: IDOR matrix (owner/other/viewer × read/write/delete over workspace, layout and nested pane ids). Migration: apply and roll back on a seeded database.

## Security notes
STRIDE: the dominant threats are Tampering and Information disclosure via IDOR on `workspaceId`/`layoutId`, both covered by the explicit test matrix and the 404-not-403 rule. Stored user content — `name`, `icon_token`, `pane_config` — is length-capped (name 1..40 per SCR-020's validation rule), control characters stripped, and `pane_config` size-capped and schema-validated so a pane cannot become an arbitrary blob store. `icon_token` is validated against the design-system token list, never a URL. No secrets, no PII, no financial data: classification is user preference data. RBAC per E09 — Viewer holds `workspaces:write` deliberately (`21-database-schema.md` §RBAC), scoped to self only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The API returns `name`, `pane_kind` and `symbol` so the client can compose accessible region names ("Chart, BTCUSDT 1m") without extra round-trips.

## Performance notes
`GET /workspaces/{id}` with 4 layouts × 8 panes < 10 ms p99. `PUT` of a 16-pane layout < 25 ms p99. The recorder's symbol query < 5 ms p99 via `ix_lp_symbol`. Restore is one request per workspace by design — the 3 s restore-to-interactive NFR cannot afford an N+1 per pane.

## Observability
`http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/workspaces*"}`, `layout_conflict_total` (412 count), `panes_per_layout` histogram on write, `workspaces_total` gauge per user bucket. Structured logs carry `user_id`, `workspace_id`, `layout_id`, `pane_count` — never `pane_config` contents.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the workspace router and repository.
- [ ] Migration applies and rolls back cleanly on a seeded database; `0011_workspace` documented in §migrations.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` merged and contract tests green; deliberate drift fails CI.
- [ ] IDOR matrix executed; Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] `EXPLAIN` evidence attached for the recorder's `ix_lp_symbol` query, linked from E16.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, merge queue, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E09** (users, sessions, `workspaces:read`/`workspaces:write` permissions). Blocks **E15-S03**, **E15-S07**; unblocks **E16**'s auto-record trigger.

`feat/e15-workspaces-api`

title: packages/dock: layout tree, reconciler and DockGrid without GL churn
body:
## Context
Every user-facing ticket in this Epic — presets, docking, save/restore, sync, responsive collapse — is a different way of mutating the same data structure. Writing that structure once, in a package with no React and no chart knowledge, is what keeps those five Stories from each inventing their own tree algebra. It also makes the hardest requirement testable in a unit test instead of an E2E: SCR-020's "layout changes never remount the WebGL context".

That requirement is a reconciliation property, not a rendering trick. If a move is expressed as "remove leaf, insert leaf", React unmounts the canvas and E11 loses its context, its buffers and its data window — a visible flash plus a refetch, and R1 exit criterion 5 ("zero loss") starts leaking. If a move is expressed as "reparent the node with this stable id", nothing unmounts. This Task builds the structure that makes the second one the only option available.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/dock` — framework-free, no React, no `fetch`, no chart-engine import (enforced by an import-linter contract in the same style as `CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16 for the engine):
  - Node model: `row | column | tabset | leaf`, each with a stable `id`, `leaf` carrying `{ paneId, kind, minWidth, minHeight }`, containers carrying fractional `sizes[]`.
  - Operations: `split(targetId, direction, newLeaf)`, `move(paneId, targetId, zone)`, `tabify`, `close(paneId)`, `resize(separatorId, delta)`, `maximise/restore(paneId)`, `float/redock(paneId)`, `applyPreset(preset, existingPanes)`.
  - `normalise(tree)` — collapses single-child containers, removes empty tabsets, clamps fractions to sum 1, enforces minimum sizes; every operation returns a normalised tree.
  - `matchPreset(tree)` → `'1x1' | '2x1' | '1x2' | '2x2' | '1+3' | '3x3' | 'custom'`, and `presetToTree(preset, panes)` — the mapping onto the `lay_preset` CHECK constraint in `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1.
  - Serialisation: `toLayoutInput(tree, panes)` / `fromLayout(layout)` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`'s `LayoutInput`/`Layout`, including the `slot_index` assignment that `layout_panes` requires.
  - `resolveDrop(tree, pointerRect, panes)` → the candidate zone set used by CMP-214, and its keyboard twin `resolveDirectionalMove(tree, paneId, direction)` used by CMP-216's "Move panel" chooser — one code path, two entry points, so the keyboard equivalent cannot drift from the pointer one.
- **CMP-081 DockGrid / Layout Manager**, **CMP-080 DockPanel**, **CMP-082 PanelHeader**, **CMP-083 SplitPane** in the app, rendering a tree from the package:
  - Reconciliation keyed by stable `paneId` so any operation is a reparent; panel content is mounted through a **pane registry** (`kind` → component) so E11/E13/E18+ panels plug in without DockGrid knowing them.
  - Lazy mount on first visibility; hidden-tab panels unsubscribe after 30 s (SCR-020 performance line).
  - Resize via CSS/flex fractions only — no per-frame React state, no layout thrash; the engine is told its new size once per commit.
- A **GL-churn guard**: a test utility that counts `webglcontextlost`/context creations and canvas unmounts across an operation sequence, wired into the package's own test suite so the invariant regresses loudly.

## Out of scope
- The drop-zone visuals, panel menu, preset gallery, floating windows — **E15-S01**, **E15-S02** consume this package.
- Persistence, debounce, conflict handling — **E15-S03**.
- Sync between panes — **E15-T03**.
- Any actual panel implementation; the registry ships with a placeholder panel plus whatever kinds E11–E14 already expose.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Moving a pane never remounts its canvas
  Given a 2x2 tree with four chart leaves each holding a live GL context
  When a pane is moved to the opposite corner, then tabified, then split out again
  Then the GL-churn guard reports zero context losses and zero canvas unmounts, and each pane keeps its data window

Scenario: Every operation returns a normalised tree
  Given a randomised sequence of 1000 split/move/close/resize operations from a property-based generator
  When each result is checked
  Then no container has a single child, no tabset is empty, every sizes[] sums to 1 within floating-point tolerance, and no leaf is smaller than its minimum

Scenario: Preset detection and reconstruction round-trip
  Given a tree built by applyPreset('2x2', panes)
  When matchPreset is called on it
  Then it returns '2x2', and presetToTree('2x2', panes) reproduces an equivalent tree with the same pane ids

Scenario: Keyboard move and pointer drop agree
  Given a pane and a target with any zone
  When the same relocation is expressed as resolveDrop and as resolveDirectionalMove
  Then both produce the identical resulting tree

Scenario: Applying a preset preserves matching panes
  Given a 2x2 layout of four chart panes
  When the 1+3 preset is applied
  Then the four existing pane instances are reused in the new slots rather than recreated, and SCR-022's <= 300 ms budget is met

Scenario: Serialisation matches the stored schema
  When toLayoutInput is called on a custom tree of 16 panes
  Then slot_index values are unique and within 0..15, grid_preset is 'custom', grid_spec validates against the layout JSON Schema, and fromLayout of the result is structurally identical
```

## Technical notes / design
The tree is immutable — every operation returns a new tree — which makes undo, conflict diffing (SCR-029's "side-by-side summary of differences") and property testing straightforward, and makes accidental in-place mutation from a React render impossible.

The package is deliberately ignorant: it knows `kind` is a string and `minWidth` is a number, nothing more. That is what lets it be unit-tested with no DOM, no canvas and no network, which in turn is what makes the 1000-operation property test cheap enough to run on every PR.

The pane registry inverts the dependency: DockGrid imports no panel, panels register themselves. Panel kinds whose Epic has not landed register a disabled stub carrying the reason string SCR-024 shows ("Needs a recorded symbol", "Owner only").

`resolveDrop`/`resolveDirectionalMove` sharing one implementation is not a tidiness preference — CMP-214's catalogue entry makes the keyboard equivalent **mandatory**, and two implementations would diverge by the second bug fix.

Minimum sizes feed SCR-021's "panel too small — showing compact view" state; the package reports the condition, the app renders it.

## Test plan
Unit (the bulk, headless): tree algebra, normalisation invariants, preset match/build, serialisation round-trip, drop resolution, directional move equivalence. Property-based: the 1000-operation sequence above, plus a shrinking check that any violating sequence is reported minimally. Component: DockGrid with fake panels — reparent without unmount (React profiler / instance identity assertions), lazy mount, 30 s unsubscribe, keyboard resize on CMP-083's `role="separator"`. Perf: preset apply ≤300 ms and panel mount ≤150 ms measured in a component benchmark with the pane counts from E15-K01. A11y: axe on DockGrid/DockPanel/PanelHeader/SplitPane; focus-order assertion that visual order and focus order agree (or that `aria-owns` corrects it, per CMP-081).

## Security notes
No network, no credentials, no user-supplied HTML: the package handles ids, numbers and enum strings. Two guards matter anyway — pane `kind` is validated against the registry before mount so a tampered or imported layout cannot name an arbitrary component, and tree depth and node count are capped (16 panes per `lp_slot`, depth cap on nesting) so a hostile imported layout cannot cause unbounded recursion in normalise. Both caps are enforced here, which is what lets E15-S07 trust the tree it imports.

## Accessibility notes
Each DockPanel is `role="region"` with an accessible name composed from kind + symbol + interval (CMP-080). SplitPane dividers are `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation` and `aria-valuenow`, arrow-key resizable (CMP-083). Panel focus order follows visual reading order, corrected via `aria-owns` when DOM order cannot match (CMP-081). Every operation exposed by the package has a keyboard entry point by construction — `resolveDirectionalMove` exists precisely so no layout operation is pointer-only (CMP-214). Layout changes are announced politely once per commit, not per intermediate frame.

## Performance notes
Tree operations are O(nodes) with n ≤ 31 for 16 panes — negligible; the budget risk is entirely in the React commit. Targets: preset apply ≤300 ms (SCR-022), panel mount ≤150 ms (SCR-024, CMP-080), layout transition ≤200 ms (CMP-081), drag preview on CSS transforms only with exactly one layout mutation on drop (SCR-021). Resize must not re-render panel content — the engine receives one resize call per commit, not per pointer move.

## Observability
The package is instrumented but does not log: it emits a `layoutChanged { op, paneCount, preset, durationMs }` callback the app forwards to analytics as `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.preset_applied` etc. The GL-churn guard's counters are exported in dev builds so a regression is visible in Storybook, not only in CI.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test, including the property-based sequence.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on `packages/dock` (engine-package floor, since it is framework-free logic), ≥80% on the app-side DockGrid components.
- [ ] Import-linter contract merged: `packages/dock` may not import React, the chart engine, or anything doing I/O.
- [ ] GL-churn guard wired into CI; a deliberate remount-causing change fails the build.
- [ ] Storybook entries per CMP-080/081/082/083 catalogue lists, including the keyboard resize and keyboard reposition demos.
- [ ] axe-core green; focus-order assertion passing.
- [ ] Perf numbers recorded against E15-K01's curve.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC per unit of work (package and app wiring split across PRs), 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-K01** (pane budget informs minimum sizes and the compact-view threshold), **E11** (engine instances to prove no GL churn), **E10** (app shell, hotkey layer, Electron window plumbing for the float hook). Blocks **E15-S01**, **E15-S02**, **E15-S03**, **E15-T03**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-dock-package`

## References
`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-080, CMP-081, CMP-082, CMP-083, CMP-214, CMP-216; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020 (performance line, >16 panels), SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-024; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`lay_preset`, `lp_slot`, `layout_panes`); `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `LayoutInput`, `Layout`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-001, US-LAY-005; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2, §5 context-loss handling; `/CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16.

2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)

title: Recorder, retention & disk budget
body:
## Context
CandleViewer can only ever analyse order flow it recorded itself: Bybit exposes no historical L2, no historical liquidations and only a ~1000-row recent-trade window (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md#13-recorder-retention-and-replay`). Every R2 surface (footprint E18, profiles E19, Deep-Stats E20, CVD E23, replay E26) is exactly as deep as this recorder has been running, which is why `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.1 schedules E16 in **S06–S07** rather than at the end of the R1 train.

Recording everything is simple and wrong: ~0.5–0.75 GB/day/symbol compressed at 200 depth (budget #12 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`) fills a personal machine in weeks. Owner decision #4 therefore locks: a user-managed recorded-symbol list **empty by default**, auto-record on open chart / open position, 30-day default retention, pin = keep forever, and a visible disk budget. Security area 8 (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.8) rates unbounded recording a **Critical** DoS against the trading host.

Backend modules: **M10 Recorder** (`RecordingPolicy`, `StreamWriter`, `RetentionManager`, `RollOffJob`, `DiskBudget` — `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.8) and **M11** storage tiering/roll-off into the Parquet lake (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §5–§7).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories US-REC-001 … US-REC-008 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#22-rec--recording--retention`).
- Postgres migration `0007_recorder`: `recorded_symbols`, `recording_sessions`, `recording_gaps`, `retention_policies` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.6).
- REST: `/recording/symbols`, `/recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}`, `…/pin`, `/recording/status`, `/recording/storage`, `/recording/retention-policies`, `/recording/sessions`, `/market/data-coverage`, `/admin/recorder/compact`, `/admin/recorder/purge`.
- WS topic `recorder` (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.8 `RecorderUpdate`), and the `no_data_recorded` topic warning contract.
- Screens SCR-140 (Admin: recorder & storage), SCR-141 (retention policy editor), SCR-142 (storage & database panel), SCR-047 (chart empty/no-data), SCR-151 (empty-state pattern).
- Components CMP-177 RecorderStatusRow, CMP-026 EmptyState (`variant="recording-not-started"`), CMP-023 ProgressBar, CMP-049 Table, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- Jobs: nightly verified hot→cold export, weekly compactor, retention reaper with dry-run, disk-pressure ladder, bulk archive importer.
- Observability: `recorder_rows_total{stream}`, `recorder_bytes_written_total{symbol,stream}`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `disk_used_ratio`; audit actions `recorder.start|stop`, `retention.change`, `retention.purge`.

## Out of scope
- The replay engine and scrubbing UI (E26, R2) — E16 only guarantees the data and the coverage metadata replay consumes.
- Footprint/profile/CVD aggregate computation (E18/E19/E23); E16 records the raw tape those are rebuilt from.
- Android or any non-web client; a separate admin app (admin screens live inside the web app, RBAC-gated).
- Non-Bybit exchanges and non-USDT-perp instruments.
- Backups/restore (`/admin/backups/*`) — owned by the platform/ops epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fresh install records nothing
  Given a freshly migrated installation
  When the owner opens /admin/recorder
  Then the recorded-symbol list is empty and no market data beyond klines is persisted

Scenario: Seven-day soak with retention and pinning
  Given three symbols recorded continuously for seven days, one of them pinned
  When the nightly retention reaper and the hot->cold export have run each night
  Then past-retention non-pinned partitions are gone from QuestDB and present in Parquet with verified checksums
  And no pinned partition has been deleted at either tier
  And the disk projection shown on SCR-140 is within +/-15% of measured actual growth

Scenario: Disk pressure never silently degrades recording
  Given free space on the data volume falls below 5%
  When the disk-budget guard evaluates
  Then recording for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols is paused, a critical system event is raised and pinned data is untouched

Scenario: Gaps are honest
  Given the recorder was down for 12 minutes for BTCUSDT
  When any dependent view queries that window
  Then an explicit recording_gaps interval is returned and rendered as a hatched region, never interpolated
```

## Technical notes / design
Effective recorded set = explicit list ∪ open-chart symbols ∪ open-position symbols, per `RecordingPolicy` in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §13.1. Auto-record starts within 2 s of a chart opening (after a 60 s open-dwell guard) and lingers `linger_minutes` (default 15) after the last reason disappears; a symbol with an open position can never stop recording. Writes are batched QuestDB ILP (10k rows / 200 ms) with a bounded 1 GB on-disk WAL spill when QuestDB is unavailable. Trades and book deltas are **never** dropped under backpressure; tickers/klines may be dropped, counted and recorded as a gap. Retention resolution order: pinned → symbol-scoped policy → default policy → hard 30-day default. No hot partition is dropped before its Parquet counterpart is written, SHA-256'd and row-count-verified.

Config/flags: `recorder.auto_record` (default true), `storage.cold_tier` (true), `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (7), `CV_RECORDER_RETENTION_DAYS` (30), `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` (500). Error codes: `no_data_recorded` (422/WS warning), `resource_purged` (410), `conflict` (409 on un-recording a symbol with an active trigger).

## Test plan
Unit (≥85% on `backend/recorder/*`, `backend/storage/*`): policy resolution, retention resolution, gap detection, projection math, importer parsing. Contract: OpenAPI + `RecorderUpdate` schema conformance. Integration (`03-testing-strategy.md` §5): auto-record trigger → QuestDB write → retention/pin → Parquet roll-off → DuckDB query of rolled-off data. E2E Playwright + Electron over SCR-140/141/142. Perf/soak: 7-day continuous recorder soak on ≥3 symbols; 24 h ingestion soak with zero dropped messages. Chaos: disk at 85/91/96 %, QuestDB down (WAL spill + replay), WS disconnect mid-session.

## Security notes
STRIDE area 8 (`04-security-program.md` §5.8): S2 disk-exhaustion DoS (SR-096), S3 path traversal via archive/export paths (SR-097), S5 retention deleting pinned data (SR-099), S1 silent Parquet corruption (SR-094), S6 exposed QuestDB/DuckDB consoles (SR-048). Purge requires an elevated session, typed `confirm_symbol` echo and a reason; all destructive runs audited (`retention.purge`). Data classification: market data is non-PII operational data; `added_by` links to a user id.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-140/141/142 are WCAG 2.2 AA: disk meters carry numeric text (never bar-only), gap lists are tables with start/end/duration, state is a word not a colour, destructive confirms are focus-trapped dialogs with typed confirmation, and the recorder-dependent empty state is heading + paragraph + real button.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: #5 zero undetected dropped messages per symbol over 24 h; #12 storage growth tracked at ≤0.75 GB/day/symbol planning figure; SCR-140 status at 1 Hz must never block ingestion; storage figures sampled server-side every 60 s. Retention/compaction run off-peak (02:15 / 03:00 UTC) and skip partitions referenced by active replay sessions.

## Observability
Prometheus: `recorder_rows_total{stream}`, `recorder_bytes_written_total{symbol,stream}`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `recorder_dropped_messages_total{symbol,stream}`, `disk_used_ratio`, `retention_deleted_rows_total`, `archive_verify_failures_total`. Alerts at `disk_used_ratio > 0.8`, any `dropped_messages > 0`, any archive verification failure. Audit: `recorder.start`, `recorder.stop`, `retention.change`, `retention.purge`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R1 exit criterion #6 demonstrated: ≥7 continuous days on ≥3 symbols, reaper deletes past-retention data, never touches pinned data, projection within ±15 %.

title: Write the black-box test plan for recorder lifecycle, retention and disk budget
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature alongside the white-box review. E16 is unusually hard to test by inspection because most of its behaviour is temporal (grace periods, nightly jobs, 7-day projections) and destructive (retention, purge), so the plan must define how time is controlled and how destruction is verified without destroying a real dataset.

This ticket produces the plan that E16-Q02..Q06 execute against.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/qa/test-plans/e16-recorder.md` covering US-REC-001 through US-REC-008, each with: preconditions, steps, expected results, oracle (how we know it passed), and the data fixture needed.
- Test matrix dimensions: role (Owner / Manager / Viewer) x action (view, add, stop, pin, retention change, purge, compact, import) x state (empty, recording, degraded, disk-warning, disk-critical).
- Time-control strategy: a documented mechanism to advance the recorder's clock and trigger nightly jobs on demand in the test environment (`CV_TEST_CLOCK` hook), so a 30-day retention rule is verifiable in minutes without faking the production code path.
- Destructive-test protocol: every retention/purge case runs against a disposable dataset on a scratch volume, with a pre/post byte-and-row manifest so "nothing was deleted" and "exactly this was deleted" are both provable assertions rather than eyeball checks.
- Fixture catalogue: a seeded dataset with (a) a continuously recorded symbol, (b) a symbol with two known gaps of known causes, (c) a pinned symbol with data past every horizon, (d) an archive-imported-only range, (e) a symbol with an open position.
- Entry/exit criteria for QA sign-off of the epic, and the regression subset that must run on every later R2 epic that consumes recorded data.

## Out of scope
- Executing the tests (E16-Q02..Q06) and writing automation code.
- Performance and chaos scripts (E16-Q04) and the a11y audit (E16-Q05), which this plan references rather than contains.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Must story has coverage
  When the plan is reviewed against docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 22
  Then every scenario of US-REC-001 to US-REC-008 maps to at least one numbered test case, and every Must story has at least one failure-path case

Scenario: Destructive cases are provable
  When a retention or purge case is specified
  Then it defines a pre-state manifest, the exact expected delta, and a post-state manifest, and it runs only against the scratch dataset

Scenario: Time-dependent behaviour is testable in minutes
  When a case depends on a 30 day retention horizon or a 30 minute grace period
  Then the plan specifies the clock-control mechanism and the exact assertion, with no test relying on real elapsed time beyond 5 minutes

Scenario: The plan is reviewable by a developer who did not write it
  When a backend engineer reads a case cold
  Then they can execute it without asking a question, because preconditions, fixture name and oracle are all stated
```

## Technical notes / design
- The `CV_TEST_CLOCK` hook must be compile-time or config gated so it cannot be enabled in production; the plan states this as a precondition and E16-X02 verifies it.
- Oracles preferred, in order: exact row/byte manifest > API response assertion > UI assertion. A UI-only oracle is acceptable only for presentation cases.
- Cross-reference each case to the acceptance scenarios already written on E16-S01..S05 and E16-T02..T10 so QA and dev assertions do not diverge.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan. Its own verification is a review: QA lead plus one backend engineer plus one frontend engineer approve, and the coverage mapping table is complete with no "TBD".

## Security notes
The plan must include the abuse cases from E16-X01 as executable QA cases (disk exhaustion via chart-opening, purge without elevation, path traversal via import parameters) so security findings have a repeatable regression home. The scratch dataset must contain no production data.

## Accessibility notes
The plan references the a11y audit in E16-Q05 and states which screens are in that audit's scope: SCR-140, SCR-141, SCR-142, SCR-047, SCR-151.

## Performance notes
The plan names the budgets to be asserted by E16-Q04: 50k msg/s ingest, p95 flush < 50 ms, API p95 < 150 ms, WS `recorder` at 1 Hz, and the measured GB/day from E16-K01.

## Observability
Each case states which metric or audit event is the secondary oracle, so a passing UI with a missing audit entry still fails.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan merged at `docs/qa/test-plans/e16-recorder.md`.
- [ ] Coverage mapping table complete for US-REC-001..008 with no gaps.
- [ ] Reviewed and approved by QA lead, one backend and one frontend engineer.
- [ ] Fixture catalogue agreed with the backend team and ticketed if new fixtures are needed.
- [ ] Entry/exit criteria for epic QA sign-off stated.

## Dependencies
`E16-D06` fixes the screen behaviour and states the plan asserts against.

## Branch

## References

- docs/plan/04-security-program.md#58-area-8--recorder-data--storage
- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md
- docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md

- Destructive-test protocol: every retention/purge case runs against a disposable dataset on a scratch volume, with a pre/post byte-and-row manifest so "nothing was deleted" and "exactly this was deleted" are both provable assertions rather than eyeball checks.

title: Implement RecordingPolicy: effective set, auto-record triggers, grace period
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The per-symbol lifecycle (`idle -> pending_start -> recording -> pending_stop -> stopped`) is now built directly on the library as machine B11 `recording`; there is no hand-rolled enum/transition table and no shim.

> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The per-symbol lifecycle (`idle -> pending_start -> recording -> pending_stop -> stopped`) is now built directly on the library as machine B11 `recording`; there is no hand-rolled enum/transition table and no shim.

> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The per-symbol lifecycle (`idle -> pending_start -> recording -> pending_stop -> stopped`) is now built directly on the library as machine B11 `recording`; there is no hand-rolled enum/transition table and no shim.

> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The per-symbol lifecycle (`idle -> pending_start -> recording -> pending_stop -> stopped`) is now built directly on the library as machine B11 `recording`; there is no hand-rolled enum/transition table and no shim.

ADR-0015 decision 1 defines the effective recorded set as *explicit user list union symbols with an open chart union symbols with an open position*. `RecordingPolicy` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.8) is the single component that owns this union and the transitions in and out of it. It implements US-REC-001 (manual list, empty by default) and US-REC-002 (auto-record triggers with a grace period), and it is the gate every other recorder component asks "should I be capturing this symbol right now".

Getting the grace periods right is a product requirement, not an optimisation: ADR-0015 consequences call out that auto-recording on chart open surprises a user who browses many symbols, mitigated by a 60 s open-before-start delay; US-REC-002 requires a configurable stop grace period defaulting to 30 min so a briefly closed chart does not fragment a session into gaps.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/policy.py` - `RecordingPolicy` with `effective_set() -> dict[symbol, EffectiveEntry]`, `on_chart_opened/closed(symbol, chart_id)`, `on_position_opened/closed(symbol, position_id)`, `add_manual(symbol, user_id, streams, depth)`, `remove_manual(symbol)`, `set_pin(symbol, pinned)`.
- Start rule: a symbol enters the set from `chart_open` only after it has been continuously open for `CV_RECORDER_AUTOSTART_DELAY_S` (default 60); from `position_open` **immediately** (no delay - a position is money at risk).
- Stop rule: when the last `reason_ref` disappears, the entry is retained for `CV_RECORDER_AUTOSTOP_GRACE_S` (default 1800) before recording stops; re-acquiring a reason within the grace window cancels the stop and does **not** open a new session.
- `reason` precedence: `manual` > `position_open` > `chart_open`; a manual entry is never auto-removed and is exempt from the auto-eviction ladder in E16-T07.
- Effective-set changes publish `RecorderSetChanged` domain events on the internal bus so `StreamWriter` (E16-T03) subscribes/unsubscribes; the round trip from user action to subscription active must complete within 5 s (US-REC-001 NFR).
- Audit `recorder.start` / `recorder.stop` with `{symbol, reason, actor, trigger_ref}` via the E09 audit log.
- Config keys added to `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §7.2: `CV_RECORDER_AUTOSTART_DELAY_S`, `CV_RECORDER_AUTOSTOP_GRACE_S`, `CV_RECORDER_AUTORECORD_ENABLED` (default true).
- Implement the `B11` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B11.machine.json`, committed by E50-S01/S02 (hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('recording', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b11_recording.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b11_recording.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.

title: Implement StreamWriter: batched QuestDB writes, WAL spill and recovery
body:
## Context
`StreamWriter` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.8) is the hot path that turns normalised exchange events into durable rows. ADR-0015 decision 2 makes the raw streams the source of truth - derived series are recomputable, so losing a tick is permanent while losing a footprint cell is not. Decision 8 requires a bounded on-disk WAL spill when QuestDB is unavailable, replayed on recovery, so a database restart costs latency rather than history.

The specific failure this component exists to prevent is silent loss: dropping messages under backpressure without recording a gap would leave a hole that later looks like a quiet market (US-REC-006, "I never mistake a gap for calm").

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/writer.py` - `StreamWriter` consuming normalised events from M4/M5/M6 for symbols in the effective set, writing to QuestDB via ILP: tables `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `tickers`, `liquidations` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4).
- Batching: flush on 10 000 rows **or** 200 ms, whichever first (§3.8); per-stream batches so a slow stream never delays another.
- Backpressure ladder: in-memory queue -> bounded on-disk WAL (`CV_RECORDER_WAL_MAX_BYTES`, default 1 GiB, under `CV_RECORDER_WAL_DIR`) -> drop with an explicit `recording_gaps` row (`cause='backpressure_drop'`) and a critical event. Never drop silently.
- WAL replay on startup and on QuestDB recovery, in `exch_ts` order, idempotent (duplicate suppression by `(symbol, stream, exch_ts, seq)`).
- Per-symbol counters written back to `recording_sessions` (`messages_received`, `messages_dropped`, `bytes_written`, `reconnect_count`) every 10 s.
- Metrics `recorder_rows_total{stream}`, `recorder_bytes_written_total{symbol,stream}`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `recorder_write_backlog_rows`, `recorder_flush_duration_seconds`.

## Out of scope
- Session and gap lifecycle from WS disconnects (E16-T04) - this task only records gaps caused by its own backpressure drops.
- Roll-off to Parquet (E16-T05) and retention (E16-T06).
- Derived series (bars, footprint, heatmap) - owned by E12/E18/E21; StreamWriter writes raw streams only.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Steady-state write path
  Given BTCUSDT is recording at depth 200
  When 10 minutes of live tape and book deltas are ingested
  Then every event appears exactly once in the corresponding QuestDB table
  And recorder_write_backlog_rows stays at 0 at p95

Scenario: QuestDB unavailable spills rather than drops
  Given QuestDB is stopped
  When 2 minutes of events arrive
  Then events are appended to the on-disk WAL, recorder_spill_bytes rises and no rows are dropped
  And when QuestDB returns, the WAL is replayed in exch_ts order and the WAL file is truncated

Scenario: WAL exhaustion is recorded as an explicit gap
  Given the WAL has reached CV_RECORDER_WAL_MAX_BYTES and QuestDB is still unavailable
  When further events arrive
  Then they are dropped, a recording_gaps row with cause "backpressure_drop" covering the dropped window is written
  And a critical system event naming the symbol is raised

Scenario: Replay is idempotent
  Given a WAL replay is interrupted halfway and restarted
  When the replay completes
  Then no duplicate rows exist for any (symbol, stream, exch_ts, seq)

Scenario: One slow stream does not stall the others
  Given orderbook_deltas writes are artificially delayed by 2 seconds
  Then trades continue to flush on their own 200 ms cadence
```

## Technical notes / design
- ILP over TCP with the QuestDB client's auto-flush disabled; the writer owns the cadence so flush timing is testable.
- Duplicate suppression on replay uses QuestDB `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS` where the table declares them, and a bloom-filtered in-process set for the current replay batch otherwise.
- WAL format: length-prefixed msgpack frames `{stream, symbol, exch_ts, seq, payload}` with a 4-byte CRC per frame; a frame failing CRC ends the replay at that point and the remainder is quarantined to `<wal>/corrupt/` with a gap recorded - never silently skipped mid-file.
- Sequence handling: a `seq` jump on `orderbook_deltas` is **not** StreamWriter's problem to heal (E08 resubscribes and resnapshots); StreamWriter records the observed jump so E16-T04 can convert it to a `seq_jump` gap.
- Error codes: `recorder_write_failed`, `recorder_wal_full`, `recorder_wal_corrupt`.

## Test plan
- Unit: batching boundaries (exactly 10 000 rows, exactly 200 ms), WAL frame round-trip, CRC failure handling, dedup on replay.
- Integration (testcontainers QuestDB): the five acceptance scenarios, including a real container stop/start for the spill case.
- Chaos: kill -9 the process mid-flush; assert on restart that the WAL replays and the resulting row count equals produced minus dropped, with a gap row for the difference (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` chaos suite, SR-154).
- Perf: sustain 50 000 events/s for 10 minutes with p95 flush < 50 ms and backlog 0; recorded as a benchmark in CI trend.
- Coverage >=85% on `recorder/writer.py`.

## Security notes
Threat S2 (disk DoS, **Critical**, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.8): the WAL is bounded and lives on the recording volume, which SR-096 requires to be separate from the volume the backend and Postgres need - assert the mount differs at startup and refuse to start recording if it does not. Raw exchange payloads retained for forensics are kept 7 days only (ADR-0015 decision 5) and are redacted of any account-scoped field before storage. Classification **internal**.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Budget: ingest 50k msg/s sustained, p95 flush < 50 ms, memory ceiling 512 MiB for queues (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`). Measured GB/day must match the E16-K01 figures within 20%; a larger divergence is a bug in batching or depth configuration.

## Observability
The metrics listed in Scope, plus alert rules: `recorder_spill_bytes > 0` for 5 min -> warning; any `recorder_rows_dropped_total` increase -> critical page.

- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated including the chaos case.
- [ ] Perf benchmark recorded and within budget.
- [ ] Coverage >=85%.
- [ ] Grafana panel added for backlog and spill.
- [ ] 2 approvals including backend code-owner.

`E16-T02` supplies the effective set; `E07` supplies QuestDB tables and connection wiring; `E08` supplies normalised events.

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for the recorder and storage subsystem
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires a STRIDE kickoff for any epic touching this kind of surface, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` explicitly schedules "STRIDE for E16 (disk-exhaustion DoS, path traversal in archive paths)" in the R1 train. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.8 already rates unbounded recording a **Critical** DoS (threat S2) with control SR-096; this ticket extends that seed into a complete model covering every component E16 ships and turns it into concrete, testable abuse cases.

The subsystem is unusual in that its worst outcomes are not confidentiality breaches but availability and integrity ones: filling the disk takes trading down, and silently deleting or misreporting history corrupts every analysis built on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Threat model document `docs/security/threat-models/e16-recorder.md` covering components `RecordingPolicy`, `StreamWriter`, `RetentionManager`, `RollOffJob`, `DiskBudget`, the archive importer, the `recording` REST surface and the `recorder` WS topic, with a data-flow diagram and trust boundaries consistent with `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §4.
- STRIDE enumeration per component with likelihood, impact, rating, existing control, residual risk. Mandatory coverage of at least:
  - **S** - forged auto-record trigger (a chart-open signal for a symbol the actor cannot otherwise record).
  - **T** - retention policy or gap-metadata tampering making absent data look present; archive file substitution during import.
  - **R** - deletion without an attributable audit entry; audit entry lost because the data it described was deleted first.
  - **I** - storage responses leaking host filesystem paths, volume names or other users' recorded symbols to a Viewer.
  - **D** - disk exhaustion by rapid chart opening or by a large import; WAL exhaustion; reaper starvation by a permanently held read lease.
  - **E** - Viewer or Manager reaching `recording:write` or purge without step-up; `CV_TEST_CLOCK` or `CV_ALLOW_SHARED_VOLUME` reachable in production.
- Abuse-case catalogue with a concrete attack narrative and an expected system response for each, written so QA can execute them directly (handed to E16-Q01).
- Mapping of every threat to an existing control (SR-096, SR-125, SR-154, permission 51) or to a new requirement raised as a ticket against the owning E16 task.
- Data classification statement for every store E16 writes: recorded market data (**public** content, **internal** operational metadata), coverage/gap metadata (**internal**, integrity-critical), audit entries (**internal**, tamper-evident).

## Out of scope
- Implementing the controls - findings become work on E16-T02/T03/T05/T06/T07/T08/T10.
- The security review of the shipped code (E16-X02) and the pen-test (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every component is enumerated
  When the model is reviewed
  Then each of the eight named components has a STRIDE row per applicable category with a rating and a named control or an open finding

Scenario: The Critical DoS has a tested control
  Given threat S2 disk exhaustion is rated Critical
  Then it maps to SR-096 and to the disk-pressure chaos test in E16-Q04, with the acceptance thresholds stated

Scenario: Path traversal is modelled at every write and delete site
  When archive import, Parquet export and Parquet deletion are analysed
  Then each has an explicit containment requirement and a corresponding test referenced

Scenario: Findings become work, not prose
  Given a threat with no adequate existing control
  Then a ticket is raised against the owning E16 task and linked from the model, and the model records the ticket key

Scenario: The model is signed off
  When the review meeting concludes

```

- Use the same table format as the existing §5 areas in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` so the model can be folded back into the security program document rather than living apart from it.

Model all four; do not model an unauthenticated internet attacker reaching the API, which the network boundary already excludes - but do state that assumption explicitly so it is re-examined if the boundary changes.
- Rate the *combined* path too: a Viewer opening many charts is individually legitimate and collectively a DoS; the model must name the aggregate, not just the single action.

The model's abuse cases are executed by E16-Q01/Q02/Q04. This ticket verifies itself by review: every abuse case must be executable as written, checked by the QA lead during sign-off.

body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires a design-QA pass before a UI surface is Done, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 names a design-QA pass as an R1 quality gate. E17's UI surface is small but unusually hard to inspect: most of its states only appear when the transport misbehaves, so they are exactly the states that ship unverified unless someone deliberately forces each one.

This ticket forces every one of them against the built implementation and signs off - or files defects.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Drive the implemented client through **every row of the E17-D02 state matrix** using the fault-injection controls added by E17-T04 and the chaos harness of E17-Q02: stale topic, `lagging`, `saturated`, `overflowing`/`slow_consumer` close, full disconnect and reconnect, retry exhaustion, `shutdown_notice` countdown, per-topic `revoked`, book resync.
- Compare against the Figma redlines: spacing, type, tokens (`color.status.*`, `color.overlay.stale`, `color.surface.scrim`, `elevation.5`), iconography, copy strings character-for-character.
- Verify every Storybook story named in the E17-D02 handoff pack exists and matches.
- **Accessibility review**: axe-core on SCR-152 and the chrome; manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass on state transitions; verify the announcement policy (assertive once for `degraded`/`offline`, polite for stale, no per-heartbeat chatter), CMP-077 focus trap and keyboard retry, CMP-078's visible age text, greyscale distinguishability, 125% and 200% zoom reflow, and `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- File defects with the standard taxonomy (`03-testing-strategy.md` section 11.3) and re-verify fixes.
- Written sign-off comment listing what was inspected and what was waived.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of the protocol (E17-Q01/Q02 own that); this pass is fidelity and accessibility only.
- Screens outside E17's surface.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every designed state is verified against the build
  When the state matrix from E17-D02 is walked against the running app
  Then every row is marked pass, or has a filed defect linked, and none is marked not-reachable

Scenario: Announcements do not chatter
  Given a connection oscillates between healthy and lagging five times in a minute with NVDA running
  Then each transition announces at most once and heartbeats produce no announcement

Scenario: Reconnect overlay traps focus and is operable
  Given the reconnect overlay is shown
  Then Tab cycles within it, the retry button is reachable and activatable by keyboard, and no affordance falsely implies the data is current

Scenario: axe is clean
  When axe-core runs on SCR-152 and the app chrome in every transport state
  Then there are zero violations

Scenario: A defect blocks sign-off
  Given an open P1 fidelity or accessibility defect
  Then design QA is not signed off and the consuming stories stay out of Done
```

## Technical notes / design
States are forced deterministically rather than waited for: E17-T04 exposes a dev-only fault-injection channel (build-flagged off in production) and E17-Q02's toxiproxy-style harness supplies the transport-level faults. ## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test pass. Evidence: annotated screenshots per state, an axe report per route, and a screen-reader transcript for the transition set. Attached to the ticket.

## Security notes
Confirm no diagnostic identifier (`request_id`, `connection_id`, `git_sha`, internal host names) is rendered to a Viewer-role user outside the "copy details" affordance.

## Accessibility notes
The whole ticket. Binding standard: `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, WCAG 2.2 AA. Manual screen-reader pass is mandatory and cannot be substituted by axe.

## Performance notes
Confirm the 1 Hz chrome update does not re-render the workspace subtree - verified with a React profiler trace attached to the ticket.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Every state-matrix row inspected with evidence attached.
- [ ] axe-core zero violations; NVDA and VoiceOver transcripts attached.
- [ ] Defects filed, triaged, and P0/P1 fixed and re-verified.

title: Build the WS protocol conformance suite and the black-box test plan
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.1 states 12 server MUSTs and 12 client MUSTs, and section 16.4 gives a test matrix with named rows. R1 exit criterion 7 requires contract tests to pass as part of declaring the protocol frozen, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 makes contract testing an R1 quality gate.

A conformance suite is different from the unit tests inside each story: it treats the gateway as a **black box reachable only through a socket** and asserts the normative requirements directly, by number. That is what makes it reusable - E26 (replay) and every R2 topic addition run the same suite unchanged and find out immediately whether they broke the contract.

This ticket also produces the human-facing black-box test plan required per story group by `03-testing-strategy.md` section 11.1.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Conformance harness** (`tests/conformance/ws/`): a protocol-level client that speaks both `cv.v1.msgpack` and `cv.v1.json`, built on the generated `packages/protocol` types but **not** on `apps/web`'s client - so a bug in the app client cannot mask a server bug.
- **One test per normative requirement**, named for it:
  - **S1** one `sub_ok` result per requested topic, in request order.
  - **S2** `snap` before any `d` on a new subscription unless `snapshot:false` was accepted.
  - **S3** `s` increments by exactly 1 per topic; never reused or skipped (including under concurrent topic writes).
  - **S4** `orders` and `executions` never coalesced or throttled.
  - **S5** causal order `executions` -> `orders` -> `positions` -> `trade_groups`.
  - **S6** outbound queue bounded; never unbounded buffering.
  - **S7** authorisation re-evaluated on grant change with `revoked` emitted.
  - **S8** heuristic payloads tagged `estimated: true`.
  - **S9** replay frames tagged `source: "replay"` / header bit2 with `wt` populated.
  - **S10** only error codes from the section 10.2 catalogue are ever emitted.
  - **S11** `bye` before every server-initiated close.
  - **S12** unknown option keys rejected, not ignored.
- **Contract tests** from section 16.4: every recorded frame validates against its section 13-15 schema; every binary frame decoded then validated against the structured schema (binary/structured equivalence, all six kinds); error-catalogue closure.
- **Named unit-level conformance checks** that belong to the suite rather than to one story: `heatmap_bucket_selection` against every row of the section 6.1.1 reference table plus the ladder clamp and the server's `500` fallback when the option is absent.
- **Integration rows** from section 16.4: upstream `u` gap produces `snap` with `reason: upstream_desync`; grant revocation mid-stream produces `revoked` within 1 s with other topics intact; token expiry produces in-place re-auth preserving subscriptions and sequences; replay subscribe-seek-finish emits the documented frame series (executed against E26 when it lands; until then, asserted against a stubbed replay clock and marked pending).
- **Black-box test plan** in `docs/qa/test-plans/e17-ws-protocol.md` covering the story groups (lifecycle, subscriptions and authorisation, snapshot and resync, backpressure, client behaviour), with per-scenario preconditions, steps, expected results and the section 10.3 UI treatment expected for each error class.
- **Suite wired into CI** as a required check on the `contracts` and `integration` jobs.

## Out of scope
- Chaos (E17-Q02), load (E17-Q03), E2E and exploratory (E17-Q04), security-specific tests (E17-X02).
- Payload *content* correctness (whether a footprint cell has the right volume) - owned by the producing epics; this suite asserts transport contract only.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every normative requirement has a named test
  When the conformance suite is listed
  Then there is at least one test per requirement S1 through S12, named for the requirement it asserts

Scenario: The suite catches a real regression
  Given the sequence generator is deliberately changed to skip a number under concurrency
  Then the S3 test fails

Scenario: Binary and structured are proven equivalent
  Given every binary body kind 1 through 6
  When each is decoded and validated against its structured schema
  Then all pass, and a deliberately corrupted layout fails

Scenario: The error catalogue is closed
  Given a full run exercising every error path
  Then every emitted code appears in section 10.2 and an injected undocumented code fails the suite

Scenario: Heatmap bucket selection is enforced, not aspirational
  Given every row of the 6.1.1 reference table plus the absent-option case
  Then the computed bucket matches the documented value including the 1000 ms ladder clamp

Scenario: The suite runs against both subprotocols
  Then every applicable test passes under cv.v1.msgpack and under cv.v1.json with base64 payloads
```

## Technical notes / design
The harness drives a real server instance from the docker-compose test environment (`03-testing-strategy.md` section 17) fed by **recorded Bybit fixtures** (section 4.1), not live Bybit - so runs are deterministic and consume no rate-limit budget.

Requirement S6 (bounded queue) is asserted here only in its *observable* form (the ladder is followed, the connection is closed rather than growing); the memory measurement itself is E17-Q02's chaos scenario.

Tests are parameterised over the topic registry table from E17-S02, so a topic added in R2 is automatically covered by the generic rows (snapshot-before-delta, sequence monotonicity, option rejection) without anyone remembering to add tests. This is the mechanism that makes the freeze cheap to maintain.

## Test plan
This ticket **is** a test deliverable. Its own quality bar: each test fails when its requirement is deliberately broken - a mutation check run once during review, with the results recorded on the ticket. A conformance test that cannot fail is worse than none.

## Security notes
The suite includes the non-adversarial half of the security matrix (error-catalogue closure, option rejection); the adversarial half - cross-account subscribe, query-string token, fuzzed bodies - is E17-X02, deliberately owned by Security rather than QA.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (protocol level). The section 10.3 UI treatment expectations recorded in the test plan feed E17-Q04's E2E assertions.

## Performance notes
The suite must run in under 5 minutes in CI so it can be a required check on every PR; long-running scenarios belong to E17-Q02 and E17-Q03's nightly jobs.

## Observability
CI output reports the requirement coverage matrix (which of S1-S12 and C1-C12 ran), so a silently skipped requirement is visible rather than green.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] A named test exists and passes for every requirement S1-S12; client obligations C1-C12 covered in E17-Q04 and cross-referenced.
- [ ] Contract rows of section 16.4 implemented and green under both subprotocols.
- [ ] `heatmap_bucket_selection` green against every reference row.
- [ ] Mutation check recorded: each test demonstrated failing on a deliberate break.
- [ ] Black-box test plan merged at `docs/qa/test-plans/e17-ws-protocol.md` and reviewed by the Architect.
- [ ] Suite wired as a required CI check, runtime under 5 minutes.
- [ ] QA lead sign-off.

## Dependencies
- **E17-S03** - a server that emits snapshots and deltas.
- **E17-T01** - generated schemas to validate against.

## Branch
`test/e17-ws-conformance`

## References

- docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md sections 4.1, 5, 11.1, 17
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md section 5.4
