title: Select LOD with hysteresis and decimate candles without losing spikes
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-001` requires that at 100,000 bars zoomed to fit, "rendering stays at or above 55 fps using level-of-detail aggregation, **and the aggregation level is indicated**". That last clause is the honesty requirement: a trader must never be shown a decimated chart that silently pretends to be the full one.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 makes the correctness rule explicit: candle decimation at L2 is **min/max preserving** — per pixel column emit min-low, max-high, first-open, last-close — "so spikes never disappear — a correctness requirement, not a cosmetic one". A naive stride-sample would drop the exact wick that a stop sat behind.

This Story also owns the **degradation ladder** of `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4: when frames go over budget, the engine steps down detail deliberately and visibly, rather than dropping frames randomly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/lod/LodSelector.ts` — the candle ladder of §3.6: `barSpacing >= 3 px` -> **L0** (full OHLC bodies + wicks); `>= 1.5 px` -> **L1** (bodies only); else **L2** (min/max column strip, one column per pixel).
- **±15 % hysteresis dead band** on every threshold so slow zooming cannot flicker between levels (gate **B2**: <=6 LOD changes over the full 0.1->50 px/bar zoom sweep).
- `src/lod/Decimator.ts` — min/max-preserving reduction producing `(minLow, maxHigh, firstOpen, lastClose)` per pixel column, computed incrementally against the columnar stores of E11-T03.
- Extension seams (thresholds registered, implementations owned elsewhere): footprint L0–L3, profile row merging below 2 px, bubble clustering <=500 instances, heatmap column aggregation; drawings are **never** decimated.
- **Automatic step-down** after **3 consecutive over-budget frames**, one level at a time, with a matching step-up only after sustained headroom (asymmetric, to avoid oscillation).
- The §4.4 **degradation ladder order**, applied in this sequence and no other: (1) reduce non-focused panes to candles+profile, (2) drop footprint cell text, (3) coarsen heatmap, (4) reduce bubble count — trading-critical overlays (order/position lines, SL/TP) are **never** shed.
- **Aggregation indicator**: a non-colour-only chip ("Aggregated — 12 bars per column") surfaced through the engine's state so SCR-030's "low-GPU degraded" state and the DOM mirror can both report it.
- `lodBias` from the density mode (E11-T04) folded into the thresholds.
- Manual override: `chart.setLod(level | "auto")` for diagnostics and for the benchmark harness.

## Out of scope
- Footprint/heatmap/profile decimation *implementations* — E18/E19/E21 register against the seams defined here.
- The memory-pressure step-down (a different trigger with a different policy) — E11-S15's `MemoryGovernor`, which calls into this Story's step-down API.
- Bar aggregation for a *requested interval* (1m -> 7m) — that is a bar-builder concern in E12; LOD is a purely visual reduction that never changes the underlying series.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Spikes survive decimation
  Given a 100k-bar series containing a single one-bar spike of 10x the surrounding range
  When the chart is zoomed to fit so that ~200 bars map to each pixel column
  Then the spike's high and low are both still visible in the rendered column strip
  And a property test over 10,000 random series confirms per-column min-low and max-high are always preserved

Scenario: No LOD flicker while zooming slowly
  Given the user performs the B2 wheel-zoom sweep from 0.1 to 50 px per bar
  When LOD transitions are counted
  Then at most 6 LOD changes occur across the whole sweep
  And p95 frame time stays <= 14 ms

Scenario: The aggregation level is always disclosed
  Given the chart is rendering at L2
  When the chart state is inspected
  Then an aggregation indicator reports the level and the bars-per-column ratio as text, not colour alone
  And the DOM mirror and the SCR-045 data table report the same ratio

Scenario: Over-budget frames trigger a deliberate, ordered step-down
  Given three consecutive frames exceed the 16.7 ms budget
  When the degradation ladder runs
  Then exactly one level is shed, following the 4.4 order, and ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN is logged with the reason
  And no order line, position line, SL or TP is ever shed

Scenario: Recovery is asymmetric and does not oscillate
  Given the engine has stepped down and frame times return to budget
  When headroom is sustained for 2 seconds
  Then the engine steps back up one level
  And a workload oscillating around the budget produces at most one transition per 2 seconds

Scenario: Drawings are never decimated
  Given 200 drawings are present at the most aggregate LOD
  When a frame is rendered
  Then every drawing is drawn at full fidelity
  And picking against them still completes within 1 ms
```

## Technical notes / design
**Hysteresis.** Thresholds are asymmetric by construction so the transition point differs by direction:

```ts
// stepping DOWN in detail requires crossing below t * (1 - 0.15);
// stepping UP requires crossing above t * (1 + 0.15).
const shouldDemote = (spacing: number, t: number) => spacing < t * 0.85;
const shouldPromote = (spacing: number, t: number) => spacing > t * 1.15;
```

**Decimation.** Per pixel column `c` covering bar index range `[i0, i1)`:

```
minLow(c)    = min(low[i0..i1))
maxHigh(c)   = max(high[i0..i1))
firstOpen(c) = open[i0]
lastClose(c) = close[i1-1]
```

Computed with a striding scan over the columnar `Float32Array`s (E11-T03) into a pre-allocated output buffer sized to the pane's pixel width — so the cost is O(visible bars) with **zero allocation**, and the output buffer is reused across frames. Incremental update: appending bars only dirties the trailing column.

**Step-down state machine.** `Nominal -> Degraded(1..4) -> Floor`. Trigger: 3 consecutive frames over budget. Recovery: 2 s of sustained headroom. The ladder order is data, not code branches — a frozen array of shed actions — so E18/E19/E21 register their action at the right rank and the order is reviewable in one place.

**Config keys**: `lod.mode` (`auto` | `l0` | `l1` | `l2`), `lod.hysteresisPct` (default 15), `lod.stepDownFrames` (default 3), `lod.recoveryMs` (default 2000).

## Test plan
- **Property** (fast-check, >=10,000 cases): decimation preserves per-column min-low and max-high for arbitrary series incl. monotonic, constant, and spike-heavy inputs; the first-open/last-close pair always comes from the correct end bars.
- **Unit**: threshold selection at every boundary and inside both dead bands; asymmetric promote/demote; step-down state machine incl. oscillation resistance with a `TestClock`; ladder ordering; assertion that trading-critical overlays are absent from the shed list.
- **Golden image**: the same series at L0, L1 and L2, and at each density mode, confirming the spike is visible at every level.
- **Perf**: **B2** (<=14 ms p95, <=6 LOD changes over the sweep) and **B5** (combined scene <=16.7 ms) as required checks; allocation-counter test asserting zero allocations in the decimation path.
- **Integration**: forced over-budget frames (via a synthetic stall) asserting the ladder runs in order and logs each step.
- **A11y**: the aggregation indicator's text is present in the DOM mirror and announced once on change, not per frame.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only**.

The security-relevant property here is **integrity of what the user sees**, which is why min/max preservation is specified as a correctness requirement and tested as a property rather than by example. A decimation bug that hides a wick is indistinguishable to the user from a data-feed bug and could lead to a real trading loss — it is treated as a P0 correctness defect, not a rendering nicety.

**Denial of service** (E11-X01): the decimation output buffer is bounded by the pane's pixel width, so no zoom level or data volume can make it allocate unboundedly; the step-down ladder is itself the engine's DoS mitigation against pathological workloads. No secrets, no I/O, no `eval`.

## Accessibility notes
- **Non-colour-only disclosure**: the aggregation indicator is text ("Aggregated — 12 bars per column"), satisfying `05-accessibility-standard.md` and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §5 rule 1. SCR-030's degraded state ("Reduced detail: footprint text hidden below 6 px cells") is the screen-level rendering of this same signal.
- The DOM mirror (E11-S13) must report the *same* LOD level as the canvas — a mirror claiming full detail while the canvas shows a column strip is a desync defect, explicitly never acceptable per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4.
- LOD changes announce **once** in a polite live region, never per frame.
- Degradation must never shed a trading-critical overlay, because for a keyboard/screen-reader user those overlays are the only positional cue available.

## Performance notes
This Story *is* the mechanism by which budget **#2** (30 fps floor under the B6 worst case) is met. Gates: **B2** <=14 ms p95 with <=6 LOD changes; **B5** <=16.7 ms p95 with <=40 draw calls; **B6** aggregate <=16.7 ms. Decimation is O(visible bars) with zero allocations. The engine must degrade rather than drop frames — a dropped frame is invisible and unaccountable, a step-down is logged and disclosed.

## Observability
Events `ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN` / `ENGINE_LOD_STEPUP` with `{ from, to, reason, frameTimeP95 }`; counters `engine.lod.level`, `engine.lod.bars_per_column`, `engine.lod.transitions_per_minute` (an oscillation alarm above 30), `engine.degradation.rung`. All surfaced on SCR-046 and included in the copied diagnostics snapshot.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S03** — `barSpacing` and the viewport transform that drive threshold selection.
- **E11-T03** — the columnar stores the decimator scans.
- **E11-T04** — `lodBias` from the density mode.
- Called by **E11-S15** (memory-pressure step-down) and consumed by **E11-T06** (B2/B5/B6 gates) and **E11-T07** (diagnostics).
- Blocks **E18**/**E19**/**E21**, which register their own rungs against this ladder.

## Branch

title: Playwright E2E for bar modes, series types and timeframe switching
body:
## Context
Groups 1, 2, 5 and 6 of the E12 black-box plan are user-journey shaped: open a chart, switch type, switch bar mode, switch symbol, change days-to-load, and never see a lie about history. Those journeys cross the WebGL canvas, which is hostile to conventional DOM assertions — a screenshot of a canvas tells you little and is flaky across GPUs (risk **R8**).

The answer, already established by E11's engine work, is that the engine exposes a **deterministic test surface**: the DOM-mirror a11y layer (`SCR-045` data-table alternative) and a diagnostics/state probe (`SCR-046`). This suite drives the real app through Playwright (web and Electron per `03-testing-strategy.md`) and asserts against those surfaces plus normal chrome (`CMP-220 IntervalPicker`, `CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle`, `CMP-199 ChartLegend`), not against pixels.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/specs/e12-bars/` Playwright specs implementing the automated cases from `E12-Q01`:
  - `candles.spec.ts` — open `SCR-041` quick-switcher, load BTCUSDT 1 m, assert first/last bar values via the data-table alternative match `GET /market/klines`; forming bar updates without a reload (US-CHART-001).
  - `series-types.spec.ts` — switch candle → OHLC bar → line → area → Heikin-Ashi → baseline; assert no network refetch occurs (request interception) and drawings/anchors stay at the same timestamps (US-CHART-002); assert the volume sub-pane mounts as a linked pane sharing the time axis.
  - `bar-modes.spec.ts` — select tick and volume modes from `SCR-042`, assert the parameter control, the resulting bar count from the data table, and the partial-history marker when the fixture's recording starts mid-window (US-CHART-003).
  - `range-renko.spec.ts` — switch to range/delta/renko, assert the rebuild progress affordance appears and is cancellable, and that an unsupported combination (Heikin-Ashi + footprint) surfaces the documented guard message rather than rendering (US-CHART-004, US-CHART-002 scenario 3).
  - `switching.spec.ts` — hotkey timeframe switch preserves the visible-window centre, no flash of empty chart (assert the skeleton `CMP-029` or prior frame persists), symbol switch without engine teardown (assert the GL context id from `SCR-046` is unchanged) (US-CHART-005).
  - `history-states.spec.ts` — days-to-load control, empty state `SCR-047` naming the first available timestamp, error state `SCR-048` on a stubbed 503, and the `no_data_recorded` 422 path (US-CHART-010, US-MKT-008).
- Deterministic backend: specs run against a **fixture-backed staging profile** that serves the `E12-Q01` tapes, with a frozen clock so bar-close countdowns and the forming bar are reproducible.
- A shared `chartProbe` page-object wrapping the data-table alternative, diagnostics overlay and legend readout, so specs never poke at canvas internals directly.
- Both runners wired: Chromium (web) and the Electron shell, with the Electron run marked required before the R1 exit review.
- Flake controls: no fixed sleeps (only web-first assertions on probe state), per-spec trace-on-failure, and a quarantine list that fails the build if anything sits in it for more than one sprint.

## Out of scope
- Builder-level value correctness (`E12-Q02` owns it); E2E asserts the *plumbing*, spot-checking a handful of values only.
- Frame-rate and memory budgets (`E12-Q05`).
- Keyboard/screen-reader conformance depth (`E12-Q07`) — this suite uses the a11y layer as a probe but does not audit it.
- Drawing tools (E14), indicators (E13), layouts (E15).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Series type switch does not refetch
  Given BTCUSDT 5m is loaded with 5000 bars
  When the user switches from candles to Heikin-Ashi via CMP-222
  Then no request to /market/klines or /market/bars is issued
  And the data-table alternative reports the same bar count with transformed OHLC values

Scenario: Symbol switch reuses the engine
  Given a chart on BTCUSDT with a known GL context id from SCR-046
  When the user switches to ETHUSDT from SCR-041
  Then the GL context id is unchanged
  And the chart never renders an empty grid between the two symbols

Scenario: Failure case - backend error surfaces the error state
  Given /market/klines is stubbed to return 503
  When a chart is opened
  Then SCR-048 is shown with a retry affordance and the failure reason
  And the app does not show an empty chart implying there is no data

Scenario: Edge case - window predates recording for a tick bar mode
  Given ETHUSDT tick:1000 is requested for a window before recording_started_at
  When the chart loads
  Then the partial-history marker is rendered at the recording start
  And the empty region is labelled rather than drawn as flat price

Scenario: Edge case - rebuild is cancellable
  Given a renko brick-size change triggers a rebuild over 1M prints
  When the user cancels mid-rebuild
  Then the previous series remains displayed and no partial series is committed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use Playwright request interception to assert absence-of-network for client-side transforms — a stronger assertion than visual equality and immune to GPU differences.
- The frozen clock is injected at the app boundary (a test-only clock provider), never by patching `Date` in page context, so the backend and frontend agree on bar boundaries.
- Electron run reuses the same specs via the Playwright Electron launcher; any spec that cannot run in Electron must state why in a comment, per `03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Probe state is read from a stable `data-testid` JSON island emitted by the diagnostics overlay, versioned so a probe-shape change is a deliberate PR, not silent breakage of the suite.

## Test plan
- The suite *is* the test artefact; its own correctness is demonstrated by seeded-failure runs: stub a wrong bar count, a missing partial-history marker, and a teardown-on-symbol-switch, and confirm each fails.
- Run three consecutive green CI passes before marking done, to establish a flake baseline.
- Trace and video retained for failures only, to keep artefact size sane.

## Security notes
- Specs run against staging with a seeded non-privileged test user holding only `marketdata:read`; no live credentials, no live environment, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8's demo/staging rule.
- Fixture responses must not contain account identifiers; the stub server is asserted to serve market data only.
- Any test-only probe (diagnostics JSON island, clock provider) must be compiled out of production builds — add an assertion in this suite that the probe is absent when the app is built in production mode, so a debug surface cannot ship by accident (cross-link `E12-X02`).

## Accessibility notes
- Because the suite drives the DOM-mirror layer, it doubles as a regression guard that the a11y alternative stays wired: if `SCR-045` regresses, these specs fail loudly rather than a11y silently rotting.
- Every interaction in the specs is performed by keyboard where the UI claims keyboard support (interval hotkeys, quick-switcher), so the claimed keyboard paths are exercised on every run.

## Performance notes
- The suite asserts *perceived* behaviour only (no flash of empty chart, skeleton shown, interactive before full history), with generous web-first timeouts; hard budgets are `E12-Q05`'s.
- Total suite wall time target ≤12 minutes on CI in parallel shards.

## Observability
- Each spec tags its run with the build sha and fixture set; results feed the QA run log rolled up in `E12-Q08`.
- On failure, the spec attaches the diagnostics probe JSON and the last 200 lines of backend logs for the fixture server, so triage does not require local reproduction.

## Definition of Done
- All six specs merged and green on Chromium and Electron; three consecutive green runs recorded.
- Seeded-failure evidence attached for at least three scenarios.
- Quarantine list empty at merge time.
- Frontend coverage contribution recorded (E2E does not count toward the ≥80% unit threshold but its journey coverage is mapped to `E12-Q01` case ids).
- Suite documented in the QA plan with how to run locally against fixtures.
- Demo: a live run of `switching.spec.ts` at sprint review.

## Dependencies
- `E12-S01`, `E12-S02`, `E12-S03`, `E12-S05` (the journeys must exist), `E12-Q01` (case ids), E11's diagnostics overlay and DOM-mirror layer.

## Branch
`chore/e12-q03-e2e-bars`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (E2E layer, Playwright web + Electron)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001..005, US-CHART-010, US-MKT-008
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047, SCR-048
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-180, CMP-181, CMP-199, CMP-220, CMP-221, CMP-222, CMP-029
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines`, `/market/bars`

title: Contract tests for /market/klines, /market/bars and the bars WS topic
body:
## Context
R1's exit criteria freeze the WS protocol: "`23-ws-protocol.md` matches the implementation, contract tests pass, and a deliberate breaking change fails CI". E12 owns two REST endpoints (`GET /market/klines`, `GET /market/bars`) and the `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` topic whose payload is normatively specified in `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.3 `BarsBatch`. E13, E18, E23 and E26 will all build on those shapes; if the implementation drifts from the document, every downstream consumer inherits an undocumented contract (risk **R6 Feed rot**).

This ticket adds schema-driven contract tests that treat the committed documents as the source of truth and the server as the thing under test — in both directions: responses must validate against the schema, and the schema must have no field the server never emits.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **REST contract tests** generated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: every documented response code for `/market/klines` and `/market/bars` (200, 400, 422, 503) exercised against the fixture-backed server, with responses validated against the referenced schemas (`KlineResponse`, `BarType`, `KlineInterval`, `meta.sources`, `meta.recording_started_at`, `meta.next_cursor`/`has_more`).
- Parameter-matrix coverage: every `bar_type` value in the documented table (`time`, `tick`, `volume`, `range`, `delta`, `renko`, `pnf`, `heikin_ashi`) with a valid `param`, plus `include_open`, `include_delta`, `price_type`, `limit` and cursor paging.
- **Documented-error conformance**: a window before `recording_started_at` on a non-time bar type returns `422 no_data_recorded` with the documented error body; an unknown `bar_type` or malformed `param` returns `400`; a store outage returns `503` — asserted by error *code string*, not just status.
- **WS contract tests** for `bars.*`: subscribe, receive snapshot then deltas, validate each frame against `cv://ws/v1/bars.schema.json`; assert `confirm:false` on exactly the forming bar; assert `close_t_ms` present for non-time types and absent-or-consistent for time; assert `coalesced`/`coalesced_count` semantics under a forced slow consumer; assert per-topic sequence numbers increase and a forced gap triggers the documented resync.
- **Schema-drift guard**: a CI job that fails when the server emits a field absent from the schema (`additionalProperties:false` enforced) *and* when a schema field is never observed across the full contract run (dead-contract detection), with an allowlist requiring a comment.
- **Breaking-change canary**: a deliberately breaking mutation (rename `confirm` → `closed`) proven to fail CI, as required by the R1 exit criterion — recorded as evidence.
- Binary framing check: for the binary encoding of `bars.*`, decode frames with the reference decoder and assert field-for-field equality with the JSON fallback encoding of the same update.

## Out of scope
- Transport-level framing, auth handshake, backpressure policy in general — owned by E17; this ticket tests only the `bars` topic's conformance to the frozen envelope.
- Bar value correctness (`E12-Q02`).
- Load and coalescing *performance* (`E12-Q05`); here only the documented coalescing *semantics* are asserted.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every documented response validates
  Given the fixture-backed server
  When the contract suite exercises /market/klines and /market/bars across the full parameter matrix
  Then every response validates against its OpenAPI schema
  And every documented status code is observed at least once

Scenario: WS frames conform to BarsBatch
  Given a subscription to bars.BTCUSDT.time.1
  When a snapshot and 50 deltas are received
  Then every frame validates against cv://ws/v1/bars.schema.json
  And exactly one bar per frame set carries confirm:false

Scenario: Failure case - a breaking change fails CI
  Given the server is patched to emit "closed" instead of "confirm"
  When the contract suite runs
  Then the suite fails naming the offending field and topic
  And the failure message points at 23-ws-protocol.md section 14.3

Scenario: Edge case - pre-recording window on a non-time bar type
  Given a /market/bars request with bar_type=tick and from before recording_started_at
  Then the response is 422 with error code no_data_recorded
  And no REST kline substitution appears in meta.sources

Scenario: Edge case - binary and JSON encodings agree
  Given the same bars update encoded in binary and in the JSON fallback
  When both are decoded
  Then all fields are equal including decimal precision
```

## Technical notes / design
- Generate cases from the spec files at test-collection time rather than hand-transcribing them; a new documented `bar_type` should produce a new test automatically and fail until implemented.
- Decimals are strings end-to-end (`common.schema.json#/$defs/decimal`); the validator must reject a numeric-typed price even if its value is right, because float serialisation is exactly how precision bugs enter.
- Reuse the E17 WS conformance harness rather than building a second client; this ticket contributes the `bars` topic rows to the conformance matrix in `23-ws-protocol.md` §16.
- Run against the fixture server so results are deterministic and the suite can be a required PR check.

## Test plan
- Contract layer per `03-testing-strategy.md`; required check on PRs touching the market-data API surface or the WS bars publisher.
- Negative self-test: three seeded mutations (drop `meta.recording_started_at`, emit a numeric price, omit `close_t_ms` on renko) must each fail.
- Nightly run against the staging server (real store, recorded symbols) to catch drift the fixture server hides.

## Security notes
- Assert `x-rbac: marketdata:read` is actually enforced: an unauthenticated request and a session lacking the permission both receive the documented auth/permission error, never data. This is a contract-level check; deeper RBAC abuse cases live in `E12-X02`.
- Assert input-validation boundaries documented in the spec: `param` maxLength 24 is enforced server-side; `limit` above the documented maximum is rejected rather than honoured (resource-exhaustion guard, `SR-042`-class control).
- Assert `category=linear` is never absent on the upstream Bybit calls made during backfill (SR-054); the fixture server records upstream call shapes for this assertion.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A (protocol-level, no UI). The suite's failure output is plain text with explicit field paths so it is usable by screen-reader users triaging CI.

## Performance notes
- Suite wall time ≤4 minutes so it can gate PRs.
- One coalescing-semantics case uses an artificially slow consumer; it asserts *correctness of the final state*, with throughput measured in `E12-Q05`.

## Observability
- The suite emits a conformance report artefact (endpoint/topic × documented case × pass/fail) that is diffed against the previous run, so newly-skipped coverage is visible.
- Report feeds the R1 protocol-freeze evidence pack referenced by the release checklist.

## Definition of Done
- REST and WS contract suites merged, green, wired as required checks and into nightly.
- Breaking-change canary demonstrated and its evidence attached to this ticket (R1 exit-criterion evidence).
- `23-ws-protocol.md` §16 conformance matrix updated with the `bars.*` rows.
- Dead-contract detection produces an empty allowlist, or each entry carries a justification comment.
- Any spec/implementation divergence found is resolved by changing whichever is wrong — with the decision recorded on the ticket, not silently adjusting the test.
- Demo: show the canary failing CI at sprint review.

## Dependencies
- `E12-T05` (REST endpoints), `E12-T06` (bars WS topic), E17 (WS envelope, binary framing, conformance harness), `E12-Q01`.

## Branch
`chore/e12-q04-bars-contract-tests`

- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §3.1 envelope, §3.4 binary, §7 snapshot+delta, §8 coalescing, §14.3 `BarsBatch`, §16 conformance matrix

title: Decimate series by LOD tier with hysteresis and min/max spike preservation
body:
## Context
US-CHART-001's second scenario is the one that decides whether the custom engine was worth building: "Given 100 000 bars are in the series, when I zoom to fit, then rendering stays at or above 55 fps using level-of-detail aggregation, **and the aggregation level is indicated**."

`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 defines the candle ladder — L0 full OHLC bodies+wicks at `barSpacing ≥ 3 px`, L1 bodies only at `≥ 1.5 px`, L2 a min/max column strip (one column per pixel) below that — and states the rule that makes this a correctness ticket rather than an optimisation: **"Decimation for candles at L2 uses a min/max preserving reduction (per pixel column emit min-low, max-high, first-open, last-close) so spikes never disappear — a correctness requirement, not a cosmetic one."** A decimation that averages or samples will hide the exact wick a trader zoomed out to find.

§3.6 also requires **±15% hysteresis** on the thresholds so slow zooming does not flicker between levels.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The three-tier candle LOD ladder with the documented `barSpacing` thresholds and ±15% dead-band hysteresis.
- Min/max-preserving reduction at L2: per pixel column emit min-low, max-high, first-open, last-close — never an average, never a sample.
- Incremental/cached aggregation: LOD buckets computed off the main thread against the columnar store and reused across frames; a pan of one column must not recompute the whole window.
- Aggregation-level indication in the UI (US-CHART-001's explicit requirement) — a text affordance stating the current level and that bars are aggregated, surfaced in the chart chrome and in the accessible readout, not merely in the diagnostics overlay.
- Correct interaction with non-time-aligned series (index-spaced renko/range decimate by index).
- Correct interaction with the forming bar: the last bar is never merged into an aggregate in a way that hides its live movement (E12-S10 depends on this).
- Benchmark scenarios added to E11-T06's harness at 5k / 50k / 100k bars across all three tiers, wired as a CI gate.

## Out of scope
- Footprint, heatmap, profile and bubble LOD ladders — E18/E19/E21/E22 (each has its own row in §3.6).
- Memory governor and eviction — E11-S15.
- The diagnostics overlay itself — E11-T07.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Spikes survive decimation
  Given a series containing a single-bar wick far outside its neighbours
  When the view is zoomed until that region occupies one pixel column
  Then the rendered column still reaches the extreme high and low
  And a property test over random series confirms the rendered extremes equal the true extremes for every pixel column

Scenario: Frame budget at 100k bars
  Given 100 000 bars zoomed to fit
  Then the p95 frame time stays within 16.6 ms and the frame rate at or above 55 fps on the reference GPU
  And the benchmark result is recorded by the CI gate

Scenario: Hysteresis prevents flicker
  Given barSpacing is hovering at the L0/L1 threshold
  When the user zooms slowly back and forth across it
  Then the level changes only after the plus or minus 15 percent dead band is exceeded
  And no per-frame level oscillation occurs

Scenario: The aggregation level is indicated
  Given the view is at L2
  Then the chart states in text that bars are aggregated and at what level
  And that statement is available to assistive technology, not only as a visual badge

Scenario: The forming bar is never hidden by aggregation
  Given the last bar is still forming
  When the view is at L2
  Then the forming bar's live movement remains visible rather than being frozen into an aggregate bucket

Scenario: Index-spaced series decimate by index
  Given a renko series at L2
  Then aggregation buckets are formed by brick index
  And no time-based bucketing is applied to a series with isTimeAligned=false
```

## Technical notes / design
- L2 buckets are keyed by device-pixel column, so they must be recomputed when the DPI or the pane width changes — but not on every pan. Cache by (first index, bars-per-column) and slide the window.
- Aggregation runs on the worker thread against the typed-array store (E11-T02/T03), writing into a reusable output buffer with no per-frame allocation.
- Hysteresis state lives with the pane, not globally, so two panes at different zooms behave independently.
- The min/max reduction is the single most test-worthy function in the engine: it deserves a dedicated property test (rendered extremes == true extremes for all columns) rather than only golden images, because a golden image of a decimated chart is very hard to read by eye.

## Test plan
- **Property** (primary gate): for random series and random zoom levels, the rendered per-column extremes equal the true extremes of the underlying bars — the anti-spike-loss invariant.
- **Unit** ≥80%: threshold selection with hysteresis, bucket keying, cache invalidation on DPI/width change, index-vs-time bucketing.
- **Golden image** per tier on SwiftShader, plus a dedicated spike fixture.
- **Perf**: 5k / 50k / 100k bars × 3 tiers in the E11-T06 harness, gated in CI with a >10% regression failing the build.
- **E2E**: zoom from L0 to L2 and back; assert the aggregation indication appears and that no flicker occurs across the threshold.

## Security notes
No new external input. The one robustness concern is a pathological bar count or a degenerate pane width (zero or negative after a resize) producing a division by zero or an unbounded bucket loop — clamp both and cover with tests, since a hung render loop is a client-side DoS at the worst possible moment for a trader.

## Accessibility notes
"The aggregation level is indicated" is an accessibility requirement as much as a product one: when bars are aggregated, the data-table alternative (SCR-045) and the crosshair readout must state that the values shown are aggregated and over how many bars, so a screen-reader user is not given decimated values as though they were per-bar truth. The indication is text, never a colour or an icon alone. Live-region announcements remain within the ≤2/s throttle of US-CHART-008.

## Performance notes
This Story *is* the mechanism by which budget #1 (p95 ≤16.6 ms) and US-CHART-001's ≥55 fps at 100k bars are met. GPU memory stays under the 512 MB per-pane cap because L2 uploads one instance per pixel column rather than per bar. Aggregation cost must be amortised: a full-window recompute is permitted on zoom, not on pan.

## Observability
`FrameStats` gains `lodTier` and `aggregatedBarsPerColumn`, surfaced in the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay and in the CI benchmark output. `series_lod_transitions_total{from,to}` to detect flicker regressions in the field.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: the anti-spike-loss property test green; every scenario automated; coverage ≥80%; golden images committed; CI perf gate wired and baselines recorded; axe-core green and the aggregation indication verified with a screen reader; design-QA pass on the indication affordance; QA sign-off; demoed (zoom to 100k bars); PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S06** — the candle series being decimated.
- **E11** — columnar stores, worker protocol, benchmark harness (E11-T06), golden-image harness (E11-T08), DPI handling (E11-S10).

## Branch
`feat/e12-series-lod`

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 LOD and decimation (candle ladder, min/max rule, hysteresis), §13 benchmarks
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-001 (scenario 2), US-CHART-008
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budget #1
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criteria 1 and 2 (degradation ladder, 30 fps floor)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: SCR-045, SCR-046
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench (if perf-labelled) · pnpm lint · pnpm typecheck
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e12-series-lod`
- PR title: `E12-S09: Decimate series by LOD tier with hysteresis and min/max spike preservation`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E12-S09)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/feature, area/chart-engine, priority/p0, qa, perf, a11y

**Done means**
- [ ] All Acceptance criteria scenarios pass under automated test
- [ ] Coverage floor held for touched packages
- [ ] CI gates (lint, typecheck, security scan) green

**Do NOT**
- No GL calls issued from scene-graph nodes — nodes append to batches only (26-chart-engine-design.md §3.1).
- No allocation in the hot render path; anything per-frame must come from an object pool.
- Do not widen a performance budget or edit a benchmark baseline to make a regression pass (AGENTS.md §8).
- Do not ship a hover-only or drag-only interaction; every affordance needs a keyboard path (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E12-S09 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.
- Move the issue's Status to `Blocked` in the project board; do not leave it silently `In Progress`.
- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

title: Indicators framework & v1 indicator set
body:
## Context
R1 "Charting alpha" makes a trader able to *read* the market. E13 is the indicators slice of that: the runtime that turns a declarative indicator spec into incrementally-computed series, the UI to add/configure/remove them, and the v1 indicator set. Roadmap scope line (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2): "Indicator runtime (declarative spec -> incremental computation, backend M9 for heavy series, frontend for cheap ones); overlay vs separate-pane placement; parameter editing with live re-compute; v1 set: MA/EMA/WMA/VWAP (+session/anchored), Bollinger, ATR, RSI, MACD, Stochastic, volume + volume MA, OBV; indicator templates; per-indicator styling from design tokens". Train window S07-S08, 47 points, area `area/charting-ui`, backend module **M9** `orderflow` (CONSTITUTION.md §3), story domain **IND**.

Two hard constraints shape the whole epic:
1. **One kernel, one result.** US-IND-002's NFR: "shared indicator kernel used by chart, alerts, rule engine and backtest - one implementation, one result." `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 makes the `MetricRegistry` the single named registry behind the rule vocabulary, the alert editor, the journal and the indicator list. E13 therefore does not build a chart-only TA library; it builds the metric kernel plus a worker-side mirror.
2. **Rule-feeding indicators are authoritative in the backend.** `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` open question O4: the rule engine runs server-side and must never depend on a browser, so any indicator referenced by a rule IR is computed authoritatively in the backend and the worker copy is a display-only mirror that must reproduce it bit-for-bit under the parity test (§14). E13 resolves O4 and records the resolution as an ADR.

Depends on E12 (bar builders and series rendering) per `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 `E12 --> E13`, and gates E15 (`E13 --> E15`, layouts persist the indicator stack and sub-pane heights). The order-flow indicators (footprint, profiles, CVD pane, OI/funding/liquidation series) are NOT in E13 - they arrive with E18/E19/E23/E24 in R2 and plug into the API this epic defines.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Goal** - a trader can add any v1 indicator to a chart, tune it live, style it from tokens, save it as a preset, read it from the legend or a screen reader, and reference its value by name from the alert/rule editors, with values identical to the backend's.

- **Runtime**: `IndicatorPlugin` API and worker-hosted runtime in `packages/chart-engine` (`src/plugins/`), incremental `update(lastBar)` with `recompute(range)` fallback, `BarSeries.densify()` handling for gapped series, pane placement (overlay / sub-pane), output buffers rendered via CMP-194 IndicatorOverlay.
- **Backend kernel**: `services/api/orderflow/` (M9) indicator kernel + `MetricDescriptor`/`MetricRegistry` registration for `sma`, `ema`, `wma`, `vwma`, `smma`, `dema`, `tema`, `vwap`, `bollinger`, `keltner`, `donchian`, `atr`, `adx`, `rsi`, `macd`, `stochastic`, `cci`, `williams_r`, `supertrend`, `zigzag`, `ichimoku`, `psar`, `volume`, `volume_ma`, `obv`, `cmf`, `mfi`, `cvd`.
- **Catalogue endpoint**: `GET /api/v1/indicators` (`listIndicators`, `IndicatorDescriptor`) so settings forms render from JSON Schema and adding an indicator needs no frontend release.
- **Presets**: `indicator_presets` table (§3.8.4), `/indicator-presets` CRUD, built-in presets of §10.5, `is_favourite`, `pane_target`.
- **Screens**: SCR-034 indicator library, SCR-035 indicator settings dialog, SCR-036 indicator manager (object tree - also the a11y-complete alternative to canvas manipulation).
- **Components consumed**: CMP-194, CMP-197, CMP-199, CMP-224 plus the atoms/molecules listed per screen in `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`.
- **Stories realised**: US-IND-001 (Must), US-IND-002, US-IND-003, US-IND-004, US-IND-005, US-IND-006, US-IND-007 (Must/Should) and US-IND-008 (Must).

## Out of scope
- Order-flow indicators and panes: footprint (E18), volume/delta/TPO profiles (E19), CVD dedicated pane (E23), OI/funding/liquidations (E24), detectors/regime (E25). E13 only ships the `cvd`/`volume` *classic indicator* forms whose values must later match those panes exactly.
- User-authored indicator scripting - explicitly a non-goal (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §1: "No indicator scripting language (indicators are TypeScript plugins)"); scripting is the P4 scripting epic.
- Alert and rule *editors* themselves (E40 / E35-E37). E13 only guarantees the metric vocabulary and the metric-in-use referential guard.
- Chart templates and workspace persistence of the indicator stack - E15.
- Backtesting use of the kernel - P4.
- Android; any separate admin app; non-Bybit / non-USDT-perp instruments.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The v1 set is complete and correct
  Given the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT fixture symbol-day used by the R1 integration suite
  When every v1 indicator is computed by the backend kernel and by the worker mirror
  Then both agree with the reference implementation to 1e-8 and with each other bit-for-bit

Scenario: A trader tunes an indicator live
  Given EMA(21) is on a 100k-bar chart
  When the period is changed to 34 in SCR-035
  Then the visible window recomputes in <=100 ms, off-screen ranges backfill in the worker, and no chart reload occurs

Scenario: Ten indicators do not break the frame budget
  Given ten indicators are active across the price pane and two sub-panes
  Then the engine benchmark reports >=55 fps and p95 frame time <=16.6 ms on reference hardware in Electron

Scenario: Indicators are operable without a mouse
  Given a keyboard-only user on SCR-036
  Then every indicator can be added, reordered, hidden, configured and removed, and the legend value is announced by the screen reader

Scenario: A metric in use cannot vanish
  Given an armed rule references ema(21, 5m)
  When the trader removes that indicator
  Then removal is blocked with the list of referencing rules and links to disarm or edit them
```

## Technical notes / design
Pipeline: `BarStore` (E12) -> worker `IndicatorHost` -> `OutputBuffers` -> `IndicatorOverlay`/sub-pane render pass. Backend: bars from M8 -> `IndicatorKernel` (M9) -> `MetricRegistry` binding -> memoised per `(symbol, spec_hash, params)` so ten rules on `atr(14)` cost one computation (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7). Determinism rules: no indicator may read wall-clock time; warmup is declared as `warmup_bars` and values before it are `None`, never 0; provisional values (ZigZag's unconfirmed leg) carry `provisional=true` and are excluded from rule evaluation.

## Test plan
Golden-vector unit tests per indicator (fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/`), property-based tests for incremental-vs-full equivalence, cross-language parity tests (Python kernel vs TypeScript mirror), contract tests for `GET /indicators` and `/indicator-presets`, Playwright E2E for add/configure/remove/preset flows in web and Electron, engine FPS benchmark with 10 indicators, axe-core on SCR-034/035/036.

## Security notes
Low-sensitivity data class (market data + user presentation preferences), but three real surfaces: (a) `params_schema` is server-supplied JSON Schema rendered into a form - must not be a rendering-time injection vector; (b) `indicator_presets.params`/`style` are user-controlled JSONB - size- and shape-bounded, RBAC-scoped to the owning user (`workspaces:read`/`write`, scope self); (c) unbounded indicator parameters (period 5000 x many instances) are a client and server CPU-exhaustion vector. STRIDE model in E13-X01.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-036 is the designated accessible equivalent for canvas objects (`role="tree"`, every object reachable and editable by keyboard). Indicator series must be distinguishable without colour - dash patterns vary alongside the token colour (SCR-035). Divergence and Supertrend flips use a glyph plus text label, never colour alone (US-IND-003, US-IND-005). Legend values are exposed in the DOM-mirror a11y layer built by E11.

## Performance notes
Budget #1 (p95 <=16.6 ms frame) and #2 (30 fps floor) are hard gates; §4.3 allocates <=2 ms per frame to profile/CVD/indicator pane redraw. SCR-034: first visible window computed in <=250 ms on a 100k-bar series; SCR-035: parameter edit recomputes the visible window in <=100 ms. US-IND-001 NFR: ten indicators must not drop below 55 fps.

## Observability
Metrics `indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,where}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}`, `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`. Analytics events `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.reordered`, `indicator.visibility_toggled`, `indicator.removed` per SCR-034/035/036. A parity mismatch is logged at ERROR with both values and the bar index.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level AC verified end-to-end on the recorded fixture day, demoed to the Owner.
- [ ] Coverage floors held (>=85% engine/backend, >=80% frontend); zero open P0/P1 bugs in E13 scope.
- [ ] O4 resolved and recorded as an ADR; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core zero violations on SCR-034/035/036 plus a manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass.
- [ ] perf: 10-indicator benchmark wired into the CI engine benchmark as a required check.
- [ ] STRIDE model finalised and findings triaged; Security engineer sign-off.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression and exploratory pass executed and recorded.

## Dependencies
- **E12** bar builders and series rendering - supplies `BarStore`/`BarSeries.densify()` and the series render passes (`E12 --> E13`).
- **E11** chart engine core - plugin host, pane stacking, legend, DOM-mirror a11y layer.
- **E05** design system v0 - tokens, `color.indicator.palette[]`, dialog/drawer primitives.
- Gates **E15** layouts (indicator stack + sub-pane heights persist per layout) and, in R2, E18/E19/E23/E24 which register their series through this plugin API.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Black-box test plan for the indicator framework and v1 set
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires a QA-executed black-box test plan per Story before Done. E13 ships eight stories across three screens, ~28 indicators and a metric-exposure contract; a per-story ad hoc pass would miss the cross-cutting cases (value identity, provisional swings, partial history, ten-indicator load). This ticket writes the plan once, structured by story group, so execution is repeatable and traceable.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Test plan document `qa/plans/e13-indicators.md` with sections per story group: framework/UI (US-IND-001), MA family (US-IND-002), oscillators & sub-panes (US-IND-003), volatility & bands (US-IND-004), trend tools (US-IND-005), volume-based (US-IND-006), VWAP (US-IND-007), metric exposure (US-IND-008).
- Per section: preconditions, fixtures used, step-by-step cases covering happy path, each documented edge case and each failure mode, and expected results phrased so a pass/fail is unambiguous.
- A traceability table mapping every Gherkin scenario in the eight stories to at least one test case id, so gaps are visible rather than assumed away.
- Cross-cutting case set that no single story owns:
  - value identity (legend value == metric registry value == backend kernel value) for ATR, EMA and CVD;
  - a provisional Zig Zag swing is never selectable in an alert/rule picker;
  - partial CVD history on a symbol whose recording started mid-day;
  - ten indicators across three panes (frame budget, legend overflow, chip overflow);
  - preset save/apply/import round-trip including a hostile `WorkspaceBundle` payload;
  - symbol and timeframe switch with a full indicator stack loaded;
  - offline/backend-unreachable behaviour of SCR-034 and of `compute: server` indicators.
- Test data definition: which recorded Bybit fixture symbol-days are used (a normal day, a gap day, a partial-recording day) and how to load them.

## Out of scope
- Automated E2E implementation (E13-Q02), performance scripts (E13-Q03), the a11y audit (E13-Q04) and the parity regression pack (E13-Q05) - this plan references them rather than duplicating them.
- Exploratory charters (E13-Q06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every acceptance scenario is covered
  When the traceability table is reviewed against docs/plan/11-user-stories.md §7
  Then every Gherkin scenario in US-IND-001..008 maps to at least one test case, and any deliberate gap is listed with a reason and an owner

Scenario: A case is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer unfamiliar with E13 picks any case
  Then preconditions, fixture, steps and expected result are sufficient to execute and judge it without asking a developer

Scenario: Failure modes are first-class
  Then each story section contains at least one failure case (catalogue fetch failure, insufficient history, unrecorded symbol, blocked removal, invalid parameter) with its expected user-visible behaviour

Scenario: The plan is versioned with the feature
  Given a story's acceptance criteria change during implementation
  Then the plan is updated in the same PR cycle and the traceability table stays green
```

## Technical notes / design
The plan follows the structure in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` for black-box plans and reuses the fixture naming convention from the R1 integration suite so QA and engineering point at the same data. Cases are numbered `E13-TC-nnn` and referenced by the E2E tests in E13-Q02 so automation and manual execution share ids.

## Test plan
Self-referential: the plan is dry-run against an early build of E13-S01/S02 to confirm the cases are executable, and revised before the bulk of execution.

## Security notes
The plan includes the abuse-adjacent black-box cases from E13-X01 that do not need a security engineer to execute: cross-user preset access via the UI, hostile bundle import, and an out-of-range parameter entered directly.

## Accessibility notes
The plan references the E13-D05 accessibility acceptance script rather than restating it, so there is one script and it cannot drift.

## Performance notes
The ten-indicator case in the plan states the expected fps floor (>=55 fps per US-IND-001 NFR) and how to observe it, so manual execution can flag a regression before the automated benchmark run.

## Observability
Cases state which analytics/metric events should be emitted (`indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total`) so missing telemetry is caught as a defect.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed to the repo and wired into CI where automatable.
- [ ] Executed at least once against a build; results recorded on the ticket with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Defects filed with repro steps, severity, environment and the failing scenario linked.
- [ ] Reviewed by the SDET lead; coverage of the story's acceptance criteria demonstrated by a traceability table.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted.

## Dependencies
E13-D06 (signed-off design defines expected behaviour and copy). Stories are executed against as they land.

## Branch
`chore/e13-qa-plan` (docs only).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §7 IND (US-IND-001..US-IND-008)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-034, SCR-035, SCR-036
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-194, CMP-195, CMP-197, CMP-199, CMP-224
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` rows US-IND-001..008

- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.4 `indicator_presets`, §10.5

title: Add, configure and remove indicators from the chart
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-001** (Must): "As a trader, I want to add indicators with editable parameters and styles, so that my chart reflects my method." This is the shell every other IND story plugs into - without it the v1 indicator set has no way onto a chart. It builds the three catalogued screens SCR-034 (indicator library), SCR-035 (indicator settings dialog) and SCR-036 (indicator manager / object tree), against the E13-D06 handoff pack.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-034 Indicator library** (`apps/web/src/features/indicators/`): modal rendering the catalogue from `GET /api/v1/indicators`, grouped Overlay / Sub-pane / Order-flow, fuzzy search (CMP-054 SearchBox + CMP-213 FuzzyList), category tabs (CMP-042), per-entry card (CMP-050) with preview thumbnail, "requires recorded history" marking for `compute: server` descriptors, empty-search state (CMP-026), favourites/recents from `indicator_presets.is_favourite`, and the "already present - add second instance" affordance.
- **SCR-035 Indicator settings dialog**: Inputs / Style / Visibility / Scale / Alerts tabs; the Inputs form is generated from the descriptor's `params_schema` (CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection); Style tab binds `color.indicator.palette[]` tokens and dash patterns via CMP-031 ColorSwatch; Scale tab offers own scale / merged / pinned right; live preview (CMP-228 PreviewTile); validation "Period must be between 1 and 5000."; "save as default for this indicator" writing an `indicator_presets` row; reset; Alerts tab links to SCR-091.
- **SCR-036 Indicator manager**: drawer (CMP-046) with `role="tree"` over panes -> indicators -> drawings -> alerts; per-item visibility, lock, rename, reorder (drag plus keyboard alternative) and delete; multi-select and bulk actions; empty state.
- **Legend and chips**: CMP-199 ChartLegend entries and the CMP-224 IndicatorChips row with current value, visibility toggle, settings and remove, each a separately named button.
- Wiring to the E13-T01 runtime: add -> `addIndicator(plugin, params)`, parameter change -> `recompute(range)`, remove -> disposal; undo for removal per US-IND-001.
- Preset consumption: apply a preset on add; "save as default"; built-in presets from §10.5 offered first.

## Out of scope
- The indicator implementations themselves (E13-S02..S07) - this story ships with SMA/EMA from S02 as the smoke case and the rest arrive behind it.
- Alert editor internals (E40); chart templates and layout persistence of the stack (E15); the metric-in-use removal guard (E13-S08 adds the blocking behaviour on top of this story's removal flow).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Add
  When I add EMA(21) from the indicator picker
  Then it renders in the price pane with a legend entry showing the parameter and current value

Scenario: Reconfigure
  Given EMA(21) is on the chart
  When I change the length to 34
  Then the series recomputes incrementally and the legend updates without a chart reload, and the visible window repaints within 100 ms

Scenario: Remove
  When I remove it
  Then it disappears from the pane, the legend and the template diff, with undo available

Scenario: Second instance
  Given EMA(21) is already present
  When I add EMA from the library again
  Then I am offered "Add second instance", the new instance takes the next palette slot, and the two legend entries are distinguishable by parameters and colour

Scenario: The catalogue cannot be loaded
  Given GET /api/v1/indicators fails
  Then SCR-034 shows an error state with a retry action, no partial list is presented as complete, and previously added indicators keep rendering

Scenario: Ten indicators keep the frame budget
  Given ten indicators are active
  Then the engine benchmark reports >=55 fps and no frame exceeds the 30 fps floor

Scenario: Keyboard only
  Given I never touch the mouse
  Then I can open the library, search, add an indicator, open its settings, change a parameter, toggle visibility, reorder it and remove it, with focus always visible and returned to a sensible element on dialog close
```

## Technical notes / design
Form generation: the Inputs tab is a JSON-Schema-driven renderer restricted to an enumerated control set (number, integer, enum select, boolean, colour token, source-series select). It must never render free-form HTML or markdown - the schema is server-authored but the renderer stays conservative so the seam cannot become an injection vector. Parameter edits are debounced (the spec value from E13-D04) and recompute the visible window first, then backfill off-screen ranges in the worker. Instance identity uses the stable key from E13-T01 (`sha1(indicatorId + canonical(params) + sourceSeriesId)`), so a reload restores the same key, the same palette slot and the same metric name. Removal emits an undoable command onto the chart's command stack.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): schema-driven form rendering for each control type, validation messages, preset application, undo of removal, palette-slot assignment determinism. Integration: add/configure/remove against a stubbed engine; catalogue fetch failure; preset save round-trip. E2E (Playwright, web and Electron): the US-IND-001 three scenarios plus second-instance and keyboard-only paths. Perf: the ten-indicator benchmark (harness owned by E13-Q03). A11y: axe-core on all three screens; NVDA spot check of the tree. Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. Additionally: the settings form must treat `params_schema` as data, not code - no `eval`, no dynamic component resolution by name from the payload. Preset writes go through the T03 endpoints which enforce owner scope, so the UI never assumes client-side authorization.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-036 is the designated accessible equivalent for canvas objects and must satisfy the full keyboard contract from E13-D05: arrow navigation in the tree, Enter to open settings, Space to toggle visibility, Delete to remove, and a documented keyboard alternative to drag-reorder. SCR-034's list is a listbox whose entries announce their pane target. SCR-035's colour pickers expose token names. Series must be distinguishable without colour: each gets a distinct dash pattern from the E13-D04 ladder. State (warming up, provisional, errored) is stated in text in the legend, never by colour alone. Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036.

## Performance notes
Budgets: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars (SCR-034); parameter re-tune of the visible window <=100 ms (SCR-035); ten active indicators must not drop the scene below 55 fps (US-IND-001 NFR) and never below the 30 fps floor (budget #2). SCR-036 tree operations are O(1) against the render list and never force a full chart rebuild (catalogue requirement).

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}` (ERROR log with both values and bar index on any mismatch), `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`; analytics `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`. SCR-036 additionally emits `indicator.reordered` and `indicator.visibility_toggled`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass via automated tests that name the scenario.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% on `packages/chart-engine` / `services/api/orderflow`, >=80% on `apps/web` for new/changed lines.
- [ ] Docs updated (`22-api-openapi.yaml` / `24-internal-schemas.md` / `14-screens-catalogue.md` as touched); changelog fragment added.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on touched screens; keyboard-only path verified; screen-reader spot check recorded.
- [ ] perf: engine benchmark re-run, no >10% regression against budget #1; the story's own budget measured.
- [ ] design-qa: compared against the E13-D03/D04 spec; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario; demoed at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue, 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; feature-flag state recorded.

## Dependencies
E13-T01 (runtime), E13-T02 (catalogue endpoint + descriptors), E13-T03 (presets), E13-D06 (signed-off design, required by the design-ahead rule). E11 supplies panes, legend and the a11y mirror; E05 supplies the dialog/drawer primitives.


**Design-ahead ledger (DoR §3.1).** The E13 design chain is scheduled so the signed-off handoff pack `E13-D06` reaches Done in **Sprint 05**: D01 (S02) -> D02 (S03) -> D03/D04/D05 (S04) -> D06 (S05). The first consuming frontend stories (E13-S01, E13-S02) start in **Sprint 07**, which is **2 full sprints** after design Done, so the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule is satisfied on its own terms and **no Architect/CDO waiver is required** for E13-S01, E13-S02, E13-S03, E13-S04, E13-S06, E13-S07 or E13-S08. Sprint 06 is deliberately left clear of E13 design work as the buffer sprint; if any design ticket slips into Sprint 06, the pack is still Done one sprint before Sprint 07 and a waiver MUST then be recorded on every consuming story before it enters Ready.
## Branch
`feat/e13-indicators-ui`; split as library modal / settings dialog / object tree to keep each PR <=400 LOC.

title: Moving-average family indicators (SMA, EMA, WMA, VWMA, SMMA, DEMA, TEMA, ribbon)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-002** (Must for SMA/EMA, Should for WMA/VWMA/SMMA/DEMA/TEMA and the MA ribbon/cross). Its NFR is the epic's central constraint: "shared indicator kernel used by chart, alerts, rule engine and backtest - one implementation, one result." `ema` and `sma` are already named metrics in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2, so this story extends the existing registry entries rather than creating parallel ones. It is also the first real exercise of the E13-T01/T02 seam, which is why it lands before the other indicator stories.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Worker plugins and backend kernel functions for `sma`, `ema`, `wma`, `vwma`, `smma` (Wilder/running MA), `dema`, `tema`, each with `length` and `source` (`close` | `open` | `high` | `low` | `hl2` | `hlc3` | `ohlc4`) parameters and an `offset` parameter.
- **MA ribbon**: one instance producing N output series (default 5 lengths) rendered as a single legend entry with an expandable list (CMP-199 variant from E13-D04).
- **MA cross**: a derived boolean/marker output (fast crosses slow) exposed as a metric so alerts and rules can reference it.
- `MetricDescriptor` registration for each: unit `price`, value_type `number`, inputs `bars`, cadence `on_bar_close`, confidence `exact`, `warmup_bars = length` (and the composed warmup for DEMA/TEMA), `nullable_when` stating exactly when the value is None.
- Golden-vector fixtures per MA type over the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT fixture symbol-day, including a day with a gap so densification is exercised.
- Insufficient-history behaviour: render from the first valid bar and state in the legend how many more bars are needed.

## Out of scope
- Oscillators (S03), bands (S04), trend tools (S05), volume-based (S06), VWAP (S07) - VWAP is its own story because it shares the anchored-VWAP drawing kernel.
- Alert/rule editor UI; the metric exposure *guarantees* are S08.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: SMA/EMA
  Given the recorded fixture symbol-day
  Then values match reference implementations to 1e-8 on the test fixtures, for both the backend kernel and the worker mirror

Scenario: Ribbon
  When I add an MA ribbon of 5 lengths
  Then it renders as one legend entry with an expandable list, and the five series are distinguishable without colour

Scenario: Insufficient history
  Given fewer bars than the period exist
  Then the indicator renders only from the first valid bar and states how many bars are still needed

Scenario: Source selection changes the result
  Given SMA(20) on close and a second instance on hl2
  Then the two instances produce different series, carry different metric keys, and are separately labelled in the legend

Scenario: Incremental equals full
  Given any MA type over a generated 100k-bar series
  When the series is built by appending bars one at a time
  Then every value equals the full recomputation, asserted by a property-based test
```

## Technical notes / design
Each indicator is a plugin against the E13-T01 `IndicatorPlugin` interface (<=150 lines per `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12) and a matching `MetricDescriptor` registration in the E13-T02 backend kernel (M9). The two implementations are held together by shared golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` and the parity assertion established by E13-K01. Every indicator declares `warmup_bars`; values before warmup are absent, never zero. No indicator reads wall-clock time. Styling comes from `color.indicator.palette[]` and the dash ladder defined by E13-D04 - never a hard-coded colour. Specific correctness traps to assert in tests: EMA seeding (first value is an SMA of the first `length` bars, not the first close - the fixture pins this); SMMA is Wilder smoothing (`alpha = 1/n`), distinct from EMA (`alpha = 2/(n+1)`) and the fixture discriminates them; DEMA/TEMA warmup composes (`2n-1` / `3n-2`); VWMA needs volume and is undefined for a synthetic densified bar with volume 0 - such bars carry the previous value forward with a stated rule rather than dividing by zero.

## Test plan
Unit: golden vectors per MA type and per source; EMA seeding; SMMA-vs-EMA discrimination; DEMA/TEMA warmup; VWMA zero-volume rule. Property-based: incremental equals full; offset shifts without recomputation error. Parity: Python kernel vs TypeScript mirror over the fixture day within the E13-K01 tolerance. Integration: ribbon rendering with five outputs from one instance. Coverage >=85% engine/backend.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model.

## Accessibility notes
Series must be distinguishable without colour: each gets a distinct dash pattern from the E13-D04 ladder. State (warming up, provisional, errored) is stated in text in the legend, never by colour alone. Legend values and per-instance names are published into the E11 DOM-mirror layer with the announcement cadence set by E13-D05. Every control introduced is reachable and operable from SCR-036. The ribbon's expandable legend entry is a disclosure control with a proper name and expanded state, not a hover-only affordance.

## Performance notes
Budgets: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars (SCR-034); parameter re-tune of the visible window <=100 ms (SCR-035); ten active indicators must not drop the scene below 55 fps (US-IND-001 NFR) and never below the 30 fps floor (budget #2). A ribbon of 5 lengths counts as 5 series for the draw-call budget; it must still be a single instanced line pass per the `26-chart-engine-design.md` draw-call table.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_parity_mismatch_total{indicator}` (ERROR log with both values and bar index on any mismatch), `indicator_active_instances{indicator}`; analytics `indicator.added`, `indicator.settings_changed`, `indicator.removed`.
