title: Indicator plugin API and worker-hosted runtime in packages/chart-engine
body:
## Context
The engine design already fixes the contract (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12): "Indicator plugin - pure computation over a `BarStore` producing one or more output series; runs in the worker; declares inputs, parameters, outputs, pane placement and default styling. Computation is incremental (`update(lastBar)`) with a `recompute(range)` fallback", and each built-in must be "<= 150 lines against the plugin API". This task builds that runtime so that every v1 indicator story (S02..S07) is a small plugin, and so that R2's order-flow series register through the same seam instead of forking the render path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/src/plugins/indicator/` implementing the published interface verbatim:
  `IndicatorPlugin { readonly id; readonly params: ParamSpec[]; readonly outputs: OutputSpec[]; compute(bars, params, out); update(bars, params, out, from); }`
- `IndicatorHost` running in the engine worker: registration, instance lifecycle (`addIndicator(plugin, params) -> IndicatorHandle` per the published `ChartApi`), parameter change, disposal, and deterministic instance ids stable across sessions (key, not display name - US-IND-008 NFR).
- `OutputBuffers`: typed-array output allocation and growth, `NaN`/`null` semantics for the warmup region (values before `warmup_bars` are absent, never 0), and the `provisional` flag channel for unconfirmed values.
- Incremental scheduling: `update()` on bar close; `recompute(range)` on parameter change, source change, symbol/timeframe switch, historical backfill prepend, and the late-trade `amended=True` bar re-emit path from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §5.
- Gap handling: consume `BarSeries.densify()` for indicators that need a continuous index; disable time-based indicators over renko series with the explanatory tooltip the internal-schemas doc requires.
- Render binding: outputs drawn through CMP-194 IndicatorOverlay (line/stepped/area/band/histogram) and CMP-195 AnnotationMarker (flips, pivots), with pane placement `price` | `sub` | `both` honoured and CMP-199 ChartLegend values fed per crosshair position.
- Back-pressure/degradation: participate in the §4.2 degradation ladder - "coalesce big-trade-bubble/CVD/indicator pane redraws to every 2nd frame" - as a first-class, tested behaviour.
- A conformance test kit any plugin author runs (`assertPluginConforms`) covering incremental-vs-full equivalence, warmup, gap handling and disposal-leak checks.

## Out of scope
- The indicators themselves (S02..S07) and the backend kernel (T02).
- Presets persistence (T03) and the settings UI (S01).
- WebGPU backend; user-authored scripting (explicit non-goals in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Incremental equals full
  Given any registered plugin and a 100k-bar series
  When the series is computed fully and then recomputed by appending bars one at a time through update()
  Then every output value is identical, verified by a property-based test over randomly generated bar series

Scenario: Warmup is absent, not zero
  Given an indicator with warmup_bars = 34 and 20 loaded bars
  Then no output value is emitted, the legend states how many more bars are needed, and no zero-valued series is drawn

Scenario: A parameter change recomputes the visible window first
  Given EMA(21) on a 100k-bar chart
  When the period changes to 34
  Then the visible window is recomputed and painted within 100 ms and the off-screen ranges backfill afterwards in the worker without blocking a frame

Scenario: Degradation sheds frequency, not correctness
  Given the engine is under the §4.2 worst-case load
  Then indicator pane redraws coalesce to every second frame and the computed values remain complete and correct

Scenario: A misbehaving plugin cannot take down the chart
  Given a plugin that throws inside compute()
  Then the instance enters an errored state, the error is stated in text in the legend, other indicators keep rendering, and the chart does not crash
```

## Technical notes / design
The host owns all buffers; plugins write into provided `OutputBuffers` and never allocate per-update - this is what keeps the per-frame allocation cost off the GC path. Recompute is range-scoped and chunked across frames with a stated settling allowance (<=3 frames for a hard jump, matching `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.1's `Home`/`End` allowance). Instance identity: `key = sha1(indicatorId + canonical(params) + sourceSeriesId)` truncated - stable across sessions and the same key the metric exposure in S08 uses. No plugin may read wall-clock time; determinism is asserted by replaying the same bars twice and comparing.

## Test plan
Unit: buffer growth, warmup boundaries, disposal, errored-instance isolation, renko/time-indicator guard. Property-based: incremental-vs-full equivalence over generated series including gaps, single-bar days and late amendments. Perf: micro-benchmark of `update()` at 1/10/100 instances; the 10-indicator scene benchmark lives in E13-Q03. Coverage target >=85% on the package.

## Security notes
Plugins are first-party TypeScript compiled into the bundle - there is no dynamic code loading and none must be introduced (scripting is explicitly out of scope). Parameter values arriving from persisted presets are validated against `ParamSpec` bounds before reaching a plugin, so a tampered preset cannot drive an unbounded loop (see E13-X01 CPU-exhaustion threat).

## Accessibility notes
The host publishes per-instance name, parameters, current value and state (warming up / provisional / errored) into the E11 DOM-mirror a11y layer so the legend is readable by a screen reader; announcement cadence is throttled per E13-D05.

## Performance notes
Budget: indicator contribution to a frame <=2 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3); first visible window on add <=250 ms at 100k bars; parameter re-tune visible window <=100 ms. Memory: indicators share the <=8 MB "profile / indicators / drawings" allocation in the engine memory table - the host enforces a ceiling and sheds the oldest off-screen recompute buffers first.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator,phase=full|incremental}`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason}`, `indicator_instance_errors_total{indicator}`, `indicator_active_instances{indicator}` exported through the engine's existing stats channel.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified with attached test output or measurement.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met on the touched package (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend).
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated where a design decision was made.

## Dependencies
E13-K01 fixes which indicators the worker owns. E11 supplies the scene graph, pane stacking, worker plumbing and DOM-mirror layer; E12 supplies `BarStore`/`BarSeries.densify()` and the amended-bar path.

## Branch
`feat/e13-indicators-plugin-runtime`; split into 2-3 PRs (interface + host, buffers + scheduling, render binding) to stay <=400 LOC each.

body:
## Context
US-IND-002's NFR is the whole point of this task: "shared indicator kernel used by chart, alerts, rule engine and backtest - one implementation, one result." `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 says the `MetricRegistry` "is a single named registry ... This is what makes the rule vocabulary and the indicator list the same list", and `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` O4 makes the backend authoritative for any indicator a rule can reference. This task builds the authoritative kernel in module **M9** (`services/api/orderflow/`, CONSTITUTION.md §3) and the catalogue endpoint the UI renders its forms from.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/orderflow/indicators/` kernel: pure functions over a bar window, incremental state objects with `snapshot()`/`restore()` so a restart or a replay seek resumes without recomputing a day, memoised per `(symbol, spec_hash, params)` so "ten rules referencing `atr(14)` cost one computation" (`24-internal-schemas.md` §7).
- `MetricDescriptor` registration for every v1 indicator with the fields the schema mandates: `name`, `title`, `unit`, `value_type`, `scope`, `inputs`, `params`, `warmup_bars`, `cadence`, `nullable_when`, `deterministic`, `confidence`. All v1 TA indicators are `confidence="exact"` except heuristic-flavoured outputs (divergence flags) which are `"estimated"`.
- Extend the §7.2 catalogue entries that already exist (`atr`, `ema`, `sma`, `rsi`, `adx`, `swing_high`/`swing_low`, `realized_vol`, `parkinson_vol`, `garman_klass_vol`, `cvd`, `delta`) rather than duplicating them, and add the missing v1 names (`wma`, `vwma`, `smma`, `dema`, `tema`, `vwap`, `bollinger`, `keltner`, `donchian`, `macd`, `stochastic`, `cci`, `williams_r`, `supertrend`, `zigzag`, `ichimoku`, `psar`, `volume`, `volume_ma`, `obv`, `cmf`, `mfi`).
- `GET /api/v1/indicators` implementing `listIndicators` exactly as specified: returns `IndicatorDescriptor` items with `id`, `name`, `category` (trend|momentum|volatility|volume|orderflow), `pane` (price|sub|both), `compute` (client_worker|server per the E13-K01 assignment table), `estimated`, `params_schema` (JSON Schema the settings form renders from), `defaults`. RBAC `marketdata:read`, scope none.
- Server-computed indicator delivery: for `compute: server` descriptors, values are published on the existing market-data WS as a derived series keyed by the same instance key the engine uses (topic and framing per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, reusing E17's snapshot+delta contract - no new transport).
- Golden-vector fixtures in `tests/fixtures/indicators/` (input bars + expected outputs per indicator) that both the Python kernel and the TypeScript mirror consume - this is the mechanism that makes "one result" testable.

## Out of scope
- Order-flow metrics that read `orderflow_metrics` (footprint/profile/CVD pane/OI/funding) - E18/E19/E23/E24 register through this same kernel later.
- The rule engine and alert evaluation themselves (E35/E40) - this task only publishes the vocabulary.
- Preset persistence (T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Values match a reference implementation
  Given the recorded Bybit BTCUSDT fixture symbol-day
  When each v1 indicator is computed by the kernel
  Then every value matches the reference implementation to 1e-8 (US-IND-002)

Scenario: One computation serves many consumers
  Given ten registered consumers all requesting atr(14) for the same symbol and bar spec
  Then the kernel computes it once per cadence and serves the memoised value, verified by a call-count assertion

Scenario: The catalogue drives the form
  When GET /api/v1/indicators is called
  Then every v1 indicator is returned with a valid JSON Schema params_schema, and adding a new indicator to the registry changes the response with no frontend change required

Scenario: Warmup is honoured
  Given atr(14) with 10 bars of history
  Then the value is None, nullable_when states exactly why, and no zero is emitted

Scenario: A bar is amended late
  Given a late trade re-emits a closed bar with amended=True
  Then the affected indicator values are recomputed from that bar forward and republished, and downstream consumers see the corrected series
```

## Technical notes / design
Constraint C3 (`24-internal-schemas.md` §1): analytics may use `float`/`numpy` inside engines, but any value crossing into OMS, journal or audit is converted via `Decimal(str(x)).quantize(...)` at the boundary - the kernel is float-internal, the boundary is explicit and tested. Wilder-smoothed indicators (ATR, ADX, RSI) must use Wilder smoothing, not EMA with alpha=1/n, and the fixture asserts it. VWAP uses the same incremental kernel as the anchored-VWAP drawing (US-IND-007 NFR, shared with US-DRAW-005). `spec_hash` is the canonical hash of `(indicator_id, params, bar_spec, source)` and is the same identity the engine's instance key derives from, so cache, metric name and UI instance agree.

## Test plan
Unit: golden vectors per indicator; Wilder-vs-EMA discrimination tests; warmup boundaries; `snapshot()`/`restore()` round-trip mid-series. Property-based: incremental equals full over generated series. Contract: `GET /indicators` validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` in the OpenAPI contract suite; every `params_schema` is itself validated as legal JSON Schema. Integration: kernel over the recorded Bybit fixture day including a gap and a late amendment. Coverage >=85% on M9.

## Security notes
`GET /indicators` is authenticated and RBAC-gated (`marketdata:read`) though the data is non-sensitive. The real surface is resource exhaustion: `compute: server` indicators let an authenticated user schedule backend work by adding chart instances - the kernel enforces a per-user cap on distinct `spec_hash` subscriptions and a parameter-bound check (period 1..5000 per SCR-035 validation) before admitting a computation. `params_schema` is server-authored static metadata, never echoed user input.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend). The `title`, `unit` and `nullable_when` fields exist so the UI can produce meaningful screen-reader text rather than raw ids - populate them for every indicator.

## Performance notes
Per-bar incremental update for the full v1 set on one symbol must stay within the ingestion stage budget (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §6.1, backend-internal <=20 ms p95 for the fan-out path). Memoisation is measured: a benchmark asserts that N consumers of the same spec cost O(1) computations.

## Observability
`indicator_compute_seconds{indicator}`, `indicator_cache_hits_total` / `..._misses_total`, `indicator_recompute_total{reason=amended|param_change|backfill}`, `indicator_subscriptions{user}`. Errors logged with symbol, spec_hash and bar index.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified with attached test output or measurement.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met on the touched package (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend).
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated where a design decision was made.
- [ ] SAST/SCA clean or triaged.
- [ ] perf benchmark recorded where labelled `perf`.
- [ ] QA verification recorded where the change is user-observable.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with required approvals/checks.

## Dependencies
E13-K01 assignment table; E12 bar builders (M8) supply the bars; E17 supplies the WS transport used to publish `server`-computed series.

## Branch
`feat/e13-indicator-kernel`; PRs: kernel + descriptors, catalogue endpoint, WS publication.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §7 IND (US-IND-001..US-IND-008)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-034, SCR-035, SCR-036

- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `GET /indicators` (`listIndicators`, `IndicatorDescriptor`), `/indicator-presets` CRUD
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.4 `indicator_presets`, §10.5 built-in presets, migration `0011_workspace`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 `MetricDescriptor` / `MetricRegistry` / §7.2 catalogue
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12 plugin API, `IndicatorPlugin`, §14 parity, open question O4
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.6 MetricRegistry; CONSTITUTION.md §3 module M9 `orderflow`
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1/#2, §4.3
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2/§5.3/§11.1

title: Indicator presets: migration, CRUD endpoints and built-in seed data
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.4 already specifies the `indicator_presets` table and §10.5 lists the built-in presets to seed (`ema(9)`, `ema(21)`, `ema(50)`, `ema(200)`, `vwap(session)`, `vwap(session, ±1σ, ±2σ)`, `atr(14)`, `cvd(session reset)`, `cvd(never reset)`, `delta(bar)`, ...). `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already specifies `/indicator-presets` GET/POST and `/indicator-presets/{presetId}` PUT/DELETE with `IndicatorPreset`/`IndicatorPresetInput`. This task implements them so US-IND-001's "save as default for this indicator" control on SCR-035 and SCR-034's favourites/recents have a backing store.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Migration in `0011_workspace` (or a follow-on migration if `0011` has already shipped) creating `indicator_presets` exactly as specified, including `ux_ip_name` (unique per owner+code+lower(name) where not deleted) and `ix_ip_fav`, and the `ip_target` / `ip_code` check constraints.
- Seeding of the §10.5 built-in presets with `owner_user_id = NULL`, `is_builtin = true`; the seed is idempotent and re-runnable.
- `GET /api/v1/indicator-presets` (`listIndicatorPresets`), `POST` (`createIndicatorPreset`), `PUT /{presetId}` (`updateIndicatorPreset`), `DELETE /{presetId}` (`deleteIndicatorPreset`) - soft delete via `deleted_at`, never a hard delete.
- Validation: `params` validated against the indicator's `params_schema` from T02 before persistence; `style` validated against the closed token-name list from E13-D04; `pane_target` in (`overlay`,`subpane`); size caps on both JSONB columns.
- Authorization: a user may read built-ins plus their own presets and may only mutate their own; built-ins are immutable (a "customise" action copies to a user-owned row). RBAC `workspaces:read` / `workspaces:write`, scope self.
- `WorkspaceBundle.indicator_presets` export/import path honoured (the bundle schema already carries `IndicatorPresetInput[]`) - import is credential-free and re-validated, never trusted.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-034/035 UI that consumes these (E13-S01).
- Chart templates and workspace persistence of the indicator stack (E15).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Built-ins are present and immutable
  Given a fresh database
  When the seed runs and a user attempts to PUT a built-in preset
  Then all presets from docs/plan/21-database-schema.md §10.5 exist with is_builtin=true and the mutation is rejected with 403

Scenario: Cross-user access is denied
  Given user A owns a preset
  When user B requests, updates or deletes it
  Then the response is 404 (not 403, so existence is not disclosed) and an authorization-denied event is recorded

Scenario: Invalid params are rejected at the boundary
  When a preset is created with a period of 0 or 10000 for an indicator whose params_schema bounds it to 1..5000
  Then the API returns 422 with the offending field named and nothing is persisted

Scenario: Names are unique per user and indicator
  Given user A already has an ema preset named "Fast"
  When they create another ema preset named "fast"
  Then the request is rejected by the ux_ip_name constraint with a clear message, and the existing preset is untouched

Scenario: Deletion is reversible at the data layer
  When a preset is deleted
  Then deleted_at is set, the row remains, and it no longer appears in list responses
```

## Technical notes / design
Style validation is the reason the token list must be closed: persisting arbitrary strings into `style` and later feeding them to the renderer would be an injection seam. JSONB size caps (params <=4 KB, style <=4 KB) prevent a storage-abuse vector. The `coalesce(owner_user_id, '000...'::uuid)` in the unique index means built-ins share a namespace - the seed must not collide with it.

## Test plan
Unit: validation, authorization matrix (owner/manager/viewer x own/other/built-in), soft-delete semantics. Migration test: up/down against a seeded database, plus the idempotent re-seed. Contract: all four operations validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: create -> list -> update -> delete -> export bundle -> import bundle round-trip. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: broken object-level authorization (mitigated by the 404-on-foreign-object rule and a test matrix), stored-payload abuse via JSONB (size caps + schema validation), and import of a hostile `WorkspaceBundle` (re-validated on import, `is_builtin` and `owner_user_id` never honoured from the payload). Data classification: user preference data, not secrets - but the RBAC scope is still `self` and is asserted by test.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (API). Error messages must be human-readable strings suitable for direct display in SCR-035's inline validation.

## Performance notes
Preset lists are small (tens of rows); a single indexed query per user. No budget risk; the only perf note is that the seed runs at migration time, not on every boot.

## Observability
Audit/analytics events on create/update/delete with `{indicator_code, preset_id}`; metric `indicator_presets_total{builtin}`; authorization denials logged with actor, target and reason.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified with attached test output or measurement.
- [ ] Coverage threshold met on the touched package (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend).
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated where a design decision was made.
- [ ] SAST/SCA clean or triaged.
- [ ] perf benchmark recorded where labelled `perf`.
- [ ] QA verification recorded where the change is user-observable.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with required approvals/checks.

## Dependencies
E13-T02 supplies `params_schema` for validation; E13-D04 supplies the closed style-token list; E09 supplies auth/RBAC.

## Branch

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §7 IND (US-IND-001..US-IND-008)

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for the indicator framework
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 require a STRIDE threat model per Epic. E13 looks low-risk (market data and presentation preferences) but has four real surfaces: a server-supplied JSON Schema rendered into a form, user-controlled JSONB persisted as preset params and styles, authenticated users scheduling backend computation via `compute: server` indicators, and an integrity path where ATR feeds `sl_offset_unit="atr"` stop sizing and Zig Zag swings could feed structure-based trailing stops. The last of those makes an "indicators are just cosmetics" assumption dangerous.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE model document `docs/security/threat-models/e13-indicators.md` covering the data flows: browser <-> `GET /indicators`, browser <-> `/indicator-presets`, kernel -> MetricRegistry -> rule/alert consumers, worker mirror -> display, and `WorkspaceBundle` import.
- Per-element STRIDE enumeration with at least these threats analysed and dispositioned:
  - **Spoofing/Elevation**: reading or mutating another user's presets (broken object-level authorization); built-in presets mutated by a non-owner.
  - **Tampering**: a hand-edited preset or imported bundle carrying out-of-range params, an unknown `indicator_code`, a style value that is not an enumerated token, or `is_builtin: true`; a provisional Zig Zag swing reaching a rule; a worker-computed (display-only) value being used where the authoritative kernel value is required - specifically for ATR-based stop offsets.
  - **Repudiation**: preset and indicator changes without audit/analytics events.
  - **Information disclosure**: the E13-S08 referencing-objects list leaking another user's rule or alert names; error messages echoing internal paths.
  - **Denial of service**: parameter-driven CPU exhaustion (period 5000 x many instances) in the worker and in the backend kernel; unbounded `compute: server` subscriptions per user; unbounded sub-pane creation; oversized JSONB in `params`/`style`; an unbounded historical backfill triggered by a far-past `custom_ts` VWAP anchor.
- **Abuse cases** written as executable statements handed to E13-Q06 (black-box) and E13-X02 (verified): each with a concrete request/action, the expected rejection, and the observable evidence.
- Control recommendations mapped to owning tickets (T02 caps and param bounds, T03 authorization and validation, S05 provisional exclusion, S08 server-side guard and filtered listing) - each either already in scope or filed as a new ticket.
- Data classification statement: market data (public), presentation preferences (user-private), and the note that indicator values become *safety-relevant* the moment a rule or a stop offset consumes them.

## Out of scope
- The rule engine's own threat model (E35) and the OMS/fan-out model (E29/E34) - this model hands off the metric-integrity boundary to them explicitly.
- Penetration testing (E43, pre-R4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every data flow is analysed
  Then each of the five enumerated data flows has a STRIDE row per category with either a threat and a control or an explicit "not applicable" with a reason

Scenario: The safety-relevant path is called out
  Then the model states explicitly that ATR feeds sl_offset_unit="atr" per-account profiles and that a display-only worker value must never be the source for a stop offset, with the control and its owning test named

Scenario: Abuse cases are executable
  Given the abuse-case list is handed to QA
  Then each case states the exact action, the expected rejection and how to observe it, with no interpretation required

Scenario: Every control has an owner
  Then each recommended control maps to an existing E13 ticket or a newly filed ticket, and no control is left as an unassigned recommendation
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the STRIDE-per-element method over a DFD drawn in mermaid inside the model document. Reuse the control vocabulary from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` so findings map onto the existing SR-nnn requirement ids where they apply. The DoS analysis should use the measured numbers from E13-K01/Q03 rather than guessing at cost.

## Test plan
The model's abuse cases are the test plan; verification is E13-X02 plus the QA charter in E13-Q06. The model itself is reviewed by the Architect and the chart-engine lead as well as the Security engineer.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security artefact for E13 and supplies the Epic DoD's "STRIDE model finalized, findings triaged" evidence.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
DoS controls (parameter bounds, instance caps, JSONB size caps) must be set from the measured costs in E13-K01/E13-Q03 so limits are defensible and do not needlessly constrain legitimate use.

## Observability
Recommend the security-relevant telemetry: authorization-denial logs on preset access, `indicator_subscriptions{user}` for cap enforcement, and an ERROR-level `indicator_parity_mismatch_total` because a parity divergence on a safety-relevant metric is a security-adjacent event, not merely a bug.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded with STRIDE category, likelihood/impact and disposition (fix / accept with Owner sign-off).
- [ ] Mitigation tickets filed and linked; accepted risks added to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.
- [ ] Any rules/checks produced are merged and running in CI.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment present on this ticket and on the affected stories.

## Dependencies
E13-K01 (which indicators run where, and their measured cost, determines the DoS analysis).

## Branch
`chore/e13-threat-model` (docs only).

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-034, SCR-035, SCR-036

title: Black-box test plan for the E14 drawing-tools story groups
body:
## Context
E14 delivers the whole drawing surface of the terminal: twelve-plus tools, magnet snapping, multi-select and group transform, per-drawing styling, server persistence per user and symbol, an object tree, templates and cross-pane sync. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 sizes it at 47 points across S07-S08, and two R1 exit criteria depend on it directly: criterion 5 ("chart state — symbol, timeframe, indicators, **drawings**, layout — survives reload, app restart and Electron relaunch with zero loss") and criterion 9 ("drawings can be created and adjusted by keyboard, and a screen-reader pass is signed off").

The E14 child tickets describe *what* to build (`E14-T01`..`E14-T04`, `E14-S01`..`E14-S10`). Nothing today tells a QA engineer how to sit in front of a staging build and declare "drawings are correct, durable and operable". `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a written black-box plan per feature and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes a recorded QA sign-off non-skippable. This ticket produces that artefact, written purely against `SCR-036`, `SCR-037`, the REST contract in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and observable canvas behaviour — no knowledge of `DrawingStore` internals or the engine's hit-test index — so it survives refactors of `E14-T02`/`E14-T04`.

The defining property under test is **anchoring**: `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 stores geometry as `{"points":[{"t","p"}]}` in chart space, never pixels, and `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings` states drawings must survive "zoom, bar-type changes and DPI changes". Almost every interesting E14 defect is an anchoring or persistence defect, so the plan is built around that.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e14-drawing-tools-test-plan.md`, with seven executable groups mapped one-to-one onto the story groups:
  1. **Toolbar, tool selection and properties** (US-DRAW-001 partial, SCR-037, `CMP-223 DrawingToolbar`, `CMP-017 Popover`, `CMP-031 ColorSwatch`, `CMP-041 Menu`, `CMP-008 NumericStepperInput`, `CMP-022 Kbd`) — covers `E14-S10`.
  2. **Line family** (US-DRAW-001, US-DRAW-002) — horizontal line/ray, vertical line, trendline, ray, extended line, magnet-to-OHLC; covers `E14-S01`, `E14-S02`.
  3. **Zone family** (US-DRAW-003) — rectangle, ellipse, parallel channel, triangle, fill opacity, flatten-opacity toggle; covers `E14-S03`.
  4. **Projection family** (US-DRAW-004, US-DRAW-005) — fib retracement/extension/time-zone with custom level sets, anchored VWAP with σ bands and the "approximate" badge; covers `E14-S04`, `E14-S05`.
  5. **Annotation and planning tools** (US-DRAW-006, US-DRAW-007) — text/note/price label with sanitisation, long/short position tool with R:R, USDT risk/reward, implied size and the send-to-ticket handoff; covers the annotation and position stories.
  6. **Object management** (US-DRAW-008) — undo/redo ≥50 ops, lock, hide, delete-all, z-order, multi-select, group transform, object tree `SCR-036` (`CMP-046 Drawer`, `CMP-049 Table`, `CMP-224 IndicatorChips`); covers `E14-T04`, `E14-T02`.
  7. **Templates, persistence and cross-chart sync** (US-DRAW-009) — style templates, per-layout vs per-symbol scope, sync groups, reload/restart durability; covers `E14-T01`, `E14-T02`.
- Per case: id `E14-TC-<group><nn>`, preconditions (named fixture symbol-day + seeded drawing set), steps, single unambiguous expected result, the `US-DRAW-*` id verified, the child ticket covered, and automation status (automated in `E14-Q02`/`E14-Q03`/`E14-Q04`, or manual-only).
- A **cross-cutting invariants section** that no single child ticket owns, executed against every tool:
  - *Anchor invariance*: zoom in/out, pan, switch linear↔log↔percent price scale, switch 1m↔1h↔1D, switch bar type time↔tick↔renko, change DPI/monitor, resize window — the drawing's `(t, p)` anchors must be unchanged in `GET /drawings` and must render over the same bars/prices.
  - *Round-trip fidelity*: create → `GET /drawings` → reload → compare geometry, style, `locked`, `visible`, `z_index`, `interval_scope` field by field.
  - *Multi-pane identity*: a symbol-scoped drawing appears in every pane showing that symbol; a `layout_id`-scoped one appears only in its pane and is marked as local in the object tree.
  - *Deletion semantics*: delete is a soft delete (`deleted_at`), disappears from every pane, is undoable, and a deleted drawing never reappears after reload.
  - *Handle ergonomics*: every grab handle has a hit area ≥24 px per US-DRAW-001 NFR, verified at 100%, 150% and 200% zoom.
- A **fixture & test-data appendix** naming the seeded sets used across all E14 QA: `draw-empty` (no drawings), `draw-mixed-24` (two of every tool, spanning a 3-day window), `draw-dense-500` (500 drawings on one symbol, for tree virtualisation and drag FPS), `draw-locked-hidden` (mixed lock/visible states), `draw-legacy-geometry` (a row whose `tool` is valid but whose geometry has an extra unknown key, for forward-compat), and `draw-hostile-text` (annotation payloads from `E14-X02`).
- A **traceability table** US-DRAW-001..009 × test cases × automation status, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, proving no story is untested.
- **Defect conventions for E14**: any case where a drawing moves relative to price/time after a view change, or where a persisted drawing is lost, is filed `priority/p0-critical` by definition — a trader treats a level as a decision record, and a silently drifted level is worse than no level.

## Out of scope
- Writing the automation: geometry conformance suite (`E14-Q02`), Playwright E2E (`E14-Q03`), contract tests (`E14-Q04`).
- Execution of perf (`E14-Q05`), chaos (`E14-Q06`) and the a11y audit (`E14-Q07`).
- Security-owned artefacts (`E14-X01`..`E14-X03`).
- Indicator behaviour (E13), layout/workspace persistence (E15), alert creation from a drawn line (E40) — referenced only at the seam.
- Order-ticket internals behind the position tool's send-to-ticket action (E29/E32); the plan verifies the handoff payload, not the ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E14 story is covered by at least one executable case
  Given the plan is merged at qa/plans/e14-drawing-tools-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against US-DRAW-001 through US-DRAW-009
  Then every story id maps to at least one E14-TC case
  And every case names the child ticket it covers and its automation status

Scenario: A QA engineer can execute the plan without asking questions
  Given a fresh staging build with the seeded fixture drawing sets loaded
  When an engineer who did not write the plan executes group 4 end to end
  Then every precondition is satisfiable from the fixture appendix alone
  And each step has exactly one expected result with no interpretation needed

Scenario: Failure case - an anchoring regression is caught by the plan
  Given a build where trendline anchors are cached in pixel space after the first render
  When the anchor-invariance invariant cases are executed with a linear-to-log scale switch
  Then the case fails with observed-vs-expected anchor values quoted from GET /drawings
  And the plan's defect convention classifies it as priority/p0-critical

Scenario: Edge case - a drawing that predates recorded history
  Given an anchored VWAP whose anchor bar precedes the recorder start for the symbol
  When the projection-family cases are executed
  Then the plan requires the visible "approximate" badge and a documented fallback value
  And a missing badge is a functional failure, not a cosmetic one
```

## Technical notes / design
- The plan is markdown with one table per group; each row is a case. No prose-only cases — every case has preconditions/steps/expected.
- Anchor verification is done through the API, not the canvas: the tester reads `GET /api/v1/drawings?symbol=BTCUSDT`, records the `geometry.points` array, performs the view change, re-reads, and diffs. This keeps the check exact rather than "it looks the same".
- Handle-size checks use the browser's own devtools measurement or the engine's debug overlay (if `E14-T04` ships one); the plan states the method so results are reproducible.
- Seeded fixture sets are created by a small script that posts to `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch`, checked in under `qa/fixtures/drawings/`, so a tester can rebuild state in one command. `draw-dense-500` deliberately sits at the 500-operation `maxItems` cap of the batch endpoint so the cap itself is exercised.
- Where a tool is marked Should/Could in `11-user-stories.md` (rays, extended lines, channels, triangles, fib extension), the plan marks the case `conditional` and records the descope decision reference rather than failing the run if the tool was descoped per `30-release-roadmap.md` §12.

## Test plan
- Self-verifying artefact: review by the E14 tech lead and the a11y specialist; a dry run of one group by an engineer who did not author it (this is scenario 2, and its result is recorded in the ticket).
- Traceability table cross-checked mechanically against `18-traceability-matrix.md` rows 148-156 to catch a story the plan forgot.
- The plan is re-run in full as the regression pack input for `E14-Q08`.

## Security notes
- The plan must not embed real user ids, session tokens or Bybit credentials in preconditions; fixtures use seeded test users (`qa-owner`, `qa-manager`, `qa-viewer`) created by the harness.
- Group 5 cases for text annotations reference the hostile-input corpus owned by `E14-X02` rather than duplicating payloads, so there is one source of truth for XSS vectors.
- Cross-user isolation is *named* in the plan (a Manager must not see the Owner's drawings) but its adversarial depth belongs to `E14-X02`; the QA case is the benign one.

## Accessibility notes
- Every group carries at least one keyboard-only case: select the tool by hotkey (`Alt+T`, `Alt+H`, `Alt+F`, `Alt+R`, `Alt+M`, magnet `Ctrl+M` per SCR-037), place anchors via the keyboard drawing mode, nudge with arrows (1 tick, Shift = 10 ticks), and delete — no mouse.
- The object tree `SCR-036` is designated in the plan as *the* accessible equivalent for canvas objects, so every canvas-only operation in groups 2-6 has a paired tree-based case.
- Deep audit (screen-reader transcripts, axe-core, focus order) is `E14-Q07`; this plan only ensures no group is mouse-only.

## Performance notes
- Each group names a perf-sensitive case handed to `E14-Q05`: drag with 200 drawings on screen (SCR-037 target ≥58 fps), object tree with 500 objects (US-DRAW-008 virtualisation NFR), anchored VWAP incremental update (≤2 ms per US-DRAW-005 NFR), and the 500-op batch write.
- The plan states that perf cases are *observed* here (obvious jank is a defect) and *measured* in `E14-Q05`.

## Observability
- The plan instructs testers to capture the analytics events named in SCR-037 (`drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`) and SCR-036 (`drawing.removed`) alongside each case, so a missing event is caught as part of functional QA rather than at release.
- Failing cases must attach: the `GET /drawings` payload before and after, a screen recording, browser console output and the `X-Request-Id` of the failing REST call.

## Definition of Done
- Plan merged at `qa/plans/e14-drawing-tools-test-plan.md` with all seven groups, the invariants section, the fixture appendix and the traceability table.
- Reviewed and approved by the E14 tech lead, a QA peer and the a11y specialist.
- Dry run of one group executed by a non-author with the result recorded on this ticket.
- Every case tagged with its automation destination ticket or an explicit `manual-only` reason.
- Linked from `18-traceability-matrix.md` and from the E14 epic ticket.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T02` (DrawingStore + sync semantics), `E14-T04` (hit-test, multi-select, group transform) and `E14-S10` (toolbar + properties popover) must be at least demo-able so the plan describes real UI, not a proposal.
- Consumes the fixture harness conventions established in `E12-Q01`.

## Branch
`chore/e14-qa-test-plan`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §6 DRAW (US-DRAW-001..009)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-223, CMP-224, CMP-008, CMP-010, CMP-017, CMP-022, CMP-031, CMP-041, CMP-046, CMP-049
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` rows 148-156, 549-550
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 `drawings`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings`, `/drawings/batch`, `/drawings/{drawingId}`, `DrawingInput`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2, §5.3 criteria 5 and 9


## Agent execution brief

title: Geometry & persistence conformance suite for drawing anchoring
body:
## Context
The single invariant that makes drawings trustworthy is that they live in **chart space**. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 stores `geometry` as a JSONB point list of `{t, p}`; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings` states drawings "survive zoom, bar-type changes and DPI changes"; US-DRAW-002's NFR is blunt — "anchors stored as (timestamp, price), never pixels; log/linear scale changes must not move them".

This is exactly the class of bug that manual QA misses: a level that drifts by two pixels after a scale change looks fine in a screenshot and is catastrophic in a trade review. It is also the class of bug that a refactor of `E14-T03` (instanced line rendering) or `E14-T04` (hit-test index) reintroduces easily, because both are tempted to cache screen coordinates. This ticket builds the automated suite that makes the invariant permanent and cheap to check.

The suite is deliberately split in two layers so a failure localises: a **projection-level property suite** in the engine package (no DOM, no server — pure `(t,p) ↔ (x,y)` round-trips across scale modes) and an **integration-level golden suite** driving the real store and the real `/drawings` API against seeded fixtures.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Layer 1 — property-based projection tests** in `packages/chart-engine/test/drawings/projection.prop.test.ts`:
  - For randomly generated `(t, p)` anchors, viewports, DPRs and scale modes (`linear`, `logarithmic`, `percent`, inverted), assert `unproject(project(t, p)) ≈ (t, p)` within one device pixel, and that `project` is monotonic in both axes.
  - Assert scale-mode independence: changing the price-scale mode changes `y` but never the stored `p`.
  - Assert bar-type independence: the same `t` maps onto the bar containing it whether the series is time, tick, volume, range, delta or renko (E12 bar families), because `bar_type_binding` is null for an unbound drawing.
  - Extremes: anchors far outside the visible window, anchors at the series edge, prices near tick-size granularity, timestamps at DST-free UTC boundaries, and `p` values with full instrument precision (no float rounding to 2 dp).
- **Layer 2 — golden persistence tests** in `apps/web/test/drawings/roundtrip.test.ts` + a server-side pack in `tests/api/test_drawings_roundtrip.py`:
  - For each of the 24 tools in the `DrawingInput.tool` enum that E14 ships, create via `POST /api/v1/drawings`, read back, and assert byte-equality of `geometry`, `style`, `locked`, `visible`, `z_index`, `interval_scope`, `layout_id`, `bar_type_binding`.
  - Assert soft-delete semantics: `DELETE` sets `deleted_at`, the row vanishes from `GET`, and an undo re-creates it with identical geometry (new or restored id per `E14-T02`'s documented contract — the test asserts whichever the contract states, and fails if the contract is silent).
  - Assert `anchor_start`/`anchor_end` denormalisation matches the min/max `t` in `geometry.points` for every tool, including single-anchor tools (hline, vline, text) where one may be null.
  - Assert the batch endpoint is transactional: a 3-op batch whose second op is invalid leaves zero rows changed and returns `422`.
  - Forward-compat: `draw-legacy-geometry` (unknown extra key inside `geometry`) round-trips unchanged rather than being silently stripped.
- **View-change matrix test** (the headline): for `draw-mixed-24`, snapshot every drawing's `geometry`, then programmatically apply each of {zoom ×0.25, zoom ×8, pan 500 bars, linear→log, log→percent, inverted on, 1m→1D, time→renko, DPR 1→2, window resize}, and re-read. Any mutation of a stored anchor fails the suite with the diff.
- **CI wiring**: both layers run on every PR touching `packages/chart-engine/src/drawings/**`, `apps/web/src/drawings/**` or the `/drawings` router; the view-change matrix is a required check.

## Out of scope
- Visual rendering correctness (does the trendline look right) — that is design-QA on `E14-S02`/`E14-S03` plus the E2E screenshots in `E14-Q03`.
- FPS and drag latency — `E14-Q05`.
- REST schema conformance against the OpenAPI document — `E14-Q04` (this suite asserts *values*, that one asserts *shape*).
- Cross-user access control — `E14-X02`.
- Anchored-VWAP numerical correctness against the tape; only its anchor persistence is covered here (value correctness lives with `E14-S05`'s own unit tests).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Anchors survive every view change
  Given the draw-mixed-24 fixture is loaded on BTCUSDT
  When the view-change matrix applies all ten transformations in sequence
  Then GET /api/v1/drawings returns geometry byte-identical to the pre-change snapshot
  And no drawing's rendered position relative to its anchor bar and price has changed

Scenario: Every shipped tool round-trips losslessly
  Given one drawing of each shipped tool created via POST /api/v1/drawings
  When each is read back and compared field by field
  Then geometry, style, locked, visible, z_index, interval_scope, layout_id and bar_type_binding all match the request
  And anchor_start and anchor_end match the min and max timestamps in geometry.points

Scenario: Failure case - pixel caching is reintroduced
  Given a build where the drawings layer caches screen coordinates across a scale change
  When the projection property suite runs with mixed linear and logarithmic viewports
  Then at least one round-trip assertion fails with the generated counterexample printed
  And the CI required check blocks the merge

Scenario: Edge case - a partially invalid batch changes nothing
  Given a three-operation batch where the second operation omits geometry
  When POST /api/v1/drawings/batch is called
  Then the response is 422
  And a subsequent GET shows none of the three operations were applied
```

## Technical notes / design
- Property tests use `fast-check` on the frontend/engine side and `hypothesis` on the Python side, matching the property-based testing already mandated for engine scale math in `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4.
- Prices are compared as decimal strings, never floats — the API models `p` as a string precisely so tick precision is not lost, and the suite asserts that contract rather than working around it.
- The view-change matrix drives the engine through its public viewport API in a headless WebGL context (the harness from `E11`), not through Playwright, so it runs in seconds and can be a required PR check.
- Golden files live in `qa/fixtures/drawings/golden/` and are regenerated by an explicit `--update-golden` flag that is refused in CI, so an anchor drift can never be "fixed" by accepting a new golden without a human diff in the PR.
- The suite is written against the tool enum in `DrawingInput`; a tool present in the enum but not exercised fails a meta-test, so adding a tool later forces adding coverage.

## Test plan
- Mutation check: deliberately introduce three seeded regressions (pixel caching on scale change, `anchor_end` computed from the first rather than the last point, batch applying ops before validating all of them) on a scratch branch and confirm each is caught by a distinct assertion.
- Runtime budget: full suite under 90 s on CI hardware; the property layer capped at 500 generated cases per property with a fixed seed recorded in the run log for reproducibility.
- Flake gate: the suite runs 20× consecutively in the nightly job; any non-determinism is a blocking defect in the suite itself.

## Security notes
- Fixtures are created through the authenticated API as the seeded `qa-owner` user; the suite must never write directly to Postgres, so it exercises the same authorisation path production uses.
- Hostile geometry (enormous point arrays, deeply nested JSON, non-numeric `p`) is asserted here only for *rejection with 422*; adversarial depth and payload corpus ownership stay with `E14-X02`.
- Golden files are scrubbed of user ids and session identifiers before commit.

## Accessibility notes

title: Contract tests for the /drawings REST surface including batch
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires interface-first contracts for every backend↔frontend story, and `03-testing-strategy.md` makes contract tests a distinct pyramid layer: the OpenAPI document is normative, and the implementation must be provably identical to it. E14 adds four operations to that document — `listDrawings`, `createDrawing`, `batchUpsertDrawings`, `updateDrawing`, `deleteDrawing` — plus the `DrawingInput`/`Drawing` schemas with a 24-value `tool` enum and a free-form `geometry` object.

The batch endpoint deserves special attention. It is the hot path (the engine debounces drag mutations at 500 ms and sends one call carrying every affected shape), it is transactional, it is capped at `maxItems: 500`, and it accepts an `Idempotency-Key`. Each of those is a contract promise that is easy to implement approximately and expensive to get wrong: a non-transactional batch corrupts a trader's chart mid-drag, and a non-idempotent retry duplicates every shape on a flaky connection.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/contract/test_drawings_contract.py` driven by the generated client / schema validator already used for the R0 contract pack:
  - **Schema conformance both ways**: every response validated against `#/components/schemas/Drawing` and `Page`; every request fixture validated against `DrawingInput` before being sent, so the tests cannot drift from the document.
  - **`additionalProperties: false` enforcement**: `DrawingInput` declares it — an unknown top-level field must yield `422`, not be silently ignored.
  - **Tool enum**: each of the 24 enum values is accepted (for shipped tools) or rejected with a documented reason (for tools descoped per `30-release-roadmap.md` §12, e.g. pitchfork/gann_fan); a value outside the enum yields `422`.
  - **Required fields**: missing `symbol`, `tool` or `geometry` → `422` with the standard error envelope.
  - **Pagination**: `GET /drawings` honours `cursor` and `limit`, returns `meta.next_cursor`/`has_more`/`count` consistently, and a cursor from a different symbol's page is rejected rather than silently reinterpreted.
  - **`layout_id` filter**: narrows to pane-scoped drawings; an unknown layout id yields `404` per the documented responses.
  - **Status-code matrix**: `201` on create, `200` on replace and batch, `204` on delete, `401` unauthenticated, `403` for a principal lacking `workspaces:write`, `404` for an unknown or soft-deleted `drawingId`, `422` for validation.
  - **RBAC annotations honoured**: `x-rbac: { permissions: [workspaces:read|write], scope: self }` is asserted behaviourally — a Viewer role can read its own and cannot write; a Manager cannot read the Owner's drawings by id.
- **Batch-specific pack**:
  - Mixed `create`/`update`/`delete` in one call applied **in order**, with the response's `created`/`updated`/`deleted` arrays matching exactly.
  - Transactionality: any single failing op rolls the whole batch back (asserted by a `GET` diff, not by trusting the response).
  - `maxItems: 500` boundary: 500 ops succeed, 501 ops yield `422` before any write.
  - `update`/`delete` without `id` → `422`; `create` with an `id` → `422`.
  - Idempotency: the same `Idempotency-Key` replayed returns the original result and creates nothing new; a different body with the same key is rejected per the platform's idempotency contract.
- **Spec-drift guard**: a CI check that diffs the live app's generated OpenAPI against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` for the `/drawings*` paths and fails on any difference, mirroring the WS-freeze discipline in `E17`.

## Out of scope
- Value-level persistence fidelity and anchor invariants — `E14-Q02`.
- UI behaviour — `E14-Q03`.
- Load characteristics of the batch endpoint — `E14-Q05`.
- Adversarial payloads (XSS in labels, JSON bombs, IDOR fuzzing) — `E14-X02`; this pack asserts the documented rejections only.
- Database-level retention/purge of soft-deleted rows (90 d per `21-database-schema.md`) — owned by E16's lifecycle work.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The implementation matches the published contract
  Given the application's generated OpenAPI document
  When the /drawings, /drawings/batch and /drawings/{drawingId} paths are diffed against 22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then there is no difference in paths, parameters, schemas or response codes
  And the check is a required CI gate on the drawings router

Scenario: A partially invalid batch is fully rejected
  Given a batch of 3 operations where the second has op=update and no id
  When POST /api/v1/drawings/batch is called
  Then the response is 422 with the standard error envelope
  And a subsequent GET /api/v1/drawings shows none of the three operations were applied

Scenario: Failure case - an unknown field is silently accepted
  Given a DrawingInput body carrying an undeclared field "pixels"
  When POST /api/v1/drawings is called
  Then the response is 422 because DrawingInput declares additionalProperties: false
  And no row is created

Scenario: Edge case - a replayed idempotency key
  Given a 200-operation batch submitted with Idempotency-Key K that succeeded
  When the identical request is replayed with the same key after a client timeout
  Then the original response is returned
  And GET shows exactly 200 drawings, not 400
```

## Technical notes / design
- The pack runs against the real FastAPI app with a real Postgres (testcontainers), not mocks, because transactionality and the partial indexes are part of what is being asserted.
- Request fixtures are generated from the schema where possible (schema-derived example generation) so a schema change automatically widens coverage instead of silently leaving the pack behind.
- The status-code matrix is table-driven: one parametrised test over `(method, path, principal, body) → expected status`, making the RBAC rows readable next to the `x-rbac` annotations they encode.
- Soft-deleted rows must be indistinguishable from never-existing rows at the API boundary (`404`), which also avoids an enumeration oracle — this is asserted here and re-checked adversarially in `E14-X02`.
- The drift guard compares a normalised (key-sorted, example-stripped) subtree so cosmetic YAML churn does not produce false failures.

## Test plan
- Self-testing: introduce, on a scratch branch, (a) a non-transactional batch, (b) an off-by-one at the 500 cap, (c) `403` returned where `404` is documented — and confirm three distinct assertions fail.
- Runtime under 60 s including container start, so it can sit on the PR path for the drawings router.
- Contract pack runs in the same CI job as the R0 contract tests to keep one reporting surface.

## Security notes
- RBAC assertions are functional contract checks here and adversarial cases in `E14-X02`; both exist because `04-security-program.md` treats broken object-level authorisation as a top-tier risk and `scope: self` is the only thing standing between users' private chart annotations.
- The pack asserts error bodies never echo another user's data, a row id that was not supplied, or a stack trace.
- `Idempotency-Key` handling is asserted not to leak across principals: the same key used by a different user must not return the first user's result.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A for the API surface itself. The one a11y-relevant contract assertion kept here: `label` is returned verbatim so the client can derive an accessible name; a server that trims or normalises `label` would break `SCR-036` naming, so round-trip equality of `label` is asserted.

## Performance notes
- Not a load test, but the pack asserts the `GET /drawings?symbol=` path uses the partial index by checking the query plan in a debug-mode assertion against budget 28 (< 5 ms) from `21-database-schema.md` §performance.
- A 500-op batch must complete within 1 s locally as a smoke bound; the real profile is `E14-Q05`.

## Observability
- Every request in the pack carries an `X-Request-Id`; failures attach the correlated server log lines, so a contract failure is triageable from the CI artefact alone.
- The drift guard publishes the normalised diff as an artefact when it fails, so the reviewer sees exactly which promise moved.

## Definition of Done
- Contract pack merged and green; drift guard wired as a required check on `apps/api/**/drawings*`.
- Status-code and RBAC matrix complete for all five operations.
- Batch transactionality, cap and idempotency all asserted.
- Seeded-regression evidence linked on the ticket.
- Backend coverage for the drawings router at or above the 85% threshold.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T01` (migration + endpoints). Reuses the contract-test harness and idempotency conventions established in R0.

## Branch
`test/e14-drawings-contract`

## References
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings`, `/drawings/batch`, `/drawings/{drawingId}`, `DrawingInput`, `Drawing`, `Page`, `IdempotencyKey`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3, migration `0011_workspace`, query budget 28, retention row for soft-deleted config rows
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 interface-first, §4
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (contract layer)
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (object-level authorisation)

title: Drawing toolbar and properties popover (SCR-037)
body:
## Context
Every DRAW story needs the same chrome: a tool rail to pick a tool, and a properties popover to style what was drawn. **SCR-037** specifies both — the left rail listing cursor/crosshair/trendline/ray/extended/h-line/v-line/rect/ellipse/triangle/fib/pitchfork/VWAP/measure/position/text/arrow/brush plus magnet, lock-all, hide-all and delete-all; and the popover with colour, width, style, extend, magnet and "save as default". Building it once, first, means the nine tool stories add a tool entry and a property schema rather than a UI.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-223 DrawingToolbar** as the left rail of the chart, grouped by tool family, with an overflow menu (CMP-041) for rarely-used tools and a persistent "keep tool active" toggle for repeated drawing.
- Properties popover (CMP-017) bound to the current selection: colour (CMP-031 ColorSwatch, design-token palette), width (CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, 1–8), dash (solid/dashed/dotted), fill colour and fill opacity (CMP-010 Slider) for fill-capable tools, label text, font size, extend-left/extend-right, magnet toggle, lock, visibility, `Save as default`, `Delete`.
- Multi-selection editing: when N drawings are selected, shared properties are editable and mixed values render as an indeterminate state.
- Global toolbar actions wired to store commands: magnet toggle (`Ctrl+M`), lock-all, hide-all, delete-all (with confirmation), and the disabled "alert when price crosses" affordance reserved for E40 with a "coming in a later release" tooltip.
- Hotkeys per SCR-037: `Alt+T` trendline, `Alt+H` horizontal, `Alt+F` fib, `Alt+R` rect, `Alt+M` measure, `Esc` cancel in-progress drawing / clear selection.
- A per-tool registry (`id`, icon, hotkey, anchor count, property schema, default style) that later stories extend — the single extension point for the whole Epic.
- States: no selection (rail only), single selection, multi-selection, locked selection (properties read-only with an unlock action), tool armed (cursor and rail state change).

## Out of scope
- The tools themselves — each is its own Story (S01–S09).
- The object tree (**E14-S08**) and templates (**E14-S09**).
- Alert creation from the popover (**E40**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Arm a tool and draw
  Given the chart has focus
  When the trader presses Alt+T
  Then the trendline tool is armed, the rail shows it as active, the cursor changes, and the status region announces "Trendline tool active"

Scenario: Style a selection
  Given a trendline is selected
  When colour is changed to a token swatch and width to 4 in the popover
  Then the change is visible within one frame and persisted after the 500 ms debounce

Scenario: Mixed multi-selection
  Given a 2 px red line and a 4 px blue line are both selected
  Then width and colour render as indeterminate, and setting width to 3 applies to both while colour stays untouched

Scenario: Locked selection is read-only
  Given a locked drawing is selected
  Then style fields are disabled with an explanatory hint and only "Unlock" is actionable

Scenario: Cancel an in-progress drawing
  Given the first anchor of a rectangle has been placed
  When Esc is pressed
  Then the in-progress drawing is discarded, nothing is persisted, and the tool returns to cursor unless "keep tool active" is on

Scenario: Delete-all is not a one-click accident
  When delete-all is chosen
  Then a confirmation states how many drawings on which symbol will be removed, and the action is undoable as one command
```

## Technical notes / design
The tool registry is a plain data structure consumed by both the rail and the popover, so a new tool is a registry entry plus an engine geometry handler; nothing in the chrome is tool-aware. The popover is anchored to the selection's screen-space bounds published by E14-T04 and repositions on pan/zoom, clamping to the viewport. All styling values come from design-system v0 tokens (E05) — no raw hex in code; the colour swatch offers the token palette plus a custom picker that still writes a `#rrggbb` value matching the API pattern.

## Test plan
Unit: registry resolution, indeterminate-value logic, hotkey dispatch, Esc semantics. Component tests for the popover states (none/single/multi/locked). E2E Playwright: arm→draw→style→persist→reload. a11y: axe-core on SCR-037; keyboard-only traversal of rail and popover; screen-reader announcement of tool arming. design-qa: built screen compared to the signed-off SCR-037 spec.

## Security notes
The label field is user content: length-capped at 120 chars client-side to match the API, rendered as text only, and never passed to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. The delete-all action is destructive and therefore confirmed and undoable, and is scoped to the current user's own drawings only.

## Accessibility notes
The rail is a toolbar (`role="toolbar"`, roving tabindex, arrow-key traversal) with each tool a toggle button exposing pressed state and its hotkey via CMP-022 Kbd in the accessible description. The popover is a standard form (SCR-037 a11y note) with labelled fields, focus trapped while open, `Esc` to close and focus returned to the trigger. Tool arming and cancellation are announced politely. All targets ≥24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8); state is never colour-only.

## Performance notes
Arming a tool or opening the popover must not trigger an engine re-render of the price layer. Popover repositioning during pan is throttled to animation frames. The rail renders once and is memoised; property edits push straight to the store's coalescing map.

## Observability
`drawing.tool_armed{tool}`, `drawing.style_changed{property}`, `drawing.default_saved{tool}`, `drawing.delete_all` analytics events; client metric `drawings_popover_open_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests referenced by name.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the toolbar/popover package.
- [ ] SCR-037 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior (design-ahead rule) and design-qa comparison recorded.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard-only path and screen-reader spot-check recorded.
- [ ] CMP-223 entry in `15-component-catalogue.md` reflects shipped API.
- [ ] Feature flag `drawings.v1` recorded with per-environment default.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed at Sprint Review.

title: STRIDE threat model for drawings persistence, sync and annotation content
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 requires a STRIDE model per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes the kickoff a DoR item for any epic with a security label. E14 is easy to underestimate: "it's just shapes on a chart". It is not. E14 introduces a **user-controlled, server-persisted, cross-session, cross-pane, free-form JSONB store** (`drawings.geometry`, `drawings.style`, `drawings.label`) that is rendered back into the DOM (object tree `SCR-036`, labels, tooltips) and into SDF text on the canvas, is writable in 500-operation transactional batches, is scoped `self` by RBAC, and — via `drawings.alert_id` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3) — is linked to the alerting subsystem. On top of that, the long/short position tool (US-DRAW-007) computes a size and hands it to the order ticket, which is the first place in R1 where a *chart annotation* influences a *trading decision input*.

That is four genuine attack surfaces: stored content that is rendered (XSS), object-level authorisation across users (IDOR — and CandleViewer has Owner/Manager/Viewer roles sharing one deployment), resource exhaustion via unbounded JSONB and batch size (DoS), and integrity of a value that feeds the order ticket. This ticket derives the model against what E14 is actually building.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Data-flow diagram** (mermaid, committed with the model) with trust boundaries drawn:
  - Browser (untrusted input: pointer, keyboard, pasted text, clipboard) → web app `DrawingStore` (`E14-T02`) → `POST/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/drawings`, `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch`.
  - API gateway → RBAC check (`x-rbac: permissions [workspaces:read|write], scope: self`) → drawings service → Postgres `drawings` table.
  - Postgres → `GET /drawings` → store → **two render sinks**: the DOM object tree `SCR-036`/properties popover (HTML) and the WebGL SDF text layer (`E14-T03`).
  - `drawings.alert_id` → alerts subsystem (E40) — a cross-epic edge created here and consumed later.
  - Position tool → sizing computation (shared with US-PROF-002) → order ticket pre-fill (E29 seam).
  - Cross-pane/cross-layout sync path (US-DRAW-009), including the boundary where a drawing scoped to `layout_id` must not leak into another layout.
- **STRIDE analysis per element and flow**, in the `04-security-program.md` §5 table format (`T` id, category, threat, likelihood, impact, risk, mitigating control, residual risk), covering at minimum:
  - **Spoofing** — a forged `owner_user_id` in a request body (the field must be server-derived from the session, never accepted from the client); a session replayed from another device creating drawings attributed to the victim; the test-only `__cvEngine.projectForTest` handle from `E14-Q03` present in a production bundle.
  - **Tampering** — stored XSS via `label`, annotation text (US-DRAW-006), template names, or a `style` value injected into a CSS context; JSON injection through the free-form `geometry`/`style` objects (`additionalProperties: true` on `geometry` by design); a drawing modified by another principal; **integrity of the position tool's computed size** — a manipulated `geometry` or profile value producing a risk figure the trader believes and acts on; `bar_type_binding` set to a value that changes how a drawing is interpreted; batch operation ordering abused to make a delete-then-create look like an edit in the audit trail.
  - **Repudiation** — drawings are user content with `created_at`/`updated_at` but no audit trail; if a Manager's drawing influenced a trade, can we say who created it and when? The model must state whether `drawings` needs audit coverage or is explicitly out of the append-only audit scope, and record the decision.
  - **Information disclosure** — **IDOR**: `GET /drawings/{drawingId}` or a `layout_id` filter returning another user's rows; enumeration of ids distinguishing "exists but not yours" (`403`) from "does not exist" (`404`) — the contract says `404`, and the model must require that; drawings leaking a trader's levels, which are genuinely sensitive strategy information in a multi-user deployment with Managers; annotation text containing sensitive notes appearing in logs, error messages, analytics events (`drawing.created` etc.) or in journal snapshots (US-DRAW-006's NFR pulls notes into the journal — a data-flow the model must trace).
  - **Denial of service** — unbounded `geometry` point arrays (a polyline/brush with 10^6 points); deeply nested JSONB causing parser or index blowup; the 500-op batch cap as the only quantitative limit today, with no stated cap on per-drawing size or on total drawings per user; a retry storm from the optimistic client (cross-referenced to `E14-Q06`); a `draw-dense` payload that makes every subsequent chart load slow (a persistent, self-inflicted or manager-inflicted DoS); disk growth in Postgres from soft-deleted rows retained 90 days.
  - **Elevation of privilege** — a Viewer role writing drawings; a drawing crafted so its send-to-ticket handoff pre-fills an order for an account the user may not trade; `alert_id` set to an alert belonging to another user, borrowing that alert's privileges or leaking its existence.
- **Asset classification** for E14: drawing content and annotations = **CONFIDENTIAL user strategy data** (not PII, not secrets, but disclosure to another user of the same deployment is a real harm); the position tool's computed size = **integrity-critical** because it feeds an order path.
- **Control mapping**: each threat mapped to an existing control or to a new security requirement (`SR-` id) with an owning ticket — notably output encoding at both render sinks, server-side geometry size limits, per-user drawing quota, `404`-not-`403` for foreign ids, and the production-bundle assertion for the test handle.
- **Explicit residual-risk statement** signed by the Security engineer, and the STRIDE table linked from `04-security-program.md`'s per-epic index.

## Out of scope
- Executing the tests (`E14-X02` runs abuse cases; `E14-X03` wires the static/dynamic rules).
- Auth/session mechanics themselves (E09 owns them); E14 consumes them and only models misuse at its own boundary.
- Alert delivery security (E40) beyond the `alert_id` reference edge.
- Order placement authorisation (E29/E34/E39); the model stops at the ticket pre-fill and asserts that pre-fill is not authorisation.
- Export/sharing of drawings to other users — not in R1 scope; the model records it as a **deferred surface** so `R13 Sharing abuse` is revisited when sharing ships.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The model covers every element of the drawings data flow
  Given the committed data-flow diagram for E14
  When each element and flow is checked against the STRIDE table
  Then every element has at least one entry for every applicable STRIDE category or a written not-applicable reason
  And every entry names a mitigating control and an owning ticket

Scenario: Both render sinks are treated as injection sinks
  Given user-controlled label, annotation text and style values
  When the tampering section is reviewed
  Then the DOM sink and the WebGL SDF text sink are modelled separately with distinct encoding controls
  And a control is specified for the accessible-name path used by SCR-036

Scenario: Failure case - an unbounded input has no control
  Given the geometry field is declared additionalProperties true with no size limit
  When the denial-of-service section is reviewed
  Then the review refuses sign-off until a server-side size and point-count limit and a per-user quota are specified with owning tickets

Scenario: Edge case - a deferred surface is recorded rather than ignored
  Given drawing sharing between users is out of R1 scope
  When the model is finalised
  Then sharing is listed as a deferred surface with the trigger condition for re-modelling
  And risk R13 Sharing abuse is annotated as not-yet-applicable rather than closed
```

## Technical notes / design
- The model is written in the same template as the E08/E09 R0 models so findings aggregate into one programme view; it lives at `docs/plan/27-adrs/` adjacent security docs or `docs/security/threat-models/e14-drawings.md` per the established location.
- The IDOR analysis must be concrete: enumerate every route that accepts an id or a filter (`/drawings/{drawingId}` PUT/DELETE, `GET /drawings?layout_id=`, batch `update`/`delete` ops carrying arbitrary ids) and state the required check for each. The batch endpoint is the highest-risk one because it accepts 500 arbitrary ids in a single authenticated call.
- Size limits are proposed quantitatively so they are testable: a recommended cap on `geometry` serialized bytes, on `points` length per tool, on `label` length, and on drawings per user per symbol, each with a rationale tied to the perf budgets in `E14-Q05` rather than invented.
- The repudiation decision matters beyond E14: if drawings are excluded from the append-only audit log, that exclusion should be explicit in `04-security-program.md` so a later reviewer does not assume coverage exists.

## Test plan
- The model is validated by review with the E14 tech lead, the Architect and the Security engineer.
- Every `SR-` produced here must be traceable to an assertion in `E14-X02`, `E14-X03`, `E14-Q04` or a story's own tests; an SR with no test is a gap and is filed as such.
- A tabletop walkthrough of two scenarios (a malicious Manager attempting to read the Owner's levels; a crafted annotation attempting stored XSS) is run and recorded.

## Security notes
- This ticket *is* the security artefact; its own hygiene requirements: the model contains no live ids, tokens or real user data; it is reviewed for accidental disclosure before merge.
- The model must state the trust posture plainly: in a single-tenant, Tailscale-only deployment with a handful of users, the realistic adversary is a lower-privileged internal user or a compromised browser session, not an internet-scale attacker — and controls are proportioned to that, without waving away stored XSS, which is equally severe in a small deployment.

## Accessibility notes
- The accessible-name path is explicitly modelled as an injection sink: `SCR-036` derives names from user text, and an `aria-label` is as injectable a context as inner HTML if built by string concatenation into markup. The model requires a control for it, which `E14-Q07` then verifies behaviourally.

## Performance notes
- The DoS section is quantitative and reuses `E14-Q05`'s measured numbers, so proposed caps are grounded: the model cites the observed cost of 500 drawings and of large point arrays rather than guessing.

## Observability
- The model specifies the security-relevant telemetry E14 must emit: authorisation-denied counters on the drawings routes, oversized-payload rejections, batch-cap rejections and per-user drawing counts, so an abuse pattern is visible rather than inferred.
- Each finding is tracked in the programme risk register (`32-risk-register.md`) if its residual risk is above the accepted threshold.

## Definition of Done
- Threat model merged with diagram, STRIDE tables, asset classification, control mapping and residual-risk statement.
- Every threat has an owning control and ticket; every new `SR-` has a test destination.
- Reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer and the Architect.
- Linked from `04-security-program.md`'s per-epic index and from the E14 epic ticket's security DoD item.
- Tabletop walkthrough recorded on the ticket.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T01` (the actual table and endpoints) so the model describes the real design.
- Inherits conventions from the E08 and E09 R0 threat models; consumes E09's RBAC model as a given.

## Branch
`chore/e14-threat-model`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 STRIDE process and table format
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 `drawings` (JSONB geometry/style, `alert_id`, soft delete), retention table
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings`, `/drawings/batch` (`maxItems: 500`, idempotency), `x-rbac` annotations, `DrawingInput`
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-006 (sanitisation NFR, journal snapshots), US-DRAW-007 (sizing shared with US-PROF-002), US-DRAW-009 (sync scope)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037 (analytics events, accessible names)
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` (R13 Sharing abuse, R15 Data lifecycle)

- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.

- drawing tool plugin contract, hit-testing API, persistence schema for saved drawings; named identifiers in this ticket: SCR-036, SCR-037
