title: Black-box test plan for the E15 layout, workspace and sync story groups
body:
## Context
E15 turns a single chart into the daily working surface: preset and custom grids, dockable panels, cross-pane sync groups, named workspaces persisted server-side, layout hotkeys, export/import and a reduced-capability profile. Every later epic (E18 footprint, E21 DOM+heatmap, E30 order ticket) mounts *inside* this dock tree, so a defect here is felt by every subsequent surface and is expensive to find late.

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes a recorded black-box QA pass non-skippable for each Story, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 requires a written per-feature test plan plus a white-box review checklist. Today the E15 story tickets describe *what to build*; there is no single artefact a QA engineer can execute against a staging build to assert "layouts and workspaces behave as specified".

This ticket produces that artefact. It is deliberately black-box — written against the screens `SCR-020..029`, `SCR-011`, `SCR-022`, `SCR-043`, `SCR-049`, `SCR-150`, `SCR-153` and the public REST contract `/workspaces*` — so it survives refactors of the internal dock-tree representation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e15-layouts-workspaces-test-plan.md`, organised as five executable groups:
  1. **Grid layouts & dock system** (US-LAY-001, US-LAY-005) — `SCR-020`, `SCR-021`, `SCR-024`, `SCR-028`; CMP-080 DockPanel, CMP-081 DockGrid / Layout Manager, CMP-082 PanelHeader, CMP-083 SplitPane, CMP-214 DockDropZone, CMP-216 PanelMenu.
  2. **Workspaces persistence & restore** (US-LAY-002) — `SCR-020`, `SCR-025`, `SCR-150`; `GET /api/v1/workspaces`, `POST /api/v1/workspaces`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, `GET|POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`; tables `workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, `chart_templates`.
  3. **Cross-pane sync & scale linking** (US-LAY-003, US-LAY-004) — `SCR-023`, `SCR-043`, `SCR-049`; CMP-196 MultiChartLinker, CMP-218 SyncMenu, CMP-188/CMP-189 scale menus.
  4. **Hotkeys & quick switching** (US-LAY-006) — `SCR-011`, `SCR-022`; `Ctrl+1..9`, `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+Shift+S`, `Ctrl+Tab`, `F6`, `F11`, `Ctrl+Shift+1..3`, `Ctrl+Shift+0`.
  5. **Export/import & reduced capability** (US-LAY-007, US-LAY-008) — `SCR-026`, `SCR-153`; `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/export`, import validation, degraded-profile prompt.
- Per case: id `E15-TC-<group><nn>`, preconditions (seeded user + seeded workspace fixture), steps, expected result, the `US-LAY-*` id verified, the child ticket covered, and automation status (automated in `E15-Q02`/`E15-Q03`, or manual-only).
- **Fixture appendix**: seeded owner / manager / viewer; three seeded workspaces (empty, 4-pane `2x2` matching the `fourPane` example in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, 16-pane stress); a workspace referencing a delisted symbol; a workspace export file at the current schema version and one at version+1.
- **Traceability table** US-LAY-001..008 × test cases × automation status, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.16, proving no story is untested.
- **White-box review checklist** for reviewers: dock-tree mutations are single-commit, layout changes never remount the WebGL context, hidden panels unsubscribe after 30 s.
- Defect-reporting conventions: severity mapping per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3; "workspace save silently loses panes" is always `priority/p0`.

## Out of scope
- Panel *content* correctness (bars, footprint, DOM) — owned by E12/E18/E21 test plans; E15 asserts only mount, bind, resize, unmount and lifecycle.
- Electron packaging/update behaviour (E10); this plan covers floating windows only as a workspace-state concern.
- Load and chaos execution (`E15-Q04`, `E15-Q05`) and adversarial import cases (`E15-X02`) — this plan references them and does not duplicate them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Plan covers every LAY story
  Given the published qa/plans/e15-layouts-workspaces-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 16
  Then each of US-LAY-001..008 maps to at least one case per Gherkin scenario in its story, including the stated edge case
  And every case names the screen or endpoint it exercises

Scenario: A case is executable by someone new to the epic
  Given a QA engineer who has not worked on E15
  When they run group 2 against a staging build using only the fixture appendix
  Then they can reach a pass/fail verdict on every case without asking the authors a question

Scenario: Failure case - stale-write conflict is specified
  Given a workspace opened in two tabs and modified in both
  When the second tab saves with a stale If-Match
  Then the plan requires a 412 PreconditionFailed and the SCR-020 "This workspace changed elsewhere. [Keep mine] [Load theirs]" dialog, and forbids silent overwrite

Scenario: Edge case - missing symbol does not fail the workspace
  Given a saved workspace whose pane references a delisted symbol
  When it is restored
  Then the plan requires that pane to show a named error state and all other panes to load normally

Scenario: Plan is reviewed and merged
  When the plan PR is opened
  Then it carries approvals from the E15 frontend lead and the SDET, and is linked from the E15 epic ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Structure the plan by *observable surface*, not by component: reviewers must be able to re-run it after the dock tree is refactored.
- The 16-pane stress fixture exists to exercise the SCR-020 ">16 panels" warning and the US-LAY-001 pane-limit confirmation, which must state the *measured* frame cost, not a static string.
- Sync cases must assert group scoping (group A changes never touch group B) and the letter-plus-colour badge rule from `SCR-023` — colour alone is a defect (`05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- Persisted shape follows `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1: `workspaces` (unique name per user, single default), `layouts` (unique name and unique `hotkey_slot` per workspace), `layout_panes` (unique `slot_index` per layout). Cases must cover each uniqueness violation returning 422, not a 500.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan; its own verification is a dry run: execute one group end-to-end against the current staging build, record timings and any ambiguity found, and fix the plan before merge. Record the dry-run log as an attachment so the plan's executability claim is evidenced rather than asserted.

## Security notes
- The plan must include the negative assertion that an exported workspace contains no secrets, tokens or account ids (US-LAY-007); the deep adversarial version lives in `E15-X02`.
- Cross-user access cases (user B requesting user A's `workspaceId`) are listed here as smoke-level and owned in depth by `E15-X02`; expected result is 404, never 403-with-existence-disclosure.
- Fixtures must never contain real Bybit API keys or live account identifiers; seeded users use deterministic throwaway credentials.

## Accessibility notes
- Every pointer-driven case has a paired keyboard case: docking via CMP-216 PanelMenu "Move panel", splitter resize via `Alt+Shift+arrows`, region cycling via `F6`, pane focus via `Ctrl+Tab`.
- Cases assert each panel is a `region` with an accessible name of the form "Chart, BTCUSDT 1m" and that dock operations announce their result in a live region ("Chart moved to bottom-right").
- Depth a11y auditing is `E15-Q06`; this plan carries the smoke-level assertions so a regression is caught in the functional pass too.

## Performance notes
- Plan records, per case where relevant, the budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2: ≥55 fps with four active order-flow panes (US-LAY-001 NFR), workspace restore to interactive ≤3 s for a 4-pane workspace from warm cache (US-LAY-002 NFR), sync propagation ≤1 frame (US-LAY-003 NFR), preset apply ≤300 ms (`SCR-022`), panel mount ≤150 ms (`SCR-024`), context menu ≤80 ms (`SCR-028`).
- Measurement is by the instrumented build; the rigorous benchmark run is `E15-Q04`.

## Observability
- Cases assert the analytics/audit events named in the screens catalogue actually fire with the documented payloads: `workspace.saved`, `workspace.updated`, `workspace.deleted`, `workspace.exported`, `panel.added`, `panel.removed`, `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.maximised`, `layout.preset_applied`, `layout.reset`, `layout.imported`, `layout.import_rejected{reason}`, `sync.group_changed`.
- The plan states where to read them during a manual run (the dev analytics sink), so "event missing" is a reportable defect rather than an invisible one.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan merged at `qa/plans/e15-layouts-workspaces-test-plan.md` with all five groups, fixtures, traceability table and white-box checklist.
- [ ] Dry-run log of at least one full group attached to the ticket.
- [ ] Traceability table shows 100% of US-LAY-001..008 covered; gaps explicitly marked N/A with a reason.
- [ ] Automation split agreed and recorded with `E15-Q02` and `E15-Q03`.
- [ ] Reviewed by the E15 frontend lead and an SDET; linked from the E15 epic.

## Dependencies
- `E15-S01` (grid layouts), `E15-S02` (saved workspaces), `E15-S03` (cross-pane sync), `E15-S05` (docking) must be far enough along that the surfaces are testable.
- Consumes `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, `11-user-stories.md` §16, `14-screens-catalogue.md` §2, `18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.16, `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*`.

## Branch
`chore/e15-qa-test-plan`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §16 LAY (US-LAY-001..008)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §2 (SCR-020..029)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-073, CMP-080..083, CMP-214..218
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2, §4

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)

5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

title: Panel docking, floating windows, panel picker and panel menu
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-005** — "dock, float, resize and hide panels (DOM, tape, positions, stats, alerts), so that my screen fits my workflow" — whose three scenarios are: dragging the DOM panel to the right edge docks it with a preview and persists its width; hiding the tape leaves it restorable from the view menu and by hotkey; floating a panel in the Electron shell opens a separate always-on-top window whose position persists per workspace. Its NFR is unambiguous: "docking has keyboard-accessible equivalents; floating windows are Electron-only and the control is hidden in the browser build with an explanation."

Surfaces: **SCR-021** Dock/panel system (drop zones, splitters, float), **SCR-024** Panel picker, **SCR-027** Floating panel window (Electron), **SCR-028** Panel context menu. Components: **CMP-214** DockDropZone, **CMP-215** FloatingWindowFrame, **CMP-216** PanelMenu, **CMP-213** FuzzyList, plus CMP-080/082 from E15-T02.

CMP-214's catalogue entry states the a11y rule as a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have: "drag-and-drop has a **mandatory** keyboard equivalent — 'Move panel' from CMP-216 PanelMenu opens a directional chooser (left/right/top/bottom/tab-into) so no layout operation is pointer-only." E15-T02 already made both paths share one resolver; this Story surfaces them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Drag docking (SCR-021)**: six drop targets (N/S/E/W/centre-tabify/float) highlighted with a 4 px accent and a translucent preview of the resulting rectangle; invalid-drop feedback ("Can't dock here"); drag preview on CSS transforms only; exactly one layout mutation on drop.
- **Keyboard docking**: "Move panel" in CMP-216 opens a directional chooser (left/right/top/bottom/tab-into) driving `resolveDirectionalMove`; splitters resize by `Alt+Shift+arrows`; a live region announces "Chart moved to bottom-right".
- **Panel picker (SCR-024)**: grouped catalogue from the pane registry with one-line descriptions, thumbnails and chips ("requires recording", "(estimated)" via CMP-227, "owner only"); fuzzy search (CMP-213); category headings as real headings; disabled entries state their reason; placement is previewed before insert; adding announces where the panel landed.
- **Panel menu (SCR-028)**: Settings…, Duplicate, Move to ▸, Float, Full screen, Sync group ▸, Reset settings, Copy panel link, Close — identical for every panel kind so muscle memory transfers; built from a static descriptor (no per-open API call); opens from the ⋮ button, `Shift+F10` and the context-menu key; disabled items show a reason; destructive items grouped last.
- **Hide/restore**: hiding a panel removes it from the grid but keeps it in the view menu and on its hotkey; minimised-to-tab state.
- **Full screen / maximise**: `F11` maximises the active panel; restoring returns it to its exact prior slot.
- **Floating windows (SCR-027, Electron only)**: pop a panel into an OS window with a slim title bar carrying panel name, symbol and environment badge (**CMP-215**, **CMP-075**), always-on-top option, "return to workspace" re-dock into the origin slot, per-workspace position persistence, and recovery to the primary display when a monitor disappears. The floating window participates in sync groups through the same in-process bus.
- **Browser fallback**: in the non-Electron build the float control degrades to a maximised overlay panel with an explanatory note — hidden-with-explanation, never a dead control.
- Panel-too-small state: below a pane's minimum size, the compact view is shown with its explanatory label (SCR-021).

## Out of scope
- The content of any panel; this Story mounts registry entries.
- Persisting the resulting layout — **E15-S03**.
- Sync group assignment UI beyond the menu entry that opens it — **E15-S04**.
- Multi-window *data* architecture (each floating window is its own renderer with its own GL context per SCR-027; the shared-worker WS client that makes that affordable is **E17**/**E11**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dragging a panel to an edge docks it with a preview
  Given a workspace with a chart and a DOM panel
  When the DOM panel is dragged toward the right edge
  Then the east drop zone highlights with a preview of the resulting rectangle
  And on release the panel docks there with exactly one layout mutation, and its width is part of the layout tree

Scenario: Every dock operation is reachable by keyboard
  Given a keyboard-only trader focused on a panel header
  When they open the panel menu with Shift+F10 and choose Move panel, then a direction
  Then the panel moves to the same position a pointer drop to that zone would have produced
  And a live region announces the new position once

Scenario: Invalid drops are refused visibly
  When a panel is dragged over a target that cannot accept it
  Then the cursor and an inline label state "Can't dock here" and releasing makes no change to the layout

Scenario: Hiding a panel keeps it recoverable
  When the tape panel is hidden
  Then it disappears from the grid and remains restorable from the view menu and by its hotkey, with its settings intact on restore

Scenario: Floating in Electron and re-docking
  Given the Electron shell and a chart panel
  When the panel is floated
  Then a separate window opens with the panel name, symbol and environment badge in its title, it can be set always-on-top, it still follows its sync group
  And re-docking returns it to its origin slot; its position is restored on the next launch of that workspace

Scenario: The browser build explains rather than pretends
  Given the app is running in a browser, not Electron
  When the trader opens the panel menu
  Then the float control is not offered as a working action, and an explanation states that floating windows require the desktop app

Scenario: A missing monitor does not lose the panel
  Given a floating panel was positioned on a second display that is no longer connected
  When the workspace is next opened
  Then the panel is restored onto the primary display rather than off-screen

Scenario: Unavailable panel kinds are disabled with a reason
  Given a panel kind whose feature is not enabled for this role or requires a recorded symbol
  When the panel picker is opened
  Then that entry is shown disabled with its reason stated, and it cannot be added
```

## Technical notes / design
Drag is pointer-events based with the preview drawn purely by CSS transform — the tree is not touched until drop, which is what keeps a drag from costing a layout pass per pointer move (SCR-021 performance line).

The float boundary is the interesting one. In Electron a floated panel is a separate renderer process with its own GL context (SCR-027), so the sync bus must reach across windows: R1 does this by keeping the workspace's sync state in the main process and mirroring it, rather than by attempting shared memory. SCR-027's budget — ≥58 fps across at most 4 GPU-heavy windows — is checked against E15-K01's numbers, and beyond that the shell warns.

Re-dock needs the origin slot to still be meaningful after the layout has changed underneath: store the origin as a pane id plus a fallback zone, and if the origin is gone, dock into the largest compatible container rather than failing.

The panel menu being a static descriptor (SCR-028: "not a per-open API call") is what holds the ≤80 ms open budget and makes the menu identical across panel kinds.

## Test plan
Unit: drop-zone geometry resolution, origin-slot fallback, hidden-panel registry, menu descriptor per kind. Component: drop-zone highlighting states, invalid drop, compact view at minimum size, picker search/filter/disabled reasons, menu keyboard open and roving focus. E2E Playwright (web): drag docking, hide/restore, maximise/restore, keyboard move path, browser float fallback notice. E2E Electron: float, always-on-top, badge presence in every window, re-dock, position persistence across relaunch, disconnected-display recovery (simulated). A11y: axe on SCR-021/024/027/028; manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass of the keyboard move flow and the floating window's independent focus scope; assertion that the floating window title includes the environment word (CMP-215). Perf: panel mount ≤150 ms, menu open ≤80 ms, drag at 60 fps, 4-window Electron FPS against SCR-027's ≥58 fps.

## Security notes
Floating windows are the notable surface: every window must repeat the DEMO/LIVE environment badge in its chrome and in its OS title (CMP-215, SCR-027) so a trader can never act in a detached window without knowing its environment — this is a safety control, and its absence is a release blocker, not a cosmetic bug. Windows are created with `nodeIntegration` off and `contextIsolation` on, inheriting E10's shell hardening; no window may be opened from untrusted input (an imported layout naming a panel kind is validated against the registry by E15-T02 before any window is created). "Copy panel link" produces an in-app route reference containing no tokens, no account ids and no user ids. Panel titles are user-influenced content rendered as text.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, and this Story carries the Epic's heaviest a11y load. No layout operation may be pointer-only (CMP-214, mandatory): the directional chooser is the keyboard twin of every drop zone. The panel menu is a full keyboard menu with type-ahead and shortcut hints, reachable via `Shift+F10` and the context-menu key (SCR-028). The picker's categories are real headings, each entry's one-line description is read with its name, and insertion announces placement ("CVD added to the right column", SCR-024). Each floating window is an independent document with its own title, skip link and focus scope, its title naming panel, symbol and environment (SCR-027). Splitters resize with `Alt+Shift+arrows`. All announcements are polite and fire once per committed operation.

## Performance notes
Panel mount ≤150 ms (SCR-024, CMP-080); menu open ≤80 ms (SCR-028); drag preview CSS-transform only with one mutation on drop (SCR-021); newly added panels subscribe WS topics only after mount, and the picker pre-warms nothing (SCR-024); Electron multi-window target ≥58 fps across ≤4 GPU-heavy windows (SCR-027), validated against E15-K01.

## Observability
`layout.panel_added {type, placement}`, `layout.panel_removed`, `layout.panel_moved {method: 'pointer'|'keyboard'}`, `layout.split_created`, `layout.panel_floated`, `layout.maximised`, `panel.redocked`, `window.opened`, `window.closed`, `panel.context_menu_opened`. Tracking `method` on moves is deliberate: it tells us whether the keyboard path is actually usable or merely present.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test, including the Electron-only ones.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on docking, picker, menu and float modules.
- [ ] SCR-021, SCR-024, SCR-027, SCR-028 design tickets Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior or waivers recorded; their sign-off checklists verified in the built UI.
- [ ] axe-core green on all four screens; manual screen-reader pass of the keyboard move flow signed off by the a11y specialist.
- [ ] Environment badge present in every floating window, verified by an Electron E2E assertion.
- [ ] Perf budgets recorded (mount, menu, drag, 4-window FPS).
- [ ] PRs ≤400 LOC each, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T02** (tree, drop resolution, registry), **E10** (Electron shell, window management, environment badge, view menu), **E05** (Menu, Dialog, Combobox, Card, Drawer tokens). Blocks **E15-S08**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-docking-and-float`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-005; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-021, SCR-024, SCR-027, SCR-028, SCR-020; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-080, CMP-082, CMP-213, CMP-214, CMP-215, CMP-216, CMP-227, CMP-075; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-LAY-005 row; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §11.3; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

title: SyncBus: cross-pane crosshair, symbol, interval and time-range propagation
body:
## Context
US-LAY-003's NFR is "sync propagation ≤1 frame", and SCR-023 is more specific about how: "crosshair sync must not trigger a React re-render — it dispatches straight into the engine (≤4 ms across 6 panels)". A crosshair moves on every pointer event; routing that through application state would put a React commit on the pointer path and blow the frame budget the moment a fourth pane joined.

The engine side already anticipates this. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2: "charts in a layout may share a `SyncGroup` for time range, crosshair position and/or price level, propagated once per frame after input integration (never re-entrantly)". `ChartOptions` carries `syncGroup?: string` and the engine emits a `sync` event carrying `{ groupId, timeRange, crosshair }` at ≤1/frame (§6). This Task builds the bus that connects those emitters to those consumers, and **CMP-196 MultiChartLinker** is its non-visual React binding.

The hard part is not fan-out; it is not looping. A propagates to B, B emits, B propagates back to A. The engine's "never re-entrantly" wording is the contract this Task must actually implement.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `SyncBus` in the app layer (not in `packages/dock`, not in the engine): group registry, per-axis membership, and a publish path that runs **once per animation frame**, after input integration, never during a pointer handler.
- Axes, independently toggleable per group, matching SCR-023's control set: `symbol`, `interval`, `crosshair`, `timeRange`, `drawings` (same-symbol only), `scale` (the last delegated to **E15-S05**), plus `account/group` selection reserved for R3.
- Loop suppression: an origin token on every propagation so a pane never re-emits a value it was just given; a per-frame coalescing buffer so N updates in one frame become one dispatch per subscriber; an assertion (dev builds) that fires if re-entrancy is ever observed.
- Timestamp-based crosshair alignment, not index-based: panes on different intervals align by time, and a pane whose interval has no bar at that timestamp shows the crosshair at the containing bar — SCR-023's "Chart 3 has a different interval — crosshair sync will align by timestamp" warning is driven from this.
- **CMP-196 MultiChartLinker**: the non-visual hook binding a DockGrid pane to its group, subscribing/unsubscribing on mount/unmount and on group change, with zero renders of its own.
- Persistence hooks: group membership and axis flags are read from and written to the layout (`layouts.crosshair_sync`, `layouts.symbol_sync`, `layouts.level_sync` plus per-pane group id in `pane_config`), so E15-S03 saves them without special-casing.
- A headless test harness with fake engine instances so fan-out, coalescing and loop suppression are unit-testable without a GPU.

## Out of scope
- The sync configuration UI (SCR-023, CMP-218) — **E15-S04**.
- Price-scale linking semantics and the incompatible-link refusal — **E15-S05**.
- Drawing synchronisation *content* (which drawings, how they merge) — **E14** owns drawings; this bus only carries the event on the same symbol.
- Cross-device or cross-window sync (a floated Electron window participates through the same in-process bus; two browser tabs do not sync in R1).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crosshair propagates within one frame without a React render
  Given panes 1, 2 and 3 are in group A with crosshair sync enabled
  When the pointer moves across pane 1
  Then panes 2 and 3 show the crosshair at the same timestamp on the next frame
  And a React profiler recording of the interaction shows zero component renders attributable to crosshair movement

Scenario: Propagation does not loop
  Given two panes in the same group with every axis enabled
  When a symbol change originates in pane 1
  Then pane 2 applies it exactly once, pane 1 receives no echo, and the dev-build re-entrancy assertion does not fire

Scenario: Groups are isolated
  Given panes 1 and 2 are in group A and pane 3 is in group B
  When any synced value changes in pane 1
  Then pane 2 updates and pane 3 is completely untouched, including its crosshair, symbol, interval and time range

Scenario: Axes are independent
  Given a group with symbol sync on and interval sync off
  When the symbol changes in one pane
  Then every member changes symbol and each member keeps its own interval

Scenario: Mismatched intervals align by timestamp
  Given a 1m pane and a 1h pane in one crosshair-synced group
  When the crosshair sits on the 14:37 bar in the 1m pane
  Then the 1h pane highlights the 14:00 bar that contains that timestamp, not the 37th bar from its right edge

Scenario: Budget holds at six panes
  Given six chart panes in one group with all axes enabled
  When the crosshair is swept for 5 seconds
  Then total sync work stays under 4 ms per frame and no frame exceeds 16.6 ms attributable to sync

Scenario: Leaving a group is clean
  Given a pane is removed from its group or unmounted mid-sweep
  Then it stops receiving updates immediately, no listener leaks, and the remaining members continue unaffected
```

## Technical notes / design
One bus per workspace, keyed by group id, holding weak references to engine handles rather than React components — the bus must outlive no component and hold up no unmount.

Publishing is scheduled, not immediate: a pointer handler writes into a per-frame slot and requests a frame; the flush runs after input integration, exactly as §4.2 specifies. That single choice gives coalescing, ordering and loop-freedom together, and it is why the bus lives in the app rather than inside the engine, which has no view of sibling instances.

The origin token is the pane id, not a boolean flag: with three-plus members, a boolean "applying" flag suppresses legitimate concurrent updates, while an origin token suppresses only the echo.

E15-K01's finding on propagation cost at 6 and 16 panes decides whether the flush stays on the main thread; if it recommends otherwise, the bus's scheduled-flush shape makes moving it a contained change.

## Test plan
Unit (headless, fake engines): fan-out per axis, group isolation, loop suppression with 2/3/6 members, coalescing (10 updates in one frame → 1 dispatch), timestamp alignment across intervals, unsubscribe on unmount and on group change, no listener leaks over 1000 mount/unmount cycles. Integration: real engine instances in a 4-pane DockGrid — crosshair sweep with a React profiler assertion of zero renders. Perf: the 6-pane sweep against the 4 ms budget, recorded. E2E: Playwright — assign panes to groups A and B, verify isolation and timestamp alignment visually via engine state, not pixels.

## Security notes
Purely in-process client state: no network, no persistence of anything beyond the flags already covered by E15-T01's validation. The only consideration worth stating is isolation — sync must never be a channel by which one pane reads another's account or environment binding, so the bus carries an explicit allow-list of axis payload shapes (`symbol`, `interval`, `timeRange`, `crosshair`, `priceLevel`) and rejects anything else, keeping R3's account-scoped sync a deliberate future addition rather than an accident.

## Accessibility notes
Sync changes are not announced per movement — a crosshair sweep announcing in every pane would be unusable. Announcements are limited to membership and axis changes ("Chart 2 joined sync group A"), emitted by **E15-S04**'s UI, not by the bus. The bus exposes the current group and axes so each panel's accessible name can include them (CMP-218 requires membership be conveyed by name and letter, never colour alone).

## Performance notes
≤1 frame propagation (US-LAY-003 NFR); ≤4 ms total across 6 panes (SCR-023); zero React renders on the crosshair path; ≤1 `sync` emission per frame per group (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §6). Measured against E15-K01's pane-count curve and benchmark B6.

## Observability
`sync.group_joined`, `sync.group_left`, `sync.axis_toggled` (emitted by the UI, defined here). Dev-build counters: dispatches per frame, suppressed echoes, re-entrancy assertion hits — surfaced in the engine debug overlay so a regression is visible while developing, not only in CI.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the SyncBus module.
- [ ] Zero-React-render assertion for the crosshair path present in CI, not just measured once.
- [ ] 6-pane perf number recorded against the 4 ms budget.
- [ ] CMP-196 Storybook/test entries per the catalogue.
- [ ] Re-entrancy assertion present in dev builds and documented.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T02** (panes must exist in a tree with stable ids), **E11** (`syncGroup`, the `sync` event and crosshair dispatch). Blocks **E15-S04**, **E15-S05**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-sync-bus`

## References
`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §4.2 pane synchronisation, §6 `sync` event, `ChartOptions.syncGroup`, R8, B6; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-003, US-LAY-004; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-023, SCR-049; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-196, CMP-218; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (`crosshair_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `level_sync`).


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/** (per Scope section), packages/chart-engine/test/**, packages/chart-engine/bench/** if perf-labelled
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Chart/Pane/SeriesHandle/ChartEvents/FrameStats/RenderContext/SeriesPlugin public API (26-chart-engine-design.md §8); worker protocol messages (§6); named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-196, CMP-218, SCR-023, SCR-049
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench (if perf-labelled) · pnpm lint · pnpm typecheck
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e15-sync-bus`
- PR title: `E15-T03: SyncBus: cross-pane crosshair, symbol, interval and time-range propagation`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E15-T03)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/tech, area/charting-ui, priority/p1, perf, qa

**Done means**
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the SyncBus module.
- [ ] Zero-React-render assertion for the crosshair path present in CI, not just measured once.
- [ ] 6-pane perf number recorded against the 4 ms budget.
- [ ] CMP-196 Storybook/test entries per the catalogue.
- [ ] Re-entrancy assertion present in dev builds and documented.

**Do NOT**
- No GL calls issued from scene-graph nodes — nodes append to batches only (26-chart-engine-design.md §3.1).
- No allocation in the hot render path; anything per-frame must come from an object pool.
- Do not widen a performance budget or edit a benchmark baseline to make a regression pass (AGENTS.md §8).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E15-T03 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.

title: STRIDE threat model for workspaces, layout persistence and export/import
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and the planning brief require a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes a threat-model kickoff a DoR item for any epic touching persisted user data. E15 looks cosmetic and is not: it introduces a **user-authored document that is persisted server-side and exchanged between users as a file**. That is a classic injection and deserialization surface, an authorization surface (`workspaces:read` / `workspaces:write`, scope `self`), and a stored-XSS surface (workspace and layout names rendered in tabs, menus and window titles).

US-LAY-007 makes it sharper: workspaces are exported as JSON and imported by *another user*, with the explicit requirement that the file contains no secrets and no account bindings, and that account-scoped elements are dropped with a report on import. An import path that trusts its input is how a "layout file" becomes a foothold.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/security/threat-models/e15-layouts-workspaces.md`, built from a data-flow diagram covering: browser dock state → debounced `PUT /workspaces/{id}/layouts/{id}` → API → Postgres (`workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, `chart_templates`); export `GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/export` → file → another user's import → validation → dock state; and the local autosave used for crash-restore.
- **STRIDE enumeration** per element and per flow, with at minimum:
  - **Spoofing** — importing a file that claims another user's workspace id or ownership; a floating window (`SCR-027`) misrepresenting DEMO/LIVE.
  - **Tampering** — a crafted layout document injecting unexpected pane kinds, oversized grids, cyclic/deeply nested trees, or a `chart_template_id` pointing at another user's template; tampering with the local autosave.
  - **Repudiation** — layout events are analytics-only by design (`SCR-021`); confirm nothing security-relevant hides in them and that `workspace.deleted`/`workspace.exported` are audited per `21-database-schema.md`.
  - **Information disclosure** — secrets, tokens, account ids, balances or symbol watchlists leaking through export files, window titles, panel names, error messages, or a cross-user `workspaceId` probe distinguishing 403 from 404.
  - **Denial of service** — unbounded pane counts, huge layout documents, import zip-bomb-equivalents (deeply nested JSON), write-storms against the 2-second debounce, and per-user workspace/layout count growth.
  - **Elevation of privilege** — an imported workspace causing a viewer to mount an owner-only panel, or a pane binding to an account the user cannot read; `workspaces:*` scope `self` being bypassed by a nested id.
- **Risk rating** (likelihood × impact) with the mitigation owner and the ticket that implements each mitigation; anything unmitigated is an explicit accepted risk with Owner sign-off.
- **Security requirements list** `SR-E15-nn` that `E15-X02` (abuse cases), `E15-X03` (SAST/DAST) and `E15-X04` (review) test against.

## Out of scope
- Auth and session design itself (E09) — consumed as an assumption, with the assumption stated.
- WS transport security (E17).
- Threats of the panels' own content (footprint, DOM, order ticket) — their epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model covers every flow
  Given the data-flow diagram
  Then every trust boundary crossing has at least one STRIDE entry, and every entry has a rating and a named mitigation owner

Scenario: Export contents are constrained by requirement, not by hope
  When the model analyses the export flow
  Then it produces an explicit allow-list of exportable fields and a denial rule for secrets, tokens, account ids and user ids
  And that allow-list is referenced by the export implementation ticket

Scenario: Failure case - an unmitigated high risk blocks the epic
  Given a High-rated threat with no mitigation
  Then the epic cannot reach Done until the mitigation ships or the Owner records an accepted risk with a review date

Scenario: Edge case - import from a newer schema version
  Given a workspace file exported by a newer app version
  Then the model requires refusal with both versions stated, not partial application, and treats partial application as a tampering risk

Scenario: Model is reviewed
  When the model is published
  Then it carries review from the Security engineer and the Architect, and is linked from the E15 epic ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Treat the imported workspace document as **fully untrusted input** even though it came from a colleague: validate against a strict JSON Schema (additionalProperties false), bound depth, node count, string lengths and numeric ranges before any of it reaches application state.
- Ids in an imported file must be *regenerated*, never honoured: importing must not let a caller assert `workspace_id`, `user_id`, `chart_template_id` or account references. This single rule kills most of the spoofing and EoP branches.
- Names are rendered in tabs, menus, live-region announcements and OS window titles — the model must require output encoding at every one of those sinks, not only the React ones (an Electron window title is not React).
- Bound the document: max panes per layout, max layouts per workspace, max workspaces per user, max serialized size; `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 already gives uniqueness constraints, and the model should demand 422 rather than 500 on violation.
- Note the RBAC shape from `24-internal-schemas.md` §3063: `workspaces:read` / `workspaces:write`, granted to owner/manager/viewer for *their own* resources — the model must verify "own" is enforced in the query, not in the handler's afterthought.

## Test plan
- The model is validated by review plus a tabletop: walk three attack narratives end-to-end (malicious import, cross-user probe, layout write-storm) and confirm the model predicted each.
- Every `SR-E15-nn` requirement must be testable; any requirement no one can write a test for is rewritten.
- Hand the requirement list to `E15-X02` and confirm each maps to at least one abuse case.

## Security notes
- This ticket *is* the security artefact; its own hygiene matters: the document names concrete endpoints and tables and avoids hand-waving categories.
- Explicitly record the assumption set inherited from E09 (authenticated session, deny-by-default RBAC, audit log) so a later change to those assumptions triggers a re-review.
- Classify a workspace export as *user-confidential*: it reveals which symbols a trader watches and how they trade, which is sensitive even without credentials.

## Accessibility notes
- Security controls must not be pointer-only or vision-only: the import rejection report, the dropped-elements report and the version-mismatch refusal must be text, keyboard-reachable and announced — a security message no one can perceive is not a control.
- The DEMO/LIVE environment indicator is a safety control; the model treats degrading it (including in floating windows and for screen-reader users) as a spoofing risk.

## Performance notes
- Validation must be bounded and cheap: schema validation of a 2 MB layout file completes in ≤500 ms in a worker (`SCR-026`) and must not be a DoS amplifier itself; the model records this as a requirement.
- Rate limits on workspace writes must protect the API without breaking the legitimate 2-second debounce; the model states the intended limit so `E15-X02` can test both sides.

## Observability
- Requires that import rejections emit `layout.import_rejected{reason}` with a bounded reason enum, and that repeated rejections from one user are visible in the ops dashboard as a possible probing signal.
- Requires that `workspace.deleted` and `workspace.exported` reach the append-only audit log, not merely analytics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Threat model published with DFD, full STRIDE enumeration, ratings, owners and `SR-E15-nn` requirements.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed by the Security engineer and the Architect.
- [ ] Every High/Critical threat has a mitigation ticket or a written accepted risk with a review date.
- [ ] Requirement list handed to `E15-X02` and `E15-X03` and referenced by the export/import story.
- [ ] Linked from the E15 epic and from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`'s per-epic index.

## Dependencies
- `E15-S02` (persistence shape must exist to model it); E09 auth/RBAC assumptions; `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1; `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*`.

## Branch
`chore/e15-threat-model`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` (permissions `workspaces:read`/`workspaces:write`)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-007


## Agent execution brief

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant sections)
4. docs/plan/20-architecture.md (apps/web module map)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- apps/web route contracts, Zustand/Jotai store shapes consumed by other routes; named identifiers in this ticket: SCR-021, SCR-026, SCR-027
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build · pnpm e2e · pnpm test:a11y
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**

- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E15-X01)

title: Hi-fi SCR-038/SCR-039 and design-system contribution for profile primitives
body:
## Context
The profile surface introduces three chart primitives that do not yet exist in the design system as anything more than a catalogue stub: **CMP-110 ProfileBar**, **CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane** and **CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane**, plus new usage of **CMP-135 VwapBandLegend**, **CMP-137 SessionVwapAnchorPicker**, **CMP-199 ChartLegend**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** and **CMP-228 PreviewTile**. `15-component-catalogue.md` already reserves the tokens `color.profile.bar`, `color.profile.poc`, `color.profile.valuearea`, `color.tpo.letter` and `color.tpo.initialbalance` — this ticket is where those tokens acquire actual values in both themes, and where the *non-colour* encodings that carry the same meaning are fixed.

This is the ticket that decides whether the panel is readable. Profiles stack up to seven distinct meanings on the same histogram (bar magnitude, buy/sell split, POC, value-area membership, HVN, LVN, naked POC, single print) and `16-design-system-brief.md` §6 plus `05-accessibility-standard.md` both forbid resolving that with hue alone. The answer must be a system — magnitude by length, membership by shading, singular levels by border/pattern plus a text label — not a palette.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi designs for **SCR-038** (docked and overlay, dark and light themes, three densities) and **SCR-039**, resolving every wireframe from E19-D02.
- Design-system contributions committed to the shared Figma library, each with a catalogue entry update in `15-component-catalogue.md`:
  - **CMP-110 ProfileBar**: volume / delta / TPO variants; POC, value-area, HVN, LVN, naked-POC and single-print states; split bid/ask rendering; zero-delta row distinguished from no-trading row (US-VP-007 scenario 3).
  - **CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane**: composite / multiples / visible / personalised period variants, developing vs final value-area treatment driven by `complete`.
  - **CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane**: letter blocks and profile forms, Initial Balance shading, single-print glyph, letter sizing at all three densities.
- Token proposals with measured contrast ratios for every new `color.profile.*` and `color.tpo.*` token in dark and light themes, plus the deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia simulation sheets.
- Non-colour encoding specification: a table mapping each of the eight meanings to its primary (non-colour) encoding and its secondary (colour) reinforcement.
- Extension-line treatment for "extend POC/VA lines to the right" and the naked-POC demotion state (US-VP-006 scenario 2), including the clutter cap ("nearest N, count of hidden ones").
- Storybook story list per component, aligned with the entries already named in `15-component-catalogue.md`.

## Out of scope
- Motion and recompute choreography — E19-D05.
- The formal a11y design review — E19-D06 (this ticket must *pass* it, not perform it).
- Footprint cell tokens (E18) — but this ticket must reuse E18's bid/ask hue decision rather than invent a parallel one.
- Engineering implementation and Storybook code; this ticket delivers the spec and the library entries.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every meaning survives a greyscale render
  Given the hi-fi SCR-038 frames are exported with all colour removed
  Then POC, value-area membership, HVN, LVN, naked POC, single prints and the buy/sell split each remain identifiable

Scenario: Token contrast is measured, not asserted
  When each new color.profile.* and color.tpo.* token is reviewed
  Then a measured contrast ratio against its background is recorded for both dark and light themes and meets the threshold in 05-accessibility-standard.md

Scenario: A zero-delta row is not an empty row
  Given a price level traded with exactly zero net delta
  And an adjacent price level did not trade at all
  Then the two render distinctly in both themes and in greyscale

Scenario: Naked POC clutter is capped
  Given more naked POCs exist than the configured limit
  Then only the nearest N are drawn and the design shows an explicit count of the hidden ones with a way to reveal them

Scenario: TPO letters stay legible at compact density
  Given the TPO pane is rendered at compact density with 30-minute periods over a full UTC day
  Then letter size, spacing and the Initial Balance shading are specified such that letters remain individually distinguishable, or a documented fallback rendering is specified

Scenario: The delta profile does not conflict with the footprint palette
  When the delta profile colours are compared with E18's footprint bid/ask colours
  Then they are the same token family or a written rationale for divergence exists
```

## Technical notes / design
These are WebGL-rendered primitives, not DOM components (`15-component-catalogue.md` tier: chart-primitive; `26-chart-engine-design.md` governs the render path). That imposes real constraints the hi-fi must respect: patterns and borders cost draw calls, text labels inside the histogram cost an atlas lookup, and anything specified as a per-row DOM element will be mirrored, not rendered. Specify encodings that a GPU renderer can produce cheaply — fill, length, a small set of border styles, a bounded label set — and state explicitly which elements are expected to be DOM-mirror-only.

POC tie-breaks are deterministic (`24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2: closest to period VWAP → closest to last price → lower ticks) and US-VP-004 scenario 3 requires the rule to be surfaced in the tooltip — design that tooltip copy here rather than leaving it to implementation. The `EstimatedBadge` (CMP-227) is mandatory whenever any part of the profile was built from bar-approximated volume, and its placement must make it impossible to read the histogram without seeing it.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification: contrast measured with the design-system contrast tooling; colour-blindness simulation sheets attached; a greyscale export reviewed at Design Review; and a render-feasibility walkthrough with a chart-engine engineer signing that each encoding is achievable within the frame budget.

## Security notes
No security surface — market-data visualisation only, no credentials, balances or account context. The design must not introduce any affordance that would imply per-account data on a shared market-data panel.

## Accessibility notes
The non-colour encoding table is the core a11y deliverable and is binding on implementation. Every derived level carries a text label or a mirrored DOM node with a text description per the CMP-110 catalogue entry ("same DOM-mirror-per-bar pattern as FootprintCell"). The table-alternative view designed in E19-D02 is given its full visual treatment here, including how POC/VAH/VAL membership is expressed as text in that table. Focus-visible treatment is specified for every interactive element including the histogram's own keyboard traversal.

## Performance notes
Each encoding is annotated with its expected render cost class so engineering can trade off before building: per-row patterns are flagged as expensive, per-row text as very expensive, fill and length as cheap. The 5 000-row budget from SCR-038 is restated as a design constraint, and the design specifies the bucketing appearance when rows exceed available pixel rows rather than deferring it.

## Observability
No new events beyond those annotated in E19-D02; this ticket confirms each annotated control's final position so the analytics spec can be frozen.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Hi-fi SCR-038 and SCR-039 complete in both themes and all three densities, every E19-D02 state resolved.
- [ ] CMP-110, CMP-183 and CMP-184 published in the shared Figma library with all variants, and `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated to match.
- [ ] All new tokens proposed with measured contrast ratios and accepted by the design-system team.
- [ ] Non-colour encoding table written and attached to the ticket.
- [ ] Greyscale export reviewed and passed at Design Review.
- [ ] Render-feasibility signed off by a chart-engine engineer.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded on the ticket; Status = Done.**

## Dependencies
- **E19-D02** supplies the structure this ticket surfaces.
- **E05** design system v0 supplies the token architecture and theming.
- **E18** footprint design supplies the bid/ask hue family the delta profile must align with.

## Branch
`design/e19-profile-hifi`

## References
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-110, CMP-135, CMP-137, CMP-183, CMP-184, CMP-199, CMP-227, CMP-228
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-038, SCR-039
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §2 tokens, §6 data-viz rules, §10 library structure
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §5.1, §5.2
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`
2. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`
3. `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`
4. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`
5. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`
6. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
Base area for `web`: apps/web/src/features/<feature>/ (+ apps/web/src/state, apps/web/src/app/routes as needed)
- Hi-fi designs for **SCR-038** (docked and overlay, dark and light themes, three densities) and **SCR-039**, resolving every wireframe from E19-D02.
- Design-system contributions committed to the shared Figma library, each with a catalogue entry update in `15-component-catalogue.md`:
- **CMP-110 ProfileBar**: volume / delta / TPO variants; POC, value-area, HVN, LVN, naked-POC and single-print states; split bid/ask rendering; zero-delta row distinguished from no-trading row (US-VP-007 scenario 3).
- **CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane**: composite / multiples / visible / personalised period variants, developing vs final value-area treatment driven by `complete`.
- **CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane**: letter blocks and profile forms, Initial Balance shading, single-print glyph, letter sizing at all three densities.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None identified beyond internal module boundaries named in Scope / Deliverables above; do not introduce a new public REST/WS surface without a contract-first change (AGENTS.md §3 step 4).

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e19-profile-hifi`
- PR title: `E19-D03: Hi-fi SCR-038/SCR-039 and design-system contribution for profile primitives`
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder until the issue number is assigned)
- Required reviewers: @CandleViewer/frontend (per `.github/CODEOWNERS` for the touched paths)
- Labels: `type/design`, `area/order-flow`, `priority/p0`, `design`, `a11y`

**Done means**
- Hi-fi SCR-038 and SCR-039 complete in both themes and all three densities, every E19-D02 state resolved.
- CMP-110, CMP-183 and CMP-184 published in the shared Figma library with all variants, and `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated to match.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.

- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).

title: Design the profile preset, period-anchoring and drawing-anchor flows
body:
## Context
Two flows in E19 are not screens and therefore fall through the SCR-038/SCR-039 design work, yet they are where most of the epic's interaction risk lives.

The first is **presets** (US-VP-009): applying a preset switches period type, row size, value-area %, VWAP overlay and node marking *together*, which means a single click can change everything a trader is looking at. Presets are stored per user and travel in the workspace export, so they also cross into E-layouts territory. The flow needs an unambiguous apply/save/overwrite/delete model, a visible indication of "modified from preset", and a recovery path when a preset is applied by accident.

The second is **anchoring** (US-VP-002, and the roadmap line for E19 which explicitly names "profile anchoring to drawings and to sessions"). A profile can be anchored to a bar and accumulate forward indefinitely, pinned to a fixed timestamp range created by a drag selection, or attached to a drawing object owned by E14 so that moving the drawing moves the profile. Each of those is a distinct direct-manipulation gesture on the chart canvas, competing for the same mouse with drawing tools, chart trading and pan/zoom.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Preset flow design covering: apply · save-as-new · overwrite existing · rename · delete · reset-to-default · "modified" indication · undo after an accidental apply. Includes the empty state (no presets yet) and the conflict state (name already used).
- Period-anchoring flow design covering: initiating a fixed-range drag selection on the chart, adjusting its handles afterwards, converting a fixed range into an anchored forward-accumulating profile, and removing an anchor.
- Drawing-anchor flow design: attaching a profile to an existing drawing object, the visual indication that the attachment exists, the behaviour when the drawing is moved, resized, locked or deleted, and the behaviour when the drawing is cloned into a sync group.
- Gesture-conflict matrix: for each modifier/drag combination on the chart canvas, which of drawing tools (E14), chart trading (E-ORD), pan/zoom and profile anchoring wins, and how the cursor communicates the active mode. Delivered as a table reviewed jointly with the E14 design owner.
- Keyboard-only equivalents for every gesture above, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` — no profile capability may be mouse-exclusive.
- Copy for every confirmation, warning and empty state in these flows.

## Out of scope
- Workspace export/import format and the layout manager itself.
- The drawing tools' own creation and editing flows (E14) — this ticket only specifies the attachment contract.
- Server-side preset storage design and the settings API shape.
- Alerts on profile levels (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A preset apply is recoverable
  Given a trader has customised a profile and then applies a preset by accident
  When the flow is reviewed
  Then a single, discoverable action restores the previous settings and the design states how long that affordance remains available

Scenario: Modified-from-preset is visible
  Given a preset is applied and then one setting is changed
  Then the design shows an explicit modified indication and offers both overwrite and save-as-new

Scenario: A deleted drawing does not orphan a profile
  Given a profile is anchored to a drawing
  When the drawing is deleted
  Then the design specifies whether the profile is removed, converted to a fixed range, or blocked with a confirmation, and shows the resulting state

Scenario: Gestures do not collide silently
  Given the gesture-conflict matrix is reviewed with the E14 design owner
  Then every modifier/drag combination has exactly one owner and a specified cursor, with no cell marked undecided

Scenario: Every gesture has a keyboard path
  When the flows are reviewed against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  Then creating, adjusting, anchoring and removing a profile range are each achievable using the keyboard alone

Scenario: A preset name collides
  When a trader saves a preset using a name that already exists
  Then the design shows an inline conflict state offering overwrite or rename, and never silently replaces the existing preset
```

## Technical notes / design
Anchoring maps onto `ProfilePeriod.kind` values `fixed_range` (start/end pinned to timestamps), `visible_range` (recomputed on pan/zoom, throttled to ≤10 Hz per US-VP-002 with a debounce on pan end) and `composite` (`composite_of` listing merged period ids). The design must make the *throttled* nature of visible-range mode legible — a profile that visibly lags a fast pan is correct behaviour, and a trader must be able to tell that apart from a stalled feed, reusing E17's degraded-feed vocabulary rather than inventing a new one.

Drawing anchoring depends on drawing objects having stable identity across edits; confirm with the E14 design owner that the identity model supports attachment before specifying behaviour on clone-into-sync-group. Presets are per user and included in workspace export, so the naming and scoping model must not assume a single symbol or a single chart — a preset applies to any profile instance for any symbol (US-VP-009 scenario 2).

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification: a click-through prototype of the preset flow and the anchoring gestures walked through with the Owner; the gesture-conflict matrix reviewed and countersigned by the E14 design owner; keyboard paths walked through by the accessibility specialist ahead of the formal review in E19-D06.

## Security notes
Presets are user-scoped and contain only display configuration — no account, key or position data. The design must not allow a preset to carry anything that would be sensitive if exported with a workspace and shared, and the export surface is annotated accordingly.

## Accessibility notes
Every gesture specified here has a documented keyboard equivalent and an announced outcome (range created, anchor set, preset applied). E06/E21-K01 produce that evidence.

- Layout of: header controls (depth, scale, trail, cell size, ARM, env badge), heatmap pane (time →), ladder columns (price, bid size, ask size, last-trade tape column, cumulative depth, own-order column, position marker), footer (qty presets, BUY/SELL/FLAT/CXL rendered **disabled** for E21), detector strip.
- Non-colour encoding spec for bid/ask: column position + `B`/`A` text label + the colour convention, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §5.
- Focus order, focus-visible treatment and the row action-menu affordance for `Enter`.
- Redlines + token mapping; Figma → `docs/design/specs/scr-050.md` summary committed to the repo.

## Out of scope


Ladder rows must be ≥24 CSS px at default density (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8) — this constrains how many rows fit and therefore how the 500-depth tier is presented (scrolling vs aggregation). The design must make the demo/live badge and the disabled-trading state unmistakable — the safety property that a trader never believes a frozen book is live (SR-038). No secrets in Figma; no real account identifiers in mock data.

Drawn against `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 (keyboard), §4 (density/roving tabindex), §5 (colour independence), §6.1–6.3 (DOM mirror, windowed tree, table alternative). The grid alternative must be presented as equal-status, not a fallback.

Any drawn affordance that would require per-cell DOM nodes at heatmap density is rejected at review — CMP-111 is explicitly texture-backed with a windowed accessible summary.

Design annotates where `dom.depth_changed` and `degraded.entered` surface to the user.

title: UX research: how traders read the tape and size on the chart
body:
## Context
E22 introduces SCR-053 (Tape / Time & Sales + big-trade bubbles panel) — a net-new interaction surface: a high-rate scrolling print feed plus a chart overlay of size markers. Before wireframes are drawn we need evidence on how the Owner and the account managers (`docs/plan/10-personas.md` P1 order-flow trader, M1 manager) actually read aggression: which columns they scan first, at what density they stop being able to read rows, whether they prefer pause-on-hover or an explicit pause, and what threshold they instinctively reach for. Design runs ≥2 sprints ahead of the S12 engineering work (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` design-ahead rule), so this lands in Sprint 10.

Relevant story NFRs that the research must pressure-test: US-BIG-001 ("2 000 prints per second … the tape coalesces per frame … and shows the coalescing factor"), US-BIG-002 scenario 3 ("threshold would flag more than 20% of prints → a warning suggests raising it"), US-BIG-003 ("radius scaled by notional (linear or log)"), US-BIG-006 (filters and column set).

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3–4 moderated sessions (Owner + ≥2 account managers) using a clickable/recorded prototype of a live tape at 3 print rates (50/s, 500/s, 2 000/s) and a chart with bubbles at 3 densities.

- A recommended default configuration for SCR-053 that D02 will wireframe.
- Explicit list of open questions handed to D02 as design hypotheses.

## Out of scope
- Visual design, tokens, hi-fi comps (D02/D03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given a prototype showing tape rates of 50, 500 and 2000 prints per second
  When at least three participants including the Owner have completed a session
  Then a findings memo records, per participant, the readable density ceiling and the preferred column order

Scenario: A default configuration is recommended
  When the research is synthesised
  Then a single recommended default column set, density, pause model, bubble scale and threshold mode is stated with the evidence for each choice

Scenario: A hypothesis is contradicted
  Given the pre-registered hypothesis that traders prefer log bubble scaling
  When participants disagree
  Then the memo records the disagreement, the chosen default, and a follow-up question for D06 design QA rather than silently keeping the hypothesis
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype can be a throwaway React harness replaying a recorded BTCUSDT fixture (the same recorded-session fixtures listed in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`) — it does not need the real engine. Record sessions with consent; store notes with participant initials only.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validity controls: pre-registered hypotheses, same fixture window per participant, questions asked in fixed order.

## Security notes
Session recordings may contain account context on screen — use a demo account and redact any account identifiers before storing. Data classification: internal.

## Accessibility notes
Include at least one session run keyboard-only and one with the OS screen reader active, to ground the `role="log"` / `aria-live="off"` decision documented in SCR-053 before it is locked in D02.

## Performance notes
The prototype must reproduce the real print rates (up to 2 000/s) or the density findings are worthless; instrument it to report the actual achieved rate.

## Observability
N/A.

Findings memo merged and linked from the SCR-053 entry; recommended defaults accepted by the Chief Design Officer; open questions filed onto E22-D02; sessions and consent recorded; no engineering ticket in E22 quotes a default that contradicts the memo without a recorded waiver.

`E08` supplies the recorded trade fixtures used by the prototype.

title: UX research: how traders study a recorded session and what replay must not hide
body:
## Context
Replay is a *study* tool, not a playback toy: the trader is trying to answer "why did this move happen and would I have seen it live?". Getting the interaction wrong in either direction is expensive — too little control and the tool is useless for post-mortems (US-RPL-007 navigation aids exist precisely because scrubbing blindly through a day finds nothing), too much chrome and the study surface competes with the chart it exists to explain.

Two risks make research mandatory before pixels. First, **replay-vs-live confusion**: SCR-097's sign-off explicitly requires "REPLAY chrome cannot be confused with live", and a trader who mistakes replay for live can act on stale prices. Second, **recorder-dependent emptiness** (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §global conventions rule 3): replay depth equals recorder depth, so the honest empty/partial states are the normal case in the first weeks, not an edge case.

This ticket produces the evidence that D02-D05 design against. It is scheduled in Sprint 07 so that the hi-fi work lands in the D-S08 design sprint (`30-release-roadmap.md` §1.2, "Replay UI, alerts UI"), two sprints ahead of the E26 frontend stories in Sprint 11+.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Structured sessions with the Owner and the two account managers (the entire real user population) covering: how they currently post-mortem a trade; what they would step through tick-by-tick versus scan at speed; what "notable moment" means to them (feeding US-RPL-007's event-jump list).
- Competitive teardown of replay UX in TradingView Bar Replay, ATAS and Sierra Chart: transport layout, speed affordances, how each signals replay mode, how each handles missing data.
- A findings memo committed at `docs/research/ux/replay-study-sessions.md` with: the ranked task list, the moment-finding vocabulary, and a recommendation on default speed presets measured against the catalogue set (0.5x/1x/2x/4x/10x/25x/100x on SCR-097 vs CMP-171's 0.5x/1x/2x/5x/10x/25x/50x/100x — the discrepancy must be resolved here and the winner written back into `15-component-catalogue.md`).
- A decision on the replay-mode signalling pattern (chrome border + clock + badge) to be validated in D06's a11y review, including a colour-blind-safe and a reduced-chrome variant.
- Concrete answers, recorded as design constraints for D02: does the trader want live panes beside replaying panes (US-RPL-005 opt-out), and is paper trading in replay (US-RPL-006) expected to feel like the real ticket or a deliberately distinct surface?

## Out of scope
- Any hi-fi or wireframe artefact (D02-D05).

```gherkin
Scenario: Findings are evidence, not opinion
  Given the research sessions are complete
  When the memo is reviewed by the CDO and the E26 tech lead
  Then every design recommendation in it cites at least one observed session moment or a competitor teardown finding
  And open questions are listed explicitly rather than resolved by assumption

  When the memo is signed off
  Then one canonical preset list is chosen with a stated rationale
  And a doc-reconciliation action is filed against E26-T07

Scenario: Replay-mode signalling is validated with users
  Given at least two candidate signalling treatments
  When participants are shown a screenshot for 2 seconds and asked "is this live?"
  Then the chosen treatment is identified correctly by every participant
  And the result is recorded in the memo
```

## Technical notes / design
Constraints to carry into the sessions: replay reuses the terminal's dockable panel set (SCR-097 wireframe), so the transport bar is the only net-new chrome on the study surface; sessions are server-side objects with a 2 h idle reclaim; speeds above 25x disable paper fills (SCR-097 validation rules); the scrubber's track must render recorded / partial / missing coverage from `GET /market/data-coverage`.

N/A for automated tests. Validation method: moderated think-aloud, 5 tasks per participant (start a session over a known window, find the biggest print of the hour, step back through a trade, discover a recorder gap, resume yesterday's session). Success threshold recorded per task.

Research artefacts must not include real API keys, account identifiers or balances; screenshots used in the memo are taken against the demo environment with synthetic accounts. Data classification: none beyond internal.

## Accessibility notes
At least one participant session includes keyboard-only operation of the current chart surface, to inform the transport-control hotkey map before it is drawn. The signalling recommendation must not rely on colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AA, `05-accessibility-standard.md`).

Research must surface the perceived-latency expectation for scrub (users typically expect "instant"); record the tolerance observed so D02 can design the honest seeking state against the 1 s p95 / 2 s ceiling budget rather than pretending seek is free.

Per-tick rule evaluation stays plain code (BENCH-2: 381 ev/s vs 2,000 needed); nothing here touches the §3 hot-path exclusion list (CV-LINT-HOTPATH). Contract suite budget < 60 s.
