title: Build the Playwright E2E suite for chart interaction, multi-pane and sync
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E at the top of the pyramid: few tests, high value, covering the paths that only exist when everything is assembled. For the chart engine that means the interaction paths — a real pointer dragging a real canvas in a real browser, with a real worker decoding real frames — which is precisely where the unit tests' assumptions get tested.

This suite also covers **multi-pane and cross-chart sync** (E11-S09, CMP-196), which is untestable at any lower level: sync is a property of several chart instances interacting through a shared worker, and a unit test of the propagation function cannot tell you whether two charts actually stay aligned.

The suite runs in **both web and Electron**, since Electron is the primary shell and has its own process model.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright suite in `packages/chart-engine/test/e2e` (and the `apps/web` harness route it drives), running against **Chromium** and **Electron**.
- **Interaction**: drag-to-pan; wheel zoom at cursor with the anchored-point invariant asserted; `Shift+wheel` horizontal pan; `Ctrl+wheel` price zoom; time-axis drag to compress/expand; double-click reset; momentum settling; pinch-zoom via synthesised touch.
- **Keyboard**: full keyboard-only traversal — focus the chart, step the data cursor, rescale both axes, reset, open the table with `Alt+T` — with **no pointer events dispatched at all** in those specs, so a regression that makes something pointer-only fails the suite.
- **Scales**: each mode via the SCR-043 menu, autoscale engage/disengage, lock badge appearance, double-click restore, and the log-unavailable case.
- **Crosshair**: pointer and keyboard movement, readout values asserted against fixture data, countdown display and its warn state, magnet behaviour.
- **Multi-pane** (E11-S09): pane stacking, splitter drag **and keyboard resize**, collapse/restore, height-ratio persistence.
- **Sync groups** (CMP-196): time-range, crosshair and price-level sync across 2–4 panes and across 2 chart instances; assertion that propagation happens **exactly once per group per frame** and that a subscriber applying a sync does not re-publish.
- **Cross-instance**: the SCR-049 multi-chart grid case with 4 charts sharing one worker.
- Fixture-driven with a **fake WS server** replaying a recorded session, so tests are deterministic and hermetic.
- Flake controls: no arbitrary sleeps (wait on engine-emitted events), deterministic virtual clock where possible, and a quarantine lane with a mandatory ticket for anything that flakes.

## Out of scope
- Perf measurement — **E11-Q03** (E2E timings are too noisy to gate on).
- Accessibility conformance — **E11-Q05** (this suite asserts keyboard *functionality*, not WCAG conformance).
- Chaos scenarios — **E11-Q04**.
- Series, indicator, drawing and footprint behaviour — those Epics' own E2E additions, which extend this harness.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The keyboard-only specs dispatch no pointer events
  Given the keyboard traversal specs
  When they execute
  Then no pointer, mouse or touch event is dispatched anywhere in those specs
  And every assertion still passes, proving the paths are genuinely keyboard-operable

Scenario: Cursor-anchored zoom holds its invariant under real input
  Given the pointer is over the bar at a known timestamp
  When the wheel is scrolled to zoom in and then back out
  Then that timestamp remains under the cursor throughout, within one pixel
  And the assertion is made on the rendered viewport, not on an internal call

Scenario: Sync propagates exactly once per frame
  Given four charts in one sync group
  When the crosshair moves on chart 1
  Then charts 2, 3 and 4 update in the same frame
  And an instrumentation counter confirms exactly one propagation per group per frame, with no echo

Scenario: The suite runs in both Chromium and Electron
  When the suite executes in CI
  Then every spec runs in both runtimes
  And an Electron-only failure is reported as such rather than being hidden behind a Chromium pass

Scenario: The suite is deterministic
  Given the same commit and the same fixture
  When the suite runs ten times
  Then it passes ten times
  And any spec that does not is quarantined with a ticket rather than retried silently

Scenario: Splitters are operable by keyboard
  Given a pane splitter has focus
  When arrow keys are pressed
  Then the pane ratio changes by the specified step and the new value is announced
  And the same end state is reachable as by dragging
```

## Technical notes / design
**Waiting on events, not on time.** The engine emits `viewport`, `frame` and `pick` messages; the harness exposes them on `window.__engineEvents` so specs await a real state change rather than `waitForTimeout`. Arbitrary sleeps are the primary cause of flaky rendering tests and are banned in this suite by lint rule, not by convention.

**Synthesising gestures.** Playwright's `mouse.wheel` and `touchscreen` APIs cover wheel and pinch; momentum requires dispatching a pointer sequence with realistic timestamps, so the harness provides a `flick(dx, dy, durationMs)` helper that produces a physically plausible velocity — a flick synthesised as two events a frame apart produces an absurd velocity and tests nothing real.

**Electron specifics.** The Electron runner uses `_electron.launch` against the built app; the worker and OffscreenCanvas paths differ subtly from the browser (different process model, different GPU process behaviour), which is exactly why both runtimes are required rather than assumed equivalent.

**Sync assertion.** Propagation counting uses the `engine.sync.propagations_per_frame` counter from E11-S09 — an assertion on observable instrumentation rather than on timing, which is what makes "exactly once per frame" testable at all.

## Test plan
The suite is the deliverable; its own quality gates:
- **Self-verification**: each spec is confirmed to fail against a deliberately broken build (sync disabled, keyboard handler removed), so a spec that can never fail is caught.
- **Determinism**: 10 consecutive green runs required before a spec joins the required check.
- **Runtime**: the full suite <=15 minutes so it can run on every PR.
- **Traceability**: every spec names the E11-Q01 plan case or user-story scenario it automates.

## Security notes
Test-only code with synthetic fixtures; no credentials and no real account data. The fake WS server binds to localhost only and serves recorded fixture frames.

One control worth naming: the E2E harness route (`/__engine-harness`) exposes engine internals on `window` for assertions, and it must be **excluded from production builds** — a debug surface that ships is a genuine information-disclosure path. This is enforced by a build-time check and verified in **E11-X02**'s rule set, not left to reviewer vigilance.

## Accessibility notes
The keyboard-only specs are this suite's most valuable accessibility contribution: they assert that every chart capability is reachable without a pointer, which is `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6's requirement expressed as an executable test. A change that makes a feature drag-only or hover-only fails here, immediately, rather than being found in a manual pass months later.

The suite also asserts splitter keyboard resize, `Alt+T` table access and focus restoration on dialog close. Full WCAG conformance auditing (axe-core, screen readers, contrast) is **E11-Q05**.

## Performance notes
E2E timings are deliberately **not** used as performance gates — browser automation adds variance that swamps the signal, and a flaky perf gate is worse than none. Budgets are measured by the benchmark harness (E11-T06) and signed off in **E11-Q03**. The suite does assert that interactions complete within generous liveness timeouts, which catches a hang rather than a slowdown.

## Observability
Playwright HTML report, traces and videos published as CI artefacts on failure. Per-spec pass rate tracked over time so a spec degrading toward flakiness is visible before it becomes a nuisance and gets retried into meaninglessness.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts (plan, charters, scripts, suites) committed to the repo, not held in a personal document.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the Gherkin acceptance criterion or the user story it verifies, so coverage is traceable rather than asserted.
- [ ] Execution results recorded with pass/fail per scenario and evidence (logs, screenshots, recordings, benchmark artefacts) attached.
- [ ] Defects filed with reproduction steps, environment, severity and `priority/*`, linked to the E11 ticket they came from.
- [ ] Automated suites wired into CI at the correct stage and green; flaky tests quarantined with a ticket, never silently retried.
- [ ] Coverage contribution recorded against the package thresholds (>= 85 % engine, >= 80 % web).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET with pass/fail per scenario and any deviation stated explicitly.
- [ ] Test plan reviewed by the chart-engine lead so the black-box view and the implementation view are reconciled.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S09** — multi-pane and sync are a major part of the suite.
- **E11-Q01** — the plan this automates.
- **E11-S04**..**S07** — the interactions under test.
- Extended by **E12**, **E13**, **E14**, **E18**, **E21** for their own surfaces; feeds **E11-Q06**'s regression pack.

## Branch
`test/chart-engine-e2e` · 2 PRs (harness + interaction specs; multi-pane + sync + Electron runner), each <=400 LOC.

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` — test pyramid, coverage floors, fixture conventions, flake policy
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` — budgets, measurement method, regression gate
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` — WCAG 2.2 AA target, canvas strategy, manual pass requirements
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` — QA sign-off gates per Kind
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 (benchmarks), §14 (test strategy)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §5 CHART — US-CHART-006, 007, 008, 010, 014
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-196 MultiChartLinker (integration-test requirement)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-049 (multi-chart grid)
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §7 (required checks)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)
2. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §4.3/§4.4 (frame budgets, degradation order)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §6 (canvas/WebGL accessibility, DOM mirror)
4. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**

- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.

title: Establish and sign off the engine performance baselines against the budgets
body:
## Context
E11-T06 builds the benchmark harness and wires it as a required check. This ticket is the **human** half: running the full suite on the reference machine, comparing every number against the budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13, deciding whether the engine meets its contract, and recording a sign-off that the R1 PRR can rely on.

The distinction matters because a green CI check answers "is this worse than last week?" while a PRR needs "is this good enough to ship?" — and those are different questions. R1 exit criterion 1 requires "p95 <=16.6 ms with 100k bars + all R1 overlays on reference hardware in Electron", and somebody has to state, with evidence, whether that is true.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Full benchmark execution on the **reference machine** (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §1: Windows 11, Ryzen 7 / 8 cores, 32 GB, RTX 3060, 2560×1440 @125 %, pinned Electron build) in **both Chromium and Electron**.
- Scenarios: **B1** (pan, <=12 ms, <=8 draw calls), **B2** (zoom sweep, <=14 ms, <=6 LOD changes), **B5** (combined, <=16.7 ms, <=40 draw calls), **B6** (4 synced charts, <=16.7 ms aggregate, worker CPU <=70 % of one core), **B9** (cold init <=900 ms, atlas <=5 ms), **B10** (30-min soak, peak <=600 MB, growth <=5 %).
- **Budget #2 verification**: the 30 fps floor under the B6 worst case, with the degradation ladder active — measured, not inferred, since this is the number that decides whether the product is usable on a bad day.
- **Per-stage attribution** across the nine `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 stages for B5, so the frame budget's internal allocation is evidenced and future regressions have a comparison point.
- **Memory verification**: measured usage vs the §7 model (~116 MB for the 100k-bar case), and the E11-S15 estimator's ±20 % accuracy claim independently confirmed.
- **Input-to-photon** (requirement R6: <=2 frames for pan/zoom/crosshair) measured with high-speed capture or the instrumented WS->pixel path.
- **Baseline commit**: the signed-off numbers become the stored baselines the CI gate compares against, with the runner's GPU, driver and Chromium versions recorded alongside them.
- **Sign-off document**: scenario, budget, measured value, verdict, and for anything not met, a named remediation ticket and owner.
- **Degradation-ladder verification**: forced over-budget conditions, confirming the ladder sheds in the specified order and never sheds a trading-critical overlay.

## Out of scope
- Building the harness — **E11-T06**.
- Backend API/WS load testing — E46 and the platform Epics.
- Optimisation work arising from findings — filed as tickets, executed by the engine team.
- Benchmarks for surfaces owned elsewhere (B3 footprint, B4 heatmap, B7 update storm, B8 drawings) — E18, E21, E17, E14, though their gates are registered in T06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every budget has a measured verdict
  Given the budgets in 06-performance-and-load-standard.md and 26-chart-engine-design.md section 13
  When the sign-off document is complete
  Then each has a measured value and a pass or fail verdict on the reference machine
  And any fail carries a named remediation ticket with an owner, not a note to revisit later

Scenario: The 30 fps floor is measured under the worst case
  Given benchmark B6 with every R1 overlay enabled and the degradation ladder active
  When frame rate is sampled over the run
  Then the minimum sustained frame rate is recorded
  And the budget-2 verdict is based on that measurement rather than on the absence of complaints

Scenario: The ladder sheds in the specified order
  Given frames are forced over budget
  When the degradation ladder runs
  Then shedding follows the 4.4 order exactly
  And no order line, position line, SL or TP is shed at any rung

Scenario: The memory estimator's accuracy claim is independently verified
  Given the E11-S15 estimator predicts a footprint for a 30-day 1-minute load
  When the actual footprint is measured after loading
  Then the prediction is within 20 % of actual
  And the verification is performed by QA, not only by the estimator's own calibration test

Scenario: Baselines are committed with their environment recorded
  When the signed-off numbers become CI baselines
  Then the GPU model, driver version and Chromium build are recorded with them
  And a later driver upgrade invalidates the baselines explicitly instead of appearing as a mysterious regression

Scenario: Electron and Chromium are both reported
  When the suite is run
  Then results are reported separately for both runtimes
  And Electron is treated as the primary result, since it is the shipping shell
```

## Technical notes / design
**Method.** Three repetitions per scenario, median of p95 taken, per E11-T06's stability analysis. The machine is prepared identically each run: no other applications, power plan set to high performance, GPU at a settled thermal state (a benchmark run on a cold GPU and one on a hot GPU differ by more than the gate threshold).

**Why measure input-to-photon separately.** Frame time and latency are different properties: an engine can hold 16 ms frames while being three frames behind the input, and the chart would feel sluggish despite perfect benchmark numbers. R6's <=2 frames is measured either with a high-speed camera against a marker or via the instrumented WS->pixel path (E11-T07), and the method used is recorded.

**Per-stage attribution** is the part that pays off later: knowing that B5's 15 ms is 3 ms decode / 2 ms model / 4 ms batch / 5 ms GL / 1 ms present means a future regression can be attributed in minutes. Recording only the total makes every future investigation start from zero.

## Test plan
Verification of the measurements themselves:
- Repeatability: three runs per scenario with variance reported; a scenario whose variance exceeds 3 % is investigated before its number is trusted.
- Cross-check: engine-reported frame times cross-checked against Chrome DevTools tracing for at least one scenario, so a self-reported metric is validated against an independent one.
- The degradation-ladder verification is executed manually as well as automatically, because the specified *order* is easier to confirm by observation than by assertion.

## Security notes
Synthetic fixtures only; no real account data enters a benchmark. The sign-off document contains timing and memory data and is safe to attach to the PRR.

One note for the PRR record: benchmark results are gathered on the reference machine, which is not necessarily representative of every machine the terminal will run on. The sign-off states this limitation explicitly rather than implying universal coverage — the GPU matrix (**E11-Q07**) is the complementary evidence, and a PRR that reads only this document should know that.

## Accessibility notes
Benchmarks run with the **DOM mirror active**, so the accessibility layer's cost is inside the measured budget rather than excluded from it. This is stated in the sign-off because an engine benchmarked with accessibility disabled would produce numbers that do not describe the shipping product. The mirror's <=1 ms/frame budget is verified as part of the B5 stage attribution.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance verification. Budgets: **#1** (16.6 ms p95, 100k bars + 200-depth heatmap at 100 ms), **#2** (30 fps floor, worst case), **#14** (100 ms heatmap cadence — prepared here, gated in E21). Requirements **R6** (<=2 frames input-to-photon) and **R7** (<=600 MB per instance). Gates B1, B2, B5, B6, B9, B10. R1 exit criterion 1 depends on this sign-off.

## Observability
Sign-off document committed to `docs/plan/` and linked from the R1 PRR. Baselines committed to the repo with their environment metadata. Per-stage attribution published as a reference artefact so future regressions have a documented comparison point.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts (plan, charters, scripts, suites) committed to the repo, not held in a personal document.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the Gherkin acceptance criterion or the user story it verifies, so coverage is traceable rather than asserted.

- [ ] Coverage contribution recorded against the package thresholds (>= 85 % engine, >= 80 % web).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET with pass/fail per scenario and any deviation stated explicitly.
- [ ] Test plan reviewed by the chart-engine lead so the black-box view and the implementation view are reconciled.
- [ ] Every budget and benchmark gate has a measured value and a verdict.
- [ ] Baselines committed with GPU, driver and Chromium versions recorded.
- [ ] Per-stage attribution for B5 published.
- [ ] Failures carry named remediation tickets with owners.
- [ ] Sign-off countersigned by the chart-engine lead and the Architect, and attached to the R1 PRR evidence pack.

## Dependencies
- **E11-T06** — the harness that produces the numbers.
- **E11-S15** — memory governance must be in place before memory budgets mean anything.
- **E11-S12** — the degradation ladder under verification.
- Feeds the **R1 PRR** and `30-release-roadmap.md` §5's exit criteria.

## Branch

## References

- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` — budgets, measurement method, regression gate
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` — WCAG 2.2 AA target, canvas strategy, manual pass requirements

title: Stack panes on a shared time axis and sync range, crosshair and levels
body:
## Context
Multi-pane is structural, not cosmetic: the volume sub-pane of `US-CHART-002`, the CVD/OI/funding panes of R2 (E23/E24) and the indicator panes of E13 are all `Pane` instances stacked under one shared time axis. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.1 fixes the tree and §3.5 fixes the rule that makes it coherent: **"panes in one chart share `timeStart/timeEnd` by construction"**, while charts in a layout may share a `SyncGroup` for time range, crosshair position and/or price level, "propagated once per frame after input integration (never re-entrantly)".

**CMP-196 MultiChartLinker** is the non-visual coordinator for that: props `groupId`, `linkedPanes`, `syncModes {crosshair, levels, scale}`, with the a11y requirement that sync-state changes are "announced once via a shared status region (*Panes linked: crosshair, levels*)".

The re-entrancy rule is the trap. A naive implementation where pane A's crosshair sets pane B's, which broadcasts back to A, produces either an infinite loop or a one-frame oscillation that looks like jitter. The design forbids it explicitly; this story implements the forbidding.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Pane stacking in the layout engine: N panes in one chart, vertical order fixed by insertion, per-pane `heightRatio` (`Pane.setHeightRatio`, §8) normalised so ratios always sum to 1, with a minimum pane height below which a pane collapses to a labelled stub rather than rendering illegibly.
- Drag-to-resize splitters between panes, with a **keyboard equivalent** (focus the splitter, `Up/Down` adjust by 2 % steps, `Home` restores equal ratios) — required by the no-drag-only rule.
- Shared time axis: one `TimeAxis` per chart (CMP-189's "master clock" role), rendered once in the bottom gutter; every pane's x-mapping derives from it by construction, so time can never drift between panes.
- Per-pane price scales that are independent by default, with an opt-in "link scale" per sync mode.
- `src/sync/SyncGroup.ts` (**CMP-196**): group registry keyed by `groupId`, membership add/remove, and per-mode propagation of `timeRange`, `crosshair` and `level`.
- **Single-phase propagation**: input is integrated, then the group publishes once per frame; subscribers apply without re-publishing (an `origin` token on the sync message suppresses echo). Re-entrant propagation is impossible by construction, and a test asserts it.
- Sync-state status region: joining/leaving a group or changing modes announces once ("Panes linked: crosshair, levels") through a shared polite status region.
- `sync` message wiring (main->worker, §6) so multiple chart instances sharing the worker propagate without a main-thread round-trip.

## Out of scope
- Grid **layouts** (1/2/3/4/6 charts), workspace save/load, and the colour-coded sync-group UI — E15 (`US-LAY-*`). This story ships the engine mechanism and the API E15 drives.
- The multi-chart grid panel screen **SCR-049** — E15.
- Indicator panes and their placement rules — E13.
- Symbol propagation across linked charts — E15.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Panes in one chart cannot drift in time
  Given a three-pane chart (price, volume, CVD)
  When the chart is panned and zoomed for 10 s
  Then all three panes show the identical time range on every frame, asserted from frame stats, not visually
  And only one TimeAxis is rendered, in the bottom gutter

Scenario: Sync propagates once per frame with no echo
  Given two charts in sync group "A" with crosshair sync enabled
  When the crosshair moves in chart 1
  Then chart 2's crosshair updates on the same frame
  And chart 1 receives no inbound sync message originating from its own broadcast
  And instrumentation shows exactly one propagation per frame

Scenario: Splitters are operable without a mouse
  Given the splitter between the price and volume panes has focus
  When the user presses Down three times and then Home
  Then the price pane shrinks by 6 % in three steps and Home restores equal ratios
  And each change is announced once, not per frame

Scenario: A pane too small to read collapses honestly
  Given a pane is dragged below its minimum height
  When it renders
  Then it collapses to a labelled stub naming the pane and offering restore
  And it does not render a squashed, illegible chart

Scenario: Sync state is announced once
  Given the user enables level sync for a group of three panes
  When the change applies
  Then a single polite announcement says "Panes linked: crosshair, levels"
  And no further announcement occurs while the state is unchanged

Scenario: Four synced charts stay within budget
  Given four synchronised charts with benchmark B5 content at half density
  When B6 runs
  Then the aggregate p95 frame time is at most 16.7 ms and shared-worker CPU is at most 70 % of one core
```

## Technical notes / design
Propagation order inside the frame (§3.5): integrate input -> apply local viewport/crosshair changes -> **publish** to the group -> subscribers apply with `applyingSync = true` -> collect/render. Subscribers set a flag that suppresses publication for that frame; the `origin` token is belt-and-braces for cross-worker cases.

Height ratios are normalised on every mutation so floating-point drift cannot make panes sum to 0.999 and leave a gap. The minimum pane height is `max(48 px, 3 × axis label height)` — below that, axis labels cannot be drawn and the pane is meaningless.

Level sync ("drawing a level on one pane reflects on linked panes", CMP-196) propagates the *price* only; it deliberately does not propagate the drawing object, because linked charts may be different symbols where the same price means something different. Cross-symbol level sync is off by default and flagged in the UI (E15's concern).

The shared time axis derives each pane's x-mapping from one `Viewport.time` instance; panes hold only their own price mapping. There is no per-pane time state that could diverge — this is "shared by construction" rather than "kept in sync".

Sync groups are identified by string ids created by the app (E15 assigns colours to them); the engine never invents or persists a group id.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ratio normalisation and minimum-height collapse; splitter keyboard steps; group membership add/remove/dispose; echo suppression (a subscriber applying a sync must not publish); propagation ordering with `TestClock`.
- **Integration** (CMP-196's catalogue requirement): sync propagation across 2–4 panes and across 2 chart instances, asserting same-frame application and exactly-once propagation.
- **Golden image**: 2-, 3- and 4-pane stacks with correct gutters and a single time axis; collapsed-stub state.
- **Interaction/E2E**: splitter drag and keyboard resize; enabling/disabling each sync mode; announcement fired once.
- **Perf**: B6 (4 synchronised charts — aggregate p95 <=16.7 ms, shared-worker CPU <=70 % of one core). This is also the test that proves the "one rAF per page" rule from E11-S01 holds.
- **A11y**: axe-core on a multi-pane chart; splitter has `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`, `aria-valuenow` and an accessible name; status region announces once.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
- Splitters are `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` and a name identifying the panes they divide; keyboard resize is mandatory (drag-only is forbidden by `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.1.6).
- Each pane is an `aria-label`led region so a screen-reader user can tell which pane the data cursor is in; moving the cursor between panes announces the pane name once.
- Sync-state changes announce **once** through a shared polite status region (CMP-196's contract) — not per frame and not per pane.
- Collapsed stubs carry a text label and a keyboard-operable restore control; a collapsed pane is never a silent disappearance.
- Design source: **E11-D02** (pane chrome, splitters, collapsed state).

## Performance notes
Budget #1 with the B6 worst case as the gate, and the §4.4 degradation rule that under the stress scenario background panes may be capped to candles+profile with an explicit, **non-colour-only** "reduced live detail" indicator. This story implements the focused/background pane distinction the ladder needs; the shedding policy itself is E11-S12. Draw-call target <=40 for a 3-pane chart (§4).

## Observability
Counters: `engine.sync.propagations_per_frame` (must be <=1 per group — an alerting condition if exceeded), `engine.sync.group_members`, `engine.panes.collapsed`. Frame stats are reported per chart instance so B6 attribution is per-chart, not aggregate-only.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S01** — layout engine and the pane node model.
- **E11-S07** — the crosshair position that is propagated.
- **E11-T02** — the `sync` message.
- Blocks **E15** (layouts/workspaces drive these APIs), **E13** (indicator panes), **E23**/**E24** (CVD/derivatives panes).

## Branch

title: Render device-pixel-correct at any DPI and survive resize and monitor changes
body:
## Context
A trading chart is judged on hairlines. If the backing store is not sized at `devicePixelRatio` and coordinates are not snapped to the device-pixel grid, gridlines shimmer, axis text blurs and a 1 px crosshair becomes a 2 px smear — precisely the "boring parity" work `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §1 warns must be finished before order-flow features pay off.

The reference machine runs **2560×1440 at 125 % scaling**, so a fractional DPR (1.25) is the *default* case, not an edge case. Owners commonly drag a window between a laptop panel and an external monitor, which changes DPR mid-session with no reload.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Backing store sized `cssPx * dpr`, canvas CSS size left to layout; all engine math in CSS pixels with a single `dpr` uniform applied at the vertex stage.
- **DPR cap for the heatmap layer at 2** per `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.4 — a 3× DPR display must not triple heatmap texture memory for no perceptual gain.
- Hairline snapping helper: `snapHairline(vCssPx, dpr)` -> aligns 1-device-pixel strokes to the half-pixel grid so gridlines, axis rules and the crosshair are crisp at any DPR.
- `ResizeObserver` on the container, debounced to one frame, forwarded as the `resize` message (E11-T02) with `{ width, height, dpr }`.
- DPR-change detection via a `(resolution: <dpr>dppx)` media query re-armed after each change (the reliable cross-browser idiom), triggering re-size plus **SDF atlas size-class re-selection** (E11-S11).
- Zero-size and hidden-container handling: a `0×0` or `display:none` container suspends the render loop instead of throwing or allocating a degenerate framebuffer.
- Framebuffer reallocation policy: grow in 128 px steps and never shrink during an interactive drag, to avoid reallocation storms while a user drags a splitter.

## Out of scope
- Pane layout and splitters — E11-S09.
- Printing/export rasterisation — E15 (screenshot export).
- The axis label typography itself — E11-S06/S11.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Hairlines are crisp at fractional DPI
  Given the chart is rendered at devicePixelRatio 1.25
  When gridlines, the axis rule and the crosshair are drawn
  Then each is exactly one device pixel wide with no anti-aliased fringe
  And the golden image matches the reference at <= 0.1 % pixel difference

Scenario: Moving to a different-DPI monitor re-renders correctly
  Given a chart rendered on a 1x display
  When the window is moved to a 2x display and devicePixelRatio changes to 2
  Then the backing store is resized, the SDF atlas size class is re-selected
  And the next frame is sharp with no stretched or stale texture

Scenario: Heatmap layer is capped at 2x
  Given a display reporting devicePixelRatio 3
  When the heatmap layer allocates its textures
  Then it allocates at an effective ratio of 2 while other layers use 3
  And heatmap texture memory stays within its 20 MB secondary gate

Scenario: A zero-size container does not crash or burn CPU
  Given the chart container is resized to 0x0 or hidden with display:none
  When a frame would be scheduled
  Then the render loop suspends and allocates nothing
  And it resumes with a correct frame within one frame of the container regaining size

Scenario: Dragging a splitter does not cause reallocation storms
  Given the user drags a pane splitter continuously for 2 seconds
  When framebuffers are inspected
  Then reallocation occurs at most once per 128 px growth step and never shrinks mid-drag
  And p95 frame time during the drag stays within budget #1
```

## Technical notes / design
Transform: world -> CSS px (E11-S03) -> device px by `* dpr` in the vertex shader, so all JS-side hit-testing, layout and drawing math stays in CSS pixels and there is exactly one place DPR is applied.

```ts
// half-pixel alignment: a 1-device-px line centred on a device-pixel boundary blurs;
// centred on a device-pixel *centre* it is crisp.
const snapHairline = (vCssPx: number, dpr: number): number =>
  (Math.round(vCssPx * dpr - 0.5) + 0.5) / dpr;
```

DPR-change detection must re-arm after every change because the media query is DPR-specific:

```ts
function onDprChange(cb: (dpr: number) => void): () => void {
  let mq: MediaQueryList;
  const arm = () => {
    mq = matchMedia(`(resolution: ${devicePixelRatio}dppx)`);
    mq.addEventListener("change", handle, { once: true });
  };
  const handle = () => { cb(devicePixelRatio); arm(); };
  arm();
  return () => mq.removeEventListener("change", handle);
}
```

Resize is debounced to exactly one frame (not a timer) so a drag produces one resize per frame, matching the <=1 message/frame rule of the worker protocol.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: `snapHairline` across dpr  in  {1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 3} with property tests asserting the result always lands on a device-pixel centre; framebuffer growth-step policy; zero-size suspension and resumption; DPR listener re-arm (asserting the listener is re-registered after each change).
- **Golden image** (E11-T08, SwiftShader): grid + axes + crosshair at dpr 1, 1.25, 2; heatmap-cap verification at dpr 3.
- **Integration**: simulated DPR change mid-session asserting atlas re-selection and a sharp next frame.
- **Perf**: splitter-drag scenario asserting <=1 reallocation per 128 px and in-budget p95.
- **Chaos**: container hidden/shown repeatedly (E11-Q04 charter) asserting no leak and no exception.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
- Crisp hairlines and text are a **low-vision requirement**, not a polish item: blurred 1 px rules at fractional DPI are the single most common legibility complaint on high-DPI Windows setups.
- Browser zoom up to 200 % (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.4) manifests as a DPR/size change and must be handled by the same path — verified in E11-Q05.
- Resizing must not move keyboard focus or reset the data cursor position (E11-S13); the cursor is expressed in world coordinates, not pixels, specifically so this holds.

## Performance notes
Resize and DPR changes are rare events, but a reallocation storm during a drag is a realistic budget #1 violation, hence the growth-step policy and its explicit test. The heatmap DPR cap directly protects budget #14's texture-memory secondary gate (<=20 MB, `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 B4).

## Observability
`frame` stats carry `dpr` and `backingStorePx` so any perf report is attributable to a resolution. Counter `engine.resize.reallocations` and event `engine.dpr.changed` (from -> to) logged at info level.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.

- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies

- Consumed by **E11-S06** (axis rules), **E11-S07** (crosshair), **E11-S11** (atlas size class) and **E21** (heatmap DPR cap).

title: Govern chart memory with a budget, eviction and days-to-load estimates
body:
## Context
Requirement **R7** of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` caps a chart instance at **600 MB** of GPU + JS heap at full load; §7 models the 100k-bar / 4 h-heatmap case at ~116 MB, leaving headroom that a careless paging policy would happily consume.

`US-CHART-010` (Must) turns that budget into a user-facing contract: setting a lookback shows **the estimated memory footprint**; a request that would exceed the configured client memory budget **warns with the estimate and requires confirmation before loading**; and each view type (chart, footprint, profile, replay) has its own default lookback. Its NFR fixes the accuracy bar: the estimate must be **accurate within ±20 %**, and **loading never blocks the UI thread**.

This Story is the engine half of that contract — the governor, the eviction policy, the paging trigger and the estimator — feeding SCR-044 ("Go to date") and SCR-047 (empty/no-data).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/memory/MemoryGovernor.ts` — samples usage **every 5 s** (§7) across the columnar stores, GPU buffers, textures and the SDF atlas; steps down when usage exceeds **70 %** of `memoryBudgetMb` by calling E11-S12's step-down API; emits `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE` at the threshold.
- **Eviction policy** per §7: footprint cells and heatmap columns outside a **3× viewport window** are dropped from GPU buffers while retained in CPU stores; under continued pressure, CPU stores are dropped too and re-fetched from the backend on demand.
- `src/memory/Estimator.ts` — the §7 formula table made executable: given `{ barCount, cellsPerBar, heatmapColumns, priceRows, panes, dpr, viewportPx }` it returns a byte estimate broken down per item (BarStore, GPU candle buffers, FootprintStore, glyph runs, heatmap rings, atlas, framebuffers). Must be within **±20 %** of measured, verified by a calibration test.
- `visibleRangeNeedsData` paging callback (the engine's request-for-more-history signal): emitted when the visible range approaches the loaded edge, debounced, cancellable, and never issuing I/O itself — the app layer performs the fetch (the engine does no I/O, `CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16).
- Per-view-type default lookbacks (`chart`, `footprint`, `profile`, `replay`) as engine config consumed by the settings UI.
- Over-budget confirmation flow: the estimate and the budget are exposed so the app can render the warning and require confirmation **before** the load starts.
- Hard ceilings `maxBars` and `memoryBudgetMb` enforced at every ingest point, so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.
- Config keys: `memory.budgetMb` (default 600), `memory.sampleIntervalMs` (5000), `memory.stepDownPct` (70), `memory.viewportWindowMultiplier` (3), `memory.defaultLookbackDays` (per view type).

## Out of scope
- Fetching history — the app/data layer and **E17**/**E12**; the engine only signals need.
- The SCR-044 "Go to date" dialog UI and SCR-047 empty-state UI — E15/E10 chrome consuming this Story's estimates and signals.
- Backend-side retention and disk budget — **E16**.
- Heatmap ring-buffer implementation — E21 (its memory is accounted for here, its rendering is not built here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The memory estimate is shown before loading and is accurate
  Given the user sets a 30-day lookback on a 1-minute chart
  When the estimate is computed
  Then a per-item breakdown and a total are returned before any data is requested
  And the total is within 20 % of the memory actually consumed once loaded

Scenario: Exceeding the budget requires explicit confirmation
  Given the configured client memory budget is 600 MB
  When the user requests a lookback whose estimate is 780 MB
  Then the load does not start
  And the estimate and the budget are surfaced for confirmation, and loading proceeds only after the user confirms

Scenario: Memory pressure steps down detail rather than crashing
  Given usage crosses 70 % of the budget during a live session
  When the governor samples at its 5 second interval
  Then ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE is emitted and one degradation rung is shed
  And GPU buffers outside the 3x viewport window are evicted while CPU stores are retained

Scenario: Evicted data is transparently re-fetched when needed again
  Given footprint cells for a range were evicted under pressure
  When the user pans back to that range
  Then visibleRangeNeedsData fires for exactly that range
  And the chart shows a loading affordance for the missing range rather than drawing a silent gap

Scenario: Loading never blocks the UI thread
  Given a 100k-bar load is in progress
  When the main thread is sampled during the load
  Then no main-thread task exceeds 50 ms
  And pan and zoom remain responsive throughout

Scenario: A malformed length field cannot exhaust memory
  Given a data message declares a bar count above maxBars
  When it reaches the ingest path
  Then it is rejected with ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR and no allocation of that size occurs
  And the existing scene continues rendering unaffected

Scenario: A 30-minute soak shows no runaway growth
  Given benchmark B10 runs a 30-minute live feed
  When peak memory and the growth trend are measured
  Then peak stays <= 600 MB and growth does not exceed 5 % over the 30 minutes
```

## Technical notes / design
**Estimator.** A direct encoding of the §7 table, so the document and the code cannot drift:

```ts
const estimate = (p: LoadParams) => ({
  barStore:      p.barCount * (8 + 4 * 4 + 4 + 4),
  candleGpu:     p.barCount * 28,
  footprintStore:p.fpBars * p.cellsPerBar * 18,
  glyphRuns:     p.fpBars * p.cellsPerBar * 12,
  heatFine:      2048 * p.priceRows * 2,
  heatCoarse:    p.heatmapColumns * p.priceRows * 2,
  atlas:         1024 * 1024,
  misc:          8 * 1024 * 1024,
  framebuffers:  p.viewportPx.w * p.viewportPx.h * 4 * Math.min(p.dpr, 2) ** 2 * FB_COUNT,
});
```

A **calibration test** loads each modelled case, measures actual usage via `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` where available and GL buffer accounting otherwise, and fails if any estimate is off by more than 20 % — which is how the ±20 % NFR becomes enforceable rather than aspirational.

**Sampling, not hooking.** The governor samples every 5 s rather than instrumenting every allocation: allocation hooks would themselves cost frame time, and pressure is a slow-moving condition. The trade-off is up to 5 s of latency before a step-down, which is acceptable because the LOD ladder (E11-S12) already handles fast-moving frame-time pressure on a 3-frame horizon. The two mechanisms are deliberately complementary: **frame time reacts in frames, memory reacts in seconds.**

**Eviction.** `3 × viewport` window, evicting GPU first (cheap to rebuild from CPU stores) and CPU second (requires a re-fetch). Eviction is never partial within a bar: a bar's cells are all present or all absent, so no half-drawn bar can appear.

## Test plan
- **Calibration test** (the headline test): estimate vs measured for each §7 modelled case, failing above ±20 %.
- **Unit**: estimator arithmetic per item; threshold crossing at 70 %; eviction window boundaries; `visibleRangeNeedsData` debouncing, cancellation and exact-range emission; `maxBars` rejection; per-view default lookbacks.
- **Integration**: pressure -> step-down -> eviction -> pan-back -> re-fetch, as one sequence.
- **Perf**: **B10** 30-minute soak (peak <=600 MB, growth <=5 %); main-thread task duration <=50 ms during a 100k-bar load; **B9** cold init <=900 ms with paging active.
- **Fuzz**: malformed length fields, negative counts, `NaN` bar counts — all rejected at the boundary, none reaching an allocator.
- **Chaos** (E11-Q04): repeated pressure cycles asserting no leak and no oscillation between evict and re-fetch.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only**; no PII, no credentials.

STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in **E11-X01**): **Denial of service** is the primary one. An attacker-controlled or corrupted frame declaring an enormous length is the classic path to memory exhaustion in a binary-protocol client, and the whole point of hard `maxBars` and `memoryBudgetMb` ceilings enforced **at the ingest boundary** is that no downstream code ever sees a value it could act on. **Tampering**: typed arrays are bounds- and value-validated (no `NaN`/`Infinity` prices) before indexing, so a corrupt frame cannot become an out-of-bounds read or poison the viewport.

Controls: ceilings enforced before allocation, not after; rejection emits `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR` and leaves the existing scene intact (fail-closed for the bad frame, not for the chart); fuzz tests over the ingest path are part of this Story's test plan, not a later hardening Epic. `security` label applies; reviewed in **E11-X03**.

## Accessibility notes
- The over-budget warning is **text stating the estimate and the budget**, with a real confirmation control — never a colour-coded gauge alone (SCR-047's "empty state is a heading + paragraph + action, not an icon alone" convention applies).
- A range that is loading or was evicted must be announced as such in the DOM mirror ("loading 3 hours of history"), so a screen-reader user is never shown a silent gap.
- Memory-pressure step-downs announce once, politely, reusing E11-S12's aggregation-indicator channel — not per sample.
- Design source: **E11-D04** (empty/error states) and **E11-D03** (scale/date menus, which host the days-to-load control).

## Performance notes
Requirement **R7**: <=600 MB GPU + JS heap per chart instance; the §7 model is ~116 MB for the 100k-bar case. Gate **B10**: 30-minute soak, peak <=600 MB, no monotonic growth beyond 5 %/30 min. Governor sampling costs <=0.2 ms every 5 s — deliberately off the frame path. `US-CHART-010` NFRs: estimate within ±20 %, loading never blocks the UI thread (<=50 ms main-thread tasks).

## Observability
Counters: `engine.memory.used_mb` (broken down per store), `engine.memory.budget_mb`, `engine.memory.evictions`, `engine.memory.refetches`, `engine.paging.requests`. Errors: `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE`, `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`. All surfaced on **SCR-046** (GPU memory estimate, buffer uploads/s) and included in the copied diagnostics snapshot, so a user reporting "it got slow" ships the memory trace with the report.

title: Make the engine benchmark harness a required CI check with enforced baselines
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §13 names the single mitigation that makes E11 survivable as a critical-path Epic: "**benchmark harness in CI from day 1 so regressions surface same-day**". Performance in a render engine is not a feature you add at the end; it is a property you lose one 3 % regression at a time, and the only defence is a gate that fails the build.

`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 already specifies the harness completely: benchmarks live in `packages/chart-engine/bench`, run headless on a **dedicated CI runner**, replay a **deterministic fixture** for 20 s, report p50/p95 frame time, draw calls, uploaded bytes and peak memory, and are **required checks on PRs touching the package**. This Task builds it and, critically, turns it on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/bench` — the harness: Playwright + Chromium with a fixed GPU flag set, deterministic fixtures from `packages/fixtures`, 20 s per scenario, **3 repetitions** with the median of p95 taken as the result (a single run of a GPU benchmark is noise).
- Scenarios implemented in this Task — the ones whose subject matter exists by Sprint 07: **B1** (100k candles, pan at 1000 px/s, <=12 ms, <=8 draw calls), **B2** (zoom sweep 0.1->50 px/bar, <=14 ms, <=6 LOD changes), **B5** (combined scene, <=16.7 ms, <=40 draw calls), **B6** (4 synchronised charts, <=16.7 ms aggregate, shared-worker CPU <=70 % of one core), **B9** (cold init to first frame, <=900 ms, atlas from cache <=5 ms), **B10** (30-min memory soak, peak <=600 MB, growth <=5 %).
- Scenario **stubs with registered gates** for B3, B4, B7, B8 — owned by E18, E21, E17 and E14 respectively; registering them here means those Epics inherit a working harness instead of building one each.
- **Baseline storage and update policy**: baselines committed as JSON; a regression **>10 %** against the stored baseline fails the check (§13); baselines are updated **only** by an explicit reviewer-approved commit that states the cause. The Epic applies a tighter **5 %** working threshold for hard budgets per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §8 — the harness enforces the tighter of the two.
- **Required-check wiring**: GitHub branch protection on `packages/chart-engine` paths; a dedicated, pinned CI runner (shared runners have unusable GPU variance, and saying this in the ticket prevents a well-meaning "let's just use the standard runner" PR).
- Per-stage attribution using the nine frame stages of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3, so a regression report names the stage, not just the total.
- Artefact output: JSON results, a trend chart and a PR comment table (before/after/delta per scenario).

## Out of scope
- Backend API/WS load testing (k6/Locust) — E46 and the platform Epics; this is the **frontend engine** harness only.
- The benchmark **fixtures** themselves beyond the seeded synthetic generator — extended from **E06**'s M0 harness, which this Task builds on rather than replaces.
- Perf sign-off as a QA activity — **E11-Q03**; this Task provides the numbers, Q03 interprets and signs off on them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The benchmark check blocks a regressing PR
  Given a stored baseline for scenario B5 of 15.0 ms p95
  When a PR raises B5 p95 to 16.0 ms, a 6.7 % regression
  Then the required check fails and the PR cannot merge
  And the PR comment names B5, the before and after values, the delta and the worst-regressing frame stage

Scenario: Results are stable enough to gate on
  Given the harness runs on the dedicated runner
  When scenario B1 is executed three times in a row with no code change
  Then the median-of-p95 values vary by less than 3 %
  And that variance figure is published so the gate threshold is demonstrably above the noise floor

Scenario: A deliberate baseline change is possible but never silent
  Given an intentional change trades 8 % of B2 frame time for a correctness fix
  When the author updates the baseline
  Then the update is a separate, explicitly reviewed commit stating the cause
  And an unexplained baseline change is rejected in review

Scenario: Every gate from the design document is enforced or explicitly deferred
  Given the harness configuration is inspected
  Then B1, B2, B5, B6, B9 and B10 are enforced with their primary and secondary gates
  And B3, B4, B7 and B8 are registered as stubs naming the Epic that will enable them

Scenario: Benchmarks are deterministic
  Given the same fixture and the same commit
  When the harness runs on two different days
  Then the same bars, trades and timestamps are replayed
  And no wall-clock time, random seed or network call influences the result
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why median-of-p95 over three runs.** GPU benchmarks have a fat right tail from driver scheduling and thermal effects. A single p95 varies by 5–10 % run to run — more than the thing we are trying to detect. Three runs and a median collapses that to under 3 %, which is what makes a 5–10 % gate meaningful. The stability scenario above exists to prove this claim continuously rather than assume it.

**Determinism.** Fixtures are pre-recorded, time is driven by a virtual clock, and the harness injects frames rather than waiting on `rAF` wall time. No network, no randomness without a fixed seed, no wall-clock branches.

**Runner pinning.** A dedicated runner with a fixed GPU, fixed driver version and fixed Chromium build, pinned in the workflow. The driver version is part of the baseline record, so a driver upgrade invalidates baselines explicitly instead of appearing as a mysterious 20 % regression across every scenario at once.

**Per-stage attribution** uses the `Performance.mark()`/`measure()` spans placed at the §4.3 stage boundaries (decode, model update, layout, viewport, cull, decimate, batch, GL submit, present), so the PR comment can say "batch stage +1.2 ms" instead of "B5 got slower".

## Test plan
- **Self-test**: the harness is tested against a deliberately regressed build (a synthetic 10 % stall injected) asserting the check fails; and against an unchanged build asserting it passes — a gate that has never been seen to fail is not a gate.
- **Stability test**: 3× repeat run reporting variance, published as an artefact each run.
- **Determinism test**: identical results across two runs on different days from the same commit.
- **Unit**: baseline comparison arithmetic, threshold selection (tighter of 5 %/10 %), PR-comment rendering, stage attribution parsing.
- Coverage >=85 % on the harness's own code — the harness is production code for the purposes of the coverage gate.

## Security notes
Data classification: **synthetic fixture data only** — no real account data, no credentials, no PII ever enters a benchmark fixture, and this is asserted by a fixture-content check so nobody "temporarily" records a real session into `packages/fixtures`.

Supply-chain note: the harness pins Playwright, the Chromium build and the GPU driver version; those pins are covered by Dependabot and npm audit like any other dependency. CI artefacts (JSON results, trend charts) contain only timing data and are safe to publish on PRs.

The dedicated runner executes repository code, so it is subject to the same untrusted-fork restrictions as any other self-hosted runner: benchmarks run on PRs from forks only after maintainer approval. Reviewed in **E11-X02**.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the harness itself — it produces numbers, not UI. Two adjacent requirements are worth stating so they are not lost: the benchmark scenarios must run with the DOM mirror **active** (so its <=1 ms/frame cost is inside the measured budget rather than excluded from it), and the a11y automated checks (axe-core) are a separate required check owned by **E11-Q05**, not folded into this one.

## Performance notes
This Task **is** the performance gate. It enforces budgets #1 and #2 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and gates B1/B2/B5/B6/B9/B10 from `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13. Regression threshold: the tighter of 5 % (Epic working threshold, §8 of the perf standard) and 10 % (§13). The harness itself must complete a full run in under 25 minutes so it can plausibly be a required check on every PR; scenarios run in parallel across runner slots where the GPU allows.

## Observability
Results published as CI artefacts and as a PR comment table. A long-run trend series (per scenario, per commit) is retained so slow drift — the regression pattern that no single PR gate catches — is visible; a 15 % drift over 20 commits triggers a review even though no individual PR crossed the threshold. Runner GPU/driver/Chromium versions recorded in every result record.

- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies

- **E06** — extends the M0 benchmark harness and seeded synthetic fixture generator built during the engine spike.
- Blocks **E11-T07** (diagnostics feed reuses the stats plumbing) and **E11-Q03** (perf sign-off consumes these numbers). Inherited by **E18**, **E21**, **E14**, **E17** for B3, B4, B8, B7.

title: Design QA of the built bar modes, series rendering and their states
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA a default-on Done gate for net-new UI: "built screen compared against design spec (spacing/tokens/type/color/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer; discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bug with `priority/*` set".

E12 needs this more than most epics, because most of what it delivers is **drawn by a renderer rather than composed from DOM components**. A token drift in a React button is caught by visual regression; a candle body that is one pixel too wide at 3 px spacing, a wick that disappears below a certain zoom, an aggregated mark that does not match the specified geometry, or a forming-bar treatment that is invisible at 1 s — none of those are caught by anything except a designer looking at the built product against the E12-D06 geometry rules on the reference hardware.

This ticket runs that pass at the end of the epic's build window (Sprint 08, after the Sprint 05–08 stories land) against the handoff pack from E12-D12.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A design-QA pass over every E12 surface in the built application: `SCR-030` series states, `SCR-031` General tab, `SCR-041`, `SCR-042`, `SCR-045`, `SCR-047`, `SCR-048`.
- **Geometry verification** against E12-D06: body width, wick width, minimum mark height, zero-range bar, gap treatment and the aggregated mark, sampled at every step of the density ladder (≥8 px, 4–8 px, 2–4 px, 1–2 px, <1 px), captured as screenshots on the reference machine at 2560×1440.
- **Per-mode verification**: candle, hollow candle, OHLC bar, line, area, baseline, Heikin-Ashi, equi-volume, delta-volume × time, tick, volume, range, delta, Renko and P&F — sampled per the risk-based matrix agreed with QA rather than exhaustively, with the sampling rationale recorded.
- **State verification**: forming vs closed, LOD-aggregated with its indicator, partial-history boundary, gap, rebuilding with progress and cancel, empty (all four `SCR-047` reasons), error (all three `SCR-048` classes).
- **Token/spacing/type audit** of the DOM surfaces in both themes and both densities, against the handoff pack's token manifest.
- **Copy audit**: every mode description, validation message, empty-state and error-state string matches the approved copy exactly — including the catalogue's fixed strings ("Needs recorded ticks", "No USDT perpetual matches 'xyz' — v1 supports linear perpetuals only.", "Values below one tick are not allowed.").
- **Motion verification** against E12-D10, including the reduced-motion path.
- A findings list with severities; each finding fixed within the epic or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*` label and a named owner, per the DoD.
- A sign-off record on the E12 epic ticket enumerating what was checked, what passed and what was deferred.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of bar construction (does a 500-tick bar actually close after 500 trades) — that is the engineering and QA tickets' job; this pass is about whether the built result matches the design.
- Performance benchmarking as a gate (owned by the E12 perf work and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §13) — though this pass records anything visibly janky as a finding.
- Footprint, profiles, indicators and drawings (their own epics' design QA).
- Backend, API and WS verification.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E12 surface is compared against its spec
  Given the built application is available on the reference machine
  When the design-QA pass is executed
  Then SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-041, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-047 and SCR-048 are each compared against the handoff pack
  And a pass or fail with evidence is recorded per surface

Scenario: Geometry matches the specified rules at every density
  Given the density ladder from E12-D06
  When the built chart is sampled at each step
  Then measured body and wick widths match the specified formulas within the stated tolerance
  And the aggregated mark below one pixel spacing matches the specified appearance

Scenario: A discrepancy is fixed or filed, never absorbed (edge)
  Given a discrepancy is found that cannot be fixed before the epic closes
  When it is triaged
  Then a Bug is filed with a priority label, an owner and a reference to the specific spec line it violates
  And the E12 epic sign-off record lists it as a known deferral rather than omitting it

Scenario: Copy has drifted during implementation (failure)
  Given a validation message in the built product differs from the approved copy
  When the copy audit runs
  Then the difference is recorded verbatim, both versions shown
  And either the build is corrected or the catalogue is updated with CDO approval, so the documentation and the product agree

Scenario: The forming bar is invisible on fast intervals (failure)
  Given a one-second interval on a busy symbol
  When the forming-bar treatment is inspected in the built product
  Then it is distinguishable from a closed bar without relying on motion or colour alone
  And if it is not, a P1 finding is raised against the implementing story
```

## Technical notes / design
- Run on the **reference machine at 2560×1440**, the configuration `SCR-030`'s budgets are stated against, and in all the runtimes R1 cares about (Chromium and the Electron shell). A design-QA pass on a designer's laptop at a different DPR measures nothing about the geometry rules, which are DPR-sensitive.
- Verify device-pixel-ratio handling explicitly (`CMP-180` owns DPR); a rule that is correct at DPR 1 and wrong at DPR 2 is a real and common defect in canvas renderers.
- Use real recorded fixtures, including one quiet symbol and one busy symbol, so the sparse and dense cases are both seen.
- Sample rather than exhaust: the full cross-product of chart types × bar modes is large, so agree a risk-based matrix with QA (every bar mode at least once; every chart type at least once; the highest-risk intersections — Renko, P&F, equi-volume, delta-volume — explicitly).
- Measure, do not eyeball, for geometry: capture screenshots and measure pixels against the formulas, with a stated tolerance.
- Where the built product is *better* than the spec, say so and update the spec — design QA is a two-way gate, not only a compliance check.

## Test plan
- Execute the pass against the handoff pack surface by surface, recording evidence (screenshots, measurements) per check.
- Re-run the E12-D11 screen-reader script against the built product in collaboration with QA/SDET; deviations are findings here as well as in the QA tickets.
- Verify the Storybook states listed in the handoff manifest actually exist and match, since they are the visual-regression baseline going forward.
- Verify axe-core is green on the touched DOM surfaces (a DoD requirement for the consuming stories) and record it.
- Reduced-motion pass: confirm no information is lost and no suppressed transition leaves an inconsistent end state.
- Both themes, both densities, and the Electron floating-panel case (`SCR-027`) for the popover surfaces.

## Security notes
- Verify that RBAC-gated affordances behave as designed in the built product: the "Record this symbol" action is absent for manager/viewer and the explanatory copy is present instead.
- Verify that error states expose no internal detail (no stack traces, hostnames or upstream URLs) and that correlation ids contain no account identifiers or tokens.
- Perform the pass against a demo/test account only; no live keys or live account data are used, and screenshots attached to findings are scrubbed of account context.

## Accessibility notes
- Re-verification of the E12-D11 script against the built product is part of this pass; findings are raised against the implementing stories.
- Check the non-negotiables in the built product: visible focus everywhere, no hover-only functionality, no colour-only direction or state encoding (verified in greyscale), disabled menu items focusable and announcing their reason, and `SCR-045` reachable from the chart panel header rather than buried in settings.
- Confirm announcement throttling in practice on a 1 s interval — the worst case for flooding.
- Any a11y finding that prevents a user from reading chart data is P0 and blocks the epic's Done.

## Performance notes
- This is not the performance gate, but visible jank, dropped frames during mode switches, or transitions that fail to drop under load are recorded as findings and cross-referenced to the E12 perf work and `SCR-046` diagnostics.
- Confirm that the aggregation indicator's stated level agrees with the diagnostics overlay's visible-bar/aggregation values, since the handoff pack requires them to agree.

## Observability
- Verify the analytics manifest was implemented: `chart.interval_changed`, `chart.bar_mode_changed`, `chart.symbol_changed`, `chart.settings_changed`, `chart.empty_state_shown` with `{reason}`, `chart.error_shown` with `{code, correlationId}`, `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`, and the rebuild start/complete/cancel events — each fires at the designed trigger with the designed properties.
- A missing or mis-propertied event is a finding, because an unmeasured rebuild duration means the 10 s budget cannot be policed in production.

## Definition of Done
- Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4 (Task) and the §3.2 `design-qa` gate.
- Pass executed across all seven surfaces with evidence attached.
- Every finding fixed or filed as a Bug with `priority/*` and an owner; none absorbed silently.
- Copy audit differences resolved in either direction, with `14-screens-catalogue.md` updated where the product legitimately diverged.
- Sign-off record posted on the E12 epic ticket listing checked/passed/deferred.
- **CDO sign-off recorded; Status = Done** — required before the E12 epic can be marked Done.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E12-D12 (the handoff pack this pass tests against).
- Requires the E12 frontend stories from Sprint 05–08 to be merged and deployable to the QA environment; if any are incomplete at Sprint 08, the pass covers what exists and the remainder is explicitly deferred with a named follow-up.
- Coordinates with the E12 QA tickets (shared screen-reader script and state matrix as oracles).

## Branch
`design/e12-design-qa` — findings, evidence and any catalogue corrections; no application code (fixes land on the implementing stories' branches).

title: Switch symbol and timeframe without tearing down the engine
body:
## Context
**US-CHART-005 (Must)**: "I want to switch intervals from 1 s to 1 D including custom intervals, so that context and execution timeframes are one keystroke apart", with NFRs of **≤200 ms from cache** and **"no flash of empty chart"**. Symbol switching (US-MKT-002: "the focused chart pane switches symbol and the search closes") has the same requirement.

The roadmap scopes this explicitly for E12: "symbol + timeframe switching **without a full engine teardown**". That constraint is what makes 200 ms possible — recreating a WebGL context, re-uploading the theme LUT and rebuilding the scene graph costs far more than the budget, and a teardown/rebuild is also how the "flash of empty chart" happens.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Re-binding the existing engine instance and pane stack to a new series: unsubscribe the old `bars` topic, subscribe the new one, swap the columnar store contents, keep the GL context, programs, LUTs, scene graph and pane layout intact.
- Cache-first switching: an already-cached (symbol, spec) window paints from the local store immediately, with only the tail fetched.
- Visible-window preservation: on an interval change, the **centre** of the visible time window is preserved (US-CHART-005 scenario 1); on a symbol change, the time window is preserved and the price scale re-autoscales to the new symbol's range.
- Drawings and indicators re-anchored by timestamp, not by bar index, so they land correctly on a different interval.
- The interval ladder of US-CHART-005: standard intervals 1 s … 1 D via hotkeys, sub-minute intervals built from recorded prints (with the partial-history marker when recording is shallower than the view), and custom intervals (e.g. 7m) aggregated from 1m data and added to a recent list.
- SCR-041 quick-switcher and CMP-219 SymbolPicker / CMP-220 IntervalPicker wired to the engine, keyboard-first.
- Delisted-symbol handling per US-MKT-001: the chart shows a delisted banner rather than an empty chart.
- Loading state: the previous series stays visible with a loading affordance until the new one is ready — never an empty pane.

## Out of scope
- Bar-mode switching and parameter-change rebuilds — E12-S12.
- Symbol search itself (US-MKT-002's fuzzy matching and ranking) — E08/E10 scope; this Story consumes the selection event.
- Watchlist (US-MKT-003) and layouts/sync groups (E15).
- Chart templates (US-CHART-012) — E15.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Interval switch from cache is fast and centred
  Given a BTCUSDT 1m chart with 5m bars already cached
  When I press the 5m hotkey
  Then the chart switches within 200 ms
  And the centre of the visible time window is preserved
  And no WebGL context is created or lost

Scenario: No flash of empty chart
  Given a switch that requires a network fetch
  Then the previous series remains visible with a loading affordance
  And at no point is an empty pane or an axes-only grid displayed

Scenario: Drawings re-anchor by time
  Given a trend line drawn on the 1m chart
  When I switch to 5m
  Then the line connects the same timestamps and prices
  And it is not shifted by the change in bar index

Scenario: Symbol switch keeps the engine
  Given a BTCUSDT chart with indicators and drawings
  When I switch to ETHUSDT from the quick-switcher
  Then the same engine instance re-binds
  And the price scale re-autoscales to the new symbol
  And BTCUSDT's bars topic is unsubscribed after the grace period

Scenario: Sub-minute interval with shallow recording
  Given the recorder holds less history than the requested 5 s view
  When I select 5 s
  Then bars are built from the available prints
  And a partial-history marker names where recorded data begins

Scenario: Custom interval
  When I enter 7m
  Then bars are aggregated from 1m data
  And 7m is added to my recent-intervals list

Scenario: Delisted symbol
  Given the selected symbol is no longer trading
  Then the chart renders the available history with a delisted banner
  And order entry for it is disabled
```

## Technical notes / design
- Re-binding must be atomic from the user's perspective: build the new store contents, then swap in one frame. A partial swap is what produces a flash or a frame of mixed data.
- Unsubscribe uses the 30-second grace of US-MKT-005 so a rapid A→B→A switch does not thrash subscriptions.
- Drawings anchor in (time, price) space already (E14's model); this Story must simply avoid re-anchoring them to index — but it must be tested explicitly because index-anchoring is the easy accidental implementation.
- Custom intervals aggregate client-side from 1m only when the requested interval is an exact multiple; otherwise a distinct server-side spec is registered. State which path was taken in the diagnostics.
- The LOD cache (E12-S09) is keyed per series and must be invalidated on re-bind without discarding the GL resources it lives in.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: window-centre preservation maths, cache-hit decision, custom-interval aggregation eligibility, recent-intervals list behaviour.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): the full switch matrix — cached/uncached × interval/symbol — asserting timing, no context loss (instrument `webglcontextlost`), no empty-pane frame, and drawing anchors unchanged.
- **Perf**: switch timed at p95 against the 200 ms budget with 100k bars loaded; a counter asserts zero GL context recreations.
- **a11y**: axe-core on SCR-041/SCR-042; keyboard-only switch path verified; focus returns to the chart after the switcher closes.

## Security notes
The symbol arriving from the switcher is validated against the instrument catalogue before any subscription or request is made — an arbitrary symbol string must never reach a topic name or a query (the same whitelist discipline as E12-T05/T06, enforced client-side too so a malformed request is not even sent). Unsubscribing reliably on switch also matters for resource fairness: a client that leaks subscriptions across switches is a slow-motion DoS against its own backend budget.

## Accessibility notes
Switching is a keyboard-first flow: CMP-219 and CMP-220 follow the combobox/menu-button patterns with the current value readable without opening the popover, and CMP-220 presents bar modes as a separate labelled group. After a switch, focus must return to the chart canvas (not be lost to the body), and the new symbol/interval must be announced once politely — not on every subsequent data update. The partial-history and delisted states are text. The loading affordance must not be a colour-only or motion-only signal, and must respect reduced-motion.

## Performance notes
≤200 ms switch from cache (US-CHART-005 NFR) at 100k bars; zero WebGL context recreations; no re-upload of theme LUTs, shaders or glyph atlas; GPU memory must not grow across repeated switches (a leak here is the classic re-bind bug — assert stable memory over a 100-switch loop).

## Observability
`chart_switch_duration_ms{kind="symbol"|"interval",cache="hit"|"miss"}`, `chart_switch_context_recreations_total` (must stay zero), `ws_subscription_churn_total`, GPU memory gauge sampled across switches.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario automated; coverage ≥80%; switch-time and memory-stability benchmarks recorded; axe-core green plus a keyboard-only and screen-reader pass on the switcher; design-QA pass against SCR-041/SCR-042; QA sign-off; demoed; feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S09** — the LOD cache that must be invalidated and rebuilt on re-bind.
- **E12-S10** — live subscription lifecycle for the `bars` topic.
- **E08 / US-MKT-001** — the instrument catalogue for validation and delisted status.

## Branch
`feat/e12-symbol-timeframe-switch`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-005 (Must), US-MKT-001, US-MKT-002, US-MKT-005 (30 s grace)
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 (E12: "switching without a full engine teardown"), §5.3 exit criterion 5
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-041, SCR-042 · `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-219, CMP-220, CMP-221
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 data model, §7 memory budgets

1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (relevant section per Scope)

**Branch & PR**
