title: Expose every enabled indicator as a named metric for alerts and rules
body:
## Context
Implements **US-IND-008** (Must): "As a rule author, I want every enabled indicator's values exposed as named metrics, so that alerts and rules can reference exactly what I see." Its NFR is the contract: "metric identity is stable across sessions (key, not display name); resolution failures surface at save time, never silently at runtime." This story closes the loop `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 opens - "This is what makes the rule vocabulary and the indicator list the same list" - and provides the referential guard that stops an armed rule from being orphaned.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Metric naming**: every indicator instance publishes a stable metric key of the form `<indicator>(<params>, <timeframe>)` - e.g. `ema(21, 5m)` - derived from the E13-T01 instance key, stable across sessions and independent of the display name the user may have set in SCR-036.
- **Vocabulary exposure**: the enabled-indicator metrics appear in the alert editor (SCR-091) and the rule editors' metric pickers with their current value shown, sourced from the registry rather than from a frontend list.
- **Ambiguity resolution**: two EMA(21) instances with different sources are each listed with a distinguishing label (source and, if needed, instance ordinal) and each gets its own metric key.
- **Referential guard**: removing an indicator referenced by an armed rule or alert is blocked; the blocking dialog lists the referencing rules/alerts and offers disarm or edit in place, per the US-IND-008 scenario. The check is server-side authoritative (a client-side-only guard would be bypassable by an API call) and the endpoint returns the referencing objects so the dialog can render them.
- **Save-time resolution**: an alert or rule referencing a metric key that cannot be resolved fails validation at save time with the unresolvable key named - never at runtime.
- Registry surface for consumers: a `resolve(name, scope) -> MetricValue` path consistent with `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.6.

## Out of scope
- The alert editor and rule editor UIs themselves (E40, E36/E37) - this story provides the vocabulary, the current values and the guard; those epics render them.
- Rule execution semantics (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Metric available
  Given EMA(21) is on my 5m chart
  Then `ema(21, 5m)` is selectable in the alert and rule editors with its current value shown

Scenario: Ambiguity resolved
  Given two EMA(21) instances with different sources exist
  Then each is listed with a distinguishing label and its own metric key

Scenario: Removed indicator in use
  When I remove an indicator referenced by an armed rule
  Then removal is blocked with the list of referencing rules, and I can disarm or edit them from there

Scenario: Identity survives a session
  Given a rule references ema(21, 5m) and the app is restarted
  Then the same indicator instance resolves to the same key and the rule remains valid, even if the user renamed the instance in SCR-036

Scenario: Unresolvable reference fails at save time
  When a rule is saved referencing a metric key that no longer exists
  Then the save is rejected naming the unresolvable key, and the rule is never armed in an unresolvable state

Scenario: The guard cannot be bypassed from the client
  When a DELETE is issued directly against an indicator instance referenced by an armed rule
  Then the server rejects it with the referencing objects listed, independently of any client-side check
```

## Technical notes / design
The metric key is canonical: parameters are serialised in a fixed order with normalised numeric formatting, so `ema(21,5m)` and `ema(21.0, 5m)` are the same key. Display names are metadata and never participate in identity. The referential guard queries rule and alert definitions for key references; because rules compile to an IR (`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md`), the reference extraction reads the IR rather than parsing editor state - that is the only representation guaranteed to be complete for both the form and node editors. Provisional values (E13-S05) are never publishable as metrics.

## Test plan
Unit: key canonicalisation including numeric normalisation and parameter ordering; ambiguity labelling with 2+ instances; reference extraction from a compiled IR covering both editor origins. Integration: removal blocked with referencing objects returned; disarm-then-remove succeeds; save-time validation rejects an unresolvable key. E2E: add EMA, create an alert on it, attempt removal, see the block, disarm from the dialog, remove successfully. Security test: direct API delete attempt bypassing the UI. Coverage >=85% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data plus user presentation preferences - no secrets, no PII. The relevant threat is CPU exhaustion through unbounded parameters (a period of 5000 across many instances); parameters are bounded by `params_schema` (period 1..5000 per SCR-035) and validated both client-side and in the kernel. Persisted parameters arriving from `indicator_presets` or an imported `WorkspaceBundle` are re-validated before reaching a plugin. See E13-X01 for the epic threat model. The specific threat here is **tampering / integrity of an armed automation**: if a referenced metric can silently disappear, an armed rule could evaluate against a missing value. Controls: server-side authoritative guard, save-time resolution, and the rule that an unresolvable reference blocks arming. Authorization: the referencing-objects list must be filtered to what the caller may see, so the guard does not leak another user's rule names - assert this with a cross-user test. Flagged for the E13-X01 threat model.

## Accessibility notes
The blocking dialog is a proper alert dialog with focus trapped, the referencing rules as a navigable list, and each disarm/edit action separately named. Current-value display in a picker is announced with the metric name and unit, not as a bare number.

## Performance notes
Metric resolution for a picker must be a single registry read per key, memoised per cadence - opening the alert editor with twenty enabled indicators must not trigger twenty recomputations. Referential-guard queries are indexed; the removal path stays interactive (<200 ms).

## Observability
`metric_resolution_failures_total{key}` (should be zero in steady state), `indicator_removal_blocked_total`, audit entries when a rule is disarmed from the blocking dialog. Log unresolvable keys with the rule id at save time.

title: Security review of indicator endpoints, presets and metric exposure
body:
## Context
E13-X01 enumerates the threats; this ticket verifies the controls in the built code before E13 can close. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes security sign-off non-optional for anything touching authorization boundaries, and E13 has two: preset ownership (`/indicator-presets`) and the metric-exposure guard that can list another user's referencing rules if filtered incorrectly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Code review** by the Security engineer of: `/indicator-presets` handlers and their authorization checks, the `params_schema`-driven form renderer, the bundle-import validation path, the E13-S08 referencing-objects endpoint, and the kernel's parameter-bound and subscription-cap enforcement.
- **Abuse-case execution** of every case from E13-X01, with evidence recorded per case:
  - request/modify/delete another user's preset (expect 404, not 403);
  - mutate a built-in preset (expect 403);
  - POST a preset with `is_builtin: true`, a foreign `owner_user_id`, an unknown `indicator_code`, a non-token style value, an out-of-range period, and an oversized JSONB blob (expect 422/403, nothing persisted);
  - import a hand-crafted `WorkspaceBundle` with the same payloads (expect the same rejections, with `is_builtin`/`owner_user_id` never honoured from the payload);
  - delete an indicator instance referenced by an armed rule directly via the API, bypassing the UI (expect rejection with the referencing objects, filtered to the caller's visibility);
  - request the referencing-objects list as a user who cannot see the referencing rule (expect the rule not to be named);
  - subscribe to `compute: server` indicators beyond the per-user cap (expect rejection with a clear error, no unbounded backend work).
- **SAST rules**: Semgrep rules committed under the repo's rule directory for the E13-specific anti-patterns - rendering a schema-derived string as HTML/markdown, constructing a component from a payload-supplied name, and any JSONB write that is not preceded by schema validation.
- **SCA/secrets**: confirm the new fixture directory carries no secrets and that no new dependency was introduced for indicator maths without SCA clearance.
- Findings triaged with the Owner where acceptance rather than fix is proposed; sign-off comment on E13 and on the affected stories.

## Out of scope
- DAST/ZAP scanning of the whole app (the security program's scheduled activity) and penetration testing (E43).
- The rule engine's own review (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case is executed with evidence
  Then each E13-X01 abuse case has a recorded execution with request, response, and a pass/fail judgement

Scenario: Object-level authorization holds
  Given user B attempts to read, update or delete user A's preset
  Then every attempt returns 404 without disclosing existence, and an authorization-denial event is recorded

Scenario: Hostile payloads are rejected at the boundary
  Given a bundle import carrying is_builtin true, a foreign owner id, an unknown indicator code and an oversized style blob
  Then the import is rejected with the offending fields named and nothing is persisted, including no partial import

Scenario: The referencing list does not leak
  Given an indicator is referenced by a rule the caller cannot see
  Then the removal is still blocked but the response does not name that rule, and the caller is told to contact the owner

Scenario: SAST rules catch the pattern they exist for
  Given a deliberate violation (rendering a schema-derived string as HTML) is introduced
  Then the Semgrep rule fires in CI and blocks the PR
```

## Technical notes / design
Execute abuse cases against a staging build with two seeded users of differing roles (owner and manager) plus a viewer, so the RBAC matrix is genuinely exercised rather than assumed. Record raw request/response pairs (credentials redacted) as evidence per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.

## Test plan
Abuse cases are the tests; the durable ones are promoted into the automated suite (the cross-user preset case joins E13-Q02, the payload-validation cases join the backend contract suite) so the checks survive beyond this review.

## Security notes
This ticket produces the Epic DoD's "findings triaged (fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off), sign-off comment from Security engineer" evidence.

## Accessibility notes

title: Playwright E2E: drawing lifecycle, object tree and cross-chart sync
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 names the R1 E2E gate explicitly: "Playwright web **and** Electron: load chart, switch symbol/timeframe, add indicator, **draw and persist a drawing**, save and restore a workspace". Exit criterion 5 adds that drawings must survive reload, app restart and Electron relaunch with zero loss. Those are E14's obligations to the release, and they can only be discharged by a browser-level test that drives the real canvas, the real store and the real server.

Drawing tools are hostile to naive E2E: the interaction surface is a WebGL canvas with no DOM nodes to click. The suite therefore leans on two stable handles that E14 already owes for other reasons — the object tree `SCR-036` (the a11y-complete alternative, per `14-screens-catalogue.md`) and the keyboard drawing mode from `E14-K01`. Where a pointer path must be exercised, it is driven by deterministic canvas-relative coordinates derived from the engine's own projection helper exposed on a test-only handle, not by hard-coded pixels.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/drawings/` Playwright specs, run in both the web and Electron projects of the existing Playwright config:
  1. **`lifecycle.spec.ts`** — for the tool set shipped by S08 (hline, vline, trendline, ray, rectangle, ellipse, parallel channel, fib retracement, anchored VWAP, text, position tool): select the tool from `CMP-223 DrawingToolbar` by hotkey, place anchors, verify the shape appears in `SCR-036`'s Drawings branch with the expected accessible name, edit a style property in the `CMP-017` properties popover, drag an anchor, delete, undo, redo.
  2. **`persistence.spec.ts`** — create a mixed set, reload the page, assert identical set; restart the Electron app, assert identical set; log in as the same user in a second context, assert identical set; verify the R1 exit-criterion-5 wording literally (zero loss of symbol, timeframe, indicators, drawings, layout).
  3. **`object-tree.spec.ts`** — `SCR-036` operations: rename, toggle visibility, toggle lock, reorder (z-order), multi-select and bulk delete, with assertions that a locked drawing cannot be moved by dragging but remains selectable, per US-DRAW-008.
  4. **`sync.spec.ts`** — US-DRAW-009: two panes on the same symbol at different intervals with level-sync on → a level drawn in one appears in the other without reload; sync off → the drawing stays local and is marked local in the tree; a second symbol's pane never receives it (the "never syncs across different symbols" NFR).
  5. **`templates.spec.ts`** — save a style as a named template, apply it, assert new drawings of that type adopt colour/width/style/label settings; assert a custom fib level set (adding 0.886) becomes the default for new fib drawings.
  6. **`position-tool.spec.ts`** — drag entry/stop/target, assert displayed R:R, USDT risk, USDT reward and implied size match the account-profile sizing maths; choose "send to ticket" and assert the ticket opens pre-filled; with risk over the profile cap, assert the error state and that the action is disabled with a stated reason.
  7. **`keyboard.spec.ts`** — a full mouse-free path: hotkey tool selection (`Alt+T`/`Alt+H`/`Alt+F`/`Alt+R`/`Alt+M`), magnet toggle `Ctrl+M`, anchor placement via the keyboard crosshair stepping with Enter to confirm, arrow-key nudge (1 tick, Shift = 10 ticks), delete, `Ctrl+Z`/`Ctrl+Shift+Z`.
- **Test-only engine handle** (`window.__cvEngine.projectForTest(t, p)`), gated behind the E2E build flag and asserted absent in a production bundle by a dedicated test, so canvas coordinates are computed rather than hard-coded.
- **Deterministic seeding**: each spec starts from a known fixture symbol-day and a known drawing set posted through `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch` in `beforeEach`, and tears down by deleting the seeded user's drawings, so specs are order-independent and parallel-safe.
- **Visual assertions** kept deliberately narrow: masked screenshots of the toolbar and the properties popover only (stable DOM), never of the canvas — canvas pixels are compared nowhere, to avoid GPU-driver flake (`R8`).

## Out of scope
- Anchor-value invariants at data level — `E14-Q02` owns those and runs far faster.
- REST schema conformance — `E14-Q04`.
- Frame-rate and drag-latency measurement — `E14-Q05`.
- Disconnect/conflict behaviour — `E14-Q06`.
- Deep screen-reader transcripts and axe-core sweeps — `E14-Q07` (this suite proves the keyboard path exists and works; it does not judge announcement quality).
- Order placement beyond the ticket pre-fill assertion.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Draw and persist across reload and Electron relaunch
  Given a chart on BTCUSDT with no drawings
  When I create a trendline, a rectangle and a fib retracement and reload the page
  Then all three are present with identical anchors, styles and labels
  And after an Electron app relaunch they are still present and identical

Scenario: Cross-pane sync respects its scope
  Given two panes showing BTCUSDT at 1m and 1h with level-sync enabled
  When I draw a horizontal level in the 1m pane
  Then it appears in the 1h pane at the same price without a reload
  And a third pane showing ETHUSDT does not receive it

Scenario: Failure case - a locked drawing is dragged
  Given a trendline marked locked in the object tree
  When a drag is attempted on its mid-handle
  Then its geometry is unchanged in GET /api/v1/drawings
  And the drawing remains selectable and inspectable

Scenario: Edge case - the entire lifecycle with no mouse
  Given keyboard-only input in the keyboard drawing mode
  When I select the trendline tool with Alt+T, place both anchors with Enter, nudge with Shift+ArrowUp and delete
  Then each step is reflected in the object tree and in the persisted drawing set
  And Ctrl+Z restores the deleted trendline with all properties intact
```

## Technical notes / design
- Specs assert against the object tree's DOM (`role="tree"`, per SCR-036) and against `GET /api/v1/drawings` responses intercepted via Playwright's request API. Two independent oracles per assertion means a UI-only or a server-only regression is distinguishable from the trace.
- Electron coverage reuses the existing Electron Playwright project; only `persistence.spec.ts` and `lifecycle.spec.ts` run there, to keep the required-check runtime bounded — the rest run web-only, with the rationale recorded in the spec header.
- Debounced batch writes (500 ms per the `/drawings/batch` description) are awaited by waiting on the network request, never by `waitForTimeout`, so the suite does not encode the debounce constant.
- Drag interactions use `mouse.move` with intermediate steps so the engine's pointer-move handling and `E14-T04`'s hit-test are genuinely exercised rather than a single teleporting event.
- Each spec is tagged `@e14` so `E14-Q08`'s regression pack can select the whole epic's E2E set in one invocation.

## Test plan
- Determinism: the full suite runs 10× in the nightly job; any spec flaking more than once is quarantined and a fix ticket filed the same day per `03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Cross-browser: Chromium is the required check; a weekly run adds WebKit and Firefox to surface `R8` GPU/driver divergence early, with failures triaged rather than gating.
- Negative control: with `E14-T02`'s persistence deliberately stubbed out on a scratch branch, `persistence.spec.ts` must fail — proving the assertions are load-bearing.

## Security notes
- The `__cvEngine.projectForTest` handle is a deliberate test-only surface; a dedicated spec asserts it is `undefined` in a production build, and the bundler config strips it. This is recorded as a threat in `E14-X01` and its mitigation is this assertion.
- Specs authenticate through the normal login flow with seeded users; no token is written into the repo or into Playwright storage state that is committed.
- `sync.spec.ts` includes a benign isolation check (a second seeded user's drawings are not visible); the adversarial version lives in `E14-X02`.

## Accessibility notes
- `keyboard.spec.ts` is the executable proof of R1 exit criterion 9's drawing clause and is a required check, not an optional one.
- Every lifecycle assertion goes through the object tree's accessible name, so a drawing that renders but has no name fails the functional suite.
- Focus management is asserted at the coarse level: after closing the properties popover, focus returns to the invoking toolbar button; deeper focus-order review is `E14-Q07`.

## Performance notes
- The suite is not a benchmark, but it fails fast on pathological slowness: each spec has a hard 60 s budget and the seeded set is capped at 24 drawings so a timeout means a real regression, not a heavy fixture.
- `draw-dense-500` is deliberately *not* used here; it belongs to `E14-Q05`.

## Observability
- Traces, videos and the intercepted `/drawings` payloads are retained for every failure as CI artefacts.
- The suite asserts the SCR-037 analytics events (`drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`) fire with the expected properties, closing the gap where analytics silently break.

## Definition of Done
- All seven specs merged and green on Chromium web and on Electron for the two designated specs.
- Wired into the PR-required E2E job for paths under `apps/web/src/drawings/**` and into the nightly full run.
- Flake rate below the `03-testing-strategy.md` threshold over 10 consecutive nightly runs.
- Negative-control demonstration evidence linked on the ticket.
- Production-bundle assertion for the test handle passing.

## Dependencies
- `E14-Q01` (cases to automate), `E14-S03` and `E14-S04` (zone and projection tools exist), `E14-S10` (toolbar), `E14-K01` (keyboard pattern decided).
- Object tree surface from the E13/E14 shared `SCR-036` implementation.
- Position-tool spec additionally depends on the profile sizing implementation shared with US-PROF-002.

## Branch
`test/e14-e2e-drawings`

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criteria 5 and 9, §5.4 E2E gate
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037 (hotkeys, analytics events)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-007, US-DRAW-008, US-DRAW-009
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings`, `/drawings/batch`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (E2E layer, flake policy)
- `qa/plans/e14-drawing-tools-test-plan.md`


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md §3.9/§3.11 (hit-testing, interaction)
2. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
3. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md (relevant CMP entries)
4. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6/§4 (no drag-only, keyboard path)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

- packages/chart-engine/src/layers/drawings/**, apps/web/src/** (drawing toolbar/UI bindings), packages/ui/** (shared controls)
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- drawing tool plugin contract, hit-testing API, persistence schema for saved drawings; named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-017, CMP-223, SCR-036, SCR-037
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**

**Branch & PR**

title: Performance pack: drag FPS with 200 drawings, dense tree and batch write load
body:
## Context
Drawings are the most common way a user makes the chart slow. `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037 sets the budget explicitly: "drawings render on a separate canvas layer above the price layer; dragging a drawing must not re-render the price/footprint layers (target: drag at >=58 fps with 200 drawings on the chart)". `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criterion 2 adds the floor for the worst case: 30 fps with a 6-chart layout, all indicators and **all drawings**, using the documented degradation ladder — and trading-critical overlays must never be the thing shed. US-DRAW-005 pins an additional numeric budget (anchored VWAP incremental update ≤2 ms) and US-DRAW-008 pins a structural one (object tree virtualised for ≥500 objects).

Those numbers exist in prose. This ticket turns them into scripts that run, record and fail. It is the E14 contribution to the `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` regime and to risk `R2 Render performance`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmarks** in `packages/chart-engine/bench/drawings/`, run on the existing seeded-dataset harness from E11:
  1. `drag-200.bench.ts` — 200 mixed drawings on a 100k-bar series; scripted drag of one trendline across 600 frames; records p50/p95/p99 frame time and asserts p95 ≤ 17.2 ms (58 fps) on reference hardware.
  2. `layer-isolation.bench.ts` — asserts the price/footprint layers issue **zero** draw calls during a drawing-only drag, using the engine's render-pass counters. This is the structural guarantee behind the FPS number; if it breaks, the FPS number is luck.
  3. `hit-test.bench.ts` — `E14-T04`'s index queried at pointer-move rate against 500 drawings; asserts p95 query ≤ 0.5 ms and that cost is sub-linear in object count (500 objects must not cost 10× the 50-object case).
  4. `avwap-incremental.bench.ts` — anchored VWAP with σ bands updated tick-by-tick over a recorded dense fixture; asserts ≤2 ms per update per anchored VWAP and asserts the update cost is independent of the distance from the anchor (i.e. genuinely incremental, not a re-scan).
  5. `worst-case-ladder.bench.ts` — the roadmap's worst case: 6 panes, full R1 indicator set, `draw-dense-500`; asserts the 30 fps floor holds and records which degradation-ladder rungs engaged, asserting drawings and trading-critical overlays are not shed before decorative work.
- **Frontend/DOM benchmarks**:
  6. `object-tree.bench.ts` — `SCR-036` with 500 objects: initial render, scroll, filter, multi-select-all and bulk-delete; asserts virtualisation (DOM node count bounded, not 500) and interaction latency p95 ≤ 100 ms.
- **API load scripts** in `load/k6/drawings/`:
  7. `batch-write.js` — sustained drag-like traffic: N virtual users each posting a 50-op `POST /drawings/batch` every 500 ms for 10 minutes; asserts p95 server time and that Postgres write amplification stays bounded; includes a 500-op max-size scenario.
  8. `list-read.js` — `GET /drawings?symbol=` against a user with 500 drawings; asserts budget 28 from `21-database-schema.md` (< 5 ms query) and p95 API latency within the `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` REST budget.
- **Reporting**: all results written to the standard benchmark JSON consumed by the CI perf dashboard; the drag and layer-isolation benchmarks are wired as **required checks** with the roadmap's >10% regression rule failing the build.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of what is drawn — `E14-Q02`, `E14-Q03`.
- Chaos/failure behaviour under load (disconnects mid-batch) — `E14-Q06`.
- Whole-application perf hardening — E46.
- Footprint/heatmap render budgets — E18/E21 own theirs; only their *coexistence* with drawings is exercised in the worst-case ladder.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Drag stays above the SCR-037 budget
  Given 200 mixed drawings on a 100k-bar BTCUSDT series on reference hardware
  When a trendline anchor is dragged across 600 scripted frames
  Then p95 frame time is at most 17.2 ms
  And the price and footprint layers issue zero draw calls during the drag

Scenario: Anchored VWAP updates incrementally
  Given an anchored VWAP with three standard-deviation bands anchored 50 000 prints back
  When 10 000 further prints are applied one at a time
  Then each update completes within 2 ms
  And the per-update cost does not grow with distance from the anchor

Scenario: Failure case - a regression exceeds the tolerance
  Given a change that makes the drawings layer re-upload all geometry each frame
  When drag-200.bench.ts runs in CI
  Then p95 frame time exceeds the budget by more than 10 percent
  And the required perf check fails the pull request with the before and after numbers

Scenario: Edge case - worst case falls back gracefully, not arbitrarily
  Given a 6-pane layout with the full R1 indicator set and 500 drawings
  When the worst-case ladder benchmark runs
  Then frame rate never drops below 30 fps
  And the engaged degradation rungs exclude drawings and trading-critical overlays
```

## Technical notes / design
- "Reference hardware" is the machine class already defined for the E11 benchmark harness; results from any other machine are recorded but never gate, to keep the gate meaningful.
- Frame timings come from the engine's own instrumentation (a monotonic per-frame timer around the render-pass scheduler), not `requestAnimationFrame` deltas, so a benchmark machine's vsync does not mask a slow frame.
- Layer isolation is asserted via counters rather than by pixel comparison; counters are cheap, exact and stable across GPUs (important for `R8`).
- Hit-test sub-linearity is asserted as a ratio rather than an absolute, so the test survives hardware upgrades.
- The k6 scripts run against a dedicated staging instance with a seeded 500-drawing user; they are nightly, not per-PR, because they need real Postgres and 10 minutes.
- Every benchmark records the fixture, seed, commit SHA and hardware tag into its result JSON so historical comparison is valid.

## Test plan
- Calibration run on three consecutive commits of `main` to establish baselines and measure run-to-run variance; the regression threshold is set above measured noise, and the variance figure is recorded in the ticket.
- Seeded-regression validation: introduce per-frame geometry re-upload, a linear-scan hit test, and a full-recompute VWAP on a scratch branch; confirm each is caught by its own benchmark and by no other (precision of attribution matters for triage).
- Tree benchmark validated by disabling virtualisation on a scratch branch and confirming the DOM-node-count assertion fires.

## Security notes
- Load scripts run only against staging with seeded users, never production or live-connected environments; the k6 config pins the base URL and refuses a host outside the allowlist, so a mistyped target cannot become an unintentional DoS against a real deployment.
- The 500-op batch scenario doubles as a resource-exhaustion probe; any observed unbounded memory growth is reported to `E14-X01` as a DoS finding rather than only as a perf number.
- Benchmark artefacts contain no user data; fixtures are synthetic.

## Accessibility notes
- The object-tree benchmark measures the surface that `SCR-036` designates as the accessible alternative to canvas manipulation. A tree that is slow at 500 objects is an accessibility failure, not just a performance one, because it is the only path available to a keyboard or screen-reader user — this framing is recorded in the benchmark's header and its failures are routed to the a11y specialist as well as the perf owner.
- Keyboard nudge latency (arrow key → visible move) is measured in the tree benchmark file and budgeted at ≤100 ms so the keyboard path is not second-class.

## Performance notes
- Budgets asserted: SCR-037 drag ≥58 fps with 200 drawings; roadmap 30 fps floor at worst case; US-DRAW-005 ≤2 ms per anchored-VWAP update; US-DRAW-008 tree virtualised at ≥500 objects; `21-database-schema.md` budget 28 < 5 ms for the drawings query; plus the global frame budget #1 (≤16.6 ms p95) which the drag benchmark must not itself violate at rest.
- Any budget met only by degradation is recorded as *met with degradation* and reported separately, so the headline number never hides a shed feature.

## Observability
- Results published to the CI perf dashboard alongside E11/E12 benchmarks; a per-epic view shows E14's four gating numbers over time.
- k6 runs export to the same Prometheus/Grafana stack as the API load profiles, so drawings write load is visible next to general API load during soak weeks.

## Definition of Done
- All eight scripts merged and producing results; baselines recorded with measured variance.
- `drag-200` and `layer-isolation` wired as required CI checks with the >10% rule.
- Seeded-regression attribution evidence linked.
- Results for all budgets recorded against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and referenced from the E14 epic ticket for its DoD perf rollup.
- Nightly k6 job scheduled and green for three consecutive nights.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T03` (drawings render layer), `E14-T04` (hit-test index), `E14-S03` (zone tools, needed for a representative mixed set), `E14-S05` (anchored VWAP) for benchmark 4.
- E11 benchmark harness and reference-hardware definition; E13 indicator set for the worst-case ladder.

## Branch
`test/e14-perf-pack`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037 performance clause, SCR-036 performance clause
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criteria 1 and 2, §5.4 perf gate
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-005 NFR, US-DRAW-008 NFR
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1, #2
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` query budget 28
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (render passes, degradation ladder)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md §3.9/§3.11 (hit-testing, interaction)
2. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
3. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md (relevant CMP entries)
4. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6/§4 (no drag-only, keyboard path)

title: Chaos scenarios for drawings: offline edits, conflicts and partial batch failure
body:
## Context
`E14-T02` gives the client an optimistic store with debounced batch writes and a local undo stack. That design is right for interaction latency and wrong by default for durability: every optimistic system has a failure mode where the user believes something is saved and it is not. Because a drawing is a trader's record of a decision, a silently lost level is a correctness failure with real consequences, and `30-release-roadmap.md` exit criterion 5 requires zero loss across reload, restart and relaunch.

`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` mandates chaos/failover tests (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate limiting) as a distinct layer. This ticket applies that discipline to the drawings write path: what happens when the network dies mid-drag, when two sessions edit the same shape, when the server rejects half a batch, when the browser is closed before the debounce fires.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/drawings/chaos/` scenarios, executed with Playwright network interception plus a toxiproxy-style fault layer on the staging API:
  1. **Offline during drag** — go offline mid-drag, complete the drag, come back online. Expected: the mutation is retried and lands; the UI shows an unsaved/pending state while offline (never a silent success); the final server state matches the final on-screen geometry.
  2. **Offline permanently** — offline, create three drawings, reload without reconnecting. Expected: the user was warned before losing them (explicit unsaved indicator and a beforeunload-class guard), and the documented behaviour (loss vs local queue) is what actually happens — the scenario asserts the *documented* contract and fails if the contract is unwritten.
  3. **Close before debounce** — mutate and close the tab within the 500 ms debounce window. Expected: a flush on pagehide/visibilitychange, or an explicitly documented acceptance of the loss window. Silent loss without either is a defect.
  4. **Server 500 on batch** — the batch endpoint returns `500` for the first two attempts and succeeds on the third. Expected: bounded exponential retry, no duplicate shapes, no lost shapes, the user informed if retries exhaust.
  5. **Server 422 on batch (poison op)** — one operation in the batch is permanently invalid. Expected: because the batch is transactional, the whole batch fails; the client must not retry forever, must isolate the poison operation, must not roll the user's canvas back to a state they did not ask for without telling them, and must surface an actionable error.
  6. **Rate limited (429)** — rapid dragging triggers API rate limiting. Expected: backoff, coalescing of pending mutations into fewer batches, and no dropped final state.
  7. **Concurrent edit, two sessions** — the same drawing moved in session A and deleted in session B. Expected: the documented conflict policy (last-write-wins with `updated_at`, per the schema's `updated_at` column) is applied deterministically, both sessions converge, and the losing session is told rather than silently overwritten.
  8. **Concurrent edit, same session two panes** — the same symbol-scoped drawing edited from two synced panes simultaneously; expected convergence with no duplicate rows.
  9. **Clock skew** — a client whose clock is 10 minutes ahead writes a drawing; expected: server-assigned `updated_at` governs ordering and a skewed client cannot win a conflict it should lose.
  10. **Undo across a failed write** — delete a drawing, the delete fails at the server, then `Ctrl+Z`. Expected: the undo stack and the server state converge to one coherent outcome, with no phantom restore of a drawing that was never deleted, and no orphan.
  11. **Postgres unavailable** — the database is down for 30 s. Expected: `503` with the standard envelope, the client queues or reports, no client crash, full recovery without user action beyond a retry.
  12. **Soft-delete/restore race** — restoring via undo while the retention purge job targets the same soft-deleted row (retention: soft-deleted config rows purged after 90 d per `21-database-schema.md`). Expected: either a clean restore or a clean, explained failure — never a dangling reference from `alert_id` or from a synced pane.
- **A written failure-mode table** in `qa/plans/e14-drawings-chaos.md`: fault, injection method, expected observable behaviour, the contract clause it comes from, and the ticket that owns the fix if behaviour is undefined.

## Out of scope
- Engine-level WebGL context loss (owned by E11's chaos work), though scenario 13 cross-references it to confirm drawings are restored with the scene.
- Exchange-side faults; drawings do not touch the exchange.
- Perf under fault (`E14-Q05` covers clean-path load).
- Security-motivated fault injection (replay, forged ids) — `E14-X02`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A drag completed offline is not silently lost
  Given a trendline being dragged when the network drops
  When the drag completes and connectivity is restored within the retry window
  Then the final geometry is persisted exactly once
  And an unsaved-state indicator was visible for the whole offline period

Scenario: A poison operation does not wedge the client
  Given a batch containing one permanently invalid operation
  When the client receives 422 three times
  Then the client stops retrying, isolates the invalid operation and surfaces an actionable error
  And the remaining valid mutations are re-submitted successfully in a subsequent batch

Scenario: Failure case - concurrent edit produces divergence
  Given session A moves a drawing while session B deletes it
  When both mutations settle
  Then both sessions display the same final state after refresh
  And the session whose change was discarded was notified

Scenario: Edge case - the database is unavailable mid-session
  Given Postgres is stopped for 30 seconds
  When the user creates two drawings and continues working
  Then the API returns 503 with the standard error envelope and the client does not crash
  And after recovery the two drawings exist exactly once each with correct geometry
```

## Technical notes / design
- Faults are injected at two levels: Playwright route interception (status codes, latency, offline) for client-behaviour scenarios, and a proxy/container control for infrastructure scenarios (Postgres down, 429 from the gateway). Each scenario names its level so it can be run in the right environment.
- Every scenario ends with a **convergence assertion**: reload both sessions and compare `GET /drawings` payloads; "looks right on screen" is never sufficient.
- Duplicate detection uses drawing ids plus a geometry hash, catching both the classic "retry created two rows" and the subtler "retry created one row with stale geometry".
- Where behaviour is currently undefined (notably scenarios 2, 3 and 7), this ticket's job is to force a decision: the scenario file records the decision, the owning ticket implements it, and the test then asserts it. An undocumented behaviour is itself a finding, recorded on `E14-T02`.
- Scenarios are tagged `@e14 @chaos` and excluded from the PR-required set; they run nightly and before the R1 PRR.

## Test plan
- Each scenario runs 5× to shake out timing-dependent passes; a scenario that passes only sometimes is treated as a product defect, not a flaky test, until proven otherwise.
- A control run with no faults injected must pass every convergence assertion, proving the assertions are not fault-dependent.
- Results feed the R1 PRR evidence pack per `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Security notes
- Retry logic is checked for unbounded amplification: a client that retries a 500-op batch without backoff is a self-inflicted DoS vector and is reported to `E14-X01`.
- Scenario 7 and 9 confirm that conflict resolution relies on server-assigned timestamps, so a malicious or broken client cannot win a write race by lying about time — a tampering mitigation the threat model claims.
- Offline queues must not persist drawing payloads in plaintext beyond the session in a way that outlives logout; scenario 2 checks that logging out clears any queued mutations.

## Accessibility notes
- Every error and pending state introduced by these scenarios must be announced, not only coloured: unsaved/pending indicators and failure messages are asserted to be exposed via a polite live region per `05-accessibility-standard.md`, so a screen-reader user learns their level was not saved.
- Scenario 10 (undo across a failed write) is asserted through the object tree as well as the canvas, since the tree is the accessible surface.

## Performance notes
- Retry/backoff must not degrade interaction: during scenarios 4 and 6, frame time is sampled and must stay within the SCR-037 drag budget — a retry storm on the main thread would show up here.
- Coalescing is asserted quantitatively in scenario 6: N rapid mutations must produce fewer than N batches.

## Observability
- Each scenario asserts the expected server-side log and metric signature: failed batch counter, retry counter, conflict counter. A fault that is invisible in telemetry is reported as an observability gap against `E14-T01`/`E14-T02`.
- Client console errors are captured; an unhandled promise rejection during any scenario fails it.

## Definition of Done
- All twelve scenarios implemented, with the failure-mode table merged at `qa/plans/e14-drawings-chaos.md`.
- Every previously undefined behaviour now documented, with the owning ticket linked and the assertion in place.
- Nightly job green for three consecutive runs; results attached to the R1 PRR evidence pack.
- No unhandled client exceptions in any scenario.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T02` (optimistic store, retry, undo), `E14-Q04` (contract behaviour the chaos cases assume), `E14-T01` (endpoints).
- Fault-injection tooling shared with E08's chaos work.

## Branch
`test/e14-chaos-drawings`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (chaos/failover layer)
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings/batch` (transactional, debounced, idempotency)
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 (`updated_at`, `deleted_at`, `alert_id`), retention table
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criterion 5
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (PRR evidence)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (live regions for status)

title: Horizontal line, horizontal ray and vertical line with server persistence
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-001 — Horizontal line and ray (Must)**: "As a trader, I want persisted horizontal levels per symbol, so that my key levels are there every session." This is the simplest tool and therefore the one that proves the whole pipeline end to end — registry entry, engine geometry, hit-test, store, batch persistence, keyboard path — before the harder geometries arrive. The vertical line (`vline` in the `drawings.tool` enum, `vertical_line` in the API enum) ships alongside it because it is the same single-anchor problem on the other axis.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `horizontal_line`, `ray` (horizontal ray variant) and `vertical_line` registered in the E14-S10 tool registry with hotkey `Alt+H` for horizontal.
- Single-click creation at the crosshair; a horizontal line spans the full pane width, a horizontal ray extends right only from its anchor, a vertical line spans full pane height at a timestamp.
- Always-visible price label on the price axis for horizontal tools (live during drag) and a time label on the time axis for vertical lines.
- Drag to move (body or handle), with the price label updating live and the value saved on pointer-up per the US scenario "Edit".
- Delete via `Del`/`Backspace` on selection, removed from **all panes showing that symbol**, undoable.
- Keyboard: create at the focused crosshair price with `Enter`; nudge 1 tick with arrow keys, 10 ticks with `Shift+arrow` (US-DRAW-001 NFR); values snapped to the symbol's tick size.
- Persistence through the store to `/api/v1/drawings` with `tool` and `geometry.points = [{t, p}]`; `interval_scope` left NULL (all intervals).
- Grab handles ≥24 px per the NFR.

## Out of scope
- Line-cross alerts on the level (**E40**).
- Two-anchor trendlines and magnet snapping (**E14-S02**).
- Styling templates (**E14-S09**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Draw and persist
  When I draw a horizontal line on BTCUSDT and reload the app
  Then the line is still there at the same price on every BTCUSDT chart

Scenario: Edit
  When I drag the line
  Then the price label updates live and the new value is saved on release

Scenario: Delete
  When I select it and press Delete
  Then it is removed from all panes showing that symbol and the action is undoable

Scenario: Keyboard nudge respects tick size
  Given a horizontal line at 64,120.5 on a 0.1-tick symbol and keyboard focus on it
  When I press ArrowUp then Shift+ArrowUp
  Then the price becomes 64,120.6 then 64,121.6, each announced, and the final value is persisted

Scenario: Interval and scale changes do not move it
  Given a horizontal line on a 1m linear chart
  When I switch to 1h and to log scale
  Then the line renders at the identical price

Scenario: Save fails
  Given the API is unavailable when the drag is released
  Then the line stays at the new price locally, a "changes not saved" chip appears, and the value is persisted when connectivity returns
```

## Technical notes / design
A horizontal line is a one-point drawing whose `t` is recorded (for the ray variant's origin and for range queries) but whose rendering ignores `t` for the full-width case; `geometry.extend_left/extend_right` distinguishes line from ray, matching `DrawingInput`. Price values are `Decimal` and quantised to the instrument's `tick_size` from the symbol metadata on every mutation, so a drag can never persist an untradeable price. The axis label reuses the crosshair label primitive from E11 so its styling and contrast are already solved.

## Test plan
Unit: tick quantisation, ray vs line geometry, nudge maths. Golden image: line, ray and vertical line in both themes, selected and locked. E2E Playwright: draw → reload → assert price; drag → release → one batch request; delete → undo; keyboard create/nudge/delete with zero pointer events. Contract: persisted payload validates against `DrawingInput`. a11y: axe-core + accessible-name assertion.

## Security notes
No new server surface beyond E14-T01. The optional label is user content, length-capped and rendered as text. Persisted prices are validated server-side as decimals; a crafted payload with a non-numeric price is rejected 422 rather than stored.

## Accessibility notes
Each line exposes a surrogate node per E14-K01 named e.g. "Horizontal line at 64,120.5, unlocked". Creation, nudge and delete are fully keyboard-driven and announced politely. The price label meets 4.5:1 contrast against both themes; the level is distinguishable from indicator lines by more than colour (label text + focus ring).

## Performance notes
Single-anchor tools are the densest in practice (traders keep dozens of levels); creation, drag and delete must each stay within the drawings-layer frame budget with 200 objects present, and picking is unchanged at ≤1 ms.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool}`, `drawing.edited{tool}`, `drawing.deleted{tool}` analytics; the "changes not saved" chip increments `drawings_batch_retry_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the touched modules.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard-only path verified; screen-reader spot-check recorded.
- [ ] design-qa comparison against SCR-037 recorded.
- [ ] Golden images committed; QA black-box plan executed; demoed.
- [ ] Feature flag state recorded.

## Dependencies

## Branch
`feat/e14-level-tools`

title: Trendline, ray and extended line with magnet-to-OHLC snapping
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-002 — Trendline (Must), ray (Should), extended line (Could)**. This is the first two-anchor tool and it introduces **magnet mode**, the snapping behaviour the roadmap calls out explicitly in the E14 scope line ("magnet-to-OHLC") and which every later two-anchor tool inherits. The story's NFR is the Epic's core invariant: "anchors stored as (timestamp, price), never pixels; log/linear scale changes must not move them."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `trendline`, `ray`, `extended_line` in the registry (`Alt+T` for trendline), sharing one two-anchor placement pipeline: click first anchor → rubber-band preview → click second anchor → selected with both handles live.
- `geometry.extend_left` / `extend_right` distinguishing segment, ray and extended line; extended geometry clipped to the viewport before rendering and hit-testing.
- **Magnet mode** (`Ctrl+M`, also a toolbar toggle): during placement and drag, anchors snap to the nearest OHLC value of the bar under the cursor within a configurable snap radius (default 12 px), and the snap target is **highlighted** with a marker plus a textual announcement of which value was hit (open/high/low/close).
- Shift-constrained angles (0/45/90°) while placing or dragging an anchor.
- Anchors stored as `{t, p}` with `barIndex` derived, never stored; re-projection on interval change, bar-type change and log/linear flips leaves them invariant (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10 "time is authoritative across bar-spec changes").
- Live readout during placement: price delta, % change, bar count and elapsed time between anchors.
- Keyboard creation mode: step the crosshair bar-by-bar/tick-by-tick, `Enter` to place each anchor, `Esc` to cancel — per the US scenario "Keyboard creation".

## Out of scope
- Parallel channels (**E14-S03**) and pitchfork (descoped to R2 per `30-release-roadmap.md` §11 descoping ladder row 3 unless capacity allows).
- Fibonacci geometry (**E14-S04**).
- Snap-to-indicator-value or snap-to-drawing — not in R1.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Two-point draw
  When I click a start and end point
  Then the line is created, anchored to bar timestamps and prices, and stays correct through zoom and scale changes

Scenario: Magnet snap
  Given magnet mode is on
  Then anchors snap to the nearest OHLC value within the snap radius and the snap target is highlighted

Scenario: Keyboard creation
  When I use the keyboard drawing mode
  Then I can place both anchors by stepping the crosshair and confirming with Enter

Scenario: Anchors survive a bar-type change
  Given a trendline placed on 1m time bars
  When the chart switches to 500-tick bars and then to range bars
  Then both anchors resolve to the same timestamps and prices, within one tick, and the line is re-projected rather than re-anchored

Scenario: Extended line off-screen costs nothing
  Given an extended line whose projection leaves the viewport
  When the chart is panned far from it
  Then it is clipped before rasterisation and hit-testing, and pick duration is unchanged

Scenario: Degenerate placement is rejected
  Given both anchors land on the same pixel
  Then no drawing is persisted and the tool returns to placement state with a hint
```

## Technical notes / design
Snapping runs in the worker where the bar data already lives: the candidate set is the OHLC of the bar under the cursor plus its immediate neighbours, so the snap test is O(1) per pointer move and adds nothing measurable to the drag budget. The snap decision is recorded in the drawing's style metadata only for the highlight; the persisted anchor is the snapped `{t, p}` itself, so reopening the chart on another device reproduces the same line without re-snapping. Re-projection on bar-spec change uses the time axis's binary search from timestamp to position — the `screenToIndex(indexToScreen(i)) === i` property from §15 covers the identity requirement.

## Test plan
Unit: two-anchor placement state machine, extend flags, snap candidate selection, angle constraint maths. Property-based: for random viewports, bar specs and scale modes, anchor (t, p) is invariant — the explicit "drawing anchors are stable across bar-spec changes" property in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15. Golden image: segment/ray/extended, selected and hovered, both themes. E2E: mouse placement, magnet snap with highlight assertion, keyboard placement with zero pointer events, scale-flip invariance. Perf: drag with 200 drawings sustains ≥58 fps.

## Security notes
No new server surface. Snap radius and angle constraints are client-side conveniences; server-side validation still enforces the two-point minimum, so a client cannot persist a one-anchor trendline.

## Accessibility notes
Keyboard creation is a first-class path, not a fallback: entering it announces the mode and the current crosshair position; each anchor placement announces price and time; magnet snaps announce the matched value ("snapped to high 65,400"). The completed line's surrogate name composes both anchors. Snap highlight is shape + text, never colour alone.

## Performance notes
Snap test O(1) per pointer move; placement preview redraws only the drawings layer; extended lines clipped before rasterisation; drag at ≥58 fps with 200 drawings (SCR-037) and pick ≤1 ms (engine §3.9).

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=trendline|ray|extended_line}`, `drawing.magnet_toggled`, `drawing.snap_applied{ohlc_field}` analytics; `engine_snap_duration_ms` metric.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Anchor-invariance property test green over ≥10k generated cases.

title: Rectangle, ellipse, parallel channel and triangle zone tools
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-003 — Rectangle (Must), parallel channel (Should), triangle (Could)**, plus `ellipse` from the roadmap's E14 scope line. These are the first *filled* tools, which introduces the legibility problem the story names directly: fills must not make the candles under them unreadable. The NFR is explicit — "fills must respect the minimum contrast of candles drawn over them" — and the story requires a "flatten opacity" toggle for stacked zones.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `rectangle` (`Alt+R`), `ellipse`, `parallel_channel`, `triangle` in the registry, reusing the two-anchor pipeline; the channel adds a **third** drag that sets the band width, and the triangle a third anchor.
- Fill rendering with configurable `fill_colour` + `fill_opacity` (default token, default 0.15) and an independent border colour/width/dash, per `DrawingInput.style`.
- **Flatten opacity** global toggle in the toolbar: when on, overlapping fills composite to a single capped alpha instead of accumulating, so N stacked zones stay legible.
- Tooltip/readout reporting the rectangle's **price height** (absolute and %) and **bar width** (bars and elapsed time), per the US scenario.
- Parallel channel: both edges provably parallel in chart space (not screen space) so they stay parallel across log/linear flips and zoom; the median line is optional.
- Resize from any corner/edge handle; body drag moves the whole shape; Shift constrains to a square/circle or to the channel's angle.
- Keyboard creation: place anchors by stepping the crosshair; resize by focusing a handle and nudging.

## Out of scope
- Pitchfork (R2 per the descoping ladder) and Gann fan.
- Zone-entry alerts (**E40**).
- Auto-detected supply/demand zones — not a drawing tool.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rectangle zone
  When I draw a rectangle over a consolidation
  Then it renders with configurable fill opacity and border, and reports its price height and bar width in the tooltip

Scenario: Channel
  When I draw a parallel channel
  Then the third drag sets the width, and both edges stay parallel through scale changes

Scenario: Overlap legibility
  Given multiple overlapping zones
  Then fills blend without making price candles unreadable, and a "flatten opacity" toggle exists

Scenario: Channel parallelism survives a log flip
  Given a parallel channel on a linear scale
  When the chart switches to logarithmic
  Then both edges remain parallel in chart space and the band width in price terms is preserved at each anchor

Scenario: Zero-area shape is rejected
  Given a rectangle dragged to zero width or zero height
  Then it is not persisted and the tool returns to placement state with a hint

Scenario: Resize by keyboard
  Given a rectangle is selected and a corner handle is focused
  When arrow keys are pressed
  Then that corner moves 1 tick (10 with Shift), the new dimensions are announced, and the change is persisted on blur
```

## Technical notes / design
Fills are drawn by the T03 quad batch with premultiplied alpha; the flatten-opacity toggle is a single uniform that switches the blend from additive accumulation to a max-alpha composite, so it costs nothing per shape. A parallel channel is stored as three points (two defining the first edge, one defining the offset) and the second edge is derived at render time from the chart-space offset — storing four independent points would let the edges drift apart on a scale change. The ellipse is stored as its bounding box and evaluated by fragment SDF. Contrast: the default fill token is chosen so candle bodies retain ≥3:1 against the filled background in both themes, and the golden images assert it.

## Test plan
Unit: shape geometry, derived channel edge, zero-area rejection, dimension readout maths. Property-based: channel edges remain parallel under random viewport/scale transforms. Golden image: each shape, filled/unfilled, overlapping stack with flatten on and off, both themes; contrast assertion on candles under a fill. E2E: draw, resize, channel third-drag, flatten toggle, keyboard resize. a11y: axe-core, announcements.

## Security notes
No new server surface. Fill opacity is clamped server-side to [0,1] by the `DrawingInput` schema, so a crafted payload cannot produce an opaque full-screen overlay that hides the trading UI (a UI-redress consideration).

## Accessibility notes
Surrogate names compose the shape, its bounds and its dimensions ("Rectangle, 2026-10-13 09:00 to 13:00, 63,900 to 64,400, height 500, 240 bars"). Zones are distinguishable without colour by their border style and label. Fill defaults preserve text and candle contrast per `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the flatten-opacity control is keyboard-reachable and its state announced.

## Performance notes
Fills add one quad instance per shape — no tessellation. Flatten mode is a uniform switch, not a second pass. Drag/resize with 200 drawings sustains ≥58 fps; pick for boxes uses rect containment within the ≤1 ms budget.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=rectangle|ellipse|parallel_channel|triangle}`, `drawing.flatten_opacity_toggled`, `drawing.resized{tool}` analytics.

- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Contrast assertion automated in the golden-image suite.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend / ≥85% engine on touched modules.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard create/resize verified; design-qa recorded.

title: Fibonacci retracement, extension and time-zone tools with configurable levels
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-004 — Fibonacci retracement (Must) and extension (Should)** plus `fib_timezone` from the roadmap's E14 scope line. The story's NFR — "level configuration stored in drawing templates" — makes this the first tool whose *configuration*, not just its geometry, is persisted and reusable, which is why it lands before templates (E14-S09) but hands its level-set schema to it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `fib_retracement` (`Alt+F`), `fib_extension`, `fib_timezone` in the registry, built on the two-anchor pipeline (extension takes a third anchor for the projection origin).
- Default level set 0 / 0.236 / 0.382 / 0.5 / 0.618 / 0.786 / 1, rendered as horizontal level lines with **price and percentage labels** per level, stored in `geometry.levels` per `DrawingInput`.
- Level editor in the properties popover: add/remove/reorder levels, per-level visibility, per-level colour, optional per-level fill band between adjacent levels, and "save as default" so new fib drawings adopt the trader's set (US scenario "Customise levels").
- Inverted drag handling: dragging high→low inverts the level ordering correctly and keeps labels readable (no overlapping or upside-down text).
- Label collision handling: when levels crowd at high zoom-out, labels decimate by priority (0, 0.5, 0.618, 1 survive longest) rather than overprinting.
- Fib time-zone: vertical lines at Fibonacci bar counts from the anchor, labelled with the index and the resulting timestamp.
- Extension with both extend-left/extend-right behaviour for the level lines.

## Out of scope
- Auto-fib from detected swings — not R1.
- Fib channels/arcs/fans/spirals.
- Alerts on level touches (**E40**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Draw retracement
  When I drag from swing low to swing high
  Then levels 0/0.236/0.382/0.5/0.618/0.786/1 render with price and percentage labels

Scenario: Customise levels
  When I add a 0.886 level and save as default
  Then new Fibonacci drawings use my level set

Scenario: Inverted drag
  When I drag high to low
  Then levels invert correctly and labels remain readable

Scenario: Crowded labels decimate rather than overprint
  Given a fib drawing compressed to 60 px of vertical space
  Then only the priority levels keep labels, the rest render as lines, and no two labels overlap

Scenario: Invalid level input is rejected
  Given a level value that is not a finite number, or a duplicate of an existing level
  Then the editor shows a field-level error and the level set is not saved

Scenario: Levels survive persistence
  Given a fib with a custom 0.886 level
  When the app is reloaded
  Then the custom level set is restored exactly, including per-level colours and visibility
```

## Technical notes / design
Level prices are computed as `p0 + (p1 - p0) * level` in `Decimal`, quantised for display to the instrument's tick size but **not** quantised in storage (levels are derived, not anchors). Percentage labels are derived from the level value itself, so an inverted drag needs no special-casing beyond label placement. Level lines are ordinary line instances from T03; the optional bands are quad instances, so a 12-level fib is 12 + 11 instances — well inside the overlay budget. Label decimation reuses the axis-decimation priority mechanism from E11 rather than inventing a second one.

## Test plan
Unit: level price maths including inverted and negative-extension cases, decimal precision, duplicate/NaN rejection, decimation priority. Golden image: default set, custom set with bands, inverted, compressed (decimated), both themes. E2E: draw → customise → save as default → new drawing adopts it → reload persists. Contract: `geometry.levels` round-trips through `/drawings`.

## Security notes
Level arrays are user-controlled: the API and client both cap the level count (default 24) so a crafted payload cannot force thousands of line instances and degrade the render loop (availability). Values are validated as finite numbers server-side.

## Accessibility notes
The surrogate exposes the fib as a group with each level as a child ("0.618 at 64,318.4"), so a screen-reader user can read the levels without seeing them. Level colours are supplemented by the numeric label, never colour-alone. The level editor is a standard keyboard-operable list with add/remove buttons, labelled fields and error text tied by `aria-describedby`.

## Performance notes
Level recomputation on drag is O(levels) and runs in the worker; label decimation is computed once per viewport change, not per frame. A fib with the maximum level count stays inside the 200-drawing overlay budget and the ≤3 text draw calls per pane limit.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=fib_retracement|fib_extension|fib_timezone}`, `drawing.fib_levels_changed{count}`, `drawing.default_saved{tool}` analytics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on touched modules.
- [ ] Golden images committed including the decimated state.
- [ ] axe-core green; level editor verified keyboard-only; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] Level-set schema handed to E14-S09 templates and documented.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-S02** (two-anchor pipeline). Feeds **E14-S09** (templates carry level sets).

## Branch
`feat/e14-fibonacci-tools`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-004; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `DrawingInput.geometry.levels`; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10, §3.7 decimation.

title: Abuse cases: stored XSS in annotations, IDOR on /drawings and payload exhaustion
body: ## Context `E14-X01` produces the theory; this ticket attacks the running system. `04-security-program.md` requires abuse-case testing per epic and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires, for anything touching authorisation, "a manual abuse-case check performed (e.g. attempt privilege escalation)". E14 has three abuse surfaces worth real effort: 1. **Stored XSS.** US-DRAW-006's NFR already says "text sanitised before storage and rendering", which is an admission that annotation text is dangerous. The text travels from a user, through JSONB, back to *two* sinks — the DOM (object tree `SCR-036`, properties popover, tooltips, accessible names) and the WebGL SDF text layer. The DOM sink is the exploitable one, and it is reached by the very component designated as the accessibility alternative, so it cannot be avoided by "we only draw it on canvas". 2. **IDOR.** Every `/drawings` route is `scope: self`. The batch endpoint accepts up to 500 arbitrary UUIDs for `update`/`delete` in one authenticated call — the single densest authorisation check in R1. In a deployment with Owner, Manager and Viewer roles sharing one server, a broken check means one user reads or destroys another's strategy levels. 3. **Resource exhaustion.** `geometry` is `additionalProperties: true` with no documented size cap; polyline/brush tools generate large point arrays legitimately, so there is no natural ceiling. ## Scope / Deliverables - **Hostile-input corpus** at `qa/security/corpus/drawings-text.json`, owned here and referenced (not duplicated) by `E14-Q01` and `E14-Q07`: classic and context-specific XSS vectors (`

title: Functional pack for cross-pane sync groups and price-scale linking
body:
## Context
Cross-pane sync (US-LAY-003) and scale linking (US-LAY-004) are the features most likely to produce subtle, hard-to-reproduce wrongness: a crosshair that aligns by index instead of timestamp, a group that leaks into another group, a drawing that syncs onto a pane showing a different symbol, or a linked price scale that silently rescales a pane the trader is reading. Those are analysis-integrity bugs (risk R7 in spirit, R2 in cost) and they are invisible in a screenshot.

`SCR-023` specifies the contract: independent toggles for symbol / interval / crosshair / time range / drawings / y-scale / account-group; membership of groups A/B/C with letter-plus-colour badges; runtime over a local sync bus with no server round-trip; propagation that must not trigger a React re-render (≤4 ms across 6 panes). This ticket builds the pack that proves it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/specs/layouts/sync-groups.spec.ts` plus a component-level harness suite under `web/src/features/layout/__tests__/syncBus.spec.ts`:
  - **Axis independence**: for each of the seven toggles, enabling it propagates exactly that axis and nothing else (a 7 × 7 matrix asserting the off-diagonal is inert).
  - **Group scoping**: panes in group A and group B; changes in A never reach B or ungrouped panes; `Ctrl+Shift+1..3` assignment and `Ctrl+Shift+0` unsync.
  - **Crosshair alignment by timestamp**: a 1 m pane and a 5 m pane on the same symbol; moving the crosshair at t aligns the 5 m pane to the bar *containing* t, and the `SCR-023` conflicting-interval notice is shown.
  - **Drawing sync same-symbol rule**: a drawing created in a BTCUSDT pane appears in the other BTCUSDT pane in the group and does **not** appear in the ETHUSDT pane.
  - **Scale linking** (`SCR-043`, CMP-188/CMP-189): linked panes on the same symbol share price-axis zoom; unlinking restores independence and the axis shows the unlinked state; linking panes with very different price magnitudes is refused with an explanation and percentage-scale is suggested.
  - **Persistence**: group membership, per-axis toggles and per-pane link state round-trip through `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}` and survive a reload.
- A **render-purity assertion**: instrumentation counting React commits during a crosshair sweep across 6 panes; the spec fails if commits exceed the documented zero-React-render expectation.
- A regression fixture `six-pane-sync` (3 symbols × 2 intervals) reused by `E15-Q04` and `E15-Q08`.

## Out of scope
- Drawing tool correctness itself (E14) — this pack asserts propagation, not geometry.
- Indicator set sync beyond what E13 already exposes.
- Sub-frame timing measurement under load — `E15-Q04`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Selective sync propagates exactly one axis
  Given panes P1 and P2 are in sync group A with symbol sync on and interval sync off
  When P1 is switched from BTCUSDT 1m to ETHUSDT
  Then P2 shows ETHUSDT and keeps its own interval
  And no other pane property on P2 changes

Scenario: Groups do not leak
  Given P1,P2 are in group A and P3,P4 are in group B
  When the crosshair moves in P1
  Then P2 shows a crosshair at the same timestamp and P3,P4 show none

Scenario: Failure case - incompatible scale link is refused
  Given a BTCUSDT pane near 60000 and a pane on a symbol near 0.5
  When the trader links their price scales
  Then linking is refused with an explanation naming the magnitude difference and offering percentage scale
  And neither pane's existing scale is mutated

Scenario: Edge case - crosshair across mismatched intervals
  Given a 1m pane and a 5m pane are crosshair-synced
  When the crosshair sits on the 1m bar at 10:03
  Then the 5m pane highlights the 10:00-10:05 bar and shows the interval-mismatch notice

Scenario: Group identity is not colour-only
  When a pane joins group B
  Then its badge renders the letter "B" as text alongside the colour
  And a screen reader announces the group change
```

## Technical notes / design
- Drive the sync bus directly in the component-level suite (fast, deterministic, covers the 7×7 matrix) and keep the E2E spec to a representative subset — a full matrix in Playwright would be slow and flaky for no extra signal.
- Assert timestamps, never pixel positions, for crosshair alignment; pixel assertions break on any axis-margin change.
- Persisted sync state lives in the layout document (`layouts` / `layout_panes` per `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1), not in a separate table — the round-trip assertion must read it back through the API to catch serializer drift.

## Test plan
- Component suite runs on every PR (sub-second); E2E subset joins the `E15-Q02` suite.
- Manual exploratory addendum: one 30-minute charter driving six panes with mixed symbols/intervals looking for propagation ordering artefacts (e.g. the last pane in a group lagging a frame).
- Negative verification: temporarily broaden a group filter locally and confirm the group-scoping specs fail.

## Security notes
- Sync is client-local (no server round-trip per `SCR-023`); a spec asserts that no network request is issued during a crosshair sweep, which also prevents a future regression from leaking per-move telemetry about what a trader is inspecting.
- Account/group sync (the "Selected account/group" toggle) must never cause a pane to display data for an account the user cannot read; a case asserts the pane refuses and shows a permission notice rather than rendering.

## Accessibility notes
- Badge text assertion (letter present, not colour alone) per `05-accessibility-standard.md` and the `SCR-023` sign-off checklist.
- Group change announcements are asserted via the live region text.
- Sync toggles are reachable and operable by keyboard with visible focus; the popover traps and restores focus correctly.

## Performance notes
