title: Saved workspaces: switcher, settings, restore and conflict handling
body:
## Context
This Story is where R1 exit criterion 5 is actually earned: "Chart state (symbol, timeframe, indicators, drawings, layout) survives reload, app restart, and Electron relaunch with zero loss." It implements **US-LAY-002** — save a workspace as "EU session" storing "panes, symbols, intervals, indicators, footprint settings, DOM config, panels and hotkey profile"; restore "including scroll position and pane sizes, with data loading progressively"; and the failure case that matters most, a delisted symbol: "the pane opens in an explicit error state naming the symbol, and the rest of the workspace still loads". Its NFR is a hard number: restore to interactive in ≤3 s for a 4-pane workspace from warm cache.

Surfaces: **SCR-020** workspace tabs and save/reset chrome, **SCR-011** workspace switcher (CMP-073), **SCR-025** Workspace settings modal, **SCR-029** Unsaved-changes / layout-conflict dialog, **SCR-150** global boot/restore state. Storage and transport are already built by **E15-T01**.

The conflict case is real, not theoretical: the same user runs the terminal in Electron and a browser tab, or two monitors' windows. The OpenAPI description of `PUT /workspaces/{id}/layouts/{layoutId}` says why `If-Match` exists — "prevents a stale tab from clobbering a newer arrangement made in another window" — and SCR-029 specifies what the user sees when it fires.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Workspace switcher** (CMP-073, SCR-011/SCR-020 tabs): list, create, duplicate, rename, delete, reorder, set default; the unsaved marker `*` on the tab.
- **Save semantics**: `Ctrl+S` saves, `Ctrl+Shift+S` saves as; autosave of layout changes with a 2 s debounce sending a full `PUT` with `If-Match`; a save that changes nothing does not write.
- **Restore**: on boot, load the default (or last-used) workspace via one `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{id}` and mount panes progressively — layout frame first, then each pane's data — so the skeleton is on screen long before the last kline page arrives (SCR-020: "loading skeleton, no data fetch until mount"; SCR-150).
- **Per-pane state captured**: symbol, interval, chart template, indicator preset ids, drawings scope, scroll/visible-range, pane-specific config (footprint/DOM settings as those Epics land), sync group and axes, scale mode — all into `layout_panes` columns and `pane_config` per `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1.
- **Per-workspace theme and density** (roadmap §5.2 scope line) plus default symbol/interval and "open on startup", edited in **SCR-025**; saving applies without a full workspace remount, only re-resolving panes bound to a changed default.
- **Delete guards** (SCR-025): deleting requires typing the workspace name; the last workspace cannot be deleted ("You need at least one workspace.").
- **Conflict handling (SCR-029)**: on 412, show the conflict variant with a plain-text side-by-side summary of differences (panel count, symbols, sync groups) and [Keep mine] / [Load theirs]; on navigation with unsaved changes, show the unsaved variant with Save / Discard / Cancel, Esc mapping to Cancel and never to Discard, and no default destructive button.
- **Crash restore**: after an abnormal exit the workspace is restored from the last autosave with a notice naming the time ("Restored your layout from 14:02").
- **Missing/delisted symbol**: the pane mounts into an explicit error state naming the symbol with a rebind action; siblings load normally; the workspace stays savable.

## Out of scope
- Export/import files — **E15-S07**.
- Server-pushed conflict notification over WS — R1 detects conflicts on write only.
- Sharing a workspace with another user — R5 collaboration.
- Account/environment binding of a workspace — **E27/E44**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full-fidelity save and restore
  Given a 4-pane workspace with distinct symbols, intervals, indicator presets, drawings, sync groups and scroll positions
  When it is saved as "EU session", the app is quit and relaunched, and the workspace is opened
  Then every pane restores with the same symbol, interval, indicators, drawings, sync group, scale mode, size and visible time range
  And it reaches interactive within 3 s from warm cache

Scenario: Progressive loading, not a blocking wait
  When a saved workspace is opened
  Then the layout skeleton with named panel frames is visible before any market data has arrived, and each pane fills in independently as its data loads

Scenario: A delisted symbol degrades one pane only
  Given a saved pane references a symbol that no longer exists on the exchange
  When the workspace is restored
  Then that pane shows an error state naming the symbol and offering to rebind it
  And the other three panes load and are fully interactive, and the workspace can still be saved

Scenario: A stale window cannot clobber a newer arrangement
  Given the workspace is open in two windows and window B has saved a change
  When window A's autosave fires with its stale token
  Then the API returns 412, window A shows the conflict dialog with a text summary of the differences, and nothing is overwritten until the user chooses

Scenario: Unsaved changes are never silently discarded
  Given the active workspace has unsaved layout changes
  When the trader switches workspaces or closes the app
  Then the unsaved-changes dialog offers Save layout, Discard changes and Cancel, no destructive button is the default, and Esc maps to Cancel

Scenario: The last workspace cannot be deleted
  Given the user has exactly one workspace
  When they attempt to delete it
  Then the action is refused with "You need at least one workspace." and the workspace remains

Scenario: Crash restore is disclosed, not silent
  Given the app exited abnormally after an autosave at 14:02
  When it next starts
  Then the layout is restored and a notice states that it was restored from 14:02

Scenario: Changing density does not remount the workspace
  When the density is changed from cosy to compact in workspace settings
  Then panel chrome re-renders at the new density, no WebGL context is recreated, and no pane refetches data
```

## Technical notes / design
Save is full replacement of the layout aggregate, not a diff — the client always holds the whole tree, and `PUT` with `If-Match` gives us conflict detection for free. The 2 s debounce means a drag that takes four seconds produces two writes, which is fine; what matters is that a write is never issued mid-drag.

Restore ordering is the whole 3 s NFR. Mount the tree first (cheap, no network), then let each pane fetch its own history in parallel with a per-pane skeleton. Nothing waits on the slowest pane. Warm cache means E12's kline cache is populated; the number is measured in that condition, as the NFR states.

The delisted-symbol case is handled at mount, not at save: symbols are validated against E08's instrument list when a pane resolves, and an unknown symbol produces an error pane rather than an exception that takes the tree down. The error pane is a first-class registry entry so it participates in focus order and announcements like any other panel.

Crash detection is a clean-shutdown flag written on graceful exit; its absence at boot means the last autosave is a crash restore and must be disclosed (SCR-020's "Restored your layout from 14:02" state).

Density and theme are token-level: they change CSS custom properties from E05's design system, which is why they can apply without a remount.

## Test plan
Unit: serialisation of pane state to `LayoutInput` and back, debounce behaviour, dirty tracking, ETag handling, clean-shutdown flag. Component: switcher CRUD, settings modal validation (name 1..40, unique, delete confirmation by typing the name), conflict and unsaved dialog variants. Integration: save→reload→restore fidelity across all captured fields against a real API; 412 path; last-workspace guard. E2E (Playwright web + Electron): the full exit-criterion-5 script — build a 4-pane workspace, reload the page, restart the app, relaunch Electron, assert zero loss each time; delisted-symbol restore using a fixture instrument list; two-window conflict. Perf: restore-to-interactive ≤3 s from warm cache at 4 panes, measured and recorded. A11y: axe on SCR-011, SCR-020, SCR-025, SCR-029; screen-reader pass of the conflict dialog (`role="alertdialog"`, verb-labelled buttons) and the boot/restore announcement.

## Security notes
All access is `scope: self` and enforced server-side by E15-T01; the client never sends a user id and cannot address another user's workspace. Workspace names and pane labels are user content rendered as text, length-capped at the boundary. The clean-shutdown flag and any autosave cache stored locally must contain no credentials — layouts reference symbols and preset ids only, never keys or tokens — which is also what makes the same payload safe to export in E15-S07. Data classification: user preference data. STRIDE note: the conflict path must fail closed — a 412 never results in a blind retry that overwrites, since that would turn a benign race into silent data loss.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Workspace tabs follow the tabs pattern with the unsaved `*` also conveyed in the accessible name ("Scalping, unsaved changes"), never by the glyph alone. SCR-029 is `role="alertdialog"` with three explicitly verb-labelled buttons ("Save layout", "Discard changes", "Cancel"), no default destructive action, Esc mapped to Cancel; the difference summary is text, not a canvas. SCR-025 is a standard modal form with grouped fieldsets and an error summary linking to fields. Boot/restore announces progress politely on SCR-150 and announces the crash-restore notice once. Each restoring pane's skeleton carries an accessible name so a screen reader hears "Chart, BTCUSDT 1 minute, loading" rather than an unlabelled region.

## Performance notes
Restore to interactive ≤3 s for 4 panes from warm cache (US-LAY-002 NFR); one `GET` per workspace, never per pane; panes mount lazily on first visibility and hidden tabs unsubscribe after 30 s (SCR-020); autosave debounced 2 s; settings changes apply without remount, re-resolving only affected panes (SCR-025); conflict dialog appears within 300 ms of detection (SCR-029).

## Observability
`workspace.saved`, `workspace.updated`, `workspace.deleted`, `workspace.duplicated`, `workspace.switched`, `layout.saved`, `layout.reset`, `layout.conflict_detected`, `layout.conflict_resolved {choice}`, `workspace.restored {source: 'normal'|'crash', panes, durationMs}`, `workspace.pane_error {reason: 'delisted'|'unknown_kind'}`. Client metric `workspace_restore_seconds` histogram tagged with pane count and cache state — this is the number R1 exit criterion 5 is audited against.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the workspace persistence, switcher and dialog modules.
- [ ] R1 exit criterion 5 script green in CI for web reload, app restart and Electron relaunch.
- [ ] Restore-to-interactive measured ≤3 s at 4 panes and recorded.
- [ ] SCR-011, SCR-020, SCR-025, SCR-029 design tickets Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior or waivers recorded.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass of conflict and restore flows.
- [ ] Security review of locally cached layout payloads (no secrets) signed off.
- [ ] PRs ≤400 LOC each, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T01** (API and storage), **E15-T02** (tree and reconciler), **E13** (indicator presets must exist to be captured), **E14** (drawings must exist to be captured). Blocks **E15-S07**.

## Branch
`feat/e15-saved-workspaces`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-002; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 (E15 scope line), §5.3 criterion 5; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-011, SCR-020, SCR-025, SCR-029, SCR-150; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-073, CMP-014, CMP-015, CMP-027, CMP-038, CMP-044, CMP-065, CMP-207; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-LAY-002 row; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts/{layoutId}`.

title: Cross-pane sync configuration: groups and per-axis toggles (SCR-023)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-LAY-003** — "sync symbol, interval, crosshair, time range and drawings across panes, so that multi-timeframe reading is coherent" — with its three scenarios: crosshair sync moves at the same timestamp across a group; selective sync lets symbol propagate while interval stays per pane; sync groups A and B are isolated and each pane's group is labelled. NFR: propagation ≤1 frame, groups persisted in the workspace.

**E15-T03** built the bus and proved the budget. This Story is the control surface: **SCR-023** Multi-chart sync configuration and **CMP-218** SyncMenu, with the per-pane badge that makes membership visible at a glance, plus the group entry in **CMP-216**'s panel menu and the shell's `sync` menu on SCR-020.

One design constraint is non-negotiable and appears in three documents: group membership is conveyed by **letter and name**, never by colour alone (SCR-023 "the badge is text ('A')", CMP-218, and the SCR-020 design checklist "symbol-group colour tags carry a letter/number too").

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-023** popover/modal from the shell's sync menu: group selector (A / B / C / none) and independent toggles for **symbol**, **interval**, **crosshair**, **time range**, **drawings (same symbol only)** and **Y-scale** (the last handing off to E15-S05), plus a list of the panels currently in the selected group.
- **CMP-218 SyncMenu** as the per-panel control, reachable from the panel header and from CMP-216's "Sync group ▸" submenu.
- **Per-pane sync badge**: letter + group name + colour, rendered in the panel header (CMP-082) and included in the panel's accessible name.
- **Hotkeys**: `Ctrl+Shift+1..3` assign the active panel to group A/B/C, `Ctrl+Shift+0` unsync — routed through E10's remappable hotkey layer.
- **Persistence**: axis flags to `layouts.crosshair_sync`, `layouts.symbol_sync`, `layouts.level_sync` and group membership into each pane's `pane_config`, saved by E15-S03's autosave; a restored workspace comes back with its groups intact.
- **Mismatch warning**: when group members have different intervals, SCR-023's explanatory notice ("Chart 3 has a different interval — crosshair sync will align by timestamp") is shown in the configuration surface, not as a blocking error.
- **Drawings sync** restricted to same-symbol members, per US-LAY-003's scenario and US-DRAW-009's prohibition on cross-symbol drawing sync.
- Leaving a group resets nothing: a pane keeps its own symbol, interval and settings on exit (SCR-023 design checklist).

## Out of scope
- The propagation machinery, loop suppression and timestamp alignment — **E15-T03**.
- Price-scale linking semantics and the refusal path — **E15-S05**.
- Account/trade-group sync (the "Selected account/group" row in SCR-023's sketch) — **R3**, rendered disabled with a reason in R1.
- Syncing across browser tabs or machines.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crosshair follows across a group by timestamp
  Given panes 1 and 2 are in group A with crosshair sync enabled and different intervals
  When the crosshair moves in pane 1
  Then pane 2's crosshair sits on the bar containing the same timestamp, within one frame

Scenario: Axes toggle independently
  Given group A has symbol sync on and interval sync off
  When the symbol is changed in any member
  Then every member changes symbol and each keeps its own interval

Scenario: Groups are isolated and labelled
  Given panes 1 and 2 are in group A and pane 3 is in group B
  Then each pane's header shows its group letter and name, pane 3 is unaffected by any change in group A, and the sync surface lists the members of the selected group

Scenario: Membership is not conveyed by colour alone
  Given a trader who cannot distinguish the group colours
  When they inspect a pane header or hear it announced
  Then the group is identified by letter and name in visible text and in the accessible name

Scenario: Drawings sync only between same-symbol panes
  Given group A contains two BTCUSDT panes and one ETHUSDT pane with drawings sync on
  When a drawing is created on one BTCUSDT pane
  Then it appears on the other BTCUSDT pane and never on the ETHUSDT pane

Scenario: Groups survive a restart
  Given a workspace with groups A and B configured and specific axes enabled
  When it is saved, the app restarted and the workspace reopened
  Then the same panes are in the same groups with the same axis flags

Scenario: Leaving a group changes nothing else
  Given a pane in group A showing ETHUSDT 5m after symbol sync had propagated
  When it is set to no group
  Then it keeps ETHUSDT 5m, its indicators and its visible range, and simply stops following the group

Scenario: Interval mismatch is explained, not blocked
  Given group members have different intervals
  Then the sync surface shows the timestamp-alignment notice and sync continues to work
```

## Technical notes / design
Groups are fixed identities (A, B, C) rather than free-form names: three is what SCR-023 specifies, it maps cleanly to three hotkeys, and it removes a naming UI plus a whole class of collision handling from R1. A pane belongs to at most one group.

Axis flags live at two levels by design — the layout row carries the group defaults that the schema already models (`crosshair_sync`, `symbol_sync`, `level_sync`), while the per-pane group id lives in `pane_config`. That matches §3.8.1 without inventing a table, and it means E15-S03's save path needs no special case.

The configuration surface never touches the engine directly; it writes flags into the SyncBus, which owns the frame-scheduled dispatch. That separation is why toggling an axis mid-sweep cannot cause a re-entrant update.

The "Selected account/group" row is rendered now and disabled with a reason, rather than omitted, so the R3 addition is a flag flip and the design stays stable.

## Test plan
Unit: flag persistence mapping to schema columns and `pane_config`, group assignment/removal, same-symbol filter for drawings. Component: SCR-023 surface states (no group, group A, all axes on, partial axes — matching CMP-218's Storybook list), the mismatch notice, the disabled account row with its reason. Integration: with real engines and the SyncBus — crosshair across differing intervals, isolation between A and B, restart persistence via E15-S03. E2E: assign groups by hotkey, verify isolation, save/restore. A11y: axe on SCR-023; assertion that group identity appears as text in both the visible badge and the accessible name; contrast check that the group colours are decorative, not load-bearing; announcement fires once on membership change. Perf: toggling axes mid-sweep does not exceed the 4 ms sync budget.

## Security notes
Client-side preference state only, persisted through E15-T01's already-validated layout write path; no new endpoint and no new stored secret. The one boundary worth stating explicitly: sync must not become a channel for account or environment context to leak between panes, which is why the account/trade-group axis is disabled in R1 rather than half-wired — when it lands in R3 it must respect each pane's own RBAC scope rather than inheriting the origin pane's.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, with SC 1.4.1 (Use of Colour) squarely in scope: group membership is text (letter + name) in the badge and in each panel's accessible name, with colour as reinforcement only. Each sync axis is an independently labelled switch (CMP-218), not a combined control. Group changes are announced once, politely ("Chart 2 joined sync group A"); crosshair movement is never announced. The surface is keyboard-operable end to end and the hotkeys are remappable. The interval-mismatch notice is text associated with the control it explains.

## Performance notes
Propagation ≤1 frame (US-LAY-003 NFR), ≤4 ms across 6 panes with all axes on (SCR-023), zero React renders on the crosshair path — all inherited from E15-T03 and re-verified here with the real UI attached, since a badge that re-renders per crosshair move would defeat the whole design.

## Observability
`sync.group_created`, `sync.group_changed`, `sync.axis_toggled {axis, enabled}`, `sync.panel_joined_group`, `sync.panel_left_group`. Axis-toggle analytics tell us which axes traders actually use, which informs whether R2 adds more or removes some.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the sync configuration module.
- [ ] SCR-023 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior or waiver recorded; its sign-off checklist verified, including the colour+letter pairing and the conflicting-sync warning.
- [ ] axe-core green; colour-independence verified manually.
- [ ] Persistence across restart demonstrated in an E2E run.
- [ ] Sync budget re-measured with the UI attached and recorded.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E15-T03** (SyncBus), **E05** (Toggle, Tag/Chip, FormField, Dialog). Blocks **E15-S05**. Persisted by **E15-S03**.

## Branch

title: Spike S6: measure real GB/day per stream for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
body:
## Context
Every retention default, the hot-tier window and `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` currently rest on an unverified first-principles estimate of 0.5-0.75 GB/day/symbol compressed at 200 depth (budget #12 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, ADR-0015 "Validation", which names this spike **S6**). ADR-0015 states plainly that the estimate "may be off by 2-3x" and makes measurement a precondition for finalising retention defaults. If the constant is wrong, E16 either wastes the volume or prunes data the owner wanted kept - both are user-visible failures that cannot be undone.

This spike measures; it does not build product. Its deliverable is a number per stream, per symbol, per depth tier, good enough to set the constants `E16-T06` and `E16-T07` bake in as defaults.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Run the E08 ingestion path (modules M3-M6) writing to QuestDB through the E07 tier wiring for **BTCUSDT** and **ETHUSDT** for **7 consecutive days**, at `orderbook_depth` 50 and 200.
- Measure the on-disk delta per QuestDB table: `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `tickers`, `liquidations` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4).
- Measure the Parquet size of the same window after a manual roll-off, giving the hot->cold compression ratio.
- Publish `docs/plan/notes/e16-storage-measurement.md`: GB/day per (symbol, stream, depth), hot/cold ratio, peak-hour vs quiet-hour ratio, recommended `CV_DISK_CAP_GB`, `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS`, `CV_RECORDER_RETENTION_DAYS`.
- PR updating budget #12 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and the Validation section of `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0015-recording-policy.md` with the measured range.

## Out of scope
- Any production code in M10/M11 - the spike uses throwaway scripts under `scripts/spikes/e16-storage/`.
- Symbols beyond BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT and any non-USDT-perp instrument.
- Tuning QuestDB partitioning/compression - a finding of this spike, not a deliverable.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Measured figures replace the estimate
  Given 7 days of continuous capture for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
  When the measurement note is published
  Then it states GB/day per stream per symbol at depth 50 and depth 200 with the observation window and the gap minutes excluded
  And budget #12 in 06-performance-and-load-standard.md is updated with the measured range

Scenario: Capture was not continuous
  Given the capture run contains a gap longer than 10 minutes
  When GB/day is computed
  Then the gap duration is subtracted from the denominator and the note records the gap explicitly rather than reporting a diluted rate

Scenario: Measurement contradicts the estimate by more than 2x
  Given the measured depth-200 rate for BTCUSDT exceeds 1.5 GB/day
  Then the spike raises a follow-up against E16-T06 and E16-T07 to revise retention defaults before those tickets close
  And the Architect is tagged for a decision on the hot-tier window
```

## Technical notes / design
- Size sampling: `SELECT table_name, diskSize FROM tables()` in QuestDB, sampled hourly into CSV. Do **not** `du` the whole volume - WAL and other tenants pollute it.
- Exclude derived tables (`bars_*`, `footprint_cells`, `heatmap_cells`) from raw-stream figures; report them separately because they are recomputable from `trades`.
- Report **mean and p95 hourly** rates: the disk ladder in E16-T07 must be sized against liquidation-cascade bursts, not the mean.
- Config keys under study: `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (7), `CV_RECORDER_RETENTION_DAYS` (30), `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` (500) - `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §7.2.

## Test plan
Spike: no production tests. The scripts must be re-runnable - a reviewer runs `scripts/spikes/e16-storage/measure.py` over a 1-hour window and obtains numbers of the same order of magnitude.

## Security notes
Public market data only; classification **public**; no credentials (asset AC-07 in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §3 holds no keys). The spike must write to the recording volume, never the volume Postgres and the backend need to operate (SR-096).

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Must not degrade the shared dev environment: two symbols only; abort the run if write backlog exceeds 100k rows for more than 60 s.

## Observability
Emit `recorder_bytes_written_total{symbol,stream}` from the harness so the metric name is identical to the one E16-T03 ships in production.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] 7-day measurement completed with <1% gap minutes, or gaps documented.
- [ ] `docs/plan/notes/e16-storage-measurement.md` merged.
- [ ] Budget #12 and ADR-0015 Validation updated, Architect approved.
- [ ] Recommended values for the three config keys stated and linked from E16-T06/E16-T07.
- [ ] Scripts committed under `scripts/spikes/e16-storage/` with a README.

## Dependencies
`E07` provides QuestDB/Parquet tier wiring; `E08` provides the Bybit WS ingestion being recorded.

## Branch
`spike/e16-storage-measurement` - notes and scripts only.

## References

title: Automate the E2E suite for recorder lifecycle, retention and empty states
body:
## Context
The recorder's failures are quiet: a symbol that stops recording, a retention change that deletes more than the preview promised, an empty state that shows a blank chart instead of an explanation. These only surface end to end, across the WS topic, the REST surface and three screens. This ticket automates the cases the E16-Q01 plan marks as E2E-level, in Playwright against the web app and the Electron shell.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `e2e/recorder/`:
  1. `empty-install.spec.ts` - fresh install shows the empty recorder list and the honest empty state; nothing is recorded.
  2. `lifecycle.spec.ts` - add BTCUSDT, observe `starting -> recording` within 5 s via the WS-driven UI, verify first-recorded timestamp, pin, unpin with the warning, stop with the confirmation, verify data is retained.
  3. `auto-record.spec.ts` - with a shortened autostart delay, open a chart for an unrecorded symbol, assert the notice, stop from the notice; assert a symbol with an open position cannot be un-recorded.
  4. `retention.spec.ts` - reduce retention, read the dry-run preview, cancel and prove nothing changed via the manifest, then confirm and prove exactly the previewed data was removed; assert the pinned symbol is untouched.
  5. `empty-states.spec.ts` - never-recorded chart, window-before-recording-start (422 path), partial-history gap hatch and its text equivalent, non-owner explanatory variants.
  6. `storage-panel.spec.ts` - trigger compaction and follow the job to completion; run a fixture archive import and assert the summary contents.
- Role coverage: each spec runs as Owner, and the permission-sensitive assertions additionally as Manager and Viewer.
- Runs in CI against a seeded stack using the E16-Q01 fixture catalogue and the `CV_TEST_CLOCK` hook; total wall time under 12 minutes.
- Electron shell run for `lifecycle` and `empty-states` (per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` E2E requirement covering both web and Electron).

## Out of scope
- Unit and contract tests (owned by the implementing tickets).
- Performance, chaos and a11y automation (E16-Q04, E16-Q05).
- Exploratory testing (E16-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Suite is deterministic
  Given the suite runs 10 consecutive times in CI
  Then it passes 10 times with no retries and no fixed sleeps longer than 1 second

Scenario: Retention preview matches reality byte for byte
  When the retention spec applies a reduction after previewing it
  Then the post-state manifest differs from the pre-state manifest by exactly the previewed symbols, ranges and byte counts

Scenario: Pinned data survives every destructive case
  When every destructive spec has run
  Then the pinned symbol fixture is byte-identical to its pre-suite manifest

Scenario: Role assertions hold
  Given the suite runs as Viewer
  Then every write control is absent from the DOM, not merely disabled, and direct API calls from the page are refused

Scenario: Failure output is diagnosable
  Given a spec fails
  Then the artifact bundle contains the trace, the WS frame log, the relevant audit entries and the pre/post manifests
```

## Technical notes / design
- The suite drives the real backend - no mocked recorder - because the behaviours under test are integration behaviours. Seeding uses the fixture catalogue, applied by a `scripts/qa/seed-e16.py` helper that is idempotent.
- Waiting is always on an observable condition (a state badge, a WS frame, a job status), never a sleep; the 5-second start requirement is asserted as a bounded wait, which also makes it a regression test for the US-REC-001 NFR.
- Manifests are produced by a QA-only endpoint or a direct scratch-volume scan documented in E16-Q01; they never touch production data.

## Test plan
Self-verifying. Additionally: a deliberate mutation test - break the pin predicate in a branch build and assert the retention spec fails - proving the suite would catch the worst regression in the epic.

## Security notes
The suite exercises the abuse cases as negative tests: purge without elevation must 403, purge with a mismatched echo must 422, and a Viewer's direct API call must be refused and audited. Test credentials are environment-scoped and never real; the scratch volume is wiped between runs.

## Accessibility notes
The empty-states spec asserts the text equivalent of the gap hatch exists and is keyboard reachable - the a11y-behaviour assertions that belong in E2E; the full audit is E16-Q05.

## Performance notes
Suite wall time under 12 minutes; it must not be the long pole of the pipeline. Parallelised by spec file with isolated seeded datasets.

## Observability
CI publishes pass/fail per user story id so the traceability matrix can be regenerated from test results.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six specs green in CI, 10 consecutive runs without flake.
- [ ] Mutation check performed and recorded.
- [ ] Role matrix covered.
- [ ] Electron run green for the two named specs.
- [ ] Linked from `docs/qa/test-plans/e16-recorder.md`.
- [ ] QA lead approval.

`E16-Q01` defines the cases and fixtures; `E16-S01`, `E16-S03`, `E16-S04`, `E16-S05` supply the UI under test.

title: Run the exploratory charter for recorder surprise, honesty and data-loss traps
body:
## Context
Scripted tests verify what we thought of. The recorder's real risks are the things we did not: a user who browses 40 symbols in five minutes and finds 40 recordings running; a retention change applied while a replay is reading; a pin toggled twice quickly; a purge started, cancelled and restarted. ADR-0015 names user surprise as a live consequence of the auto-record design, so an exploratory pass against surprise and honesty is proportionate.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Three timeboxed session-based charters (90 minutes each), documented in `docs/qa/exploratory/e16-*.md` using a session sheet (charter, areas, notes, bugs, risks, time split):
  1. **Surprise charter** - can the system record something the user did not intend or does not know about? Rapid symbol browsing, multi-window charts, watchlist hover, layouts restoring many charts at once, a rule or alert referencing a symbol.
  2. **Honesty charter** - can the UI ever show data that is not there, or hide data that is? Gap boundaries, partial history at the edge of a window, timezone boundaries, imported archive ranges presented as full history, stale figures presented as live, coverage after a purge.
  3. **Data-loss charter** - can a user destroy data without understanding they were about to? Double-clicks on destructive controls, browser back during a purge, concurrent retention edits from two sessions, unpin followed immediately by a nightly sweep, cancelled compaction.
- Every finding filed as a Bug with severity, reproduction, and a link to the charter session.
- A one-page summary of residual risk for the epic QA sign-off, including anything explicitly accepted.

## Out of scope
- Scripted regression (E16-Q02) and performance/chaos (E16-Q04).
- Fixing the bugs found - they are triaged into the epic or the backlog.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All three charters executed and documented
  When the exploratory work completes
  Then three session sheets exist with time split between setup, test design and bug investigation, and each lists the areas actually covered

Scenario: Every finding is reproducible
  Given a bug is filed from a session
  Then it carries exact steps, environment, expected versus actual, and severity, and a second tester reproduces it

Scenario: Residual risk is stated, not implied
  When the summary is written
  Then it names what was not covered and why, and lists any accepted risks with the owner who accepted them

Scenario: A critical honesty defect blocks sign-off
  Given a charter finds a case where absent data renders as present data
  Then it is filed as P0 and the epic cannot reach QA sign-off until it is fixed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Sessions run against a build with the E16-Q01 fixture dataset on a scratch volume, with the test clock available so time-dependent traps (nightly sweep during an edit) can actually be reached.
- Pair one session with a developer (pair-exploration) for the data-loss charter, because the traps there depend on internal ordering the tester cannot see.

## Test plan
N/A - this ticket is testing. Its output feeds E16-Q06 regression selection.

## Security notes
Any finding that lets a lower-privileged role cause recording or deletion is routed immediately to E16-X02 rather than the normal triage queue.

## Accessibility notes
Keyboard-only operation is an explicit area in each charter; findings feed E16-Q05 rather than being fixed ad hoc.

## Performance notes
Observed sluggishness is noted as a finding with a reproduction, and handed to E16-Q04 for measurement rather than being asserted here.

## Observability
Testers check the audit log after each destructive action; a missing or wrong audit entry is itself a finding.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Three session sheets merged.
- [ ] All findings filed and triaged with severity.
- [ ] Residual-risk summary written and reviewed by the QA lead and the epic owner.
- [ ] Any P0/P1 finding linked to a fix ticket before epic sign-off.

## Dependencies
Requires all five E16 UI stories built.

## Branch
`docs/e16-exploratory` - notes only.

title: Build the recorder perf, soak and disk-pressure chaos scripts
body:
## Context
Two of this epic's headline claims are numeric and one is behavioural: the recorder sustains live ingest without dropping messages, storage grows at the measured rate, and the disk-pressure ladder degrades exactly as ADR-0015 decision 6 specifies. ADR-0015's own Validation section names the disk-pressure chaos test (fill to 85%, 91%, 96% and assert each documented behaviour including pinned survival), and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-154 requires chaos coverage of DB unavailability and disk-full with the system failing closed on the order path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Soak script** (`perf/recorder/soak.py`): 24-hour continuous recording of 2 symbols at depth 200 against a replayed or live feed, asserting zero dropped messages, backlog p95 of 0, spill bytes 0, and GB/day within 20% of the E16-K01 measurement.
- **Ingest load script** (`perf/recorder/ingest_load.py`): synthetic 50k msg/s for 10 minutes, asserting p95 flush < 50 ms and memory ceiling 512 MiB.
- **API/WS load** (k6, `perf/recorder/api_load.js`): 5 concurrent `recorder` WS subscribers plus 1 Hz `/recording/status` polling plus coverage queries, asserting API p95 < 150 ms and frame size < 8 KiB for 20 symbols.
- **Disk-pressure chaos** (`chaos/recorder/disk_pressure.py`): a loopback volume filled to 76%, 81%, 91% and 96%, asserting at each step: warning event with suggested actions; auto-record refusal while explicit-list symbols keep recording; accelerated reaper below 15% free; ingestion pause for non-pinned auto symbols below 5% free; **pinned data byte-identical throughout**; and **order placement still succeeds at every level**.
- **DB-unavailability chaos** (`chaos/recorder/questdb_down.py`): stop QuestDB for 2 minutes and assert WAL spill then clean replay with no duplicates and no gap; then exhaust the WAL and assert an explicit `backpressure_drop` gap plus a critical event.
- **Roll-off interruption chaos**: kill the roll-off job between write and verify, and between verify and drop; assert no data loss and convergence on re-run.
- Results published to the CI perf trend so regressions in later epics are visible, with thresholds failing the build.

## Out of scope
- Functional E2E (E16-Q02) and a11y (E16-Q05).
- Chart-engine FPS benchmarks (E11).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Soak proves no silent loss
  Given a 24 hour soak at depth 200 on two symbols
  Then dropped messages are zero, spill bytes are zero, recorded rows reconcile with produced events, and measured GB/day is within 20 percent of the E16-K01 figure

Scenario: Disk ladder behaves exactly as specified at every level
  When the volume is filled to 76, 81, 91 and 96 percent in turn
  Then each documented behaviour occurs at its threshold, pinned data is byte-identical at the end, and an order placed at 96 percent still succeeds

Scenario: Database outage costs latency not history
  Given QuestDB is stopped for 2 minutes under live load
  Then events spill to the WAL and replay cleanly with no duplicates and no recorded gap
  And when the WAL is exhausted, a backpressure_drop gap covering exactly the dropped window is written and a critical event fires

Scenario: Interrupted roll-off never loses data
  Given the roll-off job is killed between write and verify
  Then the hot partition still exists, the partial Parquet file is quarantined, and a re-run completes correctly

Scenario: Thresholds gate the build
  Given a change regresses p95 flush beyond 50 milliseconds
  Then the perf job fails rather than merely recording a slower number
```

## Technical notes / design
- The loopback volume is created per run with `fallocate` + a filesystem image so fills are fast, repeatable and cannot touch the host's real disk; the harness refuses to run if the target path is not a loopback mount.
- Synthetic load reuses the E08 normaliser to generate realistic message mixes (trade bursts, depth churn, liquidation cascades) rather than uniform traffic, because the p95 that matters is the cascade.
- Reconciliation oracle: produced-event counter in the generator versus rows in QuestDB plus rows accounted for by gap records - the three must sum exactly.
- Runs nightly, not per PR, except the 10-minute ingest load which is cheap enough for the pipeline.

## Test plan
Self-verifying, with a deliberate negative control: run the disk-pressure suite against a build with the pin predicate removed and confirm the suite fails, proving the assertions have teeth.

## Security notes
Directly validates SR-096 (storage guard, recording volume separate, trading functional when the recording volume is full) and SR-154 (chaos coverage). Results are evidence for the E16-X02 security review and for the pre-Live pen-test scope.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI.

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: 50k msg/s ingest, p95 flush < 50 ms, 512 MiB queue ceiling, API p95 < 150 ms, WS frame < 8 KiB/20 symbols, storage growth within 20% of measurement (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #12 and the API/WS budgets).

## Observability
The harness scrapes the recorder metrics and attaches the Grafana snapshot to each run, so a failure comes with the panel that explains it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five scripts merged and runnable locally with one command each.
- [ ] Nightly CI job green; thresholds enforced.
- [ ] Negative control performed and recorded.
- [ ] Results for the first full run recorded on this ticket and referenced from the epic.
- [ ] DevSecOps and QA lead approval.

## Dependencies
`E16-T07` (ladder) and `E16-T05` (roll-off) must be implemented; `E16-Q01` defines the fixtures and oracles.

`test/e16-perf-chaos`.

title: Run the accessibility audit for the recorder screens and empty-state pattern
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI **and** manual screen-reader passes; automated checks catch roughly a third of what matters here. E16's specific risks are unusual: a table that updates once per second can flood a screen reader, a hatched gap region is invisible to one, and a disk meter conveyed by colour alone would hide the single most important number on the screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Manual audit of SCR-140, SCR-141, SCR-142, SCR-047 and the SCR-151 pattern instances shipped by E16-S05, against WCAG 2.2 AA.
- Screen-reader passes with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS, covering: the recorder table and its 1 Hz updates, the disk meter's numeric text, the retention form and its confirmation dialog, the storage panel's tier tables and progress bars, the empty states, and the gap-interval text equivalent.
- Keyboard-only pass: every control reachable and operable, visible focus throughout, focus trapped and returned by dialogs, no keyboard trap in the symbol picker.
- Contrast verification for state badges, the hatch pattern against the plot background (>=3:1 for non-text), meter fills, and disabled states.
- Zoom/reflow at 200% and 400% per WCAG 1.4.10, and `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for any progress animation.
- Findings filed with severity and the specific success criterion; a written audit report at `docs/qa/a11y/e16-recorder-audit.md` with a pass/fail per screen and per criterion.
- axe-core CI assertions added for all five surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Fixing findings - they are filed against the owning story or as new tickets.
- The design-level a11y review, which happened pre-build in E16-D06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live updates do not flood assistive technology
  Given a screen reader is active on the recorder table with 20 symbols updating at 1 Hz
  Then routine value changes are not announced, and only material changes such as a symbol entering error or the disk crossing a threshold are announced politely

Scenario: The gap is perceivable without sight
  Given a chart shows a hatched recording gap
  When a screen-reader user navigates the chart region
  Then a text equivalent lists the gap start, end and cause, reachable by keyboard

Scenario: No information is conveyed by colour alone
  When every state badge, meter and health indicator is inspected
  Then each carries text or an accessible name in addition to colour, and contrast meets AA

Scenario: Destructive dialogs are safe from the keyboard
  When the retention confirmation dialog opens
  Then focus moves into it, is trapped, Escape cancels without applying, and focus returns to the trigger

Scenario: Reflow holds at 400 percent
  When each screen is zoomed to 400 percent at 1280 pixels wide
  Then no horizontal scrolling of content is required and no content is lost or overlapped

Scenario: Audit is auditable
  When the report is published
  Then it records tool versions, assistive-technology versions, the criteria checked and a pass or fail per screen with evidence
```

## Technical notes / design
- axe-core runs against each screen in its populated, empty, warning and error states - an empty state is where a11y regressions hide, since it is rarely screenshotted.
- The 1 Hz announcement rule is verified by recording the screen-reader speech stream for 60 seconds and counting utterances; more than a handful is a fail.
- Contrast measured with a sampling tool on rendered pixels, not on token values, because the hatch is a composited pattern.

## Test plan
This ticket is the audit. Its own quality gate is a second reviewer spot-checking three findings and the contrast measurements.

## Security notes
N/A - no security surface. Findings must not include screenshots containing real account identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
The audit's scope is exactly the standard in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard, screen reader, contrast, focus, reflow, reduced motion.

## Performance notes
Verify that the `aria-live` strategy does not add measurable render cost at 1 Hz with 20 rows.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report merged at `docs/qa/a11y/e16-recorder-audit.md` with pass/fail per screen.
- [ ] axe-core assertions added to CI for all five surfaces, green.
- [ ] Both screen readers exercised and versions recorded.
- [ ] All findings filed with the specific WCAG criterion and severity.
- [ ] No open P0/P1 a11y findings at epic sign-off.
- [ ] Accessibility specialist approval.

title: Assemble the recorder regression pack and record epic QA sign-off
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12 rule 4 states that no view depending on recorded history ships before E16 has been recording for at least two sprints on the symbols that view will demo. That makes E16 a foundation the whole R2 train stands on, and it makes a durable regression pack - not a one-time pass - the real deliverable of QA here. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 additionally requires an epic-level regression and exploratory pass recorded on the epic, separate from child-ticket QA.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A named regression pack `e16-recorder-regression` selecting from E16-Q02's E2E specs and E16-Q04's perf/chaos scripts the subset that must run whenever a later epic touches recorded data: empty-install, lifecycle, retention preview-versus-reality, pinned-survival, gap honesty, and the disk ladder at 91%.
- Wiring: the pack runs nightly and is a required check on any PR labelled `area/recorder-replay` or `area/order-flow`.
- A traceability report generated from test results mapping US-REC-001..008 to passing cases, published as a CI artifact and reconciled against `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`.
- Epic QA sign-off record on E16: results of E16-Q02..Q05, open defect list with severities, residual risks accepted with the accepting owner, and an explicit statement of whether the exit criteria from E16-Q01 are met.
- A "recording depth" check the R2 epics can call: given a symbol and a date, does sufficient recorded history exist to demo a footprint or a profile - so E18/E19/E23/E26 planning is based on data, not hope.

## Out of scope
- Writing new test cases - this pack is assembled from existing automation.
- Sign-off for other epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The pack is a required check where it matters
  Given a pull request labelled area/order-flow
  Then the e16-recorder-regression pack runs and must pass before merge

Scenario: Traceability is generated, not hand-maintained
  When the pack completes
  Then a report maps every US-REC story to the cases that covered it, and any story with no passing case fails the report

Scenario: Sign-off is evidence-based
  When QA sign-off is recorded on the epic
  Then it links the E2E run, the perf and chaos results, the a11y report and the exploratory summary, and lists every open defect with a severity and a disposition

Scenario: Open P0 or P1 blocks sign-off
  Given a P1 defect against E16 scope is open
  Then sign-off cannot be recorded and the epic cannot move to Done

Scenario: Recording depth is queryable by later epics
  Given E18 planning asks whether BTCUSDT has 14 days of footprint-capable history
  Then the depth check answers from coverage data with the exact first-recorded timestamp and any gaps in the window
```

## Technical notes / design
- The pack is a CI job definition plus a tag selector, not copied test code - duplication would rot.
- The traceability report is produced by tagging each test with its US id and aggregating from the JUnit XML.
- The recording-depth check is a small CLI over `GET /market/data-coverage`, committed at `scripts/qa/recording-depth.py`, so roadmap conversations use the same source of truth the product does.

## Test plan
Verification is a dry run: intentionally disable one E2E spec and confirm the traceability report flags the now-uncovered story.

## Security notes
Sign-off must confirm that the E16-X01 abuse cases and the E16-X02 review findings are closed or explicitly accepted; an accepted security risk requires the Owner's name in the record.

## Accessibility notes
Sign-off requires zero open P0/P1 findings from E16-Q05.

## Performance notes
Sign-off requires the E16-Q04 budgets met, with the measured GB/day recorded on the epic so R2 capacity planning uses the real number.

## Observability
The sign-off record names the dashboards and alerts (E16-T09) that must be live before the epic is Done, since an unobserved recorder is an unfinished one.

- [ ] Regression pack defined, wired nightly and as a required check on the two labels.
- [ ] Traceability report generated and reconciled with `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`.
- [ ] Dry-run verification of the report performed.
- [ ] Epic QA sign-off comment posted on E16 with all evidence linked.
- [ ] Recording-depth CLI committed and referenced from the R2 epics.
- [ ] QA lead approval.

`E16-Q02` (E2E), `E16-Q03` (exploratory), `E16-Q04` (perf/chaos), `E16-Q05` (a11y) supply the evidence.

title: Build SCR-140 recorder & storage screen with the recorded-symbol list
body:
## Context
Implements **US-REC-001** (recorded-symbols list), **US-REC-005** (disk budget display) and **US-REC-008** (recorder health and control) as screen **SCR-140** at route `/admin/recorder` (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`). This is the screen that makes the owner decision visible: nothing is recorded by default, and the cost of every symbol you add is stated on the same row as the switch that added it.

SCR-140 is also reached from onboarding step 4 (`docs/plan/13-user-flows.md`) and from the owner CTA on SCR-047, so it is the destination for every "you have no history because you never recorded this" moment in the product.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/admin/recorder` inside the web app, RBAC-gated (`recording:read` to view, `recording:write` for controls) using CMP-087 AdminLayout - **no separate admin app**.
- Header summary: symbols recording, total disk used, default retention, and the explicit statement that nothing is recorded by default when the list is empty.
- Symbol table (CMP-049 Table of CMP-177 RecorderStatusRow): symbol, since (first recorded timestamp), depth, measured GB/day, size, pin toggle, retention, state badge (recording / starting / degraded / paused / stopped / error) and, for auto-recorded rows, an explicit **auto-recorded** badge naming the trigger (chart open / position open).
- Controls: `+ Record a symbol` (CMP-055 FilterBar-driven symbol picker), start/stop, pin (keep forever), depth tier change, per-symbol retention, and the buttons `Retention policy` (opens SCR-141), `Compact now`, `Purge expired`.
- Disk meter (CMP-023 ProgressBar) with numeric text: used / cap, and the projection ("projection 60 d: 118 GB") plus days of runway.
- States: running · starting · degraded (gap count with timestamps) · paused · disk warning at 80% ("Disk 80% full - recording stops at 95% to protect the database") · disk critical (recording stopped banner) · purge in progress · **empty** (no symbols recorded yet, CMP-026 EmptyState).
- Live updates from the WS `recorder` topic at 1 Hz, falling back to `GET /recording/status` polling if the socket is down.
- Validation rules from the screen spec: stopping warns that history stops accumulating while existing data is retained per policy; a symbol with an open position cannot be un-recorded ("SOLUSDT has an open position and is auto-recorded.").
- Analytics/audit triggers: `recorder.started|stopped|pinned|retention_changed|purged`.

## Out of scope
- The retention policy editor modal itself (E16-S03 / SCR-141) and the storage panel (E16-S04 / SCR-142) - this screen only links to them.
- Bulk import UI (E16-S04).
- Chart-side empty states (E16-S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fresh install shows an honest empty state
  Given no symbols have ever been recorded
  When the owner opens /admin/recorder
  Then the empty state states that nothing is recorded by default, explains that history begins when recording begins, and offers a single primary action to record a symbol

Scenario: Adding a symbol reflects within 5 seconds
  When the owner adds BTCUSDT
  Then a row appears in state starting, transitions to recording within 5 seconds via the WS recorder topic, and shows its first-recorded timestamp

Scenario: Auto-recorded rows are labelled, not hidden
  Given SOLUSDT was auto-recorded because a chart is open
  Then its row carries an auto-recorded badge naming the trigger and a one-click stop control

Scenario: A symbol with an open position cannot be un-recorded
  Given SOLUSDT has an open position
  When the owner attempts to stop recording it
  Then the action is refused with the message that the symbol has an open position and is auto-recorded

Scenario: Stopping explains the consequence before it happens
  When the owner stops recording ETHUSDT
  Then a confirmation states that history stops accumulating while existing data is retained per the retention policy, and only then is the stop sent

Scenario: Disk warning is visible and specific
  Given usage is at 82 percent of the configured cap
  Then a warning banner states that recording stops at 95 percent to protect the database, and the meter shows the numeric used-of-cap figure and the projected full date

Scenario: Viewer sees status but no controls
  Given a Viewer session
  Then the table and disk meter render read-only and every control is absent, with a sentence explaining that recording is managed by the owner

Scenario: Socket loss degrades gracefully
  Given the WS connection drops
  Then the page falls back to polling, shows a last-updated timestamp, and never displays stale figures as live
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data: `GET /recording/status`, `GET /recording/symbols`, `GET /recording/storage`, `POST /recording/symbols`, `PATCH|DELETE /recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}`, `POST /recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}/pin`, `POST /admin/recorder/compact`, `POST /admin/recorder/purge`; live via WS topic `recorder`.
- Use the generated client from `packages/api-client` (E16-T08); no hand-written fetchers.
- The 1 Hz WS frame replaces the row model wholesale per symbol; row identity is `recordedSymbolId` so React reconciliation never re-mounts a row on a state change.
- Mutations are optimistic only for pin (cheap, reversible); start/stop/purge are pessimistic with a pending state, because pretending recording started when it did not is exactly the silent-failure class this epic exists to prevent.
- Purge from this screen routes through the confirmation flow specified for SCR-141/CMP-044 ConfirmDialog with the typed symbol echo.

## Test plan
- Unit (Vitest + RTL): row rendering per state, badge logic, refusal when a position is open, Viewer read-only rendering, fallback-to-polling behaviour.
- Storybook: CMP-177 states Recording, Stopped, Pinned, NearDiskBudget plus the screen's empty, warning and critical states; visual regression on each.
- Contract: MSW handlers generated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; a response shape drift fails the suite.
- E2E (Playwright, added to the suite in E16-Q02): add symbol -> observe recording -> pin -> stop with confirmation -> empty state after removal.
- a11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass over the table and meter.
- Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
This is an RBAC-gated admin surface inside the web app. Controls must be rendered from the session's permissions, never merely disabled client-side; the server enforces `recording:write` regardless (E16-T08). Purge additionally requires step-up - the UI must request elevation rather than assuming the session has it, and must never cache the elevated state. Do not render absolute host paths from `StorageUsage` to any role. Classification **internal**.

## Accessibility notes
Per SCR-140 and `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: the disk meter carries numeric text (never colour alone); gaps are a real table with start/end/duration columns; state badges are text plus icon; the table is keyboard navigable with a visible focus ring; destructive controls are reachable by keyboard and their confirmation dialog traps focus and returns it on close; live 1 Hz updates use `aria-live="off"` on the table with a polite summary region announcing only material changes (a symbol entering error or the disk crossing a threshold), so a screen reader is not flooded once per second.

## Performance notes
Status updates at 1 Hz and the page never blocks ingestion (SCR-140 spec). Re-render budget: under 4 ms per frame for 20 rows; the meter and table are memoised on the symbol payload.

## Observability
Analytics `recorder.screen_viewed`; audit events are emitted server-side but the UI must surface their outcome (success/failure toast naming the symbol).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated.
- [ ] Storybook entries for every listed state; visual regression baselined.
- [ ] axe-core green; one manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] Design sign-off from E16-D02 checklist (all eight items) recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%.
- [ ] QA sign-off from E16-Q01.
- [ ] 2 approvals including frontend code-owner.

## Dependencies
`E16-T08` (REST + WS contract and generated client), `E16-D06` (signed-off design and handoff), `E10` (app shell and routing), `E09` (auth, RBAC, step-up elevation).

## Branch
`feat/e16-recorder-screen` - split table and controls into 2 PRs to stay under 400 LOC.

title: Build SCR-141 retention policy editor with destructive-change preview
body:
## Context
Implements **US-REC-003** (retention policy and pinning) as **SCR-141**, the modal that decides how long data lives. Its whole design problem is that shortening a number here destroys irreplaceable data, so the screen spec requires the consequence to be restated in text with the exact amount that becomes eligible for deletion, plus a typed confirmation for destructive reductions.

The dry-run preview the backend provides (E16-T06) is what makes this honest: the user sees exactly what would be deleted, by symbol, range and size, before anything is removed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Modal at SCR-141 using CMP-087 AdminLayout context, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- Fields: global default retention days; per-tier rules for raw ticks, L2 deltas, bars and footprint aggregates; cold-tier migration age (QuestDB -> Parquet); per-symbol override table; pin-forever control per symbol.
- Live steady-state disk estimate under the chosen policy, recomputed as the user edits.
- Client validation mirroring the server: retention >= 1 day; raw-tick retention <= bar retention with the exact message "Bars can't be deleted before the ticks they came from are kept - adjust the tiers."
- **Preview before apply**: on submit, call the dry-run and render "this will delete N GB covering dates X-Y" per symbol and stream, listing protected items with their reason (pinned / leased / inside hot window). Nothing is applied until the user confirms.
- Typed confirmation for any reduction; `apply_now` checkbox that states changes otherwise take effect at the next nightly sweep.
- Compaction job state (queued / running / complete) shown after apply, since retention changes schedule background work rather than deleting synchronously.
- Unpin warning: unpinning states the exact volume that becomes eligible for deletion at the next pass (un-pinning never deletes retroactively).

## Out of scope
- Executing retention (E16-T06) and the purge flow (part of SCR-140, E16-S01).
- Postgres-side retention for OMS/journal tables.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduction shows the real cost before applying
  Given trades retention is 30 days
  When the owner reduces it to 7 and submits
  Then a preview lists, per symbol and stream, the exact GB and date range that would be deleted, and nothing is applied yet

Scenario: Typed confirmation gates destruction
  Given the preview shows data would be deleted
  When the owner confirms without typing the required confirmation text
  Then apply stays disabled and no request is sent

Scenario: Inverted tier retention is refused with a specific message
  When raw-tick retention is set above bar retention
  Then the form shows the message that bars cannot be deleted before the ticks they came from, and submit is disabled

Scenario: Pinned symbols are shown as protected
  Given BTCUSDT is pinned
  When any reduction is previewed
  Then BTCUSDT appears in the protected list with reason pinned and zero bytes deleted

Scenario: Unpinning warns with the exact volume
  When the owner unpins BTCUSDT
  Then the dialog states how many GB covering which dates become eligible for deletion at the next retention pass, and that nothing is deleted right now

Scenario: Apply schedules rather than blocks
  Given the owner applies a policy without apply_now
  Then a message states the change takes effect at the next nightly sweep, and the modal shows the queued job state

Scenario: Viewer cannot open the editor
  Given a Viewer session
  Then the retention policy entry point is not rendered and direct navigation is refused
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data: `GET|PUT /api/v1/recording/retention-policies` (with `?apply_now=`), the dry-run preview endpoint behind `PUT` validation, and `GET /recording/storage` for the steady-state estimate.
- The steady-state estimate is computed client-side from measured `daily_growth_bytes` per symbol times the chosen retention per stream - it is labelled an estimate, while the preview figures (server-side, measured) are labelled exact.
- The whole policy set is replaced atomically by the PUT; the form therefore submits the complete set, and a concurrent change by another session is detected by an ETag/If-Match round trip and surfaced as a conflict rather than silently overwriting.
- Error mapping: `retention_invalid_policy` -> field-level errors; `403` -> permission message; conflict -> reload-and-rebase prompt.

## Test plan
- Unit: validation matrix (all inversions, boundary 1 and 3650), estimate maths, confirmation gating, conflict handling.
- Storybook: default, with overrides, preview-with-deletions, preview-all-protected, conflict, and error states.
- Contract: MSW from the OpenAPI spec, including the 422 shape.
- E2E (E16-Q02): reduce retention, read the preview, cancel and assert nothing changed; then confirm and assert the policy persisted.
- a11y: axe-core; focus trap and return; every duration field states its unit.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This form authorises data destruction. Client controls are convenience only - the server validates and audits (`retention.change`, `retention.default_changed`, `retention.symbol_override_set`, `retention.pin_changed`). The UI must request step-up elevation where the backend requires it and must never retry a destructive PUT automatically on a network error (a silent retry could apply a policy the user cancelled). **Carries the `security` label; Security engineer reviews the confirmation and elevation flow.**

## Accessibility notes
Per SCR-141: a form with a global default and a per-symbol override table; every duration field states its unit in an associated label, not a placeholder; the consequence of shortening retention is restated as text with the amount of data affected; the confirm dialog traps focus, is dismissible by Escape, and returns focus to the trigger; errors are associated with fields via `aria-describedby` and summarised at the top of the form for screen-reader users.

## Performance notes
Preview requests are debounced at 400 ms and cancelled on further edits; the modal must open in under 150 ms using cached policy data.

## Observability
Analytics `retention.editor_opened`, `retention.preview_requested`, `retention.change_cancelled_after_preview` (a high value here means the defaults are wrong). Audit events are server-side.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated.
- [ ] Storybook covers every listed state.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass on the form and dialog.
- [ ] E16-D03 sign-off checklist (all six items) recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] Security review of the destructive-confirmation flow signed off.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%.
- [ ] 2 approvals including frontend code-owner.

## Dependencies
`E16-T06` supplies policy resolution and the dry-run preview; `E16-S01` provides the entry point and shared admin scaffolding; `E16-D06` supplies the signed-off design.

title: Build SCR-142 storage panel with tier health, projections and import progress
body:
## Context
Implements **US-REC-004** (hot/cold tier management visibility), the projection half of **US-REC-005**, and **US-REC-007** (bulk backfill progress and summary) as **SCR-142**. The screen's job is to answer "where is my data, how fast is it growing, and what stops working first when the disk fills" - and the spec is explicit that recording pauses before trading is affected, and that this must be stated on screen, not merely implemented.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Page section at SCR-142 using CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-023 ProgressBar, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-049 Table.
- Three tier tables - QuestDB hot, Parquet/DuckDB cold, Postgres - each with size, row counts by table, oldest/newest timestamps, health as text, and units on every figure.
- Growth and projection: daily growth per tier and per symbol (sparkline over the sampled series), projected full date, days of runway.
- Per-symbol breakdown for the hot tier.
- Operational state: ingestion lag, slowest queries, last vacuum/compaction, migration version and pending migrations (banner with the version delta when pending).
- Maintenance actions with progress and cancel: compact (`POST /admin/recorder/compact`), vacuum, tier migration - each an explicit action, each audited.
- Bulk archive import (US-REC-007): start an import for a symbol and date range, live progress, and the completion summary (files processed, rows written, overlap discarded, files skipped with reasons).
- States: healthy · migration pending · lag warning · read-only mode (disk full) · tier unreachable (error state per tier, not a whole-page failure).
- Low-disk warning and critical states drawn with the explicit statement of what stops working first: recording pauses before trading is affected.

## Out of scope
- The recorder symbol list (E16-S01) and retention editor (E16-S03).
- Backup/restore UI (platform/ops epic).
- Implementing compaction/import themselves (E16-T05, E16-T10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All three tiers are shown with units
  When the owner opens the storage panel
  Then QuestDB, Parquet/DuckDB and Postgres each show size, row counts, oldest and newest timestamps and a textual health state, every figure carrying its unit

Scenario: Projection is visible and sourced from measurement
  Then daily growth and the projected full date are shown per tier and per symbol, sourced from the sampled series rather than computed on request

Scenario: Disk pressure states what stops first
  Given usage is in the critical band
  Then the panel states that recording has paused and that trading is unaffected, naming the threshold that was crossed

Scenario: A tier being unreachable does not break the page
  Given the Parquet tier is unreachable
  Then that tier's card shows an error state with a retry, while the QuestDB and Postgres cards continue to render live figures

Scenario: Maintenance actions show progress and can be cancelled
  When the owner triggers compaction
  Then a job appears with queued, running and complete states and a cancel control, and the outcome is reported

Scenario: Import reports its summary honestly
  Given an import overlapping recorded data completes
  Then the summary states files processed, rows written, rows discarded as overlap and files skipped with their reasons
  And the imported range is labelled archive-derived with no book data

Scenario: Figures never silently go stale
  Given the 60 second sample has not refreshed for 5 minutes
  Then the panel shows a last-updated timestamp and a stale indicator rather than presenting old numbers as current
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data: `GET /api/v1/recording/storage` (server-sampled every 60 s per the screen spec), `POST /admin/recorder/compact`, the import job endpoints and `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}` for progress.
- Polling at 60 s aligned to the server sample, with a manual refresh; no WS topic is required for this screen.
- Sparklines use CMP-024 over the persisted usage series; when fewer than 24 samples exist, render the "collecting data" variant rather than a misleading flat line.
- Long-running actions are jobs, not requests: the UI never blocks on compaction or import, and a page reload resumes progress from the job id.

## Test plan
- Unit: tier card rendering including the per-tier error state, stale detection, projection formatting, job progress state machine.
- Storybook: healthy, migration pending, lag warning, read-only/disk-full, tier unreachable, import running, import summary with skipped files.
- Contract: MSW from the OpenAPI `StorageUsage` schema.
- E2E (E16-Q02): trigger compaction and observe the job to completion; start a fixture import and read the summary.

title: Implement recorder-dependent empty and partial-history states (SCR-047, SCR-151)
body:
## Context
Implements the UI half of **US-REC-006** and the empty-state half of **US-REC-005**. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §intro rule 3 makes this a product-wide contract: recorder-dependent emptiness is a *designed state*, never a blank canvas - every dependent surface shows "History starts <ts> - recording began then", with a CTA to SCR-140 for owners and an explanatory message otherwise.

This story ships **SCR-047** (chart empty / no-data) and the reusable **SCR-151** empty-state pattern with its `recording-not-started` variant, which E18 footprint, E19 profiles, E23 CVD and E26 replay all consume in R2. Building it once, correctly, here is what stops four later epics each inventing their own blank screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `CMP-026 EmptyState` gains the documented variants: `nothing-created-yet`, `no-match-for-filter`, `recording-not-started` - the third carrying the recording-start timestamp and a role-aware action.
- **SCR-047** chart empty/no-data state covering all four cases from the spec: symbol never recorded (offers live-only view and explains history starts when recording starts), interval too fine for available data, request window entirely before recording start, exchange returned no bars.
- Role-aware action: owner gets a real `Record this symbol` button wired to `POST /recording/symbols`; Manager/Viewer get an explanatory sentence, not a disabled button.
- **Partial history** treatment: when a requested range intersects `recording_gaps`, the covered part renders and the gap renders as a hatched, labelled region with its start, end and cause - never interpolated, never silently smoothed (ADR-0015 decision 7).
- Consumption of `GET /market/data-coverage` and of the `no_data_recorded` (422) error carrying `recording_started_at`, so the state is driven by data rather than by an empty array.
- Analytics `chart.empty_state_shown {reason}` and `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}`.
- Storybook documentation of the pattern so R2 epics adopt it without re-deriving it.

## Out of scope
- Footprint/profile/CVD/replay-specific gap rendering inside their own canvases (E18, E19, E23, E26) - they consume this pattern and component but own their draw calls.
- The recorder admin screens (E16-S01, S03, S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Never-recorded symbol explains rather than shows nothing
  Given SOLUSDT has never been recorded
  When a chart is opened for it
  Then the empty state states that there is no recorded history, notes that live data is streaming now, and shows a Record this symbol action for the owner

Scenario: Window before recording start is explained with the timestamp
  Given recording for BTCUSDT started 2026-09-01 08:00 UTC and a window before that is requested
  When the API returns 422 no_data_recorded
  Then the state states that no recorded history exists before that exact timestamp, rendered as text

Scenario: Non-owner gets an explanation, not a dead button
  Given a Viewer session on an unrecorded symbol
  Then no action button is rendered and a sentence explains that recording is managed by the owner

Scenario: A gap is drawn as a gap
  Given the requested range contains a 12 minute recording gap
  Then the covered data renders, the gap renders as a hatched labelled region stating its start, end and cause, and no value is interpolated across it

Scenario: Kline-backfilled window is labelled as bar-derived
  Given part of a gap was backfilled from kline data
  Then those bars render with a bar-derived marker and the tick-level gap is still shown for tick-level views

Scenario: No infinite spinner
  Given the coverage request fails
  Then an error state with a retry is shown within 5 seconds, never a spinner that persists

Scenario: Empty chart costs no GPU
  When the chart empty state renders
  Then the GL context for the data layer is not initialised
```

## Technical notes / design
- Decision order for which state to show: coverage says nothing recorded -> `recording-not-started`; coverage exists but not in this window -> `no-data-in-range` with the nearest available range offered; instrument delisted/suspended -> instrument state; otherwise error.
- The empty state renders without initialising the GL data layer (SCR-047 performance rule), so it is a plain DOM overlay, not a GL scene.
- Gap regions are passed to the chart engine (E11) as an interval list on the render model; the engine draws the hatch, the story owns the labelling and the copy.
- Copy for all variants comes from the signed-off E16-D05 strings; every variant must name the cause, per the SCR-151 rule that "No data" alone is never acceptable.

## Test plan
- Unit: state-selection decision table (all four SCR-047 cases plus error), role-aware action rendering, timestamp formatting in the user's configured timezone.
- Storybook: every variant of CMP-026 and every SCR-047 case; visual regression baselined so R2 epics inherit a stable pattern.
- Integration: 422 `no_data_recorded` path end-to-end from the real endpoint.
- E2E (E16-Q02): open a chart for an unrecorded symbol as owner, use the CTA, and assert recording starts and the chart transitions out of the empty state.
- a11y: axe-core; screen-reader pass confirming heading + explanation + action structure.
- Perf: assert no GL context is created for the data layer in the empty state.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
The empty state must not disclose whether *other* users recorded a symbol beyond what the role may see, and the CTA must be permission-gated (`recording:write`) with server-side enforcement. No host paths, no internal error text rendered verbatim to non-owners. Classification **internal**.

## Accessibility notes
Per SCR-047 and SCR-151: the empty state is a heading plus a paragraph plus an action - never an icon alone and never a bare "No data"; the recording-start timestamp is text, not an image or a tooltip; the CTA is a real button for owners and an explicit sentence for other roles; the hatched gap region has a text equivalent (a list of gap intervals with start, end and cause) reachable by keyboard, because a hatch pattern is invisible to a screen reader; contrast of the hatch meets 3:1 against the plot background.

## Performance notes
Empty states render without initialising heavy resources - no GL context, no subscriptions (SCR-151 rule) - so an empty panel costs nothing. State transition to a populated chart happens within one frame of data arriving.

## Observability
Analytics `chart.empty_state_shown {reason}` and `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}` - used to find states users hit often and should not.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated including the no-GL-context assertion.
- [ ] CMP-026 variants documented in Storybook and added to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` by PR.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass on the gap text equivalent.
- [ ] E16-D05 sign-off checklist recorded.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%.
- [ ] 2 approvals including frontend code-owner and a design-system reviewer.

## Dependencies
`E16-T04` supplies coverage and the `no_data_recorded` contract; `E11` supplies the chart engine's interval/hatch render hook; `E16-D05` supplies the designs and copy.

`feat/e16-empty-states`.
