US-REC-006 exists to stop a trader mistaking a gap for calm, and ADR-0015 decision 7 makes coverage first-class data: "no interpolation, ever - a gap that looks like data is worse than a gap that looks like a gap". Every downstream R2 surface (E18 footprint, E19 profiles, E23 CVD, E26 replay) queries this service before rendering a historical window, so the correctness of gap intervals here bounds the honesty of the whole product.

A `recording_sessions` row is one continuous capture run; a reconnect that loses data closes the session with a gap and opens a new one (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.6.2).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/sessions.py` - session lifecycle: open on `RecorderSetChanged(start)`, transition `starting -> recording -> degraded -> stopping -> stopped|error`, close on stop/crash/restart with `end_reason`.
- Gap detection writing `recording_gaps` rows with `cause` in `ws_disconnect | backpressure_drop | process_restart | seq_jump | exchange_outage`:
  - WS disconnect/resubscribe windows reported by E08.
  - `seq` jumps on `orderbook_deltas` observed by E16-T03.
  - Crash recovery: on startup, any session in state `recording`/`degraded` with no live process is closed with `end_reason='process_restart'` and a gap from `last_event_ts` to process start.
- `CoverageService.coverage(symbol, streams, from, to)` returning contiguous covered intervals per stream with the tier that holds them plus intersecting gaps - the backing implementation of `GET /market/data-coverage` (response shape fixed by `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`).
- `recording_started_at` resolution used by the `no_data_recorded` (422) contract: the earliest `first_event_ts` across sessions for the symbol.
- Daily integrity job: per symbol and stream, verify sequence continuity and that stored intervals reconcile with session windows; anomalies are written as gaps or, if unexplainable, raised as a `recorder.integrity_anomaly` system event.
- Kline-derived partial backfill marking: where E08 can fill a gap window from Bybit REST `kline`, bars are written and the gap row is marked `backfilled=true, backfill_source='kline'` while the gap remains visible to tick-level consumers.
- Implement the `B11` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B11.machine.json`, committed by E50-S01/S02 (hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.

## Out of scope
- Rendering gaps in the UI (E16-S05 for the empty/partial states; E18/E26 own their own hatching).

- Replay session planning (E26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Disconnect produces one explicit gap
  Given BTCUSDT is recording and the public WS drops for 12 minutes
  When the connection is restored and a snapshot is re-taken
  Then the open session is closed, a recording_gaps row with cause "ws_disconnect" covering exactly the outage window is written, and a new session is opened

Scenario: Coverage is honest about what exists
  Given trades exist from 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-14 with a gap on 2026-09-04 02:11 to 02:14:20
  When coverage is requested for the trades stream over that range
  Then two contiguous intervals are returned with their tiers, and the gap is reported separately with its cause
  And the union of intervals never includes the gap window

Scenario: Window before recording started is refused, not faked
  Given recording for SOLUSDT started on 2026-09-13
  When a historical window entirely before that date is requested
  Then the API responds 422 no_data_recorded carrying recording_started_at, rather than an empty success

Scenario: Crash leaves no open session
  Given the process is killed while a session is in state recording
  When the service restarts
  Then the session is closed with end_reason "process_restart" and a gap from last_event_ts to startup is written

Scenario: Kline backfill does not erase the tick gap
  Given a 12 minute gap is partly fillable from REST kline data
  When backfill runs
  Then bars for that window exist and are marked bar-derived, the gap row is marked backfilled with source "kline", and tick-level coverage for that window is still reported as missing
```

## Technical notes / design
- Interval algebra: coverage is computed as `session windows minus gaps`, merged with a 1 s tolerance to avoid thousands of hairline intervals from reconnect churn; the merge tolerance is a constant `COVERAGE_MERGE_TOLERANCE_MS = 1000`, documented in code, never applied to gaps themselves (a real 3 s gap is never merged away).
- Coverage is cached per `(symbol, stream)` with an invalidation on any session or gap write; the cache holds intervals only for the last 90 days and falls through to SQL for older ranges.
- Tier attribution comes from the roll-off watermark maintained by E16-T05: intervals older than the watermark report `tier: parquet`, newer report `tier: questdb`, and an interval spanning the watermark is split.
- Row counts in the coverage response are estimates from QuestDB partition metadata, not `count(*)` - the response documents them as approximate.

title: Implement RollOffJob: verified hot-to-cold Parquet export and weekly compaction
body:
## Context
US-REC-004 requires recent data in the hot tier and older data archived so queries stay fast and storage stays affordable, with the hard rule that hot data is dropped **only after a verified write**. ADR-0015 decision 3 sets the hot window at `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (default 7) with a nightly export to Parquet. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §5-§6 defines the Parquet layout, the DuckDB views over it and the weekly compactor that merges the small files the nightly export produces.

The failure mode this guards against is the worst one available to a recorder: dropping a hot partition after a corrupt or partial archive write, destroying irreplaceable data (Bybit has no historical L2 to re-fetch).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/rolloff.py` - nightly job exporting QuestDB partitions older than the per-stream hot window (`retention_policies.retain_days` for the hot tier) to Parquet under the layout in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §5, then dropping the hot partition **only** after verification.
- Verification: row count match **and** checksum match between source partition and written Parquet file (US-REC-004 NFR). Mismatch -> hot data retained, `archive.verification_failed` alert raised, job retries with exponential backoff and does not advance the watermark.
- Roll-off watermark per `(symbol, stream)` persisted so `CoverageService` (E16-T04) can attribute tiers.
- DuckDB view registration so a query spanning both tiers is served seamlessly, with the tiers used reported in the query detail (`meta.sources` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` responses).
- Weekly compactor merging small Parquet files into target-sized partitions (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §5.4), exposed as `POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/compact` (async, job id polled via `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`).
- Cold-cold rollup: partitions older than 180 days for `orderbook_deltas` and `heatmap_cells` are downsampled to 1 s book snapshots per `retention_policies.action='downsample'` rather than merged.

## Out of scope
- Deleting cold data at the retention horizon (E16-T06).
- Disk-pressure acceleration (E16-T07).
- Backups and restore (`/admin/backups/*` - platform/ops epic).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Nightly roll-off archives then drops
  Given trades partitions older than the hot window exist for BTCUSDT
  When the nightly roll-off runs
  Then Parquet files are written under the documented layout, row counts and checksums match, the hot partition is dropped and the watermark advances

Scenario: Verification failure never loses data
  Given the Parquet write produces a file whose row count differs from the source partition
  When verification runs
  Then the hot partition is NOT dropped, the partial Parquet file is quarantined, an alert is raised and the job retries with backoff

Scenario: Cross-tier query is seamless
  Given trades for a symbol span Parquet and QuestDB
  When a 14-day window is queried
  Then one merged, correctly ordered result is returned and meta.sources lists both questdb and parquet

Scenario: Compaction is safe under concurrent reads
  Given a replay session is reading a cold partition
  When compaction targets that partition
  Then compaction defers it, logs the deferral and completes the remaining partitions

Scenario: Downsample past 180 days
  Given orderbook_deltas partitions older than 180 days
  When the rollup runs
  Then they are replaced by 1 second book snapshots and the coverage report labels the range as downsampled
```

## Technical notes / design
- Export unit is one (symbol, stream, day) partition, processed newest-first so an interrupted run leaves the oldest data in the hot tier rather than a half-migrated middle.
- Checksum: SHA-256 over the canonical column-ordered Arrow batches, computed on read-back of the written file (not on the in-memory buffer) - a verification that never re-reads the file does not verify anything.
- Quarantine path `<parquet_root>/_quarantine/<stream>/<symbol>/<date>/` with the failure reason in a sidecar JSON; quarantined files are never registered in DuckDB views.
- Concurrency: the job takes a Postgres advisory lock per `(symbol, stream)`; the replay engine takes a shared read lease on ranges it is using, which the compactor honours (US-REC-003 NFR: never delete or rewrite data currently being read by a replay or backtest).
- Config: `CV_RECORDER_HOT_DAYS` (7), `CV_PARQUET_ROOT`, `CV_COMPACT_TARGET_MB` (default 256), `CV_ROLLOFF_CRON` (default `0 3 * * *`).
- Error codes: `archive_verification_failed`, `archive_write_failed`, `compaction_deferred`.

## Test plan
- Unit: watermark advance/rollback, checksum computation, quarantine on mismatch, newest-first ordering, advisory-lock contention.
- Integration (QuestDB + local Parquet): full export-verify-drop cycle on a seeded day; injected mismatch asserting no drop; cross-tier query correctness against a known row set.
- Chaos: kill the job between write and verify, and between verify and drop; assert no data loss in either case and that a re-run converges.
- Perf: export of one day of depth-200 `orderbook_deltas` (the largest stream) completes within the nightly window and uses < 2 GiB RSS.
- Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Path traversal in `archive_path` / `CV_PARQUET_ROOT` is an explicit epic-level threat (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` security row for E16): every path is resolved and asserted to be inside the configured root before any write or delete; symlinks are rejected. Deletion of a hot partition is audited with symbol, stream, range and row count (`retention_purge`-class audit entry). Requires the `security` review label on the PR.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. Job progress surfaces through SCR-142 (E16-S04).

## Performance notes
The job must not degrade live ingestion: throttle to `CV_ROLLOFF_MAX_MBPS` (default 200) and yield between partitions; assert ingest p95 lag is unchanged during a roll-off in the integration test.

## Observability
Metrics `recorder_rolloff_bytes_total{stream}`, `recorder_rolloff_duration_seconds`, `recorder_rolloff_failures_total{reason}`, `recorder_watermark_lag_days{symbol,stream}`. Alert when watermark lag exceeds hot window + 2 days.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Path-containment test proving traversal is refused.
- [ ] Coverage >=85%.
- [ ] Runbook entry added to `docs/ops/runbooks/recorder-rolloff.md` covering a stuck watermark and a quarantined file.
- [ ] 2 approvals including backend code-owner and a DevSecOps review.

## Dependencies
`E16-T03` writes the hot data; `E07` provides the Parquet/DuckDB tier wiring.

title: Implement RetentionManager: policy resolution, dry-run preview, reaper and purge
body:
## Context
US-REC-003 is the ticket where data is irreversibly destroyed, so it is the ticket with the least room for error. The owner decision is a 30-day default with per-symbol overrides and `pinned = true` meaning never delete (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §6). The story requires a **dry run** that reports exactly what would be deleted by symbol, range and size before anything is removed, and an NFR that pruning is off-peak, resumable, and never deletes data currently being read by a replay or backtest.

ADR-0015 decision 9 adds that deletion is auditable and the audit entry outlives the data.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/retention.py` - `RetentionManager` with `resolve(symbol, stream) -> EffectivePolicy`, `preview(scope) -> PrunePlan`, `run(plan, dry_run: bool)`.
- Resolution order (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.6.3): pinned symbol -> infinite; else symbol-scoped policy; else default policy; else hard default 30 days. `applies_to_pinned: true` on a policy is the only way to touch pinned data, and it requires step-up.
- Nightly reaper: drops QuestDB partitions past the hot horizon (already archived by E16-T05) and deletes Parquet partition directories past the total horizon, per the matrix in §7. Resumable: progress checkpointed per `(symbol, stream, partition)` so an interrupted run resumes rather than restarts.
- Read-lease honouring: a partition covered by an active replay/backtest lease is skipped and retried on the next pass, never deleted mid-read.
- `PrunePlan`: per symbol, stream, date range, estimated bytes and row count, total bytes freed, and an explicit list of what is protected and why (pinned / leased / inside hot window).
- Irreversible purge (`POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/purge`): requires an elevated session, a mandatory `reason` (3-280 chars) and a `confirm_symbol` echo equal to `symbol`; refuses pinned symbols unless `include_pinned` is set; always audited with the exact window deleted; asynchronous with a job id.
- Audit events `retention.run`, `retention.change`, `data.deleted`, `retention.purge` carrying symbol, stream, range, row count and actor; retained after the data is gone.

## Out of scope
- Disk-pressure accelerated mode (E16-T07).
- The retention editor UI (E16-S03) and the REST policy endpoints (E16-T08).
- Postgres-side retention for OMS/journal tables (owned by their epics).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default retention prunes on schedule
  Given the default trades retention is 30 days and BTCUSDT is not pinned
  When the nightly reaper runs
  Then trades partitions older than 30 days are deleted, the freed bytes are reported and the next prune time is recorded

Scenario: Pinned data is never deleted
  Given ETHUSDT is pinned and has data older than every configured horizon
  When the reaper runs with any policy that does not set applies_to_pinned
  Then nothing for ETHUSDT is deleted and the plan lists it as protected with reason "pinned"

Scenario: Dry run deletes nothing
  When a prune preview is requested
  Then it reports exactly what would be deleted by symbol, range and size
  And a byte-for-byte comparison of the data volume before and after shows no change

Scenario: Data under active replay is not deleted
  Given a replay session holds a lease on a partition eligible for deletion
  When the reaper reaches that partition
  Then it is skipped with reason "leased", logged, and retried on the next pass

Scenario: Interrupted run resumes
  Given the reaper is killed after processing 3 of 10 symbols
  When it next runs
  Then it resumes from the checkpoint and does not re-scan the completed symbols

Scenario: Purge requires an exact confirmation
  Given an owner requests a purge of BTCUSDT with confirm_symbol "BTCUSD"
  Then the request is rejected 422 and nothing is deleted
  And with the correct echo, an elevated session and a reason, the purge is accepted, executed and audited with the exact window

Scenario: Shortening retention warns with the real number
  Given trades retention is reduced from 30 to 7 days
  When the change is previewed
  Then the plan states the exact GB and date range that become eligible for deletion before the change is applied
```

## Technical notes / design
- Deletion primitives: QuestDB `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION WHERE ts < dateadd('d', -N, now())` (§6); Parquet deletion is a directory unlink after the DuckDB view is de-registered, with the path containment check from E16-T05 applied again at the delete site.
- The reaper's **first** predicate is the pin check, exactly as §6 specifies: `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM recorded_symbols WHERE symbol = $1 AND pinned AND removed_at IS NULL)`.
- Un-pinning does not retroactively delete: the next pass applies the normal policy, and the API returns the exact volume that will be dropped so the UI (E16-S03) can warn.
- Ordering guarantee: raw-tick retention must be >= the retention of anything derived from it within the same stream family; the policy validator rejects a set where `bars_*` outlive `trades` (the SCR-141 validation rule "bars can't be deleted before the ticks they came from").
- Off-peak: default cron `0 4 * * *`, configurable via `CV_RETENTION_CRON`; the run yields if ingest lag rises above 1 s.
- Error codes: `retention_invalid_policy`, `retention_pinned_refused`, `purge_confirmation_mismatch`, `purge_requires_elevation`.

## Test plan
- Unit: resolution matrix (pinned/symbol/default/hard-default x 5 streams), validator rejecting inverted tick/bar retention, checkpoint resume, plan arithmetic.
- Integration: seeded multi-symbol dataset run through preview then real run, asserting exact byte and row deltas; pinned-symbol immunity; lease skip; purge happy path and all three refusal paths.
- Chaos: kill the reaper mid-partition; assert no partially deleted partition is left registered in DuckDB and that a re-run converges.
- Security test: purge without elevation -> 403; with mismatched echo -> 422; against a pinned symbol without `include_pinned` -> 422.
- Coverage >=90% on `recorder/retention.py` (destructive code path, above the standard bar).

## Security notes
This is the highest-severity code in the epic: an authorization or predicate bug destroys irreplaceable data. Controls: `recording:write` plus step-up for purge (permission 51 in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §13); mandatory reason; typed confirmation; pin check first; audit before delete and after delete (both, so a crash between them is detectable); path containment. Threat coverage: tampering (policy change to destroy data), repudiation (audit), DoS (mass purge). **PR requires the `security` label and Security-engineer sign-off.** Classification **internal**, but deletion is irreversible so treated as a high-impact action.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI in this ticket; consequences are surfaced by SCR-141 (E16-S03).

## Performance notes
A full reaper pass over 20 symbols x 10 streams completes in < 10 minutes and never raises ingest p95 lag above the live budget; partition drops are metadata operations, so wall time is dominated by Parquet unlinks, which are batched.

## Observability
Metrics `retention_deleted_bytes_total{symbol,stream}`, `retention_deleted_rows_total`, `retention_protected_total{reason}`, `retention_run_duration_seconds`, `retention_last_success_timestamp`. Alert if `retention_last_success_timestamp` is older than 48 h (silent retention failure is how disks fill).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every acceptance scenario automated, including the dry-run no-change assertion.
- [ ] Coverage >=90%.
- [ ] Security sign-off comment from the Security engineer.
- [ ] Audit entries verified to survive deletion of the data they describe.
- [ ] Runbook `docs/ops/runbooks/recorder-retention.md` covering a stuck reaper and an accidental over-broad policy.
- [ ] 2 approvals including backend code-owner.

## Dependencies
`E16-T05` must have archived data before the hot tier may be dropped; `E16-T01` supplies `retention_policies` and the resolution helper.

## Branch

title: Implement DiskBudget: measured growth, projection and the disk-pressure ladder
body:
## Context
Unbounded recording filling the disk and taking the trading host down is rated **Critical** (threat S2, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.8, control SR-096). US-REC-005 requires measured - not estimated - per-symbol GB/day, a projection of days of runway, a warning when the budget would be exceeded within 7 days, and a hard limit at which new recording is suspended while existing data is preserved.

ADR-0015 decision 6 fixes the ladder: alert at 80% of `CV_DISK_CAP_GB`, auto-recording stops accepting new symbols at 90% (explicit-list symbols keep recording), recording halts entirely at 95% with a critical alert. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §6 adds the free-space ladder: below 15% free the reaper accelerates; below 5% free, ingestion for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols pauses. Pinned data is never deleted automatically - the system stops recording rather than discarding what the user asked to keep.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/budget.py` - `DiskBudget` sampling volume usage and per-symbol/per-tier sizes **every 60 s** (SCR-142 requires server-side sampling, never on-request computation), persisting a rolling series for growth-rate calculation.
- Measured daily growth per symbol from the sampled series (7-day linear fit, falling back to 24 h when less data exists), projected `disk_full_at`, and days-of-runway - the fields behind `GET /api/v1/recording/storage`.
- Ladder implementation with hysteresis (re-arm 5 percentage points below each trigger):
  - 75-80%: warning system event with concrete suggested actions (reduce depth tier, shorten retention, unpin).
  - 90% of cap **or** <15% free: refuse new auto-record entries; accelerate the reaper (halve effective retention for non-pinned symbols in ascending `recorded_symbols.priority` until free space exceeds 25%).
  - 95% of cap **or** <5% free: pause ingestion for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols, then halt recording entirely; raise a critical event; existing data preserved.
- Volume separation assertion at startup (SR-096): the recording volume must differ from the volume Postgres and the backend need; if it does not, log a critical warning and refuse to enable recording unless `CV_ALLOW_SHARED_VOLUME=true`.
- Trading-path independence: recording suspension must never disable order placement - asserted by test, stated in the UI copy for SCR-142.

## Out of scope
- The UI for budget display (E16-S01, E16-S04) and the alert delivery channel (E40).
- Retention execution itself (E16-T06); this task only signals accelerated mode.
- Backup sizing.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Figures are measured, not estimated
  Given 7 days of 60-second usage samples for BTCUSDT
  When storage usage is requested
  Then daily_growth_bytes is derived from the sampled series and is within 20 percent of the measured GB/day figure from the E16-K01 note

Scenario: Budget warning fires before the wall
  Given the projection shows the configured cap will be exceeded in 6 days
  Then a warning event fires naming the projected date and listing reduce-depth, shorten-retention and unpin as actions

Scenario: Auto-record stops but the explicit list keeps recording
  Given usage reaches 90 percent of CV_DISK_CAP_GB
  When a chart is opened for an unrecorded symbol
  Then auto-record is refused with a warning event
  And symbols on the explicit manual list continue recording uninterrupted

Scenario: Hard limit preserves data and trading
  Given usage reaches 95 percent
  Then recording halts, a critical alert fires, no recorded data is deleted, and placing an order still succeeds

Scenario: Pinned data survives disk pressure
  Given free space falls below 5 percent and a pinned symbol holds most of the data
  Then the pinned data is not deleted, ingestion for non-pinned auto-recorded symbols is paused, and the critical event names the pinned symbol as the dominant consumer

Scenario: Hysteresis prevents flapping
  Given usage oscillates between 89 and 91 percent
  Then the auto-record refusal engages once and does not re-arm until usage falls below 85 percent
```

## Technical notes / design
- Sampling uses `statvfs` for the volume and QuestDB `tables()` / Parquet directory sizes for per-tier and per-symbol attribution; per-symbol attribution for Parquet comes from the partition path, so it is exact rather than apportioned.
- Growth fit ignores samples inside recorded gaps so an outage does not depress the projected rate.
- Ladder decisions are published as `DiskPressureChanged` events consumed by `RecordingPolicy` (E16-T02) and `RetentionManager` (E16-T06); the budget component never deletes anything itself, which keeps deletion authority in exactly one place.
- Config: `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` (500, revised by E16-K01), `CV_DISK_WARN_PCT` (80), `CV_DISK_AUTOSTOP_PCT` (90), `CV_DISK_HALT_PCT` (95), `CV_DISK_SAMPLE_INTERVAL_S` (60), `CV_ALLOW_SHARED_VOLUME` (false).

## Test plan
- Unit: projection maths with gaps, hysteresis state machine, ladder thresholds by both cap-percentage and free-space paths.
- Integration: a loopback volume filled to 76%, 81%, 91% and 96% asserting each documented behaviour including pinned survival and trading availability (the disk-pressure chaos test named in ADR-0015 Validation and SR-154).
- Contract: `StorageUsage` response validated against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Directly implements SR-096 and mitigates the Critical DoS S2. Additional checks: the sampler must not shell out (no `du` subprocess with user-controlled paths); volume separation asserted at startup; the suggested-actions text must not leak absolute host paths to non-owner roles. **PR carries the `security` label.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI here; the meter and its numeric text are specified in E16-D02/E16-D04 and built in E16-S01/E16-S04.

## Performance notes
Sampling costs < 50 ms per pass and never blocks ingestion; the 60 s cadence is a budget, not a target to beat.

## Observability
Metrics `disk_used_ratio`, `disk_free_bytes`, `recorder_disk_pressure_level`, `recorder_bytes_per_day{symbol}`, `recorder_projected_full_timestamp`. Alerts: warning at `CV_DISK_WARN_PCT`, critical at `CV_DISK_HALT_PCT`, and a page if `recorder_disk_pressure_level > 0` for over 24 h.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated, including the loopback-volume chaos test at all four fill levels.
- [ ] Trading-remains-functional assertion present in the 96% test.
- [ ] Coverage >=85%.
- [ ] `CV_DISK_CAP_GB` default updated from the E16-K01 measurement.
- [ ] Security sign-off on SR-096 compliance.
- [ ] 2 approvals including backend code-owner and DevSecOps.

## Dependencies
`E16-T03` supplies the write-rate signal; `E16-K01` supplies the measured constants this ladder is sized against.

title: Implement the recording REST surface and the recorder WS topic
body:
## Context
The recorder is useless without the contract the web app talks to. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already specifies every path under the `recording` tag and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.8 specifies the `RecorderUpdate` frame at a 1000 ms cadence. This task implements exactly that contract - interface-first, so the frontend stories (E16-S01..S05) can be built against a green contract test rather than a guess.

## Scope / Deliverables
- REST handlers implementing, byte-for-byte against the existing OpenAPI spec:
  - `GET /api/v1/recording/symbols` (`listRecordedSymbols`), `POST /api/v1/recording/symbols`
  - `GET|PATCH|DELETE /api/v1/recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}` (PATCH covers pin, retention, depth; DELETE stops recording and retains data, `?purge_data=true` for destruction)
  - `POST /api/v1/recording/symbols/{recordedSymbolId}/pin`
  - `GET /api/v1/recording/status` (`getRecordingStatus`)
  - `GET /api/v1/recording/storage` (`getStorageUsage`)
  - `GET|PUT /api/v1/recording/retention-policies` (`?apply_now=true` triggers an immediate sweep)
  - `GET /api/v1/recording/sessions` (cursor-paginated)
  - `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage` (`getDataCoverage`)
  - `POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/compact`, `POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/purge` (both async, returning `job_id`)
- RBAC per the spec `x-rbac` blocks: `recording:read` for reads, `recording:write` for writes, step-up elevation for purge (permission 51, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §13).
- Idempotency: `Idempotency-Key` required on compact and purge, optional on the retention PUT.
- WS topic `recorder` (param `symbols`, cadence 1000 ms, permission `recording:read`, scope none) publishing `RecorderUpdate` exactly per §15.8: `overall`, `connections[]`, `symbols[]` (with `state`, `reason`, `pinned`, `lag_ms`, `rows_last_hour`, `dropped_messages`, `resyncs_last_hour`, `disk_bytes`, `last_event_at_ms`), `ingest_rate_msgs_per_sec`, `write_backlog_rows`, `storage`.
- Error contracts: `no_data_recorded` (422) from historical endpoints whose window precedes `recording_started_at`; `recorder_symbol_limit` (422); `purge_confirmation_mismatch` (422); `403` for missing permission or elevation.
- Generated TypeScript client types regenerated in `packages/api-client` from the OpenAPI spec.

## Out of scope
- Any UI (E16-S01..S05).
- Changing the OpenAPI or WS documents - if the implementation cannot match the spec, the spec change is a separate, reviewed PR, not a silent drift.
- Backup endpoints.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Contract tests pass against the published spec
  When the contract suite runs every recording path against docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then every request and response validates, including the documented examples

Scenario: Empty by default
  Given a fresh installation
  When GET /api/v1/recording/symbols is called
  Then it returns an empty list with a 200, not a 404

Scenario: Stop retains data
  When DELETE /api/v1/recording/symbols/{id} is called without purge_data
  Then recording stops within 5 seconds, the session is closed, the recorded data remains queryable and the response states that retention policy now governs it

Scenario: Purge needs elevation and an exact echo
  Given an owner session without step-up elevation
  When POST /api/v1/admin/recorder/purge is called
  Then 403 is returned and nothing is deleted
  And with elevation but confirm_symbol not equal to symbol, 422 purge_confirmation_mismatch is returned

Scenario: Viewer cannot write
  Given a Viewer session
  When POST /api/v1/recording/symbols is called
  Then 403 is returned and the attempt is audited

Scenario: WS recorder topic streams at 1 Hz
  Given a client subscribes to the recorder topic for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
  Then a snapshot frame arrives first, followed by updates at approximately 1000 ms
  And every frame validates against the RecorderUpdate schema

Scenario: Historical request before recording start is refused honestly
  Given recording for SOLUSDT started yesterday
  When bars are requested for a window entirely before that
  Then 422 no_data_recorded is returned carrying recording_started_at
```

## Technical notes / design
- Handlers are thin: all logic lives in the M10 services from T02/T04/T06/T07. The route layer only maps DTOs, enforces RBAC via `ScopeResolver` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10) and applies idempotency.
- `GET /recording/status` and the WS topic share one cached `RecordingStatus` snapshot refreshed at 1 Hz, so N subscribers cost one computation.
- `PUT /recording/retention-policies` replaces the whole set atomically in one transaction, validated by the E16-T06 policy validator before commit; `apply_now=true` enqueues a sweep rather than running it inline.
- Storage figures are served from the 60 s sample (E16-T07), never computed per request.
- Audit: `recorder.start`, `recorder.stop`, `retention.change`, `retention.purge`, `storage.compaction_triggered` with actor, before/after and the affected window.

## Test plan
- Contract: schemathesis/openapi-core against every path and the documented examples; WS frames validated against the JSON Schema in §15.8.
- Unit: DTO mapping, idempotency replay returning the original job id, RBAC matrix (Owner/Manager/Viewer x read/write/purge = 9 cases).
- Integration: full lifecycle - add symbol, observe WS state transitions, pin, change retention, stop, purge - against a live recorder.
- E2E hook: the suite in E16-Q02 consumes these endpoints.
- Load: 5 concurrent WS subscribers to `recorder` plus 1 Hz polling of `/recording/status`; CPU attributable to the topic stays under 2% of one core.
- Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Every write path is an admin action on a destructive subsystem. Controls: permission checks from the spec's `x-rbac`, step-up for purge, mandatory reason, idempotency to prevent double-purge on retry, rate limiting on write paths, and audit-before-and-after for deletes. Input validation: `symbol` against the instruments table (no free text reaching a path join), `retain_days` 1-3650, `archive_path` rejected from the API entirely (configured server-side only - closes the path-traversal vector). **PR carries the `security` label.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. Error payloads carry human-readable `detail` strings the UI can present verbatim.

## Performance notes
API p95 < 150 ms for all recording reads; WS `recorder` frames < 8 KiB for 20 symbols; the 1 Hz cadence is coalesced per connection (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` coalescing policy).

## Observability
Metrics `http_requests_total{route}` for the new routes, `ws_topic_subscribers{topic="recorder"}`, `recorder_status_cache_age_seconds`. Audit events as listed.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated; contract suite green.
- [ ] Generated TS client committed and consumed by the E16 frontend stories.
- [ ] Coverage >=85%.
- [ ] Security sign-off on the purge and RBAC paths.
- [ ] 2 approvals including backend code-owner.

`E16-T04` (coverage/status), `E16-T06` (retention/purge), `E16-T07` (storage figures), `E17` (WS gateway, topic registry and binary framing).

title: Implement resumable bulk import of Bybit public trade archives
body:
## Context
US-REC-007 (Should) lets the owner import Bybit's public historical trade archives so there is *some* depth before the recorder existed. It is explicitly partial relief: the archives carry trades only - no book data, no liquidations - so imported ranges must be labelled archive-derived and must never let a profile or footprint pretend it has book-quality history for that window.

The rule that keeps the data honest is recorded-wins: where an import overlaps data the recorder captured, the recorded data is authoritative and the overlap is reported rather than merged.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/recorder/importer.py` - downloads a date range of Bybit public trade archives for a symbol, validates checksums, converts to the canonical `trades` schema and writes directly to the cold Parquet tier under the E16-T05 layout.
- Resumability: per-file checkpoint so an interrupted import resumes at the next unprocessed file; re-running a completed import is a no-op.
- Rate limiting on downloads (`CV_IMPORT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, default 2; `CV_IMPORT_MAX_MBPS`, default 50) so an import never starves live ingestion.
- Overlap handling: for any window already covered by `recording_sessions`, recorded data wins; imported rows in that window are discarded, counted and reported in the summary. No duplicates are created.
- Labelling: imported intervals are registered in coverage as `source='archive'` with `streams=['trades']` only, so `CoverageService` (E16-T04) reports book-level coverage for those windows as absent.
- Corrupt-file handling: a file failing checksum or parsing is skipped, recorded in the summary with its name and the failure reason, and the import continues.
- Progress and summary surfaced as an async job (`GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`) rendered on SCR-142.

## Out of scope
- Importing anything other than Bybit public trade archives (no third-party data, no book reconstruction).
- Backfilling bars from REST kline - that path belongs to E16-T04's gap backfill.
- A dedicated import screen; progress lives on SCR-142 (E16-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Import a date range
  Given the owner imports 2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30 of BTCUSDT public trade archives
  When the job completes
  Then the files are downloaded, checksum-validated, converted and written to the cold tier
  And the summary reports files processed, rows written, rows discarded as overlap and files skipped

Scenario: Recorded data wins on overlap
  Given the recorder already covers 2026-06-20 to 2026-06-30 for BTCUSDT
  When the same range is imported
  Then no imported row for that window is written, the overlap is reported with its exact bounds, and no duplicate trade exists

Scenario: Corrupt file does not abort the import
  Given one file in the range fails its checksum
  Then that file is skipped and named in the summary and the remaining files are still imported

Scenario: Import is resumable
  Given the import is cancelled after 12 of 30 files
  When it is restarted with the same parameters
  Then it resumes at file 13 and does not re-download the first 12

Scenario: Imported windows are labelled archive-derived
  When coverage is requested over an imported-only window
  Then trades coverage is reported with source "archive" and orderbook_delta coverage is reported as absent
```

## Technical notes / design
- Archive URLs and file naming follow Bybit's public data site; the base URL is config (`CV_BYBIT_ARCHIVE_BASE`) so a layout change is a config fix, not a code change. Every URL is constructed from a validated symbol and an ISO date - never from user free text.
- Downloads go to a temp directory on the recording volume, are validated, converted, then moved into place atomically (write-temp-then-rename), so a crash never leaves a half file registered in a DuckDB view.
- Overlap detection queries `CoverageService` once per day-partition rather than per row.
- Conversion asserts the schema: columns, dtypes and monotonic `exch_ts` per file; a file whose timestamps fall outside its nominal date is skipped as corrupt.
- Error codes: `import_checksum_failed`, `import_parse_failed`, `import_range_invalid`.

## Test plan
- Unit: URL construction (including rejection of an unknown symbol), checksum validation, schema assertion, overlap arithmetic, checkpoint resume.
- Integration: import a 3-day fixture set (committed sample archives) into a clean cold tier; then re-import over a recorded window asserting recorded-wins and zero duplicates; then import with one deliberately corrupted file.
- Perf: importing one month of BTCUSDT trades keeps live ingest p95 lag unchanged.
- Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Fetching remote archives is the epic's only outbound-network surface: enforce HTTPS, pin the host to the configured Bybit archive domain, cap decompressed size per file (zip-bomb guard, `CV_IMPORT_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_MB` default 2048), and validate every extracted path stays inside the temp directory (archive path traversal - the second half of the epic's named security concern in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md`). title: Security review: destructive paths, RBAC, path containment, config gating
body:
## Context
E16 ships the product's first irreversible data-destruction path and its first outbound file fetch. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §14.8 defines a dedicated review checklist for data/recorder/export tickets, including the explicit item "disk-budget guard tested: at 90% usage recording pauses and trading remains fully functional (SR-096)". This ticket is the white-box review that signs that checklist off against the code that actually shipped, not against the design.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Manual code review of `recorder/policy.py`, `writer.py`, `sessions.py`, `rolloff.py`, `retention.py`, `budget.py`, `importer.py` and the `recording` route layer, against the E16-X01 model and the §14.8 checklist.
- Focus areas, each with a written finding or an explicit pass:
  1. **Destructive-path authorization** - purge requires `recording:write` **and** step-up elevation (permission 51), a mandatory reason and an exact `confirm_symbol` echo; the pin predicate is the reaper's first predicate; `applies_to_pinned` cannot be set without elevation.
  2. **Audit completeness and ordering** - an audit entry is written before and after every delete, survives the deleted data, and is hash-chained per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10.
  3. **Path containment** - every Parquet write, delete, archive extraction and quarantine path is resolved and asserted inside its configured root; symlinks refused; no user-supplied path reaches the filesystem from the API (`archive_path` is server-config only).
  4. **Outbound fetch hardening** - HTTPS enforced, host pinned to the configured Bybit archive domain, decompressed-size cap, extraction path validation, no redirect to a different host.
  5. **Resource limits** - `CV_RECORDER_MAX_SYMBOLS`, WAL bound, import concurrency/bandwidth caps, and the disk ladder all present and not bypassable by an auto-record path.
  6. **Config gating** - `CV_TEST_CLOCK` and `CV_ALLOW_SHARED_VOLUME` cannot be enabled in a production build; volume-separation assertion runs at startup.
  7. **Information exposure** - no absolute host path, connection string or internal error text reaches a non-owner role in any response or UI string.
  8. **Idempotency** - compact and purge require `Idempotency-Key`; a retry cannot double-purge.
- Semgrep/Bandit rules added under `ci/semgrep/recorder.yml` codifying the repeatable checks: filesystem write with a non-validated path, `tarfile`/`zipfile` extraction without member validation, subprocess use in the recorder package, and destructive SQL (`DROP PARTITION`, directory unlink) outside `retention.py`.
- ZAP/DAST profile additions for the `recording` and `/admin/recorder/*` endpoints, exercising the role matrix and the purge refusal paths.
- Review record at `docs/security/reviews/e16-recorder-review.md` with the §14.8 checklist completed item by item.

## Out of scope
- Fixing findings (raised against the owning ticket).
- The pen-test itself (E43, pre-Live).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every checklist item is answered with evidence
  When the review record is published
  Then every item of 04-security-program.md section 14.8 has a pass or a finding, each citing a file, line and test

Scenario: Purge cannot be reached without elevation
  Given a session with recording:write but no step-up elevation
  When purge is invoked directly against the API
  Then it is refused with 403 and the attempt is audited, verified by both code review and a DAST case

Scenario: Path traversal is impossible at every site
  Given crafted symbol, date and archive member values containing traversal sequences
  When export, delete, import and quarantine paths are constructed
  Then every one resolves inside its root or raises, proven by a test per site

Scenario: Test-only config cannot ship
  Given a production build
  When CV_TEST_CLOCK is set
  Then the application refuses to start or ignores it, and the review records which

Scenario: New SAST rules catch a planted defect
  Given a branch that writes a Parquet file using an unvalidated path
  Then the semgrep rule fails the build

Scenario: Findings are dispositioned
  When the review concludes
  Then every finding has a severity, an owning ticket, and either a fix or an Owner-accepted risk
```

## Technical notes / design
- Review is code-reading plus targeted dynamic probes, not a scan-and-forget: for each focus area, the reviewer writes the adversarial input that should fail and confirms it does.
- The planted-defect check for the new SAST rules is mandatory - a rule that has never failed has never been shown to work.
- DAST runs against a seeded scratch environment; destructive cases run only where a purge is expected to succeed, and the fixture is restored afterwards.

## Test plan
- The dynamic probes become permanent tests in the owning packages, so the review's findings do not regress silently.
- Semgrep rules ship with positive and negative fixtures under `ci/semgrep/tests/`.
- DAST profile runs in the nightly security job.

## Security notes
This ticket is the review. Its output is a precondition for E16-Q06 epic sign-off and is referenced by the pre-Live pen-test scope (E43). Any Critical or High finding blocks the epic.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The reviewer must confirm that the resource limits (WAL bound, sampling cadence, import caps) are enforced in code rather than only documented, and that enforcement does not depend on a background task that could die silently.

## Observability
Confirms SR-125 coverage for this epic: disk high-watermark exported and alerted, permission-check failures logged, audit-chain verification covering the recorder's audit entries.

- [ ] Review record merged with the §14.8 checklist completed.
- [ ] All findings filed with severity and disposition; no open Critical or High.
- [ ] Semgrep rules merged with fixtures and a passing planted-defect check.
- [ ] DAST profile merged and running nightly.
- [ ] Dynamic probes converted into permanent tests.
- [ ] Sign-off comment from the Security engineer on E16.

title: UX research: how order-flow traders read and act on footprint cells
body:
## Context
E18 introduces the densest information surface in the product: a grid of per-bar, per-price cells each carrying up to two numbers, a colour, an outline and optional markers. Before any pixel is drawn we need evidence for four decisions that cannot be recovered later without re-drawing everything: (1) which cell mode traders actually read at which zoom, (2) at what cell height numerals stop being useful (feeding E18-K01's measured LOD threshold), (3) whether imbalance is read as a per-cell marker or as a zone bracket, and (4) what a trader wants to do the moment they notice a cell ("focus imbalance", "copy cell stats", "replay from here" are the three context-menu items SCR-030 currently assumes).

The personas are `docs/plan/10-personas.md` P1 (owner/discretionary order-flow trader) and M1 (account manager). This is a **new interaction** - nothing in R0/R1 has a canvas grid with per-cell focus - so `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1 requires research before wireframes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 4-6 moderated sessions with the Owner and any available order-flow traders, using DeepCharts/Sierra/ATAS-style reference screenshots plus a clickable static prototype of SCR-030 at three zoom levels.
- Findings memo in `docs/research/digests/` covering: preferred default cell mode (bid x ask vs delta), read order within a cell, minimum comfortable cell height in px, imbalance representation preference (per-cell marker vs zone bracket vs both), context-menu action ranking, and the acceptability of the compact-profile collapse at high density.
- A prioritised decision list feeding E18-D02 wireframes and E18-K01's threshold-measurement plan.
- Validation that US-FP-005's "order-based input is absent, not disabled" framing reads as honest rather than as a missing feature.

## Out of scope
Visual design, tokens, motion, any Figma artboard, DOM-ladder or profile research (E21/E19 own theirs).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Evidence for the default cell mode
  Given at least 4 completed sessions
  When findings are synthesised
  Then the memo states the default cell mode with the count of participants preferring it and the reasons given

Scenario: Legibility floor is evidenced, not guessed
  When participants view the prototype at 4 px, 6 px, 8 px and 12 px cell heights
  Then the memo records the height at which each participant stops reading numerals
  And that figure is handed to E18-K01 as the starting point for the measured textLod threshold

Scenario: Contradictory findings are surfaced, not averaged
  Given participants disagree on imbalance representation
  Then the memo records both positions with rationale and proposes a per-user setting or a default plus override, rather than reporting a mean
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype uses static rendered PNGs of real recorded BTCUSDT 5m data (no engine dependency, so this can run in S08 before E18-S01 exists). Sessions recorded with consent; recordings stored in the research drive, not in the repo. Use the `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md` journey-map format for the synthesis.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validation is peer review of the memo by the CDO and the chart-engine lead.

## Security notes
Session recordings may contain participant faces and voices - PII. Store in the access-controlled research drive, redact names in the published memo, delete raw recordings after synthesis per the research data policy. No product data classification impact.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session run with a participant using a screen reader or at 200% zoom, to sanity-check that the DOM-mirror and SCR-045 table-alternative plan is credible before it is designed.

## Performance notes
N/A - but the legibility-floor finding is a direct input to performance budget #1, since cell text is the dominant glyph cost.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] >= 4 sessions completed and synthesised.
- [ ] Memo merged into `docs/research/digests/` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Decision list handed to E18-D02 and E18-K01 (linked on both tickets).

title: Wireframe the footprint layer on SCR-030, SCR-032 and the SCR-056 imbalance rows
body:
## Context
Low-fidelity structure for every surface E18 introduces or changes, resolving layout and state questions before hi-fi. The ASCII wireframes already in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` for SCR-030, SCR-032 and SCR-056 are the starting contract; this ticket turns them into real artboards with every state enumerated per the catalogue's state conventions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-030 chart panel, footprint layer**: cell grid inside the candle column, four cell modes, two display modes, imbalance markers, POC/VA/unfinished-auction markers, cell tooltip (CMP-197), cell-detail drawer (CMP-046), right-click menu ("Focus imbalance", "Copy cell stats", "Replay from here"), footprint on/off in CMP-222, `Alt+F` profile/box toggle entry from SCR-042.
- **SCR-032 footprint settings dialog**: every control in the catalogue wireframe (cell type, display, input source with the order-based entry **absent** plus its explanatory note, noise filter, imbalance ratio and stack, POC/VA toggles, cell-text auto-hide threshold and font size, bid/ask colours with the CVD-safe preset), the CMP-228 preview tile, and the recompute-in-progress state.
- **SCR-056 imbalance tracker, E18-owned rows**: the diagonal/stacked rows produced by US-FP-007/US-FP-008 with price range, direction, stack depth, ratio, age and virgin/crossed state; the "only unfilled" filter; the click-to-locate behaviour.
- **States per surface**: loading, streaming, stale (>2 s), disconnected, empty history naming the first recorded timestamp, partial history, extreme density (cell budget exceeded -> compact profile + "zoom in for numbers" hint), low-GPU degraded ("Reduced detail: footprint text hidden below 6 px cells"), recompute in progress, validation errors (imbalance ratio outside 100-2000%, stack outside 2-10, negative noise filter).
- **Density variants**: comfortable / compact / dense, since density changes cell padding, font size class and LOD thresholds together as one coherent switch.

## Out of scope
Colour, type, iconography, motion (E18-D03/D04). Profile panes, Deep-Stats strip, DOM ladder.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state is drawn
  When the wireframe file is reviewed against the SCR-030, SCR-032 and SCR-056 entries in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  Then every state listed there has a corresponding artboard, with none marked "TBD"

Scenario: Density collapse is designed, not left to the engine
  Given the cell budget is exceeded
  Then the wireframe shows the compact profile representation and the exact placement and wording of the "zoom in for numbers" hint

Scenario: The absent order-based input reads as honest
  Given the input-source control in SCR-032
  Then the order-based option is shown as absent with an adjacent info note stating Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed
  And a reviewer unfamiliar with the constraint can explain it after reading only the artboard
```

## Technical notes / design
Artboards at 1280x800 (minimum supported layout) and 2560x1440. Use real recorded BTCUSDT 5m cell counts from the E18-D01 prototype material so density is honest. Annotate each control with its backing `FootprintConfig` field name from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 4.7 so hi-fi and implementation cannot drift from the backend contract.

## Test plan

## Out of scope
Motion (E18-D04), handoff packaging (E18-D05), engine implementation.

```gherkin

Scenario: Cell text contrast holds over saturated heat
  Given the most saturated cell background in each theme
  Then cell numerals meet >= 4.5:1 contrast, using the SDF outline pass if needed
  And the outline treatment is specified as a token, not as a per-screen hack

Scenario: Every cell mode has a real-data sample
  When the SCR-032 sign-off checklist is walked
  Then bid x ask, volume, delta and delta+total each have a rendered sample from recorded BTCUSDT data at all three densities
```

Cell text is rendered from a runtime-generated SDF atlas of digits plus `. , - + % x K M B` and A-Za-z for labels (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.7). Contrast measurement recorded per theme/density pair; CVD simulation screenshots attached; design review with the chart-engine lead confirming every visual effect is expressible with the available primitives (rects, lines, quads, glyph runs, textures) and no raw-GL-only effect is requested.

N/A.

WCAG 2.2 AA: >= 4.5:1 for all cell text and labels, >= 3:1 for meaningful non-text boundaries (cell borders carrying POC/VA meaning), >= 24x24 px targets for every interactive control in SCR-032 and SCR-056, visible focus ring specified for the focused cell in the DOM mirror (the ring is drawn on the canvas, synchronised with the mirror focus). The focused-cell indicator must be visible at every LOD level including when text is hidden.

## Performance notes
Constrain the design to the measured glyph budget: 2 500 visible cells x 2 numbers in one instanced draw call, <= 2.0 ms total (CI-asserted). Any design element requiring a second text pass or a per-cell texture must be justified against that budget with the chart-engine lead's agreement.

N/A.

title: Motion spec and accessibility review for the footprint surfaces
body:
## Context
Footprint has more moving parts than any prior surface: the forming bar's cells change up to 10 times a second, imbalance flags appear and disappear as thresholds are met, the LOD ladder switches text on and off while zooming, and stacked-imbalance zones transition virgin -> crossed. Without a deliberate motion spec this reads as flicker. US-FP-009's NFR is explicit: "both markers update as the forming bar evolves, without flicker", with marker updates coalesced to <= 10 Hz.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion spec**: forming-cell value updates (no transition on the number itself, only on the heat fill, <= 120 ms ease-out), imbalance marker appearance (fade-in 100 ms; never a scale/bounce), stacked-zone virgin->crossed transition, LOD text show/hide (crossfade tied to the hysteretic threshold, not an instant pop), POC marker moving between price levels within a forming bar, unfinished-auction marker appearance on bar close, cell-detail drawer open/close, settings-dialog preview-tile update.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion` variants** for every one of the above: transitions reduce to instant state changes with no crossfade; the LOD switch becomes a hard cut (which is acceptable because the hysteresis dead band prevents oscillation).
- **Flicker policy**: the rule that no marker may appear and disappear more than once per 200 ms; values that would oscillate are held until the coalescing window closes.
- **Accessibility review** of the E18-D03 hi-fi against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: focus-order walkthrough of the cell grid, announcement policy for the DOM mirror (what is announced on cell focus, on bar change, on imbalance appearance - and crucially what is **not** announced, since a polite live region firing per forming-cell update would be unusable), the `(estimated)` badge placement, and the SCR-045 table-alternative parity check.

## Out of scope
Implementation, handoff packaging.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion is complete, not partial
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When the motion spec is reviewed
  Then every transition listed has a defined reduced variant and none is left as "same as default"

Scenario: Screen-reader chatter is bounded
  Given the forming bar updates 10 times per second
  When the announcement policy is applied
  Then no automatic announcement is emitted for forming-cell value changes
  And announcements occur only on explicit user focus movement, on bar close, and on a newly formed stacked-imbalance zone

Scenario: LOD switching does not flicker
  Given a slow zoom sweep across the text-LOD threshold
  Then the +/-15% hysteresis dead band plus the specified crossfade produces at most one visible transition per crossing
```

## Technical notes / design
Motion tokens come from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` (`motion.*`); no bespoke durations. All chart-surface motion is implemented in the engine's own frame loop, not CSS, so the spec must express durations in milliseconds and easing as a named curve the engine can evaluate - state that explicitly for the implementer.

## Test plan

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket **is** the a11y design review. Output includes: focus-order diagram for SCR-030's footprint layer, the announcement policy table, the keyboard map (arrow keys move cell-to-cell, `Enter` opens the detail drawer, `Esc` returns focus to the pane, `Alt+T` to SCR-045), and confirmation that every non-colour encoding from E18-D03 survives at every LOD level.

## Performance notes
Motion must not add a second render pass. Crossfades are expressed as an alpha uniform on the existing glyph draw, not as two batched draws - confirm with the chart-engine lead and record the confirmation.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Flicker policy documented and agreed with the chart-engine lead.
- [ ] Focus-order diagram, keyboard map and announcement policy table signed off by the accessibility specialist.
- [ ] Findings from the a11y review either fixed in the E18-D03 file or filed as follow-ups.

N/A.

title: Motion spec: developing value area, recompute and profile transitions
body:
## Context
Profiles move more than any other analysis surface in the product. A live session profile grows on every print; the POC can jump several levels in one trade; the developing value area expands and contracts continuously; visible-range mode rebuilds the entire histogram on every pan; and a period or row-size change replaces the whole dataset at once. Without a deliberate motion spec, each of those becomes either a distracting flicker or an unnoticed silent change — and an unnoticed POC move is a trading error, not a cosmetic one.

`16-design-system-brief.md` §7 defines the motion system and §2.6 the duration/easing tokens. This ticket applies them to the profile surface and, critically, decides where motion must be *suppressed*: high-frequency live updates on a 5 000-row histogram cannot be animated per row within the frame budget.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Surfaces in scope: SCR-038 (profile panel) and SCR-039 (profile settings dialog); components CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge; driven by WS topic `profile.{symbol}.{kind}` and `GET /market/profile`.
- Motion spec covering, for each case: whether motion is used at all, the token (duration + easing), the property animated, and the suppression rule.
  - Live bar growth on the current session profile.
  - POC relocation to a new price level, including a multi-level jump.
  - Developing value-area expansion and contraction (`complete: false`).
  - Session close: developing → final transition when `complete` flips to true.
  - Row-size or value-area-% change (full re-bucket).
  - Period-mode change (session → visible range → composite).
  - Visible-range recompute during and after a pan, including the debounce-on-pan-end settle.
  - Naked-POC demotion when price trades through it (US-VP-006 scenario 2).
  - Panel enter/exit when docking or undocking, and the overlay fade.
- An explicit **suppression matrix**: which motions are disabled under (a) `prefers-reduced-motion`, (b) the degraded connection classes from `23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3 where `profile.*` drops to 1 000 ms cadence, (c) high row counts above the specified threshold, (d) replay fast-forward.
- Prototype clips (dark and light) of the POC relocation and the developing→final transition, since those two carry meaning rather than polish.
- Written rationale per case stating what the motion *communicates*; any motion that communicates nothing is removed rather than kept as decoration.

## Out of scope
- Motion for footprint cells (E18), CVD panes (E23) and chart trading overlays.
- Implementation and any engine-level tweening work.
- Global motion-token changes — this ticket consumes `16-design-system-brief.md` §2.6 tokens and proposes new ones only with a recorded justification.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every listed case has a decision
  When the motion spec is reviewed
  Then each of the nine cases states either a token-backed animation or an explicit no-motion decision with a rationale

Scenario: Reduced motion removes decoration but preserves meaning
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is enabled
  When a POC relocates and the value area finalises
  Then both changes remain perceivable through a non-animated treatment and no meaning is lost

Scenario: Motion is suppressed under load
  Given the profile has more rows than the specified threshold or the connection is in the saturated class
  Then per-row animation is suppressed and the spec states exactly what replaces it

Scenario: A POC jump is not missed
  Given the POC moves several price levels in a single update
  Then the spec defines a treatment that draws attention to the move without obscuring the histogram, demonstrated in a prototype clip

Scenario: Re-bucketing does not read as a data error
  When row size changes and every bar is replaced
  Then the transition is specified such that it reads as a recalculation rather than as the feed breaking

Scenario: Replay fast-forward does not animate
  Given replay is running above normal speed
  Then all profile motion is suppressed and the spec says so explicitly
```

## Technical notes / design
The render path is WebGL (`26-chart-engine-design.md`), so animating N rows means N interpolated vertex updates per frame — the spec must state a row-count threshold above which motion is dropped rather than assuming the renderer will cope. `complete: bool` on `VolumeProfile` is the authoritative trigger for the developing→final transition; `developing_poc` (a POC path over time) is available and may be used for the relocation treatment, but the spec must not require the client to retain history the model does not provide.

Under the `saturated` connection class the `profile.*` topic is throttled to 1 000 ms, which makes per-update animation both pointless and misleading — motion at that cadence implies a smoothness the data does not have. Reuse E17's degraded-feed vocabulary for that state instead of introducing new movement.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification: prototype clips reviewed at Design Review; a walkthrough with a chart-engine engineer confirming the threshold and the suppression rules are implementable within the frame budget; reduced-motion variants reviewed by the accessibility specialist ahead of E19-D06.

## Security notes
No security surface.

## Accessibility notes
`prefers-reduced-motion` handling is a first-class deliverable, not a fallback: every motion that carries meaning has a static equivalent that carries the same meaning. No meaning is conveyed by motion alone. Flashing and rapid oscillation are explicitly checked against the seizure-safety thresholds in `05-accessibility-standard.md`, which matters because a POC oscillating between two tied levels on a fast tape is a realistic input.

## Performance notes
The spec is written against the engine budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: profile motion must not reduce chart interaction below the ≥55 fps floor stated in US-VP-002, and the row-count threshold is chosen so that the worst case (5 000 rows, visible-range mode, live tape) has no per-row animation at all.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Motion spec merged covering all nine cases with token references and rationales.
- [ ] Suppression matrix complete for reduced-motion, degraded-feed, high-row-count and replay-fast-forward.
- [ ] Prototype clips attached for POC relocation and developing→final transition, in both themes.
- [ ] Implementability confirmed by a chart-engine engineer against the frame budget.
- [ ] Reduced-motion variants pre-reviewed by the accessibility specialist.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded on the ticket; Status = Done.**

## Dependencies
- **E19-D03** supplies the visual treatments this spec animates.
- **E05** design system v0 supplies the motion tokens.

title: Accessibility design review of the profile panel and settings dialog
body:
## Context
A volume profile is, structurally, a chart whose entire content is encoded in position and magnitude — the hardest possible case for non-visual access, and one our standard does not let us skip. `05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA across the product, and SCR-038 already commits to a specific remedy: "a table alternative lists each price row with volume, delta, and VA membership; POC/VAH/VAL are announced." CMP-110's catalogue entry commits to a DOM-mirror-per-bar pattern and to conveying POC/value-area status by border/pattern plus text label, never fill colour alone.

This ticket is the formal gate that checks those commitments were actually met across everything E19-D03, E19-D04 and E19-D05 produced, *before* engineering starts in Sprint 10. Finding a structural a11y problem during implementation means rework in a WebGL render path, which is expensive; finding it here means a Figma edit.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Formal review by the accessibility specialist of the complete E19 design set: SCR-038 (both hosting modes), SCR-039, CMP-110, CMP-183, CMP-184, the preset and anchoring flows, and the motion spec.
- Verification of the table-alternative view: its trigger, its reading order, its column set (price, volume, buy, sell, delta, trade count, TPO count, value-area membership), how POC/VAH/VAL are expressed textually, and how it behaves at 5 000 rows.
- Verification of the screen-reader announcement policy: what is announced on POC relocation, on value-area finalisation, on period/preset change, on entering the degraded-feed state, and at what politeness level — with an explicit rule preventing a live session profile from announcing on every print.
- Full keyboard traversal audit: header controls → histogram → legend → table alternative → settings dialog, including the canvas gestures from E19-D04, focus-visible treatment, focus trapping and return-focus in SCR-039.
- Contrast verification of every new `color.profile.*` / `color.tpo.*` token in dark and light themes, plus a colour-blindness simulation pass across all three deficiency types.
- Target-size, spacing and hit-area check on the histogram's interactive rows and the settings controls at all three density modes.
- A written findings list, each item classified blocker / must-fix / should-fix, with owners and target tickets; blockers must be resolved and re-reviewed before sign-off.

## Out of scope
- Automated axe-core CI checks and implementation-time a11y testing — those belong to the engineering stories and to E19-D08.
- Screen-reader testing against a running build — this review is against designs and prototypes; the build-time pass is E19-D08.
- Footprint, CVD and DOM surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The histogram is fully reachable without a mouse
  When the keyboard traversal audit is performed on the prototype
  Then every control, every profile row and the settings dialog are reachable and operable by keyboard with a visible focus indicator at every stop

Scenario: The table alternative carries the same information
  Given a sighted user can identify POC, VAH, VAL, HVN, LVN and naked POCs from the histogram
  Then the table alternative conveys each of those facts in text for the same dataset

Scenario: A live profile does not flood the screen reader
  Given a live session profile updating on every print
  Then the announcement policy is specified such that routine updates are not announced and only meaningful changes such as POC relocation are, at a stated politeness level

Scenario: Colour is never the sole carrier
  When each of the eight encoded meanings is checked
  Then each has a non-colour primary encoding and survives all three colour-blindness simulations

Scenario: A blocker stops sign-off
  Given a finding is classified as a blocker
  Then the ticket cannot reach Done until the fix is made and re-reviewed, and the re-review is recorded on the ticket

Scenario: Compact density does not break target sizes
  Given the panel and dialog at compact density
  Then every interactive target meets the minimum size in 05-accessibility-standard.md or a documented exception with an alternative access path exists
```

## Technical notes / design
The table alternative cannot be a naive 5 000-row DOM table — that is both a performance problem and a navigation problem for a screen-reader user. The review must land on a concrete strategy (virtualised with correct row/column count semantics, or an aggregated view with drill-down, or a bounded window around the current price) and record the decision, because it directly shapes the engineering story. Column semantics should follow `ProfileLevel` in `24-internal-schemas.md` §5.1 so the table is a faithful projection of the model rather than a parallel invention.

The announcement policy interacts with the WS cadence: `profile.*` publishes at up to 1 000 ms and is throttled further under degradation, so a naive live-region binding would produce a continuous stream. Specify a change-detection rule (announce on POC change, value-area finalisation and mode change only) rather than a cadence rule.

## Test plan
Review-based, not automated. Method: a prototype walkthrough with NVDA and with VoiceOver; a keyboard-only traversal recorded as a clip and attached; contrast measured with the design-system tooling; simulations produced for deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia. Findings are logged in the ticket with classification, owner and target ticket; blockers are re-reviewed after fix.

## Security notes
No security surface. The review confirms no account or credential data appears on this market-data panel in any state, including the table alternative and the empty states.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility deliverable. Its output — the announcement policy, the table-alternative strategy, the traversal order and the non-colour encoding confirmation — becomes normative input to the engineering stories and to the design QA in E19-D08. title: Engineering handoff pack for the profile surface (SCR-038/039, CMP-110/183/184)
body:
## Context
E19's frontend stories start in Sprint 10. The design-ahead rule in `00-planning-brief.md` and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires the design to have been Done for ≥2 sprints before those stories can enter Ready, and requires the linked artefact to be complete enough that engineering never has to guess. For a WebGL chart primitive, "complete enough" is a higher bar than for a form: there is no browser inspector to fall back on, so every number — row height, gap, minimum legible bar length, letter cell size, extension-line thickness — has to be in the pack.

This ticket assembles everything produced in E19-D01 … E19-D06 into a single pack the chart-engine and web teams can build from without a designer in the room, and formally hands it over.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Redlines and specs** for SCR-038 (docked and overlay) and SCR-039 in dark and light themes at all three densities: spacing, row height and gap, minimum and maximum bar lengths, label placement and truncation rules, legend composition, dialog section grouping, control sizing.
- **Token map**: every `color.profile.*`, `color.tpo.*`, spacing, radius, typography and motion token used, named exactly as it appears in the Style Dictionary pipeline described in `16-design-system-brief.md` §11 — no raw hex values anywhere in the pack.
- **Component specs** for CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane and CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane, each with: full variant/state matrix, the prop contract as it appears in `15-component-catalogue.md`, the DOM-mirror structure and its accessible names, and the Storybook story list (CMP-110: Volume, Delta, TPO, POC, ValueArea; CMP-183: composite/multiples/visible/personalised; CMP-184: Blocks, Profile, InitialBalanceShaded).
- **State-to-data map**: which field of `VolumeProfile` / `ProfileLevel` / `ProfilePeriod` drives each visual state, so engineering binds to the model rather than to a screenshot — including `complete` → developing/final, `naked_poc_ticks` → carried-forward levels, `hvn_ticks`/`lvn_ticks` → node markers, and the approximated-from-bars condition → CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.
- **Copy deck**: every label, unit, tooltip (including the POC tie-break explanation required by US-VP-004), validation message (VA% 1–100, custom range end after start, row-size clamp), warning ("range longer than recorded history"), partial-history chip text and both empty-state variants.
- **A11y implementation notes** carried forward verbatim from E19-D06: announcement policy, table-alternative strategy, traversal order, focus management in SCR-039.
- **Motion implementation notes** from E19-D05 including the suppression matrix and the row-count threshold.
- **Open-questions register**: anything deliberately left to engineering judgement, stated as such, so nothing is ambiguous by accident.
- A live handover session with the chart-engine and web engineers who will build it, and the QA engineer who will test it.

## Out of scope
- Implementation, Storybook code, and visual-regression baselines — engineering owns those.
- Backend profile computation, the `/market/profile` endpoint and the WS topic — those are separate E19 engineering tickets.
- Post-implementation design QA — E19-D08.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The pack is buildable without a designer
  Given an engineer who has not attended any E19 design review
  When they build CMP-110 from the pack alone
  Then every dimension, token and state they need is present, and any gap they hit is logged as a defect against this ticket

Scenario: No raw values leak into the pack
  When the pack is searched for hex colours or unlabelled pixel values
  Then every visual value is expressed as a design token or as a rule referencing one

Scenario: Every visual state names its data source
  Given the state-to-data map is reviewed
  Then each state cites a specific field of the internal profile model rather than a prose description

Scenario: The copy deck is complete
  Given every message in SCR-038 and SCR-039 including validations, warnings, chips and empty states
  Then each has final approved copy in the deck, and no screen contains lorem or placeholder text

Scenario: Handover actually happened
  Given the design-ahead rule requires sign-off two sprints before Sprint 10
  Then a handover session is recorded with attendees from chart-engine, web and QA, and questions raised are answered in the pack

Scenario: A late change is controlled
  Given a change is requested after this ticket reaches Done
  Then it follows the change-control process in 16-design-system-brief.md section 13.5 rather than being applied silently
```

## Technical notes / design
The pack must be explicit about the split between GPU-rendered content and DOM-mirrored content, because that split determines which specs engineering reads as render instructions and which as markup instructions. Per `15-component-catalogue.md`, CMP-110/183/184 are chart-primitives rendered in the engine, with a per-bar DOM mirror for accessibility only — the pack states for each element which side of that line it falls on.

Data contracts to cite precisely: REST `GET /api/v1/market/profile?symbol&period&from&to` for bootstrap; WS `profile.{symbol}.{kind}` with `kind ∈ {volume, delta, tpo}` and params `split`, `session_anchor`, `price_grouping`, `value_area_pct` for the live tail; `ProfileUpdate` as the payload schema (`23-ws-protocol.md` §14.6). The degraded-cadence behaviour under the `saturated` class (§8.3) is part of the spec, not an edge case.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification: a dry-run where an engineer who did not attend the design reviews builds one variant of CMP-110 from the pack alone and logs every gap; gaps are closed before sign-off. QA confirms the copy deck and state matrix are sufficient to write the black-box test plan from.

## Security notes
The pack contains no credentials and no real account data; all example data is fixture market data. It is stored in the design drive and linked from the ticket rather than pasted into the repo, per the documentation policy.

## Accessibility notes
The a11y implementation notes are carried into the pack verbatim from E19-D06 and marked non-negotiable: announcement policy, table-alternative strategy, traversal order, focus management, target sizes. Engineering acceptance of these notes is part of the handover record, so there is no later ambiguity about whether they were optional.

## Performance notes
The pack restates the binding budgets so they are visible at implementation time rather than at review time: 5 000 rows maximum (SCR-038), re-bucket in a worker ≤300 ms for a session-length profile (SCR-039), recompute on zoom debounced to 100 ms, visible-range recompute ≤10 Hz and interaction ≥55 fps (US-VP-002), full 24 h session rebuild ≤1 s (US-VP-001), composite over 30 sessions from the cold tier ≤2 s (US-VP-003).

## Observability
The pack lists the analytics events with their exact payloads: `profile.period_changed`, `profile.mode_changed`, `profile.va_percent_changed`, `profile.settings_changed` with `{key}` — so instrumentation ships with the feature rather than after it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Pack published and linked from the SCR-038 and SCR-039 entries in `14-screens-catalogue.md` and from the CMP-110/183/184 entries in `15-component-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] Redlines, token map, component specs, state-to-data map, copy deck, a11y notes and motion notes all present.
