title: Hi-fi SCR-051 settings dialog and the SCR-153 depth-shed banner variant
body:
## Context
Everything the user can tune about this surface lives in SCR-051 (tabs: Depth & scale · Colour · Ladder · Trading · Detectors), and every automatic reduction the app makes must be explained through the SCR-153 degraded-mode banner. US-DOM-005's NFR is explicit: "never silently degrade without telling the user". These two surfaces are therefore one design problem: what the user *chooses* and what the system *overrides*, and how the override is shown as temporary and reversible.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi SCR-051 exactly per the catalogue layout: depth tier 50/200/500, colour scale log/linear + gamma, trail length (5–600 s) with decay mode, palette (bid/ask swatches + CVD-safe set), row height 10–40 px, centre lock/auto-follow, show-toggles (own orders, position, prints, cumulative depth, queue est. with `(estimated)`), qty presets, confirm-market-in-LIVE, detector toggles + sensitivity.
- The **live preview tile** (CMP-228) on real sample data, and the **bandwidth/CPU cost warning** for higher depth tiers with the measured figure shown (checklist item).
- Validation and error states: trail out of range, row height out of range, "at least one qty preset", and the memory-guard clamp message from US-DOM-004 ("the maximum for the current depth tier").
- The SCR-153 banner variant for depth shedding: what still works, what was reduced, why, and how to pin the tier back.
- A 'preview with colour-vision simulation' toggle in the colour tab.
- `docs/design/specs/scr-051.md` summary + redlines.

## Out of scope
- SCR-050 itself (E21-D02); detector algorithm copy (E25); the other SCR-153 variants (exchange WS down, recorder down, rule engine down) which belong to E45/E16/E35.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Settings sign-off checklist satisfied
  When the reviewer runs the SCR-051 design sign-off acceptance checklist
  Then depth tier, row aggregation, trail length, intensity curve, colour theme, big-order threshold,
  tape-print overlay and click-trade behaviour are all drawn, with live preview, cost warning and reset-to-defaults

Scenario: Shedding is explained, not hidden
  Given the app has auto-reduced the depth tier
  Then the banner names the cause, names what was lost, offers "pin tier", and reads correctly in greyscale

Scenario: Resubscribe cost is disclosed
  When the depth tier is changed
  Then the dialog states that the book resubscribes and shows the 1-2 s rebuild state rather than appearing frozen
```

## Technical notes / design
Depth-tier change re-negotiates `book.{symbol}.{depth}` and triggers a fresh snapshot (`23-ws-protocol.md` §5.4 `resnapshot: true`); colour changes are shader uniform updates (≤1 frame) and must **not** drop the historized frame buffer — the design must not imply a reload for colour changes.

## Test plan
E21-D08 design QA; axe on the built dialog in E21-Q05.

## Security notes
The "confirm market orders in LIVE" control is a safety setting: its default (on) and its LIVE-vs-DEMO behaviour must be drawn unambiguously even though the trading path ships in E31.

## Accessibility notes
All controls are labelled form fields with units; the colour-scale editor exposes numeric stops as text inputs alongside the gradient widget; the banner is `role="status"` naming the degraded capability in plain sentences.

## Performance notes
The preview tile must be cheap: static sample frames, not a live subscription.

## Observability
Annotate `dom.settings_changed {key}` and `dom.depth_tier_changed` surfaces.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass with an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Coverage: ≥85% line on touched backend/engine packages, ≥80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.

title: Motion and reduced-motion spec for the trail, re-centring and resync states
body:
## Context
Three motions on this panel can either help or actively harm a trader: the heatmap trail advancing every 100 ms, the ladder re-centring when price nears the edge, and the transition into/out of "resynchronising". US-DOM-001 requires re-centring "without jitter on every tick"; US-DOM-002 and US-DOM-004 require reduced-motion modes that disable fade animation and use a static decay mode; US-DOM-003 requires colour rescale that is "smooth (no flashing)".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion spec in `docs/design/specs/e21-motion.md`: trail advance (continuous scroll vs discrete column step, and the crossover rule by column pixel width), re-centre easing/threshold/hysteresis, colour-scale rescale interpolation duration, resync enter/exit transition, depth-shed notice entry.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for each: static trail (no fade), instantaneous re-centre, instant rescale, no notice slide.
- Hysteresis numbers for re-centring (trigger band, target position, minimum interval) expressed so engineering can implement them directly.

## Out of scope
Generic app motion tokens (E05); trading-action motion (E31).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Re-centring does not jitter
  Given price oscillates across the re-centre trigger band
  Then the spec's hysteresis and minimum-interval rules prevent more than one re-centre per the stated interval

Scenario: Reduced motion is complete
  When prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then every one of the five motions has a defined non-animated equivalent that loses no information

Scenario: Rescale never flashes
  Given the adaptive colour scale rebounds after a liquidity collapse
  Then the spec defines an interpolation that avoids a full-panel luminance jump between frames
```

## Technical notes / design
Trail advance is a texture-space operation (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8) — the spec must express motion in terms of column steps and sampling offset, not CSS transitions, or it cannot be implemented.

## Test plan
Verified in E21-Q05 (a11y audit includes a reduced-motion pass) and by an engine golden-image comparison at reduced motion.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions) and the reduced-motion coverage required by `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
Any motion that requires a full-texture re-upload per frame is rejected — it would break budget #14.

## Observability
N/A.

title: Accessibility design review of the ladder grid and windowed heatmap reveal
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` names the WebGL surfaces as the highest a11y risk in the product and mandates all three layers (DOM mirror, windowed accessibility tree, data-table alternative) — no "either/or". The DOM ladder is additionally called out twice: as an explicitly non-relaxed dense surface (§1) and as the motivating example for roving tabindex (§4.2, "this prevents 200+ Tab presses to cross a DOM ladder"). This review signs off the accessible design *before* build, so the grid model is not retrofitted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Reviewed and annotated: landmark structure (Chart / DOM+Heatmap regions, `Ctrl+\` region cycling), roving-tabindex model for the ladder grid, `Enter` row action menu, `+`/`-` price-step shadowing rule (§3 precedence note), target sizes at all three densities.
- The **windowed heatmap reveal** path signed off end to end: focus a ladder row → documented key → "liquidity history at this level" sparkline+table (§6.2).
- The **DOM ladder table alternative** (§6.3, one row per price level up to 200-depth) confirmed as equal-status, including its live-patch behaviour (patch in place at the throttled cadence, preserve focus/sort) and the "no longer in view" banner.
- Live-region policy for this panel: what is announced, at what throttle, and what is deliberately silent (the trail must not flood).
- Colour-independence audit of every encoding on the panel.
- Findings logged as blocking or non-blocking against E21-D02/D03/D04 before their sign-off.

## Out of scope
Implementation (E21-S01/S02); the R5 full conformance audit (E47).

```gherkin
Scenario: All three a11y layers present in the design
  Then the DOM mirror, the windowed reveal and the table alternative are each specified for this panel, with the key bindings that reach them

Scenario: No live-region flooding
  Given the heatmap advances every 100 ms
  Then the design specifies a throttled ambient announcement (default 1 per 2 s, user-configurable) and never announces per column

Scenario: Blocking finding

  Then E21-D02 cannot be signed off until it is fixed
```

Announcement string for a focused row is fixed by the catalogue: "64 100, ask 42, own order 0.1 working". The reveal key must not collide with the chart's data-cursor bindings (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 precedence rules).

N/A.

title: Wireframe SCR-053 tape + bubble panel with all states
body:
## Context
SCR-053 "Tape / Time & Sales + big-trade bubbles panel" is defined in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` as a panel with two linked views — a scrolling print tape and an optional bubble overlay on the chart. Its catalogue entry already fixes the data source (WS `trades.{symbol}`, percentile thresholds from `GET /api/v1/market/metrics`), the interactions (click a print → crosshair jumps to that timestamp on synced charts; `Ctrl+F` filter; pause on hover; `P` pause/resume) and the four states (streaming · paused · filtered-empty · disconnected). This ticket turns that into low-fidelity wireframes that resolve layout, density and control placement, using the defaults recommended by E22-D01.

## Scope / Deliverables

- All states drawn: streaming; paused with the chip "Paused — 412 prints buffered"; filtered-empty with "No prints above 10 000 USDT in the last 5 min" plus a clear-filter action; disconnected/stale; **partial history** (global AC #7 — naming the first available recorded timestamp); **over-threshold warning** (US-BIG-002 scenario 3: >20% of prints flagged → suggest raising the threshold, highlighting capped).
- Size-tier treatment sketched with **weight/glyph as well as colour** (global AC #3).
- Clustering affordance: the `(estimated)` badge (CMP-227) placement and the tooltip listing constituent count, window and tolerance (US-BIG-004).
- Keyboard map annotated on the frames: `P`, `Ctrl+F`, row focus, `Alt+↑/↓` column reorder.

## Out of scope
Hi-fi visual design and tokens (D03); motion (D04); the alert-editor big-trade condition on SCR-091 (parked with E22-S06); speed-of-tape (E25).

```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued state is drawn

Scenario: Density is resolved with evidence

Scenario: No colour-only meaning

```

## Technical notes / design
Respect the performance constraint from the catalogue entry — "virtualised list, ≤60 rows in the DOM, ring buffer of 10 000 prints; bubble layer is part of the chart engine, not DOM" — so the wireframe must not require a design that implies unbounded DOM rows (e.g. sticky group headers per second would multiply rows; if wanted, spec them as overlay chrome).

## Test plan
Design review with the chart-engine lead (feasibility of the bubble legend inside the WebGL scene vs DOM chrome) and with QA (are the states testable as drawn).

N/A — public market data only.

Annotate the tape container as `role="log"` with `aria-live="off"` by default and an opt-in polite announcement restricted to whale prints; mark every row as individually focusable; specify visible focus treatment and ≥24×24 px targets for chips and the pause control.

## Performance notes
Wireframes must be compatible with ≥55 fps at 2 000 prints/s and the coalescing-factor indicator required by US-BIG-001.

Annotate where the `tape.filter_changed`, `tape.paused`, `tape.resumed`, `tape.print_clicked` analytics events fire.

- CMP-112 design-system entry: the four shapes, the notional→radius mapping curves for `linear` and `sizeScale: "log"`, alpha-by-age treatment (per `26-chart-engine-design.md`, bubbles fade with age), buy/sell encoding by **shape and colour** (US-BIG-003 requires both), the count badge used when the LOD ladder collapses a cluster into one bubble, and the hover/focus detail tooltip.
- Size-to-notional legend spec for the chart overlay, including the statement of which scale is active (US-BIG-003 scenario 2: "the legend states the scale").
- Colour-blind verification of the buy/sell pair under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia simulation.

## Out of scope
Motion timings (D04), engineering implementation (S01/S03), the tape's data plumbing.

```gherkin
Scenario: CMP-112 is fully specified
  Then the entry documents all four shapes, both size scales with their radius curves, the alpha-by-age treatment, the cluster count badge, and the hover/focus tooltip content

Scenario: Colour-blind safe
  Given the buy and sell bubble treatments
  When simulated under deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia
  Then the two remain distinguishable by shape independent of hue
```

## Technical notes / design
Radius mapping must be bounded: define `r_min`, `r_max` in px and the curve (`linear`: `r = r_min + k*notional` clamped; `log`: `r = r_min + k*ln(1 + notional/n0)`) so the engine implementation in E22-S03 is a transcription, not a reinvention. Specify the exact LOD behaviour the design expects when >500 instances are visible (per `26-chart-engine-design.md`: raise the size threshold, collapse to a single bubble with a count badge).

## Test plan
Design review + a Storybook parity checklist that E22-S03 will satisfy (Circle, Square, Diamond, TextMode, LogScale).

N/A.

## Accessibility notes
Contrast ≥4.5:1 for all tape text and ≥3:1 for the bubble outline against the chart background in both themes; the CMP-112 DOM-mirror `aria-label` format is fixed here as "Big {side}, {notional} USDT, {price}, {time}" per the catalogue; the `(estimated)` badge accessible name must contain the literal word "estimated".

## Performance notes
The spec must be renderable as instanced SDF discs in a single draw call — no per-bubble drop shadows, gradients with per-instance stops, or text that cannot come from the SDF glyph atlas.

N/A.

Comps and CMP-112 entry merged; CDO sign-off recorded; `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-112 entry updated if the shipped spec diverges from the sketch; tokens contributed; Storybook story list agreed with frontend.

title: Wireframe to hi-fi SCR-097 replay page: transport, coverage scrubber, states
body:
## Context
SCR-097 (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §7) is the primary surface of this epic and the one screen where a visual mistake has a trading consequence: its sign-off checklist opens with "REPLAY chrome cannot be confused with live". The page hosts the same dockable panel set as the terminal, fed by the replay clock, plus a transport bar; everything else the trader sees is an existing order-flow panel rendering replay frames through the identical pipeline (`23-ws-protocol.md` G6).

Delivered in design sprint D-S08 ("Replay UI, alerts UI", `30-release-roadmap.md` §1.2) so it is Done at least two sprints before the consuming frontend story E26-S02 in Sprint 11.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframe then hi-fi Figma frames for **SCR-097** at all supported densities and in both themes, matching the catalogue wireframe: header line (`REPLAY  <SYMBOL>  <timestamp to ms>  speed Nx`), the panel region, the transport row (`|<<  <  [PLAY]  >  >>|`), the speed picker, the scrub track with a time axis, and the option row (`[x] paper fills  [ ] keep live panes  bookmarks: #42 #43`).
- The **REPLAY chrome variant**: border treatment, clock typography (monospace, ms precision), badge placement on every replaying pane, and the visual relationship to the demo/live environment badge so the two never read as one thing.
- The **coverage scrubber**: recorded / partial / missing shading on the track, bookmark markers, the playhead, and the drag-seek affordance including the "seeking" state.
- Every state from the catalogue: configuring, buffering, playing, paused, seeking, **gap encountered** ("No data 13:52-13:55 - recorder was offline. [Skip gap] [Stop here]"), end of range, paper-fill mode active, session expired (server reclaims after 2 h idle, with a resume option).
- The **speed-limit honesty state**: when the engine cannot sustain the requested rate it must show the achieved rate rather than silently dropping (US-RPL-002 performance scenario), and speeds above 25x must visibly disable paper fills with the reason.
- The hotkey overlay contribution for the Replay context group in SCR-030 (`Space`, `<-/->`, `Shift+<-/->`, `Ctrl+<-/->`, `R`, `B`, `[`/`]`).
- Redlines: spacing, tokens, type ramp, focus rings, hit targets for the transport buttons and the scrub thumb.

## Out of scope
- SCR-098 (E26-D03) and SCR-099 (E26-D04).
- The CMP-170/171/172 design-system entries themselves (E26-D05) — this ticket specifies usage in context and hands the component contract to D05.
- Motion specification and the a11y design review (E26-D06).
- Order-flow panel design — already owned by E18/E19/E20/E21/E22/E23/E24; replay renders them unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Replay chrome passes the two-second test
  Given the hi-fi frames for playing replay and for the live terminal
  When five reviewers are shown each for two seconds
  Then all five correctly identify which is replay
  And the identification does not depend on colour alone

Scenario: Every catalogue state is drawn
  Given the SCR-097 states list in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the frame set is reviewed against it
  Then configuring, buffering, playing, paused, seeking, gap-encountered, end-of-range, paper-fill-active and session-expired each have a frame
  And the gap state shows the exact missing range with Skip gap and Stop here actions

Scenario: The scrubber tells the truth about coverage
  Given a window with a 3-minute recorder gap and a partially covered tail
  When the scrub track is rendered
  Then recorded, partial and missing segments are distinguishable without colour alone
  And the earliest available timestamp is stated in text

Scenario: Seeking is designed as a real cost
  Given the seek budget is 1 s p95 with a 2 s ceiling
  When the seeking state is drawn
  Then it shows determinate or explained progress rather than an unbounded spinner
```

## Technical notes / design
Data bindings to design against: `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions` returns `{ id, state, symbols, from, to, cursor_ts, speed, streams, depth, paper_account_id, progress_pct }`; `state` is the Postgres `replay_state` enum `created|buffering|playing|paused|finished|error` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4), and the frames must map 1:1 to those values plus the client-only `seeking` condition. Playback control is `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}/control` with actions `play|pause|seek|step` (`step` carries exactly one of `step_events` or `step_ms`). Coverage shading comes from `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage?symbol`.

## Test plan
Design validation only: prototype walkthrough of start -> play -> scrub -> hit gap -> bookmark -> end of range -> resume. Discrepancies against the built screen are caught by E26-D08 design QA and E26-Q05 a11y audit.

## Security notes
The frames must never show a real account identifier or balance. The paper-fill option must be drawn so that "simulated" is structurally unmissable — this is the visual half of the isolation invariant enforced technically in E26-S07 and reviewed in E26-X03.

## Accessibility notes
Specify: the clock as a labelled live region updated at most 1 Hz (not per frame); the scrub track as `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` in absolute time; visible focus on every transport control; a text equivalent for coverage shading; contrast >=4.5:1 for the REPLAY chrome text and >=3:1 for its non-text indicator, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Formal review is E26-D06.

## Performance notes
Design the transport for a clock that updates at most 1 Hz for assistive tech while the visual readout may update per frame; avoid per-frame layout thrash in the scrub track by specifying a fixed-width monospace timestamp field.

## Observability
Annotate the frames with the analytics events they emit: `replay.started`, `replay.seek`, `replay.paper_fill`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma frames published, versioned and linked on this ticket; redlines complete.
- [ ] Every state in the SCR-097 catalogue entry has a frame; the catalogue entry updated if a state was added or renamed during design.
- [ ] The SCR-097 design sign-off acceptance checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md` is fully satisfied and ticked with evidence.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded; Status Done at least two sprints before E26-S02 starts.
- [ ] Handoff notes captured for E26-D07.

## Dependencies
`E26-D01` supplies the validated replay-mode signalling treatment and the canonical speed-preset list.

## Branch
`design/replay-scr097` (Figma + catalogue doc updates only).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#23-rpl--replay` — US-RPL-001 .. US-RPL-009

title: Hi-fi SCR-098 replay setup modal with coverage timeline and honest preparation
body:
## Context
SCR-098 is where the recorder-dependency becomes visible to the trader: a replay session can only exist over a window the recorder actually covered. `14-screens-catalogue.md` §global rule 3 requires recorder-dependent emptiness to be a *designed state* naming the first available timestamp, never a blank canvas, and the SCR-098 validation rules require "Nothing is recorded for that window." rather than a generic error. US-RPL-001's third scenario goes further: when the chosen start precedes available data, **the earliest available timestamp is offered instead, with the reason stated** — an offer, not a rejection.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma for **SCR-098** (modal): symbol multiselect (CMP-219 SymbolPicker), date/time range with the coverage timeline (CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker, CMP-047 DateRangePicker), starting speed (CMP-171), panel-inclusion checklist, paper-trading toggle with starting balance and account selection, and the "start from a journal trade / alert / rule firing" shortcuts.
- The **coverage timeline** presentation: recorded, partial and missing windows on one track, with the total recorded depth stated in text ("History starts 2026-09-01 - recording began then").
- States: coverage loading, no coverage (CMP-026 EmptyState with a route to the recorder screen SCR-140 for owners and an explanatory read-only message otherwise), partial coverage warning, validation error (CMP-027).
- **Preparation progress**: a 1-day single-symbol session must be ready in <=10 s with progress shown; larger requests must state the estimated preparation time *before* starting, with a cancel affordance.
- The resume path for US-RPL-009: an existing saved session for this symbol is offered ("Resume 2026-09-10 13:00 at 13:38, speed 4x") alongside "Start fresh", plus the data-changed variant ("the underlying data was pruned since - nearest available start is X").
- The paper-trading copy: "Paper trading only - nothing reaches the exchange."
- Redlines and the full form validation message set.

## Out of scope
- SCR-097 (E26-D02), SCR-099 (E26-D04), the CMP design-system entries (E26-D05).
- The recorder admin screens SCR-140/141/142 (E16).
- Journal/alert/rule entry points' own surfaces — this ticket designs only the inbound shortcut in the modal.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A window with no coverage is refused helpfully
  Given the user picks a range that does not intersect any recorded coverage
  When validation runs
  Then the modal states that nothing is recorded for that window
  And it names the nearest recorded range and offers to use it

Scenario: A start before available history becomes an offer
  Given the chosen start precedes the earliest recorded timestamp
  When the user attempts to continue
  Then the earliest available timestamp is offered as a substitute with the reason stated
  And the user can accept it in one action

Scenario: Preparation cost is stated, not discovered
  Given a request spanning three symbols over a full day
  When the user submits
  Then the estimated preparation time is shown before preparation starts
  And a cancel control is available throughout

Scenario: Resuming a pruned session is explained
  Given a saved replay position whose underlying data has since been pruned
  When the modal opens
  Then it states what changed and offers the nearest available start point
```

## Technical notes / design
Bindings: `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage?symbol` for the timeline; `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions` with `{ symbols, from, to, speed, streams, depth, paper_account_id, autostart }`; a window lacking coverage is rejected server-side with `no_data_recorded` (422), so the modal must pre-empt that error rather than surface it raw. `speed` is constrained 0.1-100 by `rps_speed`; `range_end > range_start` by `rps_range`; `paper_trading = false OR paper_account_id IS NOT NULL` by `rps_paper` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4) — each constraint needs a human-language message, not a constraint name.

## Test plan
Prototype walkthrough: no coverage, partial coverage, start-before-history, resume-existing, resume-after-prune, paper toggle without an account selected. Verified against the built screen in E26-D08.

## Security notes
The paper-account selector must only list accounts the caller has been granted (`04-security-program.md` RBAC scope `granted_accounts`); the design must not imply the user can replay another user's sessions (`replay:read` is scoped `self`). No filesystem path input appears anywhere in this modal — datasets are addressed by symbol and time range only (SR-097).

## Accessibility notes
A standard labelled form: date-time range, symbol multiselect, speed, paper account. The available-history statement is text adjacent to the range field, not a tooltip. Validation errors name their field and are associated via `aria-describedby`. The coverage timeline needs a text alternative listing recorded ranges. Formal review in E26-D06.

## Performance notes
Coverage data must be fetched once per symbol selection and cached for the modal's lifetime; the design must not imply a fetch per drag frame on the range control.

## Observability
Annotate `replay.session_created {range, symbols, speed}` and `replay.session_deleted`.

- [ ] Figma frames published with redlines; every catalogue state drawn.
- [ ] The SCR-098 design sign-off checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md` fully satisfied with evidence.
- [ ] All server-side validation failures have a designed human-language message.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded; Done >=2 sprints before E26-S01.

`E26-D02` fixes the shared visual language (chrome, coverage shading, speed picker) this modal inherits.

title: Hi-fi SCR-099 replay paper-trading results with simulated framing throughout
body:
## Context
SCR-099 shows the outcome of rehearsing execution inside replay (US-RPL-006). It is the single highest-risk screen in the epic for **honesty**, because it presents P&L numbers that are entirely modelled. `14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-099 requires the simulated framing on every figure, the fill-model assumptions stated explicitly (queue position, latency, slippage model), and the caveat that these results are not a backtest guarantee. Risk R12 (backtest bias) and the product's advice-boundary stance (R9) both land here.

`24-internal-schemas.md` §12 defines the modelled behaviour these assumptions must describe: the L2-aware fill model walks the reconstructed book with a default 80 ms latency penalty, limit orders fill when prints cross the level *and* the estimated queue position is consumed, and a market order can be rejected with `INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` when the book is exhausted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma for **SCR-099** (end-of-session drawer): simulated fill list, P&L, R distribution, the equity curve (CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart), the summary stats card (CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard), the P&L badge (CMP-116 PnLBadge), the export bar (CMP-099 PrintExportBar) and the results table (CMP-049 Table).
- The **assumptions block**: latency model and its value, slippage model, queue-position assumption, and the book source (replayed recorded depth at the configured tier), each in plain language with the configured value shown rather than described generically.
- The **simulated framing**: the badge lives in the heading, not only as a chip (catalogue a11y requirement); every figure carries the framing; the "these results are not a backtest guarantee" caveat is non-dismissible.
- The **promote-to-journal** flow: saving writes journal entries flagged `simulated=true`, excluded from live analytics by default, with the confirmation copy making the exclusion explicit.
- The **opt-in comparison** against the same period's real trades, drawn as clearly separated and off by default.
- Empty state (no simulated fills in the session) and error state (results computation failed).

## Out of scope
- The paper matcher's fill model itself (E38) — this ticket only *presents* its assumptions.
- Journal and analytics screens (E41); SCR-099 links into them.
- SCR-097 and SCR-098.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No figure appears without its framing
  Given the results drawer with a positive simulated P&L
  When any numeric figure is reviewed
  Then it is within a region whose heading carries the simulated framing
  And the non-dismissible caveat is present in the drawer

Scenario: Assumptions are concrete
  Given the session ran with the default 80 ms latency penalty and the L2-aware fill model
  When the assumptions block is rendered
  Then the actual configured latency value and model name are shown, not a generic description

Scenario: Promoting to the journal states the consequence
  Given the user chooses to save the session to the journal
  When the confirmation appears
  Then it states that entries are flagged simulated and excluded from live analytics by default

Scenario: Real-trade comparison cannot be mistaken for the simulated result
  Given the opt-in comparison is enabled
  Then simulated and real series are visually and textually separated, and distinguishable without colour alone
```

## Technical notes / design
Results are computed server-side at session end and fetched once; no live subscriptions remain open (catalogue performance note). Charts must each have a table alternative. `is_paper`/`simulated=true` is the persisted marker (`24-internal-schemas.md` §2: `ExecutionMode` is internal, `is_paper` is what is persisted and published), and the environment stays its real value (`demo`, or `live` when replaying live-recorded data) because environment and paper-ness are orthogonal — the design must not collapse them into a single "replay environment" label.

## Test plan
Prototype walkthrough: profitable session, losing session, zero-fill session, rejected-for-liquidity fill present, promote-to-journal, enable comparison. Built-screen verification in E26-D08.

## Security notes
The promote-to-journal action is audited as `journal.simulated_import`; the design must show that it is a recorded action. Simulated results must never be exportable in a form that omits the simulated flag — the export bar's output format is specified to include it.

## Accessibility notes
Results are a table plus a summary description list; every chart has a table alternative; the simulated badge is in the heading so screen-reader users meet it before the numbers. Contrast and focus per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Formal review in E26-D06.

## Performance notes
Single fetch at session end; the drawer must render within the standard panel-open budget with up to 500 simulated fills, with virtualisation specified beyond that.

## Observability
`replay.results_viewed`, `replay.results_exported`, `replay.results_promoted_to_journal` (writes journal entries flagged `simulated=true`, audited as `journal.simulated_import`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma frames published with redlines; all states drawn.
- [ ] The SCR-099 design sign-off checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md` fully satisfied with evidence.
- [ ] Assumption copy reviewed and approved by the E38 paper-trading lead for factual accuracy.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded.

`E26-D02` for the shared replay visual language.

## Context
The three replay components are new design-system entries, not one-off screen parts: DoR for any Story with UI requires that "component(s) used are in `15-component-catalogue.md`; any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off" (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1). CMP-170 is an organism whose keyboard contract *is* the replay hotkey table, so it must be specified once and reused rather than reimplemented per screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-170 ReplayScrubber** (organism, trading/chart-adjacent): all variants from the catalogue Storybook list — Paused, Playing, HighSpeed, WithBookmarks, KeyboardControlDemo — plus the states D02 introduced: Seeking, GapAhead, EndOfRange, SessionExpired. Props contract per the catalogue API sketch: `currentTime`, `range {from,to}`, `speed`, `playing`, `bookmarks?`, `onPlayPause`, `onSpeedChange`, `onScrub(time)`, `onStepBar(dir)`, `onStepTick(dir)`, `onJumpToRealtime`. Specify the coverage-shading extension needed by SCR-097 and write the prop back into the catalogue.
- **CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker** (molecule): the canonical preset list decided in E26-D01, the custom-value affordance required by US-RPL-004 ("plus a custom value"), and the disabled-with-reason treatment for speeds above 25x when paper fills are on.
- **CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker** (molecule): Default, PartialAvailability and NoRecordedHistory(EmptyState) variants, with the recorder-availability shading rule ("only recorded ranges are selectable").
- Token usage: `color.action.primary` and `font.mono` for the timestamp/speed readout per the catalogue entries; specify the coverage-state tokens (recorded / partial / missing) as design-system additions rather than local colours.
- Storybook story list and the keyboard table for CMP-170 documenting `Space` play/pause, `<-/->` step bar, `Shift+<-/->` step tick, `Ctrl+<-/->` jump 1 minute, `R` jump to real time, `B` bookmark, `[`/`]` previous/next bookmark.
- Updates to `15-component-catalogue.md` for every contract change made here.

## Out of scope
- Implementation of the components (E26-S02 builds them against this spec).
- Screen composition (D02/D03/D04).
- Motion curves and reduced-motion behaviour (E26-D06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The scrubber contract covers every consumer
  Given SCR-097 needs coverage shading and SCR-098 needs range selection
  When the CMP-170 and CMP-172 contracts are reviewed
  Then each required capability maps to a named prop or documented variant
  And no screen needs a local fork of the component

Scenario: The hotkey table is single-sourced
  Given the SCR-097 hotkeys in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the CMP-170 Storybook keyboard table is reviewed
  Then it matches the screen catalogue exactly
  And any divergence is resolved in the catalogue, not in the component

Scenario: Speed presets are canonical
  Given the decision recorded in E26-D01
  When CMP-171 is specified
  Then its preset list matches the decision and 15-component-catalogue.md is updated to match
```

## Technical notes / design
The scrub thumb must meet the minimum pointer target size and the track must remain operable at the smallest supported density; specify the hit-area expansion rather than relying on the visual track height. `aria-valuetext` shows the human-readable timestamp, not a raw epoch number (catalogue a11y requirement).

## Test plan
Design-system review board sign-off; Storybook story list agreed with the frontend lead so E26-S02 can implement against it. Component unit/visual/axe/keyboard/performance tests are listed in the catalogue entries and are implemented with the components.

## Security notes
N/A — presentational components with no privileged data. They must not embed account identifiers in accessible names.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-170: transport controls are standard labelled buttons; the scrub bar is `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext`; the full hotkey table is documented. CMP-172: availability shading requires a non-colour carrier and a text summary of available ranges. All three: visible focus, 4.5:1 text contrast, 3:1 non-text contrast.

## Performance notes
Specify that the scrubber's timestamp readout uses a fixed-width monospace field so a per-frame update causes no reflow, and that scrub drag is throttled to one seek request per settle rather than per pointer move.

N/A.

title: Motion spec and accessibility design review for the replay transport and chrome
body:
## Context
Replay is the one surface where motion is the content: the playhead moves, the clock ticks, panes animate at up to 100x. Unreviewed, that becomes both an accessibility hazard (vestibular triggers, a live region that fires hundreds of times a second) and a performance hazard (per-frame DOM updates competing with the WebGL frame budget). `05-accessibility-standard.md` mandates WCAG 2.2 AA with reduced-motion respect; `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-097 caps the clock live region at 1 Hz.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion spec** for: playhead advance, scrub drag and settle, the seeking state, the play/pause state change, bookmark marker appearance, gap-encountered attention, and the REPLAY chrome entry/exit when a session starts and ends. Durations, easings and the exact `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback for each (which reduce to instant, which reduce to a cross-fade).
- The **speed-dependent motion rule**: above a stated multiplier, decorative motion is suppressed entirely so that frame budget is spent on the chart, not on chrome animation.
- **Accessibility design review** of SCR-097, SCR-098, SCR-099 and CMP-170/171/172 covering: focus order through the transport and back to the panel region, visible focus on the scrub thumb, the 1 Hz clock live region and its politeness level, `aria-valuetext` wording, the non-colour carrier for coverage shading and for REPLAY state, contrast measurements for the chrome, hit-target sizes, and the keyboard path for every action reachable by pointer (step, seek, bookmark, jump to real time, skip gap).
- A written review record listing each finding with a disposition (fixed in design / accepted / deferred to E26-Q05 with rationale).
- The reduced-motion and high-contrast variants of the REPLAY chrome.

## Out of scope
- The automated axe-core audit of the built screens (E26-Q05).
- Design QA of the built implementation (E26-D08).
- Chart-engine internal motion (E11).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every animation has a reduced-motion answer
  Given the motion spec
  When each specified animation is reviewed
  Then each has an explicit prefers-reduced-motion behaviour
  And no animation's reduced form removes information the user needs

Scenario: The clock does not flood assistive technology
  Given the replay clock updating visually per frame
  When the a11y review examines the live region
  Then the announced region is capped at 1 Hz and uses a polite politeness level
  And the visual readout is decoupled from the announced one

Scenario: Everything reachable by pointer is reachable by keyboard
  Given the SCR-097 interaction inventory
  When the keyboard path is walked
  Then play/pause, step bar, step tick, jump, seek, bookmark, skip gap and jump-to-real-time are all reachable
  And focus never becomes trapped in the scrub control

Scenario: Contrast holds in both themes and in high contrast
  Given the REPLAY chrome in light, dark and high-contrast themes
  Then chrome text meets 4.5:1 and the non-text indicator meets 3:1 in every theme
```

## Technical notes / design
The scrub slider should follow the standard slider keyboard model (arrows step, Home/End jump to range bounds, PageUp/PageDown for coarse movement) while the global replay hotkeys (`<-/->` step bar) apply when focus is outside the slider; this collision must be resolved explicitly in the spec so implementation does not invent a rule.

## Test plan
Review executed against a clickable prototype with a screen reader (NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS) and with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` forced. Findings recorded with severity; blocking findings must be resolved before D07 handoff.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility deliverable for the design phase of E26; its record is the evidence cited in the epic DoD's a11y line alongside the E26-Q05 audit.

## Performance notes
The motion spec must be authored against budget #2 — chrome animation is explicitly subordinate to the chart frame budget, and the spec states the suppression threshold rather than leaving it to implementation.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Motion spec merged into `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` motion section (or its replay appendix) and linked here.
- [ ] Accessibility review record published with every finding dispositioned.
- [ ] All blocking findings resolved in the D02/D03/D04/D05 artefacts before handoff.
- [ ] Accessibility specialist and CDO sign-off recorded.

## Context
The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1) means no frontend replay story may start until its design is Status=Done and has been Done for >=2 sprints. ## Scope / Deliverables

- An explicit **state-to-API map** so implementers do not have to derive it: each visual state mapped to the `replay_state` value and/or client condition that produces it, and each control mapped to its `POST /replay/sessions/{replayId}/control` action and payload.
- A list of **design decisions that are load-bearing** and must not be changed without returning to design: the REPLAY chrome treatment, the simulated framing placement, the coverage shading carriers, the 1 Hz clock cap.
- A recorded handoff session with the frontend implementers and the E26 tech lead; open questions raised there are answered in the pack before sign-off.
- The design-QA checklist that E26-D08 will execute, derived from the sign-off checklists in the three screen catalogue entries.

## Out of scope
- New design exploration (D02-D05) and the review itself (D06).
- Executing design QA (D08).

```gherkin
  Given the handoff pack
  When a frontend engineer who did not attend the design work reads it

  And any question they do raise is added to the pack before sign-off

Scenario: Design-ahead is satisfied
  Given the E26 frontend stories are scheduled for Sprint 11 and later
  When this ticket reaches Done

```

## Technical notes / design
The state-to-API map must cover at minimum: `created`/`buffering` -> configuring/buffering frames; `playing`/`paused` -> transport states; `finished` -> end-of-range plus the WS `revoked` with `reason: "replay_session_ended"`; `error` -> the error state with `error_message`; client-only `seeking` triggered between issuing a `seek` control call and receiving `snap` frames with `reason: "replay_seek"` on every subscribed topic.

The pack carries the a11y review record from D06 and the per-component keyboard tables; implementers must not re-derive them.

## Performance notes
The pack states the perf-relevant design constraints explicitly: 1 Hz announced clock, throttled scrub seek, motion suppression above the stated speed threshold.

The pack lists the analytics/audit events each screen emits so instrumentation is not forgotten during implementation.

title: Run design QA on the built chart engine surfaces against the specs
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA **default-on for net-new UI Stories**: "built screen compared against design spec (spacing/tokens/type/color/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer; discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bug with `priority/*` set."

E11 ships the chassis that six further Epics build on, which changes the stakes of this pass. A 2 px gutter error or a token wired to the wrong slot does not stay a 2 px error — it becomes the baseline that E12's series, E13's indicators and E18's footprint are all aligned to, and correcting it later means touching all of them. This is the cheapest moment to catch it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Surface-by-surface comparison** of the built engine against E11-D02/D03/D04/D05/D06:
  - SCR-030 chassis: pane chrome, gutters, axis rendering, gridline hierarchy, legend, watermark, countdown.
  - CMP-188/189 axes: tick density, label decimation at each zoom level, drag and keyboard rescale affordances, the scale-lock badge.
  - CMP-190/197 crosshair and tooltip: line treatment, axis pills, tooltip layout, edge-flip behaviour, the never-obscure-last-price rule.
  - SCR-043/044/031 scale menus, go-to-date and the Scales tab.
  - SCR-045 data table, including the **equal-status entry point placement**.
  - SCR-046 diagnostics, SCR-047 empty, SCR-048 error.
  - Multi-pane chrome: splitters, collapsed stubs, pane focus indication.
- **All three themes** (dark, light, high-contrast) and **all three densities** (comfortable, compact, dense) — the full 9-cell matrix for the chassis, since a density/theme combination is exactly where a token error hides.
- **Every state** from SCR-030: loading, streaming, stale, disconnected, replay, demo/live, degraded.
- **Motion conformance** against E11-D06: momentum feel, transition durations, countdown warn, stale dimming, and each reduced-motion variant.
- **Token conformance**: confirm no hard-coded colours and that every surface resolves to the design-system token specified.
- **Discrepancy log**: each item classified as fix-now or file-as-Bug with a `priority/*` label, per the DoD.

## Out of scope
- Functional testing — **E11-Q01**/**Q02**/**Q06**.
- Accessibility auditing — **E11-Q05** (this pass checks *designed* focus and contrast treatments are implemented, not full conformance).
- Performance — **E11-Q03**.
- Surfaces owned by other Epics (footprint cells, heatmap, drawings) — their own design QA.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every designed surface is compared against its spec
  Given the E11 design specs and the built engine
  When design QA completes
  Then every surface in scope has a recorded comparison result
  And no surface is marked "looks fine" without a spec-by-spec check of spacing, tokens, type, colour and states

Scenario: The full theme and density matrix is covered
  Given three themes and three density modes
  When the chassis is reviewed
  Then all nine combinations are checked
  And discrepancies that appear only in a specific combination are logged with that combination named

Scenario: Discrepancies are dispositioned, never merely noted
  Given the discrepancy log
  Then each item is either fixed within this pass or filed as a Bug with a priority label and an owner
  And no item is left as an unowned observation

Scenario: Equal status survives implementation
  Given SCR-045's equal-status requirement
  When the built product is inspected
  Then the table's entry point is in the chart panel header at the designed visual weight
  And any regression toward hiding it in a menu or settings is a blocking finding

Scenario: Reduced-motion variants are implemented as designed
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When each animated element is exercised
  Then it behaves per its designed reduced-motion variant
  And no information-carrying state change is lost
```

## Technical notes / design
**Method.** Side-by-side comparison at 1:1 scale using the Figma overlay workflow, plus browser DevTools for computed values — measuring rather than eyeballing spacing and colour, since a 2 px error is invisible to the eye and obvious to a measurement.

For canvas-rendered surfaces the comparison uses **screenshots at a fixed DPR against the golden images** (E11-T08), which conveniently means a discrepancy found here can usually be turned into a golden test so it cannot recur — design QA findings that become regression tests are worth more than findings that become fixes.

**Order of attack**: themes first (token errors are systematic and cheap to find in one theme, then confirm across all three), then densities (spacing errors), then states (coverage gaps), then motion. Going state-first would mean re-checking every state after each token fix.

## Test plan
- Comparison results recorded per surface per theme per density.
- Discrepancy log with classification, priority and owner.
- Findings converted into golden-image cases (E11-T08) wherever they are visual and reproducible.
- Re-check after fixes, with the re-check result recorded — a design QA pass that does not verify its own fixes is half a pass.

## Security notes
No security surface. One check with a safety dimension: the **demo/live badge** and the replay-mode border are verified to be unmistakable in every theme and density, because an environment indicator that is legible in dark/comfortable and washed out in high-contrast/dense is a real trading hazard, not a cosmetic defect.

## Accessibility notes
This pass verifies that **designed** accessibility treatments were implemented: focus ring visibility over canvas content in all three themes, target sizes for splitters and axis drag zones, contrast conformance of the shipped tokens, the presence of text equivalents on every state, and the reduced-motion variants. Full accessibility conformance — axe-core, NVDA and VoiceOver passes — is **E11-Q05**, and this ticket does not substitute for it.

## Performance notes
Not a performance pass, but visual discrepancies with performance causes are flagged for E11-Q03: text that looks wrong because it fell back to the 2D path, gridlines missing because a draw-call budget was hit, a density mode that silently dropped detail. A visual bug with a performance root cause is mis-triaged more often than not, so noting the possibility here saves a round trip.

## Observability
Discrepancy log attached to the ticket; filed Bugs linked back to it so the pass's completeness is auditable at Epic DoD time.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts complete in Figma at the agreed fidelity, named and organised per the design-system file conventions, and linked from the ticket.
- [ ] Every state enumerated per `14-screens-catalogue.md` conventions: empty, loading, error, populated, and the edge-density case.
- [ ] Built only from `15-component-catalogue.md` components and `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens; any new component has a design-system entry (not a one-off), filed against E11-D05.
- [ ] All three themes covered: dark (default), light, high-contrast.
- [ ] Contrast measured and recorded for every foreground/background pair (>= 4.5:1 text, >= 3:1 non-text UI).
- [ ] Nothing conveyed by colour alone; every state has a text or shape equivalent.
- [ ] Keyboard path specified for every interaction (no hover-only, no drag-only, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` 3.1.6).
- [ ] Redlines/specs sufficient for implementation without verbal clarification; motion specified in durations, easings and the reduced-motion variant.
- [ ] Screen-catalogue sign-off checklist for each covered SCR ticked item by item in a comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** the accessibility specialist; sign-off recorded as a ticket comment with date.
- [ ] Status Done at least **2 sprints before** the consuming engineering story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`); the consuming ticket key is named in the sign-off comment.
- [ ] Handed to engineering via E11-D09's handoff pack; open questions closed, not carried.
- [ ] All nine theme × density combinations checked for the chassis.
- [ ] Every SCR-030 state checked.
- [ ] Discrepancy log complete with every item dispositioned (fixed or filed with priority and owner).
- [ ] Reproducible visual findings converted into golden-image cases.
- [ ] Re-check performed and recorded after fixes.
- [ ] Signed off by the designer of record.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S14** and **E11-S09** — the last UI-bearing stories; QA-ing before they land would mean re-doing the pass.

title: Run a chaos charter for context loss, feed faults and resource pressure
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` lists chaos/failover tests among the non-negotiable SDLC requirements, and R1 exit criterion 8 is specific: a forced `WEBGL_lose_context` must restore a **fully correct scene within 2 s with zero data loss**.

The chart engine has an unusually rich set of ways to be disturbed that have nothing to do with its own logic: the GPU driver can reset, the browser can discard the context under memory pressure, the WS feed can gap or deliver out-of-order frames, the worker can be starved, the machine can sleep and wake. Each of these is a normal event over a long trading session, and each is invisible to unit tests. This charter exercises them deliberately.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Context loss**: forced `WEBGL_lose_context` during idle, during a pan, during a data storm and during atlas generation; repeated loss (3× in 10 s); loss that fails to restore (asserting the SCR-048 path with auto-retry ×3 then manual retry).
- **Feed faults**: malformed binary frames; truncated frames; out-of-order sequence numbers; a sequence gap requiring resync; duplicate frames; `NaN` and `Infinity` prices; a declared length exceeding `maxBars`; a 60-second feed stall followed by a burst.
- **Resource pressure**: memory pressure to the 70 % threshold and beyond; GPU memory exhaustion; worker starvation (main thread blocked for 5 s); many charts opened and closed repeatedly (leak detection over 100 cycles).
- **Environment disturbance**: DPR change mid-pan; monitor disconnect; window minimise/restore; machine sleep/wake; tab backgrounded for 10 minutes then foregrounded (timers throttled, `rAF` stopped — a classic source of "the chart came back wrong").
- **Degraded paths**: WebGL2 unavailable at startup; WebGL2 lost permanently mid-session and falling back to `degraded-2d`; IndexedDB unavailable (private mode) during atlas caching.
- Each scenario asserts: **no crash, no silent wrongness, no data loss, a correct disclosure to the user, and full recovery** — with "no silent wrongness" being the one that matters most, since a chart that recovers into a subtly incorrect state is worse than one that visibly fails.
- Automated where deterministic (feed faults, context loss, pressure) in `packages/chart-engine/test/chaos`; manual charter for the environment disturbances that cannot be automated reliably.

## Out of scope
- Backend chaos (exchange 5xx, rate limits, WS disconnect at the server) — **E45** and the platform Epics; this charter covers the **client engine's** response to faults it receives.
- Performance measurement — **E11-Q03**.
- GPU/driver matrix coverage — **E11-Q07**.
- Security fuzzing as an adversarial exercise — **E11-X03** (this charter's malformed-frame cases overlap and feed it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Context loss restores a correct scene within the budget
  Given a chart with 100k bars, 3 panes and an active crosshair
  When WEBGL_lose_context is forced
  Then SCR-048 announces the loss through a role="alert" region
  And a fully correct scene is restored from the DataModel within 2 seconds with zero data loss
  And the viewport, crosshair position and pane ratios are exactly as they were

Scenario: Repeated context loss does not degrade into a broken state
  Given the context is lost three times within ten seconds
  Then each loss recovers correctly
  And after the third recovery the chart is fully functional with no leaked GPU resources

Scenario: A permanent loss falls back rather than failing
  Given the context cannot be restored after three attempts
  Then a manual retry and a link to renderer settings are offered
  And choosing the fallback moves the chart to degraded-2d with its capabilities disclosed

Scenario: Malformed frames are rejected without collateral damage
  Given a malformed, truncated or out-of-range frame arrives
  Then it is rejected with ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR
  And the existing scene continues rendering correctly, with no partial application of the bad frame

Scenario: A sequence gap resyncs rather than drawing wrong data
  Given frames arrive with a gap in the sequence
  Then the engine requests a resync rather than applying the later frames onto a stale model
  And the user is shown a stale indicator until the resync completes

Scenario: Backgrounding and restoring does not corrupt state
  Given the tab is backgrounded for ten minutes with a live feed
  When it is foregrounded
  Then the chart catches up to current data without a gap and without replaying ten minutes of animation
  And no duplicate or missing bars are present

Scenario: Repeated chart lifecycle leaks nothing
  Given a chart is created and disposed 100 times
  Then GPU memory and JS heap return to their starting level within 5 %
  And no worker, listener or observer is left alive
```

## Technical notes / design
**Forcing context loss.** The `WEBGL_lose_context` extension gives deterministic control, which is what makes this testable in CI rather than only by unplugging a monitor. Restoration correctness is asserted by comparing a **golden image** of the pre-loss scene with a post-restore capture — pixel comparison catches "restored but subtly wrong" in a way that state assertions do not.

**Leak detection.** 100 create/dispose cycles with `performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory()` sampled at the start and end. The threshold is 5 %, which tolerates allocator noise while catching a per-instance leak that would matter over a trading day.

**Background throttling.** Backgrounded tabs have `rAF` stopped and timers throttled to once per minute. The failure mode is an engine that, on foregrounding, either replays every missed frame (a visible animation storm) or holds a stale model believing it is current. Both are tested, because both have shipped in real products.

**Assertion discipline.** Every scenario asserts *correctness after recovery*, not merely "did not crash". A chaos test that only checks for exceptions passes happily while the chart shows yesterday's prices.

## Test plan
- Automated chaos suite in CI (nightly rather than per-PR — these are slow), with failures raised as P1.
- Manual charter for environment disturbances, executed once per release train with a session sheet.
- Golden-image comparison for every recovery scenario.
- Leak detection as a standalone long-running job.
- Findings filed with severity; anything producing silent wrongness is automatically **P0**, since it is the failure class the product can least afford.

## Security notes
This charter overlaps deliberately with **E11-X03**'s fuzzing: the malformed-frame, out-of-range and `NaN` cases are simultaneously robustness tests and security tests, since the same input that crashes a decoder is the one that corrupts memory in a less careful implementation. Findings are shared between the two tickets rather than duplicated.

The `maxBars` and `memoryBudgetMb` ceilings (E11-S15) are verified here under adversarial input, which is the control the STRIDE model relies on for denial of service. Data classification: synthetic fixtures only.

## Accessibility notes
Every disturbance must remain **announced and comprehensible**, because a screen-reader user has no visual cue that something went wrong:
- Context loss and restoration announce through `role="alert"` — once each, unthrottled.
- Stale and disconnected states are announced and are present in the DOM mirror, not only as a dimmed canvas.
- After recovery, keyboard focus and the data cursor position are preserved — a recovery that silently drops focus leaves a keyboard user stranded.
- The `degraded-2d` fallback discloses reduced capabilities in text.
These are asserted in the charter, not assumed from the implementation tickets.

## Performance notes
Recovery budgets: context restore <=2 s (R1 exit criterion 8); resync completes without exceeding the frame budget; the post-burst catch-up after a 60-second stall must not stall the UI thread. A recovery path that meets its correctness bar by blocking for 5 seconds fails this charter.

## Observability
Every scenario asserts the **correct engine error code** is emitted: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE`, `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`. Observability is treated as a testable requirement here — an error that recovers silently without telling anyone is a defect, because it makes the same problem in production undiagnosable.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts (plan, charters, scripts, suites) committed to the repo, not held in a personal document.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the Gherkin acceptance criterion or the user story it verifies, so coverage is traceable rather than asserted.
- [ ] Execution results recorded with pass/fail per scenario and evidence (logs, screenshots, recordings, benchmark artefacts) attached.
- [ ] Defects filed with reproduction steps, environment, severity and `priority/*`, linked to the E11 ticket they came from.
- [ ] Automated suites wired into CI at the correct stage and green; flaky tests quarantined with a ticket, never silently retried.
- [ ] Coverage contribution recorded against the package thresholds (>= 85 % engine, >= 80 % web).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET with pass/fail per scenario and any deviation stated explicitly.
- [ ] Test plan reviewed by the chart-engine lead so the black-box view and the implementation view are reconciled.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S02** — context-loss recovery is the central subject.
- **E11-T05** — the `degraded-2d` fallback path.
- **E11-T03**, **E11-S15** — decode validation and the memory ceilings under test.
- Feeds **E11-X03** (shared fuzzing findings) and **E11-Q06** (regression pack).

## Branch
`test/chart-engine-chaos` · automated suite plus the manual charter document.

## References

title: Audit the chart engine for WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core and screen readers
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 9 requires that every chart is operable without a mouse, with **NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the accessibility specialist**. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes a11y default-on for any UI surface with no "internal tool" exception, and `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 identifies the canvas strategy as the highest-risk area in the product.

Automated tooling cannot verify most of what matters here. axe-core will confirm that a canvas has a `role` and that the table has headers; it cannot tell you whether the announcements make sense, whether the throttle cadence is tolerable at a 20 Hz tick rate, or whether the data table is genuinely usable as an equal-status alternative rather than technically conformant and practically miserable. That judgement requires a human using a screen reader, which is what this audit is.

**E11-D07** reviewed the design; this audits the built product against the same clauses.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated**: axe-core zero violations on every R1 chart route — SCR-030, SCR-031, SCR-043, SCR-044, SCR-045, SCR-046, SCR-047, SCR-048, SCR-049 — wired as a required CI check.
- **Manual screen-reader passes**, each following a scripted task set and recorded:
  - **NVDA + Chrome** (Windows — the owner's platform, therefore primary).
  - **VoiceOver + Safari** (macOS).
  - **JAWS + Chrome** spot-check on the table and the live regions, where behaviour is known to diverge.
- **Task set** (the same tasks for each screen reader, so results are comparable): find the current price; navigate to a specific bar; read a bar's OHLCV; switch to log scale; open the data table and read three bars; sort the table by delta; move the crosshair and confirm the table follows; discover that the chart went stale; recover from a lost graphics context.
- **Keyboard-only audit**: every function reachable and operable, focus always visible, focus order logical, no traps, `Alt+T` and all documented hotkeys working, and no operation that requires hovering or dragging (§3.1.6).
- **Low-vision audit**: 200 % and 400 % browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.10 reflow); high-contrast theme; Windows High Contrast Mode; text spacing override (1.4.12).
- **Colour-independence audit**: every state and encoding checked under deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulation — feeding open item **O5** (colour-blind-safe palette), which is due at M8 and closes here.
- **Live-region behaviour audit**: cadence tolerable under a real 20 Hz feed; no flooding; discrete alerts announced once and in full; the "reduce announcements" toggle honoured.
- **Equal-status verification** of SCR-045 against the canvas, performed with a screen reader rather than by inspection.
- Findings triaged with WCAG criterion, severity and owner; **blocking findings gate the Epic's DoD**.

## Out of scope
- Design-stage review — **E11-D07** (already done; this audits the implementation against it).
- Accessibility of surfaces owned by other Epics (footprint cells, heatmap, drawings) — their own audits against this same standard.
- The design system's base components — E05.
- Remediation work — filed as tickets and executed by the owning teams.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated checks are clean and enforced
  Given every R1 chart route
  When axe-core runs in CI
  Then zero violations are reported
  And the check is required, so a new violation blocks merge rather than being noticed later

Scenario: A screen-reader user can complete every task
  Given the scripted task set
  When it is executed with NVDA and again with VoiceOver
  Then every task is completed successfully
  And any task that cannot be completed is a blocking finding, not an observation

Scenario: The data table is genuinely equal status under a screen reader
  Given a screen-reader user reads a bar's values from the table
  When those values are compared with the canvas
  Then every value available visually is available in the table
  And the table is reachable from the panel header in at most the same number of keystrokes as any other primary chart control

Scenario: Announcements are usable at a real tick rate
  Given a live feed at 20 ticks per second
  When the ambient live region is listened to for two minutes
  Then announcements arrive at a tolerable cadence with the latest values
  And the screen reader is never flooded to the point of unusability

Scenario: The chart reflows at 400 percent zoom
  Given browser zoom at 400 percent
  When the chart and its chrome are inspected
  Then no content is lost and no two-dimensional scrolling is required for primary content
  And the data table's primary columns remain readable without horizontal scrolling

Scenario: Meaning survives without colour
  Given every state and encoding under three colour-blindness simulations
  Then each remains distinguishable
  And any encoding relying on colour alone is a blocking finding

Scenario: Recovery is perceivable without sight
  Given the graphics context is lost and restored
  When the session is observed with a screen reader
  Then both the loss and the recovery are announced once each, in full
  And focus and the data cursor position survive the recovery
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why three screen readers and not one.** NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver differ substantially in how they handle live regions, virtualised tables and `role="img"` with dynamic labels — the three features this engine depends on most. Testing one and assuming the others is how products ship "accessible" charts that are silent in JAWS. NVDA is primary (owner's platform), VoiceOver full, JAWS spot-checked on the two features where divergence is known.

**Scripted, comparable tasks.** Each screen reader runs the same task list so results can be compared rather than merely collected. Each session is recorded with audio, which is the only practical way to review an announcement-cadence problem after the fact — "it felt like too much" is not a filable defect, and a recording is.

**Severity model.** Blocking = a task cannot be completed, or information is unavailable. Major = a task is completable but substantially harder than the pointer path. Minor = friction. Blocking findings gate the Epic DoD; major findings need an owner and a date before R1 PRR.

**O5 closure.** The colour-blindness simulation over the shipped palette is the M8 validation open item O5 has been waiting for; its result is recorded as an ADR amendment, closing the item.

## Test plan
- axe-core results per route, published as CI artefacts.
- Session recordings and per-task pass/fail per screen reader.
- Zoom, contrast and text-spacing screenshots.
- Colour-blindness simulation captures per state.
- Findings register with WCAG criterion, severity, owner and target ticket.
- Re-test after remediation, with results recorded — an audit without a re-test verifies nothing.

## Security notes
No security surface. One intersection worth recording: the DOM mirror surfaces market data as real DOM, and the audit confirms values are rendered as text rather than markup — the same control **E11-X01** models, verified here from the outside.

Session recordings capture screen content, so they are made against the **demo** environment with synthetic data and stored in the private QA drive.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility verification for E11, and its authority is R1 exit criterion 9 plus `05-accessibility-standard.md`. It audits all four layers of §6 as built:
- §6.1 DOM mirror — windowing, surrogate focus, alignment, sync with the canvas.
- §6.2 Live regions — cadence, politeness routing, region hygiene, the reduce-announcements toggle.
- §6.3 Table — equal status, column parity, sort/filter announcements, live patching without focus loss.
- §6.4 Canvas — `role="img"` with a current, updating label.
Plus §3.1.6 (no hover/drag-only), §4 (focus, target size, zoom) and §7 (reduced motion). Sign-off by the accessibility specialist is a **gate on the Epic's DoD**, not advisory.

## Performance notes
Two performance-adjacent findings the audit specifically looks for, because they are invisible to the perf harness: the announcement cadence must remain tolerable at full tick rate (a correctness problem for screen-reader users even though frame time is fine), and the DOM mirror must not degrade chart responsiveness when a screen reader is attached — AT attachment changes browser behaviour, and a chart that is smooth without NVDA and janky with it is a real and frequently-missed defect.

## Observability
Findings register committed to `docs/plan/`; axe-core results as CI artefacts; session recordings in the QA drive. `engine.a11y.desync_detected` and `engine.a11y.announcements_per_minute` are reviewed against the audit's observations, so the runtime counters are validated against human experience rather than trusted blindly.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts (plan, charters, scripts, suites) committed to the repo, not held in a personal document.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the Gherkin acceptance criterion or the user story it verifies, so coverage is traceable rather than asserted.
- [ ] Execution results recorded with pass/fail per scenario and evidence (logs, screenshots, recordings, benchmark artefacts) attached.
- [ ] Defects filed with reproduction steps, environment, severity and `priority/*`, linked to the E11 ticket they came from.
- [ ] Automated suites wired into CI at the correct stage and green; flaky tests quarantined with a ticket, never silently retried.
- [ ] Coverage contribution recorded against the package thresholds (>= 85 % engine, >= 80 % web).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET with pass/fail per scenario and any deviation stated explicitly.
- [ ] Test plan reviewed by the chart-engine lead so the black-box view and the implementation view are reconciled.
- [ ] axe-core zero violations on all R1 chart routes, wired as a required check.
- [ ] NVDA and VoiceOver passes completed with recordings and per-task results; JAWS spot-check completed.
- [ ] Zoom (200 %/400 %), high-contrast, Windows High Contrast Mode and text-spacing audits completed.
- [ ] Colour-blindness simulation completed and open item **O5** closed by an ADR amendment.
- [ ] All blocking findings resolved and re-tested; major findings owned with dates before R1 PRR.
- [ ] Signed off by the accessibility specialist (R1 exit criterion 9).

## Dependencies
- **E11-S14** — the data table is the central artefact under audit.
- **E11-S13** — the mirror, cursor and live regions.
- **E11-D07** — the design review whose clauses this audits as built.
- Gates the **Epic DoD** and **R1 exit criterion 9**.
