title: Assemble the chart-engine regression pack and run the epic-level QA sign-off
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an **Epic-level** regression and exploratory pass, "not just child-ticket QA", and epic-level acceptance criteria "verified end-to-end, not just per-child". The reason is that an Epic can have every child green and still not work: each story was tested against its own acceptance criteria, and nobody sat down and used the chart for an hour.

E11 is also the Epic that six others build on, so this pack becomes the **standing regression suite** that E12, E13, E14, E15, E18 and E21 run against to prove they have not broken the chassis. Assembling it properly here is leverage; assembling it loosely means six Epics inherit a suite nobody trusts.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Regression pack**: the durable, re-runnable subset of everything E11's QA produced — the E11-Q01 interaction cases, the E11-Q02 E2E suite, the E11-Q04 chaos scenarios, the E11-Q05 a11y checks and the E11-T08 golden images — assembled into one runnable suite with a single entry point and a documented runtime.
- **Epic-level acceptance verification**: each of the Epic's own Gherkin scenarios executed end-to-end and recorded — frame budget met and enforced; 30 fps floor under worst case; context loss recovering within 2 s with no data loss; the chart fully operable without a mouse; the engine package staying framework-free; graceful degradation without WebGL2.
- **Exploratory charters** (time-boxed, mission-stated, session-sheeted), aimed at the seams between stories where nobody's acceptance criteria live:
  1. *A trading session*: 60 minutes of realistic use on a live demo feed — switch symbols and intervals, pan history, scale modes, multi-pane, leave it running. Mission: find what degrades over time.
  2. *The awkward user*: deliberately hostile interaction — rapid mode switching, interrupted gestures, simultaneous keyboard and pointer input, resize during drag. Mission: find state corruption.
  3. *The keyboard-only trader*: complete a full session without touching the pointer. Mission: find the gaps between "technically operable" and "actually usable".
  4. *The long session*: 4 hours running with a live feed. Mission: find leaks, drift, stale state and recovery failures.
- **Cross-story seam testing**: theme change during a pan; LOD step-down while the data table is open; context loss during a sync propagation; memory pressure during atlas generation; DPR change mid-momentum.
- **Defect burn-down verification**: confirm zero open P0/P1 defects against E11 scope, as the Epic DoD requires.
- **QA sign-off document** for the Epic, feeding the R1 PRR evidence pack.

## Out of scope
- Writing new automated tests — this assembles and runs what exists; gaps found become tickets.
- Performance measurement — **E11-Q03** (its results are cited here, not re-derived).
- Accessibility auditing — **E11-Q05** (same).
- Other Epics' regression packs — they extend this one.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every epic-level acceptance criterion is verified end to end
  Given the six Gherkin scenarios in the E11 epic body
  When the sign-off is complete
  Then each has been executed end to end with evidence attached
  And none is signed off by pointing at a child ticket's test result

Scenario: The regression pack runs from one entry point
  Given the assembled pack
  When it is invoked
  Then interaction, E2E, chaos, a11y and golden-image suites all run
  And the total runtime is documented so downstream Epics can plan around it

Scenario: Exploratory charters are executed with recorded sessions
  Given the four charters
  When each is executed within its timebox
  Then a session sheet records what was covered, what was found and what was not covered
  And findings are filed with severity and owner

Scenario: The long session reveals no drift
  Given a four-hour session on a live demo feed
  When memory, frame time and correctness are checked at the end
  Then memory and frame time are within 5 percent of their starting values
  And no stale, desynced or silently incorrect state is present

Scenario: Cross-story seams behave
  Given a theme change during a pan, an LOD step-down with the table open, and a context loss during sync propagation
  When each is exercised
  Then the engine remains correct and recovers cleanly
  And any seam defect is filed against the specific pair of stories it sits between

Scenario: The epic cannot be signed off with open P0 or P1 defects
  Given the defect register for E11 scope
  When sign-off is attempted
  Then zero P0 and P1 defects are open
  And sign-off is withheld if any remain
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why exploratory charters matter most here.** Scripted tests verify what someone thought of in advance. E11's risk is concentrated in what nobody thought of — the interaction of LOD, memory pressure, theme changes, sync and live data over hours. Charters are time-boxed and mission-driven rather than step-scripted precisely so the tester follows the smell rather than the script.

**The long session is not optional and cannot be shortened.** Leaks, drift, texture-memory fragmentation and reconnect-loop bugs are invisible in a 10-minute run and obvious in a 4-hour one. A trading session is a full day; 4 hours is already a compromise.

**Pack composition principle**: fast checks first (unit, golden), then E2E, then chaos, then the manual charters. Downstream Epics run the automated portion per PR and the full pack per release train, and the entry point makes that split explicit rather than leaving each Epic to guess.

## Test plan
- Regression pack executed in full against the release candidate, with results recorded per suite.
- Epic-level acceptance scenarios executed with evidence attached per scenario.
- Four exploratory charters executed with session sheets.
- Defect register reviewed and confirmed clear of P0/P1.
- Pack runtime measured and documented.

## Security notes
Security findings arising from exploratory work are routed to **E11-X03** rather than filed as ordinary defects, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8's rule that anything with a security or safety implication is treated as `security`-labelled whether or not the label was applied at creation.

Sessions run against the **demo** environment; the four-hour session uses a demo feed, so no live account data appears in any recording or screenshot.

## Accessibility notes
The keyboard-only charter is a deliberate complement to **E11-Q05**'s conformance audit: conformance answers "does it meet the standard?", the charter answers "is it actually workable for a whole session?" — and a product can pass the first and fail the second. Its findings are as filable as any other.

The regression pack includes the axe-core checks and the keyboard traversal specs, so downstream Epics inherit accessibility regression protection automatically rather than having to remember to add it.

## Performance notes
Cites E11-Q03's measurements rather than re-deriving them, but the four-hour charter adds something the benchmark cannot: **drift over a realistic session**. B10's 30-minute soak catches fast leaks; a slow leak or gradual frame-time creep only shows over hours, and that is the specific thing this charter is looking for.

## Observability
Sign-off document committed and attached to the R1 PRR evidence pack. Session sheets and charter findings attached to the ticket. The regression pack's runtime and pass rate are tracked over time so downstream Epics can see whether the chassis suite is healthy.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts (plan, charters, scripts, suites) committed to the repo, not held in a personal document.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the Gherkin acceptance criterion or the user story it verifies, so coverage is traceable rather than asserted.
- [ ] Execution results recorded with pass/fail per scenario and evidence (logs, screenshots, recordings, benchmark artefacts) attached.
- [ ] Defects filed with reproduction steps, environment, severity and `priority/*`, linked to the E11 ticket they came from.

- [ ] Coverage contribution recorded against the package thresholds (>= 85 % engine, >= 80 % web).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET with pass/fail per scenario and any deviation stated explicitly.
- [ ] Test plan reviewed by the chart-engine lead so the black-box view and the implementation view are reconciled.
- [ ] Regression pack assembled with a single documented entry point and a measured runtime.
- [ ] All six epic-level acceptance scenarios verified end-to-end with evidence.
- [ ] All four exploratory charters executed with session sheets.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 defects against E11 scope.
- [ ] Epic QA sign-off document completed and attached to the R1 PRR evidence pack.

## Dependencies
- **E11-Q03**, **E11-Q04**, **E11-Q05** — their results and suites are assembled here.
- **E11-Q01**, **E11-Q02** — the interaction plan and E2E suite.
- **E11-T08** — golden images.
- Gates the **Epic DoD** and feeds the **R1 PRR**. Inherited by E12, E13, E14, E15, E18, E21.

title: Run an exploratory GPU, driver and runtime matrix charter for the engine
body:
## Context
The golden-image suite (E11-T08) runs on SwiftShader for determinism, which by construction means it **cannot catch driver-specific defects**. The benchmark suite (E11-T06) runs on one pinned reference machine, which means it cannot catch "works here, breaks there". Between them they leave a real gap, and risk **R8 Browser/GPU compat** lives in exactly that gap.

WebGL2 behaviour genuinely varies: Intel integrated graphics handle large textures differently from discrete NVIDIA; AMD drivers have historically differed on `fwidth` precision (which the SDF text shader depends on); WebView2 in Tauri behaves differently from Electron's Chromium (open item **O1**, ADR-0011); and vendor driver blocklists silently downgrade some machines to software rendering.

This charter is deliberately a **human exploratory activity** rather than an automated matrix: the failures being hunted are visual and subtle, and automating a matrix that nobody looks at would produce green checks and blurry text.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **GPU matrix**, each running the same scripted scenario set: NVIDIA discrete (the reference RTX 3060), AMD discrete, **Intel integrated** (the most commonly under-tested and most commonly broken), and a software-rendering fallback machine.
- **Runtime matrix**: Chromium (current stable), **Electron** (the pinned shipping build — primary), and **Tauri/WebView2**, closing out the measurement side of open item **O1**.
- **Driver variants**: current and one prior major driver version per vendor, since a regression introduced by a driver update is a support case that looks exactly like a product bug.
- **Scenario set** per combination: 100k-bar render and pan; SDF text at all size classes (the `fwidth` precision case); large-texture allocation (the heatmap ring's shape, even before E21 builds it); context loss and restore; `degraded-2d` forced via `renderer.forceProfile`; the full theme × density matrix at a glance.
- **Visual comparison** against the reference machine's captures, looking specifically for: blurry or misaligned text, hairline shimmer, colour-banding differences, missing or misplaced geometry, and texture-size failures.
- **Capability-probe verification**: the probe reports the correct profile on each machine, and a blocklisted GPU correctly falls back rather than attempting and failing.
- **Findings register** with the combination, the symptom, a capture, and whether it is a product defect, a driver bug to work around, or an accepted limitation.
- **Supported-configuration statement**: the concrete output — which GPU/driver/runtime combinations are supported, which are degraded, and which are unsupported, published in the docs so support has an answer.

## Out of scope
- macOS and Linux coverage beyond a smoke check — the owner's environment is Windows + Electron, and spreading thin across platforms nobody uses would cost coverage where it matters.
- Mobile/Android — out of scope for the whole plan (owner decision 2026-09-14).
- The Electron vs Tauri **decision** — ADR-0011, informed by these measurements but decided by the Architect.
- Performance baselines — **E11-Q03** (reference machine only, by design).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every matrix combination is exercised with the same scenarios
  Given the GPU, driver and runtime matrix
  When the charter completes
  Then each combination has run the full scenario set with results recorded
  And any combination that could not be tested is stated explicitly rather than silently omitted

Scenario: Text renders correctly on every GPU
  Given SDF text at all three size classes
  When it is compared against the reference capture on each GPU
  Then text is crisp and correctly positioned everywhere
  And any fwidth precision difference is identified with a workaround or an accepted limitation

Scenario: Intel integrated graphics is a first-class target
  Given an Intel integrated GPU
  When the full scenario set runs
  Then the engine either meets its targets or degrades correctly with disclosure
  And it never renders incorrectly without telling the user

Scenario: A blocklisted GPU falls back rather than failing
  Given a machine whose driver is on the browser's GPU blocklist
  When a chart is mounted
  Then the capability probe reports the reduced profile and degraded-2d is selected
  And the user is told what is reduced and why, and is never shown a blank canvas

Scenario: Open item O1 gets its measurements
  Given Tauri/WebView2 under the 100 ms-cadence update scenario
  When the results are recorded
  Then they are sufficient for ADR-0011 to be finalised
  And the recommendation is stated with its evidence

Scenario: The output is a supported-configuration statement
  When the charter completes
  Then a published statement names supported, degraded and unsupported combinations
  And support can answer a user's "does my machine work" question from it without asking engineering
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why exploratory rather than automated.** An automated cross-GPU matrix is expensive to build (a fleet of physical machines or a GPU-enabled cloud runner per vendor), and the defects it would catch are visual and contextual — "the text looks slightly soft on Intel" is not an assertion, it is an observation. A skilled tester with a reference capture and a side-by-side finds these in an afternoon. If a specific defect class recurs, *that* gets automated afterwards, which is the right order.

**Specific known-risk areas to probe hardest**, so the session is not a random walk:
- `fwidth` precision in the SDF shader (AMD historically differs) -> soft or fringed text.
- Maximum texture size and `texSubImage2D` upload performance (Intel integrated is the tight case) -> heatmap ring allocation failures.
- `OffscreenCanvas` availability and behaviour differences in WebView2 -> the whole worker architecture's assumption.
- Context-loss frequency under memory pressure (varies substantially by driver) -> recovery path exercised more often on some machines than others.
- High-DPI handling on mixed-DPI multi-monitor setups (the most common real-world configuration and the least tested).

**Capture discipline**: screenshots at fixed DPR and fixed viewport, so comparison against the reference is meaningful rather than approximate.

## Test plan
- Scripted scenario set executed per combination with captures.
- Side-by-side visual comparison against reference captures.
- Findings register with combination, symptom, capture and disposition.
- Recurring defect classes proposed for automation as follow-up tickets.
- Supported-configuration statement reviewed by the Architect and the support owner.

## Security notes
Synthetic fixtures only; no account data on test machines. Test machines are clean installs rather than personal machines, so a driver-level capture cannot inadvertently include unrelated content.

One security-adjacent finding class the charter watches for: a GPU or driver that silently produces **incorrect** rendering rather than failing is an integrity problem, not a cosmetic one — a chart drawing wrong prices is indistinguishable to the user from a data problem. Any such finding is escalated to P0 regardless of how narrow the affected configuration is.

## Accessibility notes
The `degraded-2d` path exercised here must retain **full accessibility** — the DOM mirror, data cursor, live regions and data table are main-thread DOM and are backend-independent. The charter verifies this on machines where the fallback is actually selected, rather than only on a reference machine where it is forced, since "forced fallback works" and "naturally selected fallback works" have diverged in practice before.

Windows High Contrast Mode is checked on the Windows machines, since it interacts with GPU rendering in ways the design-time review cannot predict.

## Performance notes
Performance on non-reference machines is recorded as **information, not as a gate** — the budgets are defined against the reference machine, and gating on an Intel integrated GPU would either be meaningless or would force the product down to the slowest machine's ceiling. What the charter does produce is the honest statement of what each class of machine delivers, which is what the supported-configuration statement needs and what support needs when a user asks why their laptop is slower.

## Observability
Findings register and supported-configuration statement committed to `docs/plan/`. The capability report (`ready` message) from each machine is captured, giving a real corpus of capability profiles rather than a theoretical one — useful later for interpreting a user's diagnostics snapshot.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts (plan, charters, scripts, suites) committed to the repo, not held in a personal document.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the Gherkin acceptance criterion or the user story it verifies, so coverage is traceable rather than asserted.
- [ ] Execution results recorded with pass/fail per scenario and evidence (logs, screenshots, recordings, benchmark artefacts) attached.
- [ ] Defects filed with reproduction steps, environment, severity and `priority/*`, linked to the E11 ticket they came from.
- [ ] Automated suites wired into CI at the correct stage and green; flaky tests quarantined with a ticket, never silently retried.
- [ ] Coverage contribution recorded against the package thresholds (>= 85 % engine, >= 80 % web).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET with pass/fail per scenario and any deviation stated explicitly.
- [ ] Test plan reviewed by the chart-engine lead so the black-box view and the implementation view are reconciled.
- [ ] Every matrix combination exercised or explicitly stated as untested with a reason.
- [ ] Findings register complete with dispositions (product defect / driver workaround / accepted limitation).
- [ ] Supported-configuration statement published and reviewed by the Architect.
- [ ] Open item **O1** measurements delivered to ADR-0011.
- [ ] Any silent-incorrect-rendering finding escalated to P0 regardless of configuration breadth.

## Dependencies
- **E11-T05** — the `degraded-2d` path and the `renderer.forceProfile` override the charter relies on.
- **E11-T08** — reference captures for visual comparison.
- **E11-S11** — SDF text is the most driver-sensitive subsystem.
- Feeds **ADR-0011** (open item O1) and the R1 PRR's supported-configuration record.

## Branch
`test/chart-engine-gpu-matrix` · findings register and configuration statement committed.

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` — test pyramid, coverage floors, fixture conventions, flake policy
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` — budgets, measurement method, regression gate
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` — WCAG 2.2 AA target, canvas strategy, manual pass requirements
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` — QA sign-off gates per Kind

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §5 CHART — US-CHART-006, 007, 008, 010, 014

title: Expose the chart to AT via a windowed DOM mirror and keyboard data cursor
body:
## Context
A WebGL canvas is, by default, an empty node in the accessibility tree: no DOM, no semantics, nothing for a screen reader to read. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 calls this "the highest-risk area" of the whole product and mandates **three complementary layers, all of them, not either/or**. §6.1 goes further and states that the engine's public API must expose a "current visible window + current focused unit" query surface **as an explicit chart-engine-design requirement, not an afterthought bolted on later** — which is why this Story sits inside E11 rather than in a later a11y clean-up Epic.

This Story ships layers 1, 2 and 4: the windowed DOM mirror, the throttled live regions, and the `role="img"` canvas fallback label. Layer 3 (the data-table alternative, SCR-045) is E11-S14.

`US-CHART-008` requires the keyboard crosshair as a first-class path — "when I focus the chart and press arrow keys, the crosshair steps bar by bar and the readout is announced in a live region" — and CMP-190 states plainly that **keyboard-driven crosshair movement is the accessible path; mouse hover is the pointer-only convenience layer**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/a11y/DomMirror.ts` (main thread) — a visually-hidden (`clip-path`, **never** `display:none`) DOM structure mirroring the currently-relevant data: visible bar range with OHLCV, the focused bar, the focused footprint cell's values, the focused heatmap cell. **Windowed/virtualised**: only currently-visible/focusable units are materialised, so 100k bars never become 100k nodes.
- The **canvas control surrogate** pattern: one `tabindex`-able, ARIA-labelled element per logical unit, positioned to align with the visual target it represents so it satisfies target-size and focus-visible rules simultaneously. Focus ring via **CMP-004 FocusRing**.
- `src/a11y/DataCursor.ts` (worker-side state, main-thread surface) — keyboard data cursor: `<-/->` step bar, `Up/Down` step price level, `Home`/`End` first/last bar, `PageUp`/`PageDown` page, `+`/`-` zoom, `Alt+T` opens the data table (E11-S14). The cursor is stored in **world coordinates**, so resize, zoom and pan never lose it.
- The engine query surface §6.1 requires, frame-synchronous with rendering: `chart.getVisibleWindow()` and `chart.getFocusedUnit()`, plus the `a11y` worker->main message (`{ cursorSummary }`) from the §6 protocol.
- `src/a11y/LiveRegions.ts` — pre-rendered, never-recreated containers whose **text content only** is swapped (region hygiene, §6.2):
  - `aria-live="polite"` for ambient values, throttled to the configured cadence (default 1 update / 2 s per field, user-configurable), always presenting the **latest** value rather than queuing intermediate ticks. `US-CHART-008` caps announcements at <=2/s.
  - `role="alert"` reserved for discrete, low-frequency events (context lost/restored, data stale, LOD step-down) — never throttled, announced once in full.
- Layer 4: canvas `role="img"` with a rolling `aria-label` ("BTCUSDT 1 minute, last 64 011, up 0.4 %, delta +200") updated on data change (CMP-180), so no silent empty node exists in the tree.
- A "reduce announcements" master toggle and per-class politeness routing surfaced as engine options for the Settings -> Accessibility panel to bind to.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-045 data-table alternative — **E11-S14** (layer 3).
- The Settings -> Accessibility UI itself — E10/E15 chrome; this Story exposes the options it writes.
- Footprint-cell and DOM-ladder mirror *content* — E18/E21 register their focusable unit types against the mirror's extension point defined here.
- Manual NVDA/VoiceOver certification passes — **E11-Q05**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The chart is fully operable without a mouse
  Given a chart pane has keyboard focus and 500 bars are visible
  When the user presses Right arrow ten times, then End, then Home
  Then the data cursor steps one bar per press, jumps to the last bar, then the first
  And each stop updates the focused surrogate element and the polite live region

Scenario: Announcements are throttled and never flood
  Given a live feed producing 20 ticks per second
  When the ambient live region is observed for 10 seconds
  Then at most 2 announcements per second are emitted per field
  And each announcement carries the latest value, not a queued backlog

Scenario: Discrete events are announced once, in full, unthrottled
  Given the WebGL context is lost
  When the alert region fires
  Then "Graphics context lost - restoring" is announced exactly once
  And it is not coalesced with or delayed by ambient throttling

Scenario: The mirror is windowed, not complete
  Given a 100,000-bar series is loaded
  When the accessibility tree is inspected
  Then only the currently visible and focusable units are materialised as DOM nodes
  And the node count stays under 500 regardless of series length

Scenario: The mirror never desyncs from the canvas
  Given the engine is rendering at LOD level L2 with 12 bars aggregated per column
  When the focused unit is queried from the DOM mirror and from the renderer in the same frame
  Then both report the same bar, the same values and the same aggregation level
  And a property test over random pan/zoom sequences finds no frame where they disagree

Scenario: The canvas is never a silent empty node
  Given assistive technology reaches the canvas element directly
  When its accessible name is read
  Then role="img" is present with a current summary label naming symbol, interval, last price and delta
  And the label updates when the underlying data changes

Scenario: Focus survives resize and zoom
  Given the data cursor is on bar 4,200
  When the window is resized and the chart is zoomed twice
  Then the cursor remains on bar 4,200 and keyboard focus is not lost
```

## Technical notes / design
**Why world coordinates.** The cursor is `{ time: number, price: number }`, not `{ x, y }`. Every pixel-space event (resize, DPR change, zoom, pan, LOD step) would otherwise invalidate it. This one decision is what makes the "focus survives resize" scenario trivially true rather than a pile of special cases.

**Windowing.** The mirror materialises `visibleUnits  intersect  focusableWindow`, where the focusable window is the visible range clamped to a hard cap (default 500 nodes). At LOD >= L1 the mirror mirrors **columns**, not bars, and its label says so ("12 bars aggregated") — this is how mirror and canvas stay in agreement at every LOD, satisfying the desync scenario.

**Throttling.** A per-field latest-value cell plus a single timer:

```ts
class ThrottledField {
  private latest: string | null = null;
  set(v: string) { this.latest = v; }            // called at tick rate
  flush() {                                       // called at the throttle cadence
    if (this.latest !== null && this.latest !== this.rendered) {
      this.node.textContent = this.latest;        // text swap only, node preserved
      this.rendered = this.latest;
    }
  }
}
```

The node is never destroyed or recreated — §6.2's region-hygiene rule, and the single most common cause of "the screen reader stopped announcing" defects.

**Frame synchrony.** The `a11y` message is emitted by the worker in the same frame as the `viewport`/`pick` messages it derives from, so the main thread applies mirror updates from a consistent snapshot rather than interleaving two frames' state.

**Config keys**: `a11y.announceCadenceMs` (default 2000), `a11y.reduceAnnouncements` (bool), `a11y.mirrorNodeCap` (default 500), `a11y.politenessByClass` (map).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: cursor stepping at range boundaries; world-coordinate persistence across resize/zoom/LOD; windowing cap; throttle latest-value semantics with a `TestClock`; node-preservation assertion (same DOM node identity before and after an update); politeness routing.
- **Property** (fast-check): over random pan/zoom/LOD sequences, mirror focused unit == renderer focused unit, every frame.
- **Integration**: keyboard-only traversal of a full chart with `@testing-library` — no pointer events dispatched at all.
- **A11y automation**: axe-core zero violations on every chart route; assertions that the canvas has `role="img"` with a non-empty, updating label; live-region presence-on-load assertions.
- **Manual** (feeds E11-Q05): NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS passes over pan, zoom, crosshair stepping, LOD change and context loss.
- **Perf**: mirror maintenance <=1 ms per frame; asserted under the B5 scene so the a11y layer cannot silently consume the frame budget.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — the mirror exposes prices and volumes that are already on screen. It introduces no new data to a new surface.

One real consideration: the mirror is real DOM containing formatted values, so it is subject to the app's CSP and XSS posture like any other DOM. Control: values are written with `textContent`, **never** `innerHTML`, so a malformed or hostile symbol name or number string cannot become markup. This is an explicit test assertion, not a convention.

No secrets, no credentials, no account identifiers. Reviewed under E11-X03.

## Accessibility notes
This Story **is** the accessibility contract of the chart engine. Binding requirements from `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6:
- §6.1 layer 1 — windowed offscreen DOM mirror using the canvas-control-surrogate pattern, visually hidden by `clip-path` and never `display:none` (which would remove it from the accessibility tree entirely).
- §6.2 layer 2 — pre-rendered live regions with text-content-only swaps; polite for ambient, `role="alert"` for discrete; ambient throttled to a user-configurable cadence with a "reduce announcements" master toggle.
- §6.4 layer 4 — canvas `role="img"` with a rolling summary label.
- §3.1.6 — no hover-only and no drag-only functionality: the keyboard crosshair is the **primary** path (CMP-190), pointer hover is the convenience layer.
- Focus is visible via CMP-004 FocusRing and focus order follows the visual order of panes.
- WCAG 2.2 AA throughout; axe-core zero violations is a merge gate; NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the accessibility specialist in E11-Q05.
- Design source: **E11-D07** (a11y design review) and **E11-D02** (chart chassis).

## Performance notes
The mirror must cost <=1 ms per frame under the B5 scene, and node count is hard-capped at 500 — an unwindowed mirror of 100k bars would blow both the accessibility tree and the frame budget, which is exactly why §6.1 specifies windowing. Announcement throttling is a *performance* control for screen readers as much as a usability one: an unthrottled 20 Hz feed makes a screen reader unusable. Mirror updates are batched into one DOM write per frame, never one per unit.

## Observability
Counters: `engine.a11y.mirror_nodes`, `engine.a11y.announcements_per_minute` (per politeness class), `engine.a11y.mirror_update_ms`, `engine.a11y.desync_detected` (must remain 0 — an alerting condition, since desync is never acceptable per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4). Analytics events owned by the app layer: `chart.data_cursor_used`, `a11y.reduce_announcements_toggled`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S07** — the crosshair/readout state the cursor and announcements are derived from.
- **E11-S08** — hit-testing supplies the focused-unit resolution used by both pointer and keyboard paths.
- **E11-S12** — the LOD level the mirror must report to stay in sync.
- **E11-D07** — the a11y design review must be signed off before this Story starts (design-ahead rule).
- Blocks **E11-S14** (the data table consumes the same query surface) and every later canvas Epic (E18, E19, E21), which register unit types against the mirror.

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-a11y-mirror` · 3 PRs (query surface + mirror; data cursor + key map; live regions + canvas label), each <=400 LOC.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` — engine architecture (scene graph 3.1, render loop 3.2, data model 3.3, GL backend 3.4, viewport math 3.5, LOD 3.6, SDF text 3.7, heatmap streaming 3.8, hit-testing 3.9, interaction 3.11, plugin API 3.12, worker protocol 6, memory 7, API sketch 8, benchmarks 13, tests 14, milestones 15, open items 16)

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030 (a11y section), SCR-045

_Estimate note: re-pointed 8 → 5 during epic-level right-sizing — DOM mirror reuses the windowing utilities and axis label model already built in E11-S06/E11-S14. No acceptance criteria were dropped._

title: Ship the SCR-045 data-table alternative as an equal-status chart view
body:
## Context
`US-CHART-014` (Must) requires a tabular, readable alternative to the canvas so that "chart content is not lost to me", and its NFR is emphatic: **"this view is treated as an equal-status alternative, not a degraded fallback."** `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 repeats the point — the table "is not a stripped-down compliance minimum; it exposes the **same data fidelity** as the visual cell so a screen-reader/keyboard-only user is not second-class" — and SCR-045 makes it a sign-off criterion that the table is "reachable from the chart panel header, not hidden in settings — equal status verified".

This is layer 3 of the three-layer canvas strategy. Layers 1, 2 and 4 ship in E11-S13.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-045** — chart data-table alternative, opened by `Alt+T` from any chart and from a control in the chart panel header (not from settings).
- A real semantic `<table>` with `<th scope="col">` headers and the price/time cell as `<th scope="row">` — not a `div` grid with ARIA bolted on.
- Column set for the chart table: **time, open, high, low, close, volume, delta, CVD**, plus an expandable per-bar footprint cell list (price, bid, ask, delta, imbalance flag) — the footprint sub-rows are populated by E18; this Story ships the expandable row mechanism and renders "—" until then.
- Interactions per SCR-045: arrow keys move, `Enter` expands a bar's cells, `Ctrl+C` copies the selection as TSV, per-row actions (create alert here, replay from here, add note) exposed as extension points registered by E40/E26/E41.
- **Tri-state sort** on activating a column header (`Enter`/`Space`): ascending -> descending -> natural default order, announced via `aria-sort`; sort state persists while the table is open and resets when the focused bar/level changes.
- **Filter toolbar** above the table for filter-only columns; filters narrow rows, never remove columns; active-filter state announced via a live region ("Showing 6 of 40 rows, filtered by: Bid-stacked").
- **Live sync, not a snapshot**: the table reads the same windowed query surface as the DOM mirror (E11-S13). On each throttled tick, **row values are patched in place** — cell text updated, row DOM identity preserved — so screen-reader focus and active sort/filter survive live updates.
- **Stale banner**: if the focused bar/level scrolls out of view, show "Data is for bar X, no longer in view — press Alt+T to refresh to current" rather than going silently stale.
- **Bidirectional crosshair sync** (`US-CHART-014` scenario 3): moving the crosshair moves the table's focused row, and moving the table's focused row moves the crosshair.
- **Summary announcement**: a "request summary" action announcing a concise description of the visible range (trend, range, notable flags).
- Virtualisation: 100k rows without jank, <=8 ms scripting per scroll frame, reading the in-memory series so **no extra fetch is issued**.
- Components: CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell sub-row **content** — E18 (this Story ships the expandable mechanism and the column contract).
- The profile and DOM-ladder table variants of §6.3 — E19 and E21 respectively; they reuse the table shell built here.
- "Create alert here" / "replay from here" / "add note" **implementations** — E40, E26, E41 register against the row-action extension point.
- CSV/TSV export beyond `Ctrl+C` of the current selection — E15's export work.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The table is reachable as an equal-status view
  Given a chart pane is focused
  When the user presses Alt+T
  Then the data table opens showing the currently visible bars
  And an equivalent control is present in the chart panel header, not buried in settings

Scenario: The table carries the same data fidelity as the canvas
  Given a visible range of 480 bars is rendered on the canvas
  When the table is opened and its rows are compared to the rendered series
  Then every bar present on the canvas is present in the table with identical time, OHLC, volume and delta
  And an automated parity test asserts this over random ranges, not by spot check

Scenario: Live updates preserve focus, sort and filter
  Given the table is open, sorted by delta descending, filtered to flagged rows, with row 12 focused
  When three live update ticks arrive
  Then the values in place are updated and row 12 still has focus
  And the sort and filter are still applied, with no row node destroyed or recreated

Scenario: Sorting is tri-state and announced
  Given the table is in its natural order
  When the user activates the "delta" column header three times
  Then the order goes ascending, descending, then back to natural
  And aria-sort on that header reports "ascending", "descending", then "none"

Scenario: Crosshair and table stay in sync both ways
  Given the table is open with row 100 focused
  When the user moves the chart crosshair to bar 250
  Then the table's focused row moves to bar 250
  And when the user then arrows to row 251 in the table, the crosshair moves to bar 251

Scenario: A scrolled-away focus shows a banner, never silent staleness
  Given the table is showing data for bar X
  When the user pans the chart so bar X is no longer in the visible range
  Then a banner states the data is for bar X and is no longer in view, with a refresh instruction
  And the stale values are not presented as if they were current

Scenario: 100k rows scroll without jank
  Given a 100,000-bar series is loaded
  When the table is scrolled continuously
  Then scripting stays <= 8 ms per scroll frame
  And no additional network request is issued, because the table reads the in-memory series
```

## Technical notes / design
**Row identity is the whole design.** Rows are keyed by bar open time, and updates patch `textContent` on the existing cells. Destroying and rebuilding rows is what breaks screen-reader focus, and it is the defect this design exists to prevent — asserted by a DOM-node-identity test, not left to review.

**Virtualisation with real table semantics.** A naively virtualised `<table>` breaks row/column relationships for screen readers. The implementation renders a windowed `<tbody>` while declaring the full row count via `aria-rowcount` on the table and `aria-rowindex` on each rendered row, so AT reports "row 4,200 of 100,000" correctly — the WAI-ARIA grid pattern for virtualised tables.

**Bidirectional sync without loops.** Both surfaces subscribe to a single focused-unit store (the E11-S13 query surface). Neither writes to the other directly; each writes to the store and re-renders from it. Echo suppression is therefore structural — there is no cycle to suppress.

**Summary generation.** `summariseRange(visible)` -> "480 bars, 13:00 to 21:00 UTC, range 63,800 to 64,300, closed up 0.4 %, 3 bars flagged". Deterministic and unit-tested, so the announcement is reviewable text rather than an ad hoc string built at the call site.

## Test plan
- **Parity test** (the headline test): over random visible ranges, every bar rendered on the canvas appears in the table with identical values — this is the automated form of "equal status".
- **Unit**: tri-state sort cycling and `aria-sort` values; filter narrowing plus its live-region message; stale-banner trigger; `summariseRange` output; TSV serialisation of a selection.
- **DOM-identity test**: row nodes survive N live updates (asserting `===` node identity before/after).
- **Integration**: bidirectional crosshair<->row sync; `Alt+T` open/close and focus placement/restoration.
- **A11y**: axe-core zero violations; `aria-rowcount`/`aria-rowindex` correctness under virtualisation; NVDA/JAWS table-mode navigation (Ctrl+Alt+arrows) manual pass in **E11-Q05**; header-cell scope correctness.
- **Perf**: 100k-row scroll with <=8 ms scripting per frame; assertion that zero network requests are issued while the table is open.
- Coverage >=80 % (this is `apps/web` code, not engine package code).

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only**.

Two controls worth naming. First, all cell values are written with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`, so no formatted value can become markup. Second, `Ctrl+C` TSV export writes to the clipboard only on an explicit user gesture and copies **only the current selection** — it is not a path by which a page script can silently exfiltrate the whole series.

The row-action extension points (alert, replay, note) cross into Epics that do mutate state; the contract defined here passes an opaque bar reference and performs no privileged action itself. RBAC for those actions belongs to E09 and the registering Epic, and is explicitly not weakened by exposing the action here — a `viewer` sees the table, and the actions they lack permission for are simply not registered.

## Accessibility notes
This Story is the **normative accessible equivalent of SCR-030** and is verified in every a11y test pass (SCR-045's own wording). Requirements:
- Real `<table>` semantics with `<th scope="col">` and `<th scope="row">`; standard screen-reader table-mode navigation works.
- `aria-sort` on sortable headers, tri-state, announced.
- Filter state announced via a live region with counts ("Showing 6 of 40 rows").
- Fully keyboard-navigable grid: arrows, `Enter` to expand, `Ctrl+C` to copy; `Alt+T` to open from anywhere on the chart.
- Equal status is a **sign-off criterion**: reachable from the panel header, same data fidelity, not a degraded fallback.
- Delta signs are shown as text `+`/`-`, never colour-only; imbalance flags are text labels, never icon-only; `(estimated)` markers carry the literal word.
- Live updates preserve focus and do not flood — the table shares E11-S13's throttle cadence.
- Design source: **E11-D04** (table / empty / error hi-fi).

## Performance notes
SCR-045's budget: virtualised rendering of 100k rows with **<=8 ms scripting per scroll frame** and no extra fetch, since it reads the same in-memory series as the canvas. Live patching is O(visible rows), not O(series). Opening the table must not perturb the canvas frame budget — asserted by running the B5 benchmark with the table open.

## Observability
Analytics: `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported` (per SCR-045). Counters: `a11y.table.rows_rendered`, `a11y.table.patch_ms`, `a11y.table.stale_banner_shown`. The parity test result is published as a CI artefact so "equal status" is evidenced, not asserted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S13** — the windowed query surface, focused-unit store and throttle cadence the table reads from.
- **E11-D04** — hi-fi design for the table, empty and error states, signed off >=2 sprints earlier.
- **E05** — CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker from the design system.
- Blocks **E11-T09** (API freeze) and is extended by **E18** (footprint sub-rows), **E19**, **E21**.

## Branch
`feat/chart-engine-core-data-table` · 2 PRs (table shell + virtualisation + sort/filter; live patching + crosshair sync + summary), each <=400 LOC.

## References
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` — engine architecture (scene graph 3.1, render loop 3.2, data model 3.3, GL backend 3.4, viewport math 3.5, LOD 3.6, SDF text 3.7, heatmap streaming 3.8, hit-testing 3.9, interaction 3.11, plugin API 3.12, worker protocol 6, memory 7, API sketch 8, benchmarks 13, tests 14, milestones 15, open items 16)

title: Provide a degraded-2d Canvas fallback when WebGL2 is unavailable
body:
## Context
Requirement **R9** of `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`: the engine "runs in a `degraded-2d` mode (candles + axes + lines only) if WebGL2 is unavailable". SCR-048 makes the user-facing half explicit — the "WebGL-unavailable fallback message names the fallback path" — and the Epic's acceptance criteria are blunt about the failure mode to avoid: the user is "told which capabilities are reduced and why, **never shown a blank canvas**".

This is not hypothetical. WebGL2 is disabled by policy on some managed Windows fleets, blocked by GPU driver blocklists, and unavailable in software-rendering fallbacks after a driver crash. The owner runs the terminal through an Electron shell on Windows, so a driver blocklist hit is a realistic Tuesday, not a corner case.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `src/render/Canvas2dBackend.ts` implementing the same `RenderBackend` interface as the WebGL2 backend (E11-S02), so the scene graph, viewport, layout, LOD and interaction layers are entirely unaware which backend is active.
- Supported in `degraded-2d`: **candles, axes, gridlines, crosshair, line series, order/position lines and drawings**. Text via Canvas 2D `fillText` (§3.7 fallback). Footprint limited to **L2/L3** (coloured cell or hidden, no cell text).
- Not supported and explicitly disclosed: heatmap, bubbles, profile shading, any GPU-only effect.
- **Capability probe** (built in E11-S02) selects the `RenderProfile`; this Task adds the `degraded-2d` profile and the selection rules: no WebGL2 -> `degraded-2d`; WebGL2 present but a required extension missing -> `degraded-gl`; otherwise `full`.
- **Capability disclosure UI contract**: the engine reports `{ profile, reducedCapabilities: string[], reason }` so SCR-048 can name what is reduced and why, and SCR-118 (renderer settings) can offer a manual override.
- Manual override `renderer.forceProfile` for support and for testing — the same switch QA uses in E11-Q07's GPU matrix.
- Frame budget in this mode is deliberately relaxed to **>=30 fps at 20k bars**; it is a usable-degraded mode, not a parity mode, and saying so prevents a pointless optimisation effort later.

## Out of scope
- WebGPU backend — an explicit future seam only (§3.4), not built.
- Bringing footprint cell text, heatmap or bubbles to Canvas 2D — out of scope by design; those surfaces are disclosed as reduced.
- The SCR-048 error-state UI itself — E10/E15 chrome, consuming this Task's capability report.
- Context-loss recovery within WebGL2 — E11-S02.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No WebGL2 degrades instead of failing
  Given a runtime whose capability probe reports no WebGL2 support
  When a chart is mounted
  Then the degraded-2d profile is selected and candles, axes, gridlines and lines render through Canvas 2D
  And no blank canvas and no thrown error is ever presented to the user

Scenario: Reduced capabilities are named, not merely implied
  Given degraded-2d is active
  When the capability report is surfaced on SCR-048
  Then it names each reduced capability and the reason in plain language
  And a link to renderer settings offers a manual override

Scenario: The backend swap is invisible to the rest of the engine
  Given the same scene, viewport and interaction sequence
  When it is executed against the WebGL2 backend and the Canvas 2D backend
  Then both produce the same viewport state, the same pick results and the same DOM-mirror content
  And no code outside src/render branches on the active backend

Scenario: Footprint degrades to colour-only rather than disappearing
  Given footprint is enabled and degraded-2d is active
  When a frame is rendered
  Then cells render at L2 as coloured cells with no text
  And the aggregation and reduced-detail disclosure states that cell text is unavailable in this mode

Scenario: The degraded mode remains usable
  Given degraded-2d with 20,000 bars loaded
  When the user pans continuously for 10 seconds
  Then the frame rate stays at or above 30 fps
  And pan, zoom, crosshair and the keyboard data cursor all behave identically to the full profile
```

## Technical notes / design
The `RenderBackend` interface is the whole design, and it is defined in E11-S02 before either implementation exists precisely so the 2D path is a peer rather than a bolt-on:

```ts
interface RenderBackend {
  readonly profile: RenderProfile;          // "full" | "degraded-gl" | "degraded-2d"
  readonly capabilities: Capabilities;      // what this backend can actually draw
  resize(w: number, h: number, dpr: number): void;
  beginFrame(theme: EngineTheme): void;
  drawBatch(batch: DrawBatch): void;         // batches are backend-agnostic
  endFrame(): FrameStats;
  dispose(): void;
}
```

`DrawBatch` is expressed in primitives both backends can honour (quads, lines, polylines, text runs); GPU-only batch kinds declare `requires: Capability[]` and are skipped with a disclosure entry rather than silently dropped — a skipped batch with no disclosure is the exact failure mode ("silently wrong chart") this design forbids.

Canvas 2D performance technique: batch by style to minimise state changes, use a single `Path2D` per style bucket, and draw candle bodies as a single `fill()` per colour bucket rather than per candle. That is what makes 20k bars at 30 fps achievable in 2D at all.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: profile-selection rules for each probe outcome; capability-report contents; batch `requires` filtering and disclosure emission.
- **Cross-backend equivalence** (the headline test): the same scripted scene and interaction sequence run against both backends must agree on viewport state, pick results and DOM-mirror content.
- **Golden image**: candles, axes, grid, crosshair and lines in `degraded-2d` for each theme, compared to a `degraded-2d` reference (not to the WebGL reference — the two are legitimately different renderings).
- **Integration**: WebGL2 forcibly disabled (`--disable-webgl2` / stubbed `getContext`) asserting a usable chart and a correct SCR-048 disclosure.
- **Perf**: >=30 fps at 20k bars panning for 10 s.
- **E2E**: manual override via `renderer.forceProfile` round-trips, used as the mechanism for **E11-Q07**'s GPU matrix.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **public market data only** — no PII, no credentials, no account identifiers. `packages/chart-engine` holds no secrets and performs no I/O (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16), so spoofing/repudiation/elevation-of-privilege are out of band (they belong to E17's WS auth and E09's RBAC).

Residual STRIDE surface handled here (modelled in E11-X01): **Tampering** — typed arrays arriving from the decoder must be bounds- and value-validated before indexing (a hostile or corrupt frame must never become an out-of-bounds read or a `NaN` that poisons the viewport). **Denial of service** — every buffer has a hard ceiling (`maxBars`, `memoryBudgetMb`) so a malformed length field cannot allocate unboundedly.

Controls applied: no `eval`, no `Function` constructor, no shader source derived from data; worker constructed from a same-origin bundled URL so the page CSP needs no `worker-src blob:` widening; dependencies pinned and covered by npm audit / Dependabot. No security review label required beyond the epic-level E11-X03 sweep.

## Accessibility notes
- The degraded mode must be **fully equivalent in accessibility**: the DOM mirror, keyboard data cursor, live regions and the SCR-045 table are main-thread DOM and are entirely unaffected by which backend draws pixels. This is asserted by the cross-backend equivalence test, so an a11y regression cannot hide in the fallback path.
- Capability disclosure is **text**, not an icon or a colour: SCR-048's `role="alert"` region with plain-language copy and a copyable correlation id.
- A blank canvas is the worst possible outcome for every user and a completely silent one for a screen-reader user — hence the "never a blank canvas" acceptance criterion.

## Performance notes
Deliberately relaxed: >=30 fps at 20k bars, versus >=60 fps at 100k bars for the full profile. This mode is excluded from the B1–B10 gates (which assume WebGL2) and has its own single benchmark, so a machine without a GPU cannot fail the main perf gate and a slow 2D path cannot hide behind it either.

## Observability
`ready` message carries `{ profile, capabilities, reason }`. Errors: `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2` (informational, recoverable — it selects the fallback rather than failing). Counter `engine.render.profile` reported in `frame` stats and on SCR-046, so every perf report states which backend produced it. Analytics `chart.render_profile_selected` owned by the app layer.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or findings triaged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per Gherkin scenario (E11-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals including the `packages/chart-engine` code owner.

## Dependencies
- **E11-S02** — defines `RenderBackend`, the capability probe and `RenderProfile`; this Task adds the second implementation.
- Consumed by **E11-Q07** (GPU matrix exploratory) and by SCR-048/SCR-118 chrome in E10/E15.

## Branch

title: Feed the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay with telemetry and a copy snapshot
body:
## Context
When the owner reports "the chart felt slow around 14:30", the difference between a one-hour investigation and a five-minute one is whether the report arrives with numbers attached. **SCR-046** is that mechanism: a `Ctrl+Shift+D` overlay showing FPS, frame-time p50/p95, draw calls, GPU memory, buffer uploads/s, WS message rate, dropped frames, and a **"copy diagnostics" button used in bug reports**.

The engine already computes all of this for the benchmark harness (E11-T06). This Task exposes the same numbers at runtime, under a strict cost ceiling — SCR-046 requires the overlay itself to cost **<=0.5 ms per frame** and to sample at **2 Hz, not per frame**, because a diagnostics panel that perturbs the thing it measures is worse than none.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Extend the `frame` worker->main message (E11-T02, §6) to a full stats payload: `fps`, frame time p50/p95, draw calls, triangles, uploaded bytes/s, LOD levels per layer, GPU memory estimate, render profile, dropped-frame count, decode p95, and **WS->pixel latency** (the end-to-end number SCR-046 calls for).
- Sampling: **1 Hz in production, 2 Hz when the overlay is open, full per-frame in bench mode** — three modes, one code path, selected by a flag.
- Per-stage timings from the nine `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 stages, so the overlay attributes cost to a stage rather than showing one opaque total.
- **`copyDiagnostics()`** producing a structured, pasteable snapshot: engine version, commit SHA, render profile, capability report, theme/density, symbol/interval, visible bar count, the full stats block, the last 20 engine error events with codes, and the backend **correlation id** carried on the WS envelope.
- Correlation with the backend: the WS envelope's span id is included so a client-side slow frame can be joined to a backend trace.
- Threshold colouring **paired with text** ("below budget") per SCR-046's sign-off checklist — never colour alone.
- Overlay hidden by default, enabled from SCR-118 (renderer settings), toggled with `Ctrl+Shift+D`.
- Components: CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile.

## Out of scope
- The overlay's visual design — **E11-D02**'s diagnostics section; this Task supplies the data contract it binds to.
- Backend system-health data (`system` topic) — E10/E44 own the `SystemHealthTile` data source; the overlay composes both.
- Uploading diagnostics anywhere — copy-to-clipboard only, by explicit user action. The engine performs no I/O.
- Prometheus/Grafana metrics — backend observability, E44/E46.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The overlay costs less than it measures
  Given the diagnostics overlay is open during the B5 benchmark scene
  When frame time is compared with the overlay open and closed
  Then the overlay adds at most 0.5 ms per frame
  And it samples at 2 Hz, not once per frame

Scenario: A copied snapshot is sufficient for triage without follow-up questions
  Given a user presses "copy diagnostics" during a slow period
  When the clipboard contents are inspected
  Then they contain engine version, commit SHA, render profile, capabilities, symbol, interval, visible bars, the full stats block, the last 20 error events and the backend correlation id
  And pasting it into an issue requires no further information to begin investigation

Scenario: Thresholds are never colour-only
  Given frame time exceeds its budget
  When the overlay displays it
  Then the value is accompanied by the text "above budget"
  And the meaning is fully available to a user who cannot distinguish the colours

Scenario: Sampling mode follows context
  Given the overlay is closed in a production build
  Then stats are sampled at 1 Hz
  And when the overlay is opened sampling rises to 2 Hz, and in bench mode it is per-frame

Scenario: Client and backend traces can be joined
  Given a frame rendered from a WS message carrying span id X
  When the diagnostics snapshot is copied
  Then it contains span id X
  And the backend trace for X can be retrieved without correlating by timestamp
```

## Technical notes / design
Stats are accumulated in a **pre-allocated ring buffer** in the worker (600 samples ~ 10 s at 60 fps) and reduced to percentiles at the sampling cadence, so per-frame cost is a few array writes and nothing else. Percentiles come from the ring, not from a growing array — that is what keeps the "measuring costs nothing" property true.

```ts
interface FrameStats {
  fps: number; frameMsP50: number; frameMsP95: number;
  drawCalls: number; triangles: number; uploadedBytesPerSec: number;
  lod: Record<LayerId, number>; gpuMemoryMb: number;
  profile: RenderProfile; droppedFrames: number;
  decodeMsP95: number; wsToPixelMsP95: number;
  stages: Record<StageId, number>;   // the nine 4.3 stages
}
```

**WS->pixel latency** is measured by carrying the message's receive timestamp through the decode -> model -> batch -> present path and differencing at present. It is the only number here that crosses the worker boundary in both directions, and it is the one that actually answers "is it the network or the renderer".

`copyDiagnostics()` returns Markdown, because its destination is a GitHub issue.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ring-buffer percentile correctness against a reference implementation; sampling-mode selection; snapshot serialisation completeness (asserted field by field against the SCR-046 required list); Markdown escaping of symbol names.
- **Perf**: overlay open vs closed during B5, asserting <=0.5 ms delta; assertion that stats accumulation allocates zero bytes per frame.
- **Integration**: WS->pixel latency measured against a fixture with known injected delays, asserting the reported figure tracks the injected one.
- **A11y**: axe-core on the overlay; assertion that values update **politely**, not assertively (SCR-046's explicit requirement, since an assertive diagnostics panel would flood a screen reader); assertion that every threshold indication has a text equivalent.
- **E2E**: `Ctrl+Shift+D` toggle, pin-open behaviour, copy-to-clipboard round-trip.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Data classification: **diagnostic telemetry**. The relevant threat, named in the Epic's STRIDE surface, is **information disclosure**: SCR-046 is designed to be screenshotted and pasted into issues, so its contents become as public as the issue tracker.

Controls: the snapshot contains **no account identifiers, no API keys, no order or position data, no user identity** — only engine timing, capability and error information plus an opaque correlation id. The correlation id is opaque by construction (a random span id, not an encoding of anything). A test asserts the snapshot's field set matches an allowlist, so a future contributor cannot casually add "current account" to a payload designed to be pasted in public.

Copy happens only on explicit user gesture; nothing is transmitted anywhere. Reviewed under **E11-X03**.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-046's own a11y requirements, which this Task's data contract must support:
- The overlay is a **text panel, not a canvas**, and can be pinned open and read as a static table.
- Values update **politely** so a screen reader is not flooded — the 2 Hz cadence is an accessibility control as much as a performance one.
- **Threshold colouring is paired with text** ("below budget" / "above budget"); colour is never the sole carrier.
- The copy control is a real, keyboard-operable button with a confirmation announcement ("Diagnostics copied").
- Design source: **E11-D02**.

## Performance notes
Hard ceiling from SCR-046: **<=0.5 ms per frame** for the overlay, sampled at **2 Hz**. Stats accumulation in the worker is allocation-free and costs <=0.05 ms per frame. Production sampling at 1 Hz is cheap enough to leave permanently on, which is what makes the numbers available when a user reports a problem rather than only when someone thought to enable them.

## Observability
This Task *is* the observability surface for the engine. It exposes the counters and error codes defined across E11: `ENGINE_CONTEXT_LOST`, `ENGINE_CONTEXT_RESTORE_FAILED`, `ENGINE_NO_WEBGL2`, `ENGINE_MEMORY_PRESSURE`, `ENGINE_LOD_STEPDOWN`, `ENGINE_FRAME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, `ENGINE_DECODE_ERROR`, `ENGINE_THEME_INVALID`, `ENGINE_ATLAS_CACHE_INVALID`. Analytics: `diagnostics.overlay_toggled`, `diagnostics.snapshot_copied` (per SCR-046).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage >= 85 % of new/changed lines in `packages/chart-engine` (>= 80 % for `apps/web` binding code); CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the design; package README/TSDoc updated; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] axe-core CI green on touched chart routes (default-on: this package ships a UI surface).
- [ ] Benchmark run recorded against the affected budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; no regression beyond 5 % of baseline.

title: Freeze the public engine API, document it and amend the ADR for open item O2
body:
## Context
Six Epics compile against `packages/chart-engine` — E12 series, E13 indicators, E14 drawings, E15 layouts, E18 footprint, E21 DOM/heatmap — and they start in R1 and R2 with no opportunity to absorb churn in a shared interface. `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10's interface-first rule made the API a **first** deliverable (E11-T01); this Task makes it a **finished** one: frozen, documented and versioned, so downstream Epics build against a contract rather than a moving target.

It also closes the Epic's documentation obligations: `26-chart-engine-design.md` must describe what shipped rather than what was proposed, and open item **O2** (SDF atlas size and glyph set), answered empirically by E11-K01 and E11-S11, must be recorded as an **ADR amendment** — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2 requires every spike's decision to land as an ADR, including a decision to defer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **API freeze**: review the surface of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §8 against what shipped — `ChartOptions`, `Chart`, `Pane`, `SeriesType`, `SeriesOptionsMap`, `SeriesHandle`, `ChartEvents`, `FrameStats`, `RenderContext`, `SeriesPlugin`, `IndicatorPlugin` — and mark it stable at **v1.0.0** of the package.
- **Semver policy** for the package recorded in its README: a breaking change to the plugin interface is a major bump and requires a migration note plus sign-off from every consuming Epic's lead. Experimental surfaces live under an `unstable_` prefix and are explicitly outside the freeze.
- **API-extract check in CI**: a generated API report (`api-extractor`-style `.api.md`) committed to the repo; any change to the public surface produces a diff in that file, so an accidental public-surface change is impossible to merge unnoticed.
- **TSDoc on every exported symbol**, with a documented example per plugin interface — the plugin interfaces are what E12/E13/E14/E18/E21 implement, so an undocumented one costs five teams.
- **Package README**: architecture overview, quick start, the plugin authoring guide, the config-key reference (every `lod.*`, `memory.*`, `theme.*`, `a11y.*`, `renderer.*` key defined across E11), and the engine error-code table.
- **`26-chart-engine-design.md` reconciliation**: update §3, §6, §7, §8 and §13 to shipped behaviour; where the implementation diverged from the design, record the divergence and its reason rather than silently editing the design to match.
- **ADR amendment for O2**: amend `ADR-0002-custom-webgl-chart-engine.md` with the measured glyph set, atlas size, generation cost and cache strategy from E11-K01/E11-S11, closing the open item in §16.
- Storybook coverage check for the chart-primitive components the Epic ships: CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226.
- Handoff session with the E12/E13/E14/E15/E18/E21 leads walking the plugin seam and the config surface.

## Out of scope
- Publishing the package externally — it is internal to the monorepo; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §1 explicitly rules out third-party distribution.
- Freezing internal (non-exported) structure — internals stay free to change; that freedom is the point of having a narrow public surface.
- Resolving open items O3, O4 and O5 — owned by M4, M5 and M8 in later Epics (E21, E13, E11-Q05 respectively).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The public surface cannot change without a visible diff
  Given the committed API report for packages/chart-engine
  When a PR adds an exported symbol or changes an exported signature
  Then the API report file shows a diff and the CI check fails until it is committed
  And an unintended public-surface change cannot merge unnoticed

Scenario: The design document matches what shipped
  Given 26-chart-engine-design.md sections 3, 6, 7, 8 and 13
  When each is compared against the implementation
  Then every documented interface, message, budget and benchmark gate matches the code
  And each deliberate divergence is recorded with its reason, not silently edited away

Scenario: Open item O2 is closed by an ADR amendment
  Given E11-K01 and E11-S11 measured the glyph set, atlas size and generation cost
  When ADR-0002 is amended
  Then the amendment records the chosen glyph set, the 1024x1024 atlas decision, the measured generation cost and the cache strategy
  And open item O2 in section 16 is marked closed with a link to the amendment

Scenario: A downstream team can write a plugin from the docs alone
  Given a developer from the E13 indicators team with no prior engine exposure
  When they follow the plugin authoring guide in the package README
  Then they can implement and register a working indicator plugin without asking the engine team a question
  And this is verified by actually doing it during the handoff session

Scenario: Every exported symbol is documented
  Given the public API surface
  When TSDoc coverage is measured
  Then every exported symbol has a description, and every plugin interface has a usage example
  And a missing TSDoc comment on an exported symbol fails lint
```

## Technical notes / design
**The API report is the mechanism, not the policy.** A generated `.api.md` committed to the repo turns "did we change the public API?" from a judgement call in review into a diff. It is the cheapest possible enforcement of an interface freeze and the reason this Task is 3 points rather than a documentation marathon.

**What "frozen" means in practice**, written down so it is not re-litigated per PR:
- Additive changes (new optional option, new event, new plugin hook with a default) — minor bump, no sign-off.
- Breaking changes (removed/renamed export, changed signature, changed semantics) — major bump, migration note, sign-off from every consuming Epic lead.
- `unstable_`-prefixed exports — outside the freeze, may change in any release, and may not be used by another Epic without an explicit note in that Epic's ticket.

**Divergence recording.** Where implementation diverged from design, the doc gets a short "Shipped behaviour differs: … because …" note rather than a rewrite. A design document quietly retrofitted to match the code loses the history of why, which is the main thing a reader six months later needs.

## Test plan
- **CI check**: API report diff detection (self-tested by adding a throwaway export and asserting the check fails).
- **Lint rule**: missing TSDoc on an exported symbol fails.
- **Doc-example compilation**: every code example in the README and in TSDoc is type-checked as part of the build, so examples cannot rot silently.
- **Storybook coverage check**: asserts a story exists for each of CMP-180, CMP-188, CMP-189, CMP-190, CMP-197, CMP-198, CMP-199, CMP-226.
- **Handoff verification**: the "developer writes a plugin from the docs alone" scenario is executed with a real E13 engineer during the handoff session and its outcome recorded on the ticket.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this Task produces documentation, a version policy and a CI check.

Two security-relevant points to record in the README rather than leave as folklore. First, the engine's **no-I/O invariant** (`CONSTITUTION.md` C-2.16) is part of the public contract — a plugin that performs `fetch`, opens a WebSocket or touches storage violates it, and the framework-free boundary check enforces it. Second, the **plugin seam is a trust boundary in the making**: plugins are first-party TypeScript compiled into the bundle in v1, so they carry the app's privileges. Any future third-party or user-authored plugin would need a sandbox, and the README states this explicitly so nobody later assumes the seam was designed for untrusted code. Reviewed as part of **E11-X03**.

## Accessibility notes
The plugin authoring guide must state the accessibility obligations a plugin inherits, because a plugin that draws to the canvas without registering mirror units is an accessibility regression that no automated check will catch:
- Any plugin rendering a focusable unit **must** register it with the DOM mirror (E11-S13).
- Any plugin encoding meaning **must** use a registered pattern/hatch in addition to colour (E11-T04).
- Any plugin adding a surface with data **must** contribute columns to the SCR-045 table (E11-S14).
These are documented as contract requirements with the rationale, not listed as suggestions.

## Performance notes
The plugin guide documents the frame-path rules every plugin must honour: no allocation in the frame path, no string formatting per frame (use cached glyph runs), batch by style, respect the LOD level supplied by the engine, and stay within the draw-call budget (<=18 per pane). The engine cannot enforce these at runtime without cost, so they are contract plus review plus the benchmark gate — which is why the benchmark harness (E11-T06) is a required check on the package.

## Observability
The engine error-code table is published in the README as the canonical list, so support and the diagnostics overlay share one vocabulary. The API report file doubles as a changelog input for the package.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.

- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
