title: Add line, area, baseline, hollow-candle and Heikin-Ashi series types
body:
## Context
**US-CHART-002 (Should)**: "I want OHLC bars, line, area, Heikin-Ashi and a volume column pane, so that I can read price the way the situation demands." Two of its three scenarios are behavioural rather than visual, and both matter more than the drawing itself:

1. **"the transform is applied client-side with no refetch and drawings stay anchored to real time/price"** — Heikin-Ashi is a *derived view* of the same bars, so switching to it must not touch the network and must not move a single drawing.
2. **"When I request Heikin-Ashi together with footprint cells, then I am told footprint requires a real-price bar type and offered to switch back"** — an incompatible combination must be refused with an explanation and a way out, not silently rendered wrong.

CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle already specifies the control: SegmentedControl semantics, "each option names the chart type in text (icons alone are insufficient)", and footprint as a separate `aria-pressed` toggle because it composes with any base type.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `LineSeries`, `AreaSeries`, `BaselineSeries` and `HollowCandleSeries` as `SeriesPlugin` implementations, using the `line` and `bar` programs of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §4 with instanced thick-line segments.
- Heikin-Ashi as a **client-side transform** over the bound time series: `haClose = (o+h+l+c)/4`, `haOpen = (prevHaOpen + prevHaClose)/2`, `haHigh/haLow` from the extremes, computed incrementally on the worker thread and rendered by the existing candle series — no refetch, no new subscription, no new spec.
- Baseline series with a configurable reference level and distinct above/below fills from theme tokens.
- Chart-type switching within ≤100 ms (US-CHART-002 NFR), preserving the visible time window, the price-scale mode and every drawing's anchor.
- Incompatibility handling: requesting Heikin-Ashi with footprint cells enabled produces an explicit explanatory message offering to switch back, rendered through the design system's inline-message pattern rather than a toast that disappears.
- CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle wired to the engine, with every option named in text.

## Out of scope
- Volume column pane — E12-S08.
- Footprint cells themselves — E18 (this Story only implements the refusal when the two are combined).
- Compare/overlay symbol (US-CHART-011) — E15/E11 scope.
- Server-side Heikin-Ashi bar construction — HA is deliberately not a `BarSpec.kind`; it is a view transform.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Heikin-Ashi switches without a refetch
  Given a BTCUSDT 5m candle chart with three drawings
  When I switch to Heikin-Ashi
  Then no network request is made
  And the transform is applied within 100 ms
  And every drawing remains anchored to its original time and price

Scenario: Heikin-Ashi maths is correct and incremental
  Given a known bar sequence with a known HA reference output
  Then the computed HA series matches the reference exactly
  And appending one new bar updates only the last HA bar rather than recomputing the series

Scenario: Incompatible combination is explained, not rendered wrong
  Given footprint cells are enabled
  When I select Heikin-Ashi
  Then I am told footprint requires a real-price bar type
  And I am offered to switch back, with that offer reachable by keyboard
  And the chart continues to render the previous valid combination meanwhile

Scenario: Every type is named in text
  Given the chart-type toggle
  Then each option's accessible name states the chart type in words
  And the footprint toggle is a separate control with aria-pressed, not an option in the same group

Scenario: Baseline series honours its reference
  Given a baseline series with the reference set to the session open
  Then values above and below render with distinct fills from theme tokens
  And the distinction is not conveyed by colour alone
```

## Technical notes / design
- HA is computed on the worker thread against the columnar store, writing into a derived typed-array view rather than a copied series, so memory does not double at 100k bars.
- The HA recurrence depends on the previous HA bar, so a windowed view must seed from a deterministic warm-up point (a fixed number of bars before the visible window) and document it — otherwise scrolling changes the values, which is a classic and very visible HA bug.
- Line/area/baseline share the `line` program; area and baseline add a fill quad strip. Keep each series at its documented draw-call budget so the ≤18-call pane target survives.
- Drawings must not move: they anchor to real time/price, and the HA transform changes only the rendered geometry, never the anchor space.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: HA recurrence against a reference dataset, warm-up seeding, incremental append, baseline reference handling, line/area geometry.
- **Golden image** (SwiftShader): each series type in both themes, plus baseline above/below.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): switch through every chart type with drawings present; assert no network request on the HA switch, assert drawings unmoved, assert the incompatibility message appears and is keyboard-dismissible.
- **Perf**: chart-type switch timed against the 100 ms budget at 100k bars.
- **a11y**: axe-core on SCR-042 and the toggle; manual screen-reader pass confirming type names and the footprint toggle's separate semantics.

## Security notes
No new data path, no new inputs from the network — this Story consumes bars already validated at the store boundary by E12-S06. The only new surface is the chart-type preference persisted per pane (E15/E12-S12 own persistence); it is an enum, validated against the known set on load so a tampered stored workspace cannot select an arbitrary renderer.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-222's contract is binding: SegmentedControl semantics, every option named in text (icons alone insufficient), footprint as a separate `aria-pressed` toggle. The incompatibility message must be an inline, persistent, keyboard-reachable message with an actionable control — not a transient toast, which a screen-reader user may never perceive. Baseline above/below and HA up/down must be distinguishable without colour (fill pattern or outline), per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. The data-table alternative must state which chart type is active, and for HA must make clear the values shown are derived, not traded prices.

## Performance notes
Chart-type switch ≤100 ms (US-CHART-002 NFR) including the HA transform at 100k bars. No additional GPU memory beyond the derived HA view. Frame budget #1 unchanged — these series must not push a pane over 16.6 ms p95.

## Observability
`series_type_switch_duration_ms` histogram labelled by target type; `series_incompatible_combination_total{combination}` so a frequently attempted illegal combination becomes a product signal rather than a repeated user annoyance.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario backed by an automated test; frontend coverage ≥80%; golden images committed; switch-time benchmark recorded; axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass on the type toggle; design-QA pass against the CMP-222 spec; QA sign-off; demoed; feature-flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S06** — the candle series and the `SeriesPlugin` binding that HA renders through.
- **E05 / E11-T04** — theme tokens and LUT ingestion for baseline/area fills.

## Branch
`feat/e12-series-types`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-002 (Should)
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.12 plugin API, §4 render layers, §5 theming
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-222 ChartTypeToggle, CMP-221 ChartToolbar

title: Render the volume column sub-pane linked to the price pane
body:
## Context
US-CHART-002's second scenario: "When I enable the volume column pane, then it renders as a linked sub-pane sharing the time axis and crosshair." It is the smallest possible exercise of E11's multi-pane stacking (E11-S09) with a real data series in it — which makes it valuable out of proportion to its size, because it proves the pane-linking contract works before E13's indicator panes and E23's CVD panes depend on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A volume column series rendered in a linked sub-pane below the price pane, sharing the time axis, the visible range, the crosshair and the pan/zoom state via E11's pane-sync mechanism.
- Per-bar colouring from the bar's direction (up/down close) or from delta when `include_delta` data is present, always from theme tokens.
- Independent autoscale for the sub-pane's own value axis, with the shared time axis rendered once (the sub-pane does not duplicate time labels).
- Toggle on/off from the chart toolbar, with the pane's presence and height persisted per chart (persistence lands via E12-S12's chart settings).
- Correct behaviour on non-time-aligned series: volume columns follow the same index spacing as the bricks/range bars above them.
- Empty/partial handling: bars with null volume (kline-sourced pre-recording windows do carry volume, but tick-derived fields may be null) render honestly rather than as zero.

## Out of scope
- Volume moving average and OBV — **E13** indicators.
- Volume profile (horizontal) — **E19**.
- The Deep-Stats strip — **E20**.
- Pane stacking and sync machinery itself — **E11-S09**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Linked sub-pane shares the time axis
  Given the volume pane is enabled
  When I pan or zoom the price pane
  Then the volume pane follows exactly, with no drift at any zoom level
  And the time axis is drawn once, beneath the lowest pane

Scenario: Crosshair is shared
  When the crosshair moves over the price pane
  Then the volume pane shows the corresponding vertical position
  And the readout includes the volume for that bar

Scenario: Columns follow index spacing on renko
  Given a renko series
  Then volume columns align one-to-one with bricks by index
  And a brick with volume_allocated=false renders a zero-height column rather than a gap or an interpolated value

Scenario: Toggling does not disturb the price pane
  When I enable or disable the volume pane
  Then the price pane's visible range and price scale are unchanged
  And the layout reflows without a visible flash of empty chart

Scenario: Null volume is not shown as zero
  Given a bar whose volume is unavailable
  Then the column is omitted and the state is stated in the readout as unavailable
  And it is not drawn as a zero-height column implying no trading
```

## Technical notes / design
- The sub-pane uses the `bar` program with instanced quads — one draw call. It must not add a second time-axis renderer; the shared axis belongs to the pane stack (E11-S06).
- Autoscale for volume is independent of price autoscale but must respect the same lock/unlock affordances so the interaction model is consistent (E11-S05).
- Renko's `volume_allocated=false` bricks are the interesting case: zero-height is correct and intentional, and the tooltip/readout should say the volume is attributed to a neighbouring brick so the user is not confused by the visual.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: column geometry, direction/delta colour selection, null-volume handling, index-spacing alignment.
- **Golden image**: volume pane with time bars and with renko bars, both themes.
- **E2E**: toggle the pane, pan/zoom, assert sync; crosshair readout includes volume.
- **a11y**: axe-core; the data-table alternative includes a volume column and states unavailability in text.

## Security notes
No new inputs beyond the bars already validated at the store boundary. Defensive check: a negative or non-finite volume is rejected rather than producing an inverted or infinite column geometry.

## Accessibility notes
The volume pane must appear in the DOM mirror and the SCR-045 data table as a column, not only as pixels; the crosshair readout announces volume alongside OHLC within the ≤2/s live-region throttle of US-CHART-008. Up/down colouring must not be the only signal — the readout states the value in text. The pane toggle has a text name ("Volume pane") and its pressed state is programmatically exposed.

## Performance notes
One additional draw call and one instance buffer; must not push the pane stack over the ≤40 draw calls documented for a 3-pane chart, nor the p95 frame budget of 16.6 ms. Pane toggle reflow must not trigger a full data re-upload.

## Observability
Draw-call and frame-time attribution for `series.volume` in `FrameStats`, visible in the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay.

## Definition of Done

title: Select bar mode and parameters with a cancellable rebuild and history markers
body:
## Context
This Story is where the backend builders become a product feature. **US-CHART-003** ("Given I select 'volume bars, 1 500 contracts'…") and **US-CHART-004** ("When I change the brick or range size, then the series rebuilds from stored prints **with a progress indicator** and drawings re-anchor by timestamp") both terminate here, and both carry the NFR **"rebuild is cancellable; parameters persisted per chart template"**.

It is also where the product's honesty rules become visible. Two facts must be stated in text, never inferred: **where tick-accurate history begins** (US-CHART-003 scenario 3: "an explicit partial-history marker shows where tick data begins") and **that the x-axis no longer means clock time** for non-time-aligned modes (CMP-220's a11y contract: bar modes are "a separate labelled group with an explanatory note, since they change the meaning of the x-axis").

## Scope / Deliverables
- SCR-042 interval / bar-mode menu built on CMP-220 IntervalPicker + CMP-041 Menu: the time ladder, then a separately labelled bar-mode group (tick / volume / range / delta / renko) with the explanatory note and a CMP-069 InfoPanel describing what each mode does.
- Parameter entry per mode (trades per bar, base volume, ticks, delta threshold, brick size) with validation against the documented bounds from E12-T01/S02/S03/S04, showing the limit in the message when a value is rejected.
- Rebuild flow: changing a mode or parameter registers the new spec, shows determinate progress while the series rebuilds from stored prints, and **can be cancelled** — cancellation stops the backend rebuild (the mechanism chosen by ADR-0014) and restores the previous series.
- Drawings re-anchored by timestamp across the rebuild (they must not move).
- Partial-history marker: an explicit, text-stated boundary on the chart and in the empty/partial state (SCR-047) naming the timestamp where tick-accurate data begins, plus the `no_data_recorded` path when the whole window predates recording.
- Persistence of the bar mode and its parameter per chart via `chart_settings.bar_mode` (Postgres, E12-T02), restored on reload.
- Feature-flag gating for renko/range (`30-release-roadmap.md` §12 rung 2) so the descoping switch is a flag, not a code change.

## Out of scope
- Chart templates (US-CHART-012) and workspaces — E15 (this Story persists per-chart settings; templates compose them).
- The builders themselves (E12-S02/S03/S04) and the rebuild backend mechanism (E12-T03/T05).
- Footprint settings — E18.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Selecting a volume bar mode
  Given a BTCUSDT chart
  When I select "volume bars" with 1500 contracts
  Then the series rebuilds from stored prints with determinate progress
  And on completion the chart shows volume bars and the mode is persisted for that chart

Scenario: Rebuild is cancellable
  Given a rebuild is in progress
  When I cancel
  Then the rebuild stops within a second
  And the previous series is restored unchanged
  And no partial series is persisted or displayed

Scenario: Parameter bounds are explained
  When I enter a tick count below the documented minimum
  Then the value is rejected with a message stating the minimum
  And no rebuild is started

Scenario: Partial history is stated in text
  Given the recorder holds 3 days of prints and the view spans 30 days
  When I select tick bars
  Then bars are built for the available window
  And a marker states in text the timestamp where tick data begins
  And that statement is available to assistive technology

Scenario: Whole window predates recording
  Given the entire requested window is before recording began
  When I select a non-time bar mode
  Then the chart shows an explicit state explaining that tick-accurate data does not exist for this window
  And it offers to switch to time bars, which can be sourced from exchange klines

Scenario: Drawings survive the rebuild
  Given three drawings on the chart
  When the bar mode changes
  Then each drawing remains anchored to its original timestamps and prices

Scenario: Bar modes are presented as a distinct group
  Given the interval menu is open
  Then bar modes appear in a separately labelled group with an explanatory note
  And the note states that they change the meaning of the x-axis
  And the whole menu is operable by keyboard alone
```

## Technical notes / design
- Cancellation must propagate end to end: UI cancel → subscription teardown → backend rebuild cancellation (ADR-0014's mechanism). A UI-only cancel that leaves the backend grinding is a resource leak disguised as a feature.
- The previous series must be retained in memory (not evicted) while a rebuild is in flight so cancellation can restore it instantly without a refetch; the memory governor (E11-S15) must be told about this temporary retention.
- Rebuild progress is determinate where the total is known (trades to process) and switches to indeterminate with an explanation rather than a fake percentage when it is not.
- The renko/range feature flag gates the *menu entries*, so a descoped build simply does not offer them rather than offering them and failing.

## Test plan
- **Unit** ≥80%: parameter validation per mode, persistence round-trip, flag gating, progress-state machine including cancel.
- **E2E** (Playwright + Electron): select each bar mode, change a parameter, cancel a rebuild mid-flight, confirm drawings unmoved and the previous series restored; verify the partial-history marker on a truncated fixture.
- **Integration**: cancellation verified to stop backend work (assert the rebuild metric stops advancing).
- **a11y**: axe-core on SCR-042 and SCR-047; keyboard-only operation of the menu and parameter entry; screen-reader pass confirming the bar-mode group label, the explanatory note and the partial-history statement.

## Security notes
Parameters entered here become `param` on a topic and an endpoint, so client-side validation mirrors the server-side whitelist (E12-T01) — but the server remains authoritative; the client check is UX, not a control. Bounds exist specifically to prevent the CPU/storage-exhaustion cases documented on E12-S02/S03/S04, and rejecting client-side keeps well-behaved clients from ever issuing them. Persisted `chart_settings.bar_mode` is validated against the CHECK-constrained enum on read, so a tampered row cannot select an unsupported renderer.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-220's contract is binding and is largely an accessibility contract: the menu button's accessible name includes the current interval ("Interval: 15 minutes"); bar modes form a separate labelled group with an explanatory note because they change the meaning of the x-axis. Parameter inputs have visible labels, are announced with their units, and validation errors are associated with the input via `aria-describedby` and stated as text including the limit. Rebuild progress is announced politely once at start and once at completion — not continuously. The partial-history marker and the no-data state are text, reachable by keyboard, and present in the SCR-045 data table, never colour-only. Reduced-motion is respected by the progress affordance.

## Performance notes
Menu open and parameter entry are instant (<50 ms). Rebuilds are bounded by the 10 s / 1M-print NFR of US-CHART-003/004 measured by E12-T04; cancellation takes effect within 1 s. Retaining the previous series during a rebuild must not breach the per-pane 512 MB GPU budget — if it would, the governor sheds the retained copy and cancellation falls back to a refetch, with that behaviour documented.

## Observability
`bar_mode_selected_total{mode}`, `bar_rebuild_started_total`, `bar_rebuild_cancelled_total`, `bar_rebuild_duration_seconds{kind}`, `bar_param_rejected_client_total{reason}`, `partial_history_markers_shown_total`. Mode-selection counts tell the Owner whether the descopable renko/range rung is actually used.

## Definition of Done
Per §3.2: every scenario automated; coverage ≥80%; cancellation verified end to end; axe-core green plus a keyboard-only and screen-reader pass on SCR-042; design-QA pass against the SCR-042 spec and CMP-220; QA sign-off; demoed (switch to volume bars, cancel a rebuild); feature-flag state recorded for `bars.renko` and `bars.range`; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-S11** — the re-binding machinery a mode change rides on.
- **E12-S04** — all bar modes must exist before the menu can offer them.
- **E12-K01 / ADR-0014** — the cancellation mechanism.
- **E12-T02** — `chart_settings.bar_mode` persistence.

## Branch
`feat/e12-bar-mode-menu`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-CHART-003 (Must), US-CHART-004 (Should/Could), US-CHART-005
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-042, SCR-047 · `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-220, CMP-041, CMP-069, CMP-221
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` `chart_settings.bar_mode` (§1896–1909)

title: Build the bar determinism harness: BI-1..BI-6 properties and golden fixtures
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 4 is the single hardest gate in R1: **"All five bar types produce identical results to a reference implementation on a recorded fixture day, byte-for-byte on OHLCV."** `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.4 turns that into six named invariants (BI-1…BI-6) each with a prescribed test layer, and §16 assigns "Property tests for BI-1…BI-6 over ≥1M synthetic trades plus a recorded-day golden file" as the bar-builder test obligation.

This Task builds the machine that proves it, and wires it into CI so a regression fails the build rather than surfacing in R2 as an inexplicable footprint discrepancy. It is deliberately a single shared harness rather than six ad-hoc test files, because the invariants are cross-builder and the fixture must be identical for all of them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Synthetic trade generator**: seeded, reproducible, producing ≥1M `TradeEvent`s with configurable volatility, print-size distribution, taker-side skew and adversarial patterns (huge prints spanning N thresholds, exact-threshold hits, rapid reversals, long silences, late arrivals, duplicate `tradeId`s).
- **Property suite** implementing BI-1…BI-6 exactly as §3.4 prescribes, run against all six builders:
  - BI-1 volume conservation (with volume-bar splitting and renko single-allocation);
  - BI-2 `delta == buy_volume - sell_volume`;
  - BI-3 `min_delta <= delta <= max_delta`, both attained on the intrabar path;
  - BI-4 replay determinism including `spec_hash`;
  - BI-5 `restore(snapshot())` equivalence at random cut points;
  - BI-6 `vwap == turnover / volume` to 8 dp, or `open` when volume is 0.
- **Golden fixture**: a version-controlled recorded Bybit symbol-day (the fixed fixture `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 requires for integration), stored with its provenance, plus generated golden bar files per builder kind and parameter.
- **Reference implementation**: an independent, deliberately naive, non-optimised implementation of each builder used only as the comparison oracle — written from the spec text, not from the production code, so it is a genuine cross-check rather than a tautology.
- **Byte-for-byte comparator** producing a readable diff (bar index, field, expected, actual) rather than an assertion dump.
- **CI wiring**: the suite runs as a required check; golden-file updates require an explicit, reviewed regeneration commit with a stated reason (a silent `--update-goldens` in CI is forbidden).
- Rebuild-throughput benchmark (1M prints per builder) reported alongside, carrying forward E12-K01's baselines.

## Out of scope
- Engine-side render golden images (E11-T08 owns that harness; E12-S09 uses it).
- Footprint/profile invariants (E18/E19 add their own, reusing this generator).
- The recorder producing the fixture (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All six builders satisfy every invariant
  Given 1 000 000 generated trades and the standard spec matrix
  When the property suite runs
  Then BI-1 through BI-6 hold for every builder and every spec
  And a violation reports the invariant name, the builder, the spec and the first offending bar

Scenario: Golden comparison is byte-for-byte on OHLCV
  Given the recorded fixture day
  When each builder replays it and is compared against the reference implementation
  Then OHLCV matches exactly for every bar
  And any mismatch prints bar index, field name, expected and actual

Scenario: A deliberate regression fails CI
  Given an intentional off-by-one introduced into the time-bar boundary
  When the harness runs in CI
  Then the build fails and names the invariant or golden file that broke

Scenario: Golden regeneration is deliberate
  Given a builder change that legitimately alters output
  When goldens are regenerated
  Then the commit contains the regenerated files, a stated reason, and a build_version bump
  And CI rejects a run that would regenerate goldens implicitly
```

## Technical notes / design
- The reference implementation must be written by a different engineer than the production builders, or at minimum written from the spec document alone. A reference derived from the production code proves nothing.
- Seeded generation makes failures reproducible: every failing property run prints the seed, and the seed is the whole repro.
- The fixture day is committed (or pinned by content hash in object storage with a checked-in manifest) so the comparison is stable across machines and years.
- `build_version` (E12-T02) is the coupling point: a golden regeneration and a `build_version` bump must happen in the same commit, because the bump is what triggers rebuilds of already-persisted bars.

## Test plan
This Task *is* test infrastructure; its own correctness is verified by **mutation testing**: a set of deliberately seeded defects (off-by-one boundary, endpoint-only `min_delta`, missing volume split, phantom range bars, renko double-allocation) must each be caught by the harness. A defect the harness misses is a gap in the harness, and closing it is part of this Task's Done.

## Security notes
The fixture contains only public market data — no keys, no PII, no account identifiers. Confirm this explicitly before committing it (a recorded session captured through the app could otherwise carry authentication frames). The generator must not be usable as a load-generation tool against the live exchange; it is offline-only by construction.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — test infrastructure, no UI. The comparator's diff output should be plain text readable in a terminal and in CI logs without colour dependence.

## Performance notes
The full 1M-trade × 6-builder suite must complete within the CI budget (target ≤10 minutes) or it will be disabled by attrition; if it cannot, split into a fast PR-gate subset (100k trades) and a full nightly run, with the nightly failure treated as a build break. Rebuild throughput per builder is recorded here and becomes the baseline the 10 s / 1M-print NFR is enforced against.

## Observability
Publish per-run metrics to the CI dashboard: invariant pass/fail per builder, rebuild throughput per builder, harness wall-clock. A throughput regression >10% against the recorded baseline is a build warning and >25% a failure, mirroring the engine benchmark policy of `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3.

## Definition of Done
Per §4.2: all six invariants implemented and green; golden fixtures committed with provenance; reference implementation reviewed as independent; mutation-testing set demonstrably caught; CI required check wired; coverage met; `24-internal-schemas.md` §3.4/§16 reflect the shipped harness; demo of a deliberate regression failing the build; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E12-T03** — fan-out and snapshot/restore must exist for BI-5 to be testable.
- **E12-S03**, **E12-S04** — all six builders must exist before the suite can cover them.
- **E12-K01** — rebuild baselines.

## Branch
`feat/e12-determinism-harness`

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §3.4 invariants BI-1…BI-6, §16 test obligations
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 4, §5.4 quality gates (integration: recorded fixture)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (property testing, golden files, CI gates)

title: Add series-rendering scenarios to the engine benchmark CI gate
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 exit criterion 1 requires that the frame budget be **"met and enforced in CI"**, with regressions >10% failing the build. E11-T06 builds the harness and makes it a required check; this Task adds E12's scenarios to it so that a series-rendering regression — the most likely kind, since series code changes most often — is caught by the same gate rather than discovered during a demo.

It is deliberately small and deliberately last: it locks in the numbers the rest of the Epic produced.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Benchmark scenarios registered in the E11-T06 harness: candle series at 5k / 50k / 100k bars across LOD tiers L0/L1/L2; OHLC bar, line, area and Heikin-Ashi series at 100k bars; the volume sub-pane enabled; a forming-bar update storm (20 updates/s over 60 s); a symbol/interval switch loop (100 switches) asserting stable GPU memory and zero context recreations.
- Baselines recorded per scenario on the reference hardware, committed alongside the harness.
- CI gating consistent with E11's policy: >10% regression fails, and a baseline change requires an explicit reviewed commit stating the reason.
- Backend counterpart: the bar-build and rebuild throughput numbers from E12-T04 published into the same dashboard so engine and builder performance are read together.
- A short runbook section describing how to reproduce a failing benchmark locally and how to interpret the `FrameStats` attribution.

## Out of scope
- The harness itself, the reference-hardware definition and the required-check wiring — **E11-T06**.
- The determinism/throughput harness — **E12-T04**.
- Load testing of the WS fan-out — E17/E46.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Series scenarios run in CI
  Given a pull request touching packages/chart-engine
  When CI runs
  Then every E12 benchmark scenario executes and reports p95 frame time, draw calls and GPU memory

Scenario: A regression fails the build
  Given a change that increases candle-series p95 frame time by more than 10 percent against the baseline
  Then the required check fails and names the scenario, the baseline and the measured value

Scenario: Switch-loop leak is caught
  Given a change that leaks GPU memory across symbol switches
  When the 100-switch scenario runs
  Then the memory-stability assertion fails
  And the failure names the growth per switch

Scenario: Baseline changes are deliberate
  Given a legitimate performance change
  When baselines are updated
  Then the commit contains the new baselines and a stated reason
  And CI rejects an implicit baseline rewrite
```

## Technical notes / design
- Reuse E11-T06's harness, reference-hardware profile and reporting format exactly; a second benchmark system with its own conventions is how perf gates get ignored.
- Scenarios must be deterministic: seeded synthetic datasets, fixed viewport sizes and fixed DPI, or the gate produces flaky failures and is disabled within a month.
- The 100-switch memory scenario is the one most likely to catch a real bug, because re-bind leaks are invisible in a single-shot benchmark.

## Test plan
The Task is test infrastructure. Its own verification is a deliberate-regression run: a seeded patch that slows the candle path by 15% must fail the gate, and a seeded per-switch leak must fail the memory assertion. Both are run as part of accepting this Task.

## Security notes
Benchmark fixtures are synthetic or public market data only — no keys, no account data, no recorded authenticated sessions. Benchmark artefacts published to CI must not include screenshots or dumps that could carry account context.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — CI infrastructure, no UI. Benchmark reports are plain text/tabular and readable without colour, so a CI log conveys the failure without relying on red/green alone.

## Performance notes
This Task *is* the performance gate for E12. title: Security review and sign-off for E12 bar builders and series
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, for any epic carrying the `security` label, that the STRIDE model be finalised, findings triaged (fixed or accepted with Owner sign-off) and a sign-off comment posted by the Security engineer before the epic can be Done. §8 makes that non-skippable.

E12's security story is unusual and worth stating plainly at sign-off so that later epics inherit an accurate assumption rather than a vague one: **the bars this epic produces will be treated as ground truth by the order-flow, replay, journal and rule-engine epics, including rules that place live orders.** Signing off E12 means asserting that a bar served by the system either matches the recorded tape or is explicitly marked as not doing so.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A white-box security review of the E12 implementation against the `E12-X01` model: read the builder fan-out, persistence/dedup/`build_version` path, backfill client, the two REST handlers and the WS publisher, checking each modelled control is actually present in code and actually reachable.
- Verification that every mitigation row in the threat model has landed: input caps enforced server-side at the agreed numbers, decimal-only arithmetic, parameterised queries, explicit `category=linear`, exchange-response validation, bounded WS queues, `build_version` provenance in `meta`.
- Triage table of every finding from `E12-X02` (abuse cases), `E12-X03` (gate output), `E12-Q06` (chaos integrity findings) and any SAST/SCA/secrets result: fixed, accepted with Owner sign-off, or deferred with a dated ticket.
- **Evidence-integrity assertion**: a written statement, backed by `E12-Q02` golden results and `E12-Q06` chaos results, that served bars match the tape or are marked partial/gapped — this is the sentence downstream epics will rely on.
- A **consumer note** for E13/E18/E19/E23/E26/E37 stating exactly what guarantees they may assume (deterministic rebuild, `build_version` provenance, `confirm` semantics, `recording_started_at` honesty) and what they must not assume (no checksums per ADR-0005; non-time bars are not wall-clock aligned).
- Updated residual-risk section in `docs/plan/security/threat-models/e12-bars.md` reflecting what was built rather than what was proposed, plus a `32-risk-register.md` update if anything changed.
- The Security-engineer sign-off comment on the E12 epic ticket, with date, build sha and named signatory.

## Out of scope
- Pen-testing (E43, pre-live gate R4) — this review is internal and does not substitute for it, which the sign-off states explicitly.
- QA functional sign-off (`E12-Q08`), which is a separate, also-required gate.
- Security of consumers (E13/E18/E23) beyond issuing the consumer note.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every modelled control is verified in code
  Given the threat model's mitigation table
  When the reviewer walks the implementation
  Then each control is confirmed present, reachable and covered by a test
  And any control that is absent or unreachable is filed as a blocking finding

Scenario: All findings are triaged before sign-off
  Given findings from X02, X03 and Q06
  Then each is marked fixed, accepted with Owner sign-off, or deferred with a dated ticket
  And no finding is left untriaged

Scenario: Failure case - an open P0 blocks the epic
  Given an unfixed finding that lets the API serve bars diverging from the tape without marking them
  When sign-off is attempted
  Then sign-off is refused, E12 cannot be Done, and the finding is named in the refusal

Scenario: Edge case - a control was implemented differently than modelled
  Given the implementation enforces the window cap at the store layer rather than the handler
  Then the reviewer verifies the alternative is equivalent or stronger
  And the threat model is updated to describe what was actually built

Scenario: Edge case - downstream epics get an accurate guarantee
  Given the consumer note is published
  When an E18 engineer reads it
  Then the guarantees and non-guarantees are stated explicitly enough to design against without asking
```

## Technical notes / design
- Time-boxed to two days of review plus a one-hour walkthrough with the E12 tech lead; the goal is verification of specific modelled claims, not an open-ended code read.
- Use a checklist derived directly from the model's mitigation column so the review is reproducible and its absence of findings is meaningful.
- Where a control is claimed to be tested, follow the link to the actual test and confirm it asserts the control rather than merely exercising the path — a test that would pass with the control removed is not evidence.

## Test plan
- Verification is documentary plus spot-execution: the reviewer independently runs the `E12-X02` regression subset and one `E12-Q06` chaos scenario against the release-candidate build rather than trusting the report.
- Re-run of SAST/SCA/secrets on the RC build immediately before sign-off, so the sign-off refers to the shipped artefact.

## Security notes
- The sign-off comment must state the data classification (public market data), the evidence-integrity assertion, the explicit exclusion of pen-test coverage, and the conditions that would invalidate the sign-off (new bar type with a new parameter shape, account-scoped data entering the bars path, a privileged rebuild operation being added).
- Accepted risks require the Owner's written acceptance, recorded in the ticket, not a verbal nod.

## Accessibility notes
- Confirms one a11y-adjacent security property: security-driven rejections surface as the documented accessible error state (`SCR-048`) with a text reason, so a control never manifests as an unexplained blank chart.

## Performance notes
- Confirms the agreed caps did not silently break legitimate usage: a 30-day backfill and a 100 k-bar load still succeed within budgets #13 and #1 with the controls enabled — verified from `E12-Q05` baselines taken with the controls on.

## Observability
- Confirms the detection signals specified in `E12-X01` exist and alert: rejection counters, rebuild-rate alerting, `exchange_response_invalid_total`, `bars_gap_detected_total`, and that log fields carry `build_version`.
- Any modelled threat still lacking a detection signal blocks sign-off or is explicitly accepted.

## Definition of Done
- Review completed against the checklist; all findings triaged; blocking findings fixed and re-verified.
- Threat model residual-risk section updated to as-built; `32-risk-register.md` updated if needed.
- Consumer note published and linked from E13, E18, E19, E23, E26 epic tickets.
- SAST/SCA/secrets re-run clean on the RC build.
- Security-engineer sign-off comment posted on the E12 epic with date, build sha and signatory; Owner acceptance recorded for any accepted risk.
- Findings presented at the security review slot.

## Dependencies
- `E12-X01`, `E12-X02`, `E12-X03`, `E12-Q06`; a release-candidate build of E12; `E12-Q08` runs in parallel and is referenced, not blocking.

title: ADR-0014 drawing persistence model and chart-space geometry contract
body:
## Context
E14 makes several decisions that every later epic inherits and that no document currently records as decisions with alternatives and consequences. `21-database-schema.md` states the *shape* of the `drawings` table and `22-api-openapi.yaml` states the *shape* of the API, but neither says why geometry is chart-space JSONB rather than a normalised point table, why mutations are batched and optimistic rather than transactional-per-edit, what the conflict-resolution policy is between two sessions, or what the scoping model (symbol-global vs `layout_id`-scoped, with `interval_scope`) means for sync.

Those questions arrive again in E15 (workspaces embed drawings via `WorkspaceExport.drawings`), E26 (replay must render drawings anchored in a replayed timeline), E40 (`drawings.alert_id` links a line to an alert) and E41 (journal snapshots embed notes per US-DRAW-006). Without an ADR, each of those epics re-litigates the model or, worse, quietly assumes a different one. `docs/plan/27-adrs/` is the established home for exactly this.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-drawing-persistence-and-geometry.md` in the established ADR template (Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives considered, Consequences, Validation gate), recording:
  1. **Chart-space geometry as JSONB.** Decision: store `{"points":[{"t","p"}]}` with prices as decimal strings and times as UTC timestamps; never pixels, never bar indices. Alternatives: a normalised `drawing_points` table (queryable, join cost, schema churn per tool), bar-index anchoring (breaks on bar-type change and on history backfill), pixel storage (rejected outright). Consequences: geometry is opaque to SQL, so range queries rely on the denormalised `anchor_start`/`anchor_end`, and validation must happen in the application layer — which is why `E14-X01` demands explicit size limits.
  2. **Per-tool geometry schemas.** Decision: each of the 24 `tool` enum values has a documented geometry shape (point count, required extras such as `extend_right`, fib level sets, channel width, position-tool entry/stop/target), specified in `24-internal-schemas.md` and validated server-side, even though the OpenAPI schema is permissive.
  3. **Optimistic client store with debounced transactional batches.** Decision: 500 ms debounce, one `POST /drawings/batch` per burst, transactional server-side, idempotency-keyed. Alternatives: per-edit PUT (chatty during a drag, partial states persisted), WS-based mutation (rejected — the WS protocol is frozen for market data, and drawings are low-rate config, not a data-plane concern), no persistence until explicit save (rejected — US-DRAW-001 requires levels to simply be there next session).
  4. **Conflict policy.** Decision: last-write-wins on server-assigned `updated_at`, with the losing session notified; alternatives (optimistic locking with a version column, CRDT merge) considered and rejected with reasons proportional to a single-owner deployment. This is the clause `E14-Q06` scenarios 7-9 assert against.
  5. **Scoping model.** Decision: `layout_id` NULL means symbol-global (visible in every pane on that symbol); non-NULL means pane-local; `interval_scope` NULL means all intervals; sync is per-layout and per-symbol and never crosses symbols (US-DRAW-009's NFR). Consequences for E15 workspace export/import and for E26 replay.
  6. **Lifecycle.** Decision: soft delete with `deleted_at`, purge after 90 days per the retention table, undo operating on the soft-deleted row within the session; consequences for `alert_id` references and for the restore race in `E14-Q06` scenario 12.
  7. **Audit posture.** Record the `E14-X01` decision on whether drawings are in or out of the append-only audit log, with the reason, so it is a decision rather than an omission.
- **Doc updates flowing from the ADR**: the per-tool geometry schemas added to `24-internal-schemas.md`; a cross-reference added to `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 and to the `/drawings` description in `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the conflict policy and scope semantics reflected in `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036/SCR-037 where user-visible.
- **ADR index updated** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` with ADR-0014 and its supersedes/relates-to links.

## Out of scope
- Implementing any of it (the decisions describe what `E14-T01`/`E14-T02` build; if implementation diverges, the ADR is amended rather than the code left undocumented).
- Sharing drawings between users (deferred surface, recorded in `E14-X01`).
- Replay-specific rendering semantics (E26 writes its own ADR if needed, referencing this one).
- Alert-from-line behaviour (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR records decisions with real alternatives
  Given ADR-0014 is merged
  When it is reviewed against the ADR template
  Then each of the seven decisions states at least two considered alternatives with the reason for rejection
  And each states its consequences and a validation gate

Scenario: The plan documents agree with the ADR
  Given ADR-0014's scoping and lifecycle decisions
  When 21-database-schema.md, 22-api-openapi.yaml and 24-internal-schemas.md are checked
  Then each cross-references the ADR and none contradicts it
  And per-tool geometry schemas exist in 24-internal-schemas.md for every shipped tool

Scenario: Failure case - implementation diverges from the ADR
  Given the implemented conflict policy is optimistic locking rather than last-write-wins
  When the ADR's validation gate is evaluated at epic close
  Then the divergence is recorded and either the code or the ADR is changed before E14 reaches Done
  And the change is reflected in the E14-Q06 chaos assertions

Scenario: Edge case - a tool is descoped after the ADR is written
  Given the pitchfork tool is descoped per the roadmap descoping ladder
  When the per-tool geometry schema section is reviewed
  Then the tool's schema remains documented and is marked not-shipped-in-R1
  And the tool enum in the API is annotated accordingly rather than silently retaining an unusable value
```

## Technical notes / design
- The ADR is written after `E14-T01`/`E14-T02` are implemented but before the epic closes, deliberately: it documents decisions as made, not as hoped, which is the only way the validation gate means anything.
- Per-tool geometry schemas are expressed as JSON Schema fragments in `24-internal-schemas.md` so server-side validation can be generated from them rather than hand-written per tool — which is also how the `drawings-unbounded-geometry` rule in `E14-X03` gets a concrete validator to point at.
- Decimal-string prices are called out explicitly with the rationale (tick precision, no float drift), because this is the most likely thing a future contributor "simplifies" into a float.
- The ADR states the frozen parts (chart-space storage, decimal prices, soft delete) and the negotiable parts (debounce interval, conflict policy) separately, so later epics know what they may tune.

## Test plan
- Documentation review by the Architect, the E14 lead and the Security engineer (for the audit-posture clause).
- Consistency check: a reviewer verifies each ADR claim against the implementation and against the three plan documents; discrepancies are filed.
- The per-tool schemas are validated by feeding one real fixture drawing of each tool through them — a schema that rejects a legitimate fixture is a bug in the schema.

## Security notes
- The audit-posture and lifecycle decisions are security-relevant and are reviewed by the Security engineer; the ADR must not quietly weaken a control asserted in the threat model.
- The ADR records the size-limit and quota decisions from `E14-X01` so those numbers live in a durable, reviewable place rather than only in a threat-model appendix.

## Accessibility notes
- The ADR records that every persisted drawing must be able to produce a deterministic accessible name from its stored fields alone (tool + anchor time + price + optional label), because `SCR-036` is the accessibility contract and it depends on the persistence model rather than on render state.

## Performance notes
- The ADR records the measured basis for the debounce interval and the batch cap, citing `E14-Q05` results, so a later change to either has a baseline to argue against.
- It records the reliance on `ix_dr_user_symbol` and budget 28 (< 5 ms) as a consequence of the JSONB choice, making the index a documented dependency rather than an incidental one.

## Observability
- The ADR names the metrics that make its decisions falsifiable in production: batch size distribution, conflict counter, drawings-per-user distribution, soft-deleted row count — so a wrong assumption surfaces as data.

## Definition of Done
- ADR-0014 merged with all seven decisions, alternatives, consequences and validation gates.
- `24-internal-schemas.md` carries per-tool geometry schemas for every tool in the enum, marked shipped or not-shipped.
- Cross-references added in `21-database-schema.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`; ADR index updated.
- Reviewed and approved by the Architect, the E14 lead and the Security engineer.
- Validation gate re-evaluated at epic close with the result recorded on the E14 epic ticket.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T01`, `E14-T02` (the implemented persistence and store). Informs E15, E26, E40, E41; consumes `E14-X01`'s audit and size-limit decisions.

title: Design QA of the built drawing tools, object tree and position tool
body:
## Context
Design QA is the gate that decides whether what shipped is what was designed. For E14 it is unusually load-bearing, because most of this epic's output is drawn by a WebGL engine rather than composed from DOM components - which means the design system's normal safety net (shared components carrying the tokens) does not apply to the on-canvas half of the work. Stroke weights, handle sizes, label chips, fill opacities and snap indicators are all re-implemented in shader and geometry code, and every one of them can drift silently.

This pass runs in Sprint 09, after the E14 stories have landed and been deployed to a testable build, and it verifies the built app against E14-D03..D10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Mechanical token diff** for the DOM surfaces (rail, popover, object tree): computed styles compared against the Style Dictionary output rather than judged by eye, so near-miss values are caught.
- **Canvas fidelity pass** for the on-canvas surfaces: measured screenshots compared against the redlines for stroke weights, handle size and hit tolerance, fill opacity, label-chip contrast and the snap indicator - measured in pixels at 1x and 2x DPI, both themes.
- **State-matrix walk** across every state specified in E14-D03..D07 in dark, light, at 100/125/200% zoom: tool states, magnet modes, selection/lock/hidden, popover saving/failed/read-only, position-tool error states, tree at 0/20/500 objects.
- **Copy diff** of every string against the E14 decks, with the position tool's advice-boundary wording and the anchored-VWAP approximate badge checked specifically.
- **Interaction-model conformance**: the state machine from E14-D02 walked tool by tool in the real build - arm, place, cancel with `Esc`, commit, select, move, nudge, clone, lock, hide, delete, undo, redo - with every undefined or divergent transition logged as a defect.
- **Accessibility re-run**: the E14-D10 screen-reader script executed verbatim against the build on NVDA and VoiceOver, plus confirmation that axe-core CI covers the DOM surfaces and is green.
- **Motion pass** including the reduced-motion variants and the do-not-animate list from E14-D09.
- **Performance measurement** against the stated budgets on the reference machine.
- Defect log kept with the ticket; every entry a real ticket with an owner and a priority, not a spreadsheet row.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of persistence, sync and undo semantics - QA's black-box plan in the engineering chunk owns that; design QA reports what it happens to see but does not duplicate the coverage.
- Backend `/drawings` API behaviour.
- Re-opening design decisions: a divergence is either a build defect or an accepted amendment to the spec, never a redesign inside this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Canvas rendering matches the redlines
  Given the on-canvas drawing primitives in the built app at 1x and 2x DPI
  When stroke weight, handle size, fill opacity and label-chip contrast are measured
  Then each is within the tolerance stated in the E14-D08 specification
  And every out-of-tolerance value is logged as a defect with an owner

Scenario: A token has drifted on a DOM surface
  Given the computed styles of the rail, popover and object tree
  When they are diffed against the Style Dictionary output
  Then any value not resolving to the specified token is a defect
  And near-miss values are treated identically to obvious ones

Scenario: The keyboard-draw path works in the build
  Given the E14-D10 screen-reader script
  When it is executed verbatim on NVDA and on VoiceOver against the deployed build
  Then every step's actual announcement is recorded against its expected announcement
  And any missing or incorrect announcement is a blocking defect

Scenario: A performance budget is missed
  Given a chart with 200 drawings on the reference machine
  When one drawing is dragged
  Then the measured frame rate and frame time are recorded against the >=58 fps / <=12 ms budgets
  And a missed budget is filed as a defect with an owner, not recorded as an observation

Scenario: Approximate VWAP renders without its badge
  Given an anchored VWAP whose anchor precedes recorded tick history
  When the built drawing is inspected
  Then the approximate badge is present on the canvas, in the tooltip and in the object-tree row
  And its absence anywhere is a P1 defect, because it presents an approximation as exact
```

## Technical notes / design
The pass runs against a deployed build on the target browsers and in the Electron shell, not against Storybook alone: the seams this epic fails at - focus returning from the popover to a canvas object, the tree revealing an off-screen object, a drag not re-rendering the price layer - exist only in the integrated app.

Canvas fidelity is measured, not eyeballed. Screenshots are taken at fixed zoom and DPI with a known fixture so the same measurement can be repeated in later releases as a regression baseline.

The defect log's entries are tickets. A design-QA finding that lives only in a document is a finding that does not get fixed.

## Test plan
Structured pass in this order, each step recorded pass/fail with evidence: (1) mechanical token diff on DOM surfaces; (2) canvas fidelity measurement at 1x/2x, dark and light; (3) state-matrix walk at three zoom levels; (4) copy diff; (5) interaction-model conformance walk per tool; (6) focus-continuity walk from E14-D10's map; (7) screen-reader script re-run on NVDA and VoiceOver; (8) axe-core coverage confirmation on the DOM surfaces; (9) motion and reduced-motion pass; (10) performance measurement with the 200-drawing fixture.

## Security notes
Three checks in this pass are security checks rather than cosmetic ones, and findings in this class are escalated to the Security engineer immediately rather than queued. First, the position tool: verify in the build that send-to-ticket never places an order, that it opens the ticket unarmed, and that it is genuinely disabled - not merely styled as disabled - when implied risk exceeds the profile cap. Second, text notes and template names: verify that markup pasted into a note is rendered as literal text on the canvas, in the tooltip, in the object-tree row and in the accessible name, and that no link is auto-activated. Third, scope: verify that the drawings list and the object tree show only the current user's objects and that no other account's profile data appears in the position tool's read-out for a Manager or Viewer role.

## Accessibility notes
The E14-D10 script re-run against the build is the manual evidence the Epic DoD requires, paired with a green axe-core CI run on the DOM surfaces. Any regression against the focus-continuity map is a blocker, as is any tool whose keyboard-creation path is incomplete in the build - CMP-191 already designates the keyboard-draw interaction test an explicit CI gate, and this pass confirms that gate is genuinely exercising the shipped flow rather than a simplified harness.

## Performance notes
Measured on the reference machine with the 200-drawing benchmark fixture: drag one drawing at >=58 fps with <=12 ms frame time and <=1 ms picking (SCR-037 budget; `26-chart-engine-design.md` B8); property edits and popover interactions cause no price/footprint re-render; the object tree scrolls without jank at 500 objects; the anchored VWAP update stays <=2 ms. Each measurement is recorded in the ticket and becomes the baseline for later regression checks.

## Observability
Verifies that the analytics events annotated on the designs are actually emitted with the expected keys and payloads - `drawing.created` (with entry method), `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`, `drawing.tool_selected`, `drawing.magnet_mode_changed`, `drawing.position_tool_blocked_by_cap` - and that no event carries the body text of a user's note. Cheap to check here, expensive to retrofit after release.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ten pass steps executed with recorded evidence.
- [ ] Defect log complete; every entry classified, ticketed and owned.
- [ ] Canvas fidelity measurements recorded and within tolerance, or defects filed.
- [ ] Screen-reader script re-run on NVDA and VoiceOver; axe-core green on the DOM surfaces.
- [ ] Performance budgets measured and recorded as the regression baseline.
- [ ] Security-class findings escalated and resolved or accepted with Security-engineer sign-off.
- [ ] Catalogue documents updated for every accepted divergence.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done).

## Dependencies
- **E14-D03..E14-D10** - the signed-off artefacts and baselines this pass verifies against.
- The E14 frontend stories must be implemented and deployed to a testable build.

## Branch
`design/e14-drawing-design-qa`

## References
- `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` sections 11, 12
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-191, CMP-223
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 8, 9
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` sections 2.2, 3.2


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant sections)

5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- apps/web/src/routes/** (per Scope screen), apps/web/src/lib/state/**, packages/ui/** (components), apps/web/e2e/**
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- apps/web route contracts, Zustand/Jotai store shapes consumed by other routes; named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-191, CMP-223, SCR-036, SCR-037
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build · pnpm e2e · pnpm test:a11y
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e14-drawing-design-qa`
- PR title: `E14-D11: Design QA of the built drawing tools, object tree and position tool`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E14-D11)
- Required reviewers: `apps/web` (@CandleViewer/frontend), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/design, area/charting-ui, priority/p1, design, design-qa, a11y, perf

**Done means**
- [ ] All ten pass steps executed with recorded evidence.
- [ ] Defect log complete; every entry classified, ticketed and owned.
- [ ] Canvas fidelity measurements recorded and within tolerance, or defects filed.
- [ ] Screen-reader script re-run on NVDA and VoiceOver; axe-core green on the DOM surfaces.
- [ ] Performance budgets measured and recorded as the regression baseline.
- [ ] Security-class findings escalated and resolved or accepted with Security-engineer sign-off.

**Do NOT**
- Do not widen a performance budget or edit a benchmark baseline to make a regression pass (AGENTS.md §8).

**If blocked**

- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.

- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).

title: Accessibility audit of the drawing surface, toolbar and object tree
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 9 in `30-release-roadmap.md` is unambiguous: "every chart is operable without a mouse — keyboard data cursor reads OHLCV per bar, **drawings can be created and adjusted by keyboard**, and a screen-reader pass is signed off by the a11y specialist". The §5.4 gate adds "axe-core zero violations on all R1 routes; manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass on chart and **drawing flows**".

Drawings are the hardest a11y problem in the product, because the primary surface is a WebGL canvas with no semantics at all. `14-screens-catalogue.md` resolves this by designating `SCR-036` (the object tree, `role="tree"`) as "the a11y-complete alternative to manipulating canvas objects by mouse" and requiring that "every canvas object is reachable and editable here by keyboard". SCR-037 adds that "each drawing has an accessible name and is listed in SCR-036" and that drawings can be created entirely by keyboard via SCR-045's grid. `E14-K01` chose the concrete pattern.

This ticket is the audit that proves the claim, or produces the defect list that makes it true before R1 ships.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated sweep**: axe-core runs (via the existing CI integration) on every state of SCR-037 and SCR-036 — toolbar idle, tool armed, properties popover open for each tool family, template menu open, tree empty, tree populated, tree with 500 objects, multi-select active, error states from `E14-Q06`. Target: zero violations; any accepted exception is recorded with a rationale and an owner, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- **Keyboard-only conformance matrix**: every operation in US-DRAW-001..009 × {achievable by keyboard? via which path? how many keystrokes?}. Operations achievable only via the canvas with a pointer are defects. Explicitly covered: tool selection (`Alt+T/H/F/R/M`), magnet toggle (`Ctrl+M`), anchor placement, anchor re-adjust, nudge (arrow = 1 tick, Shift+arrow = 10 ticks), multi-select, group move, lock, hide, reorder, style edit, template apply, delete, undo/redo, send-to-ticket from the position tool.
- **Screen-reader passes**, scripted and recorded, on NVDA + Firefox, NVDA + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari, and VoiceOver + the Electron shell:
  - Create a trendline end to end and confirm each anchor placement is announced with its time and price.
  - Navigate the tree, confirm each item announces type, anchor time, anchor price, visibility and lock state (the SCR-036 contract).
  - Nudge a level and confirm the new price is announced (politely, debounced — not per keypress spam).
  - Open and complete the properties popover as a standard form.
  - Encounter an error (poison batch from `E14-Q06`) and confirm it is announced.
- **Focus management review**: focus visible at all times per `05-accessibility-standard.md`; focus returns to the invoking control when a popover closes; no focus trap in the popover except the intended modal-style trap; the tree's roving tabindex behaves per the `role="tree"` pattern; arming a tool never steals focus into the canvas without an escape route (`Esc` disarms and returns focus).
- **Contrast and non-colour encoding review**: drawing colours from `CMP-031 ColorSwatch` tokens meet WCAG 2.2 AA against both themes; selected/hover/locked states are distinguishable without colour alone (US-DRAW-003's "fills must respect the minimum contrast of candles drawn over them" is verified with the flatten-opacity toggle both on and off); the magnet-snap highlight is perceivable non-visually (announced) as well as visually.
- **Target sizes**: WCAG 2.2 AA target-size checks on toolbar buttons, popover controls and tree row controls; grab handles verified ≥24 px per US-DRAW-001's NFR at 100/150/200% zoom and at 200% browser text scaling.
- **Reduced-motion and zoom**: `prefers-reduced-motion` respected by any drawing animation; the whole surface usable at 200% zoom and at 320 px-equivalent reflow without loss of function.
- **Deliverable**: `qa/a11y/e14-drawings-audit.md` — findings list with severity, WCAG success-criterion reference, reproduction, screenshot/recording, and an owning ticket for each; plus a sign-off section for the a11y specialist.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the defects found (each becomes a Bug against the owning story; blockers must be fixed before the epic's DoD).
- The chart data cursor and OHLCV announcements (E11 owns those).
- Indicator manager rows that are not drawings (E13 owns those, though the shared tree is audited once here and the finding routed).
- Full-product a11y certification — E43/E46 own the programme-level pass.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every drawing operation is reachable without a mouse
  Given the keyboard-only conformance matrix covering US-DRAW-001 through US-DRAW-009
  When each operation is attempted with the keyboard alone on NVDA and on VoiceOver
  Then every operation completes successfully by at least one documented path
  And any operation that cannot is filed as a blocking defect against its story

Scenario: Every drawing is discoverable and named
  Given a chart with one drawing of each shipped tool
  When the object tree is navigated with a screen reader
  Then every drawing is announced with its type, anchor time, anchor price, visibility and lock state
  And no drawing exists on the canvas that is absent from the tree

Scenario: Failure case - an unnamed drawing ships
  Given a build where the text annotation tool creates objects without an accessible name
  When the audit's naming check runs
  Then the finding is recorded as a blocking WCAG 4.1.2 defect with a reproduction
  And the epic cannot reach Done until it is fixed or waived by the a11y specialist in writing

Scenario: Edge case - nudging does not flood the screen reader
  Given a level being nudged with 20 rapid Shift+ArrowUp presses
  When the announcements are captured
  Then the final price is announced via a debounced polite live region
  And the user is not read 20 consecutive interruptions
```

## Technical notes / design
- The audit runs against the S09 staging build with all S07-S08 drawing stories merged, so it judges the shipped surface rather than a prototype.
- axe-core states are driven by the `E14-Q03` Playwright specs with an axe step injected, reusing existing navigation code rather than duplicating it.
- Screen-reader passes are recorded (audio + screen) and the transcripts are attached, because "NVDA said something" is not evidence — the exact utterance is the artefact the specialist signs off.
- Announcement volume is measured, not just presence: the audit counts live-region utterances per interaction, since over-announcement is as disabling as silence (the `CMP-010`/`CMP-008` precedent in `15-component-catalogue.md` already debounces to ~250 ms).
- Findings use the standard severity ladder from `05-accessibility-standard.md`; anything that makes an operation impossible without a pointer is automatically blocking for R1 given exit criterion 9.

## Test plan
- Two auditors work independently on the keyboard matrix and reconcile, to reduce the chance a habitual path hides a gap.
- Each finding is reproduced by a second person before filing.
- After fixes land, a targeted re-test of every blocking finding is performed and recorded before sign-off; the axe sweep is re-run in full.

## Security notes
- Screen and audio recordings are scrubbed of any credentials typed during login and stored in the internal QA artefact store, not in the repository.
- The audit confirms that accessible names derived from user-entered text (annotation labels) are rendered as text content and never as markup — an accessible-name path is an injection path, and the corpus from `E14-X02` is used for the naming check on the tree.

## Accessibility notes
- Standard: WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Success criteria in explicit scope: 1.4.3 contrast, 1.4.11 non-text contrast, 1.4.12 text spacing, 1.4.13 content on hover/focus (the properties popover), 2.1.1/2.1.2 keyboard and no trap, 2.4.3 focus order, 2.4.7 focus visible, 2.4.11 focus not obscured, 2.5.7 dragging movements (**the key one for E14 — every drag must have a non-dragging alternative**), 2.5.8 target size, 3.3.1 error identification, 4.1.2 name/role/value, 4.1.3 status messages.
- SC 2.5.7 is called out because drawing is fundamentally a dragging interaction; the audit's core question is whether the keyboard placement mode and the tree together constitute a complete single-pointer-free alternative.

## Performance notes
- The 500-object tree state is audited for responsiveness as well as semantics; if virtualisation removes off-screen items from the accessibility tree in a way that breaks navigation, that is a finding, not an optimisation.
- Screen-reader interaction latency (keypress → announcement) is sampled; over ~500 ms is filed as a usability defect.

## Observability
- Findings tracked in the standard a11y defect view with the `a11y` label so the epic DoD rollup can show zero open blockers.
- axe results published as CI artefacts per run so a regression after fixes is visible without re-auditing manually.

## Definition of Done
- `qa/a11y/e14-drawings-audit.md` merged with the conformance matrix, findings, recordings and the WCAG mapping.
- axe-core zero violations across all audited states (or written, owner-approved exceptions).
- All blocking findings fixed and re-tested, or waived in writing by the a11y specialist with a follow-up ticket.
- Manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the a11y specialist, satisfying the §5.4 R1 gate for drawing flows.
- Result linked from the E14 epic ticket's a11y DoD item.

## Dependencies
- `E14-Q03` (navigation code and keyboard spec), `E14-S04`/`E14-S05` (the last of the S08 tools), `E14-S10` (toolbar), `E14-K01` (the keyboard pattern being audited), and the shared `SCR-036` tree from E13/E14.

## Branch
`test/e14-a11y-audit`
