title: Exploratory charters, E14 regression pack and epic QA sign-off
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, for an Epic to be Done, that "an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass [is] executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA", alongside a zero-open-P0/P1 condition and a demo to the Owner. E14 is the last R1 charting epic with a large human-facing interaction surface, and scripted tests by construction only find what someone thought to write down. Drawing tools are famously rich in emergent bugs — a shape dragged onto a collapsed pane, a fib drawn backwards on an inverted log scale, a template applied to a locked object, 300 shapes pasted onto a symbol with 3 days of history.

This ticket provides the two things that close the epic: time-boxed exploratory charters aimed at exactly those seams, and the assembled regression pack that every later train re-runs so drawings do not rot while E18-E46 are built on top.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (session-based, 90 minutes each, recorded per `03-testing-strategy.md`), at minimum:
  1. *Scale and geometry abuse* — explore drawings across log/percent/inverted scales, extreme zoom, 100k-bar history, and bar-type switches, to find anchoring drift the automated matrix missed.
  2. *Density and legibility* — 200-500 overlapping zones, fills, fib grids and labels; hunt for unreadable price action, unclickable handles and label collisions; exercise the flatten-opacity toggle.
  3. *Object management under stress* — deep undo/redo chains beyond the 50-op NFR, interleaved with lock/hide/delete-all, multi-select and template application; hunt for stack corruption and orphans.
  4. *Sync and layout interactions* — drawings across sync groups, multi-pane layouts, pane close/reopen, workspace save/load (E15 seam), symbol switch mid-drag.
  5. *Position tool and the trading seam* — R:R maths at edge sizes, tick/lot rounding, profile caps, send-to-ticket with a changed profile between drag and send.
  6. *Annotation content* — long text, RTL text, emoji, multi-line, pasted rich text, and text at extreme zoom; overlaps with `E14-X02` for hostile input but from a usability angle.
  7. *Keyboard-first day in the life* — an entire analysis session with no mouse at all, hunting for the operation that quietly requires one.
  8. *Persistence paranoia* — reload, relaunch, second device, second session, slow network, at every point in the drawing lifecycle.
- Each charter produces: a session sheet (charter, duration, areas covered, bugs found, notes, follow-up charters), filed under `qa/exploratory/e14/`.
- **E14 regression pack**: a curated, tagged selection (`@e14-regression`) drawn from `E14-Q02` (view-change matrix), `E14-Q03` (lifecycle, persistence, sync, keyboard), `E14-Q04` (contract + drift guard) and the highest-value chaos scenarios, plus a short manual checklist for what remains unautomatable. Runtime budget ≤20 minutes so it can run per-release, and it is registered in the release checklist of `07-release-and-prr.md` and re-run at R2-R5 as an inherited pack.
- **Bug triage and closure**: every finding filed with severity per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3; anchoring drift and persistence loss are P0 by the `E14-Q01` convention; a triage session with the E14 lead produces fix-now / fix-later dispositions, and every fix-later carries an explicit owner and target train.
- **Epic QA sign-off record** on the E14 epic ticket: pass/fail per story group, coverage numbers for `packages/chart-engine/src/drawings/**` and `apps/web/src/drawings/**` against the 85%/80% thresholds, the perf numbers from `E14-Q05`, the a11y sign-off from `E14-Q07`, the security sign-off from `E14-X02`, the open-defect list, and an explicit statement that R1 exit criteria 5 and 9 are satisfied for drawings.

## Out of scope
- Writing new automation for findings (each becomes its own ticket; the pack only assembles what exists).
- The R1 PRR itself (`07-release-and-prr.md`) — this feeds it.
- Indicator, layout or recorder regression packs (E13, E15, E16 own theirs); the E14 pack references the shared workspace save/load case rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All charters executed and recorded
  Given the eight exploratory charters for E14
  When each is executed as a time-boxed session
  Then a session sheet exists for each under qa/exploratory/e14/
  And every bug found is filed with severity, reproduction and an owning story

Scenario: The regression pack runs inside its budget
  Given the @e14-regression selection
  When it is executed on a clean staging build
  Then it completes within 20 minutes
  And it covers at least one case from every US-DRAW-001 through US-DRAW-009 story

Scenario: Failure case - an open P0 blocks the epic
  Given an unresolved anchoring-drift defect found during the scale-abuse charter
  When epic QA sign-off is attempted
  Then sign-off is refused and recorded as refused with the blocking defect linked
  And the epic stays out of Done until the defect is fixed or explicitly waived by the Owner

Scenario: Edge case - a descoped tool is encountered during exploration
  Given pitchfork and Fibonacci time-zone tools were descoped per the roadmap descoping ladder
  When a charter encounters their toolbar entries
  Then their absence or disabled state is verified as intentional against the descope record
  And a visible half-implemented tool is filed as a defect rather than accepted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Charters are genuinely exploratory: no step-by-step scripts, but each has a stated mission, a risk it is hunting, and a defined area, per session-based test management.
- Charter 7 (keyboard-first day) is run by someone who is not the a11y auditor, so it finds usability gaps rather than re-finding known conformance issues.
- The regression pack is assembled by tag, not by copying tests, so it cannot drift from the suites it selects from; a CI job asserts the tag selection is non-empty for each source suite.
- The manual remainder of the pack is deliberately short and each item carries a note on why it is not automated and what would be needed — this is the input to the next train's automation backlog.

## Test plan
- The pack is dry-run twice: once on a known-good build (must be fully green) and once on a build with a deliberately reverted drawing persistence commit (must fail, proving sensitivity).
- Charter coverage is reviewed against the story list so no story group goes unexplored.
- Sign-off is peer-reviewed by a second QA engineer before being posted.

## Security notes
- Charter 6 escalates any input-handling anomaly to `E14-X02` rather than filing it as a cosmetic bug, so a rendering oddity caused by an injection vector is not mis-triaged.
- The sign-off record explicitly requires the `E14-X02` security sign-off to be present; QA cannot sign the epic off without it, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2.
- Exploratory sessions run against staging with seeded users only; no production data is touched.

## Accessibility notes
- Charter 7 is mandatory, not optional, and its findings are routed to the a11y specialist as well as the E14 lead.
- The regression pack includes the `keyboard.spec.ts` suite from `E14-Q03` permanently, so the R1 keyboard guarantee is re-verified at every later release rather than being a one-time R1 achievement.

## Performance notes
- Charters 2 and 3 are explicitly perf-adjacent: any jank observed is reported with a trace and cross-referenced to `E14-Q05`'s benchmarks so it is either a known budgeted cost or a new finding.
- The sign-off record carries the four gating perf numbers verbatim, so a later regression has an unambiguous baseline.

## Observability
- Session sheets, bug links, pack runtime and the sign-off record are all linked from the E14 epic ticket, giving one place to audit the epic's quality evidence.
- The regression pack publishes a per-run summary to the CI dashboard with the `@e14-regression` tag so its health is trackable across trains.

## Definition of Done
- All eight charters executed, recorded and triaged.
- Regression pack assembled, tagged, runtime-verified, dry-run in both directions, and registered in the release checklist.
- Zero open P0/P1 defects against E14 scope, or explicit Owner-signed acceptances.
- Epic QA sign-off comment posted on E14 with coverage, perf, a11y and security evidence, including an explicit statement on R1 exit criteria 5 and 9.
- Follow-up automation tickets filed for every manual-only pack item.

## Dependencies
- `E14-Q02`, `E14-Q03`, `E14-Q05`, `E14-Q06`, `E14-Q07` must be complete; `E14-X02`'s sign-off is required before the final comment is posted.
- All E14 stories (`E14-S01`..`E14-S10`) merged.

## Branch
`test/e14-regression-and-signoff`

## References
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 Epic DoD
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (exploratory/session-based testing, severity ladder)
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (release checklist, PRR evidence)
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criteria 5 and 9, §12 descoping ladder
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §6 DRAW

title: Anchored VWAP drawing with standard-deviation bands and incremental update
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-005 — Anchored VWAP drawing (Must)**: "As an order-flow trader, I want to click a bar to anchor a VWAP, so that I can measure value from any event." It is the only DRAW tool that is also a *computation over market data*, which brings two constraints from the story: an incremental update budget ("never recompute the whole series per tick; ≤2 ms update per anchored VWAP") and an honesty requirement — when the anchor precedes recorded tick history, the result must be visibly badged as approximate.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tool `anchored_vwap` in the registry: single click on a bar sets the anchor; the VWAP line is computed from that bar's prints forward and **updates live** as new trades arrive.
- Standard-deviation bands at 1σ / 2σ / 3σ, individually toggleable in the properties popover, rendered as lines with optional fill bands.
- Incremental accumulator state per anchored VWAP (`Σpv`, `Σv`, `Σp²v`) advanced per new bar/trade rather than recomputed; re-anchoring or a history backfill triggers exactly one bounded recompute.
- **Approximation fallback**: when the anchor is earlier than recorded tick history (E16 recorder start), VWAP is computed from bar-approximated volume and the drawing renders a visible "approximate" badge (CMP-227 EstimatedBadge) with a tooltip explaining why and from when real ticks are available.
- Live price/σ readout in the legend; the VWAP value and current σ distance exposed on hover and to the surrogate node.
- Persistence: anchor `{t, p}` plus band configuration in `style`/`geometry`; the computed series is never persisted (derived state).

## Out of scope
- Session/rolling VWAP as an **indicator** — that is **E13** (`IND` domain); this story is the drawing-anchored variant only.
- Profile-derived VWAP and value-area overlays — **E19**.
- Anchoring to a news/derivatives event rather than a bar — R2+.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Anchor
  When I click a bar to anchor
  Then a VWAP is computed from that bar's prints forward and updates live

Scenario: Bands
  When I enable standard-deviation bands
  Then 1/2/3σ bands render and are individually toggleable

Scenario: No tick data
  Given the anchor precedes recorded tick history
  Then VWAP falls back to bar-approximated volume with a visible "approximate" badge

Scenario: Update stays inside budget
  Given an anchored VWAP spanning 50 000 bars
  When a new trade arrives
  Then the update is incremental and costs ≤2 ms, with no full-series recomputation

Scenario: Re-anchoring is bounded
  When the anchor is dragged 10 000 bars earlier
  Then exactly one recompute runs, it reports progress if it exceeds 100 ms, and the UI never blocks

Scenario: Data gap is not hidden
  Given a gap in recorded trades inside the anchored range
  Then the badge and tooltip state that the series is partial, and the numeric readout is not presented as exact
```

## Technical notes / design
The accumulator lives in the engine worker beside the bar/trade series so no market data crosses the thread boundary per tick. σ is derived from the running `Σp²v` via the standard weighted-variance identity, with `Decimal`→`float64` conversion done once at the accumulator boundary and the running sums held in a numerically stable form (compensated summation) — a naive `Σp²v` over 50k bars of a 64,000-priced instrument loses precision fast, and this is risk **R7 Data accuracy**, not a cosmetic concern. The approximate path uses kline `turnover/volume` as the per-bar typical price × volume, and the badge is bound to the *provenance* of the data, matching the pattern already used for profiles in SCR-038.

## Test plan
Unit: accumulator correctness against a brute-force reference over generated series (exact within tolerance), σ identity, compensated-summation precision at 50k bars, approximate-path fallback selection. Integration: recorded Bybit fixture replay with a known VWAP result; gap fixture asserting the partial badge. Perf: 2 ms update budget asserted in CI; re-anchor recompute bounded. E2E: anchor, toggle bands, drag anchor, reload persistence. Golden image: VWAP + 3 bands, both themes, badged state.

## Security notes
No new server surface. The approximate badge is a *correctness-disclosure* control: suppressing it would misrepresent derived data to a trader making sizing decisions, which the advice-boundary policy (R9) treats as a real risk — the badge is therefore covered by an automated test, not only a design note.

## Accessibility notes
The surrogate exposes "Anchored VWAP from 2026-10-13 09:00, current 64,180.2, price 1.4 sigma above" and the approximate state in text ("approximate: computed from bars, tick history starts 2026-10-11"). Band toggles are keyboard-operable checkboxes. The badge is text + icon, never colour-alone, and meets contrast in both themes.

## Performance notes
≤2 ms per update per anchored VWAP (story NFR); incremental only; bounded recompute on re-anchor with progress reporting beyond 100 ms; multiple simultaneous anchored VWAPs share the trade iteration pass rather than each scanning the series.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=anchored_vwap}`, `drawing.vwap_bands_toggled{sigma}`, `drawing.vwap_approximated` analytics; metrics `engine_vwap_update_ms`, `engine_vwap_recompute_total`, `engine_vwap_approx_active` gauge.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Accuracy validated against a brute-force reference on a recorded fixture.
- [ ] 2 ms update budget asserted in CI with a regression gate.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the engine accumulator, ≥80% frontend.
- [ ] axe-core green; approximate-state announcement verified; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-S02** (anchor placement pipeline); requires the trade/bar series from **E12** and recorder provenance from **E16** (US-DRAW-005 deps: US-MKT-006).

## Branch
`feat/e14-anchored-vwap`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-005; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-227 EstimatedBadge; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037, SCR-038 (provenance badge pattern); `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

title: Text note, callout, arrow and measure tool annotations
body: ## Context Implements **US-DRAW-006 — Text, note and price label annotations (Must)**: "I want to attach notes to the chart, so that my reasoning stays with the price action", and adds the `arrow`, `callout` and `measure` tools from the roadmap's E14 scope line. This is the only DRAW story with a genuine **injection surface** — the NFR says it outright: "text sanitised before storage and rendering" — and the only one whose output flows into another product surface ("notes are included in journal snapshots", E41). ## Scope / Deliverables - Tools `text`, `callout`, `arrow`, `measure` in the registry (`Alt+M` for measure). - Text/callout: place at a bar+price anchor, inline edit with a plain-text editor, font size (8–48 per `DrawingInput.style`), colour, optional background box and border; the callout adds a leader line to a second anchor. - **Overflow handling**: text exceeding its box truncates with an expand affordance and a full-text tooltip (US scenario "Long text"); the expanded view is a popover, not an unbounded canvas box. - Arrow: two-anchor directional marker reusing the trendline pipeline with a head glyph. - **Measure tool**: transient by default — drag between two points and read price delta, %, bar count, elapsed time and (when available) traded volume in the range; `Enter` pins it as a persisted `measure` drawing, `Esc` discards. - Sanitisation: control characters and bidi-override characters stripped, length capped (120 chars for labels, a configured maximum for note bodies), content stored and rendered as **plain text only** at every boundary (canvas glyphs, DOM surrogate, journal snapshot, tooltip). - Every annotation appears in the object tree (E14-S08) with its text and anchor and is keyboard-reachable — the US "Screen reader" scenario. ## Out of scope - Rich text, markdown, links or images in notes. - Emoji-marker library beyond the plain text path. - Journal integration itself (**E41**) — this story only guarantees the sanitised, plain-text contract it will consume. ## Acceptance criteria ```gherkin Scenario: Add note When I place a note and type text Then it anchors to a bar and price and persists per symbol Scenario: Long text Given the text exceeds the box Then it truncates with an expand affordance and a full-text tooltip Scenario: Screen reader Then each annotation is listed in the object tree with its text and anchor, and is reachable by keyboard Scenario: Markup is never interpreted Given a note whose text is "" When it renders on the canvas, in the object tree, in the tooltip and in a journal snapshot Then the literal characters are displayed in every surface and no script executes Scenario: Bidi and control characters are neutralised Given a note containing bidi-override or control characters Then they are stripped on write, so the stored and displayed text cannot spoof surrounding UI text Scenario: Measure is transient unless pinned When I drag a measurement and release without confirming Then the readout disappears and nothing is persisted; pressing Enter instead pins it as a drawing ``` ## Technical notes / design Sanitisation happens **on write, server-side** (E14-T01 validation) and defensively on render; the client never trusts stored text either, because a drawing may predate a sanitiser change. Canvas text goes through the SDF atlas as glyph indices, which is inherently inert, but the DOM surrogate and the tooltip use `textContent` assignment exclusively. Text boxes size to their content up to a max box, then truncate at a glyph boundary with an ellipsis; measurement of the truncation point happens in the worker using atlas metrics so no DOM reflow is involved. The measure tool's volume readout is only shown when recorded trade data covers the range, otherwise the field is omitted rather than estimated. ## Test plan Unit: sanitiser (XSS payload corpus, bidi/control characters, length caps), truncation at glyph boundaries, measure maths (delta, %, bars, elapsed). Security: the XSS corpus asserted across all four render surfaces. Golden image: note, callout, arrow, truncated note, measure readout, both themes. title: Long/short position tool with R:R, risk sizing and send-to-ticket handoff
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-007 — Long/short position tool (Must)**: "I want a drag-based long/short tool showing risk, reward and size, so that I plan the trade before I place it." It is the highest-stakes drawing in the Epic because its numbers influence real position sizing, and its NFR is unambiguous: "identical sizing maths as US-PROF-002 (shared implementation)". Two implementations of sizing that disagree by a rounding step is a money bug, so this story **imports** the sizing module rather than reimplementing it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `long_position` and `short_position`: three draggable levels — entry, stop, target — plus a time extent, rendered as the familiar two-tone box (risk zone / reward zone) with handles per level.
- Readout on the drawing and in the properties popover: **R:R ratio**, risk in USDT, reward in USDT, stop distance in ticks and %, target distance, and the **position size implied by the active account profile** (leverage, sizing rule, risk cap).
- Shared sizing implementation: the same module used by US-PROF-002 (per-account profile sizing), imported — not copied — with a contract test asserting both call sites produce identical output for a shared fixture table.
- Tick/lot validation per SCR-037 ("the position tool validates against tick/lot"): entry/stop/target quantised to tick size, size quantised to lot size and floored to `min_qty`, with the residual shown rather than silently rounded away.
- **Risk-cap error state**: when implied risk exceeds the profile cap, the tool renders its error state and "send to ticket" is **disabled with the reason stated** (US scenario).
- "Send to ticket" handoff: emits a typed intent `{side, entry, stop, target, qty, symbol, profile_id}` on the app bus. In R1 the consumer (**E30 order ticket**) does not exist yet, so the action is gated by the `trading.ticket` feature flag — flag off renders it disabled with "available when trading ships"; the intent contract and its tests ship now.
- No-profile fallback: with no account profile selected, size is shown as "—" with an explanatory chip, and R:R/risk-in-ticks still compute.

## Out of scope
- Placing any order (**E30/E29**) — this story never touches the OMS.
- Fan-out sizing across multiple accounts (**E34**).
- Fee/funding-adjusted PnL projection — R3.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Drag entry, stop and target
  Then the tool shows R:R, risk in USDT, reward in USDT and the position size implied by the account profile

Scenario: Send to ticket
  When I choose "send to ticket"
  Then the order ticket opens pre-filled with entry, stop, target and the computed size

Scenario: Risk exceeds cap
  Given the implied risk exceeds the profile cap
  Then the tool highlights it in the error state and the "send to ticket" action is disabled with the reason

Scenario: Sizing matches the profile implementation exactly
  Given the shared sizing fixture table
  When sizing is computed through the position tool and through the per-account profile path
  Then every row produces byte-identical quantities, and any divergence fails the contract test

Scenario: Tick and lot rounding is visible, not silent
  Given a stop distance that implies 0.0137 BTC on a 0.001 lot instrument
  Then the tool shows 0.013 with the rounding direction indicated, and never shows an unplaceable quantity

Scenario: Trading not yet enabled
  Given the trading.ticket feature flag is off
  Then "send to ticket" is disabled with an explanatory label, the intent is not emitted, and all readouts still compute

Scenario: Inverted levels
  Given a long position whose stop is dragged above its entry
  Then the tool shows an invalid state with the reason and does not report a negative risk as a positive reward
```

## Technical notes / design
All money maths is `Decimal` with the instrument's tick/lot metadata; no float ever touches risk or quantity. The sizing module is a pure function `(entry, stop, profile, instrument) -> {qty, risk_usdt, capped: bool, reason}` living in a shared package consumed by both this tool and the profile screen, with a golden fixture table (CSV) as the single source of truth for both — that table *is* the contract test. Levels are stored as three anchor points so the drawing survives interval changes like any other; the derived numbers are never persisted. The error state uses the design-system error token plus an icon and text, so it is not a colour-only signal.

## Test plan
Unit: R:R maths, risk/reward in USDT, inverted-level detection, tick/lot quantisation and floor-to-min-qty. Contract: the shared fixture table asserted through both call sites. Integration: profile changes (leverage, risk cap) update the readout live. E2E: drag all three levels, exceed the cap, observe the disabled action and reason; flag on/off behaviour. a11y: axe-core, announcements of each readout change. Golden image: long and short, valid/invalid/capped states, both themes.

## Security notes
The displayed size is decision-grade information: an incorrect or stale profile silently applied would misinform sizing, so the readout names which profile it used and invalidates immediately when the profile changes. The send-to-ticket intent carries no credentials and is validated by the consumer independently — the receiving ticket must re-derive size server-side rather than trusting the client-sent quantity (documented here so E30 inherits the requirement). Risk-cap enforcement in this tool is advisory UI only; the authoritative cap lives in **E39** and must never be assumed enforced by this drawing.

## Accessibility notes
The surrogate composes "Long position, entry 64,000, stop 63,700, target 64,900, R:R 3.0, risk 150 USDT, size 0.5 BTC, within cap". Each level handle is individually focusable and nudgeable by tick, with the recomputed R:R announced politely (debounced so a nudge-hold does not flood the live region). The capped/invalid state is conveyed by text and icon, and the disabled action states its reason in its accessible description, not only in a tooltip.

## Performance notes
Recomputation on drag is O(1) and runs on the main thread inside the interaction frame; live-region announcements are debounced to 300 ms. The tool renders as two quads, three lines and one label group — negligible against the overlay budget.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=long_position|short_position}`, `drawing.position_tool_capped`, `drawing.send_to_ticket{enabled}` analytics; metric `position_tool_sizing_divergence_total` (must stay zero; alerts if the shared module ever disagrees at runtime).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Shared-sizing contract test green against the fixture table used by the profile implementation.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend / ≥85% on the shared sizing package.
- [ ] Security review comment present covering the "client-sent quantity is never authoritative" note.
- [ ] axe-core green; screen-reader pass on readouts; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] Feature flag `trading.ticket` state recorded per environment.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-S03** (box/handle model). Cross-epic: shared sizing from **E28** (US-PROF-002) — if E28 lands later, the module is authored here to the agreed signature and E28 imports it; consumer **E30** (US-ORD-001) is R3 and gated by flag.

## Branch
`feat/e14-position-tool`

## References

title: Object tree, lock/hide, clone, z-order and undo/redo UI (SCR-036)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-008 — Object management: undo/redo, lock, hide, layers (Must/Should/Could)**: "I want to undo, lock, hide and manage drawing objects, so that my chart stays under control." This is the story that makes a chart with 500 objects usable, and it is also the story where the accessibility promise of the whole Epic is cashed: the object tree is the non-visual representation of the canvas. Its NFRs are hard numbers — "undo stack ≥50 operations per symbol, session-scoped; tree is virtualised for ≥500 objects" — and its home is **SCR-036** (shared with the indicator manager from E13).

## Scope / Deliverables
- The drawings section of **SCR-036** object tree (CMP-049 Table in a CMP-046 Drawer): one row per drawing showing **type, anchor time/price, label, visibility and lock state**, grouped by tool family, sorted by z-order or creation time.
- Row actions: select (highlights and scrolls the chart to it), rename label, toggle visibility, toggle lock, clone, delete, bring-forward / send-backward (z-order), with multi-row selection and bulk actions.
- Global actions surfaced both here and in the toolbar: lock-all, hide-all, delete-all — with lock-all behaving exactly as the US requires: "they cannot be moved by dragging but remain visible and selectable for inspection".
- Undo/redo UI: toolbar buttons with tooltips naming the next operation ("Undo: delete trendline"), `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z`, stack depth ≥50 per symbol (target 100 per the engine design), session-scoped, cleared on symbol change but independent per symbol within a session.
- **Virtualisation**: the tree renders only visible rows and stays responsive at ≥500 objects; filter-by-type and free-text filter on label.
- Clone semantics: a cloned drawing is offset slightly, retains style, gets a new id, and is a single undoable command.
- Empty state (CMP-026) when a symbol has no drawings, with a hint pointing at the toolbar hotkeys.

## Out of scope
- Indicator rows in SCR-036 (**E13** owns them; this story only composes into the same screen).
- Cross-pane sync toggles and templates (**E14-S09**).
- Persisted (cross-session) undo history — explicitly session-scoped by the NFR.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Undo/redo
  When I press Ctrl+Z after deleting a drawing
  Then it is restored with all properties; Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes

Scenario: Lock and hide all
  When I lock all drawings
  Then they cannot be moved by dragging but remain visible and selectable for inspection

Scenario: Object tree
  Then an object list shows every drawing on the symbol with type, anchor time/price, visibility and lock state, navigable by keyboard

Scenario: Tree stays responsive at scale
  Given 500 drawings on the symbol
  Then the tree renders in under 100 ms, scrolls at 60 fps, and only visible rows exist in the DOM

Scenario: Undo stack is bounded and per-symbol
  Given 120 operations on BTCUSDT and 5 on ETHUSDT
  Then BTCUSDT offers at least the most recent 50 undos, ETHUSDT offers its own 5, and neither affects the other

Scenario: Bulk delete is one undoable command
  Given 20 rows selected
  When they are deleted and Ctrl+Z is pressed once
  Then all 20 are restored together with their properties

Scenario: Selecting a row reveals the drawing
  Given a drawing anchored outside the current viewport
  When its row is activated
  Then the chart scrolls to bring it into view and the drawing is selected and announced
```

## Technical notes / design
The tree is a virtualised list over the same immutable store state the engine renders, so there is no second source of truth and no synchronisation code — a row is a projection of a drawing. Bulk operations compose into one composite command so undo is symmetric with the user's mental model. Scroll-to-drawing uses the chart-space anchor and the existing viewport animation from E11 rather than a jump cut, and respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. Z-order writes `z_index` (smallint per the schema) with a normalisation pass to avoid unbounded growth on repeated bring-forward.

## Test plan
Unit: command composition for bulk ops, stack bounds/scoping, z-order normalisation, filter logic. Perf: render and scroll benchmark at 500 and 1000 rows; DOM node count assertion proving virtualisation. E2E: undo/redo across every operation type, lock-all then attempt drag, hide-all then attempt pick, bulk delete + single undo, row → chart reveal. a11y: axe-core, full keyboard traversal, screen-reader row announcements.

## Security notes
Rows display user-authored labels — same plain-text-only rendering contract as E14-S06, re-asserted by the XSS corpus test on the tree surface. Delete-all and bulk delete are destructive: confirmed, scoped to the current user's own drawings, undoable, and never triggered by a single unmodified keystroke.

## Accessibility notes
This is the Epic's primary non-visual surface. The tree is a real table (CMP-049) with row headers, sortable columns, and per-row controls that are buttons with explicit accessible names ("Hide trendline at 64,120") — not icon-only ambiguity. Keyboard: arrow navigation, `Space` to toggle visibility, `L` to lock, `Delete` to remove, `Enter` to reveal on the chart. Lock and visibility state are text + icon, never colour-alone. Undo/redo announce the operation they performed. Focus returns predictably after a row is deleted (to the next row).

## Performance notes
Virtualised for ≥500 objects (NFR); initial render <100 ms at 500 rows; scrolling at 60 fps; toggling visibility on 100 rows applies as one store update and one engine snapshot, not 100.

## Observability
`drawing.locked`, `drawing.hidden`, `drawing.cloned`, `drawing.zorder_changed`, `drawing.bulk_deleted{count}`, `drawings_undo_total`, `drawings_redo_total` analytics/metrics; `drawings_tree_render_ms` client metric.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Virtualisation proven by a DOM-node-count assertion at 500 rows.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the tree and command modules.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-036; full keyboard traversal and a screen-reader pass recorded (this is the Epic's headline a11y evidence).
- [ ] design-qa comparison against SCR-036 recorded; QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

`blocked_by`: **E14-S01** (drawings exist to manage), **E14-S06** (annotation text in rows). Composes with **E13** on SCR-036. Blocks **E14-S09**.

`feat/e14-object-tree`

title: Drawing style templates and cross-pane level sync
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-009 — Drawing templates and cross-chart sync (Should)**: "I want drawing styles saved as templates and levels synced across panes, so that multi-chart layouts stay consistent." It closes the Epic by making the previous eight stories consistent and reusable, and it carries one hard safety rule from the NFR: "sync is per-layout and per-symbol; **never** syncs across different symbols."

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Style templates**: save the current drawing's style (colour, width, dash, fill, label settings, and for fib the level set from E14-S04) as a named template per tool; apply a template to a selection or set it as the tool's default for new drawings.
- Template management UI in the properties popover: save, rename, apply, set-default, delete, with a preview swatch (CMP-228 PreviewTile pattern).
- **Cross-pane sync**: a per-pane toggle (part of the layout's sync-axis group from E15); with sync on, a drawing created or edited on symbol S in one pane appears in every other pane showing symbol S in the same layout, instantly.
- Sync-off panes keep their drawings **local to that pane** (scoped by `layout_id`) and the object tree marks them as pane-local, per the US scenario.
- Hard guard: sync is keyed on `(layout_id, symbol)`; a pane showing a different symbol never receives another symbol's drawings, enforced by an assertion in the store and an explicit test.
- Migration behaviour: toggling sync off on a pane converts nothing retroactively; toggling on offers an explicit "copy existing pane-local drawings to the symbol" action rather than doing it silently.

## Out of scope
- Sharing templates between users (**collaboration, R5**).
- Layout persistence itself (**E15**) — this story consumes it.
- Syncing indicators (**E13/E15**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Style template
  When I save a style as "key level" and apply it
  Then colour, width, style and label settings apply to new drawings of that type

Scenario: Cross-pane sync
  Given two panes show BTCUSDT at different intervals and level-sync is on
  Then a level drawn in one appears in the other instantly

Scenario: Sync off
  Given sync is off for a pane
  Then drawings made there remain local to that pane and are marked as such in the object tree

Scenario: Symbols never cross
  Given one pane shows BTCUSDT and another shows ETHUSDT with sync on
  When a level is drawn on BTCUSDT
  Then the ETHUSDT pane is unchanged, and an assertion prevents any code path from delivering it there

Scenario: Template deletion does not orphan drawings
  Given drawings created from the "key level" template
  When the template is deleted
  Then existing drawings keep their concrete style values unchanged and only the reusable template disappears

Scenario: Enabling sync is explicit, never silent
  Given a pane with 4 pane-local drawings
  When sync is enabled for it
  Then nothing changes until the user confirms "copy 4 drawings to the symbol", and that action is undoable
```

## Technical notes / design
Templates are style snapshots, not references — applying a template copies concrete values into the drawing, which is why deleting a template cannot orphan anything. They persist alongside other chart config (the `chart_templates` family in migration `0011_workspace`) scoped to the owner. Sync is a *query-scope* decision, not a replication mechanism: a synced pane subscribes to `(symbol)` and a pane-local one to `(symbol, layout_id)`, so there is no copying, no conflict resolution and no chance of divergence — and the symbol guard is a single filter that cannot be bypassed per-pane.

## Test plan
Unit: template save/apply/set-default/delete, fib level-set inclusion, scope-key resolution. Property-based: for any random pane/symbol/layout combination, a drawing is delivered only to panes whose symbol matches exactly. E2E: two-pane sync on/off, enable-sync confirmation flow, template apply and default, template delete leaving drawings intact. a11y: axe-core on the template UI, keyboard operation, announcements.

## Security notes
Templates are owner-scoped like drawings; template names are user content, sanitised and length-capped on the same path as labels (E14-S06). The symbol guard is also a correctness control — a level from another instrument rendered on a chart could directly cause a mis-priced trade, so it is asserted rather than assumed.

## Accessibility notes
Template list is a keyboard-operable listbox with named actions per item; the preview swatch has a text description of the style ("2 px dashed, accent colour") because a swatch alone is colour-only information. The sync toggle states its scope in its accessible description ("Sync drawings across panes showing BTCUSDT in this layout"). Pane-local drawings are marked with text in the object tree, not only an icon.

## Performance notes
Sync adds no per-frame cost (it is a subscription scope). Applying a template to a multi-selection is one store command and one engine snapshot regardless of selection size.

## Observability
`drawing.template_saved{tool}`, `drawing.template_applied{tool}`, `drawing.default_saved{tool}`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts` (the SCR-037 analytics event), `drawing.sync_toggled{enabled}`.

- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests, including the cross-symbol guard property test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on templates and scope resolution.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard-only template management verified; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037 updated with the template UI as shipped.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed. Epic-level acceptance can now be run.

## Dependencies

title: SAST/DAST rules and CI guards for the drawings render and persistence paths
body:
## Context
`E14-X02` finds today's bugs by hand. This ticket stops tomorrow's from being written. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA, secrets scanning and DAST (OWASP ZAP) across the programme; what is missing for E14 is the epic-specific rule set that encodes its two irreducible invariants:

1. **User-controlled drawing text never reaches a raw-HTML or raw-attribute sink.** The object tree, tooltips, popovers and accessible names all consume `label`, annotation text and template names.
2. **Every `/drawings` route filters by the authenticated principal.** `scope: self` is a promise made in the OpenAPI document; nothing today makes a handler that forgets the filter fail a build.

Generic SAST catches neither reliably — the first because `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on a sanitised-looking variable is indistinguishable from a safe one without knowing the taint source, the second because a missing `WHERE owner_user_id = ...` is valid code. Targeted rules do.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Semgrep rules** under `.semgrep/e14-drawings.yml`:
  - `drawings-text-to-html-sink`: flags any flow from a drawing `label`/`text`/`template name`/`style` value into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`, or an `href`/`src`/`style` attribute built by concatenation. Severity: error, blocking.
  - `drawings-query-missing-owner-filter`: flags any SQLAlchemy/SQL statement selecting, updating or deleting from `drawings` without an `owner_user_id` predicate bound to the request principal. Severity: error, blocking.
  - `drawings-owner-from-body`: flags any assignment of `owner_user_id` from request-body data rather than from the session principal.
  - `drawings-unbounded-geometry`: flags a create/update path that persists `geometry` without passing through the size/point-count validator introduced by `E14-X01`'s SRs.
  - `drawings-batch-unvalidated-ids`: flags a batch handler that resolves ids without an ownership check applied to the whole set before any mutation.
  - `drawings-pixel-geometry`: a non-security correctness guard riding along — flags persisting a geometry object containing `x`/`y`/`px` keys, since chart-space-only storage is a contract (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) and a pixel leak is the top functional risk of the epic.
- **CodeQL**: enable the JavaScript/TypeScript XSS and Python SQL-injection/access-control query packs for the drawings paths, with a custom taint source declaring drawing text fields as user input so the existing queries actually fire.
- **ESLint/lint guards**: ban `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` outright inside `apps/web/src/drawings/**` and `apps/web/src/objecttree/**` with no eslint-disable permitted (a CI check greps for the disable comment in those paths).
- **Production-bundle guard**: a build-time assertion that `__cvEngine.projectForTest` (from `E14-Q03`) and any other test-only handle are absent from the production bundle — the mitigation `E14-X01` claims for that spoofing threat.
- **ZAP/DAST profile additions** (`security/zap/e14-drawings.conf`): authenticated scan covering `GET/POST /drawings`, `POST /drawings/batch`, `PUT/DELETE /drawings/{id}` with two authenticated contexts so ZAP's access-control testing can compare principals; active-scan policies for injection and for oversized-payload handling; ids that are known-safe (e.g. the deliberate 422 paths) added to the baseline so the scan stays actionable.
- **Dependency/SCA note**: any new frontend dependency introduced by E14 for sanitisation or geometry maths is pinned, reviewed and added to the SCA allowlist with a rationale; a sanitiser library in particular is treated as security-critical and its version is pinned with an update-watch.
- **Documentation**: a short section in `04-security-program.md` (or its rules appendix) describing the E14 rule set, what each rule protects, and the deliberate-regression test that proves it fires.

## Out of scope
- Running and triaging the full programme-wide DAST sweep (E43).
- Writing the sanitiser or the ownership filter (owned by `E14-T01`, `E14-T02` and the story tickets); this ticket enforces their presence.
- Secrets scanning configuration (already programme-wide from R0).
- Container and infrastructure scanning (E03/E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Each rule fires on a deliberately vulnerable change
  Given a scratch branch that renders a drawing label via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
  When CI runs the E14 Semgrep rule set
  Then drawings-text-to-html-sink reports an error and the pull request is blocked
  And the same holds for a drawings query with no owner filter and for owner_user_id read from the body

Scenario: The rule set is quiet on the real codebase
  Given the current main branch
  When the E14 rule set runs
  Then it reports zero findings
  And any suppression in the drawings paths is accompanied by a written rationale reviewed by the Security engineer

Scenario: Failure case - a test-only handle reaches production
  Given a production build in which the engine test handle is not stripped
  When the production-bundle guard runs
  Then the build fails naming the handle
  And the failure references the spoofing threat it mitigates in the E14 threat model

Scenario: Edge case - authenticated DAST distinguishes principals
  Given the ZAP profile configured with the qa-owner and qa-manager contexts
  When the authenticated scan runs against the drawings routes
  Then access-control comparison alerts are raised for any route where one principal can reach the other's resources
  And no alert is raised for the documented 404 behaviour
```

## Technical notes / design
- Rules are scoped by path so they are fast and so a false positive elsewhere in the monorepo cannot desensitise the team to them.
- Each rule ships with a paired fixture: one vulnerable snippet under `.semgrep/tests/e14/` that must match and one safe snippet that must not, run by Semgrep's own test runner in CI. A rule without both fixtures is not merged — this is what keeps the rule set honest as the codebase moves.
- The `drawings-query-missing-owner-filter` rule is deliberately conservative (it may flag a legitimate admin query); the escape hatch is an explicit, reviewed annotation rather than a bare suppression comment, so every exception is visible in review.
- The ZAP profile runs nightly against staging rather than per-PR, because authenticated active scanning is slow and noisy on a pull-request cadence; per-PR protection is the SAST layer.
- The pixel-geometry rule is included here rather than in QA because it is cheap, static and protects the same contract the security model depends on (chart-space storage is what makes a drawing reproducible and therefore auditable).

## Test plan
- Every rule validated by its matching/non-matching fixture pair in CI.
- End-to-end validation: three deliberately vulnerable scratch branches (HTML sink, missing owner filter, owner from body) each blocked by the expected rule and by no other, with evidence linked.
- ZAP profile validated by temporarily removing the ownership filter on staging and confirming the access-control alert appears; restored immediately afterwards with the change recorded.
- False-positive rate reviewed after two weeks of running; a rule with a high false-positive rate is tuned rather than suppressed.

## Security notes
- The rule set is the durable half of `E14-X01`'s control mapping: each rule's header comment names the `T`/`SR` id it enforces, so a future reader can trace a lint error back to the threat it prevents.
- Suppressions in drawings paths require Security-engineer review; the CI check that greps for eslint-disable in those directories makes a silent suppression impossible.
- ZAP output is stored in the internal artefact store; alerts are triaged within the programme SLA and never auto-closed.

## Accessibility notes
- The HTML-sink rule explicitly includes `aria-label`, `aria-description` and `title` attribute construction, because the accessibility path is a real injection path and is the one most likely to be built by naive string concatenation.
- The rules must not push developers toward stripping content (which would break RTL/emoji notes); the rule messages point to the approved escaping helper rather than to sanitisation-by-deletion.

## Performance notes
- The E14 rule set must add under 30 s to CI; rules are path-scoped and measured, and the budget is asserted by the CI timing report.
- The nightly ZAP scan is bounded to the drawings routes so it completes within the nightly window and does not crowd out the rest of the security job.

## Observability
- SARIF output uploaded to the code-scanning dashboard so E14 findings appear alongside the programme's.
- A monthly report counts rule hits, suppressions and false positives, giving evidence for whether the rule set is earning its place.

## Definition of Done
- All six Semgrep rules merged with passing fixture pairs; CodeQL taint sources configured; lint bans and the disable-comment check in place.
- Production-bundle guard wired into the release build and demonstrated failing on a deliberate violation.
- ZAP profile merged and running nightly with a clean triaged baseline.
- Three deliberately vulnerable branches demonstrably blocked, evidence linked.
- Rule set documented in `04-security-program.md` and cross-referenced from the E14 threat model.

## Dependencies
- `E14-X01` for the threat ids and SR list the rules enforce; `E14-T01`/`E14-T02` for the code paths to scope rules to; programme SAST/DAST tooling from R0 (E03).

## Branch
`chore/e14-sast-dast-rules`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (SAST/SCA/DAST/secrets programme, rules appendix)
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (required checks, suppression policy)
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings*` `x-rbac` `scope: self`, chart-space geometry contract
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 `drawings`
- `docs/security/threat-models/e14-drawings.md` (from `E14-X01`)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036 (accessible-name construction)

1. docs/plan/20-architecture.md (infra/ module map)
2. docs/plan/04-security-program.md (relevant controls)
3. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md (if perf-labelled)
4. AGENTS.md §4 (commands)

title: ADR and operator/user docs for the workspace document format and sharing rules
body:
## Context
The workspace document is about to become a long-lived contract: it is persisted in Postgres, exported to files that users keep, and extended by every subsequent epic that adds a panel type. Decisions made implicitly in Sprint 08 — how the dock tree is serialised, how versioning works, what may and may not be exported, what happens to an unknown pane kind — will be re-litigated for years unless they are written down once, with their rationale.

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires docs to reflect *shipped* behaviour, and the planning brief requires an ADR for decisions of this reach. This chore captures the decision, the format, and the two pieces of user-facing guidance that stop support questions from becoming tickets.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR** `docs/adr/00NN-workspace-document-format-and-sharing.md` recording:
  - The serialised dock-tree shape and its relationship to `layouts` / `layout_panes` in `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 (why the tree is persisted as panes-with-slots rather than an opaque blob, and what that buys in queryability and validation).
  - The versioning rule: documents carry a schema version; a newer version is **refused** with both versions stated (US-LAY-007), never partially applied; the forward-compat policy for unknown pane kinds within the same major version (dropped with a report).
  - The export allow-list and the id-regeneration rule from `E15-X01`, stated as architecture rather than as an implementation detail.
  - Conflict handling: ETag/`If-Match` with 412 and the [Keep mine]/[Load theirs] resolution, and why last-write-wins was rejected.
  - Rejected alternatives: opaque JSON blob; CRDT-style merge; server-side rendering of layouts; auto-migration of newer documents.
- **Panel-author guide** `docs/dev/adding-a-panel-type.md`: the registry entry, serialisation contract, lazy mount, hidden-tab unsubscribe after 30 s, accessible name, panel menu entries, density support, float/re-dock survival, and the `E15-Q07` new-panel-type checklist to run. Linked from `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-080.
- **Operator/user guidance** in the user docs: saving and restoring workspaces, what export does and does not contain (explicitly: no keys, no tokens, no account bindings), why an import may drop elements, the reduced-capability profile and how to restore the full profile, and what the pane-limit warning means.
- Updates to `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §2 and `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §16 if shipped behaviour diverged from the plan, per the DoD rule that docs describe what shipped.

## Out of scope
- Documenting other epics' panel internals.
- The collaboration/sharing features of R5 (this ADR constrains them; it does not design them).
- Release notes (release management process).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR records a decision with alternatives
  Given the published ADR
  Then it states context, decision, consequences and at least three rejected alternatives with reasons
  And it is accepted by the Architect and the Security engineer

Scenario: A new panel author needs no tribal knowledge
  Given an engineer on E18 adding the footprint panel
  When they follow docs/dev/adding-a-panel-type.md
  Then they can register, serialise, restore and float a panel without reading the dock package source

Scenario: Failure case - docs diverge from shipped behaviour
  Given the implementation refuses newer-version imports but the docs promise migration
  Then the divergence is corrected in the docs before the epic is Done, and the DoD docs checkbox cannot be ticked otherwise

Scenario: Edge case - export contents claim is verifiable
  Given the user documentation states an export contains no account bindings
  Then it links to the test that asserts it, so the claim is evidenced rather than reassuring

Scenario: Discoverability
  When a reader opens 15-component-catalogue.md CMP-080
  Then it links to the panel-author guide, and the ADR is linked from the E15 epic and from 20-architecture.md module M10
```

## Technical notes / design
- Keep the ADR short and decisive; the long-form format lives in `24-internal-schemas.md`-style documentation and the OpenAPI schema, not duplicated in the ADR.
- The panel-author guide should be a checklist with code snippets, written so that following it is faster than improvising — that is the only way a guide gets used.
- Cross-link rather than copy: the export allow-list is owned by `E15-X01`/the implementation, and the ADR references it so there is one source of truth.

## Test plan
- Doc review by the Architect, the Security engineer and one engineer from a downstream epic (E18 or E21) who has not worked on E15 — their ability to follow the panel guide is the acceptance test.
- Link-check and example-check in CI (code snippets compile against the current API).
- Verify every factual claim about export contents and version handling against the merged tests; any claim with no test is either tested or removed.

## Security notes
- The user-facing statement about export contents is a security-relevant claim; it must match the implemented allow-list exactly and link to its test. Overstating it would create false confidence about sharing a file.
- The ADR records that workspace exports are user-confidential (they reveal watched symbols and trading style), constraining any future "share a workspace" feature in R5 to explicit, audited sharing rather than public links.
- The panel-author guide includes the security checklist items a new panel must satisfy: no unescaped rendering of workspace-derived strings, no client-trusted ids, server-side permission checks for role-restricted panels.

## Accessibility notes
- The panel-author guide makes accessible name, keyboard menu entries and focus behaviour mandatory checklist items, so a11y is inherited by construction rather than retrofitted per panel in E47.
- User documentation describes the keyboard equivalents for every layout operation, so the keyboard path is discoverable and not merely present.

## Performance notes
- The guide states the two performance obligations a panel author must meet — lazy mount (`SCR-024` ≤150 ms) and unsubscribe when hidden for 30 s (`SCR-020`) — plus the rule that layout changes must never remount the WebGL context, with the `E15-Q04` benchmark named as the check.
- The ADR records the measured baselines from `E15-Q04` as the reference point future changes are compared against.

## Observability
- Documents the analytics/audit event vocabulary for the layout surface (`workspace.*`, `panel.*`, `layout.*`, `sync.*`) including which are audited versus analytics-only, so downstream epics emit consistent events instead of inventing names.
- Records where the ops dashboard shows import rejections and probing alerts, for the operator runbook.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ADR merged and accepted by Architect and Security engineer; linked from the E15 epic and `20-architecture.md` M10.
- [ ] `docs/dev/adding-a-panel-type.md` merged and linked from CMP-080 in `15-component-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] User-facing workspace documentation merged, with the export-contents claim linked to its test.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` §2 and `11-user-stories.md` §16 reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] Reviewed by a downstream-epic engineer who successfully followed the panel guide.

## Dependencies
- `E15-X01` (allow-list and versioning rules), `E15-Q04` (baseline numbers), `E15-S07` (shipped export/import behaviour).

## Branch
`docs/e15-workspace-format-adr`

## References

- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*`, `/chart-templates*`
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §2 (SCR-020..029)

title: Design QA of the built workspace, dock system, presets and sync surfaces
body:
## Context
Design QA closes the loop: the built product is compared against the signed-off specification, surface by surface, state by state, and the differences are either fixed or filed. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` makes this a Story-level DoD requirement for net-new UI, and E15 is the largest net-new UI surface in R1 - twelve screens and roughly thirty components that every later epic will inherit. A discrepancy tolerated here becomes the de facto standard for E18..E41.

This review runs in Sprint 09, alongside the tail of E15's engineering work (Sprints 06-09), so findings can be fixed inside the epic rather than carried into R2.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Surface-by-surface review** of the implemented SCR-011, SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-023, SCR-024, SCR-025, SCR-026, SCR-027, SCR-028, SCR-029, SCR-049, SCR-150 and SCR-153 against their spec pages and Figma frames.
- **State walk**: every state enumerated in the specs - loading, empty, populated, unsaved, conflict, crash-restored, over-budget, panel-too-small, invalid drop, at-minimum splitter, degraded, import rejected, version mismatch, delisted symbol - exercised in the real build, not in Storybook alone.
- **Token compliance check**: computed styles inspected against the token values from E15-D13; any hard-coded value is a finding.
- **Density and theme matrix**: compact/cosy/comfortable x dark/light at 1920x1080 and 1280x800, plus 200% zoom.
- **Interaction fidelity**: drag/drop zone geometry against the spec, keyboard move mode, splitter resize (pointer and keyboard), preset application, workspace switch, float and re-dock in the Electron build and the maximised-overlay fallback in the browser build.
- **Accessibility verification** against E15-D15: keyboard model as specified, focus destinations after every layout mutation, announcement strings matching the script verbatim, axe-core clean on every touched screen, one manual screen-reader pass.
- **Motion verification** against E15-D14: nothing animates a content box, reduced-motion behaviour correct, timings within the menu/preset budgets.
- **Copy verification** against the E15-D16 copy deck, string by string.
- **Findings register** with severity (blocker / major / minor / nit), a screenshot pair, the owning ticket, and a disposition - fixed in-epic, filed as a Bug with a priority, or accepted with a written reason.
- **Sign-off report** at `docs/design/specs/e15-design-qa-report.md`.

## Out of scope
- Functional/black-box QA (E15 QA chunk owns test-plan execution) - this review is fidelity to the design specification, though a functional defect found here is filed rather than ignored.
- Performance benchmarking (engineering owns the FPS and latency runs) - but a visually obvious frame-rate problem during a docking interaction is filed as a finding.
- New design work; anything requiring a design decision goes back to the owning design ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every specified state is verified in the real build
  Given the state inventory from the E15 specs
  When each state is exercised in the running application
  Then it is recorded as pass, fail or blocked with evidence
  And a state that cannot be reached is filed as a finding rather than skipped

Scenario: A hard-coded value is found
  Given computed styles on the implemented panel chrome
  When a value does not resolve to a design token
  Then it is filed as a finding against the implementing ticket
  And the fix uses the token rather than matching the value by hand

Scenario: Announcements do not match the script
  Given the E15-D15 announcement script
  When each state change is triggered with a screen reader running
  Then the spoken text matches the script
  And any divergence is filed as a blocker or major finding depending on whether meaning is lost

Scenario: Keyboard parity regressed during implementation
  Given every layout operation
  When each is attempted without a pointer
  Then all succeed as specified
  And any pointer-only operation is a blocker finding that cannot be accepted or deferred

Scenario: A finding is disputed
  Given a discrepancy the engineer believes is a spec error rather than a build error
  Then it is escalated to the CDO for a decision
  And the outcome is recorded, with the spec corrected if the engineer is right

Scenario: The review finds a blocker close to the release gate
  Given a blocker finding in Sprint 09
  Then it is fixed within the epic or the affected Story does not meet its DoD
  And no blocker is silently downgraded to close the epic
```

## Technical notes / design
Review in the real build, not in Storybook. Storybook proves a component in isolation; E15's failures are compositional - a panel header that is fine alone but collides with a sync badge at compact density in a 3x3 grid, or a focus ring that is correct until a floating window overlaps it (WCAG 2.4.11).

Evidence is paired screenshots - spec frame and build - because a prose description of a spacing discrepancy is unresolvable in review. For interaction findings, a short screen recording replaces the screenshot pair.

Severity should be assigned by *user consequence*, not by pixel magnitude: a 2 px gutter error is a nit, while a missing environment badge in a floating window is a blocker even though it is smaller on screen.

The review should explicitly re-check the five things E15's own specs flagged as easy to lose in implementation: the inset focus affordance (no reflow on focus), the letter on every sync badge, the environment word in every floating-window title, Esc mapping to Cancel rather than Discard, and the keyboard move mode's visible instructions.

## Test plan
(1) Screen-by-screen walk against spec pages with paired-screenshot evidence. (2) Full state walk in the real build. (3) Density x theme x zoom matrix sweep. (4) Interaction fidelity session, pointer and keyboard, in both Electron and browser builds. (5) axe-core run on every touched screen plus one manual NVDA pass on the five-task scenario from E15-D15. (6) Computed-style token audit on the chrome components. (7) Motion check including reduced-motion. (8) Copy diff against the copy deck. (9) Findings triage with the FE lead and the CDO; dispositions recorded.

## Security notes
The review verifies that the security-relevant design rules survived implementation, and treats each failure as a blocker: environment disclosure present on every order-capable panel, in every floating window title and window chrome, and preserved when a panel is maximised; RBAC-hidden controls genuinely accompanied by server-side enforcement (spot-checked by attempting a hidden action's API call with QA/Security); untrusted strings from imported workspaces rendered as capped text with no markup interpretation - verified with a crafted fixture containing markup and an overlong name; exports verified to contain no credentials, account ids or environment binding by inspecting an actual exported file; and "Copy panel link" verified to produce a link without account ids or tokens. Any failure here is escalated to the Security engineer as well as filed.

## Accessibility notes
This review executes the verification half of E15-D15. axe-core must be clean on every touched screen; the manual pass covers the five-task scenario (build a 2x2 layout, bind symbols, join a sync group, save, reopen) with NVDA and one VoiceOver spot-check. Focus destinations after every layout mutation are checked against the focus-model table. Announcement text is transcribed and diffed against the script. Target sizes are measured on splitters and panel controls. Contrast is measured in the running build over real panel content, including a dense footprint, rather than over the design's placeholder backgrounds. A pointer-only operation is a blocker that cannot be accepted.

## Performance notes
While formal benchmarking belongs to engineering, this review verifies the design-side constraints that protect the budgets and files failures: focusing a panel must not resize its canvas (observed as a visible reflow or a frame stall), drag previews must not carry live content, drop must commit one layout change, preset application must reuse panel instances rather than remounting, and no animation may change a content box. Anything that visibly stutters during a docking interaction on the reference machine is filed with a recording, since that is a user-visible failure of US-LAY-001's budget regardless of what a benchmark says.

## Observability
The review confirms that the analytics events from the E15-D16 table actually fire with the specified properties - particularly `layout.panel_moved{method}`, `layout.preset_applied{entry}` and `workspace.restore_completed{ms,paneCount,failedPanes}` - since these are the measurements that will tell the team whether E15's design assumptions were right. A missing required event is a major finding.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All fourteen screens reviewed against their spec pages with paired-screenshot evidence.
- [ ] Full state walk completed in the real build; unreachable states filed.
- [ ] Density x theme x zoom matrix swept at both reference widths.
- [ ] Interaction fidelity verified in Electron and browser builds, pointer and keyboard.
- [ ] axe-core clean on every touched screen; manual screen-reader pass completed with transcripts.
- [ ] Announcement strings diffed against the E15-D15 script.
- [ ] Token compliance audit complete; hard-coded values filed.
- [ ] Motion and reduced-motion verified against E15-D14.
- [ ] Copy diffed against the E15-D16 copy deck.
- [ ] Security spot-checks completed (env disclosure, RBAC enforcement, untrusted strings, export contents, panel link).
- [ ] Required analytics events verified as firing with correct properties.
- [ ] Findings register complete with severity, evidence and disposition; all blockers fixed in-epic, majors fixed or filed with a priority.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e15-design-qa-report.md` merged.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded (Status = Done)** - this sign-off is a DoD input for the consuming US-LAY stories and for the E15 epic itself.

## Dependencies
- **E15-D16** - the handoff pack, including the design-QA checklist published in advance.
- E15 engineering stories implementing US-LAY-001..008 being feature-complete enough to review in Sprint 09.
- A build of both the Electron shell and the browser target.

`design/e15-design-qa`

title: Playwright E2E suite for dock, workspace save/restore and preset gallery
body:
## Context
The layout surface is the one place in CandleViewer where a regression is both easy to introduce (any epic adding a panel type touches the dock registry) and easy to miss (it looks fine until you restore a saved workspace). `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` puts Playwright E2E — web *and* Electron — at the top of the pyramid precisely for journeys like this, and the R1 exit criteria require the charting alpha to survive a restart with its workspace intact.

`E15-Q01` writes the plan; this ticket automates the parts of it that are deterministic and high-value, so that every PR touching `web/` or the dock package gets an honest answer about whether a 4-pane workspace still saves and restores.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New spec files under `e2e/specs/layouts/`:
  - `dock-grid.spec.ts` — apply presets 1×1, 2×1, 2×2, 1+3 from `SCR-022`; drag a pane divider and assert persisted sizes; add a panel from `SCR-024`; remove and undo; assert the `>16 panels` warning path.
  - `dock-drag-drop.spec.ts` — drag a panel to each of the N/S/E/W/centre drop zones of `SCR-021` and assert the resulting tree; assert the invalid-drop affordance; assert the keyboard equivalent via CMP-216 PanelMenu "Move panel".
  - `workspace-persistence.spec.ts` — save (`Ctrl+S`), save-as (`Ctrl+Shift+S`), reload the page, assert full restore including pane sizes and scroll position; assert the unsaved-changes `*` marker and the `SCR-029` navigation prompt.
  - `workspace-crud.spec.ts` — create/rename/duplicate/delete through `SCR-025`; assert last-workspace-cannot-be-deleted and the type-the-name delete confirmation.
  - `layout-hotkeys.spec.ts` — `Ctrl+1..9` preset slots, `Ctrl+Tab` pane focus with a visible focus ring, `F6` region cycling, `F11` full-screen panel, `Ctrl+Alt+←/→` panel cycling.
  - `workspace-restore-edge.spec.ts` — delisted-symbol pane error state; crash-restore banner ("Restored your layout from 14:02"); stale-write 412 dialog with [Keep mine] / [Load theirs].
- An Electron-runner variant of `dock-drag-drop` and `workspace-persistence` covering `SCR-027` floating windows (float → move → re-dock → restart → position restored).
- Test-data helpers: `seedWorkspace(fixtureName)` hitting `POST /api/v1/workspaces` + `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/layouts` so specs start from a known tree instead of clicking one together.
- Stable selectors: `data-testid` on CMP-080 DockPanel, CMP-081 DockGrid, CMP-082 PanelHeader, CMP-214 DockDropZone, CMP-217 LayoutPresetMenu, CMP-218 SyncMenu — added as part of this ticket where missing.
- CI wiring: suite runs on PRs touching `web/**` and nightly in full (web + Electron), with traces and video on failure.

## Out of scope
- Sync-group behavioural assertions — `E15-Q03`.
- FPS/latency measurement — `E15-Q04` (Playwright is not a profiler; specs assert behaviour, not frame time).
- axe-core full audit — `E15-Q06` (specs here run axe only as a smoke check on `SCR-020`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A 4-pane workspace survives a reload
  Given a seeded 2x2 workspace with chart, footprint, DOM and tape panes
  When the spec saves it, reloads the page and waits for interactive
  Then all four panes are present in the same slots with the same sizes, symbols and intervals

Scenario: Keyboard docking is automated, not just documented
  When the spec opens the panel menu with Shift+F10 and chooses Move panel then Bottom
  Then the panel lands in the bottom region and a live region announces the move
  And the spec asserts the announcement text, not only the DOM position

Scenario: Failure case - stale save is refused
  Given two browser contexts have the same workspace open and context A has saved
  When context B saves with its stale ETag
  Then the API returns 412 and the spec asserts the conflict dialog appears with both resolution actions
  And choosing [Load theirs] replaces the local tree with A's version

Scenario: Edge case - delisted symbol
  Given a seeded workspace whose second pane references a delisted symbol
  When it is restored
  Then that pane shows an error state naming the symbol and the other three panes are interactive

Scenario: Flake gate
  Given the suite is run 20 times consecutively in CI
  Then it passes at least 20 of 20 times, or the offending spec is quarantined with a linked bug before merge
```

## Technical notes / design
- Drag-and-drop in Playwright is notoriously flaky: use `page.mouse` with explicit intermediate moves and wait on the drop-zone highlight state (CMP-214) rather than fixed sleeps; prefer asserting the committed tree via the app's exposed layout snapshot hook over pixel geometry.
- Assert the *serialized* dock tree (a stable JSON shape) for structural cases and reserve geometric assertions for splitter sizing, so refactors of the renderer do not churn the suite.
- Reuse the `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.1 slot model (`layout_panes.slot_index`) as the vocabulary for assertions so specs read the same way as the API examples in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Electron specs run against the packaged dev build via `_electron.launch`; floating-window assertions use the second `BrowserWindow` handle.

## Test plan
- Self-verifying: the deliverable is tests. Verification is (a) mutation-style sanity — deliberately break pane-size persistence locally and confirm `workspace-persistence.spec.ts` fails; (b) the 20-run flake gate; (c) a review that every spec maps to an `E15-TC-*` id from `E15-Q01`.

## Security notes
- Specs authenticate through the real auth flow with seeded non-privileged users; no test bypasses RBAC or injects tokens directly, so an accidental authorization regression surfaces here too.
- A spec asserts that a `viewer` role can open a workspace but cannot mutate a shared/published layout, and that the API refuses with 403 rather than the UI merely hiding the control.
- Fixture teardown deletes seeded workspaces so CI state never accumulates user data.

## Accessibility notes
- Every drag case has a keyboard twin; the suite fails if a layout operation exists with no keyboard path (CMP-214 mandates this).
- Focus assertions: after preset apply, focus lands on the first pane; after panel close, focus moves to a sane sibling, never to `body`.
- An axe-core smoke check runs on `SCR-020` in the default and 16-pane states; serious/critical violations fail the spec.

## Performance notes
- Specs assert coarse timing guards only (restore to interactive ≤3 s warm, preset apply ≤300 ms) using the app's own performance marks; the fine-grained budgets are `E15-Q04`'s job.
- Suite wall-clock target ≤8 minutes sharded on CI so it can stay on the PR gate rather than being demoted to nightly.

## Observability
- Specs subscribe to the dev analytics sink and assert the documented events fire on the modelled actions (`workspace.saved`, `panel.added`, `layout.panel_moved`, `layout.preset_applied`, `layout.reset`).
- On failure, traces, video, the serialized dock tree and the last 50 analytics events are attached to the CI artefact bundle to make triage a read rather than a re-run.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All listed specs merged and green on web and Electron runners.
- [ ] `data-testid` hooks added to the named components and documented in `15-component-catalogue.md` notes.
- [ ] Suite wired to the PR gate for `web/**` and to the nightly full run.
- [ ] 20-run flake gate passed; any quarantine has a linked bug.
- [ ] Coverage mapping from each spec to `E15-TC-*` ids recorded in the plan from `E15-Q01`.

## Dependencies
- `E15-Q01` for the case ids; `E15-S01`, `E15-S02`, `E15-S05`, `E15-S06` for the surfaces; E10 for the Electron shell harness.

## Branch
`chore/e15-e2e-layouts`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (E2E tier, flake policy)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-020, SCR-021, SCR-022, SCR-024, SCR-025, SCR-027, SCR-029
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/layouts` (If-Match, 412)
