title: Abuse cases: malicious workspace import, cross-user access and layout DoS
body: ## Context `E15-X01` enumerates the threats; this ticket tries to make them real. The highest-value target is the workspace import path (US-LAY-007, `SCR-026`): a file authored by one user, handed to another, parsed and turned into application state. Second is the authorization boundary — `workspaces:*` is scoped `self`, and the only way to know the scope is enforced is to attack it as another user. Third is resource abuse: an unbounded layout document or a write-storm is a cheap self-hosted DoS. These are adversarial tests, deliberately separate from `E15-Q01`'s functional negatives: QA asks "does the error message appear?", this ticket asks "can I make the app do something it should refuse?". ## Scope / Deliverables - Abuse-case suite `security/abuse/e15/` with automated cases where possible and a manual playbook where not, covering each `SR-E15-nn`: - **Malicious import corpus**: unknown pane kinds; `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` keys (prototype pollution); deeply nested trees (1000 levels); 100k panes; 50 MB file; NaN/Infinity/huge numbers in grid coordinates; duplicate `slot_index`; negative and fractional sizes; strings of 1 MB in names; null bytes; invalid UTF-8. - **Injection through names**: workspace/layout/pane names containing ``, `javascript:` URLs, RTL-override and zero-width characters, and template-ish `{{7*7}}` payloads — asserted safe at every sink: tab label, panel header (CMP-082), panel menu (CMP-216), live-region announcement, Electron window title (`SCR-027`), export filename, and any log line. - **Id smuggling**: import a file asserting another user's `workspace_id`, `user_id`, `chart_template_id`, or an `account_id` binding; assert ids are regenerated and account bindings dropped with a report. - **Cross-user access**: user B calls `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{A's id}` and `/layouts/{A's id}`, including id-in-body vs id-in-path mismatch and a nested `layoutId` belonging to another workspace; expected 404 with no existence disclosure and no timing oracle. - **Privilege**: a viewer importing a workspace containing an owner-only panel type or a trading panel; assert server-side refusal, not UI hiding. - **Resource abuse**: creating workspaces/layouts/panes past the documented caps; a `PUT` write-storm beating the 2-second debounce; concurrent saves from 10 tabs; assert 429/422 with backoff and no unbounded growth in Postgres. - **Export leakage**: diff a full export against the `E15-X01` allow-list; grep for token-shaped, key-shaped and uuid-shaped values; assert no account id, user id, session material or API-key fragment appears. - **CSRF / clickjacking on layout mutations**: cross-origin `PUT` attempts and framing the workspace page. - A **findings report** with severity (CVSS-style rating per `04-security-program.md`), reproduction, and the fix ticket. ## Out of scope - Auth/session attacks (E09's abuse cases) beyond using them as the entry condition. - Network-level and infrastructure attacks (E43 pen-test). - Fuzzing the WS protocol (E17). ## Acceptance criteria ```gherkin Scenario: Malicious import is refused safely Given a layout file containing a __proto__ key and a 1000-level nested tree When it is imported Then the import is rejected with a stated reason, no object prototype is modified, the UI stays responsive, and the existing workspace is unchanged Scenario: Names cannot execute Given a workspace named with an XSS payload When it is rendered in the tab, panel header, panel menu, announcement and Electron window title Then the payload is displayed as inert text at every sink and no script executes Scenario: Failure case - cross-user access must not disclose existence Given user B requests user A's workspace id Then the response is 404 with a generic body, and the response time is not measurably different from a request for a non-existent id Scenario: Edge case - id smuggling is neutralised Given an import file asserting another user's chart_template_id and an account binding When it is imported Then new ids are generated, the account binding is dropped, and the user is shown a report listing exactly what was dropped Scenario: Resource caps hold Given an attempt to create panes beyond the documented cap or to PUT the layout 100 times per second Then the API responds 422 or 429 with backoff guidance, database growth stays bounded, and no save from a legitimate client is lost ``` ## Technical notes / design - Drive the import corpus at both layers: the UI (`SCR-026`, worker-parsed, so also check the worker does not become the unguarded path) and the API directly, since a UI-only guard is not a guard. - Prototype-pollution checks need a post-condition assertion on `Object.prototype` and on a canary object, not merely "no crash". - Timing-oracle testing for 404-vs-403 should use a statistical comparison over many samples rather than a single request pair. - Reuse the `E15-Q02` seeding helpers for multi-user setup so the abuse suite starts from a realistic, RBAC-correct baseline. - Where a finding is a missing bound rather than a bug, the fix is a documented cap in `22-api-openapi.yaml` plus a 422 — record it as a contract change, not a silent server tweak. ## Test plan - Run the full suite against a staging build before the `E15-X04` review and again on the release candidate. - Each finding gets a regression test in the appropriate suite so it cannot silently return; high-severity findings graduate into the PR gate. - Re-run the export-leakage diff whenever the export schema changes — it is the cheapest control for the most sensitive output. ## Security notes - Findings are triaged per `04-security-program.md`: Critical/High block the epic; Medium needs a fix or a dated accepted risk; Low may be deferred to E43 with a link. - The corpus itself is stored as test data with a README warning; it must never be shipped in a production bundle, and CI asserts it is excluded from the build output. - Anything found here that also applies to other user-authored documents (rules import `SCR-089`, chart templates) is escalated to those epics rather than fixed only locally. ## Accessibility notes - The rejection and dropped-elements reports are the user's only feedback in every attack-adjacent path; cases assert they are text, keyboard-reachable, announced, and name the offending key (`SCR-026`) without echoing raw attacker-controlled content unescaped. - Verify that an RTL-override or zero-width payload in a name cannot visually spoof another workspace's label in the switcher (CMP-073). ## Performance notes - Validation must fail fast: an oversized or deeply nested document is rejected within the `SCR-026` ≤500 ms worker budget rather than by exhausting memory; cases assert main-thread responsiveness during rejection. - The write-storm case asserts the API's rate limiting does not degrade the legitimate debounced path measured in `E15-Q04`. ## Observability - Every rejection must emit `layout.import_rejected{reason}` with a bounded reason enum, and repeated cross-user 404s from one principal must be visible in the ops dashboard as a probing signal with a documented alert threshold. - Cases assert that no attacker-controlled string is written raw into logs (log injection), and that log lines carry a correlation id. ## Definition of Done - [ ] Abuse suite merged with the full corpus and multi-user fixtures. - [ ] All `SR-E15-nn` requirements from `E15-X01` exercised by at least one case. - [ ] Findings report published; Critical/High fixed and verified; Medium fixed or Owner-accepted with a date. - [ ] Regression tests added for every finding; corpus excluded from production bundles (CI-enforced). - [ ] Results handed to `E15-X04` for the epic security review. ## Dependencies - `E15-X01` (requirements), `E15-S02` (persistence), `E15-S07` (export/import); `E15-Q02` seeding helpers; E09 for multi-user RBAC fixtures. ## Branch `chore/e15-abuse-cases` ## References - `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (severity, triage) - `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-007 - `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-026, SCR-027, SCR-020 - `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*` - title: SAST/DAST rules and CI security gates for the workspace document surface
body:
## Context
A threat model and a round of abuse testing protect the code as it is today. Automated rules protect it against next quarter's well-meaning change — the one that adds a convenient `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to a panel header, or relaxes the import schema to accept an extra field "just for now". `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA, secrets scanning and DAST (OWASP ZAP) in CI; this ticket makes those tools actually *know about* the E15 surface instead of running generic rules over it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Custom Semgrep rules** in `security/semgrep/e15/`:
  - Ban `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `innerHTML`, `outerHTML` and `document.write` anywhere in the layout/dock packages and in anything rendering workspace-derived names.
  - Flag any Electron `BrowserWindow` title, tooltip or menu label built from unescaped workspace/pane data.
  - Flag `JSON.parse` of imported files that is not immediately followed by the project's schema validator, and flag validator calls that pass `additionalProperties: true` or omit depth/size bounds.
  - Flag assignment of client-supplied `id`, `user_id`, `workspace_id`, `chart_template_id` or account fields on the import/create paths (the id-regeneration rule from `E15-X01`).
  - Flag workspace queries lacking a `user_id` predicate — the `scope: self` enforcement rule — in the backend workspace repository.
  - Flag new `/workspaces*` handlers missing an `x-rbac` annotation or a rate-limit decorator.
- **CodeQL** query pack additions for taint flow from the import/parse entry points to DOM and window-title sinks, run on the frontend and API code.
- **Bandit/pip-audit/npm audit/Trivy** wiring confirmed to cover the new packages; the schema-validation dependency pinned and watched.
- **Secret scanning**: a rule asserting that no fixture workspace/export file in the repo contains key-shaped, token-shaped or account-id-shaped values, plus a CI check that the `E15-X02` abuse corpus is excluded from production bundles.
- **DAST (OWASP ZAP)**: an authenticated scan profile for the `/workspaces*` endpoints and the workspace page, with the import endpoint included and a tuned false-positive baseline so the job is trusted rather than ignored.
- **Gate policy**: which findings fail the build (High+ SAST, any new secret, any DAST High) vs which open a ticket, documented in the security README so the gate is predictable.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the findings the rules surface (filed to owning stories).
- The broader org-wide SAST baseline (E03/E43) — this extends it.
- Runtime WAF/Tailscale network controls (infra).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A regression is caught by the rule, not by a person
  Given a PR that renders a workspace name with dangerouslySetInnerHTML
  When CI runs
  Then the Semgrep job fails, names the rule and the line, and links the E15 threat model entry

Scenario: Scope enforcement is machine-checked
  Given a new workspace query written without a user_id predicate
  When CI runs
  Then the rule fails the build with an explanation of the scope:self requirement

Scenario: Failure case - noisy rules are not allowed to ship
  Given a proposed rule that produces more than a documented false-positive rate on the current codebase
  Then it is tuned or downgraded to warning before merge, so the gate stays credible

Scenario: Edge case - DAST authenticates correctly
  Given the ZAP profile
  When the scan runs
  Then it is authenticated as a real seeded user, exercises the import endpoint, and its baseline is committed so new alerts are visible as a diff

Scenario: Fixtures leak nothing
  Given the repository's workspace fixtures and export samples
  When the secret-scanning rule runs
  Then no key-shaped, token-shaped or account-id-shaped value is present
```

## Technical notes / design
- Rules are written against the real code paths and validated by running them over both the current codebase (expect zero findings after fixes) and the `E15-X02` corpus and a set of deliberately-vulnerable snippets (expect a finding each) — a rule with no proven true-positive is decoration.
- Prefer narrow, high-signal rules scoped by path over broad bans that teams learn to suppress; every suppression must carry a reason comment, and CI rejects bare suppressions.
- The DAST baseline must be committed and reviewed; an un-baselined ZAP job is a job everyone ignores within two sprints.
- Keep the CI wall-clock impact bounded: run the full pack nightly and the fast subset on PRs, following the E03 CI conventions.

## Test plan
- Rule unit tests: each Semgrep rule ships with a passing and a failing fixture in the standard Semgrep test format, run in CI.
- Validate the CodeQL taint queries against a deliberately introduced sink and confirm the alert appears in the PR.
- Run the ZAP profile against staging, triage every alert once, and record the baseline; re-run after the `E15-X02` fixes land.

## Security notes
- These gates implement `SR-E15-nn` requirements from `E15-X01` as enforceable controls; the mapping rule → requirement is recorded in the rules README.
- Gate policy must be explicit about what blocks a release versus what files a ticket, so a security finding is never quietly bypassed under sprint pressure.
- Scanning artefacts (SARIF, ZAP reports) are retained per the security program's evidence retention rules and are inputs to the E43 pen-test scoping.

## Accessibility notes
- One rule targets an a11y-adjacent security control: any code path that renders an error or rejection message must route through the app's announced-message helper, so security feedback cannot regress into a silent or visual-only state.
- CI reporting itself is plain text/SARIF, readable without colour, so a colour-blind reviewer can triage from the log.

## Performance notes
- PR-gate subset target ≤3 minutes; full pack nightly ≤20 minutes. If the DAST scan exceeds its window it is moved to nightly-only rather than being allowed to slow every PR into irrelevance.
- Rules must not require building the app; they run on source, keeping the gate cheap.

## Observability
- All findings publish SARIF to the code-scanning dashboard with the E15 rule ids, so trend and MTTR per rule are measurable.
- A weekly report of suppressions added is generated, because suppression growth is the leading indicator of a gate losing its meaning.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Semgrep rule pack merged with passing/failing fixtures and a rule → `SR-E15-nn` mapping.
- [ ] CodeQL taint queries merged and demonstrated to catch a seeded sink.
- [ ] ZAP authenticated profile and committed baseline in place; nightly job green.
- [ ] Secret-scanning rule for fixtures and the bundle-exclusion check enforced in CI.
- [ ] Gate policy documented; zero outstanding High findings on the E15 packages.

## Dependencies
- `E15-X01` (requirements), `E15-S07` (import/export code to scan); E03 CI pipeline; E09 seeded users for authenticated DAST.

## Branch
`chore/e15-sast-dast-rules`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (SAST/SCA/DAST tooling and gates)
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (required checks)
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/workspaces*` (`x-rbac` annotations)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-026, SCR-027

**Branch & PR**

**Done means**

- [ ] CodeQL taint queries merged and demonstrated to catch a seeded sink.
- [ ] ZAP authenticated profile and committed baseline in place; nightly job green.
- [ ] Secret-scanning rule for fixtures and the bundle-exclusion check enforced in CI.
- [ ] Gate policy documented; zero outstanding High findings on the E15 packages.

**Do NOT**

title: Security review and sign-off for E15 layouts, workspaces and sharing
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, for any epic labelled `security`, that the STRIDE model be finalised, findings triaged (fixed or accepted with Owner sign-off) and a sign-off comment recorded by the Security engineer before the epic is Done. E15 earns that label on one fact: it is the first epic that lets a document authored by one user be executed as configuration by another.

This ticket closes the loop — a white-box review of the implemented code against the model, verification that every finding is genuinely resolved rather than merely closed, and a written sign-off that the `E15-Q08` QA gate and the R1 exit review can cite.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box code review** of the layout/dock package, the workspace API handlers and the export/import path, against the `SR-E15-nn` requirements:
  - Input validation: strict schema, `additionalProperties: false`, depth/size/count bounds, numeric ranges, and validation performed server-side as well as in the import worker.
  - Id regeneration on import; no client-asserted `id`, `user_id`, `workspace_id`, `chart_template_id` or account binding is ever honoured.
  - Authorization: every `/workspaces*` handler enforces `workspaces:read`/`workspaces:write` with `scope: self` at the query level; nested `layoutId` is verified to belong to the caller's workspace; non-existent and not-owned both return 404.
  - Output encoding at every sink that renders user-authored names: tabs, CMP-082 PanelHeader, CMP-216 PanelMenu, CMP-073 WorkspaceSwitcher, live regions, Electron window titles, export filenames, logs.
  - Export allow-list implemented as an allow-list (not a deny-list), with a test asserting a newly added field is excluded by default.
  - Rate limiting and caps on workspace/layout/pane creation and on the debounced `PUT`.
  - Audit vs analytics split: `workspace.deleted` / `workspace.exported` reach the audit log; layout arrangement events stay analytics-only by design.
- **Verification pass**: independently re-test each Critical/High finding from `E15-X02` on the release candidate rather than trusting the closed state.
- **Findings disposition table**: every threat from `E15-X01` → mitigation → evidence (code ref, test id, scan result) → status (fixed / accepted / not-applicable with reason).
- **Sign-off note** `docs/security/signoff/e15.md` bound to a commit sha, with the Security engineer's name and date, plus Owner sign-off on any accepted risk.
- **Handover to E43**: a short list of E15 surfaces the pen-test should probe before Live enablement (import path, cross-user access, export contents).

## Out of scope
- New feature work or refactoring (findings are filed as fixes to owning stories).
- The pen-test itself (E43).
- Signing off other epics' sharing surfaces (rules `SCR-089`, chart templates) beyond noting shared risk.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every modelled threat has a disposition
  Given the E15-X01 threat list
  Then the disposition table accounts for 100% of entries with evidence, and no entry is left blank or "TBD"

Scenario: Fixes are verified, not assumed
  Given a Critical finding marked fixed in E15-X02
  When the reviewer independently re-tests it on the release candidate
  Then the exploit fails, and the verification is recorded with the commit sha

Scenario: Failure case - an unresolved High blocks sign-off
  Given a High-severity finding with no fix and no Owner-accepted risk
  Then sign-off is withheld and the E15 epic cannot reach Done

Scenario: Edge case - a control exists only client-side
  Given import validation implemented solely in the browser worker
  When the reviewer replays the import payload directly against the API
  Then the gap is raised as a finding and must be closed server-side before sign-off

Scenario: Sign-off is citable
  When the sign-off note is published
  Then it names the commit sha, the reviewer, the date, the accepted risks with review dates, and is linked from E15-Q08 and the R1 exit checklist
```

## Technical notes / design
- Review by requirement, not by file: walk each `SR-E15-nn` and demand the code and the test that satisfy it, which makes "we probably handle that" impossible to pass off.
- The single most important structural check is that validation and authorization live on the server: the browser worker is a UX nicety, and the reviewer must replay payloads directly at the API to prove it.
- Prefer allow-lists in two places — exported fields and accepted pane kinds — and assert the default-deny property with a test that adds a synthetic field/kind and expects exclusion.
- Record inherited assumptions from E09 and E17 explicitly, so a future change to session or transport triggers a re-review of this sign-off rather than silently invalidating it.

## Test plan
- Re-run the `E15-X02` abuse suite and the `E15-X03` scans on the release candidate; attach results.
- Perform a manual replay of the three highest-value attacks (malicious import at the API, cross-user layout access, export leakage diff) independently of the automated suite.
- Confirm each regression test added for a finding actually fails when the fix is reverted locally.

## Security notes
- This is the epic's security gate; no exceptions are granted verbally — accepted risks require the Owner's written acceptance and a dated review, per `04-security-program.md`.
- The sign-off must state the data classification conclusion: workspace exports are user-confidential and must not be treated as shareable-by-default in any future collaboration feature (a direct input to R5 collaboration work).
- Any finding with cross-epic reach (rules import, chart templates, future sharing) is escalated with a ticket in the owning epic before sign-off, not after.

## Accessibility notes
- The reviewer verifies that every security-relevant message (rejection, dropped-elements report, version mismatch, permission refusal) is perceivable: text, keyboard-reachable, announced, and adequately contrasted — a security control that only a sighted mouse user can perceive is an incomplete control.
- The DEMO/LIVE indicator's integrity in floating windows is re-checked as an anti-spoofing control.

## Performance notes
- Confirms that the added validation and rate limiting do not breach the `E15-Q04` budgets: import validation within the ≤500 ms worker budget, and the debounced save path unaffected at the legitimate 2-second cadence.
- Confirms that rejection paths fail fast and bounded, so a hostile document cannot consume the frame budget of a live trading workspace.

## Observability
- Verifies that audit entries for `workspace.deleted` and `workspace.exported` are written append-only and are queryable, and that `layout.import_rejected{reason}` uses a bounded enum.
- Verifies the probing alert (repeated cross-user 404s / repeated import rejections) exists in the ops dashboard with a documented threshold and owner.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] White-box review completed against every `SR-E15-nn` requirement with evidence recorded.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings verified fixed on the RC; Medium fixed or Owner-accepted with a date.
- [ ] Disposition table complete with no blank entries.
- [ ] `docs/security/signoff/e15.md` published, bound to a commit sha, signed by the Security engineer, with Owner signatures on accepted risks.
- [ ] Pen-test handover list delivered to E43; sign-off linked from `E15-Q08` and the R1 exit checklist.

## Dependencies
- `E15-X01` (model), `E15-X02` (abuse findings), `E15-X03` (scan gates); a release-candidate build of the E15 stories.

## Branch
`chore/e15-security-review`

- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-LAY-007

title: Design QA of the built recorder screens against spec
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec by a designer, and discrepancies are fixed or filed as bugs with a priority. E16 ships three net-new admin screens plus two empty-state patterns.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Side-by-side comparison of the implemented SCR-140, SCR-141, SCR-142, SCR-047 and SCR-151 (and CMP-177 in Storybook) against the Figma spec: spacing, type scale, colour tokens, iconography, state coverage, empty/loading/error states, motion timing, reduced-motion behaviour.
- Verification that every documented state is reachable in the running app (including disk warning, disk critical, purge-in-progress, degraded, and empty), using seeded/forced states rather than waiting for real conditions.
- A defect list with severity, each either fixed in-sprint or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*` label and linked here.
- Sign-off comment recording pass/fail per screen.

## Out of scope
- Functional/black-box testing (E16-Q01/Q02) and the a11y audit (E16-Q05) — overlapping findings are cross-linked, not duplicated.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every documented state is demonstrated
  Given the state matrix from the handoff package
  When design QA runs
  Then each state is shown in the running app and marked pass or fail with evidence

Scenario: Token drift is caught
  Given a developer used a raw colour value instead of a token
  When the built screen is inspected
  Then the discrepancy is recorded and either fixed or filed as a Bug

Scenario: Reduced motion honoured
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is enabled
  Then the disk meter and progress indicators do not animate
```

## Technical notes / design
Force states via the dev fixture seed (`seeds/dev/*`, guarded by `CV_ENV=dev`) and by a test-only override of `StorageUsage` sampling so 80 %/95 % disk states can be shown without filling a disk. Storybook is the authority for CMP-177 states.

## Test plan
Manual comparison pass with screenshots attached; Storybook visual check for CMP-177's four states.

## Security notes
Design QA runs against staging (demo) only, never live, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8.

## Accessibility notes
Focus visibility and contrast are re-checked here as a visual concern; the formal audit is E16-Q05.

## Performance notes
Confirm tabular figures are used and the table does not reflow under 1 Hz updates.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Pass/fail per screen recorded with screenshots.
- [ ] All discrepancies fixed or filed with a priority and linked.
- [ ] Designer sign-off comment posted on each consuming story.

## Dependencies
E16-D06 supplies the spec/state matrix; E16-S05 is the last UI story to land.

## Branch
`design/e16-design-qa` (notes/issues only).

title: Surface recording status and auto-record triggers across chart and watchlist
body:
## Context
Implements the user-facing half of **US-REC-002** (auto-record triggers) and the recording-status element of **US-REC-006** outside the admin screen. ADR-0015 names the risk directly: auto-recording on chart open surprises a user who browses many symbols, and the mitigation is "a visible recording indicator and a one-click stop" wherever the trigger happens - not buried on `/admin/recorder`.

Per the traceability matrix, US-REC-002 touches **SCR-041** (in-chart symbol/interval quick-switcher) and **SCR-100** (watchlist panel) as well as SCR-140; US-REC-006 touches **SCR-103** (symbol info / instrument detail), whose spec requires "recording status with a link to SCR-140 (owner)".

## Scope / Deliverables
- A shared `useRecordingStatus(symbol)` hook reading the WS `recorder` topic (one subscription per app, fanned out) so every surface shows the same state without N subscriptions.
- **SCR-041** quick-switcher: a compact recording dot per symbol row (recording / auto-recorded / not recorded) with a tooltip stating the reason and, for owners, a stop action.
- **SCR-100** watchlist (CMP-161/CMP-162 rows): the same indicator, plus an EmptyState (CMP-026) variant when no watchlist symbol is recorded that explains history will not exist for these symbols until recording starts.
- **SCR-103** symbol info: a recording-status block - state, first-recorded timestamp, size on disk, retention/pin - with a link to SCR-140 for owners and an explanatory sentence for Manager/Viewer.
- A non-modal, dismissible first-time notice when auto-record starts a symbol because a chart was opened: names the symbol, the trigger, the 60 s delay that already elapsed, and offers stop; shown at most once per session per symbol, never as a blocking dialog.
- Copy is taken verbatim from the signed-off design (E16-D05) - no ad-hoc strings.

## Out of scope
- Changing auto-record behaviour itself (E16-T02).
- The admin screen (E16-S01) and the chart empty states (E16-S05).
- Redesigning SCR-041/SCR-100/SCR-103 beyond adding these elements.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Auto-record is announced where it happens
  Given SOLUSDT is not recorded and the owner opens a chart for it
  When auto-record starts after the configured delay
  Then a dismissible notice names SOLUSDT, states that it started because a chart is open, and offers a one-click stop
  And the same notice is not shown again for SOLUSDT in this session

Scenario: Indicator agrees everywhere
  Given BTCUSDT is recording manually
  Then the quick-switcher, the watchlist row and the symbol-info block all show recording with reason manual, sourced from one subscription

Scenario: Non-owner sees status without controls
  Given a Viewer session
  Then the recording status is visible and the stop control is absent, replaced by a sentence stating that recording is managed by the owner

Scenario: Watchlist of unrecorded symbols explains the consequence
  Given no watchlist symbol is recorded
  Then the panel shows the recording-not-started empty-state variant explaining that no history will exist for these symbols until recording begins

Scenario: Indicator is never colour-only
  When the recording indicator renders in any surface
  Then it carries accessible text or an accessible name stating the state, not merely a coloured dot
```

## Technical notes / design
- One app-level subscription to the `recorder` topic with all effective symbols; the hook selects by symbol from a context store so adding a fourth surface later costs nothing.
- The first-time notice is keyed `recorder.autostart.notice.<symbol>` in session storage; it is a toast-class element using the design-system notification primitive, never a modal, because it fires while the user is reading a chart.
- If the WS topic is unavailable, surfaces show an explicit unknown state rather than defaulting to "not recording" - showing "not recording" when we do not know is the same class of lie the epic is built to avoid.

## Test plan
- Unit: hook fan-out with one subscription and three consumers; indicator state mapping for all seven `recording_state` values plus unknown; once-per-session notice logic.
- Storybook: indicator in all states within each host component; the watchlist empty variant.
- E2E (in E16-Q02): open a chart for an unrecorded symbol with a shortened autostart delay, assert the notice and that stop works from the notice.
- a11y: axe-core on each host surface; screen-reader check that the indicator has an accessible name.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Recording state is not sensitive, but the stop control must be permission-gated client-side and enforced server-side (`recording:write`). The notice must not appear for roles that cannot act on it - a Viewer gets no stop affordance. Classification **internal**.

## Accessibility notes
Indicator state is conveyed by accessible name plus shape/text, never colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The auto-start notice is `role="status"` (polite) not `role="alert"` - it must not interrupt, and it must be reachable and dismissible by keyboard. Tooltips have keyboard-accessible equivalents; the symbol-info block is plain text so it is fully readable by a screen reader.

## Performance notes
One WS subscription regardless of surface count; indicator re-render budget under 1 ms per row; the watchlist must not re-render wholesale on each 1 Hz frame (per-row memoisation keyed on state string).

## Observability
Analytics `recorder.autostart_notice_shown {symbol, trigger}` and `recorder.autostart_notice_stopped {symbol}` - a high stop rate is the signal that the delay or the trigger policy needs revisiting.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios automated.
- [ ] Storybook states added for each host component.
- [ ] axe-core green on all three surfaces.
- [ ] Copy matches the signed-off E16-D05 strings exactly.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%.
- [ ] 2 approvals including frontend code-owner.

## Dependencies
`E16-S01` establishes the recorder data hooks and permission handling reused here; `E16-D05` supplies the indicator and notice designs and copy.

title: Add recorder dashboards, alert rules and the recorder ops runbook
body:
## Context
US-REC-008's NFR states the specific failure this whole epic guards against: "silently stopped" recording. A recorder that stops without anyone noticing produces exactly the outcome ADR-0015 was written to prevent - a hole in history discovered months later when a profile or replay needs it. Metrics existing is not the same as someone being told; this task turns the metrics from T02/T03/T04/T06/T07 into dashboards, alert rules and a runbook.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Grafana dashboard `recorder` (provisioned as code in `ops/grafana/dashboards/recorder.json`): per-symbol ingest rate, lag, rows/hour, dropped messages, write backlog, spill bytes, disk used ratio with the 80/90/95 thresholds drawn, projected full date, gap count by cause, retention last-success age, roll-off watermark lag.
- Prometheus alert rules in `ops/prometheus/rules/recorder.yml`:
  - `RecorderSilentStop` - a symbol in state `recording` with zero writes for 60 s while the market is active -> **critical**, names the symbol (US-REC-008 scenario 3).
  - `RecorderMessagesDropped` - any increase in `recorder_rows_dropped_total` -> critical.
  - `RecorderSpilling` - `recorder_spill_bytes > 0` for 5 min -> warning.
  - `DiskWarn` / `DiskCritical` at `CV_DISK_WARN_PCT` / `CV_DISK_HALT_PCT` -> warning / critical.
  - `RetentionStale` - `retention_last_success_timestamp` older than 48 h -> warning.
  - `RollOffWatermarkLag` - watermark lag > hot window + 2 days -> warning.
  - `RecorderGapBurst` - more than 5 gaps in an hour for one symbol -> warning.
- Runbook `docs/ops/runbooks/recorder.md`: one section per alert with symptom, first three checks, remediation, and what NOT to do (never delete gap rows; never clear the WAL without recording a gap).
- "Market active" definition for the silent-stop rule: the shared public WS connection has received any message for any symbol in the last 10 s - so a venue-wide outage pages once, not per symbol.

## Out of scope
- Notification delivery channels (E40 alerts epic) - these rules fire into the existing E04 observability baseline.
- Application metric instrumentation itself (shipped by T02/T03/T04/T06/T07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Silent stop pages within 90 seconds
  Given BTCUSDT is in state recording and its writer is suspended while other symbols keep writing
  When 60 seconds pass
  Then RecorderSilentStop fires as critical and the alert annotation names BTCUSDT

Scenario: Venue outage does not fan out
  Given the public WS connection receives nothing for any symbol
  When the silent-stop rule is evaluated
  Then it does not fire per symbol; the connection-level alert fires once

Scenario: Every alert has a runbook
  When the alert rules file is linted
  Then every rule has a runbook_url annotation resolving to a section that exists in docs/ops/runbooks/recorder.md

Scenario: Dashboard provisions from code
  Given a clean Grafana instance
  When provisioning runs
  Then the recorder dashboard appears with every listed panel populated from live metrics
```

## Technical notes / design
- Alert rules are unit-tested with `promtool test rules` using recorded metric series fixtures - an alert rule with no test is an alert rule that fires at 3 a.m. for the wrong reason.
- Thresholds are templated from the same config keys the application uses so a change to `CV_DISK_HALT_PCT` does not silently desynchronise the alert from the behaviour.
- Dashboard panels use the exact metric names shipped by T03/T07 (`recorder_rows_total`, `recorder_bytes_written_total`, `recorder_spill_bytes`, `disk_used_ratio`, `recorder_gaps_total`, `retention_last_success_timestamp`, `recorder_watermark_lag_days`).

## Test plan
- `promtool test rules` fixtures for each of the seven rules, including the venue-outage negative case.
- Provisioning smoke test in CI: spin Grafana, provision, assert the dashboard exists and every panel query parses.
- Manual: trigger a real silent stop in the staging environment and record the time to alert in the ticket.

## Security notes
Dashboards must not expose host absolute paths or symbol-level data to unauthenticated viewers; Grafana sits behind the same Tailscale-only boundary as the app. Alert annotations must not embed credentials or full file paths. SR-125 requires the disk high-watermark metric to be exported and alerted on - this ticket is its implementation for E16.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - operational dashboards, not product UI. Panel titles still carry units so figures are unambiguous.

## Performance notes
Scrape interval 15 s; the recorder job adds fewer than 200 series per symbol; cardinality is bounded by `CV_RECORDER_MAX_SYMBOLS`.

## Observability
This ticket *is* observability. It additionally adds a synthetic `recorder_up` gauge so absence of the exporter itself is alertable.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Dashboard and rules merged as code and provisioned in staging.
- [ ] `promtool` rule tests green in CI.
- [ ] Runbook sections exist for all seven alerts and are linked from each rule.
- [ ] Time-to-alert for a real induced silent stop recorded in the ticket.
- [ ] 1 DevSecOps approval plus backend code-owner.

## Dependencies
`E16-T07` and `E16-T08` must have shipped the metrics and status surface these panels read.

## Branch
`chore/e16-recorder-observability`.

title: Write and run the k6 WS load profile and record the section 16.3 budgets
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 sets an R1 load gate: "k6: 5 concurrent WS clients x 10 symbols sustained 1 h, backend fan-out add-on at most 20 ms p95." `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.4 sets a heavier one: "8 connections x 40 symbols x full workspace for 1 h", asserting the section 16.3 budgets with **zero resyncs from backpressure**.

Until this runs, the budgets in section 16.3 are engineering estimates - open item W1 - and E17-T07 cannot close the freeze honestly. It is also the ticket that resolves **W5** (per-topic coalescing thresholds under the `saturated` class, explicitly assigned to "Load test in Sprint 05").

## Scope / Deliverables
- **k6 scripts** in `tests/load/ws/` driving the client protocol (`hello`/`auth`/`sub`, heartbeats, honouring `effective` options) against a staging backend fed by **recorded Bybit fixtures**, never live Bybit (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 7.3 - deterministic and no rate-limit consumption).
- **Profile A (roadmap gate)**: 5 concurrent WS clients x 10 symbols, sustained 1 h. Assert fan-out add-on at most 20 ms p95 (budget #6) and WS tick to screen p95 under 100 ms (budget #3) via the correlated spans E17-T06 emits.
- **Profile B (protocol gate)**: 8 connections x 40 symbols x the full reference workspace, 1 h. Assert every section 16.3 budget: bandwidth under 350 KiB/s per reference workspace, full re-snapshot under 700 KiB and under 400 ms, resyncs from `upstream_desync` under 1 per hour per topic, and **zero** resyncs attributable to backpressure.
- **Profile C (capacity driver)**: the 20-concurrent-pane-subscription shape of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 10.1 (5 users x 4 panes), to confirm the multiplicative fan-out load the capacity plan is sized for.
- **W5 resolution**: instrument per-topic coalescing cost under the `saturated` class and recommend either keeping the fixed multipliers (x2 / x4) or moving to per-topic adaptive values; record the recommendation for E17-T07.
- **Regression baseline** committed so future runs compare rather than merely pass, with a 10% regression threshold consistent with the engine benchmark policy.
- **Results** written into `docs/qa/test-plans/e17-ws-protocol.md` and fed to E17-T07 for the section 16.3 restatement.

## Out of scope
- Chart-engine frame benchmarks (E11) and the composite full-capacity 2 h scenario (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 9's final row, run at R1 exit as a release activity, not here).
- REST endpoint load (E02/E09).
- Chaos (E17-Q02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The roadmap load gate passes
  Given profile A runs for one hour
  Then backend fan-out add-on is at most 20 ms p95 and WS tick to screen is under 100 ms p95

Scenario: The protocol load gate passes
  Given profile B runs for one hour
  Then every section 16.3 budget is met and zero resyncs are attributable to backpressure

Scenario: A budget miss fails the run
  Given bandwidth exceeds 1 MiB per second for the reference workspace
  Then the run fails with the offending metric named, rather than reporting a soft warning

Scenario: W5 is answered with data
  Then the report states the measured per-topic cost under the saturated class and recommends fixed or adaptive multipliers

Scenario: Results are reproducible
  Given a second run on the same staging profile
  Then headline numbers are within 15 percent, or the variance source is identified
```

## Technical notes / design
The k6 client must be a faithful protocol client, not a socket that ignores what it receives: it decodes binary frames (so decode cost is counted), tracks sequences (so a gap fails the run rather than passing unnoticed), and replies to `ping`. A load client that silently drops frames measures the wrong system.

Staging is provisioned per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 10.2 target sizing - the **VPS-class profile** (4 vCPU / 8 GB), not the dev workstation, because all backend budgets are set to be met on the smaller profile.

Budget #3 is measured through the correlated span (backend receipt to frontend paint mark); for k6 the "paint" end is approximated by the decode-complete mark, and the report states that approximation explicitly rather than implying a real paint measurement.

## Test plan
This ticket is a test deliverable. Self-check: a deliberately throttled run (artificially inflated fan-out) must fail the profile, proving the assertions bite.

## Security notes
Load runs use fixture data on a staging environment with no live keys and no live account state. k6 scripts must not embed a real token; they authenticate against a staging identity provisioned for the purpose.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The whole ticket. Budgets asserted: #3, #6 from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; frame decode, bandwidth, re-snapshot size and duration, resync rate from `23-ws-protocol.md` section 16.3.

## Observability
The run consumes E17-T06's metrics and, in doing so, validates them: if a dashboard panel is empty during a load run, that is a defect against E17-T06 filed from this ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Profiles A, B and C implemented and run for their full durations.
- [ ] All budgets recorded; pass or fail stated per budget with numbers.
- [ ] W5 recommendation written and handed to E17-T07.
- [ ] Regression baseline committed with the 10% threshold wired.
- [ ] Results merged into the E17 test plan and referenced from section 16.3's restatement.
- [ ] Self-check performed: an inflated-latency run fails the profile.
- [ ] QA lead and Architect sign-off.

## Dependencies
- **E17-T03** - the backpressure behaviour whose thresholds are being measured.
- **E17-T06** - the metrics and spans the assertions read.

## Branch
`test/e17-ws-load`

## References
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md sections 16.3, 16.4, 16.6 (W1, W5)
- docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md sections 7.3, 9, 10.1, 10.2
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md section 5.4

title: E2E suite, exploratory charter, regression pack and QA sign-off for E17
body:
## Context
The conformance suite proves the server obeys the contract and the chaos suite proves it survives; neither proves that **a trader sitting in front of the app has a correct and honest experience** when the transport misbehaves. `03-testing-strategy.md` sections 7, 11.2 and 16 require E2E suites, an exploratory charter and an explicit QA sign-off before "In Test" can close, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 names Playwright web **and** Electron as an R1 gate.

This ticket closes E17 from the user's side and produces the regression pack that every later train runs.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Playwright E2E additions** (web and Electron), including the two rows section 16.4 names explicitly:
  - **Hidden tab drops throttles; a restored tab does not re-snapshot** (client obligation C8).
  - **A kill-switch frame disables the order ticket without a REST round-trip** (C12).
  Plus: cold start of a 4-pane workspace reaching data on every pane; symbol switch without a socket reconnect; disconnect shows SCR-152 and reconnect restores all panes with fresh snapshots; a forced sequence gap shows the resyncing state and then correct data; a slow-consumer close shows the capacity toast advising fewer panes; a `shutdown_notice` shows a countdown and disables order entry; a `revoked` on a private topic shows the withdrawal message while other panes keep streaming.
- **Exploratory charters** (`03-testing-strategy.md` section 11.2), timeboxed 90 minutes each, with session notes: (1) "break the client's state by racing pane open/close against reconnects"; (2) "find a state where the UI shows data that is not actually current"; (3) "find a combination of throttles and pane visibility that produces a wrong or frozen render". Charter 2 is the highest-value one and is run by the QA lead personally, because a silently stale price is the failure mode with real money attached.
- **Accessibility audit** of the E17 surface: axe-core on SCR-152 and the chrome in every transport state, manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes over the state transitions, keyboard operation of the reconnect overlay, `prefers-reduced-motion`, and 200% zoom reflow. Cross-checked against E17-D04's design-QA findings so the two passes do not duplicate or, worse, each assume the other covered it.
- **Regression pack**: the stable subset of the E2E scenarios tagged for the release regression suite so every later train re-runs E17's guarantees; registered in the regression pack index.
- **Traceability**: the matrix template of `03-testing-strategy.md` section 18 completed for US-MKT-003, US-MKT-005, US-MKT-006 and US-MKT-007 (transport slice), mapping each story's acceptance criteria to the tests that cover them.
- **QA sign-off** per `03-testing-strategy.md` section 16, recorded on the Epic.

## Out of scope
- Protocol-level conformance (E17-Q01), chaos (E17-Q02), load (E17-Q03), adversarial security (E17-X02).
- Chart rendering correctness (E11/E12) beyond "the pane shows data that matches the feed".
- Order placement flows (E29-E34) - only the kill-switch and shutdown gating of the ticket's *affordances* is in scope here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The named E2E rows pass on both shells
  Given the Playwright suite runs on web and on Electron
  Then the hidden-tab and kill-switch scenarios pass on both

Scenario: A trader is never shown stale data as live
  Given each of the six transport states is forced in turn
  Then every affected pane shows its stale, resyncing or disconnected treatment within 2 seconds and displays a last-good timestamp

Scenario: Reconnect restores the full workspace
  Given a 60 second outage with four panes and private topics subscribed
  When connectivity returns
  Then every pane is streaming again within 10 seconds and none shows data older than the outage

Scenario: Accessibility is clean
  When axe-core runs on SCR-152 and the chrome in every transport state
  Then there are zero violations, and the NVDA and VoiceOver transcripts confirm one announcement per transition

Scenario: Exploratory findings are dispositioned
  Given the three charters are executed
  Then every finding is filed with the standard taxonomy and severity, and no P0 or P1 remains open at sign-off

Scenario: Sign-off is evidenced
  Then the sign-off comment lists the suites run, the coverage achieved, the open defects by severity and an explicit accept or reject
```

## Technical notes / design
E2E drives transport states through E17-T04's dev-only fault-injection channel plus the chaos proxy, so scenarios are deterministic rather than timing-dependent - the usual cause of flaky transport E2E. Flake policy per section 14: quarantine within a day, fix or replace, never retry into green.

Electron coverage is not optional: the hidden-window throttling path differs between a browser tab and an Electron `BrowserWindow`, and Electron is the primary shell.

The traceability matrix is generated from test annotations rather than maintained by hand, so it cannot silently rot.

## Test plan
This ticket is a test deliverable. Coverage expectation for the E17 web client is at least 80% (frontend floor); the E2E suite is a required check on the `e2e` job, with the full set nightly and the tagged smoke subset per PR.

## Security notes
Exploratory charter 2 ("find a state where the UI shows data that is not actually current") doubles as a safety review: any finding there is triaged as at least P1 regardless of how obscure the reproduction is, because the consequence is a trade on a false price. Test identities are staging users; no live keys or accounts are used.

## Accessibility notes
The audit described above is a hard gate: `30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.4 requires axe-core zero violations on all R1 routes plus a manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass. Transcripts are attached to the ticket as evidence, not summarised.

## Performance notes
E2E asserts the perceptible budgets rather than the microscopic ones: stale treatment appears within 2 s of the last expected update; reconnect restores panes within 10 s; the chrome's 1 Hz updates do not re-render the workspace subtree (React profiler trace attached).

## Observability
Each E2E run publishes its pass/fail and duration to the CI dashboard; the regression pack's results are part of the R1 PRR evidence bundle.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] E2E scenarios implemented and green on Playwright web and Electron, including both named section 16.4 rows.
- [ ] Three exploratory charters executed with session notes attached; all findings filed and dispositioned.
- [ ] axe-core zero violations; NVDA and VoiceOver transcripts attached.
- [ ] Regression pack tagged and registered.

- **E17-T07** - sign-off happens against the frozen contract, not a moving one.

title: Generate the single-source error registry and wire the error_registry_single_source gate
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` section 10.2 is emphatic that its 28-code error table is **not** an independently maintained list: it is "a rendering of a partition of the one product-wide error registry" that lives in `22-api-openapi.yaml` under `x-error-codes` (six of which are dual-surface: `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`, `no_data_recorded`, `degraded_data`, `exchange_unavailable`, `internal_error`) and `x-error-codes-ws` (WS-only transport codes, each carrying a `rest_analogue`).

The reason is practical: the web client keeps **one** error-mapping table for both surfaces (section 10.3 maps codes to UI treatment classes), and that only works if a code means the same thing wherever it appears. Without the gate, the two documents drift within a sprint and the client's mapping silently develops holes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tools/errorcodes/generate.py`: read `x-error-codes` and `x-error-codes-ws` from `22-api-openapi.yaml` and emit `services/api/app/errors/error_codes.py` and `packages/protocol/src/errorCodes.ts` - enums plus per-code metadata (`scope`, `retryable`, `rest_analogue`, close-code association where applicable).
- `tools/contracts/check_error_registry.py` implementing the blocking gate **`error_registry_single_source`**, asserting: (a) the Code column of `23-ws-protocol.md` section 10.2 equals exactly the union of `x-error-codes-ws` and the `surface: [rest, ws]` subset of `x-error-codes` - no extras, no omissions; (b) every `rest_analogue` value resolves to a real REST code; (c) the generated enums are byte-identical to a fresh regeneration.
- Registration in the `contracts` CI job (`.github/workflows/contracts.yml`) and in `make contracts` for offline local running.
- A **runtime assertion** in the WS gateway's error path: emitting a code absent from the generated enum raises in dev and test builds, which is how requirement **S10** ("emit only error codes from the section 10.2 catalogue") becomes enforceable rather than aspirational.
- Client-side mapping table in `apps/web` driven by the generated metadata and the section 10.3 UI classes: fatal (modal, route to login), transient self-healing (inline staleness badge plus connection chip, no modal), client bug (console error plus a report-a-bug toast, never a silent swallow), capacity (toast advising fewer panes, auto-reduce throttles).

## Out of scope
- Adding or changing any error code's semantics - this task mechanises what exists.
- REST error handling (E02/E09 already own the `problem+json` path).
- The WS schema bundle (E17-T01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The registry is single-source
  When error_registry_single_source runs
  Then the section 10.2 code column equals the union of the two registry blocks exactly

Scenario: Adding a code in one place fails the build
  Given a developer adds a WS error code to 23-ws-protocol.md section 10.2 but not to 22-api-openapi.yaml
  When CI runs
  Then the gate fails naming the orphan code, and the reverse case fails likewise

Scenario: Generated enums cannot drift
  Given a developer hand-edits errorCodes.ts
  Then the gate fails because regeneration is not byte-identical

Scenario: A dangling rest_analogue is caught
  Given a WS code declares a rest_analogue that no REST code defines
  Then the gate fails naming both

Scenario: An undocumented code can never be emitted
  Given the gateway attempts to emit an error code not in the generated enum
  Then in dev and test builds it raises, and a test asserts this
```

## Technical notes / design
The section 10.2 table is parsed from the Markdown by column position with a strict parser - a malformed table row fails the gate rather than being skipped, because a silently skipped row is exactly the drift the gate exists to prevent.

Generated files carry a do-not-edit header naming the generator and the source document. Both generated artefacts are committed so the staleness check (`make gen && git diff --exit-code`) covers them.

The runtime assertion is a thin `raise_ws_error(code, ...)` helper that looks the code up in the enum; direct construction of an error frame elsewhere in the codebase is forbidden by a lint rule so the helper cannot be bypassed.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: generator output for a fixture registry; malformed table row; duplicate code; missing `rest_analogue`; case and whitespace normalisation.
- **Contract**: the gate itself, plus a negative fixture proving it fails when a code is orphaned in either direction.
- **Integration**: the runtime assertion raises on an unknown code in test builds.
- Coverage target: at least 85% on `tools/errorcodes/`.

## Security notes
Error codes are a deliberate information-disclosure boundary: the closed catalogue means no internal exception text, stack trace or SQL fragment can reach a client through the error path. The lint rule forbidding ad hoc error-frame construction is what enforces that. `internal_error` carries only a `request_id` correlating to server-side logs and the audit trail - never a message derived from the underlying exception.

## Accessibility notes
The section 10.3 UI class mapping determines whether an error interrupts the user (modal) or not (inline). Getting that mapping from generated metadata rather than ad hoc code is what stops a transient `degraded_data` from being rendered as a focus-stealing modal.

## Performance notes
The gate runs offline in `make contracts` within the section 16.5 under-10 s local budget; the generator itself is not on a runtime path.

## Observability
`cv_ws_errors_total{code}` counter, which - because the catalogue is closed - has a bounded label cardinality of 28 and is therefore safe as a Prometheus label.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Generator and gate merged, registered in the `contracts` job and in `make contracts`.
- [ ] Generated Python and TS enums committed; staleness check observed failing on a hand edit.
- [ ] Negative fixture proves the gate fails on an orphan code in both directions.
- [ ] Runtime assertion and lint rule in place.
- [ ] Client mapping table driven by the generated metadata.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85% on the tool.
- [ ] Code-owner review; merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E17-T01** - the `contracts` job and `packages/protocol` layout this extends.

## Branch
`feat/e17-error-registry`

## References
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md sections 10.1, 10.2, 10.3, 16.1 (S10), 16.4, 16.5
- docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml `x-error-codes`, `x-error-codes-ws`, `x-contract-validation`
- docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md section 5.0

title: Instrument the WS gateway: metrics, budget-#6 spans and connection-quality telemetry
body:
## Context
`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budget #6 - backend fan-out add-on at most 20 ms p95, measured from book update to outbound WS frame emitted - is a **hard** gate, and budget #3 (WS tick to screen, p95 under 100 ms) can only be measured end to end if the backend span id is propagated to the frontend **via the WS message envelope**. Section 7.2 of that document calls this out as "a specific architecture requirement, not just have logs on both sides".

Separately, `23-ws-protocol.md` attaches alert-worthy semantics to two counters: `cv_ws_resync_total{reason}` (upstream_desync and backpressure are incidents with alert thresholds) and `cv_ws_overflow_total{reason}`. Without them, a degrading connection is invisible until a user complains.

E04 built the metrics facade, correlation-id propagation and the dashboards; this task populates them for M23.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Metrics** registered through E04's facade:
  - `cv_ws_clients` (gauge), `cv_ws_topics_per_client` (gauge, per `20-architecture.md` capacity table).
  - `cv_ws_resync_total{reason}` over the closed reason enum; `cv_ws_overflow_total{reason}`; `cv_ws_conflated_total{topic_family}`.
  - `cv_ws_frame_encode_seconds{kind}`, `cv_ws_frame_bytes{kind}`, `cv_ws_snapshot_build_seconds{topic_family}`, `cv_ws_snapshot_bytes{topic_family}`.
  - `cv_ws_fanout_seconds` histogram - **the budget #6 measurement**: bus event received to outbound frame handed to the socket.
  - `cv_ws_connection_class{class}` gauge, `cv_ws_queue_bytes`, `cv_ws_queue_frames`, `cv_ws_rtt_seconds`, and the `cv_ws_coalesced_count` histogram (from E17-T03, ruling D6), aggregated per process.
  - `cv_ws_errors_total{code}` (bounded cardinality 28, from E17-T05's closed catalogue), `cv_ws_auth_failures_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_revoked_total{reason}`, `cv_ws_closes_total{reason}` (§8: `reason` alone), `cv_ws_clock_skew_ms`.
- **Cross-stack trace correlation**: carry the backend span id on the frame envelope so a single tick correlates from Bybit ingestion through fan-out to frontend paint, satisfying section 7.2's requirement. The envelope field is additive and therefore does not bump `cv.v1` (section 2.3).
- **Structured logs** with E04's correlation id on every connection lifecycle event, every server-initiated resync (`ch`, `reason`, `previous_seq`), every overflow action and every close, at the severities agreed with E04.
- **Grafana panel additions** to E04's existing dashboards: a WS row with connection count, class distribution, fan-out p95 against the 20 ms line, resync rate per reason against the under-1-per-hour-per-topic threshold, overflow actions, bandwidth per connection.
- **Alerts** via E04's two-severity Alertmanager rule set: fan-out p95 over budget for 5 minutes (warning); `upstream_desync` resyncs above 5 per hour per topic (warning, per section 16.3's hard-fail line); any `slow_consumer` close (warning, since it implies a user lost their feed); `cv_ws_sequence_gaps_detected_total` above zero (critical - a server-side gap is a correctness bug, not a condition).
- **Runbook** entries for each alert in the E04 runbook format: what it means, what to check first, what action to take.

## Out of scope
- The observability platform itself - E04 owns Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, structlog and the diagnostics bundle.
- Frontend performance marks - E17-T04 emits those; this task only guarantees the correlating span id is on the wire.
- Load testing - E17-Q03.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budget #6 is measurable, not asserted
  Given the gateway is serving the reference workspace
  Then cv_ws_fanout_seconds is populated and its p95 is visible on the dashboard against the 20 ms budget line

Scenario: A single tick correlates end to end
  Given a book update from Bybit ingestion
  Then the backend span id appears on the outbound envelope and the frontend performance mark carries the same id, so the full path is one trace

Scenario: Resync incidents alert
  Given upstream_desync resyncs exceed 5 per hour on one topic
  Then a warning alert fires with a runbook link

Scenario: Label cardinality stays bounded
  Given a full day of traffic
  Then no WS metric exceeds its documented label cardinality, and no metric carries a symbol or user id as an unbounded label

Scenario: A server-side sequence gap is treated as a bug
  Given cv_ws_sequence_gaps_detected_total increments
  Then a critical alert fires, because the server guarantees it cannot happen
```

## Technical notes / design
Cardinality discipline matters more than usual here: `topic_family` (11 public plus 9 private) and `kind` (6) are safe labels; **symbol and user id are not** and must stay out of labels - they belong in logs and in exemplars. `cv_ws_topics_per_client` is a gauge summarised per connection, not a per-topic series.

The fan-out histogram brackets exactly the span budget #6 defines - bus receipt to frame handed to the socket - excluding the client's network time, so a slow Tailscale link never flatters or condemns the backend number.

Instrumentation must not itself cost the budget: E04-K01 measured the facade's overhead; keep the hot path to counter increments and one histogram observation per emitted frame, with no string formatting.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: every metric registered exactly once; label sets fixed; the fan-out timer brackets the intended span.
- **Integration**: after a scripted session (connect, subscribe, resync, overflow, close), assert every expected metric moved and no unexpected label value appeared.
- **Perf**: instrumentation overhead under 2% of the fan-out path, measured against an uninstrumented build.
- **Ops**: each alert fired once in staging by injecting its condition, and its runbook followed end to end.
- Coverage target: at least 85%.

## Security notes
Logs and metrics must never contain an access token, an API key, a raw account identifier in a metric label, or a user's personal data. E04's structlog handler-level redaction applies; a test asserts a token-shaped string never appears in emitted logs. The diagnostics bundle (E04-S02) is secret-scanned and size-capped before it can include WS state.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (operator-facing; the Grafana panels follow E04's already-reviewed dashboard conventions).

## Performance notes
Instrumentation overhead at most 2% of the fan-out path. The measurement itself is the enforcement mechanism for budget #6 (hard) and the input to budget #3 (hard at R2 exit, measured a train early per R1 exit criterion 3).

## Observability
This ticket is observability. Its own success criterion is that budgets #3 and #6 can be read off a dashboard without ad hoc instrumentation during the R1 PRR.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All metrics registered, populated and visible on E04's dashboards.
- [ ] Span id propagated on the envelope and correlated with a frontend mark, demonstrated on one real trace.
- [ ] Four alerts wired with runbook entries; each fired once in staging.
- [ ] Cardinality audit recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] Instrumentation overhead measured and under 2%.
- [ ] Coverage at least 85%.
- [ ] Code-owner review; merged via merge queue.

title: Freeze the protocol: reconcile 23-ws-protocol.md, amend ADR-0005 and add the breaking-change gate
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 7 (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 5.3): "**WS protocol is frozen**: `23-ws-protocol.md` matches the implementation, contract tests pass, and a deliberate breaking change fails CI." R1 goal 4 gives the reason: R2 and R3 must be able to *add topics* without renegotiating transport, which is only true if the transport is settled and mechanically protected.

Implementation always teaches the spec something. This ticket is the deliberate, **one-time** reconciliation where the document is corrected to match reality, after which the direction of travel reverses permanently: from then on, code moves to match the spec (`runtime_spec_parity` gate: "spec is the source of truth; code moves to match").

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Reconciliation pass** over `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` against the shipped implementation, section by section: 2 (negotiation), 3 (framing and binary layout), 4 (lifecycle, close codes), 5 (sub/unsub/ctl), 6 (topic catalogue, options, defaults, permission matrix), 7 (snapshot, delta, resync reasons), 8 (coalescing rules, classes, overflow ladder), 9 (heartbeats, resubscription, revocation), 10 (error catalogue), 16.2 (limits). Every divergence is resolved explicitly: either the document is corrected, or a defect is filed against the implementation. **No divergence may be left undocumented.**
- **Close the open items** in section 16.6: **W1** (measured bandwidth and CPU, from E17-K01), **W2** (depth 500 keep-or-drop, from E17-K01), **W5** (per-topic coalescing thresholds under `saturated`, from E17-Q03's load results). W3 is already closed; W4 (session resumption) stays deferred with a restated rationale and a post-R2 review date.
- **Amend ADR-0005** with the measured numbers from E17-K01 and an explicit statement of whether its validation gate was met, plus any layout corrections from E17-T02 and a note on what the implementation taught.
- **The breaking-change CI gate**: a test that pins the wire contract - the binary header layout and every body-kind record stride, the control-frame required-field sets, the close-code set and the error-code set - against a committed golden fixture. Changing any of them fails CI with a message explaining that a breaking change requires `cv.v2` served in parallel for at least one release (section 2.3). The gate must be demonstrated failing on a deliberate break during review.
- **`runtime_spec_parity`** wired for the WS surface: the running server's advertised `welcome.limits`, topic catalogue and error catalogue are compared against the document, so a limit changed in config without a doc change fails the build.
- **Additive-change guidance** documented in `packages/protocol/README.md`: what is additive and therefore free (new topic, new optional field, new error code - clients must ignore unknown fields and topics) versus what requires `cv.v2`.
- **Update `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`** SCR-152 and the section 0.5.4 invariant if the shipped behaviour diverged, and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.12 if the component decomposition diverged.

## Out of scope
- New protocol features - the point of the ticket is that there are none.
- E26's replay routing, which adds no new framing.
- Re-running the load tests (E17-Q03 owns them; this ticket consumes their numbers).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The document matches the implementation
  When each section of 23-ws-protocol.md is walked against the shipped code
  Then every divergence is either corrected in the document or filed as a defect, and the reconciliation table on this ticket lists all of them

Scenario: A deliberate breaking change fails CI
  Given a developer changes the trades record stride from 22 bytes to 24
  When CI runs
  Then the wire-contract gate fails with a message directing the author to cv.v2

Scenario: An additive change does not fail CI
  Given a new optional field is added to a structured payload and a new topic is registered
  Then CI passes, because additive changes do not bump the version

Scenario: Config drift is caught
  Given max_subscriptions is changed in config from 200 to 300 without a document change
  Then runtime_spec_parity fails

Scenario: Open items are closed with evidence
  Then section 16.6 marks W1, W2 and W5 resolved, each citing the ticket and the measured numbers that resolved it
```

## Technical notes / design
The golden fixture is a committed JSON description of the wire contract - not a prose assertion - generated once from the implementation at freeze time and thereafter compared: `{header: {size, fields}, body_kinds: {1..6: {stride, fields}}, control_frames: {name: required_fields}, close_codes: [...], error_codes: [...], limits: {...}}`. Regenerating it is a deliberate act that shows up as a reviewable diff in a PR that must also explain itself, which is exactly the friction the freeze is meant to create.

The reconciliation table lives on this ticket and in the PR description: one row per divergence with section, what the doc said, what the code did, and the resolution. Reviewers check the table, not just the diff.

## Test plan
- The wire-contract gate is itself the test; it is demonstrated failing on a deliberate break (stride change, removed required field, removed error code) and passing on an additive change.
- `runtime_spec_parity` exercised against a running instance in the docker-compose test environment.
- No new functional tests - if reconciliation reveals behaviour without a test, that is a defect filed against the owning story, not patched here.

## Security notes
The freeze is itself a security control: a pinned, reviewed wire contract means a decoder-affecting change cannot land without deliberate review, which is the structural half of the mitigation for `04-security-program.md` T-W1 (malformed frame handling) - the other half being E17-T02's bounds checks and fuzzing.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Section 16.3's budget table is restated from measured values (E17-K01, E17-Q03) rather than left as engineering estimates - this is the substantive part of closing W1.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Reconciliation table complete; every divergence resolved or filed.
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md` merged in its reconciled form; section 16.6 W1, W2, W5 closed with evidence; W4 restated as deferred.
- [ ] ADR-0005 amended with measured numbers and a gate met/not-met statement.
- [ ] Wire-contract gate merged, blocking, and demonstrated failing on a deliberate break during review.
- [ ] `runtime_spec_parity` green for the WS surface.
- [ ] `packages/protocol/README.md` documents additive vs breaking.
- [ ] SCR-152, section 0.5.4 and `20-architecture.md` section 3.12 updated if they diverged.
- [ ] Architect approval recorded - the freeze is an architectural act.
- [ ] R1 exit criterion 7 demonstrated at the PRR.

## Dependencies
- **E17-K01** supplies W1 and W2 evidence; **E17-Q03** supplies W5.
- **E17-T03**, **E17-T04**, **E17-T05** must be complete - freezing before the client exists would freeze an untested contract.

## Branch
`feat/e17-protocol-freeze`

## References
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md section 5.3 exit criterion 7, section 5.1 goal 4
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md sections 2.3, 16.5, 16.6
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0005-ws-protocol-and-binary-encoding.md

title: UX research: how traders read per-bar statistics
body:
## Context
E20 introduces one net-new modal (SCR-033 Deep Stats rows configuration) and one net-new organism (CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip) that sits permanently under the chart consuming vertical space the trader would otherwise give to price. The catalogue in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 offers **21 possible rows**; SCR-033's wireframe shows 13. Which rows a trader actually wants by default, how many they will tolerate before the strip stops paying for its height, and whether they read the strip or the footprint cells first are empirical questions. US-DS-002 exists precisely because "the strip fits my screen budget" is a real constraint. This ticket produces the evidence the wireframes (E20-D02) are argued from, two sprints ahead of the consuming FE story (E20-S01, Sprint 11) per the design-ahead rule.

The stimulus for the probe is the E18-D02 footprint wireframe set (Sprint 08), not a running footprint build — this keeps the whole S09 design track startable ahead of E18's S10–S11 engineering window.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3–4 moderated sessions (Owner + up to 2 account managers + 1 proxy order-flow trader), 45 min each, screen-shared against their current DeepCharts/ATAS/Sierra setup.
- Task-based probes: read the last bar's aggression without touching the footprint; find the bar with the largest delta in the visible range; decide whether a bar is "strong" from the numbers alone; configure a strip for a 1-minute scalping session vs a 15-minute swing session.
- Row-ranking exercise over the full 21-row catalogue from `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 (card sort): produces an ordered list and a defensible **default row set** (target: 4–6 rows) plus a defensible **compact-mode row set**.
- Evidence on threshold semantics for US-DS-003: what "significant" means numerically for delta %, and whether thresholds are per-symbol in practice (the story asserts they are — confirm or refute).
- Competitive teardown of stats strips (DeepCharts "Deep Stats"/On-Candle Stats, ATAS, Sierra Chart) covering row catalogues, compact modes, alignment behaviour at narrow bar widths, and threshold highlighting conventions.
- Findings written to `docs/design/research/e20-deep-stats.md`: ranked row frequencies, the recommended default and compact row sets, vocabulary for row labels (must reconcile with the UI labels fixed in §7 — deviations flagged as doc changes, not silent renames), and 5–8 adopted design decisions each phrased as a testable statement.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design — greyscale wireframes start in E20-D02.
- Footprint cell research (E18), profile research (E19), DOM ladder research (E21).
- Recruiting participants outside the owner's circle.
- Deciding the sparkline (US-DS-004) feature's existence — it is a Could; research may report on it but does not gate it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default row set is evidence-backed
  When docs/design/research/e20-deep-stats.md is reviewed
  Then it names a default row set of 4-6 rows with the session evidence for each inclusion
  And every named row maps to a MetricDescriptor listed in 24-internal-schemas.md §7

Scenario: Narrow-bar behaviour has a decided answer
  Given US-DS-001 requires a compact form below a minimum legible bar width
  When the findings are reviewed
  Then they state what traders expect to see in that compact form and what they expect to read in the crosshair readout instead

Scenario: Threshold assumption tested
  When the threshold probe results are reviewed
  Then the per-symbol-thresholds assumption in US-DS-003 is either confirmed with evidence or explicitly refuted with a recorded recommendation to change the story
```

## Technical notes / design
Sessions are recorded (with consent) and stored under `docs/design/research/raw/e20/`. Card sort uses the exact row labels from `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 so results are directly actionable. No prototype is built; probes run against the participants' existing tools and the R1 chart build.

## Test plan
N/A (research ticket). Verification is the artefact review in the acceptance criteria, performed by the CDO and the E20 engineering lead.

## Security notes
Session recordings may capture participants' own account balances and positions on their existing tooling. Recordings must be stored access-restricted and redacted before any excerpt is shared; no credentials are ever entered during a session. Data classification: internal. No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
At least one probe is run keyboard-only to gather evidence on how a non-mouse user would reorder rows, feeding the `Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down` requirement in SCR-033.

## Performance notes
N/A — no code produced. Research does surface the perceived cost ceiling ("how many rows before this feels heavy"), which E20-K01 then measures for real.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §4.2 (Task):
- [ ] `docs/design/research/e20-deep-stats.md` merged with ranked rows, default + compact sets, and 5–8 testable design decisions.
- [ ] Acceptance criteria above verified in an artefact review by the CDO and the E20 engineering lead.
- [ ] Any recommended change to US-DS-002/US-DS-003 raised as a doc PR against `11-user-stories.md` rather than left in the research file.
- [ ] Findings presented at the design review; E20-D02 unblocked.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E18-D02` (*Wireframe the footprint layer on SCR-030, SCR-032 and the SCR-056 imbalance surfaces*, Sprint 08) — participants must be able to see a concrete footprint rendering to answer "do you read the strip or the cells first"; the E18 wireframes plus the E18-D01 research prototype are sufficient stimulus, and they land a full sprint before this ticket starts.

This deliberately does **not** block on the E18 epic as a whole: E18 runs S10–S11 per the roadmap Gantt (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.2), so an `E18` epic-level blocker would make this Sprint-09 ticket unstartable and would cascade the same violation onto E20-D02/D03. Footprint *rendering* is not required for a research probe; footprint *wireframes* are. The downstream design chain (D02 S09 → D03 S09 → D04/D05 S10) therefore inherits only the S08 dependency and is schedulable in-window, preserving the design-ahead rule for the Sprint-11 stories.

## Branch
`design/e20-research` — docs-only PR.

## References

- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.4 order-flow engines (`DeepStatsEngine`)

- **Strip-hidden state**: the "all rows off" case with the one-click restore affordance living in the pane menu (US-DS-002 scenario "All rows off").
