title: Motion spec and accessibility review for the Deep-Stats strip
body:
## Context
The strip updates continuously — the forming bar's values change up to 4 Hz (CMP-225 data contract) — while sitting in the trader's peripheral vision next to a live chart. Unspecified motion here is actively harmful: value flicker reads as noise and, for a screen-reader user, an unguarded live region would flood output. This ticket fixes the motion language and runs the formal accessibility review of the E20 designs before engineering starts in Sprint 11.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion spec** (`docs/design/e20-motion.md` + Figma prototype): value-change transition (duration, easing, and the explicit decision on whether a changing value animates at all at 4 Hz — the default position is that it does not, and the spec must argue whichever way it lands); row add/remove and reorder transitions in SCR-033 and in the strip; threshold-breach entry/exit; strip show/hide; export progress. Every duration/easing expressed as a token from `16-design-system-brief.md`.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour** for every motion above, specified as a complete alternative, not "animation off".
- **Accessibility review** of the full E20 design set against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: table semantics and header association for the strip; the accessible name of every SCR-033 control; the keyboard reorder contract (`Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down`) including the announcement made after a move ("Cumulative Delta moved to position 1 of 5"); the "read current bar's stats" shortcut's announcement text; live-region policy for the forming bar (must default to non-announcing, opt-in only, mirroring the CMP-226 BarCountdown precedent); focus management on modal open/close and after the export completes.
- A written a11y acceptance checklist that E20-Q04 executes verbatim.

## Out of scope
- Implementation of any of it (E20-S01..S04).
- Motion for the chart canvas, footprint cells or heatmap (E18/E21).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion is a designed alternative
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  When the motion spec is reviewed
  Then every animated behaviour has a specified non-animated equivalent that still communicates the same change

Scenario: The forming bar does not flood a screen reader
  When the live-region policy is reviewed
  Then the forming bar's values are non-announcing by default and announcement is opt-in, with the opt-in control named

Scenario: Reorder is announced
  When a row is moved with Alt+Up
  Then the spec defines the exact announcement string including the new position and the total count
```

## Technical notes / design
Motion tokens only. The 4 Hz coalescing cadence is the hard constraint: any transition longer than ~250 ms would still be running when the next value arrives, which is the technical argument the spec must engage with. Announcement strings are specified as i18n-ready message templates even though v1 ships English only.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). The output *is* the test script for E20-Q04; its quality is verified by the a11y specialist confirming every checklist item is objectively checkable.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility review. Sign-off by the accessibility specialist is mandatory and is a gate on E20-D05 handoff.

## Performance notes
Motion choices are bounded by the strip's <=1.5 ms/frame budget; any transition requiring per-frame layout work is rejected in favour of compositor-only properties.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] `docs/design/e20-motion.md` merged with tokens, reduced-motion alternatives and the 4 Hz argument recorded.

- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified; no open a11y objections carried into Sprint 11.

`design/e20-motion-a11y`.

title: DOM ladder & liquidity heatmap
body:
## Context
CandleViewer's DeepDOM analogue — a clickable price ladder with a time×price liquidity heatmap behind it — is the single densest, highest-frequency surface in the product and the **named first target of the mandatory WebGL engine spike** (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-050 "Mandatory WebGL engine spike gate", owner decision #2.2.1). `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.2 schedules this Epic at **S10–S12 of the R2 Order-flow beta train** with 55 points, covering: "Price ladder with bid/ask depth, aggregated size bars, last-trade tape column, position/orders column; rolling-texture liquidity heatmap (`texSubImage2D` newest-column upload) at 200 depth, 100 ms cadence, with a configurable history window; **green = bid, red = ask, user-configurable**; depth aggregation by tick grouping; heatmap↔chart time-axis alignment; liquidity-removal ('pulled orders') shading".

Architecture modules: **M7 Book Engine** (`20-architecture.md` §3.2 — `BookState`, `Resyncer`, `DepthAggregator`, `BookPublisher`, `LiquidityTracker`) and **M9 Order-Flow Engines** (§3.4 — `HeatmapEngine`). The heatmap grid model is already normatively specified in `24-internal-schemas.md` §6 (`HeatmapColumn`, `HeatmapGridSpec`, the `estimated=True` rule during resync, percentile clipping, log default). The transport is already frozen by E17: `book.{symbol}.{depth}` (binary body_kind 1/2) and `heatmap.{symbol}` (binary body_kind 6) in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, including the normative `time_bucket_ms` derivation in §6.1.1. The REST backfill contract is `GET /market/heatmap` and `GET /market/orderbook` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Persistence is `heatmap_cells` and `orderbook_deltas`/`orderbook_snapshots` in `21-database-schema.md` §4.2/4.3/4.12.

This Epic delivers the **read-only** surface. Click-to-trade (US-DOM-007) and drag-to-amend (US-DOM-008) belong to **E31 Chart & DOM trading interactions** in R3 (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2) — E21 ships the interaction *contract* (row hit-targets ≥24 px, `role="grid"` row action menu, the arm-toggle slot) so E31 plugs into it without re-laying out the panel.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (DOM domain, `11-user-stories.md` §11):** US-DOM-001 (live ladder, Must), US-DOM-002 (liquidity heatmap, Must), US-DOM-003 (adaptive colour scale, Must), US-DOM-004 (trail duration/decay, Should), US-DOM-005 (depth tiers & load shedding, Must), US-DOM-006 (own orders/position on the ladder, Must), US-DOM-009 (deep liquidity scan & book reload, Should), US-DOM-010 (book history backfill on open, Should). Also carries US-MKT-007 (book snapshot+delta) on this surface.

**Screens:** SCR-050 Heatmap + DOM ladder panel, SCR-051 Heatmap & ladder settings dialog, SCR-153 Degraded-mode state (depth-shedding variant only).
**Components:** CMP-108 DomLadderRow, CMP-111 HeatmapCell (logical model + a11y), CMP-113 HeatmapLegend, CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons, CMP-134 DetectorEventCard (mount only), CMP-193 HeatmapOverlay (engine mount point), CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-229 ArmToggle (visual state only), CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker, CMP-228 PreviewTile, CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner.
**WS topics:** `book.{symbol}.{depth}` (depth ∈ 50/200/500), `heatmap.{symbol}`, `ticker.{symbol}`, `trades.{symbol}`, `orders`, `positions`, `system` (connection_quality).
**REST:** `GET /market/orderbook`, `GET /market/heatmap`.
**Tables:** `heatmap_cells`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `orderflow_metrics` (book_imbalance, book_thickness), `chart_presets.heatmap` jsonb.

**Children**
| Key | Title | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| E21-K01 | Spike: 500-depth heatmap ring buffer & runtime parity | 3 |
| E21-T01 | Book engine: depth tiers, aggregation and ladder publisher | 5 |
| E21-T02 | HeatmapEngine columns, `heatmap.{symbol}` topic and `heatmap_cells` persistence | 5 |
| E21-T03 | `GET /market/heatmap` backfill from recorded book history | 3 |
| E21-T04 | LiquidityTracker: depth bands, thickness and refill/reload detection | 3 |

| E21-T06 | Adaptive colour scale, LUT and palette convention | 2 |
| E21-T07 | ADR-0016 depth-tier shedding policy + docs reconciliation | 2 |
| E21-S01 | Live DOM ladder grid (SCR-050) | 8 |
| E21-S02 | Liquidity heatmap surface with legend and empty state | 5 |
| E21-S03 | Adaptive / fixed / log colour scale controls | 3 |
| E21-S04 | Trail duration, decay and client memory guard | 2 |
| E21-S05 | Depth tiers and load shedding | 5 |

| E21-S08 | Book history backfill on symbol open | 3 |

| E21-X01..X03 | Security track (STRIDE, abuse cases/quotas, review) | 8 |

Engineering total (K + T + S) **62 pts** against the 55-point budget (within ±15%). Design **23**, QA **26**, Security **8** are tracked separately per the capacity rule, for **119** points on the Epic rollup.

## Out of scope
- **Click-to-trade (US-DOM-007) and drag-to-amend (US-DOM-008)** — E31, R3. E21 ships the hit-target/keyboard contract only, with all trading affordances rendered disabled.
- Iceberg / stop-run / absorption detector *algorithms* — E25. E21 only mounts CMP-134 cards and the `(estimated)` badge.
- Liquidation heatmap (`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.4) — E24.
- Replay of the ladder/heatmap — E26 (it reuses these same topics through the one code path).
- Recording the book itself — E16.
- Android / any non-web client.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The DeepDOM surface works end to end
  Given BTCUSDT is recorded and book.BTCUSDT.200 and heatmap.BTCUSDT are live
  When the owner opens SCR-050
  Then a 200-level ladder and a 60-minute heatmap trail render together on one time axis
  And the panel sustains the 100 ms heatmap cadence at >=55 fps with WS->pixel p95 <=120 ms

Scenario: The surface degrades honestly, never silently
  Given frame time exceeds budget for 5 consecutive seconds
  Then the depth tier steps down one rung, a non-blocking notice states why, and a metric records it
  And when the book desyncs the ladder greys with "Book resynchronising" and heatmap columns render as estimated

Scenario: Accessibility parity
  Given a screen-reader user focuses the ladder
  Then every price row is a focusable role=row announcing price, bid size, ask size and own-order size
  And the heatmap exposes a windowed per-level liquidity history table with no colour-only information

Scenario: Epic-level exit
  Then US-DOM-001..006, 009, 010 are Done, zero P0/P1 bugs are open against SCR-050/SCR-051,
  budgets #1 and #14 of 06-performance-and-load-standard.md are recorded as met, the STRIDE model is signed off,
  and axe-core plus one manual screen-reader pass are green on both screens
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Depth identity**: `book.BTCUSDT.50` and `book.BTCUSDT.200` are *independent subscriptions with independent sequences* (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 note). A tier change is a resubscribe + fresh snapshot, never an in-place mutation.
- **Heatmap bucket size** is client-derived per `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1 (2–8 device px per column, 3 px target, upward clamp at 1000 ms when `ideal_ms ≤ 2500`), re-derived on resize/DPR change, debounced 400 ms, and answered with `resnapshot: true`.
- **Rolling texture**: newest column only via `texSubImage2D` (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.2; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8), fine ring 2048×512×R16F ≈ 2.1 MB plus coarse ring 14400×512 ≈ 14.7 MB (§"Memory").
- **Colour**: green = bid, red = ask (owner decision #10), user-configurable, CVD-safe blue/orange alternative first-class; log scale default; `clip_percentile` normalisation over visible columns (`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.2).
- **Estimated data**: columns produced while the book is `Resyncing` carry `estimated=True`, render at 40% opacity with a hatch, and are excluded from rule-engine liquidity metrics.

## Test plan
Unit/property (book invariants, bucket selection, normalisation), golden-file (heatmap decay/normalisation per `03-testing-strategy.md` §"golden-file"), contract (WS + OpenAPI schema gates), integration (recorded `orderbook_snapshot_delta_*.jsonl.gz` fixtures incl. a seq gap), E2E Playwright incl. pixel-diff golden heatmap frames (`maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01`), perf (engine FPS harness + k6 WS profile), chaos (desync, slow consumer, exchange 5xx), a11y (axe + manual SR).

## Security notes
Primary epic-level threat named by `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4: **unbounded subscription depth as a DoS vector** — a client subscribing many symbols at depth 500 with a 100 ms bucket can exhaust server CPU/egress. Mitigations: per-connection subscription quotas, `marketdata:read` RBAC on every topic and on `GET /market/heatmap` (`04-security-program.md` §RBAC row 5), the `23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3 connection-quality classifier, and SR-038 (stale books disable trading affordances). Data classification: market data (non-secret) — but own-order/position overlay on the ladder is **account-scoped** and must be RBAC- and scope-filtered.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-050 is explicitly *not* relaxed for density (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §1): `role="grid"` ladder with roving tabindex, ≥24 px row targets, region landmark, windowed heatmap reveal (§6.2), data-table alternative (§6.3), colour never the only channel for bid/ask (§5), and 3:1 contrast at every gradient stop.

## Performance notes
Budget #1 (≤16.6 ms frame at 100k bars + 200-depth heatmap @100 ms) and budget #14 (100 ms cadence sustained, ≤1 dropped/coalesced frame per 10 s) are **hard R1 exit gates re-verified here at R2 scale**; SCR-050 additionally sets a stricter panel budget of WS→pixel ≤120 ms p95 and ≤600 GPU trail frames.

## Observability
Metrics: `heatmap_missing_columns_total` (alert >1%/min), `heatmap_column_publish_latency_ms`, `book_desync_total`, `dom_depth_tier_current`, `dom_shedding_events_total`, `dom_frame_time_ms`. Audit/analytics: `dom.depth_changed`, `dom.settings_changed`, `degraded.entered/exited`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level AC verified end to end on staging (demo), not just per child.
- [ ] Coverage floors held; zero open P0/P1 against SCR-050/SCR-051.
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `26-chart-engine-design.md`, `14/15-*` reflect shipped behaviour.
- [ ] WCAG 2.2 AA verified on SCR-050 + SCR-051 (axe CI + manual SR pass).
- [ ] Budgets #1 and #14 recorded; SCR-050 spike-gate evidence attached to the design sign-off.
- [ ] STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, Security sign-off comment present.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression/exploratory pass recorded (E21-Q06).
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at Sprint Review with acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Retro notes captured as follow-up tickets.

## Sizing
Epic estimate **55 points**, exactly the roadmap sizing for E21 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3/§6.2. This is the rollup of the delivery children (Story/Task/Spike): 8+3+2+3+3+2+2+3+2 (S01–S09) + 5+5+2+2+5+2+2 (T01–T07) + 3 (K01) = 55. Design (D01–D08), QA (Q01–Q07) and Security (X01–X03) tickets are tracked on this Epic but, per the roadmap convention, are carried in the cross-cutting design/QA/security capacity lines rather than the epic’s 55-point delivery budget, so they are excluded from this rollup.

## Dependencies

title: Prove the 500-depth heatmap ring buffer and runtime parity
body:
## Context
SCR-050 carries a **mandatory spike gate that blocks design sign-off** (owner decision #2.2.1): the heatmap is the named first target of the engine spike. E06 answered the general question (custom engine viable, ADR-0002/ADR-0011) on candles + footprint. This spike answers the four heatmap-specific sub-questions the screens catalogue enumerates, at R2 scale on the real texture pipeline rather than E06's throwaway prototype:

(a) trail advancing at 100 ms cadence at ≥60 fps at the **200-depth** tier;
(b) a 10-minute sustained run at the **500-depth** tier with no dropped frames — **or** a designed, documented cap that makes 500-depth unavailable with a visible reason in SCR-051;
(c) the full 600-frame GPU ring buffer held inside the per-panel memory budget (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Memory": fine ring 2048×512×2 B ≈ 2.1 MB, coarse ring 14400×512×2 B ≈ 14.7 MB);
(d) the same numbers in Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2 — noting that a Tauri failure here does not block sign-off but **locks the shell to Electron** and must be recorded (owner decision #7).

Timebox: **5 working days**, agreed with the Architect.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A harness in `packages/chart-engine/bench/heatmap/` driving `texSubImage2D` newest-column uploads over the E11 benchmark scene (100k bars) at 100 ms cadence, with synthetic 50/200/500-depth column streams generated deterministically from a seed.
- Measured p50/p95/p99 frame time, upload cost per column, texture memory, and dropped/coalesced frame count over 10 minutes, per depth tier, per runtime, on the reference hardware (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1).
- A comparison of column aggregation strategies when >1 column per pixel (max-of-columns preserving spikes, per `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6) and of R16F vs R8 quantisation.
- Decision recorded as an amendment/new ADR entry under `docs/plan/27-adrs/` and the evidence attached to the E21-D02 sign-off.
- Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path is chosen.

## Out of scope
Production-shippable code (explicitly a throwaway/promotable prototype); backend column production (E21-T02); the ladder.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: 200-depth budget met
  When the harness runs 10 minutes at 200 depth, 100 ms cadence, in Chromium and Electron
  Then p95 frame time is <=16.6 ms and dropped/coalesced frames are <=1 per 10 s, matching budgets #1 and #14

Scenario: 500-depth decision recorded
  Given the 500-depth tier fails the 10-minute run
  Then a documented cap is specified, SCR-051 shows 500-depth as unavailable with a visible reason,
  and the decision is recorded in an ADR rather than left as tribal knowledge

Scenario: Tauri divergence
  Given Tauri/WebView2 fails the cadence while Chromium and Electron pass
  Then the finding locks the shell to Electron, updates ADR-0011, and does not block E21-D02 sign-off

Scenario: Memory ceiling
  Then retained texture memory for a 600-frame trail at the chosen tier is measured and compared against the
  26-chart-engine-design.md budget, with the MemoryGovernor step-down behaviour exercised at 70% of budget
```

## Technical notes / design
Quantisation to R16F normalised per column max or global scale (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8 flow). DPI is capped at 2 for the heatmap layer to bound texture cost (§3.x DPI note). Eviction: columns outside a 3× viewport window are dropped from GPU buffers and kept in CPU stores until memory pressure. The harness must record per-stage frame markers matching `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 so a later regression can be stage-attributed.

## Test plan
The harness *is* the test; it is promoted into the CI benchmark suite by E21-Q03 regardless of outcome so the numbers are re-measured every release.

## Security notes
N/A — synthetic data, no network, no credentials.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the spike itself, but the spike must confirm that maintaining the windowed accessible mirror alongside the texture pipeline does not itself cost frames — measure with the mirror on and off.

## Performance notes
This spike defines the numbers the rest of the Epic is held to: budgets #1 and #14 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, plus B4 (heatmap ≤10 ms, upload ≤12 KB/s, texture ≤20 MB) and B5 (combined scene ≤16.7 ms, ≤40 draw calls) of `26-chart-engine-design.md`.

## Observability
Harness emits a machine-readable JSON result consumed by the CI benchmark reporter.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four sub-questions answered with recorded evidence (numbers per tier per runtime).
- [ ] ADR entry written under `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (a "defer/cap" outcome is itself a recorded decision).
- [ ] Evidence attached to the SCR-050 design sign-off record (E21-D02).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for the chosen path.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated for R2 Render performance and R8 Browser/GPU compat.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] Prototype either promoted (then normal Task DoD applies) or explicitly marked throwaway.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E11 (the scene graph, render-pass scheduler and OffscreenCanvas worker this measures against) and E06 (the original engine spike and ADR-0002/0011 it amends).

## Branch
`spike/e21-heatmap-ring`.

## References
`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-050 spike gate; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8, §"Memory", §B4/B5; `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1, §4.2, §4.3, budgets #1/#14; `27-adrs/ADR-0002`, `ADR-0011`.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. AGENTS.md §0 (read-first order) and §5 (coding standards for the touched stack)
2. docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md (DoR/DoD you must satisfy)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `packages/chart-engine/src/layers/`
- `packages/chart-engine/src/plugins/`
- `packages/chart-engine/bench/`
- `packages/chart-engine/test/`
- Tests alongside the above per AGENTS.md conventions for `chart-engine`.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- No wire-format or DB-schema interfaces named in this ticket's body — if your implementation needs one, add it to 22-api-openapi.yaml / 23-ws-protocol.md / 24-internal-schemas.md FIRST, in its own commit.

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test`
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `spike/e21-heatmap-ring`
- PR title: "E21-K01: Prove the 500-depth heatmap ring buffer and runtime parity"
- Body includes: "Closes #<issue>"
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/chart-engine
- Labels: type/spike, area/chart-engine, priority/p0, perf

**Done means**
- All four sub-questions answered with recorded evidence (numbers per tier per runtime).
- ADR entry written under `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (a "defer/cap" outcome is itself a recorded decision).
- Evidence attached to the SCR-050 design sign-off record (E21-D02).
- Follow-up tickets filed for the chosen path.
- `32-risk-register.md` updated for R2 Render performance and R8 Browser/GPU compat.
- Findings presented at Sprint Review.

**Do NOT**
- Do not widen this ticket's Scope beyond what is listed above — file a new ticket instead.
- Do not touch what this ticket explicitly excludes: Production-shippable code (explicitly a throwaway/promotable prototype); backend column production (E21-T02); the ladder.
- Do not add React, network I/O, or Bybit-specific knowledge to `packages/chart-engine/` (AGENTS.md placement rules).
- Do not land without recording a benchmark against the named budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` — a perf-labelled ticket with no number attached is not Done.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the specific blocker key (blocked_by: E11, E06), move Status to Blocked, and never silently work around a failing lint/test/perf gate — escalate to the Architect if the gate itself looks wrong.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Book engine: depth tiers, tick aggregation and the ladder publisher
body:
## Context
Module **M7 Book Engine** (`20-architecture.md` §3.2) already exists in skeleton form from E08 (L2 reconstruction, sequence-gap detection). This Task completes the three components the ladder needs: `DepthAggregator` (level-aggregated views: raw, 1-tick, N-tick bucketed), `BookPublisher` (snapshot at subscribe/resync, deltas thereafter, conflated to 50 ms for the ladder topic and 100 ms for the heatmap topic) and the depth-tier negotiation that makes `book.{symbol}.{depth}` real for depth ∈ {50, 200, 500}.

The transport contract is frozen by E17 and must be implemented exactly: `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 puts **depth in the topic name, not the options**, because depth changes the identity of the state — `book.BTCUSDT.50` and `book.BTCUSDT.200` are independent subscriptions with independent sequence numbers. Binary body kinds 1 (`book_snapshot`) and 2 (`book_delta`) are already specified in §3.4, including the 16-byte snapshot trailer carrying Bybit's `xu`/`xseq`.

Upstream cadences are fixed by Bybit (`24-internal-schemas.md` §2.2): depth 1 @ 10 ms, 50 @ 20 ms, 200 @ 100 ms, 500 @ 200 ms. v1 subscribes 200 for heatmap/DOM and 1 for best bid/ask. **Depth 1 is snapshot-only and is re-sent every 3 s even when unchanged** — the engine must not treat an unchanged depth-1 resend as a book event or the heatmap shows phantom columns. That is a named trap and needs a test.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/backend/book_engine/aggregator.py` — `DepthAggregator.aggregate(bucket_ticks, depth)` producing bucketed level views; buckets keyed on integer `price_ticks` (constraint C5 in `24-internal-schemas.md` §1 — floats produce phantom levels).
- `packages/backend/book_engine/publisher.py` — `BookPublisher.publish()`: emits `BookSnapshot` on subscribe and on resync, `BookDelta` thereafter, conflated to ≤50 ms (ladder) / ≤100 ms (heatmap); levels that fall outside the subscribed depth are emitted with size `0` so the client window stays exactly `depth` levels per side (`23-ws-protocol.md` §7).
- Depth-tier subscription manager: one upstream Bybit subscription per (symbol, depth) actually demanded, fanned out to N clients; unsubscribe grace window; ≤10 args per Bybit subscribe request (E08 budgeting).
- `Resyncer` completion: on gap, negative qty, or **crossed book** (best bid ≥ best ask — treated as desync, never clamped), drop the local book, emit `BookDesyncEvent`, resubscribe, buffer deltas, replay those with seq > snapshot seq.
- Binary encoder for kinds 1 and 2 wired to `packages/protocol` from E17.
- `BestQuoteEvent` emission for the DOM header (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3: bid, bid_qty, ask, ask_qty, spread_ticks, spread_bps, mid).
- Metrics and structured logs (see Observability).

## Out of scope
Heatmap columns (E21-T02); REST backfill (E21-T03); liquidity bands/refill detection (E21-T04); any frontend.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Independent depth subscriptions
  Given a client subscribes book.BTCUSDT.50 and book.BTCUSDT.200 on one connection
  Then two subscriptions exist with independent sequence counters and independent snapshots
  And each receives exactly its own depth of levels per side

Scenario: Level leaving the window
  Given a level previously inside the subscribed depth falls outside it as the top of book moves
  Then that level is sent once with size 0 and never again, so the client window stays exactly depth levels per side

Scenario: Crossed book is a desync, not a clamp
  Given applying a delta produces best bid >= best ask
  Then the engine drops the book, emits BookDesyncEvent, resubscribes and sends a fresh snapshot
  And it does not emit any conflated delta derived from the crossed state

Scenario: Depth-1 keepalive is not a book event
  Given the depth-1 topic re-sends an unchanged snapshot after 3 seconds
  Then no BookDelta, no BestQuoteEvent change and no heatmap sample are produced from it

Scenario: Conflation cadence
  Given upstream deltas arrive at 20 ms on the 50-depth topic
  Then outbound ladder frames are emitted at most every 50 ms, each carrying the merged final state, losing intermediate frames but never final state
```

## Technical notes / design
Levels held in two `SortedDict`s keyed by `price_ticks`; book memory 500 levels × 2 sides × 32 B ≈ 32 KB/symbol (`20-architecture.md` §3.2). State machine `INIT → SNAPSHOT_PENDING → LIVE → DESYNCED → SNAPSHOT_PENDING`; **`LIVE` is the only state from which derived engines consume** — E21-T02 depends on this invariant to set `estimated=True`. Conflation uses the coalescing policy of `23-ws-protocol.md` §8.2 (last-write-wins per level, whole-frame merge). Decimal↔tick conversion per constraint C5: `price_ticks = round((price - price_origin) / tick_size)`, integer form derived, Decimal authoritative.

Error codes: an unknown depth in a topic name returns `invalid_topic_format` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §10).

## Test plan
- **Property (hypothesis)**, per `03-testing-strategy.md` §"Book engine": book never negative-size after any valid delta sequence; snapshot fully resets state; replaying the same delta sequence twice from the same snapshot yields identical state; a delta with `seq` ≤ last-applied is a no-op or triggers resync; malformed/duplicate deletes do not crash.
- **Unit**: aggregation at bucket_ticks ∈ {1, 5, 25}; zero-size eviction at the depth boundary; depth-1 keepalive suppression; crossed-book detection; conflation cadence with a fake clock.
- **Integration**: replay `orderbook_snapshot_delta_*.jsonl.gz` fixture including the seeded `seq` gap and out-of-order delivery; assert exactly one `BookDesyncEvent` and a correct post-resync book.
- **Contract**: binary kind 1/2 round-trip against `ws-schemas.json` (E17's `ws_message_schemas` CI gate).
- Coverage ≥85% line / ≥75% branch on `book_engine`.

## Security notes
Subscription authorisation is `marketdata:read` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6 permission table; `04-security-program.md` RBAC row 5) and is checked server-side on every subscribe — a hand-crafted raw frame must not bypass it. Depth-500 subscriptions are the DoS surface named in `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4: this Task enforces a per-connection cap on concurrent (symbol, depth≥200) subscriptions, configurable via `ws.max_deep_book_subs` (default 4), returning a typed error rather than silently accepting. Book data itself is non-secret market data.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend.

## Performance notes
Budget #5 (sustain `orderbook.200` at 100 ms with zero dropped messages), budget #6 (≤20 ms p95 backend-added latency from book update to outbound frame) and budget #8 (≤300 MB resident per recorded symbol) of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. Per-symbol asyncio task isolation so one symbol's burst cannot starve another.

## Observability
Metrics: `book_desync_total{symbol,depth}`, `book_apply_latency_ms`, `book_publish_latency_ms`, `book_subscriptions_active{depth}`, `book_crossed_total`. Logs: structured desync event with `prev_update_id`, `got_update_id`, `resync_count`. Event `BookDesyncEvent` on bus topic `sys.md.desync` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3).

title: HeatmapEngine columns, the heatmap topic and heatmap_cells persistence
body:
## Context
The heatmap grid model is already normative in `24-internal-schemas.md` §6: a 2-D time×price grid of **resting** book size, `HeatmapColumn` and `HeatmapGridSpec` defined, colour convention locked to green=bid/red=ask by owner decision #10, log scale default because resting depth is heavy-tailed, and `clip_percentile` normalisation so one 10 000-contract wall does not black out everything else. This Task implements the `HeatmapEngine` of module **M9** (`20-architecture.md` §3.4: "Rolling (time × price) matrix; one column per 100 ms; size normalised per column; emits only the newest column as a delta"), publishes it on the frozen `heatmap.{symbol}` topic, and persists it to the `heatmap_cells` QuestDB table so backfill and replay have something to read.

The sampling contract from §6.2 is exact: the `BookEngine` holds the live L2 book; every `column_ms` the `HeatmapEngine` samples it; levels outside the price window are dropped from the column but their totals kept in `off_window_bid_qty`/`off_window_ask_qty` (rendered as edge gutters so the user knows depth exists beyond view).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/backend/orderflow/heatmap.py` — `HeatmapEngine` implementing `HeatmapGridSpec` (`column_ms` default 100, `depth` default 200, price step in ticks, window, clip percentile, lin/log).
- Incremental, checkpointable engine state (per `20-architecture.md` §3.4: no recompute from history per tick; state serialisable so a restart resumes without replaying the session).
- `estimated=True` on any column produced while the book is `Resyncing`, plus `samples` count per column; columns with `samples=0` emitted for engine stalls so the renderer can draw the grey stripe.
- WS topic `heatmap.{symbol}` with the frozen option set (`time_bucket_ms` ∈ {100,250,500,1000,5000} client-derived with server fallback 500, `price_grouping`, `depth`, `window_seconds` ≤900 default 900), binary **body_kind 6** encoding (`u32 ts_offset_ms`, `i64 price_min`, `i64 price_step`, `u32 row_count`, then `row_count` × 16 B of `u64 bid_size`, `u64 ask_size`), snapshot capped at the **2 000 most recent columns**.
- `ctl` handling: a change to `time_bucket_ms`, `price_grouping` or `depth` invalidates state → `ctl_ok` with `resnapshot: true` and an immediate fresh `snap` restarting the sequence.
- Re-bucketing rule from §6.3: when `price_step_ticks` changes, rebuild from stored native-step columns if the stored step divides the new one, otherwise rebuild the range from recorded book deltas.
- Persistence to `heatmap_cells` (`21-database-schema.md` §4.12) via the recorder's write path, respecting its 7 d hot / 90 d cold retention and the 180-day downsample policy.
- Backpressure participation: `heatmap` degrades to 1 000 ms and may be listed in `degraded_topics` when the connection is classified `saturated` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3).

## Out of scope
REST backfill endpoint (E21-T03); the client texture layer (E21-T05); liquidation heatmap (`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.4 — E24); recording the raw book (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Columns at cadence
  Given book.BTCUSDT.200 is LIVE and heatmap.BTCUSDT is subscribed with time_bucket_ms 100
  Then exactly one column is emitted per 100 ms bucket, each carrying its sample count
  And the column contains only levels inside the price window, with off-window totals carried separately

Scenario: Resync marks data estimated
  Given the book enters Resyncing after a sequence gap
  Then every column produced during that period carries estimated=true
  And those columns are excluded from any rule-engine liquidity metric

Scenario: Bucket change re-snapshots
  When the client sends ctl { time_bucket_ms: 500 } on heatmap.BTCUSDT
  Then the server answers ctl_ok with resnapshot true and immediately sends a fresh snap restarting the sequence

Scenario: Snapshot cap
  Given window_seconds is 900 at time_bucket_ms 100
  Then the snapshot carries at most the 2000 most recent columns and older columns are served by GET /market/heatmap

Scenario: Engine stall is visible
  Given the engine misses a column deadline
  Then a column with samples=0 is emitted and heatmap_missing_columns_total increments
```

## Technical notes / design
Normalisation uses `clip_percentile` of non-zero sizes over the visible columns, recomputed on viewport change; `log` is the default mapping. Analytics may use `float`/`numpy` internally (constraint C3) but values crossing into OMS/journal/audit convert at the boundary via `Decimal(str(x)).quantize(...)` — no heatmap value crosses that boundary in this Epic, which must be asserted by a boundary test. Vectorised `numpy` ops on preallocated arrays; per-symbol asyncio task consuming a coalescing bus subscription.

Bandwidth reference (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1): BTCUSDT at depth 200, `price_grouping` 1, 900 s window, ~400 populated rows/column at 4 B — the 2 000-column cap keeps a full re-snapshot inside the §16.3 budget of <700 KiB at 1 000 ms.

## Test plan
- **Golden-file** suite (mandated by `03-testing-strategy.md` §"golden-file" which names "DOM heatmap decay/normalization"): recorded fixture → engine → deterministic JSON, byte-compared (float tolerance 1e-9 relative).
- **Unit**: window clipping and off-window totals; percentile clipping with a single dominant wall; log vs linear mapping; `estimated` flag during resync; `samples=0` stall column; re-bucketing when the stored step divides / does not divide the new step.
- **Contract**: body_kind 6 round-trip and `HeatmapColumn` JSON Schema conformance via E17's CI gate.
- **Integration**: end-to-end ingestion → book → heatmap → QuestDB `heatmap_cells` → read-back.
- **Chaos**: force a book desync mid-window and assert the estimated marking and recovery.
- Coverage ≥85% line on `orderflow/heatmap`.

## Security notes
`marketdata:read` on the topic. The DoS surface: `time_bucket_ms: 100` × `window_seconds: 900` × depth 500 across many symbols is the most expensive subscription in the product — this Task enforces the server-side caps (`window_seconds` ≤900, 2 000-column snapshot cap) and reports the topic in the `most_expensive_topics` hint of the slow-consumer path (§8.4). Persisted heatmap data is market data (non-secret) but is subject to the retention policy — no unbounded growth.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend, but the column payload must carry enough information (per-level sizes, not just normalised intensity) for the client's windowed accessible reveal and data-table alternative to show real numbers rather than colours.

## Performance notes
Budget #14 (100 ms cadence sustained at 200 depth) originates here on the producer side; budget #6 (≤20 ms backend-added latency) applies per column. Engine must be O(levels in window) per column, never O(history).

## Observability
Metrics: `heatmap_missing_columns_total` (**alert above 1%/min**, per `24-internal-schemas.md` §6.3), `heatmap_column_publish_latency_ms`, `heatmap_columns_emitted_total{estimated}`, `heatmap_subscriptions_active`. Logs: re-bucketing events with old/new step and the strategy chosen.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass with an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Coverage: ≥85% line on touched backend/engine packages, ≥80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md` as touched.
- [ ] Storybook stories added/updated for every touched component variant × theme × density (if UI).
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on touched screens; manual screen-reader spot-check recorded (if UI).
- [ ] perf: benchmark recorded against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1/#14 (default-on for this Epic per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).
- [ ] security: SAST/SCA/secrets scans clean or triaged; Security engineer comment present where `security`-labelled.
- [ ] design-qa: built UI compared against the E21-D02/D03 spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo) environment.
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`engine.heatmap_renderer`, `heatmap_depth_500`).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E21-T01 (needs `LIVE` book state and the resync state machine), E17 (binary kind 6, ctl/resnapshot), E16 (recorder write path and retention for `heatmap_cells`).

## Branch
`feat/e21-heatmap-engine`.

## References
`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.1–6.3; `20-architecture.md` §3.4; `23-ws-protocol.md` §3.4 (kind 6), §6.1, §6.1.1, §8.2–8.4; `21-database-schema.md` §4.12, §7; `03-testing-strategy.md` §"golden-file".

title: GET /market/heatmap and GET /market/orderbook backfill from recorded history
body:
## Context
`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1 delegates scroll-back explicitly: "the server sends the most recent 2 000 columns in `snap` and serves anything older through REST `GET /market/heatmap` on scroll-back". US-DOM-010 requires up to 24 hours of recorded book history to load progressively, newest first, with a progress indicator, a marked boundary when only partial history exists, and prompt cancellation on symbol switch. `GET /market/orderbook` is the companion resync path: the client calls it on any sequence gap (per the endpoint's own description in `22-api-openapi.yaml`).

Both endpoints are already specified in `22-api-openapi.yaml`; this Task implements them against the storage tiers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /market/heatmap` with the specified parameters (`symbol`, `from`, `to`, `time_bucket_ms` ∈ {100,250,500,1000,5000,60000} default 1000, `price_grouping` 1..1000 default 1, `depth` ∈ {50,200,500} default 200, `normalize` ∈ {none,column,window} default window) returning `HeatmapResponse` — a dense matrix plus its axes so the engine can upload it as a texture in one step.
- Reconstruction path: read `heatmap_cells` from QuestDB for the hot window; fall back to the Parquet/DuckDB cold view for older partitions (`21-database-schema.md` §5/§6); where only `orderbook_deltas`/`orderbook_snapshots` exist (no pre-aggregated cells), reconstruct by seeking the nearest snapshot and applying deltas.
- Honour the **downsample** boundary: partitions older than 180 days are 1 s snapshots — the response must state the effective resolution rather than silently returning coarser data than requested.
- Partial-history semantics: return the actual available range and the first-available timestamp so the client can mark the boundary (US-DOM-010 "Partial history").
- Pagination/chunking suitable for progressive newest-first loading, and request cancellation handling (client aborts must release server resources promptly).
- `GET /market/orderbook` at the requested depth with its update id, used on sequence-gap resync.
- `marketdata:read` RBAC enforcement (`x-rbac` block already in the spec).

## Out of scope
The client-side backfill UX (E21-S08); recording (E16); replay seeking (E26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dense matrix response
  When GET /market/heatmap is called for a 10-minute window at time_bucket_ms 1000, depth 200
  Then the response contains a times axis, a prices axis and a dense matrix whose dimensions match those axes exactly
  And normalize=window scales cells to 0..1 over the whole window

Scenario: Partial history boundary
  Given only 3 hours of recorded book history exist but 24 hours are requested
  Then the response returns 3 hours, states the first available timestamp, and does not fabricate empty leading columns as real data

Scenario: Downsampled resolution is disclosed
  Given the requested window falls partly beyond the 180-day downsample boundary
  Then the response states the effective resolution for that segment rather than returning it as if it were native-cadence data

Scenario: No history at all
  Given the symbol has never been recorded
  Then the endpoint returns an empty matrix with an explicit "no recorded history" indication, not a 404 and not a server error

Scenario: Unauthorised
  Given a caller without marketdata:read
  Then the request is rejected with the standard authorization error and is audited
```

## Technical notes / design
Storage tiers per `21-database-schema.md`: QuestDB hot (`heatmap_cells` 7 d, `orderbook_deltas` 7 d, `orderbook_snapshots` 30 d), Parquet/DuckDB cold via the `read_parquet(... hive_partitioning=true)` views. Reconstruction from deltas seeks the nearest forced 60 s snapshot (the recorder writes these precisely so replay/backfill can seek without replaying from session start) and validates with the stored CRC32 checksum before applying deltas.

Response size guard: a 24 h × 100 ms × 500-depth request is enormous — clamp server-side by bucket coarsening with the effective resolution stated, and document the clamp in the endpoint description.

## Test plan
- **Contract**: response validates against `HeatmapResponse` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the OpenAPI contract-test gate must fail on drift.
- **Unit**: axis/matrix dimension agreement; each `normalize` mode; partial-history boundary; downsample disclosure; clamp behaviour.
- **Integration**: seed QuestDB and Parquet fixtures spanning the hot/cold boundary and assert a seamless response; reconstruct-from-deltas path validated against the checksum.
- **Perf**: p95 response time for a 1 h × 1 000 ms × 200-depth request under the realistic-peak profile.
- Coverage ≥85% on the handler package.

## Security notes
`marketdata:read` (`04-security-program.md` RBAC row 5). Threats: (a) **resource exhaustion** via a huge `from`/`to` range — mitigated by the server-side clamp and a per-user concurrent-backfill limit; (b) **path handling for archived data** — the Parquet reader must build paths from validated symbol/date parameters only, never from raw user input (this is the same class of threat `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4 names for E26). Symbol parameter validated against the instruments cache before touching the filesystem.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — API.

## Performance notes
Backfill runs off the interaction path (US-DOM-010 NFR) — the endpoint must stream/chunk rather than build the whole matrix in memory; first chunk available quickly enough for the client's ≤1 s first-useful-paint target.

## Observability
Metrics: `heatmap_backfill_requests_total{source=hot|cold|reconstructed}`, `heatmap_backfill_duration_ms`, `heatmap_backfill_clamped_total`, `orderbook_resync_fetch_total`. Logs include the resolved storage tier per request.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass with an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Coverage: ≥85% line on touched backend/engine packages, ≥80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.

title: STRIDE threat model for the DOM ladder and liquidity heatmap

## Context
`04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per Epic, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4 pre-names this Epic's headline threat: **"unbounded subscription depth as a DoS vector"**. The protocol document reinforces two load-bearing properties this Epic must not break: goal **G4** (a slow or backgrounded client can never grow server memory) and goal **G5** (server-authoritative, revocable authorisation — a manager must not be able to subscribe to another manager's accounts even by hand-crafting a raw frame).

The surface is broader than it first looks: mostly public market data, but the ladder also renders **account-scoped order and position state** (US-DOM-006), and it consumes a REST endpoint that reads **archived files from disk** (`GET /market/heatmap` over Parquet partitions).

## Scope / Deliverables

- Threats enumerated per STRIDE category with likelihood/impact and a named mitigation and owner, minimally including:
  - **S**: forged subscription frames attempting to read another account's `orders`/`positions`; session replay on reconnect.
  - **T**: tampered binary frames (inconsistent `row_count`) causing out-of-bounds reads in the decoder; manipulated settings payloads persisted as arbitrary jsonb.
  - **R**: a shed/degradation event that leaves no audit trail, so a trader's claim that "the app hid liquidity" cannot be adjudicated.
  - **I**: account-scoped markers leaking through aggregate counts; the `most_expensive_topics` hint leaking other users' activity; archived-path traversal via the backfill parameters.
  - **D**: **the named epic threat** — unbounded/deep subscriptions (depth 500 × 100 ms bucket × many symbols), oversized `from`/`to` backfill ranges, slow-consumer memory growth, heatmap column storms.
  - **E**: a `viewer` reaching recording or trading affordances through the panel's empty-state or arm-toggle surfaces.
- Mitigation mapping to existing controls (`marketdata:read` RBAC, per-connection subscription caps, `window_seconds` ≤900 and the 2 000-column snapshot cap, connection-quality classifier and `slow_consumer` close, SR-038 stale-book rule, audit logging) and identification of any **gap** requiring a new control (tracked as E21-X02).
- Abuse cases handed to QA (E21-Q04 scenario 5 already covers the slow consumer).
- Sign-off by the Security engineer with the Architect present.

## Out of scope
Implementing new controls (E21-X02); the R4 pen-test (E43); OMS/order-placement threats (E29/E31/E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model is complete and actionable
  Then every STRIDE category has at least one enumerated threat with a likelihood, an impact, a named mitigation and an owner

Scenario: The named epic threat is fully treated
  Given the roadmap names unbounded subscription depth as this Epic's DoS vector
  Then the model quantifies the worst-case cost per subscription, states the enforced caps, and names the test that proves them

Scenario: Gaps become tickets
  Given a threat has no existing control
  Then a specific ticket exists to add one, and the model links it rather than recording "to be handled later"

Scenario: Sign-off
  Then the Security engineer records a sign-off comment, and any accepted risk carries explicit Owner sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Quantify cost per subscription concretely using the protocol's own bandwidth reference (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1: BTCUSDT, depth 200, grouping 1, 900 s window, ~400 rows/column at 4 B) extrapolated to depth 500 at 100 ms, so the caps are argued from numbers rather than intuition.

Each mitigation must name its verifying test (unit, E2E, chaos or load) — a mitigation with no test is recorded as an open item, not a control.

Specifies the security-relevant telemetry required: subscription-cap rejections, slow-consumer closures, permission-denied subscribes, backfill clamps — each must be countable and alertable.

title: Spike: bubble instancing cost and LOD ladder at 5 000 visible prints
body:
## Context
US-BIG-003's NFR demands "≥55 fps with 5 000 visible bubbles; instanced rendering", while `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §LOD ladder says the bubble strategy is "Size-threshold raising as density grows; cluster into a single bubble with a count badge — **keep ≤500 visible instances**". Those two statements need reconciling *before* E22-S03 is written: either the engine can genuinely push 5 000 instanced discs inside the frame budget alongside the rest of the R2 scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + stat rows + CVD, roadmap exit criterion #2), or the LOD ladder must engage earlier and the story's AC must be expressed in terms of *qualifying prints* rather than *drawn instances*. Getting this wrong late is expensive — R2's frame budget is a hard exit gate (budgets #1, #2).

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. This spike is explicitly **not** expected to produce production-shippable code; the harness may be promoted into the benchmark suite if it proves useful.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A benchmark harness in the chart-engine package rendering N instanced SDF discs (`disc` program, per-instance radius/colour/alpha) over a realistic R2 scene on the reference hardware (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1), sweeping N ∈ {100, 500, 1 000, 2 500, 5 000, 10 000}.
- Measurements of p50/p95 frame time and fps for each N, both alone and layered on the nominal R2 scene, in Chromium and Electron.
- The point at which the LOD ladder must engage to hold ≥55 fps, and the cost of the count-badge path (SDF text) versus plain discs.
- A recommendation: the visible-instance cap, the size-threshold raising curve, and whether alpha-by-age can be done on the GPU from a per-instance timestamp (avoiding per-frame buffer rewrites).
- An ADR entry recording the decision (feeds E22-T03).

## Out of scope
Production bubble series implementation (E22-S03); tape DOM performance (E22-Q03); heatmap or footprint tuning (E21/E18).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The question is answered with numbers
  When the sweep completes on reference hardware in both Chromium and Electron
  Then a table of p50/p95 frame time and fps per instance count, alone and layered on the R2 scene, is recorded on the ticket

Scenario: A decision rule is produced
  Given the measured curve
  Then the visible-instance cap and the size-threshold raising curve are stated numerically, and E22-S03's acceptance criteria are rewritten to match before S03 enters Ready

Scenario: The budget cannot be met
  Given fewer than 55 fps even at 500 instances layered on the R2 scene
  Then the spike concludes with an explicit fallback (every-2nd-frame coalescing per 06-performance-and-load-standard.md section 6 item 3, or a reduced default density) and a risk-register update, rather than an optimistic story estimate
```

## Technical notes / design
Per-instance attributes to test: `vec2 posPx`, `float radiusPx`, `vec4 colour`, `float bornAtMs` (for GPU-side alpha decay). Compare two buffer strategies: (a) full rewrite of the instance buffer each frame, (b) ring-buffer append with a per-frame draw range, since bubbles are append-only within a window. Measure the picking cost too — the object index is "a uniform grid (64 px buckets) … radius for bubbles" (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §picking), and a 5 000-object index insertion rate is not free.

## Test plan
Benchmark only; results must be reproducible (three runs, report median) and captured in a form the CI benchmark in E22-Q03 can adopt.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
Measure the cost of the sparse DOM-mirror markers (CMP-195 contract) at the recommended cap — the mirror is affordable precisely because big trades are low-frequency, and this spike must confirm that claim at the cap, not assume it.

## Performance notes
Budgets #1 (≤16.6 ms p95) and #2 (never below 30 fps) are the pass/fail lines; report against both.

## Observability
Harness emits the same frame-time histogram shape the engine's production instrumentation uses so numbers are comparable later.

## Definition of Done
Numbers recorded; decision captured as an ADR (per DoR/DoD §5.2, even "defer" is an ADR entry); follow-up adjustments applied to E22-S03's AC and estimate; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated for R2 if the finding changes the risk; harness either promoted into the benchmark suite or explicitly marked throwaway; findings presented at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`E11` chart engine core — the `disc` program, instancing path and picking index must exist to measure.

## Branch
`spike/e22-bubble-lod`.

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-053; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-112, CMP-195, CMP-227, CMP-011, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-056.

title: STRIDE threat model for the big trades & bubbles epic
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic, and the roadmap schedules "STRIDE R2 epics [S10-S13]" as a security work stream. E22's surface looks benign — public market data — which is exactly why it needs a model: the real exposure here is **availability**, not confidentiality. An unbounded `GET /market/trades` window, a `min_size=0` subscription on a hot symbol, extreme `cluster_window_ms` values, or a client opening many `trades.*` subscriptions can exhaust backend CPU, socket buffers or per-symbol memory and degrade *every* other view, including the trading surfaces that arrive in R3. The model must land before E22-T01/T02 write their validation code, hence Sprint 10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Data-flow diagram for the epic: Bybit `publicTrade` → E08 normaliser → bus → `BigTradeEngine` (M9) → WS publisher `trades.{symbol}` / REST `/market/trades` + `/market/metrics` → shared worker → tape panel + bubble series; plus the `settings` write path for per-symbol thresholds.
- STRIDE analysis per element and per flow, with at minimum:
  - **S**poofing — unauthenticated subscription attempts; session validity on the WS handshake.
  - **T**ampering — client-supplied subscription options and `settings` values; the risk of a client-side threshold diverging from the server's (a correctness *and* trust issue, R2 §6.2's honesty goal).
  - **R**epudiation — threshold/cluster configuration changes must produce `settings.change` audit entries (global AC #2).
  - **I**nformation disclosure — market data is classification **public**; confirm no account, key or user identifier leaks into market-data frames, logs or analytics events.
  - **D**enial of service — the primary branch: unbounded REST windows, `min_size=0`, extreme cluster parameters, subscription fan-out, per-symbol memory growth, and the client-side ring buffer as a browser memory-exhaustion path.
  - **E**levation of privilege — RBAC on `marketdata:read` and on the settings endpoints; confirm a Viewer cannot write another user's settings.
- Controls mapped to concrete tickets: the documented parameter bounds (`cluster_window_ms` 0–5000, `cluster_tolerance_ticks` 0–20, `Limit`/cursor pagination), per-connection subscription caps, throttling/coalescing as load shedding, bounded engine state with a truncation metric, server-side re-validation of settings.
- Abuse cases handed to E22-X02 for execution.
- Findings recorded with severity and owner; anything not fixed requires an accepted-risk note with Owner sign-off.

## Out of scope
Executing the abuse cases (E22-X02); SAST/DAST rule authoring beyond naming what is needed; epics E21/E26 STRIDE models (their own tickets, though the unbounded-subscription-depth DoS vector is shared and should be cross-referenced).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model complete
  Then every element and flow in the diagram has been assessed against all six STRIDE categories, with "not applicable" stated with a reason rather than left blank

Scenario: Controls are actionable
  Then each identified threat maps to a named control and a ticket key that implements or verifies it

Scenario: An unmitigated threat
  Given a threat with no practical control inside R2
  Then it is recorded in docs/plan/32-risk-register.md with a severity, an owner and an explicit Owner sign-off of the accepted risk
```

## Technical notes / design
Cross-reference E21's STRIDE, which covers "unbounded subscription depth as a DoS vector" (roadmap §6.4) — the mitigation should be a shared subscription-budget mechanism, not two separate ad hoc caps. Note explicitly that big-trade evaluation is **exact, not estimated** (Bybit gives the aggressor side directly), whereas `trade_cluster` is **estimated** — the honesty badge is a trust control and belongs in the model.

## Test plan
Model review with the Architect and the M9 owner; each control gets a verification method named (unit test, contract test, abuse case in X02, or load test in Q03).

## Security notes
This ticket is the security deliverable. Data classification for everything in this epic: **public** market data plus **internal** user settings. No secrets, no PII, no financial account data flows through E22 surfaces — confirm that claim rather than assuming it.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Several controls are load-shedding mechanisms; coordinate their thresholds with the budgets in E22-Q03 so a security control does not itself break budget #3.

## Observability
Require the counters that make abuse visible: `ws_subscribe_rejected_total{reason}`, `bigtrade_state_truncated_total`, per-connection subscription gauge, REST request-size histogram.

## Definition of Done
Model document merged in the security area and linked from this ticket; findings triaged with owners and ticket keys; accepted risks recorded in `32-risk-register.md` with Owner sign-off; Security engineer sign-off comment; handed to E22-X02.

## Dependencies

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-053; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-112, CMP-195, CMP-227, CMP-011, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-056.

title: UX research: how traders read cumulative delta and divergence
body:
## Context
SCR-052 is scheduled on the **D-S07** design sprint (2026-11-06 -> 2026-11-12, "CVD/derivatives panes, detector badges + (estimated) pattern", `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§1.2) and consumed by engineering in E23-S01..S05. Before wireframes, the design org must establish how the personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md` actually read a CVD pane, because two of this epic's decisions are genuinely contested and must not be guessed: (a) which **reset anchor** is the sane default, and (b) how strongly a **divergence marker** may be presented before it reads as a trade signal â€” the R9 advice-boundary risk in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

This is new interaction territory for the product: US-CVD-002's manual anchor ("click a bar and choose *anchor CVD here*") is a novel affordance that does not exist on any other pane, and US-CVD-005's swing-divergence connector is the first cross-pane geometric annotation (it links price-pane swings to CVD-pane swings).

## Scope / Deliverables
- 4-6 moderated sessions with order-flow traders (the Owner plus recruited proxies) walking through recorded BTCUSDT footage of SCR-052 behaviour.
- Findings on: default reset anchor (`session` vs `utc_day` vs `never`); mental model of "CVD candles" (US-CVD-003) vs line vs histogram and when each is preferred; whether smoothing should default on or off; how a divergence should be *labelled* so it reads as an observation, not advice; expectations for the manual-anchor gesture and its discoverability.
- A written recommendation for the **(estimated)** copy on divergence markers, feeding the epic-wide CMP-227 EstimatedBadge popover text.
- Prioritised list of states that must be designed (D02 input), including the recorder-dependent partial-history state and the stale-data state.
- Research report in the design repo, linked from SCR-052 in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.

## Out of scope
Wireframes and hi-fi comps (D02/D03), motion (D04), engineering, and any research on the derivatives pane SCR-054 (E24) or detector badges (E25) beyond sharing the `(estimated)` copy pattern.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Defaults are evidence-backed
  When the report is reviewed
  Then the recommended default reset anchor, display mode and smoothing setting each cite at least two participant observations
  And any recommendation contradicted by a participant records the dissent and the rationale for overriding it

Scenario: The advice boundary is addressed
  Then the report proposes divergence label copy and popover copy that describes what was measured and what could make it wrong
  And the proposal is reviewed against the R9 advice-boundary risk with the Owner

Scenario: The manual anchor gesture is validated
  Given participants are asked to re-anchor CVD at a chosen bar without instruction
  Then the report records the discovery rate and the gestures attempted
  And recommends the primary affordance plus at least one keyboard-reachable alternative
```

## Technical notes / design
Use recorded footage rather than a live feed so all participants see the same market conditions; include one high-volatility burst and one thin-book period so the divergence-heuristic failure modes are visible. Capture the exact wording participants use for "CVD" and "delta" â€” the legend copy should match their vocabulary, not the codebase's.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validity controls: a fixed discussion guide, two observers per session, findings tagged to participant IDs, and a synthesis review with the CDO.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
Recruit at least one participant using a high-contrast or CVD-safe theme; record whether the delta sign was read from colour or from the numeric sign, which directly validates the "never colour alone" rule in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Report published in the design repo and linked from SCR-052
- [ ] Recommendations reviewed by the CDO and the Owner
- [ ] The states list is handed to E23-D02 as a checklist
- [ ] The `(estimated)` copy proposal is shared with E24 and E25 for pattern consistency

## Dependencies
`E18` â€” footprint research already established how traders read per-bar bid/ask aggression; this study builds on it rather than re-asking those questions.

`design/cvd-research` (design repo). No code PR.

title: Wireframe SCR-052 CVD / delta panel with every state
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-052 sketches the panel as a header of controls (`reset [session v]  smooth [EMA 9 v]  [div x]`), a CVD line, a per-bar delta histogram sharing the time axis, and a divergence text line ("price HH / CVD LH at 13:42 (flag)"). It names four states â€” **loading, streaming, reset-marker shown, recorded-history limited** â€” and the epic adds a fifth from the roadmap exit criteria: **stale data** (shaded after 2 s). This ticket turns that sketch plus the D01 findings into a complete low-fidelity specification covering every state and every control.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes for SCR-052 covering: loading; streaming (nominal); reset-marker shown (session/utc_day/manual anchors, each with its marker treatment); **recorded-history limited** (explicit partial-history state naming the first available timestamp, roadmap R2 exit criterion 5); stale data (>2 s without an update); empty (no recorded tape for the symbol); error (metrics subscription rejected); CVD-candles mode **disabled** because tick data is absent (US-CVD-003 NFR requires an explanation, not a silent absence).
- Layout of the two stacked series (CVD series above, per-bar delta histogram below) with the **shared time axis aligned to the price chart** (CMP-189 TimeAxis) and the CVD value axis (CMP-188 PriceAxis) â€” including how the zero line of the delta histogram is drawn.
- Control specification: reset anchor select (session / UTC day / never / manual), display mode (line / histogram / candlestick), smoothing (off / EMA n), divergence toggle with lookback, and the legend (CMP-199) contents showing the **active parameters** (required by US-CVD-005 scenario 3).
- Divergence presentation: the single-bar glyph + text label (US-CVD-004) and the multi-bar swing connector between the two swing pairs with a label (US-CVD-005), each with the CMP-227 `(estimated)` chip and popover.
- Crosshair/tooltip content (CMP-190/CMP-197): time, bar delta, CVD value, smoothed value, divergence flag.
- The **accessible table alternative** entry point in the panel header and its tabular layout (time, delta, CVD, divergence).
- Hatched treatment for bars covered by an ingestion gap (US-CVD-001 scenario 3: "affected bars are drawn hatched and excluded from derived metrics") and the provisional styling of the forming bar.
- Annotated redlines describing behaviour, not just appearance.

## Out of scope
Token-accurate colour and type (D03), motion (D04), the composite multi-symbol variant (deferred with US-CVD-006 to R5 â€” sketch one exploratory frame only, clearly marked "R5, not for build").

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state is drawn
  When the wireframe set is reviewed against the SCR-052 states list plus stale-data, empty, error and candles-disabled
  Then each state has a frame, and each frame states its trigger condition and its exit condition

Scenario: Partial history is explicit
  Given the recorder holds data only from 09:12 for the requested range
  Then the frame shows a persistent banner naming 09:12 as the first available timestamp
  And the CVD series is visually truncated at that point rather than starting from zero at the range start

Scenario: Divergence never reads as advice
  Then every divergence treatment carries a text label and the (estimated) chip
  And the popover content is drawn, not deferred to engineering to invent

Scenario: The provisional bar is unmistakable
  Given the forming bar is in progress
  Then its delta bar is styled as provisional and is drawn as never flagged for divergence
```

## Technical notes / design
Respect the engine's pane model (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`: `<Pane heightRatio={0.2}><CvdSeries data={cvd} /></Pane>`) â€” the CVD pane is a sibling pane of the price pane sharing one time axis, not an overlay. Do not design anything requiring per-tick reflow of the time axis; axis alignment is owned by the host chart.

## Test plan
Design review with the CDO, an engineer from `area/order-flow` and QA (feasibility + testability). QA confirms every state has an observable trigger they can drive in a test.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
Wireframes must show the focus order through the header controls, the table-alternative entry point, and how a keyboard user reaches and reads a divergence event as text. Nothing may depend on hue alone: the delta sign appears as a numeric sign and the histogram direction.

## Performance notes
Flag any treatment that would force a full-series recomputation on a settings change â€” divergence detection must run incrementally on bar close (SCR-052 performance note), so a design implying a full re-scan per keystroke is a defect at this stage, not at build time.

## Observability
Specify where the analytics events `cvd.interval_changed`, `cvd.mode_changed`, `cvd.divergence_marker_clicked` and `cvd.anchor_set` fire in the interaction flow.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states drawn, annotated and reviewed
- [ ] Engineering feasibility review recorded
- [ ] QA confirms every state is drivable in a test
- [ ] Handed to E23-D03

## Dependencies
`E23-D01` â€” the default anchor, display mode and divergence-copy recommendations are inputs to these frames.

`design/cvd-wireframes` (design repo).

CMP-185's contract is already sketched in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`: tier *chart-primitive*; props `data: CvdPoint[]`, `displayMode: "candlestick"|"histogram"|"line"`, `resetAnchor: "session"|"day"|"never"|"manual"`, `divergenceMarkers?: boolean`; tokens `color.text.buy/sell`; Storybook stories Histogram, Line, Candlestick, WithDivergenceMarkers; tests unit, visual, axe, performance.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi comps for every SCR-052 state from D02, in **light, dark, high-contrast and the CVD-safe (deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia) themes** listed in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR settings, at both the compact and comfortable densities.
- Token spec: every colour, spacing, radius, stroke width and type value resolved to a named token from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`. **No raw hex.** Missing values are contributed as new tokens with a name, a value, a rationale and a design-system changelog entry.
- **CMP-185 design-system entry**, specifying: the three display modes (line, histogram, candlestick) including how CVD-candle bodies/wicks are drawn from intrabar cumulative delta (`min_delta`/`max_delta`); the zero-line treatment of the delta histogram; the reset-anchor marker (a vertical rule plus a label carrying the anchor timestamp, distinct per anchor kind); the smoothing overlay drawn **on top of** the raw series, never replacing it; the provisional-bar treatment; the gap-hatched bar treatment; the single-bar divergence glyph and the multi-bar swing connector; the stale-data shading; and the legend row contents.
- Redline of the four named Storybook stories so E23-S01/S03/S05 implement them as a transcription.
- Colour-blind verification of the buy/sell (positive/negative delta) pair under all three simulations, proving distinguishability without hue.

## Out of scope
Motion timings and transitions (D04); the handoff pack (D05); any engineering work.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Token-pure comps
  When the hi-fi frames are inspected
  Then every colour, spacing, radius, stroke and type value resolves to a named design token
  And any new token carries a name, a value, a rationale and a design-system changelog entry

Scenario: Colour-blind safe
  Given the positive and negative delta treatments
  When simulated under deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia

Scenario: Contrast holds in every theme

```

## Technical notes / design
Specify the **CVD-candle construction** unambiguously so engineering does not invent it: within a bar, open = cumulative delta at bar open, high = `cvd_open + max_delta`, low = `cvd_open + min_delta`, close = `cvd_open + delta` â€” this is exactly the intrabar path tracked by bar invariant BI-3 (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`). Also define the stroke-width and opacity ladder the engine should use when the pane is short (`heightRatio` as low as 0.12) so the series stays legible without re-designing.

## Test plan
Design review plus a Storybook parity checklist that E23-S01/S03/S05 must satisfy (Histogram, Line, Candlestick, WithDivergenceMarkers). Contrast values captured with a contrast checker and recorded in the comp annotations.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
Comps must include the focus-visible treatment of every header control and the rendered table alternative. Contrast ratios are annotated per element. The `(estimated)` chip must be legible at the smallest supported font scale (100%) and at 150%.

## Performance notes
The comps must not imply per-frame text layout in the series area: labels are limited to the legend, the anchor marker and the divergence labels, all of which change at most on bar close. Anything implying per-tick glyph layout breaks the <=2 ms CPU pane budget and must be redesigned here.

title: Spike: intrabar CVD OHLC cost and 1M-print recompute inside 2 s
body:
## Context
Two NFRs in `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` Â§13 are quantitative and neither is obviously achievable without measurement:

- **US-CVD-002 NFR:** "recomputation from stored prints for **1M prints <=2 s**" â€” this is the reconnect-repair and anchor-change path (E23-T03).
- **US-CVD-003 NFR:** "intrabar CVD OHLC **requires tick data**; without it the mode is disabled with an explanation" â€” so we must establish exactly when tick data is and is not available, and what the per-bar cost of tracking the intrabar path is.

A spike is warranted because the answer determines whether the recompute runs in the request path (simple) or must be pushed to a background job with a "repairing" UI state (a materially different design for E23-T03 and E23-S02), and because the choice of query engine (QuestDB hot tier vs DuckDB over Parquet, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md`) for the recompute is not yet settled for this query shape.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A timed benchmark of CVD recomputation over **1,000,000 recorded prints** for a single symbol, run three ways: (a) QuestDB aggregate query over `trades`; (b) DuckDB over the Parquet cold tier; (c) a streaming Python fold over rows pulled in batches. Report p50/p95 wall time, peak RSS, and CPU.
- A measurement of the marginal cost of tracking the **intrabar path** (`min_delta`/`max_delta`, bar invariant BI-3) versus endpoint-only delta, per 100k prints, in the bar-builder hot loop.
- A written determination of when CVD-candle mode (US-CVD-003) must be **disabled**: the precise condition in terms of recorded stream availability (`recorded_symbols.streams` contains `trades`) and the requested range versus the recorder's first available timestamp.
- A recommendation for E23-T03: in-request recompute vs background repair, with the crossover print count.
- Whether `orderflow_metrics.cvd` / `cvd_session` (1 s cadence, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` Â§4.11) can serve as a **checkpoint** to bound recompute work â€” i.e. recompute only from the last persisted 1 s sample rather than from the anchor â€” and what error, if any, that introduces.
- Findings written up as a spike report and folded into ADR-0017 (E23-T05).

## Out of scope
Building the production engine (E23-T01), the repair path (E23-T03), or any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  When the 1M-print recompute benchmark is run on the reference hardware defined in 06-performance-and-load-standard.md section 3.1
  Then the report states, for each of the three approaches, whether p95 <= 2 s
  And names the recommended approach with its measured margin

Scenario: The candles precondition is defined
  Then the report states the exact machine-checkable condition under which CVD-candle mode is available
  And the condition is expressed in terms of recorded_symbols.streams and the recorder's first available timestamp

Scenario: The checkpoint question is answered
  Given the orderflow_metrics 1 s samples
  Then the report states whether recompute may start from the last sample instead of the anchor
  And quantifies any resulting deviation against a full recompute over the same window, or proves it is exact

Scenario: A negative result is still a result
  Given no approach achieves p95 <= 2 s for 1M prints
  Then the report recommends the background-repair design with a concrete UI contract for the repairing state
  And E23-T03 and E23-S02 are updated before Sprint 12 planning
```

## Technical notes / design
Use a real recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day from the E16 recorder as the fixture (a synthetic uniform tape understates the cost â€” real prints cluster). Run on the reference hardware of `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§3.1 so numbers are comparable with other budgets. Measure cold and warm cache separately; the reconnect path will usually be warm for the hot tier and cold for Parquet.

Delta per print is `+qty` when `side == "Buy"` (taker bought) and `-qty` when `side == "Sell"`, per the `TradeEvent` mapping in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`; the intrabar path requires folding prints in timestamp order and tracking the running min and max of the cumulative intrabar sum, which is why it cannot be expressed as a pure SQL aggregate without a window function â€” quantify that difference explicitly.

## Test plan
The benchmark harness itself is the deliverable artifact and is checked into `bench/orderflow/cvd_recompute_bench.py` so E23-Q03 can reuse it.
