No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes

The benchmark emits timings in the same metric names the production path will use (`cv_cvd_recompute_seconds`) so the dashboards are pre-validated.

title: STRIDE threat model for the CVD & delta panes epic
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a **STRIDE threat model per epic**, produced before implementation so its controls are requirements rather than retrofits. E23 handles no credentials and no order entry, so its risk profile is narrow but not empty: it introduces a **server-side recomputation triggered by client-controlled parameters** and a **fan-out subscription whose cost scales with the client's option choices**. Both are resource-amplification surfaces, and the R2 security gate already flags "unbounded subscription depth as a DoS vector" for E21 â€” the same class of issue appears here in a different shape.

The model must be written before E23-T01 and E23-T02, which is why it is scheduled in Sprint 10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model over the epic's data flows: Bybit `publicTrade` -> ingestion -> M9 aggregation -> `CvdEngine` -> `orderflow_metrics` (QuestDB) / Parquet -> `metrics.{symbol}` fan-out and `GET /market/metrics` -> the SCR-052 pane.
- Per-element analysis with, at minimum, these threats enumerated and rated:
  - **(D)** Subscription amplification: `metrics.{symbol}` with 12 metrics x many symbols x minimum `throttle_ms` multiplying backend CPU and egress.
  - **(D)** Recompute amplification: a client repeatedly changing the anchor (or setting distant manual anchors) forcing large historical scans over QuestDB and Parquet.
  - **(D)** Repair storm amplification: an upstream that flaps driving unbounded repair work.
  - **(D)** Unbounded range: `from`/`to` on `/market/metrics` spanning the entire retention window.
  - **(T)** Parameter tampering: `manual_anchor_ts`, smoothing period, swing lookback and the `params` JSON (max 2048 chars) used unvalidated in query construction or as allocation sizes.
  - **(T)** Malformed `params` JSON as a parser-level attack surface.
  - **(I)** RBAC: confirm `marketdata:read` is enforced on every new code path, including the WS subscribe path, and that a Viewer role sees market data but cannot cause a recompute if that is the intended boundary.
  - **(R)** Repudiation: whether anchor changes and recompute triggers need audit entries (market-data reads are not audited in general; a decision is required and recorded).
  - **(S)** Spoofing is out of scope for this epic (no new authentication surface) â€” recorded explicitly as considered and dismissed with a reason.
- Controls mapped to the tickets that must implement them: clamps and caps in E23-T02, the print clamp and coalescing queue in E23-T03, the client-side pre-validation in E23-S02.
- Abuse cases handed to E23-X02 for execution and to E23-Q06 for the chaos overlap.
- Data classification statement: market data, internal, no PII, no secrets â€” and the consequent handling rules for fixtures (E23-T04's golden fixtures must contain no account or key material).

## Out of scope
Implementation of controls (the referenced tickets), penetration testing (R4, E43), the book/DOM subscription model (E21's own model).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The model covers every element of the flow
  When the model is reviewed against the data-flow diagram
  Then every process, data store, data flow and trust boundary has a STRIDE analysis
  And every threat has a rating and either a control or an explicit accepted-risk record

Scenario: Controls become requirements
  Then each control names the ticket that implements it and the acceptance criterion that proves it
  And no control is left assigned to the epic in general

Scenario: Amplification is quantified, not just named
  Given the subscription and recompute amplification threats
  Then the model states the worst-case resource multiplier for each
  And the chosen clamp values are justified against it

Scenario: Dismissals are recorded
  Given a STRIDE category judged not applicable
  Then the model records the category, the judgement and the reason
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the data-flow diagram from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` as the base and annotate the M9 CVD path; do not draw a new architecture. Trust boundaries that matter: browser -> API/WS gateway (untrusted input), application -> QuestDB/Parquet (query construction), ingestion -> application (untrusted upstream â€” Bybit is not an attacker but it is not a guarantee either).

Clamp values should be derived from the measurements in E23-K01 where they exist, so `max_recompute_prints` is a number with a basis rather than a round figure.

## Test plan
The model is reviewed by the security engineer and the architect. Its outputs are testable by construction: each control's acceptance criterion is asserted in the implementing ticket, and the abuse cases are executed in E23-X02 and E23-Q06.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
The clamps this model mandates directly bound the epic's worst-case resource use; they must be set so that legitimate use (a full trading day at 1-minute bars, a manual anchor anywhere in the loaded range) is never refused. A control that blocks normal use will be disabled in production and is therefore not a control.

## Observability
Mandates the rejection and refusal counters (`cv_metrics_subscription_rejected_total{reason}`, `cv_cvd_recompute_refused_total{reason}`) and requires that refusals are logged with enough context to distinguish an attack from a misconfigured client.

- [ ] Controls assigned to E23-T02, E23-T03, E23-S02 with acceptance criteria

title: UX research: how perp traders read OI, funding and liquidations
body:
## Context
SCR-054 packs four semantically different derivative signals (positioning, carry, forced flow and the spot/perp spread) into one narrow panel. Before wireframing we need evidence on the questions traders actually ask of those numbers, so the panel is ordered by decision value rather than by data availability. The epic covers US-DERIV-001..008 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §14) and the panel is the only home screen for all eight.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 4-5 moderated sessions with the Owner and the account managers (the only real users - `docs/plan/10-personas.md`), using a recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day that contains a funding settlement and a liquidation cascade.
- Probe: absolute OI vs OI delta as the default view; whether quadrant classification (`long_buildup|short_covering|short_buildup|long_unwind`) is understood without a legend; what the funding countdown must say at <5 min; whether liquidation bars or a feed is the primary surface; whether the basis pane is a peer pane or a header readout.
- Probe the honesty affordances: does the partial-history chip ("history starts <ts>") actually stop mis-reads, and does the `(estimated)` badge on liquidation zones read as a warning or as decoration.
- Deliverable: a research brief in Figma/Confluence with prioritised findings, a recommended default pane order and default settings values for the `deriv.*` keys, and 3-5 explicit design implications carried into E24-D02.

## Out of scope
Visual design, tokens, prototypes; detector methodology copy (SCR-058 is E25's home but this epic adds its liquidation-cluster section, drafted in E24-K01); research on CVD/footprint panes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sessions completed
  Given the recorded symbol-day fixture with a funding settlement and a cascade
  When 4 or more sessions have been run
  Then a research brief exists with prioritised findings and a recommended default pane order

Scenario: Defaults are evidence-backed
  When the brief recommends default values for deriv.oi.mode, deriv.funding.annualised, deriv.liq.mode and deriv.liq.min_notional_usd
  Then each recommendation cites at least one observed session behaviour

Scenario: Honesty affordances tested
  When participants are shown the partial-history chip and the (estimated) badge
  Then the brief records whether each was noticed and correctly interpreted
  And any participant who read an estimated zone as exchange data is recorded as a blocking finding for E24-D03

Scenario: No participants available
  Given the Owner and managers cannot be scheduled inside the sprint
  Then the brief is produced from a heuristic walkthrough of TradingView/Coinglass equivalents with the limitation stated on its first page, and the ticket is still closed rather than blocking E24-D02
```

## Technical notes / design
Method: think-aloud over a clickable static fixture (no live data, no build dependency). Record with consent; store notes in the design repo, no account data captured. Synthesis uses affinity mapping; findings are tagged with the US id they affect so E24-D02 can trace each wireframe decision back to a finding.

## Test plan
N/A - research artefact. Validation is the CDO review of the brief.

## Security notes
No production data, no credentials and no account identifiers are captured; recordings contain public market data only and are deleted after synthesis per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` data-handling rules.

## Accessibility notes
The research explicitly includes one pass with the panel's table alternative and keyboard-only operation, so accessibility is a design input rather than a retrofit (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §11.3).

N/A

## Observability
N/A - no runtime component.

- [ ] CDO review comment recorded.

title: Wireframe SCR-054 derivatives panel with every state
body:
## Context
SCR-054 (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md#scr-054`) is a panel of three individually collapsible sub-panes (OI, funding, liquidations) plus the basis readout of US-DERIV-008. Its catalogue entry already fixes the ASCII layout, the settings set and the state list; this ticket turns that into wireframes covering every state so engineering never has to invent one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes (low fidelity, greyscale) for SCR-054: default layout, each sub-pane collapsed, OI absolute vs delta, quadrant colouring on/off, funding stepped-line vs bars, annualised toggle, liquidation bars vs heatmap, basis sub-readout with `last|mark` source selector.
- Every state named in the catalogue entry: loading · partial (liquidation history limited to recorder uptime, explicit chip naming the first available timestamp) · countdown running · next-funding imminent (<5 min warning with the estimated charge line) · stale-data shading (>2 s without an expected update, per global convention #4) · backfill-failed retry state carrying `last_success_at` (US-DERIV-008 scenario 3) · no-OI-for-bar neutral hatch (US-DERIV-002 scenario 3) · predicted-rate `n/a` (US-DERIV-004 scenario 3) · empty (symbol never recorded).
- The settings surface for the `deriv.*` keys and the acknowledgement dialog required before liquidation zones can be enabled (US-DERIV-007 scenario 3).
- The table alternative for each sub-pane (the DOM-mirror pattern) drawn as a real layout, not a note.
- Placement of CMP-227 EstimatedBadge on the zones overlay and on the predicted funding value, each linking SCR-058.

## Out of scope
Hi-fi visuals, tokens, motion (E24-D03/D04); the SCR-058 methodology copy itself (E24-K01 drafts it); chart-engine pane chrome owned by E11/E12.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue state is drawn
  Given the state list in 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-054
  When the wireframe set is reviewed
  Then each listed state has a frame, and each of the four additional states named in this ticket's scope has a frame

Scenario: Partial history is unmistakable
  When the partial-history frame is reviewed
  Then it names the first available timestamp in words and states that no exchange history endpoint exists for liquidations

Scenario: Estimated zones cannot be enabled silently
  When the liquidation-zone toggle frame is reviewed
  Then an acknowledgement step precedes enabling, and every zone in the enabled frame carries an (estimated) badge

Scenario: Table alternative exists per sub-pane
  When the accessibility frames are reviewed
  Then each of the OI, funding and liquidation sub-panes has a drawn table alternative with column headers and units

Scenario: Narrow panel
  Given the panel is docked at its minimum supported width
  Then a compact variant is drawn in which no figure loses its unit or its side label
```

## Technical notes / design
Work in Figma against the E05 design-system v0 library. Reuse CMP-036 KeyValueRow for readouts, CMP-126 FundingCountdown, CMP-199 ChartLegend for the per-pane legend and CMP-188 PriceAxis for the shared axis. Do not invent new atoms: anything that does not exist must be raised as a design-system contribution in E24-D03.

## Test plan
Review-based: CDO + chart-engine lead + a QA representative walk the frame set against the catalogue state list and the eight DERIV stories. Findings tracked as comments resolved before sign-off.

## Security notes
No security surface; but the frames must not imply that estimated or predicted values are exchange-provided, which is the epic's principal integrity threat (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, tampering/misrepresentation).

## Accessibility notes
Frames must show focus order, the keyboard path to every control, the table alternatives, and the text (not colour) encoding of quadrant classification and liquidation side (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Frames must reflect the coalescing behaviour: the liquidation surface shows aggregated 250 ms buckets with a burst counter, never a per-print row list, so the design cannot imply an unachievable render model.

N/A

title: STRIDE threat model for the derivatives metrics epic
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE model per epic before implementation. E24 carries no secrets and no PII - it is public market data end to end - so the interesting threats are **tampering/misrepresentation** (an inferred number presented as exchange fact) and **denial of service** (unbounded history queries and subscription fan-out), not confidentiality.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Data-flow diagram covering: Bybit public WS (`tickers`, `allLiquidation`) -> M4 ingestion/normalisation -> QuestDB (`tickers`, `open_interest`, `funding_rates`, `liquidations`) -> M9 `DerivativesEngine` -> REST (`/market/open-interest`, `/market/funding`, `/market/liquidations`, `/market/metrics`) and WS (`ticker.{symbol}`, `liquidations.{symbol}`) -> SCR-054.
- STRIDE enumeration per trust boundary with a rating and a named mitigation owner-ticket for every threat.
- Specific threats to model: (S) a spoofed or malformed upstream frame accepted without schema validation; (T) predicted funding or an estimated zone rendered without its flag - the flag lost anywhere between engine, schema, transport and DOM; (T) a `ws_ticker`-sourced OI point silently mixed with a `rest` point at a different granularity; (R) no record of which source a displayed value came from; (I) the endpoints losing their `marketdata:read` `x-rbac` requirement; (D) unbounded `from`/`to` or `limit` on the three history endpoints, a `liquidations` subscription over the 40-symbol cap, and a cascade amplifying fan-out to every connected client; (E) no privileged operation exists in this epic - to be asserted, not assumed.
- Abuse-case list handed to E24-X02 and to E24-Q01.

## Out of scope
Implementation of mitigations (the engineering tickets own them); pen-testing (pre-R4); threat models of other epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model produced
  Then a DFD with trust boundaries and a STRIDE table exist, reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect

Scenario: Every threat has a disposition
  When the table is reviewed
  Then each threat is either mitigated by a named ticket, accepted with an Owner sign-off, or transferred, with no blank rows

Scenario: The estimated-flag path is traced end to end
  Then the model traces the estimated and predicted flags from the engine through the JSON schema, the WS envelope and the component props to the rendered badge, and names the test that proves the flag cannot be dropped

Scenario: DoS bounds are numeric
  Then the model states the maximum range, page size and subscription symbol count for each endpoint and topic, matching the caps in 22-api-openapi.yaml and 23-ws-protocol.md

Scenario: Elevation asserted absent
  Then the model explicitly records that no operation in this epic is state-changing or privileged, so escalation has no surface here
```

## Technical notes / design
Follow the STRIDE template in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Reuse the market-data trust boundaries already modelled for E17/E08 rather than redrawing them; this model adds only the derivatives-specific flows. Data classification: public market data (lowest tier) - record that explicitly so later reviewers do not over-scope controls.

## Test plan
The model's assertions become test obligations: flag preservation becomes a contract test in E24-T04; the DoS bounds become negative tests in E24-Q01 and E24-X02.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security artefact; sign-off by the Security engineer is the exit condition.

## Accessibility notes
N/A

## Performance notes
DoS analysis must reference budget #13 (API read p95 <150 ms) so a mitigation is not itself a performance regression.

## Observability
Names the security-relevant signals to emit: rejected oversized range requests, subscription-cap rejections, upstream schema-validation failures.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] DFD + STRIDE table complete and reviewed.
- [ ] Every threat dispositioned with a ticket or an accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] Abuse cases handed to E24-X02 and E24-Q01.
- [ ] Test obligations recorded on the owning engineering tickets.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment recorded.

title: UX research: how traders read speed, imbalance and estimated signals
body:
## Context
E25 introduces five new surfaces (SCR-055..059) whose value depends entirely on whether the owner and the account managers *believe and correctly interpret* them. Two interaction problems are genuinely new to the product and are not answered anywhere in the existing design system:

1. **How is an estimate communicated without being either ignored or over-trusted?** R2 exit criterion #4 makes the `(estimated)` badge mandatory, and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` calls presenting a heuristic as certainty "a defect". But a badge that everyone learns to ignore fails the same requirement in practice. SCR-058's analytics deliberately track `methodology.opened` "so we can tell whether the honesty affordance is actually used" - this research sets the baseline expectation for that metric.
2. **What does a trader do with a regime label?** R9 (advice boundary) means the panel must read as classification-with-evidence. Whether real users read it that way is an empirical question.

Scheduled in Sprint 10, two sprints ahead of the consuming FE stories in Sprint 13, per the design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`: "Design runs ahead of engineering by >=2 sprints; no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off").

## Scope / Deliverables
- Research plan and 4-6 sessions with the owner and the account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`), each 45-60 minutes, using clickable prototypes or competitor tools as stimulus.
- Topics: reading speed-of-tape (gauge vs strip vs number; which window is the default mental model); scanning for imbalance stacks (list-first vs chart-first); interpreting a regime badge (does it read as advice?); comprehension of `(estimated)` (unprompted interpretation of the badge, then of the drawer).
- A comprehension test: show a stop-run marker with no explanation; ask what it means and how much the participant would trust it; then show SCR-058's content and re-ask.
- Findings report with prioritised design implications, verbatim quotes, and explicit recommendations for: the default window on SCR-055, list-vs-chart primacy on SCR-056, the wording of the regime badge, and the placement/affordance strength of the estimated badge.
- A recommended baseline target for the `methodology.opened` rate so the analytics have a yardstick.
- Handover briefing to the designers of D02-D04.

## Out of scope
Wireframes and visual design (D02-D04), usability testing of the built product (E25-D08 design QA / E25-Q04), quantitative A/B testing (no user base for it), any research on Android or a separate admin app (both out of scope for the plan).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sessions completed
  Given the research plan is approved
  Then at least four sessions are run with the owner and account-manager personas and are recorded with consent

Scenario: The estimated badge is tested for comprehension, not preference
  Then the report states, per participant, what they believed the badge meant before reading the drawer and after
  And it recommends a badge treatment supported by that evidence

Scenario: The advice boundary is tested
  Given participants are shown a regime badge
  Then the report states whether any participant read it as an instruction to trade
  And recommends wording that removes that reading

Scenario: Actionable implications
  Then every finding is paired with a concrete design implication assigned to D02, D03 or D04
  And the report names the default tape window, the SCR-056 primacy decision and the badge treatment

Scenario: Timely
  Then the report is published before the end of Sprint 10 so D02 can start on its findings
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the existing prototypes and, where nothing exists, competitor stimuli (the order-flow tools named in the research digests) rather than describing features verbally - verbal descriptions of an "estimated" signal produce agreement, not comprehension. Ask participants to think aloud while interpreting, and never ask "is this clear?" - ask them to explain it back.

Consent and recording per the research practice already used in the project; recordings stay in the internal research store.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Quality bar: findings are traceable to session evidence (timestamped quotes), and the report distinguishes observation from interpretation from recommendation.

## Security notes
Session recordings may capture participants' personal trading context and account details - classify as confidential, store in the internal research location only, redact account identifiers and balances from the published report, and never include real API credentials or screenshots containing them.

## Accessibility notes
Include at least one session run entirely with keyboard navigation and, if a participant with relevant assistive-technology experience is available, a screen-reader-led session; feed findings into D06.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
Recommends the baseline for the `methodology.opened{detector}` analytics event that SCR-058 emits.

## Definition of Done
Research plan approved; sessions run and recorded; findings report published and reviewed with the Chief Design Officer and the product owner; implications assigned to D02/D03/D04 as explicit checklist items; briefing delivered; report linked from this epic.

## Dependencies
None blocking. Informs D02, D03, D04 and D06.

title: Design-system contribution: detector components and the estimated badge
body:
## Context
Five components in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` are introduced or materially extended by this epic, and one of them - **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** - is load-bearing for a release exit criterion. CMP-069 InfoPanel's catalogue entry defines it as "the linked methodology drawer referenced by **every** '(estimated)' chip (CMP-011 estimated variant) - explains heuristic detector logic in plain language", and CMP-134 DetectorEventCard's a11y note makes the estimated chip **mandatory** on the card.

If these components are specified once, correctly, every surface in E25 (and E18, E21, E22's clustering, E24) inherits the honesty behaviour for free. If they are not, each surface reimplements it and one of them will get it wrong - which R2 classifies as a P1 bug.

Sprint 10, ahead of D03/D04 which compose them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**: canonical spec - variants (inline chip, marker affordance, section header), sizes, tokens, the required `onOpenMethodology(detector)` binding, and the rule that it is never purely decorative and never colour-only.
- **CMP-131 SpeedOfTapeGauge** and **CMP-187 SpeedOfTapePane**: props (`windowSec`, side split, threshold classification string, z-score, warming-up state), states and tokens; the text readout specified as a first-class element, not a tooltip.
- **CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator**: price range, direction, depth, ratio, status (active/tested/broken) with text carriers for each.
- **CMP-133 RegimeIndicatorChip**: regime label, numeric confidence, mandatory estimated variant (its catalogue entry already says it "inherits CMP-011 estimated variant").
- **CMP-134 DetectorEventCard**: card composition (CMP-050) with the mandatory estimated chip, the parameter-snapshot block, and hover/focus parity.
- Confirmation that **CMP-032 Rating/Confidence Dots** is specified as a supplement to a numeric value, never a replacement.
- Storybook specifications (states to be implemented) and token additions, contributed to the design-system library and the component catalogue.
- Greyscale and contrast verification for every new component.

## Out of scope
Screen-level design (D03/D04), implementation of the components (done inside the consuming stories), changes to CMP-049 Table / CMP-043 Dialog / CMP-046 Drawer base contracts.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One canonical estimated badge
  Then CMP-227 is specified once with all its variants
  And the spec requires an accessible label and the methodology binding on every variant
  And no variant conveys its meaning through colour alone

Scenario: Confidence is never a bare visual
  Then CMP-133 and CMP-032 are specified such that a numeric confidence value is always present alongside any dots or colour

Scenario: Detector card mandates the chip
  Then CMP-134's spec makes the estimated chip mandatory and includes the parameter-snapshot block

Scenario: Text carriers
  Given CMP-132's direction and status
  Then each is specified with a text carrier in addition to any colour or glyph

Scenario: Catalogue updated
  Then docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md entries for CMP-131, CMP-132, CMP-133, CMP-134, CMP-187 and CMP-227 match the delivered specs

Scenario: Contrast
  Then every token pairing used by these components meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, verified and recorded
```

## Technical notes / design
Specify CMP-227's API as `({ detector, variant, size })` with the drawer binding supplied by context, so a consumer cannot render the badge without it being actionable. That constraint is what makes E25-S04's "opens from any estimated badge" acceptance criterion structurally true rather than dependent on each screen remembering to wire it.

Keep the estimated treatment consistent but not shouty: it appears on many surfaces at once (footprint order-count, heatmap queue position, iceberg, stop-run, absorption, regime, trade clustering), so a heavy treatment would dominate the interface and train users to filter it out - a point D01 tests empirically.

## Test plan
N/A (design). Verification: greyscale render of each component; contrast report; a designer and a frontend engineer jointly confirm each spec is implementable with existing tokens.

## Security notes
None directly; the estimated badge is itself a risk-communication control for R7 and R9, so weakening its spec has downstream safety consequences.

## Accessibility notes
Each component spec must state its accessible name, role, keyboard behaviour and focus appearance. CMP-227 must be a real button (it opens a drawer), not a decorative span. CMP-134 must be reachable by keyboard, not hover-only.

## Performance notes
These components render on streaming panels at up to 4 Hz; specs must avoid shadows, blurs and transitions that would breach the 1-1.5 ms panel budgets.

## Observability
CMP-227 emits `methodology.opened{detector}` through its binding, so instrumentation is inherited rather than reimplemented per surface.

## Definition of Done
Specs delivered for all six components; component catalogue entries updated; tokens contributed; contrast and greyscale verification recorded; reviewed and approved by the design-system team lead and a frontend code owner; Storybook story list agreed with engineering.

## Dependencies
None blocking. Blocks D03 and D04; consumed by every E25 story.

title: Spike: calibrate iceberg/stop-run/absorption heuristics on recorded data
body:
## Context
The three L2-derived detectors in this epic (absorption, iceberg, stop-run) ship with numeric defaults already published in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` schema `DetectorConfig`: iceberg `min_reloads=3`, `price_tolerance_ticks=0`, `window_ms=5000`; stop_run `lookback_bars=20`, `penetration_ticks=2`, `reversal_pct=60`; absorption `min_volume_multiple=3`, `max_price_move_ticks=1`. Those numbers came from research digests, not from CandleViewer's own recorded Bybit data. Bybit's public feed is anonymous and aggregated and exposes no L3/MBO data, so iceberg, stop-run, absorption and regime are inferences, not observations. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` makes `confidence="estimated"` mandatory for every heuristic and states plainly that "presenting a heuristic as a certainty is a defect". Every surface that shows one of these values must render CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linked to SCR-058, the detector methodology drawer.

R2 exit criterion #4 and the roadmap risk table make detector *credibility* a release gate, and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` keeps `metrics.iceberg_detector`, `metrics.stop_run_detector` and `metrics.absorption` behind feature flags defaulting to `false` precisely because "heuristics behind flags until thresholds are tuned". This spike produces the tuning evidence that lets those flags be turned on and that fills the false-positive-mode sections of SCR-058.

Timebox: **3 days, 2 engineers max.** Output is a written decision, not production code.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A notebook/script under `research/detector-calibration/` (DuckDB over the Parquet cold tier, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`) that replays at least three recorded BTCUSDT and one ETHUSDT symbol-day through prototype implementations of the three heuristics.
- Fixture set selection: normal session, high-volatility burst, thin-book period (the integration fixture classes named in roadmap section 6.4).
- For each detector and each candidate parameter set: event count per hour, inter-event spacing distribution, and a manually labelled sample of 50 events per detector classified as plausible / implausible / undecidable by an order-flow-literate reviewer, reading the tape and book around each event.
- Recommended default parameter values and the low/medium/high sensitivity presets required by SCR-059.
- A written list of **false-positive modes per detector** in the exact wording to be used by `DetectorMethodology.false_positive_modes` (`/detectors/methodology`).
- Measured per-event CPU cost to size budget #11 (<=0.5 vCPU per symbol).
- A short decision record appended to the epic (and an ADR only if the spike concludes a published default must change).

## Out of scope
Production implementation (E25-T03/T04), UI, alerting, any change to the OpenAPI defaults without an accompanying ADR, machine-learned classifiers (explicitly not in R2 scope).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Recommendation exists
  Given three recorded BTCUSDT symbol-days and one ETHUSDT symbol-day
  When the calibration script runs each detector over each day at three candidate parameter sets
  Then the spike report recommends one default and three sensitivity presets per detector with the measured event rate for each

Scenario: False-positive modes are named
  Then each detector has at least two concretely described false-positive modes, each supported by a timestamp in the fixture data where it occurs

Scenario: Defaults are either confirmed or challenged in writing
  Given the published DetectorConfig defaults
  Then the report states for each parameter whether the recorded data supports it, and where it does not, proposes a value and raises an ADR

Scenario: Cost is known
  Then the report states measured CPU microseconds per trade and per book delta for each detector, and whether the combined cost fits budget #11

Scenario: Timebox respected
  Given the three-day timebox expires
  Then the report is published with whatever evidence exists and explicitly lists what remains unknown, rather than being extended silently
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype in Python against the Parquet tier so the run is reproducible and does not need a live feed. Iceberg prototype: track per-price resting size from `orderbook.200` deltas; count a "reload" when size at a price falls below a fraction of its prior value and returns to within `price_tolerance_ticks` and a size tolerance within `window_ms`; score = reload count. Absorption prototype: aggressive volume at a price over a window exceeding `min_volume_multiple` times the rolling median while price advance stays within `max_price_move_ticks`. Stop-run prototype: swing extreme over `lookback_bars`, penetration by `penetration_ticks`, then retracement of `reversal_pct` of the penetration excursion within the reversion window.

Label the sample blind where possible (reviewer sees the market context, not the detector's own score) to avoid confirming the heuristic with itself.

## Test plan
N/A for shipping tests; the calibration script itself must be deterministic (fixed fixture list, no wall-clock) and re-runnable by another engineer from the README in `research/detector-calibration/`. Reproduce-twice check: two runs produce identical event counts.

## Security notes
Fixture data is public market data. Do not copy recorded data outside the repo's data volume; the notebook must read from the configured data path, never from a pasted export. No credentials in the notebook.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - internal research artefact. Charts in the report must have a table alternative so the findings are reviewable by everyone.

## Performance notes
Measure per-event cost (microseconds per trade / per book delta) against budget #11 (<=0.5 vCPU sustained per actively recorded symbol) and budget #8 (<=300 MB resident per symbol) - the iceberg detector's per-price state is the memory risk.

## Observability
None shipped. The report must state which counters E25-T03/T04 should emit (at minimum `orderflow_detector_events_total{detector,symbol}` and a per-detector suppressed-by-cooldown counter).

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 5.2: question answered in writing; report committed under `research/detector-calibration/`; recommendation reviewed by the M9 owner and the architect; follow-up tickets (parameter changes, ADR) raised; timebox respected; the spike's conclusions are linked from E25-T03 and E25-T04.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E16 (recorder must have produced multi-day recorded history - roadmap note: "R2's data depth is a direct function of how early R1's recorder ships") and E21 (L2 book reconstruction, so the prototype replays the same book the production detector will see).

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for the detector subsystem
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic, and the R2 roadmap schedules "STRIDE R2 epics [S10-S13]". E25 looks like a read-only analytics feature and is not: **detector output can feed armed rules that place orders** (SCR-059's audit rationale, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` rule-action vocabulary), and detector thresholds are user-writable. That turns a market-data view into part of the trading control path, which is why the threat model must be done before E25-T02 builds the configuration write path.

Scheduled Sprint 10, ahead of the Sprint-12 implementation it constrains.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE analysis across the epic's trust boundaries (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 4): browser to API, API to M9 engines, M9 to QuestDB/Postgres, and the detector-event bus to the rule engine.
- Per category, with concrete threats and named controls:
  - **Spoofing**: unauthenticated or cross-session subscription to `metrics.{symbol}`; session fixation on the settings dialog.
  - **Tampering**: modifying detector thresholds to change armed-rule behaviour; bypassing published bounds by calling the API directly; mass-assignment via unexpected keys on `DetectorConfig`; altering methodology content to misrepresent an estimate as fact.
  - **Repudiation**: a threshold change with no attributable actor; an armed rule firing on a detector event with no record of the parameters in force (mitigated by `params_snapshot` on every event).
  - **Information disclosure**: minimal (market data is public) - but verify error responses do not leak internal table names, file paths or exchange credentials, and that recorded-history availability does not leak other users' recording configuration.
  - **Denial of service**: unbounded `metrics[]` selection; oversized REST backfill ranges; repeated `recompute` requests; unbounded per-price iceberg state; subscription amplification across many symbols.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a Viewer changing detector configuration; a detector-driven rule action escaping the acknowledgement requirement of US-DET-006's NFR.
- **Abuse cases** written as testable scenarios and handed to E25-Q01 for inclusion in the test plan.
- A control list mapped to the implementing tickets (T02 bounds/RBAC/audit, T01 caps, T03/T04 acknowledgement flag and state bounds, S05 armed-rule warning).
- Risk ratings and accepted residual risks, signed by the security engineer and the architect.
- SAST/DAST rule additions where the analysis identifies a pattern worth automating (for example a Semgrep rule forbidding threshold constants in the web client, and a ZAP scan of the detector endpoints).

## Out of scope
Implementation of the controls (the named tickets), pen-testing (scheduled before R4 live enablement), the rule engine's own threat model (E35), the recorder's (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All six STRIDE categories covered
  Then each category has at least one concrete threat for this epic, or a documented justification for why it does not apply

Scenario: Every threat has a control and an owner
  Then each identified threat maps to a named control and the ticket that implements it

Scenario: The armed-rule path is analysed
  Then the model explicitly analyses the path from a detector event to an armed rule action
  And names the controls that prevent a heuristic being the sole trigger of a live order without acknowledgement

Scenario: Abuse cases handed over
  Then at least four abuse cases are written as testable scenarios and accepted into the E25-Q01 test plan

Scenario: Automation identified
  Then any pattern worth automating is raised as a SAST or DAST rule with its rationale

Scenario: Signed off
  Then the model is reviewed and signed by the security engineer and the architect before E25-T02 begins
```

## Technical notes / design
Model the data flow concretely: `Bybit WS -> ingestion (M4) -> book/tape (M9) -> MetricsEngine -> DetectorRegistry -> DetectorEvent bus -> {WS fan-out, orderflow_metrics, alert engine, rule engine}` plus the control flow `browser -> PUT /detectors/config -> config store -> registry reconfigure`. The interesting boundary is the second one: it is a low-privilege-looking settings write that reaches into the trading control path.

Name the acknowledgement control precisely: `DetectorEvent.estimated` plus the requires-acknowledgement flag, honoured by the rule engine at arming time, is what implements US-DET-006's NFR. Without it the NFR is only a sentence.

## Test plan
Abuse cases become test cases in E25-Q01 and, where automatable, in E25-Q02 (unauthorised change) and E25-Q03 (DoS caps under load). The threat model itself is reviewed, not tested.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security work. Data classification: public market data; internal configuration; audit records are security-relevant and append-only. Review label required on E25-T02 and E25-S05.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - except the recommendation, carried into D04/S05, that security-relevant confirmations must be operable by keyboard and screen reader.

## Performance notes
DoS controls interact with budgets: caps must be set high enough not to break legitimate use (12 metrics per subscription is already the OpenAPI cap) and low enough to bound cost within budgets #8 and #11.

## Observability
Specify the security-relevant events to emit: `detector.threshold_changed`, `detector.enabled_changed`, rejected-change attempts with actor and reason, and rate-limit trips on the recompute endpoints.

## Definition of Done
STRIDE model documented in the security space and linked from the epic; threats rated with controls and owning tickets; abuse cases accepted into E25-Q01; SAST/DAST rules raised; residual risks accepted in writing; signed by the security engineer and the architect; completed before E25-T02 starts (it is a `blocked_by` of that ticket).

None blocking. Blocks E25-T02 and informs E25-S05, E25-Q01 and E25-X02.

title: Spike: measure seek cost and hot/cold source throughput at 200-depth symbol-day
body:
## Context
Two numbers decide the shape of the whole replay engine and both are currently assumed rather than measured.

**Seek cost.** `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 states seek is bounded at <=2 s for any point in a recorded day, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion #8 tightens the user-visible target to **1 s for a 200-depth symbol**. The algorithm is snapshot anchor (written every `snapshot_interval_s`, default 300 s) -> re-apply deltas to target -> restore `BuilderState` -> warm up metrics. At 200 depth and a busy session, 300 s of orderbook deltas is a large re-apply; the doc itself warns "a seek is never cheaper than a snapshot interval". If the measured cost exceeds budget, the answer is either a shorter snapshot interval (a recorder-side change with a disk cost that E16 owns) or a replay-side checkpoint cache — and that decision must be made before T04 is written, not after.

**Source throughput.** Budget #15 requires sustaining 100x. At 100x, a symbol-day must be read from QuestDB (hot) or Parquet/DuckDB (cold) and merged in `(ts_event, seq)` order fast enough to feed the live pipeline. Whether that needs a prefetching windowed reader, and how large the read-ahead buffer must be to survive a burst period without stalling the clock, is unknown.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Timebox: **4 days**, one backend engineer, agreed with the Architect.
- Measure, against a real recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day at 200 depth produced by the E16 recorder (and one thin-book symbol for contrast):
  1. Snapshot-anchor seek cost at the worst case (target just before the next snapshot), broken down into: anchor load, delta re-apply, `BuilderState` restore, metric warm-up.
  2. The same at snapshot intervals of 300 s, 60 s and 30 s, with the recorder disk cost of each recorded alongside.
  3. Sequential read throughput in events/s from the QuestDB hot tier and from the Parquet/DuckDB cold tier, and the merge cost across streams.
  4. Peak resident memory for a read-ahead buffer sized to 5 s, 30 s and 120 s of replay time at 1x, and the buffer needed to sustain 100x through the busiest minute of the day.
- A comparison table and a recommendation for: snapshot interval, read-ahead strategy (streamed cursor vs prefetched window), tier-selection rule for `source_tier='auto'`, and whether a replay-side checkpoint cache is required.
- **ADR-0018** drafted from the findings (finalised in E26-T07).
- Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path is chosen, including any recorder-side change requested of E16.

## Out of scope
- Production-shippable code. The prototype is explicitly throwaway; the branch is archived unmerged unless the Architect promotes a specific module.
- Frontend work of any kind.
- Optimising the downstream engines — this spike measures the *source and seek*, not footprint or heatmap cost.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The seek budget question is answered with numbers
  Given a 200-depth recorded symbol-day
  When worst-case seek is measured at each candidate snapshot interval
  Then a table of p50/p95/max seek durations with a stage breakdown is recorded
  And a snapshot interval that meets the 1 s p95 target is identified, or the shortfall is quantified with a stated mitigation

Scenario: The 100x question is answered with numbers
  Given the busiest minute of the recorded day
  When the source is read at maximum rate
  Then sustained events/s for both tiers and the read-ahead buffer size needed to avoid a clock stall are recorded

Scenario: A decision is recorded either way
  Given the measurements
  Then ADR-0018 is drafted with the chosen snapshot interval, read-ahead strategy and tier-selection rule
  And follow-up tickets exist for the chosen path, including any E16 recorder change
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the recorded fixture produced by E16 rather than synthetic data — synthetic depth updates do not reproduce the real delta-size distribution that dominates re-apply cost. Instrument the stages separately (`anchor_load_ms`, `delta_apply_ms`, `builder_restore_ms`, `warmup_ms`) because the mitigation differs per stage: a slow anchor load points at storage layout, a slow delta re-apply points at snapshot interval, a slow warm-up points at the metric warm-up window. Measure on the WSL Ubuntu docker-compose target, which is the real deployment shape, not on bare metal.

## Test plan

title: Create a replay session from SCR-098 with coverage-aware range selection
body:
## Context
Implements **US-RPL-001** (bar-by-bar replay, Must — its "before available history" scenario in particular) and the setup half of **US-RPL-009**. SCR-098 is where the recorder-dependency becomes concrete: a session can only exist over a window the recorder covered, and `14-screens-catalogue.md` §global rule 3 requires that limit to be a designed, explanatory state rather than an error.

Design is E26-D03, Done in Sprint 08, satisfying the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Build **SCR-098 Replay session setup modal** per the E26-D07 handoff pack, composed from CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-219 SymbolPicker, CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker, CMP-047 DatePicker/DateRangePicker, CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-027 ErrorState.
- Implement **CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker** as a design-system component per its E26-D05 spec: `symbol`, `availableRanges: {from,to}[]`, `onSelectRange`, with recorder-availability shading so only recorded ranges are selectable, and the Default / PartialAvailability / NoRecordedHistory(EmptyState) Storybook variants.
- Implement **CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker** with the canonical preset list plus the custom-value affordance (US-RPL-004 "plus a custom value").
- Fetch coverage from `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage?symbol` and render recorded / partial / missing windows on the range track with a text alternative.
- Create the session via `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions` with `{ symbols, from, to, speed, streams, depth, paper_account_id, autostart }`, sending an `Idempotency-Key`.
- Client-side validation mirroring the server contract with human-language messages: range end after start; range must intersect coverage ("Nothing is recorded for that window."); speed within 0.1-100; paper trading requires a paper account. Pre-empt the server's 422 `no_data_recorded` rather than surfacing it raw.
- **Start-before-history offer** (US-RPL-001 scenario 3): when the chosen start precedes available data, offer the earliest available timestamp with the reason stated and accept it in one action.
- **Resume** (US-RPL-009): surface an existing saved session for the symbol with its timestamp and speed alongside "Start fresh", and the data-changed variant offering the nearest available start when the underlying data was pruned.
- Preparation progress with the estimate shown before starting for large requests, and a cancel action.
- Entry points: the `/replay` route's empty state and the "open in replay" actions from the journal (SCR-094) and the footprint cell context menu, passing symbol and timestamp as prefill.

## Out of scope
- The replay page itself and playback (E26-S02).
- Paper-trading results (E26-S07).
- `GET /market/data-coverage` implementation (E16).
- Multi-symbol sessions beyond passing the array through — multi-pane behaviour is E26-S05.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Only recorded ranges can be chosen
  Given a symbol recorded from 2026-09-01 with a gap on 2026-09-05
  When the range picker renders
  Then unrecorded windows are not selectable and are distinguishable without relying on colour
  And the available ranges are also listed as text

Scenario: A start before available history becomes an offer, not a rejection
  Given the user picks a start earlier than the earliest recorded timestamp
  When they attempt to continue
  Then the earliest available timestamp is offered with the reason stated
  And accepting it takes one action and proceeds to session creation

Scenario: An uncovered window is refused in the client, with help
  Given a range intersecting no recorded coverage
  When the user attempts to create the session
  Then the modal states that nothing is recorded for that window and names the nearest recorded range
  And no request is sent

Scenario: A pruned saved session is explained on resume
  Given a saved replay position whose data has since been pruned
  When the modal opens for that symbol
  Then it states what changed and offers the nearest available start point
  And Start fresh clears the saved state for that symbol

Scenario: Preparation states its cost
  Given a three-symbol full-day request
  When the user submits
  Then the estimated preparation time is shown before preparation begins and a cancel control is available throughout

Scenario: A retried submission does not create two sessions
  Given a network retry of the create request with the same Idempotency-Key
  Then the original session is returned and only one session exists
```

## Technical notes / design
Server constraints to mirror client-side with friendly copy (`21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4): `rps_range`, `rps_speed` (0.1-100), `rps_paper` (paper requires an account). The paper-account selector lists only accounts the caller has been granted. Coverage is fetched once per symbol selection and cached for the modal's lifetime; the range control must not refetch per drag frame.

Prefill from external entry points sets symbol and centres the range on the passed timestamp with a sensible default window, then still validates against coverage.

## Test plan
Unit: validation rules, the earliest-available offer, preset and custom speed handling, coverage-to-track mapping including gaps at window edges. Component: CMP-171 and CMP-172 Storybook variants with unit, visual, axe and keyboard tests per their catalogue entries. Integration: session creation against a stubbed API including the 422 `no_data_recorded` path and the idempotent retry. E2E: covered in E26-Q02. Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
No filesystem path is ever entered or displayed (SR-097). The paper-account list is scoped to granted accounts. A session id belonging to another user is not resolvable — the resume path must handle a not-found gracefully rather than exposing existence. Data classification: recorded market data (A-10), plus account references.

## Accessibility notes
Labelled form controls for range, symbol multiselect, speed and paper account; the available-history statement is adjacent text rather than a tooltip; validation errors name their field and are wired via `aria-describedby`; the coverage timeline has a text alternative listing recorded ranges; the modal traps focus correctly and restores it on close. axe-core green; manual screen-reader spot-check on the range picker.

## Performance notes
SCR-098 budget: a 1-day single-symbol session is ready in <=10 s with progress shown; larger requests state the estimated preparation time before starting. Coverage fetch is cached per symbol for the modal's lifetime.

## Observability
`replay.session_created {range, symbols, speed}` analytics on success; `replay.session_deleted` where the modal offers deletion of a stale session.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests or by a recorded manual QA step with a follow-up automation task.
- [ ] CMP-171 and CMP-172 published to Storybook with their catalogue-specified test set.
- [ ] Coverage >=80% on the touched frontend package.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-098; keyboard-only path verified; manual screen-reader spot-check recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: compared against the E26-D03 spec (deferred sweep in E26-D08 also applies).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded; demoed at Sprint Review; feature-flag state recorded (`replay.enabled`, default on in staging).
- [ ] PRs merged via the merge queue.

`E26-T05` supplies the create endpoint and its error contract; `E26-D07` is the signed-off design handoff (design-ahead satisfied: E26-D03 Done in Sprint 08).

body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The legal state machine (`created -> buffering -> (playing <-> paused) -> finished`, `error` reachable from any state) is the library machine B12 `replay`; the migration/repository stay the bulk of the work, so the estimate is unchanged, but the service layer builds transitions on the factory, not a hand-written table.

> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The legal state machine (`created -> buffering -> (playing <-> paused) -> finished`, `error` reachable from any state) is the library machine B12 `replay`; the migration/repository stay the bulk of the work, so the estimate is unchanged, but the service layer builds transitions on the factory, not a hand-written table.

A replay session is a server-side object with a lifecycle, not a client-side toy: it is addressed on the WS by id, it holds buffers that must be reclaimed, it survives an app restart so US-RPL-009 can resume it, and it is the unit that paper fills are attributed to. `21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4 specifies the table exactly; this task lands it and the repository/service layer the rest of the epic builds on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating `replay_sessions` exactly per `21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4: columns `id`, `user_id` (FK `users` ON DELETE CASCADE), `recording_session_id` (FK `recording_sessions` ON DELETE SET NULL), `symbol`, `range_start`, `range_end`, `cursor_ts`, `speed numeric(6,2) DEFAULT 1`, `state replay_state DEFAULT 'created'`, `source_tier text DEFAULT 'auto'`, `paper_trading boolean`, `paper_account_id` (FK `exchange_accounts` ON DELETE SET NULL), `bookmarks jsonb DEFAULT '[]'`, `loop_enabled boolean`, `events_emitted bigint`, `gap_warnings integer`, `error_message`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `finished_at`; constraints `rps_range`, `rps_speed` (0.1-100), `rps_tier` (auto|questdb|parquet), `rps_cursor`, `rps_paper`; indexes `ix_rps_user_time` and the partial `ix_rps_live`.
- Confirm the `replay_state` enum (`created|buffering|playing|paused|finished|error`) exists from the base type migration; add it if the base migration did not.
- `ReplaySessionRepository`: create, get-by-id-scoped-to-user, list-by-user with cursor pagination and optional state filter, update state/cursor/counters, soft-finish, delete.
- `ReplaySessionService` lifecycle: `create` (validates the window against coverage and gaps before any buffer is allocated), `transition` (enforces the legal state machine), `reclaim_idle` (2 h idle -> `finished`, buffers freed, per SCR-097's session-expired state), `destroy`.
- A per-user **concurrent-session quota** and a **window-size cap** enforced in the service, both configurable (`CV_REPLAY_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_USER` default 2, `CV_REPLAY_MAX_WINDOW_HOURS` default 24) — the first line of defence against the resource-exhaustion threat.
- Downgrade path tested.
- Implement the `B12` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B12.machine.json`, committed by E50-S01/S02 (hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('replay', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.

```gherkin
  Then no residual objects remain and the schema matches 21-database-schema.md §3.6.4 exactly

Scenario: Invalid sessions cannot be persisted
  When a session is inserted with range_end <= range_start, or speed 0, or speed 101, or cursor_ts outside the range, or paper_trading true with a null paper_account_id
  Then the database rejects each by its named constraint
  And the service surfaces a human-readable validation error before reaching the database

Scenario: Quotas are enforced before buffers are allocated
  Given a user already at the concurrent-session limit
  When they create another session
  Then creation is refused with a quota error and no buffer is allocated

Scenario: Idle sessions are reclaimed
  Given a session with no control call for longer than the idle timeout
  When the reclaim sweep runs
  Then the session transitions to finished, its buffers are freed and its WS subscriptions are revoked with reason replay_session_ended

Scenario: One user cannot read another user's session
  Given a session owned by user A
  When user B fetches it by id
  Then the result is a not-found, not a forbidden that confirms existence
```

## Technical notes / design
The legal state machine is `created -> buffering -> (playing <-> paused) -> finished` with `error` reachable from any state and terminal; `finished` and `error` are terminal. Every transition writes `updated_at`; entering `finished` writes `finished_at`. `cursor_ts` is updated by the clock (T03) at a bounded rate — persist at most once per second to avoid write amplification at 100x, with the authoritative in-memory cursor being the source of truth during playback and the persisted value existing for restore (US-RPL-009).

`recording_session_id` is nullable and set when the window falls wholly inside one recording session; a window spanning several sessions leaves it null and relies on the coverage check instead.

title: Implement ReplaySource: hot/cold readers, ordered k-way merge and gap reporting
body:
## Context
Determinism starts at the read. `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 determinism guarantee (1) is that "events replay in `(ts_event, seq)` order, identical to the recorded order" — if the source ever emits out of order, or resolves a tie differently between two runs, every downstream guarantee collapses. The source must also span two storage tiers transparently: QuestDB for hot data and Parquet/DuckDB for cold (`21-database-schema.md` §1, `20-architecture.md` C18), because a window can straddle the roll-off boundary.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `ReplaySource` in `apps/api/.../replay/source.py` exposing an async iterator of recorded events for `(symbols, streams, from, to, depth)`.
- **Hot reader** over QuestDB and **cold reader** over Parquet via DuckDB, behind one interface, both addressed by registry ids and never by caller-supplied paths.
- **Tier selection** implementing `source_tier` `auto|questdb|parquet`: `auto` picks per sub-range using the roll-off boundary, so a window straddling the boundary reads hot for its recent part and cold for its older part, transparently and without duplicating or dropping events at the seam.
- **Ordered k-way merge** across streams (`trades`, `orderbook_delta`, `orderbook_snapshot`, `tickers`, `klines`, `liquidations`, `open_interest`, `funding`) producing a single stream strictly ordered by `(ts_event, seq)`, with a documented, stable tie-break for events sharing both (stream kind ordinal, then recorded insertion order) so two runs can never differ.
- **Read-ahead** per the E26-K01 recommendation: a bounded prefetch buffer with a configurable size (`CV_REPLAY_READAHEAD_EVENTS`), backpressure-aware so a slow consumer stops the read rather than growing memory.
- **Gap reporting**: intersect the window with `recording_gaps` and emit a typed `ReplayGap` marker in-stream at the gap boundary, carrying the gap's start, end and cause, so the clock (T03) and the UI can honour "No data 13:52-13:55 - recorder was offline" rather than silently jumping.
- **Snapshot-anchor lookup** helper used by the seek engine: latest `orderbook_snapshot` at or before a timestamp for a symbol and depth.
- Per-session memory ceiling enforcement with a typed error when exceeded.

## Out of scope
- The clock and pacing (E26-T03) — the source is pull-based and has no notion of speed.
- Seek orchestration (E26-T04) — it consumes the anchor lookup provided here.
- The recorder's write path, retention and coverage endpoint (E16).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Ordering is total and stable
  Given a recorded window containing events that share a ts_event across streams
  When the window is read twice
  Then both reads produce byte-identical event sequences
  And the sequence is non-decreasing in (ts_event, seq)

Scenario: A window straddling the roll-off boundary reads seamlessly
  Given a window whose older half is in Parquet and whose newer half is in QuestDB
  When it is read with source_tier auto
  Then no event is duplicated or dropped at the seam
  And the result equals reading the same window from a single tier holding all of it

Scenario: A gap is reported, never skipped silently
  Given the window intersects a recording_gaps row
  When the source reaches the gap boundary
  Then a ReplayGap marker is emitted carrying its start, end and cause

Scenario: A slow consumer cannot exhaust memory
  Given a consumer that stops reading
  When the read-ahead buffer fills
  Then the source stops reading from storage and resident memory stays flat
  And no events are dropped

Scenario: Paths are never accepted
  When any reader is constructed
  Then the dataset is addressed by registry id and symbol/stream/time, and no filesystem path parameter exists on the public interface
```

## Technical notes / design
Query shapes for both tiers were benchmarked in E07's storage spike ("replay scan of one symbol-day of L2 deltas") and refined in E26-K01; implement against the repository interface established by E07 so a tier swap stays a swap and not a rewrite (ADR-0003).

The merge is a standard heap-based k-way merge over per-stream cursors. The tie-break must be explicit and documented in ADR-0018, because leaving it to the heap's incidental behaviour is exactly how two runs come to differ.

`ReplayGap` is an in-stream control marker, not a market event; downstream the clock consumes it and the injector must never publish it onto a market-data topic.

## Test plan
Unit: merge ordering property test over generated interleavings (Hypothesis); tie-break stability; tier-selection boundary arithmetic; gap intersection including gaps at the exact window edges; memory ceiling error. Integration: read a real recorded fixture from each tier and from a straddling window, asserting sequence equality against a version-controlled expected digest. Perf: sustained events/s recorded against the E26-K01 baseline. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
SR-097 is the controlling requirement: the public interface accepts no filesystem paths, datasets resolve through the registry, and path-traversal and symlink-escape tests are mandatory on any internal path construction. Reads are bounded by the session's window and the window-size cap from T01, so a crafted request cannot scan the whole lake.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend.

## Performance notes
Must sustain the events/s measured in E26-K01 as the 100x floor for budget #15. Read-ahead sizing follows the K01 recommendation; the buffer is bounded in events and in bytes, whichever binds first.

## Observability
Counter `replay_events_read_total{stream,tier}`, gauge `replay_readahead_events`, counter `replay_gap_warnings_total`, histogram `replay_source_read_seconds{tier}`; the chosen tier per sub-range is logged once per session at info level.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Determinism property tests and the straddling-window integration test green.
- [ ] Tie-break rule documented in ADR-0018 (drafted in E26-K01, finalised in E26-T07).
- [ ] Path-traversal and symlink-escape tests present and green.
- [ ] Throughput benchmark recorded against the K01 baseline; no regression gate wired yet (E26-Q03 does that).
- [ ] Coverage >=85%; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-K01` decides the read-ahead strategy and tier-selection rule; `E16-T05` produces the Parquet cold tier this reads.

title: Implement ReplayClock and Injector: pacing, step modes, same-pipeline injection
body:
## Context
This is the heart of principle P2. The `Injector` publishes recorded events on `replay.{session_id}.*` topics **through the same normalizer -> book -> bars -> order-flow chain** as live ingestion (`20-architecture.md` C13), isolated from live state by an env-scoped namespace. The `ReplayClock` is the only thing that differs from live: a monotonic scheduler that emits events preserving inter-event deltas scaled by `speed`.

The most important rule in this ticket is one line from `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7: **"Backpressure from a slow consumer slows the clock rather than dropping events - replay must never lose data."** US-RPL-002's performance scenario is the user-visible half of the same rule: at high speed on a busy period, "playback keeps up or explicitly reports the achieved rate rather than silently dropping events".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `ReplayClock` in `apps/api/.../replay/clock.py`: monotonic scheduling preserving inter-event deltas scaled by `speed` (0.1-100), with drift correction against a monotonic time source rather than accumulated sleeps.
- **Step mode** (`speed=0`): `step_event`, `step_ms(n)`, `step_bar` — `step_bar` advances until the active `BarSpec` closes a bar, which is what US-RPL-001's "exactly one bar is revealed" and US-RPL-004's arrow-key semantics require.
- **Unbounded mode** (`speed=-1`): emit as fast as consumers accept, for the rule-backtest consumer in E35.
- **Backpressure**: when a consumer cannot keep up, the clock slows and records the achieved rate; it never drops. The achieved-rate figure is exposed on the session so the UI can show it (SCR-097 speed-limit honesty state).
- **Loop support** for US-RPL-008: on reaching a configured loop end, seek back to the loop start and continue, bounded by `loop_enabled` on the session.
- **Gap handling**: on a `ReplayGap` marker, either skip to the gap end (compressing the empty time) or stop at the boundary, per the session's configured behaviour, incrementing `gap_warnings` and surfacing the gap to the client either way.
- `Injector` in `apps/api/.../replay/injector.py`: publishes normalized events onto the bus under a replay-scoped namespace so no replay event can reach live state; sets `source="replay"` on every event; refuses to publish control markers onto market-data topics.
- **Structural isolation**: the OMS must be able to refuse to route replay events to a live account by construction, per determinism guarantee (4) — the `source="replay"` marker is set at injection and is not removable downstream.
- Per-session `asyncio` TaskGroup ownership consistent with `20-architecture.md` §lifecycle ("TaskGroup: replay sessions"), including clean cancellation on session destroy.

## Out of scope
- Seek and state reconstruction (E26-T04).
- REST/WS surfaces (E26-T05).
- Paper matcher behaviour (E38); the `PaperBridge` wiring is E26-S07.
- Any change to the downstream engines — if one proves not replay-safe, a Bug is filed against its owning epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Pacing is faithful and drift-free
  Given a recorded window of one hour replayed at 1x
  When playback completes
  Then total elapsed wall-clock time is within 0.5% of one hour
  And no cumulative drift is observable at the end relative to the start

Scenario: Backpressure slows, never drops
  Given a consumer that accepts events at half the required rate at 10x
  When playback runs
  Then every recorded event is still delivered in order
  And the session reports an achieved rate lower than the requested rate

Scenario: Step bar reveals exactly one bar
  Given speed 0 and an active 1-minute BarSpec
  When step_bar is issued once
  Then exactly one bar closes and every dependent view updates consistently

Scenario: Replay events cannot reach live state
  Given a replay session publishing on its namespace
  When the live book engine state for the same symbol is inspected
  Then it is unchanged by the replay traffic
  And every injected event carries source="replay"

Scenario: A gap is honoured explicitly
  Given a ReplayGap marker mid-window and skip-gap configured
  Then the clock jumps to the gap end, increments gap_warnings and notifies the client
  And with stop-at-gap configured it pauses at the boundary instead
```

## Technical notes / design
Scheduling uses a monotonic clock and computes each sleep as `target_wall = session_start_wall + (event_ts - session_start_ts) / speed`, sleeping to the absolute target rather than summing per-event deltas — the latter accumulates drift and would break the 0.5% criterion at long windows.

Speed changes mid-playback rebase `session_start_wall` and `session_start_ts` to the current position so the change takes effect continuously rather than jumping.

The injector's namespace must be part of the bus topic key, not a filter applied after publication, so isolation is structural. Determinism guarantee (4) depends on `source="replay"` being set at injection time and carried on the event object itself.

## Test plan
Unit: pacing math including speed changes mid-playback and drift over a simulated long window; step-mode semantics for each unit; backpressure never drops; loop wrap-around; gap skip and stop. Integration: replay a recorded 10-minute fixture at 1x/4x/25x and assert live state for the same symbol is untouched. Perf: sustained 100x on the K01 fixture without dropped events. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Isolation is a security control, not only a correctness one: a replay event reaching the OMS as if it were live would be a path to acting on stale prices with real money. The `source="replay"` invariant is tested adversarially in E26-X02. Per-session task ownership guarantees that destroying a session frees its CPU and memory, bounding the resource-exhaustion threat.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The achieved-rate reporting exists so the UI can be honest about degradation rather than appearing frozen.

## Performance notes
Budget #15: sustain up to 100x crash-free; visual fidelity may degrade but must never desync. Clock lag is the leading indicator and is exported as `replay_clock_lag_ms`.

## Observability
Histogram `replay_clock_lag_ms`, counter `replay_events_emitted_total`, counter `replay_backpressure_seconds_total`, gauge `replay_achieved_speed_ratio`, counter `replay_gap_warnings_total`; a log line per speed change and per gap encountered.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] 100x sustained run recorded with zero dropped events.
- [ ] `source="replay"` invariant covered by an adversarial test.
- [ ] Coverage >=85%; PR merged via the merge queue.

`E26-T02` supplies the ordered event stream and gap markers; `E26-T01` supplies the session object whose state and counters the clock updates.
