title: Implement SeekEngine: snapshot anchoring, delta re-apply, builder restore
body:
## Context
Scrubbing is the feature users judge replay by, and it is the hardest correctness problem in the epic: after a seek, the book, the in-progress bar, the footprint cells, the profiles and every warmed-up indicator must be exactly what they would have been had the session played from the start. `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion #8 states it as a hard gate: "scrubbing to an arbitrary timestamp reconstructs correct book, footprint and CVD state within 1 s for a 200-depth symbol".

`24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 gives the five-step algorithm; this ticket implements it using the parameters measured in E26-K01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `SeekEngine` in `apps/api/.../replay/` implementing, for a target timestamp:
  1. Find the latest `orderbook_snapshot` at or before the target (written every `snapshot_interval_s` plus on every subscribe and resync) via the T02 anchor lookup.
  2. Load it and rebuild the book to the recorded depth.
  3. Re-apply `orderbook_delta` events from the anchor to the target.
  4. Rebuild bar/footprint/profile state from a persisted `BuilderState` checkpoint (written every 60 s per `(symbol, spec_hash)`) or, absent one, by replaying trades from the enclosing session anchor.
  5. Prime metric warm-up by replaying `max(warmup_bars)` bars of history *before* the target, so indicators are valid at t=0 rather than `None`.
- Emission of a fresh `snap` on every subscribed topic after a seek with `reason: "replay_seek"` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11), so clients resynchronise rather than infer.
- **Seek cancellation**: a seek superseded by another seek (the user is dragging) is cancelled cleanly without leaking partial state — the scrub drag pattern makes this the common case, not an edge case.
- Seek into or across a gap: land at the nearest valid position on the correct side and report the gap rather than reconstructing from data that does not exist.
- Seek to the exact window start and to the exact window end as explicit cases.
- Optional checkpoint cache if E26-K01 concluded one is required.

## Out of scope
- Changes to bar builders or order-flow engines. `BarBuilder.snapshot()`/`restore()` and the `BuilderState` blob already exist (`24-internal-schemas.md` §4, E12) — this ticket consumes them. Any gap in that contract is a Bug on E12.
- Recorder snapshot cadence (E16 owns it; E26-K01 may have requested a change).
- The frontend scrub interaction (E26-S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Seek reconstructs exactly
  Given a recorded window played linearly from its start to timestamp X with the derived state captured
  When a fresh session seeks directly to X
  Then the book, in-progress bar, footprint cells, profile levels and CVD equal the linear-play state exactly

Scenario: Seek meets its budget
  Given a 200-depth recorded symbol-day
  When 50 seeks to uniformly random targets are timed
  Then p95 is under 1 s and the maximum is under 2 s

Scenario: Indicators are valid immediately after a seek
  Given an indicator with a 200-bar warm-up requirement
  When the session seeks to X
  Then the indicator has a value at X rather than None

Scenario: A superseded seek leaves no residue
  Given a seek to X in progress
  When a seek to Y is issued before X completes
  Then the session settles at Y with state identical to seeking directly to Y
  And no partial X state is observable

Scenario: Seeking into a gap is explicit
  Given a target inside a recording gap
  When the seek runs
  Then the session lands at the nearest valid timestamp and reports the gap rather than fabricating state
```

## Technical notes / design
Steps 2-3 dominate cost at high depth, which is why the snapshot interval chosen in E26-K01 is load-bearing; instrument each of the five steps separately under `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage=...}` using the stage names defined in K01.

The metric warm-up in step 5 must use the same warm-up path the live pipeline uses on subscribe, or replay and live will disagree on the first bars after a seek — which the determinism harness (T06) will catch, but which is far cheaper to avoid by construction.

Cancellation is implemented by scoping each seek to its own task and awaiting its cancellation before starting the next; state is only swapped into the session atomically at the end of a successful seek, never incrementally.

## Test plan
Unit: anchor selection at boundaries (target exactly on a snapshot, one event after, one before the first snapshot); delta re-apply arithmetic; warm-up bar count; cancellation atomicity. Integration: the linear-play-vs-seek equality test over a real recorded fixture at 20 random targets; gap seek; window-edge seeks. Perf: the 50-seek p95/max benchmark, recorded and later gated by E26-Q03. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Seek is the most expensive operation a client can trigger and therefore the cheapest denial of service: rate-limit control calls per session, and reject a seek while another is in flight beyond a small queue depth. The target timestamp is validated against the session window (`rps_cursor`), so a client cannot seek outside its own authorised range.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The <=1 s p95 exists so the UI's seeking state is brief and the announced clock settles quickly.

## Performance notes
Roadmap exit criterion #8 and the SCR-097 note "seek <=1 s to any point within the loaded window" are the binding targets; `24-internal-schemas.md` states the hard ceiling as 2 s. Both are asserted.

## Observability
Histogram `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage}` with stages `anchor_load`, `delta_apply`, `builder_restore`, `warmup`, `total`; counter `replay_seeks_total{result=ok|cancelled|gap|out_of_range}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Linear-play-vs-seek equality test green over a real recorded fixture.
- [ ] p95 <1 s / max <2 s recorded on the 200-depth symbol-day benchmark, or the shortfall escalated with the K01 mitigation applied.
- [ ] Cancellation atomicity test green.
- [ ] Stage metrics emitted with the agreed labels; coverage >=85%; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E26-T03` owns the session's runtime state that seek swaps; `E12` supplies `BarBuilder.snapshot()`/`restore()`, `BuilderState` and the `spec_hash` determinism property (invariant BI-4).

title: Implement the replay REST surface and WS replay_session_id routing
body:
## Context
This task exposes the engine and, more importantly, wires the one hook that makes principle G6 real: subscribing with `replay_session_id` set routes market-data topics from the replay clock instead of the live clock, over the same socket, with the same framing, into the same client rendering path (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11). Everything else in the protocol stays identical — which is precisely the point.

## Scope / Deliverables
- REST, exactly per `22-api-openapi.yaml`:
  - `GET /api/v1/replay/sessions` (cursor pagination, optional `state` filter, `replay:read`, scope self).
  - `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions` (`CreateReplaySessionRequest`; `replay:write`; idempotency recommended, honouring the `Idempotency-Key` and `Idempotency-Replayed` semantics; 201 with `ReplaySession`; **422 `no_data_recorded`** when the window lacks coverage).
  - `GET /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}` (204, frees buffers).
  - `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}/control` with `ReplayControlRequest` actions `play` (optional `speed`), `pause`, `seek` (`to`), `step` (exactly one of `step_events` or `step_ms`); returns the new `ReplaySession`.
- WS integration (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11):
  - Accept `replay_session_id` on `sub`; route the named market-data topics from that session's clock.
  - Set `source: "replay"` in `snap` metadata and **header flag bit2** on binary frames; carry `rs` (replay session id) in the envelope; add `wt` (wall-clock send time) on replay frames while `ts` remains the **original recorded time**.
  - Emit `snap` with `reason: "replay_seek"` on every subscribed topic after a seek.
  - On reaching `to`: session state `finished`, one `revoked` per topic with `reason: "replay_session_ended"`.
  - **Reject private topics** (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`) subscribed with `replay_session_id` using `invalid_options`.
  - Allow live and replay subscriptions to coexist on one connection, disambiguated by `sub_id`.
  - Error codes `replay_session_not_found` (topic-scoped, `not_found`) and `replay_session_ended` (topic-scoped, `gone`).
- Contract tests generated from the OpenAPI and WS schemas.

## Out of scope
- The engine internals (T02/T03/T04).
- `GET /market/data-coverage` (E16) — consumed only.
- Frontend consumption (E26-S01/S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Creating a session over uncovered data fails with the documented code
  Given a window with no recorded coverage
  When POST /api/v1/replay/sessions is called
  Then the response is 422 with code no_data_recorded
  And no session row and no buffer are created

Scenario: A replay subscription is marked unmistakably on the wire
  Given a subscription with replay_session_id set
  When frames arrive
  Then snap metadata carries source "replay", binary frames set header flag bit2, the envelope carries rs
  And ts is the original recorded time while wt carries wall-clock send time

Scenario: Private topics are never replayable
  When a sub with replay_session_id names orders, positions, executions or wallet
  Then it is rejected with invalid_options

Scenario: Live and replay coexist on one connection
  Given book.BTCUSDT.200 subscribed live and the same topic subscribed under a replay session
  Then both deliver independently and are disambiguated by sub_id

Scenario: Session end revokes cleanly
  Given playback reaches the end of the window
  Then the session state becomes finished and one revoked frame per topic is emitted with reason replay_session_ended

Scenario: Another user's session is invisible
  Given a session owned by user A
  When user B references it on REST or on a sub
  Then REST returns not-found and the sub is rejected with replay_session_not_found
```

## Technical notes / design
`step` carries exactly one of `step_events` or `step_ms`; enforce the exclusivity in the request model and return 422 with a field-level message otherwise. `seek` repositions `cursor_ts` and is never cheaper than a snapshot interval — the API doc says so, and the control response returns the session so the client can render the seeking state from real state rather than optimistically.

Control-call rate limiting lives here rather than in the engine, so a scrub drag that fires many seeks is coalesced at the edge: apply a short debounce window per session and treat the latest target as authoritative.

## Test plan
Contract: OpenAPI request/response validation for every operation and error; WS schema conformance for `sub` with `replay_session_id`, `snap` `reason` values, `revoked` reasons and the error registry entries. Integration: full lifecycle create -> subscribe -> play -> seek -> step -> end -> revoked against a recorded fixture. Security: cross-user access, private-topic rejection, control-call rate limit. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
`replay:read`/`replay:write`, scope `self`. Cross-user references return not-found rather than forbidden. No filesystem path is accepted by any operation (SR-097) — windows are addressed by symbol and time only. Control endpoints are rate-limited per session and per user to bound the seek-amplification denial of service. Idempotency on create prevents a retried request from allocating a second session and a second buffer.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The control response returning authoritative state is what lets the UI announce the settled position rather than a predicted one.

## Performance notes
Budget #3 (WS tick to screen p95 <100 ms) still applies to replay frames measured via `wt`, which exists precisely so latency instrumentation keeps working when `ts` is recorded time.

## Observability
Counters `replay_control_calls_total{action,result}`, `replay_subscriptions_total`; the replay-session-start OpenTelemetry span (one of the two traced paths in `20-architecture.md` §observability) is started here and carries session id, symbol, window length and tier.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every operation and error path contract-tested against `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` §11.
- [ ] Private-topic rejection and cross-user isolation tests green.
- [ ] Live+replay coexistence integration test green.
- [ ] Rate limiting on control calls implemented and tested; coverage >=85%; PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies

title: Build the replay determinism and live-parity harness as a required CI check
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion #1 is not a claim to be made in a demo, it is a test: "All order-flow views render from a single shared pipeline used identically by live and replay - **verified by a test that replays a recorded day and asserts view state equals the state captured live**". Criterion #7 adds detector reproducibility and criterion #8 adds cross-run determinism. §6.4 lists "Determinism | Replay double-run equality test; detector event-stream equality test" as a quality gate.

This harness is the single most valuable artefact in the epic: it is what converts "replay is the same code path" from an architectural intention into an enforced property, and it is what R3 relies on when it uses replay as a trading-logic test bed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **capture mode** in the recorder-adjacent test tooling that, while a fixture is recorded live (or from the synthetic feed), also captures the derived state at checkpoints: bars per active `BarSpec`, footprint cells, profile levels, CVD, Deep-Stats values and every `deterministic=True` metric, with their `spec_hash`.
- A **live-parity test**: replay the recorded fixture and diff every captured derived value against the replayed value. Tolerance 0 for exact metrics, 1e-9 for floats (`24-internal-schemas.md` §metric descriptors). Any difference fails CI with a diff report naming the first divergent timestamp, stream and field — a bare boolean failure would be useless at this scale.
- A **double-run equality test**: replay the same window twice in the same run and assert byte-identical emitted event streams and derived series; plus a cross-machine assertion by comparing against a version-controlled digest so a developer machine and CI must agree.
- A **detector event-stream equality test** (criterion #7): replaying the same recorded window twice yields identical detector events, including their inputs and threshold values.
- A **seek-parity test** delegating to E26-T04's linear-play-vs-seek equality assertion so it runs in the same gate.
- Version-controlled golden fixtures in `packages/fixtures`: one normal session, one high-volatility burst, one containing a WS disconnect and resync, one with a sequence gap, one thin-book symbol (the §6.4 integration fixture list).
- Wire the suite as a **required CI check** on `main`, with a documented procedure for regenerating goldens that requires a reviewer from both the engine and QA sides.

## Out of scope
- Fixing divergences found in downstream engines — those are Bugs filed against E18/E19/E20/E21/E23/E25.
- The offline DuckDB recomputation parity check (§6.3 criterion #6) — that is owned by the order-flow epics; this harness may reuse its fixtures.
- Performance benchmarking (E26-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live parity is enforced, not asserted
  Given a recorded fixture with derived state captured live
  When the harness replays it in CI
  Then every derived value matches within tolerance
  And any mismatch fails the build with the first divergent timestamp, stream and field named

Scenario: Double-run equality holds across machines
  Given the same window replayed on CI and on a developer machine
  Then both produce identical event streams and derived series
  And both match the version-controlled digest

Scenario: Detector events are reproducible
  Given a window containing iceberg and stop-run detector firings
  When it is replayed twice
  Then the detector event streams are identical including inputs and thresholds

Scenario: Goldens cannot drift silently
  When a golden fixture or digest is regenerated
  Then the change requires review from both an engine owner and QA
  And the PR states why the expected values changed
```

## Technical notes / design
Checkpoint at bar closes rather than per event: per-event capture would be enormous and would mostly re-assert the same property. Capture per `(symbol, spec_hash)` so a builder-config change is visible as a fixture mismatch rather than as a silent pass.

The diff report should be structured (first divergence plus a bounded context window), because a full diff of a symbol-day is unreadable and unreadable output is how a failing determinism gate becomes a disabled determinism gate.

Run the full symbol-day suite nightly and a reduced one-hour suite on every PR, so the gate is enforced on every change without making PR CI unusable.

## Test plan
The harness *is* the test plan; its own unit tests cover the diff reporter, the tolerance logic and the fixture loader. A deliberate mutation test proves the harness fails when the pipeline is perturbed: inject a one-tick offset into a bar builder behind a test flag and assert the harness catches it.

## Security notes
Fixtures are recorded market data only (classification A-10) with no account identifiers, keys or PII. Fixture integrity matters: a corrupted golden silently weakens the gate, so fixtures carry a checksum manifest verified on read, mirroring SR-094's posture for the Parquet archive.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The PR-tier suite must complete within the CI budget agreed with DevSecOps; the nightly tier carries the full symbol-day. Report harness runtime so it does not silently grow into a bottleneck.

## Observability
Publish the pass/fail and the first-divergence summary as a CI artefact; track the suite's runtime as a metric so regressions in the harness itself are visible.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Live-parity, double-run, detector-equality and seek-parity tests implemented and green.
- [ ] Five golden fixtures committed with a checksum manifest and a documented regeneration procedure requiring dual review.
- [ ] Suite wired as a required check on `main` (PR tier) plus a nightly full tier.
- [ ] Mutation test proves the harness actually fails on a perturbed pipeline.
- [ ] Roadmap exit criteria #1, #7 and #8 each map to a named test in this suite, documented on the ticket.

## Dependencies
`E26-T03` must be able to replay a window; `E18` and `E23` supply the footprint and CVD state the parity test diffs (profiles, Deep-Stats and detectors are added as their epics land, without changing this harness's structure).

## Branch
`feat/replay-engine-determinism-harness`.

title: Support footprint input types and make the order-based source honestly absent
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-005 — Footprint input types (Must/Should)**: traded volume is Must; aggregated volume and number of trades are Should. The third scenario is the one that matters most for product integrity: *"the 'Order (per-order arrival)' input is absent from the UI, with an info note that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed."*

R2's goal 2 states this as a train-level principle: *"Be scrupulously honest about fidelity"*, and `11-user-stories.md` global AC #6 requires an `(estimated)` badge with an explanation popover on any heuristic view. SCR-032's state list includes *"order-based source selected → persistent '(estimated)' warning banner"* — this story resolves that tension by making the option **absent** rather than present-and-warned, per US-FP-005, and records the divergence from the SCR-032 sketch in the catalogue.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Input source `traded volume` (default, Must): cells count quantity.
- Input source `number of trades` (Should): cells show print counts instead of quantity, with the legend stating the unit.
- Input source `aggregated volume` (Should): prints at the same price, side and millisecond are merged before display, per the configured aggregation window (0–100 ms, configurable; changing it re-aggregates from stored prints via `FootprintConfig`/`orderflow.footprint.agg_window_ms`).
- **Order-based input absent**: not rendered, not disabled-with-tooltip — absent, accompanied by a persistent info note (CMP-069 InfoPanel) in SCR-032 stating that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed and therefore per-order arrival cannot be computed.
- CMP-227 EstimatedBadge wiring: this story ensures the badge is **not** shown for the three supported sources (they are exact, not estimated), and that the catalogue-level test asserting badge presence on estimated views does not produce a false positive here.
- Changing the input source is the **only** footprint setting that triggers `POST /api/v1/market/footprint/recompute`; the UI shows the recompute-in-progress state ("Recomputing footprint from recorded trades — 40 %") driven by `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`.

## Out of scope
The rest of the settings dialog (E18-S10); the recompute job implementation (E18-T05); detector-level `(estimated)` views (E25).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Number-of-trades input
  Given the input source is number of trades
  Then cells show print counts instead of quantity
  And the legend states the unit

Scenario: Aggregated volume
  Given an aggregation window of 50 ms
  Then prints at the same price, side and millisecond bucket are merged before display
  And changing the window to 0 ms re-aggregates from stored prints without re-reading the exchange

Scenario: Order input is absent, not broken
  When I open the footprint settings input-source control
  Then no "Order (per-order arrival)" option is present
  And an info note explains that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed
  And a user reading only that note can explain why the option does not exist

Scenario: Exact sources carry no estimated badge
  Given any of the three supported input sources
  Then no (estimated) badge is rendered on the footprint pane
  And the catalogue-level estimated-badge test does not flag this surface

Scenario: Input-source change rebuilds visibly
  When I change the input source
  Then a recompute job is started and its progress is shown
  And the pane shows the previous data until the rebuild completes, then updates
  And if the job fails, an actionable error in domain language is shown with the job id available in a details disclosure
```

## Technical notes / design
- Aggregation-window merging happens server-side in `FootprintEngine` (E18-T01) so live and replay share one implementation; the client only selects the window.
- The recompute path is asynchronous by design: `202 + job_id`, polled. The UI must not block the pane or clear existing data while it runs.
- Error handling follows global AC #5: domain-language message, raw code in a details disclosure.
- Record in `14-screens-catalogue.md` that SCR-032's "order-based source" state is **withdrawn** in favour of absence, so the two documents stop disagreeing.


**Estimate rationale (re-baselined 55-pt train fit):** 2 → 1. The recompute trigger, progress and failure surfaces are implemented by E18-T03/E18-S10; what remains here is the source-selection wiring, the honest absence of the order-based option with its note, and the catalogue-level assertion that no `(estimated)` badge appears on exact sources.

## Test plan
- Unit: legend unit strings per source; aggregation-window parameter plumbing; job-polling state machine including failure and cancellation.
- Integration: input-source change end-to-end against a recorded fixture, asserting a recompute job is created and the pane updates on completion.
- E2E: assert the order-based option is absent from the DOM (not merely hidden by CSS) and the info note is present and readable.
- Catalogue test: the estimated-badge enforcement test passes without listing this surface.

## Security notes
The recompute action requires `recording:write`; a `viewer` must see the input-source control in a permission-denied state rather than triggering a 403 on click. The job id is safe to display. Threat: **DoS by repeated rebuilds** — the UI disables the control while a job for that (symbol, spec) is in flight, and the server enforces the real limit (E18-T03).

## Accessibility notes
The info note is a focusable disclosure, not a hover-only tooltip. Recompute progress is announced politely at coarse intervals (start, 50%, completion, failure) — not on every poll. The legend unit change is announced when the source changes.

## Performance notes
No frame-budget impact; the aggregation window changes cell counts, which indirectly affects density — the cell-budget collapse from E18-S01 covers that case.

## Observability
Audit `chart.footprint_settings_changed` and `market.footprint_recompute_requested`; metric `footprint_input_source_changes_total{source}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios pass via automated tests.
- [ ] SCR-032 catalogue entry updated to record the withdrawn order-based state.
- [ ] Estimated-badge catalogue test green.
- [ ] Recompute progress and failure states implemented and demonstrated.
- [ ] axe-core green; the info note reviewed by the Owner for accuracy.
- [ ] design-qa, QA sign-off, Sprint Review demo.
- [ ] PR merged with 2 approvals including a code owner.

## Dependencies
E18-S01 (rendering), E18-T01 (aggregation window and input handling server-side).

title: Flag diagonal imbalances with configurable per-symbol thresholds
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-007 — Diagonal imbalance detection (Must)**: *"I want diagonal bid/ask imbalances flagged at a configurable ratio, so that absorption and initiative are visible instantly."* The story's NFR fixes the architecture: *"computed backend-side once per bar update and streamed as flags; default 300%"* — the client never recomputes imbalance, it renders flags. That is what keeps a rule, an alert and the chart agreeing on the same number.

Screens: SCR-030 (cell markers), SCR-056 (imbalance tracker rows — the US-FP-007 half). Components: CMP-195 AnnotationMarker (cell flag), CMP-011 Tag/Chip and CMP-049 Table (tracker rows).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Render buy/sell imbalance flags on cells from the WS binary flag bits (bit0 buy-imbalance, bit1 sell-imbalance) and the structured `imbalances[]` array, with **colour plus outline pattern** (never colour alone).
- Per-symbol threshold configuration: setting 200% for BTCUSDT persists for BTCUSDT and leaves other symbols unchanged; the change recomputes flags immediately for the loaded range with **no refetch** (server-side `recompute_flags` over cached cells, delivered via the subscription's option update).
- Thin-cell exclusion: cells below the minimum-volume filter produce no flag (US-FP-007 scenario 3), preventing noise from trivial volumes — the client renders exactly what the server flags and adds no local heuristic.
- SCR-056 rows for diagonal imbalances: time, direction, price, ratio (the **actual** computed ratio, e.g. "420%"), age; click → chart crosshair jumps to the cell and highlights it.
- Threshold single-source-of-truth behaviour required by SCR-056: thresholds are shared with SCR-032, and changing one prompts to sync the other.
- The cell context menu action "Focus imbalance" (SCR-030 right-click menu).

## Out of scope
Stacked runs and zones (E18-S08), the detector inspector and absorption analytics (E25's US-DET-004 half of SCR-056), alert creation from a level (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default 300 percent
  Given ask volume at price P exceeds bid volume at P minus one tick by 300 percent or more
  Then the cell is flagged with a marker
  And the flag is counted in the imbalance tracker panel

Scenario: Threshold change is per symbol and immediate
  When I set 200 percent for BTCUSDT
  Then flags recompute immediately for the loaded range with no history refetch
  And the per-symbol threshold persists across sessions
  And ETHUSDT panes keep their own threshold

Scenario: Thin cells excluded
  Given both cells in a diagonal comparison fall below the minimum-volume filter
  Then no imbalance is flagged

Scenario: Flags come from the server, never from the client
  Given the client receives cells without flags due to a protocol error
  Then no flag is rendered and a protocol error is logged
  And the client does not compute a substitute flag

Scenario: The actual ratio is shown
  Given a flagged cell whose computed ratio is 4.2
  Then the tracker row shows 420 percent, not the 300 percent threshold

Scenario: Threshold sync prompt
  Given thresholds differ between SCR-032 and SCR-056
  When one is changed
  Then the user is prompted to sync the other rather than the two silently diverging

Scenario: Non-colour encoding
  Given a greyscale render
  Then buy and sell imbalance flags remain distinguishable by outline pattern and direction glyph
```

## Technical notes / design
- Flags arrive as bit flags in the binary payload; decode into a per-cell instance attribute so marking costs nothing extra per frame.
- Threshold persistence is per (user, symbol) in user preferences, and is applied by re-resolving the subscription options — not by a client-side filter over already-flagged cells (which would be wrong, since raising the threshold cannot be derived from a lower-threshold flag set without the ratios; use the transmitted `ratio` only for display).
- Clicking a tracker row moves the crosshair via the existing chart command bus (the same mechanism SCR-056's "click → chart crosshair jumps" requires), not by a bespoke coupling.

## Test plan
- Unit: flag-bit decoding; per-symbol threshold persistence and resolution; ratio formatting; tracker row composition.
- Integration: threshold change round-trip asserting no `/market/footprint` refetch and correct new flag counts against the golden fixture.
- Golden image: flagged cells in both directions, per theme, greyscale evidence.
- E2E: set 200% on BTCUSDT, open ETHUSDT and assert its threshold unchanged; click a tracker row and assert the crosshair moved to the right bar and price.
- Parity: flag counts and ratios covered by E18-T06.

## Security notes
Thresholds are user preferences persisted through existing endpoints with existing RBAC; no new surface. Threat: **misleading output** — a client-side substitute computation would silently disagree with rules and alerts, so the "flags come from the server" scenario is a security-adjacent correctness control, not a style preference.

## Accessibility notes
Flagged cells announce their flag in the DOM-mirror label ("... buy imbalance 420 percent"). The tracker table (CMP-049) is a real table with sortable columns and keyboard row activation. Outline pattern plus a direction glyph carries the meaning without colour. Newly formed flags are **not** announced automatically (per the E18-D04 announcement policy) — only stacked zones are, in E18-S08.

## Performance notes
Flag rendering adds one instance attribute and reuses the pattern pass from E18-S06; budget #1 impact must be under 0.2 ms at the target scene. Tracker rows are virtualised if the list exceeds the visible window.

## Observability
Metric `footprint_imbalance_flags_rendered`; analytics `chart.footprint_settings_changed` on threshold change; audit not required (display preference).

title: Render stacked imbalance zones with virgin/broken tracking
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-008 — Stacked imbalance detection (Must)**: *"I want N consecutive imbalances flagged as a stack, so that I can find likely support/resistance shelves."* Its NFR makes this the epic's outward-facing contract: *"stacks published as domain events consumable by alerts and rules"* — E25 detectors, E40 alerts and the E35 rule engine all consume `stacked_imbalance_zone`, and `22-api-openapi.yaml` already contains a rule message template referencing `footprint.sell_stack_size` and `footprint.stack_price`.

Components: **CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator** (zone marker with virgin/crossed states distinguished by **pattern, not colour alone**), CMP-049 Table and CMP-134 DetectorEventCard on SCR-056.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Zone rendering: runs of `>= min_stack` (default 3) consecutive same-direction flagged levels drawn as a bracket beside the cells, with the **price range labelled**.
- **Zone persistence**: a zone persists as a level on the chart until price trades fully through it, then is marked "broken" (US-FP-008 scenario 2). CMP-132's `state: "virgin" | "crossed"` with `pattern.hatch` distinguishing them.
- Configurable depth: requiring 4 consecutive levels recomputes stacks and removes shallower ones, immediately and without refetch.
- SCR-056 stacked rows: time, direction, stack depth ("BUY stack x4"), price range, ratio, age, and the "only unfilled" (virgin-only) filter; click → crosshair jumps and highlights the cells.
- Consumption of the `stacked_imbalance_zone` domain event so the chart, the tracker and any future alert all read the same zone identity (`stack_id`).
- Zone lifecycle across bar updates without flicker: `stack_id` stability within a recompute means the UI diffs zones rather than rebuilding them.
- Broken-zone retention policy: broken zones remain visible for a configurable look-back and are visually distinct from virgin ones.

## Out of scope
Alert creation from a zone (E40 — SCR-056's "Create alert from this level" button is stubbed and disabled with an explanatory tooltip in R2), detector inspector (E25), rule-engine wiring (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default stack of 3
  Given 3 consecutive price levels are imbalanced in the same direction
  Then the stack is highlighted as a zone with its price range labelled

Scenario: Zone persistence and breaking
  Given a virgin stacked zone
  When price trades fully through its range
  Then it is marked broken and rendered with the crossed pattern
  And it remains listed in the tracker with a broken status rather than disappearing

Scenario: Configurable depth
  When I require 4 consecutive levels
  Then stacks recompute immediately and stacks of depth 3 disappear
  And no history is refetched

Scenario: Zones are events, not decorations
  Given a new stacked zone forms
  Then a stacked_imbalance_zone domain event is published carrying symbol, bar, price range, direction, stack size and the config that produced it
  And the chart zone and the tracker row share the same stack_id

Scenario: No flicker on the forming bar
  Given the forming bar's stack membership changes several times per second
  Then zone rendering updates are coalesced to at most 10 Hz
  And a zone does not appear and disappear more than once per 200 ms

Scenario: Opposite-direction runs never merge
  Given a buy run directly adjacent to a sell run
  Then two separate zones are rendered, never one combined zone

Scenario: Virgin versus broken without colour
  Given a greyscale render
  Then virgin and broken zones remain distinguishable by hatch pattern
```

## Technical notes / design
- Zone geometry is a small number of quads per zone — cheap. The cost is in lifecycle bookkeeping, not rendering: track zones by `stack_id`, diff on update, and apply the E18-D04 flicker policy (no appear/disappear more than once per 200 ms; hold values until the coalescing window closes).
- "Traded fully through" is evaluated server-side against subsequent bars' price ranges so the chart and any rule agree; the client renders the state it is told. Define the predicate precisely in the ticket's implementation PR and mirror it into `24-internal-schemas.md` if it is not already there.
- Broken-zone look-back is bounded (`ff`-configurable, default 200 bars) so zone count cannot grow without limit on a long session.

## Test plan
- Unit: zone diffing by `stack_id`; virgin→broken transition predicate; flicker-policy timer; look-back eviction; adjacency non-merge.
- Integration: a recorded window with a known shelf that is later traded through, asserting the exact bar at which it becomes broken, twice, identically (determinism).
- Golden image: virgin and broken zones, both directions, per theme, plus greyscale.
- E2E: change `min_stack` from 3 to 4 and assert zone count drops with no network fetch; enable "only unfilled" and assert broken zones are filtered from the list but remain on the chart per the designed behaviour.
- Event contract test: `stacked_imbalance_zone` payload validated against its schema.

## Security notes
The domain event is consumed by the rule engine, which can eventually act on it — so its integrity matters more than a display element's. Controls: the event is produced only server-side from server-computed flags; the client cannot inject one; the payload includes the config that produced it so a downstream consumer can audit why a rule fired. Note this in the E18-X01 threat model as a **tampering/integrity** consideration on the analytics→automation boundary.

## Accessibility notes
Zones are DOM-mirror region markers with an `aria-label` describing the zone and state in words ("Buy imbalance stack, 4 levels, 63,980 to 64,010, unbroken"). Per the E18-D04 announcement policy, a **newly formed stacked zone is one of the three events that may be announced automatically** (the others are user focus movement and bar close) — at most one announcement per zone, politely. The tracker table supports keyboard row activation and the "only unfilled" filter is a labelled checkbox.

## Performance notes
Zone rendering must stay under 0.2 ms at the target scene; zone bookkeeping is off the render path. Marker updates coalesced to ≤ 10 Hz (US-FP-009 NFR applies to markers generally).

## Observability
Metrics: `footprint_stacks_rendered`, `footprint_zone_state_transitions_total{to}`, `stacked_imbalance_zone_events_total`. The event itself is observable on the bus for downstream epics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios pass via automated tests, including the determinism assertion.
- [ ] `stacked_imbalance_zone` schema documented and contract-tested.
- [ ] Storybook: CMP-132 Virgin, Crossed, BidSide, AskSide.
- [ ] Greyscale evidence and golden images committed.
- [ ] Flicker policy verified with a recorded high-frequency window.
- [ ] axe-core green; screen-reader pass on the zone announcement.
- [ ] design-qa, QA sign-off, Sprint Review demo.
- [ ] PR merged with 2 approvals including a code owner.

title: Mark bar POC, value area and unfinished auctions without flicker
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-009 — Bar POC and unfinished auction (Must/Should)**: intrabar point of control is Must, unfinished-auction markers are Should. *"I want the intrabar point of control and unfinished-auction markers, so that I can read bar structure."* NFR: **marker updates coalesced to ≤ 10 Hz** — the third scenario requires both markers to update as the forming bar evolves *without flicker*.

`18-traceability-matrix.md` notes US-FP-009 as one of the stories that initially resolved to zero screens; it is now mapped to SCR-030 (markers) and SCR-032 (the toggles: "[x] bold per-bar POC  [x] mark VA").

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Bar POC**: the highest-volume price level in each bar marked distinctly (bold cell border plus a text label, never fill colour alone) and exposed as a metric (`bar_poc_price`) so Deep-Stats (E20) and rules read the same value.
- **Value area**: VAH/VAL boundaries marked per bar using the server-computed `va_high_ticks`/`va_low_ticks`, with the configured `value_area_pct` (default 70%) shown in the legend.
- **Unfinished auction**: bars whose extreme has two-sided volume at the last level marked with an explanatory tooltip; the opposite case (`finished_auction_high/low`) is available in the cell detail but not marked on the canvas by default.
- SCR-032 toggles for both markers.
- Flicker-free forming-bar updates: marker position changes coalesced to ≤ 10 Hz with the E18-D04 motion spec (POC moving between levels animates within the bar; markers never blink).
- Marker rendering via CMP-195 AnnotationMarker, the shared sparse-event primitive.

## Out of scope
Session/visible-range profiles and their POC/VA (E19), naked-POC tracking (E19), the value-area **algorithm** itself (E18-T02 implements both `single_step` and `two_row_tpo`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bar POC
  Then the highest-volume price level in each bar is marked distinctly
  And the POC price is exposed as a metric readable by Deep-Stats and rules

Scenario: Unfinished auction
  Given a bar's extreme has volume on both bid and ask at the last level
  Then it is marked as unfinished with an explanatory tooltip

Scenario: Live bar updates without flicker
  Given the forming bar's POC changes level several times per second
  Then marker updates are coalesced to at most 10 Hz
  And no marker appears and disappears more than once per 200 ms

Scenario: Single-level bar is never unfinished
  Given a bar with exactly one traded level
  Then neither unfinished_high nor unfinished_low is marked

Scenario: Value area reflects the configured percentage
  Given value_area_pct is changed from 70 to 80
  Then VAH and VAL boundaries recompute immediately from cached cells with no refetch
  And the legend shows the active percentage

Scenario: POC is deterministic on ties
  Given two levels with identical maximum volume
  Then the marked POC is stable across re-renders and matches the server tie-break order

Scenario: Not colour-only
  Given a greyscale render
  Then POC, VAH/VAL and unfinished-auction markers remain identifiable by border weight, pattern and text label
```

## Technical notes / design
- All four values (`poc_price`, `value_area_high`, `value_area_low`, `unfinished_auction{high,low}`) arrive on the `FootprintUpdate` payload and in `FootprintBar` from REST — the client never recomputes them, for the same agreement reason as imbalance flags.
- The POC marker is a border/label treatment on an existing cell instance plus one annotation marker; it adds no per-cell cost.
- The ≤ 10 Hz coalescing is implemented in the same update pipeline as the forming-cell coalescing from E18-T01/T04, not as a second timer.


**Estimate rationale (re-baselined 55-pt train fit):** 3 → 2. Both algorithms (POC tie-break, value area `single_step`/`two_row_tpo`) are delivered and unit-tested by E18-T02, and markers are drawn through the shared CMP-195 AnnotationMarker primitive; the remaining work is marker placement, the SCR-032 toggles and the ≤10 Hz coalescing that E18-D04's motion spec already specifies.

## Test plan
- Unit: marker placement from payload fields; coalescing timer; single-level-bar suppression; legend percentage rendering.
- Integration: a forming-bar replay at full tick rate asserting the marker update count per second is ≤ 10 and no blink occurs.
- Golden image: POC, VA boundaries and unfinished markers, per theme, plus greyscale.
- E2E: toggle both markers in SCR-032 and assert the canvas and the SCR-045 table agree.
- Parity: POC/VA/unfinished flags covered exactly (not within tolerance) by E18-T06.

## Security notes
No new surface.

## Accessibility notes
POC and value-area status are conveyed by border/pattern plus a text label, **never fill colour alone** (CMP-110's stated contract, applied here to cells). The DOM-mirror label for a POC cell includes "point of control"; VA boundary cells include "value area high/low"; an unfinished-auction bar's mirror includes the explanation text rather than only a marker. Tooltips are keyboard-reachable. Marker changes on the forming bar are **not** announced (E18-D04 policy) — announcement happens on bar close only.

## Performance notes
Markers are sparse; target < 0.1 ms added at the target scene. The 10 Hz coalescing exists specifically to keep marker churn out of the frame budget.

## Observability
Metric `footprint_unfinished_auction_total{end}`, `footprint_poc_moves_per_bar` (histogram, a proxy for flicker risk).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios pass via automated tests.
- [ ] Flicker assertion green against a full-rate forming-bar replay.
- [ ] Golden images and greyscale evidence committed.
- [ ] `bar_poc_price` metric exposed and verified readable by the metrics registry (the contract E20 depends on).
- [ ] axe-core green; mirror labels verified.
- [ ] design-qa, QA sign-off, Sprint Review demo.
- [ ] PR merged with 2 approvals including a code owner.

E18-S01 (series and markers layer), E18-T02 (POC, value-area and auction computation).

title: Golden-fixture parity harness: served footprint vs offline DuckDB recomputation
body:
## Context
R2 exit criterion 6 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 6.3) is explicit: *"Footprint, profile, CVD and Deep-Stats values match an independent offline recomputation (DuckDB over the Parquet tier) for a full recorded symbol-day, within floating-point tolerance."* The R2 quality-gate table adds: *"Golden-fixture tests: one recorded symbol-day with expected footprint/profile/CVD/Deep-Stats outputs version-controlled; any drift fails CI."* This task builds E18's half of that harness - and because E18 is first in the train, it establishes the pattern E19/E20/E23 reuse.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A version-controlled golden fixture: one full recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day (trades tape plus instrument metadata), stored per the fixture conventions of `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, with a documented provenance note (date, source, size, checksum).
- An **independent** recomputation implemented in SQL over the DuckDB Parquet views - deliberately *not* sharing code with `FootprintEngine`, because a shared implementation would agree with itself. It computes per-(bar, price) bid/ask volume, delta, trade counts, per-bar delta/min_delta/max_delta, POC, value-area boundaries, diagonal imbalance flags and stacked runs, and unfinished/finished auction flags, for a fixed `FootprintConfig`.
- A comparator asserting equality within documented tolerances: volumes and deltas within 1e-9 relative, ratios within 1e-6, and **exact** equality for all integer and boolean fields (cell counts, trade counts, POC tick, VA boundaries, imbalance direction, stacked flags, unfinished flags) - a POC that is "nearly right" is wrong.
- Expected-output artefacts committed so a drift is visible as a reviewable diff, not only as a red test.
- CI wiring as a **required check** on any change under the orderflow or chart-engine packages.
- A second fixture set for the edge conditions the R2 integration gate names: high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol.
- A determinism assertion: recomputing the same window twice yields byte-identical output (feeds R2 exit criterion 7 and E26's replay determinism work).

## Out of scope
Profile, CVD and Deep-Stats parity (E19/E20/E23 extend the harness); replay double-run equality (E26); performance benchmarking (E18-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full symbol-day parity
  Given the golden fixture symbol-day and a fixed FootprintConfig
  When the served footprint window is compared with the DuckDB recomputation
  Then every cell, imbalance flag, stacked run, POC, value-area boundary and unfinished-auction flag matches within the documented tolerances

Scenario: Drift fails CI visibly
  Given a deliberate one-tick change to the POC tie-break order
  When CI runs
  Then the parity check fails and the diff names the affected bars and fields

Scenario: Edge fixtures are covered
  When the harness runs against the high-volatility, disconnect-resync, sequence-gap and thin-book fixtures
  Then parity holds, and for the gap fixture the harness asserts the gap is declared rather than silently interpolated

Scenario: Determinism
  When the same window is recomputed twice
  Then the outputs are byte-identical
```

## Technical notes / design
- The DuckDB implementation is the *specification executed a second way*: it is written directly from `24-internal-schemas.md` section 4 by a different engineer from the one who wrote `FootprintEngine`. State that reviewer requirement on the PR.
- Value-area expansion in SQL is awkward; implement it as a recursive CTE or a small deterministic Python-over-DuckDB routine that does not import engine code. Document which, and why, in the harness README.
- Tolerance rationale is recorded: floats accumulate differently under different summation orders, which is exactly why volumes get a relative tolerance while structural fields do not.
- Fixture size must stay reviewable - store the day as ZSTD Parquet and keep it under the repo's large-file policy; if it exceeds it, use the fixture-store mechanism defined in `03-testing-strategy.md` rather than committing a large binary.


**Estimate rationale (re-baselined 55-pt train fit):** 5 → 3. The five edge fixtures (high-volatility burst, disconnect+resync, sequence gap, thin-book, normal session) are recorded once by E18-Q02 and consumed here rather than authored twice; this ticket owns only the independent DuckDB recomputation, the comparator and the CI gate. The mutation/seeded-fault check is unchanged — the harness's job is to catch drift, and that is not where points were removed.

## Test plan
This ticket **is** test infrastructure. Its own verification: mutation testing - introduce each of five deliberate faults (wrong side attribution, off-by-one diagonal offset, zero-policy ignored, POC tie-break reordered, VA target using 0.7 of cell count instead of volume) and assert the harness catches all five. A harness that passes a known-broken engine is worthless.

## Security notes
The fixture is recorded public market data - no PII, no credentials. Confirm no API keys or account identifiers leaked into the recorded capture before committing (automated secrets scan over the fixture as part of the PR).

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The parity run must complete within the CI budget; target <= 5 minutes for the full symbol-day. If it exceeds that, shard by bar range and run the shards in parallel rather than reducing coverage.

## Observability
CI job emits the comparison summary (bars compared, fields compared, max observed deviation per field class) as a build artefact so slow drift is visible before it breaks the tolerance.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Golden fixture committed with provenance and checksum.
- [ ] Independent DuckDB recomputation implemented by a different engineer from the engine author, and that is recorded on the PR.
- [ ] Comparator with documented tolerances; structural fields compared exactly.
- [ ] Mutation test proving the harness catches all five seeded faults.
- [ ] Required CI check wired for orderflow and chart-engine paths.
- [ ] Edge fixtures covered; determinism assertion green.
- [ ] Harness README written so E19/E20/E23 can extend it without asking.

## Dependencies

`feat/e18-footprint-golden-parity`

title: Write ADR-0016 footprint aggregation and text-LOD strategy, update plan docs
body:
## Context
E18 makes three architectural decisions that later epics inherit and must not silently re-litigate: (1) cells persist at native tick resolution and every analytical parameter is display-time, (2) cell text is rendered from an SDF atlas with a measured, hysteretic LOD ladder rather than DOM or per-frame canvas text, and (3) correctness is defended by an independently implemented offline recomputation rather than by self-consistent unit tests. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 5.2 requires a spike's decision to be recorded as an ADR; E18-K01 is that spike.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0021-footprint-aggregation-and-text-lod.md` in the existing ADR format (context, decision, status, consequences, alternatives considered), covering:
  - **Storage-time vs display-time split**, with the consequence that changing ratio/stack/VA/grouping is instant and only an input-source change triggers a rebuild.
  - **Measured `lodTextThresholdPx`** per density class from E18-K01, the cell-budget collapse threshold, and the +/-15% hysteresis dead band; alternatives rejected (fixed threshold, DOM text, per-frame canvas text) with the measured reasons.
  - **Any mitigation adopted** under E18-K01 question 2 if the glyph budget was exceeded.
  - **Independent-recomputation testing strategy** as the correctness defence for all R2 order-flow epics, with the explicit "different engineer writes the second implementation" rule.
  - Runtime-parity findings (Chromium / Electron / Tauri-WebView2) and their input to ADR-0011 if any.
- Doc updates where implementation diverged: `24-internal-schemas.md` section 4, `23-ws-protocol.md` section 6.1/14.4, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `21-database-schema.md` section 4.9, `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 8, `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030/SCR-032, `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-109/CMP-182.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` update for R2 (render performance) and R8 (browser/GPU compat) based on what was measured.
- A short "how footprint works" section in the developer docs so E19/E20/E23/E26 implementers do not re-derive the model.

## Out of scope
New decisions - this records decisions already made and measured; anything genuinely undecided gets its own spike rather than a hand-wave in the ADR.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR records numbers, not intentions
  When ADR-0016 is reviewed
  Then every threshold it states is a measured value with its measurement conditions and runtime named

Scenario: Divergences are reconciled
  Given implementation diverged from any plan document
  Then that document is updated in the same change and the divergence is listed in the ADR consequences

Scenario: A later epic can rely on it
  Given an E19 implementer reading only ADR-0016 and 24-internal-schemas.md section 4
  Then they can state which footprint parameters require a rebuild and which do not, without asking
```

## Technical notes / design
Follow the format of the existing ADRs (e.g. `ADR-0003-storage-tiers.md`). Status `Accepted`. Supersedes nothing; referenced by ADR-0002 (custom engine) and ADR-0011 (Electron vs Tauri) where the runtime-parity numbers are relevant - add the cross-reference links in both directions.

## Security notes
N/A - ensure no measured host identifiers, internal hostnames or fixture credentials leak into the ADR.

## Accessibility notes
The ADR must state the a11y consequence of the LOD decision explicitly: below the text threshold the DOM mirror is the only carrier of cell values, so the mirror's completeness is a hard invariant, not an optimisation target.

## Performance notes
The ADR is the durable home for the footprint performance numbers; E18-Q03's CI benchmark thresholds are set from it, so the two must not disagree.

## Observability
N/A.

title: Black-box test plan for the E19 profile story groups
body:
## Context
E19 turns the raw trade tape into the structural picture traders actually trade off: volume-by-price, delta-by-price, TPO/time-at-price, POC, value area, HVN/LVN and naked POCs. Unlike footprint (E18), a profile is an *aggregate with a derived verdict* - the POC price and the VAH/VAL pair are single numbers a trader places orders against, and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12 publishes `profile_poc`, `profile_vah`, `profile_val` as **exact** metrics consumable by alerts (E40) and the rule engine. A one-row error in value-area expansion is invisible on screen and wrong in a rule.

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 makes a recorded black-box QA pass non-skippable per Story, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 11 requires a written per-feature test plan plus a white-box review checklist. The E19 engineering tickets state *what to build*; nothing today lets a QA engineer execute "profiles are correct and behave as specified" against a staging build.

This ticket produces that artefact, deliberately black-box: written against `SCR-038` / `SCR-039`, the public contract `GET /api/v1/market/profile` and the WS topic `profile.{symbol}.{kind}`, so it survives refactoring of the in-RAM period accumulators described in `24-internal-schemas.md` section 5.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e19-profiles-test-plan.md`, organised as six executable groups:
  1. **Session profile & live update** (US-VP-001) - `SCR-038`; CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge; `GET /api/v1/market/profile?kind=volume&split=session`, WS `profile.{symbol}.volume`; incremental update per print, full 24 h rebuild <= 1 s, "approximated from bars" badge when ticks are missing.
  2. **Period modes** (US-VP-002, US-VP-003) - fixed range, visible range (throttled <= 10 Hz, debounce on pan end), anchored, composite over N sessions and session-multiples; `split=composite|session|fixed`, `session_anchor=utc_day|funding_8h|custom`, `session_anchor_time`, `fixed_duration_minutes`; recorder-limited composite states the covered range explicitly via `meta.recording_started_at`.
  3. **POC / value area / developing VA** (US-VP-004) - `value_area_pct` 50..95 default 70, `poc_price`, `value_area_high`, `value_area_low`; closest-to-range-midpoint tie-break surfaced in the tooltip; single-step expansion approximation exactly as documented on `/market/profile`.
  4. **Node & level detection** (US-VP-005, US-VP-006) - `include_hvn_lvn`, `hvn[]`/`lvn[]` prominence-threshold sensitivity; naked/virgin POC carry-forward, flip-on-retest demotion with history toggle, nearest-N clutter cap with a count of hidden levels.
  5. **Delta & TPO representations** (US-VP-007, US-VP-008) - `kind=delta` signed rows with direction glyph, zero-delta rows distinct from never-traded rows, side-by-side volume+delta sharing one price axis; `kind=tpo` with `tpo_period_minutes` default 30, letter assignment A..Z,a..z,AA.., initial-balance marking, single-print glyph toggle.
  6. **Settings, presets & validation** (US-VP-009) - `SCR-039` (CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-031 ColorSwatch, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-228 PreviewTile); preset apply/save, `price_grouping` clamped to one tick with an explanatory message, range longer than recorded history warns rather than blocks, presets included in workspace export.
- Per case: id `E19-TC-<group><nn>`, preconditions (named fixture), steps, expected result, the `US-VP-*` id verified, the child ticket covered, and automation status (automated in `E19-Q02` / `E19-Q03`, or manual-only with a reason).
- **Fixture appendix**: a recorded 24 h `BTCUSDT` tape with a hand-computed POC/VAH/VAL; a two-way tie fixture at maximum volume; a session containing a tick-size (`metadata_version`) change; a symbol with kline history only (approximation path); a 30-session composite where only 12 sessions are recorded; a thin altcoin with fewer than 20 traded price levels.
- **Traceability table** US-VP-001..009 x cases x automation status, following `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` section 2.9.
- **White-box review checklist**: incremental accumulator and full rebuild produce identical output; `Decimal` conversion at the metrics/OMS boundary per `24-internal-schemas.md` C3; no double counting of split volume bars / renko bars carrying `volume_allocated=False`; the 5 s QuestDB flush is idempotent on replay.
- Defect severity mapping per `03-testing-strategy.md` section 11.3; "POC/VAH/VAL disagrees with the hand-computed fixture" is always `priority/p0`.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell correctness (E18) - this plan asserts only that profiles agree with the footprint aggregate totals, not the aggregates themselves.
- CVD / delta pane semantics (E23) and VWAP band maths; the VWAP +/-sigma overlay is checked only for presence and price-axis alignment.
- Performance, chaos and a11y execution (`E19-Q04`, `E19-Q05`, `E19-Q06`) and adversarial input (`E19-X02`), which are referenced, not duplicated.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Plan covers every VP story
  Given the published qa/plans/e19-profiles-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 9
  Then each of US-VP-001..009 maps to at least one case per Gherkin scenario in its story, including the stated edge case
  And every case names the screen, endpoint or WS topic it exercises

Scenario: A case is executable by someone new to the epic
  Given a QA engineer who has not worked on E19
  When they execute group 3 against a staging build using only the fixture appendix
  Then they reach a pass/fail verdict on every case without asking the authors a question

Scenario: Failure case - value area must be reproducible, not eyeballed
  Given the hand-computed fixture with a known VAH and VAL at value_area_pct=70
  When the API response and the rendered panel are compared to the fixture
  Then the plan requires an exact decimal match and fails the case on any deviation, forbidding "looks right" as evidence

Scenario: Edge case - tie for maximum volume
  Given two price levels with identical maximum volume
  When the POC is computed
  Then the plan requires the closest-to-range-midpoint tie-break, the same result on repeated runs, and the rule stated in the POC tooltip

Scenario: Edge case - history shorter than the requested window
  Given a 30-session composite where only 12 sessions are recorded
  When the profile is requested
  Then the plan requires the "Partial: only 12 of 30 requested days recorded" chip and a profile built from what exists, never a silently short profile

Scenario: Plan is reviewed and merged
  When the plan PR is opened
  Then it carries approvals from the E19 order-flow lead and the SDET, and is linked from the E19 epic ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- Structure mirrors `qa/plans/e18-footprint-test-plan.md` so QA can move between order-flow epics without relearning a format.
- Oracle strategy: every numeric case has an **independent oracle** - a small pandas/NumPy implementation under `qa/fixtures/e19/oracle/` that recomputes POC/VA/HVN/LVN from raw fixture trades. The oracle must not import production engine code; being a second implementation is the point.
- Approximation cases are labelled: the single-step value-area expansion is an accepted deviation from textbook two-row TPO expansion (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/profile`), so cases assert conformance to the documented algorithm, not to a textbook.
- Cheapest global detector, included in every group: for the same window, `sum(rows.volume)` from `/market/profile` must equal the footprint aggregate total and the bar-volume total within the documented quantisation tolerance.

## Test plan
- This ticket is itself a test artefact; verification is peer review by a second SDET plus a dry run of one case from each group against the current staging build, with dry-run evidence recorded in the PR.
- Every case declares automation status, so `E19-Q02` and `E19-Q03` have an unambiguous backlog of cases to automate.

## Security notes
- Fixtures contain public market data only - no account ids, API keys or PII; fixture files are stored via git-lfs with a size cap and no production dumps.
- Adversarial parameter cases (`price_grouping` extremes, unbounded `from`/`to`, `value_area_pct` boundaries) are delegated to `E19-X02`; this plan must not encourage unbounded-window requests against shared staging.
- Execution is performed with a `marketdata:read`-only principal so accidental privilege reliance is caught.

## Accessibility notes
- Each group contains at least one case exercising the `SCR-038` table alternative: every price row exposed with volume, delta and value-area membership, and POC/VAH/VAL announced.
- Colour is never the sole pass criterion; expected results name the text, pattern or border affordance per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- The deep audit is `E19-Q06`; this plan guarantees only that a11y is present in routine functional execution.

## Performance notes
- Functional cases carry story NFRs inline as pass/fail conditions: full 24 h rebuild <= 1 s; visible-range recompute throttled to <= 10 Hz with pan-end debounce and >= 55 fps interaction; composite of 30 sessions from the cold tier <= 2 s; row-size/period re-bucket <= 300 ms in a worker; up to 5 000 rendered rows.
- Statistical rigour (percentiles, hardware matrix) belongs to `E19-Q04`; functional cases fail only on gross violations.

## Observability
- Each case names required evidence: HAR or WS frame capture, the `x-request-id` of the `/market/profile` call, an `SCR-038` screenshot, and the oracle diff.
- Results are recorded in the QA run sheet linked from the epic; failures open bugs labelled `area/order-flow` carrying the `E19-TC-*` id in the title.

## Definition of Done
- Plan merged under `qa/plans/`, all nine US-VP stories traceable, fixture appendix complete and the fixtures actually present in `qa/fixtures/e19/`.
- Dry run of one case per group executed and recorded; two approvals (order-flow lead + SDET).
- Automation status agreed with the owners of `E19-Q02` and `E19-Q03`, and those tickets reference the case ids.

title: Profile correctness conformance suite: oracle, golden fixtures and contracts
body:
## Context
Profiles publish *decisions*, not just pixels: `profile_poc`, `profile_vah` and `profile_val` are declared **exact** metrics in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12 and are consumed by alerts and the rule engine. A drift of one row silently moves where a rule arms. Rendering tests cannot catch that; only a numeric oracle can.

`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires contract tests against `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` plus golden-fixture integration tests over recorded Bybit data. This ticket builds the automated correctness backbone for E19 so every later change - LOD row merging, composite cold-tier queries, TPO letters, naked-POC state - is regression-guarded.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Oracle package** `qa/fixtures/e19/oracle/`: an independent pandas/NumPy implementation of price bucketing at `price_grouping`, volume / delta / TPO accumulation, POC selection with midpoint tie-break, single-step value-area expansion at any `value_area_pct`, HVN/LVN prominence detection and naked-POC carry-forward. It must not import production engine modules.
- **Golden fixtures** under `qa/fixtures/e19/` with expected JSON: 24 h `BTCUSDT` session; `funding_8h` anchored session; `custom` anchor at `13:30`; 5-session composite and the same window as session multiples; a two-way POC tie; a thin symbol with fewer than 20 levels; a tick-size change mid-session; a kline-only symbol (approximation path); a tape producing split volume bars and renko bars to prove no double counting.
- **Engine tests** asserting production output equals oracle output for every fixture x `kind` in {volume, delta, tpo} x `value_area_pct` in {50, 68, 70, 95} x `price_grouping` in {1, 5, 50}.
- **Incremental-vs-rebuild equivalence**: feed the tape print-by-print through the incremental accumulator, then force a full rebuild from QuestDB, and assert identical `ProfileResponse` payloads including row order and totals.
- **Restart/flush test**: kill the engine 3 s after a flush, restart, top up from raw trades, assert equality with the uninterrupted run.
- **Contract tests**: `GET /api/v1/market/profile` validated against `ProfileResponse`; WS `profile.{symbol}.{kind}` frames validated against `cv://ws/v1/profile.schema.json` (section 14.6) including `additionalProperties:false`, key composition (`kind`, `split`, `session_anchor`, `price_grouping`, `value_area_pct`) and monotonic per-topic sequence numbers.
- **Cross-consistency test**: `sum(rows.volume)` equals the footprint aggregate total and the bar-volume total for the same window within the documented tolerance.
- CI wiring: runs on every PR touching the profile engine, the profile API router or the engine profile plugin; seeded mutations must fail.

## Out of scope
- UI rendering and interaction (`E19-Q03`); throughput and latency measurement (`E19-Q04`).
- Fuzzing and abusive input (`E19-X02`) - this suite uses valid inputs only.
- Alert/rule evaluation of the published metrics (E40 suites).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Production matches the independent oracle
  Given every golden fixture in qa/fixtures/e19
  When the production profile engine and the oracle both compute the profile
  Then poc_price, value_area_high, value_area_low, every row volume/buy_volume/sell_volume/delta/tpo_count and the hvn and lvn lists are exactly equal

Scenario: Incremental equals rebuild
  Given a 24 h tape replayed print-by-print into the incremental accumulator
  When a full rebuild from QuestDB is executed for the same period
  Then both produce identical ProfileResponse payloads including row order and totals

Scenario: Failure case - engine restart mid-period loses nothing
  Given the engine is killed 3 seconds after the last 5 second flush
  When it restarts and tops up from raw trades
  Then the resulting profile equals the uninterrupted run and no row is double counted

Scenario: Edge case - tick-size change invalidates and rebuilds
  Given a metadata_version bump mid-session
  When the profile is requested
  Then cached periods for that symbol are invalidated, a rebuild is scheduled, and the served profile is bucketed at the new tick size with no mixed-grid rows

Scenario: Contract drift fails CI
  Given a change that adds an undeclared field to a ProfileUpdate frame
  When the contract tests run
  Then the suite fails with a schema violation naming the field

Scenario: Regression guard bites
  Given a deliberately mutated value-area expansion that stops one row early
  When the suite runs
  Then at least one golden fixture fails and names the differing price level
```

## Technical notes / design
- Determinism: the oracle does all price/size maths in `Decimal` quantised to the symbol tick and qty step. Production may use floats internally per `24-internal-schemas.md` C3, but comparison happens on quantised decimal strings so float noise cannot mask a real defect.
- Fixtures store a compressed trade tape plus `expected/*.json`; regenerating expectations requires an explicit `--bless` flag and a reviewer, so expectations can never be silently rewritten to match a bug.
- TPO letters are asserted as a sequence including the rolls `Z -> a` and `z -> AA`, with initial-balance marking at `ib_periods=2` and single-print rows flagged.
- Naked POC: a three-session fixture where session 1's POC is retraded in session 3 asserts exactly one naked-to-tested flip and that the state is server-side so panes and users agree.
- The cross-consistency tolerance derives from the quantisation step and is documented; widening it requires an ADR note, not a commit.

## Test plan
- Unit: bucketing, tie-break, expansion, prominence, letter assignment, naked-POC state machine.
- Integration: engine <-> QuestDB <-> REST over recorded fixtures, plus the cold-tier composite path.
- Contract: OpenAPI and WS JSON Schema validation in both directions (valid frames pass, malformed frames rejected).
- Mutation guard: at least three seeded mutations (tie-break reversed, expansion off-by-one, delta sign flipped) each demonstrated to fail.
- Coverage: the profile engine package meets the >= 85% backend line-coverage threshold from the planning brief.

## Security notes
- Fixtures are public market data only; no account ids, keys or PII, and no production database dumps.
- The suite authenticates with a `marketdata:read`-only principal, proving the endpoints neither require nor leak elevated scope.
- Oracle code executes headlessly in CI with no network access, so no fixture is fetched from a third party at test time and supply-chain surface stays flat.

## Accessibility notes
- Not directly applicable (non-UI suite). It does emit the canonical per-row table used as the expected content for the `SCR-038` table alternative in `E19-Q06`, so the a11y audit compares against verified numbers rather than scraped pixels.

## Performance notes
- The suite completes in <= 8 minutes on CI; fixtures are sized to that budget (one 24 h tape, the rest shorter).
- A soft assertion records rebuild wall-clock per fixture so performance trends are visible here even though hard budgets live in `E19-Q04`.

## Observability
- CI publishes a JUnit report plus an expected-vs-actual row diff artefact for every failure, so a failing POC is debuggable without local reproduction.
- Integration runs assert the engine emits `profile_rebuild_duration_seconds` and `profile_rows_total`, which doubles as a check that the metrics required by `E19-Q04` exist.

## Definition of Done
- Suite merged, green on `main`, wired into required checks for the touched paths.
- Every US-VP story has at least one automated assertion traced from an `E19-Q01` case id.
- Seeded mutations demonstrated to fail, with evidence in the PR.
- `qa/fixtures/e19/README.md` records fixture provenance, size and regeneration procedure.

## Dependencies
- `E19-T01` ProfileEngine and QuestDB table, `E19-T02` REST endpoint, `E19-T03` WS topic, `E19-Q01` case ids.
- Recorded tapes from E16; footprint aggregates from E18 for cross-consistency; WS contract harness from E17.

title: Session volume profile with live update and approximated-from-bars fallback
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-001 — Session volume profile (Must)**: "a histogram of volume by price is drawn for the current session, updating live", with row size changeable from the legend and an explicit *approximate* badge where tick history is missing. This is the first end-to-end vertical slice of the Epic — engine → REST bootstrap → WS tail → renderer → **SCR-038** — and it proves the pipeline every later VP story reuses.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-038** Profile panel: docked or overlaid, symbol-bound, period selector defaulting to *Session*, input selector defaulting to *Volume*, row-size control in the legend (**CMP-199** ChartLegend), price axis shared with the host chart (**CMP-188**).
- Session anchoring: `utc_day` default, `funding_8h` and custom `HH:MM` offered (crypto has no RTH — `24-internal-schemas.md` §5.1 `anchor_utc_min`).
- Bootstrap via `GET /api/v1/market/profile?kind=volume&split=session`, live tail via `profile.{symbol}.volume`, sequence-gap re-bootstrap.
- States per SCR-038: loading · partial history chip ("Partial: only 12 of 30 requested days recorded") · no history empty state (**CMP-026**) with a "Record this symbol" CTA for the owner · **approximated-from-bars** chip (**CMP-227** EstimatedBadge) when the window predates tick recording.
- Hover readout: per-row volume, buy/sell split and price, from exact stored values.
- Accessible table alternative listing every row.

## Out of scope
- POC/VAH/VAL and value-area shading (**E19-S04**) — this story ships the raw histogram only.
- Delta mode (**E19-S07**), TPO (**E19-S08**), non-session periods (**E19-S02**), composites (**E19-S03**).
- Settings dialog and presets (**E19-S09**); the legend's row-size control is the only setting here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Session profile
  Given the UTC day boundary
  Then a histogram of volume by price is drawn for the current session, updating live

Scenario: Row size
  When I change the row size
  Then the profile re-buckets immediately and the row size is shown in the legend

Scenario: No tick history
  Given prints are unavailable before a timestamp
  Then the profile is built from bar-approximated volume for that portion with an "approximate" badge

Scenario: Nothing recorded at all
  Given the symbol has never been recorded
  Then the empty state states when history would begin and offers the owner a record action, instead of drawing an empty axis

Scenario: Live tail survives a disconnect
  Given the WS drops for 30 s and reconnects
  Then the profile re-bootstraps from REST and no level is double counted or lost

Scenario: Row size below tick size
  When a row size smaller than the instrument tick size is entered
  Then it is clamped to one tick and the clamp is explained in the legend
```

## Technical notes / design
The panel is a host for the T04 series plugin, not a second renderer. Re-bucketing on a row-size change is worker-local (T04's cached histogram) so it is instant and offline-capable; only a *period* change triggers a new REST call. Double-counting on reconnect is prevented structurally: each WS frame carries the complete current period, so a re-bootstrap replaces rather than merges. Bar-approximated portions are computed from klines and kept in a **separate** accumulator from tick-derived levels, merged only at render time with the approximate flag — so switching the window later never leaves silently mixed data.

## Test plan
Unit: legend row-size control, clamp messaging, state machine (loading/partial/empty/approximate). Integration: fixture with a recording start inside the window; disconnect/reconnect. E2E (Playwright): session profile renders and updates against a scripted WS fixture; row-size change re-buckets without a network request (asserted on the request log); empty and approximate states. Visual: golden images for each state. Perf: 24 h session initial render ≤ 1 s.

## Security notes
`marketdata:read` only; the owner-only "Record this symbol" CTA is RBAC-gated and its absence for non-owners is enforced server-side, not merely hidden. No user input reaches a query beyond the bounded parameters validated in T02.

## Accessibility notes
The table alternative is a real `<table>` with price, volume, buy, sell and (later) VA membership columns, reachable by keyboard and announced with row/column headers. The approximate and partial-history chips are text, announced politely on state change, never colour-only. The row-size control is a labelled numeric input with its unit in the label ("Row size (ticks)"). axe-core green.

## Performance notes
Full 24 h session rebuild ≤ 1 s (US-VP-001 NFR); incremental update per print; re-bucket ≤ 300 ms in the worker; ≤ 5 000 rows with merging below 2 px.

## Observability
Analytics `profile.period_changed`, `profile.mode_changed`, `profile.row_size_changed`, `profile.approximate_shown`. Metrics inherited from T01–T04 plus `ui_profile_bootstrap_duration_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on touched modules.
- [ ] axe-core green; screen-reader pass on the table alternative.
- [ ] Golden images approved; design-qa sign-off against the SCR-038 checklist; demoed.

`blocked_by`: **E19-T03** (live tail), **E19-T04** (renderer). Blocks **E19-S04**, **E19-S02**.

`feat/e19-session-volume-profile`
