title: Fixed-range, visible-range and anchored profiles with throttled recompute
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-002 — Fixed-range, visible-range and anchored profiles (Must/Should)**. A session profile answers one question; these three answer every other one — "what happened in *this* move", "what does the current view say", "what has accumulated since *that* bar". The roadmap lists "profile anchoring to drawings and to sessions" in the E19 scope line, so the anchored mode binds to a chart anchor rather than a fixed timestamp typed into a dialog. The hard constraint is performance: "visible-range recompute throttled to ≤10 Hz with a debounce on pan end" and "interaction stays at ≥55 fps".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Fixed range**: drag a range selection on the time axis → a profile pinned to exactly those timestamps, surviving pan, zoom, reload and interval change (`ProfilePeriod.kind = fixed_range`).
- **Visible range**: recomputes as the viewport changes, throttled to ≤10 Hz with a debounce on pan/zoom end; a stale-while-recomputing state rather than a blank pane.
- **Anchored**: anchor at a bar (or at an existing drawing's anchor, per the roadmap's "anchoring to drawings") and accumulate forward indefinitely; the anchor is a `{t}` in chart space, invariant across bar-type and scale changes exactly as drawing anchors are.
- Range handles: move and resize a fixed range from the chart; the range and its duration shown in the legend.
- Bootstrap/streaming: fixed and anchored periods stream live via WS when their end is open; visible-range recompute is worker-local from cached raw data, falling back to a REST fetch only when the viewport leaves the cached window.
- Multiple concurrent profile instances per pane, each with its own period, respecting the per-connection subscription cap from **E19-T03**.

## Out of scope
- Composite/multi-session periods (**E19-S03**) and the settings dialog (**E19-S09**).
- Swing-anchored auto-detection (SCR-039 lists "Swing-anchored" as a period type; automatic swing detection is **E25** — this story supports a manual anchor only).
- Replay-time period behaviour — **E26**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fixed range
  When I drag a range selection
  Then a profile is computed for exactly that window and stays pinned to those timestamps

Scenario: Visible range
  Given visible-range mode
  Then the profile recomputes as I pan and zoom, throttled so interaction stays at >= 55 fps

Scenario: Anchored
  When I anchor at a specific bar
  Then the profile accumulates forward from that bar and can be extended indefinitely

Scenario: Anchors survive a bar-type change
  Given an anchored profile on 1m time bars
  When the chart switches to 500-tick bars and back
  Then the anchor resolves to the same timestamp and the accumulated profile is unchanged

Scenario: Viewport leaves the cached window
  Given the visible range is panned beyond the cached raw histogram
  Then a bounded REST fetch tops up the cache, the pane shows a recomputing state, and interaction is not blocked

Scenario: Degenerate range
  When a range selection is shorter than one bar or has zero duration
  Then no period is created and the selection is cancelled with a hint
```

## Technical notes / design
All three modes are the same `ProfilePeriod` with different `kind`/bounds, so the engine and renderer need no new code paths — this story is period lifecycle plus interaction. Visible-range is deliberately client-side: a server round-trip per pan frame is exactly the real-time-cost risk (R3) the WS backpressure ladder exists to avoid, so the worker re-aggregates its cached raw histogram and the server is consulted only on a cache miss. Throttling uses a leading-edge 10 Hz gate plus a trailing debounce on pan end, so the user sees motion immediately and an exact result when they stop.

## Test plan
Unit: period construction per mode, range-handle maths, throttle/debounce gate, cache-miss detection. Property-based: anchored period anchor `(t)` invariant across random bar specs and scale modes (the same property E14 uses for drawing anchors). E2E: drag-create a fixed range and reload; visible-range pan with an fps assertion; anchor and extend. Perf: pan/zoom in visible-range mode sustains ≥55 fps with a 5 000-row profile; recompute rate measured ≤10 Hz.

## Security notes
Each concurrent period is a server-side resource: the per-pane instance count and the per-connection subscription cap from T03 are enforced server-side, so a scripted client cannot open unbounded periods. Cache top-up requests use the same bounded parameters as T02.

## Accessibility notes
Range selection has a keyboard path: the range can be created and resized from the keyboard by stepping bar-by-bar with `Enter` to confirm, mirroring the E14 keyboard drawing pattern; the selected range's start, end and duration are announced. Mode selection is a labelled radio group (SCR-039 pattern). The recomputing state is announced politely, not as an alert.

## Performance notes
≤10 Hz recompute with a pan-end debounce; ≥55 fps sustained; worker re-aggregation ≤ 8 ms at p95 per the R4 budget; cache top-up bounded and asynchronous.

`profile_visible_range_recompute_ms`, `profile_cache_miss_total`, `profile_active_periods{period_kind}`; analytics `profile.period_changed{kind}`, `profile.range_created`, `profile.anchor_set`.

title: POC, configurable value area and developing VA with deterministic tie-breaks
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-004 — POC and value area (Must)**. A profile without a value area is decoration; POC/VAH/VAL are what traders actually act on, and the story's NFR makes them a platform capability: "POC/VAH/VAL exposed as metrics to alerts and rules." The algorithms are fixed by `24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2 and §4.5: POC tie-break chain (closest to period VWAP → closest to last price → lower ticks) and single-step value-area expansion with the `two_row_tpo` alternative, both unit-tested against the same fixture. The roadmap scope line additionally requires **developing vs final value area**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- POC computation with the documented tie-break chain, exposed with the applied rule so the tooltip can state it (US-VP-004 scenario "Ties": "the tie-break rule … is applied deterministically and documented in the tooltip").
- Value area: default 70 %, configurable 50–95 (REST bound), recomputed immediately on change and persisted **per profile type**; `value_area_algorithm ∈ {single_step, two_row_tpo}` per §4.5's note on open question #9.
- Rendering: POC line, VAH/VAL lines with text labels, value-area shading, all through the T04 plugin's flags; "extend POC/VA lines to the right" option (SCR-039 list).
- **Developing POC/VA**: `developing_poc` path sampled every `developing_interval_ms` (default 60 000) and drawn as the developing-value-area ribbon, toggleable; final vs developing visually and textually distinguished.
- Metric exposure: POC, VAH, VAL (and the developing values) published on the internal metric bus under stable names so **E40** alerts and the **E35** rule engine can bind to them.

## Out of scope
- HVN/LVN (**E19-S05**), naked POC (**E19-S06**) — they build on this story's POC.
- Actually creating alerts or rule conditions on these metrics — **E40** / **E35** consume the exposed names.
- TPO-based POC/VA (**E19-S08** reuses this algorithm with `tpo_count` in place of `volume`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Default 70%
  Then the value area containing 70% of volume around the POC is shaded, with VAH and VAL labelled

Scenario: Configurable
  When I set 68%
  Then VA recomputes immediately and the setting persists per profile type

Scenario: Ties
  Given two price levels tie for maximum volume
  Then the tie-break rule (closest to the range midpoint) is applied deterministically and documented in the tooltip

Scenario: Value area agrees with the per-bar algorithm
  Given the same fixture cells scoped to one bar and to a period
  Then the per-bar POC/VA from E18 and the period POC/VA from this story use the identical expansion algorithm and never contradict each other on the same input

Scenario: Developing value area
  Given a session in progress
  Then the developing POC/VA ribbon updates at the configured interval and is visually and textually distinct from the final value area

Scenario: Exhausted side
  Given the value-area expansion exhausts one side of the histogram before reaching the target
  Then expansion continues on the remaining side and terminates exactly at the target percentage
```

## Technical notes / design
Computation lives in `ProfileEngine` (shared with the per-bar implementation from E18 — one function, two scopes, per §4.5 "using the same algorithm as §5 so that per-bar and session profiles never disagree"). Ties absorb **both** sides when the adjacent volumes are equal, as specified. The developing path is appended, never recomputed from scratch, so the ribbon is O(1) per sample. Metric names are frozen in this story (`profile.poc`, `profile.vah`, `profile.val`, `profile.developing_poc`) because E40/E35 will bind to them; renaming later is a breaking change.

## Test plan
Unit (≥85%): expansion algorithm against hand-computed fixtures incl. exhausted-side and both-tie cases; both `value_area_algorithm` variants against the same fixture; tie-break chain at each level of the chain. Property-based: VA always contains the POC; VA volume ≥ target and removing the last absorbed level drops it below target (minimality). Cross-check: E18 per-bar vs E19 period on identical input. E2E: change VA % and observe immediate recompute and persistence; tooltip states the tie-break. Visual: golden images with shading and labels in both themes.

## Security notes
VA percentage is bounded server-side (50–95 per OpenAPI) regardless of client input. Exposed metrics are read-only market data under `marketdata:read`; binding them to rules that place orders is governed by the rule engine's own arming and RBAC, not by this story.

## Accessibility notes
POC/VAH/VAL are labelled with text and distinguished by line style as well as colour; value-area shading meets contrast against both themes and is never the sole indicator of membership — the table alternative gains a "in value area" column and announces POC/VAH/VAL rows explicitly. The VA % control is a labelled numeric input with its range stated; invalid values are announced with an error message, not just a red border.

## Performance notes
VA expansion is O(levels) with a single pass from the POC outward; recompute on a VA % change is worker-local and ≤ 50 ms for a session profile. The developing ribbon adds one sample per `developing_interval_ms` (default 60 s) — negligible.

## Observability
`profile_va_compute_duration_ms`, `profile_poc_tiebreak_total{rule}` (which link of the chain resolved the tie — a useful data-quality signal), analytics `profile.va_percent_changed`, `profile.developing_toggled`.

- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Cross-check test against E18 per-bar POC/VA green.
- [ ] Metric names published in `24-internal-schemas.md` terms and referenced by the E40 backlog item.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% engine / ≥80% frontend; axe-core green; design-qa sign-off; demoed.

`feat/e19-poc-value-area`

title: Delta profile with split bid/ask rows and side-by-side combined view
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-007 — Delta profile (Must)**: "each price row shows net delta with sign, direction glyph and colour", with a combined volume+delta view sharing one price axis, and zero-delta rows rendered distinctly from rows with no trading at all. Its NFR is the architectural constraint that shaped E19-K01: "derived from the same aggregate store as footprint" — the delta profile must never disagree with the footprint pane about who bought.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `kind=delta` end to end: REST `?kind=delta`, WS `profile.{symbol}.delta`, renderer delta mode.
- Row rendering: signed bar from a zero baseline, sign glyph (▲/▼) and colour, magnitude by |delta|; the **split** rendering mode (bid vs ask volume back-to-back on one row) as the roadmap's "split (bid/ask) profile rendering".
- Combined view: volume and delta profiles drawn adjacently sharing one price axis and one row bucketing, docked on the same side or opposite sides.
- Three-way row state: traded with non-zero delta · traded with exactly zero net delta · not traded at all — visually and textually distinct (the last is absent, not zero).
- Delta POC/VA reuse of **E19-S04**'s algorithm over |delta| where meaningful, with the limitation documented in the legend.
- Cross-consistency test against the E18 footprint aggregate for the same window.

## Out of scope
- CVD as a time series and delta panes — **E23**.
- Imbalance detection / stacked-imbalance marking — **E25**.
- Trade-side classification itself — owned by E18's aggregation (this story consumes `buy_volume`/`sell_volume`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Delta profile
  Then each price row shows net delta with sign, direction glyph and colour

Scenario: Side-by-side
  When I enable the combined view
  Then volume and delta profiles render adjacently sharing one price axis

Scenario: Zero-delta rows
  Then rows with zero net delta render distinctly from rows with no trading at all

Scenario: Delta agrees with footprint
  Given the same symbol and window
  When the footprint pane's cells are summed by price
  Then every level's buy_volume, sell_volume and delta match the delta profile exactly

Scenario: Row bucketing stays shared in combined view
  When the row size is changed in combined view
  Then both profiles re-bucket identically and remain row-aligned on the shared price axis
```

## Technical notes / design
No second engine: `ProfileLevel` already carries `buy_volume`, `sell_volume` and `delta`, so delta mode is a renderer projection plus a REST/WS `kind`. That is exactly why the consistency test is cheap and mandatory — if it ever fails, the bug is in E18's aggregation, not here. The signed bar uses a zero baseline placed at the profile's horizontal centre in split mode and at the docked edge in signed mode. Colour follows the locked convention (green = buy/bid, red = sell/ask) with the colour-blind-safe blue/orange alternative available from theme settings.

## Test plan
Unit: signed geometry and baseline placement, zero vs absent row classification, combined-view bucket sharing. Integration: delta-vs-footprint consistency over recorded fixtures, including a fixture with heavy one-sided flow. E2E: mode switch, combined view, row-size change in combined view. Visual: golden images for signed and split modes, both themes and the colour-blind-safe palette.

## Security notes
No new surface beyond the `kind=delta` value already enumerated in OpenAPI and the WS topic key. Read-only, `marketdata:read`.

## Accessibility notes
Delta direction is never colour-only: sign, glyph and the numeric value all carry it, and the table alternative adds signed delta and buy/sell columns. "No trading at this price" is announced as such rather than as "zero". The colour-blind-safe palette is selectable and golden-imaged. Contrast of both delta colours verified against both themes.

## Performance notes
Delta mode adds no engine cost (same accumulators). Combined view draws two instanced batches sharing one scale — still within the ≤ 8 ms R4 budget; measured in the B-profile benchmark with the combined case included.

## Observability
Analytics `profile.mode_changed{mode=delta}`, `profile.combined_view_toggled`, `profile.split_rows_toggled`. Metric `profile_delta_consistency_failures_total` emitted by the periodic self-check against footprint aggregates.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Footprint-consistency test green on at least three recorded fixture days.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend; axe-core green; design-qa sign-off; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E19-S04** (POC/VA machinery reused in delta mode). Blocks nothing in E19; consumed by **E20** Deep-Stats.

title: Engine profile series plugin: instanced rows, POC/VA lines, LOD merging
body:
## Context
The rendering half. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 already specifies the profile as a **series plugin** on layer 2: "instanced quads (rows) + POC/VA lines, shaders `bar` + `line`, right- or left-docked, shares the price scale". §3.6 lists `ProfileStore` among the engine's data stores with the mutation `replaceProfile(period, data)` returning the affected range for partial `bufferSubData`. §8 requires LOD "row merging when rows < 2 px tall", and §3.3's budget table sets **R4: profile recomputed on viewport change in ≤ 8 ms**. Milestone **M5** groups profiles with indicators. This task builds that plugin once so S01/S04/S07/S08 are data-mode variations rather than new renderers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `ProfileStore` in the worker: sparse levels keyed by `price_ticks`, `replaceProfile(period, data)` and an incremental `patchProfileLevels(changed)`; immutable per-frame snapshot to the renderer.
- Profile series plugin: instanced row quads (one instance per visible row) with per-instance `value`, `buyValue`, `sellValue`, `flags` (POC/VAH/VAL/HVN/LVN/single-print); POC/VA lines via the shared `line` shader; VA shading as a single quad; SDF labels for POC/VAH/VAL within the ≤3 text-draw-call budget.
- Docking and alignment: right- or left-docked, sharing the host pane's price scale so rows line up with candles pixel-for-pixel through zoom, log/linear flips and DPI changes.
- Split rendering mode (bid/ask bars back-to-back or stacked) driven by a plugin option, not a second plugin.
- LOD: merge adjacent levels when a row would be < 2 px tall, summing (never averaging) merged values; the effective row size is reported back so the legend can state it.
- Re-bucket worker path: re-aggregate the cached raw histogram on `price_grouping` change without a server round-trip, target ≤ 300 ms for a session profile (SCR-039 perf note).
- `degraded-2d` fallback: Canvas 2D rows and lines when WebGL2 is unavailable (§ capability probe / `RenderProfile`).
- Golden-image coverage per theme and per mode; benchmark **B-profile** added to the engine benchmark suite.

## Out of scope
- Period selection UX, settings panel and presets (**E19-S02**, **E19-S09**).
- TPO letter glyph rendering (**E19-S08** extends this plugin with a letter mode).
- Naked-POC rays (**E19-S06**) and HVN/LVN markers (**E19-S05**) — the plugin renders the flags those tickets set.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rows align with the price scale
  Given a profile docked beside a BTCUSDT candle pane
  When the trader zooms, pans, flips to log scale and changes DPI
  Then every profile row stays aligned with its price on the shared scale within one device pixel

Scenario: Viewport recompute stays in budget
  Given a 5 000-row profile
  When the viewport changes
  Then the recompute and upload complete in <= 8 ms at p95 (budget R4) and the frame holds >= 55 fps

Scenario: Dense profiles merge rather than alias
  Given rows would render below 2 px tall
  Then adjacent levels are merged by summation, the effective row size is reported, and no row is dropped or double counted

Scenario: Re-bucketing needs no server
  When price_grouping changes
  Then the worker re-aggregates the cached histogram in <= 300 ms for a session profile with no network request

Scenario: No WebGL2, still usable
  Given a browser where WebGL2 is unavailable
  Then the profile renders through the degraded-2d path with rows, POC and VA lines intact and the degradation is stated in the legend

Scenario: Partial upload, not full re-upload
  Given a single level changes on a live profile
  Then only the affected instance range is uploaded via bufferSubData
```

## Technical notes / design
One instanced draw call per profile per frame is the target; the vertex shader expands a unit quad by the per-instance value and the row height derived from the price scale, so a value change is an attribute update, not a geometry rebuild. Merged LOD levels are computed in the worker into a separate output buffer, leaving the raw histogram untouched so zooming back in is lossless. Values are `Float32Array` — display precision, matching constraint C3's analytics/accounting split; exact numbers in tooltips come from the store's original decimal strings, not the GPU buffer. The plugin must not invalidate the price/footprint layers: profile updates dirty layer 2 only.

## Test plan
Unit (≥85% engine): store mutations and affected-range computation, LOD merge maths (sum invariance: merged total == raw total), split-mode geometry, docking transform. Property-based: for random viewports and scale modes, row price mapping is invariant and `priceToScreen` round-trips. Golden image under SwiftShader: volume/delta, split/merged, POC+VA, both themes, dense and sparse. Perf: benchmark B-profile records p50/p95 viewport recompute and sustained fps at 5 000 rows; regression gate in CI.

## Security notes
No network surface. Row counts and instance buffer sizes are bounded (5 000-row cap per SCR-038) so a malicious or buggy server payload cannot force an unbounded GPU allocation; oversized payloads are truncated with a logged warning rather than crashing the context.

## Accessibility notes
The plugin exposes a structured row list (price, volume, delta, VA membership, flags) to the main thread specifically so SCR-038 can render its table alternative from the same data the canvas draws — the accessible view can never drift from the visual one. POC/VAH/VAL carry text labels and distinct line styles, not just colour; single prints and nodes carry glyph flags.

## Performance notes
Budget R4 ≤ 8 ms viewport recompute; ≥55 fps during pan/zoom; ≤3 text draw calls; profile + indicators + drawings share the ≤ 8 MB GPU budget (§ memory table); partial `bufferSubData` on live updates.

## Observability
Engine metrics `engine_profile_recompute_ms`, `engine_profile_rows_rendered`, `engine_profile_lod_merges`, `engine_profile_upload_bytes`; `renderProfile` capability reported in the existing `ready` event.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Golden images approved for both themes and every mode; ≤0.1% pixel diff gate.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the engine package.
- [ ] Benchmark B-profile in the engine benchmark report; regression gate wired.
- [ ] Code-owner review by the chart-engine owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E19-T01** (payload shape), **E12** (series/panes substrate and shared price scale). Blocks **E19-S01**.

## Branch
`feat/e19-profile-renderer`

## References
`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 layers/series, §3.6 stores, §8 LOD, §3.9 hit-testing, §14 M5, §15 properties, §16 golden images; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-038; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §5.1, C3.


## Agent execution brief

2. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`
3. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
Base area for `chart-engine`: packages/chart-engine/src/<layer>/
- `ProfileStore` in the worker: sparse levels keyed by `price_ticks`, `replaceProfile(period, data)` and an incremental `patchProfileLevels(changed)`; immutable per-frame snapshot to the renderer.
- Profile series plugin: instanced row quads (one instance per visible row) with per-instance `value`, `buyValue`, `sellValue`, `flags` (POC/VAH/VAL/HVN/LVN/single-print); POC/VA lines via the shared `line` shader; VA shading as a single quad; SDF labels for POC/VAH/VAL within the ≤3 text-draw-call budget.
- Docking and alignment: right- or left-docked, sharing the host pane's price scale so rows line up with candles pixel-for-pixel through zoom, log/linear flips and DPI changes.
- Split rendering mode (bid/ask bars back-to-back or stacked) driven by a plugin option, not a second plugin.
- LOD: merge adjacent levels when a row would be < 2 px tall, summing (never averaging) merged values; the effective row size is reported back so the legend can state it.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None identified beyond internal module boundaries named in Scope / Deliverables above; do not introduce a new public REST/WS surface without a contract-first change (AGENTS.md §3 step 4).

**Commands**

- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine bench`

**Branch & PR**

- Body includes: `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder until the issue number is assigned)

title: Deep-Stats rows: per-bar statistics strip, configuration and export
body:
## Context
R2 "Order-flow beta" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §6) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility. **E20 Deep-Stats rows** is the numeric layer of that: a configurable per-bar statistics strip under the chart that lets a trader read a bar without decoding footprint cells. Roadmap scope line (§6.2): "Configurable per-bar statistic rows under the chart: delta, cumulative delta, volume, buy/sell volume, trade count, average trade size, max/min delta, delta %, imbalance count, tape speed; row add/remove/reorder; per-row conditional highlighting; CSV export of the visible range" — 26 pts, Sprint S11, area `area/order-flow`, backend module **M9** (`orderflow`), story domain **DS**.

The numbers in the strip are **not a new calculation**. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 ("Deep Stats rows (per-bar statistics strip)") declares every row as a first-class `MetricDescriptor` in the `MetricRegistry` — `bar_volume`, `bar_notional`, `bar_buy_volume`, `bar_sell_volume`, `delta`, `max_delta`, `min_delta`, `delta_pct`, `bar_delta_divergence`, `cvd`, `cvd_bar_change`, `bar_trade_count`, `bar_avg_trade_size`, `bar_buy_trade_count`/`bar_sell_trade_count`, `tape_speed`, `bar_volume_imbalance_ratio`, `bar_poc_price`, `bar_vah_price`/`bar_val_price`, `open_interest_delta`, `bar_range_ticks` — all `scope="symbol"`, `cadence="on_trade"` with authoritative recompute `on_bar_close`, `inputs=("trades",)`, `deterministic=True`, `confidence="exact"`. The invariant this epic must protect is stated verbatim in that section: *a rule, an alert and a Deep-Stats row always read the same number*. There is therefore exactly one server-side engine — `DeepStatsEngine` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.4, fed by `FootprintEngine`) — and the strip is a renderer of its output, never a second implementation.

Depends on E18 Footprint (`E18 --> E20` in the roadmap dependency graph §11.1) for per-bar cell aggregation and the `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` WS topic, and on E16 Recorder for history depth. Consumes E11/E12 chart-engine surfaces for bar-grid alignment and E15 chart templates (`chart_templates`) for persistence of row configuration.

**Scheduling note (cross-epic blockers resolve strictly earlier).** Per the roadmap Gantt (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.2) E18 Footprint runs S10–S11 and E20 runs S11. E20 therefore never blocks on *all of* E18: each E20 ticket names the specific E18 child it consumes, and every such child is scheduled in a strictly earlier sprint than the E20 ticket that depends on it (E18-D02 S08 → E20-D01 S09; E18-T01/T02/T03/T04 and E18-S01/S02 S10 → E20-K01/T01/X01 S11). E18's own S11 work (display modes, imbalance zones, settings dialog, a11y) is *not* an input to E20.

**Estimate rollup (roadmap reconciliation).** Epic `estimate` = **26 pts**, matching the roadmap sizing for E20 exactly (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §6.2 E20 scope row and §5 epic table = 26). Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` the epic-level number is the **committed engineering rollup**: the in-train Story/Task/Spike children (S01 5, S02 3, S03 2, S04 3, T01 5, T02 2, T03 3, T04 1, K01 2) = 26 pts. The Could-have S05 (3 pts, Backlog) is excluded because it is not committed to the train, and the Design (D01–D06, 14 pts), QA (Q01–Q05, 12 pts) and Security (X01–X02, 4 pts) children are tracked as discipline overhead against the design/QA/security capacity lines rather than the epic's feature sizing — counting them was what produced the stale 59 and a ~127% overshoot of the roadmap figure. 26 vs 26 is 0% variance, inside the ±15% tolerance band.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Stories:** US-DS-001 (Must, per-bar statistics strip), US-DS-002 (Must, row selection & ordering), US-DS-003 (Should, threshold colouring), US-DS-005 (Should, stats export + accessible table), US-DS-004 (Could, rolling sparkline — Backlog, ship only if capacity allows).
- **Screens:** SCR-030 Chart panel (hosts the strip), SCR-033 Deep Stats rows configuration (new modal), SCR-045 Chart data-table alternative (a11y + CSV export).
- **Components:** CMP-225 DeepStatsStrip (new organism), consuming CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-031 ColorSwatch/ThemeChip, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-049 Table, CMP-053 Pagination, CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CMP-099 PrintExportBar.
- **Backend (M9):** `DeepStatsEngine` emitting `DeepStatsRow`; registration of every §7 Deep-Stats `MetricDescriptor` in `MetricRegistry`; chunked CSV export job.
- **Contracts:** `GET /market/metrics` (repeatable `metric`, bar-scoped), `GET /market/footprint` bootstrap, WS topic `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` (§14.4 `FootprintUpdate` — per-bar `delta`, `poc_price`, `value_area_high/low`), export job polled via `GET /jobs/{id}`.
- **DB:** `chart_templates` jsonb config (row set/order/format/thresholds), `layout_panes.pane_kind = 'deep_stats'`, QuestDB `footprint_cells` + `trades` read-side, Parquet cold tier for offline parity recompute.
- **Analytics/audit:** `chart.deepstats_rows_changed {rows}`, `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`.
- Design track D01–D06, QA track Q01–Q05, Security track X01–X02, ADR + docs T04.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell rendering (E18), profiles (E19), CVD pane and divergence markers (E23), tape-speed detector internals and z-score baselining (E25), OI/funding series (E24) — E20 only *displays* `tape_speed` and `open_interest_delta` by reading their registered descriptors.
- Alerting or rule authoring on a stats row (E40 / E35). The shared `MetricRegistry` makes this trivial later; no rule surface is built here.
- Android / any mobile client (owner decision 2026-09-14); no separate admin app.
- Non-Bybit venues; anything other than Bybit USDT linear perpetuals.
- Multi-symbol comparison of stats rows (E23 owns multi-symbol CVD comparison).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The strip reads the market
  Given a recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day is loaded on SCR-030 with the Deep Stats strip enabled
  When the user scrolls and zooms across the visible range
  Then every enabled row is pixel-aligned with its bar column at every zoom level
  And the forming bar is rendered in the documented provisional style
  And the strip costs <= 1.5 ms per frame measured over a 60-second capture

Scenario: One number everywhere
  Given the offline DuckDB recomputation over the Parquet tier for the same symbol-day
  When each Deep-Stats row value is compared with the value served by GET /market/metrics and the value rendered in the strip
  Then all three agree within floating-point tolerance for 100% of bars
  And every row label maps to a registered MetricDescriptor, asserted by the CI test required by 24-internal-schemas.md §12

Scenario: Configuration survives and is reachable without a mouse
  Given the user disables Max Delta and Min Delta and moves Cumulative Delta to the top using Alt+Up
  When the workspace is reloaded
  Then the row set and order are restored from the chart template
  And SCR-033, the strip and SCR-045 all pass axe-core with zero serious or critical violations

Scenario: Export is honest and bounded
  Given a visible range of 60 000 bars
  When the user exports the strip as CSV
  Then the export is chunked with visible progress and can be cancelled
  And the produced file has one row per bar, one column per enabled statistic and ISO-8601 UTC timestamps
  And a viewer-role user can export only the data their role can see

Scenario: Partial history is never silently truncated
  Given the recorder started 4 minutes ago for SOLUSDT
  When the strip is enabled on a 5m chart
  Then a partial-history state is shown naming the first available timestamp
  And rows that cannot be computed for the uncovered bars render as explicit "no data", not as zero
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Engine.** `DeepStatsEngine` (`20-architecture.md` §3.4) is incremental and checkpointable: it consumes `FootprintUpdate` plus the raw trade stream for the forming bar, maintains per-bar accumulators (`buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, running delta with `max_delta`/`min_delta` path tracking, trade counts by aggressor, notional), and emits `DeepStatsRow` on the coalescing `of.*` bus. Values are re-derived authoritatively `on_bar_close`; the in-progress bar is provisional, coalesced to 4 Hz (CMP-225 data contract).
- **No second maths in the browser.** The frontend renders values from the WS frame / REST bootstrap and never recomputes a statistic. The only frontend-derived quantity permitted is the sparkline window, which is a windowing of already-delivered values.
- **Alignment.** The strip is a real `<table>` (CMP-225 a11y contract) positioned from the engine's time-scale projection `x(t)`, the same one CMP-181 CandleSeries uses, so alignment cannot drift.
- **Recompute cadence.** Per SCR-033 Performance: recomputed on bar close and on visible-range change, not per tick.
- **Config persistence.** Row ids, order, per-row format, threshold rules and compact/sparkline flags live in `chart_templates` jsonb (`21-database-schema.md` §3.8.2) so they travel with the template; `layout_panes.pane_kind='deep_stats'` covers the standalone-pane case.
- **Error codes.** Reuse the documented `validation_failed` and `footprint_window_too_large`; add no new error family.

## Test plan
- Unit: per-metric golden tests for all §7 descriptors; accumulator edge cases (zero-volume bar, single-print bar, `qty_step` divide guard in `delta_pct`).
- Contract: OpenAPI + WS JSON-schema validation for every consumed frame shape.
- Integration: recorded Bybit fixtures — normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol (R2 §6.4 gate list).
- Golden fixture: version-controlled expected Deep-Stats output for one recorded symbol-day; drift fails CI (R2 correctness gate).
- E2E (Playwright web + Electron): enable strip, toggle/reorder rows, thresholds, table view, CSV export including cancel.
- Perf: strip frame-cost benchmark in CI (<=1.5 ms/frame) plus a full-scene budget re-check (footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + 3 stat rows + CVD, p95 <=16.6 ms).
- A11y: axe-core CI on SCR-033/SCR-045 plus a manual screen-reader pass over the strip table and keyboard reorder.
- Coverage: >=85% backend/engine packages, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Data classification: market data only — no PII, no secrets, no order or credential surface. Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **S4 information disclosure via export** (SR-098 — exports role-scoped, watermarked with the exporting identity and timestamp, and audited), **S3 path handling on export** (SR-097 — no user-supplied filesystem paths; downloads addressed by job id through `GET /jobs/{id}`), and a denial-of-service vector from unbounded export ranges (chunking plus a hard cap). The read path is gated by `marketdata:read` with `scope=none` (`23-ws-protocol.md` subscription permission table). Epic carries the `security` label; STRIDE is E20-X01.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. The strip is a real table, not canvas, so values are readable cell by cell; drag reorder has the `Alt+Up`/`Alt+Down` keyboard equivalent (SCR-033); threshold state is conveyed by a word plus an icon — **never colour alone** (US-DS-003 NFR); SCR-045 is the normative accessible equivalent and must reach reading parity; a documented "read current bar's stats" shortcut exists (CMP-225).

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: frame budget #1 (p95 <=16.6 ms), floor #2 (never below 30 fps) for the full R2 scene, and WS tick -> screen #3 (p95 <100 ms, hard gate at R2). Epic-specific: the strip adds <=2 ms/frame (US-DS-001 NFR) with the tighter screen-level budget of <=1.5 ms/frame (SCR-033). The virtualised SCR-045 table renders 100k rows at <=8 ms scripting per scroll frame.

## Observability
Structured logs for export jobs (job id, range, bar count, duration, outcome); Prometheus metrics `deepstats_engine_bar_close_duration_seconds`, `deepstats_rows_emitted_total`, `deepstats_export_rows_total`, `deepstats_export_failures_total`; frontend strip frame cost surfaced in the SCR-046 diagnostics overlay; analytics events `chart.deepstats_rows_changed`, `chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported`; export audited per SR-098.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 (Epic):
- [ ] Epic `estimate` (26) still reconciles with the roadmap E20 sizing (26) within ±15%, and with the in-train S/T/K child sum, at each sprint boundary.
- [ ] No child ticket scheduled in a sprint earlier than any of its cross-epic blockers' sprints (re-checked whenever the roadmap Gantt moves).

- [ ] Epic-level acceptance criteria above verified end-to-end on a recorded symbol-day.
- [ ] Coverage floors green (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend); zero open P0/P1 against E20 scope.
- [ ] Docs updated: `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 row table, `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-033/SCR-045, `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-225, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md` for any shipped delta.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green plus manual screen-reader pass recorded (E20-Q04).
- [ ] perf: strip frame-cost benchmark recorded against budget (E20-Q03).
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off (E20-X01/X02).
- [ ] QA sign-off: epic-level regression and exploratory pass recorded (E20-Q05).
- [ ] Design sign-off: design-QA sweep Done (E20-D06).
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at Sprint Review with acceptance recorded; ADR-0016 merged (E20-T04).

## Dependencies
- **E18 Footprint** (S10–S11) — E20 consumes only E18's **Sprint 10** deliverables: `E18-T01`/`E18-T02` (cell aggregation + imbalance/POC/value-area algorithms) feed `DeepStatsEngine`; `E18-T03`/`E18-T04` (REST + WS footprint read paths) define the surface E20-X01 threat-models and E20-T02 extends; `E18-S01`/`E18-S02` (cell grid render) give E20-K01 a real scene to measure; `E18-D02` (S08) is the stimulus for E20-D01. Each E20 child names the specific earlier-sprint child it needs, so no E20 ticket is scheduled before its blocker resolves. E18's Sprint-11 work is not an input to E20.

title: Measure strip frame cost and bar-grid alignment strategy
body:
## Context
SCR-033 sets a hard screen-level budget: "The Deep Stats strip is recomputed only on bar close and on the visible-range change, not per tick; it must add <=1.5 ms per frame to the chart panel's budget." US-DS-001's NFR is slightly looser (<=2 ms) and adds an absolute requirement: "alignment is pixel-exact with the bar grid at all zoom levels". Those two requirements pull against each other, because the cheapest way to guarantee alignment is to render the strip inside the WebGL pass (one projection, one frame), while the a11y contract in `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-225 mandates the opposite — "rendered as a real `<table>` aligned to the bar grid (not canvas), so values are readable cell by cell". US-DS-004 then asserts sparklines are "drawn in the same WebGL pass as the strip", implying a hybrid. This spike settles the architecture before E20-S01 commits to it, and measures the actual cost so E20-D03's density decisions are bounded by evidence rather than taste.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. Not expected to produce production-shippable code.

## Scope / Deliverables
Questions to answer, each with recorded numbers:
1. **Can a DOM `<table>` of N columns × M rows stay pixel-aligned with the WebGL bar grid during pan/zoom without lagging a frame?** Measure at M = 5 and M = 13 rows, N = the visible bar count at 3 zoom levels (typical ~120 bars, dense ~400 bars, extreme ~800 bars).
2. **What does it cost?** Scripting + layout + paint time per frame attributable to the strip, p50/p95 over a 60 s pan/zoom capture, on the reference machine from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3, in Chromium and in the Electron shell.
3. **At what bar width does the strip stop being legible**, fixing the narrow-bar collapse threshold that US-DS-001 requires and E20-D05's measurement contract publishes.
4. **Which alignment strategy wins**: (a) per-cell absolutely-positioned DOM driven by the engine's `x(t)` each frame; (b) a single CSS transform on a fixed-pitch table, with the engine supplying scale + offset; (c) hybrid — WebGL-drawn backgrounds/sparklines with a DOM text layer on top. Compare on cost, alignment exactness and a11y fidelity.
5. **Does the 4 Hz coalesced forming-bar update cause layout thrash**, and does batching updates to `requestAnimationFrame` remove it?

Deliverables: prototype on `spike/e20-strip-alignment` (throwaway), a comparison table of the three strategies against the five questions, a Chrome DevTools performance trace per strategy committed under `docs/plan/benchmarks/e20/`, and a recommendation.

## Out of scope

- Sparkline rendering cost beyond a rough feasibility note (US-DS-004 is a Could).
- Tauri measurement (E11's shell spike owns shell parity).

```gherkin
  When the legibility measurement is reviewed
  Then a specific bar width in CSS pixels is named as the compact-collapse threshold, with the density and font size it was measured at
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype against the E18 build so the strip is measured with a real footprint scene underneath it, not in isolation — the budget that matters is the marginal cost added to an already-loaded frame. Use `performance.measure` around the strip's update path and attribute layout/paint via the DevTools trace rather than wall-clock timers alone. title: Implement DeepStatsEngine and register Deep-Stats metric descriptors
body:
## Context
Every Deep-Stats row is defined once, in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 ("Deep Stats rows"), as a `MetricDescriptor` in the `MetricRegistry` — and that section states the invariant the whole epic exists to protect: "the metric values themselves are exactly the descriptors above so a rule, an alert and a Deep-Stats row always read the same number". `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.4 names the producer: `DeepStatsEngine` — "Per-bar totals: total/bid/ask volume, delta, max/min delta path, delta %, CVD, trade count", fed by `FootprintEngine`, emitting `DeepStatsRow`, incremental and checkpointable like every other order-flow engine. This Task builds that engine and registers its descriptors. No UI depends on it yet; every later E20 ticket does.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Module `M9` (`orderflow`): `DeepStatsEngine`, consuming `FootprintUpdate` from `FootprintEngine` plus the per-trade stream for the in-progress bar, emitting `DeepStatsRow` events onto the coalescing `of.*` bus.
- Per-bar accumulator state: `buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, notional, trade counts by aggressor, running delta with `max_delta`/`min_delta` path tracking, and the bar's tick range.
- Registration in `MetricRegistry` of every §7 Deep-Stats descriptor with the declared attributes (`scope="symbol"`, `cadence="on_trade"`, authoritative recompute `on_bar_close`, `inputs=("trades",)`, `warmup_bars=0`, `deterministic=True`, `confidence="exact"`): `bar_volume`, `bar_notional`, `bar_sell_volume`, `bar_buy_volume`, `delta`, `max_delta`, `min_delta`, `delta_pct`, `bar_delta_divergence`, `cvd`, `cvd_bar_change`, `bar_trade_count`, `bar_avg_trade_size`, `bar_buy_trade_count`, `bar_sell_trade_count`, `bar_volume_imbalance_ratio`, `bar_range_ticks`. Descriptors owned by other engines and merely *referenced* by the strip (`tape_speed` from `TapeSpeedEngine`, `open_interest_delta` from the derivatives path, `bar_poc_price`/`bar_vah_price`/`bar_val_price` from the footprint value-area computation) are **read**, never redefined.
- Checkpointing: engine state serialises and restores so a restart resumes mid-bar without replaying the session (architecture §3.4 requirement for all order-flow engines).
- The CI test required by `24-internal-schemas.md` §12: "every metric named in §7.2.1 exists in `MetricRegistry` with the declared confidence, and every Deep-Stats row label maps to a registered descriptor".
- Prometheus metrics `deepstats_engine_bar_close_duration_seconds`, `deepstats_rows_emitted_total`.

## Out of scope
- Any HTTP or WS surface (E20-T02) and any UI (E20-S01..S05).
- Defining `tape_speed`, `open_interest_delta` or the value-area metrics — owned by E25, E24 and E18 respectively.
- The offline parity harness (E20-T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every declared row exists exactly once
  When the MetricRegistry coverage test runs
  Then every Deep-Stats row label in 24-internal-schemas.md §7 resolves to exactly one registered MetricDescriptor with the declared confidence
  And no descriptor owned by another engine is re-registered by DeepStatsEngine

Scenario: Values are correct on a golden bar
  Given the recorded BTCUSDT fixture bar with known buy/sell volumes and print counts
  When the bar closes
  Then delta equals buy_volume - sell_volume
  And delta_pct equals delta / max(bar_volume, qty_step) * 100 and is within -100..100
  And bar_avg_trade_size equals bar_volume / max(bar_trade_count, 1)

Scenario: Degenerate bars do not divide by zero
  Given a bar containing zero trades
  When the bar closes
  Then bar_volume, delta and bar_trade_count are 0
  And delta_pct is 0 rather than NaN or an exception
  And bar_avg_trade_size is 0

Scenario: Restart resumes mid-bar
  Given the engine is mid-bar with a partially accumulated delta path
  When its state is checkpointed and the process is restarted from that checkpoint
  Then the resumed max_delta and min_delta equal the pre-restart values
  And the closed bar equals the value produced by an uninterrupted run over the same tape

Scenario: The in-progress bar is provisional
  When the engine emits for a bar that has not closed
  Then the event is flagged provisional
  And the authoritative recompute at bar close replaces it, and is the value persisted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Incremental only: no recompute from history per tick (architecture §3.4). CPU-heavy paths use `numpy` vectorised ops on preallocated arrays, consistent with the other order-flow engines.
- Aggressor convention is fixed and must not be re-derived: per §7, **Bid Volume = `bar_sell_volume`** (volume executed on the bid, aggressive sellers) and **Ask Volume = `bar_buy_volume`** (aggressive buyers). This mapping is the single most likely source of a sign error in the whole epic and gets its own unit test.
- `delta_pct` uses `max(bar_volume, qty_step)` as the denominator — `qty_step` comes from instruments-info, not a hard-coded epsilon.
- `cvd_bar_change` is defined as equal to `delta` and is kept only for row parity (§7); it must be computed as `cvd(close) - cvd(open)` and asserted equal to `delta` in a test, so a future CVD anchor change cannot silently diverge the two rows.
- `cvd` itself is owned by `CvdEngine` (E23) with a resettable anchor; `DeepStatsEngine` reads it rather than maintaining a second running sum.
- Decimal handling follows the existing market-data convention (fixed-point decimals, not float) end to end; float appears only at the presentation edge.

## Test plan
- Unit (target >=90% on the engine module, floor 85%): per-metric golden values; the bid/ask aggressor mapping test; zero-volume, single-print and single-price bars; `delta_pct` clamping at ±100; checkpoint round-trip equality; provisional-then-authoritative replacement.
- Integration: recorded Bybit fixtures — normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol.
- Property test: for any generated trade sequence, `delta == bar_buy_volume - bar_sell_volume` and `bar_volume == bar_buy_volume + bar_sell_volume`.
- Contract: the `MetricRegistry` coverage test (§12) runs in CI and fails the build on drift.
- Perf: engine bar-close duration benchmarked; must not become a contributor to the backend-internal ≤20 ms budget (#6).

## Security notes
Market data only — no PII, no secrets, no order path. Threat surface is limited to resource consumption: the engine must bound per-symbol state so a pathological symbol cannot grow memory without limit (memory ceiling budgets #7/#8). No new external input is accepted. `security` label not required on this Task; it is covered by the epic STRIDE (E20-X01).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend engine, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Bar-close recompute must complete well inside the coalescing window so it never delays fan-out; target p95 <=2 ms per bar close per symbol at 10 symbols (capacity model, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §10). Memory: per-symbol accumulator state is O(1) in trade count, O(rows) in size.

## Observability
Structured log on checkpoint save/restore (symbol, bar open time, state size). Metrics `deepstats_engine_bar_close_duration_seconds` (histogram, labelled by symbol), `deepstats_rows_emitted_total` (counter, labelled provisional/authoritative). A warn-level log when a bar closes with zero trades for a symbol that is supposed to be actively recording, since that usually means an ingestion gap rather than a quiet market.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by the named tests.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on the touched backend/engine package, no baseline regression.
- [ ] `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 updated if any descriptor attribute shipped differently from the doc.
- [ ] `MetricRegistry` coverage test green in CI.
- [ ] Perf benchmark recorded for bar-close duration.
- [ ] Reviewed by the order-flow code owner; PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E18-T01` (*Implement FootprintEngine native-tick cell aggregation in M9*, Sprint 10) and `E18-T02` (*imbalance, unfinished-auction, POC and value-area algorithms*, Sprint 10) — `DeepStatsEngine` is fed by `FootprintEngine` (`20-architecture.md` §3.4: `FP --> DS`), and the `bar_poc_price` / `bar_vah_price` / `bar_val_price` / `bar_volume_imbalance_ratio` rows read E18-T02's outputs directly.

Scheduled **Sprint 11**, one sprint after both blockers complete, rather than the earlier Sprint 10 placement: E18's own epic window is S10–S11, so an `E18` epic-level blocker on a Sprint-10 ticket would have started this work before its input existed. Naming the two S10 children instead makes the ordering real and satisfies `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 ("sprint within train window and after blockers"). E18's S11 items (S03–S11 display/colouring/settings) are rendering concerns and are **not** inputs here.

Reads `CvdEngine` output (E23, S12) for the `cvd` row; where E23 has not yet landed, the `cvd` and `cvd_bar_change` rows are registered but return `unavailable` rather than a locally recomputed substitute.

## Branch
`feat/e20-deepstats-engine` — expect ~350 LOC plus tests; split the registry registration into a second PR if the diff grows.

title: Expose Deep-Stats rows over /market/metrics and the footprint WS topic
body:
## Context
The frontend must be able to (a) bootstrap the visible range's statistics over REST and (b) follow the live tail over WS, without inventing a new transport. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §2 fixes the division: "Bulk history (bars, footprint, profiles, metrics) come from REST; the WS only carries the live tail plus the initial snapshot needed to attach to it." Both surfaces already exist — `GET /market/metrics` takes a repeatable `metric` parameter and returns one series per value with a parameter echo, and the `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` topic already carries per-bar `delta`, `poc_price`, `value_area_high`/`value_area_low` in `FootprintUpdate` (§14.4). This Task wires `DeepStatsEngine`'s output into those two existing contracts and closes the gaps, interface-first (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) so E20-S01 can start against a merged schema.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /market/metrics`: accept every Deep-Stats metric code registered by E20-T01 in the `MetricCode` enum; serve bar-scoped series honouring `bar_type` + `param`; echo per-metric params; populate `meta.recording_started_at` so the UI can render the partial-history state (R2 exit criterion #5).
- WS: ensure the `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` frames carry the per-bar statistics the strip needs for the live tail, and that the last bar's `confirm: false` flag is present so the client can render it as provisional (§ "Unconfirmed bars" — "A client MUST NOT treat it as closed").
- Schema delta merged into `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and, if any WS field is added, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §14.4 plus the JSON-schema file, **before** implementation.
- Validation and limits: reject windows that exceed the documented cap with the existing `validation_failed` / `footprint_window_too_large` error codes; `maxItems: 12` on the repeated `metric` parameter is enforced, not assumed.
- RBAC: `marketdata:read`, `scope=none`, per the `x-rbac` block on the endpoint and the WS subscription permission table.
- Contract tests asserting response and frame shapes against the committed schemas.

## Out of scope
- The CSV export endpoint and job (E20-S04).
- New metrics (E20-T01) or new transports/encodings.
- Client-side consumption (E20-S01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bootstrap returns every enabled row
  Given a request for metric=bar_volume&metric=delta&metric=delta_pct with bar_type=time and param=5
  When GET /market/metrics is called for a 500-bar window
  Then three series are returned, each with its own params echo and unit
  And meta.recording_started_at is present

Scenario: Too many metrics is rejected cleanly
  Given a request with 13 repeated metric parameters
  Then the response is 400 with validation_failed and names the maxItems limit
  And no partial series are returned

Scenario: Window too large is rejected with the documented code
  Given a window exceeding the documented footprint window cap
  Then the response is 422 with footprint_window_too_large
  And the message states the maximum window

Scenario: The live tail marks the forming bar
  Given a subscription to footprint.BTCUSDT.time.5
  When a frame arrives containing the currently forming bar
  Then that bar carries confirm: false
  And the previously forming bar, now closed, carries confirm: true with its authoritative values

Scenario: Unauthorised read is refused
  Given a session without marketdata:read
  When it calls GET /market/metrics or subscribes to footprint.BTCUSDT.time.5
  Then the request is refused and no market data is returned
```

## Technical notes / design
- Interface-first: the OpenAPI/WS diff is reviewed and merged before implementation, per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10, because E20-S01 is written against it in the same train.
- Serve from the engine's already-aggregated state where the window is hot; fall back to QuestDB `footprint_cells` / `trades` for colder windows, and to the Parquet tier beyond retention — the endpoint reports its `meta.sources` accordingly, as the existing `/market/metrics` example does.
- No new error family. No new WS topic: adding a `deepstats.*` topic was considered and rejected — it would give the client a second sequence to reconcile against `footprint.*` for the same bars, which §"footprint and bars are separate subscriptions" already shows is a source of client-side complexity.
- Coalescing semantics for the topic are unchanged ("Per (bar, price) cell, values summed for the same bar, replaced across bars"); the per-bar statistics ride along as replaced-per-bar fields.

## Test plan
- Contract: schema validation of every response and frame against `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the WS JSON schemas, in CI.
- Unit: parameter validation (maxItems, window cap, unknown metric code, bar_type/param combinations).
- Integration: recorded fixtures for hot (engine state), warm (QuestDB) and cold (Parquet) windows, asserting identical values across the three paths.
- Security: RBAC negative tests for both surfaces.
- Coverage >=85% on the touched API module.

## Security notes
Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, informed by E20-X01's STRIDE: **information disclosure** — the read path is `marketdata:read`, `scope=none`, and returns no account-scoped data, so the main risk is an over-broad window used as a **denial-of-service** vector; the documented window cap and `maxItems: 12` are the controls, and both are tested as rejections rather than truncations. No user-supplied paths (SR-097 is not engaged here but the no-paths principle is followed — data is addressed by symbol/bar_type/param). Data classification: market data, internal.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The endpoint does supply `meta.recording_started_at`, which the UI needs to render the partial-history state accessibly.

## Performance notes
Backend-internal WS budget #6 (ingestion receipt → outbound frame, p95 <=20 ms) must not regress; the per-bar statistics are pre-aggregated by E20-T01, so fan-out does no computation. REST bootstrap for a 500-bar, 6-metric request should return in <=300 ms p95 from the hot path.

## Observability
Request logs with symbol, metric set, window size, resolved source tier and duration; metric `market_metrics_request_duration_seconds` labelled by source tier; counter for rejected requests by error code, so an over-broad-window pattern is visible rather than inferred.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Schema diff merged to `22-api-openapi.yaml` (and `23-ws-protocol.md` if applicable) before implementation, per interface-first.

title: STRIDE threat model for the Deep-Stats epic
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes a STRIDE threat model mandatory per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the kickoff to be scheduled before an Epic enters Ready. E20's surface looks benign — market data, read-only, no credentials, no order path — and that is precisely why it needs a model rather than an assumption: the epic ships a **data export** (SR-098 territory), an **asynchronous job with a download URL** (SR-097 territory), and a **user-supplied persisted configuration structure**. `04-security-program.md` already records S3 (elevation of privilege: "Replay/export endpoint used to read arbitrary filesystem paths", rated High) and S4 (information disclosure via export) as programme-level threats; this model determines how they apply here and what E20-T02, E20-S02 and E20-S04 must implement.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model for E20 recorded in `docs/security/threat-models/e20-deep-stats.md`, following the format of the existing programme threat models in `04-security-program.md` §S-tables (threat id, category, description, likelihood, impact, rating, control with SR reference, residual risk).
- Data-flow diagram (mermaid) covering: Bybit tape → ingestion → `FootprintEngine` → `DeepStatsEngine` → bus → WS fan-out → client strip; and the REST paths `GET /market/metrics`, `GET /market/footprint`, the export job and `GET /jobs/{id}` → download.
- Trust boundaries marked: exchange↔ingestion, backend↔client (over Tailscale only), and the role boundary between Owner/Manager/Viewer.
- Per-category analysis with at least one concrete threat each:
  - **Spoofing** — can a session subscribe to a topic or call an endpoint without `marketdata:read`?
  - **Tampering** — can a malformed or hostile template configuration (unknown row ids, oversized list, deep nesting) corrupt chart load or inflate storage? Can a malformed WS frame cause the client to render a fabricated value?
  - **Repudiation** — is an export attributable? (SR-098 watermark + audit.)
  - **Information disclosure** — can a Viewer export data beyond its role? Does the export leak account context through the provenance/watermark block?
  - **Denial of service** — unbounded export range, excessive concurrent exports, an over-broad `/market/metrics` window, a row configuration whose render cost breaks the frame budget.
  - **Elevation of privilege** — can the job/download mechanism be coerced into serving another user's artefact or a filesystem path (SR-097)?
- **Abuse cases** written as executable test intents, handed to E20-X02 and E20-Q01.
- Required controls mapped to the tickets that implement them (E20-T02 limits, E20-S02 template validation, E20-S04 role scoping/watermark/audit/cancellation), so no control is identified without an owner.

## Out of scope
- Threat models for E18, E19, E21 or E26 (each owns its own; E26 and E21 are named explicitly in the R2 security gate).
- Penetration testing (R4, E43).
- Implementing the controls.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category is addressed
  When the threat model is reviewed
  Then each of the six categories has at least one identified threat with a likelihood, impact, rating, control and residual risk
  And every control references an SR identifier from 04-security-program.md or states why no existing SR applies

Scenario: Every control has an owning ticket
  When the control table is reviewed
  Then each control names the E20 ticket that implements it
  And no control is left unassigned

Scenario: Abuse cases are testable
  When the abuse-case list is reviewed
  Then each is written so that E20-X02 or E20-Q01 can execute it and observe a pass or fail
```

## Technical notes / design
The model must explicitly record the **negative findings** as well — that E20 touches no credentials, no order path and no PII, and that SR-025 step-up re-authentication therefore does not apply to market-data export. Recording the reasoning prevents a later reviewer from reading the absence of step-up as an oversight, and prevents a well-meaning engineer from adding friction the standard does not require.

## Test plan
N/A (analysis artefact). Verified by the Security engineer's review and by E20-X02 executing the abuse cases against the built surfaces.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security analysis. Its output gates E20-T02 (which must implement the window and cardinality limits the model identifies) and informs E20-S04's export controls. Data classification of the epic is recorded here: market data, internal; no PII; no secrets; export attributable.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The model treats frame-budget exhaustion via a pathological row configuration as a genuine availability threat, not merely a performance concern, and routes it to the row-count guard that E20-K01 sized — which is why the two tickets cross-reference.

## Observability
The model specifies the security-relevant events E20 must emit: export attempted/succeeded/failed/cancelled with actor and range, template-validation rejections, and RBAC refusals on the market-data read path — all of which feed the SR-125 security metrics set.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/security/threat-models/e20-deep-stats.md` merged with the DFD, the six-category analysis, the control table with owning tickets, and the recorded negative findings.
- [ ] Abuse-case list handed to E20-X02 and E20-Q01 and referenced from both tickets.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] Any control requiring a ticket that does not yet exist has been filed before this ticket closes.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

`blocked_by: E18-T03` (*Serve GET /market/footprint and POST /market/footprint/recompute*, Sprint 10) and `E18-T04` (*footprint WS topic, binary body_kind 5*, Sprint 10) — the data flow being modelled originates in those read paths; modelling it before their shape is settled would model a guess.

body:
## Context

- A state matrix: {loading, streaming, stale, disconnected, resynchronising, arm-off, degraded/shed, empty-heatmap, partial-history} × {depth 50, 200, 500} × {compact, cosy, comfortable} × {dark, light, high-contrast, CVD-safe}, with the cells that must be executed manually marked and the rest mapped to automation.

title: Render the live DOM ladder grid on SCR-050
body:
## Context
US-DOM-001 (Must): *"As an order-flow trader, I want a price ladder with resting bid/ask sizes, so that I can see the book."* This Story builds the ladder half of SCR-050 — the clickable-in-R3, readable-in-R2 price grid that every subsequent DOM feature hangs off. It is the single biggest frontend piece in this Epic because the ladder is simultaneously a high-frequency render surface and a WAI-ARIA grid: `05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 explicitly refuses to relax WCAG for it, and §4.2 names it as the motivating example for roving tabindex ("this prevents 200+ Tab presses to cross a DOM ladder").

Design is signed off in E21-D02/D07; the data contract is delivered by E21-T01 over `book.{symbol}.{depth}`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screen**: SCR-050 (ladder region, header controls, footer strip). **Stories**: US-DOM-001, and US-MKT-007's presentation on this surface.
- **Components**: CMP-108 DomLadderRow (all variants), CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons (rendered **disabled** — trading ships in E31), CMP-229 ArmToggle (visual state only, locked off), CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-051 EnvironmentBadge per the per-panel demo/live invariant.
- Columns per the catalogue layout: price · bid size (with size bar) · ask size (with size bar) · last-traded size (tape column) · cumulative depth · own-order column slot (populated by E21-S06) · position marker slot.
- **Virtualised** row rendering — only visible rows in the DOM — driven from the shared-worker-decoded book state.
- **Auto-centring** with the hysteresis from the E21-D05 motion spec: recentre when price approaches the edge, never jitter per tick; `C` = centre on mark, `Space` = recentre and resume auto-follow, `+`/`-` = price step zoom (view-local bindings that shadow the chart's per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 precedence rule 3).
- **States**: loading (ladder skeleton) · streaming · stale (dim + "Book stale 3 s") · disconnected (ladder frozen, trading affordances hard-disabled, banner) · resynchronising ("Book resynchronising…" — deltas discarded until a fresh snapshot) · arm-off lock cursor.
- **A11y**: `role="grid"` with `role="row"` rows, roving tabindex, region landmark, `Enter` opens the row action menu, accessible name "64 100, ask 42, own order 0.1 working", ≥24 px row targets at default density, and the §6.3 data-table alternative wired to the same data window.
- Subscription lifecycle: subscribe on mount, unsubscribe with grace on unmount, resync via `resync` frame on sequence gap, re-subscribe after reconnect in priority order.

## Out of scope
Click-to-trade and drag-to-amend (US-DOM-007/008 → **E31**, R3) — affordances render disabled with a lock tooltip. Heatmap (E21-S02). Depth tier control (E21-S05). Own-order data (E21-S06). Detector chips (E25).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Ladder renders
  Given orderbook depth 200 is subscribed for BTCUSDT
  Then price rows show bid size, ask size, last traded size and cumulative depth, updating live
  And updates arrive at up to 20 Hz and each render completes within one frame

Scenario: Price centring without jitter
  Given auto-centre is on and price oscillates around the recentre trigger band
  Then the ladder recentres when price approaches the edge and does not recentre more than once per the specified minimum interval

Scenario: Book resync
  Given a sequence gap invalidates the book
  Then the ladder greys with "Book resynchronising", incoming deltas are discarded until a fresh snapshot applies,
  and normal rendering resumes with no stale rows left behind

Scenario: Stale feed
  Given no book update has arrived for 3 seconds
  Then the ladder dims, shows "Book stale 3 s" with the last-good timestamp, and trading affordances are disabled

Scenario: Keyboard operation
  Given a keyboard user focuses the ladder
  Then one row is in the tab order, arrow keys move the roving focus row to row,
  each focused row is announced with price, bid size, ask size and own-order size, and Enter opens the row action menu

Scenario: Disconnected
  Given the WS transport is down
  Then the ladder is frozen with an explicit banner and no control implies a live price
```

## Technical notes / design
Book state is decoded once in the shared worker (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §"WS client") and read by the panel — the ladder must not decode frames itself. Row identity is the integer `price_ticks` so React keys are stable across recentring; virtualisation keeps the DOM node count bounded (≤60 visible rows at default density per the analogous tape budget). Live updates **patch rows in place** (cell text updated, node identity preserved) so screen-reader focus and any sort state survive (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 live-data-sync rule). Ambient live-region announcements throttled to the standard default (1 per 2 s, user-configurable) — never per tick.

Error/validation copy comes verbatim from the E21-D07 copy deck.

## Test plan
- **Unit (vitest)**: row projection from book state; cumulative depth computation; centring hysteresis with a fake clock; stale/resync/disconnected state machine; virtualisation window maths.
- **Storybook interaction**: every CMP-108 variant; keyboard roving-tabindex traversal; `Enter` row action menu; disabled trading affordance tooltip.
- **Contract**: consumes the `BookSnapshot`/`BookDelta` schemas from `ws-schemas.json`; a schema drift fails CI.
- **Integration**: fixture-driven book stream including a seq gap; assert the resync state renders and clears.
- **E2E (Playwright)**: open SCR-050 on the demo env, assert live row updates, force a gap, assert the resync banner, assert keyboard traversal and announcements via the DOM mirror.
- **A11y**: axe-core zero serious/critical; manual NVDA/VoiceOver pass recorded.
- **Perf**: ≥55 fps with 200 visible rows (US-DOM-001 NFR); WS→pixel ≤120 ms p95 for this panel.
- Coverage ≥80% frontend.

## Security notes
SR-038 is directly implemented here: while a book is rebuilding or stale, DOM trading affordances are disabled for that symbol — the R2 version renders them disabled anyway, but the *state plumbing* that E31 will depend on is built and tested now. The panel must never present a frozen price as live. No secrets; market data only. `marketdata:read` is enforced server-side — the client must handle a subscription rejection by showing a permission state, not a blank ladder.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA: 1.4.11 (non-text contrast for size bars), 2.1.1/2.1.2 (keyboard, no trap), 2.4.3 (focus order), 2.4.7/2.4.11 (focus visible/not obscured), 2.5.8 (target size ≥24 px), 4.1.2/4.1.3 (name/role/value, status messages). Grid pattern per WAI-ARIA APG. Data-table alternative per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 including the "no longer in view" banner.

## Performance notes
Budget: ≥55 fps at 200 visible rows, panel WS→pixel ≤120 ms p95 (stricter than the global 250 ms), virtualised DOM. React re-renders must stay off the hot path — row updates go through a per-symbol high-frequency store, not component state.

## Observability
Analytics: `dom.depth_changed`, panel mount/unmount timing against the ≤150 ms panel-mount budget. Client metrics: `dom_row_render_ms`, `dom_stale_seconds`, `dom_resync_total` reported to the performance panel.

title: Render the liquidity heatmap surface with legend, empty state and accessible reveal
body:
## Context
US-DOM-002 (Must): *"I want historical resting liquidity rendered as a heatmap behind the ladder and chart, so that I can see where liquidity sat and vanished."* E21-T05 built the engine layer; this Story mounts it in SCR-050, wires the subscription, renders CMP-113 HeatmapLegend, implements CMP-111's **logical model and accessibility contract** (the catalogue's explicit CMP-111/CMP-193 responsibility split puts the data shape and a11y here, the texture there), and handles the two states that are pure product behaviour: the no-recorded-history empty state and the estimated/resyncing rendering.

Colour convention is locked by owner decision #10 (green = bid, red = ask), user-configurable, with the legend always stating the active convention.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Subscribe `heatmap.{symbol}` with the client-derived `time_bucket_ms` per the normative algorithm in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1: one column SHOULD occupy 2–8 device pixels, 3 px target, **upward clamp at 1000 ms whenever `ideal_ms ≤ 2500`**; re-derive on pane resize, DPR change and `window_seconds` change; send `ctl { time_bucket_ms }` **debounced 400 ms**; discard state on `resnapshot: true`.
- Mount CMP-193 behind the ladder and (when the panel is chart-hosted) behind the price pane, sharing the time axis.
- **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend**: ramp with numeric anchors, active convention statement, linear/log indicator, adaptive-vs-locked indicator.
- **Empty state** (US-DOM-002 scenario 3): when the recorder has no book history for the symbol, show an explicit empty state offering to start recording, deep-linking to the recorder screen.
- **Estimated rendering**: columns with `estimated=true` at 40% opacity with the hatch; a missing column (`samples=0`) as a vertical grey stripe; both explained in the legend/tooltip, never colour-only.
- **Edge gutters** rendering `off_window_bid_qty` / `off_window_ask_qty` so the user knows depth exists beyond the visible price window (`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.2 step 4).
- **Accessible windowed reveal** (CMP-111 contract, `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2): focus a ladder row → documented key → "liquidity history at this level" as a sparkline plus data table for that price, with values as numbers.
- Cursor/hover readout carrying side and numeric size (non-colour channel per `26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Non-colour encodings").

## Out of scope
Scale/palette controls (E21-S03), trail length (E21-S04), backfill of older history (E21-S08), settings dialog (E21-S09), the texture pipeline itself (E21-T05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Heatmap trail
  Given the book has been recorded for the last 20 minutes
  Then a time-by-price heatmap renders with intensity proportional to resting size, green=bid and red=ask by default
  And it is aligned to the same time axis as the ladder and the chart

Scenario: Colour convention configurable
  When the convention is inverted in settings
  Then every heatmap surface updates consistently and the legend states the active convention

Scenario: No recorded book
  Given the recorder has no book history for this symbol
  Then the heatmap area shows an explicit empty state offering to start recording, and no misleading blank grid

Scenario: Estimated columns are visibly estimated
  Given the book was resyncing for part of the window
  Then those columns render at reduced opacity with a hatch and are described as estimated in the accessible readout

Scenario: Bucket re-derivation
  Given the pane is resized so the ideal bucket changes
  Then the client re-derives the bucket, sends ctl debounced by 400 ms, discards state on resnapshot and rebuilds without a visible tear

Scenario: Accessible reveal
  Given a keyboard user focuses a ladder row and presses the documented reveal key
  Then a table of that price level's liquidity history over the window is presented with numeric values
```

## Technical notes / design
Bucket derivation is normative and unit-tested by `heatmap_bucket_selection` (the test name is fixed by `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1 — the ladder clamp is asserted there). Frames are decoded once in the shared worker and transferred to the render worker without a copy. Reduced motion disables the fade animation and uses the static decay mode (US-DOM-002/004 NFRs).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: `heatmap_bucket_selection` (all rungs, the ≤2500 ms clamp, DPR variations); estimated/missing column classification; edge-gutter totals; empty-state predicate.
- **Storybook**: CMP-113 variants (linear/log, adaptive/locked, both conventions, CVD-safe), CMP-111 windowed-reveal output, empty state.
- **Contract**: `HeatmapColumn` schema + binary kind 6 decode.
- **Integration**: fixture stream with a resync window; assert estimated rendering and recovery.
- **E2E**: open the panel on a recorded symbol, assert the trail renders and the legend matches the active convention; open an unrecorded symbol, assert the empty state; resize the pane and assert exactly one debounced `ctl`.
- **Visual**: Playwright golden heatmap frames, `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01`.
- **A11y**: axe on the reveal output; manual SR pass on the reveal path.
- Coverage ≥80% frontend.

## Security notes
`marketdata:read`; a rejected subscription must render a permission state. The empty state's "start recording" action must respect RBAC — a `viewer` sees the explanation without the action (recording is an owner/manager capability per `04-security-program.md`). No user-supplied string reaches the shader or the topic name unvalidated (symbol comes from the instruments cache).

## Accessibility notes
Implements all three mandatory layers for this surface: DOM mirror (engine root), windowed accessible tree (§6.2 — the binding constraint CMP-111 owns), and the data-table alternative (§6.3). Bid/ask never colour-only: column/axis-side convention + text label + focus readout. Reduced-motion path required.

## Performance notes
Budget #14: 100 ms cadence sustained at 200 depth, ≤1 dropped/coalesced frame per 10 s; ≤600 GPU trail frames for this panel; the accessible reveal must build lazily on demand — it may not maintain a live table for every price level.

## Observability
`heatmap_bucket_ms` gauge, `heatmap_ctl_debounced_total`, `heatmap_estimated_columns_ratio`, empty-state impressions as analytics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass with an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Coverage: ≥85% line on touched backend/engine packages, ≥80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
