title: Chart engine: rolling-texture heatmap layer (CMP-193)
body:
## Context
CMP-193 HeatmapOverlay is, by the catalogue's explicit responsibility split, the **engine mount point**: the canvas layer, pane position, axis sync and texture-upload performance contract. (Data model and a11y belong to CMP-111 / E21-S02.) `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8 specifies the pipeline — `HeatmapColumn{time, Float32Array[rows]}` → quantise to R16F normalised by column max or global scale → `texSubImage2D` of the newest column only — which is the technique that makes the cost constant regardless of retained trail length, and therefore the only reason budget #14 is reachable.

E21-K01 fixes the open parameters (tier support, ring sizes, quantisation, aggregation strategy) before this Task builds the production layer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/src/layers/heatmap/` — a series plugin registered with the engine's plugin API (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Series plugin"), rendering 1–2 quads with the `heatmap` shader (R16F + LUT), 2 draw calls, constant per-update cost.
- `HeatmapRing`: fine ring (2048 × 512 × 2 B ≈ 2.1 MB) and coarse ring (14400 × 512 × 2 B ≈ 14.7 MB) with the aggregation rule for >1 column per pixel (max-of-columns, preserving liquidity spikes — §3.6).
- `pushHeatmapColumn(time, Float32Array)` mutation returning the affected index range for partial `bufferSubData`/`texSubImage2D` (§"Mutation API").
- **Axis sync**: the layer maps through true *time* (not bar index) via `timeToScreen`, per the bar-space-vs-time-space rule in §3.x — this is what makes heatmap↔chart time-axis alignment correct when bar spacing changes.
- DPI handling: heatmap backing store capped at devicePixelRatio 2 to bound texture cost.
- Eviction and memory governance: columns outside a 3× viewport window dropped from GPU buffers (kept in CPU stores until pressure), `MemoryGovernor` step-down at 70% of budget with a logged step; out-of-memory on texture allocation drops the coarse ring first, then halves rows (§"Failure modes").
- Degradation hooks: under `RenderProfile = degraded-2d` (WebGL2 unavailable) the heatmap is **disabled with an explanatory placeholder**, not silently blank; frame-budget shedding reduces heatmap layer DPI as its rung of the ladder.
- Golden-image test fixtures per theme.

## Out of scope
The React panel, legend, settings and a11y surfaces (E21-S02/S03/S09); backend column production (E21-T02); the LUT/palette definition (E21-T06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Constant-cost update
  Given a 60-minute trail is retained
  When a new column arrives
  Then only the newest texture column is uploaded and the measured upload cost does not grow with trail length

Scenario: Frame budget
  Given the benchmark scene of 100k bars plus a 200-depth heatmap at 100 ms cadence
  Then p95 frame time is <=16.6 ms and heatmap-attributed time is <=10 ms with texture memory <=20 MB (benchmark B4)

Scenario: Time-axis alignment
  Given the user changes bar spacing or switches to a non-time bar type
  Then heatmap columns remain aligned to wall-clock time against the shared time axis, with no drift at the right edge

Scenario: Column aggregation preserves spikes
  Given more than one column maps to a single device pixel
  Then the aggregated pixel takes the maximum of those columns so a liquidity spike is never averaged away

Scenario: Graceful failure
  Given texture allocation fails
  Then the coarse ring is dropped first, then rows are halved, each step logged and surfaced as a stats event
  And when WebGL2 is unavailable the layer renders an explanatory placeholder instead of nothing
```

## Technical notes / design
Runs in the render worker against the `OffscreenCanvas` (§"Split of responsibilities") — the main thread never touches the texture path. The WS client lives in a **shared worker** so multiple chart instances and the DOM ladder decode each frame once; decoded typed arrays are transferred to the render worker without a copy (§"WS client"). Quantisation and normalisation mode (per-column max vs global scale) come from E21-K01's finding.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: ring index arithmetic, wraparound, eviction window, aggregation max rule, DPI cap.
- **Property**: `screenToIndex(indexToScreen(i)) === i` stability and column-time monotonicity across pan/zoom (fast-check, ≥10k cases, per `26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Property").
- **Golden image**: heatmap layer per theme via Playwright against SwiftShader for determinism, ≤0.1% pixel diff — a required check.
- **Perf**: benchmark B4 (heatmap, 100 ms columns, 4 h trail, panning: ≤10 ms, upload ≤12 KB/s, texture ≤20 MB) and B5 (combined scene ≤16.7 ms, ≤40 draw calls), run in CI.
- **Failure injection**: simulated allocation failure and WebGL2 context loss (E11's context-loss recovery must restore the trail from CPU stores).
- Coverage ≥85% on the engine package.

## Security notes
No network, no credentials in the engine layer. Threat: a malformed column payload (row_count inconsistent with the buffer length) must be rejected by the decoder rather than causing an out-of-bounds read — assert with a fuzz corpus reusing E17's binary fuzz fixtures.

## Accessibility notes
This layer is deliberately *not* accessible by itself; it must emit the per-cell data needed by CMP-111's windowed reveal (E21-S02) and must not be the sole holder of any value. The DOM-mirror container is owned by the engine root (CMP-180) — this layer registers into it rather than creating its own.

## Performance notes
Budgets #1 and #14 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and B4/B5 of `26-chart-engine-design.md`. Frame-marker instrumentation matching §4.3's stage breakdown is mandatory so regressions can be stage-attributed.

## Observability
Engine stats events: `heatmap_upload_ms`, `heatmap_texture_bytes`, `heatmap_ring_evictions_total`, `heatmap_memory_stepdowns_total`, plus the frame-marker stage timings surfaced to the performance panel.

## Definition of Done

title: Adaptive colour scale, LUT pipeline and the bid/ask palette convention
body:
## Context
US-DOM-003 (Must) requires the colour scale to adapt to current liquidity via a configured percentile window, to be lockable to absolute values, and to offer logarithmic mapping — with the NFR that rescaling is smooth (no flashing) and a CVD-safe palette is available. Owner decision #10 locks the default convention (green = bid, red = ask) while requiring it to be user-configurable, and `26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Conventions" adds that a colour-blind-safe blue/orange alternative ships as a **first-class option**, not an afterthought.

Because the rendering is texture+LUT based, changing the scale or palette must be a **shader uniform / LUT swap costing ≤1 frame and must not drop the historized frame buffer** (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-051 Performance). That property is what this Task guarantees.

## Scope / Deliverables
- LUT generation from a palette definition (bid ramp, ask ramp, estimated-data hatch) and upload as a texture; swap without touching the data texture.
- Scale modes: `adaptive` (percentile window over visible columns, `clip_percentile` from `HeatmapGridSpec`), `locked` (absolute bounds), and mapping `log` (default) / `linear` with a gamma parameter.
- Smooth rescale: interpolate scale bounds over the duration from the E21-D05 motion spec; instantaneous under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Palettes: default green/red, inverted, and the CVD-safe blue/orange set, all as design tokens (`color.heatmap.bid.ramp[]`, `color.heatmap.ask.ramp[]`).
- Legend data contract feeding CMP-113: ramp stops with numeric anchors, active convention, scale type, and whether the scale is adaptive or locked.
- The automated token contrast-check integration: every gradient stop ≥3:1 against the chart background in dark, light and high-contrast themes, gated in CI on token-file changes.

## Out of scope
The legend component's visual implementation and the settings UI (E21-S03/E21-S09); the palette *design* (E21-D04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Adaptive rescale
  Given liquidity drops by an order of magnitude
  Then the scale rescales using the configured percentile window and the legend reports the new numeric bounds

Scenario: Locked scale
  When the user locks the scale to absolute values
  Then it stops adapting, the locked state is exposed in the legend contract, and bounds do not change on viewport change

Scenario: Log mapping keeps small and large distinguishable
  Given resting sizes spanning four orders of magnitude
  Then under log mapping both the smallest and largest non-zero sizes map to visually distinct LUT entries

Scenario: Cheap re-colour
  When the palette or scale changes
  Then only the LUT/uniforms are updated, the historized frame buffer is retained, and the change completes within one frame

Scenario: No flashing
  Given the scale rebounds after a liquidity collapse
  Then bounds interpolate over the specified duration, and under prefers-reduced-motion the change is instantaneous with no intermediate flash

Scenario: Contrast gate
  Given a token change alters a ramp stop below 3:1 against the chart background
  Then the CI contrast check fails the build
```

## Technical notes / design
Percentile is computed over non-zero sizes of the visible columns and recomputed on viewport change (`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.2) — compute it on the CPU side over the retained ring rather than in the shader. Log default because resting depth is heavy-tailed. Estimated columns render at 40% opacity with a hatch (§6.3) — the hatch is part of the LUT/shader path, not a DOM overlay, or it would not survive at texture density.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: percentile computation incl. all-zero and single-wall cases; log/linear/gamma mapping; locked-mode invariance; LUT generation for all three palettes.
- **Golden image**: each palette × each scale mode × each theme, ≤0.1% pixel diff.
- **Perf**: assert a palette swap costs ≤1 frame and does not reallocate the data texture.
- **A11y**: automated contrast matrix over all ramp stops, plus the three CVD simulations.
- Coverage ≥85%.

## Security notes
N/A — no data crosses a trust boundary here.

## Accessibility notes
Central to `05-accessibility-standard.md` §5: colour is a reinforcing channel only. The heatmap's side (bid/ask) is additionally carried by axis-side convention and an on-focus text readout; intensity is additionally carried in the tooltip and cursor announcement (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Non-colour encodings"). Contrast ≥3:1 at every gradient stop is a CI gate, not a spot-check.

## Performance notes
LUT swap ≤1 frame; percentile recomputation must be amortised (incremental over the ring) so a viewport change does not cause a frame spike.

## Observability
`heatmap_scale_mode` gauge; `heatmap_rescale_total`; palette selection recorded with `dom.settings_changed`.

title: Subscription quotas, abuse cases and path-safety controls for market-data reads
body:
## Context
E21-X01 enumerates the threats; this Task implements and proves the controls that close the gaps it finds, concentrated on the two that are specific to this Epic: **availability** (deep/expensive subscriptions and oversized backfills) and **path safety** (archived Parquet reads driven by user-supplied parameters).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Per-connection and per-user subscription quotas** enforced server-side: maximum concurrent deep-book subscriptions (`ws.max_deep_book_subs`, default 4), maximum concurrent `heatmap` subscriptions, and a cost-weighted budget where depth 500 and a 100 ms bucket count more than depth 50 at 1 000 ms. Exceeding a quota returns a typed protocol error (not a silent drop) that the client renders as an explanation.
- **Backfill limits**: maximum window per request, maximum concurrent backfills per user, and the server-side coarsening clamp with its effective resolution disclosed (implemented in E21-T03, *verified* here).
- **Path safety**: symbol and date parameters validated against the instruments cache and a strict pattern before any filesystem path is constructed; a path-traversal test corpus must produce rejections, never reads outside the archive root.
- **Decoder hardening**: binary frame length/`row_count` consistency checks on both server and client, with a fuzz corpus (reusing E17's) proving no out-of-bounds read or crash.
- **RBAC assertions as tests**: `marketdata:read` required on every topic and on `/market/heatmap`; `orders`/`positions` filtered by account scope server-side — a hand-crafted subscribe frame from a restricted manager must fail, asserted at the protocol level, not just in the UI.
- **Audit/telemetry**: quota rejections, permission denials, backfill clamps and slow-consumer closures all counted and alertable.
- Semgrep/Bandit rules where a generic pattern exists (e.g. filesystem path construction from request parameters in the market-data package) added to the SAST config.

## Out of scope
Auth/session mechanics (E09); pen-test remediation (E43); OMS authorisation (E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Quota enforced and explained
  Given a client already holds the maximum number of deep-book subscriptions
  When it subscribes to another depth-500 topic
  Then the server rejects it with a typed error, increments a metric, and the client shows an explanation rather than retrying in a loop

Scenario: Cross-account subscription refused at the protocol level
  Given a manager permitted only account A hand-crafts a subscription implying account B
  Then the server refuses it, the refusal is audited, and no frame containing account B data is ever emitted on that connection

Scenario: Path traversal refused
  Given a backfill request carries a symbol or date parameter crafted to escape the archive root
  Then the request is rejected during validation and no filesystem access outside the archive root occurs

Scenario: Malformed binary frame
  Given a frame whose declared row_count does not match its payload length
  Then the decoder rejects it without an out-of-bounds read, on both server and client, for every case in the fuzz corpus

Scenario: Oversized backfill
  Given a request spanning 30 days at 100 ms resolution
  Then the server clamps it, discloses the effective resolution, and the clamp is counted
```

## Technical notes / design
Cost weighting formula for the quota is documented alongside the constants so it can be tuned without re-deriving it. Quotas are enforced at the gateway (single choke point) rather than per engine, so no topic can be added later that forgets them — add a test asserting that any new topic registered in the catalogue is covered by the quota accounting.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: quota accounting and cost weights; parameter validators; decoder length checks.
- **Fuzz**: binary frame corpus (server decode and client decode).
- **Integration**: restricted-scope manager attempting cross-account subscription; path-traversal corpus against the backfill endpoint.
- **Load**: quota behaviour under the worst-case profile from E21-Q03 (quotas must not falsely trigger under legitimate realistic-peak usage — a false-positive quota rejection is a defect).
- **SAST**: the new Semgrep rules fire on a deliberately vulnerable fixture and do not fire on the fixed code.
- Coverage ≥85% on touched backend packages.

## Security notes
Directly implements mitigations for the D (denial of service), I (information disclosure) and T (tampering) rows of E21-X01. Data classification: market data public; orders/positions account-scoped financial. This ticket is `security`-labelled and requires Security engineer review per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8.

## Accessibility notes
Quota and permission errors must be surfaced as readable text with a remedy, announced politely — a silently blank panel is both an a11y and a security-usability failure.

## Performance notes
Quota checks are on the subscribe path, not the frame path, so they add no per-frame cost; the assertion that legitimate realistic-peak usage never trips a quota is a required test.

## Observability
`ws_subscription_quota_rejections_total{reason}`, `ws_permission_denied_total`, `heatmap_backfill_clamped_total`, `ws_slow_consumer_closures_total`, plus audit entries for cross-account subscription attempts (which are a genuine security signal, not noise).

title: Implement BigTradeEngine: thresholds, percentiles and deterministic clustering
body:
## Context
US-BIG-002 NFR: "thresholds per symbol; **evaluation backend-side so tape, bubbles and alerts agree**". US-BIG-004 NFR: "deterministic and unit-tested; **clustering happens once, backend-side**". This task builds the single engine that both statements demand, inside module **M9** (`server/orderflow/`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` — "orderflow/ # footprint, profile, cvd, imbalance, heatmap, tape"). Everything else in E22 — the tape highlight, the chart bubbles, the future alert condition — renders this engine's output.

Input is the normalised trade stream produced by E08 (US-MKT-006: each print normalised to `{ts, price, qty, side, tradeId}`, published on the internal bus exactly once, idempotent by `tradeId`). Bybit supplies the aggressor side directly (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`: "Bybit gives the **aggressor side directly** (`S`), so no tick-rule reconstruction is needed — this is the single most important simplification in the whole order-flow stack"), so side is **exact**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/bigtrade.py`: `BigTradeEngine` with per-symbol config and three threshold modes — `absolute_size` (base units), `notional` (price × size, USDT), `percentile` (rank over a rolling window, default 3 600 000 ms).
- Rolling percentile estimator: a bounded-memory streaming quantile (t-digest or P²) over print notionals, publishing the **effective absolute threshold** so the UI can display it (US-BIG-002 scenario 2) and refreshing at most every 5 s.
- Over-flagging guard: when the flagged fraction over the trailing window exceeds **20 %**, emit a `threshold_too_low` advisory with a suggested value and cap highlighting (US-BIG-002 scenario 3).
- Deterministic cluster state machine: per `(symbol, side, price_bucket)` open cluster with a `window_ms` deadline and `tolerance_ticks` bucket width (tick size from the instruments-info cache); merge on same side + within tolerance of the anchor price + inside the deadline; else emit and open a new cluster. **Bar attribution: the cluster belongs to the bar containing its first print** (US-BIG-004 scenario 3).
- Immediate recompute on config change: changing the window recomputes clustering from the stored prints without a restart (US-BIG-004 scenario 2).
- Metric descriptors registered in `MetricRegistry` per `24-internal-schemas.md`: `big_trade_notional` (largest print notional in window, `window_ms=1000`, exact), `big_trade_zscore` (z-score of print size vs rolling mean, `window=500 trades`, `z_threshold=3.0`, exact), `trade_cluster` (`window_ms=50` default, confidence **estimated**).
- Outputs on the internal bus consumed by E22-T02 (wire) and by E40's alert evaluator later.

## Out of scope
Wire encoding and endpoints (E22-T02); UI (S01–S05); speed-of-tape and iceberg detection (E25); liquidation prints (E24).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Notional threshold flags exactly the right prints
  Given a recorded BTCUSDT window and a threshold of 250000 USDT notional
  When the window is processed
  Then the set of flagged print ids equals the set computed by an independent DuckDB query over the Parquet tier with WHERE notional >= 250000

Scenario: Percentile mode publishes its effective threshold
  Given percentile mode at the 99th percentile over a 1 hour window
  Then each emitted config echo carries the current effective absolute threshold
  And the estimator's value is within 1 percent of an exact quantile over the same window

Scenario: Clustering is deterministic
  Given cluster_window_ms = 250 and cluster_tolerance_ticks = 1
  When the same recorded window is processed twice, including once with prints delivered in differently-sized batches
  Then the emitted clusters are identical in count, membership, aggregate size and attributed bar

Scenario: A cluster spanning a bar boundary
  Given a cluster whose first print is in bar N and whose last print is in bar N+1
  Then the cluster is attributed to bar N

Scenario: Over-flagging is caught
  Given a threshold that flags more than 20 percent of prints over the trailing window
  Then a threshold_too_low advisory with a suggested value is emitted and highlighting is capped

Scenario: Duplicate print after reconnect
  Given the same tradeId is delivered twice after a resubscribe
  Then it is counted once in thresholds, clustering and metrics
```

## Technical notes / design
Config shape (mirrors the WS options in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 so there is one vocabulary):
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BigTradeConfig:
    mode: Literal["absolute_size", "notional", "percentile"] = "notional"
    value: Decimal = Decimal("250000")       # units depend on mode; percentile => 0..100
    percentile_window_ms: int = 3_600_000
    cluster_window_ms: int = 0               # 0 disables clustering
    cluster_tolerance_ticks: int = 0
```
Determinism rules: process prints in `(ts, tradeId)` order; never use wall-clock time in the state machine — deadlines are evaluated against print timestamps so replay and live take the same path (R2 exit criterion #1: one shared pipeline for live and replay). Use `Decimal` for price/size arithmetic, consistent with the `Decimal` string types in the API and WS schemas. Price bucketing: `bucket = floor(price / (tick_size * max(1, tolerance_ticks)))` with the anchor price retained for display. Memory: bounded ring per symbol sized by `max(percentile_window_ms, cluster_window_ms)` and a hard cap; emit a metric when the cap truncates.

## Test plan
- Unit: each threshold mode; percentile estimator accuracy vs exact quantile on synthetic and recorded distributions; cluster merge/emit boundaries (exactly at the deadline, one tick outside tolerance, opposite side); bar attribution across boundaries; duplicate `tradeId`; config change mid-stream; empty and single-print windows; `cluster_window_ms=0` short-circuit.
- Property: batching invariance (same prints, different batch splits → identical output); ordering invariance under `(ts, tradeId)` sort.
- Integration: recorded fixtures — normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol.
- Coverage target ≥85 % on `server/orderflow/bigtrade.py`.

## Security notes
Bounds-check every config value at the engine boundary (`cluster_window_ms` 0–5000, `cluster_tolerance_ticks` 0–20, percentile 0–100, non-negative threshold) so a malformed subscription cannot allocate unbounded state — this is the primary DoS control identified in the epic's STRIDE (E22-X01). Market data is classification **public**; no secrets touched.

## Performance notes
Evaluation must add ≤2 ms p95 to the ingest→bus path (US-MKT-006 NFR: ingest→bus ≤20 ms p95 total) and sustain 5 000 prints/s across subscribed symbols without loss (budget #5). Per-symbol memory must stay inside budget #8 (≤300 MB per actively-recorded symbol, shared with book state and bar builders).

title: Expose big trades over trades.{symbol} WS options and /market/trades
body:
## Context
The contracts this epic needs are already specified and must be *implemented*, not redesigned. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 defines `trades.{symbol}` with options `min_size`, `cluster_window_ms`, `cluster_tolerance_ticks`, snapshot "Last 200 prints", default throttle 100 ms, binary `body_kind 3`; §14.2 defines `TradesBatch` with `cluster_size`, `is_block_trade`, `is_liquidation`, `tick_direction` and `dropped` ("Prints filtered out by `min_size` since the previous frame; **never silent**"); §3.4 fixes the 22-byte binary record with `flags` bit0 block trade, bit1 liquidation-origin, **bit2 cluster-aggregated**. REST side: `GET /market/trades` (`side`, `min_size`, `cluster_window_ms` 0–5000, `cluster_tolerance_ticks` 0–20, cursor pagination) and `GET /market/metrics` for `big_trade_notional` / `big_trade_zscore`. Interface-first rule (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) applies: any diff to these documents is drafted and reviewed before implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wire the `BigTradeEngine` (E22-T01) output into the `trades.{symbol}` publisher: apply `min_size` server-side, populate `cluster_size` and binary `flags` bit2, maintain and emit `dropped` per frame.
- Implement the append-never-merge throttling rule for `trades` (§"`trades`, `liquidations` | **Append, never merge**") and set `coalesced` / `coalesced_count` so the UI can display the coalescing factor required by US-BIG-001.
- Subscribe/ack path: echo the effective options in the `ok` response (`effective: { throttle_ms, encoding, min_size, cluster_window_ms, cluster_tolerance_ticks }`) and reject out-of-range options with a topic-scoped error rather than clamping silently.
- Extend the big-trade flag and the effective absolute threshold into the subscription echo so tape and bubbles never recompute a threshold client-side.
- REST: implement `GET /market/trades` filters and clustering (delegating to the same engine), and register `big_trade_notional` / `big_trade_zscore` in `GET /market/metrics`.
- Contract tests against the OpenAPI document and the WS JSON Schemas; update `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` if a field is genuinely missing (e.g. the effective-threshold echo) via a reviewed diff.

## Out of scope
Engine logic (E22-T01); any UI; alert delivery (E40); liquidation topic (E24).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Server-side filtering is never silent
  Given a subscription to trades.BTCUSDT with min_size 0.5
  When prints below 0.5 arrive
  Then they are excluded from the frame and the frame's dropped counter reports exactly how many were excluded since the previous frame

Scenario: Clustering is signalled on both encodings
  Given cluster_window_ms 250 and cluster_tolerance_ticks 1
  Then JSON frames carry cluster_size greater than 1 for merged prints and binary kind 3 records set flags bit2
  And a client decoding either encoding reconstructs identical cluster membership counts

Scenario: Out-of-range options are rejected
  Given a subscription with cluster_window_ms 999999
  Then the subscribe response is ok false with a topic-scoped error naming the parameter and its allowed range, and no subscription is created

Scenario: REST and WS agree
  Given the same window requested over GET /market/trades and captured live over trades.BTCUSDT with identical options
  Then the flagged print set and the cluster membership are identical

Scenario: Coalescing is visible
  Given a burst that forces frames to coalesce
  Then coalesced is true and coalesced_count reports the number of merged source updates, and no print is lost from the batch
```

## Technical notes / design
Keep the 100 ms default throttle for `trades.{symbol}`; the snapshot is the last 200 prints. Binary record layout (do not deviate): `u32 ts_offset_ms`, `i64 price` (scaled), `u64 size` (scaled), `u8 side` (0 buy, 1 sell), `u8 flags`. Client obligations from §3.4 are mirrored in the contract tests: a body whose length disagrees with `record_count` is `frame_malformed`. `permessage-deflate` stays **off** for `cv.v1.msgpack` and on for JSON. RBAC: both endpoints carry `x-rbac: { permissions: [marketdata:read], scope: none }` — enforce server-side per global AC #1 (403 + audit, no state change).


**Sizing note.** Re-sized 3 → 2 pts: the WS envelope, framing, sequencing and REST pagination conventions are already established by E17; this task adds options and one payload to an existing topic. Total S/T/K engineering points for E22 are held at 22, inside the ±15% band around the roadmap's 21 pts for this epic (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 122/313).

## Test plan
- Contract: OpenAPI schema validation for `/market/trades` and `/market/metrics`; JSON-Schema validation of every emitted `TradesBatch`; binary round-trip decode of kind 3 including flags.
- Unit: `dropped` accounting across frame boundaries; option validation table (min/max/типы); effective-option echo.
- Integration: recorded fixtures incl. disconnect+resync (snapshot re-delivery) and sequence gap.
- Load: 2 000 prints/s on one symbol with 5 subscribers; assert zero lost prints and bounded frame sizes (§3.6 frame size limits).
- Coverage ≥85 % on the touched API/WS modules.

## Security notes
This is the epic's main DoS surface (STRIDE-D, E22-X01): enforce the documented parameter bounds, the per-connection subscription cap, and `Limit`/cursor pagination on the REST path; a `min_size=0` subscription on a hot symbol must be shed by throttling and coalescing rather than by unbounded buffering. Reject unknown options instead of ignoring them. Data classification public; RBAC still required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (contract layer), but `dropped` and `coalesced_count` exist precisely so the UI can be honest — do not optimise them away.

## Performance notes
Backend fan-out add-on ≤20 ms p95 (budget #6); WS tick → screen p95 <100 ms end-to-end is the hard R2 gate (budget #3) and this layer owns the server half of it.

## Observability
`ws_frames_emitted_total{topic="trades"}`, `ws_frame_bytes{topic="trades"}`, `tape_prints_dropped_total{reason="min_size"}`, `tape_frames_coalesced_total`, `ws_subscribe_rejected_total{reason}`; span `ws.publish.trades`.

title: Motion spec and accessibility review for the CVD / delta pane
body:
## Context
A streaming pane is a motion surface whether or not anyone designs it. `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` owns the motion vocabulary and the `prefers-reduced-motion` contract; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` Â§6.1 owns the canvas control surrogate pattern. This ticket makes both explicit for SCR-052 before engineering starts, and runs the formal a11y design review that must pass before handoff (D05).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion spec: the forming bar's update cadence (capped at 10 Hz by the SCR-052 performance note â€” motion must not imply anything faster), the appearance of a new divergence marker on bar close, the transition when the display mode changes (US-CVD-003 requires switching to be *instant from cached values*, so the transition must be a cross-fade of at most one frame budget, never a re-animation of the series), the anchor-change transition when CVD recomputes from a new anchor, and the stale-data shading fade-in after 2 s.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for every one of the above: values still update, but transitions collapse to instant state changes.
- Accessibility review of the D03 comps against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: focus order, focus-visible treatment, the table-alternative markup contract (headers, caption, row identity), the screen-reader announcement text for each divergence event, the `(estimated)` chip's accessible name and its popover's focus management (open, trap, dismiss on Escape, return focus), and target sizes for the header controls.
- A written a11y acceptance checklist that E23-Q04 will audit against.

## Out of scope
Implementation; the handoff pack (D05); the audit itself (Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every animated transition has a spec
  When the motion spec is reviewed
  Then each transition names its trigger, duration, easing token and its reduced-motion fallback

Scenario: Reduced motion is honoured without losing information
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then every transition collapses to an instant state change
  And no information conveyed only by animation is lost

Scenario: The a11y review produces a testable checklist
  Then the checklist enumerates focus order, the table-alternative markup contract, the per-divergence announcement text and the popover focus-management rules
  And every item is phrased so QA can pass or fail it objectively
```

## Technical notes / design
Motion durations must come from existing tokens; the pane is inside the 16.6 ms frame budget shared with the whole workspace, so no transition may drive a continuous animation while the series is also streaming. The mode-switch cross-fade in particular must be bounded: US-CVD-003 scenario 2 states switching is instant from cached values, so the cross-fade is cosmetic polish that must be skippable.

## Test plan
Review session with the accessibility specialist and an `area/order-flow` engineer; the output checklist is attached to E23-Q04 as its audit basis.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). SCR-052 is WebGL-rendered, so the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) applies: the pane exposes an **accessible table alternative** (per-bar time, delta, CVD, divergence flag) reachable from the panel header by keyboard, marked up as a real `table` with row/column headers; divergences are additionally listed as **text events**. All controls (reset anchor, display mode, smoothing, divergence toggle) are real focusable form controls with visible focus rings >=3:1 against the pane background. The sign of delta is carried by **text sign + bar direction**, never colour alone; buy/sell hues are verified under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia. The streaming series carries no `aria-live` (that would flood a screen reader at tick rate); the user polls values via the table alternative.

## Performance notes
No transition may exceed one frame's share of the pane's <=2 ms CPU budget; continuous background animation is prohibited on this pane.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Reduced-motion behaviour specified for every transition
- [ ] A11y review completed and the checklist handed to E23-Q04
- [ ] Accessibility specialist sign-off

title: Implement CvdEngine in M9: anchors, intrabar path and EMA smoothing
body:
## Context
The backend heart of the epic. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` places CVD inside **M9** (`server/orderflow/` â€” "footprint, profile, **cvd**, imbalance, heatmap, tape"), and US-CVD-001's NFR requires it to **share the delta computation used by footprint and Deep-Stats**. E18 has already built the per-bar bid/ask aggregation; this ticket adds the cumulative layer on top of it and persists the result to `orderflow_metrics`.

The engine is the single source of truth: the pane (E23-S01..S05), the alerts (E40), the rule-engine metric `cvd_divergence` (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` Â§metric vocabulary) and the detectors (E25, roadmap graph `E23 --> E25`) all read its output. There is exactly one implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/cvd/engine.py` â€” `CvdEngine`, keyed by `(symbol, bar_type, param, anchor_spec)`, consuming the per-bar aggregate emitted by E18's aggregation stage (not raw prints â€” the fold over prints already happens there).
- **Anchor semantics** (US-CVD-002): `session` (reset at `session_anchor`, default `utc_day`), `utc_day`, `never` (anchor at the first available print; the engine reports that timestamp so the UI can label the start point), `manual` (a client-supplied bar timestamp, clamped to the loaded range). A reset emits an explicit `CvdResetMarker` event carrying the anchor timestamp and kind so the UI can mark it (US-CVD-002 scenario 1: "CVD resets there and the reset is marked").
- **Intrabar path** for CVD-candle mode (US-CVD-003): per bar, `cvd_open`, `cvd_high = cvd_open + max_delta`, `cvd_low = cvd_open + min_delta`, `cvd_close = cvd_open + delta`, taken from the bar's `min_delta`/`max_delta` (bar invariant **BI-3**, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`), plus an availability flag derived from the E23-K01 precondition so the API can report the mode as unavailable with a reason rather than returning wrong candles.
- **EMA smoothing** as an additional series, never a replacement (US-CVD-003 scenario 3: "a smoothed overlay renders and the raw series remains visible"). Period configurable, default 9.
- **Gap handling** (US-CVD-001 scenario 3): bars covered by a recorded ingestion gap are flagged `gapped=true` and **excluded from derived metrics**; the flag travels with the bar to the client.
- **Provisional bar**: the forming bar's CVD value is emitted with `confirm=false` so the UI can style it as provisional and so divergence detection (E23-T01's sibling detector, built in E23-S04/S05) never fires on it.
- Persistence: write `cvd`, `cvd_session` and `delta_1s` to QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` at the 1 s cadence that table specifies (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` Â§4.11, `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol)`), so the series is cheaply scrubbable and can act as a recompute checkpoint if E23-K01 approved that.
- A pure, side-effect-free `recompute(prints_or_bars, anchor) -> series` function, so the same code serves live, replay, backfill and the parity harness â€” one code path, per roadmap R2 exit criterion 1.

## Out of scope
The WS/REST surface (E23-T02), the reconnect repair orchestration (E23-T03), divergence detection (E23-S04/S05 own the detector), composite/normalised CVD (E23-S06, R5), any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Delta is not recomputed independently
  When the CvdEngine source is reviewed
  Then it consumes the per-bar bid/ask aggregate produced by the footprint aggregation stage
  And contains no second fold over raw prints for the purpose of computing delta

Scenario: Session anchor resets and marks
  Given the anchor is session with session_anchor utc_day
  When the series crosses 00:00 UTC
  Then the cumulative value resets to zero at that boundary
  And a CvdResetMarker carrying the anchor kind and timestamp is emitted exactly once

Scenario: Never-reset labels its start
  Given the anchor is never
  Then the series accumulates across the whole loaded range
  And the engine reports the timestamp of the first available print as the series start

Scenario: Manual anchor recomputes forward only
  Given an existing series anchored at session
  When a manual anchor is set at bar T
  Then the series from T forward is recomputed from that anchor
  And values before T are unchanged in the persisted 1 s samples

Scenario: Intrabar OHLC obeys the bar invariant
  Given a bar with delta 12, min_delta -3 and max_delta 20 and cvd_open 100
  Then the CVD candle is open 100, low 97, high 120, close 112
  And low <= open <= high and low <= close <= high always hold

Scenario: Candles are refused, not faked, without tick data
  Given the requested range predates the recorder's first available print for the symbol
  When CVD-candle mode is requested
  Then the engine reports the mode unavailable with a machine-readable reason
  And emits no candle values for that range

Scenario: Gapped bars are excluded
  Given an ingestion gap covers bars 40 to 44
  Then those bars are flagged gapped
  And they are excluded from the derived smoothing and from divergence inputs

Scenario: Smoothing never hides the raw series
  Given EMA smoothing of period 9 is enabled
  Then both the raw and the smoothed series are emitted as separate series
```

## Technical notes / design
State per key: `cum: Decimal`, `anchor_ts: int`, `anchor_kind: Literal["session","utc_day","never","manual"]`, `last_bar_ts: int`. Use the same decimal/quantity type as `TradeEvent.qty` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`) â€” no float accumulation in the running sum, because a running sum over millions of prints is exactly where float error compounds and roadmap exit criterion 6 demands parity with an offline DuckDB recomputation.

An anchor change is **not** an incremental operation: it invalidates the cumulative state and triggers `recompute()` over the affected window with `reason="anchor_change"`. Reuse the recompute entry point E23-T03 wires to the resync path so there is one repair implementation.

Config keys: `orderflow.cvd.default_anchor` (default `session`), `orderflow.cvd.session_anchor` (default `utc_day`), `orderflow.cvd.smoothing_default_period` (default `9`), `orderflow.cvd.persist_cadence_ms` (default `1000`), `orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints` (clamp, default `5_000_000`). Error codes: `CVD_CANDLES_UNAVAILABLE`, `CVD_ANCHOR_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `CVD_RECOMPUTE_TOO_LARGE`.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** delta sign mapping from `TradeEvent.side`; session reset at the UTC boundary including a bar that straddles it; `utc_day` vs `session` equivalence when `session_anchor=utc_day`; never-reset start labelling; manual anchor inside, at and outside the loaded range; intrabar OHLC from (delta, min_delta, max_delta) including the degenerate `min == max == delta` case; EMA warm-up behaviour for the first n-1 bars; gapped-bar exclusion; provisional-bar `confirm=false`; decimal precision over a 1M-print fold.
- **Property:** for any print sequence, `cvd[n] == sum(delta[0..n])` from the anchor; `cvd_low <= cvd_open,cvd_close <= cvd_high` (BI-3).
- **Integration:** against recorded Bybit fixtures â€” normal session, high-volatility burst, sequence gap, thin-book symbol (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6.4 Integration gate).
- **Coverage:** >=85% line on `server/orderflow/cvd/`.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
Marginal CPU over the existing footprint aggregation must stay inside per-symbol budget #11 (<=0.5 vCPU sustained). Persistence at 1 s cadence must be batched, not per-bar-per-row. Recompute performance target comes from US-CVD-002 (1M prints <= 2 s) as validated by E23-K01.

## Observability
Add `cv_cvd_engine_updates_total{symbol,anchor}`, `cv_cvd_recompute_seconds`, `cv_cvd_recompute_total{reason}`, `cv_cvd_persist_rows_total`, and a gauge `cv_cvd_anchor_age_seconds{symbol}`. Log `cvd.anchor_changed` with old/new anchor at INFO; log `cvd.candles_unavailable` at DEBUG with the reason code. Trace span `orderflow.cvd.update`.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§3.2/Â§4.2:
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via a PR <=400 LOC diff with 2 approvals incl. 1 `area/order-flow` code-owner
- [ ] Unit coverage >=85% (backend/engine) / >=80% (frontend) on the changed package; no coverage regression

## Dependencies
`E18` â€” the per-bar bid/ask aggregation this engine consumes (hard: forking it is a defect); `E12` â€” the bar grid and per-bar `delta`/`min_delta`/`max_delta`; `E23-K01` â€” the recompute approach and the candles precondition; `E23-X01` â€” the threat model's clamping requirements must be known before the recompute entry point is written.

title: Expose CVD and delta over metrics.{symbol} WS and /market/metrics
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` Â§0.4 states the design constraint plainly: "**Derived order-flow series share one topic.** CVD, tape speed, imbalance, regime and the estimated detectors are all `metrics.{symbol}`, selected by the `metrics` option... They are one engine output family and one subscription, not five." SCR-052's data line confirms: "WS `metrics.{symbol}`, bootstrap `GET /api/v1/market/metrics?symbol&interval&from&to`".

E17 has already built the topic machinery, sequencing and resync. This ticket wires the `CvdEngine` output into that existing surface â€” it adds metric codes and options, it does not add a topic.

**Estimate note (2 pts, was 3).** E17 already owns the `metrics.{symbol}` topic machinery, sequencing, resync and the `MetricsUpdate` schema; this ticket adds metric codes, options and the REST bootstrap branch to an existing surface, so it is sized as an extension, not a new transport.

## Scope / Deliverables
- WS: support `metrics: ["cvd", "delta", "min_max_delta"]` on `metrics.{symbol}` with the documented options `bar_type`, `param`, `throttle_ms` (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§topic table), plus per-metric params via the existing params mechanism â€” specifically `{"cvd": {"anchor": "session"|"utc_day"|"never"|"manual", "session_anchor": "utc_day", "manual_anchor_ts": <ms>, "smoothing": {"kind":"ema","period":9}}}`.
- Emit frames conforming to the existing `MetricsUpdate` schema (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§14), each series carrying `metric`, `estimated` (**false** for `cvd` and `delta` â€” they are measured, not inferred), `unit` (`base_volume`), `t_ms` and `v`; the subscribe ack echoes `effective` options exactly as Â§5 requires.
- Carry the epic's extra per-bar attributes alongside: `confirm` (provisional forming bar), `gapped`, and the `CvdResetMarker` events, so the pane can render provisional styling, hatching and reset markers without a second request.
- REST bootstrap: `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` support for `metric=cvd|delta|min_max_delta` with the `params` JSON override documented in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`{"cvd":{"anchor":"utc_day"}}`), returning each series with its **parameter echo** so charts are reproducible, and returning the series start timestamp for `anchor=never`.
- REST: ensure `GET /api/v1/market/bars?include_delta=true` returns `delta`, `cvd`, `min_delta`, `max_delta` per bar as the OpenAPI examples already show, sourced from the same engine.
- **Partial-history reporting**: when the requested `from` predates the recorder's first available print, the response reports the first available timestamp in a machine-readable field rather than silently truncating â€” this is what the UI renders for roadmap R2 exit criterion 5.
- **Candles availability**: report `CVD_CANDLES_UNAVAILABLE` with a reason when the intrabar precondition is unmet, so US-CVD-003's "disabled with an explanation" is data-driven.
- Server-side clamping per the threat model: `maxItems: 12` on `metric` (already in the OpenAPI schema), a maximum range per request, a maximum `metrics` count and a minimum `throttle_ms` per session, and validation of `manual_anchor_ts` against the requested range.
- Contract tests against the `MetricsUpdate` and `BarsBatch` JSON Schemas and against the OpenAPI document; `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` updated if anything drifted.

## Out of scope
A new topic or endpoint of any kind; the reconnect repair logic (E23-T03); the frontend subscription client (E23-S01); composite multi-symbol series (E23-S06, R5).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One subscription carries the family
  Given a client subscribes to metrics.BTCUSDT with metrics ["cvd","delta"]
  Then a single subscription is created
  And the ack echoes the effective throttle_ms, bar_type, param and per-metric params

Scenario: CVD is not marked estimated
  When a cvd or delta series frame is decoded
  Then its estimated field is false
  And the unit is base_volume

Scenario: REST and WS agree
  Given a REST bootstrap for a closed range and a WS attach for the same range
  Then the overlapping values are identical to the last emitted decimal

Scenario: Partial history is reported, not hidden
  Given the recorder's first print for the symbol is at 09:12 and from is 08:00
  Then the response reports 09:12 as the first available timestamp
  And contains no values before it

Scenario: Candles unavailability is explicit
  Given the intrabar precondition is unmet for the requested range
  When min_max_delta is requested
  Then the response carries the reason code CVD_CANDLES_UNAVAILABLE
  And no fabricated high or low values are returned

Scenario: A hostile subscription is refused
  Given a client requests 12 metrics across 40 symbols with throttle_ms 1
  Then the subscription is refused or clamped to the configured session limits
  And the rejection is counted and logged with its reason

Scenario: An out-of-range manual anchor is rejected
  Given manual_anchor_ts lies outside the requested range
  Then the request fails with CVD_ANCHOR_OUT_OF_RANGE and a 422 response
```

## Technical notes / design
Do not introduce a binary `body_kind` for metrics: the Â§3.4 binary layouts cover book, trades, bars, footprint and heatmap; metrics are low-cardinality and scalar, and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§14 shows them travelling as JSON (`"e":"j"`) inside the MessagePack envelope. The 10 Hz UI cap (SCR-052) is enforced client-side by coalescing; the server's `throttle_ms` default for `metrics.{symbol}` stays as documented (250 ms) â€” do not lower it to chase perceived smoothness, because that multiplies fan-out cost (budget #6, <=20 ms p95 backend-internal add-on).

Config keys: `ws.metrics.max_metrics_per_sub` (12), `ws.metrics.min_throttle_ms` (100), `ws.metrics.max_subs_per_session`, `api.metrics.max_range_days`.

## Test plan
- **Contract:** every emitted frame validated against `MetricsUpdate`; every REST response against the OpenAPI schema; the subscribe-ack `effective` echo asserted field by field.
- **Unit:** params parsing and validation (anchor kinds, malformed JSON, oversize `params` string >2048 chars, out-of-range `manual_anchor_ts`); clamping logic; partial-history field computation.
- **Integration:** REST-then-WS handoff with no duplicated or missing points at the seam; reconnect with `from_seq` attach.
- **Load:** included in E23-Q03's k6 script â€” 10 symbols x 3 metrics, sustained, asserting budget #6.
- **Coverage:** >=85% on the changed modules.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
Backend fan-out add-on must stay within budget #6 (<=20 ms p95 from engine update to outbound frame). WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms is a **hard R2 exit gate** (budget #3) and this path is on it. Serialisation must not allocate per point in the hot path.

## Observability
`cv_ws_metrics_subs_active{metric}`, `cv_ws_metrics_frames_total{metric}`, `cv_metrics_subscription_rejected_total{reason}`, `cv_api_metrics_request_seconds{metric}`. Log rejected subscriptions at WARN with the clamped values. Trace span `ws.metrics.publish` linked to `orderflow.cvd.update`.

Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§3.2/Â§4.2:

## Dependencies
`E23-T01` â€” the engine output being exposed; `E17` â€” the `metrics.{symbol}` topic, sequencing, framing and resync machinery this ticket plugs into.

title: Recompute CVD from the recorded tape on WS gap or reconnect
body:
## Context
This is the ticket the roadmap singled out for this epic: "**correct CVD reconstruction after WS reconnect** (recompute from recorded trades, never guess)" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6.2). It matters more here than anywhere else in R2 because CVD is a *running sum*: a footprint cell that misses a print is wrong for one bar, but a CVD series that misses a print is wrong **forever after**, silently, and by an amount no user can detect by looking.

The protocol already gives us the detection primitive: `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§7 defines per-topic sequence numbers and an explicit resync protocol, and notes that for `trades` the merge rule is "**Append, never merge** ... Every print matters for the tape and CVD." Guarantee G3 states "Correctness under loss is deterministic, not best-effort."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Gap detection on the ingestion side: when the trade stream's sequence is broken, or the adapter reconnects after a disconnect, mark the affected `(symbol, window)` as **suspect** and trigger a repair rather than continuing to accumulate.
- Repair path: call `CvdEngine.recompute()` over the suspect window sourced from the **recorded tape** â€” QuestDB `trades` for the hot window, the Parquet cold tier via DuckDB beyond retention â€” using the approach E23-K01 recommended (including the `orderflow_metrics` 1 s checkpoint optimisation if it was proven exact).
- Correct the persisted `orderflow_metrics` rows for the window (the table is `DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol)`, so repair is an upsert, not a delete-and-insert) and re-derive every downstream cumulative value.
- Re-snapshot subscribed clients: after repair, push a fresh `metrics.{symbol}` snapshot rather than a delta, so no client holds a value derived from the corrupt prefix. The resync follows the existing Â§7 protocol; no bespoke mechanism.
- **Recorder-gap case:** if the recorded tape itself has a hole (the recorder was down, or the symbol was not recorded), the window is marked `gapped` and the affected bars are excluded from derived metrics (US-CVD-001 scenario 3) and surfaced to the UI â€” CVD is **not** interpolated across the hole, and the series start is re-labelled if the hole touches the anchor.
- A `repairing` state exposed to the client so the pane can show it, per the E23-K01 recommendation if repair is asynchronous.
- Clamping: repairs are bounded by `orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints`; a window exceeding it degrades to marking the range `gapped` rather than running an unbounded scan (this is the DoS control from the threat model).

## Out of scope
Book resync (E21/E08 own `BookDesyncEvent`), replay-specific reconstruction (E26), the pane's rendering of the repairing/gapped states (E23-S01/S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reconnect produces the exact uninterrupted value
  Given a client streaming metrics.BTCUSDT with anchor session
  And the upstream trade stream is severed for 45 seconds during which 8,000 prints occur
  When the stream reconnects and the gap is detected
  Then CVD is recomputed for the gap window from the recorded tape
  And the post-repair cumulative value equals, to the last decimal, the value computed by an uninterrupted run over the same recorded prints

Scenario: The corrupt prefix never reaches a client
  When a repair completes
  Then subscribed clients receive a fresh snapshot rather than a delta
  And no client retains a value derived from the pre-repair accumulation

Scenario: A hole in the recording is admitted, not smoothed
  Given the recorder was not running for part of the gap window
  Then the affected bars are flagged gapped and excluded from derived metrics
  And no interpolated CVD value is emitted for them

Scenario: Repair is bounded
  Given a gap window containing more prints than orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints
  Then the repair is refused, the window is flagged gapped, and the refusal is logged and counted
  And the service does not run an unbounded scan

Scenario: Repeated flapping does not stampede
  Given the upstream stream disconnects and reconnects five times in one minute
  Then repairs for overlapping windows are coalesced into one
  And the repair count metric reflects the coalescing
```

## Technical notes / design
Repair is idempotent by construction: `recompute(window)` is pure and the persistence is an upsert on `(ts, symbol)`. Coalesce overlapping repair requests through a per-symbol repair queue with a single in-flight repair; a new gap arriving during a repair extends the window rather than starting a second job.

Ordering guarantee: prints are folded in recorded timestamp order with a deterministic tie-break (by the exchange trade id) so that two repairs over the same window always produce the same result â€” this is what makes the replay double-run determinism test (roadmap Â§6.4) pass for CVD.

Error codes: `CVD_RECOMPUTE_TOO_LARGE`, `CVD_RECORDING_GAP`. Config: `orderflow.cvd.max_recompute_prints`, `orderflow.cvd.repair_coalesce_ms` (default 2000).

## Test plan
- **Unit:** gap-window computation from sequence numbers; repair coalescing (overlapping, adjacent, disjoint windows); the bounded-refusal path; tie-break ordering determinism.
- **Integration:** against the recorded fixture "WS disconnect + resync" and "sequence gap" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6.4 Integration gate). The key assertion is the equality of post-repair CVD with an uninterrupted run over the same fixture.
- **Chaos:** owned by E23-Q06 â€” repeated disconnects, a disconnect straddling a session anchor, a disconnect while the recorder is also down, and a disconnect during an in-flight repair.
- **Property:** for any partition of a print sequence into "live" and "repaired" segments, the final cumulative value is invariant.
- **Coverage:** >=85%.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.
Additionally: an attacker-controlled or malfunctioning upstream that flaps continuously must not be able to drive unbounded recompute work â€” the coalescing queue and the print clamp are the specific controls, and E23-X02 tests them as an abuse case.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
Repair must meet US-CVD-002's NFR envelope (1M prints <= 2 s) as validated in E23-K01; repair runs off the ingestion hot path so it must not stall live accumulation for other symbols. During repair, the per-symbol CPU budget (#11) may be exceeded transiently; sustained exceedance is a defect.

## Observability
`cv_cvd_recompute_total{reason="ws_gap"|"reconnect"|"anchor_change"|"backfill"}`, `cv_cvd_recompute_seconds`, `cv_cvd_recompute_refused_total{reason}`, `cv_cvd_repair_queue_depth{symbol}`, `cv_cvd_gapped_bars_total{symbol}`. Structured log `cvd.recompute` with `symbol`, `from`, `to`, `prints`, `duration_ms`, `source="questdb"|"parquet"`. Trace span `orderflow.cvd.recompute` as a child of the resync span. An alert fires if `cv_cvd_recompute_refused_total` increases, because a refusal means a user is looking at a knowingly incomplete series.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§3.2/Â§4.2:
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via a PR <=400 LOC diff with 2 approvals incl. 1 `area/order-flow` code-owner
- [ ] Unit coverage >=85% (backend/engine) / >=80% (frontend) on the changed package; no coverage regression

body:
## Context
`xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` is adopted completely (ADR-0016 Accepted) for every catalogue lifecycle B1-B20, but per-tick rule/aggregation evaluation stays plain code: BENCH-2 measured 381 ev/s against the statechart runtime versus the 2,000 ev/s CVD/delta needs (`29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4d). `CvdEngine` and delta aggregation are explicitly excluded from the catalogue (§3), and this Chore makes that exclusion a checked invariant instead of a comment.

- A short BENCH-2 note added to the ADR-0017 draft (the CVD/footprint architecture ADR) recording the 381 ev/s vs 2,000 ev/s measurement as the permanent reason for the exclusion.

title: Hi-fi SCR-054 and design-system entries for CMP-186, CMP-126, CMP-127
body:
## Context
Turns the E24-D02 wireframes into signed-off hi-fi and contributes the three trading components this epic introduces or extends to the design system: CMP-186 OiFundingLiqPane (chart primitive), CMP-126 FundingCountdown (atom) and CMP-127 LiquidationMarker (chart primitive), plus the SCR-058 methodology section for the liquidation-cluster heuristic drafted in E24-K01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for every SCR-054 state from E24-D02 in both themes (dark default, light) and all three density modes.
- Design-system entries with token bindings: CMP-186 (`color.status.*`, per-sub-signal display modes), CMP-126 (`font.mono`, `color.text.buy/sell`, extends the CMP-035 Countdown pattern), CMP-127 (`color.status.danger`, DOM-mirror marker per CMP-197), and the reuse contract for CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.
- Colour + pattern specification for the four OI/price quadrants such that they are distinguishable in greyscale and under both common colour-vision deficiencies; the neutral hatch for a bar with no OI sample.
- Visual distinction between settled and predicted funding values that survives greyscale (US-DERIV-004 NFR: "never present predicted values styled as settled").
- The SCR-058 drawer section for the liquidation-zone heuristic: what it infers, from what inputs, the thresholds in force, the failure modes, and the sentence "this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact".
- Storybook story list per component (CMP-186: OiOnly, FundingOnly, LiquidationBars, Combined) handed to engineering.

## Out of scope
Motion (E24-D04), handoff pack (E24-D05), implementation, the non-liquidation sections of SCR-058 (E25).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Hi-fi covers both themes and all densities
  When the frame set is reviewed
  Then every state from E24-D02 exists in dark and light, and the compact/comfortable/spacious densities are specified

Scenario: Quadrants survive greyscale
  Given the four quadrant styles rendered in greyscale
  When they are compared
  Then each is distinguishable by pattern alone and each has a text legend entry

Scenario: Predicted is never styled as settled
  When a predicted funding value and a settled value are shown side by side in greyscale
  Then they are visually distinct and the predicted one carries a text label and an (estimated) badge

Scenario: Contrast
  When every text and graphical element is measured
  Then text is >=4.5:1 and graphical boundaries >=3:1 against their background in both themes

Scenario: A new atom is needed
  Given a frame requires an element that has no CMP-* entry
  Then a design-system contribution is raised and resolved before sign-off, and no one-off component ships
```

## Technical notes / design
Tokens come from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; nothing is hand-picked. CMP-186 is a chart primitive, so its spec must state what is drawn on the GPU surface and what is DOM chrome, matching the engine's pane model in `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`. CMP-127 is specified as a sparse-event marker with a DOM mirror, sharing the pattern with BigTradeBubble (CMP-112).

## Test plan
Contrast measured with the design-system plugin on every pair; greyscale and CVD simulation passes for the quadrant palette; the frame set is reviewed against the SCR-054 design sign-off checklist in the screens catalogue.

## Security notes
Misrepresentation is the threat: the visual language must make estimated and predicted values self-evidently non-authoritative without relying on colour or opacity alone (which fails for low-vision users and is therefore a security-relevant honesty control, not a style choice).

## Accessibility notes
Focus rings, hit targets >=24x24 CSS px, reduced-motion variants noted, table alternatives styled, and CMP-227's accessible name containing the literal word "estimated" restated in the component entry.

## Performance notes
The spec must not require per-print DOM nodes or per-frame text layout in the liquidation sub-pane; text rendering follows the engine's LOD rules so the panel stays inside 2 ms scripting per frame.

## Observability
N/A

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Hi-fi complete for all states, themes and densities.
- [ ] CMP-186/126/127 design-system entries merged into the library.
- [ ] SCR-058 liquidation-zone section written and reviewed with the E24-K01 author.
- [ ] Contrast + CVD checks recorded.
- [ ] CDO sign-off comment recorded; catalogue entry updated with the Figma link.

title: Motion spec and accessibility review for the derivatives panel
body:
## Context
SCR-054 has three moving things - a per-second countdown, low-frequency OI/funding updates and bursty liquidation prints - plus a pane whose data can go stale. Motion here is a legibility tool, not decoration: an unthrottled cascade animation is both a perf hazard and an a11y hazard. This ticket fixes the motion contract and runs the formal accessibility review of the hi-fi before handoff.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion spec: countdown tick (text swap, no animation), value-change flash on OI/funding (<=120 ms, `prefers-reduced-motion` removes it entirely), liquidation bucket entry animation capped at the 250 ms coalescing cadence, stale-data shading fade, pane collapse/expand easing and duration, zone-overlay fade on enable.
- Explicit rule: nothing animates faster than the data's own cadence; during a cascade the bucket animation is suppressed rather than queued.
- Accessibility review of the E24-D03 hi-fi: focus order across the three sub-panes and the settings surface, keyboard path to every control, live-region policy (countdown announced at 5 min and 1 min only - never per second, per the SCR-054 catalogue entry), announcement throttling for bursty liquidations, table-alternative column semantics and units, non-colour encoding of quadrant and side.
- An a11y annotation layer on the Figma frames that engineering can read directly (roles, names, live-region politeness, tab order numbers).

## Out of scope
Implementation; axe automation (E24-Q04 runs the audit on the built panel).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  Then every flash, fade and bucket animation is removed and only instantaneous state changes remain, with no loss of information

Scenario: Countdown announcements
  When a screen reader is on and the funding countdown is running
  Then it is announced at 5 minutes and at 1 minute remaining only, and never once per second

Scenario: Cascade announcements
  Given 500 liquidation prints per second
  Then announcements are throttled to at most one summary every 5 seconds naming the burst rate, not one per print

Scenario: Keyboard completeness
  When the panel is operated by keyboard only
  Then every control including the sub-pane collapse, the mode toggles, the threshold input and the zone acknowledgement is reachable with a visible focus indicator

Scenario: Annotation coverage
  When an engineer opens the hi-fi
  Then every interactive element carries a role, an accessible name and a tab-order number
```

## Technical notes / design
Durations and easings come from the motion tokens in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`. The live-region policy is specified as a concrete rule set (politeness, throttle window, message template) so E24-S03/S05 implement it verbatim rather than improvising.

## Test plan
Reviewed with a screen-reader specialist against the annotation layer; the throttle rules are handed to E24-Q04 as audit checkpoints.

## Security notes
N/A

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the accessibility review; outcome is a checklist consumed by E24-Q04 (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` WCAG 2.2 AA).

## Performance notes
Motion must not add per-frame work during a cascade; the suppression rule exists precisely so the panel keeps its 2 ms/frame scripting budget.

- [ ] A11y annotation layer complete on all hi-fi frames.

title: Spike: liquidation-zone estimation methodology and its honesty limits
body:
## Context
US-DERIV-007 asks for "estimated zones derived from OI, leverage tiers and price distance". Bybit publishes neither per-account leverage nor a liquidation-price distribution, so any zone is an inference over aggregate OI plus assumed leverage buckets. Before a line of engine code is written we must decide whether an honest version of this feature is possible at all, what inputs it uses, and exactly what it may and may not claim. The epic's cross-cutting caveat (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 rule 2 and US-DERIV-007's NFR) makes the wrong answer a correctness bug, not a tuning issue.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Evaluate 2-3 candidate methods over recorded symbol-days: (a) OI-weighted leverage-bucket projection - distribute current `open_interest` across assumed leverage tiers (10x/25x/50x/100x) and map each tier to a maintenance-margin distance from a reference price, using the instruments-info risk-limit tiers cached by E08; (b) realised-liquidation histogram - cluster the recorded `liquidations` table by price to show where forced flow has actually occurred (exact, not estimated); (c) a hybrid rendering (b) as the primary surface and (a) as an optional overlay.
- Backtest: for each method, measure how often a projected zone precedes an actual recorded liquidation cluster within N ticks and M minutes, on at least three symbol-days including one cascade.
- Decide the default: whether zones ship at all, and if so which method, which parameters, and which claims the SCR-058 copy may make.
- Measure the compute cost of the chosen method per bar-grid update so E24-S07 has a budget.
- Output: a written recommendation with the numbers, the parameter set, the failure modes, and the draft SCR-058 methodology text handed to E24-D03 and E24-S07.

## Out of scope
Production implementation (E24-S07); the exact-cluster grouping of `cluster_window_ms` on `/market/liquidations`, which is not an estimate and is implemented in E24-T03; any rule-engine consumption of zones (excluded by NFR).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Methods measured
  Given at least three recorded symbol-days including one cascade
  When each candidate method is evaluated
  Then a hit-rate and a false-positive rate is recorded per method with its parameters

Scenario: A recommendation with a default
  Then the spike recommends one method, or recommends shipping only the realised-liquidation histogram
  And states the default parameter values and confirms the feature is off by default

Scenario: Claims are bounded
  Then the spike produces the exact sentences SCR-058 may use, including the statement that Bybit publishes no per-account leverage or liquidation-price data

Scenario: No method is defensible
  Given every candidate performs no better than chance on the fixtures
  Then the recommendation is to ship only the exact realised-liquidation histogram, US-DERIV-007's estimated overlay is descoped with a recorded disposition, and E24-S07 is re-scoped rather than built on a method we cannot defend

Scenario: Cost is known
  Then the per-update compute cost of the chosen method is recorded in milliseconds against the bar-grid update rate
```

## Technical notes / design
Analysis runs offline in DuckDB over the Parquet cold tier plus the QuestDB `open_interest`, `liquidations` and `tickers` tables - no production code path. Where a risk-limit tier is unavailable the method must degrade explicitly rather than assume a value. The report must state, for each input, whether it is exchange-published or assumed. Time-box: 3 days.

## Test plan
Reproducible notebook/script committed under `research/` with the fixture ids; another engineer must be able to re-run it and obtain the same numbers.

## Security notes
This spike is the epic's principal integrity control: it decides whether we publish an inference at all. Findings feed E24-X02's abuse cases ("can a user be led to trade on a number we invented?"). No credentials or account data are touched - public market data only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. The wording it produces is, however, the source of the accessible description for CMP-227 on the zones overlay.

## Performance notes
Records the compute cost per update so E24-S07 can be budgeted against the SCR-054 2 ms/frame scripting limit.

## Observability
Recommends the metric names the eventual implementation should emit (zone recompute duration, zone count) so observability is designed in.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All candidate methods evaluated on >=3 symbol-days.
- [ ] Written recommendation with numbers, parameters and failure modes.
- [ ] Draft SCR-058 text delivered to E24-D03.
- [ ] Compute budget recorded and handed to E24-S07.
- [ ] Architect review comment recorded; time-box respected.

## Dependencies
`E24-X01` (the STRIDE model frames the misrepresentation threat this spike must answer). Feeds `E24-D03` and `E24-S07`.
