title: Open-interest ingest, REST backfill and /market/open-interest endpoint
body:
## Context
The OI pane (US-DERIV-001, Must) needs two things the platform does not yet have: a continuously extended high-resolution OI series derived from the recorded `tickers` stream, and a REST backfill of the exchange's own 5min..1d OI history. Both land in the QuestDB `open_interest` table (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.7) whose dedup key is `(ts, symbol, interval, source)` precisely so the two cadences can coexist without one overwriting the other. This task is backend only; the pane is E24-S01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Ingest path (M4):** extract `open_interest` / `open_interest_value` from the merged ticker snapshot produced by E08 and write `interval='1s'`, `source='ws_ticker'` rows to `open_interest`, downsampled to at most 1 row/second/symbol.
- **Backfill job (M4):** page Bybit `GET /v5/market/open-interest` (limit <=200/page, cursor paging) for the intervals `5min|15min|30min|1h|4h|1d`, writing `source='rest'` rows. Idempotent: re-running over a covered range produces no duplicates thanks to the dedup key.
- Backfill is triggered on first subscription to a symbol's OI and on demand for a requested range; concurrency limited per symbol; retries with exponential backoff and jitter; honours the shared Bybit rate-limit budget and error code 10018.
- **Endpoint:** implement `GET /api/v1/market/open-interest` exactly per `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`symbol`, `interval` default `5min`, `from`, `to`, `cursor`, `limit`; `x-rbac` `marketdata:read`), returning `{t, open_interest, open_interest_value}` items plus the standard `Page` meta with `next_cursor`, `has_more`, `count`.
- The response must disclose which source each point came from and the coverage window, so the client can render the "native granularity 5 min" note and never silently mix cadences.
- Range and limit caps per the E24-X01 model, rejecting oversized requests with 422.

## Out of scope
The pane and its rendering (E24-S01); OI delta and quadrant computation (E24-T04/E24-S02); funding (E24-T02); liquidations (E24-T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live extension
  Given a subscribed symbol whose ticker stream is flowing
  Then open_interest rows with interval='1s' and source='ws_ticker' are written at no more than one row per second per symbol

Scenario: Backfill paging
  Given a requested range covering more than 200 points at 5min granularity
  When the backfill runs
  Then it pages with the cursor until complete, writes source='rest' rows, and a second run over the same range writes no duplicate rows

Scenario: Backfill failure does not stop live data
  Given the Bybit REST call returns 5xx or rate-limit code 10018
  Then the job retries with backoff, the failure is logged with symbol, interval, attempt and http_status, live ws_ticker rows keep being written, and the endpoint reports the gap in its coverage meta rather than fabricating points

Scenario: Endpoint contract
  When GET /api/v1/market/open-interest?symbol=BTCUSDT&interval=5min&from=..&to=.. is called with a marketdata:read token
  Then the response validates against the OpenAPI schema, points are ascending by t, and the meta reports next_cursor, has_more and count

Scenario: Oversized request
  When a range or limit beyond the documented cap is requested
  Then the endpoint returns 422 with the standard error envelope and issues no query against QuestDB

Scenario: Unauthorised
  When the endpoint is called without a token or without marketdata:read
  Then it returns 401 or 403 respectively
```

## Technical notes / design
Backfill is a supervised asyncio task per (symbol, interval) with a bounded work queue, reusing the exchange-adapter's `fetch_open_interest(symbol, interval, ...)` method declared in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`. Writes go through the existing QuestDB ILP writer used by the recorder; the dedup key makes at-least-once delivery safe. Query side uses a parameterised SQL selection on `(symbol, interval, source)` with `ts` bounds - never string interpolation. Coverage meta is computed from `min(ts)`/`max(ts)` for the requested `(symbol, interval)` so the client can distinguish 'no data recorded' from 'zero OI'.

## Test plan
Unit: downsampler (1 Hz cap, monotonic ts), cursor paging loop, backoff schedule, idempotent re-run, coverage-meta computation. Contract: schema test for the endpoint against `22-api-openapi.yaml` incl. the 401/403/422 responses. Integration: recorded Bybit fixtures for a normal session, a paged backfill >200 rows, a 5xx sequence and a 10018 rate-limit sequence. Coverage >=85% on the new modules.

## Security notes
Threats from E24-X01: (D) unbounded range/limit - mitigated by the caps tested above; (T) source confusion - mitigated by persisting and returning `source` per point; (I) endpoint must keep `marketdata:read`. Public market data only; no secrets. Upstream frames are schema-validated before write so a malformed push cannot poison the table.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend only.

## Performance notes
Endpoint p95 <150 ms backend-internal (budget #13) for a 1 000-point page; ingest adds <1 ms per ticker frame; backfill runs off the hot path and must not delay live writes. Record both numbers in the ticket.

## Observability
Metrics `deriv_oi_backfill_pages_total{symbol,interval,result}`, `deriv_oi_backfill_latency_seconds`, `deriv_oi_rows_written_total{source}`. Structured warning log on backfill failure with `symbol`, `interval`, `attempt`, `http_status`. One trace span per backfill job.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` behind review (2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner), conventional commits, PR <=400 LOC diff.
- [ ] Unit tests added; coverage >=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend on touched files.

title: Funding-rate service, interval resolution and /market/funding endpoint
body:
## Context
US-DERIV-003 (Must) and US-DERIV-004 (Should) hinge on one rule stated verbatim in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: "The funding interval is instrument-specific (`funding_interval_minutes`; 8 h common, some 1/2/4 h) - never assume 8 h." The interval drives the countdown, the annualisation factor and the `funding_8h` session anchor. This task makes the interval a resolved input everywhere and ships the settled-history plus predicted-rate service.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Interval resolution:** read `funding_interval_minutes` from the instruments-info cache (`GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`, Postgres `instruments.funding_interval_min`, column default 480) and expose a single accessor used by every consumer. A static analysis / grep check in CI asserts no other hard-coded 480 or 8-hour constant exists in the derivatives code.
- **Settled history:** backfill Bybit `GET /v5/market/funding/history` (limit <=200, cursor paging) into QuestDB `funding_rates` (`ts`, `symbol`, `funding_rate`, `annualised_pct`, `interval_min`, `source`), computing `annualised_pct = funding_rate * (525600 / interval_min) * 100` at write time.
- **Predicted rate:** the current unsettled rate is available only from the ticker `funding_rate` field; expose it flagged `predicted: true, estimated: true` and never persist it as a settled row. When absent, the API returns no predicted item at all so the client can show `n/a` rather than a stale value (US-DERIV-004 scenario 3).
- **Next settlement:** `next_funding_time_ms` from the ticker, served alongside so the client countdown needs no local schedule arithmetic beyond the clock offset.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/market/funding` per the OpenAPI contract, returning `funding_interval_minutes` at the top level and items `{t, funding_rate, predicted, estimated}` with `Page` meta; `x-rbac` `marketdata:read`; range/limit caps.

## Out of scope
The funding UI, the countdown widget and the annualisation toggle (E24-S03/E24-S04); metric-descriptor registration (E24-T04); funding cost against real positions (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Interval comes from instrument data
  Given a symbol whose instruments-info funding_interval_minutes is 240
  When the funding history and the predicted rate are served
  Then funding_interval_minutes is 240 in the response and annualised_pct uses 525600/240, not 525600/480

Scenario: No hard-coded interval
  When the CI guard scans the derivatives backend modules
  Then no literal 480 or 8-hour funding constant exists outside the instruments table column default, and a violation fails the build

Scenario: Predicted is distinct and never persisted
  Then the current unsettled rate is returned with predicted=true and estimated=true
  And no row with predicted=true is written to funding_rates

Scenario: Predicted unavailable
  Given the ticker publishes no funding rate for the symbol
  Then the response contains no predicted item and the client can render n/a rather than a stale value

Scenario: History paging
  Given a range spanning more than 200 settlements
  Then the service pages with the cursor to completion and a re-run writes no duplicates

Scenario: Contract and authorisation
  Then the response validates against 22-api-openapi.yaml, and a caller without marketdata:read receives 403
```

## Technical notes / design
`annualised_pct` is precomputed at write time so queries stay cheap and so there is exactly one implementation of the formula. Settlement timestamps are stored as the exchange's settlement time; the dedup key `(ts, symbol)` makes the backfill idempotent. The interval accessor returns the instrument value or raises if the instrument is unknown - it must not silently fall back to a default at runtime, because a wrong interval produces a wrong countdown and a wrong annualisation simultaneously.

## Test plan
Unit: annualisation across 1 h/2 h/4 h/8 h intervals; the interval accessor's raise-on-unknown behaviour; predicted-rate flagging; paging and idempotence. Contract: OpenAPI schema test incl. `funding_interval_minutes` presence and the 403 case. Integration: recorded fixtures for an 8 h symbol and a 4 h symbol, plus a settlement boundary crossing. CI guard test for the constant scan. Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
(T) presenting a predicted rate as settled is the epic's top misrepresentation threat; mitigated at the schema level (`predicted`/`estimated` are required in the response shape, not optional decoration) and asserted in E24-X02's flag-stripping abuse case. (D) range/limit caps as per E24-X01. Public data only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend only.

## Performance notes
Endpoint p95 <150 ms backend-internal (budget #13). Funding data is low-cardinality; the whole visible history of a symbol fits comfortably in one page at most chart ranges.

## Observability
Metrics `deriv_funding_refresh_total{symbol,result}`, `deriv_funding_backfill_pages_total`, `deriv_funding_interval_minutes{symbol}` (gauge, so a wrong interval is visible in Grafana). Warning log when a symbol's interval is missing from the instruments cache.

title: Liquidation socket, persistence and /market/liquidations endpoint
body:
## Context
US-DERIV-005 (Must) needs forced-flow prints in real time, and US-DERIV-006 (Must) needs them bucketed per bar. Bybit's `allLiquidation.{symbol}` topic is the only source (the legacy `liquidation` topic is retired) and **there is no REST history endpoint at all** - `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.6 states depth is strictly bounded by recorder uptime and the UI must say so. This task owns the socket, the persistence, the WS republication and the local-history endpoint, including the coverage metadata that makes the partial-history state possible.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Socket (M4):** subscribe `allLiquidation.{symbol}` through the public-stream connection manager from E08 for every recorded or auto-recorded symbol; normalise to the domain event and write to QuestDB `liquidations` (`ts`, `recv_ts`, `symbol`, `side`, `price`, `size`, `notional`, `stream='all'`) with dedup key `(ts, symbol, side, price, size)`.
- **WS republication:** publish `liquidations.{symbol}` and the multi-symbol `liquidations` topic per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §14.9 `LiquidationBatch`, honouring the 500 ms throttle, the **append-never-merge** delivery rule for this topic, and the options `min_notional_usd` and `cluster_window_ms`. The `note` field stating that Bybit batches at most one push per symbol per 500 ms (so counts are lower bounds) is always populated.
- **Exact clustering:** `cluster_window_ms` groups prints within a time window into one item with `cluster_size` - this is exact grouping, not an estimate, and must never carry an `estimated` flag.
- **Endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/market/liquidations` per the OpenAPI contract (`symbol`, `from`, `to`, `cursor`, `limit`, `side`, `min_notional_usd`, `cluster_window_ms` 0..60000), reading only the local table.
- **Coverage metadata:** every response reports the recorder's first available timestamp for the symbol so the client can render the partial-history chip and the boundary marker (US-DERIV-006 scenario 3), and a query for a window entirely before that timestamp reports the coverage window rather than returning an innocent empty list.
- Recorder policy: `stream_kind` value `liquidations` registered so retention and the recorded-symbol list cover it (E16).

## Out of scope
The feed and bars UI (E24-S05/E24-S06); the estimated zone overlay (E24-K01/E24-S07); alerts on liquidations (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Prints persist and republish
  Given the allLiquidation topic is flowing for BTCUSDT
  Then each print is written to the liquidations table and republished on liquidations.BTCUSDT within the 500 ms throttle
  And the payload validates against the LiquidationBatch schema with the lower-bound note populated

Scenario: Append never merge
  Given three prints arrive inside one throttle window
  Then all three are delivered in the batch array and none is coalesced away

Scenario: Exact clustering
  Given cluster_window_ms=1000 and five prints inside one second
  Then they are returned as one item with cluster_size=5 and no estimated flag anywhere in the payload

Scenario: Coverage is stated
  Given the recorder for BTCUSDT started 2 hours ago
  When a 24-hour range is requested
  Then the response returns only the recorded window and reports the first available timestamp in its meta

Scenario: Query entirely outside coverage
  Given a range that ends before the recorder's first record
  Then the response reports the coverage window and an explicit no-coverage indication, not a bare empty success that would read as zero liquidations

Scenario: Cascade burst
  Given 500 prints per second for 10 seconds
  Then no print is lost between socket and table, the WS fan-out stays inside the throttle, and ingest lag stays under 1 second

Scenario: Reconnect
  Given the public socket drops mid-cascade
  Then it resubscribes automatically, the gap is logged, and duplicate prints replayed by the exchange are absorbed by the dedup key
```

## Technical notes / design
Normalisation maps the Bybit payload to the domain event defined in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`; `notional` is computed at ingest (price*size) so both the endpoint and the engine read one number. `side` is the side of the liquidated position's closing order, documented in the endpoint description - keep the field comment in code to stop it being re-interpreted. Writes use the recorder's ILP path with backpressure; a bounded queue drops nothing but applies backpressure to the socket reader rather than growing without limit. Multi-symbol `liquidations` subscriptions are capped at the protocol's symbol limit.

## Test plan
Unit: normaliser, notional computation, clustering by window, coverage-meta computation, dedup behaviour on replayed prints. Contract: `LiquidationBatch` JSON-schema validation and the REST schema test incl. 422 for `cluster_window_ms` > 60000. Integration: recorded fixtures - normal session, a cascade burst, a socket drop with replay, a symbol with no coverage. Perf: the 500 prints/s for 10 s ingest soak (also exercised end-to-end in E24-Q03). Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
(D) cascade-driven fan-out amplification - mitigated by the 500 ms throttle, the batch shape and the subscription symbol cap; (D) unbounded history queries - range/limit caps; (T) an empty result being read as 'no liquidations happened' - mitigated by the explicit coverage metadata, which E24-X02 tests as an abuse case; (S) malformed upstream frames rejected by schema validation before write. Public market data only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend only, but the coverage metadata is what makes the accessible partial-history disclosure possible downstream.

## Performance notes
Ingest lag <1 s under 500 prints/s; WS tick->screen p95 <100 ms with this topic in the heaviest set (budget #3, hard R2 gate); endpoint p95 <150 ms per page (budget #13).

## Observability
Metrics `deriv_liquidation_prints_total{symbol,side}`, `deriv_liquidation_notional_total{symbol,side}`, `deriv_liquidation_burst_rate{symbol}`, `deriv_liquidation_ingest_lag_seconds`, `deriv_liquidation_socket_reconnects_total`. Warning log on socket drop with the gap duration.

## Definition of Done

title: Detectors: tape speed, imbalance, regime, iceberg/stop-run (estimated)
body:
## Context
R2 "Order-flow beta" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 6, sprints S10-S13, version `0.3.0`, staging/demo) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility. **E25 Detectors** is the *interpretation* layer of that release: it turns the raw tape and the reconstructed L2 book into a small number of named, tunable, explainable signals - speed of tape, book speed, imbalance stacks, absorption, iceberg, stop-run and market regime.

Roadmap scope line (section 6.2): "Speed-of-tape (trades/sec, volume/sec, with baseline z-score); imbalance tracker with stacked-imbalance runs; market-regime classifier (trend / balance / volatile) from range, volume and delta features; **iceberg detector (estimated)** - repeated refills at a price level beyond visible depth; **stop-run detector (estimated)** - sweep beyond a swing level followed by rapid reversion; every detector exposes its inputs and thresholds in an inspector so the user can see *why* it fired" - **34 pts, S12-S13**, area `area/order-flow`, backend module **M9** (`server/orderflow/`), story domain **DET** (9 stories: 6 Must, 3 Should).

Two invariants govern the whole epic:

1. **Honesty (R2 exit criterion #4).** Bybit publishes no L3/MBO data. Iceberg, stop-run, absorption and regime are inferences over anonymous aggregated public data. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` states: `confidence="estimated"` is mandatory for every heuristic, and "presenting a heuristic as a certainty is a defect". Every surface in this epic therefore carries CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linked to SCR-058, the methodology drawer. A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic.
2. **Single-source evaluation (R2 exit criteria #1 and #7).** Detectors are computed once, backend-side, in M9, published on the single WS topic `metrics.{symbol}` (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`: "Derived order-flow series share one topic ... They are one engine output family and one subscription, not five"), persisted to QuestDB `orderflow_metrics`, and consumed identically by the panels, the alert engine, the rule DSL (E35) and the journal. A second client-side implementation of any threshold is an explicit anti-goal. Detector outputs must be reproducible: replaying the same recorded window twice yields identical events (exit criterion #7).

## Goal
Ship every DET user story that belongs to R2, backend-first, so that a trader can see *what* the market is doing (speed, imbalance, regime) and *why the terminal thinks so* (inputs, thresholds, failure modes), with every heuristic honestly labelled and every threshold auditable - because detector output can feed armed rules that place real orders.

## Scope / Deliverables
User stories: **US-DET-001** Speed of tape (Must), **US-DET-002** Tape acceleration and threshold alerts (Should), **US-DET-003** Book speed (Should), **US-DET-004** Imbalance tracker panel (Must), **US-DET-005** Absorption detector (Must), **US-DET-006** Iceberg / hidden-order detector (Should), **US-DET-007** Stop-run / liquidity sweep detector (Must), **US-DET-008** Market regime classifier (Must), **US-DET-009** Detector configuration and audit of estimates (Must).

Screens: **SCR-055** Speed-of-tape panel; **SCR-056** Imbalance tracker panel; **SCR-057** Market regime panel; **SCR-058** Detector methodology drawer ("Why estimated?"); **SCR-059** Detector settings dialog. (SCR-104 Scanner consumes the `trades_per_sec` metric but is owned by E17.)

Components: CMP-131 SpeedOfTapeGauge, CMP-187 SpeedOfTapePane, CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator, CMP-133 RegimeIndicatorChip, CMP-134 DetectorEventCard, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-032 Rating/Confidence Dots, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-049 Table, CMP-011 Tag/Chip, CMP-021 Link, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-010 Slider, CMP-028 Callout/Banner, CMP-026 EmptyState.

Backend (module M9, `server/orderflow/`): `MetricsEngine` (rolling tape/book statistics and z-scores), `DetectorRegistry` + `DetectorEvent` bus, `AbsorptionDetector`, `IcebergDetector`, `StopRunDetector`, `ImbalanceStackTracker`, `RegimeClassifier`.
API: `GET /api/v1/market/metrics`, `GET|PUT /api/v1/detectors/config`, `GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology`, `GET /api/v1/market/regime/explain`.
WS: `metrics.{symbol}` with `metrics[]` selecting `trades_per_sec`, `volume_per_sec`, `book_updates_per_sec`, `tape_acceleration`, `imbalance_ratio`, `absorption`, `iceberg`, `stop_run`, `adx`, `atr`, `hurst`, `regime`.
DB: QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` (`trades_per_sec`, `notional_per_sec`, `book_imbalance`, `book_thickness`, `realized_vol_1m`, `atr_14`, `regime`, `regime_confidence`, `stacked_imbalance_up`, `stacked_imbalance_down`, `iceberg_score`, `stoprun_score`, `absorption_score`); Postgres detector-config rows (global plus per-symbol override) and the append-only audit log.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell aggregation and the imbalance *ratio* computation itself (E18 - this epic consumes footprint imbalance flags and only tracks *stacks* over time).
- DOM ladder, heatmap and L2 book reconstruction (E21 - consumed as an input).
- CVD/delta series (E23 - consumed as a regime sub-signal).
- Big-trade thresholds and bubbles (E22).
- Alert delivery, cooldown scheduling and the alert centre (ALRT domain - this epic only emits detector events onto the shared event bus; US-DET-002's alert UI lives there).
- Rule DSL vocabulary binding and evaluation (E35) - this epic guarantees the metric codes exist and are documented.
- Replay clock and scrubbing (E26 owns the clock; this epic must simply be clock-agnostic).
- Scanner/screener columns (E17) and journal auto-tagging.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One family, one subscription
  Given a client subscribes to metrics.BTCUSDT with metrics ["trades_per_sec","regime","iceberg","stop_run"]
  Then all four series arrive on that single subscription
  And no separate tapespeed, regime or detector topic exists

Scenario: Honesty gate
  Given any detector-derived value is rendered anywhere in the app
  Then it carries the (estimated) badge wherever the metric vocabulary marks the metric estimated
  And activating the badge opens SCR-058 at that detector's section

Scenario: Determinism
  Given the same recorded window is replayed twice
  Then the emitted detector event streams are identical

Scenario: Missing dependency
  Given a symbol has no recorded L2 history
  Then the iceberg and stop-run detectors are shown disabled, naming the missing dependency, with a one-click start-recording action

Scenario: Auditability
  When a detector threshold is changed
  Then an append-only audit record is written with detector, key, before, after and actor
```

## Exit criteria
1. All nine DET stories accepted; every Must story demonstrable on a recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day and live on demo.
2. Every estimated surface carries CMP-227 with a working link to SCR-058, and SCR-058 contains a section per estimated signal stating what it infers, from what data, with which thresholds in force, and its known false-positive modes (R2 exit criterion #4).
3. Determinism: replaying an identical recorded window twice produces identical detector event streams (R2 exit criterion #7), enforced by a CI golden-fixture test.
4. Detectors are computed only backend-side; no threshold logic exists in the web client (review plus a lint rule on the panels package).
5. `metrics.{symbol}` carries the whole family in one subscription; WS tick to screen p95 <100 ms holds with the detector metric set added (budget #3, hard R2 gate).
6. Every detector threshold change is audited, and the settings dialog warns when armed rules depend on the detector being changed.
7. Detectors degrade explicitly on missing dependencies, never to a silent zero.
8. a11y pass on SCR-055..059 (WCAG 2.2 AA): text-first values, no colour-only encodings, keyboard-navigable event lists.
9. Coverage floors held (backend/engine >=85 %, frontend >=80 %); zero open P0/P1; QA sign-off; design sign-off on all five screens.

## Story list
| Key | Kind | Title | Pts | Sprint |

| E25-K01 | Spike | Calibrate detector heuristics against recorded fixtures | 2 | 11 |
| E25-T01 | Task | MetricsEngine rolling tape and book statistics | 5 | 12 |

| E25-X01..X02 | Task | Security track (STRIDE, security review) | 4 | 10, 13 |

## Risks
| Risk | Why | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| R7 Data accuracy | Iceberg/stop-run/absorption are inferences over L2-only data; a false positive that feeds an armed rule can place a real order | Mandatory (estimated) badge plus SCR-058; detectors behind feature flags `metrics.iceberg_detector` / `.stop_run_detector` / `.absorption` until K01's calibration lands; explicit acknowledgement required before a detector may be the sole trigger of an armed live action (US-DET-006 NFR) |
| R9 Advice boundary | A "regime" badge reads like a recommendation | Regime is stated as a classification with numeric confidence and its sub-signals, never phrased as an action |
| R3 Real-time cost | Adding ~12 metric codes to `metrics.{symbol}` at 4 Hz for N symbols | One topic, server-side throttle (250 ms default), 1 Hz for regime; budget #3 re-measured in E25-Q03 |
| R2 Render performance | Panels rendering at tape rate | All rolling statistics computed backend-side; panels render <=4 Hz within a 1-1.5 ms budget (SCR-055/056 performance sections) |
| R6 Feed rot | Detector inputs depend on `orderbook.200` depth tiers; a tier change renormalises book speed | US-DET-003 requires the renormalisation to be annotated on the series |

## Technical notes / design
Engines live in `server/orderflow/` beside footprint, profile, cvd, imbalance, heatmap and tape. One `DetectorRegistry` holds `Detector` implementations with a uniform interface (`on_trade`, `on_book_delta`, `on_bar_close`, `emit(DetectorEvent)`), so replay (E26) and live share one code path with only the clock differing. Config defaults are exactly those published in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` schema `DetectorConfig` (iceberg `min_reloads=3`, `price_tolerance_ticks=0`, `window_ms=5000`; stop_run `lookback_bars=20`, `penetration_ticks=2`, `reversal_pct=60`; absorption `min_volume_multiple=3`, `max_price_move_ticks=1`).

## Test plan
See E25-Q01..Q05 plus each child ticket's own plan. Epic-level gates: golden-fixture determinism test, budget #3 re-measurement with the detector metric set, axe-core clean on SCR-055..059, coverage >=85 % backend / >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 5 STRIDE, performed per R2 epic in E25-X01. Key concerns: **Tampering** with detector thresholds (they feed armed rules, so `settings:write` plus audit), **Repudiation** (audit `detector.threshold_changed`), **Denial of service** via expensive recompute over long recorded ranges, **Information disclosure** (market data is public but the subscription is still session-gated by `marketdata:read`). Data classification: public market data plus per-user configuration (internal).

## Accessibility notes
All five screens are text-first: gauge readouts as sentences ("42 trades/s, 3.1 sigma above the 1-hour mean"), numeric confidence values, event lists as real tables, no colour-only encoding, polite live-region announcements rate-limited to at most one per 5 s. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Performance notes

Downstream: `E25 --> E35` (rule DSL vocabulary).

How to pick the next ticket in this epic when multiple agents are working it in parallel:

1. **Design track first** (E25-D01, E25-D02, E25-D03, E25-D04, E25-D05, E25-D06, E25-D07, E25-D08) must clear the design-ahead rule (Done ≥2 sprints before the Story that consumes it) before any Story in its lane starts — check each Story's own `blocked_by` for the exact design ticket.

title: Wireframe SCR-055..059 detector surfaces with all documented states
body:
## Context
Low-fidelity structure for the five screens this epic introduces, resolving layout and information hierarchy before visual design. The screens catalogue already fixes each screen's type, data source, components and states; the wireframes must honour those contracts rather than reinvent them:

- **SCR-055** Speed-of-tape panel - gauge + strip, states calm / elevated / extreme / insufficient sample.
- **SCR-056** Imbalance tracker panel - list + chart markers, states streaming / empty / recomputing / stale.
- **SCR-057** Market regime panel - badge + sub-signals + transition strip, states classified / low confidence / insufficient data.
- **SCR-058** Detector methodology drawer - one section per estimated signal.
- **SCR-059** Detector settings dialog - per-detector fieldsets, presets, backtest preview, dependency states.

Sprint 11, two sprints ahead of the consuming stories in Sprint 13.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes in Figma for all five screens, each state drawn as a separate frame (no "and also there is an empty state" annotations).
- Panel placement and docking within the workspace (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md`, `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` layout table which already places SCR-057 Regime and SCR-056 in the order-flow column).
- Information hierarchy decisions taken from D01: the default tape window, list-vs-chart primacy on SCR-056, and where the `(estimated)` badge sits relative to the value it qualifies.
- The cross-surface flow: any `(estimated)` badge -> SCR-058 at the right section -> link to SCR-059; and SCR-056 row -> chart zone highlight -> originating footprint cell.
- Density study: each panel drawn at the product's supported densities so the Sprint-13 build does not discover it does not fit.
- Annotated data bindings per frame (which WS topic / endpoint feeds which element) so hi-fi and engineering read the same source.
- Review with the M9 engineer and the chart-engine lead to confirm feasibility before hi-fi starts.

## Out of scope
Visual design, tokens and motion (D03/D04/D05), copywriting of the methodology content (E25-T07), prototyping interactions in code, redesigning SCR-032 footprint settings (E18).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every documented state is drawn
  Given the states listed for SCR-055, SCR-056, SCR-057, SCR-058 and SCR-059 in the screens catalogue
  Then each state has its own wireframe frame, including insufficient sample, recomputing, stale, disconnected and disabled-missing-dependency

Scenario: The estimated flow is drawn end to end
  Then the wireframes show activating an (estimated) badge on each of SCR-055, SCR-056 and SCR-057 opening SCR-058 at the correct section, and SCR-058 linking to SCR-059

Scenario: Research findings are applied
  Then each D01 implication assigned to this ticket is addressed, or its non-adoption is justified in writing on the frame

Scenario: Feasibility confirmed
  Then the M9 engineer and the chart-engine lead have reviewed the frames and no element depends on data the backend does not publish

Scenario: Density
  Then each panel is drawn at every supported density with no truncation or overflow
```

## Technical notes / design
Wireframes must use real data shapes: the fields available on `MetricSeries` / `MetricPoint.meta`, `RegimeExplanation.signals[]` (name, value, weight, contribution, direction) and `DetectorConfig`'s actual parameter names. Drawing a field the API does not have is the most common way a design becomes unbuildable, and the contracts here are already frozen in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.

Where a panel needs a value that does not exist, raise it against E25-T01/T02/T05 in this sprint rather than assuming it can be added in Sprint 13.

## Test plan
N/A (design). Review gate: engineering feasibility review recorded on the ticket.

## Security notes
Wireframes must not depict real account identifiers or balances. SCR-059's armed-rule warning must be drawn - omitting it would design out a required security control.

## Accessibility notes
Wireframes establish focus order, the table-first structure of SCR-056, and the text-first structure of SCR-055/057. Every state that communicates something must have a text carrier drawn, never a colour swatch alone. These are checked in D06.

## Performance notes
Frames must respect the published render budgets: SCR-055 <=4 Hz, SCR-056 <=4 Hz with a bounded 2 000-event list, SCR-057 renders only on change. A wireframe implying a continuously animating element at tape rate is a budget violation and must be flagged.

## Observability
Annotate on each frame the analytics events it triggers (`tapespeed.*`, `imbalance.*`, `regime.*`, `detector.*`, `methodology.opened`) so instrumentation is designed, not retrofitted.

## Definition of Done
All five screens wireframed with every documented state; annotated data bindings present; D01 implications addressed; engineering feasibility review recorded; reviewed and approved by the design lead; Figma file linked from this ticket and from the screens catalogue entries.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-D01 (findings drive the hierarchy decisions). Blocks D03 and D04.

## Branch
`design/detectors-wireframes`. PR size guidance: Figma links plus exported PNGs in `docs/design/e25/`.

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` - SCR-055, SCR-056, SCR-057, SCR-058, SCR-059

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**

2. docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md (DoR/DoD you must satisfy)

- Tests alongside the above per AGENTS.md conventions for `web`.

**Commands**

**Branch & PR**

**Done means**

**Do NOT**

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the specific blocker key (blocked_by: E25-D01), move Status to Blocked, and never silently work around a failing lint/test/perf gate — escalate to the Architect if the gate itself looks wrong.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Hi-fi design: speed-of-tape, imbalance and regime panels (SCR-055..057)
body:
## Context
High-fidelity design for the three live panels. Each screens-catalogue entry ends with a **design sign-off acceptance checklist** that is the literal definition of done for this ticket:

**SCR-055**: trades/sec and notional/sec both shown with units; rolling window selector; z-score/threshold band drawn **with a non-colour encoding**; spike state and its cooldown drawn; quiet-market empty state; "create alert from this threshold" affordance.

**SCR-056**: event list + chart markers drawn and cross-highlighted; threshold and stacked-count controls with live effect; **side encoded by text as well as colour**; link from an event to the originating footprint cell; empty state ("no imbalances above 3:1 in this range"); stale-data shading.

**SCR-057**: current regime label with the mandatory *(estimated)* chip; **confidence expressed as a number plus words, never a bare colour**; sub-signal breakdown (trend strength, volatility, volume profile shape, tape speed, OI trend) each with its own value; regime-change history strip; "why this classification?" link to SCR-058; insufficient-history state.

Sprint 11, two sprints ahead of the Sprint-13 build.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for SCR-055, SCR-056 and SCR-057 in every documented state, on the design-system tokens (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`) in both themes and at all supported densities.
- CMP-131 SpeedOfTapeGauge, CMP-187 SpeedOfTapePane, CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator, CMP-133 RegimeIndicatorChip specified to component-catalogue level (props, states, tokens) and contributed back through D05.
- Non-colour encodings for every signal-bearing element: threshold bands (pattern/weight), imbalance side (text + glyph), regime confidence (number + word).
- Motion specification: what animates, how long, and what does not animate at all - given the 4 Hz update cadence, most of these panels must not animate on value change.
- Empty, warming-up, stale, disconnected and insufficient-data states drawn with final copy.
- Redlines and token references for handoff (D07).

## Out of scope
SCR-058 and SCR-059 (D04), design-system primitives themselves (D05), a11y review (D06), implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Catalogue checklists satisfied
  Then every item on the SCR-055, SCR-056 and SCR-057 design sign-off acceptance checklists is demonstrably satisfied by a frame

Scenario: No colour-only meaning
  Given every element that carries meaning on these three panels
  Then each has a non-colour carrier, verified by rendering the frames in greyscale

Scenario: Estimated chip is mandatory on regime
  Then SCR-057 shows the (estimated) chip in every regime state, including insufficient data

Scenario: Confidence is a number
  Then confidence is drawn as a numeric value accompanied by a word, never as a colour or dots alone

Scenario: Motion respects the update cadence
  Then the motion spec states which elements do not animate, and no element animates on every 4 Hz update

Scenario: Both themes, all densities
  Then every frame exists in light and dark themes at each supported density with contrast checked
```

## Technical notes / design
Design against the published cadences: SCR-055 updates at 4 Hz, SCR-057 at most 1 Hz and renders only on change. A design that implies smooth interpolation between 4 Hz samples is asking engineering to violate the panel's 1 ms budget.

Use real value ranges when drawing: trades/sec in the hundreds during bursts, notional in the millions, confidence 0-1, ratios up to 2000 %. Frames drawn with tidy small numbers hide the truncation problems that appear in production.

The estimated chip on SCR-055 belongs to the **book-speed classification only** (US-DET-003), not to trades/sec and notional/sec, which are exact - misapplying the chip devalues it.

## Test plan
N/A (design). Verification: greyscale render check; contrast check against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large/graphical); density overflow check.

## Security notes
No real account data in frames. SCR-057 copy must contain no advisory or imperative phrasing (R9) - this is a design-time control, checked at sign-off.

## Accessibility notes
Contrast ratios verified for every token pairing used; focus states drawn for every interactive element; the text readout is drawn as a first-class element on SCR-055 (it is the primary accessible value, not a tooltip); SCR-056's table is drawn as the primary representation. Full review in D06.

## Performance notes
Frames must be buildable within SCR-055 <=1 ms, SCR-056 <=1.5 ms, SCR-057 <=1 ms render budgets - no per-update canvas effects, no large blur/shadow layers on streaming panels.

## Observability
Analytics touchpoints annotated per frame.

## Definition of Done
All three screens' catalogue sign-off checklists satisfied; greyscale and contrast checks passed; motion spec attached; component specs contributed to D05; reviewed and signed off by the design lead and the product owner; sign-off recorded on the ticket (status Done is the gate for the Sprint-13 stories).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-D02 (structure) and E25-D05 (the design-system parts these panels compose). Blocks D06, D07 and therefore S01, S02, S03.

## Branch
`design/detectors-hifi-panels`. PR size guidance: Figma links plus exports.

title: Hi-fi design: methodology drawer and detector settings (SCR-058, SCR-059)
body:
## Context
High-fidelity design for the two surfaces that carry the epic's honesty and safety obligations.

**SCR-058** sign-off checklist: one section per estimated signal (iceberg, stop-run, absorption, queue position, order-count footprint, regime, liquidity cluster); each section states what it infers, from what data, the exact heuristic and thresholds in force, the known failure modes, and what would be required to know it for certain; the words "this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact" appear in each section; link to the detector settings.

**SCR-059** sign-off checklist: every detector with its thresholds, look-back and minimum-confidence controls; **a warning listing armed rules that depend on the detector being changed**; reset-to-default per detector; *(estimated)* framing repeated; validation messages for out-of-range values.

SCR-059's audit note explains why its design is a safety matter: detector changes are audited "because detector output can feed armed rules that place orders".

Sprint 11, two sprints ahead of the Sprint-13 build.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for SCR-058 (drawer, one section per estimated signal, plus the degraded state where current thresholds cannot be fetched) and SCR-059 (dialog, per-detector fieldsets, presets, explicit thresholds, symbol scope, backtest preview, all validation and state variants).
- Final copy for all UI chrome, validation messages ("Enter a ratio between 100 and 2000 %"-style, matching the published bounds), the high-sensitivity warning, and the armed-rule warning - drafted with the content owner and aligned with E25-T07's methodology wording.
- The armed-rule warning designed as a blocking confirmation listing the affected rules, plus the fail-safe variant for when dependent rules cannot be enumerated.
- The apply state machine drawn: idle -> applying -> applied, and applying -> failed-with-restore; "applied" never appears before backend confirmation.
- Disabled-missing-dependency state with the exact missing dependency named and the one-click start-recording action.
- Per-symbol override indication.
- Reading-comprehension pass on SCR-058: plain-language summary first, technical detail second, glossary links for jargon.
- Redlines and token references for handoff (D07).

## Out of scope
SCR-055..057 (D03), authoring the methodology *content* itself (E25-T07 owns the substance; this ticket owns its presentation and the chrome copy), design-system primitives (D05), a11y review (D06), the rule-engine UI (E36/E37).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One section per estimated signal
  Then SCR-058 has a section for each of iceberg, stop-run, absorption, queue position, order-count footprint, regime and liquidity cluster
  And each contains the sentence that this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact

Scenario: Thresholds in force
  Then SCR-058 shows the thresholds currently in force, visually distinct from documented defaults

Scenario: Armed-rule warning
  Given a detector whose output is used by an armed rule
  Then SCR-059 is drawn with a blocking confirmation listing those rules before a change can be applied
  And a fail-safe variant is drawn for when the rule list cannot be fetched

Scenario: Never optimistic
  Then the apply state machine is drawn with applying and applied as distinct states, and applied is only reachable after backend confirmation
  And a failed apply is drawn restoring the previous values with the error shown

Scenario: Validation
  Then each numeric control is drawn with its unit, default and permitted range, and an out-of-range message naming the range

Scenario: Missing dependency
  Then a detector disabled for a missing dependency is drawn naming the exact dependency with a one-click start-recording action
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the real published bounds from `DetectorConfig` in every frame (iceberg min_reloads 2-50, window_ms 200-60000, stop_run lookback_bars 2-500, penetration_ticks 1-100, reversal_pct 0-100, absorption min_volume_multiple 1-50, max_price_move_ticks 0-50). Designing with invented ranges produces validation copy that has to be rewritten during the build.

SCR-058 is a reading surface, so typography and line length matter more than density here - deliberately break from the trading-dense defaults and specify the exception in the tokens.

## Test plan
N/A (design). Verification: copy reviewed by the content owner; every published bound represented; a designer walks the apply state machine against the SCR-059 performance contract.

## Security notes
The armed-rule warning and the non-optimistic apply are security controls in visual form; omitting or softening either in design would remove a control the threat model (E25-X01) relies on. Frames must show that a rejected change restores previous values rather than leaving an ambiguous state.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-058: plain-language first, proper heading hierarchy for screen-reader navigation, no jargon without a glossary link. SCR-059: per-detector fieldsets with legends, units and defaults visible, validation messages associated with their field, focus trap and restore drawn. Full review in D06.

## Performance notes
SCR-058 opens in <=150 ms with no streaming subscriptions - the design must not require live data to render. SCR-059's backtest preview is drawn with a progressive loading state so it never blocks the dialog.

## Observability
`methodology.opened{detector}` annotated on SCR-058; `detector.enabled_changed` / `detector.threshold_changed` annotated on SCR-059 with a note that these are audited server-side.

## Definition of Done
Both screens' catalogue sign-off checklists satisfied; copy reviewed by the content owner and aligned with T07; both themes and all densities; contrast checked; reviewed and signed off by the design lead, the product owner and a security reviewer (for the armed-rule warning); sign-off recorded (gate for E25-S04 and E25-S05).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-D02 and E25-D05. Blocks D06, D07 and therefore S04, S05.

## Branch
`design/detectors-hifi-drawer-settings`. PR size guidance: Figma links plus exports.

title: Accessibility design review of SCR-055..059 before handoff
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA as the product standard, and the R2 quality gates require "a11y pass on every new view". Reviewing accessibility *before* handoff is cheaper than auditing it after the build (E25-Q04 still audits the built product, but it should find little).

These five screens have specific hazards: two of them are value-streaming panels where colour is the natural encoding for direction and intensity; one is a classification badge where colour is the natural encoding for regime; and two are dense forms. The screens catalogue already prescribes the mitigations - text-first readouts, real tables, numeric confidence, text side encoding - and this review verifies the hi-fi designs actually deliver them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Structured review of every D03 and D04 frame against WCAG 2.2 AA and `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Colour-independence check: greyscale rendering of every frame; every meaning-bearing element must survive it.
- Contrast measurement for every token pairing in both themes, including the non-text 3:1 requirement for graphical objects (gauges, threshold bands, markers).
- Focus-order specification per screen, including the SCR-056 table row cursor, the SCR-059 dialog focus trap and restore, and the SCR-058 drawer's focus-to-section behaviour.
- Screen-reader narrative: what is announced, in what order, and what is suppressed - explicitly including SCR-055's "42 trades/s, 3.1 sigma above the 1-hour mean" readout, the 5-second announcement throttle, and SCR-056's "bid 340 vs ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1" ratio sentence.
- Target sizes and spacing checked against WCAG 2.2's target-size criterion for the dense settings dialog.
- Reduced-motion variants for anything the D03 motion spec animates.
- A findings list with each item either fixed in the frames before sign-off or raised as an accepted, documented exception.

## Out of scope
Automated axe-core testing of the built UI (E25-Q04), remediation of components outside this epic, the chart engine's DOM-mirror mechanism itself (E11; this review only confirms detector markers use it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Greyscale survival
  Given every hi-fi frame rendered in greyscale
  Then every element that carries meaning remains distinguishable

Scenario: Contrast
  Then every text pairing meets 4.5 to 1 (or 3 to 1 for large text) and every graphical object meets 3 to 1, in both themes, with measurements recorded

Scenario: Announcements specified
  Then each screen has a written screen-reader narrative, including what is deliberately not announced
  And SCR-055's throttle of at most one threshold announcement per five seconds is specified

Scenario: Focus
  Then focus order, visible focus appearance, dialog trap and restore, and drawer focus-to-section are specified for all five screens

Scenario: Findings resolved
  Then every finding is fixed in the frames or recorded as an approved exception with a rationale
  And no finding of severity high remains open at sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Review against the real announcement sentences rather than generic labels - the screens catalogue already wrote them, and a review that accepts "the gauge is announced" loses the specificity that makes the panel usable without sight.

Pay particular attention to SCR-056: its catalogue entry insists the canvas heat strip "is never the only representation". Confirm the table is drawn as primary and the canvas as supplementary, not the reverse.

## Test plan
N/A (design review). Deliverable is the findings list and the updated frames.

## Security notes
N/A. (Ensure the SCR-059 armed-rule confirmation remains operable by keyboard and screen reader - a security control that cannot be operated non-visually is not a control for every user.)

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility work. Standard: `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Performance notes
Reduced-motion variants must not introduce additional render work; the preferred implementation is to remove animation, not replace it.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
Review completed on all five screens; contrast and greyscale evidence attached; focus orders and screen-reader narratives written into the frames; all findings resolved or formally accepted; signed off by the accessibility lead; result is a precondition for D07 handoff.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-D03 and E25-D04. Blocks D07.

title: Replay engine & scrubbing
body:
## Context
Bybit publishes no historical L2 depth, no historical liquidation feed and only a ~1000-row recent-trade window. Every order-flow claim CandleViewer makes can therefore only be re-examined against **data the product recorded itself** (E16 recorder). E26 turns that recording into a deterministic, seekable time machine, and it is the third R2 goal in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §6.1: "ship deterministic replay so any order-flow claim can be re-examined tick-by-tick, and so R3's trading logic can be tested against reproducible market conditions".

The architectural principle is non-negotiable (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` principle **P2**, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` principle **G6**): **replay is not a parallel implementation**. The replay engine — backend module **M12**, architecture component **C13** — re-emits recorded events onto the *same* bus, through the *same* normalizer -> book engine -> bar builders -> order-flow engines -> WS gateway -> chart pipeline that live traffic uses. The only difference is the clock. That is why replay fidelity is structural rather than aspirational, and why `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion #1 is verified by a test that replays a recorded day and asserts derived state equals the state captured live.

R3 depends on this epic as a test harness: `30-release-roadmap.md` §12 records "E26 replay … prerequisite for deterministic testing of R3 trading logic … started S11, one train early relative to its consumer". Descoping E26 does not merely lose a feature, it raises QA cost across the whole trading train.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories (all of domain RPL):** US-RPL-001 bar-by-bar replay (Must), US-RPL-002 tick-by-tick replay (Should), US-RPL-003 order-book replay (Should), US-RPL-004 playback controls (Must), US-RPL-005 multi-pane synchronised replay (Should), US-RPL-006 simulated trading during replay (Must), US-RPL-007 replay navigation aids (Should), US-RPL-008 bookmarks and loops (Could), US-RPL-009 replay session state restore (Should).
- **Backend M12** (`apps/api/.../replay/`: `planner`, `source`, `clock`, `injector` per `20-architecture.md` §repo layout): `ReplayPlanner` (window validation against coverage and gaps, tier selection), `ReplaySource` (QuestDB hot reader + Parquet/DuckDB cold reader, k-way merge in `(ts_event, seq)` order), `ReplayClock` (monotonic scheduler, speed 0.1-100x, step modes, backpressure-slows-clock), `Injector` (publishes on `replay.{session_id}.*` through the live chain, env-scoped namespace), `SeekEngine` (snapshot anchor -> delta re-apply -> `BuilderState` checkpoint restore -> metric warm-up), `PaperBridge`.
- **Persistence:** Alembic migration creating `replay_sessions` exactly as specified in `21-database-schema.md` §3.6.4 (including `bookmarks jsonb`, `loop_enabled`, `source_tier`, `cursor_ts`, `gap_warnings`, `events_emitted`, constraints `rps_range`/`rps_speed`/`rps_tier`/`rps_cursor`/`rps_paper`).
- **REST:** `GET /api/v1/replay/sessions`, `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions`, `GET /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}`, `POST /api/v1/replay/sessions/{replayId}/control`; consumption of `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage` (owned by E16).
- **WS:** `replay_session_id` on `sub` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11), `source: "replay"` in `snap` metadata plus binary header flag bit2, `rs` in the envelope, `wt` wall-clock field on replay frames, `snap` with `reason: "replay_seek"`, `revoked` with `reason: "replay_session_ended"`, rejection of private topics with `invalid_options`, error codes `replay_session_not_found` and `replay_session_ended`.
- **Screens:** SCR-097 Replay page, SCR-098 Replay session setup modal, SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results; SCR-044 "Go to date" dialog reused for jump-to-timestamp.
- **Components:** CMP-170 ReplayScrubber, CMP-171 ReplaySpeedPicker, CMP-172 ReplayRangePicker (new design-system entries), plus reuse of CMP-180, CMP-196, CMP-028, CMP-035, CMP-043, CMP-047, CMP-219, CMP-026, CMP-027.
- **ADR-0018** Replay determinism, seek strategy and resource governance.
- Design track E26-D01..D08, QA track E26-Q01..Q06, security track E26-X01..X03.

## Out of scope
- The recorder, retention policies, snapshot cadence and the `GET /market/data-coverage` implementation — owned by **E16**.
- Bar builders, footprint, profiles, DOM ladder/heatmap, CVD and detectors — they are *consumed unmodified*. If a downstream engine turns out not to be replay-safe, that is a Bug on the owning epic (E12/E18/E19/E21/E23/E25), not scope here.
- The paper matcher fill model, queue-position modelling and demo/live parity — **E38**. E26 ships only the replay-side bridge plus the isolation invariant.
- Rule-engine simulation/backtesting over replay — **E35**.
- Backtesting over synthetic or generated (non-recorded) data.
- Android / mobile clients (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14); no separate admin app.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One code path proven, not asserted
  Given a recorded symbol-day whose live-derived bars, footprint cells, profile levels and deterministic metrics were captured at record time
  When that day is replayed end to end through the replay engine
  Then every derived value equals the live-captured value (tolerance 0 for exact metrics, 1e-9 for floats)
  And any difference fails CI

Scenario: Determinism across runs and machines
  Given the same recorded window is replayed twice, once on a developer machine and once on CI
  Then the emitted event stream and every derived series are byte-identical
  And the detector event stream is identical (roadmap exit criterion #7)

Scenario: Seek within budget
  Given a 200-depth recorded symbol-day
  When the user scrubs to an arbitrary timestamp inside the loaded window
  Then book, footprint and CVD state are reconstructed correctly and rendered within 1 s at p95, with a 2 s hard ceiling

Scenario: Replay can never be mistaken for live, and can never reach the exchange
  Given a replay session is playing with paper fills enabled
  Then every replaying pane shows the REPLAY chrome, clock and badge
  And every simulated fill is tagged simulated=true and recorded in the replay journal only
  And no replay-sourced event can be routed to a live or demo exchange account

Scenario: Missing coverage is stated, never silently skipped
  Given the requested window intersects a recording_gaps row
  When the session is created
  Then the gap is reported up front and again when playback reaches it, with Skip gap and Stop here options
```

## Technical notes / design
`24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 is the authoritative specification. Seek algorithm: (1) find the latest `orderbook_snapshot` at or before the target (written every `snapshot_interval_s`, default 300 s, plus on every subscribe/resync); (2) rebuild the book from it; (3) re-apply book deltas up to the target; (4) restore bar/footprint/profile state from a persisted `BuilderState` checkpoint (written every 60 s per `(symbol, spec_hash)`) or replay trades from the enclosing session anchor; (5) prime metric warm-up by replaying `max(warmup_bars)` bars before the target so indicators are valid at t=0 rather than `None`.

Playback: a monotonic scheduler emits events preserving inter-event deltas scaled by `speed`. `speed=0` is step mode (`step_event`, `step_ms(n)`, `step_bar`); `speed=-1` emits as fast as consumers accept (used by rule backtests). **Backpressure slows the clock rather than dropping events — replay must never lose data**; the achieved rate is reported to the client instead (US-RPL-002 NFR).

`ExecutionMode` is `"replay"` internally and never crosses the wire as an `Environment` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §2); replay is distinguished on the wire only by the frame's `source: "replay"` marker.

## Test plan
Golden-file determinism suite over a version-controlled recorded fixture; double-run equality; seek-correctness property tests; OpenAPI + WS §11 contract tests; Playwright E2E on SCR-097/098/099 (web and Electron); replay-soak at 100x over a recorded 24 h fixture (budget #15); chaos over gaps, pruned data, slow consumers, session expiry and server restart; axe-core CI plus a manual screen-reader pass. Coverage >=85% on the backend replay package, >=80% on the web replay feature.

## Security notes
STRIDE per `04-security-program.md`. Threat **S3** (replay/export endpoint used to read arbitrary filesystem paths) is rated High: mitigated by **SR-097** — no user-supplied filesystem paths anywhere in the replay API, datasets addressed only by registry ids, with mandatory path-traversal and symlink-escape tests. **Resource exhaustion**: an unbounded window at 100x is a denial of service against the trading host — per-user concurrent-session quota, window-size cap, per-session memory ceiling and 2 h idle reclaim. RBAC `replay:read` / `replay:write`, scope `self`. Private topics (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`) are never replayable. Paper fills inside replay are tagged `simulated=true` and never enter the trading audit stream. Data classification A-10 (recorded market data), integrity objective O8.

## Accessibility notes
The replay clock is a labelled live region updated at most 1 Hz; the scrubber is `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` in absolute human-readable time; transport controls are standard labelled buttons carrying shortcut hints; REPLAY state is conveyed by text and iconography, never by colour alone; the full hotkey table of SCR-097 is keyboard-reachable and documented in Storybook.

## Performance notes
Budget #2 (frame time <=16.6 ms p95, never below 30 fps, worst case explicitly includes "replay at 20x") and budget #15 (sustain up to 100x crash-free; visual fidelity may degrade by skip-render but must not desync) from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. SCR-097 additionally requires 25x on 1-minute data and 4x on raw tick data without dropped frames, and seek <=1 s within the loaded window. SCR-098 requires a 1-day single-symbol session ready in <=10 s with progress shown.

## Observability
Metrics: `replay_sessions_active`, `replay_events_emitted_total`, `replay_clock_lag_ms`, `replay_seek_duration_ms`, `replay_source_tier`, `replay_gap_warnings_total`, `replay_backpressure_seconds_total`, `replay_session_memory_bytes`. Trace: OpenTelemetry span for replay session start (one of the two traced paths in `20-architecture.md` §observability). Analytics/audit: `replay.session_created`, `replay.started`, `replay.seek`, `replay.session_deleted`, `replay.paper_fill`, `replay.results_viewed`, `replay.results_promoted_to_journal`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike/Design/QA/Security ticket is Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded Won't/Later disposition.
- [ ] Roadmap §6.3 exit criteria #1 (single shared pipeline), #7 (detector reproducibility) and #8 (determinism + 1 s scrub) demonstrated by CI checks, not by claim.
- [ ] Coverage floors held (>=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend); zero open P0/P1 bugs in E26 scope.
- [ ] ADR-0018 merged; `20-architecture.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md` reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-097/098/099 plus a manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] perf: budgets #2 and #15 recorded; seek p95 <1 s recorded in the benchmark report.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged (fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off), Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression and exploratory pass executed and recorded; design QA sign-off from the CDO track; demoed to Owner at Sprint Review against staging (demo).

## Dependencies
- **E16** recorder, retention and `GET /market/data-coverage` — supplies the recorded streams, the periodic `orderbook_snapshot` seek anchors and the gap records. Without it there is nothing to replay.
- **E17** WS protocol and binary framing — supplies the `replay_session_id` routing hook, the `source`/`rs`/`wt` envelope fields and header flag bit2.
- **E12** bar builders — the `BarBuilder.snapshot()`/`restore()` contract and `spec_hash` determinism property (invariant BI-4) underpin seek.
- **E18**, **E21** — the order-flow surfaces replay must reproduce identically; the determinism harness diffs against their live-captured output.
- **E38** paper trading — supplies the `PaperMatcher` consumed by E26-S07; the replay-side bridge ships flagged off until E38 lands.

## Branch
`feat/replay-engine-<short>` per child ticket (e.g. `feat/replay-engine-clock`). PRs <=400 LOC diff preferred; the engine tasks split along planner/source/clock/seek boundaries to hold that.

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for the replay engine and its data access
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4 names E26 explicitly in the R2 security gate: "STRIDE for E26 (**replay resource exhaustion, path handling for archived data**) and E21". `04-security-program.md` already carries the relevant pre-assessed threat, **S3 — elevation of privilege: "Replay/export endpoint used to read arbitrary filesystem paths"**, rated High and mitigated by **SR-097**. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the STRIDE kickoff before the epic can be Ready.

This ticket runs the model properly rather than inheriting the two headline threats, because replay has a third that is easy to miss: it is the only feature that presents a trading interface over stale data.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model for the replay data flow — client -> REST control -> session store -> source readers (QuestDB, Parquet/DuckDB) -> clock -> injector -> bus -> WS gateway -> client, plus the paper-matcher branch — recorded at `docs/plan/27-adrs/` adjacent security notes or the security-program appendix as the programme convention dictates, and linked here.
- Threats enumerated per element, at minimum:
  - **Spoofing**: using another user's `replay_session_id` on a WS subscription.
  - **Tampering**: modifying a session's window or paper account to read or trade against data the user is not entitled to; tampering with stored bookmarks or pane configuration (user-controlled persisted data replayed into the client).
  - **Repudiation**: a simulated fill being indistinguishable from a real one in the journal or in an export.
  - **Information disclosure**: path traversal or symlink escape into the Parquet archive (**S3/SR-097**); error messages leaking internal paths or dataset ids; accessible names or live regions leaking identifiers.
  - **Denial of service**: unbounded window, many concurrent sessions, seek amplification via scrub-drag, read-ahead memory growth from a stalled consumer, 100x playback CPU cost — the "replay resource exhaustion" the roadmap names.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a replay-sourced event routed to a live account; a private topic subscribed under a replay session; a paper account the caller has not been granted.
- **Abuse cases** written as executable test intentions for E26-X02, each with an expected refusal.
- Risk ratings with likelihood and impact, mapped to the existing controls (SR-097, RBAC scope self, the T01 quotas, the T03 `source="replay"` invariant) and any new control required.
- Data classification confirmation: recorded market data is A-10 with integrity objective O8; session metadata references accounts.

## Out of scope
- Implementing controls (T01/T02/T03/T05 own them; new gaps are filed as tickets).
- Penetration testing (programme-level, before Live enablement).
- The recorder's own threat model (E16-X01) — referenced, not repeated.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element and every STRIDE category is considered
  Given the replay data-flow diagram
  When the model is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect
  Then each element has each STRIDE category either enumerated with a threat or explicitly marked not-applicable with a reason

Scenario: The roadmap's two named threats are addressed in depth
  Then replay resource exhaustion and path handling for archived data each have threats, ratings and named controls
  And each control maps to a specific implementation ticket

Scenario: Abuse cases are executable
  Then every abuse case states the attempt, the expected refusal and the layer that refuses it
  And E26-X02 can implement them without further interpretation

Scenario: Gaps become tickets
  Given a threat with no existing control
  Then a ticket exists to add the control, referenced from the model
```

## Technical notes / design
The model must record *where* each control lives, because several replay controls are deliberately structural rather than procedural: `source="replay"` set at injection so the OMS refuses by construction; registry-id addressing so no path can be supplied; per-session task ownership so destroy actually frees resources. A control's location is what determines whether a refactor can silently remove it.

## Test plan
The model is the deliverable; its verification is E26-X02's test implementation and E26-X03's review.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the threat-modelling deliverable for the epic and is cited in the epic DoD.

## Accessibility notes
Includes the assistive-technology disclosure channel explicitly, which standard threat models routinely omit.

## Performance notes
The denial-of-service analysis must be grounded in the E26-K01 and E26-Q03 numbers so limits are set where they actually bite rather than at arbitrary round figures.

## Observability
Specify the security-relevant signals to emit: blocked live-routing attempts (must be zero), rejected cross-user session references, quota rejections, and path-validation failures.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] STRIDE model completed, reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer and the Architect.
- [ ] Abuse cases written and handed to E26-X02.
- [ ] Every threat mapped to an existing control or a filed ticket.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

## Dependencies
`E26-T01` establishes the session model, quotas and RBAC scoping the model reasons about.

## Branch
`chore/e26-threat-model`.
