title: Paper trading & demo/live parity
body:
## Context
R3 "Trading on demo" executes **everything** against Bybit demo; there is no code path that can reach live until R4 flips the gate (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7). E38 is the epic that owns that statement. It is simultaneously:

1. **The environment boundary.** SCR-075 is described in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` as "the single most safety-critical visual element in the app", and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SR-040a requires the environment capability matrix to be "enforced in code, not documentation". Threats **W9** (code assuming WS order entry exists on demo, leaving orders unplaced or duplicated) and **W10** (demo and live endpoints mixed within one session) are named in the security program with this epic's work as their control.
2. **The honest simulator.** `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12 specifies the local paper matcher (module **M16**) field by field - queue position, latency, fees, funding, margin - because a simulator that ignores those lies, and a lying simulator is worse than none: it manufactures confidence (risk **R12**).
3. **The parity evidence base.** US-PAPER-008's report is what makes R4 "a gating exercise rather than a re-architecture" (roadmap section 7.1 goal 5). The roadmap dependency graph records `E38 --> E44`: whatever this epic leaves ambiguous becomes a live-money problem in R4.

The epic sits at S18-S19, the last two sprints of R3, and depends on `E29` (OMS and order state machine) and `E26` (replay engine) per the roadmap's dependency graph.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories covered (all Must/Should in the PAPER domain, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 21):**
- **US-PAPER-001** Bybit demo integration (Must) - E38-S01
- **US-PAPER-002** Explicit Demo/Live switching (Must) - E38-S02 (backend), E38-S04 (UI)
- **US-PAPER-003** Demo/Live isolation gating (Must) - E38-T02 (server enforcement), E38-S04 (client guard)
- **US-PAPER-004** Local simulated fill engine (Should) - E38-S03, E38-S05
- **US-PAPER-005** Paper P&L identical to live (Must) - E38-S03 (same accounting path), E38-S05 (separate reporting and labelling)
- **US-PAPER-006** Reset paper balance (Should) - E38-S06
- **US-PAPER-007** Demo eligibility per manager (Should) - E38-S07
- **US-PAPER-008** Environment parity report (Should) - E38-K01, E38-S08, E38-T03

**Screens:** SCR-074 Environment switcher, SCR-075 Demo/Live banner and per-panel badges, SCR-079 Account detail drawer (reset section), SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results, SCR-122 Admin user detail (eligibility section), SCR-137 Admin security centre (parity + fidelity sections).

**Components:** CMP-074 EnvBanner, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard, plus composition of CMP-027, CMP-028, CMP-036, CMP-043, CMP-044, CMP-049, CMP-050, CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-099, CMP-104, CMP-106, CMP-116, CMP-128, CMP-129, CMP-167, CMP-168, CMP-175, CMP-178; contributes a new simulated badge to the design system.

**Backend module:** **M16 Paper Matcher** (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.7, C11) - `FillModel`, `QueueEstimator`, `FeeModel`, `PaperLedger` - plus the environment capability matrix and the isolation middleware.

**API:** `POST /session/environment` (implemented), `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` (extended with eligibility), and new: `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/paper-reset`, `GET /admin/parity` plus its verification endpoint, `GET /admin/paper-fidelity`. Environment enforcement is applied to every account-mutating trading route.

**WS:** `system` topic (environment switch phases and the resulting environment), `is_paper` on every private frame (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 13.1).

**DB:** `exchange_accounts.env`, `is_paper` columns across orders/positions/executions/trade groups, `user_account_access` extended with live eligibility and its acknowledgement, paper ledger and parity-observation storage.

## Out of scope
- **Live order entry.** The `live_trading` flag stays off through R3; turning it on is E44 after the E43 pen-test.
- **Android and any separate admin application** - owner decisions, permanently out of scope.
- Non-USDT-perp products (spot, options, inverse).
- Resetting a Bybit demo account's balance at the exchange - only the local paper ledger is reset.
- Auto-tuning the fill model from divergence results; tuning stays a human decision.
- Journal analytics computation (E41), replay transport (E26), fan-out (E34), the OMS itself (E29) - E38 consumes them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Demo and live can never mix
  Given a session in one environment
  When any account-mutating trading route is called against an account in the other environment, including by a crafted request bypassing the UI
  Then it is refused with 403, no state changes, and a high-severity audit row is written - proven across every trading route by an automated route-coverage test

Scenario: Switching to live is deliberate, gated and complete
  Given a session in demo
  When the user switches to live
  Then it requires a typed confirmation phrase, step-up authentication and the live_trading flag; no hotkey can trigger it; one-click trading is disarmed; every private subscription is torn down and rebuilt; and a half-switched state is never reachable, including across a backend restart mid-transition

Scenario: The environment is stated on every trading-capable surface
  Given any trading panel, including floated and maximised Electron windows
  When it is rendered
  Then it states DEMO or LIVE in text plus icon plus pattern, remains unambiguous in greyscale and in three colour-vision simulations, and includes the environment in its accessible name

Scenario: The simulator is honest and can never reach the exchange
  Given the paper matcher
  When orders are simulated
  Then fills respect queue position, latency, book depth, real fee rates and funding; the applied FillModelConfig is disclosed with every result set; a structural test proves the paper package imports no network client; and a nightly divergence job compares simulated against real demo fills, opening a defect above one tick p95 slippage or ten percentage points fill-rate divergence

Scenario: Paper results never contaminate live statistics
  Given a journal containing both simulated and real trades
  When analytics are computed
  Then simulated rows are excluded by default, every view labels them, and promotion of a simulated session to the journal is flagged and audited

Scenario: The parity report is generated and current
  Given the maintained parity data file plus runtime observations
  When the report is viewed
  Then every known difference is listed with its source and last-verified date, demo-only failures appear as candidate items, and items unverified for 90 days are flagged

Scenario: Eligibility is a server-side attribute with safe revocation
  Given a manager without live eligibility
  Then no live action succeeds by any path; and when live access is revoked while live positions are open, those positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode while new entries are refused
```

## Technical notes / design
- **One code path, two environments.** The only environment-aware code is the adapter's immutable capability record and key selection; an architecture test asserts the string `demo` does not appear in `cv/oms/`. This is what makes R4 a gate flip rather than a rewrite.
- **One choke point.** Environment enforcement lives in a single FastAPI dependency (E38-T02) that returns an `EnvironmentContext` handlers must accept, so omission is a type error. A route-coverage test over the OpenAPI document fails CI when a new trading route lacks it.
- **`is_paper` is orthogonal to `environment`.** A paper fill still belongs to a real environment (demo, or live when replaying live-recorded data). `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 13.1 is explicit that collapsing them would lose information; the UI must therefore show two distinct badges.
- **The matcher rides the shared bus.** Replay re-emits recorded events with the same types onto the same bus (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 13), so the matcher works identically over live and recorded data, and its determinism supports R3 exit criterion 6.
- **Structural versus enforced controls.** E38-X01 classifies each control; structural controls (separate client instances, no transport import in `cv/paper/`) get import-time or compile-time tests, enforced controls get runtime tests. The distinction drives the regression pack.

## Test plan
- **Unit** - queue estimator table-driven suite (the highest-value set in the epic), book walk VWAP, latency races, fee and funding maths, liquidation tiers, environment refusal matrix, eligibility derivation, staleness boundaries. Coverage: >=90% on `cv/paper/` and the safety-critical middleware, >=85% backend elsewhere, >=80% frontend.
- **Contract** - `enum_parity_environment`, the new endpoints, error-registry entries, WS frame shapes, and the route-coverage gate.
- **Integration** - recorded demo fixtures for submit/partial-fill/amend/cancel/reject/reconnect; replay-driven matcher sessions with restart recovery; reset atomicity; revocation with open positions.
- **E2E** - nine Playwright suites across web and Electron (E38-Q02), including the crafted cross-environment request and the floating-window badge.
- **Perf** - budget #4 (submit-to-ack p95 <300 ms on demo, hard R3 gate), matcher throughput at >=20x real time, switch transition p95 <=2 s, memory budget #8 (E38-Q03).
- **Chaos** - restart mid-switch at each phase, WS disconnect mid-order, restart with open simulated state, Postgres failure mid-reset, audit-writer failure must fail closed, clock skew, WS flapping during a switch (E38-Q04).
- **Security** - STRIDE (E38-X01), abuse cases plus durable Semgrep/ZAP rules (E38-X02), review and sign-off (E38-X03).
- **A11y** - axe-core in CI per state plus NVDA manual passes (E38-Q05).

## Security notes
- STRIDE model at `docs/security/threat-models/E38-paper-trading.md` (E38-X01). Highest-rated threats: a simulated order reaching the exchange (Critical), a demo session reaching live (Critical), a manager self-granting live eligibility (High), an unaudited environment switch or reset (High), a not-permitted message disclosing other users' grants (Medium).
- Implements **SR-040a** (environment capability matrix in code), supports **SR-119** (single backend chokepoint for exchange traffic) and **SR-043** (armed state for live). Demo keys are handled identically to live keys (SR-003, SR-004); CI never holds demo credentials (SR-140).
- Every ticket touching RBAC, order placement or account-scoped state carries the `security` label per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8, and cannot reach Done without a Security engineer review.
- Data classification: financial transaction and simulation data; API credentials by reference only; no secret is rendered on any E38 surface.

## Accessibility notes
- WCAG 2.2 AA across all six surfaces, with no "internal tool" exception for the admin screens.
- The environment distinction must be text plus icon plus pattern, unambiguous in greyscale and in deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulations - verified in design (E38-D05) and on the built app (E38-Q05).
- The band is `role="status"` and polite; the post-switch confirmation is `role="alert"` announced once; per-panel badges are `role="img"` with static labels to prevent an announcement storm.
- Every SCR-099 chart has a keyboard-reachable table alternative; the destructive reset dialog announces the counts it will discard and does not default focus to the destructive button.
- An imperceptible environment indicator is treated as a security defect, not only an accessibility one.

## Performance notes
- Budget **#4** order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo is a **hard R3 exit gate**; E38-S01 owns it and E38-Q03 measures it with backend-internal and exchange-RTT components separated.
- Budget **#8** <=300 MB resident per actively-recorded symbol during matcher replay; budget **#15** replay at up to 100x without the matcher becoming the bottleneck.
- The environment switch blocks order entry for its whole duration - p95 <=2 s per SCR-074, measured per phase.

Engineering children (Story/Task/Spike: K01 2, S01 2, S02 2, S03 5, S04 3, S05 1, S06 1, S07 2, S08 2, T01 2, T02 3, T03 2, T04 1) now total **28 points** - +7.7% against the registered sizing and inside the +/-15% tolerance band of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`.

- [ ] Epic-level acceptance criteria verified end to end on staging (demo), not merely per child.
- [ ] Coverage floors held: >=90% on `cv/paper/` and the safety-critical middleware, >=85% backend, >=80% frontend; zero open P0/P1 against E38 scope.

title: Build the footprint settings dialog SCR-032 with live preview
body:
## Context
Implements **US-FP-010 — Footprint settings panel (Must)**: *"I want one panel for all footprint settings, so that I can tune quickly mid-session."* Screen **SCR-032**, described in `14-screens-catalogue.md` as *"the deepest settings surface of the chart"*. Components: CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-031 ColorSwatch/ThemeChip, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-228 PreviewTile.

The dialog is also where the performance guard lives: the SCR-032 spike gate requires that any setting combination measured below budget is either removed or shipped with a **designed, visible cost warning** showing the measured figure.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Every control from the SCR-032 wireframe, each bound to its `FootprintConfig` field via the E18-D05 mapping table: cell type (volume / bid×ask / delta / delta+total), display (box / profile), input source (three sources; order-based **absent** with its info note), noise filter, imbalance diagonal ratio and stack depth with the highlight-stacks and add-glyph toggles, POC bold and VA mark toggles, cell-text auto-hide threshold and font size, bid/ask colours with the CVD-safe preset.
- **Live preview** (CMP-228 PreviewTile, `kind: "footprint"`): a synthetic bar rendering with the current settings, updating in ≤ 50 ms, with a textual description of what changed.
- **Per-symbol defaults**: "save as default for BTCUSDT" applies to new BTCUSDT footprint panes only; other symbols keep theirs.
- **Reset**: returns to product defaults (300% diagonal, stack 3, bucket 1 tick) behind a confirmation.
- Validation with inline errors: imbalance ratio 100–2000% ("Enter a ratio between 100 and 2000 %."), stack depth 2–10, noise filter ≥ 0, auto-hide threshold ≥ 0.
- Recompute-in-progress state ("Recomputing footprint from recorded trades — 40 %") for the one setting that triggers it (input source).
- **Cost warning**: when the selected combination was measured below budget, show the designed warning with the measured figure ("This tick aggregation renders ~180 cells per bar; measured 41 fps on your machine").
- RBAC: a `viewer` may change display-only settings for their own session but cannot trigger a recompute (`recording:write`); the control reflects that rather than failing on click.

## Out of scope
The rendering behaviours the settings drive (E18-S01..S09), the recompute job (E18-T05), the imbalance tracker panel (E18-S07/S08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live preview
  When I change a setting
  Then the chart updates immediately and the panel shows the effective value
  And the preview tile re-renders within 50 ms

Scenario: Per-symbol defaults
  When I save settings as the default for BTCUSDT
  Then new BTCUSDT footprint panes adopt them
  And other symbols keep their own settings

Scenario: Reset
  When I choose reset
  Then a confirmation is required
  And on confirm settings return to 300 percent diagonal, stack 3, bucket 1 tick

Scenario: Validation
  When I enter an imbalance ratio of 2500 percent
  Then an inline error reads "Enter a ratio between 100 and 2000 %."
  And the setting is not applied

Scenario: Only the input source rebuilds
  When I change any setting other than the input source
  Then no recompute job is started and the chart updates from cached aggregates
  And when I change the input source, the recompute progress state is shown

Scenario: Below-budget combination is guarded
  Given a tick aggregation measured below the frame budget on this machine
  Then the dialog shows the measured cost warning before the setting is applied

Scenario: Viewer cannot rebuild
  Given a user with the viewer role
  Then the input-source control is shown in a permission-denied state
  And attempting to change it neither issues a request nor silently fails
```

## Technical notes / design
- The dialog is a controlled form over `FootprintOptions`/`FootprintConfig`; there is exactly one settings object per pane, and "save as default for symbol" writes to user preferences rather than duplicating state.
- The preview tile drives a miniature engine instance with synthetic data — not a screenshot, so it is honest about the actual renderer.
- The cost warning reads from the locally measured benchmark result stored by the SET-005 "Run benchmark" action (`14-screens-catalogue.md` performance settings section) when present, and otherwise from the E18-K01 reference-machine figures with that provenance stated.
- Error handling per global AC #5: domain language, raw code in a details disclosure.

## Test plan
- Unit: form state; validation boundaries (99/100/2000/2001%, stack 1/2/10/11); per-symbol default resolution; reset confirmation; permission-gated control state.
- E2E: change each control and assert the chart reflects it; assert only the input-source change issues a network request; save a per-symbol default, open a new pane and assert adoption.
- Perf: preview re-render ≤ 50 ms measured.
- axe: full dialog, including the colour controls and their paired glyph/pattern options.

## Security notes
The recompute action is state-changing, `recording:write`-gated and audited (`chart.footprint_settings_changed`, `market.footprint_recompute_requested`). Client-side gating is a UX affordance only — the server enforces (E18-T03). Threat: **CSRF/replay on the recompute POST** — mitigated by the required idempotency key and the standard session controls. No secrets on this surface.

## Accessibility notes
Full keyboard navigation with a logical tab order and a visible focus ring; every numeric field carries its unit in the label; every colour choice is **paired with a glyph/pattern option** (SCR-032 a11y requirement); the preview tile has `role="img"` with a name describing the current configuration in words, and the settings themselves remain independently readable so the preview is never the only disclosure; reset requires confirmation; inline errors are associated with their inputs via `aria-describedby`; all targets ≥ 24×24 px; dialog focus trap and `Esc` to close per CMP-043.

## Performance notes
Settings apply without a full history refetch except for input-source changes (SCR-032 performance note). Preview renders in ≤ 50 ms. The dialog must not hold a second full engine instance alive after it closes — assert no leak in the memory soak.

## Observability
`chart.footprint_settings_changed` with `{section, key}`; `market.footprint_recompute_requested` audit; metric `footprint_settings_reset_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios pass via automated tests.
- [ ] SCR-032 design sign-off checklist fully satisfied by the built dialog.
- [ ] Cost-warning behaviour demonstrated with a deliberately below-budget combination.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass over the whole dialog.
- [ ] Preview timing and leak check recorded.
- [ ] design-qa, QA sign-off, Sprint Review demo.
- [ ] PR merged with 2 approvals including a code owner.

## Dependencies
E18-S06 and E18-S08 provide the behaviours the controls drive; E18-D05 provides the signed-off design and the control→config→API mapping table.

## Branch
`feat/e18-footprint-settings-dialog`

## References
- docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 8 (FP domain), global acceptance criteria 3-7
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-030, SCR-032, SCR-042, SCR-045, SCR-056
- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-109, CMP-132, CMP-182, CMP-195, CMP-197, CMP-222, CMP-227, CMP-228, CMP-046, CMP-049
- docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md rows US-FP-001..US-FP-010
- docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md sections 3.6, 3.7, 4, 8, 13
- docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md section 4
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md sections 6.1, 14.4; docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml `/market/footprint`
- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md sections 6.1, 11.3; docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md budgets 1, 2, 3

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`
2. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`
3. `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`
4. `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`
5. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`
6. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
Base area for `web`: apps/web/src/features/<feature>/ (+ apps/web/src/state, apps/web/src/app/routes as needed)
- Every control from the SCR-032 wireframe, each bound to its `FootprintConfig` field via the E18-D05 mapping table: cell type (volume / bid×ask / delta / delta+total), display (box / profile), input source (three sources; order-based **absent** with its info note), noise filter, imbalance diagonal ratio and stack depth with the highlight-stacks and add-glyph toggles, POC bold and VA mark toggles, cell-text auto-hide threshold and font size, bid/ask colours with the CVD-safe preset.
- **Live preview** (CMP-228 PreviewTile, `kind: "footprint"`): a synthetic bar rendering with the current settings, updating in ≤ 50 ms, with a textual description of what changed.
- **Per-symbol defaults**: "save as default for BTCUSDT" applies to new BTCUSDT footprint panes only; other symbols keep theirs.
- **Reset**: returns to product defaults (300% diagonal, stack 3, bucket 1 tick) behind a confirmation.
- Validation with inline errors: imbalance ratio 100–2000% ("Enter a ratio between 100 and 2000 %."), stack depth 2–10, noise filter ≥ 0, auto-hide threshold ≥ 0.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- /market/footprint

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e18-footprint-settings-dialog`
- PR title: `E18-S10: Build the footprint settings dialog SCR-032 with live preview`
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder until the issue number is assigned)
- Required reviewers: @CandleViewer/frontend (per `.github/CODEOWNERS` for the touched paths)
- Labels: `type/feature`, `area/order-flow`, `priority/p1`, `a11y`, `perf`, `design-qa`

**Done means**
- All scenarios pass via automated tests.
- SCR-032 design sign-off checklist fully satisfied by the built dialog.
- Cost-warning behaviour demonstrated with a deliberately below-budget combination.
- axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass over the whole dialog.
- Preview timing and leak check recorded.
- design-qa, QA sign-off, Sprint Review demo.

**Do NOT**
- Do not widen scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables section above.
- Do not hand-edit `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md` (generated from `machines/*.json`).
- Do not create/instantiate a statechart outside `cv.statechart.factory` (ADR-0016).

**If blocked**
- Comment on the GitHub issue naming the exact blocking ticket key or gate (e.g. a failing CI check, an unresolved dependency in `blocked_by`, or a missing upstream decision).
- Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**.
- Never silently work around a failing gate or an unmet dependency — stop and ask (AGENTS.md §3 step 2).

body:
## Context
Executes the E18-X01 model against the built software. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 makes a Security engineer review mandatory for anything touching these paths before Done, and R2's security gate requires the DoS-class vectors to be closed before the train exits.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case execution** against staging, each with a recorded result:
  1. Request a window exceeding 200 000 cells → expect `400 validation_failed / footprint_window_too_large`, no partial stream, bounded server memory.
  2. Subscribe with `history` = 5 000 → expect rejection or clamp to 200 with the resolved value echoed; no unbounded snapshot.
  3. Subscribe/unsubscribe churn at high rate on `footprint.*` → expect rate limiting; assert snapshot-generation amplification is bounded and observable.
  4. Fire repeated `POST /market/footprint/recompute` for the same and different windows → expect idempotency-key deduplication and concurrency limits; assert ingestion budget #6 is not breached while rebuilds run.
  5. Call both endpoints as `viewer`, `manager` and `owner` → expect the documented RBAC outcome; assert a 403 changes nothing and writes an audit record (global AC #1).
  6. Replay a recompute request with a reused idempotency key and with a tampered body → expect the documented behaviour, not a silent second job.
  7. Inject a malformed binary frame claiming an oversized `cell_count` → expect the client to reject and log, never to allocate unbounded.
  8. Attempt path traversal via `symbol`/`bar_type`/`param` reaching the cold-tier partition path → expect rejection at the vocabulary-validation layer, with no filesystem access attempted.
  9. Attempt to publish a forged `stacked_imbalance_zone` from a client connection → expect rejection; the event is server-produced only.
- **Automated rule coverage**: Semgrep/Bandit rules (or equivalents) for the recurring patterns this epic introduces — unvalidated window parameters reaching a storage query, user-influenced path components, and unbounded response materialisation — added to the SAST config so a future change cannot silently regress.
- **DAST**: OWASP ZAP pass over the new endpoints in the staging scan profile.
- **SCA/secrets**: confirm the new dependencies (if any) are clean; confirm the E18-T06 golden fixture contains no credentials or account identifiers.
- **Log hygiene review**: confirm no full query strings with user identifiers at info level, no internal paths in error bodies, and that audit records redact nothing that matters while exposing nothing that should not be.
- Findings triaged: fixed, or accepted-risk with an Owner-signed disposition.

## Out of scope
The threat model itself (E18-X01), penetration testing (E43), rendering-layer functional bugs (QA tickets).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case is executed and recorded
  When the review completes
  Then each of the nine abuse cases has a recorded expected result, actual result and verdict

Scenario: DoS limits hold under pressure
  Given the oversized-window, history-overrun, churn and recompute-spam cases run concurrently
  Then the service stays within its CPU and memory budgets
  And no request path returns a partial or unbounded response
  And the detective metrics from the threat model increment as designed

Scenario: RBAC cannot be bypassed
  Given a viewer session
  Then neither endpoint performs a privileged action
  And every denial writes an audit record naming actor, role and attempted action

Scenario: Regressions are prevented, not just fixed
  Then SAST rules covering the identified patterns are merged into CI
  And a deliberately reintroduced unvalidated-window pattern is caught by those rules

Scenario: Findings are dispositioned
  Then every finding is fixed and re-verified, or recorded as accepted risk with Owner sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Execute against staging with fixtures, never live. Use the existing security-test harness conventions from `04-security-program.md`. Where a control lives in E17's shared machinery (rate limiting, backpressure), verify it applies to the `footprint.*` topic specifically rather than assuming inheritance — assumed inheritance is how gaps happen.

## Test plan
Each abuse case is written as a repeatable script where possible and added to the security regression suite, so R3/R4/R5 re-run them. Cases that must stay manual are marked with the reason.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security review required by DoD. It must be performed by the Security engineer, not by the implementing developer, and its sign-off comment is a hard gate on E18 reaching Done.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Cases 3 and 4 are explicitly run while measuring budgets #6 and #11, since a "limit" that protects availability by destroying latency is not a working control.

## Observability
Verifies the detective controls actually fire: `footprint_window_rejected_total`, `ws_resync_total{topic="footprint"}`, rate-limit counters, `footprint_rebuild_jobs_total{status}` and the audit stream. An unobservable control is treated as a finding.

- [ ] SAST rules merged and verified by a deliberate reintroduction.
- [ ] ZAP pass completed; findings triaged.
- [ ] SCA and secrets scans clean, including the golden fixture.
- [ ] Log-hygiene review completed.
- [ ] Security regression suite updated.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted on E18.
- [ ] Accepted risks (if any) carry Owner sign-off.

title: Playwright E2E for the profile panel, period modes and settings dialog
body:
## Context
`SCR-038` is a WebGL-rendered histogram docked beside a chart and `SCR-039` is the modal that reshapes it. The user-visible risks here are not arithmetic - `E19-Q02` owns that - but *binding*: the profile must stay glued to the price axis while the chart zooms, re-bucket when row size changes, recompute on pan in visible-range mode without dropping frames, and keep POC/VA lines pinned to the right prices across symbol and timeframe switches.

`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` mandates Playwright E2E for web and the Electron shell. This ticket adds the E19 suite to that harness and automates the `E19-Q01` cases marked automatable.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/specs/e19-profiles/` specs against a seeded deterministic backend (replayed fixture tape, frozen clock, animations disabled):
  1. `session-profile.spec.ts` - open `SCR-038` from the panel menu; rows render; live prints extend rows; the legend shows the effective row size; CMP-227 EstimatedBadge "approximated from bars" appears for the kline-only symbol and disappears once ticks exist.
  2. `period-modes.spec.ts` - switch Composite / Session multiples / Visible range / Personalised range / Swing-anchored; drag a fixed-range selection and assert it stays pinned to those timestamps across pan and zoom; assert visible-range recompute fires after the pan-end debounce and not per frame.
  3. `poc-value-area.spec.ts` - POC row carries a non-colour affordance; VAH/VAL labelled; changing `value_area_pct` re-shades immediately and persists per profile type across reload; the tie-break tooltip text is present; developing VA updates while the period is open.
  4. `delta-tpo.spec.ts` - `kind=delta` signed rows with direction glyph; zero-delta rows distinct from never-traded rows; combined view shares one price axis; TPO letters render, initial balance is marked, the single-print glyph toggles.
  5. `nodes-and-naked-poc.spec.ts` - HVN/LVN mark count responds to the prominence threshold; naked POCs are drawn until retraded, demoted on retest with a history toggle, and capped to nearest-N with a hidden count.
  6. `settings-presets.spec.ts` - `SCR-039` preset apply switches period type, row size, VA%, VWAP overlay and node marking together; a saved preset is reusable on another symbol and survives workspace export/import; row size below tick size is clamped with the explanatory message; a range longer than recorded history warns rather than blocks.
- **Axis-alignment helper**: reads rendered row y-positions from the engine debug hook and compares to CMP-188 PriceAxis tick positions within 1 device pixel at three zoom levels and at DPR 1 and 2.
- **Visual regression**: masked snapshots of `SCR-038` in volume, delta, TPO and combined modes, light and dark themes.
- Runs in Chromium and the Electron shell; a WebGL-unavailable run asserts the documented fallback message rather than a blank pane.
- Traceability: each spec names the `E19-TC-*` ids it automates.

## Out of scope
- Numeric correctness of rows, POC and VA (`E19-Q02`) - specs assert which row is flagged POC by reading the API response, never by recomputing in the browser.
- FPS budgets and load (`E19-Q04`), the full a11y audit (`E19-Q06`) and chaos (`E19-Q05`).
- Alert and rule consumption of profile metrics (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Profile stays glued to the price axis
  Given SCR-038 docked beside a chart at DPR 2
  When the chart is zoomed and panned through three levels
  Then each profile row centre matches its PriceAxis price position within 1 device pixel

Scenario: Visible-range mode recomputes on pan end, not per frame
  Given visible-range period mode
  When the user pans continuously for 2 seconds
  Then recompute requests are throttled to at most 10 per second and a final recompute fires after the pan-end debounce

Scenario: Failure case - profile request fails
  Given GET /api/v1/market/profile returns 503
  When the panel loads
  Then a named error state with a retry action is shown, the chart keeps rendering, and no unhandled console error is produced

Scenario: Edge case - row size below tick size
  Given the user enters a row size smaller than the instrument tick size in SCR-039
  Then the value is clamped to one tick with an explanatory message and no request is sent with an invalid price_grouping

Scenario: Edge case - symbol switch while a fixed range is pinned
  Given a fixed-range profile pinned to a timestamp window
  When the symbol is switched away and back
  Then the pinned window is preserved and the profile is recomputed for the new symbol with no rows leaked from the previous symbol

Scenario: Preset round-trip survives export and import
  Given a preset saved on BTCUSDT and applied on a second symbol
  When the workspace is exported and reimported
  Then every setting in the preset is restored identically
```

## Technical notes / design
- Determinism comes from the replayed tape, a frozen clock, fixed viewports (1920x1080 and 1440x900) and disabled animations, which is what makes visual snapshots viable.
- The engine exposes a test-only debug hook (row y-positions, POC row index, LOD merge level) behind a build flag; specs read it instead of pixel-sniffing, keeping them robust to styling changes while still exercising real rendering.
- LOD assertion: when the pane is too short for 5 000 rows to own a pixel each, rows must be *merged*, not dropped, and POC/VAH/VAL must survive merging as distinct marks.
- The Electron run reuses the same specs through the shared fixture from the E10 harness, so desktop regressions are caught without a second suite.

## Test plan
- Pre-merge on PRs touching the profile panel, the engine profile plugin or `SCR-039`; nightly in full (both themes, both DPRs, Electron).
- Flake policy per `03-testing-strategy.md`: a spec failing twice in 20 nightly runs is quarantined with a ticket, never deleted.
- Every spec asserts zero `console.error` and zero unexpected failed network requests beyond deliberately injected faults.

## Security notes
- Specs authenticate as a `marketdata:read` user; a negative spec asserts a Viewer lacking `marketdata:read` sees an authorization error state rather than an empty profile that could be mistaken for "no data".
- Fault injection uses the test proxy only; scripts refuse non-allow-listed hosts so no spec can run against production.
- Playwright traces are scrubbed of auth headers and cookies before upload as CI artefacts.

## Accessibility notes
- Every spec runs `axe-core` on `SCR-038` and `SCR-039` and fails on new serious or critical violations.
- Keyboard path asserted end to end: open panel, move focus into the profile, traverse rows, read the table alternative, open `SCR-039`, focus trapped in the dialog, Escape returns focus to the invoking control.
- The table alternative is asserted to expose price, volume, delta and value-area membership per row, with POC/VAH/VAL announced via a live region, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
- Specs record recompute latency and frame timings as soft metrics for trend tracking; hard budgets are enforced in `E19-Q04`.
- The visible-range spec is the canonical guard against the most likely regression in this epic: recompute-per-frame during pan.

## Observability
- Traces, videos and masked screenshots are uploaded on failure; each spec logs the `x-request-id` of its profile calls so a UI failure can be correlated with server logs.
- Nightly results feed the E19 quality dashboard alongside `E19-Q02`.

## Definition of Done
- Suite merged, green on three consecutive nightly runs, wired into required checks for the touched paths.
- Every `E19-Q01` case marked "automated: E19-Q03" exists and is traced back by id.
- Visual baselines reviewed and approved in a design-QA pass rather than auto-blessed.
- Quarantine and flake policy documented in the suite README.

## Dependencies
- `E19-S01` and `E19-S04` (panel behaviour), `E19-T04` (engine profile plugin and debug hook), `E19-Q01` (case ids).
- Dock and workspace harness from E15; Electron harness from E10.

## Branch
`test/e19-profiles-e2e`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-038, SCR-039
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-110, CMP-183, CMP-184, CMP-188, CMP-199, CMP-227, CMP-228
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (series plugins, LOD, DPR handling)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`
- `qa/plans/e19-profiles-test-plan.md`

2. `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`

- **Axis-alignment helper**: reads rendered row y-positions from the engine debug hook and compares to CMP-188 PriceAxis tick positions within 1 device pixel at three zoom levels and at DPR 1 and 2.
- **Visual regression**: masked snapshots of `SCR-038` in volume, delta, TPO and combined modes, light and dark themes.
- Runs in Chromium and the Electron shell; a WebGL-unavailable run asserts the documented fallback message rather than a blank pane.

**Interfaces you must not break**

title: Performance and load pack for profile compute, WS fan-out and row rendering
body:
## Context
Profiles are the heaviest read surface in R2: up to 5 000 price rows per period, recomputation on every pan in visible-range mode, composite queries reaching into the cold Parquet/DuckDB tier, and a 1 000 ms-cadence WS topic that `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 8 explicitly degrades first under saturation alongside `heatmap`. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` requires recorded numbers against budgets before a train exits; R2 cannot be declared beta on impressions.

The stories carry hard NFRs: full 24 h rebuild <= 1 s, visible-range recompute <= 10 Hz with >= 55 fps interaction, 30-session composite <= 2 s from the cold tier, re-bucket <= 300 ms in a worker, 5 000 rows rendered.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmark** `bench/engine/profile-render.bench.ts`: frame time and fps while panning and zooming with the profile pane open at 500 / 2 000 / 5 000 rows, in volume, delta, TPO and combined modes, at DPR 1 and 2, on the GPU matrix established by the E11/E06 engine baseline. Reports p50/p95/p99 frame time, dropped frames, LOD merge level and GPU memory.
- **Compute benchmark** `bench/profile_engine/`: incremental accumulation throughput (prints/s) at realistic and 10x peak BTCUSDT rates; full 24 h rebuild wall-clock from QuestDB; composite of 5 and 30 sessions from Parquet/DuckDB, cold and warm; re-bucket from `price_grouping` 1 to 50; the cost of the 5 s flush and its effect on ingestion latency.
- **k6 API load script** `load/k6/profile-api.js`: `GET /api/v1/market/profile` with mixed shapes (`split=session|composite|fixed`), concurrency ramped to the R2 target, asserting p95 latency budgets and that bounded-window rejection from `E19-T02` keeps tail latency flat instead of letting one huge query dominate the pool.
- **WS fan-out script** `load/k6/profile-ws.js`: N clients x M symbols subscribed to `profile.{symbol}.{kind}`, verifying the 1 000 ms cadence, coalescing correctness (no lost final state), per-topic sequence continuity, and the documented degradation ladder - at `saturated` the topic drops to 1 000 ms, a `system` notice is emitted and `degraded_topics` names the profile topic.
- **Budget file** `perf/budgets/e19.yaml` encoding every threshold, consumed by CI so a regression fails a job rather than being noticed in a demo.
- **Report** `docs/perf/e19-profiles-report.md`: measured numbers against budgets, hardware matrix, flame-graph highlights and an explicit per-budget verdict (pass, or accepted deviation with owner sign-off and a follow-up ticket).

## Out of scope
- Footprint and heatmap budgets (E18/E21), present here only as background load.
- Optimisation work itself; this ticket measures and files regressions, fixes land on the owning engineering tickets.
- 24 h soak, owned by the E46 performance-hardening epic; scenarios here run <= 60 minutes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Interaction stays smooth at maximum rows
  Given a 5 000-row profile pane docked beside a chart at DPR 2
  When the user pans and zooms continuously for 60 seconds
  Then p95 frame time is within the 55 fps budget and dropped frames stay under the documented threshold, with LOD merging engaged rather than rows dropped

Scenario: Rebuild and composite budgets are met
  When a full 24 h session profile is rebuilt from QuestDB
  Then it completes in under 1 second
  And a 30-session composite served from the cold tier completes in under 2 seconds

Scenario: Failure case - oversized window is rejected, not absorbed
  Given a request whose window exceeds the bounded-window limit
  Then the API rejects it with the documented error and the p95 latency of concurrent well-formed requests is unaffected

Scenario: Degradation ladder behaves as specified
  Given the WS gateway is driven into the saturated state
  Then profile topics are throttled to 1000 ms, a system notice is emitted, degraded_topics names the profile topic, and no sequence gap is introduced

Scenario: Budget regression fails CI
  Given a change that pushes 5 000-row p95 frame time beyond perf/budgets/e19.yaml
  When the benchmark job runs
  Then CI fails and names the violated budget

Scenario: Edge case - re-bucket under peak load
  Given a live session profile receiving peak-rate prints
  When the row size is changed
  Then the worker re-buckets within 300 ms and no print is lost or double counted across the switch
```

## Technical notes / design
- Benchmarks replay a recorded tape at a controlled rate so runs are comparable; injector lag is asserted and a run whose injector falls behind is invalidated rather than reported as a result.
- Reporting uses percentiles and run-to-run variance, never a single best run; minimum three runs per configuration.
- The GPU matrix reuses the machines named in the E11/E06 engine baseline so E19 numbers are directly comparable with the engine's own budgets in `26-chart-engine-design.md`.
- Composite queries are measured cold (page cache dropped) and warm, and both are reported - a warm-only number would hide the Parquet read cost that the 2 s budget exists to bound.
- WS coalescing correctness is validated by comparing the last coalesced frame against the oracle-computed profile at that timestamp, reusing `E19-Q02` fixtures rather than trusting the server's own view.

## Test plan
- Nightly: engine and compute benchmarks on the fixed hardware matrix, results pushed to the trend dashboard.
- Pre-merge: a fast subset (2 000 rows, one mode, one DPR) as a required check on profile paths.
- Pre-R2-exit: the full pack executed once and the report merged - this is the evidence for the R2 performance gate.

## Security notes
- Load scripts refuse any target host not on the allow-list, so accidental production load is structurally prevented.
- Test principals hold `marketdata:read` only; load credentials are short-lived, injected from CI secrets and never committed.
- The oversized-window scenario doubles as a denial-of-service resilience check; any finding is handed to `E19-X02` rather than only recorded as a performance note.

## Accessibility notes
- One configuration is measured with the `SCR-038` table alternative active and a screen reader attached, proving the DOM mirror for up to 5 000 rows does not itself blow the frame budget - virtualisation must be in effect.
- Reduced-motion mode is measured separately so the accessible path is never the slow path.

## Performance notes
- Budgets enforced: 24 h rebuild <= 1 s; visible-range recompute <= 10 Hz with pan-end debounce and >= 55 fps; 30-session composite <= 2 s cold tier; re-bucket <= 300 ms; 5 000 rows renderable; WS cadence 1 000 ms with the documented degradation behaviour.
- Any accepted deviation requires an owner-signed entry in the report plus a follow-up ticket; editing a budget without that trail is forbidden and reviewers are instructed to reject it.

## Observability
- Runs export `profile_rebuild_duration_seconds`, `profile_rows_total`, WS coalesce counters and queue depth, with Grafana snapshots attached to the report.
- Every scenario records commit sha, hardware id and tape id so a number remains reproducible months later.

## Definition of Done
- Scripts and `perf/budgets/e19.yaml` merged; nightly job green; fast subset wired as a required check.
- `docs/perf/e19-profiles-report.md` merged with measured numbers, a verdict per budget, and sign-off from the architect and the order-flow lead.
- A deliberately seeded regression demonstrated to fail the CI budget check.
- Every budget miss has either a filed ticket or a recorded accepted risk with the owner named.

## Dependencies
- `E19-T04` (engine profile plugin, LOD merging), `E19-T03` (WS topic and degradation), `E19-Q02` (oracle for coalescing correctness).
- E17 WS gateway backpressure machinery; E11/E06 benchmark harness and hardware matrix; E16 recorded tapes.

## Branch
`test/e19-profile-perf`

## References
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 8 (throttling, coalescing, backpressure)
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (LOD, instancing, DPR)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 9 NFR lines for US-VP-001..003 and US-VP-009
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-038, SCR-039 performance notes


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
2. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`
3. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`
4. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`
5. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
Base area for `indicators`: packages/chart-engine/src/indicators/ and services/api/orderflow/
- **Engine benchmark** `bench/engine/profile-render.bench.ts`: frame time and fps while panning and zooming with the profile pane open at 500 / 2 000 / 5 000 rows, in volume, delta, TPO and combined modes, at DPR 1 and 2, on the GPU matrix established by the E11/E06 engine baseline. title: Chaos scenarios: feed gaps, store outages, recorder limits and restart recovery
body:
## Context
A profile is a *cumulative* structure: unlike a bar, it never re-derives itself from scratch during normal operation, so any lost, duplicated or out-of-order print silently deforms it for the rest of the period, and the deformation is invisible - the histogram still looks plausible. The planning brief makes chaos and failover testing (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) non-negotiable, and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 specifies the recovery design (5 s flush to QuestDB, rebuild on restart, top-up from trades, invalidation on `metadata_version` bump). That design must be *proven*, not assumed.

This ticket injects the realistic failures of a self-hosted stack - upstream WS drops, Bybit 5xx and rate limits, QuestDB and Parquet/DuckDB unavailability, disk pressure from retention, clock skew and process restarts - and asserts the profile either stays exactly correct or degrades visibly and honestly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/chaos/e19/` scenario pack, each scenario scripted, repeatable and asserted against the `E19-Q02` oracle:
  1. **Upstream WS disconnect mid-session** - drop the exchange trade stream for 30 s and restore; assert the gap is backfilled from REST or explicitly marked, and the final profile equals the uninterrupted oracle run or carries an explicit partial marker.
  2. **Duplicate and out-of-order prints on reconnect** - replay overlapping trade ids; assert idempotent accumulation with no double counting.
  3. **Exchange 5xx and rate-limit 10018 during backfill** - assert bounded retry with backoff, no partial double-application, and a user-visible "partial history" state rather than a wrong-but-confident profile.
  4. **QuestDB unavailable** - during flush and during rebuild; assert the in-RAM period survives a transient outage, that flushes resume without gaps, and that a rebuild attempted during an outage fails loudly with a named error state on `SCR-038`.
  5. **Cold tier (Parquet/DuckDB) unavailable** - composite request degrades to the hot-tier-covered range with the covered range stated, never a silently truncated composite.
  6. **Process restart at hostile moments** - immediately before a flush, mid-flush, and mid-rebuild; assert recovery equals the uninterrupted run.
  7. **Recorder limits and retention eviction** - the requested window extends before `recording_started_at`, or retention evicts data mid-session; assert the "History starts <ts>" empty/partial states and the approximated-from-bars path with the `EstimatedBadge`.
  8. **Clock skew and DST-free anchoring** - server clock steps forward and backward; assert UTC-anchored session boundaries and `funding_8h` anchors do not shift and no period is duplicated or lost.
  9. **WS client-side chaos** - client suspend/resume (laptop sleep), sequence gap, forced resubscribe; assert snapshot+delta re-sync per `23-ws-protocol.md` section 7 leaves the client profile identical to the server's.
  10. **`metadata_version` bump (tick size change) under load** - assert invalidation, rebuild scheduling and no mixed-grid rows served in the interim.
- Each scenario documents: injection method, expected system behaviour, expected user-visible state, and the assertion used (oracle equality, explicit marker, or named error).
- Results recorded in `docs/qa/e19-chaos-results.md` with a verdict per scenario.

## Out of scope
- Chaos for the ingestion layer itself (E16/E13) beyond its effect on profiles; this pack consumes those fault-injection hooks rather than building new ones.
- Order/OMS failover (E45) - no trading surface is involved in R2 profiles.
- Sustained multi-hour soak (E46).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A 30-second feed gap never produces a silently wrong profile
  Given the exchange trade stream drops for 30 seconds mid-session
  When the stream is restored and the gap is backfilled
  Then the resulting profile equals the oracle profile for the full session
  Or the profile is explicitly marked partial for that window with the gap stated

Scenario: Reconnect duplicates are idempotent
  Given the reconnect replays 5 000 trades already accumulated
  When accumulation continues
  Then total volume, per-row volumes and the POC are unchanged from the oracle

Scenario: Failure case - store outage fails loudly
  Given QuestDB is unavailable when a rebuild is requested
  When the user opens SCR-038
  Then a named error state with a retry action is shown and no empty profile is presented as a real one

Scenario: Edge case - restart mid-flush
  Given the process is killed while a 5 second flush is in progress
  When it restarts and tops up from raw trades
  Then the profile equals the uninterrupted run with no duplicated or missing rows

Scenario: Edge case - requested window predates recording
  Given a composite request reaching before recording_started_at
  Then the covered range is stated explicitly, the uncovered portion is either omitted with a partial chip or approximated from bars with the EstimatedBadge, and the POC is computed only over stated data

Scenario: Clock step does not move session boundaries
  Given the server clock steps back 2 seconds and later forward 5 seconds
  Then UTC-anchored and funding_8h session boundaries are unchanged and no period is duplicated or dropped
```

## Technical notes / design
- Injection uses the existing test proxy and container-level controls (pause the QuestDB container, blackhole the cold-tier mount, kill -9 the engine) so scenarios are reproducible in CI and on a developer machine.
- Every scenario ends with the same terminal assertion - oracle equality or an explicit honest marker - which keeps the pack from degenerating into "it did not crash".
- Backfill idempotency is asserted at the trade-id level, because duplicate suppression is the single mechanism protecting every cumulative surface in the product (profiles, footprint, CVD).
- Partial-state semantics are asserted against the exact `SCR-038` copy ("Partial: only N of M requested days recorded", "History starts <ts>") so the UX contract and the backend degrade in step.

## Test plan
- Run nightly in CI against a compose stack, plus once manually before the R2 gate on the staging host, since some faults (disk pressure) are only realistic there.
- Each scenario runs three times; a scenario that passes only sometimes is a failure and gets a bug, not a retry.
- Results feed the R2 exit review alongside `E19-Q04`.

## Security notes
- Fault injection tooling is confined to non-production environments by an allow-list guard; the pack refuses to run against a host without a `staging` or `local` marker.
- The pack includes one negative check that error states never leak internal details (stack traces, store hostnames, SQL) to the browser, per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- Retention-eviction scenarios confirm evicted data is genuinely unreadable afterwards, which is a data-lifecycle (R15) as well as a correctness concern.

## Accessibility notes
- Every degraded state exercised here is asserted to be announced, not merely drawn: partial chips, error states and the approximated badge must be reachable by keyboard and exposed to assistive technology, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- A profile that silently empties is treated as a defect for screen-reader users specifically, since the visual absence of bars carries no announcement.

## Performance notes
- Recovery-time budgets are asserted: rebuild after restart completes within the same <= 1 s budget as a normal 24 h rebuild, and resubscribe re-sync delivers a usable snapshot within the WS reconnect budget from `23-ws-protocol.md`.
- Backfill after a gap must not starve live accumulation; the pack asserts live cadence is maintained during backfill.

## Observability
- Each scenario asserts the expected log events and metric movements (gap detected, backfill started/completed, flush failure, rebuild scheduled, invalidation on `metadata_version`), so operators can diagnose the same fault in production from telemetry alone.
- Missing telemetry for an injected fault is itself a scenario failure, not a nice-to-have.

## Definition of Done
- Scenario pack merged, nightly job green, `docs/qa/e19-chaos-results.md` published with a verdict per scenario.
- Every scenario has an automated assertion; none rely on manual observation.
- Defects found are filed with reproduction scripts referenced from this ticket.
- Reviewed by the order-flow lead, the SDET and DevSecOps (for the injection tooling guard-rails).

## Dependencies
- `E19-T01` (engine, flush, rebuild), `E19-T03` (WS topic, resubscribe), `E19-Q02` (oracle and fixtures).
- Fault-injection hooks from E13/E16 ingestion and recorder; WS reconnect semantics from E17.

`test/e19-profile-chaos`

- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 7 (snapshot+delta, resync), section 9 (heartbeats, revocation), section 10 (errors)

title: HVN / LVN detection with configurable prominence and metric exposure
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-005 — HVN / LVN detection (Should)**. High- and low-volume nodes are where price accelerates or stalls; marking them turns the histogram from a picture into levels. The algorithm is already pinned in `24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2: centred moving-average smoothing over `smoothing_levels` (default 3), HVN = local maximum with raw volume ≥ `hvn_min_pct` (0.5) of POC volume, LVN = local minimum with raw volume ≤ `lvn_max_pct` (0.25) of POC volume, adjacent peaks within `merge_ticks` (default `3 * aggregation_ticks`) merged into the higher. The story's NFR: "detection is deterministic and unit-tested against fixture profiles."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Detection in `ProfileEngine` per §5.2, populating `hvn_ticks` / `lvn_ticks`; served through `include_hvn_lvn` on `GET /market/profile` and the `hvn`/`lvn` arrays of `ProfileUpdate`.
- Sensitivity controls in **SCR-039**: `smoothing_levels`, `hvn_min_pct`, `lvn_max_pct`, `merge_ticks` — raising the threshold yields fewer, more significant nodes.
- Rendering: node markers with labels through the T04 plugin's flags; single-print/LVN highlighting toggle (SCR-038 shows LVN and single prints marked with `*`).
- Metric exposure: HVN/LVN price levels published on the internal metric bus under stable names for **E40** alerts and **E35** rules (US-VP-005 scenario "Exposure").

## Out of scope
- Alert creation on node touches — **E40**.
- Naked POC (**E19-S06**) and TPO single prints as a *TPO* concept (**E19-S08**; this story handles volume-histogram single prints only).
- Automatic node-based support/resistance scoring — not in R2.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Detection
  Then peaks and valleys are marked using the configured prominence threshold, with labels

Scenario: Sensitivity
  When I increase the threshold
  Then fewer, more significant nodes are marked

Scenario: Exposure
  Then HVN/LVN price levels are available as metrics and can trigger alerts

Scenario: Deterministic on a fixture
  Given the committed fixture profiles
  When detection runs repeatedly and on different nodes
  Then the same node sets are produced every time, byte for byte

Scenario: Adjacent peaks merge
  Given two local maxima within merge_ticks of each other
  Then they are reported as one node at the higher of the two, not two adjacent nodes

Scenario: Flat or empty histogram
  Given a period with a single traded level or no trades at all
  Then no nodes are reported and no error is raised
```

## Technical notes / design
Smoothing is applied for **detection only**; the reported node volume is the raw level's, so a node's label never disagrees with the row the user hovers. Detection runs on the same worker/engine pass as POC/VA so a settings change recomputes all three together. Defaults are chosen to be conservative — over-marking is the common failure mode of node detection and makes the feature useless — and the fixture suite includes a deliberately noisy profile to guard against regression toward over-marking.

## Test plan
Unit (≥85%): smoothing, local-extremum detection, threshold filters, merge rule, degenerate histograms. Golden data: committed fixture profiles with expected node sets, asserted exactly. Property-based: raising `hvn_min_pct` never increases the HVN count (monotonicity). E2E: sensitivity change reduces marks; metric names appear on the metric bus. Visual: golden images with node markers in both themes.

## Security notes
Sensitivity parameters are numeric and bounded server-side; no new endpoint. Metrics are read-only market data under `marketdata:read`.

## Accessibility notes
Nodes are marked with a glyph and a text label ("HVN 63,020"), never colour alone, and appear as a flagged column in the table alternative so a screen-reader user gets the same level list. Sensitivity controls are labelled with units and their effect described in the field help ("higher = fewer, more significant nodes").

## Performance notes
Detection is O(levels) over an already-materialised histogram and runs inside the existing POC/VA pass — no measurable addition to the ≤ 8 ms viewport budget; measured in the B-profile benchmark with detection enabled.

## Observability
`profile_node_detection_duration_ms`, `profile_nodes_detected{type=hvn|lvn}`; analytics `profile.node_sensitivity_changed`, `profile.nodes_toggled`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests; fixture node sets asserted exactly.
- [ ] Monotonicity property test green.
- [ ] Metric names published and referenced by the E40 backlog item.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% engine; axe-core green; design-qa sign-off; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E19-S04** (POC volume is the reference for both thresholds). Blocks **E19-S06**.

`feat/e19-hvn-lvn`

title: Naked / virgin POC tracking with server-side tested state and clutter limit
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-006 — Naked / virgin POC tracking (Should)**: prior sessions' POCs carried forward as targets until price trades through them. The NFR is unusual and drives the design: "state maintained **server-side** so it is consistent across panes and users." `24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2 specifies the lifecycle: maintained incrementally, on every bar close any naked POC inside the bar's `[low, high]` flips to `tested` with `tested_at`; retained for `naked_poc_lookback_periods` (default 20); rendered as horizontal rays. The `naked_poc` boolean already exists in both the REST `ProfileResponse` and the WS `ProfileUpdate`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Server-side naked-POC registry per `(env, symbol)`: prior-period POCs with `tested`/`tested_at`, updated on every bar close, rebuilt deterministically from recorded history on restart.
- Retention: `naked_poc_lookback_periods` (default 20) and a **clutter limit** — only the nearest N to current price are drawn (configurable), with an explicit count of hidden ones (US-VP-006 scenario "Limit clutter").
- Rendering: horizontal rays from the originating session forward to current price; tested POCs visually **demoted** rather than deleted, with a history toggle.
- Exposure: `naked_poc` on profile payloads plus naked-POC levels on the metric bus for **E40**/**E35**.
- Backfill: on first enablement for a symbol, naked POCs are computed from recorded sessions within the look-back and the covered range is stated where history is short.

## Out of scope
- Alerting on a naked-POC touch — **E40** consumes the exposed levels.
- Naked VAH/VAL and other untested-level families — not in R2.
- Cross-symbol or higher-timeframe composite naked POCs.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Carry forward
  Then each prior session's POC is drawn as a level until price trades through it

Scenario: Flip on retest
  When price trades through a naked POC
  Then it is marked tested and visually demoted, retaining a history toggle

Scenario: Limit clutter
  Given more than N naked POCs exist
  Then only the nearest N to current price are drawn, configurable, with a count of hidden ones

Scenario: State is shared, not per-pane
  Given two panes and two users viewing the same symbol
  Then both see the identical naked/tested state at the same instant

Scenario: Restart is deterministic
  Given the service restarts
  When the registry is rebuilt from recorded history
  Then the naked/tested state is identical to the pre-restart state

Scenario: History too short to back-fill
  Given the recorder covers fewer sessions than the look-back
  Then naked POCs are computed from what exists and the covered range is stated explicitly
```

## Technical notes / design
Server-side state is the whole point: a client-side implementation would drift between panes and between users, and the level would "untest" itself on reload. The registry is a small per-symbol structure persisted alongside profile flushes, and the flip check is O(naked count) per bar close — trivial. A POC is tested when a bar's `[low, high]` **covers** it, not merely when a trade prints at it, matching the textbook definition and the §5.2 wording. Clutter limiting is a render-time selection over the full server-side set, so raising N reveals existing levels instantly without a refetch.

## Test plan
Unit (≥85%): flip rule incl. exact-touch boundary (bar low == POC), look-back eviction, nearest-N selection, hidden count. Integration: multi-session fixture with a POC tested three sessions later; restart rebuild equality; short-history backfill. E2E: two panes observe the same flip; history toggle. Visual: golden images of naked vs tested rays, both themes.

## Security notes
Shared server-side state is read-only market data with no per-user component, so there is no cross-user leakage concern; it is exposed under `marketdata:read` like every other `/market/*` surface. The registry is bounded by `naked_poc_lookback_periods` per symbol, so it cannot grow without limit.

## Accessibility notes
Naked and tested rays differ in line style and carry text labels ("naked POC 63,020" / "POC 62,410 — tested 2026-09-12"), not colour alone. The hidden-count is text ("4 more naked POCs above"), and the table alternative lists every naked POC with its state and origin session. The history toggle is a labelled switch.

## Performance notes
O(naked count) per bar close (≤20 by default); render cost is a handful of lines within the existing ≤3 text draw-call budget; no additional network traffic (levels ride on the existing profile payload).

## Observability
`profile_naked_poc_count{symbol}`, `profile_naked_poc_flips_total`, `profile_naked_registry_rebuild_duration_ms`; analytics `profile.naked_poc_toggled`, `profile.naked_poc_limit_changed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Restart-determinism test green.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% engine / ≥80% frontend; axe-core green; design-qa sign-off; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E19-S05** (shares the level-marking render path and the metric-exposure pattern); transitively **E19-S04** for POC. Blocks nothing in E19; consumed by **E40**.

`feat/e19-naked-poc`

## References

title: Profile settings dialog and presets shared across instances (SCR-039)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-009 — Profile panel settings & presets (Must)**. Nine stories' worth of knobs are worthless if switching analysis style takes a dozen clicks; the story's value is that one preset switches "period type, row size, value area %, VWAP overlay and node marking" together. The NFR extends it to the workspace layer: "presets stored per user and included in workspace export." The surface is **SCR-039 Profile settings dialog**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-039** modal implementing the full SCR-038 settings list plus per-period colouring, "extend POC/VA lines to the right", "show developing VA" and composite period anchors: components **CMP-006** RadioGroup, **CMP-008** NumericStepperInput, **CMP-031** ColorSwatch/ThemeChip, **CMP-040** FormField, **CMP-043** Dialog, **CMP-065** FormSection, **CMP-228** PreviewTile.
- Live preview tile reflecting the pending settings before apply.
- Presets: save current settings as a named preset, apply to any profile instance for any symbol, rename/delete; shipped defaults incl. "session value".
- Persistence per user (workspace/pane settings payload per `21-database-schema.md` §3.8 `pane_settings` / `indicator_instances`) and inclusion in workspace export/import.
- Validation per SCR-039: VA % 1–100 in the UI clamped to the API's 50–95 with an explanatory message; custom range end after start; look-back longer than recorded history **warns** rather than blocks; row size smaller than tick size clamped to one tick with an explanation (US-VP-009 scenario).
- Reset-to-defaults.

## Out of scope
- The underlying computations each setting drives (owned by S01–S08).
- Global app settings and hotkeys — **SCR-110/111**, E-settings.
- Sharing presets between users — collaboration, R5.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preset applied
  When I apply the "session value" preset
  Then period type, row size, value area %, VWAP overlay and node marking all switch together

Scenario: Save preset
  When I save current settings as a preset
  Then it is available to all profile instances for any symbol

Scenario: Invalid row size
  When the row size is smaller than the instrument tick size
  Then it is clamped to one tick with an explanatory message

Scenario: Look-back exceeds recorded history
  When a composite look-back longer than the recorded history is chosen
  Then a warning is shown and the dialog still applies, producing a profile that states its covered range

Scenario: Preview before apply
  Given pending changes in the dialog
  Then the preview tile reflects them and cancelling restores the previous settings exactly

Scenario: Presets survive export/import
  Given a workspace containing presets is exported and imported on another machine
  Then every preset reappears with identical values
```

## Technical notes / design
Settings are a single validated object per profile instance; a preset is that object minus instance-specific bindings (symbol, anchor timestamps), which is what makes "available for any symbol" true by construction. Re-bucketing on apply is worker-local (SCR-039 perf note: ≤ 300 ms from cached raw data) so the dialog feels instant and only a period change hits the network. UI-vs-API validation ranges deliberately differ (VA % 1–100 in the dialog per SCR-039, 50–95 at the API per OpenAPI): the dialog clamps and explains rather than silently accepting a value the server will reject.

## Test plan
Unit: settings schema validation, clamping and warning logic, preset serialisation, preview diffing, cancel-restores-exactly. E2E: apply a preset and assert every dependent control changed; save/rename/delete a preset; row-size clamp message; look-back warning; workspace export/import round-trip. Visual: golden images of the dialog in both themes. a11y: axe-core plus a keyboard-only traversal of the whole dialog.

## Security notes
Presets are per-user rows scoped by owner; a user cannot read or apply another user's preset (enforced server-side on the workspace/settings endpoints, not just by the UI). Imported workspace payloads are schema-validated and size-bounded before persistence — an imported workspace is untrusted input and is the injection vector worth guarding here. No secrets are ever stored in a preset.

## Accessibility notes
Grouped form controls with units in the label ("Value area %", "Row size (ticks)"); the mode selector is a radio group; each section has a description explaining what it changes. Focus is trapped in the dialog and returns to the invoking control on close; Esc cancels. Validation messages are associated with their fields and announced; warnings are distinguishable from errors by text, not colour. The preview tile has a text summary alternative.

## Performance notes
Row-size and period changes re-bucket from cached raw data in a worker in ≤ 300 ms for a session-length profile; composite look-backs show progress rather than blocking (SCR-039). Dialog open ≤ 80 ms.

## Observability
Analytics `profile.settings_changed{key}`, `profile.preset_applied{name}`, `profile.preset_saved`, `profile.settings_reset`. Metric `ui_profile_rebucket_duration_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Workspace export/import round-trip test green.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend; axe-core green; keyboard-only and screen-reader pass on the dialog.
- [ ] Golden images approved; design-qa sign-off against the SCR-039 checklist; demoed.

`blocked_by`: **E19-S02** (period types to configure), **E19-S04** (VA settings). Related: **E19-S03**, **E19-S05**, **E19-S08** contribute controls; the dialog degrades gracefully when the TPO flag is off.
