title: Golden-fixture parity harness: strip values vs offline DuckDB recompute
body:
## Context
R2 exit criterion #6 is explicit: "Footprint, profile, CVD and Deep-Stats values match an independent offline recomputation (DuckDB over the Parquet tier) for a full recorded symbol-day, within floating-point tolerance." The R2 quality-gate table reinforces it: "Golden-fixture tests: one recorded symbol-day with expected footprint/profile/CVD/Deep-Stats outputs version-controlled; any drift fails CI". This Task builds E20's half of that harness. It is the single strongest defence against the epic's headline risk (R7 Data accuracy): a strip that is beautiful, fast, accessible and **wrong** is worse than no strip, because the trader will act on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- An independent recomputation of every Deep-Stats row in SQL over the Parquet cold tier via DuckDB, using the documented views (`21-database-schema.md` §cold tier: `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW footprint_cells AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet(...)` and the equivalent trades view). **Independent** means written from the definitions in `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 by someone not implementing `DeepStatsEngine`, not a port of the engine code — a shared bug would otherwise pass silently.
- A version-controlled golden fixture: one full recorded symbol-day (BTCUSDT, the R2 reference day) with expected per-bar values for every row, stored under `tests/fixtures/e20/` with a documented provenance record (symbol, date, recording session id, bar type, param, tick size, `qty_step`).
- A CI job comparing engine output against the golden fixture bar-for-bar with a documented floating-point tolerance, failing the build on drift and reporting the first N divergent bars with both values.
- A comparison of the three serving tiers (engine hot state, QuestDB warm, Parquet cold) so a value does not change depending on where it was read from.
- A regeneration script with a deliberate guard: regenerating the golden fixture requires an explicit flag and produces a diff summary for review, so a real regression cannot be laundered into a "fixture update".

## Out of scope
- Footprint, profile and CVD golden fixtures (E18, E19, E23 own theirs; this harness shares their fixture day and infrastructure where it already exists).
- Frontend rendering correctness (E20-Q02 covers that at the E2E layer).
- Performance measurement (E20-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A full symbol-day agrees
  Given the recorded BTCUSDT reference day
  When the engine output and the DuckDB recomputation are compared for every bar and every Deep-Stats row
  Then 100% of values agree within the documented tolerance

Scenario: Drift fails the build
  Given a deliberately introduced sign error in the aggressor mapping
  When the CI parity job runs
  Then the job fails and names the affected metric and the first divergent bar with both values

Scenario: All three tiers agree
  Given the same 500-bar window is served from engine state, from QuestDB and from the Parquet tier
  Then the Deep-Stats values are identical across the three

Scenario: Fixture updates are deliberate
  When the golden fixture is regenerated without the explicit regeneration flag
  Then the script refuses and prints the diff summary instead of overwriting
```

## Technical notes / design
- Tolerance is documented per metric family, not global: exact equality for counts (`bar_trade_count`, `bar_buy_trade_count`, `bar_sell_trade_count`, `bar_range_ticks`), fixed-point exact for volumes and deltas, and a stated relative tolerance only for ratios (`delta_pct`, `bar_avg_trade_size`, `bar_volume_imbalance_ratio`) where division introduces representation error.
- The reference day must include at least one `recording_gaps` row so the harness proves the "partial history" behaviour rather than only the happy path (`21-database-schema.md`: every query over a range intersecting a gap must render the partial-history state).
- The SQL lives under `tests/parity/e20/*.sql` with one file per metric, each carrying the §7 definition as a comment header so a reviewer can check SQL against spec without opening another document.

## Test plan
This Task *is* test infrastructure. Its own correctness is verified by mutation: a set of seeded faults (aggressor swap, off-by-one bar boundary, wrong `qty_step` in the `delta_pct` denominator, dropped final trade of a bar) must each be caught by the harness; a fault that passes is a harness bug. Runtime target: the full-day parity job completes in <=10 minutes so it can run on every PR touching M9.

## Security notes
The harness reads recorded market data only. The fixture must be checked for accidental inclusion of account-identifying data before being committed (the recorded tape is public market data, but the provenance record must not embed a recording session's account context). Fixture files are committed with Git LFS if they exceed the repository size policy.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Parity job runtime <=10 minutes on CI hardware; it runs on PRs touching M9 and nightly on `main`. The DuckDB recomputation reads the Parquet tier directly and must not query QuestDB, so it cannot be slowed by, or interfere with, live ingestion.

## Observability
CI job emits a structured summary (rows compared, metrics compared, max observed deviation per metric) retained as a build artefact, so a slow drift toward the tolerance edge is visible before it becomes a failure.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified, including the seeded-fault mutation set.
- [ ] Golden fixture and provenance record committed; regeneration guard in place.
- [ ] CI job wired to PRs touching M9 and to the nightly build; runtime within budget.
- [ ] `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` updated with the parity harness entry if it establishes a new pattern.
- [ ] Reviewed by QA/SDET and the order-flow code owner; PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E20-T01` (there must be engine output to compare against) and `E20-T02` (the harness compares the **served** payload, not just in-process engine state). Moved to Sprint 12 to stay after T01's corrected Sprint-11 placement. Shares the recorded reference day with E18-T06/E19/E23 parity work; if that fixture day does not yet exist, this ticket creates it and the other epics adopt it.

title: ADR-0016 Deep-Stats rendering strategy and docs update

This Task writes it and reconciles the plan docs with what actually shipped, which the Epic DoD requires ("docs reflect final shipped behavior, not the original proposal").

title: Security review of the Deep-Stats export path and abuse-case testing
body:
## Context
E20's only meaningful security surface is the CSV export introduced by US-DS-005 and built in E20-S04. `04-security-program.md` rates the related programme threats highly: **S3** (elevation of privilege — "Replay/export endpoint used to read arbitrary filesystem paths", High) with control **SR-097** ("Replay, export and import endpoints MUST NOT accept filesystem paths; datasets are addressed by registry ids. Path traversal and symlink escape tests are mandatory"), and **S4** (information disclosure via export) with control **SR-098** ("Exports MUST be role-scoped, watermarked with the exporting identity and timestamp, and audited"). **SR-158** requires security acceptance criteria on every ticket touching data export. This ticket is the white-box review and the executed abuse cases that verify those controls actually hold in the built system, rather than merely appearing in a ticket body.

Note the sequencing: this ticket is scheduled alongside E20-S04 and **blocks** it, because the role-scoping and abuse-case definitions must be settled before the export control ships, not audited after.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box code review** of the export path end to end: request validation, role resolution, range bounding, chunking, cancellation, artefact lifecycle, download URL issuance via `GET /jobs/{id}`, watermark composition, and audit-record emission.
- **Executed abuse cases** from the E20-X01 model, each with recorded evidence:
  1. Viewer-role session attempts an export beyond its role → refused server-side (not merely hidden in the UI).
  2. Manager attempts to retrieve another user's export artefact by job id → refused.
  3. Path traversal and symlink escape attempts against the download mechanism → impossible by construction, asserted by test (SR-097).
  4. Over-broad range request → rejected with an explicit error, not silently truncated.
  5. Many concurrent export requests from one session → bounded by the documented concurrency limit; the service remains responsive.
  6. Cancel mid-export then attempt to download → no artefact reachable, and the cancellation is audited.
  7. Hostile chart-template payload (unknown row ids, oversized row list, deeply nested jsonb) → rejected at write-time validation without breaking chart load for the user (tampering case from E20-X01).
  8. Malformed WS footprint frame → dropped and surfaced as stale data; no fabricated value rendered.
- **Verification of the audit trail**: each export attempt produces a record naming actor, symbol, range, row set and outcome; records are append-only and survive the retention policy.
- **Watermark verification**: the exported file carries the exporting identity and timestamp in a form that survives opening in a spreadsheet application (a watermark only visible in a hex editor is not a control).
- **SAST/DAST/SCA confirmation** for the touched code: Semgrep/Bandit rules green or triaged, `pip-audit`/`npm audit` clean or triaged, and a ZAP pass over the new endpoint; a Semgrep rule added if the review finds a pattern worth preventing programme-wide.
- Findings triaged: fixed, or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded.

## Out of scope
- The threat model itself (E20-X01).
- Penetration testing (R4, E43) and audit-log infrastructure (E42).
- Security review of footprint, profiles, DOM ladder or replay (each owns its own; the R2 security gate names E26 and E21 specifically).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Role scoping is enforced where it counts
  Given a viewer-role session with the UI control bypassed
  When it calls the export endpoint directly for data beyond its role
  Then the server refuses the request
  And the refusal is audited

Scenario: No path reaches the filesystem
  When the download mechanism is reviewed and tested with traversal and symlink payloads
  Then no user-supplied value reaches a filesystem path
  And the SR-097 mandatory traversal and symlink tests are present and passing

Scenario: Exports are attributable
  When any export completes
  Then the file carries the exporting identity and timestamp legibly when opened in a spreadsheet application
  And an append-only audit record exists naming actor, symbol, range, row set and outcome

Scenario: Resource abuse is bounded
  Given repeated over-broad and concurrent export requests
  Then each over-broad request is rejected with an explicit error
  And concurrency is bounded by the documented limit with the service remaining responsive

Scenario: Cancellation leaves nothing behind
  When an export is cancelled mid-run
  Then no artefact is reachable by its job id
  And the cancellation is audited

Scenario: Hostile configuration is rejected safely
  When a template with unknown row ids and an oversized row list is written
  Then the write is rejected with a validation error
  And the user's existing chart configuration still loads
```

## Technical notes / design
- The review must confirm enforcement is **server-side**: a UI that hides the export control is a usability feature, never a security control, and the review explicitly tests with the UI bypassed.
- Artefact lifecycle: download URLs should be single-purpose and expiring; the review records the chosen lifetime and whether it is enforced.
- The watermark is a header comment block in the CSV; the review confirms it survives a spreadsheet round trip rather than being silently stripped.

## Test plan
- Security integration tests committed alongside the findings so each abuse case becomes a permanent regression test, not a one-off manual check.
- SR-097's traversal/symlink tests are mandatory and must exist even though the endpoint accepts no path — they assert the absence of the capability.
- RBAC negative tests per role for both the export endpoint and the market-data read path.
- SAST/SCA/DAST evidence attached to the ticket.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security review, required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 for any ticket carrying the `security` label and by SR-158 for anything touching data export. Data classification: market data, internal — but attributable and audited on export. Step-up re-authentication (SR-025) is confirmed as not applicable and the reasoning is recorded, consistent with E20-X01's negative findings.

## Accessibility notes
Confirms that the insufficient-role state is explained in text so the security control degrades accessibly — a user who cannot export learns why rather than encountering an unexplained disabled control.

## Performance notes
The concurrency and range limits are set with reference to the export throughput measured in E20-S04, so the bound is protective rather than arbitrary; the review records the numbers.

## Observability
Verifies the SR-125-relevant events are emitted and alertable: RBAC refusals on the market-data path, export failures, template-validation rejections, and export concurrency at the limit.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] White-box review completed with notes recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] All eight abuse cases executed with evidence; each converted into a committed regression test.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/DAST results clean or triaged with dispositions.
- [ ] All findings fixed, or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment present on this ticket and on E20-S04.
- [ ] `docs/security/threat-models/e20-deep-stats.md` residual-risk column updated to post-implementation values.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

title: E2E suite additions for SCR-050 and SCR-051
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` puts E2E on Playwright for both web and Electron and uses Playwright visual snapshots (`maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01`) for chart-engine pixel diffs — explicitly including heatmap frames. This Task builds the durable automated suite for this Epic so the R2 regression pack and every later release re-verify the surface without human effort.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/dom-heatmap/` Playwright specs, running in both the browser target and the Electron shell:
  - ladder renders and updates live; rows carry correct values against the fixture;
  - keyboard traversal: focus the grid, arrow through rows, assert roving tabindex and announced names via the DOM mirror; `Enter` opens the row action menu;
  - sequence gap → "Book resynchronising" → recovery;
  - stale feed → dim + "Book stale 3 s" + disabled affordances;
  - heatmap renders; legend states the active convention; convention inversion propagates;
  - empty state on an unrecorded symbol, including the start-recording affordance's RBAC variants;
  - depth tier change → resubscribe + rebuild state; forced shedding → notice + restoration;
  - trail clamp message names the correct maximum for the active tier;
  - backfill: progress, partial-history boundary, cancel-on-symbol-switch with no further network activity;
  - SCR-051: every validation boundary, persistence across reload, reset-to-defaults.
- **Golden visual frames** for the heatmap layer per theme and palette, captured against SwiftShader for determinism, wired as a required check.
- Deterministic fixture harness: a WS mock that replays recorded book/heatmap frames with controllable gaps, stalls and connection-quality transitions.
- CI wiring: suite runs on every PR touching `area/order-flow` or `area/chart-engine`, and nightly in full.

## Out of scope
Perf measurement (E21-Q03), chaos (E21-Q04), a11y audit depth (E21-Q05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Suite covers the automated half of the plan
  Then every case marked "automated" in docs/qa/plans/e21-dom-heatmap.md has a corresponding Playwright test id

Scenario: Deterministic visuals
  Given the golden heatmap frames are re-captured on an unchanged build
  Then the pixel diff is within maxDiffPixelRatio 0.01 across three consecutive runs

Scenario: Both runtimes
  Then the suite passes in the browser target and in the Electron shell, and a failure in either fails CI

Scenario: No flaky waits
  Then no test uses an unconditional sleep; all waits are on observable conditions, and the suite passes 10 consecutive nightly runs without a flake
```

## Technical notes / design
The WS mock speaks the real protocol (binary kinds 1/2/6 via `packages/protocol`), so the suite also acts as a de facto client-side contract test. Time is controlled via the mock's frame clock rather than the system clock so cadence assertions are stable in CI.

## Test plan
This *is* test code; its own quality gates are the flake budget above and a review by the Epic's FE lead.

## Security notes
Fixtures contain no real account data; the RBAC variants use seeded test users with distinct scopes so the own-order scoping assertions are meaningful.

## Accessibility notes
Keyboard and announcement assertions are first-class tests here, not a separate audit — the audit (E21-Q05) goes deeper, but the regressions are caught by this suite.

## Performance notes
The suite must stay inside the CI time budget; heavy visual capture runs nightly, smoke runs per PR.

## Observability
Suite emits a JUnit report plus the visual diff artefacts to the CI run so a failure is diagnosable without re-running locally.

title: Performance and load scripts for the heatmap cadence and book fan-out
body:
## Context
Two of the standard's **hard gates** live on this surface: budget #1 (≤16.6 ms/frame with 100k bars + 200-depth heatmap at 100 ms) and budget #14 (100 ms cadence sustained, ≤1 dropped/coalesced frame per 10 s). `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7 also requires the engine benchmark to be a **built-in headless harness** with a seeded synthetic dataset, not ad hoc DevTools profiling, and §9's playbook forbids "open the profiler and guess" as a first step — which only works if stage-attributed frame markers are recorded.

E21-K01 produced the exploratory numbers; this Task turns them into permanent, automated, regression-detecting measurement.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Promote the K01 harness into `packages/chart-engine/bench/` as a supported benchmark mode: seeded 100k bars + synthetic 200-depth heatmap stream + footprint density, scripted pans/zooms/overlay toggles for 5 minutes, per-stage frame markers matching §4.3's breakdown (data decode, model update, cull/batch, GL calls, heatmap texture upload ≤2 ms).
- Outputs p50/p95/p99 overall and per stage, pass/fail against budgets #1/#2/#14, plus a stage-attribution report.
- **k6/Locust WS profile** for the backend side: realistic peak (10 recorded symbols, 5 users, heatmap open on ≥2 symbols) and worst case (all symbols charted everywhere, heatmap+footprint+profile active, plus a 5× volatility burst for 60 s), asserting budget #6 (≤20 ms p95 backend-added latency) and budget #3 (WS tick→screen p95 <100 ms for the heaviest topic set — the R2 hard gate named in `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3).
- Ingestion soak assertion for budget #5 (zero dropped messages on `orderbook.200` over 24 h) restricted to this Epic's topics.
- CI integration: benchmark runs on every PR touching the engine or order-flow packages with a regression threshold; the full load profile runs on the release candidate.
- Results recorded into the PRR evidence pack (`07-release-and-prr.md`).

## Out of scope
Fixing regressions (the owning Story's job); E46's product-wide perf hardening in R5; chaos (E21-Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budgets measured, not asserted by hand
  Then a single command produces p50/p95/p99 frame time per stage and a pass/fail verdict against budgets #1 and #14

Scenario: Regression detection
  Given a change increases heatmap texture upload time beyond its 2 ms slice
  Then CI fails and the report names the stage that regressed, without requiring a manual profiling session

Scenario: Backend fan-out under realistic peak
  Given the realistic-peak profile runs for 30 minutes
  Then backend-added latency p95 is <=20 ms and WS tick-to-screen p95 is <100 ms for the heaviest topic set

Scenario: Worst case degrades per policy
  Given the worst-case profile with a 5x burst
  Then the app sheds per ADR-0016 order, the shedding is recorded in metrics, and no message loss is observed beyond detected-and-healed gaps
```

## Technical notes / design
Reference hardware per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1; the synthetic dataset is version-controlled and generated from a seed so results are comparable run to run. Frame markers use `Performance.mark()` correlated with the engine's own instrumentation. Backend spans are OpenTelemetry, so the stage-attribution story is symmetrical on both sides.

## Test plan
Self-validating: the harness is verified by deliberately injecting a known 5 ms delay into the upload path and asserting the report attributes it to the correct stage.

## Security notes
Load scripts run only against demo/staging, never live (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8). Credentials for the load profile come from the CI secret store and are scoped test users — never owner credentials. The worst-case profile is itself a DoS-shaped workload: it must be rate-limited to the staging environment and must not be runnable against a production target by configuration accident (enforced by an environment guard in the script).

## Accessibility notes
The benchmark must run with the accessible DOM mirror enabled in at least one configuration, so a11y machinery cost is measured rather than assumed free (a K01 finding requirement).

## Performance notes
This ticket is the enforcement mechanism for every performance claim in this Epic.

## Observability
Publishes benchmark results as CI artefacts and pushes key numbers to the metrics backend so trend regressions are visible between releases.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass with an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Coverage: test assets committed; any new automation counted toward the package's coverage where it executes product code.

title: Chaos scenarios: desync storms, slow consumers and exchange failures
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` requires chaos/failover tests (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) re-run every release, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4 names E21's own failure surface. The DOM/heatmap is where feed pathologies become visible fastest, which makes it the right place to prove the recovery behaviours rather than discovering them in production.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos harness scenarios, each with a defined expected user-visible outcome and a defined recovery time:
  1. **Sequence-gap storm** — repeated gaps at 1/s for 60 s: book must resync each time, the ladder must show the resync state, heatmap columns must be marked estimated, and no unbounded memory growth may occur.
  2. **Crossed book** injected via a malformed delta: treated as desync, never clamped.
  3. **Upstream WS disconnect** for 30 s: reconnect with backoff, subscriptions restored in priority order, time-to-usable ≤5 s after reconnect.
  4. **Exchange 5xx / rate-limit 10018** on the REST resync path: retries with backoff, user told, no silent stale book.
  5. **Slow consumer**: a client that stops reading — server queue must stay bounded, connection classified `lagging`→`saturated`, heatmap degraded to 1 000 ms, `degraded_topics` announced, and ultimately the documented `slow_consumer` close rather than server memory growth.
  6. **Recorder outage** mid-session: heatmap live continues, backfill reports unavailability honestly.
  7. **GPU context loss**: trail restored from CPU stores; if WebGL2 is unavailable, the documented placeholder appears.
  8. **Clock skew / stalled engine**: `samples=0` columns and the grey-stripe rendering, with `heatmap_missing_columns_total` alerting above 1%/min.
- Each scenario scripted, repeatable, and wired into the release chaos run.

## Out of scope
Fixing discovered defects (filed as Bugs); OMS/trading chaos (E45).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bounded server memory under a slow consumer
  Given a subscribed client stops reading for 5 minutes
  Then server memory attributable to that connection stays bounded, the connection is classified and degraded per protocol,
  and it is closed with the documented slow_consumer reason rather than growing without limit

Scenario: Desync storm recovery
  Given sequence gaps are injected once per second for 60 seconds
  Then the ladder shows the resync state for each, the heatmap marks affected columns estimated,
  and after the storm ends the book is correct within one snapshot interval

Scenario: Honest degradation
  Given any of the eight scenarios runs
  Then the user-visible state names what is wrong and what still works, and no scenario results in silently stale data presented as live

Scenario: Repeatability
  Then each scenario can be re-run by a single documented command and produces the same classification of outcome
```

## Technical notes / design
Fault injection sits at the fixture/WS-mock layer and at the exchange-adapter boundary, so no production code paths are modified to be testable beyond existing seams. Memory assertions use the same per-symbol accounting as budget #8.

## Test plan
Scenarios are the tests; each has a machine-checkable assertion (metric threshold, state string, recovery time) rather than a human judgement.

## Security notes
Scenario 5 is a direct test of the **DoS vector named for this Epic** (`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4: unbounded subscription depth) and of protocol goal G4 ("a slow or backgrounded client can never grow server memory"). Scenario 4 verifies that an upstream failure cannot be used to keep a stale book on screen — a market-manipulation-adjacent trust issue, not just a UX one. Findings feed E21-X01's STRIDE model.

## Accessibility notes
Every degraded state exercised here must be announced via `role="status"` and readable in greyscale — asserted, not assumed.

## Performance notes
Recovery-time targets: ≤5 s time-to-usable after a 30 s outage (SCR-152 performance note); book correct within one snapshot interval after a storm.

## Observability
Scenarios assert on `book_desync_total`, `heatmap_missing_columns_total`, `ws_slow_consumer_closures_total`, `dom_shedding_events_total` — if a scenario cannot be observed in metrics, that is itself a finding.

- [ ] Coverage: test assets committed; any new automation counted toward the package's coverage where it executes product code.

title: Accessibility audit of the ladder grid, heatmap reveal and settings dialog

## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion 10 requires "a11y pass on every new view incl. keyboard-navigable footprint cells and **DOM ladder**" before R2 completes, and `05-accessibility-standard.md` refuses any density exemption for this surface. This is the deepest a11y work in the Epic: axe-core alone cannot verify a windowed accessible tree over a WebGL texture, so manual screen-reader passes are mandatory.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated**: axe-core zero serious/critical on SCR-050 and SCR-051 in dark, light and high-contrast themes at 100/112/125/150% font scale and 200% browser zoom.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with NVDA (Windows/Electron) and VoiceOver (macOS): ladder traversal, row announcement fidelity, row action menu, own-order announcement, windowed heatmap reveal, data-table alternative including its live-patch behaviour and the "no longer in view" banner, settings dialog completion end to end.
- **Keyboard-only** completion of every user journey on both screens, including recentring, depth change, trail change, scale lock, backfill cancel, and the region-cycling entry/exit (`Ctrl+\`).
- **Target size** verification (≥24 px) for ladder rows at each density, with the documented essential-exception reasoning where applicable.
- **Colour independence** verification of every encoding (bid/ask, own order, estimated, stale, degraded) including the three CVD simulations and a greyscale pass.
- **Contrast matrix** across every heatmap ramp stop and every text pair, produced by the automated token script, ≥3:1 for chart data-ink and ≥4.5:1 for text.
- **Reduced-motion** pass against the E21-D05 spec.
- Findings logged with WCAG SC references and severity; blocking findings must be fixed before the Epic is Done; the rest feed E47.

## Out of scope
Remediation (filed against the owning Stories); the R5 full-product conformance audit and VPAT (E47).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated gate
  Then axe-core reports zero serious or critical violations on SCR-050 and SCR-051 across all themes and zoom levels tested

Scenario: Screen-reader parity
  Given a screen-reader user without sight of the canvas
  Then they can determine the best bid and ask, the size at any price level, whether they have an order at a level,
  and the liquidity history at a level, using only announced content

Scenario: No colour-only information
  Then in greyscale and in all three CVD simulations, bid vs ask, own orders, estimated data, stale state and degraded state
  all remain unambiguous

Scenario: Keyboard completeness
  Then every journey on both screens completes with the keyboard alone, with no trap and with visible focus at every step

Scenario: Blocking findings
  Given a serious violation is found
  Then it is filed against the owning Story and the Epic cannot reach Done until it is resolved or formally accepted by the CDO
```

## Technical notes / design
The windowed-reveal and table-alternative checks must be performed with live data flowing, because the standard's live-patch rule (values patched in place, node identity preserved, focus and sort preserved) is exactly where naive implementations break under a screen reader.

## Test plan
The audit is the test; its durable output is a set of assertions added to E21-Q02 so each verified behaviour is protected by automation afterwards.

## Security notes
Confirm that degraded/stale/demo-live safety signals are perceivable through non-visual channels — a screen-reader user must not be able to mistake a frozen book for a live one (SR-038's accessible corollary).

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA criteria referenced per finding; this ticket is the Epic's a11y DoD evidence.

## Performance notes
Measure the cost of the accessible machinery while auditing: if maintaining the mirror pushes frame time out of budget, that is a finding for E21-T05, not a reason to weaken the mirror.

N/A; findings tracked as issues.

title: Exploratory charter and regression pack for the order-flow DOM surface
body:
## Context
Scripted cases find the failures we predicted; a timeboxed exploratory charter finds the ones we did not. This surface is unusually rich in emergent behaviour because three independent clocks (book cadence, heatmap bucket, render frame) and two degradation controllers interact — combinations no test plan enumerates exhaustively.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (4 × 90 minutes, session-based test management, notes recorded):
  1. "Fight the two controllers": force client shedding and server saturation into conflict in every order and combination; hunt for contradictory messaging, oscillation and stuck states.
  2. "Time travel": change bucket, trail, depth and symbol rapidly and in unusual orders during backfill and resync; hunt for state leakage between symbols and for columns landing on the wrong time axis.
  3. "Extremes": zero-liquidity book, one-sided book, a single dominant wall, an instrument with an unusual tick size, 500-depth with the smallest bucket at the largest trail.
  4. "Long run": 4-hour unattended session with periodic interaction; hunt for memory growth, trail drift and accumulating estimated columns.
- Each charter produces: findings, new regression cases for the pack, and any risk-register updates.
- **Regression pack** assembled for R2 and beyond: the subset of E21-Q02's automated suite plus the manual cases that must be re-run every release, with an execution time budget and an owner.
- Bugs filed with repro steps, environment, and the test layer that should have caught them (the DoR's regression-gap field).

## Out of scope
Performance measurement (E21-Q03) and a11y depth (E21-Q05), though findings in either area are filed to those owners.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Charters executed and recorded
  Then all four charters have session notes, a findings list and a disposition for each finding

Scenario: Findings become durable
  Given an exploratory finding is confirmed as a defect
  Then a Bug is filed with repro steps and a regression case is added to the pack so it cannot silently return

Scenario: Long-run stability
  Given the 4-hour session
  Then client memory for the panel stays within its documented bound and the trail's time axis has not drifted from wall clock
```

## Technical notes / design
Sessions run against the demo environment with recorded fixtures available so a surprising behaviour can be replayed deterministically rather than described anecdotally.

## Test plan
Session-based: charter, timebox, notes, debrief. The debrief output is the deliverable.

## Security notes
Charter 1 doubles as an availability-abuse exploration; anything that looks like it could exhaust client or server resources is escalated to E21-X01/X02 rather than filed as a plain bug.

## Accessibility notes
At least one charter session is run keyboard-only, since exploratory testing with a mouse systematically misses keyboard traps.

## Performance notes
Charter 4's long run is the qualitative counterpart to E21-Q03's measured soak — it catches drift that a 5-minute benchmark cannot.

## Observability
Testers watch the metric dashboard during sessions; a behaviour with no corresponding metric is itself recorded as an observability gap.

title: QA sign-off for the DOM ladder and liquidity heatmap epic
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires an **Epic-level** regression/exploratory pass and an explicit sign-off, not merely the sum of child-ticket QA. `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 makes several of this Epic's outcomes R2 exit criteria (WS tick→screen p95 <100 ms on the heaviest topic set; a11y pass on the DOM ladder; zero open P0/P1). This ticket is the gate that records all of it in one place.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the full E21-Q01 plan on the release-candidate build in the demo environment: every manual cell of the state matrix plus a review of the automated results.
- Consolidated sign-off document `docs/qa/signoff/e21.md` containing: pass/fail per story (US-DOM-001..006, 009, 010), the automated suite result, the performance verdict against budgets #1/#3/#14, the chaos scenario results, the a11y verdict, the design-QA disposition list, and the open-defect list with priorities.
- Explicit verification of the Epic's exit conditions: zero open P0/P1 against SCR-050/SCR-051, coverage floors held, all docs reconciled.
- Any deviation (e.g. a case executed by the ticket owner rather than QA) recorded explicitly as a deviation, per §8.
- Hand-off of the regression pack to the R2 PRR evidence bundle.

## Out of scope
Fixing defects; the PRR itself (`07-release-and-prr.md`, owned by release management).

## Acceptance criteria

title: Adaptive, locked and logarithmic colour-scale controls
body:
## Context
US-DOM-003 (Must): the heatmap scale must adapt to current liquidity so it stays informative across regimes, must be lockable to absolute values with the lock indicated, and must offer a logarithmic mapping that keeps small and large resting sizes distinguishable — with the legend always showing the active bounds and mapping. E21-T06 built the LUT/scale pipeline; this Story exposes it in the product: the header quick control on SCR-050, the legend's live bounds, and the lock affordance.

## Scope / Deliverables
- SCR-050 header `scale [log v]` control: log / linear with gamma, and adaptive / locked.
- Percentile-window configuration surfaced (the `clip_percentile` of `HeatmapGridSpec`) with a sensible default and an explanation of what it does in plain language.
- Legend (CMP-113) updates live with the numeric bounds, the mapping type and the adaptive/locked state.
- Lock affordance: locking freezes the bounds at their current values (editable as absolute numbers), with an unmistakable locked indicator that is not colour-only.
- CVD-safe palette selectable here as well as in SCR-051, per US-DOM-003's NFR ("CVD-safe palette available").
- Persist the choice per symbol/panel into the workspace layout state and `chart_presets.heatmap` jsonb (`21-database-schema.md` — "colour scale, trail decay, bid=green/ask=red").

## Out of scope
The scale/LUT implementation (E21-T06); the full settings dialog (E21-S09); trail length (E21-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Adaptive scale
  Given liquidity drops by an order of magnitude
  Then the colour scale rescales using the configured percentile window and the legend shows the new bounds

Scenario: Fixed scale
  When the user locks the scale to absolute values
  Then it stops adapting, the bounds remain editable as numbers, and the locked state is indicated by text and icon, not colour alone

Scenario: Log scale
  When logarithmic mapping is chosen
  Then small and large resting sizes remain visually distinguishable and the legend states the log mapping

Scenario: Persistence
  Given the user sets log + locked bounds and reopens the workspace
  Then the same scale settings are restored for that symbol/panel

Scenario: No flashing on rescale
  Given the scale rebounds after a liquidity collapse
  Then the transition is smooth, and instantaneous under prefers-reduced-motion
```

## Technical notes / design
Changing the scale is a uniform/LUT update (≤1 frame) and must **not** drop the historized frame buffer (SCR-051 Performance note) — the UI must therefore not unmount or resubscribe the layer on a scale change. Bounds display uses the instrument's size precision from the instruments cache, not raw floats.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: control state machine (adaptive↔locked), bounds editing validation, persistence round-trip through the preset schema.
- **Storybook**: legend across mapping × adaptive/locked × palette × theme.
- **E2E**: switch to log, lock, reload the workspace, assert restoration; assert no resubscribe occurs on a scale change (network assertion).
- **A11y**: axe; the locked state must be in the accessible name; manual SR check of the legend.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
Settings persist to the user's own preset row — writes must be scoped to the authenticated user and validated server-side against the preset schema (no arbitrary jsonb).

## Accessibility notes
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §5: locked/adaptive and log/linear conveyed by text, never by colour or a bare icon; numeric bounds are readable text, not only a gradient; the CVD-safe palette is a first-class option reachable from this control.

## Performance notes
Scale change ≤1 frame; no re-subscription; no loss of the retained trail.

## Observability
`dom.settings_changed {key: heatmap.scale|heatmap.locked|heatmap.palette}` analytics; `heatmap_scale_mode` gauge.

title: Trail duration, decay mode and the client memory guard
body:
## Context
US-DOM-004 (Should): the trader controls how much liquidity history the trail shows (5 s–600 s per SCR-051's validation range, with the roadmap's "configurable history window" extending to the 60-minute case in the Epic goal), can disable age-based decay entirely, and — crucially — is told when a requested trail would exceed the client memory budget rather than being allowed to crash the panel. The NFR is explicit: *"memory per symbol bounded and displayed in the performance panel."*

## Scope / Deliverables
- SCR-050 header `trail [60s v]` control and the SCR-051 trail field (5–600 s), plus decay mode: smooth / none (static).
- **Decay off** renders intensity as true size with no age-based fading; the static mode is also what `prefers-reduced-motion` selects.
- **Memory guard**: compute the retained-frame cost for the requested trail at the current depth tier and bucket; if it exceeds the client budget, clamp the request and explain the maximum for the current depth tier in plain language (US-DOM-004 scenario 3) with an offer to reduce depth instead.
- Per-symbol heatmap memory reported into the performance panel (SCR-155-class surface owned by E10/E46 — this Story publishes the metric, it does not build the panel).
- Trail changes reuse the retained ring where possible: shortening the trail must not force a re-snapshot; lengthening beyond the retained window triggers backfill via E21-S08 rather than a blank region.

## Out of scope
The backfill fetch itself (E21-S08); ring implementation (E21-T05); depth shedding (E21-S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Trail length
  When the trail is set to 5 minutes
  Then only the last 5 minutes of book history render, and the time axis labels agree with that window

Scenario: Decay off
  When decay is disabled
  Then intensity reflects true size with no age-based fading, and the same static mode is used automatically under prefers-reduced-motion

Scenario: Memory guard
  Given a requested trail would exceed the client memory budget at the current depth tier
  Then the request is clamped, the maximum for that tier is explained in plain language, and reducing the depth tier is offered as the alternative

Scenario: Shortening is free
  When the trail is shortened
  Then no re-snapshot is requested and the retained columns are simply windowed

Scenario: Memory is visible
  Then per-symbol heatmap memory is published and readable in the performance panel
```

## Technical notes / design
Cost model: retained columns = `trail_seconds * 1000 / time_bucket_ms`; bytes ≈ columns × rows × 2 B (R16F) per ring, checked against the `26-chart-engine-design.md` memory budget (fine ring 2.1 MB, coarse ring 14.7 MB reference figures). The guard must use the *actual* current tier and bucket, not defaults, or the explanation will be wrong.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: cost model across tiers/buckets; clamp threshold boundaries; shortening path asserts no resubscribe; reduced-motion selects static decay.
- **Storybook**: the clamp explanation message for each tier.
- **E2E**: set an oversized trail, assert the clamp message names the correct maximum for the active tier.
- **Perf**: memory measured at the maximum permitted trail per tier and compared with the model's prediction (model error must be within a documented tolerance).
- **A11y**: the clamp message is announced via `role="status"` and is reachable without pointer.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
The guard is a client-side resource-exhaustion control; the server-side counterpart (`window_seconds` ≤900, 2 000-column snapshot cap) lives in E21-T02. Neither may be the only defence — this Story must assume the server could return more than requested and still not exceed its own budget.

## Accessibility notes
Clamp explanation is text, announced politely, with the alternative action reachable by keyboard. Static decay is the reduced-motion default, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` and US-DOM-002/004 NFRs.

## Performance notes
Bounded per-symbol memory is the point of this Story; the MemoryGovernor step-down at 70% of budget (E21-T05) remains the backstop.

## Observability
`heatmap_trail_seconds` gauge, `heatmap_trail_clamped_total`, `heatmap_client_memory_bytes{symbol}`.

title: Depth tiers 50/200/500 with automatic load shedding and pinning
body:
## Context
US-DOM-005 (Must), owner-facing: *"I want to choose depth tier 50/200/500 and have the app shed depth under load, so that responsiveness is preserved."* Its NFR is the one that makes this Story non-negotiable in character: **"shedding decisions logged and exposed as metrics; never silently degrade without telling the user."**

Two independent controllers can reduce fidelity: the client's frame-budget watchdog (US-DOM-005: frame time over budget for 5 consecutive seconds → step down one rung) and the server's connection-quality classifier (`23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3: `lagging`/`saturated` → throttle multipliers, forced coalescing, `degraded_topics`). E21-T07 records the combined policy as ADR-0016; this Story implements it and is the reason that ADR exists.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Depth control on the SCR-050 header (`depth [200 v]`) and in SCR-051; the active tier always shown on the DOM header.
- Tier change = resubscribe `book.{symbol}.{depth}` (new subscription identity, fresh snapshot) with the designed 1–2 s rebuild state, never a frozen-looking panel.
- **Automatic shedding**: frame time over the budget for 5 consecutive seconds → step down one rung (500→200→50), following the ADR-0016 rung order (heatmap cadence and trail are shed before depth); restore one rung when load allows, with the ADR's hysteresis and minimum dwell time so it cannot oscillate.
- **Non-blocking notice** explaining why, via CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner / the SCR-153 depth-shed variant: what was reduced, why, what still works, and how to pin.
- **Manual pin**: pinning prevents automatic shedding entirely and is clearly indicated; the app must then say what it does instead when it still cannot keep up (per ADR-0016).
- Reaction to the server-side signal: on `system` `connection_quality` with this panel's topics in `degraded_topics`, show the same vocabulary rather than a second, competing message.
- 500-depth availability gated on E21-K01's outcome: if capped, SCR-051 shows the tier as unavailable **with a visible reason** (the catalogue's own fallback wording) and the `heatmap_depth_500` feature flag governs it.

## Out of scope
The server's classifier (E17), the ADR text (E21-T07), the banner's visual design (E21-D03), backend depth caps (E21-T01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tier selection
  When depth 200 is selected
  Then the corresponding topic is subscribed, a fresh snapshot arrives, the rebuild state is shown briefly,
  and the tier is displayed on the DOM header

Scenario: Automatic shedding
  Given frame time exceeds the budget for 5 consecutive seconds
  Then the tier is reduced one step, a non-blocking notice explains why, a metric and a log entry are recorded,
  and the tier restores when load allows after the minimum dwell time

Scenario: Manual override
  When the tier is pinned
  Then automatic shedding will not change it, the pin is clearly indicated,
  and if the app still cannot keep up it says so rather than silently dropping frames

Scenario: No duplicate or contradictory messaging
  Given the server reports the connection as saturated while the client is also shedding
  Then exactly one coherent explanation is presented to the user, per ADR-0016

Scenario: 500-depth capped
  Given the engine spike capped the 500 tier
  Then SCR-051 presents 500 as unavailable with a visible reason and the feature flag state is respected

Scenario: Never silent
  Given any automatic reduction occurs
  Then a user-visible explanation, a metric increment and a structured log entry all occur; none may be omitted
```

## Technical notes / design
Frame-budget watchdog reads the engine's frame-marker instrumentation (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3) rather than a naive rAF timer, so shedding is attributed to real render cost. Thresholds (5 s trigger, dwell time, hysteresis band) are named constants imported from a single module and asserted against the ADR-0016 values in a test, so doc/code drift fails CI. Tier change discards heatmap state too, because `depth` invalidates the heatmap subscription identity as well (`23-ws-protocol.md` §5.4).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: watchdog trigger/restore with a fake clock (exactly 5 s, 4.9 s, oscillating input); rung order; pin behaviour; ADR-constant agreement test.
- **Storybook**: banner variants for each shed reason and direction.
- **Integration**: simulated `connection_quality: saturated` frame → assert single coherent message.
- **E2E**: throttle the renderer (CPU throttling in Playwright), assert step-down, notice, metric, and restoration.
- **Perf**: verify that after shedding, frame time returns inside budget on the reference hardware.
- **A11y**: banner is `role="status"`, announced once, readable in greyscale; pin state in the accessible name.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
Shedding must never disable or obscure a safety signal — the stale-book indication, the demo/live badge and the disabled-trading state keep full fidelity at every rung (ADR-0016 invariant, SR-038). A user-pinned 500-depth tier across many symbols is also the client side of the DoS concern in `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4; the client must respect the server's per-connection deep-book subscription cap and surface the rejection clearly rather than retrying in a loop.

## Accessibility notes
`role="status"` banner naming exactly which capability is degraded and what still works, in plain sentences (SCR-153 A11y); per-panel badges repeat the specific degradation in their accessible name; nothing about shedding is conveyed by colour alone.

## Performance notes
This Story *is* the enforcement of budgets #1/#14 at runtime. Shedding order per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4 as reconciled in ADR-0016.

## Observability
Metrics: `dom_depth_tier_current{symbol}`, `dom_shedding_events_total{reason,direction}`, `dom_frame_time_ms` histogram, `dom_tier_pinned`. Analytics/audit: `dom.depth_changed`, `degraded.entered{cause,sheddedFeatures}`, `degraded.exited{durationMs}`.

## Definition of Done

title: Own-order and position column on the ladder against the reconciled-OMS contract
body:
## Context
US-DOM-006 (Must): *"I want my working orders, stops and average entry shown on the ladder, so that I manage in the book."* Its NFR is a correctness rule with real money behind it: **"own-order overlay never derived from optimistic UI state alone — always reconciled with exchange truth."** Multi-account is in scope from day one because CandleViewer fans one ticket out to N accounts as a trade group: per-account markers aggregate per row with a count, expandable to per-account detail.

In R2 there is no OMS yet: E29 (OMS core) and E28 (trade groups) land in R3 (S14+), **after** this Epic's train window (S10–S12). This Story is therefore scoped to what can be completed inside R2 with no R3 blocker: the own-order/position **column, projection contract and rendering**, fed by the `OwnOrderProjection` port whose only R2 implementation is a fixture/demo adapter. No R3 ticket is a blocker; the live OMS adapter is wired in R3 by E31 (which already depends on E29/E28), consuming this Story's contract unchanged. E31 later attaches drag and click behaviour to exactly these markers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker** in the ladder's own-order column: working limit size and an identifying glyph per row; stop orders distinguished from limits; reduce-only indicated.
- **Position marker**: average entry row highlight and the position's side/size, plus the liquidation-price row marker when available.
- **Multi-account aggregation**: per-row count badge with expandable per-account detail (trade-group aware, per `24-internal-schemas.md` trade-group model).
- **`OwnOrderProjection` port** (`24-internal-schemas.md`): a versioned, read-only interface (rows keyed by `price_ticks`, side, size, kind, reduce-only, account id, confirmation state) with two R2 adapters — a deterministic fixture adapter for tests/Storybook and a demo-environment adapter reading the account-scoped WS `orders`/`positions` topics where they already exist. The R3 OMS adapter is out of scope here.
- **Reconciliation rule**: markers are rendered from reconciled OMS state; when an order is filled or cancelled externally, the marker clears **within 1 second** of the private WS event or the next reconciliation tick. No marker may exist that is derived only from a local optimistic action.
- Stale-marker safety: if the private feed is down, markers are shown with an explicit "not confirmed" treatment rather than being silently trusted or silently hidden.
- Accessible name extension: the row announcement includes own-order size and side ("…, your buy order 0.5 at this price"), and the per-account detail is keyboard-reachable.

## Out of scope
Placing/amending/cancelling from the ladder (US-DOM-007/008 → E31); the OMS itself (E29); trade-group construction (E28); **binding the projection port to live OMS/trade-group state — that wiring belongs to E31 in R3**; the order ticket (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Markers
  Given a working limit at 63,400
  Then that row shows the order size in the dedicated own-order column with an identifying glyph
  And the row's accessible name includes the own-order side and size

Scenario: Multi-account
  Given a trade group has orders at several prices
  Then per-account markers aggregate per row with a count, expandable to per-account detail, reachable by keyboard

Scenario: Stale order
  Given an order was filled or cancelled externally
  Then the marker clears within 1 second of the private WS event or the next reconciliation

Scenario: Never optimistic-only
  Given a local action has been sent but not acknowledged
  Then any marker shown is visibly marked pending and is removed if reconciliation does not confirm it

Scenario: Private feed down
  Given the orders/positions feed is disconnected
  Then existing markers are marked unconfirmed with the last-good timestamp, and the panel does not imply live order state

Scenario: RBAC scoping
  Given a manager who may see only a subset of accounts
  Then only that subset's orders and positions appear, and the aggregate count reflects only permitted accounts
```

## Technical notes / design
Marker state is a projection delivered by the `OwnOrderProjection` port (backed in R3 by the reconciled OMS store), keyed by `price_ticks` so it lines up with ladder rows exactly. Aggregation groups by row then by account; the expansion is a popover, not an inline row expansion, so ladder row heights stay uniform for virtualisation. Own-order markers must never be obscured by heatmap intensity — this is an explicit SCR-050 sign-off item and is why the column is dedicated rather than an overlay glyph.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: projection from OMS state; aggregation and count; pending/unconfirmed state machine; clearing within the 1 s budget with a fake clock.
- **Storybook**: CMP-230 variants (single, aggregated, pending, unconfirmed, stop vs limit, reduce-only).
- **Integration**: private-feed fixture with an externally-cancelled order; assert marker clearing.
- **E2E**: demo-environment order placed via the API through the demo adapter, marker appears; cancel externally, marker clears within 1 s. Contract tests pin the `OwnOrderProjection` shape so the R3 OMS adapter is a drop-in.
- **Security test**: a manager restricted to one account must not receive or render another account's markers — asserted at both the API and UI layers.
- **A11y**: axe; keyboard path into the per-account detail; SR announcement includes own-order info.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
This is the one part of E21 that renders **account-scoped, financially sensitive** data, so `04-security-program.md` §8's cross-Kind rule applies and the `security` label is mandatory. Threats: (a) **broken object-level authorisation** — the `orders`/`positions` topics must be filtered server-side by account scope, never client-side; a hand-crafted subscription must not yield another user's orders; (b) **stale/spoofed state** leading a trader to believe an order exists when it does not — mitigated by the reconciliation rule and the unconfirmed treatment; (c) information disclosure through the aggregate count (the count must not reveal the existence of orders in accounts the user cannot see). Data classification: financial, account-scoped. Abuse-case checks are covered by E21-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Own-order presence is conveyed by glyph + text + accessible name, never colour alone; the per-account expansion is keyboard-operable with a focus-return contract; the unconfirmed state is announced as text.

## Performance notes
Marker updates are low-frequency relative to book updates and must not invalidate the virtualised row list — patch markers in place. No additional frame cost at 200 visible rows.

## Observability
`dom_marker_clear_latency_ms` (the 1 s NFR), `dom_unconfirmed_markers_total`, and audit continuity with the OMS's own events (no new audit events are created by a read-only surface).

## Definition of Done

title: Deep liquidity scan panel: band thickness and reload detection
body:
## Context
US-DOM-009 (Should): *"I want cumulative book thickness and refill behaviour surfaced, so that I can judge real support."* Three requirements shape the UI: a panel of cumulative bid/ask depth within configurable distance bands and their difference; reload events flagged with an **`(estimated)`** badge and the replenished size; and an info popover that states plainly that **without L3/MBO data, replenishment is inferred from L2 changes only**. That caveat is a product-wide convention (`14-screens-catalogue.md` cross-cutting caveat 1), not optional small print.

E21-T04 produces the data backend-side; this Story renders it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Thickness panel inside/adjacent to SCR-050: cumulative bid depth, cumulative ask depth and their difference per configured distance band, updating live, with the bands configurable from SCR-051.
- Reload markers on the ladder rows and in the detector strip: replenished size, refill count, and **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** on every one.
- Pulled-liquidity shading on the heatmap surface for levels removed without matching prints (the "pulled orders" shading named in the Epic's roadmap scope), also `(estimated)`.
- **Info popover** with the fixed caveat copy from the E21-D07 copy deck: no L3 data, replenishment inferred from L2 only.
- Accessible readout: band values as a small data table, reload events as a list with numeric values and timestamps — not colour or glyph alone.

## Out of scope
The detection algorithms (E21-T04); the iceberg heuristic and its confidence score (E25); alerts/rules on these events (E40/E35 — they consume the same bus events).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cumulative thickness
  Then a panel shows cumulative bid and ask depth within each configurable distance band and their difference, updating live

Scenario: Reload detection
  Given a level is consumed and replenished within the configured window
  Then a reload event is flagged with an "(estimated)" badge and the replenished size

Scenario: No MBO caveat
  Then the info popover states that without L3 data replenishment is inferred from L2 changes only

Scenario: Estimated is never dropped
  Given a reload event is rendered anywhere (row marker, detector strip, accessible list)
  Then the estimated marking is present in every one of those places, including the accessible name

Scenario: Resyncing book
  Given the book is resynchronising
  Then no new reload or pulled markers appear, and the panel says why rather than showing stale numbers
```

## Technical notes / design
Band definitions come from SCR-051 and are expressed in ticks or bps from mid; the panel must render the instrument's own precision. Events arrive over `metrics.{symbol}`; the panel subscribes once per symbol and must tolerate the topic being degraded to a coarser cadence under backpressure without appearing broken.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: band value projection and formatting at instrument precision; estimated-badge presence invariant (a test that fails if any render path omits it); suppression during resync.
- **Storybook**: panel states (populated, empty, resyncing, degraded cadence), reload marker variants.
- **E2E**: fixture with a known refill; assert badge, size and caveat popover.
- **A11y**: axe; the accessible list carries numbers and the estimated wording.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
Market data only, `marketdata:read`. The *(estimated)* marking is a truthfulness control as much as a UX one: presenting inferred data as certain in a trading tool is the R9 advice-boundary risk, so the invariant test above is a security/compliance-relevant test, not cosmetic.

## Accessibility notes
`(estimated)` appears in the accessible name, not only as a visual chip; band values are available as text; the caveat popover is keyboard-reachable and dismissible with Esc.

## Performance notes
Low-frequency panel (≤1 Hz effective); must not add to the ladder's frame cost and must not trigger ladder re-renders.

## Observability
`dom_reload_markers_rendered_total`, `dom_pulled_markers_rendered_total`; analytics on caveat-popover opens (to learn whether the caveat is being read).

title: Progressive book-history backfill when a symbol is opened
body:
## Context
US-DOM-010 (Should): *"I want the heatmap to load recent recorded book history when I open a symbol, so that context is immediate."* The live subscription only carries the most recent 2 000 columns (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1); everything older is REST (`GET /market/heatmap`, built in E21-T03). Three behaviours matter: progressive newest-first loading with a progress indicator, an explicitly marked boundary when only partial history exists, and prompt cancellation with memory release when the user switches symbol. The NFR requires backfill to run **off the interaction path** with first useful paint ≤1 s.

## Scope / Deliverables
- On symbol open (and on trail lengthening beyond the retained window), fetch history in chunks newest-first up to 24 hours or the configured trail, whichever is smaller.
- Progress indicator that does not block interaction: the live trail is usable immediately while history fills in behind it.
- **Partial history**: load what exists and mark the boundary with the first available timestamp (a visible edge marker plus an accessible description), never an ambiguous blank.
- **Cancellation**: switching symbol or closing the panel aborts in-flight requests promptly (AbortController through to the fetch layer) and releases the decoded buffers; assertable in tests.
- Chunk decode and texture upload on the worker path, never on the main thread.
- Respect the server's disclosed effective resolution (downsampled segments) by labelling the affected region rather than rendering it as native-cadence data.
- Empty case delegates to E21-S02's empty state (offer to start recording).

## Out of scope
The REST endpoint (E21-T03); recording (E16); replay seek (E26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backfill
  Given up to 24 hours of recorded book history exists
  Then opening the symbol loads it progressively, newest first, with a progress indicator
  And the live trail remains interactive throughout

Scenario: Partial history
  Given only 3 hours exist
  Then 3 hours load and the boundary is marked with the first available timestamp, described accessibly

Scenario: Cancel
  When the symbol is switched during backfill
  Then the load cancels promptly, in-flight requests are aborted, and the decoded buffers are released

Scenario: First useful paint
  Given a recorded symbol is opened
  Then a useful heatmap is painted within 1 second, before backfill completes

Scenario: Downsampled segment disclosed
  Given part of the requested window is beyond the downsample boundary
  Then that region is labelled with its effective resolution rather than presented as native-cadence data
```

## Technical notes / design
Chunking strategy: request newest window first at the active bucket, then walk backwards; each chunk is decoded off-thread and pushed through `pushHeatmapColumn` into the coarse ring. Backfilled columns must be reconcilable with live columns at the join without a duplicate or gap — key on bucket start timestamp and make the merge idempotent.

Memory interacts with E21-S04's guard: backfill may not push retained memory past the clamp; it stops early and says so.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: chunk planning; join/merge idempotency at the live boundary; abort propagation; effective-resolution labelling.
- **Integration**: partial-history fixture; assert the boundary marker's timestamp equals the first available column.
- **E2E**: open a recorded symbol and assert first-useful-paint under 1 s with the progress indicator visible; switch symbols mid-load and assert no further network activity and no memory growth.
- **Perf**: backfill must not degrade live frame time — assert frame time during backfill stays inside budget.
- **A11y**: progress is announced politely (not per chunk); the boundary marker has a text description.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
The client must treat REST responses as untrusted input: validate matrix/axis dimension agreement before uploading to a texture (a mismatched `row_count` is the out-of-bounds risk also guarded in E21-T05). Requests carry the session credential; aborted requests must not leave the token in a retry loop. Rate: concurrent backfills are capped client-side to avoid becoming the DoS source described in `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4.

## Accessibility notes
Progress uses a polite live region with throttled updates; the partial-history boundary is described in text; nothing about load state is colour-only.

## Performance notes
First useful paint ≤1 s; backfill strictly off the interaction path; decode and upload on workers; frame budget preserved during load.

## Observability

title: SCR-051 Heatmap & ladder settings dialog
body:
## Context
Every tunable on this surface converges in SCR-051 (tabs: Depth & scale · Colour · Ladder · Trading · Detectors). It also carries two disclosure duties the catalogue makes explicit: a warning that a higher depth tier increases bandwidth and CPU **with the measured cost shown**, and a notice that changing the depth tier resubscribes the book and causes a brief resync. US-SET-005 (settings persistence) and US-DOM-003/004/005/010 all land here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The dialog per the catalogue layout and the E21-D03 hi-fi: depth tier (50/200/500), colour scale (log/linear + gamma), trail length (5–600 s) + decay mode, palette (bid/ask swatches + CVD-safe set), row height (10–40 px), centre lock / auto-follow, show-toggles (own orders, position, prints, cumulative depth, queue estimate with `(estimated)`), qty presets, "confirm market orders in LIVE", detector toggles + sensitivity.
- **CMP-228 PreviewTile** (`kind: "heatmap"`) live preview on sample data.
- **Validation**: trail 5–600 s; row height 10–40 px; at least one qty preset; inline errors with the copy-deck wording.
- **Cost disclosure**: measured bandwidth/CPU figure per depth tier shown next to the control.
- **Resubscribe notice** on depth change with the 1–2 s rebuild state.
- **Reset to defaults** per tab and for the whole dialog.
- Persistence into the user's preset (`chart_presets.heatmap` jsonb and the per-user settings key space, e.g. `recorder.default_depth`-style dotted keys in `user_settings`), scoped to the authenticated user.
- 'Preview with colour-vision simulation' toggle on the Colour tab.

## Out of scope
Trading behaviour behind the "Trading" tab's controls (E31 consumes these settings); detector algorithms and their sensitivity semantics (E25 — this Story renders the controls and persists the values against the agreed schema).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All controls present and validated
  Then depth tier, colour scale, trail, palette, row height, centre lock, show-toggles, qty presets and detector toggles
  are all present, and out-of-range values are rejected inline with the specified message

Scenario: Live preview
  When a colour or scale setting changes
  Then the preview tile updates without a live subscription and without dropping the running heatmap's frame buffer

Scenario: Cost disclosure
  When the depth tier is raised
  Then the measured bandwidth and CPU cost for that tier is shown before the change is applied

Scenario: Resubscribe notice
  When the depth tier is changed
  Then the dialog states the book will resubscribe and the panel shows the 1-2 s rebuild state rather than appearing frozen

Scenario: Persistence and reset
  Given settings are changed and the app is restarted
  Then the settings are restored for that user; reset-to-defaults restores the documented defaults and says which ones changed

Scenario: Keyboard and screen reader
  Then every control is a labelled form field with units, reachable and operable by keyboard, with numeric colour stops available as text inputs
```

## Technical notes / design
Settings apply to the running panel without rebuilding it except where the contract requires a resubscribe (depth, price grouping, bucket). Colour/scale changes are uniform updates (≤1 frame). Validation ranges are single-sourced constants shared with the backend preset schema so client and server cannot disagree.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: each validation rule at its boundaries; reset-to-defaults diff; persistence round-trip; "no resubscribe on colour change" assertion.
- **Storybook**: every tab, every error state, the CVD-simulation preview.
- **E2E**: change each setting, assert the running panel reflects it and that a reload restores it.
- **A11y**: axe; keyboard-only completion of every tab; SR labels include units.
- **Contract**: the persisted payload validates against the preset schema server-side; an invalid payload is rejected.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
Settings writes are user-scoped and server-validated against a strict schema — arbitrary jsonb must not be accepted (mass-assignment/stored-payload risk). The "confirm market orders in LIVE" control is a safety setting: its default is on, and changing it must be recorded in the audit log (it changes the risk posture of a later trading action), per `04-security-program.md`'s audit requirements.

## Accessibility notes
All controls labelled with units; the colour-scale editor exposes numeric stops as text inputs alongside the gradient widget; the CVD-simulation toggle is itself an accessibility feature and must be keyboard-reachable; dialog focus trap with Esc dismissal and focus return.

## Performance notes
The preview tile uses static sample frames, never a live subscription; applying settings must not drop the historized frame buffer.

## Observability
`dom.settings_changed {key}` analytics; `dom.depth_tier_changed` records the negotiated tier for support; audit entry for the LIVE-confirm toggle.

title: LiquidityTracker: depth bands, thickness and refill/reload detection
body:
## Context
`20-architecture.md` §3.2 lists `LiquidityTracker` as a Book Engine component: "Tracks per-price resting size over time (append-only ring per price bucket) feeding the heatmap and `distance_to_liquidity_cluster`". US-DOM-009 turns that into a user-visible feature: cumulative bid/ask depth within configurable distance bands and their difference, plus **reload detection** — a level consumed and replenished within a configured window, flagged with an `(estimated)` badge — with the explicit caveat that without L3/MBO data replenishment is *inferred from L2 changes only*. The story's NFR requires detection to run **backend-side and emit events for alerts and rules**.

This Task is deliberately the *measurement* half. The iceberg heuristic proper (`IcebergHeuristic`, `IcebergEstimate{confidence}`) belongs to E25; E21 supplies the tracker it consumes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/backend/book_engine/liquidity.py` — `LiquidityTracker.series(price_bucket, window)` over an append-only ring per price bucket, bounded at 10 minutes (≈12 MB/symbol at 100 ms × 200 buckets, per `20-architecture.md` §3.2).
- Depth-band aggregation: cumulative bid/ask size within configurable distance bands (in ticks or bps from mid) and the band difference; published on `metrics.{symbol}` alongside the existing `book_imbalance` and `book_thickness` fields of `orderflow_metrics` (`21-database-schema.md` §4.x).
- Reload/refill detection: level consumed (size drops by ≥X% after aggressive trades at/through the price) then replenished to ≥Y% of prior size within window W → emit a `LiquidityReload` event carrying `estimated: true`, the replenished size, and the refill count.
- Pulled-liquidity signal: a level removed **without** matching trade prints at that price within the window (the "pulled orders" shading the roadmap names for this Epic) — emitted distinctly from consumed liquidity.
- Config keys with documented defaults: `liquidity.bands_ticks`, `liquidity.reload_consume_pct`, `liquidity.reload_replenish_pct`, `liquidity.reload_window_ms`, `liquidity.min_size`.
- Events published on the `of.*` bus so E25/E35/E40 can consume them.

## Out of scope
`IcebergHeuristic`, `StopRunDetector`, `RegimeEngine` (all E25); the UI panel (E21-S07); the shading render (E21-T05/S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Band thickness
  Given a book with known level sizes
  Then cumulative bid and ask depth within each configured band, and their difference, match a hand-computed fixture exactly

Scenario: Reload flagged as estimated
  Given a level is consumed by aggressive prints and replenished to 90% of its prior size within the window
  Then a LiquidityReload event is emitted with estimated=true, the replenished size and the refill count

Scenario: Pulled is not reload
  Given a level disappears with no trade prints at that price in the window
  Then a pulled-liquidity event is emitted and no reload event is emitted

Scenario: Estimated data is excluded during resync
  Given the book is Resyncing
  Then no reload or pulled event is emitted from the incomplete book state

Scenario: Bounded memory
  Given 200 price buckets sampled at 100 ms for 10 minutes
  Then tracker memory stays within the documented per-symbol bound and old samples are evicted, not accumulated
```

## Technical notes / design
Detection correlates book changes against the trade stream — the tracker therefore subscribes both `md.book.{symbol}` and the trade bus. The L2-only caveat is not a disclaimer to bury: every emitted event carries `estimated: true` so every downstream surface (UI badge, alert text, rule input) inherits it, matching the product-wide "*(estimated)*" convention.

`distance_to_liquidity_cluster` (a rule-engine input listed in `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 with `estimated` provenance) is computed from this tracker's series — expose it as a named accessor so E35 does not reimplement clustering.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: band aggregation against hand-computed fixtures; reload detection at threshold boundaries (just below / just above consume and replenish percentages, just inside / outside the window); pulled vs consumed discrimination; suppression during resync.
- **Property**: ring buffer never exceeds its bound; eviction preserves ordering.
- **Integration**: recorded fixture containing a known wall that is consumed and refilled; assert event count and payload.
- **Golden-file**: band metrics series over a recorded window.
- Coverage ≥85%.

## Security notes
Non-secret market data. Threat: an attacker cannot influence this directly, but a pathological book (thousands of micro-levels) could make clustering expensive — bound the per-column work and drop to a coarser bucket rather than blocking the event loop.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. Event payloads must carry numeric values (not just categories) so the UI can render an accessible text readout.

## Performance notes
Runs inside the per-symbol engine task; must add ≤2 ms per book sample at 200 depth so budget #6 is preserved.

## Observability
Metrics: `liquidity_reload_events_total`, `liquidity_pulled_events_total`, `liquidity_tracker_memory_bytes{symbol}`, `liquidity_band_compute_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria pass with an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Coverage: ≥85% line on touched backend/engine packages, ≥80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md` as touched.

- [ ] perf: benchmark recorded against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1/#14 (default-on for this Epic per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).
- [ ] security: SAST/SCA/secrets scans clean or triaged; Security engineer comment present where `security`-labelled.
