title: CVD & delta panes: cumulative delta, anchors, display modes and divergence
body:
## Context
**R2 "Order-flow beta"** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6, sprints S10-S13, `v0.3.0`, staging/demo) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility on top of the R1 engine. **E23 CVD & delta panes** is the *cumulative aggression* layer of that release. The roadmap scope line (Â§6.2) reads:

> CVD computed from aggressor side with explicit session/rolling/anchored reset semantics; per-bar delta pane; CVD divergence markers; multi-symbol CVD comparison; **correct CVD reconstruction after WS reconnect** (recompute from recorded trades, never guess)

â€” **26 pts, Sprint S12**, area `area/order-flow`, backend module **M9** (`server/orderflow/`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`), story domain **CVD** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` Â§13).

Three facts shape every ticket in this epic:

1. **CVD is exact, not estimated.** Bybit publishes the aggressor side on `publicTrade` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` â€” `TradeEvent.side` maps Bybit's `S`), so `delta = buy_volume - sell_volume` is a *measurement*, not a tick-rule inference. The only `(estimated)` surface in this epic is **divergence detection**, which is heuristic and therefore carries CMP-227 EstimatedBadge on SCR-052 (design sign-off checklist: "divergence markers drawn with a text label and the *(estimated)* chip where the detection is heuristic").
2. **One delta computation, three consumers.** US-CVD-001's NFR is explicit: "shares the delta computation used by footprint and Deep-Stats". E18 Footprint already aggregates bid/ask volume per price per bar; E20 Deep-Stats already renders per-bar delta / cumulative-delta rows. E23 must **consume** that aggregation inside M9, not fork it. A second delta implementation is an explicit anti-goal and a review-blocking defect.
3. **Reconnect must recompute, never guess.** CVD is a running sum: one lost print corrupts every subsequent value forever. `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§7 provides snapshot+delta with per-topic sequence numbers and an explicit resync protocol, and Â§"Append, never merge" notes that for `trades` "**every print matters for the tape and CVD**". On any gap the series is **recomputed from the recorded tape** (QuestDB `trades` / Parquet cold tier) over the affected window and the client is re-snapshotted â€” never interpolated, carried forward, or silently re-based.

### Estimate reconciliation (roadmap-authoritative)

`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 (epic register, line 123) and §6.2 size **E23 at 26 points**. That register is authoritative and this epic ticket therefore carries `estimate: 26`.

| Bucket | Points | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering delivery in the R2 train (K01, T01-T05, S01-S05) | **27** | The number the roadmap's 26 pts is measured against — **+3.8%**, inside the ±15% planning band |
| R5-deferred story S06 (composite CVD) | 2 | Sprint `Backlog`; descope candidate 4 per roadmap §12, not part of the R2 train |
| Engineering total incl. deferred | 29 | |
| Design (D01-D06), QA (Q01-Q06), Security (X01-X02) | 33 | Discipline capacity tracked on the design/QA/security lanes; **not** rolled into the roadmap engineering points for E23 |

The epic's `estimate` field is deliberately **not** the arithmetic sum of all children: summing design, QA and security lanes into the engineering figure would double-count capacity that the roadmap tracks separately, and would make E23 appear to have blown its train window when it has not. Any change to the in-train engineering total that pushes it outside 22-30 pts must be reflected back into `30-release-roadmap.md` §3/§6.2 in the same PR.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories covered:** US-CVD-001 (per-bar delta pane, *Must*), US-CVD-002 (cumulative delta with reset anchors, *Must*), US-CVD-003 (CVD display modes, *Must*), US-CVD-004 (single-bar divergence detection, *Should*), US-CVD-005 (multi-bar swing divergence detection, *Must*), US-CVD-006 (composite / normalised CVD, *Could* â€” deferred to R5 per roadmap Â§12 descoping ladder row 4).
- **Screen:** SCR-052 CVD / delta panel.
- **Components:** CMP-185 CvdPane (the epic's net-new chart primitive); reuse of CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-189 TimeAxis, CMP-190 Crosshair, CMP-197 ChartTooltip, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.
- **Backend (M9, `server/orderflow/cvd/`):** `CvdEngine` (anchor semantics, intrabar CVD OHLC, EMA smoothing), `DivergenceDetector` (single-bar + swing), composite z-score normaliser, reconnect recompute path.
- **API:** `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` (`metric=cvd|delta|min_max_delta`, `params={"cvd":{"anchor":"..."}}`), `GET /api/v1/market/bars?include_delta=true`.
- **WS:** `metrics.{symbol}` with `metrics: ["cvd","delta",...]`, `bar_type`, `param`, `throttle_ms`; `bars.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` with `include_delta` (binary `body_kind` 4 carries `i64 delta`).
- **Tables:** QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` (`cvd`, `cvd_session`, `delta_1s`), `bars_*` (`delta`, `cum_delta`, `min_delta`, `max_delta`, `delta_pct`), `trades` (recompute source); Postgres `layout_panes.pane_kind = 'cvd'`, `chart_indicators.indicator_code IN ('cvd','delta')`.
- **Children:** design pack D01-D06 (D-S07 track), backend K01/T01-T05, frontend S01-S06, QA Q01-Q06, security X01-X02.

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell aggregation and imbalance (E18), volume/delta/TPO profiles (E19), the Deep-Stats row framework (E20), DOM ladder and liquidity heatmap (E21), big-trade bubbles (E22), OI/funding/liquidation panes (E24), tape-speed / imbalance / regime / iceberg / stop-run detectors (E25), the replay clock and scrubbing (E26 â€” E23 only guarantees its engine is driven through the same pipeline).
- Alert and rule wiring for divergence events: E40 Alerts consumes the events E23 emits and E35 consumes the `cvd_divergence` metric; E23 only publishes them.
- Multi-symbol composite CVD ships in **R5** (E23-S06, sprint `Backlog`) per the descoping ladder.
- Options/GEX, spot and inverse contracts, non-Bybit venues, Android.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: CVD matches an independent offline recomputation
  Given a full recorded symbol-day in the Parquet cold tier
  When CVD, per-bar delta, min/max delta and divergence flags are recomputed offline with DuckDB
  Then every value emitted by the live pipeline matches within floating-point tolerance

Scenario: Reconnect never corrupts the running sum
  Given a client is streaming metrics.BTCUSDT and the WS drops for 45 seconds
  When the client resubscribes and a sequence gap is detected
  Then the server recomputes CVD for the gap window from the recorded tape and re-snapshots the client
  And the post-reconnect CVD equals the value an uninterrupted client would hold, exactly

Scenario: The pane holds its frame budget
  Given three CVD panes are open during a 5,000 trades/min burst
  Then the workspace sustains >= 58 fps and each pane costs <= 2 ms CPU and <= 1 ms GPU per frame

Scenario: Divergence is honest about being heuristic
  Given divergence detection is enabled
  Then every divergence marker renders with a text label and the (estimated) chip
  And the popover states the active thresholds and the known failure modes

Scenario: Partial history is never silent
  Given the recorder holds only part of the requested range
  Then the pane shows an explicit partial-history state naming the first available timestamp
```

## Technical notes / design
One pipeline for live and replay (roadmap exit criterion 1): `TradeEvent` -> per-bar bid/ask aggregation in M9 (shared with E18/E20) -> `CvdEngine` -> `orderflow_metrics` persistence + `metrics.{symbol}` fan-out. Per `(symbol, bar_type, param, anchor)` the engine holds the running cumulative sum, the anchor timestamp, and the intrabar path (`min_delta`/`max_delta`) required by bar invariant **BI-3** for CVD-candle mode. Anchors: `session` (from `session_anchor`, default `utc_day`), `utc_day`, `never` (anchored at the first available print and labelled with its timestamp), `manual` (client-supplied bar timestamp, clamped to the loaded range). EMA smoothing is an **overlay**, never a replacement for the raw series.

## Test plan
Epic-level gates (children carry the detail): golden-fixture parity over one recorded symbol-day, CI-blocking on drift (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§6.4 Correctness gate); replay double-run determinism; chaos fixtures "WS disconnect + resync" and "sequence gap"; unit coverage >=85% on `server/orderflow/cvd/` and >=80% on the frontend pane; contract tests against the `MetricsUpdate` and `BarsBatch` JSON Schemas in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` Â§14.

## Security notes
Data classification: **market data â€” internal** (no PII, no credentials, no order-entry surface). Applicable STRIDE entries from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **(D) Denial of service** â€” an unbounded or highly granular `metrics.{symbol}` subscription (many metrics x many symbols x low `throttle_ms`) is a server-side CPU and fan-out amplifier, and an unclamped historical recompute is a disk/CPU amplifier; **(T) Tampering** â€” a client-supplied manual anchor timestamp or swing lookback used unvalidated as a query bound can force an unbounded scan; **(I) Information disclosure** â€” nothing beyond market data, but the surface is still RBAC-gated by `marketdata:read` (`x-rbac` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`). Controls: server-side clamping of every range/lookback/anchor, `maxItems: 12` on `metric`, per-session subscription caps, rate limiting, and structured logging of rejected requests. Full model in E23-X01, review in E23-X02.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). SCR-052 is WebGL-rendered, so the **canvas control surrogate** pattern (Â§6.1) applies: the pane exposes an **accessible table alternative** (per-bar time, delta, CVD, divergence flag) reachable from the panel header by keyboard, marked up as a real `table` with row/column headers; divergences are additionally listed as **text events**. All controls (reset anchor, display mode, smoothing, divergence toggle) are real focusable form controls with visible focus rings >=3:1 against the pane background. The sign of delta is carried by **text sign + bar direction**, never colour alone; buy/sell hues are verified under deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia. The streaming series carries no `aria-live` (that would flood a screen reader at tick rate); the user polls values via the table alternative.

## Performance notes
SCR-052 budget (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-052 Â§Performance): the CVD series updates at a **capped 10 Hz** â€” updates coalesced from the `metrics.{symbol}` stream into one render per 100 ms frame regardless of trade rate; panel budget **<=2 ms CPU + <=1 ms GPU per frame**; **>=58 fps with 3 CVD panels open during a 5,000 trades/min burst**; divergence detection runs incrementally on bar close, never over the whole series. Global budgets (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§2): #1 frame time <=16.6 ms p95, #2 never below 30 fps, #3 WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms (hard R2 exit gate), #7 frontend memory <=1.5 GB per workspace.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_cvd_engine_updates_total{symbol,anchor}`, `cv_cvd_recompute_seconds` (histogram of gap-repair duration), `cv_cvd_recompute_total{reason="ws_gap"|"anchor_change"|"backfill"}`, `cv_cvd_divergence_events_total{kind="single_bar"|"swing"}`, `cv_metrics_subscription_rejected_total{reason}`. Logs: structured `cvd.recompute` with `symbol`, `from`, `to`, `prints`, `duration_ms`. Traces: span `orderflow.cvd.recompute` as a child of the resync span. Frontend analytics (SCR-052): `cvd.interval_changed`, `cvd.mode_changed`, `cvd.divergence_marker_clicked`, `cvd.anchor_set`.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§2.2 (Epic):
- [ ] Every child ticket Done; US-CVD-001..005 demonstrated on staging against a recorded symbol-day
- [ ] Golden-fixture parity test and replay-determinism test green in CI
- [ ] Perf budgets #1/#2/#3 and the SCR-052 pane budget measured and recorded
- [ ] A11y audit passed (axe-core clean plus a manual screen-reader pass on the table alternative)
- [ ] STRIDE threat model recorded and reviewed; security review signed off
- [ ] ADR-0017 merged; `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md` updated where behaviour drifted from plan
- [ ] Storybook stories for CMP-185 (Histogram, Line, Candlestick, WithDivergenceMarkers) published
- [ ] Design sign-off (CDO) on the built pane; QA sign-off; Owner accepts at Sprint Review

## Dependencies
- **E18 Footprint** â€” roadmap graph `E18 --> E23`; supplies the shared per-bar bid/ask aggregation in M9 that US-CVD-001's NFR mandates E23 reuse.
- **E12 Bar builders & series rendering** â€” the bar grid (`time`/`tick`/`volume`/`range`/`delta`) CVD is sampled on, plus per-bar `delta`/`min_delta`/`max_delta`.
- **E17 Market-data WS protocol & binary framing** â€” the `metrics.{symbol}` topic, sequencing and resync machinery.
- **E13 Indicators framework & v1 indicator set** â€” US-CVD-005 requires the **same confirmed-swing source as US-IND-005** (Zig Zag); E23 must not fork swing detection.
- **E16 Recorder, retention & disk budget** â€” the recorded tape the reconnect recompute and the partial-history state depend on.
- **E11 Chart engine core** â€” the pane/axis/crosshair surface CMP-185 plugs into.
- Downstream: `E23 --> E25` (detectors consume CVD); E40 Alerts and E35 rule engine consume `cvd_divergence`.

## Branch
`feat/cvd-delta-panes-<short>` per child (e.g. `feat/cvd-delta-panes-engine`). PRs <=400 LOC diff; 2 approvals incl. 1 `area/order-flow` code-owner.

## Child dependency graph

```mermaid
    D01[D01 UX research] --> D02[D02 Wireframes SCR-052]
    D02 --> D03[D03 Hi-fi + CMP-185 DS entry]

```

## Risks

|---|---|
| **R7 Data accuracy** â€” one lost print silently corrupts the running sum forever | Recompute-on-gap (T03), golden-fixture parity vs DuckDB (T04), chaos test (Q06) |
| **R2 Render performance** â€” three CVD panes on top of the full order-flow scene blow the frame budget | 10 Hz coalescing cap, divergence computed incrementally on bar close only, perf scripts (Q03), spike (K01) |
| **R5 Scope** â€” composite CVD (US-CVD-006, a *Could*) eats the train | Explicitly deferred to R5 (S06, sprint `Backlog`) per roadmap Â§12 |

## Agent guidance

How to pick the next ticket in this epic when multiple agents are working it in parallel:

1. **Design track first** (E23-D01, E23-D02, E23-D03, E23-D04, E23-D05, E23-D06) must clear the design-ahead rule (Done ≥2 sprints before the Story that consumes it) before any Story in its lane starts — check each Story's own `blocked_by` for the exact design ticket.
2. **Spike/engineering foundation** (E23-K01, E23-T01, E23-T02, E23-T03, E23-T04, E23-T05, E23-T06) generally has no ticket dependency on the Stories and can start immediately in parallel with design — these define the wire contract and backend engines the Stories consume.
3. **Stories** (E23-S01, E23-S02, E23-S03, E23-S04, E23-S05, E23-S06) are blocked by their named Task/Spike and design ticket per each Story's own `blocked_by` list — do not start a Story until every key in its `blocked_by` is Done.
4. **QA** (E23-Q01, E23-Q02, E23-Q03, E23-Q04, E23-Q05, E23-Q06) and **Security** (E23-X01, E23-X02) tracks run against the Stories/Tasks they test — pick these up once their named inputs are Done, not before.
5. **Parallel lanes**: two agents may safely work any two tickets that do not appear in each other's `blocked_by` chain and do not touch the same repo paths in the same PR window — check both before starting.
6. **Shared interfaces to agree first**: any change to a WS topic, REST path, DB table, or `MetricRegistry`/`MetricDescriptor` entry named across multiple children must be raised and agreed (PR to `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md`) before two agents implement against diverging assumptions.

title: Black-box test plan and exploratory charter for CVD & delta panes
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature alongside the white-box review. This epic needs one written *before* the stories land, because several of its acceptance criteria are only observable if the test environment can produce the conditions â€” a WS gap, a recorder hole, a session boundary, a range with no tick data. Discovering in Sprint 13 that we cannot produce a recorder hole on demand would leave exit criterion 5 untested.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box test plan covering US-CVD-001..005 (US-CVD-006 is deferred with E23-S06), each scenario mapped to a test case with preconditions, steps, expected result and the fixture required.
- **Fixture inventory and procurement plan**: the recorded symbol-day used by E23-T04; a fixture with a recorded ingestion gap; a fixture spanning a UTC session boundary; a symbol-range with no recorded tick data (for the candles-disabled state); a high-volatility burst; a thin-book symbol. Each with the procedure to replay it on demand into staging.
- **Exploratory charters** (session-based, 90 minutes each), at minimum: (a) "explore anchor changes during live streaming, looking for values that disagree between the pane, the tooltip and the table alternative"; (b) "explore the pane across workspace reload, symbol change and timeframe change, looking for state that survives when it should not or is lost when it should not be"; (c) "explore divergence at the edges â€” first bar, last bar, session boundary, gapped range â€” looking for flags that repaint or appear twice"; (d) "explore the pane's behaviour while the backend is repairing after a gap".
- The **honesty checklist** for this epic, per the roadmap Â§6.4 Honesty gate: for each estimated view (single-bar divergence, swing divergence) â€” badge present, popover accurate, thresholds/parameters visible.
- The **regression pack** definition: which cases run every sprint thereafter.
- Entry and exit criteria for the epic's QA phase, and the defect severity rubric for this epic (a missing `(estimated)` badge is **P1** by roadmap exit criterion 4; a wrong CVD value after reconnect is **P0** because it is silent and permanent).

## Out of scope
Executing the plan (E23-Q02 and the exploratory sessions themselves), automation code (Q02/Q03), the a11y audit (Q04), chaos execution (Q06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Must and Should scenario has a case
  When the plan is reviewed against US-CVD-001 to US-CVD-005
  Then every Gherkin scenario in those stories maps to at least one test case
  And each case names the fixture it requires

Scenario: Every fixture is procurable
  Then each required fixture has either an existing source or a named owner and a date
  And no test case depends on waiting for a market condition to occur naturally

Scenario: The honesty checklist exists
  Then the plan contains a per-estimated-view checklist covering badge presence, popover accuracy and parameter visibility
  And it is marked as a release-blocking check

Scenario: Severity is agreed in advance
  Then the plan states that a missing estimated badge is P1 and a post-reconnect CVD error is P0
  And the rubric is agreed with the Owner and the epic lead
```

## Technical notes / design
Test-case design should lean on **oracles**, not eyeballs: the strongest oracle in this epic is the offline DuckDB recomputation (E23-T04), so black-box cases that assert a displayed value should assert it against that oracle rather than against a tester's judgement. The second oracle is the uninterrupted-run comparison for reconnect cases.

## Test plan
The plan is itself reviewed by the epic lead and one backend engineer for feasibility; coverage of the story scenarios is asserted by a mapping table in the plan document.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.
Abuse cases are covered separately in E23-X02; the plan cross-references them so QA does not duplicate.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the a11y checklist produced by E23-D04 as an appendix and hands its execution to E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
The plan references but does not duplicate the performance cases owned by E23-Q03, and states the SCR-052 budget so functional testers recognise a perf regression when they see one.

## Observability
The plan lists the metrics and logs a tester should check to confirm a scenario actually exercised the intended path (e.g. `cv_cvd_recompute_total{reason="ws_gap"}` incrementing during a reconnect case).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan reviewed and approved by the epic lead and QA lead
- [ ] Fixture inventory complete with owners and dates
- [ ] Exploratory charters scheduled
- [ ] Regression pack defined and added to the sprint regression suite

## Dependencies
`E23-D05` â€” the designed states define what "expected result" means; `E23-T02` â€” the API/WS surface tests will drive.

title: Golden-fixture parity harness: CVD vs offline DuckDB recomputation
body:
## Context
Roadmap R2 **exit criterion 6**: "Footprint, profile, **CVD** and Deep-Stats values match an independent offline recomputation (DuckDB over the Parquet tier) for a full recorded symbol-day, within floating-point tolerance." The Â§6.4 Correctness gate makes it CI-blocking: "Golden-fixture tests: one recorded symbol-day with expected footprint/profile/CVD/Deep-Stats outputs version-controlled; **any drift fails CI**."

E18 and E19 are building the footprint and profile halves of this harness; this ticket adds the CVD and per-bar-delta assertions to the same harness rather than creating a parallel one.

**Estimate note (2 pts, was 3).** E18/E19 build the golden-fixture parity harness itself (runner, fixture format, CI gate); this ticket adds CVD and per-bar-delta assertions plus the DuckDB recompute query to that existing harness.

## Scope / Deliverables
- An **independent** reference implementation of CVD in SQL over the Parquet cold tier (DuckDB), deliberately written from `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` Â§13 and `24-internal-schemas.md` rather than by reading the engine code â€” the point is independence, and a transliteration of the engine proves nothing.
- Version-controlled expected outputs for one recorded symbol-day: per-bar `delta`, `min_delta`, `max_delta`, cumulative `cvd` under each anchor kind (`session`, `utc_day`, `never`), CVD-candle OHLC, and the EMA-9 smoothed series.
- A comparison runner asserting engine output equals the reference within an explicit tolerance, with a first-divergence report (bar timestamp, expected, actual, delta) so failures are debuggable rather than merely red.
- **Replay determinism** assertion: replaying the same recorded window twice produces byte-identical CVD output (roadmap Â§6.4 Determinism gate) â€” including a run that injects a mid-window disconnect so the repair path (E23-T03) is exercised inside the determinism check.
- CI wiring: runs on every PR touching `server/orderflow/`, blocking on drift; fixture stored per the testing strategy's fixture conventions (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`).
- Documented procedure for regenerating the golden outputs, requiring an explicit human justification in the PR description â€” regeneration must be a deliberate act, never a convenient one.

## Out of scope
The footprint and profile assertions (E18/E19 own them in the same harness), performance benchmarking (E23-Q03), UI verification (E23-Q02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Parity over a full symbol-day
  Given one recorded symbol-day in the Parquet tier
  When the engine output and the DuckDB reference are compared for every bar
  Then all delta, min_delta, max_delta, cvd and CVD-candle values match within the documented tolerance
  And the tolerance is stated numerically, not described as approximately equal

Scenario: Drift fails the build
  Given a change that shifts one bar's cumulative value by one tick of quantity
  When CI runs
  Then the job fails and the report names the first diverging bar with expected and actual values

Scenario: Determinism across runs
  When the same recorded window is replayed twice
  Then the two CVD output streams are byte-identical

Scenario: Determinism across a repair
  Given a replay run in which the stream is severed mid-window and repaired
  Then its CVD output is byte-identical to the uninterrupted replay of the same window

Scenario: Regeneration is deliberate
  Given a developer regenerates the golden outputs
  Then the PR fails review unless it contains a written justification for each changed expected value
```

## Technical notes / design
Tolerance: the engine accumulates in decimal, the DuckDB reference in `DECIMAL` as well, so the expected comparison is **exact** for delta and cumulative values; only the EMA series needs a float tolerance, and it should be stated as a relative epsilon (e.g. `1e-12`). Prefer failing on exactness where exactness is achievable â€” an unnecessarily loose tolerance is how silent drift ships.

Fixture selection matters: choose a symbol-day containing a session boundary, a volatility burst, and at least one recorded ingestion gap, so the anchor reset, the intrabar path and the gapped-bar exclusion are all covered by the single golden fixture.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* test infrastructure; its own tests are meta-tests: the harness must (a) detect a deliberately seeded one-unit drift, (b) detect a reordering of prints, (c) pass on the unmodified engine. All three are asserted in CI so the harness cannot silently stop checking.

## Security notes
No new attack surface: this ticket adds no endpoint, no persistence and no user input path. It inherits the epic controls modelled in E23-X01 (subscription caps, range clamping, `marketdata:read` RBAC). No `security` review label required.
The fixture contains public market data only; no key material or account data may enter the fixture set.

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” no user interface is introduced by this ticket. The UI consuming this work is covered by E23-S01..S05 and audited by E23-Q04.

## Performance notes
The harness must complete within the CI time budget for a per-PR job; if a full symbol-day is too slow, run a fixed representative window per PR and the full day nightly â€” but the full-day run must exist and must block the release, not merely warn.

## Observability
Publishes the parity result and the first-divergence report as a CI artifact; the nightly full-day run posts its result to the team channel on failure.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§3.2/Â§4.2:
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via a PR <=400 LOC diff with 2 approvals incl. 1 `area/order-flow` code-owner
- [ ] Unit coverage >=85% (backend/engine) / >=80% (frontend) on the changed package; no coverage regression

- [ ] QA verified against the acceptance criteria; no open P0/P1

- [ ] Nightly full-day job configured and passing

## Dependencies
`E23-T01` â€” the engine under test; `E23-T03` â€” the repair path exercised by the determinism-across-repair scenario. Shares the harness scaffolding built by `E18`.

title: Derivatives metrics: open interest, funding, liquidations and basis
body:
## Context
R2 "Order-flow beta" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#6-r2--order-flow-beta`, sprints S10-S13, tag `v0.3.0`, staging/demo) delivers DeepCharts-grade order-flow visibility. **E24 Derivatives metrics (OI, funding, liquidations, basis)** is the *positioning and carry* layer of that release. Roadmap scope line (§6.2): "Open-interest series with delta-OI; funding rate current + history + countdown using the `fundingInterval` actually read from instruments-info (not assumed 8 h); liquidation feed and liquidation-cluster overlay; basis vs index/mark; OI-vs-price quadrant classification (long build-up / short build-up / long liquidation / short covering)" - **34 pts, sprints S12-S13**, area `area/order-flow`, backend modules **M4** (ingestion/normalisation of the public `tickers` + `allLiquidation` streams, owned by E08) and **M9** (`server/orderflow/`, the derived-series engines), story domain **DERIV**.

Three facts from the plan documents shape every ticket in this epic and must not be re-litigated during implementation:

1. **The funding interval is instrument data, never a constant.** `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/funding` states it verbatim: "The funding interval is instrument-specific (`funding_interval_minutes`; 8 h common, some 1/2/4 h) - never assume 8 h." The value is read from the cached instruments-info snapshot (`GET /api/v1/instruments`, field `funding_interval_minutes`; Postgres `instruments.funding_interval_min` default 480) and is used for the countdown, the annualisation factor and the `funding_8h` session anchor alike.
2. **There is no exchange history endpoint for liquidations.** `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.6: "No REST history exists for liquidations - depth is strictly bounded by recorder uptime; the UI must state this." Every liquidation surface therefore renders the partial-history state naming the first available timestamp (R2 exit criterion #5), and `GET /api/v1/market/liquidations` reads only the locally recorded `liquidations` QuestDB table populated from `allLiquidation.{symbol}` (the legacy `liquidation` topic is retired).
3. **Liquidation heat / cluster zones are an inference, not exchange data.** US-DERIV-007's NFR: "never presented as exchange-provided data; excluded from any automated rule action by default." It therefore carries the mandatory CMP-227 `(estimated)` badge, is **off by default**, and links the methodology drawer SCR-058 (global AC #6, R2 exit criterion #4 - "A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic").

Everything numeric in this epic is a first-class `MetricDescriptor` in the `MetricRegistry` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 "Derivatives"): `open_interest`, `open_interest_value`, `open_interest_delta`, `oi_price_quadrant` (`long_buildup|short_covering|short_buildup|long_unwind`), `funding_rate`, `funding_annualized`, `time_to_funding_ms`, `basis`, `premium_pct`, `liquidation_notional`. That is the single-source invariant of R2: a rule, an alert and a derivatives pane always read the same number. There is exactly one `DerivativesEngine` in M9 and the UI is a renderer of its output - a second client-side computation of basis, annualised funding or OI delta is an explicit anti-goal.

Dependency per the roadmap graph (§11.1): `E08 --> E24`. E08 Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton owns the `tickers` stream normalisation (delta ticker frames merged against last full state before write, `21-database-schema.md` §4.4) and the public-stream connection manager that the liquidation socket plugs into. E16 Recorder supplies liquidation persistence and history depth (US-DERIV-005 `Deps: US-REC-001`). E11/E12 supply the chart-engine sub-pane, shared time axis and crosshair sync that US-DERIV-008's NFR requires ("all derivative series respect the same time axis and crosshair sync as price"). E17 owns the WS envelope/topic registry that `ticker.{symbol}` and `liquidations.{symbol}` live in.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories covered (all 8 of the DERIV domain, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §14):** US-DERIV-001 (Must, OI pane), US-DERIV-002 (Should, OI delta + price quadrant colouring), US-DERIV-003 (Must, funding rate/history/countdown), US-DERIV-004 (Should, predicted & annualised funding), US-DERIV-005 (Must, liquidation feed), US-DERIV-006 (Must, liquidation bars), US-DERIV-007 (Should, liquidation heat / cluster estimate), US-DERIV-008 (Should, basis, mark/index and long/short ratio).
- **Screens:** SCR-054 OI / funding / liquidations panel (the epic's home screen, `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md#scr-054`); SCR-058 Detector methodology drawer (new entry for the liquidation-cluster heuristic); SCR-030 Chart panel hosts the liquidation markers and the sub-pane.
- **Components:** CMP-186 OiFundingLiqPane (chart primitive), CMP-126 FundingCountdown, CMP-127 LiquidationMarker, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.
- **Backend (M4 + M9):** liquidation socket + normaliser and OI/funding extraction from the merged ticker snapshot (M4); `DerivativesEngine` (M9) computing OI delta, the OI/price quadrant, basis/premium, annualised funding, per-bar liquidation notional and the estimated liquidation-cluster bands; metric descriptors registered in the `MetricRegistry`.
- **Contracts:** REST `GET /api/v1/market/open-interest`, `GET /api/v1/market/funding`, `GET /api/v1/market/liquidations`, `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` (metrics `open_interest_delta`, `funding_basis`, `liquidation_intensity` and the derivatives descriptors), `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`; WS topics `ticker.{symbol}` / `ticker` (`TickerUpdate`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.8) and `liquidations.{symbol}` / `liquidations` (`LiquidationBatch`, §14.9, options `min_notional_usd`, `cluster_window_ms`).
- **Data:** QuestDB `tickers` (`open_interest`, `open_interest_value`, `funding_rate`, `next_funding_ts`, `basis`), `open_interest`, `funding_rates`, `liquidations` (`21-database-schema.md` §4.4-4.7); Postgres `instruments.funding_interval_min`, `settings` (scope `user`, keys `deriv.*`) for pane configuration and threshold memory; `stream_kind` enum values `liquidations`, `open_interest`, `funding` for recorder policy.
- **Design:** full design track for SCR-054, CMP-186/CMP-126/CMP-127 and the SCR-058 methodology entry, scheduled S10-S11 (>=2 sprints ahead of the S12-S13 engineering work), plus a design-QA sweep in S13.
- **QA:** black-box plan + exploratory charter, Playwright E2E additions, a liquidation-cascade perf script (500 prints/s sustained for 10 s), chaos scenarios (ticker staleness, REST backfill failure), a11y audit, epic regression pack and sign-off.
- **Security:** STRIDE model for the epic and a review of the backfill/pagination/estimation surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Options / GEX data - explicitly out of scope per the locked decisions in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`.
- Non-USDT-perp instruments and non-Bybit venues; the exchange-adapter abstraction is E08's.
- Funding-cost accounting against real positions (`funding_paid` on `trades_journal`) - E41 Journal.
- Alert conditions built on derivatives metrics (alert centre, notification routing) - E40 Alerts; this epic only guarantees the metrics are registered and queryable.
- Rule-engine actions driven by OI/funding - E35; and by explicit NFR the estimated liquidation zones are excluded from automated rule actions by default.
- The liquidation-price line for the *user's own position* (SCR-063 trading overlays, CMP-127 in its position sense) - E31/E32.
- CVD, footprint, profiles, DOM heatmap, detectors, replay - E18/E19/E21/E23/E25/E26.
- Android and a separate admin app.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One engine, one number
  Given the DerivativesEngine has computed open_interest_delta and basis for BTCUSDT bar 10:35
  When the SCR-054 pane, a GET /api/v1/market/metrics query and a rule condition each read those metrics
  Then all three return byte-identical values for the same bar and params
  And no derivatives value is recomputed client-side

Scenario: The funding interval is never assumed
  Given a symbol whose instruments-info funding_interval_minutes is 240
  When the funding countdown, the annualised rate and the funding history render
  Then all three use 240 minutes (6 settlements/day, annualisation factor 1460)
  And no code path contains a hard-coded 8-hour or 480-minute default outside the instruments table column default

Scenario: Honest liquidation history
  Given the recorder for BTCUSDT started 2 hours ago
  When I open the liquidation bars for a 24-hour range
  Then bars exist only for the recorded window, a boundary marker names the first available timestamp
  And the panel states that no exchange history endpoint exists for liquidations

Scenario: Estimated zones are labelled and off by default
  Given a fresh installation
  When I open SCR-054
  Then liquidation heat/cluster zones are disabled
  And enabling them requires acknowledging that the values are estimated
  And once enabled every zone renders a CMP-227 (estimated) badge linking SCR-058

Scenario: Cascade does not drop frames
  Given a liquidation cascade producing 500 prints/second for 10 seconds
  When the feed and the liquidation bars are both visible
  Then prints are coalesced into 250 ms buckets with a burst counter
  And panel scripting stays under 2 ms per frame with no dropped frames
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Module split.** M4 (ingestion) is responsible only for *sockets and normalisation*: the `allLiquidation.{symbol}` subscription, and extracting `openInterest`/`openInterestValue`/`fundingRate`/`nextFundingTime`/`markPrice`/`indexPrice` from the merged ticker snapshot. M9 (`orderflow`) hosts `DerivativesEngine`, which is pure and testable: `(ticker snapshots, funding rows, liquidation prints, bar grid, instrument metadata) -> metric series`. No HTTP or socket code inside M9.
- **OI resolution.** Two sources with different cadences coexist in the `open_interest` table, distinguished by `(interval, source)` in the dedup key: `source='rest'` rows at 5min..1d from `GET /v5/market/open-interest` (limit <=200/page), and `source='ws_ticker'` rows at 1 s derived from the recorded `tickers` stream. The UI never silently mixes them: when the chart interval is finer than the native REST granularity the pane shows the "native granularity 5 min" note (US-DERIV-001).
- **Quadrant classification** (`24-internal-schemas.md` §7, research 08 §6): price up + OI up = `long_buildup`; price up + OI down = `short_covering`; price down + OI up = `short_buildup`; price down + OI down = `long_unwind`. A bar with no OI sample is `None` - drawn neutral-hatched and excluded from classification, never defaulted to a quadrant.
- **Annualisation.** `funding_annualized = funding_rate * (525600 / funding_interval_minutes)`; `funding_rates.annualised_pct` stores it precomputed. Predicted (unsettled) rates come only from the ticker `fundingRate` field and are flagged `predicted: true, estimated: true` by `/market/funding`; the UI must render them in a visually distinct, text-labelled style and show `n/a` rather than a stale value when absent.
- **Basis.** `basis = last - index` (or `mark - index` when `source=mark`), `premium_pct = basis / index * 100`; `tickers.basis` is precomputed at ingest so `ASOF JOIN` queries stay cheap.
- **Liquidation clustering.** Two distinct things share the word "cluster": (a) `cluster_size` on `LiquidationBatch` / `cluster_window_ms` on `/market/liquidations`, which is *exact* grouping of prints within a time window - not estimated; (b) the liquidation *heat/zone* estimate of US-DERIV-007, derived from OI, leverage tiers and price distance - always estimated, off by default, documented in SCR-058.
- **Burst handling.** Bybit pushes `allLiquidation` at most once per symbol per 500 ms, so event counts are lower bounds - the UI states this. Client-side prints are coalesced into 250 ms buckets with a burst-rate counter rather than one DOM node per print (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-054 performance note).
- **Config keys** (Postgres `settings`, scope `user`): `deriv.oi.mode` (`absolute|delta`), `deriv.oi.quadrant_colouring`, `deriv.funding.style` (`line|bars`), `deriv.funding.annualised`, `deriv.liq.mode` (`bars|heatmap`), `deriv.liq.min_notional_usd`, `deriv.liq.zones_enabled` (default `false`), `deriv.basis.source` (`last|mark`), `deriv.basis.annualised`.
- **Error codes:** reuse the standard envelope; backfill failure surfaces as a retryable pane state carrying `last_success_at`, never a blank chart (US-DERIV-008 scenario 3).

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=85%):** quadrant classification truth table incl. the `None` case; annualisation across 1 h/2 h/4 h/8 h intervals; basis/premium; per-bar liquidation notional bucketing incl. day-boundary alignment; countdown arithmetic against a skewed clock offset; coalescing buffer.
- **Contract:** OpenAPI schema tests for `/market/open-interest`, `/market/funding`, `/market/liquidations`, `/market/metrics`; WS JSON-schema validation of `TickerUpdate` and `LiquidationBatch`.
- **Integration:** recorded Bybit fixtures - normal session, cascade burst, ticker delta-merge sequence, REST backfill 5xx/rate-limit (10018), symbol with a 4 h funding interval.
- **E2E (Playwright):** open SCR-054, toggle OI absolute/delta, enable quadrant colouring, switch funding style + annualise, filter liquidations by notional, enable estimated zones through the acknowledgement, verify partial-history chip.
- **Perf:** 500 prints/s for 10 s with panel scripting <2 ms/frame; WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms with the heaviest topic set including `ticker` + `liquidations` (budget #3, R2 hard gate).
- **Chaos:** ticker socket drop and resubscribe; REST backfill failure; clock-offset jump during a countdown.
- **Golden fixture:** a recorded symbol-day recomputed offline in DuckDB over the Parquet tier must match the engine's OI delta, basis, annualised funding and per-bar liquidation notional within float tolerance (R2 exit criterion #6 extended to derivatives).

## Security notes
Data classification: public market data only - no secrets, PII or account data flows through this epic, which keeps the threat surface narrow. Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` worth modelling: (T) tampering via a fabricated predicted-funding or estimated-zone value presented as exchange data - mitigated by the mandatory `estimated`/`predicted` flags at the schema level, not only in the UI; (I) information disclosure is nil-risk here but the endpoints still require `marketdata:read` per their `x-rbac` blocks and must not become an unauthenticated path; (D) denial of service via unbounded `from`/`to` ranges or `limit` on the three REST endpoints, and via a client subscribing `liquidations` with `symbols` over the cap - mitigated by pagination caps, cursor enforcement and subscription limits; (R) repudiation of "the tool told me OI was rising" - mitigated by recording the source (`ws_ticker` vs `rest`) on every stored point. A `security` review ticket (E24-X02) and a STRIDE model (E24-X01) are in scope.

## Accessibility notes
Per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` and SCR-054's catalogue entry: every sub-pane has a **table alternative** (the DOM-mirror pattern) so the data is readable without the canvas; the funding countdown is announced at 5 min and 1 min only (never per second); quadrant classification is conveyed by pattern + text legend, never colour alone; the `(estimated)` badge carries the literal word "estimated" in its accessible name (CMP-227 contract); liquidation side is labelled in text, not only by red/green; all controls are keyboard reachable with visible focus; contrast >=4.5:1 for text and >=3:1 for the pane's graphical boundaries in both themes.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: #1 frame time p95 <=16.6 ms with the full order-flow scene including this pane; #2 never below 30 fps in degraded mode; #3 WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms / p99 <250 ms (hard R2 gate). SCR-054 specific: OI and funding arrive at <=1 Hz and render on change only; liquidation prints coalesce into 250 ms buckets; the panel must not exceed **2 ms scripting per frame** during a cascade (500 prints/s sustained for 10 s, no dropped frames). REST backfill paging must respect Bybit's <=200 rows/page limit and stay inside the API read budget (#13, p95 <150 ms backend-internal).

## Observability
Metrics: `deriv_oi_backfill_pages_total{symbol,result}`, `deriv_oi_backfill_latency_seconds`, `deriv_funding_refresh_total{result}`, `deriv_liquidation_prints_total{symbol,side}`, `deriv_liquidation_burst_rate`, `deriv_ticker_staleness_seconds{symbol}`, `deriv_engine_compute_seconds{metric}`. Logs: structured warning on backfill failure with `symbol`, `interval`, `attempt`, `http_status`; warning when a ticker snapshot is stale beyond threshold. Traces: span per backfill job and per metric batch. Audit/analytics events from SCR-054: `oi_panel.metric_toggled`, `oi_panel.interval_changed`, plus a dedicated event when the estimated-zone acknowledgement is accepted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child Stories/Tasks/Spikes/Design/QA/Security tickets Done (100% rollup) or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] All 8 DERIV stories demonstrably satisfied end-to-end on SCR-054 against a recorded symbol-day.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on `server/orderflow/derivatives*` and the ingestion additions, >=80% on the frontend pane.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-054/SCR-058 reflect shipped behaviour; ADR-0017 merged.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-054, one manual screen-reader pass, table alternatives verified.
- [ ] perf: cascade benchmark and WS tick->screen p95 recorded against budgets #1/#3.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off comment.
- [ ] design: SCR-054 and CMP-186/126/127 signed off by the CDO track; design-QA sweep closed.
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression + exploratory pass recorded; zero open P0/P1.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review with explicit acceptance recorded.

## Dependencies
- **E08 Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton** (`E08 --> E24` in the roadmap graph): ticker delta-merge normalisation, public-stream connection manager, instruments-info cache with `funding_interval_minutes`.
- **E16 Recorder, retention & disk budget**: liquidation persistence and the recorded-history depth every liquidation view depends on (US-DERIV-005 `Deps: US-REC-001`).
- **E17 Market-data WS protocol & binary framing**: envelope, subscription lifecycle and topic registry for `ticker.*` / `liquidations.*`.
- **E11/E12 chart engine**: sub-pane hosting, shared time axis, crosshair sync, pane legend.
- **E05 Design system v0**: tokens and primitives the new components build on.

## Branch
`feat/e24-derivatives-*` per child ticket (e.g. `feat/e24-derivatives-oi-backfill`). PR size guidance: <=400 LOC diff; the engine, the endpoints and each pane surface are separate PRs.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §14 DERIV (US-DERIV-001..008)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-054, SCR-058
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-036, CMP-126, CMP-127, CMP-186, CMP-188, CMP-199, CMP-227

- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/open-interest`, `/market/funding`, `/market/liquidations`, `/market/metrics`, `/instruments`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, §14.8 `TickerUpdate`, §14.9 `LiquidationBatch`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 Derivatives metric table
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (sub-pane and marker primitives)
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §6 R2, §11.1 dependency graph
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `04-security-program.md`, `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`

## Child dependency graph

## Agent guidance

How to pick the next ticket in this epic when multiple agents are working it in parallel:

1. **Design track first** (E24-D01, E24-D02, E24-D03, E24-D04, E24-D05, E24-D06) must clear the design-ahead rule (Done ≥2 sprints before the Story that consumes it) before any Story in its lane starts — check each Story's own `blocked_by` for the exact design ticket.
2. **Spike/engineering foundation** (E24-K01, E24-T01, E24-T02, E24-T03, E24-T04, E24-T05, E24-T06) generally has no ticket dependency on the Stories and can start immediately in parallel with design — these define the wire contract and backend engines the Stories consume.
3. **Stories** (E24-S01, E24-S02, E24-S03, E24-S04, E24-S05, E24-S06, E24-S07, E24-S08) are blocked by their named Task/Spike and design ticket per each Story's own `blocked_by` list — do not start a Story until every key in its `blocked_by` is Done.
4. **QA** (E24-Q01, E24-Q02, E24-Q03, E24-Q04, E24-Q05) and **Security** (E24-X01, E24-X02) tracks run against the Stories/Tasks they test — pick these up once their named inputs are Done, not before.
5. **Parallel lanes**: two agents may safely work any two tickets that do not appear in each other's `blocked_by` chain and do not touch the same repo paths in the same PR window — check both before starting.
6. **Shared interfaces to agree first**: any change to a WS topic, REST path, DB table, or `MetricRegistry`/`MetricDescriptor` entry named across multiple children must be raised and agreed (PR to `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md`) before two agents implement against diverging assumptions.

title: DerivativesEngine and metric-descriptor registration in the MetricRegistry
body:
## Context
The single-source invariant of R2 is that a pane, a `/market/metrics` query and a rule condition read the same number. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 already fixes the derivatives descriptors: `open_interest`, `open_interest_value`, `open_interest_delta` (`OI(close) - OI(open)` per bar), `oi_price_quadrant` (`long_buildup|short_covering|short_buildup|long_unwind`), `funding_rate`, `funding_annualized`, `time_to_funding_ms`, `basis`, `premium_pct` (params `source=last|mark`), `liquidation_notional` (params `side=long|short|both`). This task implements the one engine in M9 that produces them and registers them so every consumer is a renderer, not a calculator.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/derivatives.py`: a pure `DerivativesEngine` taking `(ticker snapshots, OI rows, funding rows, liquidation prints, bar grid, instrument metadata)` and returning metric series. No HTTP, no socket, no QuestDB code inside it.
- Implement each descriptor above with its documented formula: `open_interest_delta` per bar from the OI series resampled onto the bar grid; the quadrant truth table; `funding_annualized = funding_rate * (525600 / funding_interval_minutes)`; `basis = last - index` (or `mark - index` when `source=mark`), `premium_pct = basis / index * 100`; `time_to_funding_ms` from `next_funding_time_ms` and the synced clock offset; `liquidation_notional` bucketed per bar and split by side, aligned to the bar grid and the UTC day boundary.
- **The None case is first-class:** a bar with no OI sample yields `open_interest_delta = None` and `oi_price_quadrant = None`; it is never defaulted to zero or to a quadrant (US-DERIV-002 scenario 3).
- Register every descriptor in the `MetricRegistry` with unit, params, bar-scoping and the `estimated` flag (all of these are `estimated: false`; only the E24-S07 zone overlay is estimated), and wire them into `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` alongside the already-declared codes `open_interest_delta`, `funding_basis` and `liquidation_intensity`.
- Expose the derivatives fields on the `ticker.{symbol}` WS payload per `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.8 (`open_interest`, `open_interest_value`, `funding_rate`, `next_funding_time_ms`, `mark_price`, `index_price`, `stale`).
- Incremental update path: on a new ticker snapshot or liquidation print, only the current bar's metrics are recomputed, not the whole window.

## Out of scope
Rendering (E24-S01..S08); the estimated liquidation-zone computation (E24-S07, which uses the E24-K01 method and is flagged estimated); alert/rule consumption (E40/E35, which only require the descriptors to exist).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One number everywhere
  Given the engine has computed open_interest_delta and basis for BTCUSDT bar 10:35
  When the SCR-054 pane, a GET /api/v1/market/metrics query and a rule condition each read those metrics
  Then all three return identical values for the same bar and params

Scenario: Quadrant truth table
  Given price up and OI up, price up and OI down, price down and OI up, price down and OI down
  Then the classification is long_buildup, short_covering, short_buildup and long_unwind respectively

Scenario: Missing OI is not a quadrant
  Given a bar for which no OI sample exists
  Then open_interest_delta and oi_price_quadrant are both None, and the bar is excluded from classification rather than defaulted

Scenario: Annualisation follows the instrument
  Given funding_interval_minutes is 240
  Then funding_annualized equals funding_rate multiplied by 525600/240

Scenario: Liquidation bucketing
  Given prints spanning a UTC day boundary on a 1h bar grid
  Then liquidation_notional buckets align to the bar grid and the day boundary, split by side, with no print counted twice or dropped

Scenario: Registry completeness
  When the MetricRegistry is enumerated
  Then all ten derivatives descriptors from 24-internal-schemas.md section 7 are present with unit, params and estimated flag, and a registry test fails if one is missing

Scenario: Incremental update
  Given a new ticker snapshot for the current bar
  Then only the current bar's metrics are recomputed and the result is identical to a full recompute over the window
```

## Technical notes / design
Decimal handling follows the platform convention (string-decimals on the wire, exact types internally) so a basis of 0.1 does not become 0.09999999. The bar grid is supplied by the bar builders (E12) - the engine never builds bars. Resampling OI onto a coarser bar grid uses last-value-at-or-before semantics with an explicit staleness bound; beyond the bound the sample is absent, which routes into the None case rather than carrying an old value forward indefinitely. The engine is deterministic given its inputs - a property E24-T06 exploits for the golden-fixture parity harness.

## Test plan
Unit: quadrant truth table incl. None; annualisation at 1 h/2 h/4 h/8 h; basis and premium for both sources; per-bar liquidation bucketing incl. the day boundary and the side split; countdown arithmetic against a skewed clock offset; resampling staleness bound; incremental-vs-full-recompute equivalence as a property test. Contract: `/market/metrics` schema test for each derivatives code; `TickerUpdate` schema validation. Integration: recorded symbol-day producing a full metric set. Coverage >=85% on `server/orderflow/derivatives*`.

## Security notes
(T) the `estimated` flag must be a property of the descriptor, not of the caller - the registry test asserts it; (R) each OI point retains its `source` so a displayed value is attributable. No secrets, no PII. Inputs come from already-validated internal stores, so the engine may assume schema validity but must still reject NaN/infinite inputs rather than propagating them into a rendered number.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend/engine. The descriptors' `unit` field is what the UI's table alternatives and accessible names are built from, so units must be correct and human-meaningful.

## Performance notes
`deriv_engine_compute_seconds{metric}` p95 <5 ms per incremental update for a visible window of 1 500 bars; a full recompute of that window <50 ms. Both recorded in the ticket. The engine is on the path to budget #3 (WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms).

## Observability
Metrics `deriv_engine_compute_seconds{metric}`, `deriv_engine_none_bars_total{reason}` (so silently missing OI is visible in Grafana rather than only on screen). Trace span per metric batch.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` behind review (2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner), conventional commits, PR <=400 LOC diff.
- [ ] Unit tests added; coverage >=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend on touched files.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md`.
- [ ] Plan docs updated where shipped behaviour diverged; ADR referenced if a decision was made.
- [ ] Storybook entries added/updated for touched components (UI tickets).
- [ ] axe-core CI green and one manual keyboard pass (UI tickets).
- [ ] Perf budget from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` measured and recorded in the ticket.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment recorded; zero open P0/P1 against this ticket.
- [ ] Design sign-off referenced (UI tickets) - the consuming design ticket is Status Done and >=2 sprints old.

## Dependencies
`E24-T01` (OI), `E24-T02` (funding), `E24-T03` (liquidations) supply the inputs; E12 supplies the bar grid; E11 consumes the output. Blocks `E24-S01`..`E24-S08` and `E24-T06`.

## Branch
`feat/e24-derivatives-engine`. PRs: engine core, registry + `/market/metrics` wiring, WS ticker fields.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §14 DERIV
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-054, SCR-058
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-036, CMP-126, CMP-127, CMP-186, CMP-188, CMP-199, CMP-227
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.14

title: Golden-fixture parity harness for derivatives metrics vs offline DuckDB
body:
## Context
R2's exit criteria require order-flow values to be provably correct, not merely plausible: a recorded symbol-day recomputed offline must match what the live engine produced. This epic's numbers (OI delta, quadrant, annualised funding, basis, per-bar liquidation notional) are exactly the kind that look right while being subtly wrong - an off-by-one bar boundary or a carried-forward stale OI sample is invisible on a chart. The harness makes that class of bug a failing test.

## Scope / Deliverables
- An independent reference implementation of each derivatives metric as SQL over the Parquet cold tier in DuckDB, written from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §7 rather than from the engine's code, so it is a genuine second opinion.
- A harness that replays a recorded symbol-day through the `DerivativesEngine` and diffs every metric series against the reference within a declared float tolerance, reporting the first divergent bar with both values.
- Coverage of the awkward cases in the fixture set: a bar with no OI sample; a funding settlement inside the window; a symbol with a non-8 h funding interval; a liquidation cascade; a UTC day boundary; a recorder gap.
- Determinism check: replaying the same fixture twice produces identical output, and an incremental replay matches a full recompute.
- Wired into CI as a scheduled (not per-PR) job because it is minutes-long, with a per-PR fast subset over a short fixture.

## Out of scope
Black-box functional testing (E24-Q01/Q02); load and cascade performance (E24-Q03); the estimated zone overlay, which has no ground truth to compare against and is validated by E24-K01's backtest instead.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Parity on a recorded symbol-day
  Given a recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day replayed through the engine
  When every derivatives metric series is diffed against the DuckDB reference
  Then all series match within the declared tolerance and the job passes

Scenario: A divergence is actionable
  Given an injected off-by-one in the bar bucketing
  Then the harness fails and names the metric, the first divergent bar timestamp and both values

Scenario: Awkward cases included
  Then the fixture set contains a no-OI bar, a funding settlement, a 4-hour-interval symbol, a cascade, a UTC day boundary and a recorder gap, each asserted explicitly

Scenario: Determinism
  When the same fixture is replayed twice
  Then the outputs are byte-identical, and an incremental replay matches a full recompute

Scenario: CI wiring
  Then the full harness runs on a schedule and a fast subset runs per PR, and a failure of either blocks the release train
```

## Technical notes / design
Reference SQL lives under `tests/golden/e24/` next to the fixture manifest. Tolerance is declared per metric (exact for counts and classifications such as `oi_price_quadrant`; a small relative epsilon for floating-point ratios such as `premium_pct`) - a classification metric must match exactly, since 'nearly the right quadrant' is meaningless. Fixtures are referenced by id from the shared recorded-fixture store established in E16, not copied into the repo.

## Test plan
The harness is itself the test; it is validated by mutation - deliberately perturbing the engine (shifted bar boundary, carried-forward OI, 8 h interval assumption) must make it fail. Those mutation cases are committed as expected-fail tests.

## Security notes
Detects silent data-integrity regressions, which is the epic's primary risk; a persistent unexplained divergence is treated as a security-relevant integrity finding and escalated to E24-X02 rather than quietly re-baselined.

## Accessibility notes
N/A

## Performance notes
The scheduled job must complete within the CI budget for long jobs; the per-PR subset must add <2 minutes to the pipeline. Record both.

## Observability
Publishes a per-metric divergence count as a CI artefact so slow drift is visible across runs rather than only on a hard failure.

- [ ] Code merged to `main` behind review (2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner), conventional commits, PR <=400 LOC diff.

title: Author the black-box test plan and exploratory charters for detectors
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature alongside the white-box review. This epic needs one that is unusually explicit about *honesty* and *determinism*, because those are R2 exit criteria (#4 and #7) rather than ordinary quality attributes, and neither is naturally covered by functional testing of the happy path.

The roadmap also names the integration fixture classes for R2: "normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol". Detector behaviour differs sharply across them - a thin-book symbol is the false-positive-rich case for iceberg, a volatility burst is the sweep-rich case for stop-run - so the plan must exercise each deliberately.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Black-box test plan covering all nine DET stories, organised by story group: (a) tape and book speed, (b) imbalance stacks, (c) absorption/iceberg/stop-run, (d) regime, (e) configuration and methodology.
- Per group: preconditions, test data/fixture, steps, expected results, and the failure and edge cases named in each story's Gherkin (idle market, warming up, depth-tier change, no-reversion, insufficient data, missing dependency, out-of-range value, unauthorised change).
- The **honesty checklist** required by the R2 quality gates: "per estimated view: badge present, popover accurate, thresholds visible in the inspector" - enumerated per surface, executable by a tester with no knowledge of the implementation.
- Exploratory charters (session-based, 90 minutes each): "explore detector behaviour on a thin-book symbol looking for implausible events"; "explore the settings dialog looking for ways to apply a change without the armed-rule warning"; "explore the estimated affordance looking for any heuristic value with no badge"; "explore state transitions during WS disconnect and resync looking for values that keep updating when they should be stale".
- Fixture requirements handed to the engineering tickets: which recorded windows are needed and what each must contain (a stop-run, a multi-reload level, an absorption event, at least two regime transitions).
- Traceability table mapping every test case to a US-DET id and every US-DET id to at least one case.
- Entry and exit criteria for QA on this epic, and the definition of the regression pack that E25-Q05 will run.

## Out of scope
Executing the plan (done through the sprint and finalised in E25-Q05), automated E2E implementation (E25-Q02), performance scripts (E25-Q03), the a11y audit (E25-Q04), unit tests (owned by the engineering tickets).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full story coverage
  Then every one of US-DET-001 to US-DET-009 maps to at least one test case
  And every Gherkin scenario in those stories maps to a test case, including the failure and edge cases

Scenario: Honesty checklist is executable
  Then the plan lists every surface that renders a heuristic value with a per-surface check for badge presence, popover accuracy and threshold visibility
  And a tester with no implementation knowledge can execute it

Scenario: Fixture classes covered
  Then the plan exercises normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect and resync, sequence gap and thin-book symbol

Scenario: Exploratory charters defined
  Then at least four time-boxed charters are defined with a mission and a debrief template

Scenario: Reviewed
  Then the plan is reviewed and accepted by the product owner and the M9 engineer
```

## Technical notes / design
Write the honesty checklist as a table of `(surface, element, expected badge, expected drawer section)` so it is mechanical to run and can later be partly automated in E25-Q02. Its value is that it does not depend on a tester remembering the rule.

For determinism, the plan's role is to specify the *observable* check (two replays of the same window produce the same event list in the UI); the automated equality assertion lives in E25-Q03.

## Test plan
Self-referential: this ticket produces the plan. Its own quality gate is the traceability table and the review.

## Security notes
The plan includes the abuse cases from E25-X01 as test cases: unauthorised threshold change, threshold change without the armed-rule warning, and detector-driven armed action without acknowledgement. QA verifies controls, not merely features.

## Accessibility notes
The plan references E25-Q04 for the audit but includes basic keyboard-operability checks in every functional case, so a keyboard regression is caught during normal testing rather than only at audit time.

## Performance notes
The plan defines the observational perf checks (panel feels responsive at 4 Hz; no visible jank when markers cluster) and defers measurement to E25-Q03.

## Observability
The plan includes verification that the analytics and audit events named in the screens catalogue actually fire, since several of them (notably `methodology.opened` and `detector.threshold_changed`) exist for compliance and product-learning reasons.

## Definition of Done
Plan published in the QA space and linked from the epic; traceability table complete in both directions; exploratory charters defined; fixture requirements communicated to the engineering tickets in time to be built; reviewed and accepted by the product owner and the M9 engineer; entry/exit criteria agreed.

`blocked_by` E25-T02 (the detector framework defines the configurable surface the plan tests). Blocks Q02, Q03, Q04.

`chore/detectors-test-plan`. PR size guidance: documents.

title: Build MetricsEngine: rolling tape and book statistics with z-scores
body:
## Context
Every DET surface reads from one backend engine. US-DET-001 (Speed of tape, Must), US-DET-002 (Tape acceleration, Should) and US-DET-003 (Book speed, Should) are all *rolling statistics over the normalised trade and book streams*, and their screen contracts (SCR-055) state explicitly: "Rolling statistics are computed backend-side and pushed on `metrics.{symbol}` at 4 Hz; the panel renders at <=4 Hz with a 1 ms budget and **never recomputes z-scores client-side over a long window**."

`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` fixes the transport: one topic `metrics.{symbol}`, options `metrics[]`, `bar_type`, `param`, per-metric `params`, default throttle 250 ms, no binary frame. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` fixes the vocabulary: `tape_speed` (`window_ms=1000`, exact), `tape_speed_zscore` (`fast_ms=1000`, `base_ms=300000`, alert `>3.0`, exact). The OpenAPI description of `/market/metrics` names the codes as `trades_per_sec` / `volume_per_sec` / `book_updates_per_sec` (windows 1 s / 5 s / 30 s) and `tape_acceleration` (1 s vs 300 s baseline, alert >3x).

This task creates the engine and the publishing path that T02-T06 then plug detectors into.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/metrics_engine.py` (module M9): a per-symbol `MetricsEngine` consuming the normalised `publicTrade` stream and the reconstructed book deltas from E21, maintaining ring buffers for the 1 s / 5 s / 30 s windows and a 300 s baseline.
- Metric codes produced here: `trades_per_sec`, `volume_per_sec` (notional per second), `book_updates_per_sec`, `tape_acceleration` (z-score of fast window vs baseline), `imbalance_ratio` passthrough, plus the book-derived `book_imbalance`, `book_thickness`, `spread_ticks`, `realized_vol_1m`, `atr_14`.
- Per-side split of tape speed (buy/sell prints per second) as required by SCR-055 ("optionally split by side").
- Publication on WS `metrics.{symbol}` honouring `metrics[]` selection and `throttle_ms` (default 250 ms), in the `MetricsUpdate` frame shape defined in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 14.7, with `estimated` set per metric from the vocabulary.
- REST backfill via `GET /api/v1/market/metrics` for these codes, returning `MetricSeries` with `params` echo and `unit` (`ratio`, `index`, `base_volume`).
- Persistence at the fixed 1 s cadence into QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` columns `trades_per_sec`, `notional_per_sec`, `book_imbalance`, `book_thickness`, `spread_ticks`, `realized_vol_1m`, `atr_14` (DEDUP UPSERT KEYS(ts, symbol)).
- Explicit zero on idle: with no prints in the window the value is `0`, never the last value (US-DET-001 scenario "Idle market").
- "Warming up" semantics: while the baseline window has fewer than `min_samples` the z-score series emits `null` with `meta.warming_up_remaining_ms` (US-DET-002 scenario "Baseline too short").
- Depth-tier renormalisation: when the subscribed book depth tier changes, `book_updates_per_sec` is renormalised and a `meta.renormalised_at` marker is emitted on the series (US-DET-003 scenario "Depth-tier dependence").
- Prometheus counters/histograms listed under Observability.

## Out of scope
Detector heuristics (T02-T04), regime classification (T05), imbalance stacks (T06), any UI, the calm/normal/nervous *labelling* thresholds' presentation (the engine emits the classification string; the panel renders it), alert dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tape speed and notional
  Given a stream of publicTrade messages for BTCUSDT
  When the 5 second window is requested
  Then trades_per_sec and volume_per_sec are published at 4 Hz on metrics.BTCUSDT
  And each series carries its window length in params

Scenario: Window change recomputes immediately
  Given a subscription with window 5s
  When the client resubscribes with window 1s
  Then the next published value is computed over the 1 second window, not a decayed 5 second value
  And the effective window is echoed in the subscribe acknowledgement

Scenario: Idle market reads zero
  Given no prints have arrived for 10 seconds
  Then trades_per_sec publishes 0 explicitly rather than holding the last value

Scenario: Warming up
  Given the 300 second baseline has fewer than the minimum samples
  Then tape_acceleration publishes null with the remaining warm-up time in meta
  And no z-score is published until the baseline is filled

Scenario: Depth tier change
  Given the book subscription changes from depth 200 to depth 50
  Then book_updates_per_sec is renormalised and the series carries a renormalisation marker at that timestamp

Scenario: One subscription carries the family
  Given a client subscribes to metrics.BTCUSDT with metrics ["trades_per_sec","book_updates_per_sec","tape_acceleration"]
  Then all three arrive on one subscription within the throttle interval
```

## Technical notes / design
Ring buffers are fixed-size arrays of (timestamp, value) indexed by a monotonic counter, not deques of Python objects, to hold budget #8. Maintain incremental sums so a window read is O(1): on each event push and evict expired entries by timestamp; recompute the sum by add/subtract rather than re-summing. The baseline keeps Welford running mean/variance over 1 s buckets so the z-score is `(fast - mean) / stdev` with `stdev` floored to avoid division blow-ups in dead markets; when `stdev` is below the floor the z-score publishes `null` rather than a huge number.

Clock-agnostic by construction: the engine takes timestamps from the event, never from `time.time()`, so E26 replay drives it unchanged. This is a hard review item - a `time.time()` call in this module is a defect.

Interface sketch:

```python
class MetricsEngine:
    def on_trade(self, ev: TradeEvent) -> None: ...
    def on_book_delta(self, ev: BookDeltaEvent) -> None: ...
    def sample(self, ts_ms: int) -> list[MetricSample]: ...  # called on the publish tick
```

`MetricSample` carries `metric`, `value`, `unit`, `estimated`, `params`, `meta`. Publishing is done by the existing WS fan-out; the engine never touches sockets.

Config keys: `orderflow.metrics.publish_hz` (default 4), `orderflow.metrics.persist_hz` (1), `orderflow.metrics.baseline_ms` (300000), `orderflow.metrics.min_baseline_samples` (60).

## Test plan
- Unit: window eviction at boundaries; O(1) incremental sum equals a naive re-sum over 10 000 random events; idle-window zero; z-score against a hand-computed fixture; stdev floor produces null; warming-up countdown; renormalisation marker on tier change; per-side split sums to the total.
- Property test: for random event streams, `trades_per_sec` over window W equals `count(events in [t-W, t]) / W` within float tolerance.
- Determinism: the same fixture replayed twice yields identical sample streams (feeds E25-Q03).
- Contract: WS `metrics.{symbol}` frames validate against `cv://ws/v1/metrics.schema.json`; REST responses validate against `MetricsResponse`.
- Integration: recorded BTCUSDT fixture covering normal session, volatility burst and a WS disconnect/resync.
- Perf: 2 000 trades/s plus 100 ms book cadence sustained for 10 minutes within budget #11.
- Coverage >=85 % on the module.

## Security notes
Public market data, but the subscription is session-gated and requires `marketdata:read` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` x-rbac on `/market/metrics`).
