title: Detector framework, config persistence and the three detector endpoints
body:
## Context
US-DET-009 (Must) requires "one place to configure all detectors and see their assumptions", with per-symbol overrides, an explicit disabled state naming a missing data dependency, and an info popover documenting each method. SCR-059's analytics/audit section is unambiguous about why this is not ordinary settings plumbing: "`detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed` with `{detector, key, before, after}` - **audited**, because detector output can feed armed rules that place orders."

The API surface already exists in the contract: `GET|PUT /api/v1/detectors/config` (`DetectorConfig`, `settings:write` scope `self` for PUT, `marketdata:read` for GET), `GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology` (`DetectorMethodology[]`), `GET /api/v1/market/regime/explain` (`RegimeExplanation`). This task builds the framework those endpoints sit on: a `DetectorRegistry`, a uniform `Detector` interface, the `DetectorEvent` bus that alerts/rules/journal later consume, and config storage with global and per-symbol layers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/detectors/base.py`: `Detector` protocol - `id`, `estimated: bool`, `required_inputs: list[str]`, `on_trade`, `on_book_delta`, `on_bar_close`, `configure(params)`, emitting `DetectorEvent(detector, symbol, ts_ms, price, direction, magnitude, confidence, estimated, params_snapshot, meta)`.
- `server/orderflow/detectors/registry.py`: registration, per-symbol instantiation, feature-flag gating on `metrics.iceberg_detector`, `metrics.stop_run_detector`, `metrics.absorption` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` feature-flag table, all default `false`), and dependency checking (a detector whose `required_inputs` are not being recorded for the symbol is reported `disabled_missing_dependency` with the exact missing input name).
- `DetectorEvent` publication onto the shared in-process event bus and onto `metrics.{symbol}` as event-like metric points (`MetricPoint.meta` carries "per-point detail for event-like metrics (iceberg, stop_run, absorption)" per the OpenAPI schema), plus persistence of the score columns `iceberg_score`, `stoprun_score`, `absorption_score` in `orderflow_metrics`.
- Config storage in Postgres: a global `DetectorConfig` row plus per-symbol override rows; effective config = global merged with symbol override; the response marks which keys are overridden.
- Endpoint implementations: `GET /detectors/config`, `PUT /detectors/config` (validates against the published bounds: iceberg `min_reloads` 2-50, `price_tolerance_ticks` 0-10, `window_ms` 200-60000; stop_run `lookback_bars` 2-500, `penetration_ticks` 1-100, `reversal_pct` 0-100; absorption `min_volume_multiple` 1-50, `max_price_move_ticks` 0-50; exhaustion `min_delta_divergence` >=0), `GET /detectors/methodology` (content supplied by T07).
- Audit: every enable/threshold change writes an append-only audit record per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 8 with `{actor, detector, key, before, after, symbol_scope}`.
- Apply semantics required by SCR-059: "Changes are applied server-side and take effect on the next evaluation window (<=2 s); the dialog shows 'applied' only after the backend confirms, never optimistically" - so PUT returns only once the registry has re-configured live instances.
- Dependency-check endpoint data: the `GET /detectors/config` response includes, per detector, `state` (`enabled` / `disabled` / `disabled_missing_dependency`), the missing input, and `events_today` for the SCR-059 and SCR-058 displays.

## Out of scope
The individual heuristics (T03, T04), regime (T05), imbalance stacks (T06), methodology *content* (T07), the UI (S05), alert routing and cooldown (ALRT domain), rule-engine binding (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Effective config with per-symbol override
  Given a global iceberg min_reloads of 3
  And an ETHUSDT override of 5
  When GET /api/v1/detectors/config is requested for ETHUSDT
  Then min_reloads is 5 and the response marks that key as overridden

Scenario: Bounds enforced
  When PUT /api/v1/detectors/config sets iceberg.min_reloads to 99
  Then the request is rejected with a validation error naming the permitted range 2 to 50
  And no audit record of a change is written

Scenario: Change is audited and confirmed only after it takes effect
  When an authorised user changes stop_run.reversal_pct from 60 to 45
  Then an append-only audit record is written with detector, key, before, after and actor
  And the response returns only after the live detector instances have been reconfigured
  And the new value is in force within 2 seconds

Scenario: Missing dependency
  Given BTCUSDT has no recorded L2 book history
  Then the iceberg detector reports state disabled_missing_dependency naming the missing input
  And it emits no events

Scenario: Feature flag off
  Given the feature flag metrics.iceberg_detector is false
  Then no iceberg detector instance is created and the config endpoint reports the detector as disabled with the flag as the reason

Scenario: Unauthorised change
  Given a Viewer-role session
  When PUT /api/v1/detectors/config is called
  Then the request is rejected with 403 and the attempt is logged
```

## Technical notes / design
The registry owns lifecycle, not the detectors: detectors are pure state machines fed by the engine loop, which makes replay (E26) free - the same instances are driven by replayed events. Reconfiguration replaces the params snapshot on the next evaluation boundary, never mid-window, so an event can always be attributed to exactly one parameter set (`params_snapshot` on every `DetectorEvent` exists for this reason and is what SCR-058 renders as "thresholds in force").

Postgres tables: `detector_config(scope, symbol, detector, params_json, updated_at, updated_by)` with `scope in ('global','symbol')` and a unique key on `(scope, symbol, detector)`. Audit rows go to the existing append-only audit table; no update or delete path exists.

Error codes: `DETECTOR_UNKNOWN`, `DETECTOR_PARAM_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `DETECTOR_DEPENDENCY_MISSING`, `DETECTOR_DISABLED_BY_FLAG`.

## Test plan
- Unit: config merge precedence; every published bound rejected at both ends and accepted at the boundary; audit record shape; dependency resolution; flag gating; params_snapshot immutability within a window.
- Contract: `/detectors/config` GET and PUT against the OpenAPI schema (round-trip PUT then GET returns exactly what was set); `/detectors/methodology` shape.
- Integration: change a threshold, assert the next event carries the new `params_snapshot` and that it took <=2 s.
- Security: RBAC matrix test - Viewer 403, Manager/Owner per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7; audit written on every accepted change and on every rejected attempt.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
This is the highest-value tampering target in the epic: detector thresholds feed armed rules that place orders (STRIDE-T, STRIDE-R in E25-X01). Controls: `settings:write` on PUT, append-only audit with actor identity, published bounds enforced server-side (never trust the dialog), no mass-assignment (`additionalProperties: false` on `DetectorConfig` is enforced, unknown keys rejected), and a rate limit on PUT to prevent audit-log flooding. Data classification: configuration = internal; market data = public.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend) - but the API must return human-readable reason strings for disabled states so the UI never has to synthesise them.

## Performance notes
Config reads are cached in-process and invalidated on write; the read path must not hit Postgres per evaluation. Budget #13: `/detectors/config` GET p95 <150 ms, PUT p95 <300 ms backend-internal. Detector dispatch overhead (registry loop, excluding heuristic work) <=5 microseconds per event.

## Observability
`orderflow_detector_events_total{detector,symbol}`, `orderflow_detector_eval_seconds{detector}`, `orderflow_detector_state{detector,symbol,state}` (gauge), `detector_config_changes_total{detector,key}`. Audit events `detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed`. WARN log when a detector is auto-disabled for a missing dependency.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 4.2: merged with 2 approvals including the M9 code owner and a security reviewer (label `security`); contract tests green against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; migration for `detector_config` written and reversible; RBAC tests green; audit verified end to end; Grafana panels added.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T01 (engine loop and event plumbing) and E25-X01 (the STRIDE model must name the controls before the config write path is built). Blocks T03, T04, T06 and S05.

## Branch
`feat/detectors-framework`. PR size guidance: (1) base/registry, (2) config storage + migration, (3) endpoints + RBAC/audit.

title: Implement absorption and iceberg detectors (estimated) in M9
body:
## Context
Implements the backend of **US-DET-005 Absorption detector (Must)** - "aggression fails to move price ... an absorption marker is drawn with its magnitude and an (estimated) badge", NFR: "detection is deterministic given the same inputs, validated against recorded fixtures in CI" - and **US-DET-006 Iceberg / hidden-order detector (Should)** - "a level is consumed and refilled at least N times within the window ... flagged with the refill count and an (estimated) badge", NFR: "never used as the sole trigger for an automated live action unless the user explicitly acknowledges the estimate".

Bybit's public feed is anonymous and aggregated and exposes no L3/MBO data, so iceberg, stop-run, absorption and regime are inferences, not observations. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` makes `confidence="estimated"` mandatory for every heuristic and states plainly that "presenting a heuristic as a certainty is a defect". Every surface that shows one of these values must render CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linked to SCR-058, the detector methodology drawer. US-DET-006's third scenario is a product requirement, not a nicety: "the info popover states plainly that Bybit exposes no L3/MBO data and this is an L2-derived inference".

Parameters come from `DetectorConfig` as published, refined by the E25-K01 calibration report.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/detectors/absorption.py`: aggressive volume at a price over the evaluation window exceeding `min_volume_multiple` times the rolling median while the price advance stays within `max_price_move_ticks`; emits `DetectorEvent(detector="absorption", magnitude=absorbed_volume, direction=side_absorbed, estimated=True)`.
- `server/orderflow/detectors/iceberg.py`: per-price resting-size tracking from book deltas; a reload is counted when size at a price is consumed below a fraction of its prior resting size and returns within `price_tolerance_ticks` and the size tolerance inside `window_ms`; a candidate is flagged at `min_reloads`; emits `magnitude=reload_count` and `meta.executed_volume` (the `iceberg_executed_volume` metric of `24-internal-schemas.md`).
- Metric codes published on `metrics.{symbol}`: `absorption`, `iceberg` (both `estimated: true`), with per-event detail in `MetricPoint.meta`.
- Score persistence into `orderflow_metrics.absorption_score` and `.iceberg_score`.
- Recompute over the loaded range on a threshold change (US-DET-005 scenario "Thresholds"), driven server-side with a visible recompute state - the client never recomputes.
- Bounded per-price state with an eviction policy (levels untouched for `window_ms * k` are dropped) so memory holds under budget #8.
- Golden-fixture test data committed for the CI determinism gate.

## Out of scope
Stop-run (T04), regime (T05), chart markers and the event card UI (S06), settings UI (S05), methodology copy (T07), alerting (ALRT), the exhaustion detector (config surface exists, but exhaustion is delivered with the footprint/divergence work in E18/E23).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Absorption flagged
  Given aggressive volume at a price exceeds min_volume_multiple times the rolling median
  And the price advance stays within max_price_move_ticks
  Then an absorption event is emitted with its magnitude, the absorbed side and estimated true

Scenario: Threshold change recomputes
  When the absorption volume threshold or price tolerance is changed
  Then detection is recomputed server-side over the loaded range
  And the recompute is observable as a state, not as a silent gap

Scenario: Iceberg replenishment
  Given a price level is consumed and refilled at least min_reloads times within window_ms
  Then an iceberg candidate is emitted with the refill count and estimated true

Scenario: False-positive control
  When min_reloads is raised
  Then strictly fewer or equal candidates are flagged over the same fixture
  And the active parameters are present in the event's params snapshot

Scenario: Determinism
  Given the same recorded fixture is replayed twice
  Then the emitted absorption and iceberg event streams are byte-identical

Scenario: Never silently exact
  Then every absorption and iceberg point published on metrics.{symbol} has estimated set to true
```

## Technical notes / design
Both detectors are pure state machines over `(TradeEvent | BookDeltaEvent)` with no wall-clock access, so replay drives them unchanged. The iceberg tracker keeps a small per-price record `(last_size, peak_size, reloads, first_seen_ms, last_reload_ms, executed_volume)` in a dict keyed by integer tick index, capped at the subscribed depth plus a margin; eviction is a periodic sweep at the evaluation boundary, not per event.

Absorption's rolling median is computed over a fixed-size window of per-price aggressive volumes using a two-heap structure so the update is O(log n); the median rather than the mean is deliberate - a single block print must not define "normal".

Cooldown: each detector suppresses repeat events at the same price within its own window and counts suppressions, so a level that keeps reloading yields one event with a growing reload count rather than a stream.

Determinism rules (enforced in review): no `time.time()`, no `set`/`dict` iteration order dependence in output ordering (sort emissions by `(ts_ms, price, detector)`), no floating-point accumulation across the whole session - window sums are rebuilt at the window boundary.

## Test plan
- Unit: absorption triggers exactly at the threshold and not one tick below; price-move tolerance boundary; median window; iceberg reload counting with and without the tick tolerance; eviction does not lose an in-flight candidate; cooldown suppression counting; monotonicity property - raising `min_reloads` never increases the event count on a fixed fixture.
- Golden fixture: one recorded BTCUSDT symbol-day with a committed expected event stream; any drift fails CI (roadmap section 6.4 "Correctness" gate).
- Determinism: double-run equality (roadmap section 6.4 "Determinism" gate; also exercised by E25-Q03).
- Integration: fixtures for normal session, high-volatility burst and thin book; assert event rates land within the bands recommended by E25-K01.
- Perf: microbenchmark per trade and per book delta; combined detector cost within the M9 share of budget #11.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Detector output can feed armed rules (E35). US-DET-006's NFR is a hard control: the event carries `estimated=True` and `requires_acknowledgement=True` so the rule engine can refuse to arm a live action on it alone without explicit user acknowledgement. Resource exhaustion: per-price state is bounded and the recompute path is range-limited and rate-limited (STRIDE-D). No PII.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend). Events carry a text `direction` and a numeric `magnitude` so the UI never needs colour alone.

## Performance notes
Budget #11 (<=0.5 vCPU per symbol, whole of M9) and budget #8 (<=300 MB per symbol) - the per-price iceberg state is the memory risk and must be measured, with the measured figure recorded on the ticket. Evaluation must add <=2 ms p95 to the engine tick so budget #6 (<=20 ms fan-out add-on) holds.

## Observability
`orderflow_detector_events_total{detector="absorption"|"iceberg",symbol}`, `orderflow_detector_eval_seconds{detector}`, `orderflow_detector_suppressed_total{detector,reason="cooldown"}`, `orderflow_iceberg_tracked_levels{symbol}` (gauge). INFO log on recompute start/finish with the range and the resulting event delta.

## Definition of Done
Per section 4.2 of the DoR/DoD: merged with 2 approvals including the M9 code owner; golden fixture and determinism tests in CI; coverage >=85 %; K01's recommended defaults applied (or the deviation justified in the PR); `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` metric-vocabulary rows confirmed accurate; feature flags remain default-off until E25-Q03 signs off the calibration.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T02 (framework, config, event bus), E25-K01 (calibrated parameters and false-positive-mode wording), E18 (footprint aggregation supplies the per-price aggressive volume that absorption consumes).

## Branch
`feat/detectors-absorption-iceberg`. PR size guidance: one PR per detector plus one for the golden fixtures.

title: Implement market-regime classifier and /market/regime/explain
body:
## Context
Implements the backend of **US-DET-008 Market regime classifier (Must)**: "a badge shows the current regime with a confidence value and the sub-signals used (book thickness, realised volatility, tape speed)"; disabling a sub-signal recomputes the classification "using the remaining signals and states its composition"; and when the lookback cannot be filled "the badge reads 'insufficient data' rather than defaulting to a regime". NFR: "classification exposed as `regime` to the rule DSL; transitions emit events; (estimated) badge mandatory."

The contract is already fixed. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` defines `RegimeExplanation` with `regime` in `[trending_up, trending_down, ranging, volatile_expansion, compression]`, `confidence` 0-1, `as_of`, and `signals[]` each with `name`, `value`, `weight`, `contribution`, `direction` in `[supports, opposes, neutral]` - "so the regime badge is explainable rather than an opaque verdict". `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` names the composition: `market_regime` = enum from **ADX + Hurst + ATR%**, confidence basis **estimated**; and the OpenAPI `/market/metrics` description lists `adx` (14), `atr` (14), `hurst` (R/S window 256), `regime` (combined ADX/Hurst classification). QuestDB `orderflow_metrics` stores `regime` (SYMBOL, 'trend_up'|'trend_down'|'range'|'volatile'|'calm') and `regime_confidence`.

R9 applies: a regime badge must read as a *classification with evidence*, never as a recommendation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/regime.py`: computes `adx(14)`, `atr(14)`, `hurst` (R/S, window 256), `realized_vol_1m`, plus the order-flow sub-signals `book_thickness` and `trades_per_sec` from E25-T01 and CVD slope from E23; combines them into the published enum with a confidence in 0-1 and a per-signal contribution.
- Sub-signal enable/disable: the classifier accepts a signal mask; disabling a signal reweights the remainder and the response states the composition actually used (US-DET-008 scenario 2).
- Insufficient-data state: when any required lookback is unfilled, the classifier publishes `regime = null` with `meta.reason = "insufficient_data"` and the missing lookback named - never a default regime.
- Publication on `metrics.{symbol}` as the `regime` metric at **at most 1 Hz** (SCR-057 performance section), `estimated: true`; persistence into `orderflow_metrics.regime` and `.regime_confidence` at the 1 s cadence; enum mapping between the API enum and the QuestDB SYMBOL values documented in one place.
- **Transition events**: a change of classification emits a `DetectorEvent(detector="regime", meta={from, to, confidence})` onto the shared bus, which is what the SCR-057 transition strip and the rule DSL consume.
- `GET /api/v1/market/regime/explain?symbol` returning `RegimeExplanation` computed from the same evaluation that produced the current badge - the explanation must never be recomputed independently, or badge and explanation could disagree.
- Hysteresis so the badge does not flicker between regimes on a boundary value, with the hysteresis band documented and exposed in the explanation.

## Out of scope
The panel UI (E25-S03), methodology copy (T07), the ADX/ATR indicator *rendering* (E17 indicators), CVD computation (E23), rule DSL binding (E35), any ML classifier (explicitly out of R2 scope), OI-trend sub-signal beyond what E24 already publishes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Classification with evidence
  Given sufficient history for all enabled sub-signals
  Then the regime metric publishes one of trending_up, trending_down, ranging, volatile_expansion, compression
  And a numeric confidence between 0 and 1
  And GET /market/regime/explain returns each sub-signal with its value, weight, contribution and direction

Scenario: Sub-signal disabled
  When tape speed is disabled as an input
  Then the classification is recomputed from the remaining signals
  And the explanation states the composition actually used

Scenario: Insufficient data
  Given the Hurst lookback of 256 samples cannot be filled
  Then the regime publishes null with reason insufficient_data naming the unfilled lookback
  And no regime enum value is published

Scenario: Transition emits an event
  Given the classification changes from ranging to trending_up
  Then a regime transition event is emitted with from, to and confidence

Scenario: Badge and explanation agree
  When the explain endpoint is called immediately after a published regime value
  Then it returns the same regime, confidence and as_of timestamp as the published value

Scenario: Always estimated
  Then the regime metric is published with estimated true
```

## Technical notes / design
One evaluation produces one immutable `RegimeVerdict(as_of, regime, confidence, signals[], composition, hysteresis_band)`; the WS publisher and the explain endpoint both read that object from a per-symbol cache. This is the only way to satisfy "badge and explanation agree" and it also makes the explain endpoint free (SCR-057: "the sub-signal breakdown is fetched once per change, not polled").

Confidence is the normalised margin between the winning class score and the runner-up, clamped to 0-1, so it is interpretable rather than arbitrary; the definition is written into the methodology content (T07) verbatim.

Hurst via rescaled range over a 256-sample window using incremental partial sums; ADX and ATR reuse the existing indicator implementations from the indicator engine rather than being re-implemented here - a second ADX would be a correctness hazard. Evaluation is driven by event timestamps (clock-agnostic) for replay parity.

Config keys: `orderflow.regime.publish_hz` (1), `orderflow.regime.hurst_window` (256), `orderflow.regime.adx_period` (14), `orderflow.regime.atr_period` (14), `orderflow.regime.hysteresis` (default 0.05 of the score margin).

## Test plan
- Unit: each sub-signal against hand-computed fixtures; Hurst against a known fractional-Brownian series; classification boundaries; hysteresis prevents flapping on a synthetic boundary-oscillating series; confidence in 0-1; insufficient-data path for each lookback; signal-mask reweighting sums to 1.
- Contract: `RegimeExplanation` validates against the OpenAPI schema; the enum values are exactly the five published ones.
- Consistency test: published regime equals `/market/regime/explain` for 1 000 consecutive evaluations.
- Integration: trending, ranging and volatile recorded fixtures each classify as expected for the majority of their duration.
- Determinism: double-run equality on a recorded fixture.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Read-only public market data behind `marketdata:read`. R9 advice boundary is the real control: the API returns a classification and its evidence, never an instruction; no field named `signal`, `recommendation` or `action` may appear in this response. Explain is cached per symbol, so it cannot be used to force expensive recomputation (STRIDE-D).

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend) - but the classifier must emit a text enum and a numeric confidence (never a colour or a bare score) so SCR-057 can be text-first as its catalogue entry requires.

## Performance notes
SCR-057: classification computed backend-side and pushed at most 1 Hz; panel budget <=1 ms per update. Evaluation cost <=3 ms per second per symbol. Budgets #6, #11 as per the epic.

## Observability
`regime_transitions_total{symbol,from,to}`, `regime_confidence` (gauge per symbol), `regime_insufficient_data{symbol}` (gauge), `orderflow_detector_eval_seconds{detector="regime"}`. INFO log per transition with the contributing signals.

## Definition of Done
Per section 4.2: merged with 2 approvals including the M9 code owner; contract test against `RegimeExplanation`; enum mapping to the QuestDB `regime` SYMBOL values documented in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 4.11; coverage >=85 %; the confidence definition written into the methodology content ticket (T07); consistency test in CI.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T01 (tape speed, book thickness, realised volatility) and E23 (CVD/delta as a sub-signal; roadmap graph `E23 --> E25`). ADX/ATR come from the indicator engine (US-IND-004).

title: Track stacked imbalance runs over footprint cells and publish them
body:
## Context
Backend for **US-DET-004 Imbalance tracker panel (Must)**: "each active stack is listed with price range, direction, depth, age and status (active/tested/broken)". NFR: "panel updates within 200 ms of a new stack". Declared dependency: US-FP-008 (stacked imbalances in the footprint, E18).

The division of labour matters. E18 computes per-cell diagonal/horizontal imbalance flags with a configurable ratio (roadmap section 6.2: "imbalance detection with configurable ratio and diagonal/horizontal modes"). E25 turns those per-bar flags into **stacks that live over time** and tracks whether price has since traded back through them. SCR-056 states the thresholds are "shared with SCR-032 (single source of truth: changing one prompts to sync the other)" and that "recomputation on a threshold change is done backend-side, with a visible recompute state rather than a client-side full-history pass".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/imbalance_stacks.py`: consumes footprint cell imbalance flags from E18; groups `>= min_stack` consecutive same-direction imbalanced price levels within a bar into a stack with `price_low`, `price_high`, `direction`, `depth`, `ratio_max`, `created_ts`.
- Lifecycle: `active` -> `tested` (price returns into the zone) -> `broken` (price trades fully through it); status transitions emitted as events so the panel updates incrementally rather than re-fetching.
- Publication as the `imbalance_ratio` / stack metric points on `metrics.{symbol}` with per-stack detail in `MetricPoint.meta`; counts persisted to `orderflow_metrics.stacked_imbalance_up` and `.stacked_imbalance_down`.
- Threshold source-of-truth: read the ratio and `min_stack` from the same configuration E18 uses (`price_grouping`, `imbalance_ratio`, `min_stack` are already `footprint.{symbol}.{bar_type}.{param}` options); no second copy of these numbers.
- Server-side recompute over the loaded range on a threshold change, with an observable recompute state.
- Bounded retention: at most 2 000 stacks per symbol in the publishable ring (matching SCR-056's 2 000-event client ring buffer), older ones available via REST backfill.

## Out of scope
The per-cell imbalance ratio computation (E18), the panel UI (E25-S02), footprint rendering, alerting on new stacks (ALRT), the settings dialog control (E25-S05 / E18's footprint settings dialog SCR-032).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Stack formed
  Given three consecutive price levels in a bar are imbalanced in the same direction above the configured ratio
  And min_stack is 3
  Then one stack is published with its price range, direction, depth, maximum ratio and creation time

Scenario: Lifecycle
  Given an active stack
  When price returns into its price range
  Then its status becomes tested
  And when price trades fully through it the status becomes broken
  And each transition is published as an incremental update

Scenario: Latency
  Given a new stack forms
  Then it is published within 200 milliseconds of the bar update that created it

Scenario: Threshold change
  When the imbalance ratio or minimum stack depth is changed
  Then stacks are recomputed server-side over the loaded range and a recompute state is published
  And the client performs no full-history recomputation

Scenario: Single source of truth
  Then the ratio and minimum stack depth used here are read from the same configuration the footprint engine uses, with no second stored copy
```

## Technical notes / design
Stacks are keyed by `(bar_ts, price_low, direction)` so a re-emission after a bar revision replaces rather than duplicates. Lifecycle evaluation runs on trade events against the open-stack list, which is small (bounded by the visible/loaded range), so an O(n) scan per trade is acceptable at R2 volumes; if profiling says otherwise, index open stacks in a sorted price array and binary-search the traded price.

"Traded through" means price has printed beyond the far edge of the zone, not merely touched it - the distinction is the difference between `tested` and `broken` and must be stated in the methodology content (T07).

## Test plan
- Unit: grouping at exactly `min_stack` and at `min_stack - 1`; non-consecutive levels do not group; direction mixing breaks a stack; tested/broken transitions at the exact boundary price; re-emission after bar revision replaces by key; ring bound at 2 000.
- Integration: recorded fixture; stack counts match an independent DuckDB recomputation over the Parquet tier (roadmap section 6.3 exit criterion 6 pattern).
- Latency: new stack published within 200 ms of the bar update (measured in CI with a synthetic feed).
- Determinism: double-run equality.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Public data behind `marketdata:read`. The recompute path is range-limited and rate-limited (STRIDE-D). Thresholds are shared configuration - changing them is audited through the same path as the footprint settings, so there is exactly one audited write path.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend) - the published stack carries `direction` as text ("buy"/"sell") and explicit `bid_volume`/`ask_volume` numbers, because SCR-056 requires the ratio to be announced as "bid 340 vs ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1".

## Performance notes
SCR-056: panel renders <=4 Hz with a 1.5 ms budget; publication within 200 ms of stack formation. Backend evaluation <=1 ms per bar update. Budgets #6, #8 as per the epic.

## Observability
`orderflow_imbalance_stacks_total{symbol,direction}`, `orderflow_imbalance_stacks_open{symbol}` (gauge), `orderflow_imbalance_stack_transitions_total{to}`, `orderflow_imbalance_recompute_seconds`.

## Definition of Done
Per section 4.2: merged with 2 approvals including the M9 code owner; independent-recomputation parity test green; coverage >=85 %; threshold single-source verified by review (no duplicated constant); `orderflow_metrics` columns populated.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T02 (framework/bus) and E18 (per-cell imbalance flags, US-FP-008).

## Branch
`feat/detectors-imbalance-stacks`. PR size guidance: single PR, under 400 LOC.

title: Finalise ADR-0018, replay observability and plan-doc reconciliation
body:
## Context
Two things close out the engine track. First, the decisions taken in E26-K01 and implemented across T02-T05 must be recorded as an ADR, because the snapshot interval, the merge tie-break and the resource-governance limits are exactly the kind of choice a future maintainer will otherwise reverse by accident. Second, several plan documents will have drifted from shipped behaviour during implementation — and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires docs to reflect *final shipped behaviour, not the original proposal*.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR-0018 "Replay determinism, seek strategy and resource governance"** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, covering: the one-code-path injection design and why a parallel replay implementation was rejected; the `(ts_event, seq)` ordering rule and the documented tie-break; the snapshot interval chosen in E26-K01 with its disk cost; the read-ahead and tier-selection strategy; the backpressure-slows-the-clock rule; the resource-governance limits (sessions per user, window cap, memory ceiling, idle reclaim, control-call rate limit); and the consequences of each.
- **Observability completion**: register the full metric set (`replay_sessions_active`, `replay_events_emitted_total`, `replay_clock_lag_ms`, `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage}`, `replay_source_tier`, `replay_gap_warnings_total`, `replay_backpressure_seconds_total`, `replay_session_memory_bytes`, `replay_achieved_speed_ratio`), add a Grafana dashboard for replay health, and add alert rules for sustained clock lag, repeated seek-budget breaches and session-reclaim storms, per `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md`.
- **Plan-doc reconciliation**:
  - `15-component-catalogue.md` — the CMP-171 speed-preset list resolved in E26-D01 versus the SCR-097 list; CMP-170 coverage-shading prop added.
  - `14-screens-catalogue.md` — any SCR-097/098/099 state added or renamed during implementation; the SCR-097 "speed 0.25x-50x" phrasing in the sign-off checklist reconciled with the API's documented 0.1-100 range and the shipped preset list.
  - `24-internal-schemas.md` §13.7 — the seek algorithm parameters as shipped.
  - `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` §11 — any field or error added during T05.
  - `20-architecture.md` C13 — module boundaries as built.
- A changelog fragment for the replay feature per `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Out of scope
- New engineering behaviour — this task documents and instruments what exists; a needed behaviour change is a separate ticket.
- ADRs owned by other epics (ADR-0015 recording policy, ADR-0003 storage tiers) beyond cross-references.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR records decisions with their evidence
  Given ADR-0018
  When it is reviewed by the Architect
  Then each decision cites the E26-K01 measurement or the implementation constraint that drove it
  And the rejected alternatives are stated with the reason for rejection

Scenario: Docs match shipped behaviour
  Given the shipped replay feature
  When the listed plan documents are diffed against it
  Then every divergence is corrected, and the speed-preset discrepancy between SCR-097 and CMP-171 is resolved to one canonical list everywhere

Scenario: Replay health is observable before it is needed
  Given the Grafana dashboard and alert rules
  When clock lag is sustained above threshold in a soak run
  Then an alert fires and the dashboard shows the responsible stage
```

## Technical notes / design
The alert thresholds should be derived from the E26-K01 and E26-Q03 measurements rather than guessed: sustained `replay_clock_lag_ms` above the level at which the achieved rate diverges from the requested rate, and `replay_seek_duration_ms{stage=total}` p95 above the 1 s budget over a rolling window.

## Test plan

title: UX research: how the owner actually manages exchange keys, rotation and compromise
body:
## Context
E27 introduces an interaction the product has never had: handling credentials that can move real money, under a set of rules the user cannot change (withdrawal always off, IP allowlist mandatory, secrets never re-displayed, allowlist configurable only in Bybit's browser UI since Feb 2026). ADR-0009 states the design constraint that makes research necessary: "Rotation must be practical enough that it actually happens."

Before wireframes, we need evidence about how the owner and the account managers currently do this: where they keep keys, what they believe about what the app can see, what makes them avoid rotation, and what they would do first in a suspected compromise. The failure mode this research protects against is a flow that is technically correct and behaviourally ignored - keys that never rotate, allowlists never configured, and a compromise response improvised under stress.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Research plan and discussion guide covering: current key-handling practice, mental model of "the app has my keys", perceived cost of rotation, the 48-hour Bybit new-key restriction as a planning constraint, and a first-response walkthrough for suspected compromise.
- 5 to 6 sessions: the owner, 2 account managers (per the persona set in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`), and 2 to 3 comparable self-hosted-tool operators.
- A task-based think-aloud using a paper or Figma-lite mock of the rotation stepper and the revoke decision ("leave positions" versus "flatten first"), to observe which branch people pick under time pressure and why.
- Comprehension check on the three statements the UI must convey and that users typically get wrong: the secret can never be shown again; a database backup without the KEK is useless; the IP allowlist must be set in Bybit's dashboard, not here.
- Findings report with prioritised implications, each tied to a specific screen ID (SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129, SCR-079).
- A copy-deck seed: the exact wording candidates for the withdrawal verdict, the IP-mismatch remediation, the stale-balance badge and the irreversible-delete warning, to be validated in E27-D03.

## Out of scope
Visual design (E27-D02 and E27-D03); motion (E27-D04); usability testing of the built product (E27-Q04 exploratory charter); research on order entry or profiles (owned by E30 and E28).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sessions completed and synthesised
  Given the research plan is approved
  When the sessions have run
  Then at least 5 sessions are recorded and synthesised, and the findings report is published with prioritised implications

Scenario: Every implication is actionable
  When the findings report is reviewed
  Then each implication names the screen it affects, the decision it changes, and the confidence behind it

Scenario: Rotation avoidance is understood
  When participants are asked why they have not rotated keys before
  Then the reasons are categorised, and at least one concrete design response is proposed for each category

Scenario: The three hard facts are tested for comprehension
  Given the candidate copy for write-only secrets, KEK-separated backups and browser-only allowlists
  When participants read it and are asked to restate it
  Then comprehension is measured, and any statement misunderstood by more than one participant is rewritten and retested

Scenario: Research contradicts the plan
  Given a finding conflicts with a locked decision such as never re-displaying a secret
  Then the finding is recorded with its implication, the locked decision stands, and the design response is to explain rather than to change the rule
```

## Technical notes / design
Mixed methods: semi-structured interview plus task-based think-aloud. Sessions are 45 minutes, remote, recorded with consent. Analysis is thematic with two coders to reduce single-researcher bias. Sample size is small by necessity - the product has one owner and a few managers - so findings are reported as directional with explicit confidence levels rather than as statistics.

Prototype fidelity is deliberately low so that participants critique the flow rather than the visuals.

## Test plan
Validation is the comprehension check itself: candidate copy is accepted only when participants can restate it correctly in their own words. Findings feed directly into E27-D02's wireframe states and into the exploratory charter in E27-Q04.

## Security notes
No real API keys, UIDs or IP addresses are used in any prototype or discussion - placeholders only, stated to participants. Session recordings contain operational detail about how the owner secures credentials and are therefore **Confidential**: stored in the research repository with restricted access, and deleted after synthesis per the retention rule in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Participants are told explicitly that they must not read real credentials aloud.

## Accessibility notes
Recruit at least one participant who uses a screen reader or keyboard-only navigation, or run a parallel expert review with an accessibility specialist, so that the a11y implications of the stepper and the confirmation dialogs are grounded rather than assumed. Prototypes used in sessions must be keyboard-operable.

## Performance notes
N/A - no runtime performance implications. Perceived-time findings (how long users will tolerate a connection test before assuming failure) are captured and feed the <=3 s budget on SCR-126.

## Observability
N/A - no telemetry is produced by this ticket. The research does specify which analytics events would answer the open questions later: `admin.key_form_opened`, `admin.key_test_run`, `admin.key_health_viewed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Research plan approved by the Chief Design Officer before fieldwork.
- [ ] At least 5 sessions run, recorded with consent and synthesised by two coders.
- [ ] Findings report published with prioritised, screen-linked implications and stated confidence.
- [ ] Copy-deck seed handed to E27-D03.
- [ ] Recordings handled and deleted per the retention policy; no real credential appears in any artefact.
- [ ] Status Done at least 2 sprints before E27-S01 starts in Sprint 15.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E09**, which establishes the authentication, step-up and RBAC model that the key-management flows sit inside; researching rotation without knowing whether step-up is required would produce findings we could not act on.

`design/e27-ux-research` - research artefacts committed under `docs/research/e27/`; no product code.

title: Wireframe SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079 with every state
body:
## Context
E27 introduces five admin screens and one trading-side drawer, all specified in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` with wireframes, states and per-screen sign-off checklists. This ticket produces the low-fidelity structure for all six, resolving layout and information hierarchy before any visual work, and - most importantly - drawing the **failure states as primary cases**, because in this epic the failure states are the point: a key with withdrawal permission, an IP allowlist that does not match, a stale balance, a rotation whose replacement key fails validation, and a delete blocked by open exposure.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes for **SCR-125** (accounts list): the column set label, UID, environment, permissions, IP allowlist, key age, state; the aggregate "Withdrawal permission: OFF on all accounts (verified <time>)" line and its negated form; per-row actions; empty state; and the withdrawal-permission-detected state drawn as a **blocking error, not a warning**.
- **SCR-126** (add / edit account): label, environment, write-only API key and secret fields, IP allowlist display, intended-permissions checklist, the "Test connection" result panel showing what the backend verified (UID, permissions, allowlist, server-time skew), a failure state per check, edit mode with an empty optional secret, and the step-up gate before save.
- **SCR-127** (key rotation): every stage of the wizard with its success and failure state; the "orders are drained before switch-over" behaviour stated; the rollback state when the new key fails validation; the reminder to delete the old key at Bybit with a confirmation checkbox; the key-age policy restated; the step-up gate.
- **SCR-128** (key health & secrets policy): per-key age, permissions, allowlist state and rotation-due date; the secrets-at-rest policy written as plain sentences; the "mark as compromised" emergency action with its immediate effect; the overdue state.
- **SCR-129** (disable / delete): disable and delete as separate flows with different copy; open positions, orders and algos blocking deletion and listed with counts; the statement that historical records are retained; assigned users listed with what they lose; typed confirmation plus step-up; the irreversibility of delete.
- **SCR-079** (account detail drawer): equity, available balance, used margin, unrealised PnL, leverage, position mode and margin mode with units; the permission and allowlist summary; the profile summary with an owner-only link to SCR-131; the rate-limit budget; the disabled or suspended account state; and the freshness and "stale since" treatment.
- A state inventory table listing every state per screen, cross-checked against the states named in the screens catalogue, so nothing is discovered missing during hi-fi.
- Information-hierarchy rationale for SCR-125: what must be readable at a glance versus on demand.

## Out of scope
Visual design, colour and type (E27-D03); motion (E27-D04); the design-system component contributions (E27-D03); Storybook implementation; anything relating to profiles (E28) or the order ticket (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued state is drawn
  Given the states named in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md for the six screens
  When the wireframe set is reviewed against the state inventory
  Then every state has a frame and no frame exists that is not in the inventory

Scenario: Failure states are primary
  When the wireframe set is reviewed
  Then the withdrawal-permission-detected, IP-mismatch, stale-balance, failed-replacement-key and blocked-delete states are drawn at the same fidelity as the happy path, not as annotations

Scenario: No secret is renderable
  When every frame is inspected
  Then no frame shows an API secret, and every key identifier is truncated

Scenario: The three hard facts are expressed
  When the frames for SCR-126, SCR-128 and SCR-129 are read
  Then each of the three facts from E27-D01 (write-only secrets, KEK-separated backups, browser-only allowlist) is stated in plain language on the screen where it matters

Scenario: A state has no home
  Given a backend state such as "within Bybit's 48 h new-key restriction" that no frame accommodates
  Then a frame is added or the state is explicitly deferred with a written rationale before sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Wireframes are greyscale and typographically neutral so that reviewers judge structure, not style. Each frame is annotated with: the data source (the exact API path or WS topic from the screens catalogue), the RBAC requirement, and the audit event the screen emits.

The layout must accommodate the real cardinality: at most 6 accounts in v1, which means SCR-125 should not be designed as a dense data grid optimised for hundreds of rows; the space is better spent on making state legible.

The SCR-126 result panel is structured as a list of checks with an outcome per check, because the screens catalogue requires that "the test result is a list, not a colour".

## Test plan
Design critique with engineering present, so that any state impossible to produce is caught early. Walk-through against each screen's own design sign-off acceptance checklist in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, item by item. Keyboard-path dry-run on paper: every action must have a keyboard route before hi-fi begins.

## Security notes
The design must make three security properties self-evident rather than merely true: that the app cannot see the secret after save, that withdrawal is off on every account, and that deleting an account does not close positions. Misrepresenting any of these in the visual language would be a security defect, not a cosmetic one. No real UIDs, keys or IPs appear in any frame. The Security engineer reviews the SCR-126, SCR-127 and SCR-128 frames.

## Accessibility notes
Annotate focus order for every frame, name the landmark and heading structure, mark which elements are live regions (the health chips on SCR-125, the exchange error on SCR-129, the countdown on SCR-127), and state the role for each dialog (`dialog` versus `alertdialog`). Confirm that every state distinction is carried by text and not only by colour - this is a hard requirement in the catalogue for SCR-125 and SCR-128.

## Performance notes
Record the perceived-performance requirements on the frames: the SCR-126 test round-trip target of <=3 s with a validating state, SCR-127's <=10 s rotation with per-stage elapsed time, SCR-129's <=1 s consequence summary before the confirm control appears, and SCR-079's <=100 ms open from cached state.

Annotate each frame with the audit and analytics events it triggers, taken from the screens catalogue: `account.tested`, `account.disabled_by_policy`, `account.created`, `account.updated`, `account.key_rotated`, `admin.key_health_viewed`, `admin.secrets_policy_changed`, `admin.key_marked_compromised`, `account.detail_viewed`.

title: UX research: what traders need from a positions and orders blotter
body:
## Context
SCR-063 is the screen the owner watches while money is at risk, and E29 is the first epic to build it. Before wireframes we must know what a blotter has to answer at a glance, what "pending" must look like when an amend is in flight, and how a reconciliation correction should be told to a user who may have acted on the wrong number a second earlier. Net-new interaction ⇒ research first per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 and the design-ahead rule (≥2 sprints before the S15/S16 build).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Research plan + 3–5 moderated sessions with the Owner and account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) using competitor blotters (TradingView, Bybit web, DeepCharts) as think-aloud props.
- Answer with evidence, for SCR-063 / SCR-078:
  - Default column set and order for the **Positions**, **Working orders**, **Fills** tabs (candidate columns are enumerated in `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-063); what may be hidden behind CMP-056 ColumnPicker.
  - Default grouping (account vs symbol vs trade group) and whether the totals row is expected to aggregate across environments (it must not — demo and live are never summed).
  - How an **optimistic/pending** amend must read so nobody believes a stop moved when it did not (ADR-0006 rule S2 / `24-internal-schemas.md` S2).
  - How a **reconciliation correction** should be surfaced (inline row flash vs banner vs both) and what text makes "the exchange disagreed with us and won" understandable.
  - Liquidation-proximity escalation thresholds and wording (must be text+glyph, never colour alone).
  - What US-POS-004 position detail must contain to be worth opening.
- Written findings note + a decision table appended to the SCR-063 catalogue entry, signed by the Owner.

## Out of scope
Visual design (D02/D03), any implementation, the order ticket (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Column set decided
  Given competing column sets from three reference tools
  When research completes
  Then one default column set per tab is chosen, recorded in a decision table, and written into 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-063

Scenario: Pending semantics agreed
  When participants are shown three candidate treatments for an in-flight amend
  Then the chosen treatment is one that no participant misread as "already applied"

Scenario: Correction wording tested
  Given a simulated reconciliation correction
  When shown to participants
  Then at least 4 of 5 correctly state what changed, which value is now true, and that the exchange is authoritative
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the R2 builds as props where possible; no new prototype code. Record sessions per `ADR-0015-recording-policy.md` (consent, retention).

## Test plan
N/A — research. Findings are validated later by D07 design QA and Q05 a11y audit.

## Security notes
No production keys or real balances in props; use demo/fixture data only. Session recordings stored per the recording policy, deleted after synthesis.

## Accessibility notes
Include at least one session covering keyboard-only and screen-reader expectations for a dense grid; feed results into D05.

## Performance notes
Capture the density expectation (how many rows must be readable at once) so the virtualisation budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` is driven by a real number.

## Observability
N/A.

title: Wireframe to hi-fi: SCR-063 positions & orders grid panel
body:
## Context
SCR-063 (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §5, wireframe ref R-130) is the primary surface of E29 and is consumed by E30/E31/E32/E34 for flatten, reverse and group views. It must be designed once, completely, including the unhappy states, because every trading epic inherits it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Figma frames, light and dark, comfortable and compact density, for SCR-063:
  - Tabs **Positions · Working orders · Fills · Trade groups · Algos** (the last two are placeholders owned by E33/E34 but must be drawn so the tab strip does not change later).
  - Positions tab columns per the D01 decision table: account, symbol, side (as text), qty, entry, mark, uPnL, R, realised today, liq price, leverage, margin mode, position mode.
  - Working-orders tab: account, symbol, side, type, qty, filled qty, price, trigger, TIF, flags, age, parent algo/bracket; untriggered conditionals in a distinct section.
  - Inline amend affordance with an explicit **pending** treatment (US-POS-002) and the "amend rejected — your order is unchanged" resolution.
  - Row actions: Close 25 % / 50 % / Close / Reverse / SL/TP / Chart (CMP-057 SplitButton).
  - Totals row, group-by control, CMP-055 FilterBar with removable chips (US-POS-006), CMP-056 ColumnPicker, CSV export.
  - States: loading · empty ("No open positions") · reconciling · desync warning banner · liq-proximity warning rows · frozen/lockout (actions disabled **with reasons**) · viewer read-only · mixed-environment rows with per-row DEMO/LIVE badge.
- Redlines: spacing, type ramp, numeric alignment (tabular figures), token names only — no raw hex.
- The SCR-063 **design sign-off acceptance checklist** in the catalogue is satisfied item by item and ticked in the ticket.

## Out of scope
SCR-078 and the desync/SCR-152 treatment (D03); SL/TP editor SCR-064 (E32); kill-switch modal SCR-072 (E39); ticket SCR-060 (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued state is drawn
  Given the SCR-063 entry lists loading, empty, reconciling, desync, liq-proximity, lockout and viewer-read-only states
  When the Figma file is reviewed
  Then each state has a named frame and none is left to implementation improvisation

Scenario: Pending is unmistakable
  Given an inline amend in flight
  Then the row shows a pending treatment that states the old value is still the live one

Scenario: Sign-off checklist satisfied
  When the CDO reviews the file against the SCR-063 design sign-off acceptance checklist
  Then all eight checklist items pass and sign-off is recorded on this ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Build on the E05 design-system tokens and CMP-049 Table; do not invent a new table. Numeric columns use CMP-020 NumericText conventions. Mixed-environment visibility follows the global environment rules from SCR-075.

## Test plan
Design review + checklist walkthrough; no code. Verified later by D07 design QA against the built screen.

## Security notes
No screenshot may contain a real API key, account id or balance; use fixture values throughout.

## Accessibility notes
Specify focus order, focus-visible treatment on grid cells, `aria-sort` affordances, and the text alternative for every colour-carrying signal. Contrast ≥4.5:1 for text, ≥3:1 for the liq-proximity glyph. Reviewed in D05.

## Performance notes
Design must survive virtualisation: no sticky element that requires full-list measurement; row height fixed per density.

## Observability
Mark on the spec which controls emit `position.closed`, `position.reversed`, `order.cancelled`, `grid.exported`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma file complete, versioned, linked from SCR-063.
- [ ] Checklist ticked; CDO sign-off recorded; Status Done ≥2 sprints before S15.
- [ ] Tokens/components referenced by ID only; any gap raised as a D04 item.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E29-D01 (decisions that constrain columns, grouping and pending semantics).

## Branch

title: Add the footprint E2E and integration suite to CI
body:
## Context
Automates the repeatable half of E18-Q01's plan so footprint regressions surface in CI rather than in an exploratory session two sprints later. `03-testing-strategy.md` mandates E2E on both Playwright web and Electron; R2's integration gate names the exact fixture set.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **E2E specs** (Playwright, run against web and the Electron shell):
  - Toggle footprint with `F`; verify the pane renders and the legend states the bucket size.
  - Cycle all four cell modes and both display modes; assert no `/market/footprint` request is issued (proving the cached-aggregate contract).
  - Change the imbalance ratio and stack depth; assert flag and zone counts change as the golden fixture predicts, with no refetch.
  - Change the input source; assert a recompute job starts, progress is shown and the pane updates on completion; assert failure renders an actionable message with the code in a details disclosure.
  - Per-symbol defaults: save for BTCUSDT, open ETHUSDT, assert independence; reload the workspace and assert persistence.
  - Two panes on one symbol with different display modes; save/reload the workspace.
  - Keyboard-only traversal of a bar's cells and `Alt+T` parity against the canvas values.
  - Partial-history state naming the first available timestamp on a recorder-gap fixture.
  - Absence of the order-based input option in the DOM, and absence of an `(estimated)` badge on exact sources.
  - Density collapse: zoom past the cell budget, assert the compact representation and the "zoom in for numbers" hint.
- **Integration specs** against the R2-mandated recorded fixtures: normal session, high-volatility burst, WS disconnect + resync, sequence gap, thin-book symbol. Each asserts continuity (no duplicate or missing bar at the REST→WS seam) and correct gap declaration.
- **Chaos specs**: kill the upstream feed mid-stream; overflow the footprint queue to force `resync_required`; assert recovery with no lost or duplicated cells and the "feed compressed" indicator driven by `coalesced_count`.
- CI wiring: suite runs on PRs touching orderflow/chart-engine paths and nightly in full; flake budget and quarantine policy applied per `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Out of scope
Perf benchmarks (E18-Q03), a11y audit (E18-Q04), unit tests (owned by the implementing stories/tasks), golden-value parity (E18-T06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Suite covers the automatable plan
  When the E18-Q01 traceability table is re-checked
  Then every case marked automatable has a named automated test
  And cases not automated are explicitly marked manual with a reason

Scenario: Determinism
  Given the suite is run ten times against the same fixtures and build
  Then results are identical and no test is quarantined for flakiness

Scenario: Failures are diagnosable
  Given a deliberate regression in imbalance rendering
  Then the failing test names the scenario, attaches a screenshot and a trace, and points at the golden expectation it violated

Scenario: Both runtimes
  Then the E2E suite passes on Playwright web and on the Electron shell
  And any runtime-specific skip is explicit and justified in the test file
```

## Technical notes / design
- Drive from recorded fixtures through the staging backend, never live Bybit, so runs are deterministic and consume no rate-limit budget.
- Use the accessibility tree (not pixel coordinates) for cell assertions where possible — it is both more robust and doubles as a mirror-correctness check.
- Freeze the clock and the replay feed so "forming bar" behaviour is reproducible.

## Test plan
Self-verifying: seed three deliberate regressions (flag rendering removed, per-symbol threshold leaking across symbols, partial-history state suppressed) and confirm the suite catches each. A suite that passes a broken build is not a suite.

## Security notes
Test credentials for staging are managed through the existing CI secret store; no key material in the repo. Fixtures are scanned for accidentally recorded account identifiers before use.

## Accessibility notes
The keyboard-traversal and `Alt+T` parity specs are part of this suite, complementing (not replacing) the E18-Q04 audit; axe-core runs are wired per `03-testing-strategy.md` on the touched screens.

## Performance notes
The suite must complete within the CI budget; parallelise by spec file. Long soak and benchmark runs belong to E18-Q03, not here.

## Observability
CI publishes the run report with per-scenario status, screenshots and traces as build artefacts; flake rate tracked over time.

- [ ] Seeded-regression verification passing for all three seeds.

title: Footprint performance benchmark, load profile and CI gate
body:
## Context
The R2 quality-gate table states: *"Perf — Budgets #1, #2, #3, #14 all hard gates; heatmap and footprint each have a dedicated benchmark in CI."* This ticket builds footprint's half of that gate by promoting the E18-K01 harness into a maintained CI benchmark and adding the WS load profile that proves budget #3 for the footprint topic.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmark** in CI (adopted from E18-K01's harness): the target scene — 60 visible bars × 40 price levels with numerals (US-FP-001 NFR), plus the heavier 2 500-cell / ~12 500-glyph scene from `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 2. Asserts p95 frame time ≤ 16.6 ms, p99 ≤ 22 ms, glyph batching ≤ 2.0 ms, and ≥ 55 fps on the US-FP-001 scene. Runs headless Chromium on PRs, Electron nightly.
- **Worst-case / degradation benchmark**: footprint + all overlays in a multi-pane layout, asserting the 30 fps floor (budget #2) is never breached and that the degradation strategy engages visibly (the non-colour-only "reduced detail" indicator) rather than silently dropping frames.
- **Mode matrix**: benchmark each cell mode and display mode separately, so a regression can be attributed (bid×ask is the glyph-heaviest; profile must be measurably cheapest).
- **WS load profile (k6)**: 20 concurrent pane subscriptions across 10 symbols on the `footprint.*` topic against staging with recorded fixtures, asserting budget #3 (tick → screen p95 < 100 ms, p99 < 250 ms) and budget #6 (backend-internal ≤ 20 ms p95), plus the ADR-0005 criteria (≥ 40% bandwidth and ≥ 30% decode-time reduction for binary vs JSON on this topic).
- **Backend engine benchmark**: `FootprintEngine` per-trade cost and `recompute_flags` over 200 bars × 40 cells (target ≤ 30 ms), plus the 24 h / 10-symbol ingestion soak assertion that footprint work does not break budget #5 (zero undetected loss) or #8 (memory per symbol).
- **Memory soak**: the 2-hour Playwright chart-engine soak with a footprint pane open, asserting no monotonic growth (budget #7) and a bounded DOM-mirror node count.
- Threshold provenance: CI thresholds are set from ADR-0016's recorded numbers; the benchmark fails the build on regression beyond the agreed band and publishes a trend.

## Out of scope
Functional E2E (E18-Q02), the a11y audit (E18-Q04), heatmap benchmarks (E21).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budgets asserted, not merely measured
  When the benchmark runs
  Then it fails the build if p95 frame time exceeds 16.6 ms on the target scene
  And it fails if the worst-case scene drops below 30 fps at any sampled point

Scenario: Regression attribution
  Given a deliberate 20 percent slowdown introduced in glyph batching
  Then the benchmark fails and the stage-attribution report names the text stage, not just the total

Scenario: WS budget under realistic load
  Given 20 concurrent footprint subscriptions across 10 symbols for 30 minutes
  Then tick to screen p95 is under 100 ms and p99 under 250 ms
  And the backend-internal sub-span is asserted at or under 20 ms p95 independently

Scenario: Binary encoding earns its place
  Then the footprint topic shows at least 40 percent bandwidth and 30 percent decode-time reduction versus JSON
  And if it does not, the result is reported as an ADR-0005 finding rather than quietly accepted

Scenario: No leaks
  Given a two hour soak with a footprint pane open
  Then process memory shows no monotonic growth beyond the documented variance band
  And the DOM-mirror node count stays proportional to visible cells
```

## Technical notes / design
- Reference hardware per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 3.1; results are only comparable on it, so CI pins the runner class and records it in the report.
- Measure with `Performance.mark()/measure()` at the section 4.3 stage boundaries and export structured spans, matching E18-K01's format so spike and CI numbers are directly comparable.
- Use SwiftShader only for golden images, never for timing.
- The k6 profile drives staging with recorded fixtures, per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 8's rule against load-testing live Bybit.

## Test plan
Self-verification by seeded regressions (glyph slowdown, extra draw call in the pattern pass, an unbounded mirror rebuild). Each must fail the gate and be attributed correctly.

## Security notes
Load testing runs against staging only, never live. The k6 profile uses dedicated test credentials from the CI secret store and respects the demo environment's constraints. Confirm the load profile cannot be pointed at a live endpoint by configuration accident — fail closed on an unexpected host.

## Accessibility notes
The worst-case benchmark explicitly asserts that the degradation indicator is not colour-only and that the DOM mirror stays synchronised with what is rendered — `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 4.4 lists mirror desync as never acceptable, including under degradation.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance gate. Budgets in scope: #1, #2, #3, #5, #6, #7, #8. Record every figure on the ticket and in ADR-0016's consequences if it differs from the spike.

## Observability
Benchmark trend published per commit; alert on a sustained regression trend even when still inside the band, so slow rot is visible before it breaks the gate.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Engine, worst-case, mode-matrix, backend and WS load benchmarks implemented and wired into CI.
- [ ] All budgets asserted with failing thresholds, not just reported.

Explicit verification of the green=bid / red=ask convention and its CVD-safe alternative.
- **Contrast measurement** of cell numerals against the full heat range in all three themes, and of focus indicators at every LOD level.
- **Announcement-policy conformance**: assert the E18-D04 policy is implemented — silence on forming-cell updates, announcements only on focus movement, bar close and new stacked zones, polite never assertive.
- **Reduced motion**: `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured for every transition listed in the E18-D04 motion spec.

## Out of scope
Fixing the findings (they become Bugs or in-sprint fixes on the owning stories); the DOM ladder (E21); non-footprint parts of SCR-045.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

Scenario: A screen-reader user can read a bar
  Given a screen-reader user with no sight of the canvas

Scenario: Nothing depends on colour
  Given greyscale and three CVD simulations over every footprint state

Scenario: Chatter is bounded in practice
  Given a live forming bar updating at full rate for two minutes
  Then the measured announcement count matches the E18-D04 policy
  And a screen-reader user reports the surface as usable, not noisy

Scenario: Findings are dispositioned
  Then every finding is either fixed and re-verified, or filed as a Bug with a priority label and linked here
  And no finding is left as an unresolved comment
```

Audit against WCAG 2.2 AA, focusing on 1.4.1 (use of colour), 1.4.3/1.4.11 (contrast), 2.1.1/2.1.2 (keyboard, no trap), 2.4.3 (focus order), 2.4.7 (focus visible), 2.4.11 (focus not obscured), 2.5.8 (target size ≥ 24×24), 4.1.2 (name/role/value) and 4.1.3 (status messages). title: Make footprint cells keyboard-navigable and screen-reader accessible
body:
## Context
R2 exit criterion 10 requires *"a11y pass on every new view incl. keyboard-navigable footprint cells and DOM ladder"*, and the R2 a11y quality gate states *"Footprint cells and DOM rows reachable and announced via the DOM-mirror."* CMP-109's catalogue entry specifies the mechanism: **every cell is mirrored** by an off-screen DOM node per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6.1's canvas control surrogate pattern.

E18-S01 ships the mirror nodes; this story ships the **navigation, announcement policy and parity** that make them usable, plus the SCR-045 footprint content.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Keyboard cell navigation on SCR-030: arrow keys move focus cell-to-cell along the price axis (↑/↓) and the time axis (←/→); `Enter` opens the cell-detail Drawer (CMP-046); `Esc` returns focus to the pane; `Home`/`End` jump to the first/last cell of the bar; `PageUp`/`PageDown` move by bar group. The crosshair follows the focused cell (SCR-030's "crosshair is fully keyboard-driven").
- `aria-label` composition per cell: "Price 65,430; bid 12.4; ask 8.1; delta +4.3", extended with "buy imbalance 420 percent", "part of a 4-level stack", "point of control", "value area high/low" and the unfinished-auction explanation where applicable. Full values **regardless of zoom-driven text hiding**.
- Implementation of the **E18-D04 announcement policy**: nothing is announced for forming-cell value changes; announcements occur only on explicit focus movement, on bar close, and on a newly formed stacked zone. A polite live region, never assertive.
- **SCR-045 parity** (`Alt+T`): the data-table alternative exposes the visible range with per-bar time, OHLC, volume, delta, CVD and an **expandable per-bar footprint cell list** (price, bid, ask, delta, imbalance flag) — the exact content the catalogue specifies — with `B`/`A` glyph carriers so sides are never colour- or position-only.
- Mirror recycling: nodes exist for **visible** cells only and are pooled, so the DOM never grows with loaded history.
- Canvas `role="img"` rolling summary maintained ("BTCUSDT 1 minute, last 64 011, up 0.4 %, delta +200").
- Focus ring drawn on the canvas for the focused cell, visible at every LOD level including text-hidden.

## Out of scope
The DOM ladder's own a11y (E21), the full SCR-045 screen for non-footprint content (E12/E20 contribute their columns), the a11y audit itself (E18-Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cell-to-cell navigation
  Given focus is on a footprint cell
  When I press the up arrow
  Then focus moves to the next price level in the same bar and the crosshair follows
  And when I press the right arrow, focus moves to the same price level in the next bar

Scenario: Full values below the text threshold
  Given the zoom level hides cell numerals
  When a cell receives focus
  Then its announced label still contains the full bid, ask and delta values

Scenario: Screen-reader chatter is bounded
  Given the forming bar updates 10 times per second
  Then no announcement is emitted for those updates
  And announcements occur only on focus movement, bar close and a newly formed stacked zone

Scenario: Table alternative parity
  When I press Alt+T
  Then SCR-045 lists the visible bars with time, OHLC, volume, delta and CVD
  And each bar expands to its footprint cells with price, bid, ask, delta and imbalance flag
  And the values match the canvas exactly for the same visible range

Scenario: The DOM does not grow with history
  Given 100000 bars are loaded
  Then the number of mirror nodes is proportional to visible cells only
  And a memory sample shows no monotonic growth as the user pans

Scenario: Focus is always visible
  Given any LOD level including text-hidden and profile display mode
  Then the focused cell has a visible focus indicator meeting contrast requirements

Scenario: Enter opens the detail drawer
  When I press Enter on a focused cell
  Then the cell-detail drawer opens with focus moved into it
  And Esc closes it and returns focus to the originating cell
```

## Technical notes / design
- The mirror is an `aria-hidden="false"`, visually-hidden container positioned off-screen, containing one focusable element per visible cell in DOM order matching reading order (bar by bar, price descending). Rebuild on viewport change is throttled to the LOD/viewport update, not per frame.
- Node pooling: reuse elements and update labels; creating and destroying hundreds of nodes per pan would itself break the frame budget.
- Focus synchronisation is bidirectional: canvas crosshair movement updates DOM focus and vice versa, through one controller, so the two cannot disagree (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 4.4: desyncing the DOM-mirror accessibility layer from what is rendered is *never acceptable*, even under degradation).
- Announcement policy is implemented as a single gate in front of the live region, so a future feature cannot accidentally add chatter without touching that gate.

## Test plan
- Unit: label composition for every cell state; navigation key handling including edges (first/last bar, first/last level); pooling behaviour; announcement gate (assert silence for forming updates).
- E2E (Playwright): full keyboard-only traversal of a bar's cells; `Alt+T` parity check comparing table values against the engine's data for the same visible range; focus-return after the drawer closes.
- axe-core: SCR-030 with the mirror layer specifically, and SCR-045.
- Manual: screen-reader pass (NVDA and VoiceOver) recorded as evidence, per `03-testing-strategy.md`'s manual-SR requirement.
- Memory: mirror-node count asserted in the 2-hour chart-engine soak.

## Security notes
The mirror duplicates on-screen market data into the DOM; it contains no secrets. Ensure the mirror is excluded from screenshot/export paths so it cannot double-render into shared images. No new network surface.

## Accessibility notes
This story **is** the accessibility implementation for E18 and is the gate R2 exit criterion 10 checks. WCAG 2.2 AA specifics: 2.1.1 keyboard (all cell information reachable), 2.4.3 focus order (DOM order matches visual reading order), 2.4.7 focus visible (at every LOD), 1.4.1 use of colour (labels carry meaning in text), 4.1.2 name/role/value (each cell is a labelled, focusable element), 4.1.3 status messages (the bounded live region). `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured for crosshair/focus transitions.

## Performance notes
Mirror maintenance must add ≤ 1.0 ms per viewport update and **zero** per-frame cost when the viewport is static. Assert both. The mirror must not force layout thrash — batch DOM writes and measure with the frame harness.

## Observability
Metrics: `footprint_mirror_nodes` (gauge), `footprint_mirror_rebuild_duration_seconds`, `a11y_announcements_total{surface="footprint"}` (used to prove the chatter bound in CI).
