title: ADR and reference doc for profile period semantics, value area and naked POC
body:
## Context
E19 settles several decisions that are not obvious, are contested among traders, and will be depended upon by alerts (E40), the rule engine, backtesting (R4) and any future mobile client: how a "session" is defined for a 24/7 market, which value-area expansion algorithm is used, how POC ties break, how TPO periods and letters are assigned, when a POC counts as naked, and what the approximated-from-bars fallback means numerically. Today these live scattered across `22-api-openapi.yaml` prose, `24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 and the test plan.

`docs/plan/27-adrs/` is where decisions with downstream consequences are recorded, and the epic DoD requires the plan docs to reflect shipped behaviour rather than the original proposal. Without this, a future engineer will "fix" the single-step expansion to the textbook algorithm and silently change where every rule arms.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Surfaces documented: SCR-038 profile panel, SCR-039 settings dialog; components CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane.
- **ADR** `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-00XX-profile-period-and-value-area-semantics.md` (number assigned at authoring time) covering:
  - Session definition for crypto: UTC-day default, `funding_8h` and `custom` anchors, and why no RTH concept is used.
  - Value-area algorithm: single-step expansion toward the heavier adjacent row, stated as an explicit accepted approximation of two-row TPO expansion, with the consequences and the conditions under which it differs.
  - POC tie-break: closest to range midpoint, deterministic, surfaced in the tooltip.
  - TPO period and letter assignment: default 30 minutes, configurable 1..240, letters `A..Z, a..z, AA..`, initial-balance period count.
  - Naked/virgin POC definition: when a POC becomes naked, what counts as "traded through", server-side state, and the nearest-N display cap.
  - HVN/LVN prominence definition and default threshold.
  - Approximated-from-bars fallback: exactly what is derived from klines, what is not available (delta, TPO), and how it is labelled.
  - Decimal/float boundary per `24-internal-schemas.md` C3 and which published values are exact.
  - Alternatives considered and rejected, with reasons, so the decisions are not relitigated from scratch.
- **Reference doc** `docs/plan/reference/profiles.md`: a single consumer-facing page for downstream epics listing each published metric (`profile_poc`, `profile_vah`, `profile_val`, HVN/LVN levels), its parameterisation, exactness, update cadence and failure modes (partial history, approximated, stale during rebuild).
- **Doc updates**: `24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 and the `/market/profile` description reconciled with shipped behaviour if they diverged; `18-traceability-matrix.md` section 2.9 refreshed if coverage changed.
- Cross-links added from the E40 alerts and rule-engine epics so consumers find the guarantees before designing against them.

## Out of scope
- Changing any of the algorithms - this records what shipped; a change requires a new ticket and a superseding ADR.
- End-user help content and tooltips (product copy owned by design), though the ADR supplies the factual basis and the known-limitations wording from `E19-Q08` is reused.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every contested decision is recorded with a rationale
  Given the merged ADR
  When it is reviewed against the E19 implementation
  Then session anchoring, value-area expansion, POC tie-break, TPO letters, naked POC, HVN/LVN and the bar-approximation fallback each have a decision, a rationale and the alternatives rejected

Scenario: Documentation matches shipped behaviour
  Given the shipped release-candidate build
  When 24-internal-schemas.md section 5 and the /market/profile description are compared to it
  Then any divergence is corrected in the docs, and the ADR states the correction

Scenario: Failure case - an undocumented behavioural difference is found
  Given the implementation breaks a tie differently from the documented rule
  Then the discrepancy is filed as a correctness bug against the owning ticket and the ADR is not merged claiming a rule that the code does not follow

Scenario: Downstream consumers can rely on the reference page
  Given the reference doc
  When an E40 alerts engineer needs to know whether profile_vah is exact and how often it updates
  Then the page answers both without reading engine source

Scenario: ADR is approved
  When the ADR PR is opened
  Then the Architect, the order-flow lead and the Security engineer approve it and it is linked from the E19 epic
```

## Technical notes / design
- The ADR is written as a decision record, not a tutorial: context, decision, consequences, alternatives. Tutorial-style explanation belongs in the reference page, which is aimed at a different reader.
- The single most important consequence to state plainly is that these definitions are now *contract*: changing any of them alters historical comparability and the behaviour of armed rules, and therefore requires a superseding ADR and a migration note, not a bug fix.
- The reference page lists failure modes alongside guarantees, because a consumer that does not know a metric can be stale during a rebuild will design an alert that fires on a transient.
- Numbers in both documents are taken from the `E19-Q02` verified fixtures, so the documentation and the tests cannot disagree.

## Test plan
- Documentation is validated against the conformance suite: each documented rule names the test that proves it, and a rule with no test is either tested or marked unverified explicitly.
- A link check and a reference check run in CI so the new files are wired into the plan docs rather than orphaned.

## Security notes
- The ADR records the integrity and auditability guarantees agreed in `E19-X04`, so the security posture is discoverable by consumers instead of living only in a sign-off document.
- It states the parameter-recording requirement for rule evaluations (repudiation mitigation from the threat model), making it a design input to E40 rather than a late discovery.
- No secrets, hostnames or internal topology are included; the documents are safe for the repository's normal audience.

## Accessibility notes
- The reference page follows the documentation accessibility conventions (proper heading hierarchy, tables with headers, no meaning conveyed by colour alone in diagrams), per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Where profile concepts are illustrated, a text description accompanies any diagram so the page is usable with a screen reader.

## Performance notes
- The reference page records the update cadence and rebuild latency characteristics of each published metric, so consumers size their polling and alert evaluation appropriately rather than discovering the 1 000 ms cadence by experiment.

## Observability
- Documents the metric and log names emitted by the profile engine, so operators and future debuggers can find them without reading code.

## Definition of Done
- ADR merged with a status of Accepted and a number assigned; reference page merged and linked from `24-internal-schemas.md`, the epic and the consuming epics.
- Plan docs reconciled with shipped behaviour; any discrepancy found during writing filed as a bug and resolved.
- Approved by the Architect, the order-flow lead and the Security engineer.
- Link check green; `18-traceability-matrix.md` section 2.9 refreshed if needed.

## Dependencies
- `E19-Q02` (verified numbers and rules) and `E19-X04` (security guarantees to record).
- Consumed by E40 alerts, the rule engine and the R4 backtesting work.

`docs/e19-profile-semantics-adr`

- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 and section 12
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/profile`; `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 14.6
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 9

title: Design QA of the shipped profile panel, settings dialog and TPO pane
body:
## Context
Design QA is the closing gate of the design loop defined in `16-design-system-brief.md` §12: the built profile surface is compared against the signed-off pack from E19-D07, and divergences are logged, classified and driven to closure before E19 can reach Done. For a GPU-rendered surface this pass matters more than usual — subpixel row alignment, bar-length quantisation, letter legibility at small sizes and colour rendering on different GPUs are things that only appear in the real renderer, and `R8 Browser/GPU compat` is a live risk on this epic.

This runs in Sprint 13, after the E19 frontend stories land in Sprint 10–13, against a real build with real recorded data.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Side-by-side comparison of the shipped **SCR-038** (docked and overlay) and **SCR-039** against the E19-D07 pack, in dark and light themes, at all three density modes.
- Verification of every state enumerated in the catalogue: loading · partial history · no history (owner and non-owner variants) · approximated-from-bars · degraded feed · developing vs final value area.
- Verification of every mode combination: period (session / fixed range / visible range / anchored / composite) × input (volume / delta / TPO), including split bid/ask rendering and the TPO Initial Balance.
- Edge-density verification against real recorded data: 5 000 rows at minimum row size; a two-level profile on an illiquid symbol; a 30-session composite; a value area spanning the whole visible range; more naked POCs than the clutter cap.
- Derived-level verification: POC, VAH, VAL, HVN, LVN, naked POC and single prints each rendered with the specified non-colour encoding and text label; POC tie-break tooltip present and correct.
- Motion verification against the E19-D05 spec including the suppression matrix: reduced-motion, saturated connection class, high row count, replay fast-forward.
- Accessibility verification against E19-D06: keyboard traversal end to end, focus-visible at every stop, the table alternative present and faithful, the announcement policy behaving under a live tape (specifically: no per-print flooding), target sizes at compact density, axe-core results reviewed.
- Cross-GPU/browser spot check per `R8`: the profile and TPO panes rendered on at least two distinct GPU/driver combinations, checking colour rendering, line thickness and letter legibility.
- Findings log, each classified blocker / must-fix / should-fix / accepted, with an owning ticket; blockers and must-fixes closed and re-verified before sign-off.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of the profile computation itself (POC/value-area maths, composite merging) — that is the engineering stories' unit and integration tests, not design QA.
- Backend performance measurement — E19's perf tickets own that; design QA only reports where a perf problem manifests visually.
- New scope or design changes; anything that is a genuinely new requirement is raised as a separate ticket under change control, not smuggled in as a QA fix.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The build matches the signed-off pack
  When the shipped SCR-038 and SCR-039 are compared with the E19-D07 redlines in both themes and all densities
  Then every divergence is logged with a classification and an owning ticket

Scenario: No blocker or must-fix remains open at sign-off
  Given the findings log contains items classified blocker or must-fix
  Then each is closed and re-verified in a subsequent build before this ticket reaches Done

Scenario: Colour is still not the sole carrier in the real renderer
  Given the shipped panel rendered in greyscale and under all three colour-blindness simulations
  Then POC, value area, HVN, LVN, naked POC, single prints and the buy/sell split all remain identifiable

Scenario: A live profile does not flood the screen reader
  Given a live session profile on an active symbol with a fast tape
  When a screen reader is active for two minutes
  Then routine updates are not announced and only the changes named in the E19-D06 announcement policy are

Scenario: Extreme density degrades as designed
  Given a profile with 5 000 rows at the minimum row size
  Then the shipped bucketing matches the designed appearance, motion is suppressed per the matrix, and interaction remains at or above the 55 fps floor

Scenario: A GPU difference is caught, not shipped
  Given the panel is rendered on a second GPU or driver combination
  When colours, line weights and TPO letters are compared against the first
  Then any visible difference is logged, and a difference that changes meaning is classified at least must-fix
```

## Technical notes / design
QA is run against a build fed by recorded fixtures so the edge cases are reproducible: the same fixture set used in E19-D01 plus the illiquid-symbol and 30-session-composite fixtures. The degraded-feed state is produced by forcing the `saturated` connection class from `23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3 rather than by waiting for it to occur naturally. Replay (E26) is used to reproduce the fast-forward motion-suppression case deterministically.

Row alignment in docked mode is checked against the axis-alignment rule written in E19-D02 with the chart in both linear and log price scale, and during an auto-fit animation — misalignment here is a correctness-class defect, not a cosmetic one, and should be classified accordingly.

## Test plan
Structured pass, not exploratory-only: a checklist derived directly from the E19-D07 pack, the SCR-038/SCR-039 sign-off acceptance checklists in `14-screens-catalogue.md`, the §12 design QA checklist in `16-design-system-brief.md`, and the E19-D06 findings. Evidence is screenshots and short clips attached to each finding. Re-verification of closed findings is done against a named build, and the build identifier is recorded on the ticket.

## Security notes
QA is run against recorded market fixtures and, where a live environment is needed, against demo only — never against live credentials. No account identifiers, balances or keys appear in any attached screenshot or clip; screenshots are reviewed for incidental account chrome before attachment.

## Accessibility notes
The a11y portion of this pass is a build-time verification of the design-time decisions in E19-D06: axe-core results reviewed alongside a manual NVDA and VoiceOver pass, full keyboard-only traversal, the table alternative checked for faithfulness against the histogram, and target sizes measured at compact density. A manual screen-reader pass is required by the Epic DoD in `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 and this ticket is where it is recorded for E19's screens.

## Performance notes
Design QA records the observed frame rate during visible-range panning at the worst supported density and row count, and the observed re-bucket latency on a row-size change, and compares them to the budgets carried in the E19-D07 pack. Failures are routed to the owning engineering ticket rather than absorbed as design findings.

## Observability
The pass confirms `profile.period_changed`, `profile.mode_changed`, `profile.va_percent_changed` and `profile.settings_changed` are actually emitted with the payloads specified in the pack, since an event that was specified but never wired is a silent gap that only a QA pass catches.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Full QA pass completed against a named build with findings logged, classified and assigned.
- [ ] All blocker and must-fix findings closed and re-verified on a later named build.
- [ ] Manual screen-reader pass and axe-core review recorded for SCR-038 and SCR-039.
- [ ] Cross-GPU spot check completed on at least two GPU/driver combinations with results attached.
- [ ] Observed fps and re-bucket latency recorded against the stated budgets.
- [ ] SCR-038 and SCR-039 sign-off acceptance checklists in `14-screens-catalogue.md` verified against the build, not the design.
- [ ] **CDO sign-off recorded on the ticket; Status = Done.**

## Dependencies
- **E19-D07** supplies the pack this pass compares against.
- The E19 frontend stories (Sprint 10–13) must be feature-complete for the surfaces under review.
- **E26** replay is used to reproduce the fast-forward motion-suppression case.

`design/e19-profile-design-qa`

title: Accessibility audit of the profile panel, table alternative and settings dialog
body:
## Context
A volume profile is the most colour-dependent surface in the product after the heatmap: POC, value area, HVN/LVN, delta sign and TPO single prints are all conventionally signalled by hue and fill alone. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI and manual screen-reader passes, and `SCR-038` commits to a specific remedy - a table alternative listing each price row with volume, delta and value-area membership, with POC/VAH/VAL announced. That commitment needs auditing against a real build, because a 5 000-row DOM mirror is easy to implement in a way that is technically present and practically unusable.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Full manual and automated audit of `SCR-038` (profile panel, including the docked-beside-chart and overlay presentations) and `SCR-039` (settings dialog), covering CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane, CMP-188 PriceAxis, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-228 PreviewTile and the `SCR-039` form controls (CMP-006, CMP-008, CMP-031, CMP-040, CMP-043, CMP-065).
- **Automated**: axe-core runs across every state - loading, populated, partial history, no history, approximated-from-bars, error - in volume, delta, TPO and combined modes, light and dark themes, at 200% and 400% zoom and at 320 px reflow width.
- **Manual screen-reader passes**: NVDA + Firefox, JAWS + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari. Scripted tasks: find the POC price; determine whether the current price is inside the value area; read the three highest-volume rows; change the value-area percentage to 68; identify a naked POC; switch to TPO and find the initial balance.
- **Keyboard-only pass**: reach the panel, traverse rows, jump to POC/VAH/VAL, open and dismiss `SCR-039` with focus return, operate every control including the numeric steppers and colour swatches, with a visible focus indicator throughout and no keyboard trap.
- **Non-colour encoding review**: POC, value-area membership, delta sign, HVN/LVN and single prints each verified to carry a text, pattern, border or glyph affordance in addition to colour; verified under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia simulation and in the high-contrast theme.
- **Contrast measurements** for bar fills against the pane background, POC and VA markers, axis labels and legend text, recorded as measured ratios against the 4.5:1 / 3:1 thresholds.
- **Virtualisation and announcement design review** of the table alternative: how 5 000 rows are exposed without flooding the accessibility tree, how live updates are announced without constant interruption (polite live region, coalesced summary announcements rather than per-print chatter), and how the user can freeze the profile to read it.
- Deliverables: `docs/qa/e19-a11y-audit.md` with findings, severity, WCAG 2.2 success-criterion references, screen recordings, and a remediation ticket per finding; plus the axe-core assertions merged into the CI suite.

## Out of scope
- The design-system components' generic a11y (E05/E07) except as composed here.
- Chart-engine-wide a11y patterns (E11) - this audit consumes the established pattern and reports back if it fails for dense histograms.
- Alert and rule UIs consuming profile metrics (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state is axe-clean
  Given SCR-038 in loading, populated, partial, empty, approximated and error states and SCR-039 open
  When axe-core runs in both themes at 100%, 200% and 400% zoom
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations, and any moderate finding is triaged with an owner and a ticket

Scenario: A screen-reader user can find the POC without sighted help
  Given NVDA with Firefox on a populated session profile
  When the tester performs the scripted task "find the POC price and say whether the last price is inside the value area"
  Then the task is completed using announced content only, within the documented time budget

Scenario: Failure case - colour-only encoding is rejected
  Given a mode where POC, value-area membership or delta sign is distinguishable only by hue
  Then the audit records a blocking finding with the WCAG 1.4.1 reference and a remediation ticket is opened before R2 exit

Scenario: Edge case - 5 000 rows do not flood assistive technology
  Given a 5 000-row profile with live updates
  When the table alternative is navigated
  Then rows are virtualised, live updates are announced as coalesced summaries rather than per-print, and navigation stays responsive

Scenario: Keyboard-only operation is complete
  Given keyboard input only
  When the user opens the panel, changes period mode, sets value area to 68, toggles single prints and closes SCR-039
  Then every step is reachable, focus is visible at all times, the dialog traps and returns focus, and no control requires a pointer

Scenario: Reduced motion is respected
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then profile transitions and re-bucket animations are suppressed without loss of information
```

## Technical notes / design
- The audit is run against a build with the `E19-Q03` deterministic fixtures so screen-reader transcripts are reproducible and can be diffed on re-audit.
- Announcement policy is treated as a *design* artefact, not an implementation detail: the audit proposes the coalescing rule (for example, announce POC changes and value-area boundary changes only, at most once every N seconds) and records it in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` if adopted, so E21 and E23 reuse it.
- A "freeze profile" affordance is evaluated explicitly; a continuously mutating table is unreadable with a screen reader, and this is the cheapest remedy.
- Findings are severity-mapped: blocking (prevents task completion or is a serious axe violation), major (task completable but degraded), minor (polish), each with a WCAG success criterion.

## Test plan
- Automated axe assertions become part of the `E19-Q03` nightly run so regressions are caught after this one-off audit closes.
- Manual passes are re-run once after remediation to confirm fixes, with the second transcript attached.
- Third-party or specialist review is optional; if the CDO accessibility lead has capacity, one pass is performed by someone outside the E19 team.

## Security notes
- Screen recordings and transcripts are scrubbed of account identifiers and tokens before being attached to the audit document.
- No production data is used; the audit runs on the fixture stack only.
- Any assistive-technology-only bypass of an authorization state (for example, row content readable when the panel shows an authorization error) is reported as a security finding to `E19-X02`, not only as an a11y finding.

## Accessibility notes
- Success criteria explicitly exercised: 1.3.1 info and relationships, 1.4.1 use of colour, 1.4.3 contrast, 1.4.10 reflow, 1.4.11 non-text contrast, 1.4.12 text spacing, 2.1.1/2.1.2 keyboard and no trap, 2.4.3 focus order, 2.4.7 focus visible, 2.4.11 focus not obscured, 2.5.8 target size, 3.2.2 on input, 3.3.1/3.3.3 error identification and suggestion (row-size clamp message), 4.1.2 name role value, 4.1.3 status messages.
- The table alternative must convey exactly the numbers verified by `E19-Q02`, so accessible content and rendered content cannot diverge.

## Performance notes
- The audit records the cost of the accessible path: the table alternative active must not breach the frame budget, cross-checked against the `E19-Q04` configuration that measures it with a screen reader attached.
- If virtualisation is required to meet both a11y and performance, the chosen approach is documented so later panes do not reinvent it.

## Observability
- Findings are tracked as tickets labelled `a11y` and `area/order-flow`, linked from the audit document and from the E19 epic, so the epic DoD a11y checkbox has evidence behind it.
- The audit document records the exact build sha, browser and AT versions used.

## Definition of Done
- `docs/qa/e19-a11y-audit.md` merged with findings, severities, WCAG references and evidence.
- Zero open blocking findings, or an explicit owner-signed accepted risk recorded on the epic before R2 exit.
- axe-core assertions merged into CI for both screens across all enumerated states.
- Remediation tickets filed and linked; a re-audit pass recorded for every blocking finding fixed.
- Sign-off from the accessibility lead and the E19 frontend lead.

## Dependencies
- `E19-S01`, `E19-S04` (panel behaviour), `E19-D03` (hi-fi design with a11y annotations), `E19-Q03` (deterministic fixtures and axe harness).
- Design-system a11y baselines from E05/E07; engine a11y mirror pattern from E11.

`test/e19-profiles-a11y-audit`

title: Exploratory charters and the E19 profile regression pack
body:
## Context
Scripted suites confirm the behaviours someone already thought of. Profiles are a surface where the interesting defects come from *combinations* nobody enumerated: a swing-anchored profile while replay is scrubbing, a composite spanning a tick-size change, two panes on the same symbol with different row sizes, a preset saved in TPO mode applied to a delta profile, naked POCs accumulating over a weekend of thin trade. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` pairs scripted testing with time-boxed exploratory charters for exactly this reason.

This ticket also assembles the durable regression pack: the subset of E19 checks that must keep running long after R2, because profiles feed alerts and rules and will be silently depended upon by later epics.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Surfaces under charter: SCR-038 profile panel, SCR-039 settings dialog; components CMP-110 ProfileBar, CMP-183 VolumeProfilePane, CMP-184 MarketProfileTpoPane, CMP-199 ChartLegend, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge; contracts `GET /market/profile` and WS `profile.{symbol}.{kind}`; stories US-VP-001..US-VP-009.
- **Exploratory charters** in `qa/charters/e19/`, each a 90-minute time-boxed session with a stated mission, coverage area, oracle and debrief notes:
  1. *Period-mode blending* - switch rapidly between composite, session multiples, visible range, personalised range and swing-anchored while data streams; hunt for stale rows, mismatched legends and orphaned POC lines.
  2. *Multi-pane disagreement* - two or more profile panes on one symbol with different `price_grouping`, `value_area_pct` and kinds; hunt for shared-state bleed and contradictory POCs.
  3. *Thin and pathological markets* - a symbol trading at three price levels, a symbol with a single enormous print, a symbol newly listed mid-session.
  4. *Boundary times* - UTC midnight rollover, `funding_8h` anchor crossings, a custom anchor equal to the current time, weekend low-liquidity composites.
  5. *Interaction with replay and recorder* (E26/E16) - scrubbing while a visible-range profile is active, entering replay mid-period, pinning and unpinning recorded symbols.
  6. *Settings and presets abuse* - extreme but legal values (`value_area_pct` 50 and 95, `price_grouping` 1000, `tpo_period_minutes` 1 and 240), preset applied across kinds and symbols, export/import round-trips.
  7. *Long-session soak by hand* - leave a session profile open for a full trading day and inspect for drift against a fresh rebuild at the end.
- **Regression pack** `qa/regression/e19-pack.md`: the durable subset (oracle equality on three canonical fixtures, POC/VA metric publication, axis alignment, partial/approximated states, WS resubscribe equality, preset round-trip) with an owner, a cadence (per-release) and expected runtime.
- **Triage output**: every charter produces bugs or an explicit "no findings" note; findings judged systemic are proposed as new scripted cases in `E19-Q01`/`E19-Q02`/`E19-Q03` so the pack learns.
- A short **heuristics sheet** for profile testing (invariants worth checking anywhere: totals reconcile, POC is inside the value area, VAH >= POC >= VAL, rows are unique per price, sum of buy and sell equals volume, delta equals buy minus sell) reusable by E18, E21 and E23.

## Out of scope
- Automated implementation of newly found cases - charters produce tickets, the owning suites implement them.
- Performance measurement (`E19-Q04`) and the a11y audit (`E19-Q06`), though charters may surface qualitative concerns and hand them over.
- Production monitoring of profiles (E42/ops).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Charters are executed and debriefed
  Given the seven charters in qa/charters/e19
  When each is executed as a time-boxed session against a staging build
  Then each has a written debrief stating coverage achieved, bugs filed and areas deliberately not covered

Scenario: Invariants hold everywhere they are checked
  Given the heuristics sheet invariants
  When they are applied across every charter session
  Then no violation is observed, or each violation is filed as a bug with a reproduction

Scenario: Failure case - a systemic finding becomes a scripted case
  Given a charter finds that swing-anchored profiles lose their anchor after a timeframe change
  Then a bug is filed and a new scripted case is added to the relevant suite, not merely noted in the debrief

Scenario: Edge case - long-session drift
  Given a session profile left open for a full 24 h trading day
  When a fresh rebuild is compared to the live accumulated profile at the end
  Then they are identical, or the difference is filed as a P0 correctness bug

Scenario: Regression pack is executable and owned
  Given qa/regression/e19-pack.md
  When a release candidate is prepared
  Then the pack runs within its stated runtime, has a named owner, and produces a recorded pass or fail
```

## Technical notes / design
- Charters are session-based: the tester records a timestamped log, and the debrief distinguishes setup time, test design time and bug investigation time so coverage claims are honest.
- The heuristics sheet is deliberately generic across order-flow surfaces, because the same reconciliation invariants catch footprint, CVD and profile aggregation bugs, and one shared sheet avoids three divergent ones.
- The regression pack is sized to run inside a release-candidate window; anything slower belongs to nightly rather than the pack.
- Charter 7 (long-session soak by hand) is the only manual-only item that must survive into the regression pack, because it is the cheapest detector of cumulative drift and is not worth automating before E46.

## Test plan
- Two testers execute independently where charters overlap (2 and 4) to measure how much is found by a second pair of eyes; the result informs whether charters continue into R3.
- Every filed bug is verified fixed by the same tester who found it before the epic sign-off in `E19-Q08`.
- The regression pack is dry-run once end to end and its runtime recorded.

## Security notes
- Charters use non-production accounts on staging; the extreme-values charter overlaps with `E19-X02` and any finding with a security flavour (resource exhaustion, authorization bypass, information leak in an error) is routed to Security, not closed as a functional bug.
- Testers are instructed never to paste live API keys or account identifiers into charter notes or screenshots.

## Accessibility notes
- Each charter includes at least ten minutes of keyboard-only or screen-reader-on exploration, so accessibility defects are found by people using the feature rather than only by the formal audit.
- Any a11y finding is cross-filed to `E19-Q06` remediation tracking.

## Performance notes
- Charters record subjective responsiveness and any observed stutter with the conditions that produced it; these observations become candidate scenarios for `E19-Q04` rather than being dismissed as anecdote.
- The long-session charter also records memory growth of the browser tab, which is the most likely home for a profile-related leak.

## Observability
- Debriefs name the build sha, fixtures and environment; bugs carry HAR/WS captures and the `x-request-id` of relevant calls.
- Charter outcomes are summarised in the E19 quality dashboard so exploratory coverage is visible next to automated coverage.

## Definition of Done
- All seven charters executed and debriefed; every finding filed, triaged and either fixed or explicitly deferred with an owner.
- `qa/regression/e19-pack.md` merged with an owner, cadence and measured runtime, and referenced from the release checklist.
- The heuristics sheet merged and referenced by the E18/E21/E23 test plans.
- Systemic findings converted into scripted cases in the owning suites.

## Dependencies
- `E19-Q02`, `E19-Q03` and `E19-Q05` provide the automated baseline so charters spend their time on the unknown rather than re-checking the known.
- Replay/recorder surfaces from E26/E16 for charter 5.

## Branch
`test/e19-exploratory-and-regression`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (exploratory charters, session-based testing, regression packs)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 9
- `qa/plans/e19-profiles-test-plan.md`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 5 (invariants underpinning the heuristics sheet)
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (release checklist consuming the regression pack)

- **Exploratory charters** in `qa/charters/e19/`, each a 90-minute time-boxed session with a stated mission, coverage area, oracle and debrief notes:

title: E19 QA sign-off: rollup, traceability evidence and R2 exit-gate input
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 requires an epic-level QA sign-off - a regression and exploratory pass executed and recorded at the epic level, not merely the sum of child tickets - plus rolled-up coverage, no open P0/P1 bugs, a11y verification and recorded performance numbers. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` gates the R2 Order-flow beta train on those exits. E19 is one of the R2 epics whose output (POC, VAH, VAL as exact metrics) is consumed by later trains, so signing it off loosely would export uncertainty into E40 alerts and the rule engine.

This ticket is the single artefact the R2 gate reviews for profiles.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Sign-off covers SCR-038 profile panel and SCR-039 settings dialog, components CMP-110 / CMP-183 / CMP-184 / CMP-199 / CMP-227, and stories US-VP-001..US-VP-009.
- `docs/qa/e19-signoff.md` containing:

  - **Coverage rollup**: profile engine package >= 85% line coverage, frontend profile modules >= 80%, with the report links and any exclusion justified.


## Technical notes / design
- The document is assembled from links to primary evidence rather than restating numbers, with one exception: the performance verdicts and the coverage figures are copied in, because a gate reviewer must not have to open six tabs to see whether the epic passed.

title: Composite and per-session multiple profiles served from the cold tier
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-003 — Composite / multi-period profiles (Should)**. Longer-term value only shows up when sessions are merged, and "per session, side by side" multiples are how traders compare successive days' acceptance. The NFR binds this story to the storage tier: "composite queries served from the **cold tier (Parquet/DuckDB)** within 2 s for 30 sessions", and the third scenario makes recorder coverage a first-class product behaviour rather than an error: "the composite is built from what exists and **states the covered range explicitly**".

## Scope / Deliverables
- `split=composite`: N selected sessions merged into one profile — summed element-wise **before** POC/VA computation (`24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2: "Composites never average; they accumulate"), with its own POC and value area.
- `split=session` multiples: one profile per session drawn at its own time position on the chart's time axis, each with its own POC/VA.
- Composite anchors in **SCR-039**: session / day / week / custom range picker, plus look-back count.
- Cold-tier query path: Parquet/DuckDB for windows outside hot retention, `meta.sources` reporting the mix; progress indication rather than a frozen pane for long look-backs (SCR-039 perf note).
- Coverage honesty: covered range stated in the legend, the partial-history chip when the recorder covers fewer sessions than requested, and a warning (not a block) when the requested look-back exceeds recorded history (SCR-039 validation).

## Out of scope
- Recorder retention policy and Parquet export itself — **E16**; this story consumes the cold tier.
- Automatic "composite of the current balance area" detection — **E25**.
- Cross-symbol composites.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Composite of N sessions
  When I select the last 5 sessions
  Then one merged profile is drawn with its own POC and value area

Scenario: Multiples
  When I choose "per session, side by side"
  Then each session gets its own profile drawn at its own time position

Scenario: Recorder limit
  Given the recorder covers fewer sessions than requested
  Then the composite is built from what exists and states the covered range explicitly

Scenario: Cold query stays within budget
  Given a 30-session composite request
  Then it is served from Parquet/DuckDB within 2 s and meta.sources reports parquet

Scenario: Composites accumulate, never average
  Given two sessions with known level volumes
  Then every composite level equals the exact sum of the contributing sessions and the composite POC is computed after summation

Scenario: Gap inside the look-back
  Given a recording gap inside the requested sessions
  Then the affected sessions are flagged and the composite states which days are missing rather than silently omitting them
```

## Technical notes / design
The merge is element-wise on sparse level dicts, which is why accumulation order is irrelevant and the result is exactly reproducible. Long look-backs stream results per session so the pane can render progressively and show progress; the composite POC/VA are computed only once all contributing sessions have landed, so the user never sees a POC that jumps as data arrives. Where the hot and cold tiers both cover part of a window, the hot tier wins for the overlapping range to avoid double counting, and `meta.sources` lists both.

## Test plan
Unit: element-wise merge, accumulate-not-average assertion, hot/cold overlap resolution, coverage computation. Integration: 30-session Parquet fixture with a deliberate gap; hot/cold boundary fixture. E2E: composite of 5 sessions; per-session multiples; look-back exceeding history shows a warning and still renders. Perf: 30-session composite p95 ≤ 2 s, recorded in the load report.

## Security notes
Look-back is bounded by `fixed_duration_minutes ≤ 10080` and the session-count cap; combined with T02's per-user cold-query concurrency limit this is the mitigation for cold-tier resource exhaustion — a 30-session DuckDB scan is the most expensive request in the market-data API and must not be issuable without limit. No user input reaches SQL unparameterised.

## Accessibility notes
The covered range and any missing sessions are stated in text and announced on load, never implied by a faded bar. Per-session multiples are individually labelled with their session date so the table alternative can group rows by session. The composite anchor picker is a grouped, labelled form with an explicit description of what each anchor changes.

## Performance notes
≤ 2 s for 30 sessions from the cold tier (US-VP-003 NFR); progressive per-session rendering so first paint is fast; merged profile respects the 5 000-row cap with LOD merging.

## Observability
`profile_composite_duration_ms{sessions}`, `profile_cold_query_duration_ms`, `profile_composite_sessions_missing`; analytics `profile.composite_lookback_changed`, `profile.multiples_toggled`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] 2 s budget demonstrated on the 30-session fixture in CI's perf job.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% backend / ≥80% frontend; axe-core green; design-qa sign-off; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E19-S02** (period lifecycle and multi-instance panes), **E16** (recorder, retention and Parquet cold tier). Blocks **E19-S09** only informally (presets include composite anchors).

## Branch
`feat/e19-composite-profiles`

title: TPO / market profile with 24-7 periods, initial balance and single prints
body:
## Context
Implements **US-VP-008 — TPO / market profile (Should)**: letter-based time-at-price with "a 24/7-appropriate period definition". Classic market profile assumes an RTH session; crypto has none, so `24-internal-schemas.md` §5.2 pins the adaptation: `tpo_period_min` (default 30) buckets, letters assigned `A…Z, a…z, AA…` by bucket index, TPO POC/VA computed with `tpo_count` in place of `volume`, UTC-anchored by default. The document is explicit that TPO and volume profiles **can disagree** (one huge print vs. many periods at a level) and that this is a feature. Note the roadmap's §11 descoping ladder lists "TPO/market-profile mode and composite profiles" as the **first** candidate to slip to R5 if R2 capacity is short — this story is therefore built to be independently deferrable, behind a feature flag, with no other VP story depending on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- TPO accumulation in `ProfileEngine`: per-level `tpo_count` incremented once per bucket that touches the level regardless of volume; `tpo_period_minutes` configurable 1–240 (REST bound).
- `kind=tpo` on `GET /market/profile` and `profile.{symbol}.tpo` on WS.
- Letter rendering in the T04 plugin (**CMP-184** MarketProfileTpoPane): letters per price per period, letter size configurable (SCR-039), collapsing to blocks when letters fall below legibility size.
- TPO POC/VAH/VAL via **E19-S04**'s expansion algorithm over `tpo_count`, including the `two_row_tpo` option that exists precisely for reference-platform parity.
- **Initial balance**: the first N periods marked and their range labelled; N configurable.
- **Single prints**: rows touched by exactly one period highlighted with a glyph, toggleable.
- Overlay mode: TPO and volume profile drawn together on one price axis, since they intentionally disagree.
- Feature flag `profiles.tpo` so the mode can ship dark if R2 capacity is short.

## Out of scope
- RTH/overnight session semantics, open/close ranges and other equity-market profile conventions.
- TPO-based composites (composite is volume/delta in R2; TPO composites are a Could).
- Letter-based alerting — **E40**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: TPO built
  Given 30-minute TPO periods anchored to the configured day boundary
  Then letters accumulate per price per period and the profile shape is drawn

Scenario: Initial balance
  Then the first N periods are marked as the initial balance with its range labelled

Scenario: Single prints
  Then single-print rows are highlighted with a glyph and can be toggled off

Scenario: TPO and volume may disagree
  Given one very large print at a level touched by a single period
  Then the volume profile shows a high-volume level while the TPO profile shows a single print, and both are correct and can be overlaid

Scenario: Letters exceed the alphabet
  Given a session with more than 52 periods
  Then letters continue as AA, AB, ... deterministically and remain unique within the session

Scenario: Letters below legible size
  Given the period is dense enough that letters would render under the legibility threshold
  Then the profile collapses to blocks with the letter mapping still available on hover and in the table alternative
```

## Technical notes / design
TPO is a second counter on the **same** `ProfileLevel`, not a second engine — that is what lets the overlay be exactly row-aligned with the volume profile. Bucket membership is computed from the trade timestamp and the session anchor, so replay produces identical letters. Letter rendering reuses the SDF glyph atlas within the ≤3 text-draw-call budget; when letters are too small the plugin switches to the block path automatically, which also keeps the 5 000-row cap achievable. The `two_row_tpo` value-area variant is wired here because TPO is where parity with reference platforms is actually scrutinised.

## Test plan
Unit (≥85%): bucket assignment across the anchor boundary, letter sequence past Z and past z, `tpo_count` increment-once-per-bucket rule, IB range, single-print detection, TPO VA under both algorithms. Golden data: a fixture session with a published expected letter grid. E2E: TPO mode, IB labelling, single-print toggle, overlay with volume. Visual: golden images for letters and the collapsed block mode, both themes. Perf: TPO session render within the R4 budget at maximum period count.

## Security notes
`tpo_period_minutes` bounded 1–240 server-side — a 1-minute period over a week is the obvious amplification request and is covered by the existing window bounds and the cold-query concurrency limit. Read-only, `marketdata:read`. The feature flag is server-evaluated so a client cannot enable a dark mode by flipping local state.

## Accessibility notes
Letters are decorative encoding, not an accessible representation: the table alternative lists each price row with its period count, its letter set and IB/single-print membership, and POC/VAH/VAL are announced. The collapsed block mode keeps the letter mapping available on hover and in the table. Single prints and IB use glyph plus text, never colour alone. Letter size is user-configurable with a minimum that meets legibility guidance.

## Performance notes
TPO adds one integer per level per bucket — negligible engine cost. Render cost is dominated by letters; the automatic collapse to blocks keeps the ≤ 8 ms R4 budget and the ≤3 text draw calls intact at high density. Measured in the B-profile benchmark with a TPO case.

## Observability
`profile_tpo_periods{symbol}`, `profile_tpo_render_mode{letters|blocks}`, `profile_tpo_compute_duration_ms`; analytics `profile.mode_changed{mode=tpo}`, `profile.tpo_period_changed`, `profile.single_prints_toggled`, `profile.ib_periods_changed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests; expected letter grid asserted against the fixture.
- [ ] Feature flag wired and defaulted per the R2 capacity decision.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% engine / ≥80% frontend; axe-core green; screen-reader pass on the table alternative.
- [ ] Golden images approved; design-qa sign-off; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E19-S04** (value-area algorithm reused with `tpo_count`); requires **US-CHART-009** session anchoring from E12. Blocks nothing — deliberately, so it can be descoped to R5 per `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.

`feat/e19-tpo-profile`

title: SAST/DAST rules and CI security gates for the profile compute and read paths
body:
## Context
The planning brief requires SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA, secrets scanning and DAST (OWASP ZAP) as standing gates, and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` expects each epic to contribute the rules that encode *its* specific hazards. Generic rules will not catch the things that actually threaten profiles: string-built time-series queries against QuestDB or DuckDB, unbounded window handling, cost-unbounded cold-tier reads, error handlers that echo store details, and accumulation paths that are not keyed idempotently.

This ticket turns the `E19-X01` mitigations into automation that keeps enforcing them after the humans move to R3.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Custom Semgrep rules** in `security/semgrep/e19/`:
  - Ban string interpolation or f-strings in any QuestDB/DuckDB/SQL query construction inside the profile engine and market-data routers; require parameterised queries or the approved query builder.
  - Require every profile query path to pass through the bounded-window validator; flag any handler reading `from`/`to` without it.
  - Flag exception handlers in the market-data routers that serialise exception text, `repr`, or store client errors into responses instead of mapping to the documented error catalogue.
  - Flag accumulation code paths that mutate a period without a trade-id/sequence idempotency key.
  - Flag any profile endpoint or WS topic handler lacking an explicit permission declaration (`marketdata:read`).
- **CodeQL / Bandit configuration** extended to cover the profile engine package and the market-data API module, with the relevant query packs enabled and findings failing the build at the agreed severity.
- **DAST (OWASP ZAP) profile** for the read surface: an authenticated scan context for `/api/v1/market/profile` seeded with the OpenAPI definition, plus a WS-aware scripted check for `profile.*` subscription authorization, with a tuned false-positive baseline committed so the scan is actionable rather than noisy.
- **CI gates**: rules wired into the existing security workflow, scoped so they run on PRs touching the profile engine, market-data routers or WS routing; documented severity thresholds for blocking versus reporting.
- **Rule tests**: each custom rule ships with a positive and a negative fixture proving it fires on the hazard and does not fire on the approved pattern.
- Short **runbook section** in `docs/security/ci-gates.md` explaining each E19 rule, why it exists (linked to the threat it mitigates) and how to fix a violation, so a developer hitting the gate is unblocked without asking Security.

## Out of scope
- Container and dependency scanning (Trivy, pip-audit, npm audit) - programme-level, already enforced by E03/E43.
- Runtime WAF or network controls; infrastructure hardening.
- The abuse-case suite itself (`E19-X02`), which is dynamic testing rather than static analysis.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rules fire on their hazards
  Given the positive fixtures for each custom rule
  When the security workflow runs
  Then every rule reports a finding on its positive fixture and reports nothing on its negative fixture

Scenario: A string-built store query cannot merge
  Given a pull request that builds a QuestDB query by interpolating the symbol parameter
  When CI runs
  Then the security job fails and names the rule and the file and line

Scenario: Failure case - an unvalidated window handler is caught
  Given a new profile handler that reads from and to without the bounded-window validator
  Then the rule fires and the PR is blocked until the validator is applied or an explicit reviewed suppression with a reason is added

Scenario: DAST scan is actionable
  Given the ZAP scan against the staging profile endpoint
  When it completes
  Then it produces zero unreviewed high findings and its baseline file explains every suppressed alert

Scenario: Edge case - suppression requires justification
  Given a developer adds a nosemgrep or equivalent suppression
  Then CI requires an inline reason and a linked ticket, and an unjustified suppression fails the build
```

## Technical notes / design
- Rules are scoped by path so they are precise and cheap; a broad repository-wide ban on string queries would drown teams in false positives and be disabled within a sprint, which is the usual failure mode of security gates.
- The bounded-window rule is written against the *validator symbol* rather than a pattern of arithmetic, so it survives refactoring of the limit logic and only requires the call site to be present.
- The DAST context uses the OpenAPI file directly, so new parameters are scanned automatically; the WS check is scripted separately because ZAP does not natively reason about the subscription protocol.
- Severity thresholds are agreed with DevSecOps up front and recorded, so a blocking finding is never a surprise negotiated during a release crunch.

## Test plan
- Rule fixtures run in CI as part of the security workflow's own self-test.
- The DAST profile is exercised once against staging during this ticket and then nightly; the baseline is reviewed whenever the contract changes.
- A deliberate regression PR (interpolated query) is opened on a scratch branch to prove the gate blocks, with evidence attached.

## Security notes
- Scanner credentials and ZAP contexts are stored as CI secrets; the committed context file contains no tokens.
- Findings are triaged per `04-security-program.md`; high severity blocks merge, medium is time-boxed with an owner, low is tracked.
- The rules themselves are reviewed by the Security engineer, since a poorly written rule creates false confidence, which is worse than no rule.
- Suppressions are auditable: every suppression carries a reason and a ticket, and a periodic report lists all active suppressions on E19 paths.

## Accessibility notes
- Not directly applicable (CI tooling). Indirectly, the error-catalogue rule protects the accessible error states on `SCR-038` by preventing raw exception text - which is neither announced well nor comprehensible - from reaching the UI.

## Performance notes
- The added security jobs must not extend PR feedback time beyond the agreed CI budget; path scoping and rule caching keep the incremental cost under the target, and the added duration is measured and recorded in the ticket.
- The nightly DAST scan runs off the critical path so it never gates interactive development.

## Observability
- Security job results are published to the programme security dashboard with per-epic attribution, so E19's gate health is visible alongside other epics.
- Suppression counts and finding trends are reported, making a slow erosion of the gates detectable rather than invisible.

## Definition of Done
- Custom rules, CodeQL/Bandit configuration and the ZAP profile merged and running in CI.
- Every rule has passing positive and negative fixtures; the deliberate regression PR demonstrated to block.
- `docs/security/ci-gates.md` updated with the E19 section including fix guidance.
- Baseline reviewed and zero unreviewed high findings; DevSecOps and Security engineer approval recorded.

## Dependencies
- `E19-X01` (threats the rules encode), `E19-T01`/`E19-T02` (the code paths and the bounded-window validator to reference).
- Existing security workflow and scanner infrastructure from E03/E04.

## Branch
`chore/e19-security-ci-gates`

- `docs/security/threat-models/e19-profiles.md`
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` (M9 order-flow engines, M23 gateway)

title: Security review and sign-off for E19 profiles
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 requires, for any epic labelled `security`, a finalised STRIDE model, triaged findings and a written sign-off from the Security engineer before the epic can be Done - and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` gates R2 on its epics' exits. E19 publishes values that automation will trade against, so its security posture is a prerequisite for the alerting and rule work in later trains, not an afterthought that can be cleaned up during hardening.

This ticket is the white-box counterpart to the black-box abuse testing: a human review of the profile code paths against the threat model, followed by the formal sign-off artefact.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box security review** of the profile implementation:
  - Query construction in the profile engine and market-data routers (parameterisation, symbol validation against the instrument registry, window bounding, row caps).
  - Idempotency and ordering of accumulation (trade-id keying, out-of-order and duplicate handling, period assignment from timestamps, clamping of implausible timestamps).
  - Cache and store trust: the 5 s flush, restart rebuild, `metadata_version` invalidation, and what is assumed about store integrity.
  - Authorization on both transports: `marketdata:read` enforcement on REST and on WS subscribe, symbol allow-list handling, revocation on token expiry, and preset/workspace ownership checks.
  - Error handling and information disclosure across the profile surface, verified against the documented error catalogue.
  - Resource governance: bounded windows, row caps, subscription quotas, rate limits and their defaults as shipped (not as designed).
  - Dependency review of any new library introduced by the epic (statistics, compression, columnar readers), including licence and maintenance posture.
- **Findings triage**: all findings from `E19-X01` (model), `E19-X02` (abuse cases), `E19-X03` (SAST/DAST) and the security-relevant results of `E19-Q05` (chaos) consolidated into one list with severity, disposition and owner.
- **Sign-off document** `docs/security/signoff/e19-profiles.md`: scope reviewed, method, findings summary, residual risks with Owner acceptance where applicable, items deferred to the R4 pen-test scope, and an explicit verdict.
- **Handover notes** to E40 (alerts) and the rule engine: the integrity and repudiation guarantees the profile metrics do and do not provide, so consuming epics design accordingly rather than assuming.

## Out of scope
- Remediation work itself, which lands on the owning engineering tickets; this review blocks on remediation but does not perform it.
- Programme-level pen-test execution (E43) - this ticket contributes scope to it.
- Infrastructure and host hardening (E03/E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every threat has a verified control
  Given docs/security/threat-models/e19-profiles.md
  When the review walks each mitigation to the shipped code and configuration
  Then each is confirmed implemented with a code or config reference, or is recorded as a finding

Scenario: Findings are consolidated and dispositioned
  Given findings from E19-X01, E19-X02, E19-X03 and E19-Q05
  When they are triaged
  Then every finding has a severity, an owner and a disposition of fixed, accepted with Owner sign-off, or deferred with a target train

Scenario: Failure case - an open high finding blocks sign-off
  Given an open high-severity finding that symbol input reaches a store query unparameterised
  When sign-off is attempted
  Then the verdict is "not signed", the E19 epic and E19-Q08 are blocked, and no conditional sign-off is issued

Scenario: Edge case - a residual risk is accepted explicitly
  Given the store-integrity assumption cannot be fully enforced in R2
  Then the residual risk is written in plain language, accepted by the Owner with a date, and handed to the R4 pen-test scope

Scenario: Consuming epics receive the guarantees in writing
  When the sign-off is published
  Then it states what integrity and auditability guarantees profile metrics provide, and E40 and the rule engine epics are linked to it
```

## Technical notes / design
- The review is performed against the release-candidate build, not against the design: defaults as shipped (actual limit values, actual quota numbers) are what get recorded, because a control configured to an ineffective value is not a control.
- Reviewer independence: the reviewer is the Security engineer, not an E19 implementer; the order-flow lead attends as an explainer rather than a reviewer.
- The handover notes are the highest-value durable output - later epics will build automated trading behaviour on these metrics, and the failure mode to avoid is an unstated assumption that a profile value is tamper-evident when it is only tamper-resistant.
- Deferred items are written directly in pen-test-scope language so E43 can adopt them without re-analysis.

## Test plan
- Verification is evidence-based: each control confirmed by a passing test from `E19-X02`, `E19-Q02` or `E19-Q05`, or by a manual check recorded in the document; "reviewed the code and it looks fine" is not accepted as evidence for a rated threat.
- Re-verification of every fixed finding on the candidate build before the verdict is issued.

## Security notes
- Follows the `04-security-program.md` sign-off template; the verdict feeds the programme risk register and the R2 PRR.
- Sensitive finding detail remains in the private security tracker; the public document carries summaries and references.
- The review explicitly checks that nothing in the epic introduced a dependency on privileges beyond `marketdata:read`, keeping the read surface's blast radius minimal ahead of live enablement.

## Accessibility notes
- Confirms that every security-driven user-facing state introduced by remediation (rate limited, unauthorized, validation error) is present in the `SCR-038` state list and was covered by the `E19-Q06` audit, so security fixes cannot quietly create inaccessible dead ends.

## Performance notes
- Records the shipped values of the resource-governance limits and confirms they match the numbers measured in `E19-Q04`, so the security review and the performance report cannot claim different ceilings.

## Observability
- Confirms the detection telemetry from `E19-X01` exists in staging and that alerts are configured for the security-relevant signals (rejected windows, quota rejections, authorization failures, rebuild failures).
- Any missing detection is a finding with an ops owner, not a documentation note.

## Definition of Done
- `docs/security/signoff/e19-profiles.md` merged with an explicit verdict and no open high findings.
- All findings dispositioned with owners; residual risks Owner-accepted with dates; deferred items added to the R4 pen-test scope.
- Handover notes delivered and linked from the E40 and rule-engine epics.
- Signed by the Security engineer; acknowledged by the Architect and the order-flow lead; referenced from `E19-Q08` and the E19 epic.

## Dependencies
- `E19-X01`, `E19-X02`, `E19-X03` and the security-relevant results of `E19-Q05`; the R2 release-candidate build.
- E09 RBAC and E17 WS authorization as inherited controls.

## Branch
`chore/e19-security-signoff`

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (review and sign-off template, risk register)
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` (R2 exit criteria); `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`

title: Design QA sweep of the built tape and bubble overlay
body:
## Context
DoD §3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec (spacing/tokens/type/colour/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer, with discrepancies fixed or filed as follow-up Bugs. E22 ships a net-new screen (SCR-053) and a net-new chart primitive (CMP-112), and R2's design gate (roadmap §6.4) explicitly requires a "design-QA sweep on footprint/heatmap density and legibility at all supported densities" — the same legibility bar applies to the tape.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Side-by-side sweep of the built SCR-053 against the E22-D05 pack: both densities, both themes, all states (streaming, paused, filtered-empty, disconnected, partial-history, over-threshold warning).
- Bubble-layer sweep on SCR-030: radius curves at `linear` and `log`, buy/sell shape+colour encoding, alpha-by-age, cluster count badge at >500 instances, legend text naming the active scale.
- Greyscale and colour-blind simulation pass on the size tiers and buy/sell encoding.
- Reduced-motion pass (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`) confirming D04's static alternatives are implemented.
- Discrepancy log: each item either fixed in-sprint or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*` label and a link to the spec line it violates.

## Out of scope
Functional/black-box testing (E22-Q02), a11y audit (E22-Q04), performance (E22-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full state sweep
  When every state in the handoff pack is reproduced in the built app at both densities and both themes
  Then each is recorded as pass or as a logged discrepancy referencing the spec line

Scenario: Token drift caught
  Given a colour or spacing value in the build that is not a design token
  Then it is logged as a discrepancy and either fixed or filed as a Bug

Scenario: Reduced motion honoured
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  Then no continuous tape or bubble animation runs and every value snaps per the D04 spec
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the recorded high-volatility fixture to reproduce the dense states rather than waiting for a live burst; the paused state is the only reliable way to inspect a 2 000 prints/s tape frame-by-frame.

## Test plan
Manual sweep with screenshots attached per state; discrepancy log committed to the ticket.

## Security notes
N/A.

## Accessibility notes
Checks overlapping with Q04 (focus visibility, target size, contrast) are performed here too but Q04 owns the formal audit; report any finding to both.

## Performance notes
Note any state where the visual matches the spec only by dropping frames — that is a defect, not a pass.


## Observability
Verify the analytics events named in the E22-D05 handoff pack are actually wired and firing with the specified payloads: `tape.filter_changed`, `tape.paused`, `tape.resumed`, `tape.print_clicked`, plus the bubble-overlay toggle. Any event present in the pack but missing in the build is logged as a design-QA defect like a visual discrepancy. No new telemetry is introduced by this ticket; findings are recorded as counts per severity on the sweep report.

## Definition of Done
Sweep complete for every state; discrepancies fixed or filed with priorities; designer sign-off comment posted; `14-screens-catalogue.md`/`15-component-catalogue.md` updated if the shipped design legitimately diverged.

## Dependencies
E22-S01, E22-S03, E22-S05 must be functionally complete.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).

title: Playwright E2E suite for tape, thresholds, clustering and bubbles
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E (Playwright, web + Electron) at the top of the pyramid, and the Story DoD requires each Gherkin scenario to be demonstrated by an automated test where possible. E22-Q01's plan defines *what*; this ticket automates the subset that belongs in E2E — the cross-surface and stateful journeys that unit and component tests cannot cover.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under the web E2E suite, driven by a replayed recorded fixture so runs are deterministic:
  1. **Tape basics** — prints render newest-first with ms timestamps, price, size and side glyph; disconnect shows the disconnected state; resubscribe re-seeds without duplicate rows.
  2. **Pause/resume** — `P` pauses, the buffered count is shown on resume, focus and scroll anchor survive.
  3. **Click-to-locate** — clicking a print moves the crosshair on a synced chart to that timestamp.
  4. **Thresholds** — set notional, percentile and absolute modes; assert the effective absolute threshold is displayed in percentile mode; assert the over-flagging warning appears with a deliberately low threshold.
  5. **Per-symbol memory** — different thresholds on BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT survive symbol switching, reload and a new session.
  6. **Clustering** — turn clustering on, assert merged rows/bubbles with constituent counts, assert the `(estimated)` badge and popover content, change the window and assert immediate recompute.
  7. **Cross-surface agreement** — for one chosen print, assert the tape highlight, the bubble presence and the `GET /market/metrics` value refer to the same print.
  8. **Filters and columns** — filter to sells above a notional, assert chips and the filtered-empty state; enable the cumulative-delta column; reload and assert persistence; run the whole journey keyboard-only.
- Electron-shell run of the critical subset (1, 2, 4, 6) per the strategy's web + Electron requirement.
- Stable selectors (`data-testid`) added where missing, agreed with the story owners.

## Out of scope
Perf measurement (E22-Q03); axe/manual a11y audit (E22-Q04) beyond the keyboard-only journey; backend unit/contract tests (E22-T01/T02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Suite is deterministic
  When the suite runs ten times in CI against the replayed fixture
  Then it passes ten times with no retries, or any inherent flakiness is quarantined with a named cause rather than a blanket retry

Scenario: Cross-surface agreement is asserted
  Then at least one test asserts that the same print is flagged in the tape, drawn as a bubble and reported by the metrics endpoint

Scenario: A regression is caught
  Given the client is temporarily patched to filter prints locally instead of using the server flag
  Then the cross-surface agreement test fails
```

## Technical notes / design
Drive the clock from the replay engine rather than `waitForTimeout`; assert on rendered text and roles rather than CSS. Keep each spec under the suite's per-test time budget; tag the Electron subset so it can be run separately in the nightly job.

## Test plan
This is test code; its own quality gate is the ten-run determinism check and the mutation check in AC scenario 3.

## Security notes
Runs against staging (demo) with a test account; no live keys in CI; fixtures contain public market data only.

## Accessibility notes
Includes the keyboard-only journey (filter focus with `Ctrl+F`, chip removal, `Alt+↑/↓` column reorder, row navigation, pause) — findings feed E22-Q04.

## Performance notes
E2E is not a benchmark, but assert the absence of silent loss (the `dropped`/`coalesced_count` indicators appear under burst) so a perf regression surfaces functionally too.

## Observability
Attach traces/videos on failure; publish the run summary as a CI artifact.

## Definition of Done
Suite merged and green in CI (web + Electron subset); determinism check recorded; selectors documented; linked from the E22-Q01 plan's traceability table; QA sign-off comment.

## Dependencies
`E22-Q01` (plan), `E22-S01`, `E22-S03`, `E22-S05` (surfaces to drive); clustering coverage additionally depends on `E22-S04`.

## Branch
`chore/e22-e2e-suite`.

title: Perf and load scripts: 2 000 prints/s tape and 5 000-bubble scene
body:
## Context
Two of E22's NFRs are numeric and both feed hard R2 gates: the tape must hold "≥55 fps at 2 000 prints/s" (US-BIG-001) and the bubble layer "≥55 fps with 5 000 visible bubbles" (US-BIG-003), while budget #3 — **WS tick → screen p95 <100 ms** — is a hard R2 exit gate measured end-to-end from Bybit WS receipt at the backend to the paint timestamp in the frontend rAF callback (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2). E22-K01 measured the bubble cost in isolation; this ticket turns the measurements into repeatable CI benchmarks and a load profile over the full path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmark** (CI): bubble series at the instance counts from K01, alone and layered on the R2 reference scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + 3 stat rows + CVD), reporting p50/p95 frame time and fps; fails the build on regression beyond the agreed threshold.
- **Tape benchmark**: replayed burst at 500 / 2 000 / 5 000 prints/s, asserting ≥55 fps, ≤60 DOM rows, bounded worker decode time, and that the ring buffer never loses a print that the frame headers did not report as dropped or coalesced.
- **End-to-end latency harness** for budget #3 on the `trades` path: inject a timestamp at backend WS receipt, correlate with the frontend paint timestamp, report p95/p99 under nominal and realistic-peak load (`06-...` §3.2 definitions).
- **k6/Locust load profile** for the WS fan-out of `trades.{symbol}`: 10 symbols × 5 subscribers at full cadence, asserting backend fan-out add-on ≤20 ms p95 (budget #6) and zero message loss (budget #5).
- **Chaos scenarios**: WS disconnect mid-burst; exchange 5xx; Bybit rate-limit `10018`; a 5× synthetic volatility burst for 60 s — assert the UI degrades visibly (coalescing indicator, dropped counters, disconnected state) and never crashes or silently under-reports.
- A results table recorded on the ticket and carried into E22-T03's ADR.

## Out of scope
Functional E2E (E22-Q02); a11y (E22-Q04); heatmap/footprint benchmarks (E21/E18 own theirs — reuse the harness).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budgets measured, not asserted by feel
  When the benchmarks run on reference hardware
  Then p50 and p95 frame times, fps, and the WS tick to screen p95 and p99 are recorded for every configuration

Scenario: Regression gate
  Given a change that increases bubble draw time beyond the agreed threshold
  When CI runs the engine benchmark
  Then the build fails and names the regressed configuration

Scenario: Degradation is visible under chaos
  Given a 5x synthetic burst for 60 seconds
  Then the app stays above the 30 fps floor or degrades by coalescing, the coalescing factor and dropped counts are displayed, and no print is lost without being counted
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure on the reference machine profile (`06-...` §3.1) and state the hardware in every result; three runs, report the median. Use the replay engine for reproducibility. For budget #3, the Bybit-RTT component is excluded per §3.1 — measure from backend receipt.

## Test plan
This ticket is the test; validate the harness itself by injecting a known 50 ms delay and confirming it appears in the measured p95.

## Security notes
Load tests run against staging only and must respect the exchange rate limits — drive load from recorded fixtures, never by hammering Bybit. A load script pointed at live is a P0 incident; gate it by an environment check in the script itself.

## Accessibility notes
Record whether the announcement opt-in and DOM-mirror markers measurably change frame cost at the cap, so the a11y features are never quietly dropped for performance.

## Performance notes
Budgets under test: #1 (≤16.6 ms p95), #2 (never below 30 fps), #3 (WS→screen p95 <100 ms, hard R2 gate), #5 (zero message loss), #6 (≤20 ms fan-out add-on).

## Observability
Publish results as CI artifacts and push the key series into the Grafana perf dashboard so trends are visible across sprints.

## Definition of Done
Benchmarks merged and running in CI with a regression gate; load profile and chaos scenarios executable on demand and run once for R2; results recorded here and in E22-T03; any budget miss either fixed or recorded as an accepted risk with Owner sign-off in `32-risk-register.md`.

## Dependencies
`E22-K01` (baseline and method), `E22-S01`, `E22-S03` (the surfaces under test).
