title: Black-box test plan and exploratory charter for derivatives metrics
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box plan per feature group alongside the white-box review. This epic's defects are mostly *semantic* - a number that is plausible but wrong, or an absence that reads as a zero - so the plan is written from the eight DERIV stories' acceptance criteria and from the E24-X01 abuse cases rather than from the implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A test plan covering all eight US-DERIV stories: per story, the happy path, the documented edge cases, and the failure cases, each with the fixture needed and the expected observable result.
- The semantic checks that automation alone will miss: zero versus unknown in liquidation bars; predicted versus settled funding; `ws_ticker` versus `rest` OI provenance; a quadrant never invented for a bar without an OI sample; a countdown that stays correct across a settlement rollover and a clock-offset change; an interval of 4 h honoured everywhere including the session anchor.
- Negative tests derived from E24-X01: oversized ranges, missing permissions, flag-stripped payloads, coverage-less liquidation queries.
- An exploratory charter (session-based, 2 x 90 min) with a stated mission: "find a place where the panel implies data we do not have", plus a second charter for the cascade behaviour.
- Defect taxonomy and severity rules for this epic: a missing `(estimated)` badge or a fabricated value is P1; a wrong unit is P1; a spacing deviation is P3.
- Test data plan: which recorded fixtures are needed (normal session, cascade, funding settlement, 4 h-interval symbol, recorder gap, backfill failure) and how each is produced.

## Out of scope
Automation (E24-Q02 E2E, E24-Q03 perf); a11y audit (E24-Q04); the design sweep (E24-D06); unit tests, which live with their stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Coverage of every story
  When the plan is reviewed against 11-user-stories.md section 14
  Then every acceptance scenario of all eight DERIV stories maps to at least one planned test case

Scenario: Semantic checks present
  Then the plan contains explicit cases for zero-versus-unknown, predicted-versus-settled, OI provenance, the None quadrant and countdown rollover

Scenario: Abuse cases included
  Then every abuse case from E24-X01 appears as a negative test case with an expected 4xx or an expected honest UI state

Scenario: Charters executed
  When the exploratory sessions are run
  Then session notes exist with findings, and each finding is either a defect ticket or a recorded non-issue with a reason

Scenario: Fixtures are obtainable
  Then each named fixture either exists in the shared fixture store or has a recorded procedure for producing it, so no test is blocked on data at execution time
```

## Technical notes / design
Plan is written in the standard QA template and linked from the epic. Case ids are stable so E24-Q02's automated cases and E24-Q05's regression pack can reference them rather than restating them.

## Test plan
This ticket produces the plan and executes the charters; the plan itself is reviewed by the QA lead and a developer from the epic.

## Security notes
Security negative cases are included here by design so they are executed manually at least once in addition to the automation in E24-X02.

## Accessibility notes
The plan notes which cases must be repeated with a screen reader, feeding E24-Q04 rather than duplicating it.

## Performance notes
The plan names the perf cases handed to E24-Q03 so responsibility is unambiguous.

## Observability
Charter findings are reported with the observability signals that would have caught them, so gaps in telemetry are also logged as findings.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan covers all eight stories and every abuse case.
- [ ] Charters executed with notes attached.
- [ ] Findings triaged into defect tickets with severities.
- [ ] Fixture list confirmed available.

title: Playwright E2E suite additions for the SCR-054 derivatives panel
body:
## Context
Automates the durable parts of the E24-Q01 plan so the epic's honesty guarantees cannot silently regress after R2. Playwright drives the web app (and the Electron shell) against a deterministic recorded fixture served by a stubbed market-data backend, so cascades and funding settlements happen on demand.

## Scope / Deliverables
- E2E specs under `e2e/derivatives/`: open SCR-054; toggle OI absolute/delta; enable quadrant colouring and assert the text legend; switch funding style and enable annualisation, asserting the tooltip formula; assert the countdown decrements and rolls over at settlement; filter liquidations by notional and assert the legend states the filter; enable estimated zones through the acknowledgement dialog and assert a badge on every zone; assert the partial-history chip names a timestamp; switch the basis source and assert the pane states it.
- Regression guards for the semantic traps: a bar with no OI sample shows the neutral hatch and no quadrant; a window outside recorder coverage shows the no-coverage state rather than an empty list; a failed backfill shows the retry state with a timestamp while live data keeps flowing.
- Deterministic fixture harness: a stub WS/REST backend replaying the recorded symbol-day with controllable time, so the countdown, the settlement and the cascade are reproducible without waiting.
- CI wiring on the standard E2E job with retries limited to flake-detection, plus trace and video artefacts on failure.

## Out of scope
Perf/load (E24-Q03); a11y audit (E24-Q04); unit/component tests; manual exploratory testing (E24-Q01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Suite covers the plan's automatable cases
  When the suite is mapped against the E24-Q01 plan
  Then every case marked automatable has a spec, and the mapping is recorded in the plan

Scenario: Deterministic time
  Given the fixture harness controls the clock
  Then the funding countdown and the settlement rollover are asserted without waiting for real time, and the test is not time-of-day dependent

Scenario: Honesty guards
  Then specs assert the (estimated) badge on every zone, the partial-history chip, the no-coverage state and the neutral hatch for an unclassified bar

Scenario: Failure path
  Given the stub backend returns 5xx for the OI backfill
  Then the spec asserts the retry state with a last-success timestamp and that live OI continues to stream

Scenario: Stability
  When the suite runs ten consecutive times in CI
  Then it passes every time with no quarantined specs, or any flake is fixed rather than retried away
```

## Technical notes / design
Selectors use stable `data-testid` attributes agreed with the story implementers - never text matching, which would break on copy changes. The stub backend reuses the fixture format from E16 so the same recorded day drives E2E, the golden-fixture harness and the perf script. Electron and browser both run the core subset.

## Test plan
Self-testing: each spec is verified to fail when the corresponding behaviour is deliberately broken, so a spec that asserts nothing is caught during review.

## Security notes
Includes the authorisation E2E case (a Viewer-role session still sees market data; an unauthenticated session is redirected to login) without duplicating the API-level tests in E24-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Specs assert keyboard reachability of the main toggles and the presence of the table alternatives; the full audit remains E24-Q04's.

## Performance notes
The suite must complete inside the standard E2E job budget; the cascade scenario in E2E uses a reduced rate, with the full 500 prints/s load left to E24-Q03.

## Observability
Failures publish traces, videos and the client console log so triage does not require a re-run.

title: Cascade load script and perf benchmark for the derivatives surfaces
body:
## Context
The SCR-054 catalogue entry sets a specific, testable budget: liquidation prints coalesce into 250 ms buckets and the panel must not exceed **2 ms scripting per frame** during a cascade of **500 prints/s sustained for 10 s with no dropped frames**. Budget #3 (WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms) is a hard R2 gate and must still hold with `ticker` and `liquidations` in the heaviest topic set. This ticket builds the scripts that prove both, and the chaos scenarios around them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A load generator producing the cascade profile (500 prints/s for 10 s, with a ramp and a burst variant at 1 000 prints/s for 2 s) into the WS fan-out, reusing the k6/Locust harness from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.
- A browser-side benchmark capturing per-frame scripting time, dropped frames, DOM node count and memory during the cascade with SCR-054 open alongside the heaviest R2 scene.
- End-to-end WS tick -> screen latency measurement with the full topic set including `ticker` and `liquidations`, reporting p95 and p99.
- Backend measurements: liquidation ingest lag under cascade; `/market/open-interest`, `/market/funding` and `/market/liquidations` p95 at a full page; `deriv_engine_compute_seconds` p95 for incremental updates.
- Chaos scenarios: ticker socket drop and resubscribe mid-cascade; REST backfill failure during load; clock-offset jump during a running countdown; QuestDB write backpressure.
- Results recorded on this ticket and on the epic against the budget table; a regression threshold wired into the perf CI job.

## Out of scope
Functional E2E (E24-Q02); the golden-fixture correctness harness (E24-T06); optimisation work, which is raised as separate tickets if a budget is missed.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cascade budget
  Given 500 liquidation prints per second sustained for 10 seconds with SCR-054 open
  Then panel scripting stays under 2 ms per frame, no frames are dropped, and the DOM node count stays bounded

Scenario: Latency gate
  When WS tick to screen latency is measured with the heaviest topic set including ticker and liquidations
  Then p95 is under 100 ms and p99 under 250 ms

Scenario: Backend budgets
  Then each of the three history endpoints returns a full page with p95 under 150 ms backend-internal, and engine incremental compute p95 is under 5 ms

Scenario: Chaos - socket drop
  Given the ticker socket drops during a cascade
  Then the client shows stale shading within 2 seconds, resubscribes automatically, recovers without a reload, and no fabricated values appear during the gap

Scenario: Chaos - clock jump
  Given the clock offset jumps by 3 seconds while a countdown is running
  Then the countdown re-anchors to the synced offset within one tick rather than drifting or jumping backwards

Scenario: Budget missed
  Given any measured value exceeds its budget
  Then the run is recorded as a fail, a defect ticket is raised with the measurement, and the epic cannot reach Done on an unrecorded regression
```

## Technical notes / design
Load generation targets the WS fan-out directly so the exchange is never involved; the fixture is the recorded cascade day from E16. Browser measurements use the Performance API and the engine's existing FPS/scripting instrumentation from E11's benchmark harness, so numbers are comparable with other R2 epics. All runs are on the standard benchmark machine profile defined in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; ad-hoc laptops do not count.

## Test plan
The scripts are the deliverable; each is validated by an injected regression (an artificial 5 ms per-frame cost) which must make the run fail.

## Security notes
The cascade profile doubles as the DoS amplification test from E24-X01 threat (D); results are shared with E24-X02 rather than measured twice.

## Accessibility notes
Verifies that announcement throttling holds under load - a cascade must not produce a flood of live-region announcements, which is both an a11y and a performance failure.

## Performance notes
This ticket is the performance evidence for the epic DoD; budgets #1, #2, #3 and #13 plus the SCR-054-specific 2 ms/frame limit are all reported here.

## Observability
Runs export the `deriv_*` metrics to the benchmark dashboard so a later regression can be compared against this baseline.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` behind review (2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner), conventional commits, PR <=400 LOC diff.
- [ ] Unit tests added; coverage >=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend on touched files.

title: Accessibility audit of SCR-054 and the derivatives table alternatives
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI plus a manual screen-reader pass for every new screen. SCR-054 is unusually demanding: three canvas sub-panes each needing a table alternative, a countdown with a strict announcement policy, a burst surface needing announcement throttling, and honesty affordances whose entire point is that they must be perceivable non-visually.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated audit wired into CI for SCR-054, the settings surface, the zone acknowledgement dialog and the SCR-058 drawer section.
- Manual screen-reader passes (NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS) against the checklist produced by E24-D04.
- Verify per sub-pane: a table alternative exists, is reachable by keyboard, and carries units and headers; the canvas is not the only disclosure of any value.
- Verify the countdown is announced at 5 min and 1 min only, never per second; verify cascade announcements are throttled to at most one summary per 5 s.
- Verify non-colour encoding: OI quadrants (pattern + text legend), liquidation side (text), basis sign (text), predicted versus settled funding.
- Verify CMP-227's accessible name contains the literal word "estimated" everywhere it appears, and that it is focusable and opens SCR-058 with Enter.
- Verify keyboard operation end to end with visible focus, including the acknowledgement dialog's focus trap and return-focus behaviour.
- Contrast measurement in both themes for text (>=4.5:1) and graphical boundaries (>=3:1).
- Findings logged with WCAG success-criterion references and severities; re-test after fixes.

## Out of scope
Design-time a11y review (E24-D04); functional E2E (E24-Q02); other screens.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated audit clean
  When axe-core runs on SCR-054 and its dialogs in CI
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations

Scenario: Table alternatives complete
  Then each of the OI, funding and liquidation sub-panes and the basis readout has a keyboard-reachable table alternative with headers and units

Scenario: Announcement policy holds
  When the countdown runs and a cascade occurs
  Then the countdown is announced at 5 minutes and 1 minute only, and cascade announcements occur at most once every 5 seconds

Scenario: Nothing by colour alone
  When the panel is inspected in greyscale
  Then quadrant, liquidation side, basis sign and predicted-versus-settled remain distinguishable

Scenario: Estimated badge is perceivable non-visually
  When a screen reader encounters a zone or a predicted funding value
  Then the word estimated is spoken as part of the accessible name, and the badge can be activated by keyboard to open the methodology

Scenario: Contrast in both themes
  Then every text element measures at least 4.5:1 and every graphical boundary at least 3:1, in dark and light

Scenario: A violation is found
  Then it is logged with its WCAG success criterion and severity, fixed, and confirmed in a re-test before the epic can close
```

## Technical notes / design
Automated runs use the shared axe configuration; canvas surfaces are audited through their DOM mirrors, since axe cannot see pixels - the audit explicitly checks that the mirror exists and is complete rather than accepting a clean run over an empty DOM.

## Test plan
The audit is the test; evidence is the axe report, the screen-reader session recordings and the contrast measurements, all attached.

## Security notes
Overlaps E24-X02 on the badge assertion deliberately: provenance that is only visual is inaccessible, and inaccessible provenance is no provenance.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the a11y evidence for the epic DoD.

## Performance notes
Confirms the announcement throttling that protects both accessibility and the frame budget under cascade.

## Observability
N/A - findings are tracked as tickets.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] axe-core green in CI on all listed surfaces.
- [ ] Manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes recorded.
- [ ] Table alternatives verified per sub-pane.
- [ ] Contrast measured in both themes.
- [ ] All findings fixed and re-tested; accessibility specialist sign-off comment recorded.

## Context
The epic DoD requires an epic-level regression and exploratory pass, not merely the sum of per-story QA. This ticket assembles the durable regression pack that later trains run, performs the final pass across all eight DERIV stories on a release-candidate build, and records the sign-off.

title: Render the open-interest sub-pane on SCR-054 with backfill and gap states
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-001 - Open interest pane (Must)**: "OI renders in a linked sub-pane, backfilled from REST and updated from the tickers stream". This is the first surface of SCR-054 and establishes the pane scaffolding (CMP-186 OiFundingLiqPane) the funding and liquidation sub-panes then slot into. All numbers come from the `DerivativesEngine` via `/market/metrics` and `ticker.{symbol}`; the client computes nothing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The OI sub-pane inside CMP-186 on SCR-054, hosted as a linked chart-engine sub-pane sharing the price pane's time axis (CMP-188 PriceAxis) and crosshair sync (US-DERIV-008 NFR).
- Backfill on mount via `GET /api/v1/market/open-interest?symbol&interval&from&to`, then live extension from `ticker.{symbol}` (`open_interest`, `open_interest_value`).
- Interval alignment: points align to bar boundaries; when the chart interval is finer than the REST native granularity, render the "Native granularity 5 min" note from the E24-D05 copy deck (US-DERIV-001 scenario 2).
- Gap and failure states: a backfill failure renders the missing history as an explicit gap with a retry action carrying `last_success_at`, while live OI keeps streaming (US-DERIV-001 scenario 3); never a blank pane.
- Header readout via CMP-036 KeyValueRow (current OI with unit and the 1 h change), pane legend via CMP-199 ChartLegend, collapse/expand persistence.
- Stale shading after 2 s without an expected update (global convention #4) with the last-good timestamp visible.
- Table alternative: an accessible table of the visible OI points with timestamp, value and unit.
- Analytics: `oi_panel.metric_toggled`, `oi_panel.interval_changed`.

## Out of scope
OI delta and quadrant colouring (E24-S02); funding (E24-S03/S04); liquidations (E24-S05..S07); basis (E24-S08); the endpoint and engine (E24-T01/T04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backfill then live
  Given I open SCR-054 for BTCUSDT on a 5m chart
  Then historical OI is fetched and drawn, and subsequent ticker updates extend the series live without a refetch

Scenario: Interval alignment and the granularity note
  Given the chart is on 1m and the REST native granularity is 5 min
  Then points align to bar boundaries and the pane shows the native-granularity note

Scenario: Backfill failure
  Given the backfill request fails
  Then live OI still streams, the missing history renders as an explicit gap rather than a straight line, a retry action is offered, and the last successful timestamp is shown

Scenario: Stale data
  Given no ticker update arrives for more than 2 seconds
  Then the pane is shaded stale and the last-good timestamp is displayed, and the shading clears on the next update

Scenario: No history recorded
  Given the symbol has never been recorded and the exchange returns no history
  Then the pane shows the designed empty state naming the recording start, not a blank canvas

Scenario: Table alternative
  When I open the pane's table alternative with the keyboard
  Then the visible OI points are listed with timestamps, values and units, and it is reachable without a pointer

Scenario: No client-side computation
  When the pane renders any derived value
  Then it originates from the engine response, and the client performs no arithmetic beyond formatting
```

## Technical notes / design
The sub-pane is created through the chart engine's pane API (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`), sharing the time scale so pan/zoom and crosshair are automatic rather than re-implemented. Data flows through the existing market-data store: one subscription to `ticker.{symbol}`, one history fetch, and a reconciliation step that drops WS points older than the last backfilled point (the WS and REST cadences differ). Formatting uses the descriptor's `unit` from the MetricRegistry so units are never hard-coded in the component.

## Test plan
Unit: reconciliation of backfill and live points, gap detection, granularity-note condition, stale timer. Component/Storybook: CMP-186 OiOnly story with populated, loading, gap, stale and empty states. E2E (in E24-Q02): open the panel, verify the series and the note. Contract: consumes the `/market/open-interest` schema fixture. Coverage >=80% frontend on touched files.

## Security notes
Displays public market data only. The provenance rule applies: a point sourced from `ws_ticker` must not be presented as exchange REST history where the distinction matters - the pane surfaces the source in the tooltip and in the table alternative (E24-X01 threat (T)/(R)).

## Accessibility notes
Table alternative per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §11.3; the pane is a named region; the current-OI readout is a CMP-036 KeyValueRow with unit in its accessible name; the gap and stale states are conveyed in text, not only by shading; keyboard reachable with visible focus; contrast >=4.5:1 text / >=3:1 graphical.

## Performance notes
OI updates arrive at <=1 Hz and the pane renders on change only, never on a timer. Panel scripting <2 ms/frame (SCR-054 budget); frame time p95 <=16.6 ms with the full scene (budget #1); WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms (budget #3).

## Observability
Client analytics `oi_panel.metric_toggled`, `oi_panel.interval_changed`; a client-side error event on backfill failure carrying the status so the retry rate is visible.

title: OI delta mode and OI/price quadrant classification on the OI sub-pane
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-002 - OI delta and price quadrant colouring (Should)**: per-bar OI change classified by price direction so build-ups and squeezes are legible at a glance. The classification itself is `oi_price_quadrant` from the engine (E24-T04); this story is the control surface and the rendering, including the case that most often gets faked - a bar with no OI sample.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Absolute/delta toggle for the OI sub-pane, persisted per user in Postgres `settings` (scope `user`, key `deriv.oi.mode`, values `absolute|delta`).
- Delta mode renders per-bar `open_interest_delta` as a histogram aligned to the bar grid.
- Quadrant colouring toggle (`deriv.oi.quadrant_colouring`) applying the four styles from E24-D03: `long_buildup`, `short_covering`, `short_buildup`, `long_unwind` - each with a distinct **pattern** as well as colour, plus a text legend in CMP-199 ChartLegend naming all four in words.
- A bar with no OI sample renders neutral-hatched and is excluded from classification; the legend states how many bars in view are unclassified.
- Crosshair readout showing the bar's delta and its quadrant name in text.
- Table alternative gains delta and quadrant columns.
- Analytics: `oi_panel.metric_toggled` with the new mode.

## Out of scope
Computing the delta or the quadrant (E24-T04); alerts on quadrant transitions (E40); funding and liquidation panes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Quadrant classification renders
  Given price and OI both rose on a bar
  Then the bar is drawn in the long_buildup style with its distinct pattern, and the legend names long_buildup in words

Scenario: All four quadrants
  Given bars covering price-up/OI-up, price-up/OI-down, price-down/OI-up and price-down/OI-down
  Then they render as long_buildup, short_covering, short_buildup and long_unwind, each visually distinct in greyscale

Scenario: Absolute versus delta
  When I switch to delta-per-bar
  Then the pane shows the change rather than the level, and the preference survives a reload and a new session

Scenario: Missing OI for a bar
  Given no OI sample exists for a bar
  Then it is drawn neutral-hatched, is excluded from classification, and the legend reports the count of unclassified bars in view

Scenario: Colour is never the only encoding
  When the pane is viewed in greyscale or with a colour-vision-deficiency simulation
  Then every quadrant remains distinguishable by pattern and the legend text

Scenario: Crosshair readout
  When I place the crosshair on a classified bar
  Then the readout shows the delta with its unit and the quadrant name as text
```

## Technical notes / design
The component receives `open_interest_delta` and `oi_price_quadrant` series and maps quadrant enum values to style tokens through a single lookup table taken from the E24-D03 spec - no conditional colour logic scattered through the renderer. `None` is a first-class value in that lookup, mapping to the neutral hatch. Setting writes go through the existing settings API and emit the standard `settings.change` audit entry.

## Test plan
Unit: enum-to-style mapping incl. None; unclassified-bar counting; settings persistence and restore. Component/Storybook: all four quadrants, mixed window, all-unclassified window, delta vs absolute. Visual regression on the four styles in greyscale. E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
No new surface. The integrity rule is that the client must not infer a quadrant when the engine returned None - E24-Q01 includes a negative test for exactly that.

## Accessibility notes
Quadrants are conveyed by pattern + text legend, never colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1); the toggle is a labelled control with a visible focus ring; the table alternative gains quadrant names as text; the unclassified count is announced politely when it changes materially, not on every frame.

## Performance notes
Delta mode adds no per-frame computation - the series is precomputed server-side. Pattern fills must use the engine's existing instanced-geometry path so 1 500 bars do not cost 1 500 draw calls; measure and record the frame time against budget #1.

## Observability
Analytics `oi_panel.metric_toggled` with `{mode, quadrant_colouring}`; a counter of unclassified bars rendered, so a systematic OI gap shows up in telemetry as well as on screen.

- [ ] Code merged to `main` behind review (2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner), conventional commits, PR <=400 LOC diff.

title: Funding rate, stepped history and second-accurate settlement countdown
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-003 - Funding rate, history and countdown (Must)**. Its NFR is exacting: "countdown accurate to the second using the synced clock offset", and scenario 3 demands the funding interval be read from instrument metadata and used everywhere, including session anchors. The countdown appears twice - in the symbol header and in the SCR-054 funding sub-pane - and both must be the same component instance's output, not two timers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Funding sub-pane in CMP-186: settled funding history over the chart's time range, rendered as a stepped line or bars (`deriv.funding.style`, persisted per user), on the shared time axis.
- CMP-126 FundingCountdown in the symbol header and in the sub-pane, driven by `time_to_funding_ms` from the engine plus the synced clock offset (E17's clock sync), ticking to the second.
- Imminent-settlement warning at <5 min using the E24-D05 copy, including the estimated charge line where a position exists ("Funding settles in 04:12 - position will be charged ~12.40 USDT"); with no position the charge line is omitted rather than showing zero.
- Interval correctness: the symbol's `funding_interval_minutes` is displayed and used for the history step width and the countdown target; a 4 h symbol renders six settlements a day.
- States: history loading, no settled history yet, source failure with retry and `last_success_at`, stale shading.
- Table alternative for the funding history with settlement timestamps, rates and units.
- Analytics: `funding.countdown_alert_set`.

## Out of scope
Predicted and annualised display (E24-S04); the funding service and interval resolution (E24-T02); funding cost accounting against realised positions (E41 Journal); alerts on funding thresholds (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Current rate and countdown
  Given BTCUSDT is subscribed
  Then the current funding rate and the time to next settlement render in the symbol header and in the funding sub-pane, both showing the same value

Scenario: Second accuracy under clock skew
  Given the local clock is 3 seconds ahead of the exchange
  Then the countdown uses the synced clock offset and reaches zero within one second of the true settlement time

Scenario: History uses the instrument's interval
  Given a symbol whose funding interval is 4 hours
  Then the stepped history shows six settlements per day and the interval is stated in the pane, with no 8-hour assumption anywhere

Scenario: Imminent settlement
  Given less than 5 minutes remain
  Then the warning state renders with the copy from the handoff pack, and the estimated charge line appears only when a position exists

Scenario: Source failure
  Given the funding history request fails
  Then the pane shows a retry state with the last successful timestamp rather than a blank chart, and the countdown keeps running from the last known next-settlement time

Scenario: Settlement rollover
  When the countdown reaches zero
  Then the pane requests the newly settled rate, appends it to the history, and restarts the countdown for the next interval without a manual refresh

Scenario: Announcement policy
  When a screen reader is active
  Then the countdown is announced at 5 minutes and at 1 minute remaining only, never every second
```

## Technical notes / design
One countdown source of truth: a single store entry derived from `time_to_funding_ms` and the clock offset; the header and the pane both subscribe to it, so they cannot drift. The tick is driven by a single interval timer shared across all countdowns, not one timer per instance. Step width for the history comes from `funding_interval_minutes` in the `/market/funding` response - never from the spacing between observed points, which would silently break on a missing settlement.

## Test plan
Unit: countdown arithmetic against a skewed offset; rollover at zero; step-width derivation; imminent-threshold transitions; retry-state rendering. Component/Storybook: CMP-126 Positive, Negative, UnderOneMinute; CMP-186 FundingOnly with 8 h and 4 h symbols. Integration: a fixture crossing a settlement boundary. E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
A wrong countdown or a wrong interval misleads a user about a real cost, so this is an integrity-relevant surface even though it holds no secrets. The interval must come from instrument metadata; the CI guard from E24-T02 prevents a re-introduced constant.

## Accessibility notes
Countdown announced at 5 min and 1 min only (SCR-054 catalogue entry); the countdown's accessible name states what it counts down to; rate sign is conveyed by text and the CMP-020 NumericText contract, not by colour alone; table alternative for the history; visible focus on the style toggle.

## Performance notes
The countdown re-renders only its own text node once per second; the funding series redraws on change only (<=1 Hz data). Shared timer keeps per-frame cost near zero. Measure against the SCR-054 2 ms/frame budget.

## Observability
Analytics `funding.countdown_alert_set`; a client error event on funding fetch failure; a warning when the clock offset exceeds a threshold, since that directly degrades countdown accuracy.

title: Predicted and annualised funding with explicit non-settled styling
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-004 - Predicted and annualised funding (Should)** whose NFR is a hard rule: "never present predicted values styled as settled". The annualised figure is what traders actually compare across symbols, and it is only meaningful when computed with the symbol's own interval - which is why the tooltip must show the formula with the actual factor in it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Annualisation toggle (`deriv.funding.annualised`, persisted per user) switching the displayed rate and the history series between the per-interval rate and `funding_annualized` from the engine.
- Tooltip showing the formula with the symbol's real numbers: `rate x (525600 / {funding_interval_minutes}) = {annualised}`.
- Predicted (unsettled) rate rendered in the distinct style specified by E24-D03 - distinguishable in greyscale - with a text label "predicted" and a CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linking SCR-058.
- When no predicted rate is published, the field shows "n/a" (never a stale or carried-forward value), and the history shows no phantom point.
- Table alternative gains an annualised column and a settled/predicted column as text.

## Out of scope
The funding service and the predicted flag itself (E24-T02); the countdown (E24-S03); cross-symbol funding comparison screens.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Annualised toggle
  When I enable annualisation
  Then rates display annualised using the symbol's own funding interval, and the tooltip shows the formula with that interval substituted

Scenario: Annualisation is interval-correct
  Given a symbol funding every 4 hours with a rate of 0.0001
  Then the annualised value uses the factor 525600/240 and not 525600/480

Scenario: Predicted is visually and textually distinct
  Then the predicted next rate is rendered in a style distinguishable in greyscale, carries the word predicted in text, and shows an (estimated) badge linking the methodology drawer

Scenario: Predicted unavailable
  Given no predicted rate is published for the symbol
  Then the field shows n/a, no point is added to the history, and no previously seen predicted value is reused

Scenario: Toggle persistence
  When I reload the app
  Then the annualisation preference is restored, and the tooltip still shows the correct formula for the current symbol

Scenario: Screen reader
  When the predicted value is read out
  Then its accessible name contains both predicted and estimated as words
```

## Technical notes / design
Both the rate and the annualised value come from the engine's descriptors (`funding_rate`, `funding_annualized`); the client never multiplies. The tooltip formula is rendered from the same `funding_interval_minutes` the value was computed with, sourced from the API response rather than a separate lookup, so a mismatch is impossible. The predicted item is identified by the `predicted` flag in the payload - never by 'it is the last item'.

## Test plan
Unit: formula-string construction across intervals; n/a path; style selection driven by the `predicted` flag; persistence. Component/Storybook: settled-only, settled+predicted, predicted-absent. Negative test: a payload whose predicted flag is stripped must not render as settled (shared with E24-X02's abuse case). E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This is the misrepresentation control surface for funding: the `predicted`/`estimated` flags drive the rendering, and the component fails closed if they are absent. Covered by E24-X01 threat (T) and tested in E24-X02.

## Accessibility notes
The distinction between settled and predicted must not rely on colour or opacity; CMP-227's accessible name contains the literal word "estimated"; the badge is focusable and opens SCR-058 with Enter; the annualised column in the table alternative carries its unit.

## Performance notes
Negligible - a toggle and a formatting change; no additional subscriptions or recomputation.

## Observability
Analytics event when annualisation is toggled; a counter for renders of the n/a state so a persistently missing predicted rate is visible.

title: Liquidation feed with burst coalescing and recorder-bounded history disclosure
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-005 - Liquidation feed (Must)**: each event shows side, size, price and time, the pane states that no historical liquidation endpoint exists, and a cascade of hundreds of events per second coalesces per frame with a burst rate shown. The honesty requirement here is structural: an empty feed must never be readable as "no liquidations happened" when it actually means "we were not recording".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Liquidation feed surface on SCR-054: a virtualised list of prints with side (as text, not only colour), size, price, notional and time, fed by `liquidations.{symbol}` (`LiquidationBatch`) with `min_notional_usd` as a subscription option.
- Backfill of the visible window from `GET /api/v1/market/liquidations`, reading local recorder data only.
- Burst handling: prints are coalesced into 250 ms buckets with a visible burst-rate counter ("1 240 prints/s"), never one DOM node per print; the pane states that Bybit batches at most one push per symbol per 500 ms so counts are lower bounds.
- Partial-history state: an explicit chip naming the first available timestamp and stating that no exchange history endpoint exists for liquidations, from the E24-D05 copy deck; shown whenever the requested window starts before the recorder's coverage.
- CMP-127 LiquidationMarker on the chart for prints above the threshold, with the DOM-mirror pattern for accessibility.
- Click-through: `liquidation.print_clicked` analytics and crosshair sync to the print's timestamp.
- Table alternative: the feed itself is a table with headers and units, so the accessible alternative is the primary structure rather than a bolt-on.

## Out of scope
Per-bar bucketing into bars (E24-S06); estimated zones (E24-S07); the socket, persistence and endpoint (E24-T03); liquidation alerts (E40); the user's own position liquidation line (E31/E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Feed renders prints
  Given the liquidations topic is subscribed for BTCUSDT
  Then each event shows side, size, price, notional and time, with side stated in text

Scenario: No REST history is disclosed
  Then the pane states that no historical liquidation endpoint exists and that history is limited to the recorder's runtime

Scenario: Partial history chip
  Given the recorder for BTCUSDT started 2 hours ago and I request a 24-hour window
  Then a chip names the first available timestamp and the feed shows only the recorded window

Scenario: Empty is never mistaken for zero
  Given the requested window is entirely outside the recorder's coverage
  Then the pane shows the no-coverage state explaining why it is empty, and does not display an empty list that would read as no liquidations

Scenario: Cascade
  Given hundreds of events per second during a cascade
  Then prints are coalesced into 250 ms buckets, a burst-rate counter is displayed, no frames are dropped, and the DOM node count stays bounded

Scenario: Threshold filter
  Given min_notional_usd is set
  Then smaller prints are excluded server-side via the subscription option and the active filter is stated in the pane

Scenario: Announcements under load
  When a screen reader is active during a cascade
  Then at most one summary announcement every 5 seconds naming the burst rate is made, not one per print
```

## Technical notes / design
The list is virtualised with a fixed-size ring buffer of recent prints; the coalescing buffer flushes on the animation frame following the 250 ms window, so render work is decoupled from arrival rate. `min_notional_usd` is applied as a subscription option so filtering happens server-side and the wire is not saturated during a cascade. The partial-history condition compares the requested window against the coverage metadata returned by E24-T03 - it is never inferred from 'the oldest row we happened to receive'.

## Test plan
Unit: coalescing buffer (bucket boundaries, burst-rate computation), ring-buffer eviction, partial-history condition, filter-state rendering. Component/Storybook: CMP-186 LiquidationBars/feed states - populated, cascade, partial, no-coverage, filtered. Perf: 500 prints/s for 10 s with scripting <2 ms/frame (full script in E24-Q03). E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
(D) client-side cascade amplification - mitigated by coalescing and the bounded buffer; (T) an empty feed misread as zero liquidations - mitigated by the no-coverage state, tested as an abuse case in E24-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Feed is a real table with headers and units; side is text; burst announcements are throttled to one per 5 s per E24-D04's policy; CMP-127 markers use the DOM-mirror pattern so sparse events are reachable by keyboard; visible focus on rows; contrast >=4.5:1.

## Performance notes
SCR-054 budget: <=2 ms scripting per frame during a cascade of 500 prints/s sustained for 10 s with no dropped frames; DOM nodes bounded regardless of print rate; WS tick -> screen p95 <100 ms (budget #3, hard R2 gate).

## Observability
Analytics `liquidation.print_clicked`; client metrics for coalesced-bucket count and observed burst rate; an error event when the backfill request fails.

title: Per-bar liquidation bars split long/short with threshold and history boundary
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-006 - Liquidation bars (Must)**: per-bar long and short liquidation notional as a split histogram, with a minimum-notional filter stated in the legend and an explicit boundary marker where the recorder's history begins. The NFR - "bucketing aligns to the chart interval and the day boundary" - is satisfied by the engine's `liquidation_notional` descriptor (E24-T04); this story renders it honestly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Split histogram in the liquidation sub-pane: long and short notional per bar, drawn from `liquidation_notional` with `side=long|short`, aligned to the chart's bar grid and the shared time axis.
- Side labelling in text on the axis/legend, so long versus short is never colour-only.
- Minimum-notional filter (`deriv.liq.min_notional_usd`, persisted per user) applied server-side; the active threshold is stated in CMP-199 ChartLegend (US-DERIV-006 scenario 2).
- Bars/heatmap mode selector (`deriv.liq.mode`) with bars as the default; the heatmap variant is the realised-liquidation density from recorded prints (exact), not the estimated zone overlay of E24-S07.
- History boundary marker: a vertical boundary at the recorder's first available timestamp with a label, so the absence of bars before it is explained on the chart itself (US-DERIV-006 scenario 3).
- Crosshair readout of a bar's long and short notional with units.
- Table alternative gains per-bar long/short columns.

## Out of scope
The estimated liquidation-zone overlay (E24-S07); the print feed (E24-S05); bucketing computation (E24-T04); alerts.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Split histogram
  Then per-bar long and short liquidation notional render as a split histogram with both sides labelled in text

Scenario: Bucketing alignment
  Given a 1h chart spanning a UTC day boundary
  Then buckets align to the bar grid and to the day boundary, with no print counted twice or dropped

Scenario: Threshold filter
  When I set a minimum notional
  Then smaller events are excluded and the active filter is stated in the legend

Scenario: Empty history boundary
  Given the recorder started 2 hours ago
  Then bars exist only for that window and an explicit boundary marker labels the first available timestamp

Scenario: Zero versus unknown
  Given a bar inside the recorded window with no liquidations
  Then it renders as a genuine zero, visually distinct from bars before the recording boundary which render as unknown

Scenario: Mode switch
  When I switch between bars and the realised-density heatmap
  Then the same underlying recorded data is shown, the mode persists, and neither mode is labelled estimated
```

## Technical notes / design
Series come from `/market/metrics` with `metric=liquidation_notional` and `params={"side":"long"}` / `"short"`, on the chart's bar type and parameter, so the bar grid is guaranteed identical to price. The boundary marker position comes from the coverage metadata (E24-T03), not from the first non-empty bucket. Zero and unknown are separate states in the data model and must remain separate in the renderer - this is the story's main correctness trap.

## Test plan
Unit: zero-versus-unknown rendering decision; legend threshold text; boundary-marker placement from coverage metadata; mode persistence. Component/Storybook: populated, filtered, boundary-in-view, all-unknown, cascade bar. Integration: fixture spanning a day boundary. E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
(T) presenting 'no recorded data' as 'no liquidations' - mitigated by the zero/unknown distinction and the boundary marker, both tested by E24-X02 and E24-Q01.

## Accessibility notes
Sides labelled in text; the boundary marker has a text label readable by a screen reader; the table alternative distinguishes zero from unknown with words, not blanks; contrast >=3:1 for the bar fills against the pane background.

## Performance notes
Bars are a static series per view; redraws only on new bars or a threshold change. Frame time p95 <=16.6 ms with the full scene (budget #1); the histogram must use the engine's instanced path.

## Observability
Analytics on threshold and mode changes; a counter of renders showing the boundary marker, which indicates how often users look past their recording depth.

- [ ] Unit tests added; coverage >=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend on touched files.

title: Estimated liquidation zones: off by default, acknowledged, badged and disclosed
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-007 - Liquidation heat / cluster estimate (Should)**, the epic's most dangerous feature. Its NFR is absolute: "never presented as exchange-provided data; excluded from any automated rule action by default". The screens catalogue makes a missing `(estimated)` badge a P1 bug, not a cosmetic one. E24-K01 decides the method and may recommend descoping the overlay entirely - this story implements whatever K01 concluded, including the descope path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Zone overlay on the price pane rendering the bands produced by the method chosen in E24-K01, from a descriptor registered as `estimated: true`.
- **Off by default** (`deriv.liq.zones_enabled` default `false`). Enabling requires an acknowledgement dialog stating the value is an estimate derived from aggregate OI and assumed leverage tiers, not exchange data; the acknowledgement is recorded as an audit event.
- CMP-227 EstimatedBadge on every zone and in the pane legend, focusable, opening SCR-058's liquidation-cluster section by Enter or click.
- SCR-058 content wired: the method, its inputs (and which are assumed rather than published), the thresholds in force, the known failure modes, and the sentence "this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact".
- Explicit exclusion from automated actions: the descriptor is flagged so the rule engine will not accept it as a condition input by default, and the UI states this where zones are configured.
- Descope path: if E24-K01 concluded no method is defensible, this story ships the realised-liquidation density only (already exact, from E24-S06), records the descoping on the epic, and removes the toggle rather than shipping a disabled stub.

## Out of scope
The estimation method itself (E24-K01 decides it; E24-T04 hosts the computation); the exact `cluster_window_ms` grouping, which is not an estimate (E24-T03); rule-engine integration (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Disabled by default
  Given a fresh installation
  Then liquidation zones are off, and no zone geometry is requested or rendered

Scenario: Enabling requires acknowledgement
  When I enable zones
  Then a dialog states that the values are estimated and not exchange-provided, enabling only proceeds after explicit acknowledgement, and the acknowledgement is written to the audit log

Scenario: Badge on every zone
  Given zones are enabled
  Then every zone and the pane legend carry an (estimated) badge whose accessible name contains the word estimated, and each badge opens the methodology drawer

Scenario: Methodology disclosure
  When I open the methodology drawer from a zone badge
  Then it describes the method, its inputs, which inputs are assumed rather than exchange-published, the thresholds in force and the known failure modes

Scenario: Missing badge is a P1
  Given a build in which a zone renders without its badge
  Then the automated catalogue-level badge test fails and the build is rejected

Scenario: Not available to automated actions
  When a rule condition attempts to use the zone metric
  Then it is rejected by default with an explanation, and no rule can act on an estimated zone without an explicit override

Scenario: Method descoped
  Given E24-K01 concluded no method is defensible
  Then the overlay is not shipped, the toggle is absent rather than disabled, the realised-liquidation density remains available, and the descoping is recorded on the epic
```

## Technical notes / design
The overlay reads a single `estimated: true` descriptor; the badge is rendered from that flag, not from a hard-coded prop, so a future non-estimated series would not silently inherit the badge and an estimated one cannot lose it. The acknowledgement is persisted per user in `settings` and emits a `settings.change` audit entry with the acknowledged text version, so we can prove what the user agreed to if the copy later changes. Zone geometry is recomputed only on the cadence E24-K01 measured, never per frame.

## Test plan
Unit: default-off behaviour; acknowledgement gate; badge presence bound to the descriptor flag; rule-engine rejection path. Catalogue-level test (CMP-227's own contract): every surface rendering an estimated series renders the badge. Component/Storybook: zones off, acknowledgement dialog, zones on with badges, descoped build. Negative: flag stripped from the payload must not yield an unbadged zone (shared with E24-X02). E2E in E24-Q02. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This is the epic's principal misrepresentation control (E24-X01 threat (T)). Controls: default-off, an acknowledgement with an audit trail, a schema-level estimated flag driving the badge, mandatory methodology disclosure, and exclusion from automated actions. Reviewed and abuse-tested in E24-X02; a missing badge is treated as a security finding, not a UI defect.

## Accessibility notes
CMP-227 is focusable, its accessible name contains the literal word "estimated", and it opens SCR-058 by Enter; zones are distinguishable without colour (pattern + labelled legend); the acknowledgement dialog is a focus-trapped, keyboard-operable dialog; the overlay never obscures price data below the contrast floor.

## Performance notes
Zone geometry is recomputed at the cadence measured in E24-K01 and drawn as a small number of instanced bands; the overlay must add <1 ms per frame and must not increase the SCR-054 total beyond its 2 ms/frame budget. Record the measured cost.

## Observability
Audit event for the acknowledgement; analytics `methodology.opened` with `{detector}` when SCR-058 is opened from a zone badge; metrics for zone recompute duration and zone count.

title: Basis, mark/index readout and long/short ratio with retry state
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DERIV-008 - Basis, mark/index and long/short ratio (Should)**. Its NFR governs the whole epic: "all derivative series respect the same time axis and crosshair sync as price", and scenario 3 fixes the failure behaviour: a failed source shows a retry state with the last successful timestamp, never a blank chart.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Basis readout and series: mark, index and their spread from the engine's `basis` and `premium_pct` descriptors, with the `source=last|mark` selector (`deriv.basis.source`) and an annualised-basis toggle (`deriv.basis.annualised`), all persisted per user.
- Rendering on the shared time axis with crosshair sync, as a peer sub-pane or a header readout per the E24-D05 decision; values via CMP-036 KeyValueRow with units.
- Global long/short account ratio rendered at its native period with the period stated in words (e.g. "5 min, exchange-published"); if the platform's adapter cannot supply it for USDT perps, the surface states the source is unavailable rather than showing a fabricated series, and the limitation is recorded in E24-T05.
- Retry state: when a source fails, show the last successful timestamp and a retry action; never a blank chart (US-DERIV-008 scenario 3).
- Table alternative covering mark, index, basis, premium and the ratio with units and periods.
- Crosshair readout of basis and premium at the hovered bar.

## Out of scope
Computing basis/premium (E24-T04); OI, funding and liquidation panes; options/GEX (out of scope for the product); funding-cost accounting (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Basis pane
  Then mark, index and their spread render together, with an annualised basis toggle and units on every figure

Scenario: Source selector
  When I switch the basis source from last to mark
  Then the series and the readout recompute server-side, the selection persists, and the active source is stated in the pane

Scenario: Long/short ratio
  Then the global account ratio renders at its native period with the period stated in words

Scenario: Source unavailable
  Given the ratio source fails
  Then the pane shows a retry state with the last successful timestamp, not a blank chart

Scenario: Ratio not published
  Given the exchange publishes no long/short ratio for this instrument
  Then the surface states that the source is unavailable rather than rendering an empty or fabricated series

Scenario: Axis and crosshair sync
  When I pan, zoom or move the crosshair on the price pane
  Then the basis series follows the same time axis and the crosshair readout updates in lockstep with price

Scenario: No client-side computation
  Then basis, premium and the annualised basis all originate from the engine, and the client performs no arithmetic beyond formatting
```

## Technical notes / design
Basis and premium are read from `/market/metrics` with the `source` param, and live values from the `ticker.{symbol}` `mark_price`/`index_price` fields; the two paths must agree, which the golden-fixture harness (E24-T06) checks. The pane registers with the chart engine's shared time scale so sync is structural rather than event-forwarded. The retry state stores `last_success_at` in the view model so it survives re-renders.

## Test plan
Unit: source-selector state and persistence; retry-state rendering and last-success tracking; unavailable-source path; formatting with units. Component/Storybook: populated, source=mark, annualised, retry, unavailable. Integration: fixture where the ratio source 5xxs. E2E in E24-Q02, including a pan/zoom sync assertion. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
(T) an unavailable source must not be rendered as zero or as a flat line - both would be fabricated data; the unavailable and retry states are the mitigation and are covered by E24-X02's abuse cases.

## Accessibility notes
Every figure carries its unit in the accessible name; the period of the ratio is stated in words; the retry action is a labelled button with visible focus; the table alternative includes all five values; sign of basis is conveyed by text as well as colour.

## Performance notes
Low-frequency data (<=1 Hz); render on change only. The pane must not add a second time-scale computation - it reuses the shared scale, keeping frame time inside budget #1.

## Observability
Analytics on source and annualisation toggles; a client error event with the status on source failure; a counter of retry-state renders.

title: ADR-0017 derivatives provenance and plan-doc reconciliation for E24
body:
## Context
Two decisions in this epic are durable and will be questioned later: (1) derivatives values are computed once in M9 and never recomputed client-side, with every value carrying its provenance (`source`, `predicted`, `estimated`); (2) liquidation history is recorder-bounded by design because no exchange history endpoint exists, so partial history is a designed state rather than a defect. Both belong in an ADR (`docs/plan/27-adrs/`, allocated as ADR-0017, after ADR-0016 taken by the R2 rendering-strategy ADRs). The epic DoD also requires the plan docs to describe shipped behaviour, not the proposal.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Write **ADR-0017** (title: derivatives metric provenance and recorder-bounded liquidation history) in the standard template: context, decision, consequences, alternatives considered and rejected (client-side computation; synthesising liquidation history from trade prints; assuming an 8 h funding interval), status Accepted.
- Record the E24-K01 outcome in the ADR: which liquidation-zone method shipped, or that the estimated overlay was descoped.
- Reconcile the plan docs with what shipped: `22-api-openapi.yaml` (any field added to the three endpoints, e.g. the coverage/source metadata), `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.8/§14.9, `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 descriptor table, `21-database-schema.md` §4.7 if a column or dedup key changed, `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-054 states and SCR-058's liquidation-cluster section, `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-186/126/127 props, `18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.14 rows.
- Cross-link the ADR from the SCR-054 catalogue entry and from the epic.

## Out of scope
New behaviour; documentation of other epics' decisions; user-facing help content.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: ADR merged
  Then ADR-0017 exists in docs/plan/27-adrs/ with status Accepted, listing the rejected alternatives and their reasons

Scenario: Docs match the build
  When each plan document listed in scope is diffed against the shipped API, WS payloads, schema and screens
  Then no divergence remains undocumented, and each change is a reviewed edit rather than a silent rewrite

Scenario: Spike outcome recorded
  Then the ADR states which liquidation-zone method shipped and its parameters, or records the descoping decision with the evidence from E24-K01

Scenario: Traceability closed
  Then 18-traceability-matrix.md section 2.14 reflects the shipped screens, components and endpoints for all eight DERIV stories

Scenario: A divergence is found late
  Given a behaviour differs from the documented contract and was not caught in review
  Then either the code or the doc is corrected inside this ticket, and the choice is recorded - the divergence is never left standing
```

## Technical notes / design
Documentation only; no runtime change. The OpenAPI edits must keep the spectral/lint rules green (the file declares its own ruleset) and the contract tests must still pass after the edit, which is the check that the doc now matches the code.

## Test plan
CI: OpenAPI lint + contract tests; WS schema tests; markdown link check. Reviewer walks one endpoint and one WS payload end to end against the docs.

## Security notes
The provenance decision recorded here is a security control (integrity/misrepresentation), so the Security engineer reviews the ADR alongside the Architect.

## Accessibility notes
N/A

## Performance notes
N/A

## Observability
The ADR names the observability signals that make provenance auditable (`deriv_oi_rows_written_total{source}`, `deriv_engine_none_bars_total`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ADR merged with status Accepted and Architect + Security review.
- [ ] All listed plan docs updated; contract and schema tests green after the edits.
- [ ] E24-K01 outcome recorded.
- [ ] Traceability matrix §2.14 reconciled.
- [ ] ADR linked from SCR-054 and from the epic.

## Dependencies
`E24-S08` (last functional surface) and `E24-Q05` (so QA findings are reflected). Closes part of the epic DoD.

## Branch
`docs/e24-adr-derivatives`.

title: Security review and abuse-case testing of the derivatives surfaces
body:
## Context
Closes the STRIDE model against the built system: every mitigation claimed in E24-X01 is exercised on a running build, and the misrepresentation abuse cases are tested rather than reasoned about.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Verify the DoS mitigations: `from`/`to` range caps, `limit` caps and cursor enforcement on `/market/open-interest`, `/market/funding` and `/market/liquidations`; the `symbols` cap (<=40) on the `ticker` and `liquidations` multi-symbol topics; behaviour under a cascade with many subscribed clients.
- Verify authorisation: all four endpoints reject an unauthenticated request and a token lacking `marketdata:read` with 401/403, and the WS subscribe path enforces the same permission per `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.
- Abuse cases from E24-X01: strip the `estimated`/`predicted` flag at each hop and prove the UI fails closed (renders the badge or refuses to render the value) rather than silently showing an unlabelled number; request an OI range that mixes `rest` and `ws_ticker` sources and prove the response discloses the source per point; request a liquidation range older than the recorder's first record and prove the response reports the true coverage window rather than an empty success.
- Input fuzzing of the query parameters (negative limits, inverted ranges, huge `cluster_window_ms`, non-enum `side`, unknown `metric` values) expecting 400/422 with the standard error envelope and no stack trace.
- Semgrep/Bandit rule check over the new backend modules and a dependency review of anything added.

## Out of scope
Full DAST sweep and pen-test (pre-R4, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`); other epics' surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Range and page caps hold
  When a request asks for a range or limit beyond the documented cap on any of the three history endpoints
  Then it is rejected with 400 or 422 and the standard error envelope, and no unbounded query reaches QuestDB

Scenario: Permissions enforced
  When an unauthenticated client calls any derivatives endpoint or subscribes ticker.BTCUSDT or liquidations.BTCUSDT
  Then it receives 401, and a token without marketdata:read receives 403 with an audit entry

Scenario: Flag stripping fails closed
  Given a crafted response in which estimated is removed from a predicted funding point or a zone band
  When the panel renders it
  Then the value is either suppressed or rendered with the (estimated) badge, and never rendered as a settled exchange value

Scenario: Coverage is honest under abuse
  Given a liquidation query for a window entirely before the recorder's first record
  Then the response reports the true coverage window and the UI shows the partial-history state, not an empty chart implying zero liquidations

Scenario: Fuzzed input
  When malformed query parameters are submitted
  Then every case returns a 4xx with the standard envelope, no 5xx, and no stack trace or internal path in the body
```

## Technical notes / design
Automate the cases as pytest security tests under `tests/security/e24/` so they run in CI, plus a scripted ZAP active scan limited to the four endpoints. Flag-stripping is tested at the component level with a crafted payload fixture, since the failure mode lives in the frontend.

## Test plan
The tests above are the deliverable; a findings report with severities and fix tickets accompanies them. Regressions are prevented by keeping the suite in CI.

## Security notes
This is the security ticket; exit is the Security engineer's sign-off and a triaged findings list with no open high/critical.

## Accessibility notes
The badge-presence assertion overlaps the a11y audit (E24-Q04); both must pass independently since one checks provenance and the other checks the accessible name.

## Performance notes
The cap tests double as a guard on budget #13: a capped query must still return inside p95 <150 ms backend-internal.

## Observability
Confirms the security signals from E24-X01 are actually emitted: rejected oversized requests, subscription-cap rejections, schema-validation failures.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All abuse cases automated and green in CI.
- [ ] ZAP scan run against the four endpoints with findings triaged.
- [ ] SAST (Semgrep/Bandit) clean on the new modules.
- [ ] Findings report with severities; no open high/critical.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment recorded on the epic.

## Dependencies
`E24-X01` (the model), `E24-S07`/`E24-S08` (last surfaces built). Feeds the epic DoD.

## Branch
`chore/e24-security-review`.

## References

title: Design QA sweep of the built detector surfaces against the specs
body:
## Context
R2's design quality gate requires a "design-QA sweep" on the new views. This ticket compares the built SCR-055..059 and the chart detector markers against the D03/D04/D06/D07 specifications, in both themes, at all densities, and files the discrepancies.

Because the epic's honesty requirement is enforced visually, this sweep also performs the **badge audit**: every surface that renders a heuristic value must show the `(estimated)` badge, and every badge must open SCR-058 at the correct section. R2 exit criterion #4 makes a miss here a P1 bug.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screen-by-screen visual comparison against the signed-off frames: spacing, type, tokens, states, empty/stale/disconnected/warming-up/insufficient-data treatments, focus appearance.
- Both themes; every supported density; the window sizes the workspace supports.
- Badge audit across the whole app surface touched by this epic (SCR-055 book speed, SCR-056 stacks, SCR-057 regime, SCR-059 sections, chart markers from E25-S06, and the DOM ladder's detector chips rendered by E21 from the same events): badge present, correct detector id, drawer opens at the right section.
- Motion and reduced-motion verification.
- Copy verification against the D07 copy deck, including validation messages and the armed-rule warning wording.
- Findings filed as bugs with severity, screenshots and the frame reference; blocking items fixed before the epic closes.
- Design sign-off statement on the built product.

## Out of scope
Functional testing (E25-Q01/Q02), accessibility audit (E25-Q04), performance (E25-Q03), redesign - findings are discrepancies against the spec, not new design opinions.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state verified
  Then each documented state of each of the five screens has been observed in the built product and compared with its frame

Scenario: Badge audit passes
  Given every surface that renders a heuristic value
  Then it shows the (estimated) badge, and activating it opens SCR-058 at that detector's section
  And any miss is filed as a P1

Scenario: Both themes and all densities
  Then no visual discrepancy remains unfiled in either theme at any supported density

Scenario: Copy matches
  Then all chrome, empty-state, validation and warning copy matches the signed-off copy deck exactly

Scenario: Blocking findings fixed
  Then every finding of blocking severity is fixed and re-verified before the epic is closed
```

## Technical notes / design
Run the sweep against a recorded-replay fixture so stale, disconnected, warming-up and insufficient-data states can actually be produced on demand rather than waited for. Ask the QA engineer (E25-Q02) for the fixtures they built rather than creating a second set.

## Test plan
The sweep itself is the test. Findings are filed in the tracker with `design-qa` and re-verified after fixes.

## Security notes
Verify the armed-rule warning appears in the built SCR-059 and that "applied" never shows before backend confirmation - both are visible manifestations of controls from E25-X01, and their absence is a security finding, not merely a visual one.

## Accessibility notes
Verify focus appearance and focus order match the D06 specification; the full audit is E25-Q04, and findings are shared between the two tickets rather than duplicated.

## Performance notes
Note any visual treatment that appears to cost frames (panel jank at 4 Hz, animation on every update) and hand it to E25-Q03 for measurement rather than judging by eye.

## Observability
Confirm the analytics events named in the handoff actually fire from the built UI.

## Definition of Done
All five screens plus the chart markers swept in both themes at all densities; badge audit complete with zero unfiled misses; findings filed and blocking items fixed and re-verified; design sign-off on the built product recorded; sweep report linked from the epic.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` all six E25 stories. Feeds E25-Q05 sign-off.

## Branch
`design/detectors-design-qa` (report only; fixes go on the owning story's branch). PR size guidance: report.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).

title: Add Playwright E2E coverage for the detector surfaces and flows
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E (Playwright, web and Electron) above the integration layer in the pyramid, reserved for the flows whose breakage would be most costly. For E25 those are: the estimated-badge-to-methodology flow (an R2 exit criterion), the detector-settings apply flow (a security-relevant path), and the imbalance-row-to-chart navigation (the panel's entire purpose).

Tests run against a **recorded fixture replayed through the normal pipeline**, not against live Bybit, so they are deterministic and can produce stale, disconnected and warming-up states on demand.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under the existing E2E suite, tagged `@e25`, running in both the web and Electron targets per the testing strategy.
- Flow 1 - **estimated affordance**: from SCR-055's book-speed badge, SCR-057's regime badge and a chart detector marker, activating the badge opens SCR-058 scrolled and focused at the correct section; the section shows the thresholds currently in force; the link to SCR-059 works.
- Flow 2 - **settings apply**: open SCR-059, enter an out-of-range value and see the range-naming validation; enter a valid value; see the armed-rule warning when a dependent armed rule exists; apply; observe the applying-then-applied sequence (never applied first); verify the change is reflected in SCR-058's thresholds-in-force and in an audit entry.
- Flow 3 - **imbalance navigation**: a stack appears in SCR-056 within the fixture; selecting the row by mouse and by keyboard jumps and highlights the chart zone; the empty state appears when thresholds are raised beyond the fixture's stacks.
- Flow 4 - **degraded states**: WS disconnect mid-fixture leaves panels showing stale/disconnected rather than stale values presented as live; resync restores updates without duplicating rows.
- Flow 5 - **regime transition**: a transition in the fixture updates the badge and the history strip, and `/market/regime/explain` content matches the badge.
- Flow 6 - **honesty sweep (automated part of the Q01 checklist)**: a test that walks every surface listed in the checklist table and asserts a badge with the expected detector id is present.
- Fixture management: reuse the recorded windows produced for E25-T03/T04 golden fixtures rather than creating a parallel set.
- CI wiring, deflake budget, and documentation of how to run the suite locally.

## Out of scope
Unit and component tests (owned by the stories), performance and determinism measurement (E25-Q03), the a11y audit (E25-Q04), backend contract tests (owned by T01/T02/T05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Suite runs deterministically
  Given the recorded fixture is replayed through the normal pipeline
  Then the E2E suite passes on ten consecutive CI runs with no flakes
  And it does not contact the live exchange

Scenario: Estimated flow
  Then activating an estimated badge on the tape panel, the regime panel and a chart marker each opens the methodology drawer at the correct section with focus moved to that section

Scenario: Settings apply
  Then an out-of-range value is rejected with a message naming the range
  And a valid change shows the armed-rule warning where a dependent armed rule exists
  And the applied state appears only after backend confirmation
  And the change is visible in the methodology drawer's thresholds in force

Scenario: Imbalance navigation by keyboard
  Then a stack row can be reached and activated using only the keyboard, and the chart zone is highlighted

Scenario: Degraded state honesty
  Given the WebSocket disconnects
  Then the panels show a disconnected or stale state rather than continuing to present the last value as current

Scenario: Honesty sweep automated
  Then the suite asserts, for every surface in the test plan's checklist table, that the expected estimated badge is present
```

## Technical notes / design
Drive states through the replay pipeline and a controllable WS proxy rather than through UI stubbing, so the test exercises the real subscription and decode path - the failure modes this epic cares about (stale presented as live, duplicate rows after resync) only appear there.

Select elements by role and accessible name wherever possible; it keeps the E2E suite honest about accessibility as a side effect and makes it resilient to styling changes.

Keep each flow under 90 seconds; parallelise by flow. Quarantine policy per the testing strategy: a flaky test is fixed or removed, never retried indefinitely.

## Test plan
This ticket is test work. Self-verification: ten consecutive green runs; a deliberate mutation (remove a badge; make apply optimistic) must fail the suite - record that mutation check in the PR.

## Security notes
Flow 2 asserts a control, not merely a feature; add a negative case where a Viewer-role session cannot apply a change and the UI does not offer it. Test credentials come from the CI secret store, never from the repo; fixtures contain no account data.

## Accessibility notes
Keyboard paths are first-class test cases (SCR-056 row navigation, SCR-059 dialog focus trap and restore, SCR-058 focus-to-section). Role/name-based selectors mean a broken accessible name breaks the suite.

## Performance notes
Suite runtime budget: <=8 minutes in CI for the `@e25` tag. Measurement of product performance belongs to E25-Q03.

## Observability
Assert the analytics events fire for the flows covered (`methodology.opened`, `detector.threshold_changed`, `imbalance.event_clicked`, `regime.explain_opened`).
