title: Determinism, perf and chaos testing for the detector pipeline
body:
## Context
Three R2 gates land on this ticket.

- **Determinism** (exit criterion #7, quality gate "Determinism"): "Detector outputs are reproducible: replaying the same recorded window twice yields identical detector events."
- **Performance** (exit criterion #2 and #9): the full order-flow scene must hold p95 <=16.6 ms and never drop below 30 fps (budgets #1, #2) *with the detector marker layer added*, and WS tick to screen p95 must stay <100 ms (budget #3, hard R2 gate) with the detector metric set on the subscription.
- **Chaos** (quality gate "Integration" fixtures): WS disconnect and resync, sequence gap, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018 - detectors must not emit phantom events across a gap and must not present stale values as live.

This ticket also validates the E25-K01 calibration in the built system, which is the precondition for turning the `metrics.iceberg_detector`, `metrics.stop_run_detector` and `metrics.absorption` feature flags on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Determinism harness** in CI: replay a recorded symbol-day twice through the full pipeline; assert the emitted detector event streams (absorption, iceberg, stop_run, regime transitions, imbalance stacks) are identical, field by field including `params_snapshot`; assert the same across two different machines/CI runners.
- **Golden-fixture drift test** wired into CI: committed expected event streams; any drift fails the build (quality gate "Correctness").
- **Frontend perf benchmark**: the full R2 scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + 3 stat rows + CVD pane) plus the detector marker layer at worst-case event density, asserting budgets #1 and #2; plus per-panel render budgets (SCR-055 <=1 ms at 4 Hz, SCR-056 <=1.5 ms at 4 Hz with a full 2 000-entry buffer, SCR-057 <=1 ms and zero renders on unchanged verdicts).
- **Budget #3 measurement** with the detector metric set added to `metrics.{symbol}`: backend receipt timestamp to paint timestamp, p95 <100 ms and p99 <250 ms.
- **Backend load/soak**: k6/Locust driving N symbols with the full detector set enabled for a sustained window; assert budgets #6 (<=20 ms fan-out add-on), #8 (<=300 MB per symbol), #11 (<=0.5 vCPU per symbol) and flat memory over the run.
- **Chaos scenarios**: WS disconnect and resync, sequence gap forcing a book resnapshot, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018; assert no phantom detector events are emitted across the gap, panels show stale/disconnected honestly, and detector state recovers without duplicate events after resync.
- **Calibration validation**: event rates per detector on the fixture set compared against the bands recommended by E25-K01; a written go/no-go for each feature flag.

## Out of scope
Functional E2E (E25-Q02), a11y (E25-Q04), the chart engine's own baseline benchmarks (E11), replay-engine determinism itself (E26 - this ticket asserts detector determinism *given* the replay clock).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Determinism across runs and machines
  Given the same recorded symbol-day
  When it is replayed twice on the same runner and once on a different runner
  Then all three detector event streams are identical field by field, including the parameter snapshots

Scenario: Golden fixtures guard against drift
  Given committed expected event streams
  When a change alters detector output
  Then CI fails with a diff naming the detector and the first differing event

Scenario: Frame budget with detectors
  Given the full R2 order-flow scene plus the detector marker layer at worst-case density
  Then p95 frame time is at most 16.6 milliseconds and the frame rate never drops below 30 frames per second

Scenario: WS tick to screen
  Given the detector metric set is subscribed
  Then WS tick to screen is under 100 milliseconds at p95 and under 250 milliseconds at p99

Scenario: No phantom events across a gap
  Given a sequence gap forces a book resnapshot
  Then no detector event is emitted for the gap period
  And after resync detection resumes without duplicating events

Scenario: Soak is flat
  Given the detector set runs for the soak duration across N symbols
  Then memory is flat, CPU stays within budget and no messages are lost

Scenario: Flags have a written verdict
  Then each of the three detector feature flags has a documented go or no-go based on measured event rates against the calibration bands
```

## Technical notes / design
Determinism comparison must be on the *serialised event stream*, not on aggregate counts - counts can match while ordering or magnitudes differ. Sort keys are defined by the engines (`(ts_ms, price, detector)`), so an ordering difference is a genuine defect, not a test artefact.

For the perf benchmark, reuse the existing engine benchmark harness in CI rather than building a second one; add the detector marker layer as a scene variant so the comparison against the no-detector baseline is direct and a regression is attributable.

Chaos scenarios are driven through the WS proxy used by E25-Q02 so both suites share one mechanism.

## Test plan
This ticket is the test work. Its own quality bar: each assertion must fail when the corresponding behaviour is deliberately broken - record those negative checks (introduce a wall-clock call to break determinism; disable the density clamp to break the frame budget) in the PR.

## Security notes
The load test doubles as a DoS probe for the concerns raised in E25-X01: unbounded `metrics[]` selection, oversized REST backfill ranges, and repeated recompute requests. Assert the caps (12 metrics, bounded range, rate limit) hold under load and return errors rather than degrading the service.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (E25-Q04 owns accessibility), except that the perf benchmark must run with the DOM-mirror enabled, since it is part of the shipped cost.

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: #1, #2, #3, #6, #8, #11, plus the per-panel render budgets from the screens catalogue. All are hard gates for R2 except #11 (tracked).

## Observability
The harness exports its measurements to the CI performance dashboard so regressions are visible over time rather than only as a pass/fail. Detector event-rate metrics are captured per fixture for the calibration comparison.

## Definition of Done
Determinism, golden-fixture, perf, load/soak and chaos suites merged and running in CI; all asserted budgets green; negative checks recorded; the feature-flag go/no-go written and reviewed with the M9 owner and the product owner; results linked from the epic and fed into the R2 PRR.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-Q01 (plan), E25-T03, E25-T04, E25-T05 (detectors to measure) and E25-S06 (the marker layer that affects the frame budget). Feeds E25-Q05 and the R2 PRR.

title: Accessibility audit of SCR-055..059 and the detector markers
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI and manual screen-reader passes; R2's quality gates require an a11y pass on every new view, with the specific demand that "heatmap has a non-colour alternative" and that canvas-based views are reachable through the DOM mirror. E25's screens have their own explicit obligations in the screens catalogue, and this audit verifies the built product against them rather than against a generic checklist.

E25-D06 reviewed the designs; this ticket audits the implementation. If D06 did its job, this audit should find little - and if it finds a lot, that is a signal about the handoff, which should be recorded.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated scans wired into CI for SCR-055, SCR-056, SCR-057, SCR-058, SCR-059 and the detector event card, in both themes; zero violations of serious or critical severity.
- Manual screen-reader passes (the project's primary screen reader plus one alternative) covering: SCR-055's text readout as the primary accessible value and the once-per-5-seconds throttle on threshold announcements; SCR-056's table-first structure and the "bid 340 vs ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1" ratio sentence; SCR-057's text-first badge and numeric confidence; SCR-058's heading structure, focus-to-section and focus restore; SCR-059's fieldsets, units, defaults, validation association and the announcement of new effective thresholds.
- Keyboard-only pass: every control reachable and operable; SCR-056 row cursor and activation; SCR-059 focus trap and restore; chart detector markers reachable through the DOM mirror with the card content announced.
- Colour-independence verification on the built UI (greyscale and a colour-vision-deficiency simulation): threshold bands, imbalance side, regime, marker types.
- Contrast verification on rendered pixels, including graphical objects at 3:1.
- Target-size and spacing check on SCR-059.
- Reduced-motion verification.
- Findings filed with severity and WCAG success-criterion references; blocking findings fixed and re-verified before the epic closes; an audit report with a statement of conformance for these screens.

## Out of scope
Accessibility of screens outside this epic; the DOM-mirror mechanism itself (E11, though failures found here are raised against it); design-time review (E25-D06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated scans clean
  Then axe-core reports zero serious or critical violations on all five screens in both themes, and the scans run in CI

Scenario: Screen-reader narrative matches the specification
  Then each screen is announced as specified in the handoff, including the tape panel's sentence readout and the imbalance ratio sentence
  And no more than one threshold announcement occurs in any five-second period

Scenario: Keyboard-only operation
  Then every function of all five screens and the chart detector markers is operable by keyboard alone with a visible focus indicator

Scenario: No colour-only meaning
  Given greyscale and colour-vision-deficiency simulations of the built screens
  Then every meaning-bearing element remains distinguishable

Scenario: Markers reachable
  Then detector markers on the chart are reachable through the DOM mirror and their event card content is announced

Scenario: Findings resolved
  Then every blocking finding is fixed and re-verified, and the audit report records a conformance statement for these screens
```

## Technical notes / design
Test with real data flowing (replay fixture), not static stories - announcement throttling, live-region behaviour and focus stability under streaming updates are exactly what breaks, and a static Storybook pass will not reveal it.

Where a finding stems from a shared component (CMP-227, CMP-049, CMP-043), raise it against the design-system component so every consumer benefits, and note the cross-epic impact.

## Test plan
This ticket is the audit. Evidence: axe-core CI reports, screen-reader session recordings or transcripts, greyscale/CVD screenshots, contrast measurements, and the findings register.

## Security notes
Confirm the SCR-059 armed-rule confirmation is fully operable by keyboard and screen reader - a safety control that cannot be operated non-visually is not a control for every user.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the accessibility work; standard is `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Performance notes
Confirm the DOM mirror and live regions do not breach the panel render budgets; if they do, hand the measurement to E25-Q03 rather than silently trading accessibility away.

## Observability
Audit results recorded in the accessibility tracking sheet so R5 hardening can see the trend across epics.

## Definition of Done
axe-core scans in CI and clean; manual screen-reader and keyboard passes completed with evidence; colour-independence and contrast verified on the built UI; findings filed with WCAG references; blocking findings fixed and re-verified; audit report published and linked from the epic; accessibility lead sign-off.

title: Run the detector regression pack and give QA sign-off for E25
body:
## Context
The closing QA gate for the epic. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires QA sign-off before a story is Done, and R2's exit criteria require an explicit honesty check per estimated view plus zero open P0/P1 before the train can cut. This ticket executes the regression pack defined in E25-Q01, runs the exploratory charters, confirms every exit criterion, and records the sign-off that the R2 PRR depends on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the full regression pack from E25-Q01 across all nine DET stories on the release candidate, on both web and Electron.
- Execute the four exploratory charters with written debriefs; file anything found.
- Execute the **honesty checklist** across every surface rendering a heuristic value, including those owned by neighbouring epics that consume E25's events (the DOM ladder's detector chips from E21, footprint order-count from E18, trade clustering from E22) - the checklist is app-wide by design.
- Verify each E25 exit criterion explicitly, with evidence: single subscription, badge coverage, determinism (from E25-Q03), backend-only thresholds, budget #3, audit coverage, explicit degradation, a11y pass, coverage floors.
- Confirm zero open P0/P1 against the epic; triage and disposition everything else.
- Confirm the feature-flag go/no-go from E25-Q03 has been acted on and that flag states in the release candidate match the decision.
- QA sign-off statement, and the epic's contribution to the R2 PRR pack (`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`).

## Out of scope
Building new automation (Q02/Q03/Q04), fixing defects (owned by the story tickets), the R2 PRR itself (this feeds it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Regression pack executed
  Then every case in the regression pack has a recorded result on the release candidate for both web and Electron

Scenario: Exploratory charters completed
  Then all four charters are executed with written debriefs and any findings filed

Scenario: App-wide honesty check
  Then every surface rendering a heuristic value has been checked for badge presence, popover accuracy and visible thresholds
  And any miss is filed as a P1 and fixed before sign-off

Scenario: Exit criteria evidenced
  Then each of the epic's exit criteria has a named piece of evidence attached

Scenario: Clean board
  Then there are zero open P0 or P1 defects against this epic
  And every remaining defect has an agreed disposition

Scenario: Sign-off
  Then QA sign-off is recorded, and the epic's PRR contribution is submitted
```

## Technical notes / design
Run the pack against the same recorded fixtures used throughout the epic so results are comparable with earlier runs; note any case that can only be validated live (demo environment) and run those separately against Bybit demo.

Where automation already covers a case (E25-Q02/Q03/Q04), record the automated result rather than re-executing manually - the pack's manual portion should be what automation genuinely cannot cover, notably subjective plausibility of detector events and the accuracy of methodology copy.

## Test plan
This ticket is the execution. Evidence: run records, charter debriefs, checklist results, exit-criterion evidence table.

## Security notes
Confirm E25-X02's security review is closed and its findings are either fixed or formally accepted; an open high-severity security finding blocks sign-off regardless of functional quality.

## Accessibility notes
Confirm E25-Q04's blocking findings are fixed and re-verified, including on E25-S01 and E25-S06 if they landed after the audit.

## Performance notes
Confirm E25-Q03's budget assertions are green on the release candidate, not merely on the branch where they were written.

## Observability
Confirm the epic's metrics and audit events are present in Grafana and the audit log on the release candidate, since R2's PRR expects operability, not just functionality.

## Definition of Done

title: Build the speed-of-tape panel (SCR-055) with gauge, strip and z-score
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DET-001 Speed of tape (Must)**, **US-DET-002 Tape acceleration and threshold alerts (Should)** and **US-DET-003 Book speed (Should)** on **SCR-055 Speed-of-tape panel**: "Rolling trades/sec and notional/sec gauge plus a strip chart, optionally split by side, with a z-score badge used by the rule engine vocabulary (`tape_speed_zscore`)."

The screen contract from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is binding: data from WS `metrics.{symbol}`, windows 1 s / 5 s / 30 s; states calm, elevated, extreme ("threshold chips, **text labels not colour only**") and insufficient sample ("Warming up - 8 s of data"); a11y "The gauge has a text readout ('42 trades/s, 3.1 sigma above the 1-hour mean') as its **primary accessible value**; threshold crossings are announced politely at most once every 5 s; the sparkline has a table alternative"; performance "pushed on `metrics.{symbol}` at 4 Hz; the panel renders at <=4 Hz with a 1 ms budget and **never recomputes z-scores client-side over a long window**".

Design is signed off in E25-D03/D07 (Sprints 11-12), satisfying the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Panel organism for SCR-055 composed of **CMP-131 SpeedOfTapeGauge**, **CMP-187 SpeedOfTapePane** (strip-chart mode), **CMP-024 Sparkline**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** (on the book-speed classification only, which US-DET-003 requires to carry it), **CMP-026 EmptyState**.
- Subscription to WS `metrics.{symbol}` with `metrics: ["trades_per_sec","volume_per_sec","book_updates_per_sec","tape_acceleration"]` through the shared WS worker; one subscription for the whole family.
- Window selector 1 s / 5 s / 30 s; the active window length is labelled on the panel; changing it resubscribes and the next value is computed on the new window server-side (no client-side re-derivation).
- Per-side split toggle (buy/sell prints per second) rendered as two series with distinct non-colour encodings.
- Z-score badge for `tape_acceleration` with calm / elevated / extreme chips carrying **text labels**, plus the "warming up - N s remaining" state driven by `meta.warming_up_remaining_ms`.
- Book-speed readout with the calm / normal / nervous classification string from the backend, the `(estimated)` badge, and the depth-tier renormalisation annotation on the series (US-DET-003 scenario 2).
- Idle state: an explicit `0` reading when no prints have arrived, never a held last value.
- "Create alert from this threshold" affordance that hands the current metric and threshold to the alert-creation flow (owned by the ALRT epic; this story only launches it with the right payload).
- Table alternative for the strip chart, reachable from the panel header.
- Analytics: `tapespeed.window_changed`, `tapespeed.threshold_changed`, `tapespeed.alert_created`.
- Storybook stories for every documented state.

## Out of scope
The rolling statistics and z-score computation (E25-T01 - backend), alert creation, delivery and cooldown (ALRT epic), the scanner column that reuses `trades_per_sec` (E17/SCR-104), regime (S03), imbalance (S02), detector settings (S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Gauge and strip
  Given a 5 second window
  Then the gauge shows current prints per second and notional per second with units
  And a strip chart shows the recent history
  And the window length is labelled on the panel

Scenario: Window change
  When I switch to a 1 second window
  Then the metric recomputes immediately from the backend on the new window
  And the panel performs no client-side z-score recomputation over a long window

Scenario: Idle market
  Given no prints have arrived for 10 seconds
  Then the gauge reads zero explicitly rather than holding the last value

Scenario: Warming up
  Given the baseline window has insufficient samples
  Then the z-score badge reads warming up with the remaining time, and no z-score value is shown

Scenario: Threshold crossing announced politely
  Given the z-score crosses the configured threshold repeatedly within 5 seconds
  Then at most one polite screen-reader announcement is made in that 5 second period

Scenario: Book speed is labelled estimated
  Then the calm, normal or nervous classification carries the (estimated) badge whose activation opens SCR-058 at the book-speed section

Scenario: Depth tier change
  Given the depth tier changes
  Then the book-speed series shows the renormalisation annotation at that point

Scenario: Render budget
  Given metrics arrive at 4 Hz
  Then the panel renders at most 4 times per second within a 1 millisecond render budget
```

## Technical notes / design
Decode in the shared WS worker and hand the panel a small typed snapshot per tick; do not keep a long history in React state - the strip chart holds a fixed-size Float32Array ring of the displayed window only. Threshold chips are derived from backend-published classification strings; the panel must contain **no numeric threshold constants** (enforced by a lint rule added in this story, per the epic exit criterion "no threshold logic exists in the web client").

Announcements use a polite live region with a 5 s throttle implemented as a leading-edge throttle so the first crossing is announced immediately and subsequent ones are suppressed, rather than delayed.

Number formatting uses the mono numeric token from the CMP-036/CMP-049 token contract; notional is formatted with the symbol's quote currency.

## Test plan
- Unit: window-label rendering; idle-zero rendering; warming-up countdown; throttle emits at most one announcement per 5 s window; renormalisation annotation placement; no threshold constants (lint rule test).
- Component (Storybook + testing-library): each documented state renders its documented copy; window selector resubscribes with the new option; alert affordance dispatches the correct payload.
- E2E (added in E25-Q02): switch window, observe idle-zero on a quiet fixture, open SCR-058 from the estimated badge.
- Perf (E25-Q03): 4 Hz update stream for 10 minutes, assert p95 render <=1 ms and no dropped frames.
- a11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass confirming the text readout is the primary accessible value and the sparkline table alternative is reachable.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Public market data, but the subscription requires an authenticated session with `marketdata:read`. Do not render raw backend error payloads in the panel; map to user-facing copy. No secrets in analytics events.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. Primary accessible value is the sentence readout ("42 trades/s, 3.1 sigma above the 1-hour mean"). Threshold state is conveyed by text label plus shape, never colour alone. Strip chart has a table alternative. All controls keyboard reachable with visible focus; live region is polite and throttled to one announcement per 5 s.

## Performance notes
Budget: panel render <=1 ms at <=4 Hz (SCR-055). Budget #3 (WS tick to screen p95 <100 ms, hard R2 gate) applies end to end. The panel must not allocate per tick - reuse the ring buffer.

## Observability
Analytics `tapespeed.window_changed`, `tapespeed.threshold_changed`, `tapespeed.alert_created`. Client performance mark around the panel render sampled into the existing frontend performance telemetry.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2: merged with 2 approvals including a frontend code owner; design sign-off from E25-D07 referenced and design QA (E25-D08) passed; Storybook entries for all states; unit and component tests green; coverage >=80 %; axe-core clean in CI; QA sign-off on the story group; no open P0/P1.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T01 (metrics must be published before the panel can render them) and E25-D07 (design handoff - no frontend screen work starts before design sign-off).

## Branch
`feat/detectors-speed-panel`. PR size guidance: (1) gauge + strip + subscription, (2) z-score/threshold states and announcements, (3) book speed + estimated badge.

title: Build the imbalance tracker panel (SCR-056) with chart cross-highlight
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DET-004 Imbalance tracker panel (Must)**: "a chart-wide panel listing current imbalance stacks, so that I do not have to hunt for them visually" - each active stack listed with price range, direction, depth, age and status (active/tested/broken); selecting a row scrolls the chart to and highlights the zone; an explicit "no stacks at current thresholds" state links to the thresholds. NFR: "panel updates within 200 ms of a new stack; **fully keyboard navigable**".

**SCR-056** fixes the rest: data from WS `metrics.{symbol}`; "thresholds shared with SCR-032 (single source of truth: changing one prompts to sync the other)"; a11y "Each imbalance event is a row in a **real table** (time, price, ratio, side, stacked count) so the canvas heat strip is never the only representation; the ratio is read as 'bid 340 vs ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1'; the stacked-imbalance grouping is stated in text"; performance "bounded 2 000-event ring buffer, renders <=4 Hz with a 1.5 ms budget; recomputation on a threshold change is done backend-side, with a visible recompute state".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Panel for SCR-056 built from **CMP-049 Table** (virtualised, the accessible primary representation), **CMP-132 ImbalanceStackIndicator**, **CMP-134 DetectorEventCard**, **CMP-011 Tag/Chip**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**, **CMP-026 EmptyState**.
- Columns: time, price range, direction (as text plus glyph), stack depth, maximum ratio, age, status (active / tested / broken).
- Incremental updates from `metrics.{symbol}` stack events into a bounded 2 000-entry ring buffer; status transitions update the existing row in place rather than appending a duplicate.
- Row selection scrolls the chart to the bar and highlights the corresponding zone and, where the stack came from footprint cells, links to the originating footprint cell (D03 sign-off item).
- Filters from the screen sketch: "only unfilled" and "alert on new"; the latter hands off to the alert-creation flow owned by the ALRT epic.
- Threshold controls that read and write the **shared** footprint imbalance configuration, with the sync prompt required by SCR-056 when the value differs from SCR-032, and a visible **recompute state** while the backend recomputes.
- Empty state: "no stacks at current thresholds", with a link to the thresholds; stale-data shading.
- Full keyboard navigation: arrow keys move the row cursor, Enter activates (jumps the chart), and the row cursor is announced with the ratio sentence.
- Analytics: `imbalance.threshold_changed`, `imbalance.stacked_min_changed`, `imbalance.event_clicked`, `imbalance.alert_created`.
- Storybook entries for streaming, empty, recomputing, stale and disconnected states.

## Out of scope
Stack detection and lifecycle (E25-T06 - backend), per-cell imbalance computation and the footprint settings dialog SCR-032 (E18), alert delivery (ALRT), chart-side zone rendering primitives (reused from E11/E18).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Stack list
  Then each active stack is listed with its price range, direction, stack depth, ratio, age and status

Scenario: Navigate to a stack
  When I select a row with the mouse or press Enter on the focused row
  Then the chart scrolls to and highlights the corresponding zone

Scenario: No stacks
  Given no stacks exist at the current thresholds
  Then an explicit no-stacks-at-current-thresholds state is shown with a link to the thresholds

Scenario: Status transition updates in place
  Given a listed active stack becomes tested and then broken
  Then its existing row updates in place and no duplicate row is appended

Scenario: Latency
  Given a new stack is published
  Then it appears in the panel within 200 milliseconds

Scenario: Threshold change is backend-side
  When I change the ratio threshold
  Then a visible recompute state is shown until the backend returns the recomputed stacks
  And the panel performs no client-side recomputation over history
  And I am prompted to sync the value with the footprint settings

Scenario: Keyboard and screen reader
  Then every row is reachable by keyboard with a visible focus indicator
  And the focused row is announced including the ratio read as bid 340 versus ask 82, ratio 4.1 to 1
  And the direction is conveyed by text, not colour alone
```

## Technical notes / design
The table is the primary representation and the canvas markers are secondary - build the table first and derive the highlight from the selected row, not the reverse. Rows are keyed by the backend's stack key `(bar_ts, price_low, direction)` so in-place updates are trivial and re-emissions cannot duplicate.

Virtualise the list but keep the accessible row semantics intact (`role="row"` on rendered rows with `aria-rowcount` reflecting the full buffer), per the CMP-049 contract.

The threshold control is a view over shared configuration; do not cache a second copy in panel state. On change, show the recompute state until the server confirms - this mirrors SCR-059's "never optimistically" rule.

## Test plan
- Unit: ring-buffer bound at 2 000; in-place status update by key; age formatting; ratio sentence construction; empty/recomputing/stale state selection.
- Component: row activation emits the chart-jump call; threshold change shows recompute state and the sync prompt; `aria-rowcount` reflects the buffer, not the rendered window.
- E2E (E25-Q02): stack appears, click jumps the chart, keyboard path from panel focus to chart highlight.
- Perf (E25-Q03): 4 Hz updates with a full 2 000-entry buffer, p95 render <=1.5 ms; new-stack-to-visible latency <=200 ms.
- a11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass on the table and the ratio announcement.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Public market data behind an authenticated session with `marketdata:read`. Threshold writes go through the audited shared-configuration path (never a panel-local endpoint). Bound the ring buffer so a hostile or runaway stream cannot exhaust renderer memory (budget #7).

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The event list is a real table and is the primary representation; the canvas heat strip is never the only carrier. Direction and status are text; the ratio is announced in the documented sentence form; stacked grouping is stated in text. Full keyboard navigation is a story NFR, not an enhancement.

## Performance notes
SCR-056 budgets: <=4 Hz render, 1.5 ms per render, bounded 2 000-event ring. Publication-to-visible latency <=200 ms (US-DET-004 NFR). Budget #3 applies end to end; budget #7 (<=1.5 GB renderer) bounds the buffer.

## Observability
Analytics `imbalance.threshold_changed`, `imbalance.stacked_min_changed`, `imbalance.event_clicked`, `imbalance.alert_created`. Client perf mark around the panel render.

## Definition of Done
Per section 3.2: merged with 2 approvals including a frontend code owner; design sign-off (E25-D07) referenced and design QA (E25-D08) passed; Storybook entries for all states; tests green; coverage >=80 %; axe-core clean; QA sign-off; no open P0/P1.

`blocked_by` E25-T06 (stack publication) and E25-D07 (design handoff). Interfaces relied on: the chart's scroll-to-and-highlight API from E11/E18, the shared footprint imbalance configuration from E18.

`feat/detectors-imbalance-panel`. PR size guidance: (1) table + subscription, (2) chart cross-highlight, (3) thresholds + recompute/empty/stale states.

title: Build the market regime panel (SCR-057) with sub-signal breakdown
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DET-008 Market regime classifier (Must)** on the frontend: "a badge shows the current regime with a confidence value and the sub-signals used (book thickness, realised volatility, tape speed)"; disabling a sub-signal recomputes and the panel "states its composition"; when the lookback cannot be filled "the badge reads 'insufficient data' rather than defaulting to a regime". NFR: "transitions emit events; **(estimated) badge mandatory**".

**SCR-057** fixes the surface: data from WS `metrics.{symbol}` plus `GET /api/v1/market/regime/explain?symbol&ts`; "click the badge -> expand the contributing-signal breakdown with each signal's value, threshold and weight"; a11y "the badge is **text-first**; the confidence value is always **numeric**"; performance "pushed at most 1 Hz; the panel renders only on change; the sub-signal breakdown is fetched once per change, not polled. Budget <=1 ms per update."

R9 applies: the panel presents a classification with evidence, never a recommendation. No imperative wording may appear anywhere on it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Panel for SCR-057 built from **CMP-133 RegimeIndicatorChip**, **CMP-032 Rating/Confidence Dots**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-069 InfoPanel**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge** (mandatory, always visible).
- Badge showing the regime label as text plus the numeric confidence (never a bare colour or bare dots - the dots supplement the number).
- Sub-signal breakdown from `/market/regime/explain`, one row per signal with its value, weight, contribution and direction (supports / opposes / neutral) as text, fetched once per regime change.
- Sub-signal enable/disable control; disabling one triggers a backend recompute and the panel states the composition actually in use.
- Regime-change history strip built from the transition events on `metrics.{symbol}`.
- Insufficient-history state reading "insufficient data" and naming the unfilled lookback - never a defaulted regime.
- "Why this classification?" link opening **SCR-058** at the regime section (E25-S04).
- "Create alert from this regime" affordance handing off to the ALRT flow.
- Analytics: `regime.panel_opened`, `regime.explain_opened`, `regime.sensitivity_changed`, `regime.alert_created`.
- Storybook entries for each regime value, low/high confidence, insufficient data, stale and disconnected.

## Out of scope
Classification, confidence computation and the explain endpoint (E25-T05 - backend), methodology content and the drawer itself (T07 / S04), alert delivery (ALRT), rule DSL binding (E35), ADX/ATR indicator rendering (E17).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Classification with confidence
  Then the badge shows the regime as text with a numeric confidence value
  And the (estimated) badge is present

Scenario: Sub-signal breakdown
  When I activate the badge
  Then each contributing sub-signal is listed with its value, weight, contribution and direction as text

Scenario: Sub-signal disabled
  When I disable tape speed as an input
  Then the classification is recomputed by the backend using the remaining signals
  And the panel states the composition actually used

Scenario: Insufficient data
  Given the lookback cannot be filled
  Then the badge reads insufficient data naming the unfilled lookback
  And no regime value is displayed

Scenario: Render cadence
  Given regime values arrive at most once per second
  Then the panel renders only on change, within a 1 millisecond budget
  And the sub-signal breakdown is fetched once per change, never polled

Scenario: No advice
  Then no wording on the panel instructs an action; the panel states a classification and its evidence only
```

## Technical notes / design
Render only on a changed verdict: compare the incoming `as_of`/regime/confidence tuple and bail out early otherwise. Fetch `/market/regime/explain` on change (and on first open), cache it against the `as_of` timestamp so reopening the breakdown does not refetch.

Confidence renders as the number first and the dots second (`CMP-032` supplements, never replaces). The `(estimated)` badge is not conditional on anything - regime is always estimated.

Copy review gate: an explicit checklist item in the PR that no imperative/advisory phrasing is present (R9).

## Test plan
- Unit: change detection suppresses no-op renders; explain caching keyed on `as_of`; insufficient-data state; composition string construction.
- Component: activating the badge expands the breakdown and emits `regime.explain_opened`; the estimated badge opens SCR-058 at the regime section; disabling a signal issues exactly one backend call.
- E2E (E25-Q02): observe a regime transition on a recorded fixture and see the history strip update.
- Perf (E25-Q03): 1 Hz stream, p95 render <=1 ms, zero renders on unchanged verdicts.
- a11y: axe-core clean; screen-reader pass confirming the badge is text-first and the confidence is announced numerically.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Public data behind `marketdata:read`. R9 advice boundary is the governing control: the panel must not render any field that could read as an instruction, and must not synthesise one from the classification. No client-side classification logic.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Text-first badge; numeric confidence always present; direction of each sub-signal as a word (supports/opposes/neutral), not a colour or an arrow alone; the transition strip has a text list equivalent; all controls keyboard reachable with visible focus.

## Performance notes
SCR-057: <=1 Hz push, render only on change, <=1 ms per update; explain fetched once per change. Budget #3 end to end.

## Observability
Analytics `regime.panel_opened`, `regime.explain_opened`, `regime.sensitivity_changed`, `regime.alert_created`. Client perf mark around the render.

title: Build the detector methodology drawer SCR-058 ("Why estimated?")
body:
## Context
This small story carries a large part of R2's exit criteria. Exit criterion #4: "**Every estimated view carries the (estimated) badge and a popover explaining the heuristic and its failure modes.** A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic." SCR-058 is that explanation: "a drawer opened from any `(estimated)` chip. Explains, per detector, the heuristic used, the inputs, the tunable thresholds, the known false-positive modes, and the hard statement that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed so these are proxies, not ground truth."

It serves **US-DET-009 (Must)** ("every detector documents its method in an info popover; none may render without an (estimated) badge where applicable") and US-CHART-014. Data: `GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology` plus current values from `GET /api/v1/detectors/config`. Performance: "opens in <=150 ms and issues no streaming subscriptions."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Drawer for SCR-058 built from **CMP-046 Drawer**, **CMP-069 InfoPanel**, **CMP-021 Link**, **CMP-032 Rating/Confidence Dots**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**.
- One section per estimated signal - iceberg, stop-run, absorption, queue position, order-count footprint, regime, liquidity cluster - each stating: what it infers, from what data, the exact heuristic and **the thresholds currently in force** (merged from `/detectors/config`, not the documented defaults), the known failure modes, and what would be required to know it for certain.
- The sentence "this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact" present in every section (a rendering test asserts this).
- Deep-linking: the drawer opens **at the section** for the badge that was activated (`openMethodology(detector)`), from any CMP-227 anywhere in the app.
- A single shared `EstimatedBadge` open-drawer binding so no surface has to wire its own - this is the mechanism that makes the epic's honesty invariant enforceable.
- Links to the detector settings (SCR-059) and to the methodology section of the docs.
- Analytics: `methodology.opened` with `{detector}` (deliberately tracked "so we can tell whether the honesty affordance is actually used").
- Storybook entries per section plus the "config unavailable" degraded state (content still renders; thresholds show as unavailable).

## Out of scope
Authoring the content (E25-T07), the settings dialog (E25-S05), detector implementations, the docs site.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Opens from any estimated badge
  Given any (estimated) badge anywhere in the application
  When I activate it
  Then the methodology drawer opens scrolled to that detector's section

Scenario: Every section is complete
  Then each section states what it infers, from what data, the heuristic, the thresholds in force, the known failure modes, and what would be required to know it for certain

Scenario: The honesty sentence
  Then every section contains the sentence that this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact
  And the statement that Bybit provides no L3 or MBO feed is present

Scenario: Thresholds in force, not defaults
  Given the iceberg minimum reload count has been changed from 3 to 5
  Then the iceberg section shows 5

Scenario: Degraded config
  Given GET /detectors/config fails
  Then the content still renders and the thresholds area states that current values are unavailable, with a retry

Scenario: Open latency and no subscriptions
  Then the drawer opens within 150 milliseconds
  And it issues no streaming subscriptions
```

## Technical notes / design
Content is fetched once per session from `/detectors/methodology` and cached; the config overlay is fetched on open. Render content as structured sections from the API rather than hard-coding copy in the client, so T07 remains the single source of the wording.

Focus management per the drawer contract: focus moves to the drawer heading on open, is trapped while open, and returns to the invoking badge on close. The section deep-link must move focus to the section heading, not merely scroll.

## Test plan
- Unit: deep-link resolves each detector id to its section; the required sentence assertion across all sections; config-overlay merge; degraded state.
- Component: opening from a badge in three different host surfaces (SCR-055, SCR-056, SCR-057) all land on the correct section; focus returns to the invoker on close.
- E2E (E25-Q02): open the drawer from the regime badge and from an imbalance row's badge.
- a11y: axe-core clean; keyboard-only open/navigate/close; screen-reader pass on heading structure.
- Perf: open <=150 ms measured with the content cache cold and warm; assert no WS subscription is created while open.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Content is public-safe (T07 owns that constraint). The config overlay requires `marketdata:read`; a 403 renders the content without thresholds rather than an error page. No raw backend errors surfaced.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, and this screen carries an extra bar because its purpose is comprehension: plain-language summary first, technical detail second, no jargon without a glossary link (SCR-058 a11y contract). Proper heading hierarchy, focus trap and restore, and the drawer is fully operable by keyboard.

## Performance notes
Opens in <=150 ms; content bundled/cached; issues no streaming subscriptions (SCR-058 performance contract).

## Observability
Analytics `methodology.opened{detector}`. A dashboard panel tracks opens per detector so the team can see whether the honesty affordance is actually used.

## Definition of Done
Per section 3.2: merged with 2 approvals including a frontend code owner; design sign-off (E25-D07) and design QA (E25-D08); content-completeness test in CI; Storybook entries; axe-core clean; coverage >=80 %; QA sign-off.

`blocked_by` E25-T07 (content and endpoint) and E25-D07 (design handoff). Every other E25 surface depends on this story for its badge binding.

`feat/detectors-methodology-drawer`. PR size guidance: one PR.

title: Build the detector settings dialog SCR-059 with armed-rule warnings
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DET-009 Detector configuration and audit of estimates (Must)** and the configuration half of US-DET-005/006/007 on **SCR-059 Detector settings dialog**: "Per detector (iceberg, stop-run, absorption, spoof-ish cancellation burst): enable, sensitivity preset (low/medium/high) or explicit thresholds (refill count, window ms, consumed-liquidity ratio, cluster distance ticks), symbol scope, alert routing, and a backtest-on-recorded-history preview showing how many events the current settings would have produced in the last N hours."

Three contract lines govern the behaviour:
- Validation: "thresholds bounded per detector with published ranges; 'Sensitivity high may produce many false positives' warning."
- Performance: "Changes are applied server-side and take effect on the next evaluation window (<=2 s); the dialog shows 'applied' only after the backend confirms, **never optimistically**."
- Audit: "`detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed` with `{detector, key, before, after}` - **audited, because detector output can feed armed rules that place orders**."

US-DET-009 additionally requires per-symbol overrides that persist and are marked as overridden, and a disabled state naming the exact missing dependency with "a one-click action to start recording".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Dialog for SCR-059 from **CMP-043 Dialog**, **CMP-065 FormSection** (one fieldset per detector), **CMP-040 FormField**, **CMP-004 Toggle**, **CMP-008 NumericStepperInput**, **CMP-010 Slider**, **CMP-028 Callout/Banner**, **CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**.
- Per detector: enable toggle, sensitivity preset (low/medium/high) or explicit thresholds, symbol scope (global or this symbol), reset-to-default, current state, **events today**, and its data dependencies (US-DET-009 scenario 1).
- Client-side validation mirroring the published server bounds for immediate feedback, with the server remaining authoritative: iceberg `min_reloads` 2-50, `price_tolerance_ticks` 0-10, `window_ms` 200-60000; stop_run `lookback_bars` 2-500, `penetration_ticks` 1-100, `reversal_pct` 0-100; absorption `min_volume_multiple` 1-50, `max_price_move_ticks` 0-50.
- "Sensitivity high may produce many false positives" warning on the high preset.
- **Armed-rule warning**: before applying a change, list the armed rules that depend on the detector being changed (D04 sign-off item) - this is the control that stops a threshold tweak silently changing live trading behaviour.
- Per-symbol override indication: the panel shows which values are overridden for the current symbol (US-DET-009 scenario 2).
- Missing-dependency state: the detector is shown disabled with the exact missing dependency and a one-click "start recording" action (US-DET-009 scenario 3).
- Non-optimistic apply: an "applying..." state until the backend confirms, then "applied"; on failure the previous values are restored and the error is shown.
- Backtest-on-recorded-history preview: event count the current settings would have produced over the last N hours, with an explicit unavailable state when history is missing.
- Every detector section carries the `(estimated)` badge linking to SCR-058.
- Analytics/audit: `detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed` (audited server-side by E25-T02; the client emits the analytics twin).
- Storybook entries: default, overridden, disabled-missing-dependency, validation error, applying, apply-failed, armed-rule warning.

## Out of scope
Config persistence, bounds enforcement, audit writing and the backtest computation (E25-T02 - backend), methodology content (T07), alert routing destinations (ALRT), the rule engine's own UI (E36/E37), the footprint imbalance thresholds (SCR-032, owned by E18).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Central panel
  Then every detector lists its parameters, current state, event count today and its data dependencies

Scenario: Per-symbol overrides
  When I set different thresholds for ETHUSDT
  Then they persist per symbol and the panel indicates which values are overridden

Scenario: Dependency missing
  Given a detector requires book history that is not recorded for the symbol
  Then it is shown disabled with the exact missing dependency and a one-click action to start recording

Scenario: Out-of-range value
  When I enter an iceberg minimum reload count of 99
  Then a validation message names the permitted range of 2 to 50 and the change cannot be applied

Scenario: High sensitivity warning
  When I select the high sensitivity preset
  Then a warning states that it may produce many false positives

Scenario: Armed rules are named before applying
  Given an armed rule depends on the stop-run detector
  When I change a stop-run threshold
  Then the dialog lists that rule and requires confirmation before applying

Scenario: Never optimistic
  When I apply a change
  Then the dialog shows applying until the backend confirms, and only then shows applied
  And if the backend rejects the change the previous values are restored with the error shown

Scenario: Estimated framing repeated
  Then each detector section carries the (estimated) badge linking to the methodology drawer
```

## Technical notes / design
Form state is a draft copy; nothing is written until Apply. Bounds constants are **imported from the generated OpenAPI client types**, not retyped, so the dialog cannot drift from the server contract (this is the one permitted place for threshold numbers in the client, and they are generated, not authored).

The armed-rule dependency list is fetched on open from the rule-engine read API (E35) keyed by detector id; when that API is unavailable the dialog states that dependent rules could not be checked and requires an explicit acknowledgement before applying - failing safe, not silent.

Announce the new effective threshold on change (SCR-059 a11y contract) via a polite live region.

## Test plan
- Unit: bounds validation at both ends of every published range; preset-to-threshold mapping; override marking; draft/apply/rollback state machine; armed-rule fetch failure path.
- Component: applying shows applying then applied only after the server responds; a rejected apply restores previous values; the missing-dependency action calls the start-recording endpoint; high-preset warning appears.
- E2E (E25-Q02): change a threshold, confirm the armed-rule warning, apply, and verify the audit record exists (asserted via the admin audit view).
- Security test (E25-X02): a Viewer-role session cannot apply changes; the attempt is rejected and logged.
- a11y: axe-core clean; per-detector fieldsets with units and defaults shown; change announcements verified with a screen reader.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
This dialog is the user-facing half of the epic's highest-value tampering target: detector output can feed armed rules that place orders. Controls: `settings:write` enforced server-side (the dialog is not the gate), server-side bounds enforcement, append-only audit of every change, the armed-rule warning before apply, and fail-safe behaviour when dependent rules cannot be enumerated. The dialog must never disable or bypass a server validation. Reviewed under `security` label in E25-X02.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Per-detector fieldsets with legends; numeric inputs with units and default values shown; each detector has an enable switch and a text description; changing a value announces the new effective threshold politely; validation messages are programmatically associated with their field; the dialog traps focus and restores it on close.

## Performance notes
Apply takes effect within <=2 s (SCR-059). Dialog opens in <=200 ms. The backtest preview is computed backend-side and must not block the dialog - it renders progressively with a loading state.

## Observability
Client analytics `detector.enabled_changed`, `detector.threshold_changed`; the authoritative audit records are written server-side by E25-T02. A dashboard panel shows threshold changes over time alongside detector event rates so a sudden event-rate change can be correlated with a configuration change.

## Definition of Done
Per section 3.2: merged with 2 approvals including a frontend code owner and a security reviewer; design sign-off (E25-D07) and design QA (E25-D08); Storybook entries for all listed states; tests green; coverage >=80 %; axe-core clean; security review (E25-X02) closed; QA sign-off.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T02 (config endpoints, bounds, audit, dependency state) and E25-D07 (design handoff). Relies on the rule-engine read API (E35) for the armed-rule list and on the recorder API (E16) for the start-recording action.

## Branch
`feat/detectors-settings-dialog`. PR size guidance: (1) form + validation, (2) apply state machine + armed-rule warning, (3) backtest preview and dependency states.

title: Render detector event markers and DetectorEventCard on the chart
body:
## Context
US-DET-005 requires that "an absorption marker is **drawn** with its magnitude and an (estimated) badge" and US-DET-007 that "a sweep marker is **drawn** at the extreme with direction and magnitude" and that "parameters are shown in the legend". Those markers live on the chart, not in a panel, and they are rendered by the chart engine's overlay layer rather than by DOM.

The component contract already exists: **CMP-134 DetectorEventCard (iceberg/stop-run/absorption)**, whose a11y note is explicit - "Card (CMP-050) composition with CMP-011 estimated chip **mandatory**". SCR-051 (the DOM/heatmap screen) already shows detector chips with "(estimated)" in its sketch ("detectors: iceberg 63,970 (estimated) - stop-run zone 63,900 (est.)"), so the marker vocabulary must be consistent between the chart and the ladder.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chart overlay layer rendering absorption, iceberg and stop-run events from `metrics.{symbol}` event-like metric points (`MetricPoint.meta`), using the engine's existing marker/annotation primitives from `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` - no new render path.
- Marker encoding: glyph plus text label (direction and magnitude), never colour alone; an `(estimated)` affordance on every marker opening SCR-058 at that detector's section.
- **CMP-134 DetectorEventCard** on hover/focus of a marker showing detector, time, price, direction, magnitude, and the **parameter snapshot in force when it fired** (the `params_snapshot` from the event) - this is the "see *why* it fired" inspector the roadmap scope line requires.
- Legend entry naming the active detectors and their current parameters (US-DET-007 scenario "Parameters").
- Stop-run breakout annotation rendered distinctly when enabled (US-DET-007 scenario "No reversion").
- Keyboard access: markers are reachable in the chart's DOM-mirror accessibility tree (the same mechanism used for footprint cells and DOM rows, roadmap section 6.4 a11y gate), with the card content announced.
- Clamped marker density: above a configured events-per-viewport threshold, markers cluster with a count badge rather than overplotting.
- Feature-flag awareness: when a detector's flag is off or it is disabled for a missing dependency, no markers render and the legend states why.
- Storybook/engine-demo entries for each marker type and the clustered state.

## Out of scope
Detector computation (T03/T04), the methodology drawer itself (S04), settings (S05), the DOM ladder's own detector chips (E21 renders them, consuming the same events), alerting (ALRT), journal auto-tagging.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Absorption marker
  Given an absorption event is published
  Then a marker is drawn at its price and time with its magnitude and an (estimated) affordance

Scenario: Sweep marker
  Given a stop-run event is published
  Then a marker is drawn at the swept extreme with direction and magnitude
  And the legend shows the active detection parameters

Scenario: Why it fired
  When I hover or focus a marker
  Then a DetectorEventCard shows the detector, time, price, direction, magnitude and the parameter snapshot in force when it fired

Scenario: No reversion
  Given a penetration that did not revert and breakout annotations are enabled
  Then a distinct breakout annotation is drawn, visually distinguishable from a sweep marker without relying on colour

Scenario: Density clamp
  Given more detector events than the per-viewport threshold
  Then markers cluster with a count badge rather than overplotting
  And the frame budget is not exceeded

Scenario: Keyboard and screen reader
  Then markers are reachable through the chart DOM mirror and their card content is announced

Scenario: Detector disabled
  Given a detector is disabled by its feature flag or a missing dependency
  Then no markers for it render and the legend states the reason
```

## Technical notes / design
Reuse the engine's instanced-marker primitive; a detector marker is a glyph instance plus a text label subject to the same text-LOD rule the footprint uses (hide glyph text below the per-cell pixel-width threshold proven in E06/E18) so the marker layer cannot be the thing that breaks budget #1.

Events are appended to a bounded per-viewport buffer; on pan/zoom the visible window is recomputed from the buffer rather than refetched. Clustering is computed in screen space at layout time, not in data space, so it stays stable under zoom.

The card is DOM (CMP-134) positioned against the marker's screen coordinates, not drawn in WebGL, so its text is selectable and accessible.

## Test plan
- Unit: marker-to-screen placement; clustering threshold behaviour; params-snapshot rendering; disabled-detector legend copy; text-LOD suppression.
- Component: hover and keyboard focus both open the card with identical content; the estimated affordance opens SCR-058 at the right section.
- E2E (E25-Q02): markers appear on a recorded fixture; focusing one via keyboard announces the card.
- Perf (E25-Q03): full R2 scene (footprint + profile + heatmap + bubbles + 3 stat rows + CVD pane) **plus** the detector marker layer at the worst-case event density, p95 frame time <=16.6 ms and never below 30 fps (budgets #1 and #2, R2 exit criterion 2).
- a11y: axe-core on the card; DOM-mirror reachability test.
- Coverage >=80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Public market data. Markers must always carry the estimated affordance - a marker that looks like exchange-provided fact is the failure mode this epic exists to prevent. No raw backend payloads rendered in the card.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Markers are distinguishable by glyph and text, not colour alone (roadmap a11y gate: colour-blind-safe palettes; non-colour encodings). Markers reachable and announced via the chart DOM mirror, matching the footprint-cell and DOM-row treatment. The card is real DOM with selectable text.

## Performance notes
Budgets #1 (p95 <=16.6 ms with the full scene) and #2 (never below 30 fps worst case), both hard gates. The marker layer's own budget is <=0.5 ms per frame at nominal density; the density clamp exists to hold it.

## Observability
Client metric for markers rendered per frame and clustering activations; analytics `detector.marker_opened{detector}`.

## Definition of Done
Per section 3.2: merged with 2 approvals including the chart-engine code owner; design sign-off (E25-D07) and design QA (E25-D08); engine benchmark added to the CI perf suite and passing budgets #1/#2 with the marker layer enabled; Storybook/engine-demo entries; coverage >=80 %; axe-core clean; QA sign-off.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T03 and E25-T04 (the events to render) and E25-D07 (design handoff). Relies on the E11 chart-engine marker and DOM-mirror primitives and on the E25-S04 badge binding.

title: Implement stop-run / liquidity-sweep detector (estimated) in M9
body:
## Context
Implements the backend of **US-DET-007 Stop-run / liquidity sweep detector (Must)**: "Given price breaks a marked swing extreme, trades through resting liquidity above the threshold and reverts within the window, Then a sweep marker is drawn at the extreme with direction and magnitude". Its NFR binds it to three consumers: "events feed the alert engine, the rule DSL and journal auto-tags". Its declared dependencies are US-DOM-002 (book depth, delivered by E21) and US-IND-005 (swing/structure detection) - the story is explicit that the sweep is measured against *marked swing extremes*, and `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` elsewhere insists a divergence "is only drawn once both swings are confirmed by the swing detector, never on provisional swings". The same discipline applies here.

Parameters as published in `DetectorConfig`: `lookback_bars` (2-500, default 20), `penetration_ticks` (1-100, default 2), `reversal_pct` (0-100, default 60), refined by E25-K01.

Bybit's public feed is anonymous and aggregated and exposes no L3/MBO data, so iceberg, stop-run, absorption and regime are inferences, not observations. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` makes `confidence="estimated"` mandatory for every heuristic and states plainly that "presenting a heuristic as a certainty is a defect". Every surface that shows one of these values must render CMP-227 EstimatedBadge linked to SCR-058, the detector methodology drawer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `server/orderflow/detectors/stop_run.py`: maintains confirmed swing highs/lows over `lookback_bars`; on penetration beyond a confirmed extreme by `penetration_ticks`, opens a candidate recording the liquidity consumed above/below the extreme; confirms a sweep when price retraces `reversal_pct` of the penetration excursion within the reversion window; emits `DetectorEvent(detector="stop_run", price=extreme, direction, magnitude=liquidity_consumed, estimated=True, meta={penetration_ticks, reversion_ms, reversal_pct_achieved})`.
- Explicit **no-sweep** outcome: a penetration that does not revert within the window closes the candidate with no event, and optionally emits a distinct `breakout` annotation when the `breakout_annotations` option is enabled (US-DET-007 scenario "No reversion").
- Metric code `stop_run` on `metrics.{symbol}` with `estimated: true`; score persisted to `orderflow_metrics.stoprun_score`.
- Recompute over the loaded range on a parameter change, with the active parameters exposed for the legend (US-DET-007 scenario "Parameters").
- Golden-fixture test data committed for the determinism gate.

## Out of scope
Absorption/iceberg (T03), regime (T05), the chart marker rendering and legend (S06), settings UI (S05), alert delivery, journal auto-tagging (journal epic), the swing/structure detection algorithm itself (consumed from the indicator engine, US-IND-005).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sweep detected
  Given price breaks a confirmed swing extreme by at least penetration_ticks
  And trades through resting liquidity above the configured threshold
  And reverts by at least reversal_pct of the excursion within the reversion window
  Then a stop_run event is emitted at the extreme with direction, magnitude and estimated true

Scenario: No reversion is not a sweep
  Given price breaks the extreme and does not revert within the window
  Then no stop_run event is emitted
  And when breakout annotations are enabled a distinct breakout annotation is emitted instead

Scenario: Provisional swings are never used
  Given a swing extreme that the swing detector has not yet confirmed
  Then no candidate is opened against it

Scenario: Parameters change
  When reversion window or the liquidity threshold is changed
  Then detection recomputes server-side over the loaded range
  And the events carry the new parameter snapshot

Scenario: Determinism
  Given the same recorded fixture is replayed twice
  Then the emitted stop_run event streams are identical
```

## Technical notes / design
Candidate state is one small record per active extreme: `(extreme_price, side, opened_ts, peak_excursion_ticks, liquidity_consumed, deadline_ts)`. Liquidity consumed is accumulated from trades beyond the extreme, using the aggressor side that Bybit publishes directly - no tick-rule inference is needed or permitted. Deadlines are evaluated at the engine tick, driven by event timestamps, not by a timer, so replay is exact.

Only confirmed swings open candidates; when the swing detector later revises structure, already-emitted events are not retracted (events are immutable history) but the recompute path regenerates them for the loaded range, which is why the UI must render from the recomputed stream rather than accumulating locally.

Ordering: emissions are sorted by `(ts_ms, price)` before publication so double-run equality holds.

## Test plan
- Unit: penetration exactly at and one tick below the threshold; reversal exactly at `reversal_pct`; deadline boundary (reversion on the last millisecond counts, one millisecond later does not); provisional-swing rejection; breakout annotation on/off; liquidity accumulation uses feed-provided aggressor side.
- Golden fixture: recorded symbol-day with a committed expected stop_run stream; drift fails CI.
- Determinism: double-run equality.
- Integration: high-volatility burst fixture (the sweep-rich case) and thin-book fixture (the false-positive-rich case); event rates within the bands from E25-K01.
- Perf: microbenchmark per trade; combined M9 detector cost within budget #11.
- Coverage >=85 %.

## Security notes
Stop-run events feed the rule DSL and can therefore participate in armed actions; the event carries `estimated=True` and the acknowledgement flag defined in T03 so a heuristic can never silently become the sole trigger of a live order. Recompute is range- and rate-limited (STRIDE-D). No PII.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend). `direction` is emitted as text (`sweep_high` / `sweep_low`) and `magnitude` numerically, so S06 never needs colour alone.

## Performance notes
Evaluation adds <=1 ms p95 to the engine tick; candidate state is O(active extremes), bounded by `lookback_bars`. Budgets #6, #8, #11 as per the epic.

## Observability
`orderflow_detector_events_total{detector="stop_run",symbol}`, `orderflow_stop_run_candidates_open{symbol}` (gauge), `orderflow_stop_run_expired_total` (penetrations that never reverted), `orderflow_detector_eval_seconds{detector="stop_run"}`.

## Definition of Done
Per section 4.2: merged with 2 approvals including the M9 code owner; golden fixture and determinism tests in CI; coverage >=85 %; K01 defaults applied or deviation justified; the `stop_run` row of the metric vocabulary in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` verified; feature flag `metrics.stop_run_detector` stays default-off until E25-Q03 signs off.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-T02 (framework/config/bus), E25-K01 (calibration), E21 (book depth for the liquidity-consumed measure, US-DOM-002). Consumes confirmed swings from the indicator engine (US-IND-005).

## Branch

title: Author detector methodology content, vocabulary docs and feature flags
body:
## Context
R2 exit criterion #4 is a content requirement as much as an engineering one: "Every estimated view carries the (estimated) badge **and a popover explaining the heuristic and its failure modes**. A missing badge is a P1 bug, not cosmetic." SCR-058's sign-off checklist demands, per estimated signal, "what it infers, from what data, the exact heuristic and thresholds in force, the known failure modes, and what would be required to know it for certain", and that "the words 'this is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact' appear in each section".

The API schema `DetectorMethodology` requires `detector`, `inputs`, `assumption`, `false_positive_modes` (and optional `display_name`, `confidence_basis`) for each of `iceberg, stop_run, absorption, exhaustion, big_trade, regime`. This ticket writes that content - sourced from the E25-K01 calibration report and the shipped implementations - and lands the feature-flag configuration that keeps the heuristics off until they are trusted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Methodology content for every enum value of `DetectorMethodology.detector`, served by `GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology`, stored as versioned content in the repo (not in the database) so it is reviewed like code.
- For `big_trade` and `exhaustion`, coordinate the wording with E22 and E18 respectively rather than writing a competing description - one methodology entry per signal, app-wide.
- The `confidence_basis` string for `regime` stating exactly how confidence is computed (the normalised margin definition from E25-T05).
- Update the metric-vocabulary tables in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` so every DET metric code, its default params and its `exact`/`estimated` confidence are accurate against the shipped code.
- Feature flags `metrics.iceberg_detector`, `metrics.stop_run_detector`, `metrics.absorption` documented with their rollout criterion ("on only after E25-Q03 signs off the calibration") and wired so flipping a flag is audited (`config.changed`, `SYSTEM_CONFIG_EDIT`).
- A short ADR **only if** K01 concluded that a published `DetectorConfig` default must change; otherwise a note in the epic recording that the defaults were confirmed.
- Copy review by the design/content owner so SCR-058's plain-language-first requirement is met.

## Out of scope
The drawer UI (E25-S04), the settings UI (E25-S05), detector implementations, translation/localisation (single-locale app), marketing copy.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every estimated signal is documented
  When GET /api/v1/detectors/methodology is called
  Then it returns an entry for each of iceberg, stop_run, absorption, exhaustion, big_trade and regime
  And each entry has inputs, an assumption stated plainly, and at least two false-positive modes

Scenario: The honesty sentence is present
  Then each entry states that Bybit exposes no L3 or MBO data and that the value is an estimate, not exchange-provided fact

Scenario: Thresholds in force are shown
  Given the detector configuration has been changed from the defaults
  Then the drawer content combined with GET /detectors/config shows the values actually in force, not the documented defaults

Scenario: Vocabulary matches the code
  Then every DET metric code in docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md matches the code's registered metrics and its estimated flag, verified by an automated test

Scenario: Flags default off
  Then metrics.iceberg_detector, metrics.stop_run_detector and metrics.absorption default to false, and flipping any of them writes an audit record
```

## Technical notes / design
Content lives in `server/orderflow/methodology/*.md` with front-matter mapping to the schema fields; a loader validates at startup that every registered detector has a methodology entry and fails fast otherwise. That startup assertion is what makes "no estimated surface without an explanation" enforceable rather than aspirational.

Write for a trader, not for an engineer: the assumption first in one sentence, then the mechanism, then the failure modes, then "what would be required to know this for certain" (for iceberg: an L3/MBO feed with per-order identity, which Bybit does not publish).

An automated test compares the registry's metric list with the vocabulary table in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`, so documentation drift fails CI.

## Test plan
- Unit: loader rejects a detector with no methodology entry; every entry satisfies the `DetectorMethodology` schema; required phrase present in each entry.
- Contract: `/detectors/methodology` response validates against the OpenAPI schema.
- Docs-drift test: registered metric codes equal the documented vocabulary (codes, defaults, estimated flag).
- Manual: content review sign-off by the design/content owner and the M9 owner.

## Security notes
Methodology content is public-safe and must not leak internal infrastructure detail (host names, table names beyond what is already public in the plan docs, or exact rate limits that would help an adversary). Feature-flag flips are privileged (`SYSTEM_CONFIG_EDIT`) and audited as `config.changed`.

## Accessibility notes
Content must satisfy SCR-058: plain-language summary first, technical detail second, no jargon without a glossary link. Headings are properly nested so the drawer is navigable by heading; no meaning carried by formatting alone.

## Performance notes
Content is bundled/static; `/detectors/methodology` is served from memory. SCR-058 requires the drawer to open in <=150 ms with no streaming subscriptions.

title: Security review of the detector config write path and event bus
body:
## Context
Verification counterpart to E25-X01: a white-box review of the implemented controls on the two paths that matter - the detector configuration write path (browser -> `PUT /api/v1/detectors/config` -> config store -> live registry) and the detector event bus (detector -> event -> alert/rule engine), where a heuristic can reach an armed trading action.

`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a security review per feature alongside SAST/SCA/DAST. R2's security quality gate names E21 and E26 explicitly for STRIDE, but E25's write path is the one that touches trading behaviour, so it gets a dedicated review.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Code review of `PUT /detectors/config`: authentication, `settings:write` authorisation with scope, server-side bounds enforcement for every published range, rejection of unknown keys (`additionalProperties: false`), no mass assignment, rate limiting, and idempotent behaviour under retry.
- Verification that **every** accepted and rejected change writes an append-only audit record with actor, detector, key, before, after and symbol scope, and that the record cannot be updated or deleted.
- Verification that `DetectorEvent.estimated` and the acknowledgement flag are set on every heuristic event and are honoured at rule-arming time, satisfying US-DET-006's NFR ("never used as the sole trigger for an automated live action unless the user explicitly acknowledges the estimate").
- Verification of the DoS controls: `metrics[]` cap, REST backfill range bound, recompute rate limit, bounded per-price iceberg state and bounded event buffers.
- Verification that the SCR-059 armed-rule warning cannot be bypassed by calling the API directly - i.e. that the warning is a UX affordance over a server-side control, not the control itself; if it is the only control, that is a finding.
- RBAC test evidence: Viewer rejected, Manager/Owner per the RBAC matrix (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7).
- DAST (ZAP) scan of `/detectors/*` and `/market/metrics` and `/market/regime/explain`; SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL) findings triaged for the epic's modules; dependency scan for any new packages.
- Confirmation that error responses leak no internal detail.
- Findings filed with severity; all high and critical fixed before sign-off; residual risks accepted in writing.

## Out of scope
The threat model (E25-X01), penetration testing (pre-R4), the rule engine's internals (E35 has its own review), infrastructure hardening.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Authorisation is enforced server-side
  Given a Viewer-role session
  When PUT /api/v1/detectors/config is called directly, bypassing the UI
  Then the request is rejected with 403 and the attempt is logged

Scenario: Bounds cannot be bypassed
  When the API is called directly with values outside every published range
  Then each is rejected server-side with a validation error
  And no configuration change occurs

Scenario: Unknown keys rejected
  When the request body contains a key not present in DetectorConfig
  Then the request is rejected rather than the key being ignored

Scenario: Audit is complete and immutable
  Then every accepted and rejected change produces an append-only audit record containing actor, detector, key, before, after and scope
  And no code path updates or deletes those records

Scenario: Heuristics cannot silently arm a live action
  Given a rule armed on a detector event
  Then arming requires the explicit acknowledgement recorded for estimated detectors
  And the event carries its parameter snapshot for later attribution

Scenario: DoS caps hold
  Then the metrics selection cap, backfill range bound and recompute rate limit are enforced and return errors rather than degrading the service

Scenario: Scans clean
  Then DAST on the detector endpoints and SAST on the epic's modules produce no unresolved high or critical findings
```

## Technical notes / design
Attempt the bypasses directly against the API with a scripted client rather than through the UI; a control that only exists in the dialog is the specific failure this review is designed to catch, and it is an easy one to ship.

Check idempotency and races: two concurrent PUTs must not interleave into a mixed configuration, and the registry reconfigure must be atomic at an evaluation boundary (which is also a correctness property, per E25-T02).

## Test plan
Review plus targeted tests: RBAC matrix tests, direct-API bypass attempts, bounds fuzzing across every published range, concurrent-PUT race test, audit-immutability test, and the ZAP/Semgrep/Bandit runs. Tests that encode controls are merged into the permanent suite rather than run once.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security work. Data classification: configuration (internal), audit (security-relevant, append-only), market data (public). Findings of high or critical severity block E25-Q05 sign-off and therefore the R2 PRR.

## Accessibility notes
Confirm the armed-rule confirmation and validation messaging remain operable by keyboard and screen reader after any security-driven change.

## Performance notes
Confirm rate limits and caps are set so legitimate use is unaffected; measure the config read path's in-process caching so authorisation and validation do not add per-evaluation cost.

## Observability
Verify that rejected attempts, rate-limit trips and configuration changes are all observable (logs, metrics, audit) and that an operator could reconstruct who changed what and when, and which parameters were in force when a given detector event fired.

## Definition of Done
Review completed with findings filed; all high and critical findings fixed and re-verified; control tests merged into the permanent suite; DAST and SAST clean or triaged with written acceptance; RBAC evidence attached; residual risks accepted; security engineer sign-off recorded; result reported into E25-Q05 and the R2 PRR.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E25-X01 (the model that defines the controls), E25-T02 (the implemented write path) and E25-S05 (the dialog whose warning is verified). Blocks E25-Q05.

`chore/detectors-security-review`. PR size guidance: control tests plus the review report.
