title: Security review and sign-off of replay and simulated-trading isolation
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, for any epic labelled `security`, a finalised STRIDE model with findings triaged and a sign-off comment from the Security engineer; §8 makes the label mandatory regardless of whether it was applied at creation for anything touching order-placement paths — which E26-S07 does, by putting an order ticket in front of replayed market data.

This review is the last gate before E26-Q06 can record the epic QA sign-off.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Review the **shipped** implementation against the E26-X01 model: confirm every control exists where the model says it does, and that none was refactored away during implementation.
- Focused review of the **simulated-trading isolation** (E26-S07), the epic's highest-severity control:
  - `source="replay"` set at injection and non-removable downstream.
  - The OMS refusal is structural, not a UI check.
  - Replay fills persist with `is_paper=true` and `origin='replay_sim'`, in a separate replay journal, excluded from live and paper analytics by default.
  - Exports and journal promotion always carry the simulated flag; `journal.simulated_import` is audited.
  - Replay paper fills never enter the trading audit stream.
- Confirm **RBAC** enforcement: `replay:read` / `replay:write` with scope self on every operation, including the WS subscribe path, verified against the role matrix for Owner, Manager and Viewer.
- Confirm **path safety** (SR-097) in the shipped readers and that the E26-X02 tests genuinely exercise the production code path rather than a test double.
- Confirm the **resource-governance limits** are enabled by default in the shipped configuration, with their values recorded, and that disabling them requires a deliberate configuration change.
- Review SAST/SCA/secrets-scan results for the epic's code; triage each finding as fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off.
- Review the security-relevant sections of ADR-0018 so the decisions are recorded where a future maintainer will look.
- Post the **sign-off comment** with residual risks, accepted risks and any follow-ups for the pre-Live pen-test scope.

## Out of scope
- Implementing fixes (filed to owning tickets; P0/P1 findings block this sign-off).
- The programme pen-test (before Live enablement, R4) — this review contributes scope to it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Controls exist where the model says they do
  Given the E26-X01 model and the shipped code
  When each control is located in the implementation
  Then every control is present at the stated layer
  And any relocated or missing control is filed as a finding

Scenario: Isolation is structural and proven
  Given the simulated-trading path
  When the reviewer traces an order from ticket to matcher
  Then the refusal to route to an exchange depends on the source marker rather than on UI state
  And the adapter-level zero-call test is confirmed to exercise production code

Scenario: Limits ship enabled
  Given the deployed default configuration
  Then session quota, window cap, memory ceiling, idle reclaim and control-call rate limits are all enabled with recorded values

Scenario: Sign-off is conditional on a clean board
  When sign-off is attempted with an open P0 or P1 security finding
  Then it is refused until the finding is fixed or accepted by the Owner with a recorded rationale
```

## Technical notes / design
Pay particular attention to the seam between E26 and E38: the paper matcher is another epic's code, and isolation depends on both sides holding their end. The review must trace the full path rather than stopping at the E26 boundary.

## Test plan
Manual review plus confirmation that the E26-X02 suite is green against production code paths; a spot re-run of the highest-severity abuse cases in the reviewer's own environment.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security sign-off for the epic and is cited in the epic DoD and in the R2 PRR.

## Accessibility notes
Confirms the disclosure-channel check from E26-X02 was executed.

## Performance notes
Confirms the resource limits validated in E26-Q03 are the ones actually shipped.

## Observability
Confirms the security signals and their alert rules are deployed and firing correctly, especially the blocked-live-routing counter, which should be permanently zero and alarmed if it is not.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Review completed against the shipped implementation; every control located or filed as a finding.
- [ ] Isolation path traced end to end across the E26/E38 seam.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets findings triaged; no P0/P1 open.
- [ ] Shipped default limits recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted with residual and accepted risks and pen-test follow-ups.

`E26-X02` must be green; `E26-S07` is the primary subject; `E26-T07` supplies ADR-0018 and the observability the review confirms.

`chore/e26-security-review`.

title: Hi-fi design and design-system contributions for the accounts and key-vault surfaces
body:
## Context
Turns the E27-D02 wireframes into signed-off high-fidelity design and contributes the components this epic introduces or extends to the shared design system, so that no screen ships a one-off control.

The epic touches 24 catalogued components, but only three are substantially defined by it: **CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge** (the visual language of the withdrawal, scope and allowlist verdicts), **CMP-176 AccountKeyRow** (the admin accounts table row) and **CMP-034 MaskedValue**, which this epic redefines - the catalogue calls it "secret reveal", but in CandleViewer there is **no reveal control anywhere in the app or API** (US-ACCT-002), so the component must be specified as permanently masked and the misleading name annotated.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for every state from the E27-D02 inventory across SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079, in dark (default) and light themes and all three densities.
- Design-system contributions with token bindings from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`:
  - **CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge** - variants for verified, trade-only, read-only, withdrawal-detected (critical), IP-missing, IP-mismatch, expiring and expired; each distinguishable in greyscale and under both common colour-vision deficiencies; each carrying its own text label.
  - **CMP-176 AccountKeyRow** - the composite row with label, UID, environment, permission badge, allowlist state, key age and health chip, including its blocked and disabled variants.
  - **CMP-034 MaskedValue** - respecified as permanently masked with no reveal affordance, showing `...{last4}` only, with a note recording why the reveal variant is deliberately absent.
- Extensions documented, not forked, for CMP-028 Callout/Banner (the blocking KEK-unavailable banner), CMP-035 Countdown (the rotation overlap), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog (typed-label confirmation plus step-up), CMP-066 Stepper (the rotation wizard) and CMP-178 SystemHealthTile (per-key health).
- The final copy deck for all six screens, validated against the E27-D01 comprehension findings: the withdrawal verdict, the IP-mismatch remediation including the instruction to set the allowlist in Bybit's dashboard, the stale-balance badge, the irreversible-delete warning, the "revoke and leave positions" versus "flatten first" choice, and the write-only secret explanation.
- Storybook story list per contributed component, handed to engineering.

## Out of scope
Motion specification (E27-D04); the a11y audit of the built screens (E27-D05); the handoff pack (E27-D06); design QA of the implementation (E27-D07); implementation itself.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Hi-fi covers both themes and all densities
  When the frame set is reviewed
  Then every state from the E27-D02 inventory exists in dark and light, and compact, cosy and comfortable densities are specified

Scenario: Key states survive greyscale and colour-vision deficiency
  Given the CMP-175 variants rendered in greyscale and under deuteranopia and protanopia simulation
  When they are compared
  Then each remains distinguishable and each carries a text label rather than relying on colour

Scenario: Withdrawal-detected reads as blocking
  Given the withdrawal-permission-detected state beside the ordinary warning states
  When a reviewer who has not seen the designs before is shown the accounts list
  Then they identify the blocking state without prompting

Scenario: MaskedValue has no reveal
  When CMP-034's specification is reviewed
  Then it defines no reveal affordance in any variant, and the rationale is recorded in the component entry

Scenario: Contrast
  When every text and graphical element is measured in both themes
  Then text is at least 4.5:1 and graphical boundaries at least 3:1 against their background

Scenario: A frame needs an element with no CMP entry
  Given a frame requires a control that does not exist in the catalogue
  Then a design-system contribution is raised and resolved before sign-off, and no one-off component ships
```

## Technical notes / design
All colour comes from tokens in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; nothing is hand-picked. The critical and warning states must be built from the existing `color.status.*` scale, extended through the design system if the scale proves insufficient rather than overridden locally.

Density matters more than usual on SCR-128, which is a table of keys with several state columns; the compact density must remain legible at 125% zoom.

Copy is part of this deliverable, not a later concern: this epic's screens are mostly explanation, and the E27-D01 comprehension findings determine the wording. Every string is written in the copy deck with its screen and element ID so engineering does not invent text.

## Test plan
Contrast measured with the design-system plugin on every foreground and background pair. Greyscale and colour-vision-deficiency simulation passes for all CMP-175 variants. The frame set is reviewed against each screen's own design sign-off acceptance checklist in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, and the review comment ticks them item by item. Copy is re-tested for comprehension with at least two people who were not in the E27-D01 sessions.

## Security notes
The visual language is a security control here. Misrepresentation is the threat: a withdrawal-detected state that reads as a mild warning, a stale balance that reads as current, or a masked value that implies a reveal is available would each cause a wrong decision. The Security engineer reviews and signs off the CMP-175 variant set and the SCR-126, SCR-127 and SCR-128 copy. No real UID, key or IP appears in any frame.

## Accessibility notes
Every state distinction is carried by text plus shape, never colour alone. Focus indicators are specified at >=3:1 contrast against both adjacent colours. Touch and click targets meet the minimum size in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. The permanently masked value has a programmatic description explaining that the value is write-only and cannot be revealed. Live-region behaviour specified for the health chips, the rotation countdown and exchange error messages. The layout is verified at 125% zoom and 200% text scaling without loss of content or function.

## Performance notes
Specify skeleton and loading treatments consistent with the perceived-performance budgets recorded in E27-D02, especially the SCR-126 validating state (<=3 s) and the SCR-129 consequence summary (<=1 s) during which the confirm control must not be present.

## Observability
No runtime telemetry. The frames carry the audit and analytics annotations inherited from E27-D02 so that engineering implements them without re-deriving.

title: Specify motion and state-transition choreography for key verification, rotation and danger states
body:
## Context
This epic's screens are mostly about state changing over time - a connection test progressing check by check, a rotation moving through stages with a countdown, a health chip degrading, a balance going stale - and motion is how a user understands that something changed rather than that they misread it.

Motion here also carries risk: an animated transition on a destructive confirmation can make a dangerous action feel routine, and a spinner that hides per-check progress on SCR-126 turns a 3-second verification into an unexplained wait.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion specification for: the SCR-126 connection test revealing its checks progressively; the SCR-127 stepper advancing and rolling back; the CMP-035 rotation countdown; health-chip transitions on SCR-125 between healthy, degraded and down; the balance going stale on SCR-079; and the blocking KEK-unavailable banner appearing.
- Explicit anti-motion rules: destructive confirmations (SCR-129, revoke, mark-compromised) appear without decorative animation; the withdrawal-detected state does not fade in gently; nothing about a blocking error is soft.
- Durations, easing curves and stagger values expressed as design-system motion tokens, not one-off numbers.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for every specified transition: what becomes an instant state change and what, if anything, is retained as a non-motion cue.
- A statement of what must **not** animate: numeric balances never tween between values, because an intermediate frame of a balance is a number that was never true.

## Out of scope
Visual design (E27-D03); implementation; chart-engine animation, which is governed separately by `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`; motion for screens outside this epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every transition has a token-based specification
  When the motion spec is reviewed
  Then each listed transition has a duration, easing and stagger expressed in design-system motion tokens

Scenario: Reduced motion is complete
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  When each transition is reviewed
  Then each has a defined non-animated equivalent that preserves the information the motion conveyed

Scenario: Danger is not softened
  When the destructive confirmations are reviewed
  Then none uses decorative motion, and the blocking withdrawal-detected state appears immediately

Scenario: Balances never tween
  When the balance update specification is reviewed
  Then values change discretely, and no intermediate interpolated value is ever displayed

Scenario: Progressive verification is legible
  Given the connection test takes 3 seconds
  When the motion spec is applied
  Then each completed check is revealed as it completes rather than all at once at the end
```

## Technical notes / design
Motion tokens come from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`. Durations stay short - the guidance for functional state feedback is well under 200 ms - so that a user performing several key operations in sequence is never waiting on choreography.

The progressive reveal of verification checks is driven by real backend progress, not a simulated timeline; if the backend returns all checks at once, the reveal is a single step rather than a fake stagger, because a fabricated progress animation is a lie about system state.

## Test plan
Prototype the transitions in Figma and review them at 1x speed with engineering present. Verify the reduced-motion variants by walking every transition with the preference simulated. Confirm with engineering that each specified transition is implementable with CSS transitions or the existing animation utility, without a new dependency.

## Security notes
Motion must not be used to soften a security-relevant state. The specification explicitly forbids fading in the withdrawal-detected banner, animating the destructive confirmation entrance, or using motion to draw attention away from a failed check. Reviewed by the Security engineer alongside E27-D03.

## Accessibility notes
`prefers-reduced-motion` support is mandatory per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, and every transition here has a defined reduced equivalent. No transition may be the only indication that something changed - each is paired with a text or live-region change, so a user who cannot perceive motion loses nothing. No flashing above the seizure-safety threshold.

## Performance notes
Transitions are CSS-driven, composited properties only (transform and opacity), so they never trigger layout. Nothing in this epic animates per frame or competes with the chart's frame budget. Motion must not delay the availability of a control: an element is interactive from the start of its entrance.

## Observability
N/A - motion produces no telemetry.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma frames complete for every state listed in Scope, in dark and light themes and all three densities (compact/cosy/comfortable).
- [ ] Design-system contributions merged into the shared library with token bindings from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; zero one-off components.

title: Accessibility design review of the six accounts and key-vault surfaces
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA as the floor, with axe-core in CI and manual screen-reader passes. This epic is unusually dependent on getting accessibility right at design time rather than fixing it later, because its screens communicate consequential state - a key that can withdraw, a balance that is stale, an account that cannot trade - and every one of those is the kind of thing that is usually conveyed by colour alone.

The screens catalogue already fixes several requirements per screen (text chips on SCR-125, a result list rather than a colour on SCR-126, a labelled stepper with `aria-current` on SCR-127, plain-sentence policy text on SCR-128, an `alertdialog` with focus starting on Cancel on SCR-129, a description list with units on SCR-079). This review verifies that the hi-fi design actually satisfies them before a line of code is written.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Annotated accessibility review of every hi-fi frame from E27-D03, producing a defect list with a named owner and a resolution for each item.
- Verification per screen against its catalogue requirement: SCR-125 text chips and explicit withdrawal verdict; SCR-126 write-only field description and result-as-list; SCR-127 stepper regions with `aria-current="step"`; SCR-128 plain-sentence policy and text-plus-icon warnings; SCR-129 `alertdialog` with the consequences restated as a list, typed confirmation and focus starting on Cancel; SCR-079 heading naming account and environment, balances as a description list with units, permission summary as plain statements.
- Focus-order map per screen and per dialog, including where focus goes on open, on close, on error and on step change.
- Live-region plan: what is announced politely (health transitions, countdown milestones), what assertively (exchange errors, blocking banners, failed checks), and what is not announced at all to avoid chatter.
- Keyboard-only walkthrough of every flow: register an account, import a key, run a test, rotate, revoke, disable, delete, change leverage - each completable with no pointer.
- Contrast audit results for every state in both themes, including focus indicators and disabled states.
- Screen-reader script: the expected announcement for each critical state, written out, so that the manual pass in E27-Q04 has a pass criterion rather than an opinion.

## Out of scope
The automated axe-core run against the built screens (E27-Q04); implementation fixes; accessibility work on screens outside this epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue a11y requirement is verified
  Given the per-screen accessibility requirements in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the hi-fi frames are reviewed
  Then each requirement is confirmed satisfied or raised as a defect with an owner

Scenario: No state relies on colour alone
  Given every state across the six screens
  When each is rendered in greyscale
  Then every state remains identifiable from text and shape

Scenario: Keyboard-only completion
  Given each of the eight flows in scope
  When they are walked with keyboard only in the prototype
  Then each completes without a pointer, and any trap or unreachable control is raised as a defect

Scenario: Focus starts safely on destructive dialogs
  When the SCR-129 dialog is reviewed
  Then focus starts on Cancel and the dialog uses role alertdialog with the consequences restated as a list

Scenario: Announcements are specified, not assumed
  When the live-region plan is reviewed
  Then every critical state has an expected announcement written out, and the politeness level is justified

Scenario: A requirement cannot be met as designed
  Given a frame that cannot satisfy a WCAG 2.2 AA criterion
  Then the design is changed, not waived, and the change is re-reviewed before sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Review method: heuristic evaluation against WCAG 2.2 AA using the project's standard checklist, plus a prototype walkthrough. The reviewer is an accessibility specialist from the design org, not the designer who produced the frames.

The live-region plan needs judgement rather than maximalism: this epic has several things that change on a timer (heartbeat age, countdown, staleness), and announcing all of them would make the screen unusable with a screen reader. The plan must state explicitly what is deliberately silent and why, with the information available on demand instead.

## Test plan
Contrast measured on every pair including focus and disabled states. Keyboard walkthrough executed and recorded. The screen-reader script is validated against at least one real screen reader on the prototype where feasible (NVDA on Windows is the project's primary target), with the full pass deferred to E27-Q04 on the built screens.

## Security notes
Two intersections with security matter here. First, the write-only secret field must have a programmatic description saying the value cannot be revealed, so that a screen-reader user is not left hunting for a reveal control that does not exist. Second, destructive confirmations must be equally clear non-visually: the consequences list, the typed-label requirement and the irreversibility must all be announced, so that a non-visual user is not at greater risk of an accidental deletion.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is itself the accessibility deliverable; see Scope. The output is the pass criterion used by E27-Q04's manual screen-reader audit and by E27-D07's design QA.

## Performance notes
Announcement frequency is a performance concern for assistive technology: the live-region plan caps announcements so that throttled updates (`wallet` at 500 ms, `system` at 1000 ms) do not produce a stream of speech. Only discrete transitions are announced, never every tick.

## Observability
N/A - no telemetry. The review does record which states must be observable in the UI for an operator to diagnose an issue without reading logs.

- [ ] Figma frames complete for every state listed in Scope, in dark and light themes and all three densities (compact/cosy/comfortable).
- [ ] Design-system contributions merged into the shared library with token bindings from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; zero one-off components.

title: Produce and sign off the engineering handoff pack for the accounts and key-vault epic
body:
## Context
The design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` is explicit: no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off, with Status Done on the design ticket. This is the ticket whose completion unblocks E27-S01 through E27-S05, so it must be genuinely complete - a developer picking up SCR-126 should not need to ask a designer anything.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A single handoff pack covering SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079, linked from every consuming engineering ticket.
- Per screen: the final frame set with every state, redlines or the equivalent token annotations, the component inventory naming each CMP ID used, the data sources (exact API paths and WS topics), the RBAC requirement, and the audit and analytics events to emit.
- The final copy deck with every string keyed by screen and element, including all error and empty-state text, so no text is invented during implementation.
- The contributed design-system entries for CMP-175, CMP-176 and CMP-034 published in the library with their Storybook story lists.
- The focus-order maps, live-region plan and screen-reader scripts from E27-D05.
- The motion specification from E27-D04 with its reduced-motion equivalents.
- A written statement of the epic's non-negotiable visual rules: no reveal control for secrets anywhere; the withdrawal verdict is always explicit; no numeric value is shown without its freshness; destructive actions require typed confirmation plus step-up.
- A 45-minute handoff walkthrough with the frontend engineers who will build the screens, with questions captured and answered in the pack rather than in chat.
- A sign-off record listing the Chief Design Officer or delegate, the accessibility specialist and the Security engineer.

## Out of scope
Design QA of the built implementation (E27-D07); changes arising from implementation discoveries, which are handled as follow-up design tickets; implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The pack is self-sufficient
  Given a frontend engineer who has not attended any design review
  When they build SCR-126 from the pack alone
  Then they need no clarification from the design team, evidenced by zero design questions raised during the ticket

Scenario: Every string is in the copy deck
  When the implementation is compared to the copy deck
  Then every rendered string is present in the deck and no string was invented during implementation

Scenario: Sign-offs are complete before engineering starts
  When E27-S01 enters In Progress
  Then this ticket is already Done with all three sign-offs recorded, at least two sprints earlier

Scenario: Components come from the library
  When the built screens are inspected
  Then every control resolves to a catalogued CMP entry, and no one-off component exists

Scenario: A gap is found during implementation
  Given an engineer finds a state with no frame
  Then a follow-up design ticket is raised, the pack is updated, and the gap is recorded so the handoff checklist can be improved
```

## Technical notes / design
The pack lives in Figma with a committed index under `docs/design/e27/handoff.md` that links each screen to its frames, its copy-deck section and its component entries - so the authoritative pointer survives even if the Figma structure is reorganised.

Redlines are minimised in favour of token references: an engineer should read "spacing.md, color.status.critical" rather than a pixel value, because that is what makes the implementation stay consistent when tokens change.

## Test plan
Validation is the handoff walkthrough itself plus the self-sufficiency criterion above: design questions raised during E27-S01 to E27-S05 are counted, and any question that should have been answered by the pack is logged as an improvement to the handoff checklist. A link-checker validates every reference in the committed index.

## Security notes
The pack restates the epic's security-relevant visual rules explicitly, so that an engineer cannot implement a reveal affordance, a colour-only withdrawal verdict or a freshness-free balance by accident. The Security engineer's sign-off on the pack is required, not optional.

## Accessibility notes
The pack carries the full E27-D05 output - focus-order maps, live-region plan and screen-reader scripts - so that accessibility is implemented from a specification rather than retrofitted after an axe-core failure.

## Performance notes
The pack records the perceived-performance budgets per screen: SCR-126 <=3 s test round-trip with a validating state, SCR-127 <=10 s rotation with per-stage timing, SCR-129 <=1 s consequence summary before the confirm control appears, SCR-079 <=100 ms open from cache, SCR-125 health refresh every 60 s and never per second.

## Observability
The pack lists, per screen, the audit events (`account.created`, `account.updated`, `account.tested`, `account.disabled_by_policy`, `account.key_rotated`, `account.key_revoked`, `admin.secrets_policy_changed`, `admin.key_marked_compromised`) and the analytics events (`admin.accounts_list_viewed`, `admin.key_form_opened`, `admin.key_test_run`, `admin.key_health_viewed`, `account.detail_viewed`) that implementation must emit.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma frames complete for every state listed in Scope, in dark and light themes and all three densities (compact/cosy/comfortable).
- [ ] Design-system contributions merged into the shared library with token bindings from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; zero one-off components.
- [ ] Accessibility annotations present: focus order, roles, live regions, measured contrast (text >=4.5:1, graphical >=3:1).
- [ ] The screen's own design sign-off acceptance checklist in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is fully ticked, item by item, in the review comment.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer or delegate, plus the Security engineer for any frame that renders key state.
- [ ] Ticket Status = Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming frontend story starts (design-ahead rule, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`).
- [ ] Handoff pack linked from every consuming engineering ticket.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-D03**, **E27-D04** and **E27-D05**. Blocks **E27-S01**, **E27-S02**, **E27-S03**, **E27-S04** and **E27-S05** - this is the design-ahead gate for the epic.

## Branch
`design/e27-handoff` - committed index and copy deck under `docs/design/e27/`; the frames live in Figma.

## References

title: UX research: how the owner sets risk policy per account and thinks about fan-out
body:
## Context
E28 introduces five screens the product has never had - SCR-130 profiles list, SCR-131 profile editor, SCR-132 templates, SCR-133 symbol permissions matrix and SCR-062 trade-group manager - plus the preview half of SCR-061. All six express a mental model nobody has validated: that a trader thinks of "policy per account" as a durable object, and of a set of accounts as one tradable unit.

The risk of getting this wrong is concrete. SCR-131 requires "every field has units and a worked example" precisely because a sizing rule is abstract until it produces a number; if the worked example does not match how the owner reasons ("how much do I lose if this stop hits?"), the editor will be filled in wrongly and the resulting orders will be the wrong size. Equally, US-PROF-005's "2 of 3 ready" only makes sense if users expect a group to fan out partially rather than fail whole.

This is generative research ahead of wireframes, run two sprints before the wireframe ticket, consistent with the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 4-6 interviews: the owner (primary persona) plus account managers from `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, each 45 minutes, remote, recorded with consent.
- Topic guide covering: how risk per account is decided today (spreadsheet? habit? per trade?); which sizing rule is the default mental model and which is a fallback; what "max daily loss" means to them - realised only, or including open positions; whether a group is a saved thing or an ad hoc multi-select; expectations when one account of a group cannot trade; what makes an override feel exceptional rather than routine.
- Concept test of two alternative framings for the worked example: "risk in USDT" versus "risk in R", and whether both are needed simultaneously (US-PROF-002 asks for both).
- Card sort of the SCR-131 field set into the six proposed sections (Leverage & margin, Sizing, Brackets, Risk caps, Symbols, Safety) to validate the grouping before it is drawn.
- Findings report with themes, verbatim quotes, and a prioritised list of design implications, each tagged to the screen it affects.
- Explicit answers to three questions that block the wireframes: (1) is the profile list per account or per profile; (2) does a group need an armed-for-live flag distinct from the global arm control; (3) is the symbol matrix's default state allow-all or deny-all.
- A short research-debt note listing what was *not* answered and which later ticket must answer it.

## Out of scope
Any visual design, wireframe or prototype (E28-D02 onward); usability testing of built software (E28-Q04's exploratory charter covers that).

## Acceptance criteria
- At least four sessions completed and synthesised, including the owner.
- The three blocking questions each have a recorded answer with the evidence behind it, or an explicit "no signal - designer's call" with the reason.
- The card sort produces a section grouping that is either the proposed one or a documented alternative, and the chosen grouping is what E28-D02 draws.
- Findings are linked from the SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133 and SCR-062 entries in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Presented at a Design Review with the Chief Design Officer, the Owner and the consuming frontend lead present; decisions recorded in the ticket.

## Technical notes / design
Sessions use a paper-and-whiteboard protocol so participants are not anchored by an existing UI. The worked-example concept test uses two static cards with the same underlying numbers presented differently; order is counterbalanced across participants.

Consent and recording follow the same handling as E27-D01: no real API keys, UIDs or balances appear in any artefact, and recordings are stored in the project's research drive, not in the repository.

## Test plan
N/A - research, not software. Validity is protected by the counterbalanced concept test and by having a second researcher review the synthesis for interpretation bias.

## Security notes
No production data, keys or balances are shown or collected. Screenshots used as stimuli are synthetic. Recordings are Confidential and are retained only until the findings are signed off, then deleted; the deletion is recorded on the ticket.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session is run with a participant using keyboard-only navigation or a screen reader where available; if no such participant can be recruited, that gap is recorded as research debt and compensated by the dedicated a11y design review (E28-D05).

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

title: Wireframe SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133, SCR-062 and the SCR-061 preview with every state
body:
## Context
This is the structural design pass for every surface E28 introduces or changes. Each screen already has a catalogue entry in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` with its type, route, data sources, validation rules, states, components and a sign-off checklist - the wireframes must satisfy those entries rather than reinvent them, and where a wireframe departs from the catalogue, the catalogue is updated in the same PR.

Six surfaces are in scope: **SCR-130** (profiles list, `/admin/profiles`), **SCR-131** (profile editor, six sections), **SCR-132** (profile templates modal), **SCR-133** (symbol permissions matrix), **SCR-062** (trade-group manager, `/admin/trade-groups`) and the **preview half of SCR-061** (trade-group ticket) - the fan-out send, partial-failure and rate-limit states of SCR-061 belong to E34's design work and are explicitly excluded here to avoid two teams drawing the same screen.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Low-fidelity wireframes for all six surfaces, at desktop width first, with the density model from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- **Every state** enumerated by each catalogue entry, drawn - not described: loading, empty, populated, validating, error, forbidden, and each screen's specific states (SCR-130's unbound-account and allows-all-symbols warnings; SCR-131's validation-blocked and step-up states; SCR-132's live-account acknowledgement; SCR-133's locked cell with an open position and its unsaved-changes summary; SCR-062's degraded "state unknown for sub_002" and its N-of-M readiness; SCR-061's previewing, ready, warn, excluded, blocked and stale-preview states).
- SCR-131's worked example drawn as a first-class element, not a footnote, in the form the research chose (risk in USDT and in R), with its position relative to the sizing controls settled.
- SCR-131's Safety section drawing `require_native_sl` as a permanent floor - a control that visibly cannot be turned off, not a toggle that fails on save.
- SCR-133's grid drawn with sticky row and column headers, the three cell states (allowed, denied, denied-and-locked) distinguished by glyph and text, and the bulk row/column affordances.
- SCR-062 drawn with row expansion to per-account legs and the readiness strip.
- SCR-061's preview table drawn exactly to the catalogue's column set (`acct | profile | qty | lev | SL | ok`) with an inline WARN reason row and an excluded row stating its reason.
- Error and validation copy drafted for every rule named in the catalogue entries, including the exact strings the catalogue already fixes ("These accounts have no symbol in common - the group can't trade anything.", "SOLUSDT allows at most 20x - your 25x would be rejected", "sub_003 excluded: symbol not allowed by profile").
- A component inventory per screen mapping every element to a CMP id from `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`, with any gap raised as a design-system contribution in E28-D03 rather than drawn as a one-off.
- Annotated flows: create profile, apply template, edit symbol permissions in bulk, create group, preview a fan-out.

## Out of scope
Hi-fi visual design, tokens and motion (E28-D03, E28-D04); SCR-061's send, partial-failure, retry and rate-limit states (**E34**'s design); SCR-060 single-account ticket (**E30**).

## Acceptance criteria
- All six surfaces wireframed with every catalogue-listed state drawn and labelled.
- Every element maps to an existing CMP id, or the gap is listed explicitly for E28-D03 to resolve with the design-system team.
- Error and validation copy exists for every validation rule listed in the six catalogue entries; no rule is left without a message.
- The wireframes are walked through with the backend lead to confirm every displayed value is actually available from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` - nothing is drawn that cannot be fetched.
- Reviewed at a Design Review with the Owner present; feedback resolved or logged.
- Any divergence from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is landed as an update to that document in the same change.

## Technical notes / design
The profiles list and the symbol matrix are two views of the same underlying allow-list; the wireframes must make the relationship obvious (a link from a row's symbol count to the matrix filtered to that account) rather than presenting them as unrelated screens.

The editor's two-layer validation (shape on blur, exchange limits on save) has a visible consequence: some errors appear immediately and some only on save. The wireframes must show how the later class is surfaced without feeling like a rejection out of nowhere - an explicit "check limits" affordance is one option to draw.

## Test plan
N/A - design artefact. Validation is the walkthrough with engineering and the Design Review sign-off.

## Security notes
No real account labels, UIDs, balances or keys appear in any frame - synthetic data only, matching the placeholder convention used in the catalogue. The step-up gate on save is drawn explicitly because a design that omits it invites an implementation that omits it. Screens must not display any secret; this is verified in copy review.

## Accessibility notes
Wireframes carry the accessibility annotations the catalogue demands: SCR-133's cells are checkboxes with names combining account and symbol; SCR-062's group state is text not a colour pill; SCR-061's row status is text and its send button names the account count; SCR-131's fields carry units and a worked example. Focus order is annotated per screen. Anything conveyed by colour has a text or glyph equivalent drawn alongside it, not promised for later.

## Performance notes
The wireframes must respect the performance constraints the catalogue states, because they are layout constraints: SCR-133's grid is virtualised over ~400 symbols, and SCR-062's grid is virtualised for 50 groups x 5 legs. A design that requires rendering everything at once is not acceptable.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-078 fills detail and the reconciling/desync states on SCR-152
body:
## Context
US-POS-005 and US-POS-009 need a fills surface (SCR-078), and US-POS-008 needs the app to tell the truth when it has just been corrected by the exchange — which is the reconciling/desync variant of SCR-152 plus the per-panel stale treatment (CMP-078 StaleDataShade).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Figma frames for **SCR-078 Fills / executions detail** (drawer): per-fill rows (time, price, qty, fee, fee currency, maker/taker, order id, exec id, trade group, causing rule, journal link), aggregation to an average price with maker/taker split, slippage vs intended price where an intent exists, fan-out grouping by account, CSV export, empty state — satisfying the SCR-078 sign-off checklist.
- Figma frames for the **reconciling** and **desync** states used by E29: the SCR-152 banner variant ("Reconciling with the exchange…"), the SCR-063 amber desync banner ("Position data is being verified — actions temporarily limited"), the per-account **stale** treatment that disables order entry for that account after repeated reconciliation failure (US-POS-008 scenario 3), and the post-reconnect summary ("While you were offline: 1 order filled, 1 stop moved by a rule").
- Copy deck for every message above, reviewed with the Owner; wording must name which value is now authoritative.

## Out of scope
SCR-063 itself (D02); the connection/reconnect machinery visuals owned by the platform epics — this ticket only adds the OMS-specific variants.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Correction is explained, not hidden
  Given local state was corrected by reconciliation
  Then the design shows both the previous and the corrected value and states that the exchange is authoritative

Scenario: Stale account blocks entry visibly
  Given reconciliation has failed for 2 minutes on account B
  Then account B's rows are marked stale and every order-entry control for it is drawn disabled with the reason in text

Scenario: Fills drawer sign-off checklist satisfied
  When the CDO reviews SCR-078 against its catalogue checklist
  Then all six items pass
```

## Technical notes / design
Reuse CMP-028 Callout, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-049 Table, CMP-076/077/078, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-116 PnLBadge. No new components unless raised into D04.

## Test plan
Design review + copy review with the Owner; verified by D07 and by Q02 E2E assertions on the exact strings.

## Security notes
Fills expose financial data only; no key material, no exchange signature, and order diagnostics deep-links must be marked as audited-on-read.

## Accessibility notes
Banner is `role="alert"` once then persistent; countdowns are not announced per tick; fee/funding values carry sign and currency in the accessible name.

## Performance notes
Fills list is virtualised and coalesced to 5 Hz; 1 000-fill session must render without exceeding 4 ms scripting per frame — the design must not require per-row measurement.

## Observability
Spec marks `execution.detail_viewed`, `execution.exported` analytics events.

body:
## Context

## Scope / Deliverables
- Design-system entries, props and states for: **CMP-114 PositionsGrid** (extends CMP-049 with liq-proximity warning rows), **CMP-115 OrderRow** (incl. pending/optimistic and rejected variants), **CMP-116 PnLBadge** (sign, currency, R-multiple), **CMP-123 FlattenAllButton** (destructive, hold-to-confirm variant), **CMP-129 PositionModeToggle** (one-way/hedge, disabled-with-reason variant), plus the reuse contract for **CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect**.

## Context
A dense, high-frequency financial grid is one of the hardest a11y surfaces in the product, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 explicitly removes any "internal tool" exemption. Reviewing at design time is far cheaper than retrofitting after S16.

- WCAG 2.2 AA design review of SCR-063, SCR-078 and the reconciling/desync/stale states, producing a written findings list with severity and an owner per finding.

The implementation audit (E29-Q05) and axe-core wiring (CI, E03).

title: UX research: how traders decide, size and fire an order under time pressure
body:
## Context
The order ticket is the only screen in CandleViewer where a wrong pixel costs money. Before we draw it we need evidence about three things the screens catalogue currently asserts rather than proves: (1) what a trader actually looks at in the two seconds before submitting; (2) how they expect an *armed* state to feel different from a locked one; (3) what they do when an order is rejected â€” re-read, retry, or abandon.

This research also has to test a decision that is already locked and cannot be changed by the findings: the **mandatory native stop-loss** and the **arm/lock + environment badge** requirement. Research here is about making those legible and fast, not about relitigating them. That framing goes in the discussion guide explicitly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 5â€“6 moderated sessions (the owner plus account managers and, where available, comparable discretionary futures traders), 60 min each, remote, recorded with consent.
- Comparative walkthroughs of TradingView's ticket, Bookmap's arm pattern and Bybit's own web ticket, using the participant's own strategy as the task frame.
- Two concept probes: (a) arm/lock treatments â€” persistent badge vs. banner vs. tinted chrome; (b) sizing-mode switching â€” segmented control vs. mode-per-field.
- A timed task: "size this trade to risk 0.5% with a stop under that swing low, then place it" â€” measured to establish the baseline the 8 ms/50 ms budgets serve.
- Deliverable: a findings report in `docs/plan/` research notes format with prioritised implications, a quote bank, and an explicit list of questions the research could **not** answer (to be resolved by design QA or by the E30-Q06 exploratory charter).

## Out of scope
Visual design, any Figma file, chart/DOM trading interactions (E31 has its own research ticket E31-D01 â€” coordinate to avoid double-recruiting the same participants in the same fortnight), rule-engine authoring (E36/E37).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Evidence exists for each design decision that follows
  When E30-D02 begins
  Then each of its major layout decisions cites a finding, or is explicitly marked as a designer judgement with no evidence
Scenario: The locked decisions are tested for legibility, not for acceptance
  Then the report states how quickly and reliably participants could tell armed from locked and demo from live
  And it does not recommend removing either control
Scenario: Failure behaviour is characterised
  Then the report describes what participants did after a rejection and what information they looked for first
```

## Technical notes / design
Sessions run against a clickable stimulus, not the live app, so participants cannot place real orders. Consent covers recording and internal use only. Participants are told the product is self-hosted and single-owner so they do not reason about multi-tenant concerns that do not exist here.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Quality bar: two researchers independently affinity-map the sessions and reconcile; findings with only a single participant behind them are labelled as signals, not findings.

## Security notes
No participant sees real account data, balances or API keys; the stimulus uses fixture data. Recordings are stored in the internal drive with access limited to the design and product group and deleted after the Epic closes.

## Accessibility notes
At least one participant uses the product with keyboard-only navigation, and the discussion guide includes a keyboard-only pass of the placement task, so the a11y requirements in `05-accessibility-standard.md` are informed by a real user rather than only by audit.

## Performance notes
The timed sizing task establishes the human baseline the `8 ms` recompute and `50 ms` hotkey budgets are meant to protect; the report states the observed human times so engineering knows what headroom actually matters.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] 5â€“6 sessions completed and recorded.
- [ ] Findings report published with prioritised implications and a quote bank.
- [ ] Open questions listed explicitly with an owner for each.
- [ ] Read-out held with product, design and the E30 engineering lead.
- [ ] CDO sign-off that the findings are sufficient to start E30-D02.

## Dependencies
- **E27**, **E28** â€” participants must understand the account/profile model to reason about targets and limits.

title: Run UX research on bracket, ladder and mandatory-stop mental models
body:
## Context
E32 introduces three interaction models the product has never had, each with a known failure mode in trading tools: a **bracket** the user must understand as one object rather than three orders; a **generated ladder** whose child orders the user never types individually and therefore may not trust; and a **stop the system guarantees and the user may only tighten**, which is a constraint users typically experience as the app fighting them unless the rationale is visible.

The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`; `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1) requires design Done >=2 sprints before the consuming FE stories, which land in S17 — so research runs in S13. This ticket exists because SCR-064/065/069 each carry design sign-off checklists with items that cannot be answered from first principles: *what must the user see to trust a generated ladder*, and *how should a non-removable stop be expressed so it reads as protection rather than obstruction*.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 5-6 moderated sessions with the owner plus account managers matching the personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, 45 minutes each.
- Stimulus: competitor bracket/ladder UIs and two paper prototypes of the non-removable stop (hard-lock versus explain-and-restore).
- Research questions: (1) Do users read a bracket as one object, and what representation makes the relationship obvious? (2) What columns and totals must a ladder preview show before users will submit it unseen? (3) How should "native exchange-side" versus "engine-managed" be expressed so the residual risk of engine-managed stops is understood? (4) Is the R-multiple or the account-currency figure the primary risk reference, and which should lead? (5) What do users expect when a stop is cleared?
- Deliverable: a findings report in `docs/design/research/e32-brackets-ladders.md` with prioritised implications, verbatim quotes, and an explicit recommendation for each of the five questions.
- A one-page "mental model" summary consumed directly by E32-D02's wireframes.

```gherkin
Scenario: The non-removable stop has a chosen expression
  Given both paper prototypes were tested
  Then the report recommends one of hard-lock or explain-and-restore, states the evidence, and specifies the exact copy pattern for the chosen option

Scenario: A contradicted assumption is recorded, not buried (edge)

  Then the report states the contradiction explicitly and files a design change request against E32-D02 rather than proceeding as planned
```

Sessions run against clickable paper prototypes on demo data only; no live or demo account is connected. Recordings stored per the research-data handling policy in `04-security-program.md` and deleted after the report is accepted.

## Test plan
N/A — research. Quality bar: at least 5 completed sessions, findings triangulated across at least 3 participants before any recommendation is made.

## Security notes
Participant recordings may contain account balances or symbol preferences; they are stored in the restricted research space, redacted in the published report, and deleted after acceptance. No API keys or credentials are shown in any stimulus.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session runs with a participant using keyboard-only navigation so the keyboard-equivalence requirement for SCR-064 is grounded in observation rather than assumption.

N/A.

N/A.

- [ ] Reviewed with the CDO and the E32 engineering lead; sign-off recorded.
- [ ] Recordings handled and deleted per policy.

None — this is the first E32 design ticket and deliberately starts 4 sprints before the consuming FE work.

title: UX research: how rule authors reason about a node graph vs a condition list
body:
## Context
E37 introduces SCR-082, the product's only free-form 2D authoring canvas. It is a genuinely new interaction for this product: every other authoring surface (order ticket, profiles, the E36 form editor) is a linear form. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-RULE-005 asserts the graph exists so "complex logic is easier to see", but we have no evidence about *which* logic the owner and the manager persona actually find hard to read in the form, nor about how they expect a graph to behave (dataflow-like, or a visual syntax for one boolean tree + action list, which is what ADR-0007 actually delivers).

Getting this wrong is expensive twice over: the canvas is the most costly surface to build, and per `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 it is the second-highest accessibility risk in the product. The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence) requires this research to conclude before D02 draws anything, and at least two sprints ahead of the Sprint 17 frontend work. This ticket therefore runs in **Sprint 13**, in parallel with E36-D01 (form-editor research) so the same participants can be asked about both authoring surfaces in one session series, and so the whole E37 design chain can finish by the end of Sprint 15.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Semi-structured sessions (45 min, >=3 participants across the P1 Owner and P2 Manager personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, including at least one participant who prefers keyboard-first operation) covering: which real rules they want, how they currently express "A AND (B OR C)", what they expect a node to *be*, and what they expect `auto-layout` to do to their hand-placed boxes.
- A concept test using the SCR-082 ASCII wireframe in `14-screens-catalogue.md` plus one alternative framing (palette-left canvas vs. an outline-plus-canvas split) — measure whether participants can read the pictured "ATR trail 2x" rule aloud correctly.
- A comprehension test of the four round-trip indicator states defined for SCR-082 (`Round-trips ✓`, `Unsupported in form view`, `Round-trip mismatch`, `Not verified`): do participants understand what they lose by switching editors, and what "unsupported in form view" means for their rule?
- A decision test on the vocabulary used on canvas: node/port/edge vs. block/socket/wire vs. step/input/link — the chosen words must then be used identically in UI copy, `aria-label`s, validation messages and docs.
- Findings deck + a one-page "design principles for the node editor" note that D02/D03/D04 are held against, plus any resulting update to `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` F10 and `docs/plan/10-personas.md`.
- Explicit written answers to five questions: (1) is the graph a *reading* aid or an *authoring* aid for this user? (2) is the form editor the expected default entry point, with the graph opened for inspection? (3) how should the four round-trip states be worded? (4) what is the node vocabulary? (5) does auto-layout need an explicit undo affordance beyond `Ctrl+Z`?

## Out of scope
- Any hi-fi visual work (→ E37-D02), motion specs (→ E37-D03), a11y design review (→ E37-D04).
- Usability testing of built software (→ E37-Q06 exploratory charter).
- Research on the form editor (owned by E36's design work).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All five questions answered with evidence
  Given at least three completed sessions across the Owner and Manager personas
  When findings are written up
  Then each of the five questions has a written answer citing specific participant evidence, not designer preference

Scenario: The round-trip states are comprehensible
  Given participants are shown the four round-trip indicator states in isolation
  When asked what each means for their rule
  Then either >=2 of 3 participants explain each state correctly, or the failing state's wording is rewritten and re-tested within this ticket

Scenario: A keyboard-first participant is included (edge)
  Given at least one participant who states they operate keyboard-first
  Then their expectations for non-pointer authoring are recorded verbatim and carried into E37-D04 as explicit inputs

Scenario: Research contradicts the planned interaction (failure path)
  Given findings show the canvas is used only for reading, never authoring
  Then a recommendation to rescope E37-S01/S02 is written and raised with the Architect and CDO before D02 starts, rather than drawing the planned design anyway
```

## Technical notes / design
Sessions run remotely with screen share; participants think aloud over the wireframes. Use the real rule corpus from E36 (templates in SCR-083) as stimuli so participants react to rules they recognise. Record consent, store transcripts in the research repo area, anonymise quotes in the deck. No production data is used.

## Test plan
N/A for automated testing. Validation is the concept/comprehension/decision tests above; the findings note is reviewed by the CDO and the Architect before it is marked Done.

## Security notes
Participant recordings and transcripts are personal data: consent captured, storage access-restricted, retention stated in the deck, and no live account identifiers or API-key material appears in any stimulus (screenshots use the demo environment only).

## Accessibility notes
Sessions must be conducted accessibly (captions available, no colour-only stimuli). The keyboard-first participant requirement above is a hard part of the acceptance criteria, not a nice-to-have, because the canvas's keyboard equivalence is a release gate.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A — research output, no runtime telemetry. The chosen vocabulary is recorded in the findings note so the analytics event names in E37-S01 can match it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] >=3 sessions completed and transcribed; findings deck published and linked on this ticket.
- [ ] Five questions answered in writing with evidence.
- [ ] Design principles one-pager written and referenced by E37-D02.
- [ ] `13-user-flows.md` F10 / `10-personas.md` updated if findings diverge from the current text.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the CDO; Architect acknowledges any rescope recommendation.
- [ ] Findings presented at the design review; no open questions blocking E37-D02.

## Dependencies
No blockers. The inputs this research needs already exist as plan artefacts, not as shipped code: the form editor's interaction model and round-trip indicator spec are specified in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-081 and in E36's design chain (E36-D01/E36-D02, running in Sprints 13-14 alongside this ticket), and the IR's form subset — which defines what "unsupported in form view" means — is fixed by `ADR-0007` and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4. Only the *built* E37 screens (E37-S01..S05) depend on E35/E36 implementation. Feeds E37-D02, E37-D04.

> **Design-ahead note.** E37's design chain is deliberately pulled forward to Sprints 13-15 (D01 S13 - D02/D03 S14 - D04/D05 S15) so the handoff (E37-D05) is Done a full two sprints before the first consuming story (E37-S01, Sprint 17), satisfying `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 with no waiver.

title: UX research and wireframes for risk caps, lockout and kill-switch flows
body:
## Context
E39 introduces four screens the product has never had: an aggregate **risk dashboard** (SCR-071), a **kill-switch/freeze confirmation** (SCR-072), a **lockout notice** the user cannot dismiss (SCR-073), and a **global risk policy** admin page (SCR-134). Three of them are *interruption* surfaces — they appear when something has gone wrong and the user is under stress — which makes them new interaction territory and triggers the `ux-research` requirement in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence.

The design-ahead rule applies: the consuming FE stories E39-S04 and E39-S05 are scheduled for Sprint 16, so this research + wireframe ticket must be Done by end of Sprint 13, and the hi-fi tickets (E39-D02, E39-D03) by end of Sprint 14.

Key behavioural constraint to design against, from `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2: the kill-switch **"stops new risk, does not force-close"**. Every screen must make that distinction unmissable, because the single most dangerous misunderstanding in this epic is a user believing FREEZE closed their positions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Owner + Manager walkthroughs (2 scripted sessions) covering: what the owner expects FREEZE to do; what a manager needs to know the moment a lockout hits; which figure they look at first on a risk dashboard.
- Low-fi wireframes for **SCR-071**, **SCR-072**, **SCR-073**, **SCR-134**, matching the ASCII layouts already in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` and either confirming or explicitly superseding them (a supersession requires a note here plus a PR to the catalogue).
- State inventories per screen, per catalogue convention: SCR-071 normal · warning (≥80 % of a cap) · locked · frozen · stale data · reconciling; SCR-072 executing (per-account progress) · completed summary · partial failure with retry; SCR-073 active lockout · override-requested · expired; SCR-134 clean · validation warning (portfolio cap below the sum of per-account caps) · step-up required · save conflict.
- Copy deck for the danger wording: the FREEZE consequence restatement ("This cancels 14 working orders and blocks new orders on 5 accounts. Open positions are NOT closed."), lockout reason strings for each `RiskSummary.accounts[].lockout.reason` enum value (`daily_loss`, `consecutive_losses`, `max_positions`, `manual`), and the override reason-field helper text.
- Flow diagram updating `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` F20 with the breach → lockout → override path.
- Research findings written into the ticket and linked from the `14-screens-catalogue.md` sign-off checklists.

## Out of scope

title: UX research: how an owner supervises, delegates and investigates
body:
## Context
The admin area is 14 user stories and ~15 screens serving exactly one persona in a specific state of mind: **P1 Owner wearing the P4 Admin hat** (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`). Designing it as "CRUD screens for settings" would miss what the stories actually describe — supervision under time pressure (US-ADMIN-004 "supervise at a glance"), delegation with consequences (US-ADMIN-002 unbind-with-open-positions), and investigation after something went wrong (US-ADMIN-009 "so that investigation is practical").

Those three modes want different information architectures, and choosing wrongly is expensive to undo once eight screens are built. This research ticket exists to answer that before wireframes start, in line with the design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`: design runs ≥2 sprints ahead; this runs three ahead of the S16 build).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Structured sessions with the Owner (and, where available, a manager) covering three scripted scenarios: (1) *supervise* — "a manager's account is approaching its daily loss cap, what do you do?"; (2) *delegate* — "onboard a new manager and scope them to one sub-account"; (3) *investigate* — "an order was placed that you did not expect; find out who, when and under what permissions."
- Card-sort of the admin area's information: which of users / accounts / profiles / audit / health / flags / recorder / security / backups belong together, and what the owner expects on the landing page (SCR-120) versus one click away.
- Comprehension test of the vocabulary this area forces on the user: "step-up", "re-authentication", "elevation", "impersonation / view as", "hash chain", "append-only", "kill switch", "maintenance mode", "flag". Any term the owner cannot explain back is a copy defect, not a training problem.
- Specific risk probes: does the owner understand that **disabling a user revokes sessions but retains data**? That **deleting retains anonymised history**? That **unbinding with open positions forces a choice**? That **restore does not change anything on Bybit**? Each is a place where a wrong mental model causes real loss.
- Deliverable: a research report in `docs/design/research/e42-admin.md` with findings, verbatim quotes, an IA recommendation for SCR-120's tile set and grouping, a vocabulary decision list (term → keep / replace with X), and a prioritised list of comprehension risks feeding the copy work in E42-D02/D03.

## Out of scope
- Wireframes and hi-fi (E42-D02, E42-D03, E42-D04, E42-D05).
- Research for accounts/keys (E27) and profiles (E28) — already done in their own epics; this ticket reads those reports rather than repeating them.
- Quantitative usability metrics — the population is one owner plus a few managers; this is qualitative by necessity and says so.

## Acceptance criteria
- At least three scripted sessions completed and recorded (with consent), covering supervise, delegate and investigate.
- The card-sort produces a recommended SCR-120 tile set and grouping, explicitly reconciled with the catalogue's stated tiles (users, accounts, keys needing rotation, recorder, storage, health, flags, last backup) — any deviation is argued, not silently dropped.
- Every vocabulary term listed above has a decision recorded: keep (with a one-line in-product explanation) or replace (with the replacement).
- Each of the four risk probes has a finding: understood / partially understood / misunderstood, with the copy change that follows.
- Report merged and linked from E42-D02 and E42-D03; findings that imply a change to `14-screens-catalogue.md` are filed as catalogue amendments.
- CDO (or delegate) review comment recorded.

## Technical notes / design
- Sessions are moderated, think-aloud, against a clickable low-fidelity prototype or the existing catalogue wireframes — not a blank page.
- Card sort is open, then closed against the catalogue's grouping, so both "what the owner expects" and "does the proposed grouping survive" are answered.
- Comprehension test uses teach-back ("explain this to me as if I were a new manager"), which catches confident misunderstanding that recognition tests miss.

## Test plan
- Findings are validated in E42-D07 design QA against the built screens: each comprehension risk becomes a check.
- The vocabulary decisions become assertions in the QA a11y/copy pass (E42-Q05): the product must not reintroduce a rejected term.

## Security notes
- Sessions must not use production data: no real API keys, no real account balances, no real audit entries. A sanitised fixture set is prepared first.
- Recordings contain PII (voice, screen with usernames) — stored per the project's data-handling rules, retention stated in the report, deleted after the epic closes.

## Accessibility notes
- At least one session includes keyboard-only operation of the prototype, so keyboard flow problems are found in research rather than in design QA.
- The vocabulary work directly serves `05-accessibility-standard.md`'s plain-language requirement: a term a user cannot explain back cannot be an accessible name either.

## Performance notes
N/A — research ticket.

## Observability
- The comprehension-risk list becomes the source for the `empty_state_shown` and `admin.onboarding_abandoned` analytics questions — i.e. what we will watch post-launch to see whether the copy worked.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts delivered in Figma at the stated fidelity, linked from this ticket and from the relevant `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` entries.

title: Wireframe the admin area: shell, overview, users, audit, health and flags
body:
## Context
Fifteen admin screens share one shell, one re-auth model, one audit convention and one set of destructive-confirmation patterns. Wireframing them **together**, before any hi-fi work, is what prevents fifteen slightly different treatments of the same idea.

The catalogue already fixes the skeleton for each screen (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §10 contains ASCII wireframes, data sources, states, validation, a11y, performance and a per-screen sign-off checklist). This ticket turns those into structured, reviewable wireframes that resolve the cross-screen questions the catalogue leaves open: how the re-auth countdown lives in the chrome, how destructive confirmations are graded (simple confirm vs typed confirm vs typed confirm + step-up), and how a degraded subsystem is expressed consistently across SCR-120, SCR-143 and every tile.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes at low/medium fidelity for: **CMP-087 AdminLayout** shell with the re-auth freshness badge, **SCR-149** re-auth gate, **SCR-120** overview, **SCR-121** users list, **SCR-122** user detail, **SCR-123** invite, **SCR-124** view-as, **SCR-135** audit log, **SCR-136** audit event detail, **SCR-143** system health, **SCR-144** incident log, **SCR-145** feature flags, **SCR-146** backups & restore, **SCR-148** maintenance mode, **SCR-154** permission denied.
- **Cross-screen pattern decisions**, documented once and applied everywhere:
  - The **destructive-action ladder**: which actions need a plain confirm, which need a typed confirm, which need typed confirm + step-up. (The catalogue already mandates typed confirm + step-up for purge, restore, live enablement, flag changes on trading-capability flags and user deletion.)
  - The **degraded/stale expression**: one treatment for "this value is old", one for "this subsystem is down", used identically on SCR-120 tiles, SCR-143 tiles and SCR-147's summary.
  - The **audit-visibility convention**: how a screen tells the user "this action will be recorded".
  - The **re-auth interruption pattern**: gate as overlay, form content preserved, save held and resumed.
- Role variants drawn where behaviour differs: owner, manager (hard-404 / scoped audit), viewer (audit read-only).
- Every state from each screen's catalogue entry represented: loading, empty, filtered-to-nothing, error, degraded, integrity failure, action-in-flight.
- Review with engineering (feasibility) and security (does the wireframe imply an unsafe affordance) before the hi-fi tickets start.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi visual design and design-system contributions (E42-D03, E42-D04, E42-D05).
- Motion specification (E42-D04).
- Screens owned by other epics: SCR-125..129 (E27), SCR-130..134 (E28/E39), SCR-137 (E43), SCR-140..142 (E16), SCR-147 (E04/E46) — referenced for consistency, not redrawn.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every screen listed in Scope has a wireframe covering all of its catalogue-listed states.
- The four cross-screen pattern decisions are written down with a rationale and applied consistently — a reviewer can pick any two screens and find the same treatment of the same idea.
- The destructive-action ladder maps every destructive action in the epic to exactly one rung; no action is unclassified.
- Role variants drawn; the manager path shows the router-404, not a disabled admin nav item.
- Engineering feasibility review and security review comments recorded; any "this cannot be built as drawn" is resolved in the wireframe, not deferred to hi-fi.
- Findings from E42-D01 are visibly addressed (vocabulary decisions applied; each comprehension risk has a design response).

## Technical notes / design
- Wireframes are built from the catalogue's ASCII layouts as the starting skeleton so the design and the spec cannot silently diverge.
- Every wireframe annotates its data source (endpoint or WS topic) so engineering can see what a screen costs before it is beautiful.
- Tiles on SCR-120 and SCR-143 are annotated as **independently resolving** — the catalogue's hard requirement that no tile blocks another must be visible in the design, not assumed in code.

## Test plan
- Reviewed against each screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `14-screens-catalogue.md`, item by item; unticked items block the ticket.
- Walked through with QA (E42-Q01) so the test plan's scenarios and the wireframes' states are the same list.

## Security notes
- Security review specifically looks for: affordances that imply mutability of the audit log (there must be none), any path that could enable live trading from the flag console, impersonation that is not obviously read-only, and any screen that displays a secret.
- Wireframes must show the non-disclosure behaviour for non-owners (404, not 403-with-details) — a design that shows a helpful "you need owner access" page would be a spec violation.

## Accessibility notes
- Focus order annotated on every wireframe; the first tab stop on the view-as screen is Exit; the first tab stop in a destructive dialog is never the destructive button.
- All status expressions are text-first; the greyscale check is applied to the wireframes themselves.
- Tables annotated with their header semantics and sort affordances; sparklines annotated with their required table alternative.

## Performance notes
- Each wireframe carries its catalogue performance budget as an annotation (SCR-120 ≤800 ms, SCR-135 ≤400 ms filter round-trip, SCR-136 ≤300 ms, SCR-143 ≤2 ms scripting/frame), so designs that would require more data than the budget allows are caught here.

## Observability
Each wireframe annotates the audit/analytics events it emits, taken from the catalogue's Analytics/audit lines, so the instrumentation is designed rather than retrofitted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts delivered in Figma at the stated fidelity, linked from this ticket and from the relevant `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` entries.
- [ ] Every state in the screen's catalogue entry drawn (loading, empty, filtered-to-nothing, error, degraded, role variants, destructive-confirmation).

- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `04-security-program.md`, `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`

## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. AGENTS.md §0 (read-order) and §3 (how to pick up a ticket)
2. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`

**Commands**

- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/admin-screens-wireframes`
- PR title: `E42-D02: Wireframe the admin area: shell, overview, users, audit, health and flags`
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-number-for-E42-D02>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend @CandleViewer/frontend @CandleViewer/security
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels (design, area/accounts-admin, priority/p1)

**Done means**
- Artefacts delivered in Figma at the stated fidelity, linked from this ticket and from the relevant `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` entries.
- Every state in the screen's catalogue entry drawn (loading, empty, filtered-to-nothing, error, degraded, role variants, destructive-confirmation).

**Do NOT**

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
