title: Produce the STRIDE threat model for accounts, sub-accounts and the API-key vault
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes a STRIDE threat model per epic non-negotiable, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS2.1 makes it default-on for any epic touching auth, keys, OMS or money movement, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7.4 names E27 explicitly in the R3 security gate: "STRIDE for E27, E29, E34, E35, E39, E42 - all Critical/High closed".

E27 is the epic that holds credentials capable of moving real money. ADR-0009 already fixes the architecture (KEK outside the database, DEK per record, decryption narrowed to the exchange adapter, withdrawal always off, IP allowlist mandatory), but an ADR is a decision, not an analysis: it does not enumerate the ways the decision can be defeated in implementation. This ticket does that enumeration before the vault is built, so the controls land as code rather than as retrofits.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Threat model document at `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md`, linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, containing:
  - **System decomposition**: a data-flow diagram (mermaid) covering credential intake (SCR-126 -> `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys`), storage (`api_keys.secret_enc`, `dek_ref`, `kek_version`), borrow (credential broker -> exchange adapter -> signed request), verification (`/keys/{keyId}/test`, the nightly job), rotation (`/keys/{keyId}/rotate`, `api_key_rotations`), revocation (`DELETE /keys/{keyId}`), and the read paths (`GET /exchange-accounts`, the `wallet` WS topic, SCR-079, SCR-125, SCR-128).
  - **Trust boundaries** marked against `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS2.2: browser -> API, API -> Postgres, API -> host KEK source, API -> Bybit, and the WSL/host boundary that ADR-0009 depends on.
  - **STRIDE enumeration per element and per flow**, each threat with likelihood, impact, the existing control, the gap, and a concrete mitigation ticket. At minimum: **S** - session fixation on the admin routes, a forged step-up, impersonating the host KEK launcher; **T** - ciphertext substitution (mitigated by the GCM tag), tampering with `permission_snapshot` to fake a passed verification, mutating `env`/`exchange_uid` after creation, tampering with the egress IP determination; **R** - a key action without an audit row, audit-chain break, an operator denying a revoke; **I** - database dump, log line, trace attribute, metric label, exception body, support bundle, core dump, browser autofill/password manager, screenshot, clipboard, the `key_id_masked` prefix being over-long; **D** - self-check storm consuming the per-UID rate budget and starving order placement, KEK unavailability halting trading, revoking the last key of an account with open positions; **E** - a manager reaching an account outside their grant via REST or a raw WS frame, `keys:manage` leaking into a non-owner role, the development `CV_KEK_SOURCE=file` path reaching a live deployment.
  - **Abuse cases** written as adversary narratives: a stolen laptop with the Postgres volume; a malicious or coerced account manager; a compromised dependency that reads process memory; an attacker with a valid viewer session hunting for a reveal endpoint; an operator tricked into pasting a live key into a demo-bound account.
  - **Risk register updates** in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` for any new risk surfaced.
  - A **control checklist** naming, for each accepted control, the automated check that proves it (unit test, contract test, CI rule, DAST rule) and the ticket that implements it - E27-T02, E27-T03, E27-X02, E27-X03 or a new ticket.
- A kickoff and a review session with the Architect, DevSecOps and the backend lead for the epic; decisions recorded in the document.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the mitigations - those are the referenced engineering tickets.
- Threat modelling the OMS (E29), fan-out (E34) or auth itself (E09); this model consumes E09's conclusions rather than repeating them.
- The penetration test, which happens before Live enablement in R4 (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element and flow is analysed
  When docs/security/threat-models/E27.md is reviewed by the Architect
  Then every element and every data flow in the DFD has all six STRIDE categories considered, with each either analysed or explicitly marked not-applicable with a one-line reason

Scenario: Each threat has a control with a test
  When the control checklist is reviewed
  Then every Critical and High threat names a mitigation ticket and an automated check that would fail if the control were removed, and no Critical or High is closed with documentation alone

Scenario: The development KEK source cannot reach live
  Given the threat "CV_KEK_SOURCE=file used in a live deployment"
  When the mitigation is verified
  Then a start-up assertion refuses to boot when CV_KEK_SOURCE=file and CV_ENV=live, and a unit test asserts that refusal

Scenario: The model is finished before the vault is built
  Given E27-T02 is the credential broker implementation
  When E27-T02 enters In Progress
  Then this threat model is at least in review with its Critical/High list stable, and E27-T02's design reflects it

## Technical notes / design
The model follows the four-question frame (what are we building; what can go wrong; what are we going to do about it; did we do a good job) with STRIDE-per-element as the enumeration technique, matching `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Severity uses the security program's rating scale so findings are comparable across epics.

Two structural conclusions are expected to fall out and should be stated explicitly because later tickets depend on them: (1) the secret columns must never appear on any serialisable model - a structural control rather than a filtering control, because filtering fails open; (2) account scope must be derived server-side from the session on every request and every WS subscription, never accepted from the client, because the epic's highest-likelihood elevation-of-privilege path is a manager enumerating accounts.

The document is versioned in the repository and re-reviewed if the epic's scope changes; ADR-0009 gets an amendment note if the model contradicts any of its assumptions.

## Test plan
The deliverable is a document, verified by peer review rather than by execution. Its downstream verification is real: E27-X03 implements the RBAC matrix test the model demands, E27-X02 runs the review that confirms the controls exist in code, and E27-Q03's chaos scenarios exercise the denial-of-service and availability threats. A threat whose control has no test is treated as an open finding.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security deliverable. Data classification for the epic is fixed here: `secret_enc`, `enc_nonce`, `dek_ref` and the KEK are **Secret**; `exchange_uid`, `label`, `permission_snapshot`, balances and fee rates are **Confidential**; health states are **Internal**. Every later ticket in E27 cites this classification rather than re-deciding it.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. The model does, however, record the accessibility-adjacent disclosure paths (tooltips, aria-labels, clipboard, autofill) as information-disclosure threats, which E27-Q04 charter 1 then hunts for.

## Performance notes
The model records the denial-of-service threat quantitatively: the per-UID exchange rate budget from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS4.3, how much of it verification may consume, and the reserved share the order path must retain. E27-Q03 measures against those numbers.

## Observability
The model specifies the audit events that must exist for non-repudiation (`account.created`, `account.updated`, `account.tested`, `account.key_rotated`, `account.disabled`, `account.deleted`, `account.disabled_by_policy`, `admin.key_marked_compromised`, `admin.secrets_policy_changed`), that they must be hash-chained per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS3.10, and the security-relevant metrics that must exist for detection (failed verification counts, credential-borrow rate, KEK load failures).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings logged in the security register with severity, owner and due date.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings closed before the R3 gate (roadmap SS7.4 Security gate: "STRIDE for E27 ... all Critical/High closed").
- [ ] Every agreed control encoded as an automated check (CI rule, unit test, contract test or DAST rule), not only as prose.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer; the STRIDE document is stored at `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md` and linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-K01** (the KEK custody decision is an input to the model's trust boundaries) and **E09** (auth, sessions, step-up and RBAC are the foundation this model builds on). Gates the design of E27-T02 and E27-T03.

- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md#22-acct--bybit-accounts--api-keys-10-stories`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md#32-exchange-accounts-api-keys-profiles` - `exchange_accounts`, `api_keys`, `api_key_rotations`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md#313-user_account_access`

title: Hi-fi design and design-system contributions for the profile and trade-group surfaces
body:
## Context
The wireframes from E28-D02 become buildable specifications here. The six surfaces lean on a component set that is mostly existing (CMP-040 FormField, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-104 LeverageSlider, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard, CMP-138 RiskCapMeter, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-106 ProfileBadge, CMP-232 LimitsChip) but which several screens stretch: a virtualised matrix of checkboxes with sticky headers, a risk-cap meter that must read correctly at three different scales, and a safety notice that must communicate "this cannot be turned off" without looking like a broken toggle.

Anything the existing system cannot express is a **design-system contribution**, agreed with the design-system team and added to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` - never an ad hoc one-off inside this epic (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS3.1: "any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off").

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi designs for SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133, SCR-062 and the SCR-061 preview, in light and dark themes, at the standard and compact densities defined in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- Tokens only - type scale, spacing, colour, elevation, radius - with no raw values anywhere; any missing token is raised as a design-system change rather than hard-coded.
- Design-system contributions, each with states, props, tokens, a11y contract and a Storybook specification: the symbol-matrix cell (three states: allowed, denied, denied-and-locked), the readiness strip ("N of M ready" with per-member reasons), the override marker used by SCR-061 and E28-S05, and any extension needed to CMP-138 RiskCapMeter and CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice.
- Final copy for every label, unit, helper text, validation message, empty state and confirmation, reviewed by the content reviewer and checked against the exact strings the screen catalogue fixes.
- The worked-example element specified to the number: format, precision, units, and how it renders while inputs are incomplete or the equity is unknown.
- Redlines: spacing, sizes, focus rings, hit targets (>=24x24 CSS px per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), and the responsive behaviour of the matrix and both grids.
- Per-row DEMO/LIVE badge treatment for SCR-061, and the environment treatment across the admin surfaces, consistent with CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal.
- Updates to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` and `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` for everything added or changed.

## Out of scope
Motion specification (E28-D04); the a11y review pass (E28-D05); the handoff pack (E28-D06); SCR-061's send and failure states (**E34**).

## Acceptance criteria
- Hi-fi frames exist for all six surfaces in both themes and both densities, covering every state drawn in E28-D02.
- Every new or extended component has a design-system entry with states, props, tokens and an accessibility contract, agreed with the design-system team, and is added to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`.
- No raw hex, no ad hoc spacing, no off-scale type - verified by a token audit over the Figma file.
- Every screen's own "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is satisfied item by item and ticked in a comment on this ticket.
- Copy reviewed and approved; the fixed strings from the catalogue appear verbatim.
- Signed off by the Chief Design Officer and acknowledged by the frontend lead who will build E28-S01..S04.

## Technical notes / design
The risk-cap meter appears at three scales - a compact chip on the profiles list, a full meter in the editor, and a per-row indicator in the preview - and must remain legible and truthful at all three; the contribution specifies one component with a size prop rather than three lookalikes.

The safety notice communicating a non-removable floor is the hardest single piece of visual design in this epic: it must not read as a disabled control the user could enable with more permissions. The spec must therefore define its own visual language (a stated policy, not an input) and be user-tested informally with two participants before sign-off.

## Test plan
N/A - design artefact. The token audit and the checklist walkthrough are the verification.

## Security notes
The step-up gate and the audited-action affordance (CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger) are drawn on every state-changing control, so an implementation cannot omit them without visibly diverging from the spec. No frame contains a real key, UID, label or balance. The "aggressive template on a live account" acknowledgement is specified as a typed confirmation, not a single click, matching the danger-confirmation pattern in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Accessibility notes
Contrast verified at >=4.5:1 for text and >=3:1 for non-text indicators and focus rings, in both themes, with the measurements recorded. Focus states designed for every interactive element including matrix cells and virtualised rows. Nothing is conveyed by colour alone - every status has text or a glyph. Hit targets >=24x24 CSS px. The designs must be renderable inside the catalogue's budgets: SCR-133's virtualised grid over ~400 symbols in <=600 ms, SCR-062's grid under 4 ms scripting per frame at 50 groups x 5 legs, SCR-061's preview updating within 300 ms. title: Specify motion and state-transition choreography for profile saves, previews and readiness
body:
## Context
E28's surfaces change under the user's hands: a preview re-resolves as the intent is typed, a readiness strip flips from "3 of 3" to "2 of 3" when a key self-check fails, a save goes through step-up and returns a new version, and a matrix bulk action changes hundreds of cells at once. Without a specified choreography each of these will be implemented differently, and the fast-changing ones (preview, readiness) risk motion that distracts during trading or that violates reduced-motion preferences.

`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` defines the motion tokens; this ticket applies them and specifies what must *not* move.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion specification for: profile save (idle -> validating -> step-up -> saving -> saved/failed), preview recomputation (stale -> updating -> fresh, including the "keep the last good preview" transition), readiness change (N of M), matrix bulk apply and the unsaved-changes summary, group row expansion to legs, and the version-conflict recovery.
- Durations, easing curves and delays expressed **only** as tokens from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- An explicit "does not animate" list: numeric values in the preview table and the worked example do not tween between values (a tweening number is unreadable and, in a trading context, misleading); status text swaps without a transition; virtualised rows do not animate on scroll.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour specified per transition - each one either has a non-motion equivalent (an instant state change plus a text change) or is removed entirely.
- Loading and skeleton treatment for the two grids, specified so a re-render caused by a WS frame does not flash a skeleton.
- Focus-preservation rules across every transition: a coalesced WS update must never move or steal focus, and the version-conflict path must return focus to a sensible anchor.
- A prototype in Figma demonstrating the save flow and the preview refresh, for the handoff pack.

## Out of scope
Hi-fi visuals (E28-D03); implementation; SCR-061's send-in-progress and partial-failure choreography (**E34**).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every transition listed above has a specified duration, easing and trigger, all token-based.
- The "does not animate" list exists and explicitly includes preview numbers and the worked example.
- Every transition has a `prefers-reduced-motion` alternative, or is documented as removed under that preference.
- Focus-preservation rules are written per transition and are testable statements, not aspirations.
- The Figma prototype demonstrates the save flow and a preview refresh end to end.
- Signed off by the Chief Design Officer and the motion lead; acknowledged by the frontend lead.

## Technical notes / design
The preview refresh is the sensitive one: at a 150 ms debounce with a <=300 ms server round-trip, any transition longer than ~120 ms will still be running when the next update arrives. The specification therefore caps preview-related motion at the shortest token and prefers a state change with no motion at all, using a subtle staleness treatment instead of an animation.

Readiness changes are announced to screen readers through a live region (specified in E28-D05); the motion spec must not assume the visual transition is the only signal.

## Test plan
N/A - design artefact. Implementation conformance is checked in E28-D07 design QA, which includes a reduced-motion pass.

## Security notes
Motion must never be the sole indicator of a dangerous state. A blocked group, a refused save or a failed step-up is communicated by text and state, with motion at most as reinforcement - so a user with motion disabled loses no safety information.

## Accessibility notes
`prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured for every transition; no transition may flash more than three times per second (WCAG 2.2 2.3.1). Focus is never moved by an animation or by a data-driven re-render. Live-region announcements are coordinated with, not replaced by, the visual transition. Skeletons must not be announced as content changes.

## Performance notes
Motion must not compete with the render budgets: the group grid stays under 4 ms scripting per frame at 50 groups x 5 legs, so no per-row transition is permitted at that scale. Animations are composited transforms and opacity only - no layout-triggering properties.

title: Accessibility design review of the six profile and trade-group surfaces
body:
## Context
Two of E28's surfaces are accessibility-hard in ways that must be solved at design time rather than discovered in an audit. **SCR-133** is a virtualised grid of checkboxes across accounts x ~400 symbols where each cell's accessible name must combine account and symbol and where one cell state means "you cannot deny this, there is an open position". **SCR-061**'s preview is a live-updating table whose every status must be text, whose send button must name the account count, and which must not steal focus while a user types.

`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA. The catalogue entries already carry per-screen a11y rules; this review checks the hi-fi designs against them before a line of code is written, because retrofitting an accessible name onto a virtualised grid is far more expensive than designing it in.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Review of the E28-D03 hi-fi frames for all six surfaces against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` and each screen's catalogue a11y notes.
- Contrast measurements recorded for every text and non-text indicator in both themes, including the three matrix cell states, the readiness strip, the WARN and excluded row treatments and every focus ring.
- Focus-order diagrams per screen, including the modal flows (step-up, unsaved-changes summary, template acknowledgement, delete confirmation) and the return-focus target for each.
- Accessible-name specification for every non-obvious control: matrix cells (account + symbol + state), bulk row and column actions (naming their scope and count), the send button (naming the account count), expansion controls, and the reset-to-default affordances.
- Live-region plan: what is announced, with which politeness, on readiness change, preview refresh, save result, bulk-apply result and degraded-leg transitions - deliberately limited so a fast-updating preview does not flood a screen reader.
- Disabled-control reason specification: every disabled control states why in visible text exposed via `aria-describedby` - required by E28-S05's "capped by profile" and by SCR-061's exclusion reasons.
- Keyboard-operation specification for the matrix (arrow navigation, range selection, toggling, bulk actions) and for both grids, with no mouse-only path anywhere.
- Text-scaling and zoom verification at 200% and 125% with screenshots, especially for the two grids.
- A findings list with severity, each either resolved in the designs before sign-off or logged with an owner and a date.

## Out of scope
Automated axe-core runs against built code and manual screen-reader passes on the implementation (**E28-Q04**); the design QA of the built screens (**E28-D07**).

## Acceptance criteria
- All six surfaces reviewed with findings recorded, and every Critical or High finding resolved in the designs before sign-off - not deferred to implementation.
- Contrast measurements recorded for both themes, with no value below 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for non-text indicators and focus rings.
- Focus-order diagrams exist for every screen and every modal, including return-focus targets.
- Every matrix cell state, every row status and every disabled control has a specified accessible name and reason.

For the virtualised matrix, the review must settle whether the grid is exposed as a `role="grid"` with `aria-rowindex`/`aria-colindex` on the rendered window, or as a set of labelled checkboxes with an off-screen description - and the decision is recorded with its rationale, because it determines the DOM structure E28-S02 builds.

The preview's announcement rate is capped by announcing a *summary* ("3 of 4 accounts ready, total 0.430 BTC") rather than per-cell changes, at most once per second, with the full table available on demand through normal table navigation.

N/A - design review. The findings become test cases in E28-Q04's a11y audit, so nothing found here can be lost.

Accessible alternatives must not weaken a safety control: the step-up dialog remains a real gate for keyboard and screen-reader users; the "aggressive template on live" typed acknowledgement is not reduced to a single keypress; the non-removable native-SL floor is announced as policy, never as a control the user might be able to change.

This ticket *is* the accessibility work; its own DoD is the checklist above. It covers WCAG 2.2 AA including the 2.2-specific criteria that matter here: focus appearance (2.4.11), target size minimum (2.5.8), consistent help (3.2.6) and redundant entry (3.3.7) - the last two matter for the repeated step-up prompts across profile, template and matrix saves.

Accessible-name computation for a virtualised grid must not require rendering every cell; the chosen approach is checked against SCR-133's <=600 ms render budget in the review itself.

- The design-system contributions from E28-D03 confirmed as merged into the system with Storybook entries, so a story does not have to build a system component itself.
- An open-questions list, each with an owner and a decision date, and a statement that none of them blocks implementation.
- A walkthrough session with the frontend engineers who will implement E28-S01..S05, recorded, with questions answered in the pack rather than in chat.
- Confirmation that the catalogue documents (`14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`) now match the pack.

Design QA of built screens (E28-D07); any new design exploration - this ticket assembles and signs off, it does not redesign.

- The pack is complete for all six surfaces, with no "TBD" in any state, copy string or binding note.
- Every server error code that the six screens can receive (from E28-T02 and E28-T05: `validation_failed`, `native_stop_mandatory`, `conflict`, `precondition_failed`, `step_up_required`, `forbidden`, `account_scope_denied`, `env_mismatch`, `rate_limited`, `profile_forbidden`, `risk_limit_breached`) has a user-facing string in the copy deck.
- Every design-system contribution is merged with a Storybook entry before this ticket closes.
- The walkthrough has happened and its questions are answered inside the pack.
- Signed off by the Chief Design Officer; accepted in writing by the frontend lead; Status Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming stories start (S16), i.e. by the end of S14.

## Technical notes / design
The copy deck is keyed by error code rather than by screen, because the same code can surface on several screens and must read identically everywhere. Where a server message already carries a specific string (for example the exchange-limit message naming a symbol and its maximum leverage), the deck records that the server string is rendered verbatim and the client adds no wrapper text.

N/A - the acceptance of the pack by the frontend lead is the verification. Its completeness is retested implicitly in E28-D07, where any gap shows up as a build discrepancy.

## Security notes
The pack states, per screen, which actions require step-up and which emit audit events, so the implementation cannot omit them silently. It contains no real credentials, UIDs, labels or balances. It also records the rule that no secret is displayed on any of these screens, to be verified in copy review.

## Accessibility notes
The pack carries E28-D05's outputs in full - focus orders, accessible names, live-region plan, disabled-control reasons, contrast measurements - so a developer never has to infer them. Any a11y finding still open is listed with an owner and must not be Critical or High.

## Performance notes
The pack restates the per-screen budgets (SCR-133 <=600 ms grid render, SCR-062 <=4 ms scripting per frame, SCR-061 <=300 ms preview, SCR-131 <=2 s save) so they are visible to the implementer rather than buried in the catalogue.

## Observability
The pack lists the analytics and audit events each screen must emit (`profile.list_viewed`, `profile.template_applied`, `symbol_permission.changed`, `tradegroup.preview`, and the audited `profile.*` and `tradegroup.*` events), so instrumentation is part of the build rather than a follow-up.

title: OMS core & order state machine
body:
## Context
R3 ("Trading on demo", `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7) closes the execution loop, and **E29 is its foundation**: every other trading epic (E30 ticket UI, E31 chart/DOM trading, E32 brackets & native-SL invariant, E33 emulated algos, E34 fan-out, E35 rule engine, E38 paper, E41 journal, E45 resilience) submits orders through the OMS this epic builds. The roadmap starts it on day 1 of S14 and puts it on the critical path `E09 → E27 → E29 → E32 → E34 → E43 → E44` (§11.2).

The design decision is already made and is normative: `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0006-oms-state-machine.md` — an explicit state machine including an `Unknown` state, `orderLinkId` idempotency, and resolution **only** by reconciliation (never blind resubmission). `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §8 is its normative expansion (models, transition rules S1–S9, id scheme, submission pipeline, reconciliation algorithm). `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.5 names the components (`Validator`, `OrderStateMachine`, `Reconciler`, `KillSwitch` hook) inside module **M14**.

The product-visible half of the epic is the **blotters**: SCR-063 (positions · working orders · fills tabs) and SCR-078 (fills/executions detail), plus the reconciliation/desync treatment on SCR-152. These are the screens the owner stares at while money is at risk, so "the app never lies about my book" (US-POS-008) is the epic's real acceptance test.

## Estimate reconciliation (roadmap 42 — engineering 46 — epic 95)
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register (line 129) and §7 R3 scope table (line 377) size E29 at **42 pts**. That roadmap figure prices *engineering* scope only — the OMS build (state machine, submission pipeline, private-stream truth, reconciliation, REST surface) plus the blotter stories — and was never intended to cover the design, QA and security discipline tickets, which the roadmap accounts for separately in the R3 train capacity. The three numbers reconcile exactly, with no scope missing or double-counted:

| Figure | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Roadmap allocation | 42 | Engineering build for M14 + SCR-063/SCR-078, as sized during roadmap planning. |
| Engineering children (`E29-K01`, `E29-T01..T09`, `E29-S01..S08`) | 46 | The same scope, re-estimated at grooming: 46 vs 42 = **+9.5%**, inside the ±15% tolerance of `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §DoR, so the R3 train needs no re-baselining. The delta is the reconciliation UX (`E29-S07`, 5) coming in heavier than the pre-decomposition T-shirt allowed. |

Roll-up by band (the epic `estimate` field must stay equal to this total — any change requires editing both, and a move of the **engineering** figure outside 36–48 pts requires a roadmap PR, not a silent backlog edit):

| Band | Tickets | Pts |

| Spike | K01 | 2 |
| Task (engineering + docs chore) | T01–T09 | 22 |

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories — domain POS (all Must/Should) and the OMS-side of domain ORD:**
- US-POS-001 Consolidated positions panel (Must) · US-POS-002 Working orders panel (Must) · US-POS-003 Partial close (Must) · US-POS-004 Position detail view (Should) · US-POS-005 Execution marks on the chart (Must) · US-POS-006 Account and group filtering (Must) · US-POS-007 Position mode and hedge support (Must/Should) · US-POS-008 Reconciliation with the exchange (Must) · US-POS-009 Closed positions and daily PnL (Must)
- Server-side enablement of US-ORD-001 (submit), US-ORD-002 (order types/flags validation) and US-ORD-009/US-ORD-010 (cancel / cancel-all / flatten backends). The **UI** for those lives in E30/E31.

**Screens:** SCR-063 (primary), SCR-078, SCR-152 (reconciling/desync variant), SCR-064 (consumed, owned by E32), SCR-079 (consumed, owned by E27).
**Components:** CMP-114 PositionsGrid, CMP-115 OrderRow, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton, CMP-129 PositionModeToggle, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-049/055/056/057 (base table, filter bar, column picker, split button), CMP-076/077/078 (connection, reconnect, stale shade).
**DB tables:** `orders`, `order_events`, `executions`, `positions`, `position_snapshots` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.3.4–3.3.7).
**API:** `GET/POST /orders`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /orders/{orderId}`, `POST /orders/cancel-all`, `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`, `GET /positions`, `GET /positions/{positionId}`, `POST /positions/{positionId}/close`, `POST /positions/{positionId}/reverse`, `PUT /positions/{positionId}/leverage`, `POST /positions/close-all`, `GET /executions`, `GET /executions/closed-pnl`.
**WS topics:** `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet` (never throttled, never coalesced — `23-ws-protocol.md` S4/S5).
**Module:** M14 (OMS).

## Out of scope
- Order ticket UI, sizing modes, hotkeys, arm/lock (E30); chart/DOM direct manipulation (E31).
- Bracket objects, scaled ladders and the **enforcement** of the native-SL invariant (E32/M17) — E29 provides the choke point and the `native_stop_required` rejection code but the bracket/partial-fill-aware child sizing is E32's.
- Emulated algos OCO/iceberg/TWAP/chase (E33); trade-group fan-out and the rate-limit governor (E34) — E29 creates the one-leg trade group wrapper only.
- Rule engine (E35–E37), paper matcher (E38), risk caps/kill-switch implementation (E39 — E29 calls its gate), journal (E41), admin screens (E42).
- Live trading. Everything here runs against **Bybit demo (REST-only order entry)**; the live transport path is written behind `ExchangeCapabilities.supports_ws_order_entry` but is gated off until R4/E44.
- Android; separate admin app; non-Bybit venues; non-USDT-linear-perp instruments.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full lifecycle on demo matches the exchange
  Given a demo account with a valid key
  When a limit order is placed, partially filled, amended and finally cancelled
  Then every transition is present in order_events with a monotone seq
  And the local order state equals GET /v5/order/realtime and /v5/order/history for that orderLinkId

Scenario: A lost acknowledgement never duplicates a position
  Given the transport times out after the exchange accepted the order
  When the order enters Unknown and the reconciler runs
  Then the order is resolved to its true exchange state without any resubmission
  And exactly one position exists on the exchange

Scenario: The book is never misreported
  Given local state diverges from the exchange after a 60 s private-WS outage
  When reconciliation completes
  Then exchange truth wins, the correction is audited with both values, and the blotter shows the corrected state within 30 s

Scenario: Order entry is refused when we cannot record it
  Given Postgres is unavailable
  When an order submission is attempted
  Then it is rejected with 503 service_unavailable before any exchange call
```

## Technical notes / design
Pipeline (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.4): `POST /orders` → RiskGate (E39) → OMS.submit → size/round/validate filters → build `orderLinkId` → INSERT order + `order_events` (write-ahead) → rate budget acquire → adapter send → ack/reject/timeout → private-WS stream applies truth. `orderLinkId = cv{env}-{group22}-{acct4}-{seq2}{purpose2}` ≤36 chars, generated once, reused on every retry.

## Test plan
Unit (state-machine transition matrix incl. every illegal transition), contract (OpenAPI + WS schema), integration against the fixture-replay mock exchange (`packages/fixtures`, `03-testing-strategy.md` §4.1, `rest_*.json` for `/v5/order/realtime`, `/v5/position/list`, `/v5/execution/list`), E2E (Playwright web + Electron over SCR-063), perf (k6 budget #4: submit→ack p95 <300 ms demo, backend-added ≤50 ms), chaos (WS kill mid-order, backend restart, Postgres failover, duplicate acks, out-of-order fills, 10018, 10002).

## Security notes
STRIDE model required before implementation lands (E29-X01). Threats: spoofed order origin, tampered blotter data, repudiation of a placed order, information disclosure of another account's orders (cross-tenant leak), DoS via order flooding, elevation via RBAC scope bypass. Controls: `orders:write`/`positions:write` permissions with `granted_accounts` scope on every route and WS subscription, append-only `order_events`, audit on every mutation, mandatory `Idempotency-Key`, no secret material in diagnostics (redaction). Data classification: **financial / restricted**.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-063 is a real table with `aria-sort`, row-level action menus, totals associated via `scope`; liq-proximity is glyph+text never colour alone; pending/optimistic states are announced in a polite live region; virtualised grid keeps a keyboard-reachable focus model (`05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2): submit→ack p95 <300 ms on demo, backend-added ≤50 ms p95. Blotter: 500 rows at 60 fps, position updates coalesced at 10 Hz; `orders`/`executions` WS topics never throttled.

## Observability
`order_submit_seconds{transport,env}` (p99 ≤500 ms), `oms_unknown_orders` (gauge, **page if >0 for 60 s**), `oms_reconcile_corrections_total{kind}`, `oms_state_transitions_total{from,to}`, `oms_untracked_orders`, `naked_position_alerts_total`. Audit events: `order.submitted`, `order.amended`, `order.cancelled`, `position.closed`, `oms.reconcile`.

- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. title: Spike: measure the Bybit demo order path and private-WS parity before the OMS is built
body:
## Context
ADR-0006 §Validation calls for a private-WS soak ("Spike S3: 24 h soak of the private WS client on demo with zero missed executions") before the OMS commits to "the WS stream, never the REST ack, is the source of truth". Two numbers decide the shape of the implementation and must be measured, not assumed:
1. The Bybit **demo** REST round-trip for `/v5/order/create`, because budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2) allocates ≤250 ms of the 300 ms p95 to it and only ≤50 ms to us.
2. Whether the demo private stream (`stream-demo`) delivers `order`, `execution.fast`, `position` and `wallet` with the ordering and completeness ADR-0006 assumes. Demo has **no WS order entry** (locked decision) but does have private streams.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Throwaway harness on branch `spike/oms-demo-path` (not merged) using the E08 adapter to place → partially fill → amend → cancel ≥200 small orders on a demo account across ≥4 h, plus a 24 h idle private-WS soak.
- Measure and record:
  - REST `/v5/order/create` RTT distribution (p50/p95/p99) from the backend host to `api-demo.bybit.com`.
  - Private-WS event latency from exchange `execTime`/`updatedTime` to local receipt; count of executions seen **only** via `GET /v5/execution/list` backfill (target zero).
  - Observed ordering — does an `execution` ever arrive after the `order` transition it caused? `23-ws-protocol.md` S5 requires we emit execution→order→position, so a violation means T05 needs a causal reorder buffer.
  - Exact shapes of `retCode` 10018 (rate limit), 10002 (clock drift) and duplicate-`orderLinkId` (10001/110072) responses.
  - Demo 7-day order-retention behaviour (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3 rule 6).
- Contribute the captured sequences to `packages/fixtures` (`rest_*.json` + private `*.jsonl.gz`) for the integration suite.

## Out of scope
Any production code. Live-environment measurement (R4/E44). WS order entry (unavailable on demo).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budget feasibility answered
  When the REST RTT distribution is measured
  Then the spike states, with numbers, whether budget #4 (p95 <300 ms end-to-end on demo) is achievable with ≤50 ms backend overhead

Scenario: Source-of-truth assumption validated
  Given a 24 h private-WS soak
  Then the count of executions seen only via REST backfill is reported
  And if it is non-zero the reconciliation cadence is revised in ADR-0006 before T06 starts

Scenario: Error shapes captured
  Then fixtures exist for 10018, 10002 and duplicate-orderLinkId responses
  And the E08 adapter error taxonomy is confirmed or an amendment ticket is filed
```

## Technical notes / design
Timebox **4 working days** plus the unattended 24 h soak. Decision rule agreed up front: if demo REST p95 exceeds 250 ms, budget #4 is renegotiated in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` rather than silently absorbed by shrinking our 50 ms. If ordering violations are observed, E29-T05 gains a reorder buffer keyed on `(ts_exec, seq)`.

## Test plan
The spike is itself measurement. Outputs feed E29-Q03 (perf scripts) and the fixtures used by T04/T05/T06.

## Security notes
Demo keys only, withdrawal permission OFF, IP-whitelisted, obtained from the E27 vault — never a live key and never a key committed to the branch. Captured fixtures are scrubbed of keys, signatures and account identifiers before commit (`03-testing-strategy.md` §4.1). CI must not be able to reach `api-demo.bybit.com`; this harness runs manually on the dev host only.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Produces the baseline numbers against which budget #4 is gated in E29-Q03.

## Observability
The harness exports the production metric names (`order_submit_seconds`) so Grafana panels can be built against real data before the OMS exists.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Questions answered with recorded evidence (tables/histograms) in the ticket.
- [ ] Findings recorded as an addendum to `27-adrs/ADR-0006-oms-state-machine.md` §Validation.
- [ ] Fixtures committed to `packages/fixtures`.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for anything invalidated; `32-risk-register.md` updated.
- [ ] Branch left unmerged and marked throwaway; findings presented at Sprint Review.

title: Write the black-box test plan and Bybit fixtures for the OMS and its blotters
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature **before** code, and `30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4 names the integration fixture set R3 must cover: partial fills, rejections, `10018` rate-limit, WS disconnect mid-bracket, exchange 5xx and clock skew. - Error fixtures for each retCode E29 maps: 10001 duplicate, 10002 clock drift, 10006, 10018, 110001, 110017, 110020, 110025, 110072, plus an HTTP 5xx and a post-send timeout.
- A traceability table mapping each fixture to the transition rule (S1-S9) and the acceptance scenario it exercises.

## Out of scope
Writing the automation itself (E29-Q02), perf scripts (E29-Q03), chaos orchestration (E29-Q04), the a11y audit (E29-Q05). Fan-out and algo fixtures (E33/E34 extend this set).

Scenario: Fixtures are deterministic
  When any fixture is replayed twice against the mock exchange

Scenario: An unobservable transition is a defect
  Given a state transition that cannot be observed through the API, WS stream or diagnostics endpoint
  Then it is recorded as a gap and a diagnostics ticket is filed against E29-T08
```

## Technical notes / design
Fixtures are captured from the real Bybit **demo** environment through the E08 adapter's recording mode and then redacted: API keys, signatures and account UIDs are replaced with stable synthetic values by a `scrub_fixture()` helper, with a CI check that no fixture contains a string matching the key or signature patterns. Each fixture carries a header comment naming its source date, symbol and the rule it exercises. The mock exchange serving them is the fixture-replay server from `03-testing-strategy.md` section 4.1.

## Test plan
The plan is itself reviewed rather than executed: QA lead review plus an Architect review of the fixture-to-rule mapping. A CI job asserts every fixture parses against the documented Bybit response schema and that the scrubber leaves no credential-shaped strings.

## Security notes
Recorded fixtures are the classic accidental-secret-leak vector. The scrubber plus the CI secret-scan on `packages/fixtures/**` is mandatory before any fixture is committed. Fixtures are demo-environment only; capturing live-account fixtures is prohibited.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the keyboard-only and screen-reader charters that E29-Q05 later executes formally.

N/A for the plan; perf thresholds are referenced, not measured here.

Gaps found (transitions not observable) are filed against E29-T08 so the metric and diagnostics surface grows to cover them.

title: Create the OMS schema migration and repositories for orders, events, executions, positions
body:
## Context
`24-internal-schemas.md` rule S7 makes Postgres authoritative: "If Postgres is unavailable, order entry is blocked — we never accept an order we cannot durably record." Nothing else in E29 can start until the tables and repositories exist exactly as specified in `21-database-schema.md` §3.3.4–3.3.7.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating (or extending where E27/E28 already created `exchange_accounts` / `trade_group_legs` and shared enums): `orders`, `order_events`, `executions`, `positions`, `position_snapshots`, plus enums `order_state`, `order_intent`, `order_event_kind`.
- Every constraint and index from the DDL verbatim — notably `ux_orders_link` (unique `order_link_id`), `ux_orders_exch_id`, `ix_orders_open`, `ix_orders_inflight`, `ix_orders_untracked`, `ord_link_fmt` CHECK (both arms exactly as in `21-database-schema.md` §3.3.4; the format is owned by `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3), the `leaves_qty` STORED generated column, `ux_exec_id` unique `(exchange_account_id, exec_id)`, and `ix_pos_no_sl`.
- Append-only enforcement: `forbid_mutation()` triggers `trg_oe_append` on `order_events` and `trg_exec_append` on `executions`.
- Repository layer in module **M14**: `OrderRepository`, `OrderEventRepository`, `ExecutionRepository`, `PositionRepository`, `PositionSnapshotRepository` — async SQLAlchemy Core, `Decimal` end to end (never `float`), all writes in an explicit transaction, executions inserted with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
- `PositionRepository.list_unprotected()` backed by `ix_pos_no_sl` (open position with no exchange-side stop) — the query behind the naked-position alert.
- Down-migration plus a migration test that applies and reverts against empty and populated databases.

## Out of scope
Business logic (T03/T04). Monthly partitioning of `order_events` (deferred until >20 M rows; filed as a later chore). Parquet export of detached partitions (E41). Trade-group tables (E28/E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Idempotency is enforced by the database
  Given an order with order_link_id "cvl-0TLr6mSAQFGvyfsJ0nLDCh-d0hb-00en" exists
  When a second insert with the same order_link_id is attempted
  Then the unique index rejects it and the repository raises DuplicateOrderLinkId

Scenario: History cannot be rewritten
  When an UPDATE or DELETE is attempted on order_events or executions
  Then the forbid_mutation trigger raises and the transaction aborts

Scenario: Fills deduplicate across sources
  Given execution exec_id "E1" for account A is already stored
  When the same exec_id arrives again from the WS stream and again from REST backfill
  Then exactly one row exists

Scenario: Monetary precision is preserved
  When qty 0.000000000000000001 and price 63099.80 are round-tripped
  Then the values return byte-identical as Decimal with no float in the path
```

## Technical notes / design
Numeric columns are `numeric(38,18)`; a `Decimal` type decorator maps them, and a Semgrep rule forbids `float(` on any OMS monetary value. `leaves_qty` is read-only in the mapper (generated column). Config keys: `CV_DB_DSN`, `CV_DB_POOL_MIN/MAX`, `CV_OMS_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 2000).

## Test plan
Unit: CRUD per repository; constraint-violation cases (negative qty, `cum_exec_qty > qty`, malformed `order_link_id`, illegal `position_idx`, bad TIF); dedupe path; append-only triggers. Integration: `testcontainers-python` Postgres 16, migration up/down, index-presence assertions, `EXPLAIN` assertion that `list_open_orders` uses `ix_orders_open` and `list_unprotected` uses `ix_pos_no_sl`. Coverage ≥90%.

## Security notes
`order_events.payload` stores raw exchange messages and **must be redacted of credentials and signatures before insert** (`21-database-schema.md` §3.3.5): implement `redact_exchange_payload()` and unit-test it against a fixture containing `X-BAPI-SIGN`, `X-BAPI-API-KEY` and a recv-window header. Data classification financial/restricted. Every read helper takes an account-scope argument; no unscoped `select(orders)` helper is exported (defence in depth behind the RBAC layer). Label `security`: migration touches financial records.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Open-order and open-position lookups must be index-only over the partial indexes (asserted in an integration test). The hot submit path writes the order row and its first `order_events` row in a single transaction/round trip.

## Observability
`oms_db_write_seconds{table}` histogram; `order_link_id` logged on every write for correlation.

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).

title: Implement the orderLinkId generator, collision check and adoption rules
body:
## Context
`orderLinkId` is the single mechanism that structurally prevents duplicate positions (ADR-0006 decision rule 1; `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3). It is also the correlation key for logs, metrics exemplars, audit, journal, reconciliation and UI deep links, so it must be generated exactly once and never mutated.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `OrderLinkId` value object and generator in M14 implementing the scheme from `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3:
  `{prefix:2}{env:1}-{group22}-{acct4}-{seq2}{suffix:2}` = 36 chars total, e.g. `cvl-0TLr6mSAQFGvyfsJ0nLDCh-d0hb-00en`.
  - `prefix` = `cv`; `env` ∈ `l` live / `d` demo / `t` testnet / `p` paper; `group22` = base62 of the trade-group UUID padded to 22; `acct4` = `base62(crc32(str(account_id).lower()) mod 62^4)`, zero-padded to 4 (a diagnostic tag only); `seq2` = base62 leg/child sequence 0–3843; `suffix` = purpose tag `en|sl|tp|sc|fl|ac`.
- Generation rules: generated **once before the first send**, persisted immediately, reused unchanged on every retry; amends never change it; cancel-and-replace algos allocate a new id with incremented `seq2` and record `replaces_order_id`.
- Collision check at generation: if any local row, in any state, already has the id, increment `seq2` and retry (16 increments, never past `seq2` = 3843, then raise a typed `OrderLinkIdExhausted`).
- **Success-after-lookup** rule: a duplicate-id rejection from the exchange (retCode 10001 duplicate message, or 110072) is *not* an error — query `GET /v5/order/realtime` then `/v5/order/history` for that id and adopt the true state (`20-architecture.md` §9, `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3 rule 3).
- Demo-retention rule: on demo, an id older than 6 days is unresolvable-by-history; the reconciler closes it as `Rejected` with `reject_code=DEMO_RETENTION_EXPIRED` (implemented here as a policy object consumed by T06).
- Parser/validator so any stored id can be decomposed back into `(env, group, account, seq, purpose)` for diagnostics.
- `OUR_ID` and `EXT_ID` (the two `ord_link_fmt` arms, applied with `re.fullmatch`) and `ext_key(orderId)` for adopted rows, in `candleviewer.domain` beside the `OrderLinkId` primitive, so the Bybit adapter can normalise ids without importing M14 (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.3, §14.2 rule 11).

## Out of scope
The reconciliation loop itself (T06); trade-group creation (E28/E34 — this task consumes a group UUID, creating a one-leg group is T04's job).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Deterministic and bounded
  Given a trade group, an account and a purpose
  When the id is generated twice for the same leg and sequence
  Then both results are identical, 36 characters, and match ^cv-?[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ within Bybit's charset

Scenario: Retry reuses the id
  Given a submission timed out after send
  When the submission is retried
  Then the same order_link_id is sent, so the exchange deduplicates instead of creating a second order

Scenario: Duplicate rejection is adopted, not failed
  Given Bybit rejects a create with a duplicate-orderLinkId code
  When the OMS handles it
  Then it queries realtime then history for that id and adopts the returned state rather than reporting an error to the user

Scenario: Local collision is caught
  Given an id already exists locally, in any state
  When generation is attempted for the same tuple
  Then seq2 is incremented and the collision is logged at warning with both ids
```

## Technical notes / design
Base62 alphabet `0-9A-Za-z`; UUID→base62 via big-integer conversion, zero-padded left to 22. `crc32` over the canonical lowercase UUID string. The generator is pure and total — no I/O except the collision check, which is a single indexed lookup on `ux_orders_link`. Environment character is taken from the account's environment, never from a global — a paper order and a demo order for the same group must differ.

## Test plan
Unit: length invariant across 10 000 random UUIDs/accounts (property test); charset invariant; determinism; collision-increment path; parser round-trip; env character mapping for all four environments; purpose-suffix mapping for all six purposes. ## Performance notes

title: Implement the canonical order state machine with write-ahead events
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B1). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The `frozenset` transition table, `IllegalTransition` and S6 terminal immutability become the chart plus `strict`. S1-S9 bindings, `apply_execution` and the write-ahead `CvAuditPlugin` wiring stay.

## Context
This is the heart of ADR-0006 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.2. Every order-affecting path in the product — ticket, chart, DOM, hotkey, rule, algo child, fan-out leg, paper matcher — converges here, so the transition table must be exhaustive and the illegal transitions must be impossible rather than merely unused.

## Scope / Deliverables
- State set and transition graph are defined by `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (catalogue §B1), matching `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.2 exactly: `draft, validated, submitting, submitted, partially_filled, filled, cancel_pending, cancelled, amend_pending, rejected, expired, triggered, unknown, untracked`.
- Illegal transitions are impossible by chart construction (`strictTargets`, `strict_config`); the chart's guarded-fallthrough arms audit every denied attempt, never silently ignoring it.
- Binding rules S1–S9 implemented and individually unit-tested:
  - **S1** `unknown` on any post-send transport failure; **no** resubmission from `unknown`.
  - **S2** amend rejection leaves the prior order live and unchanged, and emits an explicit `amend_rejected` event for the UI.
  - **S3** a fill arriving in `cancel_pending` wins the race → `partially_filled`/`filled`.
  - **S4** executions deduped by `exec_id`; a repeat never double-counts `filled_qty`.
  - **S5** out-of-order private pushes ordered by `(ts_exec, seq)`; a push older than `last_exchange_update` is ignored **except** fills, which are always applied.
  - **S6** terminal states are immutable; a post-terminal push raises `ReconcileAnomaly`, is audited and alerted, and does not mutate the order.
  - **S7** Postgres authoritative — if the event write fails, the in-memory state is not changed.
  - **S8** write-ahead: the append-only `order_events` row is written **before** the in-memory transition.
  - **S9** `untracked` for orders discovered on the exchange that we never created — displayed, adoptable, never auto-managed by rules.
- `apply_execution(execution)` computing `cum_exec_qty`, `cum_exec_value`, `avg_price`, `fee_paid` and deriving the resulting state.
- Deterministic replay: given an `order_events` stream, rebuilding the order yields byte-identical state (used for crash recovery and diagnostics).
- Implement the `B1` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('order', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/01_order.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_01_order.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
Transport/submission (T04), private-stream consumption (T05), reconciliation (T06), rate budgeting (E34), risk gate (E39), the native-SL guard's bracket-aware logic (E32 — T03 only exposes the `native_stop_required` rejection path).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The whole transition matrix is covered
  Given every ordered pair of states
  When a transition is attempted
  Then exactly the pairs listed in 24-internal-schemas.md §8.2 succeed and every other pair raises IllegalTransition

Scenario: Cancel loses the race to a fill
  Given an order in cancel_pending
  When a full execution arrives
  Then the order becomes filled, the cancel result is recorded as lost-race, and no error is surfaced to the user

Scenario: Amend rejection does not move the stop
  Given an order in amend_pending with price 63000
  When the exchange rejects the amend
  Then the order returns to its prior live state with price 63000 and an amend_rejected event is emitted

Scenario: Duplicate fill never double-counts
  Given execution E1 for 0.1 has been applied
  When E1 is delivered a second time
  Then filled_qty is unchanged

Scenario: Terminal state is immutable
  Given a filled order
  When a further exchange push arrives for it
  Then a ReconcileAnomaly is raised, audited and alerted, and the order is unchanged

Scenario: Crash recovery is deterministic
  Given an order_events stream for an order
  When the order is rebuilt from events alone
  Then the resulting state equals the state before the simulated crash
```

## Technical notes / design
Pure-ish core: `apply(event) -> (new_state, list[SideEffect])`; persistence is injected, so the machine is unit-testable without a database. Write-ahead ordering is enforced by construction — the persistence adapter returns only after the event row is committed. `ReconcileAnomaly` raises the `oms.reconcile_anomaly` audit event and increments a counter that alerts. Error codes exposed: `ILLEGAL_TRANSITION`, `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`, `DEMO_RETENTION_EXPIRED`, `NATIVE_STOP_REQUIRED`, `POST_TERMINAL_PUSH`.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B1.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
Unit: full N×N transition matrix (table-driven); S1–S9 each with a dedicated test; execution accumulation arithmetic with `Decimal` including partial→partial→full; out-of-order and duplicate pushes; property test that no event sequence can produce `filled_qty > qty`. Integration: rebuild-from-events against a populated Postgres. Model-based test (hypothesis stateful) driving random legal event sequences and asserting the invariants `0 ≤ filled_qty ≤ qty`, `terminal ⇒ immutable`, `event.seq` monotone. Coverage ≥95%.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B1.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Repudiation is the primary threat: `order_events` is the non-repudiation record, so the write-ahead rule and the append-only trigger are security controls, not just correctness ones. Every transition records `source` ∈ `local|rest|ws_private|reconcile|paper` — a transition claiming an exchange source must carry the raw payload (redacted) that justifies it. Review for injection via exchange-supplied `retMsg` stored in `reject_message` (stored as text, never interpolated into SQL or rendered as HTML).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI. State names surfaced to the UI must have human-readable labels defined in the copy deck (E29-D06).

## Performance notes
A transition (including the event write) must complete in ≤5 ms p95 so it fits inside the ≤50 ms backend portion of budget #4. The machine holds no global lock — concurrency is per-order via a keyed lock on `order_id`.

## Observability
`oms_state_transitions_total{from,to,source}`, `oms_illegal_transitions_total` (alert >0), `oms_reconcile_anomaly_total` (alert >0), span per transition with `order_link_id` exemplar.

title: Consume the private WS streams as the source of truth for orders, fills and positions
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B1). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. Maps pushes to events; `(ts_exec, seq)` ordering stays in bindings (MUSTNOT-04).

## Context
ADR-0006 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.4 are explicit: "The synchronous REST response is an acknowledgement of acceptance, not a fill confirmation — the private WS `order`/`execution` streams are the source of truth." This task wires those streams into the state machine and out to the UI over the `orders`/`positions`/`executions`/`wallet` topics, which `23-ws-protocol.md` forbids throttling or coalescing (S4).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Private-stream consumer in M14 subscribing per account to Bybit `order`, `execution.fast`, `position`, `wallet` (live `/v5/private`, demo `stream-demo`), with re-auth on reconnect and a heartbeat watchdog.
- Normalisation into the internal models of `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.1 (`Order`, `Execution`, `Position`) and dispatch as events into the B1 `order` chart (`statechart.gateway.send`) plus `apply_execution` / `apply_position` in the binding module.
- **Causal ordering** (`23-ws-protocol.md` S5): emit `executions` → `orders` → `positions` → `trade_groups` on the outbound bus so a UI never sees an effect before its cause; a reorder buffer keyed on `(ts_exec, seq)` if K01 observed exchange-side violations.
- Position projection into `positions` plus a `position_snapshots` row on `ws_push`; `wallet` balances projected for the equity figures the blotter and risk views need.
- One `execution` message may bundle several fills — each stored individually keyed by `exec_id` (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `/executions`).
- Outbound WS publication of the four private topics with account-scope intersection and silent narrowing (`23-ws-protocol.md` §private topics), `snapshot + delta` semantics, and the slow-consumer rule: if the client cannot keep up with `orders`/`executions`, close with `bye slow_consumer` / code 4429 rather than degrade them.
- Heartbeat/watchdog: on loss of the private stream, mark affected accounts `resyncing`, notify the `system` topic, and trigger a reconciliation pass (T06) on reconnect.
- Implement the `B1` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B01.order.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('order', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/01_order.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_01_order.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
The reconciliation algorithm itself (T06); WS transport/framing (E17); market-data topics; the frontend consumer (S01–S07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: WS truth overrides the REST ack
  Given a REST ack reported state submitted
  When the private stream reports the order was already filled
  Then local state becomes filled and the ack is recorded only as an acceptance event

Scenario: Causal order is preserved
  When a fill causes an order transition and a position change
  Then subscribers receive the execution frame before the order frame and the order frame before the position frame

Scenario: Bundled fills are split
  Given one exchange execution message containing three fills
  Then three execution rows exist, each keyed by its own exec_id

Scenario: Slow consumer is disconnected, not degraded
  Given a client cannot drain the orders topic within the queue budget
  Then the server sends bye slow_consumer and closes with 4429 rather than dropping order frames

Scenario: Stream loss is visible and triggers resync
  Given the private stream drops for 30 seconds
  Then affected accounts are marked resyncing on the system topic
  And a reconciliation pass runs on reconnect
```

## Technical notes / design
One consumer task per account with its own `asyncio.TaskGroup`; module `stop()` drains with the OMS's 15 s grace window (`20-architecture.md` §Start/stop order). Backpressure: bounded queue per subscriber; `orders`/`executions` are never dropped — the connection is closed instead. Config: `CV_PRIVATE_WS_HEARTBEAT_S` (20), `CV_PRIVATE_WS_RESUB_BACKOFF` (1,2,4,8, cap 30 s, jittered).
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B1.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
Unit: normalisation of every fixture message shape; reorder buffer; bundled-fill splitting; scope intersection. Integration: fixture-replay of a recorded private session including a mid-sequence disconnect, asserting zero missed executions after backfill; slow-consumer simulation. Contract: outbound frames validated against the `orders`/`positions`/`executions` JSON Schemas in `23-ws-protocol.md` §15. Chaos (feeds Q04): 60 s stream kill, duplicate pushes, out-of-order pushes, post-terminal push. Coverage ≥90%.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B1.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Private topics are account-scoped: the server intersects requested `exchange_account_ids` with the caller's granted scope and narrows silently; requesting only out-of-scope accounts errors with `account_scope_denied` (`23-ws-protocol.md`). Permissions required: `orders:read`, `positions:read`, `executions:read`, `accounts:read`. Cross-account leakage through the outbound fan-out is the highest-value threat here and gets a dedicated abuse test in E29-X02. Raw exchange payloads are redacted before being persisted in `order_events`.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI, but the `resyncing` / `disconnected` system states drive SCR-152 messaging designed in D03.

## Performance notes
`orders`/`executions` have `throttle_ms: 0` and must never be coalesced; `positions` may be coalesced at 10 Hz for the blotter. Backend-internal fan-out portion ≤20 ms p95 (budget #6). Private-stream processing must not be shed under load — `20-architecture.md` §shedding ladder puts OMS/private stream last and states order-related work is never shed.

title: Produce the STRIDE threat model for the OMS and its order-placement path
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4 names E29 as one of six epics requiring a STRIDE model with **all Critical/High findings closed** before the R3 gate, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1 requires the model to be kicked off at epic start for anything touching the OMS. The OMS is the component that turns a request into money moving, so the model must be finished before E29-T04 (the submission pipeline) merges - it is a design input, not a review artefact.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model in `docs/security/e29-oms-threat-model.md` with a data-flow diagram covering: client -> REST `/orders` -> RiskGate -> OMS -> RateBudget -> BybitAdapter -> Bybit, and Bybit private WS -> OMS -> Postgres -> WS fan-out -> client.
- Threats enumerated per STRIDE category per element and per data flow, each with a rating, a control, and the ticket that implements the control. At minimum: spoofed order origin; tampering with quantity or account between client and OMS; repudiation of a placed or cancelled order; cross-account information disclosure through REST, WS subscription or execution marks; denial of service by order flooding or by exhausting a UID's rate budget with background traffic; elevation of privilege through a manager acting on an unt granted account or through the `untracked` adoption path.
- Explicit analysis of the idempotency key as a security control: what an attacker who can predict or replay an `order_link_id` can do, and why the collision check and the persisted-before-send rule bound it.
- Analysis of `order_events.payload` as a credential-leak channel and the redaction requirement it produces.
- Abuse cases handed to E29-X02, and any control gap filed as a ticket before the model is signed off.

## Out of scope
Key storage and envelope encryption (E27's model), fan-out unwind threats (E34), rule-engine sandbox threats (E35), kill-switch bypass (E39), penetration testing (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Complete coverage
  Then every element and data flow in the diagram has each of the six STRIDE categories either addressed with a control or explicitly argued not applicable

Scenario: Controls are traceable
  Then every Critical or High threat names the ticket implementing its control and that ticket references this model

Scenario: The model gates the pipeline
  Given E29-T04 is ready to merge
  Then this model is complete and its Critical/High controls are either implemented or scheduled with an agreed date

Scenario: Idempotency is analysed as a control
  Then the model states what an attacker who replays or predicts an order_link_id can and cannot achieve
```

## Technical notes / design
The model uses the data-flow decomposition already in `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.4 rather than inventing a parallel one, so the diagram and the implementation cannot drift. Ratings use the programme's standard likelihood/impact matrix from `04-security-program.md`. Where a control lives in another epic (RBAC in E09, keys in E27, risk caps in E39), the model records the dependency explicitly instead of restating the control.

## Test plan
Reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect; each Critical/High control is later evidenced by a test in E29-X02 or in the story that implements it. The model is re-reviewed at the R3 gate as part of the continuous OMS threat-model refresh cadence (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 12 bar `s05`).

## Security notes
This ticket is the security artefact. Data classification for the whole epic is set here: financial/restricted for orders, positions and executions; secret for anything in `order_events.payload` before redaction.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - documentation.

## Performance notes
Notes the DoS-relevant budget interactions: the protective reserve in the rate budget is a security control as well as a safety one, because it prevents a flood of normal traffic from starving a stop-loss.

## Observability
Names the audit and metric signals each threat relies on for detection: `oms_unknown_orders`, `oms_rate_reject_total`, the audit rows for every mutation, and alerting on cross-scope 403s.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact merged (threat model in `docs/security/`, rules under `.semgrep/` or the CI config, tests under `tests/security/`).

title: Hi-fi SCR-076, SCR-077, SCR-114 and the account / trade-group selector
body:
## Context
The ticket is only half the surface. The **confirmation modal** is the last thing between a human and a live order; the **rejection drawer** is where trust is won or lost after a failure; **trading defaults** decides how much friction exists at all; and the **account / trade-group selector** is where a single intent silently becomes five orders. Each has its own catalogue sign-off checklist and each is drawn here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi for **SCR-076 Order confirmation modal**: full restatement (environment, account(s), side, symbol, type, qty, price, brackets, estimated cost, resulting exposure, profile-limit results), the 20 s inactivity auto-cancel countdown, the **LIVE variant visually distinct from DEMO**, "don't ask again" available for DEMO only, the fan-out variant listing every leg, and **no default-focused confirm button for LIVE market orders**.
- Hi-fi for **SCR-077 Order rejection detail drawer**: verbatim exchange message plus plain-language translation, written copy for every common reason (insufficient margin, reduce-only violation, tick/lot rounding, leverage limit, risk-limit tier, rate limit, position-mode mismatch), the retry-with-fix affordance where the fix is unambiguous, the copyable correlation id, and the owner's link to the audit record.
- Hi-fi for **SCR-158 Rate-limited state**: the three scope variants, the countdown, what is still permitted, the fan-out case naming served vs unserved accounts, and the held-action queue with explicit replay confirmation.
- Hi-fi for **SCR-114 Trading defaults**: separate DEMO and LIVE default sets, "skip confirmation" unavailable for LIVE market orders, the default SL that cannot be "none", inline profile ceilings with the pointer to SCR-131, validation messages and reset-to-defaults.
- Hi-fi for the **account / trade-group selector** (the SCR-061 slice consumed by the ticket): single account vs named group, the per-leg expansion, would-be-rejected legs with their reasons, and the narrowed-group treatment when the user lacks scope on a member account.
- Order-template list and save/apply affordances (US-ORD-012), including the disabled template with its reason.

## Out of scope
SCR-060 itself (E30-D02), SCR-061's full group-management layout and SCR-062 (E28), SCR-131 (E28), SCR-147 (E42), motion (E30-D04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Each screen's own catalogue sign-off checklist is satisfied
  Then the SCR-076, SCR-077, SCR-158 and SCR-114 design sign-off checklists are each fully ticked
Scenario: Live is never as easy as demo
  Given the LIVE variants of SCR-076 and SCR-114
  Then confirmation cannot be skipped for market orders, the confirm button is not default-focused, and the environment is restated in the confirm copy
Scenario: Every rejection reason has written copy
  Then each reason listed in the SCR-077 checklist has final plain-language copy in the design, not a placeholder
Scenario: A fan-out is never implicit
  Given a trade-group target
  Then the confirmation lists every leg with its own account, size and stop before anything is sent
```

## Technical notes / design
Copy is a design deliverable here, not an engineering afterthought: every rejection translation, every disabled reason and every consequence line in the confirmation-policy radio group is written, reviewed and frozen in this ticket, and lands in `order-ticket-core/errors.ts` verbatim.

The confirmation modal is designed to be constructible from already-loaded state (no fetch on open) so it can meet its 100 ms appearance budget â€” that constrains what it may display, and the design respects it.

## Test plan
N/A (design). Copy is reviewed by product and by the Security engineer (for the LIVE and audit-related wording) before sign-off.

## Security notes
The rejection drawer design must show a **redacted** payload â€” the frames explicitly show what redaction looks like, so engineering does not have to invent it. No frame shows a key, signature or token, even as fake data, to avoid normalising the pattern.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-076: the confirm button's accessible name restates the whole order; `Enter` confirms only after 400 ms; focus is trapped and returns to the submit control on cancel. SCR-077: `role="alert"` on open, quoted-text vs prose distinction drawn. SCR-158: `role="status"`, countdown announced at most every 10 s. SCR-114: fieldsets per topic, units on every numeric field, consequence stated in each policy option. Contrast and focus states checked on all four.

## Performance notes
SCR-076 must be renderable from in-memory state within 100 ms; SCR-077 opens without a fetch in the common case, with the raw payload lazily expanded.

## Observability
The frames annotate which interactions emit which audit/analytics events (`order.confirmation_shown`, `order.confirmation_cancelled`, `order.rejection_viewed`, `trading_defaults.changed`) so instrumentation is specified, not inferred.
