title: Measure order-path latency: recompute, click-to-request and hotkey
body:
## Context
Three client-side numbers gate this Epic and none of them has been measured yet on the real app shell:
1. SCR-060 requires **every input to recompute risk/fee/margin in â‰¤8 ms** (pure client-side).
2. Budget #4 (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§5.2) allows **p95 <300 ms clickâ†’ack on demo**, of which â‰¤50 ms is backend-added and ~250 ms is Bybit demo REST RTT â€” leaving almost nothing for the client. We must know what the gestureâ†’`fetch()` portion actually costs inside the Electron shell with a live workspace (chart + footprint + ladder) already consuming frame budget.
3. US-ORD-006 requires **hotkeyâ†’submit â‰¤50 ms client-side**.

If the ticket cannot hit these while sharing a renderer with the WebGL chart engine, the architecture must change *before* E30-T01 is written â€” e.g. moving the sizing reducer into a worker, or decoupling the submit path from React's render cycle with a direct imperative dispatch. That is exactly what this spike decides.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. This spike is explicitly **not expected to produce production-shippable code**; the harness it builds may be promoted into E30-Q03.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A throwaway harness on `spike/e30-ticket-latency` mounting a stub of CMP-107 OrderTicket inside the real app shell (SCR-010) with a chart panel (SCR-030) and a DOM ladder panel (SCR-050) live on demo data, so the measurement includes realistic main-thread contention.
- Measure, with `performance.mark`/`measure` and 1 000 samples each: (a) full ticket recompute after a price keystroke, a qty keystroke and a sizing-mode switch; (b) gestureâ†’`fetch()` dispatch for pointer click, `Ctrl+Enter` and a bound hotkey; (c) WS `orders` event â†’ rendered state transition.
- Compare three reducer placements: synchronous in the React event handler, in a `useSyncExternalStore` store outside React rendering, and in a worker with a structured-clone hop.
- Record results against the three budgets in a comparison table on the ticket and in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`.

## Out of scope
Backend latency (E29 measures its own â‰¤50 ms), Bybit RTT, production styling, real order submission (the harness posts to a local stub).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The three budgets are answered with numbers
  When the spike closes
  Then p50/p95/p99 are recorded for recompute, click->dispatch and hotkey->dispatch under a loaded workspace
  And each is stated as PASS or FAIL against 8 ms, the budget #4 client allowance and 50 ms
Scenario: A decision follows from the numbers
  Given recompute p95 exceeds 8 ms in the synchronous-React placement
  Then the ADR records the store-outside-React or worker placement as the mandated design for E30-T01
Scenario: A failing result escalates rather than being absorbed
  Given no placement meets the hotkey budget under a loaded workspace
  Then a risk entry is added to docs/plan/32-risk-register.md and the Architect is asked for a scope decision before S16 planning closes
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure with the chart engine actually rendering (E11/E12 build), not a blank page â€” main-thread contention is the whole point. Use `chrome://tracing` / Electron's tracing to attribute time between React reconciliation, layout and the reducer itself. For the worker variant, measure the structured-clone cost of the `OrderDraft` + `Instrument` + `Wallet` snapshot payload, which is the dominant term at this size.

Sampling method: 1 000 synthetic keystrokes via `dispatchEvent` on the focused input at 20 Hz (a realistic fast-typing rate), interleaved with live WS traffic at the reference workspace rate from `23-ws-protocol.md` Â§16.3. Report p50/p95/p99 and the worst 1% tail, not the mean.

## Test plan
The harness is itself the test. Reproducibility: the run script is checked into the spike branch with a fixed synthetic-input seed; two independent runs must agree within 15% at p95 or the measurement is rejected as noisy and repeated on a quiet machine.

## Security notes
The harness must not hold a real API key or submit to a real exchange endpoint; it posts to a local stub only. No credentials on the spike branch (secret scanning applies to spike branches too).

## Accessibility notes
N/A â€” throwaway measurement harness with no shipped UI. The a11y properties of the real ticket are covered by E30-D05 and E30-Q05.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance work. Budgets under test: 8 ms recompute (SCR-060), budget #4 client portion (Â§5.2), 50 ms hotkeyâ†’submit (US-ORD-006 NFR).

## Observability
The chosen instrumentation (`cv_ticket_recompute_ms`, `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms`) is prototyped here and promoted into E30-T01 so the budgets stay measurable in production, not only in the spike.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Comparison table with p50/p95/p99 for all three placements recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] ADR written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` recording the chosen reducer placement (even if the decision is "synchronous is fine").
- [ ] E30-T01 updated with the mandated design before it starts.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a budget cannot be met.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; branch left unmerged and archived.

## Dependencies
- **E29** â€” the `/orders` request shape being dispatched (a stub is acceptable if E29's contract is merged).
- **E13** app shell / design system and **E11/E12** chart engine build, to reproduce realistic main-thread load.

`spike/e30-ticket-latency` (throwaway, never merged). PR: none; findings posted on the ticket.

title: UX research and hi-fi design for the chart trading layer (SCR-030, SCR-040)
body:
## Context
E31 introduces direct-manipulation trading (US-ORD-007..011, US-DOM-007..008) — the highest-consequence interaction in the product: a stray mouse-down can open real risk. Before any pixels are drawn we must settle the interaction vocabulary (which modifier does what, what is draggable, what confirms, what can be undone) against how the Owner and the account managers actually work today in TradingView/DeepCharts-class tools.

This is net-new interaction, so `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 design-ready and the planning brief's design-ahead rule (≥2 sprints) require research first, landing in Sprint 13 so hi-fi can be Done by Sprint 15 for build in Sprint 17.

SCR-030 is the spine of the product and already carries footprint cells, drawings, indicators and profile overlays. E31 adds the **trading layer**: position line (avg price, size, uPnL, R), SL/TP lines, working-order lines, fill markers, fan-out sibling ghost lines, liquidation-estimate line, break-even line and the arm-state display. SCR-040 is the modal that toggles each of those elements and the drag-to-modify behaviour.

Design must be Done by end of Sprint 15 so the FE stories (E31-S01/S02, Sprint 17) satisfy the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Research plan + 3–5 moderated sessions with the Owner and account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) using the existing SCR-030 chart and SCR-050 ladder builds from R1/R2 as a think-aloud prop.
- Answer, with evidence, for SCR-030 / SCR-050:
  - Which modifier map is expected for chart order entry (the catalogue currently states `Ctrl+drag` on the price axis = limit, `Alt+click` = market at market; US-ORD-007 states `Shift+click` = limit on the opposite side, `Ctrl+click` = reduce-only stop — **this conflict must be resolved and the winner written back into `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030 and `11-user-stories.md` US-ORD-007**).
  - Whether drag-to-amend should commit on release or require a release-then-confirm for live.
  - Acceptable undo window length and its affordance (toast with Undo vs. Ctrl+Z) for accidental drags/clicks.
  - Expectation for ladder left-click vs right-click vs Ctrl+click (US-DOM-007 says left = limit at row, Ctrl = market, Escape = cancel-all).
  - Confirmation tolerance: where does confirmation feel protective vs. obstructive (feeds the configurable confirm policy owned by E30/SCR-076).
- A written **interaction vocabulary decision record** (modifier map table) appended to the SCR-040 entry, signed by the Owner.
- Findings note in `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` F6/F7 annotations.

- Hi-fi Figma frames for **SCR-030 trading layer** covering every element listed in the SCR-040 catalogue entry: position line, SL line, TP line, working-order lines (limit / stop / conditional / reduce-only variants, buy and sell), fill markers, per-account ghost lines for fan-out, liquidation-estimate line with CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, break-even line, armed/disarmed chrome.
- Interaction states per line: idle · hover (drag handle revealed, ≥24 px) · dragging (ghost line + live price/Δ/R readout + snapped-to-tick indicator) · pending-amend · rejected (spring-back + reason chip) · keyboard-focused (visible focus ring on the DOM-mirrored line) · disabled-because-disarmed (lock cursor + tooltip "One-click trading is off").
- **Legibility over footprint**: specified treatment (halo/scrim, minimum contrast) so trading lines stay readable over dense footprint cells and the heatmap — the SCR-030 sign-off checklist item.
- Chart order entry affordance: the price-axis / price-area affordance for the modifier map chosen in E31-D01, incl. the invalid-side refusal inline explanation (US-ORD-007 scenario 3).
- **SCR-040 Chart trading overlay settings** hi-fi: a toggle per overlay element, the drag-to-modify on/off choice with an explicit written risk note, the "confirm when the new SL is on the wrong side of the mark" copy, and the statement in text that a keyboard alternative exists via SCR-064.
- Undo affordance: the toast/inline control, its dwell time, and what it says after the underlying order already filled.
- All copy strings written (not lorem), including the wrong-side confirm and the snapped-to-tick tooltip ("Snapped to 0.5 tick").
- Light and dark themes, comfortable and compact density, per `16-design-system-brief.md`.

## Out of scope
Visual design (E31-D02/D03). Hotkey remapping UI (E30/SET). Any implementation.

DOM ladder affordances (E31-D03). Order ticket form (E30 designs). Motion spec (E31-D04). Implementation.

```gherkin
  Given the catalogue and the story text disagree on the chart-trading modifier map

Scenario: Participants could not complete a dangerous action accidentally

```


title: Prove drag latency, overlay hit-testing and the trading-layer frame budget
body:
## Context
E31 puts *trading-critical, never-sheddable* content onto a canvas that is already at its frame budget with 100k bars, footprint and a 200-depth heatmap (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.2, §4). Two engineering unknowns must be settled before E31-T01 fixes the architecture:

1. **Hit-testing**: can the engine resolve "which order line / which ladder row is under the pointer" within the pointer-event budget while lines overlap drawings and footprint cells (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.9)?
2. **Latency**: US-DOM-007 and US-ORD-006 demand click→submit ≤50 ms client-side. Is that achievable when the pointer event must cross from the canvas/worker boundary into React state and out to `fetch`?

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype (throwaway) on the R2 engine build measuring, on the reference machine:
  - pointerdown → intent resolved (side, type, price snapped to tick, resolved qty) in ms, p50/p95, under (a) idle chart, (b) worst case: 100k bars + footprint + heatmap + 20 order lines + live ladder.
  - overlay layer redraw cost per frame with 1, 5, 20 and 50 lines (SCR-040 budget: ≤2 ms).
  - drag follow latency (pointermove → line repositioned on screen) and whether it holds at 60 fps while the shedding ladder is active.
- Determine where drag state must live: main thread vs worker (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §6 worker/OffscreenCanvas protocol) — a drag that round-trips to a worker per move may miss the budget.
- Determine the hit-test strategy: spatial index over line prices vs. GPU picking vs. DOM-mirror elements as the hit surface (the DOM mirror already exists for a11y — reusing it may be both cheapest and most accessible).
- Confirm that trading-line updates can be exempted from the shedding ladder without breaking the ladder's guarantees.

## Out of scope
Production code, visual polish, any order actually being sent (measure to the point of `fetch` call, then stub).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Latency question answered with numbers
  Given the worst-case scene
  Then p50 and p95 for pointerdown -> intent-resolved are recorded, and the result states whether the 50 ms client-side budget holds

Scenario: Overlay budget answered
  Then redraw cost at 1/5/20/50 lines is recorded against the 2 ms budget, with the line count at which it is exceeded

Scenario: A decision, not just data
  Then an ADR records the chosen hit-test strategy and drag-state location, and states the fallback if the budget fails
  (e.g. cap concurrently drawn lines with an explicit "N more orders" affordance)
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure with `performance.now()` around the real event path, and with the Chrome tracing timeline for frame attribution. Test in both Electron (primary shell) and plain Chromium. Reference machine per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Test plan
Benchmark harness only; results reproducible by a checked-in script under `packages/chart-engine/bench/`. No coverage requirement (spike).

## Security notes
Prototype must be hard-wired to a stub submit function; it must not carry any credential or reach any exchange endpoint, not even demo.

## Accessibility notes
If the DOM-mirror is chosen as the hit surface, record the implications for focus order and for the a11y mirror's sync guarantee (`06-...` §4.3 forbids desyncing the mirror from what is rendered).

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance investigation; its numbers become the baseline assertions in E31-Q03.

## Observability
Propose the metric names E31-T01 should emit: `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms`, `cv_trading_overlay_redraw_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All three questions answered with recorded evidence.
- [ ] **ADR-0017 chart-trading interaction & hit-testing** written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (even if the decision is "defer").
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path was chosen, with findings linked.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated for R2 render performance.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; prototype branch archived unmerged.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (chart engine interaction loop and hit-testing) and **E21** (the rendered DOM ladder) — both complete well before R3 opens, so this spike runs in **Sprint 16**, strictly ahead of the S17–S18 E31 train window (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2).

**Why this spike deliberately does *not* depend on E29/E30/E32/E39.** It is a rendering-and-input-latency experiment only: it drags a *fake* overlay against recorded data and submits nothing. It uses a stubbed intent sink — no API keys, no OMS, no live account — so it cannot be blocked by the order-placing stack. The real dependencies on **E29** (OMS + private WS), **E30** (arm/lock, confirm policy, hotkeys), **E32** (native-SL invariant) and **E39** (risk caps, kill-switch) are carried by **E31-T01** and by the individual stories, each of which is scheduled strictly *after* the sprint in which its blocker completes — see the epic's Dependency graph table. Running this spike a sprint early is what buys the S17–S18 window its schedule slack: the latency and hit-testing unknowns are closed before any dependent story starts.

## Branch

title: Wireframe SCR-064, SCR-065 and SCR-069 with every state enumerated
body:
## Context
`14-screens-catalogue.md` enumerates the required states for each E32 screen, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1 makes "states enumerated (empty, loading, error, populated, edge-density)" a Story DoR item. Wireframes are where those states get drawn before colour, type and motion make disagreements expensive to resolve.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Low-fidelity wireframes in Figma for `SCR-064` (position SL/TP editor), `SCR-065` (scaled / ladder builder) and `SCR-069` (bracket builder — bracket half; the OCO half is annotated as E33's extension point).
- Every state drawn: SCR-064 — loading, editing, validating, pending-acknowledgement, applied, rejected, position-closed-while-editing; SCR-065 — preview, placing with per-child progress, partial-placement failure with retry, risk-cap refusal, cancelled, error; SCR-069 — empty, editing, validating, submitting, submitted, partial placement failure, error.
- The three entry-mode variants (price / ticks / percent / R-multiple) drawn at least once each.
- The native-SL floor treatment from E32-D01's recommendation applied consistently across all three screens.
- Layout for the ladder preview table including cumulative columns and the resulting-average row.
- Annotated with the validation copy from each screen's spec ("Ladder totals 110% — reduce a step.", "Child 5 is below the minimum — reduce the order count.", "Every position keeps a native stop — you can move it, not delete it.").
- Review walkthrough with the E32 engineering lead and QA so states that are hard to implement or hard to test are caught now.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi visuals, tokens, motion (E32-D03/D04/D05/D06); the OCO half of SCR-069 (E33).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued state exists as a frame
  Given the three screens' state lists in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the wireframe file is reviewed
  Then each listed state has its own named frame and no state is represented only by a note

Scenario: Validation copy is drawn, not deferred
  Given the validation rules in each screen spec
  Then each rule's message appears in the frame where it fires, in the position it will occupy, rather than in a separate copy document

Scenario: A state that cannot be built is resolved before hi-fi (edge)
  Given engineering flags a drawn state as infeasible against the E32 API contract
  Then the state is redesigned or the API delta is filed as a change request against the owning backend ticket before this ticket closes
```

## Technical notes / design
Wireframes use the density and spacing scale from `16-design-system-brief.md` so the hi-fi step is a re-skin rather than a re-layout. Frames are named `SCR-0xx / <state>` to match the catalogue exactly, because E32-D08's design QA and E32-Q07's a11y audit both index by that naming.

## Test plan
N/A — design artefact. Review gate: engineering lead + QA + accessibility specialist walkthrough recorded.

## Security notes
Wireframes must not depict real account identifiers, balances or keys; placeholder data only.

## Accessibility notes
Focus order is annotated on every frame. Error and status regions are marked with their intended ARIA role. The keyboard path equivalent to chart drag-to-modify is drawn explicitly on SCR-064 rather than assumed.

## Performance notes
The ladder preview layout must be drawn at 50 rows (the maximum) to confirm the modal remains usable at the cap.

## Observability
Each interactive control is annotated with the analytics/audit event it must emit, taken from the screens' analytics sections, so engineering does not have to infer them.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states drawn and named to match the catalogue.
- [ ] Validation copy placed in situ.
- [ ] Walkthrough held with engineering, QA and accessibility; notes recorded.
- [ ] Open questions resolved or filed against the owning tickets.
- [ ] CDO review recorded.

`E32-D01` (mental-model findings, especially the native-SL expression).

`design/e32-wireframes` (Figma link recorded on the ticket).

title: Measure attached-SL versus trading-stop attach latency and failure modes on demo
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8 allows two ways a position acquires its native stop: **attached** on `POST /v5/order/create` (`stopLoss` field, rule 1) or **position-level** via `POST /v5/position/trading-stop` on first fill within a 2 s deadline (rule 2). The whole E32 design — the choke point (E32-T01), the watchdog deadline (E32-T02) and the bracket child-sizing policy (E32-S01) — depends on numbers we do not have yet: how long each path actually takes on Bybit demo, which Bybit `retCode`s each path returns when it fails, and whether attached SL survives partial fills and amends. Guessing these would mean re-deriving them under deadline pressure in S16, on the R3 critical path.

Section 8.9 also records a known trap: one-sided TP/SL modification via `trading-stop` breaks Bybit's OCO pairing, so our writes must always send both sides. The spike must confirm this on demo rather than trusting the note.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Timeboxed **3 days**, `spike/e32-sl-attach-latency`, throwaway harness (not production code).
- Harness in `services/oms/spikes/sl_attach_bench.py` driving a Bybit **demo** account from E27's vault against `api-demo.bybit.com`, USDT linear perps only (`BTCUSDT`, `ETHUSDT`, plus one low-liquidity symbol).
- Measure, >=200 samples per arm: (a) `order/create` with attached `stopLoss` -> ack latency; (b) `order/create` without SL, then `position/trading-stop` on first execution event -> confirmed latency, measured from the WS execution timestamp.
- Record failure taxonomy: every distinct `retCode`/`retMsg` returned by each arm, mapped to the internal taxonomy in section 8.6.
- Answer explicitly: does attached `stopLoss` survive (1) a partial fill, (2) a `PATCH` amend of the entry price, (3) a reduce-only child placed against the same position, (4) hedge-mode `positionIdx=1/2`?
- Confirm the one-sided-write OCO-pairing trap and the correct both-sides write shape.
- Measure the rate-limit cost of each arm (requests per protected position) to feed `RateBudget.reserved_for_protective` sizing in section 8.7.

## Out of scope
- Any production code; live environment; non-Bybit venues; batch/ladder submission (covered by E32-S03's own measurements).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both arms are measured with a decision-grade sample
  Given the harness has run at least 200 samples per arm on Bybit demo across three symbols
  When results are tabulated
  Then p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate and the full retCode histogram are reported per arm, and the report states whether the 2 s attach deadline in section 8.8 rule 2 is achievable with margin

Scenario: The attached-SL survival questions are answered
  Given partial fill, entry amend, reduce-only child and hedge-mode scenarios are each executed at least 10 times
  Then the report states for each, with evidence, whether the attached stopLoss persists, is cleared, or is silently altered

Scenario: The trading-stop pairing trap is confirmed or refuted (edge)
  Given a position with both TP and SL set
  When only the SL side is written via trading-stop
  Then the observed effect on the TP side is recorded, and the report prescribes the exact request shape E32-T01 must use

Scenario: The spike ends in a decision, not a document (failure path)
  Given the measurements show the 2 s deadline is not achievable on demo
  Then the ADR records "attach-only, refuse orders that cannot carry an attached SL" as the chosen fallback, and follow-up tickets are filed against E32-T01 and E32-T02 before the spike closes
```

## Technical notes / design
- Drive the harness through E29's adapter so measurements reflect real client overhead, not a bespoke HTTP client.
- Latency for arm (b) is measured from the `execution` WS message's exchange timestamp to the `trading-stop` HTTP 200, which is the interval the 2 s deadline actually covers.
- Clock skew: record `X-Bapi-*` response headers and the exchange timestamp with every sample; discard samples where local-vs-exchange skew exceeds 500 ms.
- Emit raw samples to a Parquet file under `artifacts/spikes/e32-k01/` so the numbers can be re-analysed rather than only summarised.
- Decision criteria agreed with the Architect up front: if arm (b) p99 > 1.5 s, the OMS defaults to attach-only and algo children that would over-attach are restructured rather than accepting a trading-stop window.

## Test plan
No production tests. The harness self-checks that each sample has a matching execution event and a matching position state, discarding incomplete samples; the discard rate is reported.

## Security notes
Uses a **demo** key only, read from the E27 vault at runtime — never inlined, never committed. Raw artifacts must not contain the API key, account UID, or IP; the harness redacts these on write. No live credentials may be configured for this ticket (enforced by the environment gate in M1).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
This ticket *produces* the performance inputs for budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2); it is not itself gated by a budget.

## Observability
The harness emits the same metric names the production path will use (`oms_native_sl_attach_seconds`) so the dashboards built in E32-T02 can be validated against spike data before real traffic exists.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both arms measured, tables and histograms published in the ticket.
- [ ] All four attached-SL survival questions answered with evidence.
- [ ] ADR-0016 draft section "attach vs trading-stop" written (merged later by E32-T04).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed or explicitly not needed, with reason.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` RSK-016 updated with the measured residual-exposure window.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; branch archived unmerged.

## Dependencies
`E27` (demo key vault), `E29` (adapter + order state machine to measure through).

## Branch
`spike/e32-sl-attach-latency`. Throwaway; no PR to `main` expected beyond the ADR draft.

title: UX research: how traders configure and trust an emulated algorithm
body:
## Context
E33 introduces four order types that **do not exist at the exchange**. The product promises behaviour that only holds while CandleViewer's backend is alive, which is a fundamentally different trust contract from a native order. Every screen in SCR-066..070 therefore carries an honesty burden that no other trading screen has, and `11-user-stories.md` §18 NFRs repeat it: iceberg "must be labelled (app-managed) everywhere it appears"; the OCO builder must explain race resolution and residual risk; the monitor panel must say that algos suspend while the backend reconnects and native stops still protect.

Nobody has tested whether that message actually lands. This research answers: do traders understand what "emulated" costs them, what mental model do they bring to slicing/pegging configuration, which parameters do they actually tune, and what do they expect to happen when the app goes away mid-algo?

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated sessions with the Owner and 4–6 comparable active perpetual-futures traders (recruit from the existing research panel; sessions ≤ 60 min).
- Stimuli: competitor iceberg/TWAP/chase builders, a paper prototype of the SCR-066..069 parameter sets, and a scripted "the backend just died mid-TWAP" scenario.
- Research questions:
  1. Which parameters do traders set themselves versus expect a sensible default for (slice count vs duration; visible size vs show-ratio; peg offset vs max chase distance)?
  2. How do they interpret "emulated / app-managed"? Does the phrase communicate residual risk, or do they read it as a technicality?
  3. What do they expect on disconnect — cancel everything, freeze, or continue? (The system's answer is `freeze`; the research tests whether that matches expectation and how to phrase it if it does not.)
  4. What do they need to see in a monitor panel to feel that "nothing is running invisibly" (US-ALGO-010)?
  5. What is the minimum acceptable pre-submit information — schedule preview, projected request rate, slippage estimate?
- Deliverables: a findings report in `docs/research/` with verbatim quotes, a prioritised list of design implications, recommended default parameter values per strategy, and the agreed wording for the emulation caveat and the disconnect message (which becomes binding copy for E33-D02/D03).

## Out of scope
Visual design (D02/D03). Testing built software (that is E33-Q06 exploratory + the a11y audit). Rule-engine or bracket UX (E32/E35–E37).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Findings answer every research question
  Given the sessions are complete
  Then the report answers all five research questions with evidence, not opinion,
  and each answer names the screens it affects

Scenario: Emulation wording decided
  Given participants read candidate phrasings of the emulation caveat
  Then one phrasing per strategy is chosen with evidence that participants correctly restated
  the residual risk in their own words, and that phrasing is recorded as binding copy

Scenario: Defaults recommended (edge)
  Given disagreement between participants on a parameter default
  Then the report states the disagreement, recommends a default with its rationale,
  and flags the parameter as one to revisit after the R3 soak
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the existing research protocol and consent process. Sessions recorded with consent; recordings stored per the research data-handling rules in `04-security-program.md`. Do not demo real accounts — use demo credentials and synthetic positions.

## Test plan
N/A — research. Validity controls: at least one participant unfamiliar with CandleViewer to catch jargon; the disconnect scenario is run *before* any explanation is given, so comprehension is measured rather than taught.

## Security notes
Participant data is PII: recordings, notes and recruiting records follow the research retention policy; no participant sees live account data or keys. Sessions run on demo only.

## Accessibility notes
Recruit at least one participant who uses keyboard-primary interaction or magnification, so the monitor-panel density findings are not sighted-mouse-only.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ≥ 5 sessions completed and synthesised.
- [ ] Findings report merged to `docs/research/` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Binding copy for the emulation caveat and disconnect message agreed and recorded.
- [ ] Recommended defaults per strategy listed and handed to E33-D02/D03 and to E33-T01's config defaults.
- [ ] Reviewed with the Chief Design Officer and the OMS tech lead.
- [ ] **Sign-off:** CDO + Owner accept the findings as the basis for E33-D02/D03.

## Dependencies
None blocking. Informed by E30's order-ticket research if already complete.

## Branch
`design/e33-algo-research` (docs only).

title: Measure real per-UID rate-limit behaviour and 5-account fan-out latency on demo
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §13 lists two open spikes this epic depends on: **S7 Rate-limit truth** ("actual `X-Bapi-Limit` behaviour per endpoint group on a real UID → documented per-group budgets") and **S4 Multi-account fan-out** ("latency and rate budget with 3–5 sub-accounts on demo → all legs < 1.5 s, no 10018 under the designed budget"). Both are gates on ADR-0008's validation section.

The governor in E34-T02 hard-codes a bucket split (`critical` 40% / `entry` 40% / `poll` 20% of a default 10 req/s) and a set of refill rates taken from documentation that `21-database-schema.md` §Risk table row 3 explicitly flags as *"sourced from a mirror, not primary docs"*. Building the governor on unverified numbers would make every downstream latency and back-off assumption unfalsifiable. This spike replaces the assumptions with measurements before T02 finalizes its defaults.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A throwaway async harness under `spikes/e34-rate-limits/` driving the real Bybit **demo** endpoint `api-demo.bybit.com` with 3–5 demo sub-accounts registered through E27's vault (read keys through the normal vault API — never paste keys into the harness).
- Measure, per endpoint class of `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.7 (`order.create`, `order.amend`, `order.cancel`, `order.cancel_all`, `position.read`, `account.read`):
  - the observed `X-Bapi-Limit`, `X-Bapi-Limit-Status`, `X-Bapi-Limit-Reset-Timestamp` header values and their refill behaviour over a 60 s ramp;
  - whether the budget is genuinely shared across two keys of the same UID and genuinely independent across UIDs;
  - the retCode actually returned when the limit is crossed (`10006` per-UID vs `10018` per-IP) and the real recovery time for each;
  - the shared per-IP ceiling under 5 concurrent UIDs.
- Measure fan-out latency: one intent → 3 and 5 concurrent `POST /v5/order/create` calls with attached `stopLoss`, 30 repetitions, reporting p50/p95/p99 per-leg ack and whole-group ack, plus cross-leg skew.
- Record whether `stopLoss` attaches inline on `order/create` for linear perps (which sets `sl_cost = 0` in the pre-flight reservation of `20-architecture.md` §4.3) or requires a follow-up `POST /v5/position/trading-stop` (`sl_cost = 1`).
- Output: a comparison table + an ADR amendment to `27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md` §Validation recording the measured numbers, and follow-up tickets if a number invalidates a design rule.

## Out of scope
- Any production-shippable code. The harness is explicitly throwaway (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.1).
- Live-environment measurement (R4 territory; demo only).
- Governor implementation itself → E34-T02.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Per-endpoint budgets documented
  Given the harness has run the full ramp against 5 demo UIDs
  When the spike completes
  Then a table records, per endpoint class, the observed capacity, refill rate, header semantics and the retCode at breach
  And ADR-0008 §Validation is amended with the measured values and the date they were measured

Scenario: Fan-out latency gate
  Given 5 demo accounts each submitting one entry with an attached stop-loss
  When 30 fan-out repetitions complete
  Then whole-group ack p95 is reported against the 1.5 s ADR-0008 gate
  And if p95 exceeds 1.5 s the spike files a follow-up ticket naming the dominant latency component before closing

Scenario: A measurement contradicts the design
  Given the measured per-UID order.create capacity differs from the assumed 10/s by more than 20%
  When the spike is written up
  Then the ADR is amended, E34-T02's default configuration values are updated on its ticket before it starts
  And 32-risk-register.md is updated with the revised R3 exposure
```

## Technical notes / design
Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. Decision criteria stated up front:
- If per-UID budgets prove *not* independent across UIDs, the whole three-bucket-per-account model in `20-architecture.md` §4.3 collapses into a single global governor — that is a P0 architecture change and E34-T02 is re-planned before it starts.
- If group ack p95 > 1.5 s at 5 accounts on demo, `max_concurrent_legs` and the submission ordering (descending notional, `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.4 rule 3) are retuned and the number is re-measured before T02 closes.
- If `stopLoss` cannot attach inline, `sl_cost = 1` becomes the default in the pre-flight reservation and every latency budget gains one round trip per leg.

Harness sketch: `asyncio.gather` over N signed clients, one per UID, with a shared `httpx.AsyncClient` so the per-IP ceiling is exercised realistically; every response's rate headers are appended to a Parquet file for analysis in DuckDB. Use only `reduce_only` / immediately-cancelled orders so no demo position is left open; assert flat at the end of each run.

## Test plan
Not a production ticket: no unit/coverage obligation. The deliverable's own validity is checked by (a) re-running the ramp twice and confirming the numbers reproduce within 10%, and (b) a second engineer re-reading the harness for a measurement bug (e.g. client-side queueing inflating observed latency).

## Security notes
Demo keys only, fetched through the E27 vault API — never written to the harness, a shell history, or the spike branch. The spike must not disable the withdrawal-permission self-check. Any raw response capture is scrubbed of `api_key` and signature headers before being committed. Data classification: no PII; demo financial data only. Security review label: yes (key handling).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface.

## Performance notes
This spike *is* the performance measurement. Reference budgets: `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2 budget #4 (≤50 ms backend-added + ≤10 ms/account) and ADR-0008's 1.5 s / 5-account gate.

## Observability
The harness emits the same metric names the governor will use (`oms_rate_tokens_available`, `oms_rate_wait_seconds`) so the Grafana panel built here is reusable by E34-T02 rather than rebuilt.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Questions answered with recorded evidence (tables, Parquet capture, Grafana screenshot).
- [ ] ADR-0008 §Validation amended (even if the answer is "as assumed" — that is still an ADR entry per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2).

- [ ] Harness branch left unmerged and marked throwaway.

- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated (R3 exposure re-scored).

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27** (demo accounts + key vault must exist to sign requests) and **E29** (a signed `RestClient` with the error taxonomy already exists; the spike extends it rather than writing a second signer).

## Branch
`spike/e34-fanout-rate-limits` (throwaway, never merged); no PR size guidance — the branch is archived, not reviewed for merge.

title: Per-UID rate-limit governor: three-bucket budgets, header feedback and 10018 back-off
body:
## Context
Bybit enforces REST rate limits **per UID, shared across that UID's API keys** (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.7, research 06 §13), plus a global per-IP ceiling of 600 req/5 s. A trade group fans one intent out to N accounts holding N independent, independently-exhaustible budgets. Without a governor, the first busy account either silently delays the whole group or, worse, wins the race against a protective order — the exact failure ADR-0008 rule 4 exists to prevent ("entry orders can therefore never starve an exit").

`20-architecture.md` §4.3 is the normative algorithm and this task implements it verbatim, with the default numbers corrected by the measurements from **E34-K01**. The governor is a prerequisite of fan-out execution (E34-S02) and of the kill-switch's guaranteed path (E39).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `AccountRateBudget` in M14: three token buckets per account — `critical` 40%, `entry` 40%, `poll` 20% of the UID limit (defaults `order.create` 10/s, `amend` 10/s, `cancel` 10/s, `cancel_all` 1/s linear, reads 50/s per `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.7, revised by K01). `entry` and `poll` may never borrow from `critical`; `critical` may borrow from either when idle.
- Priority classes `critical | normal | background` per `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.7 with their stated bucket behaviour; queued items age with a **2 s priority boost** so nothing starves; ties within a class break by descending order notional.
- `reserved_for_protective` slice (≥10% of capacity, min 2 tokens) drawable only by `purpose in {stop_loss, flatten}` / reduce-only traffic — the mechanism that makes principle P4 hold under rate pressure.
- **Header feedback** in M4's `RestClient`: every response's `X-Bapi-Limit`, `X-Bapi-Limit-Status`, `X-Bapi-Limit-Reset-Timestamp` corrects the bucket; the observed remaining count wins over the configured default; a drop to 0 shrinks configured capacity for 60 s (adaptive downshift) and increments `oms_rate_downshift_total`.
- **Error handling** per `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.6: `10006` (per-UID too many visits) → feed the bucket, requeue only if the request is still useful; `10018` (per-IP rate limit) → **global IP-level back-off ≥10 min per Bybit guidance, all accounts throttled**, with jitter, and a `system_events` row of kind `rate_limit` carrying `ret_code='10018'`.
- Shared per-IP bucket (600 req/5 s) checked in addition to the per-UID bucket; when the IP bucket is binding, workers are served in descending-notional order through a priority queue (`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5.1 rule 5).
- **Pre-flight reservation API** used by fan-out: `reserve(account, bucket, cost, ttl_ms)` → reservation handle; `release(handle)`; reservations expire after `CV_FANOUT_RESERVATION_TTL_MS` (default 3000).
- **Deferred queue**: per-account FIFO deadline queue for `best_effort` starvation; on each refill the queue head retries; on `CV_FANOUT_DEFER_DEADLINE_MS` (default 5000) expiry the item transitions to `Rejected(RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED)` — **never** to `Unknown`, because nothing was sent.
- Config keys (`24-internal-schemas.md` §16.1): `CV_FANOUT_RESERVATION_TTL_MS`, `CV_FANOUT_ADMIT_WAIT_MS` (750), `CV_FANOUT_DEFER_DEADLINE_MS` (5000), plus the per-endpoint capacity map — all admin-editable and audited as `config.changed`.
- Full metric set of `20-architecture.md` §4.3 and the two alert rules (page: any account with `critical` tokens < 1 for >10 s; warn: `oms_fanout_deferred_total` rate > 0 for 5 min).

## Out of scope
- Fan-out orchestration itself (who calls `reserve`) → E34-S02.
- WS inbound client rate limiting (`23-ws-protocol.md` §client_rate_limited) and the API gateway's per-user/per-IP limiter → E05/E29, a different limiter with different semantics.
- Live-environment capacity tuning → R4.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Entries can never starve an exit
  Given account A's entry bucket is fully exhausted by a burst of fan-out children
  When a protective reduce-only close is submitted at priority critical
  Then it acquires a token from the critical bucket within 100 ms and is sent
  And no entry-priority request is able to draw from the critical bucket at any point

Scenario: Header-driven adaptive downshift
  Given Bybit returns X-Bapi-Limit-Status 0 on an order.create response for account B
  When the next request for account B is scheduled
  Then the configured capacity for that endpoint class is reduced for 60 s, oms_rate_downshift_total increments
  And the request waits rather than being sent and rejected

Scenario: 10018 throttles every account, not just one
  Given account C receives retCode 10018
  Then a global IP-level back-off of at least 10 minutes with jitter is applied across all accounts
  And a system_events row of kind rate_limit with ret_code 10018 is written
  And protective critical traffic continues to be issued at the reduced rate rather than being blocked entirely

Scenario: Reservation TTL prevents leaked capacity
  Given five reservations are taken for a fan-out that then fails validation
  When CV_FANOUT_RESERVATION_TTL_MS elapses without a commit
  Then all five reservations are released and the tokens are available again

Scenario: No starvation under sustained pressure
  Given background reconciliation polls saturate the poll bucket for 60 s
  When a normal-priority entry is queued behind them
  Then the 2 s ageing boost promotes it and it is sent within 3 s
```

## Technical notes / design
```python
class Bucket(str, Enum):
    critical = "critical"; entry = "entry"; poll = "poll"

@dataclass
class Reservation:
    handle: UUID; account_id: AccountId; bucket: Bucket
    cost: int; expires_at_us: int; committed: bool = False

class AccountRateBudget:
    async def reserve(self, bucket: Bucket, cost: int, wait_ms: int) -> Reservation | None: ...
    def release(self, r: Reservation) -> None: ...
    def commit(self, r: Reservation) -> None: ...          # token actually spent
    def observe_headers(self, endpoint_class: str, hdrs: Mapping[str, str]) -> None: ...
    def on_ret_code(self, code: str) -> None: ...          # 10006 local, 10018 escalates to IpBudget
```
- Buckets are **monotonic-clock** token buckets (`time.monotonic_ns`), never wall clock, so NTP steps and the `10002` clock-drift path cannot create or destroy tokens.
- `sl_cost` for reservation is 0 when `capabilities.supports_attached_sl_tp` (SL rides on `order/create`) and 1 when a separate `POST /v5/position/trading-stop` is needed — resolved from the adapter capability record, with K01's finding as the demo value.
- The governor is a **library, not a service**: a single asyncio process owns all buckets (modular monolith, principle P7). A later process split would need a distributed bucket — recorded as a known limitation in the ADR amendment.
- Fairness across accounts is structural: *there is no shared queue* — one bucket and one drain task per account, so a throttled account cannot head-of-line-block its siblings.

## Test plan
- **Unit (≥90%):** token accounting under a deterministic fake clock — refill precision, borrow rules (`critical` may borrow, `entry`/`poll` may not), reserve/commit/release/expiry, ageing boost, descending-notional tie-break, protective reserve slice exhaustion behaviour.
- **Property test:** across 10 000 randomized request streams, invariant "a `critical` request is never delayed longer than a `normal` request submitted at the same instant" holds, and total tokens spent never exceeds capacity over any sliding window.
- **Integration:** against a stub Bybit returning scripted `X-Bapi-Limit-*` headers and injected `10006`/`10018` — assert the downshift window, the ≥10 min IP back-off with jitter bounds, and the `system_events` row.
- **Perf/benchmark:** governor decision overhead ≤0.5 ms p99 per request (it sits inside the ≤50 ms fan-out budget); 5-account fan-out bookkeeping ≤10 ms/account (budget #4).
- **Chaos (feeds E34-Q04):** kill the process with reservations outstanding; on restart no reservation is honoured and capacity is rebuilt from headers, not from stale state.
- **Fixtures:** `fixtures/bybit/rate_headers_ramp.json`, `fixtures/bybit/ret_10018.json` — both produced by E34-K01.

## Security notes
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 every ticket in this epic is treated as `security`-labelled: it touches `area/oms-execution` order placement and the fan-out safety invariant. Threats from `04-security-program.md` / STRIDE (E34-X01): **Spoofing** — a forged `arm_token` or replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; **Tampering** — client-supplied per-leg sizing overriding server-resolved sizing; **Repudiation** — a fan-out without a per-leg audit row; **Information disclosure** — another user's account labels/balances leaking through the group response or the `trade_groups` WS topic; **Denial of service** — a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; **Elevation of privilege** — a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`. Controls: server-side resolution of every leg parameter, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` enforced before any adapter call, required idempotency key, the reserved `critical` rate bucket, and an `audit_log` row per leg. Data classification: financial/execution data and account scope; API secrets are never handled here (they stay in the M2 vault) — only referenced by account id.

Ticket-specific: the governor is a **denial-of-service control**, not merely a performance feature — its failure mode is that protective traffic cannot reach the exchange. Abuse case covered in E34-X02: a hostile or buggy client issuing fan-outs in a tight loop must exhaust only its own `entry` budget and must never reduce `critical` availability below the reserve.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. (Rate-limit state is surfaced to users by SCR-061's "rate-limit backoff" state and CMP-232 LimitsChip, built in E34-S04.)

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2): the governor's bookkeeping is the "≤10 ms/account fixed cost" term. Decision path must be lock-free on the fast path (single-threaded asyncio, no `await` between check and reserve). `oms_rate_wait_seconds` p99 ≤200 ms for `entry` under normal load; `critical` p99 ≤50 ms under any load.

## Observability
`oms_rate_tokens_available{account,bucket}` gauge, `oms_rate_wait_seconds{account,bucket}` histogram, `oms_rate_downshift_total{account}`, `oms_fanout_deferred_total{account}`, `oms_fanout_rejected_total{reason}`, `oms_rate_reject_total`. Grafana panel "OMS rate budget" per `ADR-0014-observability.md`. Alerts exactly as in `20-architecture.md` §4.3. Log `10018` at WARN with the back-off deadline; log every downshift at INFO.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every acceptance-criteria scenario is verified by an automated test that names the scenario.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on touched backend packages; OMS/risk modules held to ≥90% by R3 local policy (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4).
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` updated if the shipped contract diverged; contract tests green.
- [ ] ADR-0008 amended (or a superseding ADR filed) if a normative rule changed during implementation.
- [ ] perf: budget #4 benchmark recorded (≤50 ms backend-added + ≤10 ms/account; group ack ≤1.5 s p95 for 5 accounts).
- [ ] security: SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (E34 is permanently `security`-labelled per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo) — never live.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`trading.fanout`: on in demo, off in live until R4/E44).

## Dependencies

Interfaces relied on: `ExchangeAdapter.capabilities` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §14), the internal event bus for metric emission.

title: Rule engine IR, compiler & runtime
body:
## Context
Owner decision #11 requires **two** rule authoring surfaces — a form/condition-list editor (**E36**) and a visual node-graph editor (**E37**) — that **compile to one intermediate representation executed by one runtime**. E35 builds that shared substrate: the IR schema, the compiler and validator both editors call, the deterministic evaluator (architecture module **M15**), the action executor that reaches the market only through the OMS (E29), simulation over recorded/replay data, rule versioning with a content hash, and the firing log that makes every action explainable.

The normative design already exists and must be implemented rather than re-invented: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11 (IR pydantic models, the published JSON Schema, evaluation semantics E1-E12, the trigger/condition/action vocabulary, safety limits, built-in system rules, simulation types) and `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md` (binding rules 1-8). Persistence is fixed by `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; the REST surface by `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/rules*`; the push surface by `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6.

Two properties make this epic dangerous and shape every ticket inside it:
1. **Rules place real orders.** The IR is deliberately *data, not code* (ADR-0007 principle R1) — no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting — because this is a security boundary as much as a design choice. Every action funnels through the OMS so per-account profile caps (E28) and risk caps (E39) apply *after* the rule engine and cannot be bypassed, and the native exchange-side stop-loss invariant (ADR-0008) is untouchable.
2. **Round-trip equivalence is release-blocking.** US-RULE-006's NFR states the canonical-hash comparison runs **in production**, not only in tests; a form→IR→graph→IR→form cycle must be hash-stable. R3 exit criterion 5 requires a corpus of >=30 rules to survive the cycle in both directions.

E35 starts on S14 day 1 alongside E27/E29 because E36 and E37 cannot begin until the IR, the vocabulary endpoint and the compiler exist.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories owned by this epic** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §20 RULE):
- **US-RULE-001** Rule IR and single engine (Must) — canonical IR, JCS-style canonicalisation, hashing, versioning, migration, quarantine on schema violation.
- **US-RULE-002** Metric vocabulary (Must) — the closed, typed, unit-tagged catalogue served to both editors from one registry.
- **US-RULE-003** Action vocabulary (Must) — the 25 action types, per-type parameter schemas, declared scope, idempotency guards.
- **US-RULE-006** Editor round-trip switching (Must) — the *engine-side half*: `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile`, hash equality proof, optimistic concurrency on save, node-only construct marking. The two editor UIs are E36/E37.
- **US-RULE-007** Rule scoping (Must) — the scope model plus **runtime** enforcement on every action, not only at save time.
- **US-RULE-008** Simulate-only mode (Must) — identical evaluation path, different action sink; promotion to live requires step-up auth and is audited.
- **US-RULE-009** Auto-backtest on save (Should) — same engine over recorded history with honest coverage reporting.
- **US-RULE-010** Rule runtime and firing log (Must) — every evaluation-relevant event including suppressions, replayable from its own snapshot.
- **US-RULE-011** Rule conflict resolution and precedence (Must) — arm-time detection, deterministic runtime arbitration, risk controls always win.

**Screens introduced or changed here:** SCR-084 Rule simulation / backtest panel, SCR-085 Rule arming dialog, SCR-086 Rule conflict resolver, SCR-087 Rule fire history / execution log, SCR-088 Rule IR inspector (advanced), SCR-089 Rule import / export.

**Components:** CMP-154 RuleSimulatePanel, CMP-155 RuleListRow, CMP-156 RuleEvaluationTimeline, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-159 RuleConflictWarning, CMP-233 RuleOptions, CMP-234 ValidationPanel, plus CMP-023 Progress Bar, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-033 CopyButton, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-047 DateRangePicker, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-067 FileDrop, CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart.

**API:** `GET/POST /api/v1/rules`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}`, `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/versions`, `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/versions/{versionId}`, `PUT /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/active-version`, `POST /api/v1/rules/validate`, `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile`, `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/simulate`, `PUT /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/mode`, `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs`, `GET /api/v1/rules/runs/{runId}/events`, `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary`, `GET /api/v1/schemas/rule-ir.json`.

**WS:** topic `rules` (subscription options `rule_ids`, `include_events`; 250 ms cadence; schema `RuleUpdate` / `cv://ws/v1/rules.schema.json`).

**DB:** `rules`, `rule_versions`, `rule_runs`, `rule_events`, enums `rule_scope`, `rule_mode`, `rule_run_status`. `trade_groups.origin_rule_id` and `trade_groups.origin_rule_run_id` are written through the OMS path and read here; those columns are owned by E34.

**Architecture module:** **M15** rule engine, consuming the MetricRegistry (`24-internal-schemas.md` §7) and emitting only through the M14 OMS.

## Out of scope
- The form editor UI (SCR-081, SCR-083) — **E36**; the node-graph editor UI (SCR-082) — **E37**; the rules list SCR-080 — **E36**. E35 ships only the compile/validate/vocabulary contract those editors target.
- US-RULE-012 daily loss lockout, US-RULE-013 dead man's switch, US-RULE-014 owner kill-switch — **E39**. E35 only *honours* the kill-switch and risk caps.
- US-RULE-004 and US-RULE-005 (the editors themselves) — E36/E37. E35 covers only their shared IR contract.
- Alerts, which reuse the same IR grammar with actions omitted — **E40**.
- The OMS, order state machine, brackets and native-SL enforcement — **E29**/**E32**. E35 never talks to Bybit directly.
- The paper matcher fill model used to price simulated actions — **E38**; the replay engine — **E26**.
- Any scripting language, plugin system or dynamic evaluation path — permanently out of scope per ADR-0007.
- Android and any separate admin application (owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One IR, one engine
  Given a rule authored through the form compiler and the semantically identical rule authored through the graph compiler
  When both models are compiled and canonicalised
  Then the two ir_hash values are identical
  And the evaluator produces an identical action plan for the same MetricSnapshot

Scenario: Determinism over replay
  Given a rule in simulate mode and a recorded replay window
  When the window is replayed three times
  Then the sequence of rule_events and planned actions is identical across all three runs

Scenario: A rule cannot exceed account risk (failure case)
  Given an armed rule whose place_order action would breach the account profile cap or the global kill-switch
  When the rule fires
  Then the action is blocked by the OMS-side check before any exchange call
  And the block is recorded in rule_events with blocked_by and a critical alert is raised

Scenario: Corrupt IR never executes (edge case)
  Given a stored rule_versions.ir document that fails schema validation
  When the engine loads it
  Then the rule is quarantined read-only, force-disarmed, the failing JSON path is named
  And it is never partially evaluated
```

## Technical notes / design
Epic-level shape only; per-ticket detail lives on the children.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  FORM[E36 form editor] -->|POST /rules/:id/compile| COMP[Compiler + canonicaliser]
  GRAPH[E37 node editor] -->|POST /rules/:id/compile| COMP
  COMP --> VAL[Validator: JSON Schema + semantic checks]
  VAL --> STORE[(rule_versions: ir, ir_hash)]
  STORE --> ENG[M15 evaluator]
  BUS[(Event bus + MetricRegistry)] --> ENG
  ENG --> GUARD[Limits, scope, conflict arbitration, kill-switch]
  GUARD -->|armed| OMS[E29 OMS]
  GUARD -->|simulate| SIM[Simulated action sink]
  ENG --> LOG[(rule_runs / rule_events)] --> WS[[WS topic rules]]
```

Invariants inherited from ADR-0007 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.5/§11.7 and enforced across every child: the IR is data not code; conditions are pure; `None` is false and never coerces to 0; exactly one immutable `MetricSnapshot` per evaluation; deterministic child and action ordering; stale data skips evaluation rather than acting; a per-evaluation timeout aborts and counts toward auto-disarm; `scope.environments` defaults to `["demo"]`; and a newly created or edited rule cannot be armed until it has completed a simulation on that exact `ir_hash`.

## Test plan
Rolled up from the children. Epic-level gates:
1. Round-trip property suite, >=10 000 generated IR documents per CI run, green (US-RULE-001 NFR).
2. The >=30-rule corpus round-trips form→graph→form and graph→form→graph with identical hashes (R3 exit criterion 5).
3. Determinism-over-replay suite green (R3 exit criterion 6).
4. Golden action-plan corpus (break-even at 1R, ATR trail, cancel-if-spread-too-wide, time stop, daily-loss lockout) unchanged against recorded fixtures.
5. Safety suite: no compiled rule can produce a plan that removes a native SL, or widens a stop without `rules.loosen_stop` plus the Owner role.
6. Contract tests on every `/rules*` operation and on the `rules` WS topic schema.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Roadmap §7.4 names **E35** among the epics requiring a STRIDE model with all Critical/High findings closed before the train closes; E35-X01/X02/X03 carry that work.

## Accessibility notes
Every screen in scope (SCR-084..SCR-089) must meet WCAG 2.2 AA; `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 states there is no internal-tool exception. Non-negotiables taken from the screen catalogue: simulation results are a table and the firing timeline has a text-list equivalent; the arming dialog is `role="alertdialog"` restating the rule in plain language with DEMO preselected and a visibly-labelled typed confirmation for LIVE; the IR inspector offers a structured expandable tree as a screen-reader alternative to the `<pre>` block; conflict resolutions are labelled radio options each stating its consequence in text; condition values in the fire history are a nested table so a screen reader can read exactly why a rule fired.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and the screen catalogue entries:
- Evaluation completes within `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms` (default 250 ms; hard abort, counted as an error).
- `POST /rules/validate` round-trip <=300 ms (SCR-081 performance note).
- Compile + round-trip diff <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node rule (SCR-081).
- Conflict detection <=1 s for 500 rules (SCR-086).
- A 14-day single-symbol simulation at 1-minute granularity completes <=60 s with partial results streamed (SCR-084).
- SCR-087 scrolls 10k rows without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame; SCR-080 500 rows within 4 ms/frame.

## Observability
Prometheus: `rule_evaluations_total{rule_id,trigger,outcome}`, `rule_eval_duration_seconds` histogram, `rule_actions_total{type,result}`, `rule_skipped_total{reason}` with reason in `warmup|stale_data|cooldown|once|rate_limit|scope|kill_switch|limit`, `rule_missed_triggers_total`, `rule_auto_disarmed_total`, `rule_roundtrip_mismatch_total`.
Structured logs carry `rule_id`, `version`, `ir_hash`, `scope_instance`, `run_id`, `trigger_reason`.
Audit events: `rule.created|updated|armed|disarmed|deleted|exported|imported`, `rule.fired`, `rule.roundtrip_verified`, `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved`, `rule.simulation_started|completed|cancelled`, `rule.conflict_detected|resolved`, `rule.priority_changed`.
Grafana: armed-rule count by environment, fires/hour, suppression reasons, evaluator latency p50/p95/p99, auto-disarm events.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike Done (100% rollup) or explicitly descoped with a recorded Won't/Later disposition on this Epic.
- [ ] R3 exit criteria 5 (round-trip corpus) and 6 (determinism over replay) demonstrated end-to-end and the evidence recorded here.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90%, other touched backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; zero open P0/P1 bugs against E35 scope.
- [ ] Docs final: `24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `21-database-schema.md` §3.4, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, ADR-0007.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on SCR-084..089 plus one manual screen-reader pass per screen.
- [ ] perf: evaluator and simulation benchmarks recorded against the §06 budgets.
- [ ] security: STRIDE (E35-X01) finalised, all Critical/High closed or accepted with Owner sign-off, Security engineer sign-off comment (E35-X03).
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression and exploratory pass recorded (E35-Q07), not just child-ticket QA.
- [ ] Design: all six screens signed off, design QA (E35-D06) Done.
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at Sprint Review with explicit acceptance; retro learnings filed as Chore tickets.

## Dependencies
- **E25 Detectors** — supplies the order-flow metrics the vocabulary exposes (`stacked_imbalance_zone`, `iceberg_present_at_level`, `tape_speed_zscore`, regime), each carrying its `estimated` flag which the rule UI must surface. Roadmap edge `E25 --> E35`.
- **E29 OMS core** — the only route from a rule action to the market, plus the order state machine and `orderLinkId` idempotency. Roadmap edge `E29 --> E35`.
- **E26 Replay engine** — the deterministic substrate for simulation and auto-backtest.
- **E27 Accounts & key vault** and **E09 Auth, sessions, 2FA & RBAC** — account scoping, `rules:read`/`rules:write` permissions, and step-up MFA for arming.
- Consumers, not blockers: **E36** form editor, **E37** node editor, **E40** alerts (shares the IR grammar with actions omitted), **E41** journal (`log_journal_tag` action), **E39** risk caps (the engine honours them).

## Branch
`feat/rule-engine-<short>` per child, e.g. `feat/rule-engine-ir-schema`, `feat/rule-engine-evaluator`. Each PR <=400 LOC diff. Per the interface-first rule in `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10, the IR schema and the OpenAPI/WS deltas merge in their own PRs **ahead** of any consumer work in E36/E37.

## References
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11 Rule engine (IR models, JSON Schema, evaluation semantics E1-E12, vocabulary, safety limits, built-in system rules, simulation types)
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md` — one canonical IR, binding rules 1-8
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4 — `rules`, `rule_versions`, `rule_runs`, `rule_events`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` — `/rules`, `/rules/{ruleId}`, `/rules/{ruleId}/versions`, `/rules/{ruleId}/active-version`, `/rules/validate`, `/rules/{ruleId}/compile`, `/rules/{ruleId}/simulate`, `/rules/{ruleId}/mode`, `/rules/{ruleId}/runs`, `/rules/runs/{runId}/events`, `/rules/vocabulary`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6 `RuleUpdate` — topic `rules`, options `rule_ids`/`include_events`, 250 ms cadence
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §20 RULE (US-RULE-001..011)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-080..SCR-089; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-140..159, CMP-233, CMP-234
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §US-RULE rows
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7 R3 (goals 3, exit criteria 5-6, quality gates)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `04-security-program.md`, `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`

## Child dependency graph
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  T01[T01 IR models + canonicalisation + hash] --> T02[T02 DB migration]
  T01 --> T03[T03 Vocabulary registry + endpoint]

```

## Risks
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Round-trip divergence between the two editors (R5 Scope) | Release-blocking per the US-RULE-006 NFR | One compiler target; canonical hash compared in production on every editor switch; 10k-document property suite in CI; 30-rule corpus gate |
| A rule places an unintended order (safety) | Real orders on demo now, catastrophic once R4 opens live | Mandatory simulate on-ramp before arming; per-rule notional caps; OMS-side profile and risk caps applied *after* the engine; kill-switch honoured; native-SL invariant untouched |
| Evaluator latency under many armed rules (R2 Render performance / R3 Real-time cost) | Missed triggers, actions on stale state | One snapshot per evaluation with cross-rule metric memoisation; hard timeout; auto-disarm after `kill_switch_on_error_count` consecutive errors; benchmark gate in CI |

title: UX research: how a trader decides to trust an automated rule with real orders
body:
## Context
E35 introduces a genuinely new interaction class to the product: handing a piece of software standing permission to place and modify real orders without a human in the loop. Nothing shipped in R0-R2 asks the user for that kind of trust, and the two screens that mediate it — SCR-084 simulation and SCR-085 arming — have to carry a decision that the user must get right the first time, because the failure mode is financial.

The research is also the input to a copy problem that the plan already anticipates. SCR-085 requires the line "If the backend stops, this rule stops. Native stops stay." and SCR-084 requires "Simulation replays recorded market data. Fills are modelled, not real; results are not a guarantee." Those sentences exist to manage risks R12 (backtest bias) and R9 (advice boundary), but whether users actually *understand* them — particularly the distinction between an emulated stop that dies with the backend and a native stop that lives in Bybit's matching engine — has not been tested.

This runs first in S14 so its findings shape the wireframes in D02/D03 rather than arriving as late corrections.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 5-6 moderated sessions with the owner and the account managers (the entire real user population — this is a private terminal, so a small-n qualitative study is the right instrument, not a survey).
- **Comprehension probes**, each with a right answer to score against:
  1. After reading a simulation result, what does the user believe it predicts? (Testing R12 backtest bias.)
  2. What does the user think happens to an armed rule and to their positions if the backend crashes? (Testing whether the native-vs-emulated stop distinction lands.)
  3. What does "(estimated)" on a detector-derived metric mean to them, and does it change whether they would arm a rule that depends on one?
  4. Given two rules that both want the stop, what do they expect to happen, and what would they want to happen? (Input to the SCR-086 precedence model.)
- **Decision-journey mapping** for arming: what evidence a user wants before arming, in what order, and what would make them abandon the attempt.
- A **terminology check** on the vocabulary the editors will expose: do "trigger", "condition", "action", "scope", "simulate", "arm", "disarm" read unambiguously, or do any of them carry a competing meaning from TradingView, DeepCharts or Bybit's own UI?
- Findings written up in `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md` as a decision journey for arming, plus a copy-recommendations annex feeding D02/D03 and E36/E37.

## Out of scope
- Wireframes or any visual design — D02/D03.
- Research on the editors themselves (form vs graph authoring preferences) — that belongs to E36/E37's own research.
- Quantitative usability metrics — the population is too small for them to mean anything.
- Recruiting external participants: the product has a known, closed user set.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The comprehension gaps are identified and quantified
  Given 5 to 6 completed sessions
  When the four comprehension probes are scored
  Then each probe has a recorded pass/fail per participant and a stated implication for the design

Scenario: The native-versus-emulated stop distinction is tested, not assumed
  Given participants read the proposed SCR-085 copy
  When asked what happens to their positions if the backend stops
```

title: Fix IR canonicalisation and round-trip fuzz strategy before schema freeze
body:
## Context
US-RULE-001 makes "byte-identical IR" a release-blocking product property, and US-RULE-006 requires the canonical-hash comparison to run **in production** on every editor switch. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 specifies the canonical form as "JSON with sorted keys, `node_id`s renumbered in DFS order, and `graph_layout` dropped; its sha256 is the rule's content hash", and US-RULE-001 additionally calls it "JCS-style (sorted keys, normalised numbers)".

Those two statements leave three decisions genuinely open, and each of them is expensive to change after rules exist in the database: (a) exactly how numbers normalise (`1.50` vs `1.5` vs `Decimal` string form) given that prices and quantities are `Decimal` in `24-internal-schemas.md` §2 and JSON has no decimal type; (b) whether DFS renumbering of `node_id`s is safe given that `rule_events.node_ref` links a logged evaluation back to a node in the graph editor for highlighting — renumbering across versions could mis-highlight history; (c) what the property-based generator must cover to make the ">=10 000 generated documents per CI run" NFR meaningful rather than a slow tautology.

This spike answers all three before E35-T01 freezes the models. Timebox: **3 working days**, agreed with the Architect.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Prototype three canonicalisation strategies over a hand-built corpus of ~20 representative IR documents (form-subset rules, graph-only rules with shared sub-expressions, temporal nodes, nested arithmetic, all 25 action types at least once):
  1. RFC 8785 JCS as specified, with `Decimal` serialised via JCS number rules.
  2. JCS with `Decimal` preserved as canonical **strings** (`"1.5"`), which avoids float round-tripping entirely.
  3. A CBOR-canonical intermediate hashed instead of JSON text.
- Answer: does DFS `node_id` renumbering break `rule_events.node_ref` traceability across versions? Produce a recommendation (renumber, or keep author-assigned ids and exclude them from the hash, or store a stable `node_uid` alongside a presentational `node_id`).
- Define the `presentation` block boundary: which fields are excluded from the hash (`graph_layout` node x/y, collapsed state, comment text, `editor`) per US-RULE-001's "Presentation data survives the round trip" scenario.
- Specify the Hypothesis (or equivalent) generator strategy for the round-trip fuzz suite: node-shape grammar, depth/breadth bounds matching the JSON Schema limits (max 32 boolean children, max 8 arithmetic operands, max 10 actions), and the shrinking behaviour that makes failures debuggable.
- Benchmark: canonicalise + hash a 100-node document, 1 000 iterations, report p50/p99 — this sits inside the <=500 ms p95 compile budget of SCR-081.
- Write **ADR-0016 rule-ir-canonicalisation** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` recording the decision (DoR/DoD for Spike requires an ADR even if the answer is "defer").

## Out of scope
- Any production-shippable implementation — that is E35-T01. Prototype code is explicitly throwaway.
- The IR vocabulary itself (triggers/metrics/actions) — already fixed by `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.6.
- Editor-side canonicalisation in TypeScript — the canonical hash is computed server-side only; this spike records that as a constraint for E36/E37.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A decision exists with evidence
  Given the three canonicalisation strategies were prototyped against the 20-document corpus
  When the spike closes
  Then ADR-0016 records the chosen strategy, the rejected ones and the measured hash cost for a 100-node document

Scenario: Number normalisation is unambiguous
  Given two documents differing only in numeric formatting (1.50 vs 1.5, 1e3 vs 1000)
  When both are canonicalised under the chosen strategy
  Then their hashes are equal, and the rule for producing that form is stated precisely enough to reimplement

Scenario: node_ref traceability is resolved (edge case)
  Given rule_events rows referencing node ids of version N
  When version N+1 is created after an edit that reorders nodes
  Then the ADR states exactly what the graph editor highlights for historical events, and no scenario silently mis-highlights a different node

Scenario: The generator is shown to be useful (failure case)
  Given a deliberately introduced canonicalisation bug (unsorted keys under one nested object)
  When the prototype property suite runs
  Then it fails and shrinks to a minimal reproducing document in under 60 seconds
```

## Technical notes / design
Reference implementation candidates: `rfc8785` / `canonicaljson` for JCS, `cbor2` for the CBOR variant, `hypothesis` for generation. The evaluation matrix should score each strategy on: determinism across Python versions, `Decimal` fidelity, human-readability of the stored `rule_versions.ir` jsonb (it is read by SCR-088 IR inspector and by support), diffability for the round-trip mismatch diff the UI must download, and hash cost.

Note the constraint from `21-database-schema.md` §3.4.2: `UNIQUE (rule_id, ir_hash)` means saving an unchanged rule must **not** create a new version, so a canonicalisation that is unstable under re-serialisation would manufacture spurious versions — this is a correctness requirement, not an optimisation.

Also confirm: jsonb column storage reorders keys in Postgres, so the hash must be computed **before** insert and stored, never recomputed from the jsonb round-trip. State this explicitly in the ADR because it is an easy and silent mistake.

## Test plan
Spike code is throwaway; nonetheless the prototype must include the mutation check described in the fourth acceptance scenario (a deliberately broken canonicaliser must be caught). No coverage target applies. Fixtures: the 20-document corpus is kept and promoted into `tests/fixtures/rule_ir/` by E35-T01 as the seed of the >=30-rule corpus that R3 exit criterion 5 requires.

## Security notes
Canonicalisation is a security control, not a formatting nicety: the arming audit record embeds `ir_hash` so "what exactly was armed" is provable (`21-database-schema.md` §3.4.1). A canonicalisation with collisions or instability would undermine that non-repudiation property. The ADR must state the hash algorithm (sha256, matching the `sha256_hex` domain) and that hashing happens pre-persistence. No secrets or PII are handled by this spike.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The spike does record one a11y-relevant constraint for E37: the round-trip mismatch diff must be downloadable as text, not only rendered as a visual diff.

## Performance notes
Deliverable includes the measured canonicalise+hash cost for a 100-node document; the chosen strategy must leave headroom inside the <=500 ms p95 compile budget (SCR-081) and the <=300 ms validate budget.

## Observability
Spike output feeds the metric name `rule_roundtrip_mismatch_total` defined at epic level; the ADR should state which fields appear in the mismatch telemetry event required by US-RULE-006 ("a high-severity telemetry event is emitted").

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four acceptance scenarios answered with recorded evidence (comparison table + benchmark numbers) on the ticket.
- [ ] **ADR-0025-rule-ir-canonicalisation.md** merged in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, cross-linked from ADR-0007.
- [ ] Follow-up detail folded into E35-T01's description before T01 starts (the spike's findings are linked so the implementer does not re-derive them).
- [ ] Prototype branch left unmerged and marked throwaway; the 20-document corpus extracted for reuse.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

## Dependencies
No blockers — this must precede E35-T01 and therefore runs in the first week of S14. It consumes only documents that are already locked (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11, ADR-0007).

## Branch
