title: Build the deterministic evaluator with snapshotting, guards and timeouts
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** **Excluded from the statechart migration** (29-statechart-adoption-plan §3): the deterministic evaluator is a hot-path, per-tick component (BENCH-2: 381 ev/s measured vs a 2,000 ev/s need), so it stays plain code permanently. This ticket is recorded only to confirm the exclusion; no behavioural or estimate change.

This is module **M15**, the heart of the epic: the one evaluator both editors' output runs through. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11.5 specifies its semantics as twelve binding rules (E1-E12) and a pipeline diagram; this story implements them literally, because R3 exit criterion 6 requires that "the same recorded window produces the same action sequence across runs" and simulation parity (E35-S05) depends on the live and simulated paths being the *same* code with a different sink.

The rules that most often get implemented wrongly, and which therefore carry dedicated acceptance scenarios here: `None` is false and never coerces to 0 (E3); one immutable `MetricSnapshot` per evaluation so sibling conditions cannot see different market states (E2); short-circuit evaluation that still logs which children were **not** evaluated so the trace is never misleading (E4); stale data **skips** rather than acts (E7); and `crosses_above`/`crosses_below` are false on the first evaluation after warmup or restart, so a reconnect cannot manufacture a phantom cross (§11.6).

## Scope / Deliverables
- The evaluator package implementing the §11.5 pipeline: trigger -> debounce -> build `MetricSnapshot` -> freshness check -> limits check -> evaluate the condition DAG -> mode branch. This story stops at "decide what to do"; performing it is E35-S03.
- **Trigger subscription** for all 13 trigger types (§11.6): bus subscriptions for `on_price_update`, `on_bar_close`, `on_order_fill`, `on_position_open`, `on_position_close`, `on_position_update`, `on_metric_change`, `on_signal`, `on_book_update` (throttled to 10 Hz), `on_liquidation`, `pre_trade_check` (synchronous veto before any order submission); a monotonic scheduler for `on_timer` and `on_schedule` (5-field UTC cron). Trigger-driven, never polled (E1).
- `MetricSnapshot` construction reading every referenced metric **once** into an immutable structure, with cross-rule memoisation so ten rules referencing `atr(14)` cost one computation (§7.3).
- Condition evaluation for every node type: `Comparison` (all 15 operators), `BooleanNode` (`all_of`/`any_of`/`none_of`/`n_of`), `TemporalNode` (`sustained_for`/`occurred_within`/`count_within`/`stable_for`), `ArithmeticNode` (9 ops) with unit-aware arithmetic.
- **Per-scope instances** (E6): a symbol-scoped rule over 3 symbols is 3 independent instances with independent `once`/cooldown state, keyed as `"BTCUSDT@acct-3f2a"` per the `scope_instance` field.
- Limit guards before evaluation: `once`/`once_per`, `cooldown_ms`, `max_fires_per_hour`, `max_fires_per_day`.
- Stale-data guard (E7): any metric older than `max_data_age_ms` (default 5 000, or 3x the stream cadence, whichever is larger) skips with `skipped_reason="stale_data"`.
- Evaluation timeout (E8): exceeding `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms` aborts, counts as an error, and contributes to `kill_switch_on_error_count`, after which the rule auto-disables with a `critical` alert and requires human re-arm.
- **Reconnect replay safety** (E10): after a disconnect the engine does not replay missed triggers; it re-evaluates current state once, and `once`/dedupe keys prevent duplicates. Missed triggers are counted as a metric.
- **Disconnect guard** (§11.7): while the private WS is disconnected or reconciliation is running, armed rules are **paused**; the native SL keeps protecting positions and the UI is told "rules paused — feed degraded".
- `NodeTrace` production for every evaluated and skipped node (§11.9) — the substrate the firing log (E35-S06) persists.

## Out of scope
- Executing actions and their safety limits — **E35-S03**.
- Runtime scope enforcement on actions — **E35-S04**.
- Persisting the trace — **E35-S06** (this story produces it in memory).
- Conflict arbitration between rules — **E35-S07**.
- Computing the metrics themselves — E12/E18-E25.
- The simulate sink — **E35-S05**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One snapshot per evaluation
  Given a rule whose two sibling conditions both read last_price
  And the price changes between the two reads in wall-clock terms
  When the rule evaluates
  Then both conditions observe the identical value from the single immutable snapshot

Scenario: None is false, never zero
  Given a condition referencing a metric still in warmup, with no position, or on a stale feed
  When the rule evaluates
  Then the condition is false, skipped_reason records warmup or stale_data, nothing throws
  And a comparison such as metric < 1 does not become true by treating the missing value as 0

Scenario: Short-circuit still produces a complete trace
  Given an all_of node whose first child is false
  When evaluation short-circuits
  Then the remaining children are recorded with result null meaning not evaluated, so the trace cannot be misread as all children being false

Scenario: A frozen feed never triggers action (failure case)
  Given any metric in the snapshot older than max_data_age_ms
  When the trigger fires
  Then the evaluation is skipped with skipped_reason stale_data and counted, and no condition is evaluated

Scenario: No phantom crosses after a restart (edge case)
  Given a rule using crosses_above and an engine that has just restarted
  When the first evaluation after warmup occurs
  Then crosses_above is false regardless of the current value, because no previous snapshot exists

Scenario: A slow evaluation is aborted and counted (failure case)
  Given an evaluation exceeding limits.evaluation_timeout_ms
  When the deadline passes
  Then the evaluation is aborted, recorded as an error, and after kill_switch_on_error_count consecutive errors the rule auto-disables with a critical alert

Scenario: Reconnect does not replay history (edge case)
  Given the engine was disconnected for 30 seconds while triggers fired
  When it reconnects
  Then missed triggers are counted but not replayed, current state is re-evaluated exactly once, and once/dedupe keys prevent any duplicate fire

Scenario: Deterministic ordering
  Given the same MetricSnapshot presented twice
  When the same rule evaluates
  Then children are evaluated in array order and the outcome and trace are identical
```

## Technical notes / design
Single-threaded asyncio evaluation per rule instance, with the snapshot built by a synchronous read of memoised metric values so no `await` can interleave a market update mid-evaluation — this is the mechanical guarantee behind E2 and is easier to hold than a lock discipline.

Temporal nodes need bounded state: `sustained_for` keeps the timestamp the child first became true; `occurred_within`/`count_within` keep a ring buffer of event timestamps bounded by `window_ms` (max 86 400 000 per the schema, so cap allocation accordingly); `stable_for` keeps the last change timestamp. State is per `scope_instance` and per `node_id`, and is **dropped** when the active version changes — a new version's temporal windows must not inherit the old version's history, which would be unexplainable.

`pre_trade_check` is the one synchronous trigger: the OMS calls the engine inline before submission and blocks on the verdict, with a hard budget well under the order submit -> ack p95 <300 ms gate (budget #4). Give it its own, tighter timeout (default 25 ms) and fail **open or closed** per the built-in rule's declaration — `sys.stale_feed_block` and `sys.clock_drift_block` fail **closed** (veto) because their purpose is to stop trading.

Auto-disable path: `kill_switch_on_error_count` consecutive errors -> set `rules.mode = 'disabled'` with `disabled_reason`, emit a `critical` alert, require human re-arm (§11.7 per-rule health row). Consecutive, not cumulative — a successful evaluation resets the counter.
- Per-tick evaluation is plain code (BENCH-2: 381 ev/s vs 2,000 ev/s required); this is a permanent exclusion from the `xstate-statemachine` catalogue per 29-statechart-adoption-plan §3, not a temporary gap.


## Test plan
Unit (>=90% — this package is held to the 90% R3 rule-module policy):
- Operator table: every one of the 15 comparison operators across numeric, enum and boolean operands, including `between`/`outside` bounds, `tolerance` on float `eq`, and `in_set`/`not_in_set` on enums.
- Boolean nodes incl. `n_of` boundaries (n=1, n=len, n>len rejected earlier by validation).
- All four temporal ops across window boundaries, with clock injected.
- Arithmetic ops incl. division by zero (must produce None, not raise) and unit propagation.
- `None` propagation through arithmetic into comparisons.
- Trigger dispatch for all 13 types with a fake bus and a fake monotonic scheduler; cron parsing incl. DST-free UTC assumption.
- Per-scope-instance isolation of `once`/cooldown/temporal state.
- Timeout abort, error counting, auto-disable at the threshold, counter reset on success.
Integration: against recorded fixtures from E26 replay — the determinism suite (run the same window three times, assert identical trace) which is R3 exit criterion 6; extended by **E35-Q03**.
Chaos: WS disconnect mid-evaluation and reconnect (armed rules pause, no replay) — extended by **E35-Q05**.
Perf: benchmark 200 armed rules over a 1-hour recorded window, asserting p99 evaluation latency inside the 250 ms default budget and memoisation reducing metric computations — **E35-Q04**.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: the evaluator is the DoS-sensitive component. Controls: hard per-evaluation timeout; bounded temporal-state allocation derived from `window_ms`; bounded node counts enforced upstream by the schema; a per-rule error budget that auto-disables rather than looping. The disconnect guard is a safety control, not an optimisation — acting on stale state is how an automated system compounds a bad situation; it must have an explicit test, not just documentation. No user code is ever executed (ADR-0007 R1); a Semgrep rule (E35-X02) enforces the absence of `eval`/`exec`/`compile` in this package.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend engine. It does produce `skipped_reason` and `NodeTrace` values that become user-facing text in SCR-087, so each reason code needs a plain-language mapping agreed with design in E35-D03.

## Performance notes
Budgets: evaluation within `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms` (250 ms default, hard abort); `pre_trade_check` within its own 25 ms budget so it consumes a negligible share of the order submit -> ack p95 <300 ms gate (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budget #4); `on_book_update` throttled to 10 Hz; metric memoisation must demonstrably collapse duplicate computations across rules. All measured by the E35-Q04 benchmark and tracked in CI so regressions surface same-day.

## Observability
`rule_evaluations_total{rule_id,trigger,outcome}`, `rule_eval_duration_seconds` histogram (per trigger type), `rule_skipped_total{reason}`, `rule_missed_triggers_total`, `rule_auto_disarmed_total`, `rule_metric_cache_hits_total`, `rule_pre_trade_check_duration_seconds`. Structured logs on skip and abort carry `rule_id`, `version`, `ir_hash`, `scope_instance`. A `critical` alert on auto-disable.

- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.

title: Enforce rule scope on every action at runtime, not only at save time
body:
## Context
US-RULE-007 gives a rule author scope control over accounts, symbols and positions, and its NFR is unusually explicit: **"scope is enforced at runtime on every action, not only at save time"**. The reason is a real attack and a real accident: a rule authored while the user held a grant must stop acting the moment that grant is revoked, an account is disabled, or a manager is frozen — waiting for someone to re-save the rule is not acceptable.

The second scenario in US-RULE-007 is equally pointed: an account the user cannot trade "is not listed at all, and a crafted API request is rejected with 403" — the UI filter is a convenience, the server check is the control.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `ScopeResolver` that, for each evaluation and again for each action, resolves the rule's `RuleScope` (`level`, `account_ids`, `symbols`, `applies_to`, `environments`, `exclude_algo_children`) against the **current** state of: the rule owner's grants, account enabled/frozen state, the account's allowed-symbol list from its profile (E28), the environment gate, and the manager-freeze state (E39).
- Per-scope-instance expansion: a symbol-scoped rule across three symbols yields three independent instances (§11.5 E6), each carrying its own `scope_instance` key used for `once`/cooldown/temporal state and for the log.
- Environment gating (§11.5 E12): `scope.environments` defaults to `["demo"]`; including `"live"` requires the `rules.arm_live` permission, a confirmation, and a high-severity audit entry. An armed rule whose scope includes `live` while the live gate is closed in the backend configuration layer (M1) must not act on live, regardless of its IR.
- Scope-summary derivation for the UI header chip, e.g. `"2 accounts · BTCUSDT · new positions"` (US-RULE-007 scenario 3) — computed server-side so the summary can never disagree with what is enforced.
- 403 on crafted requests naming an out-of-permission account, with no information leak about whether the account exists.
- Revocation responsiveness: a grant revoked while a rule is armed takes effect on the next evaluation, and the affected scope instance is recorded as suppressed with `skipped_reason="scope"` rather than silently vanishing.

## Out of scope
- Account and grant management — **E27**/**E42**; profile allowed-symbol lists — **E28**; the manager freeze and kill-switch — **E39**. This story reads them.
- The scope selector UI (CMP-144 RuleScopeSelector) — E36.
- Action execution — **E35-S03** (which calls this resolver as its first gate).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Scope is re-checked on every action
  Given an armed rule scoped to accounts A and B
  And the author's grant on account B is revoked after the rule was armed
  When the rule next fires
  Then actions targeting A execute and actions targeting B are suppressed with skipped_reason scope
  And no re-save of the rule was required for this to take effect

Scenario: Out-of-permission account is invisible and unusable (failure case)
  Given a manager without a grant on account C
  When they list accounts for a rule scope, then craft an API request naming account C directly
  Then C is absent from the list and the crafted request is rejected with 403 without revealing whether C exists

Scenario: Live requires explicit opt-in (failure case)
  Given a rule whose scope.environments omits live
  When a live-environment trigger occurs
  Then the rule does not evaluate for that environment, and the skip is counted

Scenario: Per-symbol instances are independent (edge case)
  Given a symbol-scoped rule over BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT with once_per position
  When it fires for BTCUSDT
  Then the ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT instances remain eligible to fire, each with their own cooldown state

Scenario: A frozen manager's rules stop acting (failure case)
  Given a manager is frozen by the owner kill-switch
  When their armed rules next evaluate
  Then every action is suppressed with the freeze recorded as the reason, within the 2-second freeze guarantee
```

## Technical notes / design
Resolution is deliberately performed twice per fire — once to build the evaluation instances, once immediately before each action — because the window between them can contain a revocation, a freeze or an account disable. The second check is cheap (an in-memory grant snapshot refreshed on the auth/account event stream) so the cost is acceptable.

`applies_to` (`open_positions`/`pending_orders`/`account`/`any`) narrows which entities an action may touch: an `open_positions` rule must not cancel a pending order, and the resolver, not each action handler, is where that is enforced — otherwise 25 handlers each get it slightly wrong.

`exclude_algo_children` (default true, §11.5 E11) is resolved here: child orders created by emulated algos (E33) or by another rule carry their parent reference and are filtered out of the actionable set.

The 403 must be indistinguishable from 404 in its information content for accounts the caller cannot see — return the standard problem document without confirming existence, matching the RBAC matrix test in R3 exit criterion 10 which asserts "403 + no state change + audit row for every disallowed combination".

## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): resolution matrix over `level` x `applies_to` x grant state x account state x environment; `exclude_algo_children` filtering; scope-summary string generation for each shape.
Security tests: crafted request naming an ungranted account (403, no state change, audit row written); grant revoked between evaluation and action; manager frozen mid-fire; live-environment attempt with the live gate closed.
Integration: three-symbol instance isolation with independent `once_per=position` state; revocation during an armed rule's lifetime.
Contract: the scope summary returned by the rules API matches the enforced scope, asserted by a property test — the summary can never claim a wider or narrower scope than what the resolver permits.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

This story *is* a security control. It is the elevation-of-privilege mitigation named in the epic's STRIDE model (E35-X01) and feeds the RBAC matrix test in R3 exit criterion 10. Every disallowed combination must produce 403, no state change and an audit row. The account-existence non-disclosure requirement is explicit. Because grants are cached in memory for speed, the cache invalidation path (on grant change, account disable, freeze) is itself security-critical and needs a test proving a revocation is visible to the engine within one evaluation cycle.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The scope-summary string it produces is rendered as the rule header chip and is read by screen readers, so it must be a complete sentence-like phrase, not an abbreviation cluster.

## Performance notes
Resolution must not dominate evaluation: target <=2 ms per fire for a rule scoped to 5 accounts and 10 symbols, achieved by an in-memory grant/account snapshot invalidated on the auth and account event streams rather than a database round trip per action.

## Observability
`rule_scope_suppressions_total{reason}` (grant_revoked|account_disabled|frozen|environment|allowed_symbols|algo_child), `rule_scope_resolution_duration_seconds`. Every suppression is a `rule_events` row with `kind=throttled` or an explicit suppression kind, so US-RULE-010's "suppressed firing is logged too" requirement is satisfied here rather than being forgotten.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.

- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-S02**. Reads grants from **E09**, accounts from **E27**, allowed symbols from **E28**, freeze state from **E39**, algo-child lineage from **E33**/**E29**. Gates **E35-S03**.

title: Implement the rule IR models, canonical serialisation and content hash
body:
## Context
This is the foundation stone of E35 and of E36/E37: the single typed representation every rule reduces to. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2 gives the complete pydantic model set (`Rule`, `RuleScope`, `Trigger`, `MetricRef`, `Comparison`, `ArithmeticNode`, `BooleanNode`, `TemporalNode`, `Action`, `RuleLimits`) and §11.3 gives the JSON Schema those models must generate. ADR-0007 fixes the binding rules.

Nothing downstream can start without this: the validator (T04), the evaluator (S02), both editors (E36/E37) and the alerts grammar (E40) all target it. It is therefore scheduled first in S14 and merges as its own PR ahead of consumers, per the interface-first rule in `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New package `packages/rule_ir/` (pure, dependency-light, no I/O, no DB, no network) containing:
  - Every pydantic v2 model in `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2, field-for-field, including the discriminated `ConditionNode` union and the `Operand` union.
  - `canonicalize(ir) -> bytes` and `ir_hash(ir) -> str` implementing the strategy chosen in **ADR-0016** (E35-K01): sorted keys, normalised numbers, `node_id` handling per the ADR, `graph_layout`/`form_model`/presentation fields excluded.
  - `to_json_schema()` emitting the document published at `GET /api/v1/schemas/rule-ir.json` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11.3 / §17.3), generated at build time rather than hand-maintained.
  - `form_compatible(ir) -> bool` plus `form_incompatibility_reasons(ir)`, implementing the **form subset** definition in §11.4: trigger + a two-level boolean tree (`all_of` of `any_of` of comparisons) + a flat action list + limits; arithmetic operands only as a parameterised metric (no nested arithmetic); temporal nodes only as `sustained_for` directly wrapping a comparison. This is what lets E36 render a graph-authored rule read-only instead of mangling it.
- A CI check that fails if the committed `rule-ir.json` differs from the generated one (schema drift guard).
- Promote the E35-K01 corpus into `tests/fixtures/rule_ir/` and grow it toward the >=30-rule corpus required by R3 exit criterion 5.
- Publish the package build so the TypeScript side can consume the generated JSON Schema for editor-side pre-validation (E36/E37 consume, do not re-derive).

## Out of scope
- Semantic validation (metric existence, type/unit compatibility, action parameter completeness) — **E35-T04**. This package does structural typing only.
- Persistence — **E35-T02**. No SQLAlchemy models here.
- Evaluation — **E35-S02**.
- IR version upcasters — **E35-T05** (the `ir_version` field exists here; migration functions do not).
- Any TypeScript reimplementation of canonicalisation: the canonical hash is computed server-side only, a constraint recorded in ADR-0016.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Canonical hash is stable under cosmetic difference
  Given two IR documents identical except for key insertion order, numeric formatting (1.50 vs 1.5) and graph_layout node coordinates
  When both are canonicalised and hashed
  Then the two ir_hash values are equal

Scenario: Presentation fields are excluded from the hash
  Given an IR document with hand-placed node positions and comment text
  When only those presentation fields change
  Then ir_hash is unchanged, and the presentation block is returned untouched by round-tripping the models

Scenario: Form-subset detection is honest (edge case)
  Given a graph rule whose output fans one node into two consumers, or that nests arithmetic inside arithmetic
  When form_compatible is called
  Then it returns false and form_incompatibility_reasons names the offending node_id and the specific construct

Scenario: Structurally invalid document is rejected loudly (failure case)
  Given a document with an unknown action type, a boolean node with 33 children, or a temporal node missing window_ms
  When it is parsed
  Then a ValidationError is raised naming the failing JSON path, and no partially-constructed Rule object is returned

Scenario: Schema drift is caught in CI
  Given a developer edits a pydantic model without regenerating rule-ir.json
  When CI runs
  Then the schema-drift check fails with a diff of the two documents
```

## Technical notes / design
Implement the models exactly as printed in `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2 — treat that section as the specification, and if implementation forces a deviation, the doc changes in the same PR (DoD requirement), it is not silently diverged from.

Key details that are easy to get wrong:
- `ConditionNode = Comparison | BooleanNode | TemporalNode` must be a **discriminated** union on `op` so error messages point at the right branch rather than producing a three-way union error dump.
- `Operand = MetricRef | Literal_ | ArithmeticNode` — the literal wrapper is `{"const": ...}` in JSON per §11.3 `$defs.operand`.
- `MetricRef.metric` is constrained by `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,48}$`; symbols by `^[A-Z0-9]{4,20}$`.
- Trigger conditionals from §11.3 (`on_timer` requires `interval_ms`, `on_bar_close` requires `timeframe`, `on_schedule` requires `cron`, `on_metric_change` requires `metric`) are model validators *and* JSON Schema `allOf/if/then` — both representations must agree, asserted by a test.
- `RuleScope.environments` defaults to `("demo",)`. This safe default is a safety control (§11.5 E12), not a convenience; a test asserts the default explicitly so a future refactor cannot quietly widen it.
- `RuleLimits` defaults must match §11.2 exactly: `cooldown_ms=1000`, `max_fires_per_hour=60`, `max_fires_per_day=500`, `max_actions_per_fire=10`, `evaluation_timeout_ms=250`, `kill_switch_on_error_count=5`.
- Hash **before** persistence; never recompute from a Postgres `jsonb` round-trip, which reorders keys (ADR-0016).

## Test plan
Unit (target >=95% on this package — it is the smallest and most consequential):
- Parse/serialise round trip for every fixture in `tests/fixtures/rule_ir/`.
- Hash stability under key reorder, number reformatting, layout change, comment change.
- Hash *inequality* under any semantic change (threshold, operator, action order, scope, limits) — a table-driven test over one mutation per field.
- `form_compatible` truth table over the subset definition, one case per disqualifying construct.
- Trigger conditional validators, one case per trigger type, valid and invalid.
- Bound violations: 33 boolean children, 9 arithmetic operands, 11 actions, `window_ms` below 100 and above 86 400 000.
Property-based (Hypothesis, strategy from ADR-0016): generate valid IR, assert `parse(serialise(x)) == x` and hash stability; this suite is grown to the 10 000-documents-per-CI-run NFR by **E35-Q02**.
Contract: generated `rule-ir.json` validates every fixture with an independent JSON Schema validator (`jsonschema`), proving the pydantic models and the published schema agree.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: `additionalProperties: false` throughout the schema is a security control — it stops an attacker or a buggy editor smuggling unrecognised fields into a stored IR that a later engine version might interpret. Do not relax it for convenience. The absence of any string-evaluated expression type is the core of the ADR-0007 R1 boundary; add a Semgrep rule (delivered in E35-X02) that fails the build on `eval`, `exec` or `compile` inside `packages/rule_ir/` and the engine package.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — pure backend package, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
`canonicalize` + `ir_hash` for a 100-node document must stay within the envelope measured in E35-K01, leaving the <=500 ms p95 compile budget (SCR-081) comfortably intact. A pytest-benchmark case records the number so regressions surface.

## Observability
No runtime metrics from a pure package. It does define the `ir_hash` value that appears in every downstream log line, audit record and WS `RuleUpdate` payload.

title: Add the rules, rule_versions, rule_runs and rule_events migration with retention
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4 specifies the rule-engine relational schema in full DDL. This ticket lands it as an Alembic migration with the retention policy attached, because the retention decision is not cosmetic: a 250 ms evaluator produces roughly **345 000 rows per day per rule** if every evaluation is persisted, so the schema doc mandates that a `rule_runs` row is written only when `matched = true`, when `status = 'error'`, or when the rule is in `simulate` mode with the per-rule `record_all` flag set. Non-persisted evaluations are counted in Prometheus only.

The append-only guarantee on `rule_events` is a non-repudiation control (the firing log is part of the audit trail per US-RULE-010's NFR: "log retained indefinitely — it is part of the audit trail").

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating enums `rule_scope`, `rule_mode`, `rule_run_status` and tables `rules`, `rule_versions`, `rule_runs`, `rule_events` exactly as specified in `21-database-schema.md` §3.4.1–§3.4.3, including every CHECK constraint (`rule_editor`, `rule_interval`, `rule_cooldown`, `rule_prio`, `rule_scope_acct`, `rule_scope_sym`, `rule_armed_shape`, `rule_fires_pos`, `rv_version_pos`, `rv_ir_obj`, `rr_trigger`, `rr_duration`, `re_kind`), every index (`ux_rules_name`, `ix_rules_active`, `ix_rules_symbol`, `ix_rules_account`, `ix_rv_rule`, `ix_rr_rule_time`, `ix_rr_matched`, `ix_rr_errors`, `ix_rr_group`, `ix_re_run`, `ix_re_time`), the deferred FK `rules_active_version_fk`, and the uniqueness pair `UNIQUE (rule_id, version)` / `UNIQUE (rule_id, ir_hash)`.
- The `trg_re_append` trigger on `rule_events` calling `forbid_mutation()` (the shared function already used by `audit_log`, `order_events`, `executions`, `alert_deliveries` per §1).
- SQLAlchemy models and a repository module mapping `rule_versions.ir` (jsonb) to the `packages/rule_ir` models from E35-T01, hashing **before** insert.
- Retention job registration per §7: prune non-matched `rule_runs` (and their cascading `rule_events`) after 7 days; keep matched runs 24 months then archive to Parquet. The job is scheduled but its Parquet writer reuses the existing cold-storage path (E03/E16), it is not rebuilt here.
- A downgrade path that is tested, not merely written.

## Out of scope
- API handlers over these tables — **E35-S01**.
- The `alerts` table, which shares the IR grammar — **E40**.
- `trade_groups.origin_rule_id` / `origin_rule_run_id` columns — owned by **E34**; this migration must simply not conflict with them (ordering handled by Alembic branch labels).
- Parquet archive writer internals — E16.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and reverses cleanly
  Given an empty database at the previous revision
  When the migration is applied and then downgraded
  Then both directions succeed with no residual objects and the test suite for the prior revision still passes

Scenario: An armed rule must be fully specified (failure case)
  Given an UPDATE setting rules.mode = 'armed' without armed_at, armed_by or active_version_id
  When the statement executes
  Then the rule_armed_shape CHECK rejects it

Scenario: Saving an unchanged rule creates no new version (edge case)
  Given a rule whose stored version already has ir_hash H
  When a save produces the same canonical IR and therefore the same H
  Then the UNIQUE (rule_id, ir_hash) constraint prevents a duplicate version row and the repository returns the existing version

Scenario: Rule events cannot be altered (failure case)
  Given a persisted rule_events row
  When an UPDATE or DELETE is attempted by any role including the application role
  Then trg_re_append raises and the row is unchanged

Scenario: Retention prunes noise but keeps evidence
  Given 8-day-old non-matched runs and 8-day-old matched runs
  When the retention job runs
  Then only the non-matched runs and their events are deleted, and the matched runs remain
```

## Technical notes / design
Copy the DDL verbatim from `21-database-schema.md` §3.4 — deviations are bugs, not improvements. Notes:
- `rules.active_version_id` FK is added **after** `rule_versions` exists (the doc shows the `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT` ordering); with `ON DELETE RESTRICT` so an executing version cannot be deleted out from under the engine.
- `rv_ir_obj` (`jsonb_typeof(ir) = 'object' AND ir ? 'conditions' AND ir ? 'actions'`) is a cheap last-line structural guard; it does not replace schema validation in the application.
- `ix_rr_matched` and `ix_rr_errors` are partial indexes — they are what keeps SCR-087's history query fast while the table stays mostly write-only.
- The per-rule `record_all` flag lives in the `settings` table under `rules.settings.record_all` per §3.4.3, not as a column on `rules`.
- The repository must never recompute `ir_hash` from the jsonb column after a read, because Postgres reorders jsonb keys; the stored hash is authoritative.
- Write the migration so it is safe to run against a database that already holds E34's `trade_groups`: use an explicit `depends_on` in the Alembic revision.

## Test plan
Unit/integration against a real Postgres 16 in testcontainers (not SQLite):
- Upgrade/downgrade idempotence.
- One test per CHECK constraint asserting the rejection, including the boundary values (`eval_interval_ms` 49/50/3600000/3600001, `cooldown_seconds` -1/0/86400/86401, `priority` -1/0/1000/1001).
- Unique-index behaviour: duplicate name for the same owner (case-insensitive, ignoring soft-deleted rows), duplicate `(rule_id, version)`, duplicate `(rule_id, ir_hash)`.
- Append-only trigger on UPDATE and DELETE.
- Cascade behaviour: deleting a `rules` row cascades to versions and runs; deleting a `rule_versions` row that is active is RESTRICTed.
- Retention job over a seeded time-spread dataset.
Coverage target >=85% on the repository module.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: `rule_runs.input_snapshot` stores the metric values the conditions saw, which can include account equity, unrealised PnL and position size — classify as **financial/confidential**. It must be readable only through `rules:read` with account scoping, never dumped into general application logs. The append-only trigger on `rule_events` is the non-repudiation control; a migration that drops or weakens it is a security regression and must be blocked in review. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — database migration, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Verify with `EXPLAIN` that SCR-087's history query (`rule_runs` by `rule_id` ordered by `started_at DESC`, cursor-paginated) uses `ix_rr_rule_time` and that the matched-only variant uses the partial `ix_rr_matched`. Insert throughput must sustain the worst-case matched-run write rate without lock contention on `rule_events`' bigserial.

## Observability
Add `rule_runs_persisted_total{reason}` (matched|error|record_all) and `rule_runs_pruned_total` so the write-amplification decision can be verified in production rather than assumed. Retention job emits a structured log with rows deleted and duration.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

Blocked by **E35-T01** (the repository maps to those models). Blocks **E35-S01**. Coordinates with **E34** on Alembic revision ordering for `trade_groups`.

title: Build the metric and action vocabulary registry and serve GET /rules/vocabulary
body:
## Context
US-RULE-002 (metric vocabulary) and US-RULE-003 (action vocabulary) require a documented, closed catalogue of everything a rule can react to and everything it can do. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` describes `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary` as the single response **both** editors render their palettes from — "which is what keeps the two editors round-trip compatible". If the two editors ever derived their palettes independently, they would drift, and the round-trip guarantee would fail in the field rather than in CI.

Critically, `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 states the `MetricRegistry` is a *single named registry* shared by the rule engine, alerts, the journal and the UI: "This is what makes the rule vocabulary and the indicator list the same list." This ticket exposes that registry rather than duplicating it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `vocabulary` module that projects the existing `MetricRegistry` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2, populated by E12/E18/E19/E20/E23/E24/**E25**) into rule vocabulary entries carrying: stable `metric` name, human label, description, **unit** (price/ratio/percent/duration/count/enum), valid range, `warmup_bars`, `deterministic`, **`confidence`** (exact vs estimated), parameter schema, required data dependencies, and the behaviour when unavailable.
- The action catalogue: all 25 `Action.type` values from `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2 with their per-type required/optional parameter JSON Schemas from §11.6, each declaring the permission it needs (`orders:write`, `rules.loosen_stop` for `only_tighten=false`, `rules.arm_live`), its target semantics (`scope_accounts`/`originating_account`/`all_accounts`), and whether it is idempotent or guarded.
- The trigger catalogue: the 13 trigger types with their required companion fields.
- The operator catalogue with type/unit compatibility rules (which operators apply to which unit classes; `in_set`/`not_in_set` only for enum-typed metrics).
- `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary` returning `RuleVocabulary` with `x-rbac: { permissions: [rules:read], scope: none }`, ETag-cacheable.
- `GET /api/v1/schemas/rule-ir.json` serving the generated document from E35-T01.
- Unavailability data: for a given symbol, which metrics are unusable because the symbol is not recorded, with the one-click "start recording" action reference the UI needs (US-RULE-002 scenario 2) — surfaced as a `requires_recording` dependency plus the recorder endpoint the UI should call.
- Every heuristic metric flagged `confidence: "estimated"` so the picker and the rule summary can badge it (US-RULE-002 scenario 3) — this is the product-wide *(estimated)* framing from the detector screens.

## Out of scope
- Implementing any metric — they come from E12/E18-E25. This ticket only projects and describes them.
- Rendering the palette — E36/E37.
- Executing actions — **E35-S03**.
- Validating a specific rule against the vocabulary — **E35-T04**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The documented catalogue is complete
  Given the vocabulary endpoint is called
  Then price, R-multiple, ATR, EMA/SMA, swing high/low, CVD and its divergences, delta, imbalance stacks, absorption, stop-run, iceberg flags,
       tape-speed z-score, book speed, regime, spread, funding rate and time-to-funding, OI change, position age, unrealised PnL,
       account equity and drawdown are each present with a unit and a description

Scenario: Estimated metrics are badged
  Given a metric whose registry descriptor has confidence other than exact
  When the vocabulary is returned
  Then that entry carries estimated: true so the picker and the rule summary can display the (estimated) badge

Scenario: Unavailable metric names its dependency (edge case)
  Given a symbol that is not in the recorded-symbol list
  When the vocabulary is requested scoped to that symbol
  Then metrics needing recorded data are returned disabled, each naming the missing dependency and the recorder action that would satisfy it

Scenario: Actions declare their permission (failure case)
  Given a user without orders:write on any account
  When the vocabulary is returned
  Then order-placing actions are present but marked as available in simulate mode only, with the restriction explained in text

Scenario: The registry is the single source (regression guard)
  Given a metric is added to the MetricRegistry without a vocabulary descriptor
  When CI runs
  Then the completeness test fails naming the metric, so the two lists cannot drift
```

## Technical notes / design
Metric identity must be **stable across versions** (US-RULE-002 NFR) — renaming a metric breaks every stored rule referencing it, so renames go through the IR migration path (E35-T05), never a silent change. Enforce with a golden file of metric names checked into the repo; removing or renaming an entry fails CI unless an accompanying upcaster exists.

Unit coherence is the mechanism ADR-0007 binding rule 2 relies on: "the compiler rejects unit-incoherent comparisons (`atr(14) > 5 %` is a compile error unless an explicit conversion is present)". The unit taxonomy published here is what E35-T04 checks against, so it must be exhaustive and every metric must carry one — a metric with a null unit is a CI failure.

Response is large and static-ish: serve with a strong ETag derived from the registry content hash plus the caller's permission set (permissions change what is marked available), and a `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`. SCR-081 states the vocabulary is cached client-side; the ETag is what makes an editor reload cheap.

The `vocabulary-unavailable (engine offline)` state named in SCR-081 must be distinguishable: return `503` with the standard problem document rather than an empty catalogue, so the editor shows the engine-offline state instead of an editor with no metrics.

## Test plan
Unit: projection of a fake registry into vocabulary entries; unit taxonomy exhaustiveness; permission-dependent availability marking; ETag stability and change-on-content-change.
Completeness tests: every `Action.type` in the IR enum has a parameter schema and a permission declaration; every trigger type has its companion-field rule; every registry metric has a descriptor (the regression guard scenario); the golden metric-name file matches.
Contract: response validates against the `RuleVocabulary` schema in `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the served `rule-ir.json` validates the whole fixture corpus.
Integration: vocabulary scoped to an unrecorded symbol returns the disabled entries with dependencies.
Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: the vocabulary is an information-disclosure surface — it must not leak account ids, account names or symbol permissions the caller lacks. `x-rbac` is `scope: none` for the catalogue itself, but the *availability* annotations are computed from the caller's grants, so the response varies per user and must not be cached in a shared cache (hence `Cache-Control: private`). Action permission declarations here are advisory for the UI only; the authoritative check happens in E35-S03/S04 at execution time — never trust the client to have respected them.

## Accessibility notes
No direct UI, but this payload carries the text the editors display: every metric and action needs a plain-language `description` and `label` written for a non-programmer, because those strings become the accessible names in CMP-157 MetricPickerCombobox and the plain-language rule summary that US-RULE-004's NFR makes the accessible description of a rule. Copy is reviewed by a designer before merge.

## Performance notes
Response is served from an in-process cache rebuilt on registry change; endpoint p95 <=50 ms. Payload is expected in the low hundreds of KB — enable gzip/brotli and verify the editors' initial load stays inside the SCR-081 budget.

## Observability
`rule_vocabulary_requests_total{cache}`, `rule_vocabulary_build_duration_seconds`. Log a warning naming any registry metric lacking a descriptor at startup (in addition to the CI failure) so a runtime-registered metric cannot silently vanish from the palette.

title: Implement the semantic validator and the compile and validate endpoints
body:
## Context
This is the contract both editors live against and the hinge of the round-trip guarantee. `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` "accepts either editor's native model and returns canonical IR plus its `ir_hash`. Compiling the form model and the graph model of the same rule MUST produce an identical hash; that equality is the round-trip guarantee asserted by the contract tests in 24-internal-schemas.md §11.4." `POST /api/v1/rules/validate` is the static analysis both editors call on debounce, checking "schema conformance, variable existence, type compatibility, action-parameter completeness, unreachable branches, missing guards, and the `require_native_stop` invariant", returning errors **and** warnings — warnings do not block saving but do block arming.

SCR-081's round-trip indicator has four designed states driven by this endpoint on every save and every editor-mode switch, and a mismatch is an audited event (`rule.roundtrip_verified`, `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved`) because "a mismatch resolution can silently change what an armed rule does".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Compiler front-ends**: `compile_form(model) -> IR` and `compile_graph(model) -> IR`, both targeting the single `packages/rule_ir` representation from E35-T01. The form model is the linear restricted subset; the graph model is the general DAG.
- **Decompilers**: `to_form_model(ir)` (valid only when `form_compatible(ir)`) and `to_graph_model(ir)` with auto-layout when no `graph_layout` exists — these are what make the round trip closed rather than one-way.
- **Graph well-formedness**: reject cycles (ADR-0007 binding rule 4 — "graphs must be acyclic and must reduce to a single boolean condition plus an ordered action list; cycles and multiple sinks are compile errors with a clear message"), report the cycle as a path of node ids, reject orphan nodes that reach no action and dangling required input ports, listing each by node id for the editor's jump-to-node error list (US-RULE-005 scenarios).
- **Node-only construct marking**: when a graph uses a construct outside the form subset (shared sub-expression fan-out, nested arithmetic, `n_of`, multi-level nesting), record it in the IR at creation time so the form editor renders it read-only rather than discovering it at switch time (US-RULE-005 final scenario, US-RULE-006 read-only fallback).
- **Semantic validator** producing `RuleValidationResult` (`valid`, `errors[]`, `warnings[]` each with `path`/`code`/`message`, `referenced_variables`, `referenced_actions`, `estimated_evaluations_per_minute`): metric existence against E35-T03's vocabulary; **unit/type coherence** per ADR-0007 binding rule 2 (`atr(14) > 5%` is an error without an explicit conversion); operator applicability; action parameter completeness against the per-action schemas; unreachable branches; missing guards (`guard_missing` warning when no cooldown is set on a high-frequency trigger); the `require_native_stop` invariant; and the **feedback-loop guard** from §11.7 — "a rule whose own action would re-trigger it is rejected at save time by static analysis".
- **Safety-class warnings** are a distinct class, because `PUT /rules/{id}/mode` refuses to arm with open warnings of class `safety`.
- `POST /api/v1/rules/validate` and `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` handlers with their documented RBAC, plus the `rule_ir_invalid` (422) error code already registered in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- The `422` response returns the offending JSON path, never a bare failure.

## Out of scope
- Persisting a compiled version — **E35-S01**.
- Evaluating the IR — **E35-S02**.
- Rendering validation results — E36 (CMP-234 ValidationPanel) and E37.
- Conflict detection *between* rules — **E35-S07** (this ticket validates one rule in isolation).
- Auto-layout aesthetics beyond a deterministic, semantics-preserving arrangement — refinement is E37.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both editors compile to the same hash
  Given the form model and the graph model of one semantically identical rule
  When each is posted to POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile
  Then both responses carry the same ir_hash and an empty issues list

Scenario: Unit-incoherent comparison is a compile error (failure case)
  Given a condition comparing atr(14), a price-unit metric, to a percent literal with no explicit conversion
  When the IR is validated
  Then valid is false and an error names the offending node path with code type_mismatch and an explanation naming both units

Scenario: A cycle is refused with a readable path (failure case)
  Given a graph model whose node output feeds back into one of its own upstream inputs
  When it is compiled
  Then a 422 rule_ir_invalid is returned naming the cycle as an ordered list of node ids
  And no IR is produced

Scenario: A self-retriggering rule is refused at save time (edge case)
  Given a rule triggered on_order_fill whose only action places an order in the same scope
  When it is validated
  Then the feedback-loop guard raises a safety-class error explaining the loop

Scenario: Warnings inform but do not block saving
  Given a rule with no cooldown on an on_price_update trigger
  When it is validated
  Then valid is true with a guard_missing warning at path guards.cooldown_seconds
  And the rule can be saved but cannot be armed while a safety-class warning is open

Scenario: Graph-only construct is marked at compile time, not at switch time
  Given a graph fanning one node output into two consumers
  When it is compiled
  Then the resulting IR records the node-only marking so the form editor renders that sub-tree read-only on first load
```

## Technical notes / design
Compilation pipeline, both front-ends: parse editor model -> build IR nodes -> topological check -> canonicalise (E35-T01) -> hash -> validate -> return `{ir, ir_hash, issues}`.

The **round-trip diff** required by SCR-081/SCR-088 is produced here: when the caller supplies both the form model and the stored graph representation, the endpoint compiles both and, on divergence, returns a structured diff of the two canonical documents. US-RULE-006 requires this to be downloadable and the switch to be **aborted** on mismatch, leaving the rule untouched and emitting a high-severity telemetry event — the server must therefore never auto-reconcile a mismatch.

`estimated_evaluations_per_minute` is computed from the trigger type, debounce and (for `on_bar_close`) the timeframe; it is what lets the UI warn about a rule that would evaluate thousands of times a minute before it is armed.

Auto-layout (`to_graph_model` when `graph_layout` is absent) must be **deterministic** — same IR gives the same coordinates — otherwise opening a form-authored rule in the graph editor twice would produce two different `presentation` blocks and confuse the user (though not the hash, since layout is excluded). A simple layered Sugiyama-style pass over the DAG is sufficient.

Every error and warning carries a stable machine `code` (`type_mismatch`, `unknown_metric`, `missing_action_param`, `guard_missing`, `unreachable_branch`, `cycle_detected`, `orphan_node`, `dangling_port`, `feedback_loop`, `native_stop_violation`, `permission_required`) because the editors key their inline messages and jump-to-node behaviour off the code, not the prose.

## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): one case per error/warning code, valid and invalid; compile/decompile round trip per fixture; auto-layout determinism; cycle detection over self-loop, two-node loop and long loop; orphan and dangling-port detection; `estimated_evaluations_per_minute` arithmetic per trigger type.
Property-based: for every generated form-subset IR, `compile_form(to_form_model(ir))` has the same hash as `ir`; for every generated IR, `compile_graph(to_graph_model(ir))` has the same hash. This is the core of the R3 exit-criterion-5 machinery; **E35-Q02** scales it to 10 000 documents per run.
Contract: `/rules/validate` and `/rules/{ruleId}/compile` request/response shapes against `22-api-openapi.yaml`, including the documented examples (`withWarning`, `invalid`) verbatim.
Integration: validation against a live vocabulary including an unrecorded symbol and an estimated metric.
Perf: 100-node compile + diff p95 <=500 ms (SCR-081); validate p95 <=300 ms.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: the validator is a **safety gate**, not a convenience. Two checks are security-relevant and must have dedicated tests that would fail loudly if removed: the `require_native_stop` invariant (no compiled rule may produce a plan that removes the native exchange-side SL — ADR-0007 binding rule 7, ADR-0008) and the `only_tighten` default on stop modifications (setting `only_tighten=false` requires the `rules.loosen_stop` permission and the Owner role). Compilation must be bounded: reject documents exceeding the schema's node limits before walking them, so a hostile model cannot make the compiler itself the DoS vector. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
No UI, but the message text produced here is read verbatim by screen readers through CMP-234 ValidationPanel and the editors' inline errors. Messages must name the row/node in words ("Row 2 is missing a value.", "`position_side` compares to long/short, not a number." — the exact examples in SCR-081), never rely on colour or position alone, and never surface a raw stack trace or JSON pointer as the only explanation.

## Performance notes
Budgets: validate round trip <=300 ms; compile + round-trip diff <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node rule (both from the SCR-081 performance note). Validation runs on debounce, not per keystroke — the server must not assume otherwise but should stay cheap enough that it would not matter. Benchmarked in CI with a 100-node fixture.

## Observability
`rule_compile_total{editor,result}`, `rule_compile_duration_seconds`, `rule_validate_total{valid}`, `rule_roundtrip_mismatch_total` (high-severity; alerts). Audit `rule.validated` and `rule.roundtrip_verified {result: identical|graph_only_construct|mismatch|unverified}`. A mismatch logs both hashes and stores the diff for support.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-T01** (IR models and canonicalisation) and **E35-T03** (vocabulary to validate against). Blocks **E35-S01**, **E35-S02**, and both editors E36/E37 — this is the contract they build to, so it merges early in S15.

title: UX research: how a trader expresses a stop-management rule in words
body:
## Context
E36 introduces the non-canvas authoring path for rules (SCR-081) and it must be good enough that nobody is *forced* onto the node canvas — `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 makes the form view the mandated accessible equivalent of the graph. Before any pixels are drawn we need to know how the Owner and the account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`, persona mode **M1 Rule-author**) actually phrase the rules they already run by hand: "move my stop to break-even once I'm up 1R", "trail two ATRs but never loosen".

The vocabulary is fixed and large (24 metrics, 16 actions — `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-081). The open question is not *what* is available but *how it should be grouped, named and defaulted* so that a rule reads back as a sentence rather than as a query builder.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 5 semi-structured sessions (Owner + managers, 45 min) capturing verbatim the last five rules each person ran manually, and how they would express them.
- A card-sort of the metric vocabulary (the 24 metrics listed on SCR-081) producing the category set for CMP-157 `category` prop (`price | position | orderflow | risk | detector`) — confirm or replace it with evidence.
- A comprehension test of the plain-language rule summary: show three summaries, ask what the rule does; target ≥4/5 correct.
- A decision on grouping UX: nested groups vs a flat "all of / any of" with one nesting level (SCR-081 shows "+ any-of group"); record the chosen model and its limits, because this decides which constructs become "graph-only".
- A decision on *(estimated)* framing: where the badge must appear (picker option, condition row, rule summary, list row, arming dialog) so it is never lost — US-RULE-002 requires it in picker and summary at minimum.
- Findings deck + a one-page "authoring principles" note that D02/D03 are held against; any resulting update to `docs/plan/10-personas.md` and `docs/plan/13-user-flows.md` F10.

## Out of scope

- The plain-language rule summary block and the scope chip ("2 accounts · BTCUSDT · new positions", US-RULE-007).
- CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice placement — persistent, non-dismissible, present in the composition.
- **SCR-083** hi-fi: template cards for all twelve catalogue templates with plain-language behaviour text, required metrics, recorded-history requirement, estimated-detector badge, which editor it opens in, search/filter, preview-before-instantiate, empty/no-results states.

Node-canvas designs (E37). SCR-080/088/089 (E36-D03). Motion beyond what the DS already defines is specified in D03. Arming dialog SCR-085 and simulate panel SCR-084 (E35).

```gherkin
Scenario: Every state has a frame

  Then each exists as its own frame with realistic content, not as a note
Scenario: Long content does not break the layout (edge)
  Given a rule with 12 conditions, 6 actions, a nested any-of group and a 40-character metric name at 200% zoom
  Then the frame shows the intended overflow, wrapping and sticky-action-bar behaviour
Scenario: A blocking mismatch is unambiguous (failure)
  Given the Round-trip mismatch state
  Then saving is visibly disabled, the diff entry point is drawn, and each of the two recovery choices restates in text exactly what will be lost
```

## Technical notes / design
Built from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` tokens only; any new token or variant is raised in D03 as a design-system contribution rather than being drawn ad hoc. Metric list used in the frames must be exactly: price, unrealized_r_multiple, unrealized_pnl_pct, realized_pnl_today, position_side, position_open, atr(n), ema(n), swing_low(n), swing_high(n), cvd_divergence, spread_bps, time_in_trade, orderbook_imbalance, funding_rate, iceberg_present_at_level *(estimated)*, distance_to_liquidity_cluster *(estimated)*, in_stop_hunt_zone *(estimated)*, stop_run_detected *(estimated)*, big_trade_notional, tape_speed_zscore, market_regime *(estimated)*, dom_imbalance_ratio, open_interest_delta. Design review with the Architect (IR representability), a rule-author persona walkthrough of three concrete rules, and a contrast/target-size check with the DS plugin before hand-off.

Frames must not contain real account ids or key material. The `flatten_all_positions` and order-placing actions are drawn in the destructive-action visual class per the safety framing.

Annotate focus order, roles and names for every control; each condition row annotated as a labelled group "Condition N of M"; error summary → in-page link behaviour annotated; contrast ≥4.5:1 for text and ≥3:1 for the amber/blocking indicator states, and none of the four round-trip states may be distinguished by colour alone.

Annotate that validation is debounced (300 ms) and that the compile/round-trip check runs on save and on mode switch only, so the indicator must have an explicit "stale/checking" treatment.

Annotate where `rule.roundtrip_verified` and `rule.template_instantiated` fire, so instrumentation is not invented by engineering.

Figma file with all frames, states and annotations; checklist initialled; CDO and Architect sign-off comments; linked from the SCR-081/SCR-083 catalogue entries; Status Done ≥2 sprints before Sprint 16.

Native stops are unaffected.").

Annotate `rule.exported`, `rule.imported`, `rule.ir_viewed`, `rule.ir_copied` trigger points.

Frontend work in Sprint 17 (E37-S01/S02/S03) cannot start until this ticket is Done and has been Done for >=2 sprints (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 design-ready). This ticket is therefore scheduled in **Sprint 14**, so the full design chain (D02 -> D03 -> D04 -> D05) completes by the end of **Sprint 15** and Sprint-17 stories get a genuine two-sprint design-ahead buffer rather than a one-sprint hand-over.

The catalogue's own sign-off checklist for SCR-082 is the contract this ticket must satisfy: palette, canvas, node, port, edge, minimap and inspector all drawn; valid/invalid connection feedback; cycle-detected state; the node-list keyboard authoring panel drawn and confirmed equal-status; round-trip indicator and the "unsupported in form view" warning; auto-layout reviewed on a 60-node graph; reduced-motion variant.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma frames for SCR-082 at the reference desktop breakpoints, covering **every** state listed in `14-screens-catalogue.md`: empty canvas ("Start from a trigger" hint) · editing · invalid connection (with the inline typed reason, e.g. "A metric output can't connect to a trigger input") · cycle detected · unsupported-construct warning · engine/vocabulary unavailable · read-only (armed rule being viewed).
- The four round-trip indicator states drawn in the header, each with its tooltip/panel: `Round-trips ✓`, `Unsupported in form view` (incl. the clickable "What won't round-trip" panel listing offending nodes by accessible name), `Round-trip mismatch` (blocking, with the diff presentation and the two named recovery choices, each restating what is lost), `Not verified`.
- Node designs for CMP-147 TriggerNode, CMP-148 ConditionNode, CMP-149 ActionNode, CMP-150 LogicGateNode, CMP-151 CommentNode: default, selected, focused, error, warning/"node-only" badged, collapsed, read-only.
- CMP-237 NodePort states (input/output × connected/unconnected × compatible/incompatible/active-connect), CMP-152 NodeGraphEdge (default, selected, invalid-preview, labelled), CMP-236 NodePalette (default, searching, no results, collapsed category), CMP-238 Minimap, CMP-153 NodeInspectorDrawer for each node type.
- The **`Alt+L` keyboard node-list panel** drawn as a first-class, equal-status surface — not a fallback — showing add/connect/delete affordances, the connection description text, and the enumerated diagnostics/badged nodes.
- CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice placement in this editor (non-dismissible), CMP-234 ValidationPanel graph-anchored variant, CMP-235 EditorModeToggle in each of its four indicator states.
- Redline/spec notes: spacing, type, tokens, node minimum target sizes (>=24×24 CSS px per `05-accessibility-standard.md`), z-order, and the density behaviour at 60 and 200 nodes.

## Out of scope
- Design-system token *creation* and motion specs (→ E37-D03); a11y review (→ E37-D04); handoff package (→ E37-D05); design QA of the built screen (→ E37-D06).
- SCR-081 form mode, SCR-083 templates, SCR-084 simulate, SCR-085 arming, SCR-088 IR inspector — E36/E35 designs.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue state exists as a frame
  Given the state list in 14-screens-catalogue.md for SCR-082
  When the Figma file is reviewed against it
  Then each state has a named frame, and the SCR-082 design sign-off checklist is ticked item by item with the frame link next to each item

Scenario: The round-trip mismatch state is unambiguous
  Given the Round-trip mismatch frame
  Then saving and arming are visibly blocked, the diverging node is highlighted on canvas and selected in the node list, and both recovery choices state in words what is lost — no auto-resolution is depicted anywhere

Scenario: The graph is never the only path (a11y-critical)
  Given the Alt+L node-list frames
  Then every operation drawn on the canvas (add, connect, delete, inspect, rename, auto-layout, navigate to a diagnostic) has an equivalent affordance drawn in the node list, reviewed item-by-item against the canvas frames

Scenario: Dense graph legibility (edge)
  Given a 60-node and a 200-node mock
  Then node chrome, edge routing and the minimap remain legible at 100% and 125% zoom, and any degradation strategy (collapsed node chrome, edge de-emphasis) is drawn rather than left to implementation

Scenario: A state cannot be represented within the design system (failure)
  Given a needed state has no existing token or component
  Then it is raised as a design-system contribution in E37-D03 rather than drawn as a one-off
```

## Technical notes / design
Build on the existing design system (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`); node colours use the `color.node.trigger|condition|action|logic|comment` tokens named in the component catalogue, and every status is text+glyph, never colour alone. The "node-only"/unsupported badge must be a non-colour glyph per SCR-082's a11y note. Frames are named `SCR-082 / <state>` so E37-D06 design QA can diff them against the build one-to-one.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification = the checklist walk-through in the acceptance criteria plus the design review with the CDO, the E37 frontend lead and the accessibility specialist.

## Security notes
Frames must depict demo-environment data only, no real account labels or key material. The arming affordance drawn here must route to SCR-085 rather than depicting an in-canvas arm control, so the step-up-auth path is never designed around.

## Accessibility notes
Contrast >=4.5:1 for text and >=3:1 for the graphical port/edge states; focus rings specified for canvas nodes, ports and edges (the shared focus-ring utility, CMP-035); reduced-motion variant with edge animation removed; target sizes specified. This ticket *draws* a11y; E37-D04 *reviews* it.

The design must not require per-frame text re-layout on pan/zoom (e.g. no node chrome that reflows with zoom level) so the 200-node 60 fps budget in SCR-082 stays reachable; any zoom-dependent detail level is drawn explicitly as discrete tiers.

## Observability
The analytics events E37-S01 emits (`rule.graph_node_added`, `rule.graph_autolayout_used`) are named in the spec notes so engineering instruments exactly what design expects to measure.

The node editor introduces primitives the design system does not yet own: a node container with typed ports, an edge, a connect-in-progress state, a minimap and a canvas surface. `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` already reserves the component IDs (CMP-146..153, CMP-236..238) and names tokens (`color.node.*`, `color.edge.default/selected`, `color.port.*`, `color.surface.canvas`, `color.surface.sunken`), but the token values, the motion behaviour and the Storybook contract do not exist. Without this ticket each node type would be styled ad hoc, which `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 explicitly forbids ("any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off").

Motion matters here specifically because edges animate on connect and auto-layout moves every node at once — both are exactly the kinds of motion that trigger vestibular issues and both must have a reduced-motion path.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Token definitions (light + dark themes, both density modes) for `color.node.trigger|condition|action|logic|comment`, `color.node.border.{default,selected,error,warning}`, `color.port.{in,out,connected,compatible,incompatible}`, `color.edge.{default,selected,invalid}`, `color.surface.canvas`, `radius.node`, `space.node.*` — each contrast-verified against its background in both themes.
- Motion spec: connect-in-progress edge preview, connection-made confirmation, node add/remove, selection change, auto-layout transition (duration, easing, stagger, maximum total duration), minimap viewport tracking, inspector drawer open/close (inherits CMP-046). Each with an explicit `prefers-reduced-motion` variant that removes movement rather than merely shortening it.
- Design-system entries for CMP-146, CMP-147..CMP-152, CMP-153, CMP-236, CMP-237, CMP-238: props table alignment with the catalogue API sketches, the Storybook story list named in the catalogue (e.g. CMP-146: EmptyCanvas, SimpleChain, BranchingLogic, ReadOnly, KeyboardNavDemo, FormViewToggleDemo), and usage/anti-usage guidance.
- Focus-ring specification for canvas-adjacent focusables (nodes, ports, edges) reusing CMP-035's shared focus-ring utility so the ring is visually identical to the rest of the product.
- Density/zoom tiers: what node chrome is shown at each zoom tier, specified as discrete tiers so rendering can switch cheaply.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi screen composition (E37-D02); the a11y review itself (E37-D04); implementation of any token or story (E37-S01/S02).
- Chart-engine canvas tokens — separate, owned by the charting epics.

## Acceptance criteria
