```gherkin
  When contrast is measured against every surface they appear on, in light and dark
  Then text meets 4.5:1 and graphical boundaries meet 3:1, with the measurements recorded in the token documentation

Scenario: Reduced motion removes movement
  Given prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  Then auto-layout repositions nodes with no animated transit, edge previews do not animate, and the spec states this explicitly per animation rather than as a blanket note

Scenario: Auto-layout motion has a hard ceiling
  Given a 200-node graph is auto-laid-out
  Then the specified transition completes within 400 ms total regardless of node count, with stagger capped rather than per-node accumulating

Scenario: A node type has no distinguishable non-colour treatment (failure)
  Given two node types are distinguished only by hue in a draft
  Then the spec is corrected to add a shape, icon or label difference before sign-off, because status and type must never be colour-only
```

## Technical notes / design
Tokens follow the naming and theming conventions in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; emitted as design tokens consumed by the web app's theme layer, not hand-copied hex. Motion values expressed as tokens (`motion.duration.*`, `motion.easing.*`) so reduced-motion overrides happen at the token layer. The zoom tiers are specified as a table (zoom range → visible chrome) that E37-S01 implements verbatim.

## Test plan
Storybook visual-regression baselines exist for each new component's story list (implemented in E37-S01/S02, specified here); contrast checks recorded in the token docs; reduced-motion variants captured as separate visual-regression stories.

## Security notes
N/A — presentation tokens only. (One exception: the "node-only"/unsupported and error treatments are safety-relevant communication, so they may not be de-emphasised for aesthetic reasons; this is stated in the usage guidance.)

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is where the non-colour encoding rule is made structural: every node type, port state and diagnostic severity has a glyph or shape in addition to hue. Focus rings must be visible against the canvas surface in both themes. Reduced-motion variants are mandatory, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
Zoom tiers are specified so the renderer can drop text and detail at low zoom; motion is capped so auto-layout on a 200-node graph cannot blow the frame budget.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Tokens defined, contrast-verified, published to the design-token source of record.
- [ ] Motion spec complete with a reduced-motion variant per animation.
- [ ] Design-system entries written for CMP-146..153, CMP-236..238, aligned with `15-component-catalogue.md` props and story lists.
- [ ] Reviewed by the design-system team lead and the CDO; frontend lead confirms implementability.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` and `16-design-system-brief.md` updated where they diverge.
- [ ] Done >=2 sprints before the Sprint 17/18 stories that consume it.

## Dependencies
> **Schedule note.** Pulled forward as part of the E37 design-ahead resequencing (D03 -> Sprint 14, D04 -> Sprint 15) so that E37-D05 closes in Sprint 15 and every consuming story has a >=2-sprint design buffer.

Blocked by **E37-D02** (frames define what needs tokenising). Feeds E37-D05 handoff and E37-S01/S02.

title: Spike: validate the graph library for 200-node fps and keyboard connect
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 names React Flow / Rete.js as the preferred candidates *specifically because they render nodes as real DOM elements*, which is what makes the mandated DOM-mirror a11y strategy possible. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 names React Flow for E37. But the two binding non-functional requirements have never been measured against the chosen library: **200 nodes at 60 fps** (SCR-082 §Performance) and a **fully keyboard-operable connect flow** (US-RULE-005, CMP-237). If React Flow cannot meet both without heroic customisation, the whole of E37-S01/S02/S05 is mis-scoped, and we need to know before Sprint 17 starts.

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5 applies: this spike answers questions and produces an ADR, not shippable code.

## Scope / Deliverables
Timebox: **4 working days**, agreed with the Architect.

Questions to answer:
1. Does React Flow (current major version, pinned) sustain **60 fps pan/zoom on a 200-node / ~260-edge graph** on the reference hardware in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1, inside Electron and Chromium, with our node chrome (not stock demo nodes)?
2. Can nodes, ports and edges each be made individually focusable with roving tabindex, without fighting the library's own pointer-first interaction layer, and can a **keyboard connect** (focus output port → `Enter` → arrow to target port → `Enter`) be implemented on top of the library's controlled state?
3. Does the library's controlled `nodes`/`edges` model let `packages/rule-graph` own state fully, so `graph_layout` can be persisted separately from the IR and excluded from the canonical hash?
4. What does auto-layout cost? Measure a layout library (`elkjs` vs `dagre`) on 60- and 200-node graphs: wall-clock, main-thread block time, and whether it must run in a worker.
5. Bundle cost of the editor route (library + layout + our code), gzipped, to confirm it can be lazily code-split out of the initial bundle (budget #9).
6. Fallback assessment of Rete.js on the same criteria, sufficient to make a decision rather than a guess.

Decision criteria agreed up front:
- If (1) fails below **45 fps** at 200 nodes after one round of reasonable optimisation (virtualised node rendering, memoised edges), the scope of SCR-082 is reduced to a documented node cap (e.g. 120 nodes with a warning beyond it) rather than switching library late — and that cap is written into SCR-082 and E37-S01.
- If (2) requires forking the library, React Flow is rejected in favour of Rete.js or a thin in-house node layer, and E37-S01/S02 are re-estimated before Sprint 17 planning.
- If (4) blocks the main thread >100 ms at 200 nodes, auto-layout moves to a web worker in E37-T02 by default.

Deliverables: a throwaway prototype branch, a benchmark table (fps p50/p95, layout time, block time, bundle delta), a keyboard-connect proof-of-concept recording, and an ADR.

## Out of scope
- Production-quality components, styling against the design tokens, or any IR integration beyond a hard-coded sample graph.
- Evaluating graph libraries not shortlisted in the component catalogue.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All six questions answered with recorded evidence
  When the timebox ends
  Then each question has a written answer backed by a benchmark number, a code snippet or a recording, and no question is left as an opinion

Scenario: The fps question is answered on a realistic graph
  Given a 200-node graph using our real node chrome and edge styling
  When pan and zoom are exercised for 60 seconds
  Then p50 and p95 frame times are recorded in Electron and Chromium on reference hardware, and compared against the 16.6 ms budget

Scenario: Keyboard connect is proven or refuted
  Given the prototype
  When a connection is made using only the keyboard
  Then either a recording shows the full flow working with announcements, or the blocking limitation is documented with the library API that prevents it

Scenario: A criterion fails (failure path)
  Given any decision criterion is not met
```

body:

This ticket turns that into a signed-off, token-accurate specification.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for **SCR-071** in every catalogue state: normal · warning (≥80 % of a cap) · locked (showing what was auto-flattened and when) · frozen · stale data · reconciling after reconnect · Manager-scoped variant (only granted accounts) · Viewer read-only.
- Hi-fi frames for **SCR-073** in states: active lockout (reason, breached limit, actual value, reset time) · what-remains-possible affordance (closing/reducing allowed, opening blocked) · manager override-request path with the owner-approval loop · post-expiry.

- Redlines/handoff annotations sufficient for E39-S04 to build without asking questions: exact data field → visual element mapping against `RiskSummary` (`22-api-openapi.yaml`), including `totals.positions_without_native_stop` (critical banner when non-zero) and `accounts[].lockout`.

```gherkin
Scenario (edge): Stale account data
  Given one account's feed is down
  Then the frame shows an explicit "stale" treatment with the last-known timestamp, never a stale number presented as current

Scenario (failure): Contrast failure blocks sign-off
  Given a token pairing measures below 4.5:1 for text
  Then the frame is reworked before sign-off; a waiver is not available
```

## Technical notes / design
Frames live in Figma `CandleViewer / R3 Trading` → `E39 Risk & safety`, named `SCR-071 / <state>` and `SCR-073 / <state>`. ## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification is the design review plus an automated contrast check over the exported token pairs.

## Security notes
No secrets rendered in any frame; account labels are fixtures. The override control must be drawn as step-up gated (SR-025) — a frame showing override without the step-up step is incorrect.

## Accessibility notes
Contrast ≥4.5:1 text / ≥3:1 non-text on every state; focus order annotated for the dashboard's control row; SCR-073 is `role="alert"` on appearance, then persists as a banner and is **not dismissible** while the lockout holds; meters expose numeric values in text (CMP-138 extends the CMP-023 ProgressBar contract); reduced-motion variants specified.

## Performance notes
Design assumes server-side aggregation and ≤1 Hz UI refresh (SCR-071 performance note); no design element may require per-tick recomputation on the client.

N/A.

title: Hi-fi SCR-072 kill-switch modal and SCR-134 risk policy, CMP-211 spec and handoff
body:
## Context
Hi-fi design for the two *action* surfaces of E39: **SCR-072 Kill-switch / freeze confirmation modal** and **SCR-134 Admin: risk policy (global)** (route `/admin/risk-policy`), plus the **CMP-211 PanicButtons** cluster that lives permanently in the app-shell top bar (SCR-010). These are the highest-consequence controls in the product: a mis-designed confirmation here is a trading incident, which is why this design ticket is P0.

`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-072 fixes the hard requirements: the modal names exactly which accounts and users are affected, restates the consequence in text ("This cancels 14 working orders and blocks new orders on 5 accounts. Open positions are NOT closed."), requires typing `FREEZE`, and offers "also cancel working orders" and "also flatten positions" as explicit checkboxes **both defaulting off**.

Consumed by E39-S05 in Sprint 16 → Done required by end of Sprint 14 (design-ahead rule).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for **SCR-072**: scope selector (this account / all accounts / this symbol) · consequence restatement with live counts · typed `FREEZE` confirmation · the two opt-in checkboxes · executing (per-account progress) · completed summary driven by `KillSwitchResult.actions` (`orders_cancelled`, `positions_flattened`, `rules_disarmed`) · partial failure with per-account retry · the **unfreeze** path with its own confirmation and step-up · DEMO vs LIVE variants.
- Hi-fi frames for **SCR-134**: every global limit drawn with units (max daily loss, max drawdown, max total notional, max positions, max leverage, max orders/min, per-symbol concentration) · breach-behaviour selector per limit (warn / block new orders / flatten) · the current measured value beside each limit · per-user and per-account override visibility · the "this cannot be disabled entirely" guard · step-up gate on save · change summary before save · the validation warning when a portfolio cap is below the sum of the smallest per-account caps.
- **CMP-211 PanicButtons** spec: the Flatten-all / Cancel-all / Kill-switch cluster for `scope: account|group|global`, `confirmMode: hold|typed|single`, enabled/disabled (Viewer) states, and the hold-confirmation progress treatment with its keyboard equivalent. PR to `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`.
- **Global hotkey treatment**: the roadmap requires the kill-switch to be flippable "from the admin screen and from a global hotkey" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2). Design the hotkey's on-screen affordance, its discoverability in the hotkey cheatsheet (SCR-013), and the confirmation it still requires — the hotkey opens SCR-072, it never fires directly.
- Formal **a11y review** of both screens and the **handoff package** for E39-S05 (redlines, token map, field→element mapping against `SetKillSwitchRequest` / `KillSwitchResult`).

## Out of scope
- SCR-071 / SCR-073 (E39-D02).
- The flatten-all *runbook* text (E39-T03).
- The feature-flag console that also exposes the kill-switch (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Consequence is unambiguous
  Given a reviewer with no prior context reads the SCR-072 primary frame
  When asked whether open positions will be closed
  Then they answer "no" without the facilitator explaining

Scenario: Defaults are safe
  Given the SCR-072 frame as first rendered
  Then "also cancel working orders" and "also flatten positions" are both unchecked
  And the primary action is not the default-focused control

Scenario: Partial failure is a first-class frame
  Given a freeze where 1 of 5 accounts failed
  Then a frame shows which account failed, why, and a per-account retry
  And the succeeded accounts are not re-executed by that retry

Scenario (edge): SCR-134 conflicting caps
  Given a portfolio cap lower than the sum of the smallest per-account caps
  Then an explanatory warning frame exists naming which caps conflict
```

## Technical notes / design
Figma page `E39 Risk & safety`, frames `SCR-072 / <state>`, `SCR-134 / <state>`, `CMP-211 / <variant>`. SCR-072 composes CMP-044 ConfirmDialog (`variant="typed"`), CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton and CMP-027 ErrorState. SCR-134 composes CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 and CMP-138. The completion summary must render zero counts gracefully ("0 orders cancelled — none were working").

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Verification is the moderated comprehension test in the acceptance criteria plus the exported-token contrast check.

## Security notes
Step-up authentication (SR-025) is a **drawn step**, not an implied one, for: releasing the kill-switch, saving SCR-134, and any override. The modal must never render an account's API key, fingerprint or balance detail beyond what SCR-071 already shows. The DEMO/LIVE variant distinction exists so a LIVE freeze can never be mistaken for a DEMO one.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-072 is `role="alertdialog"`; the exact consequence is restated in text; confirmation requires typing `FREEZE`; **focus starts on the Cancel control**; the hold-to-confirm gesture on CMP-211 exposes progress via `aria-valuenow` and has a keyboard equivalent (hold `Enter`); panic buttons are never icon-only and carry scope in their accessible name ("Flatten all positions — all accounts"). SCR-134 uses fieldsets per limit with units and the current measured value beside the limit, and a radio group for enforcement scope.

## Performance notes
The design must reflect that the freeze is one backend call halting acceptance server-side within 200 ms, with per-account completion streaming in afterwards — the UI must not appear blocked while legs report (SCR-072 performance note).

## Observability
The design annotates which control emits which audit action: `risk.freeze` (with the full option set), `risk.unfreeze`, `risk_policy.updated`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All SCR-072 / SCR-134 / CMP-211 frames delivered.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` PR merged for CMP-211.
- [ ] Comprehension test run with ≥2 reviewers, both answering the "does this close positions?" question correctly.

title: Spike: authoritative daily-PnL source and day-boundary semantics for the loss cap
body:
## Context
The daily-loss cap is the cap most likely to be wrong, because "daily loss" is not one number. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-RULE-012 NFR says it is "computed server-side from realised plus unrealised PnL; evaluated on every position/execution event and at least every 5 s". US-POS-009 says "'today' uses the configured day boundary consistently with the daily-loss limit" and warns that fee data may arrive late ("the row shows the PnL as provisional and updates when fees settle"). `24-internal-schemas.md` §11 `sys.daily_loss_lockout` states the built-in rule halts new orders "until next UTC day".

Three sources can supply the number and they disagree: (a) locally-aggregated `executions` + `positions` state, (b) Bybit `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl`, (c) wallet equity deltas. They differ by fee settlement timing, funding attribution, and the exchange's own day boundary. Locking a user out on a wrong number, or *failing* to lock them out because fees had not settled, are both incidents. This spike decides the authoritative source before E39-T01 implements the evaluator.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. This spike is not expected to produce production-shippable code; a throwaway harness is fine.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Comparison harness reading, for one demo account over a 3-day window: local `executions`/`positions`/`position_snapshots` aggregation, `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl`, and `wallet` equity deltas; tabulating divergence per hour with the cause attributed (fee lag, funding, rounding, boundary).
- A decision on: the authoritative realised-PnL source; whether unrealised PnL is included continuously or sampled; the configurable day-boundary semantics (UTC vs a user-configured offset — note `24-internal-schemas.md` says UTC for the built-in rule, so any deviation must be justified and recorded); and the provisional-fee handling policy (does a provisional figure trigger a lockout, or only a settled one?).
- A decision on the evaluation cadence that satisfies "every position/execution event and at least every 5 s" without exceeding the reconciliation rate budget (US-POS-008 NFR: "reconciliation must not exceed the rate budget").
- **ADR-0016** draft section covering the chosen source and boundary (the full ADR is authored in E39-T03).
- Follow-up tickets filed for whatever the chosen path needs that is not already in E39-T01.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the evaluator (E39-T01).
- Max-drawdown semantics beyond confirming whether it shares the same PnL source.
- Journal/analytics PnL reporting (E41) — it may reuse the decision but is not gated by it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Divergence quantified
  Given the 3-day comparison harness has run against a demo account
  Then the maximum observed divergence between each candidate source is reported in USD and as a percentage of the cap
  And each divergence episode is attributed to a named cause

Scenario: Decision recorded with criteria met
  Given the decision criteria stated up front (accuracy within 0.5% of exchange truth, availability without an extra REST call on the hot path, determinism under replay)
  When one source satisfies all three
  Then it is chosen and recorded; if none does, a hybrid is specified explicitly rather than left to implementation

Scenario (failure): Fee-lag worst case
  Given a close whose fees settle 90 seconds later
  Then the spike states what the evaluator does in that window: lock provisionally, defer, or lock on the pessimistic bound
  And the chosen behaviour is justified against "a bad day cannot become a disaster"
```

## Technical notes / design
Decision criteria, agreed before starting:
1. Accuracy within 0.5 % of `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` over the window.
2. Obtainable without an additional REST call on the order hot path (the evaluator has a ≤5 ms p95 budget, so it must read cached/streamed state).
3. Deterministic under replay (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3 exit criterion 6 requires rule-runtime determinism over replay; the risk evaluator shares that constraint because lockouts feed rule behaviour).
If the local aggregation is within 0.5 % it wins on criteria 2 and 3; otherwise a hybrid (local for the hot path, periodic REST reconciliation that can *tighten* but never silently *loosen* an active lockout) is specified.

## Test plan
Harness-level only: a comparison script under `tools/spikes/e39-daily-pnl/` with recorded fixtures checked in so the numbers are reproducible. No coverage target (throwaway code, stated explicitly per DoR §5.1).

## Security notes
The harness uses demo keys only, read through the E27 key vault interface — never plaintext keys in the spike code or in checked-in fixtures. Fixtures must be scrubbed of account identifiers before commit. A wrong decision here is a *safety* finding, so the Security engineer reviews the conclusion even though the spike ships no code.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
The chosen source must be readable within the ≤5 ms p95 evaluator budget; the spike records the measured read latency of each candidate.

## Observability
The spike specifies which metric exposes the divergence in production: `cv_risk_pnl_divergence_usd{account,source}`, alerting above a threshold set by the measured worst case.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.2:
- [ ] Questions answered with recorded evidence (divergence table, latency measurements).
- [ ] Decision recorded as ADR content handed to E39-T03 (ADR-0016).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for the chosen path.
- [ ] Spike code explicitly marked throwaway; branch left unmerged.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new data-accuracy risk surfaced.

## Dependencies
- `E29` — the OMS event stream and `executions`/`positions` tables must exist to aggregate from.
- `E27` — a working demo account with a vaulted key.

## Branch
`spike/e39-daily-pnl-source`. Not merged; findings land via E39-T03's ADR PR.

title: Implement the M17 risk evaluator core with rolling per-account counters
body:
## Context
Module **M17** is the risk/limit enforcement layer named in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 for E39 and in `20-architecture.md` §3.10 as part of the OMS `Validator` responsibilities ("per-account and per-manager risk caps, kill-switch state"). This Task builds its **core**: a pure decision function plus the stateful service that feeds it. Wiring it into the order path is E39-S01; lockouts are E39-S02; the kill-switch is E39-S03. Splitting it this way keeps every ticket ≤8 points and lets the pure evaluator be exhaustively unit-tested before any I/O exists.

Architecture principle P8 (`20-architecture.md` §1) is the reason this is backend-only: "The frontend is never trusted for account scope, risk caps or environment."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Package `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/` containing:
  - `evaluator.py` — **pure** `evaluate(state: AccountRiskState, caps: ResolvedCaps, cmd: OrderCommand) -> RiskDecision`. No I/O, no clock reads (time is passed in), fully deterministic.
  - `caps.py` — cap resolution: merge the global `risk_policy` row, the account's `account_profiles` caps, and the per-manager override `user_account_access.max_daily_loss_usd`, taking the **most restrictive** value per cap. Resolution order and tie-breaking documented in-module and in `24-internal-schemas.md`.
  - `state.py` — `RiskService` maintaining per-account rolling counters: realised PnL today, unrealised PnL, open position count, gross notional per symbol and in aggregate, orders submitted in the trailing 60 s, consecutive losing closes. Fed from the `oms.*` event bus (order/execution/position events) with a periodic reconcile from `position_snapshots` (`reason='risk_eval'`).
  - `clock.py` — day-boundary arithmetic honouring `risk_policy.day_boundary_utc_offset_minutes`, per the E39-K01 decision.
- Caps evaluated: `max_position_notional_usd`, `max_open_positions`, `max_daily_loss_usd` / `max_daily_loss_pct`, `max_drawdown_pct`, `max_orders_per_minute`, `max_consecutive_losses`, `max_leverage`, per-symbol concentration, and `allowed_symbols`/`blocked_symbols` (from `account_profiles`).
- `RiskDecision` carries `allowed: bool`, `code` (`risk_limit_breached` | `account_locked` | `trading_disabled` | `risk_state_unavailable` | `symbol_not_allowed`), a human-readable `message` naming cap, limit and current value ("would exceed max position 0.5 BTC (current 0.4)" — the exact shape US-PROF-004 requires), and a machine-readable `cap`, `limit`, `actual` triple for the UI.
- **Reduce-only exemption**: reduce-only and position-closing commands are *always* permitted by cap checks (US-PROF-004: "reduce-only orders are still allowed"; US-ADMIN-003: "reduce-only actions remain available"). This is a first-class branch in the evaluator with its own tests.
- **Fail-closed**: if `RiskService` cannot produce a fresh state for an account (staleness beyond a configured `risk_state_max_age_seconds`, default 10 s), `evaluate` returns `allowed=False, code=risk_state_unavailable`.
- Metrics and structured logging as listed under Observability.

## Out of scope
- The `Validator` integration and API error mapping (E39-S01).
- Creating/releasing lockout rows and their side effects (E39-S02).
- Kill-switch state reads (E39-S03 provides the port; `evaluate` receives its result as an input).
- Any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Position notional cap
  Given resolved caps with max_position_notional_usd 25000 and state holding 20000
  When evaluate is called with a command adding 10000 of notional
  Then the decision is not allowed with code risk_limit_breached
  And the message names the cap, the limit 25000 and the current value 20000

Scenario: Reduce-only is never capped
  Given an account in lockout and at every cap simultaneously
  When evaluate is called with a reduce-only close command
  Then the decision is allowed

Scenario: Most restrictive cap wins
  Given a global policy cap of 1000, a profile cap of 800 and a per-manager override of 500
  When caps are resolved
  Then the effective max_daily_loss_usd is 500
  And the decision message attributes the breach to the manager override

Scenario (failure): Stale state fails closed
  Given the account's risk state is older than risk_state_max_age_seconds
  When evaluate is called with any opening command
  Then the decision is not allowed with code risk_state_unavailable

Scenario (edge): Day boundary rollover
  Given realised loss of -1400 recorded before the configured day boundary
  When the boundary passes
  Then the daily counter resets to 0 and a previously blocking daily-loss cap no longer blocks
```

## Technical notes / design
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RiskDecision:
    allowed: bool
    code: str | None
    message: str | None
    cap: str | None
    limit: Decimal | None
    actual: Decimal | None
    evaluated_at: datetime
```
The evaluator runs checks in a fixed order (symbol allow/block → kill-switch → lockout → orders-per-minute → open positions → position notional → concentration → leverage → daily loss → drawdown → consecutive losses) and returns on the **first** failure, so the message is deterministic and testable; the order is documented and asserted by a test so it cannot drift.

`RiskService` keeps counters in memory with a Postgres-backed rebuild on startup (replaying today's `executions` and current `positions`), so a restart mid-day cannot silently reset a daily-loss counter — a restart that cannot rebuild leaves accounts in `risk_state_unavailable` (fail-closed) rather than in a permissive zero state. This is a deliberate, tested behaviour.

Config keys (`cvapi.settings`): `risk.state_max_age_seconds` (default 10), `risk.eval_interval_seconds` (default 5, satisfying US-RULE-012's "at least every 5 s"), `risk.counter_rebuild_on_startup` (default true).

## Test plan
- **Unit (exhaustive decision table)**: one test per cap × {under, at, over} × {opening, reduce-only} — the evaluator is pure, so this is cheap and is the primary safety net. Includes cap-resolution precedence, check-order assertion, and message formatting.
- **Unit (clock)**: day-boundary arithmetic across DST-free UTC offsets, boundary exactly at an event timestamp, and a rollover mid-evaluation.
- **Unit (state)**: counter updates from a synthetic `oms.*` event sequence including partial fills, a reversal, and a late fee settlement; startup rebuild from a seeded DB; staleness detection.
- **Integration**: against recorded Bybit demo fixtures (partial fills and a rejection) asserting counters track `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` within the tolerance chosen by E39-K01.
- **Perf micro-benchmark**: `evaluate` p95 ≤1 ms in isolation (leaving headroom inside the ≤5 ms end-to-end budget), asserted in CI with a regression gate.
- Coverage target: **≥90 %** on `cvapi/oms/risk/` per the R3 local policy for security-relevant modules.

## Security notes
Threats from `04-security-program.md`: tampering (a client-supplied value influencing a cap) — the evaluator accepts caps only from the database, never from the request body; elevation of privilege (a manager's override loosening a cap) — resolution takes the most restrictive value, and a test asserts an override can never *widen* a cap, matching US-PROF-003's "overrides never widen a hard risk cap"; denial of service (an unbounded counter rebuild) — the rebuild is bounded to today's window with a query timeout. Data classification: financial state, no secrets. `security` label required; Security engineer review is a merge gate.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Budget: the full order-path risk check adds ≤5 ms p95 (US-PROF-004 / US-ADMIN-003 NFRs), inside budget #4 (order submit → ack p95 <300 ms on demo, a hard R3 gate per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2). The pure evaluator's own budget is ≤1 ms p95; state lookup is in-memory. No database read is permitted on the hot path except the cached lockout probe.

## Observability
- `cv_risk_eval_duration_seconds` histogram (labels: `cap_hit`, `outcome`).
- `cv_risk_rejections_total{code,cap,account}` counter.
- `cv_risk_cap_utilisation_ratio{account,cap}` gauge, refreshed on each evaluation cycle.
- `cv_risk_state_stale_accounts` gauge.
- `cv_risk_pnl_divergence_usd{account,source}` gauge (from the E39-K01 decision).
- Structured log per non-allowed decision with `request_id`, account, cap, limit, actual — never the order payload in full.
- OpenTelemetry span `risk.evaluate` nested under the OMS validate span.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Decision table tests complete and passing; check order asserted.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90 % on the package.
- [ ] Micro-benchmark recorded and gated in CI.
- [ ] `24-internal-schemas.md` documents `RiskDecision` and cap-resolution precedence.
- [ ] SAST/SCA clean; Security engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Architect review of the check ordering and fail-closed behaviour.
- [ ] Demo: before/after benchmark evidence documented (no user-visible behaviour yet).
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- `E39-T02` — tables and domain models.
- `E39-K01` — the daily-PnL source and day-boundary decision.
- `E39-X01` — the STRIDE model must exist before the enforcement code is written so its mitigations are designed in, not retrofitted.

## Branch
`feat/e39-risk-evaluator`. Split across 2 PRs (pure evaluator + service/state) each ≤400 LOC.

title: Postgres migrations and internal schemas for risk_lockouts, risk_policy and kill_switch_state
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` already carries the *inputs* to risk enforcement — the cap columns on `account_profiles` (§3.3: `max_position_notional_usd`, `max_daily_loss_usd`, `max_open_positions`, `max_orders_per_minute`) and the per-manager freeze columns on `user_account_access` (§3.1.3: `frozen`, `frozen_at`, `frozen_by`, `frozen_reason`, `max_daily_loss_usd`). It does **not** yet carry the *state* E39 produces: active lockouts with their reason and expiry, the global risk policy configured on SCR-134, and the kill-switch's own persisted state.

This is an interface-first Task per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10: the schema diff is drafted and reviewed before E39-T01 implements against it, because three other epics (E30 ticket headroom, E34 fan-out pre-validation, E42 admin screens) read these shapes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration adding:
  - **`risk_lockouts`** — `id uuid PK`, `exchange_account_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES exchange_accounts(id)`, `user_id uuid NULL REFERENCES users(id)` (for per-manager lockouts), `reason text NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('daily_loss','consecutive_losses','max_positions','manual'))` — matching the `RiskSummary.accounts[].lockout.reason` enum in `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `threshold numeric(38,18)`, `actual_value numeric(38,18)`, `since timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()`, `until timestamptz NULL` (NULL = until day boundary), `released_at timestamptz NULL`, `released_by uuid NULL REFERENCES users(id)`, `release_reason text NULL`, `actions_taken jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` (orders cancelled / positions flattened counts). Partial unique index guaranteeing at most one active lockout per (account, user) pair: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_risk_lockout_active ON risk_lockouts (exchange_account_id, coalesce(user_id,'00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid)) WHERE released_at IS NULL;`
  - **`risk_policy`** — the single global policy row set from SCR-134: `id uuid PK`, `singleton boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true UNIQUE CHECK (singleton)`, `max_total_notional_usd`, `max_daily_loss_usd`, `max_drawdown_pct`, `max_open_positions`, `max_leverage`, `max_orders_per_minute`, `per_symbol_concentration_pct`, `breach_behaviour jsonb NOT NULL` (per-limit `warn|block|flatten`), `lockout_minutes_default smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 60` (bounded 0..1440, matching `RiskCaps.lockout_minutes_after_breach`), `block_trading_when_degraded boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, `day_boundary_utc_offset_minutes smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `updated_by`, `updated_at`.
  - **`kill_switch_state`** — `scope text NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('global','accounts'))`, `exchange_account_id uuid NULL`, `engaged boolean NOT NULL`, `engaged_at`, `engaged_by`, `reason text`, `options jsonb` (the `SetKillSwitchRequest` option set), with a unique index on `(scope, coalesce(exchange_account_id, ...))` so global engagement is a single row.
- `CHECK` constraints mirroring the OpenAPI bounds exactly (`max_orders_per_minute` 1..600, `lockout_minutes_after_breach` 0..1440, `max_open_positions` 0..100) so the database refuses values the API would accept through a bug.
- Pydantic/dataclass models in `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/models.py` and a documented section added to `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` describing `RiskDecision`, `LockoutState` and `KillSwitchState` as domain objects.
- Down-migration, and a seed of the `risk_policy` singleton with conservative defaults (every limit set, `block_trading_when_degraded=true`).
- Update `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` with the new tables, the ERD edge additions, and their retention statement (risk state is retained indefinitely — it is part of the accountability trail alongside `audit_log`).

## Out of scope
- The evaluator logic (E39-T01) and any endpoint (E39-S01..S03).
- QuestDB/Parquet changes — risk state is relational only.
- Migrating existing data: R3 is pre-production; there is no legacy risk state.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and reverses cleanly
  Given a database at the previous head
  When the migration is applied and then downgraded
  Then both complete without error and the schema matches the before/after snapshots

Scenario: At most one active lockout per account
  Given an active lockout exists for account A with user_id NULL
  When a second unreleased lockout row for the same pair is inserted
  Then the insert is refused by the unique index

Scenario: Bounds are enforced at the database level
  Given an attempt to write max_orders_per_minute = 900
  Then the CHECK constraint rejects it, independent of API validation

Scenario (edge): Singleton risk policy
  Given the risk_policy row exists
  When a second row is inserted
  Then the unique singleton constraint refuses it
```

## Technical notes / design
Migration id `e39_risk_state`, placed after the E28 profile migration in the Alembic chain. Timestamps are `timestamptz`; money is `numeric(38,18)` to match the rest of the schema; percentages are `numeric(9,6)`. `actions_taken` and `breach_behaviour` are `jsonb` because their shape is owned by the API contract and must not require a migration per added action counter — but each key is documented in `24-internal-schemas.md`.

`day_boundary_utc_offset_minutes` exists because US-POS-009 requires "today" to use "the configured day boundary consistently with the daily-loss limit"; its default of 0 (UTC) matches `24-internal-schemas.md` §11 `sys.daily_loss_lockout`. E39-K01's decision may constrain the allowed range; if so, tighten the CHECK in this migration.

## Test plan
- Unit: model round-trip (`RiskDecision`, `LockoutState`, `KillSwitchState`) serialise/deserialise; bound validation mirrors the CHECKs.
- Migration test: apply on an empty DB and on a seeded DB, then downgrade, asserting schema equality with the snapshot (existing `tests/migrations/` harness).
- Constraint tests: one test per CHECK and per unique index asserting the exact `SQLSTATE`.
- Coverage: ≥90 % on `cvapi/oms/risk/models.py` (M17 local policy).

## Security notes
`risk_lockouts.release_reason` is user-supplied free text rendered in the audit log and SCR-071 — it must be stored raw and escaped at render, never interpolated into SQL (parameterised queries only) or into log format strings. No secrets in any new column. `kill_switch_state` is security-critical state: the migration grants no UPDATE/DELETE to any non-owner application role beyond the risk service's own role, consistent with the least-privilege model in `04-security-program.md`. `security` label applies (the Task adds tables on the OMS safety path).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Indexes: `ix_risk_lockouts_account_active` (partial, `WHERE released_at IS NULL`) so the hot-path lockout lookup is an index-only probe well inside the ≤5 ms evaluator budget; `kill_switch_state` is a ≤N-row table read through the 5 s cache, so it needs no special indexing beyond its unique key.

## Observability
Migration emits a `system_events` row on apply. The seeded policy write emits `risk_policy.updated` with actor `system` so the audit chain starts consistent.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Migration applies/reverses in CI; snapshot test green.
- [ ] Constraint tests cover every CHECK and unique index.
- [ ] `21-database-schema.md` and `24-internal-schemas.md` updated in the same PR.
- [ ] Schema diff reviewed by the Architect before implementation started (interface-first, §10).
- [ ] Coverage threshold met; SAST clean; Security engineer reviewed the grants.
- [ ] No demo required (internal schema change) — stated explicitly per DoD §4.2.

## Dependencies
- `E27` — `exchange_accounts`, `users`, `user_account_access` must exist.
- `E28` — `account_profiles` cap columns are the per-account counterpart to `risk_policy`.

## Branch
`feat/e39-risk-schema`. One PR, ~250 LOC including tests.

title: STRIDE threat model for risk caps, lockouts and the kill-switch
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` makes "threat model STRIDE per epic" a non-negotiable SDLC requirement, and `04-security-program.md` §5 states every STRIDE area "is re-reviewed when its epic enters design". The R3 security gate names E39 explicitly: "STRIDE for E27, E29, E34, E35, E39, E42 — all Critical/High closed" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4).

E39 is modelled **before** implementation (Sprint 14, ahead of E39-T01 in Sprint 15) so mitigations are designed in rather than retrofitted — hence E39-T01 is `blocked_by` this ticket.

The distinctive property of E39's threat surface is that it is a **safety control**, so the highest-value attack is not stealing data but *disabling or spoofing the control*: convincing the system (or the operator) that trading is blocked when it is not, or clearing a lockout that should hold.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE table appended to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5 as a new area ("Risk enforcement, lockouts and kill-switch"), one row per threat with columns `T`, STRIDE category, threat, likelihood, impact, risk, mitigations (referencing `SR-*` requirements), residual risk — matching the existing format exactly.
- Threats to enumerate at minimum:
  - **Spoofing**: a forged `system` WS frame convincing a client the kill-switch is engaged/released; a replayed kill-switch REST call.
  - **Tampering**: client-supplied caps in an order body; direct DB modification of `kill_switch_state` or `risk_lockouts`; a feature-flag toggle used to disable risk enforcement (relates to existing threat **D2**).
  - **Repudiation**: a freeze or override without an audit row; an audit row whose actor is ambiguous; hash-chain gaps around risk events.
  - **Information disclosure**: `/risk/summary` leaking out-of-scope account figures to a manager; error messages revealing another account's existence or balance through cap-breach detail strings.
  - **Denial of service**: a malicious or careless manager freezing accounts to strand a trader; an unbounded counter rebuild on startup; an evaluation loop starved under load leaving accounts in `risk_state_unavailable` (fail-closed refusal is correct but is still a DoS if it can be induced).
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a manager engaging a global freeze or releasing one; self-override of one's own lockout; using the override endpoint's idempotency key to replay a prior owner override.
- New or referenced `SR-*` requirements for any mitigation not already covered — in particular the fail-closed posture, the "override never widens a cap" rule, and the one-audit-row-per-affected-entity requirement.
- Abuse-case list handed to E39-X02 for execution, and a set of security-relevant test requirements handed to E39-Q02/Q03.
- Data-classification statement for every new table from E39-T02.

## Out of scope
- Executing the abuse cases (E39-X02).
- SAST/DAST rule authoring (E39-X02).
- Pen-testing (E43, pre-R4).
- Threat modelling of the order paths themselves (E29) or the key vault (E27); E39 references their models rather than duplicating them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model covers every STRIDE category
  Given the threat table is submitted
  Then each of the six STRIDE categories has at least one threat row for this epic
  And every row has a mitigation referencing a concrete SR requirement or a named E39 ticket

Scenario: Mitigations are actionable before implementation
  Given the model is completed in Sprint 14
  When E39-T01 begins in Sprint 15
  Then every Critical/High mitigation is expressed as a specific, implementable requirement on a named E39 ticket
  And no mitigation is phrased as a generic aspiration

Scenario (failure): An unmitigated Critical
  Given a threat rated Critical with no adequate mitigation
  Then the epic cannot pass the R3 security gate
  And an explicit accepted-risk sign-off from the Owner is required and recorded, or the design changes
```

## Technical notes / design
The model is built from the existing architecture artefacts rather than from scratch: the order-path sequence (`20-architecture.md` §9), the RBAC matrix (`24-internal-schemas.md` §12), the WS authorisation rules (`23-ws-protocol.md` §10) and the new tables (E39-T02). Each trust boundary crossing is enumerated first, then threats per boundary — the boundaries being client↔API, API↔risk service, risk service↔Postgres, and API↔exchange.

Likelihood/impact use the existing L/M/H scale and the Low/Medium/High/Critical risk scale from §5 so the new rows are comparable with the existing areas.

## Test plan
Not a code deliverable. Validation: a review session with the Architect and the epic owner walking each threat; every mitigation must map to a test that E39-Q02, E39-Q03 or E39-X02 will execute — a mitigation with no test is not accepted.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security deliverable. It is authored by the Security engineer with the Architect, and its output gates E39-T01. Classification: the document is internal; it names attack paths and must not be published outside the repository.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — documentation.

## Performance notes
The model must account for the ≤5 ms budget as a *security* constraint: a mitigation that cannot be afforded on the hot path (e.g. a synchronous audit write before admission) must be designed asynchronously without weakening the guarantee, and that trade-off is recorded explicitly rather than silently made during implementation.

## Observability
The model names the detections required for each threat (e.g. an alert on any `risk.lockout_overridden`; a metric for refused out-of-scope `/risk/summary` calls; audit-chain verification covering risk events), which become the observability requirements on the implementing tickets.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] STRIDE table merged into `04-security-program.md` §5.
- [ ] Every row has a mitigation mapped to a ticket and a test.
- [ ] Any Critical/High without a mitigation has a recorded design change or an Owner-signed accepted risk.
- [ ] Abuse-case list handed to E39-X02.
- [ ] Reviewed by the Architect and the epic owner.
- [ ] Findings presented at the Security Review.

## Dependencies

- Blocks `E39-T01` (deliberately: mitigations precede implementation).

title: Spike: alert evaluation placement, subscription sharing and storm thresholds
body:
## Context
Alerts must be evaluated server-side so they fire with the client closed (US-ALRT-001 NFR), and must reuse "the same metric catalogue and evaluation engine as the rule engine" (US-ALRT-002 NFR) with "one event bus; no duplicate evaluation" (US-ALRT-003 NFR). Those three constraints leave a real design question open: does M22 run alerts as degenerate rules inside E35's evaluator, or as a separate lightweight evaluator subscribing to the same metric bus?

Getting this wrong is expensive in both directions. Folding alerts into the rule evaluator drags per-rule sandboxing, execution-time budgets and arming semantics onto something that only ever sends a notification. Running a second evaluator risks the duplicate-evaluation the NFR forbids and a slow drift in metric semantics. This spike answers it with measurements before E40-T02/T03 are written.

Timebox: **3 days**, agreed with the Architect. Not expected to produce production code.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Q1** — Placement: prototype both options against E35's `MetricRegistry` and evaluator interfaces (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11) and measure, at 500 armed alerts across 20 symbols under a recorded high-rate window from E16/E26: p50/p95/p99 condition-met → `alert_deliveries` row committed; CPU and RSS delta; number of metric subscriptions created.
- **Q2** — Subscription sharing: does keying subscriptions on `alerts.condition_hash` (already in the schema) collapse duplicate work as expected? Measure the subscription count for a corpus where 100 alerts share 12 distinct conditions.
- **Q3** — Storm thresholds: replay a detector-heavy window (E25 stacked-imbalance events) and measure the natural firing rate distribution, validating or correcting the threshold ratified in E40-D01 (">N deliveries per user per 60 s"), plus the aggregation-window choice.
- **Q4** — `once_per_bar` semantics: confirm the bar-open key can be derived deterministically from the trigger's `timeframe` for every supported timeframe, including when a bar is revised by a late tick.
- **Q5** — Cost of the notify-only IR guard: measure the validation overhead of rejecting action-bearing IR at `POST /api/v1/alerts` against the ≤300 ms budget in SCR-091.
- **Deliverable**: `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0019-alert-evaluation-placement.md` recording the decision with the numbers, plus follow-up notes attached to E40-T02/T03.

## Out of scope
Implementing the chosen design (E40-T03). Delivery-channel transport (E40-T04). Webhook egress (E40-S03).

## Decision criteria (stated up front)
- If the shared-evaluator option adds >15% p99 latency to E35's rule evaluation under the 500-alert load, alerts get their own evaluator subscribing to the same bus.
- If the separate evaluator cannot demonstrably reuse E35's metric registry without duplicating computation (Q2 subscription count > distinct condition hashes), the shared option wins regardless of latency, because the NFR is a correctness constraint, not a performance preference.
- If neither option meets the 1 s condition-to-record budget at 500 alerts, the spike escalates a capacity decision to the Architect rather than picking the least-bad option.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both options are measured, not argued
  Then Q1's table reports p50/p95/p99, CPU, RSS and subscription counts for both prototypes under the identical recorded window
Scenario: The decision follows the stated criteria
  Then the ADR names which criterion decided it and shows the number that triggered it
Scenario: Storm threshold is validated against real data (edge)
  Given the detector-heavy replay window
  Then the measured firing-rate distribution either confirms the E40-D01 threshold or the ADR proposes a corrected one with the histogram attached
Scenario: An inconclusive result is recorded as such (failure)
  Given neither option meets the latency budget
  Then the ADR records "defer, need capacity decision" with the evidence, and a follow-up ticket is filed, rather than a decision being asserted without support
```

## Technical notes / design
Prototype on a branch off E35's merged evaluator. Drive load from recorded Parquet windows via the E26 replay harness so runs are reproducible; state the exact window (symbol, date range) in the ADR so the numbers can be re-derived. Measure with the same Prometheus histograms E40-T03 will ship, not with ad hoc timers.

## Test plan
Benchmark harness only, checked in under `benchmarks/alerts/` even though the prototype code is throwaway — the harness is reused by E40-Q02.

## Security notes
The prototype must not reach any external network; webhook egress is explicitly excluded so the spike cannot accidentally establish an SSRF-shaped code path that gets promoted later.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend spike.

## Performance notes
Budgets under test: condition met → in-app record ≤1 s (US-ALRT-001); condition met → visible toast ≤2 s (SCR-092); validation round-trip ≤300 ms (SCR-091).

## Observability
Defines the metric names E40-T03/T04 will ship: `cv_alert_eval_latency_seconds`, `cv_alerts_armed`, `cv_alert_subscriptions`, `cv_alert_suppressed_total{reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Q1–Q5 answered with recorded evidence.
- [ ] `ADR-0019-alert-evaluation-placement.md` merged (a "defer" outcome is still an ADR).
- [ ] Follow-up notes attached to E40-T02/E40-T03; storm threshold confirmed or corrected in E40-D01's deliverable.
- [ ] Benchmark harness merged under `benchmarks/alerts/`.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated for R11 if the spike changes the risk picture.
- [ ] Prototype branch archived, not merged.

## Dependencies
`E35` — needs the merged IR, metric registry and evaluator. Informs `E40-T02`, `E40-T03`, `E40-Q02`.

## Branch
`spike/e40-alert-evaluation-placement` (unmerged; only the ADR and harness land on `main`).

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-014, SCR-015, SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-115

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md (alert evaluator machine, E40-T03)
2. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014, SCR-115

**Interfaces you must not break**

title: Land the 0009_alerts migration, repositories and alert outbox topics
body:
## Context
Everything else in E40 sits on two tables that are already fully specified in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.5 and listed in the migration register as `0009_alerts` (§ migrations table: `alerts`, `alert_deliveries`, `outbox`). This task lands them exactly as specified — no schema invention — plus the repository layer and the two outbox topics E40 uses.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration `0009_alerts` creating, verbatim from §3.5:
  - enums `alert_channel` (`in_app`,`email`,`webhook`,`push`,`desktop`) and `alert_trigger_mode` (`once`,`every_time`,`once_per_bar`) if not already created by an earlier migration;
  - table `alerts` with all columns and the constraints `al_cooldown` (0..86400), `al_channels` (1..5), `al_webhook` (webhook channel implies `webhook_url_enc IS NOT NULL`), and indexes `ux_alerts_name`, `ix_alerts_live`, `ix_alerts_snooze`, `ix_alerts_expiry`;
  - table `alert_deliveries` with `ad_attempt` (0..10), indexes `ix_ad_alert_time`, `ix_ad_pending`, `ix_ad_user_unack`, and the `trg_ad_append` BEFORE DELETE trigger calling `forbid_mutation()` — **append-only**: UPDATE is allowed for `queued→sent→acked` transitions, DELETE is not, except for the retention job running as `cv_owner` which the trigger exempts via `session_user`.
- `outbox` topics registered for E40: `alert.deliver` and `webhook.post` (the table itself already exists from §3.10.4; this task only registers the topic constants and their `dedup_key` construction rules).
- Repositories in `apps/api/cv/alerts/repo.py`: `AlertRepository` (create/get/list-paginated-by-cursor/update-with-optimistic-concurrency/soft-delete/set-enabled/set-snooze/bump-fire-counters) and `AlertDeliveryRepository` (insert, mark sent/failed/suppressed, ack one, ack all, list by cursor with `status`/`alert_id`/`unacked_only`/`from`/`to` filters, unacked count).
- Retention wiring: `alert_deliveries` retention per `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §retention (180 d hot / 24 mo warm / 24 mo cold / `archive_parquet`) registered with the existing retention job.
- Down-migration that drops cleanly on an empty database and refuses on a populated one with a clear error.

## Out of scope
The compiler and API (E40-T02), the evaluator (E40-T03), the dispatcher (E40-T04). The `rules` tables (E35-T02). Column-level encryption of `webhook_url_enc`/`webhook_secret_enc` — the columns are created here but only written by E40-S03 via the E27 credential broker.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration matches the specification exactly
  When the migration is applied to a clean database and the resulting DDL is diffed against 21-database-schema.md section 3.5
  Then there is no difference in columns, types, defaults, constraints, indexes or triggers
Scenario: Delivery history cannot be deleted by the application role
  Given a delivery row and a session as the application role
  When a DELETE is attempted
  Then the trg_ad_append trigger raises and the row survives
Scenario: The retention job can still purge (edge)
  Given the retention job connected as cv_owner
  When it purges deliveries older than the retained window
  Then the deletes succeed because the trigger exempts session_user = cv_owner
Scenario: Constraints reject bad data (failure)
  When an alert is inserted with cooldown_seconds = 90000, or with six channels, or with channel 'webhook' and a NULL webhook_url_enc
  Then each insert fails on al_cooldown, al_channels and al_webhook respectively
```

## Technical notes / design
`dedup_key` construction — `alert.deliver`: `f"{delivery_id}"` (one outbox row per delivery row, so replay is naturally idempotent). `webhook.post`: `f"{alert_id}:{fired_at_ms}:{attempt_group}"`. The unique index `ux_outbox_dedup (topic, dedup_key)` is what makes the transactional outbox exactly-once from the producer side.

Cursor pagination uses the existing keyset helper (opaque base64 of `(queued_at, id)`), not OFFSET, because `alert_deliveries` grows without bound between retention runs.

Optimistic concurrency on `alerts` uses `updated_at` as the ETag source so `PUT /alerts/{alertId}` can honour `If-Match` and return 412 (see E40-T02).

## Test plan
- Unit: every constraint (`al_cooldown`, `al_channels`, `al_webhook`, `ad_attempt`) proven by a rejected insert; `ux_alerts_name` case-insensitivity and its `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` partiality (a soft-deleted alert frees its name); repository CRUD; cursor pagination stability across concurrent inserts.
- Integration: migration up/down on a seeded database; the append-only trigger under both the app role and `cv_owner`; retention purge.
- Contract: none (no API surface here).
- Coverage target ≥85% on `cv.alerts.repo`.

## Security notes
`alerts.webhook_url_enc` and `alerts.webhook_secret_enc` are **SECRET** data classification; the repository must never select them into a DTO that reaches the API layer — enforce with an explicit column allow-list in the read path, and a unit test asserting the serialised alert DTO contains neither field. `alert_deliveries` is the audit-grade record of what was told to whom; its append-only property is a security control, not a convenience.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend.

## Performance notes
`ix_alerts_live ON alerts (symbol) WHERE enabled AND deleted_at IS NULL` is the index the evaluator's warm-up query uses; assert with `EXPLAIN` in a test that the armed-alert load query uses it and not a sequential scan. The unacked-count query must hit `ix_ad_user_unack`.

## Observability
Expose `cv_alerts_total{enabled}` and `cv_alert_deliveries_pending` as gauges sourced from these tables for the E04 Grafana board.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Migration applies and rolls back cleanly; DDL diff against §3.5 is empty.
- [ ] Repositories implemented with the SECRET-column allow-list and its test.
- [ ] Retention registered; append-only behaviour proven for both roles.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85%; CI green.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code owner.

## Dependencies
`E35-T02` created the `rules`/`rule_versions` tables and the shared enum conventions; `0009_alerts` follows it in the migration order.

`feat/e40-alerts-schema`. PR ~250 LOC.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi for **CMP-087 AdminLayout** including the `color.surface.admin-tint` treatment and the re-auth countdown, **SCR-149** gate, **SCR-120** overview, **SCR-121** users list, **SCR-122** user detail, **SCR-123** invite, **SCR-124** view-as, **SCR-154** permission denied.
- **Design-system contributions**: specification updates for CMP-087 (AdminLayout), CMP-088 (PageHeader in the admin context), CMP-173 (AuditRow, as used in SCR-120's recent-activity tile), CMP-178 (SystemHealthTile) and CMP-138 (RiskCapMeter in the user-detail limits context) — each contributed to `15-component-catalogue.md` with tier, props, a11y contract, tokens and the Storybook variant list, not designed ad hoc for this screen.
- All states per the catalogue: SCR-120's per-tile loading/error/degraded; SCR-121's loading/populated/filtered-to-nothing/error; SCR-122's dirty/change-summary/saving/conflict/self-edit-guard; SCR-123's invite-shown-once; SCR-124's persistent impersonation banner with every control disabled.

- Greyscale proofs for the admin tint and every status treatment.

- Data-shape annotations reference the actual schema field names (`AdminOverview`, `User`, `AccountAccessGrant`), preventing a design that implies data the API does not return.

## Security notes
- No screen may render a secret: the invite link is shown once with an explicit statement, and API-key material never appears in these screens at all.

- Focus order, focus-visible treatment and keyboard paths annotated for every interactive frame.
- Status and role rendered as text; the greyscale proof accompanies each status treatment.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-135/136 audit, SCR-145 flags, SCR-148 maintenance, motion spec
body:
## Context
The audit browser and the flag console are the two admin screens where a design mistake has security consequences rather than usability ones.

For the audit log, `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-135 requires that "no edit or delete affordance exists anywhere", that the append-only guarantee is stated on screen, and that the **integrity-failure state** is designed as a security incident ("Audit chain verification failed at 2026-09-10 — contact security"), not as a retryable UI error. A designer who draws a friendly "Retry" button on that state has created a misleading affordance.

For the flag console, SCR-145 requires risky flags to be "grouped, marked and step-up-gated", `trading.live_enabled` to be drawn **blocked with its reason**, and every toggle to be confirmed as emitting an audit event with before/after.

This ticket also owns the epic's **motion specification** in one place, so eight screens do not each invent their own transitions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi for **SCR-135** audit log (columns, filters, integrity indicator, high-severity rows distinguishable without colour, export, empty/filtered-to-nothing, retention statement), **SCR-136** audit event detail drawer (full field set, before/after diff rendering, correlated events, links to related objects, raw record with copy, "cannot be edited or deleted" statement), **SCR-145** feature flags, **SCR-148** maintenance mode.
- The **integrity-failure state** designed explicitly as an incident state: what it says, what it offers (contact security, view the break position), and what it deliberately does *not* offer (a retry that implies transience).
- The **before/after diff** visual language, including how a redacted/secret-bearing value renders (fingerprint only) — reused by SCR-136, SCR-122's change summary and SCR-145's flag history.
- **Design-system contributions**: CMP-173 AuditRow, CMP-174 AuditFilterBar, CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow, CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip, CMP-099 PrintExportBar in the audit context — contributed to `15-component-catalogue.md`.
- **Epic motion specification**: drawer open/close, row expansion, dialog entry, the re-auth gate overlay, tile state transitions (ok → stale → error), toast/banner entry. title: Spike: audit query plan and index strategy at 10 million rows
body:
## Context
US-ADMIN-009 sets a hard NFR — "search over 10 million entries returns the first page in ≤2 s" — and SCR-135 tightens it for the common case to a ≤400 ms filter round-trip. The existing indexes (`ix_audit_time`, `ix_audit_actor`, `ix_audit_action`, `ix_audit_object`, partial `ix_audit_sev`) were designed for the write path and single-column lookups; the UI offers **combinations** (actor + action + severity + range, plus full-text `q` over JSONB), and a combination that falls back to a bitmap heap scan over 10 M rows will not meet the budget.

Committing to an index set is a schema decision with a real migration cost (a GIN index over JSONB on 10 M rows is not free to build), so it is resolved by measurement before E42-T02 implements, rather than discovered during it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Generate a realistic 10 M-row `audit_log` dataset with the production action distribution (order actions dominating, auth events next, admin actions rare) and realistic `before_state`/`after_state` payload sizes; commit the generator.
- Measure `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for each filter combination the SCR-135 filter bar offers (≈12 combinations), at page 1 and at deep cursor positions.
- Compare candidate index strategies: (a) existing single-column set, (b) composite `(action, event_ts DESC)` / `(actor_user_id, action, event_ts DESC)`, (c) BRIN on `event_ts` given the append-only insert order, (d) GIN over the tsvector of the detail payload for `q`, (e) a partial index for the high-severity view.
- Measure the **build cost and ongoing write overhead** of each candidate — the audit write path is on every state-changing request, so index write amplification is a production concern, not a detail.
- Decide, and record the decision plus the numbers as **ADR-0021 Audit query and index strategy** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the endpoints (E42-T02 consumes this spike's conclusion).
- Partitioning the audit table — explicitly evaluated as a question but out of scope to implement here; if the spike concludes partitioning is required, it becomes a follow-up Task.
- Changing the hash-chain design (out of bounds; the chain is a security invariant).

## Acceptance criteria
- **Timebox**: 3 days. If the budget cannot be met by indexing alone, the decision criterion is pre-agreed: recommend monthly range partitioning on `event_ts` as a follow-up Task rather than extending the spike.
- Question 1: which index set meets ≤400 ms p95 for the common filter combinations and ≤2 s for the worst (full-text over a wide range)? Answered with numbers per combination.
- Question 2: what is the write-path overhead (ms per INSERT, p50/p99) of the recommended set versus today's? Answered with a measured benchmark at the production write rate.
- Question 3: what does the GIN index cost to build on 10 M rows, and can it be built `CONCURRENTLY` inside the deployment window?
- Deliverables: benchmark script + dataset generator committed; results table; **ADR-0021** recorded with the decision (including "defer" as a valid, recorded outcome); follow-up tickets filed; `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.
- Explicitly **not** expected to produce production-shippable code beyond the benchmark harness and the migration draft.

## Technical notes / design
- Benchmark harness: `pytest-benchmark` plus raw `psql` timings to avoid driver overhead masking plan differences; run on the reference machine described in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` with a cold and a warm buffer cache.
- Keyset pagination is assumed (OFFSET is already ruled out); deep-cursor measurements use a cursor at the 9 M-th row.
- Write overhead measured by inserting 100k rows with and without each candidate index, reporting p50/p99 per insert including the chain trigger's advisory lock.
- The canonical hash-chain trigger must remain untouched; index changes must not alter insert ordering semantics.

## Test plan
- The spike's output *is* measurement; the harness itself carries a smoke test so the numbers are reproducible by a reviewer.
- A reviewer must be able to re-run `make audit-bench` and obtain the same ranking (absolute numbers may vary by machine; the ranking must not).

## Security notes
- The generated dataset must contain **synthetic** data only — no production payloads, no real emails or IPs; the generator is reviewed for this explicitly.
- Any index over `before_state`/`after_state` must not create a new disclosure path (indexes are not readable by the app role beyond the existing table grants).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — spike, no UI.

## Performance notes
This spike exists to establish the performance facts; budgets under test are ≤400 ms common-case filter round-trip and ≤2 s worst case (US-ADMIN-009, SCR-135).

## Observability
Findings feed `cv_audit_query_duration_seconds{filter_class}` bucket boundaries chosen in E42-T02, so the dashboards are calibrated to the measured distribution rather than to guesses.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Questions answered with recorded evidence (benchmark numbers, results table, plan excerpts).
- [ ] **ADR-0021** written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` recording the decision, including a "defer with reason" outcome if that is the conclusion.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for the chosen path with the findings linked.
- [ ] Spike code promoted (benchmark harness + dataset generator) or explicitly marked throwaway.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced or one was retired.

## Dependencies
- None. Runs against a seeded database using the schema already defined in `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1; deliberately unblocked so it can precede E42-T02.

## Branch
`spike/admin-audit-index-strategy` — throwaway branch; only the harness and the ADR merge.

title: Implement audit query, hash-chain verify and signed export endpoints
body:
## Context
US-ADMIN-009 requires search over **10 million entries** returning the first page in ≤2 s, manager scoping enforced server-side, and a **signed** export that is itself audited with redaction preserved. US-ADMIN-008 requires an integrity check that "verifies the hash chain over entries and reports any break with its position".

The table, the chain trigger, the append-only grants and the checkpoint table already exist in `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1, and the writer ships with E09. What is missing — and what this task delivers — is the **read side**: `GET /admin/audit`, `POST /admin/audit/verify`, `POST /admin/audit/export` and the job plumbing behind `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`, all declared in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.

The indexes matter more than the handlers: `ix_audit_time`, `ix_audit_actor`, `ix_audit_action`, `ix_audit_object` and the partial `ix_audit_sev` exist, but the filter combinations the UI offers must be proven against a 10 M-row dataset rather than assumed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /api/v1/admin/audit` with cursor pagination (keyset on `id`, never OFFSET), filters `actor_user_id`, `action[]`, `subject_type`, `subject_id`, `outcome`, `severity`, `ip`, `from`, `to`, full-text `q` over the detail payload; returns `items`, `chain_verified` for the returned slice, and `meta.next_cursor`. Permission `audit:read`.
- **Manager scoping**: when the caller is not owner/viewer-with-`audit:read`-global, the query is narrowed server-side to `actor_user_id = caller` — implemented in the repository layer so no handler can forget it, and asserted by a test that calls the repository directly.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/verify {from_id, to_id}` → `{verified, entries_checked, first_bad_id, checked_at}`; recomputes the chain in batches with a bounded memory footprint and reports the **first** divergence.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/export {from, to, compress}` → `202 {job_id}`: an async job writing NDJSON plus a **detached Ed25519 signature** over the file digest (signing key held outside the database, per `audit_checkpoints.signed_by` convention); redaction applied at write time is preserved — the exporter never re-hydrates redacted fields.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}` job status for export (and reused by recorder/backup jobs).
- Full-text search support: a GIN index on the detail payload sufficient for the `q` filter, added by an Alembic migration with a documented build cost.
- Export rate limiting and a maximum range, so export cannot be used as a data-exfiltration or DoS primitive.
- Audit of the read side itself: `audit.viewed`, `audit.exported`.

## Out of scope
- The audit **writer**, the `audit_chain()` trigger, append-only grants and the nightly `cv-audit-verify` job (E09 + schema).
- Off-box checkpoint storage verification (E43-T10).
- The browser UI (E42-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: First page over 10 million entries
  Given the audit_log table holds 10 million rows
  When the first page is requested with a 30-day range and an action filter
  Then the response returns within 2 seconds p95 with 200 items and a next cursor

Scenario: Stable ordering while new rows append
  Given new entries are being written during pagination
  When I page forward using the cursor
  Then no entry is skipped or duplicated across pages

Scenario: Chain verification reports the break position
  Given a row's entry_hash is corrupted in a test fixture database
  When verify is called over the containing range
  Then verified is false and first_bad_id equals the corrupted row's id

Scenario: Manager scoping is enforced in the repository
  Given a manager calls the audit query with actor_user_id set to another user
  Then only their own entries are returned
  And the attempt is recorded

Scenario: Export is signed and audited
  When an export job completes
  Then an NDJSON file and a detached signature are produced
  And the signature verifies against the published public key
  And an audit.exported entry records the range, row count and actor

Scenario (failure): Export range too large
  Given a requested range exceeding the configured maximum
  Then the call returns 422 validation_failed naming the limit
  And no job is created

Scenario (edge): No rows match
  Then the response is 200 with an empty items array, chain_verified true and no cursor
```

## Technical notes / design
- Keyset pagination: `WHERE (id < :cursor_id) AND <filters> ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT :limit`, cursor = base64 of `{"id": <int>}` (matching the example cursor in the OpenAPI document). OFFSET is forbidden — it would both drift as rows append and degrade at depth.
- Query planning: every supported filter combination is covered by an existing or newly added index; the task ships an `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` report for each of the UI's offered combinations against the 10 M-row dataset, committed under `docs/perf/`.
- `q` full-text: `GIN` on `to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(before_state::text,'') || coalesce(after_state::text,''))` plus `object_label`; documented as the only non-trivial index build in the migration.
- Verify batches 10k rows at a time, recomputing the digest with the same canonical serialisation as the trigger; a mismatch between the app-side and trigger-side canonicalisation is itself a bug — a test pins the canonical form byte-for-byte.
- Export job: streams rows with a server-side cursor, writes gzip NDJSON to the job store, computes SHA-256, signs with Ed25519 (key from the KEK-protected store, never in the database), and publishes `result.download_url` with a short-lived signed URL.
- Error codes: `forbidden`, `validation_failed`, `rate_limited`, `not_found` (unknown job).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: cursor encode/decode; filter→SQL mapping incl. repeated `action` params; scoping applied in the repository (called directly, bypassing the handler); canonical-serialisation equality with the trigger; export row redaction preserved.
- **Contract**: schemathesis over `/admin/audit`, `/admin/audit/verify`, `/admin/audit/export`, `/admin/jobs/{jobId}`.
- **Integration**: 10 M-row seeded database (generator committed, seeding documented) — latency assertions for the first page and for each offered filter combination; pagination stability under concurrent writes.
- **Security**: attempt UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_log` as `cv_app` → must fail on grants **and** on the `forbid_mutation` trigger; corrupted-chain fixture; export range-limit and rate-limit tests.
- **Perf**: k6 profile from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` for the query endpoint.
- Coverage ≥90% on the audit read module (security-relevant module, per the R4 coverage rule).

## Security notes
- Threats: **repudiation** (the endpoint must never expose a write path — the router declares only GET/POST-verify/POST-export and the database grants deny mutation regardless); **information disclosure** (manager scoping in the repository layer; export contains Confidential + PII data, so it is signed, rate-limited, range-limited and audited); **tampering** (chain verification is the detection control; a break is a `critical` system event, not a 500).
- The signing key lives outside the database (per `audit_checkpoints` convention and ADR-0009); the service holds only the private key handle, and key rotation is documented.
- Data classification: Confidential + PII (`actor_ip`). Requires `security` label and Security-engineer review.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- First page ≤2 s p95 over 10 M rows (US-ADMIN-009 NFR); the realistic target from SCR-135 is ≤400 ms for a filter round-trip, which the index work must achieve for the common filters.
- Verify processes ≥100k rows/s in batches without exceeding 256 MB RSS.
- Export streams; peak memory is bounded by the batch size, independent of range length.

## Observability
- Audit: `audit.viewed {filters}`, `audit.exported {from,to,rowCount}`, `audit.integrity_check_run {verified, firstBadId}`.
- Metrics: `cv_audit_query_duration_seconds{filter_class}`, `cv_audit_export_duration_seconds`, `cv_audit_chain_verified` gauge, `cv_audit_export_rejected_total{reason}`.
- Alerting (ADR-0014): `cv_audit_chain_verified == 0` pages immediately — a chain break is a security incident.
