title: Show per-account balance, margin and connection state and control leverage and margin mode
body:
## Context
Covers **US-ACCT-008** (account balance and margin snapshot, Must), **US-ACCT-009** (leverage and margin mode control, Must) and the trading-side rendering of **US-ACCT-010** (account health), through **SCR-079 Account detail drawer (trading-side)** - the surface a trader opens from the account picker or the positions grid.

Two rules dominate. US-ACCT-008's NFR: WS-first with a periodic REST truth-check, and **never show a number without a freshness indicator**; when reconciliation also fails the figures grey out with a "stale since <time>" badge and risk-based sizing is disabled for that account. US-ACCT-009: leverage and margin-mode changes are applied through Bybit and reflected in the snapshot; an open position that blocks the change surfaces the exact exchange reason and restores the previous UI value; and a request exceeding the account profile's leverage cap is refused **client- and server-side before any exchange call**.

SCR-079 adds that no secret material is ever rendered here and that key identifiers are shown truncated.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-079** drawer opened from the account picker (CMP-105) and the positions grid: equity, wallet balance, available balance, used margin, unrealised PnL, margin mode, position mode, leverage, today's realised PnL, fees paid, funding paid and received, a profile-limits summary, key status (valid / expiring / restricted) and, for owners, quick links into SCR-125 and SCR-131.
- Freshness indicator on every figure, sourced from the E27-T04 wallet snapshot: `updated_at`, the `balance_stale` flag at the 10 s threshold, and the `stale_since` badge when both the stream and the REST reconciliation have failed.
- Health banner states from SCR-079: healthy, key expiring soon, key invalid ("This account's API key was rejected - trading disabled for it") and IP-whitelist mismatch with explicit remediation text.
- Leverage control (CMP-104 LeverageSlider) wired to `PATCH /positions/{positionId}/leverage` (`setPositionLeverage`, `positions:write`, scope `granted_accounts`), with risk-limit tiers from the instrument data shown alongside the choice (US-ACCT-009 NFR).
- Margin-mode and position-mode controls (CMP-128 MarginModeToggle, CMP-129 PositionModeToggle) wired to `PATCH /exchange-accounts/{accountId}` (`updateExchangeAccount`, which the OpenAPI defines as updating label, enabled flag, active profile and position/margin mode).
- Profile-cap enforcement: a requested leverage above the account profile's cap is refused in the client **and** by the server before any exchange call, with the message "Your profile caps leverage at 10x" (the exact copy used by SCR-060).
- Blocked-by-open-position handling: the exact exchange reason is surfaced and the previous value is restored in the UI.
- `GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate` (`getFeeRate`) rendered in the fees row.
- Subscription to the WS `wallet` topic scoped to the account, per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS13 (500 ms throttle, snapshot plus whole-object last-write-wins).
- Components: CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-104, CMP-106 ProfileBadge, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-128, CMP-129, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge.

## Out of scope
The order ticket and its sizing logic (E30); per-account profile CRUD, which owns the caps this screen enforces (E28); positions and orders blotters (E29); paper-balance reset (E38); risk caps and lockouts (E39).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Snapshot displayed with freshness
  Given an account is verified and connected
  When the drawer opens
  Then equity, available balance, used margin, margin mode and position mode are shown, each with a freshness timestamp, and no figure is rendered without one

Scenario: Reconciliation after silence
  Given the wallet stream has been silent for 60 seconds
  When reconciliation runs
  Then a REST wallet-balance call updates the figures and the freshness timestamp

Scenario: Stale data disables risk-based sizing
  Given the stream is silent and reconciliation has also failed
  When the drawer renders
  Then the figures are greyed with a "stale since <time>" badge and risk-based sizing is reported as unavailable for that account

Scenario: Set leverage
  Given I choose 10x for BTCUSDT on account A and the profile permits it
  When I apply
  Then the change is sent to Bybit and the new value is reflected in the account snapshot

Scenario: Blocked by an open position
  Given an open position prevents the leverage change
  When the exchange rejects it
  Then the exact exchange reason is displayed and the previous value is restored in the UI

Scenario: Exceeds the profile cap
  Given the account profile caps leverage at 10x
  When I request 20x
  Then the request is refused in the client and, if forced, by the server, in both cases before any exchange call is made

Scenario: Key invalid banner
  Given the account's key has been rejected
  When the drawer opens
  Then the banner reads "This account's API key was rejected - trading disabled for it" and trading controls in the drawer are disabled

Scenario: No secret is rendered
  When every field of the drawer is inspected, including the key status row
  Then no secret material appears and the key identifier is shown truncated
```

## Technical notes / design
Freshness is a first-class field, not a decoration: the view model pairs every numeric with `{value, updated_at, stale}` so that it is structurally impossible to render a number without its freshness. A lint rule or a typed wrapper (`Fresh<T>`) is the mechanism; a bare number in the template fails review.

Profile caps are read from the account profile (E28). Until E28 lands, the client reads the cap from the account payload's profile summary and the server enforces from the same source - the enforcement point is the server, and the client check exists only to give a fast, clear message.

Leverage changes are per-symbol (US-ACCT-009 speaks of "per-symbol leverage"), so the control is bound to the drawer's current symbol context and states which symbol it will affect.

The drawer opens from cached state in <=100 ms and refreshes in place (SCR-079 performance note), so it must not block on a network call to render.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): freshness rendering, including the greyed-and-stale state; cap refusal; previous-value restoration after an exchange rejection; the `Fresh<T>` wrapper preventing a bare render.
Unit (backend): server-side cap enforcement before any adapter call, asserted by a test that fails if an exchange call is made.
Contract: `setPositionLeverage`, `updateExchangeAccount`, `getFeeRate`, and the `wallet` WS payload.
Integration: against recorded Bybit fixtures for a leverage change blocked by an open position, and for a successful change.
E2E (E27-Q02): open the drawer on demo, change leverage within the cap, then attempt to exceed it.
A11y: axe-core; manual screen-reader pass on the description list and the toggles.
Coverage >=90% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: **Information disclosure** - balances, UIDs and fee rates are Confidential and the drawer is served under `accounts:read` with `scope: granted_accounts`; a manager must never see another manager's account, which the E27-X03 matrix asserts. **Tampering** - client-side cap enforcement is a convenience only; the server re-derives the cap and the account scope from the token on every call (OpenAPI note C5). **Spoofing of freshness** - showing a stale number as current is the data-accuracy risk R7 for this ticket, addressed by the structural freshness pairing. No secret material is rendered, and key identifiers are truncated to `...{key_id_last4}` (SCR-079).

## Accessibility notes
SCR-079's rules: the drawer has a heading naming the account and its environment; balances are a description list with units; the permission summary is a list of plain statements ("Trade: yes. Withdrawal: off. IP allowlist: on."). Stale state is conveyed by the badge text, not by grey alone - the greying is reinforced with the "stale since" text. The leverage slider (CMP-104) is keyboard-operable with arrow and page keys, has a text input alternative, and announces its value and the applicable risk-limit tier. Toggles announce their state and the consequence of changing it. Exchange rejection messages are announced via `aria-live="assertive"`. Focus is trapped in the drawer and returns to the invoking control on close. Contrast >=4.5:1 in both themes.

## Performance notes
The drawer opens from cached state in <=100 ms and refreshes in place. The `wallet` topic is throttled to 500 ms by the protocol and uses whole-object last-write-wins, so the client applies snapshots rather than diffing. Leverage changes are user-initiated and bounded by the exchange round-trip; the control shows a pending state and must not block the drawer. No per-frame work: this screen must never contribute to the chart's frame budget.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_leverage_changes_total{result}`, `cv_margin_mode_changes_total{result}`, `cv_wallet_snapshot_age_seconds{account}` (reused from E27-T04).
Audit: `account.leverage_changed {account, symbol, before, after}` and `account.margin_mode_changed` (US-ACCT-009 NFR: "changes are audited"); `account.detail_viewed` as analytics only.
Frontend error boundary reports render failures with the screen ID SCR-079.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via PR <=400 LOC diff, conventional commits, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner; all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/accounts` and `candleviewer/credentials` (M2 is in the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; no field shipped that is not in the spec, no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: schema/API deltas noted in the PR description; runbook entry added when the change is operational.
- [ ] Observability (metrics, audit events) added and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off (E27-D06 handoff accepted, E27-D07 design QA passed) for any ticket touching UI.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E27-Q05.
- [ ] Secret-leak assertion suite from E27-T02/E27-X02 passes: no key material in logs, traces, metrics, error bodies or support bundles.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-T04** (wallet snapshot, freshness and health), **E27-S01** (account identity and list) and **E27-D06** (signed-off handoff). Reads profile caps from **E28** (per-account profiles) - until that lands, the cap comes from the account payload's profile summary with the same server-side enforcement point. Consumes the positions context from **E29**.

## Branch
`feat/e27-account-drawer` - two PRs: (1) the drawer, freshness model and health banners, (2) leverage, margin-mode and position-mode controls with cap enforcement.

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#7-r3--trading-on-demo` - E27 scope line (34 pts, S14-S15), R3 exit criteria #9 and #10, quality gates (SS7.4), key dates (SS7.5)

title: Write the accounts and key-vault operator runbook and amend ADR-0009
body:
## Context
ADR-0009 assigns several operational obligations that only exist as prose today: an owner-held offline KEK backup with a restore runbook stating that "a backup without the KEK is unusable - that is the intended property"; a manual IP-allowlist step in the VPS migration runbook, because Bybit made allowlist configuration browser-only in Feb 2026; and a full rotation drill to be executed once before Live enablement as an R4 PRR item. E27-K01 additionally produces custody decisions that must be written down before the knowledge leaves the person who made them (risk R10, key-person).

This task turns those obligations into runbooks an operator can follow without asking anyone, and records the decisions E27 actually made as an amendment to ADR-0009.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/ops/runbooks/kek-custody.md` finalised from the E27-K01 output: where the KEK lives on the WSL host and on the VPS, how it is injected, how it is backed up offline, how it is rotated, and what happens on loss.
- `docs/ops/runbooks/key-rotation.md`: the operator-side procedure matching the SCR-127 wizard - create the new key in the Bybit dashboard (with the 48 h new-key restriction called out), configure the IP allowlist manually, run the app-side rotation, verify, then delete the old key at Bybit.
- `docs/ops/runbooks/key-compromise.md`: the emergency path - mark compromised, revoke, choose "revoke and leave positions" or "flatten first, then revoke", what to do when the Bybit delete call fails (local deletion is authoritative; revoke manually in the dashboard), and who to notify.
- `docs/ops/runbooks/restore-without-kek.md`: the restore drill, its expected outcome (nothing decrypts, the app refuses trading mode) and how to recover with the offline KEK copy.
- ADR-0009 amendment section recording: the injection mechanism chosen in E27-K01, the config vocabulary, the degraded-mode contract, and the DEK-cache TTL decision from E27-T02.
- A short operator FAQ answering the three questions this design predictably raises: why the secret can never be shown again, why a database backup alone is useless, and why the IP allowlist cannot be set from the app.
- Cross-links added from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` to each runbook.

## Out of scope
Implementation of any of the described mechanisms (E27-K01, T02, T03, S03, S04); the R4 pre-Live rotation drill execution itself (an R4 PRR item, not this ticket); backup tooling (E22).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An operator can rotate a key using only the runbook
  Given an operator who has not worked on E27
  When they follow docs/ops/runbooks/key-rotation.md end to end on the demo environment
  Then the rotation completes with no question asked of the engineering team, and the observation is recorded in the ticket

Scenario: The restore drill produces the intended failure
  Given a database backup restored on a machine without the KEK
  When the runbook's verification steps are followed
  Then no key decrypts, the app refuses trading mode, and the runbook states plainly that this is the intended property rather than a defect

Scenario: The ADR reflects what was built
  When ADR-0009 is read alongside the merged E27 code
  Then the injection mechanism, config keys, degraded contract and DEK-cache TTL described in the amendment match the implementation exactly

Scenario: The manual allowlist step is impossible to miss
  When the VPS migration runbook is reviewed
  Then the manual Bybit IP-allowlist step appears as a blocking checklist item with the consequence of skipping it stated
```

## Technical notes / design
Runbooks follow the existing house format: purpose, preconditions, numbered steps with the exact command or UI action, verification step, rollback, and an escalation contact. Every command is copy-pasteable and every UI action names the screen ID (SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129) so the reader can find it.

The compromise runbook must state the ordering explicitly, because US-ACCT-006's NFR fixes it: **local deletion is authoritative and happens first** - never leave usable material because a remote call failed.

## Test plan
Documentation review rather than automated testing: a second engineer executes each runbook on the demo environment and records the result in the ticket. A CI link-checker validates every relative path. A `docs` test asserts that every runbook referenced from `04-security-program.md` exists.

## Security notes
The runbooks themselves must contain no secret material, no real UIDs and no real IP addresses - placeholders only, with a note saying so. Classification: Internal. The compromise runbook is the response plan for the epic's worst-case threat and is reviewed by the Security engineer as part of E27-X04.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - documentation.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
No code. The runbooks do specify which metrics and audit events an operator should check at each step (`cv_keys_failing_policy`, `cv_account_health_state`, `security.kek_loaded`, `account.key_rotated`), which is what makes them actionable during an incident.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four runbooks and the ADR amendment merged.
- [ ] Each runbook executed once on demo by an engineer who did not write it, with the result recorded.
- [ ] Link-checker green; cross-links added from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- [ ] Reviewed by the Security engineer (also covered by E27-X04) and by DevSecOps.
- [ ] No secret material, real UID or real IP address appears in any runbook.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-T02**, **E27-T03**, **E27-S03** and **E27-S04**, because the runbooks document behaviour that must already exist and have been verified.

title: Security-review the credential broker, verification pipeline and key lifecycle implementation
body:
## Context
ADR-0009's security properties are only real if the implementation preserves them. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a white-box security review per security-relevant feature, and roadmap SS7.4 requires "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes". This ticket is that review, performed by the Security engineer against the code as merged rather than against the design as intended.

The review's central question is narrow and answerable: can a plaintext credential, or the KEK, reach anywhere it should not - disk, logs, traces, metrics, error bodies, the support bundle, a core dump, a database dump, an API response, a WS frame, or the browser - and can any actor cause a key to be trusted when it should not be?

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Code review** of `services/api/candleviewer/credentials/` (broker, KEK loader, wrapper type), `candleviewer/admin/accounts.py` and `keyvault.py`, the verification pipeline from E27-T03, the rotation and revocation paths, the API routers for `/exchange-accounts*`, and the frontend key-intake and rotation features - reviewed against the E27-X01 control checklist item by item, with a written verdict per control.
- **Leak-assertion suite**, owned by Security and wired as a required CI check, implementing ADR-0009's validation item in depth: a crafted log line containing a known key value is asserted absent from stdout, log files, the `/metrics` endpoint, OpenTelemetry span attributes, every 4xx/5xx response body produced by the epic's routes, and the generated support bundle. Includes a test that the wrapper type's `__repr__`, `__str__`, `__format__` and pydantic `model_dump()` all return the mask, and a test that no SQLAlchemy model exposing `secret_enc`/`dek_ref` is reachable from any response schema.
- **Abuse-case execution** against the running demo stack, from the narratives in E27-X01: attempt to retrieve a secret through every route and WS topic the epic touches; attempt to promote a key that failed verification; attempt to tamper with `permission_snapshot` directly in the database and confirm the next self-check overrides rather than trusts it; attempt to mutate `env`/`exchange_uid` via `PATCH`; attempt to cause the app to treat a live key as demo; attempt to keep a revoked key usable by racing revoke against an in-flight borrow.
- **Static-analysis rules** committed and enabled: Semgrep rules that fail the build when the secret columns appear in a serialiser, when a credential-typed value is interpolated into an f-string or log call, and when `CV_KEK_SOURCE` is read outside the loader; a Bandit profile for the module; a secrets-scanning rule tuned to Bybit key shapes so a real key committed anywhere in the repository fails CI.
- **DAST**: OWASP ZAP authenticated scan configured for the `/api/v1/exchange-accounts*` routes with the epic's session and step-up flows scripted, run in the nightly job; findings triaged.
- **Dependency review** of anything new the epic introduced into the credential path, with a note on why each dependency is trusted there.
- Findings written to the security register with severity, owner and due date; a written sign-off verdict at the end.

## Out of scope
- Re-deriving the threat model (E27-X01) or re-running the RBAC matrix (E27-X03), though the review confirms both are in place.
- The full penetration test, which is R4 (E43).
- Fixing findings - each becomes a Bug on the owning implementation ticket, re-tested here.
- Reviewing profiles, the OMS or fan-out.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No path leaks a credential
  Given the leak-assertion suite runs against a build where a known secret has been stored
  When logs, metrics, traces, error bodies, the support bundle and a database dump are scanned
  Then the secret appears in none of them, and the suite fails the build if any future change makes it appear

Scenario: A failed verification cannot be promoted
  Given a candidate key that fails the withdrawal check
  When an operator attempts, through the API directly rather than the UI, to attach it or mark it primary
  Then the server refuses with validation_failed / key_withdraw_permission, nothing is persisted, and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Database-level tampering does not win
  Given permission_snapshot is edited directly in Postgres to claim withdrawal is disabled
  When the next self-check runs
  Then the live exchange response overrides the stored snapshot, the account is force-disabled for trading, and a critical alert is raised

Scenario: Revoke wins every race
  Given a credential borrow is in flight when the key is revoked
  When the race is executed repeatedly
  Then no signed request is issued with the revoked key after revocation completes, and the borrow either completes before revocation or fails cleanly

Scenario: Static analysis blocks a regression
  Given a developer adds secret_enc to a response model on a branch
  When CI runs
  Then the Semgrep rule fails the build with a message naming the rule and the file

## Technical notes / design
The review is checklist-driven against E27-X01 rather than impressionistic, and its output is a table: control, where it is implemented, how it was verified, verdict. Controls that exist only as prose are findings.

The race test for revocation is worth the effort because it is the class of bug that code review does not find: it is executed as a loop of several hundred iterations with the borrow and the revoke started from separate tasks, asserting the invariant "no signed request after revocation completes" holds every time. ADR-0009's principle that local deletion is authoritative means the test must also confirm the local delete happens even when the remote call fails.

Semgrep rules live in `.semgrep/e27-credentials.yml` and are owned by Security in CODEOWNERS, so they cannot be weakened without Security review - a rule an engineer can delete is not a control.

## Test plan
The review includes verifying the tests that other tickets claim: Security independently confirms that the coverage claimed on the credential broker is real (the branches that matter are exercised, not just the happy path) and that the contract tests actually assert the absence of secret fields rather than merely not asserting their presence.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security deliverable. It must end with an explicit verdict for the R3 gate: whether key handling in E27 is fit to proceed toward Live enablement, with residual risks named. Any Critical or High left open blocks the R3 gate per roadmap SS7.4. The review is also the prerequisite package for the R4 pen-test, so the artefacts are written to be handed to an external tester.

## Accessibility notes
The review covers the client-side disclosure surface that accessibility affordances can create - aria-labels, tooltips, clipboard, autofill, screenshots - handing findings to and taking findings from E27-Q04 charter 1. Secret inputs must be marked so password managers and autofill do not retain them, and this is verified in a real browser.

## Performance notes
The review confirms that security controls do not themselves create a denial-of-service path: the verification pipeline's exchange calls are budgeted, the leak-assertion suite does not run in the hot path, and audit writes on the key paths are bounded. Numbers come from E27-Q03.

## Observability
Confirms every security-relevant event from E27-X01 is emitted, hash-chained and complete: actor, account, key fingerprint (never the key), outcome and reason. Confirms that failed verifications and KEK load failures raise alerts that a human actually receives, by triggering one of each and observing the notification.

title: Implement the RBAC and account-scope assertion matrix for every accounts and key route and topic
body:
## Context
E27 introduces the first surfaces where a non-owner user can see something money-related: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` marks the account routes with `x-rbac` permissions `accounts:read`, `accounts:write`, `keys:read` and `keys:manage`, with scope `granted_accounts` for reads and `none` (owner-only) for key management, and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS6.3 requires that private topics are account-scoped with out-of-scope requests silently narrowed and a wholly out-of-scope request rejected with `account_scope_denied`. The WS protocol document's own invariant table states: "Manager cannot subscribe to another manager's accounts, even by raw frame."

Elevation of privilege is the highest-likelihood threat in E27-X01's enumeration, and it is exactly the kind that a manual review misses once and nobody notices for a year. This ticket converts the permission matrix into an executable assertion that runs on every build.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A machine-readable matrix at `services/api/tests/security/rbac_matrix_accounts.yaml` enumerating, for every route and topic this epic introduces, the expected outcome for each of the three roles (Owner, Manager, Viewer) in each of three scope situations (granted account, non-granted account, non-existent account): `GET /exchange-accounts`, `POST /exchange-accounts`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}`, `GET|POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys`, `DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/keys/{keyId}`, `POST .../rotate`, `POST .../test`, `GET .../fee-rate`, `PATCH /positions/{positionId}/leverage`, and the WS topics `wallet` and `positions` as they relate to account scope.
- A parameterised test that executes the whole matrix against the running app with real sessions for each role, asserting the exact status code and error code - `403` with the documented problem type for REST, `account_scope_denied` for a wholly out-of-scope WS subscription, and silent narrowing with the effective list reported in `sub_ok.effective` for a partially out-of-scope one.
- **Enumeration-resistance assertions**: a non-granted account id and a non-existent account id must be indistinguishable to a Manager (same status, same body, comparable timing), so the API cannot be used to enumerate which accounts exist.
- **Step-up assertions**: every route the screen specs mark as step-up-gated (`account.created|updated`, key attach, rotate, revoke, disable, delete) refuses without a fresh step-up and succeeds with one, and a step-up token for one action cannot be replayed for another.
- **Coverage guard**: a test that fails when a route tagged `exchange-accounts` exists in `22-api-openapi.yaml` but has no row in the matrix, so a new endpoint cannot be added without declaring its RBAC expectations.
- Documentation of the matrix in `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md` as the evidence for the elevation-of-privilege mitigations.

## Out of scope
- Implementing RBAC itself - roles, permissions, `user_account_access` and the scope resolver are E09's; this ticket asserts their correct application to E27's surface.
- Routes belonging to other epics (profiles E28, orders E29), though the matrix pattern is intended for reuse there.
- UI-level permission hiding, which is a usability affordance and never the enforcement point.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A manager cannot reach a non-granted account
  Given a manager session with access to account A only
  When the manager requests GET /exchange-accounts/{B} for an account B they were not granted
  Then the response is 403 with the documented problem type, the body reveals nothing about whether B exists, and the attempt is audited

Scenario: A manager cannot manage keys at all
  Given a manager session with access to account A
  When the manager attempts POST /exchange-accounts/{A}/keys
  Then the request is refused because keys:manage is owner-only with scope none, regardless of the account grant

Scenario: A raw WS frame cannot widen scope
  Given a manager session granted account A
  When the client sends a sub frame naming accounts A and B on the wallet topic
  Then the subscription succeeds narrowed to A only, sub_ok.effective reports A alone, and no frame for B is ever delivered

Scenario: A wholly out-of-scope subscription is an error, not a silent no-op
  Given the same manager session
  When the client subscribes to wallet for account B only
  Then the server responds with account_scope_denied

Scenario: A new endpoint cannot skip the matrix
  Given a developer adds a route tagged exchange-accounts to the OpenAPI document
  When CI runs
  Then the coverage guard fails until a matrix row with expected outcomes for all three roles is added

Scenario: Step-up cannot be replayed across actions
  Given a fresh step-up completed for a key rotation
  When the same step-up token is presented for an account deletion
  Then the deletion is refused and requires its own step-up

## Technical notes / design
The matrix is data, not code, so it is reviewable by the Security engineer without reading Python, and its diff in a pull request is legible - "this route became readable by managers" is visible at a glance. The test harness seeds three users with the three roles and a fixed grant map in `user_account_access`, then walks the matrix.

Timing indistinguishability is asserted loosely (order-of-magnitude, not constant-time) because the goal is to prevent trivial enumeration, not to defend against a lab-grade side channel; the ticket states that limit explicitly rather than implying a stronger guarantee than it delivers.

WS assertions run against a real gateway connection rather than a mocked subscription manager, because the bug class this targets - demand aggregation that forgets to re-check scope - lives in the integration, not the unit.

## Test plan
The matrix test is the test. It runs in the `security` CI job on every PR and in the nightly full suite. Manual verification during E27-X02 spot-checks three matrix rows by hand to confirm the harness is not vacuously passing - a matrix test that asserts nothing is a common and dangerous failure mode, so the harness additionally includes a self-check that deliberately flips one expectation and confirms the suite fails.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* a security control. It addresses the elevation-of-privilege and information-disclosure branches of E27-X01 directly, and it is the standing regression guard for them. Data classification: the matrix itself is Internal; the test users' credentials are test-only and generated per run. Requires Security-engineer review and sign-off.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. The matrix does record which controls the UI is expected to hide for each role, so that E27-Q04's keyboard pass can confirm a hidden control is genuinely absent from the accessibility tree rather than merely visually hidden.

## Performance notes
The matrix run adds bounded time to CI (target under 90 seconds for the full walk); it is parameterised so it can be sharded if it grows. Scope resolution itself must stay off the hot path - the test records the per-request scope-resolution overhead so a regression into a per-request database walk is visible.

## Observability
Every denied attempt emits an audit event with the actor, the target account and the reason, so repeated denials are detectable; the test asserts those events exist. A metric counting authorisation denials by route and role is added so a spike is alertable - an attacker probing scope should be visible in Grafana, not only in a log file nobody reads.

- [ ] Findings logged in the security register with severity, owner and due date.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings closed before the R3 gate (roadmap SS7.4 Security gate: "STRIDE for E27 ... all Critical/High closed").

- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer; the STRIDE document is stored at `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md` and linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-X01** (which demands this control), **E27-T03** (the key routes must exist to be asserted) and **E27-S01** (accounts and grants must exist to scope against). Relies on E09's roles, permissions, `user_account_access` and step-up.

title: Run the key-compromise, restore and rotation drills and record the epic security sign-off
body:
## Context
ADR-0009 lists three validations that are only meaningful when actually executed: the security log-leak test, a **restore drill** ("restore a database backup on a machine without the KEK and confirm no key can be decrypted and the app refuses trading mode") and a **rotation drill** ("full 90-day rotation executed once before Live enablement (R4) as a PRR item"). Roadmap SS7.3 exit criterion #9 requires KEK separation to be *demonstrated*, not designed. `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` makes drill evidence a PRR input.

This ticket executes those drills, adds the compromise drill that the incident runbook implies, and produces the Security sign-off that - together with QA (E27-Q05) and design (E27-D07) - closes E27.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Restore drill**: take a real Postgres backup of the demo deployment, restore it on a clean machine with no access to the KEK, and prove that (a) no `api_keys` row decrypts, (b) the application refuses to enter trading mode, (c) the failure message is the documented degraded-mode banner rather than a stack trace. Evidence: terminal transcript, screenshots, and a written statement that the backup alone is unusable - the intended property.
- **Rotation drill**: execute a complete rotation on a demo account following `docs/ops/runbooks` from E27-T05 verbatim - create the replacement, verify it, overlap, confirm traffic moved, retire the old key - measuring elapsed time per stage, confirming no open order was cancelled and no private stream dropped an update, and confirming `api_key_rotations` records the full history.
- **KEK rotation drill**: bump `kek_version`, run the re-wrap job across all DEKs, confirm every key still decrypts and no ciphertext changed, and confirm `ix_api_keys_kek` drives the job to completion with a resumable checkpoint.
- **Compromise drill**: simulate a suspected compromise end to end - mark a key compromised from SCR-128, confirm the account's trading halts immediately, rules scoped to it disarm, the key is revoked locally even when the Bybit call is forced to fail, positions are surfaced for the flatten-or-leave decision, and the audit trail reconstructs the whole incident from `prev_hash`/`row_hash` with no gap. Time the drill and record the detection-to-contained interval.
- **Egress-IP and allowlist verification**: confirm the deployment's egress IP determination is correct and that a mismatch is detected and surfaced with the copy-pasteable current IP (US-ACCT-003); confirm the manual Bybit allowlist step is documented in the VPS migration runbook, since ADR-0009 records that it cannot be automated.
- **Sign-off artefact** at `docs/security/signoffs/E27.md`: the verdict, the evidence index, residual risks with owners, and the explicit statement of readiness for the R3 gate and of the package handed to the R4 pen-test.

## Out of scope
- Fixing anything the drills break - raised as Bugs against the owning tickets and re-drilled.
- The R4 penetration test itself (E43) and Live enablement gating (E44); this ticket only prepares their inputs.
- Drills for the OMS, fan-out or risk caps, which belong to their own epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A stolen database is useless
  Given a Postgres backup restored on a machine with no KEK
  When the application is started against it in trading mode
  Then no api_keys row decrypts, the app enters degraded read-only mode with the documented banner, every trading route refuses, and the transcript is captured as evidence for R3 exit criterion #9

Scenario: Rotation is boring
  Given the rotation runbook is followed verbatim on a demo account with an open order
  When the drill completes
  Then the new key is primary, the old key is revoked, the open order was never cancelled, no private stream gap was observed, and total elapsed time is recorded

Scenario: KEK rotation rewraps without touching ciphertext
  Given kek_version is bumped and the re-wrap job runs
  When it completes
  Then every key still decrypts, the ciphertext columns are byte-identical to before, and interrupting the job midway and restarting it produces the same end state

Scenario: A compromise is contained in minutes and reconstructible
  Given the compromise drill is executed with the Bybit revoke call forced to fail
  When the drill completes
  Then the key is gone locally regardless, trading for that account halted, scoped rules disarmed, the operator was told to revoke at Bybit with the exact error shown, and the audit chain verifies with no gap

Scenario: Sign-off is specific
  When docs/security/signoffs/E27.md is written
  Then it names each drill with its date, build SHA and evidence link, lists residual risks with owners, and states plainly whether E27 is fit to proceed toward Live enablement

## Technical notes / design
Drills are executed by the Security engineer with DevSecOps, on the demo deployment, following the runbooks literally - the runbook being wrong is one of the outcomes this ticket is looking for, and any deviation is filed against E27-T05 rather than silently corrected in the moment.

The restore drill uses a genuinely separate machine (or a container with no host credential access) rather than an environment variable unset on the same host, because the property being demonstrated is custody separation, and testing it by simply hiding the key from oneself proves nothing.

The compromise drill is timed because incident response is a latency problem: the recorded detection-to-contained interval becomes the baseline the R4 readiness review compares against, and it is the number the Owner actually cares about when deciding whether the response plan is adequate.

All drills are re-run before Live enablement in R4; this ticket establishes the procedure and the first evidence, and the runbook records the re-run schedule.

## Test plan
Each drill has an explicit pass criterion stated above and evidence captured in `docs/security/drills/e27/`. Failed drills are re-run after fixes; a drill is never signed off on a partial pass. The audit-chain verification uses the chain verifier from E09 rather than manual inspection.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security deliverable and the epic's closing security gate. Residual risks expected to be recorded rather than eliminated: KEK availability remains a single point of failure for starting the service (accepted in ADR-0009 with an owner-held offline backup); the Bybit IP allowlist remains a manual step; the 48-hour new-key restriction constrains how fast an emergency rotation can complete, which the compromise runbook must state honestly. The drills must never be run against `live` - a guard and a written pre-flight check enforce this.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - operational drills. The compromise drill does confirm that the blocking degraded-mode banner is announced to assistive technology, since it is the one state a user must not miss.

## Performance notes
Records the measured durations: rotation total against the SCR-127 <=10 s target for the in-app portion, re-wrap job throughput, degraded-mode entry time on KEK loss, and detection-to-contained for the compromise drill. These feed the R3 PRR.

## Observability
Confirms the drills are visible in telemetry: KEK load failures, credential-borrow failures, verification failures and authorisation denials all appear in Grafana and fire the configured alerts during the drills, with the alert actually reaching the owner's notification channel - an alert that fires into a void is a finding.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings logged in the security register with severity, owner and due date.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings closed before the R3 gate (roadmap SS7.4 Security gate: "STRIDE for E27 ... all Critical/High closed").
- [ ] Every agreed control encoded as an automated check (CI rule, unit test, contract test or DAST rule), not only as prose.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer; the STRIDE document is stored at `docs/security/threat-models/E27.md` and linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27-X02** and **E27-X03** (the controls must be reviewed and asserted before drilling them), **E27-T05** (the runbooks being executed verbatim) and **E27-Q03** (which produced the KEK-loss chaos scenario this ticket reuses). Together with E27-Q05 and E27-D07 it gates the epic's Done transition.

title: Per-account profiles & trade groups
body:
## Context
E28 is the second epic of the **R3 "Trading on demo"** train (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7, sprints S15-S16, 2027-01-01 -> 2027-01-14). It sits on the train's safety scaffolding path: the roadmap's key dates record 2027-01-07 as "Key vault + profiles + risk caps + kill-switch complete - **safety scaffolding lands before the first order ticket ships**", and the dependency graph records `E27 --> E28 --> E34`.

The epic answers one question: **when one intent is executed across several accounts, what decides the size, the leverage, the stop and whether the order is permitted at all?** The answer is the per-account profile, and it is server-side and non-negotiable (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.2: "Risk caps are **server-side and non-negotiable** - a manager cannot exceed them from the UI, an API call, or a rule"). Everything downstream depends on it: the order ticket (E30), the fan-out engine (E34), the rule engine (E35), risk lockouts (E39) and journal attribution (E41) all consume the profile, the sizer or the trade group defined here.

The roadmap's scope line for this epic reads: "Profile schema: leverage, sizing rule (% equity / fixed $ / fixed qty / risk-based), SL/TP offsets, max risk per day, max position size, allowed symbols, position mode (one-way/hedge) and margin mode; profile CRUD with validation against instruments-info precision filters; trade-group definition (named set of accounts) with per-account enable/disable; per-trade override semantics documented and enforced; profile simulation preview ('this ticket would place X on A, Y on B')."

Web app only; Bybit USDT linear perpetuals only; the admin surfaces are RBAC-gated screens **inside the web app** - there is no separate admin application (owner decision, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`).

## Goal
Make per-account risk policy a first-class, versioned, server-enforced object, and make a named set of accounts a first-class tradable unit - so that a single intent resolves into correctly-sized, correctly-protected, correctly-permitted per-account orders, and so that no client, rule or crafted request can produce an order larger, more levered or less protected than the owner's policy allows.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (domain PROF, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` SS3):**
- **US-PROF-001** Define a per-account profile (Must) - E28-T01, E28-T02, E28-S01
- **US-PROF-002** Sizing rules (Must) - E28-T03, E28-S01
- **US-PROF-003** Allowed-symbol restriction (Must) - E28-T04, E28-S02
- **US-PROF-004** Risk caps enforced server-side (Must) - E28-T04
- **US-PROF-005** Create a trade group (Must) - E28-T05, E28-S03
- **US-PROF-006** Fan-out an order to a trade group (Must) - **preview and sizing only** here (E28-T03, E28-T05, E28-S04); submission, the rate-limit governor and partial-failure remediation are **E34**
- **US-PROF-007** Trade-group lifecycle view (Must) - **definition, listing and read projection** here (E28-T05, E28-S03); the live aggregate view over open positions is completed by **E34** and **E41**
- **US-PROF-008** Per-trade profile overrides (Should) - E28-K01, E28-S05

**Screens:** SCR-130 Admin: per-account profiles list, SCR-131 Admin: profile editor, SCR-132 Admin: profile templates, SCR-133 Admin: symbol permissions matrix, SCR-062 Trade-group manager, and the **preview half** of SCR-061 Trade-group ticket. SCR-114 Trading defaults is touched for the profile-ceiling display.

**Components:** CMP-001, CMP-005, CMP-011, CMP-040, CMP-041, CMP-044, CMP-049, CMP-050, CMP-055, CMP-065, CMP-075, CMP-086, CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-100, CMP-101, CMP-102, CMP-104, CMP-105, CMP-106, CMP-107, CMP-119, CMP-121, CMP-123, CMP-124, CMP-138, CMP-158, CMP-229, CMP-231, CMP-232.

**API:** `GET`/`POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles/{profileId}`, `GET`/`POST /trade-groups`, `GET /trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}`, `POST /trade-groups/preview`. `POST /trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/amend` and `/cancel` are defined in the contract and implemented by **E34**.

**WS:** the `trade_groups` private topic (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` SS15.5, 100 ms throttle, `orders:read` + granted accounts) - read projection here, live fan-out state in E34.

**DB:** `account_profiles` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4), `trade_groups` (SS3.3.2), `trade_group_legs` (SS3.3.3), plus the `account_profile_revisions` projection this epic adds for versioning.

**Architecture module:** **M13** (fan-out / profile application), with `Sizer`, `ProfileAdmin` and `TradeGroupFanout` from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` SS3.5 and SS10.2.

## Out of scope
- Fan-out **submission**, the per-UID rate-limit governor, partial-failure remediation and unwind - **E34**.
- Order placement, the order state machine and reconciliation - **E29**; the order ticket UI - **E30**.
- The native-SL invariant's enforcement at the OMS acknowledgement boundary - **E32** (this epic guarantees the profile can never *lack* a stop definition; E32 guarantees the order never *reaches the exchange* without one).
- The lockout state machine, its 2FA-gated reset and the kill-switch - **E39** (this epic's guard detects a breach and delegates).
- Rule-engine interaction with profiles - **E35**; journal analytics over overrides and groups - **E41**; the users/roles/audit admin surfaces - **E42**.
- Accounts, sub-accounts and API keys - **E27**. Android, a separate admin app, and any non-Bybit or non-USDT-perp instrument - out of scope for the whole plan.

## Exit criteria
1. Every Must story in the PROF domain is Done, and US-PROF-006 and US-PROF-007 are Done to their E28 boundary with the remainder explicitly carried by E34.
2. A profile cannot be stored, by any path, with `require_native_sl` false - proven at the database, the API and the UI, and drilled in E28-X04.
3. The sizing algorithm produces byte-identical results to the frozen golden vectors, and ten of those vectors are independently recomputed by QA from the story text and match.
4. A preview across five accounts resolves each leg by its own profile, reports every skip with a reason, and returns within 300 ms p95.
5. The risk guard adds <=5 ms p95 to the order path, refuses a crafted non-allowed-symbol order with 403 plus an audit row, and fails **closed** when its inputs are unavailable.
6. A breached cap survives a process restart, a WS reconnect and a clock change (E28-Q03 chaos scenarios 1-3, E28-X04 drill 3).
7. No override can widen any hard cap, by UI or by crafted payload - every protected field asserted individually.
8. RBAC matrix green across every E28 route and the `trade_groups` topic x every role, asserting 403, no state change and an audit row for every disallowed cell (R3 exit criterion #10 for this epic's surface).
9. Design-QA passed on all six surfaces; axe-core clean and manual screen-reader passes done; every status expressed as text.
10. Coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and the group planner, >=80% frontend; zero open P0/P1 against E28's scope; QA and Security sign-offs recorded; demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review.

## Risks
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| A sizing bug produces wrongly-sized orders on N accounts simultaneously | Direct financial loss, multiplied by the group size | Frozen golden vectors, QA's independent recomputation from the story text, property tests asserting realised risk <= budgeted risk, and a regression pack tagged to run on every consuming epic's changes |
| A consumer (E30, E34, E35) re-derives size instead of calling the sizer | Two sources of truth, divergence discovered in production | Single-entry-point rule documented in E28-T06, enforced by the call-site review in E28-X02 |
| The risk guard's in-memory counters desynchronise and reopen a breached cap | A locked-out account trades again | Rebuild from Postgres on start and reconnect, fail-closed on unavailable inputs, chaos scenarios 1-3 and drill 3 |
| Override semantics were left open by the owner decision | Late rework of E30 and E34 | E28-K01 timeboxed to 2 days with the safety floor fixed in advance and ADR-0016 recorded regardless of outcome |
| Profile propagation has no WS topic and the protocol is frozen for R3 | Stale profiles used for sizing in an open ticket | E28-K01 decides the transport with a stated fallback (event-triggered REST re-fetch) that needs no protocol change |
| The symbol matrix at ~400 symbols x N accounts is slow or inaccessible | An unusable admin screen, an a11y gate failure | Virtualisation designed in at E28-D02/D03, the DOM approach decided in E28-D05, budgets asserted in E28-Q04 |
| E28 and E34 both draw SCR-061 | Duplicated or conflicting design | Explicit split recorded in E28-D02's scope: E28 owns the preview, E34 owns send and failure states |

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Policy decides size, not the client
  Given three accounts with different profiles in one trade group
  When one intent is previewed
  Then each account resolves its own quantity, leverage and stop from its own profile, and a client-supplied size is only ever a hint that the server clamps

Scenario: The safety invariant is unbreakable
  When any path - UI, API, template, override or a direct database write - attempts to produce a profile without a mandatory native stop-loss
  Then it is refused, and the refusal is audited

Scenario: Limits survive a hostile client
  When crafted requests attempt a non-allowed symbol, an oversized quantity, a widened cap and an ungranted account
  Then each is refused with the documented code, no state changes, no exchange call is made, and every attempt leaves an audit row

Scenario: The epic's contract holds for its consumers
  Given the order ticket, the fan-out engine and the rule engine all size an identical intent
  Then all three produce the same quantity, because all three call the one sizer
```

## Technical notes / design
The epic is built in strict dependency order: schema (E28-T01) -> contract (E28-T02) -> arithmetic (E28-T03) -> enforcement (E28-T04) -> aggregation (E28-T05), with the UI following two sprints behind its design. The one architectural rule that governs every child is **single authority**: exactly one implementation of sizing (`size_leg`, E28-T03), one of cap enforcement (`guard.check`, E28-T04) and one of group planning (`plan_group`, E28-T05). Consumers - E30, E34, E35 - call them; no consumer re-derives a quantity or re-implements a cap, and the call-site review in E28-X02 enforces it.

The second rule is **the client is never the authority**. Every number the UI computes (the worked example in SCR-131, the send-blocking predicate in SCR-061) exists for latency only and is re-derived server-side; the single permitted duplication, the TypeScript sizing port behind the worked example, is validated against the backend golden vectors in CI so drift fails the build.

The third rule is **fail closed**. Where an input is unavailable - the instrument cache during a save, the position snapshot during a guard evaluation - the operation is refused with a documented code and an alert, never permitted on an assumption.

Money and quantity are `Decimal` end to end (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` invariant C3); no float touches any value that becomes an order, a journal entry or an audit row.

## Test plan
Per-child plans roll up into **E28-Q05**. Layers: unit and property tests on the sizer and the guard (>=90% coverage); contract tests against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the `trade_groups` WS schema; integration against a seeded Postgres with recorded Bybit `instruments-info` fixtures; Playwright E2E across the six surfaces in browser and Electron (**E28-Q02**); k6/Locust load plus five chaos scenarios (**E28-Q03**); axe-core plus manual screen-reader and keyboard passes (**E28-Q04**); RBAC matrix and ten abuse cases as a required CI check (**E28-X03**); manual privilege-escalation and cap-bypass drills (**E28-X04**).

## Security notes
Assets **A-08** (per-account profiles) and **A-09** (trade-group configuration) from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SS4, both integrity-3. Threats owned by this epic: **O3** tampering with size/leverage beyond caps (High), **F2** a profile ignored so one account gets another's sizing (High), **F6** a leg without a native SL because the profile lacked offsets (High), and the repudiation risk **F4** for group actions. Controls implemented: **SR-025** step-up on every profile and cap change, **SR-052** server-side authority over sizing and caps, **SR-053** hard ceilings, **SR-054** allowed-symbol allow-list, **SR-056** the native-SL invariant at the profile layer, **SR-064** audit of every change and refusal, **SR-072** per-leg status recording. STRIDE model in **E28-X01**, review in **E28-X02**, automation in **E28-X03**, drills and sign-off in **E28-X04**. Data classification: Confidential throughout; no secret material ever enters a profile, a snapshot or an API response, proven by test.

## Accessibility notes
Six net-new or changed surfaces, all WCAG 2.2 AA. The epic's binding rules, taken from the screen catalogue: every status is text, never colour alone (SCR-062, SCR-061); matrix cells are checkboxes whose accessible names combine account and symbol (SCR-133); every profile field carries units and a worked example (SCR-131); disabled controls state their reason in visible text (SCR-061, E28-S05's "capped by profile"); live-updating surfaces announce a bounded summary and never steal focus. Design-time review in **E28-D05**, built-code audit in **E28-Q04**, conformance in **E28-D07**.

## Performance notes
Budgets owned by this epic: risk-guard evaluation <=5 ms p95 added to the order path (US-PROF-004); fan-out preview <=300 ms p95 at five accounts (SCR-061); profile save <=2 s including exchange-limit revalidation (SCR-131); symbol matrix render <=600 ms at ~400 symbols (SCR-133); group grid <=4 ms scripting per frame at 50 groups x 5 legs (SCR-062); profile-change propagation to open tickets <=2 s (SCR-130); and a contribution to the fan-out overhead budget of <=50 ms + <=10 ms per additional account p95 (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` SS5.2). Measured and recorded in **E28-Q03**.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_profile_saves_total`, `cv_profile_validation_failures_total`, `cv_profile_save_seconds`, `cv_profile_cache_hit_ratio`, `cv_sizer_duration_seconds`, `cv_sizer_outcomes_total`, `cv_sizer_clamped_total`, `cv_risk_guard_seconds`, `cv_risk_guard_refusals_total`, `cv_risk_guard_fail_closed_total`, `cv_tradegroup_preview_seconds`, `cv_tradegroup_legs_skipped_total`, `cv_override_applied_total`, `cv_override_clamped_total`.
Audit: `profile.created|updated|deleted|bound|unbound`, `profile.template_applied`, `symbol_permission.changed|bulk_changed|change_refused`, `tradegroup.created|updated|deleted|granted`, `tradegroup.preview`, `tradegroup.row_overridden`, `order.refused_by_profile`.
Alerts: any `cv_risk_guard_fail_closed_total` increment pages the owner; a cap breach raises a warning notification.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story, Task and Spike is Done (100% rollup) or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level acceptance criteria above verified end to end on the R3 demo staging environment, not merely per child.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and the group planner, >=80% frontend; no open P0/P1 against E28's scope.
- [ ] Docs updated: `21-database-schema.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `18-traceability-matrix.md`, ADR-0008 amended, ADR-0016 merged (E28-T06, E28-K01).
- [ ] a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA verified on all six surfaces - axe-core CI green plus manual screen-reader passes (E28-Q04); design QA passed (E28-D07).
- [ ] perf: all budgets above measured and recorded against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (E28-Q03).
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, abuse-case and RBAC suites green as required checks, drills executed, Security engineer sign-off (E28-X01..X04).
- [ ] QA sign-off: epic-level regression and exploratory pass executed and recorded (E28-Q05).
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at Sprint Review with acceptance recorded - a single intent fanned out in preview across three demo accounts, each sized by its own profile.
- [ ] Retro note captured; any process learnings filed as Chore tickets.
- [ ] Feature flags `ff.profiles` and `ff.trade_groups` documented with their per-environment defaults.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27** (exchange accounts, key verification, account health and wallet snapshots) and **E09** (auth, RBAC, step-up, audit chain). **E28-T04** additionally needs **E29**'s submit pipeline and execution stream. Consumes the instrument cache from **E08**, indicators (ATR) from **E13**, the WS gateway from **E10**/**E17** and the design system from **E05**. Delegates lockout to **E39**. Its outputs are consumed by **E30**, **E34**, **E35**, **E39**, **E41** and **E42**.

## Branch
Per-child feature branches under `feat/e28-*`, `design/e28-*`, `test/e28-*`, `chore/e28-*`; PRs <=400 LOC with 2 approvals including a code-owner.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Write the black-box test plan and fixture set for profiles, sizing and trade groups
body:
## Context
E28 decides how large every order in the system will be. A sizing bug here does not produce a wrong pixel; it produces a position ten times too large on five accounts at once. The testing strategy (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`) requires a black-box test plan per feature alongside the white-box review, and the R3 quality gates require recorded fixtures for partial fills, rejections, rate limits and disconnects.

This ticket writes the plan and builds the fixtures **before** the features land, so the stories are implemented against an agreed definition of correct rather than a post-hoc one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Black-box test plan at `qa/plans/e28/test-plan.md`, organised by story group: profile definition and sizing (US-PROF-001, US-PROF-002), symbol restriction (US-PROF-003), risk caps (US-PROF-004), trade groups (US-PROF-005, US-PROF-007 definition half), preview (roadmap's simulation-preview scope line), overrides (US-PROF-008).
- One test case per Gherkin scenario across all eight US-PROF stories, each with preconditions, steps, expected result and the evidence to capture - traceable back to the scenario id so coverage is provable.
- Boundary case catalogue, derived from the DDL and the sizing algorithm: leverage at 1, 100 and 101; `max_open_positions` at 1, 50 and 51; `slippage_tolerance_bps` at 0, 1000 and 1001; `max_orders_per_minute` at 1, 600 and 601; TP ladder summing to exactly 100 and to 100.000001; quantity exactly at the minimum lot and one step below; daily loss exactly at the cap; an intent at 00:00:00 UTC on the rollover boundary.
- Negative and hostile case catalogue: `require_native_sl = false` by every route; a crafted order for a non-allowed symbol; an oversized quantity hint; a group mixing demo and live; a preview attempting to mutate; a manager acting on an ungranted account; an override widening each protected cap.
- **Fixture set** committed under `tests/fixtures/e28/`: six exchange accounts (one main, five subs; four demo, two live), four profiles covering all four sizing modes including one with an empty allow-list and one with a TP ladder, two trade groups (one healthy, one with a failing key self-check), one account holding an open position so the matrix's locked cell is reachable, and a recorded `instruments-info` snapshot for BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT and DOGEUSDT with their real tick, lot, min-notional and max-leverage values.
- Shared golden sizing vectors agreed with E28-T03 so QA and engineering assert the same numbers - QA owns an independent recomputation of at least ten of them by hand, to catch an algorithm that is self-consistently wrong.
- Exploratory charters (session-based, 90 minutes each): "sizing rules under extreme equity", "the profile editor under exchange-limit conflicts", "trade-group membership edge cases", "preview under rapid intent changes".
- Entry/exit criteria and a defect-triage convention for the epic.

## Out of scope
Writing the automation (E28-Q02); load, soak and chaos runs (E28-Q03); the a11y audit (E28-Q04); security abuse cases (E28-X03 - though the hostile catalogue here feeds it).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every Gherkin scenario in US-PROF-001..008 maps to at least one written test case; a coverage table proves it with no gaps.
- The boundary and hostile catalogues exist and each entry names the constraint or control it probes.
- The fixture set is committed, loads into a clean database with one command, and is used by E28-Q02, E28-D07 and E28-X03 - verified by at least one of them consuming it before this ticket closes.
- Ten golden sizing vectors are independently recomputed by QA and match the engineering values exactly; any mismatch is raised as a Bug before the sizer merges.
- Entry/exit criteria and the triage convention are agreed with the Owner and the Architect.
- The plan is reviewed by the second QA/SDET.

## Technical notes / design
The independent recomputation is the point of this ticket, not a formality: it is the only step in the whole epic where the sizing arithmetic is derived twice from the story text rather than once from the code. It is done in a spreadsheet from US-PROF-002's stated inputs, and the spreadsheet is committed alongside the vectors.

Fixtures are expressed as SQL seeds plus JSON API-response recordings, never as live exchange calls, so the suite is deterministic and runnable offline.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan. Its own verification is the coverage table and the peer review.

## Security notes
Fixtures contain no real API keys, UIDs, labels or balances - all synthetic, with keys that are structurally valid but non-functional, checked by the secrets scanner over `tests/fixtures/`. The hostile case catalogue is shared with the Security engineer and becomes the basis of E28-X03's abuse-case suite, so the two are not written twice with different assumptions.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the a11y acceptance points from the screen catalogue as explicit test cases (text status chips, accessible names on matrix cells, disabled-control reasons), which E28-Q04 then executes in depth.

## Performance notes
The plan states the per-surface budgets as testable assertions (preview <=300 ms, save <=2 s, matrix render <=600 ms, guard <=5 ms p95, fan-out overhead <=50 ms + <=10 ms/account) and names which ticket measures each.

## Observability
The plan lists the metrics and audit events each scenario should produce, so a test can assert on telemetry as well as on the response - in particular that every refusal produces an audit row.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario of the covered stories is mapped to an executed test case with a pass/fail result recorded on the story.
- [ ] Defects raised with `priority/*`, reproduction steps, environment and evidence; P0/P1 defects closed before the epic is Done.
- [ ] Automated suites run in CI on the R3 demo environment and are green on three consecutive runs (no flakes).
- [ ] Coverage of the epic's acceptance criteria reported in the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Results and residual risk summarised on E28-Q05 and referenced by the epic ticket.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T01** (the schema the fixtures are built against). Feeds **E28-Q02**, **E28-Q03**, **E28-Q04**, **E28-X03** and **E28-D07**.

## Branch

title: Land account_profiles, trade_groups and trade_group_legs migrations and domain models
body:
## Context
E28 is the second epic of the R3 "Trading on demo" train (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS7, S15-S16, 2027-01-01 -> 2027-01-14). Its roadmap scope line reads: "Profile schema: leverage, sizing rule (% equity / fixed $ / fixed qty / risk-based), SL/TP offsets, max risk per day, max position size, allowed symbols, position mode (one-way/hedge) and margin mode; profile CRUD with validation against instruments-info precision filters; trade-group definition (named set of accounts) with per-account enable/disable; per-trade override semantics documented and enforced; profile simulation preview".

Nothing else in the epic can start until the persistence layer exists, because every other ticket - sizing (E28-T03), risk guards (E28-T04), the profile editor (E28-S01) and the group manager (E28-S03) - reads or writes these tables. The DDL is already fully specified in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4 (`account_profiles`), SS3.3.2 (`trade_groups`) and SS3.3.3 (`trade_group_legs`); this Task lands it verbatim with the Alembic migration, the SQLAlchemy models and the Pydantic domain models from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.1 and SS9.2.

The single most important line in the DDL is `CONSTRAINT ap_native_sl CHECK (require_native_sl = true)` - the database itself refuses to store a profile that disables the native stop-loss invariant (owner decision, cross-cutting consequence #3, ADR-0008). That check is not negotiable and must not be relaxed by any later migration.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating `account_profiles` exactly as specified in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4, including every CHECK constraint: `ap_leverage`, `ap_native_sl`, `ap_tif`, `ap_slip`, `ap_opm`, `ap_sl_pos`, `ap_tp_pair`, `ap_tp_pos`, `ap_maxpos`, `ap_sizing_shape`, `ap_ladder_shape`; and both partial-unique indexes `ux_ap_name` (case-insensitive name per account, live rows only) and `ux_ap_default` (one `is_default` per account).
- Trigger `trg_ap_ladder_sum` enforcing `SUM(pct) <= 100` over the `tp_ladder` JSONB array (an aggregation, so it cannot be a CHECK).
- Enum types required by the DDL: `sizing_mode`, `offset_unit`, `trade_group_status` (`draft`,`submitting`,`partially_open`,`open`,`closing`,`closed`,`failed`,`cancelled`).
- Alembic migration creating `trade_groups` (SS3.3.2) with indexes `ix_tg_open`, `ix_tg_user_time`, `ix_tg_rule`, `ix_tg_env_time`, and `trade_group_legs` (SS3.3.3) with `profile_snapshot jsonb NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE (trade_group_id, exchange_account_id)` and indexes `ix_tgl_group`, `ix_tgl_account`, `ix_tgl_open`, `ix_tgl_no_sl`.
- SQLAlchemy models and repository layer in `services/api/candleviewer/profiles/` and `candleviewer/oms/groups/`, with soft-delete (`deleted_at`) honoured in every read path.
- Pydantic domain models `AccountProfile`, `TradeGroup`, `TradeGroupLeg`, `TakeProfitLeg`, `TradeGroupAggregate` transcribed from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.1-SS9.2, with `Decimal` everywhere a value crosses into the OMS, journal or audit (invariant C3 of `24-internal-schemas.md`).
- Profile **versioning**: `version` integer on the domain model, bumped on every update; historical versions retained so `trade_group_legs.profile_snapshot` and journal attribution can point at the exact version used (US-PROF-001 scenario "Profile in use").
- Seed/bootstrap: creating an exchange account with no profile auto-creates a disabled default profile named "Default" so an account is never profile-less in the data model; it is flagged `trading_enabled = false` until the owner completes it.
- Downgrade path for every migration, and a migration test that runs `upgrade -> downgrade -> upgrade` on a scratch database.

## Out of scope
REST routes (E28-T02); sizing arithmetic (E28-T03); risk-cap evaluation in the order path (E28-T04); group membership API and WS projection (E28-T05); any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and reverses cleanly
  Given an empty Postgres 16 database with the R3 baseline schema applied
  When the E28 migrations run forward, then back, then forward again
  Then all three tables, all enums, all indexes and the ladder trigger exist and match the DDL in 21-database-schema.md byte for byte in shape

Scenario: The native-SL invariant is enforced by the database
  When an INSERT or UPDATE sets account_profiles.require_native_sl to false
  Then the statement is rejected by constraint ap_native_sl and no row is written

Scenario: Sizing shape is enforced by the database
  When a profile is written with sizing_mode 'risk_based' and size_fixed_qty set
  Then the statement is rejected by constraint ap_sizing_shape

Scenario: Exactly one default profile per account
  Given account A already has a profile with is_default true and deleted_at null
  When a second default profile is inserted for account A
  Then the unique index ux_ap_default rejects it

Scenario: TP ladder percentages cannot exceed 100
  When a profile is saved with tp_ladder [{"pct":60,"r":1},{"pct":60,"r":2}]
  Then trigger trg_ap_ladder_sum rejects the write with a message naming the 100% limit

Scenario: A soft-deleted profile frees its name
  Given profile "Scalp" on account A is soft-deleted
  When a new profile named "scalp" is created on account A
  Then it is accepted, because ux_ap_name is a partial index over deleted_at IS NULL

Scenario: Leg snapshot survives a profile edit
  Given a trade-group leg was created from profile version 3
  When the profile is edited to version 4
  Then the leg's profile_snapshot still contains version 3's values, unchanged
```

## Technical notes / design
Profile versioning is implemented as a monotonic `version` column plus an append-only `account_profile_revisions` projection written by the same transaction as the update (id, profile_id, version, payload jsonb, changed_by, changed_at). Revisions are what the journal and `trade_group_legs.profile_snapshot` reconcile against; the live row stays the fast read path. Snapshots are stored as a full frozen copy rather than a version pointer so a hard profile delete can never orphan a historical trade (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.1: "frozen copy - profiles change over time").

`allowed_symbols` and `blocked_symbols` are `text[]`; NULL/empty `allowed_symbols` means "all listed linear USDT perps" (US-PROF-003 scenario "Empty list means all"), and `blocked_symbols` is applied *after* the allow-list. Wildcard patterns (`*USDT`) are stored literally and expanded at evaluation time in E28-T04 against the instrument cache - never expanded at write time, so a newly listed symbol matching the pattern is covered automatically.

Money and quantity columns are `numeric(38,18)`; the ORM maps them to `Decimal` with no float round-trip anywhere. Percentages are `numeric(9,6)` and are stored as the user-visible percent (0..100) in Postgres while the Pydantic `AccountProfile` uses fractions 0..1 (`pct_equity`, `risk_pct_equity` documented as 0..1 in `24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.2) - the mapping happens in exactly one adapter function, `to_domain()`/`to_row()`, and is unit-tested both directions.

Error codes surfaced to callers by the repository layer: `validation_failed` with a `constraint` detail naming the violated CHECK, `conflict` for unique-index violations, `native_stop_mandatory` for `ap_native_sl` specifically (the OpenAPI document names this code for `PUT .../profiles/{profileId}`).

## Test plan
Unit: constraint matrix - one test per CHECK, asserting the exact constraint name in the raised error; sizing-shape matrix over all four `sizing_mode` values x all four size columns; percent/fraction adapter round-trip; soft-delete visibility in every repository read.
Integration: migration up/down/up on a scratch Postgres 16 container; ladder trigger with 0, 1, 5 and over-100 entries; concurrent default-profile insert under two transactions asserting exactly one succeeds.
Property test: random valid `AccountProfile` instances round-trip domain -> row -> domain with `Decimal` equality.
Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/profiles/{risk_based,fixed_qty,pct_equity,fixed_notional}.json` reused by E28-T03 and E28-Q01.
Coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles`.

## Security notes
Asset A-08 (per-account profiles) and A-09 (trade-group configuration) from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` SS4, both classified Confidential with integrity rating 3. Threat **Tampering (O3)**: a profile row whose caps are widened escalates position size on every subsequent order - mitigated here by the database-level CHECKs, which hold even if an application-layer bug lets a bad payload through, and by the append-only revision table that makes a silent edit impossible. Threat **F6**: a leg placed without a native SL because the profile lacked offsets - mitigated by `sl_offset_value > 0 NOT NULL` and `ap_native_sl`. No secret material is stored in these tables; `profile_snapshot` must never embed API-key fields, asserted by a serialisation test.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Profile reads sit on the order path and must be cache-friendly: the repository exposes `get_effective_profile(account_id, profile_id | None)` returning a frozen dataclass, backed by an in-process cache keyed by `(profile_id, version)` and invalidated by the update path. Target: cached read <=50 us, cold read <=2 ms. The whole dataset is at most a few dozen rows in v1 (6 accounts), so index choice matters for `trade_group_legs`, not for profiles.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_profile_rows_total{account}`, `cv_profile_version_bumps_total`, `cv_profile_cache_hit_ratio`.
Audit (written by E28-T02, schema reserved here): `profile.created`, `profile.updated`, `profile.deleted` with full before/after diff.
Logs: migration start/finish with the revision id at INFO; constraint violations logged at WARN with the constraint name, never with the payload.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E27** (the `exchange_accounts` table these rows hang off, plus the account CASCADE semantics) and by **E28-X01** (the STRIDE model, whose findings may add a column or a constraint before the migration is frozen). `trade_group_legs` references `orders`, which **E29** owns; land the FK as nullable and add the constraint in E29's migration if E29's table has not merged yet - the ordering is recorded in the migration's docstring.

## Branch

## References
