title: Ship partial take-profit ladders that resize the stop as legs fill
body:
## Context
`US-ALGO-003` (Should) asks for staged take-profits: "25% at 1R, 25% at 2R and 50% at 3R" becomes three reduce-only orders with quantities rounded to lot size and the remainder assigned to the last leg; when the 1R leg fills the stop quantity adjusts to the remaining position automatically; and when the position is too small to split, the ladder is refused with an explanation and a single-target alternative offered. Its NFR requires ladder state persisted server-side and reconciled after restart.

This is the feature that makes SCR-064's "Take-profit ladder: 25% @ 1R / 25% @ 2R / 50% @ 3R" wireframe real, and it is the reason `tpsl_mode` exists as `partial` in section 8.9 — a multi-leg ladder cannot use Bybit's `Full` mode.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-003`.
- Extends `BracketSupervisor` from E32-S01 with `take_profits: tuple[TakeProfitLeg, ...]` handling (section 10.7).
- Leg specification by percentage of position or absolute quantity, with price expressed as absolute price **or** R-multiple, resolved server-side against the bracket's `initial_stop`.
- Placement policy: legs are placed as reduce-only limit children on the entry's **first fill**, not at bracket creation, so the exchange never holds reduce-only orders against a non-existent position.
- Rounding: each leg floored to `qty_step`; the **remainder goes to the last leg**; legs that round below `min_order_qty` are merged into the adjacent leg; if no viable split exists the ladder is refused with error `LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE` and the response carries a single-target alternative.
- Stop resizing: when a TP leg fills, the native stop quantity is amended down to the remaining position through the shared write path, with `tpsl_mode="partial"`.
- Validation: ladder percentages must sum to <=100% (SCR-064 message "Ladder totals 110% — reduce a step.").
- Persistence and restart reconciliation; audit `position.tp_ladder_set`.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-064 / SCR-069 UI (E32-S07 / E32-S05), scaled **entries** (E32-S03), trailing (E32-S04), emulated OCO racing (E33).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A three-step ladder is placed correctly
  Given a filled long of 1.0 BTC and a ladder of 25% at 1R, 25% at 2R and 50% at 3R
  When the ladder is applied
  Then three reduce-only limit orders are placed with quantities floored to the lot size, the remainder assigned to the last leg so the quantities sum exactly to 1.0 BTC, and an audit row position.tp_ladder_set is written

Scenario: A filled leg resizes the stop
  Given the 1R leg for 0.25 BTC fills
  Then the native stop quantity is amended to 0.75 BTC in a single trading-stop call carrying both sides, and the bracket detail shows the remaining ladder

Scenario: The position is too small to split (error)
  Given a position of 0.003 BTC and a three-step ladder whose smallest leg would be below the minimum order quantity
  When the ladder is requested
  Then it is refused with LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE, the explanation names the instrument minimum and the offending leg, and a single-target alternative at the furthest leg's price is offered

Scenario: Percentages exceed the position (error)
  Given a ladder whose steps total 110%
  Then the request is rejected with a validation error naming the total, and no orders are placed

Scenario: Restart with a partially filled ladder (edge)
  Given the backend restarts after the 1R leg filled and before the stop resize was acknowledged
  When it comes back
  Then ladder state is restored from Postgres, the remaining position is recomputed from executions, the stop resize is re-sent with the original idempotency key, and no duplicate TP order is created

Scenario: Position flattened manually while the ladder rests (edge)
  Given I flatten the position by hand
  Then all resting ladder legs are cancelled as orphans within one 30-second reconciliation cycle with reason "position flat"
```

## Technical notes / design
- R-multiple resolution: `price = avg_entry +/- r * (avg_entry - initial_stop)` signed by side, using the **initial** stop recorded by E32-S01 so later tightening does not shift the ladder.
- `tpsl_mode` selection: exactly one leg covering 100% -> Bybit `Full` attached TP; otherwise `Partial` with reduce-only children (section 8.9 mapping table).
- Merging rule when a leg rounds below the minimum: merge **into the adjacent further leg**, preserving the trader's intent to keep the furthest target largest; record the merge in the response so the UI can show what actually got placed.
- Stop resize uses the same `TrailingTranslator.write_stop()` path as E32-S04/T03 (both sides in one call, ratcheted) — no second write path.
- Every leg carries its own deterministic `order_link_id` derived from `(trade_group_id, leg_index)`.

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=90%):** rounding and remainder assignment across many position sizes and lot steps; merge rule; refusal case; R-multiple resolution for long and short; percentage validation; stop-resize quantity maths.
- **Property test:** for random position sizes and ladder splits, assert placed quantities sum exactly to the position and no leg is below the minimum.
- **Contract:** `TakeProfitLeg` and `LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE` in the OpenAPI surface.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures for leg fill -> stop resize, manual flatten -> orphan cancel, restart mid-ladder.
- **E2E:** via SCR-064 in E32-Q04.

## Security notes
Order placement path — `security` handling per section 8 of the DoR/DoD. Threat: a ladder request with 50 legs used to burn the rate budget so a protective order cannot be placed — mitigated by the ladder leg cap and by `reserved_for_protective` (section 8.7), with ladder traffic tagged `priority="normal"` and never `critical`. All mutations audited.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. Ladder presentation as a real table is specified for SCR-064 in E32-S07.

## Performance notes
Ladder placement is batched; total placement time for a 5-leg ladder must stay inside budget #4's per-request allowance with the batch counted as one request. Stop resize on a leg fill within 500 ms of the execution event.

## Observability
`oms_tp_ladder_legs_total{result}`, `oms_tp_ladder_refused_total{reason}`, `oms_stop_resize_seconds`. Audit `position.tp_ladder_set`, `position.stop_modified{reason=ladder_fill}`.

title: Translate percentage and ATR trailing stops into Bybit price distances
body:
## Context
`US-ALGO-008` (**Must**) wants fixed-distance and percentage trailing stops, using "the native Bybit trailing stop where possible", with percentage trails translated to a price distance and maintained client-side with the translation shown, and app-managed trails restored from the database within 5 seconds of a restart.

The hard constraint is in `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.9: Bybit's `trading-stop.trailingStop` is a **price distance, not a percentage**. Section 10.7's `TrailSpec` adds the binding rule `only_tighten: bool = True  # ratchet — binding, cannot be set False`. And the same section records the trap that one-sided TP/SL modification via `trading-stop` breaks Bybit's OCO pairing, so **both** sides must be written in every call, sending the unchanged side's current value explicitly.

`20-architecture.md` section 9 rule 6 places this translation in the OMS, never in the UI — so that chart drags (E31), the ticket (E30), SCR-064 (E32-S07) and rule-engine trails (E35) all share one implementation and one ratchet.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-008`.
- `services/oms/algos/trailing.py` — `TrailingTranslator` (module M14), owning the **single** `trading-stop` write path for the whole product: `write_stop(position, *, stop=None, take_profit=None, trailing=None, reason, actor)`.
- Translation of `TrailSpec{kind: fixed_ticks|percent|atr|structure|ma, value, atr_period, swing_lookback, activation_r, only_tighten, update_on}` into the Bybit request: `fixed_ticks` and `percent` map to the **native** `trailingStop` distance; `atr`, `structure` and `ma` are computed per bar and pushed as `trading-stop` updates.
- Both-sides write rule enforced structurally: the function always sends the current value of the side it is not changing.
- Ratchet: any write that would loosen the stop is refused, counted and logged; `only_tighten=False` is rejected at the type boundary (it is not settable through the API).
- Activation: `activation_r` arms the trail only after that R-multiple is reached, using the frozen initial stop from E32-S01.
- App-managed trail state persisted per position; on restart, trails resume within **5 seconds** and the gap is logged, per the story's NFR.
- Percentage translation is surfaced: the API response and the `positions` topic carry both the user's unit/value and the resulting absolute distance and trigger price, so the UI can show "1.5% = 958 USDT distance, trigger 62,942".
- Labelling: app-managed (ATR/structure/MA) trails are flagged `managed_by="engine"` on the wire so CMP-227 EstimatedBadge / CMP-158 can render the distinction.

## Out of scope
- ATR/structure/MA **computation rules** authored by users (E35 rule engine supplies the signal; this story supplies the write path and the ratchet), break-even (E32-T03), the SCR-064 UI (E32-S07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A percentage trail becomes a native price distance
  Given a 1.5% trailing stop on a long position at an entry of 63,900
  When the trail is armed
  Then the OMS computes the absolute quote-currency distance, submits it as trailingStop via POST /v5/position/trading-stop in a call that also carries the current take-profit value, and the API response and positions topic report both the 1.5% input and the resulting distance and trigger price

Scenario: A fixed-distance trail uses the native field directly
  Given a 150 USDT trail on a long
  Then the native Bybit trailing stop is used with that distance and the current trigger price is shown, with no engine-managed state required

Scenario: A loosening update is refused (failure)
  Given an armed trail whose recomputed distance would move the stop further from the mark
  When the update is evaluated
  Then the write is refused, oms_stop_loosening_refused_total increments, the existing stop is unchanged, and the refusal is logged with the attempted and current values

Scenario: An app-managed trail survives a restart
  Given an engine-managed ATR trail is running and the backend restarts
  When it comes back
  Then trail state is restored from Postgres, trailing resumes within 5 seconds, the gap duration is logged, and the position's native stop was never removed during the gap

Scenario: A one-sided write is structurally impossible (edge)
  Given any caller updating only the stop-loss side
  When write_stop executes
  Then the request still carries the position's current take-profit value explicitly, so Bybit's TP/SL pairing is preserved, asserted by a test that inspects the outgoing request

Scenario: An explicit user override to loosen is audited (edge)
  Given the user explicitly confirms loosening the stop through the audited override path
  Then the write proceeds, an audit row with reason "user_override_loosen" and the actor is written, and a warning-level log records the previous and new values
```

## Technical notes / design
- `write_stop()` is the single call site of `adapter.set_trading_stop` — enforced by an architecture test mirroring E32-T01's `place_order` test, so no future feature can add a second, unratcheted write path.
- Percent-to-distance conversion uses the **position's average entry** as the reference for the initial distance and the running extreme (highest-high for longs, lowest-low for shorts) for subsequent updates; the reference used is recorded on every update for auditability.
- Rounding: the computed distance is rounded to `tickSize` in the **tightening** direction so rounding can never loosen.
- `update_on="bar_close"` (default) versus `"tick"`: bar-close updates are driven by the bar builder (M7); tick updates are rate-limited to the account's amend budget with `priority="normal"`.
- Engine-managed trails are stored with their spec and last-applied distance so a restart recomputes rather than re-derives from scratch.
- Native versus engine selection is capability-driven (`ExchangeCapabilities.supports_native_trailing`, section 14/10.8) rather than `if exchange == "bybit"`.

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=90%):** percent/ATR/tick conversions for long and short; tightening-direction rounding; ratchet refusal; activation-R gating; both-sides payload construction; restart state restoration.
- **Architecture test:** single call site of `adapter.set_trading_stop`.
- **Property test:** for random sequences of price moves and updates, the stop distance from the extreme is monotonically non-increasing.
- **Contract:** `TrailingStopSpec` in the OpenAPI surface; `positions` payload carrying unit, value, distance, trigger and `managed_by`.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures for trading-stop acceptance, rejection, and the pairing behaviour observed in E32-K01.
- **Chaos:** restart with an engine trail armed (E32-Q05), asserting the 5-second resume.

## Security notes
A bug that loosens a stop is a **P0 safety defect**. Controls: the ratchet is enforced in the single write path, `only_tighten` is not settable to false through any API, the loosening override requires explicit user confirmation and writes an audit row naming the actor, and the architecture test prevents a bypass path from being added. RBAC `positions:write` plus account scope. Security-engineer review required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The requirement that the translation is *shown* is satisfied by the wire contract above and rendered by CMP-120 in E32-S07.

## Performance notes
Translation must add <=1 ms per update. Bar-close updates are naturally rate-limited; tick-mode updates must respect the amend budget and never starve protective traffic (section 8.7).

## Observability
`oms_trailing_updates_total{kind,managed_by}`, `oms_stop_loosening_refused_total{reason}`, `oms_trailing_resume_seconds` (restart gap). Audit `position.stop_modified{reason=trail|user_override_loosen}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated, including the architecture test and the monotonicity property test.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on M14.
- [ ] Schema delta for sections 8.9/10.7 drafted for E32-T04.
- [ ] Security-engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Restart-resume measured at <=5 s.
- [ ] QA sign-off from E32-Q02.
- [ ] Demoed on demo at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E32-T01` (guard and the invariant the ratchet protects), `E29` (adapter, positions stream, persistence). Consumed by `E32-T03` (break-even), `E32-S07` (SCR-064) and later by `E35`.

title: Enforce the native-SL invariant at the single OMS submission choke point
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B8). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The protection region becomes a chart with the B610-OC-CD03 attempt counter; the choke-point guard stays.

## Context
This is the ticket that makes RSK-016 ("an order reaches the exchange without a native stop-loss", `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`) structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged. `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8 states the invariant; `21-database-schema.md` enforces the intent at rest (`account_profiles.require_native_sl` with `CONSTRAINT ap_native_sl CHECK (require_native_sl = true)`); this ticket enforces it in flight.

The design decision — taken in E32-X01's threat model and recorded here — is that the guard lives at **one** function, `OMS.submit()` in M14, through which every submission path already passes (order ticket E30, chart/DOM E31, brackets and ladders E32, emulated algos E33, fan-out legs E34, rule actions E35). Enforcement at call sites was rejected: every new caller would be a new escape hatch, and R3 exit criterion #2 demands zero escapes across paths that do not all exist yet.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/oms/risk/native_sl_guard.py` — `NativeSlGuard` (module **M17**), a pure, synchronous pre-flight evaluated inside `OMS.submit()` before any adapter call.
- Classification helper `is_position_opening(intent, reduce_only, position_state)` — `intent in {entry, scale_in, reverse}` or any non-`reduce_only` order that would increase absolute position size in the target `positionIdx`.
- Three outcomes: **PASS_ATTACHED** (request carries `stopLoss`), **PASS_DEFERRED** (attachment impossible; a `trading-stop` write is scheduled with a 2 s deadline and a `pending_native_sl` row is written transactionally *before* the adapter call), **REJECT** (no stop and no viable deferral) with error code `NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED`.
- Deferral is only permitted for reasons enumerated in a closed allow-list (`algo_child_over_attach`, `batch_ladder_leg`); any other reason rejects. The allow-list is a constant, not configuration.
- `orders.intent`, `trade_group_legs.native_sl_confirmed` / `native_sl_confirmed_at` writes; audit rows on every REJECT and every deferral.
- Wire `oms_invariant_reject_total{path,reason}` and `oms_native_sl_attach_seconds` metrics.
- Kill-switch and risk-cap consultation: the guard calls E39's `RiskGate` first, so a halted system rejects before the invariant question is even asked.
- Feature flag: **none**. The guard is unconditional; there is deliberately no flag that can disable it (recorded as a decision in the body of ADR-0016).
- Implement the `B8` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B08.position_protection.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('position_protection', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/08_position_protection.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_08_position_protection.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
- The watchdog / fallback attach (E32-T02), bracket structure (E32-S01), ladders (E32-S03), trailing translation (E32-S04), any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A position-opening order without a stop is rejected before the adapter
  Given a market buy with intent "entry", reduce_only false and no stopLoss
  When OMS.submit is called
  Then the guard returns REJECT with error code NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED, no request reaches the exchange adapter (asserted by a strict adapter mock that fails the test if called), an audit row is written, and oms_invariant_reject_total{path,reason} increments

Scenario: A reduce-only closing order is allowed without a stop
  Given a reduce-only sell against an existing long
  When OMS.submit is called
  Then the guard classifies it as non-position-opening and passes it through unchanged

Scenario: A deferred attach is persisted before the order is sent
  Given an algo child that cannot carry an attached stopLoss and whose reason is on the allow-list
  When OMS.submit is called
  Then a pending_native_sl row with a 2 s deadline is committed before the adapter call, and if the process dies immediately after the adapter call the restarted process finds that row

Scenario: An unknown deferral reason is rejected, not tolerated (edge)
  Given a caller requests deferral with a reason not on the closed allow-list
  Then the guard returns REJECT, logs at error level with the offending reason, and the caller receives NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED

Scenario: The kill-switch pre-empts the invariant check (failure)
  Given the E39 kill-switch is active
  When any position-opening submission is attempted
  Then RiskGate rejects first with KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE, and the invariant counter is not incremented (so kill-switch activity does not pollute invariant telemetry)

Scenario: Hedge mode is handled per positionIdx (edge)
  Given hedge mode with an existing long on positionIdx 1
  When a buy on positionIdx 1 without a stop is submitted
  Then it is rejected as position-opening; a sell reduce-only on positionIdx 1 passes
```

## Technical notes / design
- Signature: `NativeSlGuard.evaluate(req: PlaceOrderRequest, pos: PositionState | None, profile: AccountProfile) -> GuardVerdict`. Pure function of its inputs; no I/O, so it is exhaustively unit-testable as a truth table.
- `GuardVerdict = Literal["pass_attached","pass_deferred","reject"]` plus `reason: str` and `deadline_ms: int | None`.
- Placement: inside `OMS.submit()`, after idempotency-key resolution and after `RiskGate`, before `adapter.place_order()`. An architecture test asserts `adapter.place_order` has exactly one call site in the codebase (`tests/architecture/test_single_submit_path.py`) — this is what makes "choke point" mechanically true and is a required check.
- Deferral persistence uses the same transaction as the `order_events` write-ahead row from E29, so the sequence is: persist intent -> persist pending attach -> send. Never send first.
- `profile.require_native_sl` is read but cannot be false (DB CHECK); the code still asserts it and raises a configuration error if it is, guarding against a future migration loosening the constraint.
- Error code `NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED` maps to HTTP 422 in `22-api-openapi.yaml` and to a user-facing message defined in E32-D07's handoff pack.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B8.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
- **Unit (target >=95% on this module):** full truth table across intent x reduce_only x position_state x stopLoss present x position mode x deferral reason; hedge/one-way; zero-qty and rounding edges.
- **Architecture test:** single call site of `adapter.place_order` — fails the build otherwise.
- **Integration:** against recorded Bybit demo fixtures, confirm attached-SL orders round-trip and deferred ones create the pending row.
- **Contract:** `NATIVE_SL_REQUIRED` appears in the OpenAPI error enum and the WS `orders` rejection payload.
- **Property test:** for randomly generated submissions, assert the invariant "if the adapter was called with a position-opening request then either stopLoss was present or a pending row exists".
- Coverage gate >=90% for M14/M17.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B8.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
STRIDE (E32-X01): **Tampering** — a client stripping `stopLoss` from the payload is defeated because the guard is server-side and the profile flag cannot be disabled. **Elevation** — a rule-engine action or internal caller attempting to bypass is defeated by the single-call-site architecture test. **Repudiation** — every REJECT and deferral writes an `audit_log` row with actor, account, symbol and reason. **DoS** — the guard is pure and O(1); it cannot be made slow by input. Data classification: financial/transactional. Requires Security-engineer review before merge (label `security`).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend only. The user-facing rejection copy is specified in E32-D07 and consumed by E30/E32 UI stories.

## Performance notes
The guard must add <=1 ms p99 to `OMS.submit`, inside budget #4's <=50 ms backend-added allowance (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2). Asserted by a micro-benchmark in CI.

## Observability
`oms_invariant_reject_total{path,reason}`, `oms_native_sl_attach_seconds{mode=attached|deferred}`, `oms_native_sl_deferred_pending` gauge. Audit events `oms.native_sl_rejected`, `oms.native_sl_deferred`. Structured logs carry `order_link_id`, `trade_group_id`, `account_id`, `reason`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by the unit truth table, the architecture test and the property test.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on M14/M17; the guard module itself >=95%.
- [ ] `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8 annotated with the implemented verdict model (final wording lands in E32-T04).
- [ ] SAST/SCA clean; Security-engineer review comment present; abuse-case check from E32-X02 passes.
- [ ] Micro-benchmark recorded (<=1 ms p99).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (verification via E32-Q01's suite).
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals including an OMS code-owner and the Security engineer.
- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.

## Dependencies
`E32-K01` (attach-vs-deferral latency evidence sets the deadline), `E32-X01` (threat model defines the enforcement point), `E29` (`OMS.submit`, order state machine, idempotency), `E39` (`RiskGate`, kill-switch), `E28` (`AccountProfile`).

## Branch
`feat/e32-native-sl-guard`. Ships as its own PR, no other change bundled.

title: Build the unprotected-position watchdog with fallback attach and alert
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B8). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The watchdog is a chart state plus a coarse `after:`.

## Context
E32-T01 prevents unprotected orders from being *sent*. It cannot prevent a position becoming unprotected *afterwards*: a deferred attach can fail, the process can die between fill and attach, a user can cancel a stop directly on the Bybit app, or the exchange can drop a conditional order. `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8 rule 3 mandates the second line of defence — a watchdog scanning every open position every 5 s, raising a `critical` alert and auto-attaching a fallback stop for any position unprotected for >10 s. `21-database-schema.md` provisions the query: partial index `ix_tgl_no_sl ON trade_group_legs (trade_group_id) WHERE status IN ('open','partially_filled') AND native_sl_confirmed = false`, budgeted at <2 ms in the schema's access-pattern table (row 10, "safety monitor").

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/oms/risk/sl_watchdog.py` — `UnprotectedPositionWatchdog` (module **M17**), an asyncio task started with the OMS.
- 5 s scan over open positions joined to `trade_group_legs` via `ix_tgl_no_sl`, plus a cross-check against the reconciler's exchange-truth snapshot from E29 so a position unknown to our DB is still caught.
- Deferred-attach deadline enforcement: `pending_native_sl` rows past their 2 s deadline are retried immediately (up to 3 attempts with 250 ms backoff) using `priority="critical"` so they draw on `RateBudget.reserved_for_protective` (section 8.7).
- Fallback attach at `profile.fallback_sl_offset` (default: the tighter of 2% and 3x ATR(14)) via `POST /v5/position/trading-stop`, writing **both** TP and SL sides in one call per the section 8.9 pairing caveat.
- `NakedPositionAlert` (severity `critical`) emitted on the `system` WS topic and through E40's delivery once available; degrades to log + metric if E40 is not yet deployed.
- Sets `native_sl_confirmed` / `native_sl_confirmed_at` on success; audit event `oms.native_sl_fallback_attached`.
- Escalation: if three fallback attempts fail, the watchdog raises `NakedPositionAlert` at `critical` **and** requests E39's account-level lockout for new entries on that account (never an automatic flatten — flattening is a documented manual runbook).
- Implement the `B8` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B08.position_protection.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('position_protection', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/08_position_protection.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_08_position_protection.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
- Auto-flattening positions (explicitly forbidden — the kill-switch semantics in E39 are "stops new risk, does not force-close").
- The alert delivery channels themselves (E40); the risk lockout mechanism itself (E39).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A position that loses its stop is re-protected
  Given an open position whose native stop is cancelled out of band
  When the next 5-second scan runs
  Then within 10 seconds of the stop disappearing a fallback stop at profile.fallback_sl_offset is attached, native_sl_confirmed is set true, an audit row is written and a critical NakedPositionAlert is raised

Scenario: A missed deferred attach is retried before the watchdog interval
  Given a pending_native_sl row whose 2-second deadline has passed
  When the watchdog next runs
  Then the attach is retried immediately with priority critical drawing on the protective reserve, and succeeds or escalates within three attempts

Scenario: Repeated failure escalates rather than loops (failure)
  Given three consecutive fallback attach attempts fail with exchange 5xx
  Then the watchdog stops retrying, raises a critical alert naming the account, symbol and exposure, requests an E39 new-entry lockout for that account, and never attempts to flatten the position automatically

Scenario: A position unknown to our database is still caught (edge)
  Given the exchange reports an open position that has no matching trade_group_leg row
  When the scan cross-checks the reconciler snapshot
  Then the position is treated as unprotected until proven otherwise, adopted into the DB, and protected

Scenario: The scan stays within its query budget (edge)
  Given 500 open legs across 5 accounts
  When the scan runs
  Then the ix_tgl_no_sl query executes in under 2 ms as specified in 21-database-schema.md and the scan completes within one 5-second interval with margin
```

## Technical notes / design
- Config keys: `OmsConfig.native_sl_deadline_ms = 2000`, `native_sl_watchdog_interval_s = 5`, `native_sl_alert_after_s = 10`, `native_sl_fallback_max_attempts = 3` (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 16 configuration).
- The scan is idempotent and single-flight per account: a mutex per `exchange_account_id` prevents two overlapping scans double-attaching after a slow exchange response.
- Fallback offset is computed from the *entry/avg* price, not the current mark, so a fast adverse move cannot produce a stop on the wrong side; if the computed stop would already be through the mark, the watchdog attaches at the nearest permitted tick and flags the alert as `already_through_mark`.
- ATR(14) is read from the bar-builder cache (M7); if unavailable, the 2% branch is used and the degradation is logged — the watchdog must never block on market data.
- Ordering guarantee: the watchdog never runs on an account while an unwind plan (E34) is `running`, to avoid fighting the unwinder.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B8.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** offset computation (both branches, already-through-mark), retry/backoff, escalation after 3 failures, single-flight mutex, ATR-unavailable degradation.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures for out-of-band stop cancellation, exchange 5xx on trading-stop, unknown-position adoption.
- **Chaos (E32-Q05 hosts the scenarios, this ticket provides hooks):** kill the process between fill and attach; assert re-protection within 10 s of restart.
- **Perf:** benchmark the scan at 500 open legs asserting <2 ms query time and <5 s total scan.
- Coverage >=90% on M17.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B8.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
STRIDE: **Denial of service** — a flood of unprotected positions could exhaust the rate budget; mitigated by the protective reserve and by per-account single-flight. **Repudiation** — every fallback attach and every escalation writes an audit row. **Information disclosure** — alerts name account IDs and sizes, so `NakedPositionAlert` payloads are RBAC-filtered on the `system` topic per `23-ws-protocol.md`. Security-engineer review required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A backend; the alert's UI presentation is covered by E40 and by CMP-158 usage in E32-S05/S06/S07.

## Performance notes
Scan query <2 ms (`21-database-schema.md` access-pattern row 10); full scan cycle well inside the 5 s interval at the R3 capacity target of 5 accounts x 10 symbols. Fallback attach latency counted against budget #4's protective window.

## Observability
Metrics `oms_native_sl_missing_total{account}`, `oms_native_sl_fallback_total{result}`, `oms_sl_watchdog_scan_seconds`, gauge `oms_positions_unprotected`. Alert rule `NakedPositionAlert` (critical, page). Audit `oms.native_sl_fallback_attached`, `oms.native_sl_escalated`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance scenarios covered by automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on M17.
- [ ] Grafana panel and alert rule committed alongside the code.
- [ ] Security-engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Perf benchmark recorded at 500 legs.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.
- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.

## Dependencies
`E32-T01` (pending-attach rows and verdict model), `E29` (reconciler snapshot), `E28` (`fallback_sl_offset`), `E39` (lockout request API), `E40` (alert delivery — degrades gracefully if not yet available).

title: Produce the STRIDE threat model for brackets, ladders and the SL invariant
body:
## Context
`04-security-program.md` mandates a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1 makes it default-on for any epic touching the OMS or the fan-out safety invariant. E32 is the epic that *owns* that invariant, so its threat model is not a formality: it decides where enforcement lives, and that decision is an input to E32-T01 rather than a review of it. This ticket therefore runs **before** the guard is built.

R3's security gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) requires all Critical/High findings closed before the train closes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE model published as `docs/security/threat-models/e32-brackets-native-sl.md`.
- Data-flow diagram covering: client -> API -> `OMS.submit` -> `NativeSlGuard` -> exchange adapter -> Bybit; plus the watchdog loop, the `trading-stop` write path, the batch ladder path and the rule-engine entry point.
- Trust boundaries marked explicitly, including the boundary between our backend and Bybit (we control neither the venue's availability nor its acknowledgement semantics).
- Per-element STRIDE enumeration with at least: **Spoofing** — a caller acting for an account it does not own; **Tampering** — payload manipulation to strip or widen a stop, or to submit a preview different from what was priced; **Repudiation** — a stop loosened with no attributable audit row; **Information disclosure** — alerts and diagnostics leaking account identifiers or sizes across RBAC boundaries; **Denial of service** — a 50-level ladder exhausting the per-UID budget so a protective order cannot be placed; **Elevation of privilege** — a viewer-role session mutating protective state, or an internal caller bypassing the choke point.
- A ranked findings table with likelihood, impact, and a required control for each Critical/High.
- The explicit architectural recommendation on enforcement placement (single choke point versus per-call-site) with its rationale, handed to E32-T01.
- Abuse cases derived from the model, handed to E32-X02 as its input list.
- Update to `32-risk-register.md` RSK-016 with the modelled attack paths.

## Out of scope
- Implementing controls (the engineering tickets), penetration testing (E43), key management (E27's model).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element and boundary is enumerated
  Given the data-flow diagram
  When STRIDE is applied
  Then every element and trust boundary has all six categories considered, with either a finding or an explicit "not applicable" and a reason

Scenario: Enforcement placement is decided with rationale
  Given the choice between a single choke point and per-call-site checks
  Then the model records the decision, the rejected alternative and why, and E32-T01 cites it

Scenario: Critical and High findings carry required controls
  Given the ranked findings table
  Then each Critical or High finding names a specific control, the ticket that will implement it, and the test that will verify it

Scenario: An unmitigatable finding is escalated (edge)
  Given a finding that cannot be fully mitigated, such as venue-side acknowledgement loss
  Then it is recorded as an accepted risk with the Owner's sign-off and a detection control, rather than being downgraded to make the table look clean
```

## Technical notes / design
The model must address the specific asymmetry that makes this epic dangerous: a native stop is the only protection that survives our backend dying, so every finding is evaluated against the question "does this leave a position protected only by something we control?"

## Test plan
N/A — analysis. Verification: review session with the Architect, the OMS lead and the Owner; every finding must have an owner and a target ticket before the model is accepted.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security analysis. The published model is an internal-confidential document; it is stored in the restricted security space and referenced, not inlined, from public tickets.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The DoS findings explicitly consider the rate-budget interaction, so the protective reserve's sizing is a security control as well as a performance one.

## Observability
The model specifies which findings require a detection control (alert or audit event) rather than only a preventive one — these become E32-T02's and E32-T01's observability requirements.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Model published with the DFD, full STRIDE enumeration and ranked findings.
- [ ] Enforcement-placement recommendation delivered to E32-T01 before it starts.
- [ ] Abuse-case list handed to E32-X02.
- [ ] All Critical/High findings assigned to a ticket with a verifying test.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` RSK-016 updated.
- [ ] Review session held; Architect and Owner sign-off recorded.

`E29` (the OMS design being modelled).

title: Wireframe to hi-fi: TWAP, iceberg and chase builders (SCR-066, 067, 068)
body:
## Context
Three of the four builders are parameter-heavy modals whose screens-catalogue entries already fix their content, validation messages and states (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-066, SCR-067, SCR-068). This ticket takes them from wireframe to hi-fi in Figma using the E33-D01 findings and the recommended defaults, and produces the state coverage each entry's sign-off checklist demands.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-066 TWAP builder**: total qty, duration, slice count/interval, price limit (max slippage), randomisation, participation cap, limit-vs-market slices, price-band guard, disconnect behaviour; a **schedule preview table** (slice #, planned time, qty); states configured · running (progress, filled/remaining, average price, slices done) · paused (auto-paused on disconnect, with the banner) · degraded · completed · cancelled · failed; the "algo pauses if the backend disconnects; native stops still protect" message; cancel and cancel-and-flatten paths with confirmation.
- **SCR-067 Iceberg builder**: total qty, visible qty, refresh behaviour, price offset/peg, max show-ratio; "emulated client-side — Bybit has no native iceberg" stated prominently; **projected request rate** shown; running state with slices done/remaining; residual-risk note if the backend stops mid-algo; the validation messages drawn verbatim ("Visible size must be at least the minimum lot and no more than half the total.").
- **SCR-068 Chase-limit builder**: peg source as a radio group (best bid / best ask / mid) plus a signed tick offset with the resulting price previewed in text; re-peg threshold; max chase distance from the arrival price; max repricings; **fall-back-to-market as opt-in with its slippage risk stated**; timeout; the rate-limit estimate ("≈ 12 requests/min — within your per-account budget") and the refusal state when a configuration exceeds the budget; states running (current peg, repricings used, distance travelled) · limit reached · fell back to market · cancelled.
- Shared **`AlgoBuilderShell`** pattern drawn once: title, emulation notice, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, projected-rate chip (CMP-130), validation summary, submit/cancel — so honesty affordances are structural, not per-screen discipline.
- Light and dark, both densities, at the reference 4 K and 1 080 p displays.
- Redlines for spacing, type, tokens and every validation message, plus a state matrix per screen.

## Out of scope
SCR-069 OCO builder and SCR-070 monitor (D03). Motion (D04). A11y annotation (D05 — though obvious issues are fixed here). Scaled/ladder builder SCR-065 (E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state in the catalogue is drawn
  Given the sign-off checklists in 14-screens-catalogue.md for SCR-066, SCR-067 and SCR-068
  Then every checklist item has a corresponding frame, and the checklist is ticked in the ticket

Scenario: Emulation and residual risk are structural
  Given any of the three builders
  Then the emulation caveat and the native-stop floor appear as persistent text blocks in the
  shared shell rather than as per-screen tooltips, in every state including running and failed

Scenario: Validation messages are exact (edge)
  Given the validation rules in the catalogue entries
  Then each message is drawn with the exact wording engineering must implement,
  including the numeric interpolation points

Scenario: Budget refusal is designed, not an afterthought (edge)
  Given a chase configuration projected to exceed the account rate budget
  Then a refusal state is drawn that names the projected and the allowed rate and offers the
  nearest acceptable configuration
```

## Technical notes / design
Use only existing catalogue components (CMP-008, 043, 047, 100, 101, 118, 130, 158, 227); any new pattern goes through E33-D04 as a design-system contribution rather than a one-off. Numbers shown in examples must be plausible BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT values honouring real `tickSize`/`qtyStep`.

## Test plan
Design review with the OMS tech lead to confirm every parameter maps to a real field of `AlgoSpec` (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) and `24-internal-schemas.md` §10.3–§10.5 — a drawn control with no backing field is a defect found here, not in code review.

## Security notes
The designs must not invite unsafe configuration: fall-back-to-market is opt-in, max-chase-distance has no "unlimited" affordance, and slice counts are bounded by the drawn validation. The arm/lock and confirmation policy from E30 are shown, not re-invented.

## Accessibility notes
Contrast AA on all states incl. degraded; focus order drawn; every field labelled with units; the emulation caveat is body text, not a tooltip; the peg selector is a radio group, not a segmented control that traps screen readers. Full annotation lands in D05.

## Performance notes
Designs must respect the 2 Hz progress-update cadence (no animation implying sub-second precision) — see SCR-066's performance note.

## Observability
The analytics events `algo.twap_previewed` and `algo.iceberg_previewed` are attached to the drawn preview affordances so instrumentation is specified at design time.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma file complete: wireframes → hi-fi, all states, light/dark, both densities.
- [ ] Every catalogue sign-off checklist item ticked with a linked frame.

title: Hi-fi: OCO builder (SCR-069) and algo monitor panel (SCR-070)
body:
## Context
SCR-069 and SCR-070 are the two screens where emulation stops being a configuration detail and becomes a risk conversation. The OCO builder must explain **race resolution** and what happens if the app is offline when a leg fills; the monitor panel is the single place that discharges US-ALGO-010's promise that "nothing runs invisibly", including the degraded state in which algos are suspended and only native stops protect.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-069 Emulated OCO / bracket builder** — the **OCO half** (E32 owns the bracket half of the same modal, and this design must compose with it):
  - Both variants drawn: entry + OCO exit pair, and a standalone OCO on an existing position.
  - "Emulated — Bybit's API has no OCO" stated prominently as text.
  - Race-resolution behaviour explained as a paragraph (the losing leg is cancelled/reduced on the fill notice).
  - **Residual-risk state** drawn: app offline during a fill — what happened and what the user must do.
  - The mandatory native SL floor shown as always present and non-removable.
  - The "use native attached TP/SL instead" guidance for the plain TP+SL case, including the refusal state.
  - Validation messages: legs on opposite sides of the mark; quantities matching the position.
- **SCR-070 Algo monitor panel** (standalone panel and the Algos tab of SCR-063):
  - Table with id, type, symbol, account, type-specific progress, filled/remaining, average price, next-action countdown, controls.
  - Every algo type rendered with its own progress metric (TWAP slices, chase repricings + distance, iceberg slices, OCO leg states).
  - Rows for running · paused · degraded · completed · failed-with-reason · **halted by risk control** · orphaned (with adopt/cancel).
  - Bulk "pause all" and "cancel all" with a confirmation restating the count, and the per-item result view.
  - The degraded banner explaining suspension during backend reconnection and that native stops still protect.
  - Empty state; filter bar (account / symbol / kind / status); "last reconciled" indicator.
  - A 100-row density frame proving the layout at scale.
- Redlines, state matrix, and the exact copy for every banner and confirmation.

## Out of scope
SCR-066/067/068 (D02). Motion (D04). A11y annotation (D05). The bracket half of SCR-069 and SCR-063's other tabs (E32/E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Catalogue checklists satisfied
  Given the sign-off checklists for SCR-069 and SCR-070
  Then every item has a linked frame and is ticked in the ticket

Scenario: Residual risk is explicit
  Given the OCO builder
  Then the offline-during-fill residual-risk state is drawn as a persistent note with a clear
  statement of what the user must do, not as a transient toast

Scenario: Nothing runs invisibly
  Given the monitor panel with one algo of each kind plus one orphan
  Then each row communicates its type-specific progress and next action, the orphan offers
  adopt and cancel, and the last-reconciled time is visible

Scenario: Degraded state (failure)
  Given the backend is reconnecting
  Then a status banner explains that algos are suspended and native stops still protect,
  rows are visibly stale, and controls that cannot be honoured are drawn disabled with a reason

Scenario: Bulk action safety (edge)
  Given 40 running algos and a cancel-all action
  Then the confirmation restates the count and the consequence per algo type,
  and the per-item result view is drawn including partial failure
```

## Technical notes / design
Components: CMP-023, CMP-043, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-100, CMP-101, CMP-118, CMP-119, CMP-123, CMP-158, CMP-227. Progress must be expressible as text, so the design cannot depend on a bar alone. Countdowns are drawn at 1 s granularity consistent with a single shared ticker.

## Test plan
Review with the OMS tech lead to confirm every drawn field exists in the `AlgoRun` projection (E33-T02) and every control maps to a real verb (pause / resume / cancel / cancel-and-flatten / adopt / cancel-orphan).

## Security notes
Destructive bulk actions need confirmations proportionate to their blast radius, and `viewer` variants are drawn with controls **absent** rather than disabled-with-tooltip, so the UI does not advertise capabilities the role lacks. The adopt action is drawn as the deliberate, owner/manager-only action it is.

## Accessibility notes
The monitor is a real table with headers; progress text-first; the degraded banner is `role="status"`; each control's accessible name includes its target algo and effect; the OCO residual-risk warning is `role="note"` and always visible. Bulk confirmations are `role="alertdialog"` restating counts. Full annotation in D05.

## Performance notes
The 100-row frame must be achievable inside SCR-070's 3 ms-per-frame scripting budget: virtualised rows, no per-row timers, no per-row animation.

## Observability
Audit events per control are annotated on the frames (`algo.cancelled`, `algo.paused`, `algo.orphan_adopted`), satisfying the catalogue checklist item "every control confirmed to emit an audit event".

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma complete: both screens, every state, light/dark, both densities, 100-row density frame.
- [ ] Catalogue checklists ticked with linked frames.
- [ ] Redlines, state matrix and exact copy published.
- [ ] Reviewed by the OMS tech lead for projection/verb feasibility.

title: Trade-group fan-out & rate-limit governor
body:
## Context
R3 closes the execution loop on Bybit demo. E27 supplies accounts and the key vault, E28 the per-account profiles and the trade-group definition, E29 the OMS and its order state machine, E32 brackets and the native-SL invariant, E39 the risk caps and kill-switch. **E34 is the multi-account execution primitive that sits on top of all of them**: one intent → N per-account legs, each sized and protected by *that account's own* profile, submitted in parallel against *N independent per-UID rate-limit budgets*, and tracked as one logical trade.

This is owner decision #5 (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Locked decisions — "one ticket → fan-out to N accounts as a trade group"); the normative design lives in `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md`, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §4.3 and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §9.

Two properties make this epic uniquely dangerous and drive its whole shape:
1. **Bybit rate limits are per-UID, shared across keys.** N accounts genuinely have N budgets, but the per-IP budget (600 req/5 s) is shared. A fan-out that discovers exhaustion mid-loop leaves a group half-placed with undefined semantics, so admission control must precede placement (`20-architecture.md` §4.3).
2. **Partial failure is normal, not exceptional.** A fan-out where some legs fill and some fail must raise a P0-visible reconciliation state with a one-click unwind of the successful legs — never a silent half-executed trade group (roadmap §7.2 E34 row).

Every leg carries a native exchange-side stop-loss (architecture principle P4, `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.8). This epic contains no code path that can open a leg without one.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories**
- **US-PROF-006** Fan-out an order to a trade group (Must) — the epic's core.
- **US-PROF-007** Trade-group lifecycle view (Must) — aggregate view, group actions, divergence detection.
- **US-PROF-008** Per-trade profile overrides (Should) — per-leg overrides inside the fan-out ticket (the profile schema itself is E28).
- **US-ORD-013** Mandatory native stop-loss (Must) — the fan-out path's share of the invariant; the enforcement engine is E32/M17, this epic proves no leg escapes it.
- **US-ORD-010** Flatten and cancel-all (Must) — the *group* variants ("flatten group", "close group 50%"); the single-account variant is E31.
- **US-ORD-014** Pre-trade risk preview (Should) — the *group* aggregation of the preview; the single-account preview is E30.

US-PROF-001..005 (profile schema, sizing rules, allowed symbols, server-side risk caps, group definition) belong to **E28** and are consumed here, never re-implemented.

**Screens:** SCR-061 Trade-group ticket (multi-account fan-out), SCR-062 Trade-group manager, SCR-063 Positions & orders grid (Trade groups tab additions only).

**Components:** CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-106 ProfileBadge, CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-049 Table, CMP-041 Menu, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-107 OrderTicket (host), CMP-100/101/102/231.

**API:** `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups`, `GET /api/v1/trade-groups`, `GET /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/amend`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/cancel`.

**WS:** topic `trade_groups` (`TradeGroupUpdate`, 100 ms coalescing, filters `exchange_account_ids`/`status`, scope `orders:read` on granted accounts).

**DB:** `trade_groups`, `trade_group_legs`, `orders`, `executions`, `positions`, `system_events`, `audit_log`, plus new `unwind_plans` / `unwind_steps` tables for the restartable compensating unwind of `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5.1.

**Architecture modules:** M4 (Bybit adapter `RestClient` — per-UID token bucket, `X-Bapi-Limit-*` feedback), M13 (accounts & profiles), M14 (OMS — `TradeGroupFanout`, `AccountRateBudget`, `UnwindResumer`).

## Out of scope
- Profile schema, sizing algorithm, allowed-symbol validation, server-side risk caps, trade-group *definition* CRUD → **E28**.
- Order state machine, `orderLinkId` idempotency, reconciliation loop, order/position blotters → **E29**.
- Single-account order ticket UI → **E30**; chart/DOM direct manipulation → **E31**.
- Bracket/scaled child-order construction and the native-SL enforcement engine itself → **E32**; emulated OCO/iceberg/TWAP/chase → **E33**.
- Kill-switch and risk-cap engines → **E39**. Journal aggregation of closed groups → **E41**.
- Live-environment enablement → R4 / **E44**. Android, a separate admin app, and non-USDT-perp instruments are out of scope for the whole plan.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One ticket, five accounts, five protected legs
  Given trade group "Core5" contains five ready demo accounts with distinct profiles
  When the owner submits a market buy on BTCUSDT with a bracket against the group
  Then five legs are created, each sized by its own profile and each carrying a native exchange-side stop-loss
  And all five share one trade_group_id, are acknowledged within 1.5 s p95, and each leg is audited individually

Scenario: Two of five legs fail
  Given fault injection rejects the submissions for accounts C and D
  When the fan-out wave quiesces
  Then the group is partially_open, C and D show the exchange reason code and message, and a critical alert fires
  And the owner is offered "retry failed legs" and "unwind successful legs", each idempotent and audited

Scenario: The rate budget is the binding constraint
  Given account B's entry bucket is exhausted and atomicity is best_effort
  When the group is submitted
  Then A, C, D and E are sent immediately, B is Deferred with a visible deadline, and no request is dropped silently
  And with atomicity all_or_none nothing is sent at all and the response names the starved account and its refill ETA

Scenario: Crash mid-unwind
  Given an all_or_none unwind plan is running across three accounts and the backend is killed
  When the backend restarts
  Then UnwindResumer resumes the persisted plan before the OMS accepts new orders, skipping steps already done
  And every residual position still carries its native stop-loss
```

## Technical notes / design
Normative sources, in force verbatim: `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.7 (rate budgeting), §8.8 (native SL), §9.1–§9.6 (group model, per-account profile, sizing, fan-out algorithm, failure policy, unwind, lifecycle) and `20-architecture.md` §4.3 (three-bucket split, pre-flight reservation, deferred drain, partial-failure matrix, metrics). Where the two documents name the same policy differently (`atomic` vs `all_or_none`, `PartiallyAdmitted` vs `partially_open`), the **OpenAPI enum in `22-api-openapi.yaml` wins** and E34-T03 reconciles the prose.

Module boundaries: M14 owns `TradeGroupFanout`, `AccountRateBudget` and `UnwindResumer`; M4's `RestClient` owns the token bucket's header feedback and the `10018` IP-wide back-off; M13 supplies frozen `profile_snapshot` values at fan-out time. Modules talk over the internal bus only (principle P7).

## Test plan
Per-ticket plans live on E34-Q01..Q06. Epic-level gates that must be green at the R3 PRR: the fan-out E2E suite (Playwright web + Electron), the k6 per-UID sustained-flow profile (1 h, 5 accounts, zero lost acks), the three chaos scenarios (WS kill mid-fan-out, backend restart mid-unwind, Postgres failover mid-fan-out), the axe + manual screen-reader pass on SCR-061/062, and the native-SL-escape suite's fan-out cases (zero escapes).

## Exit criteria
1. A single ticket targeting 5 demo accounts produces 5 correctly-sized orders under each account's own profile, each with a native SL, inside the per-UID budget, backend-added overhead ≤50 ms + ≤10 ms/account, group ack ≤1.5 s p95 (roadmap §7.3 #3, budget #4).
2. A fault-injection test failing 2 of 5 legs produces a visible reconciliation state, a correct one-click unwind, an audit trail and an alert (roadmap §7.3 #4).
3. No path in this epic can open a leg without a native SL; the invariant suite's fan-out cases show zero escapes (roadmap §7.3 #2).
4. k6 sustains order flow at the per-UID limit across 5 accounts for 1 h with zero lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off; an injected `10018` produces an IP-wide back-off, never a silently dropped request.
5. Chaos: backend restart mid-fan-out and Postgres failover mid-unwind both resume to a correct, reconciled state with every residual position protected.
6. SCR-061/SCR-062 pass axe-core and a manual screen-reader pass; the partial-failure summary is announced via `role="alert"`.
7. STRIDE model finalized with all Critical/High closed; a Manager fanning out to an out-of-scope account receives 403, an audit row, and no adapter call is made.

## Risks

| **R3 Real-time cost** — rate-limit exhaustion under fan-out | Three-bucket per-UID governor with a reserved `critical` slice; pre-flight reservation across all UIDs; K01 measures the real per-endpoint numbers before the governor is finalized. |

## Security notes
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 every ticket in this epic is treated as `security`-labelled: it touches `area/oms-execution` order placement and the fan-out safety invariant. Threats from `04-security-program.md` / STRIDE (E34-X01): **Spoofing** — a forged `arm_token` or replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; **Tampering** — client-supplied per-leg sizing overriding server-resolved sizing; **Repudiation** — a fan-out without a per-leg audit row; **Information disclosure** — another user's account labels/balances leaking through the group response or the `trade_groups` WS topic; **Denial of service** — a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; **Elevation of privilege** — a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`. Controls: server-side resolution of every leg parameter, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` enforced before any adapter call, required idempotency key, the reserved `critical` rate bucket, and an `audit_log` row per leg. Data classification: financial/execution data and account scope; API secrets are never handled here (they stay in the M2 vault) — only referenced by account id.

## Accessibility notes

## Performance notes

Group ack ≤1.5 s p95 for 5 accounts (ADR-0008 validation gate S4). `oms_fanout_skew_seconds` p99 ≤1.5 s. SCR-062 grid stays under 4 ms scripting per frame with 50 open groups × 5 legs.

Audit actions: `trade_group.submit`, `trade_group.unwound`, `positions.flatten`. `system_events` rows of kind `rate_limit` on every `10018`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The seven epic-level exit criteria above are verified end to end, not merely per child.

title: UX research: how an owner reasons about a multi-account fan-out and its partial failure
body:
## Context
SCR-061 (trade-group ticket) and SCR-062 (trade-group manager) are the two screens E34 introduces. Both are new interaction territory: no prior screen in the product asks a user to reason about *N simultaneous executions with different sizes on different accounts*, and both have a failure state — a partially-executed fan-out — that `14-screens-catalogue.md` requires to be **"drawn as the primary design case, not an afterthought"**.

The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence) applies: no frontend work on E34-S04/S05 (Sprint 19) starts until the design tickets are Status=Done, and they must have been Done for ≥2 sprints.

Fan-out is the one place in the product where a single click commits capital on several accounts at once, and where "it half-worked" is an expected outcome rather than an incident. Before drawing anything we need to know how the owner and the account managers actually think about the group: as one trade, or as N trades that happen to be issued together? The answer decides whether SCR-061's primary object is the aggregate or the per-account row, and whether a partial failure reads as "the trade is damaged" or "three of my trades are fine and two need attention".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Semi-structured sessions with the Owner and the account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`), 45 min each, covering: mental model of the group, tolerance for asymmetry between accounts, what they would do first on a partial failure, and what "unwind" should mean to them.
- A concept test using the existing SCR-061 ASCII wireframe in `14-screens-catalogue.md` plus two alternative framings (aggregate-first vs per-account-first) — measure comprehension of "2 of 3 accepted" and of the three recovery actions.
- A decision test on recovery-action wording: **Retry failed** / **Unwind accepted** / **Leave as is** vs alternatives — the current catalogue copy says "Flatten accepted", and `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5.1 calls the operation an *unwind*; the vocabulary must be settled here, once, and then used identically in UI, API errors, alerts and the journal.
- A findings deck plus a one-page "design principles for fan-out" note that D02/D03 are held against, and any resulting update to `10-personas.md` / `13-user-flows.md` F5.
- Explicit answer to four questions: (1) aggregate-first or per-account-first? (2) is per-row override an expected affordance or a trap? (3) how much rate-limit detail does the user want to see (a chip, a countdown, or nothing)? (4) should "close group 50%" mean 50% of each leg or 50% of the aggregate?

## Out of scope
- Any hi-fi visual work → D02/D03. Usability testing of built software → E34-Q06.
- Research on the single-account ticket (E30's research covers it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The four questions are answered with evidence
  Given at least three sessions with the Owner and manager personas
  When the findings are written up
  Then each of the four framing questions has a recommendation with the supporting observations cited

Scenario: Partial-failure comprehension is measured
  Given participants are shown a 2-of-3 partial failure
  Then the proportion who correctly state what happened and what each recovery action would do is recorded
  And any action whose meaning is misread by more than one participant is re-worded and re-tested before the research closes

Scenario: One vocabulary is chosen
  Then a single term for each recovery operation is recorded and adopted by D02, D03, the API error copy and the alert copy
```

## Technical notes / design
Recruit from the actual users (this is a private, single-owner product; the "user base" is the Owner plus a few managers, so n is small by construction — depth over sample size). Sessions recorded with consent; recordings stored in the team drive, not the repo.

## Test plan
N/A as software testing. Research quality bar: two researchers independently code the sessions and reconcile; findings that only one observed are marked as weak signal.

## Security notes
Sessions must not surface real API keys, account ids or balances — use the standard demo fixture data. Recordings contain the Owner's trading opinions and are treated as confidential; no recording leaves the team drive. Data classification: confidential, non-PII beyond participant identity.

## Accessibility notes
At least one session must include an assistive-technology scenario walkthrough (keyboard-only, screen reader) so the a11y constraints on SCR-061 are informed by intent, not retrofitted at D04.

## Performance notes
Findings must include the users' *tolerated* latency for the preview and for group ack — used to sanity-check the 300 ms / 1.5 s budgets from the user's side rather than only the engineering side.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts published in Figma, linked on this ticket, and the matching `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated to match.
- [ ] Every state from the screen-catalogue entry drawn: previewing, ready, partial-send in progress, partial failure, rate-limit backoff, blocked (account in lockout), empty, loading, error.
- [ ] The screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `14-screens-catalogue.md` ticked item-by-item by the CDO or delegate, recorded as a comment.
- [ ] a11y annotations present: focus order, roles, live-region usage, contrast tokens, ≥24 px hit targets, text equivalents for every colour-coded state.
- [ ] Status=Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming FE story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).
- [ ] Handoff walkthrough held with the implementing FE engineer and recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] Design tokens used are existing `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens, or a design-system contribution ticket is filed for any new one.

- [ ] Findings deck linked from both D02 and D03 and referenced in their design rationale.
- [ ] Vocabulary decision recorded and adopted by the API error copy (a comment on E34-S03).

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28** — the per-account profile concepts (sizing rule, caps, allowed symbols) must be settled before we can research how users reason about differences *between* accounts.

## Branch
`design/e34-fanout-research` (research artefacts + docs updates only).

Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:

Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.

title: Wireframe to hi-fi: rule simulation panel SCR-084 and arming dialog SCR-085
body:
## Context
SCR-084 and SCR-085 are the two screens that gate a rule's promotion from draft to trading, and E35-D01's research establishes what users must understand before that promotion is safe. This ticket takes them from wireframe to signed-off hi-fi, two sprints ahead of the consuming story E35-S08 (Sprint 17) per the design-ahead rule.

Both screens have ASCII wireframes and complete sign-off checklists already in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`; those checklists are the acceptance criteria for this ticket, not a starting suggestion. The difficult part is not the happy path — it is the partial-coverage simulation state and the "you cannot arm this yet, and here is why" state, both of which are where a user's trust is actually won or lost.

## Scope / Deliverables
**SCR-084 Rule simulation / backtest panel** — hi-fi for every item on its sign-off checklist:
- range, symbol and account selectors
- the available-history statement ("13 of 14 days — recording started 09-01")
- progress and cancel
- result summary (fires, actions by type, errors)
- a per-firing timeline with the context that triggered it
- the "simulation is not a backtest of PnL" caveat, placed in the reading order rather than as a tooltip
- the insufficient-history state
Plus the remaining catalogue states: idle, running (cancellable), completed, partial (gaps named), failed, no-history with the record-this-symbol CTA.

**SCR-085 Rule arming dialog** — hi-fi for every item on its sign-off checklist:
- plain-language restatement of what the rule will do
- environment choice with DEMO default
- scope (accounts, symbols) restated, with a trade group expanded into an explicit account list
- typed confirmation for LIVE arming plus step-up
- estimated-detector dependency warning
- conflict warning linking to SCR-086
- the disarm path
Plus: the blocked state (no simulation on this version / open safety warning / no permission on a bound account), the pending state while awaiting WS confirmation, and the `flatten_all_positions` extra-acknowledgement variant.

**Copy**: final strings for both screens, incorporating D01's recommendations, including the two required verbatim sentences.
**Motion**: progress and state-transition treatment within the reduced-motion contract of `16-design-system-brief.md` — every animation has a `prefers-reduced-motion` alternative and no status change is conveyed by motion alone.

## Out of scope
- SCR-086, SCR-087, SCR-088, SCR-089 — **E35-D03**.
- The editors SCR-081/082/083 — E36/E37.
- Developer handoff specs and redlines — **E35-D05**.
- The a11y annotation pass — **E35-D04** (this ticket supplies designs for it to review).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue sign-off item is drawn
  Given the sign-off checklists for SCR-084 and SCR-085 in 14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the hi-fi is reviewed
  Then every checklist item is ticked with the specific frame that satisfies it named

Scenario: Failure states are designed as primary cases
  Given the partial-coverage, no-history and cannot-arm-yet states
  When they are reviewed
  Then each is a fully drawn frame with real copy explaining what is missing and what the user should do, not a generic error component

Scenario: The backend lead confirms every state is producible (edge case)
  Given the drawn states
  When the rule-engine backend lead reviews them
  Then each state maps to an actual API response or WS frame, and any state the API cannot produce is either removed or filed as a backend change before sign-off

Scenario: Status is never colour-only
  Given every status treatment across both screens
  When checked against WCAG 2.2 AA
  Then each carries text or an icon in addition to colour, and contrast ratios are annotated on the frames
```

## Technical notes / design
Design against real data shapes, not lorem: pull an actual `RuleSimulationResult` payload (`22-api-openapi.yaml` example) and an actual `RuleDetail` so the field lengths, number formats and timestamp precisions in the design are the ones that will really arrive. Simulation results can contain hundreds of firings — draw the dense case, not a tidy five-row example.

The arming dialog's plain-language restatement is generated from the IR server-side; the design must specify the *template* and how it degrades when the rule is complex enough that the restatement runs long, because a truncated safety summary is worse than a scrollable one.

DEMO preselection is a safety control. Draw it so that selecting LIVE is visibly a deliberate act — this is the same design intent as the always-visible environment badge in the order ticket (SCR-075), and the two should feel consistent.

## Test plan
Design validation rather than software testing: walk the drawn states against the real API payloads with the backend lead (third acceptance scenario), and run the copy past two people who did not write it for comprehension. Formal usability testing of the built screens happens in E35-Q06 and design QA in E35-D06.

## Security notes
The designs must not invent a path that weakens a server-side control. Specifically: the arm control is disabled when preconditions are unmet, but the design must not imply the client decides — the blocked-state copy names the server-enforced precondition. No design may show an API key, token or full account credential; account references are labels and last-4 identifiers only. The step-up 2FA field follows the established pattern from SCR-005 rather than a new one.

## Accessibility notes
Annotate on every frame: focus order, roles (`alertdialog` for SCR-085), accessible names, live-region behaviour for progress announcements, visible focus treatment, and contrast ratios. The environment radio group, typed confirmation and 2FA field each need a visible label and a format hint. The simulation timeline needs its text-list equivalent drawn, not merely mentioned. Reviewed formally in E35-D04.

## Performance notes
Design must respect the SCR-084 constraint that the UI stays fully interactive during a run and results stream in progressively — so the layout cannot depend on knowing the full result set up front (no "jump to the end" layouts, no totals that only appear at completion without a placeholder).

## Observability
Specify which states should emit client analytics so abandonment is diagnosable: arming abandoned at confirmation, simulation cancelled, no-history CTA followed. Feeds the event list in E35-S08.

- [ ] Presented at Sprint Review / design review.
