title: Enforce per-account risk caps server-side inside the order path
body:
## Context
**US-PROF-004 — Risk caps enforced server-side (Must)**: "As the owner, I want max position size, max daily loss and max concurrent positions enforced in the backend, so that limits survive a broken or hostile client." This story wires the M17 evaluator (E39-T01) into the OMS `Validator` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10) so that **every** order path — order ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule-engine action, trade-group fan-out leg, emulated-algo child — passes through the same check before any exchange call.

It also delivers the read surfaces the rest of the product needs to *show* headroom rather than discover it on rejection: `GET /api/v1/me/limits` (`EffectiveLimits`) and the server-side-scoped `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` (`RiskSummary`). US-POS-006's scoping NFR applies here — "the API never returns out-of-scope rows to a manager" — and `22-api-openapi.yaml` is explicit that a Viewer requesting an aggregate covering an account they cannot read gets `403 account_scope_denied` rather than a silently narrowed (and therefore misleading) number.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `RiskGate` integrated into the OMS `Validator` chain at `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/validator.py`, invoked **before** sizing and before any exchange call, for every command origin (`ticket`, `chart`, `dom`, `rule`, `fanout_leg`, `algo_child`). A test asserts the gate is unreachable-around: adding a new command origin without routing it through the gate fails a registry test.
- Error mapping to RFC 9457 problem responses using the existing catalogue in `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `risk_limit_breached` (422) with `detail` naming the cap, the limit and the current value; `account_locked`; `symbol_not_allowed`; and the new `risk_state_unavailable` (503) problem type added to the catalogue.
- `GET /api/v1/me/limits` returning `EffectiveLimits` — per-account `orders_per_minute_limit`/`used`, `rate_budget_pct_used`, `daily_loss_usd`/`daily_loss_cap_usd`, `open_positions`, `lockout_until` — so E30's order ticket can show remaining headroom before submission.
- `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` returning `RiskSummary` with `totals` (including `positions_without_native_stop`, surfaced from E32's invariant state) and per-account rows (`equity_usd`, `unrealised_pnl_usd`, `realised_pnl_today_usd`, `daily_loss_cap_usd`, `cap_utilisation_pct`, `open_positions`, `frozen`, `lockout`), with `accountIds` and `environment` query filters.
- Server-side scoping: Manager sees only granted accounts; Viewer gets the aggregate only when granted read on **every** covered account, else `403 account_scope_denied`.
- `risk_cap_usage` populated on the account-status WS payload (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15) so SCR-071 and the ticket's headroom chip update without polling.
- Audit: `risk_cap.changed` is emitted by the admin path (E39-S05); this story emits a structured audit entry for every *rejected* order with its cap, limit and actual value, so a hostile-client probe leaves a trail.

## Out of scope
- Automatic lockout creation on breach and the override flow (E39-S02) — this story refuses orders while a lockout exists but does not create one.
- Kill-switch state (E39-S03); the gate consumes it through a port with a stub until S03 lands.
- Any UI (E39-S04, E39-S05).
- Rate-limit budgeting against Bybit's per-UID limits (E34) — `max_orders_per_minute` here is a **user-configured risk cap**, not exchange rate budgeting, and the two are deliberately separate counters.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Position size cap rejects before any exchange call
  Given account C caps position size at 0.5 BTC and holds 0.4 BTC
  When an order for 0.2 BTC is submitted
  Then the response is 422 with code risk_limit_breached
  And the detail reads "would exceed max position 0.5 BTC (current 0.4)"
  And no request was made to Bybit
  And an audit entry records the rejection

Scenario: Concurrent positions cap still permits reduce-only
  Given the cap is 3 and 3 positions are open
  When an order that would open a fourth symbol is submitted
  Then it is rejected with risk_limit_breached
  When a reduce-only order on an existing position is submitted
  Then it is accepted

Scenario: Every path is gated
  Given the kill-switch is released and caps are exceeded
  When an order is attempted from the ticket, a chart drag, a DOM click, a rule action, a fan-out leg and an emulated-algo child
  Then all six are rejected with the same code and the same message
  And each rejection is audited with its origin

Scenario: Manager scoping on the risk summary
  Given manager M is granted accounts A and B only
  When M calls GET /api/v1/risk/summary without filters
  Then only A and B appear and no filter value can reveal account C

Scenario (failure): Viewer requesting an unreadable aggregate
  Given a viewer lacks read on one account covered by the requested aggregate
  When GET /api/v1/risk/summary is called
  Then the response is 403 account_scope_denied
  And no partial aggregate is returned

Scenario (edge): Risk state unavailable
  Given the risk service cannot produce fresh state for account C
  When an opening order for C is submitted
  Then it is rejected with 503 risk_state_unavailable
  And GET /api/v1/risk/summary marks account C as stale
```

## Technical notes / design
The gate is a dependency in the FastAPI order router's chain (`session -> scope -> rate limit -> validate`, `20-architecture.md` §3.12) and *also* a direct call inside `OrderService.submit`, so a future internal caller that bypasses HTTP still cannot bypass the gate. The registry test enumerates `OrderCommand.origin` values and asserts each has a gated code path.

`EffectiveLimits` and `RiskSummary` are assembled from the in-memory `RiskService` counters plus a single indexed lockout probe — no per-request aggregation query over `executions`, which would blow the latency budget.

`positions_without_native_stop` is read from E32's invariant tracker; until E32 lands it reports from the OMS position state with a `null`-free default of 0 and a feature flag `risk.native_stop_surfacing` gating the banner. Documented so E32 can flip it on without a schema change.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: gate wiring (each origin), error mapping (each code → status + problem body), scoping predicate (owner/manager/viewer × granted/ungranted).
- **Contract**: OpenAPI schemathesis run over `/me/limits`, `/risk/summary`, and the new `risk_state_unavailable` problem type; response bodies validate against `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **Integration**: recorded Bybit demo fixtures driving PnL across the daily-loss cap and position count across the concurrent-positions cap; assert no outbound exchange call occurs on a rejected order (HTTP mock asserts zero calls).
- **E2E**: covered by E39-Q02 (every path under caps).
- **Perf**: k6 profile submitting at the per-UID limit; assert added p95 ≤5 ms and total order submit → ack p95 <300 ms on demo.
- **Security**: abuse-case tests in E39-X02; this story includes a negative test that a client-supplied `risk_caps` field in an order body is ignored.
- Coverage: ≥90 % on touched M17 and validator code.

## Security notes
Directly implements the mitigation for `04-security-program.md` threat class "tampering — client-side cap bypass" and P8 server-side authority. Abuse cases covered by tests here: submitting caps in the request body; submitting with a forged account id outside scope; probing another account's existence through `/risk/summary` filters (must return the same 403 shape whether the account exists or not — no enumeration). Data classification: financial state and account identifiers; no secrets in responses or logs. `security` label mandatory per DoD §8 (any ticket touching `area/oms-execution` order-placement paths).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend only. The error `detail` strings are user-visible copy, so they are reviewed against the E39-D01 copy deck and must be full sentences naming the cap, not codes.

## Performance notes
≤5 ms p95 added to the order path (US-PROF-004 and US-ADMIN-003 NFRs); inside budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2, hard gate for R3 demo). `/risk/summary` responds within 400 ms p95 for up to 20 accounts; `risk_cap_usage` is delivered on the existing account-status WS cadence and adds no new topic.

## Observability
Metrics from E39-T01 plus `cv_risk_gate_rejections_total{origin,code}` and `cv_risk_summary_duration_seconds`. Every rejection logs `request_id`, origin, account, cap, limit, actual. Audit entries for rejections use action `order.rejected` with a `risk` reason payload. Grafana "Risk & safety" panel gains a rejection-by-origin breakdown.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios pass via automated tests referencing the scenario name.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90 % on touched packages; CI gate green.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` updated (`risk_state_unavailable`) and contract tests green.
- [ ] Perf benchmark recorded against budget #4.
- [ ] SAST/SCA clean; Security engineer review; manual abuse-case check performed (cap in body, forged scope).
- [ ] QA black-box sign-off recorded (E39-Q01 plan).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review (rejection shown from three different origins).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded: `risk.enforcement` default **on** in every environment; `risk.native_stop_surfacing` default off until E32.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E39-T01` — the evaluator and counters.
- `E29` — the OMS `Validator` chain and `OrderService`; the order/position event stream feeding counters.
- Consumed by: `E30` (headroom chip), `E34` (per-leg pre-validation), `E39-S02`, `E39-S04`.

title: Automatic lockout on cap breach with day-boundary reset and step-up override
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** the automatic-lockout, day-boundary reset and step-up override lifecycle (clear→warning→locked) is built directly on the library via the factory; the day-boundary timer and override window are the chart's coarse `after:` states, not hand-rolled bookkeeping.

**US-RULE-012 — Daily loss limit and lockout (Must)**: "As the owner, I want automatic flatten and lockout at a daily loss threshold, so that a bad day cannot become a disaster." Where E39-S01 refuses individual orders, this story adds the **state machine**: a breach transitions the account into a persisted lockout, which cancels working orders (and optionally flattens per policy), blocks new entries while leaving reduce-only available, pushes the state to every affected session, resets at the configured day boundary, and can be cleared early only by the owner with step-up re-authentication and a mandatory audited reason.

The API contract already exists: `POST /api/v1/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override` — "Lockouts are set automatically when a `RiskCaps` threshold is breached. Clearing one is an owner-only, step-up-gated, always-audited action; the reason is mandatory and is written to the audit chain" (`22-api-openapi.yaml`). `04-security-program.md` SR-025 and `24-internal-schemas.md` §12 both list clearing a risk lockout among step-up-required actions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement the `B20` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B20.risk_lockout.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('risk_lockout', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b20_risk_lockout.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b20_risk_lockout.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- `LockoutService` in `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/lockout.py`: on a breach detected by the evaluation cycle (event-driven on every position/execution event, plus a timer at `risk.eval_interval_seconds` = 5 s per the US-RULE-012 NFR), open a `risk_lockouts` row with `reason` ∈ {`daily_loss`, `consecutive_losses`, `max_positions`, `manual`}, `threshold`, `actual_value`, `since`, `until`.
- **Breach behaviour driven by `risk_policy.breach_behaviour`** per limit (`warn` | `block` | `flatten`), per the SCR-134 design: `warn` raises an alert only; `block` cancels working orders and refuses new entries; `flatten` additionally issues reduce-only closes via the OMS and records `risk.auto_flatten`. Defaults are conservative (`block` for daily loss).
- Idempotency: a breach that persists across evaluation cycles must not open a second lockout or re-cancel orders — enforced by the partial unique index from E39-T02 and an explicit "already locked" fast path.
- **Day-boundary reset**: the lockout auto-releases at the configured boundary (`risk_policy.day_boundary_utc_offset_minutes`, default UTC per `24-internal-schemas.md` §11); the reset time is exposed in the API and shown on SCR-073.
- **Override**: `POST /api/v1/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override` — owner only (`killswitch:write`), step-up token required (`elevated_until` valid), mandatory `reason` (3..280 chars per the schema; the SCR-071 UI additionally requires ≥10 characters), idempotency key required. On success the lockout is released with a **shortened override window** (US-RULE-012: "a shortened override window is applied") after which the cap re-arms — window length configurable, default 60 minutes.
- Audit: `risk.lockout_triggered` `{scope, rule, threshold, actualValue, accountIds}`, `risk.lockout_overridden` (**high severity**), `risk.auto_flatten`, `risk.lockout_acknowledged` — the exact action names from the SCR-073 catalogue entry and `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.
- WS push: a `system` frame (`SystemUpdate`, `kind: "notice"`, `severity: "critical"`) within 500 ms of the breach so SCR-073 appears without a poll; plus the account-status `lockout` field so SCR-071 rows flip to LOCK.
- Manager **override request** path: a manager cannot clear their own lockout; the request notifies the owner (via E40's channels when available, and always via the in-app notice) and the attempt is audited.

## Out of scope
- The lockout UI (E39-S04) and the freeze/kill-switch UI (E39-S05).
- Rule-engine-authored risk rules and the dead man's switch, US-RULE-013 (E35).
- Flatten-all as a manual panic action (E29 endpoint; E39-T03 runbook) — here flatten is only the automatic, policy-driven variant.
- Notification delivery channels (E40); this story emits the events they consume.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Threshold breached
  Given account C has max_daily_loss_usd 1500
  When realised+unrealised PnL reaches -1500
  Then a risk_lockouts row is opened with reason daily_loss, threshold 1500 and the actual value
  And working orders are cancelled per the configured breach behaviour
  And order placement for C is disabled while reduce-only remains available
  And every session scoped to C receives a system WS frame within 500 ms
  And risk.lockout_triggered is audited

Scenario: Owner override requires step-up
  Given account C is locked out
  When the owner calls the override endpoint without a valid step-up token
  Then the response is 403 and no lockout is released
  When the owner repeats with a valid step-up token and a 12-character reason
  Then the lockout is released, a shortened override window is applied
  And risk.lockout_overridden is audited at high severity with the reason

Scenario: Boundary reset
  Given a lockout with reason daily_loss and no explicit until
  When the configured day boundary passes
  Then the lockout is released automatically, the daily counter resets, and the reset is audited

Scenario (failure): Manager attempts self-override
  Given manager M is locked out on their granted account
  When M calls the override endpoint
  Then the response is 403
  And the attempt is audited
  And the owner is notified of the override request

Scenario (edge): Breach persists across cycles
  Given a lockout is already active for the breached cap
  When the next evaluation cycle observes the same breach
  Then no second lockout row is created and no orders are cancelled a second time

Scenario (edge): Breach during backend restart
  Given the backend restarts while a lockout is active
  When it comes back up
  Then the lockout is still in force (it is persisted, not in-memory)
  And accounts are not silently unlocked by the restart
```

## Technical notes / design

**Statechart contract.** Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B20.1–.8. Mandatory config: `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §1.2 (`79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §3 stay plain code.
Evaluation is driven by the `oms.*` event bus (immediate) and a 5 s ticker (safety net), both calling the same `LockoutService.evaluate(account)` so there is one code path. Cancellation of working orders reuses the OMS cancel-all path with a `reason=risk_lockout` tag so the audit trail attributes it correctly rather than looking like a user cancel.

The override's "shortened window" is implemented as a new `risk_lockouts` row with `reason='manual'` and `until = now + override_window_minutes` marked `released_at` NULL but non-blocking — i.e. it is a *grace* record used to re-arm the cap — documented in `24-internal-schemas.md` so the semantics are not inferred from code.

Config keys: `risk.eval_interval_seconds` (5), `risk.override_window_minutes` (60), `risk.lockout_default_minutes` (from `risk_policy.lockout_minutes_default`, bounded 0..1440).

## Test plan

**Statechart test plan additions:**
- Pure-API unit tests of the `b20_risk_lockout` binding module using a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership in `tests/xstate_contract/test_b20_risk_lockout.py`, covering both spellings and every §B20.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point this ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a `machine_hash` or HMAC mismatch.
- **Unit**: breach detection per reason; idempotency (repeat cycles); day-boundary release arithmetic; override token validation; shortened-window re-arm; manager self-override refusal.
- **Contract**: `POST /risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override` request/response and 403 shapes against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the `SystemUpdate` frame validates against the `cv://ws/v1/system.schema.json` schema in `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9.
- **Integration**: recorded fixture where partial fills walk PnL to the threshold; assert cancellation set, audit rows and WS frame ordering.
- **Chaos** (with E39-Q03): backend restart mid-lockout; Postgres failover during breach handling; WS disconnect between breach and push (client must still see the lockout on reconnect via the snapshot, not only the delta).
- **E2E**: in E39-Q02.
- Coverage ≥90 % on the lockout package.

## Security notes
Threats: elevation of privilege (self-override, manager clearing another's lockout), repudiation (unaudited release), tampering (client-supplied `until`). Controls: owner-only `killswitch:write`, SR-025 step-up, mandatory audited reason, server-computed `until` (never accepted from the client), and idempotency keys to prevent replayed overrides. Every override is `high` severity in the audit chain so E42's browser surfaces it prominently. Data classification: financial + accountability data; retained indefinitely. `security` label mandatory.

## Accessibility notes
Backend, but the copy it emits is rendered by `role="alert"` surfaces: the lockout reason string must be a full sentence naming the breached limit, the actual value and the reset time (SCR-073 requires all three), never a bare code. Reason strings come from the E39-D01 copy deck.

## Performance notes
Lockout probe on the order path is an index-only lookup within the ≤5 ms evaluator budget. Breach → WS notice ≤500 ms (SCR-073 performance note). The 5 s ticker must not exceed the reconciliation rate budget (US-POS-008 NFR) — it reads in-memory counters, issuing no extra exchange calls.

## Observability
`cv_risk_lockouts_active` gauge (labels: reason), `cv_risk_lockout_transitions_total{reason,transition}`, `cv_risk_override_total{outcome}`, `cv_risk_breach_to_notice_seconds` histogram (asserted against the 500 ms budget). Audit actions as listed. Alert rule: any `risk.lockout_overridden` pages the owner.

## Definition of Done

**Statechart DoD additions:** `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90 %; CI green.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` reflect the shipped override and grace semantics.
- [ ] Chaos scenarios (restart, failover) pass.
- [ ] Security review: step-up enforcement and audit completeness manually abuse-tested.
- [ ] QA sign-off per the E39-Q01 plan.
- [ ] Demoed: a simulated loss sequence drives a lockout and an owner override at Sprint Review.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded: `risk.auto_lockout` default on in all environments.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- `E39-S01` — the enforcement gate that consults lockout state.
- `E39-T01` — counters and the day-boundary clock.
- `E09` (via E27) — step-up re-authentication.
- `E29` — cancel-all and reduce-only close paths.

## Branch
`feat/e39-lockouts`. Two PRs (service + override endpoint), each ≤400 LOC.

title: Kill-switch engine: global and scoped freeze over REST with WS propagation
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** the KillSwitch engine (states clear→engaging→engaged/error, C-07b unguarded RELEASE fall-through) is built directly on the library via the factory; the enum, transition table and snapshot/rehydrate code it replaces are dropped.

**US-RULE-014 — Owner kill-switch (Must)**: "As the owner, I want to freeze a manager or everything instantly, so that I can stop harm immediately," with the NFR "freeze is enforced at the API boundary, not in the UI; effective within 2 s". The roadmap fixes the semantics (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E39 row): the kill-switch halts "all new order placement, all rule-engine actions and all fan-out across all accounts… with the semantics **'stops new risk, does not force-close'**".

The contract is already written in `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET|POST /api/v1/trading/kill-switch`. Engaging "(a) refuses all new order/amend requests with `trading_disabled`, (b) optionally cancels all open orders, (c) optionally flattens all positions with reduce-only market orders, and (d) disarms every `armed` rule". Managers may engage it for accounts in their own scope; **only the owner may engage it globally or release it**. Bybit's own dead-man's-switch (`POST /v5/order/disconnected-cancel-all`) is `inverse`-only, so the local kill-switch is the operative control for USDT linear perps.

R3 exit criterion 7 (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3) is this story's bar: "Kill-switch works end-to-end: activated, no new order can be placed by any path including the rule engine; existing positions untouched; released cleanly; every transition audited."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement the `B18` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B18.kill_switch.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('kill_switch', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b18_kill_switch.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b18_kill_switch.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- `KillSwitchService` in `apps/api/src/cvapi/oms/risk/killswitch.py` backed by `kill_switch_state` (E39-T02), with a **fail-closed** cached read (≤5 s staleness; unreadable state ⇒ trading refused) matching the `feature_flags.is_killswitch` re-read rule in `21-database-schema.md` §3.9.
- `GET /api/v1/trading/kill-switch` → `KillSwitch` (`engaged`, `scope`, `exchange_account_ids`, `engaged_at`, `engaged_by`, `reason`).
- `POST /api/v1/trading/kill-switch` accepting `SetKillSwitchRequest` (`engaged`, `scope` ∈ {`global`,`accounts`}, `exchange_account_ids`, `cancel_open_orders` default true, `flatten_positions` **default false**, `disarm_rules` default true, `reason` 3..280) with a **required idempotency key**, returning `KillSwitchResult` with per-account `actions` counts and a `failures` array.
- Enforcement: the gate from E39-S01 consults kill-switch state first; every order/amend path returns `trading_disabled`; fan-out legs report `kill_switch_engaged` (the enum value already present in `TradeGroupPreview.legs[].rejection.code`); the rule runtime is disarmed via the `rules` integration point so rule actions cannot fire (US-RULE-011's safety-override precedence: "a risk control always wins, regardless of configured priority").
- **Positions untouched by default** — `flatten_positions` defaults to false and is only honoured when explicitly true; a test asserts that a default-options engagement closes nothing.
- RBAC: `killswitch:write`; scope `granted_accounts` for a manager engaging within scope; **owner-only** for `scope: global` and for **any** release, enforced server-side with a test per role × scope × direction.
- Step-up: releasing the kill-switch requires a valid step-up token (SR-025 explicitly lists "disabling the kill switch").
- Propagation: a `system` WS frame (`SystemUpdate`, `kind: "kill_switch"`, with the `actions` counts) to every connection — `system` is auto-subscribed and cannot be unsubscribed (`23-ws-protocol.md` §9), so no client can miss it; affected private subscriptions are re-authorised per §10 ("Authorisation is re-evaluated… on kill-switch transitions").
- Partial-failure semantics: a per-account failure (REST timeout, exchange 5xx) is reported in `failures` with a retryable error, does not roll back successful accounts, and leaves the switch engaged.
- Audit: one record per affected entity (US-RULE-014: "one audit record per affected entity"), actions `risk.freeze` (with the full option set) and `risk.unfreeze`; `user_account_access.frozen`/`frozen_at`/`frozen_by`/`frozen_reason` maintained for per-manager freezes.
- Global-hotkey server contract: the hotkey opens the confirmation UI (E39-S05); the backend exposes no unconfirmed one-shot endpoint — engagement always carries a typed reason.

## Out of scope
- The confirmation modal, panic cluster and hotkey binding (E39-S05).
- `POST /positions/close-all` implementation (E29); this story calls it when `flatten_positions` is true.
- Bybit DCP arming for `inverse` instruments — out of scope product-wide (USDT linear perps only).
- The feature-flag console surface of the kill-switch (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Global engagement stops new risk within 2 seconds
  Given open positions and 4 armed rules across 5 accounts
  When the owner engages the kill-switch with scope global and default options
  Then within 2 seconds every order and amend request is refused with trading_disabled
  And all 4 rules are disarmed
  And zero positions are closed
  And open orders are cancelled because cancel_open_orders defaults to true
  And one audit record exists per affected entity

Scenario: Manager may freeze only their own scope
  Given manager M is granted account A only
  When M engages the kill-switch with scope accounts for A
  Then it succeeds
  When M attempts scope global, or scope accounts including account B
  Then the response is 403 and no state changes

Scenario: Release requires owner plus step-up
  Given the kill-switch is engaged globally
  When a manager attempts to release it
  Then the response is 403
  When the owner attempts release without a step-up token
  Then the response is 403
  When the owner releases with a valid step-up token and a reason
  Then the switch is released, rules remain disarmed until explicitly re-armed, and risk.unfreeze is audited

Scenario (failure): One account fails during engagement
  Given account C's REST path times out while cancelling orders
  When the owner engages the kill-switch across 5 accounts
  Then the switch is engaged, the other 4 accounts report their action counts
  And failures contains account C with a retryable error
  And nothing is rolled back

Scenario (edge): Fail-closed on unreadable state
  Given the kill_switch_state read fails
  When an order is submitted
  Then it is refused, never admitted optimistically

Scenario (edge): Idempotent re-engagement
  Given the switch is already engaged globally
  When the same request is replayed with the same idempotency key
  Then the stored result is returned and no orders are cancelled a second time
```

## Technical notes / design

**Statechart contract.** Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B18.1–.8. Mandatory config: `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §1.2 (`79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §3 stay plain code.
Engagement is ordered **refuse-first**: the state row is written and the cache invalidated *before* any cancellation or flatten work begins, so the 200 ms server-side halt (SCR-072 performance note) does not wait on exchange round-trips. Cancellation/flatten/disarm then run concurrently per account with per-account results streamed into `KillSwitchResult.failures`.

Rule disarming goes through the rule-engine port (`rule.kill_switched` audit action already defined in `24-internal-schemas.md` §12) rather than writing rule tables directly, so E35 owns its own invariants.

Idempotency reuses the OMS idempotency store keyed on the required `Idempotency-Key` header, storing the `KillSwitchResult` so a replay is byte-identical.

Config keys: `risk.killswitch_cache_max_age_seconds` (5), `risk.killswitch_action_concurrency` (per-account parallelism), `risk.killswitch_action_timeout_seconds`.

## Test plan

**Statechart test plan additions:**
- Pure-API unit tests of the `b18_kill_switch` binding module using a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership in `tests/xstate_contract/test_b18_kill_switch.py`, covering both spellings and every §B18.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point this ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a `machine_hash` or HMAC mismatch.
- **Unit**: state transitions, RBAC matrix (owner/manager/viewer × global/accounts × engage/release), option handling (each of the three flags independently), fail-closed read, idempotent replay.
- **Contract**: `KillSwitch`, `SetKillSwitchRequest`, `KillSwitchResult` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the `kind: "kill_switch"` frame against `cv://ws/v1/system.schema.json`.
- **Integration**: recorded fixtures with an injected 5xx and an injected timeout on one account, asserting partial-failure reporting and no rollback.
- **E2E** (E39-Q02): every order-placement path attempted while engaged, including a rule action and a fan-out leg — zero escapes, matching R3 exit criterion 7.
- **Perf**: measure engagement → first refusal (target ≤200 ms server-side) and engagement → WS frame at the client (target ≤2 s) under a loaded system.
- **Chaos** (E39-Q03): backend restart while engaged (must come back engaged); Postgres failover during engagement.
- Coverage ≥90 %.

## Security notes
This is the highest-value target in the product: an attacker who can *disable* the kill-switch removes the last safety control (`04-security-program.md` §5 threat D2 — "Feature-flag screen used to enable live trading without review", mitigated by SR-025 step-up on kill-switch disable). Controls implemented here: owner-only release, step-up token, mandatory audited reason, idempotency to block replay, fail-closed reads, and one audit row per affected entity so a partial or forged action is detectable. A manager engaging outside scope and any release attempt by a non-owner are logged as security events, not just 403s. Abuse cases are exercised in E39-X02.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The `reason` and per-account failure messages are rendered in `role="alertdialog"` content, so they must be plain sentences (copy deck from E39-D01), and the action counts must render meaningfully at zero.

## Performance notes
Server-side halt within 200 ms of the backend call (SCR-072); effective within 2 s end-to-end including WS propagation (US-RULE-014 NFR). The cached state read adds <0.5 ms to the order path, inside the ≤5 ms risk budget and budget #4.

## Observability
`cv_kill_switch_engaged` gauge (0/1, labelled by scope), `cv_kill_switch_transitions_total{scope,direction,actor_role}`, `cv_kill_switch_action_failures_total{action}`, `cv_kill_switch_engage_latency_seconds` histogram. Audit: `risk.freeze`, `risk.unfreeze`, `rule.kill_switched`, `position.flattened` (when opted in). Alerting: `cv_kill_switch_engaged == 1` pages immediately; a failure entry in `failures` raises a warning alert.

## Definition of Done

**Statechart DoD additions:** `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios automated, including the RBAC matrix.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90 %; CI green.
- [ ] Contract tests green against OpenAPI and the WS system schema.
- [ ] Perf numbers recorded (≤200 ms halt, ≤2 s propagation).
- [ ] Chaos scenarios pass (restart, failover).
- [ ] Security engineer review and a manual privilege-escalation attempt recorded.
- [ ] QA sign-off per E39-Q01/Q02.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review: engage, prove no path can place an order, prove positions untouched, release.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded: the kill-switch itself is an `is_killswitch` flag row; `risk.killswitch` enforcement default on everywhere and **not disableable by flag**.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- `E39-T01`, `E39-T02` — evaluator port and persisted state.
- `E29` — cancel-all, reduce-only close, and the order paths being refused.
- `E35` (rule runtime) — the disarm port; until E35 lands the port is a no-op stub with a test asserting it is called, so E35 only has to implement the receiving side.
- `E09`/`E27` — step-up authentication.

## Branch

## References

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md §B20 (risk lockout), kill-switch machine

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- services/api/risk/ (evaluator, lockout, kill-switch)
- machines/B20.risk_lockout.machine.json (or kill-switch equivalent), statechart/bindings/, tests/xstate_contract/

**Interfaces you must not break**
- `/api/v1/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override`, `/api/v1/killswitch/*`, `risk_lockouts`/`risk_policy`/`kill_switch_state` Postgres tables, `SystemUpdate` WS frame (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9), OMS cancel-all/reduce-only paths.

**Commands**
- `cd services/api && ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict .`
- `cd services/api && pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`
- `pnpm verify` (full local gate before opening the PR)

**Branch & PR**

title: ADR-0016 risk enforcement model plus the flatten-all runbook and doc updates
body:
## Context
Two documentation obligations fall out of E39 and are explicitly required rather than optional.

First, the roadmap's E39 row (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2) specifies the kill-switch semantics "stops new risk, does not force-close" **"plus a separate documented flatten-all runbook"**. That runbook does not exist yet and is a deliverable of this epic, not of E29.

Second, `docs/plan/27-adrs/` has no ADR covering risk enforcement. The decisions made in E39-K01 (authoritative daily-PnL source, day boundary) and E39-T01 (cap-resolution precedence, check ordering, fail-closed posture) are exactly the kind of non-obvious, cross-epic decisions the ADR index exists to record — E30, E34, E35, E42 and E44 all build on them. The DoR/DoD for Spikes (§5.2) also requires the spike's decision to be recorded as an ADR.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0027-risk-enforcement-and-kill-switch.md`**, status `decided`, following the existing ADR template, covering: server-side-only enforcement (P8) and why client-side pre-checks are advisory only; the authoritative daily-PnL source and day-boundary semantics from E39-K01; cap-resolution precedence (most restrictive wins; overrides never widen); the fixed check order and why message determinism matters; fail-closed on stale risk state and on unreadable kill-switch state; the "stops new risk, does not force-close" kill-switch semantics and why flatten is opt-in; step-up gating per SR-025. Consequences section names the downstream epics that rely on each decision.
- Add ADR-0016 to the ADR index table in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §13.
- **`docs/runbooks/flatten-all.md`** — the operational runbook: when to use flatten-all instead of (or after) the kill-switch; the exact sequence (engage kill-switch → verify no new orders are being accepted → `POST /api/v1/positions/close-all` with `cancel_open_orders: true` → verify via `GET /api/v1/positions` and `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` that `open_positions` is 0 and `positions_without_native_stop` is 0 → record the incident); what to do when some accounts fail (per-account retry, and the escalation path if an account remains stale); the demo-vs-live differences (demo is REST-only for order entry, so flatten is REST-driven in both but latency differs); and the post-incident audit query showing every `risk.freeze`, `panic.flatten_all` and `position.flattened` row for the window.
- Drill instruction: the runbook is exercised as part of E39-Q03's chaos scenarios and again during the R3 soak; the runbook states its own rehearsal cadence.
- Update `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §3.10 (`Validator`, `KillSwitch` rows) and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11/§12 so they describe what shipped, not what was proposed.
- Update `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` if E39-S01..S03 introduced any deviation (notably the `risk_state_unavailable` problem type).

## Out of scope
- User-facing help content for SCR-071/073 (ships with E39-S04's copy).
- The security program document itself (E39-X02 updates it if the threat model changes controls).
- Release notes / changelog fragments (handled per story).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: ADR captures every cross-epic decision
  Given ADR-0016 is submitted
  Then it records the daily-PnL source, the day boundary, cap precedence, check order, fail-closed posture and kill-switch semantics
  And each decision names the downstream epics that depend on it

Scenario: Runbook is executable by someone who did not build the system
  Given an engineer unfamiliar with E39 follows docs/runbooks/flatten-all.md on the demo environment
  When they reach the end
  Then all positions are flat, all working orders are cancelled, and they have produced the audit query output
  And they needed no clarification from the E39 authors

Scenario (failure): Partial flatten
  Given one account's REST path fails during the runbook
  Then the runbook states the retry procedure and the escalation threshold explicitly
  And it states that the kill-switch remains engaged until reconciliation confirms the account's true state

Scenario: Docs match shipped behaviour
  Given E39-S01..S03 are merged
  Then 20-architecture.md, 24-internal-schemas.md, 22-api-openapi.yaml and 23-ws-protocol.md describe the shipped behaviour
  And the traceability CI check passes
```

## Technical notes / design
The runbook is written as a numbered checklist with copy-pasteable `curl` calls against `/api/v1`, each showing the expected response shape, plus the verification query:
```sql
SELECT ts, actor, action, target, severity
FROM audit_log
WHERE action IN ('risk.freeze','risk.unfreeze','panic.flatten_all','position.flattened','risk.lockout_triggered')
  AND ts BETWEEN :from AND :to
ORDER BY id;
```
ADR-0016 uses the repository's existing ADR headings (Context / Decision / Alternatives considered / Consequences / Status).

## Test plan
- Docs CI: markdown lint, link check, and the traceability check (`scripts/check-traceability.ts`) — a PR editing the product docs without updating `18-traceability-matrix.md` fails the build.
- Runbook validation is a **rehearsal**, not a unit test: executed once on demo by an engineer who did not write E39, with the outcome recorded on this ticket (this is the acceptance evidence).

## Security notes
The runbook must not contain credentials, key material or an account's real identifiers — use the fixture labels. It must state clearly that flatten-all is step-up gated (`24-internal-schemas.md` §12 lists panic-flatten-all among step-up actions) and audited as `panic.flatten_all`. Security engineer reviews the runbook because an incorrect runbook is itself a safety control failure.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — documentation. (Markdown must still be structurally navigable: real headings, no ASCII-art-only instructions.)

## Performance notes
The runbook records the observed wall-clock time of each step during rehearsal, so an operator knows what "too slow" looks like during a real incident.

## Observability
The runbook names the exact metrics to watch during execution: `cv_kill_switch_engaged`, `cv_risk_lockouts_active`, `cv_risk_state_stale_accounts`, and the OMS open-position gauge.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged and indexed in `20-architecture.md` §13.
- [ ] `docs/runbooks/flatten-all.md` merged.
- [ ] Runbook rehearsed on demo by a non-author; outcome and timings recorded.
- [ ] `20-architecture.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md`, `18-traceability-matrix.md` updated; docs CI green.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Architect approval on the ADR.

## Dependencies

- `E39-K01` supplies the daily-PnL decision content.

## Branch

title: Research alert attention behaviour and run the a11y design review
body:
## Context
This ticket merges the former E40-D01 (UX research) and E40-D01 (accessibility design review) into one design-discovery ticket, sized against the 21-point roadmap allocation for E40. Part A runs before wireframing and decides the critical-override list; Part B gates the handoff pack produced in E40-D02.

### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
The failure mode of an alerting system is not "it didn't fire" — it is "it fired so often the trader stopped reading it". US-ALRT-003's storm-suppression scenario and US-ALRT-006's mute/quiet-hours story are both reactions to that. Before any pixel is drawn we need evidence on: which events the owner and the account managers actually want interrupted for, which they want logged only, how they expect a one-shot alert to behave after it fires, and what "critical, cannot be muted" should contain.

This research also decides the **critical-override list** (US-ALRT-006 scenario 3) whose contents must be "explicit, documented and covered by tests" per the story's NFR — that list is a product decision, not an engineering one, and this ticket is where it is made.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Notifications are the single most common place a product breaks WCAG 2.2.1 (no timing-based loss of information) and 4.1.3 (status messages). E40 ships an auto-dismissing toast, a live-updating stream, a sound channel and a preference matrix — four classic traps. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes a11y default-on for every UI surface, and `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` is the bar. This review happens *before* handoff so defects are corrected in Figma, not in React.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
- 4–6 moderated sessions (owner + the account-manager personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`) with a concept probe covering: a price alert firing, a detector alert firing, a storm of 25 firings, a muted symbol, quiet hours, and a risk lockout arriving during quiet hours.
- Competitive teardown of alerting in TradingView, Bookmap and Sierra Chart: firing modes, notification surfaces, snooze affordances, history retention.
- **Deliverable 1** — `docs/design/research/e40-alert-attention.md`: findings, verbatim quotes, and an interruption taxonomy mapping each notification kind (alert / rule fire / order reject / risk / system / recorder) to a recommended default channel set.
- **Deliverable 2** — the ratified **critical-override list** (candidate set from US-ALRT-006: daily-loss breach, liquidation proximity, connection loss; plus kill-switch engagement and fan-out partial failure from E34/E39) with a written rationale per entry, handed to E40-S02 and E40-Q01 as a test oracle.
- **Deliverable 3** — the storm-suppression product rule: threshold, aggregation window, and the wording of the summary notification, feeding E40-K01 and E40-T03.
- Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer and the Owner.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
- Written review of SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, producing `docs/design/a11y/e40-alerts-a11y-review.md`.
- **Live-region strategy** ratified and documented per surface: SCR-092 toast `role="status"`; SCR-014 `aria-live="polite"` escalating to `assertive` only for order rejects and risk lockouts; error/rejection toasts routed to CMP-212's separate `role="alert"` region so a critical rejection is never queued behind alert chatter.
- **Timing audit**: every auto-dismissing element paired with a persistent record in SCR-014; pause-on-hover/focus confirmed; no information exists only for a bounded time.
- **Keyboard maps**: full keyboard route for each surface — open centre, move through items, action an item, mark-all-read, snooze, dismiss, escape; the SCR-115 matrix navigable by row and column; the sound preview reachable.
- **Announcement throttling**: a documented rule for a burst of firings (announce the summary, not each item) so a screen reader is not flooded — the a11y counterpart of storm suppression.
- **Non-colour encoding** check: severity, status, snoozed, disabled, delivery-failed all encoded by icon + text.
- Contrast verification of every state in dark, light and high-contrast themes; focus-visible rings on every interactive element at ≥3:1.
- Defects logged back onto E40-D02/E40-D02 and fixed before those tickets close.

## Out of scope
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
Any hi-fi or wireframe pixels (E40-D02/D03). Sound design asset selection (E40-D02). Prometheus/Alertmanager operational alerting (E04).
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
The built-implementation audit (E40-Q02). Non-alert shell chrome (E10).

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
```gherkin
Scenario: Findings are evidence-backed
  Given the research report is submitted for sign-off
  Then every recommendation cites at least two participant observations or a competitive precedent
  And each is tagged with the US-ALRT id it informs
Scenario: The critical-override list is decision-ready
  Then the list names each overriding notification kind, its source module, and why muting it is unsafe
  And the Owner has explicitly accepted it in the ticket
Scenario: A contested default is escalated, not silently chosen (edge)
  Given participants split on whether desktop notifications default on
  Then both options are written up with consequences and the Owner makes the call on the ticket rather than the designer picking silently
Scenario: Storm threshold is specified numerically (failure guard)
  Then the report states a concrete threshold and window (e.g. ">20 deliveries per user per 60 s") rather than an adjective, so E40-T03 can implement it without interpretation
```
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
```gherkin
Scenario: Every surface has a documented live-region decision
  Then the review states, per surface, the region role, its politeness, what is announced and what is deliberately not
Scenario: No information is lost to timing
  Given any auto-dismissing toast
  Then the review demonstrates the same content is retrievable from SCR-014 afterwards, satisfying WCAG 2.2.1
Scenario: A firing storm does not flood the screen reader (edge)
  Given 25 alerts fire in one minute
  Then the documented announcement rule produces one summary announcement, and the individual items remain readable on demand
Scenario: Defects block handoff (failure)
  Given a review defect of severity major
  Then E40-D02 cannot start until it is fixed in the design file and re-verified
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
Sessions run against the E26 replay harness on staging (demo) so participants see real recorded bursts rather than mock data — a synthetic storm is not credible enough to elicit real preferences. Recruit through the Owner; sessions ≤45 min; consent recorded.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Use the `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` review template. Where the standard and the screen catalogue disagree (e.g. politeness level), the standard wins and the catalogue entry is corrected by a docs PR filed from this ticket.

## Test plan
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
N/A — research. Validation is the sign-off, plus the downstream check that E40-Q01 can write the critical-override test matrix directly from Deliverable 2 with no further questions.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Manual review with an accessibility specialist plus one screen-reader user session over the prototype (NVDA + VoiceOver). Findings tabled with severity (blocker / major / minor) and an owner.

## Security notes
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
Session recordings may show account balances and symbols; store in the private design drive, classify Internal, redact account identifiers in the published report. No credentials are shown to participants.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Announcement text must not read out anything the visual UI redacts — confirm no channel reads a webhook URL or secret aloud.

## Accessibility notes
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
At least one session includes keyboard-only and screen-reader use of a notification stream, so the a11y strategy in E40-D01 starts from observation rather than from the standard alone.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
This ticket *is* the accessibility note; its output is the a11y contract that E40-S01..S04 implement and E40-Q02 verifies.

## Performance notes
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
The 2 s condition-to-toast budget (SCR-092) is tested for *perceived* adequacy: does a 2 s delay change trader behaviour? Record the answer; it either confirms the budget or escalates it to the Architect.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
Announcement throttling interacts with the 250 ms WS cadence: the documented rule must not require per-message DOM live-region writes at 4 Hz.

## Observability
### Part A — UX research: how a trader wants to be told, and what they ignore
N/A.
### Part B — Accessibility design review of the alert surfaces before handoff
N/A.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Report merged at `docs/design/research/e40-alert-attention.md`.
- [ ] Critical-override list ratified by the Owner, linked from E40-S02 and E40-Q01.
- [ ] Storm threshold and window stated numerically, linked from E40-K01/E40-T03.
- [ ] CDO sign-off comment posted.
- [ ] Findings presented at a design review.

- [ ] Accessibility lead sign-off.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Informs E40-D02, E40-D02, E40-K01, E40-T03, E40-S02, E40-Q01.

title: Spike: choose the analytics query tier (Postgres vs DuckDB/Parquet)
body:
## Context
`GET /journal/analytics` must return totals plus up to seven breakdowns (`symbol`, `tag`, `hour_of_day`, `day_of_week`, `side`, `account`, `setup`) and an equity curve at `trade | hour | day | week` granularity, server-computed, for up to 10 000 trades, with SCR-095 interactive within 800 ms and breakdown queries within 2 s (US-JRN-008 NFR). `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` gives two candidate tiers: Postgres 16 (C-storage, authoritative) and Parquet+DuckDB (C18, "cold archive, analytics, long replay"), and `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` already declares a `journal_trades/ ym=.../ part-*.parquet` cold layout and a "Unified journal: cold Parquet + live Postgres" query pattern.

Choosing wrongly is expensive in both directions: Postgres-only risks blowing the 2 s budget on wide `GROUP BY` with tag joins over long ranges; DuckDB-only introduces a freshness seam (a trade closed a minute ago must appear immediately) plus a second RBAC enforcement point, which is a security risk, not just an engineering cost. This spike decides, with numbers, before E41-T03 is written.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A benchmark harness under `services/api/journal/bench/` generating synthetic `journal_trades` + `journal_trade_tags` at 1k / 10k / 100k rows with realistic tag cardinality (~40 tags, ~3 tags/trade) and 6 accounts.
- Measure, for each tier and each row count, p50/p95 wall time for: (a) totals only; (b) totals + all seven breakdowns; (c) equity curve at `trade` granularity; (d) MAE/MFE scatter payload; (e) a filtered query (account + symbol + tag + date range).
- Measure the same with a **hybrid** shape: Postgres for ranges within the hot window, DuckDB over Parquet beyond it, unioned - including the cost and correctness of the boundary.
- Evaluate index options on Postgres (the existing `ix_jt_time`, `ix_jt_symbol`, `ix_jt_account`, `ix_jt_outcome`, `ix_jt_setup`; candidate covering index and a materialised daily rollup).
- Evaluate how RBAC account scoping is enforced in each tier (a DuckDB path must not bypass the `granted_accounts` scope).
- Output: **ADR-0016 "Journal analytics query tier"** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, with the decision, the measured evidence table, the rejected options and the freshness/consistency contract.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the production endpoint (E41-T03); any change to the hot/cold roll-off job (E16); backtesting analytics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Decision is evidence-based
  When the spike closes
  Then ADR-0016 exists with a measured p50/p95 table for every tier x row-count x query combination listed in Scope
  And the chosen tier meets <=2 s for the full breakdown query at 10 000 trades on the reference dev machine

Scenario: Freshness contract stated
  Given the chosen design involves any non-authoritative store
  Then the ADR states the maximum staleness in seconds, how a just-closed trade becomes visible, and what the UI must display while a result is stale

Scenario: RBAC is not weakened
  Then the ADR shows how account scoping is enforced in the chosen tier and demonstrates a query that a Manager cannot widen to another account

Scenario: Timebox respected
  Given the spike exceeds 3 engineer-days
  Then it is closed with the best-supported recommendation and the residual uncertainty recorded as a risk on E41-T03 rather than running open-ended
```

## Technical notes / design
Reference machine: the WSL Ubuntu dev environment from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`. Synthetic data must use `numeric(38,18)` columns as declared, since decimal aggregation cost is part of what is being measured - benchmarking with `double precision` would flatter Postgres and invalidate the result. Tag breakdowns require joining `journal_trade_tags`, which is the most expensive shape; measure it explicitly rather than extrapolating from the symbol breakdown.

Default hypothesis to test, not to assume: Postgres with a covering index is sufficient at 10k, and the DuckDB path only earns its keep beyond ~100k trades, which this single-owner deployment will not reach within R3-R5. If the evidence supports it, ADR-0016 records "Postgres only for now; the Parquet layout stays as the archive format" and E41-T03 ships one code path.

## Test plan
The harness is the test: it is committed, reproducible via `make bench-journal`, and its dataset generator is seeded so numbers are comparable across reruns. A regression run of the harness is folded into E41-Q02.

## Security notes
The spike must not use production or real demo data - synthetic only. The RBAC evaluation above is a required output because an analytics path that reads Parquet directly could otherwise sidestep the API's `granted_accounts` scoping (threat: horizontal escalation, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 10 authorisation testing).

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend spike).

## Performance notes
Budgets under test: `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 13 (REST read p95 <150 ms), SCR-095 (interactive <=800 ms at 10 000 trades), US-JRN-008 NFR (breakdowns <=2 s at 10 000 trades).

## Observability
Defines the metric `journal_analytics_query_seconds` (histogram, labelled by `group_by` cardinality and tier) that E41-T03 must emit.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Benchmark harness committed and reproducible.
- [ ] Evidence table complete for all tier x size x query combinations.
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` and referenced from `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`.
- [ ] Architect review recorded; E41-T03 updated with the chosen approach before it enters Ready.
- [ ] Residual risks recorded on E41-T03 and, if material, in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E07 (Storage spike & data-tier wiring - the QuestDB/Parquet/Postgres substrate must exist to benchmark against).

## Branch
`spike/journal-analytics-tier`

## References

title: Hi-fi: SCR-143/144 health and incidents, SCR-146 backups, onboarding wizard
body:
## Context
These are the operations screens: the ones the owner opens when something is wrong, plus the one destructive flow in the product that can undo the database (**restore**), plus the guided onboarding wizard that turns an eight-step delegation procedure into something repeatable.

The visual language for system health was established by **E04-D01** ("Design the system-health, incident-log and degraded-state surfaces"), which already covers SCR-143/SCR-144/SCR-147 as part of the observability baseline. This ticket **extends** that language into the admin area rather than re-inventing it, and adds the two surfaces E04 did not cover: SCR-146 backups & restore and the US-ADMIN-013 onboarding wizard.

The restore wizard's copy is a safety control: `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-146 requires the impact preview to state "what a restore does and does not recover (market history is not restored from these backups)" and the sign-off explicitly requires that "restore impact copy reviewed by security".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Design pass for the E42-S08 statechart inspector screen (machine list, state diagram, event timeline, latch-acknowledge control), reusing this ticket's operations-screen visual language rather than a separate design track.
- Hi-fi for **SCR-143** system health and **SCR-144** incident log as admin-area applications of E04-D01's language (tiles with number + unit + state word, sparkline with table alternative, degraded and outage variants naming what stops working, link to the incident log, export diagnostics).
- Hi-fi for **SCR-146** backups & restore: the run table, backup-now with progress, verify, download-with-handling-warning, last-successful-backup age warning, failed-backup and failed-verification states, and the **restore wizard** as a stepper — choose backup → impact preview → typed confirm + step-up → progress → verification → summary.
- Hi-fi for the **manager onboarding wizard** (US-ADMIN-013, composing SCR-123 and SCR-017): the eight steps, the **blocked step** variant showing the exact 48-hour unlock time while the rest of the flow continues, the resume state with completed steps marked, and the secret-entry step with its "will not be shown again" statement.
- Hi-fi for the **trade-group governance** controls added to SCR-062 (enable/disable, who may use this group, reorder, version indicator) as an extension of E28's existing design, not a replacement.
- The **degraded-while-reporting-degradation** case drawn explicitly: SCR-143 when the health endpoint itself is unavailable — stale tiles with timestamps, shell and navigation still usable.
- Design-system contributions: CMP-178 SystemHealthTile (admin variants), CMP-210 HealthChips, CMP-023 Progress Bar in the wizard context, CMP-177 RecorderStatusRow reuse confirmation.

## Out of scope
- The Grafana dashboards (E04) — different audience, different medium.
- SCR-142 storage panel (E16/E07) and SCR-147 connectivity (E04/E46), linked to from SCR-143.
- The audit and flag screens (E42-D04).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every listed surface has hi-fi frames for every catalogue-listed state.
- Each screen's catalogue sign-off checklist ticked item by item, including SCR-146's "explicit statement of what a restore does and does not recover" and SCR-143's "the page works when the backend is partially down".
- The restore impact copy is reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer (blocking criterion, per the catalogue).
- The onboarding blocked-step variant shows the exact unlock time and demonstrably does not halt the flow.
- Every sparkline has its table alternative designed, not assumed.
- Continuity with E04-D01 demonstrated: a reviewer placing SCR-143 beside E04's designs sees one language, not two.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Done by end of Sprint 15, two sprints before the Sprint 17 builds (E42-S06, E42-S07).

## Technical notes / design
- Tiles are drawn as independently resolving units with their own status, matching the snapshot-plus-`system`-delta data model; no page-level spinner is drawn anywhere on SCR-143.
- The restore wizard's step 1 states the maintenance-mode precondition up front rather than failing at step 4, because the server enforces it as a `conflict`.
- The onboarding wizard's state is server-side and resumable across devices; the design reflects that ("continue on another device" is possible and shown), avoiding a local-draft metaphor the backend does not support.

## Test plan
- Validated in design QA (E42-D07) against the built screens, and in the chaos scenarios of E42-Q03 (the degraded-while-reporting case is both a design state and a test case).

## Security notes
- Restore and download are the two most dangerous controls in the epic: both are drawn with typed confirmation and step-up, and the download frame carries the secret-handling warning.
- The onboarding secret step must show that the secret is never redisplayed; the frame shows the fingerprint-and-status treatment for a revisited step.
- Health screens must not surface internal hostnames, connection strings or stack traces — the frames show only the fields the `HealthReport` schema exposes.

## Accessibility notes
- Each subsystem is a labelled row with a text status; no dot-colour reliance.
- The restore wizard and onboarding wizard are steppers with `aria-current="step"`; progress carries text percentages.
- Incident messages expand rather than truncate, so a screen reader can reach the full text.
- Reorder controls in trade-group governance are keyboard-operable buttons, not drag-only.
- Every figure carries units in its accessible name.

## Performance notes
- Frames annotate the ≤1 % added-load NFR for SCR-143 (one snapshot plus the existing `system` subscription, no polling), SCR-144's 10k-row 8 ms/frame budget, and the fact that backup/restore/verify are server jobs the browser only observes.

## Observability
Frames annotate `health.diagnostics_exported`, `incident.acknowledged`, `backup.run|verified|restored|downloaded` and the onboarding analytics events, including which are audited at high severity.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts delivered in Figma at the stated fidelity, linked from this ticket and from the relevant `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` entries.
- [ ] Every state in the screen's catalogue entry drawn (loading, empty, filtered-to-nothing, error, degraded, role variants, destructive-confirmation).

title: Accessibility design review and engineering handoff pack for the admin area
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 is explicit that there is no internal-tool exemption: "a11y: default-on (WCAG 2.2 AA) for any ticket that ships or changes a UI surface, **including owner/admin screens** — there is no 'internal tool, a11y doesn't matter' exception, since owner/admin screens are inside the same web app and RBAC-gated, not absent of users with accessibility needs."

This ticket is the accessibility review of the whole admin design set **before** it is built (cheap) rather than after (expensive, and often deferred), plus the handoff pack that makes the Sprint 16/17 stories implementable without a designer in the room — the condition the planning brief sets for every ticket: "a developer must not need to ask for more details."

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Accessibility design review** across E42-D03/D04/D05 outputs: keyboard paths end-to-end for every flow (elevate → administer → destructive confirm → done); focus order and focus-visible treatment; focus return after dialogs and drawers; screen-reader narration scripts for the re-auth gate, the unbind choice, the audit diff, the restore wizard and the onboarding stepper; colour-independence proofs for every status; contrast measurements for the admin tint and every state treatment; reduced-motion behaviour for every transition in the motion spec; target sizes and spacing per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- Specific high-risk reviews: the impersonation banner (must be announced and must not be dismissible into invisibility), the integrity-failure alert (announced once, then persistent), the countdown (announced at thresholds, not every tick), and disabled-with-reason controls (`aria-describedby` text supplied by design, not invented by engineering).
- **Handoff pack** per screen: annotated redlines (spacing, type, tokens), component mapping to `15-component-catalogue.md` ids, state inventory, data-source annotations (endpoint / WS topic / schema field names), copy deck (every string, including error and empty-state copy), the a11y contract per interactive element, and the motion table.
- A **single admin-area pattern sheet** engineering can hold beside the code: the destructive-action ladder, the degraded/stale expression, the audit-visibility convention and the re-auth interruption pattern.
- Handoff walkthrough session with the frontend engineers who will build E42-S01..S07, with questions captured and answered in the pack rather than in chat.

## Out of scope
- Design QA of the built screens (E42-D07) — this is the pre-build review; that is the post-build one.
- The automated a11y audit of the implementation (E42-Q05).
- Engineering implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every interactive element in the admin design set has a documented a11y contract (role, accessible name, keyboard behaviour, announcement).
- Keyboard-only paths documented end-to-end for: elevate into admin, invite a user, disable a user, bind/unbind an account, browse and export the audit log, toggle a flag, enter maintenance mode, run a restore, complete onboarding.
- Contrast measurements recorded for every text and UI-component treatment; all meet WCAG 2.2 AA (≥4.5:1 text, ≥3:1 components).
- Reduced-motion alternatives specified for every transition.
- The handoff pack is complete enough that a frontend engineer can build any listed screen without asking a question — validated by the walkthrough, with every question asked during it folded back into the pack.
- The pattern sheet is merged and referenced from every E42 story ticket.
- Accessibility specialist sign-off comment recorded; Done by end of Sprint 15.

## Technical notes / design
- The a11y contracts are written in the same vocabulary the component catalogue uses, so an implementer can move from contract to `15-component-catalogue.md` entry to code without translation.
- Copy deck is the single source for strings; engineering does not author admin copy, which is how "Are you sure?" dialogs lose their meaning.

## Test plan
- The keyboard paths documented here become the E2E keyboard tests in E42-Q02 and the manual screen-reader script in E42-Q05 — one list, three uses.
- The contrast measurements become the expected values for the automated checks.

## Security notes
- The copy deck is reviewed for security accuracy: a confirmation dialog that understates a consequence is a security defect. Specifically reviewed: delete ("history retained anonymised"), unbind ("positions remain / flatten first"), restore ("does not change anything on Bybit; market history is not restored"), purge ("irreversible; N GB covering dates X–Y"), flag change ("affects all users within 10 seconds").

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket *is* the accessibility work; its own DoD is the a11y review being complete, signed off, and reflected in the handoff pack.
- Reviewed against `05-accessibility-standard.md` in full, not selectively.

## Performance notes
The handoff pack carries each screen's performance budget so engineering treats it as a requirement rather than a footnote.

## Observability
The pack lists the audit/analytics events per control, so instrumentation lands with the first implementation PR rather than as a follow-up.

title: Write the black-box test plan and fixture set for the admin area
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` and the Story DoR both require a black-box test plan before a story is Ready. The admin area has fourteen user stories whose acceptance criteria include timing guarantees (sessions revoked within 5 s, flags propagated within 10 s, orders blocked within 200 ms), cross-user effects (a change by the owner must be observed by a manager's session), and states that only appear when something is broken (integrity failure, degraded subsystems, failed backup verification).

None of those are testable without a deliberate fixture set. This ticket writes the plan and builds the fixtures **before** the Sprint 16 stories start, so engineering and QA are testing the same list of scenarios rather than discovering the gap at the end.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Black-box test plan and fixtures for E42-T07 (statechart inspector read API) and E42-S08 (inspector screen), including a seeded chain_trips-degraded machine fixture for the latch-acknowledge scenario.
- Black-box test plan in `docs/qa/e42-admin-test-plan.md` covering US-ADMIN-001..014 as they are implemented in this epic, structured per story group: shell & re-auth (S01), users (S02), bindings & view-as (S03), audit (S04), flags & maintenance (S05), health/incidents/backups (S06), onboarding & governance (S07).
- Every Gherkin scenario from the seven stories mapped to a test case, plus the negative and boundary cases the stories imply but do not spell out: expired token mid-action, concurrent owner edits, a manager session open while their grant is revoked, an export requested over a range that exceeds the limit, a flag changed twice in one second.
- **Cross-session scenarios** defined explicitly, since they need two browser contexts: owner disables a manager while that manager is trading; owner revokes a grant while the manager is subscribed; owner enables maintenance while a manager has the order ticket open.
- **Fixture set**: seeded users in every status (`invited`, `active`, `disabled`), grant sets covering none/one/many accounts, a 10 M-row audit dataset (sharing E42-K01's generator), a **corrupted-chain** fixture, degraded and outage health payloads, a failed-verification backup, flags in every kind (boolean/percentage/variant) including a blocked `trading.live_enabled`, and an account under the 48-hour key restriction.
- **Exploratory charters** (timeboxed, one per theme): "try to see data outside your scope as a manager", "try to make the audit log look editable", "try to reach an admin screen without elevation", "try to lose form content by letting the token expire", "try to make two tiles block each other".
- Entry/exit criteria per story group and the epic-level regression pack definition (which cases re-run every sprint thereafter).

## Out of scope
- Executing the plan (E42-Q02, Q03, Q05) and the automated suites themselves.
- Security abuse cases (E42-X03) — related but owned by Security; this plan references them rather than duplicating.
- Load testing of non-admin surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every Gherkin scenario across E42-S01..S07 maps to at least one numbered test case; the traceability table is part of the plan.
- Every fixture listed in Scope exists, is committed, is deterministic, and is documented with how to load it.
- The corrupted-chain fixture reproducibly makes `POST /admin/audit/verify` report the expected `first_bad_id`.
- Cross-session scenarios specify the exact timing assertion (≤5 s, ≤10 s, ≤2 s, ≤200 ms) taken from the user story or the catalogue, not invented.
- Exploratory charters are written with a timebox and a "what would make this a finding" statement each.
- Plan reviewed by the story owners and the Security engineer; sign-off recorded.

## Technical notes / design
- Fixtures are code (seed scripts), not database dumps, so they survive schema migrations; each seed is idempotent and asserts its own post-conditions.
- The 10 M-row audit dataset is generated, not stored — the generator is shared with E42-K01 so the perf spike and QA use identical data.
- Timing assertions use the server's audit timestamps where possible rather than wall-clock in the test runner, to avoid flakiness masquerading as a failure.

## Test plan
- The plan is itself reviewed against `03-testing-strategy.md`'s pyramid: each case is labelled with the layer that should own it (unit / contract / integration / E2E / perf / security / a11y), so E42-Q02 knows what to automate and what stays manual.

## Security notes
- Fixtures must contain **no** real credentials, real Bybit keys or real user data. The generator produces obviously-synthetic values, and a test asserts no fixture matches a secret pattern.
- The corrupted-chain fixture is deliberately a *test-only* artefact and must never be loadable against a non-test database; the loader refuses if the target is not a test database.

## Accessibility notes
- The plan includes the manual screen-reader script derived from E42-D06's keyboard paths, so the a11y audit (E42-Q05) executes a written procedure rather than improvising.

## Performance notes
- The plan states the measurable budgets per screen (SCR-120 ≤800 ms, SCR-135 ≤400 ms filter / ≤2 s first page at 10 M rows, SCR-136 ≤300 ms, SCR-143 ≤1 % added load) and which ticket measures each.

## Observability
- Each test case names the audit event it expects, so "the feature works" and "the feature is recorded" are verified together — the audit log is a product requirement here, not an implementation detail.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `tests/` (or `docs/qa/` for plans) and runnable in CI.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario in the covered stories mapped to at least one executed case; traceability table posted on the ticket.
- [ ] Defects filed with repro steps, environment and `priority/*`; P0/P1 defects closed or explicitly accepted before sign-off.
- [ ] Results (pass/fail per scenario, environment, build SHA) posted as the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Flaky tests quarantined with an owner and a follow-up ticket rather than silently retried.

## Dependencies
- `E42-D02` — the wireframes enumerate the states that must be tested; writing the plan against the catalogue alone would miss the resolved cross-screen patterns.
