title: Implement GET /admin/overview and /admin/capacity read models
body:
## Context
SCR-120 Admin home is specified to aggregate "in one call plus `system` for live tiles" and to "render in <=800 ms and never block on the slowest subsystem" (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-120 performance note). That requires a **read model** in module M21 (Admin, `20-architecture.md` C15) that fans out to each subsystem with per-source timeouts and returns partial results rather than failing whole.

`GET /api/v1/admin/capacity` is the companion the users list and accounts list need: it "projects disk exhaustion from the current recorded-symbol set and retention policy (~0.5-0.75 GB/day/symbol at 200-depth) and reports per-UID rate-budget utilisation, so the owner can see a limit approaching instead of discovering it at a rejection" — and it carries the sub-account tier used by US-ADMIN-014, which "is an explicit recorded fact, never inferred".

Both endpoints are already declared in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`AdminOverview`, `CapacityReport`); this task implements them interface-first.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement `GET /api/v1/admin/overview` → `AdminOverview`: counts and headline state across users, accounts, keys nearing expiry, recorder health, storage headroom and open incidents. RBAC `admin:read`, scope none.
- Implement `GET /api/v1/admin/capacity` → `CapacityReport`: disk projection from `recorded_symbols` × `retention_policies` at the measured GB/day rate, per-UID rate-budget utilisation, and the **recorded** sub-account tier (`regular` = 5, `business_kyc` = 20) read from `settings` (scope `system`, key `accounts.subaccount_tier`) — never inferred from the observed account count.
- **Partial-result semantics**: each contributing source has its own ≤300 ms budget; a source that times out or errors yields `{status: "error", detail}` for its slice while the response still returns `200`. The response is never all-or-nothing.
- Short-TTL cache (5 s) per slice so a rapid reload does not re-fan-out; kill-switch and flag state are excluded from the cache (they are read live, matching the 5 s re-read rule for `is_killswitch` flags).
- Emit `admin.area_entered` audit rows from the admin router dependency (shared by every `/admin/*` route), carrying `{route, reauth_token_age_s}`.
- Prometheus metrics for the fan-out (per-source latency and error counters).

## Out of scope
- The health aggregation itself (`GET /admin/health`) — E04-T04; this read model consumes its summary.
- The frontend overview screen (E42-S01).
- Audit query/verify/export endpoints (E42-T02).
- Recorder/storage measurement (E16) — consumed via its existing service interface.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overview returns within budget
  Given every subsystem is healthy
  When GET /api/v1/admin/overview is called
  Then it responds 200 within 300 ms p95 with every slice populated

Scenario: A slow subsystem does not block the response
  Given the recorder service does not respond within its 300 ms budget
  When GET /api/v1/admin/overview is called
  Then the response is still 200 within 500 ms
  And the recorder slice carries status "error" with a detail string
  And every other slice is populated

Scenario: Capacity reports the recorded tier
  Given settings key accounts.subaccount_tier is "regular"
  Then CapacityReport states a sub-account cap of 5 and names the tier as a recorded fact
  And changing the recorded tier to business_kyc reports a cap of 20 and is audited

Scenario (failure): Non-owner access
  Given a manager token without admin:read
  Then both endpoints return 403 and an audit entry is written

Scenario (edge): No recorded symbols
  Then the disk projection reports zero growth with an explicit "nothing is recorded" marker rather than a null
```

## Technical notes / design
- Module M21 (Admin) service `AdminOverviewService` fans out with `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` under a per-source `asyncio.timeout(0.3)`; exceptions are mapped to a slice-level error object, logged with the source name and `request_id`, and never propagated.
- Disk projection: `projected_bytes = Σ_symbol(measured_gb_per_day × effective_retention_days)`, with `measured_gb_per_day` taken from E16's `DiskBudget` (measured, not assumed) and falling back to the documented 0.5–0.75 GB/day/symbol band with an explicit `estimated: true` marker when no measurement exists yet.
- Rate-budget utilisation is read from the backend's own accounting (server-side counters + exchange response headers), consistent with SCR-147 — the API never queries Bybit to answer this call.
- Caching via an in-process TTL cache keyed by slice; cache entries carry `generated_at` so the client can render freshness.
- Audit dependency: a FastAPI router dependency on the `/admin` router writes `admin.area_entered`; it must be impossible to add an admin route without it (enforced by the Semgrep rule in E42-X03).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: fan-out with each source failing in turn (N cases) asserting 200 + partial; timeout mapping; projection maths incl. the estimated-fallback branch; tier resolution from settings; cache TTL and `generated_at`.
- **Contract**: response validated against `AdminOverview` / `CapacityReport` schemas from `22-api-openapi.yaml`; schemathesis run over both paths.
- **Integration**: against a seeded Postgres + stubbed recorder/health services.
- **Perf**: p95 ≤300 ms healthy, ≤500 ms with one timing-out source, measured in CI with a benchmark test.
- **Security**: RBAC matrix test (owner 200, manager 403 + audit, viewer 403, unauthenticated 401).
- Coverage ≥85% on `services/admin/overview`.

## Security notes
- Threats: **information disclosure** — the overview aggregates across every subsystem, so the response must contain no secrets, no connection strings and no key material (schema-enforced; a test asserts the serialised response matches no secret pattern). **Elevation of privilege** — `admin:read` required, deny-by-default, 403 + audit on denial.
- Data classification: Confidential operational data; the tier setting change is audited (`settings.change`).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task with no UI surface.

## Performance notes
- p95 ≤300 ms healthy / ≤500 ms degraded (derived from SCR-120's ≤800 ms end-to-end render budget, leaving the client its share).
- Per-source budget 300 ms; total fan-out is concurrent, not sequential.
- 5 s per-slice cache bounds load under repeated reloads; the screen itself adds no polling.

## Observability
- Metrics: `cv_admin_overview_source_duration_seconds{source}`, `cv_admin_overview_source_errors_total{source}`, `cv_admin_capacity_projection_bytes`.
- Audit: `admin.area_entered {route, reauth_token_age_s}`, `settings.change` for the tier.
- Logs: one structured line per degraded slice with `source`, `reason`, `request_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified by tests or a recorded measurement.

title: Implement the feature-flag service, control allowlist and system push
body:
## Context
US-ADMIN-007's NFR contains the single most important constraint in this epic: "flags are server-side with a client push; **no flag may weaken a security control**." A flag system without that guarantee is a privilege-escalation mechanism with a friendly UI.

The storage model exists (`21-database-schema.md` §3.9 `feature_flags`, `feature_flag_overrides`, resolution order user → role → percentage → default, kill-switch flags bypassing cache and re-read every 5 s) and the API is declared (`GET /admin/feature-flags`, `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}`). This task implements the service behind them, the push over the WS `system` topic, and the maintenance-mode control plane that SCR-148 drives.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags` → resolved flags with kind, description, value, default, overrides, `updated_by`, `updated_at`. Permission `flags:read`.
- `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` (`flags:write`, step-up required): validates against the flag's kind, requires a `reason`, writes `feature_flags`/`feature_flag_overrides` transactionally and emits the audited `flags.change` with before/after.
- **Security-control allowlist**: a declarative registry mapping each flag key to what it may gate, with an explicit deny list of categories (authentication, RBAC enforcement, audit writing, the native-SL invariant, withdrawal permission, rate limiting). A flag whose declared gate falls in a denied category fails **at startup**, not at write time — the system refuses to boot with an unsafe flag definition.
- `trading.live_enabled` special case: enabling requires `reason` **and** `evidence_url`; without them the call fails `validation_failed` / `gate_evidence_required` (the gate's evidence binding itself is E44-T04; this service enforces the precondition).
- **Push**: on any flag change, publish a `SystemUpdate {kind: "feature_flags", feature_flags: {...}}` frame to every connected session over the auto-subscribed `system` topic, filtered by role so a client only learns about flags it may see.
- **Maintenance mode** control plane: a kill-switch-class flag that blocks order acceptance server-side within 200 ms, cancels running algos, optionally keeps the recorder running, broadcasts the notice within 2 s, and is audited as `maintenance.enabled|disabled`.
- Flag-resolution caching with the documented exception: `is_killswitch` flags bypass the cache and are re-read every 5 s.

## Out of scope
- Enabling the live gate with its evidence record (**E44-T04**, which owns US-ADMIN-012 together with `E44-S01`) and the security centre (**E43-S02**, which owns US-ADMIN-010 / SCR-137). This task only enforces the precondition; it exposes no way to satisfy it.
- The kill-switch engine (E39) — maintenance mode is a separate, lighter control that composes with it.
- The console UI (E42-S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Flag change reaches every client
  Given three authenticated sessions are connected
  When a boolean flag is changed
  Then all three receive a system frame of kind feature_flags within 2 seconds
  And the effective value at each client matches server-side resolution

Scenario: No flag may weaken a security control
  Given a flag definition declares that it gates RBAC enforcement
  When the service starts
  Then startup fails with a clear error naming the flag and the denied category

Scenario: Live enablement requires evidence
  When trading.live_enabled is set to true without an evidence_url
  Then the call fails 422 with gate_evidence_required
  And no write occurs and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Maintenance mode blocks orders promptly
  When maintenance mode is enabled
  Then order acceptance is rejected server-side within 200 ms
  And every session receives the maintenance notice within 2 seconds
  And native exchange stops are untouched

Scenario (failure): Flag write conflicts
  Given two owners change the same flag concurrently
  Then one write succeeds and the other returns 409 with the current value
  And both attempts are audited

Scenario (edge): Kill-switch-class flag freshness
  Given a kill-switch flag is changed directly in the database
  Then the service reflects the new value within 5 seconds without a restart
```

## Technical notes / design
- Resolution: user override → role override → percentage rollout (`hash(user_id || flag_key)`) → default, exactly as documented in `21-database-schema.md` §3.9. The resolver is a pure function with a table-driven test per branch.
- The allowlist registry is code (`flags/registry.py`), not configuration, so it is code-reviewed and cannot be edited at runtime: `FlagSpec(key, kind, description, gates=Category.UI_SURFACE|...)`. A `Category` in `{AUTH, RBAC, AUDIT, RISK_INVARIANT, RATE_LIMIT}` is rejected at import time.
- Push path: the flag service publishes to the WS hub, which fans out on the `system` topic (auto-subscribed, un-unsubscribable per `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2); payload content is filtered by role, matching that section's "content filtered by role" note.
- Maintenance mode sets a process-wide gate checked by the order-acceptance dependency before any OMS work, so the 200 ms bound is structural rather than best-effort.
- Concurrency: flag writes take a row lock and compare `updated_at`; a mismatch returns `409` with the current value rather than last-write-wins.
- Error codes: `validation_failed`, `gate_evidence_required`, `stepup_required`, `forbidden`, `conflict`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: resolver truth table (user/role/percentage/default × boolean/percentage/variant); allowlist rejection at import for each denied category; evidence precondition; conflict detection; kill-switch cache bypass timing.
- **Contract**: `/admin/feature-flags` GET/PUT against the OpenAPI schema; `SystemUpdate` frames validated against `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9.
- **Integration**: three connected WS clients receiving the push within 2 s; maintenance mode rejecting an order within 200 ms measured end-to-end.
- **Security**: attempt to define a flag gating auth (must fail startup); attempt a flags:write without step-up (403 `stepup_required` + audit); role-filtered push asserting a manager does not learn owner-only flag keys.
- Coverage ≥90% (security-relevant module).

## Security notes
- Threats: **elevation of privilege via configuration** — the central threat, mitigated by the compile-time allowlist and a Semgrep rule (E42-X03) forbidding flag lookups inside auth/RBAC/audit modules; **tampering** (server-side resolution only; the client store is advisory for UI, never for enforcement); **repudiation** (every change audited with actor, reason, before/after); **DoS** (maintenance mode is itself protected by step-up so it cannot be used to halt trading maliciously).
- Fail-closed rule: if the flag store is unreachable, flags resolve to their **default** values, and safety-relevant defaults are the restrictive ones.
- Data classification: Confidential configuration. Requires `security` label and Security-engineer review.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- Flag resolution ≤1 ms p99 from cache; cache TTL 30 s for normal flags, bypassed for `is_killswitch` (re-read every 5 s).
- Push fan-out to all sessions within 2 s; maintenance-mode order blocking within 200 ms.
- The push carries only changed flags, not the whole set, to keep the `system` topic within its 1 000 ms throttle budget.

## Observability
- Audit: `flags.change {key, before, after, reason, evidence_url?}` (high severity), `maintenance.enabled|disabled`.
- Metrics: `cv_feature_flag_evaluations_total{key}`, `cv_feature_flag_changes_total{key,result}`, `cv_flag_push_latency_seconds`, `cv_maintenance_mode` gauge.
- Logs: startup logs the full flag registry with its declared gate categories, so an auditor can see what flags may touch.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified by tests or a recorded measurement.
- [ ] Backend coverage ≥85% on new/changed lines (≥90% for audit/RBAC-touching modules per `30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).
- [ ] OpenAPI (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) / WS (`23-ws-protocol.md`) / internal schema (`24-internal-schemas.md`) deltas merged **before** implementation (interface-first, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) and contract tests green.
- [ ] Alembic migration is forward+backward tested on a seeded database; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` updated.
- [ ] security: SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL) and SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Observability: metrics/log fields/audit actions listed below exist and are asserted in a test.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or explicit "QA capacity deviation" note).
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E09` — permission codes `flags:read`/`flags:write`, step-up enforcement and the audit writer.
- `E42-T01` — the admin router dependency that audits area entry, reused here.

## Branch
`feat/admin-screens-flags-api` — 2 PRs: (1) resolver + registry + REST, (2) push + maintenance mode.

title: Implement user lifecycle: contract deltas and the disable cascade
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-10-15 (DoR plan and decision record on #965).** R2 split this Task: it keeps the lifecycle contract deltas and the disable cascade (plan slices S1 and S3–S7). Account-access grants moved to E42-T08, user read/PATCH, role changes and admin sessions to E42-T09, and the deferred purge to E42-T10. R3 rewrote the acceptance criteria. Every section below follows the decisions recorded on #965: R1–R7, accepted by main-orchestrator, and O1–O7, accepted on an interim basis subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed) and lists #965 O1–O7 among the interim decisions open to veto. R8 (flags) and R9 (backlog hygiene) are not decided yet; #2710 tracks them together with this Task's estimate.

US-ADMIN-001's scenarios impose exact server-side semantics that the UI cannot fake:

- **Disable** (this Task): "their sessions are revoked **within 5 seconds**, their rules are disarmed, and their data is retained."
- **Delete** (E42-T10 since the split): "their audit and journal history is retained under an **anonymised reference**, and the deletion itself is audited."

US-ADMIN-002 adds the binding half, which E42-T08 now delivers: revoking an account grant must force-close the user's WS subscriptions for that account with a `revoked` frame (reason `account_scope_changed`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5), and permissions are re-checked "at subscribe time **and again on every change to the user's grants**" (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.3). `22-api-openapi.yaml` still calls that frame `unsubscribed` on `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access`; slice S1 corrects the wording (R3).

`22-api-openapi.yaml` already declares the routes, and `21-database-schema.md` §3.1 already defines `users`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access` and `sessions`. This Task lands the contract deltas for all four Tasks and implements the disable cascade behind `DELETE /users/{userId}`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Lifecycle contract deltas first (slice S1, C-6.1; #2658).** The OpenAPI and error-code changes for this Task and for E42-T08, E42-T09 and E42-T10 land here before any implementation (R4). Under O2 they include `acknowledge_unknown_positions` on `updateUser` for a change to `status: disabled`, because that `PATCH` runs this Task's cascade (E42-T09); its description names the cascade and `409 positions_unknown`, as `deleteUser`'s does.
- **`DELETE /api/v1/users/{userId}` (soft disable).** Set `status=disabled`; revoke **all** sessions; soft-revoke every account grant (`can_view=false`, `can_trade=false`, never a `DELETE`, so the freeze columns and `max_daily_loss_usd` survive: O4, C-12.5); disarm every rule the user authored; revoke the open invite of a user who is still `invited` (R6); retain all data. Emits one `users.disable` (R5).
- **Positions (O2).** The cascade never flattens positions or cancels orders, and no lifecycle action places an order; flatten-first stays a separate OMS action. The audit `after_state` records `positions_decision=leave` and `open_position_count`. While the count is unknown, the caller must send `acknowledge_unknown_positions=true`, otherwise 409 `positions_unknown` (AC7). The disable service enforces this, so `DELETE /users/{userId}` and E42-T09's `PATCH` to `disabled` behave alike.
- **Session revocation within 5 s.** Every session is revoked with reason `user_disabled` and recorded through B16 REVOKE, one `auth.session_revoked` per session (R5). The user's sockets then get `bye` (`user_disabled`) and close code 4403 (`23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5), so the client does not reconnect, and the next REST call from a revoked session gets 401 `unauthenticated`.
- **Fail-closed scope readers (O5, C-2.21).** The scope readers check `users.status`, so a disabled user's armed rules lose their permissions at once, before the asynchronous disarm finishes. Slice S5 adds them, before slice S6 serves the route.
- **Last-owner protection on disable.** Disabling the only remaining Owner returns 409 `conflict`, a self-target returns 403, and a disable racing a demotion can never leave the installation without an enabled Owner (one transaction under the owner lock).
- **Audit (R5, C-2.9).** Every mutation is audited write-ahead with before/after, and refused calls from a forbidden role or against oneself are audited too. If the audit writer is unavailable, the call returns 503 `audit_unavailable` and nothing changes (AC8).
- **Docs (R5, slice S4, C-15.2).** `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4 adds `user_disabled` to `sessions.revoked_reason`. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5 uses the user-lifecycle names that `audit/actions.py` registers instead of `user.created`, `user.disabled` and `user.role_assigned`. SCR-122's audit line in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` names `users.access_change` instead of `user.assignment_changed`.
- **Flag (C-4.13, C-4.14).** No runtime flag on any cascade step: the cascade enforces RBAC and audit, which no flag may gate (C-4.14). The work stays dark instead: slices S3–S5 add no route, and `DELETE /users/{userId}` stays `not_mounted` in the RBAC matrix until slice S6 serves it. This is R8's proposal on #965; it has no recorded decision yet (#2710), and C-11.1 #13 needs one before this Task is marked Ready.
- Moved by the R2 split: `?purge=true` (E42-T10); `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` (E42-T08); `PATCH /users/{userId}`, `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` and admin session listing and revocation (E42-T09).

Slices kept by this Task (from the DoR plan on #965; PR titles `feat(accounts-admin): <summary> (E42-T04)`, branches under `## Branch`):

| # | Summary | Slug | ~LOC | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | lifecycle contract deltas | `lifecycle-contract` | 320 | O1–O3, R1–R5 |
| S3 | disable store, owner lock, write-ahead audit | `lifecycle-store` | 380 | S1, #2508, O4 |
| S4 | disable service: B16 revoke, socket close | `lifecycle-service` | 360 | S3, O2, R7 |
| S5 | rule-disarm and scope adapters; fail-closed scope readers | `cascade-adapters` | 330 | S4, O5 |
| S6 | serve `DELETE /users/{userId}` | `delete-user-route` | 360 | S5, the STRIDE appendix (O1, #2729) |
| S7 | SR-029 end to end | `disable-cascade-e2e` | 280 | S6 |

The fail-closed scope readers (O5) moved from S7 to S5 in the review of #2654. Otherwise an Owner could disable a manager between the S6 and S7 merges while the manager's armed rules kept their permissions until the asynchronous disarm finished (SR-029, C-2.21). The six slices still total about 2,030 LOC.

## Out of scope
- Authentication, password hashing, TOTP and session issuance (E09).
- Rule engine internals — this task calls the disarm interface (E35) rather than reimplementing it.
- The admin UI (E42-S02, E42-S03).
- The `ws` transport close semantics themselves (E10/E09) — consumed.
- Account-access grants (E42-T08); user read/PATCH, role changes and admin sessions (E42-T09); the deferred purge with its migration, anonymisation and the surrogate (E42-T10, O6) — the R2 split of 2026-10-15.
- Flattening positions or cancelling orders (O2).
- Alerts of a disabled user, which keep evaluating today: an E40 follow-up (O7).
- A user-row version counter or `grants_version` (dropped by R7).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: AC1 Disable revokes sessions within 5 seconds
  Given manager M has two active sessions and one armed rule
  When an owner disables M
  Then within 5 seconds on a fake clock M's next REST call gets 401 unauthenticated
  And every socket of M receives bye with reason user_disabled and closes with 4403
  And M's rule is disarmed
  And all of M's data is retained

Scenario (edge): AC5 Disable is audited once and idempotent
  Given manager M has no sessions
  When an owner disables M
  Then exactly one users.disable audit record is written
  When the owner disables M again
  Then the call returns 204, changes nothing and writes no further audit record

Scenario (failure): AC6 A self-target is refused
  When an owner disables themselves
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): AC6 The last owner cannot be disabled
  Given owner A is the only enabled owner
  When an owner disables A
  Then the call returns 409 conflict and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): AC6 A demotion racing a disable keeps an owner
  Given owners A and B are the only two owners
  When a demotion of A races a disable of B
  Then at least one enabled owner remains
  And the losing call writes no audit record

Scenario (failure): AC7 Unknown positions need an explicit acknowledgement
  Given M's open-position count is unknown
  When an owner disables M without acknowledge_unknown_positions=true
  Then the call returns 409 positions_unknown and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): AC8 Audit unavailable
  Given the audit writer is unavailable
  When an owner disables M
  Then the call returns 503 audit_unavailable and nothing changes
```
AC2 (history retained under an anonymised reference), AC3 (grant revocation ends the subscription with `revoked`, not `unsubscribed`) and AC4 (parallel cross-demotions, exactly one wins) moved with their scope to E42-T10, E42-T08 and E42-T09 (R2). The numbering is kept so the slice plan's test names still map; AC6–AC8 also apply to the routes of those Tasks.

## Technical notes / design
- **One transaction per disable (R7).** Lock the user row, lock the owner rows as #2508 does, apply the change (status, session rows, soft revoke of grants), run `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`, write the audit record ahead through the hook, then commit. The audit writer is WAL-first and outside the database transaction (`audit/writer.py`), so the hook runs only after the constraints pass, and a raise from it rolls the transaction back (AC8; `test_audit_hook_raise_rolls_back`).
- **After commit (R7).** Record B16 REVOKE for each revoked session, end the user's sockets, push `user_disabled` (`ConnectionRegistry` in `ws/permissions.py`, with #2318), disarm the user's rules through B9 DISARM (slice S5) and revoke an open invite (R6). A failure in any of these steps is counted and alerted, never rolled back.
- **Sockets.** End them through `ConnectionRegistry.user_disabled(user_id)` (reached as `app.state.ws_events.user_disabled`), or through `RevocationHub.revoke(session_id, "user_disabled")` per session, which sends the same `bye` and closes 4403 since #2581 merged (2026-10-15). Never end a disable with another reason: every other reason closes 4401, which tells the client to refresh its token and reconnect (comment on #965, 2026-10-15 18:59Z).
- **No version counters (R7).** A user-row counter or `grants_version` would add per-frame database reads in the WS lane. Changes are pushed through `user_disabled` and `grants_changed` plus #2318's versioned permission snapshots.
- **Last-owner protection.** Lock the owner rows inside the transaction (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, as #2508 does); a check-then-act without the lock is exactly the race AC6 tests.
- **Fail-closed scope readers (O5, slice S5).** Add `u.status = 'active' AND u.deleted_at IS NULL` to `_PERMS` (`storage/repositories/scope_sqlalchemy.py`) and `_PERMS_SQL` (`storage/repositories/identity_sqlalchemy.py`). B9 defers DISARM while a rule is evaluating or acting (`28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B9.3), so safety rests on O4 and O5. Slice S5 adds both predicates before slice S6 serves the route. The E35 lane is told.
- **Positions (O2).** Read the open-position count before the change. `_NoPositionStore` (`app.py`) reports it as unknown, which needs the acknowledgement (AC7), as `POST /users/{userId}/mfa/reset` does.
- **Error codes** come only from `x-error-codes` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `validation_failed` (400), `unauthenticated` (401), `forbidden` (403), `step_up_required` (403, no live step-up for the `users` action class), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409, last owner), `positions_unknown` (409, AC7) and `audit_unavailable` (503, AC8), which slice S1 registers (R4). `version_conflict` (412) is the stale `If-Match` of E42-T09's `PATCH /users/{userId}`, the only lifecycle route that takes `If-Match`; slice S1 documents it there.

## Test plan
Named tests per slice (from the DoR plan on #965):
- **S1:** `test_openapi_conformance`; `test_route_matrix` (new rows `not_mounted`); `error_registry_single_source`; `python scripts/generate_protocol_models.py --check`.
- **S3** (Postgres, `@pytest.mark.integration`): `test_disable_one_tx` (AC1); `test_keeps_freeze_and_cap` (O4); `test_audit_hook_raise_rolls_back`; `test_last_owner_409` (AC6); `test_concurrent_demote_and_disable_keep_owner` (AC6: 10 pairs behind #2508's lock-hold barrier; the loser gets 409 and writes no audit); `test_twice_one_audit` (AC5).
- **S4:** `test_step_order`; `test_b16_revoke_per_session`; `test_store_failure_no_post_commit`; `test_post_commit_failure_alerts`; `test_self_target_403_audited` (AC6); `test_positions_decision_never_flattens` (O2); `test_invited_revokes_invite`; `test_log_and_metrics_per_step`.
- **S5:** `test_disarms_owner_user_id_rules`; `test_refused_rule_does_not_stop_loop`; `test_idempotency_key_deterministic`; `test_scope_refresh_failure_fails_closed`; `test_disabled_user_no_rule_perms` (O5).
- **S6:** `test_guard_order_before_change`; `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; `test_self_target_403`; `test_last_owner_409`; `test_audit_down_503` (AC8); `test_positions_unknown_409` (AC7); `test_twice_204_one_audit` (AC5); `test_purge_400_flag_off` (`?purge=true` answers 400 until E42-T10's S14 serves it; the name assumes R8's flag, which is still undecided, #2710).
- **S7:** `test_rest_401_ws_4403_within_5s` (AC1); `test_rule_disarmed_audited` (AC1); `test_data_retained` (AC1); Postgres `test_delete_route_two_sessions_one_rule` (AC1).
- The 5-second bound runs on a fake clock; no sleeps and no network. Until #2525 merged (2026-10-15), WS private topics were deny-all in the deployed app, so AC1 could be proven only in-process. The real backend now loads the WS principal from the store (`build_ws_principal_loader` in `app.py`), so `test_delete_route_two_sessions_one_rule` can assert the socket close against the deployed app as well.
- Coverage ≥90% (security-relevant module M19).

## Security notes
- Interim threat model (O1): `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D1–D6 plus U4, U24 and U25 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`. The user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (#2729) merges before slice S6.
- Threats: **elevation of privilege** (`DELETE /users/{userId}` is `users:write`, Owner-only, step-up gated, never self-targeted, and audited); **denial of service** (disabling the last Owner would lock the installation out permanently, hence the locked last-owner check); **repudiation** (write-ahead audit, refused calls included); **tampering with risk state** (the soft revoke keeps freeze state and caps, so a disable and a later re-grant cannot unfreeze a manager, C-12.5).
- `password_hash` is never returned by this route (schema-enforced).
- Data classification: PII (`users.email`, session IP) + Confidential (grants). Requires `security` label and Security-engineer sign-off per DoD §8.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- Session revocation observable within 5 s (US-ADMIN-001); target p95 ≤1 s through the `user_disabled` push rather than polling.
- Lifecycle mutations ≤300 ms p95 excluding the rule-disarm fan-out, which is asynchronous with its own audit.
- The last-owner lock is held for the duration of one short transaction only; contention is negligible at this user count but the lock is still correct at scale.

## Observability
- Audit (R5): one `users.disable` per disable (AC5), with before/after and the `positions_decision` and `open_position_count` fields (O2); one `auth.session_revoked` per revoked session, recorded through B16 REVOKE; refused calls from a forbidden role or against oneself (AC6). Any new action registers in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits it.
- Metrics: `cv_user_lifecycle_total{action,result}`; post-commit step failures are counted and alerted (R7). Session-close latency goes on the `auth_revocation_latency_seconds` histogram that E09-S03 specifies (`auth/metrics.py`, `docs/ops/runbooks/auth-rbac.md` §4), not on a second histogram.
- Logs: one structured line per cascade step with the step name and outcome, correlated by `request_id`.

## Dependencies

- Before slice S3: #2508 (owner lock and write-ahead audit for role changes), which builds on #2502. Before slice S4: #2318 (versioned WS permission snapshots). Before slice S6: the user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (O1, #2729). #2525, which an end-to-end proof in the deployed app needed, merged on 2026-10-15.

## Branch

title: Wire the admin health, incidents and backups read models to the admin API
body:
## Context
SCR-143, SCR-144 and SCR-146 need three read models that sit between the observability/ops machinery and the admin UI: the full health report, the incident read model over `system_events`, and the backup run list with its verify/restore job surfaces. All three are declared in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`GET /admin/health`, `GET /admin/incidents`, `GET|POST /admin/backups`, `POST /admin/backups/{backupId}/verify|restore`).

`GET /admin/health` is implemented by **E04-T04** as part of the observability baseline; `GET /admin/incidents` is described as "read-model over `system_events` at `error` and `critical` severity, grouped into incidents with first/last occurrence and affected component". This task delivers the incident grouping and the backup admin surface, and adapts the E04 health payload to the `system` WS topic's component vocabulary so the UI has one shape, not two.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /api/v1/admin/incidents?status&cursor&limit`: group `system_events` rows at `error`/`critical` into incidents keyed by `(component, signature)` with `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `count`, `status` (`open|acknowledged|resolved`), duration and resolution text; cursor-paginated.
- Incident **acknowledge** transition with an audited `incident.acknowledged`.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/backups` (list with kind/status filters), `POST /api/v1/admin/backups` (run now), `POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/verify`, `POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/restore` — all long-running operations returning a `job_id` polled through `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}` (plumbing shared with E42-T02's export).
- **Restore preconditions enforced server-side**: maintenance mode must be active; open positions require an explicit acknowledgement flag in the request; both are rejected with `conflict` rather than being trusted from the UI.
- Backup **download** issues a short-lived signed URL, audited at high severity, and never logs the URL.
- Health payload adaptation: map E04's `HealthReport` component names onto the `SystemUpdate.components[]` vocabulary so snapshot and delta agree; unknown components pass through rather than being dropped.
- Per-component staleness: each component carries `last_good_at` so the UI can mark a tile stale rather than showing a plausible but old number.

## Out of scope
- The probes, metrics registry and the health aggregation itself (E04-T04).
- The backup engine, scheduler and restore executor (ops/E45) — this task exposes and guards them.
- The UI (E42-S06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Incidents group repeated events
  Given 40 error-severity system_events share a component and signature
  Then they appear as one incident with count 40, a first and last occurrence and status open

Scenario: Acknowledge is audited
  When an incident is acknowledged
  Then its status becomes acknowledged
  And an incident.acknowledged audit entry records the actor

Scenario: Restore refuses without maintenance mode
  Given maintenance mode is off
  When a restore is requested
  Then the call returns 409 conflict naming maintenance mode as the precondition
  And no job is created

Scenario: Restore with open positions requires acknowledgement
  Given two positions are open and maintenance mode is on
  When a restore is requested without the acknowledgement flag
  Then the call returns 409 conflict stating that open positions must be acknowledged

Scenario (failure): Backup verification fails
  Given a stored backup whose digest does not match
  When verify runs
  Then the job completes with status failed and a reason
  And the backup row records the failed verification

Scenario (edge): Health component unknown to the client
  Given the health report includes a component the UI does not know
  Then it is still returned rather than filtered out
```

## Technical notes / design
- Incident signature = stable hash of `(component, error_class, normalised_message)`; normalisation strips ids, timestamps and symbols so the same fault does not fragment into thousands of incidents.
- Grouping is a materialised read model refreshed on write (the `system_events` insert path notifies), not an on-request aggregation — the screen must not pay for the grouping.
- Restore is the most destructive operation in the product; its preconditions are enforced in the service, not the router, so any future caller inherits them.
- Job plumbing reuses `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}` from E42-T02 (`kind` in `audit_export|backup|backup_verify|backup_restore|recorder_compact|recorder_purge`).
- Signed download URLs expire in 5 minutes and are single-use.
- Error codes: `conflict` (preconditions), `not_found`, `forbidden`, `rate_limited`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: signature normalisation (table-driven, including messages differing only by id/symbol/timestamp); precondition guards; staleness computation; health component mapping incl. pass-through.
- **Contract**: all listed routes against the OpenAPI document; job status transitions.
- **Integration**: seeded `system_events` producing the expected grouping; restore precondition matrix (maintenance on/off × positions open/closed × ack flag).
- **Security**: RBAC matrix; download URL expiry and single use; audit emission for download and restore.
- Coverage ≥85%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **destruction of data** (restore) — server-side preconditions, step-up, high-severity audit; **information disclosure** (backup artefacts contain envelope-encrypted secrets — download is signed-URL, short-lived, single-use, audited, never logged); **information disclosure via incidents** (messages may contain internal detail — the read model applies the same redaction allowlist as the audit exporter).
- Data classification: operational Confidential; backup artefacts Secret-bearing.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- Incident list first page ≤400 ms p95 over 1 M `system_events` rows thanks to the materialised grouping.
- Health snapshot ≤200 ms p95 (E04 owns the probe budget; this adapter adds no I/O).
- Backup list ≤200 ms; all long operations are jobs, never synchronous requests.

## Observability
- Audit: `incident.acknowledged`, `backup.run`, `backup.verified`, `backup.restored` (high), `backup.downloaded` (high).
- Metrics: `cv_incidents_open` gauge, `cv_backup_last_success_age_seconds`, `cv_backup_verify_failures_total`, `cv_restore_jobs_total{result}`.
- Alerting: `cv_backup_last_success_age_seconds` beyond the schedule interval pages per ADR-0014.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified by tests or a recorded measurement.
- [ ] Backend coverage ≥85% on new/changed lines (≥90% for audit/RBAC-touching modules per `30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).
- [ ] OpenAPI (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) / WS (`23-ws-protocol.md`) / internal schema (`24-internal-schemas.md`) deltas merged **before** implementation (interface-first, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) and contract tests green.
- [ ] Alembic migration is forward+backward tested on a seeded database; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` updated.
- [ ] security: SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL) and SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Observability: metrics/log fields/audit actions listed below exist and are asserted in a test.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or explicit "QA capacity deviation" note).
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E04` — health report, metrics registry, `system_events` writer.
- `E42-T01` — the audited admin router dependency and the shared job plumbing conventions.

## Branch
`feat/admin-screens-ops-api` — 2 PRs: (1) incidents read model, (2) backups + restore guards.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26 ADMIN (US-ADMIN-001..014)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §10 Admin (SCR-120..149), §11 global states (SCR-150..159)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-095, CMP-099, CMP-173..179, CMP-210
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26 ADMIN
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/users`, `/roles`, `/permissions`, `/admin/*`, `/me/sessions`)
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2 private topics, §15.9 `SystemUpdate`

title: Design QA the implemented accounts and key-vault screens against the handoff pack
body:
## Context
Design QA closes the loop: the built screens are compared against the E27-D06 handoff pack, state by state, in both themes and all densities, on real data from the demo environment. R3's quality gate names it directly - "design-QA on ticket, confirmation and danger states" - and this epic's danger states are exactly where a drift between design and implementation would matter most.

It runs in Sprint 16, after the five E27 stories land in Sprint 15, so that it inspects finished screens rather than work in progress.

## Scope / Deliverables
- State-by-state comparison of SCR-125, SCR-126, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-129 and SCR-079 against the handoff pack, in dark and light themes and compact, cosy and comfortable densities.
- Verification of the epic's non-negotiable visual rules on the running application: no reveal control exists anywhere for a secret; the withdrawal verdict is always explicit and text-based; no numeric value renders without its freshness; destructive actions require typed confirmation plus step-up.
- Copy verification: every rendered string matches the copy deck exactly, including error and empty-state text.
- Token verification: spacing, colour, type and motion resolve to design-system tokens, with no hard-coded values, checked in the DOM rather than by eye.
- Motion verification including the `prefers-reduced-motion` variants, and confirmation that balances do not tween.
- Defect list with severity, each linked to the screen and state, triaged with engineering and fixed before the epic closes.
- A short drift report noting anything the implementation revealed that the design got wrong, feeding the next epic's handoff checklist.

## Out of scope
Functional QA (E27-Q01 to E27-Q05); the accessibility audit (E27-Q04); security review (E27-X02); redesign work, which is raised as follow-up design tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state matches the pack
  Given the handoff pack's state inventory
  When each state is reproduced in the running app in both themes and all densities
  Then it matches the design, or a defect is raised with a screenshot and the exact discrepancy

Scenario: No reveal control exists
  Given the running application and its API
  When every screen showing a key, and every API response, is inspected
  Then no reveal affordance and no secret value is present anywhere

Scenario: Freshness is always present
  Given the SCR-079 drawer with live and with stale data
  When every numeric field is inspected
  Then each carries a freshness indicator, and the stale state shows the "stale since" badge

Scenario: Copy matches the deck
  When every rendered string is compared to the copy deck
  Then they match exactly, and any difference is raised as a defect rather than accepted as an improvement

Scenario: Tokens, not values
  When the DOM is inspected for the six screens
  Then spacing, colour, type and motion resolve to design-system tokens with no hard-coded values

Scenario: A defect is disputed
  Given engineering believes a discrepancy is intentional
  Then it is resolved by the Chief Design Officer or delegate before the epic closes, and the decision is recorded in the drift report
```

## Technical notes / design
Design QA is performed on the demo environment with real account data, not on Storybook alone, because several states in this epic only occur against real exchange responses - the 48-hour new-key restriction, an IP mismatch, a genuinely stale wallet snapshot.

Storybook is still used for the component-level check of CMP-175, CMP-176 and CMP-034 variants, where reproducing every state in the app would be impractical.

Hard-to-reach states are produced with the fault-injection fixtures built for E27-Q01 rather than by waiting for them to occur naturally.

## Test plan
Checklist-driven review executed by a product designer who did not implement the screens, with engineering available. Screenshot evidence captured for every state. Results recorded in `qa/design-qa/e27/` and linked here.

## Security notes
Design QA is the last chance to catch a visual security defect before the epic closes: a masked value that reveals on hover, an error toast that echoes a submitted secret, a withdrawal verdict rendered as a colour-only chip, or a screenshot path that captures credential input. Each of these is checked explicitly and, if found, raised at high severity. Findings overlap deliberately with E27-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Design QA includes a visual accessibility pass - focus indicators present and at >=3:1 contrast on every interactive element, disabled states distinguishable, states identifiable in greyscale, and the layout intact at 125% zoom and 200% text scaling. The full screen-reader and axe-core audit is E27-Q04; this pass catches the visual subset.

## Performance notes
Spot-check the perceived-performance budgets on the running app: the SCR-126 validating state appearing promptly and resolving within about 3 s, SCR-129's confirm control absent until the summary loads, and SCR-079 opening in about 100 ms from cache.

## Observability
Verify that the audit and analytics events listed in the handoff pack actually fire from the screens - a missing `account.tested` or `admin.key_health_viewed` is a defect found here as easily as in functional QA, and is raised the same way.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every state compared and evidenced with a screenshot.
- [ ] Defect list triaged with engineering; all high-severity items fixed before the epic closes.
- [ ] Copy and token verification complete.
- [ ] Drift report written and fed into the handoff checklist for the next epic.
- [ ] Signed off by the Chief Design Officer or delegate.
- [ ] Results committed under `qa/design-qa/e27/` and linked from this ticket.

## Dependencies
Blocked by all five implementation stories (**E27-S01** to **E27-S05**) and by **E27-D06**, which is the specification it reviews against.

`design/e27-design-qa` - review artefacts only; fixes land on the owning engineering branches.

title: Spike: per-trade override semantics and profile-change propagation to open tickets
body:
## Context
US-PROF-008 ("Per-trade profile overrides", Should) is the one part of this epic the plan marks as unresolved: its Refs line points at `OD "still open" SSper-account profile detail`, meaning the owner recorded the *shape* of overrides but not the exact rule set. The story fixes three invariants - an override "never widens a hard risk cap", it "resets to the profile default for the next ticket" after submit or cancel, and every override is "audited and journal-tagged" - but leaves open which fields are overridable at all, and how an override interacts with a profile edited mid-ticket.

The second open question is propagation. SCR-130 states "Changes propagate to open tickets within 2 s over the private channel so a stale profile is never used for sizing", but the WS topic catalogue in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` has no `profiles` topic - private topics are flat and enumerated (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`, `trade_groups`, `rules`, `alerts`, `recorder`, `system`). Either propagation rides an existing topic or the protocol needs an addition, and the protocol is frozen for R3 unless a decision says otherwise. This must be settled before E28-T02 finishes and before E28-S05 is designed.

This is a 2-day timebox, not production code.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Decision table: for each field of `AccountProfile` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.2), whether it is (a) overridable freely, (b) overridable downward only, or (c) never overridable. Starting position from the plan: leverage is capped (SCR-061 shows "capped by profile" on the control), size is overridable within the risk cap, allowed symbols are never overridable, `require_native_sl` is never overridable.
- Decision on override lifetime: per-ticket only (reset on submit or cancel) versus per-session, with the evidence for the choice.
- Decision on propagation transport: reuse of an existing private topic versus a `system` sub-event versus a REST re-fetch triggered by an existing event, measured against the 2 s budget and against the rule that the WS topic list is frozen for R3.
- Decision on mid-ticket profile edits: what happens to an open ticket whose profile changed underneath it (silent re-price, explicit "profile changed - review" state, or block).
- A throwaway prototype measuring end-to-end propagation latency from `PUT /profiles/{id}` to a ticket re-render over the chosen transport, on the R3 staging topology over Tailscale.
- **ADR-0016 "Per-trade profile overrides and profile propagation"** written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, following the ADR template, recording the decision even if it is "defer" (per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS5.2).
- Follow-up tickets filed against whichever path is chosen, with the findings linked.

## Out of scope
Implementing the chosen design (E28-T02 for propagation, E28-S05 for overrides); any change to the OMS or to E34's fan-out.

## Acceptance criteria
- The override decision table covers every field of `AccountProfile` with no field left unclassified, and is signed off by the Owner and the Architect.
- Propagation latency is measured, with a number recorded for the chosen transport, and it is at or below the 2 s budget stated in SCR-130 - or the transport is rejected and an alternative is measured.
- The mid-ticket-edit behaviour is decided and expressed as Gherkin that E28-S05 and E30 can consume directly.
- ADR-0016 is merged with status `decided` (or `deferred` with the missing input named and an owner assigned).
- Follow-up tickets exist and are linked; the prototype branch is either promoted through a normal Task or explicitly marked throwaway and left unmerged.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if the spike surfaced or retired a risk.

## Technical notes / design
Timebox: 2 days, agreed with the Architect. Decision rule agreed up front: if reusing an existing private topic cannot meet the 2 s budget without conflation loss, the fallback is an event-triggered REST re-fetch (`GET /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`) rather than adding a topic, because the R3 protocol freeze (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` SS5 item 4) outranks transport elegance.

The safety floor is fixed before the spike starts and is not up for negotiation: no override may widen `max_position_notional`, `max_daily_loss`, `max_open_positions`, `max_leverage_cap`, the allowed-symbol set, or `require_native_sl`. The spike decides only the permitted *narrowing* and the UX of expressing it.

## Test plan
Not a production-code ticket. The prototype carries a latency measurement script committed under `spikes/e28-override-propagation/` with its raw results, so the number can be reproduced.

## Security notes
The override surface is a privilege-escalation vector: an override that widens a cap defeats SR-052, SR-053 and SR-054 in one step. The decision table is therefore reviewed by the Security engineer as part of E28-X01's threat model, and the "downward only" property becomes an automated test in E28-S05 rather than a convention.

## Accessibility notes
The chosen override UX must be expressible without colour alone and must announce the "capped by profile" disabled reason, per SCR-061. The spike records the constraint for the designer; it does not design the control.

## Performance notes
Propagation budget 2 s end to end (SCR-130). Preview recomputation triggered by a propagation event must stay inside SCR-061's <=300 ms preview budget.

## Observability
Whichever transport wins, the follow-up ticket must add `cv_profile_propagation_seconds` so the 2 s budget is observable in production rather than only at spike time.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both questions answered with recorded evidence (decision table, measured latency numbers, prototype branch link).
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` with a status.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed and linked, with findings attached so implementers do not re-derive them.
- [ ] Prototype code promoted or explicitly marked throwaway; branch left unmerged if throwaway.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review and at the Design Review that precedes E28-D03.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated.
- [ ] Explicitly recorded on the ticket that this spike is not expected to produce production-shippable code.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T01** (the profile model the decision table is written against). Its output blocks **E28-S05** (overrides) and informs **E28-T02** (propagation) and **E30** (the ticket that renders overrides).

title: Automate the profiles, symbol-permission and trade-group E2E suite in Playwright
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` puts E2E at the top of the pyramid and the R3 quality gates require "Playwright web + Electron covering ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, bracket, fan-out, rule creation in both editors, alert firing, journal capture". E28 owns the profile and trade-group portions of that suite, and the suite is what protects the sizing path from silent regression once E30, E34 and E35 start consuming it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright suite under `tests/e2e/e28/`, running against the R3 demo staging environment with the E28-Q01 fixture set, in both the browser and the Electron shell.
- Journeys automated:
  1. Create a risk-based profile through SCR-131 with step-up, observe the worked example, save, and see the row on SCR-130 with its "changed since" value.
  2. Attempt 25x leverage with SOLUSDT allowed and assert the refusal names the symbol and its 20x maximum.
  3. Attempt to disable the native stop-loss and assert it cannot be done from the UI, and that a direct API call is refused with `native_stop_mandatory`.
  4. Edit a profile that has an open position and assert a new version is created while the position keeps its originating version.
  5. Apply a template through SCR-132 and assert it prefills the editor without writing, then save through the normal path.
  6. Deny a symbol in SCR-133, save in one call, then assert an order for that symbol on that account is refused with 403.
  7. Attempt to deny a symbol with an open position and assert the refusal and the recorded event.
  8. Create a group in SCR-062, break one member's key self-check in the fixture and assert "2 of 3 ready" with a textual reason.
  9. Attempt a demo+live group and assert the refusal.
  10. Open the SCR-061 preview, enter an intent, assert three ready rows sized by their own profiles plus one excluded row with its reason, and assert send is disabled when a stop is removed.
  11. Apply an in-cap override and assert it is marked, applied and reset after cancel.
- Concurrency journey: two browser contexts editing the same profile, asserting the version-conflict recovery path rather than a lost update.
- Deterministic control of time for the daily-loss rollover journey via a clock-injection fixture, so the boundary is testable without waiting.
- Stability work: no arbitrary sleeps, explicit waits on state, and the suite green three consecutive runs before it is accepted.
- Wiring into CI as a required check for the E28 paths, with traces and video retained on failure.

## Out of scope
Fan-out submission journeys and partial-failure remediation (**E34**'s suite); load and chaos (E28-Q03); the a11y audit (E28-Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
- All eleven journeys plus the concurrency journey are automated, pass against staging, and are green on three consecutive CI runs with zero flakes.
- Each journey asserts the user-visible outcome **and** the audit row it must produce, so a silently unaudited action fails the test.
- The suite runs in both the browser and Electron, with any Electron-specific divergence documented.
- Failure artefacts (trace, video, console log) are retained and attached automatically.
- The suite is a required check on the E28 code paths.
- Total runtime under 12 minutes so it does not become a merge bottleneck.

## Technical notes / design
Tests drive the UI and assert through the UI, with two exceptions that are deliberate: audit assertions read the audit API, and the "direct API call is refused" steps issue an HTTP request outside the browser context. Both exceptions are documented in the suite README so the black-box boundary is an explicit decision rather than a drift.

Step-up is handled with a deterministic TOTP seed in the staging fixture, so the second factor is scriptable without weakening the production path.

Each journey seeds and tears down its own data from the shared fixture, so journeys can run in parallel without ordering assumptions.

## Test plan
Self-verifying. Suite health is tracked by a flake-rate metric in CI; any test flaking more than once in twenty runs is quarantined and fixed rather than retried.

## Security notes
The staging TOTP seed and fixture keys are non-production, structurally valid but non-functional, and are stored as CI secrets rather than in the repository. The suite deliberately includes negative security journeys (native-SL disable, denied-symbol order, ungranted-account access), and those assertions are duplicated in E28-X03's suite so a deletion here does not silently remove the control's coverage.

## Accessibility notes
Every journey is driven through accessible selectors - roles and accessible names, never CSS classes or test ids where a role exists - so a regression that breaks an accessible name breaks the test. This is a deliberate, low-cost accessibility regression net underneath the dedicated audit in E28-Q04.

## Performance notes
The suite asserts the user-visible budgets it can observe reliably: preview updates within 300 ms of the last input and the save completing within 2 s, both measured with generous tolerance in CI and reported as a trend rather than a hard gate (the hard gates live in E28-Q03).

## Observability
Each run publishes pass/fail counts and duration to the CI dashboard; failures link to the trace. Audit assertions double as a check that the observability described in the stories is actually emitted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario of the covered stories is mapped to an executed test case with a pass/fail result recorded on the story.
- [ ] Defects raised with `priority/*`, reproduction steps, environment and evidence; P0/P1 defects closed before the epic is Done.
- [ ] Automated suites run in CI on the R3 demo environment and are green on three consecutive runs (no flakes).
- [ ] Coverage of the epic's acceptance criteria reported in the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Results and residual risk summarised on E28-Q05 and referenced by the epic ticket.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-Q01** (plan and fixtures) and by **E28-S01** and **E28-S03** (screens to drive). Journeys 10 and 11 additionally need **E28-S04** and **E28-S05** and are landed as those merge.

title: Run the performance, load and chaos scenarios for sizing, the risk guard and group preview
body:
## Context
Three hard numbers in this epic are budgets, not aspirations: the risk guard adds **<=5 ms p95** to the order path (US-PROF-004 NFR), the fan-out preview returns in **<=300 ms** for five accounts (SCR-061), and backend-added fan-out overhead is **<=50 ms + <=10 ms per additional account p95** (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` SS5.2, budget #4 fan-out sub-clause). All three sit inside the R3 hard gate of order submit -> ack p95 <300 ms.

The chaos requirement is equally concrete: the risk guard keeps in-memory counters, so a restart or a WS disconnect must not reopen a breached cap. R3's chaos gate demands "backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out - all resume to a correct, reconciled state"; the profile-owned part of that is counter reconstruction.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6/Locust scripts under `tests/load/e28/` for: `POST /trade-groups/preview` at five accounts sustained for 10 minutes; the risk guard exercised through the OMS submit path at the per-UID order rate across five accounts for one hour; profile save under concurrent editors.
- Micro-benchmark harness for `size_leg` and `guard.check` run in CI on every change to those modules, with a regression threshold that fails the build on a slowdown beyond the agreed tolerance.
- Measurement and recording of: guard p95 and p99 with warm and cold caches; preview p50/p95/p99 at 1, 3, 5 and 20 member accounts (20 being the Business-KYC ceiling); the per-account marginal cost, to verify the <=10 ms/account slope rather than only the 5-account point.
- Soak: the `trade_groups` WS projection at 50 groups x 5 legs for 60 minutes, asserting the 100 ms throttle holds, memory is flat and no frame is lost.
- Chaos scenarios, each with a defined correct outcome:
  1. Backend restart with a breached daily-loss cap - the cap must remain breached after the counters rebuild, and an entry attempted during the rebuild window must be refused, not permitted.
  2. Private WS disconnect and reconnect mid-session - counters reconcile from Postgres and no double-count occurs.
  3. Postgres becoming unavailable during a guard evaluation - the guard fails **closed** and raises the alert.
  4. Instrument cache unavailable during a profile save - the save is refused with `instrument_cache_unavailable` and a `Retry-After`, never saved unvalidated.
  5. Clock skew of +/-90 seconds across the 00:00 UTC rollover - the daily accumulator resets exactly once.
- A results report with the numbers, the environment they were measured on, and a pass/fail against each budget; regressions filed as `perf`-labelled Bugs.

## Out of scope
Fan-out submission load and the rate-limit governor (**E34**); engine FPS work; the 7-day R3 soak (`q09` in the roadmap).

## Acceptance criteria
- Guard evaluation p95 <=5 ms with a warm cache, measured over at least 10 000 evaluations; the cold-cache number is recorded separately and documented rather than hidden.
- Preview p95 <=300 ms at 5 accounts, and the marginal per-account cost is measured and reported against the <=10 ms/account slope.
- The `trade_groups` projection soaks for 60 minutes at 50 groups x 5 legs with flat memory and no lost frames.
- All five chaos scenarios produce their defined correct outcome; scenario 1 and scenario 3 are treated as safety-critical and a failure in either blocks the epic.
- The micro-benchmark harness is wired into CI with a regression threshold.
- Results are recorded in the report and referenced from E28-Q05 and from the epic.

## Technical notes / design
Measurements are taken on the R3 staging topology over Tailscale, matching the network assumption in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` SS4 - the Bybit RTT component is excluded from the backend-internal budgets and reported separately, per that document.

The marginal-cost measurement matters more than the headline: a preview that is fast at five accounts but quadratic in member count would pass a naive test and fail at twenty. Member counts are therefore swept, and the fitted slope is what is reported.

Chaos scenario 1 is run by killing the process rather than by a graceful shutdown, so the rebuild path is genuinely exercised.

## Test plan
This ticket is the test. Its own reliability comes from running each measurement three times and reporting the median with the spread, and from pinning the staging environment's resources so runs are comparable across weeks.

## Security notes
Fail-closed behaviour is a security property, not just a reliability one: scenario 3 verifies that a database outage cannot become a path to unguarded orders. Scenario 1 verifies that a restart cannot clear a lockout - which would otherwise be an availability-shaped privilege escalation. Both results are reported to the Security engineer for E28-X04. Load scripts use synthetic accounts on demo only and never touch a live UID.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend load and chaos.

## Performance notes
This ticket owns the epic's performance evidence. Budgets: guard <=5 ms p95; preview <=300 ms p95 at 5 accounts; fan-out backend overhead <=50 ms + <=10 ms/account p95; WS `trade_groups` 100 ms throttle sustained; profile save <=2 s including revalidation.

## Observability
The runs validate that the metrics the stories promise actually exist and are usable: `cv_sizer_duration_seconds`, `cv_risk_guard_seconds`, `cv_risk_guard_fail_closed_total`, `cv_tradegroup_preview_seconds`. A missing or unusable metric is filed as a Bug against the owning ticket, because an unmeasurable budget is an unenforceable one.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario of the covered stories is mapped to an executed test case with a pass/fail result recorded on the story.

- [ ] Coverage of the epic's acceptance criteria reported in the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Results and residual risk summarised on E28-Q05 and referenced by the epic ticket.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T04** (the guard) and **E28-T05** (the preview). Coordinates with **E29** for the OMS submit path used in the guard load test and with **E39** for lockout interaction in chaos scenario 1.

title: Create and edit a per-account profile from the admin profiles list and editor
body:
## Context
Covers **US-PROF-001** ("Define a per-account profile", Must) and **US-PROF-002** ("Sizing rules", Must) as one vertical slice over **SCR-130 Admin: per-account profiles list** (`/admin/profiles`) and **SCR-131 Admin: profile editor**. These are RBAC-gated screens *inside the web app* - there is no separate admin application (owner decision, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`).

SCR-130 is a table of one row per account showing leverage, sizing rule, SL/TP offsets, daily cap, max position and the allowed-symbol count, with a "changed since" diff column and an inline warning row for an account that allows all symbols ("(!) sub_002 allows all symbols - consider restricting"). SCR-131 is the editor, organised in the six sections the catalogue names: Leverage & margin, Sizing, Brackets, Risk caps, Symbols, Safety. Its accessibility rule is unusual and is a hard requirement: "every field has units and a worked example ('0.5% of 21 300 USDT ~= 106 USDT risk ~= 0.08 BTC at a 25-tick stop')".

Saving is a step-up-gated, fully audited action with a before/after diff (SCR-131: "`profile.updated` (step-up, full before/after diff)"), and the mandatory native-SL control is rendered as a floor that cannot be removed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-130** at `/admin/profiles` using CMP-001 Button, CMP-011 Tag/Chip, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-106 ProfileBadge: one row per account, the "changed since" column driven by the profile revision projection, the all-symbols warning row, an empty state, and row actions (edit, duplicate/clone, delete) routing into their own flows.
- Unbound-account flagging: an account with no usable profile is shown as unable to trade until bound (SCR-130 sign-off: "unbound accounts are flagged (they cannot trade until bound)").
- **SCR-131** editor using CMP-040 FormField, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-104 LeverageSlider, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-138 RiskCapMeter, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice - all six sections, wired to `GET`/`POST`/`PUT /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles[/{profileId}]`.
- Sizing section offering all four modes (fixed qty, fixed notional, % equity, risk-based) with mode-specific parameter fields and a rounding control, per US-PROF-002.
- **Live worked example** beneath the sizing section, recomputed from the account's current equity and the selected symbol's tick/lot filters, showing notional, quantity, implied risk in USDT and in R, and the resulting initial margin - the three numbers US-PROF-002's scenarios demand. Below-minimum-lot results show the minimum and offer it as a one-click choice.
- Field-level validation rendering from the E28-T02 error contract, with each message bound to its input via `aria-describedby`, including the exchange-limit messages ("SOLUSDT allows at most 20x - your 25x would be rejected").
- Safety section: `require_native_sl` rendered by CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice as a permanently-on floor with an explanation of why it cannot be disabled; the control is not a toggle that fails on save, it is visibly non-removable.
- Save flow: diff summary before save, step-up re-authentication, optimistic concurrency via `If-Match` with a "someone else saved version N - reload" recovery path, and an explicit "applies to future orders only" statement (SCR-131 sign-off checklist).
- Clone/duplicate of an existing profile into a new name on the same or another account.
- Analytics `profile.list_viewed`; audit surfaced back to the user as a "last changed by X at T" line.

## Out of scope
Templates (E28-S02); the symbol permissions matrix (E28-S02); trade groups (E28-S03, E28-S04); overrides (E28-S05); the backend routes and validation themselves (E28-T02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create a profile
  Given I open sub_001's profile editor
  When I set leverage cap, sizing rule, default SL and TP offsets, max risk per trade, max daily loss, max concurrent positions and allowed symbols, and save with step-up
  Then the profile is versioned and saved, and it is shown on every ticket targeting that account

Scenario: Invalid combination is explained on the field
  When the sizing rule is risk-based but no default stop distance or ATR source is defined
  Then saving is blocked, the message appears on the stop field itself, and it is associated with the input for screen readers

Scenario: Worked example follows the inputs
  Given equity is 21300 USDT and the stop is 25 ticks
  When I set risk-based sizing at 0.5%
  Then the worked example reads approximately 106 USDT risk and 0.08 BTC, and it updates within 300 ms of the last keystroke

Scenario: Below minimum lot offers the minimum
  Given the configured rule computes a quantity below the symbol's minimum order quantity at the current equity
  Then a warning states the minimum and offers it as a one-click choice

Scenario: Leverage above an allowed symbol's exchange maximum
  Given SOLUSDT is on the allowed list
  When I set leverage to 25x
  Then saving is refused with a message naming SOLUSDT and its 20x maximum

Scenario: The native stop-loss floor cannot be removed
  When I look at the Safety section
  Then the require-a-native-stop-loss control is shown as permanently on with an explanation, and no interaction can turn it off

Scenario: Editing a profile in use creates a new version
  Given open positions exist under the current profile version
  When I save an edit
  Then a new version is created, the open positions keep their originating version, and the screen states that the change applies to future orders only

Scenario: Concurrent edit is recovered, not lost
  Given another owner saved a newer version while my editor was open
  When I save
  Then I am told the version changed and offered a reload, and my unsaved values are not silently discarded

Scenario: Step-up is required
  When I save without a current step-up session
  Then I am prompted for password and TOTP, and the save completes only after it succeeds

Scenario: An account that allows all symbols is flagged
  Given sub_002's allowed list is empty
  When the profiles list renders
  Then its row carries a textual warning suggesting a restriction, expressed in text and not by colour alone

Scenario: A manager cannot edit an account they were not granted
  Given I am a manager without a grant on sub_002
  Then sub_002 is absent from my list, and navigating directly to its editor shows a permission error rather than a form
```

## Technical notes / design
The worked example is computed **client-side for responsiveness and re-verified server-side on save** - the client number is a preview, never an authority (SR-052). It calls the same arithmetic as E28-T03 through a thin TypeScript port that is validated against the E28-T03 golden vectors in a shared test fixture; any drift fails CI. This is the only permitted duplication of the sizing logic and it exists solely for keystroke latency.

The editor is a controlled form with a dirty-state guard on navigation. The diff summary before save is generated from the loaded version versus the current form state and is the same structure the audit event records, so what the user confirms is exactly what is audited.

Validation is two-layered to match the backend: synchronous shape validation on blur, and exchange-limit validation on save (or on an explicit "check limits" action), since the latter may require an instrument-cache refresh and cannot run per keystroke.

State handling: loading, loaded, dirty, validating, saving, save-failed (with the error code surfaced in plain language), version-conflict, forbidden.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): each section's field rendering and validation binding; worked-example computation against the shared golden vectors; dirty-guard; diff generation; version-conflict recovery.
Contract: the five profile operations consumed exactly as specified in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
Integration: create -> edit -> version bump -> list reflects "changed since", against a seeded database.
E2E (Playwright, added in E28-Q02): create a risk-based profile with step-up, see the worked example, attempt 25x on SOLUSDT and read the refusal, save, and see the new version on SCR-130.
A11y: axe-core clean on SCR-130 and SCR-131; manual screen-reader pass over the sizing section, the error bindings and the safety notice; keyboard-only completion of the whole form.
Visual regression on both screens in Storybook.
Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: **Tampering (O3)** - the form must never send a computed size or an effective cap; it sends the *policy*, and the server derives everything (SR-052). **Elevation of privilege** - the list and editor are RBAC-gated, but the gate is server-side; hiding a row is cosmetic only, and direct navigation to an ungranted account must show a permission error from a 403, not a client-side guess. **SR-025** step-up is enforced on save by the backend and surfaced by this UI - a UI that forgets to prompt still cannot save, by design. Every state-changing control is wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger so an audit row cannot be forgotten. No secret is ever displayed on these screens. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. SCR-131's own rule applies literally: **every field has units and a worked example**. Each validation message is bound with `aria-describedby` and the field is marked `aria-invalid`; the error summary at the top of the form is a `role="alert"` with in-page links to each offending field. The leverage slider (CMP-104) is operable by arrow keys with a text input alternative, and announces its value with its unit. The safety notice is a `role="note"` whose text explains the floor without relying on the lock icon. The profiles table follows CMP-049 keyboard semantics with a visible focus ring at >=3:1 contrast; the all-symbols warning is text, never a colour. The step-up dialog is a focus-trapped `role="dialog"` that returns focus to the save button on cancel. Layout survives 200% text scaling and 125% zoom; contrast >=4.5:1 for text in both themes.

## Performance notes
Worked-example recompute <=300 ms after the last keystroke (debounced 150 ms), matching the preview budget family in SCR-061. Save round-trip target <=2 s including server-side revalidation against exchange limits (SCR-131). The list is a small dataset and loads in one call; initial render within 300 ms of the API response. Profile changes propagate to open tickets within 2 s (SCR-130), using the transport decided in E28-K01.

## Observability
Analytics: `profile.list_viewed`, `profile.editor_opened`, `profile.sizing_mode_changed{mode}`.
Audit (server-side, surfaced here): `profile.created`, `profile.updated` with before/after, `profile.deleted`.
Frontend: error-boundary reports tagged with the screen ids SCR-130 and SCR-131; a metric for save failures by error code.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T02** (routes, validation and the field-level error contract) and **E28-D06** (the signed-off handoff pack - no frontend screen work starts until its design ticket is Done, per the design-ahead rule). Consumes the app shell, routing and admin layout from **E10**, the design system from **E05**, RBAC and step-up from **E09**, and the account list from **E27**.

## Branch
`feat/e28-profile-editor` - three PRs: (1) SCR-130 list + warnings + empty state, (2) SCR-131 sections + validation binding, (3) worked example, diff summary, step-up and version-conflict recovery. Each <=400 LOC.
