title: Apply profile templates and manage the account-by-symbol permissions matrix
body:
## Context
Covers the remainder of **US-PROF-001** (templates as a way to define a profile) and **US-PROF-003** ("Allowed-symbol restriction", Must) on the UI side, over **SCR-132 Admin: profile templates** and **SCR-133 Admin: symbol permissions matrix**.

SCR-132's defining rule is that a template never writes directly: "Applying a template is a client-side prefill of SCR-131 - it never writes directly, so the user always sees and confirms the resulting profile." It ships built-in templates (conservative, standard, aggressive-demo-only) with their exact values, plus user-saved templates, and gates aggressive templates on live accounts behind an explicit acknowledgement.

SCR-133 is the bulk editor for the allow-list: a grid of accounts x symbols with allow/deny toggles, bulk row and column operations, and "a warning when a trade group's accounts have an empty symbol intersection" - which is the same rule E28-T05 enforces server-side when a group is saved. Its hardest constraint is a safety one: "denying a symbol with an open position is refused and recorded as `symbol_permission.change_refused`".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-132** modal using CMP-001 Button, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-049 Table, CMP-050 Card, CMP-087 AdminLayout: built-in templates with their exact values shown as readable summaries, user-saved templates with rename and delete, "save current profile as template", empty state.
- Apply flow: selecting a template **prefills SCR-131** and routes the user through the normal editor save (step-up, diff summary, validation) - there is no direct write path, and this is asserted by a test.
- Multi-account apply with a per-account preview of the resulting numbers before committing (roadmap E28 scope line: "profile simulation preview"), excluding accounts that would breach exchange limits and naming the reason (SCR-132 validation rule).
- Live-account guard: an "aggressive" template applied to a live account requires an explicit typed acknowledgement before the prefill proceeds.
- **SCR-133** at `/admin/symbol-permissions` using CMP-005 Checkbox, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger: virtualised grid over accounts x the listed USDT-perp universe, allow/deny cells with accessible names combining account and symbol, row and column bulk actions with confirmation, search/filter, and an unsaved-changes summary before save.
- Open-position guard: a symbol with an open position on that account is marked and cannot be denied; an attempt is refused with an explanation and recorded.
- Empty-intersection warning when the current selection would leave a defined trade group with no tradable symbol, naming the group.
- Bulk save as a single server call (SCR-133 performance rule), not one call per cell.
- Audit surfaced: `symbol_permission.changed`, `symbol_permission.bulk_changed`, `symbol_permission.change_refused`, `profile.template_applied`.

## Out of scope
The profile editor itself (E28-S01); backend validation (E28-T02); server-side order-path enforcement of the allow-list (E28-T04); trade groups (E28-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A template never writes directly
  Given I choose the "conservative" template for sub_001
  When I apply it
  Then the profile editor opens prefilled with the template's values, nothing has been saved, and I must confirm and step up to persist it

Scenario: Applying to several accounts previews each one
  Given I apply a template to Main, sub_001 and sub_002
  Then I see the resulting numbers per account before committing, and any account that would breach an exchange limit is excluded with a named reason

Scenario: Aggressive template on a live account
  Given the target account is live
  When I apply the aggressive-demo-only template
  Then I must acknowledge explicitly before the prefill proceeds

Scenario: Deny a symbol
  Given DOGEUSDT is allowed on account B and there is no open position in it
  When I deny it in the matrix and save
  Then the change is persisted in one call and audited, and a subsequent order for DOGEUSDT on account B is refused by the server

Scenario: A symbol with an open position cannot be denied
  Given account B holds an open ETHUSDT position
  When I attempt to deny ETHUSDT for account B
  Then the cell is marked as not deniable, the attempt is refused with an explanation, and the refusal is recorded

Scenario: Empty intersection is warned about before it breaks a group
  Given group Core3 contains accounts A and B
  When my pending changes would leave A and B with no symbol in common
  Then a warning names Core3 and states that the group could not trade anything

Scenario: Bulk row operation
  When I use "allow all" on one account's row and save
  Then one server call is made, the summary lists every added symbol, and the audit records a bulk change

Scenario: Unsaved changes are summarised
  Given I have toggled several cells
  When I press save
  Then a summary lists every addition and removal before the write is made

Scenario: The matrix is usable at full universe size
  Given six accounts and roughly four hundred listed symbols
  Then the grid renders within 600 ms and scrolls without jank, with row and column headers remaining visible
```

## Technical notes / design
The matrix is a virtualised grid (rows = accounts, columns = symbols, or transposed by a control) rendering only the visible window; header rows and columns are sticky. Cell state is a three-value model - allowed, denied, denied-and-locked (open position) - because a two-value checkbox cannot express the locked case accessibly.

Pending edits are held in a diff map (`{accountId: {symbol: allow|deny}}`) and submitted as one `PUT` of the resulting `allowed_symbols`/`blocked_symbols` arrays per touched account, through the existing E28-T02 profile route - no new endpoint is introduced. Accounts untouched by the edit are not written at all.

The empty-intersection check runs client-side against the loaded groups for instant feedback, and is re-checked server-side on save by E28-T05's validation; the client check is advisory only.

Templates are stored as local user preferences plus a set of built-ins compiled into the app; they are not profiles and never carry an account id, so a template can never leak a cap between environments.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): template prefill mapping per built-in; live-account acknowledgement gate; matrix diff-map construction; three-state cell rendering; empty-intersection detection.
Contract: the profile `PUT` used for bulk saves matches `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
Integration: bulk deny across two accounts resulting in exactly two `PUT` calls and the correct audit rows.
E2E (E28-Q02): apply a template through to a saved profile; deny a symbol and then watch the order path refuse it.
A11y: axe-core clean on both screens; manual screen-reader pass over the grid's cell naming and the locked-cell state; keyboard-only bulk operation.
Perf: 6 x 400 grid render <=600 ms, scroll without dropped frames, measured in the browser perf harness.
Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threat **SR-054 (allowed-symbol allow-list)** is the control this UI edits; because enforcement lives server-side in E28-T04, a client bug can lose a *restriction* visually but cannot grant trading rights - the server remains authoritative and that property is asserted by an E28-X03 test. The open-position deny guard exists so a permission change cannot strand an un-closable position. Bulk operations are wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and produce one audit row per account with the full added/removed lists (SR-064). Template values never cross environments. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-133's rule is explicit: "grid cells are checkboxes with accessible names combining account and symbol", and "allow/deny states are glyph + text, not colour alone". The locked (open-position) state is announced through `aria-disabled` plus a descriptive name explaining why. Sticky headers must remain associated with their cells via `aria-labelledby` so a screen reader in a virtualised grid still announces the right account and symbol. Bulk action buttons name their scope ("Allow all 412 symbols for sub_001"). The unsaved-changes summary is a focus-trapped dialog listing changes as text. SCR-132's template cards carry a readable summary of the settings they apply, and applying names the target account and lists what will change. Full keyboard operation including bulk actions; 200% text scaling and 125% zoom supported; contrast >=4.5:1.

## Performance notes

title: Define and manage trade groups with readiness, environment and symbol-intersection guards
body:
## Context
Covers **US-PROF-005** ("Create a trade group", Must) and the management half of **US-PROF-007** ("Trade-group lifecycle view", Must) over **SCR-062 Trade-group manager** (`/admin/trade-groups` for editing, with a read-only picker in the shell).

SCR-062 lists per group: "name, member accounts, default sizing basis, allowed symbols intersection, who may use it, armed-for-live flag". Its validation is the same rule set E28-T05 enforces server-side: ">=1 account; accounts must share at least one allowed symbol ('These accounts have no symbol in common - the group can't trade anything.'); group names unique". US-PROF-005 adds the readiness display - "the group shows '2 of 3 ready' and orders fan out only to ready members, with the skip reported" - and the environment guard, "a trade group cannot mix Demo and Live".

The lifecycle *aggregate* view (aggregate size, average entry, uPnL, per-account expandable rows, group actions, divergence badge) is the other half of US-PROF-007 and depends on live positions, which arrive with **E29**/**E34**; this Story delivers the definition, listing and read-only projection, and the grid shell those epics fill in.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-062** at `/admin/trade-groups` using CMP-041 Menu, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton, CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard: list of groups with name, members, default sizing basis, the computed allowed-symbol intersection, who may use it and the armed-for-live flag; row expansion to per-account legs.
- Create/edit flow with CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect: name (unique), member selection with **per-account enable/disable** (the roadmap's "trade-group definition (named set of accounts) with per-account enable/disable"), and a live summary of the resulting symbol intersection.
- Environment guard in the UI: selecting accounts from two environments is refused at selection time with the message from US-PROF-005 ("a trade group cannot mix Demo and Live"), and the server refusal is surfaced identically if it is reached.
- Readiness strip per group: "N of M ready" with per-member textual reasons (key self-check failed, account disabled, locked out), refreshed from the `trade_groups` topic and the account health state.
- Empty-intersection refusal with SCR-062's exact copy, shown before save rather than after.
- Read-only group picker used by the shell and by the ticket's target selector, exposing the member count (US-PROF-005: "the group appears in the ticket's target selector with a member count").
- Live group rows subscribed to the `trade_groups` WS topic at its 100 ms throttle with 5 Hz UI coalescing, rendering group state as **text** and expanding to a nested per-account table (SCR-062 a11y rules).
- Degraded state: when an account's private WS is down the leg is shown as "state unknown for sub_002", never assumed (SCR-062 sign-off checklist).
- Group deletion with a confirmation naming the members, refused while the group has live legs.
- Audit surfaced as a "last changed by X at T" line; `tradegroup.created|updated|deleted|granted` are emitted server-side.

## Out of scope
Fan-out submission, partial-failure remediation, retry and unwind (**E34**); flatten-group execution (**E34** - the button is rendered but wired to E34's single backend command, and is disabled with an explanatory reason until E34 lands); the fan-out ticket surface (E28-S04); aggregate PnL analytics (**E41**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create a group
  Given accounts A, B and C exist in the demo environment
  When I select all three and name the group "Core3"
  Then the group is saved and appears in the ticket's target selector with a member count of 3

Scenario: Mixed environments blocked at selection
  When I add a demo account and a live account to the same group
  Then saving is refused with "a trade group cannot mix Demo and Live", and the offending accounts are named

Scenario: Inactive member is reported, not hidden
  Given account B's key fails its self-check
  When I view the group
  Then it shows "2 of 3 ready", account B carries a textual reason, and the reason is available to screen readers

Scenario: Empty symbol intersection is refused before save
  Given account A allows only BTCUSDT and account B only ETHUSDT
  When I try to save them as one group
  Then I see "These accounts have no symbol in common - the group can't trade anything." and nothing is written

Scenario: Duplicate name
  When I save a group whose name already exists
  Then the request is refused and the name field carries the error

Scenario: Per-account disable
  Given group Core3 has three members
  When I disable sub_002 within the group
  Then the group reports two enabled members, sub_002 remains a member, and the change is audited

Scenario: A group must have at least one account
  When I remove the last member and save
  Then saving is refused with a message stating that a group needs at least one account

Scenario: Degraded leg is stated, not assumed
  Given sub_002's private WS is down
  When the group row renders
  Then the leg shows "state unknown for sub_002" rather than a stale or assumed state

Scenario: Group state is text
  When any group row renders in either theme
  Then its state is readable as text and does not depend on a colour pill alone

Scenario: Scope is server-side truth
  Given I am a manager granted only account A
  When I open the group list
  Then I see only groups whose membership I am entitled to see, and a direct navigation to another group returns a permission error
```

## Technical notes / design
The group editor is a controlled form whose member selector re-derives the symbol intersection on every change by intersecting each member's effective allow-list (taking the empty list as "all listed symbols"). The derived intersection is advisory in the client and authoritative on the server (E28-T05), so the two must produce the same result - a shared fixture drives both test suites.

Group rows subscribe to `trade_groups` with `exchange_account_ids` scoped to what the user can see; the server intersects with grants, so the client never needs to filter. Frames arrive at a 100 ms throttle and are coalesced to 5 Hz before render (SCR-062 performance rule), and the grid is virtualised to stay under 4 ms scripting per frame with 50 open groups x 5 legs.

Flatten-group is rendered via CMP-123 FlattenAllButton but issues **one** backend command - "the UI never loops client-side over legs" (SCR-062). Until E34 ships that command, the button is present and disabled with a `disabledReason` naming the dependency, so the layout is final and only the wiring changes.

States: loading, empty, populated, editing, validation-blocked, saving, save-failed, degraded (one or more legs unknown), forbidden.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): intersection derivation including the empty-list case; environment guard; readiness aggregation; per-account enable/disable; virtualised row rendering; degraded-leg rendering.
Contract: `listTradeGroups`, `getTradeGroup` and the group create/update payloads against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; `trade_groups` frames against the WS JSON schema.
Integration: create a group, disable a member, observe the audit row and the readiness recalculation.
E2E (E28-Q02): create Core3, break account B's key self-check in the fixture, and read "2 of 3 ready".
A11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass over the nested per-account table and the readiness strip; keyboard-only create and edit.
Perf: 50 groups x 5 legs at the 100 ms WS throttle staying under 4 ms scripting per frame, measured in the perf harness.
Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Asset A-09. Threat **Tampering - silently routing orders to an account the actor may not trade**: membership is server-side truth (US-PROF-005 NFR) and the client's view is a projection of what the server allows; a group containing an ungranted account is never returned. The environment guard is a safety control preventing a demo intent from reaching a live UID and is enforced in both layers deliberately - the UI guard is for clarity, the server guard is the control. Group edits are audited with before/after membership (SR-064). Every state-changing control is wrapped in CMP-093. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-062's rules apply literally: "The group list is a table with a row per group ...; group state is text, not a colour pill alone; expanding a group reveals a nested per-account table; every bulk action button names its scope ('Flatten all 5 legs of group tg_0912')." The readiness strip is text plus an `aria-live="polite"` region so a change from "3 of 3" to "2 of 3" is announced. Expansion controls use `aria-expanded` and the nested table is programmatically associated with its parent row. The degraded state is announced, not merely styled. Focus is preserved across WS-driven re-renders - a coalesced update must never steal or drop focus, which is an explicit test. Keyboard-only creation, editing and deletion; confirmation dialogs restate the exact member count; contrast >=4.5:1; 200% text scaling supported.

## Performance notes
Group state arrives on `trade_groups` and updates are coalesced to 5 Hz; the grid is virtualised and must stay under 4 ms scripting per frame with 50 open groups x 5 legs (SCR-062). Initial list render within 300 ms of the API response.

## Observability
Analytics: `tradegroup.manager_viewed`, `tradegroup.editor_opened`.
Audit (server-side): `tradegroup.created|updated|deleted|granted`.
Frontend: error boundary tagged SCR-062; metrics for frame scripting time and for WS reconnects on the `trade_groups` subscription.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T05** (group routes, readiness and the WS projection) and **E28-D06** (signed-off handoff). Consumes account health and key self-check state from **E27**, the WS client from **E17**/**E10**, and the design system from **E05**. Hands its grid and flatten command over to **E34**, which fills in live fan-out state.

`feat/e28-trade-group-manager` - two PRs: (1) list, editor and guards, (2) WS-driven rows, readiness and degraded states. Each <=400 LOC.

title: Show the per-account fan-out preview with per-leg sizing, exclusions and aggregate totals
body:
## Context
The roadmap's E28 scope line ends with "profile simulation preview ('this ticket would place X on A, Y on B')" - this Story delivers it, as the preview half of **SCR-061 Trade-group ticket (multi-account fan-out)**, serving **US-PROF-006**'s first scenario ("three per-account orders are created, each sized and levered by its own profile") in its pre-submission form.

SCR-061's wireframe fixes the table exactly: one row per account with `acct | profile | qty | lev | SL | ok`, a WARN row carrying its reason inline ("within 12% of daily loss cap"), an excluded row stating why ("sub_003 excluded: symbol not allowed by profile"), and the totals line ("total 0.430 BTC - 27,525 USDT - est. fee 1.9"). Its validation rules are equally specific: "every row must resolve a valid qty >= min lot ('sub_004 computes 0.0004 BTC, below the 0.001 minimum - excluded'); the group send is blocked if any included row lacks an SL; excluded rows always state the reason."

The split with **E34** is firm: this Story renders the preview and the send-blocking validation; E34 owns the actual send, the per-row live status, partial-failure remediation and the rate-limit budget indicator.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The SCR-061 preview surface using CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal, CMP-100 PriceInput, CMP-101 QtyInput, CMP-102 SideToggle, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-107 OrderTicket, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-231 TifSelect, CMP-232 LimitsChip.
- Intent header: side, symbol, entry type and price, SL, TP and the risk basis selector, feeding `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`.
- Per-account preview table rendered from the E28-T05 response: account, profile name, computed qty, leverage, resolved SL and a textual status (ready / WARN with reason / excluded with reason), one row per member.
- Exclusion reasons rendered verbatim from the server's skip codes, mapped to the catalogue's copy: symbol not allowed by profile; below the minimum lot with the minimum stated; profile disabled; account locked out; account not ready.
- Aggregate totals line: total quantity, total notional and estimated fee, recomputed with the table.
- Per-row include/exclude checkbox and a per-row qty override that is **visibly exceptional** and flagged as an override (SCR-061 interactions; the override rules themselves come from E28-S05).
- Send-blocking validation, evaluated client-side for immediacy and re-evaluated server-side on send: the group send is blocked if any included row lacks an SL, or if any included row resolves an invalid quantity.
- Per-account DEMO/LIVE badge on every row (SCR-061 sign-off checklist) and a blocked state when the group contains an account in lockout.
- Debounced re-preview on every intent change - the endpoint is documented as "safe to call on every keystroke" and rate-limited, so the client debounces at 150 ms and cancels in-flight requests rather than queueing them.
- The `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` send affordance and `Esc` to cancel the preview, rendered and wired to E34's submit handler behind a feature flag; until E34 lands, send is disabled with a `disabledReason`.
- Empty and error states: no group selected, group has no ready members, preview failed (with retry), preview rate-limited (with the retry-after surfaced in plain language).

## Out of scope
Actual submission and per-row live status (queued -> sent -> accepted/rejected), partial-failure summary and remediation, the rate-limit budget indicator and the stagger control - all **E34**. The single-account ticket SCR-060 - **E30**. Override permission rules - **E28-S05**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preview resolves each account by its own profile
  Given group Core3 contains Main on risk 0.5% of equity, sub_001 on fixed 0.1 BTC and sub_002 on risk 0.5% of equity
  When I enter a BUY BTCUSDT limit at 64010 with a stop at 63900
  Then three rows appear with per-account quantity, leverage and stop, and the totals line sums them with an estimated fee

Scenario: Excluded rows always say why
  Given sub_003's profile does not allow BTCUSDT
  Then its row reads "excluded: symbol not allowed by profile" as text

Scenario: Below the minimum lot is excluded with the minimum stated
  Given sub_004 computes 0.0004 BTC against a 0.001 minimum
  Then its row states the computed quantity, the minimum and that it is excluded

Scenario: A warning does not exclude
  Given sub_002 is within 12% of its daily loss cap
  Then its row shows a warning with that reason in text and remains included

Scenario: Send is blocked without a stop on every included row
  Given one included row has no resolvable stop-loss
  Then send is disabled and the reason names the row

Scenario: Preview updates as the intent changes
  When I change the entry price
  Then the preview re-runs within 300 ms of my last keystroke and stale in-flight responses are discarded

Scenario: Preview never places an order
  Given I change the intent twenty times
  Then no order is created and no exchange call is made

Scenario: Rate limiting is explained, not silent
  Given previews exceed the server's per-user rate
  Then the surface shows a plain-language wait message with the retry time and keeps the last good preview visible

Scenario: A locked-out member blocks the group
  Given sub_001 is in lockout
  Then the surface shows the blocked state naming the account, and send is disabled

Scenario: Environment is unmistakable per row
  When the preview renders
  Then each row carries its own DEMO or LIVE badge as text, and the surface's environment badge is always visible
```

## Technical notes / design
The preview is entirely server-computed - the client renders the response and performs no sizing of its own. This is deliberate and is the point of SCR-061: what is previewed is exactly what the planner would send, because the same `plan_group` code produces both (E28-T05).

Request lifecycle: on any intent change, debounce 150 ms, abort the in-flight request, issue a new one with a monotonically increasing sequence number, and discard any response whose sequence is stale. A failed preview keeps the last good result on screen, marked stale, rather than blanking the table - a blank table during a fast market is worse than a labelled stale one.

Send-blocking validation is recomputed from the rendered rows so that it cannot disagree with what the user sees; the server repeats it on submit and the client's version is never the authority.

States: no-group, previewing, ready, stale, warn, blocked, rate-limited, failed.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): row rendering per status; exclusion-reason copy mapping for every skip code; totals rendering; send-blocking predicate; debounce and stale-response discarding; last-good-preview retention on failure.
Contract: `previewTradeGroup` request and `TradeGroupPreview` response against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
Integration: preview against a seeded five-account group with mixed profiles, asserting the rendered numbers equal the E28-T03 golden vectors.
E2E (E28-Q02): open the group ticket, enter an intent, see three ready rows and one excluded row with its reason, and confirm send is disabled when a stop is removed.
A11y: axe-core clean; manual screen-reader pass over the preview table and the send button's accessible name; keyboard-only operation including the send shortcut.
Perf: preview round-trip p95 <=300 ms for 5 accounts (SCR-061); render under 16 ms per update.
Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
The preview is a read-only surface and must remain one - a test asserts no mutating call is made from it. Threat **F2 (per-account profile ignored, so one account gets another's sizing)**: the client renders the server's per-leg attribution including the profile name used, which makes a mis-attribution visible rather than silent. Threat **O3 (Tampering)**: per-row quantity overrides are a hint only - the server re-derives and clamps (SR-052), and the override is flagged and audited (`tradegroup.row_overridden`). The per-row environment badge is a safety control against placing a demo-intended group on live. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-061's rules are explicit: "the preview is a table with row status in text; the send button names the account count; partial-failure summary is `role='alert'`". Every status - ready, warn, excluded, blocked - is text, never colour alone, and every excluded row states its reason in the row itself so a screen-reader user never has to hunt for it. The send button's accessible name includes the count ("Send group to 3 accounts"). Preview updates are announced through a polite live region summarising the change ("3 of 4 accounts ready, total 0.430 BTC") rather than announcing every cell. Focus is never stolen by a re-preview. The keyboard shortcut is discoverable in the button's tooltip and in the hotkeys settings screen. Contrast >=4.5:1; 200% text scaling supported; the table remains navigable at 125% zoom.

## Performance notes
Preview <=300 ms p95 for 5 accounts (SCR-061), with client debounce 150 ms on top. Render of a preview update <=16 ms so the surface never drops a frame while the user types. The preview endpoint is rate-limited server-side; the client must not exceed it under any typing speed, which the debounce plus abort guarantees.

## Observability
Analytics: `tradegroup.preview_opened`, `tradegroup.preview_intent_changed`.
Audit (server-side): `tradegroup.preview`, `tradegroup.row_overridden`.
Frontend: metric `cv_ui_preview_latency_ms` sampled per preview; error boundary tagged SCR-061; a counter for discarded stale responses so an over-eager client is visible in telemetry.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.

- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).

- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-T05** (the preview endpoint and planner), **E28-S03** (group definition and the picker this surface consumes) and **E28-D06** (signed-off handoff). The send path, per-row live status and partial-failure UX are **E34**'s and are stubbed behind a flag here. title: Security-review the sizing, risk-guard and override implementation against its threat model
body:
## Context
E28-X01 modelled the threats; this ticket verifies the built code closes them. The three modules under review are the ones an attacker would target: the sizer (E28-T03), which decides how large every order is; the risk guard (E28-T04), which is the only thing standing between a hostile client and an unbounded position; and the override path (E28-S05), which by design permits a deviation from policy and must permit only a narrowing one.

The R3 security gate requires "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes", and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` holds the security-relevant modules to >=90% coverage.

## Scope / Deliverables
- White-box review of `candleviewer/profiles/` (validator, sizer, guard, repository) and `candleviewer/oms/groups/` (group definition, planner, preview), with findings recorded per file and function.
- Verification that each control does what its SR-* entry claims:
  - **SR-052** - no code path accepts a client-supplied size, leverage or cap as authoritative; every one is re-derived. Verified by reading every call site of the sizer and the guard, not only their definitions.
  - **SR-053** - hard notional and leverage ceilings cannot be exceeded by any combination of profile, template, override and group membership.
  - **SR-054** - the allow-list is applied on every order path including rule-originated orders, with wildcard expansion that cannot be tricked into matching an unlisted symbol.
  - **SR-056** - no path can produce a profile without a stop definition, and the database CHECK remains in place in the merged migration.
  - **SR-025** - step-up is enforced server-side on every profile, template and matrix write, not only in the UI.
  - **SR-064/SR-072** - every refusal, clamp and group edit produces an audit row at the point of decision.
- Fail-closed verification: every error path in the guard is traced to confirm it refuses rather than permits, including exception paths, and that no `except` swallows a failure into a permit.
- Confirmation that `profile_snapshot` and every API response are free of secret material, by a serialisation test over the full model rather than by inspection.
- Review of the override decision table against the safety floor, field by field, with `require_native_sl`, the allowed-symbol set and each hard cap confirmed `never`.
- Review of the preview endpoint's read-only property and its rate limit as an abuse-amplification control.
- SAST results (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) for the epic's paths triaged, with any suppression justified in writing.
- Findings filed with severity and an owner; Critical and High closed before the epic closes.
- Security sign-off comment on the epic.

## Out of scope
The threat model itself (E28-X01); automated abuse-case tests (E28-X03 - this review specifies them, X03 automates them); pen-testing (**E43**).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every module in scope is reviewed with findings recorded per file, and the review is evidenced by a written report, not only by a PR approval.
- Each of SR-025, SR-052, SR-053, SR-054, SR-056, SR-064 and SR-072 has a written verdict with the evidence that supports it, including the test that proves it.
- Fail-closed behaviour is confirmed on every error path in the guard, including exception paths, with the traced paths listed.
- The no-secrets property of `profile_snapshot` and of every profile and group API response is proven by a test, not asserted.
- The override decision table is confirmed against the safety floor field by field.
- SAST is clean or every finding is triaged with a justified disposition.
- No Critical or High finding remains open; the security sign-off comment is posted.

## Technical notes / design
The review deliberately reads **call sites** rather than definitions for SR-052: a correct sizer that some caller bypasses is worth nothing, and bypass is the realistic failure mode once E30, E34 and E35 start consuming this code. The reviewer enumerates every import of the sizer and the guard across the repository and checks each one.

Wildcard expansion is reviewed as a parsing problem: a pattern like `*USDT` must not be implemented with a substring check that would also match a symbol containing "USDT" in the middle, and must not permit a pattern that expands to something outside the listed linear USDT-perp universe.

## Test plan
The review's findings become tests in E28-X03 and in the owning tickets. The no-secrets and fail-closed properties are landed as tests in this ticket's own PR so they cannot regress, even though the rest of the ticket is a review.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security verification for the epic. Conflict-of-interest rule: the reviewer is the Security engineer, not an author of the code under review. Findings are tracked in `docs/security/e28/review.md` with severity, owner and status; accepted risks carry an Owner signature and an expiry date.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except that any accessible bypass of a control reported by E28-Q04 is triaged here as a security finding rather than an a11y one.

## Performance notes
The review confirms that the <=5 ms guard budget is met by efficiency (caching, ordering) rather than by omitting gates - a gate order change that short-circuits a control for speed is a finding.

## Observability
The review confirms that every refusal, clamp and denied attempt produces an audit row at the point of decision, and that audit emission cannot be skipped by an early return - the realistic way an audit trail silently develops holes.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Deliverable committed under `docs/security/e28/` and cross-linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding closed or accepted-risk with a written Owner sign-off and an expiry date.
- [ ] Applicable SR-* controls from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` mapped to an automated test (unit, contract, integration or e2e) so the control cannot silently regress.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets-scan clean or triaged on the branches this ticket touches.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk was found or an existing one retired.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-X01** (the model this review verifies against) and by **E28-T04** and **E28-T05** (the code to review). Its findings feed **E28-X03** and the owning engineering tickets; its sign-off is required by the epic DoD.

title: Automate the abuse-case and RBAC assertion suite for every profile and trade-group route
body:
## Context
R3 exit criterion #10 is unambiguous: "RBAC: an automated matrix test exercises **every** route x every role and asserts 403 + no state change + audit row for every disallowed combination." E28 adds seven REST routes and one WS topic to that matrix. US-PROF-003's second scenario is itself an abuse case ("a crafted request submits a DOGEUSDT order for account B / the server rejects with 403 and audits the attempt"), and US-PROF-004 exists entirely so that "limits survive a broken or hostile client".

A one-off manual check does not satisfy this; the assertions must be a suite that runs on every change, because the controls' value is that they hold in six months when E34 and E35 are modifying the same paths.

## Scope / Deliverables
- RBAC matrix test at `tests/security/e28/test_rbac_matrix.py` covering every E28 route x every role and scope: `GET`/`POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles/{profileId}`, `GET`/`POST /trade-groups`, `GET /trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}`, `POST /trade-groups/preview`, and the `trade_groups` WS topic - against owner, manager-with-grant, manager-without-grant, viewer and unauthenticated.
- For every disallowed cell the test asserts all three properties, not just the status: 403 (or the documented `account_scope_denied`), **no state change** (verified by a before/after snapshot of the affected tables), and an **audit row** recording the denied attempt.
- Abuse-case suite implementing the list from E28-X01 and E28-Q01:
  1. `require_native_sl = false` attempted through create, update, template apply and a raw payload - all refused with `native_stop_mandatory` and audited.
  2. An order for a non-allowed symbol via the API directly, bypassing the UI - 403, no exchange call, audited.
  3. An oversized quantity hint on preview and submit - clamped to the profile's computation, clamp recorded.
  4. An override widening each protected cap in turn (`max_position_notional`, `max_daily_loss`, `max_open_positions`, `max_leverage_cap`, the allow-list, `require_native_sl`) - each clamped or refused and audited.
  5. A group mixing demo and live accounts, and a group edited after creation to span environments - both refused.
  6. A preview requested for an ungranted account, and a group read whose membership includes an ungranted account - neither leaks sizing, equity or existence.
  7. A profile write without step-up - refused with `step_up_required` and audited.
  8. A wildcard allow-list pattern crafted to match an unlisted or non-USDT-perp symbol - refused.
  9. Idempotency-key reuse with a different body - `409 idempotency_key_reuse`.
  10. A crafted `profile_snapshot` supplied by the client on a submit - ignored; the server's own snapshot is used.
- WS scope assertions: a subscription requesting `exchange_account_ids` beyond the caller's grants is silently narrowed, never errored and never echoed back, and no frame for an ungranted account is ever delivered.
- Wiring into CI as a **required check** on the E28 paths, so a regression blocks merge rather than release.
- A short report mapping each abuse case to the SR-* control and the threat id it defends.

## Out of scope
The threat model (E28-X01) and the manual review (E28-X02); fan-out submission abuse cases (**E34**); pen-testing (**E43**).

## Acceptance criteria
- The RBAC matrix covers every E28 route and the WS topic x every role, with no cell untested; a coverage report proves it.
- Every disallowed cell asserts 403, no state change and an audit row - all three, with the state-change assertion implemented as a real table snapshot diff.
- All ten abuse cases are automated and pass, each asserting the refusal or clamp **and** its audit row.
- The WS scope-narrowing behaviour is asserted, including that denied ids are not echoed back.
- The suite is a required CI check on the E28 paths and runs in under 5 minutes.
- The report maps each case to its SR-* control and threat id and is reviewed by the Security engineer.

## Technical notes / design
The "no state change" assertion is the one usually skipped and the one that matters: a route that returns 403 after writing a row is still a breach. It is implemented as a checksum over the affected tables taken before and after each disallowed call, so it catches a write the test author did not anticipate.

Audit assertions query the audit chain by correlation id rather than by scanning, so the test fails on a missing row rather than on a slow one, and does not become flaky as the audit table grows.

The suite runs against a seeded fixture (shared with E28-Q01) with deterministic role grants, so adding a role or a route surfaces as an explicit test failure - the matrix is generated from the route table and the role list, so a new route without a matrix entry fails the coverage check automatically.

## Test plan
The suite is the test. Its own correctness is verified by mutation-style checks: temporarily removing a control in a scratch branch must make the corresponding case fail, and this is demonstrated once per control at review time and recorded, so the suite is proven to actually detect the breach it claims to.

## Security notes
This ticket automates controls SR-025, SR-052, SR-053, SR-054, SR-056, SR-064 and the RBAC requirements of SR-070..SR-074, and defends threats O3, F2, F4 and F6 from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Fixtures use non-functional synthetic keys and demo-only accounts. The suite must never be run against a live UID, enforced by an environment guard that aborts the run if the target configuration is live.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - API-level tests.

## Performance notes
The suite runs in under 5 minutes so it can be a required check on every PR; the RBAC matrix is parallelised by route.

## Observability
The suite asserts on audit rows, which makes it a continuous verification that the epic's observability actually works - a silently broken audit pipeline fails these tests rather than being discovered during an incident.

title: Build the k6 load scripts proving budget #4 and the blotter frame budget
body:
## Context
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2) is a **hard gate** for R3: order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo with the backend-added portion isolated and asserted <=50 ms p95. R3's load gate additionally requires "sustained order flow at the per-UID limit across 5 accounts for 1 h with zero lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off". The client side has its own budget: SCR-063 at 500 rows / 60 fps with position updates coalesced at 10 Hz.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 script `tests/load/oms_submit_ack.js`: order submit flow against (a) the fixture-replay mock for pure backend-overhead isolation and (b) Bybit demo for the end-to-end figure, reporting p50/p95/p99 for both totals and the backend-added portion derived from the `order_submit_seconds` histogram.
- k6 script `tests/load/oms_sustained_flow.js`: 1 h sustained flow across 5 demo accounts at the per-UID limit, asserting zero lost acknowledgements (every submitted `order_link_id` reaches a terminal or known state) and correct 10018 back-off behaviour.
- A blotter frontend benchmark (`tests/perf/blotter.bench.ts`) driving 500 position rows and 1 000 order rows with a scripted 10 Hz update stream, asserting p95 frame time and scripting time per frame apply.
- A results template recorded on the epic and fed into the R3 composite capacity scenario (section 5 of the standard).

## Out of scope
Fan-out overhead measurement beyond 5 accounts (E34 owns the fan-out sub-clause), engine FPS for chart layers (E11/E46), the full composite capacity run (owned by the R3 gate, this feeds it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backend-added overhead is isolated and within budget
  When the submit script runs against the fixture-replay mock
  Then the backend-added portion is p95 <=50 ms and is reported separately from exchange RTT

Scenario: End-to-end demo budget
  When the submit script runs against Bybit demo
  Then submit to ack is p95 <300 ms and the run records p50, p95 and p99

Scenario: Nothing is lost under sustained flow
  Given 1 h of sustained order flow across 5 demo accounts at the per-UID limit
  Then every submitted order_link_id ends in a known state, oms_unknown_orders returns to zero, and 10018 responses produce back-off rather than retry storms

Scenario: Blotter holds its frame budget
  Given 500 position rows updating at 10 Hz
  Then p95 frame time stays <=16.6 ms and the run reports scripting time per frame apply
```

## Technical notes / design
The backend-added portion is measured from the server histogram rather than subtracted from wall clock, so network variance cannot hide a regression. Demo runs use small quantities on demo accounts and are rate-limited by the governor under test - the script must not itself bypass the budget. The frontend benchmark drives the real store and renderer through a scripted WS transcript so the measurement includes frame apply, not just paint.

## Test plan
Self-verifying: each script asserts its own thresholds and fails the job when breached. A calibration run with an artificial 100 ms delay injected into the backend proves the scripts actually detect a regression.

## Security notes
Load scripts hold demo credentials from CI secrets only; running them against live is blocked by an environment guard that refuses any base URL that is not the demo host. Generated order volume is bounded so a misconfigured run cannot exhaust the demo account.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user-facing surface.

## Performance notes
This ticket is the budget-#4 evidence for the R3 gate; results are archived per run so a trend, not just a snapshot, is available at the gate.

## Observability
Results are pushed as CI artefacts and as Prometheus recording rules so `order_submit_seconds` p95 is dashboarded continuously rather than only during a load run.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact (plan / suite / script / report) merged under `tests/` or `docs/qa/` and runnable from CI or documented as an on-demand job.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the story or task it verifies, by ticket key.

title: Implement partial close with reduce-only sizing and protective-order quantity adjustment
body:
## Context
US-POS-003 (Must) - close part of a position by quantity or percentage. This is simultaneously a backend concern (reduce-only correctness, lot rounding, keeping the native stop sized to what remains) and a UI concern (the `[Close 25%][Close 50%][Close]` row actions in SCR-063). Getting it wrong either reverses a position accidentally or leaves a protective stop sized for a position that no longer exists - both are safety incidents, which is why this is a separate story from the read-only blotter work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-003**; endpoint `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close` (accepting `qty` or `percent`), consumed by the SCR-063 row actions via **CMP-057** SplitButton.
- Backend: quantity resolution (percent -> base qty -> floor to `lotSizeFilter.qtyStep` read from `instruments`), **always** `reduceOnly: true`, `positionIdx` carried through for hedge mode, and order `purpose="flatten"` so the request draws from the protective rate-budget reserve (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.7).
- Protective-order resizing: after the reducing fill, remaining native SL/TP quantities are rewritten to the remaining position size in a single `POST /v5/position/trading-stop` call carrying **both** TP and SL (the one-sided-modification caveat in section 8.9).
- Dust guard: if rounding would leave a remainder below `minOrderQty`, the API returns `422 dust_remainder` with the computed remainder and the UI offers "close the full position instead".
- UI: confirmation per the confirm policy, a pending state until the execution arrives, and a single reported operation rather than two.

## Out of scope
Flatten-all and the panic button (E39 owns the kill-switch; cancel-all plumbing is E29-S02), reverse (E31/E32), bracket child re-sizing on partial entry fills (E32), TP-ladder editing on SCR-064 (E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Percentage close
  Given a long position of 0.250 BTC
  When I choose 50%
  Then a reduce-only order for 0.125 rounded to the lot size is submitted with purpose "flatten"

Scenario: Protective quantities follow the remainder
  Given the partial close fills
  Then the native stop-loss and take-profit quantities are rewritten to the remaining size in one trading-stop call sending both sides
  And the position is never left with a protective order sized larger than the position

Scenario: Rounding leaves dust
  Given closing 50% would leave a remainder below the symbol minimum order quantity
  Then the request is rejected with 422 dust_remainder before any exchange call and the UI offers a full close

Scenario: Never reverses
  Given the position shrank between the request and the send
  Then the reduce-only flag causes the exchange to cap or reject the order and no opposite-side position is opened

Scenario: Hedge mode
  Given the account is in hedge mode with a long and a short on the same symbol
  Then the close applies only to the requested position_idx and the opposite side is untouched
```

## Technical notes / design
Resolution order: `qty = floor(position.size * percent / qty_step) * qty_step`; reject with `422 qty_below_minimum` when `qty <= 0`, and with `422 dust_remainder` when `position.size - qty` falls in `(0, minOrderQty)`. The close order is an ordinary OMS submission (E29-T04) with `reduce_only=True`, `close_on_trigger=False`, `purpose="flatten"`, `origin="blotter"`. The protective resize runs from the execution handler rather than optimistically, and is retried three times with 250 ms backoff before raising a `critical` over-sized-stop alert. `REDUCE_ONLY_VIOLATION` (Bybit 110017) re-derives the true position and refreshes the blotter instead of surfacing a raw exchange error.

## Test plan
Unit: percent-to-qty rounding table (33%, one-lot positions, `qty_step` 0.001 and 1), dust detection, hedge `position_idx` routing, protective-resize payload asserting both sides are present. Integration: fixture-replay covering partial close -> fill -> resize -> assert `positions.stop_loss` quantity; a race fixture in which the position shrinks mid-flight and returns 110017. Chaos (feeds E29-Q04): kill the backend between the close fill and the protective resize, restart, and assert the resize completes on recovery. Coverage >=90% backend.

## Security notes
An order-placement path, therefore `security`-labelled by default (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8). Threats: elevation (closing a position on an account outside the caller's grant), mitigated by `positions:write` plus `granted_accounts`; tampering (a client-supplied qty larger than the position), mitigated because the server re-derives from exchange-truth position state and never trusts the client's size; repudiation, mitigated by a `position.closed` audit row recording requested versus resolved quantity. An over-sized protective order after a partial close is treated as a safety defect, not a cosmetic one.

## Accessibility notes

title: Build the fills tab and the SCR-078 executions detail drawer
body:
## Context
Fills are the only exchange-truth record of what actually happened, and both the journal (E41) and the position detail (E29-S08) derive from them. US-POS-005 and US-POS-009 both need a per-fill view, and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-078 specifies it: time, price, qty, fee, fee currency, liquidity flag, order id, exec id, trade group, the rule that caused it and a journal link.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: the fills half of **US-POS-005** and **US-POS-009**; screen **SCR-078** (drawer) plus the Fills tab inside SCR-063.
- Components: **CMP-049** Table, **CMP-036** KeyValueRow, **CMP-046** Drawer, **CMP-099** PrintExportBar, **CMP-116** PnLBadge.
- Data: WS topic `executions` (never throttled) plus `GET /api/v1/executions` with cursor pagination for history.
- Aggregation: average fill price with the maker/taker split; slippage versus the intended price wherever an intent price exists; grouping by account for fanned-out orders.
- CSV export (`execution.exported` analytics); empty state; virtualised list coalesced to 5 Hz.

## Out of scope
Chart execution marks (E29-S05), closed-position PnL rollup (E29-S06), journal linkage beyond a deep link (E41), fan-out grouping semantics (E34 defines the group model; this renders it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Per-fill detail
  Then each fill row shows time, price, quantity, fee with its currency, maker/taker flag, order id and exec id

Scenario: Aggregate and slippage
  Given an order filled in 4 executions against an intended limit price
  Then an average fill price, the maker/taker split and slippage versus the intended price are shown

Scenario: No double counting
  Given the same exec_id arrives on the WS stream and again through REST backfill
  Then it appears exactly once in the list and once in the aggregate

Scenario: Volume
  Given a 1 000-fill session
  Then the list renders without exceeding 4 ms scripting per frame and stays keyboard navigable

Scenario: Empty state
  Given no fills in the selected window
  Then an explicit empty state naming the active filter is shown
```

## Technical notes / design
Deduplication is keyed on `exec_id` client-side as well as server-side, because the backfill/stream overlap is normal rather than exceptional. Fee sign and currency are always rendered together. Slippage appears only when an intent price exists (limit orders and algo children); for market orders the column reads "-" rather than a misleading zero. The list is virtualised and coalesced at 5 Hz (the SCR-078 performance note) while the underlying `executions` topic itself stays unthrottled.

## Test plan
Unit: dedupe by `exec_id`, average-price and maker/taker aggregation, slippage computation and its absence for market orders, fee formatting. Contract: WS `executions` payload against `cv://ws/v1/executions.schema.json`. Integration: a fixture with overlapping WS and REST backfill. E2E: open the drawer from an order row, export CSV, assert the row count. Perf: 1 000-fill render benchmark asserting <=4 ms scripting per frame. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Executions are immutable exchange records, so the UI must never offer an edit affordance. Cross-account scoping is server-side (`executions:read` plus `granted_accounts`). Exported CSV is an analytics artefact and is watermarked with the account scope and generation time so it is not mistaken for the audit trail.

## Accessibility notes
Table semantics; fees and funding shown with explicit sign and currency in text; maker/taker rendered as text rather than colour; the drawer has a heading naming order and account, traps focus, and returns focus to the invoking row on close.

## Performance notes
Virtualised and coalesced to 5 Hz; a 1 000-fill session renders without exceeding 4 ms scripting per frame (SCR-078 budget).

## Observability
`execution.detail_viewed` and `execution.exported` (analytics). Client metric `exec_dedupe_hits_total` - a non-zero value is expected, but a spike indicates backfill misconfiguration.

title: Render execution marks on the chart from the execution stream with clustering
body:
## Context
US-POS-005 (Must) - "I want fills marked on the chart, so that I see where I actually traded." The NFR is the important part: **marks come from the execution stream, never from optimistic order state**, so a mark on the chart is always something that really happened. The marks are an overlay layer in the custom WebGL engine (SCR-030), so they must obey the engine's frame-budget shedding ladder instead of being drawn as DOM elements on top of the canvas.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-005**; screens SCR-030 (chart panel) and SCR-078 (the detail it links to).
- An `executions` overlay layer in the chart engine renderer: one mark per fill at `(exec_ts, exec_price)`, glyph by side, size scaled by quantity within a bounded range.
- Clustering: fills within a configurable pixel radius collapse into a cluster glyph with a count badge that expands on hover **and** on keyboard focus.
- Tooltip / focus card: side, quantity, price, account, fee, maker/taker, order link id, and a deep link into SCR-078.
- A toggle in the chart trading overlay settings (SCR-040); when disabled the marks hide but stay available in the position detail (E29-S08).
- Account/group filter inherited from the workspace so a fanned-out trade shows only the selected accounts' marks.

## Out of scope
Order and position lines and their drag interactions (E31), the SCR-040 settings screen itself (E31), bracket visualisation (E32), replay-time marks (E26/E38).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Marks reflect reality only
  Given an order is submitted but not yet filled
  Then no mark appears on the chart
  And a mark appears only when the execution arrives on the executions stream

Scenario: Clustering at density
  Given 40 executions inside one bar's pixel width
  Then they render as a cluster glyph with a count badge that expands on hover or keyboard focus

Scenario: Toggle
  When I disable execution marks in the chart trading overlay settings
  Then no marks are drawn and the fills remain visible in the position detail view

Scenario: Frame budget
  Given 5 000 execution marks in the visible range
  Then the pane holds p95 frame time <=16.6 ms, shedding mark detail before it sheds price data
```

## Technical notes / design
Marks live in their own instanced draw call backed by a GPU buffer of `(x, y, side, qtyBucket)` so adding a fill is a buffer append rather than a scene rebuild (`26-chart-engine-design.md` layer model). Clustering is computed in screen space on the CPU once per viewport change - not per frame - and memoised by `(rangeStart, rangeEnd, pxPerBar)`. The overlay registers at a shedding tier below price and bar geometry so the frame-budget ladder drops mark detail first. Keyboard access uses the chart's existing overlay focus ring: marks join the focusable-object list in time order.

## Test plan
Unit: clustering algorithm (boundary radii, stable cluster identity across small pans), quantity-to-size bucketing, exclusion of optimistic state. Visual regression at three zoom levels. E2E: place a demo order, wait for the fill, assert a mark appears at the fill price and that its focus card contents are correct. Perf: 5 000-mark benchmark against budget #1 recorded in the engine bench suite. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
The focus card shows account labels, so it must respect the caller's account scope - a manager must not be able to infer the existence of another account's fills from marks. No key or signature material is exposed. Deep links carry `order_link_id`, which is a correlation id rather than a secret, and the target screen re-authorises.

## Accessibility notes
Every mark is reachable through the chart's keyboard object navigation with an announced description ("Buy 0.1 at 63,980, Main, maker"); clusters announce their count and expand on focus rather than only on hover; marks are distinguishable by glyph shape as well as colour; the SCR-045 chart data-table alternative lists the executions in the visible range as rows.

## Performance notes
Budget #1: p95 frame time <=16.6 ms on the focused pane with 5 000 marks enabled; the overlay participates in the shedding ladder. Mark buffer memory is bounded by the visible range plus a prefetch margin.

## Observability
`chart_overlay_marks_rendered` gauge and `chart_overlay_shed_events_total{layer="executions"}` so shedding is visible rather than silent.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).
- [ ] Coverage: touched backend/OMS packages ≥90% line (local R3 policy for OMS/risk modules, `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4), frontend ≥80%; CI coverage gate green.

## Dependencies

title: Ship closed positions and today's realised PnL with the configured day boundary
body:
## Context
US-POS-009 (Must) - today's closed positions and realised PnL. Two traps make this a story rather than a column: "today" must use **the same day boundary as the daily-loss limit** (E39) or the risk lockout and the PnL display will disagree; and fee data arrives late, so a freshly closed row must be explicitly provisional rather than quietly wrong. The NFR requires realised PnL to match Bybit's own figures within rounding tolerance, which means reconciling against `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` rather than only summing local fills.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-009**; screens SCR-063 (closed-positions view) and SCR-078; data via `GET /api/v1/executions/closed-pnl` (mirroring Bybit `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl`).
- Rows: entry, exit, quantity, gross PnL, fees, funding, net PnL, account, symbol, side, duration.
- Day boundary read from the same configuration key the daily-loss cap uses (`risk.day_boundary_utc_offset`, owned by E39) - one source, never a second constant.
- Provisional state: rows whose fee or funding data has not settled are marked "provisional" in text and update in place once settled.
- Reconciliation badge: when locally computed net PnL differs from the exchange's `closedPnl` beyond the rounding tolerance, the row is flagged and the divergence is audited.
- Per-account and aggregated totals consistent with the positions-tab totals.

## Out of scope
Full journal analytics - equity curve, R-multiple distribution, MAE/MFE analysis, tags (E41); per-trade-group PnL rollup (E34); risk-lockout behaviour itself (E39); Parquet export (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Closed today
  Then a list shows each closed position with entry, exit, quantity, gross PnL, fees, funding and net PnL

Scenario: Day boundary is shared
  Given the configured day boundary is 00:00 UTC+3
  Then "today" in this view starts at exactly the same instant the daily-loss limit resets
  And a contract test asserts both read the same configuration key

Scenario: Fees pending
  Given a position closed seconds ago whose fee data has not arrived
  Then the row shows its PnL as provisional in text and updates in place once fees settle

Scenario: Divergence from the exchange
  Given local net PnL differs from GET /v5/position/closed-pnl beyond the rounding tolerance
  Then the row is flagged, the exchange figure is displayed as authoritative, and the divergence is audited with both values
```

## Technical notes / design
Local net PnL is composed from `executions` (`closed_pnl` on reducing fills, minus `exec_fee`, plus rows with `exec_type='Funding'`) using `Decimal` arithmetic. The exchange figure is fetched per closed position and compared with a relative tolerance (`oms.closed_pnl_tolerance_rel`, default 1e-8). The comparison runs server-side so the flag is a data property rather than a rendering artefact. Config keys: `risk.day_boundary_utc_offset`, `oms.closed_pnl_tolerance_rel`.

## Test plan
Unit: PnL composition across gross/fee/funding, tolerance comparison, provisional-to-settled transition, day-boundary bucketing across the configured offset including the boundary minute. Contract: `GET /api/v1/executions/closed-pnl` against the OpenAPI schema, plus a shared-config test asserting E39's cap and this view resolve the same key. Integration: fixture with late-arriving fee rows. E2E: close a demo position and assert the row appears provisional then settles. Coverage >=85% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Financial data, scoped server-side (`positions:read`, `executions:read`). A divergence flag is security-relevant in the repudiation sense, so it is audited with both values and a disputed figure can be reconstructed. No client-side recomputation is trusted for the audit record.

## Accessibility notes
PnL values carry a text sign and currency alongside colour (CMP-116 PnLBadge contract); "provisional" is a text label rather than a faded style; the divergence flag is an icon plus text with an accessible description naming both figures; the totals row is associated via `scope`.

## Performance notes
The closed-PnL fetch is a `background`-priority request in the rate budget (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.7) so it can never starve order traffic. The view paginates rather than loading unbounded history.

## Observability
`oms_closed_pnl_divergence_total{account}` (warning alert on a sustained non-zero rate), `oms_closed_pnl_fetch_seconds`. Audit: `pnl.divergence_detected` with local and exchange values.

title: Implement the abuse-case suite, RBAC scope assertions and SAST rules for the OMS
body:
## Context
E29-X01 produces the threats; this ticket turns them into executable, permanently-running checks. R3 exit criterion 10 requires "an automated matrix test exercising every route by every role, asserting 403, no state change and an audit row for every disallowed combination" - for the OMS routes, that test is built here. `04-security-program.md` additionally requires SAST rules to encode project-specific invariants rather than relying on generic rulesets alone.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Abuse-case suite `tests/security/oms/`: manager acting on a non-granted account over REST and over WS subscribe; viewer attempting every mutating route; forged `order_link_id` replay; client-supplied quantity larger than the position on close; `reduce_only` stripped in transit; an out-of-scope account id smuggled in a batch or filter parameter; order flooding to exhaust a UID budget and the assertion that protective traffic still gets a token; submission attempted while an account is marked stale; submission attempted while Postgres is unavailable.
- RBAC route-by-role matrix covering every E29 REST route and every private WS topic, asserting status, absence of state change and presence of an audit row.
- Semgrep/Bandit rules under `.semgrep/oms.yml`: forbid `float(` on monetary values in OMS modules; forbid an unscoped `select(orders|positions|executions)` helper; forbid writing `order_events.payload` without passing it through `redact_exchange_payload()`; forbid any exchange call outside the adapter package; forbid environment conditionals (`if env == "live"`) outside `ExchangeCapabilities`.
- Secret-scanning coverage extended to `packages/fixtures/**` and to test artefacts.
- A CI job running the suite on every PR touching `area/oms-execution`.

## Out of scope
DAST/ZAP scanning (programme-level, `s06`), dependency scanning (programme-level), penetration testing (E43), key-vault abuse cases (E27), kill-switch bypass tests (E39).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every disallowed combination is proven
  Given every E29 route and WS topic crossed with owner, manager and viewer roles
  When the matrix runs
  Then each disallowed combination returns 403, changes no state, and writes an audit row

Scenario: Replay of an idempotency key cannot create a second order
  Given a captured order_link_id
  When it is replayed
  Then the exchange duplicate rejection triggers success-after-lookup and no second order exists

Scenario: The protective reserve cannot be starved
  Given normal-priority traffic saturating a UID rate budget
  When a stop-loss placement is requested
  Then it acquires a token from the reserve and succeeds

Scenario: SAST rules have teeth
  Given a deliberately introduced float conversion on a monetary value in an OMS module
  Then the Semgrep rule fails the build naming the file and line

Scenario: No credential reaches storage
  Given an exchange response containing signature and key headers
  When it is written to order_events.payload
  Then the stored payload contains neither, verified by an automated test
```

## Technical notes / design
The RBAC matrix is generated from the OpenAPI document's `x-rbac` annotations rather than hand-listed, so a new route without an annotation fails the test - making the matrix self-maintaining as E30-E34 add routes. Abuse cases run against the fixture-replay mock so they are deterministic and safe to run on every PR. Rate-budget starvation is tested against the real token-bucket implementation, not a stub.

## Test plan
The suite is the test; its own credibility is established with negative controls - temporarily removing a scope check, the redaction call and the reserve, and confirming the corresponding case fails each time.

## Security notes
This ticket is the primary evidence for the R3 security gate on this epic. Findings feed E29-X03. Any case that cannot be automated is recorded as a manual check on the X03 checklist rather than silently dropped.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI surface, though the suite asserts that out-of-scope rows are **absent** from responses rather than merely hidden, which is also an a11y-relevant property (a screen reader must not reach them).

## Performance notes
The suite must stay under 5 minutes on the PR path; the rate-budget starvation case uses a compressed bucket configuration rather than real-time waiting.

## Observability
Asserts that each refused attempt produces the expected audit row and increments `rbac_denied_total{route,role}`, so abuse is detectable in production and not only in tests.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact merged (threat model in `docs/security/`, rules under `.semgrep/` or the CI config, tests under `tests/security/`).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding either fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded (R3 gate, `30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4).
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present on this ticket and on the tickets it gates.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk was surfaced or an existing one retired.
