title: Order ticket UI
body:
## Context
R3 "Trading on demo" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7) closes the execution loop. E29 gives us the OMS core and order state machine, E27 the accounts and key vault, E28 the per-account profiles and trade groups, E39 the risk caps and kill-switch. **E30 is the surface the human touches**: the order ticket.

The roadmap scopes this Epic as: "Market / limit / conditional entry; qty by contracts, notional, % equity, or risk-based from the SL distance; price stepping honouring `priceFilter`/`lotSizeFilter`; post-only, reduce-only, IOC/FOK/GTC; TP/SL attachment with tpslMode Full/Partial; account/trade-group selector with the fan-out preview; **arm/lock control plus an always-visible environment badge â€” no trading control is operable unless both are visible**; hotkeys; confirmation policy configurable per environment (demo may skip, live may not)" (30-release-roadmap.md Â§7.2, 34 pts, S16â€“S17).

Two product properties are load-bearing and are the reason this Epic exists as its own Epic rather than as UI bolted onto E29:
1. **Nothing fires by accident.** One-click trading is off by default, is armed through `POST /api/v1/settings/arm` for a bounded TTL, auto-disarms on inactivity/lock/env-switch/disconnect, and the environment (DEMO/LIVE) is restated on every trading surface and in every confirmation (US-ORD-005, SCR-075, CMP-229, CMP-139).
2. **Nothing goes out unprotected.** The mandatory native exchange-side stop-loss (owner decision, `20-architecture.md` P4) is expressed in the ticket as a field that cannot be emptied, and the backend rejects `native_stop_required` if it ever is (US-ORD-013, CMP-119, CMP-158).

Backend module: **M23** (API/WS Gateway â€” the ticket's REST/WS contract surface); consumes M14 (OMS) via `POST /api/v1/orders`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`, `GET /api/v1/risk/summary`, and the `orders`, `executions`, `positions`, `wallet`, `ticker.{symbol}` WS topics. Story domain: **ORD**.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (11-user-stories.md Â§17 ORD):** US-ORD-001 (order ticket, Must), US-ORD-002 (order types and flags, Must), US-ORD-003 (quantity presets and size ladder, Must), US-ORD-004 (risk-based sizing, Must), US-ORD-005 (one-click arm/lock, Must), US-ORD-006 (trading hotkeys, Must), US-ORD-012 (order templates, Should), US-ORD-013 (mandatory native SL â€” ticket-side expression, Must), US-ORD-014 (pre-trade risk preview, Should).
US-ORD-007..011 (chart/DOM click-trade, drag, cancel-from-chart, flatten, reverse) belong to **E31**; the backend enforcement of US-ORD-013 belongs to **E32**; group construction/fan-out execution belongs to **E28/E34**. This Epic owns the *ticket surface* and its client-side guarantees only.

**Screens:** SCR-060 (order ticket panel, single account), SCR-076 (order confirmation modal), SCR-077 (order rejection detail drawer), SCR-114 (trading defaults settings), SCR-113 (hotkey editor â€” trading-action rows), SCR-158 (rate-limited state), SCR-075 (demo/live banner & per-panel badges â€” consumption), SCR-061 (trade-group ticket â€” the account/group selector + fan-out preview slice only; group management is E28).

**Components:** CMP-100 PriceInput, CMP-101 QtyInput, CMP-102 SideToggle, CMP-103 OrderTypeTabs, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-107 OrderTicket, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel, CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-231 TifSelect, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal.

**API:** `POST /api/v1/orders`, `GET /api/v1/orders`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`, `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}/ticker`, `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`, `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate`, `GET /api/v1/risk/summary`, `POST /api/v1/settings/arm`, `GET|PUT /api/v1/settings`, `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*`.
**WS topics:** `orders.{accountId}`, `executions.{accountId}`, `positions.{accountId}`, `wallet.{accountId}`, `ticker.{symbol}`.
**DB:** `hotkey_profiles` (existing, `0011_workspace`); user trading defaults and order templates ride the existing user-settings store â€” no new migration is introduced by this Epic beyond the templates column/table added in E30-S07.

**Children:** 7 Stories, 3 Tasks/Chore, 1 Spike (**34 engineering pts**), 7 Design tickets (23 pts), 6 QA tickets (22 pts), 3 Security tickets (8 pts).

### Estimate reconciliation (single number: 34)
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 budgets **34 pts** for E30 across S16–S17. That budget is the *engineering* capacity line, and this Epic reconciles to it exactly:

| Bucket | Keys | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering (Stories, Tasks, Spike) | E30-K01, E30-T01..T03, E30-S01..S07 | **34** |
| Design (design-discipline capacity, S13–S18) | E30-D01..D07 | 23 |
| QA (test-discipline capacity, S16–S18) | E30-Q01..Q06 | 22 |
| Security (security-discipline capacity, S15–S18) | E30-X01..X03 | 8 |

The Epic ticket's own `estimate` field is **34** — identical to the roadmap figure and to the rollup of its engineering children, so roadmap capacity planning, the Epic field and the child rollup are one number. Design, QA and Security children are *not* rolled into that number: they draw on their own discipline capacity (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA and QA/security sign-off mandatory companion work, not engineering scope) and several of them land outside the S16–S17 engineering window (S13–S15 design, S18 sign-off). No scope was added beyond the roadmap §7.2 sentence for this Epic; the S16–S17 engineering plan is K01 (1) + T01 (5) + S01 (5) + S02 (2) + S03 (5) + S04 (5) + S05 (2) + S06 (5) + S07 (2) + T02 (1) + T03 (1) = **34**.

## Out of scope
- Chart click-to-trade, order-line dragging, DOM ladder click-trade, flatten/reverse buttons (E31).
- Bracket child management, scaled ladders, break-even automation, trailing translation (E32); emulated OCO/iceberg/TWAP/chase builders SCR-065..069 (E33).
- Trade-group CRUD, per-account enable/disable, fan-out execution and partial-failure unwind (E28/E34).
- Server-side native-SL invariant enforcement, risk-cap evaluation, kill-switch engine (E32/E39) â€” the ticket *consumes* and *displays* these.
- Positions/orders blotter SCR-063 (E29). Journal capture (E41). Live environment enablement (E44).
- Android / any non-web client.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A complete demo order from the ticket
  Given a signed-in owner on the demo environment with account "Main" selected on SCR-060
  When they set limit buy 0.25 BTCUSDT at a valid tick price with the profile's stop attached and confirm
  Then POST /api/v1/orders returns 202, the ticket shows submitting -> accepted within 500 ms p95
  And the resulting order appears from the orders WS topic, not from the REST body alone
Scenario: No trading control is operable without arm state and environment both visible
  Given the environment badge or the arm state cannot be rendered for any reason
  Then every submit affordance on SCR-060 and SCR-061 is disabled with a stated reason
  And no order request can be issued by keyboard, hotkey or programmatic click
Scenario: The mandatory native stop cannot be removed
  Given an entry order on an account whose profile requires a native SL
  When the user clears the stop-loss field
  Then submit is blocked client-side with "This account requires a stop-loss on every order."
  And a crafted request omitting stop_loss is rejected server-side with native_stop_required
```

## Technical notes / design
Frontend package layout: `apps/web/src/features/order-ticket/` with a framework-free `packages/order-ticket-core` holding the pure validation/sizing/preview reducer so that the same code runs in unit tests, in Storybook and (as a parity fixture) against the backend's `24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3 sizing algorithm. Client-side sizing is advisory: the server recomputes and rejects a mismatch beyond one lot (US-ORD-004 NFR).

Submit path: `Idempotency-Key` is REQUIRED on `POST /api/v1/orders`; the client derives one per user-intent (not per retry) so a retried submit can never double-place. One-click submissions additionally carry the `arm_token` from `POST /api/v1/settings/arm`. Response `202` returns a `TradeGroup` (single orders are one-leg groups server-side) â€” the UI must treat it as *acceptance*, and resolve terminal state from the `orders`/`executions` WS topics, showing "Awaiting exchange confirmation â€” reconciling" after 2 s.

Error codes surfaced by name, never by raw string matching: `validation_failed`/`native_stop_required`, `tick_size_violation`, `lot_size_violation`, `risk_limit_breached`, `trading_disabled` (kill-switch), `429` rate-limited (SCR-158), `502` exchange error (SCR-077 with verbatim retCode/retMsg from `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`).

## Test plan
Per-child test plans roll up to: unit â‰¥80% on `apps/web` and â‰¥85% on `packages/order-ticket-core`; contract tests against `22-api-openapi.yaml` for every request shape the ticket emits; a **sizing-parity** test that runs the same fixture matrix through the TS core and the Python `Â§9.3` implementation and asserts identical results; Playwright E2E on demo covering keyboard-only placement, arm/disarm, rejection, rate-limit and confirmation policy; perf harness asserting â‰¤8 ms recompute and â‰¤500 ms p95 clickâ†’ack; chaos: WS drop between ack and fill, kill-switch engaged mid-ticket, stale wallet.

## Security notes
Threats (04-security-program.md): accidental or induced order placement (arm bypass, clickjacking, hotkey while unfocused), privilege escalation through the account selector (manager selecting an ungranted account), leakage of exchange credentials or raw signatures in the rejection drawer, idempotency-key reuse causing double submission, and confirmation-policy tampering to disable LIVE confirmation. Controls: server-side scope resolution on every account id, `arm_token` validated server-side and invalidated on disarm/kill-switch/risk breach, redaction in `OrderDiagnostics`, audited `order.submitted`/`order.rejected`/`order.arm_toggled`/`trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled`. Data classification: financial + account-scoped; no secrets ever rendered.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The ticket is a form with a fieldset per section; the submit button's accessible name restates the full intent; errors are summarised at the top and linked to fields; the arm state is announced assertively on change and on auto-disarm; every hotkey has a visible, focusable equivalent; nothing (buy/sell, armed/locked, demo/live) is conveyed by colour alone.

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§5.2): order submit â†’ ack p95 <300 ms on demo, of which â‰¤50 ms is backend-added â€” this Epic owns the client portion and must not add more than 20 ms between the user gesture and the request leaving the client. SCR-060 requires every input to recompute risk/fee/margin in â‰¤8 ms. Hotkeyâ†’submit â‰¤50 ms client-side (US-ORD-006). Preview recompute â‰¤100 ms (US-ORD-014).

## Observability
Audit: `orders.submit` (source=ticket|hotkey|template), `orders.cancel`, `order.arm_toggled`, `trading_defaults.changed`, `hotkey.trading_binding_changed`. Analytics: `ticket.sizing_rule_used`, `order.confirmation_shown`, `order.confirmation_cancelled`, `order.rejection_viewed`, `order.blocked_ratelimited`. Client metrics: `cv_ticket_recompute_ms`, `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms` (histogram, env label), `cv_ticket_arm_state_seconds`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike/Design/QA/Security ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic AC verified end to end on demo: place â†’ reject â†’ correct â†’ place â†’ fill, from the ticket alone.

- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on every touched screen + a manual NVDA pass on placement, arming and rejection.

- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, all Critical/High closed, Security engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] design: D-tickets Done â‰¥2 sprints before their consuming Story; design QA (E30-D07) closed.
- [ ] QA sign-off (E30-Q06) recorded; zero open P0/P1 against this Epic.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at the S17 Sprint Review (roadmap key date 2027-01-21: "first end-to-end demo trade").

## Dependencies

- **E28** Per-account profiles & trade groups â€” profile limits, sizing rule, SL/TP offsets, `POST /trade-groups/preview`.

- Consumers: **E31** (chart/DOM trading reuses the ticket's intent layer, arm state and confirmation policy), **E33** (algo builders embed the ticket's sizing and bracket blocks), **E41** (journal reads `source=ticket`).

`feat/e30-order-ticket-epic` as the umbrella name; one branch and PR per child ticket (`feat/e30-<short>`), â‰¤400 LOC diff preferred.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. title: Write the black-box test plan and fixtures for the order ticket
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature, executed and signed off by QA before a Story can reach Done. For an order ticket that plan is also the safety net for the things unit tests structurally cannot see: that a *human* cannot get an order out without a stop, cannot mistake demo for live, and cannot fire while locked.

Writing the plan first (S16, alongside the first Stories) also forces the fixtures to exist before the E2E work in E30-Q02 needs them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box test plan covering every scenario in US-ORD-001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 012, 013, 014 as executed through the UI only, with expected results stated in observable terms.
- Per-screen exploratory-charter seeds for SCR-060, SCR-076, SCR-077, SCR-114, SCR-158.
- **Fixtures**: recorded Bybit demo responses for accepted, partially filled, rejected (post-only would cross `110007`, insufficient margin, reduce-only violation, tick/lot violation, leverage limit, risk-limit tier, position-mode mismatch), `10018` rate-limited, `502` exchange error, and a `422 native_stop_required`. Instrument fixtures for BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT and 1000PEPEUSDT covering distinct tick/lot/min-notional shapes. Profile fixtures covering each sizing mode, a leverage cap, a symbol allowlist, a daily-loss cap near its limit and an account with the native-SL invariant opted out.
- A **risk-based test matrix** ranking scenarios by consequence: anything that could result in an unintended, unprotected or wrongly-sized order is P0 and is executed every regression cycle, not sampled.
- Entry/exit criteria for the E30 test cycle and the definition of a blocking defect for this Epic.

## Out of scope
Automation (E30-Q02), perf scripts (E30-Q03), chaos (E30-Q04), a11y audit (E30-Q05), backend OMS testing (E29's own QA tickets).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Must story has executable black-box coverage
  Then each Gherkin scenario in US-ORD-001..006 and US-ORD-013 maps to at least one test-plan step with an observable expected result
Scenario: Fixtures exist for every failure the UI claims to handle
  Then each rejection reason with written copy in the E30-D06 copy deck has a corresponding recorded fixture
Scenario: Safety scenarios are P0 and unsampled
  Then every scenario that could produce an unintended, unprotected or mis-sized order is marked P0 and included in every regression cycle
Scenario: The plan is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer unfamiliar with the Epic
  Then they can execute any step from the plan alone without asking a clarifying question
```

## Technical notes / design
Fixtures are recorded from the real Bybit **demo** environment and stored under `tests/fixtures/bybit/orders/` with a manifest naming the capture date and the endpoint, so they can be re-captured when Bybit changes a response shape (risk R6 Feed rot). Each fixture carries the exact `retCode`/`retMsg` â€” invented error payloads would make the copy deck untestable.

The plan distinguishes **client-blocked** from **server-rejected** for every validation: they are different code paths with different user-visible behaviour, and conflating them in the plan would let a client-side-only guard pass as if it were enforcement.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the test plan. Its own quality gate: reviewed by the E30 engineering lead and the Security engineer (for the safety and abuse scenarios) before it is used.

## Security notes
Fixtures must be scrubbed of account ids, balances, keys and signatures before being committed; a secret-scanning check runs over the fixture directory. The plan includes the negative security scenarios that QA (not Security) can execute black-box: submitting while locked, submitting with a manipulated account selection, disabling LIVE confirmation.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes a keyboard-only execution of the core placement path as a standard step in every cycle, so a11y regression is caught by routine QA and not only by the dedicated audit in E30-Q05.

## Performance notes
The plan includes the observable side of the budgets: acknowledgement visible within 500 ms, preview updating within a perceptible 200 ms, no visible lag when typing into the price field on a loaded workspace. Instrumented measurement is E30-Q03's job.

## Observability
Each P0 scenario names the audit event that must be present afterwards (`orders.submit`, `order.rejected`, `order.arm_toggled`), so QA verifies the audit trail as part of the functional pass rather than trusting it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan covers every Gherkin scenario of the in-scope user stories.
- [ ] Fixture set complete, scrubbed, committed with a manifest.
- [ ] Risk-based matrix agreed with the engineering lead.
- [ ] Reviewed by the engineering lead and the Security engineer.
- [ ] Linked from every E30 Story so their QA sign-off references it.

## Dependencies
- **E30-D06** â€” the copy deck and state inventory the plan asserts against.
- **E29** â€” the backend error taxonomy the fixtures encode.

## Branch

## References

- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-060, SCR-061, SCR-076, SCR-077, SCR-113, SCR-114, SCR-158
- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-100..107, CMP-119, CMP-121, CMP-122, CMP-130, CMP-139, CMP-158, CMP-229, CMP-231, CMP-232

title: Build packages/order-ticket-core: draft, validation, sizing, submit
body:
## Context
Every ticket surface in the product â€” SCR-060 single-account ticket, SCR-061 group ticket, E31's chart and DOM click-trade, E33's algo builders â€” must produce an identical, identically-validated order draft. If that logic lives in React components it will be duplicated and will drift, and a drift here is a mis-sized order with real money behind it.

This Task creates **`packages/order-ticket-core`**: a framework-free TypeScript package holding the order draft model, the validation rules, the client-side sizing reducer and the submit pipeline. It is pure (no DOM, no fetch, no React) apart from an injected transport port, so it is unit-testable exhaustively and can be run in a worker if E30-K01 mandates that placement.

The sizing reducer is a **mirror of the backend algorithm** in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3 (sizing), Â§9.3.1 (stop resolution), Â§9.3.2 (clamp order) and Â§9.3.3 (take-profit resolution). It is advisory: the server recomputes and rejects a mismatch beyond one lot (US-ORD-004 NFR). The parity test in the Test plan is what keeps the mirror honest.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/order-ticket-core/src/model.ts` â€” `OrderDraft`, `SizingSpec` (`fixed_qty` | `fixed_notional` | `pct_equity` | `risk_based` | `profile`), `StopSpec`/`TpSpec` (`ticks` | `percent` | `atr` | `r_multiple`), `TicketContext` (`Instrument`, `AccountProfile`, `Wallet`, `Ticker`, `RiskSummary`, `env`, `armState`).
- `validate.ts` â€” the full rule set from SCR-060 "Validation & messages": tick multiple, min qty, qty step, min notional, leverage â‰¤ profile cap, SL/TP side correctness, reduce-only requires an open position, post-only would-cross detection, insufficient margin, **mandatory native SL when the profile requires it**, symbol not allowed, lockout/kill-switch engaged. Each rule returns a stable `code` plus the exact human copy from SCR-060 â€” copy lives in one place, not in components.
- `size.ts` â€” the Â§9.3 mirror including the Â§9.3.2 clamp chain in its fixed order, returning `{qty, appliedClamps[], stop, tps, warnings}` so the UI can say "reduced from 1.2 to 0.8 by max_position_notional".
- `submit.ts` â€” the submit pipeline: build `PlaceOrderRequest`, derive the `Idempotency-Key` **per user intent** (stable across retries of the same intent, fresh for a new intent), attach `arm_token` for one-click submissions, POST via the injected transport, map `202` to an optimistic `TradeGroup` view, and resolve terminal state from the `orders`/`executions` WS topics with a 2 s "Awaiting exchange confirmation â€” reconciling" fallback.
- `errors.ts` â€” mapping from backend error codes (`validation_failed`/`native_stop_required`, `tick_size_violation`, `lot_size_violation`, `risk_limit_breached`, `trading_disabled`, `429`, `502`) to UI presentation intent (inline field / banner / SCR-077 drawer / SCR-158 state).
- Instrumentation hooks `cv_ticket_recompute_ms` and `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms`, in the placement chosen by E30-K01.

## Out of scope
Any React component (E30-S01+), the confirmation modal, network retry policy beyond idempotent replay, backend enforcement of any rule (E29/E32/E39 own that â€” this package is defence in depth, never the only check).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Sizing parity with the backend
  Given the shared fixture matrix of instruments, profiles, wallets and stop specs
  When each fixture is sized by packages/order-ticket-core and by the backend Â§9.3 implementation
  Then the resulting qty, applied clamps and resolved stop are identical for every fixture
Scenario: Idempotency key is stable per intent
  Given a submit that fails with a network error and is retried by the user without changing any field
  Then the same Idempotency-Key is sent and the server replays rather than double-placing
  And changing any field before retrying produces a new key
Scenario: Clamp explanation is preserved
  Given a requested size of 1.2 that max_position_notional reduces to 0.8
  Then the result reports qty 0.8 with appliedClamps naming max_position_notional in the Â§9.3.2 order
Scenario: A missing native stop is a hard validation failure
  Given a profile with require_native_stop and a draft with no stop
  Then validate() returns code native_stop_required and submit() refuses to build a request at all
```

## Technical notes / design
```ts
export interface TicketCore {
  size(draft: OrderDraft, ctx: TicketContext): SizingResult;
  validate(draft: OrderDraft, ctx: TicketContext): ValidationResult; // ordered, all failures returned
  buildRequest(draft: OrderDraft, ctx: TicketContext): PlaceOrderRequest;
  submit(req: PlaceOrderRequest, ports: { post: PostOrder; clock: Clock }): Promise<SubmitOutcome>;
}
```
`validate()` returns **all** failures (the SCR-060 a11y contract summarises errors at the top), ordered by field position. Stop resolution follows Â§9.3.1 exactly, including conservative rounding *away* from entry so realised risk never exceeds the budget, and the `stop_fallback` flag when ATR is still in warmup.

Config keys: `CV_TICKET_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 2000, the reconciling threshold), `CV_TICKET_PREVIEW_DEBOUNCE_MS` (default 80, used by E30-S06's `/trade-groups/preview` calls).

Decimal arithmetic only â€” all prices and quantities are strings parsed into a decimal type (never JS `number`) before arithmetic, because tick/lot multiples must be exact; a float rounding error here becomes a `tick_size_violation` at the exchange.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥85%)**: validation matrix â€” every rule Ã— pass/fail; tick and lot rounding across at least four instruments with different filters; each sizing mode; the full clamp chain in order including two clamps binding at once; stop resolution for ticks/percent/atr with ATR warmup fallback; TP ladder remainder absorption (Â§9.3.3); idempotency-key derivation stability and change detection; error-code mapping exhaustiveness (a test fails if a new backend code has no mapping).
- **Parity**: the shared fixture matrix run against the backend implementation in CI as a required check (`ticket_sizing_parity`).
- **Property**: for random valid inputs, the sized qty is always a lot multiple, never exceeds any clamp, and the resolved stop is always on the correct side of entry.
- **Contract**: every `buildRequest()` output validates against `PlaceOrderRequest` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/instruments/{BTCUSDT,ETHUSDT,SOLUSDT,1000PEPEUSDT}.json` from `GET /instruments/{symbol}`; `fixtures/profiles/*.json` per Â§9.2.

## Security notes
The package never touches credentials â€” it receives an injected transport. The `arm_token` is passed through, never stored in the package or persisted. Idempotency-key derivation must not be predictable from another user's session (derive from a session-scoped random seed plus the intent hash, not from the intent hash alone) so a third party cannot force a replay collision.

## Accessibility notes
N/A directly (no UI), but the package owns the **error copy** that the a11y error summary renders; each message must be a complete sentence naming the constraint and the fix, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`, and is reviewed as part of E30-D05.

## Performance notes
`size()` + `validate()` together must run in â‰¤8 ms p95 under the loaded-workspace conditions measured in E30-K01, benchmarked in CI with a regression gate at +20%.

## Observability
`cv_ticket_recompute_ms` (histogram), `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms` (histogram, `env` label), `cv_ticket_validation_failed_total{code}`. No PII or account ids in metric labels.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by the named tests; parity check green as a required CI check.
- [ ] Coverage â‰¥85% on the package.
- [ ] `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3 annotated with a pointer to the mirror and the parity gate.
- [ ] Recompute benchmark recorded against the 8 ms budget.
- [ ] SAST/SCA clean; Security engineer reviewed the idempotency-key derivation.
- [ ] Code-owner review; merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E30-K01** mandates the reducer placement this package must support.
- **E29** â€” `PlaceOrderRequest`/`TradeGroup` schemas and the `orders`/`executions` topics.
- **E28** â€” `AccountProfile` (Â§9.2) shape and the backend Â§9.3 implementation this is parity-tested against.

## Branch
`feat/e30-ticket-core` Â· one PR, ~350 LOC of source plus tests; tests may exceed the LOC guidance and that is acceptable.

## References
- docs/plan/11-user-stories.md Â§17 ORD
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-060, SCR-061, SCR-076, SCR-077, SCR-113, SCR-114, SCR-158
- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-100..107, CMP-119, CMP-121, CMP-122, CMP-130, CMP-139, CMP-158, CMP-229, CMP-231, CMP-232
- docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml `/orders`, `/trade-groups/preview`, `/settings/arm`, `/instruments/{symbol}`, `/risk/summary`
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md Â§14.8, Â§15.1â€“Â§15.4
- docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md Â§9.2, Â§9.3, Â§9.4
- docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md Â§5.2 budget #4
- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md Â· docs/plan/04-security-program.md Â· docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md

title: Brackets, scaled orders & native SL invariant
body:
## Context
CandleViewer's single locked safety invariant is that **every position the product opens carries a native exchange-side stop-loss** (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` "Locked decisions"; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8; architecture principle **P4** in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`; `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md`). `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` RSK-016 — "an order reaches the exchange without a native stop-loss" — is the highest-impact risk in the project, because an emulated stop dies with our backend process while a native stop lives inside Bybit's matching engine.

E32 is where that policy sentence becomes enforced code at a **single choke point** inside **M14 (OMS / execution)** and **M17 (risk, caps & kill-switch)**, together with the order-structure features that make the invariant liveable day to day: brackets as first-class objects, partial-fill-aware protective sizing, take-profit ladders, scaled/laddered entries, DCA safety ladders with a shared stop, break-even automation, and trailing stops translated from the product's percentage/ATR UX into Bybit's **price-distance** `trading-stop.trailingStop` field (`24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.9).

The epic sits in train **R3 Trading on demo** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7, sprints **S16-S17**) and is on the R3 critical path `E09 -> E27 -> E29 -> E32 -> E34 -> E43 -> E44` (section 11). Section 12 rule 2 is explicit: *"No order-placing UI ships before the key vault (E27), risk caps and kill-switch (E39), and the native-SL invariant (E32) are Done — this ordering is a safety requirement, not a preference."* R3 exit criterion #2 belongs to this epic: an automated suite must attempt, by **every** available path, to open a position without a native SL and observe **zero escapes**.

Research backing: Bybit v5 exposes attached TP/SL on `POST /v5/order/create` and a price-distance trailing stop on `POST /v5/position/trading-stop`, but exposes **no** OCO, iceberg, TWAP or scaled-order primitive; ladders therefore ride the batch-create endpoint (max 10 orders/request, `linear` supported, partial success possible) per `24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.6.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **User stories (domain ALGO — the bracket/ladder/stop subset; the emulated OCO/iceberg/TWAP/chase/monitor subset is E33):**
  - `US-ALGO-001` Bracket orders (**Must**) — E32-S01, E32-S05
  - `US-ALGO-003` Partial take-profit ladders (Should) — E32-S02, E32-S07
  - `US-ALGO-004` Scaled entry orders (Should) — E32-S03, E32-S06
  - `US-ALGO-008` Trailing stops, fixed and percentage (**Must**) — E32-S04, E32-S07
  - `US-ALGO-009` DCA / scale-in safety ladders (Should) — E32-S03, E32-S06
  - Cross-cutting: the native-SL invariant relied on by `US-ORD-007`..`US-ORD-010`, `US-POS-004` and R3 exit criterion #2.
- **Screens:** `SCR-069` Emulated OCO / bracket builder (**bracket half only**; the standalone-OCO half is E33), `SCR-065` Scaled / ladder order builder, `SCR-064` Position SL/TP editor (modal).
- **Components:** `CMP-119` BracketEditor, `CMP-120` TrailingStopEditor, `CMP-158` SafetyInvariantNotice, `CMP-228` PreviewTile, `CMP-118` AlgoProgressCard (`algoType="scaled"`); reused `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-010` Slider, `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-100` PriceInput, `CMP-101` QtyInput, `CMP-130` SlippageEstimateChip, `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge.
- **Backend modules:** **M14** OMS (`BracketSupervisor`, `ScaledSupervisor`, `TrailingTranslator`, native-SL attach path) and **M17** risk/caps (`NativeSlGuard`, `UnprotectedPositionWatchdog`).
- **API:** `POST /api/v1/orders`, `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `GET /api/v1/orders`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/amend`, `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/cancel`, `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`; schemas `AlgoSpec` (`bracket`, `scaled`), `AlgoKind`, `TpSlMode`, `TrailingStopSpec`.
- **WS topics:** `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `trade_groups`, `system` — including `TradeGroupLeg.native_sl_confirmed` / `native_sl_confirmed_at` reaching the wire.
- **DB tables:** `trade_groups` (`algo`, `algo_params`), `trade_group_legs` (`native_sl_confirmed`, `native_sl_confirmed_at`, partial index `ix_tgl_no_sl`), `orders` (`parent_order_id`, `intent`, `order_link_id`), `order_events`, `executions`, `positions`, `account_profiles` (`require_native_sl`, `fallback_sl_offset`), `audit_log`; enums `algo_kind`, `order_intent`.
- **ADR:** `27-adrs/ADR-0028-native-sl-invariant-and-brackets.md` (new, written in E32-T04).

## Out of scope
- Emulated **OCO**, **iceberg**, **TWAP**, **chase** and the **algo monitor panel** (`US-ALGO-002/005/006/007/010`, `SCR-066/067/068/070`) — epic **E33**.
- Multi-account **fan-out** orchestration, the rate-limit governor and partial-failure unwind — epic **E34** (E32 supplies the per-leg bracket/native-SL semantics E34 replicates).
- The order ticket itself (`SCR-060`..`SCR-062`) — epic **E30**; chart/DOM drag-to-amend — epic **E31**.
- Risk caps, lockouts and the kill-switch mechanics — epic **E39** (E32 consumes them).
- Rule-engine authored ATR/structure/MA trails evaluated per bar — epics **E35/E36/E37** (E32 provides only the tighten-only `trading-stop` write path they call).
- Live trading. Everything here executes against **Bybit demo**; the live gate is E44.
- Android; any non-Bybit exchange; spot/inverse/option instruments (USDT linear perps only).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The invariant holds across every entry path
  Given the zero-escape suite exercises the order ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule action, fan-out leg, bracket, scaled ladder and DCA ladder
  When each path attempts to open a position without a native exchange-side stop-loss
  Then every attempt is rejected before any request reaches Bybit, an audit row is written, and the suite records zero escapes

Scenario: A bracket behaves as one object end to end
  Given a bracket with an entry, a native stop and a three-step take-profit ladder on Bybit demo
  When the entry partially fills and then fully fills
  Then protective quantities track the filled quantity at every step, the 30-second reconciliation job finds no orphaned protective orders, and cancelling the entry before any fill cancels every dependent protective order

Scenario: A percentage trailing stop reaches Bybit as a price distance
  Given a 1.5% trailing stop configured on a long position in SCR-064
  When the OMS arms it
  Then TrailingTranslator converts the percentage to an absolute quote-currency distance, writes it with both TP and SL sides in one POST /v5/position/trading-stop call, shows the distance and trigger price in the UI, and only ever tightens it thereafter

Scenario: Backend dies between entry fill and stop attach (failure)
  Given the process is killed after an entry fills and before the position-level stop is attached
  When the backend restarts
  Then the watchdog detects the unprotected position within 10 seconds, attaches the fallback stop at profile.fallback_sl_offset, raises a critical NakedPositionAlert, and the position is never left unprotected

Scenario: A ladder that cannot be split is refused, not silently rounded away
  Given a scaled or DCA ladder whose per-level quantity would fall below the instrument minimum lot
  When the user requests it
  Then sub-minimum levels are dropped and their quantity redistributed to the survivors, and if no viable ladder exists the request is refused with an explanation and a single-order alternative offered
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Choke point, not call sites.** Per RSK-016 mitigation the invariant is enforced in the one function through which *all* submission passes (`OMS.submit`), not sprinkled at each caller. E32-T01 builds that guard; E30/E31/E33/E34/E35 inherit it for free.
- **Attach, don't chase.** Section 8.8 rule 1: entries carry `stopLoss` on `POST /v5/order/create` so there is no window of exposure. Only when attachment is impossible (algo children that would over-attach) does the OMS place a position-level stop within a **2 s** deadline, backed by a **5 s** watchdog scan and a >10 s critical alert.
- **Only-tighten ratchet.** Section 8.8 rule 5: break-even, ATR/structure/MA trails and rule-engine stops may only tighten the native stop; loosening requires an explicit, audited user confirmation.
- **Bracket model** (`BracketParams`, section 10.7): native attached `stopLoss`, plus `takeProfit` when there is exactly one TP leg and `tpsl_mode="full"`; multi-leg TP ladders are reduce-only limit children placed on first fill and re-sized per section 9.3.3.
- **Scaled model** (`ScaledParams`, section 10.6): `levels` 2..50, equal/linear/geometric/custom distribution with `skew`, conservative rounding, duplicate-price merge, remainder to the level nearest `price_start`, sub-minimum levels dropped and redistributed, batch submission at 10 orders/request with per-item `retCode` handling.
- **Trailing translation lives in the OMS, never the UI** (`20-architecture.md` section 9 rule 6).
- **Protective reserve.** `RateBudget.reserved_for_protective` (section 8.7) guarantees a stop placement or flatten always gets a token even while a 50-level ladder saturates the entry bucket; protective traffic uses `priority="critical"`.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (>=90% on M14/M17 per the R3 local policy, absolute floor >=85%): invariant guard truth table; bracket child sizing under partial fills; TP-ladder rounding; scaled weight/rounding/merge/redistribute maths; trailing unit translation; only-tighten ratchet.
- **Contract:** OpenAPI + WS schema tests for `AlgoSpec.bracket`/`.scaled`, `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl`, `TradeGroupLeg.native_sl_confirmed`.
- **Integration:** recorded Bybit demo fixtures — partial fills, rejections, `10018` rate-limit, batch partial success, WS disconnect mid-bracket, clock skew.
- **E2E:** Playwright web + Electron over SCR-069, SCR-065, SCR-064.
- **Perf:** budget #4 — submit->ack p95 <300 ms on demo end-to-end, backend-added <=50 ms p95.
- **Chaos:** process kill between entry fill and stop attach; Postgres failover mid-ladder; exchange 5xx during TP-ladder placement.
- **Safety suite (required merge check):** the zero-escape invariant suite (E32-Q01).

## Security notes
Per `04-security-program.md` and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8, everything touching `area/oms-execution` order placement or the fan-out safety invariant is **always** treated as `security`-labelled. Threats: tampering with a bracket payload to strip the stop; elevation via a rule or API client that bypasses the choke point; repudiation of a loosened stop without an audit row; denial of service by a 50-level ladder burning the account rate budget so a protective order cannot be placed. Controls: server-side-only enforcement, RBAC `orders:write` plus account scope on every path, audit rows for every stop modification (`position.stop_modified`, `position.tp_ladder_set`, `algo.scaled_created`), the protective rate reserve, and the ladder level cap. Data classification: financial/transactional.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA on SCR-064, SCR-065, SCR-069. The generated ladder is previewed as a real table (level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional, resulting average); R-multiples and percentages are both shown as text; the native-SL guarantee is a persistent `role="note"` (CMP-158), never a tooltip or toast; every drag-equivalent has a keyboard path; "(estimated)" is in the accessible name wherever CMP-227 appears.

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2): submit->ack p95 <300 ms on demo end-to-end, backend-added <=50 ms p95; fan-out adds <=10 ms/account. Native-SL attach must complete inside the same window or the "protective stop pending" state must be surfaced. The scaled-ladder preview recomputes locally within one frame (<=16.6 ms).

## Observability
Metrics `oms_native_sl_attach_seconds`, `oms_native_sl_missing_total`, `oms_invariant_reject_total{path}`, `oms_bracket_children_total{state}`, `oms_scaled_levels_submitted_total{result}`, `oms_trailing_updates_total{kind}`, plus the existing `order_submit_seconds{transport,env}`. Critical alert `NakedPositionAlert`. Audit events `algo.scaled_created`, `algo.scaled_cancelled`, `algo.scaled_partially_cancelled`, `position.stop_modified`, `position.tp_ladder_set`. Structured logs carry `trade_group_id`, `algo_id`, `order_link_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike/Design/QA/Security ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R3 exit criterion #2 demonstrated: zero escapes from the invariant suite across all entry paths, suite wired as a **required merge check**.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on M14/M17, >=85% backend overall, >=80% frontend.
- [ ] `24-internal-schemas.md` sections 8.8/10.6/10.7, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `23-ws-protocol.md` reflect shipped behaviour; ADR-0016 merged.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-064/065/069 plus one manual screen-reader pass each.
- [ ] perf: budget #4 numbers recorded on demo.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, Critical/High closed, Security-engineer sign-off comment.
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression plus exploratory pass recorded and signed off.
- [ ] Design: CDO sign-off on SCR-064/065/069 and the design-QA sweep closed.
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at a Sprint Review against **staging (demo)**; Owner acceptance recorded.

## Dependencies
- **E29 OMS core & order state machine** — supplies `OMS.submit`, the order state machine, `orderLinkId` idempotency and the reconciliation loop the guard hooks into (roadmap graph `E29 --> E32`).
- **E39 Risk caps, lockouts & kill-switch** — the M17 module the guard lives beside; ladders must respect caps and halt on kill-switch (`E39 --> E32`).
- **E28 Per-account profiles & trade groups** — `profile.require_native_sl`, `profile.fallback_sl_offset`, sizing rules and SL/TP offsets.

title: Build the zero-escape native-SL invariant suite as a required merge check
body:
## Context
R3 exit criterion #2 (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.3) is a test, not a feature: *"an automated test suite attempts, by every available path (ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule action, fan-out, emulated algo), to open a position without a native exchange-side SL — all attempts are rejected, logged, and audited. Zero escapes."* Section 7.4's Safety gate makes this suite a **required check** — a failure blocks merge, not just release. This ticket builds that suite.

The suite must be written so paths that do not exist yet (E31 chart drag, E33 algos, E34 fan-out, E35 rule actions) are enumerated as **expected-present** cases that fail loudly when their epic lands without wiring into the choke point — otherwise the suite silently shrinks to whatever exists today, which is the exact failure mode it is meant to prevent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/safety/test_native_sl_invariant.py` — a parametrised suite over an explicit `ENTRY_PATHS` registry.
- Registry entries, each with an owning epic: `order_ticket` (E30), `chart_drag` (E31), `dom_click` (E31), `bracket` (E32), `scaled_ladder` (E32), `dca_ladder` (E32), `rule_action` (E35), `fanout_leg` (E34), `emulated_oco` (E33), `emulated_iceberg` (E33), `emulated_twap` (E33), `emulated_chase` (E33).
- Each path is exercised at the **highest layer it owns** (API call for backend paths, Playwright action for UI paths) attempting a position-opening order with no stop; the assertion is threefold: rejected, no request reached the exchange adapter (strict adapter mock that fails the test if called), and an audit row exists.
- A registry completeness test: every path marked `implemented=False` must carry a linked ticket key; when that ticket's epic is merged, CI fails until the flag is flipped and the case passes — so a new entry path cannot be added without registering it.
- An **adapter-level backstop test** independent of the registry: fuzz `PlaceOrderRequest` payloads through `OMS.submit` and assert the property "position-opening implies stopLoss present or pending-attach row exists".
- The single-call-site architecture test from E32-T01 is wired into this suite so the choke point and the escapes are gated together.
- CI wiring as a required check on `main` with no skip/allow-failure, plus a nightly full run against recorded demo fixtures.
- A published "zero escapes" report artefact per run, retained for the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Out of scope
- The invariant implementation itself (E32-T01/T02); chaos scenarios (E32-Q05); the abuse-case suite from an attacker's perspective (E32-X02, which complements this from outside the trust boundary).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every implemented path is proven to reject
  Given the ENTRY_PATHS registry
  When the suite runs
  Then every path marked implemented attempts a stopless position-opening order, is rejected, reaches no adapter call, writes an audit row, and the run reports zero escapes

Scenario: An unimplemented path is tracked, not forgotten
  Given a path marked implemented false
  Then the suite asserts it carries a linked ticket key and reports it as pending coverage, and the aggregate report states how many paths remain unproven

Scenario: A new entry path that bypasses the choke point fails the build (failure)
  Given a change adding a second call site of adapter.place_order
  When CI runs
  Then the architecture test fails and the merge is blocked

Scenario: The fuzz backstop catches a classification bug (edge)
  Given a mutation that misclassifies a hedge-mode increasing order as reduce-only
  When the property test runs
  Then the property "position-opening implies protected" fails with a minimal reproducing payload

Scenario: The suite cannot be skipped (edge)
  Given a PR marking the safety job as allowed to fail
  Then branch protection rejects the configuration change, because the safety suite is a required check per roadmap section 7.4
```

## Technical notes / design
- Strict adapter mock: `raise AssertionError` on any `place_order` call during a rejection case — an escape must fail loudly rather than being inferred from a missing log line.
- UI-layer cases use Playwright against staging (demo) with the adapter mock replaced by a network-level assertion that no `order/create` request left the backend, recorded from the backend's own egress log.
- Audit assertion checks `audit_log` content (actor, account, symbol, reason), not merely row count, so a generic row cannot satisfy a specific case.
- The report artefact is JSON plus a human summary, uploaded per run so the R3 PRR can cite dated evidence.
- Runtime budget: the required-check subset must complete in <5 minutes; the exhaustive nightly may take longer.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test deliverable. Its own quality gates: the suite is verified by **mutation testing** — deliberately weakening `NativeSlGuard` (removing the hedge-mode branch, allowing an unknown deferral reason, skipping the audit write) must make the suite fail in each case. A suite that passes against a broken guard is worthless, so this verification is a DoD item, not optional.

## Security notes
This suite is the primary evidence for RSK-016 mitigation and is cited in the R3 PRR and the pen-test scope (E43). It runs against demo only. The report artefact must not contain API keys or account secrets; account identifiers are pseudonymised.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the suite itself; the UI-layer cases drive the real screens, so an a11y-blocking regression would surface as a Playwright failure but is formally covered by E32-Q07.

## Performance notes
Required-check subset <5 minutes so it does not become the reason someone argues for making it optional.

## Observability
The suite asserts that `oms_invariant_reject_total{path}` increments per path, so the metric's correctness is tested rather than assumed.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Suite implemented with the full path registry and completeness test.
- [ ] Mutation-testing verification recorded for at least three deliberate guard weakenings.
- [ ] Wired as a required check on `main`; skip/allow-failure impossible.
- [ ] Nightly exhaustive run configured with artefact retention.
- [ ] Report artefact format agreed with the Security engineer for PRR use.
- [ ] Documented in `03-testing-strategy.md` as a named safety gate.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

title: Write the black-box test plan for brackets, TP ladders and trailing stops
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 requires a black-box test plan executed by QA/SDET with a sign-off comment per scenario before any Story reaches Done. E32-S01 (brackets), E32-S02 (TP ladders), E32-S04 (trailing) and E32-T03 (break-even) form one behavioural cluster whose interactions — a ladder leg filling while a trail is armed and break-even is pending — are where defects will actually live, and no single story's own tests cover those crossings.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Test plan document `docs/qa/plans/e32-brackets.md` covering `US-ALGO-001`, `US-ALGO-003`, `US-ALGO-008` and break-even.
- Per-scenario steps, preconditions, demo-account setup, expected results and pass/fail criteria, written so someone who has not read the code can execute them.
- Cross-feature interaction scenarios: ladder leg fills while a percentage trail is armed; break-even fires while a ladder leg is resting; trail tightens past a ladder leg's price; entry cancelled while a trail is armed; partial fill followed by break-even followed by a ladder leg fill.
- Negative and boundary scenarios: minimum-lot boundaries in ladder splitting; a stop on the wrong side; a ladder totalling >100%; loosening attempts by every user-reachable route; a position closed externally mid-operation.
- Required Bybit demo fixtures named and specified: `bracket_partial_fill`, `bracket_amend_rejected`, `ladder_leg_fill`, `trading_stop_rejected`, `position_closed_midwrite`.
- Exit criteria per story and a sign-off template.
- Traceability table mapping every Gherkin scenario in E32-S01/S02/S04/T03 to at least one plan step, so no acceptance criterion is unverified.

## Out of scope

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every acceptance criterion is traceable to a plan step
  Given the Gherkin scenarios in E32-S01, S02, S04 and T03
  When the traceability table is reviewed
  Then each scenario maps to at least one executable plan step, and any unmappable scenario is raised against the owning story

Scenario: Cross-feature interactions are covered
  Given brackets, ladders, trailing and break-even can be active simultaneously
  Then the plan contains at least five interaction scenarios exercising them together, each with an unambiguous expected result

Scenario: The plan is executable by someone who has not read the code (edge)

```

title: Implement break-even automation as an only-tighten system behaviour
body:
## Context
`24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.7 `BracketParams` carries `move_to_breakeven_at_r` and `breakeven_offset_ticks` (default 2, to cover fees), and states that break-even and trailing are handled as system behaviours that **may only tighten** the native stop (section 8.8 rule 5). SCR-064's wireframe shows "Break-even at [1.0]R offset [+ fees]" as a first-class control. This ticket implements the backend behaviour so SCR-064 (E32-S07) has something to switch on, and so the rule engine (E35) inherits a tested ratchet rather than building its own.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/oms/algos/breakeven.py` — `BreakEvenSupervisor` (module M14), subscribing to position updates.
- Trigger: unrealised R-multiple >= `move_to_breakeven_at_r`, computed as `(mark - avg_entry) / (avg_entry - initial_stop)` signed by side, using the **initial** stop distance recorded at bracket creation so later tightening does not move the R denominator.
- Action: write a new stop at `avg_entry +/- breakeven_offset_ticks` via the shared tighten-only `trading-stop` write path from E32-S04 (both sides in one call).
- Ratchet enforcement: the write is refused if it would loosen the stop; refusal is logged and counted, not raised to the user as an error.
- Idempotency: fires at most once per position per arming; re-arms only if the position is closed and reopened, or the user explicitly resets it.
- `positions` WS topic surfaces `breakeven_armed` / `breakeven_applied_at` so the UI can render the state.
- Audit event `position.stop_modified` with `reason="breakeven"`.

## Out of scope
- ATR/structure/MA trails (E35 rule engine), the SCR-064 control itself (E32-S07), the trailing translation path (E32-S04, consumed here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Break-even fires once at the configured R
  Given a long with avg entry 63,000, initial stop 62,800 and break-even at 1.0R with a 2-tick offset
  When the mark reaches 63,200
  Then the native stop is moved to 63,000 plus 2 ticks in one trading-stop call carrying both TP and SL, an audit row with reason "breakeven" is written, and the position reports breakeven_applied_at

Scenario: The R denominator is frozen at creation
  Given the stop has already been tightened by a trailing update
  When the break-even R is evaluated
  Then it still uses the initial stop distance recorded at bracket creation, so tightening the stop cannot retroactively make 1R easier to reach

Scenario: A loosening break-even write is refused (failure)
  Given the stop has already been trailed above the break-even price
  When the break-even trigger fires
  Then the write is refused as a would-loosen violation, a counter increments, the stop is unchanged, and no user-facing error is raised

Scenario: The trigger does not re-fire after a flicker (edge)
  Given the mark crosses 1R, break-even applies, and the mark falls back below 1R and crosses again
  Then break-even does not fire a second time for the same arming and no additional rate budget is consumed

Scenario: Position closed mid-evaluation (edge)
  Given the position is flattened between the trigger evaluation and the trading-stop write
  Then the write is abandoned on the "position is zero" exchange response, the algo ends cleanly, and no orphaned stop remains
```

## Technical notes / design
- Evaluation is driven by `positions` updates coalesced at 100 ms (`23-ws-protocol.md`), not by a timer, so the reaction is as fast as the feed without polling.
- `initial_stop` is persisted on the bracket row at creation (E32-S01) precisely so this computation is stable across restarts.
- All writes route through `TrailingTranslator.write_stop()` from E32-S04, which owns the both-sides rule, the ratchet and the rate-priority tagging — this ticket adds no second write path.
- Fee-aware offset: `breakeven_offset_ticks` defaults to 2 but the UI may express it as "+ fees"; the conversion from a fee estimate to ticks happens server-side using the instrument's taker fee and `tickSize`.

## Test plan
- **Unit:** R computation for long/short, frozen denominator, ratchet refusal, single-fire idempotency, fee-to-ticks conversion, flicker suppression.

title: Design-system contribution and motion spec for emulated-algo surfaces
body:
## Context
D02 and D03 introduce patterns that must not remain E33-local: the shared `AlgoBuilderShell`, the type-specific progress presentation on CMP-118 AlgoProgressCard, the degraded/halted row treatments, and the "emulated" affordance built from CMP-227 EstimatedBadge + CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires that "any new component has a design-system entry, not an ad hoc one-off". This ticket lands those contributions and specifies the motion rules for a surface whose data arrives at 2 Hz.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-118 AlgoProgressCard** extension: add `oco` to `algoType` (currently `twap|iceberg|chase|scaled`) with its leg-state presentation; specify the text-first progress string per kind ("60 %, 6 of 10 slices"; "repriced 7×, 3 ticks from arrival"); document the `emulated: true` invariant that the card never hides.
- **`AlgoBuilderShell`** added to `15-component-catalogue.md` as a molecule with props, states, a11y contract and Storybook story list.
- **Status treatments** added to the design system: `degraded`, `halted by risk control`, `orphaned` — token choices, iconography, and the rule that status is never colour-only.
- **Motion spec**: progress bars and countdowns animate at most at the 2 Hz data cadence with no easing that implies sub-second precision; state transitions (running → paused → degraded) cross-fade at 120 ms; the degraded banner enters without motion (it is a `role="status"` announcement, and motion competes with the announcement); all motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion` with a specified reduced variant.
- Token/spacing audit of the four builders and the monitor against `16-design-system-brief.md`, with any drift either justified or corrected.

## Out of scope
New screens. Behavioural design decisions (D02/D03). Implementation (S05/S06). Components owned by other epics (CMP-119 BracketEditor is E32's).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Contributions are in the system, not in the epic
  Given the new patterns from D02 and D03
  Then AlgoBuilderShell and the three status treatments exist as catalogue entries with props,
  states, a11y contract and Storybook story lists, and CMP-118 documents the oco variant

Scenario: Motion respects the data cadence
  Given progress updates arriving at 2 Hz
  Then the motion spec forbids animation implying finer granularity, and specifies the exact
  durations and easings for state transitions

Scenario: Reduced motion (edge)
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then every animation has a specified reduced variant that still communicates the state change
  without movement

Scenario: Token drift caught (edge)
  Given the audit of D02/D03 frames against the design-system brief
  Then every deviation is either corrected in the frames or recorded as a deliberate,
  justified exception in the catalogue entry
```

## Technical notes / design
Contributions follow the design-system team's intake process; entries are written in `15-component-catalogue.md`'s existing format (Tier · Purpose · Props · TypeScript interface · Data contract · A11y · Storybook).

## Test plan
Design-system review board acceptance. Storybook story lists are agreed here so E33-S05/S06's DoD checkboxes are unambiguous.

## Security notes
The `emulated: true` invariant on CMP-118 is a **safety-transparency control**, not a cosmetic prop: the catalogue entry must state that no consumer may set it false or hide the badge. Reviewed as such.

## Accessibility notes
Each new entry carries a full a11y contract (roles, accessible names, announcement politeness, contrast). The status treatments must be distinguishable in greyscale and in all three colour-vision simulations.

## Performance notes
Motion must not introduce per-row animation on SCR-070 — the 100-row case is the constraint (3 ms/frame scripting budget).

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` updated with the new/extended entries.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` motion section updated with the algo cadence rules.

title: Accessibility design review of the algo builders and monitor panel
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA with no "internal tool" exception, and the SCR-066..070 catalogue entries each carry specific a11y requirements that are easy to lose in implementation: fields labelled *with units*, the emulation caveat as a paragraph rather than a tooltip, the TWAP schedule as a real table, the chase peg as a radio group with a text price preview, the OCO residual-risk warning as an always-visible `role="note"`, running states announcing refreshes politely at most once every 5 s, and the monitor's degraded banner as `role="status"` with controls whose accessible names include their target algo and effect.

This review annotates the D02/D03 designs so those requirements arrive as a spec, not as a bug report after E33-Q05.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Annotated a11y layer over every SCR-066..070 frame: semantic roles, heading structure, landmark/table semantics, focus order, focus-trap and restoration for each modal, accessible names for every control (including the "Cancel TWAP a_12 on BTCUSDT, Main" pattern), and the reading order of the emulation/residual-risk text relative to the fields it qualifies.
- Announcement policy: which changes are `polite`, which are `assertive` (validation failures and "halted by risk control"), and the 5 s politeness throttle for running-state refreshes.
- Keyboard maps: full operability of each builder and of the monitor table, including bulk actions and the orphan adopt/cancel row actions, with no mouse-only affordance anywhere.
- Contrast and non-colour-encoding verification for every status treatment (running / paused / degraded / halted / failed / orphaned) in light, dark, greyscale and the three colour-vision simulations.
- Target-size check (≥ 24 × 24 CSS px) across both densities, especially the dense monitor rows.
- A written a11y acceptance checklist that E33-Q05 executes verbatim against the built screens.

## Out of scope
Auditing built software (E33-Q05). Implementation. Chart-canvas a11y (E11/E31).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every screen is annotated
  Given SCR-066 through SCR-070
  Then each has a complete a11y annotation layer covering roles, names, focus order,
  announcements and keyboard operation

Scenario: No mouse-only path
  Given the keyboard map for each screen
  Then every action including bulk cancel-all and orphan adoption has a keyboard path,
  and each is demonstrated in the annotation

Scenario: Status is never colour-only (edge)
  Given each status treatment rendered in greyscale and the three colour-vision simulations
  Then every status remains distinguishable by glyph and text, and contrast meets AA in both themes

Scenario: Announcement throttle specified (edge)
  Given a running iceberg refreshing slices rapidly
  Then the annotation specifies a polite announcement at most once every five seconds,
  so a screen-reader user is informed without being flooded
```

## Technical notes / design
Follow the annotation conventions already used for the R3 trading screens (E30/E31) so implementers see one consistent format across the train.

## Test plan
The deliverable checklist is itself the test artefact for E33-Q05; each item must be objectively checkable (a named role, a named key, a measured ratio), never "is accessible".

## Security notes
Accessible names must not leak data a role cannot see: a `viewer`'s monitor row names must not include controls they lack, and no accessible name may expose another account's label to a manager without access.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the accessibility notes for the epic's UI; see Scope.

## Performance notes
Announcement throttling exists partly for performance: live-region churn at 2 Hz across 100 rows is both an a11y and a main-thread problem, so the annotation caps live-region updates to aggregate summaries rather than per-row messages.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Annotation layer complete for SCR-066..070 and reviewed with the accessibility specialist.
- [ ] Keyboard maps and announcement policy published.
- [ ] Contrast/colour-vision verification recorded with measured ratios.
- [ ] The a11y acceptance checklist handed to E33-Q05 and referenced from E33-S05/S06.
- [ ] **Sign-off:** accessibility lead + CDO.

title: Prove the emulated-algo scheduler, crash-resume seam and orphan adoption
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §10.1 states the universal rule that "every algo persists its state transactionally with each child submission, so a restart resumes exactly where it stopped", and US-ALGO-005/006/007 each require resumption **within 5 seconds of process start**. That is an architectural claim nobody has measured yet, and three design choices hang on it:

1. **Where the seam is.** A child submission is a Postgres write plus a Bybit REST call. Whichever order they occur in, a crash between them leaves ambiguity. The candidate patterns are *intent-first* (persist a `pending_submit` slice row with its deterministic `order_link_id`, then submit, then mark `submitted`) versus *outbox* (write to the existing `outbox` table, `21-database-schema.md` §, and let a relay submit).
2. **How the schedule survives.** TWAP slice times must be wall-clock rows, not in-memory timers (US-ALGO-006 NFR). The question is whether one supervisor task polls a `next_action_at` index, or each run holds an asyncio task rehydrated at boot.
3. **Whether orphan adoption is deterministic.** `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.x gives `order_link_id` a structured layout (group segment + `seq2` + 2-char suffix, `ac` for algo child). Adoption must recover a resting child from `GET /v5/order/realtime` by that id alone, with no local state.

This spike answers all three with a throwaway prototype against the demo environment and the recorded-fixture harness, and records the decision in ADR-0016 (written up in E33-T03).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Throwaway prototype on `spike/e33-algo-resume` implementing a two-slice TWAP against **demo** using (a) the intent-first seam and (b) the `outbox` relay seam.
- A kill harness that `SIGKILL`s the process at each of four seams: before persist, after persist/before submit, after submit/before ack persist, after ack persist.
- Measurement of **resume latency** (process start → first correct action) for 1, 10 and 100 concurrent runs, and of scheduler drift for a 100-slice TWAP.
- An orphan-adoption probe: place a child, wipe local rows, restart, and recover it from `GET /v5/order/realtime` by its whole `order_link_id` (adopted as `untracked` under its own id, `24-internal-schemas.md` §8.5 step 3c; never by prefix).
- A comparison table + recommendation appended to the spike ticket and carried into ADR-0016.
- Follow-up tickets filed if the spike surfaces work not already covered by E33-T01.

## Out of scope
Production code (this is explicitly a throwaway spike per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5.1). Strategy logic beyond a minimal TWAP. Any live-environment use.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Seam decision made
  Given both candidate seams are prototyped and killed at all four points
  Then a comparison table records duplicate-child count, lost-child count and resume latency per seam,
  and one seam is recommended with the reason stated

Scenario: Resume budget measured
  Given 100 concurrent prototype runs and a hard process kill
  When the process restarts
  Then the time from process start to the first correct action per run is recorded at p50/p95/max
  and compared against the 5-second requirement of US-ALGO-005/006/007

Scenario: Orphan adoption proven or disproven (edge)
  Given a child order resting on demo and all local algo rows deleted
  When the prototype restarts and queries GET /v5/order/realtime
  Then it either re-associates that child by order_link_id alone, or the spike records precisely
  why it cannot and what additional persisted state E33-T01 must keep

Scenario: Scheduler drift bounded (edge)
  Given a 100-slice TWAP over 10 minutes and a deliberately suspended event loop
  Then the recorded per-slice drift and the catch-up behaviour are measured, and the finding
  states whether a polled next_action_at index or per-run tasks is required
```

## Technical notes / design
Timebox **3 working days**, agreed with the Architect. Decision criteria fixed in advance: if the intent-first seam produces zero duplicate children across all four kill points **and** p95 resume < 2 s at 100 runs, it is chosen outright and the outbox relay is not pursued; if it duplicates at any seam, the outbox relay is chosen even at a latency cost, because a duplicate child is an unintended position and a slow resume is only a delay.

`order_link_id` layout is already normative (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.x): the prototype must use it as-is, not invent one.

## Test plan
Prototype-level only: the kill harness is the test. Fixtures — the recorded Bybit partial-fill and rejection fixtures from E29's harness plus a live demo account. No coverage gate applies to spike code.

## Security notes
The prototype runs against **demo keys only**; the spike branch must not contain credentials (secrets scanning applies to the branch like any other). No production data. The spike must note any finding that affects the naked-position guarantee.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI.

## Performance notes
Targets to measure, not yet to meet: resume p95 < 2 s at 100 concurrent runs; scheduler drift < 250 ms per slice at 100 slices; submission path staying inside budget #4 (submit → ack p95 < 300 ms, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2).

## Observability
The prototype emits `oms_algo_resume_seconds` and `oms_algo_child_orders_total{kind}` so the same metric names are proven before E33-T01 adopts them.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four questions answered with recorded numbers and a comparison table.
- [ ] **ADR-0016** drafted with the chosen seam, scheduler shape and adoption strategy (finalised in E33-T03).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for anything E33-T01 does not already cover.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review / architecture review.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced (expected candidates: rate-budget exhaustion on resume storms).
- [ ] Spike branch left unmerged and marked throwaway.

E29 supplies the OMS state machine, the `order_link_id` scheme and the demo adapter the prototype submits through.
