title: Emulate OCO: race two legs and settle the loser safely
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B4). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The race and settle logic is chart-defined.

## Context
**US-ALGO-002 — Emulated OCO (Must):** *"As a trader, I want one-cancels-other behaviour, so that hitting a target cancels the stop and vice versa."* Bybit's OCO is UI-only and explicitly unavailable through the v5 API (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §10.2), so we race two orders and settle the loser.

The spec is unusually opinionated here and must be implemented as written: for the plain "TP + SL on a position" case the product uses Bybit's **native attached TP/SL** (`trading-stop` with both sides in one call) — emulated OCO exists for cases native brackets cannot express, e.g. two entry orders at different prices where only one should fill. The builder must say so (SCR-069) and the API must not let a user pick emulation where native is available and safer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/oms/algo/strategies/oco.py` implementing the `AlgoStrategy` protocol against `OcoParams` (`leg_a: OrderIntent`, `leg_b: OrderIntent`, `mode: cancel_other|reduce_other` default `reduce_other`, `reduce_only: bool = True`) exactly as `24-internal-schemas.md` §10.2.
- Leg submission: both legs submitted with `oco_group_ref` set on the `orders` rows (`21-database-schema.md` §3.3.4) and `reduce_only=True` when the OCO protects a position — which makes a double fill self-limiting at the exchange (Bybit rejects the second with `110017`).
- Settlement on fill of qty `q`: `cancel_other` → cancel the sibling when the winner is fully filled; `reduce_other` (default) → **amend** the sibling down by `q`, preserving its queue position and avoiding a naked window.
- Residual/double-fill handler: net position computed **from executions, not from intent**; excess closed with a reduce-only market order; `warning` alert; journal entry; audit `algo.oco_residual_detected` at high severity.
- Failure ladder: three failed cancel/amend attempts on the loser → run `failed`, `critical` alert, native SL left in place — the failure mode is "an extra working order", never "an unprotected position".
- Orphan sweep: when the position goes flat by any other means, both legs are cancelled within one reconciliation cycle and the run closes with reason `position flat`.
- Guardrail in the create path: an OCO whose two legs are simply a TP and an SL on one position is refused with an explanatory error steering the user to native attached TP/SL.
- Implement the `B4` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B04.oco.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('oco', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/04_oco.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_04_oco.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
The SCR-069 builder UI (E33-S05) and the monitor row (E33-S06). Brackets and TP ladders (E32). Group-level OCO (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Target hit
  Given an OCO pair on an open position
  When the target fills
  Then the stop is cancelled (or amended down, per mode) within 1 second of the fill event
  and the run closes as completed

Scenario: Both legs trigger nearly simultaneously
  Given both legs fill before either settlement lands
  Then the net position is computed from executions, the excess is closed with a reduce-only
  market order, the incident is logged and alerted, and the net exposure never exceeds the intent

Scenario: Disconnected during the fill
  Given the backend is offline when the target fills
  When it reconnects
  Then the reconciler detects the fill from the execution stream, cancels the leftover leg,
  and reports the delay it incurred

Scenario: Cancel rejected because already filled (error)
  Given the cancel of the stop is rejected with "order not found / already filled"
  Then the rejection is treated as evidence of a double fill, the resulting net position is
  computed from executions, and if the position flipped sign a reduce-only correcting order is
  placed and a high-severity incident is raised — never a silent reverse position

Scenario: Crash between fill and cancel (edge)
  Given the process is killed after the fill event is persisted but before the cancel is sent
  When it restarts
  Then the OCO state machine replays from Postgres, sends the cancel with the original
  idempotency key, and completes within 5 seconds of process start

Scenario: Duplicate fill event (edge)
  Given the same fill is delivered twice by the websocket
  Then the idempotency key makes the second settlement a no-op, exactly one audit record
  describes the OCO completion, and no extra rate-limit budget is consumed

Scenario: Position closed manually (edge)
  Given I flatten the position by hand while both legs rest
  Then both legs are cancelled as orphans within one reconciliation cycle and the run closes
  with reason "position flat"

Scenario: Native path preferred (edge)
  Given an OCO request that is simply a take-profit and a stop-loss on one position
  Then it is refused with an explanation pointing at native attached TP/SL, and nothing is sent
```

## Technical notes / design
Settlement latency budget is measured from the **WS execution frame**, not from the REST ack, because the execution stream is the source of truth (E29 / ADR-0006).

Idempotency: every outbound cancel/amend carries a deterministic key derived from `(algo_run_id, slice_seq, intent_sequence)` — US-ALGO-002 NFR. The reconciler is authoritative over the UI.

Error mapping: `110001` order-not-found on the loser's cancel after a winner fill is the *expected* benign race and must not raise; the same code on an untriggered leg is a real fault.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B4.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: settlement in both modes; partial-fill amend arithmetic including lot-size rounding; residual computation from executions with duplicate and out-of-order delivery; the three-failure ladder; the native-preferred guardrail; orphan sweep on flat.
- **Integration**: recorded Bybit fixtures for `110017` reduce-only rejection, `110001` cancel-after-fill, and a synthetic simultaneous-fill fixture.
- **Chaos**: kill between fill persist and cancel send — the dedicated seam named in the story; must complete within 5 s of restart.
- **Perf**: fill event → cancel/amend request issued ≤ 300 ms p95 over 1 000 simulated races.
- Coverage ≥ 90 % on `packages/oms/algo/strategies/oco.py`.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B4.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Order-placing path → `security`-labelled. Threats: double-fill producing an unintended reverse position (the epic's most consequential integrity risk — mitigated by reduce-only legs, execution-derived netting and the correcting order); repudiation (every leg fill, cancel and residual correction audited); tampering (leg intents revalidated server-side against instrument filters and the account profile). Manual abuse-case check required: attempt an OCO as a `viewer`, and while the kill-switch is engaged.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The UI obligations live on E33-S05 / E33-S06.

## Performance notes
Fill → opposing-leg settlement request ≤ 300 ms p95 (SCR-069 performance note). Submission of both legs inside budget #4 (p95 < 300 ms per order).

## Observability
Audit `algo.oco_created`, `algo.oco_leg_filled`, `algo.oco_leg_cancelled`, `algo.oco_race_resolved {winner, resolutionMs}`, `algo.oco_residual_detected` (high severity), `algo.oco_cancelled|completed|failed`. Metric `oms_oco_race_resolution_ms` histogram, `oms_oco_residual_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a test that names it.
- [ ] Coverage ≥ 90 % on the strategy module; package ≥ 85 %.
- [ ] Chaos seam test in CI and green.
- [ ] `24-internal-schemas.md` §10.2 updated if behaviour diverged.
- [ ] Security review comment; abuse cases executed.
- [ ] Perf benchmark for race resolution recorded.
- [ ] QA sign-off with pass/fail per scenario (E33-Q01).
- [ ] Demoed on demo environment.
- [ ] Feature flag `algo.oco` recorded: demo on, live off until R4.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.
- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.

## Dependencies
E33-T01 (framework, guards, persistence, idempotency). E29 (execution stream, cancel/amend routes, reconciler). E32 (native SL that remains the floor when OCO fails).

`feat/e33-oco`.

title: Build the AlgoSupervisor framework: state store, scheduler, resume, adoption
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B4-B7). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The state store and resume come from persistence restore. `MonotonicScheduler` (hard timing) stays in plain code.

## Context
Every emulated strategy in this epic and the scaled/bracket strategies in E32 are small state machines with the *same* hard parts: transactional persistence, wall-clock scheduling, crash resume, orphan adoption, rate-budget accounting, kill-switch obedience and audit. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §10.1 specifies that common model once (`AlgoSpec`, `AlgoState`, the `pending → running → paused → completing → completed | cancelled | failed` state diagram and five universal rules). This task implements it once, so that S01–S04 are each a small strategy plug-in rather than four copies of the same risky machinery.

The seam, scheduler shape and adoption strategy are fixed by **E33-K01 / ADR-0016** — implement that decision, do not re-litigate it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New package `packages/oms/algo/` inside module **M14**:
  - `models.py` — `AlgoSpec`, `AlgoState` and the per-strategy params models exactly as in `24-internal-schemas.md` §10.1–§10.5 (`OcoParams`, `IcebergParams`, `TwapParams`, `ChaseParams`), re-exported for the API layer.
  - `supervisor.py` — `AlgoSupervisor` with `start(algo_spec) -> algo_id`, `pause(algo_id)`, `resume(algo_id)`, `cancel(algo_id, flatten: bool)`, `adopt(order_id, algo_id)`, plus the strategy registry that E32 also registers `scaled`/`bracket` into.
  - `strategy.py` — the `AlgoStrategy` Protocol: `plan_next(state, snapshot) -> Action | None`, `on_execution(state, execution)`, `on_child_terminal(state, order)`, `on_halt(state, reason)`.
  - `store.py` — transactional state persistence and the resume query.
  - `scheduler.py` — the persisted wall-clock scheduler driven by `next_action_at`.
  - `guards.py` — pre-flight and per-child guards (see below).
- Postgres migration adding:
  - `algo_runs` (`id uuid pk`, `kind algo_kind`, `account_id`, `symbol`, `side`, `total_qty`, `params jsonb`, `status`, `filled_qty`, `remaining_qty`, `slices_done`, `slices_total`, `avg_fill_price`, `started_at`, `next_action_at`, `last_error`, `failure_count`, `on_disconnect`, `created_by`, `rule_id`, `halt_reason`, timestamps) with `CREATE INDEX ix_algo_runs_due ON algo_runs (next_action_at) WHERE status IN ('running','pending')`.
  - `algo_slices` (`id`, `algo_run_id fk`, `seq int`, `order_link_id text unique`, `order_id uuid null fk orders(id)`, `planned_at`, `planned_qty`, `planned_price`, `state`, `error_code`, `error_msg`) with `UNIQUE (algo_run_id, seq)`.
  - The **chase invariant** as a DB constraint: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_algo_one_live_child ON algo_slices (algo_run_id) WHERE state = 'live'` (US-ALGO-007 NFR: "enforced by a database-level unique constraint on (algorithm id, live order)").
  - Existing `orders` columns are reused, not duplicated: `algo`, `algo_params`, `parent_order_id`, `oco_group_ref` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.3.4).
- The five universal rules of §10.1 implemented in the framework: transactional persist-per-child; `on_disconnect="freeze"` default; first-fill native-SL attach delegated to E32/M17 (**never bypassed**); child `order_link_id` derived from the parent group segment with incremented `seq2` and the `ac` suffix; `origin="algo_child"` set so rules cannot manage children.
- Resume-on-boot: rehydrate every non-terminal run, adopt resting children by `order_link_id`, recompute `filled_qty` from `executions` (never from the local accumulator), and reach the first correct action within 5 s.
- Guards: kill-switch and risk-lockout checks (E39) before every child submission; rate-budget token acquisition from the per-account bucket with the protective reserve untouched (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8); `max_children` (450) and `max_duration_ms` caps; `cancel_on_position_flat`.
- Metrics/audit plumbing consumed by all strategies (see Observability).
- Implement the `B4-B7` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B04.oco.machine.json (+B05/B06/B07)` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('algo_supervisor', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/04_algo_supervisor.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_04_algo_supervisor.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
The four strategy implementations themselves (S01–S04). API endpoints and WS projection (T02). UI (S05, S06). Scaled/bracket strategies (E32). Group-level algos (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A strategy plug-in runs end to end
  Given a two-action test strategy registered in the supervisor
  When it is started against the demo adapter
  Then each action persists its slice row and its deterministic order_link_id in the same
  transaction as the submission intent, and the run reaches "completed"

Scenario: Resume after a hard kill
  Given 100 runs of the test strategy across all four kill seams
  When the process is SIGKILLed and restarted
  Then every run resumes from Postgres, no child order is duplicated, filled quantities are
  recomputed from the executions table, and the first correct action occurs within 5 seconds
  of process start (p95)

Scenario: Orphan adoption
  Given a resting child whose algo_slices row is missing
  When the supervisor boots and reconciles against the exchange
  Then the child is adopted by order_link_id into the correct run rather than duplicated,
  or, if no run matches, it is reported as an orphan for the monitor panel

Scenario: Kill-switch blocks new children (failure)
  Given the kill-switch is engaged
  When any strategy requests a child submission
  Then the guard refuses it, the run transitions to "halted by risk control" with the reason,
  an audit event is written, and no request reaches the exchange

Scenario: Rate budget exhausted (edge)
  Given the account's order token bucket is empty
  Then the supervisor pauses the run rather than queueing stale actions, the protective reserve
  is left untouched so a stop-loss or flatten can still get a token, and resumption is automatic
  when tokens return

Scenario: Child cap (edge)
  Given a run that would exceed max_children (450)
  Then the run stops issuing children, ends in "completed" with remaining quantity reported,
  and never approaches Bybit's 500 active-orders-per-symbol limit (error 110020)
```

## Technical notes / design
State machine exactly as the `stateDiagram-v2` in `24-internal-schemas.md` §10.1. `failure_count > 3` → `failed`. Persist-then-submit ordering follows ADR-0016.

`AlgoStrategy` is a `Protocol`, so a strategy is pure planning logic: it reads `AlgoState` plus a `MetricSnapshot`/book snapshot and returns an `Action` (`Submit`, `Amend`, `Cancel`, `Sleep(until)`, `Finish(status)`); the supervisor owns every side effect. This is what makes strategies unit-testable without an exchange.

Error-code mapping reuses `24-internal-schemas.md` §8 table: `110001` order-not-found during an amend race is *benign*; `110017` reduce-only rejection is the self-limiting double-fill guard; `110020` is the order cap; `10018` is rate limiting and must back off with jitter.

Config keys: `oms.algo.max_children=450`, `oms.algo.max_failures=3`, `oms.algo.resume_deadline_ms=5000`, `oms.algo.reconcile_interval_s=30`, `oms.algo.default_on_disconnect=freeze`.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B4-B7.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (≥ 90 % on `packages/oms/algo`): state transitions for every edge of the §10.1 diagram; `order_link_id` derivation (group segment, `seq2` increment, `ac` suffix, uniqueness); slice-row transactional semantics; guard refusal for kill-switch, lockout, empty bucket, child cap, duration cap; `filled_qty` recomputation from executions including duplicate execution delivery; adoption matching and non-matching.
- **Contract**: `AlgoSpec` params models round-trip against the `22-api-openapi.yaml` `AlgoSpec` schema (enum parity for `AlgoKind`, including `scaled` and `bracket` owned by E32).
- **Integration**: recorded Bybit fixtures — partial fill, rejection, `10018`, `110017`, `110020`, WS disconnect mid-run.
- **Migration**: forward/backward migration test; the `ux_algo_one_live_child` index rejects a second live slice.
- **Chaos**: the E33-K01 kill harness promoted into CI as `tests/chaos/test_algo_resume.py`, four seams × four strategies (test strategy + the three shipping by the time it runs).
- **Perf**: resume of 100 runs, scheduler drift at 100 slices.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B4-B7.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Threats (from E33-X01 / `04-security-program.md`): **Tampering** — a client-supplied `AlgoSpec` must be validated server-side against instrument filters and the account profile's caps, never trusted; **Elevation of privilege** — `start`/`cancel` require the caller to hold the account's trade permission, re-checked at the supervisor, not only at the route; **Denial of service / denial of wallet** — an unbounded algo is the epic's worst-case abuse, bounded by `max_children`, `max_duration_ms`, the token bucket and the protective reserve; **Repudiation** — every transition writes an `audit_log` row with actor, account, params and reason. Data classification: financial. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend only.

## Performance notes
Resume p95 < 2 s at 100 concurrent runs (5 s hard requirement). Scheduler drift < 250 ms per slice. Supervisor overhead on the submission path ≤ 10 ms so budget #4 (submit → ack p95 < 300 ms, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2) is unaffected.

## Observability
Metrics `oms_algo_active{kind,status}`, `oms_emulated_algo_total{kind}`, `oms_algo_child_orders_total{kind}`, `oms_algo_resume_seconds`, `oms_algo_guard_refusals_total{reason}`, `oms_algo_scheduler_drift_ms`. Structured logs per transition with `algo_id`, `kind`, `account_id`, `seq`. Audit `algo.created|paused|resumed|cancelled|completed|failed` plus `algo.halted_by_risk_control{reason}`. Traces: run → child submission → execution.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified by the tests named above; chaos suite green in CI.
- [ ] Coverage ≥ 90 % on `packages/oms/algo`, package total ≥ 85 %.
- [ ] Migration reviewed by a code owner; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` updated with `algo_runs` / `algo_slices` and the unique partial index.
- [ ] `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §10.1 updated if the implementation diverged from the spec.
- [ ] ADR-0016 referenced; deviations from it recorded.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment; SAST/SCA clean or triaged.
- [ ] Perf benchmark recorded (resume, drift, submission overhead).
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue, each ≤ 400 LOC.
- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.

## Dependencies
E33-K01 fixes the seam and scheduler shape. E33-X01 supplies the threat model whose controls the guards implement. E32 owns the native-SL attach this framework calls and the sibling strategies it hosts. E39 supplies the kill-switch and lockout checks. E29 supplies the OMS state machine, `order_link_id` scheme, execution stream and rate-limit buckets.

## Branch
`feat/e33-algo-supervisor`. Split: migration + models PR, then supervisor + scheduler PR, then guards + resume PR.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §18 ALGO (US-ALGO-002, 005, 006, 007, 010)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-066 TWAP builder, SCR-067 Iceberg (emulated) builder, SCR-068 Chase-limit builder, SCR-069 Emulated OCO / bracket builder, SCR-070 Algo monitor panel, SCR-063 Positions & orders panel (Algos tab)

- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.18 ALGO rows
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `POST /orders`, `PATCH /orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /orders/{orderId}`, `POST /orders/cancel-all`, `GET /orders`, `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`; schemas `AlgoSpec`, `AlgoKind`, `OrderIntent`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` private topics `orders`, `executions`, `positions`; `algo_kind` enum in the order frames (§13)

title: Expose algo control API, WS projection, feature flags and audit events
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B4-B7). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The audit events come from `CvAuditPlugin`; the WS projection is `machines.algo.state` (29 SS4d).

## Context
`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already carries `AlgoSpec` / `AlgoKind` on `POST /orders` (§`/orders`, schema `AlgoSpec` with `oco`, `iceberg`, `twap`, `chase`, `scaled`, `bracket` sub-objects), so *creating* an emulated algo needs no new endpoint. What does not exist yet is the control surface the UI needs: listing runs, pausing, resuming, cancelling (optionally with flatten) and adopting an orphan — plus the WS projection that makes SCR-070 reflect **server** state rather than client memory (US-ALGO-010 NFR).

Interface-first rule (`01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10): this schema delta is drafted and reviewed **before** S05/S06 start, and it is what those stories are `blocked_by`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- OpenAPI delta in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`:
  - `GET /algos` — list runs, filters `account_id`, `symbol`, `kind`, `status`, `include_orphans`; returns `AlgoRun` (mirrors `AlgoState` of `24-internal-schemas.md` §10.1 plus `kind`, `symbol`, `side`, `account_id`, `params`, `halt_reason`, `next_action_at`).
  - `GET /algos/{algoId}` — one run with its slice history.
  - `POST /algos/{algoId}/control` — body `{action: pause|resume|cancel|cancel_and_flatten, reason?}`; idempotent by `Idempotency-Key`.
  - `POST /algos/cancel-all` — body `{account_id?, kind?}`; returns a per-run result list so the UI can report "results per item" (US-ALGO-010 scenario 2).
  - `POST /algos/orphans/{orderId}/adopt` and `POST /algos/orphans/{orderId}/cancel`.
  - New error slugs registered in the shared catalogue: `algo_not_found`, `algo_terminal`, `algo_control_conflict`, `algo_flag_disabled`, `algo_orphan_unmatched`.
- WS projection: algo state is published on the existing private **`orders`** topic (SCR-070 "Data: WS `orders`"), coalesced to **2 Hz**, as an `algo_run` record carrying the same fields as `AlgoRun`; `23-ws-protocol.md` §13 updated with the record schema and its `algo_kind` enum parity assertion.
- Feature flags `algo.oco`, `algo.iceberg`, `algo.twap`, `algo.chase` seeded `false` in `feature_flags` (`21-database-schema.md` §, defaults per `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` flag table) and enforced at the route: a disabled kind is refused with `algo_flag_disabled` **before** any exchange call.
- RBAC: `owner` full; `manager` limited to accounts granted via `user_account_access`; `viewer` read-only (`GET` only). Every mutating verb writes an `audit_log` row.
- Audit event emission for the full catalogue named in `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-066..070 (`algo.twap_created`, `algo.iceberg_slice_replaced`, `algo.oco_race_resolved`, `algo.chase_limit_reached`, …) wired from the supervisor's transition hooks.
- Implement the `B4-B7` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/machines.algo.state` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('algo_supervisor', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/04_algo_supervisor.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_04_algo_supervisor.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
Strategy behaviour (S01–S04). UI (S05, S06). Creating algos (already `POST /orders`). Group-level algo control (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Control verbs work and are idempotent
  Given a running TWAP
  When pause is sent twice with the same Idempotency-Key
  Then the run is paused, the second call returns the same result, and exactly one audit row exists

Scenario: Terminal run refuses control (failure)
  Given a completed chase run
  When cancel is sent
  Then 409 with error slug algo_terminal is returned, no exchange request is made, and the
  attempt is logged

Scenario: Disabled feature flag (failure)
  Given the algo.iceberg flag is false
  When an iceberg AlgoSpec is posted to /orders
  Then it is refused with algo_flag_disabled before any exchange call and the refusal is audited

Scenario: RBAC (edge)
  Given a viewer and a manager without access to account A
  When either calls any mutating algo verb on a run belonging to account A
  Then 403 is returned, no state changes, and an audit row records the denied attempt

Scenario: WS projection reflects server state
  Given a TWAP progressing through slices
  Then algo_run records arrive on the orders topic at no more than 2 Hz with the current
  status, filled and remaining quantities, slices done/total and next action time

Scenario: Cancel-all reports per item (edge)
  Given five running algos of which one is already terminal
  When cancel-all is called
  Then the response lists a per-run outcome, four are cancelled, the terminal one reports
  algo_terminal, and the call itself succeeds
```

## Technical notes / design
`AlgoRun` is a projection of `algo_runs` + aggregated `algo_slices`; it must never be built from in-memory supervisor state, so that a second API replica answers identically. Cancellation semantics per strategy: `cancel` cancels working children per that strategy's policy; `cancel_and_flatten` additionally submits a reduce-only close through the normal OMS path (never a raw exchange call).

Contract tests assert enum parity for `AlgoKind` across OpenAPI, the Postgres `algo_kind` type and the WS `algo_kind` enum, using the existing `enum_parity_*` harness described in `22-api-openapi.yaml`'s contract-assertion block.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B4-B7.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: projection building, control-verb state guards, flag enforcement, RBAC scoping, idempotency-key replay.
- **Contract**: OpenAPI schema validation of every new path; `enum_parity_algo_kind`; WS `algo_run` record validated against the §13 JSON Schema.
- **Integration**: control verbs against a live supervisor with the demo adapter; cancel-and-flatten produces exactly one reduce-only close.
- **E2E**: covered indirectly by S05/S06 suites.
- Coverage ≥ 85 % backend.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B4-B7.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Every route is an order-affecting path → `security`-labelled by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8. Threats: privilege escalation across accounts (mitigated by `user_account_access` scoping re-checked in the service layer), replay (idempotency keys), information disclosure (`params` may reveal strategy intent — restricted to users with access to the account), repudiation (audit rows on every verb). Abuse case for E33-X02: cancel-all used as a griefing tool by a manager against another manager's accounts.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — API only; the a11y obligations land on S05/S06.

## Performance notes
`GET /algos` p95 < 150 ms with 500 runs. WS projection coalesced to 2 Hz to keep SCR-070 inside its 3 ms-per-frame budget with 100 rows.

## Observability
Metrics `api_algo_control_total{action,result}`, `api_algo_list_seconds`. Audit events as listed in Scope. Logs carry `algo_id` and `account_id` on every verb.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria verified; contract tests green.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` updated and reviewed **before** S05/S06 begin (interface-first gate).
- [ ] Coverage ≥ 85 % backend on touched packages.
- [ ] Feature flags documented in `21-database-schema.md`'s flag table.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment; RBAC matrix test extended to the new routes.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.
- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.

## Dependencies
E33-T01 provides the supervisor and the tables this projects from. E29 supplies the RBAC-scoped order routes and the WS private-topic machinery. E39 supplies the kill-switch flag surfaced in `halt_reason`.

## Branch
`feat/e33-algo-control-api`.

title: STRIDE threat model for the emulated-algo supervisor
body:
## Context
`04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes it default-on for any epic touching the OMS. E33 introduces something new to the system's risk surface: **long-lived, autonomous, order-placing processes** that outlive the user's session, hold a standing authorisation, and issue requests at the highest rate in the product. This model must be complete **before** E33-T01 implements the guards, so the guards are controls rather than afterthoughts — hence T01 is `blocked_by` this ticket.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Data-flow diagram of the algo path: client → `POST /orders` with `AlgoSpec` → validation → `AlgoSupervisor` → strategy → guards (kill-switch, lockout, token bucket, caps) → exchange adapter → Bybit; plus the feedback path WS executions → supervisor → state store → WS projection → SCR-070.
- STRIDE analysis per element and per flow, with at minimum:
  - **Spoofing** — who may start an algo on which account; session/token reuse; the standing authorisation of a run whose creator's access is later revoked.
  - **Tampering** — client-supplied `AlgoSpec` fields (slice counts, display qty, offsets) used to exceed intended exposure; parameter mutation on a running run; tampering with the test-only fault-injection and RNG-seed hooks.
  - **Repudiation** — "I never started that TWAP": audit completeness for create/pause/resume/cancel/adopt and for every child order, with actor and parameters.
  - **Information disclosure** — algo params reveal hidden size and execution intent; cross-account visibility for managers; WS projection leaking runs on accounts the subscriber cannot see.
  - **Denial of service / denial of wallet** — reprice storms and refill storms exhausting the per-UID budget and starving protective orders; unbounded duration/child counts; resume storms after a restart; using cancel-all as a griefing tool.
  - **Elevation of privilege** — a `viewer` or an out-of-scope `manager` invoking control verbs; orphan **adopt** used to take control of an order created by another user.
- For each threat: likelihood/impact rating, the control that mitigates it, and where that control lives (E33-T01 guards, E33-T02 RBAC, DB constraint, config floor, UI affordance).
- A required-controls list handed to E33-T01/T02 as acceptance criteria, and an abuse-case list handed to E33-X02.
- Explicit treatment of the **residual risk** that defines this epic: emulated algos stop when the backend stops. The model must state the accepted mitigation (native SL always present, `on_disconnect="freeze"`, degraded banner, monitor visibility) and record Owner acceptance.

## Out of scope
Executing abuse cases (X02). Final sign-off (X03). Key management (E27/ADR-0009). Fan-out threats (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model is complete and rated
  Given the algo data-flow diagram
  Then every element and flow has a STRIDE analysis with rated threats, each mapped to a named
  control and the ticket that implements it

Scenario: Controls become acceptance criteria
  Given the required-controls list
  Then each control appears as an acceptance criterion or test on E33-T01 or E33-T02,
  verified by a cross-reference check

Scenario: Standing authorisation addressed (edge)
  Given a manager whose account access is revoked while their TWAP is running
  Then the model states the required behaviour (re-check per child, halt on revocation)
  and that behaviour is assigned to a ticket

Scenario: Residual risk accepted explicitly (edge)
  Given the backend-outage residual risk
  Then it is documented with its mitigations and carries a recorded Owner acceptance
  in 32-risk-register.md, rather than being treated as closed
```

## Technical notes / design
Use the program's STRIDE template and store the model with the other epic threat models. Rate with the program's likelihood/impact scale so E33's risks are comparable with E27/E29/E34/E35/E39/E42.

Cross-reference `24-internal-schemas.md` §8 (token buckets, protective reserve) and §10.1 (universal rules) — several needed controls already exist as design decisions and should be recorded as such rather than re-invented.

## Test plan
The model's outputs are testable artefacts: each control maps to a test in T01/T02/X02. A review session with the OMS tech lead and the Architect validates that no flow was missed.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security analysis; its own quality bar is that every Critical/High threat has a control with a named owner before E33-T01 starts, per the R3 security gate ("STRIDE for E27, E29, E34, E35, E39, E42 — all Critical/High closed"; E33 is held to the same bar as an order-placing epic).

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Several controls are performance constraints (reprice floor, token reserve); the model must state them as security controls so they cannot be "optimised away" later.

## Observability
The model specifies the minimum audit set for non-repudiation, which E33-T01/T02 implement and E33-Q01 verifies.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Threat model document merged and linked from the epic and from `04-security-program.md`'s per-epic index.
- [ ] Every Critical/High threat has a mapped control and an owning ticket.
- [ ] Required-controls list referenced by E33-T01/T02 acceptance criteria.
- [ ] Abuse-case list handed to E33-X02.
- [ ] Residual-risk entry added to `32-risk-register.md` with Owner acceptance.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed by the Security engineer and the Architect.

## Dependencies
E33-D01 informs the UI-side transparency controls. E29/E39 supply the existing OMS and risk controls this model builds on.

body:
## Context
SCR-061 (trade-group ticket) and SCR-062 (trade-group manager) are the two screens E34 introduces. Both are new interaction territory: no prior screen in the product asks a user to reason about *N simultaneous executions with different sizes on different accounts*, and both have a failure state — a partially-executed fan-out — that `14-screens-catalogue.md` requires to be **"drawn as the primary design case, not an afterthought"**.

The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence) applies: no frontend work on E34-S04/S05 (Sprint 19) starts until the design tickets are Status=Done, and they must have been Done for ≥2 sprints.

This ticket produces the signed-off hi-fi for **SCR-061**, the screen that turns one intent into N orders.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes → hi-fi in Figma for SCR-061, resolving the ASCII sketch in `14-screens-catalogue.md` into real layout, type and tokens from `16-design-system-brief.md`, at the product's supported densities.
- **Every state drawn** (the catalogue's list is the checklist): previewing · ready · partial-send in progress with per-row live status (queued → sent → accepted / rejected) · **partial failure as the primary case** (3 of 5 filled) · rate-limit backoff showing the per-UID budget and the deferral countdown · blocked (an account in lockout; the kill-switch engaged) · empty (no accounts selectable) · loading · preview-failed error.
- The per-account preview table: profile summary, resolved qty, leverage, SL, status and **WARN** rows (e.g. "within 12% of daily loss cap"), plus excluded rows that always state the reason, and the sub-minimum row that offers the minimum as a one-click choice.
- Per-row override affordance designed as **visibly exceptional** (a sign-off criterion in the catalogue), and the forbidden-override disabled state with "capped by profile".
- Recovery actions for a partial fan-out: retry failed, unwind accepted, leave as is — using the vocabulary fixed by D01, each naming its exact scope.
- Mandatory native-SL presentation per leg before submit (CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice placement), the DEMO/LIVE badge per account row, and the arm/lock indicator (CMP-229).
- Redlines: spacing, type ramp, token names, focus order, hit targets, and the copy deck for every message named above.
- Tick the catalogue's SCR-061 **Design sign-off acceptance checklist** item by item: account selector with per-account computed size/leverage/SL · partial-failure drawn as the primary case · per-account rate-limit budget indicator · aggregate vs per-account confirmation · mandatory native SL per leg before submit · retry/cancel-remaining actions · DEMO/LIVE badge per row.

## Out of scope

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue state exists
  Given the state list in 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-061
  When the Figma file is reviewed
  Then each listed state has a frame, including partial failure, rate-limit backoff and blocked

Scenario: Partial failure is primary
  Then the partial-failure frame is the file's cover frame and is specified at the same fidelity as the happy path
  And the three recovery actions each state their scope in the button label, not only in adjacent text

Scenario: Nothing is colour-only
  Given the WARN, excluded, rejected and deferred row treatments
  Then each is distinguishable in a greyscale export and each carries a text label
```

## Technical notes / design
Use only existing tokens; anything new is raised as a design-system contribution on D04 rather than drawn inline. The preview table must be specified as a real data table (not a custom grid) so the FE implementation can meet its a11y contract with native semantics.

## Test plan
Design validation: a 5-minute comprehension check with the Owner on the partial-failure frame before sign-off; any misread element is revised and re-checked.

## Security notes
No real account labels, balances, keys or order ids in any frame — use the standard demo fixture names (Main, sub_001…). The DEMO/LIVE badge treatment must be impossible to confuse at a glance; live styling must be visually dominant.

## Accessibility notes
Annotate focus order, roles (table, `role="alert"` for the partial-failure summary), accessible names for the send button (naming the account count) and for the override control, contrast ratios against `05-accessibility-standard.md`, and ≥24 px hit targets. D04 reviews these formally.

## Performance notes
Design must not require more than the 300 ms preview budget to feel correct: specify the skeleton/loading treatment for the preview table so a 300 ms wait is never a blank region.

N/A.

Scenario: Confirmations restate scope
  Given a flatten-group action on a 5-leg group
  Then the confirmation copy names the action, the leg count and the group id, generated from live data

Scenario: Motion degrades gracefully
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set

## Context

Both E34 screens are dense data tables with a critical alert state and destructive actions — precisely the combination where a11y defects are cheap to fix in design and expensive to fix in code.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Formal accessibility review of the D02 and D03 artefacts against `05-accessibility-standard.md` and WCAG 2.2 AA, producing a findings list with a severity per item and a sign-off once all blockers are resolved in the Figma files.
- Verify specifically: table semantics and header association for the preview and the nested leg table; `aria-sort` on sortable headers; the partial-failure summary as `role="alert"` with a defined focus behaviour; accessible names that carry scope ("Send group (3 accounts)", "Flatten all 5 legs of group tg_0912"); every status distinguishable without colour (greyscale test); contrast ratios for every status token incl. title: Dry-run a fan-out and return resolved per-account sizing, risk and rejections
body:
## Context
`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.4 rule 1 is binding: **"Dry-run preview is mandatory in the UI before a multi-account submit. The preview is the same code path as execution (`dry_run=True`), so what is previewed is what is sent."** SCR-061's entire top half is that preview — a row per account showing the resolved qty, leverage, SL, risk and the reason for every exclusion.

This story implements `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` (`22-api-openapi.yaml`: "Runs the full fan-out pipeline without submitting anything, returning exactly what each leg would" do). It delivers the server half of **US-PROF-006** scenario 1 and **US-ORD-014** scenario 2 (group preview aggregates across accounts and expands per account), and it is the surface on which US-PROF-008's per-leg overrides are validated before anyone can send them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` handler per `22-api-openapi.yaml` — same request schema as `POST /trade-groups`, response mirroring the resolved leg shape, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` (preview is write-scoped because it discloses per-account equity-derived sizing).
- `TradeGroupFanout.resolve(cmd, dry_run=True)` in M14 — one function, two callers (this endpoint and E34-S02), so preview/execute divergence is structurally impossible.
- Per-leg resolution pipeline in the order mandated by `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`account profile → request-level defaults → legs[].overrides`, later wins) calling into E28's sizing (`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.3) and E32's SL/TP derivation; each leg's wallet snapshot must be ≤2 s old or is refreshed first (§9.4 rule 2).
- Per-leg outcome classification, kept strictly distinct per §9.5 "Skips vs failures": **skip** (`symbol_not_allowed`, `below_min_notional`, `profile_disabled`, account key self-check failed) vs **failure** (`risk_limit_breached`, `INSUFFICIENT_MARGIN`) vs **warn** (within 12% of the daily-loss cap — the SCR-061 WARN row).
- `sizing_explanation` string per leg, human-readable and exactly as exemplified in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`"risk_based: 250 USD / (63100.00 - 62900.00) = 1.25 BTC capped by max_notional_usd 25000 -> 0.396 BTC"`).
- Group totals: total qty, total notional, estimated fee, aggregate risk in USDT and R (US-ORD-014).
- **Rate-budget visibility**: the preview reports, per account, whether the pre-flight reservation would succeed now and the refill ETA if not, without consuming tokens.
- Native-SL precondition check: a leg whose resolved parameters would produce no stop is marked rejected at preview time with `no_native_sl_possible` — it can never reach submission (`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.4 rule 5).
- Audit: `trade_group.preview` is **not** written to `audit_log` (it is not a state change) but is counted as a metric; an `arm_token` is *not* required for preview.

## Out of scope
- Actually sending anything → E34-S02. The endpoint must be provably side-effect-free apart from a possible wallet refresh.
- The sizing algorithm and risk caps themselves → E28.
- The SCR-061 UI → E34-S04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Three accounts, three different sizes
  Given accounts Main (risk 0.5% equity), sub_001 (fixed 0.1 BTC) and sub_002 (risk 0.5% equity)
  When I preview a limit buy of BTCUSDT at 64010 with SL 63900 against the group
  Then each row returns its own resolved qty, leverage and SL price with a sizing_explanation
  And the group totals report total qty, notional, estimated fee and aggregate risk in USDT and R

Scenario: Excluded account states its reason
  Given sub_003's profile does not allow BTCUSDT
  When I preview the same intent
  Then sub_003 is returned as skipped with reason symbol_not_allowed and no resolved sizing
  And the skip is presented as a skip, never counted as a failure in the totals

Scenario: Below minimum lot
  Given sub_004's resolved quantity is 0.0004 BTC and the symbol minimum is 0.001
  Then sub_004 is skipped with below_min_notional naming the minimum
  And the response includes the minimum so the UI can offer it as a one-click choice

Scenario: Preview never sends
  Given a preview request for five accounts
  When it completes
  Then zero calls were made to POST /v5/order/create and zero rate-budget tokens were committed
  And no trade_groups or trade_group_legs row was created

Scenario: A leg that cannot carry a stop is rejected in preview
  Given a leg whose profile defines no SL offset and the request supplies none
  Then that leg is rejected with no_native_sl_possible and the group is flagged not-submittable as configured

Scenario: Out-of-scope account
  Given a Manager whose granted_accounts exclude account C
  When the preview request names account C as a leg
  Then the response is 403, no sizing for C is computed or returned, and an audit row records the attempt
```

## Technical notes / design
- `resolve()` returns `ResolvedFanout(legs=[ResolvedLeg...], totals=..., admission=[AccountAdmission...])`. `ResolvedLeg` carries `status ∈ {ok, warn, skipped, rejected}`, `resolved` (qty, leverage, sl_price, tp_price, notional_usd, risk_usd, sizing_explanation) or `None`, and `error`/`skipped_reason`.
- Decimal discipline: every quantity is rounded **down** to `lotSizeFilter.qtyStep` and every price to `priceFilter.tickSize` from the instrument cache, using the quantization table of `24-internal-schemas.md` §1.5. Rounding direction is never "nearest" for size — an over-size is a risk breach.
- Wallet freshness: `equity` older than 2 s triggers a `poll`-bucket refresh; if the refresh fails the leg is returned `warn` with `stale_equity` and risk-based sizing is disabled for it (US-ORD-014 scenario 3).
- Idempotency: preview requires no idempotency key (no state change) — explicitly noted so the UI does not burn keys on every keystroke.
- Debounce contract for the UI: the endpoint must tolerate 5 calls/second/user; beyond that the gateway limiter returns 429 with `Retry-After` (E05's limiter, not the OMS governor).
- Error codes surfaced: `symbol_not_allowed`, `below_min_notional`, `profile_disabled`, `risk_limit_breached`, `stale_equity`, `no_native_sl_possible`, `rate_budget_would_exceed`.

## Test plan
- **Unit (≥90%):** resolution-order table (profile → defaults → overrides, later wins) across every overridable field; rounding-down behaviour at lot/tick boundaries; skip vs failure vs warn classification; `sizing_explanation` string composition for all four sizing modes (pct equity, fixed notional, fixed qty, risk-based).
- **Contract:** response validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`'s preview schema in CI; the request schema is asserted to be *identical* to `CreateTradeGroupRequest` by a schema-equality test, so the two endpoints can never drift.
- **Side-effect test:** the whole preview path runs against a Bybit stub that fails the build if any order-mutating endpoint is called.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures `fixtures/oms/preview_mixed_profiles.json` (3 ok, 1 skip, 1 warn) and `fixtures/instruments/btcusdt_filters.json`.
- **Perf:** preview p95 ≤300 ms for 5 accounts (SCR-061 budget) measured with warm wallet snapshots and once with a forced refresh.
- **E2E:** covered by E34-Q02.

## Security notes
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 every ticket in this epic is treated as `security`-labelled: it touches `area/oms-execution` order placement and the fan-out safety invariant. Threats from `04-security-program.md` / STRIDE (E34-X01): **Spoofing** — a forged `arm_token` or replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; **Tampering** — client-supplied per-leg sizing overriding server-resolved sizing; **Repudiation** — a fan-out without a per-leg audit row; **Information disclosure** — another user's account labels/balances leaking through the group response or the `trade_groups` WS topic; **Denial of service** — a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; **Elevation of privilege** — a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`. Controls: server-side resolution of every leg parameter, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` enforced before any adapter call, required idempotency key, the reserved `critical` rate bucket, and an `audit_log` row per leg. Data classification: financial/execution data and account scope; API secrets are never handled here (they stay in the M2 vault) — only referenced by account id.

Ticket-specific: preview discloses **per-account equity-derived sizing**, which is a balance oracle. It is therefore `orders:write`-scoped, not `orders:read`, and an out-of-scope account id must be rejected before any sizing is computed (not filtered from the response afterwards).

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the endpoint. It is however the a11y *enabler* for SCR-061: every exclusion carries a text reason and every row a text status, so the UI never has to encode meaning in colour alone.

## Performance notes
Preview ≤300 ms p95 for 5 accounts (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-061). Wallet refreshes draw from the `poll` bucket only and never from `entry`/`critical`. The endpoint is read-only with respect to the rate governor: it may *inspect* availability but never `commit`.

## Observability
`fanout_preview_total{outcome}`, `fanout_preview_duration_ms` histogram, `fanout_preview_skipped_total{reason}`. Log at DEBUG with the resolved leg table (no balances in the message body — reference the account id only).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every acceptance-criteria scenario is verified by an automated test that names the scenario.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on touched backend packages; OMS/risk modules held to ≥90% by R3 local policy (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4).
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` updated if the shipped contract diverged; contract tests green.
- [ ] ADR-0008 amended (or a superseding ADR filed) if a normative rule changed during implementation.
- [ ] perf: budget #4 benchmark recorded (≤50 ms backend-added + ≤10 ms/account; group ack ≤1.5 s p95 for 5 accounts).
- [ ] security: SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (E34 is permanently `security`-labelled per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo) — never live.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`trading.fanout`: on in demo, off in live until R4/E44).
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code owner; ≤400 LOC diff preferred.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E34-T01** (group/leg models and repo), **E28** (profile schema, sizing algorithm, allowed-symbol validation, risk caps) and **E32** (SL/TP derivation and the native-SL precondition). Interfaces relied on: `AccountProfile` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.2), `size_leg()` (§9.3), instrument filter cache (M4).

title: Trade-group persistence, lifecycle derivation and the trade_groups WS topic
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** Ticket becomes a direct `B2` (`trade_group`) lifecycle implementer on `xstate-statemachine`. Legs are invoked `B3` (`leg`) children snapshotted only at the root (C41).

Every other ticket in E34 reads or writes a trade group, so the group's storage, its derived lifecycle and its outbound stream are the interface the epic is built on and must land first (interface-first rule, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10). E28 creates the trade-group *definition* (a named set of accounts); this task creates the *execution record*: the `trade_groups` / `trade_group_legs` rows produced when that definition is actually fired, their state derivation, and the `trade_groups` WS topic the UI subscribes to.

The DDL already exists normatively in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.3.2/§3.3.3 and the domain model in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §9.1; the lifecycle state machine is `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.6; the wire shape is `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` `TradeGroupUpdate`. This task implements them, it does not redesign them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration extending `0006_trading_core`: confirm/emit `trade_groups` and `trade_group_legs` exactly as in `21-database-schema.md` §3.3.2/§3.3.3 including every CHECK constraint and the four indexes on each table — in particular `ix_tgl_no_sl` (open legs without a confirmed native SL), which powers the safety alarm.
- New tables `unwind_plans` and `unwind_steps` mirroring `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5.1 (`UnwindPlan`, `UnwindStep`), so E34-S03 has persistence to resume from: plan status enum `running|completed|incomplete|aborted`, step phase enum `cancel_children|close_position|verify_flat|verify_sl`, a UNIQUE on `order_link_id`, and an index on `status='running'` for `UnwindResumer` startup.
- Repository layer in M14: `TradeGroupRepo` with `create_group_with_legs`, `update_leg_status`, `load_open_groups`, `load_running_unwind_plans` — all writes in one transaction per state transition, all reads scoped by `granted_accounts`.
- `TradeGroupLifecycle` pure function deriving `trade_groups.status` from its legs per `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.4 rule 7 and the §9.6 state diagram: any leg open → `partially_open`; all non-skipped legs open → `open`; all terminal with ≥1 ok → `closed`; zero ok → `failed`; plus `draft`, `submitting`, `closing`, `cancelled`.
- `TradeGroupAggregate` computation (`24-internal-schemas.md` §9.1): requested/filled qty, weighted average entry, total notional, unrealised and realised PnL, fees, funding, legs ok/failed/skipped — recomputed on every position/execution event (US-PROF-007 NFR).
- WS topic `trade_groups` per `23-ws-protocol.md`: snapshot + delta in one sequence domain, filters `exchange_account_ids` and `status`, 100 ms coalescing, permission `orders:read` scoped to granted accounts, payload validated against `cv://ws/v1/trade_groups.schema.json`.
- `GET /api/v1/trade-groups` and `GET /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}` handlers per `22-api-openapi.yaml` (cursor pagination, `symbol`/`status`/`from`/`to` filters, `x-rbac` enforced before the query, 404 for a group outside scope — never 403-with-existence-leak).
- Audit: an `audit_log` row for `trade_group.submit` written in the same transaction as the group row.
- Implement the `B2` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B2.trade_group.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('trade_group', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b02_trade_group.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b02_trade_group.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- Legs run as invoked `B3` (`leg`) child machines of the `B2` root; only the root snapshots (CV-C41), children never snapshot independently.


## Out of scope
- Fan-out execution, sizing, admission control → E34-S01/S02.
- Unwind *behaviour* (this task only creates its persistence) → E34-S03.
- Trade-group definition CRUD (the named account set) → E28.
- Journal aggregation of closed groups → E41.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Lifecycle derivation matches the state diagram
  Given a group with three legs
  When one leg is open, one submitted and one rejected
  Then the derived group status is partially_open
  And when the submitted leg opens the status becomes open, and when all legs close it becomes closed

Scenario: Zero successful legs
  Given a group whose three legs all end rejected
  Then the derived status is failed, never closed
  And the group carries legs_ok=0, legs_failed=3 in its aggregate

Scenario: WS scope enforcement
  Given a Manager granted accounts A and B subscribes to trade_groups
  When a group is created on account C
  Then no frame for that group reaches the Manager's connection
  And an attempt to subscribe with an explicit exchange_account_ids filter naming C is answered with an err frame, not silently widened

Scenario: Safety index is live
  Given an open leg whose native_sl_confirmed is false
  When one second has elapsed
  Then the ix_tgl_no_sl-backed query surfaces it and a system_events row of severity critical exists

Scenario: Unwind plan survives restart
  Given a persisted unwind_plans row with status running and two of four steps done
  When the process restarts and loads running plans
  Then exactly that plan is returned with its two remaining steps in order
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Sequence domain.** The `trade_groups` topic shares the private-stream causal ordering rule of `23-ws-protocol.md` S5: `executions` → `orders` → `positions` → `trade_groups`. The group frame is emitted *after* the events that justify it, so a client never sees an aggregate it cannot explain.
- **Coalescing.** Group updates conflate at 100 ms (topic table). Conflation replaces, never buffers (principle P6).
- **Aggregate correctness.** `filled_qty` in the aggregate is the sum of leg `filled_qty`, but any operation that must be *correct against the exchange* (unwind, divergence detection) re-reads `/v5/position/list` instead — see E34-S03. This task exposes both and names them unambiguously (`local_filled_qty` vs `exchange_position_qty`).
- **Status transitions are append-only in audit.** Every derived transition writes an `order_events`-style row so the journal (E41) can reconstruct the group's history without replaying WS.
- Error codes: `not_found` (404) for out-of-scope ids, `forbidden` (403) only where the resource is in scope but the permission is missing.
- Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B2.1–.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.


## Test plan
- **Unit:** lifecycle derivation truth table over all 8 statuses × leg-state combinations (property test: derivation is a pure function of the leg multiset); aggregate arithmetic incl. mixed-sign realised PnL and fee/funding accumulation; decimal quantization per `24-internal-schemas.md` §1.5.
- **Contract:** `trade_groups` frames validated against `cv://ws/v1/trade_groups.schema.json`; REST responses validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `TradeGroup`/`Page` schemas in CI.
- **Integration:** Postgres-backed repo tests using testcontainers — transactional integrity of `create_group_with_legs` (a failure mid-insert leaves no orphan legs), CASCADE on group delete, UNIQUE `(trade_group_id, exchange_account_id)` violation surfaces as a domain error not a 500.
- **Migration test:** upgrade + downgrade round trip on a seeded database; `ix_tgl_no_sl` proven to be used via `EXPLAIN`.
- **Fixtures:** `fixtures/oms/group_3legs_partial.json`, `fixtures/oms/group_all_rejected.json`.
- Coverage target ≥90% (OMS module local policy).
- pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`
- contract-suite membership (`test_b02_trade_group.py`), covering both spellings and every §B2.7 invariant
- a snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch


## Security notes
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 every ticket in this epic is treated as `security`-labelled: it touches `area/oms-execution` order placement and the fan-out safety invariant. Threats from `04-security-program.md` / STRIDE (E34-X01): **Spoofing** — a forged `arm_token` or replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; **Tampering** — client-supplied per-leg sizing overriding server-resolved sizing; **Repudiation** — a fan-out without a per-leg audit row; **Information disclosure** — another user's account labels/balances leaking through the group response or the `trade_groups` WS topic; **Denial of service** — a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; **Elevation of privilege** — a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`. Controls: server-side resolution of every leg parameter, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` enforced before any adapter call, required idempotency key, the reserved `critical` rate bucket, and an `audit_log` row per leg. Data classification: financial/execution data and account scope; API secrets are never handled here (they stay in the M2 vault) — only referenced by account id.

Additionally for this ticket: the `trade_groups` topic is the main information-disclosure surface in the epic — scope filtering is applied in the *subscription* layer, not by filtering payloads after building them, so an out-of-scope group is never materialized for the wrong connection.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. (The topic's payload carries textual `status` and per-leg `error.message` precisely so the consuming UI can meet its a11y obligation without inferring meaning from colour.)

## Performance notes
Group list query p95 ≤50 ms at 10 000 historical groups (index `ix_tg_user_time`). WS frame build ≤2 ms for 50 open groups × 5 legs, so SCR-062's 4 ms/frame scripting budget is achievable client-side. Coalescing at 100 ms caps outbound frame rate per connection.

## Observability
Metrics `trade_groups_open` (gauge), `trade_group_transitions_total{from,to}`, `trade_group_frame_build_ms` (histogram). Log every derived transition at INFO with `trade_group_id`, `from`, `to`, `legs_ok/failed/skipped`. `system_events` kind `gap_detected` if a group's aggregate cannot be reconciled from its legs.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every acceptance-criteria scenario is verified by an automated test that names the scenario.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on touched backend packages; OMS/risk modules held to ≥90% by R3 local policy (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4).

- [ ] ADR-0008 amended (or a superseding ADR filed) if a normative rule changed during implementation.
- [ ] perf: budget #4 benchmark recorded (≤50 ms backend-added + ≤10 ms/account; group ack ≤1.5 s p95 for 5 accounts).
- [ ] security: SAST/SCA/secrets scan clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (E34 is permanently `security`-labelled per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.

title: Build the round-trip property suite and the 30-rule corpus gate
body:
## Context
R3 exit criterion 5 is a hard gate: "a corpus of >=30 rules authored in the form editor opens in the node editor and returns to the form editor with an identical IR (byte-equal serialisation) and vice versa." US-RULE-001's NFR sets the automated companion: "property-based tests (>=10 000 generated documents per CI run) assert round-trip equality across form→IR→node→IR→form". US-RULE-006's NFR makes the whole equivalence release-blocking: "the round-trip property test plus an E2E switch test for every construct in the metric/action vocabulary must be green before any rule feature ships."

This ticket owns that machinery. It is deliberately a QA-owned deliverable rather than a side effect of E35-T04, because the suite must be adversarial toward the implementation rather than shaped by it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **property-based round-trip suite** (Hypothesis) generating valid IR documents against the JSON Schema bounds and asserting, for each:
  - `hash(ir) == hash(compile_graph(to_graph_model(ir)))`
  - for form-compatible documents, `hash(ir) == hash(compile_form(to_form_model(ir)))`
  - the full hop chain from US-RULE-001's fuzz scenario: IR → node → IR → form → IR, hash unchanged at every hop, with any hop that cannot represent the document **failing loudly rather than emitting a lossy document**
  - the `presentation` block survives untouched across hops
  - >=10 000 documents per CI run, with a deterministic seed recorded per run and a shrinking configuration that produces a minimal reproducer inside 60 s.
- The **>=30-rule corpus**: hand-authored, semantically meaningful rules covering every construct in the vocabulary — all 13 triggers, every comparison operator, all four boolean ops including `n_of`, all four temporal ops, nested arithmetic, shared sub-expressions, every one of the 25 action types at least once, all five scope levels, and the eight built-in system rules. Each corpus entry carries its expected canonical hash as a golden file.
- A **golden-hash regression gate**: any change to canonicalisation, the models or the compilers that alters a corpus hash fails CI and requires an explicit, reviewed golden update with a stated reason — this is what stops a silent semantic drift.
- **Mutation sanity check**: a CI job that injects a known canonicalisation defect and asserts the suite catches it, so a suite that has quietly stopped asserting anything is detected.
- Wiring: the property suite and corpus gate are **required checks** on the merge queue for any PR touching the IR, compiler or canonicalisation packages.

## Out of scope
- The E2E editor-switch test through the real UI — **E35-Q03** (this ticket covers the compiler level).
- The editors themselves — E36/E37, which consume this suite as their regression gate.
- Performance of canonicalisation — **E35-Q04**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Ten thousand generated documents round-trip
  Given the property suite configured for at least 10 000 documents
  When CI runs it
  Then every document's canonical hash is unchanged across the full IR to node to IR to form to IR chain

Scenario: The thirty-rule corpus is hash-stable both directions
  Given the corpus of at least 30 hand-authored rules
  When each is taken form to graph to form and graph to form to graph
  Then the canonical hash matches its golden value in every case

Scenario: A lossy hop fails loudly (failure case)
  Given a document containing a construct the form editor cannot represent
  When the form hop is attempted
  Then it raises a named unrepresentable error rather than emitting a document with the construct dropped

Scenario: A canonicalisation defect is caught (failure case)
  Given the mutation job injecting an unsorted-keys defect
  When the property suite runs
  Then it fails and shrinks to a minimal reproducing document within 60 seconds

Scenario: Golden drift requires a human decision (edge case)
  Given a change that alters a corpus rule's canonical hash
  When CI runs
  Then the corpus gate fails, and merging requires an explicit golden update with a written reason in the PR
```

## Technical notes / design
The generator strategy comes from ADR-0016 (E35-K01) and must produce documents that are *valid*, not merely well-typed — generating semantically absurd but schema-valid rules is fine and desirable, but generating schema-invalid ones only tests the validator, which is a different suite.

Bias the generator deliberately toward the constructs where round-tripping is hard: shared sub-expressions, `n_of`, deeply nested booleans at the 32-child bound, temporal nodes wrapping boolean nodes, and arithmetic nested inside arithmetic. Uniform random generation would spend most of its budget on trivial two-condition rules.

Record the Hypothesis database in CI so a failure found once is replayed on every subsequent run — otherwise a rare failure is found, fixed by accident, and never re-verified.

Corpus authorship note: the 30 rules must be *meaningful*, because they are also the golden action-plan fixtures used elsewhere and the examples in the documentation. Derive them from the built-in system rules, the templates gallery (SCR-083) content, and the worked examples in ADR-0007 (break-even after 1R, ATR trailing, cancel-if-spread-too-wide, daily-loss lockout).

## Test plan
This ticket *is* test code. Its own correctness is established by the mutation sanity check (fourth acceptance scenario) plus review by the second QA/SDET and the backend lead. Suite runtime must fit the CI budget — target under 4 minutes for 10 000 documents, achieved by parallel workers if needed.

## Security notes
The round-trip guarantee is a safety property, not only a usability one: a lossy round trip could silently change what an armed rule does. Making these required merge checks is therefore a security control. The corpus must contain no real account ids, symbols beyond the public perpetuals, or credentials.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — test infrastructure.

## Performance notes
Suite runtime budget under 4 minutes in CI for the 10 000-document run; the corpus gate under 30 seconds. If the budget is exceeded, reduce per-document work rather than document count — the count is an NFR.

## Observability
CI reports the number of documents generated, the seed, and the shrink time on failure, so a flaky failure is diagnosable rather than mysterious. `rule_roundtrip_mismatch_total` is the production counterpart and is alerted on.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed to the repository (plan document, suites, fixtures, scripts) and runnable by any engineer from a documented command.
- [ ] Results recorded on the ticket with pass/fail per scenario and links to CI runs.
- [ ] Any defect found is filed as a Bug with reproduction steps, expected vs actual, severity, and the test layer that should have caught it earlier.
- [ ] New automated suites wired into CI with their runtime budget agreed, and marked required where the roadmap's quality gates demand it.
- [ ] Reviewed by the second QA/SDET and by the rule-engine backend lead.
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted; no P0/P1 defects open against the covered scope.
- [ ] The property suite and corpus gate are configured as **required checks** on the merge queue for PRs touching the IR, compiler or canonicalisation packages.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-Q01** (the plan defines coverage) and **E35-T04** (there must be compilers to round-trip through). Its corpus is consumed by **E35-Q03**, **E36** and **E37**; the suite gates all three.

## Branch

## References

- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md` — one canonical IR, binding rules 1-8
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4 — `rules`, `rule_versions`, `rule_runs`, `rule_events`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` — `/rules`, `/rules/{ruleId}`, `/rules/{ruleId}/versions`, `/rules/{ruleId}/active-version`, `/rules/validate`, `/rules/{ruleId}/compile`, `/rules/{ruleId}/simulate`, `/rules/{ruleId}/mode`, `/rules/{ruleId}/runs`, `/rules/runs/{runId}/events`, `/rules/vocabulary`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6 `RuleUpdate` — topic `rules`, options `rule_ids`/`include_events`, 250 ms cadence
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §20 RULE (US-RULE-001..011)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-080..SCR-089; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-140..159, CMP-233, CMP-234
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §US-RULE rows
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7 R3 (goals 3, exit criteria 5-6, quality gates)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `04-security-program.md`, `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3 exit criterion 5
