title: Rule form editor
body:
## Context
R3 "Trading on demo" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7) ships the rule engine with **both** editors compiling to **one IR** executed by **one runtime** (roadmap §7.1 goal 3, owner decision OD#11). **E35** owns the IR schema, the compiler, the validator, the vocabulary endpoint and the runtime. **E37** owns the node-graph editor. **E36 — this epic — owns the form / condition-list editor and the non-canvas rule surfaces**: the rules list, the structured editor page, the templates gallery, the read-only IR inspector and rule import/export.

The roadmap scopes E36 as: "Condition-list UI with typed operand pickers, grouping (AND/OR/NOT), templates for common patterns (move-SL-to-BE at R:R, trail by ATR, time-based flatten, daily-loss lockout); inline validation against the IR schema; live preview of the compiled IR; keyboard-complete authoring" — 21 pts, Sprints S16–S17 (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2).

Two properties make this epic load-bearing rather than "just a form":
1. **The form editor is the accessible equivalent of the node-graph editor.** `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 declares the always-available "Switch to form view" toggle the *primary accessible-equivalent mechanism* for the canvas, "mandated because free-form 2D graph manipulation cannot be made fully keyboard-equivalent". If the form editor is not 100 % keyboard-operable and screen-reader complete, the node editor cannot ship at all.
2. **The form editor must never lose what the graph editor authored.** `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-081 requires that a graph-only construct renders as an in-place read-only summary card and that "saving the editable parts must not drop or rewrite the read-only part — this is an explicit acceptance test" (US-RULE-006).

Nothing in this epic evaluates a rule or places an order. Every semantic decision (what is valid, what the canonical IR is, what the hash is) is delegated to E35's endpoints so that form and graph report *identical* diagnostics for the same IR (CMP-234 data contract).

## Scope / Deliverables
**Stories covered (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §20 RULE):** US-RULE-002 (metric vocabulary, Must — the picker surface), US-RULE-003 (action vocabulary, Must — the action-row surface), US-RULE-004 (form / condition-list editor, Must), US-RULE-007 (rule scoping, Must — the selector and the scope chip), US-RULE-001 / US-RULE-006 **form-side only** (round-trip indicator, graph-only read-only rendering, IR inspector, import/export; the IR, hash and compile service are E35).

**Screens:** SCR-080 Rules list · SCR-081 Rule editor — form mode · SCR-083 Rule templates gallery · SCR-088 Rule IR inspector (advanced) · SCR-089 Rule import / export.

**Components (`15-component-catalogue.md`):** CMP-140 RuleConditionRow, CMP-141 RuleConditionGroup, CMP-142 RuleActionRow, CMP-143 RuleTriggerPicker, CMP-144 RuleScopeSelector, CMP-145 RuleFormEditor, CMP-155 RuleListRow, CMP-157 MetricPickerCombobox, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-159 RuleConflictWarning, CMP-233 RuleOptions, CMP-234 ValidationPanel, CMP-235 EditorModeToggle (form side).

**API consumed (`22-api-openapi.yaml`):** `GET /rules`, `POST /rules`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /rules/{ruleId}`, `GET /rules/{ruleId}/versions`, `GET /rules/{ruleId}/versions/{versionId}`, `PUT /rules/{ruleId}/active-version`, `POST /rules/validate`, `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile`, `GET /rules/vocabulary`, `PUT /rules/{ruleId}/mode` (link-out only). **WS:** topic `rules` (`rule_ids`, `include_events`, payload `RuleUpdate`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6). **DB (read via API only):** `rules`, `rule_versions` (`21-database-schema.md` §3.4).

**Package:** `packages/rule-editor-core` (framework-free form model ↔ IR adapter, vocabulary cache, diagnostics anchoring) + `apps/web/src/features/rules/*`.

## Out of scope
- The rule IR schema, canonicalisation, hashing, compiler, validator semantics, vocabulary content and the runtime — **E35**.
- The node-graph canvas, node components CMP-146..153, CMP-236..238, auto-layout, node search — **E37**.
- SCR-084 simulation/backtest panel, SCR-085 arming dialog, SCR-086 conflict resolver, SCR-087 fire history — **E35** (they are runtime surfaces; E36 only renders link-outs and the CMP-159 warning banner fed by E35's conflict API).
- Risk caps, lockouts, kill-switch (US-RULE-012..014) — **E39**. Alerts reusing the condition editor — **E40**.
- Android / any mobile client (owner decision 2026-09-14). Non-Bybit venues.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A rule can be authored end to end without a pointer
  Given a keyboard-only user on /rules
  When they create a rule from the templates gallery, change the metric, operator and value of a condition, add an any-of group, add a move_to_breakeven action, set scope and save
  Then the rule is stored as version 1 in mode "disabled" and every step was reachable by keyboard with an audible screen-reader announcement

Scenario: Graph-authored constructs survive a form save
  Given a rule whose stored IR contains a construct the form editor cannot represent
  When it is opened in the form editor, an editable threshold is changed and the rule is saved
  Then the graph-only sub-tree is byte-identical in the new version and the presentation block is untouched

Scenario: Diagnostics are identical in both editors (failure case)
  Given an IR that fails validation with a type mismatch
  When the same IR is validated from the form editor and from the graph editor
  Then POST /rules/validate returns the same diagnostics and both editors anchor them to the corresponding row/node

Scenario: The editor cannot silently disagree with the server
  Given the compile service is unreachable
  Then the round-trip indicator reads "Not verified" in text, draft-save is allowed and arming is blocked
```

## Technical notes / design
- One-way data flow: the editor owns a **form model**; `rule-editor-core` maps form model ⇄ `RuleIr`; the server is the only authority on validity and on the canonical hash. The editor never computes a hash locally.
- Vocabulary (`GET /rules/vocabulary`) is fetched once per session, cached with an ETag, and drives every picker; an unknown metric/action in a loaded IR renders as a disabled row naming the unknown identifier rather than being dropped.
- Validation is debounced (300 ms) on edit; compile + round-trip check runs **on save and on mode switch only** (SCR-081 performance note), never per keystroke.
- Error codes surfaced verbatim from the API problem catalogue, incl. `rule_ir_invalid` (`22-api-openapi.yaml` §error catalogue) and optimistic-concurrency conflicts on `PUT /rules/{ruleId}`.

## Test plan
Unit (≥80 % FE lines) on `rule-editor-core` mapping and on every component; contract tests against `22-api-openapi.yaml` for the six rules endpoints used; Playwright E2E for authoring, templates, import/export and the graph-only read-only case; axe-core in CI plus a manual NVDA/VoiceOver pass; perf assertions for the 500-row virtualised list and the ≤300 ms validation round-trip. Fixtures: a corpus of ≥30 rule IR documents shared with E35's round-trip corpus (roadmap §7.3 exit criterion 5).

## Security notes
Threats (STRIDE, `04-security-program.md`): tampering with an imported rule bundle to smuggle actions or account references; elevation of privilege by authoring a rule scoped to an account the user cannot trade; information disclosure through exported bundles (bundles must never contain account ids, keys or armed state — SCR-089); repudiation if rule edits are not audited. Controls: server-side scope intersection, `rules:write` enforcement, import remapping with per-rule accept/skip, audit events `rule.created|updated|exported|imported`.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`05-accessibility-standard.md`). The form editor is a named a11y-critical surface: every condition row is a labelled group ("Condition 1 of 3"), validation errors are summarised with in-page links, no operation requires drag, and the plain-language rule summary is the accessible description of the rule (US-RULE-004 NFR).

## Performance notes
`06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: validation round-trip ≤300 ms; compile + round-trip diff ≤500 ms p95 for a 100-node rule; the rules list renders 500 rows within a 4 ms scripting budget per frame; template instantiation ≤300 ms.

## Observability
Audit: `rule.created`, `rule.updated`, `rule.saved`, `rule.validated`, `rule.roundtrip_verified {result}`, `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved {choice}`, `rule.exported`, `rule.imported`. Analytics: `rule.template_previewed`, `rule.template_instantiated`, `rule.ir_viewed`, `rule.ir_copied`. Frontend metrics: validation latency histogram, compile latency histogram, editor error-rate.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2: all children Done; coverage floors held; SCR-080/081/083/088/089 designs signed off ≥2 sprints ahead; axe-core green + manual SR pass; STRIDE findings closed; QA epic-level regression recorded; Owner demo accepted; `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md` and `18-traceability-matrix.md` reconciled with shipped behaviour.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`:
- **E35 - rule IR, vocabulary, validate/compile, rules CRUD.** Nothing here can be built against a moving IR; every semantic decision is delegated to it. Consumed by E36-T01, S02, S03, S04, S06.
- **E09 - auth, sessions, RBAC.** Supplies the session and the `rules:read` / `rules:write` / `rules:author` / `trade:<accountId>` grants that gate the `/rules` route (E36-S05) and the save path (E36-S02), and - critically - the server-provided grant list CMP-144 RuleScopeSelector uses to filter the scope account picker so that non-tradeable accounts are absent entirely (E36-S01, US-RULE-007). A client-side role check is explicitly not an acceptable substitute; E36-X02 asserts this.
- **E28 - per-account profiles / account and trade-group registry.** Supplies the account and trade-group universe, display names and demo/live environment badges rendered by CMP-144 (E36-S01), the SCR-080 account filter (E36-S05) and the import scope re-selection step (E36-S06), per US-PROF-005 and US-RULE-007. Without it a rule has nothing to be scoped to.

Consuming-ticket map: E35 -> E36-T01, S02, S03, S04, S06 - E09 -> E36-S01, S02, S05, X02 - E28 -> E36-S01, S05, S06. E37 (node-graph editor) is blocked *by* this epic.

**Estimate reconciliation (DoR).** Roadmap `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 declares 21 pts for E36. That figure covers the engineering tickets only - E36-T01, S01-S06, T02 - which now sum to exactly **21** after the DoR re-pointing of S04 (2 -> 1), S05 (3 -> 2) and S06 (2 -> 1); each carries an *Estimate note* explaining the reduction. The epic `estimate` field is the sum of **all** children, including the design (D01-D06), QA (Q01-Q05) and security (X01-X03) tracks, which the roadmap budgets outside the feature point total.

## Children
```mermaid
graph TD
  D01[E36-D01 UX research] --> D02[E36-D02 Hi-fi SCR-081/083]
  D01 --> D03[E36-D03 Hi-fi SCR-080/088/089 + DS]

  D03 --> D04
  D04 --> D05[E36-D05 Handoff pack]
  D05 --> T01[E36-T01 rule-editor-core]
  T01 --> S01[E36-S01 Condition & action rows]
  S01 --> S02[E36-S02 SCR-081 editor page]
  S02 --> S03[E36-S03 Round-trip indicator + SCR-088]
  S02 --> S04[E36-S04 SCR-083 templates]
  S02 --> S05[E36-S05 SCR-080 rules list]
  S03 --> S06[E36-S06 SCR-089 import/export]
  S05 --> S06
  S06 --> T02[E36-T02 Docs & ADR reconciliation]
  S02 --> D06[E36-D06 Design QA]
  S01 --> Q01[E36-Q01 Test plan]
  Q01 --> Q02[E36-Q02 E2E suite]
  Q01 --> Q03[E36-Q03 A11y audit]
  Q01 --> Q04[E36-Q04 Perf scripts]
  Q02 --> Q05[E36-Q05 Exploratory + sign-off]
  X01[E36-X01 STRIDE] --> X02[E36-X02 Abuse cases & scope assertions]
  X02 --> X03[E36-X03 Security sign-off]
  S06 --> X03
  Q05 --> X03
```

## Risks
R5 Scope (the vocabulary is large and grows with detectors — mitigated by rendering entirely from `GET /rules/vocabulary`), R4 Script sandbox (an authoring surface for automated order placement is an abuse vector — mitigated by X01/X02), R9 Advice boundary (templates must not read as trading advice — mitigated by plain-language behaviour text and the *(estimated)* badging), R14 User retention (an unusable authoring surface pushes users to the canvas, which is the less accessible path).

## Branch
`feat/rule-form-editor-<short>` per ticket; PRs ≤400 LOC.

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §20 · `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §6 · `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` §5, §7A · `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` · `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (rules tag) · `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6 · `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4 · `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11 · `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7 · `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` · `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. title: UX research: how traders tell demo from live and trust simulated fills
body:
## Context
E38 ships the two surfaces where a mistake is unrecoverable: the environment switch (SCR-074) and the permanent demo/live indication (SCR-075), plus three surfaces where a *misread* is nearly as damaging - the simulated-fill results drawer (SCR-099), the parity report (SCR-137) and the paper-balance reset (SCR-079).

`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 21 US-PAPER-002 demands that switching is 'deliberate and unmistakable'; US-PAPER-004 demands that simulated positions are 'visually marked as simulated everywhere'; US-PAPER-005 demands paper results never aggregate into live statistics. Those are research questions before they are visual questions: what do users actually look at before pressing submit, and do they discount simulated results appropriately or over-trust them?

This ticket is the research pass that de-risks D02-D04 and runs two sprints ahead of the consuming stories (design-ahead rule, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` Team & cadence).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated sessions with the Owner and 2 account managers (personas `docs/plan/10-personas.md` owner-trader, account manager), 45 min each, run against the R2 build plus clickable stubs.
- Research questions:
  1. Before submitting an order, which chrome element (if any) is consulted to confirm the environment? Test by asking participants to state the environment at unprompted moments.
  2. Does a single global band (CMP-074 EnvBanner) suffice, or is the per-panel badge (CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal) load-bearing when a panel is floated/maximised?
  3. What confirmation friction is acceptable on the demo-to-live switch (typed phrase + step-up per SCR-074) before users start defeating it?
  4. How do users interpret simulated P&L from the paper matcher - do they treat it as achievable, and what framing (per SCR-099's 'simulated' checklist) corrects over-trust?
  5. What do users expect 'reset paper balance' (US-PAPER-006) to destroy, and do they expect live data to be touched?
  6. Would a parity report (US-PAPER-008) be read proactively or only after a surprise, and what does 'last verified' need to say to be trusted?
- Greyscale/colour-vision pre-test of demo vs live differentiation (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia simulations) - required because `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-075 forbids colour-only encoding.
- Deliverable: research report in `docs/design/research/E38-paper-parity.md` with findings, verbatims, a prioritised implications list mapped to SCR-074/075/079/099/122/137, and any risk raised into `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Out of scope
- Visual design of any screen (that is D02-D04).
- Rule-editor, order-ticket or DOM research (E30/E31/E36/E37 own theirs).
- Quantitative A/B testing - the population is 3-5 users; findings are qualitative by design.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Research executed and reported
  Given 3 participants covering the owner and manager personas
  When all sessions are complete
  Then a report exists at docs/design/research/E38-paper-parity.md answering all six research questions with evidence

Scenario: Environment-recall finding is measured, not asserted
  Given each participant is interrupted at 3 unprompted moments per session
  When asked to state the current trading environment
  Then the recall rate is recorded per chrome treatment and drives an explicit recommendation on whether per-panel badges are mandatory

Scenario: Colour-independence validated
  Given the candidate demo and live treatments
  When each is rendered in greyscale and in the three colour-vision simulations
  Then any treatment that becomes ambiguous is rejected in the report and not carried into D02

Scenario: Over-trust of simulated results surfaced
  Given participants are shown a simulated results drawer with a strong equity curve
  When asked what they would size their next live trade at
  Then any evidence of over-trust is recorded and converted into a concrete framing requirement for SCR-099
```

## Technical notes / design
- Sessions recorded (with consent) and stored on the project's private research drive, not in the repo; the repo holds only the anonymised report.
- Stimuli: R2 build with a Figma-prototype overlay for the switch modal; do not use production credentials - use `CV_ENV=dev` seeds (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` seeds section) so no real key or balance is on screen.
- Colour-vision simulation via a Figma/Stark plugin against the `color.env.demo` / `color.env.live` tokens from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- Report template per question: method, evidence, finding, confidence, implication, owning ticket.

## Test plan
- N/A (research, not code). Validation is peer review of the report by the Chief Design Officer and the Architect.
- Findings that make testable claims (e.g. 'badge must repeat per panel') become acceptance criteria on D02 and QA scenarios in E38-Q01.

## Security notes
- Threat: research recordings could capture API key material or real balances. Control: run against `CV_ENV=dev` seed data only (fake encrypted keys per `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`); no live or funded demo account on screen. Data classification: internal; recordings confidential and not committed.
- No `security` review label required.

## Accessibility notes
- Colour-vision and greyscale validation is an explicit deliverable (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.1 Use of Colour, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- At least one session exercises keyboard-only operation of the switch flow to check the confirmation gate is not pointer-dependent.

## Performance notes
N/A - no runtime component.

## Observability
N/A - no runtime component. Findings that imply telemetry (e.g. 'count environment mis-reads') are filed as follow-up tickets against E38-T02.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact complete in Figma at the stated fidelity, linked on the ticket.
- [ ] Every state from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` drawn (default, loading, empty, error, not-permitted, transitional).
- [ ] The screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is fully ticked.
- [ ] Tokens used are design-system tokens from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; any new token/component raised as a design-system contribution ticket, never a one-off.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) and the Architect; sign-off comment recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] a11y annotations present: focus order, accessible names, live-region behaviour, colour-independent encoding.
- [ ] Handed to engineering >=2 sprints before the consuming FE story's sprint (design-ahead rule, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E30` (order-ticket design exists, so the badge context is real) and `E29` (OMS order flow defined) - participants must react to a realistic trading surface, not a blank page.

## Branch
`design/e38-paper-research` (report only); PR size: docs-only, single report file.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 21 PAPER (US-PAPER-002, 004, 005, 006, 008)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-079, SCR-099, SCR-122, SCR-137
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-074, CMP-075, CMP-139

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**

2. docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml (paper/environment endpoints)
3. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-099
4. docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md §B (paper matcher machine, for E38-S03)
5. docs/plan/04-security-program.md (demo/live isolation controls)
6. docs/plan/20-architecture.md (services/api/paper placement)

**Repo paths to create/modify**

- docs/design/paper-trading/ (specs, handoff pack) — no app code

**Interfaces you must not break**
- `POST /api/v1/session/environment` (env switch), `/api/v1/paper/*` (paper matcher), environment capability matrix in `services/api/exchange/base/`; WS resubscription protocol.

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm lint` && `pnpm typecheck`
- `cd services/api && ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict .`
- `cd services/api && pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`
- `pnpm verify` (full local gate before opening the PR)

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e38-paper-trading-d01`
- PR title: "E38-D01: UX research: how traders tell demo from live and trust simulated fills"
- Body: include `Closes #<issue>` (replace `<issue>` with this ticket's GitHub issue number)
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend (services/api/paper, exchange/base) + @CandleViewer/security (environment isolation is security-owned), @CandleViewer/frontend for web-component tickets
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels (type/design, area/paper-trading, priority/p1, design, ux-research) plus any CI-added labels

**Done means**
- All 4 Gherkin scenarios above pass as automated tests (unit/contract/E2E as appropriate).
- Coverage meets the package's existing threshold (85% API / package-level web target); CI green.
- Diff ≤400 LOC (or split into the PRs named in the ticket's own Branch section); PR template fully completed.
- QA/security/a11y sign-off recorded per this ticket's own Test plan / Security notes / Accessibility notes sections.

**Do NOT**
- Do not let any code path submit a live order while the session is scoped to the demo environment, or vice versa — the isolation boundary is enforced server-side, not just in the UI.
- Do not skip the step-up re-authentication or full WS resubscription on environment switch.
- Do not write application code in this ticket — deliverables are design artifacts (specs/handoff pack) only.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking key (e.g. a dependency listed under `blocked_by` or in '## Dependencies'), move Status → Blocked, and stop. Never silently work around a failing lint/test/contract gate.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:

title: Hi-fi design: environment switcher SCR-074 and demo/live chrome SCR-075
body:
## Context
SCR-075 is described in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` as 'the single most safety-critical visual element in the app'. SCR-074 is the only way to reach live, and per `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `POST /session/environment` it requires an elevated session plus the `trading.live_enabled` flag. These two must be designed together: the switcher is a moment, the chrome is the permanent consequence.

Wireframes already exist in the screens catalogue; this ticket takes them to signed-off hi-fi with every state drawn, so the consuming story E38-S04 start with zero open design questions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi Figma frames for **SCR-074 Environment switcher (Demo to Live)**, all states from the catalogue: idle, switching (progress: closing subscriptions, re-authenticating, resubscribing), switched (10 s full-width confirmation banner), failed (stays on previous environment with reason), not permitted ('The owner hasn't enabled Live for your account.'), blocked (an algo or trade group is running).
- Hi-fi frames for **SCR-075 Demo / Live banner & per-panel badges**: global band in both environments; per-panel badge placement drawn for order ticket, group ticket, DOM ladder, positions grid, algo monitor and chart-trading overlay; floating-window repetition; behaviour under a modal (the band must never be covered).
- Demo copy variant on SCR-075 stating 'Demo uses Bybit's demo matching engine - REST order entry only, no private WS order entry.'
- Design-system contributions: finalise **CMP-074 EnvBanner** and **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal** specs (tokens `color.env.demo`, `color.env.live`, `font.weight.bold`) and the disabled-with-reason presentation used by **CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard**; raise any new token as a design-system ticket rather than a one-off.
- Motion spec: the chrome transition during a switch (duration, easing, reduced-motion fallback) per `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`.
- Redlines and a state-machine diagram of the switch (idle, confirming, switching, switched | failed | not-permitted).

## Out of scope
- The step-up/2FA modal itself (owned by E09 auth).
- Order-ticket internals (E30) - this ticket specifies only where the badge sits in it.
- The parity report and paper-fidelity surfaces (E38-D03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogued state is drawn
  Given the SCR-074 and SCR-075 entries in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the Figma file is reviewed
  Then every listed state exists as a named frame and the screens' design sign-off checklists are fully ticked

Scenario: Colour is never the only signal
  Given the demo and live treatments
  When rendered in greyscale and in three colour-vision simulations
  Then DEMO and LIVE remain unambiguous through text plus icon plus pattern

Scenario: The switch cannot be hit accidentally
  Given the SCR-074 design
  When a reviewer attempts to find a single-click or hotkey path from demo to live
  Then none exists: the flow requires a typed confirmation phrase plus step-up, and the design annotates that no hotkey may be bound

Scenario: Blocked switch is designed, not left to engineering
  Given a running emulated algo or an in-flight trade group
  When the user opens SCR-074
  Then the switch action is disabled with the specific blocking reason listed, and the frame exists

Scenario: The band survives a modal
  Given any modal dialog is open over the app shell
  When the frames are reviewed
  Then the environment band remains visible and is annotated as never scrolled away or covered
```

## Technical notes / design
- Frames follow the app-shell grid from SCR-010 so the band's height is budgeted in the shell layout, not added later.
- Annotate the accessible-name contract: band is `role="status"`, read early in document order; each trading panel's accessible name includes the environment ('Order ticket - LIVE - Main') per SCR-075; CMP-075 is `role="img"` with a static label to avoid re-announcement storms.
- Annotate the 10 s post-switch confirmation banner as `role="alert"` (assertive), announced once.
- Reduced-motion: the chrome transition degrades to an instant swap under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Provide both themes (light/dark) and both density settings for every frame.

## Test plan
- Design review walkthrough with the Architect and the Security engineer (the switch is a security control, not just UI).
- Accessibility annotation review is E38-D05; design QA against the built screens is E38-D07.
- Contrast measured for every env treatment against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` thresholds (>=4.5:1 text, >=3:1 non-text) and recorded in the file.

## Security notes
- This design is the user-facing half of security requirement **SR-040a** (environment capability matrix enforced in code) and **SR-043** (armed state for live). The design must not imply any capability the backend forbids - notably it must state demo's REST-only order entry rather than hiding it.
- Threat (STRIDE spoofing/tampering): a user believing they are in demo while routed to live. Mitigation is this design plus the server-side gate in E38-T02; Security reviews before sign-off.
- Data classification: none rendered (no keys, no PII).

## Accessibility notes
- WCAG 2.2 AA: 1.4.1 (colour not sole means), 1.4.3/1.4.11 (contrast), 2.1.1 (keyboard), 2.4.3 (focus order: the typed-confirm field receives focus on open), 4.1.3 (status messages).
- The typed confirmation field must have a visible label and an announced error state, not colour-only.
- Annotate focus return: on cancel, focus returns to the env badge that opened the modal.

## Performance notes
- Annotate that the band is part of the app shell and must not remount on route change (SCR-075 performance note); badge state comes from one shared store subscription.
- The switch transition blocks order entry for the whole transition (typically <=2 s) - the design shows that blocked state rather than an optimistic UI.

## Observability
- Annotate which interaction emits `session.environment_switched` (high-severity audit event per SCR-074) so engineering wires the audit trigger at the right point (on success, not on intent).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact complete in Figma at the stated fidelity, linked on the ticket.

- [ ] Handed to engineering >=2 sprints before the consuming FE story's sprint (design-ahead rule, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).

## Dependencies

## Branch

title: Trade Bybit demo through the same code paths as live
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-001 (Must) is the foundation of the whole R3 train: every order in R3 executes against Bybit demo. Its NFR is the demanding part - 'identical code paths as live except host and key selection; contract tests run against both environments'. If demo needs its own branch in the OMS, R4's live enablement becomes a re-architecture instead of a gate flip (roadmap section 7.1 goal 5).

E38-T01 gave us the capability record and host routing. This story proves the loop end to end: a demo order behaves, looks and is recorded exactly as a live one would, the demo private WS drives the UI identically, and an operation demo cannot do is refused in plain language rather than failing obscurely.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wire the demo environment through the existing OMS order path (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8 state machine): submit via REST to `api-demo.bybit.com` with `orderLinkId` idempotency, accept the REST response as *acceptance only*, and take order state from the demo **private WS** `order`/`execution`/`position`/`wallet` streams, exactly as live does.
- Demo private WS client lifecycle: connect, authenticate, subscribe, heartbeat, reconnect with resubscribe, and the reconciliation loop against `GET /v5/order/realtime` and `/v5/position/list` on reconnect and on a timer - reusing E29's implementation, not a copy.
- Map `CapabilityUnsupported` (E38-T01) and demo-specific exchange errors to a plain-language refusal carrying the operation, the reason and the parity item id, surfaced through the standard RFC 9457 problem body.
- Ensure every persisted row carries the right environment: `orders.environment`, `positions`, `order_events.source`, and `is_paper=false` for demo (demo is a real matching engine - `is_paper` is orthogonal per `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 1.2).
- Run the existing OMS contract-test suite **twice**, once per environment, with only host and key selection differing; a divergence in the test outcome is a defect.
- Ensure the 7-day demo order retention does not lose history: local `orders`/`executions`/journal mirroring already outlives the exchange's window (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` risk row 8) - add a regression test proving local history survives beyond the exchange's retention.

## Out of scope
- The local paper matcher (E38-S03) - demo is a real exchange engine, not a simulation.
- The environment switch UX (E38-S02, E38-S04).
- Live order entry, which remains gated off until R4/E44.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Demo order behaves as a live order
  Given the session is in Demo with a demo-bound account
  When an order is submitted
  Then it is sent to the api-demo host and appears in positions exactly as a live order would, with the same fields populated

Scenario: Demo private stream drives the UI
  Given a demo account with an open order
  When the order fills at the exchange
  Then order, execution, position and wallet updates arrive over the demo private WS and drive state identically to live, with the WS stream and not the REST ack as the source of truth

Scenario: Demo-only limitation is refused plainly
  Given an operation unsupported in demo
  When it is attempted
  Then it is refused with the limitation stated in plain language and a parity item id, never a generic or obscure failure

Scenario: Identical code paths, proven
  Given the OMS contract-test suite
  When it is executed against demo and against live configuration
  Then the only configuration difference is host and key selection, and both runs produce identical assertions

Scenario: Local history outlives exchange retention
  Given demo orders older than the exchange's retention window
  When the local order history is queried
  Then the records are still present and complete, sourced from the local mirror

Scenario: Reconnect reconciles rather than duplicates
  Given the demo private WS drops mid-order
  When it reconnects
  Then reconciliation against order/realtime restores exact state with no duplicated order and no lost fill
```

## Technical notes / design
- No `if environment == demo` branches in the OMS. The only environment-aware code is the adapter's capability record (E38-T01) and key selection (E27's vault). A lint/architecture test asserts the string `demo` does not appear in `cv/oms/`.
- Idempotency via `orderLinkId` is already the OMS contract; demo reuses it unchanged, which matters because demo's shorter retention makes a duplicate submission after reconnect more likely to look novel.
- Plain-language refusals are composed from the parity item's `description` field, so the refusal text and the parity report cannot diverge.
- `is_paper` stays `false` for demo orders; this is a frequent misunderstanding and is worth a comment plus a test, because setting it true would wrongly exclude demo results from analytics.

## Test plan
- Unit: error-mapping table from capability/exchange errors to plain-language refusals, including an unknown-error fallback that is still actionable.
- Contract: the full OMS contract suite parameterised over both environments (the NFR's explicit demand).
- Integration: recorded demo fixtures covering submit, partial fill, amend, cancel, rejection, and a reconnect mid-order; asserted against the state machine in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.
- Integration: retention regression - synthesise an exchange history response missing old orders, assert the local mirror still serves them.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): place a demo order from the ticket and observe it reach the positions grid.
- Coverage target: >=85% backend; the error-mapping module >=90%.

## Security notes
- Demo keys are secrets and are handled identically to live keys: envelope-encrypted, never returned by any API, never in logs (SR-003, SR-004, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`).
- Threat W9 (assumed WS order entry on demo) is structurally prevented by E38-T01; this story adds the behavioural test proving no demo order is ever dual-dispatched.
- Repudiation: every demo order is audited exactly as a live order would be - demo is not an audit-free zone.
- Data classification: financial transaction data (simulated funds, real structure).

## Accessibility notes
- The plain-language refusal must be renderable as an accessible inline error associated with the control that triggered it; the frontend contract is specified in E38-D06's copy deck. No colour-only error indication.

## Performance notes
- Budget #4: order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo is a **hard R3 exit gate** (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`). Measure and record on this story; if demo's own latency (from the E38-K01 probe) makes the budget unreachable, escalate rather than silently miss it.
- The demo private WS must sustain the same fan-out budget #6 (<=20 ms p95 backend-internal add-on).

## Observability
- Metric `cv_orders_submitted_total{environment}` and `cv_order_ack_latency_seconds{environment}` so demo and live are comparable on one dashboard.
- Log every capability refusal with operation and parity item id (feeds E38-S08's candidate items).
- Alert if the demo private WS is disconnected for more than 30 s while orders are open.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria demonstrated by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% lines on touched backend/engine packages, >=80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour where they diverged.
- [ ] Changelog fragment added per `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §3.
- [ ] 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; PR <=400 LOC diff; merged via merge queue.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (which flag gates this, default per environment).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E38-T01` (routing and capability record), `E29` (OMS, state machine, reconciliation loop), `E27` (demo account and its encrypted keys).

## Branch
`feat/e38-demo-integration`; PR size: ~300 LOC plus fixtures; split fixtures into their own PR if needed.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-PAPER-001

title: Switch session environment safely with step-up and full resubscription
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-002 (Must) requires switching to be 'deliberate and unmistakable'. `POST /session/environment` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` already specifies the contract: switching *to* `live` requires an elevated session (`/auth/step-up`) and the `live_trading` feature flag, else `403 step_up_required` or `403 live_trading_disabled`; the switch is audited and broadcast on the `system` WS topic so every pane re-badges consistently.

SCR-074 adds the operational requirement that makes this non-trivial: on success the client tears down and re-establishes **every** private subscription, order entry is blocked for the whole transition, and 'a half-switched state is never reachable'.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement `POST /session/environment` per the OpenAPI contract: validate the target environment is in the caller's `allowed_environments`; for `live`, require an elevated session within the last 15 minutes and the `live_trading` flag on; otherwise return the specified 403 problem.
- Refuse the switch while the session has **in-flight state that would be orphaned**: a running emulated algo (E33), an in-flight trade group (E34), or a pending order submission - returning a refusal that names the specific blocker (the SCR-074 design sign-off checklist requires this state to exist).
- Orchestrate the transition server-side as an ordered, non-interleavable sequence: block order entry for the session, close private subscriptions for the old environment, re-derive the session's account scope and permissions for the new environment, open private subscriptions for the new environment, unblock. Any failure rolls back to the previous environment intact - never a partial state.
- Broadcast the resulting environment on the `system` WS topic so every open pane and every other tab re-badges; include the transition phases so the UI can show the progress states SCR-074 specifies.
- Audit `session.environment_switched` at high severity with from, to, user, session, and outcome; also audit refusals.
- On switching to live, disarm one-click trading for the session (US-PAPER-002: 'one-click trading is disarmed on switch'), independently of the arm timeout in `POST /settings/arm`.
- Working orders in the previous environment are **not** migrated and remain untouched; the response includes their count so the UI can state it.

## Out of scope
- The switch UI (E38-S04).
- The step-up/2FA mechanism itself (E09).
- The `live_trading` flag's administration (E42) and the R4 live-enablement gate (E44) - this story only reads the flag.
- Per-user eligibility grants (E38-S07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Switching to live requires step-up and the flag
  Given a session that has not been elevated in the last 15 minutes
  When a switch to live is requested
  Then the response is 403 step_up_required, the environment is unchanged, and the refusal is audited

Scenario: Live trading disabled blocks the switch
  Given the live_trading feature flag is off
  And the session is elevated
  When a switch to live is requested
  Then the response is 403 live_trading_disabled and the environment is unchanged

Scenario: Successful switch resubscribes everything
  Given a demo session with open private subscriptions
  When a valid switch to live is performed
  Then private subscriptions for demo are closed before any live subscription opens, the new environment is broadcast on the system topic, and order entry is blocked for the whole transition

Scenario: A half-switched state is never reachable
  Given the resubscription step fails midway
  When the transition aborts
  Then the session is left fully on the previous environment with its subscriptions restored, and the failure reason is returned and audited

Scenario: Switching is blocked by in-flight activity
  Given a running emulated algo or an in-flight trade group
  When a switch is requested
  Then it is refused with the specific blocker named, and no subscription is disturbed

Scenario: One-click trading is disarmed on switch to live
  Given one-click trading is armed in demo
  When the session switches to live
  Then the armed state is cleared and a new explicit arm is required

Scenario: No hotkey path exists
  Given the hotkey configuration surface
  When all bindable actions are enumerated
  Then no binding can invoke the environment switch
```

## Technical notes / design
- The transition is guarded by a per-session lock; concurrent switch requests return `409` rather than interleaving.
- Phases are emitted as `system` topic frames (`closing_subscriptions`, `reauthenticating`, `resubscribing`, `switched`) matching the SCR-074 progress states, so the UI is not guessing.
- Rollback is structured as a compensating step per completed phase, executed in reverse order; a test injects failure at each phase boundary.
- Account scope re-derivation reuses E09's session resolution rather than reimplementing it; the new scope must exclude every account whose `env` differs from the new environment.
- The 'blocked by in-flight activity' check queries the algo and trade-group registries; the blocker list is returned as structured data, not a prose string, so the UI can render each blocker with a link.

## Test plan
- Unit: authorisation matrix over (target env, elevated?, flag state, allowed_environments) with the exact expected problem code for every cell.
- Unit: rollback correctness with failure injected at each phase.
- Unit: blocker detection for running algo, in-flight group and pending submission.
- Contract: response and error shapes against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; `system` frame shape against `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`.
- Integration: full switch against a seeded two-environment account set, asserting subscription teardown/setup ordering from the WS server's connection log.
- Integration: concurrent switch requests yield exactly one switch and one 409.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): switch from demo to live with step-up on staging, asserting every open pane re-badges.
- Coverage target: >=90% (safety-critical path).

## Security notes
- This endpoint is the single gateway to live. Threats: elevation of privilege (switching without step-up), tampering (racing two switches into a mixed state), repudiation (an unaudited switch), denial of service (switch-flapping to disrupt subscriptions).
- Controls: step-up requirement (SR-043-adjacent arming semantics), feature-flag gate, per-session lock, high-severity audit on success **and** refusal, rate-limit on the endpoint.
- The refusal message for a missing grant must not reveal other users' grants (information disclosure).
- `security` label mandatory; abuse-case checks are covered by E38-X02.

## Accessibility notes
- The phase broadcasts exist so the UI can announce progress assertively (SCR-074 a11y note: the environment change is announced assertively and the chrome change is accompanied by a text badge change). The API must therefore emit phases promptly, not only a final result.

## Performance notes
- The whole transition should typically complete in <=2 s (SCR-074 performance note). Measure and record p95; the transition blocks order entry, so a slow switch is a trading outage.
- Subscription teardown/setup must not thrash the WS fan-out budget; batch the resubscribe rather than issuing one frame per topic.

## Observability
- Audit `session.environment_switched` (high severity) plus `session.environment_switch_refused` with reason.
- Metric `cv_environment_switch_duration_seconds` and `cv_environment_switch_failures_total{phase}`.
- A failed rollback is a P0 alert - it implies a possibly half-switched session.

title: Environment capability matrix and demo host routing in the exchange adapter
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` **SR-040a** is unambiguous: 'the environment capability matrix MUST be enforced in code, not documentation'. A single `ExchangeEnvironment` value selects an immutable capability record and every transport call asserts against it. Demo uses `api-demo.bybit.com` for orders only, has **no WS Trade** and **no public WS** (mainnet public streams supply market data), and limits batch orders to `linear`/`option`.

Threats W9 and W10 in the security program describe exactly what happens without this: a silent fallback or dual dispatch leaving orders unplaced or duplicated, and demo/live endpoints mixed within one session. This task makes both unreachable by construction and is the foundation every other E38 ticket stands on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Add an immutable `EnvironmentCapabilities` record in `packages/backend/cv/exchange/capabilities.py`, keyed by `Environment` (`live`|`demo`|`testnet`, matching `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 1.2 and the Postgres `exchange_env` type), carrying: REST base URL, public WS URL (or `None`), private WS URL, `ws_trade_supported: bool`, `batch_order_categories: frozenset[str]`, `order_history_retention_days`, and the parity-item ids that justify each restriction.
- Wire the adapter (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 14 exchange adapter interface) so **one client instance exists per environment**, with no shared base-URL mutation - mixing endpoints in one session must be impossible by construction, not by convention.
- Every transport call asserts its capability before dispatch and raises `CapabilityUnsupported(operation, environment, parity_item_id)` when unsupported; there is no fallback path and no dual dispatch.
- Order entry is REST-only in **both** environments for v1 (WS Trade is an explicit non-goal); the code path is structured so that if WS Trade is ever enabled it is gated on `env == live` by the capability record.
- Public market-data subscriptions for a demo trading session resolve to the **mainnet** public streams, and this resolution is explicit and logged, not incidental.
- A CI assertion that no Bybit host string appears anywhere except `capabilities.py` (extending the SR-119 CSP assertion).
- Contract test `enum_parity_environment` continues to pass: `Environment` is identical across `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and the PG type, and `paper` is a member of none of them.

## Out of scope
- The request-time isolation middleware for API routes (E38-T02).
- The local paper matcher (E38-S03).
- Any UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Demo order entry routes to the demo host
  Given a session whose environment is demo
  When an order is submitted through the adapter
  Then the request goes to api-demo.bybit.com and no mainnet order host is contacted

Scenario: WS trade on demo is unreachable
  Given the demo capability record
  When any code path attempts WS order entry
  Then a CapabilityUnsupported error is raised before any network call, and a unit test asserts no demo code path can reach a WS trade transport

Scenario: Batch order category restriction is enforced
  Given a demo session
  When a batch order is submitted for a category outside linear and option
  Then it is refused locally with the parity item id attached, without contacting the exchange

Scenario: Environments cannot be mixed in one session
  Given a live adapter client and a demo adapter client
  When their configurations are inspected at runtime
  Then they are separate instances with immutable base URLs, and a test asserting that mutating one leaves the other unchanged passes

Scenario: Market data for a demo session uses mainnet public streams
  Given a demo trading session
  When public market-data subscriptions are established
  Then they connect to the mainnet public stream host, and the resolution is recorded in a structured log line

Scenario: A new host cannot be introduced silently
  Given a developer adds a Bybit hostname outside capabilities.py
  When CI runs
  Then the host-location assertion fails the build
```

## Technical notes / design
- `EnvironmentCapabilities` is a frozen pydantic model constructed once at import; there is no setter and no environment variable that can override a URL at runtime (SR-004's spirit: transport identity is not configuration).
- `CapabilityUnsupported` maps to the RFC 9457 problem type used for refusals so the UI can render the plain-language message required by US-PAPER-001's 'Demo-only limitation' scenario; the problem body carries `parity_item_id` so the UI can deep-link into the parity report (E38-S08).
- Capability records reference `parity_items.yaml` ids produced by E38-K01, so the code and the user-facing report cannot drift apart - a capability with no matching parity item fails a unit test.
- Testnet is included in the enum for completeness but is used for smoke tests only per the locked decisions; its record mirrors demo unless K01 found otherwise.

## Test plan
- Unit: one test per capability field per environment; a parametrised test asserting every adapter operation checks a capability before dispatch (introspection over the adapter's method registry, so a newly added un-guarded method fails).
- Unit: `CapabilityUnsupported` carries a real parity item id that resolves in `parity_items.yaml`.
- Contract: `enum_parity_environment` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 19.8) green.
- Integration: against recorded fixtures, a demo-configured adapter performs a full submit/amend/cancel cycle over REST and never opens a trade WS.
- CI gate: the Bybit-host location assertion.
- Coverage target: >=90% on `cv/exchange/capabilities.py` (this is safety-critical code, above the 85% floor).

## Security notes
- Directly implements **SR-040a**; supports **SR-119** (no exchange contact from the renderer; one chokepoint in the backend).
- Mitigates threats **W9** (tampering: assumed WS order entry on demo causing unplaced or duplicated orders) and **W10** (spoofing: mixed demo/live endpoints in one session).
- Data classification: no secrets in this module - it holds hosts and capability booleans only; credentials remain in the vault (E27).
- `security` label required; Security engineer review is mandatory before merge.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. The user-facing message carried by `CapabilityUnsupported` is rendered accessibly by E38-S01.

## Performance notes
- Capability checks are dictionary lookups on frozen objects, resolved once per call; the added cost must be immeasurable against budget #4 (order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo). Assert with a microbenchmark that the guard adds <0.1 ms per call.

## Observability
- Structured log on adapter construction: environment, resolved REST host, resolved public WS host, `ws_trade_supported`.
- Counter `cv_capability_refusals_total{operation,environment}` - a non-zero value on live is an alertable anomaly.
- Every `CapabilityUnsupported` is logged at warning with the operation and parity item id, and feeds the runtime-detected candidate parity items in E38-S08.

- [ ] Coverage: >=85% lines on touched backend/engine packages, >=80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour where they diverged.

title: Server-side environment isolation middleware with 403 and high-severity audit
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-003 is a Must: 'every trading-capable view gated by environment, so that the two can never mix', with the explicit NFR 'enforced in one middleware layer with tests covering every trading route'. Its third scenario is the hard one: **a crafted request targeting a live account from a demo session must be rejected with 403 and audited as a high-severity event**.

US-PAPER-002's NFR adds that 'environment is part of every trading request; a mismatch between client intent and server session is rejected'. The client-side guard CMP-139 is defence in depth only - this task is the real boundary. It is also the environment leg of the RBAC 4-tuple `(permission, account scope, symbol allowance, environment enabled)` from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7.

## Scope / Deliverables
- One FastAPI dependency/middleware in `packages/backend/cv/api/deps/environment.py` applied to **every** mutating trading route: `POST /orders`, `PATCH /orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /orders/{orderId}`, `POST /orders/cancel-all`, `POST /trade-groups`, `POST /trade-groups/{id}/amend`, `POST /trade-groups/{id}/cancel`, `POST /trade-groups/preview`, `POST /positions/{id}/tpsl`, `POST /positions/{id}/close`, `POST /positions/{id}/reverse`, `POST /positions/{id}/leverage`, `POST /positions/close-all`, `POST /rules/{ruleId}/mode` (arming), `POST /alerts/{alertId}/enabled` where the alert has a trading action, and `POST /trading/kill-switch`.
- The check: resolve the target account(s) from the request, read their `env` from `exchange_accounts` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 3.2), compare against the session's active environment and the user's `allowed_environments`; any mismatch is a `403` RFC 9457 problem with a stable error code and **no state change**.
- **Mixed-group prevention**: reject creation of, and submission to, any trade group whose member accounts do not all share one `env` - enforced both at `POST /trade-groups` and at submit, complementing the existing DB constraint `tg_paper_env` and the `trg_ea_env_parent` trigger.
- Audit every rejection as a high-severity event with the attempted environment, the session environment, the target account and the route; emit on the `system` WS topic so the admin security centre sees it live.
- A **route-coverage test** that enumerates the OpenAPI document, selects every route tagged `trading` (or otherwise account-mutating), and asserts each one carries the environment dependency - a newly added trading route without the guard fails CI.

## Out of scope
- The switch endpoint itself (E38-S02).
- Per-user live eligibility grants (E38-S07) - this middleware consumes `allowed_environments`, it does not manage it.
- Frontend guarding (CMP-139, E38-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crafted cross-environment request is refused and audited
  Given a session whose active environment is demo
  When a request is crafted targeting a live exchange account
  Then the response is 403, no order is created, and an audit row of high severity is written naming both environments and the target account

Scenario: Every trading route is covered
  Given the generated OpenAPI document
  When the route-coverage test runs
  Then every account-mutating route has the environment dependency attached, and adding a new trading route without it fails CI

Scenario: Mixed-environment trade group is impossible
  Given a set of accounts containing one demo and one live account
  When a trade group is created from them
  Then creation is refused with 422, and a separate test asserts submission to an already-existing mixed group is also refused

Scenario: Environment mismatch between client intent and session
  Given a request that explicitly declares environment live
  And a session whose active environment is demo
  When the request is processed
  Then it is rejected before reaching the OMS, with the mismatch named in the problem detail

Scenario: A user without the environment grant cannot use it
  Given a manager whose allowed_environments contains only demo
  When any live-targeting request is made, even with a valid live account id
  Then it is refused with 403 and audited, regardless of the session's claimed environment

Scenario: Rejections do not leak other users' grants
  Given a refusal caused by a missing live grant
  When the problem detail is inspected
  Then it states only that the caller lacks live access, never who does have it
```

## Technical notes / design
- The dependency runs **after** authentication and permission resolution but **before** any handler body, so no partial work is possible; it is implemented as a FastAPI dependency returning a resolved `EnvironmentContext` that handlers must accept, making omission a type error rather than a silent gap.
- Account resolution differs per route (body field, path param, trade-group membership); implement per-route extractors registered in one table, so the extractor list is reviewable in one place.
- Error codes reuse the existing registry (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` error registry) - add `environment_mismatch` and `environment_not_permitted` there rather than inventing ad hoc strings; the registry is single-source and has its own contract test.
- Audit rows go through the existing append-only hash-chained audit writer (E42/`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`), with event name `trading.environment_mismatch_rejected` at high severity.
- The WS broadcast piggybacks on the `system` topic already used for environment switch notifications.

## Test plan
- Unit: matrix over (session env, target account env, allowed_environments) covering all combinations incl. the testnet value; assert 403 + no side effect + audit row for every disallowed cell.
- Unit: mixed-group rejection at create and at submit.
- Contract: OpenAPI route-coverage test described above; error-registry test for the two new codes.
- Integration: against a seeded DB with one demo and one live account, drive each listed route with a crafted cross-environment payload and assert 403 with zero rows written to `orders`/`positions`.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): the crafted-request scenario end to end, asserting the admin security centre shows the event.
- Chaos-adjacent: assert the guard still refuses when the audit writer is unavailable - it must fail closed (refuse) rather than fail open.
- Coverage target: >=90% on the middleware module.

## Security notes
- Implements the environment leg of the RBAC 4-tuple (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 15.2) and US-PAPER-003's server-enforcement scenario.
- Threats: elevation of privilege (demo user reaching live), tampering (crafted account id), repudiation (an attempt with no audit trail). Controls: single choke point, fail-closed audit, high-severity event, route-coverage CI gate.
- Data classification: request metadata and account ids; no secrets. Problem details must not disclose other users' grants (information disclosure).
- `security` label mandatory; per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 this ticket cannot reach Done without a Security engineer review comment and a manual privilege-escalation abuse check.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no UI. The 403 problem details are rendered by the frontend with the accessible disabled-with-reason pattern (E38-S04).

## Performance notes
- The guard adds one already-cached account lookup per request; assert p95 added latency <5 ms so budget #13 (write endpoints <300 ms p95 backend-internal) is unaffected. Account `env` is read from the request-scoped account cache, never a fresh query per leg of a fan-out.

## Observability
- Counter `cv_environment_rejections_total{route,session_env,target_env}`; any increment is alert-worthy on a healthy system.
- Audit event `trading.environment_mismatch_rejected` (high severity), visible in SCR-137.
- Trace span attribute `cv.environment` on every trading request, so a mis-routed request is diagnosable after the fact.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Coverage: >=85% lines on touched backend/engine packages, >=80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.

title: Design QA of the built risk, lockout and kill-switch surfaces
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec (spacing, tokens, type, colour, states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer. E39 ships four net-new screens, three of which are danger surfaces, so this comparison is done as one dedicated ticket rather than ad hoc per story.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Side-by-side review of the implemented **SCR-071**, **SCR-073** (from E39-S04) and **SCR-072**, **SCR-134**, **CMP-211** (from E39-S05) against the E39-D02/E39-D03 hi-fi frames.
- Verification of every enumerated state in the running app using the QA fixtures: normal · warning ≥80 % · locked · frozen · stale · reconciling · manager-scoped · viewer read-only · freeze executing · freeze partial failure · unfreeze · lockout active · lockout expired · SCR-134 conflicting-caps warning.
- Token audit: every colour, spacing and type value resolves to a design token; zero hard-coded values in the touched components.
- Reduced-motion verification: with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every E39 animation degrades to its specified non-animated state.
- Discrepancy log: each finding either fixed in-sprint or filed as a Bug with a `priority/*` label and linked here (per DoD rules).

## Out of scope
- Functional/black-box testing (E39-Q01, E39-Q02) and the full a11y audit (E39-Q04) — this is a visual/spec-conformance pass.
- Redesign work; genuine design changes are filed as new design tickets, not smuggled in as QA fixes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state reviewed
  Given the fixture harness can drive all enumerated states
  When the review is complete
  Then each state has a pass / fail / fixed verdict recorded

Scenario: Token conformance
  Given the computed styles of the E39 components are inspected
  Then no colour, spacing or type value is a literal outside the token set

Scenario (failure): Unfixed discrepancy
  Given a discrepancy cannot be fixed in-sprint
  Then a Bug ticket exists with a priority label, linked here, and design sign-off records it explicitly as accepted debt
```

## Technical notes / design
Use Storybook plus the demo environment with seeded risk fixtures (`fixtures/risk/*.json`, see E39-Q01) to reach breach and partial-failure states deterministically instead of waiting for them to occur naturally.

## Test plan
Manual spec-conformance pass + automated token lint (`pnpm lint:tokens` over `apps/web/src/features/risk`) + visual-regression snapshots added to the Storybook suite for the E39 components.

## Security notes
The reviewer must confirm no frame leaks data beyond the viewer's scope — a manager-scoped SCR-071 rendering another account's equity is a security finding, not a visual one, and is escalated to E39-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Spot-check focus order, visible focus states and non-colour status encoding; deep a11y auditing is E39-Q04, but anything found here is filed immediately.

## Performance notes
Confirm the dashboard does not repaint faster than the ≤1 Hz design target and that the panic cluster never re-renders on unrelated market ticks.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All states reviewed with recorded verdicts.
- [ ] Token lint and visual-regression snapshots green.
- [ ] Reduced-motion pass complete.
- [ ] Discrepancies fixed or filed as prioritised Bugs.
- [ ] Designer sign-off comment posted on E39-S04 and E39-S05.

## Dependencies

title: E2E suite proving no order path escapes the kill-switch or a lockout
body:
## Context
R3 exit criterion 7 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3) states the bar exactly: "Kill-switch works end-to-end: activated, no new order can be placed **by any path including the rule engine**; existing positions untouched; released cleanly; every transition audited." Exit criterion 2 establishes the pattern this suite copies from the native-SL invariant: "an automated test suite attempts, by every available path (ticket, chart drag, DOM click, rule action, fan-out, emulated algo), to open a position… all attempts are rejected, logged, and audited. **Zero escapes.**"

This ticket builds the kill-switch/lockout equivalent as a Playwright suite over web + Electron, and it is the acceptance evidence for E39-S03, E39-S04 and E39-S05.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright suite `e2e/risk/` running against **web and the Electron shell** (both are required by the R3 E2E gate), using the E39-Q01 fixture harness for deterministic state.
- **Zero-escape matrix**: with the kill-switch engaged, attempt to place an order from every available path and assert refusal, an audit row, and a user-visible reason for each: (1) order ticket SCR-060, (2) chart order-line drag SCR-030, (3) DOM ladder click, (4) rule-engine action, (5) trade-group fan-out leg, (6) emulated-algo child, (7) direct API call with a valid session (bypassing the UI entirely — the path a hostile client would use). Paths whose owning epic has not yet shipped (e.g. emulated algos, E33) are present as `test.fixme` placeholders with the owning epic named, so the matrix is visibly incomplete rather than silently missing rows.
- **Positions-untouched assertion**: after a default-options engagement, position count and sizes are byte-identical to before.
- **Lockout equivalent**: the same matrix with a daily-loss lockout instead of the kill-switch, additionally asserting that reduce-only closes **succeed** throughout.
- **Release flow**: owner unfreeze with step-up → order placement works again → rules remain disarmed until explicitly re-armed.
- **UI propagation**: SCR-073 appears in the order ticket, the positions grid and the risk dashboard within 500 ms of the breach frame; the kill-switch frame disables order-entry affordances without a REST round-trip (this is WS conformance case **C12** in `23-ws-protocol.md` §16 — "Disable order-entry affordances on `kill_switch.engaged`").
- **Audit completeness**: after each scenario, query the audit log and assert one row per affected entity with the expected action name and severity.
- Registration of the suite as part of the R3 **required checks** (safety gate).

## Out of scope
- Load and chaos testing (E39-Q03).
- a11y auditing (E39-Q04) — though the suite uses accessible selectors, which surfaces gross a11y breakage early.
- Unit/contract tests owned by the implementing stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Zero escapes with the kill-switch engaged
  Given the kill-switch is engaged globally
  When an order is attempted from every path in the matrix
  Then every attempt is refused with trading_disabled
  And every attempt produces an audit row
  And the user sees an explanatory reason on each surface

Scenario: Positions are untouched
  Given three open positions and default freeze options
  When the kill-switch is engaged
  Then the position count and sizes are unchanged afterwards

Scenario: Reduce-only survives a lockout
  Given an account in a daily-loss lockout
  When a reduce-only close is submitted from the positions grid
  Then it succeeds
  And an opening order from the same grid is refused

Scenario: WS-driven affordance disable (C12)
  Given the order ticket is open
  When a kill_switch frame arrives on the system topic
  Then the submit control becomes unavailable with an explanation
  And no REST round-trip was required to reach that state

Scenario (failure): A newly added order path is not gated
  Given a developer adds a seventh order path without gating it
  When the suite runs
  Then the matrix's path-registry assertion fails, naming the ungated path
```

## Technical notes / design
The path registry is shared with the backend's origin registry test (E39-S01) via a checked-in list `contracts/order-origins.json`, so backend and E2E cannot drift: adding an origin in one place without the other fails CI. Playwright projects: `web-chromium` and `electron`. Each scenario tears down by releasing the switch and clearing lockouts through the harness, so scenarios are order-independent and parallelisable.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan; its own meta-checks are: the suite fails when enforcement is deliberately disabled via a mutation test (a CI job that runs the suite against a build with `risk.enforcement` stubbed out and asserts the suite goes red — proving the suite has teeth rather than passing vacuously).

## Security notes
This suite is the practical proof of the product's core safety control, so its integrity matters as much as the feature's. The mutation check above prevents a vacuously-passing suite. The suite must not embed real credentials; it authenticates through the standard demo test-user flow. Findings from this suite that reveal a bypass are **security** incidents and route to E39-X02, not just to a Bug.

## Accessibility notes
Selectors use accessible roles and names (`getByRole('alertdialog')`, `getByRole('button', {name: /Flatten all positions/})`), which doubles as a smoke test that the a11y contracts from E39-D03 actually shipped.

## Performance notes
Suite wall-clock ≤15 minutes across both projects so it is viable as a required check. It asserts the 500 ms breach→notice and 2 s freeze-effectiveness budgets as test assertions, not just as monitored metrics.

## Observability
Each run publishes the zero-escape matrix as a table artefact (path × outcome) attached to the CI run, so a reviewer can see coverage at a glance rather than reading logs.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Suite green on web and Electron.
- [ ] Zero-escape matrix complete, with `fixme` placeholders naming owning epics for not-yet-shipped paths.
- [ ] Mutation check proves the suite fails when enforcement is stubbed.
- [ ] Registered as a required check.
- [ ] Audit-completeness assertions in place.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E39-S03, E39-S04 and E39-S05.
- [ ] Results reviewed by the Security engineer (feeds E39-X02).

## Dependencies
- `E39-S04`, `E39-S05` — the UI surfaces under test.
- `E39-S03` — the kill-switch engine.
- `E39-Q01` — the fixture harness.
- `E29`, `E31`, `E33`, `E34`, `E35` own the individual order paths; missing ones are placeholders.

title: Performance and chaos scenarios for risk evaluation and kill-switch propagation
body:
## Context
Two E39 numbers are hard gates rather than aspirations. Cap evaluation must add **≤5 ms p95** to the order path (US-PROF-004 and US-ADMIN-003 NFRs) inside budget #4 — "Order submit → ack p95 < 300 ms (demo), **hard for demo (R3 exit gate)**" (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2). The kill-switch must be **effective within 2 s** (US-RULE-014 NFR) with a **200 ms** server-side halt (SCR-072). And the R3 chaos gate requires "WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out — all resume to a correct, reconciled state" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4); E39's share is proving that risk state and kill-switch state survive those events **fail-closed**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **k6 load script** `perf/k6/e39-risk.js`: sustained order submission across 5 demo accounts at the per-UID limit for 1 hour (matching the R3 Load gate), measuring the risk-gate contribution via the `risk.evaluate` span and asserting p95 ≤5 ms and no drift over the hour (the counters are in-memory and must not degrade as the day's event history grows).
- **Kill-switch propagation benchmark**: under that load, engage the switch and measure (a) time to first server-side refusal, (b) time to the WS frame at a connected client, (c) time until every connected session's order affordances are disabled. Assert 200 ms / 2 s.
- **Chaos scenarios** (using the existing chaos harness from `03-testing-strategy.md`):
  1. **Backend restart while a lockout is active** — the lockout is still in force afterwards; accounts are not silently unlocked; the daily counter is rebuilt from `executions`, not reset to zero.
  2. **Backend restart while the kill-switch is engaged** — it comes back engaged; if the state read fails during startup, trading is refused (fail-closed), not permitted.
  3. **Postgres failover during kill-switch engagement** — the switch either completes or reports per-account failures; it never reports success for an account whose state was not written.
  4. **WS disconnect between breach and push** — the client, on reconnect, learns of the lockout from the snapshot rather than only from the missed delta (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11 restore order).
  5. **Exchange 5xx / rate-limit 10018 during lockout-driven cancellation** — cancellation retries with back-off, the lockout remains in force, and the failure is visible rather than swallowed.
  6. **Clock skew** — an evaluator clock skewed past the day boundary must not release a lockout early; the boundary is computed from a monotonic server time source with skew detection.
- Recorded results appended to the performance report and to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` if a new risk surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Functional E2E (E39-Q02) and a11y (E39-Q04).
- Engine FPS / rendering budgets (chart-engine epics).
- Bybit-side rate-limit governor tuning (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Risk gate stays inside its budget under sustained load
  Given 5 accounts submitting at the per-UID limit for 1 hour
  Then the risk.evaluate span p95 is ≤5 ms throughout
  And the p95 in the final 10 minutes is within 20% of the first 10 minutes

Scenario: Kill-switch propagation budget
  Given the system under that load
  When the kill-switch is engaged
  Then the first server-side refusal occurs within 200 ms
  And every connected session has order affordances disabled within 2 s

Scenario (chaos): Restart does not unlock
  Given an active daily-loss lockout
  When the backend is restarted
  Then the lockout is still in force and the daily counter matches its pre-restart value within tolerance

Scenario (chaos): Failover never reports a false success
  Given a Postgres failover during engagement
  Then any account whose state write did not commit is reported in failures
  And no account is reported as frozen unless its state is durably written

Scenario (chaos): Clock skew does not release early
  Given the evaluator's wall clock jumps past the day boundary
  Then the lockout is not released and a clock-drift warning is raised on the system topic
```

## Technical notes / design
k6 runs against the demo environment from the same network position as the app (over Tailscale) so the measurement matches the budget's stated conditions (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §"Network conditions"), and the Bybit-RTT component is excluded from the backend-internal figure as that document specifies. The chaos harness uses container-level kill/restart and a Postgres failover fixture; each scenario asserts on both the API behaviour and the audit trail.

Clock skew is injected by faking the process clock while leaving the monotonic source intact, which is precisely the condition the `clock_drift` `SystemUpdate` kind exists to report (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9).

## Test plan
The deliverable is the test. Meta-assertions: each chaos scenario has a "control" run without the fault, proving the assertion can pass, so a scenario cannot pass because the fault never injected.

## Security notes
Chaos scenarios double as **availability abuse cases**: scenario 2 verifies that a crash cannot be used to clear the kill-switch, and scenario 3 that a failover cannot be used to produce a false "frozen" report that an operator would trust. Both are fail-closed properties, and their results are inputs to the E39-X02 review. Load tests run against demo only, never live, and use demo keys from the vault.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI under test here (affordance-disable timing is measured via the DOM but is a performance assertion, not an a11y one).

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: ≤5 ms p95 risk-gate contribution; ≤300 ms p95 order submit→ack on demo (budget #4, hard gate); ≤200 ms server-side halt; ≤2 s end-to-end kill-switch effectiveness; ≤500 ms breach→lockout notice. Any regression beyond the agreed threshold blocks the release per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2.

## Observability
Results are exported to the same Prometheus series used in production (`cv_risk_eval_duration_seconds`, `cv_kill_switch_engage_latency_seconds`, `cv_risk_breach_to_notice_seconds`) so the load-test numbers and the production numbers are directly comparable rather than living in separate reports.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] k6 script merged and run; results recorded against each budget.
- [ ] All six chaos scenarios implemented, each with a control run.
- [ ] Performance report updated; regressions filed as Bugs.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.
- [ ] Results reviewed by the Architect and the Security engineer.
- [ ] Demo: before/after evidence presented at Sprint Review.
