title: Build the risk dashboard SCR-071 and the lockout notice SCR-073
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-004 — Owner risk dashboard (Must)**: "As the owner, I want an aggregate risk view across all accounts, so that I can supervise at a glance," and the user-facing half of **US-RULE-012** (the lockout banner with its expiry) and **US-PROF-004** (cap utilisation made visible before it is breached). The backend for both landed in E39-S01 and E39-S02; this story builds the surfaces: **SCR-071 Risk dashboard** at route `/risk`, and **SCR-073 Lockout notice**, the blocking banner a manager sees when trading is halted.

Design is signed off in E39-D02 (Sprint 14), satisfying the design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`: "no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off").

The story is deliberately 8 points and covers two screens because they share one data source (`RiskSummary` plus the account-status WS payload) and two components (CMP-117, CMP-138); splitting them would duplicate the data layer.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/risk` (`12-sitemap.md`), RBAC-gated: `owner` full; `manager` sees only their granted scope; `viewer` read-only when granted — scoping is displayed, but **enforced server-side** (E39-S01); the client never filters for security.
- **SCR-071** implementation per the catalogue: portfolio header (equity, uPnL, day P&L, drawdown), exposure by symbol with % of equity, and the per-account table (`account`, `equity`, `day P&L`, `cap`, `used`, `positions`, `state`) driven by `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` plus live updates from the `system` topic and the account-status `risk_cap_usage` field.
- Control row: **FREEZE per account**, **FREEZE ALL**, and **Override lockout** — each opening the shared confirmation surfaces owned by E39-S05 (this story renders the entry points and wires the callbacks; the modal itself is S05's deliverable, consumed here as a component).
- The **critical banner** when `RiskSummary.totals.positions_without_native_stop > 0` — the OpenAPI schema states this "MUST be zero in steady state; any non-zero value is a violation of the native-stop safety invariant and is surfaced as a critical banner."
- All SCR-071 states: normal · warning (≥80 % of a cap) · locked (showing what was auto-flattened and when) · frozen · stale data (per-account freshness timestamp; every figure carries one per the US-ADMIN-004 NFR) · reconciling after reconnect · manager-scoped · viewer read-only · empty (no accounts).
- **SCR-073** implementation: the non-dismissible blocking banner + panel state — "Trading locked: daily loss limit −2 % reached at 13:41 UTC. 1 position was flattened. Locked until 00:00 UTC. Contact the owner for an override." — rendered consistently in the order ticket, the positions grid and the risk dashboard (the catalogue requires it to appear in all three); the manager override-request action; the countdown to reset (CMP-035); post-expiry clearing.
- Components built/consumed: **CMP-117 RiskLockoutBanner** and **CMP-138 RiskCapMeter** implemented to their catalogue contracts with Storybook stories for every variant; plus CMP-049 Table, CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-028 Callout, CMP-035 Countdown.
- Client state: a `useRiskSummary` hook merging the REST snapshot with `system` deltas, with reconnect-safe resubscription (`23-ws-protocol.md` §11 restore order) and an explicit stale marker rather than a frozen-but-plausible number.

## Out of scope
- SCR-072 kill-switch modal, CMP-211 panic cluster, the global hotkey and SCR-134 (E39-S05).
- The positions/orders grid itself (E29) — this story only ensures SCR-073 renders inside it via a shared banner slot.
- Journal equity-curve analytics (E41); CMP-167 is consumed with the data `RiskSummary` already provides.
- Notification delivery (E40).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Aggregate view
  Given the owner opens /risk with three accounts
  Then equity, exposure, uPnL, daily PnL, drawdown, margin usage and liquidation proximity are shown per account and in aggregate
  And every figure displays a freshness timestamp

Scenario: Threshold breach escalates with text, not colour alone
  Given account sub_001 crosses 80% of its daily-loss cap
  Then its row shows WARN as text plus a glyph and its RiskCapMeter shows the numeric current and cap values
  And the row remains distinguishable when rendered in greyscale

Scenario: Lockout notice appears within 500 ms and cannot be dismissed
  Given a manager is trading and their account breaches its daily-loss cap
  When the system WS frame arrives
  Then SCR-073 appears within 500 ms with role="alert"
  And it names the reason, the breached limit, the actual value and the reset time
  And no dismiss affordance exists while the lockout holds
  And it is visible in the order ticket, the positions grid and the risk dashboard

Scenario: Manager sees only their scope
  Given manager M is granted accounts A and B
  When M opens /risk
  Then only A and B appear and no control can reveal account C

Scenario (failure): One account's feed is down
  Given account sub_002's data is stale beyond the freshness threshold
  Then its row renders an explicit "stale" state with its last-known timestamp
  And its figures are not presented as current

Scenario (edge): Native-stop invariant violated
  Given RiskSummary.totals.positions_without_native_stop is 2
  Then a critical banner is shown naming the count and linking to the affected positions

Scenario (edge): Reconnect
  Given the WS disconnects and reconnects
  Then the dashboard re-fetches the snapshot, resubscribes, and clears the reconciling state without a full page reload
```

## Technical notes / design
Code lives in `apps/web/src/features/risk/`. Data flow: `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` for the snapshot → `system` topic deltas (auto-subscribed, cannot be unsubscribed) → per-account status updates. Updates are throttled to **1 Hz** at the view layer (SCR-071 performance note) even though events may arrive faster; the throttle is in the hook, not in each component, so counts and meters never disagree within a frame.

SCR-073 is rendered from a single `LockoutBannerSlot` provider so all three host surfaces show identical copy; the state is **server-derived** (`RiskSummary.accounts[].lockout`) and persists across reloads — the catalogue explicitly forbids a client-derived lockout.

FREEZE / FREEZE ALL / Override entry points are disabled-with-reason for roles lacking `killswitch:write`; disabled state includes an accessible explanation, not a bare disabled attribute.

## Test plan
- **Unit (Vitest)**: the `useRiskSummary` merge/throttle logic; stale detection; cap-utilisation formatting; countdown arithmetic across the day boundary; role-based control enablement.
- **Component (Storybook + interaction tests)**: every CMP-117 and CMP-138 variant; SCR-071 in all nine states; SCR-073 in all four states.
- **Contract**: MSW handlers generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` so the UI cannot drift from `RiskSummary`.
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron)**: breach → lockout appears in all three surfaces → override by owner → banner clears; manager scoping; reconnect behaviour. (Shared suite maintained in E39-Q02.)
- **a11y**: axe-core CI on `/risk` and on each SCR-073 host; a manual screen-reader pass verifying the `role="alert"` announcement and that the non-dismissible banner does not trap focus.
- **Visual regression**: snapshots for the warning/locked/stale states.
- Coverage: ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
The dashboard displays cross-account financial data, so the primary threat is **information disclosure through client-side-only scoping**. Mitigation: the client renders whatever the server returns and never requests a broader scope to filter locally; an E2E test asserts a manager's network responses contain no out-of-scope account. No secrets, key fingerprints or IP allowlists are rendered here (those live on E42's security posture panel). The override control must not be rendered as enabled for non-owners — but the server is the enforcement point, and a test asserts a forced client-side enable still yields 403.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Required behaviours: every state text-labelled (`ok`/`WARN`/`LOCK`), never colour alone; CMP-138 meters expose numeric values and extend the CMP-023 ProgressBar contract; SCR-073 is `role="alert"` on appearance, then persists as a banner and is not dismissible while the lockout holds, without stealing or trapping focus; the account table is a real table with `aria-sort` on sortable headers; FREEZE has an explicit confirm dialog naming the affected accounts; reduced-motion honoured for the escalation transition. axe-core must be green and a manual screen-reader pass recorded.

## Performance notes
Aggregates are computed server-side; the UI updates at ≤1 Hz and must never block the trading surfaces (SCR-071 performance note). Lockout notice visible ≤500 ms after the breach frame (SCR-073). The dashboard must not re-render chart or DOM panels; verified by a render-count test.

## Observability
Client analytics/audit hooks: `audit.viewed` for the dashboard; `risk.lockout_acknowledged` `{actor}` when the manager acknowledges the notice; client-side error boundary reporting for a failed summary fetch. A frontend metric records observed breach→notice latency and reports it so the 500 ms budget is monitored from the client's perspective, not only the server's.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests referencing the scenario name.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80 % frontend; CI gate green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for every CMP-117/CMP-138 variant; `15-component-catalogue.md` matches the implementation.
- [ ] axe-core green on all touched surfaces; manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] design-qa performed (E39-D04) with discrepancies fixed or filed.
- [ ] Perf: 1 Hz throttle and no-cross-panel-rerender verified.
- [ ] QA black-box sign-off per E39-Q01.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded: `ui.risk_dashboard` default on in demo, on in dev, on in staging.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E39-D02` — signed-off hi-fi (Done ≥2 sprints prior).
- `E39-S01` — `/risk/summary`, `/me/limits`, scoping.
- `E39-S02` — lockout state and the `system` notice frame.
- `E39-S05` — supplies the confirmation modal component this story links to; the two stories are developed in the same sprint behind a shared component contract agreed at sprint start.

title: Build the kill-switch modal SCR-072, panic cluster, global hotkey and risk policy SCR-134
body:
## Context
The operator-facing half of the kill-switch (**US-RULE-014**) and of risk administration (**US-ADMIN-003 — Risk-limit administration, Must**). The backend landed in E39-S03 and E39-S01; this story ships the controls: **SCR-072 Kill-switch / freeze confirmation modal**, the **CMP-211 PanicButtons** cluster that lives permanently in the app shell (SCR-010), the **global hotkey** the roadmap requires ("flippable from the admin screen and from a global hotkey", `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2), and **SCR-134 Admin: risk policy (global)** at `/admin/risk-policy`.

This is the most consequence-dense UI in the product. The catalogue's requirements for SCR-072 are non-negotiable: name exactly which accounts and users are affected; restate the consequence in text; require typing `FREEZE`; offer "also cancel working orders" and "also flatten positions" as explicit checkboxes **both defaulting off**; `role="alertdialog"` with **focus starting on the cancel control**.

Design is signed off in E39-D03 (Sprint 14) per the design-ahead rule.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-072** modal: scope selector (this account / all accounts / this symbol); a live consequence restatement computed from `RiskSummary` ("This cancels 14 working orders and blocks new orders on 5 accounts. Open positions are NOT closed."); the two opt-in checkboxes mapping to `cancel_open_orders` and `flatten_positions`; the mandatory `reason` field (3..280); typed `FREEZE` confirmation via CMP-044 `variant="typed"`; execution state with per-account progress; the completed summary rendered from `KillSwitchResult.actions`; partial failure with per-account retry that does not re-execute succeeded accounts; the **unfreeze** path with its own confirmation and step-up; DEMO vs LIVE variants.
- **CMP-211 PanicButtons**: Flatten-all / Cancel-all / Kill-switch cluster with `scope: account|group|global`, `confirmMode: hold|typed|single`, RBAC-driven `enabled` map, and hold-confirm progress exposed via `aria-valuenow` with a keyboard equivalent (hold `Enter`). Wired to `POST /positions/close-all`, `POST /orders/cancel-all` and `POST /trading/kill-switch`, every invocation wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- **Global hotkey**: a binding registered in the hotkey system that **opens SCR-072** — it never fires a freeze directly. Discoverable in the hotkey cheatsheet (SCR-013). Deliberately distinct from the environment switcher, which the catalogue states is intentionally not bindable.
- **SCR-134** admin page at `/admin/risk-policy`: every global limit with units (max daily loss, max drawdown, max total notional, max positions, max leverage, max orders/min, per-symbol concentration), the per-limit breach-behaviour selector (warn / block new orders / flatten), the current measured value beside each limit, lockout durations, override policy, freeze defaults, and the "block trading while the backend is degraded" switch; validation that portfolio caps are ≥ the sum of the smallest per-account caps with an explanatory warning; the "this cannot be disabled entirely" guard; a change summary before save; **step-up gate on save** (SR-025); `risk_policy.updated` audited.
- Per-manager limit editing surface on SCR-122 (Admin: user detail) for US-ADMIN-003's per-manager caps, with the tighten-during-open-position semantics: no forced liquidation, new entries blocked, reduce-only preserved, both owner and manager informed, and every change audited with old and new values.
- Optimistic-UI prohibition: none of these controls shows success before the server acknowledges (SCR-134 performance note: "the screen confirms only after the server acknowledges").

## Out of scope
- SCR-071 / SCR-073 (E39-S04).
- The backend kill-switch engine (E39-S03) and cap enforcement (E39-S01).
- The feature-flag console (E42) and live-enablement gate (E44), both of which embed but do not own these controls.
- The flatten-all runbook document (E39-T03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Freeze with safe defaults
  Given the owner opens the kill-switch modal for all accounts
  Then "also flatten positions" is unchecked
  And "also cancel working orders" reflects the API default (checked), stated explicitly in the consequence text
  And the consequence text states that open positions are NOT closed
  And focus is on the cancel control
  And the confirm action is disabled until FREEZE is typed and a reason is entered

Scenario: Execution and completion summary
  Given the owner confirms a global freeze across 5 accounts
  Then per-account progress is shown as results arrive
  And the completed summary shows orders_cancelled, positions_flattened and rules_disarmed from KillSwitchResult
  And zero counts render as meaningful text rather than a blank

Scenario: Partial failure with retry
  Given account C failed during the freeze
  Then a partial-failure state names account C and its error
  And retry re-attempts only account C
  And the switch remains engaged throughout

Scenario: Unfreeze requires step-up
  Given the kill-switch is engaged
  When the owner chooses unfreeze
  Then a step-up authentication challenge is presented
  And on success the modal states that rules remain disarmed until explicitly re-armed

Scenario: Hotkey never fires directly
  Given the global kill-switch hotkey is pressed
  Then SCR-072 opens with the confirmation requirements intact
  And no request is sent until the user confirms

Scenario (failure): Saving a conflicting risk policy
  Given a portfolio cap lower than the sum of the smallest per-account caps
  When the owner saves SCR-134
  Then an explanatory warning names the conflicting caps
  And the save is blocked until resolved or explicitly acknowledged per the design

Scenario (edge): Tightening a limit below current exposure
  Given a manager holds exposure exceeding a newly tightened limit
  When the owner saves the tighter limit with step-up
  Then the UI states that no position will be force-closed, new entries are blocked and reduce-only remains available
  And both owner and manager see the change
  And the audit entry records old and new values

Scenario (edge): Viewer role
  Given a viewer opens the app shell
  Then the panic cluster renders disabled with an accessible explanation
  And forcing the control client-side still results in a 403 from the server
```

## Technical notes / design
Code in `apps/web/src/features/risk/killswitch/` and `apps/web/src/features/admin/risk-policy/`. The consequence text is computed from a live `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` fetched when the modal opens — never from cached counts that could be minutes old — and re-fetched if the modal stays open beyond 30 s, because presenting a stale "14 working orders" is a correctness bug in a danger dialog.

Every mutating call sends a required `Idempotency-Key`; retry after a partial failure reuses a **new** key scoped to the retried accounts, so a retry cannot replay the whole engagement.

The hotkey is registered through the existing hotkey profile system (`hotkey_profiles` table, `GET /me/keymap`) so it is rebindable and appears in the cheatsheet; it is registered with a guard so it cannot fire while a modal already has focus.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: confirmation gating (typed word + reason both required); checkbox→request-field mapping; consequence-text computation including pluralisation and zero cases; retry key scoping; SCR-134 validation rules; role-based enablement.
- **Component (Storybook + interaction tests)**: every SCR-072 state and every CMP-211 variant; keyboard hold-confirm; DEMO vs LIVE variants.
- **Contract**: MSW handlers generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` for `SetKillSwitchRequest`/`KillSwitchResult`, so the checkbox mapping cannot drift.
- **E2E (Playwright web + Electron)**: hotkey → modal → typed confirm → engaged → order attempt refused → unfreeze with step-up. Shared suite in E39-Q02.
- **a11y**: axe-core on the modal and `/admin/risk-policy`; manual screen-reader pass verifying `alertdialog` semantics, the restated consequence, focus starting on cancel, and the keyboard hold equivalent.
- **Security**: E39-X02 abuse cases; this story includes a test that a client-forced enable of a disabled control still yields 403.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
These controls are the UI for the product's last-resort safety mechanism, so the threats are: an accidental freeze (mitigated by typed confirmation, safe defaults, focus on cancel, and the hotkey opening rather than firing); a *malicious* freeze to strand a trader (mitigated server-side by RBAC scope and audit, surfaced here by always naming the actor and reason); and an unauthorised **release** (mitigated by owner-only + step-up, enforced server-side — the UI's role is to make the step-up explicit, never to be the gate). SCR-134 saves are step-up gated per SR-025 ("changing risk caps or per-account profiles"). No secrets are rendered. `security` label mandatory per DoD §8.

## Accessibility notes
`role="alertdialog"` on SCR-072 with the consequence restated in text; focus starts on the **cancel** control; typed `FREEZE` confirmation (CMP-044 `variant="typed"`); hold-to-confirm exposes `aria-valuenow` progress and has a keyboard equivalent (hold `Enter`); panic buttons are never icon-only and carry scope in their accessible name; SCR-134 uses fieldsets per limit with units and the current measured value beside the limit, a radio group for enforcement scope, and each limit has a description of what happens on breach. Danger/confirm patterns must be announced — an explicit R3 a11y gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4).

## Performance notes
The modal must render and be interactive within 100 ms of the hotkey press. The freeze is one backend call halting acceptance server-side within 200 ms; the UI must not appear blocked while per-account results stream in (SCR-072 performance note). SCR-134 confirms only after server acknowledgement, with policy changes effective on the next evaluation cycle (≤2 s).

## Observability
Audit via CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger on every invocation: `risk.freeze` (with the full option set), `risk.unfreeze`, `risk_policy.updated`, `panic.flatten_all`. Client metrics: modal open→confirm duration (to detect a confirmation flow that is too slow in an emergency), and hotkey usage counts.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80 % frontend; CI green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for every SCR-072 state and CMP-211 variant; `15-component-catalogue.md` matches.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass recorded for the alertdialog and the hold-confirm.
- [ ] design-qa performed (E39-D04).
- [ ] Security engineer review; manual abuse-case check (forced enable, non-owner release) recorded.
- [ ] QA sign-off per E39-Q01/Q02.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review including the hotkey path.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded: `ui.kill_switch_hotkey` default on; `ui.admin_risk_policy` default on for owner role only.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E39-D03` — signed-off hi-fi and handoff package (Done ≥2 sprints prior).

- `E39-S01` — `/risk/summary` for the consequence counts, and cap data for SCR-134's measured values.

5. docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md §11-§12 (risk schemas, step-up list)
6. docs/plan/04-security-program.md SR-025

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- apps/web/src/features/risk/ (dashboard SCR-071, lockout notice SCR-073, kill-switch modal SCR-072, risk policy SCR-134)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- `/api/v1/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override`, `/api/v1/killswitch/*`, `risk_lockouts`/`risk_policy`/`kill_switch_state` Postgres tables, `SystemUpdate` WS frame (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9), OMS cancel-all/reduce-only paths.

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm lint` && `pnpm typecheck`
- `cd services/api && ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict .`
- `cd services/api && pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`
- `pnpm verify` (full local gate before opening the PR)

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e39-risk-killswitch-s05`
- PR title: "E39-S05: Build the kill-switch modal SCR-072, panic cluster, global hotkey and risk policy SCR-134"
- Body: include `Closes #<issue>` (replace `<issue>` with this ticket's GitHub issue number)
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend + @CandleViewer/security (services/api/risk, services/api/oms are dual-owned per CODEOWNERS), @CandleViewer/frontend for D/S04/S05 web tickets
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels (type/feature, area/oms-execution, priority/p0, a11y, security, qa, design-qa) plus any CI-added labels

**Done means**
- All 8 Gherkin scenarios above pass as automated tests (unit/contract/E2E as appropriate).
- Coverage ≥80% on the touched package(s); CI green.
- Contract docs (OpenAPI/WS/internal-schemas) updated in the same PR if any surface changed.
- Diff ≤400 LOC (or split into the PRs named in the ticket's own Branch section); PR template fully completed.
- QA/security/a11y sign-off recorded per this ticket's own Test plan / Security notes / Accessibility notes sections.

**Do NOT**
- Do not hand-roll lockout/kill-switch state as ad-hoc booleans — the lifecycle must go through `cv.statechart.factory.build(...)`, never a direct `create_machine`/`Interpreter` call outside `statechart/`.
- Do not accept a client-supplied `until`/expiry timestamp for a lockout or kill-switch release — it is always server-computed.
- Do not widen who can clear a lockout or kill-switch beyond the owner with a valid step-up token.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking key (e.g. a dependency listed under `blocked_by` or in '## Dependencies'), move Status → Blocked, and stop. Never silently work around a failing lint/test/contract gate.

title: Design all five alert surfaces and ship the engineering handoff pack
body:
## Context
This ticket merges the former E40-D02, E40-D02 and E40-D02 into a single design-delivery ticket covering SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 plus the signed-off handoff pack. Design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`): consumed by E40-S01/E40-S01 in Sprint 18, so it must be Done by end of Sprint 16.

### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
SCR-090 and SCR-091 are the authoring surfaces of E40 and both carry explicit design sign-off checklists in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §7. SCR-091 is *not* a new editor: it reuses the rule condition editor (SCR-081, designed in E36-D02) minus the execution-action step, per digest 23 §19 and the CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm contract. This ticket's hardest job is making the reuse obvious — a trader who has authored a rule must recognise the alert editor instantly, while never being able to reach an action step.

Design-ahead: consumed by E40-S01 and E40-S01 in Sprint 18, so this must be Done by end of Sprint 16.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
Authoring an alert is half the product; being told is the other half. This ticket designs the *delivery* surfaces — the fired toast and its detail drawer (SCR-092), the content of the notification centre drawer that E10 mounted empty (SCR-014), and the notification preference matrix (SCR-115) — plus the three design-system entries (CMP-163 AlertRow, CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm, CMP-165 AlertFiredToastGroup) and the motion spec for arriving/stacking/collapsing notifications.

The governing constraint from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-092 is blunt: the toast is `role="status"`, **not assertive**, so it cannot interrupt order entry. Everything here is designed around not being the most important thing on screen.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
The design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` says no frontend work starts until its design is signed off. E40-S01..S04 start in Sprint 18, so the handoff pack must be Done in Sprint 17. This ticket turns three design tickets' output into one artifact an engineer can build from without asking a question.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
- **SCR-090 Alerts centre** (`/alerts`, tabs Active · Triggered · Snoozed): table columns name, symbol, condition, status, last triggered, delivery channels; `+ New alert`; filters by symbol and status; bulk enable/disable/delete with confirmation; row actions toggle-active, snooze (15 m / 1 h / until tomorrow), duplicate, delete, "show on chart".
  - States: empty ("No alerts yet") · active · triggered (badge) · expired one-shot moved to Triggered · snoozed with remaining time · disabled · delivery-failure chip ("Desktop notification blocked by the OS — enable it in Settings") · loading · error.
  - Alerts depending on estimated detectors carry the "(estimated)" qualifier in the condition cell.
- **SCR-091 Alert editor** (modal): condition builder (CMP-164 composing CMP-140/141/143/144/157 from the rule editor), symbol/interval scope (CMP-219), one-shot vs recurring vs once-per-bar, cooldown, expiry, delivery channels (in-app toast, notification centre, desktop, sound with preview), message template with `{{variable}}` interpolation and a live preview, `test-fire` control, CMP-234 ValidationPanel.
  - Plain-language restatement of the alert ("Notify me when BTCUSDT tape speed rises above 3 sigma").
  - Validation presentations: at least one condition, at least one delivery channel, cooldown ≥5 s, expiry in the future, estimated-metric warning, "Sound requires the desktop shell" note in the browser.
  - Explicit, drawn treatment of the **no-actions boundary**: where a rule editor has an Actions section, the alert editor shows the delivery-channel section with a one-line explanation ("Alerts notify; to act automatically, create a rule").
- Both screens drawn in dark, light and high-contrast themes, at compact and comfortable density, and at 200% zoom.
- Redlines with token names (never raw hex/px), state matrix, and Figma Dev Mode links.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
- **SCR-092 fired toast + detail drawer**: toast shows alert name, the *actual metric value* that triggered it, symbol/timeframe and time; actions open-chart-at-that-moment, snooze, disable, open detail. Detail drawer shows the full metric snapshot (the `alert_deliveries.context` payload) and a link to the bar. Multiple simultaneous alerts collapse into a counted stack ("3 alerts fired for BTCUSDT").
- **SCR-014 notification centre content**: mixed stream of alert / rule / order / risk / system / recorder items with severity by icon + text; grouped/collapsed repeats ("12 similar alerts"); per-category mute; `Shift+click` marks everything above read; deep-link presentation; empty state ("Nothing yet today"); unread badge; overflow (newest 500, older via `GET /api/v1/notifications`).
- **SCR-115 notifications settings**: full event × channel matrix (in-app toast, notification centre, desktop, sound) per category; per-category sound selection with preview and volume; quiet hours with timezone stated; desktop-permission state (granted / denied / unsupported) with per-platform remediation; the **drawn, non-negotiable** state showing that risk, lockout, kill-switch and rejection notifications cannot be fully muted; test-notification control.
- **Design-system contributions**: CMP-163 AlertRow, CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm and CMP-165 AlertFiredToastGroup specced as catalogue entries (props, variants, states, tokens, Storybook story list) and raised with the design-system team; CMP-045 Toast and CMP-060 NotificationCenter extended only via documented variants, never forked.
- **Motion spec**: toast enter/exit (transform+opacity only so the chart surface never relayouts), stack collapse, unread-badge change, drawer open; `prefers-reduced-motion` variant for each; timings expressed in `motion.*` tokens.
- **Sound assets**: ≤4 sounds, total ≤200 KB, each with a text label; a designed fallback when audio is blocked.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
- `docs/design/handoff/e40-alerts-handoff.md` containing:
  - Dev Mode links per frame for SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014, SCR-115.
  - **Token map**: every colour/space/type/elevation/motion value used, as token names only.
  - **State matrix** per screen: loading · empty · populated · active · triggered · snoozed · expired · disabled · delivery-failed · vocabulary-unavailable · permission-denied (desktop notifications) · error — each with a frame link and the copy string.
  - **Copy deck**: every string, including the estimated-detector qualifier, the "Sound requires the desktop shell" note, the auto-disarm explanation, the storm-summary wording ratified in E40-D01, the locked-row explanation in SCR-115, and all validation messages.
  - **Component contracts** for CMP-163, CMP-164, CMP-165 incl. the agreed Storybook story list.
  - **A11y contract** lifted verbatim from E40-D01: live-region roles, keyboard maps, announcement throttling, focus order.
  - **Motion table**: token, duration, easing, reduced-motion counterpart.
  - **Interaction spec** for snooze durations (15 m / 1 h / until tomorrow), bulk actions and their confirmations, `Shift+click` mark-above-read, and deep-link behaviour from a notification back to the originating chart/rule/order.
  - **Open questions: none** — anything unresolved is either decided here or explicitly deferred with a ticket link.
- Walkthrough session with the two frontend engineers who will build S01..S04, plus QA; recorded.

## Out of scope
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
SCR-092, SCR-014 content and SCR-115 (E40-D02). Motion timing (E40-D02). The a11y review pass itself (E40-D01). Handoff assembly (E40-D02).
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
SCR-090 and SCR-091 (E40-D02). The a11y review pass (E40-D01). Handoff assembly (E40-D02). Shell chrome itself (E10).
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
Building anything. Design QA of the built result (E40-D03).

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue checklist item is drawn
  Given the SCR-090 and SCR-091 design sign-off checklists in 14-screens-catalogue.md §7
  When the file is reviewed
  Then every checklist line maps to a named frame in Figma and is ticked in the review comment
Scenario: Composition uses only catalogued components
  When the file is audited against 15-component-catalogue.md
  Then every element resolves to an existing CMP id, or to a documented new/extended entry (CMP-163, CMP-164) raised against the design-system team in E40-D02
Scenario: The action boundary is visible, not implied (edge)
  Given a trader familiar with the rule editor opens the alert editor
  Then no affordance suggests an action can be attached, and the explanatory line is drawn as persistent copy, not a tooltip
Scenario: Failure states are designed (failure)
  Then the vocabulary-unavailable state (metric service offline), the delivery-failure chip and the auto-disarmed state ("metric source unavailable — alert disarmed, here is why", US-ALRT-002) are all drawn
```
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
```gherkin
Scenario: The toast never competes with order entry
  Given the SCR-092 frames
  Then the toast is annotated role="status", is positioned clear of the order ticket region, and no frame shows it taking focus
Scenario: Critical channels are visibly unmutable
  Given the SCR-115 matrix
  Then the risk, lockout, kill-switch and rejection rows are drawn in a locked state with an inline explanation, not merely omitted
Scenario: Sound is never the only channel (failure)
  Given a user disables every visual channel and leaves sound on
  Then the design shows the in-app record persisting regardless, and the matrix prevents a sound-only configuration
Scenario: Reduced motion is designed, not derived
  Then every motion entry has an explicit prefers-reduced-motion counterpart drawn, and the toast reduced-motion variant is fade-only per SCR-015
```
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
```gherkin
Scenario: The pack is self-sufficient
  Given a frontend engineer who has not attended any design review
  When they read the pack
  Then they can enumerate every state, string and token needed for SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 without asking a question
Scenario: Design-ahead is satisfied
  Then the pack is Status Done before Sprint 18 starts, meeting the >=2-sprint design-ahead rule for E40-S01..S04
Scenario: An unresolved decision is visible, not hidden (edge)
  Given a detail was deferred during review
  Then it appears in the pack under "Deferred" with a ticket link and a stated interim behaviour, never as silence
Scenario: Copy is complete (failure)
  Given any state in the state matrix
  Then it has a copy string; an empty cell fails the review
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Reuse the E36 rule-editor Figma library directly rather than copying frames; divergence between the two editors is a defect, not a design choice. The condition row, operand picker and validation panel must be *instances*, not detached copies, so E36 fixes propagate.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
The detail drawer renders `alert_deliveries.context`, a free-form JSON snapshot; design it as a key-value table (CMP-036 KeyValueRow) with a sensible ordering rule and a graceful presentation for unknown keys, because the context shape varies by metric family and the design cannot enumerate it.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
Publish the token map as a machine-readable JSON block alongside the prose so the frontend can diff it against the shipped CSS custom properties in E40-D03 rather than comparing screenshots.

## Test plan
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Design review with the CDO, a frontend lead and QA; the QA reviewer walks the state matrix and confirms every state is reachable and testable. Contrast checked with the design-system contrast tool on every theme.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
Design review incl. a frontend lead and the design-system owner (for the three CMP entries). Motion reviewed against `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` motion tokens. Storybook story list agreed with engineering so E40-S02 builds exactly those.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
Reviewed by the two implementing engineers and by QA; QA confirms every state in the matrix is reachable and observable, which is the input to E40-Q01's test plan.

## Security notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
The message-template preview must never render a secret-bearing variable. The variable allow-list drawn in the picker is the same allow-list E40-T02 enforces; list it explicitly in the redlines so the two cannot drift.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
The notification body and the detail drawer must be designed for *untrusted* text: alert names and message templates are user-authored, so the frames must specify plain-text rendering with no markup interpretation and a maximum rendered length with truncation — the visual contract that backs E40-X01's injection controls.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
The copy deck must specify that user-authored alert names and messages render as plain text with no markup interpretation, and state the truncation limit — the design-side half of E40-X01's injection control.

## Accessibility notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Table semantics drawn (name/symbol/condition/status/last-triggered/delivery as real columns with headers); status is text plus icon, never colour alone; the create button is reachable from the page heading level; focus order annotated on both frames; the sound preview has a text label.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
SCR-014 is `aria-live="polite"`, escalating to assertive only for order rejects and risk lockouts; absolute timestamps available alongside relative ones; SCR-115 is a checkbox matrix with row and column headers; every sound has a play button with a text label; the notification drawer must not steal focus when it opens on a new event.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
The a11y contract section is normative, not advisory; E40-Q02 audits against it.

## Performance notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Annotate the SCR-090 list as virtualised and cursor-paginated with ≤1 Hz live updates, and SCR-091 validation as a ≤300 ms round-trip with an explicit pending state so the design does not assume instant validation.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
SCR-014 annotated as virtualised — 500 rows at ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame, unread count debounced to 250 ms. Toast render is immediate on the `alerts` WS message; the detail fetch is lazy. Sound assets preloaded once, ≤200 KB total.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
The pack restates the budgets the design assumes: ≤2 s condition-to-toast, ≤1 Hz list updates, 500-row virtualised centre at ≤8 ms/frame, ≤200 KB sounds, ≤300 ms validation round-trip.

## Observability
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
Annotate the audited events on the frames: `alert.created`, `alert.updated`, `alert.enabled_changed`, `alert.deleted`.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
Annotate the analytics events on the frames: `alert.toast_shown`, `alert.toast_actioned`, `alert.detail_opened`, `alert.snoozed`, `notifications.opened`, `notifications.filtered`, `notifications.item_actioned`, `notifications.mark_all_read`, `notifications.preference_changed`; and the audited `notifications.risk_channel_muted`.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
Lists the analytics and audit events each surface must emit, so instrumentation is built in, not retrofitted.

## Definition of Done
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
- [ ] Both screens hi-fi in all themes/densities, 200% zoom frame included.
- [ ] Every catalogue sign-off checklist line ticked in the review comment.
- [ ] Redlines and Dev Mode links published; state matrix attached.
- [ ] Component instances (not copies) verified against the E36 library.
- [ ] CDO sign-off; ticket Status Done by end of Sprint 16 (design-ahead rule).
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
- [ ] SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi in all themes and densities, 200% zoom included.
- [ ] Catalogue sign-off checklists for all three screens ticked in the review comment.
- [ ] CMP-163/164/165 catalogue entries drafted and accepted by the design-system team.
- [ ] Motion spec published with reduced-motion counterparts.
- [ ] Sound assets delivered under the 200 KB budget with text labels.
- [ ] CDO sign-off; Done by end of Sprint 16.
### Part C — Engineering handoff pack
- [ ] Handoff pack merged and linked from E40-S01..S04.
- [ ] Walkthrough held and recorded; attendee list on the ticket.
- [ ] Token map published in machine-readable form.
- [ ] Zero open questions; deferrals ticketed.
- [ ] CDO sign-off; Status Done before Sprint 18 starts.

## Dependencies
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre and SCR-091 alert editor (wireframe → hi-fi)
`E40-D01` for the interruption taxonomy. Reuses E36's rule-editor design library (`E36-D02`). Consumed by E40-S01 and E40-S01.
### Part B — SCR-092, SCR-014 and SCR-115 hi-fi with design-system and motion specs
`E40-D01` supplies the interruption taxonomy and the critical-override list that SCR-115 renders as locked rows.

`E40-D01`. Blocks `E40-S01`, `E40-S01`, `E40-S02`.

`design/e40-alerts-centre-editor` (Figma + redline docs).

title: Implement the notify-only alert compiler and the alert CRUD API
body:
## Context
`AlertConditionIr` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` is the condition half of the rule IR with `actions` deliberately omitted, and the endpoint description states the invariant plainly: *"an alert can never place an order regardless of what the user authors"*. That invariant is enforced here, at the compiler and the write API, and nowhere else can it be weakened. This is the security-critical task of E40.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/api/cv/alerts/compiler.py` — `AlertCompiler` wrapping E35's IR validator:
  1. schema-validate against `AlertConditionIr` with `additionalProperties: false` (so an `actions` key is a schema error, not a silently ignored field);
  2. structurally reject any action-bearing node anywhere in the tree, including inside `variables`, using an allow-list of permitted node kinds rather than a deny-list of forbidden ones;
  3. resolve every referenced metric against E35's `MetricRegistry`, rejecting unknown metrics with the offending `node_id`;
  4. validate the trigger (`RuleTrigger`): `on_bar_close` requires `timeframe`, `on_timer` requires `interval_ms ≥ 100`, `on_schedule` requires a 5-field UTC cron, `on_metric_change` requires `metric`;
  5. canonicalise and compute `condition_hash` (sha256 over the canonical form) reusing E35's canonicalisation so an identical condition authored in a rule and in an alert hashes identically;
  6. flag conditions referencing **estimated** detector metrics so the UI can render the "(estimated)" qualifier (US-ALRT-003 scenario 2).
- `message_template` validation: Mustache-style placeholders resolved against an **allow-listed** variable namespace derived from the compiled condition's context (`market.*`, `footprint.*`, `position.*`, `alert.*`); any placeholder outside the allow-list is a 422, and no placeholder may resolve to a secret-bearing field.
- REST surface in `apps/api/cv/alerts/router.py`, exactly as specified:
  - `GET /api/v1/alerts` (cursor, limit, `enabled`, `symbol` filters) → `Page<Alert>`;
  - `POST /api/v1/alerts` (`AlertInput`, `Idempotency-Key` recommended) → 201 `Alert`, 422 `RuleIrInvalid`;
  - `GET /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}` → `Alert`, 404;
  - `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}` (`If-Match`) → 200 or 412 `PreconditionFailed`;
  - `DELETE /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}` → 204 (soft delete, freeing the unique name);
  - `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}/enabled` → 200 `Alert`.
- RBAC: `alerts:read` / `alerts:write`, `scope: self` — a user may only ever see and mutate their own alerts; enforced in a dependency, not per-handler.
- Audit events on every mutation: `alerts.create`, `alert.updated`, `alert.enabled_changed`, `alert.deleted` (an alert is audited because it can participate in a notification chain).
- Contract tests generated from the OpenAPI document.

## Out of scope
Evaluation (E40-T03), delivery (E40-T04), deliveries/notifications endpoints (E40-T04), webhook URL storage (E40-S03), the editor UI (E40-S01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A valid price alert compiles and persists
  When POST /api/v1/alerts is called with the priceCross example from 22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then 201 is returned, condition_hash is populated, the alert is enabled, and alerts.create is audited
Scenario: An action-bearing payload is rejected (failure)
  When condition_ir carries an actions key, or an action node nested inside variables, or an operand naming a rule action
  Then 422 RuleIrInvalid is returned naming the offending node_id, nothing is persisted, and no OMS interface is touched
Scenario: Unknown metric is refused with a usable message (failure)
  When a condition references a metric absent from the E35 registry
  Then 422 names the metric and the node_id, and lists the nearest valid metric names
Scenario: Concurrent edits do not silently overwrite (edge)
  Given two clients hold the same ETag
  When both PUT the alert
  Then the second receives 412 PreconditionFailed and its payload is not applied
Scenario: Cross-user access is impossible (failure)
  Given user B's alert id
  When user A calls GET, PUT, DELETE or PUT /enabled on it
  Then each returns 404 (not 403, so existence is not disclosed), no state changes, and the denial is audited
Scenario: A template cannot exfiltrate a secret (failure)
  When message_template references a placeholder outside the allow-listed namespace
  Then 422 is returned naming the placeholder
```

## Technical notes / design
The allow-list approach in step 2 is deliberate: a deny-list of action node kinds fails open the moment E35 adds a node kind. The permitted set is `{condition, comparison, logical, operand:metric, operand:const, operand:variable, trigger}`; anything else is rejected by construction, and a unit test enumerates E35's full node-kind registry and asserts every kind is either in the allow-list or rejected — so adding a node kind in E35 without considering alerts fails E40's tests rather than silently widening the surface.

`condition_hash` reuses E35's canonicalisation (ADR-0025-rule-ir-canonicalisation) because E40-T03 keys shared metric subscriptions on it; a private canonicalisation would silently defeat the sharing.

Error code for IR problems is the shared `RuleIrInvalid` 422 response, so the alert editor can reuse the rule editor's ValidationPanel rendering unchanged.

## Test plan
- Unit: compiler accept/reject matrix incl. the node-kind enumeration test; trigger validation per trigger type; template allow-list; canonical hash equality against an equivalent E35 rule condition; estimated-metric flagging.
- Property: fuzz IR trees (hypothesis) asserting no tree containing an action node ever compiles.
- Contract: every operation and every documented response code against the OpenAPI document.
- Integration: full CRUD lifecycle incl. soft-delete freeing the unique name and re-creation with the same name.
- Security: the cross-user matrix from the AC, run as a required check.
- Coverage ≥90% on `cv.alerts.compiler` (security-relevant module, local policy above the 85% floor).

## Security notes
Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`: **Elevation of privilege** — an alert that can act becomes an unaudited order path; mitigated by the allow-list compiler plus the fuzz property test. **Information disclosure** — cross-user alert reads; mitigated by `scope: self` enforced in a dependency and the 404-not-403 policy. **Tampering** — last-writer-wins edits; mitigated by `If-Match`. **Injection** — template placeholders; mitigated by the namespace allow-list. Data classification: alert definitions are Internal; `webhook_url_enc`/`webhook_secret_enc` are SECRET and are not writable through this task's endpoints. Security review label required — reviewed under E40-X01.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — API. The 422 payload shape (node_id + human message + suggestions) is what makes the editor's accessible ValidationPanel possible, so the message text must be plain language, not a schema dump.

## Performance notes
Compile + validate must complete in ≤300 ms p95 to meet the SCR-091 round-trip budget, including the metric-registry lookup (registry is cached in-process, invalidated on E35's vocabulary-version bump). `GET /alerts` is cursor-paginated and must use `ux_alerts_name`/`ix_alerts_live`; assert no sequential scan at 10k alerts.

## Observability
Metrics `cv_alert_compile_seconds`, `cv_alert_compile_rejected_total{reason}` (`action_node`, `unknown_metric`, `bad_trigger`, `bad_template`), `cv_alerts_total{enabled}`. Structured log on every rejection with `node_id` and `reason`, no payload echo. Audit events as listed above.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Compiler, router and RBAC dependency implemented; OpenAPI document matches the implementation (contract tests green).
- [ ] Node-kind enumeration test and IR fuzz property test in CI as required checks.
- [ ] Coverage ≥90% on the compiler; ≥85% on the module.
- [ ] Audit events emitted and asserted.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present (`security` label); SAST/SCA clean.
- [ ] `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` reconciled if the implementation revealed a spec gap.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E40-T01` (tables/repos), `E35-T04` (semantic validator, compile/validate service), `E40-K01` (placement decision informs the registry-caching strategy).

## Branch
`feat/e40-alert-compiler-api`. PR ~380 LOC; split the router and the compiler into two PRs if it exceeds 400.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §24 ALRT
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-014, SCR-015, SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-115
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-045, CMP-060, CMP-163, CMP-164, CMP-165, CMP-209, CMP-212
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.5, §3.10.4
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/alerts*`, `/notifications`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.7 `AlertUpdate`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11 rule IR and metric registry
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md`

2. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-014, SCR-115
3. docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md (alerts WS topic)
4. docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml (alert CRUD, deliveries)
5. docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md (0009_alerts migration)
6. docs/plan/04-security-program.md (webhook egress allow-list)

title: Build the server-side alert evaluator with gating and storm suppression
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** the gating, storm-suppression and snooze lifecycle (armed→…→firing→resolved) is built directly on the library via the factory; per-tick condition evaluation itself stays plain code (BENCH-2: 381 ev/s vs a 2000 ev/s target, hot-path exclusion, 29 §3).

This is module **M22**'s heart: the component that turns armed alert rows into firings. It must evaluate server-side (alerts fire with the client closed), share the E35 metric bus without duplicating evaluation, and never let a storm of detector events make the product unusable. The placement decision (shared vs separate evaluator) comes from E40-K01's ADR-0019; this task implements whichever it chose.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement the `B10` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B10.alert.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('alert', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b10_alert.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b10_alert.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- `apps/api/cv/alerts/evaluator.py` — `AlertEvaluator`:
  - **Warm-up**: load all rows where `enabled AND deleted_at IS NULL` (index `ix_alerts_live`), group by `condition_hash`, and create **one** metric subscription per distinct hash, fanned out to the alert rows sharing it.
  - **Live reconfiguration**: react to create/update/delete/enable/snooze without a restart, via the same in-process event the API emits; a changed condition re-keys its subscription and drops the old one when its last referent leaves.
  - **Gating pipeline**, evaluated in this exact order on every candidate fire: `enabled` → not soft-deleted → `expires_at` not passed → `snoozed_until` not in the future → symbol/category mute (E40-S02 preferences) unless the alert is on the critical-override list → `trigger_mode` → `cooldown_seconds` → storm suppressor → dispatch.
  - **Trigger modes**: `once` — fire, then set `enabled = false` atomically with the firing so a concurrent tick cannot double-fire; `every_time` — fire subject to `cooldown_seconds`; `once_per_bar` — fire at most once per bar keyed on `(alert_id, timeframe, bar_open_ms)`, with late-tick bar revisions not re-opening the key.
  - **Expiry semantics**: alerts do **not** expire on a timer (US-ALRT-001 scenario 3) — only an explicit `expires_at` disarms one, and when it does, the alert moves to the Triggered/Expired presentation rather than vanishing.
  - **Auto-disarm on source loss** (US-ALRT-002 scenario 2): when a referenced metric's data source becomes unavailable (E35 registry emits source-degraded), the alert is disarmed and a delivery is raised **stating why**, never failing silently.
  - **Storm suppressor**: per-user sliding window using the threshold and window ratified in E40-D01 and validated in E40-K01 (default `>20 deliveries / 60 s`); excess firings are still **recorded individually** in `alert_deliveries` with `status = 'suppressed'` and are aggregated into one summary delivery ("18 further alerts fired for BTCUSDT and 2 others"), so nothing is lost from history.
  - **Firing transaction**: the `alert_deliveries` row(s), the `outbox` row(s), and the `last_fired_at` / `fire_count` / `enabled` updates commit in one transaction — a crash between "decide" and "send" can neither lose nor duplicate (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.4).
  - **Evaluation snapshot**: the values that fired the alert are written to `alert_deliveries.context` so the alert history carries "the firing evaluation attached" (roadmap §7.2) and SCR-092's detail drawer has something to render.
- Startup/shutdown integration with the app lifespan; graceful drain so an in-flight firing completes or rolls back whole.

## Out of scope
Channel transport and the dispatcher poller (E40-T04). REST/WS surfaces for deliveries (E40-T04). Any UI. Webhook egress (E40-S03). Rule *actions* — alerts have none.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A price alert fires with no client connected
  Given an armed crossing alert at 65000 on BTCUSDT and zero WS clients
  When the recorded feed crosses 65000
  Then an alert_deliveries row is committed within 1 s with the crossing values in context
Scenario: One-shot disarms exactly once under concurrency
  Given a one-shot alert and two ticks satisfying it in the same millisecond
  Then exactly one delivery is created and the alert ends disabled
Scenario: Recurring alerts respect the cooldown
  Given an every_time alert with cooldown_seconds = 60 and a condition true continuously
  Then it fires at most once per 60 s, and the re-arm is visible in the alert row
Scenario: Bar-close semantics are honoured (edge)
  Given a once_per_bar alert on 5m and a late tick that revises the current bar
  Then the alert does not fire a second time for that bar
Scenario: A storm aggregates without losing history (edge)
  Given 25 qualifying firings for one user inside 60 s
  Then the first N are delivered normally, the remainder are recorded with status suppressed, one summary delivery is produced, and the alert centre can show all 25
Scenario: A dead metric source disarms loudly (failure)
  Given an alert on a metric whose source goes unavailable
  Then the alert is disarmed and a delivery explains why, rather than the alert silently never firing again
Scenario: A crash mid-fire loses nothing (failure)
  Given the process is killed between the delivery insert and the poller run
  Then on restart the outbox row is still pending and is delivered exactly once
```

## Technical notes / design

**Statechart contract.** Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B10.1–.8. Mandatory config: `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §1.2 (`79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §3 stay plain code.
Subscription sharing is keyed on `condition_hash` — the same hash E40-T02 computes with E35's canonicalisation, which is why both must use one canonicaliser.

Cooldown and `once_per_bar` keys live in an in-process TTL map backed by `alerts.last_fired_at` so a restart cannot reopen a cooldown window; on warm-up the map is rebuilt from the table.

`once` disarm uses a conditional update (`UPDATE alerts SET enabled = false WHERE id = :id AND enabled`) inside the firing transaction; zero rows affected means another worker won the race and this evaluation discards its firing.

The storm suppressor is per **user**, not per alert, because the user-visible failure is "too many notifications", which no per-alert limit can bound.

Critical-override entries (from E40-D01's ratified list: daily-loss breach, liquidation proximity, connection loss, kill-switch engagement, fan-out partial failure) bypass mute and quiet hours but **not** the crash-safety or recording path.

## Test plan

**Statechart test plan additions:**
- Pure-API unit tests of the `b10_alert` binding module using a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership in `tests/xstate_contract/test_b10_alert.py`, covering both spellings and every §B10.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point this ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a `machine_hash` or HMAC mismatch.
- Unit: each gate in isolation; the gating order (a test asserts snooze is checked before cooldown so a snoozed alert does not consume its cooldown); trigger-mode state machines; `once_per_bar` key derivation for every supported timeframe incl. late revision; storm-suppressor window arithmetic at boundaries (exactly N, N+1).
- Integration: recorded Bybit fixture replay asserting an exact expected firing sequence (deterministic — same window, same sequence across runs); auto-disarm on simulated source loss; subscription count equals distinct condition hashes for a 100-alert/12-condition corpus.
- Chaos: process kill between insert and dispatch (covered end-to-end in E40-Q02).
- Perf: 500 armed alerts / 20 symbols under a recorded high-rate window, asserting p95 condition→record ≤1 s (E40-Q02 owns the gate; this task ships the benchmark).
- Coverage ≥85% on `cv.alerts.evaluator`.

## Security notes
**Denial of service** is the headline threat and it is self-inflicted: an unbounded alert count or an unthrottled detector stream can starve evaluation. Controls — a per-user armed-alert cap (configurable, default 200) enforced at `POST /alerts`, the storm suppressor, and a bounded evaluation queue that sheds with a counted metric rather than growing without limit. **Tampering**: the evaluator writes history that is append-only by trigger. **Repudiation**: every firing carries its evaluation snapshot, so "why did this fire" is answerable from data.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The storm summary text produced here is read by a screen reader via SCR-014, so its wording comes from E40-D02's copy deck rather than being composed ad hoc in code.

## Performance notes
Budgets: condition met → `alert_deliveries` committed ≤1 s p95 at 500 armed alerts (US-ALRT-001 NFR). Evaluation must add ≤15% to E35 rule-evaluation p99 if the shared placement was chosen (ADR-0019 criterion). Subscriptions must equal distinct condition hashes — a regression test asserts this, because losing subscription sharing is a silent 10× cost.

## Observability
`cv_alert_eval_latency_seconds` (histogram), `cv_alerts_armed` (gauge), `cv_alert_subscriptions` (gauge), `cv_alert_fires_total{trigger_mode}`, `cv_alert_suppressed_total{reason=storm|snoozed|muted|expired|cooldown}`, `cv_alert_autodisarmed_total{reason}`, `cv_alert_eval_queue_depth`. Structured log per firing with `alert_id`, `condition_hash`, `trigger_mode`, correlation id. Grafana panel added to the E04 board.

## Definition of Done

**Statechart DoD additions:** `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.
- [ ] Evaluator implemented per ADR-0019; gating order unit-asserted.
- [ ] Deterministic replay test green and reproducible across runs.
- [ ] Subscription-sharing regression test in CI.
- [ ] Metrics exported and dashboarded; per-user alert cap enforced.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85%; CI green.
- [ ] `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` updated if the gating pipeline differs from the documented description.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E40-T02` (compiled conditions and hashes), `E40-K01` (placement + storm thresholds), `E35` evaluator/metric bus, `E25` detector metrics for US-ALRT-003 conditions.

## Branch
`feat/e40-alert-evaluator`. PR ~400 LOC; split the storm suppressor into its own PR if needed.

title: Build the delivery dispatcher, deliveries API and the alerts WS topic
body:
## Context
US-ALRT-005's NFR is the design constraint: *"no channel may be the single source of truth — the alert centre always records everything."* This task builds the fan-out from a recorded firing to the channels, the read surfaces the UI consumes, and the live `alerts` WS topic, all on top of the transactional outbox so a channel failure degrades delivery without losing the record.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/api/cv/alerts/dispatcher.py` — outbox poller for topic `alert.deliver`:
  - one `alert_deliveries` row **per channel per firing**, so a failed email and a delivered toast are separately visible;
  - channel adapters: `in_app` (always succeeds — it is the record itself, immediately visible over WS), `desktop` (delivered to the Electron shell over the existing WS as a client-side instruction; the shell's OS-permission state is reported back and surfaced as the SCR-090 delivery-failure chip), `email` (via the configured relay from E04; retried per policy), `webhook` and `push` adapters **registered but disabled** — `webhook` lands in E40-S03 (R5), `push` is not in scope (Android is out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14) and is rejected at the API with a clear message;
  - retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, `max_attempts` from the outbox row (default 8), `attempt` mirrored onto `alert_deliveries.attempt`, terminal failure sets `status = 'failed'` with `error_message` and, for the failing channel only, raises a notification about the channel failure — the underlying alert record is untouched;
  - status transitions `queued → sent | failed | suppressed`, and `sent → acked` on user ack; DELETE is impossible by trigger.
- REST surface:
  - `GET /api/v1/alerts/deliveries` (cursor, limit, `status`, `alert_id`, `unacked_only`, `from`, `to`) → `Page<AlertDelivery>`;
  - `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/{deliveryId}/ack` → `AlertDelivery`;
  - `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/ack-all` → `{acknowledged: int}`;
  - `GET /api/v1/notifications` — the unified read-model union over `alert_deliveries`, `rule_events`, `order_events` and `system_events`, filtered to what the caller may see, with `kind` (`alert|rule|order|risk|system`) and `unread_only` filters; this is the scroll-back behind SCR-014.
- WS topic `alerts` per `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`: payload `AlertUpdate` (`deliveries[]` + `unacked_count`), subscription option `unacked_only`, cadence **250 ms**, permission `alerts:read`, scope "own alerts only", snapshot-on-subscribe then deltas, resync on gap per the standard envelope.
- Backpressure: the `alerts` topic coalesces within its 250 ms window and never grows an unbounded per-connection queue; overflow drops to a "resync required" marker rather than silently truncating.

## Out of scope
Evaluation (E40-T03). Webhook egress and its SSRF controls (E40-S03). Any UI (E40-S01..S04). Email relay provisioning (E04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A firing reaches every configured channel
  Given an alert with channels [in_app, desktop]
  When it fires
  Then two alert_deliveries rows are created, the in_app row is visible over the alerts WS topic within 250 ms, and the desktop row transitions to sent when the shell confirms
Scenario: A failing channel does not erase the record
  Given email delivery returns 500 on every attempt
  Then the email delivery ends failed with its error recorded, the in-app record still exists and is unaffected, and a channel-failure notification is raised once, not per attempt
Scenario: Acknowledgement is idempotent (edge)
  When the same delivery is acked twice
  Then the second call returns the same acked state and does not change acked_at
Scenario: Exactly-once under restart (failure)
  Given the process restarts with pending outbox rows
  Then each pending row is delivered exactly once, proven by the unique (topic, dedup_key) index and a duplicate-delivery assertion
Scenario: A user cannot read another user's deliveries (failure)
  Given user B's deliveryId
  When user A acks it or lists with alert_id belonging to B
  Then 404 is returned, nothing changes, and the denial is audited
Scenario: Push is refused clearly (edge)
  When an alert is created with channel push
  Then the API returns 422 explaining push is not available in this deployment, rather than accepting an alert that can never deliver
```

## Technical notes / design
The poller leases rows with `locked_by`/`locked_until` and a `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim so multiple workers are safe. Idempotency on the consumer side comes from the delivery row itself: a channel adapter is only invoked for a row in `queued`, and the transition to `sent` is a conditional update.

`GET /notifications` is a read-model union, not a table: implement it as a UNION ALL over four sources with a shared `(ts, id)` keyset cursor, each source pre-filtered by the caller's scope. It is read-only and has no permissions of its own (`x-rbac: { permissions: [], scope: self }`) — visibility comes from the per-source filters.

Desktop notifications are not a server-side transport: the server marks the delivery `queued` for the `desktop` channel, the Electron shell renders the OS notification on receipt over WS and posts back the outcome, which is what lets SCR-090 show "Desktop notification blocked by the OS".

## Test plan
- Unit: retry/backoff schedule; status transition legality (an illegal transition raises); per-channel row creation; ack idempotency; union cursor ordering across sources with identical timestamps.
- Contract: all four REST operations and the `alerts` WS schema against `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.7 — a schema-diff test fails if the payload drifts.
- Integration: end-to-end fire → deliver → WS push → ack, with a fault-injected failing channel; restart-with-pending-outbox exactly-once test.
- Perf: WS cadence held at 250 ms under a firing burst; `GET /notifications` p95 <200 ms at 1M rows across the four sources.
- Coverage ≥85% on `cv.alerts.dispatcher` and the router.

## Security notes
**Spoofing/authorisation**: deliveries are `scope: self`; the ack endpoints must resolve ownership from the delivery's `user_id`, never from a client-supplied user id. **Information disclosure**: `GET /notifications` unions four sources with different scoping rules — the union must apply each source's own filter, and a test asserts a viewer-role user sees no order events they lack `orders:read` for. **DoS**: `ack-all` must be bounded (batched update with a cap and a continuation), not an unbounded statement. **Repudiation**: delivery history is append-only. No secret ever enters a delivery title/body/context — asserted by a test that scans serialised payloads for the SECRET column names.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — API/WS. The `unacked_count` field exists so the UI can render an accurate accessible name ("Notifications, 3 unread") without counting client-side.

## Performance notes
`alerts` topic cadence 250 ms with coalescing; unacked-count query hits `ix_ad_user_unack`; the deliveries list is cursor-paginated (never OFFSET); `GET /notifications` is the scroll-back for a 500-row virtualised client list, so it must support a page size of 500 without degradation.

## Observability
`cv_alert_delivery_total{channel,status}`, `cv_alert_delivery_latency_seconds{channel}` (firing → sent), `cv_alert_delivery_attempts` (histogram), `cv_outbox_depth{topic}`, `cv_outbox_dead_total{topic}`, `cv_ws_alerts_subscribers`. Alertmanager rule (E04): `cv_outbox_depth{topic="alert.deliver"}` sustained >100 for 5 min → warn; any `cv_outbox_dead_total` increase → warn.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Dispatcher, four REST operations and the `alerts` WS topic implemented and contract-tested.
- [ ] Exactly-once-under-restart test green in CI.
- [ ] Push rejected explicitly; webhook adapter registered but disabled with a feature flag `alerts.webhook_enabled = false`.
- [ ] Metrics exported, Alertmanager rules added.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85%; `22-api-openapi.yaml` and `23-ws-protocol.md` reconciled.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E40-T03` produces the firings this task delivers. `E04` supplies the email relay and the metrics/Alertmanager plumbing. `E09` supplies session scope and permissions.

## Branch

title: UX research + wireframes for the journal surfaces (SCR-093..096)
body:
## Context
E41 introduces four brand-new surfaces (SCR-093 Journal list, SCR-094 Trade detail / post-mortem, SCR-095 Analytics dashboard, SCR-096 Tag manager) and a new interaction the product has not had before: **retrospective review** rather than live trading. The design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, cadence section) requires design to be Done >=2 sprints before the consuming FE story; E41 stories land in S18-S19, so research and wireframes run in **S16**.

Research is required because the review loop is genuinely new interaction (not a restyle of an existing screen): what does the owner actually do after a losing session, in what order, and what does "evidence" mean to them? Getting this wrong produces an analytics page nobody opens.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Research** with the two personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md` who own this loop (Owner/principal trader, Account Manager): 3 moderated sessions, 45 min each, using the current spreadsheet/notes workflow as the baseline artefact.
- Research questions, at minimum: (a) what triggers a review session; (b) which fields are looked at first on a closed trade; (c) how tags are actually used (taxonomy vs free text); (d) whether demo results are considered meaningful; (e) what is exported and why.
- **Journey map** for "review yesterday's session" added to `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`.
- **Lo-fi wireframes** (Figma, `CandleViewer / E41 Journal` page) for SCR-093, SCR-094, SCR-095, SCR-096, each covering the states declared in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`: loading, empty, partial ("chart context unavailable"), reconciling, insufficient sample.
- **Information architecture** decision: `/journal` and `/journal/analytics` as separate routes with SCR-094 as page-or-drawer and SCR-096 as modal, consistent with `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md`.
- A written **findings memo** with 5-8 numbered findings, each mapped to a wireframe decision.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi visuals, tokens, motion (E41-D02/D03).
- Any Figma work on replay (SCR-097+, owned by E26) or alerts (E40).
- Quantitative/analytics instrumentation studies - the sample size is one owner plus a few managers.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Research completed and synthesised
  Given 3 moderated sessions have been run and recorded with consent
  When the findings memo is published
  Then it contains at least 5 numbered findings, each traced to a specific wireframe decision on SCR-093, SCR-094, SCR-095 or SCR-096

Scenario: Every declared state is drawn
  When the CDO reviews the wireframe set
  Then every state listed for each screen in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md exists as a frame, including the empty and "chart context unavailable" states
  And no frame introduces a component absent from docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md without an explicit new-component note

Scenario: Statistics are not presented as advice
  Given a wireframe shows expectancy or win rate
  Then the frame carries the low-sample caveat treatment and no prescriptive language ("you should...") anywhere on the surface
```

## Technical notes / design
Wireframes must honour two hard product constraints that emerged from the plan and are non-negotiable in review: DEMO and LIVE trades are **visibly separated and never aggregated** (SCR-093 sign-off checklist), and every chart has a **table alternative** (SCR-095 a11y note). Both are drawn at wireframe stage, not retrofitted at hi-fi.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). Validation is the moderated sessions themselves plus a CDO review; the wireframe set is re-validated by E41-D05 design QA against the built screens.

## Security notes
Session recordings contain real account identifiers and P&L. Recordings are stored in the private research drive, retained 90 days, and any screenshot used in the memo has account ids and balances redacted. No API keys or key identifiers may appear in any research artefact (asset A-12, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`).

## Accessibility notes
Wireframes annotate reading order, table semantics for SCR-093, and the "View as table" affordance for every chart on SCR-095. Density defaults chosen so that contrast can reach 4.5:1 at hi-fi (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section on dense tables).

## Performance notes
Wireframes must assume server-side aggregation and cursor pagination - no design may imply the client holds 10 000 trades in memory to compute a total (SCR-093 performance note).

## Observability
Defines which analytics events the screens must emit: `journal.list_viewed`, `journal.filtered`, `journal.detail_viewed`, `journal.analytics_viewed`, `journal.analytics_filtered`, `journal.cohort_changed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] 3 sessions run, notes and consent recorded.
- [ ] Findings memo published and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] Journey map merged into `docs/plan/17-ux-diagrams.md`.
- [ ] Wireframes for all four screens, all declared states, in Figma with a shareable link on the ticket.
- [ ] CDO review passed; sign-off comment recorded (design sign-off criterion).
- [ ] New-component candidates (CMP-166..169) flagged to the design-system team.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E05 (Design system v0 must exist so wireframes reference real primitives rather than inventing them).

## Branch
`design/journal-analytics-research` (for the docs deltas); Figma is the primary artefact.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#25-jrn--journal--analytics` - US-JRN-001..010
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` - SCR-093 Journal (trade list), SCR-094 Trade detail / post-mortem, SCR-095 Journal analytics dashboard, SCR-096 Journal tag manager
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` - CMP-166 JournalEntryRow, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard, CMP-169 TagEditor, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-047 DateRangePicker, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-058 InlineEdit, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-021 Link
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` section 2.25 JRN
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 3.7 - `journal_trades`, `journal_tags`, `journal_trade_tags`, `notes`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` - `/journal/trades`, `/journal/trades/{journalTradeId}`, `/journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/notes`, `/journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/context`, `/journal/tags`, `/journal/analytics`, `/executions/closed-pnl`
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` - C18 Parquet+DuckDB, C10 Rule Engine; module M20 `journal` (`services/api/journal/`, deps M1, M10, M14) per `CONSTITUTION.md` section 3
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` - asset A-12, threat S4, control SR-098, section 7.2 rows 35-37
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 13 - REST read p95 <150 ms
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.2 (E41 scope, 26 pts, S18-S19), section 11.1 dependency graph (`E29 --> E41`)

## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. AGENTS.md §0 (read-order) and §3 (how to pick up a ticket)
2. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`
3. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#25-jrn--journal--analytics`
4. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`

**Commands**
