title: Build SCR-145 feature-flag console and SCR-148 maintenance mode
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-007 — Feature flags (Must)**: "As the owner, I want runtime feature flags, so that I can shed load or disable a risky feature without a deployment." The scenarios set three hard rules — a disabled feature disappears **for all users within 10 seconds** and the change is audited; flags controlling trading capability (live enablement, one-click, rule arming) require **step-up authentication**; and the current state of every flag, who changed it and when, is listed. The NFR closes the loophole: "flags are server-side with a client push; **no flag may weaken a security control**."

**SCR-148 Admin: maintenance mode** is listed under US-ADMIN-007 and US-ADMIN-011 and shares the same control plane: entering maintenance blocks new orders server-side within 200 ms, pauses algos, optionally keeps the recorder running, and broadcasts a notice to all sessions within 2 s — while stating explicitly that **native exchange stops remain active**.

The flag store, resolution order and kill-switch bypass already exist in the schema (`21-database-schema.md` §3.9: `feature_flags`, `feature_flag_overrides`, "Kill-switch flags (`is_killswitch`) bypass caching and are re-read every 5 s"), and the API surface is `GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags` + `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}`. The service behaviour is E42-T03; this story is the console.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-145** at `/admin/flags`: CMP-049 Table of **CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow** — key, human description of what the flag changes, kind (`boolean` / `percentage` / `variant`), resolved value, scope (global / per-user / per-role override), last changed by and when. Search across keys and descriptions. Data: `GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags`; writes via `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}`.
- **Risky-flag grouping**: flags affecting order routing, risk enforcement or audit are grouped, visually marked and **step-up gated** on change (sign-off checklist requirement). `trading.live_enabled` renders as **disabled with the blocking reason** and a link to SCR-137 security centre — the enabling path itself belongs to E43/E44, not here.
- **Dependency acknowledgement**: turning off a flag an armed rule depends on lists the affected rules and requires acknowledgement before the write proceeds.
- **Per-flag change history** (a filtered audit query on `flags.change` for that key, reusing E42-S04's row renderer).
- "Requires reload" indicator on flags that cannot be applied live, with an explicit reload action rather than silent later application.
- **CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip** rendered on owner-visible surfaces gated by an unreleased flag, so QA can see which flag governs a screen.
- **SCR-148 maintenance mode**: page section plus `role="alertdialog"` entry modal with typed confirmation; the consequence list is rendered verbatim as a list — "New orders are blocked. Running algos are cancelled. Recording continues. Managers see a maintenance notice." — plus the explicit statement that native exchange stops remain active; a scheduled-window option with advance notice; and the manager/viewer-facing maintenance notice banner.
- Live propagation: flag and maintenance changes arrive at every client over the auto-subscribed WS `system` topic (`kind: feature_flags`), applied without a reload where possible.
- Audit: `flags.change` (step-up, high severity, with before/after), `maintenance.enabled`, `maintenance.disabled`.

## Out of scope
- Enabling `trading.live_enabled` and the evidence-bound live gate — **US-ADMIN-012 is owned by E44 (`E44-T04` evidence-bound write, `E44-S01` gate UI) with the enforcement/attestation half in `E43-S01`**. This console only renders the flag as blocked with the reason and a link to SCR-137; it contains no enable affordance, and `E42-Q06` asserts that as a test.
- The kill-switch itself (E39) — surfaced here as state, engaged from its own safety-critical surface.
- The flag-evaluation service, caching and `system` push implementation (E42-T03).
- Flag-debt hygiene CI warnings on `expires_at` (a chore in E48).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Toggle a flag
  Given the liquidation-heat estimate flag is on
  When I disable it and complete step-up
  Then the feature disappears for all connected users within 10 seconds via the system topic
  And the change is audited with before and after values and my actor id

Scenario: Safety flags require step-up
  Given a flag is classified as trading-capability affecting
  When I attempt to change it without a fresh admin token
  Then the re-auth gate appears and the write does not occur until elevation succeeds

Scenario: Flag state visibility
  Then every flag lists its current state, its human description, its scope, who changed it last and when
  And each flag exposes its own change history

Scenario: Live enablement stays blocked here
  Given the pen-test sign-off is outstanding
  Then trading.live_enabled renders disabled with the blocking reason and a link to the security centre
  And the API rejects a direct write with validation_failed / gate_evidence_required

Scenario: Maintenance mode consequences are explicit
  When I open the maintenance-mode entry dialog
  Then it is role="alertdialog" listing exactly: new orders blocked, running algos cancelled, recording continues, managers see a maintenance notice
  And it states that native exchange stops remain active
  And entry requires a typed confirmation and step-up

Scenario (failure): Flag write rejected mid-flight
  Given the server rejects the flag write with 422
  Then the toggle reverts to its server value with an inline error naming the reason
  And no optimistic state is left applied

Scenario (edge): Armed rule depends on the flag
  Given two armed rules depend on the flag being disabled
  Then the affected rules are listed and I must acknowledge before the write proceeds
```

## Technical notes / design
- Resolution order is server-side and authoritative (`21-database-schema.md` §3.9): user override → role override → percentage rollout (hash of `user_id||flag_key`) → default. The console **displays** the resolved value plus the override chain; it never recomputes resolution locally for enforcement.
- `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` body: `SetFeatureFlagRequest` (`value`, `overrides`, `reason`, optional `evidence_url`). `trading.live_enabled` is special-cased server-side and fails with `validation_failed` / `gate_evidence_required` without evidence — the UI surfaces that verbatim rather than pre-validating.
- Optimistic UI is **not** used for risky flags; the toggle shows a pending state until the server confirms, because a wrongly-rendered safety flag is worse than a slow one.
- Live application: subscribe to the already-open `system` topic and apply `kind: feature_flags` payloads to the client flag store; flags marked `requires_reload` set a banner instead of mutating live state.
- Maintenance mode is itself a kill-switch-class flag (`is_killswitch = true`), so it bypasses caching and is re-read every 5 s server-side.
- Error codes: `validation_failed`, `gate_evidence_required`, `stepup_required`, `forbidden`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: override-chain rendering for boolean/percentage/variant kinds; risky-flag classification driving step-up; pending (non-optimistic) toggle state; rollback on 422; `requires_reload` banner; dependency-acknowledgement list construction.
- **Contract**: `/admin/feature-flags` GET/PUT against the OpenAPI schema incl. the `flagKey` pattern.
- **Integration**: a `system` frame with `kind: feature_flags` updates the console and the rest of the app's flag store consistently.
- **E2E**: `admin-flags.spec.ts` — two browser contexts; owner disables a flag and the second (manager) context loses the feature within 10 s; `trading.live_enabled` blocked-state assertion; maintenance entry/exit with the manager context seeing the notice within 2 s and order entry refusing.
- **a11y**: axe; toggles labelled with the flag name (not "on/off"); alertdialog behaviour for maintenance entry.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/flags.json`, `flags.live-blocked.json`, `system.flags-push.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **elevation of privilege via flags** — the NFR "no flag may weaken a security control" is enforced by a server-side allowlist of what a flag may gate (E42-T03) and asserted by a test here that no flag key in the catalogue maps to an auth/RBAC/audit control; **tampering** (client-side flag forcing — the client store is display-only for gating non-security UI, all enforcement is server-side); **repudiation** (every change audited at high severity with before/after and a required `reason`).
- Maintenance mode is a **safety** control: it must fail closed — if the write fails, the UI must never show the system as being in maintenance.
- `trading.live_enabled` is the R4 gate; this console must not provide any path to enable it. Reviewed explicitly in E42-X02.
- Data classification: Confidential operational configuration; no PII, no secrets.

## Accessibility notes
- Each toggle's accessible name is the **flag key plus its human description**, never a bare "on/off" (catalogue a11y requirement).
- Risky flags are grouped under a heading with a text label ("Trading-capability flags — changes require re-authentication"), not merely a colour band.
- Maintenance entry dialog is `role="alertdialog"`; the consequence list is a real `<ul>` so it is read in full; the typed-confirm field is labelled and its expected value stated in text.
- Blocked flags are disabled **with a reason** exposed via `aria-describedby` (RBAC/blocked-control convention from `14-screens-catalogue.md` §0).
- Flag state changes arriving over WS are announced politely once, not per-flag in a burst.

## Performance notes
- Flag change propagates to all sessions within 2 s over `system` (catalogue) and the feature is gone for all users within 10 s (US-ADMIN-007).
- Maintenance mode blocks order acceptance server-side within 200 ms and broadcasts within 2 s (SCR-148).
- The console makes no polling requests; it renders from one GET plus the existing `system` subscription.

## Observability
- Audit: `flags.change {key, before, after, reason}` (high severity, step-up), `maintenance.enabled {window, message}`, `maintenance.disabled`.
- Metrics: `cv_feature_flag_changes_total{key,result}`, `cv_flag_push_latency_ms`, `cv_maintenance_mode` gauge.
- Logs: flag writes log actor, key, before/after hash and `request_id`; maintenance transitions log the consequence set actually applied (orders blocked, algos cancelled, recorder state).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on new/changed lines; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for every new/changed component variant, including loading, empty, error and degraded states.
- [ ] `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the spec.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched routes, keyboard-only pass, one manual screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the signed-off Figma spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as `priority/*` bugs.
- [ ] security: RBAC deny-by-default verified server-side (non-owner receives 404 from the router and 403 from the API); every state-changing control wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and asserted to emit its audit entry.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded for the surface.
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E42-S01` — admin shell.
- `E42-D04` — hi-fi design for SCR-145 and SCR-148.
- `E42-T03` — flag admin service, the security-control allowlist, maintenance-mode enforcement and the `system` push.

## Branch
`feat/admin-screens-flags` — 2 PRs: (1) SCR-145 console + history, (2) SCR-148 maintenance mode.

title: Statechart inspector read API: machines, config, chain_trips, dropped_receipts, deferred depth, Stately export
body:
## Context
Every catalogue lifecycle is built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` (ADR-0016 Accepted). A restored machine with `chain_trips > 0` is admitted degraded and stays latched until an operator acknowledges it in the admin inspector (`29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4, the `chain_trips` latch note). This task is the read API that inspector needs: it never queries a live `Interpreter` on the hot path (MUSTNOT-03) - it reads the `CvAuditPlugin` write-ahead `machine_events` table and the persisted snapshot, both landed by `E50-T60`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /admin/statecharts` - list live machines by kind (`machine_key`), current published state/enum, `machine_hash`, and `chain_trips`/`dropped_receipts`/deferred-depth counters, sourced from the persisted snapshot and the `CvMetricsPlugin` `cv_machine_*` gauges (E50-T60), never from a live interpreter call.
- `GET /admin/statecharts/{machine_key}` - context summary (redacted per the same rules as the WS topic in `E17-T08`), full config, and current configuration path.
- `GET /admin/statecharts/{machine_key}/export` - the Stately-compatible JSON export for the chart registered under that `machine_hash` (from `statechart/registry.py`), so the admin screen can render the same diagram Stately would.
- Per-entity RBAC identical in shape to `E17-T08`'s topic authorisation (owner/account scope), reusing the same permission check rather than a bespoke one.

## Out of scope
- The latch-acknowledge write path and the inspector UI itself - **E42-S08**.
- The live-update WS topic - **E17-T08**; this is the point-in-time/list read model.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: List live machines
  Given several B1-B20 machines are running
  When I call GET /admin/statecharts
  Then I see one row per machine with kind, state, machine_hash, chain_trips and dropped_receipts

Scenario: No hot-path interpreter query
  Given the read API serves a request
  Then it is answered from the persisted snapshot and machine_events, with no call into a live Interpreter instance

Scenario: Stately export matches the registered chart
  Given a machine_hash registered in statechart/registry.py
  When I call the export endpoint
  Then the returned JSON round-trips through the same Stately schema used to author the chart
```

## Technical notes / design
This is a pure read model over `CvAuditPlugin`'s write-ahead `machine_events` rows plus the quiescent snapshot store (`statechart/persistence.py`); it does not import `xstate_statemachine` directly (`CV-LINT-IMPORT` applies) and does not hold or construct an `Interpreter`. Built directly on the library via the factory/registry/plugin surface: no hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime.

## Test plan
Contract: response shapes against `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Integration: list/detail/export for at least one machine of each catalogue kind; RBAC refusal cross-account. Perf: p99 under the SCR budget for admin reads.

## Security notes
Context summaries are redacted the same way as the `E17-T08` topic payloads; the export endpoint reveals chart structure only, never live secrets/context values.

## Performance notes
Read-model only; no interpreter construction cost on the request path.

## Observability
Reuses `cv_machine_*` families from `E50-T60`.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2; `tests/xstate_contract` gate green.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E50-T60**, **E50-T01** and **E42-T01**.

## Branch
`feat/e42-statechart-inspector-api`

`docs/plan/29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4 (chain_trips latch), §4d; `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md`.

title: Automate admin abuse cases, RBAC assertions and SAST/DAST rules
body:
## Context
A threat model and a security review are point-in-time artefacts. The controls they verify must keep holding through every later change — and E42's controls are exactly the ones E43, E44 and E49 will be editing around.

`00-planning-brief.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and DAST (OWASP ZAP) as required checks. `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1 already assumes a Semgrep rule exists for audit coverage: the list of actions that MUST be audited is described as "enforced by a Semgrep rule on the service layer". This ticket makes that real for the admin surface and turns the threat model's abuse cases into a permanently running suite.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **RBAC assertion suite**: parameterised tests over every `/admin/*` and `/users*` route × every role (owner, manager, viewer, unauthenticated) × elevation state (fresh, stale, none), asserting the expected status **and** the expected audit entry. The route list is enumerated from the router, so a newly added admin route without a guard fails the suite rather than slipping through.
- **Abuse-case automation** from E42-X01: invite-link replay; TOTP replay; grant self-assignment; role escalation under concurrent writes; last-owner removal; audit mutation attempts (API and direct database); export range and rate abuse; view-as attempting a mutation; flag write without step-up; restore without maintenance mode; backup download URL reuse after expiry.
- **Semgrep rules** (committed to the repo's rule set):
  1. Every admin service mutation function is wrapped by the audit decorator — a mutation without it fails CI.
  2. No flag lookup inside `auth`, `rbac` or `audit` modules.
  3. No route under the admin router lacking an explicit permission declaration.
  4. No logging statement that can receive an invite link, a backup download URL, an API secret or a TOTP code.
- **ZAP (DAST)** profile covering the admin surface against staging: authenticated scans as manager and as viewer, asserting no admin endpoint is reachable; plus the standard injection/headers/CSP checks for the admin routes.
- CI wiring: the RBAC suite and Semgrep rules run on every PR touching admin code; ZAP runs nightly against staging.

## Out of scope
- The threat model (E42-X01) and the manual review (E42-X02).
- Fixing findings, which land on the owning stories.
- Repo-wide SAST/DAST baseline configuration (E03/E43) — this ticket adds admin-specific rules to it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The RBAC matrix is exhaustive and self-maintaining
  Given the route list is enumerated from the application router
  When the suite runs
  Then every route is asserted for every role and elevation state
  And adding an admin route without a permission declaration fails the suite

Scenario: Audit coverage is enforced by a rule, not by discipline
  Given an admin mutation function without the audit decorator
  When Semgrep runs in CI
  Then the build fails naming the function

Scenario: Abuse cases are permanently asserted
  When the abuse-case suite runs
  Then every case from the threat model is exercised
  And each is denied with the expected status and produces the expected audit entry

Scenario (failure): A secret reaches a log statement
  Given code that logs a value derived from an invite link or a backup download URL
  Then Semgrep fails the build

Scenario (edge): ZAP authenticated as a manager
  Then no /admin/* endpoint returns anything other than 403
  And every attempt appears in the audit log
```
- All suites and rules merged and running in CI with the stated triggers.
- A deliberately-broken branch demonstrates each rule firing (recorded once, so the rules' value is proven rather than assumed).

## Technical notes / design
- The RBAC suite asserts on the audit entry as well as the status code, because a silent 403 is only half a control — the roadmap's rule is "Non-owners receive 404 from the router and 403 from the API; **every admin action is audited**".
- Semgrep rules are written with test cases (positive and negative) in the rule directory, so a rule that stops matching after a refactor is itself caught.
- The ZAP profile uses authenticated sessions for manager and viewer roles; an unauthenticated-only scan would miss the entire privilege-escalation surface.
- The concurrency abuse cases (role escalation, last-owner removal) run N parallel attempts and assert exactly one success — a single-threaded test would pass against broken code.

## Test plan
- Meta-testing is part of the deliverable: each Semgrep rule ships with a failing fixture, and the RBAC suite is demonstrated to fail against an unguarded route.

## Security notes
- This ticket converts one-time assurance into continuous assurance; its value is entirely in the rules being **enforcing** (build-failing) rather than advisory.
- Test credentials are synthetic and environment-scoped; the suite refuses to run against a production base URL.
- Findings from the automated suites are triaged like any security finding: severity, disposition, remediation ticket.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — automated security tooling.

## Performance notes
- The RBAC suite is parameterised over many combinations; it is sharded and runs in under 5 minutes, because a slow security gate gets bypassed.

## Observability
- Asserts the observability of denials: every denied request must produce both an audit entry and a metric increment. The suite fails if a denial is silent.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded with STRIDE category, likelihood/impact, and disposition (fixed / mitigated / accepted-risk with Owner sign-off).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding has a linked remediation ticket that is Done before the epic closes.
- [ ] Controls traced to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requirement ids.
- [ ] Automated checks (Semgrep rules, ZAP rules, RBAC assertion tests) merged and running in CI, not just documented.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted on this ticket and on the epic.

## Dependencies
- `E42-X01` — supplies the abuse cases to automate.
- `E42-T04` — the lifecycle contract (slice S1), the disable cascade and last-owner protection on disable. The grant (E42-T08) and role-change (E42-T09) routes that the grant self-assignment and concurrent role-escalation cases exercise moved out of E42-T04 in the R2 split on #965 and sit in Sprint 19. They are not in `blocked_by` because this Task is in Sprint 16 (adding them fails SPRINT-ORDER), so those cases cannot pass before they land. The re-point and re-sprint decision is item 4 of #2710.

title: Document profile and trade-group semantics and amend ADR-0008 with the shipped model
body:
## Context
E28 defines two contracts that five other epics consume: the per-account profile (E30 ticket, E34 fan-out, E35 rules, E39 risk caps, E41 journal attribution) and the trade group (E34, E41, E42). If the shipped behaviour drifts from `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9 and ADR-0008 without the documents being updated, those epics will be built against a fiction. The Epic DoD requires exactly this: "Docs updated: relevant `docs/plan/2x-*` architecture/schema docs ... reflect final shipped behavior (not the original proposal) if they diverged during implementation."

There is also an operator-facing gap: nothing today explains to the owner how to choose a sizing rule, what a cap actually does at 00:00 UTC, what "2 of 3 ready" means, or how to recover a group whose membership is wrong. That is a runbook, not a docstring.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Amend `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md` with a "Shipped model (R3)" section recording: the final `profile_snapshot` contents, the skip-versus-failure taxonomy, the preview/planner sharing decision, and the mixed-environment guard. Record any deviation from the original decision explicitly, with the reason.
- Amend `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` SS9.2 and SS9.3 where the implementation diverged (field names, defaults, the percent-versus-fraction convention, the `LegSizing` outcome type) - one PR, reviewed by the Architect.
- Amend `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4/SS3.3.2/SS3.3.3 if any column, constraint or index differs from the shipped migration.
- Write `docs/runbooks/profiles-and-trade-groups.md` covering: choosing a sizing rule with a worked example per mode; what each risk cap measures and when it resets; the reduce-only exemption matrix; readiness states and how to clear each one; how to fix a group with a wrong or mixed-environment membership; how to read a `profile.updated` audit diff; and what to do when a cap fires unexpectedly.
- Record ADR-0016 (from E28-K01) in the ADR index `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md`.
- Update `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` if any US-PROF story's screen or component list changed during implementation.
- A short "profiles for consumers" section in the backend package README naming the three entry points other epics may call (`get_effective_profile`, `size_leg`, `guard.check`) and stating that no consumer may re-derive size or re-implement a cap.

## Out of scope
User-facing help text inside the app (owned by the design tickets and the consuming stories); the security documentation set (E28-X01/X02).

## Acceptance criteria
- ADR-0008 carries a dated "Shipped model (R3)" section, reviewed by the Architect and the Backend lead; every deviation from the original decision is listed with a reason, or the section states explicitly that there were none.
- `24-internal-schemas.md` SS9 and `21-database-schema.md` SS3.2.4/SS3.3.x match the merged code and migrations; a reviewer can diff them against the source without finding a discrepancy.
- The runbook exists, is linked from `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`'s R3 checklist, and a reviewer who did not build the feature can follow it end to end to change a cap and verify the audit entry.
- ADR-0016 appears in the ADR index.
- The consumer README section names the three entry points and the no-re-derivation rule.

## Technical notes / design
Documentation follows the code, not the plan: where the two disagree the code wins and the document is corrected, unless the divergence is a defect - in which case a Bug is filed instead of a doc edit, and this ticket records the Bug id. That distinction is made explicitly for every divergence found, so a shortcut can never be laundered into the spec.

## Test plan
Docs lint (markdownlint, link checker) green in CI. A reviewer walk-through of the runbook is recorded as a comment. Any code snippet in the runbook is executed once against staging to prove it works.

## Security notes
The runbook must not contain any real API key, UID, account label or Tailscale address; it uses placeholders throughout, checked by the secrets scanner over the docs tree. Audit-diff examples are synthetic. Data classification of the document: Internal.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - documentation. Markdown headings are hierarchical and tables carry header rows so the docs site renders accessibly.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A - but the runbook lists the exact metric and audit-event names E28 emits, so an operator can find them without reading code.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.

title: Ship the reconciliation UX: desync banner, stale-account lockout and the while-you-were-away report
body:
## Context
US-POS-008 (Must) - "I want continuous reconciliation between local state and Bybit, so that the app never lies about my book." E29-T06 builds the reconciliation loop; this story makes its results legible and safe: the SCR-152 reconnecting/desync treatment, the per-account stale lockout that disables order entry, and the explicit "while you were offline: 1 order filled, 1 stop moved by a rule" report SCR-152 specifies. Without it, a correct backend still leaves the user acting on a screen they cannot trust.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-008** (UI half; the algorithm is E29-T06); screens **SCR-152** (disconnected / reconnecting / gap-filling / restored variants) and the SCR-063 "reconciling" and "desync warning" states.
- Components: **CMP-028** Callout/Banner, **CMP-035** Countdown, **CMP-076** ConnectionStatus, **CMP-077** ReconnectOverlay, **CMP-078** StaleDataShade.
- Banner states with distinct copy: connected / reconnecting (attempt N, next in M s) / gap-filling / reconciling / desync ("Position data is being verified - actions temporarily limited") / account-stale (order entry disabled for the named accounts).
- The reassurance line "Your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected" rendered **only when it is true**, i.e. when the native-SL invariant check passed for every open position on the affected accounts.
- A "while you were away" summary built from the `ReconcileReport` (`corrected`, `resolved_from_history`, `newly_unknown`, `untracked`, `position_drift`, `sl_repaired`), each entry deep-linking to the affected row.
- Hard-disabling of trading controls while private feeds are down, with refused attempts recorded as `order.blocked_offline`.
- Per-panel stale shading showing each panel's last-good timestamp.

## Out of scope
The reconciliation algorithm, its metrics and its alerts (E29-T06/T08); the kill-switch (E39); degraded-mode variants for recorder, rule engine or GPU fallback (SCR-153, other epics); the admin System health -> OMS screen (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reconnect with a correction
  Given the private WS was down for 60 seconds and one order filled while offline
  When the connection is restored and reconciliation completes
  Then a "while you were away" summary lists the fill with a link to the affected row
  And the blotter shows the corrected state within 30 seconds of reconnect

Scenario: Trading is blocked while blind
  Given private feeds are down
  Then every trading control is disabled with the reason shown in text
  And an attempted submission is refused client-side and recorded as order.blocked_offline

Scenario: Repeated reconciliation failure
  Given REST reconciliation fails repeatedly for 2 minutes for account A
  Then account A is marked stale, its rows are shaded with their last-good timestamp, and order entry for it is disabled while other accounts remain usable

Scenario: The reassurance must be true
  Given an open position was found without a native stop-loss during reconciliation
  Then the "your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected" line is not shown
  And the repaired-stop entry appears in the summary instead

Scenario: The overlay never hides the book
  Then the reconnect overlay never fully obscures the positions grid
```

## Technical notes / design
The banner is driven by one `connectionState` machine (`connected -> reconnecting -> gap_filling -> reconciling -> {connected, degraded_stale}`) fed by the WS client and by `system` / `ReconcileReport` frames, rather than by ad-hoc booleans scattered through panels. The backoff display mirrors the client's actual schedule (1, 2, 4, 8 s capped at 30 s, jittered). The stale flag is per exchange account, so one impaired account does not disable the whole app. The summary is built from the server's `ReconcileReport` payload so the client never infers corrections by diffing its own cache.

## Test plan
Unit: connection-state machine transitions including flapping; summary builder for each `ReconcileReport` field; the truth-gate on the reassurance line. Integration: scripted WS drop and restore with a report containing corrections, untracked adoptions and an `sl_repaired` entry. E2E/chaos (feeds E29-Q04): kill the WS mid-session, assert controls disable, restore, assert the summary and the corrected rows. A11y: axe plus a screen-reader pass on the banner's single-announcement behaviour. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This is a safety surface: showing "connected", or the stop-loss reassurance, when it is not true is a security-relevant misrepresentation (integrity/repudiation), so the reassurance line is gated on the invariant check rather than on connection state alone. Client-side disabling is UX only - the server independently refuses orders from stale accounts, asserted in E29-X02. `order.blocked_offline` is recorded for forensic reconstruction.

## Accessibility notes
`role="alert"` fires once on entering a state and the banner then persists as a static region - the countdown is **not** announced on every tick (SCR-152 a11y rule); disabled controls expose `aria-disabled` with a programmatically associated reason; stale panels carry a visible, readable last-good timestamp; the summary is a keyboard-navigable list of plain sentences, each item linking to its row.

## Performance notes
Target time-to-usable after a 30 s outage is <=5 s (SCR-152): subscriptions restore in priority order - private account state first, then the focused panel, then the rest - and a gap-fill request closes the missed window.

## Observability
Analytics and incident events `ws.disconnected{reason,subscriptions}`, `ws.reconnect_attempt{attempt}`, `ws.reconnected{outageMs,gapFilled}`, `order.blocked_offline`. Client gauge `account_stale{account}` mirrored to the admin health screen.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).
- [ ] Coverage: touched backend/OMS packages ≥90% line (local R3 policy for OMS/risk modules, `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4), frontend ≥80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` / `21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] Security: SAST (Bandit/Semgrep/CodeQL) + SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (mandatory — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, order-placement path).
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo) — never live.
- [ ] PR(s) merged through the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; PR ≤400 LOC diff preferred.

- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched screen(s); keyboard-only path verified; manual screen-reader spot-check recorded (`05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the E29-D06 handoff pack; discrepancies fixed or filed with a `priority/*`.

title: Build SCR-060 order ticket with entry types and all order flags
body:
## Context
US-ORD-001 (Must) and US-ORD-002 (Must) are the heart of the product's execution loop: "a fast order ticket with type, side, size, price and target accounts, so that I can submit precisely" and "market, limit, stop, stop-limit and conditional orders with TIF, reduce-only, post-only and close-on-trigger, so that I can express any intent".

This Story builds the **SCR-060 Order ticket panel (single account)** shell and its order-type/flag surface, composing the design-system trading components onto `packages/order-ticket-core` (E30-T01). Sizing modes are E30-S02/S03, arm/confirm is E30-S04, the preview and group selector are E30-S06 â€” this Story ships the panel, the type/side/price fields, the flags, and the submit path with a fixed quantity.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-001, US-ORD-002.** Screen **SCR-060**.
- `apps/web/src/features/order-ticket/OrderTicketPanel.tsx` composing **CMP-107 OrderTicket** from **CMP-102 SideToggle**, **CMP-103 OrderTypeTabs** (Market / Limit / Conditional; emulated types rendered with the visible "(emulated)" badge but disabled until E33), **CMP-100 PriceInput** (tick-aware, with the "(rounded to nearest tick)" caption), **CMP-101 QtyInput** in `qty` mode, **CMP-231 TifSelect** (GTC/IOC/FOK/PostOnly with per-order-type availability and a stated reason when unavailable), **CMP-119 BracketEditor**, **CMP-232 LimitsChip**, **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal**.
- Flags: `reduce_only`, `post_only` (via TIF `PostOnly`), `close_on_trigger`; conditional orders with `trigger.price`, `trigger_by` (`LastPrice`/`MarkPrice`/`IndexPrice`) and `direction` (`rise`/`fall`).
- Price helpers: `Alt+B`/`Alt+A` snap to bid/ask, `Alt+M` mid, sourced from WS `ticker.{symbol}` (`23-ws-protocol.md` Â§14.8).
- Data wiring: `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` (tick, lot, min notional, leverage), `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts/{accountId}/profiles`, WS `wallet.{accountId}`, WS `ticker.{symbol}`; submit `POST /api/v1/orders`; terminal state from WS `orders.{accountId}` / `executions.{accountId}`.
- All SCR-060 states: ready Â· validating Â· submitting (button becomes a progress state, duplicate submits blocked) Â· accepted Â· rejected (inline, with the exchange code and the plain-language explanation) Â· blocked-by-profile Â· blocked-by-lockout Â· frozen Â· disconnected Â· pending-key.
- Storybook stories for every state and every order type; `CMP-107` Storybook entries Market, Limit, Conditional, Rejected, RateLimited.

## Out of scope
Sizing modes beyond explicit qty (E30-S02/S03), arm/lock and the confirmation modal (E30-S04), hotkeys (E30-S05), risk preview and the account/group selector (E30-S06), templates and trading defaults (E30-S07), the rejection drawer and rate-limited banner (E30-T02), chart/DOM entry (E31).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Limit order (US-ORD-001)
  Given BTCUSDT, account "Main", one-click disarmed, demo environment
  When I enter a limit buy of 0.1 at 63000 with the profile's stop attached and confirm
  Then the order is validated client-side, POST /api/v1/orders returns 202
  And an acknowledgement carrying the exchange order id appears within 500 ms
Scenario: Validation failure before any exchange call (US-ORD-001)
  Given a quantity of 0.0004 on an instrument whose minimum is 0.001
  When I press submit
  Then submission is blocked before any network call with the field-level message "Minimum 0.001, step 0.001."
  And the message names the constraint and the field is focusable from the error summary
Scenario: Conditional order (US-ORD-002)
  When I set trigger price 63400, trigger source Mark and direction rise
  Then the conditional order is created and displayed as untriggered with its trigger conditions restated
Scenario: Post-only rejection (US-ORD-002)
  Given time-in-force PostOnly and a limit price that would cross the spread
  Then the client warns before sending, and if the exchange still rejects, the rejection is shown verbatim with a "reprice" suggestion and my inputs are retained
Scenario: Reduce-only guard (US-ORD-002)
  Given no open position on the selected account and symbol
  When I check reduce-only
  Then submission is blocked client-side with "Reduce-only needs an open position." and the request is never issued
Scenario: Exchange rejection retains context (US-ORD-001)
  Given the exchange rejects the order with retCode 110007
  Then the ticket shows the exchange message and code, keeps every input, and the attempt is journaled and audited as order.rejected
```

## Technical notes / design
All validation and request building come from `packages/order-ticket-core` â€” this Story contains **no** arithmetic and no copy strings of its own. Components are pure and driven by a single `useSyncExternalStore` ticket store (or the worker placement, per E30-K01/ADR), so a WS `ticker` update at 100 ms cadence never re-renders the whole panel.

Submit is optimistic: on `202` the panel enters `accepted` with the returned one-leg `TradeGroup`, then reconciles against `orders.{accountId}`; if no matching event arrives within `CV_TICKET_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 000 ms) the state becomes "Awaiting exchange confirmation â€” reconciling" rather than a false "filled". Duplicate submits are blocked by disabling the button *and* by the idempotency key, not by the button alone.

Emulated order types appear in CMP-103 with the "(emulated)" badge per the safety-transparency rule but are `disabled` with `disabledReason="Available from the algo builders (coming in E33)"` â€” never silently absent.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: state machine of the panel (readyâ†’validatingâ†’submittingâ†’accepted/rejected); flag availability matrix per order type; trigger-field visibility; price-helper snapping; duplicate-submit suppression.
- **Contract**: the emitted `PlaceOrderRequest` validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` for market, limit, conditional and each flag combination.
- **Integration**: against a recorded demo fixture set â€” accepted, rejected (`110007` post-only would cross), `422` native_stop_required, `403` account scope.
- **E2E (Playwright, demo)**: keyboard-only limit order placement end to end; covered in E30-Q02.
- **Visual + axe**: every Storybook state.
- Coverage target â‰¥80% frontend.

## Security notes
The account id used on submit is taken from the selector state but is **always** re-authorised server-side (`x-rbac: orders:write, scope: granted_accounts`); a Viewer sees the panel read-only with a lock notice and no submit affordance exists in the DOM at all (not merely disabled). Rejection display uses the mapped presentation from `order-ticket-core`; raw request payloads are only ever shown through `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics` (E30-T02), which is redacted and audited on read.

## Accessibility notes
The panel is a `<form>` with a `<fieldset>` per section (side/type, price, quantity, brackets, flags). The submit button's accessible name restates the full intent: "Submit buy 0.25 BTCUSDT limit 64 010 with stop 63 900". Errors are summarised at the top of the form with links to the offending fields (`05-accessibility-standard.md`). The tick-rounding caption is `aria-live="polite"`. Unavailable TIF options are disabled **with a stated reason**. Buy/sell are labelled "Buy / Long" and "Sell / Short" in words, never colour alone. Full keyboard path verified: tab order, `Ctrl+Enter` submit, `Esc` clear.

## Performance notes
Every input recalculates risk/fee/margin in â‰¤8 ms (SCR-060). Client contribution to budget #4 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§5.2, p95 <300 ms demo) â‰¤20 ms from gesture to request dispatch. WS `ticker` updates must not cause a full-panel re-render â€” asserted by a render-count test.

## Observability
Audit `orders.submit` `{account, source: "ticket", environment}`; `order.rejected` with the exchange code. Analytics `ticket.sizing_rule_used`. Metric `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms{env}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six Gherkin scenarios pass by automated test (unit/contract/integration) or a recorded QA step with an automation follow-up filed.

- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review; feature flag `ff_order_ticket` recorded (demo on, live off).

title: Add sizing modes and the quantity preset ladder to the ticket
body:
## Context
US-ORD-003 (Must): "configurable size presets on buttons and number keys, so that sizing is one keystroke". The roadmap scope for this Epic requires "qty by contracts, notional, % equity, or risk-based from the SL distance" â€” this Story ships the first three modes plus the preset ladder; risk-based sizing has its own Story (E30-S03) because it couples to the stop and to the mandatory-SL invariant.

Presets are per symbol-class and per account profile, and the number-key mapping is remappable (US-ORD-003 NFR), which is why the binding lives in `hotkey_profiles` rather than in component state.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-003.** Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-114** (the preset ladder definition lives in Trading defaults; the editing UI itself is E30-S07 â€” this Story consumes the stored ladder).
- **CMP-101 QtyInput** wired in all of `qty`, `pctEquity` and `fixedUsd` modes, each rendering the derived quantity read-only alongside the input so the resolved size is *always* visible before submission.
- **CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons**: the preset ladder (e.g. 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5 BTC), active-preset highlighting, number-key activation `1..4` bound through the active `hotkey_profiles` row, and percent-defined presets resolving to a concrete quantity shown next to the button.
- Disabled presets: a preset resolving below the instrument minimum renders disabled with the minimum stated in its accessible name and in visible text.
- Sizing-mode switch via **CMP-003 SegmentedControl** with `aria-describedby` explaining the active formula; the mode persists per symbol-class in user settings (`GET|PUT /api/v1/settings`).
- Clamp reporting: when `Â§9.3.2` clamps reduce the size, the reduction and its cause are shown inline ("reduced from 1.2 to 0.8 by max_position_notional").

## Out of scope
Risk-based sizing and the stop coupling (E30-S03); editing the preset ladder and defaults (E30-S07); the hotkey editor screen SCR-113 (E30-S05 wires the trading rows, E13/settings owns the screen); server-side sizing (E28 Â§9.3).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preset applied (US-ORD-003)
  Given presets 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5 BTC on BTCUSDT
  When I press the number key bound to the second preset
  Then the ticket quantity becomes 0.1 and that preset is highlighted as active
Scenario: Percent presets resolve visibly (US-ORD-003)
  Given a preset defined as 5% of equity and an account equity of 20 000 USDT
  Then the resolved quantity is displayed next to the preset before I submit anything
Scenario: Preset invalid for the symbol (US-ORD-003)
  Given a preset that resolves below the instrument minimum quantity
  Then the preset is shown disabled and states the minimum, and pressing its number key does nothing
Scenario: Notional mode
  Given sizing mode "fixed notional" and 25 000 USDT with a mark price of 64 000
  Then the derived quantity is shown rounded down to the lot step, with the rounding stated
Scenario: Stale equity blocks equity-derived modes
  Given the wallet snapshot for the account is older than 2 s and cannot be refreshed
  Then % equity presets and % equity mode are disabled with "Account balance is stale" and fixed-qty sizing still works
```

## Technical notes / design
Derivation runs entirely in `packages/order-ticket-core.size()`; this Story only renders `SizingResult` (`qty`, `appliedClamps`, `warnings`). Equity comes from the WS `wallet.{accountId}` topic (`23-ws-protocol.md` Â§15.4) with a 2 s freshness rule matching `24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.4 rule 2; staleness disables the equity-dependent modes rather than silently sizing from an old balance.

Number-key bindings resolve through the active hotkey profile (`hotkey_profiles.bindings`, `21-database-schema.md` Â§3.8.5) and are suppressed while focus is in a text field (the same suppression rule as E30-S05).

Presets are stored per symbol-class (linear perp USDT) so that a BTC ladder does not leak onto a 1000PEPE ticket; a symbol with no class-specific ladder falls back to the profile's default sizing rule rather than to an empty ladder.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: each sizing mode's rendering of the derived value; preset resolution incl. percent presets; disabled-preset condition; number-key activation and its suppression in text fields; stale-equity gating; clamp message rendering.
- **Integration**: wallet WS update mid-edit recomputes the derived quantity without resetting the user's typed input.
- **E2E**: preset â†’ submit path (in E30-Q02).
- **axe + visual** on every QtyInput/QuickSizeButtons Storybook state.

## Security notes
Presets are per user and contain no secrets. A preset can never exceed the account profile's caps â€” the clamp chain applies to preset-derived sizes exactly as to typed ones, so a stale or tampered local preset store cannot enlarge a position beyond the owner's policy (and the server clamps again regardless).

## Accessibility notes
Each preset button's accessible name states the resolved quantity, not just the label ("0.1 BTC, 5 percent of equity"); disabled presets state why. The sizing-mode segmented control describes the active formula via `aria-describedby`. Every numeric field states its unit. The derived quantity is in an `aria-live="polite"` region so a screen-reader user hears the resolved size change when they switch mode or press a preset.

## Performance notes
Preset activation â†’ updated derived quantity within the 8 ms recompute budget (SCR-060). Number-key activation shares the 50 ms hotkey budget path measured in E30-K01.

## Observability
Analytics `ticket.sizing_rule_used` `{mode, presetIndex?}`; `ticket.preset_disabled_shown` `{reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five scenarios pass by automated test.
- [ ] Coverage â‰¥80%; Storybook states complete for CMP-101 and CMP-122.
- [ ] axe green; manual screen-reader check on preset announcement.
- [ ] Recompute budget re-measured with presets active.
- [ ] design-qa against the E30-D06 pack; QA sign-off recorded.

title: Build the SCR-077 rejection drawer and the SCR-158 rate-limited ticket state
body:
## Context
Every rejection the user cannot understand is a trade they will re-attempt blindly. SCR-077 exists so that "why did my order do that" has exactly one answer surface: the exchange's verbatim `retCode`/`retMsg`, a plain-language translation, what CandleViewer actually sent (redacted), and a retry-with-corrections path. SCR-158 covers the specific case where nothing was sent at all because the per-UID rate budget was exhausted (Bybit code `10018`).

Both are consumed by the ticket but are separately testable presentation surfaces, which is why they are a Task rather than folded into E30-S01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screens **SCR-077** (order rejection detail drawer), **SCR-158** (rate-limited state). Components **CMP-046 Drawer**, **CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock**, **CMP-021 Link**, **CMP-023 Progress Bar**, **CMP-028 Callout/Banner**, **CMP-035 Countdown**, **CMP-069 InfoPanel**.
- Data: `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics` (`OrderDiagnostics` â€” ordered `order_events` chain plus redacted exchange request/response pairs and the reconciliation verdict), lazily fetched only when the user expands the raw payload.
- Written plain-language copy for each common rejection: insufficient margin, reduce-only violation, tick/lot rounding, leverage limit, risk-limit tier, rate limit, position-mode mismatch, post-only would-cross, `native_stop_required`, `trading_disabled` (kill-switch), account scope denied.
- "Retry with corrections" that pre-fills a corrected ticket **only where the fix is unambiguous** (tick/lot rounding, reduce-only off, reprice off the spread) â€” never for margin or risk-cap rejections, where the correct action is a human decision.
- SCR-158: per-scope variants (exchange per-UID, backend per-user, fan-out budget), the retry-after countdown as absolute and relative time, which actions are **held** versus dropped, which accounts were served in a fan-out, and a link to SCR-147.
- Held-action queue: user actions refused for rate-limit reasons are held, not dropped, and are replayed only after an explicit confirmation â€” never silently.

## Out of scope
The rate-limit governor itself (E34); the audit-log browser linked from the drawer (E42); backend diagnostics assembly (E29); SCR-147 (admin rate-limit screen, E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A rejection is explained, not just reported
  Given the exchange rejects an order with retCode 110007
  When the rejection drawer opens
  Then the verbatim exchange message is shown as quoted text with a plain-language translation beneath it
  And the correlation id is selectable and the raw payload is available on explicit expansion only
Scenario: Retry with corrections only where unambiguous
  Given a tick-size rounding rejection
  Then a "retry with corrections" action pre-fills a corrected ticket and the correction is stated
  And for an insufficient-margin rejection no auto-correction is offered
Scenario: Nothing secret is ever rendered
  Given the raw payload is expanded
  Then no API key, signature, token or KEK-derived value appears, and the redaction is asserted by test
Scenario: Rate-limited state holds rather than drops
  Given the per-UID budget is exhausted for an account
  Then SCR-158 names the throttled scope, the retry-after time as absolute and relative values, and what is still permitted
  And queued actions are held and replayed only after explicit confirmation
Scenario: Fan-out partial rate-limiting names the accounts
  Given three of five accounts were served and two were starved
  Then the banner names which accounts were served and which were not, and links to the group's reconciliation state
```

## Technical notes / design
Drawer opens from already-received rejection data â€” no fetch in the common case (SCR-077 performance note); `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics` is fetched lazily on expansion and is **audited on read**, so the fetch must not be speculative or prefetched.

Error copy is co-located with the code map in `order-ticket-core/errors.ts` so the inline message, the drawer translation and the toast can never diverge. An exhaustiveness test fails when a new backend error code has no copy.

Countdown announcements are throttled to at most one per 10 s (SCR-158 a11y note) while the visual countdown ticks every second.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥85% on the copy/mapping module, â‰¥80% on the components)**: one case per documented rejection reason asserting code â†’ translation â†’ correction availability; redaction assertion against a payload seeded with key-shaped and signature-shaped strings; held-queue replay requiring confirmation; countdown throttling.
- **Contract**: `OrderDiagnostics` parsed per `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **Integration**: a `429` response drives SCR-158; a `502` exchange error drives SCR-077.
- **axe**: `role="alert"` on drawer open, `role="status"` on the rate-limit banner, quoted-text semantics.

## Security notes
The diagnostics endpoint is the **only** place raw exchange retCode/retMsg and request/response pairs are exposed, it is redacted server-side, and reading it is audited. The client must not log the payload to the console or to any client-side telemetry sink. A test seeds credential-shaped strings into a fixture payload and asserts none reach the DOM or any analytics call.

## Accessibility notes
The drawer announces itself with `role="alert"` on open. The verbatim exchange message is marked up as quoted text with the plain-language translation as adjacent prose, so a screen reader distinguishes the two voices. The correlation id and the raw payload are selectable text, not images. SCR-158 is a `role="status"` region naming the throttled capability and stating what the user can still do; countdown announcements are throttled to at most one per 10 s.

## Performance notes
Drawer opens from in-memory state in â‰¤100 ms with no network call; the raw payload fetch is lazy and does not block the drawer. The rate-limit client honours the server's `Retry-After` and issues no further requests to the throttled scope until it expires.

## Observability
Analytics `order.rejection_viewed`, `order.rejection_payload_expanded`, `order.rejection_retried`, `ratelimit.hit{scope, endpointClass, retryAfterMs}`. Audit `order.blocked_ratelimited`; the diagnostics read is audited server-side.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five scenarios pass by automated test; the redaction test is a required check.
- [ ] Copy written and reviewed for every documented rejection reason; exhaustiveness test green.
- [ ] Coverage thresholds met; Storybook for each rejection reason and each SCR-158 scope variant.
- [ ] axe green; manual screen-reader pass on drawer announcement and countdown.
- [ ] Security engineer confirms the redaction and the no-client-logging rule.
- [ ] QA sign-off; design-qa against E30-D06; merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E30-S01** â€” the ticket state machine that raises these surfaces.
- **E29** â€” `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics` and the backend error taxonomy.

## Branch
`feat/e30-rejection-and-ratelimit` Â· one PR.

title: Chart & DOM trading interactions
body:
## Context
R3 closes the execution loop. E29 gives the OMS and its state machine, E30 gives the order ticket, E21 gives the readable DOM ladder, E32 gives brackets and the native-SL invariant. **E31 is the direct-manipulation layer on top of all of them**: trading *where you analyse* — on the chart price axis and on the DOM ladder rows — instead of retyping into a ticket.

Per `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 the epic delivers: draggable order and position lines with drag-to-amend and snap-to-tick, drag SL/TP from the position tool, click-to-trade on the ladder, one-click flatten and reverse with a configurable confirmation policy, overlays that never degrade under the frame-budget shedding ladder, and an undo window for accidental drags.

Every path added here is an order-placing path, so it inherits the R3 safety rules verbatim: arm/lock gating (US-ORD-005 / CMP-229), the native exchange-side stop-loss invariant (US-ORD-013, enforced server-side by E32/M17 — **this epic never bypasses it**), risk caps and kill-switch (E39), and full auditing of every click/drag with the price row and modifier used.

## Scope
**User stories (all of the chart/DOM direct-manipulation half of domain ORD, plus the two DOM trading stories):**
- US-ORD-007 Order from chart (Must)
- US-ORD-008 Drag order, stop and target lines (Must)
- US-ORD-009 Cancel order from chart and DOM (Should)
- US-ORD-010 Flatten and cancel-all (Must)
- US-ORD-011 Reverse position (Should)
- US-DOM-007 Click-to-trade from the DOM (Should)
- US-DOM-008 Drag to modify from the DOM (Should)

**Screens:** SCR-030 (chart panel trading layer), SCR-040 (chart trading overlay settings), SCR-050 (ladder trading affordances), SCR-063 (flatten entry points), SCR-064 (position SL/TP editor as the keyboard alternative), SCR-072 (flatten/cancel-all confirmation), SCR-076 (order confirmation modal), SCR-077 (rejection drawer reuse).

**Components:** CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker, CMP-119 BracketEditor, CMP-120 TrailingStopEditor, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge.

**Backend/API consumed (not created here):** `POST /api/v1/orders`, `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all`, `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close`, `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/reverse`, `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`, `POST /api/v1/positions/close-all`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`; WS `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`. Module **M14** (OMS) gains a thin *chart-trading intent* facade and audit-event enrichment only.

## Out of scope
- The order ticket form itself, sizing rules, hotkey infrastructure (E30).
- OMS state machine, reconciliation, blotters (E29).
- Bracket objects, scaled ladders, native-SL enforcement logic (E32).
- Emulated algos (E33), fan-out governor (E34), rule engine (E35–E37).
- DOM ladder rendering, heatmap, depth tiers (E21) — this epic only adds the trading affordances on top.
- Android; separate admin app; non-Bybit venues; non-USDT-perp instruments.

## Exit criteria
1. Every one of the seven user stories has its Gherkin scenarios passing in CI (unit + E2E), including the failure scenarios (amend rejected, drop on wrong side, already-filled cancel, nothing to flatten, insufficient margin on reverse).
2. **Safety:** an automated suite proves no chart drag, chart click, DOM click or DOM drag can open a position without a native exchange-side SL, and none is operable while disarmed, locked-out or kill-switched. Zero escapes (R3 exit criterion 2).
3. **Latency:** chart/DOM click → submit ≤50 ms client-side p95; click → ack p95 <300 ms on demo (budget #4); amend round trip ≤500 ms p95.
4. **Frame budget:** with 20 order/position lines plus a live ladder, the trading overlay layer redraws in ≤2 ms and order-line/position updates are *never* shed (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 "never acceptable" list) — proven by a benchmark under the stress scenario.
5. **A11y:** every drag has a verified keyboard equivalent (focus line → arrow keys by tick → Enter to commit; ladder row → Enter → row action menu), announced pending/confirmed/rejected states, ≥24 px targets, no colour-only side encoding.
6. Undo window works: an accidental drag or click-trade can be reverted inside the configured window, with the revert itself audited.
7. Design QA, a11y audit, QA sign-off and Security sign-off all recorded; coverage ≥85 % on touched backend/engine packages, ≥80 % frontend.

## Risks
- **R2 Render performance** — trading overlays share the chart frame with footprint + heatmap; mitigated by a dedicated overlay layer with its own budget and by the "never shed trading data" rule.
- **R11 Alert reliability / mis-execution** — optimistic UI showing an amend that never landed; mitigated by pending states reconciled against exchange truth within 1 s and by spring-back on reject.
- **R5 Scope** — drag semantics can grow without bound; the undo window and modifier map are frozen by design sign-off before build.
- Fat-finger risk is the headline abuse case: covered by arm gating, confirm policy, notional thresholds and the undo window (E31-X02).

## Dependency graph
```
E11 chart engine (R1)          ─┐
E21 DOM ladder (R2)            ─┼─> E31-K01 spike (S16, render/input only, submits nothing)
E29 OMS + private WS (ends S16)─┼─> E31-T01 intent layer (S17) ─> E31-S01, E31-S04 (S17)
E39 risk caps/kill-switch(S16) ─┘
E30 order ticket (ends S17)    ─┬─> E31-S02, S03, S05, S06 (S18, strictly after)
E32 native-SL invariant (S17)  ─┘
```

**Sequencing rule applied throughout this epic: no E31 ticket is scheduled in the same sprint in which one of its blockers completes.**

| E31 tickets | Sprint | Heaviest blocker | Blocker completes | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D01 | 14 | E21 | R2 | design-ahead, 3 sprints |
| D02, D03 | 15 | E31-D01 | end S14 | design-ahead, 2 sprints |
| K01 | 16 | E11, E21 | R1 / R2 | ≥1 train |
| T01, S01, S04, Q01, X01 | 17 | E29, E39 | end S16 | starts the following sprint |
| S02, S03, S05, S06, D07, Q02, X02, T02 | 18 | E30, E32 | end S17 | starts the following sprint |

The S17 cohort deliberately carries **only** work whose blockers closed in S16; everything needing E30's arm/lock and confirmation policy or E32's native-SL invariant is deferred to S18. **E31-K01 is pulled forward to S16** (a render/input experiment on recorded data — no OMS, no API keys, submits nothing) so the latency and hit-testing unknowns are closed before the train opens; that pull-forward is the epic's schedule slack. **E31-X01 moved from S16 to S17** for the same reason — it previously ran concurrently with E29's and E39's completion sprint instead of after it.

**Design track (design-ahead, `00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).** E31-D01 Done end of **S14**; E31-D02 — which carries *all* design-system contributions, the motion spec and the a11y design review — Done end of **S15**; E31-D03 handoff Done end of **S15**. That is two to three sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story (S17). **E31-D07 is a post-build design-QA audit only**, contributes no design-system entries, and therefore does not violate the design-ahead rule by sitting in S18.

## Story list
Children sum to **26 points**, mirroring `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2.

| Key | Kind | Title | Pts | Sprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E31-D01 | Task | UX research and hi-fi design for the chart trading layer (SCR-030, SCR-040) | 2 | 14 |
| E31-D02 | Task | Hi-fi DOM trading, design-system, motion spec and a11y review | 2 | 15 |
| E31-D03 | Task | Design handoff package for chart and DOM trading | 1 | 15 |
| E31-K01 | Spike | Prove drag latency, overlay hit-testing and the trading-layer frame budget | 1 | 16 |
| E31-T01 | Task | Chart/DOM trading intent layer: guards, optimistic state, undo window and audit | 2 | 17 |
| E31-S01 | Story | Place an order by clicking a price on the chart | 2 | 17 |
| E31-S04 | Story | Click-to-trade on the DOM ladder | 2 | 17 |
| E31-Q01 | Task | Test plan and E2E suite for chart and DOM trading | 1 | 17 |
| E31-X01 | Task | STRIDE threat model for chart and DOM trading interactions | 1 | 17 |
| E31-S02 | Story | Drag order, stop and target lines on the chart to amend | 3 | 18 |
| E31-S03 | Story | Cancel orders from the chart and the DOM ladder | 1 | 18 |
| E31-S05 | Story | Drag an order marker on the ladder to reprice it | 1 | 18 |
| E31-S06 | Story | One-click flatten, cancel-all and reverse with the confirmation policy | 2 | 18 |
| E31-D07 | Task | Design QA of shipped chart and DOM trading | 1 | 18 |
| E31-Q02 | Task | Perf, chaos and a11y audit plus QA sign-off | 2 | 18 |
| E31-X02 | Task | Abuse cases, RBAC/arm bypass checks and security sign-off | 1 | 18 |
| E31-T02 | Chore | Reconcile plan docs with the shipped chart and DOM trading behaviour | 1 | 18 |
| **Total** | | | **26** | |

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The whole direct-manipulation loop works on demo
  Given an armed chart and ladder on BTCUSDT with a demo account selected
  When I Shift+click a price to place a limit, drag its line to reprice, drag the SL, then flatten
  Then each action is acknowledged by the exchange, mirrored by the WS orders/positions topics,
  audited with the modifier and price used, and the position never exists without a native stop

Scenario: Nothing is operable when it must not be
  Given one-click is disarmed, or the kill-switch is engaged, or a risk lockout is active
  Then no chart click, chart drag, ladder click or ladder drag can submit anything,
  and each attempt shows the reason and is logged

Scenario: Overlays hold under load
  Given 100k bars, footprint on, a 200-depth heatmap and 20 working order lines
  Then the shedding ladder degrades heatmap cadence and footprint text first,
  order and position lines keep updating every frame, and fps stays above 30
```

## Technical notes / design
The frontend never talks to Bybit. All actions go through the existing REST endpoints and are confirmed by the private WS topics, which remain the source of truth (ADR-0006). Optimistic UI is allowed only as a *pending* visual state that must reconcile within 1 s or spring back.

**Sizing note.** `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 fixes E31 at **26 points**; the epic ticket estimate mirrors that rollup exactly and every child is sized against it (children sum to 26). The earlier draft sized this epic at 82 points by splitting the design, QA and security tracks into one ticket per activity; those tracks have been consolidated (D01+D02, D03+D04+D05, Q01+Q02, Q03+Q04+Q05+Q06, X02+X03) with no loss of scope — every deliverable, acceptance criterion and sign-off from the merged tickets is preserved in the surviving ticket bodies. Work that would push the epic past its 26-point budget is merged into a sibling or explicitly deferred, never silently re-sized.

## Test plan
Rolls up the child test plans; epic-level gates are the R3 §7.4 rows for Safety (native-SL suite as a required check), E2E (chart trading, DOM trading), A11y (ladder keyboard-operable) and Design (D-tickets Done ≥2 sprints ahead).

## Security notes
All child tickets touch `area/oms-execution` order placement, therefore are `security`-labelled for DoD purposes per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 whether or not the label was applied at creation.

## Accessibility notes
No drag-only affordance may ship. SCR-064 is the declared keyboard alternative for SL/TP manipulation; CMP-192 lines are DOM-mirrored and focusable; ladder rows are a roving-tabindex grid.

## Performance notes
Budget #4 (order ack) and §4.3 (shedding ladder) are the gates; the trading overlay layer has a ≤2 ms redraw budget per SCR-040.

## Observability
`order.submitted`, `order.amend_requested`, `order.cancel_requested`, `position.flattened`, `position.reversed`, `trading.chart_drag_modify_enabled` audit events; analytics `chart.trade_from_chart`, `dom.click_trade`, `trading.undo_used`; metrics `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms`, `cv_trading_overlay_redraw_ms`, `cv_trading_undo_total`.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 — 100 % child rollup, epic-level AC verified end-to-end on demo, coverage floors, docs updated, a11y verified, perf recorded, STRIDE finalised and signed off, QA epic-level regression pass, demoed to the Owner, retro note.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E29** (OMS + private WS mirror, ends S16), **E39** (risk caps, lockouts, kill-switch, ends S16), **E11** (chart engine interaction/hit-testing, R1), **E21** (ladder surface, R2), **E30** (ticket, arm/lock, hotkeys, confirm policy, ends S17) and **E32** (native-SL invariant + brackets, ends S17).

E11/E21/E29/E39 gate the Sprint-17 cohort; E30/E32 gate the Sprint-18 cohort. See the Dependency graph section for the per-ticket sprint-vs-blocker slack table.

## Branch
`feat/e31-chart-dom-trading` (epic umbrella; children branch as `feat/e31-<short>`). PRs ≤400 LOC.

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-040, SCR-050, SCR-063, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-076, SCR-077

Pick the next ticket for E31 in this order: Spikes (`E31-K*`) first to de-risk unknowns, then design (`D*`) tickets up to the handoff gate, then engineering `T*`/`S*` tickets in `blocked_by` dependency order, running QA (`Q*`) and security (`X*`) tickets in parallel once their prerequisite stories are Done. title: Place an order by clicking a price on the chart
body:
## Context
**US-ORD-007 — Order from chart (Must):** *"As a trader, I want to click a chart price to create an order, so that I trade where I analyse."* This is the first of the direct-manipulation stories and establishes the chart trading layer that S02 (dragging) builds on.

The interaction is modifier-driven on SCR-030's price area; the exact map is frozen by E31-D01 and published in the E31-D06 handoff (the story text and the screens catalogue disagreed before that decision, so **implement the handoff table, not either document's original wording**).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-030 (chart panel — the trading layer), SCR-040 (the settings modal that toggles working-order lines and the arm-state display), SCR-076 (order confirmation modal when the confirm policy requires it), SCR-077 (rejection drawer on failure).
- **Components**: CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay (the placed order's line), CMP-229 ArmToggle (scope `chart`), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge (liquidation line).
- Chart trading layer mount on SCR-030 rendering working orders and the position from the `orders` / `positions` WS topics, filtered to the visible price window; per-account ghost lines when a trade group is the active target.
- Price-area pointer handling producing a `TradeIntent` via `packages/trading-intent` (E31-T01): limit on the correct side, reduce-only stop, and market-at-market per the frozen modifier map, with the price snapped to `tickSize` and the snap surfaced as a tooltip ("Snapped to 0.5 tick").
- Hover preview stating in words what a click will do before it happens.
- Refusal path: an invalid side/price combination is refused inline with an explanation and **nothing is sent** (US-ORD-007 scenario 3).
- Disarmed path: with one-click locked, the click opens a **pre-filled SCR-060 ticket** requiring explicit confirmation, never a submission ("One-click trading is off — press Ctrl+Shift+T to arm").
- SCR-040 wiring for the overlay element toggles this story introduces (working orders, arm-state display, liquidation-estimate line) and the drag-to-modify toggle's *display* (drag itself lands in S02); enabling drag-to-modify on LIVE emits audit `trading.chart_drag_modify_enabled`.
- Keyboard path: focus the price area, move the crosshair with ↑/↓ by tick, and commit an order at the crosshair price with the documented key, subject to the same confirm policy.

## Out of scope
Dragging existing lines (S02). Cancelling from the chart (S03). DOM surfaces (S04/S05). Flatten/reverse (S06). Bracket construction and native-SL attachment logic (E32) — the entry simply carries the profile's SL and the server enforces it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Limit from chart
  Given BTCUSDT on SCR-030, chart trading armed, and a price above the market
  When I use the limit-sell modifier at that price
  Then a limit sell is created at the tick-snapped price with the profile's native stop attached,
  a pending order line appears immediately, and the acknowledgement arrives within 500 ms

Scenario: Stop from chart on a long
  Given an open long position
  When I use the stop modifier at a price below the market
  Then a reduce-only stop order is created at that price and rendered as a stop line

Scenario: Invalid side/price
  Given the chosen price is on the wrong side for the chosen order type
  Then the action is refused with an inline explanation, nothing is sent to the exchange,
  and the refusal is recorded with its reason

Scenario: Disarmed
  Given one-click trading is locked
  When I click a price with a trading modifier
  Then a pre-filled ticket opens requiring explicit confirmation and no order is submitted

Scenario: Kill-switch engaged
  Given the kill-switch is engaged
  Then no chart click can create an order, the reason is shown, and the attempt is logged

Scenario: Exchange rejection
  Given the exchange rejects the order
  Then the pending line disappears, the exact exchange code and message are surfaced,
  the rejection drawer is reachable, and the attempt is journaled and audited

Scenario: Keyboard equivalent
  Given a keyboard user with the chart focused
  When they move the crosshair to a price and press the commit key
  Then the same intent is produced, the same confirm policy applies,
  and the outcome is announced (pending, then acknowledged or rejected)
```

## Technical notes / design
The overlay is a dedicated engine layer above footprint/drawings/indicators and below modals (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §4), with the hit-test strategy chosen in E31-K01/ADR-0017. Lines are DOM-mirrored for a11y and (per the spike's likely finding) the mirror doubles as the hit surface.

Price ↔ pixel conversion uses the shared viewport transform (§3.5); snapping uses the instrument's `priceFilter.tickSize` from the cached `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`.

Order submission goes through E31-T01 only — this story contains no `fetch` of its own.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: modifier→intent mapping for every entry in the frozen table; price↔pixel and snapping at pane edges; hover-preview text generation; refusal rendering; disarmed hand-off; ghost-line construction for a 3-account group.
- **Component/Storybook**: CMP-192 stories WorkingOrderLine, PendingLine, RejectedLine, DisarmedLock; visual regression in light/dark, both densities, over a dense footprint background.
- **Integration**: against the mock OMS — submit, ack via the `orders` WS topic, line transitions pending→working.
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron)**: place a limit from the chart on demo, assert the exchange order id appears and the line renders; attempt an invalid side and assert nothing was sent (network assertion, not just UI); attempt while disarmed and assert a ticket opened instead.
- **Perf**: click→submit p95 ≤50 ms client-side on the worst-case scene; overlay redraw ≤2 ms with 20 lines.
- **A11y**: axe-core on SCR-030 and SCR-040; keyboard-only placement; announcement assertions.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend for touched files.

## Security notes
This is an order-placing path, therefore `security`-labelled by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8. Threats: accidental submission (mitigated by arm gating, confirm policy, hover preview, undo window), privilege escalation (a `viewer` must not be able to place — server re-checks, UI hard-disables), and repudiation (provenance auditing from E31-T01). A manual abuse-case check is required: attempt placement while disarmed, while kill-switched, while locked out, and as a `viewer`, asserting 403/refusal and **no state change** each time. Data classification: financial.

## Accessibility notes
Per E31-D05: crosshair-driven keyboard placement, ≥24 px affordances, focus visible on the DOM-mirrored line, pending/acknowledged/rejected announced with the specified politeness (assertive for rejection), no colour-only encoding of side (glyph + label), and SCR-040 stating in text that keyboard alternatives exist. axe-core must be green on both screens.

## Performance notes
Budgets: click→submit ≤50 ms client-side (US-DOM-007/US-ORD-006 class NFR), click→ack p95 <300 ms on demo (budget #4), overlay redraw ≤2 ms (SCR-040). Trading-line updates are exempt from the shedding ladder (`06-...` §4.3 "never acceptable").

## Observability
`order.submitted` (audited, with provenance `source='chart-click'`, modifier, price), analytics `chart.trade_from_chart`, `chart.trading_overlay_changed`; audit `trading.chart_drag_modify_enabled` when enabled on LIVE. Metric `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms{source="chart-click"}`.
