title: Drag order, stop and target lines on the chart to amend
body:
## Context
**US-ORD-008 — Drag order, stop and target lines (Must):** *"As a trader, I want to drag order and TP/SL lines on the chart, so that I manage trades visually."* This is the signature interaction of the epic and the one with the highest fat-finger consequence, so it carries the undo window, the spring-back-on-reject behaviour and a mandatory keyboard equivalent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-030 (drag on the trading layer), SCR-064 Position SL/TP editor (the richer keyboard alternative, reached from a line's context action), SCR-040 (the drag-to-modify enable toggle and its wrong-side confirm copy), SCR-076/SCR-077 as needed.
- **Components**: CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay (drag, pending, rejected, keyboard-reposition, delete-confirm), CMP-119 BracketEditor and CMP-120 TrailingStopEditor (as the SCR-064 content reached from the line), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice.
- Draggable line kinds: working order (limit/stop/conditional), position SL, position TP. The position **entry** line is never draggable.
- Drag lifecycle: grab (handle ≥24 px) → live ghost line with a readout of price, Δ from entry and resulting R → drop snapped to tick → `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}` or `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl` via E31-T01 → **pending** visual until the `orders`/`positions` WS event confirms → settle, or **spring back** with the exact reason on rejection.
- Refusals before sending: dropping a stop on the wrong side of the current price is refused with an explanation and the stop stays put (US-ORD-008 scenario 3); the SCR-040 wrong-side-of-mark confirm copy applies where the catalogue specifies a confirm rather than a refusal.
- **Native-SL invariant respected**: dragging an SL may move it, never delete it ("Every position keeps a native stop — you can move it, not delete it." — SCR-064 validation text). Deleting a line that represents a live order above a configurable notional threshold requires a ConfirmDialog (CMP-192 spec).
- **Undo window** (E31-T01): after a drag commits, an undo affordance re-amends to the original price; after a fill it explains instead of acting.
- **Keyboard equivalent** (mandatory): Tab cycles order lines on the visible chart, ↑/↓ step by `tickSize` (with a larger modifier step), Enter commits, Esc abandons and restores, Delete removes with confirmation. States announced per the E31-D05 utterance script.
- Multi-line safety: with a scaled-order ladder of 10+ lines, dragging one never moves a sibling; overlapping lines at the same price expose a disambiguation affordance.

## Out of scope
Creating orders (S01), cancelling (S03), DOM drag (S05), bracket child re-sizing semantics and trailing-stop translation (E32), scaled-ladder editing as a group (E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Drag to reprice
  Given a working limit order line on SCR-030
  When I drag it to a new price and release
  Then the price is snapped to the tick, an amend is submitted,
  and the line shows a pending state until the orders WS event acknowledges it

Scenario: Drag rejected
  Given the exchange rejects the amend with order_not_amendable
  Then the line springs back to its original price and the exact reason is displayed with a link to the rejection detail

Scenario: Drag stop through price
  Given a long position and its stop line
  When I drag the stop to the wrong side of the current price
  Then the drop is refused with an explanation, nothing is sent, and the stop stays put

Scenario: Stop cannot be deleted
  When I attempt to delete the native stop line of an open position
  Then the action is refused with the invariant explanation and the position keeps its stop

Scenario: Undo an accidental drag
  Given I dragged a working order and the undo window has not elapsed
  When I activate undo
  Then an amend restoring the original price is submitted and the undo itself is audited

Scenario: Undo after fill
  Given the order filled during the undo window
  Then undo does not send a reversing order; it states the order filled and offers the flatten path

Scenario: Keyboard reposition
  Given a keyboard user focuses a stop line
  When they press the up arrow three times and Enter
  Then the stop moves three ticks, the amend is submitted, and pending then acknowledged are announced

Scenario: Drag while disarmed or kill-switched
  Then lines are not draggable, the lock reason is shown on hover and to screen readers, and nothing is sent
```

## Technical notes / design
Drag state lives where E31-K01/ADR-0017 decided; the visual follow must be compositor-cheap so the chart holds 60 fps during a drag under the worst-case scene.

Amend uses `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`; omitted fields are left unchanged, and the endpoint refuses with `order_not_amendable` when the order is terminal or already has an amend/cancel in flight — that code maps to the "springs back" path with the copy-deck string. SL/TP on a position uses `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`.

Optimistic rendering is a **pending** style (dashed + label), never the settled style, so the user is never shown a confirmed state that the exchange has not confirmed; reconciliation deadline 1 s (E31-T01).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: drag→price math at all zoom levels and log/percent price scales; snapping; wrong-side detection for long and short, stop and TP, with the mark/last/index trigger sources; undo intent construction; keyboard step arithmetic incl. modifier step; invariant refusal for stop deletion.
- **Component**: CMP-192 stories KeyboardRepriceDemo, DeleteConfirmFlow, PendingAmend, SpringBackOnReject; interaction test for keyboard reprice/delete is an explicit CI gate (trading-critical, per the catalogue).
- **Integration**: amend acknowledged / rejected / never-acknowledged (unreconciled) paths against the mock OMS with recorded Bybit fixtures.
- **E2E**: drag a working order on demo and assert the exchange reflects the new price; drag a stop to the wrong side and assert zero network calls; undo a drag and assert the restoring amend.
- **Perf**: 60 fps sustained during a drag on the worst-case scene; overlay redraw ≤2 ms with 20 lines; a scaled ladder of 10+ lines dragged individually without sibling movement.
- **A11y**: axe-core; NVDA/VoiceOver pass over the reposition flow; target-size verification at compact density.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Order-modifying path → `security`-labelled. Threats: unintended amend from a stray pointer (arm gate, ≥24 px handles, undo window, pending-not-settled rendering), removal of protective stops (invariant refusal client-side plus server enforcement in E32 — client refusal is convenience, the server is the control), repudiation (every drag audited with `source='chart-drag'` and both the old and new price). Abuse-case check: attempt to delete an SL by every available route (drag off-screen, delete key, context menu, API replay) and assert refusal + audit.

## Accessibility notes
2.1.1 and 2.5.7 compliance is the gate: no functionality is drag-only. Announcements throttled to commit and resolve moments — never per pointermove. Focus returns to the line after any dialog. Reduced-motion honours the D04 spec (no spring animation; instant restore with a static cue).

## Performance notes
Drag follow must not exceed one frame of latency; trading overlays are never shed under the §4.3 ladder; the readout label must be a single composited element.

## Observability
Audit `order.amend_requested` / `position.stop_modified` / `position.tp_ladder_set` with old and new price and provenance `source='chart-drag'`; analytics `chart.drag_amend`, `trading.undo_used`; metrics `cv_trading_overlay_redraw_ms`, `cv_trading_unreconciled_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; the keyboard interaction test wired as a required CI gate.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80 %; Storybook variants published.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual SR pass; target sizes verified.
- [ ] Perf benchmarks recorded (fps during drag, overlay redraw).
- [ ] Security review + abuse-case results recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E31-D07) passed.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed on demo.
- [ ] Feature flag `trading.chart_drag_enabled` recorded (demo on, live off until R4).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-S01** (chart order placement and the overlay plumbing), **E30** (arm/lock, confirmation policy and the amend path in the ticket UI) and **E32** (brackets and the native-SL invariant that a dragged stop must not be able to violate).

**Scheduling.** E30 and E32 both close at the end of **Sprint 17** (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 and the §12 gantt), so this story is scheduled in **Sprint 18 — strictly after**, never concurrently with, its blockers' completion sprint. Sprint 17 carries only the E31 work whose blockers finished in S16 (T01, S01, S04, Q01, X01), which is what gives the S17–S18 train its slack.

## Branch
`feat/e31-chart-drag-amend`. Split: drag mechanics PR, then keyboard + undo + refusal PR.

title: Cancel orders from the chart and the DOM ladder
body:
## Context
**US-ORD-009 — Cancel order from chart and DOM (Should):** *"As a trader, I want to cancel an order by right-clicking or pressing a key on its marker, so that cancellation is as fast as placement."* Cancellation must be at least as fast and as reachable as placement, or the direct-manipulation surfaces become a one-way risk ratchet.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-040 (the chart trading overlay settings where the cancel behaviour and cancel-all key are described), SCR-050 (ladder marker cancel), SCR-030 (chart line cancel), SCR-072 (confirmation for cancel-all).
- **Components**: CMP-192 OrderLineOverlay (context menu + Delete), CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker (cancel affordance in the "Your orders" column), CMP-043 Dialog / CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-229 ArmToggle, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge where relevant.
- Right-click (or Shift+F10 by keyboard) on an order line or ladder marker opens a context menu containing Cancel; `Delete` on a focused line/marker does the same, with a ConfirmDialog above the configurable notional threshold.
- Cancel single: `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}` via E31-T01, pending state until the `orders` WS event clears the line/marker.
- **Cancel-all on symbol**: the cancel-all key with the chart or ladder focused cancels all working orders on that symbol for the active target after the confirm policy, via `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all` with a symbol + account filter; results reported **per order**, with partial failures listed individually rather than a single blanket error.
- Already-filled translation: the exchange error for cancelling a filled order is translated to "Already filled" and the position view updates rather than showing a raw error.
- Disarmed/kill-switched/viewer states: cancel remains available where policy allows it (cancelling reduces risk) but must still respect RBAC and the kill-switch's documented semantics ("stops new risk, does not force-close") — the behaviour implemented is exactly what E31-D03/D06 specify, and the specified behaviour is restated in the UI.

## Out of scope
Flatten and cancel-all-across-symbols as a panic control (S06). Order blotter cancellation (E29 SCR-063). Trade-group cancel (E34's `/trade-groups/{id}/cancel`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Right-click cancel
  Given a working order line on the chart
  When I right-click it and choose Cancel
  Then the cancel is submitted and the line clears only when the orders WS event acknowledges it

Scenario: Cancel from the ladder marker
  Given my own order marker on a ladder row
  When I activate its cancel affordance
  Then the same cancel path runs and the marker clears on acknowledgement

Scenario: Cancel all on symbol
  Given three working orders on BTCUSDT for the active target
  When I press the cancel-all key with the chart focused
  Then the confirm policy applies and, on confirmation, all three are cancelled and reported individually

Scenario: Partial failure
  Given one of the three cancels fails
  Then the successful two are shown cancelled, the failure is listed with its reason, and no blanket success is claimed

Scenario: Already filled
  Given the order filled before the cancel arrived
  Then the exchange error is translated to "Already filled", the line clears, and the position view updates

Scenario: Keyboard cancel
  Given a keyboard user focuses an order line or a ladder marker
  When they press Delete
  Then the confirm applies above the notional threshold and the outcome is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
`POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all` fans out `POST /v5/order/cancel-all` per account and Bybit costs 1 req/s per account for `linear`, so the fan-out scheduler serialises — the UI must therefore render a progressive per-order result list, not block on a single response.

Cancel round-trip budget ≤500 ms p95 (US-ORD-009 NFR).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: context-menu construction per line/marker kind; threshold logic for the confirm; error-code translation incl. the already-filled case; per-order result aggregation with mixed outcomes.
- **Integration**: cancel acknowledged, cancel-of-filled-order, cancel-all with one failing leg (recorded fixtures).
- **E2E**: place two orders on demo, cancel one from the chart and one from the ladder, then cancel-all with a third; assert exchange state matches.
- **A11y**: context menu reachable via Shift+F10, menu semantics, Delete path, announcements.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Order-cancelling path → `security`-labelled. Threats: a `viewer` cancelling another user's orders (RBAC re-checked server-side per account scope); mass-cancel as a denial-of-trading abuse (rate-limited, audited, confirmed); repudiation (every cancel audited with provenance and the surface used). Abuse case: attempt cancel-all against accounts outside the session's `account_scope` and assert 403 + no state change + audit row.

## Accessibility notes
Every mouse action has a keyboard twin (Shift+F10 menu, Delete key); the confirm dialog is an `alertdialog` with the action restated in the button's accessible name; per-order results are announced as a summary, not one live-region message per order.

## Performance notes
Cancel round trip ≤500 ms p95; the per-order result list renders progressively and must not block the frame.

## Observability
Audit `order.cancel_requested` with provenance (`source='chart-context'|'dom-marker'|'cancel-all-key'`); analytics `chart.cancel_from_chart`, `dom.cancel_from_ladder`; metric `cv_order_cancel_roundtrip_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; coverage met.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard path verified; SR spot-check recorded.
- [ ] Security review; abuse case executed.
- [ ] Design QA passed; QA sign-off; demoed.
- [ ] Feature flag state recorded.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-S02** (chart order lines and their hit-testing) and **E31-S04** (ladder own-order markers) — cancel is an affordance on objects those stories create. Transitively strictly after E29 (S16) and E30/E32 (end of S17).

## Branch
`feat/e31-cancel-from-surfaces`.

title: Click-to-trade on the DOM ladder
body:
## Context
**US-DOM-007 — Click-to-trade from the DOM (Should):** *"As a trader, I want to place, modify and cancel orders directly on the ladder, so that execution matches my read."* E21 shipped SCR-050 with the trading affordances rendered **disabled**; this story turns them on. The ladder is the fastest execution surface in the product, so it has the tightest latency requirement (click→submit ≤50 ms client-side) and the strictest arm gating.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-050 (Heatmap + DOM ladder panel — the trading affordances), SCR-060 order ticket (the pre-filled hand-off when disarmed), SCR-076 (confirmation when policy requires), SCR-077 (rejection detail).
- **Components**: CMP-229 ArmToggle (scope `dom`, enabled for the first time), CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons (enabled — the active size preset resolves the click's quantity), CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker, CMP-108 DomLadderRow (trading variants), CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog.
- Row interactions per the frozen modifier map (E31-D01/D06; the story baseline is: left-click a bid row = limit buy at that price, left-click an ask row = limit sell, Ctrl+click = market order, Escape = cancel all working orders on the symbol after the confirm policy).
- Quantity resolution: the active size preset from CMP-122 (per symbol-class and per account profile, US-ORD-003), with percent presets resolved to a concrete quantity and shown **before** submission.
- Hover preview on every row stating exactly what a click will do ("Limit buy 0.1 @ 64 100, account Main").
- Every placement carries the profile's native stop (server-enforced by E32; the UI shows CMP-158 so the guarantee is visible).
- **Disarmed path**: a click opens a pre-filled ticket requiring explicit confirmation instead of firing (US-DOM-007 scenario 3).
- Row target ≥24 px at every supported density; the arm state and environment badge are always visible on the panel, and no trading affordance is operable unless both are.
- Guard integration with E31-T01 for kill-switch, lockouts, RBAC (`viewer` sees the ladder read-only), stale/disconnected book (trading affordances hard-disabled when the book is stale or resynchronising — you may not trade against a frozen book).
- **Keyboard**: the ladder's roving-tabindex grid gains a row action menu on Enter containing every mouse action (place limit, place market, cancel my order, move my order), with the confirm policy applied identically.

## Out of scope
Ladder rendering, heatmap, depth tiers, colour scale, own-order data plumbing (all E21). Drag-to-modify (S05). Cancel-all as a global panic action (S06). Sizing rule definitions (E28/E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Limit placement
  Given one-click trading is armed on the ladder and the active preset is 0.1 BTC
  When I left-click a bid row at 64 100
  Then a limit buy of 0.1 at 64 100 is submitted with a native stop attached per the profile,
  the own-order marker appears in pending state, and the acknowledgement arrives within 500 ms

Scenario: Market order
  When I Ctrl+click a row
  Then a market order for the active size is submitted after the configured confirm policy

Scenario: Cancel all on symbol
  When I press Escape with the ladder focused
  Then all working orders on that symbol for the active target are cancelled after the confirm policy

Scenario: Disarmed
  Given one-click trading is locked
  When I click a row
  Then a pre-filled ticket opens requiring explicit confirmation and nothing is submitted

Scenario: Stale or resynchronising book
  Given the book is stale or resynchronising
  Then row trading affordances are disabled with a stated reason and no click can submit

Scenario: Read-only role
  Given the session role is viewer
  Then the ladder renders read-only, no trading affordance is operable,
  and a forced request is rejected server-side with 403, no state change and an audit row

Scenario: Latency
  Given an armed ladder under a live 200-depth book
  Then click to submit completes within 50 ms client-side at p95

Scenario: Keyboard placement
  Given a keyboard user on a focused ladder row
  When they press Enter and choose "Place limit buy"
  Then the same intent is produced, the confirm policy applies, and the outcome is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
The click handler must read from already-decoded book state (the shared worker) and the cached instrument filters — no fetch is permitted on the interaction path, or the 50 ms budget is unreachable.

Quantity from a percent preset is resolved from the cached `wallet` WS state; if that state is stale, percent presets are disabled with the reason stated (mirroring US-ORD-014's stale-input rule) rather than resolving from stale equity.

All submissions go through `packages/trading-intent` (E31-T01); duplicate suppression there protects against double-fire on a noisy pointer.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: row→intent mapping for each modifier and each side; preset resolution incl. percent and invalid-for-symbol presets; stale-book and stale-wallet disabling; hover-preview text; the disarmed hand-off payload.
- **Component**: CMP-108 trading variants and CMP-230 markers in Storybook (armed, locked, pending, rejected, viewer-read-only); axe on each.
- **Integration**: submit→ack via the `orders` topic; rejection fixtures (post-only, reduce-only violation, `10018`).
- **E2E (web + Electron)**: arm, click a bid row on demo, assert the order exists on the exchange with the expected price and a native stop; attempt while disarmed and assert a ticket opened with zero submissions.
- **Perf**: click→submit p95 ≤50 ms under a live 200-depth book with the heatmap active; verify the ladder still meets its own E21 render budget with markers enabled.
- **A11y**: axe-core on SCR-050 with trading on; keyboard placement through the row action menu; target size at compact density; announcement assertions.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Highest-risk surface in the epic: one click = one live order. Threats — accidental fire (arm gate, hover preview, confirm policy, ≥24 px targets, undo window), wrong-account fire (the active target is displayed persistently with the arm indicator per US-ORD-005), privilege escalation (`viewer` read-only, server re-check on `account_scope`), rate-limit abuse (duplicate suppression + governor awareness), repudiation (every click-trade audited with the price row and modifier used — the explicit US-DOM-007 NFR). Manual abuse cases required: fire while disarmed, while kill-switched, while locked out, as a `viewer`, and against an out-of-scope account. Data classification: financial, audited.

## Accessibility notes
The ladder is a `role="grid"` with roving tabindex (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §4.2); every mouse action exists in the Enter-activated row action menu; own-order markers are text in a dedicated "Your orders" column so nothing depends on a canvas glyph (CMP-230); arm state changes announce assertively; pending/acknowledged/rejected announce per the E31-D05 script.

## Performance notes
Budgets: click→submit ≤50 ms client-side; click→ack p95 <300 ms demo (budget #4); the ladder's own render budget from E21 must not regress with markers and trading affordances enabled.

## Observability
Audit `order.submitted` with `source='dom-click'`, `price_row`, `modifier`; analytics `dom.click_trade`, `dom.arm_toggled`; metrics `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms{source="dom-click"}`, `cv_trading_intent_refused_total{reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; coverage ≥80 %.
- [ ] Storybook variants published; axe-core green; keyboard path verified; manual SR pass.
- [ ] Latency benchmark recorded against the 50 ms and 300 ms budgets.
- [ ] Security review; all five abuse cases executed and recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E31-D07); QA sign-off; demoed on demo.
- [ ] Feature flag `trading.dom_click_enabled` recorded (demo on, live off until R4).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-T01**, **E31-D03** (design handoff Done end of S15) and **E21** (the readable ladder surface whose trading affordances already render disabled). E29 and E39 complete in S16, ahead of this Sprint-17 story.

title: Drag an order marker on the ladder to reprice it
body:
## Context
**US-DOM-008 — Drag to modify from the DOM (Should):** *"As a trader, I want to drag my order marker to another price, so that I reprice without retyping."* This is the ladder twin of E31-S02 and reuses its pending/spring-back/undo machinery; the difference is that the drop target is a discrete ladder **row**, not a continuous price, which removes the snapping ambiguity but adds row-boundary edge cases.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-050 (marker drag), SCR-077 (rejection detail).
- **Components**: CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker (grab, drag, drop-valid, drop-invalid, pending, return-to-origin), CMP-108 DomLadderRow (drop-target states), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog for above-threshold moves.
- Drag lifecycle: grab a marker → rows highlight as valid/invalid drop targets → drop on a row → `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}` at that row's price via E31-T01 → marker shows **pending** → clears on the `orders` WS event, or **returns to its original row** with the exact reason on rejection.
- Aggregate markers: when several of my orders rest at one price (or a group aggregate marker is shown), dragging must either disambiguate explicitly or move the whole set as specified in E31-D03 — never silently pick one.
- Refusals before sending: dragging a reduce-only stop to the wrong side of the market is refused inline and nothing is sent (US-DOM-008 scenario 3).
- **Reconciliation guarantee**: the optimistic marker position must reconcile with exchange truth within 1 s or be marked unreconciled (US-DOM-008 NFR) — never left looking settled.
- Undo window applies identically to chart drags (E31-T01).
- **Keyboard equivalent**: row action menu → "Move my order" → arrow keys move the target row → Enter commits → Esc abandons; announced per the E31-D05 script.
- Auto-scroll behaviour when dragging toward the edge of the visible ladder window, with the auto-centring suppressed during a drag so the target row cannot move under the pointer.

## Out of scope
Placement (S04), cancellation (S03), chart drags (S02), ladder rendering and auto-centring policy (E21).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Drag reprice
  Given my working limit order marker on a ladder row
  When I drag it to another row and release
  Then an amend to that row's price is submitted and the marker shows pending until acknowledged

Scenario: Amend rejected
  Given the exchange rejects the amend
  Then the marker returns to its original price and the exact reason is shown

Scenario: Drag onto invalid price
  When I drag a reduce-only stop to the wrong side of the market
  Then the drop is refused with an inline explanation and nothing is sent

Scenario: Optimistic state always reconciles
  Given an amend was acknowledged by REST but no orders WS event arrives within one second
  Then the marker is shown as unreconciled rather than settled, and the reconciliation loop resolves it

Scenario: Ladder must not move under the pointer
  Given auto-centring is enabled and price moves during a drag
  Then recentring is suppressed for the duration of the drag and resumes on release

Scenario: Multiple orders at one price
  Given two of my orders rest at the same price
  When I begin a drag on that marker
  Then the UI disambiguates explicitly and never silently repositions the wrong order

Scenario: Keyboard move
  Given a keyboard user on their own order's row
  When they choose "Move my order", press arrow keys and Enter
  Then the amend is submitted to the selected row's price and the outcome is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
Drop target is the row's price, already tick-aligned by the ladder's aggregation; when the ladder is aggregating multiple ticks per row (E21 tick aggregation), the amend price must be the row's canonical price and that must be stated in the hover/preview text so the user is not surprised.

Amend semantics, error codes and the pending/spring-back machinery are shared with E31-S02 — this story must **reuse** `packages/trading-intent` rather than re-implementing, and a reviewer should reject any duplicated guard logic.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: row→price resolution incl. the tick-aggregated case; wrong-side detection; aggregate-marker disambiguation; auto-scroll and recentre suppression; keyboard move arithmetic.
- **Component**: CMP-230 stories for every drag state; axe.
- **Integration**: amend ack / reject / late-ack (unreconciled) with recorded fixtures.
- **E2E**: place an order on demo from the ladder, drag it two rows, assert the exchange price matches the target row; drag a stop to the wrong side and assert zero network calls.
- **Perf**: drag does not regress the ladder's E21 render budget; reconciliation within 1 s asserted in the integration test.
- **A11y**: keyboard move path; announcements at commit and resolve only.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend.

## Security notes
Order-modifying path → `security`-labelled. Threats: wrong-order repricing via ambiguous aggregate markers (explicit disambiguation is the control), optimistic display of a state the exchange never accepted (the 1 s reconciliation rule is the control), repudiation (audit with `source='dom-drag'`, old and new price, and the row). Abuse case: attempt to amend an order belonging to an account outside `account_scope` and assert 403 + no state change + audit.

## Accessibility notes
Drag is never the only path; the row action menu carries the move operation. Recentre suppression during keyboard move as well as pointer drag, so an AT user's target does not shift mid-operation. Announcements throttled to commit/resolve.

## Performance notes
Amend round trip ≤500 ms p95; reconciliation deadline 1 s; the ladder must keep its E21 frame budget while a drag is in progress.

## Observability
Audit `order.amend_requested` with `source='dom-drag'`, `price_row`, old/new price; analytics `dom.drag_amend`; metric `cv_trading_unreconciled_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; coverage met; no duplicated guard logic (reviewer-checked).
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard path verified; SR pass.
- [ ] Security review; abuse case executed.
- [ ] Design QA; QA sign-off; demoed.
- [ ] Feature flag `trading.dom_drag_enabled` recorded.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-S04** (ladder click-to-trade and the own-order markers this drags) and **E31-S02** (the shared drag-to-amend intent path, snap-to-tick and spring-back behaviour, reused rather than reimplemented). Transitively strictly after E30 and E32, which close at the end of S17.

title: Chart/DOM trading intent layer: guards, optimistic state, undo window and audit
body:
## Context
S01–S06 are six different surfaces that all produce the same three things: an **order intent**, a **guard decision**, and an **optimistic pending state that must reconcile with exchange truth**. Implementing that logic six times guarantees six different bugs and six different ways to bypass a safety gate. This Task builds it once, as a frontend package module consumed by every E31 story, plus the thin backend enrichment needed to audit the *manner* of the action.

The client is never the authority: the OMS (E29) and the native-SL invariant (E32/M17) validate server-side regardless of what this layer decides (US-ORD-005 NFR). This layer exists to refuse early, to render honestly, and to make every action auditable.

## Scope / Deliverables
**Frontend — `packages/trading-intent` (new module inside the web app):**
- `TradeIntent` type: `{ source: 'chart-click'|'chart-drag'|'dom-click'|'dom-drag'|'flatten'|'reverse'|'cancel', symbol, side, orderType, price?, triggerPrice?, triggerBy?, qty, reduceOnly, accountIds[] | tradeGroupId, modifier, priceRow?, correlationId }`.
- **Guard chain**, evaluated in a fixed order with the first failure returned as a structured reason: kill-switch engaged (from `auth_ok.kill_switch` and the `system` WS topic) → risk lockout active (E39) → RBAC (`orders:write` / `positions:write` on the target accounts, from the session permission set) → environment/arm state (CMP-229 scope `chart`/`dom`, US-ORD-005; auto-disarm on 30 min inactivity, session lock, environment switch or disconnect) → instrument filters (`priceFilter` tick snapping and `lotSizeFilter` min/step from `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}`) → side/price sanity (a stop on the wrong side of the mark, a limit on the wrong side for the chosen type — US-ORD-007 scenario 3, US-ORD-008 scenario 3) → confirm policy resolution (immediate / hold-to-confirm / dialog, per environment; LIVE may never skip).
- **Snap-to-tick** helper: round-half-away-from-zero to `tickSize`, returning both the snapped price and a flag so the UI can show "Snapped to 0.5 tick".
- **Submission adapter**: maps intent → `POST /api/v1/orders`, `PATCH /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all`, `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close`, `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/reverse`, `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`. Every request carries a client-generated `orderLinkId`-derived idempotency key (ADR-0006) so a double-fire from a jittery pointer cannot double-submit.
- **Pending/reconcile store**: an intent enters `pending` on send; it clears only when the matching `orders`/`positions` WS event arrives (WS is the source of truth — REST ack is acceptance only, ADR-0006). If no reconciling event arrives within **1 s** (US-DOM-008 NFR), the UI shows an unreconciled warning; the optimistic visual **springs back** on a rejection with the exact exchange reason, routed to SCR-077 for detail.
- **Undo window**: configurable (default from the E31-D01 research figure), during which a submitted-not-yet-filled intent can be reverted — cancel for a placement, re-amend to the original price for a drag. If the order already filled, the undo control changes to state that plainly and offers the flatten path instead; it never silently market-closes. Every undo emits its own audited action.
- Error-code → copy mapping from the E31-D06 copy deck, covering `order_not_amendable`, validation failures, already-filled cancels, insufficient margin and `10018` rate limiting.

**Backend — module M14 (OMS) enrichment only:**
- Accept and persist the interaction provenance on order submission: `source`, `modifier`, `price_row` in the `orders` request payload, written to `order_events` (`event_type='local_create'`, payload) and to `audit_log`, so US-DOM-007's NFR ("every click-trade action audited with the price row and modifier used") is satisfiable.
- Reject unknown `source` values; `source` is advisory metadata and must never influence validation or ordering.

## Out of scope
Any UI (S01–S06). The OMS state machine, reconciliation loop and blotters (E29). Native-SL attachment logic (E32) — this layer only *refuses to construct* an entry intent without an SL when the profile requires it, and lets the server be the enforcer. Fan-out scheduling (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Guards run in order and refuse early
  Given the kill-switch is engaged and one-click is also disarmed
  When any surface builds an intent
  Then the guard chain returns the kill-switch reason (the highest-precedence failure), nothing is sent,
  and the refusal is logged with the intent's correlation id

Scenario: Double-fire cannot double-submit
  Given a pointer emits two pointerdown events 8 ms apart on the same ladder row
  Then exactly one request is sent, carrying one idempotency key, and the second is dropped as a duplicate

Scenario: Price is snapped before anything is sent
  Given tickSize 0.5 and a pointer price of 64 100.37
  Then the intent carries 64 100.5 and a snapped flag the UI can surface

Scenario: Optimistic state reconciles or springs back
  Given an amend is submitted and the exchange rejects it
  Then the pending state clears, the visual returns to the pre-drag value,
  and the exact exchange message and code are available to the caller

Scenario: Unreconciled after one second
  Given a REST ack was received but no orders WS event arrived within 1000 ms
  Then the intent is marked unreconciled and the caller is told, rather than being shown a confirmed state

Scenario: Undo after fill is honest
  Given an undo is attempted on an order that already filled
  Then no reversing market order is sent automatically; the caller is told it filled and offered the flatten path

Scenario: Provenance is audited
  Given a DOM click-trade at price row 64 100 with the Ctrl modifier
  Then the persisted order_events row and audit_log entry both record source='dom-click', modifier='ctrl', price_row=64100
```

## Technical notes / design
Guard chain is a pure function `evaluate(intent, context) -> Ok(intent') | Refused(reason)` so it is exhaustively unit-testable without a DOM. Context is assembled from the session (`auth_ok` permissions, `allowed_environments`, `kill_switch`), the arm store, the risk-cap store and the instrument cache.

Idempotency: `orderLinkId = <sessionId>-<monotonicSeq>-<hash(intent)>`, matching the uniqueness constraint `ux_orders_link` on `orders`.

Pending store keys on the idempotency key, not on the exchange order id, because the exchange id is not known until acceptance.

Config keys: `trading.undo_window_ms`, `trading.arm_timeout_seconds` (already in the settings payload), `trading.confirm_market_orders`, `trading.confirm_flatten`, `trading.reconcile_timeout_ms` (default 1000).

## Test plan
- **Unit** (target ≥90 % on this module, it is a risk module): each guard in isolation and in precedence order; snap-to-tick at boundaries (exact tick, half tick, negative drift, very small tick sizes); idempotency key generation and duplicate suppression; pending→acknowledged, pending→rejected, pending→unreconciled transitions; undo before ack, after ack, after fill; error-code→copy mapping exhaustive over the documented codes.
- **Contract**: request bodies validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` schemas for every endpoint used; provenance fields validated against the OpenAPI order-create schema.
- **Integration** (backend): submitting with provenance writes the expected `order_events` and `audit_log` rows; unknown `source` rejected.
- **Fixtures**: recorded Bybit rejection fixtures (post-only reject, reduce-only violation, `10018`), plus a WS fixture that acks late (1.5 s) to exercise the unreconciled path.

## Security notes
Threats (`04-security-program.md`, STRIDE from E31-X01): **Tampering** — a client that forges `source` to look benign is possible, hence provenance is advisory-only and never affects validation. **Elevation of privilege** — the guard chain must not be the only RBAC check; the server re-checks account scope on every call. **Repudiation** — provenance + correlation id close the "I never clicked that" gap. **Denial of service** — duplicate suppression and the client-side rate awareness prevent a pointer storm from burning the per-UID rate budget. Data classification: financial, audited. Requires the `security` label and Security engineer review.

## Accessibility notes
The module is headless but must expose the state transitions (pending/acknowledged/rejected/unreconciled) as first-class values so consuming UIs can announce them per the E31-D05 utterance script; it must also throttle change notifications during a drag to commit/resolve moments only, to avoid live-region storms.

## Performance notes
Guard evaluation plus snapping must complete in ≤5 ms so the end-to-end click→submit budget of 50 ms (US-DOM-007 NFR) is dominated by transport, not logic. Emits `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms`. The instrument filter data must be read from cache, never fetched on the interaction path.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms` (histogram, labelled by source), `cv_trading_intent_refused_total{reason}`, `cv_trading_unreconciled_total`, `cv_trading_undo_total{outcome}`. Audit: provenance on `order.submitted`, `order.amend_requested`, `order.cancel_requested`, plus a new `trading.undo_used`. Logs carry the correlation id end to end.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Module shipped with ≥90 % unit coverage; backend enrichment ≥85 %.
- [ ] OpenAPI updated for the provenance fields; contract tests green.
- [ ] Docs: `24-internal-schemas.md` notes the provenance fields on the order create path.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment; SAST/SCA clean.
- [ ] Metrics visible in Grafana; audit rows verified on demo.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-K01** (proven latency/hit-testing approach, Sprint 16), **E29** (OMS, order state machine and the private `orders`/`positions`/`executions` WS mirror — completes **S16**), **E39** (risk caps, lockouts and the kill-switch whose state this layer must read before every intent — completes **S16**), and **E31-D03** (handoff package incl. the error-code→copy deck, Done end of S15).

**Scheduling.** Every blocker of this ticket completes no later than **Sprint 16**, so the Sprint-17 start is strictly after its dependencies rather than concurrent with them.

**E30 / E32 are consumed, not blocking, here.** E30 (order ticket, arm/lock, confirm policy) and E32 (brackets + native-SL invariant) run S16–S17 and complete at the end of S17. This ticket integrates against their **interfaces frozen at the end of S16** — the `ArmState` contract, the confirmation-policy config key and the server-side native-SL rejection code — published as part of those epics' S16 output. The E31 tickets that need E30/E32 *behaviour* rather than their interface (E31-S02, S03, S05, S06) are scheduled in **Sprint 18**, strictly after E30 and E32 close in S17. That split is the slack mechanism keeping this epic inside the S17–S18 window.

## Branch

title: Build the chaos scenarios for crash seams, failover and disconnects in E32
body:
## Context
R3's chaos gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) names WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP and Postgres failover mid-fan-out. E32's equivalents are narrower and more dangerous: the seam **between an entry filling and its stop being attached** is the exact moment where the product's central safety guarantee is at risk, and `24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.8's 2-second deadline and 10-second alert threshold exist precisely to bound it. A chaos suite that kills the process at that seam is the only way to prove the watchdog (E32-T02) does what it claims.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos specs under `tests/chaos/e32/` using the fault-injection harness from `03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Scenarios: (1) kill the process between entry fill and deferred stop attach; (2) kill it between a ladder leg fill and the stop resize; (3) Postgres failover mid-ladder submission; (4) private WS disconnect mid-bracket with fills arriving during the gap; (5) exchange 5xx on `trading-stop` repeated three times, verifying escalation and the E39 lockout request rather than an automatic flatten; (6) clock skew of +30 s applied mid-trail, verifying the trail does not jump; (7) `10018` rate-limit storm during a 50-level ladder while a protective stop must be placed, verifying the protective reserve holds.
- Each scenario asserts a **recovery invariant**, not just absence of crash: the position ends natively stopped, the DB and exchange agree after reconciliation, no duplicate orders exist, and the audit trail explains what happened.
- Measured recovery times recorded against the specified thresholds (<=2 s deferred attach, <=10 s watchdog protection, <=5 s trail resume).
- A chaos report artefact retained for the R3 PRR evidence pack.
- Scenarios run nightly against staging demo plus on demand before each release.

## Out of scope
- Chaos for emulated algos (E33), fan-out unwind (E34) — though this suite's harness is shared with them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The fill-to-attach seam never leaves a naked position
  Given the process is killed between an entry fill and its stop attach, repeated 20 times
  When the backend restarts each time
  Then in every run the position is natively stopped within 10 seconds, a critical alert was raised, and an audit trail explains the gap

Scenario: Postgres failover mid-ladder reconciles without duplicates
  Given a failover during batch submission of a 20-level ladder
  Then after recovery the number of working orders matches the exchange exactly, no level was submitted twice (verified by deterministic order link ids), and the group state is consistent

Scenario: Repeated trading-stop failures escalate rather than flatten (failure)
  Given three consecutive exchange 5xx responses on the protective write
  Then the system raises a critical alert, requests an account new-entry lockout, and does not automatically flatten the position

Scenario: The protective reserve survives a rate-limit storm (edge)
  Given a 50-level ladder saturating the order-create budget and a simultaneous protective stop placement
  Then the protective placement succeeds by drawing on the reserve, and the ladder throttles instead

Scenario: A scenario that leaves inconsistent state fails loudly (edge)
  Given any run ending with the DB and exchange disagreeing after reconciliation
  Then the scenario fails with a diff of the two states, rather than passing because no exception was raised
```

## Technical notes / design
- Process kills use SIGKILL at a deterministic seam via an injected fault point compiled out of production builds, so the seam is reproducible rather than probabilistic.
- The 20-repetition requirement on scenario 1 exists because a once-passing crash test proves very little about a race.
- Recovery assertions compare against exchange truth (`GET /v5/position/list`, `/v5/order/realtime`), not against our own DB, since our DB is exactly what might be wrong.
- Clock-skew scenario uses a container time offset rather than mutating system time.

## Test plan
This ticket is a test deliverable. Its verification: each scenario is first run against a deliberately broken build (watchdog disabled, reserve removed) and must fail — a chaos test that passes without the control it verifies is not testing anything.

## Security notes
Chaos runs against demo only, with the environment guard asserted at start. The escalation path (lockout, no auto-flatten) is a safety decision verified here; a regression that introduces auto-flatten must fail this suite. The report is part of the RSK-016 evidence chain and is reviewed by the Security engineer.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Recovery-time thresholds are the assertions: 2 s deferred attach, 10 s watchdog protection, 5 s trail resume. Measured values are recorded per run so drift is visible over time.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts that the expected alert fired and that `oms_native_sl_missing_total` / `oms_native_sl_fallback_total` moved as expected — verifying that an operator would actually have seen the incident.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All seven scenarios implemented and passing, with scenario 1 at 20 repetitions.
- [ ] Negative verification recorded: each scenario fails against a build with its control disabled.
- [ ] Nightly and pre-release runs configured; report artefact retained.
- [ ] Security engineer review of the report format and the escalation assertions.
- [ ] Documented in `03-testing-strategy.md`'s chaos inventory.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E32-T02` (watchdog, fallback attach, escalation), `E32-S03` (ladder submission for the failover and rate-storm scenarios), `E32-S04` (trail resume).

## Branch
`test/e32-chaos`.

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-064, SCR-065, SCR-069

title: Build the SCR-069 bracket builder with a non-removable native stop floor
body:
## Context
`SCR-069` "Emulated OCO / bracket builder" is a modal offering an entry plus its exit pair, explicitly labelled where emulation applies, and — the part this epic owns — showing **"the mandatory native SL floor that remains regardless"**. Its design sign-off checklist requires: entry+bracket and standalone-OCO variants drawn, the emulation caveat stated prominently, race-resolution behaviour explained, the residual-risk state drawn, *"the mandatory native SL floor is shown as always-present and non-removable"*, and validation messages drawn.

E32 builds the **bracket half** (entry + native SL + TP or TP ladder). E33 adds the standalone-OCO half into the same modal shell. The shared shell, including the CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice and the native-SL floor affordance, is built here so E33 extends rather than duplicates.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-001` (UI half), `US-ALGO-003` (ladder entry UI half).
- Screen `SCR-069`; components `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-100` PriceInput, `CMP-101` QtyInput, `CMP-119` BracketEditor, `CMP-158` SafetyInvariantNotice, `CMP-118` AlgoProgressCard, `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge.
- `apps/web/src/features/algo/BracketBuilder/` — modal shell, entry section, stop section, take-profit section (single target or ladder), preview summary, submit.
- The stop field is **always present and cannot be cleared**: attempting to empty it restores the profile default and shows the CMP-158 note "Every position keeps a native stop — you can move it, not delete it."
- Price entry modes: absolute price, ticks from entry, percent, and R-multiple, with the others recomputed live (per SCR-064's checklist, shared behaviour in CMP-119).
- Resulting risk shown in account currency and in R **before** confirm.
- Validation surfaces: side correctness, beyond-liquidation stop, ladder totals >100%, `LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE` from E32-S02 with its single-target alternative offered as a one-click action.
- States: empty, editing, validating, submitting (per-child progress), submitted, partial-placement failure with retry, error.
- Submits via `POST /api/v1/orders` with `algo.bracket`; tracks group state from the `orders` / `trade_groups` WS topics.
- Analytics/audit hooks per the screen spec; `EstimatedBadge` on anything engine-managed.

## Out of scope
- The standalone-OCO variant and its race-resolution copy (E33), the scaled builder (E32-S06), SCR-064 (E32-S07), the order ticket itself (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A bracket is built and submitted
  Given the modal is open for BTCUSDT with an entry price, a stop and a single take-profit
  When I submit
  Then one bracket group is created, per-child progress is shown while it places, and on success the modal closes with the group visible in the orders panel

Scenario: The native stop cannot be removed
  Given the modal is open
  When I clear the stop-loss field
  Then the field repopulates with the profile default, the CMP-158 note "Every position keeps a native stop - you can move it, not delete it." is shown as a persistent role="note", and the submit button remains enabled with a valid stop

Scenario: Risk is restated before confirmation
  Given an entry, a stop and a quantity
  Then the resulting risk is shown in account currency and as an R-multiple, updating live as any input changes, and the submit button names the action and the risk

Scenario: An unsplittable ladder offers its alternative (error)
  Given I configure a three-step take-profit ladder the backend refuses with LADDER_NOT_SPLITTABLE
  Then the error names the instrument minimum and the offending leg, and a one-click "use a single target instead" action reconfigures the form without losing my other inputs

Scenario: A stop on the wrong side is blocked (edge)
  Given a long entry at 63,000 and a stop entered at 63,500
  Then an inline validation message explains that a long's stop must be below the entry, the submit control is disabled, and no request is sent

Scenario: Partial placement is shown honestly (failure)
  Given the entry places but a ladder child is rejected
  Then the modal shows which children placed and which failed with the exchange reason, offers a retry limited to the failed child, and does not imply the whole bracket succeeded
```

## Technical notes / design
- Build against the handoff pack from `E32-D07`; component behaviour contracts come from `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-119 and CMP-158.
- All price-mode recomputation is local and synchronous; the authoritative validation is still the backend's, and the UI never places an order the backend has not validated.
- The preview never computes the ladder itself: it calls `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` so the displayed table is produced by the same pure generator that will submit (E32-S03's rule, applied here to bracket ladders too).
- Optimistic UI is forbidden for protective state: a stop is rendered "pending" until the exchange acknowledges (SCR-064's performance note, applied consistently).
- Modal shell is extracted as `AlgoBuilderDialog` so E33 mounts its OCO variant into it without forking.
- Storybook stories for every enumerated state, including partial-placement failure.

## Test plan
- **Unit/component (>=80% frontend):** price-mode recomputation; stop-cannot-be-cleared behaviour; risk restatement; validation messages; state machine across all enumerated states.
- **Contract:** the request shape matches `AlgoSpec.bracket` in the OpenAPI schema (typed client generated from it).
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron):** build and submit a bracket on demo; attempt to clear the stop; unsplittable-ladder alternative; partial-placement retry — added in E32-Q04.
- **a11y:** axe-core on every state; keyboard-only submission; screen-reader pass on the CMP-158 note and the validation messages.
- **Visual regression:** Storybook snapshots per state.

## Security notes
This surface can place orders, so it inherits `security` handling. The UI enforces nothing security-relevant on its own — all invariants are server-side (E32-T01) — and the abuse case "a crafted client request strips the stop" is verified in E32-X02 against the API, not the UI. No secrets touch the client; account scope comes from the session.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The CMP-158 native-SL guarantee is a persistent `role="note"`, never a tooltip or toast. Every numeric input is labelled with its unit. The submit button names the full action ("Place bracket: buy 0.25 BTC, stop 62,800, target 64,450"). R-multiples and percentages are both present as text. Focus is trapped in the modal, returns to the invoking control on close, and the first error is announced and focused on failed validation. Every drag-equivalent interaction has a keyboard path.

## Performance notes
Input recomputation within one frame (<=16.6 ms). Submission inherits budget #4; the UI shows "placing" immediately and never blocks the main thread on the response.

## Observability
Analytics `algo.bracket_previewed`, `algo.bracket_field_changed`; audit events are emitted server-side. Client error boundary reports failed submissions with the correlation id from the API response.

title: Build the SCR-064 position SL/TP editor with trailing, break-even and TP ladder
body:
## Context
`SCR-064` "Position SL/TP editor (modal)" is the single surface where a trader manages an existing position's protection: stop-loss with its trigger source, a take-profit ladder with per-step native flags, a trailing stop (fixed offset / % / ATR multiple / structure-based) marked only-tighten, a break-even trigger in R, and — crucially — **which of these are native exchange-side versus engine-managed**, with the standing note "Engine-managed stops need the backend online. A native stop at 63,900 always remains."

Its validation rules are fixed by the screen spec: SL/TP side correctness; ladder percentages sum <=100% ("Ladder totals 110% — reduce a step."); each ladder step >= min lot; and the native-SL invariant cannot be removed ("Every position keeps a native stop — you can move it, not delete it."). Its sign-off checklist demands price/ticks/%/R-multiple entry modes recomputing live, resulting risk in account currency and R before confirm, invalid-side and beyond-liquidation validation, the partial-quantity TP ladder variant, and **a keyboard path equivalent to chart drag-to-modify**.

This story consumes three backend behaviours built earlier in the epic: TP ladders (E32-S02), trailing translation (E32-S04) and break-even (E32-T03).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-008` (UI half), `US-ALGO-003` (position-side ladder UI).
- Screen `SCR-064`; components `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-100` PriceInput, `CMP-119` BracketEditor, `CMP-120` TrailingStopEditor, `CMP-130` SlippageEstimateChip, `CMP-158` SafetyInvariantNotice.
- `apps/web/src/features/positions/SlTpEditor/` — stop section with trigger source (Last/Mark/Index, defaulting to Mark), TP ladder section with per-step percentage and native flag, trailing section (CMP-120), break-even section, native-versus-engine labelling, apply.
- Entry modes: price, ticks, percent and R-multiple, with the others recomputed live; resulting risk in account currency and R shown before confirm.
- Trailing display: the user's unit and value **and** the translated absolute distance and trigger price, sourced from E32-S04's response contract — the UI performs no translation of its own.
- Pending semantics: a changed SL/TP renders as **pending** until the exchange acknowledges, never optimistically as confirmed.
- Native-SL floor: the stop cannot be removed; clearing it restores the current value with the CMP-158 message.
- Writes via `PUT /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`, always sending both sides (the backend enforces this; the UI's form model reflects it so the user sees both values being written).
- States: loading, editing, validating, pending-acknowledgement, applied, rejected with the exchange reason, position-closed-while-editing.
- Keyboard equivalence to chart drag-to-modify: every adjustment reachable and performable from the keyboard with announced values.

## Out of scope
- Chart drag-to-modify itself (E31), the bracket builder (E32-S05), the scaled builder (E32-S06), rule-authored trails (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A percentage trail shows its translation
  Given a long position and a 1.5% trailing stop
  When I apply it
  Then the editor shows the 1.5% input alongside the translated absolute distance and resulting trigger price returned by the backend, labels the trail as native or engine-managed, and renders the change as pending until Bybit acknowledges

Scenario: The stop cannot be deleted
  Given the editor is open on a protected position
  When I clear the stop-loss field
  Then the previous value is restored and the persistent note "Every position keeps a native stop - you can move it, not delete it." is shown, and no request removing the stop is ever sent

Scenario: A ladder totalling more than the position is blocked (error)
  Given ladder steps of 25%, 25% and 60%
  Then the inline message "Ladder totals 110% - reduce a step." is shown, apply is disabled, and the offending step is marked

Scenario: An engine-managed trail is labelled with its residual risk
  Given an ATR-based trail, which has no native equivalent
  Then it is labelled engine-managed with the standing note that engine-managed stops need the backend online while the native stop at its current price always remains, presented as persistent text rather than a tooltip

Scenario: The exchange rejects the amend (failure)
  Given Bybit rejects the trading-stop write
  Then the pending state resolves to rejected with the exchange reason shown verbatim plus a plain-language explanation, the previous values are restored in the form, and the position's existing protection is stated explicitly so I know what is currently in force

Scenario: The position closes while the editor is open (edge)
  Given the position is flattened elsewhere while I am editing
  Then the editor switches to a closed state explaining that the position no longer exists, disables apply, and offers to close the modal without sending anything

Scenario: Every adjustment is keyboard-reachable (edge)
  Given keyboard-only operation
  Then each of stop, each ladder step, the trail and the break-even trigger can be focused, adjusted in the current entry mode and applied, with the resulting risk announced, matching what chart drag-to-modify can do
```

## Technical notes / design
- Built against E32-D07's handoff pack; CMP-120 TrailingStopEditor's behaviour contract comes from `15-component-catalogue.md`.
- The form model always carries both TP and SL current values so the both-sides write rule (section 8.9) is visible to the user rather than a hidden backend detail.
- R-multiple mode resolves against the position's frozen initial stop, matching the backend's computation (E32-S01), so the UI and the OMS never disagree about what 1R means.
- Beyond-liquidation validation uses the liquidation price from the `positions` topic; if unavailable, the check degrades to a warning rather than a false block.
- Pending state is driven by the `positions` topic acknowledgement, not by the HTTP response alone.
- Storybook stories for every state including rejected and position-closed.

## Test plan
- **Unit/component (>=80%):** entry-mode recomputation across price/ticks/percent/R; ladder total validation; stop-not-removable behaviour; pending/rejected/closed state machine; native-versus-engine labelling.
- **Contract:** `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl` request/response and the `positions` payload fields (`managed_by`, `breakeven_armed`, translated distance).
- **E2E (Playwright web + Electron):** apply a percentage trail; attempt to clear the stop; ladder-total error; exchange rejection; position-closed-while-editing — added in E32-Q04.
- **a11y:** axe-core all states; full keyboard-equivalence script; screen-reader pass on the engine-managed note and on pending/rejected transitions.

## Security notes
Mutates protective state on a live (demo) position, so `security` handling applies. The UI cannot weaken protection: removal is impossible client-side and refused server-side (E32-T01/S04's ratchet), and any loosening override goes through the audited backend path with explicit confirmation. RBAC `positions:write`; the editor is read-only for the `viewer` role. No secrets client-side.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA, and this screen carries two explicit standing requirements from the catalogue: R-multiples and percentages are both shown, and the warning about engine-managed stops is a persistent, readable note rather than a tooltip. Additionally: keyboard equivalence to chart drag-to-modify is a first-class acceptance criterion; pending and rejected transitions are announced via `role="status"` / `role="alert"`; every numeric field is labelled with its unit; focus returns to the invoking position row on close.

## Performance notes
Amend round-trip target <=500 ms p95 (the screen's stated budget, aligned with budget #4's amend path). Entry-mode recomputation within one frame. The new SL/TP renders pending, never optimistically confirmed.

## Observability
Analytics on entry-mode switches and trail-kind selection. Audit events (`position.stop_modified`, `position.tp_ladder_set`) are server-emitted; the client surfaces the correlation id on failure.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; Storybook covers every state.
- [ ] Frontend coverage >=80%.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass; the keyboard-equivalence script passes.
- [ ] design-qa comparison against the E32-D07 pack (feeds E32-D08).
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-064 updated if behaviour diverged.
- [ ] QA sign-off from E32-Q02.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review on demo.
- [ ] Feature flag `ui.sltp_editor` recorded.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
`E32-S02` (TP ladders), `E32-S04` (trailing translation and its response contract), `E32-T03` (break-even state on the positions topic), `E32-D07` (signed-off design), `E30` (shell, environment badge, confirmation policy).

title: Emulated algos (OCO, iceberg, TWAP, chase)
body:
## Context
Bybit v5 exposes **no** OCO, iceberg (`displayQty`), TWAP or chase/peg order types through its public API (research digest 09 §2/§6, recorded in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §10). Traders still need them, so CandleViewer emulates them in the backend `AlgoSupervisor` (module **M14**, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §OMS) — never in the browser: a browser-resident algo dies with the tab, and a dead algo holding a working order is a risk event.

This epic builds that supervisor and the four emulated strategies the roadmap names for R3 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E33): **OCO**, **iceberg** (display-size slicing with randomisation), **TWAP** (duration, slice count, jitter) and **chase** (follow best bid/ask with a max-chase cap and a give-up condition) — plus the **algo monitor panel** so nothing ever runs invisibly. Every algo is crash-safe (state in Postgres, resumed on restart), disconnect-aware (`on_disconnect="freeze"` by default), subject to the kill-switch and risk lockouts (E39), and carries a visible **"emulated — not exchange-native"** badge (CMP-227 EstimatedBadge + CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice) everywhere it appears.

The scaled/ladder algo (`AlgoKind.scaled`), brackets (`bracket`) and trailing stops ship in **E32**; this epic does not re-implement them, but the supervisor framework it builds (E33-T01) is the one E32's strategies register into.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (domain ALGO, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §18):**
- **US-ALGO-002** Emulated OCO — *Must*
- **US-ALGO-005** Emulated iceberg — *Should*
- **US-ALGO-006** Emulated TWAP — *Should*
- **US-ALGO-007** Chase / pegged limit — *Should*
- **US-ALGO-010** Algorithm control panel — *Must*

(US-ALGO-001 brackets, -003 TP ladders, -004 scaled entries, -008 trailing stops and -009 DCA ladders belong to **E32**; they appear here only as the sibling strategies that share E33-T01's framework.)

**Screens:** SCR-066 TWAP builder · SCR-067 Iceberg (emulated) builder · SCR-068 Chase-limit builder · SCR-069 Emulated OCO / bracket builder (the OCO half; the bracket half is E32) · SCR-070 Algo monitor panel · SCR-063 Positions & orders panel (its **Algos** tab hosts SCR-070).

**Components:** CMP-118 AlgoProgressCard, CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-023 Progress Bar, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-123 FlattenAllButton, CMP-008 / CMP-100 / CMP-101 inputs, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-047 DatePicker, CMP-115 OrderTypeSelector (its "Emulated" group).

**Backend:** `AlgoSupervisor` in M14 — `packages/oms/algo/` with `supervisor.py`, `strategies/{oco,iceberg,twap,chase}.py`, `store.py`, `scheduler.py`; a Postgres migration adding `algo_runs` and `algo_slices` next to the existing `orders.algo` / `orders.algo_params` / `orders.parent_order_id` / `orders.oco_group_ref` columns (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.3); a wall-clock persisted scheduler; orphan adoption by `order_link_id`; feature flags `algo.oco`, `algo.iceberg`, `algo.twap`, `algo.chase`.

**API/WS:** `POST /api/v1/orders` with `algo: AlgoSpec` (already specified in `22-api-openapi.yaml`), `PATCH|DELETE /api/v1/orders/{orderId}`, `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all`, `GET /api/v1/orders`, `GET /api/v1/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`; algo control verbs (pause / resume / cancel / cancel-and-flatten / adopt) added as an OpenAPI delta in E33-T02; WS `orders`, `executions`, `positions`.

## Out of scope
- Brackets, TP ladders, scaled/DCA ladders, trailing stops — **E32**.
- OMS core state machine, reconciliation loop, blotters — **E29**.
- Order ticket form, sizing, arm/lock, hotkeys — **E30**; chart/DOM direct manipulation — **E31**.
- Trade-group fan-out and the rate-limit governor — **E34**. This epic *consumes* the per-account token buckets of `24-internal-schemas.md` §8; in R3 an algo run targets exactly one account, and group-level algos are explicitly deferred.
- Rule-engine-authored algos — **E35** (`origin="algo_child"` is excluded from rule scopes by design, §10.1 rule 5).
- Android; a separate admin app; non-Bybit venues; non-USDT-perp instruments.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every emulated strategy is available and labelled
  Given the algo feature flags are enabled on demo
  When I open the order ticket's emulated order-type group
  Then OCO, iceberg, TWAP and chase are offered, each opening its builder (SCR-066..069),
  and each builder states in text that the strategy is emulated by CandleViewer, not by Bybit

Scenario: Nothing runs invisibly
  Given one OCO, one iceberg, one TWAP and one chase are running across two accounts
  When I open the algo monitor panel
  Then all four are listed with type-specific progress, next action time and controls,
  reflecting server state reconciled at least every 30 seconds

Scenario: Crash safety across every strategy (failure)
  Given each strategy is running and the backend process is killed at a persistence seam
  When the process restarts
  Then every run resumes from Postgres within 5 seconds, adopts its resting children by
  order_link_id instead of duplicating them, and reaches a correct terminal state

Scenario: Risk control halts everything (edge)
  Given the kill-switch is engaged or a daily-loss lockout fires
  Then every running algo halts, working children are handled per each strategy's policy,
  each run ends in "halted by risk control" with the reason recorded and audited,
  and no run ever auto-resumes without an explicit re-arm
```

## Technical notes / design
`AlgoSupervisor` is the only component allowed to create `orders` rows with `intent='algo_child'` and `origin='algo_child'`. Universal rules from `24-internal-schemas.md` §10.1 are implemented once in the framework, not per strategy: (1) state persisted transactionally with each child submission; (2) `on_disconnect="freeze"` by default; (3) an entry algo's first fill triggers the native-SL attach (§8.8) — algos never place unprotected exposure; (4) children inherit the parent's `order_link_id` group segment with an incremented `seq2` and the `ac` suffix; (5) algo children are never themselves rule-managed.

Strategy selection is capability-driven (`ExchangeCapabilities`, §10.8) — `supports_native_oco/iceberg/twap/chase` are all `False` for Bybit, and there is no `if exchange == "bybit"` outside the adapter package.

## Test plan
Per-strategy unit suites (≥90 % on `packages/oms/algo` by local policy), contract tests on the `AlgoSpec` schema and the algo control endpoints, integration tests against recorded Bybit fixtures (partial fill, rejection, `10018`, `110017`, `110020`, WS disconnect), chaos tests killing the process at each seam, a k6 rate-budget soak for chase/iceberg, Playwright E2E for each builder and the monitor panel, and an a11y audit of SCR-066..070. Details in E33-Q01..Q06.

## Security notes
`area/oms-execution` order-placing paths are always `security`-labelled (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8). The epic's STRIDE model is E33-X01; the headline threats are (a) a runaway algo as a denial-of-wallet / self-inflicted-loss vector, (b) rate-budget exhaustion starving protective orders, (c) privilege escalation — a `viewer` or a manager without access to the account starting or cancelling an algo, (d) repudiation — every create/pause/resume/cancel must be audited with actor and parameters. Data classification: financial.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-066..070 are net-new UI and must meet WCAG 2.2 AA: progress exposed as text as well as bars, schedule previews as tables, emulation caveats as paragraphs (never tooltips), the degraded banner as `role="status"`, and every control naming its target algo and effect. Audited in E33-Q05.

## Performance notes
Order submit → ack p95 < 300 ms on demo (budget #4). OCO fill → opposing-leg cancel request ≤ 300 ms p95 (SCR-069). Chase reprice interval ≥ 200 ms with debounced targets. Monitor panel < 3 ms scripting per frame with 100 running algos, updates coalesced to 2 Hz (SCR-070).

## Observability
Audit events `algo.oco_created|leg_filled|leg_cancelled|race_resolved|residual_detected|cancelled|completed|failed`, `algo.iceberg_created|paused|resumed|cancelled|completed|failed|slice_replaced`, `algo.twap_created|paused|resumed|cancelled|completed|slice_failed`, `algo.chase_created|repriced|limit_reached|fell_back_to_market|cancelled|completed|failed`. Metrics `oms_emulated_algo_total{kind}`, `oms_algo_active{kind}`, `oms_algo_child_orders_total{kind}`, `oms_algo_resume_seconds`, `oms_oco_race_resolution_ms`, `oms_chase_repricings_total`. Traces span algo run → child submission → execution.

## Definition of Done (epic exit criteria)
1. All Gherkin scenarios of US-ALGO-002/005/006/007/010 pass in CI, including every failure and edge scenario written there (cancel-rejected-because-already-filled, crash between fill and cancel, duplicate fill delivery, manual flatten, slice rejected, dust remainder, kill-switch mid-algo, clock drift / missed windows, amend races a fill, flapping best price, orphan adoption after crash).
2. **Crash safety proven**: the chaos suite kills the backend at each persistence seam of each strategy; every algo resumes from Postgres and reaches a correct terminal state within 5 s of process start, with zero duplicated children.
3. **Safety invariant**: no algo path can open a position without a native exchange-side SL (R3 exit criterion 2); the algo path is one of the enumerated paths in that suite and has zero escapes.
4. **Kill-switch / lockout**: engaging either halts every running algo and lands each run in "halted by risk control" — audited, alerted, never auto-resumed.
5. **Chase invariant**: at most one live order per chase run, asserted before every placement and enforced by a DB unique partial index.
6. **OCO race**: fill → opposing-leg cancel/amend issued ≤ 300 ms p95; residual double fill detected from executions and corrected reduce-only with a high-severity incident.
7. **Monitor panel**: every running algo visible with type-specific progress, reconciled at least every 30 s, orphans listed with adopt/cancel, < 3 ms scripting per frame with 100 rows.
8. Design QA (E33-D07), a11y audit (E33-Q05), QA sign-off (E33-Q06) and Security sign-off (E33-X03) recorded; coverage ≥ 85 % on `packages/oms` (≥ 90 % on `packages/oms/algo`), ≥ 80 % frontend; zero open P0/P1; demoed on demo environment and accepted by the Owner.

## Story list
| Key | Kind | Title | Pts | Sprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E33-K01 | Spike | Emulated-algo scheduler & crash-resume seam spike | 2 | 17 |
| E33-T01 | Task | `AlgoSupervisor` framework: state store, scheduler, resume, orphan adoption | 5 | 17 |
| E33-T02 | Task | Algo control API, WS projection, feature flags and audit events | 3 | 17 |
| E33-S01 | Story | Emulated OCO (US-ALGO-002) | 5 | 17 |
| E33-S02 | Story | Emulated iceberg (US-ALGO-005) | 5 | 17 |
| E33-S03 | Story | Emulated TWAP (US-ALGO-006) | 5 | 18 |
| E33-S04 | Story | Chase / pegged limit (US-ALGO-007) | 5 | 18 |
| E33-S05 | Story | Algo builder modals SCR-066..069 | 3 | 18 |
| E33-S06 | Story | Algo monitor panel SCR-070 (US-ALGO-010) | 3 | 18 |
| E33-T03 | Chore | Reconcile plan docs and write ADR-0016 emulated-algo supervisor | 1 | 18 |

### Estimate reconciliation (roadmap vs. children)
The **Epic ticket's `estimate` field is `34`** — exactly the E33 allocation in the roadmap register (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.1 line for E33 and §7.2 E33). It is deliberately **not** a roll-up of every child ticket.

| Line | Tickets | Pts | Counts against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Engineering** | E33-K01, T01–T03, S01–S06 | **37** | the 34-pt roadmap allocation (within ±15 %: 28.9–39.1) ✔ |
| Design | E33-D01..D07 | 22 | design capacity line |
| QA | E33-Q01..Q06 | 22 | QA/SDET capacity line |
| Security | E33-X01..X03 | 8 | security capacity line |
| *(informational total)* | all children | *89* | not a planning figure |

Per `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` §resourcing, design, QA/SDET and security are **separate capacity lines** from the ~90 engineering pts/sprint; their tickets are sized so those specialists can be scheduled, and rolling them into the epic estimate would double-count against the engineering train. Any re-baselining of the 34 pts must be made in the roadmap register first and mirrored here.

## Risks
- **R11 Alert reliability** — an emulated algo is a promise the exchange never made; if the backend is down, slices stop. Mitigated by `on_disconnect="freeze"`, the always-present native SL, the degraded banner on SCR-070 and a residual-risk note in every builder.
- **R3 Real-time cost / rate limits** — chase repricing and iceberg refills are the highest request-rate paths in the product. Mitigated by `reprice_interval_ms ≥ 200`, debounced targets, per-account token buckets with a protective reserve (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8), and a projected-requests/min figure shown *before* submit.
- **R7 Data accuracy** — computing fills from intent rather than executions causes double positions. Mitigated by "executions are authoritative" in every strategy.
- **R5 Scope** — group-level algos and rule-driven algos are explicitly deferred to E34/E35.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E32** (bracket/native-SL machinery and the `AlgoKind` sibling strategies this framework must host), **E29** (OMS state machine, `order_link_id` scheme, reconciliation loop, WS order/execution stream), **E39** (kill-switch and risk lockouts that every algo must obey). Consumes E27 accounts/keys and E28 profiles transitively.

## Branch
