Two agents may work in parallel provided neither is in the other's `blocked_by` chain; agree shared interfaces (API/WS/DB/machine contracts) before either starts coding, and land the contract change (schemas/OpenAPI/WS/ADR chore ticket) before the stories that depend on it.

title: Black-box test plan for the four emulated strategies
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires an executed black-box test plan with a per-scenario sign-off before any Story reaches Done. The four strategies of this epic have an unusually large edge surface — US-ALGO-002, -005, -006 and -007 between them enumerate **26 Gherkin scenarios**, most of them failure or edge cases — and several are only reachable by fault injection (crash seams, duplicate WS delivery, rate-budget exhaustion, kill-switch mid-run). The plan must therefore specify not just what to verify but how to *produce* each condition.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box test plan document covering every Gherkin scenario of US-ALGO-002, US-ALGO-005, US-ALGO-006, US-ALGO-007, each with: preconditions, exact steps, expected observable result (UI, API, audit log, exchange state), and the method used to induce the condition.
- **Condition-induction cookbook**: how to force each abnormal state on demo — lot-size and minimum-notional rejections (undersized slice on a high-tick instrument), insufficient margin (deliberately over-leveraged sub-account), `10018` rate limiting (saturating the account budget), `110001` amend-after-fill (amend against a marketable order), post-only crossing rejection, duplicate WS execution delivery (fixture replay), kill-switch and daily-loss lockout activation, backend restart at a chosen seam, and a flapping best price (synthetic book fixture).
- A **cross-strategy invariant matrix** checked for every strategy: no unprotected position; no duplicated child after restart; executions (not intent) drive filled quantities; the protective rate reserve is never consumed; every state transition is audited.
- Traceability table mapping every scenario to its automated test (where automated) or to a manual step (where not), satisfying §3.2's "manual step with a Task filed to automate it".
- Exit report template for the per-story sign-offs on S01–S04.

## Out of scope
E2E automation (Q02). Perf/load scripts (Q03). Chaos automation (Q04). A11y audit (Q05). UI-specific exploratory testing (Q06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every story scenario is covered
  Given US-ALGO-002, 005, 006 and 007
  Then every Gherkin scenario in each story maps to a numbered plan step with preconditions,
  steps, expected result and induction method

Scenario: Abnormal conditions are reproducible
  Given the condition-induction cookbook
  When a tester follows any entry on the demo environment
  Then the intended exchange or system error is produced reliably,
  verified by each entry being executed at least once during plan authoring

Scenario: Invariants are checked per strategy (edge)
  Given the cross-strategy invariant matrix
  Then each of the five invariants is verified separately for OCO, iceberg, TWAP and chase,
  with the evidence source named (audit row, exchange query, database query)

Scenario: Gaps are visible (edge)
  Given a scenario that cannot be automated in this train
  Then it is marked manual, a follow-up automation Task is filed and linked,
  and the deviation is recorded rather than silently accepted
```

## Technical notes / design
Observable truth for a black-box check is the **exchange** (`GET /v5/order/realtime`, `/v5/position/list`) and the **audit log**, not the UI — the UI is a third assertion, never the only one. The plan states, per step, which of the three is authoritative.

Use a dedicated demo sub-account per strategy so parallel execution does not cross-contaminate position state.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the test plan; its own quality gate is a peer review by the second QA/SDET plus the OMS tech lead confirming that each expected result is stated precisely enough to fail a wrong implementation.

## Security notes
Test steps must never use live keys; the plan states demo-only in its preamble and the induction cookbook contains no credential material. Abuse-flavoured steps (rate saturation) are coordinated with E33-X02 so they are run once, not twice.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend-focused plan; a11y is Q05.

## Performance notes
N/A — perf is Q03, though the plan records observed submit→ack times as context.

## Observability
Every plan step names the audit event(s) it expects, which doubles as a check that the events specified in `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-066..070 are actually emitted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan document merged and linked from S01–S04.
- [ ] Every cookbook entry executed at least once and confirmed reproducible.
- [ ] Peer-reviewed by the second QA/SDET and the OMS tech lead.
- [ ] Traceability table complete; automation gaps filed as Tasks.
- [ ] QA lead sign-off recorded.

## Dependencies
E33-T02 (control verbs and `GET /algos` give the plan its observation surface). E29 for the demo accounts and fixture harness.

## Branch
`chore/e33-qa-test-plan` (docs only).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §18 ALGO (US-ALGO-002, 005, 006, 007, 010)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-066 TWAP builder, SCR-067 Iceberg (emulated) builder, SCR-068 Chase-limit builder, SCR-069 Emulated OCO / bracket builder, SCR-070 Algo monitor panel, SCR-063 Positions & orders panel (Algos tab)

- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.18 ALGO rows
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `POST /orders`, `PATCH /orders/{orderId}`, `DELETE /orders/{orderId}`, `POST /orders/cancel-all`, `GET /orders`, `GET /orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`; schemas `AlgoSpec`, `AlgoKind`, `OrderIntent`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` private topics `orders`, `executions`, `positions`; `algo_kind` enum in the order frames (§13)

- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §10 Emulated order algorithms (§10.1 common model, §10.2 OCO, §10.3 iceberg, §10.4 TWAP, §10.5 chase, §10.8 capability-driven selection), §8 OMS state machine, §8.5 reconciliation, §8.8 native-SL attach, §8 rate-limit token buckets

- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0006-oms-state-machine.md`, `ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md`, `ADR-0012-testing-pyramid.md`, `ADR-0014-observability.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E33, §7.3 exit criteria 2, §7.4 R3 quality gates
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2 budget #4
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (test pyramid, coverage floors, fixture policy, chaos)
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (PRR gates, soak)
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `CONSTITUTION.md #scope-guardrails-and-invariants`
2. `AGENTS.md #0-read-these-first`
3. `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md#b4--emulatedalgo---oco`
4. `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md#b5--emulatedalgo---iceberg`
5. `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md#b6--emulatedalgo---twap`
6. `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md#b7--emulatedalgo---chase`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `services/api/oms/`
- `services/api/tests/oms/`
- `machines/emulated-algo.machine.json`

**Interfaces you must not break**
- REST algo control endpoints (`/algos/*`); WS `algos` projection topic; machine B4-B7 EmulatedAlgo events (ARM, TICK, ADOPT, CRASH_RESUME)

**Commands**
- `ruff check .`, `black --check .`, `mypy --strict .`, `pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`, `pytest -m integration` (if touching persistence/OMS), `lint-imports`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e33-blackbox-test-plan-for`
- PR title: `E33-Q01: Black-box test plan for the four emulated strategies`
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend (+ @CandleViewer/security for oms/risk/rules paths)
- Labels: type/test, area/oms-execution, priority/p1, qa

**Done means**
- All Gherkin scenarios in `## Acceptance criteria` pass as automated tests referencing the scenario name.
- Coverage gate met for touched files/packages (frontend >=80%, backend `--cov-fail-under=85`).
- CI required checks green (lint, typecheck, unit, and any contract-suite/a11y/perf gate this ticket triggers).
- Security review / abuse-case notes recorded where the ticket carries the `security` label.
- Definition of Done checklist in the ticket body fully checked off.

**Do NOT**
- Do not create/manage statechart interpreters outside `cv.statechart.factory` (ADR-0016, C-hot-path).
- Do not widen ticket scope beyond `## Scope / Deliverables`; split into a follow-up ticket instead.
- Do not edit already-applied Alembic migrations; add a new migration.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the GitHub issue for `E33-Q01` naming the exact blocking ticket/gate; set Status -> Blocked on the board; never silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or bypass CI checks to get green.

title: Design handoff package for the fan-out ticket and trade-group manager
body:
## Context
SCR-061 (trade-group ticket) and SCR-062 (trade-group manager) are the two screens E34 introduces. Both are new interaction territory: no prior screen in the product asks a user to reason about *N simultaneous executions with different sizes on different accounts*, and both have a failure state — a partially-executed fan-out — that `14-screens-catalogue.md` requires to be **"drawn as the primary design case, not an afterthought"**.

The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence) applies: no frontend work on E34-S04/S05 (Sprint 19) starts until the design tickets are Status=Done, and they must have been Done for ≥2 sprints.

This is the gate the FE stories wait on: `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 makes a Story not-Ready until its linked design ticket is Done and has been Done for ≥2 sprints. E34-S04 and E34-S05 run in Sprint 19, so this package must be Done in Sprint 17.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Consolidated handoff package: final Figma frames for every SCR-061 and SCR-062 state, redlines, token map, copy deck (every message, error, confirmation and empty-state string in final wording), iconography, and the reduced-motion specs.
- **Component mapping table**: every region of both screens mapped to a catalogue component id (CMP-041, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-075, CMP-100, CMP-101, CMP-102, CMP-105, CMP-106, CMP-107, CMP-119, CMP-121, CMP-123, CMP-124, CMP-158, CMP-229, CMP-231, CMP-232), naming which are reused unchanged, which gain a new variant, and which are new — with a design-system ticket referenced for each new variant.
- **State → data mapping**: each visual state annotated with the API/WS field that produces it (`TradeGroupStatus`, leg `status`, `error.code`, `skipped_reason`, deferral deadline, `native_sl_confirmed`, `unwind_incomplete`, divergence), so the FE engineer never guesses which server value drives which pixel.
- Accessibility annotations carried over from D04 (roles, names, focus order, live regions, the screen-reader script).
- A recorded handoff walkthrough with the implementing FE engineers for E34-S04 and E34-S05, plus a written Q&A log appended to this ticket.
- Updates to `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-061/SCR-062 so the plan doc matches the final design.

## Out of scope
- Implementation → E34-S04/S05. Post-build comparison → E34-D06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state has a data source
  Given the state → data mapping table
  Then every visual state names the API or WS field and value that produces it
  And no state exists that the backend cannot actually emit

Scenario: Copy is final
  Then every user-visible string across both screens appears in the copy deck in final wording, including error and empty-state text
  And the recovery-action vocabulary matches D01's decision and the API error copy

Scenario: Handoff actually happened
  Then a walkthrough with both implementing engineers is recorded on the ticket with a Q&A log
  And this ticket is Done no later than Sprint 17, two sprints before the consuming stories
```

## Technical notes / design
The state → data mapping is the highest-value artefact here: it is what prevents the FE from inventing client-side status derivation, which is explicitly forbidden (the server derives group status — E34-T01).

## Test plan
A "can you build it without asking?" check: a designer-free FE engineer reads the package and lists any question; any question found becomes a package gap and is filled before sign-off.

## Security notes
The package must state explicitly that all client-side guards (arm state, SL presence, override limits, account scope) are UX affordances only and are re-enforced server-side, so no engineer implements the UI as if it were the control.

## Accessibility notes
All D04 annotations are part of the package; the FE DoD for E34-S04/S05 references them directly.

## Performance notes
Package states the 300 ms preview and 1.5 s group-ack budgets alongside the loading/skeleton treatments that must hold while they elapse.

## Observability
Package names the client telemetry events the screens should emit (`ui_fanout_*`, `ui_group_action_*`) so they are designed in, not bolted on.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts published in Figma, linked on this ticket, and the matching `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated to match.
- [ ] Every state from the screen-catalogue entry drawn: previewing, ready, partial-send in progress, partial failure, rate-limit backoff, blocked (account in lockout), empty, loading, error.
- [ ] The screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `14-screens-catalogue.md` ticked item-by-item by the CDO or delegate, recorded as a comment.
- [ ] a11y annotations present: focus order, roles, live-region usage, contrast tokens, ≥24 px hit targets, text equivalents for every colour-coded state.
- [ ] Status=Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming FE story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).
- [ ] Handoff walkthrough held with the implementing FE engineer and recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] Design tokens used are existing `16-design-system-brief.md` tokens, or a design-system contribution ticket is filed for any new one.

- [ ] Component mapping and state → data mapping tables complete and reviewed by the Architect.
- [ ] Status=Done in Sprint 17 (two sprints before E34-S04/S05 in Sprint 19).

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E34-D04** (no handoff with open a11y blockers).

## Branch
`design/e34-handoff`.

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 (E34 scope row), §7.3 exit criteria 3 & 4, §7.4 quality gates, §11.1 dependency graph
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §3 PROF (US-PROF-005..008), §17 ORD (US-ORD-001, US-ORD-010, US-ORD-013, US-ORD-014)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-061, SCR-062, SCR-063
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-041, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-075, CMP-100, CMP-101, CMP-102, CMP-105, CMP-106, CMP-107, CMP-119, CMP-121, CMP-123, CMP-124, CMP-158, CMP-229, CMP-231, CMP-232
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` rows US-PROF-005..008, SCR-061, SCR-062

title: Write the black-box test plan for trade-group fan-out
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` §SDLC requires a black-box QA test plan per feature, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes QA sign-off non-skippable for every Story. E34 has two properties that make a written plan indispensable rather than ceremonial: its most important behaviours (partial failure, rate-limit deferral, unwind) are **hard to produce by accident**, and its acceptance depends on *what did not happen* (no leg without a stop, no silent drop, no double close) as much as on what did.

This ticket writes the plan before the code exists, from the specification, so it tests the requirement rather than the implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box test plan document at `qa/plans/E34-trade-group-fanout.md` covering every story in the epic, organised as scenario → preconditions → steps → expected → evidence to capture.
- Coverage of, at minimum:
  - **Preview (E34-S01):** mixed-profile sizing, skip vs failure vs warn classification, below-minimum handling, stale-equity handling, out-of-scope account, side-effect-freeness.
  - **Execution (E34-S02):** 3- and 5-account success; per-profile sizing correctness checked against a hand-computed expectation; native SL present on every leg verified **at the exchange**, not in our UI; `all_or_none` pre-validation rejecting without sending; `best_effort` deferral; idempotent re-submit; arm-token and kill-switch refusal.
  - **Partial failure and unwind (E34-S03):** 2-of-5 rejection; retry-failed; unwind-accepted; unwind restart; fill-during-unwind; qty drift; deadline exceeded → incomplete with residual still protected; divergence badge within 30 s.
  - **Group actions:** close 50% with heterogeneous lot sizes; move stop across legs with different offsets; cancel working orders; per-leg result reporting.
  - **UI (E34-S04/S05):** every catalogue state; confirmation copy restating leg counts; Viewer/Manager/Owner RBAC rendering.
- **Environment and data plan**: which demo accounts, which profiles, which symbols, how to force each failure (fault-injection hooks, fixture names, feature flags), and how to return the environment to a flat, clean state after each run.
- **Exploratory charter set** (session-based, 90 min each) with explicit charters, e.g. "explore what happens when an account's key is revoked between preview and send", "explore rapid repeated sends of the same group", "explore browser tab close mid-fan-out".
- Traceability table mapping every plan scenario to a US id and to an acceptance criterion of the implementing ticket, so gaps are visible.

## Out of scope
- Executing the plan → E34-Q06 (and per-story QA sign-off). Automation → E34-Q02/Q03/Q04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Must story is covered
  Given US-PROF-006, US-PROF-007, US-PROF-008, US-ORD-010, US-ORD-013 and US-ORD-014
  When the traceability table is reviewed
  Then every scenario in those stories maps to at least one plan case, and every plan case maps back to a story or an acceptance criterion

Scenario: Failure states are reachable
  Given each negative scenario in the plan
  Then the plan names the concrete mechanism used to produce it (fault-injection hook, fixture, flag, or manual exchange action)
  And no scenario is documented as "observe if it happens"

Scenario: The environment returns to clean
  Then each case ends with a stated teardown that leaves all demo accounts flat with no working orders
```

## Technical notes / design
The "verify at the exchange, not in our UI" rule is the plan's backbone for the safety invariant: every SL assertion is made by querying Bybit demo directly (`GET /v5/position/list`, `GET /v5/order/realtime`), because a UI that believes a stop exists is exactly the failure mode we are guarding against.

## Test plan
Self-referential: the plan is reviewed by the Architect and a backend engineer for scenarios the spec implies but the plan misses; the review is recorded.

## Security notes
The plan includes the abuse cases from E34-X02 as black-box cases (out-of-scope account, tampered quantity, replayed idempotency key, forged arm token) so security behaviour is verified by QA as well as by the security track. Demo keys only; the plan must forbid using live keys anywhere.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes the keyboard-only and screen-reader walkthroughs for SCR-061/062 as black-box cases, using D04's screen-reader script as the expected result. The formal audit remains E34-Q05.

## Performance notes
The plan records where the budget assertions live (preview ≤300 ms, group ack ≤1.5 s p95) and that they are measured by E34-Q03 rather than by stopwatch during manual runs.

## Observability
Each case names the metric or audit row that should also confirm the outcome (e.g. `oms_fanout_deferred_total` for the deferral case, `trade_group.unwound` for the unwind case) — cross-checking behaviour against telemetry catches silent instrumentation gaps.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test assets committed under the repo's test tree and wired into CI where automatable.
- [ ] Execution evidence attached (run log, k6 summary, Playwright report, axe report, chaos run notes).
- [ ] Defects filed as Bug tickets with `priority/*`, linked to this ticket and to the offending Story.
- [ ] Coverage/quality-gate impact recorded; no existing gate weakened.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E34-D05** (final states and copy must be known to write expected results) and **E28** (profile semantics the sizing expectations are computed from).

title: STRIDE threat model for trade-group fan-out and the rate governor
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 names E34 in the R3 security gate: **"STRIDE for E27, E29, E34, E35, E39, E42 — all Critical/High closed"**, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 requires the STRIDE kickoff to be scheduled for any epic touching auth, keys, OMS, fan-out or money movement — all four of which E34 touches.

Fan-out is the product's largest blast radius in a single request: one authenticated call places orders across every account the caller can reach. The model must be complete before E34-S02 (the order-placing path) starts, which is why this ticket lands in Sprint 17 while S02 is in Sprint 18.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model at `docs/security/threat-models/E34-trade-group-fanout.md` covering the full data flow: client → API gateway (authn/z, RBAC scope, rate limiter) → `TradeGroupFanout` (resolution, risk gate, admission control) → `AccountRateBudget` → M4 `RestClient` (signing, key retrieval from the M2 vault) → Bybit, plus the return paths (private WS → OMS → `trade_groups` topic → client) and the persistence (`trade_groups`, `trade_group_legs`, `unwind_plans`, `audit_log`).
- Per-element analysis across all six STRIDE categories, with at minimum these threats enumerated, rated (likelihood × impact) and mitigated:
  - **S**: forged or replayed `arm_token`; replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; session fixation on a long-lived trading session; a compromised client impersonating the rule engine as the group's origin.
  - **T**: client-supplied per-leg quantity overriding server-resolved sizing (US-PROF-002 NFR); overrides widening a hard risk cap (US-PROF-008 NFR forbids it); tampering with `profile_snapshot` after the fact; modifying an unwind plan row to skip a step.
  - **R**: a fan-out with no per-leg audit row; an unwind whose plan was never persisted before the first request; audit hash-chain gaps around group actions.
  - **I**: another user's account labels, balances or sizing leaking via the preview response, the group list, or the `trade_groups` WS topic; error messages disclosing the existence of out-of-scope accounts (403-vs-404 oracle); key material in logs or traces.
  - **D**: a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; a malicious or buggy client driving preview at high rate; unbounded unwind retries against a failing exchange; WS subscription amplification on `trade_groups`.
  - **E**: a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`; a Viewer reaching a mutating endpoint directly; the rule engine acting with more authority than its originating user; test/chaos hooks (`CV_TEST_HOOKS`, `CV_CHAOS_HOOKS`) reachable in a deployed environment.
- Explicit treatment of the **safety invariant as a security property**: any path that could open a position without a native SL is modelled as a tampering/DoS-of-safety threat, not merely a bug.
- Mitigation mapping: each threat → the concrete control (code location, config key, test) → the ticket that implements it, with anything unmitigated raised as a new ticket before S02 starts.
- Data-classification table for every field crossing a boundary (account ids, balances, sizing, keys-by-reference, audit rows).
- Review session with the Architect, the Backend lead and the Owner; outcomes recorded.

## Out of scope
- Penetration testing → E43 (pre-live). Key vault internals → E27/ADR-0009. RBAC model itself → E09/ADR-0010 (consumed here).
- Implementation of mitigations → the engineering tickets; this ticket only specifies and tracks them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Complete coverage
  Given every element and data flow in the fan-out architecture
  When the model is reviewed
  Then each element has all six STRIDE categories considered, with either a threat and a mitigation or an explicit "not applicable" and why

Scenario: Nothing Critical or High is unowned
  Given the rated threat list
  Then every Critical and High threat names a mitigating control and the ticket that delivers it
  And any threat without an existing mitigation has a new ticket filed before E34-S02 starts

Scenario: The model gates the code
  Given E34-S02 is an order-placing path
  Then it cannot enter Ready until this model is Done, per 02-definition-of-ready-done.md §3.1 security-ready
```

## Technical notes / design
Model at the level of `20-architecture.md` §10.2's sequence, not at class level, so the model survives refactoring. Use the existing product-wide threat-model template from `04-security-program.md`. Record explicitly that the governor is a **security control** (availability of protective traffic), so a change to its parameters is a security-relevant change requiring review.

## Test plan
Each Critical/High mitigation must name a test that proves it; those tests are implemented in E34-X02 and in the owning engineering ticket. A mitigation with no test is recorded as unverified and blocks the gate.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security note for the epic. Data classification: financial/execution data, account scope, secrets-by-reference. Review label: yes, permanently, for every ticket in E34 (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8).

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The model must not propose a control that breaches budget #4 — e.g. a synchronous per-leg permission round trip. Where a control costs latency, the cost is stated and accepted explicitly.

## Observability
Specifies the security-relevant telemetry the epic must emit: audit rows per leg, `oms_fanout_rejected_total{reason="forbidden"}`, failed-authorization counters, and alerting on any attempt to fan out to an out-of-scope account (which is either a bug or an attack and is never routine).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded in `docs/security/threat-models/E34-trade-group-fanout.md`.
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding fixed, or accepted-risk signed by the Owner, before the R3 train closes (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 Security gate).
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment on this ticket.
- [ ] Any new detection rule / abuse-case test committed and running in CI.

title: Build the determinism suite and the rule-engine end-to-end tests
body:
## Context
Two gates converge in this ticket. R3 exit criterion 6: "Rule runtime is deterministic over replay: the same recorded window produces the same action sequence across runs." And the R3 E2E quality gate: "Playwright web + Electron covering ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, bracket, fan-out, **rule creation in both editors**, alert firing, journal capture."

Determinism is the property that makes everything else in this epic testable — if the same input can produce two different action sequences, no simulation result means anything and no firing can be explained. It is also the property most easily broken by an innocuous change (a dict iteration, a wall-clock read, an unordered set), which is why it needs a permanent automated gate rather than a one-off verification.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Determinism suite**: run a fixed set of recorded replay windows (from E26) through the engine N times (N>=3, and >=10 in the nightly run) with a corpus of armed-in-simulate rules, asserting byte-identical sequences of `RuleEvent` records, planned actions, timestamps and `skipped_reason` values.
  - Include windows chosen to be awkward: a dead market where `on_bar_close` fires with no trades, a burst where `on_price_update` fires thousands of times, a window containing a feed gap, and one spanning a UTC day boundary (for `once_per=day` and daily counters).
  - Assert cross-process determinism too — run in separate processes with different `PYTHONHASHSEED` values, which is how unordered-iteration bugs surface.
- **E2E suite (Playwright, web and Electron)** covering the rule-engine journeys this epic owns:
  1. Create a rule via the API, simulate it over a recorded window, read the coverage statement, arm it on demo, observe it fire, open its firing in SCR-087 and follow the link to the resulting order.
  2. The **editor-switch test for every construct in the metric/action vocabulary** required by US-RULE-006's NFR — driven through the real UI, asserting the round-trip indicator state and that the IR hash is unchanged.
  3. Attempt to arm without a simulation, with an open safety warning, and on an account without permission — each refused with its specific reason.
  4. Two conflicting rules: detection at arm time, precedence set through SCR-086, arbitration observed in the firing log with one action superseded.
  5. Export a rule, re-import it, assert no account ids or armed state in the bundle and that the import lands disarmed.
  6. Inspect a rule's canonical IR in SCR-088 and confirm the round-trip diff is empty.
- **Contract test suite** for all thirteen `/rules*` operations and the `rules` WS topic, replaying every documented example from `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Wiring into CI with the determinism suite as a **required check** on PRs touching the evaluator.

## Out of scope
- The compiler-level round-trip property suite — **E35-Q02** (this ticket covers the UI-level switch test).
- Load and performance measurement — **E35-Q04**; chaos — **E35-Q05**.
- E2E for the editors' own authoring interactions — E36/E37 own those; this ticket covers the switch and the IR equivalence.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The same window always produces the same actions
  Given a recorded replay window and a corpus of simulate-mode rules
  When the window is replayed ten times across separate processes with differing hash seeds
  Then the sequence of rule events, planned actions and skip reasons is identical in every run

Scenario: A dead market still fires scheduled rules (edge case)
  Given a replay window with no trades for several bar intervals
  When an on_bar_close rule is evaluated
  Then it fires on schedule in every run, because a bar closes on the clock even with no trade

Scenario: Every vocabulary construct survives an editor switch
  Given one rule per construct in the metric and action vocabulary
  When each is opened in the other editor and returned through the real UI
  Then the round-trip indicator reports identical and the IR hash is unchanged

Scenario: Arming preconditions are enforced through the UI and the API (failure case)
  Given a rule with no completed simulation on its current version
  When arming is attempted through the dialog and then by a crafted API call
  Then both are refused with the same reason and no mode change occurs

Scenario: A non-deterministic regression is caught (failure case)
  Given a deliberately introduced unordered iteration in the evaluator
  When the determinism suite runs
  Then it fails and names the first divergent event
```

## Technical notes / design
Determinism assertions compare a normalised event stream: strip wall-clock fields that are legitimately variable (`duration_ms`, absolute `started_at`) and compare everything that is supposed to be a function of the input — event order, `node_ref`, condition results, metric values, planned actions, `skipped_reason`. Be explicit about which fields are excluded and why, in a comment, because a lenient comparison quietly stops testing anything.

The `PYTHONHASHSEED` variation is the highest-value trick here: most non-determinism in Python engines comes from iterating a set or a dict built from unordered input, and it is invisible in a single-process run.

The Electron E2E run covers the same journeys as the web run; per `03-testing-strategy.md` both targets are required for R3. Keep the journey definitions shared and the drivers thin so the two do not diverge.

E2E tests run against staging (demo) with seeded accounts and recorded fixtures, never against live — and the suite must assert, via a network spy, that no request reached a live endpoint during a simulation-mode journey.

## Test plan
This is test code. Its own guard is the fifth acceptance scenario (a deliberately introduced non-determinism must fail the suite). Runtime budgets: determinism suite under 6 minutes in PR CI (3 repeats) and unbounded nightly (10 repeats); E2E suite under 15 minutes.

## Security notes
Journey 3 and journey 5 are security journeys: arming-precondition bypass and export content. They must run in CI as ordinary tests rather than being treated as a security-team activity, because a control that is only checked during a security review regresses between reviews. No real credentials appear in any fixture; demo accounts are seeded with test keys held in the CI secret store.

## Accessibility notes
The E2E suite includes a keyboard-only variant of the arming journey (journey 1) since SCR-085's keyboard path is a named requirement; the comprehensive a11y audit is E35-Q06.

## Performance notes
Not a performance suite, but it must not become the slowest gate on the queue: budgets above are enforced, and the nightly deep run carries the expensive repetitions.

## Observability
On failure the determinism suite emits the first divergent event with its full context, and the E2E suite captures traces, screenshots and the server logs for the window — a failing E2E without an artefact is a flake report, not a bug report.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed to the repository (plan document, suites, fixtures, scripts) and runnable by any engineer from a documented command.
- [ ] Results recorded on the ticket with pass/fail per scenario and links to CI runs.
- [ ] Any defect found is filed as a Bug with reproduction steps, expected vs actual, severity, and the test layer that should have caught it earlier.
- [ ] New automated suites wired into CI with their runtime budget agreed, and marked required where the roadmap's quality gates demand it.

- [ ] Sign-off comment posted; no P0/P1 defects open against the covered scope.
- [ ] The determinism suite is a **required check** for PRs touching the evaluator package; the E2E suite runs on the merge queue and nightly.

title: Build the rule-engine performance and load benchmarks
body:
## Context
The rule engine sits on the hot path twice: as an always-on evaluator reacting to the same tick stream that drives the charts, and as a synchronous `pre_trade_check` veto inside the order submission path, which is governed by budget #4 (order submit → ack p95 <300 ms, a hard R3 gate).

The published budgets this ticket must measure are scattered across the specification: evaluation within `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms` (250 ms default); `POST /rules/validate` <=300 ms; compile + round-trip diff <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node rule; conflict detection <=1 s for 500 rules; a 14-day single-symbol simulation <=60 s; SCR-087 10k rows within 8 ms scripting per frame. Without an automated benchmark each of these is an aspiration.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Evaluator benchmark**: N armed rules (N in 10, 50, 200, 500) over a recorded high-activity window, measuring evaluation latency p50/p95/p99 per trigger type, total CPU, and the metric-memoisation hit rate (ten rules referencing `atr(14)` must cost one computation — assert it, do not assume it).
- **`pre_trade_check` micro-benchmark**: latency distribution of the synchronous veto path, asserting it consumes a negligible share of the 300 ms submit→ack budget and that its own 25 ms budget holds at the 99th percentile with the built-in `sys.*` pre-trade rules enabled.
- **API benchmarks** (k6): `/rules/validate` and `/rules/{id}/compile` at a 100-node document against their 300 ms and 500 ms p95 budgets; `GET /rules` paging a 500-rule dataset; `GET /rules/{id}/runs` paging a 100k-run history.
- **Conflict-detection benchmark** over a seeded 500-rule dataset against the 1 s budget.
- **Simulation benchmark**: 14 days of one symbol at 1-minute granularity against the 60 s budget, including the streamed-partial-results behaviour.
- **Log write-path benchmark**: sustained matched-run write throughput, asserting logging adds <=1 ms to an evaluation at p99 and that the queue's back-pressure drop order is respected under saturation.
- **Frontend budget check**: SCR-087 with a 10k-row fixture measured against the 8 ms scripting-per-frame budget.
- CI wiring with recorded baselines and a regression threshold that fails the build on a breach, so a regression surfaces same-day rather than at the R3 gate.

## Out of scope
- Chaos and failure-injection — **E35-Q05**.
- Optimisation work itself — that is filed as Tasks against the owning story if a budget is breached.
- The platform-wide load profile (WS fan-out, ingestion soak) — the performance epic and E05/E08 own those; this ticket measures the rule engine's share.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every published budget is measured
  Given the budgets for evaluation, validate, compile, conflict detection, simulation and the fire-history table
  When the benchmark suite runs
  Then each produces a recorded number compared against its budget with a pass or fail

Scenario: Memoisation is proven, not assumed
  Given ten armed rules each referencing atr(14) on the same symbol and timeframe
  When a trigger fires for all ten
  Then the metric is computed once and the cache-hit counter confirms it

Scenario: The pre-trade veto does not endanger the submit budget (failure case)
  Given the built-in pre-trade rules enabled
  When order submission is benchmarked
  Then the rule-engine contribution stays within its 25 ms budget at p99 and the end-to-end submit to ack p95 remains under 300 ms

Scenario: A regression fails the build (failure case)
  Given a change that increases p99 evaluation latency beyond the agreed threshold over baseline
  When CI runs the benchmark
  Then the build fails naming the regressed metric, its baseline and its new value

Scenario: Logging degrades gracefully under saturation (edge case)
  Given the log write queue saturated
  When the benchmark applies sustained load
  Then non-matched simulate records are dropped first, matched runs and errors are never dropped, and the drop counter increments
```

## Technical notes / design
Benchmarks run on a pinned runner profile so numbers are comparable run to run; a benchmark on variable hardware measures the hardware. Record the profile alongside the results.

Use recorded replay windows rather than synthetic tick generators for the evaluator benchmark — synthetic uniform ticks understate the cost of the bursty real distribution, which is exactly where the timeout risk lives.

For the 500-rule case, scope the rules across multiple symbols and accounts so per-scope-instance expansion is exercised: 500 rules over 10 symbols is 5 000 instances, which is the number that actually matters.

Regression thresholds should be generous enough not to flake (suggest 15% over baseline on p99) but tight enough to catch a real regression; agree the number with the Architect and record it in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Test plan
This is measurement code. Its guard is a self-check that the harness detects a deliberately inserted 50 ms sleep in the evaluation path.

## Security notes
Benchmarks run against staging (demo) with seeded data and no real credentials. One security-relevant finding class to watch for: if the evaluator's cost scales badly with rule count, a user could create many rules as an accidental denial of service — if the numbers suggest that, file it against the STRIDE model in E35-X01 rather than only as a performance note.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — measurement infrastructure, except that the SCR-087 frontend budget check protects the usability of the log for everyone, including assistive-technology users whose stack is more sensitive to heavy DOM work.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance deliverable. Budgets restated: evaluation within 250 ms default timeout; `pre_trade_check` within 25 ms p99; validate <=300 ms; compile+diff <=500 ms p95 at 100 nodes; conflict detection <=1 s at 500 rules; simulation <=60 s for 14 days of one symbol; log write <=1 ms added at p99; SCR-087 <=8 ms scripting per frame at 10k rows.

## Observability
Results are published to the CI performance dashboard with the run's commit and runner profile, and the measured numbers are folded into `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and E35-T06's documentation reconciliation so future work compares against reality.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed to the repository (plan document, suites, fixtures, scripts) and runnable by any engineer from a documented command.
- [ ] Results recorded on the ticket with pass/fail per scenario and links to CI runs.
- [ ] Any defect found is filed as a Bug with reproduction steps, expected vs actual, severity, and the test layer that should have caught it earlier.
- [ ] New automated suites wired into CI with their runtime budget agreed, and marked required where the roadmap's quality gates demand it.
- [ ] Reviewed by the second QA/SDET and by the rule-engine backend lead.
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted; no P0/P1 defects open against the covered scope.
- [ ] Baselines recorded and the regression threshold agreed with the Architect and documented in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-Q03** (a working end-to-end path to benchmark). Consumes **E26** replay windows. Its numbers feed **E35-T06** and the R3 PRR.

title: Build the rule simulation panel and the rule arming dialog
body:
## Context
These two screens are the human gate between "a rule I wrote" and "a rule that trades". SCR-084 is the evidence and SCR-085 is the decision, and the product deliberately couples them: a rule cannot be armed without a completed simulation on its exact `ir_hash` (E35-S01, `22-api-openapi.yaml` arming preconditions), and `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.7's new-rule gate makes simulate the mandatory on-ramp.

Both screens carry copy requirements that are part of the specification rather than decoration. SCR-084: "Simulation replays recorded market data. Fills are modelled, not real; results are not a guarantee." SCR-085: "If the backend stops, this rule stops. Native stops stay." Those sentences manage risk R12 (backtest bias) and the user's mental model of what automation guarantees; they ship verbatim.

Design must be Status=Done for >=2 sprints before this story starts (design-ahead rule), which is why E35-D02/D05 sit in S15 and S16.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-084 Rule simulation / backtest panel** (page section or drawer from either editor): range, symbol and account selectors; the available-history statement rendered from the API's true coverage ("history available: 13 of 14 days (recording started 09-01)"); run with progress and cancel; result summary (fires, actions by type, errors); the per-firing timeline with the triggering context; "open in chart at this moment" deep link; CSV export.
  States: idle, running (cancellable), completed, **partial** (history gaps listed explicitly with the missing windows), failed, **no-history** (CTA to record the symbol).
- **SCR-085 Rule arming dialog** (modal): environment radio group with **DEMO preselected**; scope confirmation expanding a trade group into an explicit account list; the safety summary (does it place orders? can it flatten? does it depend on estimated detectors?); engine-availability note; conflict warning linking to SCR-086 when another armed rule targets the same scope; typed confirmation plus step-up 2FA for LIVE; the disarm path.
  Validation: cannot arm a failing-validation rule; cannot arm live on an account the user cannot trade; `flatten_all_positions` needs an extra acknowledgement.
- **Components**: CMP-154 RuleSimulatePanel, CMP-023 Progress Bar, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-047 DateRangePicker, CMP-049 Table, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-159 RuleConflictWarning, CMP-233 RuleOptions.
- **Data**: `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/simulate`, progress on WS `rules`, results via `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs`; `PUT /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/mode` with the step-up token.
- Analytics/audit emission: `rule.simulation_started|completed|cancelled`, `rule.armed`.

## Out of scope
- The editors that host the panel (SCR-081/082) — E36/E37; this story ships the panel as a mountable surface with a route-level demo host.
- The conflict resolver modal (SCR-086) — **E35-S09**; this story only links to it.
- Step-up MFA mechanics — **E09**; this story invokes it.
- The chart deep link's target rendering — E11/E26.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Simulation reports coverage honestly
  Given a requested 14-day range where recording covers 13 days
  When the simulation completes
  Then the panel shows the partial state naming the missing window explicitly
  And the required caveat copy about modelled fills is visible without interaction

Scenario: No recorded history offers the fix (failure case)
  Given a symbol that has never been recorded
  When a simulation is requested
  Then the no-history state is shown with a call to action to start recording the symbol, not an empty result table

Scenario: Arming live demands deliberate confirmation
  Given a rule scoped to an account the user may trade live
  When the arming dialog opens
  Then DEMO is preselected, the accounts and symbols are restated explicitly, and arming LIVE requires typing the confirmation and a step-up 2FA code

Scenario: Armed state is never optimistic (edge case)
  Given the user confirms arming
  When the API responds but the rules WS confirmation has not yet arrived
  Then the dialog stays open in a pending state and closes only once the armed state is confirmed over the rules topic

Scenario: A rule that cannot be armed says why (failure case)
  Given a rule with open safety-class validation warnings or no simulation on its current version
  When the arming dialog opens
  Then the arm action is disabled with a visible reason naming the missing precondition and what to do about it

Scenario: Keyboard-only arming
  Given a user operating without a pointer
  When they open the arming dialog
  Then focus moves into the dialog, the environment radio group is reachable and operable, the typed confirmation and 2FA fields have visible labels,
  And Escape cancels without arming
```

## Technical notes / design
Both surfaces are thin over the API — resist re-deriving anything. Specifically: coverage text, the safety summary (does it place orders / can it flatten / estimated-detector dependency) and the arming preconditions all come from the server, because a client-side re-derivation would eventually disagree with what the server enforces, and the disagreement would appear precisely at the moment a user is deciding to risk money.

Simulation progress arrives on the WS `rules` topic at its 250 ms cadence; the UI must stay fully interactive during a run (SCR-084 performance note) — run result parsing off the main thread if a large timeline arrives.

The arming dialog is `role="alertdialog"`. The typed confirmation uses CMP-044 ConfirmDialog's `variant="typed"` pattern already established for dangerous actions (CMP-145 uses the same pattern for live-arming from the form editor).

Never close the dialog on the HTTP 200 alone — SCR-085 is explicit that the armed state is confirmed over `rules` before the dialog closes.

## Test plan
Unit/component (>=80% frontend): every enumerated state of both screens rendered from fixtures — idle, running, completed, partial, failed, no-history for SCR-084; default, live-selected, blocked-by-precondition, conflict-warning, engine-offline and disarm for SCR-085.
Interaction: cancel a running simulation; progress updates from a mocked WS; pending-until-WS-confirmation arming; Escape cancels.
a11y: axe-core on both screens in every state; keyboard-only traversal test; screen-reader label assertions on the radio group, typed field and 2FA field.
E2E (Playwright, extended in **E35-Q03**): simulate a rule over a recorded window then arm it on demo, asserting the audit events were emitted.
Visual regression on the two screens' primary states.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.

The arm control being disabled is a courtesy — every precondition is enforced server-side (E35-S01), and a test crafting the API call directly must still be refused. The step-up 2FA token is passed through, never cached in component state beyond the request. The environment radio defaulting to DEMO is a safety control, not a convenience default, and needs an explicit test. ## Performance notes
SCR-084: the UI stays fully interactive during a run; partial results stream in rather than arriving as one blocking payload; a 14-day run's timeline renders without blocking input. SCR-085: arming takes effect server-side within 1 s including the WS confirmation the dialog waits for.

## Observability
Client analytics: `rule.simulation_started|completed|cancelled` and `rule.armed` are emitted server-side; the client emits the UI-only events for funnel analysis. Client errors on the arming path are reported with the rule id and precondition code so a stuck user is diagnosable.

title: Build the fire history, IR inspector, conflict resolver and import/export UI
body:
## Context
Four smaller surfaces that together make the rule engine explainable, portable and safe to operate:
- **SCR-087 Rule fire history** answers "why did / didn't my rule fire" — US-RULE-010's whole purpose.
- **SCR-088 Rule IR inspector** shows the canonical IR read-only plus the compiled evaluation plan, and is the surface that makes the round-trip guarantee visible to a human ("used for debugging, support and for verifying form↔graph round-trip equivalence").
- **SCR-086 Rule conflict resolver** forces an explicit precedence ordering before two overlapping rules can both stay armed — US-RULE-011.
- **SCR-089 Rule import / export** moves rules between installations, with two hard rules from the sign-off checklist: "the exported bundle never contains account ids, keys or armed state" and "imported rules always land disarmed", both **stated and verified**.

Design must be Done >=2 sprints before this story starts (E35-D03/D05).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-087** (page/drawer): virtualised, cursor-paginated table over `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs` with live append from WS `rules`; columns time, rule version, trigger, metric snapshot, actions attempted, results, environment; failure rows highlighted with the exchange reason; engine-restart markers; filters by outcome and environment; link from a firing to the resulting order and audit record; "replay this moment" link; export. States: empty, streaming, failure-highlighted, engine-restart markers.
- **SCR-088** (drawer): read-only canonical IR with copy/export, the compiled evaluation plan, the round-trip diff view, version and compiler-version stamps, clear advanced/diagnostic labelling, and an error state when compilation fails naming the offending node or row. Syntax highlighting in a worker for documents over 100 KB.
- **SCR-086** (modal): the overlap matrix as a table (rule A, rule B, overlapping scope, conflicting actions, proposed resolution); conflict kinds (opposing actions, duplicate stops, overlapping flatten, priority ambiguity); resolution choices (set priority, narrow scope, disarm one) each stating its consequence; "arm anyway" behind an explicit acknowledgement; the no-conflict state.
- **SCR-089** (modal): export selection (single / selected / all) with the scope-stripping note; import preview with per-rule accept/skip and reasons; version-mismatch handling; validation failure list naming the rule and the field.
- **Components**: CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-047 DateRangePicker, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-156 RuleEvaluationTimeline, CMP-033 CopyButton, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock, CMP-234 ValidationPanel, CMP-001 Button, CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-155 RuleListRow, CMP-159 RuleConflictWarning, CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-067 FileDrop.
- **Data**: `GET /api/v1/rules/runs/{runId}/events`, `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs`, `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile`, WS `rules`.

## Out of scope
- The rules list SCR-080 that hosts the conflict banner — E36; this story ships the modal it links to.
- The audit-log browser — **E42**.
- Replay playback itself — **E26**; this story only deep-links into it.
- Import of workspaces or layouts (US-LAY-007) — E17; only rule bundles here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A firing explains itself
  Given a rule fired and moved a stop
  When the user opens that row in the fire history
  Then the condition values that produced the decision are shown as a nested table, alongside the actions attempted and the resulting order ids

Scenario: A suppressed firing is visible too
  Given a rule that would have fired but was suppressed by a cooldown
  When the history is filtered by outcome
  Then the suppressed evaluation appears with its specific reason in words

Scenario: The IR inspector proves the round trip
  Given a rule authored in one editor and opened in the other
  When the inspector is opened
  Then the canonical IR, its hash, the version and the compiler version are shown read-only, and the round-trip diff view is empty for a matching pair

Scenario: Compilation failure names the offender (failure case)
  Given a rule whose compilation fails
  When the inspector is opened
  Then an error state names the offending node or row rather than showing an empty document

Scenario: Conflicts cannot be ignored silently
  Given two armed-candidate rules targeting the same stop
  When the resolver opens
  Then each resolution option states its consequence in text, and arming anyway requires an explicit acknowledgement

Scenario: Exported rules carry no secrets and import disarmed (failure case)
  Given a rule bound to two accounts and currently armed
  When it is exported and then imported into another installation
  Then the bundle contains no account ids, keys or armed state, the import preview shows how references are remapped
  And the imported rule lands disarmed
```

## Technical notes / design
SCR-087 is the performance-sensitive one: a virtualised table over cursor pagination with live append from the WS, budgeted at 10k rows without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame. Live rows append at the top without disturbing the user's scroll position or stealing focus — a log that jumps while being read is worse than no log.

SCR-088's diff view renders the structured diff the server produced (E35-T04); the client does not compute a diff, because a client-side diff of two canonical documents could disagree with the server's verdict on whether a round trip succeeded.

SCR-089's guarantees are enforced server-side — the client displays them. The import preview is rendered from the server's per-rule accept/skip decision including its reason; "unknown metric or action names are rejected with the offending path named" (SCR-089 validation note).

All four surfaces must handle the engine-offline state coherently: SCR-080's banner copy ("The rule engine is not running — armed rules are not evaluating. Native stops are unaffected.") sets the tone — always say what is still protecting the user.

## Test plan
Unit/component (>=80%): each screen in every enumerated state from fixtures; virtualised table with 10k rows; live append preserving scroll and focus; worker-based highlighting above 100 KB; import preview with accept, skip and version-mismatch rows.
a11y: axe-core on all four screens in every state; the nested condition-value table read correctly by a screen reader; the IR inspector's structured tree alternative navigable by keyboard; the resolver's radio options announced with their consequences.
E2E (extended in **E35-Q03**): fire a rule on demo, open its history row, inspect its IR, export it, re-import it and assert it is disarmed.
Perf: the SCR-087 scripting budget measured under the 10k-row fixture.
Visual regression on the primary state of each screen.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: export is a data-exfiltration surface. The bundle must never contain account ids, API keys, armed state or any `rule_runs.input_snapshot` content; this is verified by a test that exports a fully-populated rule and asserts the serialised bundle against a deny-list of field names. Import is an injection surface: the server validates and compiles every imported document, remaps references to what the importing user can access, and lands the rule disarmed — the client must never construct a rule locally and POST it as pre-validated. `rule.imported`/`rule.exported` are audited. The fire history exposes financial data and is gated by `rules:read` with account scoping.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-087: condition values in a nested table so a screen reader can read exactly why a rule fired; filters keyboard-operable; live-appended rows announced politely, never assertively, and never moving focus.
SCR-088: the `<pre>` region has a described-by note explaining it is read-only canonical JSON; a copy button is provided; a structured expandable tree alternative is offered for screen-reader navigation.
SCR-086: conflicts are a table; each proposed resolution is a labelled radio with its consequence in text.
SCR-089: export and import are separate labelled sections; the import diff is a table; every validation failure names the rule and the field.

## Performance notes
SCR-087: 10k rows scroll within 8 ms scripting per frame; history is cursor-paginated, never offset-paginated. SCR-088: IR fetched on demand; highlighting in a worker above 100 KB. SCR-086: conflict detection returns within 1 s for 500 rules (server-side, E35-S07). SCR-089: a 100-rule bundle validates in <=2 s with per-rule results streamed.

## Observability
Client analytics: `rule.history_viewed`, `rule.history_exported`, `rule.fire_detail_opened`, `rule.ir_viewed`, `rule.ir_copied`, `rule.template_previewed`. Server-side audits `rule.imported`, `rule.exported`, `rule.conflict_resolved`, `rule.priority_changed` are emitted by the API, not the client.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.

- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

- [ ] Storybook entries added under `RuleEngine/*` for every new or changed component, covering each state including empty, loading, error and the degraded/engine-offline variants.

title: Reconcile the plan documents and ADRs with the shipped rule engine
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires that the plan documents "reflect final shipped behavior (not the original proposal) if they diverged during implementation". E35 implements a large, precisely-specified surface across five documents and two ADRs; some divergence between the September 2026 specification and what actually ships in S14-S17 is certain, and an undocumented divergence in the rule engine is expensive, because E36, E37, E40 and E41 all read these documents as their contract.

## Scope / Deliverables

title: Abuse-case suite, SAST rules and permission checks for the rule engine
body:
## Context
E35-X01 identifies the threats; this ticket turns the ones that can be tested continuously into automated controls, so they hold between security reviews rather than only during them. `04-security-program.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA, secrets scanning and DAST across the product; this ticket adds the rule-engine-specific rules and the abuse-case suite on top of that baseline.

The single most important control to automate is also the simplest to state: **the IR is data, never code**. ADR-0007 R1 makes that a security boundary, and the way such boundaries erode is a well-intentioned PR that adds a small dynamic-expression convenience. A Semgrep rule makes that PR fail rather than requiring a reviewer to remember.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Custom Semgrep rules** for the rule-engine packages, each with a test case proving it fires:
  1. No `eval`, `exec`, `compile`, `__import__` or `pickle.loads` anywhere in the IR, compiler, evaluator or executor packages (the ADR-0007 R1 boundary).
  2. No direct exchange-adapter import from the rule-engine packages — actions must route through the OMS.
  3. No logging of `input_snapshot` or account-balance fields at INFO or below.
  4. No construction of an order payload in the rule engine that bypasses the OMS's native-SL attachment path.
  5. No permission check performed only at save time where the specification requires runtime enforcement (heuristic rule flagging scope checks outside the resolver).
- **Automated abuse-case suite** (runs in CI alongside the functional tests), each case asserting refusal, no state change, and an audit row:
  a. Arm a rule on an account the caller lacks, by crafted API call.
  b. Arm without a completed simulation on the current `ir_hash`.
  c. Arm with an open safety-class validation warning.
  d. Arm to an environment including `live` without `rules.arm_live` or without fresh step-up MFA.
  e. Set `only_tighten=false` or use `widen_stop` without `rules.loosen_stop` and the Owner role.
  f. Use `targets: all_accounts` without the widest grant.
  g. Act after a grant revocation that occurred post-arming.
  h. Act while the kill-switch is engaged or the author is frozen.
  i. Disable or delete `sys.native_sl_watchdog` or `sys.clock_drift_block`.
  j. Export a rule and find an account id, key or armed state in the bundle.
  k. Import a rule and have it land armed, or with references remapped to accounts the importer cannot access.
  l. Submit an IR at or beyond every schema bound and one designed to be expensive to evaluate, asserting bounded cost and refusal.
  m. Build an `emit_signal`/`on_signal` loop and assert the chain-depth limit holds.
  n. Read another user's rules, runs or events through the REST API and through WS subscription options.
- **DAST (OWASP ZAP) configuration** for the `/rules*` surface, including authenticated scanning with a low-privilege session to surface authorisation gaps rather than only injection classes.
- **RBAC matrix contribution**: every `/rules*` operation x every role asserted to produce the documented outcome, feeding R3 exit criterion 10's route-by-role matrix test.

## Out of scope
- The platform-wide SAST/SCA/secrets baseline — owned by the DevSecOps epic; this ticket adds rule-engine-specific rules on top.
- Penetration testing — **E43** in R4.
- Fixing findings — filed against the owning engineering tickets.
- The editors' client-side security (XSS in node labels) — E36/E37.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dynamic evaluation cannot be reintroduced
  Given a pull request adding an eval or exec call to the rule-engine packages
  When CI runs
  Then the Semgrep rule fails the build naming the ADR-0007 principle it violates

Scenario: Every abuse case is refused with evidence
  Given the fourteen abuse cases
  When the suite runs
  Then each is refused with the documented status code, no state changes, and an audit row is written

Scenario: A safety built-in cannot be disabled by any path (failure case)
  Given sys.native_sl_watchdog
  When disablement is attempted through the API, the repository layer and a direct database update
  Then the API and repository refuse, and the database attempt is detectable in the audit trail

Scenario: Authorisation gaps surface in DAST (edge case)
  Given an authenticated low-privilege ZAP session against the rules surface
  When the scan completes
  Then any endpoint returning data outside the session's grants is reported as a High finding

Scenario: A pathological rule cannot degrade shared trading (failure case)
  Given a rule engineered to be maximally expensive on the pre_trade_check path
  When it is armed and order submission is exercised
  Then the rule's own timeout bounds its cost and order submit to ack p95 remains within 300 ms
```

## Technical notes / design
Write the abuse-case suite as ordinary pytest tests in the main suite, not as a separate security project. A control that lives in a separate repository run quarterly regresses silently; a control in the merge-queue suite cannot.

Case (g) — acting after a post-arming grant revocation — is the most valuable and the trickiest to automate, because it requires changing a grant while a rule is armed and then driving an evaluation. Build the harness for it properly; it is the direct test of E35-S04's central claim.

Case (l) needs a deliberately expensive but schema-valid IR: maximum nesting, maximum boolean children, temporal nodes with the largest permitted windows, and metrics with high computation cost. Assert both that the timeout bounds it and that the auto-disable path eventually removes it.

For the Semgrep rules, prefer precise AST patterns over regex; a noisy rule gets suppressed, and a suppressed rule is no rule.

## Test plan
This ticket produces tests. Its own guard is that each Semgrep rule ships with a positive fixture proving it fires and a negative fixture proving it does not fire on legitimate code.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

This ticket is the continuous-enforcement half of the epic's security posture; E35-X01 is the analysis and E35-X03 the review. Together they satisfy the R3 gate requirement that E35's STRIDE findings are closed and that a targeted abuse-case review of privilege escalation has been performed before the train closes.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — security tooling.

## Performance notes
Case (l) and the pre-trade case intersect with E35-Q04's benchmarks; share the harness rather than duplicating it. The Semgrep and abuse-case suites must stay inside the merge-queue time budget — target under 3 minutes combined.

## Observability
Every abuse case asserts its audit row, which doubles as a test of the audit trail's completeness. DAST findings are tracked in the security dashboard with the endpoint, severity and disposition.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts committed under `docs/security/e35/` and linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- [ ] Every finding triaged with a severity, an owner and a disposition (fixed / accepted-risk with Owner sign-off / deferred with a dated ticket).
- [ ] No Critical or High finding left open — the R3 quality gate names E35 explicitly and requires all Critical/High closed before the train ends.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment posted on this ticket.
- [ ] Relevant findings reflected in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.
- [ ] Presented at the security review; the Architect and rule-engine backend lead acknowledge the model.
- [ ] Semgrep rules and the abuse-case suite wired into CI as required checks; each Semgrep rule has positive and negative fixtures.
- [ ] RBAC matrix rows for every `/rules*` operation contributed to the product-wide matrix test.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-X01** (which threats to automate) and **E35-S04** (runtime scope enforcement must exist to be tested). Coordinated with **E35-Q07** charters 1 and 6 so the manual and automated efforts complement each other. Feeds **E35-X03**.

- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6 `RuleUpdate` — topic `rules`, options `rule_ids`/`include_events`, 250 ms cadence

```gherkin
Scenario: No ad hoc visuals
  Given a token audit of the rules feature styles
  Then no hard-coded colour, spacing or duration values remain outside the design tokens
Scenario: A blocker is found late (failure)
  Given a blocker-severity mismatch discovered in Sprint 17
  Then the epic does not close until it is fixed or an explicit CDO waiver with rationale is recorded on this ticket
Scenario: Dark mode and density parity (edge)

```

## Technical notes / design

## Test plan

## Security notes

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

title: Write the black-box test plan, fixtures and exploratory charters for the form editor
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature alongside the white-box review. E36 is a large surface (five screens, thirteen components) whose defects are subtle rather than loud: a dropped opaque region, a diagnostic anchored to the wrong row, an account visible that should not be. The plan is written before the code lands so the acceptance scenarios are testable by construction.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Boundary and negative cases enumerated explicitly: 0 conditions, 1 condition, 12 conditions, a nested any-of group, 0 actions, a duplicate action, a metric with no data source, an unknown identifier, an armed rule being edited, a concurrent save, an unreachable compile service, a quarantined IR, a newer-version import bundle, a 100-rule bundle, a 500-rule list.
- **Fixtures**: the shared `fixtures/rule-ir/*.json` corpus (≥30 documents, shared with E35 and E36-T01) plus recorded `GET /rules/vocabulary` responses (current, stale-ETag, malformed, missing-metric), recorded `POST /rules/validate` responses (valid, warnings-only, errors), a deliberately divergent form/graph pair for the mismatch path, and a 500-rule list fixture.
- **Exploratory charters** (session-based, 90 min each): "author the five most likely real rules and try to make the editor lose data"; "attack the boundary between form and graph representations"; "use the editor with the keyboard only and no mouse plugged in"; "import hostile bundles"; "operate the list while rule state changes underneath you".
- A per-story traceability table mapping every acceptance scenario in E36-S01..S06 to at least one test case, so a missing test is visible.
- Entry/exit criteria for QA sign-off and the bug-severity rubric to be used (blocker = data loss, wrong scope, or a11y Level A/AA failure).

Writing the automation (E36-Q02), the a11y audit (E36-Q03), performance scripts (E36-Q04), security testing (E36-X02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given the acceptance criteria of E36-S01 through E36-S06
  Then the traceability table maps each scenario to at least one test case with no gaps
Scenario: Fixtures are reusable, not one-off
  Given the IR corpus
  Then it is the same corpus E35 and packages/rule-editor-core use, so a change to the IR breaks all three at once
Scenario: A case is untestable as written (failure)
  Given an acceptance criterion with no observable outcome
  Then it is sent back to the story author and the story does not enter Ready until it is measurable
Scenario: Charters are time-boxed and reportable (edge)
  Then each charter states its mission, the areas in scope, the time box and the debrief format
```

## Technical notes / design
