title: Write the black-box test plan for the node-graph editor
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires a QA-executed black-box test plan per Story before Done, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 names both rule editors in the R3 E2E and A11y gates. The node editor has more states than any other rule-engine screen (nine per SCR-082) and one property — lossless round-trip — that cannot be judged by looking at the screen, so the plan must be written deliberately rather than improvised per story.

Written from the design handoff (E37-D05) so it exists before the code does, per the test-ready DoR item.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box plan covering SCR-082 grouped by story: canvas & palette (E37-S01), node library & inspector (E37-S02), validation (E37-S03), round-trip switching (E37-S04), keyboard authoring (E37-S05), layout/search/minimap (E37-T02).
- Per group: preconditions, data fixtures, step-by-step cases, expected results referencing the exact copy from the D05 copy deck, and the audit/analytics events expected.
- State coverage matrix: every SCR-082 state (empty · editing · invalid connection · cycle detected · unsupported-in-form-view · round-trip mismatch · not verified · engine unavailable · read-only/armed) × each role (owner, manager with `rules:author`, manager without live-arming, viewer).
- Negative and boundary cases: second trigger, cycle, orphan, dangling port, `flatten_all_positions` without acknowledgement, action scoped to a forbidden account, 200-node graph, empty rule save, concurrent two-tab save, migrated older-IR rule, vocabulary unavailable.
- Fixture definitions QA owns: the 30-rule round-trip corpus (shared with E37-Q03), the 60- and 200-node graphs, an intentionally corrupted IR document for the quarantine case, and a rule already armed in demo.
- Traceability table mapping every US-RULE acceptance scenario in scope (US-RULE-002, 003, 005, 006, and the round-trip parts of 001) to at least one test case, so no Must scenario is unverified.

## Out of scope
- Executing the plan (E37-Q06), automating it (E37-Q02), a11y audit (E37-Q05), perf (E37-Q04), security abuse cases (E37-X02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Must scenario is covered
  Given the acceptance scenarios of US-RULE-002, 003, 005, 006 and the round-trip parts of 001
  When the traceability table is reviewed
  Then each maps to at least one test case, with no gaps and no cases lacking an expected result

Scenario: Expected results quote the real copy
  Given the D05 copy deck
  Then every expected result that asserts user-visible text quotes it exactly, so a wording regression fails the case

Scenario: Role coverage is complete
  Then the state x role matrix has an entry for every combination, with denied combinations asserting 403 plus no state change plus an audit row

Scenario: A case cannot be executed black-box (edge)
  Given a property such as canonical hash equality that is invisible in the UI
  Then the plan states the observable proxy (the round-trip indicator state and the exported IR from SCR-088) rather than omitting the property
```

## Technical notes / design

title: Render the node canvas with palette, typed ports and pointer connect
body:
## Context
This story stands up SCR-082 (`/rules/:ruleId/graph`) as a working authoring surface: the canvas (CMP-146 NodeGraphCanvas), the categorised searchable palette (CMP-236 NodePalette), typed connection points (CMP-237 NodePort), edges (CMP-152 NodeGraphEdge) and the minimap mount (CMP-238). It delivers the pointer half of **US-RULE-005**; the keyboard half is E37-S05, which is a peer path, not a follow-up — the DOM structure laid down here is what makes E37-S05 possible, so nodes, ports and edges must be real focusable DOM elements from the first commit (CMP-146 a11y contract).

Design is handed over in E37-D05; the library and any node cap are settled by E37-K01; the IR translation lives in `packages/rule-graph` (E37-T01).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/rules/:ruleId/graph` behind the `rules.node_editor` feature flag, RBAC per SCR-080/SCR-082 (`owner`; `manager` with `rules:author`; `viewer` denied → route hidden, 403 on direct call).
- CMP-146 NodeGraphCanvas: controlled nodes/edges state owned by the app (not the library), pan (`Space+drag`, wheel), zoom (wheel, `Ctrl+0` reset), selection, multi-select, `Del` delete selection, `Ctrl+A` select all, marquee select; zoom/density tiers per the D03 tier table.
- CMP-236 NodePalette: categories (triggers, metrics, comparators, logic gates, actions, comments) built from `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary`; search with no-results state; drag-to-canvas **and** select+`Enter` insertion (the non-drag path is mandatory per CMP-236's a11y contract and is implemented here, not deferred).
- CMP-237 NodePort: typed input/output ports rendered per node, each a focusable element with a name stating direction, type and connection state; pointer connect with live compatibility feedback using the `PORT_COMPAT` matrix from `packages/rule-graph`; incompatible drops refused with the matrix's inline reason string.
- CMP-152 NodeGraphEdge: bezier routing, default/selected/invalid-preview/labelled states, memoised routing, click-to-select, `Delete` to remove.
- Empty state ("Start from a trigger" hint), editing state, read-only state (armed rule viewed without editing), engine/vocabulary-unavailable banner.
- Undo/redo stack (`Ctrl+Z`/`Ctrl+Shift+Z`) covering add, delete, connect, disconnect, move — one stack shared with the keyboard path added in E37-S05.
- Dirty-state tracking and navigation guard (unsaved edits prompt to apply or discard, per US-RULE-006 "Unsaved changes").
- Save via `PUT /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}` with the compiled model from `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile`; optimistic-concurrency handling (reject with the version conflict error rather than last-writer-wins, per US-RULE-006).
- Storybook stories for CMP-146/152/236/237/238 exactly as listed in `15-component-catalogue.md`.

## Out of scope
- Node type bodies, inspector drawer and vocabulary parameter editing → **E37-S02**.
- Validation/diagnostics rendering → **E37-S03**. Round-trip indicator and editor switching → **E37-S04**. Keyboard authoring, node-list panel and live-region announcements → **E37-S05**. Auto-layout, node search-and-jump, minimap behaviour → **E37-T02**.
- Arming (SCR-085), simulation (SCR-084), rules list (SCR-080).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Author a minimal graph by pointer
  Given a draft rule opened at /rules/:ruleId/graph
  When I drag a trigger, a condition and an action node from the palette and connect them port to port
  Then edges render, the graph is held in app-owned state, and saving stores a version whose IR was compiled by POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile

Scenario: Incompatible connection is refused with a reason
  When I drag from a boolean output onto a numeric input
  Then the drop is refused, the target port shows the incompatible state, and the reason string from the port compatibility matrix is displayed inline

Scenario: Non-drag insertion works
  When I select a palette entry and press Enter
  Then the node is inserted, connected to the current selection where types allow, and becomes the new selection

Scenario: Viewer is denied (security edge)
  Given a user with the viewer role
  When they navigate directly to /rules/:ruleId/graph
  Then the route is not rendered, the API returns 403, no rule content is exposed, and an audit row is written

Scenario: Concurrent save is rejected (error)
  Given the same rule was saved from another tab after this editor loaded
  When I save
  Then an optimistic-concurrency error names the other editor and session and offers reload-and-reapply; no silent overwrite occurs

Scenario: Feature flag off
  Given rules.node_editor is disabled
  Then the graph route and the graph entry points in SCR-080/SCR-081 are absent, and the form editor remains fully usable
```

## Technical notes / design
State: `GraphModel` from `packages/rule-graph` is the single source of truth; the graph library receives derived props and emits intents which the reducer applies — no library-internal mutable state. Undo/redo is a command stack over that reducer so E37-S05's keyboard commands reuse it verbatim. Vocabulary is fetched once and cached (SCR-081 §Performance: "vocabulary cached"); a stale/unavailable vocabulary renders the palette disabled with the engine-unavailable banner rather than an empty palette. Compile is called on save and on mode switch only — never per keystroke or per drag (SCR-082 §Performance). Node/edge caps from E37-K01's ADR are enforced client-side with a warning and server-side as the real limit.

## Test plan
- Unit: reducer (every command), port compatibility wiring, dirty-state guard, flag gating, RBAC route guard.
- Component/Storybook: every state for CMP-146/152/236/237/238 with visual-regression baselines from D03's fixtures.
- Integration: save path against a mocked then a live backend, incl. the 409/version-conflict branch.
- E2E (Playwright, extended in E37-Q02): author-and-save happy path; refused incompatible connection; viewer 403.
- a11y: axe on the editor route; assert nodes/ports/edges are real focusable DOM elements (a structural test, since the whole keyboard strategy depends on it).
- perf: 200-node fixture pan/zoom benchmark (fuller measurement in E37-Q04).
- Coverage: >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: elevation of privilege (a viewer or an out-of-scope manager reaching the editor or a rule for an account they cannot trade — mitigated by route guard plus server-side `rules:read`/`rules:write` with `granted_accounts` scoping, and asserted by a test); tampering (client-built model diverging from stored IR — mitigated because the server compiles authoritatively and the client hash is advisory); repudiation (every save emits the audited `rule.graph_saved`); DoS (node/edge caps). Editing a rule that is currently armed is blocked here per US-RULE-006 — view is allowed, the first edit requires disarm or "edit as a new draft version". Data classification: financial-control configuration, integrity-critical.

## Accessibility notes
Mandatory in this story (not deferred): nodes, ports and edges are real focusable DOM elements with accessible names; the canvas region is a labelled ARIA landmark ("Rule builder canvas" per `05-accessibility-standard.md`); the palette's select+`Enter` insertion path exists; focus rings use CMP-035's shared utility; minimap is `aria-hidden`; target sizes meet §4. Full keyboard authoring, roving tabindex and announcements are completed in E37-S05 and audited in E37-Q05.

## Performance notes
Budget: 200 nodes at 60 fps pan/zoom on reference hardware (SCR-082); edge routing memoised; node re-render limited to changed nodes; compile+diff <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node graph and only on save/mode switch. The editor route is lazily code-split so budget #9 (<=8 MB gz initial bundle) is unaffected — asserted by the bundle-size CI check.

## Observability
Emit `rule.graph_saved` (audited, server-side on save) and analytics `rule.graph_node_added {type}`, `rule.graph_edge_added`, `rule.graph_connect_rejected {fromType,toType}`; frontend metric `rule_graph_compile_duration_ms`; error log with `RuleGraphError` codes from `packages/rule-graph`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests referencing the scenario name.
- [ ] Coverage >=80% frontend, CI gate green, no baseline regression.
- [ ] Storybook stories per `15-component-catalogue.md` for every component in scope, with visual-regression baselines.
- [ ] axe-core green on `/rules/:ruleId/graph`; structural focusability test green; keyboard-only path verified so far as this story delivers it.
- [ ] perf benchmark recorded against the 200-node fixture.
- [ ] Docs: `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 and `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if behaviour diverged; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] Security review comment present (RBAC + armed-rule edit guard checked manually).
- [ ] design-QA deferred to E37-D06 but no known spec deviations at merge; QA sign-off recorded.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo); feature-flag state recorded per environment.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E37-T01** (graph model, port matrix) and **E37-D05** (handoff must be Done >=2 sprints, per the design-ahead rule). Consumes E35's `/rules/vocabulary` and `/rules/{ruleId}/compile`.

## Branch
`feat/e37-rule-graph-canvas`. Split into >=3 PRs (canvas+state, palette, ports+edges) to stay near the 400 LOC guidance.

title: Implement the node library and inspector over the rule vocabulary
body:
## Context
The canvas from E37-S01 is only useful once nodes carry real semantics. This story implements the five node types named in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` — CMP-147 TriggerNode, CMP-148 ConditionNode, CMP-149 ActionNode, CMP-150 LogicGateNode, CMP-151 CommentNode — plus CMP-153 NodeInspectorDrawer, all driven by the closed vocabulary served by `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary`, which `22-api-openapi.yaml` describes as the single response both editors render their palettes from ("which is what keeps the two editors round-trip compatible").

This covers the graph rendering of **US-RULE-002** (metric vocabulary: units, descriptions, disabled-when-unavailable, `(estimated)` badging) and **US-RULE-003** (action vocabulary: scope declaration, permission-gated actions available only in simulate mode).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-147 TriggerNode**: `on_price_update`, `on_bar_close`, `on_order_fill`, `on_timer`, `on_indicator` with timeframe where applicable; exactly one trigger per rule enforced with a clear message on a second insertion.
- **CMP-148 ConditionNode**: metric + operator + value/reference, using CMP-157 MetricPickerCombobox for the metric; typed output port; displays the metric's unit; renders `(estimated)` as text for heuristic metrics (`iceberg_present_at_level`, `distance_to_liquidity_cluster`, `in_stop_hunt_zone`, `stop_run_detected`, `market_regime`) per US-RULE-002 and CMP-227 EstimatedBadge conventions.
- **CMP-150 LogicGateNode**: `AND` / `OR` / `NOT` with variable input count; the graph-native expression of what the form editor models implicitly; plus `n_of` where the vocabulary exposes it (a graph-only construct, badged as such via `packages/rule-graph`'s `isFormRepresentable`).
- **CMP-149 ActionNode**: the full action vocabulary (`place_order`, `modify_stop_loss`, `modify_take_profit`, `cancel_order`, `move_to_breakeven`, `scale_out`, `scale_in`, `flatten_all_positions`, `halt_new_orders`, `resume_new_orders`, `send_notification`, `log_journal_tag`, `reduce_leverage`, `widen_stop`, `arm_chase_limit`, `start_iceberg_slice`); each node shows the action's declared scope (which accounts/positions it may affect) per US-RULE-003; `flatten_all_positions` requires the explicit acknowledgement documented for SCR-081; order-placing actions are offered to a manager without live-arming permission in simulate-only framing with the restriction explained, and are absent from the palette entirely for accounts the user cannot trade.
- **CMP-151 CommentNode**: free text, non-executable, stored in the presentation block only (never affects the canonical hash).
- **CMP-153 NodeInspectorDrawer**: opened with `Enter` on a focused node (the keyboard contract in CMP-146), hosting dense parameter editing per node type so canvas chrome stays minimal; inspector edits must not trigger a re-layout (SCR-082 §Performance).
- **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice** mounted non-dismissibly in this editor, with the presence test that fails if it is removed from the composition.
- Unavailable-metric handling per US-RULE-002: a metric requiring recorded data the symbol lacks is shown disabled with the missing dependency named and a one-click action to start recording.
- Storybook stories exactly as listed in the component catalogue for CMP-147..151, CMP-153.

## Out of scope
- Validation/diagnostic rendering and the blocking-save logic → **E37-S03**.
- Round-trip indicator, editor switching, the "What won't round-trip" panel → **E37-S04**.
- Keyboard node-list authoring and announcements → **E37-S05**.
- Any change to the vocabulary itself, the metric registry or action semantics → **E35**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The whole vocabulary is reachable on canvas
  Given GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary
  When the palette and the metric picker are opened
  Then every metric and every action in the response is reachable with its unit and description, and nothing is hard-coded in the client

Scenario: Estimated metrics are badged as text
  Given a heuristic metric such as stop_run_detected
  When it is selected in a condition node
  Then "(estimated)" appears as text on the node and in the rule summary, not as colour or an icon alone

Scenario: Unavailable metric is explained, not hidden
  Given a metric requiring recorded data the symbol lacks
  Then the option is disabled, the missing dependency is named, and a one-click start-recording action is offered

Scenario: A forbidden action is not silently offered (security edge)
  Given a manager without live-arming permission
  Then order-placing actions appear only in simulate framing with the restriction explained, and actions scoped to accounts they cannot trade are not listed at all; a crafted save containing one is rejected by the server with 403

Scenario: Second trigger is refused (error)
  When a second trigger node is inserted
  Then insertion is refused with a message naming the existing trigger, and the graph remains valid

Scenario: Inspector editing does not disturb the layout (edge)
  Given a node positioned by hand
  When its parameters are edited in the inspector drawer
  Then no auto-layout runs, positions are unchanged, and the canonical hash changes only if a semantic parameter changed
```

## Technical notes / design
Node components are thin renderers over `GraphNode.data`; all semantics (allowed operators per metric type, parameter shapes, port types) come from the vocabulary response, cached per session. The `(estimated)` flag, units and permission requirements are vocabulary fields — the client must not maintain its own list, because `22-api-openapi.yaml` states the vocabulary is what keeps the two editors compatible. Comment nodes are written into `GraphLayout.comments` by `packages/rule-graph`, never into the IR. Action scope display reads the account/trade-group scope on the rule (US-RULE-007) and the action's own declared scope.

## Test plan
- Unit: one case per node type render+edit; vocabulary-driven operator filtering; estimated badging; unavailable-metric state; single-trigger enforcement; forbidden-action filtering by permission; comment nodes excluded from the hash.
- Component/Storybook: every story in the catalogue lists for CMP-147..151, CMP-153, with visual-regression baselines.
- Contract: the client renders correctly for the full published vocabulary fixture; a new vocabulary entry appears without a client change (asserted with an extended fixture).
- Integration: inspector edit → compile → IR reflects the change; comment/position edits → hash unchanged.
- a11y: axe on each node type and the inspector drawer; accessible names match the CMP-147/148 patterns ("Trigger node: on bar close, 5m").
- Coverage >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
This story is where privilege boundaries become visible in the UI. Threats: elevation of privilege (authoring an action against an account the user cannot trade), spoofing of safety posture (an emulated stop presented as if it replaced the native exchange SL). Controls: permission-filtered palette and metric picker fed from the server-scoped vocabulary; server-side rejection of out-of-scope actions on save (client filtering is convenience only, and a test asserts the server rejects a crafted payload); CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice non-dismissible with a presence test; `flatten_all_positions` acknowledgement required. Data classification: financial-control configuration.

## Accessibility notes
Every node has an accessible name and description (CMP-147/148 contracts); the inspector drawer is the dense-editing surface reachable by `Enter` from a focused node and returns focus to that node on close; the metric picker extends CMP-048 Combobox semantics with `(estimated)` in the option text itself; estimated/disabled states are text, never colour-only; drawer traps focus and is dismissible with `Esc`.

## Performance notes
Vocabulary cached; node rendering memoised per node so a single parameter edit re-renders one node, not the graph; inspector edits never re-layout. Contributes to the 200-node 60 fps budget — node chrome must not reflow with zoom (discrete tiers from the D03 spec).

## Observability
Analytics `rule.graph_node_added {type}` (extended with the metric/action id), `rule.graph_estimated_metric_used {metric}` (so reliance on heuristic detectors is measurable, per the detector-change warning in SCR-076), `rule.graph_inspector_opened`. No new audit events — saves are audited in E37-S01.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Storybook stories per catalogue for CMP-147..151, CMP-153; visual-regression baselines committed.
- [ ] axe-core green; accessible names verified against the catalogue patterns; manual screen-reader spot-check on the inspector recorded.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; CI gate green.
- [ ] Docs: `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if props diverged; changelog fragment.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment (permission filtering + server-side rejection test) present.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded; demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E37-S01** (canvas, palette and port infrastructure). Consumes E35's `/rules/vocabulary` and the metric registry; consumes E27/E28 account scoping indirectly via the vocabulary's permission fields.

## Branch
`feat/e37-rule-graph-nodes`. Suggested PR split: trigger+condition, logic+action, comment+inspector.

## References

title: Surface validation, cycles, orphans and diagnostics on the offending node
body:
## Context
US-RULE-005 requires that "the graph validates continuously and errors are shown on the offending node", that cycles are refused with the offending path highlighted, and that orphan/dangling nodes are warnings on canvas but blocking errors on save, listed by node name in a jump-to-node error list. CMP-234 ValidationPanel is the shared surface for **both** editors and has a contract test of its own: the same IR must produce identical diagnostics in form and graph modes (`15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-234 §Data contract).

Diagnostics come from the server (`POST /api/v1/rules/validate` over the compiled IR) so that what the editor shows is exactly what the engine will enforce; local analysis from `packages/rule-graph` (cycles, dangling ports, orphans, form-subset) supplies instant feedback for structural problems the server would also reject.

## Scope / Deliverables
- CMP-234 ValidationPanel mounted in graph mode with `anchor.kind = "node" | "edge"`; `role="log"`, errors first, error count announced on every recompile; each entry is a button that moves focus to the offending node/edge — the sole keyboard mechanism for navigating graph diagnostics.
- Local structural analysis wired from `packages/rule-graph`: `findCycles` (highlight the whole cycle path on canvas and enumerate it in the panel), `findOrphans` (nodes reaching no action — warning on canvas, blocking on save), `findDanglingPorts` (required inputs unconnected — same treatment).
- Server validation on save and on demand (`Validate` action, `Ctrl+Enter`): compile via `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile`, validate via `POST /rules/validate`, render returned `RuleValidationIssue`s anchored to nodes.
- On-canvas error/warning treatment per node and per edge (text + glyph, never colour-only), plus the header error/warning counters shown in the SCR-082 footer strip ("errors: 0").
- Save blocking: a graph with any error cannot be saved as anything but a draft, and can never be armed; arming entry points are disabled with the reason stated in text.
- Quarantine handling (US-RULE-001): a stored IR failing schema validation loads read-only and force-disarmed, names the failing JSON path, offers export-as-JSON, and is never partially rendered as editable.
- Engine-unavailable state: `POST /rules/validate` unreachable → the `Not verified` posture, draft-save only, arming blocked, stated in text (never silently "valid").

## Out of scope
- The round-trip indicator's four states and the mismatch diff → **E37-S04** (this story provides the diagnostics plumbing it reuses).
- Backend validation rules themselves → **E35**. Rule conflict/precedence detection across rules (US-RULE-011) → **E35/E36** surfaces; this story only renders CMP-159 RuleConflictWarning if the save response contains conflicts.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An error is shown on the offending node
  Given a condition node missing its value
  When validation runs
  Then the node renders an error treatment with text, the ValidationPanel lists the issue anchored to that node, and activating the entry moves focus to it

Scenario: A cycle is refused and drawn as a path
  When I connect a node output back into one of its own upstream inputs
  Then the connection is refused, the cycle is highlighted as a path on canvas and enumerated in the panel, and no IR containing a cycle is ever produced

Scenario: Orphans warn on canvas and block on save
  Given nodes reaching no action node and a required input left unconnected
  Then both are warnings while editing, and attempting to save raises blocking errors listing each node by its accessible name with a jump-to-node action

Scenario: Both editors report identical diagnostics (contract)
  Given one rule IR
  When it is validated from the form editor and from the graph editor
  Then the returned diagnostics are identical in set and severity, anchored to the corresponding row and node respectively

Scenario: Validation service unavailable (failure)
  Given POST /rules/validate is unreachable
  Then the editor shows "Not verified" in text, permits draft save only, blocks arming, and never presents the graph as valid

Scenario: Quarantined rule (error edge)
  Given a stored IR that fails schema validation
  Then the rule opens read-only and force-disarmed, the failing JSON path is named, export-as-JSON is offered, and no partial execution or partial editing is possible
```

## Technical notes / design
Diagnostic pipeline: local analysis runs on every graph mutation (cheap, structural) and is merged with server diagnostics (authoritative, semantic) into one list keyed by `{severity, anchor}`; on conflict the server wins. Debounce local analysis to one run per animation frame. Compile+validate runs on save and on mode switch (SCR-082 §Performance), plus explicitly via `Ctrl+Enter`; it must not run per keystroke. Error counts are announced through a single polite live region, coalesced per recompile (per E37-D04's announcement-coalescing rule).

## Test plan
- Unit: merge logic (local vs server precedence), debounce, save-blocking predicate, arming-disabled predicate, quarantine branch, engine-unavailable branch.
- Component: CMP-234 stories Valid/WithErrors/WithWarnings/GraphAnchored, focus-to-anchor interaction test in graph mode.
- Contract: **same IR ⇒ same diagnostics in both editors** (the named CMP-234 contract test), run against the live validate endpoint.
- Integration: cycle, orphan, dangling, missing-value and type-mismatch fixtures each producing the specified UI state.
- E2E: validate-blocked save; unreachable-service posture.
- a11y: `role="log"` semantics, focus movement on anchor activation, announcement coalescing, non-colour error encoding.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Validation shown in the UI must never be more permissive than the server's: a test asserts a graph the client believes valid is still rejected if the server disagrees, and that the UI then blocks rather than retries silently. Quarantine exists precisely to stop a hand-edited or truncated IR from being partially executed (tampering/integrity). Arming remains impossible from this editor; the arming entry point only routes to SCR-085's step-up flow.

## Accessibility notes
The ValidationPanel is the keyboard user's map of the graph: `role="log"`, errors first, every entry focus-moving, error count announced once per recompile. On-canvas error state must be text+glyph. This is the mechanism `05-accessibility-standard.md` §5 requires so canvas-only information does not exist.

## Performance notes
Local analysis <=5 ms per mutation on a 200-node graph (it runs on every edit); compile+validate round trip <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node graph and only on save/mode switch/explicit validate.

## Observability
Analytics `rule.graph_validation_run {errors,warnings,durationMs}`, `rule.graph_cycle_rejected`, `rule.graph_save_blocked {reason}`; metric `rule_graph_validation_duration_ms`; error logs carry the `RuleGraphError` codes. The audited `rule.validated` event is emitted server-side.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios covered by named automated tests, incl. the cross-editor diagnostics contract test.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; CI green.
- [ ] axe green; focus-to-anchor and announcement behaviour manually verified with a screen reader and recorded.
- [ ] Docs: `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-234 updated if the diagnostics contract changed; changelog fragment.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E37-S02** (nodes to anchor diagnostics to) and **E37-T01** (structural analysis functions). Consumes E35's `/rules/validate` and its `RuleValidationIssue` schema; shares CMP-234 with **E36**.

title: Implement round-trip switching, the four-state indicator and the mismatch diff
body:
## Context
This story delivers the graph side of **US-RULE-006** and the product promise behind owner decision #11: a rule may be opened in either editor, and switching must never change what it does. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.3 makes this R3 exit criterion 5 ("a corpus of >=30 rules authored in the form editor opens in the node editor and returns to the form editor with an identical IR ... and vice versa"), and US-RULE-006's NFR states the hash comparison "runs in production, not only in tests".

`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 specifies the mirrored four-state indicator in detail; E36 implements the form side. Both read the same `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` response.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-235 EditorModeToggle** in graph mode with the four indicator states: `Round-trips ✓` · `Unsupported in form view` · `Round-trip mismatch` · `Not verified`, each rendered as text+glyph with its specified tooltip/panel.
- **"What won't round-trip" panel**: clickable from the `Unsupported in form view` state; lists each offending node by its accessible name, why it cannot be represented in the form (nested sub-graph, fan-out edge feeding two actions, nested arithmetic, `n_of`, multi-level nesting), and what the form editor will show instead (a read-only summary card). Offending nodes are additionally badged on canvas with a non-colour glyph **and** enumerated in the `Alt+L` node list so the warning is never canvas-only.
- **Graph-only construct marking at creation time** (US-RULE-005 edge scenario): the moment a node-only construct is created — e.g. fanning one output into two consumers — the node is badged, the rule header shows "contains node-only constructs", and this is recorded in the IR so the form editor renders it read-only rather than discovering it at switch time.
- **Hash proof on every switch** (US-RULE-006): switching without editing compares the canonical `ir_hash` before and after; on difference the switch is **aborted**, the rule is left untouched, a "round-trip integrity failure" error is raised showing both hashes with a downloadable diff, and a high-severity telemetry event is emitted.
- **`Round-trip mismatch` resolution UI**: saving and arming blocked; the diff rendered (reusing SCR-088's diff renderer) with the diverging node selected on canvas and focused in the node list; exactly two explicit recovery choices — "Keep the form version (the graph layout will be regenerated)" / "Keep the graph version (discard form edits)" — each restating what is lost; never auto-resolved; the choice is audited.
- **Switch-while-armed** (US-RULE-006): viewing an armed rule in either editor is allowed; the first edit requires either disarming or explicitly choosing "edit as a new draft version", so the running version can never mutate under the runtime.
- **Unsaved-changes prompt** on switch (apply or discard) and **optimistic-concurrency** rejection when the other tab saved a version this editor did not see, naming the other editor and session and offering reload-and-reapply.
- **Migration during a switch**: if the rule was migrated on open (older IR version), comparison is made against the post-migration hash, the migration is recorded once as its own version entry, and the rule stays disarmed until reviewed.
- Presentation preservation: switching to the form editor, editing a threshold and returning must show the original hand-placed layout, not an auto-layout (US-RULE-001 "Presentation data survives the round trip").

## Out of scope
- The form editor's own indicator and read-only summary cards → **E36** (mirrored spec; this story coordinates with it).
- The IR, canonicalisation and the compile endpoint → **E35**; SCR-088 IR inspector itself → E35/E36 (this story reuses its diff renderer).
- The >=30-rule corpus test execution → **E37-Q03** (this story provides the behaviour it verifies).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Switching without editing preserves the IR
  Given a rule open in the graph editor
  When I switch to the form editor and back without editing
  Then the canonical ir_hash is identical at every hop and the indicator reads "Round-trips" throughout

Scenario: A graph-only construct is declared at creation time
  When I fan one node's output into two action nodes
  Then that node is badged immediately, the header states "contains node-only constructs", the fact is recorded in the IR, and the form editor will render that sub-tree read-only

Scenario: Hash proof fails on switch (failure path)
  Given the pre-switch and post-switch canonical hashes differ
  Then the switch is aborted, the rule is untouched, a round-trip integrity failure is shown with both hashes and a downloadable diff, and a high-severity telemetry event is emitted

Scenario: Mismatch is never auto-resolved (error)
  Given the form and graph representations compile to different IR
  Then saving and arming are blocked, the diff is shown with the diverging node selected on canvas and focused in the node list, and only the two explicit recovery choices are offered, each restating what is lost; the chosen resolution is audited

Scenario: Switching an armed rule (edge)
  Given the rule is currently armed
  When I switch editors and then attempt the first edit
  Then I must either disarm or choose "edit as a new draft version", and the armed version is never mutated

Scenario: Layout survives a form-side edit (edge)
  Given a graph with hand-placed node positions
  When I edit a threshold in the form editor and return
  Then my original layout is shown rather than an auto-layout, and the canonical hash changed only because of the threshold

Scenario: Concurrent edit in two tabs (error)
  Given the same rule is open in the form editor in another tab which saves first
  When this editor saves
  Then the save is rejected with an optimistic-concurrency error naming the other editor and session, offering reload-and-reapply, with no last-writer-wins overwrite
```

## Technical notes / design
- Authority: `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` (`{editor, model}` → `{ir, ir_hash, issues}`) is the only source of the canonical hash. The client mirror in `packages/rule-graph` is used to pre-empt a switch, but a client/server disagreement is itself reported as `Round-trip mismatch` — never resolved locally.
- The four indicator states map 1:1 to the `rule.roundtrip_verified {result}` values `identical | graph_only_construct | mismatch | unverified` defined in `14-screens-catalogue.md`, so the UI state and the audit vocabulary cannot drift.
- `graph_layout` is persisted on the rule version but excluded from the hash (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 guarantee 3), which is what makes "layout survives" and "moving a box creates no new version" simultaneously true.
- Form-subset determination uses `isFormRepresentable` from `packages/rule-graph` for instant marking, confirmed by the server's `issues` on compile.
- Version conflicts use the rule's version/ETag from `GET /rules/{ruleId}`; the reject path must name the other session (available from the WS `rules` topic / conflict response).

## Test plan
- Unit: indicator state machine (all four states + transitions), hash-compare gate, abort-on-mismatch, armed-edit gate, migration path, concurrency rejection.
- Integration: compile round trip against a live backend for form- and graph-authored fixtures; the layout-preservation case; the migration case with an older stored IR version.
- E2E (Playwright): full switch cycle for every construct in the metric/action vocabulary (the explicit requirement in US-RULE-006's NFR), graph-only construct flow, mismatch resolution flow, armed-rule flow, two-tab concurrency flow.
- Chaos-ish: compile endpoint 5xx and timeout → `Not verified`, arming blocked.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
This is a security-relevant story: a silent round-trip change could alter what an armed rule does — an integrity and repudiation threat. Controls: server-authoritative hash; abort-not-repair on mismatch; `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved {choice}` audited because a resolution can silently change an armed rule's behaviour; armed rules are immutable to in-place edits; optimistic concurrency prevents last-writer-wins. A high-severity telemetry event on integrity failure ensures the condition is noticed rather than absorbed by the user. Abuse case coverage in E37-X02.

## Accessibility notes
Indicator states are text+glyph with an accessible name stating the state and its consequence; the "What won't round-trip" panel is a keyboard-reachable list whose entries move focus to the offending node; the mismatch dialog is `role="alertdialog"` restating the loss of each choice in plain language; all badges are enumerated in the `Alt+L` node list so nothing is canvas-only; the switch confirmation before entering a lossy form view is announced.

## Performance notes
Compile+diff completes <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node rule and runs on save and mode switch only (SCR-081/SCR-082 §Performance). The switch must feel immediate: show a determinate pending state rather than blocking the UI while the compile is in flight.

## Observability
`rule.roundtrip_verified {result}` and `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved {choice}` (both audited, server-side), `rule.graph_saved`; high-severity telemetry `rule.roundtrip_integrity_failure {hashBefore,hashAfter,ruleId}`; metrics `rule_graph_roundtrip_mismatch_total` (alerting on any non-zero in staging), `rule_graph_compile_duration_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios covered by named automated tests incl. the per-construct E2E switch matrix.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; CI green.
- [ ] Security review comment present; audit events verified end-to-end in the audit log.
- [ ] axe green; mismatch dialog and indicator verified with a screen reader.
- [ ] perf: compile+diff p95 recorded on the 100-node fixture.
- [ ] Docs: `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 round-trip section reconciled with shipped behaviour; `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 updated if clarified; changelog fragment.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E37-S03** (diagnostics plumbing) and **E36** (the form editor must exist and implement the mirrored indicator; the corpus of form-authored rules comes from it). Consumes E35's compile endpoint and canonicalisation. Feeds E37-Q03 and E37-D06.

## Branch
`feat/e37-rule-graph-roundtrip`. Split: indicator+switch gate, unsupported-construct panel, mismatch diff+resolution.

title: Deliver keyboard-equal authoring: node list, connect, announcements
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 makes "the node canvas has a verified non-canvas alternative" an R3 quality gate, and §7.3 exit criterion 13 requires "a11y pass incl. the node editor's keyboard alternative". US-RULE-005 carries an explicit keyboard-only-construction scenario as a Must acceptance criterion, and `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 mandates a three-layer strategy (DOM-mirror nodes, roving-tabindex navigation with keyboard connect, and the form-view toggle as an equal-status alternative). SCR-082's a11y section adds the `Alt+L` node list panel: "the canvas is never the only way to author".

E37-S01 laid down real focusable DOM elements; this story turns them into a complete, announced, keyboard-first authoring path built exactly to the keyboard authoring map signed off in E37-D04.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`Alt+L` node-list panel**: a linear, non-spatial view of the graph — every node with its accessible name, type, parameters summary and its connections described in text ("ATR 14, output connects to Multiply input A"); add / connect / disconnect / delete / rename / open-inspector affordances as real form controls; diagnostics and node-only badges enumerated here (never canvas-only).
- **Roving tabindex navigation**: `Tab` enters the graph region (a labelled ARIA landmark), arrow keys move between connected nodes, `Enter` opens the node inspector (CMP-153), `F2` renames, `Delete` removes the selection, `Esc` returns focus to the region.
- **Keyboard connect** (CMP-237/CMP-148 contract): focus an output port → `Enter` starts a connection → arrow-select a target port → `Enter` confirms; incompatible targets are *announced as incompatible with the reason string* from `packages/rule-graph`'s port matrix rather than merely being un-droppable; `Esc` cancels the pending connection.
- **Keyboard edge handling**: an edge is reachable (node → `Tab` to its edges, or from the node list), selectable, and deletable with `Delete`, with "Delete connection" also exposed in its context menu (CMP-152 contract).
- **Non-drag node insertion** completed end-to-end: palette entry selected + `Enter` inserts and connects to the current selection where types allow (the pointer-free path from CMP-236).
- **Live-region announcements**: one polite announcement per completed operation (node added, connection made naming both endpoints, connection refused with reason, node deleted, auto-layout applied, error count after recompile), coalesced per E37-D04's rule so rapid editing does not flood.
- **Shared undo/redo**: keyboard-initiated edits use the same command stack as pointer edits (US-RULE-005: "the same undo/redo stack applies as for pointer edits").
- **Form-view toggle as equal status**: wording and placement per E37-D04, presented as an alternative rather than a fallback.
- Reduced-motion support: edge animation disabled; focus movement without animated transit.

## Out of scope
- The a11y *audit* of the result → **E37-Q05**. Design of the keyboard map → **E37-D04**.
- Auto-layout, node search and minimap → **E37-T02** (this story consumes their keyboard entry points).
- The form editor's own keyboard completeness → **E36**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Build a complete rule without a pointer
  Given a user who never uses a pointer
  When they add a trigger, a condition, a logic gate and an action from the keyboard palette, connect them via the port keyboard-connect flow, edit parameters in the inspector and save
  Then a valid rule is produced, identical in IR to the same rule built by pointer

Scenario: A connection is announced
  When a connection is completed by keyboard
  Then a live region announces "connected CVD divergence output to AND input 1", naming both endpoints

Scenario: An incompatible target is announced, not merely ignored (error)
  When a boolean output is aimed at a numeric input by keyboard
  Then the attempt is refused and the announcement states the incompatibility and its reason, and focus remains on the pending connection so another target can be chosen

Scenario: Every canvas operation exists in the node list (a11y gate)
  Given the operation inventory from E37-D04's keyboard authoring map
  When each row is exercised through the Alt+L panel
  Then every operation completes, with zero operations reachable only on canvas

Scenario: Undo is shared (edge)
  Given a mix of pointer and keyboard edits
  When Ctrl+Z is pressed repeatedly
  Then edits unwind in a single chronological order regardless of input modality

Scenario: Announcement flooding is prevented (edge)
  When ten nodes are added in rapid succession
  Then announcements are coalesced per the agreed rule rather than queueing ten separate messages
```

## Technical notes / design
Keyboard commands dispatch the same reducer commands as pointer interactions (E37-S01), so behaviour cannot diverge; this is asserted by a test that builds the same rule through both paths and compares canonical hashes. The node list renders from `GraphModel` + diagnostics, so it is automatically complete as new node types are added. Announcements use a single `aria-live="polite"` region with a coalescing queue; errors use `role="alert"` sparingly (blocking conditions only). Focus management: opening the inspector moves focus into it and returns focus to the originating node on close.

## Test plan
- Unit: command parity (keyboard vs pointer command dispatch), announcement coalescing, focus return, roving tabindex model.
- Interaction tests (named CI gate per CMP-146 §Tests): keyboard node navigation, keyboard connect incl. type rejection with a spoken reason, keyboard edge delete, keyboard-only node insertion.
- E2E: the full "build a rule with the keyboard only" journey, asserting the resulting IR hash equals the pointer-built equivalent.
- a11y: axe on the editor and the node-list panel; manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes against E37-D04's screen-reader script, recorded.
- Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
No new data paths. One safety property is asserted here: **no keyboard shortcut arms a rule** — arming always routes to SCR-085's step-up flow, so the keyboard map cannot be used to bypass 2FA. A test asserts the editor registers no binding that reaches `PUT /rules/{ruleId}/mode` directly.

## Accessibility notes
This story is the accessibility deliverable of the epic: WCAG 2.2 AA with particular attention to 2.1.1 Keyboard (no trap), 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.5.8 Target Size, 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value and 4.1.3 Status Messages. The `Alt+L` panel is an *equal-status* authoring surface; the minimap remains `aria-hidden` because the node list and diagnostics anchors are its complete alternatives.

## Performance notes
Node-list rendering is virtualised above 50 rows (CMP-049 convention) so a 200-node graph does not stall; announcement coalescing bounds live-region churn; keyboard navigation must respond within one frame.

## Observability
Analytics `rule.graph_keyboard_authoring_used` (the adoption signal specified in E37-D04), `rule.graph_keyboard_connect_rejected {fromType,toType}`; no new audit events.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every row of E37-D04's keyboard authoring map implemented and tested.
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios automated; keyboard interaction tests wired as a named CI gate.
- [ ] axe green; manual NVDA + VoiceOver passes recorded against the D04 script.
- [ ] Coverage >=80%; CI green.
- [ ] Docs: `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 a11y section and `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146/152/236/237 updated to match shipped behaviour; changelog fragment.
- [ ] QA sign-off; demoed at Sprint Review with a keyboard-only demo specifically.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E37-S02** (node types and inspector must exist to navigate and edit) and **E37-D05/E37-D04** (keyboard map and screen-reader strings). Feeds E37-Q05 and E37-D06.

## Branch

title: STRIDE threat model for the node-graph editor and its compile/save path
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 defaults a STRIDE kickoff on for any epic touching the OMS path, and `04-security-program.md` requires a threat model per epic. The node editor authors documents that, once armed, place and cancel real orders through the rule engine (C10 → OMS). `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 names E35 in the R3 STRIDE list; E37 is its authoring surface and inherits the same exposure with its own client-side twist: a rich client model compiled into an executable document.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE model over the editor's data flow: browser editor state → `POST /rules/{ruleId}/compile` → `POST /rules/validate` → `PUT /rules/{ruleId}` → `rule_versions` → (later) arming via `PUT /rules/{ruleId}/mode` → engine execution → OMS actions. Trust boundaries drawn explicitly (browser ↔ API, API ↔ engine, engine ↔ OMS).
- Threat enumeration with at least: **S** — authoring as another user / session fixation on the editor route; **T** — client model diverging from the stored IR, layout data smuggling semantics into the presentation block, a hand-edited or pasted IR document, hash-comparison bypass; **R** — a graph edit changing an armed rule's behaviour without an audit trail, ambiguous resolution of a round-trip mismatch; **I** — vocabulary or rule content leaking accounts/symbols the user cannot see, error messages disclosing internals; **D** — pathological graph (node/edge explosion, deep nesting) stalling the compiler or the editor thread, fuzz-scale compile requests; **E** — authoring actions scoped to accounts without trade permission, reaching the editor as a viewer, arming without step-up auth.
- Risk rating (likelihood × impact) per threat, with existing controls named and gaps recorded as actionable items assigned to E37 stories or E35.
- Explicit verification that the presentation block (`graph_layout`, comments, collapsed state) cannot carry semantics — i.e. that nothing in it can influence evaluation — since it is excluded from the canonical hash and therefore from the integrity guarantee.
- Confirmation of the arming boundary: no path from this editor sets `mode` without the SCR-085 step-up flow.
- Feed into `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` for any new or retired risk.

## Out of scope
- The rule engine's own runtime threat model, sandboxing and execution budget (E35); OMS and fan-out models (E29/E34).
- Penetration testing (E43) and the abuse-case execution (E37-X02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category is addressed
  When the model is reviewed
  Then each of the six categories has at least one enumerated, rated threat with named controls or a recorded gap, and no category is dismissed without a written reason

Scenario: Presentation cannot carry semantics
  Given the graph_layout / comment / collapsed-state block
  When it is analysed against the evaluator's inputs
  Then it is demonstrated that no field in it reaches evaluation, or the finding is raised as a blocking gap against E35/E37-T01

Scenario: Gaps become tickets
  Given any control gap
  Then it is filed against a specific ticket with an owner and a due sprint, not left as prose in the model

Scenario: Arming cannot be reached from the editor (security edge)
  Then it is verified by inspection and by test that no editor interaction, hotkey or API call path sets rule mode without the SCR-085 step-up flow

Scenario: A Critical/High finding is open at train close (failure)
  Then the epic cannot be Done; the finding is either fixed or carries an Owner-signed accepted-risk record per the R3 security gate
```

## Technical notes / design
Model follows the `04-security-program.md` template with a data-flow diagram in mermaid, trust boundaries annotated, and a threat table. Reviewed in a session with the Security engineer, the Architect, and the E37 and E35 leads. Where a control lives in E35 (server-side compile authority, schema validation, node caps, execution budget), the model records the dependency explicitly rather than duplicating the control.

## Test plan
Each control named in the model must map to a test — server-side rejection of an out-of-scope action, node/edge cap enforcement, quarantine on schema violation, RBAC 403 with audit row, mismatch-never-auto-resolved. Missing mappings are filed as gaps. Verification of the tests themselves happens in E37-X02.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security work product. Data classification for the editor's data: financial-control configuration — not secret, but integrity-critical, since a silently altered rule can move money on demo today and live after R4.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except the check that no accessible path (keyboard shortcut, node-list action) bypasses a confirmation or step-up flow that the pointer path enforces.

## Performance notes
The DoS branch sets the node/edge caps and the compile request rate limits that E37-S01 and E35 enforce; those numbers are an output of this ticket.

## Observability
Defines the minimum audit/telemetry set required for non-repudiation on this surface: `rule.graph_saved`, `rule.roundtrip_verified {result}`, `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved {choice}`, plus the high-severity `rule.roundtrip_integrity_failure` event, and confirms each is written to the hash-chained `audit_log` where required.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Model published with DFD, trust boundaries, rated threats and named controls.
- [ ] All gaps filed as tickets with owners and sprints.
- [ ] Presentation-block and arming-boundary verifications recorded.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer and the Architect.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated; feeds E37-X02 and E43.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E37-S01** (the real data flow must exist to be modelled accurately). Depends on E35's compile/validate/arming design. Feeds E37-X02 and the epic's security DoD.

## Branch
`chore/e37-threat-model` (docs only).

title: Hi-fi design: parity report, paper fidelity panel, reset and eligibility
body:
## Context
Three smaller surfaces round out E38 and all are 'honesty' surfaces: the environment parity report (US-PAPER-008, on SCR-137 Admin security centre and linked from SCR-074), the admin **paper fidelity** panel showing the nightly paper-vs-demo divergence metrics (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12.5), the paper-balance reset on SCR-079 (US-PAPER-006), and the demo/live eligibility control on SCR-122 (US-PAPER-007).

They are grouped into one design ticket because they share a pattern language (admin tables, destructive confirmation, disabled-with-reason) and the same reviewer, and none is big enough to justify its own.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-137 Admin: security centre** - an 'Environment parity' section: table of known demo-vs-live differences with columns difference, area, source, last verified, status; a 'needs re-verification' treatment for items older than 90 days; a 'candidate parity item' inbox fed by runtime-detected demo-only failures. Components: CMP-028, CMP-036, CMP-050, CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-175, CMP-178.
- **Admin paper fidelity panel** - the nightly divergence report: mean and p95 slippage difference, fill-rate difference for resting limits, fee difference, with the defect threshold (p95 slippage >1 tick or fill-rate >10 pp) drawn as an explicit breach state. Reuses CMP-178 SystemHealthTile and CMP-049 Table.
- **SCR-079 Account detail drawer (trading side)** - the 'Reset paper balance' control: starting-balance input, the warning when open paper positions exist, the explicit confirmation, and the **hidden-entirely-in-live** treatment (US-PAPER-006 requires hidden, not merely disabled).
- **SCR-122 Admin: user detail / edit** - demo/live eligibility control: demo-only vs live-enabled, the reason shown when Live is disabled for a manager, the acknowledgement-at-next-sign-in pattern on promotion, and the reduce-only state after revocation while positions are open.
- Empty, loading, error and RBAC-denied states for each.
- Design-system: reuse only; any new pattern raised as a contribution ticket.

## Out of scope
- The switcher and global chrome (E38-D02).
- Replay simulated-results drawer (E38-D04).
- The wider admin screens (E42 owns SCR-122's and SCR-137's overall structure; this ticket designs only the E38 sections inside them).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Parity report communicates freshness
  Given a parity item last verified 95 days ago
  When the SCR-137 parity section is reviewed
  Then a distinct 'needs re-verification' state is drawn, using text plus icon, not colour alone

Scenario: Reset is hidden in live
  Given the environment is LIVE
  When the SCR-079 frames are reviewed
  Then the reset control is absent from the drawer entirely, and a note states it must not render as a disabled control

Scenario: Destructive reset is guarded
  Given open paper positions exist
  When the user initiates a reset
  Then a confirmation is drawn that names the count of positions and orders to be discarded and requires an explicit confirm

Scenario: Revocation with open positions is designed
  Given a manager's live access is revoked while they hold live positions
  When the SCR-122 frames are reviewed
  Then a reduce-only state is drawn with copy explaining existing positions remain manageable and new entries are refused

Scenario: Fidelity breach is unmissable
  Given the nightly divergence job reports p95 slippage divergence above one tick
  When the fidelity panel is reviewed
  Then a breach state is drawn that states the threshold, the measured value and the resulting action (a defect ticket is opened)
```

## Technical notes / design
- Table density and sorting follow the admin table conventions set by E42's SCR-120..SCR-140 work; do not invent a new table.
- Parity items are data-driven (US-PAPER-008 NFR: 'generated from a maintained data file plus runtime observations, never hand-written prose only') - the design must accommodate a variable-length, machine-generated list including items with missing 'source' values.
- The reset confirmation uses CMP-044 ConfirmDialog; specify which variant (typed vs plain) and justify it.
- Annotate audit triggers: reset writes to the paper journal and an audit row; eligibility grant/revoke is audited (US-PAPER-007).

## Test plan
- Review walkthrough with the Owner (these are owner-facing admin surfaces) and the Architect.
- Accessibility annotation review in E38-D05; design QA in E38-D07.

## Security notes
- SCR-122 eligibility is a privilege control: the design must make the current grant state unambiguous and must not offer a path for a manager to self-grant. Reviewed against `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 7 RBAC 4-tuple.
- SCR-137 is a security surface; no secret or key material may appear in any frame (keys are never readable back, per the locked decisions).
- Data classification: admin/operational metadata; no PII beyond usernames.

## Accessibility notes
- Tables need real table semantics with header associations; 'needs re-verification' and 'breach' states must carry text, not only icon colour.
- Destructive confirm: focus moves into the dialog, the confirm button is not the default focus, and the dialog is labelled by its heading.
- Reduce-only and disabled-with-reason states follow the CMP-079 RbacGate pattern so the reason is programmatically associated with the control.

## Performance notes
- The parity table is small (tens of rows) - no virtualisation needed; annotate that the fidelity panel loads a single pre-aggregated nightly document rather than querying raw executions.

## Observability
- Annotate the audit events the surfaces trigger: paper reset, eligibility grant/revoke, parity item verification.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact complete in Figma at the stated fidelity, linked on the ticket.
- [ ] Every state from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` drawn (default, loading, empty, error, not-permitted, transitional).
- [ ] The screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` is fully ticked.
- [ ] Tokens used are design-system tokens from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; any new token/component raised as a design-system contribution ticket, never a one-off.
- [ ] Reviewed and signed off by the Chief Design Officer (or delegate) and the Architect; sign-off comment recorded on the ticket.

title: Hi-fi design: simulated-fill results SCR-099 and simulated-everywhere labelling
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-004 requires that simulated positions are 'visually marked as simulated everywhere', and US-PAPER-005 requires that paper results 'never aggregate into live statistics, with a clear label on every view'. That is not one screen - it is a cross-cutting labelling system riding on the `is_paper` boolean (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 3.3, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 13.1).

This ticket designs SCR-099 (Replay paper-trading results) and the `is_paper` labelling system that every blotter, position row, journal entry and analytics view must adopt.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for **SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results** per its catalogue entry: simulated fills, P&L, R distribution, the modelled slippage assumptions, the explicit 'these are simulated' statement, per-trade list with entry/exit and R, opt-in comparison against the same period's real trades (clearly separated), export, and the 'not a backtest guarantee' caveat. Components: CMP-049 Table, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard.
- A **fill-model disclosure block** design: queue position, latency (submit/cancel/market-data), slippage mode, fee source, funding applied - readable by a non-engineer, sourced from `FillModelConfig` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12.1).
- The **simulated labelling system**: one badge spec plus placement rules for the orders blotter, positions grid, journal list, journal trade detail and analytics headers; rule that the badge appears in the heading, not only as a chip (SCR-099 a11y note); rule for how analytics excludes simulated rows by default and how the include-toggle is presented.
- Table alternatives for every chart on SCR-099 (a11y requirement from the catalogue entry).
- Design-system contribution: the simulated badge as a catalogue entry rather than a page-local element.

## Out of scope
- Journal analytics screens themselves (E41) - this ticket contributes the simulated treatment they must adopt.
- Replay transport/scrubbing UI (E26).
- The environment badge (that is D02; environment and simulated are orthogonal and must be visually distinguishable).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Simulated framing is inescapable
  Given any frame showing paper-matcher output
  When reviewed
  Then the word 'Simulated' appears in the region heading and in the accessible name, not only as a coloured chip

Scenario: Environment and simulated are not confused
  Given a demo-environment simulated fill
  When the frames are reviewed
  Then the DEMO environment badge and the SIMULATED badge are visually and textually distinct, and a note explains they are orthogonal

Scenario: Fill assumptions are stated, not buried
  Given the SCR-099 results drawer
  When a user opens it for the first time
  Then the queue-position, latency, slippage and fee assumptions are visible without expanding a disclosure, and each names its configured value

Scenario: Every chart has a table alternative
  Given the equity curve and R-distribution visualisations
  When the frames are reviewed
  Then a table alternative is drawn for each and is reachable by keyboard

Scenario: Comparison against real trades is opt-in and separated
  Given the comparison feature
  When reviewed
  Then it is off by default and the simulated and real series are separated visually and in the legend, never merged into one total
```

## Technical notes / design
- Visual encodings follow the project's data-visualisation conventions: categorical series distinguishable without colour, direct labelling preferred over legends for two-series comparisons.
- Numeric formatting uses the mono token and the instrument's tick/lot precision from `instruments` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`).
- Annotate that results are computed server-side at session end and fetched once (SCR-099 performance note) - so the design has a loading state and no live-updating figures.
- Specify the export affordance (CMP-099) and its formats (CSV/Parquet, matching E41's export).

## Test plan
- Review with the Owner focused specifically on over-trust: show the frames and ask what the numbers mean (carrying forward the E38-D01 finding).
- Accessibility annotation review in E38-D05; design QA in E38-D07.

## Security notes
- Threat: simulated results promoted into live analytics and used to justify real risk (R12 backtest bias). Control: designed-in separation plus the `simulated=true` journal flag audited as `journal.simulated_import` (SCR-099 analytics/audit note).
- Data classification: trading performance data - internal, not public; the export affordance must not offer an unauthenticated share link.

## Accessibility notes
- 'Simulated' must be in the heading and in each region's accessible name (SCR-099 a11y note).
- Every chart needs a table alternative; results are a table plus a summary description list.
- Export controls need accessible names stating format and scope ('Export 42 simulated trades as CSV').

## Performance notes
- Single fetch at session end; no open subscriptions remain. Annotate a skeleton loading state sized to the final layout to avoid layout shift.

## Observability
- Annotate `replay.results_viewed`, `replay.results_exported`, `replay.results_promoted_to_journal` triggers so engineering places them precisely.

E38's surfaces carry an unusually heavy a11y load: the environment distinction must survive colour blindness and greyscale, the switch is a destructive-class action requiring announced confirmation, and SCR-099 charts each need a table alternative.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Review SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-079 (reset), SCR-099, SCR-122 (eligibility) and SCR-137 (parity + fidelity) frames against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

- Verify colour-independence and contrast measurements for `color.env.demo`/`color.env.live` and for the simulated badge; record measured ratios.
- Confirm reduced-motion fallbacks for the environment-switch transition.
- Deliver a defect list against D02/D03/D04 (Figma comments plus a checklist on this ticket); blocking items must be fixed before D06 handoff.

## Out of scope
- Automated axe-core runs against built code (E38-Q05).

- Remediation of non-E38 screens the review happens to pass through.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given the six reviewed screens
  When the annotation layer is complete
  Then every control has an explicit accessible-name annotation and none is left to engineering's judgement

Scenario: Contrast is measured, not eyeballed
  Given the environment and simulated treatments in both themes
  When measured
  Then every text pairing is at least 4.5:1 and every non-text indicator at least 3:1, with the measured value recorded per pairing

Scenario: A failure blocks handoff
  Given a blocking accessibility defect is found in a D02/D03/D04 frame
  When E38-D06 handoff is attempted
  Then handoff is refused until the defect is fixed and re-reviewed

Scenario: Keyboard-only path exists for the environment switch
  Given a keyboard-only user
  When the annotated switch flow is traced
  Then the full path from badge to typed confirmation to step-up to completion is operable without a pointer, with visible focus at each step
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use the annotation conventions in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` (focus-order numbering, live-region tags, name/role/value callouts).
- Special attention to announcement storms: CMP-075 repeats on every trading panel; the spec must prevent every panel re-announcing the environment on each render (`role="img"` with a static label per the component catalogue).
- The post-switch banner is assertive and announced once; the band itself is `role="status"` and polite.

## Test plan
- Peer review by the accessibility specialist plus one screen-reader walkthrough of the annotated prototype (NVDA on Windows, the primary target since the shell is Electron on Windows).
- Output feeds the E38-Q05 audit scenarios so the audit tests exactly what was specified.

## Security notes
- No threats of its own; note only that the not-permitted state on SCR-074 must not leak whether other users have live access (avoid information disclosure in the reason copy).

- This ticket *is* the accessibility work: WCAG 2.2 AA across 1.3.1, 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.11, 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11 (focus not obscured), 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

N/A.

title: STRIDE threat model for paper trading and demo/live separation
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.1 makes it default-on for any epic touching the OMS. E38 sits on top of the most dangerous boundary in the product: the one between practice and real money.

The security program already names two E38-relevant threats - **W9** (code assuming WS order entry exists on demo, causing unplaced or duplicated orders) and **W10** (demo and live endpoints mixed in one session) - with SR-040a as the control. This ticket completes the model before the implementation stories start, so the controls are designed in rather than retrofitted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Produce `docs/security/threat-models/E38-paper-trading.md` with a data-flow diagram covering: the session's environment attribute, the environment switch, the adapter's per-environment clients, the isolation middleware, the paper matcher, the paper ledger, eligibility grants, and the parity report.
- STRIDE enumeration per element and per flow, with at minimum:
  - **Spoofing**: a UI claiming demo while the session is live; a forged `system` WS frame re-badging panels.
  - **Tampering**: a crafted account id targeting live from a demo session; mutating an adapter base URL at runtime; modifying the parity data file to hide a known difference.
  - **Repudiation**: an environment switch or a paper reset with no audit trail; an audit writer failure allowing an unrecorded action.
  - **Information disclosure**: a not-permitted message revealing other users' live grants; raw exchange payloads stored in candidate parity items; demo keys in logs.
  - **Denial of service**: switch-flapping to disrupt subscriptions; unbounded candidate-parity-item growth from a repeating error.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a manager self-granting live eligibility; acting on a live grant before acknowledgement; the paper matcher reaching the network and placing a real order.
- Risk rating (likelihood x impact) per threat, with the control, the owning ticket and the verifying test named for each - a threat with no named test is not considered mitigated.
- Explicit abuse-case list handed to E38-X02 and cross-referenced into `qa/plans/E38-paper-parity.md`.
- Update `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` with any new risk and its owner.

## Out of scope
- Executing the abuse cases (E38-X02) or the final review (E38-X03).
- Threat-modelling the OMS, key vault or fan-out (E29, E27, E34 own theirs) - E38's model references them as trust boundaries rather than re-analysing them.
- Pen-testing, which is an R4 activity (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every element and flow is enumerated
  Given the E38 data-flow diagram
  When the model is reviewed
  Then every element and flow has a STRIDE pass recorded, with 'not applicable' stated explicitly and justified rather than left blank

Scenario: Every threat has a control and a test
  Given the enumerated threats
  When the model is complete
  Then each names its control, the ticket implementing it, and the specific test that verifies it

Scenario: Critical and High threats are scheduled
  Given a threat rated Critical or High
  When the model is signed off
  Then its control is implemented by a ticket inside this epic's sprint window, or the risk is explicitly accepted by the Owner in writing

Scenario: The known security-program threats are carried forward
  Given W9 and W10 from docs/plan/04-security-program.md
  When the model is reviewed
  Then both appear with SR-040a as their control and E38-T01 as the implementing ticket, with their verifying tests named

Scenario: The simulator-reaches-the-network threat is treated as Critical
  Given the paper matcher
  When the elevation-of-privilege analysis is reviewed
  Then the possibility of a simulated order reaching the exchange is rated Critical with the structural no-transport test named as its control
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use the project's existing threat-model template so findings aggregate across epics for the R4 pen-test scope.
- Trust boundaries to draw explicitly: browser/backend, backend/exchange (per environment), backend/Postgres, and the user/owner privilege boundary for eligibility.
- The model must state which controls are **structural** (impossible by construction, e.g. separate client instances) versus **enforced** (checked at runtime, e.g. the isolation middleware) - structural controls need less ongoing verification and this distinction shapes the regression pack.

## Test plan
- The model is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect; review sign-off is the acceptance.
- Its output becomes test cases in E38-X02, E38-Q01 and E38-Q04, so the model's quality is measured by whether those tickets can be written from it without further analysis.

## Security notes
- This ticket *is* the security analysis. It must be completed before E38-T01/T02 merge, so the controls those tickets implement are the ones the model asked for.
- Classification of data touched: session attributes, account identifiers, API credentials (by reference only), financial simulation data.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - analysis artefact. One note is in scope: the model should record that an inaccessible environment indicator is a security failure, not only an a11y one, since a user who cannot perceive the indicator cannot verify their environment.

## Performance notes
N/A - though the model should note that any control added to the per-order path must respect budget #4, so controls are placed at session or startup level where possible rather than per request.

## Observability
- The model specifies the audit events and alerts each control requires, which E38-T02, S02, S06 and S07 then implement - so observability is derived from the threat analysis rather than invented per ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded in the epic's STRIDE worksheet under `docs/security/threat-models/E38-paper-trading.md`.
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md`).
- [ ] SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) and secrets scan clean or triaged on the touched paths.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present on the ticket.
