title: Accessibility audit, exploratory charter and epic QA sign-off for E39
body:
## Context
Two DoD obligations close out E39. First, a11y: `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 states a11y is "default-on (WCAG 2.2 AA) for any ticket that ships or changes a UI surface, **including owner/admin screens** — there is no 'internal tool, a11y doesn't matter' exception", and the R3 a11y gate specifically requires that "danger/confirm patterns [are] announced" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4). Second, the epic-level QA sign-off: §2.2 requires "an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA".

E39's screens are the product's danger surfaces, and a blocking `role="alert"` banner that traps focus, or a typed-confirmation dialog a screen-reader user cannot complete, would lock a user out of their own safety controls. That is the specific failure mode this ticket exists to prevent.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Manual screen-reader passes** on SCR-071, SCR-072, SCR-073, SCR-134 and CMP-211 with **two** screen readers (NVDA on Windows and the Electron shell's platform reader), covering: the `role="alert"` lockout announcement; that the non-dismissible banner does **not** trap focus; the `role="alertdialog"` kill-switch flow end-to-end including typing `FREEZE`; the hold-to-confirm keyboard equivalent (hold `Enter`) with `aria-valuenow` progress; the `aria-sort` account table; and SCR-134's per-limit fieldsets, units and breach descriptions.
- **Keyboard-only traversal**: complete a freeze, an unfreeze with step-up, a lockout override and a risk-policy save using only the keyboard, with visible focus at every step and no focus loss on modal open/close or on an async state change.
- **axe-core CI** configured for the four screens with zero violations at `serious`/`critical`; documented exceptions (if any) recorded with a rationale and a follow-up ticket.
- **Colour-independence and contrast verification**: greyscale rendering of every status state; contrast measurement of every status token pairing at ≥4.5:1 text / ≥3:1 non-text.
- **Exploratory charter** (session-based, 2×90 minutes): "Explore the risk and kill-switch surfaces with the mission of producing a state where the UI and the server disagree about whether trading is permitted" — plus a second charter targeting role transitions (a user's role or grant changes while a freeze dialog is open; `23-ws-protocol.md` §10 requires subscriptions to be re-authorised on kill-switch transitions and on grant changes, with `revoked` rather than silent emptying).
- **Epic-level regression pass** across E39's full scope on demo, and the recorded **QA sign-off** for the epic.

## Out of scope
- Functional E2E automation (E39-Q02) and perf/chaos (E39-Q03).
- Visual/spec conformance (E39-D04 design QA).
- a11y of surfaces owned by other epics (order ticket, DOM ladder, rule editors) even though SCR-073 renders inside some of them — only the banner's behaviour in those hosts is in scope here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A screen-reader user can complete a freeze
  Given NVDA is active
  When the user opens the kill-switch modal via the global hotkey
  Then the dialog is announced as an alert dialog with its consequence text
  And focus starts on the cancel control
  And the user can type FREEZE, enter a reason and confirm without sighted assistance

Scenario: The lockout banner announces without trapping
  Given a lockout fires while the user is in the positions grid
  Then the banner is announced via role="alert"
  And keyboard focus remains where the user left it
  And the user can still reach and operate reduce-only controls

Scenario: Status is legible without colour
  Given every status state rendered in greyscale
  Then ok, WARN and LOCK remain distinguishable by text and glyph

Scenario (failure): A serious axe violation blocks sign-off
  Given axe-core reports a serious or critical violation on any E39 screen
  Then epic QA sign-off is withheld until it is fixed or a documented exception with a follow-up ticket exists

Scenario (exploratory): UI and server disagree
  Given the exploratory charter is executed
  Then any state where the UI permits an action the server refuses (or vice versa) is filed as a Bug with a reproduction
  And the absence of such a state is recorded explicitly as the charter's outcome
```

## Technical notes / design
axe-core runs in the Playwright suite from E39-Q02 against the same fixtures, so a11y checks exercise real states (locked, frozen, stale, partial failure) and not just an empty happy path — auditing only the default state is the most common way an a11y audit passes while the product remains unusable in its failure states.

Screen-reader sessions are recorded (screen + audio) and attached to the ticket, per the DoD's evidence expectations.

## Test plan
Manual + automated as described. The epic-level regression pass replays the E39-Q01 regression pack plus the E39-Q02 E2E suite against a fresh demo deployment and records pass/fail per scenario in the sign-off document.

## Security notes
The exploratory charter's central mission — producing a UI/server disagreement about whether trading is permitted — is simultaneously an a11y/UX charter and a **security** charter, because any such disagreement is a potential control bypass. Findings of that class route to E39-X02 and to the Security engineer immediately, not through the normal Bug queue. Recordings must not capture credentials or real account identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
The standard is WCAG 2.2 AA per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. Specific gates for this epic: danger/confirm patterns announced; the node-canvas exception does not apply here (that is E37); every status text-labelled; meters expose numeric values; the hold-to-confirm gesture has a keyboard equivalent; no focus trap on non-dismissible banners.

## Performance notes
The audit confirms that assistive-technology usage does not push any surface outside its budget (e.g. the 1 Hz dashboard throttle must not cause the screen reader to re-announce the whole table each second — a real and commonly missed defect; the table uses `aria-live="off"` with targeted announcements instead).

## Observability
Findings are logged against the epic with severity; the sign-off document records pass/fail per scenario and is linked from the epic's DoD checklist.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Screen-reader passes completed on all four screens with two readers; recordings attached.
- [ ] Keyboard-only traversal completed for all four flows.
- [ ] axe-core green (no serious/critical) in CI on all E39 screens, exercising failure states.
- [ ] Greyscale and contrast verification recorded.
- [ ] Both exploratory charters executed, findings filed.
- [ ] Epic-level regression pass executed against demo.
- [ ] **QA sign-off comment posted on E39** with pass/fail per scenario — the epic cannot reach Done without it.

## Dependencies
- `E39-Q02` — the suite and fixtures the audit runs against.
- `E39-D04` — design QA completed so the audit is not chasing known visual defects.

## Branch
`test/e39-a11y-signoff`. One PR (axe config + charters + sign-off doc), ≤250 LOC.

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2, §3.2, §8
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 A11y row
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-071, SCR-072, SCR-073, SCR-134
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §10 re-authorisation on kill-switch transitions

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md §B20 (risk lockout), kill-switch machine
2. docs/plan/29-statechart-adoption-plan.md §1.2, §3 (mandatory config, hot-path exclusions)
3. docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md
4. docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml (/risk/lockouts, /killswitch)
5. docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md §11-§12 (risk schemas, step-up list)
6. docs/plan/04-security-program.md SR-025

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- apps/web/src/features/risk/ (dashboard SCR-071, lockout notice SCR-073, kill-switch modal SCR-072, risk policy SCR-134)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- `/api/v1/risk/lockouts/{accountId}/override`, `/api/v1/killswitch/*`, `risk_lockouts`/`risk_policy`/`kill_switch_state` Postgres tables, `SystemUpdate` WS frame (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9), OMS cancel-all/reduce-only paths.

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm lint` && `pnpm typecheck`
- `cd services/api && ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict .`
- `cd services/api && pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`
- `pnpm verify` (full local gate before opening the PR)

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e39-risk-killswitch-q04`
- PR title: "E39-Q04: Accessibility audit, exploratory charter and epic QA sign-off for E39"
- Body: include `Closes #<issue>` (replace `<issue>` with this ticket's GitHub issue number)
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend + @CandleViewer/security (services/api/risk, services/api/oms are dual-owned per CODEOWNERS), @CandleViewer/frontend for D/S04/S05 web tickets
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels (type/test, area/oms-execution, priority/p1, qa, a11y) plus any CI-added labels

**Done means**
- All 5 Gherkin scenarios above pass as automated tests (unit/contract/E2E as appropriate).
- Coverage meets the package's existing threshold (85% API / package-level web target); CI green.
- Diff ≤400 LOC (or split into the PRs named in the ticket's own Branch section); PR template fully completed.
- QA/security/a11y sign-off recorded per this ticket's own Test plan / Security notes / Accessibility notes sections.

**Do NOT**
- Do not hand-roll lockout/kill-switch state as ad-hoc booleans — the lifecycle must go through `cv.statechart.factory.build(...)`, never a direct `create_machine`/`Interpreter` call outside `statechart/`.
- Do not accept a client-supplied `until`/expiry timestamp for a lockout or kill-switch release — it is always server-computed.

title: Execute abuse cases, add SAST/DAST rules and complete the E39 security review
body:
## Context
E39-X01 produced the threat model; this ticket proves the mitigations hold. The R3 security gate requires "STRIDE for … E39 … all Critical/High closed; **a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation** before the train closes" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4). `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 additionally requires, "for anything touching keys/withdrawal/RBAC, a manual abuse-case check performed (e.g. attempt privilege escalation…)".

E39's mitigations are only credible if someone actively tries to break them, which is what this ticket funds.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Executed abuse cases**, each as an automated test where possible and a recorded manual attempt where not:
  1. Manager engages a global kill-switch → must 403 and be logged as a security event.
  2. Manager or viewer releases an engaged kill-switch → must 403 regardless of scope.
  3. Owner releases the kill-switch without a valid step-up token → must 403 (SR-025).
  4. Manager clears their own lockout → must 403; the owner is notified; the attempt is audited.
  5. Replay a captured override request with its original idempotency key → must return the stored result and must not re-release a *new* lockout.
  6. Submit an order carrying `risk_caps` / `max_daily_loss_usd` in the body → the values are ignored, and the attempt is logged.
  7. Request `/risk/summary` with an account id outside scope, and with an id that does not exist → responses must be indistinguishable (no account enumeration).
  8. Forge a `system` WS frame claiming the kill-switch is released → clients must not trust client-side state for enforcement; the server still refuses (proving the UI state is advisory only).
  9. Disable risk enforcement via a feature flag → must be impossible; `risk.enforcement` and the kill-switch itself must not be flag-disableable (existing threat D2).
  10. Direct UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_log` rows describing a freeze → refused by the grant model, and the attempt itself recorded (US-ADMIN-008).
  11. Tighten a cap and immediately attempt to force-close another user's position through the tightened path → confirms the "no forced liquidation" semantics are not abusable.
  12. Induce `risk_state_unavailable` under load and confirm the system refuses rather than admits (availability-abuse case, results reused from E39-Q03).
- **SAST/DAST rules**: Semgrep rules asserting (a) no order-submission code path exists that does not call the risk gate (pattern over `OrderCommand` construction sites), (b) no code reads caps from a request body, (c) no `kill_switch` read bypasses the fail-closed helper. OWASP ZAP DAST profile extended to cover `/risk/*` and `/trading/kill-switch` with authenticated scans per role.
- **Security review** of the E39 diff (white-box) covering the evaluator, the lockout service, the kill-switch service and the two UI stories, with a posted sign-off comment on E39.
- Update `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` with any newly discovered residual risk and any new `SR-*` requirement; update `32-risk-register.md` if the risk profile changed.

## Out of scope
- The pen-test itself (E43, before R4 live enablement).
- Key-vault abuse cases (E27) — referenced, not repeated.
- Fan-out and rate-limit abuse (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every privilege-escalation attempt fails closed and is logged
  Given abuse cases 1 through 4 are executed
  Then each returns 403, changes no state, and produces an audit row identifying the actor

Scenario: Enforcement cannot be disabled
  Given an owner with full admin rights attempts to disable risk enforcement via feature flags
  Then no flag exists that can do so
  And a Semgrep rule fails the build if such a code path is introduced

Scenario: No account enumeration
  Given a request for an out-of-scope account and a request for a non-existent account
  Then the two responses are byte-identical apart from the request id

Scenario (failure): An abuse case succeeds
  Given any abuse case produces an unintended state change
  Then it is filed as a P0 security Bug
  And the R3 security gate cannot pass until it is closed

Scenario: Static rules have teeth
  Given a deliberately ungated order path is introduced on a scratch branch
  Then the Semgrep rule fails CI and names the offending file
```

## Technical notes / design
Abuse cases 1–7 and 9–11 are added to `tests/security/e39/` and run in the standard CI security job; case 8 (forged WS frame) is executed with a local proxy injecting frames, and case 12 reuses the E39-Q03 load harness. Each case asserts on three things: the HTTP/behavioural outcome, the absence of a state change, and the presence of the expected audit row — a 403 without an audit row is still a finding.

Semgrep rules live in `.semgrep/e39-risk.yml` and are registered in the CI SAST job alongside the existing CodeQL/Bandit configuration.

## Test plan
The ticket is a test deliverable. Meta-check: each Semgrep rule ships with a positive fixture (code that must trigger it) and a negative fixture (code that must not), so a silently-broken rule is detected.

## Security notes
This is the epic's security sign-off gate. Findings are triaged with the standard severity scale; **no Critical or High may remain open** when the R3 train closes, and an accepted risk requires the Owner's recorded sign-off per the DoD. The abuse-case suite must run with least-privilege demo credentials and never against live.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — though case 8's conclusion (client state is advisory only) matters for a11y too: an assistive-technology user must never be shown an "armed" state the server does not agree with. Any mismatch found is filed jointly with E39-Q04.

## Performance notes
The security test suite must complete within the CI security job's budget (≤10 minutes); case 12 runs in the nightly load window rather than on every PR.

## Observability
Confirms the detections specified by E39-X01 are actually emitted: an alert on `risk.lockout_overridden`, a metric for refused out-of-scope `/risk/summary` calls, security-event logging on every failed privilege attempt, and audit-chain coverage of all risk events.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All 12 abuse cases executed; automated where feasible, recorded where manual.
- [ ] Semgrep rules merged with positive/negative fixtures; ZAP profile extended.
- [ ] White-box security review of the E39 diff completed.
- [ ] Zero open Critical/High findings, or Owner-signed accepted risk recorded.
- [ ] `04-security-program.md` and `32-risk-register.md` updated.
- [ ] **Security engineer sign-off comment posted on E39** — the epic cannot reach Done without it.
- [ ] Findings presented at the Security Review before the R3 train closes.

## Dependencies

- `E39-S05` — the full UI surface must exist to attack.
- `E39-Q03` — supplies the availability-abuse results (case 12).

title: Hi-fi SCR-094 trade post-mortem and SCR-095 analytics dashboard
body:
## Context
SCR-094 is where a trade is understood (fills, fees, funding, MAE/MFE, R-multiple, the managing rule, the trade-group siblings, the context chart and the replay jump); SCR-095 is where a *method* is judged. SCR-095 carries the highest interpretation risk in the epic: a confident-looking expectancy figure over 12 trades is misinformation (risk R12), so the low-sample treatment is a first-class design problem, not a footnote.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-094 hi-fi**, satisfying its checklist: entry/exit markers on a context chart with footprint available; the full fill list (time, price, qty, fee, fee currency, liquidity maker/taker, order id, trade group, causing rule); rule/algo/manual attribution of every action; notes and tags editor; R-multiple, MAE/MFE and time-in-trade shown with units; the "context not recorded" state; the link into replay at the trade's timestamp; trade-group sibling P&L row ("group Scalp x3: Main +65.0 | sub_001 +26.0 | sub_002 -3.0").
- **MAE/MFE presentation**: price, USDT and R for each, plus the timestamp at which each occurred, and a `bar-derived` marker when only bar extremes were available (US-JRN-005).
- **SCR-095 hi-fi**, satisfying its checklist: the metric set (win rate, expectancy, avg R, profit factor, max drawdown with depth and duration labelled, streaks, by-symbol, by-hour-of-day, by-day-of-week, by-tag, by-account, by-rule/setup); DEMO excluded by default with an explicit toggle; a table alternative for every chart; the small-sample warning ("12 trades - not statistically meaningful"); date-range and cohort controls; empty state; R-distribution histogram; MAE/MFE scatter with outcome encoded by **shape** as well as colour; balance transfers marked on the equity curve and excluded from performance.
- **New design-system entries**: CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart (Default / WithDrawdown / TableViewToggle) and CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard (Default).
- A one-page **statistics legend** design: every metric links to its formula (US-JRN-006 NFR requires a documented formula reference reachable from the UI; the content is authored in E41-T05).

## Out of scope
- SCR-093 / SCR-096 (E41-D02); the replay screen itself (E26); implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Low-sample honesty
  Given fewer than 20 trades match the active filter
  Then every headline statistic on SCR-095 renders with the low-sample caveat attached to the number, not only in a page-level banner

Scenario: Small buckets
  Given a breakdown bucket contains fewer than 5 trades
  Then that row or bar is visually marked low-confidence and the marking is conveyed in text, not only by opacity

Scenario: Context unavailable
  Given the recorded market data covering a trade has been pruned
  Then SCR-094 shows a "context not recorded" state that names what is missing and offers bar-level review if bars remain, and never shows an indefinite spinner

Scenario: Chart table alternative
  Given any chart on SCR-095
  Then a "View as table" control is drawn that renders the same data through CMP-049, reachable by keyboard
```

## Technical notes / design
Charts are lightweight (CMP-167 may reuse the series primitive CMP-181 in a minimal pane) and are not the WebGL engine; the design must not assume engine features like LOD or crosshair sync. The context chart on SCR-094 is fed by `GET /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/context`, which returns a `coverage` descriptor - the design consumes that descriptor to render partial coverage honestly. Equity curve is derived from journal entries, never from wallet balance snapshots (US-JRN-007 NFR), so a transfer marker is an annotation, not a step in the series.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact); verified by E41-D05 design QA and by the a11y audit in E41-Q03 (colour-blind simulation on the scatter, contrast on the histogram).

## Security notes
SCR-094 shows sibling accounts within a trade group; frames must show only legs the viewer is granted, and an ungranted leg is rendered as an explicit "not in your scope" row rather than silently omitted (which would misstate group P&L) - this constraint is carried into E41-X01's threat model.

## Accessibility notes
MAE/MFE and the SL path are described in text; the mini chart has a table alternative; every chart carries a text summary ("Expectancy +0.34R over 42 trades"); colour is never the sole encoding; drawer focus management specified for the SCR-094 drawer variant.

## Performance notes
SCR-095 is interactive <=800 ms for 10 000 trades with server-side aggregation; SCR-094's context window renders <=1.5 s or falls back to the "context not recorded" state. No design may require a client-side scan of the full trade set.

## Observability
Annotates `journal.detail_viewed`, `journal.note_added` (audited), `journal.screenshot_exported`, `journal.replay_from_trade`, `journal.analytics_viewed`, `journal.analytics_filtered`, `journal.analytics_exported`, `journal.cohort_changed`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Figma frames complete for both screens and all declared states; link on the ticket.
- [ ] Every sign-off checklist item in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` for SCR-094 and SCR-095 is satisfied.
- [ ] CMP-167 and CMP-168 specs handed to the design-system team.
- [ ] Colour-blind simulation run on the MAE/MFE scatter and the R-histogram; evidence attached.
- [ ] CDO design sign-off comment recorded (gates E41-S02 and E41-S03 via E41-D04).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E41-D01.

## Branch
`design/journal-analytics-hifi`

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` - SCR-093 Journal (trade list), SCR-094 Trade detail / post-mortem, SCR-095 Journal analytics dashboard, SCR-096 Journal tag manager
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` - CMP-166 JournalEntryRow, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard, CMP-169 TagEditor, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-047 DateRangePicker, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-058 InlineEdit, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-024 Sparkline, CMP-021 Link

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.

- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).

title: Journal a11y design review, motion spec and engineering handoff
body:
## Context
Under the design-ahead rule no frontend story in E41 may start until its design is Status=Done. This ticket is that gate: a dedicated accessibility design review across all four screens, the motion specification, and the handoff package engineering builds from in S18-S19.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **A11y design review** of SCR-093, SCR-094, SCR-095, SCR-096 against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: contrast measured (body >=4.5:1, large text >=3:1) at the default density and at 200% zoom; focus order and visible focus rings for every interactive element; ARIA pattern selection for the filter bar (combobox/listbox), the tag editor, the dialogs, and the sortable table (grid pattern); screen-reader announcement text authored for sort changes, bulk-selection counts, filter changes, the low-sample caveat and the "context not recorded" state.
- **Keyboard map** for the journal area, added to the screen entries: list navigation, open detail, bulk select, apply tag, export, and the replay jump.
- **Motion spec**: row selection, drawer open/close for SCR-094, chart transition on filter change, and the "recomputing totals" affordance - all honouring `prefers-reduced-motion` with an explicit reduced variant per transition; durations and easing from `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` tokens, no bespoke curves.
- **Handoff package**: annotated frames, redlines, token names (not hex values), component mapping table (frame region -> CMP id), state inventory, copy deck (all strings incl. empty states, caveats, confirmations) and the RBAC-dependent variants.
- Copy review of every statistic label against the formula reference authored in E41-T05 so the UI and the docs use identical names.

## Out of scope
- Building the components (E41-S01..S04 and the design-system team); post-build design QA (E41-D05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Contrast verified, not assumed
  When the reviewer samples every text/background pair across the four screens in both themes
  Then each pair meets the ratio required by docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md and the measurements are attached to the ticket

Scenario: Reduced motion
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then every specified transition has a defined reduced variant and none of them conveys information that is lost when motion is removed

Scenario: Handoff is self-sufficient
  When a frontend engineer opens the handoff package
  Then every string, token, component id, state and announcement text needed to build SCR-093..096 is present without asking the designer a question

Scenario: Gate
  Given this ticket is not Status Done
  Then E41-S01, E41-S02, E41-S03 and E41-S04 remain blocked
```

## Technical notes / design
Announcement texts are authored as literal strings so engineering does not invent them; e.g. sort change -> "Sorted by R-multiple, descending. 42 trades."; low sample -> "Fewer than 20 trades - statistics are noisy."; pruned context -> "Market context for this trade was not recorded and has been removed by retention. Bar-level review is available."

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact). The authored announcement strings become assertions in the E41-Q03 screen-reader pass.

## Security notes
The copy deck includes the RBAC-scoped variants (what a Viewer and a Manager see); no copy may reveal the existence of accounts outside the viewer's grant beyond the explicit "not in your scope" row agreed in E41-D03.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the a11y design review; its output is the acceptance baseline for the E41-Q03 audit.

## Performance notes
Motion durations bounded so that a filter change on SCR-095 still meets the <=800 ms interactive budget including the transition.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Keyboard map merged into the SCR-093..096 entries in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] Motion spec published with reduced-motion variants.

title: Build SCR-143 system health, SCR-144 incident log and SCR-146 backups/restore
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-011 — System health screen (Must)**: "As the owner, I want live system health, so that I can diagnose problems quickly" — WS connection states, ingest rates and lag, rate-limit budget per account, queue depths, database sizes and latency, error rates and process uptime; drill-down to recent errors and reconnects; and a degraded state that "is escalated with a text label, the affected features are named, and a remediation hint is given". The NFR bounds the cost: "health data is served from the metrics pipeline, with the screen adding ≤1 % load."

The traceability matrix maps US-ADMIN-011 to **SCR-120, SCR-143, SCR-146 and SCR-148**; SCR-120 is E42-S01 and SCR-148 is E42-S05, leaving **SCR-143 Admin: system health** and **SCR-146 Admin: backups & restore** here. **SCR-144 Admin: incident / connectivity log** is the drill-down target SCR-143's sign-off checklist requires ("link to the incident log") and is built with it. **SCR-147 exchange connectivity & rate limits** is designed and owned elsewhere (E04/E46); this story only links to it and renders its summary tile.

The metrics pipeline, health probes and the aggregated health endpoint come from **E04 Observability baseline** (`E04-T04` implements health/readiness/aggregate). This story is the admin surface over them plus the backup/restore operator flow.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-143** at `/admin/health`: per-subsystem rows (API, WS, Bybit public/private/REST plus per-UID rate-limit budget, Ingest, Engine, Recorder, DB tiers, Client FPS) as **CMP-178 SystemHealthTile** with CMP-024 Sparkline and a table alternative for every sparkline; CMP-076 ConnectionStatus; CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner; CMP-210 HealthChips in the shell. Data: `GET /api/v1/admin/health` for the snapshot plus live patches from the WS `system` topic (`kind: health | exchange_state | connection_quality`).
- Drill-down: selecting a subsystem opens its recent errors, recent reconnects and last-hour metrics.
- **Degraded/outage states** per the catalogue: each tile states what stops working and gives a remediation hint; the outage variant states what is still safe — "Native stops on the exchange are unaffected".
- The page must **remain usable while the system it reports on is degraded**: every tile resolves independently, no tile can block another, and a failed probe renders that tile's error state only.
- **SCR-144 incident / connectivity log**: cursor-paginated table (time, subsystem, severity, message, duration, resolution) over `GET /api/v1/admin/incidents`, with filters by subsystem, severity and date, open vs resolved states, an **acknowledge** action (audited) and export; long messages expand into a detail row rather than truncating silently. Live incidents append over `system`.
- **SCR-146** at `/admin/backups`: schedule and retention summary; per-run table (when, target, size, status, verified) from `GET /api/v1/admin/backups`; **Back up now** (`POST /api/v1/admin/backups`), **Verify** (`POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/verify`), **Download** and the **Restore wizard** (`POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/restore`) as a CMP-023-progressed stepper: choose backup → impact preview → typed confirm + step-up → progress → verification → summary.
- Restore guardrails from the catalogue: restore is blocked while any position is open unless the owner explicitly acknowledges ("You have 2 open positions. A restore does not change anything on Bybit. Continue?"); the impact preview states that trading is halted during restore, that exchange state is untouched, and that **market history is not restored from these backups**; downloading a backup containing encrypted secrets warns about handling; last-successful-backup age warning; failed-backup and failed-verification states.
- "Export diagnostics" action on SCR-143 wired to E04's secret-scanned support bundle (`E04-S02`), emitting the audited `health.diagnostics_exported`.
- Audit: `backup.run`, `backup.verified`, `backup.restored` (high), `backup.downloaded` (high), `incident.acknowledged`, `health.diagnostics_exported`.

## Out of scope
- The metrics pipeline, probes, Grafana dashboards and alert rules (E04).
- SCR-147 exchange connectivity & rate limits as a full screen (E04/E46) and SCR-142 storage & database panel (E16/E07) — both linked to, not built here.
- The backup engine, scheduler and restore executor (E45 resilience / ops) — this story consumes the admin API surface listed in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Chaos scenarios proving degraded rendering (E42-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Health overview
  When I open /admin/health
  Then WS connection states, ingest rates and lag, rate-limit budget per account, queue depths, database sizes and latency, error rates and process uptime are shown
  And each tile shows a number with units plus a state word, never colour alone

Scenario: Drill down
  When I select the recorder subsystem
  Then recent errors, recent reconnects and relevant metrics over the last hour are shown

Scenario: Degraded state names the impact
  Given the private WS for sub_002 is down
  Then that tile escalates with a text label, names the affected features, and gives a remediation hint
  And the page states that native exchange stops are unaffected

Scenario: The page survives the outage it reports
  Given GET /api/v1/admin/health times out and the system topic is the only live source
  Then the shell and navigation remain usable
  And each tile renders its own last-known value marked stale rather than an empty page

Scenario: Restore is gated
  Given I have 2 open positions
  When I start the restore wizard
  Then I must acknowledge that a restore does not change anything on Bybit before continuing
  And the impact preview states that trading is halted during restore and that market history is not restored
  And completion requires a typed confirmation and step-up
  And backup.restored is audited at high severity

Scenario (failure): Backup verification fails
  Given the most recent backup fails verification
  Then its row shows the failed-verification state with the reason
  And a warning states how old the last successfully verified backup is

Scenario (edge): No backups yet
  Then the empty state explains that no backup has run, names the schedule, and offers "Back up now"
```

## Technical notes / design
- Snapshot + delta: one `GET /admin/health` on mount, then patches from the auto-subscribed `system` topic at its 1 000 ms throttle (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2). No independent polling timer is created — that is what keeps the screen inside the ≤1 % load NFR.
- `SystemUpdate.components[]` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9) maps 1:1 onto tiles by `name`; unknown component names render generically rather than being dropped, so a backend addition is visible before the frontend knows about it.
- Each tile is an independent subscriber with its own `status` and `lastGoodAt`; a tile older than 3× its expected cadence renders `stale` with the timestamp.
- Restore is a long-running server job with staged progress (`GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`), requires maintenance mode (SCR-148, E42-S05) and is therefore mutually exclusive with an active trading session — the wizard states this rather than discovering it at step 4.
- Downloads are served through a short-lived signed URL from the job result; the URL is never logged and never placed in analytics.
- Sparklines always ship with a table alternative behind a disclosure (a11y requirement), rendered from the same series.
- Error codes: `forbidden`, `conflict` (restore while maintenance is off), `rate_limited`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: tile state machine (`loading → ok → stale → error`) and per-tile isolation; unknown-component fallback; restore wizard step guards (open positions, maintenance mode, typed confirm); last-successful-backup age computation; sparkline↔table equivalence.
- **Contract**: `/admin/health`, `/admin/incidents`, `/admin/backups`, `/admin/backups/{id}/verify|restore`, `/admin/jobs/{jobId}`.
- **Integration**: a `system` frame with a degraded component escalates only its own tile.
- **E2E**: `admin-health.spec.ts` (health render, drill-down, degraded fixture, diagnostics export) and `admin-backups.spec.ts` (backup now → verify → restore wizard happy path and the open-positions guard).
- **Chaos (with E42-Q03)**: kill the health endpoint and the WS mid-session — the page must degrade to stale values, not blank.
- **Perf**: measure the screen's added load against the ≤1 % NFR and the ≤2 ms scripting-per-frame budget with 12 tiles updating at 1 Hz.
- **a11y**: axe; keyboard traversal of tiles and the wizard stepper; screen-reader pass on progress percentages.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/health.ok.json`, `health.degraded.json`, `incidents.page.json`, `backups.list.json`, `backups.verify-failed.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **information disclosure** — a health screen is a reconnaissance surface; internal hostnames, connection strings and stack traces must never be rendered (the support bundle is secret-scanned by E04-S02, and this screen renders only the fields in the `HealthReport` schema). **Tampering/destruction** — restore is the single most destructive action in the product: typed confirm, step-up, maintenance-mode precondition, high-severity audit, and an impact preview that is accurate rather than reassuring. **Information disclosure via download** — a backup contains encrypted secrets; the download warns about handling, is step-up gated and audited at high severity.
- Data classification: operational **Confidential**; backup artefacts are **Secret-bearing** (envelope-encrypted) and are never decrypted client-side.
- `security` review requested on the restore copy specifically (SCR-146 sign-off: "restore impact copy reviewed by security") — tracked in E42-X02.

## Accessibility notes
- Each subsystem is a labelled row with a **text status**; no reliance on dot colour (catalogue a11y requirement).
- Every sparkline has an equivalent data table reachable by keyboard.
- The restore wizard is a stepper with `aria-current="step"`, and progress exposes text percentages, not just a bar.
- Incident messages expand into a detail row rather than truncating silently, so a screen reader can reach the full text.
- Degraded banners are `role="status"`; a new outage is announced once via `role="alert"` and then persists as static text.
- All figures carry units in their accessible names.

## Performance notes
- US-ADMIN-011 NFR: the screen adds ≤1 % load — enforced by consuming the existing `system` subscription and one snapshot GET, with no per-tile polling.
- SCR-143 budget: under 2 ms scripting per frame; SCR-144: 10k rows scroll without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame.
- Storage figures are sampled server-side every 60 s, never computed on request (SCR-142 convention, inherited by the linked tile).
- Restore/verify are server jobs; the browser never performs the work.

## Observability
- Audit: `backup.run`, `backup.verified`, `backup.restored` (high), `backup.downloaded` (high), `incident.acknowledged`, `health.diagnostics_exported`.
- Analytics: `admin.health_viewed`, `incident.log_viewed`, `incident.exported`.
- Metrics consumed (from E04): `cv_ws_clients`, `cv_ingest_lag_ms`, `cv_rate_budget_free_pct`, `cv_db_size_bytes`, `cv_api_request_duration_seconds`. Added here: `cv_admin_health_render_ms`, `cv_backup_restore_total{result}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on new/changed lines; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for every new/changed component variant, including loading, empty, error and degraded states.

- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the signed-off Figma spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as `priority/*` bugs.
- [ ] security: RBAC deny-by-default verified server-side (non-owner receives 404 from the router and 403 from the API); every state-changing control wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and asserted to emit its audit entry.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded for the surface.
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies

- `E42-D05` — hi-fi design for SCR-143/SCR-144/SCR-146 (building on E04-D01's system-health design language).

title: Document admin operations and record ADR-0022 on the admin re-auth model
body:
## Context
Two decisions made in this epic deserve a written record because they will be questioned later and re-litigating them from memory is expensive:

1. **The admin re-auth model** — owner-only plus a 15-minute server-issued elevation token, with router-404/API-403 non-disclosure and a pending-save queue rather than a logout on expiry. This is a deliberate trade-off between friction and blast radius, and it is not obvious.
2. **Flags may never gate a security control** — enforced at startup by a compile-time registry (E42-T03). A future engineer will want to add "just one" auth-related flag; the ADR is what stops that.

Separately, `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` and `22-api-openapi.yaml` must be reconciled with what actually shipped, per the Story/Task DoD ("docs reflect final shipped behavior … if they diverged").

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR-0022 — Admin re-authentication and elevation model** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`: context, the options considered (per-action step-up, session-long elevation, the chosen 15-minute windowed elevation), consequences, and the explicit non-disclosure decision (404 from the router, 403 from the API).
- Extend the flag-safety decision into the same ADR or a short **ADR-0023 — Feature flags may not gate security controls**, whichever the Architect prefers at review; record the compile-time registry as the enforcement mechanism.
- Reconcile `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` entries for SCR-120..124, SCR-135, SCR-136, SCR-143..146, SCR-148, SCR-149 and SCR-154 with shipped behaviour; reconcile `15-component-catalogue.md` for CMP-087, CMP-173, CMP-174, CMP-178, CMP-179.
- Update `22-api-openapi.yaml` examples where the implemented responses differ, and `21-database-schema.md` if the audit index strategy from E42-K01/ADR-0021 changed the DDL.
- Contribute the admin-area sections of the operations runbook owned by **E48-T03** (admin re-auth troubleshooting, audit integrity-failure response, flag rollback, maintenance-mode entry/exit, restore drill) — written here, assembled there.
- Add a changelog fragment describing the admin area for the R3 release notes.

## Out of scope
- The full operations runbook and GA documentation set (E48).
- Pen-test findings documentation (E43).
- User-facing help content (E48).

## Acceptance criteria
- ADR-0022 (and ADR-0023 if split) merged in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` with status Accepted, following the existing ADR template used by ADR-0001..0020.
- Every screen and component listed in Scope either matches the catalogue or has its catalogue entry updated in the same PR; a reviewer can diff the two and find no discrepancy.
- The admin runbook sections are merged and referenced from E48-T03.
- The changelog fragment is present and describes user-visible behaviour, not implementation.
- No documentation change contradicts `00-planning-brief.md`'s locked decisions (web app only, no separate admin app, Bybit USDT perps only).

## Technical notes / design
- ADRs follow the existing format in `27-adrs/README.md` (Context / Decision / Status / Consequences / Alternatives considered).
- Documentation changes ship as one PR per document family to keep diffs reviewable (≤400 LOC guidance).

## Test plan
- Docs CI: markdown lint, link check (relative links must resolve), and the OpenAPI lint/validate job for any `22-api-openapi.yaml` edit.
- A reviewer checklist: each reconciled screen entry is compared against the shipped UI by the design-QA reviewer from E42-D06.

## Security notes
- The ADRs describe security controls; they must not include secrets, key material, internal hostnames or exploit detail beyond what the threat model already records.
- The runbook sections covering audit integrity failure are reviewed by the Security engineer before merge — a wrong instruction there turns an incident into a cover-up.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — documentation task.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
The runbook sections name the exact metrics and alerts that trigger each procedure (`cv_audit_chain_verified`, `cv_backup_last_success_age_seconds`, `cv_maintenance_mode`), so an on-call responder can go from alert to procedure without guessing.

- [ ] Architect review approval on the ADR(s).

title: Ship risk-based sizing and the mandatory native stop-loss field in the ticket
body:
## Context
US-ORD-004 (Must): "size derived from my risk and stop distance, so that every trade risks what I intend". US-ORD-013 (Must): "every entry carries an exchange-side stop, so that my risk survives the app dying" â€” the product's **core safety invariant** (`docs/research/24-owner-decisions.md` cross-cutting Â§3, `20-architecture.md` principle P4).

These two ship together because they are the same control: the stop distance is simultaneously the risk denominator and the protective order. A ticket that lets you clear the stop is a ticket that lets you both trade unprotected and size meaninglessly.

The server is the enforcement point (`POST /api/v1/orders` rejects with `validation_failed` / `native_stop_required`, and E32 owns the OMS-side invariant). This Story is the *user-facing expression*: a field that cannot be emptied, a persistent non-dismissible notice, and a live risk read-out.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-004, US-ORD-013 (ticket surface).** Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-131** (read-only reference to the per-account requirement flag).
- **CMP-119 BracketEditor**: SL and TP in `ticks` / `%` / `R` units, `trigger_by` selector (Last/Mark/Index), `tpsl_mode` Full or Partial, and `nativeSlConfirmed` gating submit â€” submit is disabled until a native SL is present whenever the profile requires it.
- **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice** rendered persistently and non-dismissibly in the bracket section.
- **CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel**: risk in USDT and in R, implied risk % of equity, the resolved stop price and distance, recomputed on every stop or price change with the change visibly highlighted.
- Risk-based sizing mode in **CMP-101 QtyInput**: `riskPct` with a required `stopDistance`; quantity is derived, rounded to the lot step, and the implied risk restated after rounding (rounding down risk, never up).
- Opt-out surfacing: when the owner has disabled the invariant for an account, the ticket shows a persistent warning banner on that account and states that every order will be journaled as unprotected (US-ORD-013 scenario 3) â€” the ticket never offers the opt-out itself; it is set on SCR-131 by the owner.
- Attach-failure state: when the entry is accepted but the protective stop is not yet confirmed, the ticket shows the distinct **"order live, protective stop pending"** state required by `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` Â§5.2, non-colour-only.

## Out of scope
Server-side invariant enforcement and the retry/flatten policy on attach failure (E32); trailing-stop translation (E32); partial TP ladders beyond expressing `tpsl_mode` (E32/E33); profile editing (E28/SCR-131).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Risk sizing (US-ORD-004)
  Given risk 0.5% of a 20 000 USDT equity and a stop 120 USDT away from entry
  Then the quantity is computed, rounded to the lot step, and displayed together with the implied risk in USDT and in R
Scenario: Stop moved recomputes instantly (US-ORD-004)
  When I change the stop price
  Then the quantity and the implied risk recompute within 8 ms and the changed values are visibly highlighted
Scenario: No stop defined (US-ORD-004)
  Given risk-based sizing is selected and no stop is set
  Then submit is blocked with "Risk sizing requires a stop distance." and no request is issued
Scenario: The mandatory native stop cannot be cleared (US-ORD-013)
  Given an account whose profile requires a native stop-loss
  When I clear the stop-loss field
  Then submit is blocked with "This account requires a stop-loss on every order." and the SafetyInvariantNotice remains visible
Scenario: Server disagreement is fatal, not silent (US-ORD-004 NFR)
  Given the client-computed quantity differs from the server's recomputation by more than one lot
  Then the server rejects the order and the ticket shows the server's quantity and the discrepancy rather than retrying
Scenario: Protective stop pending (US-ORD-013)
  Given the entry is acknowledged but no exchange-side stop is confirmed yet
  Then the ticket shows a distinct "order live, protective stop pending" state in text and icon, not colour alone
  And a critical alert has been raised by the backend, which the ticket surfaces as a link
Scenario: Explicit opt-out is loud (US-ORD-013)
  Given the owner has disabled the invariant for this account
  Then a persistent warning banner names the account and states that orders are journaled as unprotected
```

## Technical notes / design
Stop resolution follows `24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3.1 exactly: `ticks` â†’ `ref Â± value*tick_size`; `percent` â†’ `ref*(1âˆ“value)`; `atr` â†’ `ref âˆ“ atr(period)*multiple`; `r_multiple` is invalid *for the stop itself* and is not offered as an SL unit. Rounding is conservative â€” the resolved stop moves **further** from entry, never closer, so realised risk never exceeds the budget. ATR warmup falls back to `fallback_sl_offset_pct` with a visible `stop_fallback` flag.

Risk-based quantity: `qty = floor((equity * riskPct) / stopDistancePerUnit / lotStep) * lotStep`, then the Â§9.3.2 clamp chain, then a restatement of the *post-rounding* risk (which is always â‰¤ the requested risk). All arithmetic is decimal, in `order-ticket-core`.

The "protective stop pending" state is driven by the backend's `NakedPositionAlert` path (`20-architecture.md` Â§10.2) observed on the `orders`/`positions` WS topics â€” the ticket never infers it from the absence of data, because absence is also what a WS gap looks like.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: risk formula across equity/stop/lot combinations incl. sub-lot results; conservative rounding direction; ATR fallback; "no stop" block; cleared-stop block; opt-out banner rendering; pending-stop state transitions.
- **Contract**: `stop_loss` spec serialisation for each unit against `PlaceOrderRequest`.
- **Integration**: server recomputation mismatch (>1 lot) surfaces the discrepancy; attach-failure fixture drives the pending state.
- **Safety suite**: a dedicated test asserts that **no** code path in the ticket can build a request without `stop_loss` when the profile requires it â€” this test is part of the R3 required-check safety suite (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4 Safety gate), so a failure blocks merge, not just release.
- **E2E** in E30-Q02; **chaos** (ack without stop confirmation) in E30-Q04.

## Security notes
This is a safety-critical surface and is `security`-labelled by default per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§8. Abuse case: a crafted client request omitting `stop_loss`, or with a stop on the wrong side, must be rejected server-side (`native_stop_required`) â€” asserted in E30-X02, not assumed here. The opt-out must never be togglable from the ticket; a manual abuse-case check confirms the ticket exposes no such control and that a crafted profile-update request from a manager is refused.

## Accessibility notes
The stop and TP fields are in a labelled fieldset stating the unit; the SafetyInvariantNotice is `role="note"` and always in the accessibility tree. The risk read-out is `aria-live="polite"` and announces "risk 27.5 USDT, 0.8 percent of equity, 1 R" on change (throttled to at most one announcement per 500 ms so fast typing does not flood the screen reader). The "protective stop pending" state is `role="alert"` and is distinguishable in greyscale. The blocked-submit reason is announced when submit is attempted, not only rendered.

## Performance notes
Recompute on stop change â‰¤8 ms (SCR-060). The announcement throttle must not delay the visual update. Risk-read-out updates driven by `ticker` must not exceed one recompute per animation frame.

## Observability
Audit: `orders.submit` includes the resolved stop and the sizing mode; `order.blocked_native_sl_missing` (audited, high severity) when the invariant blocks a submit; `order.unprotected_submitted` when an opt-out account submits. Analytics `ticket.risk_sizing_used`, `ticket.stop_fallback_used`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All seven scenarios pass by automated test; the safety suite test is wired as a required check.
- [ ] Coverage â‰¥80%; CMP-119/CMP-121/CMP-158 Storybook states complete.
- [ ] axe green; manual screen-reader pass on the risk read-out and the pending-stop alert.
- [ ] 8 ms recompute re-measured with risk sizing active.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present; abuse-case check recorded.
- [ ] design-qa against E30-D06; QA sign-off recorded per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed; PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E30-S02** â€” sizing modes and the QtyInput wiring.
- **E30-T01** â€” Â§9.3.1 stop resolution and the risk formula.
- **E32** â€” server-side native-SL invariant, attach-failure policy and the NakedPositionAlert this Story renders.
- **E28** â€” the profile's `require_native_stop` flag, SL/TP offsets and risk caps.

## Branch
`feat/e30-risk-sizing-native-sl` Â· two PRs (bracket + invariant, then risk calculator) to stay â‰¤400 LOC.

## References
- docs/plan/11-user-stories.md Â§17 ORD
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-060, SCR-061, SCR-076, SCR-077, SCR-113, SCR-114, SCR-158
- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-100..107, CMP-119, CMP-121, CMP-122, CMP-130, CMP-139, CMP-158, CMP-229, CMP-231, CMP-232
- docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml `/orders`, `/trade-groups/preview`, `/settings/arm`, `/instruments/{symbol}`, `/risk/summary`
- docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md Â§14.8, Â§15.1â€“Â§15.4
- docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md Â§9.2, Â§9.3, Â§9.4
- docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md Â§5.2 budget #4
- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md Â· docs/plan/04-security-program.md Â· docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md Â§7

title: Implement arm/lock, the environment badge and confirmation policy
body:
## Context
US-ORD-005 (Must): "an explicit arm/lock toggle for one-click trading, so that I never fire an order by accident." The roadmap states this Epic's hardest constraint outright: **"arm/lock control plus an always-visible environment badge â€” no trading control is operable unless both are visible"** (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.2).

That sentence is an availability-of-the-guard requirement, not a styling note: if the arm state or the environment cannot be determined and displayed, trading must fail closed. This Story implements that, plus the per-environment confirmation policy â€” demo may skip confirmation, **live may not**.

Arming is server-backed: `POST /api/v1/settings/arm` returns an `arm_token` with a TTL (default 300 s, max 3600 s) that must accompany any order flagged `one_click`, and that the server invalidates on disarm, session end, kill-switch engagement or a risk-cap breach.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-005**, and the confirmation-policy half of **US-SET-003** as consumed by the ticket. Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-076** (order confirmation modal), **SCR-075** (demo/live banner and per-panel badges â€” consumption), **SCR-040** (arm-state display in the chart trading overlay settings â€” the shared arm store only).
- **CMP-229 ArmToggle** (`scope: "global"` here; chart/DOM scopes are E31), **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal**, **CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard** wrapping every submit affordance, **CMP-044 ConfirmDialog** composing SCR-076 with **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip**, **CMP-232 LimitsChip**, **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice**.
- Arm lifecycle: `POST /api/v1/settings/arm {armed, ttl_seconds}` â†’ token held **in memory only, never persisted** (US-ORD-005 NFR: "state never persists across restarts"); auto-disarm on 30 min inactivity, session lock, environment switch, WS disconnect, kill-switch engagement, risk-cap lockout â€” each with the reason displayed.
- A persistent, high-visibility armed indicator naming the armed state, the target account(s) and the active size (US-ORD-005 scenario 2).
- Confirmation policy from user settings (`GET|PUT /api/v1/settings`, edited on SCR-114 by E30-S07): `always` / `live only` / `never when armed`; **"never" is unavailable for LIVE market orders** and the option is rendered disabled with the reason. SCR-076 restates environment, account(s), side, symbol, type, qty, price, brackets, estimated cost, resulting exposure and profile-limit results, with a configurable 20 s inactivity auto-cancel.
- Fail-closed guard: if `armState` or `environment` is `unknown` (store not hydrated, settings fetch failed, WS auth lost), every submit affordance is disabled with a stated reason and `CMP-139` refuses to dispatch.

## Out of scope
Chart/DOM arm scopes and their click-trade gating (E31); the kill-switch engine and risk lockout evaluation (E39); the environment switcher SCR-074 and live enablement (E44); editing the confirmation policy UI (E30-S07 builds SCR-114).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Disarmed by default (US-ORD-005)
  Given a brand-new session, including after an app restart
  Then one-click is locked and every order requires confirmation, regardless of what was armed before
Scenario: Arming is visible and specific (US-ORD-005)
  When I arm one-click
  Then a persistent high-visibility indicator states the armed state, the target account(s) and the active size
  And the server has issued an arm_token with a stated expiry shown in the indicator
Scenario: Auto-disarm states its reason (US-ORD-005)
  Given 30 minutes of inactivity, or a session lock, or an environment switch, or a WS disconnect
  Then one-click auto-disarms, the reason is displayed, and the arm_token is discarded client-side
Scenario: Fail closed when the guard cannot be shown
  Given the environment badge or the arm state cannot be resolved
  Then every submit affordance is disabled with a stated reason and no request can be dispatched by click, keyboard or hotkey
Scenario: Live cannot skip confirmation
  Given the live environment and a market order
  Then the "never confirm" policy is unavailable and disabled with a reason, and SCR-076 is shown with no default-focused confirm button
Scenario: Confirmation restates the whole order
  When the confirmation modal opens
  Then environment, account(s), side, symbol, type, quantity, price, brackets, estimated cost, resulting exposure and profile-limit results are all restated
  And the modal auto-cancels after the configured inactivity period without submitting
Scenario: Kill-switch invalidates arming immediately
  Given the kill-switch is engaged while one-click is armed
  Then the client disarms within one second of the WS event, the reason is announced, and a subsequent one-click submit is refused server-side with trading_disabled
```

## Technical notes / design
The arm state lives in a single app-wide store with three values: `locked`, `armed{token, expiresAt, scope}`, `unknown`. `unknown` is the initial value and is *also* the value on any error â€” there is no optimistic default. `CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard` is a wrapper, not a hook, so that no submit handler can exist outside it; a lint rule (`no-unguarded-order-submit`) and a unit test assert that every call site of `submit()` is inside a guard.

TTL handling: the client tracks `expiresAt` and disarms locally at expiry, but the **server is authoritative** â€” an expired token is refused with `403` and the client reconciles to `locked`. Clock skew is handled by treating the server's `expires_at` as absolute and disarming 5 s early.

Arming in Live requires a deliberate second action and announces assertively (CMP-229 a11y contract); a single keystroke can never arm in Live.

The environment value is included in every trading audit record (SCR-075) and is read from one shared store subscription so the badge can never disagree between panels.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: the three-state store incl. `unknown` on every error path; auto-disarm for each of the six triggers; TTL expiry and early-disarm; confirmation-policy resolution matrix (env Ã— order type Ã— policy); "never" unavailable for live market; the guard wrapper refusing dispatch.
- **Lint/architecture test**: `no-unguarded-order-submit` fails the build if a submit call escapes CMP-139.
- **Integration**: `POST /settings/arm` happy path, `403` on expired token, kill-switch WS event forcing disarm within 1 s.
- **E2E (Playwright)**: arm â†’ one-click submit on demo; disarm on env switch; live-policy refusal (against a live-shaped fixture, never a real live account).
- **Security**: covered by E30-X02 abuse cases (forged `arm_token`, replay after disarm, guard bypass via programmatic click).
- Coverage â‰¥80%.

## Security notes
Threats (STRIDE from E30-X01): **Spoofing** a forged or replayed `arm_token`; **Tampering** with the persisted confirmation policy to disable LIVE confirmation; **Elevation** by dispatching a submit programmatically outside the guard; clickjacking an armed one-click control. Controls: token validated server-side on every one-click order and invalidated on disarm/kill-switch/risk breach; the policy is stored server-side (`/settings`) and the LIVE-market exclusion is enforced server-side as well as in the UI; the guard-wrapper lint rule plus a runtime assertion; `frame-ancestors 'none'` CSP already set by E09 is re-asserted in a test for the trading routes. Audited: `order.arm_toggled`, `trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled` (high severity), `env.switch_live`.

Arm and auto-disarm changes are announced **assertively** (`role="alert"`), because a silent disarm is a safety problem. The environment band (SCR-075) is a `role="status"` landmark read early in document order, and every trading panel repeats the environment in its accessible name ("Order ticket â€” LIVE â€” Main"). On SCR-076 the confirm button's accessible name restates the whole order and `Enter` only confirms after 400 ms to prevent double-entry pass-through; for LIVE market orders the confirm button is never default-focused.

Analytics `order.confirmation_shown`, `order.confirmation_cancelled`. Metric `cv_ticket_arm_state_seconds{state}` and `cv_ticket_guard_blocked_total{reason}`.

title: Wire trading hotkeys with focus suppression and hold-to-confirm
body:
## Context
US-ORD-006 (Must): "hotkeys for buy/sell, size, flatten and cancel-all, so that execution keeps pace with my read." Hotkeys are where speed and safety collide: the same keystroke that makes a scalper viable can fire a market order into a text field typo. The story's own NFRs set the rules â€” **hotkeyâ†’submit â‰¤50 ms client-side, destructive keys default to hold-to-confirm, everything remappable** â€” and SCR-113's audit rule adds that rebinding a *trading* action is itself an audited event.

This Story owns the trading hotkey **runtime** and the trading rows of the hotkey editor. The editor screen SCR-113 as a whole is a settings surface owned by the settings area; here we contribute its trading-action group, its caution treatment and its conflict rules for destructive bindings.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-006** (and the trading slice of US-SET-002). Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-113** (trading-action rows), **SCR-040** (arm display only).
- Bound actions: buy market, sell market, buy limit at bid, sell limit at ask, set size preset `1..4`, cycle sizing mode, toggle reduce-only, submit (`Ctrl+Enter`), clear ticket (`Esc`), arm/disarm (`Ctrl+Shift+T`), cancel-all on symbol, flatten. (Flatten/cancel-all *execution* belongs to E31/E29; this Story binds the keys and applies the confirm policy, dispatching through the shared intent layer.)
- Persistence in `hotkey_profiles` (`21-database-schema.md` Â§3.8.5) via `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys`, `/settings/hotkeys/{hotkeyProfileId}` and `/settings/hotkeys/{hotkeyProfileId}/activate`; `requires_arm` respected â€” a trading binding does nothing while locked, and says so.
- **Focus suppression**: trading hotkeys never fire while focus is in a text field, a `contenteditable`, or a modal that is not the confirmation modal; a subtle persistent indicator shows that they are suppressed (US-ORD-006 scenario 3).
- **Hold-to-confirm**: destructive actions (flatten, cancel-all, reverse) default to a hold gesture with a visible progress affordance and an announced countdown; the alternatives are immediate and dialog, chosen per action in SCR-114.
- Conflict rules on SCR-113's trading rows: single-letter bindings for destructive commands are refused while the "require a modifier for destructive commands" safety option is on; conflicts name the conflicting action.
- **CMP-022 Kbd**, **CMP-064 KeyboardShortcutRow**, **CMP-054 SearchBox**, **CMP-027 InlineError** on SCR-113; **CMP-229 ArmToggle** for the arm binding.

## Out of scope
The full SCR-113 editor (capture mode, import/export, non-trading actions) â€” settings area; flatten/cancel-all execution semantics (E31, US-ORD-010); chart/DOM-scoped keys (E31); OS-level global hotkeys in Electron (E44/shell).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Buy market (US-ORD-006)
  Given one-click is armed, demo environment, and B is mapped to buy market
  When I press B with the chart or ticket focused and no text field active
  Then a market buy for the active size is submitted to the active target with a native stop attached per the profile
  And the gesture-to-request time is under 50 ms
Scenario: Flatten applies the confirm policy (US-ORD-006)
  When I press the flatten key
  Then the configured policy applies (immediate, hold-to-confirm or dialog)
  And on confirmation the position closes and working orders are cancelled, reported as one operation
Scenario: Hotkey while unfocused (US-ORD-006)
  Given focus is inside a text field
  When I press B
  Then no order is submitted and a subtle indicator shows that trading hotkeys are suppressed
Scenario: Locked means inert (US-ORD-005 interaction)
  Given one-click is locked
  When I press a trading hotkey
  Then nothing is submitted and the reason "One-click trading is locked" is announced
Scenario: Destructive single-letter binding refused
  Given the "require a modifier for destructive commands" option is on
  When I try to bind flatten to F alone
  Then the binding is refused with a message naming the rule, and the previous binding is retained
Scenario: Rebinding a trading action is audited
  When I change the binding of any trading action
  Then hotkey.trading_binding_changed is written to the audit log with the before and after values
```

## Technical notes / design
A single keyboard dispatcher subscribes at the window level in the capture phase, resolves the active `hotkey_profiles` binding map (O(1) lookup), and checks, in this order: (1) focus target is not a text-entry context; (2) no blocking modal; (3) `requires_arm` satisfied; (4) environment and arm state resolved (the E30-S04 fail-closed guard); (5) confirm policy. Only then does it dispatch through the shared ticket intent layer. Ordering matters: the arm check must precede any side-effectful preview so a locked session cannot even warm the request.

To hit the 50 ms budget the dispatch path must not wait on React rendering â€” the handler calls `order-ticket-core.submit()` directly through the store (per the E30-K01/ADR placement) and lets the UI catch up.

Hold-to-confirm uses `pointerdown`/`keydown` with a configurable hold duration (default 600 ms), cancels on early release, and exposes the progress both visually and as an `aria-live` countdown announced at most once per 200 ms.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: dispatcher precedence order; suppression in input/textarea/contenteditable/select and inside modals; `requires_arm` gating; hold-to-confirm complete/cancel; conflict detection incl. the destructive-modifier rule; binding persistence and activation.
- **Perf**: a benchmark asserting keydownâ†’`submit()` call under 50 ms p95 on the loaded workspace (harness from E30-K01).
- **Integration**: profile activation switches the map without a reload; `requires_arm=false` on a non-trading action still works while locked.
- **E2E**: armed hotkey buy on demo; suppressed hotkey in a text field; hold-to-confirm flatten (E30-Q02).
- **axe**: SCR-113 trading rows; bindings readable as text.

## Security notes
Threats: a malicious or accidental key sequence firing an order (mitigated by arm + suppression + hold-to-confirm); a tampered local binding map firing an unintended action (mitigated because the *action semantics* come from the app, not from the stored map â€” only the key is stored â€” and every order is re-authorised and re-validated server-side); binding changes as a social-engineering vector (mitigated by the audit event). Data classification: user preference data, no secrets. Security label applies because this is an order-placement path (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§8).

## Accessibility notes
Every hotkey has a visible, focusable UI equivalent â€” the keyboard is an accelerator, never the only path (`05-accessibility-standard.md`). Suppression state is exposed in text, not only as an icon. The hold-to-confirm progress is announced. SCR-113 capture mode has a keyboard-only alternative (choose modifiers and key from selects) and bindings are readable as text for screen-reader users. Announcements of refusal ("One-click trading is locked") are assertive, since the user expected an order to be placed.

## Performance notes
Hotkeyâ†’submit â‰¤50 ms p95 client-side (US-ORD-006 NFR), measured under a loaded workspace. Binding lookup is O(1) against a precomputed map; the map is rebuilt only on profile change, never per keystroke.

## Observability
Audit `hotkey.trading_binding_changed` `{action, before, after}`; `orders.submit{source:"hotkey"}`. Analytics `hotkey.fired{action}`, `hotkey.suppressed{reason}`. Metric `cv_ticket_hotkey_dispatch_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six scenarios pass by automated test.
- [ ] 50 ms budget measured and recorded.
- [ ] Coverage â‰¥80%; Storybook for the SCR-113 trading rows incl. conflict and refusal states.
- [ ] axe green; manual screen-reader pass on suppression and hold-to-confirm announcements.
- [ ] Security review comment; audit event verified present in the audit chain.
- [ ] QA sign-off; design-qa against E30-D06; demoed.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E30-S04** â€” arm state, the fail-closed guard and the confirmation policy the dispatcher consults.
- **E30-S02** â€” size presets bound to the number keys.
- **E13** â€” the settings shell hosting SCR-113 and the CMP-022/CMP-064 primitives.

## Branch
`feat/e30-trading-hotkeys` Â· two PRs (dispatcher + suppression, then SCR-113 trading rows).

title: Add the pre-trade risk preview and account / trade-group selector
body:
## Context
US-ORD-014 (Should): "a compact preview of what an order will do, so that I never submit blind." The roadmap adds the multi-account half: "account/trade-group selector with the fan-out preview".

The preview is not cosmetic. `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` runs the **full fan-out pipeline** (`24-internal-schemas.md` Â§9.3 sizing, Â§9.4 fan-out) without submitting, returning exactly what each leg would send and, crucially, which legs would be **rejected** and why (cap breach, symbol not allowed, insufficient margin, rate budget exhausted). Showing that before the user commits is what turns a partial fan-out failure from a surprise into a decision.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-014**, plus the selector slice of **SCR-061**. Screens **SCR-060**, **SCR-061** (selector + preview only), **SCR-076** (the fan-out variant of the confirmation, listing every leg).
- **CMP-121 RiskCalculatorPanel** extended to the full preview: resulting position size, average entry, initial margin, estimated liquidation price, risk in USDT and in R, and fees (from `GET /api/v1/exchange-accounts/{accountId}/fee-rate`).
- **CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip** for the estimated slippage on market orders.
- **CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect** + trade-group selection: single account (SCR-060) or a named trade group (SCR-061); groups are read from `GET /api/v1/trade-groups` (CRUD is E28) with per-account enable/disable respected.
- Fan-out preview via `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview`, debounced (`CV_TICKET_PREVIEW_DEBOUNCE_MS`, default 80 ms), showing an aggregate that expands per account, with each would-be-rejected leg listed with its reason.
- **CMP-232 LimitsChip** showing the **binding** constraint by name and its authority (profile / exchange / global), fed by `GET /api/v1/risk/summary` and the instrument filters.
- Stale-input handling: when wallet/balance data is stale the preview shows what it can, marks the stale inputs, and disables risk-based sizing (US-ORD-014 scenario 3).

## Out of scope
Trade-group CRUD and per-account enable/disable editing (E28, SCR-062); fan-out execution, the rate-limit governor, partial-failure unwind (E34); the positions/orders blotter (E29); per-account PnL views (E34/E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preview (US-ORD-014)
  Given a configured ticket on a single account
  Then the preview shows resulting position size, average entry, initial margin, estimated liquidation price, risk in USDT and in R, and fees
Scenario: Group preview (US-ORD-014)
  Given a trade group of three accounts is selected as the target
  Then the preview aggregates across accounts and can be expanded to show each account's own resolved quantity, stop and margin
Scenario: Rejected legs are shown before committing
  Given one account's profile disallows the symbol and another has insufficient margin
  Then both legs are listed as would-be-rejected with their reasons, the aggregate excludes them, and submitting is still possible for the remaining legs only after an explicit acknowledgement
Scenario: Preview unavailable (US-ORD-014)
  Given account balance data is stale and cannot be refreshed
  Then the preview shows what it can, marks the stale inputs explicitly, and risk-based sizing is disabled with a stated reason
Scenario: Preview never places an order
  When the preview endpoint is called on every keystroke
  Then no state is mutated, no idempotency key is consumed, and calls are debounced and rate-limited client-side
Scenario: Manager scope
  Given a manager who has been granted only two of the group's three accounts
  Then the selector offers only the granted accounts and the server refuses the ungranted one with 403 rather than silently narrowing the group
```

## Technical notes / design
`POST /trade-groups/preview` is documented as safe to call on every keystroke and is rate-limited rather than idempotency-keyed â€” but "safe" is not "free": the client debounces at 80 ms, cancels in-flight requests with `AbortController`, and renders the last-known preview greyed while a new one is in flight rather than blanking (a blanking preview during fast typing is worse than a slightly stale one, provided staleness is marked).

Liquidation price and margin are **estimates** and are labelled as such per architecture principle P10 ("estimated is labelled"), with the `(estimated)` chip.

The aggregate must never be silently partial: if any leg's data is unavailable, the aggregate states "aggregate excludes sub_002 (state unknown)" rather than presenting a smaller number as complete â€” the same rule `GET /risk/summary` applies server-side when it refuses a partial aggregate with `403 account_scope_denied`.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: preview field rendering incl. estimated labelling; aggregate vs per-account expansion; rejected-leg listing per reason; stale marking and the risk-sizing disable; debounce and abort behaviour; partial-aggregate refusal copy.
- **Contract**: `CreateTradeGroupRequest` sent to `/trade-groups/preview` and `TradeGroupPreview` parsed, validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **Integration**: fixtures for all four rejection reasons (cap breach, symbol not allowed, insufficient margin, rate budget exhausted); a 403 account-scope response.
- **Perf**: preview recompute path within 100 ms of an input change for the locally-derived parts (US-ORD-014 NFR), with the network part excluded and measured separately.
- **E2E**: three-account group preview then submit, in E30-Q02.
- **axe**: expansion control, table semantics of the per-leg breakdown.

## Security notes
Account scope is the central threat: the selector must be populated from the server's granted-accounts list only, and every preview and submit re-authorises server-side (`scope: granted_accounts`). A manager must not be able to discover the existence of ungranted accounts through the group selector â€” groups containing ungranted accounts are shown with those legs omitted **and** labelled as narrowed, so no hidden fan-out occurs. Preview responses contain financial data and are account-scoped; they are never cached across account switches. Covered by the E30-X02 abuse-case suite.

## Accessibility notes
The per-account breakdown is a real `<table>` with row headers per account, not a div grid, so screen-reader users can navigate it. The binding limit is named in text and announced when it changes ("Blocked by daily loss cap: 480 of 500 USDT used"). Every estimate carries the word "estimated" in its accessible name, not only a visual chip. The expand/collapse control states the number of legs. Stale inputs are marked in text.

## Performance notes
Local preview recompute â‰¤100 ms (US-ORD-014 NFR); the debounce must not push the perceived update beyond 200 ms. The preview must not contribute to the budget #4 submit path â€” it runs on a separate connection concern and is cancelled on submit.

## Observability
Analytics `ticket.preview_expanded`, `ticket.preview_leg_rejected{reason}`, `ticket.group_selected{legCount}`. Metric `cv_ticket_preview_latency_ms`. No audit event (preview mutates nothing), but a submit following a preview records the preview's correlation id so the journal can show what the user was shown.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six scenarios pass by automated test.
- [ ] Coverage â‰¥80%; Storybook for aggregate, expanded, rejected-leg, stale and narrowed-group states.
- [ ] axe green; manual screen-reader pass on the per-leg table and the binding-limit announcement.
- [ ] 100 ms local recompute measured; preview shown not to affect budget #4.
- [ ] Security review of the account-scope behaviour; E30-X02 scope abuse cases green.
- [ ] design-qa against E30-D06; QA sign-off; demoed.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E30-S03** â€” risk figures and the resolved stop the preview reports.
- **E28** â€” trade groups, per-account profiles and the Â§9.3/Â§9.4 pipeline behind `/trade-groups/preview`.
