title: Ship order templates and the SCR-114 trading-defaults settings section
body:
## Context
US-ORD-012 (Should): "saved combinations of order, bracket and size, so that repeated setups are one click." Templates are the user-facing half; **SCR-114 Trading defaults** is the settings half that decides what a *fresh* ticket looks like and, importantly, which confirmation policy applies. SCR-114 also carries a hard product rule: **user defaults can never exceed the per-account profile limits set by the owner**, and each limit is shown inline as a ceiling.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **US-ORD-012**, and the storage/editing of the confirmation policy consumed by E30-S04. Screens **SCR-114** (trading defaults), **SCR-077** (template application from a rejection retry is E30-T02; templates appear in its "retry with corrections" affordance).
- Template model: name, order type, side, sizing spec, bracket spec, TIF and flags, optional pinned account or trade group. Stored per user through `GET|PUT /api/v1/settings` (templates live in the user-settings document; a dedicated migration is added only if the settings document exceeds its size guard â€” recorded as a decision on the ticket).
- Template list with apply, rename, delete, duplicate and **bind to a hotkey** (through the E30-S05 dispatcher and `hotkey_profiles`).
- Applying a template populates every field and applies the pinned target if the template has one; a template pinning an account the user cannot trade is shown **disabled with the reason**, never silently applied to a different account.
- SCR-114 sections: default order type, TIF, default qty and the preset ladder, default sizing rule (`fixed_qty` / `fixed_notional` / `pct_equity` / `risk_based`), default SL/TP offsets (ticks / % / R), confirm-before-send rules (always / live only / never when armed), one-click arm persistence, auto-reset ticket after send, sound on fill â€” with **separate DEMO and LIVE default sets**.
- Enforced rules on SCR-114: "skip confirmation" is unavailable for LIVE market orders; the default SL is mandatory and cannot be set to "none"; every limit is shown inline as a ceiling with a pointer to SCR-131 for per-account overrides.
- **CMP-040 FormField**, **CMP-065 FormSection**, **CMP-086 SettingsLayout**, **CMP-119 BracketEditor**, **CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons**, **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice**, **CMP-231 TifSelect**.

## Out of scope
Per-account profile editing (E28, SCR-131); algo/bracket templates that include emulated algos (E33); sharing or exporting templates between users (not in scope for v1); the hotkey editor screen itself (E30-S05 contributes its trading rows).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Save template (US-ORD-012)
  Given a fully configured ticket
  When I save it as "scalp long"
  Then it appears in the template list and can be bound to a hotkey
Scenario: Apply template (US-ORD-012)
  When I apply "scalp long"
  Then every field populates, and the pinned account or trade group is applied if the template pins one
Scenario: Template invalid for context (US-ORD-012)
  Given a template pinning an account I am not granted, or a symbol my profile disallows
  Then the template is shown disabled with the reason and cannot be applied by click or by its hotkey
Scenario: Defaults cannot exceed profile limits
  Given the account profile caps leverage at 10x
  When I set a default above that
  Then the value is refused with "Your profile caps leverage at 10x." and the ceiling is shown inline
Scenario: LIVE confirmation cannot be switched off for market orders
  Given the LIVE default set
  Then the "never confirm" option for market orders is disabled with a stated reason
  And attempting it via a crafted settings request is refused server-side and audited
Scenario: The default stop cannot be "none"
  When I try to clear the default SL offset
  Then it is refused with the safety-invariant message and the SafetyInvariantNotice stays visible
Scenario: Templates contain no secrets
  Then an exported or stored template contains no API key, token or account credential of any kind
```

## Technical notes / design
Templates are validated against the current context at **render** time, not only at apply time, so a disabled template explains itself before the user reaches for it. Validation reuses `order-ticket-core.validate()` against a synthetic draft, so template validity and ticket validity can never disagree.

DEMO and LIVE default sets are stored as two distinct documents keyed by environment; switching environments switches the applied set and never carries a LIVE-unsafe setting (like skipped confirmation) across from DEMO. Defaults apply to **newly opened tickets only**; existing tickets keep their state (SCR-114 performance note). Save round-trip â‰¤400 ms.

## Test plan
- **Unit (â‰¥80%)**: template save/apply/rename/delete/duplicate; disabled-template conditions (ungranted account, disallowed symbol, unavailable order type); defaults-vs-profile ceiling enforcement per field; LIVE confirmation exclusion; mandatory default SL; DEMO/LIVE set isolation.
- **Contract**: settings payload validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/settings`.
- **Integration**: a settings write that violates a profile ceiling is refused server-side (not only client-side).
- **Security test**: serialised templates are asserted to contain no secret-shaped values.
- **axe + visual** on all SCR-114 sections and the template list.

## Security notes
Threats: tampering with stored defaults to disable LIVE confirmation (mitigated â€” the rule is enforced server-side and the attempt is audited at high severity as `trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled`); a template pinning an ungranted account as a scope-probing oracle (mitigated â€” the disabled reason must not reveal the existence or name of an account the user cannot see; it says "this template targets an account you cannot trade"); secrets in templates (mitigated â€” a test asserts the shape). Every defaults change is audited as `trading_defaults.changed {key, before, after, environment}`.

## Accessibility notes
Fieldsets per topic; every numeric field states its unit; the confirmation-policy radio group states the **consequence** of each option, not just its name. Disabled templates and disabled options always state why in text. The ceiling annotations are associated with their field via `aria-describedby`, so a screen-reader user hears the cap when they enter the field rather than only on failure.

## Performance notes
Save round-trip â‰¤400 ms (SCR-114). Template apply populates the ticket within the 8 ms recompute budget. The template list is rendered from already-loaded settings â€” no fetch on open.

## Observability
Audit `trading_defaults.changed`, `trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled` (high severity). Analytics `template.saved`, `template.applied{hasPinnedTarget}`, `template.disabled_shown{reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All seven scenarios pass by automated test.
- [ ] Coverage â‰¥80%; Storybook for the template list and every SCR-114 section incl. the refusal states.
- [ ] axe green; manual screen-reader pass on the ceiling annotations and consequence copy.
- [ ] Security review of the defaults-tampering path; audit events verified in the chain.
- [ ] design-qa against E30-D06; QA sign-off; demoed.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E30-S04** â€” the confirmation policy this screen edits and the arm-persistence setting.
- **E30-S02** â€” the preset ladder definition edited here and consumed there.

title: One-click flatten, cancel-all and reverse with the confirmation policy
body:
## Context
**US-ORD-010 — Flatten and cancel-all (Must)** and **US-ORD-011 — Reverse position (Should)**. These are the exit controls: the ones a trader reaches for when something is going wrong, and therefore the ones that must be fastest, most reliable and least ambiguous. They are also the most destructive, so the confirm policy and the per-account result reporting matter as much as the action itself.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screens**: SCR-063 Positions & orders grid (the flatten entry point per the traceability matrix), SCR-072 Kill-switch / freeze confirmation modal (the flatten / cancel-all confirmation variant), SCR-076 Order confirmation modal (the **reverse** variant), SCR-030 and SCR-050 (the chart/ladder entry points and the flatten/reverse hotkeys in those scopes).
- **Components**: CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-093, CMP-123, CMP-211 (per the SCR-072 catalogue entry), CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-130 SlippageEstimateChip, CMP-232 LimitsChip, CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal (per SCR-076).
- **Flatten symbol**: cancel working orders then close the position with a **reduce-only market order** (never a plain market order — reversal by accident is the failure mode being designed out), reported as **one operation** with a per-step result. Uses `POST /api/v1/orders/cancel-all` + `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/close`.
- **Flatten group**: each account flattens; results reported **per account**; a failed leg is retried **once** automatically and the residual failure is surfaced with a next action (US-ORD-010 scenario 2). Completes within 2 s for 5 accounts.
- **Nothing to flatten**: reports "nothing to flatten" with **no exchange call at all** (asserted by a network-level test).
- **Reverse**: `POST /api/v1/positions/{positionId}/reverse` — closes and opens the opposite side in one operation with a fresh native stop attached in the same operation (US-ORD-011 NFR: never leave a position without a stop after a reverse). Reverse **always requires explicit confirmation even when one-click is armed**, and the confirmation restates current position, resulting position, quantity, the stop that will attach, and margin required vs available.
- **Insufficient margin**: refused *before* sending, showing required versus available margin.
- Confirm policy integration: immediate / hold-to-confirm / dialog per environment, with LIVE never permitted to skip; destructive hotkeys default to hold-to-confirm (US-ORD-006 NFR).
- Kill-switch interaction documented and implemented per its stated semantics ("stops new risk, does not force-close") — flatten is a separate, documented panic path (`POST /api/v1/positions/close-all` is the flatten-all control referenced by SCR-072) and the UI must make the distinction explicit rather than implying the kill-switch closes positions.

## Out of scope
The kill-switch control itself and risk lockouts (E39). Trade-group definition and fan-out scheduling/rate governance (E28/E34) — this story consumes the group target and reports per-leg outcomes. Blotter-level bulk actions beyond flatten (E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Flatten symbol
  Given an open BTCUSDT position and two working orders on account A
  When I flatten BTCUSDT on account A
  Then the working orders are cancelled and the position is closed with a reduce-only market order,
  and the whole thing is reported to me as one operation with its per-step results

Scenario: Flatten group
  Given a trade group of three accounts, one of which fails on the first attempt
  Then each account's result is reported separately, the failed leg is retried once automatically,
  and a residual failure is shown with an explicit next action

Scenario: Flatten with nothing open
  Given no position and no working orders
  Then the action reports "nothing to flatten" and makes no exchange call

Scenario: Reverse
  Given a long of 0.2 BTC
  When I confirm a reverse
  Then a market order of 0.4 is sent, the resulting short is shown, and a fresh native stop is attached in the same operation

Scenario: Reverse always confirms
  Given one-click trading is armed
  When I trigger reverse
  Then explicit confirmation is still required and the LIVE variant offers no "don't ask again"

Scenario: Insufficient margin
  Given margin is insufficient for the resulting position
  Then the reverse is refused before any exchange call, showing required versus available margin

Scenario: Destructive hotkey is not a single tap
  Given the flatten hotkey with the default policy
  Then it requires hold-to-confirm, and a single tap does nothing

Scenario: Timing
  Given a flatten across five accounts
  Then the operation completes within two seconds
```

## Technical notes / design
Flatten is composed, not atomic at the exchange: cancel-all then reduce-only close. The UI must therefore model it as a small local saga with per-step state, and must never report success until both steps have their acknowledgements — a cancelled-but-not-closed outcome is a visible partial state, not a success.

Reduce-only is mandatory on the close leg (US-ORD-010 NFR). `POST /api/v1/positions/close-all` is the flatten-all panic control referenced from SCR-072; the symbol/account-scoped flatten uses the per-position endpoint.

Automatic retry is exactly **one** attempt, with jitter, and must respect the rate-limit governor; a second failure escalates to the user rather than looping.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: saga state machine (cancel ok/close fail, cancel fail/close ok, both fail, nothing-open short-circuit); per-account result aggregation; single-retry logic; margin pre-check arithmetic; confirm-policy resolution per environment and per action.
- **Integration**: recorded fixtures for a failing close, a `10018` rate-limited leg, and an exchange 5xx mid-flatten.
- **E2E (web + Electron)**: on demo, open a position, flatten it from SCR-063 and assert both cancellation and closure on the exchange; reverse a position and assert the resulting side, size and the attached stop; trigger flatten with nothing open and assert **zero** network calls.
- **Chaos** (feeds E31-Q04): kill the WS mid-flatten and assert the operation reconciles to a correct, visible state.
- **Perf**: 5-account flatten within 2 s.
- **A11y**: confirmation dialogs as `alertdialog`, focus trap and return, action restated in the accessible name, per-account results announced as a summary.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend; the saga module held to ≥90 % as a risk module.

## Security notes
Destructive, position-closing path → `security`-labelled. Threats: accidental flatten/reverse (hold-to-confirm, always-confirm on reverse, no default-focused confirm for LIVE market actions per SCR-076), unauthorised flatten of another user's accounts (server-side `account_scope` re-check), accidental **reversal** instead of close (reduce-only on the close leg is the structural control), and leaving a position unprotected after a reverse (stop attaches in the same operation; E32 enforces server-side). Repudiation: every flatten/reverse audited per account with the operation id. Abuse cases: flatten accounts outside scope; reverse while kill-switched; reverse with the SL attachment stubbed to fail, asserting the documented failure policy fires.

## Accessibility notes
Hold-to-confirm must have a keyboard-operable equivalent that is not a timed key-hold trap for AT users (per E31-D05: a dialog path is always available); the confirm button's accessible name restates the whole action; `Enter` confirms only after the 400 ms guard (SCR-076); per-account results are a table, not a stream of alerts.

## Performance notes
Flatten across 5 accounts ≤2 s; hotkey→submit ≤50 ms client-side; the confirmation modal is prepared from loaded state and appears ≤100 ms (SCR-076).

## Observability
Audit `position.flattened`, `position.reversed`, `order.cancel_requested` (per account, with the operation id and provenance); analytics `trading.flatten_invoked`, `trading.reverse_invoked`, `order.confirmation_shown/cancelled`; metrics `cv_flatten_duration_ms{accounts}`, `cv_flatten_leg_failures_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated, including the zero-network-call assertion for the no-op case.
- [ ] Coverage met (≥90 % on the saga module).
- [ ] axe-core green; dialogs verified with a screen reader; hold-to-confirm alternative verified.
- [ ] 5-account timing benchmark recorded.
- [ ] Security review; abuse cases executed and recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E31-D07); QA sign-off; demoed on demo.
- [ ] Feature flags `trading.flatten_enabled`, `trading.reverse_enabled` recorded with per-environment defaults.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-T01** (intent layer and audit), **E31-D03** (design handoff), **E30** (confirmation policy per environment and the arm/lock control), **E32** (the fresh native stop that must attach on reverse) and **E39** (kill-switch and lockout state, which must short-circuit flatten/reverse).

**Scheduling.** E39 completes in S16; E30 and E32 complete at the end of S17; this story therefore sits in **Sprint 18**, strictly after every blocker's completion sprint.

## Branch
`feat/e31-flatten-reverse`. Split: flatten saga PR, then reverse + confirmations PR.

title: Generate and submit scaled entry ladders and DCA ladders with a shared stop
body:
## Context
Two Should-stories share one engine. `US-ALGO-004` (scaled entry orders) wants a size split across N price levels with equal/linear/geometric distribution, partial-placement failure that keeps the placed legs and retries only the failed one, and group cancellation that leaves any filled portion with its protective orders intact. `US-ALGO-009` (DCA / scale-in safety ladders) adds a size multiplier, a **shared stop**, refusal when the fully-filled ladder would exceed the account risk cap, and a concurrent-order cap that queues the rest.

`24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.6 (`ScaledParams`) specifies the maths exactly: 2..50 levels, conservative rounding, duplicate-price merge, remainder to the level nearest `price_start`, sub-minimum levels dropped and redistributed proportionally, and submission via Bybit's batch endpoint at 10 orders per request where **partial success is possible** and must be handled per-item from the batch response's `retCode`.

The critical safety subtlety in `US-ALGO-009`'s NFR: *"projected risk computed for the fully-filled ladder, never for the first leg alone."*

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-004`, `US-ALGO-009`.
- `services/oms/algos/scaled.py` — `ScaledSupervisor` (module M14) implementing `AlgoSpec{kind="scaled"}` / `ScaledParams`.
- Pure ladder generator `generate_levels(params, instrument) -> tuple[Level, ...]`: price spacing, weight computation (`equal`, `linear` and `geometric` with `skew`, `custom` normalised weights), conservative rounding, duplicate-price merge, remainder to the level nearest `price_start`, sub-minimum drop-and-redistribute.
- DCA mode: levels expressed as percentage offsets from a reference price with a size multiplier; **one shared stop** covering the whole ladder rather than one stop per level; projected average entry, total position and total risk computed for the **fully-filled** ladder.
- Risk-cap integration (E39): the projected fully-filled risk is checked against the account cap before any order is sent; on breach the ladder is refused with the projected risk and the cap both stated.
- Concurrent-order cap: at most `max_concurrent_legs` resting at once; the remainder queues and is placed as earlier legs fill, with the queue exposed on the `trade_groups` topic.
- Batch submission at 10 orders/request with per-item `retCode` handling; failed legs recorded with their own error codes and individually retryable via `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/amend`.
- Group cancel via `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/{tradeGroupId}/cancel` -> `cancel-batch`, leaving any filled portion and its protective orders intact.
- Preview endpoint support: `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` returns the generated ladder plus the projected rate-limit cost, so SCR-065 can show the table before anything is sent.
- Native SL: every level passes through E32-T01; DCA's shared stop is attached to the resulting position and re-sized as legs fill.
- Audit `algo.scaled_created`, `algo.scaled_cancelled`, `algo.scaled_partially_cancelled`.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-065 UI (E32-S06), TWAP/iceberg slicing (E33), multi-account fan-out of a ladder (E34), the risk-cap mechanism itself (E39).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A linear ladder is generated and placed
  Given 5 orders between 63,000 and 62,500 with linear distribution and a total of 1.0 BTC
  When the ladder is submitted
  Then five limit orders are placed with sizes per the linear weights, quantities summing exactly to 1.0 BTC with the remainder on the level nearest the start price, and a single group summary is returned

Scenario: Partial batch placement is surfaced and individually retryable (error)
  Given the third leg is rejected by the batch response with its own retCode
  Then the four placed orders remain working, the failure is reported with the exchange reason against that leg, the group is marked partially placed, and I can retry only the failed leg without disturbing the others

Scenario: Cancelling the group preserves the filled portion
  Given two of five legs have filled
  When I cancel the group
  Then all unfilled legs are cancelled, the filled position remains with its protective orders intact and still natively stopped, and algo.scaled_partially_cancelled is audited

Scenario: A DCA ladder that breaches the risk cap is refused (failure)
  Given a three-step DCA ladder at -0.5%, -1.0% and -1.8% with a 1.5 size multiplier whose fully-filled risk exceeds the account cap
  When it is requested
  Then it is refused before any order is sent, the response states the projected fully-filled risk and the cap it exceeds, and no partial ladder is placed

Scenario: Levels below the minimum lot are redistributed, not silently dropped (edge)
  Given a ladder whose levels 4 and 5 would round below the instrument minimum order quantity
  Then those levels are dropped, their quantity is redistributed proportionally to the surviving levels, the response names which levels were dropped and why, and if no viable ladder remains the request is refused with a single-order alternative

Scenario: The concurrent-leg cap queues the rest (edge)
  Given a 10-level ladder with a concurrent cap of 3
  Then exactly three legs rest at once, the remaining seven are visible as queued on the trade_groups topic, and each queued leg is placed as an earlier one fills

Scenario: Duplicate prices after rounding are merged (edge)
  Given a narrow price range where two levels round to the same tick
  Then the two levels are merged into one order with their quantities summed, so the ladder never contains two orders at the same price
```

## Technical notes / design
- The generator is a **pure function** with no I/O so the same code runs in the preview endpoint and in submission — SCR-065's preview table and the placed orders can never disagree.
- Weights per section 10.6: `equal` -> `1/n`; `linear` -> weight `i` scaled by `skew` (>1 weights the far end, <1 the near end); `geometric` -> `skew^i`; `custom` -> normalised `custom_weights` whose length must equal `levels`.
- Rounding is **conservative** (floor to `qty_step`, prices to `tickSize` away from the market for entries) so a ladder never exceeds the requested total.
- Batch transport: `submit_mode="batched"`, `batch_size=10` (Bybit's cap); the response is processed per item, and a whole-request failure is distinguished from per-item failures.
- Risk projection for DCA: `projected_qty = sum(level_qty)`, `projected_avg = weighted mean`, `projected_risk = projected_qty * |projected_avg - shared_stop|`, checked against E39's cap for the account. This is the fully-filled figure the NFR demands.
- Rate-limit awareness: the preview returns the projected request count; submission tags legs `priority="normal"` so they can never consume the protective reserve.
- Cross-check with `instruments-info` precision filters (`priceFilter`, `lotSizeFilter`) supplied by E28's validation layer.

## Test plan
- **Unit (>=90%):** each distribution's weights; skew behaviour; rounding and remainder placement; duplicate merge; sub-minimum drop and redistribution; the no-viable-ladder refusal; DCA multiplier and projected-risk maths; concurrent-cap queueing.
- **Property tests:** placed quantities always sum to the requested total (or the request is refused); no level below the minimum ever reaches the adapter; no two levels share a price.
- **Contract:** `AlgoSpec.scaled`, `/trade-groups/preview` response, per-leg error shape.
- **Integration:** recorded fixtures — batch partial success, whole-batch rejection, `10018` rate-limit mid-ladder, leg fill during queueing.
- **E2E:** via SCR-065 in E32-Q04.
- Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/bybit/batch_partial_success.json`, `batch_rate_limited.json`.

## Security notes
Order placement path (`security` label mandatory). Threats: **DoS** — a 50-level ladder saturating the order-create bucket so a stop cannot be placed, mitigated by the level cap, the `normal` priority class and `reserved_for_protective`; **tampering** — a preview computed client-side diverging from what is submitted, mitigated by the shared pure generator and server-side re-computation at submit time (the client's preview is never trusted); **elevation** — account scope checked per leg. All group mutations audited with the full parameter set per SCR-065's audit spec.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The preview table contract exists specifically so SCR-065 can render an accessible real table (E32-S06).

## Performance notes
Preview generation must complete in <=5 ms server-side so SCR-065 can recompute within one frame. Submission of a 50-level ladder is 5 batch requests; total submit->ack p95 must stay inside budget #4 per request, and the ladder must not push the account over its per-UID budget (checked before the first request is sent).

## Observability
`oms_scaled_levels_submitted_total{result}`, `oms_scaled_ladder_refused_total{reason}`, `oms_scaled_batch_partial_total`, `oms_scaled_queued_legs` gauge. Audit `algo.scaled_created` with `{symbol, side, levels, totalQty, priceRange, distribution, accountIds, environment}`, `algo.scaled_cancelled`, `algo.scaled_partially_cancelled`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; property tests in place.
- [ ] Coverage >=90% on M14.
- [ ] Schema delta for section 10.6 drafted for E32-T04.
- [ ] Security-engineer review comment; abuse case "ladder burns the protective reserve" verified failing to reproduce.
- [ ] Perf: preview <=5 ms, submission within budget #4.
- [ ] QA sign-off from E32-Q03.
- [ ] Demoed on demo at Sprint Review.
- [ ] Feature flag `oms.scaled_orders` recorded.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue (split into generator and transport PRs to stay under 400 LOC).

## Dependencies
`E32-T01` (guard), `E29` (submission pipeline, batch transport, reconciler), `E28` (profiles, instrument precision filters, risk inputs), `E39` (risk-cap evaluation for the DCA projection).

title: Build the SCR-065 scaled and DCA ladder builder with a full preview table
body:
## Context
`SCR-065` "Scaled / ladder order builder" is the modal that splits size across N orders between two prices with equal/linear/geometric distribution and a **preview table of every child order**. Its spec fixes the validation rules (2-50 child orders; each child >= min lot, with the message "Child 5 is below the minimum — reduce the order count"; a range crossing the mark is a warning, not a block), the states (preview, placing with per-child progress, partial placement failure with retry), and the a11y requirement that the generated ladder is previewed as a **real table** with level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional and resulting average, with a submit button that names the total ("Place 8 orders, 0.64 BTC total").

Its performance note is explicit: preview recomputes locally within one frame, and submission fans the levels out in a **single backend request** so the per-account rate-limit budget is evaluated server-side and reported back before any order is sent. The screen also demands the mandatory native SL be drawn explicitly, per level or per resulting position.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories: `US-ALGO-004` (UI half), `US-ALGO-009` (UI half).
- Screen `SCR-065`; components `CMP-010` Slider, `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-100` PriceInput, `CMP-101` QtyInput, `CMP-119` BracketEditor, `CMP-130` SlippageEstimateChip, `CMP-228` PreviewTile, `CMP-158` SafetyInvariantNotice.
- `apps/web/src/features/algo/ScaledBuilder/` — generator inputs (from price, to price, order count, total qty, distribution, skew, reduce-only, TIF), DCA mode (percent offsets, size multiplier, shared stop), the preview table, the rate-limit estimate, and submit.
- Preview is fetched from `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` so the table is generated by the same server-side pure generator that submits (never a client re-implementation), with a local optimistic recompute for slider responsiveness that is always reconciled against the server result before submit is enabled.
- Preview table columns: level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional, resulting average entry.
- Summary tiles (CMP-228): total quantity, average entry, total notional, projected risk for the **fully-filled** ladder versus the account cap, and the projected request count as a share of the minute budget.
- Native SL affordance: the shared stop (DCA) or per-position stop is shown as always-present and non-removable via CMP-158.
- Validation surfaces: 2-50 levels; sub-minimum child message; range-crosses-mark warning; risk-cap refusal from E32-S03 restated with projected risk and cap.
- States: preview, placing (per-child progress), partial placement failure with per-leg retry, cancelled, error.
- Analytics/audit per the screen spec: `algo.scaled_previewed`, `algo.scaled_distribution_changed` (analytics); server emits the audited events.

## Out of scope
- The ladder maths itself (E32-S03 owns it server-side), TWAP/iceberg builders (E33), SCR-064 (E32-S07), multi-account fan-out selection (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The preview table matches what gets placed
  Given 5 orders between 63,900 and 63,700 with linear distribution, skew 1.4 and a total of 1.00 BTC
  When the preview renders
  Then a real table shows level, price, qty, cumulative qty, cumulative notional and the resulting average for each of the five children, and submitting places exactly those orders

Scenario: The submit control names the whole action
  Given a valid 8-level ladder totalling 0.64 BTC
  Then the submit button reads "Place 8 orders, 0.64 BTC total" and the rate-limit estimate is shown before submission

Scenario: A child below the minimum lot is explained (error)
  Given an order count that would push child 5 below the instrument minimum
  Then the message "Child 5 is below the minimum - reduce the order count" is shown inline, submission is blocked, and the offending row is marked in the table

Scenario: A range that crosses the mark warns without blocking (edge)
  Given a buy ladder whose upper price is above the current mark
  Then a warning is shown explaining the immediate-fill consequence, and submission remains possible

Scenario: A DCA ladder over the risk cap is refused with numbers (failure)
  Given a DCA ladder whose fully-filled risk exceeds the account cap
  When I submit
  Then the refusal states the projected fully-filled risk and the cap it exceeds, the ladder is not placed, and my inputs are preserved so I can reduce size

Scenario: Partial placement offers a per-leg retry (failure)
  Given three of five legs place and two are rejected
  Then the table marks each leg placed or failed with the exchange reason, a retry action is offered for the failed legs only, and cancelling the group leaves any filled portion with its protective orders intact
```

## Technical notes / design
- The local recompute exists only for slider smoothness; a `previewToken` from the server response gates the submit button, so a stale local preview can never be submitted.
- Table is virtualised at 50 rows (trivially, but consistently with CMP-049's contract) and remains a real `<table>` with header associations for screen readers.
- Rate-limit estimate comes from the preview response, not a client guess.
- Slider and numeric inputs stay in sync bidirectionally; the distribution selector changes only weights, never the price bounds.
- Storybook stories for all states including partial failure and risk-cap refusal.

## Test plan
- **Unit/component (>=80%):** input binding and slider sync; preview token gating; validation messages; per-leg retry state; DCA mode inputs.
- **Contract:** preview request/response against `/trade-groups/preview` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **E2E (Playwright web + Electron):** generate, preview, submit, partial-failure retry, risk-cap refusal — added in E32-Q04.
- **a11y:** axe-core on every state; table semantics verified with a screen reader; keyboard-only generation and submission.
- **Perf:** preview interaction measured within one frame.

## Security notes
Order-placing surface, `security` handling. The client's preview is advisory only — the server regenerates and revalidates at submit time (E32-S03), so a tampered client preview cannot place a different ladder. The rate-limit estimate is informational; enforcement is server-side. Account scope from the session; no secrets client-side.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The ladder preview is a real table with row and column headers, not a styled grid of divs. Every generator input is a labelled numeric field with its unit. The submit button names the total order count and quantity. The CMP-158 native-SL note is a persistent `role="note"`. Warnings (range crosses mark) use `role="status"`; blocking errors use `role="alert"` and move focus to the first offending field. Slider controls have keyboard equivalents and expose value text.

## Performance notes
Preview recomputes within one frame (<=16.6 ms) per the screen spec. Submission is a single backend request regardless of level count. The table must not re-render every row on a single-input change (memoised rows).

## Observability
Analytics `algo.scaled_previewed`, `algo.scaled_distribution_changed`. Audited events are server-emitted (`algo.scaled_created` etc.). Failed submissions report the API correlation id.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All scenarios automated; Storybook covers every state.
- [ ] Frontend coverage >=80%.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass on the preview table; keyboard-only path verified.
- [ ] design-qa comparison against the E32-D07 pack done (feeds E32-D08).
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-065 updated if behaviour diverged.
- [ ] QA sign-off from E32-Q03.

- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

title: Update schemas, OpenAPI, WS contract and write ADR-0016 for E32
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 requires that plan docs reflect **shipped** behaviour, not the original proposal, and section 5.2 requires an ADR for every design decision taken during implementation. E32 makes four decisions that are not yet written down anywhere: the single-choke-point enforcement model with its closed deferral allow-list, the frozen-R-denominator rule for break-even, the ladder rounding/redistribution policy as actually implemented, and the attach-vs-trading-stop default chosen from E32-K01's measurements. R3's quality gate also requires the OMS contract to be **frozen** once shipped (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4, Contract row).

## Scope / Deliverables

Cross-linked from ADR-0006 and ADR-0008.

title: Design QA of the shipped algo builders and monitor panel
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA default-on for net-new UI stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec (spacing, tokens, type, colour, states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer, and discrepancies are fixed or filed as bugs with a priority. E33-S05 and E33-S06 ship five net-new screens, several of which carry safety-transparency affordances whose absence would be a defect rather than a polish item.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screen-by-screen comparison of the built SCR-066, SCR-067, SCR-068, SCR-069 (OCO half) and SCR-070 against the E33-D06 package version they were built from.
- Full **state sweep**: every state in the matrices — configured, running, paused, degraded, halted by risk control, completed, cancelled, failed-with-reason, orphaned, empty — in light and dark, both densities, at 4 K and 1 080 p.
- **Copy audit**: every label, helper, validation message and banner compared to the exact strings in the handoff, including the binding emulation and disconnect wording.
- **Safety-affordance audit** (treated as blocking, not cosmetic): the emulation caveat present as text in every state; CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice present and stating the non-removable native stop; CMP-227 EstimatedBadge present on every emulated surface; the degraded banner present and correctly worded; `viewer` variants showing no mutating controls.
- Motion check against the D04 spec including the `prefers-reduced-motion` variants.
- Findings list with severity; blocking items fixed before the stories close, non-blocking items filed as Bugs with `priority/*` and linked here.

## Out of scope
Functional testing (E33-Q01/Q02/Q06). A11y auditing (E33-Q05 — though a11y regressions noticed here are filed). Backend behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full state sweep performed
  Given the five shipped screens
  Then every state in the handoff matrices has been compared in both themes and densities,
  and the result is recorded per state

Scenario: Safety affordances present
  Given every emulated surface in every state
  Then the emulation caveat, the safety-invariant notice and the estimated badge are present
  and correctly worded; any absence is raised as a blocking defect, not a polish item

Scenario: Copy matches exactly (edge)
  Given the handoff's exact strings
  Then every shipped string matches, and any deviation is either corrected or recorded as a
  deliberate change with CDO approval and fed to E33-T03 for doc reconciliation

Scenario: Reduced motion honoured (edge)
  Given prefers-reduced-motion
  Then the reduced variants specified in D04 are what the build renders
```

## Technical notes / design
Review against the running demo environment, not Storybook alone — Storybook cannot show the degraded or halted states driven by real backend conditions; use the QA chaos fixtures (E33-Q04) to reach them.

## Test plan
N/A (this is the QA activity). Evidence is screenshots per state attached to the ticket.

## Security notes
The safety-affordance audit is a security control check: hiding or weakening the emulation/native-SL notices defeats a transparency control agreed in E33-X01's threat model, so such findings are blocking and are copied to the Security engineer.

## Accessibility notes
Any a11y deviation observed (missing focus ring, colour-only status, tooltip-only caveat) is filed immediately and cross-linked to E33-Q05 rather than deferred.

## Performance notes
Confirm no per-row animation crept into SCR-070 and that countdowns share a single ticker — visually verifiable by profiling the 100-row case.

## Observability
Confirm the analytics/audit affordances annotated in D06 actually fire from the built controls (spot-check via the audit log).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five screens swept across every state, theme and density; evidence attached.
- [ ] Blocking findings fixed and re-verified; non-blocking findings filed as Bugs with priorities and linked.
- [ ] Safety-affordance audit passed and countersigned by the Security engineer.
- [ ] **Sign-off:** CDO records design-QA acceptance on E33-S05 and E33-S06.

## Dependencies
E33-S05 and E33-S06 must be feature-complete; E33-Q04's chaos fixtures are used to reach degraded/halted states.

N/A (review activity); fixes land on `fix/e33-design-qa-*` branches.

title: E2E suite additions for algo builders, monitor panel and full algo lifecycles
body:
## Context
The R3 quality gate requires Playwright E2E coverage on **web and Electron** for the train's trading surfaces (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4). For E33 the valuable E2E is not "the modal opens" but the **lifecycle**: configure → submit → observe progress in the monitor → intervene → verify the exchange agrees. That spans the builders (S05), the monitor (S06), the supervisor (T01) and the strategies (S01–S04), which is exactly why it belongs in one suite rather than per story.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `e2e/algos/`, run against the **demo** environment in both the web and Electron targets:
  1. **TWAP lifecycle** — configure 10 slices over a short window from SCR-066, assert the schedule preview, submit, observe ≥ 2 slices fill in SCR-070 with correct progress text, pause, resume, cancel, assert no working children remain at the exchange.
  2. **Iceberg lifecycle** — configure from SCR-067, assert only one slice rests at a time (exchange assertion, not UI), let it refill once, cancel, assert the filled portion remains as a position with its protective stop.
  3. **Chase lifecycle** — configure from SCR-068 against a moving instrument, assert repricings are reflected in the monitor and that the reprice count respects the interval, hit max-chase or timeout, assert the configured end policy executed.
  4. **OCO lifecycle** — create from SCR-069 on an existing position, force the target leg to fill, assert the opposing leg is cancelled/reduced and the run completes.
  5. **Monitor bulk actions** — four runs of different kinds, cancel-all, assert the confirmation restates the count, per-item results render, and the exchange has no residual working algo children.
  6. **Orphan adoption** — create an order carrying an algo `order_link_id` whose run row is removed, assert it appears as orphaned and that adopt associates it correctly.
  7. **Degraded state** — sever the WS connection, assert the degraded banner and staleness marking appear and that unhonourable controls disable.
  8. **Guard rails** — attempt a sub-minimum-slice TWAP and an over-budget chase, asserting **no network request** was made (route interception), and attempt submission while disarmed and while kill-switched.
- Deterministic fixtures: a demo sub-account per spec, a seeded RNG override so slice jitter is reproducible, and time control for window-based specs.
- Flake controls: exchange-truth polling with explicit timeouts, no arbitrary sleeps, and a quarantine policy for any spec that flakes twice.
- Wire the suite into CI as part of the R3 E2E job with per-spec timing reported.

## Out of scope
Unit/integration tests (owned by the stories). Chaos scenarios (Q04). Load (Q03). A11y assertions beyond smoke-level axe checks (Q05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every lifecycle passes on web and Electron
  Given the demo environment and the eight specs
  Then all pass in both targets in CI, with exchange-state assertions rather than UI-only ones

Scenario: Guard rails assert absence of traffic
  Given a sub-minimum-slice configuration and an over-budget chase configuration
  Then the specs assert via route interception that no order request left the client

Scenario: Deterministic despite jitter (edge)
  Given randomised slice sizes and times
  Then the seeded RNG override makes each run reproducible, and no spec depends on
  wall-clock timing beyond its declared time control

Scenario: Flake discipline (edge)
  Given a spec that fails intermittently twice
  Then it is quarantined with a Bug filed rather than retried into green,
  and the quarantine is visible in the CI report
```

## Technical notes / design
Specs assert against three sources in priority order: exchange (`GET /api/v1/orders` proxying exchange truth, or the diagnostics endpoint), audit log, then UI. The seeded-RNG override is a test-only backend config (`oms.algo.rng_seed`) that must be rejected in the live environment — coordinate with E33-X02.

Electron target reuses the existing Playwright Electron harness from E30/E31.

## Test plan
Self-testing: each spec is run 10× consecutively in a soak job during authoring to establish flake rate < 1 % before it enters the gating suite.

## Security notes
Specs run against demo credentials injected from CI secrets; no key material in the repo. The RNG-seed override and any other test hook must be proven inert outside demo — an explicit spec asserts the backend refuses the override when the environment is live.

## Accessibility notes
Each spec performs a smoke-level axe-core scan of the screen it visits so a gross a11y regression fails the E2E job; the full audit remains Q05.

## Performance notes
The suite must complete within the R3 E2E job budget; window-based specs use short durations (≤ 3 min) with time control rather than real 30-minute windows.

## Observability
Specs assert the presence of the expected audit events via `GET /api/v1/admin/audit`, making instrumentation part of the E2E contract.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All eight specs green on web and Electron in CI.
- [ ] Flake rate < 1 % measured over the 10× soak.
- [ ] Exchange-truth assertions present in every lifecycle spec.
- [ ] Quarantine policy documented in the suite README.
- [ ] QA lead sign-off; results referenced from E33-S05/S06 DoD.

## Dependencies
E33-S05 and E33-S06 (the surfaces under test); E33-T02 (audit/list endpoints used as assertions); E33-Q01 (the plan these specs automate).

## Branch
`test/e33-e2e-algos`.

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-066 TWAP builder, SCR-067 Iceberg (emulated) builder, SCR-068 Chase-limit builder, SCR-069 Emulated OCO / bracket builder, SCR-070 Algo monitor panel, SCR-063 Positions & orders panel (Algos tab)

title: Performance and load scripts for algo request rate and scheduler fidelity
body:
## Context
Chase and iceberg are the highest request-rate paths in the product, and the R3 load gate is explicit: *"k6: sustained order flow at the per-UID limit across 5 accounts for 1 h with zero lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off"* (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4). Separately, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2 fixes budget #4 (submit → ack p95 < 300 ms) and the epic adds two of its own: OCO race resolution ≤ 300 ms p95 and scheduler drift < 250 ms per slice.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6/Locust scripts under `perf/algos/`:
  1. **Chase reprice storm** — a synthetic flapping book driving N chase runs; asserts the ≥ 200 ms reprice-interval floor holds, that amends never exhaust the protective reserve, and that `10018` back-off is exponential with jitter.
  2. **Iceberg refill rate** — a 450-slice run measuring sustained request rate against the account budget and the projected-rate estimate shown pre-submit (the estimate must not understate reality by more than 10 %).
  3. **Scheduler fidelity** — 50 concurrent TWAPs totalling 5 000 planned slices; measures per-slice drift p50/p95/max and asserts < 250 ms p95.
  4. **Resume storm** — 100 non-terminal runs, hard restart; measures process-start → first-correct-action p95 against the 5 s requirement and 2 s target.
  5. **OCO race latency** — 1 000 simulated fills; measures WS-fill → cancel/amend-request issued, asserting ≤ 300 ms p95.
  6. **Monitor panel frame cost** — 100 running algos rendered in SCR-070; asserts < 3 ms scripting per frame and that updates arrive coalesced at ≤ 2 Hz.
- A results dashboard fragment and a recorded baseline committed so regressions are detectable in later trains (E46 performance hardening consumes it).
- Budget assertions wired as CI-visible pass/fail, not just reported numbers.

## Out of scope
Functional correctness (Q01/Q02). Chaos/failure injection (Q04). Ingestion or chart-engine budgets (E46/E11).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All six scripts run and assert budgets
  Given the perf suite
  Then each script asserts its named budget and fails the job when breached,
  rather than only reporting a number

Scenario: One-hour sustained flow
  Given chase and iceberg runs across five demo accounts at the per-UID limit
  When the load runs for one hour
  Then there are zero lost acknowledgements, back-off is exponential with jitter on 10018,
  and the protective reserve is never consumed

Scenario: Estimate honesty (edge)
  Given the projected requests/min shown by the iceberg and chase builders
  Then the measured rate is within 10 percent of the estimate, or the estimate is corrected

Scenario: Baseline recorded (edge)
  Given the first green run
  Then p50/p95/max for every budget is committed as a baseline that later runs compare against
```

## Technical notes / design
Per-UID rate limits mean 5 accounts are 5 budgets (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E34) — the scripts must not aggregate them into one and must exercise the token bucket's protective reserve explicitly by interleaving a stop-loss placement during saturation.

Run against demo with dedicated sub-accounts; the synthetic flapping book is a recorded/generated fixture fed to the BookEngine, not a real market dependency, so results are repeatable.

## Test plan
Each script is validated by a negative control — deliberately breaking a budget (e.g. lowering the reprice floor) must make the assertion fail — so a green result means something.

## Security notes
Load testing is indistinguishable from abuse at the network layer: scripts run only against demo, are rate-capped to the account's own budget, and are coordinated with E33-X02 so the rate-DoS abuse case reuses these harnesses rather than inventing its own.

## Accessibility notes
The SCR-070 frame-cost script records whether live-region announcements are aggregated rather than per-row, feeding E33-Q05.

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: submit → ack p95 < 300 ms (#4); OCO resolution ≤ 300 ms p95; scheduler drift < 250 ms p95; resume p95 < 2 s (5 s hard); SCR-070 < 3 ms scripting/frame at 100 rows; iceberg/chase rate estimates within 10 %.

## Observability
Scripts scrape `oms_algo_*`, `oms_chase_*`, `oms_oco_race_resolution_ms` and `oms_algo_scheduler_drift_ms`, which validates that those metrics exist and are correctly labelled.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Six scripts merged, each asserting its budget, each with a negative control demonstrated.
- [ ] One-hour sustained run executed and its report attached.
- [ ] Baselines committed; dashboard fragment added.
- [ ] Results referenced from S03/S04 DoD and from the epic's exit criteria.
- [ ] QA lead + Architect sign-off.

## Dependencies
E33-S03 and E33-S04 (the strategies under load); E33-T01 (metrics and buckets); E29/E34 for the governor behaviour being asserted.

## Branch
`test/e33-perf-algos`.

title: Chaos scenarios: crash seams, disconnects and risk-control halts for algos
body:
## Context
The R3 chaos gate names one E33 scenario explicitly — *"backend restart mid-TWAP"* — and requires that all such scenarios "resume to a correct, reconciled state" (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4). The user stories go further, each naming a specific seam: OCO's "crash between fill and cancel", iceberg's "crash with a slice resting", TWAP's "backend restart mid-TWAP", chase's "chase orphan after crash". These are the scenarios where an emulated algo can produce a **real, unintended position**, so they are P0 and they are automated, not exploratory.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A chaos suite `tests/chaos/algos/` executed in CI against a containerised backend + demo adapter:
  1. **Crash seam matrix** — for each of the four strategies × four seams (before persist, after persist/before submit, after submit/before ack persist, after ack persist): SIGKILL, restart, assert no duplicated child, filled quantity recomputed from executions, correct terminal state, and first correct action within 5 s.
  2. **OCO fill/cancel seam** — kill precisely after the fill event is persisted and before the cancel is sent; assert the cancel is re-sent with the original idempotency key and the run completes within 5 s of restart.
  3. **Iceberg resting-slice adoption** — kill with a slice resting; assert adoption by `order_link_id`, not duplication.
  4. **Chase orphan adoption** — kill with a chase order resting; assert the price is read back from the exchange and chasing resumes only after confirmation; assert the one-live-order DB constraint holds throughout.
  5. **WS disconnect** — sever the private execution stream for 30 s mid-run; assert `on_disconnect="freeze"` semantics (no new children, existing children left working, native SL intact), the degraded state surfaces, and reconciliation catches up on reconnect.
  6. **Exchange 5xx and 10018 storms** — assert back-off, no runaway retries, no state corruption.
  7. **Kill-switch and daily-loss lockout mid-run** — for all four strategies; assert immediate halt, children handled per policy, terminal state "halted by risk control", audit + alert emitted, and **no automatic resumption**.
  8. **Postgres failover mid-run** — assert the run resumes with no duplicated child and no lost slice history.
  9. **Clock jump / event-loop suspension** — suspend for ≥ 2 TWAP intervals; assert no back-to-back firing and correct re-planning.
- Reusable fixtures exported for E33-D07 (to reach degraded/halted states visually) and for E33-Q06.
- A chaos report template capturing, per scenario, the observed recovery time and the exchange-vs-local reconciliation result.

## Out of scope
Load (Q03). Functional happy paths (Q01/Q02). Fan-out and multi-account chaos (E34/E45).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crash matrix is exhaustive and green
  Given four strategies and four seams
  Then all sixteen combinations run in CI and each asserts zero duplicated children,
  execution-derived fill quantities and a correct terminal state

Scenario: Recovery is bounded
  Given any crash scenario
  Then the time from process start to the first correct action is recorded and is under
  five seconds, with the p95 across the matrix reported

Scenario: Risk-control halt is unconditional (failure)
  Given the kill-switch fires during each of the four strategies
  Then every run halts, ends in "halted by risk control" with a reason, emits audit and alert,
  and never resumes without an explicit re-arm

Scenario: Disconnect leaves protection intact (edge)
  Given the private stream is severed mid-run
  Then no new children are issued, existing children remain working, the native stop remains
  in place at the exchange, and reconciliation on reconnect produces no duplicate or orphan

Scenario: Database failover (edge)
  Given Postgres fails over mid-run
  Then the run resumes with complete slice history and no duplicated child
```

## Technical notes / design
Seams are identified by the instrumentation points E33-T01 exposes for exactly this purpose (a test-only fault-injection hook that must be inert outside test builds — verified by E33-X02).

Exchange truth after each scenario is read from `GET /v5/order/realtime` and `/v5/position/list` through the adapter, and compared against `orders`, `algo_runs` and `algo_slices`; any discrepancy fails the scenario.

## Test plan
The suite is itself validated by negative controls: disabling adoption must make the adoption scenarios fail; disabling the idempotency key must make the OCO seam scenario fail. Both are demonstrated once during authoring.

## Security notes
Fault-injection hooks are a security surface — the suite includes an assertion that the hook is absent/refused in a production-mode build, and E33-X02 independently attempts to invoke it. Chaos runs use demo credentials only.

## Accessibility notes
Scenario 5 and 7 fixtures are reused by E33-Q05 and E33-D07 to verify the degraded and halted states are announced and rendered correctly — which is the only practical way to test those states.

## Performance notes
Recovery time is a budget, not a curiosity: 5 s hard, 2 s target at 100 concurrent runs (cross-checked with Q03's resume-storm script).

## Observability
Each scenario asserts the expected audit events and that `oms_algo_resume_seconds` is emitted with a plausible value — chaos doubles as observability verification.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All nine scenario groups automated and green in CI; the crash matrix runs on every merge to `main`.
- [ ] Negative controls demonstrated for adoption and idempotency.
- [ ] Recovery times recorded and within budget.
- [ ] Fixtures exported and consumed by E33-Q05/Q06/D07.
- [ ] Chaos report attached to the epic; feeds the R3 PRR.
- [ ] QA lead + Architect + Security engineer sign-off (the halt scenarios are a safety gate).

## Dependencies
E33-S01/S03/S04 (strategies under test; S02 is exercised via the matrix), E33-T01 (fault-injection hooks, adoption, persistence), E39 (kill-switch and lockouts).

## Branch
`test/e33-chaos-algos`.

title: Accessibility audit of the algo builders and monitor panel
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` mandates WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI plus **manual screen-reader passes**; the R3 a11y gate additionally calls out that danger/confirm patterns must be announced. E33 ships five net-new screens whose a11y requirements were specified in E33-D05 and handed off in E33-D06; this audit executes that checklist against the built software and is the epic's a11y evidence.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated**: axe-core scans of SCR-066, SCR-067, SCR-068, SCR-069 and SCR-070 in every state (configured, running, paused, degraded, halted, completed, failed, orphaned, empty), light and dark, both densities — wired as a CI job, not a one-off run.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with NVDA + Chrome and VoiceOver + Safari/Electron:
  - Every builder completed and submitted using the screen reader alone.
  - The TWAP **schedule preview** read as a table with headers.
  - The **emulation caveat** and the **OCO residual-risk note** encountered in reading order, not buried after the form.
  - Running-state refresh announcements throttled to at most one per 5 s (iceberg) and not flooding at 2 Hz (monitor).
  - The **degraded banner** announced as a status, and "halted by risk control" announced with its reason.
  - Monitor controls announcing their target and effect ("Cancel TWAP a_12 on BTCUSDT, Main").
  - Bulk cancel-all confirmation announced as an alert dialog restating the count.
- **Keyboard-only passes**: full operation of all five screens including bulk actions and orphan adopt/cancel; focus trap and restoration per modal; visible focus throughout; no keyboard trap in the 100-row virtualised table.
- **Contrast and non-colour encoding** verification for every status treatment in both themes and the three colour-vision simulations; target size ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px in both densities.
- Findings triaged by severity with WCAG success-criterion references; blockers fixed before the stories close, others filed as Bugs with priorities.
- Reuse of E33-Q04's fixtures to reach the degraded and halted states.

## Out of scope
Design intent review (E33-D07). Functional testing (Q01/Q02). Other epics' screens.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: axe-core green across all states
  Given the five screens in every enumerated state, theme and density
  Then axe-core reports no violations, and the scan runs in CI rather than manually

Scenario: Screen-reader completion
  Given a screen-reader user with no sighted assistance
  Then each builder can be completed and submitted, and the monitor's controls, statuses and
  bulk confirmations are understandable from speech alone

Scenario: Announcements are throttled (edge)
  Given a running iceberg and a monitor with 100 rows updating at 2 Hz
  Then announcements are aggregated and polite, at most one per five seconds for slice refresh,
  and the screen reader is not flooded
```

title: Exploratory charter, regression pack and QA sign-off for emulated algos
body:
## Context
Scripted tests only find the failures someone imagined. Emulated algos fail in combinations — a chase whose account is simultaneously being used by a TWAP while a lockout fires — and the epic's DoD requires an epic-level regression/exploratory pass beyond per-child QA (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2). This ticket provides the charters, builds the durable regression pack, and produces the epic's QA sign-off.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (time-boxed 90 min each, session notes recorded):
  1. *Concurrency* — multiple algos of different kinds on one account and one symbol; look for interference, double-counting of filled quantity, and rate-budget starvation.
  2. *Interference with manual trading* — manually amend, cancel or flatten while an algo owns children; look for orphans, for the algo fighting the user, and for a position closed twice.
  3. *Boundary parameters* — minimums, maximums and one-beyond for every parameter of all four strategies (slices 2 and 500, display qty at min lot and at 50 %, chase offset 0 and max, durations at 10 s and 24 h).
  4. *Environment and flags* — algo kinds disabled mid-run, environment switch attempted while an algo runs (must be blocked per SCR-073's checklist), RBAC changes mid-run.
  5. *Recovery under stress* — repeated restarts during heavy slicing; combine with Q04 fixtures beyond the scripted matrix.
  6. *Trustworthiness of the monitor* — try to create a state the monitor shows wrongly (stale rows, missing orphan, wrong progress after adoption).
- **Regression pack**: the durable subset of Q01's plan plus any exploratory finding worth re-running each train, packaged as a named suite with an execution time budget (≤ 2 h manual + the automated suites) and added to the R3 soak checklist.
- **Bug triage**: every finding filed with repro steps, severity and the missing-test-layer note required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.1.
- **Epic QA sign-off report**: per-story pass/fail against Q01's scenarios, the invariant matrix result, chaos and perf results referenced, open-defect list with severities, and an explicit statement of any QA-capacity deviations.

## Out of scope
Writing new automation (belongs to Q02/Q03/Q04 or to follow-up Tasks filed from findings). Design QA (D07). A11y audit (Q05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All charters executed with notes
  Given the six charters
  Then each is executed within its time box and produces session notes listing what was tried,
  what was observed and what was filed

Scenario: Regression pack exists and is runnable
  Given the packaged regression suite
  When a QA engineer new to the epic executes it
  Then it completes within its stated budget and produces an unambiguous pass/fail per item

Scenario: Sign-off is evidence-based
  Given the sign-off report
  Then every user-story scenario has a recorded result, the five cross-strategy invariants are
  each evidenced, and no story is signed off on the basis of "no issues seen"

Scenario: Concurrency interference (edge)
  Given a TWAP and a chase on the same account and symbol while a lockout fires
  Then the observed behaviour is documented, and any interference, double-counting or
  starvation is filed as a defect with the layer that should have caught it
```

## Technical notes / design
Charters run on demo with dedicated sub-accounts; session notes follow the existing exploratory-testing template. Findings that reveal a *specification* gap are routed to E33-T03 for doc reconciliation, not only to a Bug.

## Test plan
N/A — this is the testing activity. Its own quality control is a peer review of the sign-off report by the second QA/SDET.

## Security notes
Charter 4 overlaps with E33-X02's abuse cases (RBAC changes mid-run, flags disabled mid-run); results are shared so the Security engineer's review has QA evidence to lean on rather than duplicating effort.

## Accessibility notes
Any a11y issue noticed during exploration is filed and cross-linked to Q05 rather than absorbed silently.

## Performance notes
Charter 5 records recovery times informally; anything worse than Q03's baseline is escalated as a perf defect.

## Observability
Charter 6 explicitly attacks the monitor's trustworthiness, which is the practical test of whether the WS projection and 30 s reconciliation actually hold.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Six charters executed; session notes attached.
- [ ] Regression pack packaged, time-budgeted and added to the R3 soak checklist.
- [ ] All findings filed with severity, repro and missing-test-layer notes; P0/P1 closed before sign-off.
- [ ] Epic QA sign-off report published with per-scenario results and the invariant matrix.
- [ ] Peer-reviewed by the second QA/SDET; QA lead signs off the epic.

title: Emulate iceberg: slice a large order into randomised visible tranches
body:
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** this ticket's lifecycle is now built directly on `xstate-statemachine` 0.9.1 via `statechart.factory` from the first line of code (catalogue B5). No in-house shim, no dual-runtime harness, no hand-rolled state enum/transition table. The tranche lifecycle is in the chart; the release timing is the scheduler.

## Context
**US-ALGO-005 — Emulated iceberg (Should):** *"As a trader, I want a large order sliced into visible tranches, so that I do not show my full size."* Bybit's `orderType` is Market/Limit only — there is no `displayQty` and no native iceberg (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §10.3), so this is entirely app-managed and must be labelled "(app-managed)" everywhere it appears.

Randomisation is not a nicety: a perfectly regular refill is trivially detectable by the very iceberg detector CandleViewer itself ships (E25 / §7 `iceberg_present_at_level`), so jitter is on by default.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/oms/algo/strategies/iceberg.py` against `IcebergParams` (`display_qty`, `total_qty`, `price_mode: fixed|peg_best|peg_offset`, `price`, `peg_offset_ticks`, `reprice_threshold_ticks`, `randomize_pct` default 0.2, `min_slice_qty` defaulting to the instrument's `min_order_qty`, `refill_delay_ms` 250, `refill_jitter_ms` 250, `post_only` True, `max_slices` 450) exactly as §10.3.
- Slicing loop: submit one visible child of `display_qty` jittered by ±`randomize_pct`, floored to `qty_step`, never below `min_slice_qty`; on **full** fill wait `refill_delay_ms + U(0, refill_jitter_ms)` and submit the next; on **partial** fill leave the child working and only refill after it terminates.
- Dust rule: the final slice is exactly the remainder; if that remainder is below `min_order_qty` it is **merged into the previous slice** so the algo never strands an unsendable quantity. If even the merged size is unfillable, the run completes with status detail `remainder unfillable`.
- Repricing: in `peg_best`/`peg_offset` the price is re-evaluated **per slice**, not continuously (continuous repricing is `chase`, E33-S04), and only when drift ≥ `reprice_threshold_ticks`; every reprice is logged.
- Rejection handling: a slice rejected for minimum-notional, lot-size or insufficient-margin **pauses** the run rather than retrying in a loop; the exact exchange reason and the filled-so-far quantity are surfaced, and the user chooses resume-with-smaller-slice, convert-remainder-to-a-single-order, or abandon (these three resolutions exposed as `POST /algos/{algoId}/control` extensions agreed in E33-T02).
- Post-only edge: a `post_only` slice rejected for crossing is retried **once** at the new best; two consecutive post-only rejections pause the run for 1 s.
- Crash edge: the resting slice is **adopted** by `order_link_id` rather than duplicated; filled-so-far is recomputed from `executions`; slicing resumes within 5 s.
- Kill-switch edge: slicing stops immediately, the resting slice is cancelled, the run ends `halted by risk control` with the reason recorded.
- Projected request-rate calculation exported for SCR-067's pre-submit estimate.
- Implement the `B5` lifecycle as `statechart/machines/B05.iceberg.machine.json` (committed by E50-S01/S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('iceberg', lane=...)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/05_iceberg.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_05_iceberg.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.

## Out of scope
The SCR-067 builder UI (E33-S05). Monitor row (E33-S06). Continuous repricing (S04). Scaled ladders (E32).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Slicing
  Given a total of 5 BTC with a visible slice of 0.25
  Then only one slice rests at a time and a replacement is placed after each fill until the
  total is complete, with slice sizes jittered by the configured randomisation

Scenario: Price moves away
  Given the reprice policy is peg-to-best
  Then remaining slices reprice per the policy once drift exceeds the threshold, each reprice
  is logged, and repricing happens per slice rather than continuously

Scenario: Cancelled mid-way
  When I cancel the run
  Then the working slice is cancelled, no further slices are placed, and the filled portion is
  reported as a normal position with its protective stop intact

Scenario: Slice rejected by the exchange (error)
  Given a replacement slice is rejected for minimum-notional, lot-size or insufficient margin
  Then slicing pauses instead of retrying in a loop, the exact exchange reason and the filled
  quantity are surfaced, and resume-with-smaller-slice, convert-remainder or abandon are offered

Scenario: Final remainder below the minimum lot (edge)
  Given the untraded remainder is smaller than the instrument's minimum order quantity
  Then the last slice absorbs the remainder rather than leaving a dust order, and if even the
  combined size is below the minimum the run completes with "remainder unfillable"

Scenario: Crash with a slice resting (edge)
  Given the backend restarts while one slice rests
  Then that slice is adopted by client order id rather than duplicated, the filled total is
  recomputed from executions, and slicing resumes within 5 seconds

Scenario: Kill-switch during slicing (edge)
  Given the owner triggers a freeze or the daily-loss lockout fires
  Then slicing stops immediately, the resting slice is cancelled, and the run ends in
  "halted by risk control" with the reason recorded

Scenario: Post-only rejection (edge)
  Given a post-only slice is rejected for crossing
  Then it is retried once at the new best, and two consecutive such rejections pause the run
  for one second rather than hot-looping
```

## Technical notes / design
Every slice carries a client order id encoding the run (`order_link_id` group segment + `seq2` + `ac`), so orphan adoption is deterministic — US-ALGO-005 NFR.

Jitter uses the supervisor's seeded RNG so tests are reproducible; the seed is persisted with the run so a resume continues the same sequence.

Rate cost: one submission per slice plus one cancel per reprice; the projected requests/min figure is `slices_remaining / expected_fill_interval` and is what SCR-067 refuses configurations on.
Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B5.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2 (79-r14 §7 FINAL block). Hot-path parts listed in 29 §3 stay plain code.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: jittered slice sizing with `qty_step` flooring and `min_slice_qty` floor; dust merge including the unfillable case; partial-fill hold-off; reprice threshold; rejection classification (minimum-notional vs lot-size vs margin vs post-only crossing); pause-and-resolve transitions; seeded-RNG reproducibility.
- **Integration**: recorded fixtures for lot-size rejection, insufficient margin, post-only rejection, and a partial-fill-then-terminate sequence.
- **Chaos**: restart with a slice resting → adoption, not duplication; kill-switch mid-run.
- **Perf**: 450-slice run staying inside the account rate budget with the protective reserve untouched.
- Coverage ≥ 90 % on the strategy module.
- Pure-API unit tests of the binding module with a `SimulatedClock`.
- Contract-suite membership, covering both spellings and every §B5.7 invariant.
- A snapshot round-trip (persist->restore) at every quiescence point the ticket introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch.

## Security notes
Order-placing path → `security`-labelled. Threats: rate-budget exhaustion starving protective orders (mitigated by the reserve and the projected-rate refusal); tampering with `display_qty` to produce thousands of children (bounded by `max_slices` 450 and `min_slice_qty`); information disclosure — `params` reveal hidden size and are restricted to users with account access. Abuse case: an iceberg configured with a minimum slice as a request-flood vector (E33-X02).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend.

## Performance notes
Per-slice submission inside budget #4. A run must never exceed its account's order token-bucket allowance nor touch the protective reserve (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8).

## Observability
Audit `algo.iceberg_created {symbol, side, totalQty, visibleQty, refreshPolicy, accountIds}`, `algo.iceberg_paused|resumed|cancelled|completed|failed`, `algo.iceberg_slice_replaced` (sampled — it is rate-relevant). Metrics `oms_algo_child_orders_total{kind="iceberg"}`, `oms_iceberg_slice_rejections_total{reason}`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Coverage ≥ 90 % strategy module, ≥ 85 % package.
- [ ] Chaos adoption test green.
- [ ] `24-internal-schemas.md` §10.3 updated on divergence.

## Dependencies
