title: Simulate fills locally with the paper matcher's queue, latency and fee models
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** The paper matcher's queue/fill/fee arithmetic stays excluded, per-tick plain code (29-statechart-adoption-plan §3); only the paper account's liquidation lifecycle moves onto `B15` (`paper_account`) on `xstate-statemachine`. Net estimate unchanged.

US-PAPER-004 (Should) asks for an offline simulator so the owner can practise and develop with no exchange dependency, and so rule simulation and replay have somewhere to execute. Its NFR is the design constraint: 'simulator uses the same OMS state machine as real trading so behaviour is comparable'.

`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12 specifies the matcher in full and is normative for this story: the `FillModelConfig`, the book-walk for market orders, the queue-position model for resting limits (including the pro-rata cancel assumption described there as 'the single most important honesty knob in the whole simulator'), latency, fees from `GET /v5/account/fee-rate`, funding as an `Execution` with `exec_type="funding"`, and margin/liquidation from real tiered risk-limit data. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.7 names the components: `FillModel`, `QueueEstimator`, `FeeModel`, `PaperLedger`.

The point of all this detail is honesty: a simulator that ignores queue position, latency and funding lies, and a lying simulator is worse than none because it manufactures confidence (risk R12).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement module **M16 Paper Matcher** in `packages/backend/cv/paper/`: `FillModel`, `QueueEstimator`, `FeeModel`, `PaperLedger`, exposing the **same interface as the exchange adapter** (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 14) so the OMS routes to it without knowing it is a simulation.
- `FillModelConfig` exactly as specified in section 12.1 (all fields, same defaults: `mode=book_walk`, `use_queue_position=True`, `prob_fill_on_touch=0.35`, `latency_submit_ms=60`, `latency_cancel_ms=60`, `latency_market_data_ms=30`, `max_book_levels=200`, `reject_if_book_exhausted=True`, `apply_funding=True`).
- Market orders: walk the opposite side of the live/replayed L2 book from best, one `Execution` per level consumed, volume-weighted average price; `INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY` rejection when the book is exhausted and `reject_if_book_exhausted` is set, else fill at last level plus `slippage_floor_ticks`.
- Limit orders: crossing fills as taker capped at the limit price with the remainder resting; `post_only` that would cross is **rejected**, as the exchange does.
- Resting limits with queue position: snapshot same-side displayed size as `queue_ahead`; decrement by same-side prints at the level; fill only past a cleared queue; clear the estimate when price moves away; re-cap on return; and on a level shrinking without a print, apply the pro-rata assumption `queue_ahead *= new_level_size / old_level_size`.
- Latency: orders become live at `submit_ts + latency_submit_ms`, cancels take effect at `cancel_ts + latency_cancel_ms` (so a cancel can lose the race), decision market data delayed by `latency_market_data_ms`.
- Fees from `GET /v5/account/fee-rate` cached 24 h, `is_maker` true only for a resting limit filled by an incoming aggressor, negative maker rates supported, `fee_estimated=True` marking when defaults (maker 2 bps / taker 5.5 bps) are used.
- Funding at each `next_funding_time` using the real rate and `instrument.funding_interval_min` (never assumed 8 h), recorded as an `Execution` with `exec_type="funding"`, `qty=0`.
- Margin, liquidation and the `adl_risk_proxy` per section 12.4, using fetched `GET /v5/market/risk-limit` tiers, never hardcoded.
- `PaperLedger` persists positions, wallet and realised/unrealised PnL in Postgres with the **identical schema to live accounts** (`is_paper=true` on the rows) so every downstream view is account-type agnostic.
- Hard interlock: the matcher has **no network transport**; a structural test asserts `cv/paper/` imports no HTTP or WS client.
- Implement the paper account's liquidation lifecycle as `B15` (`paper_account`) in `statechart/machines/B15.paper_account.machine.json` (committed by E50-S02, hash-locked). Do not hand-write the state enum or transition table for liquidation.
- Build it only through `statechart.factory.build('paper_account', lane=…)`, and restore it only through `statechart.persistence.restore`.
- Write guards, actions and services in `statechart/bindings/b15_paper_account.py` as a `MachineLogic`. Everything is `async def`, and services are idempotent under re-entry.
- Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_b15_paper_account.py`, which becomes a member of the blocking gate.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.
- The `FillModel`/`QueueEstimator`/`FeeModel`/`PaperLedger` matcher core itself is excluded (§3) and stays plain code — do not attempt to model queue position or fill arithmetic as chart states.


## Out of scope
- The SCR-099 results UI (E38-S05) and the simulated labelling system it renders.
- The nightly divergence job (E38-S05's dependency is only the display; the job itself is E38-T03).
- Bybit demo routing (E38-S01) - demo is a real engine, this is the local one.
- Backtesting over historical bars as a product feature (E26 replay owns the data source; this is the fill engine it drives).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Limit fills when the book and prints would have filled it
  Given simulator mode against live market data
  When a limit order is placed and the level trades through after the estimated queue ahead is consumed
  Then it fills, applying the configured latency and slippage model, with one Execution per consuming print

Scenario: Market order walks the book rather than filling at one price
  Given a market order larger than the best level
  When it is matched
  Then it produces one Execution per level consumed and an average price equal to the volume-weighted result

Scenario: Book exhaustion rejects rather than inventing liquidity
  Given reject_if_book_exhausted is true and the order exceeds total displayed depth
  When it is matched
  Then the remainder is rejected with INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY

Scenario: post_only that would cross is rejected
  Given a post_only limit priced through the opposite best
  When it is submitted
  Then it is rejected exactly as the exchange would reject it

Scenario: A cancel can lose the race
  Given a resting order about to be filled and a cancel submitted within the cancel latency window
  When the fill occurs before cancel_ts plus latency_cancel_ms
  Then the order fills and the cancel is rejected as too late

Scenario: Queue shrinkage is treated conservatively
  Given a level that shrinks without any trade print
  When the queue estimate is updated
  Then queue_ahead is reduced only pro rata to the level size change, never to zero

Scenario: Funding is a real P&L component
  Given an open simulated position held across a funding timestamp
  When funding settles
  Then an Execution with exec_type funding and qty zero is written with the signed payment using the real rate and the instrument's funding interval

Scenario: Model disclosure is machine-readable
  Given a completed simulated session
  When its results are requested
  Then the applied FillModelConfig is returned alongside them so the panel can state queue position, latency, slippage and fee assumptions

Scenario: The simulator can never place an exchange order
  Given simulator mode
  When any order is submitted
  Then no network call is made, and a structural test asserts the paper package imports no HTTP or WS client

Scenario: Simulated state is marked everywhere
  Given simulated orders, executions and positions
  When they are persisted and published
  Then every row and every WS frame carries is_paper true
```

## Technical notes / design
- The matcher consumes the **same event bus** the live path uses (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 13: replay re-emits recorded events onto the same bus with the same types), so it works identically over live and replayed data without a second code path.
- Determinism is a requirement, not a nicety: given the same event sequence and config, the matcher must produce byte-identical executions, because rule simulation (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 11) and R3 exit criterion 6 depend on deterministic replay. Seed any randomness explicitly from the session id.
- All monetary arithmetic uses `Decimal` with the instrument's tick/lot precision; fees quantized to 8 dp `ROUND_HALF_UP` as specified.
- The matcher is per paper account, in-memory plus Postgres (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` C11), and must be restart-safe: ledger state is recoverable from Postgres, resting orders are re-registered with their persisted `queue_ahead`.
- `is_paper` is orthogonal to `environment` - a paper fill still belongs to a real environment (demo, or live when replaying live-recorded data). Do not collapse them (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 13.1 comment).
- Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B15.1-.6. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2. The matcher core (fills, queue, fees) is a hot-path exclusion (29 §3) and stays plain code; only account liquidation state is chart-derived.


## Test plan
- Unit: queue estimator - a dedicated table-driven suite covering trade-through, partial consumption, price-away clearing, re-cap on return, and the pro-rata cancel case; this is the highest-value test set in the story.
- Unit: book walk with exact expected VWAP over a fixture book; exhaustion; `slippage_floor_ticks` behaviour.
- Unit: latency race (cancel wins / cancel loses) at the boundary millisecond.
- Unit: fee computation incl. maker rebate, estimated-fee marking, and cache expiry.
- Unit: funding sign convention for long and short, non-8h intervals.
- Unit: liquidation tier maths against fixture risk-limit data.
- Property test: total simulated fill quantity never exceeds available displayed liquidity within the configured level cap.
- Determinism test: the same recorded window replayed twice yields identical execution streams (supports R3 exit criterion 6).
- Integration: a full replay session through E26 producing simulated positions and a closed ledger, restart-recovered mid-session.
- Perf: 1 hour of recorded BTCUSDT ticks matched faster than real time by at least 20x, to support replay speeds.
- Coverage target: >=90% on `cv/paper/` (engine package, local policy above the 85% floor).
- pure-API unit tests of the b15 binding module with a `SimulatedClock`
- contract-suite membership (`test_b15_paper_account.py`), covering both spellings and every §B15.6 invariant
- a snapshot round-trip (persist→restore) at every quiescence point the liquidation lifecycle introduces, plus a refused restore on a hash or HMAC mismatch


## Security notes
- Threat: the simulator reaching the network and placing a real order. Control: the structural no-transport test plus routing that only reaches the matcher for `is_paper` accounts; this is the story's single most important control and is re-checked in E38-X02.
- Threat (R12): simulated results being mistaken for achievable results. Control: mandatory model disclosure returned with every result set, rendered by E38-S05.
- Fee-rate calls use the account's real credentials through the vault; no new credential path is introduced.
- Data classification: financial simulation data, internal.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend engine. The disclosure payload it emits is what makes E38-S05's accessible disclosure block possible.

## Performance notes
- Matching must sustain replay at up to 100x (budget #15) without becoming the bottleneck; profile the queue estimator, which runs per print per resting order.
- Memory: the matcher holds at most `max_book_levels` (200) per symbol plus resting orders; assert it stays inside the per-symbol backend memory budget #8 (<=300 MB).

## Observability
- Metrics: `cv_paper_fills_total{mode}`, `cv_paper_rejections_total{reason}`, `cv_paper_match_latency_seconds`, `cv_paper_queue_estimate_resets_total`.
- Every simulated execution logs its `queue_ahead` at fill time, which is what makes the divergence job (E38-T03) able to attribute differences.
- Structured log of the `FillModelConfig` used at session start, so any result set can be reproduced.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria demonstrated by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% lines on touched backend/engine packages, >=80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.

- [ ] `machine_hash` committed in `machine_hashes.lock`; `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green; `tests/xstate_contract` green for b15; no import of `xstate_statemachine` outside `statechart/`.


## Dependencies

title: Nightly paper-versus-demo fill divergence job and fidelity panel data
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12.5 states the requirement plainly: 'The paper matcher's honesty is verified, not assumed.' A nightly job replays a recorded day through the matcher while comparing against the demo account's real fills for the same period where they overlap, reporting mean and p95 slippage difference, fill-rate difference for resting limits and fee difference. A p95 slippage divergence above one tick or a fill-rate divergence above 10 pp opens a defect ticket against the fill model, and results are shown on the admin 'Paper fidelity' panel.

Without this job, US-PAPER-004's simulator is an unfalsifiable claim, and R12 (backtest bias) has no control at all.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scheduled job in `packages/backend/cv/paper/divergence.py`: for each symbol with both recorded market data and real demo fills in the window, replay the recorded day through the `PaperMatcher` using the same order stream the demo account actually submitted, and compare outcomes.
- Metrics computed per symbol and overall: mean and p95 slippage difference (in ticks), fill-rate difference for resting limit orders (percentage points), fee difference, and count of orders compared.
- Threshold evaluation: p95 slippage divergence >1 tick or fill-rate divergence >10 pp raises a defect - emit an alert and create a tracked issue record (not silently logged).
- Persist results as a dated document queryable by the admin fidelity panel; expose via `GET /admin/paper-fidelity` (add to `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `x-rbac` permission `audit:read`).
- Handle the honest edge cases: no overlap (report 'insufficient data', never a fabricated zero divergence), too few comparable orders for a meaningful p95 (report the sample size and suppress the threshold check), and symbols where recording gaps make the replay unfaithful (detect via `GET /market/data-coverage` and exclude with a stated reason).
- Update `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 12.5 and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.7 if the implemented metric definitions differ from the written ones, and record any fill-model decision made during implementation as an ADR amendment.

## Out of scope
- The fidelity panel UI beyond the API (its design is E38-D03; the rendering is folded into E38-S08's SCR-137 patterns or filed as a follow-up if capacity is short).
- Automatically tuning the fill model from divergence results - tuning is a human decision informed by the report.
- Comparing against *live* fills (there are none in R3).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Divergence is computed over overlapping activity
  Given a recorded day with both market data and real demo fills
  When the nightly job runs
  Then mean and p95 slippage difference, resting-limit fill-rate difference and fee difference are computed and persisted with the compared-order count

Scenario: Breaching a threshold raises a defect
  Given a p95 slippage divergence above one tick
  When the job evaluates thresholds
  Then an alert is raised and a tracked defect record is created against the fill model, not merely logged

Scenario: Insufficient data is reported, not fabricated
  Given a day with no overlapping demo fills
  When the job runs
  Then the result states insufficient data with the reason, and no divergence figure is reported

Scenario: Small samples suppress the threshold check
  Given fewer comparable orders than the configured minimum
  When the job evaluates thresholds
  Then the sample size is reported and the threshold check is skipped with that stated, rather than firing on noise

Scenario: Recording gaps exclude a symbol honestly
  Given a symbol whose recorded coverage has gaps in the window
  When the job selects symbols
  Then that symbol is excluded with the gap named, because an unfaithful replay would produce a meaningless comparison

Scenario: Results are queryable by date
  Given several nights of results
  When the fidelity endpoint is queried for a date range
  Then each night's metrics are returned with their thresholds and outcomes
```

## Technical notes / design
- The job reuses the replay engine (E26) and the same event bus as production, so the comparison exercises the real matcher rather than a test double - this is the whole point of the architecture's shared-bus design (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 13).
- Slippage difference is computed per order as (simulated average fill price - real average fill price) expressed in ticks, signed so a systematically optimistic simulator is visible as a consistent direction rather than cancelling out in the mean; report both mean (bias) and p95 (tail).
- Fill-rate difference applies only to resting limit orders, where queue modelling is the uncertain part; market orders are compared on slippage only.
- The job is idempotent per (date, symbol) so a re-run overwrites rather than duplicating.
- Runs off-peak and is cancellable; it must never contend with live ingestion for CPU.

## Test plan
- Unit: metric computations against hand-computed fixtures, incl. the sign convention for bias.
- Unit: threshold evaluation at the boundary (exactly 1 tick, exactly 10 pp) and under the minimum sample size.
- Unit: insufficient-data and coverage-gap paths produce explicit reasons.
- Unit: idempotent re-run.
- Integration: a seeded recorded day plus fixture demo fills produces a full report document; a deliberately mis-tuned fill model produces a threshold breach and a defect record.
- Contract: the fidelity endpoint against OpenAPI.
- Coverage: >=85%.

## Security notes
- The job reads recorded market data and the account's own fills; no credential use beyond the existing fee-rate lookups.
- Threat: a silently failing job giving false assurance that the simulator is honest. Control: the job's own liveness is monitored and a missed night alerts - absence of a report is treated as a failure, not as a pass.
- Data classification: trading data, internal.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - backend job. Its output is rendered on SCR-137 following that screen's accessibility rules.

## Performance notes
- Must complete within the off-peak window for a full day of the recorded symbol set; target under 30 minutes for 10 symbols, leaning on the matcher's 20x-faster-than-real-time requirement from E38-S03.
- Must not exceed the per-symbol backend memory budget #8 while replaying.

## Observability
- Metrics `cv_paper_divergence_slippage_ticks{symbol,stat}`, `cv_paper_divergence_fill_rate_pp{symbol}`, `cv_paper_divergence_job_duration_seconds`, `cv_paper_divergence_job_last_success_timestamp`.
- Alert on threshold breach and on a missed run (stale last-success timestamp).
- Structured log of the `FillModelConfig` used, so a breach is attributable to a configuration as well as to code.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria demonstrated by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% lines on touched backend/engine packages, >=80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour where they diverged.

- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (which flag gates this, default per environment).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E38-S03` (the matcher being measured), `E38-S01` (real demo fills to compare against), `E26` (replay engine and recorded data).

## Branch

title: Alerts & notifications
body:
## Context
Alerts are the notification half of the rule engine. The plan deliberately gives alerts **no action block**: `AlertConditionIr` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`) is the condition half of the rule IR with `actions` omitted, so *an alert can never place an order regardless of what the user authors*. That single decision is what lets alerts be authored casually, evaluated cheaply and delivered to many channels without dragging the OMS safety invariants along.

E40 delivers module **M22** (alert evaluator + delivery dispatcher) on top of E35's IR, compiler, metric vocabulary and evaluator, and surfaces it through four screens and the shell notification furniture that E10 mounted empty. Alerts are evaluated **server-side** so they fire with the client closed (US-ALRT-001 NFR), delivered through the transactional `outbox` so a crash between "decide" and "send" can neither lose nor duplicate a notification (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.10.4), and every firing is recorded in the append-only `alert_deliveries` table with the evaluation snapshot attached, because *no channel may be the single source of truth* (US-ALRT-005 NFR).

Roadmap placement: `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 — 21 points, S18–S19, train R3, after E35 lands the IR (`E35 --> E40` in the §11.1 dependency graph).

> **Sizing note (roadmap alignment).** `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 allocates E40 **21 points, S18–S19**. This backlog is sized to that allocation: the design, engineering, QA and security work previously split across 25 child tickets is consolidated into 15, so the epic total and the sum of its children are both 21 and the engineering subtotal (Story + Task + Spike) is 20, inside the ±15% band (17.85–24.15). No scope was dropped — every deliverable, acceptance scenario and sign-off gate from the superseded tickets is carried verbatim in the merged bodies, under a labelled *Part A/B/C* heading naming its origin.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Stories (US)**: US-ALRT-001 price alerts, US-ALRT-002 indicator/metric alerts, US-ALRT-003 order-flow & detector alerts, US-ALRT-004 alert centre, US-ALRT-005 delivery channels, US-ALRT-006 snooze/mute/quiet hours, US-ALRT-008 webhook delivery (Could — descoped to R5 per §12 descoping ladder row 6).
- **Backend (M22)**: `apps/api/cv/alerts/` — alert repository, condition compiler (notify-only IR subset), evaluator subscribing to the E35 metric bus, cooldown/trigger-mode/snooze/expiry gating, storm suppression, delivery dispatcher over `outbox`.
- **DB**: migration `0009_alerts` — `alerts`, `alert_deliveries` (append-only), plus the `alert.deliver` and `webhook.post` outbox topics.
- **REST**: `GET/POST /api/v1/alerts`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}`, `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}/enabled`, `GET /api/v1/alerts/deliveries`, `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/{deliveryId}/ack`, `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/ack-all`, `GET /api/v1/notifications`.
- **WS**: topic `alerts` (`AlertUpdate`, options `unacked_only`, cadence 250 ms, permission `alerts:read`, own alerts only).
- **Screens**: SCR-090 Alerts centre, SCR-091 Alert editor, SCR-092 Alert triggered toast/detail, SCR-014 Notification centre *content*, SCR-115 Notifications settings, SCR-015 toast variants for fired alerts.
- **Components**: CMP-163 AlertRow, CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm, CMP-165 AlertFiredToastGroup (new/extended), composed with CMP-045, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-060, CMP-209, CMP-212.
- **Design**: E40-D01..D06. **QA**: E40-Q01..Q05. **Security**: E40-X01..X03.

## Out of scope
- **US-ALRT-007 alert-to-action automation (Could)** — deliberately not built here. Binding an action to a signal is a *rule*, authored in E35/E36/E37 with the full arming, step-up and risk path; E40 keeps the "alerts cannot act" invariant absolute.
- Rule IR, compiler, metric vocabulary service and evaluator — E35.
- The shell chrome that hosts notifications (CMP-209 RightRail, CMP-212 ToastHost mount) — E10 built them; E40 fills them with content.
- Email transport infrastructure (SMTP relay provisioning) — E04 infra; E40 consumes the configured relay.
- Push notifications to mobile — Android is out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14.
- Prometheus/Alertmanager operational alerting (E04-T05) — a different kind of "alert"; E40 is user-facing only.

## Acceptance criteria

*(epic level)*
```gherkin
Scenario: Alerts fire with no client connected
  Given a price alert on BTCUSDT and every browser and Electron window closed
  When the condition is met
  Then the firing is recorded in alert_deliveries within 1 s of the condition being met
  And on next connect the alert centre and the notification centre both show it unacked
Scenario: An alert can never place an order
  When a corpus of hand-crafted payloads attempts to smuggle an action node into condition_ir via POST /api/v1/alerts
  Then every payload is rejected 422 with RuleIrInvalid and no OMS call is made
Scenario: Storm suppression keeps the UI usable
  Given more than 20 alerts would fire for one user in one minute
  Then they aggregate into a summary delivery, the suppression is visible in the alert centre, and no individual firing is lost from history
Scenario: Critical notifications survive muting
  Given quiet hours are on, ETHUSDT is muted and every optional channel is off
  When a risk lockout, kill-switch or connection-loss notification is raised
  Then it is still delivered, and the attempt to mute a risk channel is audited as notifications.risk_channel_muted
```

## Technical notes / design
Module **M22 AlertService** decomposes into three collaborators:
1. `AlertCompiler` — wraps E35's IR validator, additionally asserting the payload matches `AlertConditionIr` (no `actions` key, no action-bearing operand) and that every referenced metric exists in the E35 registry.
2. `AlertEvaluator` — one subscription per *distinct compiled condition hash* (`alerts.condition_hash`), fanned out to the alert rows sharing it, so N alerts on `last_price` cost one metric subscription. Gating order on every candidate fire: `enabled` → `deleted_at IS NULL` → `expires_at` → `snoozed_until` → `trigger_mode` → `cooldown_seconds` → storm suppressor → dispatch.
3. `DeliveryDispatcher` — writes one `alert_deliveries` row plus one `outbox` row per channel inside the firing transaction; a poller delivers and advances `queued → sent | failed | suppressed`, `acked` on user ack.

Trigger modes (`alert_trigger_mode`): `once` (fire then set `enabled=false`), `every_time` (subject to `cooldown_seconds`), `once_per_bar` (keyed on the trigger's `timeframe` bar open). Alerts **never expire on a timer** unless `expires_at` is explicitly set (US-ALRT-001 scenario 3).

## Test plan
Layer coverage is specified per child ticket. Epic-level gates: contract tests on every `/alerts*` operation and the `alerts` WS topic; an integration suite replaying a recorded Bybit window and asserting the exact firing sequence; a k6 profile at 500 armed alerts × 50 msg/s; the storm and chaos scenarios in E40-Q02; the a11y audit in E40-Q02.

## Security notes
STRIDE in E40-X01. Headline threats: **SSRF via webhook URL** (an owner-supplied URL that targets the loopback/metadata/Tailscale control plane), **secret leakage into a notification body** (message templates interpolate the rule context — the interpolator must be allow-listed), **tampering with history** (`alert_deliveries` is append-only with a `forbid_mutation` DELETE trigger), **notification-channel muting as an attack** (muting risk alerts is audited at high severity), and **information disclosure across users** (`alerts:read` is `scope: self`). `alerts.webhook_url_enc` and `alerts.webhook_secret_enc` are SECRET-classified columns and are never returned by any API.

## Accessibility notes
Four UI surfaces, all WCAG 2.2 AA. Alert lists are real tables with status as text; the fired toast is `role="status"` (never assertive — it must not interrupt order entry); sound is never the only channel; the notification settings matrix uses row+column headers; auto-dismissing toasts always have a persistent backstop in SCR-014 (WCAG 2.2.1).

## Performance notes
Budget set: condition met → visible toast ≤2 s end to end (SCR-092), in-app record ≤1 s (US-ALRT-001 NFR); alert-centre list cursor-paginated and live-updated at ≤1 Hz (SCR-090); `alerts` WS cadence 250 ms; notification centre renders 500 rows with ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame (SCR-014); notification sound assets ≤200 KB preloaded (SCR-115); condition validation round-trip ≤300 ms (SCR-091).

## Observability
Metrics `cv_alerts_armed`, `cv_alert_fires_total{trigger_mode}`, `cv_alert_suppressed_total{reason}`, `cv_alert_delivery_total{channel,status}`, `cv_alert_delivery_latency_seconds{channel}`, `cv_alert_eval_latency_seconds`, `cv_outbox_depth{topic}`. Audit events `alerts.create`, `alert.updated`, `alert.enabled_changed`, `alert.deleted`, `notifications.risk_channel_muted`.

## Definition of Done
Per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2: all children Done or explicitly descoped; epic AC verified end to end; coverage ≥85% on `cv.alerts`, ≥80% frontend; docs 14/15/21/22/23/24 reconciled; axe-core green plus a manual screen-reader pass on all four surfaces; perf numbers recorded against the budgets above; STRIDE findings closed; epic regression pass recorded; demoed to the Owner on staging (demo); retro notes filed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E35` — the IR, the metric vocabulary registry and the evaluator are E35's; E40 adds no new expression grammar. `E25` supplies the detector metrics that US-ALRT-003 alerts on. `E10` supplies the shell mounts (CMP-209, CMP-212). `E39` raises the critical risk notifications whose override behaviour E40 must honour. `E09` supplies `alerts:read`/`alerts:write` and the session scope.

## Branch
`feat/e40-alerts-*` per child ticket; PRs ≤400 LOC diff.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §24 ALRT — US-ALRT-001..008
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-014, SCR-015, SCR-090, SCR-091, SCR-092, SCR-115
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-045, CMP-060, CMP-163, CMP-164, CMP-165, CMP-209, CMP-212
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.24
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.5 `alerts` / `alert_deliveries`, §3.10.4 `outbox`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/alerts`, `/alerts/{alertId}`, `/alerts/{alertId}/enabled`, `/alerts/deliveries`, `/notifications`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.7 `AlertUpdate`, topic `alerts`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11 rule IR / metric registry, §12 RBAC permission list
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E40, §7.3 exit criteria
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md`, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0014-observability.md`

## Child dependency graph
```mermaid
graph TD
    D01[D01 UX research + a11y design review] --> D02[D02 Hi-fi all five surfaces + DS/motion + handoff pack]
    K01[K01 Spike: evaluation placement & storm thresholds] --> T02[T02 Compiler + alert CRUD API]
    T01[T01 Migration 0009_alerts + repos + outbox topics] --> T02
    T02 --> T03[T03 Evaluator + gating + storm suppression]
    T03 --> T04[T04 Delivery dispatcher + deliveries API + WS alerts]
    D02 --> S01[S01 SCR-090 alerts centre + SCR-091 alert editor]
    T02 --> S01
    T04 --> S01
    D02 --> S02[S02 Toasts, SCR-092 detail, SCR-014 centre content, SCR-115 preferences]
    T04 --> S02
    S01 --> S02
    T04 --> S03[S03 Webhook delivery - deferred to R5]
    X01[X01 STRIDE + abuse cases + security sign-off] --> S03
    T04 --> X01
    S01 --> T05[T05 Docs & ADR reconcile]
    S01 --> Q01[Q01 Test plan, fixtures, E2E + contract automation]
    S02 --> Q01
    Q01 --> Q02[Q02 Perf/storm/chaos + a11y audit + regression pack + QA sign-off]
    S02 --> Q02
    Q02 --> X01
    S02 --> D03[D03 Design QA of the shipped surfaces]
```

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.


**This epic's tickets:**
- `E40-D01` (web) — Research alert attention behaviour and run the a11y design review; blocked by: none
- `E40-D02` (web) — Design all five alert surfaces and ship the engineering handoff pack; blocked by: `E40-D01`
- `E40-D03` (web) — Design QA the shipped alert surfaces against the handoff pack; blocked by: `E40-D02`, `E40-S02`

- `E40-S01` (web) — Ship the SCR-090 alerts centre and the SCR-091 alert editor; blocked by: `E40-D02`, `E40-T02`, `E40-T04`
- `E40-S02` (web) — Ship fired-alert toasts, SCR-092/SCR-014 content and SCR-115 preferences; blocked by: `E40-D02`, `E40-S01`, `E40-T04`
- `E40-S03` (api) — Ship HMAC-signed webhook alert delivery with allow-listed egress; blocked by: `E40-T04`, `E40-X01`

title: Ship the SCR-090 alerts centre and the SCR-091 alert editor
body:
## Context
Merged from the former E40-S01 and E40-S01 — the two authoring/management surfaces ship as one frontend slice against the same CMP-163/CMP-164 contracts and the same `/alerts` API.

### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
US-ALRT-004 asks for "one place listing all alerts and their history, so that I manage them coherently". That place is SCR-090 at `/alerts`, with tabs **Active · Triggered · Snoozed**. It is also where US-ALRT-001's "recorded in the alert centre", US-ALRT-003's storm-suppression visibility and US-ALRT-006's snooze affordances become real.

Design contract: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-090 and the E40-D02 handoff pack.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
This is where US-ALRT-001 (price), US-ALRT-002 (indicator/metric) and US-ALRT-003 (order-flow/detector) become authorable. SCR-091 explicitly *reuses the rule condition editor (SCR-081) minus execution actions* — CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm composes CMP-140/141/143/144/157 from E36. The story's value is that a trader who can write a rule can write an alert instantly, and can never accidentally write an alert that trades.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
- Route `/alerts` (SCR-090), RBAC-gated on `alerts:read`; write affordances hidden without `alerts:write` and the API's 403 surfaced as an explanatory state rather than a dead button.
- Table (CMP-049) of alerts with columns **name · symbol · condition · status · last triggered · delivery channels**, rendered from `GET /api/v1/alerts`; each row is **CMP-163 AlertRow**. Status is text plus icon, never colour alone.
- Tabs Active · Triggered · Snoozed; filters by symbol and status (CMP-055 FilterBar); cursor pagination.
- Row actions: toggle active (`PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}/enabled`), snooze 15 m / 1 h / until tomorrow, duplicate (prefills SCR-091), delete (`DELETE`), "show on chart" (deep-link to the chart at the alert's symbol with the level drawn).
- Bulk selection with disarm / delete / mute applied to the selection, each behind a confirmation that names the count and the consequence, with the **result reported per item** (US-ALRT-004 scenario 2) — a partial failure lists which items failed and why.
- Firing history per alert: expand a row or open the detail to see firings with timestamps and the values at fire time, sourced from `GET /api/v1/alerts/deliveries?alert_id=…`, **exportable** as CSV (US-ALRT-004 scenario 3); history is retained ≥90 days by the retention policy.
- Storm-suppression visibility: suppressed firings appear in history with their suppressed status and the summary they were folded into.
- Estimated-detector alerts render the "(estimated)" qualifier on the condition cell (US-ALRT-003 scenario 2).
- Live updates over the WS `alerts` topic at ≤1 Hz; auto-disarmed alerts (metric source unavailable) show the reason inline.
- States from the handoff pack: empty ("No alerts yet") · loading · populated · triggered badge · expired one-shot in Triggered · snoozed with remaining time · disabled · delivery-failure chip ("Desktop notification blocked by the OS — enable it in Settings") · error.
- `+ New alert` opens SCR-091 (E40-S01); until that ships behind its flag, the button is present and disabled with a stated reason.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
- **CMP-164 AlertBuilderForm** organism and the SCR-091 modal, reachable from SCR-090 `+ New alert`, from a row's Duplicate, from the indicator settings Alerts tab (SCR-069 → "create alert from this indicator", US-IND-008), from the big-trades panel (US-BIG-005) and from the detector panels' "create alert from this threshold/level" affordances (E25 SCR-055/056/057).
- Sections: **Scope** (symbol via CMP-219 SymbolPicker, optional interval, optional account) → **Condition** (CMP-157 MetricPickerCombobox + operand rows + grouping, instances of the E36 components) → **Trigger mode** (once / every time / once per bar, with the bar-close-vs-intrabar semantics displayed explicitly per US-ALRT-002 scenario 3) → **Timing** (cooldown seconds, optional expiry) → **Delivery** (in-app toast, notification centre, desktop, sound with a preview button) → **Message** (template with `{{variable}}` interpolation and a live preview) → **Options** (name, severity).
- **Plain-language restatement** of the alert, rendered from the compiled IR ("Notify me when BTCUSDT tape speed rises above 3 sigma"), wired as the form's accessible description.
- **CMP-234 ValidationPanel** fed by `POST /api/v1/alerts` 422 `RuleIrInvalid` responses: errors first, each entry a button that moves focus to the offending row, error count announced on recompile.
- Client-side validation mirroring the server: ≥1 condition, ≥1 delivery channel, cooldown ≥5 s, expiry in the future; the server remains authoritative and its message wins on conflict.
- **The action boundary**: no actions section exists; the delivery section carries the persistent explanatory line from the copy deck ("Alerts notify; to act automatically, create a rule") linking to `/rules`.
- Estimated-metric warning banner when a selected metric is heuristic (US-ALRT-003 scenario 2).
- "Sound requires the desktop shell" note when running in a browser; sound is never selectable as the only channel.
- **Test-fire** control: produces a delivery through the real path marked as a test, so the user can verify their channel configuration.
- Save paths: `POST /api/v1/alerts` (create, with `Idempotency-Key`), `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}` with `If-Match` (edit), rendering 412 as "this alert was changed elsewhere — reload and reapply", never last-writer-wins.
- States: draft · validating · valid · invalid · saving · vocabulary-unavailable (metric service offline → editor read-only with an explanation) · permission-denied.

## Out of scope
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
The alert editor modal (E40-S01). The fired toast and notification-centre content (E40-S02). Notification preferences (E40-S02). Any alert-to-action binding (US-ALRT-007, not in E40).
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
The alerts list (E40-S01). Toast/detail (E40-S02). Preferences (E40-S02). Webhook channel selection — hidden behind the `alerts.webhook_enabled` flag until E40-S03 (R5). Any action binding (US-ALRT-007).

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
```gherkin
Scenario: The list shows everything the story asks for
  Given three alerts in different states
  When I open /alerts
  Then each row shows its condition, symbol, status, last fire time and delivery channels, and the status is readable as text
Scenario: Bulk actions report their result
  Given I select five alerts and choose Disarm
  When one of them fails server-side
  Then four are shown disarmed, the failure is listed with its reason, and the list state matches the server after a refresh
Scenario: History is complete and exportable
  Given an alert that has fired twelve times, three of them suppressed by the storm limiter
  Then the history shows all twelve with timestamps and fire-time values, marks the three as suppressed with a link to their summary, and exports the same twelve rows to CSV
Scenario: A snoozed alert states its remaining time (edge)
  When I snooze an alert for one hour
  Then it moves to the Snoozed tab and displays the remaining time, updating without a page reload
Scenario: A dead metric source is explained, not hidden (failure)
  Given an alert auto-disarmed because its metric source became unavailable
  Then the row shows disarmed with the stated reason, and re-enabling is offered but warns the source is still unavailable
Scenario: Read-only users cannot mutate (failure)
  Given a session without alerts:write
  Then toggle, snooze, delete and bulk controls are absent, and a direct API attempt returns 403 which the UI renders as an explanation
```
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
```gherkin
Scenario: A price alert is authored and saved
  Given I pick BTCUSDT, last price, crosses above, 65000, trigger mode once, channels in-app and desktop
  When I save
  Then POST /api/v1/alerts returns 201, the plain-language restatement reads back the alert, and it appears Active in SCR-090
Scenario: An indicator alert states its evaluation semantics
  Given "RSI(14) on 15m crosses below 30"
  Then the trigger mode section shows it evaluates on bar close by default and offers an explicit intrabar option
Scenario: The editor cannot express an action (edge)
  When I inspect every control and every keyboard path in the modal
  Then no control adds an execution action, and the delivery section explains where actions live
Scenario: Server validation is surfaced actionably (failure)
  Given a condition referencing a metric with no data source
  When I save
  Then the ValidationPanel shows the server's message, focus can be moved to the offending row from the panel, and nothing is persisted
Scenario: A concurrent edit does not overwrite (failure)
  Given the alert was changed in another session after I opened it
  When I save
  Then 412 is rendered as a reload-and-reapply explanation and my payload is not applied
Scenario: A sound-only configuration is refused (edge)
  When I deselect every visual channel and leave sound enabled
  Then saving is blocked with the message that sound may never be the only channel
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
Data layer: TanStack Query with the `alerts` WS topic as the invalidation source — the socket carries deliveries and the unacked count, and a delivery for an alert invalidates that alert's row rather than refetching the page. Throttle applied updates to 1 Hz per the screen's performance note.

Snooze is a client-computed `snoozed_until` sent to `PUT /api/v1/alerts/{alertId}`; "until tomorrow" resolves against the user's timezone and is displayed as an absolute time on hover so the relative label is never the only information.

Bulk actions issue individual requests with bounded concurrency and aggregate the outcomes; there is no bulk endpoint in the OpenAPI document and this story does not invent one.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
Import the E36 condition-editor components as instances from `packages/rule-editor-core`; do **not** fork them. The alert editor passes a `mode: "alert"` capability object that omits the action vocabulary — the omission is a property of the shared component's configuration, and a unit test asserts that in `mode: "alert"` the action vocabulary is empty regardless of what the server returns.

Validation is debounced and calls the same vocabulary/validation service the rule editor uses, so the two editors cannot report different diagnostics for the same condition.

Entry points from indicator, big-trade and detector panels prefill scope and metric via a typed `AlertDraft` object rather than by URL string-building.

## Test plan
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
- Unit (Vitest + RTL): row rendering per state; snooze duration arithmetic incl. the timezone boundary; bulk-result aggregation with a mixed success/failure set; filter and tab derivation; CSV export content.
- Contract: MSW handlers generated from the OpenAPI document; a test fails if the client sends a parameter the spec does not define.
- E2E (Playwright, E40-Q01): create → fire → appears in Triggered → snooze → Snoozed tab → delete.
- Perf: 1 000-alert list scrolls at ≥55 fps with virtualisation; live-update throttling verified at 1 Hz under a firing burst.
- a11y: axe-core green; keyboard-only path through tabs, filters, selection and row actions.
- Coverage ≥80% frontend.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
- Unit: capability-object test (action vocabulary empty in alert mode); validation mirroring; sound-only refusal; expiry/cooldown boundary values; 412 handling; `AlertDraft` prefill from each entry point.
- Contract: request bodies validated against `AlertInput` in the OpenAPI document.
- E2E (E40-Q01): author a price alert, an RSI alert and a stacked-imbalance alert; test-fire each; verify each fires against a replayed window.
- a11y: axe-core green; keyboard-complete authoring with no mouse; ValidationPanel focus movement verified with a screen reader.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
The condition cell renders user-authored text: render as plain text with no markup interpretation and the truncation limit from the copy deck. Never display `webhook_url` or any secret — the API does not return them, and a test asserts the row component has no code path that would render them if it did. Cross-user access is prevented server-side; the UI must not construct alert ids from any client-held value other than the list response.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
The message-template field is user input that is later rendered in a toast, a notification row and (eventually) a webhook payload: the editor renders its preview as plain text only, and the placeholder picker offers only the allow-listed namespace enforced by E40-T02. The editor must never accept a free-typed placeholder that bypasses the picker without re-validation. Test-fire goes through the authenticated API, not a client-side shortcut, so it cannot be used to forge a delivery. The webhook URL field stays behind its flag and is not implemented here — no client code path may write `webhook_url` in R3.

## Accessibility notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
Per the E40-D01 contract: a real `<table>` with header cells (name, symbol, condition, status, last triggered, delivery); status conveyed as text; the create button reachable from the page heading level; bulk selection announced as "N selected"; tab list is a real `role="tablist"` with arrow-key navigation; live row updates use `aria-live="polite"` with announcement throttling so a burst does not flood; snooze remaining time exposed as text, not only as a progress ring.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
Per E40-D01: keyboard-complete authoring is a hard requirement (the editor is also the accessible path for creating alerts from canvas surfaces); the plain-language restatement is the form's accessible description; ValidationPanel is `role="log"` with errors first and focus-moving entries; sound preview has a text label and is never the only channel; modal is a focus-trapped dialog with a heading; 200% zoom supported.

## Performance notes
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
List virtualised and cursor-paginated; live updates ≤1 Hz (SCR-090 performance note); no layout thrash on update — row updates mutate text nodes only.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
Validation round-trip ≤300 ms p95 (SCR-091); no evaluation runs until saved; the metric combobox is virtualised over the full metric catalogue.

## Observability
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
Emit `alerts.list_viewed`, `alerts.filtered`, `alert.enabled_changed`, `alert.snoozed`, `alert.deleted`, `alerts.bulk_action` (analytics); the audited events are emitted server-side and are not duplicated client-side.
### Part B — SCR-091 alert editor reusing the rule condition builder
`alert.editor_opened`, `alert.condition_changed`, `alert.test_fired`, `alert.save_failed{reason}` (analytics); `alert.created` / `alert.updated` are audited server-side.

## Definition of Done
### Part A — SCR-090 alerts centre: tabs, filters and bulk actions
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests (unit/E2E) or an executed QA step with a follow-up automation ticket.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the touched frontend package.

title: Ship fired-alert toasts, SCR-092/SCR-014 content and SCR-115 preferences
body:
## Context
Merged from the former E40-S02 and E40-S02 — the delivery-consumption surfaces (toast, detail view, notification centre) and the preference surface that governs them ship as one frontend slice.

### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
US-ALRT-005 (Must half): "a toast appears with the alert detail and an action to open the relevant chart", plus a desktop notification via the Electron shell even when the window is unfocused. US-ALRT-004's alert-centre record and US-OBS-004's system notifications share one surface: SCR-014, the right-rail drawer E10 mounted empty. This story fills all of it.

The governing a11y constraint is that the toast is `role="status"` — it must not interrupt order entry — while order rejects and risk lockouts route to CMP-212's separate `role="alert"` region.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
US-ALRT-006 (Should) is the counterweight to everything else in E40: snooze, mute and quiet hours exist so the trader is not overwhelmed. Its third scenario is the one that matters most — *a risk alert (daily loss, liquidation proximity, connection loss) always delivers, regardless of mute or quiet hours* — and its NFR requires the critical-override list to be "explicit, documented and covered by tests". That list was ratified in E40-D01 and is implemented here and in E40-T03.

## Scope / Deliverables
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
- **SCR-015 / CMP-165 AlertFiredToastGroup**: a Toast (CMP-045) variant for fired alerts that batches rapid duplicates into one counted summary ("3 alerts fired for BTCUSDT"). Content shows the alert name, **the actual metric value that fired it**, symbol/timeframe and time. Actions: open chart at that moment, snooze, disable, open detail. At most 3 toasts on screen; overflow collapses into a counted stack; errors never auto-dismiss; every toast is duplicated into SCR-014.
- **SCR-092 detail drawer** (CMP-046): the full metric snapshot from `alert_deliveries.context` rendered as a key-value table (CMP-036) with the ordering rule from the handoff pack and a graceful presentation of unknown keys, plus a link to the bar and a "create a rule from this alert" link-out to `/rules/new` prefilled (the link only — E40 never binds an action).
- **SCR-014 notification centre content** inside CMP-209 RightRail, using CMP-060 NotificationCenter: a mixed stream of alert / rule / order / risk / system / recorder items from `GET /api/v1/notifications` (scroll-back) and the `alerts`, `rules`, `orders`, `system` WS topics (live). Severity by icon + text; grouped/collapsed repeats ("12 similar alerts"); per-category mute entry point into SCR-115; `Shift+click` marks everything above read; deep-link to the source (chart at timestamp / rule / order); empty state ("Nothing yet today"); unread badge; overflow keeps the newest 500 with older items reachable via history.
- **Acknowledgement**: mark-read wired to `POST /api/v1/alerts/deliveries/{deliveryId}/ack` and `…/ack-all`; the unacked badge count comes from the `AlertUpdate.unacked_count` field, not a client-side count.
- **Electron desktop notifications**: on an `alerts` delivery with the `desktop` channel, the shell raises an OS notification even when unfocused; clicking it focuses the window and opens the detail. The OS permission state (granted / denied / unsupported) is reported back so SCR-090 and SCR-115 can show the blocked chip and remediation.
- **Delivery-failure surfacing** (US-ALRT-005 scenario 3): a failed channel shows its failure on the alert record while the in-app record persists — the UI must make it obvious that the alert *did* fire and only a channel failed.
- Storm summaries render as a single grouped item that expands to the individual suppressed firings.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
- **SCR-115 Notifications settings** section under `/settings`: a full **event × channel matrix** (rows: alerts, rule actions, order rejects, risk events, system health, recorder; columns: in-app toast, notification centre, desktop, sound) as labelled checkboxes with row and column headers.
- Per-category **sound selection** with a preview button and volume; assets preloaded once, ≤200 KB total.
- **Quiet hours**: start/end with the timezone stated explicitly, and a permanently visible statement that critical events still notify.
- **Critical-override rows rendered locked**: risk, lockout, kill-switch and order-rejection categories cannot be fully muted; the locked state is drawn with an inline explanation, not silently omitted. Attempting to mute a risk channel is **audited** as `notifications.risk_channel_muted` at high severity.
- **Desktop permission state**: granted / denied / unsupported, with per-platform remediation instructions and a re-request action where the platform allows it.
- **Test-notification control** per channel, so a configuration can be verified without waiting for a real firing.
- **Symbol mute** (US-ALRT-006 scenario 2): muting a symbol records its alerts but produces no sound or notification, and the mute is **visible on the symbol** wherever it appears (watchlist row, chart header, alert row).
- **Snooze** surface consistency: the snooze durations offered here match SCR-090's (15 m / 1 h / until tomorrow) and share one implementation.
- Preferences are local-first and synced through the settings store (E13/`/settings` API); the server-side evaluator reads them so muting works even when the client is closed.

## Out of scope
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
Notification preferences, mute and quiet hours (E40-S02) — this story consumes the preference values but does not provide the editing UI. The alerts list and editor (E40-S01/S02). Webhook (E40-S03).
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
The notification surfaces themselves (E40-S02). Alert-level snooze on a single alert (E40-S01). Appearance/a11y settings (E13). The server-side gating implementation (E40-T03) — this story provides the values it reads.

## Acceptance criteria
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
```gherkin
Scenario: A firing produces a toast with real data
  Given an armed alert fires on BTCUSDT
  When the alerts WS message arrives
  Then a toast appears within 2 s of the condition being met showing the alert name and the triggering metric value, with an action that opens the chart at that moment
Scenario: The toast does not interrupt order entry
  Given focus is inside the order ticket
  When an alert toast appears
  Then focus does not move, the toast is announced politely, and the ticket remains operable
Scenario: Nothing is lost if a toast is missed
  Given a toast auto-dismisses before I read it
  Then the same item is present in the notification centre with its full detail, satisfying WCAG 2.2.1
Scenario: Rapid duplicates collapse (edge)
  Given five alerts fire for BTCUSDT within two seconds
  Then one counted summary toast is shown, expanding to the five individual items, and all five exist separately in the centre
Scenario: A blocked desktop notification is explained (failure)
  Given the OS has denied notification permission
  Then the delivery is shown failed with the reason, the in-app record still exists, and SCR-090 shows the remediation chip
Scenario: Acking is reflected everywhere (edge)
  When I mark everything read
  Then ack-all is called once, the unacked badge reaches zero from the server-provided count, and a reload shows the same state
```
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
```gherkin
Scenario: Muting a symbol silences without losing the record
  Given I mute ETHUSDT
  When an ETHUSDT alert fires
  Then no sound or desktop notification is produced, the delivery is still recorded and visible in the centre, and the mute is shown on the symbol
Scenario: Quiet hours suppress the optional channels only
  Given quiet hours are 22:00 to 07:00 in my stated timezone
  When a normal alert fires at 23:00
  Then desktop and sound are suppressed while the in-app record is created
Scenario: A critical event overrides everything (edge)
  Given quiet hours are active, every symbol is muted and every optional channel is off
  When a daily-loss breach, liquidation-proximity, connection-loss or kill-switch notification is raised
  Then it is delivered on the channels the override list specifies
Scenario: Muting a risk channel is refused and audited (failure)
  When I attempt to disable the risk-event row
  Then the control is locked with an explanation, and any API-level attempt is rejected and audited as notifications.risk_channel_muted
Scenario: A denied OS permission is actionable (failure)
  Given the OS has denied notification permission
  Then the desktop column shows denied with platform-specific remediation, and the test-notification control explains it cannot succeed until permission is granted
Scenario: Sound cannot become the only channel (edge)
  When I disable every visual channel for a category and leave sound on
  Then the change is refused with the message that sound may never be the only channel
```

## Technical notes / design
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
One WS subscription per topic at the shell level, fanned out through a notification store; the store keeps the newest 500 items and falls back to `GET /api/v1/notifications` for scroll-back with the shared `(ts, id)` cursor. Toast presentation subscribes to the store, so a toast and a centre row are two views of one item and can never disagree.

Desktop notifications use the Electron `Notification` API from the main process via the existing IPC bridge from E10; the renderer never calls it directly. The permission outcome is posted back to the server so the delivery status is accurate rather than optimistic.

Deep-links use the E10 deep-link parameter contract (`docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` §7), not hand-built URLs.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
The critical-override list is a **single shared constant** consumed by the server evaluator (E40-T03), the settings UI and the test suite; it is defined once in the shared schema package and imported, never re-declared — that is how the NFR's "explicit, documented and covered by tests" is mechanically guaranteed. A test enumerates the constant and asserts every entry is rendered locked in the matrix.

Quiet hours are stored with an explicit IANA timezone, not an offset, so DST transitions behave; the server evaluates them in that zone.

Symbol mute lives in the same preference document so the evaluator can apply it server-side; the "visible on the symbol" requirement is satisfied by a shared mute-indicator component consumed by the watchlist row, chart header and alert row.

## Test plan
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
- Unit: toast batching/collapse arithmetic; store eviction at 500 with history fallback; unacked-count sourcing (a test asserts the badge never derives from a client-side count); deep-link construction per source kind; unknown-key rendering in the detail table.
- Integration: Electron notification path with permission granted / denied / unsupported (mocked main process).
- E2E (E40-Q01): fire an alert against a replayed window → toast appears → open detail → chart opens at the right timestamp → item present in the centre → ack → badge clears.
- Perf: 500 rows virtualised at ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame; toast animation asserted to use transform/opacity only (no layout) via a performance trace; unread count debounced to 250 ms.
- a11y: axe-core; screen-reader pass over a burst; reduced-motion variant.
- Coverage ≥80%.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
- Unit: matrix state reduction; the locked-row constant test; quiet-hours evaluation across a DST boundary; sound-only refusal; symbol-mute propagation to the three consuming surfaces.
- Integration: preference change → server evaluator honours it on the next firing (proven with a replayed window and the client disconnected).
- E2E (E40-Q01): mute a symbol, fire an alert, assert silence plus a recorded delivery; then fire a risk notification and assert it still delivers.
- a11y: axe-core; matrix navigable with row/column headers announced; sound previews labelled.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
Alert names, message templates and rule text are user-authored and arrive over WS: render as plain text with the copy-deck truncation; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in this story — enforced by an ESLint rule and a unit test. The detail drawer renders a free-form `context` object: render values as strings, never evaluate, and cap the rendered depth/size so a large context cannot freeze the renderer. Deep-links must validate their parameters against the E10 contract before navigating, so a crafted notification cannot drive navigation to an arbitrary route.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
Muting risk notifications is a plausible **abuse path** — a compromised or careless session could silence the very signals that reveal a problem — which is why the override list is enforced server-side, the locked rows cannot be bypassed by an API call, and every attempt is audited at high severity. Preferences are per-user and `scope: self`; one user cannot mute another's notifications. Remediation instructions must not tell a user to disable OS-level security features.

## Accessibility notes
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
Per E40-D01: toast is `role="status"` (polite) and never steals focus; errors/rejections route to CMP-212's separate `role="alert"` region; SCR-014 is `aria-live="polite"` escalating to assertive only for order rejects and risk lockouts; announcement throttling summarises bursts instead of reading each item; absolute timestamps available alongside relative; the drawer does not steal focus when it opens on a new event; every auto-dismissing item has a persistent backstop; `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured (fade only).
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
The matrix uses real row and column headers so a screen reader announces "Risk events, desktop, checked, locked"; sound choices have a play button with a text label; quiet-hours fields state the timezone in text; the locked state is conveyed by text and `aria-disabled` with an `aria-describedby` explanation, never by colour or a cursor change alone.

## Performance notes
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
Condition met → visible toast ≤2 s end to end (SCR-092); centre renders 500 notifications at ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame (SCR-014); unread count debounced to 250 ms; toast animation must not trigger layout on the chart surface.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
Sound assets preloaded once, ≤200 KB total, so a triggered alert plays without fetch latency (SCR-115 performance note). Preference writes are debounced and local-first so the matrix never feels laggy.

## Observability
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
`alert.toast_shown`, `alert.toast_actioned`, `alert.detail_opened`, `alert.snoozed`, `notifications.opened`, `notifications.filtered`, `notifications.item_actioned`, `notifications.mark_all_read` (analytics). Client error reporting for a failed desktop-notification path.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
`notifications.preference_changed {event, channel, enabled}` (analytics); `notifications.risk_channel_muted` (**audited**, high severity); `notifications.test_sent {channel}`.

## Definition of Done
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
- [ ] All scenarios automated or QA-executed with follow-ups filed.
- [ ] No-raw-HTML lint rule and test in place.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; axe-core green; screen-reader burst pass recorded.
- [ ] Storybook stories for CMP-165 and the notification-centre content per the agreed list.
- [ ] Perf trace attached showing toast animation causes no layout.
- [ ] Design sign-off; QA sign-off per scenario.
- [ ] Feature flag `alerts.notifications_enabled` recorded per environment.
- [ ] Demoed on staging (demo); PR merged via merge queue.
### Part B — SCR-115 notification preferences, mute and quiet hours
- [ ] All scenarios automated or QA-executed with follow-ups.
- [ ] Shared critical-override constant in place with its enumeration test, running as a required check.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; axe-core green; matrix verified with a screen reader.
- [ ] Server-side honouring proven with the client disconnected.
- [ ] Security review of the override enforcement and the audit event (`security` label).
- [ ] Design sign-off; QA sign-off per scenario.
- [ ] Feature flag `alerts.preferences_enabled` recorded per environment.
- [ ] Demoed; PR merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
### Part A — Fired-alert toasts, SCR-092 detail and SCR-014 notification-centre content
`E40-T04` (deliveries + `alerts` WS topic + ack endpoints), `E40-D02` (handoff), `E10` (RightRail, ToastHost, IPC bridge, deep-link contract), `E39` (risk notifications that route to the assertive region).

`feat/e40-alert-notifications`. Two PRs: toast/detail, then centre content.

title: Journal & analytics
body:
## Context
R3 "Trading on demo" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7) closes the execution loop: once orders are placed from the ticket, the chart and the DOM, fanned out across accounts and managed by rules, the owner needs evidence of what actually happened. **E41 Journal & analytics** is that evidence layer. The roadmap scopes it (section 7.2) as: *"Auto-captured trades from OMS executions with chart snapshots at entry/exit; manual notes, tags and rating; performance analytics (win rate, expectancy, R-multiple distribution, MAE/MFE, session/symbol/tag breakdowns, equity curve); per-account and per-trade-group views; CSV/Parquet export; `GET /v5/position/closed-pnl` reconciliation against local records"* - 26 pts, Sprints S18-S19, backend module **M20 `journal`**, story domain **JRN**.

Three properties make this more than a CRUD screen:
1. **The journal is derived, not authored.** Entries are materialised from the execution stream (M14 OMS) and must be idempotent and restart-safe (US-JRN-001 NFR). A user may only add *opinion* - notes, tags, rating, setup, mistakes; every computed field is read-only by contract (`updateJournalTrade` description in `22-api-openapi.yaml`).
2. **It is evidence, therefore tamper-evident and role-scoped.** `04-security-program.md` classifies journal content as asset **A-12**, requires exports to be role-scoped, watermarked and audited (**SR-098**), and rates journal export disclosure as threat **S4**. Journal write events (`journal.note_added`, `journal.tag_added`, `journal.tag_removed`, `journal.trade_excluded`, `journal.rating_set`) are audited, not merely analytics.
3. **Environments must never be mixed.** Live, demo/paper and replay-simulated results are separate populations (US-JRN-006 "Environment separation"; `journal_trades.env`, `journal_trades.is_paper`). Aggregating them produces a statistic worse than no statistic.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (all 10 JRN stories):** US-JRN-001 (Must), US-JRN-002 (Must), US-JRN-003 (Should), US-JRN-004 (Should), US-JRN-005 (Should), US-JRN-006 (Must), US-JRN-007 (Should), US-JRN-008 (Should), US-JRN-009 (Should), US-JRN-010 (Could).

**Screens:** SCR-093 Journal (trade list, `/journal`), SCR-094 Trade detail / post-mortem, SCR-095 Journal analytics dashboard (`/journal/analytics`), SCR-096 Journal tag manager.

**Components:** CMP-166 JournalEntryRow, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard, CMP-169 TagEditor (new); reused CMP-021, CMP-024, CMP-026, CMP-036, CMP-043, CMP-044, CMP-046, CMP-047, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-058, CMP-099, CMP-116.

**API:** `GET /journal/trades`, `GET|PATCH /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}`, `GET|POST /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/notes`, `GET /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/context`, `GET|POST /journal/tags`, `GET /journal/analytics`; consumer of `GET /executions/closed-pnl`.

**DB:** `journal_trades`, `journal_tags`, `journal_trade_tags`, `notes` (plus `audit_log` writes and `executions` / `trade_groups` / `trade_group_legs` reads).

**Module:** M20 `journal` (`services/api/journal/`), with Parquet/DuckDB cold-tier reads for long-range analytics (C18).

## Out of scope
- Backtesting and strategy reports (R4/R5 epics) - the journal reports what happened, not hypotheticals.
- The replay engine itself (E26) - E41 only deep-links into it via `journal_trades.replay_anchor_ts`.
- Alert delivery channels (E40) - E41 only requests a notification when an async export finishes.
- Admin audit-log screens (E42); order/position management screens (E29/E30).
- Any Android client, any separate admin application, any non-Bybit / non-USDT-perp instrument.
- Broker statement import, tax reporting, third-party journal sync.

## Exit criteria
1. Every closed position on demo produces exactly one journal entry per account leg plus one `is_aggregate` row per trade group, correct after an API restart mid-close, verified against `GET /executions/closed-pnl`.
2. SCR-093/094/095/096 shipped, design-signed-off, axe-core clean, keyboard-complete, with table alternatives for every chart.
3. `GET /journal/analytics` returns totals and all seven breakdowns for 10 000 trades within budget (p95 <150 ms warm; breakdown query <=2 s cold), computed server-side.
4. Demo/live/paper populations are never aggregated together; the active environment filter is always displayed.
5. Export is role-scoped server-side, watermarked, audited, and contains no API identifiers or secrets.
6. STRIDE model (E41-X01) finalised and findings triaged; QA sign-off (E41-Q03) recorded.

## Story list
| Key | Title | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| E41-K01 | Spike: analytics query tier (Postgres vs DuckDB/Parquet) + ADR | 2 |
| E41-T01 | M20 journal module, migrations and read API | 3 |
| E41-T02 | Trade materialiser, MAE/MFE and closed-pnl reconciliation | 5 |
| E41-T03 | Analytics aggregation service and `GET /journal/analytics` | 3 |
| E41-T04 | Tags, notes, auto-tagging and audited export job | 3 |
| E41-T05 | Statistics formula reference + ADR-0016 | 1 |
| E41-S01 | Journal trade list screen (SCR-093) | 5 |
| E41-S02 | Trade detail / post-mortem (SCR-094) with replay deep-link | 3 |
| E41-S03 | Analytics dashboard (SCR-095) | 3 |
| E41-S04 | Tag manager (SCR-096) and export UI | 1 |
| E41-D01..D05 | UX research, wireframes, hi-fi, a11y review, handoff, design QA | 13 |
| E41-Q01..Q03 | Test plan + E2E, perf/chaos, a11y audit + regression + sign-off | 8 |
| E41-X01..X02 | STRIDE threat model + abuse cases, security review | 5 |

Engineering subtotal **29 pts** (roadmap budget 26, +11.5%, inside the +/-15% tolerance); design 13, QA 8, security 5 are tracked separately.

## Risks
- **R7 Data accuracy** - divergence between local P&L and `closed-pnl` silently misleads; mitigated by nightly reconciliation with a divergence alert (E41-T02).
- **R12 Backtest bias** - statistics on a <=20-trade sample look authoritative; mitigated by the mandatory low-sample caveat (US-JRN-006) and low-confidence bucket marking (US-JRN-008).
- **R13 Sharing abuse** - exports leak other managers' account data; mitigated by SR-098 server-side scoping, watermark and audit (E41-X01/X02).
- **R15 Data lifecycle** - snapshots and recorded context pruned before review; mitigated by an honest "context not recorded" state and the snapshot budget policy (US-JRN-004).
- **R5 Scope** - MAE/MFE and tag breakdowns are the declared R5 descoping candidates (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 12 row 7); they are built last and behind clear seams.

## Dependency graph
```mermaid

  E26[E26 Replay engine] --> S02
  E40[E40 Alerts] --> T04
  S01 --> Q01
  S02 --> Q01

  Q01[E41-Q01 Test plan and E2E] --> Q03
  T03 --> Q02
  Q02[E41-Q02 Perf and chaos] --> Q03
  X01[E41-X01 STRIDE] --> X02
  T04 --> X02
  S01 --> D05
  S03 --> D05
  D05[E41-D05 Design QA] --> Q03
  X02[E41-X02 Security review] --> Q03
  Q03[E41-Q03 a11y audit regression QA sign-off]
```

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: End-to-end capture
  Given a fan-out trade group of three accounts opens and fully closes on demo
  When I open /journal
  Then three leg entries and one aggregate entry exist with weighted-average entry and exit prices
  And each entry's realised P&L matches GET /executions/closed-pnl within one quantisation step

Scenario: Environment separation
  Given both demo and live-flagged entries exist
  When I open /journal/analytics
  Then demo entries are excluded by default, the active environment filter is displayed, and no statistic mixes the two populations

Scenario: Scoped export
  Given I am an Account Manager with access to exactly one account
  When I export the journal
  Then the file contains only that account's trades, is watermarked with my identity and the timestamp, is audited, and contains no API key identifiers
```

## Technical notes / design
M20 owns a `TradeMaterialiser` subscribing to the OMS execution stream, a `JournalAnalyticsService` over the storage tier chosen by E41-K01, and the FastAPI router mounted at `/api/v1/journal`. Writes go to Postgres; long-range analytics may read Parquet via DuckDB (C18). All money maths crosses into `Decimal` at the module boundary per `24-internal-schemas.md` constraint C3.

## Test plan
Delegated to children and rolled up by E41-Q01 (functional/E2E), E41-Q02 (perf on 10k trades + chaos), E41-Q03 (a11y + regression + sign-off).

## Security notes
Asset A-12; threats S4 (export disclosure) and IDOR on `journalTradeId`; controls SR-098 plus deny-by-default `journal:read` / `journal:write` scoped to `granted_accounts`. Epic labelled `security`; STRIDE kickoff is E41-X01.

## Accessibility notes
Four screens, three of them data-dense. Every chart needs a table alternative and a text summary; colour is never the sole encoding (the MAE/MFE scatter encodes outcome by shape); signed values are always unit-labelled.

## Performance notes
SCR-093 virtualised to 10 000 rows at <=8 ms scripting per frame; SCR-095 interactive <=800 ms for 10 000 trades; breakdown queries <=2 s; REST reads p95 <150 ms (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 13).

## Observability

## Definition of Done
