title: Implement tags, notes, auto-tagging and the audited export job
body:
## Context
This ticket carries the user-authored half of the journal - US-JRN-002 (Must, notes and tags), US-JRN-003 (Should, automatic tagging) and US-JRN-010 (Could, export) - plus their audit obligations. Journal writes are **audited**, not merely analytics (SCR-093: *"journal content is user-authored evidence and must be tamper-evident"*), and exports are the epic's highest-rated disclosure threat (S4 / SR-098, risk R13).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **`PATCH /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}`** writing only the user-authored fields the contract permits - `rating`, `tags`, `setup`, `mistakes`, `checklist`. Any attempt to write a computed field (`realised_pnl`, `r_multiple`, `mae_r`, `mfe_r`, durations) returns `422` naming the offending field; computed fields are never silently ignored.
- **`POST /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/notes`** creating markdown notes with an optional chart snapshot reference (`NoteInput` -> `Note`), with **edit history retained** (US-JRN-002) - an edit writes a new revision rather than overwriting - and server-side sanitisation of the markdown (no raw HTML, no script URIs, no external image auto-fetch).
- **`GET /journal/tags`** (usage counts) and **`POST /journal/tags`** (create; unique on `lower(name)` per `ux_jtag_name`, `<=40` chars by contract, `<=24` by the SCR-096 validation rule - implement the stricter UI limit as a validation and document the contract's wider bound), plus rename / merge / delete server-side operations backing SCR-096.
- **Merge and rename are single transactions** with a reported affected-trade count, not client-side loops (SCR-096 performance note); renaming a tag used by 5 000 trades completes as one transaction.
- **Bulk tagging**: apply/remove a tag across a selected set, returning the count of affected trades (US-JRN-002 "Bulk tagging").
- **Auto-tagging** (US-JRN-003): on materialisation, apply provenance tags - the managing rule's name and version when a rule controlled the exit (`origin_rule_id`, closing the loop with the rule engine's `log_journal_tag` action), and detector-context tags when a detector fired within the configured window before entry. Auto tags are written with `journal_trade_tags.auto_applied = true`, carry provenance, **never overwrite manual tags**, and a user removal is *recorded* (an audit event plus a suppression record) so the tag does not silently reappear on reprocessing.
- **Export** (US-JRN-010): CSV (one row per trade, documented column semantics) and Parquet over the filtered set; role-scoped **server-side**; watermarked with the exporting identity and timestamp (SR-098); audited; **never** containing API keys, key identifiers, secrets or internal ids beyond the journal trade id. Above 50 000 matched rows the export runs asynchronously and notifies on completion via the E40 notification channel.

## Out of scope
- Tag manager UI (E41-S04); export UI affordance (E41-S04); the analytics payload (E41-T03); the rule engine itself (E35).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Computed fields are not writable
  When a PATCH attempts to set realised_pnl
  Then the response is 422 naming realised_pnl and the stored entry is unchanged

Scenario: Note sanitisation and history
  When a note containing a script tag and an onerror attribute is submitted
  Then the stored content has them removed, the note renders safely, and a subsequent edit creates a new revision with the previous revision retained

Scenario: Audited writes
  When a tag is added, a tag is removed, a rating is set or a trade is excluded
  Then an audit entry is written with actor, subject and before/after values, and it is present in the append-only audit log

Scenario: Tag merge
  Given a tag applied to 5000 trades is merged into another
  Then the operation completes in a single transaction, reports affectedTrades 5000, and writes journal.tag_merged with that count

Scenario: Auto tag provenance and removal
  Given a rule managed the exit and an auto tag was applied
  When the user removes that auto tag
  Then the removal is recorded and reprocessing the same trade does not re-add the tag

Scenario: Auto tags never overwrite manual ones
  Given a manual tag with the same name exists
  Then auto-tagging leaves the manual tag intact and does not downgrade its provenance

Scenario: Export scoping
  Given a Manager with access to one account exports the journal
  Then the file contains only that account's trades, enforced server-side, is watermarked with the exporter's identity and timestamp, and is recorded in the audit log

Scenario: Export contains no secrets
  When any export is produced
  Then no API key, key identifier, credential or exchange account secret appears in any column, asserted by an automated scan of the output

Scenario: Large export
  Given 60 000 rows match
  Then the export is generated asynchronously and the user is notified when it is ready
```

## Technical notes / design
Sanitisation uses an allowlist markdown renderer server-side (store sanitised, render sanitised - defence in depth rather than trusting the client). Note revisions live in the `notes` table's history mechanism with `subject_kind = 'journal_trade'`, validated by `trg_notes_subject`.

Auto-tag suppression is a small table keyed `(journal_trade_id, journal_tag_id)` recording the user's removal, checked before any auto-apply. Without it, "auto tags editable" (US-JRN-003) is not actually true because reprocessing would undo the user's decision.

CSV column semantics are documented in the same reference E41-T05 produces, so an exported file is interpretable without the app. Watermark: a header comment row in CSV and file-level metadata in Parquet, both carrying exporting user, timestamp, applied filters and the account scope.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: field-allowlist enforcement; sanitiser against an XSS payload corpus; tag name uniqueness case-insensitively; merge transaction counts; suppression logic; watermark content.
- **Contract**: PATCH/POST endpoints against the OpenAPI schemas incl. `409` on duplicate tag.
- **Integration**: 5 000-trade merge in one transaction; async export path above the 50k threshold incl. the notification.
- **Security**: an automated secret-scan assertion over generated exports; a cross-manager export attempt asserted to return only in-scope rows.
- **E2E** (with E41-Q01): bulk tag from SCR-093, merge from SCR-096, export and download.
- Coverage target >=85%.

## Security notes
Directly mitigates **S4** (journal exports contain account identifiers shared across managers) via **SR-098**: role-scoped, watermarked, audited exports. Additional threats handled: stored XSS via notes (sanitisation server-side), tampering with evidence (audited writes + note revision history + computed fields immutable), auto-tag forgery (provenance flag distinguishes auto from manual so a manual tag cannot be passed off as rule-derived). Data classification A-12. **This ticket requires the `security` review label and is an input to E41-X02.**

## Accessibility notes
N/A (backend); the error messages returned (e.g. the `422` field name, the affected-trade count) are surfaced verbatim by the UI, so they are written as user-facing copy, not developer strings.

## Performance notes
Tag merge/rename must be O(1) round-trips regardless of usage count; export streams rather than materialising the full set in memory; async threshold at 50 000 rows.

## Observability
`journal_export_rows_total{format}`, `journal_export_duration_seconds`, `journal_tag_operations_total{op}`, `journal_autotag_applied_total`, `journal_autotag_suppressed_total`; audit events `journal.note_added`, `journal.tag_added`, `journal.tag_removed`, `journal.trade_excluded`, `journal.rating_set`, `journal.tag_created`, `journal.tag_renamed`, `journal.tag_merged`, `journal.tag_deleted` (with `affectedTrades`), `journal.exported`.

title: STRIDE threat model and abuse cases for journal & analytics
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic and already names the journal's headline concerns: asset **A-12** (trade notes, screenshots, P&L; classification C2/I2/A1), threat **S4** ("journal exports contain account identifiers shared across managers", Medium), control **SR-098** (exports role-scoped, watermarked, audited), objective **O8** (integrity of journal history as evidence), and permission rows 35-37 in section 7.2. This ticket turns those into a worked model with concrete abuse cases before the write and export paths (E41-T04) are reviewed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **STRIDE model** for the M20 journal trust boundary, documented in `docs/security/threat-models/E41-journal.md`, covering each element: the materialiser's consumption of the execution stream, the Postgres journal tables, the snapshot object store, the analytics query path (including the DuckDB/Parquet path if ADR-0016 selected it), the export job, and the four UI surfaces.
- Per-category analysis with likelihood/impact and a named control, at minimum:
  - **S (Spoofing)**: forging an auto tag so a manual decision appears rule-derived; impersonating the exporting identity in a watermark.
  - **T (Tampering)**: editing a computed field (P&L, R-multiple) to rewrite history; deleting or altering a note to remove evidence; altering the audit trail.
  - **R (Repudiation)**: denying that a note, rating, exclusion or export happened.
  - **I (Information disclosure)**: S4 export scope leakage; IDOR on `journalTradeId`; cross-manager visibility through the account breakdown; snapshots served without authorisation; scope-blind response caching; error messages disclosing the existence of out-of-scope entries.
  - **D (Denial of service)**: an unbounded export or a seven-breakdown query over a huge range exhausting the API; snapshot capture back-pressuring the execution stream.
  - **E (Elevation of privilege)**: a Viewer obtaining write access via PATCH; a Manager widening `account_ids` beyond their grant; a Parquet/DuckDB path bypassing the API's scoping.
- **Abuse cases** written as adversarial narratives with the tester actions that prove the control, handed to E41-Q01 charter (c) and E41-X02:
  1. Manager B enumerates journal trade ids to read Manager A's trades;
  2. a user exports "all accounts" by tampering with the request parameters;
  3. a user edits a losing trade's P&L to improve their record;
  4. a user removes an audit-relevant note after a bad trade;
  5. a user injects script into a note to attack the Owner's session;
  6. a user requests every breakdown over a ten-year range repeatedly to degrade the API;
  7. a departed manager's cached analytics response is served after their grant is revoked.
- **SAST/DAST rules**: a Semgrep rule asserting that every journal repository query carries the account-scope predicate, a rule forbidding raw HTML rendering of note content, and an OWASP ZAP scan profile for the `/journal/*` routes.
- **Permission verification matrix** for rows 35-37 of `04-security-program.md` section 7.2, listing the exact test that proves each cell.
- Findings entered into the risk register where they change a rating.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the controls (E41-T01/T04); the security review of the built code (E41-X02); the R4 pen-test (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Model completeness
  When the model is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect
  Then every element of the journal trust boundary has all six STRIDE categories considered, each with either a named control or an explicitly accepted risk signed by the Owner

Scenario: Abuse cases are executable
  Then each of the seven abuse cases states the attacker, the precondition, the exact request or action, the expected defensive behaviour, and the test that proves it

Scenario: Rules land in CI
  Then the Semgrep scope-predicate rule and the note-rendering rule are merged into the CI security job and fail a deliberately introduced violation

Scenario: Cache poisoning by scope covered
  Then the model explicitly addresses analytics response caching keyed without scope and names the test that proves the scope is part of the cache key
```

## Technical notes / design
Two findings deserve special attention because they are easy to miss and cheap to fix now: (1) the deliberate disclosure agreed in E41-D03, where an out-of-scope trade-group leg is shown as "not in your scope" rather than omitted - this is a *reviewed* information-disclosure decision, chosen because silently omitting a leg misstates group P&L; the model must record the reasoning and its bounds (no symbol, size or P&L disclosed, only existence). (2) grant revocation timing: a cached analytics response or an in-flight export must not outlive the grant that authorised it.

## Test plan
The abuse cases are the test plan; they are executed by E41-Q01 charter (c) and verified in E41-X02. The Semgrep rules are tested with deliberately violating fixtures.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security artefact. Data classification A-12; it must itself contain no real account identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The DoS analysis sets the hard bounds implemented elsewhere: the export async threshold (50 000 rows), a maximum analytics range, and the bounded snapshot work queue.

## Observability
Specifies the security-relevant events that must be observable: `journal_authz_denied_total`, export audit entries, and an alert on an anomalous export volume.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/security/threat-models/E41-journal.md` merged.
- [ ] All six STRIDE categories covered per element with controls or signed accepted risks.
- [ ] Seven abuse cases written and handed to QA.
- [ ] Semgrep rules and the ZAP profile merged into CI and proven to fail on a violation.
- [ ] Permission matrix rows 35-37 verified with named tests.
- [ ] Security engineer and Architect review comments recorded; risk register updated where ratings changed.

title: Build SCR-122 user detail with role/account binding, limits and SCR-124 view-as
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-002 — Role assignment and account binding (Must)** is the isolation boundary of the whole product: "bindings are the single source of truth for scoping on every API route." Its scenarios require that binding manager M to sub-account S lets M see and trade **only** S subject to S's profile; that a second binding appears in M's scope selector *and* in server-side scoping; and that **unbinding with open positions forces an explicit choice** — leave the positions (owner takes over) or flatten first.

**US-ADMIN-003 — Risk-limit administration (Must)** adds the per-manager limits surface on the same screen (SCR-122 is listed for both in `18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26), with the hard rule that tightening a limit during an open position **never force-liquidates**: new entries are blocked, reduce-only remains available, and both owner and manager are informed. Each change is audited with old and new values.

**SCR-124 Admin: "view as" (read-only impersonation)** is listed under US-ADMIN-002/US-ADMIN-008 and audited at high severity (`admin.view_as_started|ended`).

The enforcement engines live elsewhere — `user_account_access` scoping in E09, per-account risk caps in **E39** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1: `E39 --> E42`), profiles in **E28**. This story is the owner-facing administration surface over them and the safety semantics of changing them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-122** at `/admin/users/:userId`: identity block; role selector (CMP-009 Select, options from `GET /api/v1/roles`); **account assignments** table with per-account permission level (`trade` / `read`) via CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, driven by `GET|PUT /api/v1/users/{userId}/account-access`; rule-authoring permission; live-trading permission per account; **risk-cap overrides** (CMP-138 RiskCapMeter showing the current measured value beside each limit); session list with per-session revoke (`GET /api/v1/me/sessions` equivalent admin view + `DELETE`); 2FA state with reset; and the user's own audit trail (a filtered embed of E42-S04's list).
- Role changes call `PUT /api/v1/users/{userId}/roles`; account bindings call `PUT /api/v1/users/{userId}/account-access` (full replace semantics — the UI must send the complete grant set, and shows a change summary before saving).
- **Unbind-with-open-positions flow**: before saving a grant removal, the UI calls the positions read model for the affected account; if positions are open, a blocking choice is presented — *Leave positions (owner takes over)* or *Flatten first* — with no third silent path, and the chosen option is recorded in the audit `after_state`.
- **Limit tightening flow**: on save, if the new cap is below current exposure, an explicit notice states "No positions will be closed. New entries are blocked; reduce-only actions remain available." Both the owner's confirmation and the manager's notification are produced (the manager-facing notice is rendered by E39's CMP-117 RiskLockoutBanner, consumed here).
- **SCR-124 view-as**: entry from SCR-121/SCR-122, an unmistakable persistent banner (CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner + CMP-028 Callout) naming the impersonated user, a **read-only** mode in which every state-changing control is disabled with a reason, and an always-visible Exit control. Emits audited `admin.view_as_started` / `admin.view_as_ended` at high severity.
- All saves step-up gated and wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger; audit actions `roles.grant`, `roles.revoke`, `users.access_change`, `risk.limits_changed`, `auth.mfa_reset`, `auth.session_revoked` (vocabulary per R5 on #965).
- States: loading · populated · dirty-with-change-summary · saving · conflict (412) · error · self-edit guard (owner cannot demote themselves) · impersonating.

## Out of scope
- The risk-evaluation engine, lockout behaviour and the risk dashboard SCR-071 (E39).
- Per-account profiles SCR-130..133 (E28) — linked to from here, not edited here.
- Bybit account/key management SCR-125..129 (E27).
- Writable impersonation — explicitly never built; view-as is read-only by design.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bind a manager to a sub-account
  Given manager M has no account grants
  When I grant M trade access to sub-account S and save with step-up
  Then M can see and trade only S, subject to S's profile
  And the change is audited with the full before and after grant sets

Scenario: Multiple bindings
  When I add a second sub-account grant for M
  Then both accounts appear in M's scope selector on next request
  And server-side scoping covers both, verified by M's own /me response

Scenario: Unbind with open positions
  Given M holds open positions on S
  When I remove M's grant for S
  Then the save is blocked until I choose explicitly: leave the positions (owner takes over) or flatten first
  And the chosen option is recorded in the audit entry

Scenario: Tighten a limit during an open position
  Given M's current exposure exceeds the new maximum position size
  When I save the tightened limit
  Then no position is closed
  And new entries for M are blocked while reduce-only actions remain available
  And both the owner and M are informed, and the change is audited with old and new values

Scenario: View-as is unmistakably read-only
  When I start "view as" for M
  Then a persistent banner names M and states the session is read-only
  And every state-changing control is disabled with a reason
  And admin.view_as_started is audited at high severity, and admin.view_as_ended on exit

Scenario (failure): Concurrent edit
  Given another owner session changed M's roles after I loaded the page
  When I save
  Then a 412 is surfaced as "This user changed while you were editing" with a reload action
  And my change is not applied silently
```

## Technical notes / design
- Grant editing is **replace-semantics**: `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` takes the full `grants` array. The UI computes an added/removed/changed diff purely for the confirmation summary; the payload is always complete.
- Revoked grants force-close the user's WS subscriptions with a `revoked` frame (reason `account_scope_changed`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5), which E42-T08 delivers; E42-T04's contract slice S1 replaces the older `unsubscribed` wording in `22-api-openapi.yaml`. The UI states this in the confirmation copy so the owner knows the effect is immediate.
- Open-position check before unbinding reads the positions read model for the affected account scope; if the check itself fails, the save is blocked (fail-closed) with a retry — never assumed to be zero.
- Limit tightening posts through the E39 risk-administration endpoint; the client renders the returned "effect summary" rather than predicting it locally.
- Optimistic concurrency via `If-Match`/ETag on `PATCH /users/{userId}`.
- View-as: the server issues a **read-only impersonation context**; the client marks the whole app tree with an `impersonation` provider that disables mutations at the request layer as well as visually — defence in depth, but the server remains authoritative (any mutation attempted under impersonation is rejected and audited).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: grant diff → confirmation summary; fail-closed behaviour when the open-position check errors; tightening notice copy; ETag conflict path; impersonation provider disabling every mutation hook.
- **Contract**: `/users/{userId}`, `/users/{userId}/roles`, `/users/{userId}/account-access`, `/roles`, `/permissions` against the OpenAPI schema.
- **Integration**: unbind-with-open-positions renders exactly two choices and no dismissal path.
- **E2E**: `admin-user-detail.spec.ts` — bind/unbind across two browser contexts asserting M's scope changes without a reload; view-as session asserting no mutation is possible and both audit entries exist; tighten-limit asserting no position closes.
- **Security test (with E42-X02)**: attempt a grant payload naming an account the owner does not administer → 403 + audit.
- **a11y**: axe; keyboard-only grant editing; screen-reader pass on the change summary and the unbind choice dialog.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/user.detail.json`, `account-access.two-grants.json`, `positions.open-on-S.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- This is the **isolation boundary between managers** — the highest-value target in the epic. Threats: **elevation of privilege** (granting oneself or another user access to an account); **tampering** (client-side grant forgery); **repudiation** (unattributed binding changes); **information disclosure** (view-as leaking another user's data without a record).
- Controls: server-side authority over every grant, step-up on save, replace-semantics with a full audit `before_state`/`after_state`, high-severity audit on impersonation start/end, fail-closed open-position check, and a Semgrep rule (E42-X03) asserting no admin mutation route is reachable without the audit decorator.
- Data classification: **Confidential** (account scope, risk limits) + **PII** (user identity). No secrets are rendered; 2FA reset never displays a secret.
- Mandatory `security` label per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 (touches RBAC and admin screens); Security-engineer review comment required.

## Accessibility notes
- Form sections use CMP-065 FormSection with a single `h1` per route (CMP-088 PageHeader contract).
- The grant table is a labelled table; permission level is a labelled radio/select per row, not an icon toggle.
- The unbind choice is `role="alertdialog"` with two clearly named buttons and no default destructive focus; Escape cancels the save rather than picking an option.
- Limit fields state their unit; the current measured value sits beside the limit as text.
- View-as banner is `role="status"` (persistent, not a one-shot alert) and its text — not colour — carries the impersonated username; the Exit control is the first tab stop on the page.

- Detail page ≤700 ms p95 to interactive; the embedded audit trail loads lazily after first paint.
- Grant save round-trip ≤500 ms p95; the scope change must be observable by the affected user's next request (no client cache older than the last `grants_changed` push).
- Per US-ADMIN-003's NFR, limit evaluation on the order path stays ≤5 ms p95 — owned and benchmarked by E39; this story asserts it does not add client-side work to that path.

title: Build SCR-135 audit log browser and SCR-136 event detail with integrity state
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-008 — Append-only audit log (Must)** and **US-ADMIN-009 — Audit log search and export (Must)** are the accountability backbone of a self-hosted trading terminal. US-ADMIN-008's NFR is absolute: "append-only enforced at the database level (no UPDATE/DELETE grants); entries hash-chained; retained indefinitely." US-ADMIN-009's NFR sets the bar for usability: "search over 10 million entries returns the first page in ≤2 s", with manager scope enforced server-side and exports signed and themselves audited.

`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-135 is uncompromising about the surface: "no edit or delete affordance exists anywhere — the log is append-only by design and this is stated on screen", and the integrity-failure state is "a security incident, not a UI error".

The database guarantees already exist (`21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1: `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_log`, the `audit_chain()` trigger, `audit_checkpoints`, the nightly `cv-audit-verify` job) and the writer ships with E09. This story builds the owner/viewer-facing browser over them; the query, verify and export API surface is E42-T02.

Note on role: `22-api-openapi.yaml` gives **viewers `audit:read` deliberately** — "a reviewer must be able to read the log without any write capability" — so this screen is reachable by viewer as well as owner, while US-ADMIN-009 scenario 2 requires a manager to see only their own actions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-135** at `/admin/audit`: CMP-049 Table of CMP-173 AuditRow with columns time, actor, role, action, target, environment, IP, severity, result; **CMP-174 AuditFilterBar** + CMP-047 DateRangePicker for actor, action class, subject type/id, outcome, severity, IP, date range and full-text `q`; cursor pagination at 200 rows per page; stable ordering by `id`.
- Row expansion to the **before/after diff**, rendered as a definition list with before/after labelled (a11y requirement), secrets shown as fingerprints only — never values.
- **SCR-136 Admin: audit event detail** drawer (CMP-046 Drawer): full field set (actor, role at the time, session, IP, user agent, action, target, before, after, `request_id`, environment, outcome), **correlated events** sharing the same `request_id`, links to the related order / rule version / account / user, and the raw record in a CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock with CMP-033 CopyButton and the statement "this record cannot be edited or deleted".
- **Integrity indicator**: the page states the chain-verification status from `chain_verified` on the query response and from the on-demand `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/verify`; the **integrity-failure state** is a critical banner naming the position of the break ("Audit chain verification failed at <ts> — contact security") and is treated as an incident, with no retry-as-if-transient affordance.
- **Export** (CMP-099 PrintExportBar): `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/export` over the current filter range, producing signed NDJSON via an async job polled through `GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}`; the export itself emits `audit.exported`, and redaction is preserved in the exported payload.
- **Manager scoping** honoured and *displayed*: a manager sees only entries describing their own actions, with an explicit on-screen statement that the view is scoped — enforcement is server-side (E42-T02), the client never filters for security.
- Explicit absence of mutation: no edit, delete, or "correct this entry" control exists anywhere on either screen, and the append-only guarantee plus the retention statement are rendered as page text.
- States: loading · populated · filtered-to-nothing (SCR-151 pattern) · integrity verified · integrity failure · export in progress/failed · manager-scoped · retention notice.

## Out of scope
- The audit **writer**, the hash-chain trigger and the nightly verifier job (E09 + `21-database-schema.md`); off-box checkpoint handling is verified in E43-T10.
- Query/verify/export endpoints and their indexes (E42-T02).
- The security centre SCR-137 and its posture checks (E43).
- Journal/analytics exports (E41) — unrelated surface despite also using CMP-099.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Search the log
  Given 10 million audit entries exist
  When I filter by actor, action type, subject, severity and a time range
  Then matching entries are listed with cursor pagination and stable ordering
  And the first page returns within 2 seconds

Scenario: No mutation affordance exists
  When I inspect any row, the detail drawer and the page chrome
  Then no edit, delete or correct control is present anywhere
  And the page states that the log is append-only and that entries are retained indefinitely

Scenario: Integrity verification
  When I run the integrity check
  Then the hash chain over the selected range is verified
  And a break is reported with its position as a critical banner naming it a security incident, not a UI error

Scenario: Manager scope
  Given I am signed in as a manager
  When I open the audit log
  Then I see only entries describing my own actions, enforced server-side
  And the screen states that the view is scoped to my own actions

Scenario: Export is signed and audited
  When I export the filtered set
  Then a signed NDJSON file is produced through an async job with visible progress
  And payload redaction is preserved in the exported file
  And an audit.exported entry records the range and the requesting actor

Scenario (failure): Export job fails
  Given the export job returns status failed
  Then the failure is shown with its reason and a retry action
  And no partial file is offered for download

Scenario (edge): Secret-bearing entry
  Given an entry whose before/after state referenced key material
  Then the diff renders fingerprints only and never a secret value
```

## Technical notes / design
- Query: `GET /api/v1/admin/audit?cursor&limit&actor_user_id&action&subject_type&subject_id&outcome&severity&ip&from&to&q`; response carries `items`, `chain_verified` and `meta.next_cursor`. Offset paging is never used — ordering must stay stable while new rows append at the head.
- New rows arriving during browsing are **not** spliced into the current page; a "N new entries" affordance re-queries from the head, preserving pagination stability.
- Verify: `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/verify {from_id, to_id}` → `{verified, entries_checked, first_bad_id, checked_at}`. `first_bad_id` drives a deep link to that entry.
- Export: `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/export {from, to, compress}` → `202 {job_id}`; poll `GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}` until `succeeded`, then use `result.download_url`. Poll with backoff (1 s → 5 s), never a tight loop.
- Diff rendering: `before_state`/`after_state` are JSONB; the renderer walks keys, marks added/removed/changed, and applies a redaction allowlist so any key matching the secret patterns from `04-security-program.md` renders as a fingerprint.
- Table rows are memoised and windowed at 200 rows/page (the catalogue's stated page size) — the scripting budget for SCR-144-class tables is ≤8 ms per frame.
- Error codes: `forbidden` (no `audit:read`), `validation_failed` (bad range), `rate_limited` (export abuse guard).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: filter → query-param mapping incl. repeated `action` params; cursor advance/retreat; redaction of secret-shaped keys in the diff renderer (table-driven, ≥10 key patterns); integrity-failure banner copy and its non-retry semantics; export job polling with backoff and terminal states.
- **Contract**: `/admin/audit`, `/admin/audit/verify`, `/admin/audit/export`, `/admin/jobs/{jobId}` against the OpenAPI document.
- **Integration**: manager-scoped response renders the scope statement; an unscoped fixture must not be renderable as if scoped (guard test).
- **E2E (Playwright)**: `admin-audit.spec.ts` — filter round-trip; row → detail drawer → correlated events by `request_id`; export to a completed job and a failed job; integrity-failure fixture rendering the critical banner.
- **Perf**: k6/Playwright-trace measurement of first-page latency against a 10 M-row seeded database (fixture generator in E42-Q03); filter round-trip ≤400 ms budget from the catalogue.
- **a11y**: axe on page and drawer; screen-reader pass on the diff definition list and the severity-as-text column.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/audit.page.json`, `audit.chain-broken.json`, `audit.manager-scoped.json`, `jobs.export.succeeded|failed.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **repudiation** (the log's whole purpose — any UI that appears to allow correction undermines it, hence zero mutation affordances); **information disclosure** (a diff leaking a secret or full PII — mitigated by fingerprint-only rendering and server-side redaction at write time); **tampering** (chain break surfaced loudly rather than swallowed); **elevation of privilege** (a manager reading others' entries — server-side scoping, asserted by an abuse-case test in E42-X03).
- Reading the audit log is itself audited (`audit.viewed`, `audit.record_viewed`, `audit.exported`) per SCR-136 — "so that reading the audit log is also on the record".
- Exported bundles carry a detached signature; the UI states that the file contains **Confidential** data and must be handled accordingly.
- Data classification: Confidential + PII (`actor_ip` is marked PII in `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1).

## Accessibility notes
- Table semantics with a caption; **severity and outcome are text**, never colour alone; high-severity rows are additionally marked with a text label so they remain distinguishable in greyscale.
- Diffs render as definition lists with before/after explicitly labelled (catalogue a11y requirement); the raw record sits in a `<pre>` region with an accessible copy control.
- The integrity-failure banner is `role="alert"` announced once, then persists as static text.
- Date-range picker is fully keyboard operable with typed-date entry as an alternative to the calendar grid.
- Filtered-to-nothing state follows SCR-151: heading, cause sentence, one action (clear filters).

## Performance notes
- US-ADMIN-009 NFR: first page over 10 M entries ≤2 s; SCR-135 budget: filter round-trip ≤400 ms.
- SCR-136: single-record fetch ≤300 ms; the raw payload expands lazily.
- 200 rows per page; scrolling stays under 8 ms scripting per frame (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` table budget).
- Export never blocks the UI thread — it is an async server job with progress.

## Observability
- Audit: `audit.viewed`, `audit.record_viewed {recordId}`, `audit.exported {from,to,rowCount}`, `audit.integrity_check_run {verified, firstBadId}`.
- Metrics: `cv_audit_query_latency_ms` (server), `cv_audit_export_jobs_total{result}`, `cv_audit_chain_verified` gauge (0/1) — alert-worthy per ADR-0014.
- Logs: chain-verification failures logged at `critical` and raised as a `system_events` incident, surfaced on SCR-143.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on new/changed lines; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for every new/changed component variant, including loading, empty, error and degraded states.
- [ ] `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the spec.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched routes, keyboard-only pass, one manual screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the signed-off Figma spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as `priority/*` bugs.
- [ ] security: RBAC deny-by-default verified server-side (non-owner receives 404 from the router and 403 from the API); every state-changing control wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and asserted to emit its audit entry.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded for the surface.
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E42-S01` — admin shell and re-auth gate.
- `E42-D04` — hi-fi design for SCR-135/SCR-136 incl. the integrity-failure state.
- `E42-T02` — query, verify and export endpoints with their indexes and manager scoping.

title: Build the manager onboarding wizard and trade-group/recorder governance
body:
## Context
Three Should/Must administration stories remain, and each is a thin governance layer over machinery another epic already owns — so they are deliberately grouped into one small story rather than three thin ones.

**US-ADMIN-013 — Manager onboarding workflow (Should)**: a guided flow through sub-account creation, the **48-hour key restriction**, key creation with 2FA, permission scoping, IP whitelisting, profile creation, limits and the invite; a blocked step must show the exact unlock time while the rest of the flow continues; leaving and returning resumes where you left off with completed steps marked. NFR: "the flow never stores a secret outside the encrypted store, and never displays one after entry." Screens: **SCR-017** (invited-user side) and **SCR-123** (invite), orchestrated here.

**US-ADMIN-005 — Trade-group administration (Must)**: central governance of fan-out targets on **SCR-062** — create, rename, reorder, enable, disable, and **set which users may use each group**; a disabled group disappears from ticket targets while existing positions opened through it remain fully manageable; a membership change during an open group trade keeps the **original membership snapshot**, shown in the trade detail. NFR: "group definitions are versioned so historical trades reference the version used." E28 builds SCR-062's definition surface; this story adds the admin governance controls (who may use it, enable/disable, version visibility).

**US-ADMIN-006 — Recorder & retention administration (Must)**: the requirement that recorder and retention settings live "in the admin section … so that data policy is managed in one place". E16 builds SCR-140/SCR-141 in full; this story mounts them inside the admin shell, guarantees the admin-area audit and step-up wrapping applies to their destructive paths, and links them from SCR-120.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Onboarding wizard** (`/admin/users/onboard`): a resumable stepper over the existing endpoints — create sub-account (E27) → 48-hour key restriction check → create key with 2FA (E27) → permission scoping (`PUT /users/{userId}/account-access`) → IP whitelisting (E27) → profile creation (E28) → limits (E39) → invite (`POST /api/v1/users`, SCR-123). Components: CMP-001, CMP-009, CMP-027, CMP-033, CMP-040, CMP-043, CMP-050, CMP-066, CMP-097, CMP-105.
- **Blocked-step behaviour**: when Bybit's 48-hour new-sub-account key restriction is active, the key step renders blocked with the **exact unlock timestamp** and the remaining steps stay available — the flow is not halted.
- **Resume**: wizard progress is persisted server-side against the in-progress user record (not in localStorage, so it survives a device change); returning shows completed steps marked and lands on the first incomplete step.
- **Trade-group governance on SCR-062**: enable/disable a group; rename and reorder; **who may use this group** (per-user allowlist); the version indicator with a link from a historical trade to the group version it used; and the disable confirmation stating that existing positions opened through the group remain fully manageable. Components CMP-041, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-105, CMP-123, CMP-124.
- **Recorder/retention admin integration**: SCR-140 and SCR-141 mounted at `/admin/recorder` inside CMP-087 AdminLayout; their destructive paths (purge, retention reduction) inherit the admin re-auth gate and CMP-093 audit wrapping; SCR-120's recorder and storage tiles link here; the dangerous-change preview and typed confirmation required by US-ADMIN-006 are verified to be present (implemented by E16-S03).
- Audit: `user.onboarding_started|resumed|completed`, `trade_group.enabled|disabled|renamed|reordered`, `trade_group.membership_changed`, and (verified, not re-implemented) `retention.change`, `retention.purge`.

## Out of scope
- Sub-account and API-key creation, the 48-hour restriction detection and IP whitelisting (E27).
- Per-account profile creation and the trade-group definition surface (E28).
- Risk limits (E39).
- The recorder engine, retention manager, disk budget and SCR-140/141/142 implementations (E16) — mounted, not rebuilt.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Guided steps
  When I start the manager onboarding flow
  Then it walks through sub-account creation, the 48-hour key restriction, key creation with 2FA, permission scoping, IP whitelisting, profile creation, limits and the invite
  And each completed step is marked

Scenario: Blocked step does not halt the flow
  Given the 48-hour key restriction is active for the new sub-account
  Then the key step is blocked showing the exact unlock time
  And the remaining steps continue to be available

Scenario: Resume
  Given I left the flow after the profile step
  When I return, on a different device
  Then the flow resumes at the first incomplete step with earlier steps marked complete

Scenario: Disable a trade group
  Given group G is enabled and has an open group trade
  When I disable G
  Then G disappears from ticket targets
  And the existing positions opened through G remain fully manageable

Scenario: Membership change during an open trade
  Given a group trade opened through G is still open
  When I change G's membership
  Then the open trade keeps its original membership snapshot
  And the trade detail shows which group version it used

Scenario (failure): Secret never re-displayed
  Given I entered an API secret at the key step
  When I navigate back to that step
  Then the secret is not displayed, only its fingerprint and status
  And no secret value was written outside the encrypted store

Scenario (edge): Recorder purge from the admin area
  Given I open /admin/recorder with a stale admin token
  Then the re-auth gate appears before any destructive control is reachable
  And a purge shows the impact preview and requires a typed confirmation
```

## Technical notes / design
- Wizard state is a server-side record keyed by the pending user id with `steps[] {key, status, completedAt, blockedUntil}`; the client renders from it and never infers completion locally. Resume is therefore device-independent (NFR: nothing sensitive is cached client-side).
- The 48-hour restriction is reported by E27's account read model (`restricted_until`); the wizard renders that timestamp verbatim in the viewer's locale with the UTC value in the accessible name.
- Secret handling: the key secret is posted straight to E27's import endpoint and cleared from memory on step completion; the field is `autocomplete="off"`, never rendered back, and excluded from any analytics or error payload (a test asserts the redaction).
- Trade-group governance writes go through E28's group endpoints with the group **version** bumped on membership change; open group trades reference the version they were created with, so the UI reads the snapshot from the trade, not from the live group.
- Recorder mounting is routing plus layout only — no duplicate data layer. The admin guard wraps the route; E16's components are reused unchanged.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: step-state machine incl. blocked-but-not-halting; resume targeting the first incomplete step; secret-field redaction in error/analytics payloads; group disable → removal from ticket targets while open positions persist; version-snapshot rendering.
- **Contract**: the wizard's composed calls validated against the OpenAPI document for each underlying endpoint.
- **Integration**: recorder route mounted under the admin guard — a stale token blocks destructive controls.
- **E2E**: `admin-onboarding.spec.ts` — full flow with the 48-hour restriction fixture, abandon-and-resume in a fresh context, ending with a redeemable invite; `admin-trade-groups.spec.ts` — disable with an open group trade.
- **a11y**: axe on the wizard and SCR-062 governance controls; keyboard-only completion of the whole wizard; screen-reader pass on the stepper.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/onboarding.partial.json`, `account.key-restricted.json`, `trade-groups.with-open-trade.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **key leakage** — the NFR is explicit that no secret is stored outside the encrypted store or displayed after entry; controls are direct-to-vault submission, memory clearing, redaction in logs/analytics and a regression test. **Elevation of privilege** — the wizard grants account access and limits in one flow, so every step is step-up gated and audited individually, not once at the end. **Tampering** — group membership snapshots are server-side and immutable for open trades.
- Data classification: **Secret** (API key material, handled but never rendered), **PII** (invitee email), **Confidential** (scope and limits).
- Mandatory `security` label (touches API-key handling and RBAC grants); Security-engineer review comment required.

## Accessibility notes
- The wizard is a labelled stepper with `aria-current="step"`; each step announces its status; a blocked step states *why* and *until when* in text.
- Progress is never only a graphic — completed/blocked/current are words.
- The secret field has a visible label, a format hint, and an explicit statement that it will not be shown again.
- Group governance controls are named with their scope ("Disable trade group G — removes it from ticket targets"), never icon-only.
- Reorder is operable by keyboard (move-up/move-down buttons), not drag-only.

## Performance notes
- Each wizard step's round-trip ≤500 ms p95; step transitions never re-fetch the whole flow, only the changed step.
- Mounting SCR-140/141 adds no additional data fetching beyond E16's existing hooks — asserted by a network-call count test.
- The group list is small by construction (a handful of groups); no virtualisation, with the reason recorded in a comment.

## Observability
- Audit: `user.onboarding_started|resumed|completed`, `trade_group.enabled|disabled|renamed|reordered`, `trade_group.membership_changed` (with the version before/after); verified pass-through of `recorder.*` and `retention.*` from E16.
- Analytics: `admin.onboarding_step_completed {step, durationMs}`, `admin.onboarding_abandoned {step}` — used to find steps that block owners.
- Metrics: `cv_admin_onboarding_completions_total`, `cv_trade_group_state_changes_total{action}`.

- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.

- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the signed-off Figma spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as `priority/*` bugs.
- [ ] security: RBAC deny-by-default verified server-side (non-owner receives 404 from the router and 403 from the API); every state-changing control wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and asserted to emit its audit entry.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.

## Dependencies

title: Build the admin statechart inspector screen: machine list, state diagram, event timeline, latch acknowledge
body:
## Context
Every catalogue lifecycle is built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` (ADR-0016 Accepted). Operators need one screen to see it: which machines are running, what state each is in, its transition history, and - critically - the place to acknowledge a `chain_trips`-latched machine so it can rejoin the order path (`29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4, the `chain_trips` latch note).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Machine list view sourced from `E42-T07`'s `GET /admin/statecharts`: kind, current state, `machine_hash`, `chain_trips`, `dropped_receipts`, deferred depth; degraded rows (`chain_trips > 0`) visually distinct and filterable.
- State diagram rendered from the Stately-compatible JSON export (`E42-T07` export endpoint), with the current state highlighted.
- Event timeline from `machine_events` (the `CvAuditPlugin` write-ahead audit trail, E50-T60): transitions, guard refusals, dropped-receipt events, in chronological order per machine.
- **Latch-acknowledge action**: an operator control that clears a `chain_trips` latch, gated by step-up re-auth (`E09-S04`'s elevation, action class `killswitch`-equivalent severity) and written to the audit trail with actor, machine, and prior `chain_trips` count.

## Out of scope
- The read API itself and RBAC on it - **E42-T07**.
- Any change to how `chain_trips` is incremented or to the degraded-admission behaviour - that is the B-chart/gateway logic (`statechart/gateway.py`), not this screen.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: See a degraded machine
  Given a machine restored with chain_trips > 0
  When I open the inspector
  Then it is listed as degraded with its chain_trips and dropped_receipts counts visible

Scenario: Acknowledge a latch
  Given I am viewing a degraded machine
  When I acknowledge it with step-up re-auth
  Then the latch clears, the machine resumes serving order-path commands, and the acknowledgement is audited with my identity

Scenario: Acknowledge without elevation is refused
  Given I have not completed step-up recently
  When I attempt to acknowledge a latch
  Then the server refuses it and I am prompted for step-up

Scenario: State diagram matches the running chart
  Given a machine of a given machine_hash
  When I view its diagram
  Then it matches the Stately export for that hash and highlights the current state
```

## Technical notes / design
The screen consumes `E42-T07`'s read API for the list/detail/export and `E17-T08`'s `machines.{entity}.state` topic for live updates while the screen is open; it never opens a bespoke polling loop against the interpreter. The acknowledge action calls a dedicated admin write route (paired with `E42-T07`) that is itself gated by the E09-S04 step-up elevation and goes through `statechart/gateway.py` (`cv_re_mint`-style payload-only wrapper, CV-C68 containment) rather than touching the interpreter directly. Built directly on the library via the factory/registry/plugin/gateway surface: no hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime.

## Test plan
Unit: degraded-row filter, diagram highlight logic. Contract: acknowledge route against `22-api-openapi.yaml`, step-up gate enforced. Integration: end-to-end latch-and-acknowledge against a machine seeded with `chain_trips > 0`. E2E: list -> detail -> diagram -> timeline -> acknowledge with step-up, refusal without step-up. a11y: axe-core plus a manual pass on the diagram and timeline (non-visual equivalents for state/edges).

## Security notes
The acknowledge action is a dangerous action per the `E09-S04` permission registry (`is_dangerous`); it is audited at high severity with actor, machine, and prior `chain_trips` count, and it never reveals context values not already redacted by the read API.

## Accessibility notes
The state diagram and event timeline provide a non-visual equivalent (a text list of states/edges and a table for the timeline) so the screen is usable without the rendered diagram; the acknowledge control has an explicit accessible name naming the machine, not a generic "Confirm".

## Performance notes
Diagram and timeline are read from the E42-T07 API; live updates ride the existing `E17-T08` topic rather than a per-screen poll.

## Observability
`cv_machine_latch_acknowledged_total`, reusing the `cv_machine_*` families from `E50-T60`.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2; Security engineer sign-off on the acknowledge gate; design-qa and QA sign-off absorbed into E42-D05/E42-Q04 per the plan's one-line Scope additions.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E42-T07**, **E42-S01** and **E09-S04**.

## Branch
`feat/e42-statechart-inspector-screen`

## References
`docs/plan/29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4 (chain_trips latch), §4d; `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md`; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.

title: Wireframe to hi-fi: SCR-137 security centre and the Live-enablement gate
body:
## Context
SCR-137 `Admin: security centre` (`/admin/security`) is the screen on which the Owner decides whether this installation is safe enough to touch live money. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-137 specifies it as: failed-login trends, active sessions across all users, step-up usage, key-policy compliance, the dependency/vulnerability summary from the last scan, **the pen-test status gate for Live enablement**, and links to the security program doc. Its three states are *compliant*, *findings outstanding (count by severity)* and *Live enablement blocked* ("Live trading stays disabled until the pen-test sign-off is recorded").

It serves two user stories: **US-ADMIN-010 Security posture panel** (Must) and **US-ADMIN-012 Live-trading enablement gate** (Must), both in `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 26. US-ADMIN-010's NFR is decisive for the design: *"every check is machine-evaluated, not a manual checklist"* - so the screen must never look like a to-do list the Owner can tick. US-ADMIN-012 requires that when the gate is closed it *"lists exactly which items are outstanding"*, and that opening it needs step-up authentication plus typed confirmation.

This is a **net-new interaction** (a gated, evidence-bearing control that refuses to be operated), so it carries a UX-research component: a short structured walkthrough with the Owner persona (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) to establish what evidence the Owner actually needs to feel entitled to flip the switch.

Design must be Done by end of Sprint 18 so that E43-S01 (Sprint 20) satisfies the design-ahead rule in `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **UX research note** (1-2 pages): 3 structured questions to the Owner persona - what evidence is required before enabling live, what "outstanding" must say to be actionable, what the emergency re-disable must feel like. Findings recorded in the ticket and reflected in the wireframes.
- **Wireframes then hi-fi in Figma** for SCR-137 covering all three states (`compliant`, `findings outstanding`, `Live enablement blocked`), plus: loading, partially-stale (one check's result older than its schedule), and check-failed-to-run.
- **Finding categories drawn** exactly as SCR-137's sign-off checklist demands: keys without allowlist, overdue rotations, users without 2FA, stale sessions, failed-login spikes, permission anomalies, withdrawal permission detected.
- **Severity as text**, never colour alone; remediation action per finding as a named button; dismiss-with-reason path; all-clear state; last-scan timestamp with freshness.
- **Live-enablement gate block**: the four gate items from `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` section 6 rendered as machine-checked vs attested rows, each showing evidence, attester and date; disabled-control treatment that explains *why* rather than merely greying out; the step-up + typed-confirmation enable dialog (CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger); the **emergency re-disable** path and its consequence copy ("no new live orders are accepted; existing positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode").
- Gate-blocked states of the two hosting surfaces: **SCR-010 App shell** live badge and **SCR-074 Environment switcher** (Live option present but unselectable with the reason inline).
- Components used: CMP-028 Callout/Banner, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-050 Card, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-043 Dialog.
- Redline/spec page with tokens, spacing, type ramp and motion notes (severity escalation must not animate distractingly; reduced-motion honoured).

## Out of scope
- SCR-128 and SCR-136 (E43-D02); the a11y review and design QA (E43-D03); any implementation.
- The environment-separation visual language (live-mode colour, badge, confirm-on-every-order) - that is **E44**'s design.
- Mobile/Android layouts - out of scope for the plan.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Blocked gate explains itself
  Given at least one Live-enablement gate item is outstanding
  When the Owner views the hi-fi SCR-137 gate block
  Then each outstanding item is named with what is missing and what action resolves it
  And the enable control is rendered disabled with the reason adjacent to it, not only as a tooltip

Scenario: No colour-only severity
  Given a design reviewer inspects any finding row in greyscale
  Then the severity, the affected object and the remediation action are all readable as text

Scenario: Machine-evaluated, not a checklist
  Given the Owner views the posture section
  Then every check displays its own last-evaluated timestamp and its source, and no check is presented as something the Owner ticks manually
  And attested (non-machine-checkable) items are visually distinct and show the attester name and date

Scenario: Emergency re-disable is reachable and unambiguous
  Given Live is enabled
  Then the design shows a re-disable control with copy stating that new live orders stop while open positions stay manageable in reduce-only mode
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data source: `GET /api/v1/admin/security/summary` returning the `SecuritySummary` schema (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`): key ages and expiry, IP-whitelist drift, withdrawal-permission verification results, failed-login and denied-request counts, MFA enrolment coverage, last audit-chain verification. **The schema never includes secret material** - the design must not invent a field that would require it.
- Findings are computed server-side on a schedule and cached; a manual re-scan is an explicit action with progress, never an automatic refresh (SCR-137 performance note) - the design needs an in-progress treatment for re-scan.
- Audit events the design must visibly account for: `security.centre_viewed`, `security.rescan_requested` (analytics) and `security.finding_dismissed {findingId, reason}` (audited) - the dismiss dialog must collect a reason.

## Test plan
Design-stage verification only: greyscale review; Figma prototype walkthrough of blocked -> attested -> enabled -> re-disabled; contrast check of all tokens used; a state-matrix review against SCR-137's documented states; a copy review confirming no screen renders secret material.

## Security notes
Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 5.7 (admin screens): information disclosure through a well-meaning UI, and elevation through a control that looks advisory but is authoritative. Controls the design must express: step-up re-authentication (SR-025) before enabling live, typed confirmation, audited dismissal with a reason. Data classification: metadata about secrets, never secrets. Security review label required - the Security engineer signs off the gate block.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). Headings per section; each finding states risk, affected object and remediation as a named button; severity conveyed in text; the disabled enable-control must be programmatically described (`aria-describedby` pointing at the reason) rather than merely inert; focus order runs posture -> findings -> gate; the enable dialog traps focus and returns it on close; reduced-motion respected.

## Performance notes
N/A for design output, except that the design must not require per-finding live polling: the specified model is scheduled server-side computation plus an explicit re-scan.

## Observability
Design must leave room for a "last evaluated" line per check and a global "last full scan" timestamp so the observability data has somewhere to land.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] UX research note recorded on the ticket with the Owner's answers.
- [ ] Wireframes and hi-fi published in Figma and linked here; all documented states covered.
- [ ] SCR-137's design sign-off acceptance checklist in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` fully satisfied, each box ticked in a review comment.
- [ ] Contrast and greyscale checks passed.
- [ ] Sign-off: Chief Design Officer (or delegate) **and** Security engineer, recorded as comments.
- [ ] Status Done by end of Sprint 18 so the design-ahead rule holds for E43-S01.

title: Hi-fi SCR-128 key health panel and SCR-136 audit event detail hardening states
body:
## Context
Two existing admin surfaces gain states in E43 because the posture engine (E43-S02) starts producing verdicts they must display.

**SCR-128 Admin: key health & secrets policy panel** (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`) shows key ages against policy, last successful use, failure counts, rate-limit consumption per UID, envelope-encryption status (KEK id, last re-wrap), and the standing statement that secrets are never displayed, exported or logged. E43 adds the *verified-against-Bybit* dimension: the withdrawal-permission verification result and the IP-allowlist drift result now arrive from `SecuritySummary` rather than from app belief - R4 exit criterion 2 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 8.3 requires the audit record to carry *"the Bybit-reported scopes, not just the app's belief about them"*.

**SCR-136 Admin: audit event detail** gains the integrity dimension: when the hash-chain verification (SR-063) reports a break, the detail view must show the position of the break and state plainly that the record cannot be edited or deleted. SCR-135/SCR-136's sign-off checklist already requires the "integrity failure state designed" box.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-128 hi-fi additions**: per-key rows carrying withdrawal-permission verdict (verified-off / verified-on / unverifiable, each with the verification timestamp and source), IP-allowlist state incl. **drift** ("allowlist no longer contains the current egress IP" - see OQ-05 in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` section 16.1a), key age vs the 90-day rotation policy (SR-030 family) with an overdue state, and the `mark as compromised` emergency action with its immediate effect stated (key disabled, orders halted for that account).
- The SCR-128 checklist items must all be drawn: per-key age, permissions, allowlist and rotation-due state; the secrets-at-rest policy statement (where keys live, how they are encrypted, who can read them); the overdue-rotation state; and a copy review proving **no secret material is rendered anywhere**.
- **SCR-136 hi-fi additions**: the hash-chain integrity banner (verified at <timestamp> / **break detected at sequence N**), the "this record cannot be edited or deleted" statement, and before/after diff rendering for a security-relevant change (role change, flag change, key change) with redaction visibly applied.
- **Design-system contributions**: a `VerificationVerdict` variant set for CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge (`verified-off`, `verified-on`, `unverifiable`, `stale`) and a `severity` text-first variant set for CMP-028 Callout/Banner, both contributed to `packages/ui` documentation with Storybook stories specified.
- Motion spec: verdict changes fade only; no attention-grabbing pulsing on a security screen; reduced-motion honoured.

## Out of scope
- SCR-137 (E43-D01); a11y review and design QA (E43-D03); implementation.
- Key rotation *flow* design (SCR-127, owned by E27); the audit search screen SCR-135 list layout (owned by E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: App belief and exchange truth are visually distinct
  Given a key whose withdrawal permission has been verified against Bybit
  Then the badge states that the verdict came from the exchange and when
  And a key whose verification has not run, or failed, renders as "unverifiable" rather than as safe

Scenario: Allowlist drift is surfaced, not hidden
  Given the deployment's egress IP is no longer in a key's allowlist
  Then SCR-128 shows a drift state naming the current egress IP and the remediation step

Scenario: Integrity break is unmissable and precise
  Given the audit hash chain fails verification at sequence N
  Then SCR-136 shows a persistent banner naming sequence N as the break position, in text
  And the banner does not offer any control that would mutate the record

Scenario: No secret material anywhere
  Given a copy review of every SCR-128 and SCR-136 state
  Then no state renders an API secret, session token, TOTP seed or KEK material, masked or otherwise
```

## Technical notes / design
- Fields come from `SecuritySummary` (`GET /api/v1/admin/security/summary`) and from `audit_log` / `audit_checkpoints` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`). Verification results are cached server-side for 60 s; the panel never calls the exchange from the browser (SCR-128 performance note; SR-119 forbids any exchange contact from the renderer).
- Audited events this design must accommodate: `admin.secrets_policy_changed {key, before, after}` and `admin.key_marked_compromised` (both high severity), `audit.record_viewed {recordId}` and `audit.record_exported` - reading the audit log is itself audited, so the design must not hide that fact from the user.

## Test plan
Greyscale review; state-matrix review against SCR-128/SCR-136 documented states; contrast checks; Storybook story list agreed with the design-system team; copy review for secret leakage.

## Security notes
Threats: `04-security-program.md` section 5.1 (key material) and section 5.7 (admin screens) - information disclosure through UI, and false assurance (a UI that shows "safe" when the check never ran). Control: `unverifiable` is a first-class state, never collapsed into "ok". SR-069 forbids secrets in audit payloads; the design mirrors that by rendering redaction explicitly.

## Accessibility notes
Table of keys with age, permissions, allowlist state and next-rotation-due date, plus a policy section written as plain sentences; warnings are text with an icon (SCR-128 a11y note). Badges must have accessible names that include the verdict word. The integrity banner is `role="status"` for non-blocking updates and reachable in the tab order.

## Performance notes
N/A (design). The design must not require per-row live polling; the panel is a 60 s server-cached read.

## Observability
Leaves space for "verified at" timestamps per key and "chain verified at" on SCR-136, which back the `cv_audit_chain_verify_status` metric.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Hi-fi published in Figma and linked; all new states covered.
- [ ] SCR-128 and SCR-136 sign-off checklists in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` ticked in a review comment.
- [ ] Design-system contributions accepted by the design-system team with Storybook stories specified in `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` for CMP-175 and CMP-028.
- [ ] Contrast/greyscale checks passed; copy review recorded.

title: Wireframe the live-enablement gate, hardened switch and live visual language
body:
## Context
The design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, team & cadence) requires design Done ≥2 sprints before the consuming FE story. E44's frontend stories land in **S20-S21**, so wireframes run in **S18**.

E44 changes four existing surfaces rather than inventing new ones, so this is a *targeted* wireframe pass, not a new-product discovery: SCR-145 (Admin: feature flags) gains a blocked/unblocked gate treatment for `trading.live_enabled`; SCR-137 (Admin: security centre) gains the four-item gate checklist; SCR-074 (Environment switcher) gains the hardened live path; SCR-010/SCR-075 gain the pervasive live chrome; SCR-122 (Admin: user detail) gains the live-eligibility control.

The one genuinely new interaction is the **gate checklist**: a machine-checked/attested mixed list where some items are computed (key-permission audit results, kill-switch test record) and some are human attestations (pen-test sign-off, Owner authorisation), per US-ADMIN-012's NFR ("criteria are machine-checked where possible and explicitly attested where not, with the attester and date recorded"). A short research touch with the Owner is warranted for that item only.

Refs: `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-PAPER-002/003/007, US-ADMIN-010/012; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010, SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-122, SCR-137, SCR-145; `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §6.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Research touch (1 session, 45 min, with the Owner)** on the gate checklist only: which of the four items they expect to be automatic, what evidence they want to see attached, and what "blocked" should say when several items are outstanding. Written as 3-5 numbered findings mapped to frames.
- **Lo-fi wireframes** in Figma page `CandleViewer / E44 Live gating`, covering every state declared in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` for each screen:

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` SS3.2 makes design QA a default-on gate for net-new UI stories: "built screen compared against design spec (spacing/tokens/type/color/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer; discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bug with `priority/*` set." Where a state cannot be produced by normal interaction, it is forced with a fixture, and the fixture is committed.
- Token audit of the built code: spacing, type scale, colour, radius and elevation come from tokens, with no raw values - checked by inspecting computed styles, not by eye.
- Copy verification against the copy deck, including that server-supplied strings are rendered verbatim and that every error code maps to the agreed string.
- Motion verification including a `prefers-reduced-motion` pass, and confirmation that preview numbers and the worked example do not tween.
- Focus-order and focus-preservation verification against the pack's diagrams, including that a WS-driven update never steals focus.
- Contrast spot-checks on the built screens in both themes.
- Discrepancy log, each item either fixed within the epic or filed as a Bug with a priority and an owner.
- A sign-off comment recording the result per screen.

Functional testing (E28-Q01..Q05); the accessibility audit proper (E28-Q04) - this pass checks design conformance and flags a11y regressions it happens to see, rather than replacing the audit.

## Acceptance criteria
- All six surfaces reviewed in both themes and both densities, with a per-screen verdict recorded.
- Every state in the pack has been observed in the build, with a committed fixture for any state that needed forcing.
- The token audit finds no raw values; any found are fixed, not waived.
- The reduced-motion pass is clean and the no-tweening rule holds for every numeric display.
- Discrepancies are all either fixed or filed with a priority, and none of the open ones is P0 or P1.
- Sign-off comment posted by a designer or a design-system-trained reviewer, and referenced by E28-S01..S04 and by the epic.

## Technical notes / design
Review runs against the staging build on the R3 demo environment with a seeded fixture set: six accounts, four profiles including one with an empty allow-list, two trade groups including one with a failing key self-check, and one account holding an open position so the matrix's locked cell is reachable. The comparison itself is the test. Evidence is screenshots per screen and state, attached to the ticket; the token audit is evidenced by computed-style dumps rather than screenshots.

A missing step-up prompt is a P0 discrepancy, not a cosmetic one, and is escalated to E28-X02 rather than merely logged.

Focus rings, focus order, disabled-control reasons, accessible names on matrix cells and bulk actions, and live-region behaviour are all checked against the pack. Any regression is filed with `a11y` and fed to E28-Q04. The reduced-motion pass is part of this ticket.

## Performance notes
The reviewer confirms the built screens meet their stated budgets under the fixture load - SCR-133's grid render, SCR-062's grid scripting time and SCR-061's preview latency - using the browser performance panel, and files a `perf`-labelled Bug for any breach.

## Observability
The reviewer confirms that the analytics and audit events listed in the pack are actually emitted, by observing them in the dev tools network log and the audit browser.

title: Audit accessibility and run exploratory charters across the six profile and group screens
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI plus manual screen-reader passes, and the R3 a11y gate is explicit about keyboard operability of trading surfaces. E28's two grids are the hard cases: SCR-133's virtualised accounts x ~400 symbols matrix of checkboxes, and SCR-062's virtualised group grid with nested per-leg tables. E28-D05 specified how these should behave; this ticket verifies that the built code does.

Alongside the audit, the epic's exploratory charters from E28-Q01 are executed - scripted tests confirm what was anticipated, exploratory sessions find what was not.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated scans on SCR-130, SCR-131, SCR-132, SCR-133, SCR-062 and SCR-061-preview, in both themes, in every reachable state, wired as a CI check.
- Manual screen-reader passes with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS covering: matrix cell names combining account and symbol; the denied-and-locked cell's reason; bulk action names and their scope; the readiness strip's live-region announcement; the preview table's row statuses and exclusion reasons; the send button's account count; disabled-control reasons including "capped by profile"; the safety notice's non-removable framing; and the step-up dialog's focus trap and return focus.
- Keyboard-only completion of every task in the epic: create a profile, apply a template, bulk-edit the matrix, create a group, produce a preview, apply and reset an override - with zero mouse use and no keyboard traps.
- Focus-preservation verification under live updates: with a WS-driven readiness change and a preview refresh in flight, focus must not move - tested deliberately, since it is the failure mode most likely to ship.
- Text scaling at 200% and zoom at 125% on both grids, with screenshots.
- Contrast verification on the built screens in both themes against the E28-D05 measurements.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` verification.
- Execution of the four exploratory charters from E28-Q01, 90 minutes each, with session notes, and an additional charter "profiles and groups with a screen reader" run by a QA engineer experienced with assistive technology.
- Findings filed with severity and an owner; Critical and High findings fixed inside the epic.

## Out of scope
Design conformance review (E28-D07); functional regression (E28-Q05); load and chaos (E28-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
- axe-core is clean (zero violations at serious or critical severity) on all six surfaces in both themes in every reachable state, and the scan runs in CI.
- Manual screen-reader passes completed on both NVDA and VoiceOver, with notes per surface.
- Every task in the epic is completable keyboard-only, evidenced by a recording, with no traps.
- Focus is verifiably preserved across a WS update and a preview refresh.
- 200% text scaling and 125% zoom leave both grids usable, evidenced by screenshots.
- All five exploratory charters executed with session notes and a debrief.
- No Critical or High a11y finding remains open at epic close; Medium and Low findings are filed with owners.

## Technical notes / design
Virtualised grids are the audit's centre of gravity: a screen reader must report a sane row and column count, and navigating beyond the rendered window must load and announce correctly rather than silently ending the table. Both are explicitly tested against the approach E28-D05 chose.

The preview surface is audited while actively updating, not in a frozen state, because the announcement-rate cap and the focus-preservation rule can only fail under motion.

## Test plan
This ticket is the audit. Evidence: axe reports per screen and state, screen-reader session recordings, keyboard-only task recordings, zoom and scaling screenshots, contrast measurements and exploratory session notes - all attached.

## Security notes
The audit confirms that accessible paths do not weaken safety controls: the step-up prompt is a real gate for keyboard and screen-reader users; the typed acknowledgement for an aggressive template on a live account is not reducible to a single keypress; and the native-SL floor is announced as immutable policy rather than as a control that might be enabled with more permissions. Any accessible bypass of a control is a security finding and is escalated to E28-X02.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility verification for the epic and covers WCAG 2.2 AA including 2.4.11 focus appearance, 2.5.8 target size, 3.2.6 consistent help and 3.3.7 redundant entry - the last being relevant to the repeated step-up prompts across profile, template and matrix saves.

## Performance notes
Screen-reader performance on the virtualised matrix is itself a finding class: if navigating the grid with a screen reader is unusably slow at ~400 columns, that is filed as a P1 even when the visual render meets its 600 ms budget.

## Observability
Findings are tracked in the QA dashboard by severity and surface; the axe-core CI check publishes its violation count as a trend so a slow regression is visible before it becomes a gate failure.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario of the covered stories is mapped to an executed test case with a pass/fail result recorded on the story.
- [ ] Defects raised with `priority/*`, reproduction steps, environment and evidence; P0/P1 defects closed before the epic is Done.
- [ ] Automated suites run in CI on the R3 demo environment and are green on three consecutive runs (no flakes).
- [ ] Coverage of the epic's acceptance criteria reported in the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Results and residual risk summarised on E28-Q05 and referenced by the epic ticket.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-S02** and **E28-S04** (the last screens to land) and by **E28-D05** (the specification being verified). Findings feed **E28-Q05** and, if a control is bypassable, **E28-X02**.

## Branch
`test/e28-a11y-exploratory` - evidence and axe configuration committed.

## References
