title: Assemble the E28 regression pack and record QA sign-off for the epic
body:
## Context
The Epic DoD requires "QA sign-off: an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA". E28 is also the epic that every later trading epic builds on: E30, E34, E35, E39 and E41 all consume its profiles, its sizer and its groups. A regression pack that outlives this epic is therefore worth more than the sign-off itself - it is the net that catches E34 or E35 quietly changing a sized quantity.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Regression pack at `qa/regression/e28/` selecting the highest-value cases from E28-Q01's plan: the safety invariants (native SL cannot be disabled by any path; a non-allowed symbol is refused by the API; every risk cap holds; an override cannot widen a cap), the ten independently-recomputed golden sizing vectors, the group guards (mixed environment, empty intersection, minimum one member), and the preview's read-only property.
- Tagging of these cases so they run on every change to `candleviewer/profiles`, `candleviewer/oms/groups` and the consuming epics' paths - not only inside E28.
- A full epic-level regression run against the R3 staging build with all E28 stories merged, executed end to end with results recorded per case.
- Cross-epic smoke: confirm that a profile change is reflected in the order path (E29), in the preview, and in the audit browser (E42 when available), so the epic's contract holds outside its own boundary.
- Defect triage summary: every defect found during the epic with its status; a written statement that no P0 or P1 remains open against E28's scope.
- Consolidation of results from E28-Q02 (E2E), E28-Q03 (perf and chaos), E28-Q04 (a11y and exploratory) and E28-X03 (abuse cases) into one epic report.
- Residual-risk statement naming what was not tested and why, with each item either accepted by the Owner or turned into a follow-up ticket.
- The QA sign-off comment on the epic ticket.

## Out of scope
New feature testing (covered by the earlier Q tickets); the R3 train-level soak `q09` and the PRR (`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`).

## Acceptance criteria
- The regression pack exists, runs green against the staging build, and completes within 20 minutes so it is cheap enough to run often.
- The safety cases are tagged to run on changes in the consuming epics' paths, and that wiring is demonstrated by a deliberate trial run from an E34 branch.
- The full epic-level run is executed with per-case results recorded.
- Cross-epic smoke passes for the profile-change-to-order-path contract.
- Zero P0 or P1 defects remain open against E28's scope, stated explicitly.
- The consolidated report exists and is linked from the epic; the residual-risk statement is accepted by the Owner.
- The QA sign-off comment is posted on the epic.

## Technical notes / design
Selection criterion for the pack is blast radius, not coverage percentage: a case earns its place if its failure would produce a wrongly-sized or unprotected order. Cases that merely confirm UI text are left in the E2E suite and out of the regression pack, so the pack stays fast enough to run on unrelated changes.

The golden vectors are included by value, not by reference to the engineering fixture, so a change to the engineering fixture cannot silently change the expected answer - a divergence fails the pack loudly.

## Test plan
The pack is the test. Its health is measured by runtime and flake rate; a case that flakes is fixed or removed, never retried, because a flaky safety test is worse than no safety test - it trains people to ignore a red.

## Security notes
The pack includes the four abuse cases from E28-X03 that map to SR-052, SR-053, SR-054 and SR-056, so the security controls are re-verified on every subsequent change to the sizing and fan-out paths rather than only once at review time. The residual-risk statement is co-signed by the Security engineer where a security control is not fully automated.

## Accessibility notes
The pack includes the axe-core scan on the six surfaces so an a11y regression from a later epic is caught; the deeper manual passes remain in E28-Q04 and are re-run per release rather than per change.

## Performance notes
The pack includes the guard and preview micro-benchmarks with their regression thresholds, so a performance regression introduced by a consuming epic fails there rather than in a release gate.

## Observability
The consolidated report records the metric values observed at sign-off as a baseline, so later drift is measurable against a known-good point rather than against memory.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/plans/e28/` (plans, charters) and `tests/e2e/e28/` (automation), reviewed by the second QA/SDET.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario of the covered stories is mapped to an executed test case with a pass/fail result recorded on the story.

- [ ] Automated suites run in CI on the R3 demo environment and are green on three consecutive runs (no flakes).
- [ ] Coverage of the epic's acceptance criteria reported in the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Results and residual risk summarised on E28-Q05 and referenced by the epic ticket.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-Q02**, **E28-Q03**, **E28-Q04** and **E28-S05** (the last story to merge). Consumes abuse-case results from **E28-X03**. Its sign-off is required by the epic DoD and by the R3 PRR.

`test/e28-regression-pack` - pack and report committed.

title: Apply audited per-trade profile overrides that can narrow but never widen a risk cap
body:
## Context
Covers **US-PROF-008** ("Per-trade profile overrides", Should) across **SCR-061** (the per-row override in the fan-out preview), **SCR-114** (Trading defaults settings, where the user's own defaults are shown against the profile ceiling) and **SCR-132**. The story's three invariants are fixed and non-negotiable: an override "never widens a hard risk cap"; "the control is disabled with 'capped by profile'" when it would; and "given the ticket is submitted or cancelled, the override resets to the profile default for the next ticket". Its NFR adds: "each override is audited and journal-tagged".

The exact field-by-field rule set was the open question resolved by **E28-K01**, whose ADR-0016 this Story implements. The safety floor was fixed before that spike ran and does not depend on its outcome: no override may widen `max_position_notional`, `max_daily_loss`, `max_open_positions`, `max_leverage_cap`, the allowed-symbol set, or `require_native_sl`.

SCR-114 states the related rule for user defaults: "user defaults can never exceed the per-account profile limits set by the owner - the section shows each limit inline as a ceiling ('Your profile caps leverage at 10x')."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Override model and client state: a per-ticket override map applied on top of the effective profile, cleared on submit and on cancel, never persisted across tickets (US-PROF-008 scenario 3).
- Overridable-field enforcement per ADR-0016's decision table, implemented as data (a declarative table) rather than scattered conditionals, so the classification is auditable in one place and unit-tested field by field.
- Narrowing-only semantics: an override may reduce size, reduce leverage or tighten a stop; any attempt to widen is refused. Controls that could only widen are rendered **disabled with the reason "capped by profile"** (US-PROF-008 scenario 2) rather than allowed and then rejected.
- Server-side re-validation: the override travels as a hint on the preview and submit payloads and is re-derived and clamped by **E28-T04**'s guard and **E28-T03**'s sizer; a widening hint is clamped, recorded and reported back, never honoured.
- Override indication: an overridden row or field is visibly exceptional - a text marker naming what was overridden and its original value, per SCR-061 ("override is visibly exceptional" on the sign-off checklist).
- Audit and journal tagging: `tradegroup.row_overridden` and an order-level override tag carried into the journal so the trade is later identifiable as an override (US-PROF-008 NFR; **E41** consumes the tag).
- **SCR-114** ceiling display: each trading-default control shows its profile ceiling inline and refuses a value above it with the profile's wording.
- Reset affordance: "reset to profile default" per field and for the whole ticket, and an automatic reset on submit or cancel with a confirmation-free, announced transition.
- Mid-ticket profile-change behaviour exactly as decided in ADR-0016 (re-price, review state or block), implemented as specified there.

## Out of scope
Changing the profile itself (E28-S01); the rule engine's interaction with overrides (**E35**); journal analytics over override outcomes (**E41**); the submit path (**E34**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Allowed override
  Given the profile permits overriding size within its risk cap
  When I raise size for this ticket only, to a value still inside the cap
  Then the override applies to this order only and is recorded in the journal as an override

Scenario: Forbidden override is disabled, not rejected late
  When I try to raise leverage above the profile cap
  Then the control is disabled with "capped by profile" and never accepts the value in the first place

Scenario: Override expiry
  Given the ticket is submitted or cancelled
  Then the override resets to the profile default for the next ticket, and the reset is announced

Scenario: A crafted widening hint is clamped server-side
  When a request carries an override widening max position notional
  Then the server clamps to the profile cap, proceeds with the clamped value, records the clamp, and audits the attempt

Scenario: Every field is classified
  Given the override decision table from ADR-0016
  Then every field of AccountProfile has exactly one classification, and a unit test fails if a new field is added without one

Scenario: Overridden values are visibly exceptional
  Given a row's quantity is overridden
  Then the row states that it is overridden and names the original computed value

Scenario: Narrowing is always allowed
  When I reduce size, reduce leverage or tighten the stop
  Then the override is accepted, because it reduces risk

Scenario: Trading defaults cannot exceed the profile ceiling
  Given my profile caps leverage at 10x
  When I set a personal default of 20x in trading defaults
  Then it is refused with "Your profile caps leverage at 10x" and the ceiling is shown inline

Scenario: Mid-ticket profile change
  Given the owner edits the profile while my ticket is open
  Then the behaviour decided in ADR-0016 occurs, the ticket never silently uses stale sizing, and the change is surfaced within 2 seconds
```

## Technical notes / design
The decision table is a single declarative structure (`OVERRIDE_POLICY: dict[field, Literal["free","narrow_only","never"]]`) shared between the frontend (for control enablement) and the backend (for clamping) via the generated schema, so the two can never disagree. A test enumerates `AccountProfile.model_fields` and fails if any field is missing from the table - which is how a future field cannot silently become overridable.

"Narrowing" is defined per field with an explicit comparator rather than a generic less-than, because tightening a stop means moving it *closer* to entry while reducing size means a *smaller* number - the direction of safety differs by field and is encoded per entry.

Override state lives in the ticket's local store with an explicit lifetime, cleared by the same reducer that handles submit-success and cancel, so there is exactly one code path that can clear it and one that can set it.

The server treats an override as an upper-bound hint on the sizer's input, never as a replacement for the profile - the sizer signature is unchanged (E28-T03), and the clamp is recorded in the leg's explanation object.

## Test plan
Unit (frontend): control enablement per classification; narrowing comparator per field; override lifetime across submit and cancel; ceiling display in SCR-114; overridden-row marker.
Unit (backend): clamping of a widening hint for every `narrow_only` field; rejection for every `never` field; the field-coverage test over the decision table.
Contract: the override payload shape on preview and submit against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
Integration: override applied end to end through preview, with the audit row and the journal tag asserted.
Security/abuse (feeds E28-X03): crafted payloads widening each protected cap, each asserting a clamp plus an audit row and no widened order.
E2E (E28-Q02): override size within the cap, submit, and confirm the next ticket starts from the profile default.
A11y: axe-core clean; screen-reader pass on the disabled control's reason and on the reset announcement.
Coverage >=90% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
This is the epic's most direct privilege-escalation surface: an override that widens a cap defeats SR-052, SR-053 and SR-054 in a single step. Two independent defences are required and both are tested - the client disables the control, and the server clamps regardless of what arrives. The "downward only" property is an automated test, not a convention (agreed in E28-K01). Every override is audited (`tradegroup.row_overridden`) and journal-tagged so an override can never be laundered into looking like normal policy. `require_native_sl` and the allowed-symbol set are classified `never` and a test asserts that classification explicitly by name, so a refactor cannot quietly reclassify them. Data classification: Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
A disabled control must state **why** it is disabled - "capped by profile" is rendered as visible text and exposed via `aria-describedby`, never as a tooltip alone, because a tooltip is unreachable by keyboard-only and touch users (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`). The overridden state is text plus an optional glyph, never colour alone. Reset-on-submit is announced through a polite live region so a screen-reader user knows the ticket returned to defaults. The SCR-114 ceiling is part of each field's accessible description, so it is heard before the value is typed rather than after it is refused. Full keyboard operation; contrast >=4.5:1; 200% text scaling.

## Performance notes
Override application must not trigger a full re-preview beyond the existing 150 ms debounce; the recomputation stays inside SCR-061's <=300 ms preview budget. Mid-ticket profile changes surface within the 2 s propagation budget from SCR-130.

## Observability
Metrics: `cv_override_applied_total{field}`, `cv_override_clamped_total{field}`, `cv_override_refused_total{field}`.
Audit: `tradegroup.row_overridden{field, from, to}`, plus an audit row for every clamped widening attempt.
Journal: the override tag on the resulting order, consumed by **E41**.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` via the merge queue, conventional commits, PRs <=400 LOC diff, 2 approvals including 1 code-owner, all required checks green.
- [ ] Unit coverage >=90% on `candleviewer/profiles` and `candleviewer/oms/fanout` (M13/M14 are on the roadmap's >=90% list), >=80% frontend.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`; no field shipped that is not in the spec and no spec field left unimplemented.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), SCA (pip-audit/npm audit), secrets scanning and Trivy clean on the branch.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` and ADR-0008 amended if behaviour diverged from the plan.
- [ ] Observability added: metrics and audit events listed above are emitted and visible on the admin Grafana dashboard.
- [ ] Design sign-off: E28-D06 handoff accepted and E28-D07 design QA passed (UI tickets only).
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on E28-Q05; a11y axe-core green and one manual screen-reader pass for UI tickets.
- [ ] Security review comment from the Security engineer present for anything touching profile caps, sizing or fan-out targeting (E28-X02).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`ff.profiles`, `ff.trade_groups`) with its per-environment default.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-K01** (ADR-0016 defines the decision table this Story implements - it cannot start before that decision is recorded), **E28-S04** (the surface the per-row override lives on) and **E28-T04** (the guard that clamps a widening hint). Its journal tag is consumed by **E41** and its payload shape by **E34** and **E30**.

## Branch

title: Run the cap-bypass and privilege-escalation drills and record the E28 security sign-off
body:
## Context
Automated suites prove the controls that were thought of. A drill is where a person tries to get around them with the system in front of them, which is how the R3 gate phrases it: "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes". This ticket runs the drills for E28's two assets and records the epic's security sign-off, which the Epic DoD requires.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Drill 1 - **cap bypass**: with a manager account granted one demo account, attempt to place an order larger than the profile permits by every available path: the UI, the REST API directly, a per-row override, a template applied to widen caps, a bulk symbol change, a group whose other members are wider, a replayed idempotency key, and a concurrent edit race between a profile widening and an order submit. Each attempt is recorded with its outcome and its audit trail.
- Drill 2 - **privilege escalation**: attempt to read or act on an ungranted account through the profile routes, the group routes, the preview endpoint and the WS topic, including by guessing identifiers, by supplying an ungranted id in a list parameter, and by subscribing with a broad `exchange_account_ids` set.
- Drill 3 - **counter desynchronisation**: with a cap breached, attempt to clear it by forcing a restart, a WS reconnect and a clock change, in coordination with E28-Q03's chaos scenarios; confirm the cap survives all three.
- Drill 4 - **native-SL invariant**: attempt to create or use a profile that yields an order without a stop, by every path including the templates and the override surface; confirm every attempt is refused and audited. This is a rehearsal for R3 exit criterion #2, which will be run train-wide.
- For each drill: a written outcome, the audit evidence, and a finding if any attempt succeeded or was not audited.
- Verification that every attempt - successful or not - left an audit row, since an unaudited failed attempt is itself a finding.
- Consolidated security report at `docs/security/e28/signoff.md` with the control verdicts from E28-X02, the suite results from E28-X03 and these drill outcomes.
- Risk-register update and the security sign-off comment on the epic.

## Out of scope
Fan-out submission drills (**E34**); the key-compromise drills (**E27-X04**); pen-testing (**E43**); the R3 train-wide safety-invariant suite (run at the train gate).

## Acceptance criteria
- All four drills executed with written outcomes and audit evidence attached.
- Every attempt, successful or not, is shown to have produced an audit row; a missing row is filed as a finding regardless of whether the attempt succeeded.
- Any successful bypass is a P0 finding, fixed and re-drilled before the epic closes - not accepted as a risk.
- The consolidated report exists, links E28-X02 and E28-X03 results, and states a verdict per SR-* control in scope.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated with anything found or retired.
- The security sign-off comment is posted on the epic by the Security engineer.

## Technical notes / design
Drills run on the R3 demo staging environment with the E28-Q01 fixtures and a manager account created for the purpose. The drill operator is the Security engineer, working from the system as a user would - not from the code - so that a control which exists but is unreachable through a real path is discovered.

Drill 1's concurrent-edit race is the subtlest case: a profile widened between the guard's read and the order's submission could, with an unlucky cache design, permit an order neither version would allow. It is executed deliberately with timing control, because it is unlikely to be found by chance.

## Test plan
Drills are manual by design. Anything a drill finds that can be automated is added to E28-X03's suite before the epic closes, so the same gap cannot reopen silently.

## Security notes
This ticket is the epic's final security gate. Its report is an input to the R3 PRR (`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`) and to **E43**'s pen-test scoping - the drills' findings tell the pen-testers where this system is weakest, so the report is shared with them rather than filed away. All drills are demo-only; an environment guard is verified before each run.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except that drill 2 includes attempting a control bypass via keyboard-only paths and via any skip-link or shortcut, since an accessible shortcut that skips a confirmation is a real escalation path.

## Performance notes
N/A - though drill 3 is coordinated with E28-Q03 so the restart and reconnect measurements are taken once and used by both.

## Observability
Drills double as a verification that the audit trail is complete and usable under adversarial conditions: the Security engineer must be able to reconstruct every attempt from the audit browser alone, without database access. If they cannot, that is a finding against the observability of the epic.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Deliverable committed under `docs/security/e28/` and cross-linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding closed or accepted-risk with a written Owner sign-off and an expiry date.
- [ ] Applicable SR-* controls from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` mapped to an automated test (unit, contract, integration or e2e) so the control cannot silently regress.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets-scan clean or triaged on the branches this ticket touches.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk was found or an existing one retired.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E28-X02** (review verdicts), **E28-X03** (the automated suite the drills complement) and **E28-S05** (the override surface drill 1 probes). Coordinates with **E28-Q03** on chaos scenarios. Its sign-off is required by the epic DoD and feeds the R3 PRR.

Functional testing (Q-series) and a11y auditing (Q05) — though findings are cross-linked.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Token fidelity
  When the built screens are inspected
  Then no hard-coded colour, spacing or type value is present where a token exists

Scenario: States match
  Given each state in the state matrix is forced in the test environment
  Then the built rendering matches the spec or a Bug is filed with a screenshot pair

Scenario: Sign-off
  Then the CDO (or a design-system-trained reviewer) records design sign-off on E29 with zero open P0/P1 design bugs
```

States are forced using the fixture-replay mock exchange and feature flags rather than hand-editing the DOM.

## Accessibility notes

## Performance notes

## Context
R3's E2E gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) requires Playwright coverage on web **and** Electron for the trading surfaces, and the contract gate requires "contract tests on every order/position event shape". E29 owns the order/position/execution shapes everything else builds on, so its suites become the regression floor for E30-E34.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright suite `tests/e2e/oms/` running against a backend wired to the fixture-replay mock exchange, executed in both the web and Electron projects: full lifecycle (place, partial fill, amend, cancel), blotter grouping/filtering, inline amend accept and reject, cancel-all with partial failure, partial close including the dust path, reconnect with a correction summary, and manager-scope negative cases.
- Contract tests: every WS private payload (`orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`) validated against its `cv://ws/v1/*.schema.json`; every E29 REST route validated against `22-api-openapi.yaml` in both directions (request and response), failing CI on drift.
- A state-machine conformance test driving the fixtures from E29-Q01 through the public API and asserting the observable state sequence for rules S1-S9.
- Test-data helpers: session factories for owner, manager (single account) and viewer roles.
- CI wiring: the suite runs on every PR touching `area/oms-execution` paths and nightly in full.

## Out of scope
Perf and load (E29-Q03), chaos (E29-Q04), a11y (E29-Q05), fan-out and algo E2E (E33/E34), live-environment runs (forbidden until R4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Lifecycle end to end on both shells
  When the lifecycle spec runs in the web project and in the Electron project
  Then both pass with identical assertions and no shell-specific skips

Scenario: Contract drift fails the build
  Given a WS payload field is renamed without updating its schema
  Then the contract test fails with the offending field named

Scenario: Manager scope negative case
  Given a manager session granted only account B
  When the suite requests account A orders, positions and executions over REST and WS
  Then each returns 403 or a narrowed result, no A data appears, and an audit row exists

Scenario: Flake budget
  Given the suite runs 20 consecutive times in CI
  Then the flake rate is below 1% and any flaky spec is quarantined with a ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
No `sleep`-based waits: every assertion waits on an application signal (a WS frame applied, a state attribute set) exposed through `data-testid` and a test-only readiness event. The mock exchange is driven through an HTTP control plane so a spec can inject a rejection or a disconnect at an exact point in the lifecycle. Electron runs use the same specs with the Playwright Electron launcher to prove no shell-specific regression.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* test code; its own verification is a 20-run stability soak in CI plus a mutation check - deliberately breaking three known behaviours (amend-reject restores prior values, dust guard, manager scope) and confirming the suite fails each time.

## Security notes
The suite includes the RBAC negative matrix for E29 routes (owner, manager, viewer against every route), which is the evidence for R3 exit criterion 10 for this epic's surface. Test credentials are demo-only and injected from CI secrets, never committed.

## Accessibility notes
Each E2E spec ends with an axe-core scan of the screen it exercised, so a11y regressions surface with the functional run; the full audit remains E29-Q05.

## Performance notes
Suite wall-clock target <=12 minutes on the PR path through sharding; the nightly full run has no cap.

## Observability
CI publishes a per-scenario pass/fail report and a trend of flake rate; failures attach the Playwright trace and the mock-exchange transcript.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact (plan / suite / script / report) merged under `tests/` or `docs/qa/` and runnable from CI or documented as an on-demand job.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the story or task it verifies, by ticket key.
- [ ] Results recorded on the ticket with pass/fail per scenario and any defect filed with a `priority/*` label.
- [ ] Reviewed by the QA lead; deviations (e.g. a scenario that cannot yet be automated) stated explicitly with a follow-up ticket.
- [ ] PR merged through the merge queue with required approvals and checks.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E29-Q01 (plan and fixtures), E29-S02 and E29-S07 (the surfaces under test must exist).

title: Build the chaos scenarios for lost acks, reconnect storms and Postgres failover
body:
## Context
ADR-0006's whole justification is what happens when acknowledgements are lost, and R3's chaos gate requires "WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out - all resume to a correct, reconciled state". E29 owns the first and third of those and the recovery machinery the other two depend on. A chaos suite that only proves the app survives is insufficient: it must prove the *book* is correct afterwards.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos harness `tests/chaos/oms/` with injectable faults through the mock exchange control plane and container orchestration: post-send timeout, duplicate ack, out-of-order fills, post-terminal push, private-WS kill mid-lifecycle, backend SIGKILL mid-submission, Postgres failover mid-transaction, 10002 clock drift, 10018 IP rate limit.
- A correctness oracle run after every scenario: local order and position state is compared field by field against the mock/demo exchange truth, and any difference fails the scenario.
- Scenario: crash between a partial-close fill and the protective resize (E29-S03) - on restart the resize must complete and the position must not be left with an over-sized stop.
- Scenario: `Unknown` resolution - a lost ack must resolve by reconciliation only, with an assertion that **zero** resubmissions were sent (counted at the mock exchange).
- Scenario: two consecutive reconciliation passes finding nothing must transition to `Rejected` with `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`.
- Runbook notes for each scenario: what the operator sees, which alert fires, expected recovery time.

## Out of scope
Fan-out unwind chaos (E34), algo resume chaos (E33), exchange-wide outage simulation (E45), Tailscale/network-layer faults (E45).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A lost acknowledgement never duplicates
  Given the transport times out after the exchange accepted the order
  Then the order enters Unknown, the reconciler resolves it to its true state, and the mock exchange recorded exactly one create request

Scenario: Crash mid-partial-close
  Given the backend is killed between the reducing fill and the protective resize
  When it restarts
  Then the protective stop is resized to the remaining position within the recovery window and no over-sized stop persists

Scenario: Postgres failover
  Given Postgres fails over during a submission
  Then order entry is refused while it is unavailable, no order is accepted that was not durably recorded, and after recovery the book matches the exchange

Scenario: Post-terminal push
  Given the exchange pushes an update for an order already in a terminal state
  Then the order is not mutated, a ReconcileAnomaly is audited and alerted

Scenario: The oracle is authoritative
  Then every scenario ends with a field-by-field comparison against exchange truth and fails on any difference
```

## Technical notes / design
Faults are injected deterministically at named lifecycle points rather than by random timing, so a failure is reproducible from the scenario name alone. The resubmission counter lives at the mock exchange, not in the app, so "no blind resubmission" is proven from outside. Postgres failover uses a two-node test topology in the compose profile; the assertion is on behaviour (refuse to accept), not on failover speed.

## Test plan
Each scenario runs in CI nightly and as a required check before the R3 gate. A meta-test deliberately disables the reconciler and asserts every relevant scenario fails - proving the suite has teeth.

## Security notes
Chaos runs use demo accounts only, guarded by the same environment check as the load scripts. Fault injection endpoints exist only in the test profile and are compiled out of production images, verified by a CI check that the production image does not expose the control plane.

## Accessibility notes
The scenarios assert the user-facing consequences from E29-S07 (controls disabled, banner state, summary contents) so the recovery UX is chaos-verified, not just the backend.

## Performance notes
Recovery-time expectations are recorded per scenario: reconciliation resolves an Unknown order within one cycle (<=30 s) and time-to-usable after a 30 s outage is <=5 s.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts the expected metric and alert fired: `oms_unknown_orders` rising then returning to zero, `oms_reconcile_corrections_total` incrementing, `naked_position_alerts_total` for the over-sized/absent stop case.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact (plan / suite / script / report) merged under `tests/` or `docs/qa/` and runnable from CI or documented as an on-demand job.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the story or task it verifies, by ticket key.
- [ ] Results recorded on the ticket with pass/fail per scenario and any defect filed with a `priority/*` label.
- [ ] Reviewed by the QA lead; deviations (e.g. a scenario that cannot yet be automated) stated explicitly with a follow-up ticket.
- [ ] PR merged through the merge queue with required approvals and checks.

## Dependencies

title: Run the accessibility audit of the blotters, fills detail and reconciliation states
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 makes WCAG 2.2 AA default-on for every UI surface with no internal-tool exception, and the R3 a11y gate names the danger/confirm patterns specifically. SCR-063 is the hardest a11y surface in this epic: a virtualised grid with live-updating rows, per-row destructive actions and a banner that must announce once without chattering.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A formal audit of SCR-063 (all tabs), SCR-078 and the SCR-152 states, covering: keyboard-only operation of every control, screen-reader passes with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS, focus order and visible focus, target sizes, contrast including the liq-proximity and PnL treatments, and reduced-motion behaviour.
- Verification of the windowed-grid rules in `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 6.1: roving tabindex stability across virtualisation, position-in-set announcements, and that scrolling does not strand focus.
- Verification of the live-region policy: order state changes announce politely and debounced; the reconnect countdown does **not** announce on every tick; `role="alert"` fires once per state entry.
- Verification that no status is colour-only anywhere: side, order state, liq-proximity, PnL sign, maker/taker, provisional PnL.
- Findings filed as Bugs with `priority/*` and a re-test pass after fixes; an audit report in `docs/qa/e29-a11y-audit.md`.

## Out of scope
The order ticket, chart trading and DOM surfaces (E30/E31 run their own audits), the chart canvas keyboard model beyond execution marks (E11/E47), the epic-wide a11y sweep at R5 (E47).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Keyboard-only completion
  Given only a keyboard
  Then every blotter task can be completed: switch tabs, sort, filter, group, open a row menu, amend, cancel, partial close, export, and open the detail drawer

Scenario: Screen-reader comprehension
  When a screen-reader user reviews the positions tab
  Then account, symbol, side, quantity and liq-proximity are all conveyed without relying on colour and the totals row is identified as a total

Scenario: The banner does not chatter
  Given the reconnecting banner with a live countdown
  Then the state is announced once and the countdown is not announced on each tick

Scenario: axe-core is clean
  Then axe-core reports zero violations of serious or critical impact on SCR-063, SCR-078 and every SCR-152 state

Scenario: Findings are closed
  Then every finding is fixed or filed with a priority label and the re-test pass is recorded
```

## Technical notes / design
Automated axe-core runs are necessary but not sufficient - the virtualisation, live-region and focus-management defects this surface is prone to are invisible to axe, so the manual passes are the substance of the ticket. Each state is forced through the fixture-replay mock and feature flags rather than by hand-editing the DOM, so the audited rendering is the real one.

## Test plan
Audit execution is the work; its output is the report plus filed bugs. A regression guard is added to E29-Q02 so each E2E spec ends with an axe scan, preventing silent regression between audits.

## Security notes
Verify that assistive-technology exposure does not leak out-of-scope data - e.g. a manager's screen reader must not be able to reach hidden rows for accounts outside the grant (they must be absent from the DOM, not merely hidden).

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the accessibility verification; findings map to `05-accessibility-standard.md` clause numbers so remediation is unambiguous.

## Performance notes
Confirm that live-region and announcement handling does not itself breach the 500-row / 60 fps budget - announcement debouncing must not be implemented with per-frame DOM writes.

## Observability
Audit findings are tracked to closure on the epic; the axe regression guard reports per-screen violation counts as a CI trend.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact (plan / suite / script / report) merged under `tests/` or `docs/qa/` and runnable from CI or documented as an on-demand job.
- [ ] Every scenario mapped to the story or task it verifies, by ticket key.

- [ ] Reviewed by the QA lead; deviations (e.g. a scenario that cannot yet be automated) stated explicitly with a follow-up ticket.
- [ ] PR merged through the merge queue with required approvals and checks.

title: Execute the exploratory charters, assemble the regression pack and record E29 QA sign-off
body:
## Context
The epic DoD requires "an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA". E29 is also the first epic whose regression pack every later trading epic inherits, so the pack must be curated rather than accumulated: the scenarios that would catch a book-correctness regression, runnable in under an hour.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execution of the exploratory charters from E29-Q01 as time-boxed, session-based testing with session notes per charter.
- A curated regression pack `docs/qa/e29-regression-pack.md` plus the CI tag `@oms-regression` applied to the E2E specs that constitute it: full lifecycle, amend-reject, cancel race, partial close with dust, manager scope, reconnect with correction, untracked adoption.
- A 48 h continuous demo run (place, partial fill, amend, cancel, close on a schedule) with a daily book-correctness comparison against the exchange, feeding the R3 7-day soak.
- Defect triage: every finding filed with priority, P0/P1 closed before sign-off.
- The QA sign-off comment on E29 with pass/fail per story and an explicit statement of any deviation.

## Out of scope
The R3 7-day soak itself (train-level, `30-release-roadmap.md` section 12 `q09`), fan-out and algo regression (E33/E34 extend the pack), the PRR.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Charters executed
  Then every exploratory charter has session notes recording what was tried, what was observed and what was filed

Scenario: The regression pack is fast and meaningful
  Given the @oms-regression tag is run
  Then it completes in under one hour and covers every book-correctness scenario listed in the pack

Scenario: 48 h continuous run is clean
  Given a 48 h scheduled demo lifecycle run
  Then local state matches the exchange at every daily comparison and oms_unknown_orders is zero at the end of each day

Scenario: Sign-off is conditional on defects
  Given an open P0 or P1 against E29 scope
  Then QA sign-off is withheld and the blocking defect is named on the epic
```

## Technical notes / design
The 48 h run uses tiny quantities on a dedicated demo account and is driven by the same harness as the load scripts, with the governor active so it exercises the real rate-budget path. The book comparison reuses the E29-Q04 correctness oracle rather than a second implementation.

## Test plan
This ticket executes tests rather than adding them; its verification is the recorded evidence - session notes, run logs, comparison reports, and the sign-off comment.

## Security notes
Sign-off explicitly checks that the RBAC negative matrix for E29 routes passed (R3 exit criterion 10 for this surface) and that no fixture or log captured during the run contains credential material.

## Accessibility notes
Sign-off is conditional on E29-Q05 being closed with no open serious or critical findings.

## Performance notes
Sign-off is conditional on E29-Q03's budget-#4 numbers being recorded and within budget.

## Observability
The 48 h run's metrics are retained as the baseline profile for the epic: submit latency distribution, reconcile correction rate, unknown-order count.

- [ ] Artefact (plan / suite / script / report) merged under `tests/` or `docs/qa/` and runnable from CI or documented as an on-demand job.

title: Build the position detail view assembled from OMS state and executions
body:
## Context
US-POS-004 (Should) - a detail view per position showing entry executions, fees, funding, MAE/MFE so far, attached protective orders, controlling rules and the journal entry. Its NFR is the design constraint: the detail is "assembled from the journal and OMS state, not recomputed ad hoc" - otherwise the drawer becomes a fourth opinion about the book.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Story: **US-POS-004**, rendered as a drawer from a SCR-063 row, reusing SCR-078's fill list and linking to SCR-064 (the SL/TP editor owned by E32) and SCR-079 (the account drawer, E27).
- Components: **CMP-036** KeyValueRow, **CMP-046** Drawer, **CMP-049** Table, **CMP-116** PnLBadge.
- Data: `GET /api/v1/positions/{positionId}` plus the executions already in the store; MAE/MFE so far computed server-side from `position_snapshots`.
- Sections: identity (account, symbol, side, position_idx, leverage, margin mode), entry executions, fees and funding paid, MAE/MFE, attached protective orders with their native-versus-engine-managed status, controlling rule ids (rule detail is E35) and the journal link (E41, a disabled link until E41 ships).
- A "show on chart" action navigating the chart to the entry time with this position's executions highlighted.
- Externally-modified notice: when the position was changed outside the app, a reconciliation notice explains the difference and when it was detected.

## Out of scope
Editing anything (SL/TP editing is SCR-064 in E32), journal note authoring (E41), rule inspection (E35), MAE/MFE analytics history and distributions (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Detail contents
  Then entry executions, fees paid, funding paid, MAE/MFE so far, attached protective orders, controlling rule ids and the journal link are shown

Scenario: Jump to chart
  When I choose "show on chart"
  Then the chart navigates to the entry time and this position's executions are highlighted

Scenario: Externally modified
  Given the position was changed outside CandleViewer and reconciliation detected it
  Then a notice explains what differed and when it was detected

Scenario: No ad-hoc recomputation
  Then every figure shown matches the server-side aggregation exactly, asserted by a contract test comparing the drawer payload with the positions and executions endpoints
```

## Technical notes / design
The drawer fetches one aggregate payload; it does not assemble numbers from three stores. MAE/MFE so far is derived server-side from `position_snapshots` (`reason in ('ws_push','minute_tick')`) bounded to the position's lifetime. Protective orders are listed with their `purpose` (`stop_loss` / `take_profit`) and a native-versus-engine-managed badge sourced from `orders.intent` plus the position's `stop_loss` field, so an engine-managed trail is never mistaken for exchange-side protection.

## Test plan
Unit: payload-to-section mapping, native-versus-engine badge logic, external-modification notice rendering. Contract: the aggregate payload against the OpenAPI schema and against the individual endpoints (the "no ad-hoc recomputation" scenario). E2E: open from a row, jump to chart, assert the chart range and the highlighted marks. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Account-scoped read (`positions:read`). The drawer surfaces rule ids and order link ids - correlation identifiers rather than secrets - and never key material or exchange signatures. The external-modification notice is sourced from audited reconciliation output, so it cannot be spoofed by client state.

## Accessibility notes
The drawer has a heading naming account, symbol and side; sections are a description list; the native-versus-engine badge is text; "show on chart" moves focus to the chart pane and announces the navigation; the drawer traps focus and restores it to the originating row on close.

## Performance notes
Opens from cached state in <=100 ms and refreshes in place (the SCR-079 drawer budget applied here).

## Observability
`position.detail_viewed` (analytics) with `{has_external_modification}` so the frequency of external modification is trackable.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified by an automated test referencing the scenario name (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2/§4.2).
- [ ] Coverage: touched backend/OMS packages ≥90% line (local R3 policy for OMS/risk modules, `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4), frontend ≥80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `22-api-openapi.yaml` / `23-ws-protocol.md` / `24-internal-schemas.md` / `21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour; changelog fragment added.
- [ ] Security: SAST (Bandit/Semgrep/CodeQL) + SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present (mandatory — `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8, order-placement path).
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario.

- [ ] PR(s) merged through the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; PR ≤400 LOC diff preferred.

- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched screen(s); keyboard-only path verified; manual screen-reader spot-check recorded (`05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the E29-D06 handoff pack; discrepancies fixed or filed with a `priority/*`.

## Dependencies

title: Security review and sign-off of the shipped OMS
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 makes a Security engineer sign-off mandatory for the order-placement path regardless of labelling, and the R3 gate requires all Critical/High STRIDE findings closed for E29 before the train can complete. This is the closing review: code review of the security-relevant paths, verification that each modelled control actually shipped, and the recorded sign-off.

## Scope / Deliverables
- White-box review of the security-relevant code: the submission pipeline's authorisation and scoping, `order_link_id` generation and collision handling, the redaction of `order_events.payload`, the rate-budget reserve, the reconciliation adoption path (`untracked` orders must never become rule-managed), and the WS subscription narrowing.
- Verification that every Critical/High threat from E29-X01 has a shipped control and a passing test, with the evidence linked per threat.
- Execution of the manual abuse checks that E29-X02 could not automate, recorded on a checklist.
- Confirmation that no secret material appears in logs, metrics labels, diagnostics payloads, audit rows, error messages or fixtures - sampled from a real 48 h demo run (E29-Q06).
- Confirmation that the live transport path remains structurally unreachable: no code path can reach live while the R4 gate is off, verified by inspection of the capability wiring and by a test.
- The sign-off comment on E29 with any accepted risks named and Owner-signed.

## Out of scope
Penetration testing (E43), live-enablement gating implementation (E44), remediating findings (filed as their own tickets against the owning story).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every modelled control shipped
  Then each Critical or High threat in the E29 threat model links to shipped code and a passing test

Scenario: No secret leaks
  Given logs, metrics, diagnostics payloads, audit rows and fixtures from a 48 h demo run
  When they are sampled and scanned
  Then no API key, signature or other credential material is found

Scenario: Live is structurally unreachable
  Given the R4 live gate is off
  Then no code path can submit an order to the live environment, proven by inspection and by an automated test

Scenario: Untracked orders stay unmanaged
  Given an order adopted as untracked during reconciliation
  Then no rule or algo can act on it, asserted by test

Scenario: Sign-off is recorded
  Then a Security engineer sign-off comment exists on E29 with any accepted risks named and Owner-signed
```

## Technical notes / design
The review follows the threat model element by element rather than file by file, so coverage is argued rather than assumed. Accepted risks must state the compensating control and an expiry - an accepted risk with no review date is not accepted.

## Test plan
Review activity, evidenced by the completed checklist, linked test runs and the sign-off comment. Any finding becomes a ticket on the owning story with a priority label, and P0/P1 findings block the epic's Done.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security gate for the epic. It also feeds the continuous OMS threat-model refresh running across S14-S19 and hands its open items to E43's hardening backlog.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - review activity.

## Performance notes
Confirms that no security control was disabled or weakened to meet budget #4 - specifically that validation, scoping and audit writes are all inside the measured path rather than deferred out of it.

## Observability
Confirms the detection signals exist and alert correctly: `rbac_denied_total`, `oms_unknown_orders` paging, audit rows on every mutation, and that the audit hash chain covers OMS events.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefact merged (threat model in `docs/security/`, rules under `.semgrep/` or the CI config, tests under `tests/security/`).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding either fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off recorded (R3 gate, `30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4).
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present on this ticket and on the tickets it gates.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk was surfaced or an existing one retired.
- [ ] PR merged through the merge queue with required approvals and checks.

title: Automate the Playwright E2E suite for the order ticket on demo
body:
## Context
R3's E2E gate requires "Playwright web + Electron covering ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, bracket, fan-out, rule creation in both editors, alert firing, journal capture" (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4). This ticket delivers the **ticket** slice of that suite, running against the **demo** environment â€” never live, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§8.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `tests/e2e/order-ticket/` running in both the browser and the Electron shell:
  - `place-limit.spec` â€” keyboard-only limit order placement end to end, asserting the acknowledgement and the WS-driven state transition.
  - `place-market-armed.spec` â€” arm â†’ one-click market with the profile stop attached.
  - `hotkey.spec` â€” armed hotkey buy; hotkey suppressed in a text field; hotkey inert while locked.
  - `validation.spec` â€” client-blocked cases (min qty, tick, reduce-only without a position, missing native SL) asserting no network call is made.
  - `rejection.spec` â€” a seeded exchange rejection producing the inline error and the SCR-077 drawer with the verbatim message and the retained inputs.
  - `ratelimit.spec` â€” a seeded `10018` producing SCR-158 with a held action and an explicit replay confirmation.
  - `confirmation.spec` â€” demo skip-when-armed; live-shaped fixture refusing to skip for a market order; auto-cancel on inactivity.
  - `group-preview.spec` â€” three-account group preview with one would-be-rejected leg, then submit of the remaining legs after acknowledgement.
  - `templates.spec` â€” save, apply, and a disabled template with its reason.
- Deterministic test data: a dedicated demo account set and a fixture-seeded backend mode for the failure cases, so rejections do not depend on market conditions.
- CI wiring: the suite runs on every PR touching `apps/web/src/features/order-ticket` or `packages/order-ticket-core`, and nightly in full; flake budget â‰¤1%, with a quarantine process rather than a retry-until-green default.
- Trace/video artefacts retained for failures.

## Out of scope
Chart/DOM trading E2E (E31-Q02), fan-out execution E2E (E34), backend unit/integration tests (E29), perf measurement (E30-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The suite proves an order can be placed with the keyboard alone
  When place-limit.spec runs
  Then the entire path from focus entry to acknowledgement uses keyboard input only and passes in both browser and Electron
Scenario: Client-blocked cases prove no network call
  When validation.spec runs
  Then the network log shows zero requests to /api/v1/orders for each blocked case
Scenario: The suite never touches live
  Then every spec asserts the environment is demo before acting, and fails immediately if it is not
Scenario: Flake is controlled
  Given ten consecutive nightly runs
  Then the flake rate is at or below 1% and any flaky spec is quarantined with a tracking ticket rather than retried blindly
```

## Technical notes / design
Selectors are role- and name-based (`getByRole('button', {name: /submit buy/i})`), which doubles as a continuous check that the accessible names specified in E30-D05 are actually present â€” a broken accessible name breaks the E2E suite, which is exactly the coupling we want.

WS-driven assertions wait on the rendered state transition, never on a fixed timeout; the ack-timeout path is tested by holding the WS event back deliberately.

The live-policy test uses a **live-shaped fixture environment**, not a real live account: the environment flag is set to live in a sandboxed backend so the UI's live behaviour is exercised without any possibility of a real order.

## Test plan
Meta-tests: each spec is verified to fail when its feature is deliberately broken (mutation check on a sample of three specs), so a spec that passes vacuously is caught.

## Security notes
Test credentials are demo-only, injected from CI secrets, never committed, and scoped to accounts with no withdrawal permission (which the platform guarantees anyway). Traces and videos are scanned before retention because they can capture balances; artefacts are retained privately and expire after 14 days.

## Accessibility notes
Role/name-based selectors enforce the accessible-name contract. `keyboard-only.spec` behaviour is embedded in `place-limit.spec` rather than being a separate optional test, so it cannot be skipped when the suite is trimmed.

## Performance notes
The suite asserts the *observable* budget (acknowledgement rendered within 500 ms on demo) but does not attempt statistical measurement â€” that is E30-Q03. Suite wall-clock â‰¤8 minutes so it can gate PRs.

## Observability
Failing runs attach the correlation id of the last order request so a failure can be traced into backend logs without re-running.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All nine specs implemented and green in both browser and Electron.
- [ ] CI wiring done: per-PR on the touched paths, nightly in full.
- [ ] Mutation check performed on three specs.
- [ ] Flake â‰¤1% across ten nightly runs; quarantine process documented.
- [ ] Artefact retention and scanning configured.
- [ ] Reviewed by the E30 engineering lead; QA lead sign-off.

- **E30-S05**, **E30-S06** â€” the last behaviours the suite covers.

`chore/e30-e2e-suite`.

title: Build the performance and load scripts for the ticket's latency budgets
body:
## Context
Three client budgets and one end-to-end budget govern this Epic, and `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` treats budget #4 (order submit â†’ ack, p95 <300 ms demo) as a **hard gate**. E30-K01 measured them on a prototype; this ticket turns that into a repeatable, CI-runnable measurement that fails when a regression lands, rather than when someone notices the app feels slow.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A benchmark harness (promoted from E30-K01) measuring, on the reference loaded workspace (chart + footprint + DOM ladder live on demo data):
  - ticket recompute after price, qty and sizing-mode changes â€” budget **8 ms** (SCR-060);
  - gesture â†’ request dispatch for click, `Ctrl+Enter` and hotkey â€” the client share of budget #4, target **â‰¤20 ms**, and the **50 ms** hotkey budget (US-ORD-006);
  - preview local recompute â€” **100 ms** (US-ORD-014);
  - end-to-end click â†’ acknowledgement rendered against a demo account â€” budget #4, **p95 <300 ms**.
- A k6 script driving sustained ticket-shaped order flow against the demo backend at the per-UID limit for one hour, asserting zero lost acknowledgements and correct `10018` back-off (the R3 Load gate), with the ticket's own client behaviour observed under that pressure.
- CI wiring: the client benchmarks run nightly with a **+20% regression gate** against a stored baseline; the end-to-end budget is measured in the nightly demo run and reported, gating the R3 PRR rather than every PR (because it includes uncontrolled Bybit RTT).
- A results dashboard panel and the recorded figures fed into E30-T03's docs reconciliation.

## Out of scope
Backend-internal latency budgeting (E29/E34 own the â‰¤50 ms backend-added share), chart-engine FPS (E11/E46), fan-out load beyond the ticket's role in it (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every budget has an automated measurement
  Then recompute, dispatch, hotkey, preview and click-to-ack each have a scripted measurement reporting p50, p95 and p99
Scenario: A regression fails the build
  Given a deliberate 30% slowdown injected into the recompute path
  Then the nightly benchmark fails against the stored baseline
Scenario: Measurement is honest about what it includes
  Then each reported figure states whether it includes network and Bybit RTT, per the exclusion rules in 06-performance-and-load-standard.md section 2
Scenario: The suite runs under realistic contention
  Then measurements are taken with the chart engine and ladder actively rendering, not on an idle page
```

## Technical notes / design
Baselines are stored per hardware class; CI runners and the developer workstation are different classes and are never compared to each other. Each run records the build sha, the workspace definition and the WS traffic rate so a regression can be attributed rather than merely detected.

p95 is computed over â‰¥1 000 samples per metric; runs with a coefficient of variation above a threshold are rejected as noisy and repeated, rather than reported.

## Test plan
The harness self-tests: an injected artificial delay of a known size must be detected within 10% by each metric, proving the measurement is actually measuring the intended span.

## Security notes
Load scripts run against demo only and use demo credentials from CI secrets. The k6 script must respect the per-UID budget deliberately â€” a load test that ignores rate limits would both invalidate its own results and risk the demo account's standing.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (measurement tooling). Note that the announcement throttles specified in E30-D05 are part of what keeps the accessibility tree cheap; the harness records accessibility-tree recomputation cost as a secondary metric so a regression there is visible.

## Performance notes
This ticket is the performance work. Budgets: 8 ms recompute (SCR-060), â‰¤20 ms client dispatch and p95 <300 ms end to end (budget #4, Â§5.2), 50 ms hotkey (US-ORD-006), 100 ms preview (US-ORD-014), plus the one-hour sustained-flow Load gate.

## Observability
Publishes `cv_ticket_recompute_ms`, `cv_ticket_click_to_ack_ms`, `cv_ticket_hotkey_dispatch_ms` and `cv_ticket_preview_latency_ms` to the Grafana dashboard so the budgets are observable in staging continuously, not only during the benchmark window.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five client/e2e measurements scripted and reporting p50/p95/p99.
- [ ] Nightly CI wiring with the +20% regression gate; injected-slowdown test proves the gate works.
- [ ] One-hour k6 sustained-flow run executed once with results recorded.
- [ ] Figures recorded for E30-T03 and for the R3 PRR.
- [ ] Dashboard panel provisioned; reviewed by the Architect.

title: Chaos scenarios for in-flight orders, lost acknowledgements and revoked arming
body:
## Context
R3's Chaos gate requires that "WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out â€” all resume to a correct, reconciled state" (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4). The ticket's share of that is the **client's** behaviour when the ground moves under an order it has already sent: it must never invent a fill, never lose the user's inputs, never stay armed when it cannot verify that it should be, and never show a position as protected when the stop has not been confirmed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scripted fault injection against the demo stack, each asserting an observable UI outcome:
  1. **WS drop between ack and fill** â€” the ticket shows "Awaiting exchange confirmation â€” reconciling" after `CV_TICKET_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS`, and reconciles correctly on reconnect without duplicating the order.
  2. **REST timeout with the order actually placed** â€” the retry uses the same idempotency key and the server replays rather than double-placing; the UI ends in one order, not two.
  3. **Backend restart mid-submit** â€” the client surfaces a clear unknown state and reconciles from `GET /api/v1/orders` on recovery.
  4. **Kill-switch engaged while armed** â€” the client disarms within one second and a subsequent one-click submit is refused with `trading_disabled`.
  5. **Risk-cap lockout mid-ticket** â€” the submit affordance becomes blocked-by-lockout with the reason and the reset path stated.
  6. **Arm token expiry mid-gesture** â€” the submit is refused with `403`, the client reconciles to locked, and the user's inputs are retained.
  7. **Stop attach failure** â€” the entry is accepted but no exchange-side stop is confirmed; the ticket shows "order live, protective stop pending" and surfaces the critical alert, and never shows a plain "filled".
  8. **Stale wallet / `wallet` topic silence** â€” equity-derived sizing modes disable themselves rather than sizing from stale data.
  9. **Clock skew** between client and server â€” arm expiry is driven by the server's absolute `expires_at`, not by a local countdown drifting into an over-long armed window.
  10. **Rate-limit exhaustion mid-fan-out** â€” SCR-158 names served and unserved accounts and holds rather than drops the remaining intent.
- Each scenario scripted and repeatable in CI (nightly, not per-PR), with pass criteria stated as UI-observable outcomes.

## Out of scope
Backend recovery correctness itself (E29/E45 own reconciliation and failover), Postgres failover mechanics (E45), fan-out unwind semantics (E34).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No invented outcomes
  Given any injected fault between submit and fill
  Then the UI never displays a filled or rejected state it has not observed on the orders or executions topic
Scenario: No duplicate orders
  Given a REST timeout on an order that actually reached the exchange
  When the user retries without changing any field
  Then exactly one order exists at the exchange and the UI shows exactly one
Scenario: Arming fails closed under every fault
  Given a kill-switch, a lockout, a token expiry or a disconnect
  Then the client ends in the locked state with the reason displayed, in every case
Scenario: A pending stop is never presented as protection
  Given the entry is filled and the stop is not confirmed
  Then the UI shows the pending-stop state in text and icon until the stop is observed
```

## Technical notes / design
Fault injection uses a proxy layer in front of the backend for network faults (drop, delay, kill), plus backend test hooks for kill-switch, lockout and stop-attach failure. Each scenario runs from a clean, known account state and asserts the final exchange-side truth via `GET /v5/order/realtime` through the backend, not only the UI â€” a UI that agrees with itself while disagreeing with the exchange is the exact failure we are hunting.

## Test plan
This ticket is the chaos test plan. Each scenario is also verified to *fail* when the corresponding guard is disabled, proving it discriminates.

## Security notes
Chaos runs on demo with demo credentials only. Scenario 4 (kill-switch) and scenario 5 (lockout) double as security assertions â€” the client must not be able to proceed by ignoring either, and the server refusal is verified independently of the UI.

## Accessibility notes
Each degraded state's announcement is asserted, not just its rendering: reconciling, pending-stop, locked-by-kill-switch and rate-limited must all be announced (the first three assertively), since a screen-reader user otherwise has no way to learn that the world changed under them.

## Performance notes
The reconciling threshold (`CV_TICKET_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS`, 2 000 ms) is validated here: too short and normal demo latency produces false reconciling states; too long and the user is left believing an unconfirmed order is fine.

## Observability
Each scenario asserts the expected audit and metric side effects (`order.blocked_ratelimited`, `order.auto_disarmed{reason}`, the naked-position critical alert), so a silent failure of instrumentation is itself caught.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ten scenarios scripted, runnable nightly, and passing.
- [ ] Each scenario shown to fail with its guard disabled.
- [ ] Exchange-side truth asserted independently of the UI in scenarios 1â€“3 and 7.
- [ ] Results recorded and fed into the R3 Chaos gate evidence.
- [ ] Reviewed by the Architect and the Security engineer.

## Dependencies
- **E30-S04** â€” arm state and the fail-closed guard under test.
- **E30-S06** â€” the fan-out preview and rate-limit surfaces.
- **E29** â€” reconciliation behaviour the client depends on.

title: Accessibility audit of ticket, confirmation, rejection, defaults
body:
## Context
R3 cannot ship without "Order ticket ... fully keyboard-operable; danger/confirm patterns announced" (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4), and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§8 makes WCAG 2.2 AA default-on with no internal-tool exemption. E30-D05 specified the a11y contract at design time; this ticket verifies the built product against it, with a real screen reader, not only with axe.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **axe-core** runs wired into CI for SCR-060, SCR-076, SCR-077, SCR-113 trading rows, SCR-114 and SCR-158, in both themes and both densities, with zero serious/critical violations as a merge-blocking gate.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with NVDA (Windows, primary) and VoiceOver (macOS, secondary) against the E30-D05 screen-reader script: placing an order, arming and auto-disarming, being refused while locked, being blocked by the native-SL invariant, being rejected by the exchange, being rate-limited, and the risk read-out changing.
- **Keyboard-only pass** of the full numbered sequence from E30-D05, including escaping every state, the confirmation modal's focus trap and focus return, and the `Enter`-after-400 ms rule.
- **Contrast verification** in the built product for every state including disabled, armed, live and pending-stop, in both themes.
- **Reduced-motion verification**: every motion-specified state change still conveys its change with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- **Announcement-rate verification**: live regions respect the specified throttles under a live `ticker` feed â€” over-announcing is filed as a defect, not tolerated.
- Findings filed as Bugs with severity; all serious/critical fixed before the Epic closes; a written audit report attached.

## Out of scope
Chart/DOM trading a11y (E31-Q05), rule-editor a11y (E36/E37), the chart's DOM-mirror (E11), design-side review (E30-D05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: axe is clean and gating
  Then axe-core reports zero serious or critical violations on all six surfaces in both themes, and the check blocks merge
Scenario: The built product matches the screen-reader script
  Given the E30-D05 script of expected utterances
  Then NVDA's actual utterances match for placing, arming, refusal, invariant block, rejection and rate-limiting
  And any divergence is reconciled by fixing the build or amending the script, never by ignoring it
Scenario: The whole order path is keyboard-operable
  Then an order can be configured, submitted, confirmed and abandoned with the keyboard alone, and focus returns correctly from every modal and drawer
Scenario: Announcements do not flood
  Given a live ticker feed updating at 100 ms
  Then the risk read-out announces at most twice per second and countdowns at most once per ten seconds
Scenario: Nothing is colour-only
  Then buy/sell, armed/locked, demo/live, valid/invalid and protected/pending are each distinguishable in greyscale in the built product
```

## Technical notes / design
axe runs both in component tests (per Storybook story) and in the E2E suite against assembled screens â€” the two catch different classes of problem, and only the second sees focus order and modal interaction.

Announcement-rate verification is done by capturing the live-region mutation log over a 60 s window with a live feed and asserting the counts, which is more reliable than a human counting utterances.

## Test plan
This ticket is the audit. Regression protection: the axe checks and the live-region rate assertions become permanent CI checks so the result does not decay after the audit closes.

## Security notes
The audit runs on demo. Verify that no announcement leaks scope information â€” specifically that a narrowed trade group or a disabled template never announces the name or existence of an account the user cannot access.

## Accessibility notes
Standard: WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Particular attention to 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (the confirmation modal and the rejection drawer over the ticket), 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (a rejected order retains inputs), 4.1.3 Status Messages (every degraded state is announced), and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (the armed indicator and focus rings).

## Performance notes
Accessibility-tree recomputation cost under the live feed is recorded as a secondary metric; an excessive cost indicates over-broad live regions and is filed as a defect even when the audit otherwise passes.

## Observability
N/A directly; findings are tracked as Bugs.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] axe-core gating checks wired and green on all six surfaces in both themes.
- [ ] NVDA and VoiceOver passes completed against the script, with recordings or transcripts attached.
- [ ] Keyboard-only pass completed for the full sequence.

- [ ] All serious/critical findings fixed and re-verified; remaining findings triaged with owners.
- [ ] Audit report attached; accessibility lead sign-off recorded.

title: Run exploratory charters, assemble regression pack, QA sign-off
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§2.2 requires an **Epic-level** regression and exploratory pass, "not just child-ticket QA", before an Epic can be Done. For the order ticket this is the last human look before the surface that places real orders is declared finished, and it is also where the R3-wide regression pack acquires its ticket chapter.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (time-boxed, session-based, ~90 min each) with written debriefs:
  1. "Try to place an order that is not what the UI told you it would be" (sizing, clamps, rounding, stale data).
  2. "Try to get an order out without a stop, by any path in this Epic."
  3. "Try to make demo look like live, or armed look like locked, to a hurried user."
  4. "Break the retry story: rejections, corrections, held actions and idempotency."
  5. "Use the ticket for twenty minutes with the keyboard only and no mouse at all."
- **Regression pack**: the P0 subset of the E30-Q01 matrix, formalised as the ticket chapter of the R3 regression pack, executable in â‰¤2 hours, with each step naming its expected audit event.
- **Cross-Epic interaction pass**: ticket behaviour while E39's kill-switch is engaged, while an E28 profile is edited underneath it, and with an E27 account whose key is inside Bybit's 48 h restriction (the pending-key state).
- **Defect triage and closure**: all findings filed with priority, P0/P1 closed before sign-off, P2/P3 triaged with owners and target sprints.
- **QA sign-off comment** with pass/fail per scenario of the E30-Q01 plan, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§3.2, referenced by every E30 Story.

## Out of scope
The R3 7-day soak (roadmap `q09`, S19), live-environment testing (R4), backend-only regression (E29's own pack).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Exploratory charters are executed and debriefed
  Then five charters are completed with written debriefs and every finding is filed with a priority
Scenario: The regression pack is executable and bounded
  Given a QA engineer and a clean demo environment
  Then the pack completes in under two hours and covers every P0 scenario in the E30-Q01 matrix
Scenario: No P0 or P1 defects remain open
  Then every P0 and P1 defect against this Epic's scope is closed and re-verified before sign-off
Scenario: Sign-off is specific, not a rubber stamp
  Then the sign-off comment records pass or fail for each scenario of the black-box plan, with dates and build shas
```

## Technical notes / design
Charters are run against the demo build in the Electron shell, since that is the primary target, with a browser spot-check. Session notes record the build sha, so a finding can always be reproduced against the right code.

The cross-Epic interaction pass is deliberately placed here rather than in any single Story: these are the failures that only exist at the seams, and no Story owns a seam.

## Test plan
This ticket is the QA close-out. Its own quality bar: every charter produces either findings or an explicit statement of what was tried and did not break â€” a charter with an empty debrief is not accepted.

## Security notes
Charters 2 and 3 are security-adjacent and their findings are copied to the Security engineer for the E30-X03 sign-off, since "get an order out without a stop" and "make live look like demo" are abuse cases as much as usability ones.

## Accessibility notes
Charter 5 (twenty minutes keyboard-only) is a lived-experience complement to the formal audit in E30-Q05; findings from it are routed to the same owner and are not downgraded merely because the formal audit passed.

## Performance notes
The regression pack includes the observable performance checks (acknowledgement within 500 ms, no typing lag on a loaded workspace) so a perf regression is caught by routine regression even between benchmark runs.

## Observability
Each regression step names the audit event that must be present; the pack includes one verification that the audit chain for a placed order is complete and hash-verifiable (a cross-check against E42's audit browser).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] E30-D07 design QA complete with no open blocking findings before sign-off is recorded.
- [ ] Five charters executed with written debriefs.
- [ ] Regression pack written, executed once end to end, and added to the R3 pack.
- [ ] Cross-Epic interaction pass completed.
- [ ] All P0/P1 defects closed and re-verified; P2/P3 triaged with owners.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with per-scenario results, referenced from every E30 Story.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 confirmed for the Epic-level DoD.
