title: Implement the abuse-case suite, scope assertions and SAST rules for the ticket
body:
## Context
A threat model that is not executed is an opinion. This ticket turns E30-X01's Critical and High threats into **automated tests and static rules** that run in CI, so that the guarantees hold not only on the day of the review but on every subsequent commit â€” including commits made by other Epics that touch the same surfaces (E31, E33, E34 all reuse this ticket's intent layer).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case test suite** (`tests/security/order-ticket/`), each derived from a named threat:
  - forged `arm_token`, expired `arm_token`, and an `arm_token` replayed after disarm â†’ all refused server-side with `403`, audited, no order created;
  - a one-click order submitted with **no** `arm_token` â†’ refused;
  - a submit dispatched programmatically outside `CMP-139` â†’ impossible by construction (lint) and refused at runtime (assertion test);
  - a crafted `PlaceOrderRequest` omitting `stop_loss` on an invariant-required account â†’ `422 native_stop_required`, audited;
  - a crafted request with a stop on the wrong side of entry â†’ refused;
  - a manager submitting to an ungranted `exchange_account_id` â†’ `403`, no state change, audit row present;
  - a manager previewing a trade group containing an ungranted account â†’ the ungranted leg omitted **and** labelled, never silently included;
  - a settings write disabling LIVE market confirmation â†’ refused server-side and audited at high severity;
  - a tampered hotkey map binding a destructive action to a bare letter with the safety option on â†’ refused;
  - idempotency-key collision attempted across sessions â†’ rejected, no cross-session replay;
  - `10018` storm induced via preview spam â†’ client-side rate limiting holds, real orders are not starved.
- **RBAC/scope assertion matrix** for every ticket-originated route Ã— role (owner, manager with grant, manager without grant, viewer), asserting `403` + no state change + an audit row for every disallowed combination â€” the ticket's contribution to R3 exit criterion 10.
- **SAST rules**: a Semgrep rule set banning (a) `submit()` call sites outside the guard wrapper, (b) rendering of any field named like a credential/signature in the diagnostics view, (c) `console.log` of an order payload or diagnostics response, (d) persistence of the arm token to any storage API. Wired as a blocking CI check.
- **DAST**: an OWASP ZAP pass over the trading routes checking CSP (`frame-ancestors 'none'` for clickjacking of the armed control), security headers, and that no order endpoint is reachable without authentication.
- **Secrets check** extended over test fixtures and Playwright artefacts.

## Out of scope
Backend OMS abuse cases (E29-X02), key vault (E27), fan-out rate governor abuse (E34), the full RBAC matrix across all routes (E09/E42 own the global matrix â€” this contributes the ticket's rows), pen-test (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every Critical and High threat has an executable test
  Then each Critical/High threat from E30-X01 maps to at least one test in this suite, and the mapping table is complete
Scenario: The suite fails when a control is removed
  Given the arm-token server-side check is disabled in a mutation build
  Then the corresponding abuse-case test fails
Scenario: Scope violations produce 403, no state change and an audit row
  Given every role and every ticket-originated route
  Then each disallowed combination returns 403, mutates nothing, and writes an audit entry
Scenario: SAST rules block, not warn
  Given a commit introducing a submit call outside the guard wrapper
  Then CI fails on the Semgrep rule and the commit cannot merge
```

## Technical notes / design
Abuse cases are executed against the **backend**, using crafted requests rather than the UI, because the point is to prove the server does not rely on the client. Where a control is genuinely client-only (the hold-to-confirm gesture, focus suppression), the test says so explicitly and the threat model records the residual risk â€” an honest boundary is better than a test that pretends otherwise.

The mutation check (disabling a control and asserting the test fails) is run once per control during this ticket, and the results are recorded; it is not left running in CI.

## Test plan
The suite is the test plan. It runs per-PR on the trading paths and nightly in full. Failures are treated as release-blocking, in line with R3's Safety gate where "a failure blocks merge, not just release".

## Security notes
This ticket is the security verification work. It must not itself introduce weakness: crafted-request fixtures must not contain real credentials, the ZAP configuration must be committed (so the scan is reproducible) and its findings triaged rather than baselined away.

## Accessibility notes
The SAST rule banning credential-shaped rendering must not be so broad that it blocks legitimate accessible labels; rules are written against field names and known shapes, not against arbitrary text. No control introduced here may be colour-only or pointer-only.

## Performance notes
The client-side rate limiting verified in the preview-spam case exists to protect budget #4: if preview traffic can starve the `entry` bucket, real orders slow down. The test asserts that real-order latency is unaffected while preview is spammed.

## Observability
Every abuse case asserts the expected audit row exists and is correctly attributed â€” an unauditable refusal is a finding. Metric `cv_ticket_guard_blocked_total{reason}` must increment for guard refusals.

## Definition of Done

title: Security review and sign-off of the shipped order ticket
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` Â§2.2 requires, for any `security`-labelled Epic, that "STRIDE model finalized, findings triaged (fixed or accepted-risk with Owner sign-off), sign-off comment from Security engineer". R3's gate adds "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes". This ticket is that close-out for the order ticket surface â€” and, because E31/E33/E34 inherit this Epic's intent layer, arm state and confirmation policy, signing it off is also signing off the foundation those Epics build on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Code review, security-focused**, of the shipped implementation: `packages/order-ticket-core` (idempotency-key derivation, error mapping, no credential handling), the arm store and `CMP-139` guard, the account/group selector's scope handling, the settings/defaults write path, the diagnostics rendering and its redaction, and the hotkey dispatcher's precedence order.
- **Verification that every Critical/High threat** from E30-X01 is closed: fixed with a test, or accepted with the Owner's recorded sign-off and a residual-risk statement.
- **Audit-chain verification**: place, reject, arm, disarm, rebind a trading hotkey and change a trading default on demo, then verify each produced the expected audit entry with correct attribution, and that the chain hash-verifies (cross-checking E42's audit browser).
- **Client-only-control ledger**: an explicit written list of the controls that exist only on the client (hold-to-confirm, focus suppression, the visual environment distinction), each with its server-side counterpart named or its absence justified â€” handed to E43 as pen-test input.
- **Findings triage** with severity, owner and target; Critical/High closed before sign-off.
- **Sign-off comment** on this ticket and on the Epic, naming the reviewed commit shas.

## Out of scope
Fixing defects (they are filed against their owning Stories), backend OMS security sign-off (E29-X03), the R4 pen-test itself (E43), live-enablement gating (E44).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No Critical or High threat is open
  Then every Critical and High threat from E30-X01 is either verified closed by a test or accepted with the Owner's recorded sign-off
Scenario: The audit trail is complete and attributable
  Given a placed order, a rejection, an arm, a disarm, a hotkey rebinding and a defaults change performed on demo
  Then each produced its expected audit entry with correct user, account and environment attribution, and the chain hash-verifies
Scenario: Client-only controls are documented, not assumed
  Then a written ledger names every control with no server-side counterpart and states the accepted residual risk
Scenario: Sign-off is specific
  Then the sign-off comment names the reviewed commit shas, the tests relied upon, and any accepted risks
```

## Technical notes / design
The review pays particular attention to three places where a plausible implementation would be subtly wrong: (1) the arm token being kept in any persistent store (it must be memory-only, and a restart must land in `locked`); (2) the guard being implemented as a hook that a call site can forget rather than a wrapper it cannot escape; (3) the diagnostics view redacting on render instead of relying on the server's redaction â€” the server must redact, and the client must additionally not log.

## Test plan
No new tests; this ticket verifies that the existing ones actually cover what they claim. Where they do not, a gap is filed against E30-X02 rather than being noted and forgotten.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security close-out. Standard: `04-security-program.md`; R3 Security gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` Â§7.4). Data classification: financial, account-scoped. Reviewed on demo only; no live credentials are used at any point.

## Accessibility notes
The review confirms that no security control added late in the Epic broke the a11y contract â€” specifically that refusals are announced, that the guard's disabled state states a reason, and that nothing security-relevant is signalled by colour alone.

## Performance notes
Confirms that the security controls sit inside the measured budgets â€” in particular that the arm-token check and the guard wrapper do not add measurably to the 50 ms hotkey path or the client's share of budget #4, using E30-Q03's figures.

## Observability
Confirms that `cv_ticket_guard_blocked_total`, `order.arm_toggled`, `order.auto_disarmed` and the high-severity `trading_defaults.live_confirmation_disabled` are all emitted and visible on the dashboards, so a future regression is detectable in production rather than only in CI.

- [ ] E30-D07 design QA complete with no open blocking findings on safety/LIVE treatments.
- [ ] Security-focused code review completed over the named modules, with comments resolved.
- [ ] Every Critical/High threat verified closed or accepted with Owner sign-off.

## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA default-on for net-new UI stories, and R3's Design gate calls out design-QA on ticket, confirmation and danger states specifically. This ticket audits the **built** product against the E31-D01 / E31-D02 / E31-D03 specs.

**This is an audit ticket, not a design-system contribution.** Every component variant, token and motion rule E31 needs was contributed in **E31-D02 (Sprint 15)** — two sprints ahead of the first consuming story — so the design-ahead rule in `00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence is satisfied upstream. A design-QA pass must by definition run *after* the code it inspects, so scheduling it in Sprint 18 behind E31-S02/S05/S06 is correct and is not a design-ahead violation. If this audit uncovers a need for a genuinely new component, token or motion rule, it is **not** authored here: it is filed as a Bug plus a design-system request against `16-design-system-brief.md`, and the consuming story is fixed in-sprint using existing tokens.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Side-by-side audit of the running demo build against the redlines for: SCR-030 trading layer (all line kinds and states), SCR-040, SCR-050 armed/locked and drag states, SCR-072 flatten/cancel-all confirmations, SCR-076 reverse confirmation.
- Check spacing, type, tokens (no raw colours), target sizes at both densities, light and dark, z-order over dense footprint and an active heatmap.
- Motion audit against the D04 spec including `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Copy audit against the copy deck — verbatim, including the snapped-to-tick tooltip, the wrong-side confirm, "Already filled", "nothing to flatten", and the disarmed lock tooltip.
- Every discrepancy either fixed within the sprint or filed as a Bug with `priority/*` set and linked here.

## Out of scope
Functional correctness (E31-Q02) and a11y automation (E31-Q05) — though obvious defects in either are still filed.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Pixel and token conformance
  Given the built trading overlay next to the redlines
  Then spacing, type and colour tokens match, and any deviation is logged with a screenshot

Scenario: Danger states audited
  Given flatten, cancel-all and reverse
  Then each confirmation matches its spec exactly, including the absence of a default-focused confirm for LIVE market actions

Scenario: Reduced motion honoured
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then no pulse or spring animation plays and every state remains distinguishable
```

## Technical notes / design
Audit on the reference machine at 2560×1440 and on the smallest supported window size, with footprint + heatmap active so overlay legibility is tested at worst case.

## Test plan
Checklist-driven manual pass; screenshots attached per screen/state; a re-check pass after fixes.

## Security notes
Verify the environment badge and arm indicator are present and unmistakable on every trading-capable surface; a missing badge is a `priority/p0-critical` bug, not a cosmetic one.

## Accessibility notes
Spot-check focus rings, target sizes and the keyboard reposition path; full audit is E31-Q05.

## Performance notes
Note any visual stutter during drag; hand measurements to E31-Q03 rather than diagnosing here.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every screen/state audited with evidence attached.
- [ ] Discrepancies fixed or filed with priority.
- [ ] Designer sign-off comment posted on each consuming story.
- [ ] Re-check after fixes recorded.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-S02**, **E31-S05**, **E31-S06** — the drag-to-amend, ladder-drag and flatten/reverse surfaces must be merged to demo before they can be audited. All three land in Sprint 18 and this audit runs in the second half of the same sprint, after their merge.

Reference artefacts: E31-D01 (chart hi-fi), E31-D02 (DOM hi-fi, design-system variants, motion, a11y review), E31-D03 (redlines and copy deck). Contributes no new design-system entries — see Context.

## Branch
`design/e31-design-qa` (findings only; fixes land on feature branches).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §17 ORD (US-ORD-007..011), §11 DOM (US-DOM-006..008)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-040, SCR-050, SCR-063, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-076, SCR-077
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-192, CMP-229, CMP-230, CMP-119, CMP-120, CMP-130, CMP-158, CMP-232, CMP-227, CMP-044, CMP-043
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` rows US-ORD-007..011, US-DOM-007..008
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/orders`, `/orders/{orderId}` (PATCH/DELETE), `/orders/cancel-all`, `/positions/{positionId}/close`, `/positions/{positionId}/reverse`, `/positions/{positionId}/tpsl`, `/positions/close-all`, `/orders/{orderId}/diagnostics`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §private topics `orders`, `positions`, `executions`, `wallet`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` `orders`, `order_events`, `positions`, `audit_log`
- `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` OrderState / OrderIntent
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.9 hit-testing, §3.11 interaction, §4 layers, §12 accessibility
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 shedding ladder, §5 order-ack budget (#4)
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7 R3 train, §7.3 exit criteria 2 (safety invariant by every path incl. chart drag and DOM click)
- ADR-0006 OMS state machine, ADR-0008 trade-group fan-out, ADR-0002 custom WebGL engine

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `CONSTITUTION.md #scope-guardrails-and-invariants`
2. `AGENTS.md #0-read-these-first`
3. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md#39-hit-testing`

6. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web/src/features/e31/`
- `apps/web/tests/e31/`
- `packages/chart-engine/src/layers/`

**Interfaces you must not break**
- REST `/orders`, `/orders/{orderId}`, `/orders/cancel-all`, `/positions/{id}/close|reverse|tpsl`; WS topics `orders`, `positions`, `executions`; machine B1 Order events

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`, `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:a11y` (web UI tickets), `pnpm e2e` (E2E tickets)

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e31-design-qa-of-shipped`
- PR title: `E31-D07: Design QA of shipped chart and DOM trading`
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/frontend (+ @CandleViewer/security for oms-execution/risk paths, @CandleViewer/design-system for packages/ui)
- Labels: type/design, area/charting-ui, priority/p1, design, design-qa

**Done means**
- All Gherkin scenarios in `## Acceptance criteria` pass as automated tests referencing the scenario name.
- Coverage gate met for touched files/packages (frontend >=80%, backend `--cov-fail-under=85`).
- CI required checks green (lint, typecheck, unit, and any contract-suite/a11y/perf gate this ticket triggers).
- Security review / abuse-case notes recorded where the ticket carries the `security` label.
- Definition of Done checklist in the ticket body fully checked off.

**Do NOT**
- Do not create/manage statechart interpreters outside `cv.statechart.factory` (ADR-0016, C-hot-path).
- Do not widen ticket scope beyond `## Scope / Deliverables`; split into a follow-up ticket instead.
- Do not edit already-applied Alembic migrations; add a new migration.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the GitHub issue for `E31-D07` naming the exact blocking ticket/gate; set Status -> Blocked on the board; never silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or bypass CI checks to get green.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Test plan and E2E suite for chart and DOM trading
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan per feature, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes QA sign-off non-skippable for every Story. E31 spans six interaction surfaces with heavy state coupling (arm state, environment, kill-switch, risk lockouts, RBAC role, book freshness, connection state), so the plan must be written from the specification (E31-D06 handoff) before the build, not derived from the implementation afterwards.

R3's E2E quality gate explicitly names "chart trading, DOM trading" among the Playwright web + Electron flows that must exist. These are the automated proof that the direct-manipulation surfaces behave — and, critically, the automated proof of R3 exit criterion 2: that **no path** can open a position without a native stop.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A black-box plan covering US-ORD-007, US-ORD-008, US-ORD-009, US-ORD-010, US-ORD-011, US-DOM-007, US-DOM-008 across SCR-030, SCR-040, SCR-050, SCR-063, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-076, SCR-077.
- **State matrix** to be exercised for every action: {armed, disarmed} × {demo} × {kill-switch on/off} × {lockout on/off} × {owner, manager, viewer} × {book fresh, stale, resynchronising, disconnected} — with the expected outcome stated per cell (submit / refuse-with-reason / open-ticket / hard-disabled) so testers are never guessing.
- Per-story scenario scripts including every Gherkin failure case: invalid side/price, amend rejected, drag through price, already-filled cancel, nothing to flatten, insufficient margin on reverse, partial flatten-group failure, late/absent WS acknowledgement.
- Boundary catalogue: tick-size rounding at the half tick, min-lot boundaries, percent-preset resolution with stale wallet data, notional threshold for the delete confirm, undo window at expiry ±1 s, 24 px targets at compact density.
- Data setup: demo accounts, a 3-account trade group, a symbol with a coarse tick size and one with a fine tick size, a pre-seeded position and pre-seeded working orders.
- Defect-reporting conventions: any missing native stop, any action possible while disarmed/kill-switched, and any silent partial success are `priority/p0-critical` by definition.
- Entry/exit criteria for the QA pass and the traceability table story → scenario → test case id.

- Playwright specs (web **and** Electron shell) under the existing E2E project, against **demo**:
  1. **Chart click** → limit placed at the tick-snapped price → line renders → order visible via the API → cancel from the chart.
  2. **Chart drag** → amend → exchange price matches → undo within the window restores the original price.
  3. **Chart drag refusal** → stop dragged through price → assert **zero** order-amend network requests (network-level assertion, not a UI assertion).
  4. **DOM click** → limit at a bid row → own-order marker appears → drag to another row → price matches → cancel from the marker.
  5. **Disarmed** → chart click and ladder click each open a pre-filled ticket and submit nothing.
  6. **Flatten** → position + two working orders → flatten → both cancelled and position closed, reported as one operation.
  7. **Flatten no-op** → nothing open → assert zero network calls and the "nothing to flatten" message.
  8. **Reverse** → long → reverse → resulting short with a fresh native stop, confirmation mandatory even when armed.
  9. **Safety sweep (the exit-criterion test)**: parameterised over every E31 entry path (chart click, chart drag, DOM click, DOM drag, flatten, reverse) asserting that (a) every position-opening action results in a native exchange-side stop, and (b) the action is refused while disarmed, while kill-switched and while locked out. Zero escapes.
  10. **RBAC**: a `viewer` session cannot operate any E31 affordance; a forced API call returns 403 with no state change and an audit row.
- Deterministic fixtures and helpers: demo account seeding, position/order seeding and teardown, a helper asserting "no request matched this endpoint", and a helper reading the audit log to assert provenance fields.
- Stability requirements: no arbitrary sleeps — wait on the private WS events; each spec idempotent and re-runnable; tagged so the safety sweep can run as a **required check** on PRs touching `area/oms-execution`.

## Out of scope
Writing automation (E31-Q02). Performance scripting (E31-Q03). A11y audit (E31-Q05).

Perf/load (Q03), chaos (Q04), a11y automation (Q05), unit/component tests (owned by the stories).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every story scenario has a test case
  Given the seven user stories and their Gherkin scenarios
  Then each scenario maps to at least one numbered manual test case, including every failure scenario

Scenario: The state matrix is exhaustive and decided
  Then every cell of the state matrix has a stated expected outcome, with no "TBD"

Scenario: The plan is executable by someone who did not write it
  Given a tester new to the epic
  Then they can set up the data and execute the plan from the document alone
```

```gherkin
Scenario: All ten flows green in both shells
  Given the Playwright suite on web and Electron against demo
  Then all ten specs pass, three consecutive runs, with no flakes

Scenario: Safety sweep is a gate
  Given a deliberately broken build in which one path skips the native stop
  Then the safety sweep fails and blocks the merge queue

Scenario: Refusals are proven at the network layer
  Given the refusal specs
  Then they assert the absence of the corresponding network request, not merely the presence of an error message

Scenario: Provenance asserted
  Given a DOM click-trade
  Then the suite reads back the audit record and asserts source, modifier and price row
```

## Technical notes / design
Execute exclusively against **staging (demo)** per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 — never live. Use the demo environment's REST-only order-entry constraint as a deliberate test condition.

Demo has **no WS order entry** (REST only) — the suite must not assume WS submission. Acknowledgements still arrive on the private WS topics and are the correct thing to await.

Run the suite against a dedicated demo sub-account so parallel CI runs cannot interfere; serialise the safety sweep if account state contention is observed.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the plan; its own validation is a review by the SDET lead and the E31 engineering lead confirming testability of every case.

Self-referential: the suite's own reliability is validated by three consecutive clean runs and by the deliberately-broken-build check for the safety sweep.

## Security notes
The plan must include the security-relevant negative cases (disarmed, kill-switched, locked out, viewer role, out-of-scope account) as first-class test cases, not as a security-team-only concern; results feed E31-X03.

Credentials for the demo accounts come from the CI secret store, never from the repo; the suite must fail closed if it detects a `live` environment target. Add an explicit assertion at suite start that `environment === 'demo'`.

## Accessibility notes
The plan includes keyboard-only execution of the full happy path for each surface as a mandatory case (the detailed audit remains E31-Q05).

At least the chart-click and DOM-click flows must have a keyboard-only variant in the suite, so the keyboard paths are regression-protected rather than only manually checked.

## Performance notes
Includes the felt-latency observations (click→visible acknowledgement) as a qualitative case, with the measured version in E31-Q03.

Suite wall-clock ≤12 min in CI; the safety sweep alone ≤4 min so it is viable as a required check.

## Observability
Each test case states which audit event should exist afterwards, so testers verify auditing as part of functional testing.

Suite emits per-spec timings; failures attach the correlation ids of the orders involved so backend logs can be joined.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan merged in the QA test-plan repo/space and linked from every E31 story.
- [ ] State matrix complete with no TBDs.
- [ ] Reviewed and accepted by the SDET lead and engineering lead.
- [ ] Test data setup scripted or documented step by step.

- [ ] All ten specs implemented, green on web and Electron, three consecutive runs.
- [ ] Safety sweep wired as a required check for `area/oms-execution` PRs.
- [ ] Fixtures/helpers documented for reuse by E32/E33/E34.
- [ ] Demo-only guard asserted; secrets handled via CI store.
- [ ] Reviewed by the SDET lead; linked from every E31 story.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-D03** (the handoff package and copy deck the black-box cases are written from, Done end of S15), plus **E31-S01** and **E31-S04** for the first executable slices. The plan is authored in Sprint 17 as the S17 stories land, and the suite is extended in Sprint 18 as E31-S02/S03/S05/S06 merge.

Merges the former E31-Q01 (test plan) and E31-Q02 (E2E suite) into one QA deliverable to fit E31's 26-point roadmap budget; no planned case or scenario was dropped.

## Branch
`test/e31-trading-e2e` — plan in `docs/qa/`, specs under `apps/web/e2e/trading/`. PRs ≤400 LOC.

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-040, SCR-050, SCR-063, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-076, SCR-077

title: Perf, chaos and a11y audit plus QA sign-off for chart & DOM trading
body:
## Context
E31 carries three hard numbers: click→submit ≤50 ms client-side, click→ack p95 <300 ms on demo (budget #4), and a ≤2 ms trading-overlay redraw with trading data exempt from the shedding ladder (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3, §5). These must be measured in CI, not asserted in a ticket.

R3's Chaos gate requires "WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out — all resume to a correct, reconciled state". E31's contribution is the *direct-manipulation* half: what happens to an optimistic drag, a pending click-trade or a half-finished flatten when the world breaks underneath it. The failure mode being hunted is a UI that shows a settled state the exchange never agreed to.

R3's A11y gate requires the DOM ladder to be fully keyboard-operable and danger/confirm patterns to be announced. E31 is the epic that makes the ladder and the chart *actionable*, so this audit decides whether the R3 gate passes. `05-accessibility-standard.md` grants no "trading tools are special" exemption.

Scripted tests only find the failures someone imagined. E31's danger lies in the combinations nobody wrote down: dragging while the symbol changes, clicking while the arm timer expires, flattening while a fill lands. This ticket adds time-boxed exploratory testing, folds E31 into the standing regression pack, and carries the epic-level QA sign-off required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmark** (extends the existing chart-engine bench harness): overlay redraw cost at 1/5/20/50 order lines, measured under the worst-case scene (100k bars, footprint on, 200-depth heatmap live), in Electron and Chromium, on the reference machine. Asserts ≤2 ms and asserts fps ≥30 floor.
- **Shedding-ladder assertion**: drive the engine into the stress scenario and assert that heatmap cadence and footprint text degrade first while **order-line and position-line updates continue every frame** — the "never acceptable" rule made executable.
- **Client-side interaction latency harness**: instrument pointerdown→`fetch` issued for chart click, chart drag commit, DOM click and DOM drag commit; assert p95 ≤50 ms; publish p50/p95/p99.
- **k6 script** for the order path: sustained click-trade-equivalent order submission against demo at a realistic manual rate and at the per-UID limit, asserting ack p95 <300 ms and correct `10018` back-off behaviour without lost acknowledgements.
- Baseline numbers recorded from E31-K01 promoted into assertions with an agreed regression threshold; results published to the perf dashboard per `06-...` reporting conventions.
- CI wiring: engine benchmark on every PR touching the overlay or the engine; k6 on a nightly schedule against demo.

Chaos scenarios, automated where possible and scripted-manual otherwise, run against demo:
1. **WS dropped mid-amend**: drag commits, REST ack received, WS killed before the order event → assert the marker/line shows *unreconciled* (not settled), reconnect restores truth, and the final rendered price equals the exchange price.
2. **REST times out, order actually placed**: inject a timeout after the exchange accepted → assert the idempotency key prevents a duplicate on retry and the reconciliation loop surfaces the real order rather than an orphan.
3. **Backend restart mid-flatten**: kill the backend between the cancel-all leg and the close leg → assert the UI reports a visible partial state, and after restart the reconciliation shows the true position; assert no silent "flattened" claim.
4. **Exchange 5xx / `10018` storm during click-trading**: assert back-off with jitter, the user-visible rate-limit message, and no lost acknowledgements.
5. **Clock skew**: skew the client clock → assert undo-window timing and stale-book detection degrade safely (fail closed: disable trading affordances rather than trust the clock).
6. **Slow consumer**: force the client into the WS slow-consumer path → assert `orders`/`executions` are never dropped (protocol rule) and the client is disconnected with `4429` rather than shown a wrong position.
7. **Kill-switch flipped mid-drag**: assert the in-flight commit is refused, the line springs back, and the reason is shown.
8. **Disconnect during the undo window**: assert undo is unavailable rather than silently failing, with an honest message.
- Each scenario documents: injection method, expected system behaviour, observable evidence (UI state, audit rows, metrics), and pass criteria.

- **Automated**: axe-core in CI across SCR-030 (trading layer on), SCR-040, SCR-050 (armed and locked), SCR-063, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-076 — zero serious/critical violations, with any accepted exception documented and approved.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with NVDA + Chrome/Electron and VoiceOver + Safari/Chrome, covering:
  - Placing an order from the chart by keyboard; repositioning a line by arrow keys; committing and abandoning.
  - Ladder grid navigation with roving tabindex; opening the row action menu; placing, moving and cancelling by keyboard.
  - Flatten, cancel-all and reverse confirmations: focus trap, focus return, action restated in the accessible name, the 400 ms Enter guard.
  - Pending → acknowledged → rejected announcements: correct politeness, no announcement storms during a drag, auto-disarm announced when it fires.
- **Target size** measurement (2.5.8) for line handles, ladder rows and marker cancel affordances at every density; **non-text contrast** (1.4.11) for lines/handles/focus rings measured over dense footprint and an active heatmap.
- **Colour independence** (1.4.1): buy/sell, SL/TP and pending state each verified distinguishable in greyscale and with a deuteranopia simulation.
- **Reduced motion**: all E31 motion verified to degrade per the D04 spec with state still conveyed.
- **DOM-mirror parity**: verify the accessible mirror matches rendered state, including under the shedding ladder (cross-check with E31-Q03's parity assertion).
- Findings logged per WCAG SC with severity; blockers must be fixed before the epic's DoD.

- **Exploratory charters** (2 hours each, session-based, with notes and any defect filed immediately):
  1. "Race the state": change symbol, switch account/trade group, let the arm timer expire, toggle environment and flip the kill-switch *while* drags and click-trades are in flight.
  2. "Fat fingers": rapid repeated clicks, click-and-micro-drag, drag off-canvas, drag onto another pane, double-click, middle-click, touch/trackpad gestures, browser zoom at 200 %.
  3. "Fills during interaction": arrange for fills and partial fills to land during a drag, during a pending amend and during a flatten.
  4. "Multi-pane and multi-window": two charts on the same symbol, chart plus ladder on the same symbol, Electron second window — assert overlays and pending state stay consistent everywhere.
  5. "Undo boundaries": undo at the window's edge, undo after a partial fill, undo twice, undo after the symbol changed.
- **Regression pack additions**: the E31 smoke path (place from chart, drag, cancel, DOM place, flatten) added to the standing pre-release regression suite, plus the safety sweep referenced as a required gate.
- **Epic-level QA sign-off**: execute the E31-Q01 black-box plan end to end on the release candidate build, record pass/fail per scenario, confirm all E31 tickets' QA sign-offs exist, and confirm no open P0/P1 defects in E31 scope.
- A short QA report for the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Out of scope
Backend ingestion/fan-out load (E17/E21/E34 scripts). Chaos (Q04).

Backend-internal failover mechanics (E45 owns reconciliation/chaos at large; this ticket is the E31 surface behaviour and feeds E45's suite).

Design-stage review (E31-D05, already done) and non-E31 chart surfaces.

Fixing defects (they route to the owning story or a new Bug). Non-E31 regression content.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overlay budget enforced
  Given the worst-case scene with 20 order lines
  Then the measured overlay redraw is at most 2 ms and the benchmark fails the build if it regresses beyond the agreed threshold

Scenario: Trading data is never shed
  Given the engine is driven into the stress scenario
  Then heatmap cadence and footprint text degrade, order and position lines still update every frame,
  and the test fails if a trading-line update is dropped

Scenario: Interaction latency measured, not estimated
  Then p50, p95 and p99 for pointerdown to request-issued are published per surface, and p95 is at most 50 ms

Scenario: Order ack budget holds under load
  Given the k6 profile at the per-UID limit
  Then ack p95 is under 300 ms, no acknowledgement is lost, and 10018 back-off is observed with jitter
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Never a false settled state
  Given any injected failure in any of the eight scenarios
  Then the UI never displays an order or position state that the exchange did not confirm

Scenario: No duplicate orders from retries
  Given a REST timeout on an order that was actually accepted
  Then no duplicate order exists on the exchange after the client's retry behaviour completes

Scenario: Partial flatten is visible
  Given the backend dies between the cancel and close legs
  Then the user sees an explicit partial state with a next action, never a success message

Scenario: Fail closed on clock skew
  Given a skewed client clock
  Then trading affordances disable with a stated reason rather than acting on untrustworthy timing
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Zero critical automated violations
  Given axe-core over the seven screens in their trading-enabled states
  Then there are no serious or critical violations, or each has a documented, approved exception

Scenario: Full keyboard operation proven
  Given a keyboard-only user
  Then they can place, reprice, cancel, flatten and reverse from both the chart and the ladder,
  with every outcome announced

Scenario: No drag-only functionality
  Then every pointer-driven capability in E31 has a verified keyboard equivalent, evidenced by a recorded pass

Scenario: Targets and contrast measured
  Then every interactive target is at least 24 px at compact density and every line/handle/focus ring
  meets 3:1 non-text contrast over the worst-case background
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Charters executed with evidence
  Given the five charters
  Then each has a session sheet with notes, coverage areas touched and defects raised

Scenario: No open P0/P1 at sign-off
  Given the epic-level pass
  Then no P0 or P1 defect remains open in E31 scope, or sign-off is withheld

Scenario: Regression pack updated
  Then the E31 smoke path runs as part of the standing pre-release regression and passes on the candidate build

Scenario: Sign-off is recorded per scenario
  Then the black-box plan shows an explicit pass or fail for every numbered case, with the tester and build id
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure on the reference machine defined in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; record GPU/driver and shell versions with every result, since R8 browser/GPU compatibility is a live risk.

The k6 script must use demo credentials from the secret store and must be rate-aware — the point is to prove the governor, not to trip the exchange into punishing the account.

Injection via the existing test proxy/toxiproxy-style layer for WS and REST, container restarts for the backend, and a clock-offset harness for the client. Every run captures the audit log slice and the relevant metrics window as evidence.

Test in the Electron shell as the primary environment (it is the primary shell) *and* in a browser, because AT behaviour differs; record versions of AT, OS and shell with every result.

All execution on demo, on the release-candidate build, in both web and Electron. Session notes follow the team's session-based test management format.

## Test plan
The scripts are the tests; their validity is checked by injecting a known 5 ms artificial delay into the overlay path and confirming the benchmark detects it.

Each scenario is a scripted run with a written expected/actual record; the four automatable ones (1, 2, 4, 7) join the nightly chaos job.

Automated axe run in CI plus a scripted manual protocol per surface; each manual pass produces a recording and a findings sheet keyed to WCAG SCs.

## Security notes
Scripts must be hard-guarded to demo; a live target must abort the run. No credential appears in the results or the dashboard. Load generation must not be usable as an unauthenticated tool — it authenticates through the normal session path.

Chaos runs are demo-only and must not disable the safety invariant as part of the injection — a scenario that would place an unprotected position is itself a failure to report, not a test setup step. Verify audit continuity across restarts (the hash-chained `audit_log` must remain verifiable).

Confirm that keyboard/AT paths enforce the same arm, confirm-policy, kill-switch and RBAC gates as pointer paths — an accessibility path must never become a safety bypass. Explicitly test: arming via keyboard in LIVE requires the deliberate second action (CMP-229 spec).

Charters must include at least one deliberate attempt to trade while disarmed, kill-switched, locked out and as `viewer`; any success is a `priority/p0-critical` security defect routed to E31-X03 immediately rather than merely filed.

## Accessibility notes
Assert that the DOM-mirror accessibility layer stays in sync with the rendered state under shedding (`06-...` §4.3 forbids desync) — an automated parity check of mirrored line prices vs rendered line prices.

Assert that degraded/unreconciled/disconnected states are announced, not merely styled, since these are exactly the moments a user most needs to be told something changed.

This ticket is the accessibility evidence for the epic and for the R3 gate.

One charter session is run keyboard-only to catch a11y regressions the automated audit could miss.

## Performance notes
This ticket is the performance evidence for the epic's DoD and feeds the R3 §7.4 Load gate.

Assert recovery time: after reconnect, the UI reflects true exchange state within the reconciliation loop's stated interval.

Check that live-region updates during drags and high-frequency ladder updates do not cause AT lag; if they do, the throttling from E31-T01/D05 is insufficient and a defect is filed.

Testers record any perceptible stutter or latency and cross-check against E31-Q03's numbers before filing.

## Observability
Results published to the perf dashboard; `cv_trading_overlay_redraw_ms` and `cv_chart_trade_click_to_submit_ms` histograms validated against the harness numbers so production telemetry is trusted.

Every scenario asserts the expected log/metric/audit evidence exists — `cv_trading_unreconciled_total` increments, back-off metrics move, audit rows persist across restart.

N/A (findings are recorded in the QA system).

Sign-off includes a check that audit rows exist for a sample of every action type performed during the pass — auditing is part of the acceptance, not an afterthought.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four scripts implemented and wired into CI/nightly.
- [ ] Baselines recorded with machine/driver/shell metadata.
- [ ] Injected-regression check proves the benchmarks detect regressions.
- [ ] Results attached to E31 and to the R3 perf evidence pack.
- [ ] Reviewed by the chart-engine lead and the SDET lead.

- [ ] All eight scenarios documented with injection, expectation and evidence.
- [ ] Four automated and wired into the nightly chaos job; four scripted-manual runs executed and recorded.
- [ ] Any defect found filed with `priority/p0-critical` where it involves a false settled state or a duplicate order.
- [ ] Results handed to E45 for inclusion in the broader resilience suite.
- [ ] SDET lead and Architect sign-off.

- [ ] axe-core green in CI across all seven screens in trading-enabled states.
- [ ] NVDA and VoiceOver passes executed and recorded with AT/OS/shell versions.
- [ ] Target-size and contrast measurements recorded.
- [ ] Colour-independence and reduced-motion verified.
- [ ] All blocking findings fixed and re-verified; non-blocking findings filed with priority.
- [ ] Accessibility lead sign-off; result attached to the R3 A11y gate evidence.

- [ ] Five charters executed with session sheets attached.
- [ ] Regression pack updated and green on the candidate.
- [ ] Black-box plan executed with per-scenario results; QA sign-off comment posted on the epic.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 in E31 scope.
- [ ] QA report filed for the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-Q01** (the test plan and E2E harness these extend), **E31-K01** (the Sprint-16 latency methodology and baseline numbers), **E31-S03 / S05 / S06** (the last functional slices) and **E31-D07** (design-QA findings must be dispositioned before sign-off).

Runs in the second half of Sprint 18, strictly after the stories it verifies.

title: STRIDE threat model for chart and DOM trading interactions
body:
## Context
`04-security-program.md` mandates a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.1 makes it default-on for any epic touching the OMS. E31 adds four new order-originating paths (chart click, chart drag, DOM click, DOM drag) plus two destructive ones (flatten, reverse). Each is a new place where an order can be created, so each is a new place where the safety architecture can be bypassed. The model must be done in Sprint 16 so its controls are inputs to E31-T01, not retrofits.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model over the E31 data flow: pointer/keyboard event → intent construction → client guard chain → REST call → OMS validation → exchange → private WS → optimistic-state reconciliation → audit.
- Enumerate and rate (likelihood × impact) at minimum:
  - **Spoofing**: a forged `source`/`modifier` provenance field; a replayed request with a reused idempotency key.
  - **Tampering**: client-side manipulation of the arm state or the guard chain to reach a submission path; manipulation of the cached instrument filters to defeat tick/lot validation; DOM-mirror manipulation to move a line the user cannot see.
  - **Repudiation**: "I never clicked that" — coverage of the audit trail for every surface, incl. undo actions and keyboard paths.
  - **Information disclosure**: ghost lines or aggregate markers exposing accounts outside the session's `account_scope`; rejection details leaking exchange credentials or internal identifiers.
  - **Denial of service**: pointer-storm order flooding burning the per-UID rate budget and denying the user the ability to exit a position (the most dangerous DoS in this product); mass cancel-all abuse.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a `viewer` reaching an order-placing path through a keyboard shortcut, a context menu or a direct API call.
- For each threat: existing control, gap, and the required mitigation with an owning ticket (mitigations land in E31-T01 or the relevant story; anything not mitigated is an explicit accepted risk with Owner sign-off).
- Explicit treatment of the **safety invariant**: enumerate every way an E31 path could produce a position without a native exchange-side stop, and confirm each is closed server-side (client-side refusals are convenience only).
- Abuse-case list handed to E31-X02 and to E31-Q01 so the negative cases are tested, not just modelled.
- Data-classification statement for everything E31 touches (financial, audited; no PII beyond the acting user id).

## Out of scope
The OMS state machine's own threat model (E29-X), key vault (E27), fan-out (E34) — reference them rather than re-deriving.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every STRIDE category covered for every new path
  Given four order-originating and two destructive paths
  Then each has at least one enumerated threat per applicable STRIDE category, with likelihood, impact and a control

Scenario: Invariant escape analysis is exhaustive
  Then every hypothesised route to an unprotected position is listed with the server-side control that closes it,
  and any route without one becomes a P0 ticket

Scenario: Mitigations have owners
  Then every identified gap maps to a specific ticket key, or to a recorded accepted risk signed by the Owner
```

## Technical notes / design
Model against the actual endpoints (`/orders`, `/orders/{id}` PATCH/DELETE, `/orders/cancel-all`, `/positions/{id}/close|reverse|tpsl`, `/positions/close-all`) and the private WS topics, using the architecture module M14 boundary as the trust boundary — everything client-side is untrusted.

## Test plan
The model's assertions become test cases: each claimed control must name the test (unit, E2E safety sweep, or manual abuse case) that proves it.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security analysis; output is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Architect, and its Critical/High findings must be closed before the R3 Security gate.

## Accessibility notes
Include the a11y paths in the model explicitly — keyboard shortcuts and AT-driven interactions are order-placing paths and must not be modelled as second-class.

## Performance notes

title: Abuse cases, RBAC/arm bypass checks and security sign-off for trading surfaces
body:
## Context
E31-X01 produces the theory; this ticket produces the proof and the automation. Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, anything touching order placement requires a *manual abuse-case check* — attempting the attack, not just reasoning about it — plus clean SAST/SCA.

The final security gate for E31 before the epic can be Done and before R3's Security quality gate is assessed. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 states that anything touching order placement is treated as `security`-labelled for DoD purposes whether or not the label was applied — this ticket is where that is enforced across all E31 children.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Executed abuse cases** against demo, each with recorded evidence (request, response, UI state, audit row):
  1. Place an order from chart and from ladder while **disarmed** — expect refusal, no request, logged.
  2. Same while the **kill-switch is engaged** — expect refusal at the client and rejection (`trading_disabled`) at the server if forced.
  3. Same while a **risk lockout** is active (E39) — expect refusal + audit.
  4. As a **`viewer`** role: exercise every E31 affordance in the UI (expect hard-disabled) and force each endpoint directly (expect 403, **no state change**, audit row).
  5. Against an **account outside `account_scope`**: force order create, amend, cancel, close and reverse — expect 403 + audit for each.
  6. **Idempotency replay**: resend an identical order request with the same key — expect exactly one order.
  7. **Provenance forgery**: submit with a fabricated `source`/`modifier`/`price_row` — expect the order to be validated identically (provenance advisory only) and the forged value recorded as-received without influencing behaviour; confirm unknown `source` values are rejected.
  8. **Filter tampering**: submit a price off-tick and a quantity off-lot directly to the API — expect server-side rejection regardless of client-side snapping.
  9. **Invariant bypass attempt**: attempt, via each E31 path and via direct API calls, to open a position without a native stop — expect zero escapes (this is R3 exit criterion 2 and must be evidenced here as well as in the E2E sweep).
  10. **Order flood**: burst submissions from the ladder path — expect duplicate suppression, governor back-off, and — critically — that the user can still **exit** a position while throttled (exit paths must not be starved by entry flooding).
- **SAST/Semgrep rules** added for this area: flag any component issuing an order/position mutation without going through `packages/trading-intent`; flag any client-side-only authorisation check presented as the sole gate; flag direct `fetch` to order endpoints outside the adapter.
- **DAST**: ZAP profile additions covering the E31 endpoints with an authenticated `viewer` session, asserting 403 on every mutation.
- SCA/secrets scan confirmation for the new frontend module.

- **White-box review** of the shipped code for: `packages/trading-intent` (guard chain ordering, idempotency, reconciliation), the chart trading layer, the ladder trading affordances, the flatten/reverse saga, and the M14 provenance enrichment.
- Verify against the E31-X01 model that every claimed control exists in code and is covered by a named test; any control that is asserted but untested is a finding.
- Confirm: client-side checks are never the sole gate; the server validates independently on every path; provenance cannot influence validation; RBAC is enforced per account on every mutation; the safety invariant has no E31-reachable escape.
- Review the audit completeness: every E31 action type produces an audit row with actor, account, symbol, surface, modifier, price and correlation id, and the `audit_log` hash chain still verifies after an E31-heavy session.
- Confirm the R3 Security gate items relevant to E31: STRIDE findings all Critical/High closed; abuse-case results recorded; SAST/DAST/SCA clean or triaged.
- Post the sign-off comment on E31 and on each child story that requires one; record any accepted risks with Owner sign-off and an expiry/review date.
- Hand the residual risk list to E43 (hardening & pen-test remediation) so the pre-R4 pen-test scopes these surfaces explicitly.

## Out of scope
Pen-test (E43, pre-R4). Key vault abuse cases (E27). Fan-out partial-failure abuse (E34).

Re-running the abuse cases (E31-X02) or the QA pass (E31-Q06) — this ticket consumes their evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case executed with evidence
  Given the ten cases
  Then each has a recorded attempt, the observed result, and the audit row it produced

Scenario: No escape from the safety invariant
  Given every E31 path and direct API calls
  Then no attempt produces a position without a native exchange-side stop

Scenario: Exit is never starved
  Given an order flood that trips the rate governor
  Then flatten and cancel remain possible for the user within the documented time, and this is demonstrated

Scenario: SAST rules catch a real violation
  Given a deliberately introduced direct fetch to the order endpoint from a component
  Then the Semgrep rule fails the build
```

```gherkin
Scenario: Every modelled control is real and tested
  Given the E31-X01 threat model
  Then each control is located in code and mapped to a named test, or it is raised as a finding

Scenario: No Critical or High remains open
  Then all Critical and High findings are fixed and re-verified, or accepted in writing by the Owner with a review date

Scenario: Audit chain verifies
  Given a session containing every E31 action type
  Then every action has an audit row with the required fields and the hash-chain verification passes

Scenario: Sign-off recorded where required
  Then a Security engineer sign-off comment exists on the epic and on every child requiring one
```

## Technical notes / design
Direct-API attempts use the same session tokens the UI would hold, to prove server-side enforcement rather than client-side absence. Every forced attempt must be verified to produce an audit row — a silent 403 is itself a finding.

Review with the E31-X01 model open as the checklist; treat the guard-chain ordering as the highest-value review target, since a reordering bug silently weakens every surface at once.

## Test plan
Abuse cases are executed manually and, where stable, promoted into the E2E safety sweep (E31-Q02 spec 9/10) so they regress automatically.

Review-driven; validation is the mapping table (control → code location → test name) with no unmapped rows.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security verification for E31. Findings are triaged with the Security engineer; Critical/High must be fixed before the R3 Security gate closes; accepted risks need Owner sign-off.

This ticket is the sign-off itself. Findings raised here that cannot be fixed within R3 must be logged in `32-risk-register.md` and explicitly scoped into E43.

## Accessibility notes
Repeat cases 1–4 through keyboard/AT paths, confirming accessible routes enforce identical gates.

Confirm the a11y paths were included in the abuse testing and enforce identical gates — a keyboard route that skips a confirm is a security finding, not a UX nit.

## Performance notes
Case 10 must record the observed back-off behaviour and the latency of the exit path under flood, feeding E31-Q03's evidence.

Confirm the security controls (duplicate suppression, back-off, guard evaluation) stay inside the ≤5 ms guard budget so they are not disabled later for speed.

## Observability
Confirm `cv_trading_intent_refused_total{reason}` increments correctly per refusal type and that audit rows carry the acting user, account, surface and correlation id in every forced case.

Confirm security telemetry is wired and visible: refusal counts by reason, 403 counts by route and role, anomalous submission rate.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ten abuse cases executed with evidence attached.
- [ ] Semgrep rules merged and proven by an injected violation; ZAP profile updated.
- [ ] SAST/SCA/secrets scans clean or triaged.
- [ ] Findings triaged; Critical/High fixed and re-verified.
- [ ] Stable cases promoted into the E2E safety sweep.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off.

- [ ] Control → code → test mapping complete with no unmapped rows.
- [ ] All Critical/High closed or accepted with Owner sign-off and a review date.
- [ ] Audit completeness and hash-chain verification demonstrated.
- [ ] Sign-off comments posted on E31 and its children.
- [ ] Residual risks handed to E43 and recorded in `32-risk-register.md`.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E31-X01** (the threat model whose Critical/High items these checks close), **E31-S04** and **E31-S06** (the click-to-trade and flatten/reverse surfaces under test) and **E31-Q02** (QA sign-off, which must precede security sign-off).

Merges the former E31-X02 (abuse cases + SAST) and E31-X03 (security review and sign-off) into one Sprint-18 deliverable within E31's 26-point roadmap budget. Also re-verifies the **E30** and **E32** integration points (arm/lock, confirmation policy, native-SL invariant) now that both epics have closed at the end of Sprint 17.

body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 makes design QA a default-on DoD item for net-new UI stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec (spacing, tokens, type, colour, states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer, with discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bugs with a priority. E32 ships three net-new screens, and their most important detail — the way the native-SL guarantee is presented — is exactly the kind of thing that silently degrades during implementation.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the per-screen design-QA checklists from E32-D07's handoff pack against the built `SCR-064`, `SCR-065` and `SCR-069` on staging (demo), in light and dark themes and both densities.
- Verify every enumerated state by driving the app into it (including partial-placement failure, risk-cap refusal, pending, rejected and position-closed-while-editing), not by reading code.
- Specific verifications: CMP-158's note is persistent text and never a tooltip or toast on all three screens; the stop field restores rather than clears; the ladder preview is a real table; the submit buttons name their full action; the trailing translation readout shows both the user's unit and the absolute distance; pending never renders as confirmed.
- Motion checked against the spec including the reduced-motion fallback.
- Published report with pass/fail per checklist item and evidence (screenshots per state).
- p0/p1 discrepancies fixed on the owning story's branch before it closes; p2/p3 filed as Bugs with owners and priorities.
- Confirm that each audited control listed in the handoff pack's event map actually produces its audit event.

## Out of scope

```gherkin
Scenario: All three screens are reviewed against their checklists
  Given the built screens on staging
  When the checklists are executed in both themes and densities
  Then a report records pass or fail per item with screenshot evidence for every enumerated state

Scenario: The safety notice survived implementation
  Given CMP-158 on SCR-064, SCR-065 and SCR-069

Scenario: A discrepancy is dispositioned, not just noted (failure)

  Then it is filed as a Bug with a priority and an owner rather than listed only in the report

Scenario: Audited controls emit their events (edge)

```

title: Write the black-box test plan for scaled and DCA ladders
body:
## Context
`US-ALGO-004` and `US-ALGO-009` concentrate their risk in arithmetic and in partial-failure handling — the two things that are hardest to verify by reading code and easiest to verify by black-box execution with awkward numbers. `24-internal-schemas.md` section 10.6 specifies rounding, duplicate-price merging, remainder placement and sub-minimum redistribution precisely enough that each rule is independently testable, and `US-ALGO-009`'s NFR ("projected risk computed for the fully-filled ladder, never for the first leg alone") is a single sentence that, if wrong, lets a trader ladder straight through their risk cap.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Test plan `docs/qa/plans/e32-ladders.md` covering `US-ALGO-004` and `US-ALGO-009`.
- Arithmetic scenarios executed against deliberately awkward instruments and sizes: quantities that do not divide evenly, price ranges narrower than `levels * tickSize` (forcing duplicate-price merges), totals near the minimum notional, 2-level and 50-level boundaries, each distribution (equal, linear, geometric, custom) and skew above and below 1.
- Verification that the preview table and the placed orders match exactly, level by level, in every arithmetic scenario — this is the single highest-value check in the plan.
- Partial-placement scenarios: one leg rejected, several rejected, whole batch rejected, `10018` rate-limit mid-ladder, and per-leg retry behaviour.
- Cancellation scenarios: cancel with none filled, some filled, all filled; verification that a filled portion keeps its protective orders and stays natively stopped.
- DCA scenarios: multiplier laddering, shared-stop behaviour as legs fill, risk-cap refusal with the projected fully-filled figure stated, and the concurrent-leg cap queueing.
- Fixtures named: `batch_partial_success`, `batch_rate_limited`, `batch_full_reject`, `ladder_cap_breach`.
- Traceability table to E32-S03's Gherkin scenarios and to E32-S06's UI scenarios.

## Out of scope
- Bracket/trailing cluster (E32-Q02), automation (E32-Q04), chaos (E32-Q05), perf (E32-Q06), a11y (E32-Q07).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preview and placement are compared level by level
  Given each arithmetic scenario
  When the ladder is previewed and then placed
  Then every level's price and quantity in the preview matches the corresponding placed order exactly, and any divergence is a P0 finding

Scenario: The fully-filled risk projection is verified against the cap
  Given a DCA ladder whose first leg is within the cap but whose fully-filled position is not
  Then the plan verifies the request is refused before any order is sent and the stated projection equals the fully-filled figure, not the first leg's

Scenario: Sub-minimum redistribution is verified, not assumed (edge)
  Given a ladder whose last two levels round below the instrument minimum
  Then the plan checks which levels were dropped, that their quantity was redistributed proportionally, that the response named them, and that the placed total still equals the requested total

Scenario: A partial batch failure is verified end to end (failure)
  Given a batch where legs 2 and 4 are rejected
  Then the plan verifies the other legs remain working, the failures carry their exchange reasons, retry affects only the failed legs, and the audit record reflects the partial outcome
```

## Technical notes / design
Scenarios pin a specific demo instrument and its `tickSize`/`qtyStep`/`minOrderQty` so expected values are exact numbers in the plan, not formulas the tester must evaluate under time pressure. Where Bybit demo will not reliably produce a partial batch failure, the plan specifies the fixture-driven equivalent and says so.

## Test plan
Dry run once on staging before sign-off; expected values recomputed independently by a second person for the arithmetic scenarios (two independent derivations, because a plan that repeats the implementation's arithmetic mistake proves nothing).

## Security notes
Demo only. The "50-level ladder starves the protective reserve" abuse case is owned by E32-X02; this plan cross-references it rather than duplicating it.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — a11y coverage of SCR-065 is E32-Q07.

## Performance notes
The plan includes a step verifying the preview responds within one frame perceptually and that submission is a single backend request regardless of level count.

## Observability
Steps name the expected `algo.scaled_created` / `algo.scaled_partially_cancelled` audit rows and the `oms_scaled_levels_submitted_total` increments.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Plan published and reviewed by the E32 engineering lead.
- [ ] Arithmetic expected values independently derived by a second person.
- [ ] Traceability complete against E32-S03 and E32-S06.
- [ ] Fixtures specified and requested.
- [ ] Dry run executed and findings folded in.

title: Automate the Playwright E2E suite for the three E32 screens on demo
body:
## Context
R3's E2E quality gate (`30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) requires Playwright coverage on **web and Electron** for ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, **bracket**, fan-out, rules, alerts and journal. E32 owns the bracket, ladder and SL/TP editor share of that gate. `03-testing-strategy.md` places E2E at the top of the pyramid: few, high-value, whole-journey tests — so this suite covers the journeys the unit and integration layers structurally cannot.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `e2e/specs/e32/`, running against staging (demo) in **both** the web build and the Electron shell.
- Journeys: (1) build and submit a bracket with a stop and single TP via SCR-069, verify the group appears in the blotter and the position is natively stopped; (2) build a 5-level scaled ladder via SCR-065, verify the preview table matches the placed orders, then cancel the group; (3) open SCR-064 on a live demo position, apply a 1.5% trail, verify the translated distance is displayed and the change resolves from pending to applied; (4) configure a 3-step TP ladder and verify the stop resizes when a leg fills; (5) attempt to clear the stop on each of the three screens and verify the restore-and-explain behaviour.
- Failure-path journeys: unsplittable ladder offering its single-target alternative; risk-cap refusal restating the projection; exchange rejection resolving pending to rejected with the reason shown; position closed while SCR-064 is open.
- Deterministic setup/teardown: each spec creates its own position from a known state and flattens it afterwards, so specs can run in any order and a failed spec cannot poison the next.
- Electron parity: the same specs run in the desktop shell, with any divergence recorded as a Bug rather than a skipped test.
- Wired into CI as a nightly job plus a pre-release gate; flake budget and quarantine policy per `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Out of scope
- Backend-only paths (covered by E32-Q01/Q02/Q03), perf (E32-Q06), a11y audit (E32-Q07), chaos (E32-Q05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All five happy journeys pass in web and Electron
  Given the suite runs against staging demo
  Then each journey passes in both the web build and the Electron shell, and any Electron-only failure is filed as a Bug rather than skipped

Scenario: The preview-versus-placement check is a first-class assertion
  Given the scaled ladder journey
  Then the spec reads the preview table from the DOM and asserts each row against the orders returned by GET /api/v1/orders, failing on any divergence

Scenario: Specs are independent and self-cleaning (edge)
  Given the suite runs in a random order with a deliberately failing spec injected
  Then every other spec still passes, and no demo position or working order is left behind after the run

Scenario: A flaky spec is quarantined, not deleted (failure)
  Given a spec failing intermittently above the flake budget
  Then it is quarantined with a linked Bug and an owner, and the quarantine is visible in the suite report rather than silently removed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Selectors use stable `data-testid` attributes agreed with the FE stories, never CSS classes or text that copy changes will break.
- Waits are event-based (WS state, network idle for the specific request) rather than fixed sleeps, because order placement latency on demo is variable.
- Teardown uses the flatten-all API path with a guard that it only ever runs against a demo-tagged account, asserted at spec start — a teardown that could touch live is itself a safety risk.
- Test data: a dedicated demo sub-account per CI runner to avoid cross-run interference.

## Test plan
Self-verifying: the suite is run 10 times consecutively before sign-off to measure flake rate, which must be under the budget in `03-testing-strategy.md`.

## Security notes
Demo credentials are injected from CI secrets, never committed, and the environment guard asserts the target is demo before any order is placed. Screenshots and traces on failure are scrubbed of account identifiers before upload.

## Accessibility notes
Specs navigate by role and accessible name where practical, which incidentally smoke-tests the accessible names; formal a11y coverage remains E32-Q07's.

## Performance notes
Suite wall-clock under 15 minutes so it can gate releases; parallelised per sub-account.

## Observability
Failures upload Playwright traces plus the backend correlation ids for the failed requests, so a failure is diagnosable without re-running.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All journeys automated and green in web and Electron.
- [ ] Flake rate measured over 10 runs and within budget.
- [ ] CI nightly and pre-release gating configured.
- [ ] Teardown demo-guard verified by a test that asserts it refuses a non-demo target.
- [ ] Documented in `03-testing-strategy.md`'s E2E inventory.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

title: Build the perf and load scripts proving budget #4 for E32's order paths
body:
## Context
`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 5.2 budget #4 requires order submit -> ack p95 <300 ms end-to-end on demo with the **backend-added portion isolated and asserted at <=50 ms p95**, and it is a **hard gate** regardless of environment. R3 exit criterion #11 restates it. E32 adds three new shapes to that path — a bracket with an attached stop, a batched ladder, and a `trading-stop` write — none of which are covered by E29's baseline scripts, and each of which could plausibly blow the backend-added allowance through extra validation, generation or persistence work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 scripts under `perf/k6/e32/`: (1) bracket submission with attached SL; (2) 10-level batched ladder submission; (3) `trading-stop` write via `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl`; (4) protective amend on fill (the 500 ms target).
- Backend-added isolation: each script runs in two modes — against Bybit demo (end-to-end) and against a recorded-fixture mock adapter (backend-only), so the backend's own contribution is measured rather than inferred.
- Micro-benchmarks committed alongside: `NativeSlGuard.evaluate` (<=1 ms p99), `generate_levels` for 50 levels (<=5 ms), `TrailingTranslator` conversion (<=1 ms).
- A sustained profile: continuous bracket + ladder flow at the per-UID order-create budget for 30 minutes, asserting no latency drift, no lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off.
- Results published to the perf dashboard with a committed baseline, and CI comparison failing on regression beyond the agreed threshold.
- Frontend-side measurement of the SCR-065 preview recompute within one frame, captured via Playwright tracing.

## Out of scope
- Fan-out multi-account budgets (E34 owns the +10 ms/account sub-clause), engine FPS budgets, ingestion soak.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budget #4 holds for every new order shape
  Given the bracket, ladder and trading-stop scripts run against demo
  Then submit-to-ack p95 is below 300 ms end-to-end for each shape and the isolated backend-added portion is below 50 ms p95, recorded with the run date and build sha

Scenario: The guard and generator stay inside their micro-budgets
  Given the committed micro-benchmarks
  Then NativeSlGuard.evaluate is under 1 ms p99, generate_levels for 50 levels is under 5 ms, and the trailing conversion is under 1 ms, asserted in CI

Scenario: Sustained flow does not drift (edge)
  Given 30 minutes of continuous bracket and ladder submission at the per-UID budget
  Then p95 at minute 30 is within 10% of p95 at minute 1, no acknowledgement is lost, and rate-limit back-off behaves as specified

Scenario: A regression blocks the merge (failure)
  Given a change pushing the backend-added portion above 50 ms p95
  When CI compares against the committed baseline
  Then the perf check fails and the merge is blocked, because budget #4 is a hard gate
```

## Technical notes / design
- End-to-end runs exclude the uncontrolled Bybit RTT component from the backend-added figure by measuring the adapter's own send-to-receive interval separately, per the measurement convention in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`'s network-conditions note.
- The fixture-mock mode removes venue variance entirely, which is what makes the <=50 ms assertion stable enough to gate on.
- Baselines are committed per build and compared with a tolerance band rather than an absolute threshold, to avoid flapping on shared-runner noise; the absolute budget remains the hard ceiling.

## Test plan
This is a test deliverable. Verification: run each script three times and confirm the spread is small enough for the gate to be meaningful; a metric too noisy to gate on is reported and re-scoped rather than gated blindly.

## Security notes
Demo credentials from CI secrets with an environment guard; the sustained profile must not be pointed at live under any configuration. Results contain no account secrets.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except the frontend preview measurement which supports SCR-065's one-frame requirement.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance verification for E32 and produces the numbers cited in the epic DoD and the R3 PRR.

## Observability
Scripts assert that `order_submit_seconds{transport,env}` and `oms_native_sl_attach_seconds` are populated during the run, so the production dashboards are validated by the same exercise.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four scripts and three micro-benchmarks implemented and committed.
- [ ] Baselines committed and CI regression comparison wired.
- [ ] Budget #4 numbers recorded for all three new order shapes, both modes.
- [ ] Sustained 30-minute profile executed and reported.
- [ ] Results linked from the epic DoD and added to the R3 PRR evidence pack.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.
