title: Run the accessibility audit of SCR-064, SCR-065 and SCR-069
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI **and** manual screen-reader passes; `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 states there is no "internal tool" exemption. R3's a11y gate specifically calls out that the order ticket, DOM ladder and both rule editors must be fully keyboard-operable — E32's three screens carry two equivalent hard requirements of their own: SCR-064's keyboard path equivalent to chart drag-to-modify, and SCR-065's ladder preview as a real table. E32-D07 verified both in design; this ticket verifies them in the built product, where they are frequently lost.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated scans across **every enumerated state** of SCR-064, SCR-065 and SCR-069 (not just the default state), wired into CI as a gate for these routes.
- Manual screen-reader passes with NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS, covering: the CMP-158 persistent guarantee note, validation errors and their focus behaviour, the pending -> applied and pending -> rejected announcements, the ladder preview table's header associations and navigation, the trailing translation readout, and the submit buttons' accessible names.
- Keyboard-only walkthrough of all three screens including the SCR-064 chart-drag-equivalence script from E32-D07.
- Contrast verification in light and dark at both densities, including non-text elements (focus indicators, table borders, status colours).
- Reduced-motion verification against E32-D06's spec.
- Zoom/reflow check at 200% and 400% per WCAG 2.2, confirming the ladder table and modal remain usable.
- Findings triaged p0-p3 with p0/p1 fixed before the epic closes; p2/p3 filed as Bugs with owners.
- Audit report published and added to the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Out of scope
- Design-stage review (E32-D07), visual design QA (E32-D08), functional testing.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state passes axe-core
  Given all enumerated states of the three screens
  When axe-core runs in CI
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations, and the check gates these routes

Scenario: The two hard requirements hold in the built product
  Given SCR-064's keyboard path and SCR-065's table preview
  Then a keyboard-only user can perform every chart-drag-equivalent adjustment with values announced, and a screen-reader user can navigate the ladder preview by row and column with headers announced

Scenario: Protective state changes are announced (edge)
  Given a stop change moving from pending to applied, and another moving to rejected
  Then each transition is announced to the screen reader with enough information to know what protection is currently in force

Scenario: A p0 finding blocks the epic (failure)
  Given a control operable only by pointer
  Then it is fixed and re-verified before the epic's DoD a11y item can be ticked, rather than deferred to R5
```

## Technical notes / design
Manual passes follow the scripted scenarios in `05-accessibility-standard.md`'s screen-reader protocol so results are comparable across epics. Each finding records the WCAG success criterion it violates, the state it occurs in, and a reproduction path.

## Test plan
This is a verification deliverable. Its own quality check: a sample of findings is independently re-verified by a second reviewer to guard against false positives from tooling configuration.

## Security notes
Audits run on staging demo; screenshots and recordings are scrubbed of account identifiers before publication.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility verification for E32 and produces the evidence cited in the epic DoD and the R3 a11y gate.

title: Run exploratory charters, assemble the regression pack and record QA sign-off
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 requires an **epic-level** regression and exploratory pass, not merely the sum of child-ticket QA, before an Epic reaches Done. Scripted tests verify what was anticipated; exploratory charters are where the unanticipated interactions between a bracket, a ladder, a trail and a risk cap actually surface. This ticket also produces the regression pack that R4 and R5 will re-run, so E32's behaviour is protected after the team's attention moves on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Four timeboxed exploratory charters (90 minutes each, session-based test management notes recorded):
  1. *"Explore bracket and ladder interactions under adverse fills"* — partial fills, rapid re-fills, legs filling out of expected order.
  2. *"Explore every route to weakening protection"* — attempt to remove, loosen, orphan or outlive a stop through the UI, the API, cancellation orders and timing races.
  3. *"Explore ladder arithmetic at instrument boundaries"* — minimum notional, extreme skew, narrow ranges, the 2 and 50 level bounds.
  4. *"Explore recovery experience"* — behave as a user during a reconnect, a rejected amend and a watchdog fallback; judge whether what is displayed is sufficient to act on.
- A **regression pack** for E32: the subset of E32-Q01/Q02/Q03/Q04/Q05 scenarios that must re-run for every release, packaged as a named suite with an execution runbook and expected duration.
- Verification that R3 exit criteria #2 (zero escapes) and #11 (submit-ack p95) have recorded evidence from E32-Q01 and E32-Q06 respectively.
- Bug triage of all E32 findings: zero open P0/P1 against E32's scope is an exit condition.
- The formal **QA sign-off comment** for the epic with pass/fail per story, plus a statement of residual risk and anything deliberately untested.

## Out of scope
- Writing new automation (belongs to the owning Q tickets), security abuse cases (E32-X02/X03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All four charters are executed and debriefed
  Given the charters
  When each 90-minute session completes
  Then session notes record what was explored, what was found, and what was not covered, and every finding is filed as a Bug with a priority or explicitly dismissed with a reason

Scenario: The regression pack is executable by someone else
  Given the packaged suite and its runbook
  When a QA engineer who did not build it executes it
  Then it runs end to end within the stated duration and produces an unambiguous pass or fail per scenario

Scenario: Exit criteria have cited evidence
  Given R3 exit criteria 2 and 11
  Then the sign-off cites the specific dated artefacts from E32-Q01 and E32-Q06 rather than asserting compliance

Scenario: An open P1 blocks sign-off (failure)
  Given an open P1 defect in E32's scope
  Then QA sign-off is withheld and the epic cannot reach Done until the defect is fixed or explicitly accepted with Owner sign-off recorded
```

## Technical notes / design
Charters follow session-based test management: charter, time box, notes, bug list, coverage statement, and a debrief with the engineering lead. The regression pack is registered in the release checklist in `07-release-and-prr.md` so it is actually re-run rather than forgotten.

## Test plan
This is the epic's QA closure activity. Quality check: the regression pack is dry-run once by a second person before it is accepted.

## Security notes
The "explore every route to weakening protection" charter overlaps deliberately with E32-X02's abuse cases; findings are cross-filed and the Security engineer is invited to the debrief for that charter specifically.

## Accessibility notes
Accessibility findings from exploration are cross-filed to E32-Q07 rather than judged here.

## Performance notes
Perceived-performance observations from exploration are cross-filed against E32-Q06's measured baselines.

## Observability
The recovery-experience charter explicitly judges whether alerts, banners and audit trails give an operator enough to act on — which is an observability verification as much as a UX one.

- [ ] Four charters executed with notes and debriefs recorded.
- [ ] All findings filed with priorities; zero open P0/P1 in E32 scope.
- [ ] Regression pack packaged, dry-run by a second person and registered in the release checklist.

title: Implement the abuse-case suite, RBAC scope assertions and SAST rules for E32
body:
## Context
E32-Q01 proves the invariant holds for *legitimate* callers using the product's own paths. This ticket attacks it from outside the trust boundary: crafted API requests, wrong-account references, role escalation, replayed idempotency keys and resource exhaustion. `04-security-program.md` requires abuse cases plus SAST/DAST coverage per epic, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 requires a **manual abuse-case check** for anything touching the safety invariant.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/security/e32/test_abuse_cases.py` implementing every abuse case from E32-X01's list, at minimum:
  1. Submit a position-opening order with `stopLoss` omitted, then with it null, empty string, zero, negative, and NaN-like values.
  2. Submit with a `stopLoss` on the wrong side of the entry (a stop that can never trigger protectively).
  3. Submit with `intent` deliberately mislabelled as `take_profit` or `algo_child` to dodge the position-opening classification.
  4. Submit with `reduceOnly=true` while the account has no position (a stopless opening order in disguise).
  5. Request a deferral with a reason not on the closed allow-list, and with a reason string crafted to match by prefix.
  6. Replay a previously successful `orderLinkId` to try to duplicate an entry without a new stop.
  7. Reference another user's `accountId` / `positionId` on every E32 endpoint (horizontal escalation).
  8. Perform every E32 mutation as a `viewer` role and as a `manager` outside their granted account scope (vertical escalation).
  9. Submit a 50-level ladder repeatedly to exhaust the order-create budget, then attempt a protective stop placement (reserve exhaustion).
  10. Attempt to loosen a stop via `PUT /positions/{positionId}/tpsl` without the explicit-override flag, and with a forged override flag.
- Assertions for each: rejected with the correct error code, **no state change**, and an `audit_log` row recording the attempt — per the RBAC matrix requirement in R3 exit criterion #10.
- Semgrep/Bandit custom rules: flag any new call site of `adapter.place_order` or `adapter.set_trading_stop` outside the sanctioned modules; flag any construction of a `PlaceOrderRequest` outside the OMS submission pipeline.
- ZAP/DAST profile additions for the E32 endpoints, including authorization-bypass and parameter-pollution checks.
- A documented **manual abuse-case check** performed by the Security engineer against staging, with results recorded on the ticket.

## Out of scope
- Penetration testing (E43), key-vault attacks (E27), the functional invariant suite (E32-Q01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case is rejected with no state change
  Given each of the ten abuse cases
  When executed against staging demo
  Then each is rejected with the documented error code, a database diff before and after shows no state change, and an audit row records the attempt with the actor

Scenario: Horizontal and vertical escalation are both blocked
  Given a manager scoped to account A and a viewer role
  When either attempts any E32 mutation on account B, or the viewer attempts any mutation at all
  Then the response is 403, no state changes, and an audit row exists for every disallowed combination

Scenario: The reserve survives deliberate exhaustion (failure)
  Given repeated 50-level ladders saturating the order-create budget
  When a protective stop placement is attempted
  Then it succeeds by drawing on the protective reserve, and the attack is visible in metrics

Scenario: A new unsanctioned call site fails SAST (edge)
  Given a change introducing a direct adapter.place_order call outside the OMS pipeline
  When Semgrep runs in CI
  Then the custom rule fires and the build fails with a message naming the sanctioned path
```

## Technical notes / design
- Database diffing uses a transactional snapshot before and after each case; "no state change" is asserted mechanically rather than by inspection.
- Case 5's prefix-matching variant exists because allow-lists implemented with `startswith` are a recurring real-world bypass.
- Case 6 depends on E29's idempotency semantics; the assertion is that the replay is a no-op returning the original result, never a second order.
- The suite runs in CI on every PR touching `services/oms/**` and nightly in full.

## Test plan
This is a security test deliverable. Verification: each case is first run against a deliberately weakened build (allow-list widened, RBAC check removed, reserve disabled) and must fail — proving the case tests the control rather than the happy path.

## Security notes
Runs against demo with the environment guard asserted. Findings are triaged with the Security engineer; any Critical/High must be fixed before the epic closes per R3's security gate. The suite becomes part of the standing regression set cited in E43's pen-test scope.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Case 9 deliberately stresses the rate budget; it runs in an isolated window so it does not distort E32-Q06's measurements.

## Observability
Each case asserts the expected audit row and, where applicable, the expected metric increment — so an attack would be visible to an operator, not only blocked.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ten abuse cases implemented and passing, with negative verification against weakened builds.
- [ ] Custom Semgrep/Bandit rules committed and firing in CI.
- [ ] DAST profile updated for the E32 endpoints.
- [ ] Manual abuse-case check performed and recorded by the Security engineer.
- [ ] All findings triaged; Critical/High closed.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue.

`E32-X01` (abuse-case list), `E32-T01` (the guard under attack), `E32-S03` (the ladder path used for exhaustion cases).

body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 requires a Security-engineer sign-off comment for any epic labelled `security`, with the STRIDE model finalised and findings triaged; section 8 makes that mandatory for anything touching the fan-out safety invariant. E32 is the epic whose failure mode is a genuinely unprotected position, so its sign-off is also the primary evidence for RSK-016 in the R3 PRR and the input to E43's pen-test scoping.

## Scope / Deliverables
- White-box review of the shipped code for `NativeSlGuard`, `UnprotectedPositionWatchdog`, `BracketSupervisor`, `ScaledSupervisor` and `TrailingTranslator`, focused on: the completeness of the position-opening classification, the closed deferral allow-list, the ratchet's correctness, transaction ordering (persist before send), and the absence of any bypass path.
- Verification that the two architecture tests (single call site for `place_order` and for `set_trading_stop`) are present, required, and cannot be skipped.
- Review of the E32-X01 findings table: every Critical/High closed with evidence, every accepted risk carrying Owner sign-off and a detection control.
- Confirmation that E32-Q01's zero-escape suite and E32-X02's abuse suite are both required checks with no allow-failure configuration.
- Review of E32-Q05's chaos report specifically for the escalate-not-flatten behaviour and the recovery-time evidence.
- RBAC verification for the E32 routes against the matrix, confirming 403 plus no state change plus an audit row for every disallowed role/route combination.
- Audit-completeness check: every stop modification, ladder creation and refusal produces an attributable, hash-chained audit row.
- SAST/SCA/secrets-scan review across the E32 changes, with findings triaged.
- Published sign-off comment with an explicit residual-risk statement, plus the E32 section of the R3 PRR evidence pack and the pen-test scope note for E43.

## Out of scope
- Fixing defects found (filed as Bugs against the owning tickets), the pen-test itself (E43), live enablement gating (E44).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The invariant has no reachable bypass
  Given the shipped OMS code
  When the reviewer traces every path that can reach the exchange adapter
  Then all of them pass through the guard, the architecture tests enforce it, and the reviewer records the traced paths in the sign-off

Scenario: Every Critical and High finding is closed with evidence
  Given the E32-X01 findings table
  Then each Critical or High is closed with a named test or control as evidence, or is an accepted risk with Owner sign-off and a detection control

Scenario: RBAC holds for every route and role
  Given the E32 routes and the role matrix
  Then every disallowed combination returns 403 with no state change and an audit row, verified by executing the matrix rather than reading the code

Scenario: Sign-off is withheld on an open High (failure)
  Given an open High finding at review time
  Then sign-off is withheld, the epic cannot reach Done, and the blocking finding is stated explicitly on the epic
```

## Technical notes / design
The review is white-box and deliberately adversarial: the reviewer's working question is "how would I open a position without a stop", and the sign-off records the paths tried and closed, so a future reviewer can see what was already considered.

## Test plan
N/A — review. Verification: the RBAC matrix is executed, not inspected; the architecture tests are run against a deliberately violating branch to confirm they fail.

## Security notes
This ticket is the epic's security gate. The sign-off and its residual-risk statement are cited by the R3 PRR (`07-release-and-prr.md`) and by E43's pen-test scoping, and are stored in the restricted security space.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The reviewer confirms that the protective reserve's sizing, as shipped, still guarantees a protective token under E32-Q06's measured peak load — a performance number being used as a security control.

## Observability
Confirms that every preventive control also has a detection control where E32-X01 required one, and that alerts route somewhere a human will see them.

- [ ] All Critical/High findings closed or accepted with Owner sign-off.

title: Design QA of the shipped trade-group ticket and manager
body:
## Context
SCR-061 (trade-group ticket) and SCR-062 (trade-group manager) are the two screens E34 introduces. Both are new interaction territory: no prior screen in the product asks a user to reason about *N simultaneous executions with different sizes on different accounts*, and both have a failure state — a partially-executed fan-out — that `14-screens-catalogue.md` requires to be **"drawn as the primary design case, not an afterthought"**.

The design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence) applies: no frontend work on E34-S04/S05 (Sprint 19) starts until the design tickets are Status=Done, and they must have been Done for ≥2 sprints.

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec and discrepancies are fixed or filed. E34 ships two net-new screens whose most important state — partial failure — is also the state least likely to be exercised during normal development, so it is exactly the state most likely to have drifted.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Side-by-side comparison of the built SCR-061 and SCR-062 against the D05 package: spacing, type ramp, tokens, colour, iconography, density, focus styling, and **every state** including partial failure, rate-limit backoff, blocked, unwind-incomplete, divergent, state-unknown, empty, loading and error.
- Verify the copy deck was implemented verbatim — error and confirmation strings especially, since they are where paraphrasing is most tempting and most dangerous ("Flatten all 5 legs of group tg_0912" must restate the live leg count).
- Verify motion against the spec and the reduced-motion alternative.
- Verify the state → data mapping: each state is driven by the server field the package names, not by a client-side inference (spot-checked with the FE engineer using devtools and a forced WS payload).
- Findings triaged with the FE owner: fixed in-sprint, or filed as Bugs with `priority/*` and linked to the offending story.
- Design sign-off comment on E34-S04 and E34-S05.

## Out of scope
- Functional testing → E34-Q01..Q06. a11y audit → E34-Q05 (this ticket only checks visual focus styling and reduced motion).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Partial failure matches the spec
  Given the built screen is forced into a 2-of-5 partial failure using an injected WS payload
  Then its layout, copy, action labels and alert behaviour match the D05 package
  And any divergence is fixed in-sprint or filed as a Bug with a priority

Scenario: Copy is verbatim
  Given the copy deck
  Then every user-visible string in both screens matches it exactly, with any deliberate change back-ported into the deck and the screens catalogue

Scenario: No client-side status invention
  Given a forced WS payload setting the group status to partially_open with all legs reporting ok
  Then the UI renders partially_open, proving it renders the server's derived status rather than deriving its own
```

## Technical notes / design
Use Storybook stories plus a WS payload injector to reach states that are hard to produce naturally; both screens' stories are a DoD item on E34-S04/S05, so the material exists.

## Test plan
Design QA checklist executed and attached; each item pass/fail with a screenshot.

## Security notes
Confirm the DEMO/LIVE badge renders correctly per row and that no build-time flag can hide it — a missing environment badge on a trading surface is a safety defect, not a cosmetic one (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 E30 row: "no trading control is operable unless both are visible").

## Accessibility notes
Focus styling and reduced-motion conformance are checked here; the full audit is E34-Q05.

## Performance notes
Note any visual treatment that measurably costs frame budget in the 50×5 stress story and file it as a Bug if it breaches the 4 ms scripting budget.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Artefacts published in Figma, linked on this ticket, and the matching `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` entries updated to match.
- [ ] Every state from the screen-catalogue entry drawn: previewing, ready, partial-send in progress, partial failure, rate-limit backoff, blocked (account in lockout), empty, loading, error.
- [ ] The screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `14-screens-catalogue.md` ticked item-by-item by the CDO or delegate, recorded as a comment.
- [ ] a11y annotations present: focus order, roles, live-region usage, contrast tokens, ≥24 px hit targets, text equivalents for every colour-coded state.
- [ ] Status=Done at least 2 sprints before the consuming FE story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md` §Team & cadence).

Blocked by **E34-S04** and **E34-S05** (there is nothing to QA until they are built).

title: Add the fan-out end-to-end suite (Playwright web + Electron)
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 names fan-out explicitly in the R3 E2E gate: "Playwright web + Electron covering ticket, chart trading, DOM trading, bracket, **fan-out**, rule creation in both editors, alert firing, journal capture". This ticket contributes the fan-out journeys, driven from E34-Q01's plan and running against a backend wired to recorded Bybit fixtures plus a fault-injection hook, so failures are deterministic rather than dependent on the exchange's mood.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `e2e/trading/fanout/`, each run in both the web and the Electron project configurations:
  1. **Happy path 3 accounts** — select group, preview shows three different sizes, send, all three accepted, group reaches `open`, every leg shows its native SL, positions grid reflects the group.
  2. **Partial failure 2 of 5** — fault injection rejects two legs; assert the `role="alert"` summary text, the three recovery actions, the audit rows and the alert.
  3. **Retry failed legs** — retry succeeds; assert a new idempotency key was used and no duplicate order exists on the successful legs.
  4. **Unwind accepted legs** — assert reduce-only closes only, per-account ordering (cancel before close), group ends `failed` with `unwind_incomplete=false`, and every account flat.
  5. **Rate-limit deferral** — governor forced into starvation for one account; assert the deferred row, its countdown, and the terminal rejection on deadline with no order sent.
  6. **all_or_none rejection** — assert nothing was sent at all and the response names the starved account.
  7. **Group lifecycle on SCR-062** — open → partial failure banner → retry → "close group 50%" with heterogeneous lot sizes → closed, with the confirmation restating the leg count.
  8. **Kill-switch refusal** — engage kill-switch, attempt a fan-out from the ticket, assert refusal and audit.
  9. **RBAC** — Manager sees only granted accounts in the selector and receives 404/403 appropriately for a foreign group; Viewer sees no mutating controls.
- A shared fixture/harness: a fault-injection API on the test backend (`/__test__/fail-leg`, `/__test__/starve-account`) available only when `CV_TEST_HOOKS=1`, plus a deterministic clock control for deadlines.
- Wire the suite into the CI pipeline as a required check for `area/oms-execution` changes, with trace/video artefacts on failure.
- Flake budget: any spec flaking more than 1 in 50 runs is quarantined with a Bug filed the same day — the suite's value is entirely in being believed.

## Out of scope
- Load/soak → E34-Q03. Chaos/infrastructure faults → E34-Q04. a11y audit → E34-Q05. Unit/integration tests belong to their implementing tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All nine journeys pass in both projects
  Given the web and Electron Playwright projects
  When the fan-out suite runs in CI
  Then all nine specs pass in both, with traces retained for any failure

Scenario: Deterministic failure injection
  Given the fault-injection hook is used to reject legs C and D
  When the partial-failure spec runs 50 times
  Then it produces the same outcome every time and the flake rate is zero

Scenario: Test hooks cannot exist in production
  Given a production build
  Then the fault-injection routes are absent and a test asserting their absence is part of the suite

Scenario: The suite proves the safety invariant end to end
  Given the happy-path and partial-failure specs
  Then each asserts, by querying the exchange stub directly, that every opened leg carries a native stop-loss
```

## Technical notes / design
- Selectors use role/name queries (the same semantics the a11y work guarantees), never CSS classes — this couples the suite to the accessible contract rather than to styling and makes a11y regressions fail the E2E suite too.
- WS-driven assertions wait on application state, not timeouts; the only real sleeps permitted are the explicit deadline tests, which use the controllable clock.
- Each spec is fully self-cleaning: teardown flattens every account and cancels every working order, asserted before the test reports success.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* test code; its own quality gate is: 50 consecutive green runs of the full suite before it becomes a required check, and a deliberate mutation (disable the native-SL attach) must turn the suite red — a suite that cannot detect the thing it exists for is not done.

## Security notes
Test hooks are the main risk introduced here: they are compiled out unless `CV_TEST_HOOKS=1`, never enabled in staging or production, covered by a CI assertion, and flagged in the threat model (E34-X01) as an accepted, controlled surface. Tests use demo keys from the vault fixture, never live keys.

## Accessibility notes
Because selectors are role/name-based, the suite implicitly asserts accessible names exist ("Send group (3 accounts)", "Flatten all 5 legs of group tg_0912"). The dedicated audit is E34-Q05.

## Performance notes
Suite wall-clock ≤12 min in CI with sharding, so it can be a required check without throttling the merge queue.

## Observability
Specs assert the corresponding audit rows (`trade_group.submit`, `trade_group.unwound`, `positions.flatten`) and key metrics move as expected — turning telemetry into a tested contract instead of an afterthought.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test assets committed under the repo's test tree and wired into CI where automatable.
- [ ] Execution evidence attached (run log, k6 summary, Playwright report, axe report, chaos run notes).
- [ ] Defects filed as Bug tickets with `priority/*`, linked to this ticket and to the offending Story.
- [ ] Coverage/quality-gate impact recorded; no existing gate weakened.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR merged via the merge queue.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E34-Q01** (the plan being automated) and by **E34-S02/S03/S04/S05** (the behaviour under test).

title: Build the k6 load profile for sustained fan-out at the per-UID rate limit
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 sets the R3 load gate precisely: **"k6: sustained order flow at the per-UID limit across 5 accounts for 1 h with zero lost acknowledgements and correct governor back-off"**. `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §5.2 budget #4 sets the latency target (≤50 ms backend-added + ≤10 ms/account) and §6 requires load tests to run against **recorded Bybit fixtures**, not live Bybit, so they are deterministic and consume no real rate budget.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 scripts under `load/k6/fanout/`:
  - `fanout_sustained.js` — 1 h, 5 accounts, order flow held at the per-UID limit derived from E34-K01's measurements; asserts zero lost acknowledgements (every submitted leg reaches a terminal state), correct back-off behaviour, and no naked position at any sample point.
  - `fanout_burst.js` — bursts that deliberately exhaust the `entry` bucket, asserting deferral rather than loss, and asserting `critical` availability never drops below the reserve.
  - `fanout_latency.js` — budget #4 measurement: backend-added overhead per group at N = 1..5 accounts, reporting the fixed and per-account components separately so the "≤50 ms + ≤10 ms/account" shape is verified, not just the total.
  - `preview_load.js` — SCR-061's preview endpoint at realistic typing rates, asserting the ≤300 ms p95.
- A staging backend profile wired to recorded Bybit fixtures with a configurable synthetic exchange latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), so results are reproducible across runs and machines.
- Thresholds encoded as k6 `thresholds` (build fails on breach), not as eyeballed dashboards.
- A results record committed per run (date, commit, environment, numbers) so regressions are detectable across the train, plus a Grafana dashboard snapshot.
- CI wiring: the latency and preview profiles run on every `area/oms-execution` PR (short duration); the 1 h sustained profile runs nightly and before the R3 PRR.

## Out of scope
- Chaos/fault-injection → E34-Q04. Functional correctness → E34-Q02. Frontend rendering performance → E34-S05's own budget checks.
- Live-environment load — explicitly forbidden.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The R3 load gate
  Given 5 accounts driven at the per-UID limit for one hour
  When the run completes
  Then every submitted leg reached a terminal state with zero lost acknowledgements
  And the governor's back-off behaviour matches the expected token accounting within 5%

Scenario: Budget #4 shape is verified
  Given latency runs at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 accounts
  Then the fitted fixed cost is ≤50 ms and the marginal per-account cost is ≤10 ms
  And a regression beyond 10% of either component fails the threshold

Scenario: Starvation defers, never drops
  Given a burst that exhausts the entry bucket on two accounts
  Then those legs are deferred and then either sent or rejected with RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
  And no leg ends in an unknown state and critical bucket availability never falls below the reserve

Scenario: Preview holds its budget under typing load
  Given preview requests at 4 per second per user across 3 concurrent users
  Then p95 latency stays ≤300 ms
```

## Technical notes / design
- The synthetic exchange must model **per-UID independence and per-IP sharing**, otherwise the test cannot exercise the interesting contention. Its parameters come from E34-K01.
- "Zero lost acknowledgements" is asserted by reconciling the script's submitted set against the backend's terminal set at the end of the run — not by trusting HTTP responses.
- Run the sustained profile at least once against **demo** (not fixtures) before the PRR, at a deliberately reduced rate, to confirm the fixture model has not drifted from reality; record both numbers.

## Test plan
The scripts are themselves validated by a negative control: artificially lower a bucket's capacity and confirm the thresholds fail, proving the assertions can detect a regression.

## Security notes
Load tests never run against live and never use live keys (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §6 rationale: avoid consuming real rate budget and risking account state). The synthetic exchange must not be reachable from staging's normal routing. Any captured payloads are scrubbed of signatures and key ids.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
This ticket *is* the performance verification for the epic: budget #4, the 1.5 s group-ack gate from ADR-0008, `oms_fanout_skew_seconds` p99 ≤1.5 s, and the ≤300 ms preview.

## Observability
Runs export to the same Prometheus/Grafana stack (`ADR-0014-observability.md`) so a load run and a production incident are read on identical panels. The run record includes `oms_rate_wait_seconds`, `oms_fanout_deferred_total` and `oms_fanout_skew_seconds` distributions.

title: Run chaos scenarios against in-flight fan-outs and unwinds
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 sets the R3 chaos gate: **"WS kill mid-order, backend restart mid-TWAP, Postgres failover mid-fan-out — all resume to a correct, reconciled state"**, and `24-internal-schemas.md` §17 lists the unwind's specific obligations including a "restart-mid-unwind resume test". E34 owns the fan-out and unwind halves of that gate.

The epic's whole safety argument rests on claims that are only true if tested destructively: that a crash mid-fan-out cannot double-place, that a crash mid-unwind cannot double-close, and that a residual position always keeps its native stop.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos scenarios under `chaos/e34/`, automated and repeatable, each asserting a *reconciled end state* rather than the absence of an error:
  1. **Backend kill immediately after the first leg's ack** (ADR-0008's own validation scenario) — on restart, reconciliation finds the leg, its native SL exists, and the group is `partially_open`.
  2. **Backend restart mid-fan-out** with legs in mixed states, including one leg whose `place_order` was in flight — assert the in-flight leg is resolved by `order_link_id` lookup, never blind-retried, and no duplicate order exists.
  3. **Backend restart mid-unwind** — `UnwindResumer` resumes the persisted plan before the OMS accepts new orders; steps already `done` are skipped; identical `order_link_id`s are re-sent; no position is closed twice.
  4. **Postgres failover mid-fan-out** and **mid-unwind** — assert no lost group/leg rows, no orphan legs, and that a plan interrupted between step transitions resumes from the last committed step.
  5. **Private WS kill for 60 s mid-group** — group state goes `unknown` for the affected account rather than optimistic, reconciliation restores truth on reconnect, and the UI shows "state unknown for sub_00N".
  6. **Injected `10018` during a fan-out wave** — IP-wide back-off engages, protective traffic still flows, and no request is dropped without a terminal status.
  7. **Key revoked mid-unwind** — the step fails permanently, a critical alert names the account, and the residual position retains its native SL.
  8. **Clock skew (`10002`) during submission** — requests are rejected and retried after correction; no leg is left `Unknown` without resolution.
- A chaos harness with deterministic injection points (process kill at a named await boundary, DB failover trigger, WS server kill) so scenarios are reproducible rather than opportunistic.
- Each scenario asserts the invariant set: **no naked position, no duplicate order, no double close, no orphan row, no unresolved Unknown**, plus the expected audit rows and alerts.
- Results recorded per run; the suite runs nightly against staging and is a PRR gate item for R3.

## Out of scope
- Chaos for emulated algos (TWAP restart) → E33; for replay/recording → E26; general infrastructure failover → E45 (this ticket contributes its fan-out scenarios to that epic's wider programme).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Kill after first ack
  Given a five-account fan-out and the backend is killed immediately after the first leg's acknowledgement
  When the backend restarts
  Then reconciliation finds that leg, confirms its native stop-loss exists at the exchange, and sets the group to partially_open
  And no duplicate order exists for that leg

Scenario: Restart mid-unwind does not double-close
  Given an unwind plan with close_position sent for account A and unacknowledged
  When the backend is killed and restarted
  Then the same order_link_id is re-sent, the exchange de-duplicates or the lookup resolves it
  And account A's position is closed exactly once

Scenario: Postgres failover loses nothing
  Given a failover during the submission wave
  Then every leg row is present with a consistent status, no orphan legs exist
  And the group's derived status matches the exchange's actual state after reconciliation

Scenario: Every scenario ends protected
  Given any chaos scenario that leaves a residual position
  Then that position carries a native exchange-side stop-loss when the scenario ends
```

## Technical notes / design
Injection points are named constants in the production code paths guarded by `CV_CHAOS_HOOKS` (off by default, absent from production builds), because "kill it at a random moment" is not reproducible and reproducibility is the entire value here.

## Test plan
Each scenario is run 20 times; a scenario that passes 19 of 20 is treated as failing, because the failure mode it guards against is precisely the rare interleaving.

## Security notes
Chaos hooks are a deliberate production-code surface and are threat-modelled in E34-X01 alongside the E2E test hooks: compiled out of production, asserted absent by a CI test, never enabled on any environment reachable from outside Tailscale. Demo accounts only.

## Accessibility notes
Scenario 5 asserts the UI's degraded copy ("state unknown for sub_002") is rendered and announced — a chaos test doubles as an a11y assertion for the degraded state that is otherwise nearly impossible to reach.

## Performance notes
Recovery-time assertions: reconciliation completes within 10 s of restart for 5 accounts; `UnwindResumer` starts before the OMS opens for new orders (ordering assertion, not a latency one).

## Observability
Each scenario asserts its expected `system_events` rows, alerts (`unwind_incomplete_total`, `naked_position_alert_total`) and audit entries. A scenario that produces the right end state with no telemetry is a failure — silent correctness is unverifiable in production.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test assets committed under the repo's test tree and wired into CI where automatable.
- [ ] Execution evidence attached (run log, k6 summary, Playwright report, axe report, chaos run notes).
- [ ] Defects filed as Bug tickets with `priority/*`, linked to this ticket and to the offending Story.
- [ ] Coverage/quality-gate impact recorded; no existing gate weakened.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR merged via the merge queue.

title: Accessibility audit of the trade-group ticket and manager
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` and the R3 a11y gate require WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI plus manual screen-reader passes, with no exemption for owner/admin surfaces. E34's two screens combine dense tables, a critical live-region alert, destructive confirmations and a timed countdown — four of the hardest a11y patterns in the product, all on a money-moving surface.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Automated: axe-core runs across every Storybook story of SCR-061 and SCR-062 (all states, including partial failure, rate-limit backoff, blocked, unwind-incomplete, divergent, state-unknown), wired as a CI gate for the touched packages.
- Manual screen-reader passes with **NVDA + Firefox** and **VoiceOver + Safari**, executed against D04's screen-reader script, covering: preview ready, row statuses and exclusion reasons, override control naming, send button naming the account count, partial-failure announcement and focus landing, destructive confirmation announcement and default focus, deferral countdown (must not spam the live region), and the nested leg table in SCR-062.
- Keyboard-only traversal of both screens end to end, including `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` submit, `Esc` cancel, modal focus trapping and focus return, and reaching every row action without a pointer.
- Contrast and non-colour verification: greyscale pass over every status, badge and banner; contrast measurements for WARN, deferred, rejected and divergent tokens.
- Reduced-motion verification against the D03 spec.
- Findings filed as Bugs with severity; blockers must be fixed before the R3 a11y gate; a written audit report attached.

## Out of scope
- Design-stage review → E34-D04 (already done; this audits the built result against it).
- Other R3 screens' audits (order ticket, DOM ladder, rule editors) → their own epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: axe-core is clean in CI
  Given every Storybook story for SCR-061 and SCR-062
  Then axe-core reports zero violations at the serious and critical levels, and the check is required for these packages

Scenario: The alert is announced correctly
  Given a 2-of-3 partial failure occurs while focus is on the send button
  Then both screen readers announce the summary once, focus lands on the summary region
  And the three recovery actions are reachable and each announces its scope

Scenario: The countdown does not spam
  Given a deferred leg with a visible countdown
  Then the countdown does not cause repeated live-region announcements
  And the leg's terminal outcome is announced once when it resolves

Scenario: Keyboard-only fan-out succeeds
  Given no pointer is used
  Then a complete fan-out can be previewed, adjusted, sent, and its partial failure acted upon

Scenario: Colour is never the only channel
  Given a greyscale export of every state
  Then every status remains identifiable from text alone
```

## Technical notes / design
Run the manual passes against the real application, not Storybook, for the alert and confirmation scenarios — live-region behaviour differs meaningfully between an isolated story and a full page with other regions present.

## Test plan
Each finding is reproduced twice, on two machines, before being filed, so screen-reader configuration artefacts are not mistaken for product defects.

## Security notes
One overlap: a screen reader must not announce data from accounts outside the caller's scope (it cannot, if the client never receives it — spot-checked). The confirmation for a destructive action must not be operable by a single `Enter` from its opening focus position.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the epic's a11y verification. Standard: WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`; evidence required by `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 for the two UI stories and by the Epic DoD.

## Performance notes
Confirm that the reduced-motion path does not degrade the 5 Hz update rendering, and that live-region updates are throttled so assistive technology is not overwhelmed at 50 groups × 5 legs.

## Observability
N/A beyond recording the audit result on the ticket.

- [ ] Execution evidence attached (run log, k6 summary, Playwright report, axe report, chaos run notes).

title: Execute the exploratory charters, regression pack and QA sign-off for E34
body:
## Context
The Epic DoD requires "an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA" (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2), and the R3 train closes with a 7-day soak and a PRR. This ticket is E34's closing QA activity: run the human half of E34-Q01's plan, run the exploratory charters, assemble the regression pack that protects fan-out for the rest of the product's life, and record the sign-off.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the manual black-box cases from `qa/plans/E34-trade-group-fanout.md` that are not automated, on staging (demo), recording pass/fail and evidence per case.
- Execute the **exploratory charters** (session-based, 90 min, with notes): key revoked between preview and send; rapid repeated sends of the same group; browser tab closed mid-fan-out (server-side fan-out must complete regardless — ADR-0008 rule 1); a group whose accounts have wildly different equity; a symbol delisted mid-group; two users acting on the same group concurrently; sending a group while a rule engine action targets the same accounts; clock change on the client during a deferral countdown.
- Assemble the **E34 regression pack**: the subset of automated and manual cases that must be re-run for any future change touching `area/oms-execution`, documented with expected runtime and owner, and referenced from the release checklist in `07-release-and-prr.md`.
- Verify the epic's exit criteria one by one (roadmap §7.3 items 2, 3, 4 as they pertain to fan-out) with recorded evidence, and confirm the safety-invariant suite's fan-out cases show **zero escapes**.
- Participate in the 7-day R3 soak: define what fan-out-specific signals are watched (`unwind_incomplete_total`, `naked_position_alert_total`, `oms_fanout_rejected_total`, divergence counts) and triage anything that appears.
- Post the QA sign-off comment on the Epic and on each Story, and file any residual defects with priorities.

## Out of scope
- Writing the plan → E34-Q01. Building automation → E34-Q02/Q03/Q04/Q05. Fixing defects → the owning stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every plan case has an outcome
  Given the black-box test plan
  When this ticket closes
  Then every case is marked pass, fail-with-bug, or explicitly deferred with a reason — none are blank

Scenario: Charters produced findings or evidence of absence
  Given the eight exploratory charters
  Then each has a session note recording what was explored, what was found, and what was deliberately not covered

Scenario: Exit criteria are evidenced
  Given roadmap §7.3 criteria 2, 3 and 4
  Then each has attached evidence: the zero-escape safety run, the 5-account correctness and latency run, and the 2-of-5 partial-failure run with its audit trail and alert

Scenario: Sign-off is real
  Then a sign-off comment exists on the Epic and every Story with pass/fail per scenario
  And no P0 or P1 defect against E34's scope is open at sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
The charters are chosen for the gaps automation structurally cannot cover: concurrency between humans, client-environment weirdness, and the exchange doing something the fixtures never recorded. Each session ends with a decision: automate it, accept it, or file it.

## Test plan
Self-referential; quality bar is that a second QA engineer can re-run the regression pack from the document alone without asking questions.

## Security notes
Includes the black-box execution of the abuse cases from E34-X02 (out-of-scope account, tampered quantity, replayed idempotency key, forged arm token) as an independent check on the security track's own testing — two independent parties must both have failed for an escape to reach production. Demo only; no live keys.

## Accessibility notes
The keyboard-only and screen-reader walkthroughs are re-run once at sign-off as a regression check even though E34-Q05 audited them, because the last sprint's fixes are the most likely to have broken them.

## Performance notes
Confirms E34-Q03's numbers are reproduced on the staging build that will be tagged, not only on the build the load work was developed against.

## Observability
Soak-watch list is defined and handed to Ops as part of the PRR package; each fan-out alert is confirmed to be routed and actionable (`ADR-0014-observability.md`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test assets committed under the repo's test tree and wired into CI where automatable.
- [ ] Execution evidence attached (run log, k6 summary, Playwright report, axe report, chaos run notes).
- [ ] Defects filed as Bug tickets with `priority/*`, linked to this ticket and to the offending Story.
- [ ] Coverage/quality-gate impact recorded; no existing gate weakened.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR merged via the merge queue.

- [ ] QA sign-off comments posted on the Epic and on E34-S01..S05.
- [ ] Regression pack documented and referenced from the release checklist.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1 defects against E34 scope.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E34-Q02**, **E34-Q03**, **E34-Q04**, **E34-Q05** — sign-off cannot precede the evidence it signs off.

title: Build the trade-group ticket (SCR-061) with per-account preview and partial-failure state
body:
## Context
SCR-061 is the surface where a single intent becomes N orders. `14-screens-catalogue.md` describes it as "one intent → N per-account orders, each sized by its own profile, each with a native SL", and its design sign-off checklist insists that **"partial-failure state (3 of 5 accounts filled) is drawn as the primary design case, not an afterthought"**. That framing drives this story: the happy path is the easy half; the screen's job is to make a partially-failed fan-out impossible to misread.

It implements the UI half of **US-PROF-006** (fan-out with its three scenarios), **US-PROF-008** (per-trade overrides), **US-ORD-014** scenario 2 (group preview), and **US-ORD-013** visibility (every leg shows its native SL before submit, via CMP-158).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screen **SCR-061 Trade-group ticket** as a panel/modal hosted by the order ticket shell (CMP-107 OrderTicket), RBAC: Owner creates/edits; Manager may use groups granted to them.
- Intent header: side toggle (CMP-102), symbol, entry type and price (CMP-100), SL/TP via CMP-119 BracketEditor, risk basis selector, TIF (CMP-231), arm state (CMP-229 ArmToggle), environment badge per row and globally (CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal).
- Target selection via **CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect** with **CMP-106 ProfileBadge** per account and the sub-account cap (`maxSelectable`) honoured.
- **Preview table** driven by `POST /api/v1/trade-groups/preview` (debounced ≤5 req/s, cancel-in-flight on new input): one row per account with profile summary, resolved qty, leverage, SL price and status (`ready` / `WARN` + reason / excluded + reason). Totals row: total qty, total notional, estimated fee, aggregate risk in USDT and R.
- **Per-row controls**: include/exclude checkbox, per-row qty override (US-PROF-008) rendered as visibly exceptional and flagged as an override in the submit payload; a disabled control with "capped by profile" where the override is forbidden.
- **Send**: `POST /api/v1/trade-groups` with a generated idempotency key and the arm token; `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` submits, `Esc` cancels the preview; the button names the account count ("Send group (3 accounts)").
- **All screen states** from the catalogue entry: previewing · ready · partial-send in progress (per-row live status queued → sent → accepted/rejected, driven by the `trade_groups` WS topic) · **partial failure** with the explicit summary ("2 of 3 accepted. sub_002 rejected: insufficient margin.") and the three actions **[Retry failed] [Unwind accepted] [Leave as is]** wired to E34-S03's endpoints · rate-limit backoff (per-UID budget shown via **CMP-232 LimitsChip** with the deferral deadline) · blocked (group contains an account in lockout or the kill-switch is engaged).
- **CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice** permanently visible; the group send is blocked client-side if any included row lacks an SL (with the server as the real enforcement).
- Validation copy exactly as specified: excluded rows always state the reason; a sub-minimum row states the minimum and offers it as a one-click choice.
- Optimistic-state discipline: a row never shows `accepted` until the WS says so; a REST 202 shows `sent`, not `filled`.

## Out of scope
- The preview/execute/unwind endpoints themselves → E34-S01/S02/S03.
- The single-account order ticket (SCR-060) → E30; chart/DOM entry points → E31.
- Trade-group *definition* editing (which accounts are in "Core3") → E28/SCR-062.
- Emulated-algo configuration UI → E33.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Preview shows each account its own size
  Given accounts Main, sub_001 and sub_002 are selected with different profiles
  When I set a limit buy of BTCUSDT at 64,010 with SL 63,900
  Then within 300 ms each row shows its own resolved qty, leverage and SL, and the totals row shows total qty, notional, fee and aggregate risk

Scenario: Excluded row always states why
  Given sub_003's profile does not allow BTCUSDT
  Then its row renders as excluded with the text "symbol not allowed by profile" and cannot be included
  And the exclusion reason is available to a screen reader as row text, not as a colour or icon alone

Scenario: Partial failure is the loud state
  Given I send to three accounts and sub_002 is rejected for insufficient margin
  Then a summary with role="alert" announces "2 of 3 accepted. sub_002 rejected: insufficient margin."
  And [Retry failed], [Unwind accepted] and [Leave as is] are offered, each naming its exact scope
  And the summary persists until I act on it — it is not a transient toast

Scenario: Rate-limit backoff is visible, not silent
  Given account sub_001's entry budget is exhausted and its leg is Deferred
  Then its row shows "queued — retrying in 2.4 s" with the per-UID budget chip
  And on deadline expiry the row becomes "rejected: rate budget exceeded" with the retry action available

Scenario: Send is blocked without a stop
  Given an included row resolves with no stop-loss price
  Then the send button is disabled with an explanation naming the row
  And a crafted submit bypassing the client still fails server-side with no_native_sl_possible

Scenario: Keyboard-only fan-out
  Given I never touch the pointer
  Then I can select accounts, toggle rows, edit an override, read every row status, submit with Ctrl+Shift+Enter and act on the partial-failure summary
  And focus moves to the partial-failure summary when it appears

Scenario: Kill-switch engaged
  Given the kill-switch is engaged
  Then the ticket renders in the blocked state naming the reason, and the send control is not operable
```

## Technical notes / design
- State machine in the client: `idle → previewing → ready → submitting → (open | partially_open | failed)`, driven by REST for transitions the user causes and by the `trade_groups` WS topic for everything the exchange causes. The client never derives group status itself — it renders the server's derived status (E34-T01).
- Preview requests are debounced at 250 ms with in-flight cancellation (`AbortController`); the last response wins by request sequence number, never by arrival order.
- Overrides are diffs against the resolved preview, sent as `legs[].overrides` so the server re-resolves rather than trusting a client-computed quantity (US-PROF-002 NFR: "computation is server-verified on submit so a tampered client cannot oversize").
- Idempotency key is generated once per *send attempt* and reused for retries of the same attempt; a "retry failed legs" action generates a new key (they are different operations — see E34-S03).
- Rendering: the preview is a real `<table>` with `aria-sort` where sortable; row status is text in its own cell; the partial-failure summary is a `role="alert"` region that receives focus on appearance.
- Frame cost: rows update at the WS topic's 100 ms coalescing rate; with ≤20 rows this is trivially inside budget, but the row component is memoized on `(status, filled_qty, error.code)` so a totals recompute does not re-render every row.

## Test plan
- **Unit (RTL, ≥80% FE):** each state renders its specified copy; exclusion reasons always present; override control disabled where forbidden; send disabled without SL; debounce/cancellation ordering; idempotency-key lifecycle.
- **Storybook + visual:** Previewing, Ready, PartialSendInProgress, PartialFailure(2 of 3), RateLimitBackoff, Blocked(lockout), Blocked(kill-switch), Empty(no accounts), Error(preview failed) — one story each, all snapshot-tested.
- **a11y:** axe-core on every story; keyboard-only walkthrough test; screen-reader script verified manually (NVDA + VoiceOver) confirming the alert announcement and row-status reading.
- **Contract:** the client's request/response types are generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml`; a CI check fails on drift.
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron):** the fan-out journeys in E34-Q02 — 3-account success, 2-of-5 partial failure with retry, partial failure with unwind, rate-limit deferral.
- **Perf:** preview round trip rendered ≤300 ms p95; no more than 1 preview request per 250 ms of typing.

## Security notes
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 every ticket in this epic is treated as `security`-labelled: it touches `area/oms-execution` order placement and the fan-out safety invariant. Threats from `04-security-program.md` / STRIDE (E34-X01): **Spoofing** — a forged `arm_token` or replayed idempotency key re-submitting a group; **Tampering** — client-supplied per-leg sizing overriding server-resolved sizing; **Repudiation** — a fan-out without a per-leg audit row; **Information disclosure** — another user's account labels/balances leaking through the group response or the `trade_groups` WS topic; **Denial of service** — a fan-out loop exhausting the shared per-IP budget and starving protective traffic; **Elevation of privilege** — a Manager fanning out to an account outside `granted_accounts`. Controls: server-side resolution of every leg parameter, `x-rbac: {permissions:[orders:write], scope: granted_accounts}` enforced before any adapter call, required idempotency key, the reserved `critical` rate bucket, and an `audit_log` row per leg. Data classification: financial/execution data and account scope; API secrets are never handled here (they stay in the M2 vault) — only referenced by account id.

Ticket-specific: the client holds **no authority**. Arm state, overrides, exclusions and the SL check are all UX affordances mirrored by server-side enforcement; the story's security test is that disabling every client guard (via devtools) changes nothing about what the server accepts. The screen displays per-account balances and sizing — it must render only accounts inside `granted_accounts` and must not cache another user's preview response in any shared store.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. Specifically (from `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-061 and `05-accessibility-standard.md`): the preview is a table with row status as text; the send button names the account count; the partial-failure summary is `role="alert"` and takes focus; every state conveyed by colour also has text; hit targets ≥24 px; the override control has an accessible name stating it is an override; `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` is documented and remappable; no keyboard trap in the modal; focus returns to the trigger on close.

## Performance notes
Preview ≤300 ms p95 (screen budget). Fan-out send dispatches server-side in parallel; full group ack ≤1.5 s p95 for 5 accounts. Row updates coalesced at the topic's 100 ms; interaction-to-paint for a row status change ≤50 ms.

## Observability
Client metrics via the app's telemetry: `ui_fanout_preview_latency_ms`, `ui_fanout_submit_to_ack_ms`, `ui_fanout_partial_failure_shown_total`, `ui_fanout_action_total{action=retry|unwind|leave}`. Every user action posts through the API and is audited server-side — the client adds no audit path of its own.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every acceptance-criteria scenario verified by an automated test (RTL unit / Playwright E2E) naming the scenario.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on touched packages; no regression to the package baseline.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched screen(s); keyboard-only path verified; manual screen-reader spot-check recorded; focus order and visible focus checked against `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the Figma spec (spacing/tokens/type/colour/all states) by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs with `priority/*`.
- [ ] Storybook stories added for every new/changed component state incl. the partial-failure state.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if behaviour diverged from the spec.
- [ ] security: no client-side authority added — every guard mirrored server-side; Security engineer comment present.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario; Story demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`trading.fanout`).
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code owner.

## Dependencies

title: Build the trade-group manager (SCR-062) with aggregate and per-account PnL
body:
## Context
**US-PROF-007** asks for the group to be "visible as one logical trade, so that I manage it without mental arithmetic": aggregate size, average entry, aggregate uPnL, expandable per-account rows, group actions, and a divergence badge when an account was modified outside the app. `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-062 is that screen, and it is also where the roadmap's "per-account and aggregated PnL views" (E34 scope row) live.

It is the calm counterpart to SCR-061: the ticket is where a group is created under time pressure, the manager is where it is understood and managed afterwards.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screen **SCR-062 Trade-group manager**: a page at `/admin/trade-groups` plus a read-only picker embedded in the shell, listing groups with id, symbol, side, accounts, filled/total, aggregate average price and state.
- Group list built on **CMP-049 Table** (virtualised), with **CMP-055 FilterBar** (symbol, status, date range, account) and **CMP-041 Menu** for row actions, driven by `GET /api/v1/trade-groups` (cursor pagination) and live-updated from the `trade_groups` WS topic.
- Row expansion to a **nested per-account table**: account (CMP-106 ProfileBadge), profile used, target vs filled qty, avg entry, uPnL, realised PnL, fees, native-SL confirmed flag, leg status and any error/skip reason.
- **CMP-124 TradeGroupSummaryCard** for the aggregate header of an expanded group: aggregate size, weighted average entry, aggregate uPnL and realised PnL, legs ok/failed/skipped — all read from the server-derived aggregate (E34-T01), never recomputed client-side.
- **Group actions** with confirmations that restate the exact leg count (e.g. "Flatten all 5 legs of group tg_0912"): close group (100%/50%/custom %), move stop (one `trading-stop` per leg at each leg's own price), cancel working orders, retry failed legs, retry incomplete unwind — all via `POST /trade-groups/{id}/amend` and `/cancel`, using **CMP-123 FlattenAllButton** for the destructive one. The UI issues **one backend command that fans out server-side — it never loops client-side over legs**.
- **Degraded and exceptional states**: `partially_open` with the unresolved-failure banner; `unwind_incomplete` as a persistent red banner with one-click "Retry unwind"; **divergent** badge naming the account and the difference (US-PROF-007 scenario 3); "state unknown for sub_002" when that account's private WS is down — marked unknown, never assumed; empty; loading; error.
- Additions to **SCR-063**'s "Trade groups" tab: the same group rows reachable from the positions panel, linking through to this screen.

## Out of scope
- Editing the trade-group *definition* (membership, name, who may use it) → E28.
- Journal/analytics of closed groups (equity curve, R-multiples, exports) → E41.
- The unwind mechanics → E34-S03.
- Admin RBAC matrix editing and audit-log browsing → E42.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Aggregate view
  Given a group trade is open across three accounts
  When I open the group
  Then I see aggregate size, weighted average entry and aggregate uPnL, with per-account rows that expand
  And the aggregate values match the server-derived aggregate exactly — the client performs no arithmetic of its own

Scenario: Group action closes each account by its own lot size
  When I choose "close group 50%"
  Then a confirmation restates "close 50% of 3 legs of group tg_0912" before anything is sent
  And each account closes 50% of its own position rounded to its own lot size, and partial failures are listed per account

Scenario: Divergence is named, not hinted
  Given account sub_002's position was modified outside the app
  When reconciliation runs within 30 s
  Then the group shows a "divergent" badge naming sub_002 and the difference in quantity as text

Scenario: An account's private stream is down
  Given sub_002's private WS is disconnected
  Then that leg renders as "state unknown for sub_002" and its row actions are disabled with the reason
  And the group is not reported as healthy on the basis of the remaining legs

Scenario: Incomplete unwind never disappears
  Given a previous unwind ended incomplete with a residual position on sub_003
  Then a persistent red banner names sub_003 and its residual quantity with a one-click "Retry unwind"
  And the banner cannot be dismissed while the residual exists

Scenario: Scale
  Given 50 open groups of 5 legs each are streaming updates
  Then the virtualised grid stays under 4 ms scripting per frame and updates are coalesced at 5 Hz
```

## Technical notes / design
- Updates arrive on the `trade_groups` topic at 100 ms coalescing and are further throttled to 5 Hz for rendering (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-062 performance note). Rows are memoized on `(status, filled_qty, unrealised_pnl_bucket)`.
- Every destructive action goes through a confirmation that names the scope, per the R3 a11y gate ("danger/confirm patterns announced"); the confirmation text is generated from the live leg count so it can never be stale.
- Group state is text first, colour second — never a colour pill alone (catalogue a11y note).
- Route is RBAC-gated: Owner full, Manager limited to groups on granted accounts, Viewer read-only with every mutating control absent (not merely disabled) — absence is the accessible and the safe choice.

## Test plan
- **Unit (RTL, ≥80%):** expansion behaviour; confirmation copy generation from the live leg count; per-leg action disabling under "state unknown"; banner persistence rules; RBAC rendering per role.
- **Storybook + visual:** List, Expanded, PartialFailure, UnwindIncomplete, Divergent, StateUnknown, Empty, Loading, Error, Viewer(read-only).
- **a11y:** axe-core per story; `aria-sort` on sortable headers; nested table semantics verified with a screen reader; every bulk action button announces its scope.
- **Perf:** 50 groups × 5 legs streaming at 5 Hz measured under Chrome DevTools scripting budget ≤4 ms/frame; virtualisation verified by DOM node count.
- **E2E:** group lifecycle journey in E34-Q02 (open → partial failure → retry → close group 50% → closed).

## Security notes
Read and act only on groups inside `granted_accounts`; a group id outside scope returns 404 from the API and the UI must render "not found", never "forbidden" (no existence oracle). Viewer role must not render mutating controls at all. No balances or account labels outside the caller's scope may enter the client store. Otherwise as per the epic-level STRIDE (E34-X01); no new threat surface beyond authorization and information disclosure.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. From the catalogue: group list is a table with one row per group; group state is text, not a colour pill alone; expansion reveals a nested per-account table with proper header association; every bulk action button names its scope ("Flatten all 5 legs of group tg_0912"); the unwind-incomplete banner is `role="alert"` and focusable; sortable headers carry `aria-sort`; keyboard path covers expand, act, confirm and cancel.

## Performance notes
Grid virtualised; <4 ms scripting per frame with 50 groups × 5 legs; updates coalesced to 5 Hz; group list query p95 ≤50 ms server-side (E34-T01). Flatten-group is one backend command — the UI never loops over legs client-side (explicit catalogue requirement).

## Observability
`ui_group_action_total{action}`, `ui_group_action_confirm_abandoned_total` (a high value means the confirmation copy is unclear — a design signal), `ui_group_render_frame_ms`. Server-side audit covers the actions themselves.

- [ ] Every acceptance-criteria scenario verified by an automated test (RTL unit / Playwright E2E) naming the scenario.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on touched packages; no regression to the package baseline.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched screen(s); keyboard-only path verified; manual screen-reader spot-check recorded; focus order and visible focus checked against `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the Figma spec (spacing/tokens/type/colour/all states) by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs with `priority/*`.
- [ ] Storybook stories added for every new/changed component state incl. the partial-failure state.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if behaviour diverged from the spec.
- [ ] security: no client-side authority added — every guard mirrored server-side; Security engineer comment present.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment with pass/fail per scenario; Story demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`trading.fanout`).
- [ ] PR(s) merged via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. a code owner.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E34-D05** (handoff Done ≥2 sprints earlier), **E34-T01** (list/detail endpoints, WS topic, server-derived aggregate) and **E34-S03** (group actions, divergence detection, unwind-incomplete state).

title: Reconcile the plan docs and ADR-0008 with the shipped fan-out behaviour
body:
## Context
The epic's normative material is spread across four documents that already disagree on naming: `22-api-openapi.yaml` uses `atomicity: best_effort | all_or_none`, `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5 uses `leg_failure_policy: best_effort | all_or_none | abort_on_first`, and `20-architecture.md` §4.3 uses `fanout_policy: atomic | best_effort` with group states `PartiallyAdmitted` / `PartiallyFilled` against the OpenAPI enum's `partially_open`. ADR-0008 additionally describes group states in older uppercase form (`PENDING | PARTIAL | ACTIVE | …`).

Leaving this drift in place guarantees a future implementer reads the wrong document. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires docs to "reflect final shipped behaviour (not the original proposal) if they diverged during implementation", so this chore closes the epic by making one vocabulary authoritative.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Adopt the **OpenAPI enums as authoritative** (`22-api-openapi.yaml` `TradeGroupStatus`, `atomicity`) and update, with a single terminology table plus in-place edits:
  - `20-architecture.md` §4.3 — rename `fanout_policy: atomic` → `atomicity: all_or_none`, `PartiallyAdmitted`/`PartiallyFilled` → `partially_open` (+ an explicit note that "admitted but deferred" is a *leg* status, not a group status).
  - `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5 — state that `abort_on_first` is an internal, rule-originated policy with no REST surface, or remove it if E35 did not use it.
  - `27-adrs/ADR-0008-trade-group-fanout.md` — align the state names in the Decision-outcome model block, and append the measured numbers from E34-K01 plus any rule amended during S02/S03 to the §Validation section.
- Update `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-061/SCR-062 if any state, control or copy shipped differently (in particular the "Stagger sends 150 ms apart" control — record whether it shipped, was replaced by the governor's automatic pacing, or was dropped).
- Update `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-124 if the shipped `TradeGroupSummary` prop shape differs from the sketch (it almost certainly will: the catalogue says the group is "aggregated client-side from the order-update WS stream", whereas we ship a server-derived aggregate on the `trade_groups` topic — that contradiction must be resolved in the doc).
- Add a changelog fragment for R3 describing fan-out and the unwind in user-facing terms.
- File follow-up tickets for any divergence too large to be a doc edit.

## Out of scope
- Any code change. If a doc edit would require a behaviour change to be true, file a Bug/Task instead of changing the doc to match a defect.
- Rewriting the research digests.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One vocabulary
  Given the four normative documents
  When the chore is complete
  Then a grep for "fanout_policy", "PartiallyAdmitted" and "PartiallyFilled" across docs/plan returns no hits outside an explicit historical-note block
  And every remaining status string matches a member of the TradeGroupStatus enum in 22-api-openapi.yaml

Scenario: ADR records what actually happened
  Given E34-K01 measured the real per-UID limits and S02/S03 amended two rules
  Then ADR-0008 §Validation contains the measured numbers with their measurement date and the amended rules

Scenario: A doc cannot be made true by editing
  Given CMP-124's client-side aggregation contradicts the shipped server-side aggregate
  Then the component catalogue is updated to the shipped contract and a Task is filed if any consumer still aggregates client-side
```

## Technical notes / design
Do the terminology change as one mechanical pass with a checked-in `sed`-style script recorded in the PR description, so a reviewer can verify the substitution was total rather than reading every diff hunk.

## Test plan
- Docs lint (markdown link check) green; the OpenAPI file still validates (`openapi-spec-validator`) after any edit.
- A CI grep guard added: fail if a deprecated status string reappears in `docs/plan/`.

## Security notes
N/A — documentation only, no threat surface. (Confirm no measured rate-limit table entry leaks a UID or key identifier.)

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] All four documents consistent; the CI grep guard is in place and green.
