title: Abuse cases, permission checks and SAST/DAST rules for the fan-out path
body:
## Context
E34-X01 enumerates the threats; this ticket turns the Critical and High ones into **executable checks**, so that a regression re-opens a known hole loudly rather than silently. `00-planning-brief.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), DAST (OWASP ZAP) and a per-epic abuse-case review; `30-release-roadmap.md` §7.4 additionally requires "a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Abuse-case test suite** under `tests/security/e34/`, each case asserting both the refusal *and* the absence of side effects (no adapter call, no state change) *and* the presence of an audit row:
  1. Manager fans out to an account outside `granted_accounts` → 403, no adapter call, audit row (ADR-0008's own security-test requirement).
  2. Viewer calls `POST /trade-groups` directly → 403; and calls `/preview` → 403 (preview is write-scoped because it discloses balances).
  3. Crafted request submits a symbol not allowed by the target account's profile → 403 + audit (US-PROF-003 scenario 2).
  4. Client-computed quantity exceeding the server's resolution by more than one lot → rejected (US-ORD-004 NFR).
  5. Per-trade override attempting to widen a hard risk cap or raise leverage above the profile cap → rejected (US-PROF-008 NFR).
  6. Replayed idempotency key → returns the original group, creates no second set of orders.
  7. Missing/forged/expired `arm_token` under a confirm-required policy → rejected.
  8. Fan-out while the kill-switch is engaged, including via a rule-originated group → `trading_disabled`, no adapter call.
  9. Group id outside scope on `GET`/`amend`/`cancel` → 404 (no existence oracle), never 403-with-detail.
  10. WS `sub` to `trade_groups` with an explicit out-of-scope `exchange_account_ids` filter → `err` frame, never a silently narrowed subscription.
  11. Unwind initiated for a group outside scope → refused; unwind proven structurally incapable of issuing a non-reduce-only order (assert the request builder rejects it).
  12. Attempt to cancel, during `cancel_children`, an order that is not the group's by relation (no local row bound to one of its legs, directly or through `parent_order_id`, `24-internal-schemas.md` §9.5.1) → refused, even when its `order_link_id` is a §8.3 id carrying the group's `group22`.
  13. Preview used as a balance oracle: rate-limited by the gateway; repeated out-of-scope probing produces audit entries and alerts.
  14. Test/chaos hooks absent in a production build (`CV_TEST_HOOKS`, `CV_CHAOS_HOOKS`) — asserted by a build-artifact test.
- **SAST rules**: Semgrep rules committed under `.semgrep/e34/` that fail the build on (a) an adapter order-mutating call reached without passing through the risk gate + kill-switch validator, (b) a `place_order` construction lacking a stop-loss field on an `intent=entry` path, (c) logging of any variable named like a key/secret/signature in the OMS package, (d) a REST handler under `/trade-groups` missing an `x-rbac`-derived dependency.
- **DAST**: OWASP ZAP profile for the `/trade-groups*` endpoints in the staging scan — authz matrix probing, injection payloads on free-text fields (`note`, `tags`), and header-manipulation of the idempotency key.
- **Key/permission checks**: verify keys used by the fan-out are withdrawal-OFF and IP-whitelisted at use time (E27 self-check) and that a key failing self-check causes its account to be reported "not ready" and skipped, with the skip visible (US-PROF-005 scenario 3).
- Findings triaged and fed back into the X01 model.

## Out of scope
- Full pen-test → E43. RBAC matrix test across all routes × roles (that is E09/E42's matrix test; this ticket covers the fan-out routes' participation in it).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Privilege escalation is refused with evidence
  Given a Manager whose granted accounts exclude account C
  When they submit a fan-out including account C
  Then the response is 403, no call is made to the exchange adapter, and an audit row records the attempt
  And the test asserts all three, not only the status code

Scenario: SAST catches a reintroduced hole
  Given a deliberately introduced order-mutating call that bypasses the kill-switch validator
  When CI runs
  Then the Semgrep rule fails the build and names the file and line

Scenario: No existence oracle
  Given a group id belonging to another user
  Then GET, amend and cancel all return 404 with an identical body shape to a genuinely missing id

Scenario: Unwind cannot open exposure
  Given any input to the unwind path
  Then the constructed order is always reduce-only, asserted at the request-builder level as well as behaviourally
```

## Technical notes / design
Every abuse case asserts the **three-part** outcome (refusal, no side effect, audit) because a refusal that still made an adapter call, or one that left no trace, is a different and worse bug than the one being tested. Use a spy adapter that fails the test on any unexpected call.

## Test plan
The suite is itself mutation-tested: temporarily removing each control must turn exactly the expected case red. A control whose removal breaks nothing is either untested or dead.

## Security notes
This ticket implements the epic's controls verification. Data classification unchanged from X01. No live keys, no live environment; DAST runs only against staging behind Tailscale.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
The abuse suite must run in under 3 minutes so it can be a required check on every `area/oms-execution` PR rather than a nightly job.

## Observability
Asserts that failed-authorization attempts increment `oms_fanout_rejected_total{reason="forbidden"}` and raise an alert — an out-of-scope fan-out attempt is never routine traffic.

- [ ] Findings recorded in `docs/security/threat-models/E34-trade-group-fanout.md`.

## Context

This ticket is that review and sign-off, performed against the shipped code rather than the design.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Targeted review of **privilege escalation**: `granted_accounts` scope is applied before any resolution or adapter call on every entry point (REST, WS, rule-originated groups, retry and unwind paths); the rule engine cannot exceed its originating user's authority.
- Confirm the **audit completeness** property: for every state-changing operation in the epic there is exactly one audit row, written before the network call, with the hash chain intact — verified on a tampered-row test.
- Review the epic's two deliberate production-code surfaces (`CV_TEST_HOOKS`, `CV_CHAOS_HOOKS`) and confirm their absence from the production artifact.
- Confirm no live code path exists: the environment gate is enforced in the backend configuration layer (M1), not in the UI, and a demo-configured deployment cannot reach live endpoints (roadmap §7 preamble).

```gherkin

  And a deliberately tampered row is detected by hash-chain verification

Scenario: Sign-off is conditional, not ceremonial
  Given any open Critical or High finding
  Then sign-off is withheld and the R3 security gate does not pass for this epic
```

## Technical notes / design
Review by reading the code paths against the X01 data-flow diagram element by element, not by sampling. Pair with the implementing engineers for the unwind state machine specifically — it is the epic's hardest path and the one where a subtle authorization or reduce-only mistake has the worst consequences.

## Test plan

This ticket is the epic's security gate. Outcome feeds the R3 PRR package and `32-risk-register.md`. Any accepted risk requires the Owner's explicit written acceptance on the ticket, per the roadmap's gate wording.

N/A, except to confirm that the security-relevant states (blocked, kill-switch engaged, account not ready) are conveyed accessibly — a safety state a user cannot perceive is not a control.

title: Design QA of the shipped rule-engine screens
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design-qa default-on for net-new UI stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec (spacing, tokens, type, colour, states) by a designer, and discrepancies are either fixed or filed as follow-up Bugs with a priority set.

E35 ships six screens whose failure states matter more than their happy paths — the partial-coverage simulation, the cannot-arm-yet block, the suppressed-firing row, the compilation-failure inspector state, the import validation list. Those are exactly the states most likely to have been built from imagination rather than from the spec, because they are the least often exercised during development.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Compare the built SCR-084, SCR-085, SCR-086, SCR-087, SCR-088 and SCR-089 against the E35-D05 handoff package: spacing, type ramp, colour tokens, density, iconography, copy (string by string against the copy deck), and **every enumerated state**, not only the populated one.
- Verify the required verbatim copy is present and unaltered: "Simulation replays recorded market data. Fills are modelled, not real; results are not a guarantee." and "If the backend stops, this rule stops. Native stops stay."
- Verify the motion implementation against the spec, including the `prefers-reduced-motion` alternatives.
- Verify the design-system components were used rather than re-implemented: CMP-154, CMP-156, CMP-158, CMP-159, CMP-233, CMP-234 appear as catalogue components with their documented props, and their Storybook entries cover every state.
- Check both themes and both density settings.
- File each discrepancy as a Bug with `priority/*` and a reference to the spec item it violates, or confirm it fixed in place.
- Sign off, which is a precondition for the epic's DoD.

## Out of scope
- Functional testing — **E35-Q06** and the QA tickets.
- The accessibility audit of the built screens — **E35-Q06**.
- The editors' design QA — E36/E37.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state is compared, not just the happy path
  Given the enumerated states for all six screens
  When design QA runs
  Then each state is exercised in the running application and compared against its spec frame, with the result recorded per state

Scenario: Safety copy is verbatim (failure case)
  Given the two required sentences
  When the built screens are checked
  Then each appears word for word; any alteration is filed as a priority p1 Bug because the wording is a risk control, not a style choice

Scenario: Components are reused, not reinvented (edge case)
  Given a screen element that duplicates a catalogue component's behaviour with bespoke markup
  When identified
  Then it is filed as a Bug requiring the catalogue component, so the design system does not fork

Scenario: Sign-off is evidence-based
  When design QA completes
  Then a sign-off comment lists every state checked, every discrepancy found, and the disposition of each
```

## Technical notes / design
Run against the staging (demo) deployment with seeded data that reaches the awkward states: a rule with no recorded history, a partial-coverage window, a rule blocked from arming, a suppressed firing, a deliberately corrupted IR for the inspector's failure state, and an import bundle with one invalid rule. Seeding this data is part of the ticket — a state that cannot be reached cannot be QA'd, and "could not reproduce" is not an acceptable outcome for a designed state.

Use the browser's device-pixel and zoom controls to check 125% and 200%, and the theme toggle for both themes, rather than trusting screenshots.

## Test plan
This ticket is itself a QA activity. Its output is the per-state comparison record and the Bug list. Functional and a11y verification are E35-Q06's job; where design QA notices a functional defect it files it and routes it there rather than absorbing it.

## Security notes
One security-adjacent check belongs here: confirm that SCR-089's export preview and SCR-088's IR inspector display no account ids, keys or armed state contrary to spec, and that SCR-087 masks account references per the product's labelling discipline. A finding here is a security Bug, not a cosmetic one.

## Accessibility notes
Design QA checks the visual a11y properties — contrast in both themes, non-colour status encoding, visible focus treatment, and reflow at 125% and 200%. The behavioural a11y audit (screen reader, keyboard traversal, axe-core) is E35-Q06.

## Performance notes
Spot-check that the implemented SCR-087 row design still meets its budget with the 10k-row fixture — a design QA fix that adds per-row cost would breach it, so any fix filed here notes the budget.

## Observability
Verify the specified client analytics events actually fire from the built screens, since a missing event is invisible until someone asks the question it was meant to answer.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six screens compared against the handoff spec in every enumerated state, both themes, both densities, at 100%, 125% and 200% zoom.
- [ ] Verbatim safety copy verified.
- [ ] Motion and reduced-motion alternatives verified.
- [ ] Catalogue component usage verified; Storybook coverage confirmed.
- [ ] Every discrepancy fixed in place or filed as a Bug with `priority/*` and a spec reference.
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted listing states checked and dispositions — this sign-off is a precondition for the E35 epic DoD.

## Dependencies

title: Document the node editor and add the ADR-0007 addendum on graph-only constructs
body:
## Context
> **Classification note.** This is a documentation/ADR reconciliation chore (kind `Chore`, mirroring E36-T02), not net-new delivery engineering. It is excluded from the E37 delivery-engineering subtotal reconciled against the roadmap's 26-point epic estimate; see "Estimate reconciliation" in the E37 epic body.

ADR-0007 fixed the single-IR decision before the node editor existed; it states that graphs "must be acyclic and must reduce to a single boolean condition plus an ordered action list" and that layout lives in `meta.layout`. Implementation in E37-S04 pins down details ADR-0007 left open: exactly which constructs are graph-only, how they are marked *at creation time*, how round-trip integrity failures behave in production, and the audit vocabulary (`identical | graph_only_construct | mismatch | unverified`). `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` requires docs to reflect shipped behaviour, not the original proposal.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR-0007 addendum** (appended to `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md`, or ADR-00xx superseding-in-part if the change is material): the definitive graph-only construct list (nested arithmetic, `n_of`, boolean nesting deeper than the two-level form subset, an output fanning into multiple consumers, nested sub-graphs), the creation-time marking rule, the production hash-comparison behaviour (abort, never repair), and the resolution-choice audit.
- Update `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4 where implementation clarified the round-trip guarantees (notably the presentation block's exact contents and its exclusion from the hash).
- Update `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 and `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146..153 / CMP-234..238 to match shipped props, states, hotkeys and a11y behaviour.
- A short **rule-authoring guide** section for the user-facing docs: when to use the graph vs the form editor, what "node-only" means for your rule, how to read the four round-trip states, and the complete keyboard authoring map (from E37-D04) as a printable reference.
- A changelog fragment for the R3 release describing the node editor and its feature flag.

## Out of scope
- Rewriting the IR specification itself (E35 owns §11.1–§11.3, §11.5, §11.6).
- Marketing/tutorial content; video walkthroughs.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR matches shipped behaviour
  Given the implemented graph-only construct detection
  When the ADR addendum is reviewed against packages/rule-graph's isFormRepresentable
  Then the construct list in the ADR and the code's detection set are identical, with a test referencing the ADR list as its fixture

Scenario: Catalogue entries match the build
  Given SCR-082 and CMP-146..153/234..238 entries
  When compared with the shipped screen and component props
  Then states, hotkeys, props and a11y contracts match, and any divergence is corrected in the docs rather than left stale

Scenario: The keyboard map is published
  Then the complete keyboard authoring map appears in the user-facing guide and matches the bindings registered in the app, verified by a test that enumerates registered bindings against the documented list

Scenario: A divergence cannot be resolved (failure)
  Given shipped behaviour that contradicts a locked plan decision
  Then it is escalated to the Architect and either the code or the decision is changed, never silently documented as-is
```

## Technical notes / design
Prefer an addendum over a new ADR unless the decision changed materially; ADR-0007's "Consequences" section gains the graph-only list. The binding-enumeration test is a small unit test in the web app that asserts the registered hotkey table equals the documented one — this is how the docs stay true.

## Test plan
Docs lint/link check in CI; the ADR-construct-list fixture test; the hotkey-enumeration test. No runtime behaviour changes.

## Security notes
The guide must describe arming, simulate-only mode and the native-SL invariant accurately — a document that implies a rule-engine stop replaces the exchange-side SL would undermine the safety invariant. Security engineer reviews the safety-relevant paragraphs.

## Accessibility notes
The published keyboard map is itself an accessibility deliverable (a printable, plain-text reference per the hotkeys-overlay conventions in SCR-012).

## Performance notes
Document the 200-node/60 fps budget and the <=500 ms compile+diff budget as user-visible expectations (e.g. the documented node cap from E37-K01, if any).

## Observability
Document the audit vocabulary (`rule.graph_saved`, `rule.roundtrip_verified {result}`, `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved {choice}`) so operators reading the audit log know what each value means.

- [ ] ADR addendum merged and referenced from `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.4.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md` updated to shipped behaviour.

title: Automate the E38 end-to-end suite in Playwright web and Electron
body:
## Context
The R3 quality gate requires Playwright coverage across web and Electron (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4). E38's most important behaviours are cross-cutting and stateful - a switch that must tear down and rebuild every subscription, a badge that must appear on every panel including floating windows - which is precisely the class of behaviour unit tests cannot cover.

Electron matters specifically here because detached/floating windows are separate BrowserWindows, and SCR-075 requires the band to repeat in every one of them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Add to `tests/e2e/e38/` the following suites, each running in both the web and Electron projects:
  1. **Demo order loop**: place, partial fill, amend, cancel on demo; assert state matches the orders and positions views and that the local mirror retains history.
  2. **Environment switch**: demo to live with typed confirmation and step-up; assert phase progress is shown, order entry is blocked during the transition, every open pane re-badges, one-click trading is disarmed, and working demo orders are reported as not migrated.
  3. **Switch refusals**: without step-up, with the flag off, without eligibility, and while an algo is running - each asserting the previous environment survives intact.
  4. **Badge ubiquity**: enumerate every trading-capable panel including a floated Electron window and a maximised panel, asserting the environment appears in the visible text and in the accessible name.
  5. **Cross-environment refusal**: issue a crafted API request from the browser context targeting a live account from a demo session; assert 403, no state change and an audit row visible in the security centre.
  6. **Paper reset**: reset with open positions, confirm counts, assert the control is absent in live.
  7. **Simulated results**: run a short replay with the paper matcher, open SCR-099, assert the disclosure block values, the default-off comparison, export, and promotion writing `simulated=true` journal rows.
  8. **Parity report**: view the report, trigger a demo-only failure, assert a candidate item appears and the refusal deep-links to its row.
  9. **Eligibility**: grant, acknowledge at next sign-in, revoke with open positions and assert reduce-only.
- Wire all suites into the CI E2E job with the `CV_FEED=synthetic` profile plus recorded fixtures; cases requiring a real demo account are tagged and excluded from CI per SR-140, and run on the trading host as part of the release checklist.

## Out of scope
- Load and chaos testing (E38-Q03, E38-Q04).
- The a11y audit (E38-Q05), though these suites assert accessible names where they are functionally load-bearing.
- Other epics' E2E suites.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every mandatory plan case is automated or explicitly deferred
  Given the E38-TC case list from E38-Q01
  When the suite is complete
  Then each mandatory case is either automated with its case id referenced, or deferred with a filed automation Task

Scenario: Suites pass in both web and Electron
  Given the Playwright web and Electron projects
  When CI runs
  Then all nine suites pass in both, including the floating-window badge assertion which only Electron can exercise

Scenario: The crafted cross-environment request is genuinely blocked
  Given a demo session in the browser
  When a live-targeting request is issued directly from the page context, bypassing the UI guard
  Then the API returns 403, no order exists afterwards, and the audit row is visible in the admin security centre

Scenario: Tests fail for the right reason
  Given a deliberately introduced regression removing a per-panel badge
  When the suite runs
  Then the badge-ubiquity suite fails and names the offending panel

Scenario: No credentials in CI
  Given the CI configuration
  When the suite runs
  Then it uses synthetic feeds and fixtures only, and demo-credential-requiring cases are tagged out
```

- Avoid timing flakiness on the switch suite by asserting on the `system` WS phase frames rather than sleeping.
- Badge ubiquity is driven by a panel registry rather than a hardcoded list, so a newly added trading panel is automatically covered - a new panel without a badge should fail this suite the day it lands.
- Accessible-name assertions use Playwright's accessibility snapshot, which is also the cheapest early warning for the E38-Q05 audit.

## Test plan

- Mutation check: the deliberately-introduced-regression scenario above is run once per suite to confirm each actually detects its target.

- The crafted-request suite is an automated abuse case; it complements, and does not replace, E38-X02's manual review.
- Test credentials are seed-generated fakes; SR-140 forbids real demo keys in CI and the suite configuration must make that structurally impossible (no secret referenced by the workflow).

## Performance notes

title: Performance and load validation of the demo order path and paper matcher
body:
## Context
Budget #4 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` - order submit to ack p95 <300 ms on demo - is a **hard R3 exit gate**, and E38-S01 is the story that owns the demo half of it. Budget #15 requires replay at up to 100x, which the paper matcher must not bottleneck.

The environment switch adds a budget of its own: it blocks order entry for its whole duration (SCR-074 states typically <=2 s), so a slow switch is a trading outage rather than a slow page.

## Scope / Deliverables
- k6 (or Locust) script `tests/load/e38_demo_orders.js`: sustained order submit/amend/cancel against the demo path at the per-UID rate budget, measuring submit-to-ack p50/p95/p99 separated into backend-internal and exchange RTT components (budget #4 excludes Bybit RTT from the backend-internal figure, per section 3.1).
- Paper-matcher throughput benchmark: replay a recorded BTCUSDT day through the matcher, measuring matched-events per second and asserting the 20x-faster-than-real-time requirement from E38-S03 and the 100x replay ceiling of budget #15.
- Environment-switch timing: measure the full transition (teardown, re-auth, resubscribe) at a realistic subscription count (10 symbols, multi-pane workspace), asserting p95 <=2 s and recording the per-phase breakdown so a regression is attributable.
- Memory: assert the matcher stays within budget #8 (<=300 MB per actively-recorded symbol) during a full-day replay.
- Frontend: assert an environment change does not exceed the frame budget (#1) - measure the render cost of re-badging every panel in a worst-case layout.
- Record all results in `docs/perf/results/E38.md` with the reference-hardware profile stated (section 3.1) and compare against the budget table.

## Out of scope
- Chaos and failure-injection (E38-Q04).
- Load testing other epics' paths (E34 owns fan-out load).
- Tuning - this ticket measures and reports; a breach becomes a defect ticket against the owning story.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Demo order latency is measured against the hard gate
  Given sustained order flow on the demo path
  When the load script completes
  Then submit-to-ack p95 is reported with backend-internal and exchange-RTT components separated, and compared against the 300 ms budget

Scenario: A breach becomes a defect, not a footnote
  Given a measured p95 above the budget
  When results are recorded
  Then a defect ticket is filed against the owning story with the measurement attached, and the R3 exit gate is flagged as at risk

Scenario: The matcher sustains replay speed
  Given a full recorded day
  When replayed through the paper matcher
  Then it matches at least 20x faster than real time and does not become the limiting factor at 100x replay

Scenario: The switch completes inside its window
  Given a 10-symbol multi-pane workspace with full private subscriptions
  When the environment is switched
  Then p95 transition time is at or under 2 s, with a per-phase breakdown recorded

Scenario: Memory stays inside budget
  Given a full-day replay through the matcher
  When memory is sampled
  Then per-symbol resident memory stays at or under 300 MB

Scenario: Re-badging does not drop frames
  Given a worst-case layout with all trading panels open
  When the environment changes
  Then no frame exceeds the 16.6 ms budget as a direct result of re-badging
```

## Technical notes / design
- Measurement methods follow `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 7 exactly; deviating would make the numbers incomparable with other epics' results.
- Order-path load runs against a real demo account on the trading host, not in CI (SR-140); the matcher and frontend benchmarks run in CI against fixtures and become tracked regression gates.
- Separate the exchange RTT component by timestamping at the adapter boundary, since budget #4's hard gate applies to the backend-internal portion and the Bybit RTT is explicitly an uncontrolled factor.
- The matcher benchmark pins the `FillModelConfig` so a config change cannot silently flatter the numbers.

## Test plan
- The scripts are the artefact; they are self-verified by running against a deliberately throttled backend and confirming they detect the induced latency.
- Results are re-run at the end of the sprint to confirm no late regression before the R3 gate.

## Security notes
- Load scripts must not embed credentials; they read from the same encrypted store as the application (SR-004, SR-144).
- Sustained order flow on demo must respect the per-UID rate governor (E34-T02) rather than bypassing it - the test measures the real path including its admission control.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - measurement only. The re-badging frame-cost test protects users who rely on a responsive UI, but has no direct a11y assertion.

## Performance notes
- This ticket *is* the performance work: budgets #1, #4, #8, #13 and #15 from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
- Results feed the Grafana perf dashboard; the matcher throughput and switch duration become tracked metrics with regression alerts, not one-off measurements.

title: Chaos scenarios for environment switching and paper state recovery
body:
## Context
The R3 chaos gate (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 7.4) requires that WS kill, backend restart and Postgres failover all resume to a correct, reconciled state. E38 adds two specifically fragile moments: the environment transition, which deliberately tears down and rebuilds every private subscription, and the paper matcher's in-memory state, which must survive a restart without inventing or losing simulated positions.

SCR-074's requirement that 'a half-switched state is never reachable' is exactly the kind of claim only fault injection can test.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Scenario 1: **backend restart mid-switch** at each phase boundary (after teardown, after re-auth, after partial resubscribe) - assert the session resolves to exactly one environment with consistent subscriptions and that the UI reflects it, never a mixed state.
- Scenario 2: **WS disconnect during a demo order's lifetime** - assert reconciliation against `GET /v5/order/realtime` restores exact state with no duplicate submission and no lost fill.
- Scenario 3: **backend restart with open simulated positions and resting simulated orders** - assert the `PaperLedger` and queue estimates recover from Postgres with no ghost orders and no duplicated fills.
- Scenario 4: **Postgres unavailable during a paper reset** - assert the transaction aborts cleanly and the pre-reset state is fully intact (E38-S06's atomicity criterion under real failure rather than an injected exception).
- Scenario 5: **audit writer unavailable during a cross-environment refusal** - assert the request still fails closed (refused), because failing open would trade an audit gap for a safety breach.
- Scenario 6: **clock skew** between backend and exchange beyond the 1000 ms incident threshold during a demo order - assert the condition is detected and surfaced rather than silently producing mis-sequenced state.
- Scenario 7: **demo private WS flapping** during a switch - assert the transition either completes or rolls back, never stalls indefinitely, and that a stall has a timeout with a stated outcome.
- Record results in `docs/chaos/results/E38.md` with the injection method for each scenario so they are repeatable each release.

## Out of scope
- Fan-out and algo chaos (E34, E33 own theirs).
- Infrastructure-level failover testing of Postgres itself (E45).
- Performance measurement (E38-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No half-switched state survives a restart
  Given the backend is killed at each phase boundary of an environment switch
  When it restarts
  Then the session resolves to exactly one environment with a consistent subscription set, and the UI reflects that environment truthfully

Scenario: Paper state recovers without ghosts
  Given open simulated positions and resting simulated orders
  When the backend restarts
  Then the ledger, positions and resting orders with their queue estimates are restored from Postgres, with no duplicated fill and no order that no longer exists

Scenario: Reset is atomic under real database failure
  Given Postgres becomes unavailable mid-reset
  When the operation fails
  Then the pre-reset balance, positions and orders are all intact and the failure is reported to the user

Scenario: Refusals fail closed without the audit writer
  Given the audit writer is unavailable
  When a cross-environment request is made
  Then it is still refused, and the audit failure is itself alerted

Scenario: A stalled switch resolves rather than hanging
  Given the demo private WS flaps during a transition
  When the configured timeout elapses
  Then the transition rolls back to the previous environment with a stated reason, and order entry is unblocked

Scenario: Clock skew is detected
  Given backend-to-exchange clock offset exceeds one second
  When a demo order is placed
  Then the condition is surfaced as an incident rather than silently accepted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Injection via the project's existing chaos harness (toxiproxy for network faults, container kill for restarts, a fault-injection hook for the audit writer), documented per scenario so the suite is repeatable by anyone.
- Each scenario asserts on **observable state after recovery**, not on log lines, so the test is about correctness rather than implementation detail.
- Phase-boundary restarts are driven by pausing at the `system` phase frames E38-S02 emits, which makes the injection points precise rather than timing-based.
- Scenarios 3 and 4 need a seeded matcher state fixture; build it once and share it with E38-Q02.

## Test plan
- The scenarios are the test artefact. Each must be demonstrated to fail against a deliberately broken build (e.g. a matcher that rebuilds state from memory only), proving the scenario has teeth.
- Run as part of the release checklist, not on every PR, given their runtime.

## Security notes
- Scenario 5 is a security-relevant chaos case: fail-closed behaviour under audit-writer failure is a control, and its verification is shared with E38-X02.
- No real credentials are used; the demo-dependent scenarios run on the trading host per SR-140.

## Accessibility notes
- Scenario 7 includes verifying the UI communicates the stalled/rolled-back state accessibly (announced, not merely visual), because a silent stall during a blocked-order-entry window is dangerous.

## Performance notes
- Record recovery times per scenario; a restart that takes minutes to rebuild matcher state is a defect even if it is eventually correct.

## Observability
- Each scenario asserts that the expected alert fires (WS disconnect with open orders, audit-writer failure, clock skew incident) - verifying the alerting path at the same time as the recovery path.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/` (plans) or `tests/e2e`/`tests/load`/`tests/chaos` (code) and wired into CI where automated.
- [ ] Every scenario has an explicit pass/fail result recorded on the ticket.

- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET; deviations ("QA capacity deviation") stated explicitly if any.
- [ ] Coverage/quality gates for the epic re-checked after execution.

title: Accessibility audit of every E38 surface with screen-reader passes
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` mandates WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI plus manual screen-reader passes, and there is explicitly no exception for owner/admin screens (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8).

E38 is a hard case: the environment distinction must survive colour blindness and greyscale; the band repeats on every panel and must not create an announcement storm; SCR-099's charts each need a table alternative; and the reset confirmation is a destructive dialog whose counts must be announced.

## Scope / Deliverables
- axe-core automated runs against SCR-074 (modal open, each state), SCR-075 (shell in both environments, with a modal open, in a floating Electron window), SCR-079 reset section incl. the open confirmation, SCR-099 incl. table alternatives and comparison-on, SCR-122 eligibility section, SCR-137 parity section - wired as CI checks, not one-off runs.
- Manual screen-reader passes with **NVDA on Windows** (the primary target given the Electron shell) and a secondary pass with the platform reader in the browser build: full keyboard-only operation of the switch flow, the reset confirmation, the results drawer and the parity table.
- Verify against the E38-D05 annotation layer specifically: the band is announced on demand but does not re-announce per panel render; the post-switch banner announces once assertively; focus moves into and returns from every dialog; the typed-confirm error is announced and associated.
- Colour-independence verification on the built app: greyscale plus deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulations for the environment treatments and the simulated badge.
- Contrast re-measurement on the built app against the D05 recorded values.
- Reduced-motion verification: the chrome transition degrades to an instant swap.
- File every finding as a Bug with the WCAG success criterion referenced; blocking findings prevent epic sign-off.

## Out of scope
- Design-time annotation review (E38-D05, already done).
- Design QA of visual fidelity (E38-D07).
- Auditing other epics' panels, except to confirm the E38 badge they host is accessible.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: axe-core is green and wired into CI
  Given every E38 surface and state
  When axe-core runs
  Then there are zero violations, and the checks run on every PR rather than only during this audit

Scenario: The switch is fully keyboard operable
  Given a keyboard-only user with a screen reader
  When they switch environments
  Then the entire path from band to typed confirmation to step-up to completion is operable, with visible focus at every step and the outcome announced

Scenario: No announcement storm from repeated badges
  Given a workspace with many trading panels
  When a panel re-renders
  Then the environment is not re-announced for each panel

Scenario: Destructive counts are announced
  Given a reset with open positions
  When the confirmation opens
  Then the number of positions and orders to be discarded is announced, and focus does not default to the destructive button

Scenario: Charts have usable table alternatives
  Given the SCR-099 equity curve and R distribution
  When navigating with a screen reader only
  Then each has a reachable table alternative conveying the same information

Scenario: Environment survives colour-vision simulation on the built app
  Given the running application
  When rendered in greyscale and the three colour-vision simulations
  Then DEMO and LIVE remain unambiguous, and any failure is filed as priority p0 with the security label
```

## Technical notes / design
- axe-core runs are per-state, not per-page: a modal's states are separate assertions, since most violations hide in states the default render never reaches.
- Screen-reader passes are recorded (screen plus audio) so findings are reviewable without re-running the session.
- Colour-vision simulation on the built app uses a browser-level filter rather than a design tool, because token resolution at runtime is what actually matters.
- Findings reference both the WCAG criterion and the D05 annotation that specified the intended behaviour, so it is clear whether the build or the spec was wrong.

## Test plan
- The audit is the test artefact; its outputs are the axe CI checks (permanent) and the findings list (point-in-time).
- Re-verification of fixed findings is part of this ticket.

## Security notes
- An ambiguous or absent environment indication found during the audit is filed as `priority/p0-critical` with the `security` label - it defeats the user-facing half of SR-040a regardless of whether the cause is an accessibility defect.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket *is* the accessibility verification: WCAG 2.2 AA across 1.3.1, 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.11, 1.4.12, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 3.2.2, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
- Confirm the announcement strategy does not cause a render storm (cross-check with E38-Q03's re-badging frame measurement).

## Observability
N/A - though the audit confirms that status announcements correspond to real state changes rather than to arbitrary re-renders.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `qa/` (plans) or `tests/e2e`/`tests/load`/`tests/chaos` (code) and wired into CI where automated.
- [ ] Every scenario has an explicit pass/fail result recorded on the ticket.
- [ ] Defects raised as Bug tickets with repro steps, severity and the failing scenario id linked.
- [ ] Fixtures used are named and reproducible (recorded Bybit fixture ids or the `CV_FEED=synthetic` generator).
- [ ] Sign-off comment posted by QA/SDET; deviations ("QA capacity deviation") stated explicitly if any.

title: Show demo/live chrome everywhere and switch environments from the shell
body:
## Context
SCR-075 is called 'the single most safety-critical visual element in the app' in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`, and US-PAPER-002's second scenario requires that 'a persistent accent and a text badge mark every trading-capable surface, and the badge is never colour-only'. US-PAPER-003 requires every trading-capable view to reflect and enforce the current environment.

This story builds SCR-074 (the switcher) and SCR-075 (the permanent chrome) against the signed-off designs from E38-D06 and the backend from E38-S02/T02.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-074 EnvBanner**: persistent global band in the app shell (SCR-010), rendering `DEMO`/`LIVE` as text plus icon plus pattern, never colour alone; `role="status"` region read early in document order; never scrolled away and never covered by a modal. The demo variant states 'Demo uses Bybit's demo matching engine - REST order entry only, no private WS order entry.'
- **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal**: repeated in the header of every trading-capable panel - order ticket (CMP-107), group ticket, DOM ladder, positions grid, algo monitor and the chart-trading overlay - and repeated in every floating window. `role="img"` with a static label so it does not re-announce on each panel re-render.
- Every trading panel's accessible name includes the environment ('Order ticket - LIVE - Main') per SCR-075.
- **SCR-074 switcher modal**: opened only by clicking the band (no hotkey may be bound - assert this in the hotkey registry), listing live accounts available, stating that working orders in the current environment stay there and are not migrated, requiring the typed confirmation phrase plus step-up, and rendering all catalogued states: switching (with the phase progress from E38-S02's `system` frames), switched (10 s full-width confirmation banner), failed (stays on the previous environment with the reason), not permitted, and blocked-by-in-flight-activity with the blocker list.
- **CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard**: wrap the order ticket and DOM click-to-trade handlers so a mismatch renders the wrapped control disabled-with-reason rather than silently rerouting; this is defence in depth over E38-T02's server check.
- Order confirmation copy restates the environment ('You are about to send a **LIVE** order') per SCR-075.
- A single shared environment store subscription feeds every badge; the band does not remount on route change.

## Out of scope
- The backend switch endpoint (E38-S02) and isolation middleware (E38-T02).
- Parity report, reset, eligibility and simulated-results surfaces (S05-S08).
- The step-up modal (E09).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Environment is visible on every trading-capable surface
  Given any trading panel including a floated or maximised one
  When it is rendered
  Then it shows the environment badge in its header and includes the environment in its accessible name

Scenario: Switching is deliberate
  Given the session is in Demo
  When the user attempts to reach Live
  Then the only path is clicking the band, typing the confirmation phrase and passing step-up, and no hotkey binding can invoke it

Scenario: One-click trading is disarmed on switch
  Given one-click trading is armed
  When the environment switches
  Then the UI reflects the disarmed state returned by the server and no one-click action is operable until re-armed

Scenario: The transition blocks order entry
  Given a switch is in progress
  When the user attempts to submit an order
  Then every order-entry control is disabled with the transition stated, and the phase progress is shown and announced

Scenario: A failed switch leaves the previous environment intact
  Given the server returns a failure mid-transition
  When the modal handles it
  Then the previous environment's chrome is restored unchanged and the failure reason is displayed

Scenario: Not-permitted state is explanatory but not disclosing
  Given a manager without live access
  When they open the switcher
  Then the switch action is disabled with the reason that the owner has not enabled Live for their account, without naming who does have access

Scenario: Mismatched order is blocked client-side too
  Given the workspace environment context is demo and a control targets a live account
  When submission is attempted
  Then CMP-139 disables the control with a reason and no request is sent

Scenario: Distinguishable without colour
  Given the built application
  When rendered in greyscale and in three colour-vision simulations
  Then DEMO and LIVE remain unambiguous
```

## Technical notes / design
- One Zustand (or the project's chosen store) slice holds `{environment, phase, allowedEnvironments, armed}`, hydrated from `GET /auth/session` and updated from the `system` WS topic; badges subscribe with selectors so an environment change does not re-render panel bodies.
- The band lives in the shell layout above the router outlet so it never unmounts on navigation; modals render in a portal *below* the band in stacking order.
- The hotkey assertion is a unit test over the hotkey registry (`GET /settings/hotkeys` vocabulary) asserting no action id maps to the environment switch.
- All colours come from `color.env.demo` / `color.env.live` tokens; a lint rule forbids literal hex in these components.
- Phase progress consumes the `system` frames from E38-S02 rather than a client-side timer, so the UI cannot claim completion the server has not reached.
- Electron: the band must render identically in detached/floating windows, which are separate BrowserWindows - the store is synchronised across windows via the existing IPC bridge, not duplicated fetches.

## Test plan
- Unit: badge renders text for each environment; accessible name composition for each panel type.
- Unit: hotkey registry assertion (no binding reaches the switch).
- Interaction (Testing Library): typed-confirm gate - the switch button stays disabled until the exact phrase is typed; cancel restores focus to the band.
- Interaction: CMP-139 mismatch disables with reason and emits no request.
- Storybook + visual regression: Demo, Live, SwitchConfirmFlow, switching, switched, failed, not-permitted, blocked - in both themes and both densities.
- axe-core: zero violations on the shell with the band and on the open modal.
- E2E Playwright (web and Electron, feeds E38-Q02): full switch with step-up; badge presence on every trading panel; floating-window badge; band not covered by a modal.
- Coverage target: >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
- This is the user-facing half of SR-040a and the visible part of US-PAPER-003. A missing or wrong badge is a `priority/p0-critical` security-labelled defect.
- CMP-139 is defence in depth only - the test suite must include a case proving that bypassing the client guard still results in a server 403 (cross-referenced with E38-T02), so nobody is tempted to treat the client as the boundary.
- Not-permitted copy must not disclose other users' grants.
- No credential or key material is rendered on any of these surfaces.

## Accessibility notes
- WCAG 2.2 AA per the E38-D05 annotation layer: band is `role="status"` and polite; the post-switch confirmation is `role="alert"` announced once; the modal traps focus, focuses the typed-confirm field on open and returns focus to the band on close; visible focus throughout; error states announced and associated with their field.
- The environment distinction is text plus icon plus pattern (1.4.1); contrast >=4.5:1 text and >=3:1 non-text (1.4.3/1.4.11).
- Reduced-motion: the chrome transition degrades to an instant swap.
- Manual NVDA pass required; recorded on the ticket.

## Performance notes
- The band is part of the shell and must not remount on route change; verify with the React profiler.
- An environment change must not trigger a full re-render of trading panels - only the badge subtree; assert with a render-count test.
- No regression to budget #10 (cold start <=3 s) or #9 (bundle size) - the band and badges are tiny and must stay in the initial bundle since they are safety chrome and may never be lazily loaded.

## Observability
- Client analytics: switcher opened, confirmation typed, switch confirmed, switch cancelled, switch failed (with phase).
- Verify the server-side `session.environment_switched` audit row appears after a UI-driven switch (checked in E38-D07 and E38-Q02).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria demonstrated by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% lines on touched backend/engine packages, >=80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour where they diverged.
- [ ] Changelog fragment added per `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §3.
- [ ] 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner; PR <=400 LOC diff; merged via merge queue.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (which flag gates this, default per environment).
- [ ] Design sign-off: built screen compared against the Figma spec by a designer (`design-qa`); discrepancies fixed or filed as Bug with priority.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched screens, manual screen-reader pass recorded, keyboard-only path verified (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- [ ] Storybook stories added/updated for every touched component with all states.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E38-D06` (signed-off handoff, design-ahead rule), `E38-S02` (switch endpoint and `system` phase frames), `E38-T02` (server-side isolation this UI reflects).
- Consumes the app shell (SCR-010) and the order ticket (E30), DOM ladder (E31) and positions grid (E29) surfaces it badges - coordinate with those epics on header slot availability.

## Branch
`feat/e38-env-chrome-ui`; PR size: split into (1) store + band, (2) per-panel badges + guard, (3) switcher modal.

title: Present simulated results with model disclosure and simulated-everywhere labels
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-004's third scenario requires that simulator positions are 'visually marked as simulated everywhere', and US-PAPER-005 requires paper results to be 'stored separately and never aggregate into live statistics, with a clear label on every view' and journaled 'with the same fields plus an environment tag'.

SCR-099's design sign-off checklist demands that every figure carries the 'simulated' framing, that fill-model assumptions are stated explicitly, and that comparison against real trades is opt-in and clearly separated. This story ships SCR-099 and the cross-cutting `is_paper` labelling designed in E38-D04.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Build **SCR-099 Replay paper-trading results** as a drawer at the end of a replay session: simulated fills, P&L, R distribution, per-trade list with entry/exit and R, the modelled slippage assumptions, export (CMP-099), and the 'these results are not a backtest guarantee' caveat. Components: CMP-049 Table, CMP-099 PrintExportBar, CMP-116 PnLBadge, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard.
- The **fill-model disclosure block**, rendered from the `FillModelConfig` returned by E38-S03 - queue position on/off, submit/cancel/market-data latency, slippage mode, fee source (live rate vs estimated default), funding applied - with each value shown, not merely named.
- Opt-in comparison against the same period's real trades, **off by default**, with the two series visually and textually separated and never summed into one total.
- The **simulated labelling system** applied across surfaces that render `is_paper` rows: orders blotter, positions grid, journal list, journal trade detail and analytics headers - badge in the heading and in the accessible name, not only a chip.
- Analytics exclusion: paper rows are excluded from live statistics by default with an explicit, labelled include-toggle; promoting a session to the journal writes entries flagged `simulated=true`.
- A table alternative for every chart on SCR-099, reachable by keyboard.

## Out of scope
- The matcher itself (E38-S03) and the divergence job (E38-T03).
- Journal analytics computation (E41) - this story contributes the simulated treatment and the exclusion rule that E41's queries honour.
- Replay transport controls (E26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every figure carries simulated framing
  Given a completed replay paper session
  When the results drawer opens
  Then the word Simulated appears in the region heading and in the accessible name of every results region

Scenario: Fill-model assumptions are stated with their values
  Given the session used a specific FillModelConfig
  When the disclosure block renders
  Then queue position, submit latency, cancel latency, market-data latency, slippage mode, fee source and funding application are each shown with the value actually used

Scenario: Estimated fees are flagged
  Given the matcher fell back to default fee rates
  When results render
  Then the fee figures are marked as estimated, with the reason available

Scenario: Comparison is opt-in and separated
  Given the comparison against real trades
  When the drawer first opens
  Then comparison is off, and when enabled the simulated and real series remain separately labelled and are never aggregated into a single total

Scenario: Paper results never aggregate into live statistics
  Given a journal containing both simulated and real trades
  When live analytics are computed
  Then simulated rows are excluded by default and the include-toggle is explicit and labelled

Scenario: Every chart has a keyboard-reachable table alternative
  Given the equity curve and the R distribution
  When navigating by keyboard only
  Then a table alternative for each is reachable and readable by a screen reader

Scenario: Promotion to journal is tagged and audited
  Given the user promotes the session to the journal
  When the entries are written
  Then each is flagged simulated true and the action is audited as journal.simulated_import
```

## Technical notes / design
- Results are computed server-side at session end and fetched once (SCR-099 performance note); the drawer has a skeleton state sized to the final layout and no live subscriptions remain open.
- The simulated badge is a design-system component contributed by E38-D04, not a page-local element, so every consuming surface picks it up by upgrading the package.
- `is_paper` drives the badge; `environment` drives the env badge. The two must render distinctly - a unit test asserts a demo simulated row shows both and that neither substitutes for the other.
- Analytics exclusion is implemented as a default query filter in the journal data layer (coordinated with E41), not as a per-component filter, so a new view cannot accidentally include paper rows.
- Chart colour/series encodings must be distinguishable without colour; prefer direct labelling over a legend for the two-series comparison.
- Export reuses E41's CSV/Parquet export path with the simulated flag included as a column.

## Test plan
- Unit: disclosure block renders every `FillModelConfig` field including the estimated-fee marking.
- Unit: badge placement rules across blotter/positions/journal/analytics; simulated and environment badges coexist.
- Unit: analytics default excludes `is_paper` rows; the include-toggle changes the query, not just the display.
- Interaction: comparison toggle defaults off; enabling never merges totals.
- axe-core: zero violations on the drawer, incl. the table alternatives.
- Storybook: populated, empty (no simulated trades), loading, error, comparison-on, estimated-fees.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): run a short replay session with the paper matcher, open the drawer, export, promote to journal and assert the journal rows are flagged and audited.
- Coverage target: >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
- Threat R12: simulated results leaking into live performance statistics and driving real position sizing. Controls: data-layer default exclusion, mandatory labelling, audited promotion.
- Export must not create an unauthenticated shareable artefact; it downloads through the authenticated session only.
- Data classification: trading performance data, internal.

## Accessibility notes
- 'Simulated' in headings and accessible names (SCR-099 a11y note); results are a table plus a summary description list.
- Table alternative for every chart, keyboard reachable, with a programmatic association to the chart it replaces.
- Export controls have accessible names stating format and scope.
- Badge is not colour-only; contrast verified per E38-D05's measurements.
- Manual screen-reader pass required.

## Performance notes
- Single fetch at session end; no open subscriptions. The per-trade table virtualises above 200 rows.
- Rendering the drawer must not disturb the chart frame budget (#1) if a chart is still mounted behind it - measure with the profiler during the replay-to-results transition.

## Observability
- Emit `replay.results_viewed`, `replay.results_exported` and `replay.results_promoted_to_journal`; the last is audited as `journal.simulated_import` (SCR-099 analytics/audit note).
- Count include-toggle activations on analytics - frequent use suggests the default is wrong and is worth revisiting with the Owner.

title: Reset a paper balance safely and never in live
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-006 (Should) lets a trader start a clean practice run. Two of its three scenarios are safety requirements rather than features: open positions must be warned about and explicitly confirmed as discarded, and **the reset control is unavailable in Live and hidden entirely, not merely disabled**. Its NFR adds that reset never touches live data and that each reset starts a new paper session id used by analytics.

The control lives on SCR-079 (Account detail drawer, trading side) per `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Backend: `POST /exchange-accounts/{accountId}/paper-reset` (new endpoint; add to `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` with `x-idempotency: required` and `x-rbac` permissions `accounts:write`, scope `granted_accounts`), taking a starting balance and requiring the account to be a paper/demo-bound account.
- Reset semantics, executed in one transaction: cancel and clear simulated resting orders in the matcher, close and clear simulated positions, set the `PaperLedger` wallet to the chosen starting balance, allocate a **new paper session id**, and write a reset record into the paper journal plus an audit row.
- Hard refusal if the target account's `env` is `live` or the account is not paper-capable - returning 403 and auditing the attempt at high severity (this is a data-destruction path pointed at the wrong account type).
- Frontend on **SCR-079**: the reset control with a starting-balance input validated against the instrument/account constraints; a warning naming the exact count of open simulated positions and resting orders that will be discarded; an explicit confirmation (CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, variant per E38-D06); and **complete absence of the control when the environment is live** - not a disabled control.
- Analytics: the new paper session id partitions results so a fresh run is not blended with the previous one; surfaced in the journal filter.

## Out of scope
- Resetting a Bybit demo account's real balance at the exchange (not possible through the API; only the local paper ledger is reset - state this in the UI copy).
- The matcher itself (E38-S03).
- Journal analytics grouping beyond exposing the session id (E41).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reset clears state and sets the balance
  Given a paper account with simulated positions and resting orders
  When the user resets with a chosen starting balance
  Then positions and orders are cleared, the balance is set, a new paper session id is allocated, and the reset is recorded in the paper journal

Scenario: Open positions require explicit confirmation
  Given open paper positions exist
  When the user initiates a reset
  Then a warning names the exact number of positions and orders to be discarded and the reset proceeds only after explicit confirmation

Scenario: The control is hidden, not disabled, in live
  Given the session environment is live
  When the account drawer renders
  Then the reset control is absent from the DOM entirely, and a test asserts no disabled reset control exists

Scenario: Reset never touches live data
  Given a live account id is submitted to the reset endpoint
  When the request is processed
  Then it is refused with 403, no live row is modified, and the attempt is audited at high severity

Scenario: Reset is atomic
  Given a failure occurs partway through clearing state
  When the transaction aborts
  Then no partial reset is visible: balance, positions and orders are all as they were before

Scenario: Analytics separate the runs
  Given two paper sessions separated by a reset
  When journal analytics are viewed
  Then results are attributable to each session id and are not blended by default
```

## Technical notes / design
- The endpoint is idempotency-keyed so a retried request after a network blip does not double-reset into a second session id.
- The reset runs inside a Postgres transaction covering the ledger, positions, orders and journal rows; the in-memory matcher state is rebuilt from the committed state afterwards, so a crash between commit and rebuild recovers correctly rather than leaving ghosts.
- The 'hidden in live' requirement is enforced by conditional rendering at the container level plus a unit test asserting absence - a CSS-hidden control would satisfy neither the story nor a screen-reader user.
- Copy must state plainly that this resets the **local paper ledger**, not any exchange-side demo balance, so the user is not misled about what changed.

## Test plan
- Unit: refusal matrix over account env and paper-capability.
- Unit: atomicity - inject a failure after positions are cleared and assert full rollback.
- Unit: idempotent retry yields one reset and one session id.
- Unit (frontend): the control is absent in live; present in demo; the warning renders exact counts.
- Contract: the new endpoint against the OpenAPI document; error registry entry for the refusal code.
- Integration: reset with open positions, then verify matcher state, ledger, journal record and audit row.
- axe-core on the drawer with the confirmation open.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): reset from the UI and confirm analytics partition by session id.
- Coverage: >=85% backend, >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
- This is a destructive data operation. Threats: wrong-target destruction (live account), unauthorised destruction (a manager resetting an account they merely view), repudiation.
- Controls: server-side env/paper-capability check, `accounts:write` on granted accounts only, explicit confirmation, idempotency, high-severity audit of both successes and refused attempts.
- Data classification: financial simulation data; destruction is irreversible, so the journal reset record is the only recovery trail and must be written before the clear commits.
- `security` label applied per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 (touches account-scoped state).

## Accessibility notes
- The confirmation dialog is labelled by its heading, traps focus, does not default focus to the destructive button, and announces the counts of what will be discarded.
- The starting-balance field has a visible label, an accessible error message on invalid input, and is not validated by colour alone.
- Absence-in-live is the accessible behaviour: a disabled control would be announced and confuse; the design explicitly requires removal.

## Performance notes
- Reset is a small transactional operation on a single account; it must complete within budget #13 (write endpoints <300 ms p95 backend-internal). Clearing a large number of resting simulated orders should be a set operation, not a per-order loop.

## Observability
- Audit `paper.balance_reset` with account, previous balance, new balance, discarded position and order counts, and the new session id; audit `paper.balance_reset_refused` with the reason.
- Metric `cv_paper_resets_total{outcome}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria demonstrated by automated tests referencing each scenario by name.
- [ ] Coverage: >=85% lines on touched backend/engine packages, >=80% on touched frontend packages; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` reflect shipped behaviour where they diverged.

- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (which flag gates this, default per environment).
- [ ] Design sign-off: built screen compared against the Figma spec by a designer (`design-qa`); discrepancies fixed or filed as Bug with priority.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched screens, manual screen-reader pass recorded, keyboard-only path verified (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).
- [ ] Storybook stories added/updated for every touched component with all states.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E38-D06` (SCR-079 reset design and copy), `E38-S03` (the `PaperLedger` and matcher state being reset), `E38-S01` (paper-capable account routing established).
- SCR-079's shell is owned by E27/E28 - land this as a section inside it, not a new screen.

## Sizing

This story is one idempotent transactional endpoint plus a confirmation dialog and a conditional-render guard; the ledger it truncates belongs to E38-S03 and the audit plumbing to E38-T02. No new schema, no new shared component, no cross-surface rollout. Epic engineering total is now 28 points against the roadmap's registered 26 (+7.7%, inside the +/-15% tolerance band).

title: Grant, revoke and acknowledge per-user demo and live eligibility
body:
## Context
US-PAPER-007 (Should) lets the owner control who may use demo and live so new managers start safely. Its NFR is precise: 'eligibility is a server-side attribute of the user-account binding'. That binding already exists as `user_account_access` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 3.1.3), and the session already exposes `allowed_environments` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `SessionInfo`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` `auth_ok`).

The hardest requirement is revocation while positions are open: existing positions must remain manageable in **reduce-only** mode while new entries are refused - a graceful degradation, not a hard cut that would trap a manager in a position they cannot close.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Persist live eligibility as a server-side attribute of the user-account binding: extend `user_account_access` (migration) with `live_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` and `live_enabled_acknowledged_at timestamptz`, and derive `allowed_environments` for a session from the union over the user's granted accounts, intersected with the `live_trading` flag.
- Grant and revoke through the existing `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` surface, extending `AccountAccessGrantInput` with the eligibility field; changes are audited and take effect on the next request, with existing WS subscriptions for revoked scope terminated with a `revoked` frame (reason `account_scope_changed`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5), which E42-T08 delivers for that endpoint; E42-T04's contract slice S1 replaces the older `unsubscribed` wording in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- **Acknowledgement on promotion**: when live access is granted, the user must acknowledge the change at next sign-in before any live-targeting action is permitted; the acknowledgement is recorded and audited.
- **Revocation with open positions**: when live access is revoked while the user holds live positions, their session enters reduce-only for those accounts - amend/cancel/close are permitted, position-opening is refused with a clear reason - until the positions are flat.
- Frontend on **SCR-122 Admin: user detail / edit**: the eligibility control, the current-state display, the reason surfaced to a demo-only manager on SCR-074 ('The owner hasn't enabled Live for your account.'), the acknowledgement prompt at sign-in, and the reduce-only banner state.
- Wire `allowed_environments` into E38-T02's isolation check so eligibility is enforced at the same choke point rather than in a second place.

## Out of scope
- Role and permission administration generally (E42 owns SCR-122's structure and the RBAC matrix).
- The `live_trading` global flag (E42) and the R4 live-enablement gate (E44).
- Reduce-only enforcement mechanics in the OMS (E29/E39 own the reduce-only order path; this story sets the flag that turns it on for a user-account pair).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A demo-only manager cannot select live
  Given a manager whose grants include no live-enabled account
  When they open the environment switcher
  Then no live account is selectable and the Live switch is disabled with the reason shown

Scenario: Promotion requires acknowledgement
  Given the owner grants live access to a manager
  When that manager next signs in
  Then they must acknowledge the change before any live-targeting action is permitted, and both the grant and the acknowledgement are audited

Scenario: Revocation with open positions degrades to reduce-only
  Given a manager holds live positions
  When the owner revokes their live access
  Then existing positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode while new entries are refused with a stated reason

Scenario: Revocation with no open positions is immediate
  Given a manager holds no live positions
  When live access is revoked
  Then live-targeting requests are refused with 403 from the next request, and live subscriptions are force-closed

Scenario: Eligibility is enforced server-side, not in the UI
  Given a manager without live eligibility
  When a crafted live-targeting request is sent directly to the API
  Then it is refused with 403 and audited, independently of what the UI offered

Scenario: A manager cannot self-grant
  Given a manager with accounts:write on their own grants
  When they attempt to set live eligibility on themselves
  Then the request is refused: eligibility changes require the owner's users:write permission
```

## Technical notes / design
- Reuse the existing account-access endpoint rather than inventing an eligibility endpoint - the story's NFR explicitly places eligibility on the user-account binding, and a second surface would split the decision across two places (the same reasoning `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` gives for rejecting a `rules:arm_live` permission).
- Session `allowed_environments` derivation is cached per session and invalidated on grant change; the force-close of revoked subscriptions is the existing mechanism from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` section 9.
- Reduce-only is expressed as a per-(user, account) flag consumed by the OMS's existing reduce-only path; it is set at revocation and cleared automatically when the account's live positions reach flat.
- Acknowledgement is a row, not a client-side dismissal: the API refuses live actions while `live_enabled_acknowledged_at` is null for a currently-granted account.
- Migration is additive with a safe default (`false`), so no existing user silently gains live access.

## Test plan
- Unit: `allowed_environments` derivation over grant combinations, incl. the `live_trading` flag being off.
- Unit: self-grant refusal; owner-only enforcement.
- Unit: acknowledgement gate blocks live actions until recorded.
- Unit: reduce-only flag set on revocation with open positions, cleared on flat.
- Contract: extended `AccountAccessGrantInput`/`AccountAccessGrant` schemas; session `allowed_environments`; `auth_ok` frame.
- Integration: revoke while positions are open, then assert close succeeds and open is refused; assert WS force-close on revoked scope.
- Migration test: default `false` for all existing rows; rollback tested.
- E2E (feeds E38-Q02): owner grants, manager acknowledges at sign-in, manager switches to live; then owner revokes and the manager sees reduce-only.
- Coverage: >=90% on the eligibility derivation module.

## Security notes
- This is a privilege-management surface: threats are elevation of privilege (self-grant, forged grant), bypass (acting on a grant before acknowledgement), and trapping a user in an unmanageable position (availability harm) - the reduce-only design addresses the last.
- Controls: owner-only `users:write` for eligibility, audited grant/revoke/acknowledge, enforcement at E38-T02's single choke point, additive migration defaulting to no access.
- The reason shown to a demo-only manager must not disclose other users' grants.
- `security` label mandatory (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8: anything touching RBAC). Abuse cases are exercised in E38-X02.

## Accessibility notes
- The eligibility control on SCR-122 has a clear current-state label and an accessible confirmation for a change that affects another person's capabilities.
- The acknowledgement prompt at sign-in is a focused, keyboard-operable dialog that cannot be dismissed by clicking away, with its consequences stated in text.
- The reduce-only banner uses the disabled-with-reason pattern so the reason is programmatically associated with the blocked controls.

## Performance notes
- Eligibility resolution is per-request but cache-backed; it must not add a query per request. Assert p95 added latency <2 ms, consistent with E38-T02's budget.

## Observability
- Audit `user.live_access_granted`, `user.live_access_revoked`, `user.live_access_acknowledged`, each with actor, subject, account and timestamp.
- Metric `cv_live_eligible_users` gauge, visible on the admin security centre - an unexpected increase is a security signal.
- Log reduce-only activations and their automatic clearance.
