title: Author the journal black-box test plan and extend the E2E suite
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box test plan plus white-box review per feature, and names the **Trading-demo** E2E suite that must cover "order fills reflected in positions/PnL/journal". This ticket owns the journal's black-box plan, its fixtures, its exploratory charter and the E2E additions that prove capture works end to end from a real demo fill.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Black-box test plan** `docs/qa/plans/E41-journal.md` covering US-JRN-001..010, organised by story group: capture (001, 004, 005), annotation (002, 003), analytics (006, 007, 008), review (009), export (010). Each case states preconditions, steps, expected result, and the requirement id it verifies.
- **Shared fixtures** (used by E41-D05, E41-Q02 and the dev suites - defined once here): `journal_fixture_empty`, `journal_fixture_12_trades` (low sample), `journal_fixture_100` (the worked example for E41-T05), `journal_fixture_10k` (density/perf), `journal_fixture_pruned_context`, `journal_fixture_reconciling`, `journal_fixture_fanout_group3`, `journal_fixture_divergent_pnl`, `journal_fixture_external_close`. Fixtures are seeded, synthetic and committed.
- **E2E additions** (Playwright, web + Electron) to the Trading-demo suite:
  1. place and close a demo trade -> journal entry appears with correct weighted averages;
  2. fan-out group of three -> three legs plus one aggregate;
  3. add a note and tags; bulk-tag from the list;
  4. open trade detail; verify MAE/MFE and the fills timeline; jump to replay and back;
  5. analytics dashboard: filter, toggle demo, switch every chart to its table alternative;
  6. tag merge with the affected-count confirmation;
  7. export as Owner and as Manager, asserting scope, watermark and the audit entry;
  8. pruned-context path: "context not recorded" shown, no spinner.
- **Exploratory charters** (session-based, 90 min each, with notes recorded): (a) "break the materialiser" - odd fill sequences, reversals, flat-and-reverse, zero-qty, dust; (b) "mislead me with statistics" - hunt for any surface where an unqualified figure over a tiny sample is presented as fact; (c) "see what I shouldn't" - cross-account visibility from every role.
- **Regression pack** entries added to the R3 suite for every fixed defect.
- Defect triage and re-test through to closure.

## Out of scope
- Performance and chaos runs (E41-Q02); a11y audit and final sign-off (E41-Q03); unit tests (owned by the implementing tickets).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Coverage of requirements
  When the test plan is reviewed against docs/plan/11-user-stories.md section 25
  Then every acceptance scenario of US-JRN-001..010 maps to at least one black-box case, and the mapping table is in the plan

Scenario: E2E proves real capture
  Given a trade is opened and closed on Bybit demo through the app
  When the E2E suite runs
  Then it asserts the resulting journal entry's weighted average entry and exit, R-multiple and fees against the executions, with no fixture short-circuit

Scenario: Exploratory findings are actioned
  When each charter session completes
  Then its notes, coverage and findings are recorded and every finding is filed as a Bug or explicitly dismissed with a reason

Scenario: Fixtures are reusable
  Then every fixture named in Scope exists, is seeded and deterministic, and is referenced by at least one other E41 ticket rather than duplicated
```

## Technical notes / design
E2E runs against the demo environment with the REST-only order-entry constraint, so the suite must tolerate the absence of WS order entry on demo (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` locked decisions). The capture assertions compare against `GET /executions/closed-pnl` as an independent oracle rather than against the journal's own maths - checking a calculation against itself proves nothing.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* the test plan. Its own quality gate is the requirement-to-case mapping table plus QA lead review.

## Security notes
Charter (c) is an authorisation-testing session covering horizontal escalation (Manager A -> Manager B's trades) and IDOR on `journalTradeId`, feeding evidence into E41-X02. Test fixtures contain no real account data or credentials.

## Accessibility notes
The E2E suite includes keyboard-only paths for the core journeys (list -> detail -> replay; analytics -> table alternative), but the conformance audit itself is E41-Q03.

## Performance notes
E2E asserts functional correctness only; timing assertions live in E41-Q02 so a slow CI agent does not produce flaky functional failures.

## Observability
Test runs publish results to the CI dashboard; the suite asserts that the expected audit events (`journal.note_added`, `journal.tag_added`, `journal.exported`) actually appear in the audit log, which makes observability itself testable.

## Context
Three budgets in the plan are only claims until measured: REST reads p95 <150 ms (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` section 13), SCR-095 interactive <=800 ms at 10 000 trades, breakdown queries <=2 s at 10 000 trades (US-JRN-008 NFR), and SCR-093 scrolling at <=8 ms scripting per frame. Separately, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` mandates chaos/failover tests, and the journal has a specific failure mode worth rehearsing: the materialiser losing or duplicating an entry across a restart or a Postgres outage would corrupt every downstream statistic (risk R7).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **k6 load scripts** under `tests/load/journal/`: `list_trades.js` (cursor paging at 100/page over 10k entries), `analytics_totals.js`, `analytics_all_breakdowns.js` (all seven `group_by` values), `trade_detail.js`, `trade_context.js`. Each reports p50/p95/p99 and error rate against the declared budget and fails the run on breach.
- **Frontend perf benchmarks**: SCR-093 virtualised scroll (scripting ms/frame over a 5 s continuous scroll at 10k rows) and SCR-095 time-to-interactive at 10k trades, both recorded as numbers in the ticket and wired as CI performance checks.
- **Export load**: 60 000-row CSV and Parquet exports, measuring duration, memory ceiling (must stream, not materialise) and that the async path engages.
- **Materialiser throughput**: replay a recorded execution burst and assert `journal_materialiser_lag_seconds` p95 <5 s.
- **Chaos scenarios** (each asserting both correctness and recovery):
  1. kill the API mid-close, restart -> exactly one entry, byte-identical (idempotency);
  2. Postgres unavailable for 60 s during active trading -> writes buffer to the bounded WAL and replay on recovery with no loss or duplication (`20-architecture.md` F8);
  3. execution stream disconnect and redelivery of an already-processed batch -> no duplicates;
  4. object storage unavailable during snapshot capture -> trades still journaled, failure reason recorded, no back-pressure on the execution stream;
  5. exchange 5xx / rate-limit 10018 during the nightly reconciliation -> job backs off, retries, and reports incomplete rather than reporting false divergences;
  6. clock skew of +/-2 s between the app and exchange timestamps -> trade grouping and hour-of-day breakdowns remain correct or degrade explicitly.
- A **results report** with the measured numbers against each budget, attached to this ticket and summarised for the R3 PRR.

## Out of scope
- Functional E2E (E41-Q01); a11y audit (E41-Q03); tuning work itself (defects are filed against the owning ticket).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Read budgets met
  When the k6 suite runs against a 10 000-entry dataset on the staging backend
  Then GET /journal/trades and the analytics totals query are p95 under 150 ms and the full seven-breakdown query completes within 2 s

Scenario: Frontend budgets met
  When SCR-093 is scrolled continuously for 5 seconds over 10 000 rows
  Then scripting time stays at or below 8 ms per frame
  And SCR-095 is interactive within 800 ms for the same dataset

Scenario: Idempotency under crash
  Given the API is killed between writing an entry and committing its consumer offset
  When it restarts and the batch is redelivered
  Then exactly one entry exists and it is byte-identical to the pre-crash row

Scenario: Postgres outage
  Given Postgres is unavailable for 60 seconds while trades close
  Then journal writes buffer to the bounded WAL and replay on recovery with no lost or duplicated entries

Scenario: Reconciliation under exchange failure
  Given the exchange returns 5xx and then rate-limit 10018 during reconciliation
  Then the job backs off and retries, reports the run as incomplete, and raises no false divergence alerts

Scenario: Export streams
  Given a 60 000-row export
  Then process memory does not grow proportionally to row count and the asynchronous path is used

Scenario: Budget breach fails loudly
  Given any measured value breaches its declared budget
  Then the CI performance check fails and a defect is filed against the owning ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
Load runs use the E41-Q01 fixtures so perf and functional testing share one dataset definition. Analytics measurements must be taken both cold (cache empty) and warm, and both numbers reported - a warm-only number would flatter the endpoint and hide the real first-open experience that SCR-095's 800 ms budget describes. The E41-K01 benchmark harness is re-run here as a regression check against the tier decision recorded in ADR-0016.

## Test plan
This ticket is the test. Its own gate is that every scenario in Scope has a recorded numeric result or an explicit pass/fail, not a narrative.

## Security notes
Chaos scenario 2 and 5 must confirm that a failure never causes a *silent* data gap - a journal that quietly omits trades is an integrity failure against objective **O8** ("integrity of recorded market data and journal history") in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Load tests run against synthetic data only and use non-production credentials.

## Accessibility notes
N/A (measurement ticket); the scroll benchmark must run with the default density that a11y review approved, not a reduced density that would flatter the number.

## Performance notes
Budgets under test are listed in Context; all results are recorded against them in the R3 PRR evidence pack.

## Observability
Verifies that `journal_analytics_query_seconds`, `journal_materialiser_lag_seconds`, `journal_reconciliation_divergence_total` and `journal_export_duration_seconds` are actually emitted and correctly labelled - an unemitted metric is a defect filed here.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] k6 scripts committed and runnable via `make load-journal`.
- [ ] Frontend perf benchmarks wired as CI performance checks.
- [ ] All six chaos scenarios executed with recorded outcomes.
- [ ] Results report attached with cold and warm numbers against every budget.
- [ ] Defects filed for every breach; blockers closed before E41-Q03 sign-off.

title: Journal accessibility audit, regression pack and QA sign-off
body:
## Context
This is the epic's closing gate. `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core in CI **and** manual screen-reader passes; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 2.2 requires an epic-level regression and exploratory pass plus recorded QA sign-off before E41 can be Done. Four new screens and four new components make this a real audit, not a formality.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated a11y**: axe-core runs on `/journal`, `/journal/:id`, `/journal/analytics` and the tag manager modal, plus every Storybook story for CMP-166, CMP-167, CMP-168, CMP-169. Zero serious or critical violations; any moderate violation is either fixed or recorded as an accepted deviation with the accessibility specialist's sign-off.
- **Manual screen-reader passes** with NVDA (Windows) and VoiceOver (macOS), covering: navigating and sorting the journal table; bulk-selecting and tagging; opening and reading a trade post-mortem including the MAE/MFE and SL-path text descriptions; switching every analytics chart to its table alternative and reading the text summary; completing a tag merge including hearing the affected-trade count; completing an export including hearing the watermark/audit notice. Announcements are asserted against the literal strings authored in E41-D04.
- **Keyboard-only pass** of every journey with no pointer at all, including modal focus traps, return focus, and the drawer variant of SCR-094.
- **Contrast and zoom verification** in both themes at 100% and 200% zoom, including tag chip colours from the picker.
- **Colour-independence check**: MAE/MFE scatter (shape by outcome), R-distribution histogram, low-confidence bucket marking, demo/live separation, auto vs manual tags - each verified to convey its meaning with colour removed.
- **Epic-level regression pack** run across all four screens plus the journal's integration points (positions -> journal, rules -> auto tags, replay -> post-mortem), added to the R3 regression suite.
- **QA sign-off record** consolidating E41-Q01 functional results, E41-Q02 performance and chaos results, E41-D05 design QA, and E41-X02 security review, with an explicit statement of any open defects and their agreed disposition.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the defects found (filed against the owning tickets); the pen-test (E43, R4).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated conformance
  When axe-core runs on all four journal surfaces and every new component story
  Then there are zero serious or critical violations, and any moderate violation is recorded as an accepted deviation with the accessibility specialist's sign-off

Scenario: Screen-reader completeness
  Given a screen-reader user with no pointer
  When they filter the journal, open a trade, read its MAE and MFE, switch an analytics chart to its table and export
  Then every step is completable and every announcement matches the strings authored in E41-D04

Scenario: Colour independence
  Given all colour is removed from the rendering
  Then win/loss outcome, low-confidence buckets, demo versus live separation, and auto versus manual tags all remain distinguishable

Scenario: Zoom
  Given 200% browser zoom in both themes
  Then no content is lost or clipped, no horizontal scrolling is required for reading order, and contrast still meets AA

Scenario: Sign-off gate
  Given an open P0 or P1 defect against E41 scope
  Then QA sign-off is withheld and E41 cannot move to Done
```

## Technical notes / design
The audit runs against the real build with the E41-Q01 fixtures so states that are hard to reach (empty, low-sample, pruned context, reconciling, divergent) are all actually audited - a11y defects hide in exactly the states that are hard to produce.

## Test plan
Structured manual passes with a checklist derived from `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` plus the axe-core CI job; evidence (recordings, screenshots, axe reports) attached to the ticket.

## Security notes
The regression pass is executed as each of Owner, Manager and Viewer, confirming that scoping behaves identically across all four screens and that no role sees data outside its grant - this is the QA-side confirmation of the controls E41-X02 reviews.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility audit; its output is the WCAG 2.2 AA evidence for E41's Definition of Done and a contribution to the E47 conformance epic's evidence base.

## Performance notes
Confirms that the a11y-approved default density is the density the E41-Q02 numbers were measured at, so the two evidence sets describe the same build.

## Observability
Verifies that analytics and audit events fire from the real UI (not just from API tests) for `journal.list_viewed`, `journal.filtered`, `journal.detail_viewed`, `journal.analytics_viewed`, `journal.exported` and the audited mutations.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] axe-core CI green on all four surfaces and all new component stories.
- [ ] NVDA and VoiceOver passes completed with recordings attached.
- [ ] Keyboard-only pass completed for every journey.
- [ ] Contrast and 200% zoom verified in both themes; evidence attached.
- [ ] Colour-independence check evidenced.
- [ ] Epic regression pack added to the R3 suite and green.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment recorded with the disposition of every open defect - this is the gate for E41 Done.

title: Build the journal trade list screen SCR-093
body:
## Context
SCR-093 (`/journal`) is the entry point to the journal area and delivers the visible half of US-JRN-001 (Must), US-JRN-002 (Must), US-JRN-003 (Should) and the list-side of US-JRN-008 (Should). It is a dense, virtualised table over 10 000+ entries where the two non-negotiables are that **demo and live are never aggregated** and that **aggregate statistics come from the server**, never from a client-side scan.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/journal` in `apps/web/src/routes/journal/`, guarded by `journal:read`.
- **Table** built on CMP-049 with virtualisation; columns: open/close time, symbol, side, size, entry, exit, P&L (CMP-116 PnLBadge), R-multiple, fees, account, environment, tags (CMP-169 TagEditor inline), rating. Rows rendered via **CMP-166 JournalEntryRow** (new component: variants Winner, Loser, WithRuleTag, WithManualTags).
- **Filters** via CMP-055 FilterBar + CMP-047 DateRangePicker: date range, symbol, account (multi), environment, tag, outcome - each mapped to the `GET /journal/trades` query parameters (`account_ids`, `symbol`, `side`, `tag[]`, `outcome`, `from`, `to`).
- **Environment separation**: demo and live entries are rendered in visibly separate, individually totalled groups; no combined total is ever rendered across them; the active environment filter is always displayed.
- **Server-side totals row** ("42 trades - win 57% - expectancy +0.34R - P&L +1,204") sourced from `GET /journal/analytics` totals for the active filter, with the designed "recomputing" affordance while it refreshes.
- **Cursor pagination / infinite virtual scroll** over the `Page` envelope with `next_cursor`.
- **Bulk selection and bulk tagging** through the E41-T04 bulk endpoint, reporting the affected-trade count.
- **Row actions**: open detail (E41-S02), open in replay, edit tags, exclude from analytics (audited), set rating.
- **States** per the screen entry: loading, empty ("No trades in this range", tied to recording/trading start with the recorder CTA for the Owner per the catalogue's empty-state convention), partial ("chart context unavailable" for trades predating recording), reconciling (fills still arriving), and the `divergent` flag from E41-T02 surfaced rather than hidden.
- Analytics events `journal.list_viewed`, `journal.filtered`, `journal.exported`; audited actions routed through the API so the audit entry is server-written.

## Out of scope
- Trade detail (E41-S02), analytics dashboard (E41-S03), tag manager modal (E41-S04); the export *job* (E41-T04) - this screen only triggers it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Listing and filtering
  Given 10 000 journal entries exist across two accounts
  When I filter to one account, one symbol and the last 30 days
  Then only matching entries are listed, the filter chips reflect the selection, and the totals row recomputes from the server for that filter

Scenario: Environments are never aggregated
  Given the range contains both demo and live entries
  Then they render as separate groups with separate totals and no combined figure appears anywhere on the screen

Scenario: Bulk tagging
  Given I select 12 entries
  When I apply the tag "absorption"
  Then the server applies it, the UI reports "12 trades updated", and the tag becomes available as a filter

Scenario: Auto tags are distinguishable and protected
  Given an entry carries a rule-sourced auto tag
  Then it renders visually distinct from manual tags and cannot be removed by the inline editor's manual-tag control

Scenario: Empty state
  Given no trades exist in the selected range
  Then the empty state states the fact, its cause, one primary action and a learn-more link, following the CMP-026 anatomy

Scenario: Loading and error
  Given the journal API returns 503
  Then an error state with a retry action is shown, no partial or stale totals are displayed as if current

Scenario: Scoping
  Given I am a Manager granted one account
  Then the account filter offers only that account and no entry outside my grant is listed or countable

Scenario: Density budget
  Given 10 000 rows are loaded
  When I scroll continuously for 5 seconds
  Then scripting time stays at or below 8 ms per frame
```

## Technical notes / design
Build against the signed-off hi-fi and handoff package from E41-D02/E41-D04; every string comes from the approved copy deck, every colour and spacing from tokens. Data fetching uses the shared query client with the cursor envelope; the totals request is a separate, debounced call so a slow aggregate never blocks the row list from painting. Sorting is server-side (it must be, given pagination) - a client-side sort over a partial page would be a lie.

`is_aggregate` rows and leg rows both arrive from the API; the default view shows aggregate rows for trade groups with legs expandable inline, so a fan-out trade reads as one trade by default.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: filter state -> query param mapping; environment grouping logic; totals debounce; auto-tag read-only enforcement; cursor append without duplication.
- **Component/Storybook**: CMP-166 variants; empty, loading, error, partial, reconciling, divergent states; axe on each story.
- **E2E (Playwright, with E41-Q01)**: close a trade on demo -> it appears in the list; filter; bulk tag; open detail; export.
- **Perf**: 10k-row virtualised scroll benchmark asserting <=8 ms scripting per frame.
- **a11y**: axe-core CI on the route; keyboard-only pass (navigate, sort, select, bulk tag, open detail).
- Coverage target >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
The account filter is populated from the user's grant, never from a full account list. All audited actions (`journal.tag_added`, `journal.tag_removed`, `journal.rating_set`, `journal.trade_excluded`) are performed via the API so the audit record is server-authored and cannot be spoofed by the client. Note and tag content rendered here is already sanitised server-side (E41-T04) and is additionally rendered as text, never as HTML.

## Accessibility notes
Table semantics with sortable headers announcing sort state; R and P&L always signed and unit-labelled; bulk-selection count announced via a live region; tag chips reachable and removable by keyboard; the announcement strings are those authored in E41-D04. Virtualisation must not break `aria-rowcount` / `aria-rowindex`.

## Performance notes
10 000 rows scroll without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame; aggregate stats server-side only (SCR-093 performance note); initial route interactive well inside the page budget with the first page of 100 rows.

## Observability
Emits `journal.list_viewed`, `journal.filtered`, `journal.exported`; client error boundary reports to the frontend error channel with `request_id` correlation.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` behind review (2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner), conventional commits, PR <=400 LOC diff.
- [ ] Unit tests added; coverage >=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend on touched packages.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (no undocumented field or status code).
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged (`21-database-schema.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`).
- [ ] Observability (metrics/logs/audit events listed above) shipped and visible on the Grafana journal panel.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on touched surfaces; manual keyboard pass recorded (UI tickets).
- [ ] QA sign-off referenced on E41-Q03; security sign-off on E41-X02 where security-relevant.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review with Owner acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Storybook stories for CMP-166 and for every screen state, with axe checks.
- [ ] Design QA (E41-D05) passed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E41-T01 (list/detail read API), E41-T04 (tags, bulk tagging, export trigger), E41-D04 (design-ahead gate: designs must be Status Done).

## Branch

title: Build the trade detail / post-mortem screen SCR-094 with replay deep-link
body:
## Context
SCR-094 delivers US-JRN-002 (notes/tags on a trade), US-JRN-004 (snapshots), US-JRN-005 (MAE/MFE) and US-JRN-009 (replay-linked post-mortem). It is where a trade is actually understood, and its hardest requirement is honesty about missing data: when retention has pruned the market context, the screen must say so and offer bar-level review, never spin (risk R15).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Page/drawer at `/journal/:journalTradeId` (drawer variant via CMP-046 when opened from SCR-093), guarded by `journal:read`.
- **Header**: symbol, side, size, account, environment, entry/exit price and time, R-multiple, net P&L (CMP-116).
- **Fills timeline** (CMP-049): time, price, qty, fee, fee currency, liquidity (maker/taker), order id, trade group, causing rule if any, and external-action rows marked as external (from E41-T02).
- **Attribution**: for every action taken on the trade, whether it was manual, an algo, or a named rule (with version).
- **MAE/MFE** shown in price, USDT and R with the timestamp of each extreme, and the `bar-derived` marker when applicable; described in text as well as drawn.
- **Fees and funding** broken out; `fee_estimated` entries flagged per the paper-matcher rule.
- **Trade-group siblings** row ("group Scalp x3: Main +65.0 | sub_001 +26.0 | sub_002 -3.0"); a leg outside the viewer's grant renders as an explicit "not in your scope" row rather than being omitted.
- **Context chart** fed by `GET /journal/trades/{journalTradeId}/context` (bars + footprint + own fills, `pad_seconds` default 900), honouring the returned `coverage` descriptor; entry/exit markers and the SL path drawn; a **table alternative** for the chart.
- **"Context not recorded" state** when coverage is absent: names what is missing, why (retention), and offers bar-level review if bars remain.
- **Snapshots** (US-JRN-004) displayed when present; when capture failed, the reason is shown rather than a broken image.
- **Notes and tags** editing via CMP-058 InlineEdit and CMP-169 TagEditor against the E41-T04 endpoints, with edit history visible.
- **"Open in replay"** (US-JRN-009) deep-linking into E26's replay at `replay_anchor_ts` (entry minus the configured lead) with the user's executions marked; when the recorded data is pruned, the action explains what is unavailable and offers bar-level replay if bars remain. Notes added during a replay review attach to the same journal entry.
- **"Open chart at entry"** and **export** (CMP-099 PrintExportBar).
- Analytics/audit events: `journal.detail_viewed`, `journal.note_added` (audited server-side), `journal.screenshot_exported`, `journal.replay_from_trade`.

## Out of scope
- The replay engine and its screens (E26); the snapshot capture pipeline (E41-T02); analytics aggregates (E41-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Full post-mortem renders
  Given a closed trade with five fills across two orders managed by a rule
  When I open its detail
  Then all five fills, their fees and liquidity flags, the managing rule name and version, MAE/MFE in price, USDT and R, and the context chart render within 1.5 s

Scenario: Context pruned
  Given the recorded tick data covering the trade has been deleted by retention
  Then the "context not recorded" state is shown naming what is missing, bar-level review is offered if bars remain, and no indefinite spinner appears

Scenario: Replay jump
  When I choose "replay this trade"
  Then replay opens at entry minus the configured lead time with my executions marked
  And notes I add during that review attach to this same journal entry

Scenario: Replay unavailable
  Given the recorded data for the trade has been pruned
  When I choose "replay this trade"
  Then the action explains precisely what is unavailable and offers bar-level replay if bars remain, instead of failing silently

Scenario: Out-of-scope sibling leg
  Given the trade group includes a leg on an account I am not granted
  Then that leg is shown as "not in your scope" and the group total states that it is partial

Scenario: Snapshot capture failed
  Given snapshot capture failed at entry
  Then the screen states the failure reason and the rest of the post-mortem renders normally

Scenario: Bar-derived excursions
  Given MAE/MFE were computed from bar extremes
  Then both values carry the bar-derived marker in text, not only as an icon
```

## Technical notes / design
One request paints the context (`/context` returns bars, footprint and fills together, explicitly so the review chart does not issue a burst of market-data requests). The chart is the lightweight primitive, not the full WebGL engine. The `coverage` descriptor drives the partial/absent states - never infer coverage from a short series, which would silently misrepresent a gap as an early start.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: coverage descriptor -> state mapping (full / partial / absent); MAE/MFE unit conversion; sibling-leg scoping; replay anchor computation.
- **Component/Storybook**: full, partial-coverage, no-coverage, snapshot-failed, bar-derived, out-of-scope-sibling, fee-estimated states; axe on each.
- **E2E**: open from SCR-093, add a note, add a tag, jump to replay, return; pruned-context path with a fixture whose recording was deleted.
- **a11y**: keyboard pass incl. drawer focus trap and return focus; screen-reader pass asserting the MAE/MFE and SL-path text descriptions and the chart table alternative.
- Coverage target >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Enforces nothing itself - scoping is server-side - but must not leak the existence of out-of-scope data beyond the agreed "not in your scope" row (a deliberate, reviewed disclosure so group totals are not silently wrong; recorded in E41-X01's model). Note content is rendered as sanitised text; snapshots are fetched through the authenticated API, never from a public URL.

## Accessibility notes
MAE/MFE and the SL path described in text; the mini chart has a table alternative; drawer focus management per E41-D04; all numeric values signed and unit-labelled; the timeline is a semantic table.

## Performance notes
Context window renders <=1.5 s or falls back to the "context not recorded" state rather than a spinner (SCR-094 performance note).

## Observability
`journal.detail_viewed`, `journal.replay_from_trade`, `journal.screenshot_exported`; client-side timing of the context render reported for the 1.5 s budget.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` behind review (2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner), conventional commits, PR <=400 LOC diff.
- [ ] Unit tests added; coverage >=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend on touched packages.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (no undocumented field or status code).
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged (`21-database-schema.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`).
- [ ] Observability (metrics/logs/audit events listed above) shipped and visible on the Grafana journal panel.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on touched surfaces; manual keyboard pass recorded (UI tickets).
- [ ] QA sign-off referenced on E41-Q03; security sign-off on E41-X02 where security-relevant.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review with Owner acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Storybook covers every declared state; design QA (E41-D05) passed.

## Dependencies

title: Build the journal analytics dashboard SCR-095
body:
## Context
SCR-095 (`/journal/analytics`) delivers US-JRN-006 (Must), US-JRN-007 (Should), US-JRN-008 (Should) and the export entry point for US-JRN-010 (Could). Its defining constraint is epistemic: every number must be honest about its sample. A confident expectancy over 12 trades is the epic's main way of doing harm (risk R12), so the low-sample and low-confidence treatments are acceptance criteria, not polish.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route `/journal/analytics` guarded by `journal:read`, fed entirely by `GET /journal/analytics` - **no client-side aggregation of the trade set**.
- **Summary tiles** via **CMP-168 JournalStatsSummaryCard** (new): win rate, expectancy in R, average R, profit factor, average hold time, max drawdown (depth and duration), current and best streaks, trade count.
- **Equity curve** via **CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart** (new) with drawdown overlay, maximum drawdown marked and its depth and duration labelled, balance-transfer markers shown and excluded from performance, and a `TableViewToggle` rendering the same points through CMP-049.
- **R-distribution histogram** with the documented bucket edges from E41-T05.
- **MAE/MFE scatter** for stop-quality review, outcome encoded by **shape as well as colour**, filterable by tag, with `bar-derived` points flagged.
- **Breakdown tables**: by symbol, tag, hour of day, day of week, side, account and setup/rule-source - each with count alongside P&L, sortable by any column, buckets with fewer than 5 trades visually **and textually** marked low-confidence.
- **Cohort controls**: date range (CMP-047), account multi-select, symbol, tag, and the environment toggle - **DEMO excluded by default** with an explicit toggle, and the active environment filter always displayed.
- **Low-sample treatment**: when fewer than 20 trades match, every headline statistic carries the caveat attached to the number, not only a page banner.
- **"How these are calculated"** link opening the reference authored in E41-T05.
- **Export** (CMP-099 PrintExportBar) triggering the E41-T04 job, with the async path above 50 000 rows showing a "we'll notify you" state.
- **States**: loading, empty, insufficient sample.
- Analytics events `journal.analytics_viewed`, `journal.analytics_filtered`, `journal.analytics_exported`, `journal.cohort_changed`.

## Out of scope
- Computing any statistic client-side; the formula reference content (E41-T05); trade list and detail (E41-S01/S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dashboard renders within budget
  Given 10 000 journal entries match the filter
  When I open /journal/analytics
  Then the page is interactive within 800 ms and every statistic came from the server

Scenario: Demo excluded by default
  Given both live and demo entries exist
  When the page loads
  Then demo entries are excluded, the environment toggle shows this, and enabling demo renders it as a separate population rather than merging it into the live figures

Scenario: Low sample
  Given 12 trades match
  Then each headline statistic displays with the low-sample caveat attached to it, and the page does not present the figures as conclusive

Scenario: Low-confidence bucket
  Given the "hour 03" bucket contains 4 trades
  Then that row is marked low-confidence in text as well as visually

Scenario: Table alternative
  Given any chart on the page
  When I activate "View as table" using only the keyboard
  Then the same data renders as an accessible table with a text summary such as "Expectancy +0.34R over 42 trades"

Scenario: Transfers annotated not counted
  Given a balance transfer occurred in the range
  Then it is marked on the equity curve and none of the performance statistics change because of it

Scenario: Large export
  Given 60 000 rows match and I export
  Then the UI states the export is being prepared and that I will be notified, rather than appearing to hang
```

## Technical notes / design
One request per cohort change, debounced, with the `group_by[]` set matching the visible breakdowns so the server does not materialise breakdowns nobody is looking at. The response carries counts alongside percentages precisely so the text summaries need no client-side maths. Charts are the lightweight primitives (CMP-167 may reuse the series primitive CMP-181 in a minimal pane), not the WebGL engine.

Each chart's table alternative renders the identical data array the chart consumed - not a re-fetch and not a rounded copy - so the two can never disagree.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: cohort state -> query params; low-sample and low-confidence threshold rendering at exactly 20 and exactly 5; transfer markers excluded from displayed totals; table-alternative data identity with the chart's series.
- **Component/Storybook**: CMP-167 (Default, WithDrawdown, TableViewToggle) and CMP-168 (Default); empty, loading, insufficient-sample states; axe on each.
- **E2E**: filter by tag and account, toggle demo, switch every chart to its table, export.
- **Perf**: 10k-entry fixture, time-to-interactive asserted <=800 ms (E41-Q02).
- **a11y**: axe-core; colour-blind simulation on the scatter and histogram; screen-reader pass on the text summaries.
- Coverage target >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Account breakdowns show only granted accounts; the export button respects the same scope and the server re-enforces it (SR-098). No statistic may be computed from a client-side cache that predates a scope change - the query key includes the scope so a grant revocation invalidates it.

## Accessibility notes
Every chart has a table alternative and a text summary; colour never the sole encoding (scatter uses shape by outcome); small buckets marked in text; headline numbers signed and unit-labelled; charts have accessible names and descriptions.

## Performance notes
Interactive <=800 ms for 10 000 trades; breakdown query <=2 s (US-JRN-008 NFR); no client-side scan of the trade set at any point.

## Observability
`journal.analytics_viewed`, `journal.analytics_filtered`, `journal.analytics_exported`, `journal.cohort_changed`; client timing reported against the 800 ms budget.

## Definition of Done

title: Build the journal tag manager SCR-096 and the export flow UI
body:
## Context
SCR-096 is the tag taxonomy's only editing surface (US-JRN-002 Must, US-JRN-003 Should) and the place where destructive operations - merge and delete - are confirmed against a stated affected-trade count. This story also ships the user-facing export flow for US-JRN-010 (Could), whose disclosure risk (R13, threat S4) is why the confirmation copy must state exactly what leaves the system.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Tag manager modal** (CMP-043 Dialog) reachable from SCR-093 and SCR-095: a table (CMP-049) of tags with name, colour, category, usage count and description.
- **Create / rename / merge / delete** flows against the E41-T04 endpoints, with CMP-058 InlineEdit for rename and CMP-044 ConfirmDialog for destructive operations.
- **Validation**: unique names (case-insensitive), <=24 characters per the screen's validation rule; category from `setup | mistake | emotion | session | general` matching `journal_tags.category`.
- **Merge/delete confirmation** restating the exact number of affected trades before the operation and reporting the result after; operations are server-side with progress, never a client-side loop.
- **Colour picker** whose output is validated for contrast in both themes, with colour always paired with the tag's text label.
- **Auto-tag rules** display: tags carrying an `auto_rule` predicate are shown as such and their provenance explained; auto-applied tags on trades are read-only in the manual editor.
- **Empty state** (CMP-026).
- **Export flow UI**: format choice (CSV / Parquet), a summary of exactly what will be exported (row count, date range, accounts in scope, columns), the watermark notice ("this file is watermarked with your identity and the export time and the export is recorded in the audit log"), the synchronous download path, and the asynchronous path above 50 000 rows with a "we'll notify you when it's ready" state and a link to the notification centre.
- Analytics/audit events `journal.tag_created`, `journal.tag_renamed`, `journal.tag_merged`, `journal.tag_deleted` (with `affectedTrades`), `journal.exported` - all server-written.

## Out of scope
- The tag/merge/export server logic (E41-T04); the notification channel (E40); the analytics dashboard (E41-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create and rename
  When I create a tag "absorption" in category setup and later rename it to "absorption-reclaim"
  Then both operations succeed, the usage count is preserved, and the rename is reported as a single server-side operation

Scenario: Duplicate name
  When I create a tag whose name differs only by case from an existing one
  Then the form rejects it with a clear message and no request creates a duplicate

Scenario: Merge confirmation
  Given a tag applied to 5 000 trades
  When I merge it into another
  Then the confirmation states "5,000 trades will be affected", the operation runs server-side with progress, and the result restates the count

Scenario: Delete confirmation
  When I delete a tag used by 120 trades
  Then the confirmation restates that 120 trades lose the tag, and cancelling changes nothing

Scenario: Auto tags are protected
  Given a tag is applied automatically by a rule
  Then it is shown as auto with its provenance and cannot be removed through the manual tag control

Scenario: Export discloses its scope
  When I open the export flow as a Manager granted one account
  Then the summary names that account only, states the row count and date range, and states that the file is watermarked and audited

Scenario: Large export
  Given 60 000 rows match
  Then the flow switches to the asynchronous path, states that I will be notified, and does not block the UI

Scenario: Colour contrast
  When I pick any offered tag colour
  Then the paired label meets 4.5:1 in both themes and the picker rejects or warns on any value that does not
```

## Technical notes / design
The modal is a focus-trapped dialog with return focus to its invoker. The affected-trade count shown in a confirmation is fetched immediately before the confirmation renders (not cached from the list) so the number a user confirms against is current. Export summary figures come from the same filter the user is currently viewing, so "what will be exported" and "what I can see" are provably the same set.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: name validation incl. case-insensitive collision and the 24-char limit; confirmation copy interpolation with thousands separators; export threshold branching at exactly 50 000; auto-tag read-only enforcement.
- **Component/Storybook**: tag table populated and empty; merge/delete confirmations; colour picker in both themes; export flow sync and async variants; axe on each.
- **E2E**: create, rename, merge, delete a tag end to end; export as Owner and as Manager verifying scope copy; async export notification.
- **a11y**: keyboard-only pass through the modal and the export flow; focus trap and return focus; screen-reader announcement of the affected-trade count.
- Coverage target >=80% frontend.

## Security notes
Directly user-facing mitigation for threat **S4** / control **SR-098**: the export flow must state the scope, the watermark and the audit before the user confirms. The UI never constructs the export itself and never widens the filter beyond what the server will honour. Tag names are user input rendered as text, never as HTML.

## Accessibility notes
Tag list is a table with name, colour, usage count and description; colour is always paired with the tag's text label; merge/rename dialogs restate the affected trade count in text; modal focus trap and return focus; all controls keyboard reachable.

## Performance notes
Tag operations are server-side; renaming a tag used by 5 000 trades completes as a single transaction with progress rather than a client-side loop (SCR-096 performance note).

## Observability
Client emits `journal.exported` analytics; all tag mutations are audited server-side with `affectedTrades`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Code merged to `main` behind review (2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner), conventional commits, PR <=400 LOC diff.
- [ ] Unit tests added; coverage >=85% backend/engine, >=80% frontend on touched packages.
- [ ] Contract tests green against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (no undocumented field or status code).
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged (`21-database-schema.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `14-screens-catalogue.md`).
- [ ] Observability (metrics/logs/audit events listed above) shipped and visible on the Grafana journal panel.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on touched surfaces; manual keyboard pass recorded (UI tickets).
- [ ] QA sign-off referenced on E41-Q03; security sign-off on E41-X02 where security-relevant.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review with Owner acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Storybook covers the tag table, both confirmations and both export paths; design QA (E41-D05) passed.

## Dependencies

title: Author the journal statistics formula reference and ADR-0016 follow-up
body:
## Context
US-JRN-006's NFR is explicit: *"all statistics are defined in a documented formula reference available from the UI"*. This is not documentation hygiene - it is the control that keeps risk R12 in check. A win rate whose denominator is undefined, or an expectancy that silently treats stopless trades as 0R, is a number that misleads its only reader. This ticket authors that reference and links it from SCR-095.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `docs/plan/25-journal-statistics-reference.md` (new) documenting, for every statistic returned by `GET /journal/analytics`: the plain-English definition, the exact formula, the population (which entries are included and which excluded and why), the units, the edge cases, and a worked example against the shipped `journal_fixture_100` fixture.
- Statistics covered: trade count, win / loss / breakeven counts, win rate, average win, average loss, expectancy in R, profit factor, average R, average hold time, max drawdown (depth absolute and %, duration), streaks, R-distribution bucket edges, MAE, MFE (price, USDT, R; and what `bar-derived` means), equity curve construction and the treatment of balance transfers.
- Explicit statements of the three decisions that most affect interpretation: (1) entries with no planned stop are excluded from R statistics and the exclusion count is reported; (2) profit factor with zero losses is `null`, not infinity; (3) environments are never aggregated.
- The **CSV export column dictionary** for US-JRN-010 ("documented column semantics"), in the same document so an exported file is interpretable standalone.
- The low-sample and low-confidence thresholds (20 trades; 5 per bucket) stated with their rationale.
- A UI entry point: the reference is reachable from SCR-095 (a "How these are calculated" link), specified with E41-D03's statistics legend.
- Update `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0029-journal-analytics-query-tier.md` with the as-built outcome if implementation diverged from the spike's recommendation.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the statistics (E41-T03); rendering the legend (E41-S03); backtesting metrics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every returned statistic is documented
  When the JournalAnalytics response schema is enumerated
  Then every numeric field in it has an entry in docs/plan/25-journal-statistics-reference.md with formula, population, units and edge cases

Scenario: Worked example matches the implementation
  When the worked example is recomputed against journal_fixture_100 by the test suite
  Then every documented value matches the endpoint's output exactly, and the test fails if either drifts

Scenario: Export is self-describing
  Given a CSV export and the reference document
  Then every column is defined, including units, sign convention and null semantics
```

## Technical notes / design
The worked example is executable: a test reads the markdown tables, calls the endpoint against the fixture and asserts equality, so the document cannot silently rot. This is cheap and it is the only way a formula reference stays true past its first sprint.

## Test plan
The doc-vs-implementation test described above, run in CI with the backend suite. No other automated testing applies.

## Security notes
The reference must not include real account identifiers or balances in examples - the fixture is synthetic. Documenting export column semantics is also a security artefact: it makes it obvious if a column that should not be exported ever appears (SR-098).

## Accessibility notes
The document is rendered in-app; it must use semantic headings and real tables (not ASCII art) so it is navigable by a screen reader, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/plan/25-journal-statistics-reference.md` merged.
- [ ] Doc-vs-implementation test green in CI.
- [ ] Link from SCR-095 specified and implemented in E41-S03.
- [ ] ADR-0016 reconciled with the as-built implementation.
- [ ] Reviewed by the Owner (the reference is written for the reader who will act on these numbers).

`blocked_by` E41-T03 (the formulas must be implemented before they can be documented as-built).

title: Security review of journal writes, scoping and export controls
body:
## Context
E41-X01 modelled the threats; this ticket verifies the built system against them. It is the security gate for the epic and a prerequisite for the QA sign-off in E41-Q03. The focus is the three places where the journal can actually do harm: **export** (threat S4, control SR-098, risk R13), **scoping** (horizontal escalation between managers), and **integrity of evidence** (objective O8 - computed fields immutable, writes audited, notes versioned).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box review** of `services/api/journal/` against the threat model: every repository query inspected for the account-scope predicate; the PATCH field allowlist; the note sanitiser and its allowlist; the auto-tag provenance and suppression logic; the export scoping, watermarking and audit path; the analytics cache key.
- **Executed abuse cases** 1-7 from E41-X01, each with recorded evidence (request, response, log/audit entry).
- **Authorisation testing** per `04-security-program.md` section 10: horizontal (Manager A -> Manager B), vertical (Manager -> Owner), IDOR on `journalTradeId` and on note ids, across every journal route and both UI and API entry points; grant-revocation timing against cached analytics and in-flight exports.
- **Export verification**: automated assertion that no export in any format contains an API key, key identifier, credential or exchange account secret; watermark present and correct in both CSV and Parquet; audit entry written with the applied filters and scope; the 50 000-row async threshold enforced server-side and not bypassable by a crafted request.
- **Injection testing**: stored XSS via note markdown, tag names and setup/mistake text, verified both at storage and at render; SQL injection attempts on the filter and `group_by` parameters.
- **DAST**: the ZAP profile from E41-X01 run against `/journal/*` with findings triaged.
- **SAST**: CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit results for the journal module reviewed with zero unresolved high findings.
- **Sign-off**: a written security review comment stating pass, pass-with-conditions, or fail, with every finding either fixed or recorded as an accepted risk with Owner sign-off.

## Out of scope
- The external pen-test (E43, R4); rewriting controls (defects are filed against the owning ticket); infrastructure hardening.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: No export leaks scope
  Given a Manager granted exactly one account
  When they export via the UI and again via a directly crafted API request widening account_ids
  Then both exports contain only that account's trades and the widened request is rejected server-side

Scenario: Exports contain no secrets
  When exports are produced in CSV and Parquet across every filter combination under test
  Then an automated scan finds no API key, key identifier, credential or account secret in any output

Scenario: Evidence is tamper-evident
  When an attempt is made to modify realised_pnl or r_multiple via the API
  Then it is rejected with 422, the stored value is unchanged, and the attempt is logged

Scenario: Note history survives deletion attempts
  When a note is edited to remove incriminating content
  Then the prior revision is retained and the edit is audited

Scenario: Stored XSS blocked
  When a note, tag name or setup field containing script payloads is stored and later rendered in the Owner's session
  Then no script executes, at storage or at render

Scenario: Grant revocation
  Given a Manager's account grant is revoked
  When a previously cached analytics response for that scope is requested
  Then it is not served, and any in-flight export for that scope is cancelled or completes containing only still-authorised data

Scenario: Gate
  Given any unresolved high or critical finding
  Then security sign-off is withheld and E41-Q03 cannot complete
```

## Technical notes / design
Review the analytics cache key explicitly: scope-blind caching is the single most likely way this epic's RBAC gets defeated, and it is invisible in a functional test because every individual request looks correct. Likewise verify the ADR-0016 query path - if analytics reads Parquet directly, confirm the scope predicate is applied in that path too rather than only in the Postgres path.

## Test plan
Abuse cases executed manually with evidence; automated assertions (secret-scan on exports, Semgrep scope-predicate rule) wired into CI so the controls cannot silently regress after this review; ZAP scan automated in the security pipeline.

## Security notes
This is the security review. Findings are rated per `04-security-program.md`; high and critical findings block the R3 gate. Evidence is stored in the security evidence pack for the R3 PRR and the R4 pen-test's scoping input.

## Accessibility notes
N/A, except that the export confirmation copy asserting scope, watermark and audit must be verified as *present and accurate* - a control the user cannot perceive is not a control.

## Performance notes
Verifies the DoS bounds from E41-X01: the analytics range cap, the export async threshold, and that the snapshot queue cannot back-pressure the execution stream.

## Observability
Confirms `journal_authz_denied_total` increments on every denial and that export and mutation audit entries are complete, correct and append-only.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] White-box review completed with notes on every element in Scope.
- [ ] All seven abuse cases executed with evidence attached.
- [ ] Authorisation, injection, DAST and SAST results triaged; zero unresolved high or critical findings.
- [ ] Export secret-scan and Semgrep scope rule running in CI.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment recorded (gates E41-Q03 and E41 Done).
- [ ] Evidence filed in the R3 PRR security pack.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E41-X01 (the model defines what to verify), E41-T04 (writes, tags, notes, export must be built), E41-S04 (the export flow UI and its disclosure copy).

## Branch
`chore/journal-security-review`

title: Design QA the built admin screens against spec and sign off
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA a Done gate for net-new UI: "built screen compared against design spec (spacing/tokens/type/color/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer; discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bug with `priority/*` set."

The admin area is fifteen screens built by several engineers across two sprints from one shared pattern set. Drift is the expected failure mode — not gross deviation, but fifteen slightly different paddings, three variants of the same empty state, and a destructive dialog that quietly dropped its typed confirmation. This ticket catches that before the epic closes and before E43's security hardening builds on top of it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Screen-by-screen comparison of the built implementation against the signed-off hi-fi for: CMP-087 shell, SCR-149, SCR-120, SCR-121, SCR-122, SCR-123, SCR-124, SCR-135, SCR-136, SCR-143, SCR-144, SCR-145, SCR-146, SCR-148, SCR-154, the onboarding wizard and the SCR-062 governance controls.
- Per screen: spacing, type scale, token usage (no hard-coded colours), component fidelity to `15-component-catalogue.md`, and **every state** — not just the populated one. Empty, loading, filtered-to-nothing, error, degraded and destructive-confirmation states are where drift hides.
- **Pattern-conformance audit** against the E42-D06 pattern sheet: is every destructive action on the correct rung of the ladder? Is the degraded/stale expression identical across SCR-120, SCR-143 and SCR-144? Does every state-changing control announce that it will be recorded?
- **Copy audit** against the copy deck: every string matches, including error and empty-state copy; no engineer-authored placeholder survives.
- Motion conformance: durations, easings and reduced-motion behaviour match the motion spec.
- Cross-screen consistency sweep at both breakpoints (1280×800, 2560×1440) and in both themes if the admin area supports them.
- Discrepancy log with a disposition for each: fixed in-sprint, or filed as a Bug with `priority/*` and an owner. Nothing is left as "noted".

## Out of scope
- Functional testing (E42-Q02) and accessibility auditing (E42-Q05) — separate tickets with separate skills; this is visual and pattern conformance.
- Screens owned by other epics, even though they render inside the admin shell (E16, E27, E28, E39, E43) — each has its own design QA.
- Redesign. Findings that are design changes rather than implementation drift are filed as new design tickets, not smuggled in here.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every listed screen reviewed in every catalogue-listed state, with evidence (screenshots) attached.
- The pattern-conformance audit produces an explicit pass/fail per pattern, with every failure dispositioned.
- The copy audit confirms 100% match with the copy deck, or files the differences.
- Discrepancy log complete: each entry is fixed, or filed as a Bug with a priority and an owner; none are undispositioned.
- Design sign-off comment recorded on this ticket and on the epic — this is the design gate the epic's DoD requires.

## Technical notes / design
- Reviewed against a staging (demo) build at a pinned commit SHA, recorded on the ticket, so "fixed later" claims are verifiable.
- Token conformance is checked with the design-system linting where available, and by inspection where not — a hard-coded hex in the admin area is a finding, even if it matches the token's current value.

## Test plan
- Visual-regression snapshots for the admin screens are added or refreshed as part of the fixes, so the same drift cannot recur silently.
- Findings that indicate a missing test (a state nobody ever rendered) are cross-filed to E42-Q02.

## Security notes
- Security-relevant visual checks are part of the pass, not an afterthought: the impersonation banner is present and unmissable; the audit screens still contain no mutation affordance; `trading.live_enabled` still renders blocked; no screen displays a secret; typed confirmations were not downgraded to plain confirms during implementation.

## Accessibility notes
- Visual a11y conformance only (contrast, focus-visible treatment, text-not-colour status); the full audit is E42-Q05.
- Any contrast regression introduced during implementation is a finding here, with the measured value recorded.

## Performance notes
Findings that reveal a perf-driven design compromise (for example, a tile that was made page-blocking to simplify the code) are escalated rather than accepted, since SCR-120 and SCR-143 have explicit independence requirements.

## Observability
Confirms that the audit/analytics events named in the handoff pack are actually emitted by the built controls, by inspecting the events in the staging build.

title: Automate the admin E2E suite including cross-session and timing assertions
body:
## Context
The admin stories make promises that only a multi-context E2E test can verify: a manager's session dies within 5 s of being disabled; a flag change reaches every client within 10 s; a revoked grant force-closes a live subscription. Unit tests cannot see these, and manual testing cannot re-run them every sprint.

`03-testing-strategy.md` puts Playwright (web + Electron) at the top of the pyramid for exactly this. This ticket builds the admin suite from the plan written in E42-Q01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `tests/e2e/admin/`: `admin-shell.spec.ts`, `admin-users.spec.ts`, `admin-user-detail.spec.ts`, `admin-audit.spec.ts`, `admin-flags.spec.ts`, `admin-health.spec.ts`, `admin-backups.spec.ts`, `admin-onboarding.spec.ts`.
- **Cross-session harness**: a reusable helper that opens an owner context and a manager context against the same backend, so the effect of an owner action on a manager's live session is directly assertable. This is the piece the suite is worth building for.
- Timing assertions with the budgets from the stories: session revocation ≤5 s, flag propagation ≤10 s, maintenance broadcast ≤2 s, order blocking ≤200 ms (asserted via the API response, not the UI).
- Negative-path specs: manager hard-404 on every `/admin/*` route (parameterised over the full route list, so a newly added admin route without a guard fails the suite); stale-token deep link; 412 conflict on concurrent edit; export range rejection.
- Fixture wiring from E42-Q01, with per-spec seeding and teardown so specs are order-independent.
- CI integration: the suite runs on PRs touching `apps/web/src/features/admin` or `services/admin`, and nightly in full; flaky specs are quarantined with an owner rather than retried into green.
- Contract-test additions: schemathesis/Dredd runs over the `/admin/*` and `/users*` paths added by this epic.

## Out of scope
- Perf, load and chaos scenarios (E42-Q03).
- Accessibility audit (E42-Q05).
- Security abuse cases (E42-X03) — the RBAC assertion suite lives there; this suite asserts the user-visible half.
- Unit and component tests, which ship with their stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The suite proves cross-session effects
  Given an owner context and a manager context are both signed in
  When the owner disables the manager
  Then the manager's next request fails within 5 seconds
  And the assertion is on the observed time, not a fixed sleep

Scenario: Every admin route is guarded
  Given the suite enumerates the admin route list from the router
  When each route is visited by a manager
  Then every one renders the 404 surface
  And adding a new admin route without a guard fails this spec

Scenario: The suite is deterministic
  When the full admin suite runs 10 times in CI
  Then it passes 10 times with no retries
  And any spec that does not is quarantined with an owner and a ticket
```
- All specs listed in Scope exist and pass against staging (demo).
- Contract tests cover every `/admin/*` and `/users*` path added by this epic.
- CI wiring merged; the suite's runtime is under 10 minutes on the standard runner, or it is sharded.
- Traceability table posted mapping each E42-Q01 case to its automated spec (or to "manual, by design" with a reason).

## Technical notes / design
- No fixed `sleep`: timing assertions poll with a deadline and report the observed duration, so a passing test still tells you how close to the budget you are.
- The route list for the guard spec is imported from the application's router definition rather than hard-coded, which is what makes the "new route without a guard" case fail automatically.
- Each spec seeds its own data with a unique prefix and tears it down, so specs can run in parallel shards.
- The step-up gate is handled by a helper that performs a real TOTP computation against the seeded secret — never by disabling the gate for tests, which would make the suite prove nothing about the guard.

## Test plan
- The suite is its own deliverable; its quality bar is the determinism criterion above.
- Meta-test: a deliberately unguarded route added in a scratch branch must fail the guard spec — verified once and recorded, so the spec's value is demonstrated rather than assumed.

## Security notes
- Test credentials are seeded, obviously synthetic, and scoped to the test environment; the suite must never run against production (a guard asserts the target base URL is not the production host).
- The TOTP secret used in tests is generated per run, not committed.
- Specs that attempt privilege escalation belong to E42-X03; this suite asserts the legitimate paths and the visible denials.

## Accessibility notes
- Each spec includes an axe-core scan of the screens it visits, so an a11y regression fails the functional suite rather than waiting for the audit.
- The keyboard paths from E42-D06 are automated here as keyboard-only specs for the highest-risk flows (elevate, delete a user, run a restore).

## Performance notes
- The suite records the observed timings for the budgeted assertions and publishes them as CI artefacts, giving a trend rather than a pass/fail snapshot.

## Observability
- Specs assert the expected audit entries exist after each action, querying `GET /admin/audit` — so the suite verifies accountability, not just behaviour.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `tests/` (or `docs/qa/` for plans) and runnable in CI.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario in the covered stories mapped to at least one executed case; traceability table posted on the ticket.
- [ ] Defects filed with repro steps, environment and `priority/*`; P0/P1 defects closed or explicitly accepted before sign-off.
- [ ] Results (pass/fail per scenario, environment, build SHA) posted as the QA sign-off comment.
- [ ] Flaky tests quarantined with an owner and a follow-up ticket rather than silently retried.

title: Run admin performance, load and chaos scenarios including degraded rendering
body:
## Context
Three of this epic's requirements are performance claims that will be believed unless measured: the audit log's **≤2 s first page over 10 million entries** (US-ADMIN-009), the health screen's **≤1 % added load** (US-ADMIN-011), and SCR-120's **≤800 ms render that never blocks on the slowest subsystem**.

One is a resilience claim: SCR-143 "must itself remain responsive when the system it is reporting on is degraded (all tiles resolve independently, no tile can block another)". That is precisely the property that quietly breaks during implementation, and precisely the moment it matters.

`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and `03-testing-strategy.md` require chaos/failover testing (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) as a first-class layer, not an afterthought.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Audit query performance**: k6 profile against the 10 M-row dataset measuring first-page latency for each filter combination the UI offers, at page 1 and at deep cursor positions; assert ≤2 s worst case and ≤400 ms for the common combinations; publish the distribution, not just the pass/fail.
- **Export under load**: concurrent export jobs plus interactive queries — the interactive path must not degrade beyond its budget while an export streams.
- **Overview and health render**: measure SCR-120's end-to-end render with all subsystems healthy and with one subsystem timing out; assert ≤800 ms in both cases and that the slow tile does not delay the others.
- **Added-load measurement**: quantify the health screen's server-side cost with the screen open versus closed, against the ≤1 % NFR, at the expected session count.
- **Chaos scenarios**:
  1. Health endpoint returns 503 while the `system` topic stays up → tiles render stale with timestamps; shell usable.
  2. WS disconnects mid-session on an admin screen → reconnect, resubscribe, no duplicated or lost incident rows.
  3. Postgres becomes slow (injected latency) → admin screens degrade with explicit stale markers rather than hanging.
  4. Audit chain break injected → the critical banner appears, the alert fires, and the screen offers no misleading retry.
  5. Backup verification fails → the age warning appears with the correct last-verified time.
  6. Flag store unreachable → flags resolve to defaults and the console says so, rather than showing stale values as current.
- Results recorded against budgets in a report under `docs/qa/` and fed into the epic's PRR evidence.

## Out of scope
- Trading-path load testing (E29/E34/E46) — different surfaces, different budgets.
- Fixing the defects found; those are filed as Bugs against the owning story.
- The chaos framework itself, if one exists from E45 — reused, not rebuilt.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Audit first page at scale
  Given 10 million audit entries
  When the first page is requested with each of the UI's filter combinations
  Then every combination returns within 2 seconds p95
  And the common combinations return within 400 ms p95
  And the full distribution is published

Scenario: One slow subsystem does not block the overview
  Given the recorder subsystem does not respond
  When the admin overview is opened
  Then it renders within 800 ms with the recorder tile in its error state
  And every other tile shows its value

Scenario: The health screen survives the outage it reports
  Given the health endpoint returns 503
  Then every tile shows its last-known value marked stale with a timestamp
  And the shell and navigation remain usable
  And no tile shows a plausible but stale number as if it were current

Scenario (failure): Chain break is unmistakable
  Given an injected audit chain break
  Then the critical banner names the break position
  And the cv_audit_chain_verified alert fires
  And no retry control implies the failure is transient

Scenario (edge): Flag store unreachable
  Then flags resolve to their defaults, safety-relevant defaults being the restrictive ones
  And the console states that values are defaults, not current
```
- All six chaos scenarios executed with results recorded; each either passes or has a filed Bug with a priority.
- Budget table published with measured values beside the required values.

## Technical notes / design
- Latency injection via a proxy/toxiproxy-style layer rather than code changes, so the system under test is the shipped build.
- The chain-break injection operates on a disposable test database only, with the loader refusing any non-test target.
- Measurements use server-side timings plus client RUM (`cv_admin_overview_render_ms`), so a fast server with a slow client is not mistaken for success.
- The ≤1 % added-load figure is measured as the delta in server CPU/request rate with N admin screens open versus none, at the expected session count — stated as a method, because the NFR is otherwise unfalsifiable.

## Test plan
- This ticket *is* the test execution; its own quality bar is reproducibility: a reviewer must be able to re-run `make admin-perf` and `make admin-chaos` and obtain the same conclusions.

## Security notes
- Chaos scenarios must not be runnable against production; the harness asserts its target environment.
- The injected chain break is a security-sensitive test artefact: its presence in any non-test environment would itself be an incident, so the fixture is clearly marked and the loader is guarded.
- Load testing the export endpoint doubles as a check that the export rate limit and range limit actually bound exfiltration.

## Accessibility notes
- The degraded and stale states exercised here are also a11y states: the audit confirms their announcements behave correctly under repeated transitions (no announcement storms when a subsystem flaps).

## Performance notes
- Budgets under test, all sourced from the plan docs: ≤2 s audit first page at 10 M rows and ≤400 ms common filter round-trip; SCR-120 ≤800 ms with and without a slow subsystem; SCR-136 ≤300 ms; SCR-143 ≤1 % added load and ≤2 ms scripting per frame; SCR-144 10k rows without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame.

## Observability
- Verifies the alerting path end-to-end, not just the metric: `cv_audit_chain_verified == 0` must actually page, and `cv_backup_last_success_age_seconds` must fire at the configured threshold. A metric that exists but never alerts is a false sense of security.

title: Run exploratory charters and assemble the E42 regression pack with QA sign-off
body:
## Context
Scripted tests find what was anticipated. The admin area's most expensive failures would be the unanticipated ones: a path that leaks scope, a confirmation that can be bypassed by a keyboard shortcut, a form that loses twenty minutes of work on token expiry. `03-testing-strategy.md` therefore pairs the automated pyramid with timeboxed exploratory charters.

This ticket also assembles the **regression pack** — the subset that re-runs every sprint afterwards — and records the epic-level QA sign-off that `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires before the Epic can be Done ("an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA").

## Scope / Deliverables
- Exploratory charter and regression-pack entry for the E42-S08 statechart inspector screen, covering the latch-acknowledge step-up gate.
- Execute the exploratory charters defined in E42-Q01, each timeboxed to 90 minutes with a written session report:
  1. *Scope escape* — as a manager, try every route, deep link, API call and WS subscription to see data outside your grants.
  2. *Audit credibility* — try to make the audit log appear editable, incomplete, or reorderable; try to take an action that produces no entry.
  3. *Elevation bypass* — try to reach or act on an admin surface without a fresh token, including via back/forward navigation, a restored session, and a second tab.
  4. *Work loss* — try to lose form content: token expiry mid-edit, concurrent edit, navigation, reload, network drop.
  5. *Tile interference* — try to make one slow or failing tile degrade another on SCR-120 and SCR-143.
  6. *Destructive-action pressure* — try to complete a destructive action faster than the confirmation intends (double-submit, Enter-key, browser autofill of the typed confirmation).
- File every finding as a Bug with repro steps, environment, build SHA and a priority.
- **Regression pack**: select the subset of cases (automated + manual) that must re-run every sprint for the rest of the project — the RBAC denials, the audit-integrity path, the session-revocation timing, the destructive confirmations, and the flag/maintenance propagation. Document it and wire the automated portion into the nightly run.
- **Epic QA sign-off**: execute the pack against a release candidate build, record pass/fail per case, and post the sign-off comment on the epic.

## Out of scope
- Automation of newly found gaps (filed as follow-up tickets against E42-Q02 or the owning story).
- Security abuse cases (E42-X03) — charter 1 and 3 overlap deliberately; findings are cross-referenced, and the Security ticket owns the formal verdict.
- Accessibility audit (E42-Q05).

## Acceptance criteria
- All six charters executed with a written session report each (what was tried, what was found, what was not covered).
- Every finding filed as a Bug with repro steps and a priority; P0/P1 findings are closed or explicitly accepted with Owner sign-off before the epic closes.
- The regression pack is documented, its automated portion runs nightly, and its manual portion has an owner and an execution cadence.
- The epic-level QA sign-off comment is posted with pass/fail per case against a named build SHA.
- Charter 2's outcome is explicit: either "no way was found to make the audit log appear mutable or incomplete", or findings that block the epic.

## Technical notes / design
- Charters are session-based: a stated mission, a timebox, notes taken during rather than after, and an explicit list of what the session did **not** cover — that list is how the next session avoids re-treading.
- Findings are reproduced once before filing, so the Bug carries deterministic steps rather than a narrative.

## Test plan
- Each finding that reveals a missing automated case produces a follow-up ticket naming the pyramid layer that should have caught it (the Bug DoR requirement in `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.1).

## Security notes
- Charters 1, 2, 3 and 6 are security-relevant; findings are shared with the Security engineer immediately rather than at the end of the ticket, and any privilege-escalation or scope-leak finding is treated as P0 regardless of its apparent exploitability.
- Exploration is performed against staging (demo) with synthetic data only.

## Accessibility notes
- Charter 6 explicitly includes keyboard-driven bypass attempts (Enter-key submission, focus order permitting a destructive action before the warning is read), which is both a security and an accessibility concern.

## Performance notes
- Charter 5 is the exploratory counterpart to E42-Q03's measured tile-independence scenario; findings here often explain measurements there.

## Observability
- Charter 2 verifies that every action taken during exploration produced its expected audit entry — in practice the most effective way to find an unaudited mutation path.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `tests/` (or `docs/qa/` for plans) and runnable in CI.

- [ ] Flaky tests quarantined with an owner and a follow-up ticket rather than silently retried.
