title: Run the WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility audit across every admin screen
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 forbids the "internal tool" exemption explicitly for admin screens, and `05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA plus axe-core in CI plus **manual screen-reader passes** as the standard. axe-core catches perhaps a third of real barriers; the rest — focus management after a dialog, announcement of an alert that appears without user action, a countdown that spams a screen reader, a status conveyed only by position — need a person.

This audit covers fifteen screens with several patterns that are genuinely hard: an interrupting re-auth overlay, a persistent impersonation banner, a live-updating health grid, a long audit table with expandable diffs, and two multi-step wizards.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Automated: axe-core runs on every admin route in every major state (loading, populated, empty, error, degraded, dialog-open), wired into CI so a regression fails a PR.
- Manual screen-reader passes with **two** screen readers (NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS at minimum) executing the written script from E42-D06, covering: elevate into admin; invite, disable and delete a user; bind and unbind an account with open positions; start and exit view-as; browse, expand and export the audit log; toggle a flag; enter and exit maintenance mode; run a restore; complete the onboarding wizard.
- Keyboard-only pass of the same flows: no mouse, verifying focus order, focus visibility, focus return after dialogs and drawers, no keyboard traps, and that no destructive action is reachable before its warning is read.
- Specific high-risk checks: the re-auth gate's `alertdialog` semantics and assertive failure announcement; the countdown announcing at thresholds rather than every tick; the impersonation banner announced and not silently dismissible; the integrity-failure alert announced once then persistent; live health updates not producing announcement storms; every status word-not-colour verified in greyscale; sparklines' table alternatives reachable; typed-confirmation fields labelled with their expected value stated in text.
- Contrast verification of the shipped build (not the design) for the admin tint and every state treatment.
- Zoom/reflow at 200% and 400% per WCAG 2.2, and target-size checks on the dense tables.
- Findings filed with the WCAG success criterion, severity and a remediation suggestion; report published under `docs/qa/`.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the findings (filed against the owning stories).
- The design-side a11y review (E42-D06) — done pre-build.
- Screens owned by other epics rendering inside the admin shell (E16, E27, E28, E39, E43), which have their own audits; the **shell itself** is in scope here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated checks are clean and enforced
  When axe-core runs on every admin route in every major state
  Then there are no violations at serious or critical level
  And the check is wired into CI so a regression fails the PR

Scenario: Screen-reader operability
  Given a screen-reader user follows the written script with two screen readers
  Then every flow can be completed without sighted assistance
  And every status, severity and outcome is conveyed as text

Scenario: The re-auth interruption is announced and recoverable
  Given the gate appears while I am editing a form
  Then it is announced as an alertdialog stating why and for how long
  And focus moves into it and returns to my form afterwards
  And my form content is intact

Scenario (failure): Announcement storm
  Given twelve health tiles update every second
  Then the screen reader is not flooded; updates are announced politely and coalesced

Scenario (edge): 400% zoom
  Then every admin screen reflows without horizontal scrolling and without content loss
```
- All findings filed with their WCAG criterion; no serious/critical finding is left unowned.
- The audit report is published and the epic's a11y DoD item is satisfiable from it.

## Technical notes / design
- axe-core runs against real application states driven by the Playwright suite, not against static Storybook snapshots alone — the states that fail are usually the ones only reachable through interaction.
- Announcement behaviour is verified by recording the screen-reader speech output for the high-risk flows, so a regression can be compared against a baseline rather than re-argued.
- Contrast is measured on the rendered build with a colour picker, because token values and shipped values can diverge.

## Test plan
- The manual script is versioned; each audit run records the script version and the build SHA, so results are comparable over time.
- Findings become regression cases in E42-Q04's pack where they are automatable.

## Security notes
- One overlap worth naming: a control that is disabled for RBAC reasons must expose its reason accessibly, **and** must still be enforced server-side. The audit verifies the first; E42-X03 verifies the second. Neither substitutes for the other.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket is the accessibility work; its scope is the full WCAG 2.2 AA criteria set as applied in `05-accessibility-standard.md`, not a spot check.
- Both automated and manual layers are required; passing axe alone does not satisfy this ticket.

## Performance notes
- Verifies that live-updating surfaces do not create announcement storms — an accessibility failure caused by an update cadence, which is where a11y and performance meet.

## Observability
Findings are categorised by pattern (dialogs, tables, live regions, wizards) so recurring causes are fixed in the design system rather than per screen.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `tests/` (or `docs/qa/` for plans) and runnable in CI.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario in the covered stories mapped to at least one executed case; traceability table posted on the ticket.
- [ ] Defects filed with repro steps, environment and `priority/*`; P0/P1 defects closed or explicitly accepted before sign-off.

- [ ] Flaky tests quarantined with an owner and a follow-up ticket rather than silently retried.

- `E42-D06` — supplies the written screen-reader script and the expected a11y contracts.
- `E42-S04`, `E42-S05`, `E42-S06` — the screens must be built.

## Context
The DoR review found that two ADMIN-domain **Must** stories are not built by E42: **US-ADMIN-010** Security posture panel (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26, SCR-137) and **US-ADMIN-012** Live-trading enablement gate (§26, SCR-137 + SCR-145). Both are deferred by design — US-ADMIN-010 to **E43** (`E43-D01`, `E43-S02`) and US-ADMIN-012 to **E44** (`E44-T04`, `E44-S01`, with the attestation half in `E43-S01`) — because neither can be honestly built before the R4 hardening and environment-separation work exists to back them.

A deferral is only safe if two things stay true: the downstream epic really does own the story to closure, and the deferring epic really does ship **no** partial or back-door implementation in the meantime. Both decay silently. Backlogs get re-scoped; a "temporarily disabled" toggle becomes an enabled one during a refactor. The most consequential switch in the product — live trading with real money — is exactly the wrong place to rely on a planning-document assertion.

This ticket turns the deferral into a check: an automated assertion that E42 contains no enable path, plus a recorded backlog verification before E42 closes. It is QA work, carries no product scope, and is deliberately **not** an engineering (S/T/K) ticket so it does not consume the 34-point engineering budget.

Refs: `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26 (US-ADMIN-007, US-ADMIN-010, US-ADMIN-012) · `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-137, SCR-145 · `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26 · `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 (epic-level exit) · `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3, §11.1.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated no-enable-path suite** (`tests/e2e/admin/deferred-must.spec.ts`), run in CI with the rest of the E42 pack:
  - As owner with a fresh admin token, `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/trading.live_enabled {enabled: true}` returns `403 gate_not_available` (or `validation_failed`/`gate_evidence_required` per `E42-T03`) — never `200` — with and without `reason`/`evidence_url`.
  - SCR-145 renders the `trading.live_enabled` row **disabled**, with its blocking reason visible and a link to SCR-137; the row exposes no control that can reach an enabled state by click, keyboard, or form submission.
  - `/admin/security` renders the placeholder registered by `E42-S01` — the R4 notice and nothing that claims a posture verdict.
  - A source-level assertion (Semgrep rule, contributed to `E42-X03`'s ruleset) that no E42-owned module writes `trading.live_enabled = true` and no admin component renders a posture pass/fail verdict.
- **Backlog verification record** (`docs/plan/backlog/verification/E42-deferred-must.md`), produced at epic close, stating for each of US-ADMIN-010 and US-ADMIN-012: the owning epic, the owning ticket keys, their sprint and milestone, and confirmation that `18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26 points at those epics.
- **Traceability reconciliation**: confirm rows US-ADMIN-010 and US-ADMIN-012 in `18-traceability-matrix.md` name E43/E44 (raise a docs PR if they still name E42), and that SCR-137 is listed under E43's screen set.
- Hand the record to `E42-Q04` so it is part of the epic QA sign-off packet.

## Out of scope
- Building, designing or testing the security posture panel or the live gate themselves — E43-S02, E43-Q01, E44-S01, E44-Q01.
- Judging whether E43/E44 are well specified — only that they exist, are scheduled and own the two stories.
- Any change to E42 product behaviour; if the suite fails, the fix lands on the owning story (`E42-S01`, `E42-S05`, `E42-T03`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The live-trading flag cannot be enabled from anywhere in E42
  Given an owner with a valid session and an admin token less than 15 minutes old
  When the API is called to set trading.live_enabled to true, with and without a reason and evidence_url
  Then every call is rejected with a documented error code and no flag value changes
  And an audit entry is written for each attempt

Scenario: The deferred surfaces are visibly deferred, not half-built
  Given the owner opens SCR-145 and the /admin/security route
  Then the trading.live_enabled row is disabled with its blocking reason and a link to SCR-137
  And /admin/security shows only the R4 placeholder with no posture verdict
  And a screen reader announces the flag row as disabled with its reason, not merely as unavailable

Scenario: The downstream owners are verified before E42 closes
  Given the E43 and E44 backlogs
  When the verification record is produced
  Then US-ADMIN-010 is traced to E43-D01 and E43-S02 and US-ADMIN-012 to E44-T04 and E44-S01 with E43-S01
  And each named ticket has a sprint in the R4 window and milestone "R4 Live enablement"
  And the record is attached to the E42 QA sign-off

Scenario (failure): A downstream owner has disappeared or been descoped
  Given a re-scope has removed US-ADMIN-012 from E44 without reassigning it
  When the verification runs
  Then the check fails, E42 cannot be signed off, and the gap is escalated to the Owner as an R4 Must-coverage risk

Scenario (edge): A regression re-introduces an enable path after E42 closes
  Given a later change adds a writable control for trading.live_enabled outside E44
  When the E42 regression pack runs in CI
  Then the suite fails with the offending route or component named
```

## Technical notes / design
- The API assertions run against the seeded staging (demo) stack used by `E42-Q02`, reusing its owner and manager fixtures and its fresh-admin-token helper; no new harness.
- The UI assertions are Playwright, asserting `aria-disabled="true"` plus the presence of the `data-blocking-reason` attribute specified by `E42-S05`, rather than asserting pixels.
- The Semgrep rule is written as a deny-list pattern over `packages/web/src/features/admin/**` and `services/api/app/modules/admin/**`: any literal `trading.live_enabled` in a write position outside the E44-owned module is a finding. It ships into the ruleset maintained by `E42-X03` so it keeps running after this epic.
- The verification record is a short markdown table plus the date and the reviewer; it is checked in so a later reader can see when the claim was last true, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2's requirement that epic-level exit evidence be recorded rather than asserted.
- Error codes referenced: `gate_not_available`, `gate_evidence_required`, `validation_failed`, `forbidden`, `stepup_required`.

## Test plan
- **E2E**: the five scenarios above, in the E42 Playwright project; tagged `@regression` so `E42-Q04` picks them into the standing pack.
- **Contract**: schemathesis assertion that the OpenAPI definition of `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` documents the refusal codes for the live flag.
- **Static**: the Semgrep rule with positive and negative fixtures (a file that writes the flag → finding; the E44 module → no finding).
- **Manual**: one-pass screen-reader check of the disabled flag row (coordinated with `E42-Q05`, not duplicated).
- Fixtures: reuse `E42-Q01`'s owner/manager/viewer seed; no new data needed.
- Coverage target: N/A (assertion suite); the gate is that all five scenarios pass in CI.

## Security notes
- Directly mitigates the **elevation-of-privilege / tampering** threats catalogued by `E42-X01` for the flag surface, and the `04-security-program.md` control that safety-critical switches must not be reachable without their evidence binding.
- Data classification: configuration metadata only; no secrets or PII touched.
- The verification record names ticket keys only — no credentials, no host names.
- Review label: `security` — the finding of an enable path is a Critical by definition and blocks the epic.

## Accessibility notes
- Asserts the disabled flag row is announced with its reason (not a bare "dimmed" state) and that the placeholder on `/admin/security` is reachable in tab order with a heading in the page's heading hierarchy — the R4 notice must be readable by a screen-reader user, not implied visually.
- Coordinated with `E42-Q05` so the manual pass is done once.

## Performance notes
- Negligible: the suite is fewer than twenty assertions and adds <30 s to the CI run. No budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` apply.

## Observability
- Each rejected enable attempt must appear in the audit log as `admin.flag_change_denied` with actor, flag key and reason — the suite asserts the entry exists, which also exercises the `E42-T02` audit read path.
- The CI job publishes a single pass/fail signal named `e42-deferred-must` so the epic sign-off checklist can reference it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] The no-enable-path suite is merged, green in CI and tagged into the E42 regression pack
- [ ] The Semgrep rule is merged into the `E42-X03` ruleset with fixtures
- [ ] `docs/plan/backlog/verification/E42-deferred-must.md` is checked in, dated and names the owning tickets
- [ ] `18-traceability-matrix.md` rows US-ADMIN-010 / US-ADMIN-012 verified (or corrected by PR) to point at E43/E44
- [ ] The record is included in `E42-Q04`'s epic QA sign-off packet
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded; no design sign-off required (no new UI); security reviewer acknowledges the finding severity rule
- [ ] Any failure found has a fix landed on the owning E42 story before the epic closes

## Dependencies
- `E42-S01` — registers `/admin/security` and its placeholder.
- `E42-S05` / `E42-T03` — render and enforce the blocked `trading.live_enabled` flag that this ticket asserts against.
- `E42-Q01` — fixtures and the black-box plan this suite extends.
- `E42-X03` — owns the ruleset the Semgrep rule ships into.
- Reads (does not depend on code from) the **E43** and **E44** backlogs: `E43-D01`, `E43-S02`, `E43-S01`, `E44-T04`, `E44-S01`.

## Branch
`test/admin-deferred-must-verification` — one small PR: spec file + Semgrep rule + verification record template. PR size guidance: <300 lines.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26 ADMIN (US-ADMIN-007, US-ADMIN-010, US-ADMIN-012)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-137 security centre, SCR-145 feature flags

title: Implement account-access grants: soft revoke and revoked-frame push
body:
## Context
Split from E42-T04 (#965) on 2026-10-15 by R2 of the DoR plan on #965, accepted by the orchestrator; the owner items it relies on (O2, O4) are accepted on an interim basis, subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed) and lists #965 O1–O7 among the interim decisions open to veto. This Task owns plan slices S8–S9: the account-access grant set behind `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access`.

US-ADMIN-002 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`) requires that revoking an account grant force-closes the user's WS subscriptions for that account, and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5 re-evaluates authorisation on every change to a user's account grants. The frame is `revoked` with reason `account_scope_changed`, not `unsubscribed` (§9.5). E42-T04's contract slice S1 corrects the OpenAPI wording on this route and adds its 403 for a self-target (R3, R4).

Grant removal is a soft revoke (O4): `can_view=false, can_trade=false`, never a `DELETE`, so the freeze columns and `max_daily_loss_usd` survive (`services/api/candleviewer/db/models.py`). Delete-then-regrant would silently unfreeze a frozen manager without `risk.unfreeze_manager` (C-12.5).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **S8 account-access store** (`feat(accounts-admin): account-access store (E42-T08)`, branch `feat/e42-t08-access-store`, ~340 LOC):
  - Replace a user's grant set in one transaction, with a write-ahead `users.access_change` audit record (R5).
  - Removed grants become soft revokes (O4); an unknown account rolls the whole change back.
  - A grant change on a user who is not `active` returns 409.
  - A disable racing a replacement leaves no live grant.
  - Onboarding's `_BOUND` reader (`storage/repositories/onboarding_sqlalchemy.py`), the one reader that does not filter on `can_view`, ignores revoked grants.
- **S9 serve GET/PUT account-access** (`feat(accounts-admin): serve GET/PUT account-access (E42-T08)`, branch `feat/e42-t08-access-route`, ~360 LOC):
  - `GET` and `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` per the contract from E42-T04 slice S1: Owner-only and deny by default; `PUT` is step-up gated for the `users` action class (`04-security-program.md` §7.2.1: step-up for write).
  - After commit, push `grants_changed` (`ws/permissions.py`, with #2318) so every affected subscription ends with `revoked` (`account_scope_changed`) within 2 s and a resubscribe gets `account_scope_denied`.
  - Self-target → 403; unknown account → 404; audit unavailable → 503 `audit_unavailable`.
  - Removing the user's last grant while their open-position count is unknown needs `acknowledge_unknown_positions=true`, otherwise 409 `positions_unknown` (O2). The change records `positions_decision=leave` and the open-position count; it never flattens positions or cancels orders.
  - The route's row in `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` flips to `executed`.
- **Flag (C-4.13, C-4.14).** No runtime flag on grant revocation or its `revoked` push, which enforce RBAC (C-4.14). S8 adds no route, and `GET|PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` stay `not_mounted` in the RBAC matrix until S9 serves them. This follows R8's proposal on #965, which has no recorded decision yet (#2710); C-11.1 #13 needs one before this Task is marked Ready.

## Out of scope
- The contract deltas, the disable cascade and `DELETE /users/{userId}` (E42-T04).
- User read/PATCH, role changes and admin sessions (E42-T09); the deferred purge (E42-T10).
- Flattening positions or cancelling orders on unbind (O2): flatten-first stays a separate OMS action.
- Version counters such as `grants_version` (dropped by R7).
- The grant editor UI (E42-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: AC3 Grant revocation ends the subscription with a revoked frame
  Given manager M is subscribed to positions for account S
  When an owner revokes M's grant for S
  Then within 2 seconds on a fake clock the subscription is terminated with a revoked frame whose reason is account_scope_changed, not unsubscribed
  And a resubscribe attempt for S fails with account_scope_denied

Scenario: Soft revoke keeps the freeze state and the cap
  Given M's grant for account S is frozen and carries a max_daily_loss_usd cap
  When the grant is revoked and later granted again
  Then the freeze state and the cap are unchanged

Scenario (failure): Self-target is refused
  When an owner changes their own account access
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): An unknown account rolls the change back
  When the replacement grant set names an account that does not exist
  Then the call returns 404 and no grant changes

Scenario (failure): The user is not active
  Given M is invited, locked or disabled
  When an owner replaces M's grants
  Then the call returns 409 and no grant changes

Scenario (failure): Forbidden role
  When a manager or a viewer calls GET or PUT /users/{userId}/account-access
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): AC7 Last grant with unknown positions
  Given M's open-position count is unknown
  When an owner removes M's last grant without acknowledge_unknown_positions=true
  Then the call returns 409 positions_unknown and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): AC8 Audit unavailable
  Given the audit writer is unavailable
  When an owner replaces M's grants
  Then the call returns 503 audit_unavailable and nothing changes
```
AC numbers follow the rewritten criteria of E42-T04 (R3): AC3 moved here with its scope, and AC7 and AC8 apply to this route as well.

## Technical notes / design
- One transaction (R7): lock the user row, apply the replacement set as soft revokes and upserts, run `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`, write the audit record ahead, then commit. The audit writer is WAL-first and outside the database transaction (`audit/writer.py`), so the record is written only after the constraints pass. After commit, push `grants_changed`; a failure there is counted and alerted, never rolled back.
- No `grants_version` counter (R7): it would add per-frame database reads in the WS lane. Pushes go through `grants_changed` plus #2318's versioned permission snapshots.
- Every other grant reader already filters on `can_view` (`storage/repositories/identity_sqlalchemy.py`, `rules/scope_state.py`); S8 fixes onboarding's `_BOUND`.
- Error codes come only from `x-error-codes` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: `validation_failed` (400), `unauthenticated` (401), `forbidden` (403), `step_up_required` (403, a `PUT` without a live step-up), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409), `positions_unknown` (409, AC7), and `audit_unavailable` (503), which E42-T04 slice S1 registers (R4). The route takes no `If-Match`, so `version_conflict` (412) does not apply.
- Until #2525 merged (2026-10-15), WS private topics were deny-all in the deployed app, so AC3 could be proven only in-process. The real backend now loads the WS principal from the store (`build_ws_principal_loader` in `app.py`), so AC3 can be proven end to end there as well.

## Test plan
- **S8** (Postgres, `@pytest.mark.integration`): `test_replace_write_ahead_audit`; `test_keeps_freeze_and_cap`; IDOR `test_unknown_account_rolls_back`; `test_non_active_user_409`; `test_disable_vs_replace_race_no_live_grant`; `test_onboarding_ignores_revoked`.
- **S9:** `test_revoked_frame_within_2s` (AC3); `test_resubscribe_scope_denied` (AC3); `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; `test_self_target_403`; `test_stepup_and_audit_503` (AC8); `test_unknown_account_404`; `test_last_grant_needs_ack` (AC7).
- The 2-second bound runs on a fake clock; no sleeps and no network (C-13.5).
- Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).

## Security notes
- Interim threat model (O1): `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D1–D6 plus U4, U24 and U25 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`. The user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (#2729) merges before E42-T04's route slice S6, and therefore before S9.
- Elevation of privilege: grant mutation is Owner-only, step-up gated, cannot target the acting user, and is audited (SR-055).
- Tampering with risk state: soft revoke keeps freeze state and caps, so revoking and re-granting cannot unfreeze a manager (C-12.5).
- IDOR: an unknown or foreign account rolls the whole change back.
- Data classification: grants are Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task. The grant editor UI is E42-S03.

## Performance notes
- A grant change completes within 300 ms p95, excluding the post-commit push.
- The `revoked` frame reaches affected subscriptions within 2 s (AC3).

## Observability
- Audit: `users.access_change` with before and after, registered in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits it (R5).
- Post-commit push failures are counted and alerted (R7).
- Logs: one structured line per step with its outcome, correlated by `request_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every scenario above passes as an automated test; Postgres cases run as `@pytest.mark.integration`.
- [ ] Both slices merged; S8 says `Refs #2648` plus `Partial: slice 1 of 2`, and S9 carries the closing line for #2648.
- [ ] Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules; RBAC matrix row `executed`.
- [ ] Security-reviewer and code-reviewer approvals on both slices.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or an explicit QA capacity deviation note).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E42-T04` — its slice S1 lands the contract first (C-6.1), and S9 builds on its route slice S6.
- #2318 (versioned WS permission snapshots) before S9. #2525, which an end-to-end proof in the deployed app needed, merged on 2026-10-15.
- Feeds E38-S07 (an eligibility field on this route), which lists this Task in `blocked_by`, and E42-S03 (user detail with role and account binding), which does not yet (#2710, item 4).
- Open in #2710: this Task's estimate, an author proposal sized from the slice LOC (C-11.1 #7), and the flag record (R8).

## Branch
`feat/e42-t08-access-store` (S8), then `feat/e42-t08-access-route` (S9).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ADMIN-002
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/users/{userId}/account-access`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.3, §9.5
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 (`user_account_access`)
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7, SR-055
- `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md` U4, U24, U25
- #965 (DoR plan and decision record, 2026-10-15)


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. The DoR plan and decision record on #965 (2026-10-15): O2, O4, R2–R7

**Repo paths to create/modify**

- `pytest -m integration` (from `services/api/`, needs the docker compose stack)

**Branch & PR**
- Branches: `feat/e42-t08-access-store`, then `feat/e42-t08-access-route`

title: Implement user read/PATCH, role changes under owner lock and admin sessions
body:
## Context
Split from E42-T04 (#965) on 2026-10-15 by R2 of the DoR plan on #965, accepted by the orchestrator; the owner item it relies on (O3) is accepted on an interim basis, subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed) and lists #965 O1–O7 among the interim decisions open to veto. This Task owns plan slices S10–S12: the user read model with an ETag, `PATCH /users/{userId}`, role and status changes under the owner lock, and the admin view of a target user's sessions.

US-ADMIN-001 and US-ADMIN-002 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`) need last-owner protection: at least one enabled Owner must always exist (SR-055; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D6), enforced in one transaction under a lock so two concurrent demotions cannot both succeed. C-12.2 makes TOTP mandatory for every user, so `mfa_required: false` is refused (O3). R4 adds the admin session routes and a `getUser` ETag to the contract in E42-T04 slice S1, and R6 fixes the status rules.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **S10 GET user with an ETag; PATCH name and MFA flag** (`feat(accounts-admin): GET user with ETag and PATCH name and MFA flag (E42-T09)`, branch `feat/e42-t09-get-patch-user`, ~330 LOC):
  - `GET /users/{userId}` returns an ETag that changes when the user's roles change.
  - `PATCH /users/{userId}` honours `If-Match`; a stale ETag gets 412.
  - `mfa_required: false` gets 400 `validation_failed` for every target role (O3).
  - `password_hash` is never returned.
  - Owner-only, step-up for the `users` action class, audited; audit unavailable gets 503 `audit_unavailable`.
- **S11 status and roles under the owner lock** (`feat(accounts-admin): PATCH status and roles under the owner lock (E42-T09)`, branch `feat/e42-t09-patch-status-roles`, ~360 LOC):
  - `PATCH` changes status only between `active` and `disabled`; `invited` or `locked` gets 400 (R6).
  - Status changes and `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` take the owner lock from #2508, so of two parallel cross-demotions exactly one wins and the other gets 409 `conflict`, in each of 10 rounds (AC4).
  - A `PATCH` disable racing a demotion keeps at least one enabled Owner (AC6).
  - A `PATCH` to `disabled` calls E42-T04's disable service, so it runs the whole cascade (sessions through B16, sockets with 4403, rules, grants, an open invite) rather than only changing the status column (SR-029). While the open-position count is unknown it needs `acknowledge_unknown_positions=true`, otherwise 409 `positions_unknown` (O2, AC7), exactly as `DELETE /users/{userId}` does; E42-T04 slice S1 adds the parameter to `updateUser`.
  - Enabling a user never restores their grants or sessions (R6).
- **S12 admin user sessions** (`feat(accounts-admin): admin user sessions (E42-T09)`, branch `feat/e42-t09-admin-sessions`, ~300 LOC):
  - `GET /users/{userId}/sessions` and `DELETE /users/{userId}/sessions/{sessionId}` (R4): step-up for the `users` action class; a session that belongs to another user gets 404.
  - No token material in any response.
  - Each revoked session writes one `auth.session_revoked` record ahead of the change, by recording B16 REVOKE as `reset_totp` does (R5).
  - The revoked session's socket closes with 4401 within 5 s.
- Each route's row in `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` flips to `executed`.
- **Flag (C-4.13, C-4.14).** No runtime flag on the owner lock, step-up or audit (C-4.14). `GET` and `PATCH /users/{userId}` stay `not_mounted` until S10 serves them, and the admin session routes until S12. Still open: what S10's `PATCH` answers to a `status` change before S11 lands. Both follow R8 on #965, which has no recorded decision yet (#2710); C-11.1 #13 needs one before this Task is marked Ready.

## Out of scope
- The contract deltas and the disable cascade (E42-T04); grants (E42-T08); the deferred purge, including cancelling a pending purge on re-enable (E42-T10).
- `GET /users`, `/roles` and `/permissions` list routes (R9 on #965 proposes a separate ticket; not yet decided).
- Self-service sessions (`/me/sessions`, E09).
- The admin UI (E42-S02, E42-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario (failure): AC4 Parallel cross-demotions leave an owner
  Given owners A and B are the only two enabled owners
  When A's session demotes B to manager while B's session demotes A, in parallel
  Then exactly one of the two requests succeeds and the other returns 409 conflict
  And at least one enabled owner remains
  And the same holds in each of 10 rounds, every round starting again from two enabled owners

Scenario (failure): AC6 A disable racing a demotion keeps an owner
  Given owners A and B are the only two owners
  When a demotion of A races a PATCH that disables B
  Then at least one enabled owner remains
  And the losing call writes no audit record

Scenario: A PATCH disable runs the whole disable cascade
  Given manager M has an active session, an open socket and an armed rule
  When an owner sends PATCH /users/{userId} with status disabled and acknowledge_unknown_positions=true
  Then the outcome is the same as for DELETE /users/{userId}: M's next REST call gets 401, every socket of M receives bye with reason user_disabled and closes with 4403, and M's rule is disarmed
  And exactly one users.disable record is written

Scenario (failure): AC7 A PATCH disable with unknown positions needs the acknowledgement
  Given M's open-position count is unknown
  When an owner sends PATCH /users/{userId} with status disabled and without acknowledge_unknown_positions=true
  Then the call returns 409 positions_unknown and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): MFA cannot be switched off
  When an owner sends PATCH /users/{userId} with mfa_required false
  Then the call returns 400 validation_failed whatever the target's role

Scenario (failure): A stale ETag is refused
  Given an owner read user M and holds M's ETag
  And M's roles changed since
  When the owner sends PATCH /users/{userId} with that ETag in If-Match
  Then the call returns 412 and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): Only active and disabled are settable
  When an owner sets M's status to invited or locked
  Then the call returns 400 and nothing changes

Scenario (edge): Re-enabling restores nothing
  Given M was disabled, losing M's grants and sessions
  When an owner re-enables M
  Then M is active with no grants and no sessions restored

Scenario: The owner revokes one of M's sessions
  Given manager M has two sessions
  When an owner deletes one of them through DELETE /users/{userId}/sessions/{sessionId}
  Then one auth.session_revoked record is written before the change
  And that session's socket closes with 4401 within 5 seconds on a fake clock
  And M's other session is untouched and no response carries token material

Scenario (failure): A session of another user is not found
  When an owner deletes a session id that belongs to a user other than {userId}
  Then the call returns 404 and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): Forbidden role
  When a manager or a viewer calls any route of this Task
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): AC8 Audit unavailable
  Given the audit writer is unavailable
  When an owner sends any mutation of this Task
  Then the call returns 503 audit_unavailable and nothing changes
```
AC numbers follow the rewritten criteria of E42-T04 (R3): AC4 moved here with its scope, and AC6, AC7 and AC8 apply to these routes as well (AC7 to a `PATCH` to `disabled`). AC4 runs as 10 rounds of one cross-demotion pair, so every outcome is fixed. A repeat of a demotion that already took effect is a state-based no-op that succeeds and changes nothing, as the shipped `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` route and E42-T04's AC5 treat a repeat.

## Technical notes / design
- One transaction per mutation (R7): lock the user row, lock the owner rows as #2508 does, apply the change, run `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`, write the audit record ahead, then commit. After commit, end sockets and record B16 transitions; a failure there is counted and alerted, never rolled back.
- The ETag covers the fields `GET /users/{userId}` returns, roles included, so a role change makes an earlier ETag stale.
- `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` keeps its shipped `{id, roles}` body, which E42-T04 slice S1 documents (R4).
- Error codes come only from `x-error-codes` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: `validation_failed` (400), `unauthenticated` (401), `forbidden` (403), `step_up_required` (403, a mutation without a live step-up), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409), `positions_unknown` (409, AC7), `version_conflict` (412, a stale `If-Match`), and `audit_unavailable` (503), which E42-T04 slice S1 registers (R4).

## Test plan
- **S10:** `test_etag_tracks_roles`; `test_no_password_hash`; `test_stale_if_match_412`; `test_mfa_required_false_400` (O3); `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; `test_step_up_and_audit_503` (AC8).
- **S11** (Postgres, `@pytest.mark.integration`): `test_ten_parallel_demotions_one_wins` (AC4); `test_patch_disable_vs_demote_keeps_owner` (AC6); property test `test_owner_always_remains`; `test_enable_no_regrant`; `test_invited_or_locked_400`; `test_patch_disable_runs_disable_cascade`; `test_patch_disable_positions_unknown_409` (AC7).
- **S12:** `test_no_token_material`; IDOR `test_other_users_session_404`; `test_revoked_audit_ahead`; `test_audit_down_503` (AC8); `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; `test_socket_4401_within_5s`.
- Time-bound assertions run on a fake clock; no sleeps and no network (C-13.5).
- Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).

## Security notes
- Interim threat model (O1): `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D1–D6 plus U4, U24 and U25 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`; the user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (#2729) merges before E42-T04's route slice S6, and so before these routes.
- Elevation of privilege: role and status changes are Owner-only, step-up gated, cannot target the acting user, and are audited (SR-055).
- Denial of service: removing the last Owner would lock the installation out, hence the locked owner check (§5.7 D6).
- Information disclosure: no token material or `password_hash` in any response. A session id that belongs to a user other than `{userId}` answers 404, so one user's sessions cannot be reached through another user's path (IDOR).
- Data classification: PII (`users.email`, session IP); Confidential (roles).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task. The admin UI is E42-S02 and E42-S03.

## Performance notes
- Mutations complete within 300 ms p95; the owner lock is held for one short transaction.
- A revoked session's socket closes within 5 s.

## Observability
- Audit: `users.enable` (R5), `users.disable` for a `PATCH` disable, `roles.grant` and `roles.revoke`, and one `auth.session_revoked` per revoked session, all with before and after where they apply. New actions register in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits them.
- Post-commit step failures are counted and alerted (R7).
- Logs: one structured line per step with its outcome, correlated by `request_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every scenario above passes as an automated test; Postgres cases run as `@pytest.mark.integration`.
- [ ] All three slices merged; S10 and S11 say `Refs #2649` plus `Partial: slice k of 3`, and S12 carries the closing line for #2649.
- [ ] Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules; RBAC matrix rows `executed`.
- [ ] Security-reviewer and code-reviewer approvals on every slice.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or an explicit QA capacity deviation note).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E42-T04` — its slice S1 lands the contract first (C-6.1), and S10 and S12 build on its route slice S6.
- #2508 (owner lock and write-ahead audit for role changes) before S11.
- Feeds E42-S02 and E42-S03; neither is a `blocked_by` edge yet (#2710).
- E42-T10's S14 lands after S11 and adds the purge cancel to S11's enable path.
- Open in #2710: this Task's estimate, an author proposal sized from the slice LOC (C-11.1 #7), and the flag record (R8).

## Branch
`feat/e42-t09-get-patch-user` (S10), `feat/e42-t09-patch-status-roles` (S11), `feat/e42-t09-admin-sessions` (S12).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ADMIN-001, US-ADMIN-002
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/users/{userId}`, `/users/{userId}/roles`, `/users/{userId}/sessions`, `/me/sessions`

title: Implement deferred PII purge: purge columns, anonymisation reaper, ?purge=true
body:
## Context
Split from E42-T04 (#965) on 2026-10-15 by R2 of the DoR plan on #965, accepted by the orchestrator; the owner item it relies on (O6) is accepted on an interim basis, subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed) and lists #965 O1–O7 among the interim decisions open to veto. This Task owns plan slices S2, S13 and S14: deferred PII anonymisation after a user is deleted with `?purge=true`.

US-ADMIN-001 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`) requires that a deleted user's "audit and journal history is retained under an anonymised reference, and the deletion itself is audited". O6 fixes how:
- The surrogate is `deleted-user-` followed by the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256(`cv-user-surrogate:` + user id); the email becomes `<surrogate>@deleted.invalid`.
- `display_name` and `last_login_ip`, and the `ip`, `user_agent`, `device_label` and `tailscale_node` of the user's sessions, are nulled. Main has no session reaper (`storage/retention/schedule.py`), so this Task's reaper does it.
- Two nullable columns, `users.purge_after` and `users.anonymised_at`, carry the schedule.
- Audit rows keep the name they were written with: `auth.login` stores the typed identifier and invites store the username, and audit is never updated (C-5.7, C-12.8). Lifecycle audit records therefore carry ids, status and roles only.
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §12 is corrected to match.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **S2 users purge columns** (`feat(accounts-admin): users purge columns (E42-T10)`, branch `feat/e42-t10-users-purge-columns`, ~150 LOC): one Alembic revision adding nullable `users.purge_after` and `users.anonymised_at`. Additive and reversible (C-5.1, C-5.2); exactly one revision, re-parented onto the head current when it lands (C-5.3): #2516 merged `0023_replay_sessions` on 2026-10-15, and #2614 (open) claims 0024; round trip on an empty and a seeded database (C-5.5).
- **S13 anonymisation reaper** (`feat(accounts-admin): anonymisation reaper (E42-T10)`, branch `feat/e42-t10-purge-reaper`, ~350 LOC): anonymises only users whose `purge_after` has passed, in bounded batches; writes `users.anonymise` ahead of each user (R5); sets `anonymised_at`; never updates an audit row.
- **S14 `DELETE /users/{userId}?purge=true`** (`feat(accounts-admin): DELETE user with purge (E42-T10)`, branch `feat/e42-t10-purge-route`, ~300 LOC): on top of E42-T04's disable, schedules `purge_after` 90 days out and writes `users.delete` ahead (R5). Re-enabling the user before `purge_after` cancels the pending purge (R6): S14 adds that step to the enable path of E42-T09's S11. Owner-only, step-up for the `users` action class, audited.
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`: §3.1 gains the two columns and §12 the anonymisation rules (O6).
- **Flag: open.** R8 on #965 proposes a `users_purge_enabled` Settings field, default off, gating only `?purge=true` until S14; it has no recorded decision yet (#2710). Record one before S14 starts and before this Task is marked Ready (C-11.1 #13). No flag gates any step of the disable cascade (C-4.14).

## Out of scope
- The contract deltas, the disable cascade and `DELETE /users/{userId}` without `purge` (E42-T04).
- Grants (E42-T08); user read/PATCH, role changes and admin sessions (E42-T09).
- Rewriting or redacting audit rows (C-5.7, C-12.8).
- Journal anonymisation: the journal is not on main yet, so it is covered by foreign-key retention only.
- The admin UI (E42-S02, E42-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: AC2 History is retained under an anonymised reference
  Given manager M was deleted with purge
  When purge_after passes on a fake clock and the reaper runs
  Then M's username is the surrogate and M's email is <surrogate>@deleted.invalid
  And M's display name, last login IP, and every session's IP, user agent, device label and Tailscale node are null
  And every audit row about M is byte-identical to before
  And M's journal history stays attached through foreign-key retention only

Scenario: Deletion and anonymisation are audited ahead
  When an owner deletes M with purge
  Then a users.delete record is written before the change
  And the reaper writes users.anonymise before it anonymises M

Scenario: The surrogate is stable and not derived from PII
  When the surrogate for a user id is computed on separate runs
  Then it is identical every time
  And it depends on the user id alone, never on the email, username or any IP

Scenario (edge): Only expired purges run
  Given M's purge_after is in the future
  When the reaper runs
  Then M is unchanged

Scenario (edge): Re-enabling cancels a pending purge
  Given M was deleted with purge and purge_after has not passed
  When an owner re-enables M
  Then purge_after is cleared and the reaper never anonymises M

Scenario (failure): Forbidden role
  When a manager or a viewer calls DELETE /users/{userId}?purge=true
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario: The migration round-trips
  When the purge-columns revision is upgraded, downgraded and upgraded again on an empty and on a seeded database
  Then every step succeeds and the downgrade removes only the two new columns
```
AC numbers follow the rewritten criteria of E42-T04 (R3): AC2 moved here with its scope.

## Technical notes / design
- The surrogate is deterministic but not reversible from PII: the hash input is a fixed domain prefix plus the user id, so historical joins still group by user while nothing about the email or name is recoverable.
- The reaper runs off the request path under the retention scheduler, takes bounded batches, and holds each user's anonymisation and its `users.anonymise` record in one transaction.
- `users.delete` and `users.anonymise` register in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits them (R5).
- Error codes come only from `x-error-codes` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, plus `audit_unavailable`, which E42-T04 slice S1 registers (R4).

## Test plan
- **S2:** `test_<rev>_adds_nullable_columns`; `test_<rev>_downgrade_only_new_columns`; upgrade, downgrade and upgrade on an empty and a seeded database. `<rev>` is the revision number the slice takes at the head when it lands, as the migration tests name themselves.
- **S13:** property tests `test_surrogate_stable` and `test_surrogate_not_from_pii`; Postgres (`@pytest.mark.integration`): `test_only_past_purge_after`, `test_audit_byte_identical` (AC2), `test_nulls_session_pii`, `test_batch_bounded`, `test_users_anonymise_ahead`.
- **S14** (Postgres): `test_history_under_surrogate_after_90d` (AC2); `test_users_delete_ahead`; `test_reenable_cancels_purge`; `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; if R8 adds a flag, a test that it is removed.
- The 90-day window runs on a fake clock; no sleeps and no network (C-13.5).
- Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).

## Security notes
- Interim threat model (O1): `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D1–D6 plus U4, U24 and U25 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`; the user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (#2729) merges before E42-T04's route slice S6, and so before S14.
- Information disclosure: the surrogate must not be reversible from PII; PII columns are nulled, never copied elsewhere.
- Repudiation: deletion and anonymisation are audited ahead; audit rows are never updated (C-5.7, C-12.8).
- Data classification: PII (`users.email`, `users.display_name`, `users.last_login_ip`, the session columns above, `audit_log.actor_ip`). The migration also needs the CODEOWNERS of `services/api/candleviewer/migrations/`.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- The reaper processes bounded batches off the request path.
- `DELETE /users/{userId}?purge=true` completes within 300 ms p95.

## Observability
- Audit: `users.delete` and `users.anonymise`, registered in the PR that first emits each (R5).
- Logs: one structured line per reaper batch with its count and outcome, correlated by `request_id` for the route.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every scenario above passes as an automated test; Postgres cases run as `@pytest.mark.integration`.
- [ ] All three slices merged; S2 and S13 say `Refs #2650` plus `Partial: slice k of 3`, and S14 carries the closing line for #2650.
- [ ] Migration round trip on an empty and a seeded database attached to S2; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 and §12 updated.
- [ ] The R8 flag decision recorded and applied before S14.
- [ ] Security-reviewer and code-reviewer approvals on every slice.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or an explicit QA capacity deviation note).

title: Security review: RBAC, elevation, audit and destructive admin paths
body:
## Context
The threat model (E42-X01) says what should be true. This ticket verifies it against the code that shipped, before the epic closes and before E43's hardening and pen-test build on top of it.

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes this non-optional: any ticket touching RBAC, API-key handling, admin screens or order-placement paths is "always treated as `security`-labelled for DoD purposes, whether or not the label was applied at creation — reviewers must add the label and block Done if missing." This epic touches three of those four.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box review** of the admin implementation against the threat model:
  - Every `/admin/*` and `/users*` route: permission declared, deny-by-default, step-up where required, audit emitted on both success and denial. Reviewed as a table, route by route, with no route unexamined.
  - The elevation model: token TTL server-issued and non-extendable by the client; elevation bound to the session; the router-404 / API-403 non-disclosure split actually implemented.
  - The audit read side: no mutation path exists; manager scoping is in the repository layer; export is signed, range-limited and rate-limited; redaction is applied at write time and preserved on export.
  - Append-only enforcement verified **independently of the application**: as `cv_app`, attempt UPDATE and DELETE on `audit_log` and confirm both the grant and the trigger refuse.
  - The flag registry: confirm the compile-time rejection of security-gating categories actually fails startup, and that no auth/RBAC/audit module reads a flag (the Semgrep rule from E42-X03 is verified, not just merged).
  - The user lifecycle: last-owner protection under concurrency (reviewed as a locking argument, not just a test); anonymisation irreversibility; grant-change propagation to live WS subscriptions (the `grants_changed` push and the `revoked` frame; R7 on #965 dropped `grants_version`).
  - Destructive paths: restore preconditions enforced server-side; backup download URL short-lived and single-use; maintenance mode step-up gated and fail-closed.
- **Copy review** of the security-relevant confirmations, as required by SCR-146's sign-off ("restore impact copy reviewed by security") and extended here to delete, unbind, purge and flag-change copy — understated consequences are findings.
- SAST/SCA results for the epic's code triaged; false positives annotated with a reason, not suppressed silently.
- Findings filed with severity; Critical/High must be closed before the epic is Done.
- Security sign-off comment on the epic.

## Out of scope
- The pen-test (E43) — this review is an input, and deliberately precedes it so the pen-testers spend their time on what a review cannot find.
- Automating the abuse cases (E42-X03).
- Remediation implementation, which lands on the owning story branches.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every admin route is accounted for
  When the review enumerates every /admin/* and /users* route
  Then each has a declared permission, deny-by-default behaviour, and an audit entry on success and on denial
  And any route missing one is a finding

Scenario: The audit log is immutable in practice, not just in intent
  Given a direct database connection as the application role
  When UPDATE and DELETE are attempted on audit_log
  Then both fail, once on grants and once on the trigger
  And the attempt is itself recorded

Scenario: No flag can weaken a security control
  Given a flag definition declaring an auth-gating category
  When the service starts
  Then startup fails
  And no auth, RBAC or audit module contains a flag lookup

Scenario: Elevation cannot be extended by the client
  When a client attempts to extend or forge the admin token TTL
  Then the server rejects it and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): A destructive path missing a precondition
  Given restore is called with maintenance mode off
  Then the service refuses regardless of what the UI sent
```
- All Critical/High findings closed or accepted with Owner sign-off before the epic closes.
- Security sign-off comment posted on this ticket and on the epic.

## Technical notes / design
- The route table is generated from the application's router at review time rather than written by hand, so a route cannot be omitted from the review by oversight.
- The append-only check runs as a real database session with the application role, because reasoning about grants is not the same as exercising them.
- Concurrency arguments (last-owner, chain forking) are reviewed as locking proofs plus the stress tests from E42-T04 (a disable racing a demotion) and E42-T09 (parallel cross-demotions) — either alone is insufficient.

## Test plan
- Every finding produces a regression test at the appropriate layer before it is closed, so the same defect cannot return silently.
- Review conclusions that depend on a control being tested reference the specific test id.

## Security notes
- This ticket *is* the security review. Its scope is the epic's full attack surface as enumerated in E42-X01.
- Particular attention to the three controls the rest of the product trusts: the audit chain's immutability, the RBAC grant boundary between managers, and the flag registry's inability to gate security.

## Accessibility notes
- One cross-cutting check: controls that are disabled for RBAC reasons must be enforced server-side, not merely rendered disabled. A UI-only restriction is a finding here even though it looks like an accessibility nicety.

## Performance notes
Reviews the export range limit and rate limit as DoS controls, cross-checking the measured behaviour from E42-Q03.

## Observability
- Verifies that denials are observable: `admin.access_denied` entries, denied-request counters and elevation-failure metrics must exist and fire, since an undetectable denial is an undetectable attack.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded with STRIDE category, likelihood/impact, and disposition (fixed / mitigated / accepted-risk with Owner sign-off).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding has a linked remediation ticket that is Done before the epic closes.
- [ ] Controls traced to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requirement ids.
- [ ] Automated checks (Semgrep rules, ZAP rules, RBAC assertion tests) merged and running in CI, not just documented.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted on this ticket and on the epic.

## Dependencies
- `E42-X01` — the model this review verifies.
- `E42-S03`, `E42-S04`, `E42-S05` and `E42-T02`, `E42-T03`, `E42-T04`, `E42-T08`, `E42-T09`, `E42-T10` — the implementation under review (E42-T08–T10 split from E42-T04 on 2026-10-15, R2 on #965).

## Branch
`chore/admin-screens-security-review` — findings and regression tests; fixes land on owning branches.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26 ADMIN (US-ADMIN-001..014)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §10 Admin (SCR-120..149), §11 global states (SCR-150..159)

- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `04-security-program.md`, `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register (E42, R3, S16–S17), §7 R3, §11 dependency graph

## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. AGENTS.md §0 (read-order) and §3 (how to pick up a ticket)
2. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`
3. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`

**Branch & PR**

- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-number-for-E42-X02>`

**Done means**

- Every Critical/High finding has a linked remediation ticket that is Done before the epic closes.
- Controls traced to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requirement ids.
- Automated checks (Semgrep rules, ZAP rules, RBAC assertion tests) merged and running in CI, not just documented.

**Do NOT**
- Do not widen an RBAC scope or auth boundary beyond what this ticket's Acceptance criteria require.

**If blocked**

- `E42-S03`, `E42-S04`, `E42-S05` and `E42-T02`, `E42-T03`, `E42-T04`, `E42-T08`, `E42-T09`, `E42-T10` — the implementation under review (E42-T08–T10 split from E42-T04 on 2026-10-15, R2 on #965).); move ticket Status → Blocked; never silently work around a failing gate or a missing dependency ticket.

title: Accessibility review, design QA and handoff for E43 security surfaces
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI and makes a11y default-on for every UI surface including RBAC-gated admin screens - "there is no 'internal tool, a11y doesn't matter' exception". E43 ships or changes three admin surfaces (SCR-137, SCR-128, SCR-136) plus two host-surface states (SCR-010, SCR-074). This ticket closes the design phase: an accessibility review of the hi-fi, a formal handoff package to engineering, and the design-QA pass performed against the built screens in Sprint 20/21.

It is scheduled in Sprint 19 for the review + handoff halves so E43-S01/S02 start Sprint 20 with a signed-off, annotated spec; the design-QA half executes against the build before E43-X07's evidence pack closes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Accessibility review** of every state in E43-D01 and E43-D02 against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: contrast ratios for all token pairs used, focus order diagrams, visible focus treatment, keyboard operability of every control including the disabled enable-control and the dismiss-with-reason dialog, screen-reader copy for badges/banners/verdicts, reduced-motion behaviour, and target sizes.
- **Handoff package**: annotated Figma frames with token names (not hex values), spacing/type references to `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`, a per-state data-binding table mapping each rendered field to its `SecuritySummary` / `audit_log` source, an interaction spec for step-up + typed confirmation, and an explicit empty/loading/error/stale matrix per screen.
- **Design-QA pass** (executed once E43-S01/S02 are on staging): built screens compared against spec for spacing, tokens, type, colour and states; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs with `priority/*` set and linked here.
- Sign-off record capturing CDO delegate, accessibility specialist and Security engineer.

## Out of scope
- Producing the designs themselves (E43-D01/D02); the automated axe-core audit run (E43-Q05 owns the executed audit); implementation.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every interactive control is keyboard reachable
  Given the annotated handoff package
  Then every control on SCR-137, SCR-128 and SCR-136 has a defined keyboard path, a visible focus treatment and a documented tab position
  And the disabled Live-enablement control has a documented programmatic description of why it is disabled

Scenario: Contrast passes at AA
  Given every token pair used in the E43 hi-fi
  Then each text/background pair meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast for its size class, recorded in a table on the ticket

Scenario: Design QA finds nothing unrecorded
  Given the built screens on staging
  When the design-QA pass is executed
  Then every discrepancy is either fixed in the same sprint or filed as a Bug linked to this ticket with a priority label
  And no discrepancy is closed by amending the design retroactively without a recorded decision

Scenario: Handoff is self-sufficient
  Given an engineer who has not attended any design review
  When they open the handoff package
  Then every rendered field names its data source and every state names its trigger condition
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data-binding table must reference real sources only: `SecuritySummary` fields from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `audit_log` / `audit_checkpoints` columns from `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, and feature-flag state from `feature_flags` / `feature_flag_overrides`.
- Screen-reader copy is specified as literal strings so engineering does not improvise accessible names for security verdicts.

## Test plan
- Manual screen-reader script (NVDA + VoiceOver) written here and reused verbatim by E43-Q05.
- Keyboard-only walkthrough script per screen.
- Contrast table computed from the token set.

## Security notes
The handoff must not embed any real credential, real user identity or real audit payload in example frames; use synthetic fixtures with an obvious dummy prefix (mirrors SR-145 for test fixtures). Accessible names must not leak information the visual design deliberately withholds.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility work for the epic's design phase: WCAG 2.2 AA across all states, manual screen-reader passes, focus management for dialogs, `role="status"` vs `role="alert"` decisions for verdict and integrity banners, and reduced-motion compliance.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Accessibility review recorded with the contrast table and focus-order diagrams.
- [ ] Handoff package published and linked; engineering (E43-S01/S02 owners) confirm it is sufficient in a comment.
- [ ] Design-QA pass executed against staging with pass/fail per screen; discrepancies fixed or filed.
- [ ] Sign-off comments from CDO delegate, accessibility specialist and Security engineer.
- [ ] Screen-reader scripts handed to QA for E43-Q05.

`design/e43-a11y-handoff`. PR size guidance: N/A - artefacts plus any Bug tickets filed.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:

title: Hi-fi designs for SCR-137/SCR-145 gate and SCR-074 hardened switch
body:
## Context
Turns the E44-D01 wireframes for the two admin gate surfaces and the environment switcher into token-accurate hi-fi designs that engineering can build from without asking questions. These are the screens where a mistake enables real-money trading, so the visual language must make "blocked" and "enabled" unmistakable and must make the enable action feel as heavy as it is.

Refs: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-074, SCR-137, SCR-145; `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` (tokens, density, theming).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames (light + dark, comfortable + compact density) for:
  - **SCR-145** feature-flag row for `trading.live_enabled`: disabled toggle with the blocking reason inline, the link to SCR-137, the step-up requirement indicator, and the enabled/rollback-available variants. Uses CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow, CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip, CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
  - **SCR-137** gate panel: four rows (Pen-test, Key-permission audit, Kill-switch test, Owner sign-off), each with machine-checked vs attested provenance, evidence link, attester + date, last-evaluated timestamp, and the all-clear state. Uses CMP-050 Card, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-028 Callout, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile.
  - **SCR-074** hardened switch: the LIVE path with typed confirmation + 2FA, the working-demo-orders statement, the transition progress, the 10 s post-switch banner, the gate-closed refusal, and the "owner hasn't enabled Live for your account" refusal. Uses CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog `variant="typed"`, CMP-074 EnvBanner, CMP-027 InlineError.
- Redlines: spacing, type scale, token names (`color.env.demo`, `color.env.live`, `color.status.success/danger`), focus rings, minimum hit targets.
- Greyscale and colour-vision-simulation exports proving the demo/live distinction survives without colour.
- Copy deck for every string, reviewed against risk R9 (no advice framing) and stating consequences in plain language.

## Out of scope
- SCR-010/SCR-075 chrome and SCR-122 eligibility (E44-D03 covers their hi-fi as part of the visual-language + handoff pass).
- Motion spec (E44-D03).
- Any change to the admin shell layout (E42).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Blocked state is unambiguous without colour
  Given the greyscale export of the SCR-145 gate row
  Then the blocked state is distinguishable from the enabled state by text and shape alone

Scenario: Every token is named
  When an engineer opens any frame's redline
  Then every colour, spacing and type value resolves to a token from docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md, with no raw hex or pixel value

Scenario: The enable action is heavy
  Then the SCR-145 enable path shows step-up, a typed confirmation, a mandatory reason field and a mandatory evidence URL field before the action becomes available
```

## Technical notes / design
The enable request body carries `value`, `reason` and `evidence_url` (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}`); the form must therefore require both text fields, and the design must show the `422 gate_evidence_required` error rendering.

## Test plan
N/A (design artefact); visual-regression baselines are produced later by the implementing stories.

## Security notes
No real evidence URLs or key material in frames.

## Accessibility notes
Contrast ≥4.5:1 for text and ≥3:1 for the focus ring and non-text status indicators; the typed-confirmation field has a visible label and format hint; error text is programmatically associated with its field.

## Performance notes

body:
## Context
The "pervasive live-mode visual language" is E44's most far-reaching design deliverable: it touches the shell (SCR-010), every trading-capable panel badge (SCR-075), the order confirmation (SCR-076, owned by E30 but re-specified here for its live variant) and the floating windows. It is the visual half of the safety invariant "Demo vs Live is never colour-only" (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5.1). This ticket also produces the SCR-122 live-eligibility hi-fi, the motion spec, the accessibility review and the engineering handoff for the whole epic.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Hi-fi live visual language**: SCR-010 chrome band LIVE variant; CMP-074 EnvBanner and CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal LIVE states; badge placement drawn for order ticket, group ticket, DOM ladder, positions grid, algo monitor, chart trading overlay and floating windows; the live variant of the order confirmation copy ("You are about to send a **LIVE** order") with "don't ask again" absent in live.
- **Hi-fi SCR-122 live eligibility**: demo-only, live-granted (with the audited grant note), revoked-with-open-positions showing reduce-only, and the acknowledgement-at-next-sign-in state (US-PAPER-007).
- **Motion spec**: the environment-switch transition (progress through closing → re-authenticating → resubscribing), the 10 s confirmation banner entry/exit, and the flag-propagation re-badge — all with a `prefers-reduced-motion` variant that degrades to instant state change with the same text announcements.
- **Accessibility design review** against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`: focus order for SCR-074 and the SCR-145 enable flow, live-region politeness levels (assertive for environment change, polite for flag propagation), accessible names that include the environment ("Order ticket - LIVE - Main"), and confirmation that the switch is unreachable by keyboard shortcut.
- **Engineering handoff package**: annotated frames, token map, component-prop mapping table (frame element → CMP-nnn prop), state machine diagram for the switch, and a written walkthrough session with the implementing frontend engineers recorded in the ticket.

## Out of scope
- Building anything (E44-S01..S04).
- Re-designing CMP-076 ConnectionStatus or the health tiles (E42/E04).
- Demo-side chrome, already shipped in E38.

```gherkin

  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set

```

The environment badge must be announced on every route change (SCR-010 a11y note), which is a shell-level live-region concern, not a per-screen one — the handoff must state that explicitly so it is implemented once.

The visual language is a safety control, not decoration: the handoff must state that removing or suppressing a badge is a `priority/p0-critical` defect.

This ticket *is* the a11y design review for the epic; its output is the checklist E44-Q03 audits against.

The chrome band is part of the app shell and must never remount on route change; badge state comes from one shared store subscription (SCR-075 performance note) — stated in the handoff.

N/A.

title: Contribute the conformance suite upstream
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** re-sprinted S10→S08.

Give back tests/xstate_contract patterns to upstream.

Runtime: xstate-statemachine==0.9.1 (tag v0.9.1 = 45bb7f3; wheel == tag 42/42; sha256 d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162; PEP 740 attested). There is no in-house shim and no dual runtime; this ticket builds directly on the library.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Upstream PR with library-generic contract tests

## Out of scope
- Anything beyond this ticket title

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Upstream PR opened
  Then a PR exists upstream with the suite and passes upstream CI
```

## Technical notes / design
- See 29 §1.7

FINAL mandatory config block (79-r14 §7, applied unconditionally by `statechart/factory.py`): `strict_config=True` + chart `"strictConfig": true`; recursive key walk (CV-C57); `actionErrorPolicy:"rollback"`; `guardErrorPolicy:"raise"` on order/control charts with an ordered unguarded auditing fall-through; `onUnhandled:"defer"` (control lane escalates via `CvErrorHooks`); `strictTargets:true`; `strict=True, event_schemas=CV_EVENT_SCHEMAS`; `max_queue_size=CV_INBOX_BOUND[lane], overflow_policy="refuse"`; `maxIterations` sized to the descent plateau (CV-C62); `service_pool_size` order 32 / control 8 / platform 16; injected `clock=`; plugins `[CvErrorHooks(), CvMetricsPlugin(), CvAuditPlugin()]` (restores pass `from_snapshot(plugins=...)`); `await asyncio.wait_for(interp.start(), CV_START_TIMEOUT)`; async `Interpreter` only (MUSTNOT-06).

## Test plan
- Self-verifying CI job
- Contract-suite membership: runs inside `tests/xstate_contract/` (or its lint/registry jobs) with `pytest -W error::RuntimeWarning`; both service spellings (`def`→coroutine and `async def`).

## Security notes
Library imported only via `candleviewer.statechart` (CV-LINT-IMPORT); pin is hash-locked and attestation-verified in CI (E50-T57). No secrets in machine context or snapshots.

## Accessibility notes
Not applicable: backend/tooling ticket with no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Per-tick rule evaluation stays plain code (BENCH-2: 381 ev/s vs 2,000 needed); nothing here touches the §3 hot-path exclusion list (CV-LINT-HOTPATH). Contract suite budget < 60 s.

## Observability
Failures surface through `CvErrorHooks` and `cv_machine_*` metrics (E50-T60); CI job output names the machine key and `machine_hash`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Merged and green
- [ ] CI green, including `tools/lint_statecharts.py` and `pytest tests/xstate_contract -W error::RuntimeWarning`
- [ ] Reviewed; docs in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` still accurate

`chore/e50-upstream-suite`
