title: Key-permission and RBAC-grant verification audit ahead of the pen-test
body:
## Context
R4 exit criterion 2 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 8.3) is unusually specific: *"every configured key on every account manually verified in **Bybit's own settings** (not merely trusted from app config) to have withdrawal OFF, IP whitelist limited to the Tailscale-reachable addresses, and trade+read scope only. The audit record includes the Bybit-reported scopes, not just the app's belief about them."* Section 13.5 repeats it as a live-enablement exit criterion, and `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` section 6 makes the key-permission audit one of the four gate items.

The roadmap schedules the audit as work item `s10` for **2027-02-19 to 2027-02-21**, deliberately in the first week of S22 so findings have a full week to be fixed before the 2027-02-25 gate. This ticket performs the **pre-test** half in S21 - verifying the demo/staging key estate and the grant model that the tester will probe - so the tester does not spend a day discovering a misconfigured key that we could have found ourselves. E44 owns the production key-permission audit *tooling*; this ticket owns the security verification act and the record.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Per-key verification record** for every key configured in the environments under test: Bybit-reported scopes from `GET /v5/user/query-api` (the authority), the app's stored belief, agreement or divergence, IP-whitelist contents versus the current egress address, key age versus the 90-day rotation policy, last successful use, and the UID the key resolves to.
- **Manual cross-check** in Bybit's own settings UI for at least the demo estate, with evidence captured - the requirement is explicitly that the exchange's own view is consulted, not only the API's answer.
- **Withdrawal assertion**: no key has withdrawal permission; any that does is disabled immediately and an incident note written (this is a standing invariant, not a preference).
- **IP whitelist assertion**: every key's whitelist is limited to the Tailscale-reachable addresses; record any drift (OQ-05 in section 16.1a acknowledges a home egress IP may change, with the documented decision to accept brief trading outage over removing the whitelist).
- **Scope assertion**: trade + read only; no unexpected permission (transfer, sub-account management) unless justified and recorded.
- **UID mapping record**: which credentials resolve to which UID - this matters because rate limits are per UID and shared across keys (SR-044a), so the audit record doubles as the input to E43-Q04's budget assertions.
- **RBAC grant audit**: for every user, the role and the account grants actually stored in `user_roles` and `user_account_access`, compared against the intended assignment; any orphaned grant, any user with more scope than intended, and any disabled user retaining a grant is corrected and audited.
- **2FA coverage check**: every trading-capable user has TOTP enrolled (SR-020); any exception is closed before the test.
- Results recorded in the audit record and surfaced through E43-S02's posture checks, so the same facts drive the panel and the gate.

## Out of scope
- The production (live) key audit itself, which happens in S22 against live keys as an R4 exit item with E44's tooling; this ticket verifies the estate under test and proves the procedure.
- Key rotation flows (E27); building the verification call (E27/E43-S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Exchange truth is recorded, not app belief
  Given every configured key in the environments under test
  Then the audit record contains the Bybit-reported scopes for each
  And any divergence between exchange-reported scopes and the app's stored belief is recorded and resolved

Scenario: No key carries withdrawal permission
  Given the audit
  When any key is found with withdrawal enabled
  Then that key is disabled immediately, an incident note is written, and the account is treated as compromised until the key is replaced

Scenario: Whitelists are correct or drift is recorded
  Given each key's IP whitelist
  Then it is limited to the Tailscale-reachable addresses
  And any drift from the current egress address is recorded with the remediation decision

Scenario: Grants match intent
  Given the stored role and account grants for every user
  Then each matches the intended assignment
  And any orphaned or excessive grant is removed and the removal is audited

Scenario: Every trading-capable user has 2FA
  Given the user list
  Then every user with any trading capability has TOTP enrolled
  And any exception is closed before the pen-test window opens

Scenario: The record feeds the panel and the gate
  Given the completed audit
  Then the same verdicts appear on SCR-137 and SCR-128
  And the key-permission gate item reflects the audit's completion date and attester
```

## Technical notes / design
- `GET /v5/user/query-api` is rate-limited at 10 req/s per UID and shares the UID's budget (SR-044b's table), so the audit sweep acquires from the per-UID tracker rather than bursting.
- The record's schema mirrors E43-S02's `Verdict` shape so the audit and the continuous checks are the same data, captured at different cadences.
- Manual cross-check evidence: screenshots of Bybit's key settings with the secret fields absent/masked, stored in the secure evidence store. Never capture a secret in evidence.
- Any disabled key triggers the existing `admin.key_marked_compromised` audited action rather than an out-of-band database edit.

## Test plan
- **Procedure verification**: perform the audit on the staging estate and confirm every field can be filled from real sources.
- **Integration**: the divergence case (app believes withdrawal off, exchange reports on) exercised against a recorded fixture and confirmed to produce a failing verdict and an alert.
- **Contract**: the audit record fields align with `SecuritySummary` so the panel and the record cannot disagree.
- Coverage target: N/A (procedure); the artefact is the record plus the fixes it triggers.

## Security notes
This is a crown-jewel control (assets A-01/A-02). Threats (`04-security-program.md` section 5.1): a key silently gaining withdrawal permission after registration; a whitelist removed to "fix" connectivity; a grant left behind after a role change. The audit is the compensating control for all three, and its value depends entirely on consulting the exchange rather than our own database. No secret material is ever read, displayed, exported or captured in evidence (SR-069, SR-005 family). Security review mandatory; the record is an input to the Owner's written sign-off.

## Accessibility notes
The audit's verdicts are rendered on SCR-128/SCR-137 by E43-S02 and are covered by E43-Q05; this ticket ensures every verdict has a text remediation string so the panel is not left with a status and no action.

## Performance notes
The sweep must not consume rate-limit budget needed by the order path; it runs off-peak and respects the SR-071 reserve.

## Observability
Metrics `cv_key_withdrawal_verified{key_id,state}`, `cv_key_whitelist_drift{key_id}`, `cv_key_age_days{key_id}`, `cv_grants_unexpected_total`, `cv_2fa_coverage_ratio`. Audit events for every correction made during the audit.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Per-key verification record complete for every key in the environments under test, including Bybit-reported scopes.
- [ ] Manual cross-check performed in Bybit's own settings with sanitised evidence stored.
- [ ] Zero keys with withdrawal permission; whitelists correct or drift recorded with decisions.
- [ ] UID mapping recorded and handed to E43-Q04.
- [ ] RBAC grant audit complete with corrections audited; 2FA coverage complete for trading-capable users.
- [ ] Verdicts visible on SCR-137/SCR-128 and reflected in the gate item.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off; record filed for the Owner's R4 sign-off.

## Dependencies
- **E43-S02** (posture checks and the verification call), **E43-T09** (grant model correctness), **E27** (key vault and key metadata).
- Feeds **E43-X02** (tester briefed on a verified estate), **E43-S01** (gate item), **E43-X07** (evidence pack).

## Branch
`chore/e43-key-permission-audit` (record and any corrective scripts; no secret material in the repository).

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 8.3 exit criterion 2, section 13 work item `s10`.
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` sections 6.1, 6.2, 5.1, 13.5, 16.1a (OQ-05), SR-020, SR-044b, SR-071.
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` section 6.
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` `api_keys`, `api_key_rotations`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access`.
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ACCT-003, US-ACCT-005, US-ADMIN-010.

## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. AGENTS.md §0 (read-order) and §3 (how to pick up a ticket)
2. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`
3. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md`
4. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`
5. `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`
6. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`
7. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `services/api/auth/` (module code), `packages/protocol/src/auth/` (protocol types if the contract changes)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- None beyond what is already named in this ticket's Technical notes / References.

**Commands**
- `ruff check .` (from `services/api/`)
- `mypy --strict .` (from `services/api/`)
- `pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85` (from `services/api/`)

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e43-key-permission-audit`
- PR title: `E43-X06: Key-permission and RBAC-grant verification audit ahead of the pen-test`
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-number-for-E43-X06>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/security @CandleViewer/backend @CandleViewer/architecture
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels (type/security, area/auth-rbac, priority/p0, security)

**Done means**
- Per-key verification record complete for every key in the environments under test, including Bybit-reported scopes.
- Manual cross-check performed in Bybit's own settings with sanitised evidence stored.
- Zero keys with withdrawal permission; whitelists correct or drift recorded with decisions.
- UID mapping recorded and handed to E43-Q04.
- RBAC grant audit complete with corrections audited; 2FA coverage complete for trading-capable users.

## Context

Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:

title: Author the live-gating black-box test plan and extend the E2E suite
body:
## Context
E44's failure modes are silent and expensive, so black-box coverage must be written from the *user's* claims (the Gherkin in `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-PAPER-002/003/007, US-ADMIN-007/010/012) rather than from the implementation. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a black-box plan plus E2E additions per feature.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Black-box test plan** covering every scenario of US-PAPER-002, US-PAPER-003, US-PAPER-007, US-ADMIN-012 and the gate scenarios of US-ADMIN-007/010, with explicit pass/fail steps, preconditions, fixture accounts and expected audit entries for each.
- **Exploratory charter** (2 × 90 min, timeboxed, session-notes format): "As a manager with demo-only access, try to reach a live account by any means available in the UI, the API and the WS" and "As an owner, try to enable live trading without satisfying the gate".
- **Playwright E2E additions** (web + Electron):
  1. Gate walkthrough: blocked with named outstanding items → attest each → enable with step-up + typed confirm + reason + evidence → verify propagation to a second session within 2 s.
  2. Switch walkthrough: demo → live (typed confirm + 2FA) → assert one-click disarmed, chrome and every panel badge changed, order confirmation restates LIVE with no "don't ask again" → place and cancel a confirmed order on the staging fixture → switch back.
  3. Eligibility walkthrough: owner grants live to a manager → manager acknowledges at next sign-in → manager switches → owner revokes while a position is open → manager's entries refused, reduce-only succeeds.
  4. Negative walkthrough: tampered client state attempting a cross-environment order; assert `403 environment_mismatch` and a high-severity audit entry.
  5. Emergency re-disable: live enabled → disable → new live orders refused within 2 s, reduce-only still works.


Tests must never enable live against a real live credential; the "live" fixture account is demo-backed but configured with `env='live'` in a dedicated staging database, which is exactly what the environment-separation work makes safe to do. title: Prove environment isolation and run gating perf, load and chaos scenarios
body:
## Context
R4 exit criterion 4 names a specific artefact: "a test asserts that no demo credential, cache entry, OMS row or storage partition can be read or written by a live-configured process and vice versa" (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §8.3). This ticket builds that suite and the accompanying performance and fault-injection coverage for the gating machinery.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Isolation assertion suite** (the criterion-4 artefact), covering all four named surfaces in both directions:
  1. *Credentials* — a live-configured process cannot resolve or decrypt a demo key handle, and vice versa.
  2. *Cache entries* — the OMS/flag/key caches refuse a key from the other environment; asserted by the programming-error test from E44-T02.
  3. *OMS rows* — a `cv_live` connection attempting any DML on a demo-schema table fails with a database permission error, and symmetrically.
  4. *Storage partitions* — the QuestDB namespace for one environment is unreadable by the other's writer/reader.
  The suite runs in CI on every PR touching M1/M14/M17 and is a required check.
- **Grant-assertion test** enumerating the actual Postgres grants of `cv_live`/`cv_demo` and failing on any unexpected privilege (drift detector).
- **Performance**: k6/Locust profile measuring order-path p95 with the environment + flag legs enabled vs a baseline build, asserting ≤1 ms added by the guard (E44-T03) and ≤2 ms added by the storage split (E44-T02); flag-propagation latency to 20 concurrent WS sessions asserting ≤2 s; environment-switch wall time asserting ≤2 s p95.
- **Chaos/fault scenarios** specific to gating:
  - Flag store unavailable at read time → the system must fail **closed** (treat live as disabled), never open.
  - `system` WS broadcast lost → a client that missed a disable must still be refused server-side on its next order.
  - Step-up service unavailable during an enable attempt → refusal, no partial enable.
  - Key-audit exchange call rate-limited (`10018`) → gate item becomes/stays outstanding rather than silently passing.
  - Process restart mid-switch → the session resolves to exactly one environment, never a hybrid.
  - Clock skew beyond `clock_block_threshold_ms` during a live-targeted order → refusal, consistent with the existing exchange guard.
- Results recorded against `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets and fed to the R4 PRR.

## Out of scope
- The broad chaos catalogue (WS disconnect storms, Postgres failover, disk-full, renderer crash) — **E45**.
- Functional black-box and E2E coverage (E44-Q01).
- Pen-testing (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Criterion 4 is proven in both directions
  When the isolation assertion suite runs
  Then every one of the four surfaces is asserted unreachable from the other environment in both directions
  And the suite is a required CI check on M1/M14/M17 changes

Scenario: The gating machinery fails closed
  Given the flag store is unavailable
  When a live-targeted order is submitted
  Then it is refused with live_trading_disabled, and the failure mode is recorded as fail-closed in the results

Scenario: Budgets hold
  Then the guard adds <=1 ms p95 to the order path, the storage split adds <=2 ms p95, flag propagation completes within 2 s to 20 sessions, and an environment switch completes within 2 s p95
  And any breach fails the ticket rather than being waived

Scenario: No hybrid state survives a restart
  Given a process is restarted while a session switch is in flight
  Then on reconnect the session reports exactly one environment and the client re-badges accordingly
```

## Technical notes / design
Fault injection uses the existing test harness hooks rather than production toggles. The fail-closed assertions are the most important output: each scenario's result is recorded explicitly as "failed closed" or "failed open", and any "failed open" is an automatic `priority/p0-critical` defect.

## Test plan
Self-describing; peer-reviewed by the second SDET and by the Architect for the fail-closed reasoning.

## Security notes
This suite is the evidence that the isolation control actually works; its results are attached to the Live-enablement gate's key evidence and reviewed in E44-X02. Any scenario that fails open is a release blocker.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; the order-path total risk-check overhead must remain ≤5 ms p95 (US-ADMIN-003 NFR) with E44's legs included.

## Observability
Verify that every refusal increments `cv_environment_mismatch_rejections_total` with the right reason label, and that the `cv_live_trading_enabled` gauge matches the stored flag after every scenario.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Isolation suite merged and wired as a required check.
- [ ] Grant-assertion drift test in CI.
- [ ] Perf results recorded against budgets; no breach.
- [ ] Every chaos scenario recorded as fail-closed; any fail-open filed as p0.
- [ ] Results package attached for the R4 PRR.

## Dependencies
E44-T02 (storage split), E44-T03 (guard), E44-T04 (flag/gate).

`test/e44-isolation-and-chaos`.

## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes WCAG 2.2 AA default-on for every UI surface including owner/admin screens — "there is no 'internal tool, a11y doesn't matter' exception". E44's surfaces carry the safety-critical demo/live distinction, which is precisely the kind of information that must not depend on colour or on sight.

This ticket also closes the epic's QA loop: the regression pack and the sign-off that `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires at epic level.

title: Build the live-enablement gate UI on SCR-137 and SCR-145
body:
## Context
Implements **US-ADMIN-012 Live-trading enablement gate** (Must) and the gate half of **US-ADMIN-007 Feature flags** (Must). The gate is the Owner's control surface for the most consequential switch in the product: until all four items of `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §6 are satisfied, the control must be disabled *and must say exactly which items are outstanding* — US-ADMIN-012's first scenario is explicit about that.

Screens: **SCR-137** Admin: security centre (`/admin/security`, the gate's source of truth) and **SCR-145** Admin: feature flags (`/admin/flags`, where the enable action lives). `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` already specifies SCR-145's validation rule: "`live_trading_enabled` cannot be turned on until the PRR/pen-test gate is satisfied — the toggle is disabled with the blocking reason and a link to SCR-137".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-137 gate panel**: renders `live_enablement_gate` from `GET /api/v1/admin/security/summary` as four rows (Pen-test, Key-permission audit, Kill-switch test, Owner sign-off), each showing provenance (machine-checked vs attested), status as text, evidence link, attester + date, and last-evaluated timestamp; plus the "Live enablement blocked" and all-clear states declared in the screen catalogue. Uses CMP-050 Card, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-028 Callout/Banner, CMP-175 KeyPermissionBadge, CMP-178 SystemHealthTile, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger.
- **Attestation flow**: recording the pen-test, kill-switch-test and Owner-sign-off attestations from SCR-137 — step-up gated, with a mandatory evidence URL and reason, and an explicit statement that attestations are append-only (a correction supersedes, never edits).
- **SCR-145 gate row** for `trading.live_enabled` via CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow + CMP-004 Toggle + CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip: disabled toggle with the blocking reason inline and a link to SCR-137 when the gate is closed; when open, the enable action requires step-up, a typed confirmation, a reason and an evidence URL, and surfaces `422 gate_evidence_required` / `403 step_up_required` inline.
- **Emergency re-disable** path on SCR-145 with its own confirmation copy stating that existing positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode (US-ADMIN-012 scenario 3).
- Live update: both screens re-render from the `system` WS topic when the flag or gate changes, within 2 s, without a reload.

## Out of scope
- Backend gate evaluation and the flag write path (E44-T04).
- The key-audit run itself (E44-T05) — this screen renders its latest result.
- Generic flag CRUD, flag history and the rest of SCR-145 (E42).
- The environment switcher (E44-S02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Gate closed lists exactly what is outstanding
  Given the pen-test attestation and the key-permission audit are outstanding
  When the owner opens SCR-145
  Then the trading.live_enabled toggle is disabled
  And the row names both outstanding items in text with a link to SCR-137
  And SCR-137 shows both rows as outstanding with their provenance and last-evaluated timestamp

Scenario: Gate open, enablement succeeds and is audited
  Given all four gate items are satisfied
  When the owner enables live with step-up, a typed confirmation, a reason and an evidence URL
  Then the toggle reflects enabled within 2 seconds in every open session
  And the audit entry for flag.changed records before/after, reason, evidence URL and actor

Scenario: Enablement attempted without evidence
  When the owner submits the enable form with an empty evidence URL
  Then the form blocks submission with a field-level error, and no request is sent

Scenario: Server-side refusal is surfaced honestly
  Given the client believes the gate is open but the server disagrees
  When the enable request returns 422 gate_evidence_required
  Then the outstanding item keys from the response are rendered inline and the toggle returns to disabled

Scenario: Emergency re-disable
  Given live trading is enabled
  When the owner disables it and confirms
  Then the confirmation copy states that new live orders stop and existing positions remain manageable in reduce-only mode
  And the change propagates to all sessions within 2 seconds

Scenario: A non-owner cannot see or act
  Given a manager opens /admin/flags
  Then the trading.live_enabled row is absent or read-only per RBAC, and no enable affordance is rendered
```

## Estimate re-check (2026-09-14)
Re-sized **5 -> 3** during the DoR sizing review. The surface is predominantly *read-only rendering* of the gate-status payload already computed server-side by E44-T04 (`GET /admin/security/summary`), mounted into admin chrome that E42 delivers (SCR-137/SCR-145 shells, table/panel primitives, step-up dialog from E09). The only genuinely new interactive element is one special-cased toggle with a reason + evidence-URL form, whose validation lives in T04. No new data fetching layer, no new component family, no new route. 3 points reflects "compose existing primitives over an existing payload"; the original 5 double-counted work that T04 owns.

## Technical notes / design
Data: `GET /api/v1/admin/security/summary` (gate + key-audit results), `GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags`, `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` with `{value, reason, evidence_url}`, `POST /api/v1/auth/step-up` for the elevated token. Live updates arrive on the `system` topic. The gate is read-only on SCR-145 (mirrored) and authoritative on SCR-137, per the E44-D01 IA note — the client must not compute gate satisfaction locally; it renders what the server says.

## Test plan
- Unit (RTL): each gate row state; blocked-toggle rendering; form validation; error mapping for 403/422.
- Contract: MSW handlers generated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Integration: WS-driven re-render on flag change within 2 s.
- E2E (Playwright, extended in E44-Q01): gate-blocked → attest → gate-open → enable → verify chrome change → re-disable.
- a11y: axe-core on both screens in both themes; manual screen-reader pass on the enable flow.
- Visual regression: blocked and enabled rows in both themes.
- Coverage ≥80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: a client-side-only gate check being bypassed (mitigated: the server is authoritative and the client never computes satisfaction); an evidence URL used as an injection vector (mitigated: rendered as text with a validated scheme allowlist, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`); RBAC leakage of gate details to non-owners (mitigated: the endpoint is `audit:read` owner-only and the UI renders nothing it did not receive). Data classification: security metadata. Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
Gate status is text, never colour alone; the disabled toggle exposes its blocking reason via `aria-describedby` rather than a tooltip only; the typed-confirmation field has a visible label and format hint; errors are announced assertively and associated with their field; the whole flow is keyboard-operable with a visible focus ring ≥3:1.

## Performance notes
Both screens render from cached server-computed findings (SCR-137 performance note: findings are computed server-side on a schedule; a manual re-scan is an explicit action with progress). Flag propagation to the UI ≤2 s (SCR-145 performance note).

## Observability
Analytics `security.centre_viewed`, `security.rescan_requested`; audited `flag.changed` and the attestation events come from the server. Client logs the correlation id of a failed enable attempt.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All AC scenarios pass via automated tests or a recorded manual QA step.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E44-D04) passed; Storybook entries for the gate row states added.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; docs updated if behaviour diverged.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted; demoed at Sprint Review against staging.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded: this UI is itself gated by `admin.feature_flags_ui`.

## Dependencies
E44-D03 (handoff), E44-T04 (gate + flag API), E42 (SCR-137/SCR-145 shells), E09 (step-up).

## Branch
`feat/e44-gate-ui`.

## References
- docs/plan/11-user-stories.md US-ADMIN-007, US-ADMIN-012
- docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-137, SCR-145
- docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md CMP-004/028/036/050/087/093/095/175/178/179
- docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md §6

## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. AGENTS.md §0 (read-order) and §3 (how to pick up a ticket)

title: Harden the Demo to Live switch on SCR-074 with gate, step-up and disarm
body:
## Context
Implements the **live half of US-PAPER-002 Explicit Demo↔Live switching** (Must). E38 shipped the switcher for demo; E44 hardens the path *into* live so that, per the story, "switching to Live requires typing a confirmation phrase and passing step-up authentication, and one-click trading is disarmed on switch", and "no hotkey can change the environment; it requires a deliberate click".

Screen **SCR-074** (Environment switcher) already specifies the transition contract: the client tears down and re-establishes every private subscription, order entry is blocked for the whole transition (typically ≤2 s), and a half-switched state is never reachable.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The LIVE path of SCR-074: typed confirmation (`ConfirmDialog variant="typed"`, must type `LIVE`) + 2FA/step-up, the list of working demo orders with the statement that they stay on demo and are not migrated, and the Live accounts available list.
- **New gate-closed state**: when `trading.live_enabled` is OFF, the switch to LIVE is unavailable with the reason and a link to SCR-137 for owners (non-owners see the plain refusal, not the gate internals).
- **Not-permitted state**: "The owner hasn't enabled Live for your account." driven by `allowed_environments` from `GET /auth/session` / WS `auth_ok` (US-PAPER-007).
- **Transition orchestration**: close private subscriptions → call `POST /api/v1/session/environment` with the step-up token → re-authenticate the WS → resubscribe; order entry disabled for the whole transition with the progress states drawn in the design; failure returns to the previous environment with the reason and no partial state.
- **One-click disarm on switch**: CMP-229 ArmToggle is forced to disarmed on any environment change, and cannot be re-armed within the transition.
- **Hotkey prohibition**: a test asserts the switch action is not registered in the hotkey map and cannot be triggered by any key binding (SCR-074: "deliberately not bindable to a hotkey; the control is click-only").
- Post-switch: a full-width confirmation banner for 10 s; the chrome and all badges re-render together (E44-S03 owns the badges themselves).

## Out of scope
- The demo-direction switch (E38, already shipped) beyond regression coverage.
- The badge/chrome visual language (E44-S03).
- Backend environment switching, the guard and the flag (E44-T03/T04).
- Blocking the switch while an algo or trade group is running is drawn in design and enforced here as a client-side precondition; the authoritative server refusal lives in E44-T03.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Switching to live requires typed confirmation and step-up
  Given the gate is open and the user is permitted live
  When the user opens SCR-074 and selects LIVE
  Then the switch button stays disabled until the exact word LIVE is typed and a valid 2FA code is supplied
  And on success POST /api/v1/session/environment is called with the step-up token

Scenario: One-click is disarmed by the switch
  Given one-click trading is armed in demo
  When the environment switches to live
  Then one-click is disarmed, and the arm control cannot be re-armed until the transition completes

Scenario: No hotkey can switch environment
  When every registered hotkey is exercised
  Then none triggers an environment change, asserted by a test over the hotkey registry

Scenario: Gate closed blocks the switch
  Given trading.live_enabled is OFF
  Then the LIVE option is unavailable with the reason stated, and owners see a link to SCR-137

Scenario: A failed switch leaves no partial state
  Given POST /api/v1/session/environment returns 403 live_trading_disabled mid-transition
  Then the session remains in demo, private subscriptions are restored, order entry is re-enabled, and the reason is shown
  And no panel is left displaying a live badge

Scenario: Switching is blocked while an algo or trade group is running
  Given a running emulated algo
  When the user attempts to switch
  Then the switch is refused with the running items listed by name
```

## Technical notes / design
Transition is a client state machine (`idle → confirming → closing_subscriptions → authenticating → resubscribing → done|failed`) with a single owner in the session store; every trading surface reads `activeEnv` from that one store subscription so a half-switched render is impossible. The step-up token is single-scope and 5-minute lived (SCR-014); it is never persisted. On `403 step_up_required` the flow re-opens the step-up modal rather than failing outright.

## Test plan
- Unit (RTL): each transition state; typed-confirm gating; disarm-on-switch; error mapping for 403 `live_trading_disabled` / `step_up_required` / not-permitted.
- Hotkey-registry test asserting no binding maps to the switch.
- Integration: subscription teardown/resubscribe ordering against a mock WS; assert order entry is disabled throughout.
- E2E (E44-Q01): demo → live → place a confirmed live order against the demo-backed staging fixture → switch back.
- a11y: assertive announcement of the environment change; focus trap in the dialog; axe-core green.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
Threats: an attacker-triggered environment change via CSRF or a crafted deep link (mitigated: step-up token required, POST with CSRF protection, no URL-triggered switch); a stale client continuing to act as live after a server-side revocation (mitigated: the server is authoritative on every request via E44-T03, and `system`/`auth_ok` refresh `allowed_environments`). Data classification: financial data. Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
The environment change is announced assertively; the dialog is `role="alertdialog"` with the action named in its accessible description; the typed-confirmation field has a visible label; the transition progress is a live region so a screen-reader user knows order entry is blocked; no colour-only signalling.

## Performance notes
The whole transition completes in ≤2 s p95 including teardown and resubscribe (SCR-074 performance note); order entry is blocked for the duration rather than racing.

## Observability
Audit `session.environment_switched` (high severity, server-side). Client metric `cv_ui_environment_switch_seconds` and an analytics event for abandoned switches.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All AC scenarios automated or covered by a recorded QA step.
- [ ] Hotkey-prohibition test in CI.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E44-D04) passed.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; QA sign-off; demoed at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
E44-D03 (handoff + motion), E44-T04 (flag/gate), E44-T03 (server guard and refusal codes), E38 (existing switcher), E09 (step-up).

title: Ship the pervasive live-mode visual language and confirm-on-every-order default
body:
## Context
Implements the visual-distinction scenario of **US-PAPER-002** ("a persistent accent and a text badge mark every trading-capable surface, and the badge is never colour-only"), the gated-surfaces scenario of **US-PAPER-003**, and the roadmap's E44 scope line "pervasive live-mode visual language (colour, badge, confirm-on-every-order default)".

Screens **SCR-010** (app shell chrome), **SCR-075** (Demo/Live banner & per-panel badges) and the live variant of **SCR-076** (order confirmation). `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5.1 states the invariant plainly: "Demo vs Live is never colour-only… every trading-capable surface repeats the badge locally".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-074 EnvBanner** live variant in the SCR-010 shell: text `LIVE` + icon + pattern, `role="status"`, announced on every route change, never remounted on navigation.
- **CMP-075 EnvBadgeLocal** applied to every trading-capable panel: order ticket, group ticket, DOM ladder, positions grid, algo monitor, chart trading overlay, and repeated in floating windows; every such panel's accessible name includes the environment ("Order ticket - LIVE - Main").
- **CMP-139 EnvironmentAwareOrderGuard** wired around the order ticket and DOM click-to-trade handlers as client-side defence in depth: a mismatch renders the control disabled-with-reason (never silently rerouted), matching the server refusal from E44-T03.
- **Confirm-on-every-order in live**: `confirm_market_orders` and the order-confirmation modal default ON in live; "don't ask again" is available in demo only and absent in live (SCR-076 design checklist); the confirmation copy restates the environment ("You are about to send a **LIVE** order").
- **Gated surfaces**: order ticket, DOM click-to-trade, chart trading, positions actions and rule arming all reflect the current environment and refuse cross-environment actions in the UI, with the reason shown.
- A **catalogue-level test** asserting that every screen listed as trading-capable renders an environment badge — the same pattern already used for CMP-227's "(estimated)" contract.

## Out of scope
- The switcher itself (E44-S02) and the gate UI (E44-S01).
- Redesigning the order ticket, ladder or positions grid (E30/E21/E29).
- Server-side enforcement (E44-T03) — this story is the client half and must never be the only barrier.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every trading-capable surface is badged in live
  Given the session environment is live
  When the catalogue-level badge test runs over every trading-capable screen
  Then each renders an environment badge whose accessible name contains LIVE
  And a missing badge fails the build

Scenario: The distinction survives without colour
  Given the app is rendered in greyscale and in all three colour-vision simulations
  Then DEMO and LIVE chrome remain distinguishable by text, icon and pattern

Scenario: Confirmation cannot be silenced in live
  Given the session is live
  When the order confirmation modal appears
  Then no "don't ask again" affordance is present, and the copy restates LIVE, the account and the full order

Scenario: A mismatched order is blocked client-side with a reason
  Given the active environment is demo and a control targets a live account
  Then CMP-139 renders the control disabled with the reason stated, and no request is sent

Scenario: The banner is never lost
  Given the user navigates between routes and opens a modal
  Then the banner is never scrolled away, covered by the modal, or remounted, and floating windows repeat it
```

## Technical notes / design
`activeEnv` comes from the single session store subscription established in E44-S02; `orderEnv` derives from the target account's `env` (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-139 data contract). The shell-level route-change announcement is implemented once in the shell, not per screen (E44-D03 handoff note). Confirmation defaults come from the trading settings block in `GET /me/settings` (`trading.confirm_market_orders`, `default_environment`) with the live override applied client-side *and* asserted server-side.

## Test plan
- Unit (RTL): banner and badge rendering per environment; CMP-139 matched/mismatched; confirmation default resolution per environment.
- Catalogue test: iterate the trading-capable screen list and assert badge presence and accessible name.
- Visual regression: CMP-074 in both states at every theme (mandated by `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-074 tests), plus greyscale exports.
- Integration: CMP-139 attempts a live order while env=demo and asserts a hard block plus the audit entry (the component's mandated test).
- a11y: axe-core across the shell and each badged panel; manual screen-reader pass verifying the badge is announced on route change without being re-announced on every panel re-render (CMP-075 contract).
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
This is a safety control, not decoration: suppressing or failing to render a badge is a `priority/p0-critical` defect. Threats: a user misreading the environment and submitting a live order believing it was demo (mitigated: text+icon+pattern, per-panel repetition, mandatory confirmation); client-side-only guarding being trusted (mitigated: E44-T03 is authoritative and the mismatch test asserts the server also refuses). Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
Text always rendered, never icon/colour alone; `role="status"` for the banner and `role="img"` with a static label for the local badge so it is not re-announced on every re-render; contrast ≥4.5:1 in both themes; the distinction is verified in greyscale.

## Performance notes
The band is part of the app shell and never remounts on route change; badge state comes from one shared store subscription (SCR-075 performance note). Adding the badges must not regress panel render time measurably (<1 ms per panel).

## Observability
No analytics of its own (SCR-075 is presentational); the environment value is included in every trading audit record server-side. Add a client-side assertion metric `cv_ui_missing_env_badge_total` that should always be zero and alerts if it ever increments.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All AC scenarios automated; catalogue badge test in CI.
- [ ] Visual-regression baselines for CMP-074/075 in both states and themes.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] Design QA (E44-D04) passed; Storybook entries updated.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; QA sign-off; demoed at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
E44-D03 (visual language + badge placement sheet), E44-T03 (server refusal semantics the client mirrors), E30/E21 (the panels being badged), E38 (demo-side chrome already shipped).

`feat/e44-live-visual-language`.

title: Implement per-manager live eligibility with audited grant and revocation
body:
## Context
Implements **US-PAPER-007 Demo eligibility per manager** (Should). Its NFR is the design constraint: "eligibility is a server-side attribute of the user-account binding" — not a client preference, not a role. This is what lets a new manager start demo-only and be promoted deliberately, and what makes revocation safe for someone holding open live positions.

Screens: **SCR-122** Admin: user detail / edit (the owner's control) and **SCR-074** (the manager's experience of the restriction, already stubbed in E44-S02's not-permitted state).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Backend: a `live_enabled` attribute on the user↔account binding (the binding model from US-ADMIN-002, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14 account scope), default OFF for every new binding; migration included. It feeds `allowed_environments` on `GET /auth/session` and the WS `auth_ok` frame, and is one of the facts the E44-T03 guard checks.
- Owner UI on SCR-122: grant/revoke live per binding, step-up gated, with the audited grant recorded (actor, target user, account, before/after).
- **Acknowledgement at next sign-in**: when live access is granted, the manager must acknowledge the change at their next sign-in before live becomes selectable; the acknowledgement is recorded with its timestamp.
- **Revocation with open positions**: revoking while the manager holds live positions must not force-close anything — new entries are refused while reduce-only actions remain available, and both the owner and the manager are informed (mirrors the US-ADMIN-003 tighten-during-open-position pattern).
- Manager-side rendering: the Live switch is disabled with the reason shown (not silently absent), and no live account is selectable.

## Out of scope
- Roles, bindings CRUD and the rest of SCR-122 (E42 / US-ADMIN-002).
- Risk caps (E39 / US-ADMIN-003).
- The global gate — a grant is meaningless while `trading.live_enabled` is OFF, and the UI must say so.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A new binding is demo-only by default
  When the owner binds a manager to a sub-account
  Then live_enabled is false, no live account is selectable for that manager, and the Live switch is disabled with the reason shown

Scenario: Promotion requires acknowledgement
  Given the owner grants live access with step-up
  Then the grant is audited with before/after
  And at the manager's next sign-in they must acknowledge the change before live becomes selectable, and the acknowledgement is recorded

Scenario: Revocation with open live positions
  Given a manager holds an open live position
  When the owner revokes live access
  Then no position is force-closed
  And new live entries are refused with a stated reason while reduce-only actions still succeed
  And both the owner and the manager are informed

Scenario: The grant cannot be forged client-side
  Given a manager tampers with the client to select a live account
  When any trading request is made
  Then the server refuses with 403 and the attempt is audited as high severity

Scenario: Grant is inert while the global gate is closed
  Given trading.live_enabled is OFF
  Then a granted manager still cannot switch to live, and the UI states that the deployment-level gate is closed rather than blaming their permissions
```

## Technical notes / design
No new permission is introduced (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14 explicitly rejects splitting live into its own permission); `live_enabled` is an attribute of the binding consumed by the existing environment leg of the 4-tuple. `allowed_environments` = deployment `environment_allowlist` ∩ per-binding eligibility ∩ flag state, computed server-side only. Reduce-only enforcement reuses the OMS intent classification from E29.

## Test plan
- Unit: eligibility resolution truth table (allowlist × binding × flag); acknowledgement state machine.
- Contract: `allowed_environments` identical between `GET /auth/session` and WS `auth_ok`.
- Integration: grant → acknowledge → switch; revoke-with-open-position → reduce-only still permitted, entry refused; tampered client refused and audited.
- E2E (E44-Q01): owner grants, manager acknowledges and switches.
- a11y: axe-core on SCR-122 control and the disabled-with-reason state.
- Coverage ≥90% backend, ≥80% frontend.

## Security notes
Threats: elevation of privilege (a manager granting themselves live — mitigated: owner-only + step-up + audit); repudiation of a grant (mitigated: audited with before/after and actor); a revoked manager continuing to trade on a cached session (mitigated: eligibility is re-evaluated server-side per request and pushed on the `system` topic). Data classification: financial data + access control. Security review required.

## Accessibility notes
The disabled Live switch exposes its reason via `aria-describedby`; the acknowledgement dialog is `role="alertdialog"` with the change stated in plain language; the grant/revoke controls are labelled with the target user and account, not just "on/off".

## Performance notes
Eligibility resolution is in-memory on the request path; ≤0.5 ms p95, inside the ≤5 ms total risk-check budget.

## Observability
Audit: a grant/revoke event with before/after (reusing the `user.role_assigned`-class vocabulary extended for bindings), plus the acknowledgement. Metric `cv_live_eligible_bindings` gauge.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Binding attribute, migration, API and UI implemented; all AC scenarios automated.
- [ ] `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14 and `21-database-schema.md` updated.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader spot-check.
- [ ] Design QA (E44-D04) passed.
- [ ] Coverage targets met; QA sign-off; Security review comment; demoed at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
E44-D03 (SCR-122 hi-fi), E44-T03 (the guard that enforces eligibility), E42/US-ADMIN-002 (bindings), E09 (step-up), E29 (reduce-only intent).

## Branch

title: Write ADR-0016 environment separation and update the affected plan docs

## Context
`docs/plan/27-adrs/` currently ends at ADR-0015. The environment-separation mechanism chosen in E44-K01 and implemented in E44-T02 is exactly the kind of decision the ADR set exists for: it constrains every future storage, migration and backup decision, and a future engineer must be able to see why application-level filtering was rejected.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Update `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md` index.
- Update `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` with the schema/grant layout and the migration-drift check.

title: Security review and abuse-case verification of the live gate and isolation
body:
## Context
The final security gate on E44 before its evidence feeds the R4 Live-enablement gate (`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §6). `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes a Security engineer review mandatory for anything touching `area/oms-execution` order paths, key handling or RBAC — E44 is all three.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box review** of the merged E44 code: `authorize()`'s environment and flag legs (E44-T03), the flag write path and gate evaluation (E44-T04), the key-audit tool's redaction and record integrity (E44-T05), the config validators and startup self-check (E44-T01), and the grant model from the storage split (E44-T02).
- **Abuse-case execution** against staging, from the E44-X01 charters, at minimum:
  1. Attempt a live order from a demo session by tampering with every client-controlled input (session store, request body, WS `sub` options).
  2. Attempt to enable `trading.live_enabled` without step-up, without evidence, and by direct database write (the latter must be detected by the flag-vs-audit reconciliation).
  3. Attempt to forge or edit a key-audit pass record and an attestation.
  4. Attempt to read gate details and key scopes as a manager and as a viewer.
  5. Attempt to grant yourself live eligibility as a manager.
  6. Grep the entire log stream, the audit export and the key-audit JSON artefact for key material.
- **SAST/DAST rule additions**: a Semgrep rule forbidding direct reads of the environment from anywhere but `EnvironmentContext`; a rule forbidding `SET ROLE` / cross-schema qualified names in application code; a ZAP profile exercising the enable endpoint and the environment-switch endpoint for authz bypass and CSRF.
- **Key/permission verification**: confirm every configured key's Bybit-reported scopes against the E44-T05 record, independently of the tool's own claim, for the audit record required by the R4 gate.
- **Findings triage**: Critical/High must be fixed and re-verified within E44; Medium/Low fixed or risk-accepted in writing by the Owner with an expiry date in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.
- A **sign-off comment** on E44 stating the review scope, the abuse cases executed, findings and their disposition.

## Out of scope
- The independent pen-test (E43) — this review is internal and precedes it; its findings scope the pen-test.
- Remediation of findings outside E44's code (filed to the owning epic).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every abuse case is executed and recorded
  When the review completes
  Then each of the six abuse cases has a recorded outcome with evidence, and every one that succeeded is filed as a finding

Scenario: No key material anywhere
  When the log stream, audit export and key-audit artefact are searched for key material
  Then no secret or full key identifier is found, evidenced by the search transcript

Scenario: A direct database flag flip is detected
  Given trading.live_enabled is set to true by a direct database write
  When the flag-vs-audit reconciliation runs
  Then the discrepancy is detected and raised as a high-severity security event

Scenario: Findings are dispositioned
  Then no Critical or High finding remains open, and every Medium/Low is fixed or risk-accepted in writing with an expiry date in the risk register
```

## Technical notes / design
Run against staging with fixture accounts; the key-scope verification is the only part that touches real key metadata and is performed by the Security engineer with the Owner present, producing the audit record the R4 gate requires.

## Test plan
Abuse cases are executed manually and, where they are cheap to automate, promoted into E44-Q01's negative walkthrough so they regress forever.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security review of record for E44. Data classification: secrets (handled read-only, never copied), financial data, access control.

## Accessibility notes
N/A.

## Performance notes
Confirm no control added during remediation pushes the order-path risk-check overhead past the ≤5 ms p95 budget.

## Observability
Verify every abuse attempt produced the expected high-severity audit entry and metric increment — a successful attack that leaves no trace is itself a finding.

- [ ] All six abuse cases executed with recorded evidence.

title: Reconciliation, chaos & failover resilience
body:
## Context
R4 adds almost no features; **its product is assurance** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` #8). E45 proves the third R4 goal - *"prove resilience: reconnect, reconcile, fail over and roll back, under fault injection, without inventing or losing an order"* - and owns R4 exit criteria 5 (chaos suite green), 6 (rollback rehearsal) and 7 (restore drill).

Two bodies of already-specified design converge here; this epic is their **implementation and proof**:

1. **Reconciliation.** The algorithm is fully specified in `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` section 8.5 (`reconcile(account, gap_from) -> ReconcileReport`), the state machine including `Unknown` in section 8.3 and `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0006-oms-state-machine.md`, and the operational shape in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.5 (`Reconciler`: startup, reconnect, every 30 s). Security requirement **SR-058** (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md`) makes it mandatory. US-POS-008 is the user-visible contract. E29 shipped the *reactive* reconnect UX (E29-S07); E45 ships the **complete, scheduled, multi-dimension reconciler** (orders, executions, positions, balances, trade groups), its persisted report, its admin surface and the manual resolution of `untracked` orders and position drift.
2. **Chaos and failover.** The scenario catalogue lives in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 9, with the private-WS reconnect sequence asserted step-by-step in section 9.1. **SR-154** requires chaos coverage of WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, `10006`/`10018`, clock drift, DB unavailability and disk-full, asserting the system *fails closed on the order path* while risk-reducing actions still work. `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 11 enumerates failure modes F1-F9 with expected detection, degradation and recovery, and an **RTO of <=90 s** from backend restart to fully reconciled trading.

The user-story domain is **OBS** (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` section 28): **US-OBS-006** (chaos and failure drills) is this epic's headline Must; **US-OBS-004** (alerting on reconciliation divergence) and **US-OBS-007** (support bundle as a drill artefact) are touched at their reconciliation/drill edges, their base implementation having been delivered by E04.

Why R4 and not earlier: chaos needs the *whole* order path to exist (E29 OMS, E32 native SL, E34 fan-out, E39 kill-switch) and needs the environment boundary (E44) so drills can run against a live-shaped deployment without touching real money.

Backend modules: **M4** (Bybit REST/WS adapter, rate governor) and **M14** (OMS, reconciler, kill-switch integration) per `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`.

## Goal
Make every injected fault end in a **reconciled, correct state**: no orphaned orders, no duplicate submissions, no position the system is unaware of, no position without a native stop - and prove it with an automated, repeatable suite plus a rehearsed rollback and a rehearsed restore.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Reconciliation service (M14)** - `candleviewer.oms.reconciler`: the section 8.5 algorithm implemented in full (executions applied first, diff by `order_link_id`, resolution from order history, `Unknown` two-pass abandonment with `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`, adoption of `untracked` exchange orders, position-drift detection, native-SL invariant repair), driven on **startup**, **private-WS reconnect**, a **30 s timer** and **on demand**.
- **Balance and trade-group reconciliation** - wallet snapshot diffing and trade-group leg re-binding, including legs adopted as `untracked`.
- **Persisted reports** - `ReconcileReport` rows, the `oms.reconcile` audit event, `order_events.source='reconcile'` with `kind='reconcile_diff'`, `position_snapshots.reason='rest_reconcile'`, and the `orders.last_reconciled_at` / `positions.last_reconciled_at` watermarks (tables per `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`).
- **Stale-account lockout** - two minutes of repeated reconciliation failure marks the account stale and disables order entry for it (US-POS-008 scenario 3).
- **Dead-man's-switch policy** - `POST /v5/order/disconnected-cancel-all` integration behind an **explicit opt-in**, correctly documented as `inverse`-only on Bybit, so the local kill-switch (`POST /api/v1/trading/kill-switch`, E39) remains the operative control for USDT linear perps.
- **Chaos harness** - fault-injection framework over the fixture-replay mock exchange plus container, network, clock and disk faults, wired as the CI `@chaos` job (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 9) and runnable as a staging game-day.
- **Chaos scenario catalogue** - WS disconnect storms (public and private), sequence gaps, exchange 5xx and 403, `10018` floods, Postgres failover, QuestDB unavailability, disk-full, clock skew (`10002`), partial fan-out failure and Electron renderer crash mid-order.
- **Rollback rehearsal automation** and **restore drill automation** (Postgres and the Parquet cold tier), each producing a timed, archived report.
- **Admin surfaces** - reconciliation status and discrepancy resolution on **SCR-143** (system health) and **SCR-144** (incident / connectivity log), plus the untracked-order and position-drift resolution flow.
- Design (D), QA (Q) and Security (X) tickets carrying their own points.

**User stories covered:** US-OBS-006 (Must, primary), US-OBS-004 (reconciliation-divergence alerting edge), US-OBS-007 (drill/incident bundle edge), US-POS-008 (completion of the reconciliation contract begun in E29).

## Out of scope
- The observability baseline itself (metrics, logs, alert routing, dashboards, `/metrics`) - **E04**.
- The pen-test and its remediation - **E43**.
- Environment separation, the live feature flag and the live gate - **E44**.
- Kill-switch engine and risk caps - **E39** (E45 only *exercises* them).
- Performance budget enforcement and load testing - **E46**.
- Backup *scheduling* and the backups screen (SCR-146) - E42/E04; E45 adds only the **drill automation** on top.
- Any new exchange; Bybit USDT linear perpetuals only.

## Points baseline vs roadmap

`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` line 145 registers **E45 = 47 pts**. This backlog file totals **72 pts** across all children. The two numbers measure different things and both are correct:

| Bucket | Tickets | Pts |
|---|---|---|
| Engineering (dev-discipline: `K`, `T`, `S`) | K01, T01-T11, S01, S02 | **50** |
| Design overhead (`D`) | D01, D02, D03 | 8 |
| QA overhead (`Q`) | Q01, Q02, Q03 | 9 |
| Security overhead (`X`) | X01, X02 | 5 |
| **Total (epic `estimate`)** | 23 children | **72** |

The roadmap register counts **engineering-discipline points only** - the work drawn against the ~90 pts/sprint engineering capacity in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` section 3. Design, QA and security are staffed from the separate UI/UX org, the 2 QA/SDET and the 1 Security engineer, and are *not* charged to the engineering budget; that is why the R4 capacity table in `30-release-roadmap.md` section 3.1 allocates 144 pts to E43+E44+E45 rather than their summed child totals. The same convention holds backlog-wide (e.g. E11: 89 registered / 89 engineering / 154 total; E21: 55 / 55 / 112).

**Variance against the registered baseline: 50 vs 47 = +6.4 %, inside the +/-15 % DoR tolerance.** No re-baselining or splitting is required, and the roadmap figure is not stale. The epic `estimate` field remains 72 because the DoR requires an epic estimate to be the sum of its children; readers comparing against the roadmap must use the engineering row.

## Exit criteria
1. Reconciliation runs on startup, on every private-WS reconnect, every 30 s and on demand, for every configured account, within the `poll` rate bucket, and is **idempotent** (a second immediate run produces an empty report).
2. Every chaos scenario in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 9 passes in CI, and a full staging game-day pass is recorded and signed off by QA.
3. `oms_unknown_orders` returns to 0 after every drill; the alert (>0 for 60 s) has been test-fired and received.
4. No drill produces a duplicate order for any `order_link_id`, an unprotected open position, or a position absent from local state.
5. Rollback rehearsal executed on staging and timed; restore drill executed for Postgres and one symbol's Parquet history, with time-to-restore recorded.
6. The dead-man's-switch policy is documented, opt-in, and its `linear`-unavailability is stated in the runbook and in the UI.
7. STRIDE model complete and reviewed; a11y audit clean on the new admin surfaces; design signed off at least two sprints before the consuming FE story.

## Story list
| Key | Kind | Title | Pts |
|---|---|---|---|
| E45-K01 | Spike | Choose the fault-injection mechanism for the chaos harness | 2 |
| E45-T01 | Task | Implement the reconciliation core over orders, executions and positions | 5 |
| E45-T02 | Task | Drive reconciliation from startup, reconnect, timer and on demand; stale-account lockout | 3 |
| E45-T03 | Task | Persist, expose and instrument the reconciliation report | 3 |
| E45-T04 | Task | Reconcile wallet balances and trade-group legs | 3 |
| E45-T05 | Task | Dead-man's-switch integration with an explicit opt-in policy | 3 |
| E45-T06 | Task | Build the chaos harness and the CI @chaos job | 5 |
| E45-T07 | Task | Chaos catalogue part 1 - exchange and transport faults | 5 |
| E45-T08 | Task | Chaos catalogue part 2 - infrastructure, clock and client faults | 5 |
| E45-T09 | Task | Automate the rollback rehearsal | 3 |
| E45-T10 | Task | Automate the Postgres and Parquet restore drills | 3 |
| E45-S01 | Story | Resolve untracked orders and position drift from the admin UI | 5 |
| E45-S02 | Story | Surface reconciliation and drill state on SCR-143 and SCR-144 | 3 |
| E45-T11 | Task | Write the resilience runbooks and record ADR-0016 | 2 |
| E45-D01 | Task | Wireframe the reconciliation and drill surfaces | 3 |
| E45-D02 | Task | Hi-fi designs and handoff for the discrepancy resolution flow | 3 |
| E45-D03 | Task | Design QA and accessibility review of the shipped surfaces | 2 |
| E45-Q01 | Task | Black-box test plan for reconciliation and the drills | 3 |
| E45-Q02 | Task | Chaos game-day execution and exploratory charter | 3 |
| E45-Q03 | Task | E2E additions, regression pack and QA sign-off | 3 |
| E45-X01 | Task | STRIDE threat model for reconciliation, chaos and failover | 2 |
| E45-X02 | Task | Security review, abuse cases and detection rules | 3 |

Engineering total **48 pts** (budget 47, within +-15%); design 8, QA 9, security 5 tracked separately. Epic estimate 72 = sum of all children.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Chaos suite is green before the R4 gate
  Given every scenario in docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md section 9 is automated
  When the @chaos CI job runs on the release candidate
  Then every scenario passes and the run report is archived as a release artefact

Scenario: A drill leaves no uncertainty behind
  Given the private WS is dropped mid-order-lifecycle during a drill
  When reconciliation completes after reconnect
  Then oms_unknown_orders returns to 0, no order_link_id maps to two exchange orders, and every open position carries a native stop

Scenario: An unresolvable failure blocks the gate
  Given any chaos scenario ends with an orphaned order or an unprotected position
  Then the R4 gate is blocked, a risk-register entry is opened, and the epic cannot be closed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Reconciler module: `apps/backend/src/candleviewer/oms/reconciler.py`, matching the `Reconciler` component of `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 3.5 and running in the `oms` TaskGroup (section 7 process model) as one task per account plus one reconciler task.
- `gap_from = min(last_private_ws_message_ts, last_successful_reconcile_ts) - 5s`.
- Rate budget: all reconciliation REST calls use the `poll` bucket (20 % / about 2 req/s per UID, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 4.3); reconciliation must never starve the `critical` bucket.
- Chaos harness lives in `tests/chaos/` as a pytest plugin plus a docker-compose profile; faults are injected at four layers - mock-exchange responses, network, container lifecycle and host (clock, disk).
- Error codes referenced: `10002` clock drift, `10018` rate limit, `110001` order does not exist, `110079` not yet final; internal `UNRESOLVED_AFTER_RECONCILE`, `DEMO_RETENTION_EXPIRED`, `RATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`.

## Test plan
Authored in E45-Q01/Q02/Q03. Epic level: the chaos catalogue is this epic's own regression pack; coverage for `oms/reconciler` and the adapter fault paths must be **>=90 %** (R4 quality gate: security-relevant modules M2/M14/M17/M18/M19 held >=90 %).

## Security notes
Threats: anything that can suppress reconciliation hides an unprotected position; adopted `untracked` orders are exchange-controlled input into our state; drills run with real credentials could cancel real orders; a support bundle produced during a drill can leak keys. Controls: SR-058, SR-083, SR-154; drills are gated by E44's typed environment; `untracked` orders are never rule-managed; every resolution action is step-up-gated and audited. Data classification: OMS state is financial data, high sensitivity.

## Accessibility notes
The new admin surfaces (SCR-143/SCR-144 additions and the discrepancy resolution flow) meet WCAG 2.2 AA: real table semantics, status conveyed as text not colour, keyboard-operable resolution actions, `role="alertdialog"` for destructive confirmations. Covered by E45-D03 and E45-Q03.

## Performance notes
A full reconciliation pass across six accounts completes in <=3 s p95 and consumes <=20 % of the `poll` budget; RTO from backend restart to fully reconciled trading <=90 s (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` section 11); the 30 s timer adds <=1 % CPU.

## Observability
New metrics: `oms_reconcile_duration_seconds`, `oms_reconcile_corrections_total{kind}`, `oms_untracked_orders`, `oms_position_drift_total`, `oms_reconcile_failures_total{account}`, `oms_stale_accounts`, `chaos_scenario_result{scenario}`. Audit: `oms.reconcile`, `oms.untracked_adopted`, `oms.untracked_resolved`, `drill.executed`. Incidents written to `system_events` (component `oms`) and surfaced on SCR-144.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done; engineering, design, QA and security sign-offs recorded.
- [ ] Chaos suite green in CI and in a staging game-day; report archived.
- [ ] Rollback and restore drills executed and timed; times recorded in the release ticket.
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged; runbooks written and read through by the on-call rotation.
- [ ] Coverage >=90 % on `oms/reconciler` and the adapter fault paths.
- [ ] Storybook entries for any changed component states; docs updated.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at a Sprint Review with explicit acceptance recorded.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated with any new failure mode discovered.
- [ ] Engineering-points total (50) re-checked against the roadmap register (47) at epic close; variance kept within +/-15 % or the register updated by the Architect.
- [ ] E44 confirmed Done before E45-T09 starts (the one cross-train sequencing link); confirmation recorded on T09.

## Dependencies
- **E29** OMS core and order state machine - the state machine, `order_link_id` idempotency and the `Unknown` state this epic resolves.
- **E34** Trade-group fan-out and rate-limit governor - trade-group legs and the rate buckets reconciliation must live inside.
- **E32** brackets and the native SL invariant - the invariant reconciliation repairs.
- **E39** risk caps, lockouts and kill-switch - exercised by the chaos scenarios and by the dead-man's-switch policy.
- **E44** live-enablement gating and environment separation - drills must run against a live-shaped deployment safely. Runs S20-S21, overlapping E45's S21; the only child that consumes it is **E45-T09 (S22)**, so the overlap is safe. See *Cross-epic completion timing* above.
- **E04** observability baseline - metrics, alert routing and `system_events` this epic emits into.
- **E42** admin screens - SCR-143 and SCR-144, which E45 extends. Closes S17, three sprints before E45-D01 opens in S20.


### Cross-epic completion timing (verified against the roadmap Gantt)

The DoR gate requires each blocking epic to be Done before E45's first dependent child starts. There is no `31-sprint-plan.md` in this plan set; the authoritative schedule is the Gantt in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 10 plus the `S..-S..` windows in the epic tables. Verified window-by-window:

| Blocker | Scheduled window | Latest E45 child that needs it | Needed by | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **E04** Observability baseline | S02-S03 | T03 (metrics, `system_events`) | S21 | Done 18 sprints early |
| **E29** OMS core | S14-S16 | K01, X01, T01 | S21 | Done 5 sprints early |

Two notes the gatekeeper flagged:

1. **E44 is the only blocker that is not already complete when E45 opens.** E44 runs S20-S21 and E45 runs S21-S22 (Gantt lines 664-665), so they overlap in S21. This is deliberate and safe because **no E45 child scheduled in S21 depends on E44**: the single E44-dependent child is **E45-T09** (rollback rehearsal against a live-shaped deployment), which is scheduled **S22**, one sprint after E44 closes. E45's S21 children depend only on E29/E32/E34/E04/E03, all long since Done. The epic-level `blocked_by` on E44 therefore constrains T09, not the epic start date.
2. **E42 vs the S20 design tickets.** E45-D01/D02 sit in S20 to satisfy the design-ahead rule (>=2 sprints before the S22 FE stories S01/S02). They extend E42's SCR-143/SCR-144, which close in S17 - three sprints of headroom, so the design-ahead rule and the blocker are both satisfied.
