title: Black-box accessibility test plan for the E47 remediation story groups
body:
## Context
E47 is the epic that converts `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` from a written standard into demonstrated WCAG 2.2 AA conformance across every screen in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`. R5 exit criterion 2 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` section 9.3 requires a published, evidence-backed conformance report (VPAT-shaped); a report is only credible if the underlying test pass is written down, repeatable and executable by someone who did not build the features.

Today the E47 remediation stories (`E47-S01`..`E47-S04`) say *what to fix*. There is no single artefact a QA engineer can run against a staging build to assert "CandleViewer meets AA". `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.2 makes a recorded black-box QA pass non-skippable per Story, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 11 requires a written per-feature test plan plus a white-box review checklist. This ticket produces that artefact for the accessibility dimension specifically.

The plan is deliberately black-box: it is written against screen ids, hotkeys, announced strings and rendered contrast - never against React component internals - so it survives the refactors that remediation inevitably causes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e47-accessibility-test-plan.md`, organised as six executable groups mirroring the standard:
  1. **Keyboard operation** (standard section 3) - SCR-010 app shell, SCR-011 navigation rail, SCR-012 command palette, SCR-013 hotkey cheatsheet, SCR-020/021 workspace + dock, SCR-030 chart panel, SCR-037 drawing toolbar, SCR-050 heatmap + DOM ladder, SCR-060/061 order tickets, SCR-081/082 rule editors (form + node graph), SCR-121 admin users. Verifies `US-SET-002` (global hotkey layer) and the keyboard-only mode of `US-SET-007`.
  2. **Screen-reader semantics and streaming announcements** (standard sections 6.1, 6.2, 8) - DOM mirror and live-region behaviour on SCR-030, SCR-050, SCR-052, SCR-053, SCR-063, SCR-092.
  3. **Table alternatives and data parity** (standard section 6.3) - SCR-045 chart data-table alternative vs SCR-030 canvas; footprint cell parity; profile and heatmap table equivalents; `Alt+T` reachability from the panel header (equal status, per the SCR-045 sign-off checklist).
  4. **Colour-independence and contrast** (standard sections 4, 5) - every buy/sell, bid/ask, P&L, order-status, connection-health and Demo/Live surface across SCR-060, SCR-063, SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-143, in dark, light, high-contrast and the three CVD-safe themes delivered by `E47-D01`/`E47-T03`.
  5. **Reduced motion, flash and zoom** (standard section 7) - heatmap trails, big-trade bubbles, price flash, toasts; `Ctrl+Shift+M` override; SCR-117 preferences; 200% zoom and 400% reflow on SCR-110..SCR-119.
  6. **Preferences, statement and report surfaces** - SCR-116 appearance/density, SCR-117 accessibility settings, the accessibility statement page and the conformance report page designed in `E47-D02`; persistence via `GET|PUT /api/v1/me/preferences` and `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*`, tables `settings` and `hotkey_profiles`.
- Per case: id `E47-TC-<group><nn>`, preconditions (seeded user, theme, AT combo from the standard section 8.1 matrix), steps expressed as keystrokes, expected observable result (including the *exact expected announcement text* where applicable), the `US-SET-*` / WCAG 2.2 success criterion verified, the child ticket covered, and automation status (automated in `E47-Q03`, or manual-only).
- **Fixture appendix**: seeded owner / manager / viewer accounts; a demo-environment account with open positions and working orders so P&L, status and fill announcements can be observed; a replay session pinned to a high-tick-rate window so the streaming-announcement throttle can be exercised deterministically; a symbol with a wide tick size and one with a very fine tick size for the ladder.
- **Traceability table**: WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria x screens x test cases, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, so `E47-T06` can cite this file directly as report evidence.
- **White-box review checklist** for reviewers: no `outline: none` without a compliant replacement, no `aria-live` region mounted inside a virtualised list, no focus call inside a WS message handler, every canvas has an `aria-label` and a mirror root.
- Defect severity mapping: a task in the standard section 8.2 script that cannot be completed keyboard+SR-only is `priority/p0` and a release blocker; awkward-but-completable is P1/P2 per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` section 11.3.

## Out of scope
- Executing the manual screen-reader passes (that is `E47-Q02`) and running the automated suites (`E47-Q03`, `E47-Q04`).
- Design-time review of tokens and redlines - owned by `E47-D01` and `E47-D03`.
- Writing the conformance report itself (`E47-T06`); this plan supplies its evidence rows only.
- Non-web surfaces: there is no Android client in scope, and no non-Electron browser is a shipped target.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: E47 accessibility black-box test plan

  Scenario: Every in-scope screen and criterion is covered
    Given the published qa/plans/e47-accessibility-test-plan.md
    When its traceability table is checked against docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
    Then every screen listed in that catalogue maps to at least one case
    And every WCAG 2.2 AA success criterion maps to at least one case or to an explicit, justified "not applicable" row

  Scenario: A case is executable by someone new to the epic
    Given a QA engineer who has never worked on CandleViewer
    When they execute group 3 against a staging build using only the fixture appendix
    Then they can reach a pass/fail verdict on every case without asking the authors a question
    And each expected announcement is quoted precisely enough to judge a mismatch

  Scenario: Failure case - announcement flooding is specified as a defect
    Given the replay fixture pinned to a 2000 messages per second window
    When the tape panel is focused with NVDA running and verbosity at default
    Then the plan requires announcements to be coalesced per 05-accessibility-standard.md section 6.2
    And continuous announcement of every print is recorded as a P0 defect, not a preference

  Scenario: Edge case - table alternative must not silently diverge
    Given a bar whose footprint cells include an imbalance-flagged cell
    When the same bar is read in SCR-045 and inspected on the SCR-030 canvas
    Then the plan requires numeric parity for price, bid, ask, delta and the imbalance flag
    And any divergence is a P0 defect because the table is the normative equivalent

  Scenario: Plan is reviewed and merged
    When the plan PR is opened
    Then it carries approvals from the Accessibility role and the SDET
    And it is linked from the E47 epic ticket and referenced by E47-T06
```

## Technical notes / design
- Structure by *observable surface and success criterion*, not by component; remediation will move code around and the plan must not need rewriting.
- Expected announcements are recorded as quoted strings with tolerated variance noted (for example, NVDA may prefix the role); this avoids arguments at execution time.
- The AT combos and their pinned versions come from `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 8.1 - the plan references that table rather than duplicating versions, so the quarterly version bump happens in one place.
- Cases that depend on the high-contrast or CVD-safe themes must name the token pair under test so a failure can be handed straight to `E47-T03`'s contrast linter as a reproduction.
- Group 5 must use the replay fixture rather than live market data so the flash-rate observations are deterministic and re-runnable.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test plan; its own verification is a dry run. Execute group 1 and group 4 end-to-end against the current staging build, record execution timings, ambiguities and dead cases, then fix the plan before merge. Attach the dry-run log so "executable" is evidenced rather than asserted. Record the time taken per group; `E47-Q09` uses these figures to size the release-candidate regression window.

## Security notes
- Fixtures must use the demo environment only; no live API keys, no real account identifiers, no real P&L in any attached evidence, matching the redaction rule established in `E47-D02`.
- Group 2 must include a negative assertion: no live region, DOM mirror node or table export ever contains an API-key fragment, session token, account id or the full email of another user. Deeper adversarial versions live in `E47-X02`.
- Any screenshot or SR transcript attached to a case is reviewed for sensitive strings before it is committed.

## Accessibility notes
The deliverable is itself an accessibility artefact: the plan is a markdown document with a proper heading hierarchy, tables with header rows, and no information conveyed by colour alone (pass/fail is written as a word, never a coloured cell). The traceability table must be readable as plain text.

## Performance notes
The plan must state a time budget per group so a full pass fits inside the release-candidate window defined in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`. Group 2 is the expensive one (manual SR); the plan marks the minimum subset that must run for every RC versus the full pass that runs before GA.

## Observability
- Case results are recorded in the QA result store used by `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, tagged `epic:E47` and `criterion:<wcag-id>` so the conformance report can be generated by query rather than by hand.
- Defects filed carry the `a11y` label plus the screen id, feeding the burn-down dashboard maintained in `E47-Q04`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `qa/plans/e47-accessibility-test-plan.md` merged with all six groups, the fixture appendix and the traceability table.
- [ ] Dry-run log for groups 1 and 4 attached, with measured durations.
- [ ] Every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md` and every AA success criterion mapped or explicitly marked not applicable with a reason.
- [ ] Approved by the Accessibility role and the SDET; linked from the E47 epic and from `E47-T06`.
- [ ] Automation status column agreed with `E47-Q03` so there is no gap and no duplication.

## Dependencies
- `E47-D01` - contrast and CVD expectations must exist before group 4 can state expected results.
- `E47-D02` - the statement and report surfaces must be designed before group 6 can be written.

## Branch
`chore/e47-a11y-test-plan` (docs-only; PR well under the 400 LOC preference).

title: axe-core, pa11y and Lighthouse CI gates with a violation burn-down dashboard
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9 items 1, 2 and 7 require axe-core to run against every screen on every frontend PR with zero new serious/critical violations as a merge blocker, a Lighthouse Accessibility score of at least 95 on every top-level screen tracked over time, and both to be required checks on `main` exactly like the security scans in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`. Moderate and minor violations are to be tracked as backlog with a burn-down.

Partial versions of these checks may exist from earlier epics as advisory steps. E47 is where they become enforcing, complete (every screen, not a sample) and visible (a dashboard the Accessibility role and the owner can read).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **axe-core via `@axe-core/playwright`** executed against every screen in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` that can be reached in a test harness, including modal, empty, error, degraded, disconnected and rate-limited states (SCR-047, SCR-048, SCR-151..SCR-159) which are routinely missed by happy-path scans.
- A **baseline file** recording the currently-accepted moderate/minor violations, each with an owner, a ticket and a target date; the gate fails on any new serious/critical violation and on any regression above baseline.
- **pa11y-ci** configured as the secondary engine so rules axe does not implement are still covered; disagreement between engines is triaged rather than suppressed.
- **Lighthouse CI** on the tracked top-level screens (chart workspace SCR-020/030, order ticket SCR-060, positions SCR-063, admin users SCR-121, journal SCR-093, watchlist SCR-100, settings SCR-110, alerts SCR-090), asserting score >= 95 and storing the score history.
- **Burn-down dashboard**: a generated page (and a Grafana panel where the metric fits the existing stack) showing open a11y defects by severity, by screen and by WCAG criterion, plus the axe/Lighthouse/keyboard-suite trend; sourced from the same QA result store `E47-Q01` and `E47-Q02` write to.
- Suppression policy: a suppression requires an inline justification, an owner, an expiry date and a linked ticket; expired suppressions fail the build. No blanket rule disables.
- CI wiring as required checks on `main`, mirroring the security-gate placement in `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the violations - remediation stories own that.
- Keyboard journeys and a11y-tree snapshots - `E47-Q03`.
- Token contrast linting - that is `E47-T03`'s design-system CI job; this ticket only surfaces its result on the dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Automated accessibility gates and burn-down

  Scenario: Every screen is scanned, including its error and empty states
    Given the screen inventory from docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
    When the axe job runs
    Then every screen id appears in the scan report with a result
    And a screen absent from the report fails the job rather than passing silently

  Scenario: A new serious violation blocks merge
    Given a PR introducing an input without an accessible name
    When the axe gate runs
    Then the check fails naming the rule, the screen and the selector
    And the PR cannot be merged

  Scenario: Failure case - an expired suppression fails the build
    Given a suppression whose expiry date has passed
    When the gate runs
    Then the build fails with the suppression owner and ticket in the message

  Scenario: Edge case - a Lighthouse score drop is caught even when axe is clean
    Given a change that degrades heading structure without producing an axe violation
    When Lighthouse CI runs on the affected top-level screen
    Then the score falls below 95 and the build fails

  Scenario: The dashboard reflects reality
    Given defects filed by E47-Q01 and E47-Q02
    When the dashboard refreshes
    Then open counts by severity, screen and WCAG criterion match the QA result store
    And the burn-down trend is visible over at least the last four sprints
```

## Technical notes / design
- Screens are enumerated from a machine-readable inventory derived from the catalogue so "new screen, unscanned" is impossible; adding a screen without a scan entry fails CI. This inventory is the same one `E47-Q03` uses for snapshots.
- Error/empty/degraded states are reached via test hooks that force the state rather than by trying to provoke real failures, keeping the scan deterministic.
- Baseline entries are keyed by rule plus a stable selector path, not by DOM index, so trivial markup moves do not invalidate the baseline.
- Lighthouse runs against the built Electron-renderer bundle in headless Chromium matching the shell's Chromium version, per the standard section 9.2, otherwise scores are not comparable with the shipped surface.
- The dashboard reads the QA result store rather than parsing CI logs; log-scraping dashboards rot the first time output format changes.

## Test plan
- Fault injection: introduce one serious axe violation, one heading-structure regression and one expired suppression on a scratch branch; each must fail its respective gate with an actionable message.
- Determinism: run the axe job five times on an unchanged build; the violation set must be identical. Non-determinism (usually animation-dependent scans) is fixed by disabling motion during scans via the reduced-motion override.
- Verify the baseline genuinely blocks regressions by re-adding a baselined violation on a second screen and confirming failure.

## Security notes
- Scan reports embed DOM snippets. The report post-processor must redact values from fields that can hold secrets or personal data (API-key inputs on SCR-126/SCR-127, TOTP fields on SCR-002/SCR-003, email fields on SCR-121/SCR-123) before artefacts are uploaded.
- CI credentials for the scan harness are seeded demo users only; the harness must not be able to authenticate against the live environment.
- Dashboard access follows existing RBAC on observability surfaces; it exposes defect counts, not user data.

## Accessibility notes
The dashboard is itself held to the standard: it is one of the screens scanned, has a table with proper headers, conveys severity with text as well as colour, and its charts have an accessible table equivalent (the same rule the product applies to canvas surfaces).

## Performance notes
- The axe matrix across all screens is the slowest a11y job; shard by screen group so the per-PR envelope from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` is respected. Full-inventory scans may run on merge to `main` and nightly, with the per-PR job scoped to changed areas plus a fixed smoke set - this split must be documented, not implicit.
- Lighthouse runs on a pinned CI machine class; score comparisons across machine classes are meaningless and must be prevented by tagging results with the runner class.

## Observability
- Metrics published: `a11y_axe_violations{severity,screen}`, `a11y_lighthouse_score{screen}`, `a11y_open_defects{severity}`, `a11y_suppressions_active`, `a11y_suppressions_expiring_7d`.
- Alerting: a serious/critical violation reaching `main` (for example via an admin override) raises a notification to the Accessibility role.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] axe, pa11y-ci and Lighthouse CI jobs merged, covering the full screen inventory including non-happy-path states.
- [ ] Baseline file committed with owners, tickets and target dates; suppression policy enforced including expiry.
- [ ] Checks required on `main`; fault-injection evidence attached.
- [ ] Burn-down dashboard live and reading from the QA result store.
- [ ] Per-PR versus nightly scan split documented in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`.
- [ ] Handover note to E48/E49 describing how a new screen joins the inventory.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q01` - the screen inventory and severity conventions come from the plan.

## Branch
`feat/e47-a11y-ci-gates`.

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9 (items 1, 2, 3, 7).
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (gate placement pattern this mirrors).
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (required checks).
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (where the scan split is documented).
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (CI budget, regression-gate philosophy).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` (screen inventory, incl. SCR-151..SCR-159 state screens).

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e47-a11y-ci-gates`
- PR title: "E47-Q04: axe-core, pa11y and Lighthouse CI gates with a violation burn-down dashboard"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-Q04>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/test, area/design-system, priority/p0, qa, a11y

**Done means**
- axe, pa11y-ci and Lighthouse CI jobs merged, covering the full screen inventory including non-happy-path states.
- Baseline file committed with owners, tickets and target dates; suppression policy enforced including expiry.
- Checks required on `main`; fault-injection evidence attached.
- Burn-down dashboard live and reading from the QA result store.
- Per-PR versus nightly scan split documented in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Handover note to E48/E49 describing how a new screen joins the inventory.

**Do NOT**
- Fixing the violations - remediation stories own that.
- Keyboard journeys and a11y-tree snapshots - `E47-Q03`.
- Token contrast linting - that is `E47-T03`'s design-system CI job; this ticket only surfaces its result on the dashboard.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

title: Chart canvas surrogate and table alternative reach AA (SCR-030, SCR-045)
body:
## Context
The chart is the product, and it is a WebGL canvas — opaque to assistive technology by default. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6 mandates three complementary layers for it: the offscreen DOM mirror (§6.1), throttled ARIA live regions (§6.2), and the equal-status data-table alternative **SCR-045** (§6/§5.4), whose catalogue entry states plainly: "this is the normative accessible equivalent of SCR-030 and must reach feature parity for reading data; verified in every a11y test pass." **US-CHART-014** owns the table alternative; §3.1.7 of the standard requires that pan, zoom and the crosshair be fully keyboard operable (arrow keys per bar, `Shift+arrows` pan, `+`/`-` zoom, `Home`/`End` jump).

These pieces shipped across E11/E12 as each feature landed. This Story closes the gap between "shipped" and "conformant" using the E47-T01 findings: mirror/canvas correspondence, announcement usefulness at real tick rates, focus never being stolen by a price update (§3.4.3), and true parity of the table view.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-030 chart panel**: canvas exposes an accessible name and role; the windowed DOM mirror materialises exactly the focusable units in view; keyboard crosshair navigation announces the focused bar as a useful sentence (time, O/H/L/C, volume, delta) rather than a number soup; `Home`/`End`/`Shift+arrow`/`+`/`-` behave per §3.2.
- **Live-region discipline**: ambient fields (last price, best bid/ask, mark, unrealised P&L) on a polite region throttled to the user's configured cadence, always presenting the latest value and never queueing intermediate ticks; discrete events (WS disconnect, data gap) on assertive/`role="alert"`.
- **Focus stability**: assert that no streaming update, reconnect, or auto-scroll moves keyboard focus (§3.4.3); a reconnect that re-mounts the chart restores the previously focused bar.
- **SCR-045 parity**: `Alt+T` from any chart; arrow-key grid navigation; `Enter` expands a bar's footprint cells; `Ctrl+C` copies TSV; per-row actions (create alert here, replay from here, add note) reachable by keyboard; the table is opened from the chart panel header (equal status) and not buried in settings; virtualised rendering keeps the accessibility tree windowed.
- Remediation of every E47-T01 finding tagged to the chart surrogate pattern, including target-size and focus-obscured issues on the chart chrome (CMP-180…CMP-199 primitives, chart chrome CMP-200+ band).

## Out of scope
- Footprint cell grid, DOM ladder and heatmap surrogates — **E47-S02**.
- Rendering performance optimisation of the mirror — **E46** (this Story files tickets if the mirror exceeds its budget).
- New chart features or new table columns beyond what SCR-045 specifies.
- Drawing-tool keyboard creation, already delivered under E14 and only re-verified here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A blind trader reads the chart
  Given NVDA is running on the Electron build and BTCUSDT 1m is displayed
  When the trader focuses the chart and presses the left arrow key
  Then focus moves to the previous bar and the screen reader announces its time, open, high, low, close, volume and delta
  And the announcement is a single coherent utterance, not one field per event

Scenario: Streaming does not flood or steal
  Given the symbol is ticking at 20 updates per second and announcement cadence is the 2 s default
  Then the polite region is updated at most once per 2 s per field with the latest value
  And keyboard focus remains on the bar the trader selected throughout

Scenario: The table alternative has parity
  Given the chart shows a visible range with footprint data
  When Alt+T is pressed
  Then a keyboard-navigable grid of that same range opens from the panel header
  And expanding a row reveals that bar's footprint cells with price, bid, ask, delta and imbalance flag
  And every datum visible on the canvas is present in the grid

Scenario: Reconnect preserves context
  Given the WS connection drops while bar 13:58 is focused
  When the connection is restored and the chart re-subscribes
  Then the disconnect and reconnect are announced assertively
  And focus returns to bar 13:58 rather than to the document body or the latest bar

Scenario: Mirror stays windowed
  Given 100 000 bars are loaded
  Then the accessibility tree contains only the focusable units for the visible range plus a small buffer
  And the axe and accessibility-tree snapshot gates pass on SCR-030 and SCR-045

Scenario: No-data and error states are announced
  Given the chart enters the SCR-047 empty state or the SCR-048 error state
  Then the state is conveyed as text to the screen reader with the recovery action reachable by keyboard
```

## Technical notes / design
The engine already exposes the "current visible window + current focused unit" query surface that `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 made a binding engine-design requirement and `26-chart-engine-design.md` implements; the React layer consumes it to keep mirror and draw calls frame-synchronised. Announcement composition happens in one place (a formatter shared with SCR-045) so canvas and table cannot describe the same bar differently. Throttling reads the user's cadence preference from the settings document rather than a hard-coded constant.

## Test plan
Unit: announcement formatter, throttle behaviour under burst input, mirror windowing at range boundaries. Integration: focus-stability test driving a synthetic 20 Hz tick stream. E2E keyboard-only: crosshair traversal, `Alt+T` round trip, TSV copy, row actions. Manual SR: NVDA task script on SCR-030 and SCR-045 (JAWS and VoiceOver covered in **E47-T04**). Gates: axe, accessibility-tree snapshot, Lighthouse on the workspace screen.

## Security notes
The mirror and table render the same data the canvas is authorised to show — they must derive from the same RBAC-filtered series, never a broader fetch. TSV copy is clipboard-only and must not include account identifiers unless they are already on screen. Announcements must not read API keys or session tokens under any state.

## Accessibility notes
Direct implementation of `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1–§6.3 and §3.1.7. Canvas carries `aria-label`; the mirror is visually hidden by off-screen positioning/clip-path, never `display:none`. Targets ≥24×24 CSS px; the dense-footprint essential exception is only claimed where SCR-045 provides the alternative. WCAG SCs in play: 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Mirror maintenance ≤1 ms per frame at the reference bar count; announcement throttling must not allocate per tick. The SCR-045 grid renders 100k rows virtualised at ≤8 ms scripting per scroll frame, per its catalogue entry. Regressions go to **E46** with measurements attached.

## Observability
`chart.data_table_opened`, `chart.data_table_exported` (already specified on SCR-045); client metrics `a11y_mirror_update_ms`, `a11y_announcements_per_minute`, `a11y_focus_steal_count` (expected zero — alert if non-zero).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named automated test or a recorded manual SR step.
- [ ] All E47-T01 chart-surrogate findings closed or converted to registered exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the touched frontend packages; ≥85% on the engine package.
- [ ] axe, keyboard-E2E, Lighthouse and a11y-tree-snapshot gates green on SCR-030, SCR-045, SCR-047, SCR-048.
- [ ] NVDA spot-check recorded; deferral to E47-T04 stated explicitly for JAWS/VoiceOver.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030/SCR-045 and `26-chart-engine-design.md` reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed keyboard-only at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T01** (scopes the findings). Feeds **E47-T04** (SR sign-off scripts) and **E47-T05**.

## Branch

title: Rule form and node-graph editors keyboard/screen-reader operable
body:
## Context
The node-graph rule editor is the third surface `05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 names as dense-but-not-exempt, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §9.1 goal 2 calls it out by name — AA conformance "across every screen, including the chart surfaces and **the node editor**". A spatial, drag-and-connect canvas is the hardest possible case for WCAG 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements): every node move and every edge connection is natively a drag.

§3.2 already defines the keyboard model (`Ctrl+Shift+N` add node, `Enter` to connect after `Tab`-selecting source then target port, `Delete` to remove), and §3.3 item 6 requires **SCR-082**'s spec to cross-link to the global hotkey conflict rules rather than inventing its own. Both editors must merge or not at all (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.3 rule 5), so a form editor that is accessible and a node editor that is not still leaves a rule a user cannot author — the two are audited together here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-081 rule form editor**: every condition/action row fully labelled (persistent labels, not placeholder-only, per US-SET-001 NFR); dynamic row add/remove announced; validation errors associated with their fields and announced on submit; nested condition groups exposed with correct structural semantics so a screen reader can perceive the boolean nesting.
- **SCR-082 node-graph editor**: nodes and edges are focusable with a documented traversal order; arrow keys move focus between connected nodes; `Ctrl+Shift+N` adds, `Enter` connects a selected source port to a selected target port, `Delete` removes the focused node or edge; node *position* is adjustable by arrow-key nudge with discrete steps (WCAG 2.5.7 non-drag alternative); every node announces its type, its parameter summary, and its inbound/outbound connections.
- A **structural text view** of the graph (a tree/list of nodes and their connections) as the equal-status alternative for anyone who cannot perceive the canvas layout — the same principle SCR-045 applies to the chart; reachable from the editor header, not from settings.
- Conflict and error surfaces: **SCR-086** rule conflict resolver, **SCR-088** IR inspector and **SCR-085** arming dialog audited — arming is destructive and must satisfy the keyboard-operable confirm rules (§3.1.4).
- Remediation of all E47-T01 findings tagged to the rule-editor pattern, including focus return from node property popovers and focus-not-obscured (2.4.11) when the canvas pans a focused node under a floating toolbar.

## Out of scope
- Node-editor auto-layout and node search — descoped to R5 backlog per `30-release-roadmap.md` §12 row 8 and not resurrected here.
- Rule IR, compiler or runtime semantics — **E35**.
- Rule templates gallery visual polish — **E49**.
- New node types.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A rule is authored end to end without a mouse
  Given the node editor is open on an empty canvas
  When the user adds a trigger node, adds an action node, selects the source port, selects the target port and presses Enter
  Then the edge is created and announced
  And the rule validates and can be saved, all without a pointer event

Scenario: Dragging always has an alternative
  Given a node is focused
  When arrow keys are pressed
  Then the node moves by a discrete step and its new position is announced or otherwise conveyed
  And no repositioning capability exists that is reachable only by dragging

Scenario: Graph structure is perceivable without the canvas
  When the structural text view is opened from the editor header
  Then every node, its parameters and its inbound and outbound connections are listed and navigable
  And edits made there are reflected in the canvas and vice versa

Scenario: A focused node is never hidden behind chrome
  Given the canvas auto-pans to reveal a focused node
  Then the node is not fully obscured by the floating toolbar or the property panel

Scenario: Arming is a deliberate, keyboard-operable act
  Given a rule is ready to arm in the Live environment
  When the arm action is invoked from the keyboard
  Then the confirm surface states the environment, the rule and its actions, traps focus, is dismissible with Esc, and returns focus to the trigger on close

Scenario: Invalid input is announced, not merely coloured
  Given a required parameter is left empty in the form editor
  When save is attempted
  Then the error is programmatically associated with its field, announced, and focus moves to the first invalid field
```

## Technical notes / design
The structural text view is the pragmatic answer to a spatial canvas: rather than pretending arrow-key spatial navigation alone makes a graph perceivable, it exposes the same model in a linear form, which is also what the IR inspector (SCR-088) already renders — so this is a presentation of an existing model, not a second source of truth. Node traversal order is derived from the graph topology (trigger-first, then breadth-first over edges) rather than from canvas coordinates, which are meaningless to a non-visual user. Hotkey bindings register through the global layer (E47-S08's remap machinery) so conflicts surface at bind time per §3.3.

## Test plan
Unit: traversal-order derivation, port-selection state machine, nudge stepping. E2E keyboard-only: author, validate, save, arm and disarm a rule with zero pointer events. Manual SR: NVDA pass over both editors including the structural view. Gates: axe and a11y-tree snapshot on SCR-081, SCR-082, SCR-085, SCR-086, SCR-088.

## Security notes
Arming a rule in Live is a privileged, audited action; no accessibility affordance may bypass the confirm or the RBAC check, and the structural text view must respect the same rule-visibility permissions as the canvas. Rule names and parameters are user content rendered as text only. The IR inspector must not expose internal sandbox details beyond what the existing screen already permits.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §3.2 (rule-builder bindings), §3.3 item 6 (cross-linked conflict rules), §3.4.4 (dialog focus trap and return), §3.4.6 (focus not obscured), §3.4.8 (dragging alternatives). WCAG SCs: 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Focus traversal on a large graph must be O(degree) not O(nodes); the structural view is virtualised beyond a few hundred rows. Canvas auto-pan on focus is animated under the motion token pair so reduced-motion users get an instant jump.

## Observability
`rule.editor_keyboard_authored` analytics flag on save (records whether the session used any pointer event on the canvas — a direct measure of whether the keyboard path is genuinely complete); `rule.structural_view_opened`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named test or recorded manual step.
- [ ] All E47-T01 rule-editor findings closed or registered as exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the touched packages.
- [ ] axe, keyboard-E2E and a11y-tree-snapshot gates green on the listed screens.
- [ ] NVDA pass recorded over both editors.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-082 keyboard spec reconciled with shipped behaviour and its cross-link to `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.3 verified to resolve.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; keyboard-only authoring demoed at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T01**. Related to **E47-S08** (hotkey layer conflict rules); feeds **E47-T04**, **E47-T05**.

title: Reduced-motion coverage and the three-flashes-per-second ceiling
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §7 sets two rules that a fast-moving trading UI breaks easily. First, every animated component must consume a shared `motion-safe`/`motion-reduce` token pair — "reduced-motion is a design-system token/mode, not a per-component ad hoc CSS override" — and "a component cannot ship with only a hard-coded animation" (§11.4). Second, the seizure threshold: no content flashes more than three times per second, audited explicitly for big-trade bubble bursts, liquidation-heatmap flash, alert-toast entrance and price-flash-on-tick, because "it is easy for a naive flash green/red on every tick implementation to exceed 3 Hz on a fast-moving symbol".

This is the one accessibility area where a defect can cause physical harm, and the one most likely to have regressed silently as order-flow features were tuned for visual punch through R2.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Audit every animated surface for a motion token pair: chart inertia and auto-pan, heatmap fade and trail, big-trade bubbles (**SCR-053**), liquidation flashes (**SCR-054**), price flash on tick, toast entrance (**SCR-015**), panel/dock transitions (**SCR-021**), coach marks (**SCR-018**), skeleton shimmer (CMP-015), spinner (CMP-014), node-editor canvas pan. Replace any hard-coded animation with the token pair.
- Under reduced motion (OS preference or the in-app override, including the `Ctrl+Shift+M` session toggle from §3.2): animations are disabled or replaced with instant changes; parallax and inertia stop; nothing animates longer than 5 s without a pause control.
- Enforce the flash ceiling in the *implementation*, not only in the test: price-flash and bubble-burst effects coalesce so that at any tick rate the visible flash frequency is capped below 3 Hz, degrading to a sustained state change rather than a faster blink.
- Wire and calibrate the motion/flash audit script from **E47-T02** against a recorded high-tick-rate fixture for each named component, with the luminance-delta threshold and its justification documented.
- Remediate every E47-T01 finding in the motion pattern.

## Out of scope
- Adding new animations or motion design work — **E49** / design.
- Frame-rate optimisation — **E46**.
- The preference UI itself — **E47-S07**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Reduced motion is honoured everywhere
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is reduce
  When the heatmap updates, a bubble fires, a toast appears and a panel is docked
  Then each uses its motion-reduce variant with no easing, inertia or parallax

Scenario: The flash ceiling holds under a fast symbol
  Given a recorded fixture ticking at 40 updates per second
  When price flash and big-trade bubbles render
  Then the measured flash frequency for each component stays below 3 per second
  And the effect degrades to a sustained state change rather than a faster blink

Scenario: The session override works without settings
  When Ctrl+Shift+M is pressed
  Then reduced motion toggles for the session, the new state is announced, and it does not overwrite the persisted preference

Scenario: No hard-coded animation survives
  Given the design-system lint runs over component styles
  Then any animation or transition lacking a motion-safe/motion-reduce token pair fails the build with the component named

Scenario: Long animations offer control
  Given any animation would run longer than 5 seconds
  Then a pause or stop control is available, or the animation is not shipped

Scenario: The audit script catches a regression
  Given a change makes the liquidation flash fire at 5 Hz
  When CI runs the motion audit
  Then the build fails naming the component and the measured rate
```

## Technical notes / design
Coalescing is the real fix: capping flash rate by throttling the *effect trigger* (one flash per 400 ms window, carrying the net direction of the ticks in that window) preserves the visual signal traders rely on while making the 3 Hz bound structural rather than incidental. The motion token pair lives in the design system so the lint can enforce it; components consume variants, never raw durations. The `Ctrl+Shift+M` override is session state layered over the persisted preference from E47-S07, not a write to it.

## Test plan
Unit: coalescing window behaviour at burst and idle rates; token-pair resolution under both modes. Automated: the luminance-delta audit over each named component against the recorded fixture. Lint: hard-coded-animation check across the component library. E2E: reduced-motion toggle end to end including the session override. Manual: a reviewer with the fixture confirms the degraded effect is still readable as a signal.

## Security notes
None directly; the flash coalescer must not be usable to suppress a *safety* signal — risk-breach and kill-switch surfaces convey state by persistent text and icon (§4.4), never by flashing alone, so coalescing cannot hide them.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §7.1–§7.4 and §11.4. WCAG SCs: 2.2.2 (pause/stop/hide), 2.3.1 (three flashes), 2.3.3 (animation from interactions, AAA-adjacent but adopted here via the preference). Reduced motion must never remove *information*, only motion — a bubble that no longer animates must still appear.

## Performance notes
Disabling animation must measurably reduce frame work (the SCR-117 claim this Story makes true); record before/after frame times for the heatmap and bubble scenes. Coalescing reduces draw work at high tick rates, so it should improve, never worsen, the hot path.

## Observability
Client metrics `motion_reduced_active` (share of sessions) and `flash_events_per_minute{component}`; a CI-published flash-rate table per audited component.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests.
- [ ] Every animated component consumes a motion token pair; lint enforces it.
- [ ] Flash audit calibrated, documented and green for all named components.
- [ ] E47-T01 motion findings closed or registered as exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on touched packages; before/after frame-time measurements attached.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` motion tokens reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed at Sprint Review with the high-tick fixture.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-S07** (preference substrate and the session override). Uses the audit gate from **E47-T02**; feeds **E47-T05**.

## Branch
`feat/e47-reduced-motion-flash`

`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2, §7, §9.5, §11.4; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-015, SCR-018, SCR-021, SCR-053, SCR-054, SCR-117; `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-007.

title: Focus order, focus visibility, target size and drag alternatives
body:
## Context
The WCAG 2.2-specific criteria are the ones most likely to be outstanding, because they postdate most teams' habits and because CandleViewer's multi-pane density makes them genuinely hard: **2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured** (floating toolbars and docked panels over a focused control), **2.5.7 Dragging Movements** (order-line reprice, drawing handles, node moves, panel resize), **2.5.8 Target Size** (24 px minimum in a UI whose compact density exists specifically to fit more), **3.2.6 Consistent Help**, **3.3.7 Redundant Entry**, **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication**.

`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.4 specifies the answers — landmark regions with `Ctrl+\` cycling, roving tabindex, focus never stolen, dialog focus trap and return, skip links, a ≥2 px ≥3:1 focus ring that is a design token and never removed, the 24 px rule with its documented essential exception, a non-drag alternative for every drag, consistent help placement, and redundant-entry/auth rules. This Story closes the E47-T01 findings across all of them, app-wide.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Landmarks and skip links**: every major panel (Chart, DOM/Heatmap, Order Ticket, Positions & Orders, Watchlist, Rule Builder) is a labelled region; `Ctrl+\` cycles regions; skip links appear on the app shell (**SCR-010**) and are visible on focus.
- **Focus visibility and obstruction**: the focus-ring token audited across dark, light and high-contrast themes for ≥2 px and ≥3:1; any `outline: none` without an equivalent replacement removed; sticky toolbars, docked panels and floating windows (**SCR-021**, **SCR-027**) audited so a focused control is never fully obscured, with scroll-into-view padding where needed.
- **Focus order and return**: tab order matches visual order per screen; every dialog (**SCR-029**, **SCR-064**, **SCR-072**, **SCR-074**, **SCR-076**, **SCR-085**, **SCR-129**, **SCR-149**) traps focus, is `Esc`-dismissible, and returns focus to its trigger; no live update moves focus.
- **Target size**: a 24 px audit across all interactive controls at both densities, with each essential exception explicitly registered plus its alternative.
- **Drag alternatives**: order-line reprice, drawing handle move, node move, panel resize and column resize each gain (or are verified to have) a discrete keyboard or menu equivalent.
- **Consistent help, redundant entry, accessible auth**: the `?` cheatsheet and help entry point occupy the same relative position on every screen; order tickets pre-fill safely per US-SET-003's defaults; **SCR-001…SCR-006** and **SCR-149** verified to require no cognitive-function test, with TOTP/WebAuthn treated as the permitted alternative.

## Out of scope
- Canvas-internal focus models — **E47-S01**, **E47-S02**, **E47-S03**.
- Visual redesign to create space for larger targets — findings needing layout change are routed to **E49** with the a11y rationale attached.
- Changing authentication factors — **E43**/**E09**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Regions are reachable and named
  Given the workspace is open with chart, ladder, ticket and positions panels
  When Ctrl+backslash is pressed repeatedly
  Then focus moves between named regions and each region's name is announced
  And the same regions appear in the screen reader's landmark list

Scenario: A focused control is never hidden
  Given a control near a sticky toolbar receives focus by keyboard
  Then it is scrolled into view such that it is not fully obscured

Scenario: Every drag has a discrete equivalent
  Given an order line, a drawing handle, a graph node, a panel edge and a table column
  Then each can be repositioned or resized using keyboard or a menu with discrete values
  And no capability exists that requires dragging

Scenario: Dialogs trap and return focus
  Given any confirmation dialog is opened from a keyboard-focused trigger
  Then focus is trapped inside it, Esc cancels safely, and focus returns to the trigger on close

Scenario: Targets meet the minimum or are registered exceptions
  Given compact density is active
  Then every interactive control is at least 24 by 24 CSS px or has 24 px spacing
  And any exception is present in the register with a named alternative

Scenario: Authentication needs no puzzle
  Given the login and step-up flows
  Then no cognitive-function test is required and credentials may be pasted from a password manager

Scenario: Help is where it always was
  Given any screen in the app
  Then the help entry point and the cheatsheet shortcut are in the same relative location and order
```

## Technical notes / design
The focus ring is fixed once in the token layer rather than per component, which converts a long tail of findings into one change plus a lint that forbids removing outlines. Focus-not-obscured is handled by a shared scroll-into-view helper that accounts for registered sticky-chrome insets, so future chrome does not reintroduce the defect. Drag alternatives reuse the existing nudge/menu patterns from E14 drawings rather than inventing new interaction vocabulary.

## Test plan
Automated: accessibility-tree snapshots for landmark and heading structure per screen; a focus-order test per top-level screen; a target-size scan against computed styles at both densities; a lint forbidding un-replaced `outline: none`. E2E keyboard-only: region cycling, skip links, dialog trap/return, each drag alternative. Manual: NVDA landmark navigation spot-check.

## Security notes
Dialog focus-trap fixes must not weaken destructive-action confirms; `Esc` always means cancel, never confirm. Skip links must not bypass an authentication or step-up gate. Accessible-authentication work must not reduce 2FA strength — the exemption covers object-recognition factors, not removing the factor.

## Accessibility notes
Direct implementation of §3.4.1–§3.4.10. WCAG SCs: 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8, 4.1.2.

## Performance notes
The scroll-into-view helper runs on focus change only and must not force synchronous layout in a frame that also renders the canvas. Landmark structure is static markup with no runtime cost.

## Observability
CI-published counts of focus-order snapshot diffs and target-size violations per screen; client metric `a11y_focus_steal_count` (expected zero) shared with E47-S01.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests or recorded manual steps.
- [ ] E47-T01 findings in the focus, target-size and drag patterns closed or registered as exceptions with alternatives.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on touched packages.
- [ ] axe, keyboard-E2E and a11y-tree-snapshot gates green across all top-level screens.
- [ ] Focus-ring token verified in all three themes; outline lint enabled.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` focus contracts and `16-design-system-brief.md` focus token reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T01**. Feeds **E47-T04**, **E47-T05**; layout-change findings hand off to **E49**.

## Branch
`feat/e47-focus-target-drag`

## References
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.4; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010, SCR-021, SCR-027, SCR-029, SCR-064, SCR-072, SCR-074, SCR-076, SCR-085, SCR-129, SCR-149; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`; `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-001, US-SET-003.

title: High-contrast and CVD-safe themes across every order-flow encoding
body:
## Context
**US-SET-004 Themes and density (Must)** requires that a theme switch update "every surface including WebGL canvases immediately without reload, keeping contrast ratios compliant", and that compact density keeps targets ≥24 px. **US-SET-005 Colour conventions and CVD-safe palettes (Must)** requires that changing the convention or selecting a CVD-safe palette updates "every chart, DOM, heatmap, footprint, bubble and profile surface consistently", that side and direction remain distinguishable without colour "through glyphs, signs or patterns everywhere", and — as an NFR — "an automated check asserts no view depends on hue alone".

**E47-T03** has by now produced the evidence: which token pairs and which gradient stops fail, in which theme and density, and which colour pairs collapse under CVD simulation. This Story fixes them and makes the no-hue-alone rule enforceable rather than aspirational.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Remediate every failing pair and gradient stop from the T03 matrix across dark, light and high-contrast themes at both densities — adjusting tokens and gradient ramps, not adding per-component overrides.
- Ship/complete the **high-contrast theme** (`Ctrl+Shift+H`, §5.6) as a full token-set swap reaching the ≥7:1 body-text bar, covering chrome *and* data-ink, with the WebGL surfaces re-uploading their palettes on switch without a reload.
- Ship/complete the **CVD-safe palettes** as tested design tokens (US-SET-005 NFR) selectable on **SCR-116**, applied consistently to chart, DOM, heatmap, footprint, bubbles and profiles.
- Implement the **no-hue-alone automated check**: an enumerated inventory of semantic encodings (buy/sell, bid/ask, order status, P&L, connection health, demo/live, imbalance, delta sign, risk severity) each asserted to carry at least one non-colour channel (glyph, sign, text, pattern or position) on every surface that renders it; a surface that renders an encoding without a registered non-colour channel fails the build.
- Legend obligations: every affected view states its convention in a legend (US-SET-005 scenario 1) and the LIVE/DEMO badge remains text-plus-colour on every screen (§4.1).
- Density verification: compact density keeps ≥24 px targets and re-evaluates the large-text contrast threshold (paired with E47-S05).

## Out of scope
- Generating the contrast/CVD evidence — **E47-T03**.
- The accessibility preference UI — **E47-S07**; theme selection lives on SCR-116.
- Re-designing order-flow visual language beyond what conformance requires — **E49**/design.
- Print/export colour.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Theme switch reaches the canvas immediately
  Given the chart, heatmap and footprint are rendering
  When the theme is switched to high contrast
  Then every DOM and WebGL surface repaints in the new palette without a reload
  And the contrast matrix for that theme reports no failing pair

Scenario: A CVD-safe palette applies everywhere at once
  When a colour-blind-safe palette is selected
  Then chart, DOM, heatmap, footprint, bubble and profile surfaces all adopt it
  And no surface is left on the previous palette

Scenario: No view depends on hue alone
  Given the encoding inventory covers buy/sell, bid/ask, order status, P&L, health, demo/live, imbalance and delta sign
  When the automated check runs
  Then every surface rendering an encoding declares a non-colour channel
  And a surface that declares none fails the build naming the surface and encoding

Scenario: Inverting the convention is consistent
  Given the user inverts the buy/sell convention
  Then every affected surface and every legend reflects the inversion
  And no surface retains the old convention

Scenario: High contrast holds the higher bar
  Given the high-contrast theme
  Then body text pairs meet 7:1 and non-text pairs meet 3:1 across chrome and data-ink

Scenario: Compact density does not break the rules
  Given compact density in any theme
  Then targets remain at least 24 px or spaced accordingly
  And text that drops below the large-text threshold is evaluated at 4.5:1 and passes
```

## Technical notes / design
The encoding inventory is the durable artefact: a declarative registry mapping each semantic encoding to the surfaces that render it and the non-colour channel each provides. That registry is what makes the NFR testable — without it, "no view depends on hue alone" can only be spot-checked. Palette changes propagate to the engine as a uniform/texture update rather than a scene rebuild, which is what makes the no-reload requirement achievable.

## Test plan
Unit: registry completeness (every enumerated encoding has at least one surface and one channel). Automated: contrast matrix regeneration green; CVD discriminability green; the no-hue-alone check. Visual regression: grayscale and CVD-simulated snapshots of chart, footprint, ladder, heatmap, bubbles and profiles per theme. E2E: theme and palette switch while streaming, asserting no reload and no re-subscription. Manual: designer + Accessibility role review of the simulated snapshots.

## Security notes
The demo/live distinction must never become colour-only under any theme or palette — the LIVE badge is text plus colour on every screen, and a CVD palette selection may not remove it. Theme and palette are per-user presentation settings with no authorisation effect.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §4.1–§4.4 (colour independence), §5.1–§5.7 (contrast, high-contrast theme, text resize). WCAG SCs: 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.4, 1.4.10, 1.4.11, 1.4.12.

## Performance notes
Palette switching must be a uniform/texture update, not a geometry rebuild; measure switch cost and keep it under one frame on the reference machine. The no-hue-alone check is static analysis plus registry validation with no runtime cost.

## Observability
`settings.theme_changed{theme}` and `settings.palette_changed{palette}` analytics; CI-published failing-pair count per theme, trending to zero.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests.
- [ ] T03 matrix reports zero failing pairs across all three themes and both densities.
- [ ] Encoding inventory complete and enforced by the no-hue-alone check.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on touched packages.
- [ ] SCR-116 design-qa comparison recorded; CVD-simulated snapshots reviewed and signed off.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` palettes and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-116 reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed at Sprint Review with a live theme switch over streaming data.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T03** (evidence and the failing list). Related to **E47-S02** (surfaces that consume the palette) and **E47-S05** (density/target size); feeds **E47-T05**.

`feat/e47-contrast-cvd-themes`

title: Accessibility preferences applied everywhere incl. WebGL (SCR-117)
body:
## Context
**US-SET-007 Accessibility preferences (Must)** is the one SET story whose whole subject is accessibility, and its NFR is the demanding part: "preferences persist per user and apply immediately across all views **including WebGL surfaces**". A preference that reflows the DOM but leaves the canvas animating, or that requires a reload, fails the story.

**SCR-117** enumerates the option set: reduced motion, disable canvas animation, always show data-table alternatives, increase focus-ring thickness, announce price updates (off / on significant change / always), screen-reader verbosity for the tape, keyboard-only mode (disables drag-only interactions and reveals their form equivalents), and a link to the accessibility statement. Its catalogue entry also sets the bar for the screen itself: "This screen is itself the exemplar" and "the page passes its own standard at 200% zoom".

## Scope / Deliverables
- The preference model as a scoped key set inside the existing `settings` JSONB document, read/written via `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings` and mirrored on `GET /api/v1/me/preferences`; per-user scope, applied on load and on change without a reload.
- **SCR-117** built/remediated to the catalogue spec: every control has a visible persistent label plus a plain-language description of its effect; OS-level `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-contrast` detection shown as the default with an explicit override; the announcement-throttle control; links to the accessibility statement and the hotkey cheatsheet (**SCR-013**).
- Propagation: a single preference context consumed by DOM components *and* by the engine — canvas animation, heatmap fade, chart inertia and flash-on-tick all read the same flags; changing a flag takes effect on the next frame.
- `keyboard-only mode`: drag-only affordances hide and their discrete equivalents (nudge controls, numeric position fields, "…" repositioning menus) are revealed across chart drawings, order lines, node editor and panel resize.
- `always show data-table alternatives`: panels default to their table view (SCR-045 and the order-flow equivalents) without re-fetching data.
- Verbosity and announce-price-updates settings feed the live-region throttling used by **E47-S01** and **E47-S02**.
- Components: CMP-004 Toggle, CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-069 InfoPanel, CMP-086 SettingsNav/SettingsLayout, CMP-228 PreviewTile.

## Out of scope
- Theme and density selection — **SCR-116** / **E47-S06** (US-SET-004, US-SET-005).
- Performance profile settings — **SCR-118**, US-SET-008, **E46**.
- Adding preferences beyond the SCR-117 option set.
- Server-side enforcement of any preference (they are presentation-only).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A preference applies immediately, canvas included
  Given the chart is animating and the heatmap is fading
  When "disable canvas animation" is enabled on SCR-117
  Then within one frame the canvas stops animating and the heatmap updates instantly
  And no reload or re-subscription occurs

Scenario: OS preference is the default, not the ceiling
  Given the operating system reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce
  Then the reduced-motion control shows "On (from system)" as its default
  And an explicit user override to "Off" is honoured and persisted

Scenario: Verbosity limits announcements
  Given screen-reader verbosity is set to low
  When prices tick rapidly
  Then the live region announces only significant events rather than every update
  And raising verbosity restores per-cadence announcements without a reload

Scenario: Keyboard-only mode reveals the alternatives
  When keyboard-only mode is enabled
  Then drag-only affordances are hidden and their discrete equivalents are visible on chart drawings, order lines, node editor and panel resize

Scenario: Preferences persist per user
  Given preferences are changed and the app is restarted
  Then the same preferences are restored for that user and are unchanged for any other user

Scenario: The screen passes its own standard
  Then SCR-117 at 200% zoom shows no clipping or lost functionality
  And axe reports zero serious or critical violations on it

Scenario: A failed save does not silently lie
  Given the settings API returns an error on save
  Then the failure is announced and the control reverts to its persisted value with a retry offered
```

## Technical notes / design
One preference context, two consumers: React components subscribe directly; the engine receives a flags message on change so the worker/render loop reads plain booleans rather than querying React. Defaults derive from OS media queries evaluated at load and re-evaluated on change, with an explicit "user override" tri-state (`system` / `on` / `off`) so an override is distinguishable from a coincidence. Disabling animation must remove the transition work from the frame budget — a measurable reduction, per the SCR-117 performance note, not a no-op that merely sets duration to zero on a still-running loop.

## Test plan
Unit: tri-state resolution against media-query changes; flags propagation to the engine message. Integration: preference change while streaming, asserting no re-subscription. E2E keyboard-only: traverse and set every control on SCR-117. Visual/perf: frame-time measurement before and after disabling animation, asserting a real reduction. Gates: axe, Lighthouse, a11y-tree snapshot on SCR-117 at 100% and 200% zoom.

## Security notes
Preferences are per-user and written through the authenticated settings endpoint; the API must reject writes scoped to another user's id. Preference values are a closed enum set — no free-form values are persisted or echoed. No preference may disable a security-relevant confirm, the arm-token requirement, or the LIVE/DEMO badge.

## Accessibility notes
This screen is the exemplar per SCR-117: persistent labels, effect descriptions, state announced on change, 200% zoom clean. Implements `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2 (announcement throttling as a user-configurable cadence), §7 (reduced motion), §3.4.6 (focus-ring thickness). WCAG SCs: 1.4.4, 1.4.10, 1.4.12, 2.4.7, 3.2.2, 3.3.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Preference propagation must not cause a full re-render of the workspace; the engine receives flags, not a scene rebuild. Enabling every accommodation at once must stay within the 1 ms/frame ceiling stated on the Epic; measure with the E46 harness and report the before/after frame time as evidence for the SCR-117 claim.

## Observability
`a11y.preference_changed{key,value}` per the SCR-117 spec, aggregated so it is visible which accommodations are actually used; client metric `a11y_pref_apply_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the settings and preference-context packages.
- [ ] SCR-117 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior; design-qa comparison recorded.
- [ ] axe and Lighthouse green at 100% and 200% zoom; keyboard-only path recorded; NVDA spot-check recorded.
- [ ] Frame-time before/after measurement attached for "disable canvas animation".
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-117 and `22-api-openapi.yaml` settings schema reconciled with shipped behaviour.
- [ ] Feature flag state recorded; QA black-box plan executed; demoed at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: none (the preference substrate is needed by the rest of the Epic and therefore lands first). Blocks **E47-S04**; consumed by **E47-S01**, **E47-S02**.

## Branch
`feat/e47-a11y-preferences`

title: Settings, hotkey layer and destructive-confirm keyboard conformance
body:
## Context
Three SET Must stories carry accessibility NFRs that only a conformance pass can settle. **US-SET-001** requires the settings screen be "fully keyboard operable; every control has a persistent label, not placeholder-only text". **US-SET-002** requires one global hotkey layer with conflict detection and reserved-key refusal — which `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.3 elaborates into precedence rules, a detection algorithm, permanently reserved keys (`Esc`, `Ctrl+K`) and an OS-combo blocklist. **US-SET-003** requires each destructive action to be configurable as dialog, hold-to-confirm or immediate — and §3.1.4 forbids any mouse-hold-only or timing-only gate: hold-to-confirm must have a discrete-press keyboard fallback.

These are the SET stories where accessibility and *trading safety* are the same requirement: a hotkey a keyboard user cannot reach, or a confirm they cannot complete, is both an AA failure and a risk of an unintended order.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-110 Settings home / SCR-111 / SCR-112 / SCR-114 / SCR-115 / SCR-118 / SCR-119**: full keyboard traversal, persistent visible labels on every control, scope indicator (per user / workspace / symbol / account) exposed as text, search results announced with count and section path, and the reset-preview flow operable and announced.
- **SCR-113 Hotkey editor**: bind-time conflict detection announced, not merely coloured; conflicting action pairs named in text with the one-click swap reachable by keyboard; reserved keys (`Esc`, `Ctrl+K`) excluded from the pickable set with an explanation; OS/Electron-reserved combos filtered out rather than allowed-then-failed; trading-critical bindings refused as unmodified single letters with the reason announced.
- **SCR-013 cheatsheet** (`?`) reflects current, possibly remapped bindings, read from `GET /api/v1/me/hotkeys`, and is reachable from every screen in the same relative place (3.2.6).
- **Hold-to-confirm**: a discrete-press keyboard fallback everywhere hold is offered; the 300–2000 ms duration is configurable with a visible, non-colour-only progress indicator; progress is announced at start and completion; releasing early cancels and says so.
- **Immediate mode** acknowledgement dialog is keyboard-operable and the choice is audited; the Live-stricter-than-Demo rule holds regardless of accessibility settings.
- Remediation of E47-T01 findings on **SCR-015**, **SCR-029**, **SCR-072**, **SCR-076**, **SCR-129** confirm surfaces.

## Out of scope
- Accessibility preferences — **E47-S07**; appearance/theme — **E47-S06**.
- Adding new hotkeys or changing the default keymap in §3.2.
- Confirm-policy business rules beyond their keyboard operability — **E39**/**E44**.
- Settings persistence backend changes.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Settings are fully operable from the keyboard
  Given the settings home screen
  When the user traverses with Tab and arrow keys only
  Then every control is reachable, labelled with persistent visible text, and its scope is announced
  And searching announces the number of matches and each match's section path

Scenario: A conflict is explained, not just coloured
  Given Ctrl+Shift+F is already bound to flatten
  When the user tries to bind it to another action
  Then the conflict is announced naming both actions, the save is blocked, and a keyboard-reachable swap option is offered

Scenario: Reserved and OS keys are refused with a reason
  When the user attempts to bind Esc, Ctrl+K or an OS-reserved combination
  Then the key is not offered or the attempt is refused with a spoken reason

Scenario: Hold-to-confirm has a keyboard path
  Given flatten is configured as hold-to-confirm
  When the action is invoked from the keyboard
  Then a discrete-press confirmation is available that does not require holding
  And if hold is used, progress is announced and releasing early cancels with an announcement

Scenario: Immediate mode is an informed choice
  When any destructive action is set to immediate
  Then a keyboard-operable acknowledgement states the consequence, and the choice is written to the audit log

Scenario: Live is never weakened by an accessibility path
  Given Demo has a weaker confirm policy than Live
  Then Live does not inherit it, and no accessibility setting can relax a Live confirm

Scenario: The cheatsheet tells the truth
  Given bindings have been remapped
  When the cheatsheet is opened with the question-mark key
  Then it lists the current bindings, from the same relative location on every screen
```

## Technical notes / design
Conflict detection already exists as specified in §3.3.2 (compute the new combo's active focus-context set, intersect with existing bindings); the accessibility work is making its *output* perceivable — announced text naming both actions — rather than an inline red border. Hold-to-confirm gains a paired discrete control rather than a separate code path, so the policy engine sees one confirmation result either way. The cheatsheet reads resolved bindings from the API so remaps cannot drift from documentation.

## Test plan
Unit: conflict detection across focus contexts; reserved/blocklisted key filtering; hold-progress state machine including early release. E2E keyboard-only: settings traversal and search, remap with conflict and swap, each confirm mode for flatten and cancel-all in demo. Manual SR: NVDA pass over SCR-110, SCR-113, SCR-117 and one confirm of each mode. Gates: axe, Lighthouse, keyboard-E2E on the settings band.

## Security notes
This Story touches destructive-action policy, so it is `security`-labelled: no accessibility affordance may reduce a confirmation below its configured strength, bypass the arm token for one-click entry, or weaken the Live-stricter-than-Demo invariant. Setting a policy to immediate is an audited event with actor, timestamp and prior value. Hotkey profiles are per-user and written via the authenticated `/settings/hotkeys` endpoints; a profile may not bind an action the user's role cannot perform.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §3.1.3–§3.1.6, §3.2, §3.3, §3.4.4 and §3.4.9. WCAG SCs: 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 2.1.4 (character key shortcuts — the modifier requirement on trading-critical bindings is the mitigation), 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 3.2.6, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 3.3.4, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Hotkey dispatch stays O(1) per keystroke via the resolved binding map; announcement of hold progress is throttled to start/complete rather than per animation frame so a screen reader is not flooded during a 2 s hold.

## Observability
`settings.hotkey_conflict_shown`, `settings.hotkey_swapped`, `settings.confirm_policy_changed{action,mode}` (also audited), `confirm.hold_cancelled` analytics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named tests or recorded manual steps.
- [ ] E47-T01 findings on the settings and confirm surfaces closed or registered as exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on touched packages.
- [ ] axe, Lighthouse and keyboard-E2E green across the settings band; NVDA pass recorded.
- [ ] Security review comment present (destructive-policy surface); audit entries verified for immediate-mode changes.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-013/SCR-110/SCR-113 and `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2/§3.3 reconciled with shipped bindings.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed keyboard-only at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T01**. Related to **E47-S03** (rule-editor bindings register through the same global layer); feeds **E47-T04**, **E47-T05**.

## Branch

title: Full WCAG 2.2 AA sweep of SCR-001..SCR-159 into a findings register
body:
## Context
This is the audit itself: the single pass over every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md` that turns "we followed the standard" into a list of specific, reproducible defects with WCAG success-criterion references. `30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 names it first in E47's scope ("Full WCAG 2.2 AA audit of every screen in `14-screens-catalogue.md`"), and §9.3 exit criterion 2 requires per-screen evidence.

The method and finding schema come from **E47-K01**; the automated gates from **E47-T02** have already pre-populated the easy half. What this Task adds is coverage of what automation cannot judge: announcement quality, focus intent, whether an offscreen mirror actually corresponds to what is drawn, whether a dense grid is navigable in practice rather than in principle, and the six WCAG 2.2-specific criteria (2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8) that tooling detects poorly.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Execute the sweep across **SCR-001…SCR-159** and their enumerated states, per the K01 plan: automated pass for every screen/state; deep manual pass for the canvas, dense, destructive and authentication surfaces (**SCR-001…SCR-006**, **SCR-030**, **SCR-032**, **SCR-045**, **SCR-050**, **SCR-052**, **SCR-053**, **SCR-060/061**, **SCR-063**, **SCR-064**, **SCR-072**, **SCR-074/075/076**, **SCR-081**, **SCR-082**, **SCR-090**, **SCR-093**, **SCR-097**, **SCR-113**, **SCR-116**, **SCR-117**, **SCR-121**, **SCR-135**, **SCR-143**, **SCR-152**, **SCR-156**).
- Record every finding in the checked-in register with: screen id, CMP id where applicable, WCAG SC and level, severity, reproduction steps, detection source, and the remediation ticket it is assigned to.
- Group findings by **pattern** (canvas surrogate, roving-tabindex grid, dialog focus-return, motion token, colour-only encoding, target size, drag-only interaction, label/name mismatch) and assign each group to one of **E47-S01…S06**; anything that fits no group and is small becomes a directly-attached remediation item on this Task.
- Produce the per-screen conformance matrix skeleton (one row per screen, columns for each evidence type) that **E47-T05** publishes.
- Triage: every Level A finding is P0/P1 and must be fixed in R5; AA findings are sized and either scheduled or nominated as exceptions with a compensating control proposal.

## Out of scope
- Remediation of grouped findings — **E47-S01…S06**.
- The manual screen-reader *sign-off* passes — **E47-T04** runs the pinned matrix after remediation; this sweep uses SR only as a detection instrument.
- Non-accessibility design-QA findings (spacing, token drift, copy) — routed to **E49**.
- Bugs in feature behaviour discovered incidentally — filed as ordinary bugs against the owning epic.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Coverage is complete and provable
  When the sweep closes
  Then every screen from SCR-001 to SCR-159 has at least one register entry or an explicit "no findings" record
  And every state listed in the screen's catalogue entry is marked covered or marked unreachable with a reason

Scenario: A finding is actionable by someone who did not find it
  Given any register entry
  Then it states the WCAG success criterion and level, exact reproduction steps, the observed and expected behaviour
  And a second engineer can reproduce it from the entry alone

Scenario: WCAG 2.2-specific criteria are explicitly checked
  Then each of 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7 and 3.3.8 has a recorded check result per applicable screen
  And these are not inferred from the axe result, which does not fully cover them

Scenario: Level A findings cannot be deferred
  Given a finding is classified Level A
  Then it is assigned priority P0 or P1 and a remediation ticket in R5
  And it cannot be moved to the exception register

Scenario: Duplicates collapse into patterns
  Given the same defect appears on eight screens
  Then it is recorded once as a pattern finding listing all eight screens
  And remediation is scheduled against the shared component, not eight times
```

## Technical notes / design
The register is the Epic's spine: E47-S01…S06 are scoped *by* it, E47-T05 is generated *from* it, and E49 consumes its leftovers. Keeping it as a checked-in structured file (schema from K01) is what makes the published report reproducible months later. Pattern grouping is done during the sweep, not after — retrofitting grouping onto 300 flat findings is where audits usually lose a sprint.

## Test plan
Quality control on the audit itself: 10% of screens are re-audited by a second auditor and inter-rater agreement is recorded; disagreements are adjudicated by the Accessibility role and the criteria clarified in the method doc. Automated results are cross-checked against manual results on the deep-pass screens to calibrate what automation is missing.

## Security notes
The sweep runs in the demo environment against synthetic accounts; reproduction steps must not embed live credentials, account ids or API keys. Findings on authentication screens (**SCR-001…SCR-006**, **SCR-149**) are handled with the same care as security findings — no screenshots of tokens, and 3.3.8 checks must not weaken 2FA requirements.

## Accessibility notes
The deep-pass protocol follows `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.2 task scripts and §3/§4/§5/§6/§7 rules. Auditors record not just "does it pass" but "is the announced text useful" — a technically-labelled control that announces "button button" is a finding even if axe is silent.

## Performance notes
The automated portion must fit the nightly budget established in E47-T02. During the deep passes, record any case where the DOM mirror or live regions visibly lag the canvas — those become E46 tickets rather than being absorbed silently.

## Observability
Register metrics published per build: open findings by level and severity, findings per screen band, pattern-group sizes; a burn-down chart that GA readiness is judged against.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Register complete for all 159 screens with covered/unreachable state accounting.
- [ ] Findings grouped into patterns and assigned to remediation tickets.
- [ ] Conformance matrix skeleton generated.
- [ ] Inter-rater check executed on ≥10% of screens with results recorded.
- [ ] Level A findings all scheduled; AA exception nominations documented with compensating controls.
- [ ] Accessibility role and QA lead sign off that the sweep is complete.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-K01** (method and schema), **E47-T02** (gates pre-populate and prevent drift during the sweep). Blocks **E47-S01**, **E47-S02**, **E47-S03**, **E47-S05**; feeds **E47-T05** and **E49**.

`chore/e47-wcag-sweep`
