title: Promote the six accessibility CI gates to required checks
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §9 specifies six automated gates and §9.7 requires them to be *required checks* on `main` per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`. Through R0–R4 several of them have run advisory (reporting without blocking) so that feature trains were not stopped by pre-existing violations. R5 exit criterion 2 depends on those gates being real: a published conformance report is worthless if the next merge can silently break it.

This Task flips them on. It runs early in the Epic on purpose — the gates then *find* much of what **E47-T01** would otherwise have to find by hand, and they immediately prevent remediation work from being undone by parallel E46/E48/E49 work.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **axe-core** (Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright`) across every screen state: fail on any new serious/critical violation; existing moderate/minor violations captured into the findings register with a baseline file so the gate blocks *regressions* from day one and *absolute* violations once E47-T01's remediation lands.
- **Lighthouse accessibility ≥95** on the tracked top-level screens (chart workspace SCR-020/030, order ticket SCR-060, positions SCR-063, admin users SCR-121, journal SCR-093, watchlist SCR-100), run against the built Electron-renderer bundle in headless Chromium.
- **Contrast-token linter** on any change to design-system token files, validating text, non-text and chart data-ink pairs for the dark, light and high-contrast themes (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §5.4).
- **Keyboard-only E2E** suite: no mouse events dispatched, driving the §8.2 task script (submit an order in demo, switch symbol, toggle the SCR-045 table view, trigger the reduced-motion override).
- **Motion/flash audit script**: frame-capture + luminance-delta analysis against heatmap, big-trade bubbles and price-flash at a fixed high-tick-rate fixture, asserting <3 flashes/second (§7.3).
- **Accessibility-tree snapshot** diff per top-level screen, reviewable in the PR.
- Branch-protection configuration updated so all six are required; a documented, time-limited break-glass path for an infrastructure outage (not for a genuine violation).

## Out of scope
- Fixing the violations the gates surface — that is the remediation Stories' job; this Task only establishes the baseline and the block.
- Performance budget gates — **E46**.
- Adding new screens to the tracked Lighthouse set beyond the six named (a deliberate cost decision; the axe gate covers the rest).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A regression is blocked
  Given main is green
  When a PR introduces a serious axe violation on any in-scope screen
  Then the axe check fails, the merge queue rejects the PR, and the output names the screen, rule and node

Scenario: The baseline cannot be silently widened
  When a PR modifies the axe baseline file
  Then CODEOWNERS requires the Accessibility role's review on that file
  And the PR description must state which finding id justifies the change

Scenario: Infrastructure failure is distinguishable from a violation
  Given the Lighthouse runner cannot start
  Then the check reports an infrastructure error distinct from a score failure
  And the documented break-glass path is usable without disabling the gate for violations

Scenario: Flash threshold is enforced on a realistic fixture
  Given the high-tick-rate fixture is replayed against the heatmap and bubble components
  When luminance deltas are analysed
  Then any component exceeding 3 flashes per second fails the build with the offending component named

Scenario: Gate runtime stays affordable
  Then the combined per-PR accessibility gate wall-clock time is under 12 minutes
  And the full nightly sweep is under 20 minutes
```

## Technical notes / design
Baselining is the crux: a hard "zero violations" flip on day one would block every unrelated PR in R5 and would be waived within a day, which is worse than not having the gate. So: snapshot current violations into a reviewed baseline file, block anything new immediately, and shrink the baseline to empty as **E47-S01…S06** land. The baseline file is CODEOWNERS-protected so shrinking is the only easy direction. Accessibility-tree snapshots are stored as text so PR diffs are human-reviewable.

## Test plan
Meta-tests: deliberately inject a keyboard trap, a colour-only status, a 5 Hz flash and a contrast-failing token in a scratch branch and assert each gate fails with an actionable message; assert a clean branch passes. Measure gate runtime on the CI runner class actually used.

## Security notes
Gate runs use a demo-environment build with synthetic fixtures — never live credentials. Lighthouse/axe artefacts (HTML reports, traces) may embed page content and are retained only on the internal CI artefact store with the same retention as other build artefacts, not published.

## Accessibility notes
Gate output itself must be readable: failures are reported as text in the check summary (screen, rule, selector, WCAG SC), not only as an attached HTML report or screenshot.

## Performance notes
Gates run in parallel with the existing test matrix; the nightly full sweep runs off the PR path. If the per-PR budget is exceeded, the axe sweep is sharded by screen band rather than sampled — sampling would make the gate non-deterministic.

## Observability
Per-build metrics: axe violation count by severity, Lighthouse a11y score per tracked screen, keyboard-E2E pass rate, baseline file size. Dashboard panel plus an alert when the baseline file grows.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six checks configured as required on `main` with break-glass documented.
- [ ] Baseline file committed, CODEOWNERS-protected, and its shrink-only policy documented in `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`.
- [ ] Meta-tests for all six gates pass (injected defect fails, clean branch passes).
- [ ] Runtime budgets measured and recorded.
- [ ] `05-accessibility-standard.md` §9 updated to reflect the gates as shipped.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: none (runs first deliberately). Feeds **E47-T01** by pre-populating the findings register; constrains **E47-S01…S06**, **E46**, **E48**, **E49**.

## Branch
`chore/e47-a11y-required-checks`

`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §9; `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §7; `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3.

title: Contrast and colour-vision validation matrix for every theme and data-ink token
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §5.4 requires that candle body/wick colours, footprint cell background+text pairs, heatmap gradient stops and profile-histogram bars each independently meet 3:1 against the chart background **at every point in the gradient**, validated by an automated script producing a pass/fail matrix per token pair — "not just spot-checked visually". §4.2 additionally requires deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia simulation of every buy/sell and heatmap palette.

Today the design system validates the *chrome* palette. What has never been validated end-to-end is the **data-ink** palette: the continuous gradients the order-flow surfaces use, which are generated at runtime and were exempt from the token linter because they are not discrete tokens. That exemption is exactly where a conformance report gets challenged.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Extend the contrast validator to sample **continuous gradients** (heatmap intensity ramp, delta divergence ramp, profile histogram fill, liquidation intensity) at N stops (N≥16, configurable) and evaluate each against the theme background, failing if any stop falls below 3:1.
- Cover all three themes: dark (default), light, high-contrast (`Ctrl+Shift+H`, §5.6, ≥7:1 body text) — plus both density modes, since compact density changes text sizes and therefore the applicable ratio (§5.1 large-text threshold).
- Cover the **CVD-safe palettes** shipped under US-SET-005: each alternative palette is validated to the same bar, not just the default.
- Produce the machine-readable pass/fail matrix (token pair × theme × density) checked in and consumed by **E47-T05**'s report.
- Add CVD simulation output (deuteranopia, protanopia, tritanopia) for buy/sell, bid/ask and imbalance encodings, with a discriminability assertion between the paired colours after simulation — a pair that collapses to the same simulated colour fails.
- Wire both into the **E47-T02** contrast-linter gate.

## Out of scope
- Changing palettes to fix failures — that is **E47-S06**; this Task produces the evidence and the failing list.
- The no-hue-alone structural rule (glyphs, signs, patterns) — audited under **E47-S06** and **E47-T01**.
- Print/export colour fidelity.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every gradient stop is evaluated
  Given the heatmap intensity ramp is defined for the dark theme
  When the validator runs
  Then at least 16 sampled stops are each evaluated against the chart background
  And a single failing stop fails the whole ramp with the stop's position and ratio reported

Scenario: CVD-collapsing pairs are caught
  Given the buy and sell tokens under deuteranopia simulation
  When their simulated values differ by less than the configured discriminability threshold
  Then the pair fails with both simulated values reported

Scenario: High-contrast theme is held to its own bar
  Given the high-contrast theme is selected
  Then body-text pairs are evaluated at 7:1, not 4.5:1
  And a pair passing AA but failing the high-contrast bar fails only in that theme's column

Scenario: The matrix is generated, never hand-maintained
  When the token files change
  Then the matrix file is regenerated in CI and a stale checked-in matrix fails the build

Scenario: Compact density does not silently lower the bar
  Given compact density reduces a label below the large-text threshold
  Then that pair is evaluated at 4.5:1 rather than 3:1 in the compact column
```

## Technical notes / design
Gradients are evaluated by sampling the same interpolation function the renderer uses — importing it, not reimplementing it — so the matrix cannot drift from what is drawn. Contrast uses the WCAG relative-luminance formula; CVD uses a standard published transform matrix, with the chosen transform and its source recorded so results are defensible. Discriminability threshold is a documented, reviewed constant, not a magic number.

## Test plan
Unit tests for the luminance and CVD transforms against published reference values. Fixture tests: a deliberately failing ramp and a deliberately CVD-collapsing pair must both fail; a known-good pair must pass. Snapshot test on the generated matrix.

## Security notes
None beyond standard supply-chain hygiene for any colour-science dependency added (pinned, SCA-scanned); prefer a small vendored transform over a large transitive dependency.

## Accessibility notes
This Task is a direct implementation of §4.2 and §5.4. The generated matrix is a text/markdown table with explicit pass/fail words, not a colour-coded grid — the accessibility evidence must itself not depend on colour.

## Performance notes
Matrix generation must complete in under 60 s so it can run on every token change; gradient sampling is pure computation with no rendering.

## Observability
CI metric: count of failing pairs per theme, trended per build so palette work is visibly converging.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Validator covers discrete tokens and continuous gradients across three themes and two densities.
- [ ] CVD simulation with discriminability assertion implemented and unit-tested against reference values.
- [ ] Matrix generated in CI, checked in, and consumed by the conformance report.
- [ ] Wired into the required contrast-linter gate from E47-T02.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` updated with the validated palette status and the transform used.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: none. Blocks **E47-S06**; feeds **E47-T02** and **E47-T05**.

`chore/e47-contrast-cvd-matrix`

title: STRIDE threat model for a11y surfaces: mirrors, live regions, preferences
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` and `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` require a STRIDE threat model per epic. E47 looks benign - it is "just" accessibility - but it introduces a genuinely new attack surface: a **parallel representation of every piece of data on screen**. The DOM mirror (standard section 6.1), the ARIA live regions (6.2) and the table alternatives (6.3) re-express canvas-rendered market data, order state, account P&L and admin content as DOM text. Any control applied to the visual surface that is not also applied to the mirror is a bypass.

The epic also adds persisted user preferences (SCR-116, SCR-117) written through `PUT /api/v1/me/preferences` and hotkey profiles via `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*`, backed by the `settings` and `hotkey_profiles` tables, plus a published accessibility statement and conformance report (`E47-D02`, `E47-T06`) that are, by design, documents describing exactly how the system behaves.

There is also a safety-critical interaction: accessibility affordances must never weaken trading-safety controls. The Demo/Live distinction (SCR-074, SCR-075), destructive-action confirmations (US-SET-003), the arming flow (`/settings/arm`) and the RBAC-gated admin screens all have accessible equivalents that must carry the same guarantees.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE model (`docs/security/threat-models/e47-accessibility.md`) over a data-flow diagram covering: canvas -> DOM mirror -> AT; event -> live region -> AT; table alternative -> clipboard/export; preference UI -> `/api/v1/me/preferences` -> `settings` table; hotkey profile UI -> `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*` -> `hotkey_profiles` table; statement/report content -> renderer.
- Per STRIDE category, at minimum:
  - **Spoofing**: an accessible name or announcement that misrepresents environment (Demo announced where Live is active) or account identity; focus-visible styling faked by content.
  - **Tampering**: a persisted preference or hotkey profile modified so a destructive action loses its confirmation, or a hotkey rebound onto a trading action; injection of markup into mirror text.
  - **Repudiation**: a preference change (for example disabling confirmations or widening arming) that is not audited, leaving no record of who weakened a control.
  - **Information disclosure**: mirror or live-region text exposing data the visual surface redacts (masked API-key fragments on SCR-127/SCR-128, other users' emails on SCR-121, balances for accounts outside the user's `user_account_access`); table export (`Ctrl+C` TSV on SCR-045) as an exfiltration path; the conformance report disclosing internal architecture.
  - **Denial of service**: announcement flooding and unbounded mirror growth as a client-side DoS; a table alternative materialising an unbounded range.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: a viewer reaching an owner-only control because it is present-but-hidden visually yet exposed in the accessibility tree, or a keyboard path that skips the SCR-149 admin re-authentication gate.
- Ranked findings with owners, each mapped to a mitigation in a specific ticket (`E47-S0x`, `E47-X02`, `E47-X03`) or accepted with a recorded rationale.
- A control checklist handed to `E47-X04` for the review, and to `E47-Q03`/`E47-Q06` as assertions where mechanically checkable.

## Out of scope
- Threat modelling of the underlying trading, auth and admin functionality - owned by their own epics' models; this model assumes those controls exist and asks only whether the accessible surface preserves them.
- Penetration testing - performed before R4 live enablement per the security program; this is a design-time analysis.
- Abuse-case construction and exploit attempts - `E47-X02`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: STRIDE threat model for E47

  Scenario: Every data flow is modelled
    Given the data-flow diagram in the model
    When it is compared with the surfaces E47 introduces
    Then the mirror, live-region, table-alternative, preference and hotkey flows each appear with trust boundaries marked

  Scenario: Every category yields a considered result
    Given the six STRIDE categories
    When the model is reviewed
    Then each category has at least one analysed threat with a rating and a disposition
    And a category dismissed as not applicable states why

  Scenario: Failure case - parity gap between visual and accessible surfaces
    Given a field masked in the visual UI
    When the accessible representation is analysed
    And the mirror or live region would expose the unmasked value
    Then the finding is rated high and assigned to a remediation ticket before GA

  Scenario: Edge case - a preference that weakens a safety control is audited
    Given a user disables destructive-action confirmations or increases arming scope
    When the model analyses repudiation
    Then an audit-log requirement is specified for that preference change
    And its absence is filed as a finding

  Scenario: The model is reviewed and owned
    When the model PR is opened
    Then it is reviewed by the Security engineer and the Accessibility role
    And every finding has an owner and a disposition of mitigate, transfer or accept with rationale
```

## Technical notes / design
- Trust boundaries: the AT process is outside the app's process boundary - text handed to a screen reader leaves the application's control entirely (it may be spoken aloud in a shared room, logged by AT software, or routed to a braille display). That physical-context exposure is a real consideration for a product displaying account balances, and belongs in the model rather than being waved away.
- The mirror must be derived from the *same authorisation-filtered data* the renderer receives, never from a pre-filter source. A finding template is provided for reviewers to check this per surface.
- Hotkey rebinding is a genuine tampering vector precisely because E47 expands keyboard reach; the model must consider whether any single keystroke can reach an irreversible trading action without confirmation, tying back to US-SET-002 and US-SET-003.
- Follow the existing model template and rating scale in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` so E47's findings aggregate with other epics' rather than using a bespoke scale.

## Test plan
- The model is validated by a walkthrough with the frontend a11y engineer and the Security engineer, tracing three concrete scenarios end-to-end: a viewer opening a chart on a permitted symbol, a manager opening the admin users screen, and an owner rotating an API key on SCR-127 - each read entirely through the accessible surface.
- Every mechanically checkable mitigation is written as an assertion into `E47-Q03` or `E47-Q06` and confirmed to fail on a deliberately vulnerable build.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security analysis. Two standing conclusions must be stated explicitly even if no finding materialises: (1) the accessibility surface is subject to the same RBAC and data scoping as the visual surface, with no exception; (2) no accessibility accommodation may remove a confirmation, an arming step or the Demo/Live signal - accommodations may change modality, never remove a control. Both become review criteria in `E47-X04`.

## Accessibility notes
The model must not produce mitigations that degrade accessibility - "do not mirror sensitive screens" is not an acceptable mitigation, because it would make those screens unusable with a screen reader. Correct mitigations preserve equivalent access while applying the same protections the visual surface has. This constraint is written into the model's ground rules.

## Performance notes
The DoS analysis overlaps with `E47-Q05`: announcement flooding and unbounded mirror growth are simultaneously an availability threat and a performance defect. The model references the measured budgets rather than inventing separate thresholds.

## Observability
- Findings are tracked in the security findings register per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, tagged `epic:E47`.
- Any mitigation implemented as an audit-log requirement must specify the event name and fields so the admin audit screens (SCR-135, SCR-136) can surface it.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Threat model merged with a data-flow diagram, trust boundaries and all six STRIDE categories analysed.
- [ ] Findings rated, owned and dispositioned; mitigations mapped to tickets.
- [ ] Walkthrough completed with the three traced scenarios recorded.
- [ ] Mechanically checkable mitigations written into `E47-Q03` / `E47-Q06`.
- [ ] Control checklist handed to `E47-X04`.
- [ ] Reviewed and approved by the Security engineer and the Accessibility role.

## Dependencies
- `E47-D01`, `E47-D02` - the designed surfaces (themes, statement, report) define part of what is modelled.

## Branch
`chore/e47-threat-model` (docs-only).

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE template, rating scale, findings register).
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 3.2-3.3 (hotkeys), 6.1-6.3 (mirror, live regions, table alternative).
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/me/preferences`, `/settings`, `/settings/arm`, `/settings/hotkeys`, `/settings/hotkeys/{hotkeyProfileId}`, `/settings/hotkeys/{hotkeyProfileId}/activate`.
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` `settings`, `hotkey_profiles`, `users`, `user_account_access`.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-045, SCR-074, SCR-075, SCR-116, SCR-117, SCR-121, SCR-127, SCR-128, SCR-135, SCR-136, SCR-149.
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-002, US-SET-003, US-SET-007.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e47-threat-model`
- PR title: "E47-X01: STRIDE threat model for a11y surfaces: mirrors, live regions, preferences"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-X01>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/security, area/design-system, priority/p1, security, a11y

**Done means**
- Threat model merged with a data-flow diagram, trust boundaries and all six STRIDE categories analysed.
- Findings rated, owned and dispositioned; mitigations mapped to tickets.
- Walkthrough completed with the three traced scenarios recorded.
- Mechanically checkable mitigations written into `E47-Q03` / `E47-Q06`.
- Control checklist handed to `E47-X04`.
- Reviewed and approved by the Security engineer and the Accessibility role.

**Do NOT**
- Threat modelling of the underlying trading, auth and admin functionality - owned by their own epics' models; this model assumes those controls exist and asks only whether the accessible surface preserves them.
- Penetration testing - performed before R4 live enablement per the security program; this is a design-time analysis.
- Abuse-case construction and exploit attempts - `E47-X02`.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E47-X01` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Design the Help & about surface and the user-guide information architecture
body:
## Context

**SCR-119 Help & about** (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-119) is specified but has never been designed in hi-fi: it is the home for version/build information, the changelog link, the keyboard cheatsheet, the order-flow glossary, the detector-methodology entry point (**SCR-058**), the guided-tour restart, the diagnostics-bundle export and the licence/attribution list. E48 makes it the front door of the GA documentation set, which is more content and more structure than the original sketch anticipated.

The design-ahead rule (`docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`; `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1) requires design Done ≥2 sprints before the consuming frontend story. E48-S01 and E48-S02 are built in Sprint 25/26, so this ticket lands in **Sprint 23**. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §1.2 notes that after D-S18 the design org is in design-QA and defect-support mode with reserved R5 polish capacity — this is one of the few net-new R5 design items and is funded from that reserve.

The user guide itself is persona-shaped (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`: P1 Owner/discretionary order-flow trader, P2 Account Manager, P3 Viewer/analyst, P4 Admin, plus the M1 Rule-author mode). Deciding how a manager finds "how do I place a bracket" without wading through admin material is an information-architecture problem, not a writing problem, so it is designed before it is written.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **UX research (light, 1 day)**: three sessions — Owner (P1/P4 hats) and two proxy managers — on how help is actually reached during trading: what they look for, whether they would ever leave the chart to read a guide, and what they currently do when they do not know what a value means. Written up as 6–10 findings that justify the IA. This is new interaction territory (the app has had no help surface until now), hence the `ux-research` label.
- **Information architecture** for the guide: the section tree per persona, the entry points from the app (SCR-119, the `(estimated)` chip → SCR-058, the empty-state CTAs, the onboarding checklist), and the rule for what lives in-app versus on the docs site — with the offline constraint respected (SCR-119: "fully available offline").
- **Wireframes → hi-fi (Figma)** of **SCR-119** using **CMP-086 SettingsNav/SettingsLayout** (it sits under `/settings/*`), **CMP-051 Accordion** for grouped sections, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow** for the version table, **CMP-021 Link**, **CMP-001 Button**, **CMP-096 WhatsNewPanel**, **CMP-207 BuildFooter**.
- **States**: loaded; update-check idle / checking / up-to-date / update-available / check-failed; diagnostics-bundle idle / generating / generated / failed-due-to-secret-detected (US-OBS-007 scenario 2 — the failure is loud by design and needs a designed treatment) / truncated-due-to-size; offline; browser build where shell-only items are hidden with an explanation rather than shown disabled (US-SET-009 scenario 2).
- **The keyboard cheatsheet layout** — it renders the *active* hotkey profile, so it must handle a remapped, a conflicting and a very long binding list (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2 default map, §3.3 conflict rules).
- **The glossary pattern** — term, one-sentence plain-language definition, "why it matters here", link to the screen where it appears; plus the inline term-reference treatment.
- **Design-system contribution**: a `DefinitionList` molecule for glossary/cheatsheet pairs (or an explicit decision that CMP-036 KeyValueRow covers it), a `DocSection` pattern, and tokens for long-form prose (measure, line height, heading rhythm) which the design system does not currently carry — the product has had no long-form text surface before.
- **Motion**: accordion expand/collapse, drawer entry for the methodology link and the What's New panel, all respecting `prefers-reduced-motion` (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §7).
- **Accessibility review** before handoff: heading order, the version table as a real table, the licence list as a named scrollable region, the copy-diagnostics button's accessible name stating exactly what it copies, focus order through the accordion.
- **Engineering handoff**: annotated Figma with tokens, spacing, states, empty/error copy, and the SCR-119 design sign-off acceptance checklist from the screens catalogue answered item by item.

## Out of scope

- Writing the guide or glossary content (E48-S01, E48-S02).
- Redesigning the settings shell (CMP-086 exists from E05/E10).
- SCR-016/SCR-017 onboarding wizard visuals — existing designs; this ticket only defines the restart entry point into them.
- SCR-058 detector-methodology drawer — already designed; this ticket defines the link-in treatment only.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every catalogue sign-off item is answered
  Given the SCR-119 design sign-off acceptance checklist in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md
  When the hi-fi is reviewed
  Then app version, engine version, backend version, build hash and Bybit API version are all shown
  And the copy-diagnostics control, the cheatsheet/accessibility-statement/methodology links, the four update-check result states and the third-party licence list are all specified

Scenario: The browser build hides shell-only settings with an explanation
  Given US-SET-009 scenario 2
  When the design is reviewed for the plain-browser build
  Then shell-only items are absent with an explanatory line, not rendered disabled
  And the explanation copy is specified, not left to engineering

Scenario: The cheatsheet survives a remapped and conflicting hotkey set
  Given a hotkey profile with a remapped binding and a conflict flagged per 05-accessibility-standard.md §3.3
  When the cheatsheet layout is reviewed
  Then the remapped binding is shown in place of the default and the conflict has a designed treatment
  And the layout holds at the maximum documented binding count without horizontal scrolling

Scenario: Accessibility review passes before handoff (failure path)
  Given the hi-fi is submitted for handoff
  When the accessibility reviewer checks heading order, contrast, focus order and non-colour-only signalling
  Then any failure blocks handoff until corrected
  And the correction is recorded on the ticket rather than fixed silently in Figma

Scenario: Design is signed off at least two sprints before the consuming story
  Given E48-S01 is scheduled in Sprint 25
  Then this ticket reaches Status Done no later than the end of Sprint 23
  And the CDO or design lead sign-off comment is present
```

## Technical notes / design

Constraints the design must honour, all pre-existing:

- **Offline-first.** SCR-119 makes no network call except the explicit update check; the guide, cheatsheet, glossary and licences are bundled content. A design that assumes fetched content is wrong.
- **RBAC.** SCR-119 is available to every authenticated role; nothing on it may leak admin-only data. Build info comes from `GET /system/build` (`x-rbac: { permissions: [], scope: self }`) and exposes "no infrastructure detail beyond version and commit".
- **Density.** The app has a compact density mode; long-form prose needs its own measure token set rather than inheriting the trading-surface density (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`).
- **The diagnostics bundle is a security-relevant control** — the design states what is included, what is redacted, and that generation fails loudly if a secret pattern is detected (US-OBS-007), because a vague "Export diagnostics" button invites a user to send a bundle somewhere it should not go.

Deliverables live in the Figma project `CandleViewer / R5 / Help & Docs`, linked from the ticket, with the components published to the design-system library where they are new.

## Test plan

- **Design QA against spec** is E48-D02 (post-build); this ticket is tested by review: CDO/design-lead sign-off, accessibility-reviewer sign-off, and an engineering feasibility review with the frontend lead who will build E48-S01.
- **Research validity**: findings are attributed to sessions, not asserted; contradicting findings are recorded rather than averaged away.
- **Prototype walkthrough**: a clickable prototype covering the update-check and diagnostics-bundle state machines is walked through with QA so the state list is complete before build.

## Security notes

The diagnostics-bundle flow is the security-sensitive part: the design must make it obvious what the bundle contains, that it is stored locally and never uploaded automatically (US-OBS-007 NFR), and that generation is audited. The copy-diagnostics control on SCR-119 must state its scope in its accessible name. No design may surface build/infrastructure detail beyond what `GET /system/build` returns. Reviewed under E48-X01/E48-X02.

## Accessibility notes

This is the screen where the product explains itself, so it must be exemplary: correct heading hierarchy, real table semantics for the version table, accessible names on all links ("read the accessibility statement", not "click here"), the licence region named and keyboard-scrollable, accordion per the WAI-ARIA pattern (CMP-051), visible focus everywhere, ≥4.5:1 text and ≥3:1 non-text contrast, reduced-motion variants for every transition. The accessibility statement itself is linked from here (E47 publishes it). Standard: WCAG 2.2 AA (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes

Design must fit a ≤150 ms panel mount and ≤200 ms route transition (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 item 7): no large hero imagery, no blocking font load for a screen that must work offline, licence list virtualised or collapsed by default if it exceeds a screen height.

## Observability

Design specifies the trigger points for the already-defined analytics keys `help.about_viewed`, `help.diagnostics_copied`, `help.update_check_requested`, plus `whatsnew.panel_opened` for the panel entry point.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Research findings written up and linked.
- [ ] IA, wireframes and hi-fi complete for SCR-119 in all listed states.
- [ ] Cheatsheet and glossary patterns specified including remapped/conflicting/overflow cases.
- [ ] New design-system contributions published to the library with Storybook-ready specs, or an explicit decision recorded that existing components suffice.
- [ ] Motion specs with reduced-motion variants.
- [ ] Accessibility review passed and recorded.
- [ ] Every item of the SCR-119 catalogue sign-off checklist answered.
- [ ] Engineering handoff session held with the E48-S01 implementer; open questions closed.
- [ ] CDO / design-lead sign-off comment present; Status Done by end of Sprint 23.

## Dependencies

- **E42** — admin screens establish the settings/admin visual conventions this page sits beside.
- **E10** — app shell, `/settings/*` routing and CMP-086 exist.
- Consumed by **E48-S01** and **E48-S02** (Sprint 25/26), satisfying the ≥2-sprint design-ahead rule.

## Branch

`design/docs-ga-readiness-help` (design artefacts + catalogue updates). No production code.

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-119 (incl. its design sign-off acceptance checklist), SCR-058, SCR-016, SCR-017, SCR-157, §0.5
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-001, CMP-021, CMP-036, CMP-046, CMP-051, CMP-086, CMP-096, CMP-207
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` SCR-119 row
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-009, US-OBS-007
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md`, `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md`
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2, §3.3, §7

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/docs-ga-readiness-help`
- PR title: "E48-D01: Design the Help & about surface and the user-guide information architecture"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E48-D01>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: design, ux-research, handoff, type/design, area/docs, priority/p2, a11y

**Done means**
- Research findings written up and linked.
- IA, wireframes and hi-fi complete for SCR-119 in all listed states.
- Cheatsheet and glossary patterns specified including remapped/conflicting/overflow cases.
- New design-system contributions published to the library with Storybook-ready specs, or an explicit decision recorded that existing components suffice.
- Motion specs with reduced-motion variants.
- Accessibility review passed and recorded.

**Do NOT**
- Writing the guide or glossary content (E48-S01, E48-S02).
- Redesigning the settings shell (CMP-086 exists from E05/E10).
- SCR-016/SCR-017 onboarding wizard visuals — existing designs; this ticket only defines the restart entry point into them.
- SCR-058 detector-methodology drawer — already designed; this ticket defines the link-in treatment only.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E48-D01` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Spike: choose the documentation toolchain and reference-generation pipeline
body:
## Context

R5 exit criterion 6 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3) requires a published user guide, ops runbooks, API/WS reference, ADR index and onboarding guide. §9.4 adds that docs must be reviewed by a non-author. Both imply a *built, linked, searchable* documentation set rather than a pile of Markdown files, and the API/WS reference must be **generated** from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` so it cannot drift (the same staleness discipline already applied to `packages/protocol` in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §5).

Choosing the toolchain is a one-off decision with long consequences (search, versioning, offline availability, CI cost, who can edit). It is deliberately timeboxed and decided by ADR before E48-T02 starts building on it.

## Scope / Deliverables

- A 2-day timeboxed comparison of at least three candidates for the prose site: **MkDocs Material**, **Docusaurus**, and **a minimal Vite/Astro static build reusing `packages/ui` tokens**; plus at least two candidates for the REST reference renderer (**Redocly CLI** — already in the toolchain as the OpenAPI linter per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §5.0 — and **Scalar/Elements**), and a decision for rendering the WS protocol reference from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` + the bundled `ws-schemas.json`.
- A comparison table scoring: build time on CI, offline/air-gapped build (no network at build time), search quality, Markdown-authoring ergonomics for non-frontend engineers, theming cost to match the product's dark theme, versioning support, mermaid support (the plan docs are mermaid-heavy), link-checking hooks, maintenance burden, and licence.
- A throwaway prototype building the existing `docs/plan/*.md` set plus a generated REST reference, measured end to end.
- **ADR-0016 (or next free number) `docs-toolchain`** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, added to `27-adrs/README.md` and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16 in the same PR (ADR house rules, `27-adrs/README.md` §"Writing a new ADR").

## Out of scope

- Building the production site (E48-T02).
- Authoring any content.
- A public-facing/marketing site — the docs site is private, Tailscale-reachable only.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: The question is answered with evidence
  Given the timebox has elapsed
  Then a comparison table with measured CI build times and a prototype link exists for every candidate
  And the chosen option is stated with the decision drivers that selected it

Scenario: Offline build is proven, not assumed
  Given the prototype build is run in a container with networking disabled
  Then the chosen toolchain completes the build successfully
  And any candidate that cannot is eliminated on that basis alone and this is recorded

Scenario: Mermaid and OpenAPI rendering are both proven
  Given docs/plan/20-architecture.md (mermaid C4 diagrams) and docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml
  When the prototype builds
  Then every mermaid diagram renders and every operation in the OpenAPI file appears in the reference
  And an operation added to the YAML but not regenerated is detectable by a staleness check

Scenario: Decision is recorded even if it is "defer"
  Given the spike concludes
  Then an ADR exists in docs/plan/27-adrs/ with status decided or proposed-with-deadline
  And follow-up tickets are filed against whichever path was chosen
```

## Technical notes / design

Decision criteria are pre-committed so the result is not argued after the fact:

- **Hard requirement**: builds with no network access (CI runners for this repo are already network-restricted for tests, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.4 network-allowlist lint); renders mermaid; total docs build ≤3 min.
- **Hard requirement**: the REST reference is generated from the single OpenAPI source; no second copy of endpoint documentation exists anywhere (the C-16.5 single-source-of-truth rule applied to docs).
- **Tiebreaker**: authoring ergonomics for backend engineers writing runbooks at 2 a.m. — plain Markdown with front-matter beats anything requiring JSX.

Prototype lives on `spike/docs-toolchain`, explicitly throwaway unless the ADR says otherwise. Expected output of the staleness check is the `make docs && git diff --exit-code` pattern, error code `DOC-002`.

## Test plan

- Prototype build executed three times per candidate; median CI wall-clock recorded.
- Offline build executed in `docker run --network=none`.
- Link-check run over the prototype output; count of false positives recorded (a noisy link checker is a real maintenance cost).
- No production tests; this spike ships no production code.

## Security notes

The chosen toolchain becomes a build-time dependency of a repo that holds trading-system source: evaluate supply-chain surface (transitive dependency count, maintenance status, whether it executes arbitrary plugins from config) per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §6.13. Any candidate requiring a network fetch at build time is rejected on both determinism and supply-chain grounds. Record the SCA result for the chosen tool.

## Accessibility notes

The docs site is a UI surface the team uses: the chosen theme must give ≥4.5:1 text contrast, keyboard-navigable search, and real heading structure — checked in the prototype with axe-core on one representative page. Any candidate failing this is documented as failing, not silently accepted.

## Performance notes

Build ≤3 min on CI; the built site's first contentful paint on a docs page ≤1 s on the reference hardware (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1) — it is read during incidents, so it must not be slow.

## Observability

None in production. The spike records build-time measurements as ticket artefacts.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Comparison table with measured numbers attached to the ticket.
- [ ] Prototype branch linked; marked throwaway or promoted explicitly.
- [ ] ADR written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, indexed in `27-adrs/README.md` and `20-architecture.md` §16.
- [ ] Follow-up scope for E48-T02 confirmed or adjusted.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

## Dependencies

None blocking; informed by the existing Redocly usage in the `contracts` CI gate (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §5.0).

## Branch

`spike/docs-toolchain`. PR: ADR only; prototype not merged.

## References

- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3, §9.4
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §5, §16
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §5.0
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md`

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md (PRR/runbook procedures)
2. docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md (R5 exit criteria)
3. docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md (DoR/DoD)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan` (owner: @CandleViewer/architecture)
- `docs/runbooks/ or docs/plan/ per ticket Scope`

**Interfaces you must not break**
- WS topics/framing in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (contract-first per C-6.1)

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint  # docs-site link/markdown checks`
- `make gen && git diff --exit-code  # if generated reference docs touched`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `spike/docs-toolchain`
- PR title: "E48-K01: Spike: choose the documentation toolchain and reference-generation pipeline"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E48-K01>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/docs/plan/` (@CandleViewer/architecture); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/spike, area/docs, priority/p2

**Done means**
- Comparison table with measured numbers attached to the ticket.
- Prototype branch linked; marked throwaway or promoted explicitly.
- ADR written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`, indexed in `27-adrs/README.md` and `20-architecture.md` §16.
- Follow-up scope for E48-T02 confirmed or adjusted.
- Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.

**Do NOT**
- Building the production site (E48-T02).
- Authoring any content.
- A public-facing/marketing site — the docs site is private, Tailscale-reachable only.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E48-K01` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Reconcile architecture, schema and ADR documents with the system as built
body:
## Context

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, at Epic close, that "relevant `docs/plan/2x-*` architecture/schema docs and `docs/plan/1x-*` product docs reflect final shipped behavior (not the original proposal) if they diverged during implementation". Across 48 epics and 26 sprints that reconciliation will have been done unevenly. R5 exit criterion 6 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3) requires a complete and correct ADR index, and §9.4's Docs gate requires review by a non-author.

This task is the single sweep that makes the architecture set trustworthy at GA: `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` (C4 L1–L3, module register, failure register F1–F18, observability §12, ADR index §16), `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` (Postgres DDL, QuestDB tables, retention, migrations), `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` (domain events, rule IR, OMS state machine, trade-group model, exchange-adapter interface), `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`, and every record in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`.

One record is explicitly unfinished: **ADR-0011 Electron vs Tauri** is still `proposed` with a decision deadline of "end of Sprint 03" (`docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md`). Shipping GA with a `proposed` ADR whose deadline passed 23 sprints earlier is exactly the drift this task exists to eliminate.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Drift audit** of `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`, `21-database-schema.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `26-chart-engine-design.md` against the shipped code (`services/api/candleviewer/**`, `packages/chart-engine/**`, `services/api/candleviewer/migrations/**`), producing a written delta list before any edits, so the size of the divergence is itself recorded.
- **Corrections applied** to those documents, each as a separate reviewable PR per document.
- **Postgres schema reconciliation**: the DDL in `21-database-schema.md` regenerated/diffed against the actual Alembic head for every table (`users`, `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access`, `sessions`, `mfa_methods`, `exchange_accounts`, `api_keys`, `account_profiles`, `trade_groups`, `trade_group_legs`, `orders`, `order_events`, `executions`, `positions`, `wallet_balances`, `instruments`, `rules`, `rule_versions`, `rule_runs`, `rule_events`, `alerts`, `alert_deliveries`, `recorded_symbols`, `recording_sessions`, `recording_gaps`, `retention_policies`, `replay_sessions`, `journal_trades`, `journal_tags`, `workspaces`, `layouts`, `layout_panes`, `chart_templates`, `drawings`, `indicator_presets`, `hotkey_profiles`, `settings`, `feature_flags`, `feature_flag_overrides`, `audit_log`, `audit_checkpoints`, `system_events`, `backups`, `outbox`) and the QuestDB tables (`trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `tickers`, `klines`, `liquidations`, `open_interest`, `funding_rates`, `bars_time`, `footprint_cells`, `profiles`, `orderflow_metrics`, `heatmap_cells`, `engine_metrics`).
- **Failure register refresh**: `20-architecture.md` §11.1 F1–F18 updated with the behaviour actually implemented and verified by E45's chaos catalogue; §11.2 recovery objectives updated with measured, not aspirational, numbers (feeding E48-T04).
- **ADR sweep**: every ADR-0001..0015 re-read; each marked `decided` (unchanged), amended with a dated amendment section, or superseded by a new record. **ADR-0011 resolved** to `decided` (Electron, per the locked decision in `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`) or superseded with the actual outcome of the E06/E10 spike. Every ADR written during R1–R5 by other epics (E44-T06, E45-T11, E46-T11 each write an "ADR-0016") **de-conflicted into unique sequential numbers** and indexed.
- **ADR index reconciled** in both `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md` and `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §16 — the two must agree exactly, checked by a script (`DOC-001` class).
- `scripts/check-adr-index.py` enforcing: every file in `27-adrs/` appears in both indexes with matching status; no duplicate ADR numbers; no `proposed` ADR whose stated deadline has passed.

## Out of scope

- Changing system behaviour to match a document — if the document was right and the code is wrong, that is a Bug filed against E49, not a doc edit.
- Product docs `10-*`..`18-*` other than where an architecture change invalidated them (screen/component catalogue corrections belong to E49's design-QA sweep).
- Writing new ADRs for decisions made inside other R5 epics — those epics own their own records; this task only de-conflicts numbering and indexing.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: The ADR index is internally consistent
  Given every file in docs/plan/27-adrs/ matching ADR-*.md
  When scripts/check-adr-index.py runs
  Then each record appears in 27-adrs/README.md and in 20-architecture.md §16 with identical status
  And adding an ADR file without indexing it makes the script exit non-zero

Scenario: No ADR is left proposed past its deadline
  Given ADR-0011 has status proposed with deadline "end of Sprint 03"
  When the check runs during Sprint 25
  Then it fails until ADR-0011 is decided or superseded
  And after resolution the check passes and the outcome names the shell actually shipped

Scenario: Documented schema matches the migrated database
  Given a scratch database migrated to the Alembic head
  When the schema comparison runs against docs/plan/21-database-schema.md
  Then every table, column, type, nullability and enum matches
  And a column present in the database but absent from the document fails the comparison naming the table and column

Scenario: Divergence is recorded, not silently fixed
  Given the drift audit finds a difference between a document and the code
  Then the delta list records the difference, its direction, and the decision taken (document corrected / bug filed)
  And a difference resolved as "bug filed" has a real E49 ticket key recorded against it
```

## Technical notes / design

The database comparison reuses the mechanism already mandated by the `contracts` CI gate: `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §5.0 requires "all `x-db-enum` schemas match the migrated database". This task extends that from enums to full table shape, using SQLAlchemy reflection against a migrated scratch Postgres and comparing to the parsed DDL blocks in `21-database-schema.md`. QuestDB tables are compared via `SHOW COLUMNS`.

Checker error codes introduced here (registered in the shared `DOC-` table used by E48-T02): `DOC-001` missing/unindexed artefact, `DOC-008` ADR index mismatch, `DOC-009` schema/document divergence.

ADR renumbering rule: `27-adrs/README.md` forbids editing a `decided` record's outcome in place. Where two R5 epics both wrote "ADR-0016", the earlier-merged record keeps 0016 and the later is renumbered at file level with a redirect note; both indexes are updated in the same PR (README rule 4).

The drift audit is captured as `docs/plan/reconciliation/2027-09-ga-drift.md` — a dated artefact, because "how far did the docs drift over 26 sprints" is a process input for the retro, not just a chore.

## Test plan

- **Unit** — `scripts/check-adr-index.py`: clean tree exits 0; unindexed ADR, duplicate number, status mismatch, and expired `proposed` deadline each exit non-zero with the right code. Coverage ≥85%.
- **Integration** — schema comparison run against a scratch Postgres migrated to head in CI; a deliberately dropped column must fail it.
- **Contract** — the existing `contracts` job must remain green after any `x-db-enum` correction.
- **Review** — each corrected document reviewed by an engineer who did not work on the corresponding subsystem (the §9.4 non-author rule applied at the subsystem level, which is stricter and cheap here).
- Fixtures: scratch database from `packages/fixtures` bootstrap; no live Bybit calls.

## Security notes

The architecture documents describe trust boundaries (`20-architecture.md` §2.2), the key vault (`ADR-0009`) and the auth model (`ADR-0010`). Corrections must not add operational secrets, real hostnames or real account identifiers; the `DOC-006` secret scan from E48-T02 runs over these files too. Classification: internal/confidential. If the drift audit reveals that a shipped control is weaker than the documented one (e.g. an RBAC scope widened during implementation), that is a **security finding**, raised to E48-X02 and the Security engineer immediately, not a documentation edit.

## Accessibility notes

N/A — no UI surface. (Mermaid diagrams gain or retain a text summary sentence beneath them so the architecture set is readable without rendering, which is a docs-quality rule, not a WCAG obligation here.)

## Performance notes

The schema comparison adds ≤60 s to CI. No runtime impact.

## Observability

`docs.checker_failed{code="DOC-008"|"DOC-009"}` emitted by CI so index/schema drift is trended rather than rediscovered each release.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Drift audit artefact `docs/plan/reconciliation/2027-09-ga-drift.md` merged.
- [ ] All four architecture/schema documents corrected; each PR approved by a non-author.
- [ ] ADR sweep complete; ADR-0011 resolved; numbering de-conflicted; both indexes agree.
- [ ] `scripts/check-adr-index.py` and the schema comparison are required CI checks.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the new scripts.
- [ ] Any code/document divergence resolved as a bug has an E49 ticket linked.
- [ ] Demo: before/after drift summary shown at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PR(s) merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

- **E46**, **E45**, **E44** must have landed their behaviour changes and their own ADRs, or the reconciliation reconciles against a moving target.

## Branch

`chore/docs-ga-readiness-arch-reconcile`. Split into one PR per document plus one for the scripts; ≤400 LOC each.

## References

- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §5, §11, §12, §16
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `26-chart-engine-design.md`
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md` (ADR house rules), `ADR-0011-electron-vs-tauri.md`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §5.0
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3, §9.4

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md (PRR/runbook procedures)
2. docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md (R5 exit criteria)
3. docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md (DoR/DoD)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan` (owner: @CandleViewer/architecture)
- `docs/runbooks/ or docs/plan/ per ticket Scope`

**Interfaces you must not break**
- DB tables named in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` (no schema change without a reviewed migration)

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint  # docs-site link/markdown checks`
- `make gen && git diff --exit-code  # if generated reference docs touched`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/docs-ga-readiness-arch-reconcile`
- PR title: "E48-T01: Reconcile architecture, schema and ADR documents with the system as built"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E48-T01>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/docs/plan/` (@CandleViewer/architecture); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/chore, area/docs, priority/p1, documentation

**Done means**
- Drift audit artefact `docs/plan/reconciliation/2027-09-ga-drift.md` merged.
- All four architecture/schema documents corrected; each PR approved by a non-author.
- ADR sweep complete; ADR-0011 resolved; numbering de-conflicted; both indexes agree.
- `scripts/check-adr-index.py` and the schema comparison are required CI checks.
- Coverage ≥85% on the new scripts.
- Any code/document divergence resolved as a bug has an E49 ticket linked.

**Do NOT**
- Changing system behaviour to match a document — if the document was right and the code is wrong, that is a Bug filed against E49, not a doc edit.
- Product docs `10-*`..`18-*` other than where an architecture change invalidated them (screen/component catalogue corrections belong to E49's design-QA sweep).
- Writing new ADRs for decisions made inside other R5 epics — those epics own their own records; this task only de-conflicts numbering and indexing.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E48-T01` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Burn down defects and sweep design QA to a defensible GA bar
body:
## Context
R5 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9, sprints S23–S26, 2027-02-26 → 2027-03-25, version `1.1.0` GA) has four goals; this epic owns goal 3: *"Burn down accumulated defects, accepted risks and design-QA findings to a defensible level."* By the time R5 opens, twenty-two months of delivery (E01–E45) have produced a bug backlog that was triaged under the SLAs in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 but deliberately deferred where severity allowed ("P2 … may be scheduled next sprint with owner sign-off", "P3 … backlog, no release block"). In parallel, every net-new UI story shipped with a `design-qa` DoD clause (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2) whose discrepancies were allowed to be *"filed as a follow-up Bug"* rather than fixed in-story. Those two deferral valves are what this epic closes.

E49 is a **cross-area sweep**: it touches every module and every story domain rather than introducing new capability. Its four workstreams are (1) defect triage and burn-down, (2) a design-QA pass over every screen in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` against the checklist in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12, (3) an empty/loading/error state and copy audit centred on the shared state patterns SCR-150…SCR-159, and (4) a hotkey conflict audit plus the accepted-risk re-review with expiry enforcement demanded by `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` §1.3 and roadmap exit criterion 9.3.4.

E49 is the last epic to close before GA (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §12.6: `R5 → GA | e49 [S23-S26], e48 [S25-S26] | 2027-03-25`), and the roadmap dependency graph records `E47 --> E49` and `E43 --> E49`: accessibility findings (E47) and pen-test remediation leftovers (E43) both flow into this burn-down queue.

References: `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`, `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6 (Bug DoR/DoD), `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11, `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md` §12–§13, `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` §1.3, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Triage & measurement**: a single defect queue with enforced severity/SLA fields, saved board queries, a weekly triage ritual, and a burn-down/ageing dashboard so "defensible level" is a number, not an opinion (E49-T01, E49-T02).
- **Root-cause clustering spike** over the accumulated backlog so fixes attack themes, not symptoms (E49-K01).
- **Three burn-down waves**: P0/P1 to zero (E49-S01, E49-S02) and P2 down to ≤10 with owners and target sprints (E49-S03), matching roadmap exit criterion 9.3.3.
- **Design-QA remediation** of token/spacing/type/state discrepancies across the screens catalogue (E49-S04), driven by the audit protocol and findings ledger from E49-D01.
- **State-pattern remediation**: every empty / loading / error / disconnected / degraded / 403 / 404 / crash / rate-limited surface conforms to SCR-150…SCR-159 and CMP-014, CMP-015, CMP-026, CMP-027, CMP-028, CMP-029, CMP-089, CMP-090, CMP-091, CMP-092 (E49-S05, design in E49-D02).
- **Copy review** across all user-visible strings incl. error registry messages (E49-S06, design/content spec in E49-D03).
- **Hotkey conflict audit** across every context in SCR-013 and SCR-113 satisfying US-SET-002's conflict-detection and reserved-key scenarios, plus a CI lint that keeps the keymap conflict-free (E49-S07, E49-T04).
- **Accepted-risk re-review with expiry enforcement** over `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` (E49-T03).
- **Doc reconciliation + ADR** recording the GA defect-disposition policy (E49-T05).
- **Design track**: E49-D01…E49-D05 (audit protocol, state-pattern spec, copy/terminology spec, motion sweep, final design sign-off).
- **QA track**: E49-Q01…E49-Q04 (GA regression pack, exploratory charters/bug bash, state-matrix black-box plan, a11y + QA sign-off).
- **Security track**: E49-X01, E49-X02 (STRIDE of the fix/hotfix path, security regression verification of every fix).

## Out of scope
- New product capability of any kind. A defect whose fix requires new capability is re-filed as a post-GA Story, not absorbed here.
- Performance optimisation work — owned by **E46**; E49 only files and verifies perf *defects* against E46's budgets.
- Accessibility remediation of the WCAG audit itself — owned by **E47**; E49 verifies that E47's fixes did not regress and absorbs only the residual, non-a11y design-QA findings.
- Documentation authoring, runbooks and the GA checklist — owned by **E48**.
- Pen-test finding remediation — owned by **E43**; residual low-severity findings that E43 deferred enter this queue as normal bugs.
- Android and any separate admin application (owner decision 2026-09-14; admin screens are RBAC-gated screens inside the web app).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The GA defect bar is met
  Given the GA candidate build at the end of S26
  When the defect queue is reported
  Then there are zero open P0 and zero open P1 bugs against shipped scope
  And open P2 bugs number at most 10, each with a named owner and a target post-GA sprint
  And every open P3 has been triaged with a recorded disposition

Scenario: Design QA is closed out per screen
  Given the design-QA findings ledger produced by E49-D01
  When the ledger is reviewed at the S25 design sign-off
  Then every screen in docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md has a recorded verdict of pass or accepted-exception
  And every accepted exception names an owner, a reason and a post-GA ticket

Scenario: Accepted risks are re-decided, not extended
  Given docs/plan/32-risk-register.md contains risks with Status "Accepted"
  When the R5 expiry enforcement pass runs
  Then every accepted risk has a current owner, an expiry date and a dated review record
  And any acceptance whose expiry has passed has been explicitly re-decided (re-accepted with a new expiry, mitigated, or escalated), never silently carried

Scenario: A regression sneaks in during burn-down
  Given a fix merged in a burn-down wave breaks an unrelated area
  When the GA regression pack (E49-Q01) runs nightly
  Then the failure is detected within one nightly cycle
  And the regression is filed at the severity of the broken area, blocking the wave's closure until fixed

Scenario: No bug closes without a guard
  Given a bug ticket in this epic is moved to Done
  When its Definition of Done is checked
  Then a regression test exists at the appropriate pyramid layer that fails on the pre-fix commit and passes after
  Or the bug is a pure documentation/cosmetic P3 with that exemption stated explicitly on the ticket
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Queue model.** One GitHub Project view backed by the existing schema (`Kind=Bug`, `Priority`, `Component`, `Perspective`, `Risk`, `Sprint`). No new tracker. Severity mapping is exactly `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 (P0 2 h triage / P1 1 business day / P2 3 business days / P3 1 sprint).
- **Wave cadence.** S23 = triage + clustering + wave 1; S24 = wave 2 + design-QA remediation + copy; S25 = P2 sweep + state remediation + design sign-off; S26 = verification, GA regression, sign-offs. Fix PRs stay ≤400 LOC per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`; each wave is a series of small PRs, never a mega-PR.
- **Themes over symptoms.** E49-K01 clusters the backlog by root-cause family (state-machine races, token drift, missing empty/error states, formatting/locale, keymap, WS reconnect edge cases, RBAC copy leakage). A cluster with ≥3 members must be fixed at its shared root, with a single guard test covering the family.
- **Freeze discipline.** From the start of S26 week 2 the GA candidate is under change freeze: only P0/P1 fixes merge, each requiring the hotfix review path in `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §8.
- **Definition of "defensible".** Codified in the ADR from E49-T05: zero P0/P1; ≤10 P2 with owners; all P3 triaged; every accepted risk in-date; every design-QA finding pass-or-accepted; regression guard per closed bug.

## Test plan
- **Regression pack (E49-Q01)**: consolidated Playwright web + Electron suite covering the primary trading flow, admin surfaces, replay and the state matrix; runs nightly across S23–S26 and on every burn-down PR's merge queue entry.
- **Exploratory charters (E49-Q02)**: 60–120 min charters per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 for OMS/order path, rule engine, fan-out, chart-engine visual correctness at extreme density, admin/RBAC probing; plus two cross-team bug bashes.
- **State matrix (E49-Q04)**: black-box plan asserting every panel's empty / loading / error / disconnected / degraded / permission-denied / rate-limited rendering against SCR-150…SCR-159.
- **A11y (E49-Q03)**: axe-core, pa11y-ci catalogue sweep and a manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass over the GA candidate, confirming E47's remediation held.
- **Security (E49-X02)**: SAST/SCA/secrets/DAST sweep on the GA candidate; targeted re-test of every fix touching auth, RBAC, keys, OMS or fan-out.
- Coverage gates unchanged: ≥85% backend/engine, ≥80% frontend; a burn-down PR may not regress its package baseline.

## Security notes
Threats from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` relevant to a burn-down epic are process threats rather than feature threats: a rushed fix bypassing review (tampering), a hotfix path used to ship unreviewed code (elevation of privilege), a "cosmetic" copy change leaking existence of admin objects in a 403/404 (information disclosure — SCR-154/SCR-155 explicitly require identical 404 copy for admin routes), and a regression re-opening a closed pen-test finding (repudiation of the E43 sign-off). E49-X01 models these with STRIDE; E49-X02 verifies them on the candidate. Data classification: fixes may touch secrets (`api_keys`), financial state (OMS tables) and PII (users) — any such fix carries the `security` label and a Security-engineer review per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8.

## Accessibility notes
Every UI fix in this epic re-enters the a11y gate: axe-core green on the touched screen, keyboard-only path verified, focus order and visible focus checked against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. Copy fixes must preserve accessible names and live-region semantics (a shorter string is not automatically a better accessible name). The state-pattern work is a11y-load-bearing: SCR-151 forbids a bare "No data", SCR-152 mandates a single `role="alert"` then a persistent banner, SCR-153 mandates `role="status"` naming the degraded capability.

## Performance notes
E49 must not regress E46's budgets: the CI-enforced budget checks from E46 (frame budget, WS→pixel latency, startup and workspace-restore time) are required checks on every burn-down PR, and a >5% regression on any hard budget fails the build per `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.4. Fixes to hot paths (chart engine, book application, fan-out serialisation) additionally record a before/after benchmark on the ticket.

## Observability
- Metrics: `defects_open{severity}`, `defects_opened_total`, `defects_closed_total`, `defect_age_days` histogram, `sla_breach_total{severity}` exported from the triage tooling into the existing Prometheus/Grafana stack.
- A GA-readiness Grafana panel showing the burn-down curve against the S26 target line.
- Audit: risk-register re-review decisions are recorded as dated entries in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`; hotkey rebinding of trading actions remains audited as `hotkey.trading_binding_changed`.
- Analytics already emitted by the state screens (`empty_state_shown`, `error.403_shown`, `error.404_shown`, `app.error_boundary_triggered`, `degraded.entered`, `ratelimit.hit`) is used as the *input* to the state audit: surfaces users hit often and should not.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child ticket Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded Won't/Later disposition.
- [ ] Zero open P0/P1; ≤10 open P2 with owners and target sprints; all P3 triaged.
- [ ] Design-QA ledger closed: every screen pass-or-accepted; CDO/design sign-off recorded (E49-D05).
- [ ] Every accepted risk in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` in-date with a dated review record.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core + pa11y-ci clean on the GA candidate; manual screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] perf: no E46 budget regression on the GA candidate; 72 h soak unaffected by burn-down merges.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, GA scan sweep clean or accepted, Security-engineer sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off: GA regression pack green, charter notes attached, epic-level exploratory pass recorded.
- [ ] Docs: plan docs reconciled with shipped behaviour; ADR for the GA defect-disposition policy merged.
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at the final Sprint Review with the burn-down curve and the design-QA ledger shown.
- [ ] Retro note filed with process learnings as Chore tickets.

## Dependencies
- **E47 Accessibility conformance** (roadmap edge `E47 --> E49`): a11y findings that E47 cannot close in S23–S25 arrive here as bugs; E49's verification pass confirms E47's fixes.
- **E43 Security hardening & pen-test remediation** (roadmap edge `E43 --> E49`): residual low-severity pen-test findings enter this queue.

**Non-blocking scope inputs (not `blocked_by`).** The roadmap dependency graph (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §13) encodes exactly two direct predecessors of E49 — `E47 --> E49` and `E43 --> E49` — so only those two appear in `blocked_by`. The epics below supply scope and gates to E49 but are *not* direct graph predecessors; they are reached transitively (E42 → E43, E44 → E47, E44 → E46 → E48) and E49 can start without them being complete:
- **E46 Performance hardening** (transitive via `E44 --> E46`): E46's CI-enforced budgets are the gate every burn-down PR must pass once they land; until then the pre-existing budget checks apply.
- **E44 Live-enablement gating** (transitive via `E44 --> E47 --> E49`): live-mode surfaces are included in the design-QA and state sweeps as they become available.
- **E42 Admin screens** (transitive via `E42 --> E43 --> E49`): admin surfaces (SCR-120…SCR-149) are in the sweep scope.
- **E48 Documentation, runbooks & GA readiness**: consumes E49's ledger and ADR for the GA checklist.

## Branch
`feat/defect-burndown-<short>` per child; fixes use `fix/<area>-<short>` per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`. PR size: ≤400 LOC diff; one root-cause cluster per PR; never batch unrelated fixes.

## References

- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 (black-box QA process, bug taxonomy, white-box checklist), §12 (a11y protocol).
