title: Tune QuestDB replay-scan queries and the engine_metrics write path
body:
## Context
Replay is a hard budget: **#15** requires sustaining up to 100× playback "without violating budget #1's frame floor… must not crash/desync", and §9's replay scenario runs it against a recorded 24 h fixture. At 100× the data-fetch path, not the render path, is the likely limiter: replay scans `trades`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `bars_time`, `footprint_cells` and `heatmap_cells` in QuestDB (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4) over wide time ranges, and `orderbook_deltas` is noted there as "the largest stream by far" (~10.6 GB/day/symbol at 200 depth per §'s sizing table). These queries have never been tuned or even systematically measured.

Additionally, E46-T01 optionally writes 2 Hz engine telemetry into `engine_metrics` (§4.13), and `questdb_write_seconds` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12.1) is listed as a saturation signal — the new write volume must not disturb the ingestion write path that budget #5's zero-loss guarantee depends on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Build a replay-scan benchmark: for each of the six tables above, measure cold and warm query latency for the access patterns replay actually uses (a forward window scan with a moving cursor, a point-in-time snapshot fetch, and a bulk pre-fetch of the next N seconds), at 1×, 20× and 100× playback against a recorded 24 h fixture.
- Tune what the measurements show. Candidates to confirm: partition-aligned range predicates so QuestDB prunes partitions rather than scanning; designated-timestamp ordering exploited rather than re-sorted; `SAMPLE BY`/`LATEST ON` used where it replaces an application-side loop; column selection narrowed (never `SELECT *` on `orderbook_deltas`); symbol-column indexing where the cardinality justifies it; prefetch window sized so replay stays ahead of playback at 100× without pulling the whole day into memory.
- Verify the replay prefetch honours the backend memory budget (#8) — pulling a 100× window must not become an unbounded buffer, which would also violate E46-T07's bounded-buffer rule.
- Validate the cold-tier path: replay over a window that has been archived to Parquet/DuckDB (`21-database-schema.md` §5, the `read_parquet` views) must work and be measured too, because the 30-day retention default means any replay older than that hits cold storage. Record the cold-tier numbers separately — they will be slower, and the product needs to know by how much.
- Measure `engine_metrics` write cost at the 2 Hz × panes rate and confirm ingestion write latency (`questdb_write_seconds`) is unaffected; if it is affected, batch the telemetry writes or drop the `engine_metrics` sink (it is explicitly secondary — "Prometheus remains the primary metrics path", §4.13).
- Confirm the retention/eviction jobs (§'s retention table: `orderbook_deltas` 7 d hot, `heatmap_cells` 7 d hot, `engine_metrics` 14 d then drop) run without disturbing live ingestion, since a compaction storm during market hours is a realistic cause of a budget breach.

## Out of scope
- Changing the schema, partitioning strategy or retention policy as a product decision — measuring and proposing is in scope; a schema change requires an ADR and the storage owner (E16/E03).
- Postgres query tuning (no evidence it is hot; file a separate ticket if E46-T04's report says otherwise).
- Replay UX, scrubbing or speed controls (E26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Replay sustains 100x from hot storage
  Given a recorded 24-hour fixture in QuestDB and replay at 100x speed
  Then the data-fetch path keeps the replay cursor supplied without stalling
  And frame rate stays at or above the 30fps floor and no desync is detected, satisfying budget #15

Scenario: Query cost is measured per table and per pattern
  When the replay-scan benchmark runs
  Then cold and warm latency is reported for each of trades, orderbook_deltas, orderbook_snapshots, bars_time, footprint_cells and heatmap_cells, for each of the three access patterns

Scenario: Prefetch stays bounded
  Given replay at 100x with a wide prefetch window
  Then the replay buffer respects a documented maximum size
  And backend resident memory stays within budget #8

Scenario: Cold-tier replay works and its cost is known
  Given a replay window older than the hot retention period so it resolves through the Parquet/DuckDB views
  Then the replay completes correctly
  And its measured latency is recorded and documented as the cold-tier expectation, distinct from the hot-tier number

Scenario: Telemetry writes do not disturb ingestion
  Given engine_metrics is being written at the 2Hz sampling rate while 10 symbols ingest at full cadence
  Then questdb_write_seconds for the ingestion path is unchanged within measurement noise
  And the ingestion message-loss counter remains zero
```

## Technical notes / design
Partition pruning is the single highest-leverage item in QuestDB: a range predicate on the designated timestamp that the planner can use to skip partitions turns a full scan into a bounded read. Verify with the query plan, not by timing alone — a query that got faster because the OS page cache was warm teaches nothing.

`orderbook_deltas` is the table that will hurt. If per-delta replay at 100× cannot be made to work from raw deltas, the correct answer is likely to replay from `orderbook_snapshots` plus a shorter delta tail (the same shape the retention policy's downsample-to-1 s-snapshots action already uses past 180 days). That is a replay-architecture proposal, so raise it with E26's owner and the Architect rather than implementing it unilaterally.

Keep measurements honest: report cold (page cache dropped) and warm separately, state which is which, and run ≥3 repetitions per §7.4's flake-tolerance rule.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: query-builder tests asserting the generated SQL carries a partition-aligned timestamp predicate and an explicit column list for every replay query (a `SELECT *` on `orderbook_deltas` should fail a test, not a review).
- **Integration**: replay correctness over a recorded fixture — the reconstructed book at time T must equal the recorded book at time T, before and after tuning (no optimisation may change replayed data).
- **Perf**: the replay-scan benchmark at 1×/20×/100×, hot and cold tier, 3 runs each; §9's replay scenario end-to-end.
- **Soak-adjacent**: telemetry write load concurrent with a 1 h ingestion run, asserting `questdb_write_seconds` unchanged.
- Coverage ≥85 % on changed backend lines.

## Security notes
Query construction must remain parameterised — a replay window or symbol arriving from the UI and concatenated into SQL is an injection surface (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md`); assert parameterisation in the query-builder tests and keep the SAST rule that flags string-built SQL (E46-X02 owns the rule). Recorded market data is not secret, but a replay endpoint that accepts an arbitrary unbounded range is a denial-of-service surface against the database — confirm the range is validated and bounded server-side, not merely by the UI.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend/storage only.

## Performance notes
Binding: budget #15 (100× replay, no crash/desync, 30 fps floor); budget #8 ≤300 MB per symbol including replay buffers; budget #5 zero undetected ingestion loss while replay and telemetry writes run; `questdb_write_seconds` unchanged for the ingestion path; §12 storage growth figures unaffected.

## Observability
Adds a `replay_scan_seconds{table,pattern,tier}` histogram (tier = hot|cold) — currently no metric describes replay fetch cost at all, which is why this is a measurement ticket as much as a tuning one. `questdb_write_seconds` asserted, not just scraped.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five Gherkin scenarios verified.
- [ ] Per-table, per-pattern, hot and cold latency table recorded in the ticket and summarised in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.14 operational notes.
- [ ] Query plans (not just timings) evidencing partition pruning attached.
- [ ] Replay-correctness integration test green before and after tuning.
- [ ] Any proposed schema/replay-architecture change raised as an ADR with E26 and the Architect rather than implemented here.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85 % on changed lines.
- [ ] Reviewed by a backend code owner + the storage owner.

## Dependencies
- **E46-T04** for the backend profile that shows whether storage is on the hot path.
- **E26** owns the replay engine whose queries are being tuned.

## Branch
`feat/e46-perf-questdb-replay-scans`. PR size ≤400 LOC; benchmark first, tuning second.

## References
`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §9, §2 budgets #5, #8, #15 · `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.1, §4.2, §4.9, §4.12, §4.13, §4.14, §5, retention table · `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §12.1 · `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`

1. docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §7 (harness/CI gates)
2. docs/plan/20-architecture.md §12 (observability)
3. .github/workflows/ (existing CI jobs to extend, not replace)

**Repo paths to create/modify**

**Do NOT**

title: Build the startup and workspace-restore harness and hit the 3s cold-start budget
body:
## Context
Budget #10 in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 is a **hard** budget: ≤3 s cold start from Electron app launch to "last-used workspace fully interactive, symbols subscribed", measured by an instrumented `app.whenReady()` → "workspace ready" event on reference hardware (§3.1). §9's load-test table lists "Startup time, cold launch — instrumented Electron launch harness, CI + manual on reference hardware". Budget #9 (bundle size, ≤8 MB gzipped, soft) is measured alongside it and gates at >+10 % vs the last tagged baseline. `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 gate **B9** covers the engine's own slice: cold init to first frame with 100k bars ≤900 ms, SDF atlas from cache ≤5 ms.

Neither the harness nor the "workspace ready" event exists. Budget #10 is described as an R1 exit gate in §2 but has never been mechanically measured, which means it is currently an assertion rather than a fact — exactly the kind of gap R5 exists to close.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Define and emit the **`workspace_ready`** event with a precise, defensible definition: last-used workspace layout restored, every pane's initial data painted (not merely requested), every symbol subscription confirmed by the WS `sub` ack (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §5), and the UI accepting input. Ambiguity here is the main risk — write the definition into `docs/plan/06-…` §2's budget-#10 row so it cannot drift.
- Instrument the intervening phases so a regression is attributable in the same spirit as §4.3: process launch → `app.whenReady()` → renderer created → bundle parsed/evaluated → auth/session restored → workspace layout loaded → WS connected and authenticated → subscriptions acked → first paint per pane → `workspace_ready`.
- An automatable cold-start harness (CI-runnable on the Electron build, plus a documented manual procedure on reference hardware per §3.1) producing a per-phase report over ≥3 runs with the median compared to a stored baseline, in the same report schema as E46-T01.
- A **workspace-restore** variant: restoring a heavy 4-pane workspace, measured separately from first-run startup because the two have different bottlenecks.
- Bundle-size measurement (budget #9) wired into the same report: gzipped initial bundle from the bundle analyzer, with the code-split boundary respected (chart-engine core counted, lazy-loaded heavy panels excluded).
- Optimise whatever the per-phase report says is over. Candidates to confirm, not assume: deferring non-critical module evaluation, SDF atlas cache warm (B9's ≤5 ms path), parallelising WS connect/auth with layout restore, prefetching the last-used workspace's first data window, and lazy-loading panels that are not in the restored layout.
- Cold-start and bundle-size results handed to E46-T10 for CI enforcement.

## Out of scope
- Backend startup time (covered under E46-T07's process-level work if it proves to matter).
- Changing what a workspace *is* or how layouts are persisted (owned by the LAY domain epics).
- Installer/update-download time — not part of budget #10's definition.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Cold start meets budget
  Given a cold Electron launch on reference hardware with a previously-saved 4-pane workspace
  When the app starts three times and the median is taken
  Then the interval from process launch to workspace_ready is at or below 3 seconds

Scenario: A startup regression is phase-attributable
  Given a deliberate 500ms delay is injected into workspace layout loading
  When the harness runs
  Then the report names the layout-loading phase as the one that grew, without requiring a manual profile

Scenario: workspace_ready means genuinely ready
  Given workspace_ready has fired
  Then every pane in the restored layout has painted real data, every subscription has an acked sub_id, and a keyboard input is accepted and acted upon

Scenario: Bundle budget is measured and tracked
  Given the CI bundle-analyzer step runs on a merge to main
  Then the gzipped initial bundle size is reported
  And a size increase of more than 10% versus the last tagged baseline fails the soft gate and opens a tracked ticket

Scenario: Engine cold init holds its own gate
  Given benchmark B9 (cold init to first frame with 100k bars)
  Then time to first frame is at or below 900ms and the SDF atlas loads from cache in at most 5ms
```

## Technical notes / design
Measurement honesty is the whole point: `workspace_ready` must not fire on "layout painted with skeletons". The acked-subscription condition is what makes it meaningful — a workspace showing empty panes is not interactive in any sense the user recognises. Use the `sub` ack's `sub_id` from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §5 as the machine-checkable condition.

Phase timings use the same report schema (`"schema": 1`) as E46-T01 so E46-T10 has one comparator implementation, not two.

Reference-hardware caveat (§3.1): CI runners are not reference hardware, so the CI gate must run against a *CI baseline* recorded on the CI runner, while the ≤3 s absolute figure is asserted by the documented manual procedure on reference hardware, re-run per release. Both numbers are recorded; conflating them would produce either a permanently-red or a permanently-meaningless gate.

Cold means cold: the harness must clear the OS file cache where the platform allows, or explicitly document that it measures warm-cache start and record the reference-hardware cold number manually. State which was done — an undocumented warm measurement presented as cold is worse than no measurement.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: phase-timer bookkeeping; `workspace_ready` predicate (all conditions required, any one missing keeps it unfired) table-driven over pane/subscription combinations.
- **Integration**: harness runs against the packaged Electron build in nightly CI; injected-delay attribution test kept permanently.
- **Perf**: 3-run median per §7.4 flake-tolerance rules; B9 per-PR; bundle analyzer per merge to `main`.
- **E2E**: a Playwright check that input is accepted immediately after `workspace_ready`.
- Coverage ≥80 % frontend on changed lines.

## Security notes
Startup timing and phase reports include the restored workspace's symbol list, which is user data but not secret. Auth/session restore is one of the measured phases — the harness must never log session tokens or the restored credential material, only phase durations. Confirm the harness's log output against the redaction allow-list from US-OBS-003 ("secrets, keys and tokens are never present in any log at any level, enforced by a serialiser allow-list and verified by a CI test").

## Accessibility notes
`workspace_ready` should coincide with the app being usable by keyboard and by a screen reader, not just by mouse: the ready predicate includes input acceptance, and the E2E check should exercise a keyboard input specifically. Any startup optimisation that defers the DOM-mirror or focus management past `workspace_ready` is not acceptable.

## Performance notes
Binding: budget #10 ≤3 s cold start (hard, reference hardware); budget #9 ≤8 MB gzipped initial bundle (soft, >+10 % vs baseline fails); B9 ≤900 ms engine cold init, ≤5 ms SDF atlas from cache.

## Observability
Emits a `startup_phase_seconds{phase}` histogram through the pushed-frontend-metrics path so field startup regressions are visible, plus the `workspace_ready` duration as a single recorded value per launch.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five Gherkin scenarios verified.
- [ ] `workspace_ready` definition written into `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 budget-#10 row via a reviewed docs PR.
- [ ] Per-phase report emitted in the E46-T01 report schema; injected-delay attribution test permanent.
- [ ] CI baseline (CI runner) and reference-hardware manual number both recorded; cold-vs-warm stated explicitly.
- [ ] Bundle-size step wired and baselined.
- [ ] Before/after numbers in the PR for any optimisation made.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80 % frontend on changed lines; B9 green.

## Dependencies
- **E46-T01** for the shared report schema and baseline file format.

## Branch
`feat/e46-perf-startup`. PR size ≤400 LOC; harness and optimisations in separate PRs.

## References
`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 budgets #9 and #10, §3.1, §7.4, §9 · `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §13 (B9) · `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §5 · `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-OBS-003, US-CHART-010

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- WS topics/framing in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (contract-first per C-6.1)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e46-perf-startup`
- PR title: "E46-T09: Build the startup and workspace-restore harness and hit the 3s cold-start budget"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E46-T09>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/tech, area/chart-engine, area/web, priority/p2, perf

**Done means**
- All five Gherkin scenarios verified.
- `workspace_ready` definition written into `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 budget-#10 row via a reviewed docs PR.
- Per-phase report emitted in the E46-T01 report schema; injected-delay attribution test permanent.
- CI baseline (CI runner) and reference-hardware manual number both recorded; cold-vs-warm stated explicitly.
- Bundle-size step wired and baselined.
- Before/after numbers in the PR for any optimisation made.

**Do NOT**
- Backend startup time (covered under E46-T07's process-level work if it proves to matter).
- Changing what a workspace *is* or how layouts are persisted (owned by the LAY domain epics).
- Installer/update-download time — not part of budget #10's definition.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E46-T09` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Promote every hard budget to a CI-enforced required check with regression alarms
body:
## Context
This is the ticket that makes E46's work permanent. `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.4 specifies the enforcement model precisely and it is currently implemented only for the chart-engine's B1–B10 gates (`docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §13): every merge to `main` (or nightly for the expensive variants) runs the relevant harnesses, compares p95 against a stored baseline, fails the build on a **>5 % regression** of any hard-budget metric as a **required check**, moves baselines forward only through an explicit reviewed "update performance baseline" PR, and reports p50/p95/p99 across **≥3 repeated runs** with the gate comparing medians to suppress runner noise.

The remaining budgets — WS tick→screen, fan-out, ingestion, memory ceilings, bundle size, startup, backend CPU, storage growth, REST latency, heatmap cadence, replay — have no gate. Without this ticket, every optimisation in E46 decays silently over the first post-GA quarter. The R5 quality gate in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.4 and the epic's first acceptance scenario both require that a deliberate 6 % regression fails the build.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A single **budget registry** (`bench/budgets.yaml` or equivalent, version-controlled) that is the machine-readable form of `06-…` §2: one entry per budget with id, target, hard/soft, harness that measures it, metric key in the harness report, comparison mode (absolute threshold and/or ≤5 % vs baseline), CI trigger (per-PR / nightly / per-release), and the owning plan-doc anchor. One source of truth; the markdown table and this file must not drift, so add a CI check that the registry lists every numbered row in §2.
- A shared **comparator** consuming the E46-T01 report schema (also emitted by T09 and the load harnesses) that applies the §7.4 rules: ≥3 runs, median comparison, absolute-threshold check for hard budgets, ≤5 % regression check vs baseline, >+10 % for the bundle soft gate, and a clear failure message naming the budget, the stage (where applicable), the baseline, the measured value and the delta.
- CI wiring per budget with the right cadence — per-PR for the fast engine benches and bundle size; nightly for Electron, soaks, ingestion, k6/Locust load and replay; per-release-candidate for the manual reference-hardware items (startup absolute figure, 72 h soak).
- **Required-check** registration on `main` for every hard budget's gate, per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`'s required-checks model.
- The **baseline-forward-only** workflow: a `bench/baselines/` directory, a documented "update performance baseline" PR template requiring harness output plus a written rationale, a CODEOWNERS entry so baseline changes need the Architect's approval, and a CI check that a baseline change is never bundled with a functional change in the same PR.
- **Soft-budget alerting**: Prometheus alert rules for sustained breach of the soft budgets (backend CPU/symbol, storage growth/day/symbol, bundle size trend) with the "repeated identical alerts are grouped with an occurrence count" behaviour required by US-OBS-004, and the epic's 3-consecutive-alert escalation to a tracked ticket.
- A **Grafana "Performance budgets" dashboard**: one panel per §2 budget showing the live/field value with the CI baseline drawn as a threshold line.
- The **injected-regression self-test**: a CI job (or a documented, periodically-executed procedure) that injects a 6 % regression into each hard-budget metric and asserts the gate fails — a gate nobody has ever seen fail is not a gate.

## Out of scope
- Writing new harnesses (T01, T06, T09 and the QA tickets own those) — this ticket consumes their outputs.
- Changing any budget target. If a measured reality cannot meet a documented budget, the budget is changed via a reviewed docs PR with the Architect (owned by the ticket that measured it), not by loosening a gate here.
- Post-GA capacity re-planning (§10.3).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every hard budget has a gate
  Given the budget registry
  Then every hard budget in docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §2 has a registry entry with a harness, a metric key and a CI trigger
  And a CI check fails if a budget row exists in the markdown table but not in the registry

Scenario: A regression fails the build
  Given a 6% regression is injected into a hard-budget metric
  When the gate runs
  Then the build fails
  And the failure message names the budget, the measured value, the baseline and the percentage delta

Scenario: Runner noise does not fail the build
  Given three repeated harness runs with normal CI-runner variance and no real regression
  Then the gate compares medians and passes
  And the individual run values are recorded in the job output

Scenario: Baselines only move forward deliberately
  Given a pull request that changes a stored baseline
  Then the PR must contain the harness output and a written rationale
  And it requires Architect approval via CODEOWNERS
  And a PR that mixes a baseline change with a functional change is rejected by a CI check

Scenario: Soft budgets alarm rather than block
  Given backend CPU per symbol exceeds 0.5 vCPU for a sustained window
  Then an alert fires without blocking any build
  And repeated identical alerts are grouped with an occurrence count
  And three consecutive alerts escalate to a tracked ticket

Scenario: The dashboard shows budget versus reality
  Given the Performance budgets Grafana dashboard
  Then each §2 budget has a panel showing the current value with the CI baseline as a threshold line
```

## Technical notes / design
One comparator, one report schema, one registry. The failure mode to avoid is fifteen bespoke gate scripts that each interpret §7.4 slightly differently and rot at different rates; the registry plus comparator is what keeps the enforcement cost near zero as budgets change.

Hard budgets get **two** checks where both are meaningful: the absolute target (e.g. p95 frame ≤16.6 ms) and the ≤5 % relative-to-baseline check. A build that is inside the absolute target but 5 % worse than last week is still a regression worth catching, and a build that improved the baseline should ratchet the baseline forward (via the reviewed PR, never automatically).

Cadence honesty: putting a 24 h soak on a per-PR trigger would be absurd, so the registry's trigger field is load-bearing and the PR-level gate must state clearly which budgets it does *not* cover, so nobody mistakes a green PR for a fully-validated build. The release checklist in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` is where the nightly/per-release budgets get their sign-off.

Reference-hardware budgets (startup absolute, 72 h soak) cannot be CI-enforced on a CI runner; the registry marks them `trigger: release-manual` with a named owner and a procedure link, and the PRR gate checks the recorded evidence exists. Marking them as automated when they are not would be the worst outcome — a false sense of coverage.

## Test plan
- **Unit** (≥85 %): comparator arithmetic (median-of-3, percentage delta, absolute vs relative, soft vs hard); registry parsing and validation; the markdown-vs-registry drift check with a deliberately-desynced fixture.
- **Integration**: the injected-regression self-test per hard budget; the mixed-PR rejection check; the baseline-update workflow exercised end to end on a scratch branch.
- **Contract**: the harness report schema version pinned; a schema bump without a comparator update fails a test.
- **Operational**: alert rules unit-tested with `promtool`; grouping behaviour verified per US-OBS-004.

## Security notes
CI gates that publish performance artefacts must not publish profiling captures, heap snapshots or diagnostics bundles as build artefacts — those can contain order/account data (per E46-T04/T06/X01). Restrict published artefacts to the JSON reports and confirm those carry no market/order data. The baseline-update path is a supply-chain-adjacent control surface: CODEOWNERS approval on `bench/baselines/` prevents a silent "just bump the baseline" that would hide a real regression, and that control is itself worth a line in the security review (E46-X02).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — CI/infrastructure. Related: the axe-core a11y CI checks already required by `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` are unaffected by this work and must remain green.

## Performance notes
Meta-budget: the per-PR gate subset must complete within the existing CI time budget for `main` PRs; if the engine benches at 3 runs each exceed it, move the expensive scenarios to nightly and record that decision in the registry rather than reducing the repetition count below the §7.4 minimum of three.

## Observability
Grafana "Performance budgets" dashboard; alert rules for soft budgets with grouping; CI job output retained per run so a trend can be reconstructed; budget pass/fail published as a build status per budget id so the PRR checklist can read it mechanically.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six Gherkin scenarios verified.
- [ ] Budget registry covers every §2 row; drift check green.
- [ ] Required checks registered on `main` for every hard budget.
- [ ] Injected-regression self-test passes for each hard budget (evidence in the ticket).
- [ ] Baseline-update PR template, CODEOWNERS entry and mixed-PR rejection check in place.
- [ ] Soft-budget alert rules merged as version-controlled config (US-OBS-004 NFR) and `promtool`-tested.
- [ ] Grafana dashboard merged.
- [ ] `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.4 and `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` updated to reference the registry and the release-manual budgets.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85 % on new comparator/registry code.
- [ ] Reviewed by DevSecOps + the Architect.

## Dependencies
All optimisation tickets land first so the baselines captured here are the post-optimisation numbers: **E46-T02, T03, T05, T07, T08, T09**. Baselining before the optimisations would lock in the numbers E46 exists to improve.

## Branch
`feat/e46-perf-ci-budget-gates`. PR size: registry+comparator one PR, CI wiring a second, alerting+dashboard a third.

## References

- **Quarterly full-profiling-pass procedure** (§8 step 7) written down: what is run (the §3.2/§6.4 worst-case stress composite), by whom (Architect + rotating engineer), what is recorded, where the output goes, and how a finding becomes a ticket. - **Doc reconciliation**: update `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` where E46 measured something different from the planned number — with the divergence explained rather than silently rewritten (an epic DoD item). ```gherkin

The "why the CI gate did not catch it" field is the highest-value part of the incident template: every entry that answers it either produces a new gate or a documented, accepted blind spot, which is how the enforcement model improves instead of ossifying.

title: Manual screen-reader passes across the NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver matrix
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 8 defines a pinned screen-reader coverage matrix (NVDA 2024.x in the Electron shell as the P0 release blocker, JAWS 2024.x as a P1 that must fully pass before R4, Chromium+NVDA as the fast-iteration gate, VoiceOver on macOS 14 as a P1 that must fully pass before GA) and a manual protocol: setup, landmark/structure pass, task-based pass, regression checklist, severity bar. R5 is the release where those "before GA" obligations come due.

Automation cannot substitute here. axe-core does not know whether a fill announcement arrives before the user has moved on, whether the DOM mirror of a footprint grid is *comprehensible*, or whether the node-graph rule editor can actually be operated by a blind user. This ticket executes the human passes and turns them into defects and evidence.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Full execution of the standard section 8.2 protocol on the release-candidate build for each matrix row:
  - Row 1 (Electron + NVDA, Windows 11): **full pass**, all six task scripts, every top-level screen's landmark/heading structure.
  - Row 2 (Electron + JAWS): **full pass** - the R4 obligation is re-verified here plus the R5 delta.
  - Row 4 (macOS 14 + VoiceOver): **full pass** - this is the GA gate that has never been run in full.
  - Row 3 (Chromium headless/manual + NVDA): spot-check only, to confirm the CI surface still matches the shell.
- Task scripts executed keyboard+SR only, from the standard section 8.2 item 3 and extended for E47 scope: symbol switch from the watchlist (SCR-100 -> SCR-030); limit order placement on SCR-060 including the SCR-076 confirmation; footprint navigation via the DOM mirror and independently via SCR-045; simulated rule-engine flatten with the position-closed announcement (SCR-063, SCR-087); Demo -> Live switch on SCR-074 with the SCR-075 badge change; admin user creation and permission scope assignment on SCR-121/SCR-122; alert creation and trigger on SCR-091/SCR-092; both rule editors on SCR-081 and SCR-082.
- A **transcript** per task per AT: keystrokes issued and announcements heard, in a plain-text log committed under `qa/evidence/e47/<at>-<date>/`.
- Defect filing for every finding with the `a11y` label, the screen id, the WCAG criterion, the AT and version, severity per the standard section 8.2 item 5, and a reproduction that names keystrokes.
- An updated **living regression checklist** (the file referenced by `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`) recording what was checked, what changed since the previous pass, and the pinned AT versions used.
- A pass summary table feeding `E47-T06` (the conformance report) and `E47-Q09` (sign-off): screen x AT x verdict x blocking defects.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the defects found - remediation is `E47-S01`..`E47-S04` and follow-on tickets.
- Automated axe/Lighthouse/keyboard-E2E execution (`E47-Q03`, `E47-Q04`).
- Any mobile screen reader (TalkBack, iOS VoiceOver) - no mobile client is in scope.
- Non-Electron browsers as production targets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Manual screen-reader conformance passes

  Scenario: NVDA full pass completes on the release candidate
    Given the RC Electron build on Windows 11 23H2 with NVDA 2024.x at default verbosity
    And the tester uses no pointing device for the entire pass
    When every task in the E47 task script is attempted
    Then each task is either completed with correct announcements or filed as a defect
    And a transcript exists for every task

  Scenario: VoiceOver GA gate is executed for the first time in full
    Given the RC Electron build on macOS 14 Sonnoma or later with VoiceOver
    When the full protocol is executed
    Then a verdict is recorded per screen
    And any macOS-only defect is filed separately from its Windows equivalent

  Scenario: Failure case - a task cannot be completed keyboard and SR only
    Given the node-graph rule editor on SCR-082
    When the tester attempts to connect two nodes without a pointing device
    And no documented non-drag equivalent is discoverable
    Then a P0 release-blocking defect is filed against that screen
    And E47-T06 records the screen as non-conformant until the defect is closed

  Scenario: Edge case - streaming data does not steal focus
    Given the tester is midway through the SCR-060 order ticket with the tape streaming
    When a burst of market updates arrives
    Then focus remains on the control the tester left it on
    And any silent focus move is a P0 defect regardless of cause

  Scenario: Regression checklist is updated and versions are pinned
    When the passes complete
    Then the living regression checklist records the exact AT and OS versions used
    And any AT version drift from the standard section 8.1 matrix is recorded as a dated changelog entry
```

## Technical notes / design
- Each pass starts from a **fresh profile** with the default hotkey map and default theme, per the protocol; a pass run on a customised profile is void.
- The replay fixture from `E47-Q01` is used for any task that needs market motion, so two testers on two machines observe the same data.
- JAWS and NVDA disagree on table and grid verbosity; the plan records the AT-specific expected behaviour rather than treating a difference as a defect by default. The rule is: information must be *obtainable*, not identical.
- VoiceOver in Electron historically needs `NSAccessibility` activation; the setup section of the log records the exact launch flags used so the pass is reproducible.
- Findings on canvas surfaces are triaged against the three-layer strategy in the standard section 6 - a missing mirror node is an engine defect (`E47-S02`), a wrong announcement policy is a live-region defect.

## Test plan
The pass is the test. Its own quality gate is a **calibration exercise**: two testers independently run task 3 (footprint navigation) on the same build; their verdicts must agree, and any disagreement is resolved by the Accessibility role and written back into `E47-Q01` as a clarified expected result before the main pass proceeds.

## Security notes
- Passes run against the demo environment. Live credentials are never used, so no real order can be emitted by a tester exploring the order ticket.
- The Demo -> Live switch task is executed against a demo-flagged build where the "Live" target is a sandbox, so the badge and confirm behaviour is exercised without live trading capability.
- Transcripts are scanned for secrets before commit; any accidental capture of a key fragment, token or real account id is scrubbed and reported per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` incident handling.

## Accessibility notes
This entire ticket is accessibility work. Two constraints on the work itself: at least one pass should be run or co-run by a tester who uses a screen reader daily (engaged via the UX research function) rather than only by sighted testers simulating; and evidence artefacts (transcripts, checklists) are plain text so they are themselves accessible.

## Performance notes
The streaming-announcement tasks double as a perceived-performance check: if the DOM mirror or live-region updates cause the UI to stutter under the replay fixture, that is filed as a perf defect against `E47-Q05` rather than dismissed as an AT quirk. The standard's budget is that mirror and live-region work shares the frame budget discipline of `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
- Verdicts land in the QA result store tagged `epic:E47`, `at:<nvda|jaws|voiceover>`, `screen:<SCR-id>`, so the conformance report and the burn-down dashboard both read from one source.
- The pass summary is posted to the release-candidate checklist in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` as a PRR input.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver full passes executed on the RC build, with transcripts committed.
- [ ] Every finding filed with severity, AT, version, screen and WCAG criterion.
- [ ] Living regression checklist updated with the pinned versions and the delta since the previous pass.
- [ ] Calibration exercise completed and any clarified expectations written back into `E47-Q01`.
- [ ] Pass summary table handed to `E47-T06` and `E47-Q09`.
- [ ] Accessibility role signs the passes.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q01` - the task script and expected announcements come from the plan.
- `E47-S01`, `E47-S02` - remediation of the chrome and canvas layers must land or the pass degenerates into re-finding known defects.

## Branch
`chore/e47-sr-passes` (evidence and checklist only; no product code).

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 6 (canvas strategy), 8.1 (matrix), 8.2 (protocol), 8.3 (ownership).
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (manual SR cadence, living regression checklist).
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (RC checklist and PRR gates).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-045, SCR-050, SCR-060, SCR-074, SCR-081, SCR-082, SCR-121.
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (DOM-mirror sync API and canvas aria requirements).
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (evidence handling, incident reporting).

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e47-sr-passes`
- PR title: "E47-Q02: Manual screen-reader passes across the NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver matrix"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-Q02>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/test, area/design-system, priority/p0, qa, a11y

- NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver full passes executed on the RC build, with transcripts committed.

**Do NOT**

title: Keyboard-only Playwright E2E suite and accessibility-tree snapshot regression
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9 items 4 and 6 mandate two automated gates that do not exist yet: a **keyboard-only E2E smoke suite** that never dispatches a mouse event and drives the section 8.2 task script programmatically, and a **focus-order/landmark accessibility-tree snapshot** per top-level screen, diffed on every PR so semantic regressions surface as reviewable diffs rather than silent losses.

Without these, every regression is caught only by the expensive manual passes in `E47-Q02`, which run per release candidate rather than per PR. The economics are the point: keyboard traps and focus loss are the two defect classes most likely to be reintroduced by ordinary feature work in E48/E49 and beyond, and they are cheap to detect automatically.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A Playwright project `e2e/a11y-keyboard/` that runs against the built Electron renderer bundle and enforces, via a test-level guard, that no `page.mouse`, `click()` or pointer event is issued - any attempt fails the test.
- Keyboard-only journeys covering the `E47-Q01` group 1 script: app shell navigation and skip links (SCR-010, SCR-011), command palette (SCR-012), hotkey cheatsheet (SCR-013), workspace/pane focus cycling with `F6` and `Ctrl+Tab` (SCR-020, SCR-021), chart focus and data cursor movement (SCR-030), toggling the table alternative with `Alt+T` and reading a bar (SCR-045), placing and confirming a limit order (SCR-060, SCR-076), cancelling an order from the grid (SCR-063), reduced-motion override `Ctrl+Shift+M` and high-contrast `Ctrl+Shift+H` (SCR-116, SCR-117), rule editor form mode (SCR-081) and the non-drag node-connection equivalent (SCR-082), admin user creation (SCR-121, SCR-123).
- **Keyboard-trap detection helper**: for each journey, tab forward through the whole screen and assert the focus sequence returns to the starting element within N stops and that every stop is a visible, named element; a focus stop on an element with no accessible name fails.
- **Focus-visibility assertion**: computed outline/box-shadow present and its contrast against the adjacent background is >= 3:1, using the same contrast function as the `E47-T03` token linter so the two never disagree.
- **Accessibility-tree snapshots** per top-level screen (`accessibility.snapshot()`), committed as fixtures, with a reviewer-friendly diff on change; landmark and heading structure asserted against the structure defined in the standard section 3.4.1.
- **Live-region assertions**: after a simulated fill, exactly one assertive announcement node is present with the expected text shape; after a burst of market updates, the polite region's mutation count stays within the coalescing budget of the standard section 6.2.
- CI wiring: the suite runs on every PR touching `web/` or the design-system package, as a required check per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`; snapshot updates require an explicit flag and a reviewer note.
- A short `README` for the suite explaining how to add a journey when a new screen ships (the mechanism E48/E49 will reuse).

## Out of scope
- axe-core, pa11y and Lighthouse gates and their burn-down dashboard - `E47-Q04`.
- Motion/flash frame analysis - `E47-Q05`.
- Manual screen-reader verification - `E47-Q02`. This suite asserts structure and reachability, never "it sounds right".
- Visual regression of themes - covered by design QA in `E47-D03`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Keyboard-only E2E and a11y-tree snapshot gates

  Scenario: The suite cannot cheat with a mouse
    Given a journey that calls page.click
    When the suite runs
    Then the guard fails that test with a message naming the forbidden API

  Scenario: A keyboard trap fails the build
    Given a branch that removes the Escape handler from the SCR-076 order confirmation modal
    When the keyboard-only suite runs in CI
    Then the trap-detection helper fails
    And the PR cannot merge because the check is required on main

  Scenario: Failure case - a lost accessible name is caught
    Given a refactor that replaces a labelled button with an icon-only button
    When the accessibility-tree snapshot is compared
    Then the diff shows the name loss and the check fails
    And updating the snapshot requires an explicit flag and a reviewer note

  Scenario: Edge case - focus must survive a streaming update
    Given the order ticket has focus on the quantity field
    When a scripted burst of 500 market messages is injected
    Then focus remains on the quantity field at the end of the burst
    And the polite live region mutated no more times than the coalescing budget allows

  Scenario: The suite is fast enough to be a per-PR gate
    When the suite runs on CI hardware
    Then the whole keyboard-only project completes within its agreed wall-clock budget
    And a timeout is reported as an infrastructure failure, not silently retried into a pass
```

## Technical notes / design
- Market data is injected through the deterministic replay/fixture path rather than a live WS, so the streaming assertions are reproducible; the fixture is the same one `E47-Q01` defines.
- The forbidden-mouse guard is implemented by wrapping the Playwright page object in a proxy in the project's fixture, so the ban is structural rather than a review convention.
- Snapshots are stored per screen and normalised (volatile values such as prices, timestamps and ids are masked) so diffs show semantic change only; an unmasked value causing daily churn is a bug in the normaliser.
- The contrast helper must import the same implementation used by the token linter in `E47-T03`; duplicating the formula is explicitly forbidden because a drift between the two produces unfalsifiable disagreements.
- Node-graph keyboard journeys assert the documented non-drag equivalent from SCR-082; if the product has no such equivalent, the test is written as an expected failure referencing the remediation ticket rather than skipped silently.

## Test plan
- Self-verification by fault injection: deliberately break the Escape handler, remove an `aria-label`, drop a focus ring and introduce a focus-stealing `focus()` in a WS handler on a scratch branch; each must fail the corresponding assertion. Record the four injected-fault runs as evidence.
- Flake budget: the suite runs 20 consecutive times on the fixture; any test failing non-deterministically is fixed or quarantined with a linked ticket before the gate becomes required.

## Security notes
- Test fixtures use seeded demo users with deterministic throwaway credentials held in CI secrets, never live Bybit keys; the admin journeys must not require a real API key.
- Accessibility-tree snapshots are committed artefacts - the normaliser must mask account identifiers, emails and balances so the repository does not accumulate real user data through snapshot files.
- The suite runs against a staging/demo backend on the tailnet; CI must not be able to reach the live environment.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is the automated enforcement arm of the accessibility standard. It deliberately encodes *structural* accessibility (reachability, names, roles, landmarks, focus) and leaves *experiential* accessibility to `E47-Q02`; the README states that division explicitly so future contributors do not assume a green suite means conformance.

## Performance notes
- Budget the whole keyboard-only project to fit the per-PR check envelope agreed in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; parallelise by screen.
- The burst test doubles as a cheap guard on live-region cost: if mutation counts creep up over time the dashboard shows it before a human notices lag.

## Observability
- CI publishes per-journey pass/fail and duration; the a11y dashboard in `E47-Q04` shows the trend alongside axe and Lighthouse numbers.
- Snapshot diffs are attached to the PR as a rendered artefact so reviewers do not have to read raw JSON.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `e2e/a11y-keyboard/` merged with all listed journeys and the mouse guard.
- [ ] Accessibility-tree snapshots committed for every top-level screen with a documented update procedure.
- [ ] Four injected-fault runs evidenced; 20-run flake check clean.
- [ ] Check wired as required on `main` per `01-sdlc-and-branching.md`.
- [ ] README explains how to add a journey for a new screen; linked from the design-system contribution guide.
- [ ] Coverage cross-checked against the `E47-Q01` automation-status column - no gaps, no duplication.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q01` - the journeys implement that plan's automated cases.
- `E47-S01` - the chrome remediation must land or the suite is red on day one for known reasons.

## Branch
`feat/e47-keyboard-e2e`.

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 3.4 (focus management), 6.2 (live regions), 9.4 and 9.6 (the two gates this ticket builds).
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (E2E layer, flake policy).
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (required checks on `main`).
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (CI budget philosophy).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-010..SCR-013, SCR-020, SCR-030, SCR-045, SCR-060, SCR-063, SCR-076, SCR-081, SCR-082, SCR-116, SCR-117, SCR-121.
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` (focus contracts per component).

1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`

- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e47-keyboard-e2e`

title: Motion/flash audit script and accessibility-overhead performance benchmarks
body:
## Context
Two accessibility requirements are measurable rather than reviewable, and both are performance work.

First, `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9 item 5 requires an automated **motion/flash audit**: frame capture plus luminance-delta analysis against the heatmap, big-trade bubbles and price-flash components at a fixed high-tick-rate scenario, asserting the flash rate stays below the WCAG three-flashes-per-second threshold (section 7.3). In a trading terminal the risk is real - a heatmap under a liquidation cascade and a price flash on every tick are exactly the patterns that produce photosensitive-seizure hazards.

Second, the accessibility machinery itself costs frames. The DOM mirror (standard section 6.1), the live regions (6.2) and the table alternatives (6.3) all run inside the same frame budget the WebGL engine defends in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md`. If enabling accommodations makes the terminal unusable, users will turn them off, which is a conformance failure dressed as a preference.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Motion/flash audit harness** (`perf/a11y-motion-audit/`): drives a fixed replay scenario at a pinned high tick rate, captures frames off the canvas, computes relative-luminance deltas over the flashing region per the WCAG general and red flash thresholds, and asserts fewer than three flashes per second for the heatmap (SCR-050), big-trade bubbles (SCR-053), price flash on the ladder and positions grid (SCR-050, SCR-063), alert toasts (SCR-092) and connection-state banners (SCR-152).
- The same harness run with **reduced motion enabled** (OS setting and the in-app `Ctrl+Shift+M` override surfaced on SCR-117), asserting the motion-reduce variants are used and that animation work disappears from the frame profile rather than merely being visually hidden - the SCR-117 performance note requires a *measurable* reduction.
- **Accessibility-overhead benchmarks**: frame-time p50/p95 and dropped-frame counts on the SCR-030 chart with footprint at the standard benchmark scenario, measured in four configurations - baseline, DOM mirror on, live-region announcements on at each SCR-117 verbosity setting, and table alternative open alongside the canvas (SCR-045 + SCR-030). Budget: accommodations must not push p95 frame time past the engine budget in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.
- **Table-alternative scale benchmark**: SCR-045 renders 100k virtualised rows with scripting under the 8 ms per scroll frame stated in its catalogue entry, and issues no extra data fetch (it reads the same in-memory series).
- **Announcement-throttle load script**: inject 500, 2000 and 5000 messages per second through the fixture and record live-region mutation counts, announcement latency and main-thread cost per verbosity level; assert coalescing holds at every level.
- CI wiring: motion audit runs on any change to the listed components' animation code and before every release; overhead benchmarks run nightly with a regression gate against stored baselines.
- A results appendix handed to `E47-T06` (the conformance report needs a defensible statement about SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold) and to `E47-Q09`.

## Out of scope
- Engine-level rendering optimisation - if a benchmark fails, this ticket files the defect; the fix lands in the engine or remediation tickets.
- Backend load testing - the accommodations are client-side; WS fan-out load is owned by the data-plane epics.
- Subjective judgement about whether an animation is pleasant - that is design QA in `E47-D03`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Motion/flash audit and accessibility-overhead benchmarks

  Scenario: Flash threshold is enforced automatically
    Given the pinned liquidation-cascade replay scenario
    When the motion audit runs against the heatmap and big-trade bubbles
    Then the measured flash rate for every analysed region is below three per second
    And the report records the measured rate, not merely a pass verdict

  Scenario: Reduced motion removes work, not just visuals
    Given prefers-reduced-motion is enabled via the Ctrl+Shift+M override
    When the same scenario is profiled
    Then animation-related scripting and GPU work is measurably lower than the motion-safe run
    And a run where only opacity is forced constant while the animation loop still executes fails the check

  Scenario: Failure case - an accommodation blows the frame budget
    Given the DOM mirror and always-on announcements are enabled on SCR-030 with footprint
    When the benchmark scenario runs
    And p95 frame time exceeds the engine budget
    Then the benchmark fails and a perf defect is filed against the owning component
    And the conformance report cannot claim the accommodation is usable until it is closed

  Scenario: Edge case - extreme message rate degrades by coalescing, not by dropping frames
    Given 5000 messages per second injected at the highest verbosity
    When the announcement-throttle script runs
    Then live-region mutations stay within the coalescing budget
    And the main thread remains responsive to keyboard input within its interaction budget

  Scenario: Baselines make regressions visible
    Given stored baselines from the previous nightly run
    When a change increases p95 frame time beyond the agreed tolerance
    Then the nightly gate fails and names the configuration that regressed
```

## Technical notes / design
- Flash analysis operates on captured frames from a deterministic replay window, never live market data; reproducibility is the entire value of the check.
- Luminance delta uses the same relative-luminance implementation as the contrast helper in `E47-Q03` and the `E47-T03` token linter - one implementation, three consumers.
- Regions analysed are declared per component (a rectangle or selector-derived bounding box) so a flash is not averaged away across a mostly-static screen; whole-viewport averaging is the classic way these audits produce false passes.
- Benchmarks pin renderer configuration via the SCR-118 settings (renderer mode, FPS cap) and record it with the result; comparing results across renderer modes is invalid and is blocked by tagging.
- The overhead benchmark must include compact density, because dense layouts are where mirror node counts are largest.

## Test plan
- Validate the audit with a **known-bad synthetic component** flashing at 6 Hz: the harness must fail it. Validate with a known-good 1 Hz component: it must pass. Both fixtures are committed so future analyser changes can be re-validated.
- Validate the overhead benchmark by artificially inflating mirror node counts tenfold and confirming the regression gate trips.
- Run the full set three times to establish variance, and set the regression tolerance from measured variance rather than a guessed percentage.

## Security notes
- Captured frames may contain account balances, position sizes and symbol exposure. Captures run against seeded demo data only; the harness deletes raw frame captures after analysis, retaining aggregate numbers plus at most one redacted sample image per finding.
- Benchmark artefacts uploaded to CI are scanned for the same sensitive-string set used by `E47-Q04`'s report post-processor.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket protects two groups directly: photosensitive users (flash thresholds) and AT users (accommodations must remain usable at speed). A passing benchmark with a failing flash audit is not a trade-off to negotiate - the flash threshold is a hard WCAG requirement at AA and blocks release.

## Performance notes
- Budgets are referenced, not redefined: engine frame budget and interaction budget come from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; SCR-045's 8 ms scripting per scroll frame and SCR-118's renderer settings come from `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- Results feed the same performance dashboard used by the engine epics, so accessibility overhead is visible alongside ordinary render metrics rather than in a silo.

## Observability
- Metrics: `a11y_flash_rate{component,scenario}`, `a11y_frame_p95_ms{config,density}`, `a11y_live_region_mutations_per_s{verbosity,rate}`, `a11y_table_scroll_script_ms`.
- Nightly results posted to the release dashboard; a flash-threshold breach pages the Accessibility role and blocks the release candidate.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Motion/flash harness merged, validated against known-good and known-bad fixtures, wired to run on animation-code changes and per release.
- [ ] Overhead benchmarks merged with baselines, variance-derived tolerances and a nightly regression gate.
- [ ] Announcement-throttle load script merged with results at 500/2000/5000 messages per second.
- [ ] Any breach filed as a defect with an owner; no breach accepted without recorded owner sign-off.
- [ ] Results appendix delivered to `E47-T06` and `E47-Q09`.

## Dependencies
- `E47-Q01` - scenarios and fixtures.
- `E47-T05` - motion-reduce variants must exist before the reduced-motion comparison is meaningful.

## Branch
`feat/e47-motion-audit`.

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 6.1-6.3 (canvas strategy cost), 7 (reduced motion, flash), 9.5 (motion audit gate).
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (frame and interaction budgets, regression-gate philosophy).
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (DOM-mirror sync API, windowed accessibility tree).
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-045, SCR-050, SCR-053, SCR-063, SCR-092, SCR-117, SCR-118, SCR-152.
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-007, US-SET-008, US-CHART-014.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- WS topics/framing in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` (contract-first per C-6.1)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e47-motion-audit`
- PR title: "E47-Q05: Motion/flash audit script and accessibility-overhead performance benchmarks"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-Q05>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/test, area/design-system, priority/p1, qa, a11y, perf

**Done means**
- Motion/flash harness merged, validated against known-good and known-bad fixtures, wired to run on animation-code changes and per release.
- Overhead benchmarks merged with baselines, variance-derived tolerances and a nightly regression gate.
- Announcement-throttle load script merged with results at 500/2000/5000 messages per second.
- Any breach filed as a defect with an owner; no breach accepted without recorded owner sign-off.
- Results appendix delivered to `E47-T06` and `E47-Q09`.

**Do NOT**
- Engine-level rendering optimisation - if a benchmark fails, this ticket files the defect; the fix lands in the engine or remediation tickets.
- Backend load testing - the accommodations are client-side; WS fan-out load is owned by the data-plane epics.
- Subjective judgement about whether an animation is pleasant - that is design QA in `E47-D03`.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E47-Q05` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Footprint, DOM ladder and heatmap grids reach AA keyboard-only
body:
## Context
The footprint grid and the DOM ladder + liquidity heatmap are the densest surfaces in the product and the ones `05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 explicitly refuses to exempt: "the DOM ladder, footprint grid and rule node-graph editor are dense, high-information-density surfaces; WCAG AA still applies — density is solved via information architecture (§4), not by exempting a screen." §3.4.2 prescribes the mechanism — roving tabindex per the WAI-ARIA APG grid pattern, "this prevents 200+ Tab presses to cross a DOM ladder" — and §4 forbids colour-only encoding of bid/ask, imbalance and delta sign anywhere.

The ladder is also a *trading* surface: `Enter` places a limit at the focused row, `Ctrl+Enter` goes aggressive, `Ctrl+Delete` cancels all at that row (§3.2). Accessibility defects here are not cosmetic — an ambiguous announcement before a keyboard order placement is a financial risk. This Story remediates the E47-T01 findings on these surfaces.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Footprint (SCR-030 footprint mode, SCR-032 settings)**: roving-tabindex cell grid with `role="grid"` semantics on the surrogate layer; arrow keys move cell focus, `PageUp`/`PageDown` by bar, announcements give price, bid volume, ask volume, delta with explicit sign, and imbalance status as words; imbalance-flagged cells carry a border/pattern distinction that survives grayscale (§4.3).
- **DOM ladder + heatmap (SCR-050, settings SCR-051)**: roving tabindex over ladder rows; each row announces price, bid size, ask size, side and any resting order/position at that price; the heatmap cell readout gives price, size and side on focus (§4.1); bid/ask side is conveyed by text and axis-side convention with a persistent legend, never hue alone.
- **Keyboard trading safety**: `Enter`/`Ctrl+Enter`/`Ctrl+Delete` at the focused row route through the confirm policy (**US-SET-003**) with the resolved price, side, quantity and account read back before commit; the 1-click ARMED state is announced and shown with icon + text (§3.1.5).
- **Adjacent panes** re-verified with the same pattern: **SCR-052** CVD/delta, **SCR-053** tape + bubbles, **SCR-055** speed of tape, **SCR-056** imbalance tracker, **SCR-038** profile panel — sign and side always carry `+`/`-` or a glyph.
- Target-size accounting: rows and cells ≥24×24 CSS px at default zoom, or the essential exception claimed with SCR-045/table alternatives named as the compensating control (§3.4.7).

## Out of scope
- Chart price-series surrogate and SCR-045 — **E47-S01**.
- Changing palettes — **E47-S06** (this Story consumes whatever palette ships and enforces the non-colour channel).
- Order-flow algorithm behaviour or detector methodology.
- Heatmap render-path optimisation — **E46**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Crossing the ladder costs a few keystrokes, not two hundred
  Given the DOM ladder has 200 visible price rows and one row is focused
  When the trader presses Tab
  Then focus leaves the ladder as a single composite widget
  And arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown and Home/End move within it

Scenario: A keyboard order is read back before it is placed
  Given a ladder row at 64 010 is focused and confirm policy is "dialog"
  When Enter is pressed
  Then a keyboard-operable confirmation announces side, price, quantity and the target account or accounts
  And Esc cancels with nothing sent

Scenario: Footprint imbalance survives grayscale
  Given a cell is flagged as an imbalance
  When the display is rendered in grayscale or a high-contrast theme
  Then the flag remains distinguishable by border or pattern
  And the screen reader announces the imbalance state as a word

Scenario: Delta sign is never colour-only
  Given a footprint cell with delta -8 and another with +8
  Then both render an explicit sign or glyph in addition to any colour
  And the automated no-hue-alone check passes for the footprint, CVD, tape and imbalance surfaces

Scenario: Dense targets are accounted for, not ignored
  Given footprint cells fall below 24 px at maximum zoom-out
  Then the essential exception is recorded with SCR-045 named as the alternative
  And at default zoom, ladder rows and cells meet the 24 px minimum

Scenario: A fill does not hijack the keyboard
  Given the trader is navigating ladder rows
  When an order fills
  Then the fill is announced assertively and focus stays on the current row
```

## Technical notes / design
One composite-grid implementation is shared by footprint, ladder and profile surrogates — `15-component-catalogue.md` §11.3 already requires the pattern be "specified once in the component catalogue and reused everywhere the pattern repeats", so this Story consolidates any divergent copies found by the sweep into CMP-113/CMP-136 and their shared grid behaviour. Announcement text is produced by the same formatter family as E47-S01 so a price reads identically everywhere. Keyboard order paths reuse the existing confirm-policy machinery rather than introducing a ladder-specific dialog.

## Test plan
Unit: roving-tabindex state machine at edges and on data churn; announcement formatting for zero, negative and very large sizes. Integration: focus stability under a replayed high-rate book fixture. E2E keyboard-only: navigate ladder, place and cancel a demo order, toggle 1-click and confirm the armed announcement. Visual: grayscale and high-contrast snapshots asserting imbalance distinguishability. Gates: axe, a11y-tree snapshot, no-hue-alone check on SCR-050, SCR-051, SCR-052, SCR-053, SCR-055, SCR-056.

## Security notes
Keyboard order entry is the highest-consequence path in this Story: the read-back must show the *resolved* per-account quantities (per §3.3.5, guarding the silent multi-account fat-finger), the arm token requirement for one-click entry is unchanged, and no accessibility preference may bypass the confirm policy or the native-SL invariant. Announcements must never expose accounts the user lacks RBAC access to.

## Accessibility notes
Implements §3.4.2 (roving tabindex), §3.4.7 (target size and essential exception), §4.1/§4.3 (non-colour encoding of side, status and sign), §6.1 (surrogate layer). WCAG SCs: 1.3.1, 1.4.1, 1.4.11, 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.11, 2.5.8, 4.1.2, 4.1.3.

## Performance notes
Surrogate rows are virtualised to the visible window; a full-depth ladder must not materialise 1 000 DOM nodes. Focus moves must not trigger a full re-render of the canvas layer. Measure surrogate update cost under the E46 harness and file E46 tickets for overruns rather than silently accepting them.

## Observability
Client metrics `a11y_grid_focus_move_ms`, `a11y_surrogate_nodes` (alert above the windowing ceiling); analytics `dom.keyboard_order_placed` to confirm the path is actually usable, not merely present.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario covered by a named test or a recorded manual step.
- [ ] All E47-T01 findings in the grid/colour-encoding patterns closed or registered as exceptions.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on touched packages.
- [ ] axe, keyboard-E2E, a11y-tree-snapshot and no-hue-alone gates green on the listed screens.
- [ ] NVDA spot-check recorded; grayscale and high-contrast snapshots attached.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-113/CMP-136 a11y contracts updated to the shipped shared pattern.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; keyboard-only demo of a demo-environment order at Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T01**. Related to **E47-S06** (palette) and **E47-S05** (focus/target audit); feeds **E47-T04**, **E47-T05**.

## Branch

title: Screen-reader scripts and pinned-matrix sign-off passes (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver)
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 names "screen-reader scripts for the chart data cursor, footprint inspection, DOM ladder and both rule editors" as an E47 deliverable, and §9.3 exit criterion 2 requires a "manual screen-reader pass signed off" per screen. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.1 pins the matrix: NVDA on Electron/Windows is P0 and a release blocker; JAWS is P1 and must fully pass before R4 with smoke checks thereafter; VoiceOver on macOS is P1 with a **full pass required before R5 GA**. §8.1 also requires pinned versions with a dated changelog rather than floating "latest".

Remediation (S01–S03, S05–S08) has landed by now; this Task is the evidence-producing pass that GA is judged on, plus the durable scripts that make it repeatable after GA — which matters because the standard's §8 cadence continues past this release, and R10 key-person risk means the procedure must not live only in one person's head.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Author the **task scripts** as durable, versioned documents: chart data cursor (traverse bars, read OHLCV/delta, open and read SCR-045), footprint inspection (navigate cells, read bid/ask/delta/imbalance), DOM ladder (navigate rows, read depth, place and cancel a demo order), rule form editor (author, validate, save) and rule node editor (author, connect, arm/disarm), plus the §8.2 cross-cutting script (login and 2FA, switch symbol, toggle table view, trigger reduced-motion override, read a fill notification).
- Each script states: preconditions and fixture, ordered steps, the expected *announcement content* at each step (not merely "it announces something"), and a pass/fail line per step.
- Execute the full pass on the pinned matrix: NVDA (P0, full), JAWS (P1, full), VoiceOver (P1, full before GA), each against the production Electron build; record results per screen band with evidence per the K01-decided capture procedure.
- Record the pinned versions with a dated changelog entry per §8.1 and file the quarterly re-pin as a recurring Chore.
- Any failure found becomes a register finding routed to the owning remediation Story if fixable in R5, or to the exception register with Owner acceptance if not.
- Sign-off: Accessibility role signs the full passes; QA/SDET co-signs the RC checklist.

## Out of scope
- Remediating what the passes find — routed back to S01–S08 or to E49; this Task owns detection and evidence.
- Mobile/Android screen readers and Safari (excluded by §8.1).
- Automated SR emulation — these are human passes by design.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Scripts are executable by someone who did not write them
  Given a QA engineer who has not used the app with a screen reader
  When they follow a script
  Then every step is unambiguous and the expected announcement content is stated
  And they can produce a pass or fail per step without asking the author

Scenario: The pinned matrix is fully executed before GA
  When the GA gate is evaluated
  Then NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver full passes are recorded against the production Electron build
  And each is signed off by the Accessibility role with a date and the pinned tool versions

Scenario: A failure is not absorbed silently
  Given a script step fails on JAWS only
  Then a register finding is created naming the screen reader, step and expected announcement
  And it is either fixed in R5 or accepted as an expiring exception with a compensating control

Scenario: Versions are pinned and dated
  Then the matrix records exact screen-reader and shell versions with a dated changelog entry
  And a recurring re-pin Chore exists for the next quarter

Scenario: A trading task is completable non-visually
  Given the DOM ladder script on the demo environment
  Then a demo order is placed and cancelled using keyboard and screen reader alone
  And the confirmation read-back states side, price, quantity and account before commit
```

## Technical notes / design
The scripts specify expected *content*, which is what turns a subjective pass into a reproducible one — "announces the focused bar's time, open, high, low, close, volume and delta in one utterance" is checkable; "is accessible" is not. Scripts live in the repo beside the standard so they version with the product, and they are the same scripts the post-GA cadence in §8.1 re-runs.

## Test plan
This Task *is* a test plan; its own quality control is that each script is dry-run by a second person before the formal pass, and that the formal pass is executed on a clean production build rather than a dev server.

## Security notes
Passes run in the demo environment with synthetic accounts; the DOM ladder script places demo orders only and must never be executed against Live. Captured speech recordings and screenshots are reviewed for account identifiers and key material before being stored as evidence.

## Accessibility notes
This is the human half of conformance that automation cannot replace: announcement usefulness, focus intent, and whether the mirror actually corresponds to what is drawn. Deferred SR spot-checks from earlier Stories are discharged here and their deferral notes closed.

## Performance notes
During the passes, note any perceptible lag between a keyboard action and its announcement; anything above roughly 200 ms is logged as an E46 candidate rather than tolerated.

## Observability
Results recorded in the findings register and the conformance matrix; pass/fail counts per screen reader published with the RC report.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All five surface scripts plus the cross-cutting script authored, dry-run and merged.
- [ ] NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver full passes executed on the production Electron build and signed off.
- [ ] Pinned versions recorded with a dated changelog; re-pin Chore filed.
- [ ] All failures routed to remediation or to registered exceptions.
- [ ] Earlier Stories' deferred SR spot-checks closed.
- [ ] `05-accessibility-standard.md` §8 updated with the executed cadence and results location.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-K01** (harness and capture procedure), **E47-S01**, **E47-S02**, **E47-S03** (the surfaces must be remediated before a sign-off pass is meaningful). Blocks **E47-T05**.

## Branch
`chore/e47-sr-scripts-and-passes`

## References
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2, §9.3; `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-045, SCR-050, SCR-081, SCR-082.

- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-T04>`

- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/chore, area/design-system, priority/p1, a11y, qa

**Done means**

- Pinned versions recorded with a dated changelog; re-pin Chore filed.
- All failures routed to remediation or to registered exceptions.

**Do NOT**
