title: Publish the VPAT-shaped conformance report and the exception register
body:
## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2 closes E47's scope with "a published accessibility conformance report (VPAT-shaped)", and §9.3 exit criterion 2 requires that "any non-conformance is a documented, Owner-accepted exception with a remediation ticket". §9.3 criterion 4 adds the discipline that every accepted risk must have "a current owner, an expiry date, and a review record; expired acceptances are re-decided, not silently extended".

This Task produces the artefact the GA gate reads. It is deliberately *generated* from the findings register and the T03 matrix rather than written by hand, so it can be regenerated after any post-GA change without a re-transcription that quietly drifts from reality.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The **conformance report**, VPAT-shaped: one row per WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA success criterion, with a conformance level (Supports / Partially Supports / Does Not Support / Not Applicable) and remarks naming the surfaces involved — generated from the register, the contrast/CVD matrix and the SR pass results.
- A **per-screen conformance matrix** appendix covering SCR-001…SCR-159 with the four evidence columns (axe, keyboard, screen reader, sign-off).
- The **exception register**: every non-conformance with WCAG SC, level, affected surfaces, compensating control, named Owner acceptance, expiry date and linked remediation ticket. Level A entries are prohibited — a Level A entry fails the build that generates the report.
- The **in-app accessibility statement**, linked from **SCR-117** and **SCR-119**, in plain language: what is supported, what is known-limited, the keyboard and table alternatives, and how to report a problem.
- Documented regeneration: a single command, run in CI on the release candidate, that fails if the checked-in report is stale relative to the register.
- Handover: the remaining open findings and their owners handed to **E49** for burn-down, and the post-GA §8.1 cadence recorded in the ops documentation for **E48**.

## Out of scope
- Any remediation — everything fixable in R5 is already in S01–S08.
- A third-party audit or a legally-filed VPAT (this is an internal tool; §1 of the standard states there is no external AA mandate).
- Marketing or external publication of the report.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The report is generated, not transcribed
  When the generation command runs against the findings register and the contrast matrix
  Then the report and the per-screen appendix are produced without manual editing
  And CI fails if the checked-in report differs from the generated one

Scenario: Every A and AA criterion is addressed
  Then each WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA success criterion has a conformance level and a remark
  And no criterion is left blank or marked "unknown"

Scenario: A Level A gap blocks GA
  Given a Level A finding remains open
  When the report is generated
  Then generation fails naming the finding, and the GA gate cannot be satisfied

Scenario: An AA exception is complete or it is not an exception
  Given an entry in the exception register
  Then it has a success criterion, affected surfaces, a compensating control, a named Owner acceptance, an expiry date and a remediation ticket
  And an entry missing any field fails generation

Scenario: Users can find the statement
  Given a user on SCR-117 or SCR-119
  Then the accessibility statement is reachable in one action and states the supported keyboard and table alternatives and how to report a problem

Scenario: Expiry is enforced, not aspirational
  Given an exception's expiry date passes
  Then the next generation flags it for re-decision rather than carrying it forward
```

## Technical notes / design
Generation-not-transcription is the whole design point. The register (schema from K01), the T03 matrix and the T04 pass results are three machine-readable inputs; the report is their join. The staleness check is what keeps the artefact honest after GA, when nobody is watching the register daily. Expiry enforcement is a date comparison at generation time, which converts §9.3 criterion 4 from a policy into a mechanism.

## Test plan
Unit: generator joins and the four failure modes (Level A open, incomplete exception, stale checked-in report, expired acceptance). Fixture: a synthetic register producing a known report. Review: Accessibility role, QA lead and Owner read the generated report before GA; a non-specialist reads the in-app statement for plain-language clarity.

## Security notes
The report and statement must contain no hostnames, account identifiers, API-key material or screenshots with live data — an automated content check runs before publication. The exception register describes *accessibility* gaps only; it must not become a place where security findings are recorded (those belong to the E43 process).

## Accessibility notes
The report and the in-app statement must themselves conform: semantic headings, real tables with headers, no colour-only conformance indicators ("Supports" as a word, not a green dot), and readable at 200% zoom. Publishing an inaccessible accessibility report would be the most avoidable defect in the Epic.

## Performance notes
Generation runs in under 30 s so the staleness check is affordable on every release-candidate build.

## Observability
Published metrics alongside the report: open findings by level, exception count and nearest expiry date, per-screen evidence completeness — the same numbers the PRR reads.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report, per-screen appendix and exception register generated, reviewed and merged.
- [ ] Generation command documented and the staleness check wired into the RC build.
- [ ] Zero open Level A findings; every AA exception complete with Owner acceptance and expiry.
- [ ] In-app accessibility statement linked from SCR-117 and SCR-119 and verified conformant itself.
- [ ] Remaining findings handed to **E49**; post-GA SR cadence documented for **E48**.
- [ ] Owner acceptance recorded; report attached to the GA PRR.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E47-T04** (SR evidence), **E47-S04**, **E47-S05**, **E47-S06**, **E47-S08** (remediation complete). Consumes **E47-T01** and **E47-T03** outputs. Feeds **E48** (documentation) and **E49** (burn-down), and satisfies `30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 exit criterion 2.

## Branch
`docs/e47-conformance-report`

## References
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2, §9.3, §9.4; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §1, §8, §9, §10; `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-117, SCR-119; `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

title: Abuse cases: accessible-surface leakage, hotkey tampering, announcement DoS
body:
## Context
`E47-X01` identifies threats analytically; this ticket tries to make them happen. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires abuse cases to be executed, not merely enumerated, and the accessible surface is the least-tested surface in the product - precisely the condition under which parity bugs survive to production.

The central hypothesis under test: **the accessible representation of a screen is subject to exactly the same authorisation, masking and confirmation controls as the visual representation**. Every abuse case below is an attempt to falsify it.

## Scope / Deliverables
An executed abuse-case suite (`security/abuse-cases/e47/`) with a result per case, automated where feasible in the `E47-Q03` harness and manual otherwise:
1. **Masked-value leakage**: on SCR-127 (API key rotation) and SCR-128 (key health), read every accessible name, description, live-region text and DOM-mirror node; assert no unmasked key material, no full secret, and no value the visual surface masks.
2. **Cross-account exposure via the mirror**: as a user whose `user_account_access` covers account A only, open surfaces that aggregate accounts (SCR-063 positions, SCR-071 risk dashboard, SCR-062 trade-group manager) and assert no account-B identifier, balance or position appears in any accessible node - including nodes rendered but visually clipped or collapsed.
3. **Hidden-but-exposed controls**: as a viewer, enumerate the full accessibility tree of owner/manager screens (SCR-120..SCR-149) and assert no owner-only action is present, focusable or activatable; specifically attempt activation of any node found.
4. **Re-auth bypass**: attempt to reach an admin action requiring the SCR-149 re-authentication gate purely by keyboard and AT navigation, including via the command palette (SCR-012) and hotkeys, asserting the gate always interposes.
5. **Confirmation stripping via preferences**: modify `PUT /api/v1/me/preferences` payloads directly (including values the UI cannot produce) and attempt to disable destructive-action confirmations (US-SET-003), the Demo/Live confirm (SCR-074) or the arming requirement; assert server-side rejection and that safety controls are not client-configurable.
6. **Hotkey tampering**: craft a hotkey profile via `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys` binding a single unmodified key to an irreversible trading action, activate it, and assert either rejection or that the confirmation still interposes; assert the change is audited.
7. **Announcement and mirror DoS**: drive extreme update rates and extreme visible ranges to attempt unbounded live-region or mirror growth, and attempt to open SCR-045 over an unbounded range; assert coalescing, windowing and range caps hold and the client stays responsive.
8. **Table-export exfiltration**: use the SCR-045 `Ctrl+C` TSV export and any CSV export on the table alternatives to attempt extraction of data beyond the user's scope; assert exports are scoped and, where the security program requires it, audited.
9. **Injection into accessible text**: place attacker-controlled strings (symbol aliases, watchlist names, journal tags, rule names, user display names) into fields that flow into accessible names and announcements; assert they are treated as text, cannot break out of the accessible name, and cannot forge a system message such as a fake Live-environment warning.
10. **Report/statement disclosure**: review the published accessibility statement and conformance report for internal hostnames, architecture detail, account identifiers or screenshots with real data.

Deliverables: a result table (case, method, expected, actual, verdict), defects for every failure with severity per `04-security-program.md`, and regression assertions added to `E47-Q03` or the security suite for every confirmed issue.

## Out of scope
- Network-level and backend-only attacks - owned by the API and auth epics.
- Full penetration testing (performed before R4 live enablement).
- Social-engineering scenarios.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: E47 abuse cases executed

  Scenario: Every case is executed with a recorded verdict
    Given the ten abuse cases
    When the suite is run against the release-candidate build
    Then each case records method, expected result, actual result and verdict
    And a case that could not be executed states why and is not recorded as a pass

  Scenario: Accessible surface enforces the same scoping as the visual surface
    Given a user with access to one account only
    When the full accessibility tree of an aggregating screen is enumerated
    Then no identifier, balance or position of any other account is present in any node

  Scenario: Failure case - a viewer finds an owner-only action in the tree
    Given a viewer session on an admin screen
    When a control absent from the visual UI is found in the accessibility tree and activated
    Then a high-severity finding is filed
    And the fix must remove the control server-side or from the render tree, not merely hide it with aria-hidden

  Scenario: Edge case - safety controls are not client-configurable
    Given a crafted preferences payload disabling destructive-action confirmation
    When it is sent directly to the API
    Then the server rejects it
    And the client-side confirmation still interposes if the preference is somehow set

  Scenario: Edge case - attacker-controlled text cannot forge a system announcement
    Given a watchlist named so as to imitate a live-environment warning
    When the name is announced
    Then it is announced as user content and cannot be mistaken for a system message
    And no markup or role injection occurs
```

## Technical notes / design
- Enumerating the accessibility tree is done programmatically (Playwright `accessibility.snapshot()` plus a DOM walk including `aria-hidden` and visually clipped nodes) rather than by listening with a screen reader; the machine finds nodes a human listener would never reach.
- The `aria-hidden` caveat is central: hiding a privileged control from AT is not authorisation. Cases 3 and 4 explicitly test for controls that are merely hidden, and the accepted fix is server-side enforcement plus not rendering.
- Preference and hotkey tampering is executed at the API level with a direct client, because the point is to bypass UI validation entirely.
- Case 9 strings include the standard injection corpus adapted for accessible names (markup, RTL overrides, zero-width characters, very long strings, newline-bearing values that could split an announcement).
- Every confirmed issue gets a regression assertion so the fix cannot silently regress in a later epic.

## Test plan
- The suite is the test. Its own validation: run cases 1, 2 and 3 against a deliberately vulnerable build (unmasked key in an `aria-label`, unscoped mirror data, an owner action left in the tree with `aria-hidden`) and confirm every case detects the issue. Without this, a clean result is indistinguishable from a broken detector.
- Re-run the suite after remediation to confirm closure; record both runs.

## Security notes
- Execution uses seeded demo accounts across roles (owner, manager, viewer) and the demo environment only; no live keys and no live order flow.
- Any confirmed leakage of real data during testing triggers the incident process in `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`, including rotation if key material is involved.
- Findings and evidence are stored in the security findings register with restricted access; raw captures containing leaked values are not committed to the repository.

## Accessibility notes
Remediation must preserve accessibility: the correct fix for an exposed privileged control is to not render it for that role (matching the visual surface), never to strip the accessible name or add `aria-hidden` to a control the user is legitimately allowed to use. Every fix proposed by this ticket is reviewed against that rule by the Accessibility role before it is accepted.

## Performance notes
Cases 7 and 8 double as availability tests: acceptance is not only "no crash" but that keyboard interaction stays within the interaction budget from `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` while under attack-rate load, using the measurement approach from `E47-Q05`.

## Observability
- Findings tagged `epic:E47`, `type:abuse-case` in the security register.
- Where a mitigation is an audit event (hotkey profile activation, preference change affecting a safety control), the abuse case verifies the event is actually emitted and visible on SCR-135.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ten abuse cases executed with recorded verdicts and evidence references.
- [ ] Detector validation against a deliberately vulnerable build evidenced for cases 1-3.
- [ ] Findings filed, severity-rated, owned; high-severity items fixed and re-tested before GA.
- [ ] Regression assertions added for every confirmed issue.
- [ ] Results fed to `E47-X04` and `E47-Q09`.

## Dependencies
- `E47-X01` - the threat model defines which cases are worth executing.
- `E47-Q03` - the enumeration and keyboard harness is reused rather than rebuilt.

## Branch
`chore/e47-abuse-cases`.

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (abuse-case requirement, severity scale, incident process).
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 3.2-3.3, 6.1-6.3.
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/me/preferences`, `/settings/arm`, `/settings/hotkeys*`.
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` `settings`, `hotkey_profiles`, `user_account_access`.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-012, SCR-045, SCR-062, SCR-063, SCR-071, SCR-074, SCR-120..SCR-149.
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-002, US-SET-003, US-SET-007.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**

**Commands**

title: Author the black-box state-matrix test plan for every panel and failure mode
body:
## Context
E49-S05 must bring every empty, loading and error surface into conformance with SCR-150…SCR-159. It cannot do that without a list of which surfaces are currently wrong, and E49-D05 cannot sign off without evidence that they are now right. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1 requires a black-box test plan per story, authored or reviewed by QA before development starts.

This ticket is that plan plus the harness that makes it executable: a matrix of *every panel* × *every applicable state*, driven mechanically, asserting structure and accessible semantics rather than pixels. It lands in S24 so E49-S05 has its oracle when it starts in S25.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **The matrix**: rows are every panel and page in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` that can enter a non-populated state; columns are the applicable states — loading, empty (three classes: nothing created yet / nothing matches the filter / data not recorded yet), error, stale/disconnected, degraded, permission-denied, not-found, rate-limited, crashed. Each cell is applicable or explicitly not-applicable with a reason.
- **State-injection harness**: deterministic mechanisms to drive each state without waiting for nature — a test-only control plane that can force a 403 or 404 response, force a degraded cause, force rate-limit `10018`, sever the websocket, empty a data source, throw inside a named panel, and simulate a version mismatch. Available only in test builds, with a build assertion that it is absent from production bundles.
- **Assertions per cell**, derived from E49-D02's spec: required structural elements present (heading, causal sentence, action or explicit no-action statement); correct component used; accessible role and live-region behaviour per the catalogue (`role="alert"` once then banner for SCR-152; `role="status"` naming the degraded capability for SCR-153; correlation id as selectable text for SCR-154 and SCR-156); the required analytics event emitted with the specified payload; and for empty states, that no WebGL context or subscription was created.
- **Baseline run** against the pre-remediation build, producing the non-conformance list that E49-S05 works from, published as `docs/plan/backlog/artifacts/e49-state-matrix-baseline.md`.
- **Playwright implementation** of the matrix as the `@state-matrix` tagged subset contributed into E49-Q01's GA regression pack.
- **Trading-safety assertions**: in disconnected and rate-limited states, order-entry controls are asserted disabled with a visible reason; in degraded state, whether trading is permitted is asserted to be unambiguous.

## Out of scope
- Fixing non-conformances — E49-S05.
- Pixel-level visual comparison, which belongs to design QA (E49-S04's visual-regression baselines), not to this structural matrix.
- Testing the underlying failure behaviour itself (reconnect strategy, load shedding) — **E45** and **E46**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The matrix is complete and honest
  Given the panel list from the screens catalogue
  When the matrix is reviewed
  Then every panel has a row and every cell is applicable with assertions, or not-applicable with a written reason
  And a panel present in the catalogue but missing from the matrix fails the matrix's self-check

Scenario: Every state can be driven deterministically
  Given the state-injection harness
  When each state is requested for a given panel
  Then the panel reliably enters that state within five seconds
  And no state requires waiting for a real-world condition such as an actual exchange outage

Scenario: The harness cannot ship
  Given a production build
  When the bundle is inspected by the build assertion
  Then no state-injection control-plane code is present
  And the assertion fails the release build if it is

Scenario: Trading is asserted blocked where required
  Given a panel in the disconnected state
  When the assertions run
  Then order-entry controls are disabled and the reason is present in the accessible name
  And the test fails if a control remains enabled

Scenario: The baseline is actionable
  Given the baseline run against the pre-remediation build
  When the non-conformance list is produced
  Then each entry names the panel, the state, the specific assertion that failed and the SCR clause it violates
```

## Technical notes / design
- The harness is a test-only module registered behind a build flag; it exposes a typed command channel (`forceState(panelId, state, options)`) used by Playwright, plus server-side hooks for forcing HTTP statuses and rate-limit responses. Determinism matters more than realism here — realism is the chaos suite's job.
- Assertions target the accessibility tree and the DOM contract, not screenshots, so they stay stable under legitimate visual change and actually encode the requirements that matter.
- The analytics assertion captures emitted events through a test sink, asserting name and payload shape against E49-D02's contract.
- The no-GL-context assertion hooks context creation and subscription registration for the panel under test, which is how SCR-151's "empty panels cost nothing" clause becomes testable rather than aspirational.
- Matrix definition lives as data (YAML) with the Playwright specs generated from it, so adding a panel is a data change and the self-check can compare the data against the catalogue.

## Test plan
- **Self-check**: matrix data versus the screens catalogue panel list; unreferenced or missing panels fail.
- **Harness unit tests**: each force-state command produces the intended state in a component harness; the production-absence build assertion is itself tested against a mock production bundle.
- **Meta-test**: a deliberately non-conformant fixture panel is asserted to fail the relevant cell, proving the assertions can actually fail (a test suite that cannot fail is the most common silent defect in this kind of work).
- **Integration**: the generated specs run in CI against the current build to produce the baseline.
- **Coverage**: ≥80% frontend for the harness and generator.

## Security notes
The state-injection harness is a deliberate control-bypass mechanism — forcing a 403 or an authorization state is exactly what an attacker would want. Controls: it is excluded from production builds by a build flag and a bundle assertion that fails the release build if present; it never bypasses server-side authorization, only forces the *client* to render a state the server already sanctioned in a test context; the server-side hooks are gated behind a test-environment-only configuration that is asserted absent in the production configuration; and the harness is reviewed by the Security engineer as part of E49-X01's threat model, where "test hook reaches production" is an explicit abuse case. Assertions must not log tokens or key material captured from the test sink.

## Accessibility notes
This matrix is the primary automated guard for the accessible semantics of failure states, which are the states users most need to understand and the ones least often tested. It asserts the specific requirements from the catalogue: SCR-150's polite per-phase progress announcements and the prohibition on a bare spinner; SCR-151's heading plus causal sentence plus action-or-explicit-no-action; SCR-152's single `role="alert"` then persistent banner with a countdown that is not announced per tick; SCR-153's `role="status"` naming the degraded capability and per-panel badges repeating it in their accessible names; SCR-154's selectable correlation id; SCR-156's `role="alert"` region with technical detail behind a labelled disclosure; SCR-158's at-most-every-10-seconds countdown announcements. axe-core runs on every cell in addition to these targeted assertions.

## Performance notes
The matrix asserts the catalogue's state budgets where they are cheaply checkable: empty panels create no GL context or subscription; SCR-154 renders in ≤200 ms from the 403 response with no additional fetches; SCR-155 resolves with no network call. The matrix run itself must fit inside E49-Q01's 45-minute pack budget as a shard.

## Observability
The analytics assertions double as a guard on the observability contract: if a state stops emitting `empty_state_shown` or `degraded.entered` with the right payload, the matrix fails, which prevents the silent dashboard breakage that normally accompanies UI refactors.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Matrix data complete; self-check green against the screens catalogue.
- [ ] Harness implemented with the production-absence build assertion green.
- [ ] Assertions implemented per cell, including a11y semantics and analytics payloads.
- [ ] Meta-test proves assertions can fail.
- [ ] Baseline run published with an actionable non-conformance list for E49-S05.
- [ ] Specs contributed into E49-Q01's pack as the `@state-matrix` shard within budget.
- [ ] security: Security-engineer review of the harness gating.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%.
- [ ] QA sign-off that the matrix is fit to be E49-S05's oracle and E49-D05's evidence.
- [ ] Docs: matrix documented in `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.
- [ ] Demo: driving a panel through its state set shown at Sprint Review.
- [ ] PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E49-D02** supplies the normative spec the assertions encode; writing assertions before the spec would encode current behaviour as correct.
- **E49-Q01** hosts the resulting specs.

## Branch
`chore/e49-state-matrix` · PR size: harness, then matrix data and generator, then baseline.

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-150…SCR-159 with their A11y, Performance and Analytics clauses.
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1 test plans, §12 a11y protocol.
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-026, CMP-027, CMP-028, CMP-076, CMP-077, CMP-078, CMP-079, CMP-089, CMP-090, CMP-091, CMP-092.
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/e49-state-matrix`
- PR title: "E49-Q04: Author the black-box state-matrix test plan for every panel and failure mode"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E49-Q04>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: qa, type/chore, area/qa, priority/p2, a11y

**Done means**
- Matrix data complete; self-check green against the screens catalogue.
- Harness implemented with the production-absence build assertion green.
- Assertions implemented per cell, including a11y semantics and analytics payloads.
- Meta-test proves assertions can fail.
- Baseline run published with an actionable non-conformance list for E49-S05.
- Specs contributed into E49-Q01's pack as the `@state-matrix` shard within budget.

**Do NOT**
- Fixing non-conformances — E49-S05.
- Pixel-level visual comparison, which belongs to design QA (E49-S04's visual-regression baselines), not to this structural matrix.
- Testing the underlying failure behaviour itself (reconnect strategy, load shedding) — **E45** and **E46**.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E49-Q04` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Burn down wave 3: bring open P2s to the GA bar and triage every P3
body:
## Context
R5 exit criterion 3 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 is precise: "Zero open P0/P1 bugs; open P2 count ≤10 with owners and target sprints; open P3 triaged." Waves 1 and 2 handled P0/P1. Wave 3 is the P2 sweep plus the P3 triage discipline that makes "triaged" mean something.

`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 defines P2 as a partially-broken feature, non-blocking, cosmetic-but-confusing, or an accessibility AA violation — "should fix before release; may be scheduled next sprint with owner sign-off". The GA bar accepts up to ten such items, but only with a named owner and a target sprint, which is what stops the category from becoming a landfill.

Wave 3 runs in S25, leaving S26 for verification, the GA regression pack and sign-offs rather than for fixing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **P2 sweep**: fix P2s in cluster order until the open count is ≤10, prioritising by (a) cluster size, (b) user-facing frequency evidenced by the analytics in E49-D02's event list (`empty_state_shown`, `error.403_shown`, `error.404_shown`, `app.error_boundary_triggered`, `degraded.entered`, `ratelimit.hit`), and (c) proximity to trading-critical surfaces.
- **The surviving ≤10 P2s**: each given a named owner, a written user-impact statement, a target post-GA sprint and an Owner sign-off, recorded on the ticket per §11.3's "may be scheduled next sprint with owner sign-off".
- **P3 triage pass**: every open P3 reviewed and given a disposition — fix now (cheap and adjacent to work already in flight), keep in backlog with a target, or close as won't-fix with a one-line reason. No P3 remains untouched.
- **Accessibility AA P2s**: verified as routed to and accepted by **E47**, or fixed here where E47 has closed and the finding is residual.
- **Batch fixes for trivial clusters**: P3 cosmetic items sharing a root (a spacing token, a truncation rule, a tooltip pattern) fixed together, using the `p3-cosmetic-exempt` regression-guard exemption only where a test genuinely adds no value, with the reason stated per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3.
- **Final forecast check** and wave report in the triage log.

## Out of scope
- P0/P1 work (waves 1 and 2) — any new P0/P1 raised during S25 is handled under the wave-1/2 rules and the freeze policy, not absorbed silently here.
- Design-QA, state, copy and hotkey remediation — E49-S04…S07, even though many are P2-severity, because they are tracked as their own ledgers.
- Any P2 whose fix requires new capability — re-filed as a post-GA Story.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The P2 bar is met with evidence
  Given the open P2 set at the end of Sprint 25
  When the count is reported on the burn-down dashboard
  Then at most 10 P2 bugs remain open
  And each has a named owner, a user-impact statement, a target post-GA sprint and a recorded Owner sign-off

Scenario: Every P3 has a disposition
  Given the open P3 backlog
  When the triage pass completes
  Then every P3 carries one of: scheduled with a target, kept with an explicit backlog disposition, or closed won't-fix with a reason
  And a query for untriaged P3s returns zero results

Scenario: Frequency evidence drives priority, not taste
  Given two P2 bugs of equal cluster size
  When they are prioritised
  Then the one whose surface shows the higher analytics occurrence rate is scheduled first
  And the ordering rationale is recorded so it can be challenged

Scenario: A cosmetic exemption is not a loophole
  Given a P3 closed using the p3-cosmetic-exempt label
  When the closure is reviewed
  Then the label carries a written reason explaining why a regression test adds no value
  And any exemption used on a non-cosmetic change is rejected in review

Scenario: The bar is reached by fixing, not by re-grading
  Given the P2 count is above 10 late in Sprint 25
  When a bug's severity is proposed for downgrade
  Then the downgrade requires the QA lead's agreement against the section 11.3 definition
  And downgrades are counted and reported in the wave report so the bar cannot be met by relabelling
```

## Technical notes / design
- Each fix follows `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2: root cause fixed, or a deliberate symptom patch with a follow-up Task filed; a regression test added at the layer identified in the bug's DoR test-gap field, proven to fail pre-fix and pass post-fix.
- PRs stay ≤400 LOC per `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md`; one cluster or one bug per PR; never batch unrelated fixes, because a mixed PR cannot be reverted cleanly during a GA train.
- Cluster fixes touching the OMS order-submission path must preserve the native-SL-on-every-fanned-out-order invariant with an explicit asserting test (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.4).
- Every merged fix runs the full required-check set including E46's CI-enforced performance budgets; a >5% regression on any hard budget fails the build (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.4).
- Incident notes are written for every P0 and P1 per `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.2, capturing detection-to-fix timeline, and feed `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: a regression test per closed P2 at its identified layer; cosmetic P3 exemptions used only where justified.
- **Visual regression**: for token/spacing/truncation clusters, screenshot-comparison tests on the affected Storybook stories, so a cosmetic cluster gets one mechanical guard rather than none.
- **Contract/integration**: re-run for any touched surface.
- **E2E**: additions for user-visible P2s on trading-critical surfaces, folded into E49-Q01.
- **A11y**: axe-core and pa11y-ci on every touched screen; AA violations are P2 minimum per `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §12.
- **Perf**: E46 budget checks required.
- **Coverage**: ≥85% backend/engine, ≥80% frontend; no baseline regression.

## Security notes
P2s rarely look like security work, which is exactly the risk. Reviewers apply `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8: a "cosmetic" change to a 403 or 404 message, an error string, a tooltip on an admin surface, or a disabled-control reason can become an information-disclosure defect. Specific checks in this wave: 403/404 copy must not reveal whether an admin-only resource exists (SCR-154, SCR-155); error strings must not gain raw exception text or internal hostnames; a fix that makes a disabled control's reason more specific must not leak another user's or account's state. Any P2 touching auth, keys, OMS or RBAC gets the full security gate regardless of its cosmetic appearance.

## Accessibility notes
Accessibility AA violations are P2 by policy (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §12), so this wave carries real a11y content. Every fix re-runs axe-core on its screen, verifies the keyboard-only path, checks focus order and visible focus per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`, and preserves accessible names. Residual a11y items not fixed here must be accepted by **E47** with a written non-conformance entry in its conformance report, not left implicit.

## Performance notes
E46's budgets are required checks. Visual-regression tests must run on the reference configuration and not in a degraded rendering mode, or they produce false diffs. A cosmetic fix that adds a layout-thrashing style is a perf regression and is caught by the budget check, not waved through as "just CSS".

## Observability
- The dashboard's P2/P3 series is the acceptance instrument for this wave; the wave report cites the dashboard at the S25 boundary.
- Downgrade count is published explicitly, so the bar's integrity is auditable.
- Analytics occurrence rates used for prioritisation are recorded on the tickets, making the ordering reproducible.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Open P2 count ≤10, each with owner, impact statement, target sprint and Owner sign-off.
- [ ] Every P3 triaged with a recorded disposition; zero untriaged.
- [ ] Regression guard per closed bug, or a justified cosmetic exemption.
- [ ] Visual-regression guards added for cosmetic clusters.
- [ ] a11y gate green on touched screens; residual items accepted by E47 in writing.
- [ ] perf: no E46 budget regression.
- [ ] security: §8 gating applied; disclosure checks performed on copy and state changes.
- [ ] QA sign-off with repro re-verification and adjacent sweep.
- [ ] Wave report published including the downgrade count and the final forecast.
- [ ] All PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies
- **E49-S02** — the P1 queue must be empty before P2 capacity is spent, or a P1 regression competes with cosmetic work.
- **E47** must have published its conformance verdicts so residual a11y P2s can be routed or accepted.

## Branch
`fix/<area>-<short>` per bug or cluster · PR size ≤400 LOC; cosmetic clusters may batch within a single root cause only.

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3 taxonomy, §12 a11y protocol.
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 exit criteria.
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6, §8.
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-154, SCR-155 (disclosure constraints on copy fixes).
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md
2. docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md
3. docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan` (owner: @CandleViewer/architecture)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm verify`
- `cd services/api && pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `fix/<area>-<short>`
- PR title: "E49-S03: Burn down wave 3: bring open P2s to the GA bar and triage every P3"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E49-S03>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/docs/plan/` (@CandleViewer/architecture); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/bug, area/cross-cutting, priority/p2, qa

**Done means**
- Open P2 count ≤10, each with owner, impact statement, target sprint and Owner sign-off.
- Every P3 triaged with a recorded disposition; zero untriaged.
- Regression guard per closed bug, or a justified cosmetic exemption.
- Visual-regression guards added for cosmetic clusters.
- a11y gate green on touched screens; residual items accepted by E47 in writing.
- perf: no E46 budget regression.

**Do NOT**
- P0/P1 work (waves 1 and 2) — any new P0/P1 raised during S25 is handled under the wave-1/2 rules and the freeze policy, not absorbed silently here.
- Design-QA, state, copy and hotkey remediation — E49-S04…S07, even though many are P2-severity, because they are tracked as their own ledgers.
- Any P2 whose fix requires new capability — re-filed as a post-GA Story.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E49-S03` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Execute the 72-hour soak and the full-capacity composite load scenario on the GA candidate
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 makes a **72-hour continuous-use soak with flat memory** an explicit R5 exit criterion, and `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §9's consolidated scenario table ends with a composite row — 10 symbols, 5 accounts, 5 users, 20 concurrent pane subscriptions, sustained — whose pass criteria must all hold *simultaneously*. Neither has ever been run: the existing harness windows are 2 h (frontend memory, budget #7) and 24 h (ingestion, budget #5).

This is the ticket where the epic's claims meet reality. Every optimisation in E46 is validated in a short window against a seeded fixture; a 72-hour run against a live-shaped generator is the only thing that catches the failure modes that matter most in a trading terminal — slow leaks, fragmentation, texture-atlas growth, unbounded caches, ring buffers that wrap wrong on day three, a QuestDB partition rollover that stalls, a reconnect path that leaks a subscription each time.

It is P0 because a GA that has never been left running over a weekend is not a GA for a tool whose user leaves it running over the weekend.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **72 h continuous-use soak**: a realistic 4-pane workspace (candles + footprint + heatmap + CVD) on the GA candidate build, driven by a live-shaped tick generator (or a long-loop replay of recorded fixtures with timestamps rebased so the app sees continuous live-shaped data, not a loop boundary every hour), with periodic realistic user interaction (pan, zoom, symbol switch, layout switch, replay session, order-ticket open/close on demo) scripted so the run exercises more than an idle window.
- **Sampling regime**: frontend RSS and GPU memory, backend RSS per symbol, JS heap, `fe_frame_time_ms{stage}` p50/p95, `fe_dropped_frames_total`, `ws_fanout_latency_seconds`, `event_loop_lag_seconds`, QuestDB on-disk growth, open file descriptors and socket counts — sampled at a fixed interval for the whole window, archived as a CI/release artefact.
- **Full-capacity composite scenario**: the §9 composite row executed for a sustained 2 h via E46-Q01's Locust scenario, with *all* its pass criteria asserted simultaneously (frame budget, WS→screen latency, backend fan-out, REST latency, per-symbol CPU and RSS, zero ingestion loss).
- **Ingestion 24 h soak re-run** on the GA candidate for budget #5 (zero undetected loss), since the earlier run predates E46's backend changes.
- **Replay soak** at 100× on a recorded 24 h symbol-day for budget #15 (crash-free, no desync).
- **Analysis and verdict**: a written report per run — leak verdict (monotonic growth vs bounded variance, with the statistical test used stated, not eyeballed from a graph), budget-by-budget pass/fail, and for any failure a filed Bug with the profiling artefacts attached and an owning ticket.
- **Restart-free assertion**: no backend process OOM, crash or supervisor restart during any window; the run is invalidated (not silently restarted) if one occurs.

## Out of scope
- Fixing what the soak finds — failures are filed as Bugs against E46-T06 (frontend memory) / E46-T07 (backend memory & CPU) / the owning epic, and re-run; this ticket executes and adjudicates.
- Chaos injection during the soak — E45 owns failure drills; the soak is a *steady-state* test and deliberately keeps its variables few. A separate short chaos-under-load pass is E46-Q03's charter.
- Live-environment execution — soaks run against demo/staging per the environment separation from E44.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Frontend memory is flat over 72 hours
  Given the GA candidate runs the scripted 4-pane workspace for 72 hours
  Then resident memory stays within the documented variance band with no monotonic upward trend
  And it never exceeds the 1.5GB ceiling of budget #7
  And GPU memory at hour 72 is within the same band as at hour 2

Scenario: Frame time has not drifted
  Given the same 72-hour run
  Then p95 frame time measured in the final hour is within 5% of the value measured in the first full hour
  And no stage from the §4.3 breakdown has grown beyond its slice over the window

Scenario: Backend is flat and within budget
  Given the same window with 10 recorded symbols
  Then backend RSS per symbol stays at or below 300MB (budget #8)
  And per-symbol CPU stays at or below 0.5 vCPU sustained (budget #11)
  And no process OOMs, crashes or is restarted by the supervisor

Scenario: The composite capacity scenario passes as a whole
  Given 10 symbols, 5 accounts, 5 users and 20 concurrent pane subscriptions sustained for 2 hours
  Then every pass criterion in the composite row of docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §9 holds simultaneously
  And a failure of any single criterion fails the scenario, even if the others pass

Scenario: Ingestion loses nothing in 24 hours
  Given the ingestion soak runs for 24 hours per symbol on the GA candidate
  Then the message-loss counter is zero
  And every detected gap has a corresponding recorded gap entry

Scenario: A leak is caught rather than explained away
  Given resident memory grows by a sustained amount across the window
  Then the run is failed
  And a heap or allocation capture is taken at the point of growth and attached to a filed Bug
  And the run is not marked pass on the grounds that the ceiling was never reached

Scenario: Replay at 100x survives
  Given a recorded 24-hour symbol-day is replayed at 100x
  Then playback completes without crash and without desync between panes
  And the 30fps floor is never breached
```

## Technical notes / design
"Flat" needs a definition, or it becomes an argument: the verdict uses a linear regression over the RSS samples of the final 48 h, and fails if the fitted slope implies growth beyond the documented variance band extrapolated over a further week. Sawtooth from GC is expected and is not growth; the regression is run on the post-GC minima envelope, not the raw samples. State the method in the report.

The tick generator must be live-shaped, not uniform: bursts, quiet periods and at least one synthetic volatility event per 24 h (5× message rate for 60 s, per §3.2's worst-case definition), otherwise the soak measures an unrealistically kind workload.

Loop-boundary artefacts are the classic false negative and false positive of long soaks: if replay looping is used, timestamps are rebased and continuity is asserted, and any metric discontinuity at a loop boundary invalidates the window.

Run scheduling: the 72 h window must be started early enough in Sprint 25 to allow one full re-run after a failure. Plan for two windows, not one; a single 72 h run late in the sprint is a plan with no failure budget.

## Test plan
This ticket *is* a test execution. Its own correctness controls: the sampling agent is verified against a process with a known synthetic leak before the real run (proving the harness detects growth); the composite scenario is smoke-run for 10 minutes before the 2 h execution; artefact archival is verified before the long window starts, so a 72 h run is never lost to a full disk or an unwritten artefact path.

## Security notes
Soak artefacts (heap snapshots, `memray` captures, `py-spy` dumps, log bundles) may contain order, account and symbol data from the demo environment and are classified Confidential per `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; they are stored in the release artefact store with access control, never attached to a public issue, and are subject to a stated retention. Demo credentials used by the driver come from the environment. The run must not be pointed at live (E44 environment separation; the target allow-list from E46-Q01 applies).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface introduced. The scripted interaction should include at least one keyboard-driven navigation cycle so that the keyboard path is exercised under sustained load too.

## Performance notes
Budgets asserted: #1, #2, #3, #5, #6, #7, #8, #11, #13, #14, #15. This ticket is the single largest evidence producer for E46-Q04's sign-off pack and for the R5 exit criterion in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3.

## Observability
The run exercises and validates the whole metric surface added by E46-T01 and E46-T04; any metric that turns out to be missing, wrong or unbounded in cardinality over a 72 h window is itself a finding and is filed.

- [ ] Leak verdict states its statistical method and its variance band.

- [ ] Sign-off comment from QA lead; results presented to the Owner.

title: Run the exploratory performance charter, degradation-ladder verification and a11y audit of SCR-046/SCR-118
body:
## Context
Scripted load tests measure what someone thought to measure. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` pairs them with exploratory testing for exactly that reason, and the performance failures that actually reach users are usually the ones no script models: switching layouts twenty times in a minute, dragging a drawing while replay runs at 50×, opening the DOM heatmap on five symbols and then minimising the window, a monitor hot-unplug, a laptop suspend/resume, an Electron window moved between a high-DPI and a low-DPI display.

This ticket also owns two things that are performance-adjacent but user-facing: proving the `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4 **degradation ladder** behaves as documented — including the non-negotiable rules that frames never drop below 30 fps, that trading-critical overlays are *never* shed, and that the "reduced live detail" indicator is not colour-only — and auditing the two screens this epic ships (SCR-046, SCR-118) against WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (time-boxed, session-based, each with a written debrief): (1) *layout and window churn* — rapid layout/workspace switching, floating-window creation and destruction, monitor changes, DPI changes, minimise/restore, suspend/resume; (2) *interaction under load* — drawing, crosshair, order-ticket use while at realistic-peak load and during replay at high speed; (3) *the long tail of symbols* — switching symbols rapidly, subscribing/unsubscribing, symbols with sparse history, a symbol with extreme footprint density; (4) *recovery* — behaviour after WebGL context loss, after backend restart, after a network drop over Tailscale, each while under load; (5) *settings extremes* — every SCR-118 control at both ends of its range, including combinations the recommended presets never produce.
- **Degradation-ladder verification**: drive the engine into each of the four §4.4 rungs deliberately, in order, and assert documented behaviour at each — heatmap cadence relaxing toward 250 ms, footprint text LOD hiding, redraw coalescing, and the focused-pane-only fallback — plus the three "never acceptable" invariants (no sub-30 fps, no dropped order-line/position overlay updates, no DOM-mirror desync).
- **Chaos-under-load pass**: reuse E45's chaos harness for WS disconnect, exchange 5xx and rate-limit 10018 *while at realistic-peak load*, verifying that failure handling does not itself blow the frame or latency budget (E45 proves correctness; this proves correctness-under-load).
- **a11y audit** of SCR-046 and SCR-118: axe-core automated pass, manual screen-reader passes (one Windows/NVDA, one macOS/VoiceOver if available, otherwise one screen reader with the deviation recorded), keyboard-only traversal, focus order and visible focus, contrast verification of every tone used for budget states, and specific verification that no performance state is communicated by colour alone anywhere in the epic's surface.
- **Findings**: every finding filed as a Bug with a reproduction, a severity and an owner; the charters' debriefs retained as release artefacts.

## Out of scope
- The long soaks and the composite capacity scenario (E46-Q02).
- The standing, product-wide a11y audit and remediation (E47) — this ticket audits only the two screens E46 ships.
- Authoring chaos scenarios (E45 owns them).
- Security abuse cases (E46-X02).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every charter is executed and debriefed
  Given the five exploratory charters
  Then each has a time-boxed session with a written debrief listing what was covered, what was found and what was not reached
  And every finding is filed with a reproduction and a severity

Scenario: The degradation ladder engages in the documented order
  Given load is increased progressively toward the worst-case scenario of §3.2
  Then heatmap cadence relaxes first, then footprint text LOD engages, then redraw coalescing, then the focused-pane-only fallback
  And no later rung engages before an earlier one

Scenario: The floor holds
  Given the worst-case stress scenario including a 5x message-rate burst
  Then the frame rate never drops below 30fps
  And no order-line or position-overlay update is dropped at any rung
  And the DOM-mirror never desyncs from what is rendered

Scenario: Degradation is announced non-visually
  Given the focused-pane-only fallback has engaged
  Then a "reduced live detail" indicator is present
  And it is conveyed by text, not by colour alone
  And a screen reader announces the state change politely

Scenario: Failure handling does not break the budget
  Given the market WS is dropped while the system is at realistic-peak load
  Then reconnection, resubscription and book resync complete per US-OBS-006
  And during recovery the frame rate stays above the 30fps floor
  And WS-to-screen latency returns within budget #3 once resync completes

Scenario: Both new screens pass the a11y audit
  Given SCR-046 and SCR-118 on the GA candidate
  Then axe-core reports no violations
  And every control is reachable and operable by keyboard alone
  And a manual screen-reader pass confirms labels, units, measured values and state changes are announced
  And all contrast ratios meet WCAG 2.2 AA

Scenario: A found defect is not lost
  Given an exploratory session finds an intermittent stutter that cannot be reproduced on demand
  Then it is filed with the captured diagnostics snapshot and the conditions observed
  And it is triaged rather than closed as unreproducible without investigation
```

## Technical notes / design
Session-based test management: each charter gets a stated mission, a time box (90 minutes), a tester, and a debrief covering coverage / findings / obstacles / next session. Charters are not scripts — a step-by-step charter is a test case that has been mislabelled.

Driving the degradation ladder deliberately needs a hook: use the SCR-118 controls plus a synthetic load injector to raise pane count, depth and message rate independently, so each rung can be reached in isolation rather than only under an avalanche where the order is unobservable.

The copy-diagnostics snapshot from SCR-046 (E46-S01) is the standard attachment for every finding filed by this ticket — that is what it was built for, and using it here validates it.

Intermittent findings are the norm in performance exploratory work. The rule is: captured and triaged, never dismissed. A finding with a diagnostics snapshot and stated conditions is actionable even without a deterministic repro.

## Test plan
This ticket is test execution. Evidence: five debriefs, one degradation-verification report with a table of rung → observed behaviour → verdict, one chaos-under-load report, one a11y audit report per screen with axe output and manual pass notes.

## Security notes
Exploratory sessions run against the demo environment only. Diagnostics snapshots attached to findings must be the redacted snapshot produced by SCR-046, not a raw state dump; if a tester finds that the snapshot contains anything sensitive, that is itself a security finding and is routed to E46-X02 rather than filed as a normal Bug. Screen recordings from sessions can capture account balances and order data and are handled as Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket contains the epic's a11y audit; the standards applied are `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` and WCAG 2.2 AA. Particular attention: the colour-independence rule as it applies to every threshold/tone in SCR-046, SCR-118 and the degradation indicator; polite (never assertive) live regions for values that update at 2 Hz; the pinned-overlay static-table reading mode; `aria-busy` during the SCR-118 benchmark; and keyboard access to `Ctrl+Shift+D` for users who cannot chord (command-palette route).

## Performance notes
Asserts budget #2 (30 fps floor, degraded mode), budget #14 (heatmap cadence, including its documented relaxation), budget #15 (replay), and the §4.4 ladder's invariants. Also verifies that the diagnostics overlay's own ≤0.5 ms/frame budget holds during the charters, since the overlay is open for much of the session.

## Observability
Findings reference the metric values observed at the time from the E46-T01/T04 surface; where a finding cannot be explained by the existing metrics, the gap is filed as an observability improvement rather than left as a mystery.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All seven Gherkin scenarios adjudicated.
- [ ] Five charter debriefs written and retained.
- [ ] Degradation-ladder verification table complete, with the three "never acceptable" invariants explicitly signed off.
- [ ] Chaos-under-load report complete.
- [ ] a11y audit reports for SCR-046 and SCR-118, axe output attached, manual screen-reader pass recorded (with the deviation noted if only one screen reader was available).
- [ ] Every finding filed, triaged, severity-assigned and owner-assigned; P0/P1 findings fixed and re-verified before GA.
- [ ] QA lead sign-off comment.

## Dependencies
- **E46-Q01** for scenarios, injectors and fixtures.
- **E46-S01** and **E46-S02** must be built — two of the audit targets are those screens, and the diagnostics snapshot is the evidence mechanism.
- **E45** chaos harness reused for the chaos-under-load pass.

## Branch
`chore/e46-exploratory-and-a11y-audit` for any harness/test-hook additions.

## References
`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` · `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` · `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.2, §4.4, §2 budgets #2/#14/#15 · `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-046, SCR-118 · `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-OBS-002, US-OBS-006, US-SET-008, US-DOM-005 · `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2

body:
## Context
`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` gates each release behind a production-readiness review, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.4 lists "Perf" as an R5 quality gate. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires epic-level QA sign-off — *"an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA"* — and epic-level acceptance criteria verified end to end rather than per child.

E46 produces a large amount of evidence across many tickets: harness reports, soak reports, k6/Locust runs, the degradation verification table, a11y audits, the CI gate configuration and the security review. This ticket makes that evidence a single reviewable artefact for the PRR, checks it for gaps against the 15 budgets, and closes the epic.

It is deliberately small in points and sits at the very end of the epic's train window: E46 is bounded to **S23–S25** by `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.2/§12 and the §12 gantt entry `E46 Performance hardening [S23-S25]`, so this ticket is scheduled in the back half of **Sprint 25**, immediately after E46-Q02/Q03/X02 land in the same sprint. It produces no new measurement, it adjudicates — so it does not need a sprint of its own, and scheduling it into Sprint 26 would put E46 outside its stated train window without a waiver.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Gap analysis**: any budget without a GA-candidate measurement is listed explicitly as a gap with a disposition (measured late / waived with Owner sign-off / descoped), because an unmeasured budget silently presented as green is the failure mode this pack exists to prevent.
- **CI gate inventory**: the list of required checks E46-T10 established, with evidence that the injected-regression test proves each bites, and the named owner for each gate.
- **Baseline snapshot**: the `bench/baselines/` contents at GA, tagged with the release, so post-GA drift is measurable against a known point.
- **Open-risk statement**: remaining performance risks carried into GA, each with a mitigation, a trigger and an owner — fed into `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` and the perf-incidents log created by E46-T11.
- **Epic-level acceptance verification**: each of the five epic acceptance scenarios in E46's body adjudicated with a pointer to its evidence.
- **QA sign-off comment** on the epic recording pass/fail per scenario, plus the explicit list of deviations (any scenario verified manually rather than automatically, with a follow-up ticket filed to automate it, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2).
- **PRR input**: the pack submitted as the performance section of the R5 production-readiness review.

## Out of scope
- Running any new test (Q02/Q03 own execution; if a gap requires a new measurement, this ticket files it back to them rather than absorbing it).
- Fixing defects.
- Documentation and runbooks beyond the pack itself (E48).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given the GA performance evidence pack
  Then each of the 15 budgets in docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md §2 has a measured value, a method, an environment and a verdict

Scenario: The gates are proven, not assumed
  Given the CI gate inventory
  Then each required performance check has evidence that an injected regression fails it
  And each has a named owner

Scenario: Epic acceptance is adjudicated end to end
  Given E46's five epic-level acceptance scenarios
  Then each is marked pass or fail with a direct link to the evidence that decided it
  And a fail blocks the epic from Done

Scenario: A waived budget is visible, not hidden
  Given one budget cannot be measured on reference hardware before GA
  Then it appears in the pack as waived with the Owner's recorded sign-off and a follow-up ticket
  And it is not presented as green

Scenario: Sign-off records its deviations
  Given the QA sign-off comment
  Then it lists every scenario verified manually rather than automatically
  And each has a filed follow-up ticket to automate it
```

## Technical notes / design
The pack is assembled from artefacts, not re-typed from memory: every number in it links to the archived report that produced it (commit, runner, fixture hash). A number in the pack that cannot be traced to an artefact is treated as absent.

Structure mirrors §2's table so a reviewer can diff the pack against the standard line by line; this is deliberate, because the reviewer's job at the PRR is to find the row that is quietly missing.

## Test plan
Verification is by review: the pack is reviewed by the Architect, the frontend and backend leads, and the Security engineer (for the artefact-handling and telemetry-exposure statements). The traceability table from E46-Q01 is the checklist used.

## Security notes
The pack aggregates artefacts that individually may be Confidential (profiling captures, soak logs with demo order data). The pack itself must contain only measured numbers and links, so that the pack can circulate at the PRR while the underlying artefacts stay access-controlled. This split is stated explicitly in the pack's header. E46-X02's review outcome and residual-risk acceptances are summarised (not reproduced in full) in the open-risk statement.

## Accessibility notes
The a11y audit outcomes from E46-Q03 are included as a section of the pack, so that the PRR sees performance and accessibility evidence together rather than treating a11y as a separate afterthought. N/A otherwise — no UI surface.

## Performance notes
This ticket asserts nothing new; it is the consolidated statement of every budget's GA state, and is the input to the R5 exit criterion in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3 and the PRR gate in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Observability
The baseline snapshot and the gate inventory are the mechanism by which post-GA performance regressions remain detectable; the pack names where they live and who watches them.

title: Security review, abuse cases and SAST rules for the E46 telemetry and benchmark surface
body:
## Context
E46-X01 produces the model; this ticket proves the mitigations exist and hold, and leaves behind automation so they cannot silently rot. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 requires, for anything labelled `security`, that SAST/SCA/secrets scanning is clean or triaged and that a Security engineer review comment is present; the planning brief additionally mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit), DAST (OWASP ZAP) and secrets scanning as standing controls.

The specific risk this ticket exists to close is quiet and durable: the copy-diagnostics snapshot and the support bundle are built from an allow-list *today*, and six months from now someone adds a convenient field. A one-off manual review does not prevent that. A committed Semgrep rule and a test that fails when a secret-shaped key reaches the snapshot builder does.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Security review** of the epic's code surface: the snapshot builder and clipboard path (E46-S01), the benchmark runner, its guards and the local settings read path (E46-S02), the stage-timer and metric label construction (E46-T01, E46-T04), the trace/span-id and ingestion-timestamp propagation into the WS envelope (`docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §3.1), the CI gate and baseline-update workflow (E46-T10), and the load/soak script target configuration (E46-Q01).
- **Abuse cases executed**, from E46-X01's seeds:
  1. A user with RBAC **Viewer** opens SCR-046 and SCR-118 and attempts to read or change anything beyond their role.
  2. The local settings store is hand-edited to out-of-range, wrong-typed and hostile values (huge panel counts, negative cadences, a string where a number belongs, a deeply nested object) and the app is launched.
  3. "Run benchmark" is triggered repeatedly and concurrently, and while an order ticket is open and while replay runs, attempting to starve the trading path.
  4. A crafted state object containing secret-shaped keys is fed to the snapshot builder; the output is inspected for leakage.
  5. A metric label is driven from user-controlled input (symbol name, workspace name) to attempt a cardinality explosion.
  6. A load script is pointed at the live environment base URL.
  7. A baseline file is modified in a PR without the required review path, attempting to move a gate silently.
  8. The injected-regression build flag is sought in a production bundle.
- **SAST rules** committed (Semgrep for the repo, Bandit for Python where applicable): a rule forbidding construction of a diagnostics/support artefact by serialising a whole state object; a rule flagging any Prometheus/OTel label whose value is not drawn from a closed enum or a bounded constant; a rule flagging any log or artefact write of an identifier field name from the deny list. Each rule ships with a passing and a failing test case.
- **DAST**: a ZAP pass over any new or changed HTTP surface touched by this epic (the metrics endpoint's network binding, `/admin/health` and `/system/build` as consumed by the overlay) confirming the private-network binding of the metrics endpoint from US-OBS-001's NFR and that no new unauthenticated endpoint appeared.
- **Regression tests**: a permanent test asserting the snapshot allow-list (secret-shaped key absent from output), a test asserting the injected-regression flag is absent from the release bundle, and a test asserting metric label cardinality stays within the modelled bound.
- **Findings triage**: each finding fixed, or accepted with Owner sign-off and recorded; **Security engineer sign-off comment** posted on the epic.

## Out of scope
- Threat modelling (E46-X01).
- Pen-test and its remediation (E43 / the R4 gate) — this ticket does not re-run a pen-test.
- Product-wide RBAC implementation (E09/E42); abuse case 1 verifies RBAC behaviour on these two screens, it does not change RBAC.
- Functional QA (E46-Q01..Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Nothing sensitive leaves in the snapshot
  Given a state object seeded with a session token, an API key, an account id and an order id
  When the copy-diagnostics snapshot is built
  Then none of those values or key names appear in the output
  And the test that proves this is permanent and runs in CI

Scenario: The benchmark cannot starve the trading path
  Given "Run benchmark" is triggered repeatedly and concurrently
  Then only one run executes at a time
  And it is refused with a stated reason while an order ticket is open or replay is active
  And it is cancellable

Scenario: Hostile local settings do not crash or escalate
  Given the local settings store contains out-of-range, wrong-typed and hostile values
  When the app launches
  Then each invalid value falls back to its documented default with a logged warning
  And the app starts normally and no value is used unvalidated

Scenario: Metric cardinality cannot be driven by user input
  Given an attempt to use a user-controlled string as a metric label value
  Then the committed SAST rule flags it in CI
  And at runtime the label set remains within the bound stated in the E46-X01 model

Scenario: A load script cannot target live
  Given a load script configured with the live environment base URL
  Then it refuses to start with an explicit error

Scenario: A baseline cannot move silently
  Given a PR that modifies a file in bench/baselines/ without the required review and rationale
  Then the CI workflow blocks the merge

Scenario: A Viewer sees nothing beyond their role
  Given a user with the Viewer role
  When they open SCR-046 and SCR-118
  Then no control that mutates shared or account state is available to them
  And no account or order data is present in anything either screen displays

Scenario: The debug slowdown harness is not shipped
  Given a production build
  Then the injected-regression build flag and its code path are absent from the bundle
```

## Technical notes / design
Allow-list testing is done by seeding rather than by inspection: build a state object containing deliberately secret-shaped values and assert their absence in the output, so the test keeps working when the snapshot gains new legitimate fields. Both key names and values are asserted.

Semgrep rules live alongside the repo's existing ruleset with the same review requirements; each rule is accompanied by a fixture pair (should-flag, should-not-flag) so that a rule that stops matching is itself caught.

Abuse case 7's control is a CI workflow condition on the `bench/baselines/` path plus a CODEOWNERS entry — the policy is stated in ADR-0016 (E46-T11) and enforced here.

DAST scope is deliberately narrow: E46 adds essentially no HTTP surface, so the pass is a confirmation (nothing new appeared, the metrics binding is unchanged) rather than a full scan, and the report says so.

## Test plan
- **Unit/CI**: the three permanent regression tests (snapshot allow-list, release-bundle flag absence, label cardinality bound).
- **SAST**: rule fixture pairs; full-repo run clean or triaged.
- **Manual**: the eight abuse cases, each with a written result.
- **DAST**: ZAP pass report attached.
- **SCA/secrets**: `pip-audit`, `npm audit`, secrets scan clean or triaged over the epic's changed paths.

## Security notes
This ticket is the security verification for E46. Classification of its outputs: the review report and abuse-case results are Internal; any finding that reveals an exploitable path is handled per the program's vulnerability-handling process and is not discussed in a public issue until fixed.

## Accessibility notes
Abuse case 1 (Viewer role) is executed with keyboard-only navigation as well as mouse, so that a role restriction implemented only as a visual hide is caught — a control that is invisible but still focusable and operable is both an a11y defect and a security one.

## Performance notes
The permanent regression tests must be cheap enough to run on every PR; the cardinality test reads the registered metric descriptors rather than scraping a live endpoint. The SAST rules must not add more than a trivial amount to the existing Semgrep run time.

## Observability
Confirms that the audit trail required by E46-X01 (baseline changes, profiling captures) actually exists and is queryable, and that the new metric surface is free of user-controlled labels.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All eight Gherkin scenarios verified with recorded results.
- [ ] Security review report merged; every reviewed surface listed.
- [ ] Eight abuse cases executed and written up.
- [ ] SAST rules committed with fixture pairs and green in CI; Bandit/Semgrep/CodeQL clean or triaged.
- [ ] DAST pass report attached; metrics endpoint private-network binding confirmed.
- [ ] Three permanent regression tests merged and running on every PR.
- [ ] `bench/baselines/` CODEOWNERS + workflow guard in place.
- [ ] Findings fixed or accepted with Owner sign-off; **Security engineer sign-off comment posted on E46**.
- [ ] Outcome summarised for E46-Q04's evidence pack.

## Dependencies
- **E46-X01** supplies the model and the abuse-case seeds.
- **E46-S01**, **E46-S02**, **E46-T01**, **E46-T04**, **E46-T10** supply the code and configuration under review; all must be landed before the review is meaningful.

## Branch
`chore/e46-security-review`. Rules and tests may land as separate small PRs.

`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` · `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2, §4.2 · `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-OBS-001, US-OBS-003, US-OBS-007 · `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-046, SCR-118 · `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §3.1 · `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/admin/health`, `/system/build` · `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.4, §8 · `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`

- `cd services/api && pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`

- Pen-test and its remediation (E43 / the R4 gate) — this ticket does not re-run a pen-test.
