title: SAST/DAST rules and CI guards for accessible-surface data parity
body:
## Context
`E47-X02` proves the abuse cases at a point in time. Without automation those proofs expire: the next epic adds a panel, someone writes an `aria-label` from an unmasked field, and the parity guarantee quietly dies. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep) and DAST (OWASP ZAP) as CI gates; this ticket adds the rules specific to the accessible surface so the E47 guarantees are enforced continuously.

The rules encode one idea: **anything that can be read by a person can be read by a machine, and the accessible text path must be as carefully controlled as the visual one**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Semgrep/CodeQL rules** for the web and design-system packages:
  1. A taint-style rule flagging values from fields classified as secret or masked (API key fields, TOTP, session tokens) flowing into `aria-label`, `aria-describedby` targets, live-region text, DOM-mirror node text or table-alternative cells.
  2. A rule flagging `aria-hidden="true"` applied to an interactive element, and flagging any use of `aria-hidden` as the sole mechanism gating a privileged control (the anti-pattern `E47-X02` case 3 tests).
  3. A rule flagging `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or equivalent inside mirror, live-region or accessible-name construction paths - accessible text must be text.
  4. A rule flagging `outline: none` (or equivalent focus suppression) without an adjacent compliant focus style, enforcing standard section 3.1 statically as well as at runtime.
  5. A rule flagging construction of accessible names by string concatenation with user-controlled values without the shared sanitiser, so case 9 of the abuse suite cannot recur.
  6. A rule requiring every `<canvas>` creation site in product code to register a mirror root, complementing the runtime guardrail in `E47-Q08`.
- **DAST/ZAP configuration additions**: authenticated scans as viewer, manager and owner against the screens that render accessible mirrors, with a passive rule inspecting response bodies for privileged field names appearing in accessibility attributes; plus a scan profile exercising `/api/v1/me/preferences` and `/api/v1/settings/hotkeys*` with malformed and privilege-escalating payloads.
- **CI wiring**: new rules run in the existing SAST/DAST jobs as required checks; findings are triaged into the security findings register, not printed and forgotten.
- A short rule-authoring note so future teams can extend the rule set, including how to add a field to the secret/masked classification list that rule 1 reads.

## Out of scope
- Generic web SAST/DAST coverage - already established by the security program; this ticket only adds accessibility-surface-specific rules.
- Dependency scanning and container scanning - unchanged.
- Fixing the issues the new rules surface on existing code (beyond suppressions with owners and dates); those become defects.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Feature: Accessibility-surface SAST and DAST rules

  Scenario: Secret-to-accessible-text flow is detected statically
    Given code that assigns an unmasked API-key value to an aria-label
    When SAST runs
    Then the rule fires with the file, line and the classified field name
    And the check blocks merge

  Scenario: aria-hidden on an interactive element is flagged
    Given a focusable button marked aria-hidden true
    When SAST runs
    Then the rule fires and references 05-accessibility-standard.md

  Scenario: Failure case - false positives are managed, not normalised
    Given a rule that fires on a legitimate pattern
    When a suppression is added
    Then it carries a justification, an owner and an expiry date
    And an expired suppression fails the build

  Scenario: Edge case - DAST detects a privileged field name in an accessibility attribute
    Given an authenticated viewer scan of an admin-adjacent screen
    When the passive rule inspects the response
    And a privileged field name appears inside an aria attribute
    Then a finding is raised with the URL and the attribute

  Scenario: Rules are maintainable
    Given the rule-authoring note
    When an engineer adds a new masked field to the classification list
    Then rule 1 covers it without any rule code change
```

## Technical notes / design
- Rule 1 depends on a **field classification list** (which fields are secret/masked). That list must be a single committed artefact shared with the redaction post-processors in `E47-Q04` and `E47-Q05`; three copies of the list is how this rots.
- Static analysis of accessible names is inherently approximate in a React codebase; the rules are tuned for a low false-positive rate and paired with the runtime checks in `E47-Q03`/`E47-Q08`, which catch what static analysis cannot see. Neither layer is claimed sufficient alone, and the note says so.
- ZAP authenticated scans reuse the seeded role accounts from the existing security jobs; scans run against staging/demo only, never live.
- Findings flow into the same register as `E47-X01`/`E47-X02` so the epic's security posture is one list.

## Test plan
- Each rule is validated against a **positive fixture** (code that must trigger it) and a **negative fixture** (similar code that must not), both committed under the rule set - the only way to keep rules honest as the codebase changes.
- The DAST addition is validated against a deliberately vulnerable staging build exposing a privileged field name in an aria attribute; the scan must report it.
- Run the rules across the full existing codebase, record the baseline, and triage every hit before the check becomes blocking.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* security tooling. Two cautions: rule output can itself disclose sensitive values if it echoes matched content, so findings report locations and classifications rather than raw values; and scan artefacts inherit the redaction and retention rules used elsewhere in the epic.

## Accessibility notes
The rules are written so the compliant fix is always the accessible one: rule 2 pushes towards not rendering privileged controls rather than hiding them from AT; rule 4 pushes towards a compliant focus style rather than removing focus indication; rule 3 pushes towards plain text rather than markup in announcements. A rule whose easiest fix degrades accessibility is a badly written rule and must be revised.

## Performance notes
The added SAST rules must not materially extend CI time; measure before and after and keep the delta within the envelope agreed in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. Authenticated DAST scans are slower and run on merge to `main` and nightly rather than per PR, with the split documented.

## Observability
- Metrics: `sec_a11y_rule_findings{rule,severity}`, `sec_a11y_suppressions_active`, `sec_dast_a11y_findings`.
- New findings notify the Security engineer; a rule firing for the first time in months is worth a human look rather than an auto-suppression.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Six SAST rules merged with positive and negative fixtures each.
- [ ] DAST profile additions merged and validated against a vulnerable staging build.
- [ ] Shared field-classification list extracted and consumed by the rules and both redaction post-processors.
- [ ] Baseline triaged; checks required on `main`; suppression policy with expiry enforced.
- [ ] Rule-authoring note merged and linked from the security program docs.
- [ ] CI duration delta measured and within the agreed envelope.

## Dependencies
- `E47-X01` - the threat model determines which rules are worth writing.
- `E47-X02` - confirmed issues become the rules' positive fixtures.

## Branch
`feat/e47-a11y-security-rules`.

## References
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (SAST/DAST tooling, gate placement, findings register, suppression policy).
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 3.1 (focus visibility), 6.1-6.3 (mirror, live regions, tables).
- `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` (required checks).
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` (CI time envelope).
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/me/preferences`, `/settings/hotkeys*` (DAST targets).
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` (web module boundaries the rules apply to).

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (this ticket's SCR-xxx entry)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant §)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `apps/web` (owner: @CandleViewer/frontend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`
- `pnpm e2e`
- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e47-a11y-security-rules`
- PR title: "E47-X03: SAST/DAST rules and CI guards for accessible-surface data parity"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E47-X03>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/apps/web/` (@CandleViewer/frontend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/security, area/design-system, priority/p2, security, a11y

**Done means**
- Six SAST rules merged with positive and negative fixtures each.
- DAST profile additions merged and validated against a vulnerable staging build.
- Shared field-classification list extracted and consumed by the rules and both redaction post-processors.
- Baseline triaged; checks required on `main`; suppression policy with expiry enforced.
- Rule-authoring note merged and linked from the security program docs.
- CI duration delta measured and within the agreed envelope.

**Do NOT**
- Generic web SAST/DAST coverage - already established by the security program; this ticket only adds accessibility-surface-specific rules.
- Dependency scanning and container scanning - unchanged.
- Fixing the issues the new rules surface on existing code (beyond suppressions with owners and dates); those become defects.
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E47-X03` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Documentation, runbooks & GA readiness
body:
## Context

CandleViewer reaches GA at the end of Sprint 26 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.5, tag `v1.1.0`, 2027-03-25). Everything else in R5 makes the *system* good enough to ship; this epic makes the system **operable and comprehensible by someone who did not build it** — which `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.1 goal 4 states as an explicit R5 goal and §9.3 exit criteria 5 and 6 turn into hard gates:

- exit criterion 5: "All runbooks rehearsed at least once; DR playbook executed with measured RTO/RPO recorded";
- exit criterion 6: "Documentation complete: user guide, ops runbooks, API/WS reference, ADR index, onboarding guide";
- §9.4 Docs quality gate: "Every runbook rehearsed and dated; docs reviewed by someone who did not write them".

The PRR checklist (`docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §5.2, §5.3, §5.6) already *requires* runbooks for WS disconnect/reconnect storms, exchange outage, rate-limit breach, OMS stuck-order reconciliation, fan-out partial failure, Postgres failover, QuestDB/Parquet corruption recovery, feature-flag emergency kill and full-system rollback, plus a restore drill measured against the RPO/RTO table in §5.3. Those runbooks are *named* there but not written; E45 automated the drills (`E45-T09`, `E45-T10`) and wrote the resilience subset (`E45-T11`). E48 completes the set, indexes it, and — critically — **rehearses** every entry so that "the runbook exists" and "the runbook works" are not confused.

The second half of this epic is the user-facing documentation the plan has been deferring: a persona-shaped user guide (P1 Owner/trader, P2 Account Manager, P3 Viewer, P4 Admin from `docs/plan/10-personas.md`), an in-app help surface that already has a designed home at **SCR-119 Help & about** (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-119) and is traced to **US-SET-009** and **US-OBS-007** in `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, and a published API/WS reference generated from the contracts (`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`) rather than hand-written and therefore rotting.

The dependency graph in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 has `E46 --> E48`: performance hardening lands the final numbers that the docs must quote, so E48 sits at S25–S26, the last two sprints, after the rest of R5 has stopped changing behaviour.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Docs toolchain decision and site** (E48-K01, E48-T02): a published, searchable documentation site built in CI from the repo, including an **API/WS reference generated from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`** so it can never drift from the contract.
- **Architecture and ADR reconciliation** (E48-T01): `docs/plan/20-architecture.md`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md`, `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` and `docs/plan/27-adrs/` brought into agreement with the system as built; the ADR index in `27-adrs/README.md` and `20-architecture.md` §16 reconciled; ADR-0011 (Electron vs Tauri, still `proposed`) resolved or formally superseded.
- **Operations runbook set** (E48-T03) covering every runbook named in `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` §5.2 plus the failure register F1–F18 in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §11.1, each with a trigger, a detection signal, numbered steps, a verification step and a rollback step.
- **Disaster-recovery playbook with measured RTO/RPO** (E48-T04) executed against the §5.3 targets (Postgres RPO ≤15 min / RTO ≤2 h; QuestDB hot tier RPO ≤24 h / RTO ≤4 h; Parquet cold tier RPO 0 / RTO ≤4 h) and the `20-architecture.md` §11.2 objectives (backend RTO ≤90 s, relational RPO ≤5 min).
- **Engineer onboarding guide** (E48-T05): zero-to-running-system in a day, mapped onto the monorepo layout in `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §5.
- **GA checklist execution and release artefacts** (E48-T06, E48-T07): the `07-release-and-prr.md` §4 release checklist and §5 PRR checklist run for `v1.1.0`, with evidence collected mechanically rather than screenshotted by hand; `CHANGELOG.md` finalised and fed into the in-app **CMP-096 WhatsNewPanel**.
- **User guide per persona and its in-app surfacing** (E48-S01): US-SET-009, US-OBS-007 on **SCR-119**, with **CMP-051 Accordion**, **CMP-086 SettingsNav/SettingsLayout**, **CMP-096 WhatsNewPanel**, **CMP-207 BuildFooter**, **CMP-036 KeyValueRow**, **CMP-021 Link**, **CMP-001 Button**, backed by `GET /system/build`.
- **In-app help content surfaces** (E48-S02): keyboard cheatsheet driven by the live hotkey map (`GET /me/keymap`, `GET /settings/hotkeys`), order-flow glossary, and the link into the detector methodology drawer **SCR-058** (`GET /detectors/methodology`), plus guided-tour restart into SCR-016/SCR-017 onboarding.
- **Design** (E48-D01 hi-fi + handoff in Sprint 23, E48-D02 design-QA and a11y review in Sprint 26).
- **QA** (E48-Q01 documentation-accuracy test plan and exploratory charter; E48-Q02 runbook-rehearsal verification, GA regression evidence and epic QA sign-off).
- **Security** (E48-X01 STRIDE for the documentation/diagnostics surface; E48-X02 security review, leakage abuse cases and secret-scanning rules over published docs and support bundles).

## Story-domain rollup & traceability (no domain section exists — read this instead)

E48's roadmap row carries `domains: —`: it is the only R5 epic with **no story-domain section of its own** in `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`, because its output is documentation and operational readiness rather than a product domain. That is deliberate, but it means a DoR reviewer cannot open a domain section to check coverage. This section is the substitute rollup and is the authoritative statement of what user-facing scope E48 owns.

**Complete set of user stories tracing to E48** (source: `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, screen row **SCR-119 Help & about** → `US-SET-009, US-OBS-007`; confirmed by `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-119 "Stories: US-SET-009, US-OBS-007"):

| Story | Domain §in 11-user-stories.md | MoSCoW | Screens | E48 ticket | Portion owned by E48 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **US-SET-009** Electron shell preferences | §27 SET (line ~4457) | Should | SCR-027, **SCR-119**, SCR-157, SCR-159 | **E48-S01** (+ **E48-S02**) | Only the SCR-119 portion: version/build/commit/shell-and-GPU-mode information and the update/What's-New entry point. The shell *preference controls* (launch-on-login, restore-last-workspace, window bounds, hardware-acceleration flags) and SCR-027/SCR-157/SCR-159 belong to the Electron/settings epics, not here. |
| **US-OBS-007** Support bundle | §28 OBS (line ~4569) | Should | **SCR-119**, SCR-146, SCR-156 | **E48-S01** | The user-facing bundle generation entry point on SCR-119 and its secret-scan/size-cap/audit behaviour as experienced there. SCR-146 (admin backups & restore) is E42/E45; SCR-156 (error boundary) is E47/E49. |

**Exhaustiveness check (the thing a reviewer would otherwise have to redo by hand).** Grepping `18-traceability-matrix.md` for `SCR-119` returns exactly one screen row, and it lists exactly these two stories; no third story anywhere in `11-user-stories.md` names SCR-119. Both are `Should`, not `Must`, so E48 introduces **no Must-story risk to the GA gate** — the GA gate risk in this epic is entirely in T03/T04/T06 (runbooks, DR drill, PRR evidence), which are process gates from `07-release-and-prr.md`, not stories. Every other E48 ticket (K01, T01–T07, Q01, Q02, X01, X02, D01, D02) traces to a **roadmap exit criterion or PRR checklist item**, not to a user story, and each names its source clause in its own Context section.

**Components in scope via SCR-119** (from the same matrix row): CMP-001 Button, CMP-021 Link, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-051 Accordion (SCR-119 is its *only* consumer — any change to it is an E48 change), CMP-086 SettingsNav/SettingsLayout, CMP-096 WhatsNewPanel (shared with SCR-157), CMP-207 BuildFooter.

## Out of scope

- Writing the resilience runbooks for reconciliation, chaos and dead-man's-switch — owned by **E45-T11**; E48 indexes, rehearses and quality-gates them but does not re-author them.
- Fixing defects found while rehearsing — those are filed as Bugs against **E49** (defect burn-down), not absorbed silently here.
- Accessibility remediation of screens other than SCR-119 — owned by **E47**.
- Performance numbers themselves — owned by **E46**; E48 quotes E46's published figures and fails its own docs build if the quoted figure has no source artefact.
- **Android and any mobile client — structurally excluded, not merely absent.** Per `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` ("Android: OUT OF SCOPE for the current plan", owner decision 2026-09-14): "no Android tickets, designs or architecture docs are to be produced now". For a documentation epic this is an *active* obligation rather than a passive one, because E48 is the epic that would otherwise quietly reintroduce it — in the persona user guide, in the onboarding guide, in the generated API reference, in the GA release notes. Concretely, and enforced as a check (`DOC-007`, E48-T02) rather than left to reviewer memory: no page under `docs/`, `docs/guide/`, `docs/runbooks/` or the generated reference may describe, screenshot, or give instructions for a mobile/Android client; no installation or "supported platforms" page may list Android; the client-agnosticism of the API/WS contract is documented as an architectural property (it is, and E48-T01 records it) **without** implying a mobile client is planned, staged or forthcoming. A GA release note or roadmap page that promises Android is a **release-blocking** defect, not a copy nit, because the evidence pack (E48-T06) is the artefact an account manager reads as a commitment.
- **A separate admin application — structurally excluded.** The owner/admin functions (users & roles, exchange accounts & keys, audit log, recorder/storage, system health, feature flags) are RBAC-gated screens **inside the same web app** (`00-planning-brief.md`, locked decisions). Every runbook, the onboarding guide and the ops index must therefore route the operator to `SCR-135`/`SCR-140`..`SCR-149` *within the app*, and must never describe, link to or assume a standalone admin console, a separate admin deployment, a second login or a distinct admin URL. This is checked by the same `DOC-007` rule (forbidden-phrase list: "admin app", "admin console", "admin portal", "mobile app", "Android app", "Play Store", "APK"), with an allow-list entry required — and a reason recorded — for any legitimate historical mention (e.g. an ADR explaining *why* there is no separate admin app).
- Additional exchanges beyond Bybit USDT linear perpetuals: the adapter abstraction is documented as an extension point; no guide, runbook or reference may imply another venue is supported in v1.
- A public/marketing website or external developer portal: the documentation site is private and Tailscale-reachable only.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every required document exists and is reachable from one index
  Given the R5 exit criterion 6 list (user guide, ops runbooks, API/WS reference, ADR index, onboarding guide)
  When the docs site is built in CI and the docs-completeness checker runs
  Then every listed artefact is present, non-empty and linked from the docs landing page
  And a deliberately removed runbook makes the checker exit non-zero naming the missing artefact

Scenario: Every runbook has been rehearsed and dated
  Given the runbook index at docs/runbooks/index.md
  When the rehearsal checker runs at the GA gate
  Then every runbook entry carries a rehearsal date, a rehearser and an outcome
  And any runbook whose rehearsal date is absent or older than the current release train fails the check

Scenario: The API reference cannot drift from the contract
  Given docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml is edited to add an operation
  When the docs build runs without regenerating the reference
  Then CI fails with a stale-reference error naming the operation
  And regenerating the reference makes the build pass

Scenario: The DR playbook is executed and measured, not merely written
  Given the disaster-recovery playbook and a scratch environment
  When the drill is executed end to end
  Then measured RTO and RPO per system are recorded and compared against 07-release-and-prr.md §5.3 targets
  And a measurement exceeding a target is recorded as a P1 finding in docs/plan/32-risk-register.md with a remediation ticket, and blocks PRR sign-off

Scenario: Documentation cannot reintroduce an excluded platform or a separate admin app
  Given the structural exclusions in docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md (no Android/mobile client, no separate admin app, Bybit USDT perps only)
  When any page under docs/, docs/guide/, docs/runbooks/ or the generated reference is built in CI
  Then the DOC-007 scope-boundary checker finds no forbidden phrase outside the reviewed allow-list
  And a page stating "download the Android app" or "open the admin console" fails the build naming file, line and phrase
  And an allow-list entry without a written reason also fails the build

Scenario: Documentation is reviewed by someone who did not write it
  Given a PR touching docs/ or docs/plan/
  When it is opened
  Then CODEOWNERS routing requires an approval from a reviewer who is not a commit author on that PR
  And a self-approved documentation PR cannot be enqueued in the merge queue

Scenario: Published documentation leaks no secrets (failure path)
  Given the generated docs site and every example payload it contains
  When the secret-scanning and redaction rules run over the built output
  Then no API key, token, session cookie, internal hostname or real account identifier is present
  And seeding a fixture key pattern into an example makes the scan fail the build
```

## Technical notes / design

**Documentation lives in the repo, is built by CI, and is verified mechanically.** Three layers, mirroring the governance approach established in E01:

1. **Authored prose** under `docs/` (`docs/guide/`, `docs/runbooks/`, `docs/onboarding/`) — Markdown, reviewed like code.
2. **Generated reference** — the REST reference rendered from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`; the WS topic/frame reference rendered from `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` and the bundled `ws-schemas.json`; the DB reference rendered from `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`. Regeneration is a `make docs` target; CI runs `make docs && git diff --exit-code`, exactly the staleness pattern already used for `packages/protocol` (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §5).
3. **Checkers** (`scripts/check-docs-*.py`) with stable error codes: `DOC-001` missing required artefact, `DOC-002` stale generated reference, `DOC-003` unrehearsed or stale-rehearsal runbook, `DOC-004` broken internal link, `DOC-005` quoted figure with no source artefact, `DOC-006` secret/PII pattern in published output, `DOC-007` orphan document (not linked from any index).

**In-app help is content-driven, not hard-coded.** SCR-119 renders sections from a versioned content bundle shipped with the web app so the app remains fully usable offline (SCR-119 performance note: "No network calls except an explicit update check; the page is fully available offline"). The only live calls are `GET /system/build` (version/commit/environment, RBAC `permissions: []`, scope `self`) and `GET /detectors/methodology` for the SCR-058 drawer. The keyboard cheatsheet is rendered from the **active** hotkey profile (`GET /me/keymap`) so it always matches the user's remapping rather than a stale screenshot.

**Runbook format** (enforced by front-matter schema, checked by `DOC-003`): `id`, `title`, `failure_ids` (F1–F18 from `20-architecture.md` §11.1), `trigger`, `detection` (the metric/alert from `20-architecture.md` §12), `severity`, `steps` (numbered, each with expected observable result), `verification`, `rollback`, `owner`, `rehearsals: [{date, rehearser, outcome, duration_minutes, notes}]`.

**GA evidence pack** is assembled by a script into `artifacts/ga/v1.1.0/` from CI artefacts (coverage reports, perf budget results from E46, a11y conformance report from E47, chaos catalogue results from E45, scan outputs from E43) rather than transcribed; the PRR ceremony reviews the pack, it does not build it.

## Test plan

- **Unit** — each `scripts/check-docs-*.py` checker: clean tree exits 0; one seeded violation per `DOC-00n` code exits non-zero with that code; malformed front-matter produces a clear message, not a traceback. Target ≥85% line coverage on `scripts/` (Python gate, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §15).
- **Contract** — the generated REST/WS reference is diffed against the contract in CI (`make docs && git diff --exit-code`); a synthetic contract change must break the build.
- **Integration** — docs site builds from a clean checkout in a container with no network; all internal links resolve; search index builds.
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron)** — SCR-119 renders version/commit/environment, the cheatsheet reflects a remapped hotkey, the methodology link opens SCR-058, the diagnostics-copy control copies a redacted payload, the What's-New panel shows the `v1.1.0` entry.
- **Manual/QA** — runbook rehearsals (E48-Q02) executed against staging (demo) by an engineer who did not write the runbook, timed and recorded.
- **Perf** — SCR-119 mount ≤150 ms and route transition ≤200 ms per `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 item 7.
- **a11y** — axe-core clean on SCR-119; manual NVDA/VoiceOver pass per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.2.
- **Security** — `DOC-006` secret scan over built output; support-bundle redaction assertions (US-OBS-007 scenario 2).

## Security notes

Data classification: the documentation set is **internal/confidential** — it describes the trust boundaries (`docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §2.2), the key-vault design (`27-adrs/ADR-0009`) and the incident runbooks, so it is an attacker's shortcut if exposed. Primary STRIDE concerns (detailed in E48-X01): **I**nformation disclosure via generated examples containing real identifiers, via the support bundle (US-OBS-007), or via publishing the docs site outside the Tailscale boundary; **T**ampering with a runbook to induce a destructive operation during an incident; **E**levation via a runbook instructing an over-privileged shortcut ("just run as superuser") that becomes normalised. Controls: docs site bound to the private network only (same rule as the metrics endpoint in US-OBS-001), `DOC-006` secret scanning in the docs build, CODEOWNERS protection on `docs/runbooks/**` so an incident procedure cannot be changed without review, and an explicit rule that no runbook step may disable an audit or a safety control without naming the compensating control. `security` review label required on this epic.

## Accessibility notes

SCR-119 is a static content page: headings in order, a version table as a real `<table>`, links with meaningful text, the licence list in a scrollable region with an accessible name, the copy-diagnostics button announcing exactly what it copies. The keyboard cheatsheet must itself be operable and readable by a screen reader — a cheatsheet that only exists as an image would be a Level A failure. Accordion sections follow the WAI-ARIA Accordion pattern (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-051). WCAG 2.2 AA, verified by axe-core plus a manual pass (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes

Docs site build ≤3 min in CI. SCR-119: panel mount ≤150 ms, route transition ≤200 ms, zero network calls on first paint beyond `GET /system/build` (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; `14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5). Support-bundle generation must be bounded and must not stall the event loop (US-OBS-007 NFR: capped size, truncation stated).

## Observability

- Analytics events already specified for SCR-119: `help.about_viewed`, `help.diagnostics_copied`, `help.update_check_requested`.
- New: `docs.checker_failed{code}` emitted by CI so documentation rot is visible as a trend rather than a surprise at the gate; `runbook.rehearsal_recorded{runbook_id,outcome}`; `ga.evidence_pack_built{version}`.
- Audit: support-bundle generation is audited (US-OBS-007 NFR) via the existing `audit_log` table; runbook edits are captured by normal git history plus CODEOWNERS.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R5 exit criteria 5 and 6 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3) evidenced: every runbook rehearsed and dated; the six documentation artefacts complete and linked.
- [ ] §9.4 Docs gate satisfied: every doc reviewed by a non-author.
- [ ] DR playbook executed with measured RTO/RPO recorded and compared to `07-release-and-prr.md` §5.3 targets; failures logged to `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` with remediation tickets.
- [ ] Docs checkers `DOC-001`..`DOC-007` are required CI checks.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core green on SCR-119 + manual screen-reader pass signed off.
- [ ] security: STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, Security engineer sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (E48-Q02) including the rehearsal log.
- [ ] Design sign-off on SCR-119 (E48-D01) and design-QA pass (E48-D02).
- [ ] GA evidence pack assembled; PRR + GA checklist executed; demoed to Owner; `v1.1.0` tagged.
- [ ] Retro note filed.
- [ ] `DOC-007` scope-boundary checker green: no documentation artefact describes an Android/mobile client, a separate admin application, or a non-Bybit venue as supported; allow-list reviewed and every entry justified.
- [ ] Story-domain rollup verified: SCR-119 traces to exactly US-SET-009 and US-OBS-007 (both Should), both covered by E48-S01/E48-S02, and no other story references SCR-119 (re-grep of `18-traceability-matrix.md` recorded on the ticket at DoR review).

## Dependencies

- **E46** — the roadmap graph edge `E46 --> E48`; performance figures quoted in the docs must be final.
- **E45** — restore/rollback drill automation (`E45-T09`, `E45-T10`) and the resilience runbooks (`E45-T11`) that this epic indexes and rehearses.
- **E44**, **E43** — live-enablement gate and security-hardening outcomes documented in the ops and GA material.
- **E42** — admin screens (SCR-140..SCR-148) the ops runbooks instruct operators to use.
- **E47** — the accessibility conformance report is one of the GA evidence-pack inputs, and SCR-119's a11y baseline comes from it.
- Interfaces relied on: `GET /system/build`, `GET /detectors/methodology`, `GET /me/keymap`, `GET /settings/hotkeys`, `GET /admin/health`, `GET /admin/backups`, `POST /admin/backups/{backupId}/restore`.

## Branch

`feat/docs-ga-readiness-*` (per child ticket, e.g. `feat/docs-ga-readiness-runbooks`). PR size guidance: ≤400 LOC of prose-equivalent diff per PR; split long documents by chapter so reviewers actually read them.

## References

title: Author the documentation-accuracy test plan, charter and E2E additions
body:
## Context

`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires a test plan authored or reviewed by QA **before development starts** for every Story, and `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.1 requires it to live inline with the ticket. E48 ships two UI stories (S01, S02) plus a set of documentation artefacts whose correctness is a GA exit criterion — and documentation has a failure mode automated tests do not catch: it can be complete, well-formatted, link-valid and *wrong*.

This ticket produces the black-box test plan for the E48 story group, the exploratory charter that probes the parts a checklist cannot, and the E2E additions that keep the help surfaces honest after GA.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Black-box test plan** `docs/qa/test-plans/e48-docs-ga.md` covering:
  - **E48-S01**: SCR-119 in all states; build information completeness and role-safety across owner/manager/viewer; support-bundle generation happy path, secret-detected abort, oversized-window truncation, partial-collection; browser-vs-Electron differences; offline behaviour; per-persona guide navigation and role-capability accuracy against `docs/plan/10-personas.md` §7.
  - **E48-S02**: cheatsheet against default, remapped, conflicting and overflow keymaps; role-filtered cheatsheet for a viewer; glossary completeness and `(estimated)` chips; methodology drawer entry; non-destructive tour restart verified by capturing workspace/settings/checklist state before and after.
  - **E48-T07**: changelog↔panel parity; "since last seen version" aggregation including the equal-version and downgrade cases; Breaking Changes prominence; security-entry redaction.
  - **Documentation accuracy** (the distinctive part): a sampled verification protocol in which a tester follows 20 randomly selected procedural passages from the guide and the runbook set *literally* against staging (demo) and records whether the stated outcome occurs. Documentation that cannot survive literal execution is defective regardless of how it reads.
- **Exploratory charters** (60–120 min each, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.2 format — mission, areas, oracles, debrief):
  - *"A new manager's first hour"* — reach the answer to five realistic questions ("how do I set a stop", "why is this value estimated", "why can't I trade this symbol", "what does PARTIAL mean", "where do I see my risk cap") using only the app and the guide; oracle: any question that takes >3 minutes or ends outside the product is a finding.
  - *"The incident tourist"* — from a firing alert, reach the correct runbook and the first actionable step; oracle: >60 s to the right runbook, or an ambiguous first step, is a finding.
  - *"Documentation vs reality"* — hunt for statements in the guide, runbooks and architecture docs that the built system contradicts; oracle: any contradiction is at least P2.
- **E2E suite additions** (Playwright, web + Electron) for the help surfaces, tagged so they run in the standard suite and in the pre-cut release checklist.
- **a11y audit protocol** for SCR-119 and its content surfaces per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.2, feeding E48-D02 and E47.
- **Regression pack** entries added to the standing pack so help/docs surfaces are covered in future trains.

## Out of scope

- Executing the runbook rehearsals and GA regression — **E48-Q02**.
- Perf and load testing of the docs site beyond the stated build/FCP budgets — E46 owns performance methodology.
- Security abuse cases — **E48-X02** (this plan links to them rather than duplicating).

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Every Gherkin scenario in the epic's stories has a test-plan step
  Given the acceptance criteria of E48-S01, E48-S02 and E48-T07
  When the test plan is reviewed for coverage
  Then each scenario maps to at least one explicit black-box verification step with data setup and expected result
  And an unmapped scenario blocks the plan's approval

Scenario: Documentation is verified by literal execution, not by reading
  Given 20 sampled procedural passages from the guide and runbooks
  When a tester follows each literally against staging (demo)
  Then each stated outcome occurs, or a finding is raised naming the passage and the divergence
  And findings are severity-rated per 03-testing-strategy.md §11.3

Scenario: The test plan exists before development starts
  Given E48-S01 is scheduled in Sprint 25
  Then this test plan is approved before E48-S01 leaves Ready
  And the DoR test-readiness item on E48-S01 references this plan

Scenario: E2E additions fail when the surfaces regress (failure path)
  Given the cheatsheet is changed to render the default keymap instead of the active profile
  When the E2E suite runs
  Then the remapped-binding spec fails
  And the failure message names the expected binding and the one rendered

Scenario: The a11y protocol produces evidence, not an assertion
  Given the a11y audit protocol is executed
  Then axe-core results and NVDA/VoiceOver transcripts are attached per surface
  And any WCAG 2.2 AA violation is logged at P2 minimum
```

## Technical notes / design

The sampled-execution protocol is deliberately random and re-drawn each run so authors cannot optimise for a known subset; the sample is drawn with a seed recorded in the plan so a run is reproducible. Sample size 20 is a pragmatic floor — it is enough to detect a systematically wrong document, not enough to prove every passage, and the plan says so explicitly rather than implying stronger assurance than it gives.

Test data: a manager account with a restricted symbol set and a risk cap, a viewer account, and an owner account, all on staging (demo); keymap fixtures (default/remapped/conflicting); a configuration fixture with a seeded secret for the bundle-abort case; `CHANGELOG.md` fixtures for the version-aggregation cases.

E2E specs live in `apps/web/e2e/help/` and `apps/desktop/e2e/help/`; order-entry is not involved, so the `@demo-rest-only` constraint does not apply to this suite, but the suite must still avoid live Bybit calls (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11.4 network-allowlist lint).

## Test plan

(This ticket's deliverable *is* a test plan; its own verification is review-based.)
- Plan reviewed by the QA lead and by the E48-S01/S02 implementers for feasibility and data availability.
- Coverage matrix from story scenarios → plan steps generated and checked for completeness.
- The E2E additions are themselves verified by mutation: each new spec is confirmed to fail against a deliberately broken build before being accepted.

## Security notes

The plan exercises the support bundle, which produces restricted artefacts: test bundles are generated on staging (demo) with synthetic data only, are inspected within the test environment, and are deleted at charter end with deletion recorded. Testers must not attach a generated bundle to a ticket. Abuse cases proper are E48-X02; this plan notes the handling rules so QA does not create the exposure the feature is designed to avoid.

## Accessibility notes

The a11y audit protocol is part of this deliverable: per-surface axe-core runs, keyboard-only traversal, NVDA + VoiceOver scripts including the announcement-order checks for Breaking Changes and `(estimated)` status, contrast verification via tokens, reduced-motion verification. Results feed E48-D02 and E47's conformance report. Standard: WCAG 2.2 AA.

## Performance notes

The plan records the ≤150 ms mount and ≤200 ms transition budgets for SCR-119 as verification steps with the measurement method, so QA measures rather than judges.

## Observability

Plan execution results recorded in the QA sign-off note; findings carry stable ids reconciling with E48-D02's design-QA log and with E49 bug tickets.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Test plan merged at `docs/qa/test-plans/e48-docs-ga.md`, approved by the QA lead, referenced from E48-S01/S02/T07.
- [ ] Coverage matrix shows every story scenario mapped.
- [ ] Three exploratory charters written with mission, areas, oracles and debrief template.
- [ ] E2E additions merged, green, and mutation-verified.
- [ ] a11y audit protocol documented and scheduled.
- [ ] Regression-pack entries added.
- [ ] Test data and fixtures available in staging (demo) before E48-S01 leaves Ready.

## Dependencies

- **E48-T02** — the docs site and checkers define what "documentation is complete" means mechanically, which this plan complements with accuracy.
- **E48-D01** — the state list the plan enumerates comes from the design spec.

## Branch

`chore/docs-ga-readiness-qa-plan` for the plan; `test/docs-ga-readiness-e2e` for the specs.

## References

- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §7 E2E, §11.1 test plans, §11.2 charters, §11.3 severity, §12 a11y protocol
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1, §3.2
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.2
- `docs/plan/10-personas.md` §7
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-119, SCR-113, SCR-058

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md (PRR/runbook procedures)
2. docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md (R5 exit criteria)
3. docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md (DoR/DoD)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan` (owner: @CandleViewer/architecture)
- `docs/runbooks/ or docs/plan/ per ticket Scope`

**Interfaces you must not break**
- Public exports of the package(s) this ticket touches (no widening of package APIs without an ADR)

**Commands**
- `pnpm lint  # docs-site link/markdown checks`
- `make gen && git diff --exit-code  # if generated reference docs touched`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `chore/docs-ga-readiness-qa-plan`
- PR title: "E48-Q01: Author the documentation-accuracy test plan, charter and E2E additions"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E48-Q01>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/docs/plan/` (@CandleViewer/architecture); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: qa, type/test, area/docs, priority/p2, a11y

**Done means**
- Test plan merged at `docs/qa/test-plans/e48-docs-ga.md`, approved by the QA lead, referenced from E48-S01/S02/T07.
- Coverage matrix shows every story scenario mapped.
- Three exploratory charters written with mission, areas, oracles and debrief template.
- E2E additions merged, green, and mutation-verified.
- a11y audit protocol documented and scheduled.
- Regression-pack entries added.

**Do NOT**
- Executing the runbook rehearsals and GA regression — **E48-Q02**.
- Perf and load testing of the docs site beyond the stated build/FCP budgets — E46 owns performance methodology.
- Security abuse cases — **E48-X02** (this plan links to them rather than duplicating).
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E48-Q01` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Ship the persona user guide and the Help & about screen with diagnostics
body:
## Context

R5 exit criterion 6 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §9.3) requires a user guide, and §9.2 scopes it as an "Owner/manager user guide per persona". `docs/plan/10-personas.md` defines P1 Owner/discretionary order-flow trader, P2 Account Manager, P3 Viewer/analyst, P4 Admin (owner hat) and the M1 Rule-author mode, with an authoritative permission matrix in §7 — so "per persona" has a concrete meaning: each guide covers only what that role can actually do, and the permission matrix is the contract that keeps it honest.

The guide needs a front door inside the app. **SCR-119 Help & about** is that door, traced in `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` to **US-SET-009** (Electron shell preferences — version/build/shell information) and **US-OBS-007** (Support bundle). US-OBS-007 is a *Should* story that has not been implemented anywhere else in the plan, and its natural home is exactly here: "generate a diagnostic bundle … logs, metrics snapshots, configuration with secrets removed, health results and recent errors", with the hard requirement that "the bundle is scanned for secret patterns before being written, and generation fails loudly if any are found".

## Scope / Deliverables

**User stories covered: US-OBS-007 (Should), US-SET-009 (Should, the version/build/shell-information portion surfaced on SCR-119).**

- **Guide content** under `docs/guide/`, published to the docs site (E48-T02) and bundled into the app for offline reading:
  - `p1-trader.md` — reading the chart and order-flow surfaces, the `(estimated)` rule, placing an order via the ticket and via chart/DOM, brackets and the native-SL guarantee, scaled and emulated orders, positions management, replay, journal.
  - `p2-manager.md` — the same trading loop within the constraints a manager actually has (allowed symbols, risk caps, per-account profile, what a lockout means and who lifts it), plus what a trade group does to their account when the Owner fans out.
  - `p3-viewer.md` — read-only analysis: charts, order-flow, journal review, why controls are disabled with a reason rather than hidden.
  - `p4-admin.md` — users and roles, accounts and API keys (including the withdrawal-OFF and IP-allowlist invariants and the 48-hour new-key restriction), per-account profiles, recorder and retention, feature flags, audit log, health, backups.
  - `m1-rule-author.md` — the rule engine in both editors, arming semantics, versions and activation, simulation before arming, cooldowns and the auto-disarm behaviour.
  - Each guide opens with "what this role can and cannot do", generated from the `docs/plan/10-personas.md` §7 permission matrix so it cannot contradict the implementation.
- **SCR-119 built** per the E48-D01 hi-fi: version table (app, engine, backend, build hash, Bybit API version, environment) from `GET /system/build`; changelog/What's-New entry point (populated by E48-T07); links to the guide sections, the accessibility statement (E47) and the detector methodology; third-party licence list; update-check control with its four result states (US-SET-009 shell path, hidden with an explanation in the plain-browser build).
- **US-OBS-007 support bundle**: a time-window picker, generation with logs, metrics snapshots, redacted configuration, health results and recent errors; pre-write secret scan that **fails loudly** if any pattern matches; size cap with an explicit truncation statement that preserves the most recent data; local-only storage with no automatic upload; generation audited.
- Components: **CMP-086**, **CMP-051**, **CMP-036**, **CMP-021**, **CMP-001**, **CMP-096**, **CMP-207**, plus the new long-form prose pattern from E48-D01.

## Out of scope

- The keyboard cheatsheet, glossary, methodology drawer link and guided-tour restart — **E48-S02** (split to keep this story ≤8 points).
- The release-notes content pipeline — **E48-T07**.
- The Electron updater mechanism itself — E10; this story consumes its state.
- Shell preference *controls* (launch-on-login, window bounds, GPU flags) — those live on SCR-118/SCR-116 per the settings catalogue; only the version/build/shell-information surface of US-SET-009 is in scope here.
- Screen-reader scripts for chart surfaces — E47.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: Build information is complete and role-safe
  Given any authenticated user on SCR-119
  When the page loads
  Then app version, engine version, backend version, build hash, Bybit API version and environment are shown from GET /system/build
  And no infrastructure detail beyond version and commit is exposed, for any role

Scenario: A support bundle is generated for a time window
  Given the owner selects a 2-hour window
  When a support bundle is generated
  Then it contains logs, metrics snapshots, configuration with secrets removed, health results and recent errors
  And it is written only to the local machine and the generation is recorded in the audit log

Scenario: Bundle generation fails loudly on a detected secret (failure path)
  Given a configuration value matching a secret pattern survives redaction
  When the pre-write scan runs
  Then generation fails with an explicit error naming the category of the detected pattern, not its value
  And no partial bundle file is left on disk

Scenario: An oversized window is capped and says so
  Given a 30-day window that exceeds the size cap
  When the bundle is generated
  Then the bundle is capped, the truncation is stated in the bundle and in the UI, and the most recent data is preserved
  And the stated truncation names the window actually captured

Scenario: Shell-only items are hidden with an explanation in the browser build
  Given the app runs in a plain browser rather than the Electron shell
  When SCR-119 renders
  Then shell-only items are absent with an explanation rather than shown disabled

Scenario: The guide matches what the role can actually do
  Given the permission matrix in docs/plan/10-personas.md §7
  When the guide's role-capability section is generated and checked
  Then it matches the matrix exactly
  And a divergence between the matrix and the implemented RBAC scopes fails the check and is raised as a bug, not papered over in prose

Scenario: The page is fully usable offline
  Given no network connectivity
  When SCR-119 is opened
  Then all guide content, the licence list and the version table render from bundled data and the last known build info
  And the update check reports "check failed" rather than blocking the page
```

## Technical notes / design

**Guide content is bundled, not fetched** (SCR-119 performance note). Markdown is compiled at build time into the app bundle, lazily loaded per section so the page mount stays within budget. The docs site (E48-T02) renders the same source files, so there is exactly one copy.

**Role-capability generation**: `scripts/gen-role-capabilities.py` reads the §7 permission matrix and the `x-rbac` blocks in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, emits the per-persona capability table, and fails (`DOC-005` class) when the two disagree — which makes a documentation check into an RBAC regression test, cheaply.

**Support-bundle pipeline** (backend, `services/api/candleviewer/observability/`): collect → redact (serialiser allow-list, the same mechanism US-OBS-003 mandates for logs) → scan (secret patterns, fail-closed) → size-cap (newest-first, truncation manifest) → write locally → audit. Fail-closed is the design: any scanner error aborts generation. Errors: `BUNDLE-001` secret detected, `BUNDLE-002` window invalid, `BUNDLE-003` size cap exceeded before the minimum useful window, `BUNDLE-004` collection partial (named subsystem unavailable — the bundle still generates and says which part is missing, because a partial bundle during an incident beats none).

**Audit**: bundle generation writes an `audit_log` entry `{actor, role, action: "support_bundle.generated", target: window, ts}` per `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 item 8.

## Test plan

- **Unit** (frontend ≥80%): version-table rendering from `GET /system/build`; update-check state machine across idle/checking/up-to-date/available/failed; browser-vs-shell conditional rendering; offline rendering; licence-list virtualisation.
- **Unit** (backend ≥85%): redaction allow-list; secret-scan positives and negatives including near-miss patterns; size-cap newest-first truncation; partial-collection handling; audit emission.
- **Contract** — `GET /system/build` response consumed per the OpenAPI schema; support-bundle endpoint (if exposed) covered by schemathesis.
- **Integration** — bundle generated against a running stack with a seeded secret in configuration; generation must fail and leave no file.
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron)** — SCR-119 loads offline; bundle generated for a window and downloaded; shell-only items hidden in the browser build; guide navigation reaches every persona section.
- **a11y** — axe-core on SCR-119; manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §8.2.
- **Perf** — panel mount ≤150 ms, route transition ≤200 ms, no network call on first paint beyond `GET /system/build`.
- Fixtures: seeded-secret configuration fixture; recorded log/metric snapshots under `packages/fixtures`.

## Security notes

This story ships the single most dangerous convenience feature in the product: a button that packages the system's state into a file a user can send anywhere. Threats (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md`): **I**nformation disclosure of API keys, session tokens, correlation-identifiable account data or internal hostnames via the bundle; **I** via the licence/version surface fingerprinting the deployment; **T**ampering with the redaction allow-list; **R**epudiation of who generated a bundle. Controls: allow-list redaction (deny-by-default, not pattern-blacklist), a mandatory pre-write scan that fails closed, local-only storage with no automatic upload (US-OBS-007 NFR), audited generation, and a CI test asserting that a seeded secret aborts generation. Data classification: the bundle is **restricted** even after redaction; the UI says so. Requires `security` review (E48-X02) and a manual abuse-case check (attempt to obtain another user's data in a bundle as a manager).

## Accessibility notes

Per E48-D01 and `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-119: static content with a correct heading hierarchy, the version table as a real `<table>` with headers, the copy-diagnostics button stating exactly what it copies in its accessible name, the licence text in a named scrollable region, accordion sections following the WAI-ARIA pattern, full keyboard operation, visible focus, ≥4.5:1 contrast, reduced-motion respected. The long-form guide must be navigable by heading with a screen reader — this is the screen a user with a disability is most likely to reach first. axe-core green + manual pass required.

## Performance notes

Panel mount ≤150 ms; route transition ≤200 ms (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 item 7). Guide sections lazily loaded; total added bundle ≤250 KB gzipped. Support-bundle generation runs off the request path and must not block the event loop; progress is reported and the operation is cancellable.

## Observability

`help.about_viewed`, `help.diagnostics_copied`, `help.update_check_requested` (analytics, already specified for SCR-119); new: `support_bundle.generated{outcome,window_seconds,size_bytes}` metric and the `support_bundle.generated` audit event; `support_bundle.secret_detected` raises an alert, because a detected secret means redaction has a gap.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios pass via automated tests, each referencing its scenario.
- [ ] Coverage: frontend ≥80%, backend ≥85%, no package regression.
- [ ] Guide content for P1, P2, P3, P4 and M1 merged, reviewed by a non-author, published to the docs site and bundled offline.

- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the E48-D01 spec (formally in E48-D02); discrepancies fixed or filed.
- [ ] QA sign-off per the E48-Q01 test plan.
- [ ] `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-119 updated if the design changed during implementation.
- [ ] Feature flag recorded: `help_center` (default on in all environments; the support bundle behind `support_bundle` default on for owner, off for viewer).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review; PRs merged via merge queue.

title: Add the keyboard cheatsheet, glossary, methodology link and tour restart
body:
## Context

**SCR-119 Help & about** is specified to carry, beyond version information, "a keyboard cheatsheet, glossary of order-flow terms, detector methodology (SCR-058), the guided tour restart" (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §SCR-119). E48-S01 built the page and the guide; this story adds the four content surfaces that make it useful in the middle of a trading session rather than only on the first day.

Two of them have hard correctness requirements that make them more than content:

- The **cheatsheet must reflect the user's active hotkey profile**, not a static list. The app ships a default map (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2) and a hotkey editor (**SCR-113**, `POST /settings/hotkeys`, `GET /me/keymap`); a cheatsheet that shows defaults to a user who has remapped is worse than no cheatsheet, and §3.3 defines conflict-resolution rules that the sheet must surface.
- The **`(estimated)` methodology** link is a product-integrity obligation, not a nicety: `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 item 2 mandates that any heuristic value renders an `(estimated)` chip linking the methodology drawer **SCR-058**, which states plainly that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed and these are proxies, not ground truth. The glossary and help surface must reinforce that boundary, and `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` lists **R9 Advice boundary** as a standing risk.

## Scope / Deliverables

**User stories covered: US-SET-009 (Should) and US-OBS-007 (Should) — continuation of the SCR-119 portion opened by E48-S01.** These are the only two stories tracing to SCR-119 (`docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, screen row SCR-119); this story completes their SCR-119 acceptance criteria and leaves no residual SCR-119 scope. There is no story-domain section for E48 in `11-user-stories.md` — see the rollup table in the **E48** epic body.


- **Keyboard cheatsheet** on SCR-119, rendered from the active hotkey profile (`GET /me/keymap`, `GET /settings/hotkeys`), grouped by context (global, chart, DOM, order ticket, rules, replay) per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2; shows remapped bindings in place of defaults; flags conflicts per §3.3; printable/copyable; deep-links to **SCR-113** to change a binding.
- **Order-flow glossary** — the terms a user meets on the trading surfaces: footprint, delta, cumulative delta (CVD), imbalance, POC, value area, LVN/single print, TPO, DOM, liquidity heatmap, speed of tape, big trade, iceberg *(estimated)*, stop run *(estimated)*, market regime *(estimated)*, open interest, funding, basis, liquidation, trade group, fan-out, native SL, arming, paper/demo/live. Each entry: plain-language definition, "why it matters here", where it appears (screen id), and — for heuristic terms — the mandatory `(estimated)` chip (**CMP-227 EstimatedBadge**) linking **SCR-058**.
- **Inline term references**: glossary terms referenced from the guide and from the in-app tooltips resolve to the same entries, so there is one definition of "delta" in the product.
- **Detector methodology entry point** from SCR-119 into **SCR-058** (`GET /detectors/methodology`), alongside the existing entry from every `(estimated)` chip.
- **Guided tour restart** — re-entry into the onboarding experience (**SCR-016** owner first-run wizard / **SCR-017** invited-user onboarding, re-openable from Help per `docs/plan/12-sitemap.md` R-008), correctly role-aware, and non-destructive (restarting the tour must not reset settings, workspaces or the onboarding checklist's completed real-world steps such as key creation).
- **Accessibility statement link** into the conformance report published by E47.

## Out of scope

- The hotkey editor itself (SCR-113) — existing from E10/E42 settings work; this story links to it.
- SCR-058's content and the detector heuristics — owned by E25.
- The onboarding wizard's own screens — owned by E09/E42; this story only adds a safe restart entry point.
- Localisation of glossary terms.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Scenario: The cheatsheet shows the user's own bindings
  Given the user has remapped the order-ticket submit hotkey in SCR-113
  When the cheatsheet is opened on SCR-119
  Then the remapped binding is shown for that action and the default is not
  And changing the active hotkey profile updates the cheatsheet without a reload

Scenario: A hotkey conflict is visible where the user will look for it
  Given two actions bound to the same key combination per 05-accessibility-standard.md §3.3
  When the cheatsheet renders
  Then both entries are flagged as conflicting with the resolution rule stated
  And a link to SCR-113 offers to resolve it

Scenario: Heuristic terms carry the estimated boundary
  Given the glossary entries for iceberg, stop run and market regime
  When they render
  Then each shows the (estimated) chip and links to SCR-058
  And the entry text states that Bybit provides no L3/MBO feed and the value is a proxy, not ground truth

Scenario: Restarting the tour destroys nothing (failure path)
  Given a user with configured workspaces, settings and a completed API-key setup step
  When the guided tour is restarted from Help
  Then the tour replays and no workspace, setting or completed real-world onboarding step is reset
  And the user can exit the tour at any point back to the screen they came from

Scenario: Cheatsheet and glossary are keyboard and screen-reader operable
  Given a keyboard-only user with a screen reader
  When the cheatsheet and glossary are navigated
  Then every entry is reachable and announced with its term, definition and estimated status where applicable
  And no information is conveyed by colour alone

Scenario: Both surfaces work offline
  Given no network connectivity
  When the cheatsheet and glossary are opened
  Then the glossary renders from bundled content and the cheatsheet renders from the locally cached active keymap
  And the methodology link states that the drawer requires connectivity rather than failing silently
```

## Technical notes / design

The cheatsheet is a projection of the keymap, not a document: it reads the same store the hotkey system uses at runtime (`GET /me/keymap`, cached locally for offline), so it cannot disagree with the behaviour. A build-time check asserts that every action in the default map (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2) has a cheatsheet label — a newly added hotkey with no label fails CI, which is what keeps the sheet complete over time (`DOC-001` class).

The glossary is a single source consumed three ways: the SCR-119 list, the guide's inline term references, and tooltips on the trading surfaces. It lives as structured data (`term`, `plain`, `why_here`, `screens: [SCR-nnn]`, `estimated: bool`, `methodology_anchor`) so the `(estimated)` obligation can be enforced by a check rather than remembered: any term flagged `estimated` without a `methodology_anchor` fails the build, and any term appearing in the detectors' output vocabulary but absent from the glossary is reported.

Tour restart is implemented as a replay of the onboarding *presentation* layer only; the underlying checklist state (`GET /onboarding/checklist`) is read, never reset, and the restart is audited so an unexpected tour appearance is explicable.

## Test plan

- **Unit** (frontend ≥80%): cheatsheet projection from a keymap fixture including remapped, conflicting, unbound and overflow cases; glossary rendering including estimated entries; term-reference resolution including an unknown term; tour-restart guard asserting no state mutation.
- **Contract** — `GET /me/keymap`, `GET /settings/hotkeys`, `GET /detectors/methodology`, `GET /onboarding/checklist` consumed per their OpenAPI schemas.
- **Integration** — glossary completeness check against the detector output vocabulary; cheatsheet label completeness against the default hotkey map.
- **E2E (Playwright, web + Electron)** — remap a hotkey and see the cheatsheet update; open the methodology drawer from a glossary entry; restart the tour and assert workspaces/settings/checklist are unchanged; offline rendering.
- **a11y** — axe-core on both surfaces; manual screen-reader pass confirming `(estimated)` status is announced, not merely coloured.
- **Perf** — cheatsheet and glossary open ≤150 ms; no layout thrash on a 200-entry glossary.
- Fixtures: keymap fixtures (default, remapped, conflicting) under `packages/fixtures`.

## Security notes

Low direct threat surface, with two real cases. **I**nformation disclosure: the cheatsheet must not list actions the user's role cannot perform (that would enumerate the privileged surface for a viewer) — entries are filtered by the user's scopes, same as the controls themselves. **T**ampering/misleading content: the `(estimated)` boundary is a risk control (R9 Advice boundary in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`), so removing or weakening an estimated chip is treated as a security-adjacent defect and the completeness check is a required CI gate. Tour restart is audited to prevent it being used as a social-engineering vector ("the app asked me to re-enter my key"). Classification: internal. Reviewed under E48-X02.

## Accessibility notes

The cheatsheet is an accessibility feature in its own right (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 keyboard-first operation) and must be exemplary: bindings expressed as text, not images; `<kbd>` semantics; grouped under real headings; conflicts announced, not just coloured (§4 colour-independence). Glossary entries expose the `(estimated)` status as text to assistive technology (CMP-227 EstimatedBadge). Full keyboard operation, visible focus, ≥4.5:1 contrast, reduced motion respected on the drawer transitions. axe-core green plus a manual pass required.

## Performance notes

Open-to-render ≤150 ms for both surfaces; glossary content lazily loaded and ≤80 KB gzipped; cheatsheet derives from an in-memory store with no network call (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; `14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 item 7).

## Observability

`help.cheatsheet_opened`, `help.glossary_term_opened{term}` (bounded cardinality — term ids only, from a fixed vocabulary), `help.tour_restarted`, plus the existing `regime.explain_opened`-style routing when SCR-058 is opened from a glossary entry. Tour restart emits an audit event.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios pass with automated tests referencing them.
- [ ] Cheatsheet reflects the active profile, flags conflicts, and links to SCR-113.
- [ ] Glossary complete against the detector vocabulary; every heuristic term carries the `(estimated)` chip and methodology link; completeness checks required in CI.
- [ ] Tour restart proven non-destructive and audited.
- [ ] Accessibility statement linked.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend; a11y axe-core green + manual pass; perf budgets measured.
- [ ] Security review comment (E48-X02); role-filtered cheatsheet verified for a viewer account.
- [ ] design-qa pass (E48-D02).
- [ ] QA sign-off per E48-Q01.
- [ ] Feature flag recorded: `help_center` (shared with E48-S01, default on).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review; PRs merged via merge queue.

## Dependencies

- **E48-S01** — SCR-119 and the bundled-content pipeline.
- Interfaces: `GET /me/keymap`, `GET /settings/hotkeys`, `GET /detectors/methodology`, `GET /onboarding/checklist`; screens SCR-058, SCR-113, SCR-016, SCR-017; component CMP-227.

## Branch

`feat/docs-ga-readiness-help-content`. PRs: (1) cheatsheet + completeness check; (2) glossary data + surfaces; (3) methodology link + tour restart + E2E.

## References

- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-119, SCR-058, SCR-113, SCR-016, SCR-017, §0.5 items 2 and 7
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §3.2 default hotkey map, §3.3 conflict rules, §4
