- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-26 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #48). `RealClock` delivers a fired `after` through a **priority lane** the async run loop checks ahead of the inbox, so a due timer can no longer be starved behind a burst of external events. `AfterEvent` gains `scheduled_for`, `fired_at` and `lateness_ms`. Constraint CV-C10 requires the shared `cv.testing.advance()` helper.

> **Round-6 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `cec108b`).** #147 raises a **non-downgradable** `RootTargetError` at build time under *both* `strict_targets` settings (8/8 combinations), while genuine unresolvable targets still only warn. #133/#134 add `on_event_dropped(reason="unresolved_target")` and `on_resolve_error` on both engines. This retires the CV-C29 lint and E50-T13's root-target rule. Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §1/§5.

**Severity: High. Register ids: LC-06, LC-07, LC-08.**

This is one of the nineteen High items that must have either an upstream fix or a documented, tested, mechanically enforced mitigation before adoption.

This Chore tracks the upstream fix. It is not a CandleViewer implementation ticket - the CandleViewer-side mitigation is already scoped elsewhere and is listed under "Current mitigation" below. The Chore exists because ADR-0016 gates adoption on these being fixed **upstream** and re-verified, and because a tracking item that lives only in a research document is a tracking item nobody looks at.

**Why this matters to us.** Would remove our build-time target validator entirely, and would close three High items with one change.

**Measured evidence.** A leading-dot relative target (`.A2`) resolves to `None` and is treated as "no transition" - a silent no-op indistinguishable from a typo (probes A5/A18). An unknown target name passes machine construction and does nothing at runtime (probe C15). The repro must be **minimal and runnable without CandleViewer** - a single file against a clean install of the library - or it cannot be part of the gate and cannot be acted on upstream. Where the original evidence came from a probe under `docs/research/xstate/probes/` or `docs/research/xstate/adversarial/`, the repro is the reduced form of that probe, and the reduction is part of this Chore.

The register groups some upstream filings (several LC ids to one issue) where the underlying cause is shared. This Chore covers LC-34, LC-41, LC-42, LC-43, LC-48, LC-49 as one filing; the gate still evaluates each id's repro separately, because a partial fix that closes one id and not another is a realistic outcome and the report should say so.

## Test plan
The repro **is** the test, and it is a negative test today: it must **fail** against the current release, proving it actually exercises the defect. A repro that passes against the current release is broken and must be fixed before this Chore proceeds - a gate item that has always passed tests nothing. `E50-T04` executes it on every release and records the result.

## Security notes
The upstream issue carries reproduction code and measured behaviour only. It must contain no CandleViewer account identifiers, no strategy detail, no credentials and no data from a live or demo account (C-2.7). Standard disclosure hygiene applies.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
No CandleViewer runtime impact; this Chore ships no product code. If this item is ever fixed upstream, the corresponding mitigation's cost can be removed, and that removal is scoped at `E50-X01` rather than assumed here.

## Observability
Visible through `cv_ci_xstate_gate_items_open{severity}` and the per-version gate reports. The count of open Blockers is the headline number at the Sprint 08 go/no-go.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Upstream issue filed with evidence, minimal repro and proposed fix; number recorded in `12-challenge-register.md` against LC-34, LC-41, LC-42, LC-43, LC-48, LC-49.
- [ ] Minimal repro committed under `docs/research/xstate/issues/repro/` and **verified to fail** against the current release.

- [ ] Architect review (ADR-0016 is architect-owned).

## Verified on 0.8.0 — 2026-09-17

**Gate run:** `xstate-statemachine` 0.8.0, commit `9bf6065`, CPython 3.13.7,
Windows 11 x64, `gate/run_gate.py` against the primary check set
(`docs/research/xstate/issues/verify-0.8.0/`). Evidence:
`docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md`.

- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-48 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #33). Five error hooks on `PluginBase` — `on_transition_failed`, `on_guard_error`, `on_unhandled_event`, `on_error`, `on_done` — all implemented by `LoggingInspector`, all firing **under the 0.7.x defaults**. Existing plugins load unchanged. This is the right shape: observability unconditional, recovery opt-in.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-41 — FIXED-DEFAULT (`queue_depth`) / FIXED-OPT-IN (bounding)** (upstream #38). Bounded inbox with `RAISE` / `BLOCK` / `DROP_NEWEST`, plus `on_event_dropped`. Attacked hard: **13/13, no findings** — `RAISE` fires at exactly the bound, `BLOCK` applies real backpressure with zero loss, and a `BLOCK` send issued *from inside an action* correctly reroutes to the internal queue instead of self-deadlocking.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-42 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #39). `send(wait=True)` resolves to a `Receipt(state_ids, changed, error)` only after the whole macrostep, reports the **settled** state after `always` transitions, carries the action error, and resolves with `InterpreterStoppedError` rather than hanging on a stopped interpreter. `send(priority=True)` jumps a 20-deep backlog and is exempt from the bound.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-49 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #58). `interpreter.value` gives the active configuration in XState's hierarchical form, tree-walked so state keys containing `.` are safe. Lets us delete our bespoke id-string projector for the WebSocket UI feed.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-34 — FIXED-OPT-IN** (upstream #51). `strict` raises `UnknownEventError` synchronously at the call site with a difflib suggestion; `event_schemas` validates payloads independently of `strict`.
- **LC-43 — PARTIAL, with a regression** (upstream #37). The core fix is real: bare cross-thread `send()` now raises `WrongThreadError` instead of losing the event. **But `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(interp.send(...), loop)` — the pattern the original issue named as the only correct 0.7.0 form — now raises too**, undocumented and with no deprecation window, because the thread check runs eagerly before the coroutine is scheduled (new defect N-6). Constraint CV-C14 bans it and routes everything through a validating gateway wrapper.
- **NEW HIGH DEFECT (N-1), drafted for filing.** `send(event, wait=True)` keys its receipt map on `id(event_obj)`, so two concurrent sends with the **same `Event` instance** collide and the first future is never resolved — an unkillable coroutine, no error, no timeout. Controls rule out `id()` recycling (200-way concurrent with fresh objects all resolve). Constraint CV-C06 + CV-LINT-XS9 require a freshly-constructed event at every `wait=True` call site. Draft + repro: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-01-send-wait-receipt-id-collision.md`.
- **NEW MEDIUM DEFECT (N-4), drafted for filing.** `send_threadsafe()` — now the *only* cross-thread API — bypasses `strict` and `event_schemas` entirely. Verified: an invalid-payload `FILL` skips the validator **and transitions the machine**. Draft + repro: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-04-send-threadsafe-bypasses-strict.md`.
- **NEW MEDIUM DEFECT (N-8), drafted for filing.** Events named `error.*` or `done.*` are invisible to a `"*"` handler and exempt from `onUnhandled: "error"`. Constraint CV-C15 bans such names; `E50-T05`'s event-name gate enforces it. Draft + repro: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-08-error-done-namespace-invisible.md`.
- **Residual on LC-48:** `on_transition_failed` fires **twice** per transition under `"continue"` (once per action slot), and the async engine emits no `on_transition` for the initial entry while the sync engine does. Constraint CV-C09 requires our plugins to dedupe and to filter the synthetic init event.

**Acceptance criteria status:** **PARTIALLY MET — stays open.** Four of the six register ids are FIXED-DEFAULT, one is FIXED-OPT-IN, and **LC-43 is PARTIAL with a regression**. Two new defects (N-1 High, N-4 Medium) landed inside the features this Chore asked for. Keep open against LC-43, N-1 and N-4.

## Verification on `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: substantially improved - STAYS OPEN against newly-surfaced gaps in the same feature area.** Three items this Chore was held open against are now **FIXED**:

- **N-1** (`#39` / `#75`): receipts are no longer keyed on `id()` - the queued envelope gets its own identity via `Interpreter._detach()` at the send boundary. Held at 500-way concurrency under three policies simultaneously, and with `stop()` racing outstanding duplicates. **CV-C06's fresh-`Event` clause RETIRES**, and with it **CV-LINT-XS9**'s reuse rule and `test_send_receipt_fresh_event_only`.
- **N-4** (`#51` / `#78`): `send_threadsafe()` now runs `_check_strict` (name + schema) on the calling thread before anything is queued, under loop saturation and 10-thread contention. **CV-C14's gateway-validation clause RETIRES**; CV-C14 becomes a ban-only rule.
- **LC-43** (`#37`): the `WrongThreadError` message now names the `run_coroutine_threadsafe(interp.send(...))` idiom, states it is rejected since 0.8.0, and points to `send_threadsafe()`. The ban in CV-C14 is reinforced.

Stays open against: **M-2** (async `max_iterations` does not bound an action-side `send()` - drives new constraint **CV-C16** / CV-LINT-XS11), **M-6** (`send_threadsafe` error precedence before `start()`, riding along on `#78`), and the fact that a cut `raise` chain is entirely silent with `status` still `"running"` and `last_transition_ok` still `True` (drives **CV-C17**).

Note also that `#43` / LC-28 remains **NOT-FIXED** for its task-count criterion - still a flat 2.0 asyncio tasks per idle child at n=2/10/50. That is a capacity-planning input, not a correctness one: continue to budget 2 tasks per invoked/spawned child actor. The latency and idle-CPU wins from the poll removal are real and hold.

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: substantially improved again - STAYS OPEN, with one item closed and one new async hole.**

**Closed on this commit:** `#43`/LC-28's task-count criterion finally landed. An idle invoked child now costs **one** asyncio task, not two (`children + 1`; 1.0 tasks/child at n=2/10/50, independently reproduced three ways), `onDone` latency drops to 0.96 ms median, zero stray timer callbacks while idle, and teardown is clean on state exit, on parent `stop()` and on rollback of the entering transition. **Revise any capacity planning that used `2 x children`.** `#43` is confirm closed.

**Also landed:** `#80`'s `ErrorEvent(type, error, src)` gives us the programmatic error channel this Chore has been asking for on the invoke path - drives new constraint **CV-C21** (branch on `isinstance(event, ErrorEvent)`, read `event.error`; never `.data`, never `event.type.startswith("error.")`, never `event.payload.get(...)` on an error-shaped event). Note `escalate` is the one failure path **not** converted (G-6).

**New and open:** **G-1 (High)** - `Event.system` is a public, user-settable dataclass field, so `send(Event("X", system=True))` bypasses `strict`, `event_schemas`, `onUnhandled` and `"*"` on both engines and via `send_threadsafe`. Drives new constraint **CV-C19** (never forge it; never trust library provenance as a routing or trust boundary). **G-9 (Low)** - the completion-delivery task is created via `_loop_create_task` and registered with neither the `TaskManager` nor a strong reference (latent; 0/300 lost under a GC-hostile probe), riding along on `#43`. **G-8 (Medium)** - `SyncInterpreter` still never delivers `onError` for a failed invoked **child machine**, a fourth sync-only gap under CV-C03.

Stays open against M-2, M-6, G-1 and the still-silent chain cut (CV-C17).

title: Track upstream [VERIFIED FIXED main@3c527b0]: `send(wait=True)` hangs forever on a reused `Event` instance
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
> **Round-7 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `221ce7c`).** **Still VERIFIED FIXED at `221ce7c`** for cases A/B/C. **Case D is NOT fixed** - `stop()` never resolves duplicate-`Event`-instance receipts with `InterpreterStoppedError` (160/160 across 20 trials resolved as ordinary success), and the shipped regression test pins only a weaker `ok == applied` invariant that passes while the defect is live. Reopened upstream as #175.
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md`, `docs/research/xstate/43-r7-findings-register.md`.

**Severity: High. Register id: N-1. Found by the 0.8.0 re-evaluation, not present in the 0.7.0 register.**

`Interpreter.send(event_obj, wait=True)` keys its pending-receipt map on `id(event_obj)`. Two concurrent sends passing the **same `Event` instance** collide on that key: the second `_make_receipt` overwrites the first future, which is then never resolved and never failed. The awaiting coroutine hangs forever - no exception, no timeout, no log line, and `stop()` does not resolve it because the future is no longer in `_receipts`.

This is a silent hang inside the API 0.8.0 added specifically to make `send` answerable, in the release whose stated theme is eliminating silent failure. That is why it is High rather than Medium.

**Measured evidence.** `docs/research/xstate/issues/new-0.8.0/repro/N-01_send-wait-receipt-id-collision.py`, exit 1 on 0.8.0:

```
OBSERVED control_fresh_2way              : resolved
OBSERVED control_fresh_200way            : resolved
OBSERVED control_same_object_sequential  : resolved
OBSERVED subject_same_object_concurrent  : HUNG
```

The 200-way fresh-object control rules out `id()` recycling of dead objects; the sequential control rules out "an `Event` is single-use by design". It is specifically caller-side identity reuse, and reusing a pre-built `Event` as a template is a natural pattern since `send()` accepts `Event` instances in every documented overload.

**Affected contracts.** Every machine that gates a decision on a receipt - B18 `kill_switch`, B20 `risk_lockout`, B17 `live_gate`, and the order path's synchronous checks (constraint CV-C06).

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** Constraint CV-C06 plus lint rule CV-LINT-XS9: every `send(..., wait=True)` call site must pass a literal event type or a freshly-constructed `Event`, never a name bound outside the call. This is a convention backed by an AST check - adequate, but it is exactly the "fails silently if forgotten" shape this Epic exists to remove.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **File the upstream issue** from the prepared draft at `docs/research/xstate/issues/new-0.8.0/N-01-send-wait-receipt-id-collision.md`, which already carries the evidence, the minimal repro, the controls and the proposed fix. Also post the follow-up comment drafted at `issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-42.md` on the parent issue #39.
- **Record the issue number** in `12-challenge-register.md` against the LC-42 row and in `17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md` section 7.3.
- **Keep the repro in the gate**: it already lives under `issues/new-0.8.0/repro/` with the standard exit-1-while-present convention; wire it into `run_gate.py`'s primary set so `E50-T04` executes it per release.
- **Proposed fix to carry into the issue**: replace the identity key with a monotonic per-send token carried on the queued envelope rather than on the caller's object, so caller-side reuse is irrelevant by construction.
- **Verify CV-LINT-XS9 covers it** in the interim.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fix upstream (library repo work).
- Removing CV-C06 / CV-LINT-XS9, which stay until the gate shows the repro passing against a released version.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The issue is filed with evidence and a repro
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then an upstream issue exists carrying the controls, the repro and the proposed fix
  And its number is recorded in 12-challenge-register.md against LC-42

  Given a new upstream release

  Given the upstream issue is marked closed
  Then this Chore closes only if N-01's repro exits 0 in a gate report
  And CV-LINT-XS9 may only be relaxed after that report exists
```

## Technical notes / design
The repro is four lines at its core and runs against a clean install with no CandleViewer dependency, so it is directly actionable upstream. Keep the three controls in the filed version - without them the report invites the "you are holding it wrong" response, and the 200-way control is what proves this is not `id()` recycling.

## Test plan
The repro is the test and is a negative test today: it must fail against 0.8.0, proving it exercises the defect. `E50-T04` runs it per release. Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_send_receipt_fresh_event_only.py` asserting our own call sites comply with CV-C06.

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: VERIFIED FIXED. This Chore may close once a gate report exists against a tagged release.**

`verify-main-5327ba6/N-1_send-wait-receipt-collision.py` and the original `new-0.8.0/repro/N-01_*.py` both exit 0. All acceptance criteria pass:

- Two concurrent `send(ev, wait=True)` calls sharing one `Event` instance both resolve with their own `Receipt`; the caller's object is not mutated and remains usable as a template.
- 200 concurrent sends of one reused instance all resolve.
- `stop()` resolves all outstanding duplicate-instance receipts with `Receipt.error` set to `InterpreterStoppedError`.
- The three named regression tests in `tests/test_interpreter_send_receipt.py` are present and pass.
- Independently re-probed at **500-way concurrency under three policies simultaneously** in the adversarial pass - no collision path remains.

**Root cause fixed structurally, not patched:** `Interpreter._detach()` gives the queued envelope its own identity before it is keyed into the receipt map, so caller-side object reuse can no longer collide.

**Consequence for us: CV-C06's fresh-`Event` clause RETIRES.** Delete the **CV-LINT-XS9** reuse rule and `test_send_receipt_fresh_event_only`. The rest of CV-C06 stands and is **strengthened** by the new deferred-receipt clause - see `E50-C05`.

Upstream `#39` and `#75` are both closable; drafts at `issues/comments-main-5327ba6/39.md` and `75.md`. **Formal closure still requires a gate report against a tagged release** per this Chore's own "close on evidence, not on assertion" criterion - 0.8.1 is not yet tagged, and `__version__` on this commit still reports `0.8.0`.

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: VERIFIED FIXED, unchanged, and re-confirmed against a redesigned interpreter.**

Re-run on `3c527b0` at **500-way concurrency** under `actionErrorPolicy: "rollback"` + `onUnhandled: "defer"` + a bounded `RAISE` inbox: all resolve, none hang - **and `#43`'s one-task-per-child redesign, which reworked `interpreter.py` substantially, did not disturb receipt resolution at all.** That is a meaningful independent confirmation that the `_detach()` fix is structural rather than incidental.

`#39` and `#75` are **confirm closed** (`issues/post-3c527b0/39.md`, `75.md`). CV-C06's fresh-`Event` clause stays retired. **Formal closure of this Chore still requires a gate report against a tagged release** - 0.8.1 is not tagged and `__version__` still reports `0.8.0`.

title: Track upstream [N-3 REOPENED on main@3c527b0]: the sync macrostep budget no longer loses events, but overflow is still silent
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
**Severity: High (N-2) and Medium (N-3). Found by the 0.8.0 re-evaluation, not present in the 0.7.0 register.**

Two independent defects in `SyncInterpreter`, filed together because they share an owner and a decision: both are reasons **MUSTNOT-06 (never use `SyncInterpreter`) is reinforced rather than relaxed** by 0.8.0.

**N-2 (High) - timers unreachable by `tick()` in a running loop.** `RealClock.set_timeout` branches on the *caller's* context, not on which engine owns the clock. A `SyncInterpreter` constructed inside a running asyncio loop parks its `after` deadlines on `loop.call_later`, leaving `clock._heap` empty; `tick()` and the `send()` pump drain only the heap, so `tick()` cannot deliver a genuinely-due deadline. Measured, same machine, `after: {40: "b"}`:

| context | `clock.pending` | state after `tick()` |
|---|---|---|
| off-loop thread (control) | 1 | `{'sy.b'}` |
| inside a running loop | 0 | `{'sy.a'}` |

This is #50's defect displaced rather than resolved: the thread-per-timer is genuinely gone (25 machines -> +0 threads), but the deadline now lands somewhere the sync engine's own API cannot reach. It bites any async app keeping one sync machine for a hot path, and **any async test that constructs a sync machine** - so a suite can be green while production differs.

**N-3 (Medium) - macrostep budget still discards legitimate external events.** `_process_event_queue` increments its runaway counter per *event* and, past `max_iterations` (1000), calls `self._event_queue.clear()`. The 0.8.0 CHANGELOG claims "the two engines now agree"; they do not - `replay_credit` exempts only replayed deferred events. Measured via `send_events()`:

| batch | sync processed | async processed |
|---|---|---|
| 999 | 999 | 999 |
| 1001 | **1000** | 1001 |
| 1501 | **1000** | 1501 |
| 3000 | **1000** | 3000 |

A silent 501-event drop on the default configuration of a shipped engine.

**Affected contracts.** None directly - MUSTNOT-06 bans `SyncInterpreter` everywhere in CandleViewer, and CV-LINT-XS8 enforces that by AST check. This Chore exists because (a) we owe the fixes upstream as the filer of the original issues, and (b) N-2 and N-3 are the evidence that MUSTNOT-06 must not be quietly relaxed now that the thread-per-timer defect is fixed.

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** MUSTNOT-06 + CV-C03 + CV-LINT-XS8: the async `Interpreter` only, in every process. Cost to us: none.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **File two upstream issues** from the prepared drafts: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-02-sync-timer-unreachable-in-loop.md` and `issues/new-0.8.0/N-03-sync-macrostep-budget-clears-queue.md`, each with its runnable repro under `issues/new-0.8.0/repro/`.
- **Post the follow-up comment** drafted at `issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-38.md` on issue #50, since N-2 is the same class that issue addressed.
- **Ask for the CHANGELOG correction** on the "the two engines now agree" line, which is inaccurate as written (part of the N-3 filing).
- **Record the issue numbers** in `12-challenge-register.md` against LC-38 and in `17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md` section 7.3.
- **Wire both repros into `run_gate.py`'s primary set** so `E50-T04` runs them per release.
- **Proposed fixes to carry into the issues**: for N-2, bind the clock lane at attachment time from the `owner` the clock already receives, or reject constructing a `SyncInterpreter` with a `RealClock` inside a running loop (this release's own `WrongThreadError` precedent). For N-3, port the async engine's `_raise_depth` concept - count microstep depth within a macrostep, not events across a drain - and raise on overflow rather than clearing.
- **Record explicitly in the register that MUSTNOT-06 is reinforced**, so a future reader does not read "thread-per-timer fixed" as "sync engine now safe".

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fixes upstream.
- Any relaxation of MUSTNOT-06. These defects are the argument against it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both issues are filed with evidence and repros
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then two upstream issues exist, each with its controls, repro and proposed fix
  And their numbers are recorded in 12-challenge-register.md against LC-38

Scenario: Both repros run in the gate on every release
  Given a new upstream release
  When the scheduled gate job runs
  Then N-02 and N-03 are executed and their results appear in the gate report

Scenario: MUSTNOT-06 survives the fixes
  Given both defects are fixed upstream
  Then MUSTNOT-06 is re-reviewed on evidence at E50-X01, not relaxed automatically
```

## Technical notes / design
Both repros carry controls that isolate the engine: N-2 runs the identical machine on an off-loop thread in the same process and the same run (it fires correctly), and N-3 runs the identical batch through the async engine (all 1501 processed). Without those controls neither report is credible, because both failures look like machine-wide timing artefacts.

N-3's boundary was swept at 999 / 1001 / 1501 / 3000 to confirm `max_iterations = 1000` as the mechanism rather than inferring it from source.

## Test plan
Both repros are negative tests today and must fail against 0.8.0. `E50-T04` runs them per release. On our side the only test needed is `tests/xstate_contract/test_no_sync_interpreter.py` - an AST check that `SyncInterpreter` appears nowhere in `src/`.

## Security notes
Reproduction code and measured behaviour only - no account identifiers, no strategy detail, no credentials, no live or demo account data (C-2.7).

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface.

## Performance notes
No CandleViewer runtime impact; this Chore ships no product code and we do not use the affected engine.

## Observability

## Verification on `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: N-2 VERIFIED FIXED; N-3 PARTIAL. Stays open against N-3's residual and three new defects in the same fix.**

**N-2 - FIXED.** `verify-main-5327ba6/N-2_sync-timer-clock-lane.py` exits 0. `RealClock.set_timeout` now takes an explicit `sync=` lane selector and `BaseInterpreter._clock_sync_lane` decides the lane at construction from the **owning engine**, not from ambient loop state. A `SyncInterpreter` built inside `asyncio.run(...)` shows `clock.pending == 1` for an armed `after`, does not advance on a bare `await asyncio.sleep()`, and `tick()` delivers the elapsed deadline on the caller's thread. Off-loop behaviour is unchanged (25 sync machines, 0 extra threads). Upstream `#76` and `#50` are **closable**.

**N-3 - PARTIAL.** The data-loss defect is genuinely fixed: `send_events(["T"]*1501)` and `*5000` are processed in full with `queue_depth == 0` afterwards, 3,000 independent one-deep raises in one batch are all delivered, sync and async produce byte-identical action traces for a 2,000-event batch, and named parity tests exist in `tests/test_core_algorithm.py`. **But overflow is still silent** - `send()` returns normally, `status` stays `"running"`, and the only signal is a log line. The issue's acceptance criteria asked for the guard to trip *by raising*; the shipped fix stopped the clearing but did not add the raising. `#77` stays open, re-scoped.

**Three new defects landed in this fix's own code path**, all drafted in `issues/new-main/`:

- **F-1 (High)** - the `tripped` flag is scoped to the drain rather than the chain, so one self-feeding event starves every later unrelated event's one-deep `raise` in the same `send_events()` batch. The async engine delivers all of them: this is the engine-parity divergence `#77` claims to have closed, in the opposite direction.
- **F-6 (Medium)** - a `done.invoke` from a sync service is classed as self-generated, so after a trip a legitimate completion is dropped and the machine parks permanently in the invoking state. A silent hang.
- **M-2 (Medium)** - on the async engine the budget does not bound an action-side `send()` at all, so the parity claim covers the `raise` built-in only.

**CV-C03 (async `Interpreter` only) stands, with its rationale shifted**: the sync defects that originally motivated it are fixed; it now stands on F-1 / F-6 and the remaining sync surface. It does **not** protect us from M-2, which is an async hole - hence new constraint **CV-C16** (no action may call `send()` on its own interpreter; use the `raise` built-in), enforced by CV-LINT-XS11, plus **CV-C17** for the silent chain-depth cut.

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

**Status: unchanged - `#77` REOPENED.** Nothing in PR #83 touches the `maxIterations` path. The data-loss defect stays fixed; **overflow is still silent** (`send()` returns normally, `status` stays `"running"`, `last_transition_ok` stays `True`, only a log line), and the acceptance criteria asked for a raise. All three defects in the fix's own code path reproduce identically on `3c527b0` and are now filed as new issues 5 (F-1, High - the `tripped` flag is scoped to the drain, not the chain; `INNER handled: 0 of 5`), 7 (M-2, Medium) and 11 (F-6, Medium) in `issues/post-3c527b0/`. F-9 rides along on `#77`.

**CV-C03, CV-C16 and CV-C17 all stand unchanged.**

title: Track upstream [N-4 VERIFIED FIXED; #79 REOPENED on main@3c527b0] [VERIFIED FIXED main@cec108b]: `send_threadsafe()` strict bypass and `error.*`/`done.*` namespace visibility
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
> **Round-6 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `cec108b`).** #150 charges `send_threadsafe` self-sends to `maxIterations` on both the flag and the contextvars-inherited route. Residuals: R6-05 (Medium, loop-side RAISE refusals are silent → E50-T18) and R6-12 (Medium, the in-flight counter leaks). Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §1/§5.

**Severity: Medium (N-4) and Medium (N-8). Found by the 0.8.0 re-evaluation, not present in the 0.7.0 register.**

Two silent-drop defects in the validation surface 0.8.0 added, filed together because both defeat the same guardrail from different directions.

**N-4 - `send_threadsafe()` bypasses `strict` and `event_schemas`.** `_check_strict` is called from `Interpreter.send`, `SyncInterpreter.send` and the `raise` built-in, but **not** from `send_threadsafe()`, which goes `_prepare_event` -> `_enqueue` directly. Verified on a `strict: True` machine with a registered schema:

```
OBSERVED send_typo               : UnknownEventError
OBSERVED send_bad_payload        : InvalidEventPayloadError
OBSERVED threadsafe_typo         : accepted      <- silently dropped at dispatch
OBSERVED threadsafe_bad_payload  : accepted      <- AND the machine transitioned to st.b
```

The payload case is the worse of the two: an event the registered schema rejects drives a real transition. This matters because 0.8.0 made `send_threadsafe()` the *recommended* - and after the `run_coroutine_threadsafe` break (N-6), effectively the *only* - cross-thread API. The path a multi-threaded app is required to take is the one without the guardrail.

**N-8 - `error.*` / `done.*` user event names are invisible.** `_matching_descriptors` exempts the prefixes `("done.", "error.", "after.", "xstate.", "___xstate")` from wildcard and partial matching by **prefix-testing the name string**, not by checking provenance. That list is now load-bearing in three places (the matcher, the `onUnhandled` policy, `_check_strict`). Verified: a user-sent `error.myapp.validation` does **not** match `on: {"*": ...}`, and an unhandled `done.review` does **not** trip `onUnhandled: "error"` - while the `my.namespaced` control matches fine and the `UNKNOWN_PLAIN` control trips correctly. For any domain naming events `done.review` / `error.validation` this is a silent-drop class, reachable purely by choosing an unlucky name.

**Affected contracts.** N-4: any machine fed from a foreign thread - B13 `ws_conn`, B14 `book`, B11 `recording`. N-8: potentially all twenty, since `done.*`/`error.*` are idiomatic names we would otherwise have used.

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** N-4: constraint CV-C14 - all cross-thread sends go through `cv.statechart.gateway`, which performs the `strict`/`event_schemas` check itself before delegating, since the library's own path does not. N-8: constraint CV-C15 - no CandleViewer event may be named `error.*` or `done.*`, enforced by the event-name gate (`E50-T05`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **File two upstream issues** from the prepared drafts: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-04-send-threadsafe-bypasses-strict.md` and `issues/new-0.8.0/N-08-error-done-namespace-invisible.md`, each with its runnable repro.
- **Post the follow-up comments** drafted at `issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-34.md` (on #51, strict mode) and `issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-03.md` (on #28, which asks for the namespace exemption to be documented).
- **Record the issue numbers** in `12-challenge-register.md` against LC-34 and in `17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md` section 7.3.
- **Wire both repros into `run_gate.py`'s primary set**.
- **Proposed fixes to carry into the issues**: for N-4, route `send_threadsafe()` through the same prepare-and-validate helper `send()` uses, so the two cannot drift again - one validation path, two delivery strategies, matching #60's own lesson. For N-8, tag engine-synthesised events at mint time and test that flag instead of prefix-matching the name, keeping the prefix list only as a fallback for 0.7.x snapshots; plus a `create_machine()` warning when a machine declares an `on:` key in a reserved namespace.
- **Confirm `E50-T05`'s event-name gate rejects reserved namespaces** before any catalogue machine is authored against the library.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fixes upstream.
- Removing CV-C14's gateway wrapper or CV-C15's name ban, both of which stay until a gate report shows the repros passing.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both issues are filed with evidence and repros
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then two upstream issues exist, each with its controls, repro and proposed fix
  And their numbers are recorded in 12-challenge-register.md against LC-34

Scenario: Our own guardrails are in place regardless of upstream
  Given the gateway wrapper and the event-name gate
  Then a cross-thread send of an unknown event is rejected by our code
  And CI fails if any machine declares or any gateway sends an event named error.* or done.*

Scenario: The Chore closes on evidence
  Given the upstream issues are marked closed
  Then this Chore closes only if N-04's and N-08's repros exit 0 in a gate report
```

## Technical notes / design
Both repros carry the controls that make them credible: N-4 shows the ordinary `send()` path correctly raising both `UnknownEventError` and `InvalidEventPayloadError` on the same machine in the same run, so strict mode and the schema are provably armed; N-8 shows `PLAIN` and `my.namespaced` matching `"*"` and `UNKNOWN_PLAIN` tripping `onUnhandled: "error"`, so the mechanism works and only the reserved prefixes are swallowed.

N-8 is arguably a documentation issue rather than a bug, and the draft says so - but "documented silent drop" is still a silent drop, so the draft asks for provenance-tagging first and documentation only as the fallback.

## Test plan
Both repros are negative tests today and must fail against 0.8.0. `E50-T04` runs them per release. On our side: `tests/xstate_contract/test_threadsafe_send_validates_event_name.py` (CV-C14) and an extension to `E50-T05`'s event-name gate covering the reserved namespaces (CV-C15).

## Security notes
Reproduction code and measured behaviour only - no account identifiers, no strategy detail, no credentials, no live or demo account data (C-2.7). N-4 is worth flagging to DevSecOps in passing: an unvalidated event path into a machine that gates order submission is a defence-in-depth concern, which is why CV-C14 wraps rather than trusts.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface.

## Performance notes
The CV-C14 gateway wrapper adds one dict lookup and one schema call per cross-thread send. Negligible against the ~29 us per-event floor, and cross-thread sends are not on the order hot path.

## Observability
Visible through `cv_ci_xstate_gate_items_open{severity}` and the per-version gate reports. The gateway wrapper exports `cv_machine_rejected_events_total{kind,reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both upstream issues filed from the prepared drafts; numbers recorded in the register.
- [ ] Follow-up comments posted on #51 and #28.
- [ ] Both repros wired into `run_gate.py`'s primary check set.
- [ ] CV-C14 gateway wrapper and CV-C15 name ban implemented and tested.
- [ ] Closed only when a gate report shows both repros passing against a released version.
- [ ] Architect review; DevSecOps sighted on N-4.

## Dependencies
- **E50-T04** - the scheduled gate job that verifies closure.
- **E50-T05** - the event-name coverage gate, extended for CV-C15.
- Feeds **E50-X01**.

## Branch
`chore/e50-c15-upstream-n04-n08-validation-bypass`

## References
- docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md (section 5, new defects; section 6, constraints)
- docs/research/xstate/15-reeval-0.8.0-adversarial.md
- docs/research/xstate/16-reeval-0.8.0-diff-review.md
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md (Amendment 1)
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md section 1.3b

## Verification on `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: N-4 VERIFIED FIXED; N-8 PARTIAL and deferred upstream to 0.9. Stays open against N-8.**

**N-4 - FIXED.** `verify-main-5327ba6/N-4_send-threadsafe-strict.py` exits 0; all five acceptance criteria pass. `send_threadsafe()` now calls `_check_strict` before scheduling the enqueue, raising `UnknownEventError` (with a difflib "Did you mean...?" suggestion) or `InvalidEventPayloadError` **on the calling thread**, with nothing queued or processed - verified under loop saturation and 10-thread contention. The schema guardrail applies even when `strict` is unset. All three named tests are present in `tests/test_strict.py` (renamed from `test_strict_mode.py`). Additionally, static `raise` targets are now validated at `create_machine()` time on `strict` machines, with a Did-you-mean suggestion.

**Consequence for us: CV-C14's gateway-validation clause RETIRES.** Delete the duplicate `strict` / `event_schemas` check from `cv.statechart.gateway`. **The `run_coroutine_threadsafe` ban is unaffected and stands** - CV-C14 becomes a ban-only rule. Upstream `#78` and `#51` are **closable**.

**N-8 - PARTIAL, and the real fix is explicitly deferred to 0.9.** What shipped: `events.SYSTEM_EVENT_PREFIXES` as a documented importable constant, a build-time `UserWarning` for reserved-namespace `on` keys the engine will never synthesise (confirmed not to false-positive on engine-shaped keys), and documentation across five guide pages. What did **not** ship: the runtime behaviour. A user event named `done.review` or `error.myapp.validation` is still invisible to `on: {"*": ...}`, still exempt from `onUnhandled: "error"`, and still accepted silently by `strict`. The CHANGELOG defers the fix honestly ("provenance-tagged system events... are planned for 0.9").

**CV-C15 therefore STANDS, and `E50-T05`'s event-name gate must run and must be CASE-INSENSITIVE** - the library's own warning is case-sensitive (`DONE.review` slips through), does not cover `send()`, and only inspects `on` keys (M-5, riding along on `#79`). One new CI risk to note: because `create_machine()` now warns on these keys, a `-W error` setup will break machines that previously worked with the silent-drop bug.

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: the reported defect is FIXED; `#79` is REOPENED for a different criterion, and CV-C15 is RE-SCOPED.**

`#79`'s runtime half landed in PR #83, and landed well. System status is now decided by **provenance** (`Event.system`, `is_system_event()`, `ENGINE_EVENT_TYPES`), not by name. A user-sent `done.review` or `error.validation` is matched by `"*"` and by `"done.*"`, trips `onUnhandled: "error"`, and is rejected by `strict` - **case variants included**, because neither spelling is exempt any longer. The build-time reserved-namespace warning is correctly withdrawn, taking the `-W error` CI risk this Chore flagged with it.

**CV-C15's case-insensitivity clause therefore RETIRES**, and the constraint is **re-scoped**: no CandleViewer event may be named with any prefix in `ENGINE_EVENT_SHAPES` - `done.invoke.`, `done.state.`, `error.platform.`, `after.`, `xstate.`, `___xstate`. Those are the only names `models.is_known_event` still exempts **by name** (G-7), so a typo inside them is still silent under `strict` (`after.party` - not even a well-formed `after.` shape - is accepted undeclared). **`E50-T05` must be re-specified to that list, case-sensitively.**

**`#79` is reopened for acceptance criterion 8**, which is unmet by code in two ways: **G-1** - `Event.system` is a public, user-settable field, so provenance is spoofable from user code (the name rule it replaced was at least hard to hit by accident). **G-2** - provenance is **not persisted**, so a restored engine event becomes user traffic and fails a machine configured `onUnhandled: "error"`; under the old name rule the answer was the same either side of a restore. **G-2 is the one behavioural regression in this window.** G-7, G-10, G-11 and G-12 ride along or are filed separately.

Comment + reopen drafted at `issues/post-3c527b0/79.md`.

title: Order-path receipt gate: a working defer discriminator, or hold (M-1)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context

This Chore exists because a mitigation we had already written down turned out not to work, and the failure mode it was guarding is one that carefulness cannot catch.

**The defect (M-1, High, still present on `main` @ `3c527b0`).** The two library settings the order path is *mandated* to use together - `onUnhandled: "defer"` (CV-C01) and `send(wait=True)` receipts (CV-C06) - compose into a confident false negative. When `defer` parks an event, the run loop still resolves that event's receipt at the end of the macrostep by diffing configuration and context. Nothing changed, because the event was never processed, so the receipt reports `changed=False, error=None`.

That is **byte-identical to "the machine looked at your event and correctly did nothing"**, for an event that is parked and *will* drive its transition on replay - after the caller has already acted on the receipt. A FILL arriving one microstep early (the precise scenario `defer` was adopted to fix) returns a receipt saying the fill did not land. A caller that retries, or reports "not filled" and unwinds, does so against a machine that is about to fill.

Not a hang, not data loss: a gate that says *no* about an event that is about to say *yes*.

**Why this is a new ticket rather than a line in `E50-C05`.** The verdict at `5327ba6` specified a mitigation - *treat `changed=False, error=None` as inconclusive unless `interpreter.deferred_count` is `0` at the same instant* - and recorded it as CV-C06's new clause, to be locked by `test_receipt_is_inconclusive_when_deferred`. **Re-testing on `3c527b0` shows it does not work.** At the caller's `await` point `deferred_count` reads **`0`** for the deferred case *and* for the genuine no-op; the `1` observed in the original probe is read from inside the macrostep, where a caller cannot stand. The test cannot be written as specified, and had we not re-tested, it would have shipped into `cv.statechart` and `tests/xstate_contract/` as a mitigation that reads the wrong value and always passes.

`Receipt` on this commit is still `('state_ids', 'changed', 'error')`. PR #83 rewrote `_handle_unhandled_event` (for #79) and reworked `interpreter.py` (for #43) without either change reaching the receipt.

## Scope

**Until this Chore closes, the rule is a prohibition, not a mitigation:**

> A `send(wait=True)` receipt reading `changed=False, error=None` is **inadmissible** as a gate on any machine configured `onUnhandled: "defer"` - which is every catalogue machine. **No order-path statechart ships** while that holds.

Three ways out, in order of preference:

1. **Upstream fixes it.** `Receipt` gains a `deferred` flag (or a tri-state `disposition`) set from the `defer` decision `_handle_unhandled_event` has already made, or the receipt resolves on replay so `wait=True` means "wait until this event is actually processed". Filed as new issue 1 in `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-3c527b0/` with a runnable repro and acceptance criteria. **This is the outcome to push for.**
2. **The library exposes a correlatable hook.** An `on_event_deferred(event)` plugin hook carrying enough identity to match a specific send would let `cv.statechart` wrap `send(wait=True)` and return a three-valued result of its own. The library does not currently expose one; ask for it as a fallback in the same issue.
3. **We stop depending on the receipt for this class of decision.** Gate on an explicit acknowledgement event from the machine (an `entry` action on the committed state raising a correlated `ACK`), rather than on the transport-level receipt. More work, no upstream dependency, and arguably the more honest design for an order path.

Whichever lands, the enforcement is the same shape: a single wrapper in `cv.statechart`, one lint rule, one contract test that **fails** if the wrapper is bypassed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **CV-LINT-XS9** (re-purposed from the retired fresh-`Event` rule) rejects any direct `send(..., wait=True)` outside `cv.statechart`'s wrapper.
- [ ] `cv.statechart` exposes a send API whose result distinguishes **three** outcomes - processed-and-changed, processed-and-no-op, deferred-and-pending - and the distinction is proved by a test that would fail under today's library behaviour.
- [ ] `test_receipt_is_inconclusive_when_deferred` is **replaced** with a test that asserts against the mechanism actually chosen. The old name must not survive as a green test against a discriminator that reads `0` in both cases.
- [ ] A negative test pins the trap: a deferred event and a genuinely-handled action-less event are both driven, and the test asserts our API reports them **differently** (the library reports them identically).
- [ ] The choice between routes 1/2/3 is recorded in ADR-0016 with its date and its reason.
- [ ] No order-path machine is added to the registry until this is green - enforced by a registry assertion, not by convention.
- [ ] Architect review.

## Dependencies

- Blocks the order-path families in **E50-S01** (B1-B9).
- Feeds **E50-X01** - the go/no-go review must confirm this is closed, not planned.
- Related: **E50-C05** (the `onUnhandled: "defer"` chore this was split out of), **E50-C13** (the `wait=True` receipt chore, verified fixed for its own defect).

## Branch

`chore/e50-c16-order-path-defer-discriminator`

## References

- docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md (section 4.3 - M-1 stated explicitly; section 5.2 - CV-C06 restated)
- docs/research/xstate/23-verify-3c527b0-findings.md (section 2 - the four-variant deep re-test, incl. the `deferred_count` check)
- docs/research/xstate/issues/post-3c527b0/1.md (the upstream issue body)
- docs/research/xstate/issues/post-3c527b0/repro/a2_confirm_deferred_receipt.py, p3_m1_deep.py
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md (Amendment 3)
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md section 1.3

title: Spike: fix the statechart subset and prove the in-house shim is ~1,500 LOC, not a second interpreter
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: shim/dual-runtime/gate/decision work withdrawn by the owner decision for full adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted; 29-statechart-adoption-plan §4a)**

## Context
ADR-0016 Part 2 commits to executing the twenty contracts with a thin in-house interpreter shim until the adoption gate passes. "Thin" is the entire load-bearing word. The ADR's own negative consequences list says it plainly: the shim is real code on the order path, and a shim that grows into a general interpreter is a worse outcome than either adopting the library or hand-rolling.

This spike closes that risk before any of it is built, by answering two questions with evidence rather than confidence: exactly which statechart features do the twenty contracts in `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md` actually use, and what does a shim implementing precisely that subset - and nothing else - cost in lines?

The answer is bounded from above by an unpleasant fact: the library implementing the *full* feature set is 12,104 LOC across nine modules, and `12-challenge-register.md` LC-57 records that its two engines duplicate rather than share the core algorithm. A subset shim that lands anywhere near that number is a failed spike, and the honest response is to say so in the spike report rather than to start building.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **feature census** across all twenty contracts: for each of compound states, parallel regions, guarded transition arrays, `entry`/`exit`, `always`, final states, `tags`, wildcard handlers, `invoke` with `onDone`/`onError`, and snapshot/restore - which machines use it, how many times, and what breaks if it is dropped. Published as a table.
- A **negative census**: every XState v5 feature the contracts do **not** use (`after`, `history`, `delayed transitions`, `spawn` outside `invoke`, actions with parameters, typed events, `sendParent`, nested `always` chains). Each is recorded as explicitly out of the shim's scope, with a note on what a future contract would have to change to need it.
- A **walking skeleton**: the shim's transition core plus B17 (`live_gate`, 3 states) and B8 (`position_protection`, 2 parallel regions, invokes) executing end to end, with LOC measured.
- An **extrapolated LOC estimate** for the full subset, with the walking skeleton as the denominator, and a stated go/no-go against the 1,500-LOC target.
- A **semantics decision record** for each of the seven Blockers: exactly what the shim does instead, written as the test name that will assert it.
- A **spike report** in `docs/research/xstate/21-shim-subset.md` with a recommendation.

## Out of scope
- Building the production shim - that is E50-T07, and it starts from this report.
- The JSON registry and CI gates (E50-T01).
- Any comparison against the library's performance; the library is not adopted and adoption is gated. Throughput measurement belongs to E50-T06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The subset is known, not assumed
  Given all twenty contracts in 28-statechart-catalogue.md
  When the feature census runs
  Then every statechart feature used by any contract is listed with its using machines and a count
  And every XState v5 feature not used is listed as explicitly out of the shim's scope

Scenario: The walking skeleton actually runs two real contracts
  Given the skeleton shim and the B17 and B8 contracts unmodified from the catalogue
  When each is driven through its documented happy path and one failure path
  Then the observed state trace matches the contract's transition table exactly
  And B8's two parallel regions advance independently

Scenario: The size question is answered with a number
  When the spike reports
  Then it states measured skeleton LOC, extrapolated full-subset LOC, and a go/no-go against 1,500
  And if the estimate exceeds 1,500 the report recommends an alternative rather than proceeding

Scenario: Each Blocker has a decided answer before any production code exists
  Given LC-01, LC-02, LC-03, LC-15, LC-16, LC-17 and LC-22
  Then the report names, for each, the shim's behaviour and the test that will assert it
```

## Technical notes / design
Timeboxed to one sprint; the deliverable is the report, and throwaway code is expected and acceptable (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, Spike DoD).

B17 and B8 are chosen deliberately: B17 is the smallest contract in the catalogue (three states, no invokes) so the skeleton can be exercised immediately, and B8 is the hardest shape that is not also the largest - two parallel regions, four invokes, guarded `onError` arrays and a wildcard deferral - so the skeleton meets every structural feature except sheer size.

The census must read the JSON, not the prose: a script over the machine files, so it can be re-run when a contract changes and so the shim's scope can be re-derived rather than remembered.

## Test plan
A spike's tests are its evidence. The skeleton carries trace-assertion tests for B17 and B8 that are **kept and promoted** into E50-T07's suite rather than discarded, because they are the first two conformance cases. The census script gets one unit test asserting it fails loudly on a machine it cannot parse, so a silently shrinking census is impossible.

## Security notes
The spike establishes a security-relevant rule that E50-T07 inherits: the shim resolves actions and guards from a static registry only. It does not `eval`, does not import by name from machine JSON, and does not accept a machine definition from outside the repository. A machine definition is executable configuration and is treated as code. The report states this as a design constraint.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Not a performance spike, but the skeleton records a rough per-transition cost so that E50-T06 has a starting point. For calibration only: the library measures ~33 us per transition and ~8,813 ev/s on a realistic machine shape. The shim is not required to beat that; it is required to be within the same order of magnitude, because the budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` were set against those numbers.

## Observability
None - throwaway code. The report names the `cv_machine_*` series E50-T07 will emit.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/research/xstate/21-shim-subset.md` merged with the feature census, the negative census, the LOC estimate and a go/no-go recommendation.
- [ ] Walking skeleton runs B17 and B8 unmodified; trace tests committed for promotion into E50-T07.
- [ ] A decided shim behaviour recorded for each of the seven Blockers, each named as a test.
- [ ] Census script committed and re-runnable.
- [ ] Reviewed by the Architect; outcome reflected in E50-T07's estimate before it enters a sprint.

## Dependencies
- **E02-T01** - the Python workspace and `services/api` package layout the skeleton lives in.

`spike/e50-shim-subset`
